title: Positive Family Intervention for Severe Challenging Behavior I
authors: Durand V, Hieneman M, Clarke S, Wang M, Rinaldi M

claim.es: En un ensayo aleatorizado con familias de niños con discapacidades del desarrollo y conducta muy difícil, añadir al apoyo conductual positivo un trabajo sobre el pesimismo de los padres mejoró más la conducta que el apoyo conductual solo. Ambos grupos mejoraron.
claim.en: In a randomized trial with families of children with developmental disabilities and severe behaviour that challenges, adding work on parents' pessimism to positive behaviour support improved behaviour more than positive behaviour support alone. Both groups improved.
claim.sv: I en randomiserad studie med familjer till barn med utvecklingsfunktionsnedsättningar och mycket svårt beteende gav positivt beteendestöd plus arbete med föräldrarnas pessimism större förbättring än enbart positivt beteendestöd. Båda grupperna förbättrades.

supports.es: Cuidar también los pensamientos y el desgaste del cuidador dentro de un plan de conducta, no solo la conducta del niño.
supports.en: Caring for the caregiver's own thoughts and exhaustion inside a behaviour plan, not only the child's behaviour.
supports.sv: Att även ta hand om vårdgivarens egna tankar och utmattning i en beteendeplan, inte bara barnets beteende.

doesNotSupport.es: Que sea un resultado específico para niños autistas (el grupo mezclaba discapacidades del desarrollo) ni que los padres tengan la culpa de la conducta.
doesNotSupport.en: That the result is specific to autistic children (the group mixed developmental disabilities), or that parents are to blame for the behaviour.
doesNotSupport.sv: Att resultatet gäller specifikt autistiska barn (gruppen blandade olika utvecklingsfunktionsnedsättningar), eller att föräldrarna bär skulden för beteendet.

title: Challenging behaviour and learning disabilities: prevention and interventions for people with learning disabilities whose behaviour challenges (NICE guideline NG11)
authors: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
journal: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)

claim.es: La guía británica NICE pide entender la conducta antes de actuar: buscar su función, revisar salud física y dolor, apoyar a la familia y reducir al mínimo las intervenciones restrictivas.
claim.en: The UK NICE guideline asks to understand behaviour before acting: look for its function, check physical health and pain, support the family and keep restrictive interventions to a minimum.
claim.sv: Den brittiska NICE-riktlinjen säger att man ska förstå beteendet innan man agerar: leta efter dess funktion, kontrollera kroppslig hälsa och smärta, stödja familjen och hålla begränsande åtgärder till ett minimum.

supports.es: Un plan basado en evaluación funcional y apoyo conductual positivo, revisando primero dolor y salud.
supports.en: A plan built on functional assessment and positive behaviour support, checking pain and health first.
supports.sv: En plan byggd på funktionell bedömning och positivt beteendestöd, där smärta och hälsa kontrolleras först.

doesNotSupport.es: Usar sujeción, encierro o castigo como estrategia, ni consejos sobre medicamentos (NeuroLjus nunca los da).
doesNotSupport.en: Using restraint, seclusion or punishment as a strategy, or advice on medication (NeuroLjus never gives it).
doesNotSupport.sv: Att använda fasthållning, avskiljning eller straff som strategi, eller råd om läkemedel (NeuroLjus ger aldrig sådana).

title: A meta-analysis of sensory modulation symptoms in individuals with autism spectrum disorders.
authors: Ben-Sasson A, Hen L, Fluss R, Cermak SA, Engel-Yeger B, Gal E
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders

claim.es: Las diferencias sensoriales (hiper e hiporreactividad, búsqueda sensorial) son muy frecuentes en autismo y mayores que en otros grupos.
claim.en: Sensory differences (over- and under-responsivity, sensory seeking) are very common in autism and larger than in other groups.
claim.sv: Sensoriska skillnader (över- och underreaktivitet, sensoriskt sökande) är mycket vanliga vid autism och större än i andra grupper.

supports.es: Tomar en serio la carga de sonido, luz y tacto como primer paso del cuidado.
supports.en: Taking sound, light and touch load seriously as a first step in care.
supports.sv: Att ta ljud-, ljus- och beröringsbelastning på allvar som ett första steg i omsorgen.

doesNotSupport.es: Que todas las personas autistas tengan el mismo perfil sensorial; los perfiles son individuales.
doesNotSupport.en: That every autistic person has the same sensory profile; profiles are individual.
doesNotSupport.sv: Att alla autistiska personer har samma sensoriska profil; profilerna är individuella.

title: Sleep problems in autism spectrum disorders: prevalence, nature, & possible biopsychosocial aetiologies.
authors: Richdale AL, Schreck KA

claim.es: Los problemas de sueño afectan a una gran parte de los niños autistas (a menudo 40-80 %) y agravan el día siguiente.
claim.en: Sleep problems affect a large share of autistic children (often 40-80%) and make the next day harder.
claim.sv: Sömnproblem drabbar en stor andel autistiska barn (ofta 40-80 %) och gör nästa dag svårare.

supports.es: Una rutina de noche predecible y de baja estimulación como primera medida.
supports.en: A predictable, low-stimulus evening routine as a first measure.
supports.sv: En förutsägbar kvällsrutin med låg stimulans som första åtgärd.

doesNotSupport.es: Decisiones sobre medicación; la melatonina y otros tratamientos son cosa de profesionales.
doesNotSupport.en: Medication decisions; melatonin and other treatments are for clinicians.
doesNotSupport.sv: Beslut om medicinering; melatonin och andra behandlingar är klinikers sak.

title: A meta-analysis of single case research studies on aided augmentative and alternative communication systems with individuals with autism spectrum disorders.
authors: Ganz JB, Earles-Vollrath TL, Heath AK, Parker RI, Rispoli MJ, Duran JB
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders

claim.es: Los sistemas de CAA con apoyos (PECS, dispositivos de voz) tienen efectos positivos en comunicación para personas autistas.
claim.en: Aided AAC systems (PECS, speech-generating devices) have positive effects on communication for autistic people.
claim.sv: Hjälpmedelsbaserad AKK (PECS, talhjälpmedel) har positiva effekter på kommunikation för autistiska personer.

supports.es: Dar a una persona no hablante una forma fiable de pedir, rechazar y comentar.
supports.en: Giving a non-speaking person a reliable way to request, refuse and comment.
supports.sv: Att ge en icke-talande person ett pålitligt sätt att be om, avböja och kommentera.

doesNotSupport.es: Que la comunicación solo cuente cuando es habla.
doesNotSupport.en: That communication only counts when it is speech.
doesNotSupport.sv: Att kommunikation bara räknas när den är tal.

title: The impact of parenting stress: a meta-analysis of studies comparing the experience of parenting stress in parents of children with and without autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Hayes SA, Watson SL
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders

claim.es: Los padres y madres de niños autistas presentan niveles de estrés claramente más altos que otros padres; el apoyo al cuidador es parte del cuidado.
claim.en: Parents of autistic children show clearly higher stress than other parents; caregiver support is part of care.
claim.sv: Föräldrar till autistiska barn visar tydligt högre stress än andra föräldrar; stöd till vårdgivaren är en del av omsorgen.

supports.es: Planificar descanso y apoyo para quien cuida, no solo rutinas para la persona.
supports.en: Planning rest and support for the caregiver, not only routines for the person.
supports.sv: Att planera vila och stöd för vårdgivaren, inte bara rutiner för personen.

doesNotSupport.es: Culpar al niño o la niña del estrés familiar.
doesNotSupport.en: Blaming the child for family stress.
doesNotSupport.sv: Att skylla familjens stress på barnet.

title: Feeding problems and nutrient intake in children with autism spectrum disorders: a meta-analysis and comprehensive review of the literature.
authors: Sharp WG, Berry RC, McCracken C, Nuhu NN, Marvel E, Saulnier CA, Klin A, Jones W, Jaquess DL
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders

claim.es: Los niños autistas tienen muchas más dificultades de alimentación (selectividad, rechazo) que otros niños.
claim.en: Autistic children have far more feeding difficulties (selectivity, refusal) than other children.
claim.sv: Autistiska barn har betydligt fler svårigheter med mat (selektivitet, vägran) än andra barn.

supports.es: Bajar la presión en las comidas y respetar los límites sensoriales con la comida.
supports.en: Lowering pressure at meals and respecting sensory limits around food.
supports.sv: Att sänka pressen vid måltider och respektera sensoriska gränser kring mat.

doesNotSupport.es: Forzar alimentos; las dudas de nutrición van a un profesional.
doesNotSupport.en: Forcing foods; nutrition concerns go to a clinician.
doesNotSupport.sv: Att tvinga i mat; näringsfrågor går till en kliniker.

title: Evaluating visual activity schedules as evidence-based practice for individuals with autism spectrum disorders.
authors: Knight V, Sartini E, Spriggs AD
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders

claim.es: Los horarios visuales (secuencias de imágenes de lo que viene) son una práctica con evidencia para transiciones y autonomía.
claim.en: Visual activity schedules (picture sequences of what comes next) are an evidence-based practice for transitions and independence.
claim.sv: Visuella scheman (bildsekvenser av vad som kommer) är en evidensbaserad metod för övergångar och självständighet.

supports.es: La tarjeta visual de cada rutina de Companion.
supports.en: The visual card in every Companion routine.
supports.sv: Bildkortet i varje Companion-rutin.

doesNotSupport.es: Que los horarios eliminen la necesidad de escuchar el «no» de la persona.
doesNotSupport.en: That schedules remove the need to listen to the person's refusal.
doesNotSupport.sv: Att scheman tar bort behovet av att lyssna på personens nej.

title: Evidence-Based Practices for Children, Youth, and Young Adults with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Comprehensive Review.
authors: Wong C, Odom SL, Hume KA, Cox AW, Fettig A, Kucharczyk S, Brock ME, Plavnick JB, Fleury VP, Schultz TR
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders

claim.es: Una revisión de 29 000 artículos identificó 27 prácticas con evidencia, entre ellas apoyos visuales, modelado en vídeo, historias sociales y enseñanza de comunicación aumentativa.
claim.en: A review of 29,000 articles identified 27 evidence-based practices, including visual supports, video modelling, social narratives and augmentative communication instruction.
claim.sv: En genomgång av 29 000 artiklar identifierade 27 evidensbaserade metoder, bland dem visuellt stöd, videomodellering, sociala berättelser och undervisning i alternativ kommunikation.

supports.es: Preparar transiciones (dentista, escuela, salidas) con imágenes, vídeo o una historia corta de lo que va a pasar.
supports.en: Preparing transitions (dentist, school, outings) with pictures, video or a short story of what will happen.
supports.sv: Att förbereda övergångar (tandläkare, skola, utflykter) med bilder, video eller en kort berättelse om vad som ska hända.

doesNotSupport.es: Que una práctica funcione para todos o sustituya escuchar a la persona en el momento.
doesNotSupport.en: That a practice works for everyone or replaces listening to the person in the moment.
doesNotSupport.sv: Att en metod fungerar för alla eller ersätter att lyssna på personen i stunden.

title: Social Stories™ to alleviate challenging behaviour and social difficulties exhibited by children with autism spectrum disorder in mainstream schools: design of a manualised training toolkit and feasibility study for a cluster randomised controlled trial with nested qualitative and cost-effectiveness components.
authors: Wright B, Marshall D, Adamson J, Ainsworth H, Ali S, Allgar V, Collingridge Moore D, Cook E, Dempster P, Hackney L, McMillan D, Trepél D, Williams C

title: What Is the Male-to-Female Ratio in Autism Spectrum Disorder? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Loomes R, Hull L, Mandy WPL
journal: Journal of the American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry

claim.es: La proporción real hombre:mujer en autismo es cercana a 3:1, no 4:1: muchas niñas y mujeres quedan sin identificar.
claim.en: The true male-to-female ratio in autism is closer to 3:1, not 4:1: many girls and women go unidentified.
claim.sv: Den verkliga könsfördelningen vid autism är närmare 3:1, inte 4:1: många flickor och kvinnor förblir oidentifierade.

supports.es: Tomar en serio las necesidades de una niña o mujer aunque no tenga una presentación «típica».
supports.en: Taking a girl's or woman's needs seriously even without a 'typical' presentation.
supports.sv: Att ta en flickas eller kvinnas behov på allvar även utan en «typisk» bild.

doesNotSupport.es: Ningún diagnóstico; la identificación es clínica.
doesNotSupport.en: Any diagnosis; identification is clinical.
doesNotSupport.sv: Ingen diagnos; identifiering är klinisk.

title: Sensory perception in autism.
authors: Robertson CE, Baron-Cohen S

claim.es: La percepción sensorial atípica es un rasgo central del autismo y se relaciona con el bienestar diario, no un detalle secundario.
claim.en: Atypical sensory perception is a core feature of autism tied to daily wellbeing, not a side detail.
claim.sv: Avvikande sensorisk perception är ett centralt drag vid autism kopplat till dagligt välbefinnande, inte en bisak.

supports.es: Adaptar el entorno (ruido, luz, gente) antes de añadir exigencias.
supports.en: Adapting environments (noise, light, crowds) before adding demands.
supports.sv: Att anpassa miljön (ljud, ljus, folkmängd) innan man ställer krav.

doesNotSupport.es: Un único mecanismo o una «cura» de las diferencias sensoriales.
doesNotSupport.en: A single mechanism or 'cure' for sensory differences.
doesNotSupport.sv: En enda mekanism eller ett «botemedel» för sensoriska skillnader.

title: Guided self-help for depression in autistic adults: the ADEPT feasibility RCT.
authors: Russell A, Gaunt D, Cooper K, Horwood J, Barton S, Ensum I, Ingham B, Parr J, Metcalfe C, Rai D, Kessler D, Wiles N

title: The 'double empathy problem': Ten years on.
authors: Milton D, Gurbuz E, Lopez B
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice

claim.es: La dificultad de entenderse es mutua: las personas no autistas también fallan al leer a las autistas. No es un déficit de un solo lado.
claim.en: Misunderstanding runs both ways: non-autistic people also struggle to read autistic people. It is not a one-sided deficit.
claim.sv: Missförstånd går åt båda hållen: icke-autistiska personer har också svårt att läsa autistiska. Det är inte en ensidig brist.

supports.es: Que los cuidadores adapten su propia comunicación, no solo la de la persona.
supports.en: Caregivers adapting their own communication, not only the person's.
supports.sv: Att vårdgivare anpassar sin egen kommunikation, inte bara personens.

doesNotSupport.es: Que el apoyo a la comunicación sea innecesario.
doesNotSupport.en: That communication support is unnecessary.
doesNotSupport.sv: Att kommunikationsstöd är onödigt.

title: Indifference or hypersensitivity? Solving the riddle of the pain profile in individuals with autism.
authors: Hoffman T, Bar-Shalita T, Granovsky Y, Gal E, Kalingel-Levi M, Dori Y, Buxbaum C, Yarovinsky N, Weissman-Fogel I

claim.es: Adultos autistas puntuaron más alto el dolor por calor y mostraron un perfil pronociceptivo: más sensibilidad, no menos.
claim.en: Autistic adults rated heat pain higher and showed a pronociceptive profile: more sensitivity, not less.
claim.sv: Autistiska vuxna skattade värmesmärta högre och visade en pronociceptiv profil: mer känslighet, inte mindre.

supports.es: No dar por hecho que a la persona «no le importa» un procedimiento o una lesión.
supports.en: Not assuming a person 'doesn't mind' a procedure or an injury.
supports.sv: Att inte anta att en person «inte bryr sig» om ett ingrepp eller en skada.

doesNotSupport.es: Una regla universal para todas las personas; el dolor experimental no es el dolor cotidiano.
doesNotSupport.en: A universal rule for every person; experimental pain differs from daily pain.
doesNotSupport.sv: En universell regel för alla; experimentell smärta skiljer sig från vardaglig smärta.

title: Community-Delivered Collaborative and Proactive Solutions and Parent Management Training for Oppositional Youth: A Randomized Trial.
authors: Murrihy RC, Drysdale SAO, Dedousis-Wallace A, Rémond L, McAloon J, Ellis DM, Halldorsdottir T, Greene RW, Ollendick TH
abstract: The aim of this study was to examine the relative effectiveness of Collaborative and Proactive Solutions (CPS) and Parent Management Training (PMT) for youth with oppositional defiant disorder (ODD) in a community setting. Based on a semistructured diagnostic interview, 160 youth with ODD (ages 7-14; 72% male; ethnicity representative of the wider Australian population) were randomized to CPS (n = 81) or PMT (n = 79) for up to 16 weekly sessions. The primary hypothesis was that participants in the CPS group, treated in a community setting, would exhibit significant improvement in ODD, equivalent to that of an evidence-based treatment, PMT. Assessment was conducted at baseline, post-intervention, and at 6-month follow-up, using independently rated semistructured diagnostic interviews, parent ratings of ODD symptoms, and global ratings of severity and improvement. Analyses were conducted with hierarchical growth linear modeling, ANCOVA, and equivalence testing using an intent-to-treat sample. Both treatments demonstrated similar outcomes, with 45-50% of youth in the nonclinical range after treatment, and 67% considered much improved. No differences were found between groups, and group equivalency was shown on the independent clinician and parent-rated measures. Gains were maintained at the 6-month follow-up. In conclusion, CPS works as effectively as the well-established treatment, PMT, for youths with ODD, when implemented in a community-based setting. As such, CPS provides a viable choice for families who seek alternate treatments.

sheet.es: Si le cuesta que su hijo o hija coopere, existen dos enfoques de trabajo con la familia: uno basado en resolver juntos los problemas (Collaborative and Proactive Solutions) y otro de entrenamiento para madres y padres. Puede preguntar a un profesional cuál encaja mejor con su familia. Es un ensayo aleatorizado con 160 jóvenes de 7-14 años con trastorno negativista desafiante; ambos enfoques dieron resultados similares y las mejoras se mantuvieron a los 6 meses. Límites: el resumen no indica cuántas personas eran autistas, así que no sirve como regla para todas las familias ni para todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If getting your child to cooperate is hard, there are two ways of working with families: one built on solving problems together (Collaborative and Proactive Solutions) and one that trains parents. You can ask a professional which might suit your family better. This was a randomized trial of 160 young people aged 7-14 with oppositional defiant disorder; both approaches gave similar results, and gains held at 6 months. Limits: the abstract does not say how many participants were autistic, so it is not a rule for every family or every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om det är svårt att få ditt barn att samarbeta finns två sätt att arbeta med familjer: ett bygger på att lösa problem tillsammans (Collaborative and Proactive Solutions) och ett tränar föräldrar. Du kan fråga en professionell vilket som passar din familj bäst. Detta var en randomiserad studie med 160 unga i åldern 7-14 med trotssyndrom (ODD); båda metoderna gav liknande resultat och förbättringarna höll i sig efter 6 månader. Begränsningar: sammanfattningen anger inte hur många deltagare som var autistiska, så resultatet gäller inte som regel för alla familjer eller alla autistiska personer.

claim.es: En servicios comunitarios, un ensayo aleatorizado encontró que CPS fue tan eficaz como el entrenamiento de padres para la conducta oposicionista, con mejoras mantenidas en el seguimiento.
claim.en: In community services, a randomized trial found CPS as effective as parent management training for oppositional behaviour, with gains kept at follow-up.
claim.sv: I kommunal verksamhet fann en randomiserad studie att CPS var lika effektivt som föräldraträning vid trotsbeteende, med förbättringar som höll vid uppföljning.

supports.es: Que el enfoque colaborativo también funciona fuera de clínicas universitarias, en servicios del día a día.
supports.en: That the collaborative approach also works outside university clinics, in everyday services.
supports.sv: Att det samarbetsinriktade arbetssättet fungerar även utanför universitetskliniker, i vardaglig verksamhet.

doesNotSupport.es: Conclusiones directas sobre autismo, discapacidad intelectual o personas que no hablan.
doesNotSupport.en: Direct conclusions about autism, intellectual disability or non-speaking people.
doesNotSupport.sv: Direkta slutsatser om autism, intellektuell funktionsnedsättning eller icke-talande personer.

title: A group intervention for parents and carers to recognise and understand restricted and repetitive behaviour in autistic children: a multisite RCT.
authors: Grahame V, Kernohan A, Kharati E, Mathias A, Butcher C, Dixon L, Fletcher-Watson S, Garland D, Glod M, Goodwin J, Heron S, Honey E, Le Couteur A, Mackie L, Ogundimu E, Probert H, Riby D, Rob P, Rogan

title: Stress State Classification Based on Deep Neural Network and Electrodermal Activity Modeling.
authors: Vasile F, Vizziello A, Brondino N, Savazzi P
abstract: Electrodermal Activity (EDA) has become of great interest in the last several decades, due to the advent of new devices that allow for recording a lot of psychophysiological data for remotely monitoring patients' health. In this work, a novel method of analyzing EDA signals is proposed with the ultimate goal of helping caregivers assess the emotional states of autistic people, such as stress and frustration, which could cause aggression onset. Since many autistic people are non-verbal or suffer from alexithymia, the development of a method able to detect and measure these arousal states could be useful to aid with predicting imminent aggression. Therefore, the main objective of this paper is to classify their emotional states to prevent these crises with proper actions. Several studies were conducted to classify EDA signals, usually employing learning methods, where data augmentation was often performed to countervail the lack of extensive datasets. Differently, in this work, we use a model to generate synthetic data that are employed to train a deep neural network for EDA signal classification. This method is automatic and does not require a separate step for features extraction, as in EDA classification solutions based on machine learning. The network is first trained with synthetic data and then tested on another set of synthetic data, as well as on experimental sequences. In the first case, an accuracy of 96% is reached, which becomes 84% in the second case, thus demonstrating the feasibility of the proposed approach and its high performance.

sheet.es: Los sensores de actividad electrodérmica (sudoración de la piel) podrían algún día ayudar a notar señales de estrés, pero hoy no sustituyen observar a la persona. Mañana, fíjate en sus señales habituales de malestar y reduce las exigencias o el ruido si las ves. Es un estudio técnico con personas autistas: entrenaron una red neuronal con datos sintéticos y la probaron con otros datos sintéticos (precisión del 96%) y con secuencias experimentales (84%). Como límites, es una prueba de viabilidad, no una herramienta lista para el hogar, y cada persona puede reaccionar de forma distinta.
sheet.en: Skin-sweat sensors (electrodermal activity) might one day help flag signs of stress, but today they do not replace watching the person. Tomorrow, notice their usual signs of distress and lower demands or noise if you see them. This was a technical study involving autistic people: a neural network was trained on synthetic data, then tested on other synthetic data (accuracy of 96%) and on experimental sequences (84%). Its limits: it shows feasibility, not a tool ready for home use, and each person may respond differently.
sheet.sv: Sensorer som mäter hudens svettning (elektrodermal aktivitet) kan kanske en dag hjälpa till att upptäcka stress, men ersätter inte att observera personen. I morgon kan du uppmärksamma personens vanliga tecken på obehag och sänka krav eller ljudnivå om du ser dem. Det var en teknisk studie med autistiska personer: ett neuralt nätverk tränades på syntetiska data och testades på andra syntetiska data (noggrannhet på 96%) och på experimentella sekvenser (84%). Begränsningar: den visar genomförbarhet, inte ett färdigt verktyg för hemmet, och varje person kan reagera olika.

title: Medical student perceptions of autism education: A qualitative study.
authors: Gallaher L, Butler C, Banerjee S, Wright J, White A, Daley S
abstract: Background The global prevalence of autism is reported to be at least 1% and is rising. Autistic people have a range of comorbidities resulting in a high use of health services. Doctors of nearly all specialties are likely to encounter autistic people in their practice. Autistic people report dissatisfactory care and encounter disproportionately worse health-related outcomes than non-autistic people, which in part has been attributed to a lack of skill and awareness in the medical workforce. At present, autism education is not always included in undergraduate medical curricula. In England, the Department of Health and Social Care has mandated that autism education should be included in all undergraduate medical curricula but current evidence relating to the delivery and receipt of autism education is poor. A greater understanding of medical student perceptions of autism education is required to inform curriculum development. This qualitative study sought to explore the perceptions of autism education in final year medical students at a medical school in South-East England by 1) assessing their perceived preparedness to care for autistic people once they have graduated from medical school and 2) determining their perceived acceptability of a new undergraduate education programme, Time for Autism (TfA). Materials and methods A purposeful sample of ten final-year medical students were recruited. Students completed in-depth, individual interviews. Data was analysed using thematic analysis. Results Four key themes were identified: Learning environment, Exposure, Relevance and Curricular priority. The findings of this study indicate that medical students perceived greatest value in autism education when it was directly relevant to developing preparedness for practice. Value was influenced by the perceived curricular priority attached to autism education. The new autism programme, Time for Autism was perceived to add relevance and priority to autism education in the existing curriculum in this medical school setting. Discussion The study findings shed new light on medical education literature, emphasising the importance of congruence between the provision of autism education and the prioritisation of autism education within the curriculum. Consideration of relevance and curricular priority can be used to support the development of autism education in future medical curricula.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista a una consulta médica, puedes explicar de antemano qué apoyos necesita y pedir que se tengan en cuenta. Muchos profesionales aún están aprendiendo sobre autismo. La evidencia es un estudio cualitativo con entrevistas a 10 estudiantes de medicina de último curso en el sureste de Inglaterra; valoraron más la formación sobre autismo cuando era relevante para su práctica y tenía prioridad en el plan de estudios. Sus límites: es un grupo pequeño de una sola facultad, no participaron personas autistas y no muestra cómo atienden después a los pacientes, así que no vale para todos los casos.
sheet.en: If you go with an autistic person to a medical appointment, you can explain beforehand what supports they need and ask for them to be taken into account. Many professionals are still learning about autism. The evidence is a qualitative study with interviews of 10 final-year medical students in South-East England; they valued autism education most when it was relevant to practice and given priority in the curriculum. Its limits: it is a small group from one medical school, no autistic people took part, and it does not show how students care for patients later, so it cannot be applied to every situation.
sheet.sv: Om du följer med en autistisk person till ett läkarbesök kan du i förväg förklara vilket stöd personen behöver och be om att det beaktas. Många yrkesutövare lär sig fortfarande om autism. Underlaget är en kvalitativ studie med intervjuer av 10 läkarstudenter på sista året i sydöstra England; de värderade utbildning om autism mest när den var relevant för yrkespraktiken och prioriterad i utbildningsplanen. Begränsningar: en liten grupp från en enda läkarutbildning, inga autistiska personer deltog och studien visar inte hur studenterna senare vårdar patienter, så den gäller inte alla situationer.

title: Autistic Adult Perspectives on Occupational Therapy for Autistic Children and Youth.
authors: Sterman J, Gustafson E, Eisenmenger L, Hamm L, Edwards J
abstract: The Autistic community values neurodiversity-positive approaches rather than behavioral interventions for Autistic children; however, little is known about what that would look like in occupational therapy. Frequently, researchers seek parent perspectives for understanding Autistic children's preferences, while to date insufficient attention has been paid to Autistic adults as valuable informants on the Autistic experience of Autistic children. The objective of the study was to understand Autistic adult perspectives on pediatric occupational therapy for Autistic children. We sought and thematically analyzed data from a large Facebook group and an occupational therapy podcast on Autistic values, needs, and experiences in pediatric occupational therapy. Participants described wanting therapy that supported Autistic identities rather than trying to "fix" children, changing environments or tasks to promote participation, and setting goals that address self-advocacy and autonomy. Occupational therapy practitioners should critically reflect on their practice's alignment with Autistic values and start to shift their practice as needed.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija autista recibe terapia ocupacional, puede preguntar al terapeuta si los objetivos apoyan su identidad autista, si se pueden adaptar el entorno o las tareas, y si se trabaja la autodefensa y la autonomía. Es un estudio con personas autistas adultas: se analizaron temáticamente datos de un grupo grande de Facebook y de un pódcast de terapia ocupacional. Estas personas pedían terapia que no intente "arreglar" a la infancia. Como los datos provienen de espacios en línea, no representan a todas las personas autistas ni muestran qué funciona para cada niño o niña.
sheet.en: If your autistic child has occupational therapy, you can ask the therapist whether the goals support their autistic identity, whether the environment or tasks can be adapted, and whether self-advocacy and autonomy are addressed. This was a study with autistic adults: researchers thematically analyzed data from a large Facebook group and an occupational therapy podcast. Participants wanted therapy that does not try to "fix" children. Because the data came from online spaces, they do not represent all autistic people or show what works for each child.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn går i arbetsterapi kan du fråga terapeuten om målen stödjer barnets autistiska identitet, om miljön eller uppgifterna kan anpassas och om självadvokatur och autonomi ingår. Det är en studie med autistiska vuxna: forskarna analyserade tematiskt data från en stor Facebook-grupp och en podd om arbetsterapi. Deltagarna ville ha terapi som inte försöker "fixa" barn. Eftersom data kommer från nätforum representerar de inte alla autistiska personer och visar inte vad som fungerar för varje barn.

title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of suicidality in autistic and possibly autistic people without co-occurring intellectual disability.
authors: Newell V, Phillips L, Jones C, Townsend E, Richards C, Cassidy S
abstract: Background Suicidality is highly prevalent in autistic people without co-occurring intellectual disabilities, and high autistic traits are found in adults who have attempted suicide. However, prevalence rates for both autistic and possibly autistic people have not been synthesised meta-analytically. Aims To (1) calculate pooled prevalence estimates of suicidality in autistic people and possibly autistic people without co-occurring intellectual disability; (2) evaluate the influence of participant and study level characteristics on heterogeneity; and (3) determine the quality of evidence. Methods Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis guidelines were followed. PsycINFO, Embase, MEDLINE and Web of Science were systematically searched from 1992 to January 25, 2022. Empirical quantitative studies reporting prevalence of suicidal ideation, suicide plans, or suicide attempts and behaviours were considered for inclusion. Random effects models were used to estimate pooled prevalence of each suicidality outcome with 95% confidence intervals. Heterogeneity was explored using sensitivity and moderator analyses. Results Data from 48,186 autistic and possibly autistic participants in 36 primary studies were meta-analysed. Pooled prevalence of suicidal ideation was 34.2% (95% CI 27.9-40.5), suicide plans 21.9% (13.4-30.4), and suicidal attempts and behaviours 24.3% (18.9-29.6). High levels of heterogeneity (I 2 > 75) were observed in all three analyses. Estimates did not differ between autistic or possibly autistic samples. Geographical location (p = 0.005), transgender or gender non-conforming samples (p Conclusions The results confirm suicidality is highly prevalent in both autistic and possibly autistic people without co-occurring intellectual disability and highlights potential moderators. Possibly autistic individuals require more attention in clinical and research considerations going forward to further understand and prevent suicide in both groups.

title: Centering the Inner Experience of Autism: Development of the Self-Assessment of Autistic Traits.
authors: Ratto AB, Bascom J, daVanport S, Strang JF, Anthony LG, Verbalis A, Pugliese C, Nadwodny N, Brown LXZ, Cruz M, Hector BL, Kapp SK, Giwa Onaiwu M, Raymaker DM, Robison JE, Stewart C, Stone R, Whetsell
abstract: Current tools for identifying autism are critiqued for their lack of specificity and sensitivity, especially in autistic people who are older, have higher verbal ability or significant compensatory skills, and are not cisgender boys. This may reflect the following: the historical focus of autism research on White (cisgender) male, upper and middle class children; limited interest in the inner, lived experience of autism; and the predominance of a deficit-based model of autism. We report here on the first attempt of which we are aware to develop a clinical self-report measure of autistic traits as described by autistic people . We believe this is an advance in methodology because prior work in the development of autistic trait/diagnostic measures has prioritized the perspectives of nonautistic clinicians and scientists. The measure was developed under the leadership of two autistic researchers and constructed by leveraging descriptions of autism by autistic people to generate items designed to encompass the range of the autistic experience, using strength-based, accessible language. The team utilized iterative feedback from a panel of autistic experts to refine and enhance the measure, called the Self Assessment of Autistic Traits (SAAT). It is intended for people 16 years or older and uses a format that is designed to increase its accessibility and acceptability for autistic respondents. Future work will report on the preliminary psychometrics of the SAAT, with a long-term goal of advancing our understanding of the inner autistic experience and enhancing the clinical and scientific assessment of autism.

sheet.es: Si usted o la persona a quien acompaña (16 años o más) busca entender sus rasgos autistas, puede ser útil valorar herramientas que describen la experiencia interna con lenguaje basado en fortalezas. Este estudio presenta el SAAT, un cuestionario de autoevaluación creado bajo el liderazgo de dos investigadores autistas, a partir de descripciones de personas autistas y refinado con un panel de expertos autistas. Pensado para captar mejor a mujeres, personas no cisgénero, adultas o con estrategias de compensación, a quienes otras herramientas suelen pasar por alto. Es un estudio de desarrollo: aún no se ha comprobado su precisión, no sustituye una evaluación profesional y no sirve para diagnosticar por sí solo.
sheet.en: If you or the person you support (aged 16 or older) wants to understand their autistic traits, it may help to look for tools that describe inner experience in strength-based language. This study presents the SAAT, a self-report questionnaire led by two autistic researchers, built from autistic people's own descriptions and refined with a panel of autistic experts. It aims to better recognise women, people who are not cisgender, adults and those who use compensatory strategies, groups older tools often miss. This is a development study: its accuracy has not yet been tested, it does not replace a professional assessment, and it cannot diagnose on its own.
sheet.sv: Om du eller personen du stöttar (16 år eller äldre) vill förstå sina autistiska drag kan det vara värdefullt att söka verktyg som beskriver den inre upplevelsen med styrkebaserat språk. Studien presenterar SAAT, ett självskattningsformulär som leddes av två autistiska forskare, byggdes på autistiska personers egna beskrivningar och förfinades med en panel av autistiska experter. Det ska bättre fånga kvinnor, icke-cispersoner, vuxna och personer som kompenserar, grupper som äldre verktyg ofta missar. Detta är en utvecklingsstudie: träffsäkerheten är ännu inte prövad, formuläret ersätter inte en professionell utredning och kan inte ensamt ställa diagnos.

title: Characterizing the physical and mental health profile of children, adolescents and adults with autism spectrum disorder in Spain.
authors: Vidriales-Fernández R, Plaza-Sanz M, Hernández-Layna C, Verde-Cagiao M, Benito-Ruiz G, Carvajal-Molina F
abstract: Introduction Autistic men and women are more likely to experience health issues than the general population, although the available epidemiological studies addressing co-occurrence conditions are limited. This is the first Spanish epidemiologic study addressing the health profile and poor-health exacerbating factors in individuals of all ages with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Methods We analyzed 2,629 registries extracted from Autism Spain's sociodemographic registry (November 2017-May 2020). A descriptive health data analysis was conducted to assess the prevalence of other conditions associated to ASD in the Spanish population. Nervous system disorders (12.9%), mental health diagnoses (17.8%), and other comorbidities (25.4%) were reported. Men-to-women ratio was 4:1. Results Women, elder individuals and those with intellectual disability (ID) were at an increased risk of health comorbidities and psychopharmacological exposure. Women were also more prone to severe intellectual and functional impairment. Nearly all individuals had difficulties in their adaptative functioning, especially those with ID (50% of the population). Almost half of the sample received psychopharmacological treatments starting from infancy and early childhood, mostly antipsychotics and anticonvulsants. Discussion This study represents an important first approach to the health status of autistic people in Spain and can contribute to the development of public policies and innovative health strategies.

sheet.es: Conviene que la salud física y mental de las personas autistas se revise con regularidad, sobre todo en mujeres, personas mayores y personas con discapacidad intelectual, que mostraron más problemas de salud asociados. Puede ayudar llevar a la consulta un registro de síntomas y cambios. Se analizaron 2.629 registros de personas autistas de todas las edades en España, en un estudio descriptivo. Sus límites: los datos vienen de un registro de asociaciones, no muestran causas y no describen a cada persona. Las decisiones sobre tratamientos médicos corresponden siempre a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: It is worth reviewing autistic people's physical and mental health regularly, especially for women, older people and people with intellectual disability, who showed more associated health problems. Bringing a record of symptoms and changes to appointments can help. The study analysed 2,629 registry records of autistic people of all ages in Spain, using a descriptive design. Its limits: the data come from an association registry, show no causes, and cannot describe any individual person. Decisions about medical treatment always belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Det är värt att regelbundet följa upp autistiska personers fysiska och psykiska hälsa, särskilt hos kvinnor, äldre och personer med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning, som hade fler samtidiga hälsoproblem. Det kan hjälpa att ta med anteckningar om symtom och förändringar till besöken. Studien analyserade 2,629 registerposter om autistiska personer i alla åldrar i Spanien, med en beskrivande design. Begränsningar: uppgifterna kommer från ett föreningsregister, visar inga orsaker och kan inte beskriva en enskild person. Beslut om medicinsk behandling fattas alltid av en kliniker.

title: Autism Spectrum Disorder and auditory sensory alterations: a systematic review on the integrity of cognitive and neuronal functions related to auditory processing.
authors: Gonçalves AM, Monteiro P
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition with a wide spectrum of symptoms, mainly characterized by social, communication, and cognitive impairments. Latest diagnostic criteria according to DSM-5 (Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition, 2013) now include sensory issues among the four restricted/repetitive behavior features defined as "hyper- or hypo-reactivity to sensory input or unusual interest in sensory aspects of environment". Here, we review auditory sensory alterations in patients with ASD. Considering the updated diagnostic criteria for ASD, we examined research evidence (2015-2022) of the integrity of the cognitive function in auditory-related tasks, the integrity of the peripheral auditory system, and the integrity of the central nervous system in patients diagnosed with ASD. Taking into account the different approaches and experimental study designs, we reappraise the knowledge on auditory sensory alterations and reflect on how these might be linked with behavior symptomatology in ASD.

sheet.es: Si a tu hijo o familiar autista le molestan, le abruman o le fascinan ciertos sonidos, tómalo en serio: es una diferencia real en cómo procesa la audición, no un capricho. Mañana puedes observar qué sonidos le afectan, ofrecer cascos o tapones, avisar antes de ruidos fuertes y pactar un rincón tranquilo. Pregúntale qué le ayuda. Esta revisión sistemática reunió estudios de 2015 a 2022 sobre audición, oído y cerebro en personas autistas. Sus límites: los estudios usaron métodos muy distintos, describen diferencias más que soluciones probadas, y cada persona vive el sonido a su manera.
sheet.en: If your autistic child or family member is bothered, overwhelmed or fascinated by certain sounds, take it seriously: it reflects a real difference in how hearing is processed, not a whim. Tomorrow you could notice which sounds affect them, offer headphones or earplugs, give warning before loud noises and agree on a quiet corner. Ask them what helps. This systematic review gathered studies from 2015 to 2022 on hearing, the ear and the brain in autistic people. Its limits: the studies used very different methods, they describe differences rather than tested solutions, and every person experiences sound in their own way.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn eller din anhörige störs, överväldigas eller fascineras av vissa ljud, ta det på allvar: det speglar en verklig skillnad i hur hörseln bearbetas, inte ett infall. I morgon kan du lägga märke till vilka ljud som påverkar, erbjuda hörselkåpor eller öronproppar, förvarna inför höga ljud och komma överens om en lugn plats. Fråga vad som hjälper. Denna systematiska översikt samlade studier från 2015 till 2022 om hörsel, öra och hjärna hos autistiska personer. Begränsningar: studierna använde mycket olika metoder, de beskriver skillnader snarare än prövade lösningar, och varje person upplever ljud på sitt eget sätt.

title: Language in autism: domains, profiles and co-occurring conditions.
authors: Schaeffer J, Abd El-Raziq M, Castroviejo E, Durrleman S, Ferré S, Grama I, Hendriks P, Kissine M, Manenti M, Marinis T, Meir N, Novogrodsky R, Perovic A, Panzeri F, Silleresi S, Sukenik N, Vicente A,
abstract: This article reviews the current knowledge state on pragmatic and structural language abilities in autism and their potential relation to extralinguistic abilities and autistic traits. The focus is on questions regarding autism language profiles with varying degrees of (selective) impairment and with respect to potential comorbidity of autism and language impairment: Is language impairment in autism the co-occurrence of two distinct conditions (comorbidity), a consequence of autism itself (no comorbidity), or one possible combination from a series of neurodevelopmental properties (dimensional approach)? As for language profiles in autism, three main groups are identified, namely, (i) verbal autistic individuals without structural language impairment, (ii) verbal autistic individuals with structural language impairment, and (iii) minimally verbal autistic individuals. However, this tripartite distinction hides enormous linguistic heterogeneity. Regarding the nature of language impairment in autism, there is currently no model of how language difficulties may interact with autism characteristics and with various extralinguistic cognitive abilities. Building such a model requires carefully designed explorations that address specific aspects of language and extralinguistic cognition. This should lead to a fundamental increase in our understanding of language impairment in autism, thereby paving the way for a substantial contribution to the question of how to best characterize neurodevelopmental disorders.

sheet.es: Mañana puede observar con calma cómo se comunica su hijo o hija: qué entiende, cómo forma frases, cómo usa el lenguaje en la conversación y si prefiere otras formas, como gestos, imágenes o dispositivos. Cada perfil es distinto, así que conviene apoyar sus fortalezas y pedir una valoración del lenguaje si tiene dudas, sin suponer que todo se explica solo por el autismo. Esta revisión resume investigaciones sobre el lenguaje en personas autistas y describe tres grupos amplios: hablantes sin dificultades estructurales, hablantes con ellas y personas mínimamente verbales. Sus límites: no aporta datos nuevos y reconoce que aún no existe un modelo claro, y que dentro de cada grupo hay muchísima variedad.
sheet.en: Tomorrow, you might calmly notice how your child communicates: what they understand, how they build sentences, how they use language in conversation, and whether they prefer other ways, such as gestures, pictures or devices. Every profile is different, so it helps to build on strengths and ask for a language assessment if you have concerns, rather than assuming everything is explained by autism alone. This review summarises research on language in autistic people and describes three broad groups: speakers without structural language difficulties, speakers with them, and minimally speaking people. Its limits: it offers no new data, admits there is no clear model yet, and notes huge variety within each group.
sheet.sv: I morgon kan du lugnt lägga märke till hur ditt barn kommunicerar: vad hen förstår, hur hen bygger meningar, hur hen använder språket i samtal och om hen föredrar andra sätt, som gester, bilder eller hjälpmedel. Varje profil är olika, så det hjälper att bygga på styrkor och be om en språkbedömning om du är orolig, i stället för att anta att allt förklaras av autismen. Denna översikt sammanfattar forskning om språk hos autistiska personer och beskriver tre breda grupper: talande utan strukturella språksvårigheter, talande med sådana svårigheter och personer med minimalt tal. Begränsningar: den ger inga nya data, saknar ännu en tydlig modell och visar stor variation inom varje grupp.

title: Gut microbiota and Autism Spectrum Disorder: From pathogenesis to potential therapeutic perspectives.
authors: Mehra A, Arora G, Sahni G, Kaur M, Singh H, Singh B, Kaur S
journal: Journal of traditional and complementary medicine
abstract: Autism is a complex neurodevelopmental disorder which disrupts communication, social and interactive skills followed by appearance of repetitive behavior. The underlying etiology remains incomprehensible but genetic and environmental factors play a key role. Accumulated evidence shows that alteration in level of gut microbes and their metabolites are not only linked to gastrointestinal problems but also to autism. So far the mix of microbes that is present in the gut affects human health in numerous ways through extensive bacterial-mammalian cometabolism and has a marked influence over health via gut-brain-microbial interactions. Healthy microbiota may even ease the symptoms of autism, as microbial balance influences brain development through the neuroendocrine, neuroimmune, and autonomic nervous systems. In this article, we focused on reviewing the correlation between gut microbiota and their metabolites on symptoms of autism by utilizing prebiotics, probiotics and herbal remedies to target gut microflora hence autism.

title: Face processing in young adults with autism and ADHD: An event related potentials study.
authors: Aydin Ü, Cañigueral R, Tye C, McLoughlin G
abstract: Background Atypicalities in perception and interpretation of faces and emotional facial expressions have been reported in both autism and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) during childhood and adulthood. Investigation of face processing during young adulthood (18 to 25 years), a transition period to full-fledged adulthood, could provide important information on the adult outcomes of autism and ADHD. Methods In this study, we investigated event-related potentials (ERPs) related to visual face processing in autism, ADHD, and co-occurring autism and ADHD in a large sample of young adults ( N = 566). The groups were based on the Diagnostic Interview for ADHD in Adults 2.0 (DIVA-2) and the Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule-2 (ADOS-2). We analyzed ERPs from two passive viewing tasks previously used in childhood investigations: (1) upright and inverted faces with direct or averted gaze; (2) faces expressing different emotions. Results Across both tasks, we consistently found lower amplitude and longer latency of N170 in participants with autism compared to those without. Longer P1 latencies and smaller P3 amplitudes in response to emotional expressions and longer P3 latencies for upright faces were also characteristic to the autistic group. Those with ADHD had longer N170 latencies, specific to the face-gaze task. Individuals with both autism and ADHD showed additional alterations in gaze modulation and a lack of the face inversion effect indexed by a delayed N170. Conclusion Alterations in N170 for autistic young adults is largely consistent with studies on autistic adults, and some studies in autistic children. These findings suggest that there are identifiable and measurable socio-functional atypicalities in young adults with autism.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona joven autista, este estudio sugiere que su cerebro puede procesar rostros y expresiones de forma algo distinta, a veces más lenta. Puede ayudar dar más tiempo, hablar con claridad y no depender solo de la expresión facial. Fue un estudio con registros de actividad cerebral (ERP) en 566 adultos jóvenes, con autismo, con TDAH, con ambos o sin ninguno, que miraban rostros en pantalla. Muestra diferencias de grupo, no lo que le ocurre a cada persona, y no evalúa cómo ayudar en la vida diaria.
sheet.en: If you support a young autistic person, this study suggests their brain may process faces and expressions a little differently, sometimes more slowly. It may help to allow extra time, speak clearly and not rely only on facial expression. It was a brain-activity (ERP) study of 566 young adults, autistic, with ADHD, with both, or neither, who viewed faces on a screen. It shows group differences, not what happens for each person, and it did not test what helps in daily life.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en ung autistisk person tyder studien på att hjärnan kan bearbeta ansikten och uttryck lite annorlunda, ibland långsammare. Det kan hjälpa att ge extra tid, tala tydligt och inte bara förlita sig på ansiktsuttryck. Det var en studie med mätning av hjärnaktivitet (ERP) på 566 unga vuxna, autistiska, med ADHD, med båda eller ingetdera, som tittade på ansikten på skärm. Den visar gruppskillnader, inte vad som gäller för varje person, och prövade inte vad som hjälper i vardagen.

title: The Potential of Flavonoids and Flavonoid Metabolites in the Treatment of Neurodegenerative Pathology in Disorders of Cognitive Decline.
authors: Melrose J
abstract: Flavonoids are a biodiverse family of dietary compounds that have antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antiviral, and antibacterial cell protective profiles. They have received considerable attention as potential therapeutic agents in biomedicine and have been widely used in traditional complimentary medicine for generations. Such complimentary medical herbal formulations are extremely complex mixtures of many pharmacologically active compounds that provide a therapeutic outcome through a network pharmacological effects of considerable complexity. Methods are emerging to determine the active components used in complimentary medicine and their therapeutic targets and to decipher the complexities of how network pharmacology provides such therapeutic effects. The gut microbiome has important roles to play in the generation of bioactive flavonoid metabolites retaining or exceeding the antioxidative and anti-inflammatory properties of the intact flavonoid and, in some cases, new antitumor and antineurodegenerative bioactivities. Certain food items have been identified with high prebiotic profiles suggesting that neutraceutical supplementation may be beneficially employed to preserve a healthy population of bacterial symbiont species and minimize the establishment of harmful pathogenic organisms. Gut health is an important consideration effecting the overall health and wellbeing of linked organ systems. Bioconversion of dietary flavonoid components in the gut generates therapeutic metabolites that can also be transported by the vagus nerve and systemic circulation to brain cell populations to exert a beneficial effect. This is particularly important in a number of neurological disorders (autism, bipolar disorder, AD, PD) characterized by effects on moods, resulting in depression and anxiety, impaired motor function, and long-term cognitive decline. Native flavonoids have many beneficial properties in the alleviation of inflammation in tissues, however, concerns have been raised that therapeutic levels of flavonoids may not be achieved, thus allowing them to display optimal therapeutic effects. Dietary manipulation and vagal stimulation have both yielded beneficial responses in the treatment of autism spectrum disorders, depression, and anxiety, establishing the vagal nerve as a route of communication in the gut-brain axis with established roles in disease intervention. While a number of native flavonoids are beneficial in the treatment of neurological disorders and are known to penetrate the blood-brain barrier, microbiome-generated flavonoid metabolites (e.g., protocatechuic acid, urolithins, γ-valerolactones), which retain the antioxidant and anti-inflammatory potency of the native flavonoid in addition to bioactive properties that promote mitochondrial health and cerebrovascular microcapillary function, should also be considered as potential biotherapeutic agents. Studies are warranted to experimentally examine the efficacy of flavonoid metabolites directly, as they emerge as novel therapeutic options.

sheet.es: Por ahora, este estudio no aporta nada que cambie la rutina de mañana: no indica qué darle de comer a una persona autista ni sustituye el consejo clínico. Es una revisión de la literatura sobre flavonoides, compuestos presentes en alimentos, y su posible relación con el cerebro a través del intestino. Plantea que podrían ser útiles en trastornos neurológicos, entre ellos el autismo, pero pide más estudios que prueben directamente sus metabolitos. Al ser una revisión, no probó nada por sí misma y mezcla trabajos muy distintos. Cualquier suplemento o cambio importante de dieta conviene consultarlo con un profesional de la salud.
sheet.en: For now, this study offers nothing that should change tomorrow's routine: it does not say what an autistic person should eat, and it does not replace clinical advice. It is a review of the literature on flavonoids, compounds found in food, and how they might affect the brain through the gut. It suggests they could help in several neurological conditions, autism among them, but calls for more studies testing their metabolites directly. As a review, it did not test anything itself and brings together very different work. Any supplement or major diet change is worth discussing with a health professional.
sheet.sv: Just nu ger den här studien inget som bör ändra morgondagens rutiner: den säger inte vad en autistisk person ska äta och ersätter inte råd från vården. Det är en översikt av litteraturen om flavonoider, ämnen i mat, och hur de kan påverka hjärnan via tarmen. Den antyder att de kan vara till nytta vid flera neurologiska tillstånd, däribland autism, men efterlyser fler studier som direkt testar deras metaboliter. Eftersom det är en översikt har den inte testat något själv och sammanfattar mycket olika arbeten. Tillskott eller större kostförändringar bör diskuteras med vårdpersonal.

title: Autism and ADHD: A Literature Review Regarding Their Impacts on Parental Divorce.
authors: Anchesi SD, Corallo F, Di Cara M, Quartarone A, Catalioto R, Cucinotta F, Cardile D
abstract: Introduction The change in family structure as a consequence of divorce can be a traumatic event for a child that can undermine his or her emotional security. For this reason, it becomes a major health concern. Many divorce-related risk factors have been identified, including attention deficits or autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in children. The aim of this review is to evaluate if and how a diagnosis of ASD or attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in children is associated with an increase in divorce within families. Method Searches were performed in two databases evaluating studies focusing on articles pertaining to the topic. A total of 20 articles were found, but only 8 were included in the study according to the criteria. Results The results showed that divorce does not appear to be specifically related to a diagnosed pathology of the child, but rather presents itself as a risk factor in certain situations. In particular, this occurs when the coping strategies required to deal with the diagnosis are dysfunctional. However, it would appear that families in which there are children with ADHD have a greater chance of divorce than families in which there is a child with a diagnosis of ASD. It may be hypothesised that in the latter case, parents receiving a diagnosis early in the child's life have more time to develop adaptive strategies to cope with the condition than parents with children with ADHD who mostly find themselves having to deal with their child's behavioural problems at a school age. Moreover, ASD is a disorder more likely genetic than environment-related, so parents receive more socio-medical support, and they are less likely to blame themselves or be blamed by others.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una criatura autista, el diagnóstico en sí no determina que una pareja se separe. Lo que parece pesar más es cómo se afronta: buscar apoyo médico y social, y desarrollar estrategias de afrontamiento que funcionen para la familia, puede ayudar. Cuidar de la pareja y repartir tareas también cuenta. La evidencia es una revisión de la literatura: de 20 artículos encontrados, se incluyeron 8. Sus límites: son pocos estudios, y las explicaciones sobre por qué ocurre son hipótesis, no hechos probados. No describe a todas las familias.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic child, the diagnosis itself does not decide whether a couple separates. What seems to matter more is how the family copes: seeking medical and social support and building coping strategies that work for your family may help. Looking after the couple relationship and sharing tasks also counts. The evidence is a literature review: of 20 articles found, 8 were included. Its limits: few studies were included, and the explanations for why this happens are hypotheses, not proven facts. It does not describe every family.
sheet.sv: Om du tar hand om ett autistiskt barn avgör inte diagnosen i sig om ett par separerar. Det som verkar väga tyngre är hur familjen hanterar situationen: att söka medicinskt och socialt stöd och bygga strategier som fungerar för just er kan hjälpa. Att värna om parrelationen och dela på uppgifterna spelar också roll. Underlaget är en litteraturöversikt: av 20 artiklar som hittades ingick 8. Begränsningar: få studier ingick, och förklaringarna till varför det sker är hypoteser, inte bevisade fakta. Den beskriver inte alla familjer.

title: The Autism Spectrum: Behavioral, Psychiatric and Genetic Associations.
authors: Genovese A, Butler MG
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) consists of a group of heterogeneous genetic neurobehavioral disorders associated with developmental impairments in social communication skills and stereotypic, rigid or repetitive behaviors. We review common behavioral, psychiatric and genetic associations related to ASD. Autism affects about 2% of children with 4:1 male-to-female ratio and a heritability estimate between 70 and 90%. The etiology of ASD involves a complex interplay between inheritance and environmental factors influenced by epigenetics. Over 800 genes and dozens of genetic syndromes are associated with ASD. Novel gene-protein interactions with pathway and molecular function analyses have identified at least three functional pathways including chromatin modeling, Wnt, Notch and other signaling pathways and metabolic disturbances involving neuronal growth and dendritic spine profiles. An estimated 50% of individuals with ASD are diagnosed with chromosome deletions or duplications (e.g., 15q11.2, BP1-BP2, 16p11.2 and 15q13.3), identified syndromes (e.g., Williams, Phelan-McDermid and Shprintzen velocardiofacial) or single gene disorders. Behavioral and psychiatric conditions in autism impacted by genetics influence clinical evaluations, counseling, diagnoses, therapeutic interventions and treatment approaches. Pharmacogenetics testing is now possible to help guide the selection of psychotropic medications to treat challenging behaviors or co-occurring psychiatric conditions commonly seen in ASD. In this review of the autism spectrum disorder, behavioral, psychiatric and genetic observations and associations relevant to the evaluation and treatment of individuals with ASD are discussed.

sheet.es: Si te preguntas si la genética importa en el apoyo a una persona autista, esta revisión sugiere que puede ser útil comentar con su equipo clínico la historia familiar y las condiciones que pueden acompañar al autismo, porque influyen en la evaluación y el acompañamiento. Es una revisión de la literatura científica, no un estudio con participantes propios. Señala que más de 800 genes y decenas de síndromes genéticos se asocian con el autismo. Sus límites: resume asociaciones, no demuestra causas en una persona concreta, y no sirve como regla para todas. Las decisiones médicas, incluidas las pruebas y los fármacos, corresponden a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If you wonder whether genetics matters when supporting an autistic person, this review suggests it may be worth talking with their clinical team about family history and conditions that can co-occur with autism, since these shape assessment and support. It is a review of existing scientific literature, not a study with its own participants. It notes that over 800 genes and dozens of genetic syndromes are associated with autism. Its limits: it summarises associations, does not prove causes in any one person, and is not a rule for everyone. Medical decisions, including testing and medicines, belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om du undrar om genetik spelar roll i stödet till en autistisk person tyder denna översikt på att det kan vara värt att prata med vårdteamet om släkthistoria och tillstånd som kan förekomma samtidigt med autism, eftersom de påverkar utredning och stöd. Det är en översikt av befintlig forskning, inte en studie med egna deltagare. Den anger att över 800 gener och dussintals genetiska syndrom är kopplade till autism. Begränsningar: den sammanfattar samband, bevisar inte orsaker hos en enskild person och är ingen regel för alla. Medicinska beslut, inklusive tester och läkemedel, hör till en kliniker.

title: Food Selectivity in Children with Autism: Guidelines for Assessment and Clinical Interventions.
authors: Esposito M, Mirizzi P, Fadda R, Pirollo C, Ricciardi O, Mazza M, Valenti M
journal: International journal of environmental research and public health
abstract: Autisms Spectrum Disorders (ASD) are characterized by core symptoms (social communication and restricted and repetitive behaviors) and related comorbidities, including sensory anomalies, feeding issues, and challenging behaviors. Children with ASD experience significantly more feeding problems than their peers. In fact, parents and clinicians have to manage daily the burden of various dysfunctional behaviors of children at mealtimes (food refusal, limited variety of food, single food intake, or liquid diet). These dysfunctional behaviors at mealtime depend on different factors that are either medical/sensorial or behavioral. Consequently, a correct assessment is necessary in order to program an effective clinical intervention. The aim of this study is to provide clinicians with a guideline regarding food selectivity concerning possible explanations of the phenomenon, along with a direct/indirect assessment gathering detailed and useful information about target feeding behaviors. Finally, a description of evidence-based sensorial and behavioral strategies useful also for parent-mediated intervention is reported addressing food selectivity in children with ASD.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija autista come pocos alimentos, antes de cambiar nada conviene averiguar por qué: pueden influir factores médicos, sensoriales o de conducta. Anote qué come, cuándo y cómo reacciona en la mesa, y compártalo con el equipo clínico. Es una revisión que ofrece una guía para profesionales sobre evaluación y estrategias sensoriales y conductuales, algunas aplicables con la participación de las familias. Sus límites: no es un estudio con participantes ni prueba qué funciona mejor, y cada persona es distinta, así que cualquier plan debe ajustarse con un profesional.
sheet.en: If your autistic child eats a narrow range of foods, it helps to understand why before changing anything: medical, sensory or behavioural factors can all play a part. Note what they eat, when, and how they react at the table, and share this with their clinical team. This is a review offering guidance for clinicians on assessment and on sensory and behavioural strategies, some usable with parents' involvement. Its limits: it is not a study with participants and does not show which approach works best, and every person is different, so any plan should be adapted with a professional.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn äter ett begränsat urval av mat hjälper det att förstå varför innan du ändrar något: medicinska, sensoriska eller beteendemässiga faktorer kan spela in. Anteckna vad barnet äter, när och hur det reagerar vid bordet, och dela det med vårdteamet. Det här är en översikt med vägledning för kliniker om bedömning samt sensoriska och beteendemässiga strategier, varav några kan användas med föräldrars medverkan. Begränsningar: det är inte en studie med deltagare och visar inte vilket tillvägagångssätt som fungerar bäst. Alla är olika, så en plan bör anpassas tillsammans med en professionell.

title: Neuroinflammation and Oxidative Stress in the Pathogenesis of Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Usui N, Kobayashi H, Shimada S
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder (NDD) characterized by impairments in social communication, repetitive behaviors, restricted interests, and hyperesthesia/hypesthesia caused by genetic and/or environmental factors. In recent years, inflammation and oxidative stress have been implicated in the pathogenesis of ASD. In this review, we discuss the inflammation and oxidative stress in the pathophysiology of ASD, particularly focusing on maternal immune activation (MIA). MIA is a one of the common environmental risk factors for the onset of ASD during pregnancy. It induces an immune reaction in the pregnant mother's body, resulting in further inflammation and oxidative stress in the placenta and fetal brain. These negative factors cause neurodevelopmental impairments in the developing fetal brain and subsequently cause behavioral symptoms in the offspring. In addition, we also discuss the effects of anti-inflammatory drugs and antioxidants in basic studies on animals and clinical studies of ASD. Our review provides the latest findings and new insights into the involvements of inflammation and oxidative stress in the pathogenesis of ASD.

sheet.es: Este estudio no ofrece nada que hacer mañana por la mañana: es una revisión teórica sobre posibles vías biológicas, no una guía de crianza ni de apoyo. Ninguna conducta o decisión de la familia causa el autismo. Revisa lo que se ha publicado sobre inflamación y estrés oxidativo, sobre todo en la activación inmune materna durante el embarazo, con estudios en animales y estudios clínicos. Sus límites: es una revisión, no prueba causas en una persona concreta, y parte de la evidencia viene de animales. Sobre fármacos o antioxidantes, las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: This study offers nothing to act on tomorrow morning: it is a theoretical review of possible biological pathways, not parenting or support advice. Nothing a family does or decides causes autism. The review gathers published work on inflammation and oxidative stress, mainly maternal immune activation during pregnancy, including animal studies and clinical studies. Its limits: it is a review, it cannot show the cause in any one person, and part of the evidence comes from animals. For any medicine or antioxidant, medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Den här studien ger inget att göra i morgon bitti: den är en teoretisk översikt av möjliga biologiska mekanismer, inte råd om föräldraskap eller stöd. Inget en familj gör eller beslutar orsakar autism. Översikten samlar publicerad forskning om inflammation och oxidativ stress, främst maternell immunaktivering under graviditet, med både djurstudier och kliniska studier. Begränsningar: det är en översikt, den kan inte visa orsaken hos en enskild person, och en del av underlaget kommer från djur. När det gäller läkemedel eller antioxidanter hör medicinska beslut till en läkare.

title: What Are You Worried About? Content and Extent of Worry in Autistic Adults.
authors: Black MH, Greenwood DL, Hwa JCC, Pivac J, Tang J, Clarke PJF
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Autistic adults commonly experience anxiety and worry, although knowledge on how worry presents and the content, extent, and experiences among autistic adults is limited. A convergent parallel mixed-methods approach was used to explore the presentation and experiences of worry in autistic and non-autistic adults. Quantitative surveys were used to compare the content and extent of worry in autistic adults to non-autistic adults, with semi-structured interviews also conducted with autistic adults to gain a deeper understanding of the experiences, impacts and content of worry in autistic adults. Findings indicated that autistic adults demonstrated clinically significant levels of worry which were substantially higher than non-autistic adults. Autistic adults described worry as a cycle of negative thoughts impacting their daily life. Findings indicate that autistic adults may worry more than non-autistic adults, impacting on participation in activities of daily living, sleep, and mental health.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta te dice que le preocupa algo, tómalo en serio: pregunta con calma cómo le afecta, por ejemplo al sueño o a las actividades del día, y ofrécele ayuda concreta. Este estudio combinó encuestas, que compararon a adultos autistas y no autistas, con entrevistas a adultos autistas. Los autistas mostraron niveles de preocupación más altos y describieron un ciclo de pensamientos negativos que afecta a su vida diaria. El resumen no indica cuántas personas participaron, y los resultados no valen para todas las personas autistas: cada una vive la preocupación a su manera.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult tells you they are worried, take it seriously: calmly ask how it affects them, for example their sleep or daily activities, and offer concrete help. This study combined surveys, comparing autistic and non-autistic adults, with interviews with autistic adults. Autistic adults showed higher levels of worry and described a cycle of negative thoughts that affects daily life. The abstract does not say how many people took part, and the results do not apply to every autistic person: each person experiences worry in their own way.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen berättar att hen oroar sig, ta det på allvar: fråga lugnt hur det påverkar till exempel sömnen eller vardagens aktiviteter, och erbjud konkret stöd. Studien kombinerade enkäter, som jämförde autistiska och icke-autistiska vuxna, med intervjuer med autistiska vuxna. De autistiska vuxna hade högre nivåer av oro och beskrev en cirkel av negativa tankar som påverkar vardagen. Sammanfattningen anger inte hur många som deltog, och resultaten gäller inte alla autistiska personer: var och en upplever oro på sitt sätt.

title: Camouflage and masking behavior in adult autism.
authors: Alaghband-Rad J, Hajikarim-Hamedani A, Motamed M
abstract: Introduction Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is characterized by persistent deficits in social communication and social interaction across multiple contexts. Social camouflaging was first shown to be a characteristic of autistic persons, who actively try to disguise and compensate for their autism features in social contexts in an effort to socially blend in better. Recently, an increasing, though still insufficient, number of studies has been conducted on the concept of camouflage; however, different aspect of it, from psychopathology and etiology to its complications and consequences, are not clearly defined. We aimed to systematically review the existing literature on camouflage in autistic adults to describe the correlates of camouflage, motivations for exhibiting camouflage behavior, and the potential impacts of camouflage on the mental health of autistic individuals. Methods We followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) checklist guidelines to conduct a systematic review. The databases of PubMed and Scopus, and PsycInfo were searched for eligible studies. Studies were published between January 1st, 1980, to April 1st, 2022. Results We included 16 articles, of which four studies were qualitative and 11 were quantitative. One study used a mix method. The assessment tools used for camouflage, the correlates of camouflage including autism severity, gender, age, cognitive profile and neuroanatomical correlates, reasons for camouflage and the impacts of camouflaging behavior on mental health are discussed in this review. Discussion In synthesizing the literature, we conclude that camouflage seems to be more common among females who report more autistic symptoms themselves. There may also be some differences between men and women in reasons of exhibiting it and its neuroanatomical correlates. Further research is needed as to why this phenomenon is more prevalent in females with implications for gender related cognitive and neuroanatomical differences. Effects of camouflage on mental health and daily life measures of individuals such as employment, university graduation, relationship, financial status, and quality of life should be studied with more details in future studies.

sheet.es: Muchas personas autistas adultas se camuflan: ocultan rasgos autistas para encajar socialmente, y esto puede agotar y afectar a la salud mental. Mañana puedes ofrecer espacios donde no haga falta fingir: permitir pausas, movimientos o silencio sin comentarios, y preguntar qué situaciones le exigen más esfuerzo. Un día tranquilo en apariencia puede esconder mucho cansancio. Es una revisión sistemática de 16 estudios con personas autistas adultas; el camuflaje pareció más frecuente en mujeres. Límites: son pocos estudios, con métodos de medición distintos, y no explican bien por qué ocurre ni sus efectos en el trabajo, las relaciones o la calidad de vida; cada persona lo vive a su manera.
sheet.en: Many autistic adults camouflage: they hide autistic traits to fit in socially, and this can be exhausting and affect mental health. Tomorrow you could offer spaces where no pretending is needed: allow breaks, movement or silence without comment, and ask which situations take the most effort. A day that looks calm on the surface may hide a lot of tiredness. This is a systematic review of 16 studies with autistic adults; camouflaging appeared more common among women. Limits: the studies are few, measured camouflage in different ways, and do not clearly explain why it happens or its effects on work, relationships or quality of life; each person experiences it differently.
