sheet.sv: Många autistiska vuxna kamouflerar: de döljer autistiska drag för att passa in socialt, och det kan vara utmattande och påverka den psykiska hälsan. I morgon kan du erbjuda sammanhang där ingen behöver låtsas: tillåt pauser, rörelse eller tystnad utan kommentarer, och fråga vilka situationer som kräver mest ansträngning. En dag som ser lugn ut kan dölja mycket trötthet. Detta är en systematisk översikt av 16 studier med autistiska vuxna; kamouflering verkade vanligare bland kvinnor. Begränsningar: studierna är få, mätte kamouflering på olika sätt och förklarar inte tydligt varför det sker eller hur det påverkar arbete, relationer eller livskvalitet; varje person upplever det olika.

title: Distinct and shared therapeutic neural mechanisms of mindfulness-based and social support stress reduction groups in adults with autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Pagni BA, Hill E, Walsh MJM, Delaney S, Ogbeama D, Monahan L, Cook JR, Guerithault N, Dixon MV, Ballard L, Braden BB
abstract: Background Mindfulness-based stress reduction (MBSR) alleviates depression and anxiety in adults with autism spectrum disorder (ASD); however, underlying therapeutic neural mechanisms and mindfulness-specific effects have yet to be elucidated. Methods We randomly assigned adults with ASD to MBSR or social support/education (SE). They completed questionnaires that assessed depression, anxiety, mindfulness traits, autistic traits and executive functioning abilities as well as a self-reflection functional MRI task. We used repeated-measures analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) to evaluate behavioural changes. To identify task-specific connectivity changes, we performed a generalized psychophysiological interactions (gPPI) functional connectivity (FC) analysis on regions of interest (ROIs; insula, amygdala, cingulum and prefrontal cortex [PFC]). We used Pearson correlations to explore brain-behaviour relationships. Results Our final sample included 78 adults with ASD - 39 who received MBSR and 39 who received SE. Mindfulness-based stress reduction uniquely improved executive functioning abilities and increased mindfulness traits, whereas both MBSR and SE groups showed reductions in depression, anxiety and autistic traits. Decreases specific to MBSR in insula-thalamus FC were associated with anxiety reduction and increased mindfulness traits, including the trait "nonjudgment;" MBSR-specific decreases in PFC-posterior cingulate connectivity correlated with improved working memory. Both groups showed decreased amygdala-sensorimotor and medial-lateral PFC connectivity, which corresponded with reduced depression. Limitations Larger sample sizes and neuropsychological evaluations are needed to replicate and extend these findings. Conclusion Together, our findings suggest that MBSR and SE are similarly efficacious for depression, anxiety and autistic traits, whereas MBSR produced additional salutary effects related to executive functioning and mindfulness traits. Findings from gPPI identified shared and distinct therapeutic neural mechanisms, implicating the default mode and salience networks. Our results mark an early step toward the development of personalized medicine for psychiatric symptoms in ASD and offer novel neural targets for future neurostimulation research. Clinical trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT04017793.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta quiere apoyo para el estrés, tanto un grupo de mindfulness como un grupo de apoyo social y educación pueden ser opciones razonables; conviene que ella elija según sus gustos y su energía. Es un ensayo aleatorizado con 78 adultos autistas: 39 recibieron mindfulness y 39 apoyo social y educación. En ambos grupos bajaron la depresión y la ansiedad; solo el mindfulness mejoró además las funciones ejecutivas y los rasgos de atención plena. Límites: la muestra es pequeña y los propios autores piden repetir el estudio con más personas; los resultados no valen igual para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult wants support with stress, either a mindfulness group or a social support and education group may be a reasonable option; it helps to let the person choose based on their preferences and energy. This was a randomised trial with 78 autistic adults: 39 received mindfulness and 39 received social support and education. Depression and anxiety went down in both groups; only mindfulness also improved executive functioning and mindfulness traits. Limits: the sample is small and the authors say larger studies are needed to replicate the findings; results will not apply equally to every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen vill ha stöd vid stress kan både en mindfulnessgrupp och en grupp för socialt stöd och utbildning vara rimliga alternativ; låt gärna personen välja utifrån sina önskemål och sin energi. Studien var en randomiserad studie med 78 autistiska vuxna: 39 fick mindfulness och 39 fick socialt stöd och utbildning. Depression och ångest minskade i båda grupperna; bara mindfulness förbättrade dessutom exekutiva funktioner och mindfulnessegenskaper. Begränsningar: urvalet är litet och forskarna anger att större studier behövs för att bekräfta resultaten; de gäller inte lika för alla.

title: How autistic adults' priorities for autism research differ by gender identity: A mixed-methods study.
authors: Putnam OC, Eddy G, Goldblum J, Swisher M, Harrop C
abstract: Background Recent studies suggest that the funding breakdown of autism research in the United States may not align with stakeholder priorities. Furthermore, the majority of stakeholder-engaged research involves parents of autistic individuals rather than autistic adults themselves, who may have differing perspectives on research and funding priorities. Women and non-binary adults have been historically underrepresented in autism research. Objectives The goal of the current study was to examine the autism research priorities of a group of autistic adults, with a particular focus on how these priorities are influenced by one's gender identity. Design A concurrent mixed-methods design was used for this study. Methods Seventy-one autistic adults ( n = 18 men, n = 29 women, n = 24 non-binary adults) completed an online survey regarding the current funding landscape for autism research. Participants ranked the main research topics of the Interagency Autism Coordinating Committee (IACC) and identified top-priority research areas through free-text responses. Response themes were analyzed using content analysis and compared with the existing topic rankings. Results Overall rankings of IACC research areas had a near inverse relationship with the amount of funding per research area. Main themes of stakeholder-generated research topics included "Characterization," "Societal Change," "Well-Being & Trauma," "Diagnosis & Healthcare," and "Accessibility & Services." There was a relatively high overlap between topics identified by the IACC and by the stakeholder-generated topics. Subtle but important differences in topics arose based on gender, with women and non-binary adults identifying topics that were not identified by autistic men. Conclusion Unique priorities generated by those typically excluded from autism research development underscore the importance of co-creating research with underrepresented stakeholders impacted by this work. The current study echoes the growing movement in the field of autism research to center autistic perspectives at every stage of research, including the establishment of funding priorities.

sheet.es: Si participas en decisiones sobre investigación (consultas, encuestas, comités), pregunta a personas autistas adultas de distintos géneros qué les importa, no solo a madres y padres. Este estudio mixto con 71 personas autistas adultas (18 hombres, 29 mujeres, 24 personas no binarias) les pidió ordenar temas de investigación en una encuesta en línea. Sus prioridades casi invertían el orden de la financiación, y mujeres y personas no binarias mencionaron temas que los hombres no. Es un grupo pequeño, de Estados Unidos, y no representa a todas las personas autistas; sirve como pista, no como regla.
sheet.en: If you take part in decisions about research (consultations, surveys, boards), ask autistic adults of different genders what matters to them, not only parents. This mixed-methods study had 71 autistic adults (18 men, 29 women, 24 non-binary adults) rank research topics in an online survey. Their priorities were almost the reverse of how funding is spread, and women and non-binary adults named topics that men did not. The group was small and focused on the United States, and does not represent every autistic person, so treat it as a clue, not a rule.
sheet.sv: Om du deltar i beslut om forskning (samråd, enkäter, styrgrupper), fråga autistiska vuxna av olika kön vad som är viktigt för dem, inte bara föräldrar. I den här studien med blandade metoder rangordnade 71 autistiska vuxna (18 män, 29 kvinnor, 24 icke-binära) forskningsämnen i en webbenkät. Deras prioriteringar var nästan tvärtemot hur finansieringen fördelas, och kvinnor och icke-binära nämnde ämnen som männen inte tog upp. Gruppen var liten och fokuserade på USA och representerar inte alla autistiska personer, så se det som en vink, inte en regel.

title: Police suspect interviews with autistic adults: The impact of truth telling versus deception on testimony.
authors: Bagnall R, Cadman A, Russell A, Brosnan M, Otte M, Maras KL
abstract: Investigative interviews by police are socially and cognitively demanding encounters, likely presenting significant challenges to those on the autism spectrum. Behavioral and communication differences mean that autistic people may also be more likely to be perceived as deceptive in the context of an investigative interview. In the present study, 32 autistic and 33 (age and IQ-matched) non-autistic adults took part in a novel virtual burglary scenario in either an 'innocent' or 'guilty' condition. In a subsequent mock-police interview, innocent suspects were instructed to tell the truth about what they did, while guilty suspects were instructed to lie in order to convince the interviewer of their innocence. In the mock-interviews, innocent autistic mock-suspects reported fewer details that would support their innocence than non-autistic mock-suspects, although both innocent and guilty autistic and non-autistic mock-suspects reported similar levels of investigation-relevant information and had similar levels of statement-evidence consistency. In post-interview questionnaires, innocent and guilty autistic mock-suspects self-reported greater difficulty in understanding interview questions, higher anxiety and perceived the interview as less supportive than non-autistic participants. Implications for investigative interviewing with autistic suspects and cues to deception are discussed.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista a una entrevista policial, conviene pedir antes adaptaciones: preguntas claras y cortas, pausas y un trato de apoyo. Es un estudio experimental con 32 adultos autistas y 33 adultos no autistas en una entrevista policial simulada tras un robo virtual. Las personas autistas, inocentes o no, dijeron haber entendido peor las preguntas, sentir más ansiedad y percibir la entrevista como menos de apoyo. Las inocentes aportaron menos detalles que respaldaran su inocencia. Límites: fue una situación simulada, no una entrevista real, y no describe a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If you are supporting an autistic person before a police interview, it helps to ask in advance for adjustments: short, clear questions, pauses and a supportive manner. This was an experiment with 32 autistic and 33 non-autistic adults in a mock police interview after a virtual burglary. Autistic participants, whether innocent or guilty, reported more difficulty understanding questions, more anxiety and found the interview less supportive. Innocent autistic participants gave fewer details supporting their innocence. Limits: it was a simulation, not a real interview, and it cannot describe every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person inför ett polisförhör kan det hjälpa att i förväg be om anpassningar: korta, tydliga frågor, pauser och ett stödjande bemötande. Det var ett experiment med 32 autistiska och 33 icke-autistiska vuxna i ett låtsasförhör efter ett virtuellt inbrott. De autistiska deltagarna, oavsett om de var oskyldiga eller skyldiga, uppgav att de förstod frågorna sämre, kände mer ångest och upplevde förhöret som mindre stödjande. Oskyldiga autistiska deltagare gav färre detaljer som stödde deras oskuld. Begränsningar: det var en simulering, inte ett verkligt förhör, och gäller inte alla autistiska personer.

title: 'Autistic person' or 'person with autism'? Person-first language preference in Dutch adults with autism and parents.
authors: Buijsman R, Begeer S, Scheeren AM
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract There are different words to describe people with an autism diagnosis. For instance, we can put the person before autism (e.g. 'person with autism'), or we can put autism before the person (e.g. 'autistic person'). Previous research showed that autistic adults in English-speaking countries generally liked it better when autism is placed before the person. Yet, people also greatly differ in the words they like and dislike. In this study, we examined word preference in Dutch autistic adults ( n = 1026; 16-84 years; 57% women) and parents of autistic children ( n = 286). Via an online questionnaire, we asked our participants to select one term for autistic people that they liked best. The results showed that most adults with autism (68.3%) and parents (82.5%) preferred to put the person before autism. Younger adults, with a higher intelligence, and with more autistic traits, were a bit more likely to put autism before the person. We conclude that there are large differences in the words that people prefer. Because we found different results in our Dutch participants compared to participants in English-speaking countries, we think that the Dutch language or culture may also play a role in word preference. For now, we advise autism researchers to use both person-first and autism-first language.

sheet.es: Pregunta a la persona autista cómo prefiere que se hable de ella, y usa sus palabras. No hay un término único que valga para todas. Se trata de un estudio con cuestionario en línea en el que participaron 1026 personas adultas autistas neerlandesas y 286 madres y padres de menores autistas. La mayoría de las personas adultas (68.3%) y de las familias (82.5%) prefirió poner a la persona antes que el autismo, aunque hubo grandes diferencias entre individuos. Los límites: se hizo solo en neerlandés, así que no se puede aplicar sin más a otros idiomas o culturas, y cada preferencia es personal.
sheet.en: Ask the autistic person how they like to be described, and use their words. There is no single term that suits everyone. This was an online questionnaire study with 1026 Dutch autistic adults and 286 parents of autistic children. Most adults (68.3%) and parents (82.5%) preferred putting the person before autism, yet preferences differed widely between individuals. A limit: it was done only in Dutch, so the results may not carry over to other languages or cultures, and each person's preference is their own.
sheet.sv: Fråga den autistiska personen hur hen vill bli beskriven och använd hens ord. Det finns inget enskilt uttryck som passar alla. Detta var en enkätstudie online med 1026 nederländska autistiska vuxna och 286 föräldrar till autistiska barn. De flesta vuxna (68.3%) och föräldrar (82.5%) föredrog att sätta personen före autism, men preferenserna skilde sig mycket mellan individer. En begränsning: studien gjordes bara på nederländska, så resultaten kanske inte gäller andra språk eller kulturer, och varje persons val är personligt.

title: The impact of a positive autism identity and autistic community solidarity on social anxiety and mental health in autistic young people.
authors: Cooper K, Russell AJ, Lei J, Smith LG
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autism is a diagnosis given to individuals by professionals but is also increasingly seen as an identity which an individual can choose for themselves. We wanted to explore how having autism as an identity affects autistic young people. There is evidence that autistic adults have better psychological well-being when they feel more solidarity with other autistic people and feel positively about being autistic. We know that autistic teenagers often feel anxious in social situations. Having a positive autism identity might help alleviate social anxiety associated with being autistic. We wanted to find out if autistic young people who felt more solidarity with other autistic people, and had more positive feelings about autism, had better psychological well-being and less social anxiety. We asked 121 autistic people aged 15-22 years to complete some questionnaires. These questionnaires asked about the young person's autism traits, social anxiety, and psychological well-being. The questionnaires also asked how satisfied they felt to be autistic (satisfaction) and how much solidarity they felt with the autism community (solidarity). We found that autistic young people who had higher autism satisfaction had better psychological well-being and lower social anxiety. Young people who felt more solidarity with other autistic people had higher psychological well-being. There was no association between autism solidarity and social anxiety. We conclude that is important to support autistic young people to develop positive feelings about autism and to feel solidarity with other autistic people.

sheet.es: Puedes ayudar a tu joven a sentirse bien siendo autista: hablad del autismo con naturalidad y respeto, señalad sus fortalezas y facilitad el contacto con otras personas autistas (grupos, foros, actividades compartidas), si lo desea. En este estudio, quienes se sentían más satisfechos de ser autistas tenían mayor bienestar y menos ansiedad social; sentirse parte de la comunidad autista se asoció con más bienestar, aunque no con menos ansiedad social. Se basa en cuestionarios respondidos por 121 personas autistas de 15 a 22 años. Sus límites: muestra una asociación en un solo momento, no demuestra causa y efecto, y cada joven es distinto.
sheet.en: You can help your young person feel good about being autistic: talk about autism openly and respectfully, notice their strengths, and make it easier to connect with other autistic people (groups, online spaces, shared activities) if they want to. In this study, young people more satisfied with being autistic had better well-being and less social anxiety; feeling solidarity with the autistic community was linked to better well-being, though not to lower social anxiety. It was a questionnaire study with 121 autistic people aged 15–22. Its limits: it shows associations at one point in time, not cause and effect, and every young person is different.
sheet.sv: Du kan hjälpa din ungdom att känna sig bra med att vara autistisk: prata om autism öppet och respektfullt, lyft fram styrkor och gör det lättare att träffa andra autistiska personer (grupper, nätforum, gemensamma aktiviteter) om hen vill. I studien hade unga som var mer nöjda med att vara autistiska bättre välmående och mindre social ångest; att känna gemenskap med den autistiska gemenskapen hängde ihop med bättre välmående, men inte med mindre social ångest. Det var en enkätstudie med 121 autistiska personer i åldern 15–22 år. Begränsningar: den visar samband vid ett enda tillfälle, inte orsak och verkan, och varje ung person är olik.

title: The Autism-Spectrum Quotient-Hebrew version: Psychometric properties of a full and a short form, adapted for DSM-5.
authors: Golan O, Terner M, Israel-Yaacov S, Allison C, Baron-Cohen S
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Despite the attempt to diagnose autism at an early age, there are still many individuals who would only get an autism diagnosis in adulthood. For these adults, a questionnaire that could assist in highlighting their need to seek diagnostic assessment is needed. The Autism-Spectrum Quotient is a self-report scale used to assess autistic traits. It was tested cross-culturally, and a short version was recommended to help identify adults who should be referred for an autism assessment. However, its relevance for the up-to-date diagnostic criteria, according to the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (5th ed.), has not been tested. This study aimed to examine the psychometric properties of the Hebrew version of the Autism-Spectrum Quotient and to create a short version of the Hebrew Autism-Spectrum Quotient, based on items which map on to Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (5th ed.) criteria. Ninety-three autistic adults (24 females), aged 18-51, clinically diagnosed according to Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (5th ed.), and 147 comparable controls (34 females) filled out the Hebrew version of the Autism-Spectrum Quotient. Ten clinicians who specialize in diagnosing autism in adults classified the Autism-Spectrum Quotient's items according to Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (5th ed.) criteria. The short version of the Hebrew Autism-Spectrum Quotient comprised items that best differentiated between adults with and without autism, five items representing each of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (5th ed.) diagnostic domains. The overall probability for participants to be correctly classified as autistic or neurotypical was 86% for the Hebrew version of the Autism-Spectrum Quotient and 88% for the short version of the Hebrew Autism-Spectrum Quotient. We conclude that both versions are reliable and sensitive instruments that can help referring adults for autism assessment.

sheet.es: Si una persona adulta se pregunta si podría ser autista, un cuestionario breve de autoinforme puede ayudar a decidir si conviene pedir una evaluación diagnóstica; no sustituye esa evaluación. El estudio contó con 93 adultos autistas con diagnóstico clínico y 147 personas de comparación, que completaron la versión hebrea del Cociente del Espectro Autista. La versión corta, con cinco ítems por cada ámbito diagnóstico del DSM-5, clasificó correctamente en un 88%. Sus límites: se hizo solo con adultos hebreohablantes, con pocas mujeres, y no sirve para diagnosticar ni vale para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an adult wonders whether they might be autistic, a short self-report questionnaire can help them decide whether to seek a diagnostic assessment; it does not replace that assessment. The study involved 93 clinically diagnosed autistic adults and 147 comparison participants, who completed the Hebrew version of the Autism-Spectrum Quotient. The short version, with five items for each DSM-5 diagnostic domain, classified people correctly 88% of the time. Limits: it was done only with Hebrew-speaking adults, with relatively few women, and it cannot diagnose anyone or apply to every person.
sheet.sv: Om en vuxen funderar på om hen kan vara autistisk kan ett kort självskattningsformulär hjälpa hen att avgöra om det är värt att söka en diagnostisk utredning; det ersätter inte utredningen. Studien omfattade 93 kliniskt diagnostiserade autistiska vuxna och 147 jämförelsepersoner som fyllde i den hebreiska versionen av Autism-Spectrum Quotient. Den korta versionen, med fem frågor för varje diagnostiskt område i DSM-5, klassificerade rätt i 88 %. Begränsningar: studien gjordes bara med hebreisktalande vuxna, med relativt få kvinnor, och formuläret kan inte ställa diagnos eller gälla för alla.

title: Alexithymia and intolerance of uncertainty predict somatic symptoms in autistic and non-autistic adults.
authors: Larkin F, Ralston B, Dinsdale SJ, Kimura S, Hayiou-Thomas ME
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic people have more physical health problems than non-autistic people. We were interested in whether autistic people experience more discomfort in their bodies than non-autistic people and whether certain psychological traits contribute to that. A survey was completed online by older adolescents and adults, 51 of whom were autistic, 32 of whom thought they might be autistic but were not diagnosed and 119 who were not autistic. They completed measures of somatic symptoms (daily experience of pain, discomfort, dizziness), alexithymia (difficulty identifying and expressing feelings), interoception (how much people are aware of their bodies) and intolerance of uncertainty (how people handle doubt or uncertainty), and reported any physical or mental health conditions. We found that the autistic participants had more physical and mental health conditions than the non-autistic participants, but even when we took account of this, they experienced higher levels of somatic symptoms. We looked at which psychological factors influenced levels of somatic symptoms across the whole sample, and found that alexithymia, intolerance of uncertainty, having physical health problems, being female and the number of mental health conditions predicted somatic symptoms, while interoception and autism diagnosis did not. The findings suggest that people may be more likely to experience physical discomfort if they are female, and have difficulty identifying and expressing feeling and difficulty tolerating doubt. As these psychological factors are more prominent in autism, we think this is important for physical and mental health providers to know about, so that these psychological factors can be considered when assessing and treating autistic people.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista habla de dolor, mareo o malestar corporal, tómalo en serio y revisa también si le cuesta poner nombre a lo que siente o si la incertidumbre le pesa. Puede ayudar ofrecer opciones, avisar de los cambios y explicar qué va a pasar en una consulta. Es un estudio con encuesta en línea: 51 personas autistas, 32 que creían serlo sin diagnóstico y 119 no autistas. Las personas autistas tenían más síntomas físicos, y la alexitimia y la intolerancia a la incertidumbre los predecían. Solo muestra asociaciones, no causas, y no vale para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person tells you about pain, dizziness or bodily discomfort, take it seriously, and also notice whether naming feelings is hard or uncertainty feels heavy. It may help to offer choices, warn about changes and explain what will happen at an appointment. This was an online survey of 51 autistic people, 32 who thought they might be autistic without a diagnosis, and 119 non-autistic people. Autistic participants reported more somatic symptoms, and alexithymia and intolerance of uncertainty predicted them. It shows associations, not causes, and does not apply to every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person berättar om smärta, yrsel eller obehag i kroppen, ta det på allvar och lägg också märke till om det är svårt att sätta ord på känslor eller om osäkerhet känns tung. Det kan hjälpa att erbjuda val, förvarna om förändringar och förklara vad som ska hända vid ett besök. Studien var en webbenkät med 51 autistiska personer, 32 som trodde sig vara autistiska utan diagnos och 119 icke-autistiska personer. De autistiska deltagarna hade mer somatiska symtom, och alexitymi och svårigheter med osäkerhet förutsade dem. Studien visar samband, inte orsaker, och gäller inte alla.

title: Estimated Therapy Costs and Downstream Cost Consequences of iBASIS-Video Interaction to Promote Positive Parenting Intervention vs Usual Care Among Children Displaying Early Behavioral Signs of Autism in Australia.
authors: Segal L, Green J, Twizeyemariya A, Hudry K, Wan MW, Barbaro J, Iacono T, Varcin KJ, Pillar S, Cooper MN, Billingham W, Upson G, Whitehouse AJO
abstract: Importance The growing global prevalence of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is associated with increasing costs for support services. Ascertaining the effects of a successful preemptive intervention for infants showing early behavioral signs of autism on human services budgets is highly policy relevant. Objective To estimate the net cost impact of the iBASIS-Video Interaction to Promote Positive Parenting (iBASIS-VIPP) intervention on the Australian government. Design, setting, and participants Infants (aged 12 months) showing early behavioral indicators of autism were recruited through community settings into the multicenter Australian iBASIS-VIPP randomized clinical trial (RCT), a 5- to 6-month preemptive parent-mediated intervention, between June 9, 2016, and March 30, 2018, and were followed up for 18 months to age 3 years. This economic evaluation, including cost analysis (intervention and cost consequences) and cost-effectiveness analyses of iBASIS-VIPP compared with usual care (treatment as usual [TAU]), modeled outcomes observed at age 3 through to 12 years (13th birthday) and was conducted from April 1, 2021, to January 30, 2023. Data analysis was conducted from July 1, 2021, to January 29, 2023. Exposures iBASIS-VIPP intervention. Main outcomes and measures To project the diagnostic trajectory and associated disability support costs drawing on the Australian National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS), the main outcome was the differential treatment cost of iBASIS-VIPP plus TAU vs TAU and disability-related government costs modeled to age 12 years, using a clinical diagnosis of ASD and developmental delay (with autism traits) at 3 years. Costs were calculated in Australian dollars and converted to US dollars. Economic performance was measured through the following: (1) differential net present value (NPV) cost (iBASIS-VIPP less TAU), (2) investment return (dollars saved for each dollar invested, taking a third-party payer perspective), (3) break-even age when treatment cost was offset by downstream cost savings, and (4) cost-effectiveness in terms of the differential treatment cost per differential ASD diagnosis at age 3 years. Alternate values of key parameters were modeled in 1-way and probabilistic sensitivity analysis, the latter identifying the likelihood of an NPV cost savings. Results Of the 103 infants enrolled in the iBASIS-VIPP RCT, 70 (68.0%) were boys. Follow-up data at age 3 years were available for 89 children who received TAU (44 [49.4%]) or iBASIS-VIPP (45 [50.6%]) and were included in this analysis. The estimated mean differential treatment cost was A $5131 (US $3607) per child for iBASIS-VIPP less TAU. The best estimate of NPV cost savings was A $10 695 (US $7519) per child (discounted at 3% per annum). For each dollar invested in treatment, a savings of A $3.08 (US $3.08) was estimated; the break-even cost occurred at age 5.3 years (approximately 4 years after intervention delivery). The mean differential treatment cost per lower incident case of ASD was A $37 181 (US $26 138). We estimated that there was an 88.9% chance that iBASIS-VIPP would deliver a cost savings for the NDIS, the dominant third-party payer. Conclusions and relevance The results of this study suggest that iBASIS-VIPP represents a likely good-value societal investment for supporting neurodivergent children. The estimated net cost savings were considered conservative, as they covered only third-party payer costs incurred by the NDIS and outcomes were modeled to just age 12 years. These findings further suggest that preemptive interventions may be a feasible, effective, and efficient new clinical pathway for ASD, reducing disability and the costs of support services. Long-term follow-up of children receiving preemptive intervention is needed to confirm the modeled results.

sheet.es: Si su bebé muestra señales tempranas de autismo, esta investigación no cambia lo que puede hacer mañana, pero indica que los programas breves de apoyo a la interacción entre familia y bebé podrían ser una inversión razonable para los sistemas de apoyo. Es un análisis económico basado en un ensayo aleatorizado en Australia con bebés de 12 meses; se analizaron 89 niños a los 3 años. Sus límites: los costes futuros son estimaciones modeladas hasta los 12 años, se centran en un solo sistema público y no demuestran qué le conviene a cada familia. Cualquier decisión debe tomarse con los profesionales que le acompañan.
sheet.en: If your baby shows early signs of autism, this research does not change what you can do tomorrow, but it suggests that short programmes supporting parent-infant interaction may be a reasonable investment for support systems. It is an economic analysis based on a randomised trial in Australia of infants aged 12 months; 89 children were included at age 3. Its limits: future costs are modelled estimates up to age 12, focus on one public scheme, and cannot show what suits any individual family. Decisions are best made together with the professionals who support you.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn visar tidiga tecken på autism ändrar den här studien inte vad du kan göra i morgon, men den antyder att korta program som stödjer samspelet mellan förälder och barn kan vara en rimlig investering för stödsystemen. Det är en hälsoekonomisk analys baserad på en randomiserad studie i Australien med barn som var 12 månader; 89 barn ingick vid 3 års ålder. Begränsningar: framtida kostnader är modellerade uppskattningar till 12 års ålder, gäller ett enda offentligt system och kan inte visa vad som passar en enskild familj. Beslut tas bäst tillsammans med de yrkespersoner som stödjer er.

title: Turn-timing in conversations between autistic adults: Typical short-gap transitions are preferred, but not achieved instantly.
authors: Wehrle S, Cangemi F, Janz A, Vogeley K, Grice M
abstract: The organisation of who speaks when in conversation is perhaps the most fundamental aspect of human communication. Research on a wide variety of groups of speakers has revealed a seemingly universal preference for between-speaker transitions consisting of very short silent gaps. Previous research on conversational turn-taking in Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) consists of only a handful of studies, most of which are limited in scope and based on the non-spontaneous speech of children and adolescents. No previous studies have investigated dialogues between autistic adults. We analysed the conversational turn-taking behaviour of 28 adult native German speakers in two groups of dyads, in which both interlocutors either did or did not have a diagnosis of ASD. We found no clear difference in turn-timing between the ASD and the control group overall, with both groups showing the same preference for very short silent-gap transitions that has been described for many other groups of speakers in the past. We did, however, find a clear difference between groups specifically in the earliest stages of dialogue, where ASD dyads produced considerably longer silent gaps than controls. We discuss our findings in the context of the previous literature, the implications of diverging behaviour specifically in the early stages of conversation, and the general importance of studying the neglected aspect of interactions between autistic adults.

sheet.es: Si conversas con una persona autista adulta, es normal que al principio haya pausas algo más largas antes de responder; darles tiempo puede ayudar a que la charla fluya. Este estudio analizó conversaciones entre 28 adultos hablantes nativos de alemán, en parejas donde ambas personas eran autistas o ninguna lo era. En general no hubo diferencias claras en el ritmo de los turnos: ambos grupos preferían pausas muy cortas. Las parejas autistas hicieron pausas más largas solo al comienzo del diálogo. Es un estudio pequeño, con hablantes de alemán, y no describe a todas las personas autistas ni a todas las situaciones.
sheet.en: If you talk with an autistic adult, slightly longer pauses before replying at the start of a conversation are normal; giving time can help the exchange flow. This study analysed conversations between 28 adult native German speakers, in pairs where both people were autistic or neither was. Overall there was no clear difference in turn timing: both groups preferred very short pauses. Autistic pairs left longer pauses only in the earliest stage of the dialogue. It is a small study with German speakers, and it does not describe every autistic person or every situation.
sheet.sv: Om du pratar med en autistisk vuxen är det normalt med lite längre pauser före svaret i början av ett samtal; att ge tid kan hjälpa samtalet att flyta. Studien analyserade samtal mellan 28 vuxna med tyska som modersmål, i par där båda var autistiska eller ingen var det. Överlag syntes ingen tydlig skillnad i turtagning: båda grupperna föredrog mycket korta pauser. De autistiska paren hade längre pauser bara i samtalets början. Studien är liten och gäller tyskspråkiga, och beskriver inte alla autistiska personer eller alla situationer.

title: A Systematic Review of the Efficacy of Early Initiation of Speech Therapy and Its Positive Impact on Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Osman HA, Haridi M, Gonzalez NA, Dayo SM, Fatima U, Sheikh A, Puvvada CS, Soomro FH, Khan S
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a condition that consists predominantly of an apparent early delay in communication and social skills. Among the multiple identified etiologies, genetics play a key role. The implementation of early interventional therapy for children with ASD is starting to show promising results. A few medical databases were used to collect multiple published types of research, which were thoroughly screened. Ultimately, a small amount was selected according to the defined eligibility criteria. The 12 articles that were reviewed involved a more significant number of boys than girls, and most clinical trials displayed the importance of starting early therapy. Astonishingly, the overwhelming effects of the COVID-19 pandemic did not affect the continuation of speech therapy in certain areas. In addition, studies emphasize knowledge scarcity, insufficient resources in certain areas, and the demand to educate the community. Conversely, no difference in the level of severity was noted with the implementation of early therapy. Early therapy, chiefly speech therapy used to treat children with ASD, demonstrated favorable outcomes. Communities require awareness about the condition on a broader scale to educate caregivers on early alarming symptoms. All in all, additional exploration needs to be done.

sheet.es: Si le preocupa cómo se comunica su criatura, puede hablar pronto con el equipo de pediatría o con un logopeda para explorar apoyos; no hace falta esperar. Es una revisión sistemática de 12 artículos sobre terapia temprana, sobre todo del habla, en niños autistas; participaron más niños que niñas. La mayoría de los ensayos destacó la importancia de empezar pronto y los resultados fueron favorables. Los límites: son pocos estudios, no se observó diferencia en el nivel de gravedad y los propios autores dicen que hace falta más investigación. No demuestra que valga para cada persona. Además, el apoyo debe respetar su forma de comunicarse y sus preferencias.
sheet.en: If you are wondering about how your child communicates, you can talk early with your paediatric team or a speech therapist about possible supports; there is no need to wait. This is a systematic review of 12 articles on early therapy, mainly speech therapy, for autistic children; more boys than girls took part. Most trials highlighted the importance of starting early, and outcomes were favourable. Limits: few studies were included, no difference in level of severity was noted, and the authors say more research is needed. It does not show the same result for every person. Support should also respect how your child communicates and what they prefer.
sheet.sv: Om du undrar över hur ditt barn kommunicerar kan du tidigt prata med barnhälsovården eller en logoped om möjligt stöd; du behöver inte vänta. Detta är en systematisk översikt av 12 artiklar om tidiga insatser, främst logopedi, för autistiska barn; fler pojkar än flickor deltog. De flesta studier betonade vikten av att börja tidigt, och resultaten var gynnsamma. Begränsningar: få studier ingick, ingen skillnad i svårighetsgrad noterades och författarna menar att mer forskning behövs. Det visar inte samma resultat för alla. Stödet bör också respektera hur barnet kommunicerar och vad barnet föredrar.

title: Phenomenology of gender dysphoria in autism: a multiperspective qualitative analysis.
authors: Cooper K, Mandy W, Butler C, Russell A
journal: Journal of child psychology and psychiatry, and allied disciplines
abstract: Background Autistic people are overrepresented in gender clinic settings, but limited evidence is available to guide clinical decision making for this patient group. We aimed to generate a comprehensive understanding of the phenomenology of gender dysphoria in autistic people. Methods We conducted a multi-perspectival interpretative phenomenological analysis (IPA), from five different perspectives; autistic young people and adults with experience of gender dysphoria, parents of young people, and clinicians working with autistic people with gender dysphoria in both adult and young person settings (n = 68). Results IPA analysis resulted in two themes, 'discovering gender identity' and 'the complexities of moving towards gender comfort'. Participants agreed that there was often an interaction between gender dysphoria and features of autism such as sensory sensitivities. There was relative consensus across groups about the need for autism adaptations to be made in gender clinics. Autistic adults were more likely to see autism as an important identity than young people, but both groups were clear that autism did not impair their understanding of gender. In contrast, some parents and clinicians working with young people expressed concern that autism did impact self-understanding. Discussion While the groups tended to agree on the ways in which particular features of autism can compound gender dysphoria, there were a range of perspectives on the ways in which autism impacted on self-knowledge. Conclusion Recommendations for adaptations when working with autistic people with gender dysphoria are presented.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista habla de su género, escúchala con calma y créela: las personas autistas del estudio dijeron con claridad que el autismo no afectaba su comprensión del género. Conviene pedir adaptaciones en los servicios de género, por ejemplo atender a las sensibilidades sensoriales. La evidencia es un estudio cualitativo con 68 participantes: personas autistas jóvenes y adultas, madres y padres, y profesionales clínicos. Los límites: refleja experiencias y opiniones, no mide qué funciona, y algunos padres y profesionales no coincidían con las personas autistas. No sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person talks about their gender, listen calmly and take them seriously: the autistic participants in this study were clear that autism did not impair their understanding of gender. It helps to ask gender services for adaptations, such as attention to sensory sensitivities. The evidence is a qualitative study with 68 participants: autistic young people and adults, parents, and clinicians. Its limits: it captures experiences and views, does not measure what works, and some parents and clinicians disagreed with autistic people. It is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person berättar om sin könsidentitet, lyssna lugnt och ta den på allvar: de autistiska deltagarna i studien var tydliga med att autism inte försämrade deras förståelse av kön. Det kan hjälpa att be könsvården om anpassningar, till exempel hänsyn till sensorisk känslighet. Underlaget är en kvalitativ studie med 68 deltagare: autistiska unga och vuxna, föräldrar och kliniker. Begränsningar: den beskriver erfarenheter och åsikter, mäter inte vad som fungerar, och vissa föräldrar och kliniker höll inte med de autistiska deltagarna. Den är ingen regel för alla.

title: 'Why are we stuck in hospital?' Understanding delayed hospital discharges for people with learning disabilities and/or autistic people in long-stay hospitals in the UK.
authors: Ince R, Glasby J, Miller R, Glasby AM
journal: Health & social care in the community
abstract: Despite longstanding efforts at de-institutionalisation, around 2000 people with learning disabilities and/or autistic people in England currently live in hospital settings, amidst reports of protracted stays, limited progress towards living more ordinary lives and scandals of abuse and poor care. Yet, there is relatively little research on why people with learning disabilities and/or autistic people are delayed in hospitals, and what exists has significant limitations. In particular, previous studies have rarely talked directly to people with learning disabilities and/or autistic people, their families and frontline staff about their experiences of living or working in such settings, the barriers to discharge and what would help more people to lead chosen lifestyles. This paper presents the findings of a structured literature review conducted between January and March 2021 on delayed discharges of people with learning disabilities in long-stay hospital settings. It investigated: the proportion of people with learning disabilities delayed in long-stay hospital settings, the suggested reasons for these delays and the proposed solutions. The literature reported delays for 11%-80% of inpatients in different settings. The reasons reported are related either to particular characteristics of the person (which we find problematic) or limitations of the system supporting them. However, delays were defined and reported inconsistently, reasons usually lacked depth and detail, and the majority of included studies did not engage directly with the people living in long-stay settings, their families or frontline staff. Without listening to these voices, genuine solutions will be difficult to find.

sheet.es: Si un familiar autista lleva mucho tiempo ingresado, pregunte por escrito al equipo cuál es el plan de alta, qué apoyos faltan en la comunidad y quién es responsable de cada paso. Pida que la persona y la familia participen en esas decisiones. Es una revisión estructurada de la literatura, hecha entre enero y marzo de 2021, sobre retrasos en el alta de personas con discapacidad intelectual en hospitales de larga estancia. Los estudios informaron retrasos en 11%-80% de las personas ingresadas. Sus límites: los retrasos se definían de forma desigual, las razones eran poco detalladas y casi ningún estudio escuchó directamente a las personas, a las familias ni al personal.
sheet.en: If an autistic relative has been in hospital for a long time, ask the team in writing what the discharge plan is, which community supports are missing and who is responsible for each step. Ask that the person and family take part in those decisions. This was a structured literature review, done between January and March 2021, on delayed discharge of people with learning disabilities in long-stay hospitals. The studies reported delays for 11%-80% of inpatients. Its limits: delays were defined inconsistently, reasons lacked detail, and most studies did not speak directly with the people, their families or frontline staff.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk anhörig har varit inlagd länge, be teamet skriftligt om utskrivningsplanen, vilket stöd i kommunen som saknas och vem som ansvarar för varje steg. Be att personen och familjen deltar i besluten. Detta var en strukturerad litteraturöversikt, gjord mellan januari och mars 2021, om försenad utskrivning av personer med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning på långtidssjukhus. Studierna rapporterade förseningar för 11%-80% av patienterna. Begränsningar: förseningar definierades olika, orsakerna var knapphändigt beskrivna och de flesta studier lyssnade inte direkt på personerna, familjerna eller personalen.

title: Fostering Friendship and Dating Skills Among Adults on the Autism Spectrum: A Randomized Controlled Trial of the Polish Version of the PEERS® for Young Adults Curriculum.
authors: Płatos M, Wojaczek K, Laugeson EA
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: PEERS ® for Young Adults is an evidence-based program aimed at teaching social skills needed to establish and maintain close relationships, including friendship and romantic relationships. The study investigated the effects of the Polish adaptation of the curriculum on the social functioning of adults on the autism spectrum. Fifteen young adults (aged 18-32, M = 23.5) were randomly allocated to an immediate or delayed (control) treatment condition. By self and parent report, individuals who participated in the PEERS ® program showed significant improvements in social skills, social cognition, and social knowledge, but limited gains in social engagement. The effects were maintained over six months after the treatment. The intervention was well-accepted and deemed feasible by young adults, their parents, and peers involved in the program.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta joven quiere trabajar la amistad o las citas, un programa grupal estructurado como PEERS puede ser una opción para explorar, siempre que ella lo desee. Se trata de un ensayo aleatorizado con 15 adultos jóvenes autistas de 18-32 años. Según ellos mismos y sus familias, mejoraron las habilidades sociales, la cognición social y el conocimiento social, con menos avance en la participación social, y los efectos se mantuvieron seis meses. Sin embargo, el grupo era muy pequeño y los datos son informes propios y familiares, así que no sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic young adult wants support with friendship or dating, a structured group program like PEERS may be worth exploring, as long as they want it. This was a randomized trial with 15 autistic young adults aged 18-32. By their own and their parents' reports, social skills, social cognition and social knowledge improved, with limited gains in social engagement, and the effects were maintained over six months. However, the group was very small and the results rely on self and parent reports, so it cannot be treated as a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk ung vuxen vill få stöd med vänskap eller dejting kan ett strukturerat gruppprogram som PEERS vara värt att undersöka, så länge personen själv vill det. Det var en randomiserad studie med 15 autistiska unga vuxna i åldern 18-32. Enligt deras egna och föräldrarnas rapporter förbättrades sociala färdigheter, social kognition och social kunskap, med begränsade framsteg i socialt engagemang, och effekterna höll i sig i sex månader. Gruppen var dock mycket liten och resultaten bygger på självrapporter och föräldrarapporter, så studien kan inte ses som en regel för alla.

title: A working taxonomy for describing the sensory differences of autism.
authors: He JL, Williams ZJ, Harris A, Powell H, Schaaf R, Tavassoli T, Puts NAJ
abstract: Background Individuals on the autism spectrum have been long described to process sensory information differently than neurotypical individuals. While much effort has been leveraged towards characterizing and investigating the neurobiology underlying the sensory differences of autism, there has been a notable lack of consistency in the terms being used to describe the nature of those differences. Main body We argue that inconsistent and interchangeable terminology-use when describing the sensory differences of autism has become problematic beyond mere pedantry and inconvenience. We begin by highlighting popular terms that are currently being used to describe the sensory differences of autism (e.g. "sensitivity", "reactivity" and "responsivity") and discuss why poor nomenclature may hamper efforts towards understanding the aetiology of sensory differences in autism. We then provide a solution to poor terminology-use by proposing a hierarchical taxonomy for describing and referring to various sensory features. Conclusion Inconsistent terminology-use when describing the sensory features of autism has stifled discussion and scientific understanding of the sensory differences of autism. The hierarchical taxonomy proposed was developed to help resolve lack of clarity when discussing the sensory differences of autism and to place future research targets at appropriate levels of analysis.

sheet.es: Al hablar de los sentidos con profesionales o en informes, conviene describir con detalle qué ocurre: qué estímulo, qué reacción y en qué situación, en lugar de usar una sola palabra como «sensibilidad». Así es más fácil que os entiendan. Esta es una revisión que argumenta que las palabras usadas para describir las diferencias sensoriales de las personas autistas son inconsistentes, y propone una taxonomía jerárquica para ordenarlas. Es una propuesta de terminología: no probó ninguna estrategia con personas ni dice cómo es la experiencia sensorial de cada una. Cada persona autista vive los sentidos de forma distinta.
sheet.en: When you talk about senses with professionals or in reports, it helps to describe what happens in detail: which stimulus, what reaction, and in which situation, rather than using one word like "sensitivity". This makes it easier to be understood. This is a review arguing that the words used for autistic people's sensory differences are inconsistent, and it proposes a hierarchical taxonomy to organise them. It is a proposal about terminology: it did not test any strategy with people, and it does not say what sensory experience is like for any one person. Every autistic person experiences the senses differently.
sheet.sv: När du pratar om sinnesintryck med yrkesverksamma eller i utredningar hjälper det att beskriva i detalj vad som händer: vilket intryck, vilken reaktion och i vilken situation, i stället för ett enda ord som "känslighet". Då blir det lättare att bli förstådd. Detta är en översikt som menar att orden för autistiska personers sensoriska skillnader används inkonsekvent, och den föreslår en hierarkisk taxonomi för att ordna dem. Det är ett förslag om terminologi: den prövade ingen strategi med människor och säger inte hur sinnesupplevelser är för en enskild person. Varje autistisk person upplever sinnena olika.

title: Examining the relationship between cognitive inflexibility and internalizing and externalizing symptoms in autistic children and adolescents: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Lei J, Charman T, Leigh E, Russell A, Mohamed Z, Hollocks MJ
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Compared to neurotypical peers, autistic adolescents show greater cognitive inflexibility (CI) which manifests at the behavioral and cognitive level and potentially increases vulnerability for the development of internalizing (INT) and externalizing (EXT) symptoms. This systematic review and meta-analysis explored the association between CI and INT/EXT in autistic adolescents. PubMed, EMBASE, MEDLINE, PsycINFO and Web of Science databases were searched to identify relevant studies until April 2022 (PROSPERO protocol: CRD42021277294). Systematic review included 21 studies (n = 1608) of CI and INT, and 15 studies (n = 1115) of CI and EXT. A pooled effect size using Pearson's correlation between CI and INT/EXT was calculated and the moderating effects of age, sex, IQ and study quality were investigated using meta-regressions. Sensitivity analyses were completed to investigate the impact of measure variance for CI and co-occurring ADHD on the overall effects. Greater CI is associated with increased INT (nine studies; n = 833; r = 0.39 (moderate effect), 95% confidence interval [0.32, 0.46]) and EXT (six studies; n = 295; r = 0.48 (large effect), 95% confidence interval [0.38, 0.58]). Results withheld when only using parental reports of CI and excluding autistic adolescents with co-occurring ADHD. Increased CI may be a transdiagnostic vulnerability factor that can increase autistic adolescents' rigid or perseverative patterns of unhelpful cognition and behaviors and reduce their ability to access psychological interventions. Addressing CI may improve autistic children and adolescents' engagement with psychological therapy for co-occurring mental health difficulties.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista tiene dificultad para cambiar de plan o de forma de pensar, conviene tenerlo en cuenta cuando aparecen ansiedad, tristeza o enfado. Ayudan los avisos previos, las rutinas claras y dar tiempo para cambiar. Es un metaanálisis que reunió estudios con autistas de la infancia y la adolescencia: 21 estudios (n = 1608) sobre inflexibilidad cognitiva y síntomas internalizantes, y 15 (n = 1115) sobre externalizantes. Encontró que mayor inflexibilidad se asociaba con más síntomas de ambos tipos. Sin embargo, es una asociación: no prueba que una cosa cause la otra, y no describe a cada persona. Si hay preocupación, consulte con un profesional.
sheet.en: If an autistic person finds it hard to switch plans or ways of thinking, keep that in mind when anxiety, sadness or anger appear. Advance notice, clear routines and extra time to shift may help. This was a meta-analysis that pooled studies of autistic children and adolescents: 21 studies (n = 1608) on cognitive inflexibility and internalizing symptoms, and 15 (n = 1115) on externalizing symptoms. Greater inflexibility was linked with more symptoms of both kinds. However, this is an association: it does not show that one causes the other, and it does not describe every person. If you are worried, talk with a professional.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person har svårt att byta plan eller sätt att tänka kan det vara bra att ha det i åtanke när oro, nedstämdhet eller ilska dyker upp. Förvarning, tydliga rutiner och extra tid att ställa om kan hjälpa. Det var en metaanalys som sammanställde studier om autistiska barn och ungdomar: 21 studier (n = 1608) om kognitiv inflexibilitet och internaliserande symtom och 15 (n = 1115) om externaliserande symtom. Större inflexibilitet hängde ihop med fler symtom av båda slagen. Det är dock ett samband: det visar inte att det ena orsakar det andra och beskriver inte varje person. Om du är orolig, tala med en yrkesperson.

title: Intestinal Barrier Dysfunction and Microbiota-Gut-Brain Axis: Possible Implications in the Pathogenesis and Treatment of Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Dargenio VN, Dargenio C, Castellaneta S, De Giacomo A, Laguardia M, Schettini F, Francavilla R, Cristofori F
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a complex neurodevelopmental disorder with multifactorial etiology, characterized by impairment in two main functional areas: (1) communication and social interactions, and (2) skills, interests and activities. ASD patients often suffer from gastrointestinal symptoms associated with dysbiotic states and a "leaky gut." A key role in the pathogenesis of ASD has been attributed to the gut microbiota, as it influences central nervous system development and neuropsychological and gastrointestinal homeostasis through the microbiota-gut-brain axis. A state of dysbiosis with a reduction in the Bacteroidetes / Firmicutes ratio and Bacteroidetes level and other imbalances is common in ASD. In recent decades, many authors have tried to study and identify the microbial signature of ASD through in vivo and ex vivo studies. In this regard, the advent of metabolomics has also been of great help. Based on these data, several therapeutic strategies, primarily the use of probiotics, are investigated to improve the symptoms of ASD through the modulation of the microbiota. However, although the results are promising, the heterogeneity of the studies precludes concrete evidence. The aim of this review is to explore the role of intestinal barrier dysfunction, the gut-brain axis and microbiota alterations in ASD and the possible role of probiotic supplementation in these patients.

title: Predictors of individual differences in minimally verbal peer communication exchanges following peer-oriented social intervention.
authors: Kedar M, Bauminger-Zviely N
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: School-age children on the autism spectrum who are minimally verbal (MVAS) use a limited repertoire of spontaneous communicative spoken words and reveal large heterogeneity in cognitive functioning. Despite the challenges to form peer social engagement posed by their unique social-communicative profile, few interventions have targeted peer interactions in the MVAS population. This study explored predictors of individual differences in treatment response among 54 school-age minimally verbal autistic children (8-16 years) following an RCT "school-based peer social intervention" (S-PSI) that compared two peer-oriented intervention modalities (conversation versus collaboration) versus a waitlisted control group. We examined autistic-symptom severity, age, verbal and nonverbal IQ, executive functions, and sensory-processing profile for their contribution to children's ability to form relevant spontaneous communication exchanges with a peer partner. Main findings revealed that larger deficits in sensory-processing (sensory-avoidance and sensory low-registration) and in executive functions contributed to greater growth in "relevant" (i.e., adequately attuned, participatory, reciprocal) communication following both interventions, but not for the waitlisted controls. Additionally, older participants with lower verbal and nonverbal IQ improved communication's relevancy more after the conversation intervention, whereas the collaboration intervention was more beneficial for younger participants. Lower autistic-symptom severity contributed to larger growth in relevancy for all groups. By identifying individual-level predictors of spontaneous, attuned, participatory, and reciprocal (i.e., "relevant") communication exchanges with peers, we optimized S-PSI personalization for this uniquely nonverbal, heterogeneous MVAS population. These new channels for tailoring peer interventions to better meet individuals' needs may result in reduced social isolation and loneliness and enhanced well-being.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a un niño autista con pocas palabras habladas, puedes ofrecerle ratos breves con un compañero, ya sea conversando o haciendo algo juntos, y observar qué formato le va mejor. El estudio incluyó a 54 niños autistas de 8-16 años con pocas palabras habladas, en un ensayo aleatorizado escolar con conversación, colaboración y lista de espera. Los niños mayores con menor CI verbal y no verbal mejoraron más con la conversación, y los más jóvenes con la colaboración. Es un solo estudio con un grupo reducido, y los resultados describen tendencias de grupo, no lo que le pasará a cada niño. Su ritmo y sus preferencias cuentan.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic child who uses few spoken words, you can offer short times with a peer, either chatting or doing a task together, and watch which format suits them. The study followed 54 minimally verbal autistic children aged 8-16 in a school-based randomised trial comparing conversation, collaboration and a waitlist group. Older children with lower verbal and nonverbal IQ improved more with conversation, and younger children with collaboration. It is one study with a small group, and the results describe group trends, not what will happen for each child. Their pace and preferences matter.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar ett autistiskt barn som använder få talade ord kan du erbjuda korta stunder med en kamrat, antingen samtal eller en gemensam uppgift, och se vilket upplägg som passar. Studien omfattade 54 autistiska barn i åldern 8-16 med få talade ord, i en randomiserad skolbaserad studie som jämförde samtal, samarbete och en väntelista. Äldre barn med lägre verbal och icke-verbal IQ förbättrades mer med samtal, yngre barn med samarbete. Det är en enda studie med en liten grupp, och resultaten visar gruppmönster, inte vad som händer för varje barn. Barnets tempo och önskemål räknas.

title: Heart rate monitoring to detect acute pain in non-verbal patients: a study protocol for a randomized controlled clinical trial.
authors: Kildal ESM, Quintana DS, Szabo A, Tronstad C, Andreassen O, Nærland T, Hassel B, Hassel B
abstract: Background Autism entails reduced communicative abilities. Approximately 30% of individuals with autism have intellectual disability (ID). Some people with autism and ID are virtually non-communicative and unable to notify their caregivers when they are in pain. In a pilot study, we showed that heart rate (HR) monitoring may identify painful situations in this patient group, as HR increases in acutely painful situations. Objectives This study aims to generate knowledge to reduce the number of painful episodes in non-communicative patients' everyday lives. We will 1) assess the effectiveness of HR as a tool for identifying potentially painful care procedures, 2) test the effect of HR-informed changes in potentially painful care procedures on biomarkers of pain, and 3) assess how six weeks of communication through HR affects the quality of communication between patient and caregiver. Methods We will recruit 38 non-communicative patients with autism and ID residing in care homes. Assessments HR is measured continuously to identify acutely painful situations. HR variability and pain-related cytokines (MCP-1, IL-1RA, IL-8, TGFβ1, and IL-17) are collected as measures of long-term pain. Caregivers will be asked to what degree they observe pain in their patients and how well they believe they understand their patient's expressions of emotion and pain. Pre-intervention: HR is measured 8 h/day over 2 weeks to identify potentially painful situations across four settings: physiotherapy, cast use, lifting, and personal hygiene. Intervention Changes in procedures for identified painful situations are in the form of changes in 1) physiotherapy techniques, 2) preparations for putting on casts, 3) lifting techniques or 4) personal hygiene procedures. Design Nineteen patients will start intervention in week 3 while 19 patients will continue data collection for another 2 weeks before procedure changes are introduced. This is done to distinguish between specific effects of changes in procedures and non-specific effects, such as caregivers increased attention. Discussion This study will advance the field of wearable physiological sensor use in patient care. Trial registration Registered prospectively at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05738278).

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista con discapacidad intelectual que no se comunica con palabras, su dolor puede pasar desapercibido. Un pulsómetro podría ayudar a notar qué momentos del cuidado (fisioterapia, yesos, levantarla o la higiene) duelen, para cambiar cómo se hacen. Esto es un protocolo de ensayo aleatorizado: describe un estudio planificado con 38 personas en residencias, aún sin resultados. No sabemos todavía si funciona, y el pulso también sube por otras razones, como la emoción. Úsalo como idea para observar con atención, no como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person with intellectual disability who does not communicate in words, their pain can go unnoticed. A heart rate monitor might help show which care moments (physiotherapy, casts, lifting or personal hygiene) hurt, so the way they are done can change. This is a randomized trial protocol: it describes a planned study with 38 people in care homes, with no results yet. We do not know yet whether it works, and heart rate also rises for other reasons, such as excitement. Treat it as an idea for careful observation, not a rule for everyone.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning som inte kommunicerar med ord kan smärta lätt missas. En pulsmätare kan kanske visa vilka omsorgsmoment (fysioterapi, gips, lyft eller personlig hygien) som gör ont, så att man kan ändra hur de utförs. Det här är ett protokoll för en randomiserad studie: den beskriver en planerad studie med 38 personer på boenden och har inga resultat än. Vi vet ännu inte om det fungerar, och pulsen stiger även av andra skäl, till exempel spänning. Se det som en idé för noggrann observation, inte en regel för alla.

title: Interactions between the lipidome and genetic and environmental factors in autism.
authors: Yap CX, Henders AK, Alvares GA, Giles C, Huynh K, Nguyen A, Wallace L, McLaren T, Yang Y, Hernandez LM, Gandal MJ, Hansell NK, Cleary D, Grove R, Hafekost C, Harun A, Holdsworth H, Jellett R, Khan F,
abstract: Autism omics research has historically been reductionist and diagnosis centric, with little attention paid to common co-occurring conditions (for example, sleep and feeding disorders) and the complex interplay between molecular profiles and neurodevelopment, genetics, environmental factors and health. Here we explored the plasma lipidome (783 lipid species) in 765 children (485 diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder (ASD)) within the Australian Autism Biobank. We identified lipids associated with ASD diagnosis (n = 8), sleep disturbances (n = 20) and cognitive function (n = 8) and found that long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids may causally contribute to sleep disturbances mediated by the FADS gene cluster. We explored the interplay of environmental factors with neurodevelopment and the lipidome, finding that sleep disturbances and unhealthy diet have a convergent lipidome profile (with potential mediation by the microbiome) that is also independently associated with poorer adaptive function. In contrast, ASD lipidome differences were accounted for by dietary differences and sleep disturbances. We identified a large chr19p13.2 copy number variant genetic deletion spanning the LDLR gene and two high-confidence ASD genes (ELAVL3 and SMARCA4) in one child with an ASD diagnosis and widespread low-density lipoprotein-related lipidome derangements. Lipidomics captures the complexity of neurodevelopment, as well as the biological effects of conditions that commonly affect quality of life among autistic people.

sheet.es: Si vuestra familia se pregunta por el sueño y la alimentación, este estudio sugiere que ambos merecen atención en sí mismos, porque se relacionan con el bienestar y con el funcionamiento adaptativo. Puede ser útil anotar cómo duerme y come la persona autista y comentarlo con su profesional de salud. Es un estudio de investigación con 765 niños, 485 de ellos con diagnóstico de autismo, que analizó lípidos en sangre. Sus límites: muestra asociaciones, no demuestra qué hacer en cada caso, y no sirve como regla para todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If your family is wondering about sleep and eating, this study suggests both deserve attention in their own right, as they are linked to wellbeing and adaptive function. It may help to note how the autistic person sleeps and eats and to talk it over with a health professional. It is a research study of 765 children, 485 of them with an autism diagnosis, which analysed blood lipids. Its limits: it shows associations, does not prove what to do in any single case, and is not a rule for every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om ni funderar på sömn och mat tyder den här studien på att båda förtjänar uppmärksamhet i sig, eftersom de hänger ihop med välbefinnande och adaptiv funktion. Det kan hjälpa att anteckna hur den autistiska personen sover och äter och prata om det med vårdpersonal. Det är en forskningsstudie med 765 barn, varav 485 hade autismdiagnos, där man analyserade blodfetter. Begränsningar: den visar samband, bevisar inte vad som ska göras i enskilda fall och är ingen regel för alla autistiska personer.

title: Co-design of an NHS primary care health check for autistic adults.
authors: Taylor H, Ingham B, Mason D, Finch T, Wilson C, Scarlett C, Moss S, Buckley C, Urbanowicz A, Raymaker D, Seiboth C, Lees R, Garland D, Osbourne M, Lennox N, Cooper SA, Nicolaidis C, Parr JR
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic people are on average more likely to experience poor health than people who are not autistic. Health checks have been shown to improve access to effective healthcare. This study investigated people's views about a primary care health check for autistic adults. We held discussion groups and interviewed autistic adults, adults with intellectual disabilities, supporters and health professionals. People wanted the health check to look at a person's physical and mental health, and how they were doing socially. They thought people should be able to share information about their needs and the reasonable adjustments they would like before the health check. They wanted healthcare services to change the way they communicate with autistic people, such as being able to book appointments online rather than by telephone. They wanted a choice in how the health check was completed, with video call or email offered as well as face-to-face appointments. People thought further training of primary care staff on autism was needed, to increase awareness of the diversity of experiences of autistic people and ways in which difficulties, such as pain, may present differently to non-autistic people. Clinicians raised questions about whether mental health and social care services could meet the additional needs that might be identified through the health check. We used this information to design an NHS primary care health check for autistic people in collaboration with autistic people, supporters and health professionals.

sheet.es: Antes de una revisión de salud en atención primaria, conviene preguntar si se puede compartir por adelantado qué necesita la persona y qué adaptaciones razonables prefiere, y si se puede reservar la cita en línea en vez de por teléfono. También se puede preguntar si la revisión puede hacerse por videollamada o correo electrónico. Es un estudio con grupos de discusión y entrevistas a adultos autistas, adultos con discapacidad intelectual, personas de apoyo y profesionales de la salud, y con ello se diseñó una revisión del NHS. Son opiniones, no se probó si la revisión mejora la salud, y los servicios del Reino Unido pueden diferir de los de otros lugares.
sheet.en: Before a primary care health check, it may help to ask whether you can share in advance what the person needs and which reasonable adjustments they prefer, and whether the appointment can be booked online rather than by phone. You can also ask whether the check can be done by video call or email. This study used discussion groups and interviews with autistic adults, adults with intellectual disabilities, supporters and health professionals, and from this an NHS health check was designed. It reports people's views; it did not test whether the check improves health, and services in the UK may differ from those elsewhere.
sheet.sv: Inför en hälsokontroll i primärvården kan man fråga om det går att i förväg dela vad personen behöver och vilka rimliga anpassningar hen föredrar, och om tiden kan bokas online i stället för per telefon. Man kan också fråga om kontrollen kan ske via videosamtal eller e-post. Studien använde diskussionsgrupper och intervjuer med autistiska vuxna, vuxna med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning, stödpersoner och vårdpersonal, och utifrån dem utformades en hälsokontroll inom NHS. Den visar människors åsikter, inte om kontrollen förbättrar hälsan, och tjänster i Storbritannien kan skilja sig från andra platser.

title: Experiences of Performing Daily Activities in Middle-Aged and Older Autistic Adults: A Qualitative Study.
authors: Hwang YIJ, Foley KR, Elley K, Brown S, Joy-Leong D, Li X, Grove R, Trollor J, Pellicano E, Zheng L
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: This is the first study to investigate instrumental activities of daily living in older autistic adults. We conducted interviews with fifteen adults (mean age = 60.1, SD = 7.4, range = 50-73) from Australia with no intellectual disability. Analysis included both deductive and inductive steps, to categorise responses using the Occupational Performance Model Australia and identify themes across participants' experiences. Strengths and challenges were unique to the individual, as were the methods they had developed to manage tasks. Challenges occurred mostly at the interaction between aspects of the environment (sensory, cognitive, social and cultural) and personal factors such as health conditions and sensory sensitivities. Enhanced person-environment fit is needed, as is a shift in wider sociocultural attitudes to enable comfort and autonomy in later life.

sheet.es: Pregunte a la persona autista mayor qué tareas cotidianas le resultan cómodas y cuáles no, y qué métodos ha desarrollado ella misma. Después, ajuste el entorno (sensorial, social, cognitivo) en lugar de pedirle que cambie. Es un estudio cualitativo con entrevistas a quince adultos autistas de Australia, de 50 a 73 años, sin discapacidad intelectual. Describió fortalezas y dificultades distintas en cada persona, sobre todo en la relación entre el entorno y factores personales como la salud y la sensibilidad sensorial. Es un grupo pequeño y de un solo país, así que no sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: Ask the older autistic person which everyday tasks feel comfortable and which do not, and what methods they have developed themselves. Then adjust the environment (sensory, social, cognitive) rather than expecting them to change. This was a qualitative study with interviews of fifteen autistic adults from Australia, aged 50-73, without intellectual disability. Strengths and challenges differed from person to person, and difficulties arose mostly where the environment met personal factors such as health and sensory sensitivities. The group was small and from one country, so it is not a rule for everyone.
sheet.sv: Fråga den äldre autistiska personen vilka vardagssysslor som fungerar bra och vilka som inte gör det, och vilka egna metoder hen har utvecklat. Anpassa sedan miljön (sensoriskt, socialt, kognitivt) i stället för att förvänta dig att personen ska ändra sig. Det var en kvalitativ studie med intervjuer av femton autistiska vuxna från Australien, 50-73 år, utan intellektuell funktionsnedsättning. Styrkor och svårigheter skilde sig mellan personer, och svårigheterna uppstod mest där miljön möter personliga faktorer som hälsa och sensorisk känslighet. Gruppen var liten och från ett enda land, så resultaten är ingen regel för alla.

title: The Nrf2 Pathway in Depressive Disorders: A Systematic Review of Animal and Human Studies.
authors: Sani G, Margoni S, Brugnami A, Ferrara OM, Bernardi E, Simonetti A, Monti L, Mazza M, Janiri D, Moccia L, Kotzalidis GD, Chieffo DPR, Janiri L
abstract: There is increasing interest in the involvement of antioxidative systems in protecting from depression. Among these, Nrf2 occupies a central place. We aimed to review the role of Nrf2 in depression.
