In breakout rooms, sharing the groups in advance and giving a gentle warning before rejoining the main group can help. Support with technology also matters. The evidence is a qualitative study, run together with an autistic developer, with 16 attendees of an autistic-led online programme, using questionnaires and interviews. Its limits: it is a small group from a single programme, and online delivery did not suit everyone, so it is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du söker digitalt stöd till en nyligen identifierad autistisk vuxen är det bra att erbjuda val: på plats, online eller hybrid. I grupprum hjälper det att dela grupperna i förväg och ge en mild påminnelse innan man går tillbaka till huvudgruppen. Stöd med tekniken är också viktigt. Underlaget är en kvalitativ studie, utförd tillsammans med en autistisk programutvecklare, med 16 deltagare i ett autistledt onlineprogram, med enkäter och intervjuer. Begränsningar: det är en liten grupp från ett enda program, och onlineformatet passade inte alla, så det är ingen regel för alla.

title: The experiences of autistic doctors: a cross-sectional study.
authors: Shaw SCK, Fossi A, Carravallah LA, Rabenstein K, Ross W, Doherty M
abstract: Introduction Medicine may select for autistic characteristics. As awareness and diagnosis of autism are growing, more medical students and doctors may be discovering they are autistic. No studies have explored the experiences of autistic doctors. This study aimed to fill that gap. Methods This is a cross-sectional study. A participatory approach was used to identify the need for the project and to modify a pre-existing survey for use exploring the experiences of autistic doctors. Results We received 225 responses. 64% had a formal diagnosis of autism. The mean age of receiving a formal diagnosis was 36 (range 3-61). Most were currently working as doctors (82%). The most common specialties were general practice / family medicine (31%), psychiatry (18%), and anesthesia (11%). Almost half of those working had completed specialty training (46%) and 40% were current trainees. 29% had not disclosed being autistic to anyone at work. 46% had requested adjustments in the workplace but of these, only half had them implemented.Three quarters had considered suicide (77%), one quarter had attempted suicide (24%) and half had engaged in self-harm (49%). 80% reported having worked with another doctor they suspected was autistic, but only 22% reported having worked with another doctor they knew was autistic. Having never worked with a potentially autistic colleague was associated with having considered suicide.Most preferred to be called "autistic doctors" (64%). Most considered autism to be a difference (83%). Considering autism to be a disorder was associated with preference for the term "doctors with autism," and with having attempted suicide. Conclusion Autistic doctors reported many challenges in the workplace. This may have contributed to a culture of nondisclosure. Mental health was poor with high rates of suicidal ideation, self-harm, and prior suicide attempts. Despite inhospitable environments, most were persevering and working successfully. Viewing autism as a disorder was associated with prior suicide attempts and a preference for person-first language. A neurodiversity-affirmative approach to autism may lead to a more positive self-identity and improved mental health. Furthermore, providing adequate supports and improving awareness of autistic medical professionals may promote inclusion in the medical workforce.

title: Information and communication technologies-based interventions for children with autism spectrum conditions: a systematic review of randomized control trials from a positive technology perspective.
authors: Scarcella I, Marino F, Failla C, Doria G, Chilà P, Minutoli R, Vetrano N, Vagni D, Pignolo L, Di Cara M, Settimo C, Quartarone A, Cerasa A, Pioggia G
abstract: Information and communication technologies (ICTs) have become more widely used in the past years to help people with autism spectrum conditions (ASC). Serious games embedded into computers or tablets, as well as social robots, are the most employed ICT-related tools that are appealing to and appropriate for autistic children. The goal of ICT applications is to enhance behavioral abnormalities associated with ASC while also creating an interactive link between one person and one computer. Comparatively, to human-based therapy, ICT tools aid to inspire autistic children by providing predictability and regularity of tasks. Regaining social skills is the primary behavioral goal for which ICT tools have been designed and implemented. In the past several years, many studies have been created to show how effective it is at improving targeted behaviors. However, only a small number of researchers have used an RCT approach to evaluate its effectiveness. In this systematic review, we only included RCT studies where ICT technologies were used to help children with ASC in improving their social skills. Only 14 RCT studies satisfied the criteria and 12 described significant improvements, showing how the use of technology in educational contexts produced better improvement in developing several social skill facets with respect to the traditional face-to-face approach. Some studies used interventions and outcome measures focused on the core ASC symptoms, but many others addressed neurocognitive functions directly, like social cognition or emotional regulation, while other more general functions such as language or adaptive behaviors. We propose a classification based on processes and outcome measures to foster future research in this specific area of research. The behavioral intervention mediated by technological tools such as computer-based, tablet, and social robotics, undoubtedly provides a comfortable environment that promotes constant learning for people with ASC. Evidence provided in this review highlights the translational potential of this field of study in primary care practice and educational settings.

sheet.es: Si quieres probar juegos en tableta u ordenador, o robots sociales, para practicar habilidades sociales con tu hijo o hija autista, puede ser una opción, siempre que le resulte cómodo y a su ritmo. La tarea predecible suele resultar atractiva. Es una revisión sistemática que reunió 14 ensayos controlados aleatorizados con niñas y niños autistas; 12 describieron mejoras frente al enfoque tradicional cara a cara. Límites: son pocos estudios, muy distintos entre sí, y no sirven como regla para cada persona. Observa qué le gusta y qué no.
sheet.en: If you want to try tablet or computer games, or social robots, to practise social skills with your autistic child, it may be an option, as long as it feels comfortable and goes at their pace. Predictable tasks often appeal. This was a systematic review of 14 randomized controlled trials with autistic children; 12 reported improvements compared with the traditional face-to-face approach. Limits: there were few studies, quite different from one another, and the findings are not a rule for every person. Watch what your child enjoys and what they do not.
sheet.sv: Om du vill prova surfplatte- eller datorspel, eller sociala robotar, för att öva sociala färdigheter med ditt autistiska barn kan det vara ett alternativ, så länge det känns tryggt och går i barnets takt. Förutsägbara uppgifter tilltalar ofta. Det här var en systematisk översikt av 14 randomiserade kontrollerade studier med autistiska barn; 12 rapporterade förbättringar jämfört med traditionellt ansikte mot ansikte-arbete. Begränsningar: studierna var få och ganska olika, och resultaten gäller inte som regel för alla. Lägg märke till vad ditt barn gillar och inte gillar.

title: Abbreviating the Early Start Denver Model for community-based family-centered care.
authors: Vismara LA, Nyugen L, McCormick CEB
abstract: Introduction Parent-mediated approaches for young children with or with a higher likelihood of autism have gained traction, with mounting evidence of efficacy, but a research-to-gap practice exists, and community effectiveness remains to be firmly established. Methods Using a community-participatory framework, a total of 10 parent-child dyads received a five-day workshop and six follow-up sessions of ESDM parent coaching. Intervention was implemented across two phases with in-person and telehealth delivery. Results From pre to post intervention across both phases, parents improved in their fidelity of intervention implementation and children maid gains on proximal measures of social communication. Discussion Community delivery of an evidence-based parent-mediated interventions for toddlers on the autism spectrum is feasible and promising. Giving resource efficiencies associated with parent-mediated approaches, particularly when delivered through government-funded programs, findings bolster current efforts to promote earlier and more widespread community access to necessary interventions. Facilitators and barriers to supporting parent learning and behavior change via interactive strategies are discussed.

sheet.es: Si su hijo pequeño es autista o podría serlo, un programa breve en el que usted aprende a usar estrategias de juego y comunicación en casa puede ser una opción que merece preguntar en los servicios de su comunidad. Es un estudio con 10 díadas de padres e hijos que recibieron un taller de cinco días y seis sesiones de seguimiento, en persona y por telemedicina. Los padres mejoraron en la aplicación de las estrategias y los niños avanzaron en medidas cercanas de comunicación social. Es un grupo muy pequeño, sin grupo de comparación, así que no demuestra que funcione para todas las familias ni para cada niño.
sheet.en: If your young child is autistic or might be, a short program where you learn play and communication strategies to use at home may be worth asking about in your community services. This study followed 10 parent-child dyads who received a five-day workshop and six follow-up sessions, in person and by telehealth. Parents improved at using the strategies, and children made gains on close measures of social communication. The group was very small and had no comparison group, so it does not show this will work for every family or every child.
sheet.sv: Om ditt lilla barn är autistiskt eller kan vara det kan det vara värt att fråga i er kommun eller region om ett kort program där du lär dig lek- och kommunikationsstrategier att använda hemma. Studien omfattade 10 par av förälder och barn som fick en femdagarsworkshop och sex uppföljningstillfällen, på plats och via telehälsa. Föräldrarna blev bättre på att använda strategierna och barnen gjorde framsteg på närliggande mått på social kommunikation. Gruppen var mycket liten och saknade jämförelsegrupp, så resultaten visar inte att det fungerar för alla familjer eller alla barn.

title: Self-Harm Events and Suicide Deaths Among Autistic Individuals in Ontario, Canada.
authors: Lai MC, Saunders NR, Huang A, Artani A, Wilton AS, Zaheer J, Ameis SH, Brown HK, Lunsky Y
abstract: Importance Reasons for elevated suicide risks among autistic people are unclear, with insufficient population-based research on sex-specific patterns to inform tailored prevention and intervention. Objectives To examine sex-stratified rates of self-harm events and suicide death among autistic individuals compared with nonautistic individuals, as well as the associated sociodemographic and clinical risk factors. Design, setting, and participants This population-based matched-cohort study using linked health administrative databases in Ontario, Canada included all individuals with physician-recorded autism diagnoses from April 1, 1988, to March 31, 2018, each matched on age and sex to 4 nonautistic individuals from the general population. Self-harm events resulting in emergency health care from April 1, 2005, to December 31, 2020, were examined for one cohort, and death by suicide and other causes from April 1, 1993, to December 31, 2018, were examined for another cohort. Statistical analyses were conducted between October 2021 and June 2023. Exposure Physician-recorded autism diagnoses from 1988 to 2018 from health administrative databases. Main outcomes and measures Autistic and nonautistic individuals who were sex stratified a priori were compared using Andersen-Gill recurrent event models on self-harm events, and cause-specific competing risk models on death by suicide or other causes. Neighborhood-level income and rurality indices, and individual-level broad diagnostic categories of intellectual disabilities, mood and anxiety disorders, schizophrenia spectrum disorders, substance use disorders, and personality disorders were covariates. Results For self-harm events (cohort, 379 630 individuals; median age at maximum follow-up, 20 years [IQR, 15-28 years]; median age of first autism diagnosis claim for autistic individuals, 9 years [IQR, 4-15 years]; 19 800 autistic females, 56 126 autistic males 79 200 nonautistic females, and 224 504 nonautistic males), among both sexes, autism diagnoses had independent associations with self-harm events (females: relative rate, 1.83; 95% CI, 1.61-2.08; males: relative rate, 1.47; 95% CI, 1.28-1.69) after accounting for income, rurality, intellectual disabilities, and psychiatric diagnoses. For suicide death (cohort, 334 690 individuals; median age at maximum follow-up, 19 years [IQR, 14-27 years]; median age of first autism diagnosis claim for autistic individuals, 10 years [IQR, 5-16 years]; 17 982 autistic females, 48 956 autistic males, 71 928 nonautistic females, 195 824 nonautistic males), there was a significantly higher crude hazard ratio among autistic females (1.98; 95% CI, 1.11-3.56) and a nonsignificantly higher crude hazard ratio among autistic males (1.34; 95% CI, 0.99-1.82); the increased risks were associated with psychiatric diagnoses. Conclusions and relevance This cohort study suggests that autistic individuals experienced increased risks of self-harm events and suicide death. Psychiatric diagnoses were significantly associated with the increased risks among both sexes, especially for suicide death, and in partially sex-unique ways. Autism-tailored and autism-informed clinical and social support to reduce suicide risks should consider multifactorial mechanisms, with a particular focus on the prevention and timely treatment of psychiatric illnesses.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista, vale la pena hablar con calma sobre su bienestar emocional, prestar atención a señales de angustia y buscar pronto apoyo de salud mental, que sea comprensivo con el autismo. El estudio siguió a población de Ontario, Canadá, con cohortes emparejadas por edad y sexo: personas autistas y 4 personas no autistas por cada una. Las personas autistas tuvieron más autolesiones atendidas en urgencias y más muertes por suicidio, y los diagnósticos psiquiátricos se asociaron con ese riesgo. Es un estudio observacional: no demuestra causas ni describe a cada persona. Si te preocupa alguien, contacta con un profesional clínico, un servicio de salud o de crisis; si hay peligro inmediato, llama al número de emergencias de tu país.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic person, it helps to talk calmly about their emotional wellbeing, notice signs of distress, and seek mental health support early, ideally from people who understand autism. The study followed people in Ontario, Canada, using cohorts matched on age and sex: autistic people and 4 nonautistic people for each. Autistic people had more self-harm events needing emergency care and more suicide deaths, and psychiatric diagnoses were linked to this risk. It is an observational study, so it cannot show causes or describe any one person. If you are worried about someone, contact a clinician, a health service or a crisis service; in immediate danger, call your country's emergency number.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person är det bra att prata lugnt om hur hen mår, uppmärksamma tecken på nöd och söka psykisk hälsovård tidigt, helst hos personer med kunskap om autism. Studien följde människor i Ontario, Kanada, i kohorter matchade på ålder och kön: autistiska personer och 4 icke-autistiska personer för varje. Autistiska personer hade fler självskadehändelser som krävde akutvård och fler självmordsdödsfall, och psykiatriska diagnoser hängde samman med risken. Studien är observationell: den visar inte orsaker och beskriver inte varje enskild person. Om du är orolig för någon, kontakta en läkare, vården eller en krisjour; vid akut fara, ring nödnumret i ditt land.

title: School-based social skills group training (SKOLKONTAKT™): a pilot randomized controlled trial.
authors: Fridell A, Coco C, Borg A, Bölte S
abstract: Purpose Differences in socio-communicative behaviors contribute to social challenges for autistic learners at school and, in turn, are associated with increased risks of educational underachievement, social exclusion, and mental health issues. Given that intervention delivery in natural contexts may enhance skills generalization, build support capacities in society, and have practical advantages for youth and families, SKOLKONTAKT™ has been adapted from the clinically based social skills group training KONTAKT™ for mainstream educational settings to mitigate these risks. Methods A pilot, randomized controlled trial with active controls was conducted in a mainstream Swedish high school. Autistic learners and students with social skills challenges ( N = 33; M AGE = 17.5) were randomized to SKOLKONTAKT™ ( n = 17) or active control ( n = 16). Efficacy was measured at post and follow-up (3 months) on social skills [Social Skills Group Assessment Questionnaire (SSGQ); primary outcome] by parent-, self-, and (masked) teacher-report as well as self-reported life quality and social goal attainment. Results Despite COVID-19 challenges, 70.6% ( n = 12) completed SKOLKONTAKT™, and 87.5% ( n = 14) completed control groups. SKOLKONTAKT™ improved on a series of items on SSGQ as well as subjective life quality beyond controls. A larger proportion of social goals were attained, and side-effects were of little impact and proportionally fewer in SKOLKONTAKT™. Conclusion SKOLKONTAKT™ is a safe, feasible, and promising intervention option for autistic learners in mainstream educational settings. A larger-scale study is desirable to confirm the effects identified in this pilot study.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista de instituto tiene dificultades sociales, un grupo de habilidades sociales dentro del propio centro escolar puede ser una opción que merezca preguntar al equipo educativo. Es un ensayo piloto aleatorizado con 33 estudiantes de un instituto sueco, autistas o con dificultades sociales, con una edad media de 17.5 años. SKOLKONTAKT™ mejoró algunos ítems de habilidades sociales y la calidad de vida referida, y se lograron más metas sociales. Pero es un estudio pequeño, en un solo centro, y 12 participantes completaron el grupo. Hacen falta estudios mayores, y no sirve igual para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic teenager finds social situations hard, a social skills group run inside their own school may be worth asking the school team about. This was a pilot randomized controlled trial with 33 students in one Swedish high school, autistic or with social skills challenges, average age 17.5. SKOLKONTAKT™ improved some social skills items and self-reported life quality, and more social goals were reached. However, it was a small study in a single school, and 12 participants completed the group. Larger studies are needed, and it may not suit everyone.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk tonåring tycker sociala situationer är svåra kan en social färdighetsgrupp i den egna skolan vara värd att fråga skolans personal om. Detta var en pilotstudie med slumpmässig fördelning av 33 elever på en svensk gymnasieskola, autistiska eller med sociala svårigheter, med medelåldern 17.5. SKOLKONTAKT™ förbättrade vissa delar av social förmåga och självrapporterad livskvalitet, och fler sociala mål uppnåddes. Studien var dock liten, gjordes på en enda skola, och 12 deltagare slutförde gruppen. Större studier behövs, och upplägget passar inte nödvändigtvis alla.

title: General practitioners' perspectives regarding early developmental surveillance for autism within the australian primary healthcare setting: a qualitative study.
authors: Barbaro J, Winata T, Gilbert M, Nair R, Khan F, Lucien A, Islam R, Masi A, Diaz AM, Dissanayake C, Karlov L, Descallar J, Eastwood J, Hasan I, Jalaludin B, Kohlhoff J, Liaw ST, Lingam R, Ong N, Tam CW
abstract: Background Significant challenges remain in the early identification of child developmental disabilities in the community. Implementing supports and services early in the life course has been shown to promote positive developmental outcomes for children at high likelihood of developmental disabilities, including autism. As part of a cluster randomised controlled trial, this study seeks to examine and compare the perspectives and experiences of Australian general practitioners (GPs) in relation to a digital developmental surveillance program for autism and usual care pathway, in general practice clinics. Methods A qualitative research methodology with semi-structured interviews and thematic inductive analysis underpinned by grounded theory was utilised. All GPs from South Western Sydney (NSW) and Melbourne (Victoria) who participated in the main program ("GP Surveillance for Autism") were invited to the interview. GPs who provided consent were interviewed either over online or in-person meeting. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed, and coded using NVivo12 software. Inductive interpretive approach was adopted and data were analysed thematically. Results Twenty-three GPs across the two sites (NSW: n = 11; Victoria: n = 12) agreed to be interviewed; data saturation had reached following this number of participants. Inductive thematic coding and analysis yielded eight major themes and highlighted common enablers such as the role of GPs in early identification and subsequent supports, enhanced communication between clinicians/professionals, relationship-building with patients, and having standardised screening tools. Specific facilitators to the feasibility and acceptability of a digital screening program for the early identification of developmental disabilities, including the early signs of autism, and encouraging research and education for GPs. However, several practical and socioeconomic barriers were identified, in addition to limited knowledge and uptake of child developmental screening tools as well as COVID-19 lockdown impacts. Common and specific recommendations involve supporting GPs in developmental/paediatrics training, streamlined screening process, and funding and resources in the primary healthcare services. Conclusions The study highlighted the need for practice and policy changes, including further training of GPs alongside sufficient time to complete developmental checks and appropriate financial remuneration through a Medicare billing item. Further research is needed on implementation and scale up of a national surveillance program for early identification of developmental disabilities, including autism.

sheet.es: Si le preocupa el desarrollo de su criatura, pida a su médico de cabecera una revisión del desarrollo y lleve anotado lo que ha observado; así la consulta rinde más. El estudio entrevistó a 23 médicos de cabecera de Sídney y Melbourne, dentro de un ensayo sobre un programa digital de vigilancia del desarrollo. Ellos valoraron las herramientas estandarizadas y la buena comunicación entre profesionales, pero señalaron falta de formación, de tiempo y de financiación. Solo recoge la opinión de médicos, no la de familias ni de personas autistas, y en un contexto australiano, así que puede no valer para su caso.
sheet.en: If you are concerned about your child's development, ask your GP for a developmental check and bring notes on what you have observed; it helps the visit go further. This study interviewed 23 general practitioners in Sydney and Melbourne, as part of a trial of a digital developmental surveillance program. They valued standardised tools and good communication between professionals, but named gaps in training, time and funding. It only reflects doctors' views, not those of families or autistic people, and it was set in Australia, so it may not apply to your situation.
sheet.sv: Om du är orolig för ditt barns utveckling kan du be din allmänläkare om en utvecklingsbedömning och ta med anteckningar om det du har märkt; det gör besöket mer givande. Studien intervjuade 23 allmänläkare i Sydney och Melbourne, som en del av en studie av ett digitalt program för utvecklingsuppföljning. De ansåg att standardiserade verktyg och god kommunikation mellan yrkesgrupper hjälper, men pekade på brist på utbildning, tid och finansiering. Studien speglar bara läkares synpunkter, inte familjers eller autistiska personers, och gjordes i Australien, så den gäller inte nödvändigtvis din situation.

title: Psychosocial interventions for autistic children and adolescents delivered by non-specialists in low- and middle-income countries: a scoping review.
authors: Cherewick M, Daniel C, Shrestha CC, Giri P, Dukpa C, Cruz CM, Rai RP, Matergia M
abstract: Background Most autistic individuals reside in low- and middle-income countries (LMIC) and have limited access to medical providers and specialists. Support for delivery of psychosocial interventions by non-specialists is growing to address this mental health care gap. This scoping review involved a systematic analysis of studies of non-specialist delivered psychosocial interventions for children and adolescents diagnosed with autism and living in low- and middle-income countries. Methods The primary objective of this review was to identify psychosocial interventions for autistic children and adolescents in LMIC delivered by non-specialists (parent, teacher, peer, community, multi-level) and to summarize resulting effects on targeted outcomes. The search strategy was completed in four databases with predetermined inclusion and exclusion criteria. The systematic search generated 3,601 articles. A total of 18 studies met inclusion/exclusion criteria. Data extraction was completed, and results summarized by; (1) participant sample; (2) intervention procedures; (3) implementation by non-specialists; (4) effect on evaluated outcomes; and (5) assessment of risk of bias. Studies examined a range of child and adolescent outcomes including assessment of communication skills, social skills, motor skills, functional and adaptive behaviors, emotional regulation, attention and engagement, sensory challenges, depression, anxiety, and quality of life. Several studies also evaluated intervention effects on family relationships, parent/caregiver stress and parent/caregiver mental health. Results Collectively, the 18 studies included a total of 952 ASC participants ranging in age from 2 to 16 years. Of the included studies, 8 studies were parent/caregiver-mediated, 1 study was peer-mediated, 2 studies were teacher-mediated, and 7 studies included multi-level non-specialist mediated components. Effects on evaluated outcomes are reported. Conclusion Non-specialist delivered interventions for autistic children and adolescents are effective for an array of outcomes and are particularly well suited for low- and middle-income countries. Implications for future research are discussed.

sheet.es: Si no tienes acceso a especialistas, el apoyo guiado a madres, padres, docentes u otras personas cercanas puede ser una vía útil para trabajar la comunicación, las habilidades sociales o el bienestar familiar. Es una revisión sistemática (de alcance) de 18 estudios en países de ingresos bajos y medios, con 952 participantes autistas de 2 a 16 años. Los autores concluyen que estas intervenciones son eficaces para varios resultados. Límites: los estudios son muy distintos entre sí, los resultados varían y no sirven como regla para cada persona. Consulta con profesionales de confianza si puedes.
sheet.en: If specialists are hard to reach, support in which parents, teachers or other people close to the child are guided to deliver strategies may be a useful route for communication, social skills or family wellbeing. This is a scoping systematic review of 18 studies in low- and middle-income countries, with 952 autistic participants aged 2 to 16 years. The authors conclude these approaches are effective for a range of outcomes. Limits: the studies differ a lot, results vary, and findings are not a rule for every person. Check with a professional you trust if you can.
sheet.sv: Om det är svårt att nå specialister kan stöd där föräldrar, lärare eller andra nära personer får handledning i strategier vara en användbar väg för kommunikation, social förmåga eller familjens välmående. Det är en systematisk kartläggning av 18 studier i låg- och medelinkomstländer, med 952 autistiska deltagare i åldrarna 2 till 16 år. Författarna drar slutsatsen att metoderna är effektiva för flera utfall. Begränsningar: studierna skiljer sig mycket, resultaten varierar och gäller inte som regel för alla individer. Rådgör gärna med en professionell du litar på om det går.

title: Effectiveness of rational emotive occupational health coaching in reducing burnout symptoms among teachers of children with autism.
authors: Uzodinma UE, N Onyishi C, Ngwoke AN, Ugwu JI, Okorie CO, A Amujiri B, Ani CK, Ngwu CN, Nwankwo FM, Okoli CN, Eze HO, Orabueze FO, Ogbu EO, Okoro KN, Solomon KC, Okeke IJ, Nwamuo BE, Ani U, Moguluwa SC
abstract: Background/objectives The negative impacts of Job-related burnout on job performance have been widely documented in the literature. Burnout accounts for both physical and mental health outcomes that increase work turnover in teachers, especially those who teach special needs children, like those with Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASD). The current study assessed the effectiveness of Rational Emotive Occupational Health Coaching (REOHC) in minimizing job burnout amongst autistic children teachers in Anambra state, Nigeria. Method The study used a group-randomized waitlist control trial design. teachers who teach ASD children in private and public special and inclusive schools participated in the study. All participants were randomly allocated to REOHC and waitlist group (WLG). REOHC group were exposed to a single session 120 min REOHC programme every week for 12 weeks. Data were collected using Maslach Burnout Inventory for Educators (MBI-ES), at baseline; post-intervention as well as follow-up evaluations 1 and 2 evaluations. All the data gathered for the study were analysed using mean, Standard Deviation (SD), t-test statistics, repeated measures ANOVA, and charts. Results Results indicated a significant decrease in teachers' burnout, following REOHC intervention, which was sustained through follow-ups 1 and 2. Conclusion In conclusion, we stated that REOHC is valuable in treating burnout symptoms in teachers of children with ASDs.

sheet.es: Si enseñas a niños autistas y te sientes agotado o agotada, hablar de ello y buscar apoyo estructurado para el trabajo puede ayudar. Un programa de coaching en salud laboral, con sesiones semanales de grupo, redujo el agotamiento de docentes. Es un ensayo aleatorizado con lista de espera, con docentes de escuelas especiales e inclusivas de Anambra, Nigeria. Las sesiones fueron de 120 minutos cada semana durante 12 semanas, y la mejora se mantuvo en dos seguimientos. Como límites: es un solo estudio en una región, y no mide el bienestar de los niños ni sirve igual para todas las personas. Si el agotamiento te afecta mucho, consulta con un profesional.
sheet.en: If you teach autistic children and feel worn out, talking it through and getting structured, work-focused support may help. A workplace health coaching programme, delivered in weekly group sessions, reduced burnout in teachers. This was a randomised waitlist trial with teachers from special and inclusive schools in Anambra state, Nigeria. Sessions lasted 120 minutes a week for 12 weeks, and the improvement held at two follow-ups. As limits: it is a single study in one region, it does not look at the children's wellbeing, and it will not fit everyone equally. If burnout is weighing on you heavily, speak with a professional.
sheet.sv: Om du undervisar autistiska barn och känner dig utmattad kan det hjälpa att prata om det och få strukturerat, arbetsinriktat stöd. Ett coachingprogram för hälsa i arbetslivet, med veckovisa gruppträffar, minskade lärares utbrändhet. Det var en randomiserad studie med väntelista, med lärare från special- och inkluderande skolor i delstaten Anambra, Nigeria. Träffarna var 120 minuter i veckan under 12 veckor, och förbättringen höll i sig vid två uppföljningar. Begränsningar: det är en enda studie i en region, den undersöker inte barnens välbefinnande och passar inte alla lika bra. Om utbrändheten tynger dig mycket, tala med en yrkesperson.

title: Coping with uncertainty in everyday situations (CUES©) to address intolerance of uncertainty in autistic children: an intervention feasibility trial.
authors: Rodgers J, Goodwin J, Garland D, Grahame V, Isard L, Kernohan A, Labus M, Osborne MM, Parr JR, Rob P, Wright C, Freeston M
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Background Anxiety related to uncertainty is common in autism. Coping with Uncertainty in Everyday Situations (CUES©) is a parent-mediated group intervention aiming to increase autistic children's tolerance to uncertain situations. A pilot study was conducted to test its feasibility and acceptability. Methods Parents of 50 autistic children were randomised to receive CUES© or enhanced services as usual. Results All children met the clinical threshold for at least one anxiety disorder. Of the 26 participants randomised to CUES©, 72% attended 4-8 sessions. Parents and therapists reported they found CUES© useful and acceptable. Conclusions Families were willing to be recruited and randomised, the format/content was feasible to deliver, and the outcome measures were acceptable. CUES© should be evaluated in a clinical and cost effectiveness randomised controlled trial.

sheet.es: Si a su hijo autista le cuesta lo imprevisto, puede ayudar practicar con él, poco a poco, situaciones cotidianas inciertas, con apoyo de otras familias y de profesionales. CUES© es un programa grupal en el que participan las madres y los padres. Fue un ensayo piloto: 50 niños autistas con ansiedad se asignaron al azar a CUES© o a los servicios habituales mejorados. De los 26 asignados a CUES©, el 72% asistió a 4-8 sesiones, y familias y terapeutas lo valoraron útil y aceptable. Solo mostró que es viable; no probó que reduzca la ansiedad, y no sirve igual para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If your autistic child finds uncertainty hard, it may help to practise uncertain everyday situations together, step by step, with support from other families and professionals. CUES© is a group programme in which parents take part. This was a pilot trial: 50 autistic children with anxiety were randomly assigned to CUES© or enhanced services as usual. Of the 26 assigned to CUES©, 72% attended 4-8 sessions, and parents and therapists found it useful and acceptable. It only showed the programme is feasible; it did not show that it reduces anxiety, and it will not suit every child or family.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn har svårt för det oväntade kan det hjälpa att öva på osäkra vardagssituationer tillsammans, steg för steg, med stöd av andra familjer och yrkesverksamma. CUES© är ett gruppprogram där föräldrar deltar. Detta var en pilotstudie: 50 autistiska barn med ångest lottades till CUES© eller förstärkt vanlig hjälp. Av de 26 som fick CUES© deltog 72% i 4-8 tillfällen, och föräldrar och terapeuter tyckte att det var användbart och acceptabelt. Studien visade bara att programmet är genomförbart, inte att det minskar ångest, och det passar inte alla barn eller familjer.

title: The Extent and Nature of Autistic People's Violence Experiences During Adulthood: A Cross-sectional Study of Victimisation.
authors: Gibbs V, Hudson J, Pellicano E
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: This study investigated the extent and nature of violence experiences reported by autistic adults. Autistic (n = 118) and non-autistic (n = 110) adults completed a questionnaire about their experiences of sexual harassment, stalking and harassment, sexual violence and physical violence since the age of 15. Autistic adults reported higher rates of all violence types, multiple forms of violence and repeated instances of the same type of violence. Typical gender differences in the patterns of violence (more physical violence reported by men and more sexual violence reported by women) were apparent in the non-autistic but not the autistic group. Findings add to the limited research in this area and highlight the need to identify risk and protective factors. Policy and practice implications are also discussed.

sheet.es: Conviene tomarse en serio la posibilidad de que una persona autista adulta haya vivido acoso o violencia, y crear espacios tranquilos donde pueda contarlo sin ser juzgada ni cuestionada. Escuchar y creer es un buen comienzo. Se trata de un estudio transversal con cuestionarios: participaron 118 adultos autistas y 110 adultos no autistas. Las personas autistas informaron más violencia de todos los tipos, de varias formas y repetida. Como el estudio solo describe lo que se informó en un momento, no explica las causas ni vale para todas las personas. Aún faltan estudios sobre factores de riesgo y de protección.
sheet.en: It is worth taking seriously that an autistic adult may have experienced harassment or violence, and creating calm spaces where they can talk about it without being judged or doubted. Listening and believing is a good start. This was a cross-sectional questionnaire study: 118 autistic adults and 110 non-autistic adults took part. Autistic adults reported higher rates of every type of violence, multiple forms of violence, and repeated violence. Because it only describes what people reported at one point in time, it cannot explain causes and does not apply to every person. More research is needed on risk and protective factors.
sheet.sv: Det är värt att ta på allvar att en autistisk vuxen kan ha utsatts för trakasserier eller våld, och att skapa lugna sammanhang där hen kan berätta utan att bli dömd eller ifrågasatt. Att lyssna och tro på personen är en bra början. Det var en tvärsnittsstudie med enkäter: 118 autistiska vuxna och 110 icke-autistiska vuxna deltog. De autistiska vuxna rapporterade högre nivåer av alla typer av våld, flera olika former av våld och upprepat våld. Studien beskriver bara vad som rapporterades vid ett tillfälle, kan inte förklara orsaker och gäller inte alla personer. Mer forskning behövs om risk- och skyddsfaktorer.

title: Interventions for Young Children's Mental Health: A Review of Reviews.
authors: Hudson JL, Minihan S, Chen W, Carl T, Fu M, Tully L, Kangas M, Rosewell L, McDermott EA, Wang Y, Stubbs T, Martiniuk A
journal: Clinical child and family psychology review
abstract: To determine the efficacy of intervention programs for young children (4-9 years) with emerging mental health needs, we conducted a review of meta-analytic and systematic reviews of the intervention literature. Of 41,061 abstracts identified and 15,076 screened, 152 review articles met the inclusion criteria. We reviewed interventions across multiple disciplines targeting: (1) general mental health concerns; (2) internalizing symptoms; (3) externalizing symptoms; (4) anxiety; (5) depression; (6) trauma; (7) symptoms of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder; and (8) mental health concerns associated with autism spectrum disorder. Substantial evidence was found for the efficacy of behavioral and cognitive behavioral interventions for general mental health concerns, externalizing symptoms (generally, as well as ADHD, conduct, and other behavioral symptoms) and internalizing symptoms (generally, as well as anxiety) aged 4-9 years. Emerging evidence was identified for interventions targeting trauma symptoms, depression symptoms, and social, emotional and behavioral symptoms in autism spectrum disorder in children aged 4-9 years. Currently there is only limited emerging evidence regarding non-behavioral or non-cognitive behavioral interventions for programs targeting children ages 4-9 years where the aim is to deliver an evidence-based program to improve child social, emotional and/or behavioral functioning. Given the recent rises in mental health needs reported in children, targeted behavioral-and/or cognitive behavior therapy-based interventions should be made widely available to children (and their families) who experience elevated symptoms.

sheet.es: Si le preocupa la salud mental de su hijo o hija de 4 a 9 años, puede preguntar a un profesional por programas conductuales o de terapia cognitivo-conductual, que son los que cuentan con más respaldo. Esta es una revisión de revisiones: analizó 152 artículos de revisión sobre intervenciones, incluidas las dirigidas a necesidades de salud mental en niños autistas. Para ese grupo, la evidencia es todavía incipiente. Las conclusiones son generales: no indican qué funcionará para cada niño, y otros tipos de programas apenas se han estudiado. Cualquier decisión debe tomarse con un profesional, atendiendo a las necesidades de su hijo o hija.
sheet.en: If you are worried about the mental health of a child aged 4-9, you can ask a professional about behavioral or cognitive behavioral programs, which have the most support. This is a review of reviews: it examined 152 review articles on interventions, including those for mental health needs in autistic children. For autistic children, the evidence is still emerging. The findings are general: they do not show what will work for any one child, and other kinds of programs have barely been studied. Any decision should be made with a professional, based on your child's needs.
sheet.sv: Om du oroar dig för psykisk hälsa hos ett barn i åldern 4-9 år kan du fråga en yrkesperson om beteendeinriktade program eller kognitiv beteendeterapi, som har starkast stöd. Detta är en översikt av översikter: den granskade 152 översiktsartiklar om insatser, bland annat för psykiska behov hos autistiska barn. För autistiska barn är evidensen fortfarande på ett tidigt stadium. Resultaten är generella: de visar inte vad som fungerar för ett enskilt barn, och andra typer av program har knappt studerats. Beslut bör fattas tillsammans med en yrkesperson utifrån just ditt barns behov.

title: Omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids and/or vitamin D in autism spectrum disorders: a systematic review.
authors: Jiang Y, Dang W, Nie H, Kong X, Jiang Z, Guo J
abstract: This systematic review aims to offer an updated understanding of the relationship between omega-3 supplementation and/or vitamin D and autism spectrum disorders (ASD). The databases PubMed, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, EMBASE, CINAHL, Vip, CNKI, Wanfang, China Biomedical Database databases were searched using keywords, and relevant literature was hand-searched. Papers ( n = 1,151) were systematically screened and deemed eligible since 2002. Twenty clinical controlled studies were included in the final review. The findings were analyzed for intervention effects focusing on the core symptoms of ASD, included social functioning, behavioral functioning, speech function and biomarkers changes. The review found that the effects of omega-3 supplementation on ASD were too weak to conclude that core symptoms were alleviated. Vitamin D supplementation improved core symptoms, particularly behavioral functioning, however, the results of the literatures included in this study were slightly mixed, we cannot directly conclude that vitamin D supplementation has a beneficial effect on a specific symptom of ASD, but the overall conclusion is that vitamin D supplementation has a positive effect on behavioral functioning in ASD. Omega-3 and vitamin D combination supplementation has a good combined effect on social and behavioral outcomes in patients with ASD.

title: Lockdown Experiences and Views on Future Research Participation of Autistic Adults in the UK During the First 6 Months of the COVID-19 Pandemic.
authors: Realpe AX, Mills N, Beasant L, Douglas S, Kenny L, Rai D
abstract: Background The COVID-19 pandemic resulted in large-scale public health restrictions and lockdowns across many countries. There is an increasing literature on the varied impact of such lockdowns in autistic adults. However, there is very little research on how the pandemic and related public health measures may impact the willingness of autistic people in engaging and taking part in research. The aim of this qualitative study was to explore autistic adults' experiences of the COVID-19 lockdown and how the pandemic may affect future research participation. Methods We conducted in-depth interviews with 31 autistic adults between March and July 2020. Transcripts were analyzed thematically within a critical realism framework. Results Participants identified positive aspects of lockdown such as enjoying the lack of social pressures and using their well-developed skills for dealing with uncertainty. Autistic people also shared challenges of adjusting to lockdown, for example, rapid change in daily routines. While hopeful about the freedom gained from easing restrictions, participants were concerned about the inconsistent communication and application of rules during the transition out of lockdown. This may have exacerbated already rising mental health issues among autistic people. The participants viewed research participation and engagement with increased relevance during the pandemic and welcomed efforts to conduct research using online methods of communication. Conclusion The COVID-19 lockdown had a varied effect in the lives and routines of autistic people. However, health care providers and researchers need to be mindful of rising mental health issues in the aftermath of the pandemic, especially for people who were already vulnerable. The response to the pandemic may have offered opportunities for innovation in research processes enabling more autistic people to engage with research and making studies more inclusive.

sheet.es: Cuando haya cambios grandes en las rutinas, conviene avisar con antelación, dar información clara y coherente, y preguntar a la persona autista qué le ayuda. Para algunas personas, ofrecer opciones en línea para citas o actividades puede facilitar la participación. Este estudio cualitativo entrevistó a 31 adultos autistas en el Reino Unido entre marzo y julio de 2020. Algunos disfrutaron de la menor presión social y otros tuvieron dificultades con el cambio rápido de rutinas; les preocupó la comunicación inconsistente de las normas al salir del confinamiento. Son experiencias de un grupo pequeño en un momento concreto y no valen para todas las personas.
sheet.en: When big changes to routine are coming, give notice early, share clear and consistent information, and ask the autistic person what would help. Offering online options for appointments or activities may make taking part easier for some people. This qualitative study interviewed 31 autistic adults in the UK between March and July 2020. Some enjoyed having less social pressure, while others found the rapid change in routines hard, and they were worried by inconsistent communication of rules as lockdown eased. These are the views of a small group at one point in time, and they will not apply to every autistic person.
sheet.sv: När stora förändringar i rutinerna väntar är det bra att säga till i god tid, ge tydlig och konsekvent information och fråga den autistiska personen vad som skulle hjälpa. Onlinealternativ för möten eller aktiviteter kan göra det lättare för vissa att delta. Den här kvalitativa studien intervjuade 31 autistiska vuxna i Storbritannien mellan mars och juli 2020. Vissa uppskattade den minskade sociala pressen, medan andra tyckte att de snabba rutinförändringarna var svåra, och de oroades av oenhetlig kommunikation om reglerna när restriktionerna lättade. Det är erfarenheter från en liten grupp vid en viss tidpunkt och gäller inte alla autistiska personer.

title: Benefits of Gut Microbiota Reconstitution by Beta 1,3-1,6 Glucans in Subjects with Autism Spectrum Disorder and Other Neurodegenerative Diseases.
authors: Raghavan K, Dedeepiya VD, Yamamoto N, Ikewaki N, Sonoda T, Iwasaki M, Kandaswamy RS, Senthilkumar R, Preethy S, Abraham SJK
abstract: Background Aureobasidium pullulans (black yeast) AFO-202 strain-produced beta glucan, Nichi Glucan, has been shown to improve the behavior and sleep pattern along with an increase in α-synuclein and melatonin in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Objective In this randomized pilot clinical study, we have evaluated the gut microbiota of subjects with ASD after consumption of Nichi Glucan. Methods Eighteen subjects with ASD were randomly allocated: six subjects in the control group (Group 1): conventional treatment comprising remedial behavioral therapies and L-carnosine 500 mg per day, and 12 subjects (Group 2) underwent supplementation with Nichi Glucan 0.5 g twice daily along with the conventional treatment for 90 days. Results Whole genome metagenome (WGM) sequencing of the stool samples at baseline and after intervention showed that among genera of relevance, the abundance of Enterobacteriaceae was decreased almost to zero in Group 2 after intervention, whereas it increased from 0.36% to 0.85% in Group 1. The abundance of Bacteroides increased in Group 1, whereas it decreased in Group 2. The abundance of Prevotella increased while the abundance of Lactobacillus decreased in both Group 1 and Group 2. Among species, a decrease was seen in Escherichia coli, Akkermansia muciniphila CAG:154, Blautia spp., Coprobacillus sp., and Clostridium bolteae CAG:59, with an increase of Faecalibacterium prausnitzii and Prevotella copri, which are both beneficial. Conclusion AFO-202 beta 1,3-1,6 glucan, in addition to balancing the gut microbiome in children with ASD and its role in effective control of curli-producing Enterobacteriaceae that leads to α-synuclein misfolding and accumulation, may have a prophylactic role in Parkinson's and Alzheimer's diseases as well.

sheet.es: Este estudio no ofrece nada para cambiar mañana en casa. Si le preocupan la digestión o los suplementos de su familiar autista, hable con su profesional de salud antes de añadir nada. Es un ensayo piloto aleatorizado con 18 personas autistas: 6 siguieron el tratamiento habitual y 12 tomaron además un suplemento de beta glucano durante 90 días; se analizó su flora intestinal en heces. Hubo cambios en algunas bacterias. Sus límites: muestra muy pequeña, solo se midió la flora intestinal, y las afirmaciones sobre Parkinson y Alzheimer van más allá de lo que se probó. Las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: This study gives nothing to change at home tomorrow. If you wonder about digestion or supplements for your autistic family member, talk with a health professional before adding anything. It was a randomized pilot trial with 18 autistic people: 6 followed usual care and 12 also took a beta glucan supplement for 90 days, and stool samples were analysed for gut bacteria. Some bacteria changed. Its limits: a very small group, only gut bacteria were measured, and the claims about Parkinson's and Alzheimer's go beyond what was tested. Medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Den här studien ger inget att ändra hemma i morgon. Om du funderar på mage eller kosttillskott för din autistiska närstående, prata med en vårdgivare innan du lägger till något. Det var en randomiserad pilotstudie med 18 autistiska personer: 6 fick sedvanlig vård och 12 tog dessutom ett betaglukantillskott i 90 dagar, och avföringsprover analyserades för tarmbakterier. Vissa bakterier förändrades. Begränsningar: mycket liten grupp, bara tarmfloran mättes, och uttalandena om Parkinson och Alzheimer går längre än vad som testades. Medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker.

title: Autistic adults benefit from and enjoy learning via social interaction as much as neurotypical adults do.
authors: De Felice S, Hatilova A, Trojan F, Tsui I, Hamilton AFC
abstract: Background Autistic people show poor processing of social signals (i.e. about the social world). But how do they learn via social interaction? Methods 68 neurotypical adults and 60 autistic adults learned about obscure items (e.g. exotic animals) over Zoom (i) in a live video-call with the teacher, (ii) from a recorded learner-teacher interaction video and (iii) from a recorded teacher-alone video. Data were analysed via analysis of variance and multi-level regression models. Results Live teaching provided the most optimal learning condition, with no difference between groups. Enjoyment was the strongest predictor of learning: both groups enjoyed the live interaction significantly more than other condition and reported similar anxiety levels across conditions. Limitations Some of the autistic participants were self-diagnosed-however, further analysis where these participants were excluded showed the same results. Recruiting participants over online platforms may have introduced bias in our sample. Future work should investigate learning in social contexts via diverse sources (e.g. schools). Conclusions These findings advocate for a distinction between learning about the social versus learning via the social: cognitive models of autism should be revisited to consider social interaction not just as a puzzle to decode but rather a medium through which people, including neuro-diverse groups, learn about the world around them. Trial registration Part of this work has been pre-registered before data collection https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/5PGA3.

sheet.es: Si quieres enseñar algo a una persona autista adulta, prueba a hacerlo en directo, en una conversación de ida y vuelta, en lugar de solo con un vídeo. Pregunta a la persona qué prefiere. En un estudio con 60 adultos autistas y 68 adultos neurotípicos, que aprendieron por Zoom, el aprendizaje en directo fue el mejor y no hubo diferencias entre los grupos. Ambos grupos disfrutaron más la interacción en vivo y mostraron niveles de ansiedad similares. Límites: la muestra se reclutó en línea, algunas personas autistas no tenían diagnóstico formal y los resultados no se aplican a todas las personas ni a otros contextos, como la escuela.
sheet.en: If you are teaching something to an autistic adult, try doing it live, in a two-way conversation, rather than only through a video. Ask the person what they prefer. In a study of 60 autistic adults and 68 neurotypical adults learning over Zoom, live teaching worked best, with no difference between groups. Both groups enjoyed the live interaction more and reported similar anxiety levels. Limits: people were recruited online, some autistic participants were self-diagnosed, and the results do not apply to every person or to other settings, such as schools.
sheet.sv: Om du ska lära en autistisk vuxen något, prova att göra det live, i ett samtal med växelverkan, i stället för bara via en film. Fråga personen vad hen föredrar. I en studie med 60 autistiska vuxna och 68 neurotypiska vuxna som lärde sig via Zoom fungerade live-undervisning bäst, utan skillnad mellan grupperna. Båda grupperna tyckte att den levande interaktionen var roligare och uppgav liknande ångestnivåer. Begränsningar: deltagarna rekryterades online, några autistiska deltagare hade självdiagnos, och resultaten gäller inte alla personer eller andra miljöer, som skolan.

title: The workplace masking experiences of autistic, non-autistic neurodivergent and neurotypical adults in the UK.
authors: Pryke-Hobbes A, Davies J, Heasman B, Livesey A, Walker A, Pellicano E, Remington A
abstract: Masking entails hiding or concealing one's traits during social interactions. Research suggests that masking is particularly common for autistic people, though many non-autistic people also conceal aspects of their identity. Existing research has identified the key motivations and consequences of masking. No research to date, however, has considered how this might be affected by the social context in which masking is employed. This study compared the masking experiences of 285 autistic, 88 non-autistic neurodivergent and 99 neurotypical adults within a context in which masking is expected to be highly prevalent, namely the workplace. We used reflexive thematic analysis to explore the motivations, consequences, and contextual differences of workplace masking compared to other social contexts. Workplace masking was considered by participants in all three groups to be an adaptive response to a range of socially grounded workplace challenges and was usually employed as a strategy to safeguard against the threat of negative social and employment outcomes. Our non-autistic neurodivergent and autistic participants, however, reported experiencing unique pressures to mask, given the limited understanding of neurodiversity in workplaces and society more broadly. These findings have important implications for the wider masking literature and for workplace practice.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista a la que apoyas parece agotada después del trabajo, el enmascaramiento puede ser parte de la razón. Podéis hablar con calma sobre en qué momentos siente que debe ocultar sus rasgos, qué le cuesta más y qué ajustes o espacios seguros podrían ayudar, sin presionarla a revelar su diagnóstico. Este estudio cualitativo recogió experiencias de 285 adultos autistas, 88 neurodivergentes no autistas y 99 neurotípicos en Reino Unido; todos enmascaraban en el trabajo para protegerse, pero las personas neurodivergentes sentían presiones extra por la falta de comprensión. Límites: se basa en relatos de personas de un solo país y no mide efectos ni prueba soluciones.
sheet.en: If an autistic person you support seems drained after work, masking may be part of the reason. You could talk calmly about when they feel they must hide their traits, what costs them most, and which adjustments or safe spaces might help, without pushing them to disclose. This qualitative study gathered experiences from 285 autistic, 88 non-autistic neurodivergent and 99 neurotypical adults in the UK; all groups masked at work to protect themselves, but neurodivergent people described extra pressure because workplaces understand neurodiversity poorly. Limits: it relies on self-reports from one country and does not measure outcomes or test solutions.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person du stöttar verkar slutkörd efter jobbet kan maskering vara en del av förklaringen. Ni kan lugnt prata om när hen känner att hen måste dölja sina drag, vad som kostar mest och vilka anpassningar eller trygga platser som kan hjälpa, utan att pressa hen att berätta om sin diagnos. Denna kvalitativa studie samlade erfarenheter från 285 autistiska, 88 icke-autistiska neurodivergenta och 99 neurotypiska vuxna i Storbritannien; alla maskerade på jobbet för att skydda sig, men neurodivergenta beskrev extra press på grund av bristande förståelse för neurodiversitet. Begränsningar: studien bygger på egna berättelser från ett land och mäter inte effekter eller testar lösningar.

title: Neurological and psychiatric disorders among autistic adults: a population healthcare record study.
authors: Underwood JFG, DelPozo-Banos M, Frizzati A, Rai D, John A, Hall J
abstract: Background Co-occurring psychiatric disorders are common in autism, with previous studies suggesting 54-94% of autistic individuals develop a mental health condition in their lifetime. Most studies have looked at clinically-recruited cohorts, or paediatric cohorts followed into adulthood, with less known about the autistic community at a population level. We therefore studied the prevalence of co-occurring psychiatric and neurological conditions in autistic individuals in a national sample. Methods This retrospective case-control study utilised the SAIL Databank to examine anonymised whole population electronic health record data from 2001 to 2016 in Wales, UK ( N = 3.6 million). We investigated the prevalence of co-occurring psychiatric and selected neurological diagnoses in autistic adults' records during the study period using International Classification of Diseases-10 and Read v2 clinical codes compared to general population controls matched for age, sex and deprivation. Results All psychiatric conditions examined were more common amongst adults with autism after adjusting for age, sex and deprivation. Prevalence of attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (7.00%), bipolar disorder (2.50%), obsessive-compulsive disorder (3.02%), psychosis (18.30%) and schizophrenia (5.20%) were markedly elevated in those with autism, with corresponding odds ratios 8.24-10.74 times the general population. Depression (25.90%) and anxiety (22.40%) were also more prevalent, with epilepsy 9.21 times more common in autism. Conclusions We found that a range of psychiatric conditions were more frequently recorded in autistic individuals. We add to understanding of under-reporting and diagnostic overshadowing in autism. With increasing awareness of autism, services should be cognisant of the psychiatric conditions that frequently co-occur in this population.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista adulta, conviene estar atento a señales de ansiedad, depresión, TDAH o epilepsia, y no atribuir automáticamente todo cambio al autismo. Si notas cambios en el sueño, el ánimo, la energía o episodios extraños, coméntalo con su médico y pide que se valoren por separado. Llevar un registro breve puede ayudar. Este estudio revisó historias clínicas anónimas de toda la población de Gales (3,6 millones de personas, 2001-2016), comparando adultos autistas con personas similares en edad, sexo y nivel socioeconómico. Sus límites: solo refleja diagnósticos registrados, que pueden ser erróneos o incompletos, y no describe a cada persona autista.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult, it helps to stay alert to signs of anxiety, depression, ADHD or epilepsy, rather than assuming every change is simply part of being autistic. If you notice shifts in sleep, mood, energy or unusual episodes, mention them to their doctor and ask for them to be looked at on their own terms. A short written log can help. This study reviewed anonymised health records for the whole population of Wales (3.6 million people, 2001–2016), comparing autistic adults with people matched for age, sex and deprivation. Its limits: it only captures recorded diagnoses, which may be wrong or incomplete, and it does not describe every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen är det bra att vara uppmärksam på tecken på ångest, depression, ADHD eller epilepsi, i stället för att anta att varje förändring bara hör till autismen. Märker du förändringar i sömn, stämning, energi eller ovanliga episoder, ta upp det med läkaren och be att de bedöms för sig. En kort anteckningsbok kan hjälpa. Studien granskade anonymiserade journaler för hela Wales befolkning (3,6 miljoner personer, 2001–2016) och jämförde autistiska vuxna med personer av samma ålder, kön och socioekonomiska situation. Begränsningar: den visar bara registrerade diagnoser, som kan vara felaktiga eller ofullständiga, och beskriver inte varje autistisk person.

title: Effects of a Nonwearable Digital Therapeutic Intervention on Preschoolers With Autism Spectrum Disorder in China: Open-Label Randomized Controlled Trial.
authors: Chu L, Shen L, Ma C, Chen J, Tian Y, Zhang C, Gong Z, Li M, Wang C, Pan L, Zhu P, Wu D, Wang Y, Yu G
abstract: Background Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder that can cause difficulty with communication and social interactions as well as complicated family dynamics. Digital health interventions can reduce treatment costs and promote healthy lifestyle changes. These therapies can be adjunctive or replace traditional treatments. However, issues with cooperation and compliance prevent preschool patients with ASD from applying these tools. In this open-label, randomized controlled trial, we developed a nonwearable digital therapy called virtual reality-incorporated cognitive behavioral therapy (VR-CBT). Objective The aim of this study was to assess the adjunctive function of VR-CBT by comparing the effects of VR-CBT plus learning style profile (LSP) intervention with those of LSP-only intervention in preschool children with ASD. Methods This trial was performed in China on 78 preschool children (age 3-6 years, IQ>70) diagnosed with ASD who were randomized to receive a 20-week VR-CBT plus LSP intervention (intervention group, 39/78, 50%) or LSP intervention only (control group, 39/78, 50%). The primary outcome was the change of scores from baseline to week 20, assessed by using the parent-rated Autism Behavior Checklist (ABC). Secondary outcomes included the Childhood Autism Rating Scale (CARS), Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Rating Scale-IV (ADHD-RS-IV), and behavioral performance data (accuracy and reaction time) in go/no-go tasks. All primary and secondary outcomes were analyzed in the intention-to-treat population. Results After the intervention, there was an intervention effect on total ABC (β=-5.528; P Conclusions We found potentially positive effects of nonwearable digital therapy plus LSP on core symptoms associated with ASD, leading to a modest improvement in the function of sensory, motor, and response inhibition, while reducing impulsivity and hyperactivity in preschoolers with both ASD and ADHD. VR-CBT was found to be an effective and feasible adjunctive digital tool. Trial registration Chinese Clinical Trial Registry ChiCTR2100053165; http://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.aspx?proj=137016.

sheet.es: Si su criatura autista de 3 a 6 años tiene dificultades para tolerar herramientas digitales con dispositivos puestos, una opción sin dispositivos portátiles podría explorarse con su equipo profesional, como complemento y no como sustituto de los apoyos actuales. Evidencia: ensayo aleatorizado abierto en China con 78 niños y niñas en edad preescolar (3-6 años, IQ>70); 39 recibieron terapia cognitivo-conductual con realidad virtual más un perfil de estilo de aprendizaje durante 20 semanas, y 39 solo el perfil. Los autores describen mejoras posibles, modestas. Límites: el estudio era abierto, solo incluyó a niños con IQ>70 y los resultados no sirven para todas las personas autistas ni garantizan el mismo efecto en su hija o hijo.
sheet.en: If your autistic child aged 3 to 6 finds wearable digital tools hard to tolerate, a non-wearable option may be worth exploring with your professional team, as an addition to current supports rather than a replacement. Evidence: an open-label randomized trial in China with 78 preschool children (age 3-6 years, IQ>70); 39 received virtual reality cognitive behavioral therapy plus a learning style profile for 20 weeks, and 39 received the profile only. The authors describe possible, modest improvements. Limits: the trial was open-label, included only children with IQ>70, and its results do not apply to every autistic person or guarantee the same effect for your child.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn i åldern 3 till 6 år har svårt att tolerera digitala verktyg som bärs på kroppen, kan ett alternativ utan bärbar utrustning vara värt att ta upp med ert professionella team, som ett tillägg och inte en ersättning för nuvarande stöd. Evidens: en öppen randomiserad studie i Kina med 78 förskolebarn (3-6 år, IQ>70); 39 fick kognitiv beteendeterapi med virtuell verklighet plus en inlärningsstilsprofil i 20 veckor, och 39 fick enbart profilen. Författarna beskriver möjliga, måttliga förbättringar. Begränsningar: studien var öppen, inkluderade bara barn med IQ>70, och resultaten gäller inte alla autistiska personer eller garanterar samma effekt för ditt barn.

title: Cognitive behavior therapy for autistic adolescents, awareness and care for my autistic traits program: a multicenter randomized controlled trial.
authors: Oshima F, Mandy W, Seto M, Hongo M, Tsuchiyagaito A, Hirano Y, Sutoh C, Guan S, Nitta Y, Ozawa Y, Kawasaki Y, Ohtani T, Masuya J, Takahashi N, Sato N, Nakamura S, Nakagawa A, Shimizu E
abstract: Background Autistic people demonstrate focused interests, sensitivity to sensory stimulation, and, compared with the general population, differences in social communication and interaction. We examined whether a combination of the Awareness and Care for My Autistic Traits (ACAT) program and treatment-as-usual is more effective than only treatment-as-usual in increasing the understanding of autistic attributes, reducing treatment stigma, and improving mental health and social adaptation among autistic adolescents and their parents/guardians. Methods Forty-nine adolescents and their parents/guardians were randomly assigned to either a combination of ACAT and treatment-as-usual or only treatment-as-usual. The combined group received six weekly 100-minute ACAT sessions, while the treatment-as-usual group received no additional intervention. The primary outcome was the change in understanding of autistic attributes (Autism Knowledge Quiz-Child), administered from pre- to post-intervention. The secondary outcomes included the change in Autism Knowledge Quiz-Parent, reduced treatment stigma, and improved mental health and social adaptation among autistic adolescents and their parents/guardians. A primary outcome measure scale was scored by assessors who were blind to the group assignment. Results The combined group (both autistic adolescents and their parents/guardians) showed an increase in Autism Knowledge Quiz scores compared to those in the treatment-as-usual group. Autistic adolescents in the combined group also demonstrated a decrease in treatment-related stigma and an improvement in general mental health compared to those in the treatment-as-usual group, while there were no group differences in the change in social adaptation. For parents/guardians, there were no group differences in the change in treatment-related stigma, general mental health, adaptive skills, or attitudes toward their children. Conclusions The ACAT program could be an effective treatment modality to increase the understanding of autistic attributes among both autistic adolescents and their parents/guardians. The ACAT program positively affects self-understanding, reduces treatment stigma, and stabilizes behavioral issues for autistic adolescents as a part of mental health measures, but it does not effectively reduce treatment barriers or improve mental health for parents/guardians. Further research should consider whether additional support for parents/guardians could be beneficial. Trial registration The study was registered in UMIN (UMIN000029851, 06/01/2018).

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adolescente de tu entorno tiene dudas sobre cómo funciona su mente, puede ayudar buscar un programa que le explique sus rasgos autistas de forma estructurada, junto a la atención habitual, y que incluya a la familia. Este ensayo aleatorizado reunió a 49 adolescentes autistas y a sus padres o tutores. Con seis sesiones semanales de 100 minutos, el grupo del programa mostró más conocimiento sobre el autismo; los adolescentes también mostraron menos estigma hacia el tratamiento y mejor salud mental general. No hubo diferencias en adaptación social, ni mejoras en la salud mental de los adultos. El grupo es pequeño y no sirve como regla para todas las personas; los adultos pueden necesitar apoyo adicional.
sheet.en: If an autistic teenager in your life is curious about how their mind works, it may help to look for a structured program that explains autistic traits alongside usual care and includes the family. This randomized trial included 49 autistic adolescents and their parents or guardians. After six weekly 100-minute sessions, the program group showed more knowledge about autism; the adolescents also showed less stigma about treatment and better general mental health. There were no differences in social adaptation, and parents' mental health did not improve. The group was small and the results are not a rule for every person; parents and guardians may need extra support too.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk tonåring i din närhet är nyfiken på hur hens sinne fungerar kan det hjälpa att söka ett strukturerat program som förklarar autistiska drag, vid sidan av ordinarie vård, och som inkluderar familjen. I denna randomiserade studie deltog 49 autistiska ungdomar och deras föräldrar eller vårdnadshavare. Efter sex veckovisa sessioner på 100 minuter visade programgruppen mer kunskap om autism; ungdomarna visade också mindre stigma kring behandling och bättre psykisk hälsa i allmänhet. Det fanns ingen skillnad i social anpassning, och föräldrarnas psykiska hälsa förbättrades inte. Gruppen var liten och resultaten gäller inte alla; föräldrar och vårdnadshavare kan behöva extra stöd.

title: Prevalence of Victimisation in Autistic Individuals: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Trundle G, Jones KA, Ropar D, Egan V
abstract: Autistic individuals are at an increased risk of experiencing victimisation. Previous reviews have focussed specific types of victimisation. Thus, a clearer picture considering the range of victimisation experiences autistic people face is required. This systematic review aims to identify the prevalence of victimisation in autistic individuals considering a variety of victimisation types (e.g., bulling, sexual victimisation, and crime) in both adults and children from clinical and community settings. Through systematic searches of relevant databases, 291 studies met the criteria for review. Of those, 34 studies met the inclusion criteria: a) quantitative studies, b) involving autistic individuals, c) reporting prevalence rates of victimisation. Meta-analysis found a pooled prevalence rate of victimisation of 44% in autistic individuals. Subgroup analysis examined moderating factors as high heterogeneity was present. This found the pooled prevalence rates for bullying to be 47%, 16% for child abuse, 40% for sexual victimisation, 13% for cyberbullying, and 84% for multiple forms of victimisation in autistic individuals, though heterogeneity remained. Correction for participants' age, reporter used, and the population which the sample was recruited from did not reduce heterogeneity. Although heterogeneity impedes the definitive interpretation of the findings, this review illustrates the need for strategies and interventions to reduce the incidence of victimisation.

sheet.es: Vale la pena preguntar con calma y de forma regular a tu hijo, hija o familiar autista cómo le tratan en la escuela, el trabajo, en internet y en otros lugares, usando la forma de comunicación que le resulte más cómoda. Creerle, anotar lo que cuenta y contar con adultos de confianza puede ayudar a detectar el acoso o el abuso a tiempo. Esta revisión sistemática con metaanálisis reunió 34 estudios con niños y adultos autistas y encontró que alrededor del 44 % había sufrido algún tipo de victimización, como acoso escolar o violencia sexual. Las cifras variaron mucho entre estudios, así que no predicen lo que vivirá cada persona.
sheet.en: It is worth gently and regularly checking in with your autistic child or family member about how they are treated at school, work, online and elsewhere, using whatever way of communicating suits them best. Believing them, keeping notes and having trusted adults around can help spot bullying or abuse early. This systematic review and meta-analysis combined 34 studies of autistic children and adults and found that about 44% had experienced some form of victimisation, such as bullying or sexual victimisation. Results varied widely between studies, so the figures cannot predict what any one person will experience.
sheet.sv: Det kan vara klokt att lugnt och regelbundet fråga ditt autistiska barn eller din autistiska anhörige hur hen blir bemött i skolan, på jobbet, på nätet och på andra ställen, på det sätt att kommunicera som passar hen bäst. Att tro på det hen berättar, anteckna och ha trygga vuxna runt omkring kan hjälpa till att upptäcka mobbning eller övergrepp tidigt. Denna systematiska översikt med metaanalys sammanställde 34 studier med autistiska barn och vuxna och fann att ungefär 44 % hade utsatts för någon form av utsatthet, till exempel mobbning eller sexuella övergrepp. Resultaten skilde sig mycket mellan studierna, så siffrorna kan inte förutsäga vad en enskild person kommer att uppleva.

title: A realist review of health passports for Autistic adults.
authors: Ellis R, Williams K, Brown A, Healer E, Grant A
abstract: Background Autism is a normal part of cognitive diversity, resulting in communication and sensory processing differences, which can become disabling in a neurotypical world. Autistic people have an increased likelihood of physical and mental co-occurring conditions and die earlier than neurotypical peers. Inaccessible healthcare may contribute to this. Autism Health Passports (AHPs) are paper-based or digital tools which can be used to describe healthcare accessibility needs; they are recommended in UK clinical guidance. However, questions remained as to the theoretical underpinnings and effectiveness of AHPs. Methods We undertook a systematic literature search identifying studies focused on AHPs for adults (aged over 16 years) from five databases. Included literature was subjected to realist evaluation. Data were extracted using a standardised form, developed by the research team, which considered research design, study quality for realist review and the Context, Mechanisms and Outcomes (CMOs) associated with each AHP tool. Findings 162 unique records were identified, and 13 items were included in the review. Only one item was considered high quality. Contextual factors focused on the inaccessibility of healthcare to Autistic patients and staff lack of confidence and training in supporting Autistic needs. Interventions were heterogeneous, with most sources reporting few details as to how they had been developed. The most frequently included contents were communication preferences. Mechanisms were often not stated or were inferred by the reviewers and lacked specificity. Outcomes were included in four studies and were primarily focused on AHP uptake, rather than Outcomes which measured impact. Conclusion There is insufficient evidence to conclude that AHPs reduce the health inequalities experienced by Autistic people. Using an AHP tool alone in a healthcare Context that does not meet Autistic needs, without the inclusion of the local Autistic community developing the tool, and a wider intervention to reduce known barriers to health inequality, may mean that AHPs do not trigger any Mechanisms, and thus cannot affect Outcomes.

sheet.es: Un pasaporte de salud autista (un documento en papel o digital que explica cómo comunicarse con la persona, qué sensibilidades sensoriales tiene y qué ajustes necesita) puede ser útil, pero no basta por sí solo. Si lo usas, complétalo junto con la persona autista, llévalo a las citas y pide al personal que lo lea y aplique los ajustes. Pregunta también qué formación tiene el centro.
