Esta revisión realista analizó 13 trabajos sobre pasaportes de salud para adultos autistas mayores de 16 años. Solo uno era de alta calidad y casi ninguno midió si mejoraban la salud, así que aún no sabemos si reducen las desigualdades sanitarias.
sheet.en: An autism health passport (a paper or digital document describing how someone prefers to communicate, their sensory needs and the adjustments they need) may help, but it is unlikely to be enough on its own. If you use one, fill it in together with the autistic person, bring it to appointments, and ask staff to read it and act on it. It is also fair to ask what autism training the service has. This realist review looked at 13 sources on health passports for autistic adults over 16. Only one was high quality and few measured real health effects, so we do not yet know whether passports reduce health inequalities.
sheet.sv: Ett autismhälsopass (ett papper eller digitalt dokument som beskriver hur personen vill kommunicera, sensoriska behov och vilka anpassningar som behövs) kan vara till hjälp, men räcker sannolikt inte ensamt. Om ni använder ett, fyll i det tillsammans med den autistiska personen, ta med det till besök och be personalen läsa det och göra anpassningarna. Det är också rimligt att fråga vilken autismkunskap vårdenheten har. Denna realistiska översikt granskade 13 källor om hälsopass för autistiska vuxna över 16 år. Bara en höll hög kvalitet och få mätte faktiska hälsoeffekter, så vi vet ännu inte om passen minskar ojämlikheten i hälsa.

title: Early Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Review and Analysis of the Risks and Benefits.
authors: Okoye C, Obialo-Ibeawuchi CM, Obajeun OA, Sarwar S, Tawfik C, Waleed MS, Wasim AU, Mohamoud I, Afolayan AY, Mbaezue RN
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition made up of enduring challenges in social communication and interaction and the presence of repetitive and restricted behavior patterns. Early diagnosis of autism is crucial for timely intervention and improved long-term outcomes. This review aims to explore some of its signs and symptoms, look into some diagnostic tools, and analyze the benefits and risks associated with an early diagnosis of autism. The symptoms of ASD vary from child to child, some of which are: avoidance of eye contact, lack of response to names, excessive fear, and lack of interactive and pretend play. Early identification of these symptoms by caregivers and healthcare providers facilitates the need for diagnosis and appropriate interventions. Some screening and diagnostic tools that have been found to help make the diagnosis are the Modified Checklist for Autism in Toddlers, Revised with Follow-Up (M-CHAT-R/F), the Social Communication Questionnaire (SCQ), the Parents' Evaluation of Developmental Status (PEDS), and the Childhood Autism Rating Scale (CARS), amongst others. The benefits of early diagnosis include the opportunity for early intervention, which has been shown to enhance developmental outcomes and improve adaptive skills. Early identification allows for the implementation of specialized interventions tailored to the specific needs of individuals with autism, targeting social communication, language development, and behavioral challenges. Furthermore, early diagnosis enables families to access appropriate support services, educational resources, and community programs, facilitating better coping mechanisms, reducing parental stress, and increasing adult independence. However, early diagnosis of autism also entails certain risks. One significant concern is the potential for labeling and stigmatization, which can impact the child's self-esteem and social interactions. There is a risk of overdiagnosis or misdiagnosis, leading to unnecessary interventions and treatments. Additionally, the diagnostic process can be lengthy, complex, and emotionally challenging for families, requiring comprehensive assessments by multidisciplinary teams. This review highlights the importance of a balanced approach when considering the benefits and risks of early diagnosis. Early identification allows for timely interventions that significantly improve developmental outcomes and quality of life for individuals with autism. To mitigate the risks, it is crucial to ensure accurate and reliable diagnostic procedures, support families throughout the process, and promote societal awareness and acceptance. We also highlighted some future directions in the management of autism, including the use of biomarkers and the use of artificial intelligence and learning for diagnosing ASD.

sheet.es: Si notas señales como poca respuesta al nombre, poco juego simbólico o evitar el contacto visual, puedes comentarlo pronto con el pediatra o un profesional de salud; pedir una evaluación no obliga a nada y puedes ir a tu ritmo. Es una revisión que recoge las ventajas y los riesgos del diagnóstico temprano. Entre las ventajas cita el acceso a apoyos y recursos para la familia; entre los riesgos, el estigma, el sobrediagnóstico y un proceso largo y agotador. Los límites: es una revisión, no prueba qué ocurrirá con cada niño o niña, y las señales varían mucho de una persona a otra.
sheet.en: If you notice signs such as little response to their name, little pretend play or avoiding eye contact, you can raise it early with a paediatrician or health professional; asking for an assessment commits you to nothing, and you can go at your own pace. This is a review weighing the benefits and risks of early diagnosis. Benefits it names include access to supports and resources for the family; risks include stigma, overdiagnosis and a long, tiring process. Its limits: it is a review, it cannot say what will happen for any one child, and signs vary a great deal from person to person.
sheet.sv: Om du ser tecken som att barnet svarar lite på sitt namn, leker lite låtsaslekar eller undviker ögonkontakt kan du ta upp det tidigt med barnläkare eller annan vårdpersonal; att be om en utredning förpliktar inte till något, och du kan gå i din egen takt. Det här är en översikt som väger fördelar och risker med tidig diagnos. Fördelarna den nämner är bland annat tillgång till stöd och resurser för familjen; riskerna är stigma, överdiagnostik och en lång, tröttsam process. Begränsningar: det är en översikt, den kan inte säga vad som händer för ett enskilt barn, och tecknen varierar mycket mellan personer.

title: The mechanism and effectiveness of mindfulness-based intervention for reducing the psychological distress of parents of children with autism spectrum disorder: A protocol of randomized control trial of ecological momentary intervention and assessment.
authors: Wang Q, Ng SM, Zhou X
abstract: Background Existing studies have unequivocally demonstrated that parents of children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) experience various stressful daily life events and suffer from psychological distress. Mindfulness level is found to be an effective buffer between parents' appraisal of stress life events and psychological distress. However, the mechanism behind the function of mindfulness is unclear, and traditional mindfulness-based intervention (MBI) in experimental settings is not tailored to personal real-life needs. This study proposes to conduct a randomized controlled trial (RCT) to examine the effectiveness of MBI delivered by ecological momentary intervention (EMI) and assessed by ecological momentary assessment (EMA) in changing participants' cognitive appraisal of stressful life events and thus reducing the psychological distress of parents of children with ASD. Method The proposed study will recruit 670 parents of children with ASD and randomly assign them to the intervention and control groups (335 in each group). Participants in the intervention group will install the EMI/A app on their smartphones. In the app, participants can receive practice prompts daily, browse and practice different mindfulness exercises in the intervention library at any time, talk to a virtual counselor (chatbot) when feeling stressed, complete EMA on the cognitive appraisal of life events, and receive the log of change of psychological status daily. Participants in the control group will only receive audio-based standardized mindfulness practice instructions three times per week. The effects of MBI will be assessed based on the EMA data, right after the intervention and at the 2-month follow-up. The primary outcome will be participants' psychological distress measured by the depression anxiety stress scale. The secondary outcomes will include participants' subjective well-being, measured by the satisfaction with life scale, and level of resilience, measured by the psychological empowerment scale. Multilevel structural equational modelling will be applied to examine the pathways of the relationship between daily life events, cognitive appraisal, and psychological distress. Discussion The potential benefit of the proposed study is to increase the psychological well-being of parents of children with ASD, and the method may extend to participants suffering from other psychological issues in the future. Trial registration: This trial has been registered on clinicaltrials.gov with the ID of NCT05746468.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a un niño autista y sientes estrés, una app de mindfulness en el móvil, con ejercicios breves a lo largo del día, es una opción que se está estudiando; aún no se sabe si funciona. Es el protocolo de un ensayo aleatorizado: describe un estudio planificado con 670 madres y padres de niños autistas, repartidos al azar en dos grupos, y todavía no ofrece resultados. Por eso no se puede saber si ayuda ni a quién. Si el estrés pesa mucho, habla con un profesional sanitario.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic child and feel stressed, a smartphone mindfulness app with short exercises through the day is one option being studied; it is not yet known whether it works. This is the protocol of a randomized trial: it describes a planned study of 670 parents of autistic children, split at random into two groups, and reports no results yet. So we cannot say whether it helps, or for whom. If stress feels heavy, talk to a health professional.
sheet.sv: Om du är förälder till ett autistiskt barn och känner stress är en mindfulness-app i mobilen med korta övningar under dagen ett alternativ som studeras; ännu vet man inte om det fungerar. Detta är protokollet för en randomiserad studie: den beskriver en planerad studie med 670 föräldrar till autistiska barn, slumpmässigt fördelade på två grupper, och redovisar inga resultat än. Därför går det inte att säga om det hjälper, eller för vem. Om stressen känns tung, prata med någon inom vården.

title: Advice for autistic people considering a career in academia.
authors: Jones SC
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract One of the recognised strengths of autistic people is their ability to absorb and retain large amounts of information; autistic children and adolescents are often described as 'little professors'. So, is the life of a university researcher or teacher the ideal career for an autistic person? In this study, 37 autistic people working in universities and colleges provide advice to young people considering a future career as an academic. They emphasise the importance of understanding the complexities and requirements of the role, understanding and valuing yourself and your strengths, and finding the right people to work with and learn from. They also discuss the importance of maintaining a balance between work and well-being, and between caution and passion. The life of an academic can be ideally suited to an autistic person, but it can also be very challenging.

sheet.es: Si un joven autista piensa en una carrera académica, puede ayudarle hablar con autistas que ya trabajan en universidades. Pueden explorar juntos qué exige el puesto, qué fortalezas tiene la persona, con quién le gustaría trabajar y cómo cuidar el equilibrio entre trabajo y bienestar. Es un estudio con 37 personas autistas que trabajan en universidades y colleges, y que dieron consejos a jóvenes. Sus consejos reflejan experiencias personales: no sirven como regla para todas las personas autistas, y el abstract no mide resultados de ninguna estrategia concreta.
sheet.en: If a young autistic person is thinking about an academic career, it may help to talk with autistic people who already work in universities. Together you can explore what the role demands, what the person's strengths are, who they would like to work and learn with, and how to protect a balance between work and well-being. This was a study with 37 autistic people working in universities and colleges, who gave advice to young people. Their advice reflects personal experience, so it is not a rule for every autistic person, and the abstract does not measure the results of any particular strategy.
sheet.sv: Om en ung autistisk person funderar på en akademisk karriär kan det hjälpa att prata med autistiska personer som redan arbetar på universitet. Ni kan tillsammans utforska vad rollen kräver, vilka styrkor personen har, vem hen vill arbeta och lära med, och hur balansen mellan arbete och välmående kan skyddas. Det var en studie med 37 autistiska personer som arbetar på universitet och högskolor och gav råd till unga. Råden bygger på personliga erfarenheter och gäller inte alla autistiska personer, och sammanfattningen mäter inte effekten av någon särskild strategi.

title: The Foundations of Autistic Flourishing.
authors: Pellicano E, Heyworth M
abstract: Purpose of review All people-including Autistic people-deserve to live flourishing lives. But what does a flourishing life look like for Autistic people? We suggest that the hidden biases, methodological errors, and key assumptions of autism science have obscured answers to this question. Here, we seek to initiate a broader discussion about what the foundations for a good Autistic life might be and how this discussion might be framed. Recent findings We identify five ways in which autism science can help us all to secure those foundations, including by (1) giving Autistic well-being prominence in research, (2) amplifying Autistic autonomy, (3) attending better to everyday experiences, (4) acknowledging context, and (5) working in partnership with Autistic people and their families and allies to ensure that they are at the heart of research decision-making. Such an approach would direct the focus of autism research to help shape good Autistic lives.

sheet.es: Una idea práctica para mañana: pregunte a la persona autista qué hace que su día vaya bien, y deje que esa respuesta guíe las decisiones. Fíjese en lo cotidiano (descanso, intereses, entorno sensorial, relaciones) más que en corregir rasgos, respete su autonomía y ajuste el contexto antes de pedirle que cambie. Planifique junto a ella, no por ella. Se trata de una revisión escrita con personas autistas que propone cinco prioridades para la investigación: bienestar, autonomía, experiencias diarias, contexto y colaboración. Su límite: es un análisis y una propuesta, no un estudio con participantes que mida resultados, y cada persona definirá su bienestar a su manera.
sheet.en: A practical idea for tomorrow: ask the autistic person what makes a day go well for them, and let that answer guide decisions. Pay attention to everyday life (rest, interests, sensory surroundings, relationships) rather than correcting traits, respect their autonomy, and adjust the context before asking them to change. Plan with them, not for them. This is a review written with autistic people that proposes five research priorities: well-being, autonomy, daily experiences, context and partnership. Its limit: it is an analysis and a proposal, not a study with participants measuring outcomes, and each person will define flourishing in their own way.
sheet.sv: En praktisk idé för i morgon: fråga den autistiska personen vad som gör att en dag fungerar bra, och låt svaret styra besluten. Uppmärksamma vardagen (vila, intressen, sensorisk miljö, relationer) snarare än att rätta till drag, respektera personens självbestämmande och anpassa sammanhanget innan du ber hen att ändra sig. Planera tillsammans med hen, inte åt hen. Detta är en översikt skriven tillsammans med autistiska personer som föreslår fem forskningsprioriteringar: välmående, autonomi, vardagserfarenheter, sammanhang och samarbete. Begränsning: det är en analys och ett förslag, inte en studie med deltagare som mäter resultat, och varje person definierar sitt välmående på sitt eget sätt.

title: The role of interpersonal synchrony in forming impressions of autistic and non-autistic adults.
authors: Plank IS, Traiger LS, Nelson AM, Koehler JC, Lang SF, Tepest R, Vogeley K, Georgescu AL, Falter-Wagner CM
abstract: When people meet, they almost instantaneously form an impression of each other. First impressions of character traits and rapport are less favourable when people with autism spectrum condition (ASC) are judged compared to non-autistic people. Little is known about the behavioural differences that drive these altered impressions. In the present study, we investigated the influence of interpersonal synchrony on impression formation of autistic and non-autistic people. Specifically, we used lagged cross-correlations to assess how much each interactant's motion energy, a measure which can be determined from video recordings, influenced the other interactant's motion energy. In short, silent clips of dyadic conversations, we asked non-autistic participants to rate their impression of one of the two interactants, which was solely based on the outlines of both interactants. We expected that the amount of leading of the target interactant, their diagnostic status as well as the interaction of these factors would influence impression formation. We found that while the amount of leading had a positive effect on the impressions of non-autistic interactants, this was not true for interactants with ASC. This suggests that interpersonal synchrony of motion energy is one driver of less favourable impressions of autistic compared to non-autistic people.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista a situaciones sociales, recuerda que las primeras impresiones de otras personas pueden verse afectadas por diferencias en el movimiento compartido durante la conversación, no por su carácter. Puedes explicar esto a familiares, docentes o empleadores para que no juzguen demasiado rápido. Se trata de un estudio con personas autistas y no autistas que hablaban en parejas; otras personas no autistas valoraron clips breves y sin sonido, solo con siluetas. Sus límites: mide un solo aspecto del movimiento, y no demuestra que ocurra igual en cada persona ni en la vida diaria.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person in social situations, remember that other people's first impressions may be shaped by differences in shared movement during conversation, not by the person's character. You can explain this to relatives, teachers or employers so they avoid judging too quickly. This was a study with autistic and non-autistic adults who talked in pairs; non-autistic participants then rated short silent clips showing only outlines. Its limits: it looks at just one aspect of movement, and it does not show the same happens for every person or in everyday life.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person i sociala situationer: kom ihåg att andras första intryck kan påverkas av skillnader i delad rörelse under samtal, inte av personens karaktär. Du kan förklara detta för anhöriga, lärare eller arbetsgivare så att de dömer mindre snabbt. Det var en studie med autistiska och icke-autistiska vuxna som pratade i par; icke-autistiska deltagare bedömde sedan korta ljudlösa klipp med enbart konturer. Begränsningar: den mäter bara en aspekt av rörelse och visar inte att samma sak gäller för varje person eller i vardagen.

title: Addressing the autism mental health crisis: the potential of phenomenology in neurodiversity-affirming clinical practices.
authors: Pantazakos T, Vanaken GJ
abstract: The neurodiversity movement has introduced a new era for autism research. Yet, the neurodiversity paradigm and the autism clinic remain largely unconnected. With the present work, we aim to contribute to filling this lacuna by putting forward phenomenology as a foundation for developing neurodiversity-affirming clinical interventions for autism. In the first part of this paper, we highlight that autistic people face a severe mental health crisis. We argue that approaches focused on reducing autistic 'symptoms' are unlikely to solve the problem, as autistic mental health is positively correlated with autism acceptance and perceived quality of support provided, not necessarily with lack of 'symptomatologic severity'. Therefore, the development and dissemination of neurodiversity-affirming clinical interventions is key for addressing the autism mental health crisis. However, therapists and researchers exploring such neurodiversity-affirming practices are faced with two significant challenges. First, they lack concrete methodological principles regarding the incorporation of neurodiversity into clinical work. Second, they need to find ways to acknowledge rightful calls to respect the 'autistic self' within the clinic, while also challenging certain beliefs and behaviors of autistic clients in a manner that is sine qua non for therapy, irrespective of neurotype. In the second part of the paper, we introduce phenomenological psychology as a potential resource for engaging with these challenges in neurodiversity-affirming approaches to psychotherapy. In this vein, we put forward specific directions for adapting cognitive behavioral and interpersonal psychotherapy for autism.

sheet.es: Si buscas apoyo psicológico para una persona autista, merece la pena preguntar si el profesional trabaja desde la aceptación del autismo y no solo desde reducir 'síntomas'. Este trabajo es un artículo teórico de argumentación, que plantea que la salud mental autista se relaciona con la aceptación del autismo y con la calidad percibida del apoyo, no necesariamente con la gravedad de los 'síntomas'. Propone la fenomenología como base para adaptar la terapia cognitivo-conductual y la interpersonal. Sus límites: son propuestas y direcciones, no una intervención probada, y no sirven como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you are looking for psychological support for an autistic person, it is worth asking whether the therapist works from autism acceptance rather than only from reducing 'symptoms'. This is a theoretical paper that argues that autistic mental health is linked to autism acceptance and to the perceived quality of support, not necessarily to 'symptomatologic severity'. It proposes phenomenology as a foundation for adapting cognitive behavioral and interpersonal psychotherapy. Its limits: these are proposals and directions, not a tested intervention, and they are not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du söker psykologiskt stöd för en autistisk person är det värt att fråga om terapeuten utgår från acceptans av autism och inte bara från att minska 'symtom'. Arbetet är en teoretisk artikel som resonerar om att autistisk psykisk hälsa hänger ihop med acceptans av autism och upplevd kvalitet på stödet, inte nödvändigtvis med 'symtomens svårighetsgrad'. Den föreslår fenomenologi som grund för att anpassa kognitiv beteendeterapi och interpersonell psykoterapi. Begränsningar: det är förslag och riktningar, inte en prövad insats, och det är ingen regel för alla personer.

title: Increased rates of chronic physical health conditions across all organ systems in autistic adolescents and adults.
authors: Ward JH, Weir E, Allison C, Baron-Cohen S
abstract: Background The poorer physical health of autistic adults compared to non-autistic adults has been highlighted by several epidemiological studies. However, research has so far been limited to specific geographical areas and has primarily focused on young autistic individuals (aged 35 years and younger). Recent studies indicate a higher rate of mortality in autistic people, as well as poorer quality of self-reported healthcare interactions. This study aims to determine, first, whether autistic people experience greater levels of non-communicable health conditions and second, whether these are explained by differences in demographics (i.e. sex, country of residence, ethnicity, education level), alcohol use, smoking, body mass index (BMI), or family history of medical conditions. Method We employed a cross-sectional, convenience-sampling study via an anonymous, online survey of autistic and non-autistic adults (n = 2305, mean age = 41.6, 65.9% female, 49% autistic). The survey asked participants to self-report information about their demographics, autism diagnosis, diet, exercise, sleep, sexual health, substance use, personal medical history, and family medical history (for all first-degree, biological relatives). Binomial logistic regression across four iterative models of increasing complexity was applied to assess rates of physical health conditions. The Benjamini-Hochberg correction was used to account for multiple testing, and only physical health conditions that achieved at least 1% endorsement within the overall sample (n > 22) were included in the analysis to reduce risk of Type I errors. We also used novel network analysis methods to test whether there are increased levels of multimorbidity between autistic and non-autistic people. Results There were significantly elevated rates of non-communicable conditions across all organ systems in autistic people, including gastrointestinal, neurological, endocrine, visual, ear/nose/throat, skin, liver and kidney, and haematological conditions. We confirmed previous findings by showing highly significant differences in rates of neurological and gastrointestinal symptoms (p Limitations Our study is biased towards females, white individuals, highly educated people, and UK residents, likely due to sampling biases. Our self-report study design may also exclude those who lack access to computers, or those with intellectual disability. Our network analysis is also limited in size. Conclusions This study provides evidence of widespread, physical health comorbidity that spans nearly all major organ systems in autistic adults compared to non-autistic adults, using both binary logistic regression and network models. Healthcare professionals must be made aware of the range of co-occurring physical health conditions that may be more common among autistic people. However, our findings also point towards potential avenues requiring further exploration, such as the association of autism with both Coeliac's disease and EDS.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista, o lo eres, puede ser útil mencionar en las citas médicas cualquier síntoma físico, aunque parezca no tener relación, y pedir que se revise con calma. Es un estudio transversal con una encuesta anónima en línea: participaron 2305 adultos, el 49% autistas, que informaron ellos mismos de su salud. Hubo más afecciones físicas crónicas en personas autistas, en casi todos los sistemas del cuerpo. Sus límites: la muestra tiene más mujeres, personas blancas, con estudios altos y residentes en el Reino Unido, y puede excluir a quien no usa ordenadores o tiene discapacidad intelectual. No describe a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person, or are autistic, it may help to mention any physical symptoms at medical appointments, even ones that seem unrelated, and ask for them to be checked calmly. This was a cross-sectional study using an anonymous online survey: 2305 adults took part, 49% of them autistic, reporting their own health. Autistic people reported more chronic physical health conditions across nearly all body systems. Its limits: the sample included more women, white people, highly educated people and UK residents, and may leave out people without computer access or with intellectual disability. It does not describe every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person, eller själv är autistisk, kan det vara bra att ta upp alla fysiska symtom vid vårdbesök, även sådana som verkar orelaterade, och be om en lugn kontroll. Det var en tvärsnittsstudie med en anonym enkät på nätet: 2305 vuxna deltog, 49% av dem autistiska, och de rapporterade själva om sin hälsa. Autistiska personer uppgav fler kroniska fysiska hälsotillstånd i nästan alla kroppens system. Begränsningar: urvalet hade fler kvinnor, vita personer, högutbildade och bosatta i Storbritannien, och kan missa personer utan datoråtkomst eller med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning. Studien beskriver inte alla autistiska personer.

title: Applications of identity-based theories to understand the impact of stigma and camouflaging on mental health outcomes for autistic people.
authors: Rivera RA, Bennetto L
abstract: Autistic people have long been conceptualized from a deficit-based model of disability, but recent self-advocates and scholars have asserted the importance of recognizing autism as both a disability and an important part of a person's social identity. The autistic identity is subject to specific stigma and stressors beyond everyday discrimination and prejudice, which can have many downstream implications on mental health and well-being. Prior research on camouflaging has explained both quantitatively and qualitatively how autistic people conform to norms and mask their autistic traits to better fit in with non-autistic societal standards. Given this paradigm shift in understanding autistic peoples' lived experiences, researchers must also begin to reshape the theories guiding their work in order to improve diagnosis, intervention, and supports. This review examines the extant research on identity-related stigma and camouflaging and their subsequent impacts on mental health outcomes in autism. A model is proposed integrating identity-based theories-specifically the social model of disability, social identity theory, and minority stress model-to explain relationships across research areas and better explain the experiences of autistic people. We discuss how identity-based theories can be applied in autism research to better understand the impacts of stigma and camouflaging on autistic peoples' lived experiences and reduce disparities in their mental health outcomes.

sheet.es: Si la persona autista a la que acompañas parece agotada después del colegio, el trabajo o reuniones sociales, puede estar camuflando: ocultando rasgos autistas para encajar. Mañana puedes ofrecer espacios en casa donde no tenga que fingir, valorar su identidad autista y reducir exigencias de parecer «normal». Reconocer el estigma que vive puede proteger su bienestar. Esta revisión reúne investigaciones previas sobre estigma, camuflaje y salud mental en personas autistas, y propone un modelo basado en teorías de identidad y estrés minoritario. Su límite: es un marco teórico, no un estudio que pruebe intervenciones, y cada persona vive su identidad de forma distinta.
sheet.en: If the autistic person you support seems drained after school, work or social events, they may be camouflaging: hiding autistic traits to fit in. Tomorrow you could offer spaces at home where they don't have to perform, value their autistic identity, and ease expectations to appear 'typical'. Acknowledging the stigma they face may help protect their wellbeing. This review gathers earlier research on stigma, camouflaging and mental health in autistic people, and proposes a model based on identity theories and minority stress. Its limit: it is a theoretical framework, not a study testing supports, and every person experiences their identity differently.
sheet.sv: Om den autistiska person du stöttar verkar utmattad efter skola, jobb eller sociala sammanhang kan hen kamouflera: dölja autistiska drag för att passa in. I morgon kan du erbjuda platser hemma där hen inte behöver spela en roll, visa uppskattning för hens autistiska identitet och sänka kraven på att verka ”typisk”. Att erkänna stigmat hen möter kan skydda välmåendet. Denna översikt sammanställer tidigare forskning om stigma, kamouflering och psykisk hälsa hos autistiska personer och föreslår en modell byggd på identitetsteorier och minoritetsstress. Begränsning: det är en teoretisk ram, inte en studie som prövar stöd, och varje person upplever sin identitet olika.

title: Lived Experiences of Iranian Parents of Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review.
authors: Jamshidian E, Abed EH, Sourtiji H, Azar EF, Hashemzadeh M, Mirzaie H
abstract: Background Autism is a lifelong condition that seriously affects many aspects of children's and families' lives. The experience attained by living with a child with autism can be a valuable source of information to provide support and satisfactory services to children with autism and their families. We aimed to investigate the lived experiences of Iranian parents of children with autism. Methods The search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Google Scholar, CINAHL, PsychInfo, SID, and Magiran until Nov 2021. Two reviewers screened the articles, applied inclusion criteria, critically evaluated articles using the Critical Appraisal Skills Program (CASP), and extracted study details according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) checklist. Thematic synthesis was used to analyze included studies. Results From 2772 articles in the initial search, sixteen studies entered the final analysis. Four themes emerged, including treatment-related lived experience, individual lived experience, social lived experience, and occupational lived experience. Iranian parents of children with autism are confronted with negative experiences, including inaccurate diagnostic processes, lack of adequate support at the diagnosis time, low-quality treatment, psychological problems, and concern about the child's future. Also, Parent's experiences showed family problems, stigma, and problems with doing occupations. Conclusion Practitioners, policy-makers, and regulatory organizations should urgently consider issues mentioned in the parents' experiences to provide proper healthcare services for children with autism and their families.

title: Toward understanding and enhancing self-determination: a qualitative exploration with autistic adults without co-occurring intellectual disability.
authors: Thompson-Hodgetts S, Ryan J, Coombs E, Brown HM, Xavier A, Devlin C, Lee A, Kedmy A, Borden A
abstract: Introduction Self-determination is a fundamental human right positively related to quality of life. However, Autistic people are reported to be less self-determined than non-autistic people. We aimed to (1) understand what self-determination means to Autistic people from their perspective, (2) explore their perceptions of current barriers to being self-determined, and (3) learn from Autistic people about how they would like to be supported to be self-determined. Methods Semi-structured interviews were done with 19 Autistic adults without co-occurring intellectual disability. Data were analyzed by three Autistic and two non-autistic researchers through an iterative process of data familiarization, coding, and theme development, informed by reflexive thematic analysis. Autistic Community Partners (ACP) were also engaged throughout the study, and provided substantive feedback on all methods and results. Results Self-determination held the same meaning for Autistic people as non-autistic people. More specifically, participants discussed having the opportunity and support to make choices and decisions in life without unnecessary control from others. Experiences of self-determination were centered around: (1) lack of opportunity, influenced by ableist expectations and discrimination, and (2) executive processing differences that interfered with choice and decision-making. Desired areas of support related to providing opportunities to (1) make choices and exert autonomy, (2) be supported to unmask and be valued as one's authentic Autistic self, and (3) offering pragmatic support for executive processing differences. Conclusion Autistic adults desire to be self-determined and can flourish with support, as they determine to be appropriate, which might look different from support commonly offered or sought by non-autistic people. Although individualized support was discussed, the ideal desired support was for an inclusive society that values and respects their neurodivergence, rather than imposing ableist expectations. An inclusive society is only achievable through reduced (or eliminated) stigma and prejudice against Autistic people.

sheet.es: Ofrezca opciones reales y deje que la persona autista decida, con apoyo práctico cuando planificar o elegir resulta difícil, sin controlar más de lo necesario. Permita que sea ella misma, sin obligarla a disimular. En este estudio cualitativo se entrevistó a 19 adultos autistas sin discapacidad intelectual, y el análisis incluyó a investigadores autistas. Los resultados reflejan experiencias de ese grupo; no sirven como regla para todas las personas autistas, por ejemplo quienes tienen discapacidad intelectual. Pregunte siempre a la persona qué apoyo prefiere.
sheet.en: Offer real choices and let the autistic person decide, with practical help when planning or choosing is hard, and without more control than needed. Make room for them to be themselves rather than having to mask. This qualitative study interviewed 19 autistic adults without co-occurring intellectual disability, and autistic researchers took part in the analysis. The findings reflect this group's experiences; they are not a rule for every autistic person, for example those with intellectual disability. Always ask the person what support they prefer.
sheet.sv: Erbjud verkliga val och låt den autistiska personen bestämma, med praktiskt stöd när det är svårt att planera eller välja, och utan mer kontroll än nödvändigt. Ge utrymme att vara sig själv i stället för att behöva maskera. I den här kvalitativa studien intervjuades 19 autistiska vuxna utan samtidig intellektuell funktionsnedsättning, och autistiska forskare deltog i analysen. Resultaten speglar den gruppens erfarenheter och gäller inte som regel för alla autistiska personer, till exempel de med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning. Fråga alltid personen vilket stöd hen vill ha.

title: Anti-ableism and scientific accuracy in autism research: a false dichotomy.
authors: Bottema-Beutel K, Kapp SK, Sasson N, Gernsbacher MA, Natri H, Botha M
abstract: It was recently argued that autism researchers committed to rejecting ableist frameworks in their research may sacrifice "scientifically accurate" conceptualizations of autism. In this perspective piece, we argue that: (a) anti-ableism vs. scientific accuracy is a false dichotomy, (b) there is no ideology-free science that has claim to scientific accuracy, and (c) autism science has a history of false leads in part because of unexamined ableist ideologies that undergird researcher framings and interpretations of evidence. To illustrate our claims, we discuss several avenues of autism research that were promoted as scientific advances, but were eventually debunked or shown to have much less explanatory value than initially proposed. These research programs have involved claims about autism etiology, the nature of autism and autistic characteristics, and autism intervention. Common to these false leads have been ableist assumptions about autism that inform researcher perspectives. Negative impacts of this work have been mitigated in some areas of autism research, but these perspectives continue to exert influence on the lives of autistic people, including the availability of services, discourses about autism, and sociocultural conceptualizations of autistic people. Examining these false leads may help current researchers better understand how ableism may negatively influence their areas of inquiry. We close with a positive argument that promoting anti-ableism can be done in tandem with increasing scientific accuracy.

sheet.es: Cuando lea sobre autismo, puede preguntarse con calma: ¿esta afirmación parte de la idea de que ser autista es un defecto? Varias teorías presentadas como avances sobre causas, naturaleza o intervenciones del autismo resultaron falsas o mucho menos útiles de lo prometido, en parte por supuestos capacitistas. Mañana puede elegir fuentes que escuchen a personas autistas y valorar lo que su hijo o hija comunica, sin aceptar etiquetas sin examinarlas. Evidencia: es un artículo de perspectiva que revisa la historia de la investigación sobre autismo; no recoge datos nuevos de participantes. Límite: es una argumentación de expertos, no un estudio empírico, y no ofrece pautas aplicables a cada persona.
sheet.en: When you read about autism, you can calmly ask: does this claim assume that being autistic is a defect? Several theories promoted as breakthroughs about autism's causes, nature or interventions were later debunked or proved far less useful than promised, partly because of ableist assumptions. Tomorrow, you might choose sources that listen to autistic people and value what your child communicates, rather than accepting labels unexamined. Evidence: this is a perspective article reviewing the history of autism research; it does not collect new data from participants. Limit: it is an expert argument, not an empirical study, and offers no rules that fit every person.
sheet.sv: När du läser om autism kan du lugnt fråga dig: utgår påståendet från att det är en brist att vara autistisk? Flera teorier som lanserades som genombrott om autismens orsaker, natur eller insatser visade sig senare vara fel eller mycket mindre användbara än utlovat, delvis på grund av funkofobiska antaganden. I morgon kan du välja källor som lyssnar på autistiska personer och ta vara på det ditt barn kommunicerar, i stället för att godta etiketter oprövade. Evidens: detta är en perspektivartikel som granskar autismforskningens historia; den samlar inga nya data från deltagare. Begränsning: det är en expertargumentation, inte en empirisk studie, och ger inga regler som passar alla.

title: 'Living in a world that's not about us': The impact of everyday life on the health and wellbeing of autistic women and gender diverse people.
authors: Grove R, Clapham H, Moodie T, Gurrin S, Hall G
abstract: Background Autistic women and gender diverse people have specific needs related to their physical and mental health. They also experience more barriers to accessing services. While there are autobiographical accounts of the 'invisible' challenges that autistic women and gender diverse people face day-to-day, there has been limited research that explores how these experiences impact health and wellbeing. Objectives This study aimed to understand the everyday experiences of autistic women and gender diverse people, and their impact on health and wellbeing. Design Qualitative methods were used to elicit rich information about the unique experiences of autistic women and gender diverse people. Methods We conducted semi-structured interviews with 31 autistic adults. The data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Results We identified 3 themes and 10 subthemes. Our first theme described 'all the stuff that you have to do to get through life', including managing domestic tasks, parenting, unique health needs and co-occurring physical conditions. The second theme outlined the impact of 'living in a world that's not about us', describing how navigating the neurotypical world, managing gender role expectations and trying to fit impacts on mental health. Our third theme outlined the positive impacts of 'shedding all the layers and being myself', including the importance of formal identification, exploring autistic identity and community, and including autistic people in research to support them to 'have a good life on their own terms'. Conclusion This study emphasized the importance of shifting the responsibility of health and wellbeing from the individual, and the importance of interpersonal, community, cultural, policy and societal factors in ensuring positive health outcomes for autistic women and gender diverse people. It also highlighted areas that enable autistic women and gender diverse people to flourish, including autistic community connectedness, positive relationships and autistic-affirming support from health professionals.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una mujer o persona de género diverso autista, reconoce el esfuerzo invisible de las tareas diarias: casa, crianza, salud y adaptarse a un mundo neurotípico. Ayuda reducir exigencias de «encajar», repartir tareas, apoyar el contacto con la comunidad autista y buscar profesionales que respeten su identidad. Ser ella misma, sin máscaras, se asoció con más bienestar. La evidencia procede de entrevistas cualitativas con 31 adultos autistas, analizadas temáticamente. Sus límites: es una muestra pequeña, sin grupo de comparación, y describe experiencias, no causas; no todas las personas vivirán lo mismo.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic woman or gender diverse person, recognise the invisible effort behind everyday life: household tasks, parenting, health needs and navigating a neurotypical world. It can help to ease pressure to 'fit in', share tasks, support connection with autistic community and look for affirming health professionals. Being able to drop the layers and be themselves was linked to better wellbeing. The evidence comes from qualitative interviews with 31 autistic adults, analysed thematically. Its limits: a small sample, no comparison group, and it describes experiences rather than causes; not everyone will share them.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk kvinna eller person med annan könsidentitet, erkänn den osynliga ansträngningen i vardagen: hushåll, föräldraskap, hälsobehov och att navigera i en neurotypisk värld. Det kan hjälpa att minska kraven på att passa in, dela på uppgifter, stödja kontakt med autistisk gemenskap och söka bekräftande vårdpersonal. Att få släppa fasaden och vara sig själv kopplades till bättre välmående. Underlaget är kvalitativa intervjuer med 31 autistiska vuxna, analyserade tematiskt. Begränsningar: litet urval, ingen jämförelsegrupp, och studien beskriver upplevelser, inte orsaker; alla delar inte dessa erfarenheter.

title: Role of gastrointestinal health in managing children with autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Al-Beltagi M, Saeed NK, Bediwy AS, Elbeltagi R, Alhawamdeh R
abstract: Children with autism spectrum disorders (ASD) or autism are more prone to gastrointestinal (GI) disorders than the general population. These disorders can significantly affect their health, learning, and development due to various factors such as genetics, environment, and behavior. The causes of GI disorders in children with ASD can include gut dysbiosis, immune dysfunction, food sensitivities, digestive enzyme deficiencies, and sensory processing differences. Many studies suggest that numerous children with ASD experience GI problems, and effective management is crucial. Diagnosing autism is typically done through genetic, neurological, functional, and behavioral assessments and observations, while GI tests are not consistently reliable. Some GI tests may increase the risk of developing ASD or exacerbating symptoms. Addressing GI issues in individuals with ASD can improve their overall well-being, leading to better behavior, cognitive function, and educational abilities. Proper management can improve digestion, nutrient absorption, and appetite by relieving physical discomfort and pain. Alleviating GI symptoms can improve sleep patterns, increase energy levels, and contribute to a general sense of well-being, ultimately leading to a better quality of life for the individual and improved family dynamics. The primary goal of GI interventions is to improve nutritional status, reduce symptom severity, promote a balanced mood, and increase patient independence.

sheet.es: Si su hijo autista muestra cambios en el apetito, el sueño o el ánimo, vale la pena preguntarse si hay malestar digestivo y comentarlo con su pediatra. Anote qué come, cómo duerme y cuándo parece incómodo, y llévelo a la consulta. La evidencia es una revisión de estudios sobre niños autistas, que indica que los problemas digestivos son frecuentes y que atenderlos puede mejorar el bienestar. Sus límites: es una revisión narrativa del tema, no prueba que el tratamiento digestivo cambie la conducta de cada persona, y las pruebas digestivas no siempre son fiables. Las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If your autistic child shows changes in appetite, sleep or mood, it is worth considering whether digestive discomfort plays a part, and raising it with your paediatrician. Jot down what they eat, how they sleep and when they seem uncomfortable, and bring the notes along. The evidence is a review of studies about autistic children, suggesting that gut problems are common and that addressing them may improve wellbeing. Its limits: it is a broad review, it does not show that treating gut problems changes things for every person, and the abstract notes that GI tests are not always reliable. Medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn har förändringar i aptit, sömn eller humör kan det vara värt att fundera på om magbesvär spelar in och ta upp det med barnläkaren. Skriv ner vad barnet äter, hur det sover och när det verkar må dåligt, och ta med anteckningarna. Underlaget är en översikt av studier om autistiska barn, som tyder på att magproblem är vanliga och att behandling av dem kan förbättra måendet. Begränsningar: det är en bred översikt, den visar inte att det fungerar för alla, och magtester är inte alltid tillförlitliga. Medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker.

title: An internet-based behavioral intervention for adults with autism spectrum disorder - A randomized controlled trial and feasibility study.
authors: Westerberg B, Holländare F, Bejerot S
abstract: Background The increased prevalence of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) diagnoses in combination with psychiatric comorbidity, has led to an increased need for effective interventions. The evidence for internet-based interventions for several mental health problems is established but has not been evaluated for adults with ASD. Objective The aim of this randomized controlled trial is to evaluate the feasibility and effects of an internet-based intervention targeting quality of life and psychiatric symptoms (depression and anxiety) in adults with ASD. Methods 84 participants were randomly allocated to intervention ( n = 42) or control (n = 42). The 18-week internet-based intervention covered a range of themes related to difficulties common in ASD, and exercises based on cognitive behavioral strategies. Participants were provided with individual feedback following each module and were invited to regular chat sessions with peer participants. The primary outcomes were subjective quality of life and sense of coherence, and secondary outcomes were symptoms of depression and anxiety. All outcomes were measured at five occasions and analysed with linear mixed effect models. Participant satisfaction and adherence was also analysed. Results Participant satisfaction and adherence was satisfactory but no significant interaction between group and time was found for any outcome measure. Autistic traits were negatively related to quality of life and sense of coherence and positively related to anxiety and depressive symptoms. Conclusions This internet-based intervention showed feasibility regarding adherence and participant satisfaction. However, no significant effects on quality of life, sense of coherence or psychiatric symptoms were found, likely due to limitations in the design and methodology of this specific trial in combination to the heterogeneity of the group. Individuals with ASD may require interventions that are flexible and individually tailored in regard to both format, content and therapeutic support. The current trial provides useful information and suggestions for the future research on internet-based interventions for ASD.

sheet.es: Si te planteas un programa en línea para una persona adulta autista, conviene buscar uno flexible y adaptado a ella, tanto en formato como en contenido y apoyo. Este ensayo aleatorizado asignó a 84 participantes adultos autistas a un programa de 18 semanas por internet, con ejercicios cognitivo-conductuales, o a un grupo de control. La satisfacción y la participación fueron satisfactorias, pero no se hallaron efectos significativos en calidad de vida, sentido de coherencia, depresión ni ansiedad. Los límites: el diseño y la metodología del ensayo, y la gran diversidad del grupo, pudieron influir. No sirve como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If you are considering an online program for an autistic adult, look for one that is flexible and tailored to the person, in format, content and support. This randomized trial assigned 84 autistic adult participants to an 18-week internet-based program with cognitive behavioral exercises, or to a control group. Satisfaction and adherence were satisfactory, but no significant effects were found on quality of life, sense of coherence, depression or anxiety. Limits: the trial's design and methods, and the wide diversity within the group, may have affected the results. It is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du funderar på ett nätbaserat program för en autistisk vuxen, leta efter ett som är flexibelt och anpassat till personen, både i format, innehåll och stöd. I denna randomiserade studie fördelades 84 autistiska vuxna till ett 18 veckor långt internetbaserat program med kognitiva beteendeövningar eller till en kontrollgrupp. Nöjdheten och följsamheten var tillfredsställande, men inga signifikanta effekter sågs på livskvalitet, känsla av sammanhang, depression eller ångest. Begränsningar: studiens upplägg och metod, samt gruppens stora variation, kan ha påverkat resultaten. Det är ingen regel för varje person.

title: Effects of Parent-Implemented Interventions on Outcomes of Children with Autism: A Meta-Analysis.
authors: Cheng WM, Smith TB, Butler M, Taylor TM, Clayton D
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) have been shown to benefit from parent-implemented interventions (PIIs). This meta-analysis improved on prior reviews of PIIs by evaluating RCTs and multiple potential moderators, including indicators of research quality. Fifty-one effect sizes averaged moderately strong overall benefits of PIIs (g = 0.553), with studies having lower risk of research bias yielding lower estimates (g = 0.47). Parent and observer ratings yielded similar averaged estimates for positive behavior/social skills (g = 0.603), language/communication (g = 0.545), maladaptive behavior (g = 0.519), and to a lesser extent, adaptive behavior/life skills (g = 0.239). No other study, intervention, or participant characteristic moderated outcomes. PIIs with children with ASD tend to be effective across a variety of circumstances.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a un niño autista, las intervenciones en las que las familias aplican las estrategias en casa pueden ser una opción útil, sobre todo para la comunicación y las habilidades sociales. Puedes preguntar a los profesionales cómo practicarlas en la rutina diaria. La evidencia es un metaanálisis de ensayos controlados aleatorizados con 51 tamaños de efecto, que halló beneficios moderadamente fuertes (g = 0.553); los estudios con menor riesgo de sesgo mostraron estimaciones menores (g = 0.47). Límites: son promedios de grupo, no garantizan el resultado en cada niño o familia, y el resumen no detalla qué intervenciones concretas funcionaron mejor ni cuánta carga supone para los padres.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic child, interventions where families use the strategies at home may be a helpful option, especially for communication and social skills. You can ask professionals how to practise them within daily routines. The evidence is a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials with 51 effect sizes, which found moderately strong benefits (g = 0.553); studies with lower risk of bias showed smaller estimates (g = 0.47). Limits: these are group averages, so they cannot promise results for every child or family, and the abstract does not say which specific approaches worked best or how much effort they ask of parents.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar ett autistiskt barn kan insatser där familjen använder strategierna hemma vara ett hjälpsamt alternativ, särskilt för kommunikation och sociala färdigheter. Du kan fråga professionella hur man övar i vardagens rutiner. Underlaget är en metaanalys av randomiserade kontrollerade studier med 51 effektstorlekar, som visade måttligt starka fördelar (g = 0.553); studier med lägre risk för bias gav lägre skattningar (g = 0.47). Begränsningar: det är gruppmedelvärden som inte garanterar resultat för varje barn eller familj, och sammanfattningen anger inte vilka metoder som fungerade bäst eller hur betungande de är för föräldrar.

title: Investigating how Explicit Contextual Cues Affect Predictive Sensorimotor Control in Autistic Adults.
authors: Arthur T, Brosnan M, Harris D, Buckingham G, Wilson M, Williams G, Vine S
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Research suggests that sensorimotor difficulties in autism could be reduced by providing individuals with explicit contextual information. To test this, we examined autistic visuomotor control during a virtual racquetball task, in which participants hit normal and unexpectedly-bouncy balls using a handheld controller. The probability of facing each type of ball was varied unpredictably over time. However, during cued trials, participants received explicit information about the likelihood of facing each uncertain outcome. When compared to neurotypical controls, autistic individuals displayed poorer task performance, atypical gaze profiles, and more restricted swing kinematics. These visuomotor patterns were not significantly affected by contextual cues, indicating that autistic people exhibit underlying differences in how prior information and environmental uncertainty are dynamically modulated during movement tasks.

sheet.es: Avisar con antelación de lo que probablemente va a ocurrir quizá no baste, por sí solo, para facilitar tareas de movimiento y coordinación con situaciones inesperadas. Conviene combinarlo con práctica, tiempo y apoyos que la persona elija. Es un estudio con personas autistas adultas que, en un juego virtual de raquetbol, golpeaban pelotas normales y otras inesperadamente rebotadoras, con y sin información explícita sobre su probabilidad. Las personas autistas rindieron peor que el grupo de comparación, miraron de otro modo y movieron el brazo de forma más restringida, y las pistas no cambiaron esto de forma significativa. Es una sola tarea virtual con adultos: no sirve como regla para cada persona ni para la vida diaria.
sheet.en: Warning someone in advance about what is likely to happen may not be enough, on its own, to make movement and coordination easier when things are unexpected. It may help to combine it with practice, time and supports the person chooses. This was a study with autistic adults who played a virtual racquetball game, hitting normal balls and unexpectedly bouncy ones, with and without explicit information about how likely each was. Autistic participants performed less well than the comparison group, looked at the task differently and moved their swing in a more restricted way. The cues did not change this significantly. It was one virtual task with adults, so it is not a rule for every person or for everyday life.
sheet.sv: Att varna i förväg om vad som sannolikt kommer att hända räcker kanske inte ensamt för att göra rörelser och koordination lättare när något oväntat inträffar. Det kan hjälpa att kombinera det med övning, tid och stöd som personen själv väljer. Det här var en studie med autistiska vuxna som spelade virtuell racquetball och slog normala bollar och oväntat studsiga bollar, med och utan tydlig information om hur troligt varje slag var. De autistiska deltagarna presterade sämre än jämförelsegruppen, tittade annorlunda och hade en mer begränsad svingrörelse. Ledtrådarna ändrade inte detta signifikant. Det var en enda virtuell uppgift med vuxna, så resultatet är ingen regel för varje person eller för vardagen.

title: Emotional dysregulation as a part of the autism spectrum continuum: a literature review from late childhood to adulthood.
authors: Dell'Osso L, Massoni L, Battaglini S, De Felice C, Nardi B, Amatori G, Cremone IM, Carpita B
abstract: The concept of emotional dysregulation (ED) has recently gained interest in the scientific literature and is commonly defined as the inability to use the modulatory mechanisms involved in emotion regulation, resulting in a functioning meaningfully below the baseline. Even though the data available are still limited, an increasing number of studies have hypothesized a promoting role for some of the core features of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in the development of ED, in particular being repetitive behaviors, social difficulties and alexythimia. In this framework, the purpose of this study was to review the literature that is currently available about presence and correlates of ED in young adults with autism spectrum conditions as well as to offer some insights about possible implications for illness trajectories. The data reported seems to point to a shared etiology between ED and repetitive/restricted ASD symptoms, with perseveration features serving as the foundation for the inability to control one's emotions. In this context, a neurodevelopmental basis for ED could be consistent with the transnosographic conceptualization of ASD, which hypothesizes a potential neurodevelopmental basis for several psychiatric disorders, whose autistic traits would be the phenotypical presentation.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista se desborda emocionalmente, conviene mirar qué ocurre alrededor: cambios, rutinas interrumpidas, dificultad para poner nombre a lo que siente. Ofrecer calma, previsibilidad y apoyo para identificar emociones puede ayudar. La evidencia es una revisión de la literatura sobre la desregulación emocional en autistas desde la infancia tardía hasta la adultez. Sugiere un vínculo con conductas repetitivas, dificultades sociales y alexitimia. Sus límites: los datos todavía son limitados, hablan de hipótesis y no describen a todas las personas autistas ni prueban causas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person becomes emotionally overwhelmed, look at what is happening around them: changes, interrupted routines, difficulty putting feelings into words. Offering calm, predictability and support to name emotions may help. The evidence is a review of the literature on emotional dysregulation in autistic people from late childhood to adulthood. It suggests links with repetitive behaviours, social difficulties and alexithymia. Its limits: the available data are still limited, the findings are hypotheses, and they do not describe every autistic person or prove causes.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person blir känslomässigt överväldigad, titta på vad som händer runt omkring: förändringar, avbrutna rutiner, svårigheter att sätta ord på känslor. Lugn, förutsägbarhet och stöd att namnge känslor kan hjälpa. Underlaget är en litteraturöversikt om emotionell dysreglering hos autistiska personer från sen barndom till vuxenliv. Den antyder samband med repetitiva beteenden, sociala svårigheter och alexitymi. Begränsningar: data är fortfarande begränsade, resultaten är hypoteser och beskriver inte alla autistiska personer eller bevisar orsaker.

title: Community-based care for autistic youth: community providers' reported use of treatment practices in the United States.
authors: Drahota A, Sridhar A, Moskowitz LJ, Kerns CM, Soorya L, Wainer A, Cohn E, Lerner MD
abstract: Introduction To illustrate the landscape of community-based care for autistic youth in the United States, we identified transdisciplinary psychosocial intervention practice sets that community providers report utilizing to care for this population, and examined characteristics associated with provider-reported utilization. Methods The Usual Care for Autism Study (UCAS) Survey assessed provider demographics and provider-reported use of transdisciplinary practices for common ASD co-occurring problems: social difficulties, externalizing behaviors, and anxiety. Community practitioners ( N = 701) from allied health, behavioral, education, medical, mental health and other disciplines who treat or work with autistic youth (7-22 years) participated. Results Exploratory factor analysis yielded four factors: Consequence-Based Strategies (CBS), Cognitive-Behavioral and Therapy Strategies (CBTS), Antecedent-Based Strategies (ABS), and Teaching Strategies (TS). Providers across disciplines reported utilizing ABS more often than other sets. Providers from behavioral disciplines, with less than 4-year or Master degrees, or with more experience reported the most use of ABS, CBS and CBTS. Medical and behavioral providers reported the most use of TS. Setting and child characteristics were associated with practice set use, indicating variability by disability and client socioeconomic status. Discussion Findings reflect the complexity and inconsistency of the service landscape for autistic youth across the U.S. Only by understanding the service landscape and predictors of practice utilization, can researchers, policymakers, provider groups, and the autistic community facilitate effective implementation strategy development and use to ultimately improve community-based care.

sheet.es: Al buscar apoyo para una persona autista joven, pregunte a cada profesional qué estrategias usa y por qué, porque la práctica varía mucho entre servicios. Es un estudio con una encuesta a 701 profesionales de distintas disciplinas que trabajan con jóvenes autistas de 7-22 años en Estados Unidos. Las estrategias basadas en los antecedentes fueron las más usadas en todas las disciplinas. Límites: se basa en lo que los profesionales dicen que hacen, no mide si funciona ni qué opinan las personas autistas, y puede no reflejar su situación.
sheet.en: When looking for support for an autistic young person, ask each professional which strategies they use and why, because practice varies a lot between services. This was a survey of 701 professionals from different disciplines who work with autistic youth aged 7-22 in the United States. Antecedent-based strategies were the ones used most often across disciplines. Limits: it relies on what professionals say they do, does not show whether the strategies work or what autistic people think of them, and may not match your situation.
sheet.sv: När du söker stöd åt en ung autistisk person kan du fråga varje yrkesperson vilka strategier hen använder och varför, eftersom praxis varierar mycket mellan verksamheter. Det var en enkätstudie med 701 yrkespersoner från olika discipliner som arbetar med autistiska ungdomar i åldern 7-22 i USA. Strategier som bygger på förändringar i miljön före en situation användes oftast i alla discipliner. Begränsningar: studien bygger på vad yrkespersonerna själva säger att de gör, visar inte om strategierna fungerar eller vad autistiska personer tycker, och stämmer kanske inte med din situation.

title: Tract- and gray matter- based spatial statistics show white matter and gray matter microstructural differences in autistic males.
authors: DiPiero M, Cordash H, Prigge MB, King CK, Morgan J, Guerrero-Gonzalez J, Adluru N, King JB, Lange N, Bigler ED, Zielinski BA, Alexander AL, Lainhart JE, Dean DC
abstract: Background Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition commonly studied in the context of early childhood. As ASD is a life-long condition, understanding the characteristics of brain microstructure from adolescence into adulthood and associations to clinical features is critical for improving outcomes across the lifespan. In the current work, we utilized Tract Based Spatial Statistics (TBSS) and Gray Matter Based Spatial Statistics (GBSS) to examine the white matter (WM) and gray matter (GM) microstructure in neurotypical (NT) and autistic males. Methods Multi-shell diffusion MRI was acquired from 78 autistic and 81 NT males (12-to-46-years) and fit to the DTI and NODDI diffusion models. TBSS and GBSS were performed to analyze WM and GM microstructure, respectively. General linear models were used to investigate group and age-related group differences. Within the ASD group, relationships between WM and GM microstructure and measures of autistic symptoms were investigated. Results All dMRI measures were significantly associated with age across WM and GM. Significant group differences were observed across WM and GM. No significant age-by-group interactions were detected. Within the ASD group, positive relationships with WM microstructure were observed with ADOS-2 Calibrated Severity Scores. Conclusion Using TBSS and GBSS our findings provide new insights into group differences of WM and GM microstructure in autistic males from adolescence into adulthood. Detection of microstructural differences across the lifespan as well as their relationship to the level of autistic symptoms will deepen to our understanding of brain-behavior relationships of ASD and may aid in the improvement of intervention options for autistic adults.

sheet.es: Este estudio no ofrece nada que cambiar mañana en casa: describe diferencias medias en el cerebro, no necesidades de una persona concreta. Si buscas apoyos, parte de lo que la persona dice y muestra que necesita. Evidencia: estudio con resonancia magnética en 78 varones autistas y 81 varones neurotípicos, de 12 a 46 años. Encontró diferencias de grupo en la microestructura cerebral, y no detectó interacciones significativas entre edad y grupo. Límites: solo incluyó varones, midió un único momento y no muestra causas ni sirve para valorar a una persona individual.
sheet.en: This study gives nothing to change at home tomorrow: it describes average brain differences, not what one person needs. If you are looking for supports, start from what the person tells and shows you they need. Evidence: an MRI study of 78 autistic males and 81 neurotypical males, aged 12-to-46 years. It found group differences in brain microstructure, and no significant age-by-group interactions. Limits: it included only males, measured a single point in time, and shows neither causes nor anything that can assess an individual person.
sheet.sv: Studien ger inget att ändra hemma i morgon: den beskriver genomsnittliga skillnader i hjärnan, inte vad en enskild person behöver. Om du söker stöd, utgå från vad personen själv säger och visar att hen behöver. Evidens: en MRI-studie med 78 autistiska och 81 neurotypiska män, 12 till 46 år. Den fann gruppskillnader i hjärnans mikrostruktur och inga signifikanta samspel mellan ålder och grupp. Begränsningar: den omfattade bara män, mätte vid ett tillfälle och visar varken orsaker eller något som kan bedöma en enskild person.

title: Linehan's biosocial model applied to emotion dysregulation in autism: a narrative review of the literature and an illustrative case conceptualization.
authors: Bemmouna D, Weiner L
abstract: Emotion dysregulation (ED) is a transdiagnostic difficulty prevalent in autism spectrum condition (ASC). Importantly, recent research has suggested that ED is involved in self-harm and suicidality. Pre-existing models on the etiology of ED in ASC focus mainly on biological factors to ASC features, such as sensory sensitivities, poor flexibility, and sensitivity to change. However, although psychosocial factors seem to play a role in the emergence of ED in ASC as well (e.g., childhood maltreatment and camouflaging), there is a lack of a comprehensive model conceptualizing biosocial factors involved in ED in autistic people. Linehan's biosocial model (1993) is one of the leading etiological models of ED in borderline personality disorder (BPD). It conceptualizes ED as emerging from transactions between a pre-existing emotional vulnerability in the child and an invalidating developmental environment. Beyond its clinical relevance, Linehan's model has gathered empirical evidence supporting its pertinence in BPD and in other psychiatric disorders. Although ASC and BPD are two distinct diagnoses, because they may share ED, Linehan's biosocial model might be useful for understanding the development of ED in ASC. Hence, this article aims to provide an application and extension of Linehan's model to conceptualize ED in ASC. To do so, we conducted a narrative review of the literature on ED and its underlying factors in ASC from a developmental perspective. To investigate the pertinence of the biosocial model applied to ED in autistic people, we were interested on data on (i) ED and its behavioral correlates in ASC, in relation to the biosocial model, (ii) the potential biological and psychosocial correlates of ED in ASC and (iii) the overlapping difficulties in ASC and BPD. Finally, to assess the pertinence of the model, we applied it to the case of an autistic woman presenting with ED and suicidal behaviors. Our review and application to the case of an autistic woman suggest that ED in ASC encompasses factors related to both biological and psychosocial risk factors as conceptualized in the BPD framework, although in both domains ASC-specific factors might be involved.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista tiene emociones muy intensas y difíciles de regular, conviene mirar tanto sus rasgos de base (por ejemplo, sensibilidades sensoriales) como el entorno: sentirse invalidada o tener que camuflarse puede pesar mucho. Validar lo que siente ayuda a empezar. La evidencia es una revisión narrativa de la literatura, aplicada a un solo caso ilustrativo de una mujer autista con conductas suicidas. No prueba causas ni vale para todas las personas, y es una propuesta de modelo. Si le preocupan las autolesiones o el suicidio, busque ayuda profesional: un clínico, un servicio de salud o un servicio de crisis. Ante peligro inmediato, llame al número de emergencias de su país.
sheet.en: If an autistic person has intense emotions that are hard to regulate, it helps to look at both their built-in traits (such as sensory sensitivities) and their surroundings: feeling invalidated or having to camouflage can weigh heavily. Validating what they feel is a good place to start. The evidence is a narrative review of the literature, applied to one illustrative case of an autistic woman with suicidal behaviors. It does not prove causes, is a proposed model, and does not apply to every person. If you are worried about self-harm or suicide, seek professional help: a clinician, a health service or a crisis service. In immediate danger, call the emergency number of your country.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person har starka känslor som är svåra att reglera hjälper det att se både personens grundläggande drag (till exempel sensoriska känsligheter) och omgivningen: att känna sig invaliderad eller behöva maskera kan väga tungt. Att bekräfta det personen känner är en bra början. Underlaget är en narrativ översikt av litteraturen, tillämpad på ett enda illustrativt fall av en autistisk kvinna med suicidala beteenden. Den visar inte orsaker, är ett förslag på modell och gäller inte alla personer. Om du är orolig för självskada eller självmord, sök professionell hjälp: en kliniker, vården eller en krisjour. Vid akut fara, ring ditt lands nödnummer.

title: A randomised controlled trial of clinical and cost-effectiveness of the PASS Plus intervention for young children with autism spectrum disorder in New Delhi, India: study protocol for the COMPASS trial.
authors: Roy R, Leadbitter K, Shields G, Taylor C, Aldred C, Juneja M, Gulati S, Vajaratkar V, Davies L, Emsley R, Patel V, Divan G, Green J, COMPASS team
abstract: Background Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disability affecting at least 5 million children in South Asia. Majority of these children are without access to evidence-based care. The UK Pre-school Autism Communication Therapy (PACT) is the only intervention to have shown sustained impact on autism symptoms. It was systematically adapted for non-specialist community delivery in South Asia, as the 'Parent-mediated Autism Social Communication Intervention for non-Specialists (PASS)' and extended 'PASS Plus' interventions. RCTs of both showed feasibility, acceptability and positive effect on parent and child dyadic outcomes. Methods The Communication-centred Parent-mediated treatment for Autism Spectrum Disorder in South Asia (COMPASS) trial is now a scale-up two-centre, two-arm single (rater) blinded random allocation parallel group study of the PASS Plus intervention in addition to treatment as usual (TAU) compared to TAU alone, plus health economic evaluation embedded in the India health system. Two hundred forty children (approximately 120 intervention/120 TAU) with ASD aged 2-9 years will be recruited from two tertiary care government hospitals in New Delhi, India. Accredited Social Health Activists will be one of the intervention delivery agents. Families will undertake up to 12 communication sessions over 8 months and will be offered the Plus modules which address coexisting problems. The trial's primary endpoint is at 9 months from randomisation, with follow-up at 15 months. The primary outcome is autism symptom severity; secondary outcomes include parent-child communication, child adaptation, quality of life and parental wellbeing. Primary analysis will follow intention-to-treat principles using linear mixed model regressions with group allocation and repeated measures as random effects. The cost-effectiveness analysis will use a societal perspective over the 15-month period of intervention and follow-up. Discussion If clinically and cost-effective, this programme will fill an important gap of scalable interventions delivered by non-specialist health workers within the current care pathways for autistic children and their families in low-resource contexts. The programme has been implemented through the COVID-19 pandemic when restrictions were in place; intervention delivery and evaluation processes have been adapted to address these conditions. Trial registration ISRCTN; ISRCTN21454676 ; Registered 22 June 2018.

title: Psychiatric conditions in autistic adolescents: longitudinal stability from childhood and associated risk factors.
authors: Hollocks MJ, Leno VC, Chandler S, White P, Yorke I, Charman T, Pickles A, Baird G, Simonoff E
abstract: Autistic people experience high rates of co-occurring psychiatric diagnoses. Current prevalence estimates vary considerably due to an over-reliance on clinical cohorts and the longitudinal stability of diagnoses from childhood into adolescence is poorly understood. This study aims to provide prevalence rates of co-occurring DSM-5 psychiatric diagnosis for autistic adolescence and investigate, for the first time, the stability of diagnoses from childhood.
