Las personas autistas contaron más vivencias sensoriales y físicas intensas, más depresión y ansiedad prenatales, y menor satisfacción con la atención prenatal. Sus límites: es una encuesta, muestra asociaciones y no sirve como regla para cada persona. Si hay síntomas de depresión o ansiedad, conviene consultarlo con profesionales sanitarios.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person during pregnancy, ask ahead of time which sensory and communication adjustments would help at appointments and antenatal classes, and request them from the healthcare team. This was an online survey of 417 autistic and 524 non-autistic people. Autistic people reported heightened sensory and physical experiences, more prenatal depression and anxiety, and lower satisfaction with prenatal healthcare. Limits: a survey shows associations only and is not a rule for every person. If depression or anxiety are a worry, a healthcare professional can help.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person under graviditeten: fråga i förväg vilka sensoriska anpassningar och kommunikationsanpassningar som skulle hjälpa vid besök och föräldraklasser, och be vårdteamet om dem. Det var en webbenkät med 417 autistiska och 524 icke-autistiska personer. De autistiska deltagarna rapporterade starkare sensoriska och fysiska upplevelser, mer depression och ångest under graviditeten och lägre nöjdhet med mödravården. Begränsning: en enkät visar samband och är ingen regel för varje person. Om du oroar dig för depression eller ångest kan vårdpersonal hjälpa till.

title: Children with autism spectrum disorder in high technology medicine environments; a qualitative systematic review of parental perspectives.
authors: Pettersson E, Christensen BM, Berglund IG, Nylander E, Huus K
abstract: Background Children with autism spectrum disorders are frequent visitors to high technology environments, and their needs may differ from those of their typically developed peers. Procedures in high technology environments can constitute a challenge for these children and their parents since the environment presents many challenges relevant to the child's impairments. This systematic review aimed to explore the experiences of children with autism spectrum disorders and their parents during procedures in a high technology environment. Methods The following sources were searched for this systematic review: Cochrane CENTRAL Trials, CINAHL, Dentistry and Oral Sciences Source, MEDLINE, PsycINFO, Scopus, and Web of Science Core Collection. The search terms included variants of the following concepts: (1) children with autism spectrum disorder and/or their parents and (2) anesthesia or radiographic departments. Publications were not limited by date or study design. Result Out of 13,389 bibliographic records, nine studies were eligible for synthesis. After another search in October 2022, one additional study was eligible for synthesis.None of the studies reported children's experiences, and all ten reported their parents' experiences. Only one study was conducted in a radiographic context. Parents' experiences were both positive and negative and were categorized into two main categories: (1) challenges in a new environment and (2) health care professionals' approaches. Conclusion Studies describing children's experiences with procedures in high technology environments are lacking. The parents described a need for health care professionals to work in structured ways with their child and to be able to make suitable adaptations. Systematic review registration This systematic review was registered in advance on the Open Science Framework, https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/5TXWJ .

sheet.es: Antes de una intervención o prueba en un hospital, cuente al equipo sanitario qué necesita su hijo autista y pídales una forma de trabajar estructurada y adaptaciones concretas. Es una revisión sistemática de diez estudios con las experiencias de madres y padres en entornos médicos de alta tecnología, como anestesia o radiología. Las experiencias fueron positivas y negativas, y se centraron en los retos de un entorno nuevo y en cómo actúa el personal. Ningún estudio recogió la voz de los niños y solo uno se hizo en radiología, así que no sabemos cómo lo viven ellos ni si esto sirve para todas las personas.
sheet.en: Before a hospital procedure or scan, tell the health care team what your autistic child needs, and ask for a structured way of working and specific adaptations. This is a systematic review of ten studies on parents' experiences in high technology medical settings, such as anesthesia or radiology. Experiences were both positive and negative, centred on the challenges of a new environment and on how staff approached the child. No study reported the children's own experiences, and only one took place in radiology, so we do not know how children see it or whether this fits every person.
sheet.sv: Inför en undersökning eller ett ingrepp på sjukhus: berätta för vårdteamet vad ditt autistiska barn behöver och be om ett strukturerat arbetssätt och konkreta anpassningar. Detta är en systematisk översikt av tio studier om föräldrars erfarenheter i högteknologisk vård, till exempel anestesi eller röntgen. Erfarenheterna var både positiva och negativa och handlade om utmaningar i en ny miljö och om hur personalen bemötte barnet. Ingen studie beskrev barnens egna upplevelser och bara en gjordes inom röntgen, så vi vet inte hur barnen upplever det eller om det gäller alla.

title: The lived experiences of relatives of autistic adults, and their perceptions of their relationships with autistic adults across multiple age-related transitions and demands: A qualitative interview study with reflexive thematic analysis.
authors: Hamilton J, Finch T, Le Couteur A, Mackintosh J, Petrou A, Garland D, Parr JR
abstract: Background There is a need to better understand autism across the life course, including the lives of both autistic people and supporting relatives. As part of a larger mixed methods cohort study involving autistic adults, carers and relatives this sub-study focused on the experiences of relatives alone to learn more about the lives of people from the wider personal networks. Our research questions were: 1. What are the experiences of family members who care for and/or support autistic adults, 2. How can the viewpoints of relatives add to what we know about transitions and challenges experienced by autistic adults, and 3. What strategies/support have been helpful for adults and relatives? Methods Relatives of autistic adults were purposively sampled and recruited using the Relatives/Carers cohort from the Adult Autism Spectrum Cohort-UK. 18 participants aged 31-81years who were related to 16 autistic adults aged 18-57years were interviewed for 24-91minutes. Interview transcripts were examined using reflexive thematic analysis. Main findings Two overarching themes were developed, 'Family support goes a long way in caring for autistic adults' and 'When families turn to society for support' with subthemes. Relatives described benefits they had gained and their admiration for autistic adults. They reflected on how they gave support for independence in various contexts of dependence. They also identified the challenges that both autistic adults and families face navigating support systems (for example for healthcare and employment). An important novel outcome was the advocated value of role-models with lived experience who come from outside of the family. Recommendations The findings lead to recommendations for: (i) Strategies to reduce the barriers for support that are faced by autistic individuals and relatives during crisis points; (ii) recognition and support for what enables both relatives and autistic adults to function independently (e.g. funded activities, flexible employment); (iii) future planning conversations to include relatives who can enhance knowledge and help plan for future care or support needs for autistic adults and (iv) opportunities for role models (persons with lived experience, autistic adults and relatives) to inspire others and disseminate knowledge. Conclusions These findings add valuable insights into the experiences of relatives of autistic adults and challenge the reader to have greater appreciation of the many roles relatives can contribute across time and in a variety of contexts. These perspectives add important information for those working with and planning provision for autistic adults.

sheet.es: Si apoyas a un adulto autista, puede ayudar incluir a la familia en las conversaciones sobre el futuro y buscar modelos a seguir con experiencia propia, fuera de la familia, como otras personas autistas o familiares. Evidencia: entrevistas con 18 familiares de entre 31-81 años, que estaban relacionados con 16 adultos autistas de 18-57 años, analizadas de forma temática. Contaron beneficios, admiración y dificultades para acceder a apoyos como salud y empleo. Límites: son vivencias de pocas personas en el Reino Unido, no hablan por los propios adultos autistas y no valen para todas las familias.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult, it may help to include family in conversations about the future and to look for role models with lived experience from outside the family, such as other autistic adults or relatives. Evidence: interviews with 18 relatives aged 31-81years, related to 16 autistic adults aged 18-57years, analysed thematically. They described benefits, admiration, and difficulty getting support such as healthcare and employment. Limits: these are the views of a small group in the UK, they do not speak for autistic adults themselves, and they will not fit every family.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen kan det hjälpa att ta med familjen i samtal om framtiden och att söka förebilder med egen erfarenhet utanför familjen, till exempel andra autistiska vuxna eller anhöriga. Evidens: intervjuer med 18 anhöriga i åldern 31-81 år, släkt med 16 autistiska vuxna i åldern 18-57 år, analyserade tematiskt. De berättade om fördelar, beundran och svårigheter att få stöd, till exempel inom vård och arbete. Begränsningar: det är en liten grupp i Storbritannien, de talar inte för de autistiska vuxna själva och det passar inte alla familjer.

title: Compassion focused therapy for self-stigma and shame in autism: a single case pre-experimental study.
authors: Riebel M, Krasny-Pacini A, Manolov R, Rohmer O, Weiner L
abstract: Introduction Exposure to public stigma can lead to the internalization of autism-related stigma (i.e., self-stigma), associated with negative health, occupational and social outcomes. Importantly, self-stigma is linked to shame and social isolation. Although elevated self-stigma has been reported in autistic adults, to the best of our knowledge, interventions designed to target this issue are lacking. Compassion is an effective way to reduce the emotional correlates of self-stigma (i.e., shame) and their impacts on mental health. However, no study has investigated whether compassion focused therapy (CFT) can effectively reduce self-stigma in autistic adults. The present study aims at investigating whether and how self-compassion improvement following CFT may reduce self-stigma and shame in an autistic individual. Methods A single case pre-experimental design (SCED) was used with weekly repeated measures during four phases: (i) pure baseline without any intervention (A), (ii) case conceptualization (A'), (iii) intervention (B) where CFT was delivered, (iv) follow-up without intervention (FU). The participant is a 46-year-old autistic man with high self-stigma and shame. Self-report measures of self-compassion and self-stigma and a daily idiographic measure of shame were used. Results There was a large increase in self-compassion between pure baseline (A) and the intervention phase (A'B) (Tau-U = 0.99), maintained at follow-up. Similarly, there was a moderate decrease of self-stigma (Tau-U = 0.32). In contrast, when we compared the whole baseline phase AA' (i.e., considering the conceptualisation phase as baseline) to the intervention (B), there was no change in self-stigma (Tau-U = -0.09). There was no change in self-stigma between the intervention (B) and follow-up (Tau-U = -0.19). There was a moderate decrease in daily shame reports between the baseline (AA') and the intervention (B) (Tau-U = 0.31) and a moderate decrease between the pure baseline (A) and intervention phase (A'B) (Tau-U = 0.51). Conclusion CFT was feasible for this autistic client and our results show that CFT led to the improvement of self-compassion. Changes on self-stigma measures were moderate. Self-stigma may need more time to change. Because self-stigma is involved in poorer social functioning and mental health in autistic adults, our results are promising and suggesting conducting more large-scale studies on CFT in autistic adults.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista siente vergüenza o se juzga con dureza por ser autista, puede ayudar ofrecerle espacios de trato amable hacia sí misma y no esperar cambios rápidos. Es un estudio de caso único con un solo participante: un hombre autista de 46 años con mucha autoestigma y vergüenza. Tras una terapia centrada en la compasión, su autocompasión aumentó mucho y se mantuvo en el seguimiento; la vergüenza diaria y el autoestigma bajaron de forma moderada, aunque según la comparación el autoestigma no cambió. Con una sola persona no se puede generalizar, y hacen falta estudios más amplios. Cualquier decisión terapéutica conviene hablarla con un profesional.
sheet.en: If an autistic person feels shame or judges themselves harshly for being autistic, it may help to offer room for kind self-treatment, without expecting quick change. This was a single-case study with one participant: a 46-year-old autistic man with high self-stigma and shame. After compassion focused therapy, his self-compassion rose a lot and stayed up at follow-up; daily shame and self-stigma fell moderately, though depending on the comparison self-stigma did not change. One person cannot represent everyone, and larger studies are needed. Talk over any therapy decisions with a professional.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person känner skam eller dömer sig hårt för att vara autistisk kan det hjälpa att ge utrymme för vänlighet mot sig själv, utan att vänta sig snabb förändring. Det var en enfallsstudie med en deltagare: en autistisk man på 46 år med hög självstigma och skam. Efter compassionfokuserad terapi ökade hans självmedkänsla mycket och höll i sig vid uppföljningen; daglig skam och självstigma minskade måttligt, men beroende på jämförelsen förändrades självstigmat inte. En person kan inte representera alla, och större studier behövs. Prata med en professionell om beslut kring terapi.

title: Incidence of Otolaryngological Manifestations in Individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Special Focus on Auditory Disorders.
authors: McKenna K, Prasad S, Cooper J, King AM, Shahzeidi S, Mittal J, Zalta M, Mittal R, Eshraghi AA
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by stereotyped and repetitive behavior patterns. In addition to neurological and behavioral problems, individuals with ASD commonly experience otolaryngological comorbidities. Individuals with ASD often have auditory disorders including hearing loss and auditory processing disorders such as central auditory processing disorder (CAPD), as well as both chronic and recurrent otitis media. These challenges negatively impact a person's ability to effectively communicate and may further impact their neurological functioning, particularly when not appropriately treated. Individuals diagnosed with ASD also have difficulty sleeping which contributes to increased irritability and may further aggravate the core behavioral symptoms of autism. The individuals with ASD also have a higher rate of sinusitis which contributes to the worsening of the autism behavior phenotype. The high prevalence of otolaryngological comorbidities in individuals with ASD warrants a better collaboration between their various healthcare providers and otolaryngologists with expertise in auditory, sleep, and sinus disorders in pursuit of improving the quality of life of affected individuals and their families/caregivers.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista tiene dificultades para comunicarse, duerme mal o se irrita con frecuencia, puede valer la pena preguntar a su equipo de salud por una revisión de oído, sueño y senos nasales (otorrinolaringología). Estas causas a veces pasan desapercibidas. Se trata de una revisión de la literatura que describe que los problemas auditivos, las otitis, las dificultades de sueño y la sinusitis aparecen con frecuencia en personas autistas. El resumen no indica cuántas personas participaron ni cifras concretas, y no demuestra que ocurra en cada persona. Cualquier decisión médica corresponde a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If an autistic person has trouble communicating, sleeps badly or is often irritable, it may be worth asking their health team about checking hearing, sleep and sinuses (ear, nose and throat care). These causes can go unnoticed. This is a review of the literature, describing that hearing problems, ear infections, sleep difficulties and sinusitis appear often in autistic people. The abstract gives no number of participants or specific figures, and it does not show this applies to every person. Any medical decision belongs to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person har svårt att kommunicera, sover dåligt eller ofta är irriterad kan det vara värt att fråga vårdteamet om en kontroll av hörsel, sömn och bihålor (öron-, näs- och halsvård). Dessa orsaker kan förbises. Detta är en översikt av litteraturen som beskriver att hörselproblem, öroninflammationer, sömnsvårigheter och bihåleinflammation är vanliga hos autistiska personer. Sammanfattningen anger inte antal deltagare eller exakta siffror, och visar inte att det gäller varje person. Medicinska beslut hör till en läkare eller annan klinisk personal.

title: Integrated Life Skills Training and Executive Function Strategies in Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder in Qatar: A Pilot Study of a Randomized Controlled Trial.
authors: Yousef BM, Bhaskar Raj N, Nadiah WA, Dhas BN, Mansour AM, Abd Alhadi SA, Rosal FV, Dizon MM
abstract: Background and aim Executive function (EF) impairment is common in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). EF strategies are considered effective in improving the therapeutic outcomes of children with ASD. This study primarily aimed to explore whether integrating EF strategies combined with regular occupational therapy intervention is more effective in improving daily life skills (DLS) and sensory integration/processing (SI/SP) skills than regular occupational therapy alone in children with ASD and secondarily aims to assess treatment outcomes on improving visual motor integration (VMI) skills. Methods A total of 17 participants (13 males, mean age 4.29 years, standard deviation 0.66) completed the study. Following the baseline assessments, the participants were randomly assigned to the treatment group (45-minute once-weekly individual occupational therapy plus EF strategies) or control group (45-minute once-weekly individual therapy sessions alone). All participants received one intervention per week for 14 weeks. All children were systematically evaluated using a pediatric functional independent measure (WeeFIM) and the Verbal Behavior Milestones Assessment and Placement Program (VB-MAPP) to assess DLS, the Short Sensory Profile 2 (SSP2) to assess SP/SI, and the Beery VMI test (Beery VMI) to assess VMI. Assessments were conducted at baseline, seven weeks, and 14 weeks of treatment. Results The analysis of the results between the treatment and control groups revealed that the treatment group had greater gains and significant differences in the mean values of both the WeeFIM and SSP2. In addition, notable distinctions were observed in the VB-MAPP transition subscale; although these differences did not reach statistical significance, they were clinically significant. Minimal differences were noted in the VMI between the two groups. Nevertheless, both groups showed statistically significant improvements across all outcome measures. Conclusions Our study provides preliminary evidence of the efficacy of EF strategies combined with regular occupational therapy for DLS, SP/SI, and VMI in children with ASD. The differences between the groups support further evaluation of the effectiveness of EF strategies for the next stage of a larger randomized clinical trial.

sheet.es: Si su hijo recibe terapia ocupacional, puede preguntar al terapeuta si es posible añadir estrategias de función ejecutiva (por ejemplo, apoyos para organizar y planificar las rutinas diarias). Es un ensayo piloto aleatorizado en Catar con 17 niños autistas, con una edad media de 4.29 años. Durante 14 semanas, un grupo recibió terapia ocupacional con estas estrategias y otro solo terapia ocupacional. El primer grupo mejoró más en habilidades de la vida diaria y en procesamiento sensorial, pero ambos grupos mejoraron. Es un estudio muy pequeño y preliminar, y no demuestra que funcione igual para cada persona.
sheet.en: If your child has occupational therapy, you could ask the therapist whether executive function strategies, such as supports for organising and planning daily routines, could be added. This was a pilot randomized trial in Qatar with 17 autistic children, mean age 4.29 years. For 14 weeks, one group had occupational therapy with these strategies and the other had occupational therapy alone. The first group improved more in daily life skills and sensory processing, though both groups improved. The study is very small and preliminary, and it does not show the same result for every child.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn går i arbetsterapi kan du fråga terapeuten om strategier för exekutiva funktioner, till exempel stöd för att organisera och planera vardagsrutiner, kan läggas till. Det här var en randomiserad pilotstudie i Qatar med 17 autistiska barn, medelålder 4.29 år. Under 14 veckor fick en grupp arbetsterapi med dessa strategier och en annan enbart arbetsterapi. Den första gruppen förbättrades mer i vardagsfärdigheter och sensorisk bearbetning, men båda grupperna förbättrades. Studien är mycket liten och preliminär, och visar inte att resultatet gäller för varje barn.

title: Psychosocial therapeutic approaches for high-functioning autistic adults.
authors: Schweizer T, Endres D, Dziobek I, Tebartz van Elst L
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is characterized by impaired social interaction and communication skills, repetitive behaviors, restricted interests, and specific sensory processing. Particularly, adults with high-functioning ASD often remain unrecognized, presumably due to their high compensatory skills, but at the cost of high stress, which is often linked to anxiety and depression. This may further explain the significantly high suicide rates and reduced life expectancy among individuals with ASD. Thus, providing support to high-functioning autistic adults in managing core symptoms, as well as co-occurring anxiety and depression, appears essential. To date, only a limited number of evidence-based psychosocial therapeutic options are available, and very few of them have undergone rigorous evaluation in a clinical context. To obtain a comprehensive understanding, a systematic literature search was conducted according to the PRISMA checklist, and only studies demonstrating robust methodological quality were included and discussed in this review article. Although promising initial key factors and methods have been identified, additional evidence-based studies are imperative to ascertain the optimal treatment and evaluate the long-term outcomes for adults with high-functioning ASD.

sheet.es: Si cuidas o acompañas a una persona autista adulta, considera que el estrés mantenido por compensar puede relacionarse con ansiedad y depresión, y que apoyar ese malestar importa. Hablar con un profesional de salud sobre opciones psicosociales puede ser un buen paso. La evidencia es una revisión sistemática de estudios de buena calidad metodológica sobre terapias psicosociales en adultos autistas. Sus límites: hay pocas opciones con evidencia, pocas evaluadas en contextos clínicos, y faltan estudios sobre resultados a largo plazo; no sirve como regla para todas las personas. El abstract menciona tasas altas de suicidio. Si tú o alguien cercano pensáis en hacerse daño, buscad ayuda profesional en un servicio de salud o de crisis; si hay peligro inmediato, llamad al número de emergencias de vuestro país.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult, keep in mind that the ongoing stress of compensating can be linked to anxiety and depression, and that supporting that distress matters. Talking with a health professional about psychosocial options can be a good step. The evidence is a systematic review of studies with solid methodological quality on psychosocial therapies for autistic adults. Its limits: few options have evidence, few were tested in clinical settings, and long-term outcomes are still unknown; it is not a rule for every person. The abstract notes high suicide rates. If you or someone close thinks about self-harm, seek professional help from a clinician, health service or crisis service; in immediate danger, call your country's emergency number.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen: tänk på att den ständiga stressen av att kompensera kan hänga ihop med ångest och depression, och att stöd vid det måendet är viktigt. Att prata med vårdpersonal om psykosociala alternativ kan vara ett bra steg. Underlaget är en systematisk översikt av studier med god metodologisk kvalitet om psykosociala terapier för autistiska vuxna. Begränsningar: få alternativ har stöd i evidens, få har prövats i kliniska miljöer och långtidsresultat saknas; det är ingen regel för alla. Sammanfattningen nämner höga självmordstal. Om du eller någon nära tänker på att skada sig själv, sök professionell hjälp hos vården eller en krisjour; vid akut fara, ring landets nödnummer.

title: Breaking Barriers-The Intersection of AI and Assistive Technology in Autism Care: A Narrative Review.
authors: Iannone A, Giansanti D
abstract: (Background) Autism increasingly requires a multidisciplinary approach that can effectively harmonize the realms of diagnosis and therapy, tailoring both to the individual. Assistive technologies (ATs) play an important role in this context and hold significant potential when integrated with artificial intelligence (AI). (Objective) The objective of this study is to analyze the state of integration of AI with ATs in autism through a review. (Methods) A review was conducted on PubMed and Scopus, applying a standard checklist and a qualification process. The outcome reported 22 studies, including 7 reviews. (Key Content and Findings) The results reveal an early yet promising interest in integrating AI into autism assistive technologies. Exciting developments are currently underway at the intersection of AI and robotics, as well as in the creation of wearable automated devices like smart glasses. These innovations offer substantial potential for enhancing communication, interaction, and social engagement for individuals with autism. Presently, researchers are prioritizing innovation over establishing a solid presence within the healthcare domain, where issues such as regulation and acceptance demand increased attention. (Conclusions) As the field continues to evolve, it becomes increasingly clear that AI will play a pivotal role in bridging various domains, and integrated ATs with AI are positioned to act as crucial connectors.

sheet.es: Si te ofrecen tecnología de apoyo con inteligencia artificial, como robots o gafas inteligentes, puedes explorarla con curiosidad, pero sin prisa y sin darla por probada. Pregunta siempre a la persona autista si le resulta útil y cómoda. La evidencia es una revisión narrativa de PubMed y Scopus que reunió 22 estudios, 7 de ellos revisiones. Apunta a un interés temprano y prometedor para la comunicación y la interacción. Sus límites: el campo está en fase inicial, se prioriza la innovación y quedan pendientes la regulación y la aceptación, así que no sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you are offered assistive technology that uses artificial intelligence, such as robots or smart glasses, you can explore it with curiosity, but without hurry and without assuming it is proven. Always ask the autistic person whether it feels useful and comfortable. The evidence is a narrative review of PubMed and Scopus that gathered 22 studies, 7 of them reviews. It points to an early, promising interest in communication and interaction. Its limits: the field is young, researchers prioritise innovation, and regulation and acceptance still need attention, so it is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du erbjuds hjälpmedelsteknik med artificiell intelligens, som robotar eller smarta glasögon, kan du utforska den nyfiket, men utan brådska och utan att anta att den är bevisad. Fråga alltid den autistiska personen om det känns användbart och bekvämt. Underlaget är en narrativ översikt av PubMed och Scopus med 22 studier, varav 7 översikter. Den visar ett tidigt, lovande intresse för kommunikation och interaktion. Begränsningar: fältet är ungt, forskarna prioriterar innovation, och reglering och acceptans behöver mer uppmärksamhet, så det är ingen regel för alla personer.

title: Social Validity of Pivotal Response Treatment for Young Autistic Children: Perspectives of Autistic Adults.
authors: Schuck RK, Dwyer P, Baiden KMP, Williams ZJ, Wang M
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: The social validity of autism behavioral intervention has been questioned. Naturalistic Developmental Behavioral Interventions (NDBIs) attempt to address some concerns, but it is unclear whether autistic people consider NDBIs socially valid. Social validity of an NDBI, Pivotal Response Treatment (PRT), was investigated through autistic adults commenting on videos of autistic children receiving PRT. Qualitative coding of responses generated three themes: respect for individuals; assessment of intervention implementation; and socioemotional considerations. Although video brevity limits the scope of the present study's conclusions, participants highlighted PRT components that appeared socially valid (e.g., reinforcing attempts, following the child's lead) and aspects appearing invalid (e.g., overemphasis on spoken language). Therefore, adjustments appear necessary for PRT to be fully acceptable to the autistic community.

sheet.es: Si valoras una intervención como la Pivotal Response Treatment (PRT), fíjate en si respeta a la niña o al niño: si se refuerzan sus intentos, si se sigue su iniciativa y si se da el mismo valor a otras formas de comunicación y no solo al habla. Es un estudio cualitativo en el que personas adultas autistas comentaron vídeos de niñas y niños autistas que recibían PRT. Señalaron aspectos que parecían aceptables y otros no, como poner demasiado énfasis en el lenguaje hablado. Los vídeos eran breves, así que las conclusiones son limitadas y no valen para todas las personas ni para todas las sesiones.
sheet.en: If you are weighing up an approach like Pivotal Response Treatment (PRT), look at whether it respects the child: are their attempts reinforced, is their lead followed, and are other ways of communicating valued, not just speech? This was a qualitative study in which autistic adults commented on videos of autistic children receiving PRT. They pointed to parts that seemed socially valid and others that did not, such as overemphasis on spoken language. The videos were brief, so the conclusions are limited and do not apply to every child or every session.
sheet.sv: Om du överväger ett arbetssätt som Pivotal Response Treatment (PRT), titta på om det respekterar barnet: förstärks barnets försök, följer man barnets initiativ och värderas andra sätt att kommunicera, inte bara tal? Detta var en kvalitativ studie där autistiska vuxna kommenterade videor av autistiska barn som fick PRT. De pekade på delar som verkade socialt giltiga och andra som inte gjorde det, till exempel för stor tonvikt på talat språk. Videorna var korta, så slutsatserna är begränsade och gäller inte alla barn eller alla tillfällen.

title: The diversity of speech-perception difficulties among autistic individuals.
authors: Bendo GJ, Sturrock A, Hanks G, Plack CJ, Gowen E, Guest H
abstract: Background & aims Communicative and sensory differences are core autistic traits, yet speech-perception abilities and difficulties among autistic individuals remain poorly understood. Laboratory studies have produced mixed and inconclusive results, in part because of the lack of input from autistic individuals in defining the hypotheses and shaping the methods used in this field of research. Little in-depth qualitative research on autistic experiences of speech perception has been published, yet such research could form the basis for better laboratory research, for improved understanding of autistic experiences, and for the development of interventions. Existing qualitative research describes widespread autistic listening differences with significant impacts, but these results rely on data gathered via oral interviews in a small sample. The present study addresses these limitations and employs a mixed-methods approach to explore autistic listening experiences. Methods We gathered survey data from 79 autistic individuals aged 18-55 without diagnosed hearing loss. The questionnaire included 20 closed-set questions on listening abilities and difficulties and three free-text questions on listening experiences. The free-text questions underwent deductive content analysis using a framework composed of themes from previous interview data on listening experiences (including auditory differences, contributing factors, impacts, and coping strategies). Concepts in the free-text data that were not part of the analysis framework were analyzed inductively. Results In the closed-set data, participants reported listening difficulties in most specified environments, but complex background sounds and particularly background voices caused the most difficulty. Those who reported listening difficulties expressed having substantially greater difficulties than other people the same age. Participants indicated multiple impacts from listening difficulties, most prominently in their social lives. Concepts in the free-text data strongly supported previous interview data on listening differences and factors that affect listening ability, especially the diversity of types of listening difficulties. Consistent with the closed-set data, background-sound complexity and concurrent voices were especially troubling. Some concepts in the free-text data were novel, particularly difficulties with remote, broadcast, and recorded audio, prompting the creation of new themes. Conclusions Both forms of data indicate widespread listening differences-predominantly listening difficulties-affecting most autistic adults. Diverse types of listening difficulty are evident, potentially indicating heterogeneous underlying mechanisms, and complexity of background noise is consistently identified as an important factor. Listening difficulties are said to have substantial and varied impacts. Autistic adults are keen to share coping strategies, which are varied and usually self-devised. Implications Based on both the quantitative and qualitative results, we provide recommendations to improve future research and support the autistic community. The data-revealing types of listening difficulties can guide better quantitative research into underlying mechanisms. Such research should take into account potential heterogeneity in listening difficulties. Suggestions for optimized collection of self-report data are also offered. Additionally, our results could be used to improve societal understanding of autistic listening differences and to create beneficial interventions for and with autistic individuals. Moreover, given the willingness of the autistic community to share coping strategies, systematic collation of these strategies could form the basis for self-help and clinical guidance.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista dice que no entiende bien el habla, créale y reduzca el ruido de fondo: apague la tele, evite varias conversaciones a la vez y pregunte qué le ayuda. Es un estudio con encuesta a 79 personas autistas de 18-55 años sin pérdida auditiva diagnosticada. Las voces de fondo y los sonidos complejos fueron lo más difícil, con efectos sobre todo en la vida social, y también el audio remoto o grabado. Sus límites: son respuestas autoinformadas de adultos, no sirven para predecir a cada persona, y las dificultades fueron muy variadas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person says they struggle to follow speech, believe them and lower background noise: turn off the TV, avoid several conversations at once, and ask what helps them. This was a survey of 79 autistic adults aged 18-55 without diagnosed hearing loss. Background voices and complex sounds were hardest, with the biggest impact on social life, and remote or recorded audio also caused difficulty. Limits: the answers are self-reported by adults, so they cannot predict any one person, and the difficulties varied widely.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person säger att hen har svårt att uppfatta tal, tro på det och minska bakgrundsljud: stäng av tv:n, undvik flera samtal samtidigt och fråga vad som hjälper. Det var en enkät till 79 autistiska vuxna i åldern 18-55 utan diagnostiserad hörselnedsättning. Bakgrundsröster och komplexa ljud var svårast, med störst påverkan på det sociala livet, och även ljud på distans eller inspelat var svårt. Begränsningar: svaren är självrapporterade av vuxna, säger inte hur just en person har det, och svårigheterna varierade mycket.

title: Machine learning classification of autism spectrum disorder based on reciprocity in naturalistic social interactions.
authors: Koehler JC, Dong MS, Bierlich AM, Fischer S, Späth J, Plank IS, Koutsouleris N, Falter-Wagner CM
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder is characterized by impaired social communication and interaction. As a neurodevelopmental disorder typically diagnosed during childhood, diagnosis in adulthood is preceded by a resource-heavy clinical assessment period. The ongoing developments in digital phenotyping give rise to novel opportunities within the screening and diagnostic process. Our aim was to quantify multiple non-verbal social interaction characteristics in autism and build diagnostic classification models independent of clinical ratings. We analyzed videos of naturalistic social interactions in a sample including 28 autistic and 60 non-autistic adults paired in dyads and engaging in two conversational tasks. We used existing open-source computer vision algorithms for objective annotation to extract information based on the synchrony of movement and facial expression. These were subsequently used as features in a support vector machine learning model to predict whether an individual was part of an autistic or non-autistic interaction dyad. The two prediction models based on reciprocal adaptation in facial movements, as well as individual amounts of head and body motion and facial expressiveness showed the highest precision (balanced accuracies: 79.5% and 68.8%, respectively), followed by models based on reciprocal coordination of head (balanced accuracy: 62.1%) and body (balanced accuracy: 56.7%) motion, as well as intrapersonal coordination processes (balanced accuracy: 44.2%). Combinations of these models did not increase overall predictive performance. Our work highlights the distinctive nature of non-verbal behavior in autism and its utility for digital phenotyping-based classification. Future research needs to both explore the performance of different prediction algorithms to reveal underlying mechanisms and interactions, as well as investigate the prospective generalizability and robustness of these algorithms in routine clinical care.

sheet.es: Esta investigación no ofrece nada que hacer mañana en casa: no sirve para evaluar a nadie ni para decidir nada sobre una persona concreta. Si buscas una valoración, acude a un equipo clínico con experiencia. Se trata de un estudio con 28 adultos autistas y 60 adultos no autistas, en parejas que conversaban y fueron grabadas en vídeo. Un programa informático analizó el movimiento y la expresión facial, y los mejores modelos acertaron con precisiones equilibradas de 79.5% y 68.8%. Sus límites: es un grupo pequeño, aún no se ha probado en la práctica clínica real y no demuestra que la comunicación autista sea un problema. Solo muestra que hay estilos no verbales distintos.
sheet.en: This research gives nothing to act on tomorrow at home: it cannot assess anyone and should not shape decisions about a particular person. If you are seeking an assessment, turn to an experienced clinical team. It is a study of 28 autistic and 60 non-autistic adults, paired in conversations that were filmed. Software analysed movement and facial expression, and the best models reached balanced accuracies of 79.5% and 68.8%. Its limits: the sample is small, it has not yet been tested in routine clinical care, and it does not show that autistic communication is a problem. It only suggests that non-verbal styles differ.
sheet.sv: Den här forskningen ger inget att göra hemma i morgon: den kan inte bedöma någon och bör inte styra beslut om en enskild person. Om ni söker utredning, vänd er till ett erfaret kliniskt team. Det är en studie med 28 autistiska och 60 icke-autistiska vuxna, i par som samtalade och filmades. Ett program analyserade rörelser och ansiktsuttryck, och de bästa modellerna nådde balanserad träffsäkerhet på 79.5% och 68.8%. Begränsningar: gruppen är liten, metoden är inte prövad i vanlig klinisk vård och studien visar inte att autistisk kommunikation är ett problem. Den antyder bara att icke-verbala stilar skiljer sig.

title: Understanding profound autism: implications for stigma and supports.
authors: Clarke EB, McCauley JB, Lutz A, Gotelli M, Sheinkopf SJ, Lord C
abstract: Introduction Societal perceptions and lack of understanding of autism spectrum disorder can be stigmatizing for autistic individuals and their families. This may be particularly the case for individuals who meet criteria for profound autism. Despite the considerable service needs of this marginalized group, there is little data on the prevalence of profound autism, nor on the experiences of those with profound autism and their families. Methods The current study leveraged a mixed-methods approach to address these gaps. First, the prevalence of profound autism was examined in six samples-three from the United States and three from Western Europe. Second, inductive thematic analysis was used to code interviews from 20 caregivers of profoundly autistic adults. Results The prevalence of profound autism varied widely across the six samples-from 11% to 48%. There were also notable differences between samples in prevalence by gender, race, and ethnicity. Two overarching themes were identified via inductive thematic analysis: Community Perceptions of Autism and Family Support Needs and Advocacy Challenges . Though caregivers were not directly asked about stigmatization during interviews, 85% of caregivers reported at least one instance of perceived stigma. Discussion Future research should continue to examine the unique needs and stigmatization experiences of profoundly autistic individuals and their families across the life course.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista con grandes necesidades de apoyo, es normal que sientas la mirada ajena y que te cueste conseguir ayuda. Conviene buscar a otras familias y llevar por escrito las necesidades de apoyo cuando pidas servicios. Este estudio combinó datos de seis muestras de Estados Unidos y Europa occidental con entrevistas a 20 cuidadores de adultos autistas con autismo profundo. El 85% de los cuidadores mencionó al menos una situación de estigma percibido. Sin embargo, la frecuencia del autismo profundo varió mucho entre muestras, del 11% al 48%, y las entrevistas son pocas, así que no describen a todas las familias.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic person with high support needs, feeling judged by others and struggling to get help is a common experience. It may help to connect with other families and write down support needs when you ask for services. This study combined data from six samples in the United States and Western Europe with interviews with 20 caregivers of profoundly autistic adults. 85% of caregivers reported at least one instance of perceived stigma. However, how common profound autism was varied widely between samples, from 11% to 48%, and the interviews were few, so they cannot describe every family.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person med stora stödbehov är det vanligt att känna sig dömd av andra och att ha svårt att få hjälp. Det kan hjälpa att hitta andra familjer och skriva ner stödbehoven när du ansöker om insatser. Studien kombinerade data från sex urval i USA och Västeuropa med intervjuer med 20 vårdgivare till autistiska vuxna med profound autism. 85 % av vårdgivarna berättade om minst ett tillfälle av upplevd stigma. Hur vanlig profound autism var skilde sig dock mycket mellan urvalen, från 11 % till 48 %, och intervjuerna var få, så de beskriver inte alla familjer.

title: Policies for Individuals With Autism: Gaps, Research, and Recommendations.
authors: Doda V, Kennedy C, Kaur M
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a complex neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by social, behavioral, and learning challenges. Individuals with autism and their families often struggle to get an appropriate diagnosis and continuation of specialty services, including general healthcare, mental health and transition services, special education, employment, and social and emotional support. This paper presents information about the current policies and support mechanisms that exist to help these individuals and their families. This paper identifies the gaps and recommends areas of improvement based on evidence-based research and current data. ASD is a lifelong disability without a cure, but by constructing robust policies and providing enhanced support, the quality of lives of those with ASD and their families can be improved.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista, conviene anotar qué servicios necesita (salud, apoyo emocional, educación, transición a la vida adulta, empleo) y cuáles se han interrumpido, para pedirlos con claridad. Es una revisión que describe las políticas y los apoyos actuales, señala carencias y propone mejoras; el resumen no indica que se midieran resultados en personas concretas. No ofrece una pauta que valga para todas las personas ni para todos los países, y las normas locales pueden diferir mucho. Para decisiones concretas, consulta con los servicios y profesionales de tu zona.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person, it can help to write down which services they need (health care, emotional support, education, transition to adulthood, employment) and which have been interrupted, so you can ask for them clearly. This is a review that describes current policies and supports, points out gaps and suggests improvements; the abstract does not say outcomes were measured in individual people. It is not a rule for every person or every country, and local systems can differ a lot. For specific decisions, talk with the services and professionals in your area.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person kan det hjälpa att skriva ner vilka insatser hen behöver (hälso- och sjukvård, emotionellt stöd, utbildning, övergång till vuxenlivet, arbete) och vilka som har avbrutits, så att du kan be om dem tydligt. Det här är en översikt som beskriver nuvarande policyer och stöd, pekar ut luckor och föreslår förbättringar; sammanfattningen säger inte att resultat mättes hos enskilda personer. Den är ingen regel för alla personer eller alla länder, och lokala system kan skilja sig mycket. För konkreta beslut, prata med tjänster och yrkespersoner där du bor.

title: Community perspectives on the appropriateness and importance of support goals for young autistic children.
authors: Waddington H, Minnell H, Patrick L, van Der Meer L, Monk R, Woods L, Whitehouse AJ
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Researchers do not know much about what autistic adults, parents and professionals think about support goals for young autistic children. People's views of support goals might also be influenced by their beliefs about early support more generally. This survey involved 87 autistic adults, 159 parents of autistic children and 80 clinical professionals living in New Zealand and Australia. We asked participants questions about themselves and what they thought about early support for young autistic children in general. We then asked participants to rate whether different support goals were appropriate for young autistic children and, if they were appropriate, to rate their level of priority. We found that autistic adults, parents and professionals all rated goals about the adult changing to better support the child, reducing and replacing harmful behaviours and improving the child's quality of life as the highest priorities. They all rated goals about autism characteristics, play skills and academic skills as the lowest priorities. Compared to parents and/or professionals, autistic adults gave lower priority ratings for play skills, autism characteristics and participation goals. Autistic adults were also more likely to rate goals related to play skills and autism characteristics as inappropriate. While these three participant groups generally agreed on the order of priority of early support goals for young autistic children, autistic adults found goals related to autism characteristics, play and/or participation to be an even lower priority and less appropriate than parents and professionals.

sheet.es: Al pensar en los objetivos de apoyo para un niño autista pequeño, conviene empezar por lo que puede cambiar el adulto para apoyarle mejor y por su calidad de vida, y no por reducir sus rasgos autistas. Es una encuesta a 87 adultos autistas, 159 madres y padres y 80 profesionales de Nueva Zelanda y Australia. Los tres grupos dieron más prioridad a que el adulto cambie para apoyar al niño, a reducir y sustituir conductas dañinas y a la calidad de vida; y menos a los rasgos autistas, el juego y las habilidades académicas. Las personas autistas les dieron aún menos prioridad. Son opiniones, no resultados de un apoyo concreto, y no sirven como regla para todos los niños.
sheet.en: When thinking about support goals for a young autistic child, it may help to start with what the adult can change to support the child better, and with the child's quality of life, rather than with reducing autistic characteristics. This was a survey of 87 autistic adults, 159 parents and 80 professionals in New Zealand and Australia. All three groups gave highest priority to the adult changing to support the child, reducing and replacing harmful behaviours, and quality of life. They gave lowest priority to autism characteristics, play skills and academic skills. Autistic adults rated these even lower. These are opinions, not results of a specific support, and they are not a rule for every child.
sheet.sv: När du funderar på stödmål för ett litet autistiskt barn kan det hjälpa att börja med vad den vuxne kan ändra för att stötta barnet bättre, och med barnets livskvalitet, snarare än att minska autistiska drag. Detta var en enkät med 87 autistiska vuxna, 159 föräldrar och 80 yrkespersoner i Nya Zeeland och Australien. Alla tre grupperna prioriterade högst att den vuxne ändrar sig för att stötta barnet, att minska och ersätta skadliga beteenden samt livskvalitet. Lägst prioritet fick autistiska drag, lekfärdigheter och skolfärdigheter. Autistiska vuxna prioriterade dessa ännu lägre. Det är åsikter, inte resultat av ett visst stöd, och inte en regel för alla barn.

title: Mindfulness-based stress reduction for autistic adults: A feasibility study in an outpatient context.
authors: Agius H, Luoto AK, Backman A, Eriksdotter C, Jayaram-Lindström N, Bölte S, Hirvikoski T
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic adults report high stress levels and difficulties dealing with everyday stressors. Mindfulness-based stress reduction groups aim to help regulate stress responses. We asked 50 autistic adults, without intellectual disability, to participate in a study of mindfulness-based stress reduction. The group program was made accessible through clear group leader communication and good program predictability, as well as reduced exposure to disturbing sensory stimuli. The mindfulness and yoga based exercises from the original mindfulness-based stress reduction program were included. The participants were positive and would even recommend an autistic friend to participate in a mindfulness-based stress reduction group. They reported that mindfulness-based stress reduction could lower symptoms of stress and improved stress coping. We still need to investigate these effects further in larger studies. The findings of this work show that mindfulness-based stress reduction groups can be adapted for autistic adults and that the participants overall were positive to the intervention and the group format.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta quiere probar un grupo de reducción del estrés basado en mindfulness, conviene buscar uno adaptado: comunicación clara de quien lo dirige, programa predecible y pocos estímulos sensoriales molestos. Sobre la evidencia: es un estudio de viabilidad en el que se invitó a 50 personas autistas adultas, sin discapacidad intelectual, a un programa grupal con ejercicios de mindfulness y yoga. Los participantes lo valoraron bien y lo recomendarían a un amigo autista. Sobre los límites: no es una prueba definitiva de que reduzca el estrés, hacen falta estudios más grandes, y no sabemos si sirve a quienes tienen discapacidad intelectual ni a cada persona.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult wants to try a mindfulness-based stress reduction group, look for one that is adapted: clear communication from the group leader, a predictable programme and few disturbing sensory stimuli. On the evidence: this was a feasibility study in which 50 autistic adults, without intellectual disability, were invited to a group programme with mindfulness and yoga exercises. Participants were positive and would recommend it to an autistic friend. On the limits: it does not prove that the programme lowers stress, larger studies are still needed, and we do not know whether it suits autistic people with intellectual disability or every individual.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen vill prova en grupp för mindfulnessbaserad stressreducering, sök en som är anpassad: tydlig kommunikation från gruppledaren, ett förutsägbart program och få störande sinnesintryck. Om evidensen: detta var en genomförbarhetsstudie där 50 autistiska vuxna, utan intellektuell funktionsnedsättning, tillfrågades om ett gruppprogram med mindfulness- och yogaövningar. Deltagarna var positiva och skulle rekommendera det till en autistisk vän. Om begränsningarna: studien visar inte säkert att programmet minskar stress, större studier behövs, och vi vet inte om det passar autistiska personer med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning eller varje individ.

title: Barriers to healthcare for Australian autistic adults.
authors: Arnold SR, Bruce G, Weise J, Mills CJ, Trollor JN, Coxon K
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract This study looked at how Australian autistic and non-autistic adults experience barriers to healthcare. We asked autistic and non-autistic adults to complete the Barriers to Healthcare Checklist Short-Form (BHC). We analysed data from 263 autistic adults and 70 non-autistic adults. We found that autistic adults experienced more barriers to healthcare than non-autistic adults. Gender diversity, feeling more anxious, having greater disability and feeling unsatisfied with social support contributed to barriers to healthcare in autistic participants. We recommend interventions such as developing and implementing a national action plan, similar to the National Roadmap for Improving the Health of People with Intellectual Disability (2021) to reduce barriers and address unmet healthcare needs of Australian autistic adults. We also recommend working with autistic adults to develop new policies and strategies, implementing environmental adaptations to health care facilities, and increasing Autism education opportunities for health professionals to address gaps in knowledge.

sheet.es: Antes de una cita médica, prepara con la persona autista qué necesita: avisar de sus necesidades de comunicación y sensoriales, escribir de antemano lo que quiere contar y pedir ajustes concretos. Si se siente ansiosa o poco apoyada, acompáñala si ella lo desea. La evidencia es un estudio con 263 personas autistas adultas y 70 no autistas de Australia, que completaron un cuestionario; las autistas encontraron más barreras para acceder a la atención sanitaria. Sus límites: refleja a personas de un solo país y no predice la experiencia de cada persona.
sheet.en: Before a medical appointment, plan with the autistic person what they need: share their communication and sensory needs, write down in advance what they want to say, and ask for specific adjustments. If they feel anxious or poorly supported, offer to come along if they want that. The evidence is a study of 263 autistic adults and 70 non-autistic adults in Australia who completed a questionnaire; autistic adults met more barriers to healthcare. Its limits: it reflects people in one country and cannot predict any one person's experience.
sheet.sv: Inför ett läkarbesök kan ni planera tillsammans med den autistiska personen vad hen behöver: berätta om kommunikations- och sensoriska behov, skriv ner i förväg vad hen vill ta upp och be om konkreta anpassningar. Om hen känner oro eller saknar stöd kan du följa med, om hen vill det. Underlaget är en studie med 263 autistiska vuxna och 70 icke-autistiska vuxna i Australien som fyllde i ett frågeformulär; autistiska vuxna mötte fler hinder i vården. Begränsningar: den speglar människor i ett enda land och förutsäger inte en enskild persons upplevelse.

title: Parent, child, and family outcomes following Acceptance And Commitment Therapy for parents of autistic children: A randomized controlled trial.
authors: Maughan AL, Lunsky Y, Lake J, Mills JS, Fung K, Steel L, Weiss JA
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Parents of autistic children commonly experience difficulties with their own mental health. This study looked at the effects of a brief group-based Acceptance and Commitment Therapy program, developed for parents of autistic children, youth, and adults. ACT focuses on increasing psychological flexibility, which is the ability to be mindful and accepting of difficult thoughts and experiences, shown to be important for mental wellness. Participants included 54 parents of autistic people, ages 3-34. Parents were randomly divided into two groups: a Treatment group that received the intervention right away, and a Waitlist group that completed the program after the Treatment group completed the trial. All parents filled out questionnaires right before the program began, and at 3, 7, and 17 weeks after randomization. Compared to the group that was waiting to participate in the program, parents in the Treatment group reported greater improvements in depression and family distress, and these improvements were still present 4 months later. Parents in the Treatment group also reported short-term improvements in their positive feelings and personal goals, compared to those waiting. Results showed that ACT may help improve some aspects of mental health for parents of autistic children, but further research is recommended.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista y notas que tu propio ánimo o el estrés familiar pesan mucho, un programa breve de grupo basado en la Terapia de Aceptación y Compromiso (ACT) puede ser una opción que vale la pena consultar. Es un ensayo aleatorizado con 54 madres y padres de personas autistas de 3-34 años: quienes hicieron el programa de inmediato informaron mayores mejoras en depresión y malestar familiar que quienes esperaban, y esas mejoras seguían 4 meses después. Límites: es un estudio pequeño, los datos son cuestionarios que responden los propios padres y los resultados no valen para todas las familias; los autores piden más investigación.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic person and your own mood or family stress feels heavy, a brief group program based on Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) may be worth looking into. This was a randomized trial with 54 parents of autistic people aged 3-34: parents who took the program right away reported greater improvements in depression and family distress than those on the waitlist, and these were still present 4 months later. Limits: it is a small study, results come from questionnaires the parents filled in themselves, and it cannot tell us what will work for every family; the authors call for more research.
sheet.sv: Om du stödjer en autistisk person och själv känner dig nedstämd eller familjen är stressad kan ett kort gruppprogram baserat på Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) vara värt att undersöka. Det var en randomiserad studie med 54 föräldrar till autistiska personer i åldrarna 3-34: de som gick programmet direkt rapporterade större förbättringar av depression och familjens påfrestning än de som stod på väntelista, och förbättringarna fanns kvar 4 månader senare. Begränsningar: studien är liten, resultaten bygger på enkäter som föräldrarna själva fyllt i och kan inte visa vad som fungerar för alla familjer; forskarna efterlyser mer forskning.

title: Mapping autism's research landscape: trends in autism screening and its alignment with sustainable development goals.
authors: Nedungadi P, Shah SM, Stokes MA, Kumar Nair V, Moorkoth A, Raman R
abstract: Introduction Autism Spectrum Disorder is a complex neurodevelopmental syndrome that profoundly affects social interactions, communication, and sensory perception. The research traced the evolution of autism research from 2011-2022, specifically focusing on the screening and diagnosis of children and students. Methods Through an analysis of 12,262 publications using the PRISMA framework, bibliographic coupling, science mapping, and citation analysis, this study illuminates the growth trajectory of ASD research and significant disparities in diagnosis and services. Results The study indicates an increasing trend in autism research, with a strong representation of female authorship. Open Access journals show a higher average citation impact compared to their closed counterparts. A keyword co-occurrence analysis revealed four central research themes: Child Development and Support Systems, Early Identification and Intervention, Prevalence and Etiology, and Mental Health. The pandemic's onset has prioritized research areas like mental health, telehealth, and service accessibility. Discussion Recommendations on a global level stress the importance of developing timely biological markers for ASD, amplifying Disability Inclusion research, and personalizing mental health services to bridge these critical service gaps. These strategies, underpinned by interdisciplinary collaboration and telehealth innovation, particularly in low-resource settings, can offer a roadmap for inclusive, context-sensitive interventions at local levels that directly support SDG3's aim for health and well-being for all.

sheet.es: Para tu día a día: este estudio no ofrece pasos concretos para casa, pero sugiere que conviene preguntar por servicios de evaluación y apoyo accesibles, incluida la atención por telesalud si la distancia o los recursos son un obstáculo. Evidencia: revisión sistemática de 12.262 publicaciones sobre cribado y diagnóstico en niñez y estudiantes, entre 2011 y 2022. Identificó cuatro temas: desarrollo infantil y apoyos, identificación e intervención tempranas, prevalencia y causas, y salud mental. Límites: analiza tendencias de investigación, no a personas autistas, y no demuestra qué funciona para tu familia. Las decisiones médicas corresponden a profesionales clínicos.
sheet.en: For your day-to-day: this study offers no concrete steps for home, but it suggests it is worth asking about accessible assessment and support services, including telehealth if distance or resources are a barrier. Evidence: a systematic review of 12,262 publications on screening and diagnosis in children and students, from 2011-2022. It found four themes: child development and support systems, early identification and intervention, prevalence and etiology, and mental health. Limits: it maps research trends, not autistic people themselves, and does not show what works for your family. Medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: För din vardag: studien ger inga konkreta steg för hemmet, men antyder att det är värt att fråga efter tillgängliga utrednings- och stödtjänster, även via telehälsa om avstånd eller resurser är ett hinder. Evidens: en systematisk översikt av 12 262 publikationer om screening och diagnos hos barn och studenter, 2011–2022. Den fann fyra teman: barns utveckling och stödsystem, tidig identifiering och insatser, förekomst och orsaker samt psykisk hälsa. Begränsningar: den kartlägger forskningstrender, inte autistiska personer, och visar inte vad som fungerar för din familj. Medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker.

title: Evidence for investing in parenting interventions aiming to improve child health: a systematic review of economic evaluations.
authors: Sampaio F, Nystrand C, Feldman I, Mihalopoulos C
abstract: A comprehensive review of the economic evidence on parenting interventions targeting different aspects of child health is lacking to support decision-making. The aim of this review is to provide an up to date synthesis of the available health economic evidence for parenting interventions aiming to improve child health. A systematic review was conducted with articles identified through Econlit, Medline, PsychINFO, and ERIC databases. Only full economic evaluations comparing two or more options, considering both costs and outcomes were included. We assessed the quality of the studies using the Drummond checklist. We identified 44 studies of varying quality that met inclusion criteria; 22 targeting externalizing behaviors, five targeting internalizing problems, and five targeting other mental health problems including autism and alcohol abuse. The remaining studies targeted child abuse (n = 5), obesity (n = 3), and general health (n = 4). Studies varied considerably and many suffered from methodological limitations, such as limited costing perspectives, challenges with outcome measurement and short-time horizons. Parenting interventions showed good value for money in particular for preventing child externalizing and internalizing behaviors. For the prevention of child abuse, some programs had the potential of being cost-saving over the longer-term. Interventions were not cost-effective for the treatment of autism and obesity. Future research should include a broader spectrum of societal costs and quality-of-life impacts on both children and their caregivers.

sheet.es: Si le ofrecen un programa de apoyo a la crianza, pregunte qué busca lograr y si encaja con su familia; el valor económico no dice si le servirá a su hijo o hija. Esta revisión sistemática analizó 44 estudios de costes y resultados de programas para madres, padres y cuidadores. Cinco se centraron en otros problemas de salud mental, entre ellos el autismo y el abuso de alcohol. Los programas parecían rentables sobre todo para prevenir conductas externalizantes e internalizantes, pero no resultaron rentables para el tratamiento del autismo. Los estudios eran de calidad variable, con horizontes cortos y medidas limitadas, y no evalúan el bienestar de cada persona autista.
sheet.en: If you are offered a parenting programme, ask what it aims to achieve and whether it fits your family; value for money does not tell you whether it will help your child. This systematic review looked at 44 studies comparing the costs and outcomes of programmes for parents and caregivers. Five focused on other mental health problems, including autism and alcohol abuse. Programmes seemed good value mainly for preventing externalizing and internalizing behaviours, but were not cost-effective for the treatment of autism. Study quality varied, time horizons were short and measures limited, and the findings say nothing about how any one autistic person is doing.
sheet.sv: Om du erbjuds ett föräldrastödsprogram, fråga vad det syftar till och om det passar din familj; kostnadseffektivitet säger inte om det hjälper just ditt barn. Denna systematiska översikt granskade 44 studier som jämförde kostnader och resultat för program riktade till föräldrar och vårdnadshavare. Fem handlade om andra psykiska hälsoproblem, bland annat autism och alkoholmissbruk. Programmen verkade ge god valuta för pengarna främst för att förebygga externaliserande och internaliserande beteenden, men var inte kostnadseffektiva för behandling av autism. Studiernas kvalitet varierade, tidsperspektiven var korta och måtten begränsade, och resultaten säger inget om hur en enskild autistisk person mår.

title: Theoretical-Methodological Foundations for the Global Integration Method (Método de Integração Global-MIG) in the Treatment of Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Loffi RG, Cruz TKF, Paiva GM, Souto DO, Barreto SR, Santana PAN, Nascimento AAAC, Costa FRM, Cota EB, Haase VG
abstract: Currently, there is no intervention model for autism spectrum disorder (ASD) that addresses all levels and factors of the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF, WHO). The most researched programs focus on naturalistic, developmental and behavioral approaches to socio-communication. Less attention has been paid to motor and environmental reactivity aspects (behavior/interest restriction and sensory reactivity). The evidence rationale for the Global Integration Method (MIG, "Método de Integração Global"), a model addressing sensorimotor reactivity in addition to socio-communication, is presented. MIG is an integrative, interdisciplinary, family-oriented intervention and naturalistic program that addresses all levels and moderating factors of ASD's impact. MIG's theoretical rationale is based on the predictive coding impairment and embodied cognition hypotheses. MIG incorporates both bottom-up (flexible therapeutic suit, social-motor synchronization) and top-down (schematic social information processing, narratives, imagery) strategies to promote the building and use of accurate, flexible and context-sensitive internal predictive models. MIG is based on the premises that predictive coding improves both socio-communication and environmental reactivity, and that the postural stabilization provided by the flexible therapeutic suit frees information processing resources for socio-cognitive learning. MIG builds on interdisciplinary, professionally and parentally mediated work based on behavioral principles of intensive training in a situated environment.

sheet.es: Si le interesan enfoques que tengan en cuenta no solo la comunicación social, sino también los movimientos, los intereses y la sensibilidad sensorial, este trabajo describe uno de ellos. Es una revisión teórica que presenta la base de un método llamado MIG, pensado para trabajar con las familias y en entornos cotidianos. No informa de resultados en personas concretas, así que no demuestra que funcione. Úsela como idea para conversar con el equipo profesional, y recuerde que cada persona autista tiene necesidades y preferencias propias.
sheet.en: If you are interested in approaches that look beyond social communication to include movement, interests and sensory sensitivity, this paper describes one. It is a theoretical review setting out the rationale for a method called MIG, designed to involve families and work in everyday settings. It does not report results from specific people, so it does not show that the method works. Use it as a starting point for a conversation with your professional team, and remember that every autistic person has their own needs and preferences.
sheet.sv: Om du är intresserad av insatser som ser bortom social kommunikation och även rör rörelse, intressen och sensorisk känslighet beskriver den här artikeln en sådan. Det är en teoretisk översikt som presenterar grunden för en metod kallad MIG, som är tänkt att involvera familjen och användas i vardagliga miljöer. Den redovisar inga resultat från enskilda personer och visar därför inte att metoden fungerar. Använd den som underlag för samtal med det professionella teamet, och kom ihåg att varje autistisk person har egna behov och preferenser.

title: Autism Spectrum Disorder: Brain Areas Involved, Neurobiological Mechanisms, Diagnoses and Therapies.
authors: Lamanna J, Meldolesi J
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD), affecting over 2% of the pre-school children population, includes an important fraction of the conditions accounting for the heterogeneity of autism. The disease was discovered 75 years ago, and the present review, based on critical evaluations of the recognized ASD studies from the beginning of 1990, has been further developed by the comparative analyses of the research and clinical reports, which have grown progressively in recent years up to late 2023. The tools necessary for the identification of the ASD disease and its related clinical pathologies are genetic and epigenetic mutations affected by the specific interaction with transcription factors and chromatin remodeling processes occurring within specific complexes of brain neurons. Most often, the ensuing effects induce the inhibition/excitation of synaptic structures sustained primarily, at dendritic fibers, by alterations of flat and spine response sites. These effects are relevant because synapses, established by specific interactions of neurons with glial cells, operate as early and key targets of ASD. The pathology of children is often suspected by parents and communities and then confirmed by ensuing experiences. The final diagnoses of children and mature patients are then completed by the combination of neuropsychological (cognitive) tests and electro-/magneto-encephalography studies developed in specialized centers. ASD comorbidities, induced by processes such as anxieties, depressions, hyperactivities, and sleep defects, interact with and reinforce other brain diseases, especially schizophrenia. Advanced therapies, prescribed to children and adult patients for the control of ASD symptoms and disease, are based on the combination of well-known brain drugs with classical tools of neurologic and psychiatric practice. Overall, this review reports and discusses the advanced knowledge about the biological and medical properties of ASD.

sheet.es: Si sospechas que tu hijo o hija es autista, tu observación cuenta: la revisión señala que las familias suelen notarlo primero y que después se confirma con pruebas cognitivas y estudios de actividad cerebral en centros especializados. Es una revisión de la literatura científica sobre autismo desde 1990 hasta finales de 2023, no un estudio con participantes propios. Describe sobre todo mecanismos biológicos y usa un lenguaje médico; no ofrece pautas para el día a día. Las decisiones sobre tratamientos médicos corresponden siempre a un profesional clínico, y cada persona autista es distinta.
sheet.en: If you suspect your child is autistic, your observation matters: the review notes that families often notice first, and that this is later confirmed with cognitive tests and brain activity studies in specialised centres. It is a review of the scientific literature on autism from 1990 to late 2023, not a study with its own participants. It mostly describes biological mechanisms in medical language and offers no day-to-day guidance. Decisions about medical treatment belong to a clinician, and every autistic person is different.
sheet.sv: Om du misstänker att ditt barn är autistiskt räknas din observation: översikten noterar att familjer ofta märker det först, och att det sedan bekräftas med kognitiva tester och studier av hjärnaktivitet vid specialiserade centrum. Det är en översikt av forskningslitteratur om autism från 1990 till slutet av 2023, inte en studie med egna deltagare. Den beskriver mest biologiska mekanismer med medicinskt språk och ger inga råd för vardagen. Beslut om medicinsk behandling fattas tillsammans med en läkare, och alla autistiska personer är olika.

title: The importance and challenges of observing social interactions in autistic preschoolers during inclusive educational settings: A scoping review.
authors: Tsamitrou S, Plumet MH
abstract: Background and aims A growing number of autistic children have access to inclusive education programs as early as kindergarten. However, little is known about how they actually participate in social interactions and develop their communicative skills according to the parameters of this environment. The aim of this article is to review observational studies on this topic and critically analyze their methodological choices by arguing on the aspects of communication skills noted in the observation grids. Disparities in the information collected depending on the method used have implications for understanding and supporting autistic children in an inclusive school environment. Methods Observational studies on social interactions of autistic preschoolers within inclusive preschool settings were scoped. The studies were analyzed according to the following parameters: aims of observation, method used for coding, communication partners considered (adults and peers), type of children's social engagement (initiatives and responses), diversity of communicative forms and communication functions, distinction and comparison of interactional contexts related to the activities, and whether changes linked to developmental variables are studied on an interindividual or longitudinal basis. Results Seventeen studies using the observation method in inclusive preschool settings were identified. Recordingmethods are mostly based on video recording. The coding grids mainly focus on autistic children while partners' behaviors (adults, peers) are often coded in less detail, thus providing littleinformation on their dynamic role in the interactions. Overall, autistic children were found to initiate interactions much less often than they respond to it. The data generally distinguish thecommunicative forms used by children and indicate a predominance of nonverbal means at preschool level. However, a few studies coded communicative functions, whether they areaddressed to children or produced by them. In addition, very few studies compare interactions across activity contexts.
