In addition, very few studies compare interactions across activity contexts.Results of some studies showed that children initiated interaction more frequently during free play than during work activity, but results are heterogeneous. Developmental trajectories in socialskills seem to be associated with the severity of autism and language skills, but longitudinal designs are still rare. Conclusions and implications Direct and fine-grained observation in the classroom is a key source of information about how communication takes place in preschool-inclusive settings. The data, despite some methodological challenges, offer opportunities for better adjustment based on professional objectives. Our review highlights the importance of offering occasions for initiatives to autistic children and training of neurotypical peers to better interact with autistic children and promote verbal communication. Further observational studies are needed to use more microanalytic measures of the functional quality of social interactions in autistic children, including joint comparisons between partners (adults vs. peers) and across contexts (e.g., play vs. structured development) so that appropriate strategies can be proposed in inclusive preschool settings.

sheet.es: Mañana, si acompañas a un niño autista en preescolar, observa cuándo y con quién se comunica, y ofrécele ocasiones para tomar la iniciativa, por ejemplo durante el juego libre. Puedes pedir al centro que ayude a sus compañeros a interactuar con niños autistas. Esta es una revisión de alcance de 17 estudios observacionales en aulas inclusivas de preescolar. Los resultados varían entre estudios, pocos compararon actividades o siguieron a los niños en el tiempo, y no sirven como regla para cada niño.
sheet.en: Tomorrow, if you support an autistic child in preschool, notice when and with whom they communicate, and offer chances for them to take the initiative, for example during free play. You can ask the school to help classmates learn to interact with autistic children. This is a scoping review of 17 observational studies in inclusive preschool classrooms. Results varied between studies, few compared activities or followed children over time, and they are not a rule for every child.
sheet.sv: Imorgon, om du stödjer ett autistiskt barn i förskolan, lägg märke till när och med vem barnet kommunicerar, och ge möjligheter att ta initiativ, till exempel under fri lek. Du kan be förskolan hjälpa kamraterna att samspela med autistiska barn. Detta är en kartläggande översikt av 17 observationsstudier i inkluderande förskolemiljöer. Resultaten varierade mellan studierna, få jämförde aktiviteter eller följde barn över tid, och de gäller inte som regel för varje barn.

title: Autistic Adults' Priorities for Future Autism Employment Research: Perspectives from the United Kingdom.
authors: Davies J, Romualdez AM, Malyan D, Heasman B, Livesey A, Walker A, Pellicano E, Remington A
abstract: Background A growing body of research has sought to understand autistic people's research priorities. Several of these studies have identified employment as a key research priority. Yet, there have been a few attempts to identify specific, actionable priorities within this area. Methods Using an online survey, we asked 197 autistic people in the United Kingdom about their priorities for future autism-employment research. Results Participants spoke of their challenges in gaining and sustaining meaningful employment and called for researchers to conduct research that results in direct improvements to employment experiences. Regarding their research priorities, participants indicated a need for research covering all aspects of the employment lifecycle from accessing employment to transitioning out of employment. Importantly, participants also discussed how such research should be conducted: with autistic people as co-researchers and ensuring a diverse range of autistic people are listened to. Conclusion While much existing autism-employment research appears to align with the priorities outlined in this study, seemingly minimal attention has been paid to later stages of the work lifecycle (e.g., progressing into more senior job roles or transitioning out of work). By identifying disparities between autistic people's priorities and the research being conducted, we can support autistic people to drive the research agenda and ensure autism-employment research positively impacts the community it aims to serve.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista en su vida laboral, pregúntale qué necesita en cada etapa: acceder a un empleo, mantenerlo, ascender o dejarlo. No te limites a la búsqueda de trabajo. Este estudio encuestó en línea a 197 personas autistas del Reino Unido sobre qué debería investigarse en empleo. Pidieron investigación que mejore de forma directa sus experiencias laborales, con personas autistas como coinvestigadoras y escuchando a perfiles diversos. Es una sola encuesta en un país, recoge opiniones y no mide qué apoyos funcionan, así que no sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person with work, ask what they need at each stage: getting a job, keeping it, moving up, or leaving it. Don't focus only on job hunting. This study surveyed 197 autistic people in the United Kingdom online about what employment research should cover. They asked for research that directly improves their work experiences, with autistic people as co-researchers and a diverse range of autistic voices heard. It is a single survey in one country that gathers views and does not test which supports work, so it is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person i arbetslivet, fråga vad hen behöver i varje skede: att få ett jobb, behålla det, avancera eller lämna det. Fokusera inte bara på jobbsökandet. Studien frågade 197 autistiska personer i Storbritannien i en webbenkät vad forskning om arbete bör handla om. De ville ha forskning som direkt förbättrar arbetslivet, med autistiska personer som medforskare och med många olika autistiska röster. Det är en enda enkät i ett land som samlar åsikter och inte testar vilket stöd som fungerar, så den gäller inte som regel för alla.

title: Retinal Thinning in Adults with Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Friedel EBN, Tebartz van Elst L, Schäfer M, Maier S, Runge K, Küchlin S, Reich M, Lagrèze WA, Kornmeier J, Ebert D, Endres D, Domschke K, Nickel K
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Since the retina shares its embryological origin with the central nervous system, optical coherence tomography (OCT), an imaging technique frequently employed in ophthalmology to analyze the macula and intraretinal layer thicknesses and volumes, has recently become increasingly important in psychiatric research. We examined 34 autistic and 31 neurotypical adults (NT) using OCT. Autistic adults had reduced overall macular and outer nuclear layer (ONL) thickness and volume compared to NT. Both macular and ONL thickness showed significant inverse associations with the severity of autistic symptoms measured with the Social Responsiveness Scale 2 (SRS-2). Longitudinal studies across different age groups are required to clarify whether retinal changes may represent a possible trait marker.

sheet.es: Este estudio no ofrece nada que cambiar mañana en casa: no es una herramienta de detección ni una guía de apoyo. Si surge una duda sobre la vista, consulta a un profesional de la oftalmología. Evidencia: un estudio con 34 adultos autistas y 31 adultos neurotípicos, a quienes se les midió la retina con tomografía de coherencia óptica. Las personas autistas tuvieron un grosor y un volumen menores en la mácula y en una capa de la retina. Límites: es una comparación en un momento dado, con pocas personas; no explica la causa, no sirve para diagnosticar y no describe a cada persona autista. Los autores piden estudios a lo largo del tiempo.
sheet.en: This study gives nothing to change at home tomorrow: it is not a screening tool or a support guide. If you have a question about someone's vision, an eye care professional is the right person to ask. Evidence: a study of 34 autistic adults and 31 neurotypical adults, whose retinas were scanned with optical coherence tomography. The autistic adults had lower thickness and volume in the macula and in one retinal layer. Limits: it compares groups at one point in time, with few people; it does not explain the cause, cannot diagnose, and does not describe every autistic person. The authors call for studies following people over time.
sheet.sv: Den här studien ger inget att ändra hemma i morgon: den är inget screeningverktyg och ingen stödguide. Om du undrar över någons syn är en ögonspecialist rätt person att fråga. Underlag: en studie med 34 autistiska vuxna och 31 neurotypiska vuxna, vars näthinnor undersöktes med optisk koherenstomografi. De autistiska vuxna hade lägre tjocklek och volym i makulan och i ett av näthinnans lager. Begränsningar: den jämför grupper vid ett enda tillfälle, med få personer; den förklarar inte orsaken, kan inte användas för diagnos och beskriver inte varje autistisk person. Forskarna efterlyser studier som följer människor över tid.

title: Autism spectrum disorder: pathogenesis, biomarker, and intervention therapy.
authors: Zhuang H, Liang Z, Ma G, Qureshi A, Ran X, Feng C, Liu X, Yan X, Shen L
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) has become a common neurodevelopmental disorder. The heterogeneity of ASD poses great challenges for its research and clinical translation. On the basis of reviewing the heterogeneity of ASD, this review systematically summarized the current status and progress of pathogenesis, diagnostic markers, and interventions for ASD. We provided an overview of the ASD molecular mechanisms identified by multi-omics studies and convergent mechanism in different genetic backgrounds. The comorbidities, mechanisms associated with important physiological and metabolic abnormalities (i.e., inflammation, immunity, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial dysfunction), and gut microbial disorder in ASD were reviewed. The non-targeted omics and targeting studies of diagnostic markers for ASD were also reviewed. Moreover, we summarized the progress and methods of behavioral and educational interventions, intervention methods related to technological devices, and research on medical interventions and potential drug targets. This review highlighted the application of high-throughput omics methods in ASD research and emphasized the importance of seeking homogeneity from heterogeneity and exploring the convergence of disease mechanisms, biomarkers, and intervention approaches, and proposes that taking into account individuality and commonality may be the key to achieve accurate diagnosis and treatment of ASD.

sheet.es: Tomorrow morning, lo más útil es recordar que cada persona autista es distinta, y que lo que ayuda a una puede no ayudar a otra. Conviene observar sus preferencias, su ritmo y sus necesidades individuales antes de elegir apoyos educativos o conductuales. La evidencia es una revisión que resume estudios sobre mecanismos biológicos, marcadores diagnósticos e intervenciones. Sus límites: no es un estudio con participantes propios, no ofrece una pauta para cada persona y habla de ideas de investigación todavía en desarrollo. Si aparecen dudas médicas, corresponde decidirlas con un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: Tomorrow morning, the most useful point is that every autistic person is different, and what helps one person may not help another. Before choosing educational or behavioural supports, it helps to notice the person's own preferences, pace and needs. The evidence is a review that summarises studies on biological mechanisms, diagnostic markers and interventions. Its limits: it is not a study with its own participants, it gives no rule that fits everyone, and it describes research ideas that are still developing. Any medical questions are decisions for a clinician.
sheet.sv: I morgon bitti är det mest användbara att komma ihåg att varje autistisk person är unik, och att det som hjälper en kanske inte hjälper en annan. Innan man väljer pedagogiskt eller beteendeinriktat stöd hjälper det att lägga märke till personens egna preferenser, tempo och behov. Underlaget är en översikt som sammanfattar studier om biologiska mekanismer, diagnostiska markörer och insatser. Begränsningar: den har inga egna deltagare, ger ingen regel som passar alla och beskriver forskningsidéer som fortfarande utvecklas. Medicinska frågor avgör man tillsammans med en kliniker.

title: Using mobile health technology to assess childhood autism in low-resource community settings in India: An innovation to address the detection gap.
authors: Dubey I, Bishain R, Dasgupta J, Bhavnani S, Belmonte MK, Gliga T, Mukherjee D, Lockwood Estrin G, Johnson MH, Chandran S, Patel V, Gulati S, Divan G, Chakrabarti B
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autism is diagnosed by highly trained professionals- but most autistic people live in parts of the world that harbour few or no such autism specialists and little autism awareness. So many autistic people go undiagnosed, misdiagnosed, and misunderstood. We designed an app (START) to identify autism and related conditions in such places, in an attempt to address this global gap in access to specialists. START uses computerised games and activities for children and a questionnaire for parents to measure social, sensory, and motor skills. To check whether START can flag undiagnosed children likely to have neurodevelopmental conditions, we tested START with children whose diagnoses already were known: Non-specialist health workers with just a high-school education took START to family homes in poor neighbourhoods of Delhi, India to work with 131 two-to-seven-year-olds. Differences between typically and atypically developing children were highlighted in all three types of skills that START assesses: children with neurodevelopmental conditions preferred looking at geometric patterns rather than social scenes, were fascinated by predictable, repetitive sensory stimuli, and had more trouble with precise hand movements. Parents' responses to surveys further distinguished autistic from non-autistic children. An artificial-intelligence technique combining all these measures demonstrated that START can fairly accurately flag atypically developing children. Health workers and families endorsed START as attractive to most children, understandable to health workers, and adaptable within sometimes chaotic home and family environments. This study provides a proof of principle for START in digital screening of autism and related conditions in community settings.

sheet.es: Si vives en un lugar con pocos especialistas, esta investigación sugiere que una app de cribado podría ayudar algún día a detectar antes a niñas y niños que quizá necesiten apoyos. Por ahora no sustituye una evaluación profesional. Es un estudio con 131 niñas y niños de dos a siete años, en hogares de barrios pobres de Delhi, India. Agentes de salud sin formación especializada usaron la app START, con juegos y un cuestionario para las familias, y detectó con bastante precisión a quienes se desarrollaban de forma atípica. Familias y agentes la valoraron como atractiva y adaptable. Sus límites: es una prueba de concepto, se probó con diagnósticos ya conocidos y no confirma que funcione igual en otros contextos.
sheet.en: If you live where specialists are scarce, this research suggests a screening app might one day help spot earlier those children who may need support. For now it does not replace a professional assessment. It is a study with 131 children aged two to seven, in homes in poor neighbourhoods of Delhi, India. Health workers without specialist training used the START app, with games and a parent questionnaire, and it fairly accurately flagged children developing atypically. Families and health workers found it appealing and adaptable. Its limits: it is a proof of principle, tested on children whose diagnoses were already known, and it does not show the app works the same in other settings.
sheet.sv: Om du bor där det finns få specialister tyder den här forskningen på att en screeningapp i framtiden kan hjälpa till att upptäcka tidigare barn som kan behöva stöd. Just nu ersätter den inte en professionell utredning. Det är en studie med 131 barn mellan två och sju år, i hem i fattiga stadsdelar i Delhi, Indien. Vårdpersonal utan specialistutbildning använde appen START, med spel och ett frågeformulär till föräldrar, och den identifierade ganska träffsäkert barn som utvecklades atypiskt. Familjer och vårdpersonal tyckte den var tilltalande och anpassningsbar. Begränsningar: det är ett principbevis, testat på barn vars diagnoser redan var kända, och det visar inte att appen fungerar likadant i andra miljöer.

title: Short report: Recommendations for education, clinical practice, research, and policy on promoting well-being in autistic youth and adults through a positive focus on sexuality and gender diversity.
authors: Dewinter J, Giwa Onaiwu M, Massolo ML, Caplan R, Van Beneden E, Brörmann N, Crehan ET, Croen LA, Faja S, Gassner DL, Graham Holmes L, Hughes C, Hunter M, Huysamen M, Jelonche P, Lai MC, Noens I, Pukki
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract In this article, we propose recommendations on what we can do to promote that autistic people can enjoy their sexuality and gender identity, because that contributes to overall well-being.First, we briefly summarize the existing research on sexuality and gender diversity in autistic individuals.Next, we propose recommendations for how to promote sexual and gender diversity-related health and well-being. Based on what is known about sexuality, gender diversity, and relationships in autistic adolescents and adults, we convened an international group of autistic and non-autistic researchers, advocates, parents, and professionals to develop recommendations to promote sexual and gender health in autistic people.The resulting recommendations were checked through an online survey distributed to autistic people across the world. The online participants endorsed the importance of eight final recommendations related to:1. Providing education and information on sexuality, relationships, and gender diversity to autistic individuals and their families;2. Improving expertise in and accessibility to healthcare for sexuality, relationships, and gender-related questions, with specific attention to prevention of and support after sexual victimization; and3. Meaningfully including the autism community in future research that addresses well-being relating to sexuality, relationships, and gender diversity.These community-driven recommendations aim to promote sexual health and well-being in autistic individuals internationally.

sheet.es: Hable con la persona autista sobre sexualidad, relaciones y diversidad de género como parte de su bienestar, con información clara y sin juicios, y busque profesionales con formación en el tema. Los autores reunieron a un grupo internacional de personas autistas y no autistas (investigadoras, familias y profesionales) para redactar recomendaciones, y una encuesta en línea a personas autistas respaldó ocho. Piden educación para personas autistas y familias, atención sanitaria accesible, apoyo ante la victimización sexual y participación de la comunidad autista en la investigación. Son recomendaciones, no una prueba de que funcionen, y no sirven igual para todas las personas.
sheet.en: Talk with the autistic person about sexuality, relationships and gender diversity as part of their well-being, giving clear, non-judgemental information, and look for professionals trained in these topics. The authors convened an international group of autistic and non-autistic researchers, advocates, parents and professionals to draft recommendations, and an online survey of autistic people endorsed eight. They call for education for autistic people and families, accessible healthcare, support after sexual victimization, and autistic involvement in research. These are recommendations, not proof that they work, and they will not fit every person equally.
sheet.sv: Prata med den autistiska personen om sexualitet, relationer och könsmångfald som en del av välbefinnandet, med tydlig och icke-dömande information, och sök yrkespersoner med kunskap i ämnet. Författarna samlade en internationell grupp av autistiska och icke-autistiska forskare, intresseföreträdare, föräldrar och yrkespersoner för att ta fram rekommendationer, och en onlineenkät till autistiska personer stödde åtta. De efterlyser utbildning för autistiska personer och familjer, tillgänglig vård, stöd efter sexuellt våld och att autistiska personer deltar i forskningen. Det är rekommendationer, inte bevis för att de fungerar, och de passar inte alla lika bra.

title: Examining a model of anxiety in autistic adults.
authors: Riedelbauch S, Gaigg SB, Thiel T, Roessner V, Ring M
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Abstract Anxiety disorders commonly occur in autism. Existing studies implicate intolerance of uncertainty, alexithymia, sensory processing differences and emotion regulation difficulties as influencing factors of anxiety in autism. To date, a few studies have considered the combination of these factors within the same sample. This study used structural equation modelling to test the prediction that intolerance of uncertainty and emotion regulation constitute more direct causes of anxiety in autism that mediate the influences of sensory processing difference and alexithymia as more sequential contributing factors. Autistic (n = 86) and non-autistic adults (n = 100) completed a battery of self-report questionnaires. Only when applied to each group separately, the broad predictions of the model were confirmed for the autistic group following data-driven additions of paths between sensory processing difference and anxiety and alexithymia implying that sensory processing difference contribute indirectly as well as directly to individual differences in anxiety. For the non-autistic group, model fit could only be achieved after removing autism-related traits and sensory processing differences as predictors of anxiety. These results suggest that aetiology and expression of anxiety in autism partially overlap with what is observed in the general population except that sensory processing differences appear to play a relatively unique role in the context of autism.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta siente ansiedad, puede ayudar fijarse en varias piezas a la vez: la dificultad con la incertidumbre, la regulación de las emociones y las diferencias sensoriales. Anticipar los cambios y reducir la sobrecarga sensorial puede ser un buen punto de partida. Es un estudio con cuestionarios de autoinforme: participaron 86 adultos autistas y 100 adultos no autistas. Sus límites: solo muestra asociaciones en un momento dado, el modelo se ajustó con datos y no sirve como regla para todas las personas. Las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult feels anxious, it may help to look at several pieces together: how hard uncertainty is, how emotions are regulated, and sensory differences. Preparing for changes and easing sensory overload could be a good place to start. This was a study using self-report questionnaires, with 86 autistic adults and 100 non-autistic adults. Its limits: it shows links at one point in time, the model was adjusted using the data, and it is not a rule for every person. Medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen känner ångest kan det hjälpa att se flera delar samtidigt: svårigheter med osäkerhet, känsloreglering och sensoriska skillnader. Att förbereda förändringar och minska sensorisk överbelastning kan vara en bra start. Studien använde självskattningsformulär med 86 autistiska vuxna och 100 icke-autistiska vuxna. Begränsningar: den visar samband vid ett tillfälle, modellen justerades utifrån data och gäller inte som regel för alla. Medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker.

title: Uncovering employment outcomes for autistic university graduates in the United Kingdom: An analysis of population data.
authors: Vincent J, Ralston K
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract International research suggests that more autistic people are entering higher education. Currently, very little is known about this group in the United Kingdom, for example, we have little information about how many autistic people enrol at UK-based higher education institutions, their backgrounds, the academic programmes they study and what they do once they have graduated. Our study tries to explore these issues by comparing outcomes between autistic students, other disabled students and non-disabled students. We use population data collected by the Higher Education Statistical Agency in the United Kingdom, which included 1,326,416 graduates across the years 2012-2018. Our findings indicate that the degree subjects studied at university by autistic students are more diverse than often people think. We also found that graduates go on to work in a range of employment sectors following graduation but often experience worse outcomes in terms of access to full-time work and worse pay. We argue that universities and colleges must focus greater attention on developing better employment transition support for autistic students and graduates.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista que está terminando la universidad, conviene empezar pronto a planificar la transición al empleo: preguntar al servicio de orientación laboral de la universidad qué apoyos ofrece y hablar de sus intereses sin dar por hecho una sola carrera posible. Es un análisis de datos de población del Reino Unido con 1,326,416 graduados entre 2012-2018, que comparó a estudiantes autistas, con otras discapacidades y sin discapacidad. Las personas autistas estudiaron materias muy variadas y trabajaron en distintos sectores, pero a menudo tenían menos acceso a trabajo a tiempo completo y peor salario. Solo describe tendencias de grupo en el Reino Unido y no explica sus causas ni predice a cada persona.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person finishing university, start planning the move into work early: ask the university careers service what support it offers, and talk about their interests without assuming only one career path fits. This was an analysis of UK population data on 1,326,416 graduates from 2012-2018, comparing autistic students, other disabled students and non-disabled students. Autistic graduates studied a wide range of subjects and worked in many sectors, but often had less access to full-time work and lower pay. It only describes group patterns in the UK and does not explain their causes or predict any one person's path.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person som snart tar examen, börja planera övergången till arbete i god tid: fråga universitetets karriärservice vilket stöd som finns och prata om personens intressen utan att utgå från att bara en yrkesväg passar. Det var en analys av brittiska befolkningsdata om 1,326,416 examinerade 2012-2018, där autistiska studenter jämfördes med studenter med andra funktionsnedsättningar och utan funktionsnedsättning. Autistiska examinerade hade mycket varierande ämnen och arbetade inom många sektorer, men hade ofta sämre tillgång till heltidsarbete och lägre lön. Studien beskriver bara gruppmönster i Storbritannien och förklarar inte orsakerna eller förutsäger någon enskild persons väg.

title: Trajectory research in children with an autism diagnosis: A scoping review.
authors: Gentles SJ, Ng-Cordell EC, Hunsche MC, McVey AJ, Bednar ED, DeGroote MG, Chen YJ, Duku E, Kerns CM, Banfield L, Szatmari P, Georgiades S
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract The types of outcomes studied in children on the autism spectrum include clinical characteristics, such as social functioning, communication, language, or autism symptoms. Research that measures these outcomes at multiple timepoints is useful to improve our understanding of what to expect as children develop. In trajectory studies, researchers assess outcomes at three or more timepoints. This method has advantages over two-timepoint studies because it allows researchers to describe changes in the speed of development, such as accelerations, plateaus, or slowdowns. We identified and reviewed 103 published trajectory studies in children (to age 18 years) with an autism diagnosis. Importantly, we did not include studies of treatments or their effects, nor did we summarize the results of studies. Instead, this review summarizes the characteristics of the available published research, including the methods used, the many different outcomes that have been studied over time and the ages over which they have been studied. This summary may be of interest to autistic people and caregivers (parents) who want to know about the existence of research that provides answers about what to expect during an autistic child's development. We have recommended that future trajectory research efforts try to make up for the lack of studies from low- and middle-income countries; that more attention is given to the following outcomes that are meaningful to caregivers and autistic people; and to try to fill in the age gaps where more outcome-specific data are needed.

sheet.es: Si quiere saber qué esperar del desarrollo de su hijo o hija autista, existen estudios que lo siguen a lo largo del tiempo, pero esta revisión no resume sus resultados. Es una revisión de la literatura que describió 103 estudios de trayectoria en niñez y adolescencia (hasta 18 años) con diagnóstico de autismo; no incluyó estudios de tratamientos. Sus límites: solo describe qué se ha investigado, no qué ocurre, y faltan estudios de países de ingresos bajos y medios. Úsela como mapa para buscar información, no como predicción para su hijo o hija.
sheet.en: If you want to know what to expect as your autistic child develops, studies that follow children over time exist, but this review does not summarise their results. It is a scoping review that described 103 trajectory studies of children and teenagers (up to age 18) with an autism diagnosis; it left out studies of treatments. Its limits: it only maps what has been researched, not what happens, and studies from low- and middle-income countries are lacking. Use it as a map for finding information, not as a prediction for your child.
sheet.sv: Om du vill veta vad du kan förvänta dig av ditt autistiska barns utveckling finns studier som följer barn över tid, men den här översikten sammanfattar inte deras resultat. Det är en kartläggande översikt som beskrev 103 studier av utvecklingsförlopp hos barn och unga (upp till 18 år) med autismdiagnos; studier av behandlingar ingick inte. Begränsningar: den visar bara vad som har studerats, inte vad som händer, och studier från låg- och medelinkomstländer saknas. Använd den som en karta för att hitta information, inte som en förutsägelse för ditt barn.

title: Parenting Practices and Externalizing Behaviors in Autistic Children: A Systematic Literature Review.
authors: Suvarna V, Farrell L, Adams D, Emerson LM, Paynter J
journal: Clinical child and family psychology review
abstract: There is limited recent research on the association between parenting practices and externalizing behaviors in autistic children. To address this gap, the current systematic review examined the associations between parenting practices and externalizing behaviors in autistic children, along with the mediating and moderating effects of parent and child variables (PROSPERO registration number CRD42022268667). Study inclusion criteria were (1) Peer-reviewed journals, (2) Participants included parents of autistic children and their children, (3) Quantitative measures of both parenting practices or behaviors/style and child externalizing behaviors, (4) Cross-sectional or longitudinal studies only, and (5) Studies published in English. Study exclusion criteria were: (1) Qualitative studies, (2) Published in a language other than English, (3) Participants included non-human participants, (4) Participants that did not include parents and their autistic children as participants or did not report this group separately, (5) Systematic review and meta-analyses, and (6) No quantitative measures of parenting practices and/or child externalizing behaviors. Quality appraisal and risk of bias were conducted using the McMaster Tool and results were synthesized in Covidence and Excel. Thirty studies were included in the review. Results demonstrated that mindful parenting was associated with fewer or lower levels of externalizing behaviors; positive parenting practices had non-significant associations with externalizing behaviors; specific parenting practices had differing associations with externalizing behaviors; and negative parenting practices were associated with higher levels of externalizing behaviors. We are unable to draw causal relationships due to focus on cross-sectional and longitudinal articles only. The potential for future research to target specific parent practices to support children's externalizing behaviors is discussed.

sheet.es: Si cuida a una niña o un niño autista, puede ser útil practicar una crianza atenta: estar presente, escuchar con calma y responder sin reaccionar de golpe. En esta revisión sistemática, la crianza atenta se asoció con menos conductas externalizantes (las que se dirigen hacia fuera, como gritar o golpear), y las prácticas negativas, con más. Se revisaron 30 estudios de tipo transversal y longitudinal con madres, padres y sus hijos autistas. Sin embargo, estos diseños no permiten saber qué causa qué, y las prácticas concretas mostraron resultados distintos. No es una regla para todas las familias.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic child, it may help to practise mindful parenting: being present, listening calmly and responding without reacting suddenly. In this systematic review, mindful parenting was linked to fewer externalizing behaviors (those directed outward, like shouting or hitting), while negative parenting practices were linked to more. The review covered 30 cross-sectional and longitudinal studies with parents and their autistic children. However, these designs cannot show what causes what, and specific practices had differing results. This is not a rule for every family.
sheet.sv: Om du tar hand om ett autistiskt barn kan det hjälpa att öva sig i medveten föräldraskap: att vara närvarande, lyssna lugnt och svara utan att reagera hastigt. I denna systematiska översikt hängde medvetet föräldraskap ihop med färre externaliserande beteenden (som riktas utåt, till exempel att skrika eller slå), medan negativa föräldrametoder hängde ihop med fler. Översikten omfattade 30 tvärsnitts- och longitudinella studier med föräldrar och deras autistiska barn. Upplägget kan dock inte visa vad som orsakar vad, och enskilda metoder gav olika resultat. Det är ingen regel för alla familjer.

title: Serious Games for Developing Social Skills in Children and Adolescents with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review.
authors: Carneiro T, Carvalho A, Frota S, Filipe MG
abstract: Serious games represent a promising avenue for intervention with children diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder, a neurodevelopmental disorder marked by persistent challenges in social communication and the presence of restricted, repetitive behaviors. Despite this potential, comprehensive reviews on this subject are scarce. This systematic review aims to evaluate the effectiveness of serious games and their specific characteristics in enhancing social skills among children and adolescents with autism. Employing PICO strategies and adhering to PRISMA guidelines, we screened 149 studies initially identified through PubMed and EBSCOhost databases. Nine studies met inclusion criteria and found a positive influence of serious games on social skills and related domains, encompassing emotion recognition/encoding/decoding, emotional regulation, eye gaze, joint attention, and behavioral skills. Nevertheless, despite these promising results, the limited available evidence underscores the need for rigorous study designs to consolidate findings and integrate evidence-based intervention strategies.

sheet.es: Si le interesa que su peque o adolescente autista pruebe juegos serios (videojuegos pensados para practicar habilidades sociales), puede probarlos como una actividad más, observar si le gustan y respetar su ritmo y sus preferencias. Es una revisión sistemática: de 149 estudios revisados, 9 cumplieron los criterios y encontraron una influencia positiva en habilidades sociales y áreas relacionadas, como reconocer emociones, regularlas y la atención conjunta. Sin embargo, la evidencia es limitada y hacen falta estudios más rigurosos, así que no sirve como regla para todas las personas ni garantiza resultados.
sheet.en: If your autistic child or teen is curious about serious games (video games designed to practise social skills), you could try them as one activity among others, watch whether they enjoy them, and follow their pace and preferences. This is a systematic review: of 149 studies screened, 9 met the criteria and found a positive influence on social skills and related areas, such as recognising and regulating emotions and joint attention. However, the evidence is limited and more rigorous studies are needed, so it is not a rule for everyone and promises no particular result.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn eller din tonåring är nyfiken på seriösa spel (datorspel utformade för att öva sociala färdigheter) kan du prova dem som en aktivitet bland andra, se om de tycker om dem och följa deras tempo och önskemål. Det här är en systematisk översikt: av 149 granskade studier uppfyllde 9 kriterierna och fann en positiv påverkan på sociala färdigheter och närliggande områden, som att känna igen och reglera känslor samt gemensam uppmärksamhet. Evidensen är dock begränsad och mer rigorösa studier behövs, så resultaten gäller inte alla och ger inga garantier.

title: Participatory translational science of neurodivergence: model for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder and autism research.
authors: Sonuga-Barke EJS, Chandler S, Lukito S, Kakoulidou M, Moore G, Cooper N, Matejko M, Jackson I, Balwani B, Boyens T, Poulton D, Harvey-Nguyen L, Baker S, Pavlopoulou G, RE-STAR team*
journal: The British journal of psychiatry : the journal of mental science
abstract: Background There are increasing calls for neurodivergent peoples' involvement in research into neurodevelopmental conditions. So far, however, this has tended to be achieved only through membership of external patient and public involvement (PPI) panels. The Regulating Emotions - Strengthening Adolescent Resilience (RE-STAR) programme is building a new participatory model of translational research that places young people with diagnoses of attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and autism at the heart of the research team so that they can contribute to shaping and delivering its research plan. Aims To outline the principles on which the RE-STAR participatory model is based and describe its practical implementation and benefits, especially concerning the central role of members of the Youth Researcher Panel (Y-RPers). Method The model presented is a culmination of a 24-month process during which Y-RPers moved from advisors to co-researchers integrated within RE-STAR. It is shaped by the principles of co-intentionality. The account here was agreed following multiple iterative cycles of collaborative discussion between academic researchers, Y-RPers and other stakeholders. Results Based on our collective reflections we offer general guidance on how to effectively integrate young people with diagnoses of ADHD and/or autism into the core of the translational research process. We also describe the specific theoretical, methodological and analytical benefits of Y-RPer involvement in RE-STAR. Conclusions Although in its infancy, RE-STAR has demonstrated the model's potential to enrich translational science in a way that can change our understanding of the relationship between autism, ADHD and mental health. When appropriately adapted we believe the model can be applied to other types of neurodivergence and/or mental health conditions.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija adolescente es autista o tiene TDAH, su voz puede valer mucho más que una opinión puntual: puede ayudar a decidir qué se investiga y cómo. Mañana puedes preguntarle qué temas le importan y, si le interesa, buscar proyectos que integren a jóvenes como co-investigadores, no solo como asesores. Este artículo describe el modelo RE-STAR, construido durante 24 meses en el que jóvenes autistas y con TDAH pasaron de asesores a miembros del equipo investigador. Es una reflexión colectiva, no un ensayo que mida resultados, y el propio programa reconoce que está en sus inicios.
sheet.en: If your teenager is autistic or has ADHD, their voice can count for much more than a one-off opinion: they can help decide what gets researched and how. Tomorrow you might ask them which topics matter to them and, if they are interested, look for projects that include young people as co-researchers, not just advisors. This paper describes the RE-STAR model, built over 24 months as autistic and ADHD young people moved from advisors to full members of the research team. It is a collective reflection rather than a trial measuring outcomes, and the programme itself says it is still in its early stages.
sheet.sv: Om din tonåring är autistisk eller har adhd kan deras röst betyda mycket mer än en enstaka åsikt: de kan vara med och bestämma vad som forskas på och hur. I morgon kan du fråga vilka frågor som känns viktiga för dem och, om de vill, leta efter projekt där unga är medforskare och inte bara rådgivare. Artikeln beskriver modellen RE-STAR, som växte fram under 24 månader när autistiska unga och unga med adhd gick från rådgivare till fullvärdiga medlemmar i forskargruppen. Det är en gemensam reflektion, inte en studie som mäter effekter, och programmet beskriver sig självt som i ett tidigt skede.

title: A US national update of health condition prevalence among privately-insured autistic adults.
authors: Longo A, Radford D, Hand BN
abstract: Aim: Previous research using state or regional samples has shown that autistic adults have a higher prevalence of health conditions in comparison to the general population. Methods: To build upon this important previous research, we conducted a cross-sectional retrospective study of 2019-2020 healthcare claims to determine the prevalence of conditions in a US national sample of privately insured autistic adults (n = 30,258) and an age- and sex-matched population comparison (n = 60,516) group of adults without autism diagnoses. Results: Like previous studies, we found that autistic adults had significantly greater odds of most mental and physical health conditions. However, our prevalence estimates differed from previous studies for several mental and physical health conditions. For example, our sample of autistic adults had higher prevalence of anxiety disorders (55%) and attention deficit hyperactivity disorders (34%), but lower prevalence of asthma (9%) and sleep disorders (3%) than previous studies. Discussion & conclusion: Our use of a large US national sample, more recent healthcare claims data, and different methods for identifying health conditions may have contributed to these differences. Our findings alert healthcare providers and policymakers to the health conditions most common among the growing population of autistic adults. We hope these findings lead to improved screening and management of these conditions, inform initiatives to improve access to healthcare, and guide future funding.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista adulta, puede ser útil preguntar en la próxima cita médica por la salud física y mental, y pedir que se revisen ambas con regularidad. Es un estudio retrospectivo que analizó datos de seguros médicos privados de 2019-2020 en EE. UU.: 30,258 adultos autistas y 60,516 adultos sin diagnóstico de autismo. Los adultos autistas tenían más probabilidades de presentar la mayoría de las condiciones de salud mental y física; por ejemplo, ansiedad (55%). Los límites: solo incluye a personas con seguro privado y diagnóstico registrado, y no explica las causas ni describe a cada persona.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult, it may help to ask at the next medical appointment for regular checks of both physical and mental health. This was a retrospective study of private health insurance claims from 2019-2020 in the US: 30,258 autistic adults and 60,516 adults without an autism diagnosis. Autistic adults had higher odds of most mental and physical health conditions; for example, anxiety disorders (55%). Limits: it covers only people with private insurance and recorded diagnoses, it does not explain causes, and it cannot describe any one person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen kan det hjälpa att be om regelbundna kontroller av både fysisk och psykisk hälsa vid nästa vårdbesök. Studien var retrospektiv och byggde på privata sjukförsäkringsdata från 2019-2020 i USA: 30,258 autistiska vuxna och 60,516 vuxna utan autismdiagnos. Autistiska vuxna hade högre odds för de flesta psykiska och fysiska tillstånd, till exempel ångestsyndrom (55%). Begränsningar: den omfattar bara personer med privat försäkring och registrerad diagnos, förklarar inte orsaker och kan inte beskriva en enskild person.

title: Co-designing behavioural activation for depression for autistic adolescents: A case series.
authors: Mohamed Z, Russell A, Palmer M, Simonoff E, Hollocks MJ
abstract: Autistic youth are at high risk of depression , but there are few psychological interventions that have been specifically designed for use with this population. Behavioural activation (BA) is a particularly promising approach for autistic adolescents, having an established evidence-base for the treatment of depression in non-autistic people, and with a strong focus on behavioural, rather than cognitive change, which is a challenge for some autistic people. In this study, we worked with autistic adolescents and clinicians to co-design a BA-informed intervention to be delivered in an online format. We then conducted a pilot case-series with seven autistic adolescents with depression. Our focus was on establishing the acceptability and feasibility of the intervention but clinical outcomes on both self- and parent-reported symptoms of depression and anxiety are also presented. Our results indicate the intervention to be acceptable and feasible for autistic adolescents, with six out of seven participants being retained to the end of the intervention. Qualitative feedback indicated that all participants found the intervention a positive experience and would recommend it to others. Similarly, all participants found the online format acceptable, with 64% preferring this format to face-to-face therapy. Qualitative feedback and suggestions for refinement will also be discussed.

sheet.es: Si un adolescente autista tiene depresión, puede valer la pena preguntar a su equipo clínico por la activación conductual en línea, que se centra en actividades y acciones más que en cambiar pensamientos. Es un estudio piloto de serie de casos, diseñado junto con adolescentes autistas y profesionales, con siete adolescentes autistas con depresión. Seis de los siete completaron la intervención, todos la valoraron como una experiencia positiva y el 64% prefirió el formato en línea a la terapia presencial. Sin embargo, el grupo es muy pequeño y no hubo grupo de comparación, así que no demuestra eficacia ni sirve para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic teenager has depression, it may be worth asking their clinical team about online behavioural activation, which focuses on activities and actions rather than on changing thoughts. This was a small pilot case series, co-designed with autistic adolescents and clinicians, with seven autistic adolescents with depression. Six out of seven stayed to the end, all found it a positive experience, and 64% preferred the online format to face-to-face therapy. However, the group was very small and had no comparison group, so it cannot show that the approach works or that it suits everyone.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk tonåring har depression kan det vara värt att fråga vårdteamet om beteendeaktivering på nätet, som fokuserar på aktiviteter och handlingar snarare än på att ändra tankar. Det var en liten pilotstudie (fallserie), utformad tillsammans med autistiska tonåringar och kliniker, med sju autistiska tonåringar med depression. Sex av sju fullföljde, alla upplevde det som positivt och 64 % föredrog nätformatet framför mottagningsbesök. Gruppen var dock mycket liten och saknade jämförelsegrupp, så studien visar inte att metoden fungerar eller passar alla.

title: "…in the middle of nowhere…" Access to, and quality of, services for autistic adults from parents' perspectives: a qualitative study.
authors: Németh V, Győri M, Ehmann B, Völgyesi-Molnár M, Stefanik K
abstract: Introduction Adequate education, employment, and services for autistic individuals contribute significantly to their and their parents' quality of life. Services and support for adults are dramatically more limited than those for children. The main purpose of this study was to explore how parents perceive factors supporting/hindering access to services, and how they assess the quality of services. Methods Qualitative data provided by 12 parents via a semi-structured interview with a broader focus on parental quality of life and its factors were analyzed. Their autistic children were between 20 and 34 years of age. A thematic analysis was performed on parts of the narratives on their adult periods of life. Results A complex pattern of parental perception of supportive and hampering factors influencing access to services unfolded. The sparsity of services/activities and reliable information on them made the space for autonomous decisions on service take highly limited. Parents have modest expectations on quality of services, evaluating them along two key aspects: a safe, positive atmosphere, and communication between parents and professionals. Other aspects of individualized autism-specific support were not or just rarely mentioned. Discussion Parents perceive themselves as investing a lot of effort and resources in getting some form of regular service and/or activity for their adult child. However, these parental efforts often fail, their child becoming inactive, and dependent on their presence. This suggests system-level problems with services for autistic adults in Hungary, with literature showing it is not specific to this country.

sheet.es: Si buscas servicios para tu hijo o hija autista adulta, empieza por observar si el lugar ofrece un ambiente seguro y positivo, y si los profesionales se comunican bien contigo; son los dos criterios que las familias de este estudio más valoraron. Pide la información por escrito y anota lo que encuentres. Se trata de un estudio cualitativo con entrevistas a 12 madres y padres de jóvenes autistas de entre 20 y 34 años. Sus límites: es un grupo muy pequeño, de Hungría, y no recoge la voz de las propias personas autistas, así que no vale para todas las familias.
sheet.en: If you are looking for services for your autistic adult child, start by checking whether the place offers a safe, positive atmosphere and whether professionals communicate well with you; these were the two criteria families in this study valued most. Ask for information in writing and keep notes on what you find. This was a qualitative study based on interviews with 12 parents of autistic young adults aged between 20 and 34. Its limits: the group is very small, comes from Hungary, and does not include the voices of autistic adults themselves, so it cannot speak for every family.
sheet.sv: Om du söker stöd för ditt autistiska vuxna barn kan du börja med att se om platsen har en trygg, positiv stämning och om personalen kommunicerar bra med dig. Det var de två kriterier som föräldrarna i studien värderade mest. Be om information skriftligt och anteckna vad du hittar. Det här är en kvalitativ studie med intervjuer av 12 föräldrar till autistiska unga vuxna mellan 20 och 34 år. Begränsningarna: gruppen är mycket liten, kommer från Ungern och inkluderar inte de autistiska vuxnas egna röster, så den gäller inte alla familjer.

title: Autism-related language preferences of English-speaking individuals across the globe: A mixed methods investigation.
authors: Keating CT, Hickman L, Leung J, Monk R, Montgomery A, Heath H, Sowden S
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Over the past two decades, there have been increasing discussions around which terms should be used to talk about autism. Whilst these discussions have largely revolved around the suitability of identity-first language and person-first language, more recently this debate has broadened to encompass other autism-related terminology (e.g., 'high-functioning'). To date, academic studies have not investigated the language preferences of autistic individuals outside of the United Kingdom or Australia, nor have they compared levels of endorsement across countries. Hence, the current study adopted a mixed-methods approach, employing both quantitative and qualitative techniques, to explore the linguistic preferences of 654 English-speaking autistic adults across the globe. Despite variation in levels of endorsement between countries, we found that the most popular terms were similar-the terms 'Autism', 'Autistic person', 'Is autistic', 'Neurological/Brain Difference', 'Differences', 'Challenges', 'Difficulties', 'Neurotypical people', and 'Neurotypicals' were consistently favored across countries. Despite relative consensus across groups, both our quantitative and qualitative data demonstrate that there is no universally accepted way to talk about autism. Our thematic analysis revealed the reasons underlying participants' preferences, generating six core themes, and illuminated an important guiding principle-to respect personal preferences. These findings have significant implications for informing practice, research and language policy worldwide.

sheet.es: Pregunta a la persona autista cómo prefiere que se hable de su autismo y usa sus palabras. Si aún no lo sabes, 'autista' o 'persona autista' son opciones que muchas personas prefirieron. Este estudio mixto, con 654 adultos autistas de habla inglesa de distintos países, halló términos favoritos parecidos entre países, pero ninguna forma aceptada por todas las personas. Sus límites: participaron adultos que hablan inglés, así que no refleja necesariamente a niños ni a otros idiomas. Respetar la preferencia personal es el principio central.
sheet.en: Ask the autistic person how they prefer autism to be talked about, and use their words. If you don't know yet, 'autistic' or 'autistic person' are terms many people favored. This mixed-methods study of 654 English-speaking autistic adults across the globe found similar favorite terms between countries, but no way of talking about autism that everyone accepts. Its limits: participants were English-speaking adults, so it may not reflect children or other languages. Respecting personal preference is the central principle.
sheet.sv: Fråga den autistiska personen hur hen vill att man talar om autism, och använd hens ord. Om du inte vet ännu är 'autistisk' eller 'autistisk person' termer som många föredrog. Den här studien med blandade metoder, med 654 engelskspråkiga autistiska vuxna runt om i världen, fann liknande favoritord mellan länder, men inget sätt att tala om autism som alla godtar. Begränsningar: deltagarna var engelskspråkiga vuxna, så resultaten gäller inte nödvändigtvis barn eller andra språk. Att respektera personliga önskemål är den centrala principen.

title: Efficacy of very early interventions on neurodevelopmental outcomes for infants and toddlers at increased likelihood of or diagnosed with autism: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: McGlade A, Whittingham K, Barfoot J, Taylor L, Boyd RN
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: The aim of this systematic review was to determine the efficacy of very early interventions for infants and toddlers at increased likelihood of or diagnosed with autism for autism symptomatology, developmental outcomes and/or neurocognitive markers. Eight databases were searched (14 April 2022) with inclusion criteria: (i) RCTs with care as usual (CAU) comparison group, (ii) participants at increased likelihood of or diagnosed with autism and aged <24 months corrected age (CA), (iii) parent-mediated and/or clinician directed interventions, and (iv) outcome measures were autism symptomatology, cognition, language, adaptive skills, or neurocognitive assessments (EEG and eye tracking). Quality was assessed using Risk of Bias 2 and GRADE. Nineteen publications from 12 studies reported on 715 infants and toddlers. There was low to moderate certainty evidence that clinician-assessed outcomes did not show significant treatment effects for: autism symptomatology (ADOS CSS: MD -0.08, 95% CI -0.61, 0.44, p = 0.75), cognitive outcome (Mullen Scales of Early Learning-Early Learning Composite (MSEL-ELC): SMD 0.05, 95% CI -0.19, 0.29, p = 0.67), receptive language (MSEL-Receptive Language: SMD 0.04, 95% CI -0.21, 0.3, p = 0.74) or expressive language (MSEL-Expressive Language: SMD 0.06, 95% CI -0.1, 0.23, p = 0.45). Neurocognitive outcomes (EEG and eye tracking) were heterogeneous, with inconsistent findings. There is low to moderate certainty evidence that very early interventions have limited impact on neurodevelopmental outcomes by age 3 years.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija es muy pequeño y autista, o tiene mayor probabilidad de serlo, no hace falta vivir la intervención temprana como una carrera. Conviene valorar si el apoyo encaja con la familia y con las necesidades del niño o la niña, y si es llevadero en el día a día. La evidencia es un metaanálisis de ensayos aleatorizados: 12 estudios con 715 bebés y niños pequeños menores de 24 meses. Con certeza baja a moderada, las evaluaciones de profesionales no mostraron efectos significativos en síntomas de autismo, cognición ni lenguaje; los resultados neurocognitivos fueron dispares. Los límites: mide promedios hasta los 3 años y no refleja el bienestar, la comunicación cotidiana ni cada caso individual.
sheet.en: If your child is very young and autistic, or likely to be, early support doesn't need to feel like a race. It helps to ask whether the support fits your family and your child's needs, and whether it is manageable day to day. The evidence is a meta-analysis of randomised trials: 12 studies with 715 infants and toddlers under 24 months. With low to moderate certainty, clinician-assessed outcomes showed no significant effects on autism symptoms, cognition or language; neurocognitive results were mixed. Limits: it looks at group averages up to age 3 and does not capture wellbeing, everyday communication or any individual child.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn är mycket litet och autistiskt, eller sannolikt är det, behöver tidigt stöd inte kännas som ett lopp. Fundera på om stödet passar familjen och barnets behov och om det går att hantera i vardagen. Evidensen är en metaanalys av randomiserade studier: 12 studier med 715 spädbarn och småbarn under 24 månader. Med låg till måttlig säkerhet visade bedömningar av kliniker inga signifikanta effekter på autismsymtom, kognition eller språk; de neurokognitiva resultaten varierade. Begränsningar: studien visar gruppgenomsnitt upp till 3 års ålder och fångar inte välmående, vardagskommunikation eller enskilda barn.

title: The role of anxiety and depression in suicidal thoughts for autistic and non-autistic people: A theory-driven network analysis.
authors: Pelton MK, Crawford H, Bul K, Robertson AE, Adams J, de Beurs D, Rodgers J, Baron-Cohen S, Cassidy S
abstract: Background Autistic adults experience more frequent suicidal thoughts and mental health difficulties than non-autistic adults, but research has yet to explain how these experiences are connected. This study explored how anxiety and depression contribute to suicidal thoughts according to the Interpersonal Theory of Suicide for autistic and non-autistic adults. Methods Participants (autistic adults n = 463, 61% female; non-autistic n = 342, 64% female) completed online measures of anxiety, depression, thwarted belonging, and perceived burdensomeness. Network analysis explored whether: (i) being autistic is a risk marker for suicide; and (ii) pathways to suicidal thoughts are consistent for autistic and non-autistic adults. Results Being autistic connected closely with feeling like an outsider, anxiety, and movement, which connected to suicidal thoughts through somatic experiences, low mood, and burdensomeness. Networks were largely consistent for autistic and non-autistic people, but connections from mood symptoms to somatic and thwarted belonging experiences were absent for autistic adults. Conclusion Autistic people experience more life stressors than non-autistic people leading to reduced coping, low mood, and suicidal thoughts. Promoting belonging, reducing anxiety, and understanding the role of movement could inform suicide prevention for autistic people. Research should accurately capture autistic lived experience when modeling suicide to ensure suicide prevention meets autistic needs.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista, puede ayudar prestar atención a su sensación de pertenencia, a su ansiedad y a si siente que es una carga para otros, y hablar de ello con calma y sin juzgar. Es un estudio en línea con personas autistas (n = 463) y no autistas (n = 342) que completaron cuestionarios sobre ansiedad, depresión, pertenencia y sentirse una carga. Los resultados describen patrones de grupo, no explican a una persona concreta, y no demuestran causas. Si te preocupa alguien, busca ayuda profesional: un clínico, un servicio de salud o un servicio de crisis. Si hay peligro inmediato, llama al número de emergencias de tu país.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person, it may help to notice their sense of belonging, their anxiety, and whether they feel like a burden to others, and to talk about it calmly and without judgement. This was an online study with autistic adults (n = 463) and non-autistic adults (n = 342) who completed questionnaires on anxiety, depression, belonging and feeling like a burden. The results describe group patterns, do not explain any one person, and do not prove causes. If you are worried about someone, seek professional help: a clinician, a health service or a crisis service. In immediate danger, call the emergency number of your country.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person kan det hjälpa att lägga märke till känslan av tillhörighet, ångest och om personen upplever sig vara en börda, och att prata om det lugnt och utan att döma. Det var en webbaserad studie med autistiska vuxna (n = 463) och icke-autistiska vuxna (n = 342) som fyllde i frågeformulär om ångest, depression, tillhörighet och att känna sig som en börda. Resultaten beskriver gruppmönster, förklarar inte en enskild person och visar inte orsaker. Om du är orolig för någon, sök professionell hjälp: en läkare eller annan vårdgivare, en hälsoverksamhet eller en krisjour. Vid akut fara, ring ditt lands nödnummer.

title: Mediation of 6-year mid-childhood follow-up outcomes after pre-school social communication (PACT) therapy for autistic children: randomised controlled trial.
authors: Carruthers S, Pickles A, Charman T, McConachie H, Le Couteur A, Slonims V, Howlin P, Collum R, Salomone E, Tobin H, Gammer I, Maxwell J, Aldred C, Parr J, Leadbitter K, Green J
journal: Journal of child psychology and psychiatry, and allied disciplines
abstract: Background There are very few mechanistic studies of the long-term impact of psychosocial interventions in childhood. The parent-mediated Paediatric Autism Communication Therapy (PACT) RCT showed sustained effects on autistic child outcomes from pre-school to mid-childhood. We investigated the mechanism by which the PACT intervention achieved these effects. Methods Of 152 children randomised to receive PACT or treatment as usual between 2 and 5 years of age, 121 (79.6%) were followed 5-6 years after the endpoint at a mean age of 10.5 years. Assessors, blind to the intervention group, measured Autism Diagnostic Observation Scale Calibrated Severity Score (ADOS CSS) for child autistic behaviours and Teacher Vineland (TVABS) for adaptive behaviour in school. Hypothesised mediators were child communication initiations with caregivers in a standard play observation (Dyadic Communication Measure for Autism, DCMA). Hypothesised moderators of mediation were baseline child non-verbal age equivalent scores (AE), communication and symbolic development (CSBS) and 'insistence on sameness' (IS). Structural equation modelling was used in a repeated measures mediation design. Results Good model fits were obtained. The treatment effect on child dyadic initiation with the caregiver was sustained through the follow-up period. Increased child initiation at treatment midpoint mediated the majority (73%) of the treatment effect on follow-up ADOS CSS. A combination of partial mediation from midpoint child initiations and the direct effect of treatment also contributed to a near-significant total effect on follow-up TVABS. No moderation of this mediation was found for AE, CSBS or IS. Conclusions Early sustained increase in an autistic child's communication initiation with their caregiver is largely responsible for the long-term effects from PACT therapy on autistic and adaptive behaviour outcomes. This supports the theoretical logic model of PACT therapy but also illuminates fundamental causal processes of social and adaptive development in autism over time: early social engagement in autism can be improved and this can have long-term generalised outcome effects.

sheet.es: Idea práctica: dar a tu hijo o hija autista muchas oportunidades para iniciar la comunicación contigo en el juego, y responder a esos intentos, puede ser un buen foco. Evidencia: ensayo controlado aleatorizado con 152 niños autistas de 2 a 5 años, que recibieron terapia PACT mediada por madres y padres o atención habitual; 121 fueron seguidos hasta una edad media de 10.5 años. Los autores concluyen que el aumento temprano de las iniciativas comunicativas explicó gran parte de los efectos a largo plazo. Límites: es un análisis estadístico de un solo programa, no prueba que sirva igual a cada niño, y un resultado en la escuela quedó cerca de ser significativo, no confirmado.
sheet.en: Practical idea: giving your autistic child plenty of chances to start communication with you during play, and responding to those attempts, may be a useful focus. Evidence: a randomised controlled trial of 152 autistic children aged 2 to 5, who received parent-mediated PACT therapy or usual treatment; 121 were followed up at a mean age of 10.5 years. The authors conclude that early increases in the child's communication initiations explained much of the long-term effects. Limits: this is a statistical analysis of one programme, it does not show it works the same for every child, and one school-based outcome was only near-significant, not confirmed.
sheet.sv: Praktisk idé: att ge ditt autistiska barn många chanser att ta egna kommunikationsinitiativ med dig i leken, och att svara på dem, kan vara ett bra fokus. Evidens: en randomiserad kontrollerad studie med 152 autistiska barn i åldern 2 till 5 år som fick föräldramedierad PACT-terapi eller sedvanlig behandling; 121 följdes upp vid en medelålder på 10.5 år. Författarna drar slutsatsen att tidigt ökade kommunikationsinitiativ förklarade en stor del av de långsiktiga effekterna. Begränsningar: det är en statistisk analys av ett enda program, det visar inte att det fungerar likadant för varje barn, och ett skolresultat var bara nära signifikant, inte bekräftat.

title: Psychological interventions targeting mental health and the mother-child relationship in autism: Systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Kulasinghe K, Whittingham K, Mitchell AE, Boyd RN
abstract: Aim To investigate the efficacy of psychological interventions delivered to mothers of young children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in improving maternal mental health and the parent-child relationship. Method Electronic databases were searched from inception to December 2021. Studies were included if they were randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of psychological interventions that targeted maternal mental health (primary outcome) and/or the parent-child relationship (secondary outcome), delivered to mothers of children (mean age Results Thirty-two RCTs met the inclusion criteria (2336 participants). Six RCTs showed improved maternal mental health (Cohen's d = 0.41-1.15), with moderate certainty of evidence for improvement in parental stress. There was low and high certainty of evidence of treatment effect on parental depressive symptoms and general mental health respectively, which did not show significant treatment effects post-intervention. Seventeen RCTs showed improved parent-child relationship (d = 0.33-2.28; low certainty of evidence). Interpretation Results demonstrated that parenting interventions promoting responsiveness had the largest positive effect on the parent-child relationship and a moderate effect on overall parenting stress; however, the studies were heterogeneous, making it difficult to identify the intervention components that were responsible for the positive treatment effects. There was no significant treatment effect for studies targeting depression or general mental health, likely due to the lack of an interventional component directly targeting mental health.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a un niño autista pequeño, los programas psicológicos que enseñan a responder con sensibilidad a sus señales pueden mejorar la relación entre madre e hijo y aliviar algo el estrés de crianza. Conviene preguntar qué incluye cada programa. La evidencia es un metaanálisis de 32 ensayos aleatorizados con 2336 participantes, dirigidos a madres de niños autistas pequeños. Sus límites: los estudios eran muy distintos entre sí, no se sabe qué componentes funcionan, la certeza fue baja o moderada y no hubo efectos claros sobre la depresión ni la salud mental general. No sirve como regla para toda familia.
sheet.en: If you care for a young autistic child, psychological programmes that teach responsive parenting, meaning tuning in to the child's cues, may strengthen the mother-child relationship and ease some parenting stress. It is worth asking what a programme actually includes. The evidence is a meta-analysis of 32 randomized controlled trials with 2336 participants, delivered to mothers of young autistic children. Its limits: the studies differed a lot, so it is unclear which components work, certainty was low to moderate, and there were no clear effects on depression or general mental health. It is not a rule for every family.
sheet.sv: Om du har ett litet autistiskt barn kan psykologiska program som lär ut lyhört föräldraskap, att fånga upp barnets signaler, stärka relationen mellan mor och barn och lätta en del av föräldrastressen. Fråga gärna vad ett program faktiskt innehåller. Underlaget är en metaanalys av 32 randomiserade kontrollerade studier med 2336 deltagare, riktade till mödrar till små autistiska barn. Begränsningar: studierna skilde sig mycket åt, så det är oklart vilka delar som fungerar, tillförlitligheten var låg till måttlig och inga tydliga effekter sågs på depression eller allmän psykisk hälsa. Det är ingen regel för alla familjer.

title: Cross-cultural variation in experiences of acceptance, camouflaging and mental health difficulties in autism: A registered report.
authors: Keating CT, Hickman L, Geelhand P, Takahashi T, Leung J, Monk R, Schuster B, Rybicki A, Girolamo TM, Clin E, Papastamou F, Belenger M, Eigsti IM, Cook JL, Kosaka H, Osu R, Okamoto Y, Sowden-Carvalho S
abstract: Recent findings suggest that stigma and camouflaging contribute to mental health difficulties for autistic individuals, however, this evidence is largely based on UK samples. While studies have shown cross-cultural differences in levels of autism-related stigma, it is unclear whether camouflaging and mental health difficulties vary across cultures. Hence, the current study had two aims: (1) to determine whether significant relationships between autism acceptance, camouflaging, and mental health difficulties replicate in a cross-cultural sample of autistic adults, and (2) to compare these variables across cultures. To fulfil these aims, 306 autistic adults from eight countries (Australia, Belgium, Canada, Japan, New Zealand, South Africa, the United Kingdom, and the United States) completed a series of online questionnaires. We found that external acceptance and personal acceptance were associated with lower levels of depression but not camouflaging or stress. Higher camouflaging was associated with elevated levels of depression, anxiety, and stress. Significant differences were found across countries in external acceptance, personal acceptance, depression, anxiety, and stress, even after controlling for relevant covariates. Levels of camouflaging also differed across countries however this effect became non-significant after controlling for the covariates. These findings have significant implications, identifying priority regions for anti-stigma interventions, and highlighting countries where greater support for mental health difficulties is needed.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista, tómate en serio el desgaste de ocultar o disimular rasgos autistas, y favorece espacios donde pueda ser como es, sin presión por "pasar por neurotípica". Es un estudio con cuestionarios en línea en el que participaron 306 adultos autistas de ocho países. La aceptación se asoció con menos depresión, y más camuflaje con más depresión, ansiedad y estrés. Los niveles diferían entre países. Sus límites: solo muestra asociaciones, no causas, y no sirve como regla para cada persona ni para su país.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person, take the toll of hiding or masking autistic traits seriously, and help create spaces where they can be themselves without pressure to "pass" as non-autistic. This was an online questionnaire study with 306 autistic adults from eight countries. Acceptance was linked to lower depression, and more camouflaging was linked to more depression, anxiety and stress. Levels differed between countries. Limits: it shows associations, not causes, and it is not a rule for every person or every country.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person: ta på allvar tröttheten som kan följa av att dölja eller maskera autistiska drag, och skapa miljöer där personen kan vara sig själv utan krav på att "passera" som icke-autistisk. Det var en studie med webbenkäter där 306 autistiska vuxna från åtta länder deltog. Acceptans hängde ihop med mindre depression, och mer kamouflering hängde ihop med mer depression, ångest och stress. Nivåerna skilde sig mellan länder. Begränsningar: studien visar samband, inte orsaker, och är ingen regel för varje person eller land.

title: Effects of Parent-Delivered Traditional Thai Massage on Gait and Heart Rate Variability in Children with Autism: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
authors: Ruan H, Eungpinichpong W, Wu H, Wu H, Aonsri C
journal: Journal of integrative and complementary medicine
abstract: Aim: To examine the effects of parent-delivered traditional Thai massage (TTM) intervention on heart rate variability (HRV) and gait in children with autism. Methods: This was a two-armed, randomized controlled trial conducted at the Haikou Special Education School in Haikou Province, China, between October 2021 and March 2022. A total of 48 children with autism, aged between 7 and 12 years, were selected from the school and randomly divided into either the parent-delivered TTM group or the control group (no intervention) in a 1:1 ratio. In addition to their regular daily school routines, the TTM group received 16 TTM interventions (twice a week), with each session lasting ∼50 min. HRV and gait parameters were measured at baseline, completion of the 8-week intervention, and 2 months follow-up. Results: The results of this study showed that the TTM intervention had a notable positive effect on HRV, with a significant reduction in low-frequency value ( p = 0.001), and increased high-frequency value ( p = 0.001), compared with the controls, and the advantages persisted during the follow-up period. However, only the stride length in the TTM group was significantly longer than that in the control group at the post-test ( p = 0.039) and follow-up test ( p = 0.043), while none of the other parameters of gait comparison showed statistical significance. Conclusions: Parent-delivered Thai massage increased HRV levels and stride length in comparison to the control group, and some effects of the intervention were maintained over the follow-up period. Clinical Trials Registry Identifier ChiCTR2100051355; September 21, 2021.

sheet.es: Si le interesa el contacto físico como parte de la rutina, un masaje tailandés tradicional dado por madres o padres podría ser una actividad compartida, siempre que a la persona autista le resulte agradable y pueda pararlo cuando quiera. Fue un ensayo aleatorizado con 48 niños autistas de 7 a 12 años en una escuela de China; el grupo de masaje tuvo 16 sesiones y se comparó con un grupo sin intervención. Mostró cambios en la variabilidad de la frecuencia cardíaca y una zancada más larga, pero no en los demás parámetros de la marcha. Es un estudio pequeño, de un solo lugar, y no demuestra que sirva a todas las personas.
sheet.en: If physical touch is already part of your routine, a traditional Thai massage given by a parent could be a shared activity, as long as the autistic person enjoys it and can stop whenever they want. This was a randomized trial with 48 autistic children aged 7 to 12 at a school in China; the massage group had 16 sessions and was compared with a group receiving no intervention. It found changes in heart rate variability and a longer stride length, but not in the other gait measures. It was a small study at one site, and it does not show that this works for everyone.
sheet.sv: Om fysisk beröring redan är en del av vardagen kan thaimassage som ges av en förälder vara en gemensam aktivitet, så länge den autistiska personen tycker om det och kan avbryta när hon eller han vill. Det var en randomiserad studie med 48 autistiska barn i åldern 7 till 12 år på en skola i Kina; massagegruppen fick 16 tillfällen och jämfördes med en grupp utan insats. Studien visade förändringar i hjärtfrekvensvariabilitet och längre steglängd, men inte i de andra gångmåtten. Den var liten och gjordes på ett enda ställe, och visar inte att det fungerar för alla.
