title: Functional contribution of the intestinal microbiome in autism spectrum disorder, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, and Rett syndrome: a systematic review of pediatric and adult studies.
authors: Caputi V, Hill L, Figueiredo M, Popov J, Hartung E, Margolis KG, Baskaran K, Joharapurkar P, Moshkovich M, Pai N
abstract: Introduction Critical phases of neurodevelopment and gut microbiota diversification occur in early life and both processes are impacted by genetic and environmental factors. Recent studies have shown the presence of gut microbiota alterations in neurodevelopmental disorders. Here we performed a systematic review of alterations of the intestinal microbiota composition and function in pediatric and adult patients affected by autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and Rett syndrome (RETT). Methods We searched selected keywords in the online databases of PubMed, Cochrane, and OVID (January 1980 to December 2021) with secondary review of references of eligible articles. Two reviewers independently performed critical appraisals on the included articles using the Critical Appraisal Skills Program for each study design. Results Our systematic review identified 18, 7, and 3 original articles describing intestinal microbiota profiles in ASD, ADHD, and RETT, respectively. Decreased Firmicutes and increased Bacteroidetes were observed in the gut microbiota of individuals affected by ASD and ADHD. Proinflammatory cytokines, short-chain fatty acids and neurotransmitter levels were altered in ASD and RETT. Constipation and visceral pain were related to changes in the gut microbiota in patients affected by ASD and RETT. Hyperactivity and impulsivity were negatively correlated with Faecalibacterium (phylum Firmicutes) and positively correlated with Bacteroides sp. (phylum Bacteroidetes) in ADHD subjects. Five studies explored microbiota-or diet-targeted interventions in ASD and ADHD. Probiotic treatments with Lactobacillus sp. and fecal microbiota transplantation from healthy donors reduced constipation and ameliorated ASD symptoms in affected children. Perinatal administration of Lactobacillus sp. prevented the onset of Asperger and ADHD symptoms in adolescence. Micronutrient supplementation improved disease symptomatology in ADHD without causing significant changes in microbiota communities' composition. Discussion Several discrepancies were found among the included studies, primarily due to sample size, variations in dietary practices, and a high prevalence of functional gastrointestinal symptoms. Further studies employing longitudinal study designs, larger sample sizes and multi-omics technologies are warranted to identify the functional contribution of the intestinal microbiota in developmental trajectories of the human brain and neurobehavior. Systematic review registration https://clinicaltrials.gov/, CRD42020158734.

title: Access and cost of services for autistic children and adults in Italy: a carers' perspective.
authors: Micai M, Fulceri F, Salvitti T, Romano G, Scattoni ML
abstract: Background Limited information exists on autistic service access and costs in Italy. Objectives This study aims to investigate access to educational, healthcare, social, and related services for autistic individuals in Italy as part of the Autism Spectrum Disorder in the European Union (ASDEU) project. Methods Italian carers of autistic individuals completed an online survey regarding services and costs in the 6 months before completion. Results Three hundred and three carers of autistic people participated in the survey. The majority of those receiving care were children, males, and lived at home with their parents. Autistic adults were often students (17%) or unemployed but willing to work (17%). Employed carers (49%) worked on average 32.23 ± 9.27 hours per week. A significant portion (82%) took work or school absences to care for autistic individuals, averaging 15.56 ± 14.70 days. On average, carers spent 58.84 ± 48.36 hours per week on caregiving duties. Fifty-five of the autistic individuals received some form of support, 5% utilized residential care, and 6% were hospitalized. Thirty-four percent received outpatient hospital care, and 20% underwent some form of autism-related psychopharmacological therapy. School support was primarily provided by support teachers (18.16 ± 7.02 hours/week). Educational psychologists (80.73%), psychomotor therapists/physiotherapists (53.85%), and speech therapists (50.91%) were frequently paid by carers who paid more per hour. Autistic children received support from educators (73.96 hours/week), group therapy (32.36 hours/week), and speech therapists (31.19 hours/week). Psychologists (76.00%) and counseling/individual therapists (89.13%) were often paid by carers. Carers reported high costs for psychiatrists and psychologists, with frequent use of psychiatric services (8 ± 8 times in 6 months). Conclusions Carers' perspectives on the access and costs of services for autistic individuals in Italy can provide insights into areas for improvement in the delivery of autism services.

title: Toward recovery-oriented perinatal healthcare: A participatory qualitative exploration of persons with lived experience and health providers' views and experiences.
authors: Dubreucq M, Thiollier M, Tebeka S, Fourneret P, Leboyer M, Viaux-Savelon S, Massoubre C, Dupont C, Dubreucq J
journal: European psychiatry : the journal of the Association of European Psychiatrists
abstract: Background Perinatal mental health disorders (PMHD) remain often undetected, undiagnosed, and untreated with variable access to perinatal mental health care (PMHC). To guide the design of optimal PMHC (i.e., coproduced with persons with lived experience [PLEs]), this qualitative participatory study explored the experiences, views, and expectations of PLEs, obstetric providers (OP), childcare health providers (CHPs), and mental health providers (MHPs) on PMHC and the care of perinatal depression. Methods We conducted nine focus groups and 24 individual interviews between December 2020 and May 2022 for a total number of 84 participants (24 PLEs; 30 OPs; 11 CHPs; and 19 MHPs). The PLEs group included women with serious mental illness (SMI) or autistic women who had contact with perinatal health services. We recruited PLEs through social media and a center for psychiatric rehabilitation, and health providers (HPs) through perinatal health networks. We used the inductive six-step process by Braun and Clarke for the thematic analysis. Results We found some degree of difference in the identified priorities between PLEs (e.g., personal recovery, person-centered care) and HPs (e.g., common culture, communication between providers, and risk management). Personal recovery in PMHD corresponded to the CHIME framework, that is, connectedness, hope, identity, meaning, and empowerment. Recovery-supporting relations and peer support contributed to personal recovery. Other factors included changes in the socio-cultural conception of the peripartum, challenging stigma (e.g., integrating PMH into standard perinatal healthcare), and service integration. Discussion This analysis generated novel insights into how to improve PMHC for all users including those with SMI or autism.

sheet.es: Si estás en el embarazo o el posparto, puede ayudarte pedir a los profesionales una atención centrada en ti y preguntar por el apoyo de otras personas con experiencia propia. Es un estudio cualitativo con 84 participantes: 24 personas con experiencia vivida (mujeres con enfermedad mental grave o mujeres autistas) y profesionales de obstetricia, salud infantil y salud mental, mediante grupos focales y entrevistas. Las personas con experiencia vivida valoraron la recuperación personal y la atención centrada en la persona; los profesionales, la comunicación entre equipos y el manejo del riesgo. Es una exploración de opiniones, no prueba qué funciona mejor, y las experiencias de cada persona pueden ser distintas.
sheet.en: If you are pregnant or postpartum, it may help to ask providers for care centred on you, and to ask about support from others with lived experience. This was a qualitative study using focus groups and interviews with 84 participants: 24 people with lived experience (women with serious mental illness or autistic women), plus obstetric, child health and mental health providers. People with lived experience prioritised personal recovery and person-centred care; providers stressed communication between teams and risk management. It explores views and does not prove what works best, and each person's experience may differ.
sheet.sv: Om du är gravid eller nyförlöst kan det hjälpa att be vården om stöd som utgår från dig och att fråga om stöd från andra med egen erfarenhet. Studien var kvalitativ, med fokusgrupper och intervjuer med 84 deltagare: 24 personer med egen erfarenhet (kvinnor med allvarlig psykisk sjukdom eller autistiska kvinnor) samt vårdgivare inom förlossning, barnhälsa och psykiatri. De med egen erfarenhet prioriterade personlig återhämtning och personcentrerad vård; vårdgivarna lyfte kommunikation mellan team och riskhantering. Studien undersöker åsikter och visar inte vad som fungerar bäst, och varje persons erfarenhet kan se annorlunda ut.

title: Supporting autistic communities through parent-led and child/young person-led digital social story interventions: an exploratory study.
authors: Camilleri LJ, Maras K, Brosnan M
abstract: Introduction Social Stories (SS) is a socially-valid intervention for autistic children and young people (CYP) which is used widely by professionals and parents. Research suggests that whilst parents are in an ideal position to deliver interventions for their autistic CYP, a lack of procedural integrity can result in a great deal of variability in parent-mediated intervention outcomes. Methods This exploratory study investigated the extent to which SS can be effectively developed and delivered, through digital mediation, by parents with little to no researcher input ( n = 17, sample 1) and the factors that impact effectiveness. Furthermore, the study also investigated the extent to which digitally-mediated SS can support autistic CYP to develop and deliver their own stories, thereby utilising the intervention as a means for self-support and self-management ( n = 5, sample 2). Results The outcomes of the study indicate that digital mediation can effectively support parent-led SS intervention. Findings also indicate that receptive/expressive language skills of autistic CYP, their level of systemizing, as well as the practice of consulting with the autistic CYP whilst identifying goals and developing stories, are individual and procedural characteristics which positively influence the effectiveness of the parent-led intervention. The study also found that digitally-mediated SS can be utilised as a self-support tool by autistic CYP themselves. Discussion The results inform the developing literature on digital interventions and support tools that aim to engage with, and involve further, the autistic community in the setting and authoring of interventions and research.

sheet.es: Si piensa usar Historias Sociales con su hijo o hija autista, pruebe a consultarle al elegir el objetivo y al escribir la historia juntos; una herramienta digital puede ayudar a prepararla. Se trata de un estudio exploratorio con 17 familias que crearon las historias por su cuenta y 5 niños y jóvenes autistas que hicieron las suyas. Los resultados apuntan a que la mediación digital apoyó la intervención dirigida por madres y padres, y que consultar al niño o joven ayudó. El estudio es pequeño y exploratorio, así que no sirve como regla para todas las personas; cada persona es distinta.
sheet.en: If you are thinking of using Social Stories with your autistic child or young person, try asking for their input when choosing the goal and writing the story together; a digital tool may help you prepare it. This was a small exploratory study: 17 parents created stories with little researcher input, and 5 autistic children and young people wrote their own. Results suggest digital support helped parent-led stories, and that consulting the young person made them work better. Because the study was small and exploratory, it is not a rule for everyone, and each person is different.
sheet.sv: Om du funderar på att använda sociala berättelser med ditt autistiska barn eller din unga person kan du fråga hen om synpunkter när ni väljer mål och skriver berättelsen tillsammans; ett digitalt verktyg kan hjälpa till i förberedelserna. Detta var en liten utforskande studie: 17 föräldrar skapade berättelser med lite stöd från forskarna, och 5 autistiska barn och unga skrev egna berättelser. Resultaten tyder på att digitalt stöd hjälpte förälderledda berättelser och att det gynnade när den unga fick vara delaktig. Studien var liten och utforskande, så den är ingen regel för alla; varje person är olika.

title: Harnessing the Power of Mobile Phone Technology: Screening and Identifying Autism Spectrum Disorder With Smartphone Apps.
authors: Reddy K, Taksande A, Kurian B
abstract: Integrating smartphone applications into screening and identifying autism spectrum disorder (ASD) represents a promising and innovative frontier within healthcare. This forward-looking paper examines the current landscape of ASD screening apps, shedding light on their potential advantages and addressing and navigating significant challenges. One of the most compelling aspects of these apps lies in their potential to democratize access to ASD screening, effectively breaking down geographical barriers. By using the widespread availability of smartphones, these apps make it possible for individuals, caregivers, and healthcare providers to engage in early ASD screening from virtually anywhere. This accessibility is especially crucial in underserved areas or regions with limited access to specialized healthcare services. Moreover, these apps offer a degree of objectivity that traditional screening methods may need help to match. By relying on data-driven algorithms and machine learning, they can provide a more impartial assessment of a child's behavior, minimizing the potential for subjective bias. This objectivity, combined with the ability to monitor and assess a child's development over time, empowers caregivers with valuable insights into their child's progress. However, as with any technological advancement in healthcare, integrating smartphone apps for ASD screening is not without its share of ethical and privacy considerations. Ensuring informed consent is obtained, especially when collecting data from children, is complex and critical. Striking the right balance between collecting necessary data and protecting an individual's privacy requires careful thought and transparent communication. Additionally, the "digital divide" represents a challenge that needs to be acknowledged and addressed. Not all individuals and families have equal access to smartphones or the technological literacy required to use these apps effectively. This disparity in access must be considered when developing and implementing app-based screening solutions to prevent exacerbating existing healthcare inequalities. Nevertheless, the future of ASD screening apps holds significant promise. Advancements in technology, including integrating advanced sensors, wearables, augmented reality, and machine learning, can further enhance the accuracy and depth of screening. Interdisciplinary collaboration between researchers, developers, clinicians, and educators is crucial to ensure that these apps are effective, culturally sensitive, and user-friendly. Furthermore, integrating these apps into broader healthcare systems, including electronic health records and telehealth platforms, can streamline the screening process and enable a more seamless transition from screening to diagnosis and intervention.

sheet.es: Si le preocupa el desarrollo de su hijo o hija y vive lejos de servicios especializados, una app de cribado puede ser una forma de dar un primer paso, pero no sustituye una evaluación profesional. Antes de usarla, consulte cómo se tratan los datos y qué consentimiento se pide. Esta es una revisión que describe el panorama de las apps de cribado del autismo, sus posibles ventajas y sus dificultades. No presenta resultados propios con participantes. Además, no todas las familias tienen el mismo acceso a smartphones, y la objetividad que se atribuye a estas apps no es una garantía para cada niño o niña.
sheet.en: If you are concerned about your child's development and live far from specialist services, a screening app may be a way to take a first step, but it does not replace a professional assessment. Before using one, check how the data is handled and what consent is requested. This is a review describing the landscape of autism screening apps, their possible advantages and their difficulties. It does not report its own results from participants. Not every family has the same access to smartphones, and the objectivity claimed for these apps is not a guarantee for every child.
sheet.sv: Om du oroar dig för ditt barns utveckling och bor långt från specialistvård kan en screeningapp vara ett första steg, men den ersätter inte en professionell bedömning. Kontrollera innan du använder en app hur data hanteras och vilket samtycke som krävs. Detta är en översikt som beskriver hur appar för autismscreening ser ut, deras möjliga fördelar och svårigheter. Den redovisar inga egna resultat från deltagare. Inte alla familjer har samma tillgång till smartphones, och den objektivitet som appar sägs ge är ingen garanti för varje barn.

title: Dropping the mask: It takes two.
authors: Cook JM, Crane L, Mandy W
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract In some situations, autistic people feel pressure to change their social behaviour by camouflaging. In other situations, autistic people feel they don't need to change their social behaviour. Instead, they feel they can socialise in ways that feel authentic or true to themselves. Past research has tended to focus on autistic people's experiences of camouflaging rather than their experiences of authenticity. In this study, we asked autistic people what it is like for them when they can socialise in ways that feel authentic or true to themselves. Autistic people described authentic-feeling socialising as more free, spontaneous and open than camouflaging. In supportive environments, this kind of socialising had more positive and less negative consequences than camouflaging. Autistic people felt that having self-awareness and acceptance of their own social needs and being around autistic and nonautistic people who were accepting and understanding helped them to socialise in authentic-feeling ways. Autistic people also spoke about communication behaviours they felt nonautistic people should use to help overcome misunderstandings and create autism-friendly social environments. These findings suggest it is helpful for autistic people to have access to supportive and accepting social environments in which they feel able to socialise in ways that feel authentic to them. In creating such social environments, it is important to focus on nonautistic people's knowledge and attitude towards autistic people and also their ability to use helpful communication behaviours.

sheet.es: Tras una jornada de máscara, ayuda crear ratos en los que la persona autista pueda relacionarse sin tener que cambiar su forma de ser, con gente que la acepte y la entienda. Como cuidador, puedes informarte sobre sus necesidades sociales y adaptar tu forma de comunicarte. La evidencia es un estudio cualitativo en el que participaron personas autistas, que describieron la socialización auténtica como más libre, espontánea y abierta que el camuflaje. Sus límites: refleja experiencias concretas de quienes participaron y no sirve como regla para todas las personas autistas; conviene preguntar a cada persona qué le resulta cómodo.
sheet.en: After a day of masking, it helps to make room for time when an autistic person can socialise without changing how they are, with people who accept and understand them. As a caregiver, you can learn about their social needs and adapt how you communicate. The evidence is a study with autistic people, who described authentic-feeling socialising as more free, spontaneous and open than camouflaging. Its limits: it reflects the experiences of those who took part and is not a rule for every autistic person, so ask each person what feels comfortable for them.
sheet.sv: Efter en dag med maskering kan det hjälpa att skapa utrymme där den autistiska personen får umgås utan att förändra sig, tillsammans med människor som accepterar och förstår. Som anhörig kan du lära dig om personens sociala behov och anpassa hur du kommunicerar. Underlaget är en studie med autistiska personer, som beskrev äkta umgänge som friare, mer spontant och öppnare än att kamouflera sig. Begränsningar: den speglar erfarenheter hos dem som deltog och gäller inte som regel för alla autistiska personer, så fråga var och en vad som känns bra.

title: Understanding the post-diagnostic support priorities of autistic adults in the United Kingdom: A co-produced modified Delphi study.
authors: Crowson S, Poole D, Scargill K, Freeth M
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic adults in the United Kingdom report that support for themselves and their peers is not suitable for their needs. There has been an increase in adults receiving an autism diagnosis, which many have reported as having a positive impact on their lives. However, the lack of support and understanding after diagnosis, combined with long wait times for an assessment to obtain a diagnosis and to access follow-on support, is having a negative impact on people's lives. This study took place to find out what support autistic people need and want after receiving their diagnosis. It was co-designed with a group of 10 autistic adults which means that the researchers and group members collaboratively designed the research. For the study, 43 autistic adults, diagnosed aged 18 or older, completed three questionnaires. A fourth questionnaire followed that was completed by 139 autistic people who received their diagnosis in adulthood. These questionnaires aimed to help people identify their own priorities when it came to the support they would have liked to receive after being given their autism diagnosis. Participants ranked access to support where they live , training of professionals , support to process the impact of a late diagnosis , use of their preferred mode of contact and a personalised support plan as their top priorities. This demonstrates that local support is highly valued by autistic adults, as are well-trained professionals who offer a range of contact options, support to process a late-in-life autism diagnosis and help to develop and implement support plans.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista que ha recibido el diagnóstico de adulta, pregúntale qué apoyo quiere: cerca de casa, con profesionales formados, por el canal de contacto que prefiera, con ayuda para procesar un diagnóstico tardío y con un plan personalizado. Es un estudio con autistas en el Reino Unido, diseñado junto con 10 adultos autistas: 43 completaron tres cuestionarios y 139 un cuarto. Sus prioridades salen de ahí, pero no sirven como regla para cada persona, y el estudio no prueba qué apoyos funcionan mejor.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person diagnosed as an adult, ask what help they want: support close to home, trained professionals, their preferred way of being contacted, help processing a late diagnosis, and a personalised support plan. This was a study with autistic people in the United Kingdom, co-designed with 10 autistic adults: 43 completed three questionnaires and 139 completed a fourth. These were their top priorities, but they are not a rule for every person, and the study does not test which supports work best.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person som fått sin diagnos som vuxen, fråga vilket stöd hen vill ha: stöd nära hemmet, utbildad personal, hens föredragna kontaktsätt, hjälp att bearbeta en sen diagnos och en personlig stödplan. Det här var en studie med autistiska personer i Storbritannien, utformad tillsammans med 10 autistiska vuxna: 43 besvarade tre enkäter och 139 en fjärde. Det var deras främsta prioriteringar, men de gäller inte alla, och studien prövar inte vilket stöd som fungerar bäst.

title: Autistic Adults Show Intact Learning on a Visuospatial Serial Reaction Time Task.
authors: Treves IN, Cannon J, Shin E, Li CE, Bungert L, O'Brien A, Cardinaux A, Sinha P, Gabrieli JDE
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Some theories have proposed that autistic individuals have difficulty learning predictive relationships. We tested this hypothesis using a serial reaction time task in which participants learned to predict the locations of a repeating sequence of target locations. We conducted a large-sample online study with 61 autistic and 71 neurotypical adults. The autistic group had slower overall reaction times, but demonstrated sequence-specific learning equivalent to the neurotypical group, consistent with other findings of typical procedural memory in autism. The neurotypical group, however, made significantly more prediction-related errors early in the experiment when the stimuli changed from repeated sequences to random locations, suggesting certain limited behavioural differences in the learning or utilization of predictive relationships for autistic adults.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista o eres autista, este estudio sugiere que aprender patrones repetidos mediante la práctica puede funcionar igual de bien; conviene ofrecer tiempo y repetición sin dar por hecho que habrá dificultades. Fue un estudio en línea con 61 adultos autistas y 71 adultos neurotípicos que debían anticipar la posición de objetivos en una secuencia repetida. El grupo autista respondió más despacio en general, pero aprendió la secuencia igual. Los neurotípicos cometieron más errores de predicción cuando la secuencia pasó a ser aleatoria. Sus límites: era una tarea de laboratorio con adultos, no refleja la vida diaria y no sirve como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person, or are autistic, this study suggests that learning repeated patterns through practice can work just as well, so offer time and repetition without assuming difficulty. It was an online study with 61 autistic adults and 71 neurotypical adults, who learned to predict where targets would appear in a repeating sequence. The autistic group responded more slowly overall but learned the sequence equally well. The neurotypical group made more prediction errors when the sequence turned random. Limits: it was a lab-style task with adults, it does not reflect everyday life, and it is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person, eller själv är autistisk, tyder studien på att det kan gå lika bra att lära sig upprepade mönster genom övning. Ge gärna tid och repetition utan att anta att det blir svårt. Det var en onlinestudie med 61 autistiska vuxna och 71 neurotypiska vuxna som skulle förutsäga var mål dök upp i en upprepad sekvens. Den autistiska gruppen svarade långsammare överlag men lärde sig sekvensen lika bra. De neurotypiska gjorde fler förutsägelsefel när sekvensen blev slumpmässig. Begränsningar: det var en laboratorieliknande uppgift med vuxna, den speglar inte vardagen och gäller inte som regel för alla.

title: Attention-deficit Hyperactivity Disorder and Autism Spectrum Disorder: Towards Better Diagnosis and Management.
authors: Al Ghamdi K, AlMusailhi J
abstract: Background Attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHA) is one of the most common comorbid disorders of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) that can accompany autism, triggered by it, or be a consequence of it. Objective This review explored the prevalence of the comorbidity of both disorders, neurobiological background, symptoms, latest assessment methods, and therapeutic approaches. Results and Discussion: It concluded that effective assessment, diagnosis and management of ADHD in ASD children and adults is essential for this group of patients to thrive and live a good quality of life. Further research is recommended to explore the most effective intervention for such important members of our society. Conclusion More studies are needed to understand the mechanisms underlying these comorbidities, and to prevent the misdiagnosis and mismanagement of these disorders. Also, to develop up to date personalized therapeutic plans for such children.

sheet.es: Si cree que una persona autista también tiene rasgos de TDAH, como dificultad para sostener la atención o inquietud constante, anótelos con ejemplos concretos y llévelos a una evaluación con profesionales que conozcan ambas condiciones. Una valoración cuidadosa ayuda a evitar diagnósticos erróneos y a ajustar el apoyo. La evidencia es una revisión de la literatura sobre niños y adultos autistas con TDAH; el resumen no detalla estudios concretos. Sus límites: concluye que faltan investigaciones sobre qué intervenciones funcionan mejor, así que no ofrece una receta válida para todas las personas. Las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If you think an autistic person may also have ADHD traits, such as trouble holding attention or constant restlessness, jot down concrete examples and bring them to an assessment with professionals who know both conditions. Careful assessment helps avoid misdiagnosis and shapes better support. The evidence is a review of the literature on autistic children and adults with ADHD; the abstract does not describe individual studies. Its limits: it says more research is needed on which interventions work best, so it offers no recipe that fits everyone. Medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om du tror att en autistisk person också har ADHD-drag, som svårigheter att hålla uppmärksamheten eller ständig rastlöshet, skriv ner konkreta exempel och ta med dem till en utredning hos yrkesverksamma som känner till båda tillstånden. En noggrann bedömning hjälper till att undvika felaktiga diagnoser och anpassa stödet. Underlaget är en översikt av litteraturen om autistiska barn och vuxna med ADHD; sammanfattningen beskriver inga enskilda studier. Begränsningar: den säger att mer forskning behövs om vilka insatser som fungerar bäst, så den ger inget recept för alla. Medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker.

title: Retinal GABAergic Alterations in Adults with Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Huang Q, Ellis CL, Leo SM, Velthuis H, Pereira AC, Dimitrov M, Ponteduro FM, Wong NML, Daly E, Murphy DGM, Mahroo OA, McAlonan GM
journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
abstract: Alterations in γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) have been implicated in sensory differences in individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Visual signals are initially processed in the retina, and in this study, we explored the hypotheses that the GABA-dependent retinal response to light is altered in individuals with ASD. Light-adapted electroretinograms were recorded from 61 adults (38 males and 23 females; n = 22 ASD) in response to three stimulus protocols: (1) the standard white flash, (2) the standard 30 Hz flickering protocol, and (3) the photopic negative response protocol. Participants were administered an oral dose of placebo, 15 or 30 mg of arbaclofen (STX209, GABA B agonist) in a randomized, double-blind, crossover order before the test. At baseline (placebo), the a-wave amplitudes in response to single white flashes were more prominent in ASD, relative to typically developed (TD) participants. Arbaclofen was associated with a decrease in the a-wave amplitude in ASD, but an increase in TD, eliminating the group difference observed at baseline. The extent of this arbaclofen-elicited shift significantly correlated with the arbaclofen-elicited shift in cortical responses to auditory stimuli as measured by using an electroencephalogram in our prior study and with broader autistic traits measured with the autism quotient across the whole cohort. Hence, GABA-dependent differences in retinal light processing in ASD appear to be an accessible component of a wider autistic difference in the central processing of sensory information, which may be upstream of more complex autistic phenotypes.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista reacciona de forma distinta a la luz, puede ser una diferencia sensorial real y no una exageración; conviene tenerlo en cuenta al ajustar la iluminación y ofrecer pausas. Fue un ensayo con 61 adultos, 22 de ellos autistas, que midió la respuesta de la retina a la luz. Fue un estudio médico con un fármaco: las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico. Es un grupo pequeño de adultos, no incluye a niños y no demuestra qué ocurre en cada persona ni sirve como regla general.
sheet.en: If an autistic person reacts differently to light, it may be a real sensory difference rather than an exaggeration; it is worth keeping in mind when adjusting lighting and offering breaks. This was a trial with 61 adults, 22 of them autistic, measuring the retina's response to light. It was a medical study involving a drug, so medical decisions belong to a clinician. The group was small and made up of adults, children were not included, and it does not show what happens for any one person or serve as a rule for everyone.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person reagerar annorlunda på ljus kan det vara en verklig sensorisk skillnad och inte en överdrift; det är värt att ha i åtanke när du justerar belysningen och erbjuder pauser. Det var en studie med 61 vuxna, varav 22 autistiska, som mätte näthinnans svar på ljus. Det var en medicinsk studie med ett läkemedel, och medicinska beslut hör till en läkare. Gruppen var liten och bestod av vuxna, barn ingick inte, och studien visar inte vad som gäller för varje person eller som en regel för alla.

title: Systematic review and meta-analysis: multimodal functional and anatomical neural alterations in autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Guo Z, Tang X, Xiao S, Yan H, Sun S, Yang Z, Huang L, Chen Z, Wang Y
abstract: Background This meta-analysis aimed to explore the most robust findings across numerous existing resting-state functional imaging and voxel-based morphometry (VBM) studies on the functional and structural brain alterations in individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Methods A whole-brain voxel-wise meta-analysis was conducted to compare the differences in the intrinsic functional activity and gray matter volume (GMV) between individuals with ASD and typically developing individuals (TDs) using Seed-based d Mapping software. Results A total of 23 functional imaging studies (786 ASD, 710 TDs) and 52 VBM studies (1728 ASD, 1747 TDs) were included. Compared with TDs, individuals with ASD displayed resting-state functional decreases in the left insula (extending to left superior temporal gyrus [STG]), bilateral anterior cingulate cortex/medial prefrontal cortex (ACC/mPFC), left angular gyrus and right inferior temporal gyrus, as well as increases in the right supplementary motor area and precuneus. For VBM meta-analysis, individuals with ASD displayed decreased GMV in the ACC/mPFC and left cerebellum, and increased GMV in the left middle temporal gyrus (extending to the left insula and STG), bilateral olfactory cortex, and right precentral gyrus. Further, individuals with ASD displayed decreased resting-state functional activity and increased GMV in the left insula after overlapping the functional and structural differences. Conclusions The present multimodal meta-analysis demonstrated that ASD exhibited similar alterations in both function and structure of the insula and ACC/mPFC, and functional or structural alterations in the default mode network (DMN), primary motor and sensory regions. These findings contribute to further understanding of the pathophysiology of ASD.

sheet.es: Este estudio no ofrece nada que cambiar mañana por la mañana en casa: describe diferencias medias en el cerebro, no lo que una persona necesita. Para apoyar a alguien autista, sigue siendo más útil observar sus preferencias y su manera de percibir y comunicarse. Es un metaanálisis que reunió 23 estudios de imagen funcional (786 personas autistas, 710 con desarrollo típico) y 52 estudios de volumen de materia gris (1728 autistas, 1747 con desarrollo típico). Encontró diferencias en la ínsula y en regiones frontales. Sus límites: compara promedios de grupo, no explica causas y no sirve para valorar a una persona concreta.
sheet.en: This study gives nothing to change at home tomorrow morning: it describes average brain differences, not what a person needs. To support an autistic person, it is still more useful to notice their preferences and how they sense and communicate. It is a meta-analysis that combined 23 functional imaging studies (786 autistic people, 710 typically developing) and 52 grey matter volume studies (1728 autistic, 1747 typically developing). It found differences in the insula and frontal regions. Its limits: it compares group averages, does not explain causes, and cannot be used to judge any individual person.
sheet.sv: Den här studien ger inget att ändra hemma i morgon bitti: den beskriver genomsnittliga skillnader i hjärnan, inte vad en person behöver. För att stödja en autistisk person är det fortfarande mer användbart att lägga märke till personens preferenser och hur hen uppfattar och kommunicerar. Det är en metaanalys som slog ihop 23 funktionella bildstudier (786 autistiska, 710 med typisk utveckling) och 52 studier av grå substans (1728 autistiska, 1747 med typisk utveckling). Den fann skillnader i insula och frontala områden. Begränsningar: den jämför gruppgenomsnitt, förklarar inte orsaker och kan inte användas för att bedöma en enskild person.

title: Facilitators and barriers in psychotherapy from the perspective of autistic adults: an enhanced critical incident study.
authors: Jubenville-Wood T, Nicholas DB, Weiss J, Cairns S
journal: International journal of qualitative studies on health and well-being
abstract: Purpose A significant portion of autistic adults experience mental health challenges. Currently, the literature is incomplete when it comes to understanding the needs and preferences of autistic adults who receive therapy. This study elicited the perspectives of autistic adults, focusing on the facilitators, barriers and ways to enhance psychotherapy based on receiving this care for mental health problems. Methods Using the qualitative, exploratory approach of the Enhanced Critical Incident Technique, eight autistic adults took part in interviews. Results A total of 147 critical incidents were extracted from participant interviews and categories salient to therapeutic practice. The study identified key factors influencing therapy, such as trust and respect, practical approaches, client factors, structure of sessions, knowledge about autism, support for individualized needs, access to mental health services, and involvement of family/advocate. These factors were categorized into eight main areas relevant to therapeutic practice. Conclusions Findings from this research reveal that psychotherapy with autistic adults is analogous to performing this work with non-autistic adults, in the sense that this work too entails elements of individually tailored treatment and the reliance on common therapeutic factors. There are also differences in this work that necessitate providers having foundational knowledge about autism. Learning directly from autistic adults' insights may help to improve upon the delivery of mental health care for autistic adults.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista adulta en terapia, puede ayudar hablar con ella de lo que necesita: confianza y respeto, sesiones con estructura clara, adaptaciones individuales y terapeutas que conozcan el autismo. Eso es lo que señalaron las personas participantes. La evidencia es un estudio cualitativo con entrevistas a 8 adultos autistas, de las que salieron 147 incidentes críticos. Sus límites: es un grupo muy pequeño y la experiencia de cada persona es distinta, así que no sirve como regla general. Úsalo como punto de partida para conversar con la persona y con su terapeuta.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult in therapy, it may help to talk with them about what they need: trust and respect, clear session structure, individual adjustments, and a therapist who understands autism. These are the factors participants named. The evidence is a qualitative study based on interviews with 8 autistic adults, from which 147 critical incidents were extracted. Its limits: the group is very small and every person's experience differs, so it is not a rule for everyone. Use it as a starting point for conversation with the person and their therapist.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen i terapi kan det hjälpa att prata om vad personen behöver: tillit och respekt, tydlig struktur i sessionerna, individuella anpassningar och en terapeut som förstår autism. Det var dessa faktorer deltagarna lyfte. Underlaget är en kvalitativ studie med intervjuer av 8 autistiska vuxna, som gav 147 kritiska händelser. Begränsningar: gruppen är mycket liten och varje persons erfarenhet är olika, så det är ingen regel för alla. Använd det som en utgångspunkt för samtal med personen och dennes terapeut.

title: Perceived misdiagnosis of psychiatric conditions in autistic adults.
authors: Kentrou V, Livingston LA, Grove R, Hoekstra RA, Begeer S
abstract: Background Many autistic people, particularly women, do not receive an autism diagnosis until adulthood, delaying their access to timely support and clinical care. One possible explanation is that autistic traits may initially be misinterpreted as symptoms of other psychiatric conditions, leading some individuals to experience misdiagnosis of other psychiatric conditions prior to their autism diagnosis. However, little is currently known about the frequency and nature of psychiatric misdiagnoses in autistic adults. Methods Using data collected in the first half of 2019 from an ongoing longitudinal register of autistic adults in the Netherlands, this study explored the frequency of perceived psychiatric misdiagnoses before receiving an autism diagnosis. Gender differences were also explored. A sample of 1211 autistic adults (52.6% women, mean age 42.3 years), the majority of whom were Dutch and relatively highly educated, was evaluated. Findings Results showed that 24.6% ( n = 298) of participants reported at least one previous psychiatric diagnosis that was perceived as a misdiagnosis. Personality disorders were the most frequent perceived misdiagnoses, followed by anxiety disorders, mood disorders, chronic fatigue syndrome/burnout-related disorders, and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder. Autistic women (31.7%) reported perceived misdiagnoses more frequently than men (16.7%). Women were specifically more likely than men to report perceived misdiagnoses of personality disorders, anxiety disorders, and mood disorders. Women also reported prior psychiatric diagnoses more often in general (65.8% versus 34.2% in men). Within the group of individuals with a prior diagnosis, perceived misdiagnoses were equally likely for men and women. Interpretation One in four autistic adults, and one in three autistic women, reported at least one psychiatric diagnosis, obtained prior to being diagnosed with autism, that was perceived as a misdiagnosis. Inaccurate diagnoses are linked to long diagnostic pathways and delayed recognition of autism. These findings highlight the need for improved training of mental health practitioners, in order to improve their awareness of the presentation of autism in adulthood and of the complex relationship between autism and co-occurring conditions. The current study constitutes a first step towards showing that autistic adults, and particularly women, may be at greater risk of experiencing misdiagnoses. Future studies based on larger, more representative samples are required, to replicate current findings and provide more reliable estimates of the overall frequency of misdiagnoses as well as the frequency of misdiagnoses for specific psychiatric conditions. Funding This study was made possible by funding from the Netherlands Organisation for Health Research and Development (ZonMW), project number 60-63600-98-834.

sheet.es: Si tú o la persona a la que cuidas recibisteis antes otros diagnósticos psiquiátricos que nunca encajaron del todo, puede valer la pena revisarlos con un profesional que conozca el autismo en adultos. Llevar por escrito el historial y las experiencias propias ayuda a esa conversación, sin descartar que algunas condiciones sí coexistan. Este estudio neerlandés preguntó a 1211 adultos autistas: una de cada cuatro personas, y una de cada tres mujeres, sentía que algún diagnóstico previo había sido erróneo, sobre todo trastornos de personalidad, ansiedad o ánimo. Sus límites: se basa en la percepción de los participantes, no en una revisión clínica, y la muestra era mayoritariamente neerlandesa y con estudios altos.
sheet.en: If you or the person you support received earlier psychiatric diagnoses that never quite fit, it may be worth reviewing them with a clinician who understands autism in adulthood. Bringing a written history and your own experiences can help that conversation, while keeping in mind that some conditions genuinely co-occur. This Dutch study surveyed 1,211 autistic adults: one in four, and one in three women, felt at least one earlier diagnosis had been wrong, most often personality, anxiety or mood disorders. Its limits: it relies on participants' own perceptions rather than clinical review, and the sample was mostly Dutch and highly educated.
sheet.sv: Om du eller personen du stöttar tidigare fått psykiatriska diagnoser som aldrig riktigt stämde kan det vara värt att gå igenom dem med en kliniker som känner till autism hos vuxna. En skriftlig sammanställning av historik och egna erfarenheter kan underlätta samtalet, samtidigt som vissa tillstånd faktiskt kan finnas samtidigt. Denna nederländska studie frågade 1 211 autistiska vuxna: var fjärde, och var tredje kvinna, upplevde att minst en tidigare diagnos varit fel, oftast personlighetssyndrom, ångest eller förstämning. Begränsningar: studien bygger på deltagarnas egna upplevelser snarare än klinisk granskning, och urvalet var mest nederländskt och högutbildat.

title: The relationship between psychopathy and autism: a systematic review and narrative synthesis.
authors: Maguire K, Warman H, Blumenfeld F, Langdon PE
abstract: Background and methods The aim of this systematic review was to synthesise research examining the relationship between autism and psychopathy to: (a) better understand the relationship between these two constructs, and (b) describe the clinical manifestation of the two when they co-occur. A systematic search of the literature returned 36 studies. Results Across all ages, autistic individuals and those with elevated autistic traits but no autistic diagnoses appeared to have increased callous and unemotional traits or psychopathy relative to the general population. Several studies evidenced that although both constructs are associated with empathetic dysfunction, the underlying mechanisms differ. In adults, psychopathy/psychopathic traits were associated with diminished affective empathy and intact cognitive empathy, whilst the opposite was seen autistic adults and those with elevated autistic traits. In children, those with autistic traits or a diagnosis of autism had diminished cognitive empathy, but not affective empathy, while the relationship between callous and unemotional traits/psychopathy and empathy amongst children was less clear. The co-occurrence of autism and psychopathy was seen to lead to additional empathic and cognitive impairment, but findings were mixed making it challenging to clearly describe the clinical manifestation. Conclusion There remains a paucity of research investigating the interaction between autism and psychopathy and included studies were characterised by multiple measurement difficulties. Attention should be directed toward developing better methods for identifying psychopathic traits in autistic individuals to advance our understanding of the relationship between autism and psychopathy to allow for the development of appropriate care pathways for this population. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/display_record.php?RecordID=413672, identifier CRD42023413672.

sheet.es: Si le preocupa que una persona autista pueda tener rasgos de psicopatía, no saque conclusiones: autismo y psicopatía no son lo mismo, y la empatía funciona de forma distinta en cada uno. Fíjese en cómo se expresa cada persona y consulte con un profesional si tiene dudas. Es una revisión sistemática de 36 estudios, de varias edades. Sus límites: hay poca investigación sobre la combinación, las medidas usadas tenían dificultades y los resultados fueron mixtos, así que no sirve como regla para ninguna persona concreta.
sheet.en: If you worry that an autistic person might have psychopathic traits, avoid jumping to conclusions: autism and psychopathy are not the same thing, and empathy seems to work differently in each. Notice how this particular person expresses themselves, and talk with a professional if you have concerns. This is a systematic review of 36 studies, covering different ages. Its limits: there is little research on the two together, the measures used had difficulties, and findings were mixed, so it cannot serve as a rule for any individual person.
sheet.sv: Om du oroar dig för att en autistisk person kan ha psykopatiska drag, dra inga snabba slutsatser: autism och psykopati är inte samma sak, och empatin verkar fungera olika i dem. Lägg märke till hur just den här personen uttrycker sig och prata med en yrkesperson om du är osäker. Det är en systematisk översikt av 36 studier, med olika åldrar. Begränsningar: det finns lite forskning om kombinationen, måtten hade svagheter och resultaten var blandade, så den kan inte användas som regel för någon enskild person.

title: Korean autistic persons facing systemic stigmatization from middle education schools: daily survival on the edge as a puppet.
authors: Yoon WH, Seo J, Je C
abstract: Introduction Korean autistic persons who have endured an integrated secondary education system have been exposed to school bullying, causing trauma and stigma to them. It also blocks them from entering a tertiary education system and a decent work, resulting in a lower quality of life. However, research on how it affects autistic persons has not yet been conducted in Korea. Methods Fourteen adult autistic persons in the Republic of Korea participated in the semi-structured focused group interviews. Their conversations were analyzed through qualitative coding. Results The interview results show the rare voice of Korean autistic people. Although interviewees experienced physical, verbal, and sexual violence against them during the secondary education period, they could not get substantial assistance from schools and society. Interviewees agreed that bullying is inherent in the secondary education system of Korea, even in Korean culture. They experienced the cause of bullying being attributed to them as victims rather than perpetrators, and impunity is given to the bullying assailants. Early analyses of this article confirm that such experiences are combined with the sociocultural climate of elitism, meritocracy, and authoritarianism in the Republic of Korea. Conclusion The study confirmed that the autistic person's bullying experience does not come from the social inability of autistic people but the "profound" competition and discriminative atmosphere of the society. The result urges further studies on the bullying experience of East Asian autistic persons and the construction of Korean intervention strategies to prevent school violence against Koreans with disabilities, especially autistic pupils.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista cuenta que sufre acoso en el colegio, créele y actúa: documenta lo ocurrido, pide a la escuela medidas concretas por escrito y no le atribuyas la causa. Evidencia: estudio cualitativo con entrevistas en grupo a 14 personas autistas adultas de la República de Corea sobre su etapa en la educación secundaria. Contaron violencia física, verbal y sexual, y poca ayuda de escuelas y sociedad. Límites: es un grupo pequeño de un solo país y refleja su contexto cultural, así que no describe a todas las personas ni a todos los centros.
sheet.en: If an autistic person tells you they are being bullied at school, believe them and act: write down what happened, ask the school for concrete steps in writing, and don't treat them as the cause. Evidence: a qualitative study using group interviews with 14 autistic adults in the Republic of Korea about their secondary school years. They described physical, verbal and sexual violence, and little help from schools or society. Limits: it is a small group from one country and reflects its cultural context, so it does not describe every person or every school.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person berättar att hen blir mobbad i skolan, tro på hen och agera: skriv ner vad som hänt, be skolan om konkreta åtgärder skriftligt och lägg inte skulden på hen. Evidens: en kvalitativ studie med gruppintervjuer av 14 autistiska vuxna i Republiken Korea om deras tid i högstadiet och gymnasiet. De beskrev fysiskt, verbalt och sexuellt våld och fick lite hjälp från skolor och samhälle. Begränsningar: det är en liten grupp från ett land och speglar dess kultur, så studien beskriver inte alla personer eller alla skolor.

title: Immediate effect of physical activity on the autonomic nervous system in individuals with autism spectrum disorders of different age groups: a randomised trial.
authors: Ahmed MM, Alawna M, Youssef ASA, Amin WM, Alajam RA, Morsy WE, Fayed E, Mohamed AA
abstract: Background Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is one of the most complex neurodevelopmental disorders. It affects almost all human physiological systems. Individuals with ASD often display dysregulation in their autonomic nervous system (ANS), which may elicit differing effects across age groups. Also, studying the ANS missed several important parameters related to ANS. Studying the ANS is crucial in developing adaptive behavioural strategies and maintaining communication abilities and social behaviours. Thus, this study compared the immediate effect of physical activity on the ANS in individuals with ASD in different age groups. Methods 200 participants (106 males and 94 females) took part in a double-blinded randomised design. All participants were divided into four groups according to their age (4-7, 7-10, 10-13 and 14-18 years old). Participants performed a 60 min treadmill walk. The main outcome measurements were heart rate (HR), saturation of peripheral oxygen (SpO 2 ), respiratory rate (RR) and end-tidal carbon dioxide (etCO 2 ). Results Before the study, there were non-significant differences between groups in their physical characteristics (body mass index, Childhood Autism Rating Scale, physical activity level, both parents' existence, aerobic capacity and gender) (p>0.05). At baseline measurements, there were non-significant differences between all groups for all outcome measurements (p>0.05). Immediately after physical activity, there was significant difference between group 1 and other groups (p 0.05). At the follow-up (after 15 min of rest), group 1 maintained significant differences with the other groups for all outcome measurements (p 0.05). Conclusion This study revealed that the SpO 2 significantly decreased immediately after the physical activity, while HR, RR and etCO 2 significantly increased immediately after physical activity in comparison to the baseline measurements. Contrary to other ANS parameters (SpO 2 , RR and etCO 2 ), HR in early ages (4-7 years old) was higher after physical activity and remained elevated longer than other ages. The early ages (4-7 years old) take more time to return to the normal status of ANS parameters including SpO 2 , HR, RR and etCO 2 . Trial registration number NCT05725733.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista de 4 a 7 años camina mucho rato, conviene darle más tiempo de descanso después, porque su cuerpo puede tardar más en recuperarse. Es un ensayo aleatorizado con 200 participantes autistas de 4 a 18 años, que caminaron 60 min en cinta; se midieron frecuencia cardiaca, oxígeno, respiración y CO2 espirado. Los más pequeños (4-7 años) tardaron más en volver a su estado habitual tras 15 min de reposo. Los límites: fue una sola sesión, mide efectos inmediatos y no sirve como regla para cada persona. Observa a tu hijo o hija y consulta con su profesional de salud si tienes dudas.
sheet.en: If an autistic child aged 4-7 walks for a long stretch, it may help to build in extra rest afterwards, because their body may take longer to settle. This was a randomised trial with 200 autistic participants aged 4-18, who walked on a treadmill for 60 min; heart rate, oxygen, breathing and exhaled CO2 were measured. The youngest group (4-7 years) took longer to return to their usual state after 15 min of rest. Limits: it was a single session looking at immediate effects, and it is not a rule for every person. Watch how your child responds and ask a health professional if you have questions.
sheet.sv: Om ett autistiskt barn mellan 4 och 7 år går en längre stund kan det vara bra att planera in extra vila efteråt, eftersom kroppen kan behöva längre tid på sig att återhämta sig. Det var en randomiserad studie med 200 autistiska deltagare i åldern 4-18 år som gick 60 min på löpband; puls, syrenivå, andning och utandad koldioxid mättes. De yngsta (4-7 år) tog längre tid på sig att återgå till sitt vanliga tillstånd efter 15 min vila. Begränsningar: det var ett enda tillfälle med fokus på omedelbara effekter, och det gäller inte som regel för alla. Lägg märke till hur ditt barn reagerar och fråga vårdpersonal vid frågor.

title: Use of an adaptive sensory environment in patients with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in the perioperative environment: a parallel, randomized controlled trial.
authors: Antosh S, Drennan C, Stolfi A, Lawson R, Huntley E, McCullough-Roach R, Hill M, Adelekan T, Vachhrajani S
abstract: Background Patients with autism spectrum disorders (ASD) experience higher rates of perioperative anxiety and are likely to receive premedication. Little is known about nonpharmaceutical interventions which may decrease anxiety. This study aims to evaluate the use of an adaptive sensory environment (ASE) to reduce ASD patient anxiety during the perioperative process. Methods Our feasibility study (ClinicalTrials.govNCT04994613) enrolled 60 patients in two parallel groups randomized to a control (no ASE) or intervention group (ASE). We included all surgical patients aged three to twelve years, with a formal diagnosis of ASD, Asperger's Syndrome, or pervasive developmental disorder not otherwise specified. Preoperative behaviors were recorded by an unblinded nurse utilizing the validated Modified Yale Preoperative Anxiety Scale (mYPAS). The difference in score on the mYPAS was the primary outcome, and an intention-to-treat analysis was employed. A generalized estimating equations model was used to compare mYPAS scores controlling for significant independent variables. Findings 58 patients were analyzed after 1:1 randomization of 30 patients to each group. Groups were balanced except the median number of intraoperative pain medications was significantly lower in the ASE group (1 vs. 3, p = 0.012). Mean (SD) age for all patients was 7.2 (2.9) years, range 2.6-12.7. 72.4% (42/58) were White and all were Non-Hispanic or Latino. 74% were Male (21/30 ASE and 22/28 Control) and 26% were Female (9/30 ASE and 6/28 Control). No differences were found in mYPAS scores between groups at three time periods (43.5 vs. 42, p = 0.88, 47.8 vs. 48.4, p = 0.76, and 36.4 vs. 43.8, p = 0.15, ASE vs. control group, respectively). The ASE group had a significant within-group decrease in mYPAS scores from nursing intake to transition (p = 0.030). Interpretation An ASE did not significantly reduce perioperative anxiety. However, the promising results deserve further investigation. Funding Dayton Children's Hospital Foundation Robert C. Cohn Memorial Research Grant.

sheet.es: Si un niño autista va a una cirugía, vale la pena preguntar al hospital si puede adaptar el entorno sensorial (luces, sonidos, estímulos), pero este estudio no demuestra que reduzca la ansiedad. Fue un ensayo aleatorizado con 60 niños de 3 a 12 años con diagnóstico de TEA; se analizaron 58. No hubo diferencias significativas en la ansiedad entre quienes usaron el entorno adaptado y quienes no, aunque los autores ven resultados prometedores. Es un estudio pequeño de viabilidad, con una enfermera que sabía qué grupo era cada uno, y no sirve como regla para cada niño.
sheet.en: If an autistic child is facing surgery, it is worth asking the hospital whether the sensory environment (lights, sounds, stimulation) can be adapted, but this study did not show that it reduces anxiety. It was a randomized trial of 60 children aged three to twelve with a formal autism diagnosis; 58 were analyzed. Anxiety scores did not differ significantly between children who had the adaptive environment and those who did not, though the authors call the results promising. It was a small feasibility study, the nurse scoring behavior knew each child's group, and it cannot be taken as a rule for every child.
sheet.sv: Om ett autistiskt barn ska opereras kan det vara värt att fråga sjukhuset om den sensoriska miljön (ljus, ljud, stimuli) kan anpassas, men den här studien visade inte att det minskar oro. Det var en randomiserad studie med 60 barn i åldern tre till tolv år med formell autismdiagnos; 58 analyserades. Orospoängen skilde sig inte signifikant mellan barn med anpassad miljö och barn utan, även om författarna beskriver resultaten som lovande. Studien var liten, sköterskan som bedömde beteendet visste vilken grupp barnet tillhörde, och resultaten gäller inte automatiskt varje barn.

title: Comparison of the efficacy of parent-mediated NDBIs on developmental skills in children with ASD and fidelity in parents: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
authors: Ouyang Y, Feng J, Wang T, Xue Y, Mohamed ZA, Jia F
abstract: Background Recently, studies on behavioral interventions for autism have gained popularity. Naturalistic Developmental Behavior Interventions (NDBIs) are among the most effective, evidence-based, and widely used behavior interventions for autism. However, no research has been conducted on which of the several NDBI methods is most effective for parents and children with autism spectrum disorders. Therefore, we conducted a network meta-analysis to compare the specific effects of each type of parental-mediated NDBI on children's developmental skills and parent fidelity. Methods PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Medline, Web of Science, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), CINAHL, and Wanfang databases were searched from inception to August 30, 2023. A total of 32 randomized controlled trial studies that examined the efficacy of different NDBIs were included. Results Parents of children with ASD who received Pivotal Response Treatment (PRT) reported significant improvements in their children's social skills (SUCRA, 74.1%), language skills (SUCRA, 88.3%), and parenting fidelity (SUCRA, 99.5%). Moreover, parents who received Early Start Denver Model (ESDM) reported significant improvements in their children's language (SMD = 0.41, 95% CI: 0.04, 0.79) and motor skills (SMD = 0.44, 95% CI: 0.09, 0.79). In terms of the efficacy of improving parent fidelity, the results showed that the Improving Parents as Communication Teachers (ImPACT) intervention significantly improved parent fidelity when compared with the treatment-as-usual group (TAU) (SMD = 0.90, 95% CI: 0.39, 1.42) and the parental education intervention (PEI) (SMD = 1.10, 95% CI:0.28, 1.91).There was a difference in parent fidelity among parents who received PRT(SMD = 3.53, 95% CI: 2.26, 4.79) or ESDM(SMD = 1.42, 95% CI: 0.76, 2.09) training compared with PEI. Conclusion In conclusion, this study revealed that parents can achieve high fidelity with the ImPACT intervention, and it can serve as an early first step for children newly diagnosed with ASD. It also showed that parent-mediated ESDM is effective in improving language and motor skills for children with ASD and can be used as part of the second stage of parent training. Parent-mediated PRT can also be used as a third stage of parent training with sufficient training intensity to further improve language, social, and motor skills.

sheet.es: Si está pensando en un programa en el que madres, padres o cuidadores aprenden a apoyar el desarrollo de su criatura autista en la vida diaria, esta revisión sugiere que hay varios enfoques posibles y que conviene hablar de ellos con el equipo profesional. Es un metaanálisis en red que reunió 32 ensayos controlados aleatorizados sobre intervenciones de este tipo. Los autores concluyen que ImPACT podría ser un primer paso, ESDM ayudaría en lenguaje y motricidad, y PRT en lenguaje, habilidades sociales y motricidad. Límites: gran parte de los resultados se basa en lo que informan las familias, y no sirve como regla para cada niña, niño o familia.
sheet.en: If you are considering a programme where parents or caregivers learn to support an autistic child's development in daily life, this review suggests several approaches exist and are worth discussing with the professional team. It is a network meta-analysis that pooled 32 randomized controlled trials of such interventions. The authors conclude that ImPACT may work as a first step, ESDM may help language and motor skills, and PRT language, social and motor skills. Limits: many results rely on what parents report, and the findings are not a rule for every child or family.
sheet.sv: Om du funderar på ett program där föräldrar eller andra vårdnadshavare lär sig stödja ett autistiskt barns utveckling i vardagen, tyder den här översikten på att det finns flera upplägg som är värda att diskutera med det professionella teamet. Det är en nätverksmetaanalys som slog ihop 32 randomiserade kontrollerade studier av sådana insatser. Författarna menar att ImPACT kan vara ett första steg, ESDM kan stödja språk och motorik, och PRT språk, sociala färdigheter och motorik. Begränsningar: många resultat bygger på vad föräldrar själva rapporterar, och fynden är ingen regel för varje barn eller familj.

title: The 'PSILAUT' protocol: an experimental medicine study of autistic differences in the function of brain serotonin targets of psilocybin.
authors: Whelan TP, Daly E, Puts NA, Smith P, Allison C, Baron-Cohen S, Malievskaia E, Murphy DGM, McAlonan GM
abstract: Background The underlying neurobiology of the complex autism phenotype remains obscure, although accumulating evidence implicates the serotonin system and especially the 5HT 2A receptor. However, previous research has largely relied upon association or correlation studies to link differences in serotonin targets to autism. To directly establish that serotonergic signalling is involved in a candidate brain function our approach is to change it and observe a shift in that function. We will use psilocybin as a pharmacological probe of the serotonin system in vivo. We will directly test the hypothesis that serotonergic targets of psilocybin - principally, but not exclusively, 5HT 2A receptor pathways-function differently in autistic and non-autistic adults. Methods The 'PSILAUT' "shiftability" study is a case-control study autistic and non-autistic adults. How neural responses 'shift' in response to low doses (2 mg and 5 mg) of psilocybin compared to placebo will be examined using multimodal techniques including functional MRI and EEG. Each participant will attend on up to three separate visits with drug or placebo administration in a double-blind and randomized order. Results This study will provide the first direct evidence that the serotonin targets of psilocybin function differently in the autistic and non-autistic brain. We will also examine individual differences in serotonin system function. Conclusions This work will inform our understanding of the neurobiology of autism as well as decisions about future clinical trials of psilocybin and/or related compounds including stratification approaches. Trial registration NCT05651126.

sheet.es: Este estudio no cambia nada que puedas hacer mañana: es un protocolo de investigación y no ofrece pautas para el día a día. Es un estudio médico, y las decisiones médicas corresponden siempre a un profesional clínico. Sobre la evidencia: describe un plan de ensayo con adultos autistas y no autistas, que compara con placebo las respuestas cerebrales, medidas con resonancia magnética funcional y EEG. Aún no presenta resultados. Sus límites: busca entender mejor la neurobiología, no dice nada sobre qué le conviene a una persona concreta y no debe leerse como una regla general. Si te preocupa algo, habla con su equipo clínico.
sheet.en: This study changes nothing you can do tomorrow: it is a research protocol and offers no everyday guidance. It is a medical study, and medical decisions always belong to a clinician. On the evidence: it describes a planned trial with autistic and non-autistic adults, comparing brain responses against placebo using functional MRI and EEG. It reports no results yet. Its limits: it aims to understand neurobiology better, says nothing about what suits any one person, and should not be read as a rule for everyone. If something worries you, talk with the person's clinical team.
sheet.sv: Den här studien ändrar inget du kan göra i morgon: det är ett forskningsprotokoll och ger inga råd för vardagen. Det är en medicinsk studie, och medicinska beslut hör alltid till en kliniker. Om underlaget: den beskriver en planerad studie med autistiska och icke-autistiska vuxna, där hjärnsvar jämförs med placebo med funktionell MRI och EEG. Inga resultat redovisas ännu. Begränsningar: syftet är att förstå neurobiologin bättre, studien säger inget om vad som passar en enskild person och ska inte läsas som en regel för alla. Om något oroar dig, prata med personens kliniska team.

title: Effects of Physical Activity on Cognition, Behavior, and Motor Skills in Youth with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review of Intervention Studies.
authors: Suárez-Manzano S, Ruiz-Ariza A, de Loureiro NEM, Martínez-López EJ
abstract: The aim of this paper was to analyze the acute and chronic effects of physical activity (PA) on cognition, behavior, and motor skill in youth with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), taking into account potential confounders. In addition, it was intended to elaborate a guide of educational applications with strategies for PA use. Studies were identified in four databases from January 2010 to June 2023. A total of 19 interventional studies met the inclusion criteria. PA programs ranged from two weeks to one year in duration, with a frequency of one to five sessions per week. More than 58% of the studies showed positive effects of PA on cognition, and 45.5% on behavior and motor skill. Moderate-vigorous PA for 15-30 min has shown acute effects on cognition, general behavior, and stereotypic/repetitive behaviors in youth with ASD. A total of 9 out of 14 studies showed chronic effects on general behavior and stereotypic behaviors, and only 6 on motor skills.

sheet.es: Si quiere probar actividad física con una persona autista joven, puede empezar con sesiones de movimiento de intensidad moderada a vigorosa de 15-30 min, según sus gustos y su comodidad. Es una revisión sistemática de 19 estudios de intervención en jóvenes autistas; los programas duraron de dos semanas a un año. Algunos estudios mostraron efectos positivos en cognición, conducta y habilidades motoras, pero no todos. Los resultados varían mucho entre estudios y personas, así que no son una regla. Observe cómo responde cada joven y respete su ritmo y sus preferencias.
sheet.en: If you want to try physical activity with an autistic young person, you could start with moderate-to-vigorous movement sessions of 15-30 min, guided by what they enjoy and find comfortable. This is a systematic review of 19 intervention studies with autistic youth; programs lasted from two weeks to one year. Some studies showed positive effects on cognition, behavior and motor skills, but not all did. Results varied across studies and people, so they are not a rule. Watch how each young person responds and respect their pace and preferences.
sheet.sv: Om du vill prova fysisk aktivitet med en ung autistisk person kan du börja med rörelsepass av måttlig till hög intensitet på 15-30 min, utifrån vad personen gillar och trivs med. Det här är en systematisk översikt av 19 interventionsstudier med autistiska unga; programmen varade från två veckor till ett år. Vissa studier visade positiva effekter på kognition, beteende och motorik, men inte alla. Resultaten varierade mellan studier och personer och är ingen regel. Observera hur varje ung person reagerar och respektera tempo och önskemål.

title: 'It wasn't the strategies on their own': Exploring caregivers' experiences of accessing services in the development of interventions for autistic people with intellectual disability.
authors: Hughes J, Roberts R, Tarver J, Warters-Louth C, Zhang B, Southward E, Shaw R, Edwards G, Waite J, Pearson E
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Many autistic individuals with intellectual disability experience anxiety, and for those who use few or no words, anxiety may present as behaviour that challenges, such as self-injury and avoiding anxiety-provoking situations. Families report difficulty accessing support from services for autistic individuals experiencing anxiety. Moreover, once receiving support, effective interventions for autistic people with intellectual disability are limited. We completed individual and group discussions with 16 caregivers of autistic people with intellectual disability, to (a) explore their experiences of accessing services for anxiety and/or behaviour that challenges for their child; and (b) understand what matters to caregivers when developing interventions that have been designed for them and the autistic individual with intellectual disability that they support. Caregivers reported that services, in their experience, did not deliver the support that they expected, and that they often needed to 'fight' for support. Caregivers considered services and families working together, the inclusion of peer support, and families being offered interventions that are flexible to individual circumstances to be important. These considerations are valuable for clinicians and researchers developing interventions and aiming to improve outcomes for autistic people with intellectual disability and their families.

sheet.es: Si buscas apoyo para la ansiedad de tu hijo o hija autista con discapacidad intelectual, puede ayudarte saber que otras familias también sintieron que debían «luchar» por ese apoyo. Anota qué funciona en casa y pide que el servicio trabaje contigo, con opciones flexibles y, si es posible, apoyo entre familias. Es un estudio con discusiones individuales y en grupo con 16 cuidadores de personas autistas con discapacidad intelectual. Recoge experiencias de pocas familias y no demuestra qué intervención funciona; cada persona es distinta. Si te preocupa la autolesión, habla con un profesional de la salud o un servicio de crisis. En peligro inmediato, llama al número de emergencias de tu país.
sheet.en: If you are seeking support for anxiety in your autistic child with intellectual disability, it may help to know that other families also felt they had to 'fight' for it. Note what works at home and ask services to work with you, offering flexible options and, where possible, peer support from other families. This study held individual and group discussions with 16 caregivers of autistic people with intellectual disability. It reflects the experiences of a small number of families and does not show which intervention works; every person is different. If you are worried about self-injury, speak with a clinician, a health service or a crisis service. In immediate danger, call your country's emergency number.
sheet.sv: Om du söker stöd för ångest hos ditt autistiska barn med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning kan det hjälpa att veta att andra familjer också upplevde att de måste ”kämpa” för stöd. Anteckna vad som fungerar hemma och be att tjänsterna samarbetar med dig, erbjuder flexibla alternativ och helst stöd från andra familjer. Studien bygger på enskilda samtal och gruppsamtal med 16 vårdnadshavare till autistiska personer med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning. Den speglar erfarenheter från få familjer och visar inte vilken insats som fungerar; varje person är olika. Om du oroar dig för självskada, kontakta en läkare, vården eller en krisjour. Vid akut fara, ring larmnumret i ditt land.

title: Post-traumatic stress disorder and experiences involving violence or sexual abuse in a clinical sample of autistic adults with intellectual disabilities: Prevalence and clinical correlates.
authors: Kildahl AN, Helverschou SB
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Post-traumatic stress disorder is a mental health disorder that may be triggered by the experience of events perceived as terrifying or overwhelming. Examples of such events include being the victim of violence or sexual abuse. Compared with other people, autistic people have increased risk of being exposed to violence or sexual abuse. In addition, autistic people may be more vulnerable to developing post-traumatic stress disorder following such exposure. However, knowledge is limited concerning the prevalence of experiences involving violence and sexual abuse, and post-traumatic stress disorder, in autistic people with co-occurring intellectual disabilities. Detection of these experiences, and identification of post-traumatic stress disorder, may be challenging in these individuals, and previous research indicates that post-traumatic stress disorder symptoms may be overlooked or misinterpreted. In this study, we examined prevalence of post-traumatic stress disorder, violence and sexual abuse in a clinical sample of 88 autistic adults with intellectual disabilities referred for mental health assessment. Only 3.4% were diagnosed with post-traumatic stress disorder, even if experiences involving violence (34.1%) or sexual abuse (17.0%) were common. Anxiety and affective disorders were common diagnoses among participants with these experiences. Controlling for autism characteristics, level of intellectual disability and communication skills, experiences of violence/sexual abuse were found to be associated with a measure of 'challenging' behaviours.
