These results indicate that potentially traumatic experiences are common in autistic adults with intellectual disabilities referred for mental health assessment, and that post-traumatic stress disorder may be under-recognised. The findings highlight the importance of trauma screening and post-traumatic stress disorder assessment, as well as the importance of trauma-informed care, in this population.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista adulta con discapacidad intelectual, tenlo presente: un cambio en su conducta o su estado de ánimo puede estar relacionado con experiencias dolorosas del pasado, como violencia o abuso. Conviene pedir a su equipo clínico que pregunte por ello con cuidado y ofrecer un trato que dé seguridad. El estudio revisó datos clínicos de 88 adultos autistas con discapacidad intelectual derivados a una evaluación de salud mental: el 34,1% había vivido violencia y el 17,0% abuso sexual, pero solo el 3,4% tenía diagnóstico de estrés postraumático. Es una muestra clínica pequeña, así que no describe a todas las personas ni prueba causas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult with intellectual disability, keep in mind that changes in behaviour or mood may be linked to painful past experiences, such as violence or abuse. It can help to ask their clinical team to explore this gently, and to offer a safe, predictable way of supporting them. The study looked at clinical records of 88 autistic adults with intellectual disabilities referred for mental health assessment: 34.1% had experienced violence and 17.0% sexual abuse, yet only 3.4% had a post-traumatic stress disorder diagnosis. It was a small clinical sample, so it does not describe everyone and cannot show causes.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning: tänk på att förändringar i beteende eller humör kan hänga ihop med smärtsamma upplevelser, till exempel våld eller övergrepp. Be gärna vårdteamet att utforska detta varsamt, och erbjud ett tryggt och förutsägbart stöd. Studien granskade kliniska uppgifter om 88 autistiska vuxna med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning som remitterats till psykisk hälsobedömning: 34,1% hade varit med om våld och 17,0% sexuella övergrepp, men bara 3,4% hade diagnosen posttraumatiskt stressyndrom. Urvalet var litet och kliniskt, så det gäller inte alla och visar inte orsaker.

title: Autistic adults' experiences of financial wellbeing: Part II.
authors: Pellicano E, Hall G, Ying Cai R
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Money matters in people's lives. It helps to meet people's basic needs (food, clothes, shelter) and live the lives they want to. When people talk about 'financial wellbeing', they mean how much you feel in control over day-to-day finances and how much freedom you have to make choices to enjoy life. We don't know what autistic people think about these things. That's why we did our study. We spoke to 21 autistic adults (24-69 years) about how they felt about their financial situation. We deliberately spoke to people who had told us previously they felt 'financially well' or 'financially unwell' so we could hear a range of opinions. Autistic people told us financial wellbeing meant having enough money to pay for their basics needs, to have a safety net for unexpected bills and not having to worry about money now or in the future. But many felt that good financial wellbeing was not possible for them. They often did not have a stable income to cover day-to-day expenses. This limited the choices they could make. Despite these challenges, autistic people told us they worked hard to budget and save money when they could - because feeling financial insecure was just too stressful, especially when they could not rely on family or friends for support. It made them feel mentally unwell. Our study shows there are many factors that influence autistic people's financial wellbeing. We need more research to help us understand how autistic people can be supported to achieve financial security.

sheet.es: Si cuidas o acompañas a una persona autista adulta, pregúntale con calma qué significa para ella sentirse tranquila con el dinero: cubrir lo básico, tener un colchón para gastos imprevistos y no vivir preocupada. Escuchar su visión puede orientar cómo ayudar. Es un estudio cualitativo en el que se habló con 21 adultos autistas de 24-69 años, elegidos para recoger opiniones variadas. Muchos contaron que no tenían ingresos estables, que presupuestaban y ahorraban con esfuerzo, y que la inseguridad económica les afectaba a la salud mental. Como límites: es un grupo pequeño, refleja experiencias propias y no sirve como regla para cada persona. Hace falta más investigación sobre apoyos.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult, ask them calmly what feeling secure with money means to them: covering basic needs, having a safety net for unexpected bills, and not worrying about money. Their own view can guide how you help. This was a qualitative study in which researchers spoke with 21 autistic adults aged 24-69, chosen to capture a range of opinions. Many described lacking a stable income, working hard to budget and save, and feeling mentally unwell from financial insecurity. A limit: the group was small and shared personal experiences, so it is not a rule for every person. More research on supports is needed.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen kan du lugnt fråga vad ekonomisk trygghet betyder för just hen: att täcka grundbehoven, ha en buffert för oväntade räkningar och slippa oroa sig för pengar. Hens egen syn kan visa hur du kan hjälpa. Det var en kvalitativ studie där forskarna talade med 21 autistiska vuxna i åldern 24-69, utvalda för att ge olika åsikter. Många beskrev att de saknade stabil inkomst, ansträngde sig för att budgetera och spara, och mådde psykiskt dåligt av osäker ekonomi. En begränsning: gruppen var liten och delade personliga erfarenheter, så resultaten är ingen regel för alla. Mer forskning om stöd behövs.

title: Comparison of network structures between autistic and non-autistic adults, and autism subgroups: A focus on demographic, psychological, and lifestyle factors.
authors: Radhoe TA, van Rentergem JAA, Torenvliet C, Groenman AP, van der Putten WJ, Geurts HM
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract There are large differences in the level of demographic, psychological, and lifestyle characteristics between autistic and non-autistic adults but also among autistic people. Our goal was to test whether these differences correspond to differences in underlying relationships between these characteristics-also referred to as network structure-to determine which characteristics (and relationships between them) are important. We tested differences in network structure in (1) autistic and non-autistic adults and (2) two previously identified subgroups of autistic adults. We showed that comparing networks of autistic and non-autistic adults provides subtle differences, whereas networks of the autism subgroups were similar. There were also no sex differences in the networks of the autism subgroups. Thus, the previously observed differences in the level of characteristics did not correspond to differences across subgroups in how these characteristics relate to one another (i.e. network structure). Consequently, a focus on differences in characteristics is not sufficient to determine which characteristics (and relationships between them) are of importance. Hence, network analysis provides a valuable tool beyond looking at (sub)group level differences. These results could provide hints for clinical practice, to eventually determine whether psychological distress, cognitive failures, and reduced quality of life in autistic adults can be addressed by tailored support. However, it is important that these results are first replicated before we move toward intervention or support.

sheet.es: Por ahora, no hay un cambio concreto para mañana: que una persona autista tenga más o menos de una característica no dice cómo se relacionan entre sí sus necesidades, así que conviene preguntarle a ella qué le ayuda. Es un estudio de investigación con personas autistas y no autistas adultas que comparó redes de relaciones entre rasgos demográficos, psicológicos y de estilo de vida. Halló diferencias sutiles entre autistas y no autistas, y redes similares entre dos subgrupos de personas autistas. Sus autores piden que los resultados se repliquen antes de usarlos en apoyos, y no sirve como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: For now there is no concrete change for tomorrow: having more or less of a characteristic does not tell you how a person's needs connect, so it is best to ask the autistic person what helps them. This was a research study with autistic and non-autistic adults, comparing networks of relationships between demographic, psychological and lifestyle characteristics. It found subtle differences between autistic and non-autistic adults, and similar networks across two subgroups of autistic adults. The authors say the results must be replicated before being used for support, and they are not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Just nu finns ingen konkret ändring till i morgon: att ha mer eller mindre av en egenskap säger inte hur en persons behov hänger ihop, så fråga helst den autistiska personen vad som hjälper. Det här var en forskningsstudie med autistiska och icke-autistiska vuxna som jämförde nätverk av samband mellan demografiska, psykologiska och livsstilsrelaterade egenskaper. Den fann subtila skillnader mellan autistiska och icke-autistiska vuxna, och liknande nätverk i två undergrupper av autistiska vuxna. Författarna menar att resultaten måste upprepas innan de används i stöd, och de gäller inte som regel för varje person.

title: 'I live in extremes': A qualitative investigation of Autistic adults' experiences of inertial rest and motion.
authors: Rapaport H, Clapham H, Adams J, Lawson W, Porayska-Pomsta K, Pellicano E
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract 'Autistic inertia' is a term used by Autistic people to refer to difficulties with starting and stopping tasks. However, there has not been much research on Autistic inertia. The research that is available on Autistic inertia has mostly focused on the negative aspects of inertia, rather than on the possible benefits of needing to continue tasks. In this research, we wanted to understand more about Autistic people's experiences of inertia and to work out what things might influence these experiences. Autistic and non-Autistic researchers spoke in-depth to 24 Autistic adults. We identified four key ideas from people's responses. Autistic people spoke about their inertial 'difficulties moving from one state to another' and described how these challenges affected them 'every single day'. While they experienced inertia as 'the single most disabling part of being Autistic', people also described the positive aspects of inertia, including the joy they felt when completely immersed in a task. Our Autistic participants emphasised that inertial difficulties are experienced by everyone, the intensity of these task-switching difficulties might be especially challenging for Autistic people. Our findings also reveal how Autistic inertia can be seen both as a disabling and as an enabling condition.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista tarda en empezar o en parar una tarea, conviene darle tiempo y avisos suaves en los cambios, y proteger los momentos en que está totalmente inmersa, porque pueden ser una fuente de alegría. Se trata de un estudio cualitativo: investigadores autistas y no autistas conversaron en profundidad con 24 adultos autistas. Describieron la inercia como difícil cada día, pero también con aspectos positivos. Sus límites: recoge experiencias de pocas personas adultas y no demuestra qué estrategia funciona, ni sirve como regla para todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person takes time to start or stop a task, it can help to allow extra time, give gentle notice before changes, and protect moments of deep immersion, which can bring real joy. This was a qualitative study: autistic and non-autistic researchers spoke in depth with 24 autistic adults. They described inertia as difficult every day, yet also as having positive sides. Its limits: it reflects the experiences of a small group of adults and does not prove which strategy works, so it is not a rule for every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person behöver tid för att starta eller avsluta en uppgift kan det hjälpa att ge extra tid, mjuka förvarningar inför byten och skydda stunder av djup fördjupning, som kan ge verklig glädje. Detta var en kvalitativ studie: autistiska och icke-autistiska forskare samtalade på djupet med 24 autistiska vuxna. De beskrev inertia som svårt varje dag, men också med positiva sidor. Begränsningar: studien speglar en liten grupp vuxnas erfarenheter och visar inte vilken strategi som fungerar, så den är ingen regel för alla autistiska personer.

title: 'Most people have no idea what autism is': Unpacking autism disclosure using social media analysis.
authors: Edwards C, Love AMA, Jones SC, Cai RY, Nguyen BTH, Gibbs V
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autism disclosure - that is sharing their autism diagnosis or identity with a person or people - is a difficult decision for many autistic people. While telling people they are autistic can be positive and helpful, it can also create a lot of problems. What we have learnt is that disclosure is really complicated. Rather than asking research participants questions about what might happen, we looked at what people were saying on public social media posts (Reddit and Twitter) about what did happen. We used three years of posts that were related to autism disclosure from a wide range of adults (autistic and non-autistic). Four main ideas were created from our data, with the key finding being that society does not understand autism. This lack of understanding creates problems for autistic people in work, dating, healthcare and mental health. The remaining ideas were that autistic people should have privacy and be treated with respect, that autistic representation can help society and that non-autistic people need to do more to help autistic people. Our findings support that society needs to do more through autism advocacy, better media representation and more public role models. Increasing the accuracy of understanding of autism across society will mean that autistic people can feel safer to disclose if they want to.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista decide contarte que es autista, o si decide no hacerlo, tómalo con calma: la decisión es suya y merece privacidad y respeto. Si te lo cuenta, escucha sin minimizar y pregunta qué apoyo le sirve. Evidencia: estudio que analizó tres años de publicaciones públicas en Reddit y Twitter de adultos autistas y no autistas sobre la revelación del autismo. Señala que la sociedad entiende poco el autismo, lo que genera problemas en trabajo, citas, salud y salud mental. Límites: son opiniones en redes sociales, no entrevistas, y no reflejan a todas las personas autistas ni a quienes no usan esas plataformas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person chooses to tell you they are autistic, or chooses not to, take it calmly: the decision is theirs and deserves privacy and respect. If they do tell you, listen without minimising and ask what support helps them. Evidence: a study analysing three years of public Reddit and Twitter posts about autism disclosure from autistic and non-autistic adults. It found that society understands autism poorly, which creates problems in work, dating, healthcare and mental health. Limits: these are social media posts, not interviews, so they may not reflect all autistic people or those who do not use these platforms.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person väljer att berätta att hen är autistisk, eller väljer att inte göra det, ta det lugnt: beslutet är hens och förtjänar integritet och respekt. Om hen berättar, lyssna utan att förminska och fråga vilket stöd som hjälper. Evidens: en studie som analyserade tre års offentliga inlägg på Reddit och Twitter om att berätta om autism, från autistiska och icke-autistiska vuxna. Den visade att samhället förstår autism dåligt, vilket skapar problem i arbete, dejting, vård och psykisk hälsa. Begränsningar: det är inlägg på sociala medier, inte intervjuer, så de speglar kanske inte alla autistiska personer eller dem som inte använder dessa plattformar.

title: Differences in own-face but not own-name discrimination between autistic and neurotypical adults: A fast periodic visual stimulation-EEG study.
authors: Nijhof AD, Catmur C, Brewer R, Coll MP, Wiersema JR, Bird G
journal: Cortex; a journal devoted to the study of the nervous system and behavior
abstract: Self-related processing is thought to be altered in autism, with several studies reporting that autistic individuals show a diminished neural response relative to neurotypicals for their own name and face. However, evidence remains scarce and is mostly based on event-related potential studies. Here, we used EEG to measure the neural activity of autistic adults (20 for faces, 27 for names) and neurotypical adults (24 for faces, 25 for names) while they were watching rapidly alternating faces and names, through a relatively new technique called Fast Periodic Visual Stimulation. We presented strangers' faces or names at a base frequency of 5.77 Hz, while one's own, a close other's, and a specific stranger's face/name was presented at an oddball frequency of 1.154 Hz. The neurotypical group showed a significantly greater response to their own face than both close other and stranger faces, and a greater response for close other than for stranger faces. In contrast, in the autism group, own and close other faces showed stronger responses than the stranger's face, but the difference between own and close other faces was not significant in a bilateral parieto-occipital cluster. No group differences in the enhanced response to familiar names were found. These results replicate and extend results obtained using traditional electroencephalographic techniques which suggest atypical responses to self-relevant stimuli in autism.

sheet.es: Por ahora, esto no cambia nada en el día a día: es un estudio de laboratorio, no una guía de actuación. Si algo se desprende, es que cada persona autista procesa lo familiar a su manera. Se midió con EEG la actividad cerebral de adultos autistas (20 con caras, 27 con nombres) y adultos neurotípicos (24 con caras, 25 con nombres) al ver caras y nombres. Hubo diferencias en la respuesta a la propia cara, pero no en la respuesta a nombres familiares. Limitaciones: muestras pequeñas, solo adultos y una tarea de laboratorio; no dice cómo es una persona concreta ni qué necesita.
sheet.en: For now, this changes nothing in daily life: it is a lab study, not a guide for action. If anything, it is a reminder that each autistic person may process familiar things in their own way. Researchers used EEG to record brain activity in autistic adults (20 for faces, 27 for names) and neurotypical adults (24 for faces, 25 for names) viewing faces and names. Responses to their own face differed between groups, but responses to familiar names did not. Limits: small samples, adults only and a lab task; it cannot tell you how a particular person is or what they need.
sheet.sv: Just nu ändrar detta ingenting i vardagen: det är en laboratoriestudie, inte en handledning. Om något är det en påminnelse om att varje autistisk person kan bearbeta det välbekanta på sitt sätt. Forskarna mätte hjärnaktivitet med EEG hos autistiska vuxna (20 för ansikten, 27 för namn) och neurotypiska vuxna (24 för ansikten, 25 för namn) som tittade på ansikten och namn. Svaren på det egna ansiktet skilde sig mellan grupperna, men svaren på välbekanta namn gjorde det inte. Begränsningar: små grupper, bara vuxna och en laboratorieuppgift; studien säger inget om hur en enskild person är eller vad hen behöver.

title: Bridging Genetic Insights with Neuroimaging in Autism Spectrum Disorder-A Systematic Review.
authors: Vilela J, Rasga C, Santos JX, Martiniano H, Marques AR, Oliveira G, Vicente AM
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is an early onset neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by impaired social interaction and communication, and repetitive patterns of behavior. Family studies show that ASD is highly heritable, and hundreds of genes have previously been implicated in the disorder; however, the etiology is still not fully clear. Brain imaging and electroencephalography (EEG) are key techniques that study alterations in brain structure and function. Combined with genetic analysis, these techniques have the potential to help in the clarification of the neurobiological mechanisms contributing to ASD and help in defining novel therapeutic targets. To further understand what is known today regarding the impact of genetic variants in the brain alterations observed in individuals with ASD, a systematic review was carried out using Pubmed and EBSCO databases and following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. This review shows that specific genetic variants and altered patterns of gene expression in individuals with ASD may have an effect on brain circuits associated with face processing and social cognition, and contribute to excitation-inhibition imbalances and to anomalies in brain volumes.

sheet.es: Este estudio no ofrece nada que cambie la rutina de mañana: no propone estrategias ni pruebas para casa. Lo útil es saber que la investigación intenta entender cómo ciertas variantes genéticas se relacionan con la forma en que funciona el cerebro de algunas personas autistas. Es una revisión sistemática de estudios publicados, buscados en dos bases de datos. Sugiere que algunas variantes genéticas podrían influir en circuitos cerebrales del procesamiento de caras y la cognición social, y en volúmenes cerebrales. Sus límites: no explica a cada persona autista, no demuestra causas claras y no indica qué hacer en la práctica. Si tiene dudas, consulte con un profesional.
sheet.en: This study offers nothing that changes tomorrow morning's routine: it suggests no strategies or home tests. What is useful is knowing that researchers are trying to understand how certain genetic variants relate to how the brain works in some autistic people. It is a systematic review of published studies, searched in two databases. It suggests some variants may influence brain circuits for face processing and social cognition, and brain volumes. Its limits: it does not explain every autistic person, does not prove clear causes, and gives no guidance on what to do in daily life. If you have questions, talk with a professional.
sheet.sv: Den här studien ger inget som ändrar morgondagens rutiner: den föreslår inga strategier eller tester hemma. Det användbara är att veta att forskare försöker förstå hur vissa genetiska varianter hänger ihop med hur hjärnan fungerar hos en del autistiska personer. Det är en systematisk översikt av publicerade studier, sökta i två databaser. Den antyder att vissa varianter kan påverka hjärnkretsar för ansiktsbearbetning och social kognition samt hjärnvolymer. Begränsningar: den förklarar inte varje autistisk person, visar inga säkra orsaker och ger ingen vägledning för vardagen. Har du frågor, prata med en professionell.

title: The Unmasking of Autism in South Africa and Nigeria.
authors: Adams SN
abstract: This review is of interest to researchers, policymakers, and healthcare professionals working in the field of autism in Africa. The review aims to describe autism in sub-Saharan Africa, focusing on South Africa and Nigeria regarding prevalence, incidence, identification, treatment, and attitudes towards autistic children. There are several challenges, such as lack of awareness, limited access to professional support and diagnostic tools, and cultural considerations in establishing the autism prevalence in the African region compared to other parts of the world. Additionally, South Africans and Nigerians exhibit diverse perspectives and attitudes that significantly influence the provision of treatment, including stigma and misconceptions held by healthcare professionals themselves. As a result, it is difficult to determine prevalence in South Africa and Nigeria. However, research has indicated that autism prevalence is rising globally, and in these contexts. Rising prevalence highlights the need to increase access to services, rehabilitation, and provide support to families of children with autism. Furthermore, research has emphasized the inequitable support and access available to families living in low-and high-income households and the need to provide contextually relevant and responsive interventions, education and training, research and policy in these countries.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a un niño autista en un entorno con pocos recursos, busca información y apoyo comunitario, y pregunta con claridad a los profesionales sobre evaluación y servicios; tu experiencia familiar cuenta. Es una revisión de la literatura sobre autismo en Sudáfrica y Nigeria, que describe la falta de conocimiento, el acceso limitado a apoyo y herramientas diagnósticas, el estigma y las desigualdades entre hogares con ingresos bajos y altos. Sus límites: no es un estudio con participantes propios, dificulta calcular la prevalencia y no sirve como regla para cada familia.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic child where resources are scarce, look for community information and support, and ask professionals clearly about assessment and services; your family's experience matters. This is a review of the literature on autism in South Africa and Nigeria. It describes lack of awareness, limited access to support and diagnostic tools, stigma, and inequity between low- and high-income households. Its limits: it has no participants of its own, it finds prevalence hard to determine, and it is not a rule for every family.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar ett autistiskt barn där resurserna är små, sök information och stöd i din närmiljö, och fråga yrkespersoner tydligt om utredning och insatser; din familjs erfarenhet räknas. Detta är en översikt av forskning om autism i Sydafrika och Nigeria. Den beskriver bristande kunskap, begränsad tillgång till stöd och diagnostiska verktyg, stigma samt orättvisor mellan hushåll med låg och hög inkomst. Begränsningar: den har inga egna deltagare, det är svårt att fastställa förekomsten, och den är ingen regel för varje familj.

title: Effectiveness of IMPUTE ADT-1 mobile application in children with autism spectrum disorder: An interim analysis of an ongoing randomized controlled trial.
authors: Panda PK, Elwadhi A, Gupta D, Palayullakandi A, Tomar A, Singh M, Vyas A, Kumar D, Sharawat IK
journal: Journal of neurosciences in rural practice
abstract: Objectives IMPUTE Inc., a software firm dedicated to healthcare technology, has developed a mobile medical application known as IMPUTE ADT-1 for children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) based on the principle of applied behavior analysis. Materials and methods The primary objective of this trial was to compare the efficacy of add-on treatment with IMPUTE ADT-1 in children with ASD aged two to six years as compared to standard care alone for 12 weeks (in terms of change in Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule [ADOS-2] scores). The secondary objective of the study was to assess the compliance with IMPUTE ADT-1 among participants and also to evaluate the feedback of parents regarding IMPUTE ADT-1 at the end of 12 weeks. The application provides personalized programs tailored to each user's needs, and the program evolves based on the user's progress. It also utilizes face tracking, eye tracking, and body tracking to gather behavior-related information for each child and apply it in reinforcement learning employing artificial intelligence-based algorithms. Results Till the time of interim analysis, 37 and 33 children had completed 12-week follow-up in IMPUTE ADT-1 and control arm. At 12 weeks, as compared to baseline, change in social affect domain, repetitive ritualistic behavior domain, total ADOS-2 score, and ADOS-2 comparison score was better in the intervention group as compared to the control group ( P Conclusion IMPUTE ADT-1 mobile application has the efficacy to improve the severity of autism symptoms in children. Parents of these children also feel that the application is beneficial for improving the socialization and verbal communication of their children.

sheet.es: Si se plantea usar una aplicación móvil basada en análisis de conducta aplicada, conviene tratarla como un complemento y comentarla con el equipo profesional, observando cómo la vive cada niño. Es un ensayo aleatorizado, todavía en curso, con análisis intermedio: 37 niños con la aplicación y 33 en el grupo de control, de dos a seis años, durante 12 semanas. El grupo con la aplicación mostró mejores puntuaciones en la escala ADOS-2, y las familias percibieron beneficios en socialización y comunicación verbal. Sin embargo, el análisis es parcial, la aplicación procede de la empresa que la desarrolló, la medida se centra en reducir síntomas y no en el bienestar, y los resultados no valen para todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If you are considering a mobile app based on applied behavior analysis, treat it as an add-on to current support and talk it over with your professional team, watching how each child experiences it. This was a randomized trial, still ongoing, with an interim analysis: 37 children used the app and 33 were in the control group, aged two to six, over 12 weeks. The app group had better ADOS-2 scores, and parents felt it helped socialization and verbal communication. However, the analysis is partial, the app comes from the company that developed it, the measure focuses on reducing symptoms rather than wellbeing, and results may not apply to every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om ni funderar på en mobilapp baserad på tillämpad beteendeanalys, se den som ett komplement till nuvarande stöd och prata om den med teamet, och följ hur varje barn upplever den. Detta var en randomiserad studie, fortfarande pågående, med en interimsanalys: 37 barn använde appen och 33 fanns i kontrollgruppen, i åldern två till sex år, under 12 veckor. Appgruppen hade bättre ADOS-2-resultat, och föräldrarna upplevde att appen hjälpte socialt samspel och verbal kommunikation. Analysen är dock delvis, appen kommer från företaget som utvecklat den, måttet fokuserar på att minska symtom snarare än välbefinnande, och resultaten gäller inte alla autistiska personer.

title: Correlations between sleep problems, core symptoms, and behavioral problems in children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Kim H, Kim JH, Yi JH, Kim JY, Solmi M, Cortese S, Smith L, Koyanagi A, Shin JI, Cheon KA, Fusar-Poli P
abstract: Children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) experience various sleep problems. Sleep problems co-occur in a bidirectional relationship with ASD core symptoms and behavioral problems. However, studies on how these three factors are intricately linked to each other are limited. This meta-analysis examined the differential relationship between specific sleep problems, core symptoms, and behavioral problems in this population. This study was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42022339695). We systematically searched the PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, and Scopus databases from inception to April 27, 2022. Observational studies that reported correlations between measures of sleep problems, ASD core symptoms, or ASD behavioral problems were included, and participants aged 18 years or below were enrolled. The correlation coefficient (r) was assessed as the primary effect metric. Total 22 cross-sectional studies were included, which comprised 2655 participants (mean age = 6.60 years old; mean percentage of boys = 80.64%). We found correlations between total sleep problems and total core symptoms (r 0.293 [95% confidence interval - 0.095 to 0.604]), total sleep problems and total behavioral problems (r 0.429 [0.299-0.544]), and total core symptoms and total behavioral problems (r - 0.050 [- 0.177 to 0.079]) and identified statistically significant correlations between specific components of sleep problems, ASD core symptoms, and ASD behavioral problems. Each specific sleep problem showed a unique association with core symptoms and behavioral problems. Sleep problems in ASD should be explored in detail, and the closely linked core symptoms and behavioral problems should be common therapeutic targets.

sheet.es: Si su hijo autista duerme mal, vale la pena observar con detalle qué tipo de problema de sueño aparece (por ejemplo, al acostarse o durante la noche) y anotar cómo se relaciona con su día a día. Es un meta-análisis de 22 estudios transversales con 2655 participantes de 18 años o menos. Muestra que el sueño y los problemas de conducta se asociaron (r 0.429), pero son correlaciones: no prueban que una cosa cause la otra, y cada niño es distinto. Comente lo que observa con su profesional de referencia.
sheet.en: If your autistic child sleeps poorly, it may help to notice which kind of sleep difficulty appears (for example at bedtime or during the night) and to jot down how it connects with their day. This is a meta-analysis of 22 cross-sectional studies with 2655 participants aged 18 or under. Sleep problems and behavioral problems were associated (r 0.429), but these are correlations: they do not show that one causes the other, and every child is different. Share what you notice with your clinician.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn sover dåligt kan det hjälpa att lägga märke till vilken typ av sömnsvårighet det gäller (till exempel vid läggning eller under natten) och anteckna hur det hänger ihop med dagen. Detta är en metaanalys av 22 tvärsnittsstudier med 2655 deltagare som var 18 år eller yngre. Sömnproblem och beteendeproblem hängde ihop (r 0.429), men det är samband: de visar inte att det ena orsakar det andra, och varje barn är olika. Berätta vad du ser för din vårdkontakt.

title: Autistic adults perceive and experience laughter differently to non-autistic adults.
authors: Cai CQ, White SJ, Chen SHY, Mueller MAE, Scott SK
abstract: Human interaction is immersed in laughter; though genuine and posed laughter are acoustically distinct, they are both crucial socio-emotional signals. In this novel study, autistic and non-autistic adults explicitly rated the affective properties of genuine and posed laughter. Additionally, we explored whether their self-reported everyday experiences with laughter differ. Both groups could differentiate between these two types of laughter. However, autistic adults rated posed laughter as more authentic and emotionally arousing than non-autistic adults, perceiving it to be similar to genuine laughter. Autistic adults reported laughing less, deriving less enjoyment from laughter, and experiencing difficulty in understanding the social meaning of other people's laughter compared to non-autistic people. Despite these differences, autistic adults reported using laughter socially as often as non-autistic adults, leveraging it to mediate social contexts. Our findings suggest that autistic adults show subtle differences in their perception of laughter, which may be associated with their struggles in comprehending the social meaning of laughter, as well as their diminished frequency and enjoyment of laughter in everyday scenarios. By combining experimental evidence with first-person experiences, this study suggests that autistic adults likely employ different strategies to understand laughter in everyday contexts, potentially leaving them socially vulnerable in communication.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista te dice que no entiende bien una risa, tómalo en serio y explícale con calma qué quería decir: si era broma, nervios o cortesía. Es un estudio con personas autistas y no autistas adultas, que valoraron risas genuinas y fingidas y contaron su experiencia diaria. Ambos grupos distinguieron los dos tipos de risa, pero las personas autistas veían la risa fingida como más auténtica, decían reír y disfrutar menos de la risa y les costaba entender su significado social. Aun así, usaban la risa socialmente con la misma frecuencia. Es un solo estudio con adultos y no describe a todas las personas autistas; cada una puede vivir la risa de forma distinta.
sheet.en: If an autistic person tells you a laugh was hard to read, take it seriously and calmly explain what it meant: a joke, nerves or politeness. This study involved autistic and non-autistic adults who rated genuine and posed laughter and described their everyday experience of laughing. Both groups could tell the two types apart, but autistic adults rated posed laughter as more authentic, reported laughing and enjoying laughter less, and found its social meaning harder to understand. They still used laughter socially as often as others. It is a single study with adults and does not describe every autistic person; each person may experience laughter differently.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person säger att ett skratt var svårt att tolka, ta det på allvar och förklara lugnt vad det betydde: ett skämt, nervositet eller artighet. Studien omfattade autistiska och icke-autistiska vuxna som bedömde äkta och spelade skratt och beskrev sina vardagliga erfarenheter av skratt. Båda grupperna kunde skilja de två typerna åt, men autistiska vuxna bedömde spelat skratt som mer äkta, uppgav att de skrattade och njöt av skratt mindre och hade svårare att förstå dess sociala betydelse. De använde ändå skratt socialt lika ofta. Det är en enskild studie med vuxna och beskriver inte alla autistiska personer; var och en kan uppleva skratt olika.

title: Putting the Spotlight Back Onto the Flanker Task in Autism: Autistic Adults Show Increased Interference from Foils Compared with Non-autistic Adults.
authors: Poole D, Grange JA, Milne E
abstract: Autistic people may have a less focused spotlight of spatial selective attention than non-autistic people, meaning that distracting stimuli are less effectively suppressed. Previous studies using the flanker task have supported this suggestion with observations of increased congruency effects in autistic participants. However, findings across studies have been mixed, mainly based on research in children and on response time measures, which may be influenced by differences in response strategy between autistic and non-autistic people rather than differences in selective attention. In this pre-registered study, 153 autistic and 147 non-autistic adults completed an online flanker task. The aims of this study were to test whether increased congruency effects replicate in autistic adults and to extend previous work by fitting a computational model of spatial selective attention on the flanker task to the data. Congruency effects were increased in the autistic group. The modelling revealed that the interference time from the foils was increased in the autistic group. This suggests that the activation of the foils was increased, meaning suppression was less effective for autistic participants. There were also differences in non-interference parameters between the groups. The estimate of response caution was increased in the autistic group and the estimate of perceptual efficiency was decreased. Together these findings suggest inefficient suppression, response strategy and perceptual processing all contribute to differences in performance on the flanker task between autistic and non-autistic people.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista se distrae con estímulos cercanos en tareas de atención, puede ayudar reducir lo que hay alrededor de lo importante: menos elementos en pantalla, más espacio y más tiempo para responder. Es un estudio con personas autistas: 153 adultos autistas y 147 adultos no autistas hicieron una tarea de atención en línea. Los autistas mostraron más interferencia de los estímulos distractores, más cautela al responder y menor eficiencia perceptiva. Son resultados de grupo, de una tarea de laboratorio y sin niños, así que no describen a cada persona ni indican con certeza qué ocurre en la vida diaria.
sheet.en: If an autistic person gets pulled in by nearby distractions during attention tasks, it may help to reduce clutter around what matters: fewer items on screen, more space, and more time to respond. This was a study with autistic people: 153 autistic and 147 non-autistic adults did an online attention task. The autistic group showed more interference from distracting items, more response caution and lower perceptual efficiency. These are group results from one lab-style task, with no children, so they do not describe every person or show for certain what happens in daily life.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person lätt dras till distraktioner i närheten vid uppmärksamhetsuppgifter kan det hjälpa att minska rörigheten kring det viktiga: färre objekt på skärmen, mer utrymme och mer tid att svara. Det var en studie med autistiska personer: 153 autistiska och 147 icke-autistiska vuxna gjorde en uppmärksamhetsuppgift online. Den autistiska gruppen visade mer störning från distraherande objekt, mer försiktighet vid svar och lägre perceptuell effektivitet. Resultaten gäller grupper och en enda laboratorieliknande uppgift, inga barn deltog, så de beskriver inte varje person och visar inte säkert vad som sker i vardagen.

title: Theories on the Link Between Autism Spectrum Conditions and Trans Gender Modality: a Systematic Review.
authors: Wattel LL, Walsh RJ, Krabbendam L
journal: Review journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: While research on the prevalence of co-occurring autism spectrum conditions (ASC) and trans gender modality (TGM) is available, less is known about the underlying mechanism of this association. Insight is needed to improve treatment of trans autistic people. This review provides an overview of theories on the ASC-TGM link and the available evidence for/against them published between January 2016 and October 2020. A systematic search was performed in PubMed, PsycINFO, Web of Science, and Scopus. This resulted in 36 studies, in which 15 theories were identified. Results indicate all theories lack substantial empirical support. Unlikely and promising theories were identified. The most promising theories were those on resistance to social norms and weakened sex differences. Future directions are provided.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista que explora su identidad de género, escúchala y tómala en serio: no hace falta una teoría que explique por qué coinciden ambas cosas. La revisión sistemática buscó en cuatro bases de datos y halló 36 estudios con 15 teorías sobre el vínculo entre autismo y diversidad de género. Concluye que ninguna teoría tiene apoyo empírico sustancial; las más prometedoras hablan de resistencia a las normas sociales y de diferencias sexuales atenuadas. Límites: solo incluye estudios de 2016 a octubre de 2020, y estas teorías no explican a ninguna persona concreta ni deben guiar decisiones sobre ella.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person who is exploring their gender identity, listen and take them seriously: no theory is needed to explain why the two go together. This systematic review searched four databases and found 36 studies covering 15 theories about the link between autism and gender diversity. It concludes that no theory has substantial empirical support; the most promising involve resistance to social norms and weakened sex differences. Limits: it only covers studies from 2016 to October 2020, and these theories do not explain any individual person or guide decisions about them.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person som utforskar sin könsidentitet: lyssna och ta personen på allvar. Ingen teori behövs för att förklara varför de två hänger ihop. Den systematiska översikten sökte i fyra databaser och fann 36 studier med 15 teorier om kopplingen mellan autism och könsmångfald. Slutsatsen är att ingen teori har substantiellt empiriskt stöd; de mest lovande handlar om motstånd mot sociala normer och försvagade könsskillnader. Begränsningar: den omfattar bara studier från 2016 till oktober 2020, och teorierna förklarar ingen enskild person eller bör styra beslut om hen.

title: Autistic adults' views on the design and processes within randomised controlled trials: The APRiCoT study.
authors: Beasant L, Realpe A, Douglas S, Kenny L, Rai D, Mills N
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Large randomised controlled trials are used to test healthcare treatments. Yet there are no large randomised controlled trials on effective treatments for common mental health issues affecting autistic adults. The purpose of this study was to learn what autistic adults think about randomised controlled trials in preparation for a randomised controlled trial testing a medication for anxiety. This means we wanted to know their opinions about the way randomised controlled trials are done, such as how people are chosen to be in the study and how the study is carried out. We did this by talking to 49 autistic adults individually and asking them questions. We found that most of the people we talked to were okay with the way randomised controlled trials are done. They thought it was fair and they liked that it was based on evidence. However, some autistic people might find it hard to take part in randomised controlled trials. Some people did not like the uncertainty of not knowing what treatment they would receive in a randomised controlled trial. Others felt too vulnerable and may have had bad experiences with healthcare in the past. We found that it is important to involve autistic people early on and at every stage when designing a clinical trial. Care about how clear and precise the study communication is will build trust and improve access to research. Our study indicates that it is possible to conduct large randomised controlled trials with and for autistic people. This can ultimately contribute to the improvement of healthcare outcomes for this population.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta se plantea participar en un ensayo clínico, ayuda pedir por adelantado información clara y precisa sobre cómo se elige a los participantes, qué pasará en cada paso y qué significa el azar en la asignación. Este estudio entrevistó individualmente a 49 adultos autistas; a la mayoría le pareció justo el diseño de estos ensayos y valoraba que se basara en evidencia. Algunas personas sintieron incomodidad ante la incertidumbre de no saber qué tratamiento recibirían, o vulnerabilidad por malas experiencias previas en la atención sanitaria. Es un estudio previo a un ensayo con un medicamento, así que las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico. Recoge opiniones, no sirve como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult is considering joining a clinical trial, it helps to ask in advance for clear, precise information about how participants are chosen, what happens at each step, and what chance-based allocation means. This study interviewed 49 autistic adults individually; most found the design of these trials fair and liked that it is based on evidence. Some disliked the uncertainty of not knowing which treatment they would receive, or felt vulnerable because of earlier bad experiences with healthcare. It was preparation for a trial of a medication, so medical decisions belong to a clinician. It reports opinions, not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen överväger att delta i en klinisk studie hjälper det att i förväg be om tydlig och exakt information om hur deltagare väljs, vad som händer i varje steg och vad slumpmässig fördelning innebär. Studien intervjuade 49 autistiska vuxna individuellt. De flesta tyckte att upplägget var rättvist och uppskattade att det bygger på evidens. Några ogillade osäkerheten i att inte veta vilken behandling de skulle få, eller kände sig sårbara på grund av tidigare dåliga erfarenheter av vården. Studien förberedde en prövning av ett läkemedel, så medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker. Den redovisar åsikter och är ingen regel för varje person.

title: A meta-ethnography of autistic people's experiences of social camouflaging and its relationship with mental health.
authors: Field SL, Williams MO, Jones CRG, Fox JRE
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Some autistic people describe trying to hide autistic behaviour and seem more neurotypical. Researchers called this 'social camouflaging' and have linked it with mental health difficulties. We used a step-by-step approach to identify research where autistic people talk about social camouflaging to explore the relationship between camouflaging and poor mental health. Thirteen studies were combined. The results describe how society negatively impacts autistic people's mental health, and camouflaging is a way to try and cope with this. Many autistic people find their camouflaging strategies have accidental negative consequences which also affect their mental health. Strategies which seemed 'successful' involved a lot of self-monitoring, were very mentally demanding or were very habitual and seemed to have more of an effect on mental health. This might be important for clinicians who support autistic people with mental health difficulties.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista oculta rasgos autistas para encajar, conviene preguntarle con calma cómo se siente después y ofrecerle espacios donde no tenga que hacerlo. Es una revisión que combinó 13 estudios en los que personas autistas hablaban de su experiencia de camuflaje social. Describe que el camuflaje es una forma de afrontar el impacto negativo de la sociedad, pero puede tener consecuencias no buscadas para la salud mental; las estrategias que parecen más exitosas, con mucha autovigilancia y esfuerzo mental, parecían pesar más. Sus límites: reúne relatos de otros estudios y no describe a todas las personas autistas ni dice qué hacer en cada caso.
sheet.en: If an autistic person hides autistic traits to fit in, you can calmly ask how they feel afterwards and offer spaces where they don't have to do it. This was a review combining 13 studies in which autistic people talked about social camouflaging. It describes camouflaging as a way of coping with society's negative impact, though it can have unintended consequences for mental health; strategies that seemed 'successful', with a lot of self-monitoring and mental effort, seemed to weigh more. Its limits: it brings together accounts from other studies, does not describe every autistic person and cannot say what to do in each case.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person döljer autistiska drag för att passa in kan du lugnt fråga hur hen mår efteråt och erbjuda miljöer där det inte behövs. Det här var en översikt som sammanställde 13 studier där autistiska personer berättade om social kamouflering. Den beskriver kamouflering som ett sätt att hantera samhällets negativa påverkan, men den kan ge oavsiktliga konsekvenser för den psykiska hälsan; strategier som verkade ”lyckade”, med mycket självövervakning och mental ansträngning, verkade väga tyngre. Begränsningar: den bygger på berättelser från andra studier, beskriver inte alla autistiska personer och kan inte säga vad man bör göra i varje enskilt fall.

title: 'I'm not just being difficult . . . I'm finding it difficult': A qualitative approach to understanding experiences of autistic parents when interacting with statutory services regarding their autistic child.
authors: Radev S, Freeth M, Thompson AR
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Becoming a parent is an important part of adult life for many people, including autistic people. Many parents of autistic children can find getting the right support for their children difficult. Knowledge is currently poor about how this is experienced by parents who are also autistic themselves. The main researcher is also an autistic parent to an autistic child and other experts by experience were consulted in the development of the study. Ten autistic mothers with autistic children in mainstream education were interviewed about their experiences of seeking support for their autistic children from services such as healthcare and education. Participants talked about finding the overall system being the main problem, rather than the individuals working in it, and about needing to fight to get the right support for their children. These are points that non-autistic parents have also raised before. Participants also talked about feeling judged and stigmatised for being autistic, and about struggling to manage sensory and communication difficulties, which is something that has not been talked about by non-autistic parents. Improving services to offer better support to autistic families is important and can be achieved through better training. This training should be developed and run by autistic adults and focus on positive aspects of autism, rather than negative.

sheet.es: Si eres madre o padre autista y tratas con servicios de salud o educación, puede ayudarte saber que no estás sola ni solo: las dificultades que sientes son reales. Antes de una reunión, puedes pedir por escrito la información y avisar de tus necesidades sensoriales y de comunicación. Es un estudio cualitativo con entrevistas a diez madres autistas con hijos autistas en educación ordinaria. Contaron que el problema principal era el sistema, que debían luchar por el apoyo y que se sentían juzgadas por ser autistas. Es un grupo pequeño, solo madres, así que no representa a todas las familias.
sheet.en: If you are an autistic parent dealing with health or education services, it may help to know you are not alone: the difficulties you feel are real. Before a meeting, you could ask for information in writing and tell staff about your sensory and communication needs. This was a qualitative study, with interviews of ten autistic mothers whose autistic children were in mainstream education. They described the overall system as the main problem, needing to fight for support, and feeling judged for being autistic. The group was small and only mothers, so it cannot speak for every family.
sheet.sv: Om du är en autistisk förälder som har kontakt med vård eller skola kan det hjälpa att veta att du inte är ensam: svårigheterna du upplever är verkliga. Inför ett möte kan du be om information skriftligt och berätta om dina sensoriska behov och kommunikationsbehov. Det här var en kvalitativ studie med intervjuer av tio autistiska mammor vars autistiska barn gick i ordinarie skola. De beskrev systemet som det största problemet, att de måste kämpa för stöd och att de kände sig dömda för att vara autistiska. Gruppen var liten och bestod bara av mammor, så den talar inte för alla familjer.

title: A qualitative exploration of an autism-specific self-compassion program: The ASPAA.
authors: Edwards C, Gibbs V, Love AMA, Brown L, Cai RY
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic people often struggle to find the right support for their mental health. We wanted to change that by trying a new approach to help autistic adults with their emotions and well-being. We focused on something called "self-compassion," which is a way of being kind and understanding toward ourselves. This approach has worked well for many people, but we didn't know if it would work for autistic individuals. We invited 39 autistic adults to join an online program that taught them about self-compassion. The program lasted 5 weeks and included educational materials, meditation exercises, and self-reflection activities. We asked the participants for feedback each week and at the end of the program. From their responses, we discovered four important things. First, self-compassion had a big positive impact on the well-being of autistic adults. Second, they faced some challenges during the program. Third, they saw self-compassion as a journey that takes time and practice. Finally, they described how they valued changes to help autistic people engage with the program. Our findings show that self-compassion can really help autistic adults. We learned about the benefits they experienced and the difficulties they faced. Most importantly, we found that personalized support is crucial for autistic individuals. By creating programs that consider their specific needs, we can improve their mental health and make their lives better.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta quiere cuidar su bienestar emocional, puede valer la pena explorar la autocompasión, es decir, tratarse con amabilidad y comprensión, con apoyos adaptados a sus necesidades y a su ritmo. Es un camino que requiere tiempo y práctica. La evidencia es un estudio cualitativo en el que 39 adultos autistas siguieron un programa en línea de 5 semanas, con materiales, meditación y autorreflexión, y dieron opinión cada semana y al final. Sus límites: no compara con otro grupo y recoge experiencias de quienes participaron, así que no sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult wants to look after their emotional well-being, self-compassion, meaning treating yourself with kindness and understanding, may be worth exploring, with supports adapted to their needs and pace. It is a journey that takes time and practice. The evidence is a qualitative study in which 39 autistic adults followed a 5-week online program of educational materials, meditation and self-reflection, giving feedback each week and at the end. Its limits: it has no comparison group and reports the experiences of those who took part, so it is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen vill ta hand om sitt känslomässiga välmående kan självmedkänsla, att möta sig själv med vänlighet och förståelse, vara värt att utforska, med stöd som anpassas efter personens behov och takt. Det är en process som kräver tid och övning. Underlaget är en kvalitativ studie där 39 autistiska vuxna följde ett onlineprogram på 5 veckor med material, meditation och självreflektion och gav återkoppling varje vecka och i slutet. Begränsningar: studien har ingen jämförelsegrupp och beskriver deltagarnas upplevelser, så den är ingen regel för alla.

title: An ecological systems model of employee experience in industry-led autism employment programmes.
authors: Bury SM, Zulla R, Spoor JR, Flower RL, Nicholas DB, Hedley D
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract We asked 33 autistic adults from two industry-led employment programmes about their experiences in the programmes. These are programmes started by companies to recruit and support autistic people in work. We also asked about their workplace supports, relationships and how they thought the programme had impacted their life. Understanding the experiences of people in these industry-led employment programmes is important as the information can help to improve the programmes and participants' experiences. After reviewing the interviews, we found five themes that best described the employee's experience: (1) working involves multiple job tasks that evolve as the employment context changes; (2) relationships in the workplace are diverse and are influenced by the type of work participants do and the work environment; (3) workplace needs change as the autistic employees learn to navigate their work environment; (4) autistic employees develop a professional identity in the workplace as they master work and feel more integrated in the workplace; and (5) recommendations for the development of supportive workplace environments for autistic people. We explored the way that aspects of the two employment programmes (e.g. training) and factors outside the programme changed with time and contributed to the participant's experience. We developed a new model to capture individual and workplace factors that contribute to the experience of autistic people who participate in industry employment programmes.

sheet.es: Si apoyas a una persona autista en su trabajo, revisa con ella de forma periódica qué apoyos necesita, porque esas necesidades pueden cambiar a medida que aprende su entorno laboral. Evidencia: estudio con entrevistas a 33 adultos autistas de dos programas de empleo creados por empresas. Describieron tareas que evolucionan, relaciones laborales diversas y una identidad profesional que crece al dominar el trabajo y sentirse integrados. Límites: son solo dos programas y es una descripción de experiencias, así que no sirve como regla para todas las personas ni todos los lugares de trabajo.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person at work, check in with them regularly about which supports they need, because those needs can change as they learn their work environment. Evidence: an interview study with 33 autistic adults from two employment programmes started by companies. They described tasks that evolve, varied workplace relationships, and a professional identity that grows as they master the work and feel included. Limits: it covers only two programmes and describes experiences, so it is not a rule for every person or every workplace.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person i arbetslivet, prata regelbundet med hen om vilket stöd som behövs, eftersom behoven kan förändras när hen lär sig arbetsmiljön. Evidens: en intervjustudie med 33 autistiska vuxna från två anställningsprogram som startats av företag. De beskrev uppgifter som utvecklas, varierande relationer på jobbet och en yrkesidentitet som växer när de behärskar arbetet och känner sig inkluderade. Begränsningar: endast två program och beskrivningar av erfarenheter, så det är ingen regel för alla personer eller arbetsplatser.

title: "A perfect storm": Autistic experiences of menopause and midlife.
authors: Brady MJ, Jenkins CA, Gamble-Turner JM, Moseley RL, Janse van Rensburg M, Matthews RJ
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Previous studies report that menopause can be a very difficult transition for some autistic people. This study focuses on how autistic people experience menopause and what support and information might help them. Autistic Community Research Associates played an important role in the research and co-authored this article. We held four focus groups and eight interviews online with 24 autistic participants who lived in either Canada ( n = 13) or the United Kingdom ( n = 11). We analysed participant conversations using a method called reflexive thematic analysis. Participants described many intense challenges during menopause. Four themes and eight subthemes were identified across participant groups: (1) Complexity, multiplicity and intensity of symptoms (0 subthemes); (2) Life experience and adversity converging at midlife (three subthemes); (3) The importance of knowledge and connection (two subthemes); and (4) Barriers to support and care (three subthemes). The experiences of our participants may not be the same as other autistic people, and the study could have been more inclusive of diverse autistic groups. However, hearing about the experiences of others may provide reassurance to autistic people who struggle with menopause and let them know they are not alone.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista en la menopausia o en la mitad de la vida, escucha sus experiencias, ayúdala a encontrar información clara y a conectar con otras personas autistas, y acompáñala a consultas para que su relato sea tomado en serio. Este estudio cualitativo reunió a 24 personas autistas de Canadá (13) y del Reino Unido (11) en grupos de conversación y entrevistas en línea. Describieron síntomas intensos, vidas con mucha carga acumulada, la importancia del conocimiento y la conexión, y barreras para recibir apoyo. Sus vivencias pueden no coincidir con las de otras personas autistas, y el estudio podría haber incluido más diversidad.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person going through menopause or midlife, listen to their experience, help them find clear information and connect with other autistic people, and offer to go with them to appointments so they are taken seriously. This qualitative study held online focus groups and interviews with 24 autistic people from Canada (13) and the United Kingdom (11). They described intense symptoms, lives with a lot of accumulated strain, the value of knowledge and connection, and barriers to support and care. Their experiences may differ from those of other autistic people, and the study could have included more diverse autistic groups.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person i klimakteriet eller i medelåldern: lyssna på hennes eller hans upplevelse, hjälp till att hitta tydlig information och kontakt med andra autistiska personer, och följ gärna med på besök så att hen tas på allvar. Studien var kvalitativ och bestod av fokusgrupper och intervjuer online med 24 autistiska deltagare från Kanada (13) och Storbritannien (11). De beskrev intensiva symtom, liv med mycket ackumulerad belastning, vikten av kunskap och gemenskap samt hinder för stöd och vård. Upplevelserna kan skilja sig från andra autistiska personers, och studien kunde ha inkluderat fler olika autistiska grupper.

title: "I am afraid of being treated badly if I show it": A cross-sectional study of healthcare accessibility and Autism Health Passports among UK Autistic adults.
authors: Grant A, Turner S, Shaw SCK, Williams K, Morgan H, Ellis R, Brown A
abstract: Background Autistic people are more likely to experience stigma, communication barriers and anxiety during healthcare. Autism Health Passports (AHPs) are a communication tool that aim to provide information about healthcare needs in a standardised way. They are recommended in research and policy to improve healthcare quality. Aim To explore views and experiences of AHPs among Autistic people from the UK who have been pregnant. Methods We developed an online survey using a combination of open and closed questions focused on healthcare impairments and views and experiences of AHPs. Data were anlaysed using descriptive statistics, Kruskal-Wallis tests, and content analysis. Findings Of 193 Autistic respondents (54% diagnosed, 22% undergoing diagnosis and 24% self-identifying), over 80% reported anxiety and masking during healthcare always or most of the time. Some significant differences were identified in healthcare (in)accessibility by diagnostic status. Only 4% of participants knew a lot about AHPs, with 1.5% of participants using one at least half of the time. Almost three quarters of respondents had not previously seen an AHP. Open text responses indicated that the biggest barrier to using an AHP was a belief that health professionals would discriminate against Autistic patients. Additional barriers included staff lack of familiarity with AHPs and respondents expecting a negative response to producing an AHP. Conclusions Our findings suggest that AHPs are not reducing health inequalities for Autistic adults who have been pregnant. Alternative solutions are needed to reduce health inequalities for Autistic people.

sheet.es: Si vas a una cita médica con una persona autista, hablad antes de qué le preocupa y qué apoyos necesita, y decidid juntas si quiere usar un pasaporte de salud para autismo u otra forma de explicarlo. Es una encuesta en línea a 193 personas autistas del Reino Unido que habían estado embarazadas. Más del 80% refirió ansiedad y enmascaramiento en la atención sanitaria siempre o casi siempre. Casi tres cuartos nunca habían visto un pasaporte, y muchas temían un trato discriminatorio. Es un estudio transversal con un grupo concreto, así que no vale para todas las personas. Las conclusiones sugieren que los pasaportes por sí solos no bastan.
sheet.en: If you are going to a medical appointment with an autistic person, talk beforehand about what worries them and what support they need, and decide together whether they want to use an Autism Health Passport or another way of explaining it. This was an online survey of 193 autistic adults in the UK who had been pregnant. Over 80% reported anxiety and masking during healthcare always or most of the time. Almost three quarters had never seen a passport, and many feared discrimination from professionals. It is a cross-sectional study of one specific group, so it does not apply to everyone. The authors conclude that passports alone are not enough.
sheet.sv: Om du följer med en autistisk person på ett läkarbesök, prata i förväg om vad som oroar och vilket stöd som behövs, och bestäm tillsammans om hen vill använda ett hälsopass för autism eller något annat sätt att förklara. Studien var en webbenkät med 193 autistiska vuxna i Storbritannien som hade varit gravida. Över 80 % uppgav ångest och maskering i vården alltid eller oftast. Nästan tre fjärdedelar hade aldrig sett ett hälsopass, och många fruktade diskriminering från vårdpersonal. Det är en tvärsnittsstudie av en särskild grupp och gäller därför inte alla. Forskarna menar att hälsopass ensamma inte räcker.

title: Camouflaging in Autism: Age Effects and Cross-Cultural Validation of the Camouflaging Autistic Traits Questionnaire (CAT-Q).
authors: Lundin Remnélius K, Bölte S
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Given that camouflaging has been suggested to contribute to delayed diagnosis and mental health problems among autistic people, validated measures of the construct are needed. This study describes the psychometric evaluation of the Swedish adaptation of the self-reported Camouflaging Autistic Traits Questionnaire (CAT-Q) in autistic (n = 100) and general population (n = 539) samples aged 10 to 83 years. Analyses indicated good-to-excellent internal consistency and test-retest reliability. Construct validity was supported by autistic participants scoring higher than non-autistic, and autistic females scoring higher than autistic males on the measure. Also as expected, camouflaging was associated with theoretically linked traits, including autistic behaviors and depressive symptoms. On the other hand, the factor structure of the original CAT-Q did not provide a good fit in the Swedish data set, and validity issues were found, particularly in children younger than 15 years, warranting further investigation of the construct validity of the scale. Different age trajectories were observed, where camouflaging behaviors decreased during adulthood in non-autistic people but remained at an elevated level among autistic people.

sheet.es: Si cuidas de una persona autista, puede ayudar preguntarle con calma si a veces oculta rasgos autistas para encajar, y ofrecerle espacios donde no tenga que hacerlo. La evidencia: un estudio con personas autistas (100) y población general (539), de 10 a 83 años, evaluó la versión sueca de un cuestionario de autoinforme sobre camuflaje. Las personas autistas puntuaron más alto, y el camuflaje se asoció con más síntomas depresivos. Límites: el cuestionario no funcionó bien en menores de 15 años y su estructura no encajó del todo, así que los resultados no valen como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person, it may help to ask calmly whether they sometimes hide autistic traits to fit in, and to offer spaces where they don't have to. The evidence: a study with autistic people (100) and the general population (539), aged 10 to 83, tested the Swedish version of a self-report questionnaire on camouflaging. Autistic people scored higher, and camouflaging was linked to more depressive symptoms. Limits: the questionnaire did not work well for children under 15 and its structure did not fit fully, so the results are not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person kan det hjälpa att lugnt fråga om hen ibland döljer autistiska drag för att passa in, och erbjuda miljöer där det inte behövs. Evidensen: en studie med autistiska personer (100) och allmänbefolkning (539), 10 till 83 år, prövade den svenska versionen av ett självskattningsformulär om kamouflering. Autistiska personer fick högre poäng, och kamouflering hängde ihop med fler depressiva symtom. Begränsningar: formuläret fungerade dåligt för barn under 15 år och dess struktur passade inte helt, så resultaten gäller inte som regel för varje person.

title: Enhanced sensitivity to pitch perception and its possible relation to language acquisition in autism.
authors: Hisaizumi M, Tantam D
abstract: Background and aims Fascinations for or aversions to particular sounds are a familiar feature of autism, as is an ability to reproduce another person's utterances, precisely copying the other person's prosody as well as their words. Such observations seem to indicate not only that autistic people can pay close attention to what they hear, but also that they have the ability to perceive the finer details of auditory stimuli. This is consistent with the previously reported consensus that absolute pitch is more common in autistic individuals than in neurotypicals. We take this to suggest that autistic people have perception that allows them to pay attention to fine details. It is important to establish whether or not this is so as autism is often presented as a deficit rather than a difference. We therefore undertook a narrative literature review of studies of auditory perception, in autistic and nonautistic individuals, focussing on any differences in processing linguistic and nonlinguistic sounds. Main contributions We find persuasive evidence that nonlinguistic auditory perception in autistic children differs from that of nonautistic children. This is supported by the additional finding of a higher prevalence of absolute pitch and enhanced pitch discriminating abilities in autistic children compared to neurotypical children. Such abilities appear to stem from atypical perception, which is biased toward local-level information necessary for processing pitch and other prosodic features. Enhanced pitch discriminating abilities tend to be found in autistic individuals with a history of language delay, suggesting possible reciprocity. Research on various aspects of language development in autism also supports the hypothesis that atypical pitch perception may be accountable for observed differences in language development in autism. Conclusions The results of our review of previously published studies are consistent with the hypothesis that auditory perception, and particularly pitch perception, in autism are different from the norm but not always impaired. Detail-oriented pitch perception may be an advantage given the right environment. We speculate that unusually heightened sensitivity to pitch differences may be at the cost of the normal development of the perception of the sounds that contribute most to early language development. Implications The acquisition of speech and language may be a process that normally involves an enhanced perception of speech sounds at the expense of the processing of nonlinguistic sounds, but autistic children may not give speech sounds this same priority.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista reacciona con fuerza a ciertos sonidos o repite con exactitud lo que oye, quizá perciba detalles del sonido, como el tono, que otros no notan. Puede ser una fortaleza: ofrezca entornos sonoros que respeten esa forma de oír. La evidencia es una revisión narrativa de estudios previos sobre percepción auditiva en personas autistas y no autistas, sobre todo niñas y niños. Sus límites: las autoras plantean la relación con el desarrollo del lenguaje como hipótesis y especulación, y no sirve como regla para todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person reacts strongly to certain sounds or repeats exactly what they hear, they may be perceiving fine details of sound, such as pitch, that others miss. This can be a strength: offer sound environments that respect how they hear. The evidence is a narrative review of earlier studies on auditory perception in autistic and nonautistic people, mostly children. Its limits: the authors present the link to language development as a hypothesis and speculation, and it is not a rule for every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person reagerar starkt på vissa ljud eller upprepar exakt det hon hör, kan hon uppfatta finare ljuddetaljer, som tonhöjd, som andra missar. Det kan vara en styrka: erbjud ljudmiljöer som respekterar hur hon hör. Underlaget är en narrativ översikt av tidigare studier om hörselperception hos autistiska och icke-autistiska personer, främst barn. Begränsningar: författarna beskriver kopplingen till språkutveckling som en hypotes och spekulation, och den gäller inte som regel för alla autistiska personer.

title: Trajectories of adaptive functioning from early childhood to adolescence in autism: Identifying turning points and key correlates of chronogeneity.
authors: Chen YJ, Duku E, Szatmari P, Salt M, Smith I, Richard A, Zwaigenbaum L, Vaillancourt T, Zaidman-Zait A, Bennett T, Elsabbagh M, Kerns C, Georgiades S
abstract: Background Previous research has demonstrated heterogeneous adaptive outcomes across the autism spectrum; however, the current literature remains limited in elucidating turning points and associated factors for longitudinal variability (chronogeneity). To address these empirical gaps, we aimed to provide a finer-grained characterization of trajectories of adaptive functioning from early childhood to adolescence in autism. Methods Our sample ( N = 406) was drawn from an inception cohort of children diagnosed Autistic at ages 2-5. Adaptive functioning was assessed with Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scales (VABS, 2 nd Edition) across 6 visits from the time of diagnosis by age 18. Parallel-process latent growth curve modeling were used to estimate domain-level VABS trajectories, followed by latent class growth analysis to identify trajectory subgroups. Child characteristics at diagnosis, family demographics, and participation outcomes at adolescence were compared across subgroups. Results Piecewise latent growth models best described VABS trajectories with two turning points identified at around ages 5-6 and 9-10, respectively reflecting transitions into school age and early adolescence. We parsed four VABS trajectory subgroups that vary by level of functioning and change rate for certain domains and periods. Around 16% of the sample exhibited overall adequate functioning (standard score >85) with notable early growth and social adaptation during adolescence. About 21% showed low adaptive functioning (standard score ≤70), with decreasing slopes by age 6 followed by improvements in communication and daily-living skills by age 10. The other two subgroups (63% in total) were characterized by adaptive functioning between low and adequate levels, with relatively stable trajectories entering school age. These subgroups differed most in their cognitive ability at diagnosis, household income, and social participation in adolescence.
