Conclusions We identified key individual and family characteristics and time windows associated with distinct adaptive functioning trajectories, which have important implications for providing timely and tailored supports to Autistic people across developmental stages.

sheet.es: Conviene revisar los apoyos en los cambios de etapa, sobre todo al entrar en la escuela y al inicio de la adolescencia, y ajustarlos a cada persona. El estudio siguió a 406 niñas y niños autistas diagnosticados entre los 2 y 5 años, con seis valoraciones de habilidades de la vida diaria hasta los 18 años. Encontró dos puntos de giro, hacia los 5-6 y los 9-10 años, y cuatro trayectorias distintas, que se relacionaron con la capacidad cognitiva al diagnóstico, los ingresos del hogar y la participación social en la adolescencia. Describe grupos, no predice el camino de una persona concreta, y no explica las causas de las diferencias.
sheet.en: It is worth reviewing supports at points of transition, especially school entry and early adolescence, and tailoring them to the individual. The study followed 406 autistic children diagnosed at ages 2-5, with six assessments of adaptive functioning up to age 18. It found two turning points, around ages 5-6 and 9-10, and four distinct trajectories, linked to cognitive ability at diagnosis, household income and social participation in adolescence. It describes groups, so it cannot predict any one person's path, and it does not show what causes the differences.
sheet.sv: Det är värt att se över stödet vid övergångar, särskilt vid skolstart och i början av tonåren, och anpassa det till varje person. Studien följde 406 autistiska barn som fått diagnos vid 2-5 års ålder, med sex bedömningar av adaptiv förmåga fram till 18 års ålder. Den fann två vändpunkter, runt 5-6 och 9-10 års ålder, och fyra olika utvecklingsmönster, kopplade till kognitiv förmåga vid diagnos, hushållets inkomst och social delaktighet i tonåren. Den beskriver grupper och kan inte förutsäga en enskild persons väg, och den visar inte vad som orsakar skillnaderna.

title: Associations between atypical intracortical myelin content and neuropsychological functions in middle to older aged adults with ASD.
authors: Kohli JS, Linke AC, Martindale IA, Wilkinson M, Kinnear MK, Lincoln AJ, Hau J, Shryock I, Omaleki V, Alemu K, Pedrahita S, Fishman I, Müller RA, Carper RA
abstract: Introduction In vivo myeloarchitectonic mapping based on Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) provides a unique view of gray matter myelin content and offers information complementary to other morphological indices commonly employed in studies of autism spectrum disorder (ASD). The current study sought to determine if intracortical myelin content (MC) and its age-related trajectories differ between middle aged to older adults with ASD and age-matched typical comparison participants. Methods Data from 30 individuals with ASD and 36 age-matched typical comparison participants aged 40-70 years were analyzed. Given substantial heterogeneity in both etiology and outcomes in ASD, we utilized both group-level and subject-level analysis approaches to test for signs of atypical intracortical MC as estimated by T1w/T2w ratio. Results Group-level analyses showed no significant differences in average T1w/T2w ratio or its associations with age between groups, but revealed significant positive main effects of age bilaterally, with T1w/T2w ratio increasing with age across much of the cortex. In subject-level analyses, participants were classified into subgroups based on presence or absence of clusters of aberrant T1w/T2w ratio, and lower neuropsychological function was observed in the ASD subgroup with atypically high T1w/T2w ratio in spatially heterogeneous cortical regions. These differences were observed across several neuropsychological domains, including overall intellectual functioning, processing speed, and aspects of executive function. Conclusions The group-level and subject-level approaches employed here demonstrate the value of examining inter-individual variability and provide important preliminary insights into relationships between brain structure and cognition in the second half of the lifespan in ASD, suggesting shared factors contributing to atypical intracortical myelin content and poorer cognitive outcomes for a subset of middle aged to older autistic adults. These atypicalities likely reflect diverse histories of neurodevelopmental deficits, and possible compensatory changes, compounded by processes of aging, and may serve as useful markers of vulnerability to further cognitive decline in older adults with ASD.

sheet.es: Tras los 40 años, conviene observar el ritmo y las necesidades de cada persona autista, sin suponer que todas cambiarán igual. Si notas cambios en la velocidad de pensar o en la organización diaria, anótalos y coméntalos con un profesional. Se trata de un estudio con resonancia magnética: 30 personas autistas y 36 sin autismo, de 40-70 años. Por término medio no hubo diferencias entre grupos, pero un subgrupo autista con patrones cerebrales atípicos mostró menor rendimiento en pruebas cognitivas. Los autores lo describen como preliminar; la muestra es pequeña y no sirve como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: After age 40, it helps to notice each autistic person's own pace and needs, rather than assuming everyone will change in the same way. If you see changes in thinking speed or daily organisation, jot them down and discuss them with a professional. This was an MRI study of 30 autistic adults and 36 non-autistic adults aged 40-70. On average the groups did not differ, but one autistic subgroup with atypical brain patterns scored lower on cognitive tests. The authors call the findings preliminary; the sample is small and it is not a rule for any individual.
sheet.sv: Efter 40 års ålder är det bra att se varje autistisk persons eget tempo och behov, utan att anta att alla förändras likadant. Om du märker förändringar i tankehastighet eller vardagsplanering kan du anteckna dem och ta upp dem med en professionell. Det här var en MR-studie med 30 autistiska vuxna och 36 icke-autistiska vuxna i åldern 40-70 år. I genomsnitt skilde sig grupperna inte åt, men en autistisk undergrupp med atypiska hjärnmönster presterade lägre på kognitiva tester. Författarna kallar resultaten preliminära; urvalet är litet och det är ingen regel för den enskilda personen.

title: European Autism GEnomics Registry (EAGER): protocol for a multicentre cohort study and registry.
authors: Bloomfield M, Lautarescu A, Heraty S, Douglas S, Violland P, Plas R, Ghosh A, Van den Bosch K, Eaton E, Absoud M, Battini R, Blázquez Hinojosa A, Bolshakova N, Bölte S, Bonanni P, Borg J, Calderoni S,
abstract: Introduction Autism is a common neurodevelopmental condition with a complex genetic aetiology that includes contributions from monogenic and polygenic factors. Many autistic people have unmet healthcare needs that could be served by genomics-informed research and clinical trials. The primary aim of the European Autism GEnomics Registry (EAGER) is to establish a registry of participants with a diagnosis of autism or an associated rare genetic condition who have undergone whole-genome sequencing. The registry can facilitate recruitment for future clinical trials and research studies, based on genetic, clinical and phenotypic profiles, as well as participant preferences. The secondary aim of EAGER is to investigate the association between mental and physical health characteristics and participants' genetic profiles. Methods and analysis EAGER is a European multisite cohort study and registry and is part of the AIMS-2-TRIALS consortium. EAGER was developed with input from the AIMS-2-TRIALS Autism Representatives and representatives from the rare genetic conditions community. 1500 participants with a diagnosis of autism or an associated rare genetic condition will be recruited at 13 sites across 8 countries. Participants will be given a blood or saliva sample for whole-genome sequencing and answer a series of online questionnaires. Participants may also consent to the study to access pre-existing clinical data. Participants will be added to the EAGER registry and data will be shared externally through established AIMS-2-TRIALS mechanisms. Ethics and dissemination To date, EAGER has received full ethical approval for 11 out of the 13 sites in the UK (REC 23/SC/0022), Germany (S-375/2023), Portugal (CE-085/2023), Spain (HCB/2023/0038, PIC-164-22), Sweden (Dnr 2023-06737-01), Ireland (230907) and Italy (CET_62/2023, CEL-IRCCS OASI/24-01-2024/EM01, EM 2024-13/1032 EAGER). Findings will be disseminated via scientific publications and conferences but also beyond to participants and the wider community (eg, the AIMS-2-TRIALS website, stakeholder meetings, newsletters).

sheet.es: Si le ofrecen participar en un registro de investigación genética, tómese tiempo para preguntar qué datos se recogen, cómo se comparten y qué preferencias puede indicar la persona autista. La decisión es suya y puede ser revisada. Esto es un protocolo: describe un estudio de cohorte y registro europeo con personas autistas, que prevé reclutar a 1500 participantes en 13 centros de 8 países, con muestra de sangre o saliva y cuestionarios en línea. Aún no presenta resultados, así que no dice nada sobre ninguna persona concreta. La secuenciación genética no sustituye la valoración clínica, y las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional sanitario.
sheet.en: If you are offered a place in a genetics research registry, take your time to ask what data are collected, how they are shared, and what preferences the autistic person can state. The choice is theirs and can be revisited. This is a protocol: it describes a European cohort study and registry with autistic people, planning to recruit 1500 participants at 13 sites across 8 countries, using a blood or saliva sample and online questionnaires. It reports no results yet, so it says nothing about any individual person. Genetic sequencing does not replace clinical assessment, and medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om du erbjuds att delta i ett forskningsregister med genetik, ta god tid på dig att fråga vilka data som samlas in, hur de delas och vilka önskemål den autistiska personen kan ange. Beslutet är personens eget och kan omprövas. Detta är ett protokoll: det beskriver en europeisk kohortstudie och ett register med autistiska personer, där man planerar att rekrytera 1500 deltagare vid 13 centra i 8 länder, med blod- eller salivprov och webbenkäter. Inga resultat redovisas ännu, så det säger inget om någon enskild person. Genetisk sekvensering ersätter inte klinisk bedömning, och medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker.

title: New advances in the diagnosis and treatment of autism spectrum disorders.
authors: Qin L, Wang H, Ning W, Cui M, Wang Q
abstract: Autism spectrum disorders (ASD) are a group of neurodevelopmental disorders that affect individuals' social interactions, communication skills, and behavioral patterns, with significant individual differences and complex etiology. This article reviews the definition and characteristics of ASD, epidemiological profile, early research and diagnostic history, etiological studies, advances in diagnostic methods, therapeutic approaches and intervention strategies, social and educational integration, and future research directions. The highly heritable nature of ASD, the role of environmental factors, genetic-environmental interactions, and the need for individualized, integrated, and technology-driven treatment strategies are emphasized. Also discussed is the interaction of social policy with ASD research and the outlook for future research and treatment, including the promise of precision medicine and emerging biotechnology applications. The paper points out that despite the remarkable progress that has been made, there are still many challenges to the comprehensive understanding and effective treatment of ASD, and interdisciplinary and cross-cultural research and global collaboration are needed to further deepen the understanding of ASD and improve the quality of life of patients.

sheet.es: Lo práctico: cada persona autista es distinta, así que conviene buscar apoyos individualizados y combinados (educativos, sociales y de comunicación) en lugar de un único enfoque para todos. Pregunte siempre qué le resulta útil a la persona. Evidencia: es una revisión de la literatura que repasa definición, diagnóstico, causas, intervenciones e integración social y educativa; no describe un grupo de participantes. Límites: es un panorama general, no prueba que una estrategia concreta funcione para una persona determinada, y habla de futuras posibilidades como la medicina de precisión que aún no son rutina. Las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: Practical takeaway: every autistic person is different, so look for individualised, combined supports (educational, social and communication) rather than one approach for everyone. Always ask the person what helps them. Evidence: this is a review of the literature covering definition, diagnosis, causes, interventions and social and educational inclusion; it does not describe a group of participants. Limits: it is a broad overview, not proof that a specific strategy will work for a particular person, and it discusses future possibilities such as precision medicine that are not yet routine. Medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Praktiskt: varje autistisk person är olika, så sök individanpassat och kombinerat stöd (pedagogiskt, socialt och kommunikativt) i stället för en enda metod för alla. Fråga alltid personen själv vad som hjälper. Evidens: det här är en översikt av litteraturen som tar upp definition, diagnostik, orsaker, insatser samt social och pedagogisk inkludering; den beskriver ingen grupp deltagare. Begränsningar: det är en bred överblick och visar inte att en viss strategi fungerar för en enskild person, och den diskuterar framtida möjligheter som precisionsmedicin som ännu inte är rutin. Medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker.

title: Feasibility and acceptability of autism adapted safety plans: an external pilot randomised controlled trial.
authors: Rodgers J, Cassidy S, Pelton M, Goodwin J, Wagnild J, Bhattarai N, Gordon I, Wilson C, Heslop P, Ogundimu E, O'Connor RC, Ramsay SE, Townsend E, Vale L
abstract: Background Autistic people are a high-risk group for self-harm and suicide. There are no evidence-based suicide prevention interventions developed specifically for autistic people. We undertook a pilot feasibility randomised controlled trial of autism adapted safety plans (AASP) to reduce self-harm and suicide for autistic people. Methods This study took place in the United Kingdom and followed a randomised, two-arm, controlled design. Autistic adults (n = 53, mean age = 39, gender = 49% female, 29% not male or female) were recruited via third sector organisations and self-referral between 11.8.21 and 19.10.22. Participants were randomised without stratification to usual care with or without AASP. The AASP was completed by the autistic adults together with someone trained to support them. Research staff who completed follow-up assessments were blind to participant allocation. Primary outcomes were feasibility and acceptability. Participants were assessed at baseline, 1 and 6 months. Primary data were analysed under the intention to treat principle. Study protocol is published. The trial is closed to new participants. This study is registered with the ISRCTN registry, ISRCTN70594445. Findings 53 participants consented, 49 were randomised to either AASP with usual care (n = 25) or usual care (n = 24). 68% of participants in the AASP arm were satisfied with the AASP and 41% rated it as useable. Feedback on the AASP and research methods were positive with suggested adaptations to some outcome measures. Retention and completion of outcomes measures in both arms was excellent, as was fidelity of delivery of the AASP. Interpretation Study progression criteria were met, suggesting that the parameters of a future definitive trial of clinical and cost effectiveness of AASP to reduce self-harm and suicide in autistic adults are achievable, with minor recommended adaptions to outcome measures and AASP. Future research should explore the use of AASP in routine clinical practice. Funding This study is funded by the NIHR [Public Health Research Programme (NIHR129196)].

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista con riesgo de autolesión o suicidio, puede valer la pena preguntar a un profesional por un plan de seguridad adaptado al autismo, que se completa junto a alguien formado para apoyar. Evidencia: ensayo piloto aleatorizado en el Reino Unido con 53 personas autistas adultas; el 68% de quienes recibieron el plan quedó satisfecho y el 41% lo valoró como utilizable. Límites: es un estudio piloto pequeño que midió si el plan es viable y aceptable, no si reduce la autolesión o el suicidio, y no sirve como regla para todas las personas. Busca ayuda profesional (clínico, servicio de salud o servicio de crisis). Si hay peligro inmediato, llama al número de emergencias de tu país.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person at risk of self-harm or suicide, it may be worth asking a professional about an autism adapted safety plan, completed together with someone trained to support them. Evidence: a pilot randomised trial in the United Kingdom with 53 autistic adults; 68% of those given the plan were satisfied with it and 41% rated it as useable. Limits: this was a small pilot that tested whether the plan is feasible and acceptable, not whether it reduces self-harm or suicide, and it is not a rule for every person. Please seek professional help (a clinician, a health service or a crisis service). In immediate danger, call your country's emergency number.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person med risk för självskada eller självmord kan det vara värt att fråga en yrkesperson om en autismanpassad säkerhetsplan, som görs tillsammans med någon som är utbildad att stödja. Evidens: en randomiserad pilotstudie i Storbritannien med 53 autistiska vuxna; 68% av dem som fick planen var nöjda och 41% bedömde den som användbar. Begränsningar: det var en liten pilotstudie som testade om planen är genomförbar och acceptabel, inte om den minskar självskada eller självmord, och den gäller inte som regel för alla. Sök professionell hjälp (en läkare, vården eller en krisjour). Vid akut fara, ring ditt lands nödnummer.

title: What is the Meaning of Paid Employment for Well-Being? A Focus Group Study on Differences and Similarities Between Autistic Adults With and Without Employment.
authors: Brouwers EPM, Bergijk M, van Weeghel J, Detaille S, Dewinter J
abstract: Purpose The aim of the present study was to explore the meaning of work for the subjective well-being of autistic adults with and without paid (competitive) employment and to evaluate the differences and similarities between these groups. Methods Eight focus groups were conducted, including a total of 64 autistic adults. Four groups entailed participants with current paid employment (including part-time) and four groups entailed participants without paid employment. All discussions were audiotaped and transcribed verbatim to enable inductive thematic content analysis. Data were analyzed using ATLAS.ti 9. Results Generally, both groups viewed paid employment as very important for well-being, albeit for different reasons. Three themes were found: (1) Not having paid employment was associated with lacking societal recognition, and subsequent low self-esteem, which was a dominant theme in those without work; (2) Work can seriously damage (mental) health and well-being, found in both groups; and (3) Paid employment provides many benefits for well-being, with subthemes: 'purpose,' 'social contacts,' 'growth and use of talents,' 'structure and calmness,' and 'income and freedom', which was a dominant theme in those with paid employment. Conclusions Both groups found paid employment highly important for their well-being, albeit for different reasons. However, both also agreed that paid employment can be very harmful to (mental) health and well-being. Suitable, well-supported jobs are important for well-being, may help to buffer stress in other life areas, and may even prevent autistic burnout. More studies are needed on how healthy jobs can be created where autistic individuals get positive energy and experience high well-being. This will also help to reduce socio-economic inequality.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista en temas de trabajo, pregúntale qué significa el empleo para ella: reconocimiento, estructura, contactos o ingresos, y qué lo haría sostenible. Un puesto adecuado y con apoyo puede ayudar al bienestar, pero un trabajo que no encaja puede dañar la salud mental. Es un estudio con grupos de discusión en los que participaron 64 personas adultas autistas, con y sin empleo remunerado. Recoge opiniones, no mide resultados, y no se puede aplicar a todas las personas ni demuestra causas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person around work, ask what employment means to them: recognition, structure, social contact or income, and what would make a job sustainable. A suitable, well-supported job may help well-being, but a poor fit can harm mental health. This was a focus group study with 64 autistic adults, with and without paid employment. It captures views and experiences, not measured outcomes, so it cannot show cause and effect or describe every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person kring arbete, fråga vad arbete betyder för hen: erkännande, struktur, sociala kontakter eller inkomst, och vad som skulle göra ett jobb hållbart. Ett passande jobb med bra stöd kan gynna välbefinnandet, men ett jobb som inte passar kan skada den psykiska hälsan. Detta var en fokusgruppstudie med 64 autistiska vuxna, med och utan avlönat arbete. Den visar upplevelser och åsikter, inte uppmätta resultat, så den kan inte visa orsak och verkan eller gälla alla autistiska personer.

title: Effectiveness of animal-assisted activities and therapies for autism spectrum disorder: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Xiao N, Bagayi V, Yang D, Huang X, Zhong L, Kiselev S, Bolkov MA, Tuzankina IA, Chereshnev VA
abstract: Background Given the rising interest in complementary therapeutic strategies for autism spectrum disorder (ASD), this research aims to provide a comprehensive analysis of the impact of animal-assisted activities and therapies (AAAT) on various ASD symptoms. Methods A meticulous search of databases, including Scopus and PubMed, was conducted to gather relevant research on AAAT for ASD. This process led to the selection of 45 studies encompassing 1,212 participants. The chosen studies were then subjected to a meta-analysis to evaluate the efficacy of AAAT in alleviating core ASD symptoms. Results The meta-analysis revealed significant improvements in several core ASD symptoms due to AAAT. Notably, there were improvements in social communication (MD = -4.96, 95% CI [-7.49, -2.44]), irritability (MD = -2.38, 95% CI [-4.06, -0.71]), hyperactivity (MD = -4.03, 95% CI [-6.17, -1.89]), and different word usage skills (MD = 20.48, 95% CI [7.41, 33.55]). However, social awareness (MD = -1.63, 95% CI [-4.07, 0.81]), social cognition (MD = -3.60, 95% CI [-9.36, 2.17]), social mannerisms (MD = -0.73, 95% CI [-2.55, 1.09]), social motivation (MD = -1.21, 95% CI [-2.56, 0.13]), lethargy (MD = -1.12, 95% CI [-3.92, 1.68]), and stereotypical behaviors (MD = -0.23, 95% CI [-1.27, 0.80]) did not significantly improve. Conclusion The study demonstrates the potential of AAAT in improving certain core symptoms of ASD, such as social communication, irritability, hyperactivity, and word usage skills. However, the effectiveness of AAAT in other ASD symptom domains remains uncertain. The research is limited by the absence of long-term follow-up data and a high risk of bias in existing studies. Therefore, while the findings indicate the promise of AAAT in specific areas, caution is advised in generalizing its efficacy across all ASD symptoms.

sheet.es: Si le interesa que una persona autista pase tiempo con animales en una actividad guiada, puede probarlo con calma y observar si le agrada y si le resulta útil; no es imprescindible ni sirve igual para todas. La evidencia es un metaanálisis de 45 estudios con 1,212 participantes. Halló mejoras en comunicación social, irritabilidad, hiperactividad y uso de palabras, pero no en otros ámbitos, como la motivación social o las conductas estereotipadas. Sus límites: no hay seguimiento a largo plazo y los estudios tienen un alto riesgo de sesgo, así que conviene ser prudente.
sheet.en: If an autistic person is interested in spending time with animals in a guided activity, you can try it calmly and watch whether they enjoy it and find it useful; it is not essential and will not suit everyone equally. The evidence is a meta-analysis of 45 studies with 1,212 participants. It found improvements in social communication, irritability, hyperactivity and word use, but not in other areas, such as social motivation or stereotypical behaviors. Its limits: there is no long-term follow-up and the studies have a high risk of bias, so caution is advised.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person är intresserad av att umgås med djur i en guidad aktivitet kan ni prova det lugnt och se om hen trivs och har nytta av det; det är inte nödvändigt och passar inte alla lika bra. Underlaget är en metaanalys av 45 studier med 1,212 deltagare. Den fann förbättringar i social kommunikation, irritabilitet, hyperaktivitet och ordanvändning, men inte inom andra områden, till exempel social motivation eller stereotypa beteenden. Begränsningar: det saknas långtidsuppföljning och studierna har hög risk för bias, så försiktighet rekommenderas.

title: Overlap of eating disorders and neurodivergence: the role of inhibitory control.
authors: Norton B, Sheen J, Burns L, Enticott PG, Fuller-Tyszkiewicz M, Kirkovski M
abstract: Background Difficulties with inhibitory control have been identified in eating disorders (EDs) and neurodevelopmental disorders (NDs; including attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and autism spectrum disorder), and there appear to be parallels between the expression of these impairments. It is theorised that impairments in inhibitory control within NDs may represent a unique vulnerability for eating disorders (EDs), and this same mechanism may contribute to poorer treatment outcomes. This review seeks to determine the state of the literature concerning the role of inhibitory control in the overlap of EDs and neurodivergence. Method A scoping review was conducted to summarise extant research, and to identify gaps in the existing knowledge base. Scopus, Medline, PsycInfo, Embase, and ProQuest were systematically searched. Studies were included if the study measured traits of ADHD or autism, and symptoms of ED, and required participants to complete a performance task measure of inhibitory control. Where studies included a cohort with both an ND and ED, these results had to be reported separately from cohorts with a singular diagnosis. Studies were required to be published in English, within the last 10 years. Results No studies explored the relationship between autism and EDs using behavioural measures of inhibitory control. Four studies exploring the relationship between ADHD and EDs using behavioural measures of inhibitory control met selection criteria. These studies showed a multifaceted relationship between these conditions, with differences emerging between domains of inhibitory control. ADHD symptoms predicted poorer performance on measures of response inhibition in a non-clinical sample; this was not replicated in clinical samples, nor was there a significant association with EDs. Both ADHD and ED symptoms are associated with poor performance on attentional control measures; where these diagnoses were combined, performance was worse than for those with a singular diagnosis of ADHD. This was not replicated when compared to those with only ED diagnoses. Conclusion Impairments in attentional control may represent a unique vulnerability for the development of an ED and contribute to poor treatment outcomes. Further research is needed to explore the role of inhibitory control in EDs, ADHD and autism, including the use of both self-report and behavioural measures to capture the domains of inhibitory control.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista tiene dificultades con la comida, conviene comentarlo pronto con un profesional que conozca la neurodivergencia, y tener presente que la atención y el autocontrol pueden influir en cómo se vive la alimentación. Es una revisión de alcance de estudios publicados en los últimos 10 años. Ningún estudio analizó la relación entre autismo y trastornos alimentarios con pruebas de control inhibitorio; solo cuatro estudios sobre TDAH cumplieron los criterios. Por eso no sabemos qué ocurre en el autismo, y los resultados no valen como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If an autistic person has difficulties with eating, it is worth raising it early with a professional who understands neurodivergence, and keeping in mind that attention and self-control may shape how eating is experienced. This is a scoping review of studies from the last 10 years. No study looked at autism and eating disorders using performance tasks of inhibitory control; only four studies on ADHD met the criteria. So we do not know what happens in autism, and the findings are not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person har svårigheter med ätandet är det värt att ta upp det tidigt med en professionell som förstår neurodivergens, och komma ihåg att uppmärksamhet och självkontroll kan påverka hur ätandet upplevs. Det är en kartläggande översikt av studier från de senaste 10 åren. Ingen studie undersökte autism och ätstörningar med prestationsuppgifter för hämmande kontroll; bara fyra studier om ADHD uppfyllde kriterierna. Därför vet vi inte vad som gäller vid autism, och resultaten är ingen regel för varje person.

title: Sex differences in social brain neural responses in autism: temporal profiles of configural face-processing within data-driven time windows.
authors: Del Bianco T, Lai MC, Mason L, Johnson MH, Charman T, Loth E, Banaschewski T, Buitelaar J, Murphy DGM, Jones EJH, AIMS-2-TRIALS LEAP Team
abstract: Face-processing timing differences may underlie visual social attention differences between autistic and non-autistic people, and males and females. This study investigates the timing of the effects of neurotype and sex on face-processing, and their dependence on age. We analysed EEG data during upright and inverted photographs of faces from 492 participants from the Longitudinal European Autism Project (141 neurotypical males, 76 neurotypical females, 202 autistic males, 73 autistic females; age 6-30 years). We detected timings of sex/diagnosis effects on event-related potential amplitudes at the posterior-temporal channel P8 with Bootstrapped Cluster-based Permutation Analysis and conducted Growth Curve Analysis (GCA) to investigate the timecourse and dependence on age of neural signals. The periods of influence of neurotype and sex overlapped but differed in onset (respectively, 260 and 310 ms post-stimulus), with sex effects lasting longer. GCA revealed a smaller and later amplitude peak in autistic female children compared to non-autistic female children; this difference decreased in adolescence and was not significant in adulthood. No age-dependent neurotype difference was significant in males. These findings indicate that sex and neurotype influence longer latency face processing and implicates cognitive rather than perceptual processing. Sex may have more overarching effects than neurotype on configural face processing.

sheet.es: Este estudio no ofrece una pauta para mañana: sugiere que las diferencias en cómo el cerebro procesa las caras pueden variar con el sexo y la edad, así que conviene observar cómo mira y responde cada persona, sin comparar con una norma. Fue un estudio con registros de actividad cerebral (EEG) de 492 participantes de 6 a 30 años, autistas y no autistas, mientras veían fotos de caras. Sus límites: mide la respuesta cerebral en un laboratorio, no la vida diaria, y los resultados no valen para todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: This study offers no set routine for tomorrow: it suggests that how the brain processes faces may vary with sex and age, so it helps to notice how each person looks at and responds to faces, rather than comparing them with a norm. It was a research study recording brain activity (EEG) in 492 autistic and non-autistic participants aged 6-30 years while they viewed photos of faces. Its limits: it measures brain responses in a lab, not daily life, and the findings do not apply to every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Studien ger ingen färdig rutin för i morgon: den antyder att hjärnans bearbetning av ansikten kan skilja sig åt med kön och ålder, så det hjälper att lägga märke till hur varje person tittar på och reagerar på ansikten, utan att jämföra med en norm. Det var en forskningsstudie med mätning av hjärnaktivitet (EEG) hos 492 autistiska och icke-autistiska deltagare i åldern 6-30 år som tittade på bilder av ansikten. Begränsningar: den mäter hjärnsvar i labb, inte vardagen, och resultaten gäller inte alla autistiska personer.

title: What do parents of nonverbal and minimally verbal autistic children think about genomic autism research?
authors: Asbury K, Toseeb U, Barrow N
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract In Summer 2021, a genomic study of autism, Spectrum 10 K, was paused due to backlash from the autistic and autism communities. This raised important questions about how these communities perceive genomic research. The Personal Experiences of Autism and Perceptions of DNA-based research study was established to address this issue among a range of sub-groups within these communities. Twenty parents of nonverbal or minimally verbal autistic children took part in the current study. Data were provided in diverse formats including online interviews, telephone interviews, and writing. This approach was co-produced with autistic experts by experience and involved a parent of a minimally verbal autistic child. Data were analysed using reflexive Thematic Analysis. We found that participants were supportive of autism research, including some genomic research, as long as it is designed to support autistic people and is ethical and transparent. However, while some believed that polygenic scores, genomic predictors of the statistical probability of being autistic, would be helpful, others argued that this would only be true in an ideal world and that the world is too far from ideal. Participants felt excluded from the autistic and autism communities and that the dominant voices in those communities do not represent them or their children. We concluded that genomic researchers need to work with the autistic and autism communities to design future work, and that it is important to ensure a representative range of voices are heard.

sheet.es: Si le piden participar en investigación genómica, pregunte qué beneficiará a las personas autistas, cómo se protegen los datos y quién decide. Sus dudas son legítimas. En este estudio cualitativo, 20 madres y padres de niños autistas no verbales o con poco lenguaje oral compartieron sus opiniones mediante entrevistas o textos, con participación de personas autistas expertas por experiencia. Apoyaban la investigación ética y transparente, pero opinaban distinto sobre las puntuaciones poligénicas. Se sentían excluidos de las comunidades autistas dominantes. Es un grupo pequeño, habla la familia y no las propias personas autistas, y no representa a todas las familias.
sheet.en: If you are invited to join genomic research, ask how it will benefit autistic people, how data are protected and who makes decisions. Your doubts are legitimate. In this qualitative study, 20 parents of nonverbal or minimally verbal autistic children shared views through interviews or writing, with autistic experts by experience involved. They supported ethical, transparent research, but disagreed about polygenic scores. They also felt excluded from the dominant autistic and autism communities. The group was small, it reflects parents rather than autistic people themselves, and it cannot speak for every family.
sheet.sv: Om du blir tillfrågad om att delta i genomisk forskning, fråga hur den gynnar autistiska personer, hur data skyddas och vem som bestämmer. Dina tvivel är rimliga. I denna kvalitativa studie delade 20 föräldrar till icke-verbala eller minimalt verbala autistiska barn sina åsikter i intervjuer eller skriftligt, med autistiska experter genom erfarenhet involverade. De stödde etisk och transparent forskning, men var oeniga om polygena poäng. De kände sig också utanför de dominerande autistiska och autismrelaterade gemenskaperna. Gruppen var liten, speglar föräldrar snarare än autistiska personer själva och kan inte tala för alla familjer.

title: Experiences of interpersonal victimization and abuse among autistic people.
authors: Douglas S, Sedgewick F
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract What do we already know? Autistic people are more likely to have negative life experiences than non-autistic people, from bullying and ostracization, to being victims of crime, to unemployment and homelessness. This includes being victims of intimate partner violence, sexual assault and domestic abuse. Quantitative work has suggested that as many as 90% of autistic people experience these forms of abuse in some form during their lives, but there is little work asking them to talk about harmful relationships in their own words. What does this article add? This article reports on interviews with 24 autistic adults about their experiences of being victims of intimate partner violence, sexual assault and/or domestic abuse. Some of the themes which came from these interviews are shared with non-autistic victims, but others appeared unique to autistic people. One of these was evidence for unique autism-related vulnerabilities, as well as the impact the abuse had on their relationships long term. Participants also talked about how the sex and relationship education they had received had inadequately prepared them for adult relationships, and how this had contributed to their struggle to recognize and react to abusive behaviour. Implications for practice, research and policy Policies around intimate partner violence and sexual assault need to be updated to account for the different ways in which neurodivergent people (people whose brains process information differently from the majority) may discuss their experiences, rather than looking for 'standard narratives' as an indicator of a need for support. Relationship and sex education should be tailored for autistic young people to help them recognize abusive behaviours, and include how to respond to these safely. We recommend that future research tries to focus specifically on the abuse experiences of autistic men, non-binary and trans people, who have been under-represented in studies to date. In addition, much less is known about the abuse experiences of autistic people of colour or autistic people with intellectual disabilities, who also need to be actively included in these discussions.

sheet.es: Hable con la persona autista sobre relaciones sanas y señales de abuso de forma clara, concreta y sin juicios, y dígale que puede contar lo que vive con sus propias palabras y a su ritmo. Si cuenta algo preocupante, créale aunque no lo explique de forma habitual. Es un estudio de entrevistas con 24 adultos autistas que habían sufrido violencia de pareja, agresión sexual o abuso doméstico. Muchos dijeron que la educación sexual y afectiva recibida no los preparó para reconocer y responder al abuso. Sus límites: son pocas personas, y los hombres, las personas no binarias y trans, las personas racializadas y quienes tienen discapacidad intelectual están poco representados.
sheet.en: Talk with the autistic person about healthy relationships and signs of abuse in a clear, concrete, non-judgmental way, and let them know they can describe what happens in their own words and at their own pace. If they share something worrying, believe them even if it is not told in the usual way. This was an interview study with 24 autistic adults who had experienced intimate partner violence, sexual assault or domestic abuse. Many said the sex and relationship education they received did not prepare them to recognize and respond to abuse. Limits: it is a small group, and autistic men, non-binary and trans people, people of colour and people with intellectual disabilities are under-represented.
sheet.sv: Prata med den autistiska personen om sunda relationer och tecken på övergrepp på ett tydligt, konkret och icke-dömande sätt, och säg att hen kan berätta med egna ord och i sin egen takt. Om hen berättar något oroande, tro på hen även om det inte berättas på det vanliga sättet. Studien bestod av intervjuer med 24 autistiska vuxna som utsatts för våld i nära relation, sexuella övergrepp eller våld i hemmet. Många sa att sex- och samlevnadsundervisningen inte förberett dem på att känna igen och agera vid övergrepp. Begränsningar: det är en liten grupp, och autistiska män, icke-binära och transpersoner, färgade personer och personer med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning är underrepresenterade.

title: Barriers to healthcare and a 'triple empathy problem' may lead to adverse outcomes for autistic adults: A qualitative study.
authors: Shaw SC, Carravallah L, Johnson M, O'Sullivan J, Chown N, Neilson S, Doherty M
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic people live with more mental and physical health conditions and, on average, die younger than non-autistic people. Despite widespread commitments to tackling these issues, autistic people still report various barriers to accessing healthcare. This article aims to explore the area in depth, from the perspective of autistic people. This research benefits from being led by autistic people, for autistic people - all of the researchers are autistic, and most of us are also medical doctors. Data, in the form of written comments and stories, were collected as part of a large survey. Here, we explored these for common themes and possible deeper meaning within the experiences. People who took part reported a variety of barriers. Here, our article gives voice to their stories, in their own words. Themes included: early barriers; communication mismatch; doubt - in oneself and from doctors; helplessness and fear; and healthcare avoidance and adverse health outcomes. Our findings allowed us to create a model that aimed to understand and explain the reported barriers in the context of the previously known consequences. We also built on wider autism theories to explain our findings in more depth.

sheet.es: Si vas a acompañar a una persona autista a una consulta médica, prepara antes por escrito lo que quiere explicar y pide que el equipo sanitario lo lea con calma y le crea. Esto puede reducir el malentendido en la comunicación. La evidencia viene de un estudio cualitativo dirigido por investigadores autistas, que analizó comentarios escritos e historias de una encuesta amplia sobre barreras en la atención sanitaria. Sus límites: recoge experiencias concretas de quienes participaron, no mide qué ayuda funciona y no describe a todas las personas autistas. Cada persona decide qué apoyo necesita.
sheet.en: If you are going with an autistic person to a medical appointment, prepare in writing beforehand what they want to explain, and ask the healthcare team to read it calmly and take it seriously. This may reduce communication mismatch. The evidence comes from a qualitative study led by autistic researchers, who analysed written comments and stories from a large survey about barriers to healthcare. Its limits: it shares the experiences of those who took part, does not test which support works, and does not describe every autistic person. Each person decides what support they need.
sheet.sv: Om du följer med en autistisk person till ett läkarbesök, förbered gärna i förväg skriftligt vad personen vill ta upp, och be vårdpersonalen läsa det lugnt och ta det på allvar. Det kan minska missförstånd i kommunikationen. Underlaget är en kvalitativ studie ledd av autistiska forskare, som analyserade skrivna kommentarer och berättelser från en stor enkät om hinder i vården. Begränsningar: studien återger erfarenheter från dem som deltog, testar inte vilket stöd som fungerar och beskriver inte alla autistiska personer. Varje person avgör vilket stöd hen behöver.

title: School absenteeism in autistic children and adolescents: A scoping review.
authors: Nordin V, Palmgren M, Lindbladh A, Bölte S, Jonsson U
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic children and teenagers are, on average, absent from school more than their peers. The aim of this review was to provide an overview of the research on absence from school in autistic learners in primary and secondary school, to help guide future research. We sifted through 4632 reports and found 42 studies with a focus on school absence and autism. We looked at how, when, and where the studies were conducted. We also summarized the results and outlined how absence was measured in the studies. Absence from school may lead to problems later in life, like incomplete education and unemployment. It is therefore important to know how common this problem is among autistic learners, what the reasons may be, and what type of support they need. The studies were from high-income countries and were mainly published in the last 10 years. Studies based on school registers from the United States and the United Kingdom clearly showed that children and teenagers with autism had higher risk of school absence than those without autism. Absence was often linked to problems with mental health or additional neurodevelopmental conditions. Several studies also showed that absence in autistic children and adolescents was related to problems in school, like bullying or lack of knowledge about autism. Support programs were only evaluated in a few studies with a small number of study participants. We conclude that more research is needed to better understand why autistic learners are absent and what they need to thrive in school.

sheet.es: Si un niño o adolescente autista falta a la escuela, conviene mirar qué ocurre en el centro: acoso, falta de conocimiento sobre el autismo o salud mental, y hablarlo con la escuela para buscar apoyos. Se trata de una revisión de alcance que examinó 4632 informes y halló 42 estudios, todos de países de ingresos altos. Los registros escolares de Estados Unidos y Reino Unido mostraron mayor riesgo de ausencia en el alumnado autista. Límites: pocos estudios evaluaron programas de apoyo y con pocos participantes, y no explica por qué falta cada persona. Cada situación es distinta.
sheet.en: If an autistic child or teenager is missing school, it helps to look at what is happening at school, such as bullying, little understanding of autism, or mental health, and to talk with the school about support. This was a scoping review that sifted through 4632 reports and found 42 studies, all from high-income countries. School registers from the United States and the United Kingdom showed a higher risk of absence for autistic learners. Limits: only a few studies evaluated support programs, with small numbers of participants, and the review cannot explain why any one person is absent. Every situation is different.
sheet.sv: Om ett autistiskt barn eller en autistisk tonåring missar skolan hjälper det att se vad som händer i skolan, till exempel mobbning, bristande kunskap om autism eller psykisk hälsa, och att prata med skolan om stöd. Detta var en kartläggande översikt som gick igenom 4632 rapporter och hittade 42 studier, alla från höginkomstländer. Skolregister från USA och Storbritannien visade högre risk för frånvaro bland autistiska elever. Begränsningar: bara några få studier utvärderade stödprogram, med få deltagare, och översikten kan inte förklara varför en enskild person är frånvarande. Varje situation är olika.

title: Social motor synchrony in autism spectrum conditions: A systematic review.
authors: Glass D, Yuill N
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract When two people interact, they often fall into sync with one another by moving their bodies at the same time. Some say autistic people are not as good as non-autistic people at moving at the same time as a partner. This has led some researchers to ask whether measuring synchrony might help diagnose autism. We reviewed the research so far to look at differences in Social Motor Synchrony (SMS) (the way we move together) between autistic people and people they interact with. The research suggests that interactions involving an autistic partner (either two autistic partners, or an autistic and non-autistic partner) show lower synchrony than a non-autistic pair. However, we recognised elements in the research so far that may have affected SMS in interactions involving an autistic person. One way SMS may have been affected in research so far might be the way interactions have been set up in the research studies. Few papers studied interactions between two autistic people or looked at synchrony in comfortable environments with autistic-preferred tasks. The studies also do not explain why synchrony might be different, or weaker, in pairs involving autistic partners. We use these limitations to suggest improvements for future research.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o la persona autista con quien convives no se mueve "al compás" contigo (gestos, ritmo, postura), no es un fallo ni algo que corregir. Puedes buscar momentos cómodos y actividades que le gusten, donde la sincronía puede surgir de forma natural, y valorar otras formas de conexión. Esta revisión sistemática reunió estudios sobre la sincronía motora social en interacciones con personas autistas; las parejas con una persona autista mostraron menos sincronía que las parejas no autistas. Sus límites: pocos estudios observaron a dos personas autistas juntas o usaron entornos y tareas preferidos por personas autistas, y no explican por qué aparecen las diferencias.
sheet.en: If your child or the autistic person you live with doesn't move "in step" with you (gestures, rhythm, posture), it isn't a failure or something to fix. Try sharing comfortable moments and activities they enjoy, where moving together may happen naturally, and value other ways of connecting too. This systematic review gathered studies on social motor synchrony in interactions involving autistic people; pairs including an autistic partner showed less synchrony than non-autistic pairs. Its limits: few studies looked at two autistic people together or used comfortable settings and autistic-preferred tasks, and the research doesn't explain why the differences appear.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn eller den autistiska person du lever med inte rör sig "i takt" med dig (gester, rytm, hållning) är det inget misslyckande och inget som behöver rättas till. Försök dela lugna stunder och aktiviteter som personen tycker om, där samspelet kan uppstå naturligt, och värdesätt andra sätt att få kontakt. Denna systematiska översikt samlade studier om social motorisk synkronisering i samspel med autistiska personer; par med en autistisk person visade mindre synkronisering än icke-autistiska par. Begränsningar: få studier undersökte två autistiska personer tillsammans eller använde trygga miljöer och uppgifter som autistiska personer föredrar, och forskningen förklarar inte varför skillnaderna uppstår.

title: Aging Well and Autism: A Narrative Review and Recommendations for Future Research.
authors: Klein CB, Klinger LG
abstract: With autism first recognized in the 1940s, the early cohorts of autistic children are beginning to enter older adulthood. Little is known about the experiences and outcomes of autistic older adults. In the general population, "successful aging" is a dominant model among gerontologists and is used to evaluate outcomes in older adulthood. This narrative review aims to provide a framework for understanding and supporting successful aging in older autistic adults. Using Fernández-Ballesteros' four-domain model of "aging well" we review knowledge on aging and autism by examining outcomes in health and functioning, cognitive and physical functioning, positive affect and control, and social participation and engagement. Findings indicate that outcomes in autistic older adults are generally poor, marked by increased medical conditions, low adaptive skills, elevated risk of cognitive decline, limited physical activity, high rates of mental health conditions, low quality of life, and reduced social or community participation. Patterns of challenges are similar across cognitive abilities and profiles of autistic traits. Challenges and next steps in aging and autism research are identified, and future directions for the field are discussed.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista que está envejeciendo, vale la pena planificar con antelación: revisiones médicas regulares, atención a la salud mental, oportunidades de movimiento que disfrute y contactos sociales a su ritmo. Pregúntale qué significa para ella «envejecer bien» y adapta los apoyos a sus preferencias sensoriales y de comunicación. Esta revisión narrativa reunió estudios sobre adultos autistas mayores en salud, cognición, bienestar y participación social, y encontró más problemas médicos, mayor riesgo de deterioro cognitivo y menos participación comunitaria. Sus límites: hay pocos estudios en este grupo, no es una revisión sistemática y los resultados generales no describen a cada persona.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person who is getting older, it helps to plan ahead: regular health check-ups, attention to mental health, ways of moving they actually enjoy, and social contact at their own pace. Ask them what 'aging well' means to them, and shape support around their sensory and communication preferences. This narrative review gathered research on older autistic adults across health, thinking skills, wellbeing and social participation, finding more medical conditions, higher risk of cognitive decline and less community participation. Its limits: research on this group is still scarce, it is not a systematic review, and group-level findings do not describe every individual.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person som blir äldre är det klokt att planera i förväg: regelbundna hälsokontroller, uppmärksamhet på psykisk hälsa, rörelse som personen tycker om och social kontakt i egen takt. Fråga vad ”att åldras väl” betyder för just hen, och anpassa stödet efter sensoriska behov och kommunikationssätt. Denna narrativa översikt samlade forskning om äldre autistiska vuxna kring hälsa, kognition, välmående och delaktighet, och fann fler medicinska tillstånd, högre risk för kognitiv nedgång och mindre delaktighet i samhället. Begränsningar: forskningen om gruppen är fortfarande begränsad, översikten är inte systematisk och resultat på gruppnivå beskriver inte varje person.

title: Affirming Neurodiversity within Applied Behavior Analysis.
authors: Mathur SK, Renz E, Tarbox J
abstract: Criticisms of applied behavior analysis (ABA) from the autistic community continue to intensify and have an appreciable impact on research, practice, and conversation in stakeholder groups. ABA providers aspire to increase quality of life for autistic people; thus, it is imperative for providers to listen with humility and openness to the population we serve. Autistic individuals have unparalleled expertise in their own lives and their own communities. The concerns raised by the autistic community cannot, morally or ethically, be swept aside. There may be a misguided and harmful tendency to devalue concerns due to the speaker's identification as autistic or due to their difference in professional credentials. The concept of neurodiversity can help the ABA field respond to these concerns and collaborate with the largest stakeholders of our services, the autistic clients we serve. This article summarizes some of the key criticisms that autistic advocates raise concerning ABA, discusses the social model of disability and the neurodiversity paradigm, and proposes practical guidance to help the field of ABA integrate neurodiversity and thereby evolve our research and practice. By openly acknowledging the criticisms against ABA and recognizing how we can do better as a field, we believe we can take practical steps towards a profession and a society that more fully embraces inclusion.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija recibe apoyo conductual (ABA), puede preguntar con tranquilidad: ¿los objetivos mejoran su calidad de vida o solo lo hacen parecer menos autista? Pida que se respeten el stimming, la comunicación propia y el derecho a decir no, y que se escuche la opinión de la persona autista. Las críticas de adultos autistas merecen tomarse en serio. Este artículo es una revisión que resume críticas de defensores autistas, el modelo social de la discapacidad y la neurodiversidad, y propone pautas para profesionales. Sus límites: no es un estudio con datos nuevos ni prueba que estas pautas funcionen en la práctica para cada persona.
sheet.en: If your child receives behavioural support (ABA), you can calmly ask: do the goals improve their quality of life, or just make them seem less autistic? Ask that stimming, their own ways of communicating and their right to say no are respected, and that the autistic person's views are heard. Criticism from autistic adults deserves to be taken seriously. This article is a review summarising concerns raised by autistic advocates, the social model of disability and the neurodiversity paradigm, and offering guidance for practitioners. Its limits: it presents no new data and does not show that this guidance works in practice for every person.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn får beteendestöd (ABA) kan du lugnt fråga: förbättrar målen barnets livskvalitet, eller gör de bara att barnet verkar mindre autistiskt? Be om att stimming, barnets egna sätt att kommunicera och rätten att säga nej respekteras, och att den autistiska personens åsikter lyssnas på. Kritik från autistiska vuxna förtjänar att tas på allvar. Artikeln är en översikt som sammanfattar autistiska förespråkares kritik, den sociala modellen för funktionsnedsättning och neurodiversitetsperspektivet, och ger råd till yrkesverksamma. Begränsningar: den bygger inte på nya data och visar inte att råden fungerar i praktiken för varje person.

title: Study Protocol: Pegasus: psychotherapy incorporating horses for 'therapy-resistant' adolescents with autism spectrum disorders, a study with series of randomised, baseline controlled n-of-1 trials.
authors: den Boer JC, Klip H, Blonk A, Lenselink M, Kaijdoe SPT, Tielkes M, van Zandbeek A, Bres G, Herinx M, Staal WG, Rommelse N
abstract: Background For people with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), daily life can be highly stressful with many unpredictable events that can evoke emotion dysregulation (ED): a strong difficulty with appropriately negative affect regulation. For some of the patients with ASD, treatment as usual does not prove to be effective for ED. They may be at risk of life-long impairment, development of other disorders and loss of motivation for most regular forms of therapy. A highly promising method that may prove effective for therapy-resistant individuals with ASD is Psychotherapy incorporating horses (PIH). PIH uses the interactions of the horse and the patients on the ground and does not include horseriding. While often met with prejudgment and scepticism, reports from parents and therapists as well as a recent systematic review suggest that PIH may have beneficial effects on youths with ASD. Therefore, we examine clinical outcomes both in the short and in the long terms of PIH offered to adolescents with ASD and severe ED despite regular therapy. Methods A total of 35 adolescents aged 11-18 years with ASD will receive PIH during 15 sessions once a week with randomization to five different groups differentiating in baseline phase from 2 to 6 weeks. PIH uses horses to promote social awareness and self-awareness as well as relationship management and self-management. The primary outcome is the response to treatment on the Emotion Dysregulation Index (EDI). The secondary outcome measures include ASD symptom severity, quality of life, self-esteem, global and family functioning, and goal attainment. Assessments take place at the baseline (T0), at the end of baseline phase A (T1), after completion of intervention phase B (T2), after the end of post-measurement phase C (T3) and after one year (T4). Qualitative interviews of participants, parents and therapists will be held to reveal facilitators and barriers of PIH and a cost-effectiveness study will be performed. Discussion This study aims at contributing to clinical practice for adolescents with ASD and persistent emotion regulation problems despite 1.5 year of treatment by offering Psychotherapy incorporating horses in a study with series of randomised, baseline controlled n-of-1 trials. Trial registration www. Clinicaltrials gov NCT05200351, December 10th 2021.

sheet.es: Si un adolescente autista tiene mucha dificultad para regular sus emociones aunque lleve tiempo en terapia, quizá valga la pena preguntar a su equipo clínico por opciones nuevas, y observar qué le ayuda a calmarse. Este artículo es solo el protocolo de un ensayo: describe cómo se estudiará la psicoterapia con caballos, con trabajo desde el suelo y sin montar, en 35 adolescentes de 11-18 años, con 15 sesiones semanales. Todavía no hay resultados, así que no sabemos si funciona. Tampoco se puede suponer que sirva para cada persona.
sheet.en: If an autistic teenager has great difficulty regulating emotions despite long-running therapy, it may be worth asking their clinical team about other options, and noting what helps them calm. This paper is only a trial protocol: it describes how psychotherapy incorporating horses, done on the ground without riding, will be studied in 35 adolescents aged 11-18, with 15 weekly sessions. There are no results yet, so we do not know whether it works. It also cannot be assumed to suit every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk tonåring har stora svårigheter att reglera känslor trots lång tids terapi kan det vara värt att fråga vårdteamet om andra alternativ, och att notera vad som hjälper hen att varva ner. Artikeln är bara ett studieprotokoll: den beskriver hur psykoterapi med hästar, arbete från marken utan ridning, ska studeras hos 35 ungdomar i åldern 11-18 med 15 veckovisa sessioner. Resultat saknas ännu, så vi vet inte om det fungerar. Det går heller inte att anta att det passar alla.

title: Unraveling the Spectrum: A Comprehensive Review of Autism Spectrum Disorder in India.
authors: Uke P, Gaikwad S, Vagha K, Wandile S
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a complex neurodevelopmental condition characterized by deficits in social interaction, communication difficulties, and repetitive behaviors that profoundly impact the lives of affected individuals and their families. This article provides a comprehensive overview of ASD, focusing on screening, diagnosis, and intervention strategies. Early signs of ASD can manifest in infancy, but parents may not recognize them until their child falls behind in meeting social milestones. This delay in recognition is often due to a lack of awareness, societal stigma, and limited knowledge about developmental and behavioral disorders. Globally, ASD prevalence is increasing potentially due to broader diagnostic criteria, increased awareness, and improved screening practices. Screening for ASD is crucial for early identification and intervention. Various tools are available such as the Modified Checklist for Autism in Toddlers (M-CHATs), Trivandrum Autism Behavioral Checklist (TABC), and the Social Communication Questionnaire (SCQ). Diagnosing ASD involves using established criteria such as the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition (DSM-5), and specific diagnostic tools like the Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule (ADOS) and the Indian Scale for the Assessment of Autism (ISAA). Interventions for ASD should be multidisciplinary, involving professionals such as developmental pediatricians, psychologists, psychiatrists, special educators, occupational therapists, physiotherapists, speech therapists, and social workers. Applied behavior analysis (ABA), naturalistic developmental behavioral interventions (NDBIs), and parent-mediated treatment are among the evidence-based approaches. Additionally, speech-language therapy, motor therapy, and sensory integration therapy play vital roles in addressing the diverse needs of individuals with ASD. Medical interventions should be used alongside behavioral and environmental strategies. Early screening, accurate diagnosis, and tailored interventions are essential for improving the lives of individuals with ASD. A multidisciplinary approach and increased awareness are crucial in addressing the growing prevalence of ASD worldwide.

sheet.es: Si le preocupa cómo se comunica o juega su hijo o hija, puede pedir una valoración a su pediatra sin esperar a que se noten retrasos mayores. Esta revisión sobre el autismo en la India describe herramientas de cribado y diagnóstico, y propone que el apoyo lo den varios profesionales, con la familia como parte activa del equipo. Es una revisión narrativa que reúne información existente, no un estudio con participantes propios. Sus límites: se centra en el contexto indio, usa un lenguaje de déficits y no demuestra qué apoyo sirve a cada persona. Las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If you wonder about how your child communicates or plays, you can ask a paediatrician for an assessment without waiting for bigger delays to show. This review of autism in India describes screening and diagnostic tools and suggests support from several professionals, with the family as an active part of the team. It is a review that gathers existing information, not a study with its own participants. Its limits: it focuses on the Indian context, uses deficit-based language, and cannot show which support suits each person. Medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om du undrar över hur ditt barn kommunicerar eller leker kan du be barnläkaren om en bedömning, utan att vänta tills större skillnader syns. Den här översikten om autism i Indien beskriver verktyg för screening och diagnos och föreslår stöd från flera yrkesgrupper, där familjen är en aktiv del av teamet. Det är en översikt som samlar befintlig kunskap, inte en studie med egna deltagare. Begränsningar: den fokuserar på indisk kontext, använder ett språk om brister och visar inte vilket stöd som passar varje person. Medicinska beslut hör till en läkare.

title: Effect of fractional exhaled nitric oxide (F ENO )-based asthma management during pregnancy versus usual care on infant development, temperament, sensory function and autism signs.
authors: Whalen OM, Campbell LE, Lane AE, Karayanidis F, Mallise CA, Woolard AJ, Holliday EG, Mattes J, Collison A, Gibson PG, Murphy VE
abstract: Asthma during pregnancy is associated with a range of adverse perinatal outcomes. It is also linked to increased rates of neurodevelopmental conditions in the offspring. We aimed to assess whether fractional exhaled nitric oxide (F ENO )-based asthma management during pregnancy improves child developmental and behavioural outcomes compared to usual care. The Breathing for Life Trial was a randomised controlled trial that compared F ENO -based asthma management during pregnancy to usual care. Participants were invited to the developmental follow-up, the Breathing for Life Trial - Infant Development study, which followed up infants at 6 weeks, 6 months and 12 months. The primary outcomes were measured in infants at 12 months using the Bayley-III: Cognitive, Language and Motor composite scores. Secondary outcomes included Bayley-III social-emotional and adaptive behaviour scores, autism likelihood and sensory and temperament outcomes. The exposure of interest was the randomised intervention group. Two hundred and twenty-two infants and their 217 participating mothers were recruited to the follow-up; 107 mothers were in the intervention group and 113 were in the control group. There was no evidence of an intervention effect for the primary outcomes: Bayley-III cognitive (mean = 108.9 control, 108.5 intervention, p = 0.93), language (mean = 95.9 control, 95.6 intervention, p = 0.87) and motor composite scores (mean = 97.2 control, 97.9 intervention, p = 0.25). Mean scores for secondary outcomes were also similar among infants born to control and F ENO group mothers, with few results reaching p Conclusion In this sample, F ENO -guided asthma treatment during pregnancy did not improve infant developmental outcomes in the first year of life. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: ACTRN12613000202763. What is known • Maternal asthma during pregnancy has been associated with increased rates of neurodevelopmental conditions in offspring, including intellectual disability and autism. What is new • This is the first study to examine how managing asthma during pregnancy via a F ENO -guided algorithm or usual care affects infant developmental and behavioural outcomes. While the results of the study showed no impact of the intervention, and therefore do not support the integration of F ENO -based management of asthma in antenatal settings for optimal infant development, they do send a positive message about the implications of active asthma management during pregnancy on infant developmental outcomes.

title: Early treatment for children with mental health problems and genetic conditions through a parenting intervention (The GAP): study protocol for a pragmatic randomized controlled trial.
authors: Serrano M, Elias M, Llorens M, Bolasell M, Vall-Roqué H, Villalta L
abstract: Background Children with genetic conditions are at increased risk for mental health and neurodevelopmental problems, often accompanied by significant parental distress. Genetic and family factors can impact children and parents' mental health. Early parenting interventions, like the Incredible Years® programs, have demonstrated to improve parental distress and children's mental health. The recent version for young children with language delays or autism spectrum disorder (IY-ASLD®) has shown to be feasible and effective to support parents in their children's developmental trajectories. The effectiveness of treatments for children with genetic conditions and neurodevelopmental problems is largely unexplored, leaving significant gaps in evidence-based options. Clinicians lack guidance, especially when patients exhibit language or social communication impairments but do not meet diagnostic criteria for a full-blown autism spectrum disorder (ASD). We aim to fill this gap, providing evidence on the feasibility and effectiveness of the IY-ASLD® intervention for such patients. Methods We designed a prospective multicenter pragmatic randomized controlled trial including approximately 68 children aged 3 to 7 years, recruited from three tertiary care reference hospitals. Inclusion criteria will necessitate genetic confirmation of a neurodevelopmental disorder along with language, communication, or socialization difficulties. Individuals with an ASD diagnosis will be excluded. All subjects are included in a territorial register for rare conditions (ReMin, Registre de Malalties Minoritàries de Catalunya). Families will randomly be assigned to the intervention or the control group. The intervention will be held online by clinical psychologists and child and adolescent psychiatrists. Discussion Our group has recently piloted the online implementation of the IY-ASLD® intervention for the first time in Spain, for parents of children with language delays, socialization difficulties, or ASD, but not genetically determined. Our multicenter research consortium is well-positioned to recruit patients with rare conditions and implement efficient treatment pathways within the National Health System. Given the geographical dispersion of families affected by rare conditions, the online format offers logistical advantages and improved therapy access, enhancing homogeneity across all patients. The results of this study will inform clinicians and policymakers about evidence-based treatment options for this vulnerable and overlooked group of young children. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06125093 . Date of registration: first submitted 2023-10-23; first posted 2023-11-09. URL of trial registry record.

sheet.es: Si su hijo tiene una condición genética y dificultades de lenguaje o comunicación social, pregunte a su equipo clínico por programas de apoyo a madres y padres, incluidos los que se ofrecen en línea. Esto es un protocolo de un ensayo aleatorizado: describe un estudio planificado, con unos 68 niños de 3 a 7 años con condición genética confirmada y sin diagnóstico de autismo, que aún no ofrece resultados. Por eso no sabemos todavía si el programa Incredible Years ayuda a estas familias, ni sirve como regla para todos. Cada familia necesita decidir con su equipo qué apoyo encaja con su situación.
sheet.en: If your child has a genetic condition and differences in language or social communication, ask your clinical team about support programmes for parents, including ones offered online. This is a trial protocol: it describes a planned randomized study of about 68 children aged 3 to 7 with a confirmed genetic condition and no autism diagnosis. It has no results yet. So we do not know whether the Incredible Years programme helps these families, and it is not a rule for everyone. Each family can decide with their team which support fits their situation.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn har ett genetiskt tillstånd och skillnader i språk eller social kommunikation kan du fråga vårdteamet om stöd till föräldrar, även sådant som ges online. Detta är ett studieprotokoll: det beskriver en planerad randomiserad studie med cirka 68 barn i åldern 3 till 7 år med bekräftat genetiskt tillstånd och utan autismdiagnos. Några resultat finns ännu inte. Vi vet därför inte om programmet Incredible Years hjälper dessa familjer, och det är ingen regel för alla. Varje familj kan tillsammans med sitt team avgöra vilket stöd som passar.

title: Cognitive and brain morphological deviations in middle-to-old aged autistic adults: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Wang J, Christensen D, Coombes SA, Wang Z
abstract: Cognitive challenges and brain structure variations are common in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) but are rarely explored in middle-to-old aged autistic adults. Cognitive deficits that overlap between young autistic individuals and elderlies with dementia raise an important question: does compromised cognitive ability and brain structure during early development drive autistic adults to be more vulnerable to pathological aging conditions, or does it protect them from further decline? To answer this question, we have synthesized current theoretical models of aging in ASD and conducted a systematic literature review (Jan 1, 1980 - Feb 29, 2024) and meta-analysis to summarize empirical studies on cognitive and brain deviations in middle-to-old aged autistic adults. We explored findings that support different aging theories in ASD and addressed study limitations and future directions. This review sheds light on the poorly understood consequences of aging question raised by the autism community to pave the way for future studies to identify sensitive and reliable measures that best predict the onset, progression, and prognosis of pathological aging in ASD.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista de mediana edad o mayor, vale la pena observar con calma cualquier cambio en memoria o pensamiento y comentarlo con su médico o médica, sin dar por hecho que sea normal ni que sea grave. Se trata de una revisión sistemática con metaanálisis de estudios con personas autistas adultas de mediana edad o mayores, publicados entre el 1 de enero de 1980 y el 29 de febrero de 2024. Según el resumen, el envejecimiento autista se entiende todavía poco y aún faltan medidas fiables para anticipar su evolución. No sirve como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person in middle or older age, it is worth calmly noticing any change in memory or thinking and mentioning it to their doctor, without assuming it is either normal or serious. This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies with middle-to-old aged autistic adults, published between Jan 1, 1980 and Feb 29, 2024. According to the abstract, aging in autism is still poorly understood, and sensitive, reliable measures to predict its course are still needed. It is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person i medelåldern eller äldre är det värt att lugnt uppmärksamma förändringar i minne eller tänkande och ta upp dem med personens läkare, utan att anta att de är normala eller allvarliga. Det här är en systematisk översikt med metaanalys av studier med autistiska vuxna i medelåldern eller äldre, publicerade mellan 1 januari 1980 och 29 februari 2024. Enligt sammanfattningen är åldrande vid autism fortfarande dåligt förstått, och det saknas ännu tillförlitliga mått för att förutsäga förloppet. Den gäller inte som regel för varje person.

title: Mental Health Professionals' Experiences of Adapting Mental Health Interventions for Autistic Adults: A Systematic Review and Thematic Synthesis.
authors: Moore L, Larkin F, Foley S
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Autistic adults experience high rates of metal health difficulties and face significant barriers to accessing appropriate mental health care. Empirical research and recent professional guidelines emphasise the importance of modifying standard mental health interventions to best meet the needs of autistic adults. This systematic review explored mental health professionals' experiences of adapting mental health interventions for autistic adults. A systematic search was conducted on CINAHL, PsychINFO, PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science in July 2022. The findings from 13 identified studies were synthesised using thematic synthesis. Three major analytical themes were generated, the unique experience of adapting interventions for autistic clients, factors which facilitate successful adaptations, and challenges to adapting interventions. Each theme contained a number of subsequent sub-themes. Professionals view the process of adapting interventions to be a highly individualised process. A range of personal traits, professional experiences, and systemic, service-based issues were identified in facilitating or challenging this individualised process.
