Further research regarding adaptations with different intervention models and increased supportive resources are required to enable professionals to successfully adapt interventions for autistic adult clients.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta va a empezar terapia psicológica, es razonable pedir al profesional que adapte la intervención: por ejemplo, lenguaje concreto, apoyos visuales, ritmo más pausado, ajustes sensoriales en la consulta o integrar sus intereses. Puede ayudar llevar una lista breve de lo que funciona y lo que no. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 13 estudios sobre experiencias de profesionales de salud mental que adaptan terapias para adultos autistas; describen la adaptación como algo muy individual, facilitado por la experiencia y la formación, y dificultado por limitaciones de los servicios. Su límite: refleja la visión de los profesionales, no la de las personas autistas, y no mide si las adaptaciones mejoran los resultados.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult is starting mental health therapy, it is reasonable to ask the professional to adapt it: for example, concrete language, visual supports, a slower pace, sensory adjustments in the room, or building on the person's interests. Bringing a short list of what helps and what does not can make this easier. This systematic review combined 13 studies on mental health professionals' experiences of adapting therapy for autistic adults; they described adaptation as highly individual, helped by experience and training, and held back by service limitations. Its limit: it reflects professionals' views, not autistic people's own, and it does not measure whether adaptations improve outcomes.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen ska börja psykologisk behandling är det rimligt att be behandlaren anpassa den: till exempel konkret språk, visuellt stöd, lugnare tempo, sensoriska justeringar i rummet eller att utgå från personens intressen. Det kan hjälpa att ta med en kort lista över vad som fungerar och inte. Denna systematiska översikt sammanställde 13 studier om hur yrkesverksamma inom psykiatri upplever att anpassa behandling för autistiska vuxna; de beskrev anpassning som mycket individuell, underlättad av erfarenhet och utbildning och försvårad av begränsningar i verksamheten. Begränsning: den speglar behandlarnas perspektiv, inte autistiska personers egna, och mäter inte om anpassningarna ger bättre resultat.

title: "My Autism is Linked with Everything": at the Crossroads of Autism and Diabetes.
authors: Vinayagam R, Tanner C, Harley D, Karatela S, Brooker K
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Autistic adults experience stark health disparities and difficulties accessing health care. Their realities of managing complex health conditions are unknown. Our research explored the experience of Autistic adults self-managing diabetes. Interviews with Autistic adults with diabetes and their support people were thematically analysed to identify three key themes. The Autistic experience influenced diabetes self-management, including autism-unique challenges and strengths. Participants prioritised avoiding Autistic burnout over diabetes self-management; mitigating the psychosocial pressures of neurotypical systems took precedence. Health professionals often separated autism and diabetes subsequently overlooking key factors impacting diabetes self-management. To better meet the needs of Autistic adults, diabetes care and health management more broadly should be considered within the context of autism, including supports for self-management during Autistic burnout.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista con diabetes, conviene hablar de cómo el autismo influye en su día a día con la diabetes, y no tratar ambas cosas por separado. Pregunta qué le resulta difícil, qué se le da bien y qué apoyo necesita, sobre todo en épocas de agotamiento autista (burnout). Es un estudio con entrevistas a personas autistas adultas con diabetes y a sus personas de apoyo, analizadas por temas. Sus límites: el resumen no indica cuántas personas participaron, y las experiencias de cada persona pueden ser muy distintas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person with diabetes, it helps to talk about how autism shapes their daily diabetes management, rather than treating the two separately. Ask what is hard, what goes well and what support they need, especially during Autistic burnout. This was an interview study with autistic adults with diabetes and their support people, analysed by themes. Its limits: the abstract does not say how many people took part, and each person's experience can be very different.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person med diabetes hjälper det att prata om hur autismen påverkar vardagen med diabetes, i stället för att se dem som två skilda saker. Fråga vad som är svårt, vad som fungerar och vilket stöd som behövs, särskilt vid autistisk utbrändhet (burnout). Detta var en intervjustudie med autistiska vuxna med diabetes och deras stödpersoner, analyserad i teman. Begränsningar: sammanfattningen anger inte hur många som deltog, och varje persons upplevelse kan skilja sig mycket.

title: Autism in Taiwan and Thailand: Influences of Culture.
authors: Westby C, Chen KM, Cheng L, Jithavech P, Maroonroge S
abstract: The prevalence of autism is increasing worldwide. The majority of autism research and development of autism assessments and interventions has been conducted in Western cultures. The prevalence of autism is reportedly lower in Asian versus Western cultures, but this is likely due to lack of personnel and uniform criteria for diagnosing autism. This article describes how two Asian cultures, Taiwan and Thailand, are dealing with the increasing identification of autistic children. National universal healthcare in both Taiwan and Thailand provides a mechanism for assessment and diagnosis of young children, but a lack of a sufficient number of trained professionals limits the availability of intervention services. A focus of research in these cultures has been on parents' experiences and coping with the stigma and stress of having an autistic child. Cultural values associated with Confucianism and Buddhism influence attitudes toward persons with disability and how parents of autistic children experience and cope with stigma and stress. Both areas have national laws that provide a range of educational opportunities for autistic children, including inclusion into general education classrooms. Special education and general education teachers, however, have little specific training in autism. Speech and language services are rarely offered in public school programs. Available speech and language services are limited to consultation with teachers a few times a year. In general, parents of autistic children are supportive of inclusion programs, but teachers and parents of both autistic and typically developing children express concerns about the ability to implement such programs in ways that are beneficial to all children.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una niña o un niño autista, conviene saber que la cultura y los valores familiares influyen en cómo se vive el estigma y el estrés, y que buscar apoyo de otras familias puede ayudar. Pide a la escuela un plan concreto de apoyos. Esta es una revisión sobre Taiwán y Tailandia, centrada en sistemas de salud, educación y experiencias de madres y padres. Sus límites: describe dos contextos concretos, no mide qué apoyo funciona mejor y no sirve como regla para todas las familias ni para otros países.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic child, it helps to know that culture and family values shape how stigma and stress are experienced, and that finding support from other families can help. Ask the school for a concrete plan of supports. This is a review about Taiwan and Thailand, covering health systems, education and parents' experiences. Its limits: it describes two specific settings, does not measure which support works best, and is not a rule for every family or for other countries.
sheet.sv: Om du ger omsorg till ett autistiskt barn kan det vara bra att veta att kultur och familjens värderingar påverkar hur stigma och stress upplevs, och att stöd från andra familjer kan hjälpa. Be skolan om en konkret plan för stöd. Detta är en översikt om Taiwan och Thailand som beskriver hälso- och sjukvård, utbildning och föräldrars erfarenheter. Begränsningar: den beskriver två specifika miljöer, mäter inte vilket stöd som fungerar bäst och är ingen regel för alla familjer eller för andra länder.

title: Experiences of caregivers of children with autism during the COVID-19 pandemic: A scoping review.
authors: Berson J, Adams SN
journal: The South African journal of communication disorders = Die Suid-Afrikaanse tydskrif vir Kommunikasieafwykings
abstract: Background The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) outbreak has had a profoundly negative impact on people all over the world, particularly those with disabilities such as autism. However, there are gaps in research understanding the impact of COVID-19 on this population and the support required. Aim To explore the evidence available on the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on caregivers of children with autism. Method A scoping review methodology using the Arksey and O'Malley framework was employed. Five electronic databases from March 2020 to December 2022 were reviewed. Two thousand two hundred and six articles were retrieved with primary search terms: caregivers (population), autism (diagnosis) and COVID-19 (context). Following the screening of titles, abstracts and articles, 36 articles were included in the final review. Thematic and content qualitative analysis was completed. Results Preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses extension for scoping reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guided the reporting of the findings. Three main themes were identified: (1) caregiver's mental health and wellbeing, (2) response to remote health care and support and (3) caregiver resilience. Conclusion The pandemic affected children with autism and their families regarding changes in routine, difficulties with support and emotional states. However, little research has been conducted on the impact in upper-middle-income countries such as South Africa.Contribution: The findings from this review carry practical implications that extend beyond the pandemic, such as political instability or natural disasters that may present similar stressors for children with autism and their families.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista, tu bienestar emocional importa tanto como el suyo: buscar apoyo para ti, mantener rutinas claras cuando haya cambios y reconocer lo que ya te ha ayudado a salir adelante puede ser un buen punto de partida. La evidencia es una revisión de alcance de 36 artículos sobre cuidadores de niños autistas durante la pandemia de COVID-19; identificó tres temas: salud mental y bienestar, respuesta a la atención y el apoyo a distancia, y resiliencia. Sus límites: resume estudios muy distintos y hay poca investigación en países de ingresos medios-altos como Sudáfrica, así que no sirve como regla para cada familia.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic person, your own emotional wellbeing matters as much as theirs. Seeking support for yourself, keeping routines clear when things change, and noticing what has already helped you cope can be a good starting point. The evidence is a scoping review of 36 articles about caregivers of autistic children during the COVID-19 pandemic. It identified three themes: mental health and wellbeing, response to remote health care and support, and caregiver resilience. Its limits: it brings together very different studies, and little research exists in upper-middle-income countries such as South Africa, so it is not a rule for every family.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person är ditt eget mående lika viktigt som hens. Att söka stöd för egen del, hålla rutiner tydliga när saker förändras och uppmärksamma vad som redan har hjälpt dig att klara dig kan vara en bra start. Underlaget är en kartläggande översikt av 36 artiklar om vårdnadshavare till autistiska barn under covid-19-pandemin. Den fann tre teman: psykisk hälsa och välbefinnande, hur man upplevde stöd och vård på distans, samt vårdnadshavares motståndskraft. Begränsningar: den sammanfattar mycket olika studier, och det finns lite forskning från övre medelinkomstländer som Sydafrika, så den är ingen regel för varje familj.

title: Diagnosis of common health conditions among autistic adults in the UK: evidence from a matched cohort study.
authors: O'Nions E, Brown J, Buckman JEJ, Charlton R, Cooper C, El Baou C, Happé F, Hoare S, Lewer D, Manthorpe J, McKechnie DGJ, Richards M, Saunders R, Mandy W, Stott J
abstract: Background Autistic people are disproportionately likely to experience premature mortality and most mental and physical health conditions. We measured the incidence of diagnosed conditions accounting for the most disability-adjusted life years in the UK population according to the Global Burden of Disease study (anxiety, depression, self-harm, harmful alcohol use, substance use, migraine, neck or back pain, and gynaecological conditions). Methods Participants were aged 18 years or above and had an autism diagnosis recorded in the IQVIA Medical Research Database between 01/01/2000 and 16/01/2019. We included 15,675 autistic adults without intellectual disability, 6437 autistic adults with intellectual disability, and a comparison group matched (1:10) by age, sex, and primary care practice. We estimated crude incidences and incidence rate ratios (IRRs) adjusted for age and sex. Findings Autistic adults without intellectual disability experienced a higher incidence (IRR, 95% CI) of self-harm (2.07, 1.79-2.40), anxiety (1.91, 1.76-2.06), depressive disorders (1.79, 1.67-1.92), and substance use (1.24, 1.02-1.51) relative to comparison participants. Incidences of harmful alcohol use (1.01, 0.85-1.18), migraine (0.99, 0.84-1.17), and gynaecological conditions (1.19, 0.95-1.49) did not differ. Neck or back pain incidence was lower (0.88, 0.82-0.95). Autistic adults with intellectual disability experienced a higher incidence of self-harm (2.08, 1.69-2.56). Incidences of anxiety (1.14, 1.00-1.30), gynaecological conditions (1.22, 0.93-1.62), and substance use (1.08, 0.80-1.47) did not differ, and lower incidences were found for depressive disorders (0.73, 0.64-0.83), harmful alcohol use (0.65, 0.50-0.84), migraine (0.55, 0.42-0.74), and neck or back pain (0.49, 0.44-0.55). Interpretation Although our findings cannot be directly compared to previous prevalence studies, they contrast with the higher frequency of mental and physical health conditions in autistic adults reported in studies that directly assessed and/or surveyed autistic people about co-occurring conditions. The present findings may suggest under-diagnosis of common conditions in autistic people, particularly those with intellectual disability. Improved detection should be a clinical and policy priority to reduce health inequalities. Funding Dunhill Medical Trust, Economic and Social Research Council, National Institute of Health and Care Research.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista adulta, conviene vigilar con calma cómo está su ánimo, su ansiedad y su dolor, y preguntarle de forma directa, porque algunas condiciones pueden pasar sin diagnosticar. Anota lo que observes y llévalo a su médico. Es un estudio de cohortes con historiales médicos del Reino Unido: 15,675 personas autistas adultas sin discapacidad intelectual y 6437 con discapacidad intelectual, comparadas con otras personas. Las autolesiones se diagnosticaron más en ambos grupos (2.07 y 2.08). Pero no mide lo que cada persona vive y no sirve como regla para todas. Si hay autolesiones o pensamientos suicidas, acude a un profesional sanitario o a un servicio de crisis; ante un peligro inmediato, llama al número de emergencias de tu país.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult, it helps to calmly check in on their mood, anxiety and pain, asking directly, because some conditions may go undiagnosed. Note what you see and share it with their doctor. This was a cohort study using UK medical records: 15,675 autistic adults without intellectual disability and 6437 with intellectual disability, compared with matched people. Diagnosed self-harm was higher in both groups (2.07 and 2.08). But records do not capture what each person lives with, and the findings are not a rule for everyone. If there is self-harm or thoughts of suicide, contact a clinician, a health service or a crisis service; in immediate danger, call your country's emergency number.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen kan det hjälpa att lugnt fråga hur personen mår i humör, ångest och smärta, eftersom vissa tillstånd kan förbli odiagnostiserade. Anteckna det du ser och ta med det till läkaren. Detta var en kohortstudie med brittiska journaldata: 15,675 autistiska vuxna utan intellektuell funktionsnedsättning och 6437 med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning, jämförda med matchade personer. Diagnostiserad självskada var vanligare i båda grupperna (2.07 och 2.08). Journaler visar dock inte vad varje person upplever, och resultaten gäller inte alla. Vid självskada eller tankar på självmord, kontakta en läkare, vården eller en krisjour; vid akut fara, ring ditt lands nödnummer.

title: Barriers and facilitators to ethical co-production with Autistic people with an eating disorder.
authors: Nimbley E, Maloney E, Buchan K, Sader M, Gillespie-Smith K, Duffy F
abstract: Background Co-production is the collaboration between researchers and the lived experience community in designing, conducting and sharing research. The importance of co-production is increasingly advocated in both the autism and eating disorder fields. Despite this, there remains a lack of clarity at how to define, apply and conduct ethical co-production. Understanding common challenges and what we can do to overcome these challenges are integral to ensuring ethical and meaningful research with Autistic people with an eating disorder. The current study therefore explored: What are the barriers and facilitators to ethical co-production with Autistic people with an ED? Methods Five workshops were conducted with 30 collaborators exploring barriers and facilitators to ethical co-production. Synchronous (online workshops) and asynchronous (offline discussion forum) data was analysed using thematic analysis. Themes were co-produced by a neurotypical and Autistic researcher with lived/living experience of an eating disorder. Results Four themes were identified that explored barriers to ethical co-production: unequal partnerships, the inaccessibility of research, excluded by diagnoses and communication differences. Three themes were identified with regards to facilitators of ethical co-production: shared power (with sub-themes relationships, not roles and creative compensation), clarity and transparency and autism-affirming approaches. Discussion Conducting ethical co-production with Autistic people with eating disorders has the potential to generate meaningful research that can be translated into improving the lives of the Autistic and eating disorder community. To achieve this, co-production teams should strive towards shared power and long-term relationships, adapting for communication differences and preferences and operating firmly within an autism-affirming framework. It is hoped that study findings will inspire collaboration, discussion and novel, translatable research.

sheet.es: Si te invitan a participar en una investigación sobre autismo y trastornos alimentarios, o la apoyas, pregunta cómo se compartirá el poder, qué se adaptará en la comunicación y qué se pagará o reconocerá. Este estudio hizo 5 talleres con 30 colaboradores y analizó sus ideas. Señalaron como barreras las alianzas desiguales, la investigación poco accesible, la exclusión por diagnósticos y las diferencias de comunicación. Como apoyos destacaron compartir el poder, la claridad, la transparencia y los enfoques que afirman el autismo. Es un estudio cualitativo: refleja las voces de este grupo y no tiene por qué valer para todas las personas ni todos los proyectos.
sheet.en: If you are invited to take part in research on autism and eating disorders, or you support someone who is, ask how power will be shared, what will be adapted in communication, and how people will be paid or recognised. This study held 5 workshops with 30 collaborators and analysed their input. They named barriers such as unequal partnerships, inaccessible research, exclusion by diagnoses and communication differences. Helpful factors were shared power, clarity, transparency and autism-affirming approaches. It is a qualitative study, so it reflects the views of this group and may not apply to every person or every project.
sheet.sv: Om du blir inbjuden till forskning om autism och ätstörningar, eller stöttar någon som är det, fråga hur makten ska delas, vad som anpassas i kommunikationen och hur människor får ersättning eller erkännande. Studien höll 5 workshops med 30 medskapare och analyserade deras synpunkter. Hinder var ojämlika partnerskap, otillgänglig forskning, uteslutning på grund av diagnoser och kommunikationsskillnader. Det som hjälpte var delad makt, tydlighet, transparens och autismbekräftande arbetssätt. Det är en kvalitativ studie, så den speglar den här gruppens röster och gäller inte nödvändigtvis alla personer eller alla projekt.

title: Diversity in Autistic Play: Autistic Adults' Experiences.
authors: Pritchard-Rowe E, de Lemos C, Howard K, Gibson J
abstract: Background Play is important for mental health and well-being. Descriptions of autistic play have typically focused on "deficits" and are based on comparisons to neurotypical "norms". According to the neurodiversity paradigm, it is important that autistic voices are highlighted and that difficulties, differences, and strengths are explored. With this in mind, we designed the present study to focus on the experiences and perspectives of autistic people concerning the topic of autistic play. Methods We conducted a consultation with autistic stakeholders, as well as with parents and teachers of autistic individuals to help us design the study and interview questions. We used semi-structured interviews with 22 autistic adults aged 18-57 years (clinically confirmed diagnosis, n = 21; self-diagnosed, n = 1) who live in the United Kingdom. We analyzed the data using interpretative phenomenological analysis to identify themes. Results We found important commonalities and differences in the ways that socialization in play, imaginary play, and flow (a state involving intense focus on the play) are experienced. Autistic adults discussed the importance of both solitary play and social play, with solitary play having an important recuperative function. They also reported preferences for parallel play and playing with similar autistic people. They also discussed imaginary play experiences, including social role-play and grounded-in-reality play, and the dual nature of flow experiences during play. Conclusions The findings of this study contrast with deficit-focused understandings of autistic play and build on neurodiversity-informed studies. We highlight, for example, the importance of considering the different circumstances under which solitary play or social play are preferred, as well as the importance of taking an individual approach to play. We encourage wider understanding and acceptance of these play preferences and experiences to support autistic people's well-being.

sheet.es: Tome el juego como algo valioso en sus distintas formas: deje espacio para jugar solo, para jugar junto a otras personas sin interactuar mucho (juego paralelo) y para jugar con personas autistas similares. Pregunte a la persona qué prefiere en cada momento, porque el juego en solitario puede ayudarle a recuperarse. Evidencia: entrevistas a 22 adultos autistas de 18-57 años en el Reino Unido, analizadas por temas. Límites: es un grupo pequeño, de un solo país, y recuerda experiencias de adultos; no muestra que todas las personas autistas, ni niñas y niños, jueguen o prefieran lo mismo.
sheet.en: Treat play as valuable in all its forms: leave room for solo play, for playing alongside others without much interaction (parallel play), and for playing with similar autistic people. Ask the person what they prefer at the moment, since solo play can help them recover. Evidence: interviews with 22 autistic adults aged 18-57 in the United Kingdom, analysed for themes. Limits: it is a small group from one country, sharing adult experiences; it does not show that all autistic people, or children, play or prefer the same things.
sheet.sv: Se lek som värdefull i alla dess former: ge utrymme för att leka själv, leka bredvid andra utan mycket samspel (parallellek) och leka med liknande autistiska personer. Fråga personen vad hen föredrar just nu, eftersom ensamlek kan hjälpa till att återhämta sig. Belägg: intervjuer med 22 autistiska vuxna i åldern 18-57 år i Storbritannien, analyserade i teman. Begränsningar: det är en liten grupp från ett land som delar vuxnas erfarenheter; studien visar inte att alla autistiska personer, eller barn, leker eller föredrar samma saker.

title: Perinatal and Postpartum Health Among People With Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities.
authors: Shea L, Sadowsky M, Tao S, Rast J, Schendel D, Chesnokova A, Headen I
abstract: Importance Small, geographically limited studies report that people with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD) have increased risk for serious pregnancy-related and birth-related challenges, including preeclampsia, preterm birth, and increased anxiety and depression, than their peers. United States-based population-level data among people with IDD are lacking. Objectives To identify perinatal and postpartum outcomes among a national, longitudinal sample of people with IDD enrolled in public health insurance, compare subgroups of people with IDD, and compare outcomes among people with IDD with those of peers without IDD. Design, setting, and participants This retrospective cohort study used national Medicaid claims from January 1, 2008, to December 31, 2019, for 55 440 birthing people with IDD and a random sample of 438 557 birthing people without IDD. Medicaid funds almost half of all births and is the largest behavioral health insurer in the US, covering a robust array of services for people with IDD. Statistical analysis was performed from July 2023 to June 2024. Exposure People who had a documented birth in Medicaid during the study years. Main outcome and measures Perinatal outcomes were compared across groups using univariate and multivariate logistic regression. The probability of postpartum anxiety and depression was estimated using Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards regression. Results The study sample included 55 440 birthing people with IDD (including 41 854 with intellectual disabilities [ID] and 13 586 with autism; mean [SD] age at first delivery, 24.9 [6.7] years) and a random sample of 438 557 birthing people without IDD (mean [SD] age at first delivery, 26.4 [6.3] years). People with IDD were younger at first observed delivery, had a lower prevalence of live births (66.6% vs 76.7%), and higher rates of obstetric conditions (gestational diabetes, 10.3% vs 9.9%; gestational hypertension, 8.7% vs 6.1%; preeclampsia, 6.1% vs 4.4%) and co-occurring physical conditions (heart failure, 1.4% vs 0.4%; hyperlipidemia, 5.3% vs 1.7%; ischemic heart disease, 1.5% vs 0.4%; obesity, 16.3% vs 7.4%) and mental health conditions (anxiety disorders, 27.9% vs 6.5%; depressive disorders, 32.1% vs 7.5%; posttraumatic stress disorder, 9.5% vs 1.2%) than people without IDD. The probability of postpartum anxiety (adjusted hazard ratio [AHR], 3.2 [95% CI, 2.9-3.4]) and postpartum depression (AHR, 2.4 [95% CI, 2.3-2.6]) was significantly higher among autistic people compared with people with ID only and people without IDD. Conclusions and relevance In this retrospective cohort study, people with IDD had a younger mean age at first delivery, had lower prevalence of live births, and had poor obstetric, mental health, and medical outcomes compared with people without IDD, pointing toward a need for clinician training and timely delivery of maternal health care. Results highlight needed reproductive health education, increasing clinician knowledge, and expanding Medicaid to ensure access to care for people with IDD.

sheet.es: Si estás embarazada o acompañas a una persona autista durante el embarazo y el posparto, conviene pedir pronto controles prenatales y posparto, y vigilar con calma señales de ansiedad o tristeza persistente para consultarlas con el equipo sanitario. Es un estudio retrospectivo con registros nacionales de Medicaid en EE. UU.: 55 440 personas con discapacidad intelectual y del desarrollo (13 586 autistas) frente a 438 557 sin ella. Las autistas tuvieron más ansiedad y depresión posparto. Sus límites: son datos de seguros en un solo país, no explican causas y no describen a cada persona. Las decisiones médicas corresponden a profesionales de la salud.
sheet.en: If you are pregnant, or support an autistic person through pregnancy and the postpartum period, it helps to arrange prenatal and postpartum check-ups early and to calmly watch for lasting anxiety or low mood, raising them with the health team. This was a retrospective study of national US Medicaid records: 55 440 people with intellectual and developmental disabilities (13 586 autistic) compared with 438 557 without. Autistic people had higher postpartum anxiety and depression. Limits: it uses insurance data from one country, cannot explain causes, and does not describe every person. Medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om du är gravid, eller stöttar en autistisk person under graviditet och tiden efter förlossningen, kan det hjälpa att boka kontroller före och efter förlossningen i god tid och i lugn och ro uppmärksamma ihållande oro eller nedstämdhet, och ta upp det med vårdteamet. Det var en retrospektiv studie av nationella amerikanska Medicaid-uppgifter: 55 440 personer med intellektuell och utvecklingsrelaterad funktionsnedsättning (13 586 autistiska) jämfördes med 438 557 utan. Autistiska personer hade mer ångest och depression efter förlossningen. Begränsningar: försäkringsdata från ett land, orsaker kan inte förklaras och resultaten beskriver inte alla individer. Medicinska beslut hör till vårdpersonal.

title: Developing Knowledge of Autism in Majority World Countries: Examples of Bolivia and Paraguay.
authors: Westby C, Roman R
abstract: Bolivia and Paraguay are Majority World countries, which are defined as areas within which most of the world's population live, natural resources and landmass are located, but are often economically poor. Minority world countries, such as, the United States, have a smaller percentage of the world's population, but often a greater share of the world's wealth. Many Majority World countries, such as Bolivia and Paraguay, have not collected prevalence data on autism and assessments and interventions for persons are quite limited, if they are available at all. Persons with autism in Bolivia and Paraguay are at most underserved and the majority are unserved. This article reviews topological, demographic, and economic/political factors affecting the identification and provisions of services for autistic children and the current health and educational status for autistic persons in Bolivia and Paraguay. Descriptions of the efforts of outside consultants to assist parents and professional within those countries to gain information and develop assessment and intervention programs for autistic children are described. Attention is given to methodologies employed by United States consultants to ensure the implementation of culturally responsive practices. Consultants employed skilled dialogue when interviewing parents and professionals in Bolivia and Paraguay to understand their perspectives so as to guide content of trainings. The PRECEDE-PROCEED framework was employed to develop a culturally-responsive approach to assessment and intervention.

sheet.es: Si vives en un lugar con pocos servicios para autistas, tu experiencia como familia es una fuente valiosa: conviene compartirla con los profesionales y pedir que la escuchen antes de decidir qué apoyos ofrecer. La evidencia es una revisión que describe la situación en Bolivia y Paraguay y el trabajo de consultores de Estados Unidos, que usaron diálogo hábil con familias y profesionales y el marco PRECEDE-PROCEED. Sus límites: no mide resultados en niñas, niños o familias concretas, describe solo dos países y no sirve como regla para todas las personas ni para todos los contextos.
sheet.en: If you live somewhere with few services for autistic people, your experience as a family is valuable: share it with professionals and ask them to listen before deciding which supports to offer. The evidence is a review describing the situation in Bolivia and Paraguay and the work of consultants from the United States, who used skilled dialogue with parents and professionals and the PRECEDE-PROCEED framework. Its limits: it does not measure outcomes for particular children or families, it covers only two countries, and it is not a rule for every person or every setting.
sheet.sv: Om du bor på en plats med få tjänster för autistiska personer är din familjs erfarenhet värdefull: dela den med yrkespersoner och be dem lyssna innan de bestämmer vilket stöd som ska erbjudas. Underlaget är en översikt som beskriver situationen i Bolivia och Paraguay och arbetet av konsulter från USA, som använde skickad dialog med föräldrar och yrkespersoner samt ramverket PRECEDE-PROCEED. Begränsningar: den mäter inte resultat för enskilda barn eller familjer, omfattar bara två länder och är ingen regel för alla personer eller alla miljöer.

title: Dental Hygiene Challenges in Children with Autism: Correlation with Parental Stress: A Scoping Review.
authors: Alegría PL, Landim SF, Branco BHM, Carmine F, Birditt K, Sandoval C, González MM
abstract: Background Children diagnosed with autism spectrum disorders are shown to have poor periodontal health and dental hygiene habits. Extensive research has revealed that parents of children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) frequently encounter heightened levels of stress, despair, and anxiety in comparison to parents of neurotypical children. The aim was to understand the relationship between the dental hygiene of children with ASD and the stress generated in their parents. Methods : A scoping review was carried out to identify any gaps or research opportunities for clinical practice concerning oral care and stress levels in parents in the PubMed, Medline, ScienceDirect, and Scopus databases. Results : A total of 139 articles were reviewed. Of these, only 10 met the selection criteria for inclusion. Our results reveal a lack of studies presenting evidence on the topic of poor dental hygiene in children with ASD and high stress levels in their parents. Discussion : There is ample evidence that children with ASD have poor dental hygiene, as well as higher levels of stress in their parents. However, little or no evidence links these two variables. Future studies should focus on this link, which could have practical implications for improving dental care for children with ASD.

sheet.es: Si cepillar los dientes se vive como una carga en casa, no es un fallo de la familia: conviene pedir apoyo al equipo dental y comentarle qué le resulta difícil a la persona autista (texturas, sabores, ruidos, tiempos). La evidencia es una revisión de alcance: se revisaron 139 artículos y solo 10 cumplieron los criterios. Hay bastante evidencia de peor higiene dental en niños autistas y de más estrés en sus madres y padres, pero casi ninguna que relacione ambas cosas. Por eso no sabemos si una causa la otra, y no sirve como regla para cada familia.
sheet.en: If tooth brushing feels like a heavy load at home, it is not a family failing: ask the dental team for support and tell them what the autistic person finds hard (textures, tastes, noises, timing). The evidence is a scoping review: 139 articles were reviewed and only 10 met the criteria. There is plenty of evidence of poorer dental hygiene in autistic children and of higher stress in their parents, but almost none linking the two. So we cannot say whether one causes the other, and this is not a rule for every family.
sheet.sv: Om tandborstning känns som en tung börda hemma är det inte familjens fel: be tandvårdsteamet om stöd och berätta vad den autistiska personen tycker är svårt (strukturer, smaker, ljud, tidpunkt). Underlaget är en kartläggande översikt: 139 artiklar granskades och bara 10 uppfyllde kriterierna. Det finns gott om belägg för sämre munhygien hos autistiska barn och mer stress hos deras föräldrar, men nästan inga som kopplar ihop de två. Vi vet därför inte om det ena orsakar det andra, och det är ingen regel för varje familj.

title: Finding Similarities in Differences Between Autistic Adults: Two Replicated Subgroups.
authors: Radhoe TA, Agelink van Rentergem JA, Torenvliet C, Groenman AP, van der Putten WJ, Geurts HM
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Autism is heterogeneous, which complicates providing tailored support and future prospects. We aim to identify subgroups in autistic adults with average to high intelligence, to clarify if certain subgroups might need support. We included 14 questionnaire variables related to aging and/or autism (e.g., demographic, psychological, and lifestyle). Community detection analysis was used for subgroup identification in an original sample of 114 autistic adults with an adulthood diagnosis (autism) and 58 non-autistic adults as comparison group (COMP), and a replication sample (N Autism = 261; N COMP = 287), both aged 30-89 years. Next, we identified subgroups and assessed external validity (for cognitive and psychological difficulties, and quality of life [QoL]) in the autism samples. To test specificity, we repeated the analysis after adding 123 adults with ADHD, aged 30-80 years. As expected, the autism and COMP groups formed distinct subgroups. Among autistic adults, we identified three subgroups of which two were replicated. One of these subgroups seemed most vulnerable on the cluster variables; this subgroup also reported the most cognitive and psychological difficulties, and lowest QoL. Adding the ADHD group did not alter results. Within autistic adults, one subgroup could especially benefit from support and specialized care, although this must be tested in future studies.

sheet.es: Para tener en cuenta mañana: dos autistas adultos con la misma edad y capacidad intelectual pueden necesitar apoyos muy distintos, así que conviene preguntar a cada persona qué le resulta difícil y qué le ayuda, en lugar de suponerlo. Este estudio con personas autistas usó cuestionarios en dos muestras de adultos de 30 a 89 años. Encontró dos subgrupos que se repitieron; uno refirió más dificultades cognitivas y psicológicas y menor calidad de vida. Sus límites: los grupos son estadísticos, sólo incluyó adultos con inteligencia media o alta y no prueba qué apoyo funciona. No describe a ninguna persona concreta.
sheet.en: For tomorrow: two autistic adults of the same age and intellectual ability can need very different support, so ask each person what is hard and what helps rather than assuming. This study with autistic people used questionnaires in two samples of adults aged 30-89 years. It found two subgroups that appeared in both samples; one reported more cognitive and psychological difficulties and lower quality of life. Limits: the groups are statistical, only adults with average to high intelligence were included, and the study does not test which support works. It does not describe any one individual.
sheet.sv: Att tänka på imorgon: två autistiska vuxna med samma ålder och intellektuella förmåga kan behöva helt olika stöd, så fråga varje person vad som är svårt och vad som hjälper i stället för att anta det. Studien med autistiska personer använde enkäter i två grupper av vuxna i åldern 30-89 år. Den fann två undergrupper som återkom i båda; en rapporterade fler kognitiva och psykologiska svårigheter och lägre livskvalitet. Begränsningar: grupperna är statistiska, bara vuxna med normal till hög intelligens ingick och studien testar inte vilket stöd som fungerar. Den beskriver ingen enskild person.

title: Cost-utility analysis of Social Stories™ for children with autism spectrum disorder in mainstream primary schools: results from a randomised controlled trial.
authors: Wang HI, Bell K, Blackwell J, Welch C, Mandefield L, Watson J, Standley E, McMillan D, Gilbody S, Wright B, Hewitt C, Parrott S
abstract: Background One in 57 children are diagnosed with autism in the UK, and the estimated cost for supporting these children in education is substantial. Social Stories™ is a promising and widely used intervention for supporting children with autism in schools and families. It is believed that Social Stories™ can provide meaningful social information to children that can improve social understanding and may reduce anxiety. However, no economic evaluation of Social Stories has been conducted. Aims To assess the cost-effectiveness of Social Stories through Autism Spectrum Social Stories in Schools Trial 2, a multi-site, pragmatic, cluster-randomised controlled trial. Method Children with autism who were aged 4-11 years were recruited and randomised ( N = 249). Costs measured from the societal perspective and quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs) measured by the EQ-5D-Y-3L proxy were collected at baseline and at 6-month follow-up for primary analysis. The incremental cost-effectiveness ratio was calculated, and the uncertainty around incremental cost-effectiveness ratios was captured by non-parametric bootstrapping. Sensitivity analyses were performed to evaluate the robustness of the primary findings. Results Social Stories is likely to result in a small cost savings (-£191 per child, 95% CI -767.7 to 337.7) and maintain similar QALY improvements compared with usual care. The probability of Social Stories being a preferred option is 75% if society is willing to pay £20 000 per QALY gained. The sensitivity analysis results aligned with the main study outcomes. Conclusions Compared with usual care, Social Stories did not lead to an increase in costs and maintained similar QALY improvements for primary-aged children with autism.

sheet.es: Si su hija o hijo autista usa Social Stories™ en el colegio, no hay indicios de que cueste más que el apoyo habitual ni de que cambie la calidad de vida de forma distinta. Puede hablar con el centro sobre si encaja con su criatura. Es un ensayo aleatorizado por grupos, con 249 niñas y niños autistas de 4-11 años en colegios de primaria ordinarios, que comparó costes y calidad de vida a los 6 meses. Sus límites: el ahorro estimado (-£191 por niño) tiene mucha incertidumbre (IC 95% -767.7 a 337.7) y los resultados no sirven como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If your autistic child uses Social Stories™ at school, this study found no sign that it costs more than usual support, or that quality of life changes differently. You can talk with the school about whether it suits your child. It was a cluster-randomised trial with 249 autistic children aged 4-11 in mainstream primary schools, comparing costs and quality of life at 6 months. Its limits: the estimated saving (-£191 per child) is very uncertain (95% CI -767.7 to 337.7), and the results are not a rule for every individual child.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn använder Social Stories™ i skolan visade studien inga tecken på att det kostar mer än vanligt stöd, eller att livskvaliteten förändras på ett annat sätt. Du kan prata med skolan om det passar ditt barn. Det var en klusterrandomiserad studie med 249 autistiska barn i åldern 4-11 år i vanliga grundskolor, som jämförde kostnader och livskvalitet efter 6 månader. Begränsningar: den uppskattade besparingen (-£191 per barn) är mycket osäker (95 % KI -767.7 till 337.7), och resultaten är ingen regel för varje enskilt barn.

title: A Rapid Evidence Assessment on The Effectiveness of Interventions for Autistic Adolescents with Harmful Sexual Behaviors.
authors: Trew S, Russell DH
abstract: The management and treatment of harmful sexual behaviors (HSBs) in autistic adolescents is a complex area of research and clinical practice. Autistic adolescents face unique challenges in understanding social and sexual interactions, putting them at a higher risk of engaging in HSBs. Existing research on interventions for HSBs among autistic adults is growing, but evidence for adolescents is not well understood. Thus, understanding the effectiveness of interventions targeting HSBs in autistic adolescents is crucial. We conducted a rapid evidence assessment to review peer-reviewed research on the effectiveness of interventions for autistic adolescents at risk of or engaging in HSBs. In all, 12 studies met the criteria for review. Inclusion criteria required articles to be published in a peer-reviewed journal, be related to HSB prevention and intervention in adolescents aged 12 to 18 with autism spectrum disorder, be written in English, and include original data. Six databases were used, and we screened the titles and abstracts of 34 studies. The reviewed studies described cognitive-behavioral therapy, pharmacological interventions, family involvement, and multidisciplinary team approaches in addressing HSBs. However, the literature has significant limitations and we suggest that the literature is not robust enough to indicate a promising evidence-based approach for interventions for autistic adolescents who are at risk of or who display and engage in HSBs, and the findings are not transferable to practice. Additional research is required to better prepare healthcare professionals for addressing HSBs in autistic adolescents.

sheet.es: Si le preocupa la conducta sexual de un adolescente autista, busque pronto apoyo de profesionales con experiencia en autismo y trabaje con la familia y el equipo. Mientras tanto, explique con claridad y sin juicios las reglas sobre el cuerpo, el consentimiento y la intimidad. Esta revisión rápida analizó 12 estudios sobre intervenciones para adolescentes autistas de 12 a 18 años en riesgo de conductas sexuales dañinas o que las presentaban. Describían terapia cognitivo-conductual, intervenciones farmacológicas, participación familiar y equipos multidisciplinarios. Sus autores concluyen que la evidencia no es lo bastante sólida para señalar un enfoque prometedor ni para trasladarlo a la práctica. Las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If you are worried about a sexual behavior in an autistic teenager, seek support early from professionals who know autism, and work together with the family and team. Meanwhile, explain rules about bodies, consent and privacy clearly and without judgment. This rapid evidence assessment reviewed 12 studies of interventions for autistic adolescents aged 12 to 18 at risk of or engaging in harmful sexual behaviors. They described cognitive-behavioral therapy, pharmacological interventions, family involvement and multidisciplinary teams. The authors conclude the evidence is not robust enough to point to a promising approach or to apply in practice. Medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om du är orolig för ett sexuellt beteende hos en autistisk tonåring: sök stöd tidigt hos yrkespersoner som kan autism och samarbeta med familjen och teamet. Förklara under tiden regler om kroppen, samtycke och privatliv tydligt och utan skuldbeläggning. Denna snabba kunskapsöversikt granskade 12 studier om insatser för autistiska ungdomar mellan 12 och 18 år som riskerade att uppvisa eller uppvisade skadligt sexuellt beteende. Studierna beskrev kognitiv beteendeterapi, farmakologiska insatser, familjens delaktighet och multidisciplinära team. Forskarna menar att underlaget inte är starkt nog för att peka ut ett lovande tillvägagångssätt eller för att användas i praktiken. Medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker.

title: Physiological and communicative emotional disconcordance in children on the autism spectrum.
authors: Finkel E, Sah E, Spaulding M, Herrington JD, Tomczuk L, Masino A, Pang X, Bhattacharya A, Hedley D, Kushleyeva Y, Thomson P, Doppelt N, Tan J, Pennington J, Dissanayake C, Bonafide CP, Nuske HJ
abstract: Background Individuals on the autism spectrum commonly have differences from non-autistic people in expressing their emotions using communicative behaviors, such as facial expressions. However, it is not yet clear if this reduced expressivity stems from reduced physiological reactivity in emotional contexts or if individuals react internally, but do not show these reactions externally to others. We hypothesized that autism is characterized by a discordance between in-the-moment internal psychophysiological arousal and external communicative expressions of emotion. Methods Forty-one children on the autism spectrum and 39 non-autistic, typically developing (TD) children of two age groups (2-4 and 8-12 years) participated in a low-level stress task whilst wearing a wireless electrocardiogram. Children's negative emotional expressions (facial, vocal, bodily) were coded following standardized protocols. Alexithymia traits were assessed using the Children's Alexithymia Measure with school-aged children only. Data analyses involved ANOVAs, correlations, and sensitivity analyses. Results There were no group differences in physiological arousal (heart rate) or in communicative expressions of stress to the stress task. For TD preschoolers, physiological arousal during the stress task was associated with vocal expressions and for TD school-aged children, they were associated with facial and bodily expressions. By contrast, for children on the autism spectrum, physiological arousal during the stress tasks was not associated with communicative expressions across age groups. Conclusions Our findings suggest that children on the autism spectrum might experience emotional disconcordance, in that their physiological arousal does not align with their communicative expressions. Therefore, the internally experienced stress of children on the autism spectrum may be inadvertently missed by teachers and caregivers and, consequently, learning opportunities for teaching emotional communication and regulation may be also missed. Our results support the use of wearable biosensors to facilitate such interventions in children on the autism spectrum.

sheet.es: Si su hijo parece tranquilo, no dé por hecho que lo está: el estrés interno puede no verse en la cara, la voz o el cuerpo. Pregúntele cómo se siente, ofrezca pausas y observe otras señales, como el contexto. El estudio comparó a 41 niños autistas y 39 niños no autistas de dos grupos de edad (2-4 y 8-12 años) durante una tarea de estrés leve, midiendo la frecuencia cardíaca y las expresiones. En los niños autistas, la activación del cuerpo no se relacionó con lo que expresaban. Es un estudio pequeño, con una sola tarea, y no describe a todos los niños autistas.
sheet.en: If your child looks calm, don't assume they are: inner stress may not show in the face, voice or body. Ask how they feel, offer breaks, and watch other cues, such as the situation. The study compared 41 autistic children and 39 non-autistic children in two age groups (2-4 and 8-12 years) during a low-level stress task, measuring heart rate and expressions. In autistic children, bodily arousal was not linked to what they expressed. It is a small study with one task, and it does not describe every autistic child.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn ser lugnt ut, utgå inte från att det är lugnt: inre stress syns kanske inte i ansikte, röst eller kropp. Fråga hur barnet mår, erbjud pauser och se på andra signaler, som situationen. Studien jämförde 41 autistiska barn och 39 icke-autistiska barn i två åldersgrupper (2-4 och 8-12 år) under en lätt stressuppgift, med mätning av hjärtfrekvens och uttryck. Hos de autistiska barnen hängde kroppens upphetsning inte ihop med det de uttryckte. Studien är liten, har en enda uppgift och beskriver inte alla autistiska barn.

title: Low-intensity parent- and clinician-delivered support for young autistic children in Aotearoa New Zealand: a randomised controlled trial.
authors: Waddington H, Jordan P, Hammond M, Tupou J, Patrick L, Macaskill E, Davies G, Pillar S, van der Meer L, Whitehouse AJO
journal: The Lancet regional health. Western Pacific
abstract: Background Aotearoa New Zealand does not provide publicly-funded intensive autism support. While parent-mediated supports are promising, children and families may also benefit from direct clinician support. We tested the efficacy of a low-intensity programme involving parent- and clinician-delivered support for autistic children. Methods This single-blind, two-arm randomised controlled trial assessed outcomes of a six-month low-intensity parent- and clinician-delivered support (2-3 h per week) based on the Early Start Denver Model compared to a control group who received monthly support calls and assistance with referrals. Children aged 1-4.5 years who were autistic or showing signs of autism and their parents were randomised to the low-intensity or control group by a blinded statistician using the Urn minimisation method. Assessments were conducted at baseline and immediately following the support period (24-weeks post-baseline). The primary outcome was child engagement during an interaction with their parent. The trial was pre-registered with ANZCTR: U1111-1260-2529. Findings From March 2021 to May 2023, 56 families were randomised to either the low-intensity or control group. Following drop-outs, 21 families in the low-intensity group and 24 in the control group were included in analysis. There was large and significantly greater improvement in children's engagement in the low-intensity group compared to the control group (F (1, 43) = 21.47, p p 2 = 0.33). There was one recorded adverse event unrelated to the support and two adverse effects related to the support. Interpretation A low-intensity parent- and clinician-delivered support can improve engagement between an autistic child and their parent during play. Low-intensity supports may be beneficial in areas where access to clinical autism supports is limited. Funding Emerging Researcher First Grant from the Health Research Council of New Zealand.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a un niño autista pequeño y el acceso a apoyos es limitado, un apoyo de baja intensidad, en el que la familia y un profesional trabajan juntos y el juego es el centro, puede ayudar a que el niño y tú os conectéis mejor al jugar. Es un ensayo aleatorizado con 56 familias de niños de 1-4.5 años, basado en el Early Start Denver Model, durante seis meses (2-3 h por semana). Los niños del grupo de apoyo mejoraron más en su participación con sus padres que los del grupo de control. Hubo dos efectos adversos relacionados con el apoyo. Limitaciones: algunas familias abandonaron, solo se midió justo al terminar, y no todos los niños responderán igual.
sheet.en: If you care for a young autistic child and access to support is limited, low-intensity support in which the family and a clinician work together, centred on play, may help you and your child connect better during play. This was a randomised trial of 56 families with children aged 1-4.5 years, based on the Early Start Denver Model, lasting six months (2-3 h per week). Children in the support group improved more in engagement with their parent than those in the control group. Two adverse effects were related to the support. Limits: some families dropped out, measures were taken only right at the end, and not every child will respond the same way.
sheet.sv: Om du har ett litet autistiskt barn och tillgången till stöd är begränsad kan lågintensivt stöd, där familjen och en kliniker arbetar tillsammans med leken i centrum, hjälpa dig och ditt barn att samspela bättre i leken. Det var en randomiserad studie med 56 familjer med barn i åldern 1-4.5 år, baserad på Early Start Denver Model, under sex månader (2-3 h per vecka). Barnen i stödgruppen förbättrade sitt engagemang med föräldern mer än barnen i kontrollgruppen. Två biverkningar hade samband med stödet. Begränsningar: några familjer hoppade av, mätningen gjordes bara direkt efter stödet, och alla barn svarar inte på samma sätt.

title: The Face of Autism in Israel.
authors: Ferman S, Segal O
abstract: This article seeks to offer a comprehensive perspective on autism in Israel, aligning with global reports. It aims to serve as a foundational resource for policymakers in developing relevant support and point to unmet needs. The data was drawn from publications by Israeli government authorities and academic publications. In 2022, the prevalence of child and adolescent autism in Israel was approximately 1.13%, with a male-to-female ratio of 4:1, and an annual increase of 23%, particularly among young children. In Israel, the diagnosis of autism follows the DSM-5 guidelines and is conducted by a physician and a psychologist specializing in autism. Typically, diagnosis is at age 2. The autism intervention approaches prevalent in Israel are consistent with those that are globally accepted. Children with autism are entitled to special education services adapted to their needs and developmental levels. The legally established package of services for children with autism includes sessions with occupational therapists, speech-language pathologists (SLPs), physical therapists, psychologists, and social workers. Children and adults with autism are eligible for disability allowance along with support regarding residence, educational programs, and employment opportunities. Nonetheless, underdiagnosis and low accessibility to services are common in minority populations and rural areas. Furthermore, in recent years, services for autistic individuals have declined. This decline, particularly considering the ongoing rise in the prevalence of autism, pose significant challenges for Israeli government authorities in ensuring that autistic persons receive appropriate support.

sheet.es: Si cuidas de una persona autista en Israel, conviene saber que existe un paquete legal de servicios (terapia ocupacional, logopedia, fisioterapia, psicología y trabajo social) y educación especial adaptada. Pregunta por ellos y por las ayudas por discapacidad. Es una revisión que reúne publicaciones de autoridades gubernamentales israelíes y de revistas académicas. Sus límites: describe el sistema de Israel, no explica la vida de cada familia, y señala que el infradiagnóstico y el acceso limitado a servicios son frecuentes en minorías y zonas rurales, y que los servicios han disminuido en los últimos años.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person in Israel, know that a legal package of services exists (occupational therapy, speech-language therapy, physical therapy, psychology and social work), along with adapted special education. Ask about these and about disability allowance. This is a review drawing on publications from Israeli government authorities and academic sources. Its limits: it describes Israel's system, not every family's experience, and it notes that underdiagnosis and low access to services are common in minority populations and rural areas, and that services have declined in recent years.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person i Israel är det bra att veta att det finns ett lagstadgat servicepaket (arbetsterapi, logopedi, fysioterapi, psykologi och socialt arbete) samt anpassad specialundervisning. Fråga om dessa och om funktionsnedsättningsbidrag. Det är en översikt som bygger på publikationer från israeliska myndigheter och akademiska källor. Begränsningar: den beskriver Israels system, inte varje familjs vardag, och den visar att underdiagnostik och dålig tillgång till tjänster är vanligt bland minoriteter och på landsbygden, samt att tjänsterna minskat de senaste åren.

title: Mortality risk among Autistic children and young people: A nationwide birth cohort study.
authors: Vu H, Bowden N, Gibb S, Audas R, Dacombe J, McLay L, Sporle A, Stace H, Taylor B, Thabrew H, Theodore R, Tupou J, Schluter PJ
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Existing literature indicates that Autistic people have shorter life expectancy, but little is known about the mortality risk among Autistic children and young people (0-24 years). We used a 15-year nationwide birth cohort study to estimate the mortality risk among Autistic children and young people in Aotearoa/New Zealand. The study included 895,707 children and 11,919 (1.4%) were Autistic. We found that autism was associated with a significantly higher mortality risk compared to the non-Autistic population. In addition, we found that this risk was significantly higher among females compared to males and for those with a co-occurring intellectual disability. Increased efforts are required to better meet the health needs of this population.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista, merece la pena asegurarte de que sus necesidades de salud se atiendan con regularidad y de que los equipos médicos la escuchen, sobre todo si hay discapacidad intelectual. Este estudio de cohorte de nacimiento en Aotearoa/Nueva Zelanda siguió durante 15 años a 895,707 niños y jóvenes; 11,919 (1.4%) eran autistas. El autismo se asoció con mayor riesgo de mortalidad, más alto en mujeres y con discapacidad intelectual. Es un estudio de asociación: no explica las causas ni predice qué pasará con una persona concreta, y los resultados pueden no ser iguales en otros países.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person, it is worth making sure their health needs are checked regularly and that health teams listen to them, especially when there is also an intellectual disability. This birth cohort study followed 895,707 children and young people in Aotearoa/New Zealand for 15 years; 11,919 (1.4%) were autistic. Autism was associated with a higher mortality risk, higher still among females and those with intellectual disability. It shows an association only: it does not explain causes or predict what will happen for any one person, and results may differ in other countries.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person är det värt att se till att hälsobehoven följs upp regelbundet och att vårdteamen lyssnar på personen, särskilt vid intellektuell funktionsnedsättning. Denna födelsekohortstudie följde 895,707 barn och unga i Aotearoa/Nya Zeeland under 15 år; 11,919 (1.4%) var autistiska. Autism var förknippat med högre dödlighetsrisk, ännu högre bland kvinnor och vid intellektuell funktionsnedsättning. Studien visar bara ett samband: den förklarar inte orsaker eller förutsäger vad som händer för en enskild person, och resultaten kan skilja sig i andra länder.

title: What are the autism research priorities of autistic adults in Scotland?
authors: Cage E, Crompton CJ, Dantas S, Strachan K, Birch R, Robinson M, Morgan-Appel S, MacKenzie-Nash C, Gallagher A, Botha M
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Although research has the potential to improve autistic people's lives, lots of funding goes towards research looking at topics which autistic people say has little impact in their everyday lives. Autistic people's lives can be different depending on where they live, and Scotland is a unique country in many ways. We wanted to find out which topics autistic people in Scotland want to see research on. Our team of autistic and non-autistic researchers (including university-based and community researchers) created a survey where 225 autistic adults rated and ranked the importance of possible research topics and shared their thoughts on what topics mattered to them. The five most important topics were mental health and well-being, identifying and diagnosing autistic people, support services (including healthcare and social care), non-autistic people's knowledge and attitudes and issues impacting autistic women. The three least important topics were genetics or biological aspects of autism, autism treatments/interventions and causes of autism. Our findings indicate that autistic people in Scotland want research to focus on things that matter to their day-to-day lives. Also, the Scottish government says they will be listening to autistic people in their latest policy plans, and we believe that considering autistic people's research priorities is an important part of this. Our findings also add to growing calls for change to happen in how and what autism researchers do research on.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista, puedes preguntarle qué le importa en su día a día: salud mental y bienestar, acceso al diagnóstico, servicios de apoyo, actitudes de las personas no autistas y la experiencia de las mujeres autistas. Esas fueron sus prioridades; la genética, las causas y los «tratamientos» quedaron al final. Úsalo para orientar conversaciones con profesionales y servicios hacia lo cotidiano. La evidencia viene de una encuesta diseñada por investigadores autistas y no autistas, respondida por 225 adultos autistas en Escocia. Sus límites: refleja opiniones de quienes participaron en un país concreto y puede no representar a todas las personas autistas, incluidas quienes no usan encuestas escritas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person, you can ask what matters in their daily life: mental health and well-being, access to diagnosis, support services, non-autistic people's attitudes and autistic women's experiences. These were the top priorities; genetics, causes and 'treatments' came last. Use this to steer conversations with professionals and services towards everyday needs. The evidence comes from a survey designed by autistic and non-autistic researchers and answered by 225 autistic adults in Scotland. Its limits: it reflects the views of people who took part in one country and may not represent all autistic people, including those who find written surveys inaccessible.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person kan du fråga vad som spelar roll i vardagen: psykisk hälsa och välmående, tillgång till diagnos, stödinsatser, icke-autistiska personers attityder och autistiska kvinnors erfarenheter. Det var de högsta prioriteringarna; genetik, orsaker och ”behandlingar” hamnade sist. Använd detta för att rikta samtal med vårdpersonal och stödverksamheter mot vardagens behov. Underlaget är en enkät utformad av autistiska och icke-autistiska forskare, besvarad av 225 autistiska vuxna i Skottland. Begränsningar: den speglar deltagarnas åsikter i ett enda land och representerar inte nödvändigtvis alla autistiska personer, till exempel de som har svårt med skriftliga enkäter.

title: The Gestalt of functioning in autism revisited: First revision of the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health Core Sets.
authors: Bölte S, Alehagen L, Black MH, Hasslinger J, Wessman E, Lundin Remnélius K, Marschik PB, D'Arcy E, Crowson S, Freeth M, Seidel A, Girdler S, Zander E
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic people experience individual strengths and challenges as well as barriers and facilitators in their environment. All of these factors contribute to how well autistic people can cope in everyday life, fulfill the roles they choose, and meet their needs. The World Health Organization has developed a system aiming to capture the many factors within people (like how someone thinks and feels) and outside of people (things around a person) that influence their daily living, called the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health. The International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health can be used for different purposes in research and practice to assess people's situations and plan support measures. Previously in 2019, the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health was adapted to autism by developing so-called Core Sets, which are shorter International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health versions for use in specific conditions. Here, we present the first revisions of the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health Core Sets for autism, based on research, development results, and community feedback. Some factors influencing daily life for autistic people were added to the Core Sets, and other factors deemed less relevant were removed. Changes were also made in Core Sets designed for different age groups (0-5, 6-16, and ⩾17 years). Particularly, contents for sensory processing (like smell, touch, seeing, hearing) were added. We recommend these updated Core Sets for future use in autism research and practice. These changes to the Core Sets after 4 years indicate that there should be ongoing updates based on research and experience from practice and involvement of stakeholders.

sheet.es: Cuando hable con profesionales sobre apoyos, puede pedir que miren el día a día completo: fortalezas, dificultades y también el entorno (ruido, luz, actitudes, adaptaciones). La versión revisada de los Core Sets de la CIF para el autismo añade aspectos sensoriales como olfato, tacto, vista y oído, así que puede mencionarlos con confianza. Este trabajo revisó listas de la OMS para tres grupos de edad (0-5, 6-16 y 17 años o más), combinando investigación, resultados de desarrollo y opiniones de la comunidad autista y otras partes interesadas. Su límite: es una herramienta de evaluación y planificación, no prueba qué apoyos funcionan, y seguirá cambiando con el tiempo.
sheet.en: When you talk with professionals about support, you can ask them to look at the whole of daily life: strengths, difficulties, and the environment too (noise, light, attitudes, adjustments). The revised ICF Core Sets for autism now include sensory aspects such as smell, touch, sight and hearing, so you can raise these with confidence. This work updated World Health Organization checklists for three age groups (0-5, 6-16 and 17+), drawing on research, development results and feedback from the autistic community and other stakeholders. Its limit: it is a tool for assessment and planning, it does not show which supports work, and it will keep changing over time.
sheet.sv: När du pratar med professionella om stöd kan du be dem se hela vardagen: styrkor, svårigheter och även miljön (ljud, ljus, bemötande, anpassningar). De reviderade ICF Core Sets för autism innehåller nu sensoriska aspekter som lukt, beröring, syn och hörsel, så du kan med trygghet ta upp dem. Arbetet uppdaterade Världshälsoorganisationens checklistor för tre åldersgrupper (0–5, 6–16 och 17 år och äldre), baserat på forskning, utvecklingsresultat och synpunkter från den autistiska gemenskapen och andra berörda. Begränsning: det är ett verktyg för bedömning och planering, det visar inte vilka stöd som fungerar, och det kommer att fortsätta förändras.

title: Suicide risk in transition-aged autistic youth: The link among executive function, depression, and autistic traits.
authors: Cook ML, Tomaszewski B, Lamarche E, Bowman K, Klein CB, Stahl S, Klinger LG
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic people are more likely to consider suicide than non-autistic people, with transition-aged youth (ages 16-21 years) at potentially the highest risk. Research has also shown that difficulties with executive functioning (e.g., difficulties with organization, sequencing, and decision-making) may heighten suicide risk among non-autistic people, but it is not clear whether this is also true for autistic people. This study explored this question by asking 183 transition-aged autistic youth about their experience with suicidal behavior and examining the relationship between their responses and additional measures of depression, autistic traits, and executive function skills. About one-third of autistic transition-aged youth (33.3%) said that they had experienced thoughts of hurting themselves with the intent to end their lives (i.e., suicidal ideation). Both depression and executive function challenges predicted suicide risk (i.e., participants who experienced depression were more likely to have had suicidal thoughts than those who had not, and participants who had more difficulty with executive function skills were more likely to have had suicidal thoughts than those who had less difficulty). These findings suggest that executive functioning, a common area of difficulty among autistic people, is an important indicator of suicide risk in this population.

sheet.es: Si cuidas de un joven autista de 16 a 21 años, pregúntale con calma y sin juicio cómo se siente, y presta atención a la tristeza y a las dificultades para organizarse o tomar decisiones; pueden ser señales para pedir apoyo. Es un estudio con 183 jóvenes autistas en transición a la vida adulta: el 33,3% dijo haber tenido pensamientos de hacerse daño con intención de morir, y la depresión y las dificultades de función ejecutiva se relacionaron con ese riesgo. Muestra una asociación, no una causa, y no describe a cada persona. Si te preocupa alguien, habla con un profesional sanitario o un servicio de crisis. Si hay peligro inmediato, llama al número de emergencias de tu país.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic young person aged 16-21, ask calmly and without judgement how they are feeling, and notice sadness or difficulty with organisation and decision-making; these can be signs that support is needed. This study asked 183 autistic youth in transition to adulthood: 33.3% said they had had thoughts of hurting themselves with intent to end their lives, and depression and executive function difficulties were linked to that risk. It shows an association, not a cause, and does not describe every person. If you are worried about someone, contact a clinician, a health service or a crisis service. In immediate danger, call the emergency number of your country.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk ungdom mellan 16 och 21 år: fråga lugnt och utan att döma hur hen mår, och uppmärksamma nedstämdhet eller svårigheter med organisering och beslut; det kan vara tecken på att stöd behövs. Studien frågade 183 autistiska ungdomar på väg mot vuxenlivet: 33,3 % sa att de hade haft tankar på att skada sig själva med avsikt att avsluta sina liv, och depression och svårigheter med exekutiva funktioner hängde ihop med risken. Den visar ett samband, inte en orsak, och beskriver inte varje person. Är du orolig för någon, kontakta en läkare, vården eller en krisjour. Vid akut fara, ring larmnumret i ditt land.

title: Employment profiles of autistic people: An 8-year longitudinal study.
authors: Bury SM, Hedley D, Uljarević M, Uljarević M, Li X, Stokes MA, Begeer S
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic adults experience difficulties finding and keeping employment. However, research investigating reasons that might explain this difficulty produce mixed results. We gave a survey to 2449 autistic adults and used a statistic method to group them based on their employment status over 8 years. We identified four employment groups that best captured the experiences of autistic adults; this included a group that experienced stable unemployment, a group that experienced stable employment, a group that had high employment that reduced over time, and a group whose employment increased over the 8 years. Further analysis showed that those with fewer autistic traits, younger age, male gender, higher education, later diagnosis age and no co-occurring conditions were more likely to have stable employment. People whose employment changed over time were more likely to have a higher level of education than the stable unemployment group, and those in the increasing employment group were younger age and had no co-occurring conditions. These findings help us better understand that not all autistic adults' experiences of employment are the same, which helps focus where employment programmes and support may be most needed, for example, people who identify as women or have a co-occurring condition.

sheet.es: Si apoyas a una persona autista con el trabajo, no des por hecho que su camino será igual al de otras: los recorridos laborales varían mucho. Pregunta qué apoyos necesita ahora, sobre todo si es mujer o tiene otras condiciones asociadas. El estudio fue una encuesta longitudinal a 2449 adultos autistas, seguidos durante 8 años, y los agrupó en cuatro perfiles de empleo: desempleo estable, empleo estable, empleo que baja y empleo que sube. Sus límites: muestra asociaciones, no causas, y no predice lo que le pasará a una persona concreta.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person with work, don't assume their path will match anyone else's: employment journeys vary a lot. Ask what support they need now, especially if they are a woman or have co-occurring conditions. This was a longitudinal survey of 2449 autistic adults followed over 8 years, which grouped them into four employment profiles: stable unemployment, stable employment, employment that decreased, and employment that increased. Its limits: it shows associations, not causes, and it cannot predict what will happen for any one person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person med arbete: anta inte att vägen blir som för andra, eftersom arbetslivet ser mycket olika ut. Fråga vilket stöd som behövs nu, särskilt om personen är kvinna eller har samtidiga tillstånd. Studien var en longitudinell enkät med 2449 autistiska vuxna som följdes under 8 år och delades in i fyra profiler: stabil arbetslöshet, stabil sysselsättning, minskande sysselsättning och ökande sysselsättning. Begränsningar: den visar samband, inte orsaker, och kan inte förutsäga vad som händer för en enskild person.

title: How healthcare systems are experienced by autistic adults in the United Kingdom: A meta-ethnography.
authors: Radev S, Freeth M, Thompson AR
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic adults are more likely to experience mental and physical health difficulties, and yet can find it difficult to get the support that they need. A meta-ethnographic approach was used to review the existing research on autistic adults' experiences of accessing healthcare. Four databases were searched for qualitative and mixed-method studies which looked at the experiences of autistic adults who did not also have a learning disability when using healthcare services in the United Kingdom. Fifteen papers met the criteria to be included, and seven steps were used to analyse the information and develop new themes. Three main themes were identified: Professionals' lack of knowledge can be damaging , Need to reduce processing demands and Adaptation to improve engagement. This review highlights how damaging misdiagnosis, inappropriate treatment, overwhelming environments and systems that are difficult to access can have on the well-being of autistic adults.
