Limited knowledge and understanding about autism knowledge among healthcare professionals along with autistic adult's own communication and sensory differences indicate that there is a need for improved training developed with autistic adults and adaptations.

sheet.es: Antes de una cita médica, puede ayudar preparar una nota breve con las necesidades sensoriales y de comunicación de la persona autista: pedir una sala tranquila, la primera cita del día, preguntas por escrito o más tiempo para responder. También es razonable explicar al profesional cómo se expresa el dolor o el malestar. Esta revisión meta-etnográfica reunió 15 estudios cualitativos sobre adultos autistas sin discapacidad intelectual en el Reino Unido, que describieron diagnósticos erróneos, entornos abrumadores y sistemas difíciles de usar. Sus límites: solo incluye el Reino Unido, deja fuera a personas con discapacidad intelectual y las experiencias varían de una persona a otra.
sheet.en: Before a medical appointment, it can help to prepare a short note on the autistic person's sensory and communication needs: asking for a quiet room, the first slot of the day, written questions or extra time to answer. It is also reasonable to explain to the clinician how pain or distress is expressed. This meta-ethnographic review brought together 15 qualitative studies of autistic adults without a learning disability in the UK, who described misdiagnosis, overwhelming environments and hard-to-navigate systems. Its limits: it covers only the UK, leaves out people with learning disabilities, and experiences vary from person to person.
sheet.sv: Inför ett vårdbesök kan det hjälpa att förbereda en kort lapp om den autistiska personens sensoriska behov och kommunikationsbehov: be om ett lugnt rum, dagens första tid, skriftliga frågor eller extra tid att svara. Det är också rimligt att förklara för vårdpersonalen hur smärta eller obehag visar sig. Denna metaetnografiska översikt samlade 15 kvalitativa studier om autistiska vuxna utan intellektuell funktionsnedsättning i Storbritannien, som beskrev feldiagnoser, överväldigande miljöer och svårnavigerade system. Begränsningar: den gäller bara Storbritannien, utesluter personer med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning, och erfarenheter skiljer sig mellan personer.

title: Efficacy and safety of Bacteroides fragilis BF839 for pediatric autism spectrum disorder: a randomized clinical trial.
authors: Lin CH, Zeng T, Lu CW, Li DY, Liu YY, Li BM, Chen SQ, Deng YH
abstract: Background The clinical utility of Bacteroides fragilis in treating autism spectrum disorder (ASD) remains unclear. Therefore, this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study aimed to explore the therapeutic effects and safety of B. fragilis BF839 in the treatment of pediatric ASD. Methods We examined 60 children aged 2-10 years diagnosed with ASD, and participants received either BF839 powder (10 g/bar with ≥10 6 CFU/bar of viable bacteria, two bars/day) or placebo for 16 weeks. The primary outcomes was Autism Behavior Checklist (ABC) score. The secondary outcomes were Childhood Autism Rating Scale (CARS), Social Responsiveness Scale (SRS), Normal Development of Social Skills from Infants to Junior High School Children (S-M), Gastrointestinal Symptom Rating Scale (GSRS) scores, and fecal microbiome composition. Assessments were performed on day 0 and at weeks 8 and 16. Results Compared with the placebo group, the BF839 group showed significant improvement in the ABC body and object use scores at week 16, which was more pronounced in children with ASD aged bifidobacteria and change in the metabolic function of neuroactive compounds encoded by intestinal microorganisms. Conclusion BF839 significantly and safely improved abnormal behavior and gastrointestinal symptoms in children with ASD.

title: Everyday executive function issues from the perspectives of autistic adolescents and their parents: Theoretical and empirical implications.
authors: Kenny L, Remington A, Pellicano E
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autism researchers have a long-time interest in a set of skills called executive function. These skills include planning, inhibition, and switching between one activity and another. There was a theory that these skills explained the social and thinking difficulties autistic people might have. After years of study into this, the evidence is confusing and contradictory. Autistic people tend to report struggling quite a lot with these skills. Yet, when researchers test these skills, they do not tend to find such big difficulties. In this study, we spoke to 12 autistic teenagers and seven of their mothers about this. We asked them what they thought about their own, or their child's, executive function skills. We wanted to know about things they were good at and things they struggled with. They told us that their skills were very changeable from one context to the next and from one time to the next. According to their reports, their skills depended on how motivated they were by doing the task. Another thing that influenced their skills were how anxious they felt at the time they needed to use the skill. Finally, they told us that sometimes they think differently about how best to perform a task. We discuss what these insights mean for autism researchers who study these skills. In future, research should ask people about their experiences alongside testing their abilities in different contexts. Combining these information sources will give us a better understanding of autistic people's everyday skills as well as how best to support them.

sheet.es: Si tu adolescente autista tiene días en que planificar o cambiar de actividad le resulta fácil y otros en que le cuesta, puede ser normal: estas habilidades varían según el momento y el lugar. Fíjate en cuánto le motiva la tarea y en su nivel de ansiedad, y pregúntale cómo prefiere hacerla. Es un estudio de investigación con 12 adolescentes autistas y siete de sus madres, que contaron sus experiencias. Es una muestra pequeña, con pocas voces, y no sirve como regla para todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If your autistic teenager finds planning or switching activities easy some days and hard on others, that may be quite common: these skills change from one context and moment to the next. Notice how motivated they are by the task and how anxious they feel, and ask how they prefer to do it. This was a research study with 12 autistic teenagers and seven of their mothers, who shared their experiences. The sample is small, with few voices, so it is not a rule for every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om din autistiska tonåring ibland har lätt för att planera eller byta aktivitet och ibland svårt, kan det vara vanligt: förmågorna varierar mellan olika sammanhang och tillfällen. Lägg märke till hur motiverad tonåringen är av uppgiften och hur orolig hen känner sig, och fråga hur hen helst vill göra den. Det var en forskningsstudie med 12 autistiska tonåringar och sju av deras mammor som delade sina erfarenheter. Urvalet är litet och har få röster, så det är ingen regel för alla autistiska personer.

title: Occurrence and predictors of lifetime suicidality and suicidal ideation in autistic adults.
authors: Bentum JV, Sijbrandij M, Huibers M, Begeer S
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Over the past few years, more and more research is showing that many autistic people are at an increased risk for suicide. In this study, we asked participants from the Netherlands Autism Register, which is longitudinal register including individuals with autism, about their possible experiences with thoughts and feelings about suicide. Specifically, we looked at whether these thoughts and feelings in their lifetime and in the past month were related to various factors (such as their age, gender, and having psychiatric disorder diagnoses). We found that 80% of the participants had experienced thoughts about or even attempted to take their own life at least once throughout their lifetime. Furthermore, in a subgroup of participants, we found that the presence of a psychiatric disorder diagnosis, feelings of loneliness, and a higher number of autistic traits were associated with experiencing suicidal thoughts and feelings in their lifetime. For those who experienced these suicidal thoughts in the past month, we found that having (multiple) psychiatric disorder diagnoses and a higher number of autistic traits were related to more severe and frequent thoughts about suicide in the past month. Our findings show that additional factors in autistic individuals should be considered when assessing the suicide risk, and it brings us one step closer to understanding why suicide is more common for autistic people.

title: E-Health Family Interventions for Parents of Children With Autism Aged 0-6 Years: A Scoping Review.
authors: Shang C, Xie W, Zeng J, Osman N, Sun C, Zou M, Wang J, Wu L
abstract: Objective Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder with onset in infancy. Early intervention is critical to improve the prognosis for these children. E-health interventions have tremendous potential. This review aimed to determine the status and effectiveness of family interventions for parents of children aged 0-6 years with ASD in the context of e-health. Methods The review methodology was guided by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews. PubMed, Web of Science, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure were searched from inception to June 2022. The searches were limited to children with ASD of the age range between 0 and 6 years. We collated the available information and used descriptive statistics to analyze the synthesized data. Results Our initial search identified 3,672 articles, of which 30 studies met the inclusion criteria. The 30 articles selected were released between 2012 and 2022. All articles are in English. Most articles reviewed were from high-income countries (27/30, 90.0%), especially from the United States (16/30, 53.3%). Four major themes emerged from the 30 studies that matched the inclusion criteria, as follows: 1) type of e-health interventions, 2) duration of interventions, 3) clinical aspects of e-health interventions, and 4) evidence for intervention effectiveness, looking into the positive, negative, and mixed findings of previous studies. Conclusion These findings suggest that a wide variety of e-health interventions may actually help support both children with ASD aged 0-6 years and their parents.

sheet.es: Si tiene un hijo o hija autista pequeño, las intervenciones familiares en línea (videollamadas, programas web) pueden ser una opción para apoyar a la familia, sobre todo si es difícil acudir a un centro. Puede preguntar a los profesionales qué formatos existen. La evidencia es una revisión de alcance de 30 estudios sobre familias de niños de 0-6 años; los resultados fueron positivos, negativos y mixtos. Casi todos los estudios venían de países de ingresos altos (27/30), y las intervenciones eran muy distintas entre sí, así que no sirve como regla para cada familia.
sheet.en: If you have a young autistic child, online family programmes (video calls, web-based courses) may be one option for supporting your family, especially when getting to a clinic is hard. You can ask professionals which formats are available. The evidence is a scoping review of 30 studies on families of children aged 0-6 years; findings were positive, negative and mixed. Nearly all studies came from high-income countries (27/30), and the interventions varied widely, so this is not a rule for every family.
sheet.sv: Om du har ett litet autistiskt barn kan digitala familjeprogram (videosamtal, webbkurser) vara ett sätt att få stöd, särskilt när det är svårt att ta sig till en mottagning. Du kan fråga yrkespersoner vilka format som finns. Underlaget är en översikt (scoping review) av 30 studier om familjer med barn i åldern 0-6 år; resultaten var positiva, negativa och blandade. Nästan alla studier kom från höginkomstländer (27/30) och insatserna skilde sig mycket åt, så det är ingen regel för varje familj.

title: Effects of different exercise interventions on executive function in children with autism spectrum disorder: a network meta-analysis.
authors: Hou Y, Wang Y, Deng J, Song X
abstract: Background A large body of research has identified the positive effects of physical activity on children with autism spectrum disorders (ASD). However, the specific benefits of different types of sports on executive functioning in children with ASD remain unclear. The aim of this study was to further analyze the effects of different sports on executive functioning in children with ASD using reticulated meta-analysis and to establish their effectiveness ranking. Methods This study conducted a comprehensive online search in Web of Science, PubMed, Cochrane, Embase, and CNKI databases. It included randomized controlled trials and quasi-experimental studies, and synthesized the data using a Bayesian framework. Results Several relevant studies were included. The results showed that physical activity significantly improved all three dimensions of executive functioning (inhibitory control, cognitive flexibility, and working memory) in children with ASD. The improvement in cognitive flexibility and inhibitory control both reached a medium effect size. However, the improvement in inhibitory control was better than that in cognitive flexibility, while the improvement in working memory did not reach the level of a medium effect. Mini Basketball was effective in improving inhibitory control and cognitive flexibility, but not working memory. Ping Pong was more effective in cognitive flexibility and working memory, but weaker in inhibitory control. Fixed Bicycle was less effective in all three dimensions. Among other interventions, Learning Bicycles, Animal-assisted therapy, and Exergaming performed better in cognitive flexibility. SPARK, Neiyang Gong, and Martial Arts were also effective in improving inhibitory control. However, SPARK and Fixed Bicycle were not significant in improving working memory. Conclusion Physical activity as an intervention can significantly improve the executive function of children with ASD. The intervention effects of different sports on different dimensions of executive function vary. Mini Basketball was outstanding in improving inhibitory control and cognitive flexibility. Ping Pong was effective in improving cognitive flexibility and working memory. Fixed Bicycle was not effective in any dimension.

sheet.es: Si quiere probar actividad física con un niño autista, puede elegir deportes de pelota o de raqueta que le resulten agradables y observar cómo responde. Este estudio reunió ensayos previos en un metaanálisis en red, con niños autistas, y sugiere que el movimiento se asocia con mejoras en control inhibitorio, flexibilidad cognitiva y memoria de trabajo. El minibásquet y el pimpón destacaron en algunas áreas; la bicicleta fija, menos. Sus límites: el resumen no indica cuántos niños participaron, los estudios eran distintos y no todos aleatorizados, y los resultados no valen para cada persona. Los gustos y la comodidad del niño importan más que cualquier clasificación.
sheet.en: If you want to try physical activity with an autistic child, you could offer ball or racket games they enjoy and watch how they respond. This network meta-analysis pooled earlier trials with autistic children and suggests movement is linked to improvements in inhibitory control, cognitive flexibility and working memory. Mini basketball and ping pong stood out in some areas; the stationary bike did less. Limits: the abstract does not say how many children took part, the studies differed and not all were randomised, and results do not apply to every person. The child's interests and comfort matter more than any ranking.
sheet.sv: Om du vill prova fysisk aktivitet med ett autistiskt barn kan du erbjuda bollspel eller racketspel som barnet tycker om och se hur det reagerar. Den här nätverksmetaanalysen sammanställde tidigare studier med autistiska barn och tyder på att rörelse hänger ihop med förbättringar i hämmande kontroll, kognitiv flexibilitet och arbetsminne. Minibasket och pingis stack ut inom vissa områden; motionscykel gav mindre. Begränsningar: sammanfattningen anger inte hur många barn som deltog, studierna skilde sig åt och inte alla var randomiserade, och resultaten gäller inte alla. Barnets intressen och trygghet väger tyngre än en rangordning.

title: Study protocol of a randomized control trial on the effectiveness of improvisational music therapy for autistic children.
authors: Jaschke AC, Howlin C, Pool J, Greenberg YD, Atkinson R, Kovalova A, Merriam E, Pallás-Ferrer I, Williams S, Moore C, Hayden K, Allison C, Odell-Miller H, Baron-Cohen S
abstract: Background Music therapy is the clinical use of musical interventions to improve mental and physical health across multiple domains, including social communication. Autistic children, who have difficulties in social communication and often increased anxiety, tend to show a strong preference for music, because it can be structured and systematic, and therefore more predictable than social interaction. This makes music therapy a promising medium for therapeutic support and intervention. Previous clinical trials of music therapy compared to traditional therapy for autistic children have shown encouraging but nevertheless mixed results. Key aims The primary aim is to conduct a randomised controlled trial (RCT) of improvisational music therapy for autistic children and test its effectiveness in at improving social communication and wellbeing, and to reduce anxiety. Research plan The RCT will be conducted with 200 autistic children in the UK aged 7 to 11 years old. Participants will be randomly assigned to either improvisational music therapy or support as usual. The trial will be an assessor-blind, pragmatic two-arm cluster RCT comparing the impact of 12-weeks of improvisational music therapy in addition to support as usual, vs. support as usual for autistic children. Methods Researchers who are blind to which arm the children are in will conduct assessments and obtain data via caregiver reports. The primary outcome will be the absolute change in the total score of the Brief Observation of Social Communication Change (BOSCC) assessed at baseline, T1 (13 weeks) and T2 (39 weeks) follow-ups. The BOSCC consists of specific items that were developed to identify changes in social-communication behaviours. Secondary outcome measures include: (1) Parent reported anxiety scale for youth with ASD (Note that we do not use the term 'ASD' or Autism Spectrum Disorder, because many autistic people feel it is stigmatising. Instead, we use the term 'autism') (PRAS-ASD) (2) Young Child Outcome Rating Scale, for wellbeing (YCORS), (3) Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ); and (4) Vineland Adaptive Behaviour Scale (VABS). (5) The Children's Communication Checklist-2 (CCC-2) will be completed to evaluate pragmatic speech with fluent speakers only; (6) The Music Engagement Scale (MES); and (7) Assessment of the Quality of Relationship (AQR) will be used to evaluate the child-therapist relationships using video-analysis of music therapy sessions. Additional data will be collected by administering the Wechsler Abbreviated Scale of Intelligence (WASI-II), Music at Home Questionnaire (M@H), and children's versions of the Empathy Quotient (EQ) and Systemizing Quotient (SQ). Audio and video data from the therapy sessions will be collected and analysed (using both human and computer-based feature-coding, e.g., machine learning and AI-driven methods) to identify how music and non-musical interactions foster change throughout the therapy. Discussion This study aims to observe if the interactions, engagement, and therapeutic modalities fostered during music therapy sessions can translate to non-musical contexts and improve autistic children's social communication skills, identifying possible mediating factors contributing to the effectiveness of music therapy, potentially informing policy making and governance. Trial registration This randomised control trial is registered with the NIH U.S. National Library of Medicine: https://clinicaltrials.gov/search?term=NCT06016621 , clinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT0601662, Registration Date 19th August 2023.

sheet.es: Si buscas apoyo para tu hija o hijo autista, la música improvisada puede ser una vía a explorar, pero este estudio aún no ofrece resultados. Observa si le atrae la música y si le resulta más predecible que la interacción social. Es el protocolo de un ensayo aleatorizado: describe cómo se probará la musicoterapia improvisada durante 12 semanas, además del apoyo habitual, frente al apoyo habitual solo, con 200 niñas y niños autistas de 7 a 11 años en el Reino Unido. Límites: todavía no sabemos si funciona, y los resultados no valdrán igual para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you are looking for support for your autistic child, improvised music may be worth exploring, but this study does not yet give results. Notice whether they are drawn to music and find it more predictable than social interaction. It is a trial protocol: it describes how improvisational music therapy for 12 weeks, on top of usual support, will be compared with usual support alone, with 200 autistic children aged 7 to 11 in the UK. Limits: we do not yet know whether it works, and results will not apply equally to every person.
sheet.sv: Om du söker stöd till ditt autistiska barn kan improviserad musik vara värd att utforska, men den här studien ger ännu inga resultat. Se om barnet dras till musik och upplever den som mer förutsägbar än social interaktion. Det är ett studieprotokoll för en randomiserad studie: den beskriver hur improviserad musikterapi i 12 veckor, utöver vanligt stöd, ska jämföras med enbart vanligt stöd, med 200 autistiska barn i åldern 7 till 11 år i Storbritannien. Begränsningar: vi vet ännu inte om det fungerar, och resultaten gäller inte lika för alla.

title: Study Protocol for a Cluster, Randomized, Controlled Community Effectiveness Trial of the Early Start Denver Model (ESDM) Compared to Community Early Behavioral Intervention (EBI) in Community Programs serving Young Autistic Children: Partnering for Autism: Learning more to improve Services (PALMS).
authors: Stahmer AC, Dufek S, Rogers SJ, Iosif AM
abstract: Background The rising number of children identified with autism has led to exponential growth in for-profit applied behavior analysis (ABA) agencies and the use of highly structured approaches that may not be developmentally appropriate for young children. Multiple clinical trials support naturalistic developmental behavior interventions (NDBIs) that integrate ABA and developmental science and are considered best practices for young autistic children. The Early Start Denver Model (ESDM) is a comprehensive NDBI shown to improve social communication outcomes for young autistic children in several controlled efficacy studies. However, effectiveness data regarding NDBI use in community-based agencies are limited. Methods This study uses a community-partnered approach to test the effectiveness of ESDM compared to usual early behavioral intervention (EBI) for improving social communication and language in autistic children served by community agencies. This is a hybrid type 1 cluster-randomized controlled trial with 2 conditions: ESDM and EBI. In the intervention group, supervising providers will receive training in ESDM; in the control group, they will continue EBI as usual. We will enroll and randomize 100 supervisors (50 ESDM, 50 EBI) by region. Each supervisor enrolls 3 families of autistic children under age 5 (n = 300) and accompanying behavior technicians (n = 200). The primary outcome is child language and social communication at 6 and 12 months. Secondary outcomes include child adaptive behavior, caregiver use of ESDM strategies, and provider intervention fidelity. Child social motivation and caregiver fidelity will be tested as mediating variables. ESDM implementation determinants will be explored using mixed methods. Discussion This study will contribute novel knowledge on ESDM effectiveness, the variables that mediate and moderate child outcomes, and engagement of its mechanisms in community use. We expect results from this trial to increase community availability of this model and access to high-quality intervention for young autistic children, especially those who depend on publicly funded intervention services. Understanding implementation determinants will aid scale-up of effective models within communities. Trail registration Clinicaltrials.gov identifier number NCT06005285. Registered on August 21, 2023. Protocol version Issue date 6 August 2024; Protocol amendment number: 02.

sheet.es: Si buscas apoyo temprano para un niño autista menor de 5 años, pregunta a los programas qué enfoque usan y si trabajan a través del juego y la relación, con participación de la familia. Este documento es el protocolo de un ensayo aleatorizado, aún sin resultados: compara el Early Start Denver Model con la intervención conductual temprana habitual en programas comunitarios, con 300 niños autistas menores de 5 años y sus familias. Como solo describe el plan, no demuestra todavía que un enfoque sea mejor, ni sirve como regla para cada niño. Tus observaciones sobre cómo responde tu hijo siguen siendo importantes.
sheet.en: If you are looking for early support for an autistic child under age 5, ask programs which approach they use and whether it works through play and relationship, with the family involved. This paper is the protocol for a randomized trial, with no results yet: it compares the Early Start Denver Model with usual early behavioral intervention in community programs, with 300 autistic children under age 5 and their families. Because it only describes the plan, it does not yet show that either approach is better, and it is not a rule for every child. Your own observations of how your child responds still matter.
sheet.sv: Om du söker tidigt stöd för ett autistiskt barn under 5 år kan du fråga verksamheter vilket arbetssätt de använder och om det bygger på lek och relation, med familjen delaktig. Detta är protokollet för en randomiserad studie och resultat saknas ännu: den jämför Early Start Denver Model med vanlig tidig beteendeinriktad insats i kommunala verksamheter, med 300 autistiska barn under 5 år och deras familjer. Eftersom den bara beskriver planen visar den ännu inte att något arbetssätt är bättre, och den är ingen regel för varje barn. Dina egna iakttagelser av hur ditt barn svarar är fortsatt viktiga.

title: A handbook for Rhythmic Relating in autism: supporting social timing in play, learning and therapy.
authors: Daniel S, Laurie M, Delafield-Butt JT
abstract: We present a handbook for Rhythmic Relating, an approach developed to support play, learning and therapy with young autistic children, unconventional communicators, and autistic people who have additional learning needs. Rhythmic Relating is based on the Movement Sensing perspective, a growing body of research that recognizes that autistic social difficulties stem from more basic sensory and motor differences. These sensorimotor differences directly affect embodied experience and social timing in communication. The Rhythmic Relating approach acknowledges that autistic/non-autistic interactive mismatch goes both ways and offers bidirectional support for social timing and expressive action in play. This handbook is presented in an accessible fashion, allowing the reader to develop at their own pace through three skill-levels and encouraging time out to practice. We begin with the basics of building rapport (seeing, copying, and celebrating interactional behaviors), introduce the basic foundations of sensory stability, and then move on to developing reciprocal play (using mirroring, matching, looping, and "Yes…and" techniques), and further to understanding sensory impetus (using sensory contours, accents and flows) and its potential in support of social timing. Rhythmic Relating is offered in support of each practitioner's creative practice and personal sense of fun and humor in play. The model is offered as a foundation for interaction and learning, as a base practice in schools, for Occupational Therapists, Speech Therapists and Physiotherapists, and can also provide a basis for tailoring creative arts therapies when working with autistic clients.

sheet.es: Mañana puede probar a jugar junto a su hijo o hija: observe lo que hace, cópielo con calma y celébrelo, y vaya después hacia el juego por turnos, imitando o añadiendo algo con un «Sí… y». El estudio es un manual que presenta el enfoque Ritmo Relacional (Rhythmic Relating) para el juego, el aprendizaje y la terapia con niños autistas pequeños, personas que se comunican de forma no convencional y personas autistas con otras necesidades de aprendizaje. Parte de la idea de que el desajuste en la interacción es mutuo. Sus límites: el resumen no describe ninguna prueba de resultados, así que no demuestra que funcione y no sirve igual para todas las personas.
sheet.en: Tomorrow you could try playing alongside your child: notice what they do, copy it calmly and celebrate it, then move towards taking turns by mirroring or adding something with a "Yes…and". The study is a handbook presenting the Rhythmic Relating approach for play, learning and therapy with young autistic children, unconventional communicators and autistic people with additional learning needs. It starts from the idea that the interaction mismatch goes both ways. Its limits: the abstract describes no test of results, so it does not show that the approach works, and it will not suit every person in the same way.
sheet.sv: I morgon kan du prova att leka vid sidan av ditt barn: lägg märke till vad barnet gör, härma det lugnt och fira det, och gå sedan mot turtagning genom att spegla eller bygga vidare med ett "Ja… och". Studien är en handbok som presenterar metoden Rhythmic Relating för lek, lärande och terapi med små autistiska barn, personer som kommunicerar okonventionellt och autistiska personer med ytterligare inlärningsbehov. Utgångspunkten är att missförståndet i samspelet går åt båda hållen. Begränsningar: sammanfattningen beskriver ingen prövning av resultat, så den visar inte att metoden fungerar, och den passar inte alla på samma sätt.

title: "I'm Trying to Reach Out, I'm Trying to Find My People": A Mixed-Methods Investigation of the Link Between Sensory Differences, Loneliness, and Mental Health in Autistic and Nonautistic Adults.
authors: Qdtua L, Williams G, Mulcahy J, Larsson DEO, Silva M, Arnold AJ, Critchley HD, Garfinkel SN
abstract: Background Rates of loneliness are substantially higher among autistic compared with nonautistic individuals. This observation refutes the persistent stereotype that autistic individuals are not motivated to seek meaningful social relationships. More plausibly, social environments systematically exclude people with higher levels of sensory differences, impeding on opportunities for autistic individuals to form meaningful relationships. In this study, we sought to quantify the level of distress associated with loneliness (Study A) and provide complementary qualitative insight into experiences of loneliness in relationship to sensory differences in autistic adults (Study B). Methods In Study A, N = 209 participants completed a range of self-report questionnaires. In Study B, nine autistic adults took part in 10-minute unstructured dyadic conversations around the topic of loneliness. We derived a qualitative understanding of autistic individuals' experience of loneliness, enriched by inductive and deductive analyses. Results In Study A, the autistic group showed significantly higher levels of loneliness, loneliness distress, anxiety, depression, and sensory reactivity. We found significant positive correlations between variables, but no group differences in differential relationships. The effect of sensory reactivity on anxiety and depression was mediated by levels of loneliness in both groups. In Study B, autistic participants described the pain of feeling lonely and socially disconnected, while simultaneously experiencing a need for restorative solitude after social overstimulation. Discussion Our results indicate that sensory differences are related with higher loneliness and associated poor mental health in both autistic and nonautistic adults. This effect was exacerbated in autistic adults due to higher levels of sensory reactivity. First-hand reports from autistic adults on intense loneliness and the obstructive role of sensory environments refute stereotypes about a lack of social motivation in autistic adults. We conclude that to enable meaningful and inclusive social interaction, a societal effort is needed to create spaces that consider the sensory needs of all neurotypes.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista se siente sola, no asuma que no quiere compañía. Puede ayudar buscar espacios sociales con menos ruido, luz o bullicio, y respetar el tiempo a solas para recuperarse después. La evidencia: un estudio con métodos mixtos en adultos autistas y no autistas; N = 209 respondieron cuestionarios y nueve adultos autistas conversaron sobre la soledad. Los adultos autistas indicaron más soledad, ansiedad, depresión y reactividad sensorial, y la soledad medió la relación entre lo sensorial y la salud mental. Límites: es un estudio pequeño, solo con adultos, y no muestra qué le ocurre a cada persona ni prueba causas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person feels lonely, don't assume they don't want company. It may help to look for social settings with less noise, light or crowding, and to respect time alone to recover afterwards. The evidence: a mixed-methods study of autistic and nonautistic adults; N = 209 completed questionnaires and nine autistic adults talked about loneliness. Autistic adults reported more loneliness, anxiety, depression and sensory reactivity, and loneliness mediated the link between sensory differences and mental health. Limits: the study is small, covers only adults, cannot show what is true for each person, and does not prove causes.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person känner sig ensam, anta inte att hen saknar lust till sällskap. Det kan hjälpa att välja sociala miljöer med mindre buller, ljus eller trängsel och att respektera tid ensam för att återhämta sig efteråt. Evidensen: en studie med blandade metoder på autistiska och icke-autistiska vuxna; N = 209 fyllde i enkäter och nio autistiska vuxna samtalade om ensamhet. De autistiska vuxna rapporterade mer ensamhet, ångest, depression och sensorisk reaktivitet, och ensamheten förmedlade sambandet mellan sensoriska skillnader och psykisk hälsa. Begränsningar: studien är liten, omfattar bara vuxna, visar inte vad som gäller varje person och bevisar inte orsaker.

title: "I have to charge my social battery": Perspectives from autistic young adults on Quality of Life.
authors: Øverland E, Hauge ÅL, Orm S, Øie MG, Skogli EW, Pellicano E, Andersen PN
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract In this study we have asked a group of autistic young adults to describe what is important for their quality of life. The 14 participants (aged 21-29 years) were recruited from a 10-year follow-up study of autistic people. During interviews, our participants described the importance of having relationships with family, friends and pets. Having meaningful activities and being able to immerse themselves in particular interests was also reported to be important for a good quality of life. Interests had also guided their choice of what to study and what to do for work. They also spoke of how communication problems with professionals, bullying and sensory and emotional overload could have a negative impact on quality of life. Future interventions should focus on how professionals can help autistic people to connect to people/animals and meaningful activities, as the participants described this as important for having a good quality of life. These findings may be helpful in enhancing how passions and interests can be seen as opportunities for both academic and work careers for autistic people. Future research and interventions should also look at the communication barriers between autistic people and professionals, and how two-way understanding can be improved.

sheet.es: Mañana puedes preguntar a la persona autista qué relaciones y actividades le dan más bienestar, y protegerlas: tiempo con familia, amigos o mascotas, y espacio para sus intereses. También ayuda reducir la sobrecarga sensorial y emocional y apoyar la comunicación con profesionales. La evidencia es un estudio con entrevistas a 14 jóvenes autistas de 21-29 años, que formaban parte de un seguimiento de 10 años. Es un grupo pequeño y sus experiencias no representan a todas las personas autistas, así que lo mejor es preguntar a cada persona.
sheet.en: Tomorrow you can ask the autistic person which relationships and activities matter most to their wellbeing, and protect them: time with family, friends or pets, and room for their interests. It also helps to reduce sensory and emotional overload and to support communication with professionals. The evidence is an interview study with 14 autistic young adults aged 21-29, who were part of a 10-year follow-up study. It is a small group and their experiences do not represent every autistic person, so it is best to ask each person.
sheet.sv: I morgon kan du fråga den autistiska personen vilka relationer och aktiviteter som betyder mest för välbefinnandet, och skydda dem: tid med familj, vänner eller husdjur, och utrymme för intressen. Det hjälper också att minska sensorisk och känslomässig överbelastning och stödja kommunikationen med yrkespersoner. Underlaget är en intervjustudie med 14 autistiska unga vuxna i åldern 21-29 år, som ingick i en 10 år lång uppföljningsstudie. Gruppen är liten och deras erfarenheter gäller inte alla autistiska personer, så det bästa är att fråga varje person.

title: How are Autistic People Involved in the Design of Extended Reality Technologies? A Systematic Literature Review.
authors: Newbutt N, Glaser N, Francois MS, Schmidt M, Cobb S
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: The primary aim of this systematic review is to investigate the inclusion of autistic individuals in the design process of immersive technologies. This study follows the preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses standards for systematic literature reviews. To ensure the research questions and subsequent stages of the review incorporate pertinent parameters, the problem, interest, context framework has also been employed. Findings highlight that, while early proponents of immersive technology emphasized the importance of user involvement in design of new technology, immaturity of the technology often limited the implementation of direct user input to the design process. Nonetheless, analysis of the literature published between 2002-2022 identified 20 studies in which substantial influence of autistic individuals and stakeholders was found in the design process of immersive technologies. The roles of autistic individuals varied from active co-designers and co-creators to essential contributors in refining prototypes and providing critical feedback, ensuring the final products align with their needs and preferences. Results underscore the need to align research and design of immersive technologies more closely with the priorities and preferences of autistic individuals. Further is needed regarding actively involving autistic individuals in the design and implementation of immersive technology applications. On this basis, we maintain that more inclusive and effective deployment of immersive technologies is needed in order to ensure that resultant technologies are fit for purpose and address the actual needs of the autistic community.

sheet.es: Si te ofrecen una aplicación o programa de realidad virtual o aumentada para tu hijo o hija autista, puedes preguntar: ¿participaron personas autistas en su diseño? Mañana, pruébalo juntos con calma, observa su comodidad (sonidos, luces, casco) y deja que su opinión guíe si seguir o no. Su experiencia es información valiosa. Esta revisión sistemática analizó estudios publicados entre 2002 y 2022 y encontró solo 20 en los que personas autistas influyeron de verdad en el diseño, como co-diseñadoras o probando prototipos. Limitación: describe cómo se diseñan estas tecnologías, no demuestra que funcionen ni que sirvan para cada persona.
sheet.en: If you are offered a virtual or augmented reality app or program for your autistic child, it is fair to ask: were autistic people involved in designing it? Tomorrow, try it together calmly, notice their comfort (sounds, lights, headset) and let their feedback guide whether to continue. Their experience is valuable information. This systematic review looked at studies published between 2002 and 2022 and found only 20 where autistic people had real influence on design, as co-designers or by testing prototypes. Limitation: it describes how these technologies are designed, not whether they work or suit every person.
sheet.sv: Om du erbjuds en app eller ett program med virtuell eller förstärkt verklighet för ditt autistiska barn kan du fråga: var autistiska personer med och utformade det? I morgon kan ni prova tillsammans i lugn takt, lägga märke till hur bekvämt det känns (ljud, ljus, headset) och låta barnets åsikt avgöra om ni fortsätter. Deras upplevelse är värdefull information. Denna systematiska översikt granskade studier publicerade 2002–2022 och fann bara 20 där autistiska personer verkligen påverkade designen, som meddesigners eller genom att testa prototyper. Begränsning: den beskriver hur tekniken utformas, inte om den fungerar eller passar alla.

title: Increasing Face Mask Wearing in Autistic Individuals Using Behavior Analytic Interventions: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
authors: Cowell R, Vostanis A, Langdon PE
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: The current review aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of behavior-analytic procedures in increasing face mask-wearing in autistic individuals. This comes following recommended guidance during the COVID-19 pandemic. A systematic review and meta-analysis were completed of peer-reviewed and grey literature. Six databases were searched and seven studies using single-case experimental designs met the eligibility criteria which were then quality appraised. Data were extracted on participant characteristics, study design, independent and dependent variables, fidelity, generalization, maintenance, and social validity outcomes. Both the non-overlap of all pairs and Baseline Corrected TAU were used to estimate effect size. Two studies were rated strong and borderline strong quality and five were rated as adequate or below. All studies showed positive outcomes for mask-wearing, with an average of 0.92 for non-overlap of all pairs and 0.47 for Baseline Corrected Tau effect sizes. The most common and effective procedures for increasing mask-wearing were graded exposure and differential and positive reinforcement. Factors such as mode of delivery, implementer, and setting did not appear to influence study outcomes. Procedures were found to be rated as acceptable by parents and professionals in five of the studies. The existing literature on increasing face mask-wearing in autistic individuals provides promising findings to add to existing literature around increasing tolerance to medical equipment and hygiene practices in autistic populations. However, these findings are based on a small sample size, with six of the studies taking place in the United States with varying study quality.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista necesita llevar mascarilla, probar una introducción gradual y reforzar con algo que le guste cada pequeño paso puede ayudar, a su ritmo y sin forzarla. Esta revisión sistemática con metaanálisis reunió siete estudios de diseño de caso único sobre procedimientos conductuales; los más habituales y eficaces fueron la exposición gradual y el refuerzo diferencial y positivo. Todos mostraron resultados positivos, y padres y profesionales valoraron los procedimientos como aceptables en cinco estudios. Sus límites: muestra pequeña, seis estudios hechos en Estados Unidos y calidad desigual, así que no sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person needs to wear a face mask, introducing it gradually and rewarding each small step with something they enjoy may help, at their own pace and without pressure. This systematic review and meta-analysis pooled seven single-case experimental studies of behavior-analytic procedures; the most common and effective were graded exposure and differential and positive reinforcement. All studies showed positive outcomes, and parents and professionals rated the procedures acceptable in five studies. Limits: the sample was small, six studies took place in the United States, and quality varied, so it is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person behöver bära munskydd kan det hjälpa att introducera det stegvis och belöna varje litet steg med något hen tycker om, i hens egen takt och utan tvång. Denna systematiska översikt och metaanalys sammanställde sju singelfallsstudier om beteendeanalytiska metoder; de vanligaste och mest effektiva var gradvis exponering samt differentiell och positiv förstärkning. Alla studier visade positiva resultat, och föräldrar och yrkespersoner bedömde metoderna som acceptabla i fem studier. Begränsningar: litet underlag, sex studier genomfördes i USA och kvaliteten varierade, så det är ingen regel för alla.

title: A Pilot Randomised Control Trial Exploring the Feasibility and Acceptability of Delivering a Personalised Modular Psychological Intervention for Anxiety Experienced by Autistic Adults: Personalised Anxiety Treatment-Autism (PAT-A).
authors: Rodgers J, Brice S, Welsh P, Ingham B, Wilson C, Evans G, Steele K, Cropper E, Le Couteur A, Freeston M, Parr JR
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Anxiety is commonly experienced by autistic people and impacts on quality of life and social participation. New anxiety interventions are required to effectively meet the needs of autistic people. Personalised Anxiety Treatment-Autism (PAT-A©) is a bespoke, modular approach to treating anxiety in up to 12 sessions. This study explored the feasibility and acceptability of delivering PAT-A© in the UK National Health Service (NHS). A single-blind randomised controlled trial design. Thirty-four autistic adults were recruited via clinical services and randomised to receive either PAT-A© or enhanced treatment as usual (CCSP). Outcome assessments relating to anxiety, quality of life and related constructs were completed at baseline, immediately post intervention; and at 3 and 12 months. Seventy-one percent of the PAT-A© group and 65% of the CCSP met diagnostic threshold for at least three anxiety disorders. Retention was good across both groups, with 82% (N = 14/17) completing the full course of PAT-A© and 71% (N = 12/17) attending both psychoeducational sessions in CCSP. 94% in PAT-A© and 82% in CCSP completed some follow up assessment 3 months post-intervention. Thematic analysis of interview data revealed that many participants valued the personalised approach, developed transferable skills and experienced positive changes to their anxiety. Participants were willing to be recruited and randomised, PAT-A© was feasible to deliver in the NHS and the trial methods and materials were acceptable. Our findings indicate that a fully powered clinical and cost-effectiveness trial of PAT-A© is warranted.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta vive con ansiedad, puede ser útil preguntar a su servicio de salud por terapias psicológicas personalizadas, adaptadas a lo que cada persona necesita. Este ensayo piloto aleatorizado incluyó a 34 adultos autistas en el sistema de salud británico (NHS) y comparó PAT-A, un enfoque modular de hasta 12 sesiones, con un tratamiento habitual reforzado. 82% (N = 14/17) completó todo PAT-A, y muchas personas valoraron el enfoque personalizado y dijeron haber aprendido habilidades útiles en otros contextos. Límites: es un estudio pequeño, pensado para ver si es viable y aceptable, no para demostrar que funciona mejor; hace falta un ensayo mayor. Cualquier decisión sobre tratamiento se comenta con un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult lives with anxiety, it may help to ask their health service about personalised psychological therapy that is shaped around what that person needs. This pilot randomised trial included 34 autistic adults in the UK National Health Service (NHS) and compared PAT-A, a modular approach of up to 12 sessions, with enhanced treatment as usual. 82% (N = 14/17) completed the full course of PAT-A, and many participants valued the personalised approach and said they gained skills they could use elsewhere. Limits: it is a small study designed to test feasibility and acceptability, not to prove it works better; a larger trial is needed. Any treatment decision is best discussed with a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen lever med ångest kan det vara värt att fråga vården om personanpassad psykologisk behandling som utgår från just den personens behov. Denna lilla randomiserade pilotstudie inkluderade 34 autistiska vuxna inom den brittiska hälso- och sjukvården (NHS) och jämförde PAT-A, ett modulärt upplägg på upp till 12 sessioner, med förstärkt vanlig behandling. 82% (N = 14/17) genomförde hela PAT-A, och många uppskattade det personanpassade arbetssättet och sa att de lärt sig färdigheter som gick att använda i andra sammanhang. Begränsningar: studien är liten och avsedd att pröva genomförbarhet och acceptans, inte att visa att metoden är bättre; en större studie behövs. Beslut om behandling tas tillsammans med en kliniker.

title: Socialization, Education, and Learning for the Internet (SELFI): A Pilot RCT of a Social Media Skills Group Program for Autistic Adults.
authors: Osuna A, Sabini K, Yamane E, Flores J, Pierce N, Lemus-Valle J, Vernon T
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Many autistic adults report preference for computer-mediated communication and social media use. Despite many benefits to online socialization, there are many challenges including anxiety and cyber-victimization. To date, support is limited related to helping autistic adults with safe and effective internet use. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary efficacy of the novel SELFI program. This pilot study utilized a randomized controlled trial design. A total of 25 autistic adults enrolled in the study and were randomized to the nine-week SELFI program or a waitlist control condition. Feasibility assessed enrollment, attrition, and fidelity of delivery. Acceptability examined attendance and feedback from participants and peer mentors. Efficacy evaluated change in Facebook activity, social media utility/anxiety, and individualized goals. Regarding feasibility, the recruitment goal was met within one month, there was limited attrition, and therapists delivered the program with high fidelity. Participants attended a majority of scheduled sessions and feedback from participants reflected high levels of agreement with several facets of the program. Compared to the control group, more participants assigned to the SELFI condition were perceived by autistic and non-autistic raters as having improved Facebook activity. SELFI participants also reported reduced difficulty meeting their individualized goal. Findings support the piloted SELFI program as feasible and acceptable with signals of preliminary efficacy. This study establishes an exciting foundation regarding an innovative social media skills program, however more research is necessary.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta quiere usar las redes sociales con más seguridad y confianza, un programa grupal con objetivos individuales puede ser una opción que vale la pena explorar. Podéis preguntar qué metas le importan a ella. Es un ensayo piloto aleatorizado: 25 adultos autistas fueron asignados al programa SELFI de nueve semanas o a una lista de espera. Quienes hicieron el programa mostraron más mejoría en su actividad en Facebook y menos dificultad para lograr su meta personal. Es un estudio pequeño y preliminar, así que no demuestra que funcione para todas las personas; se necesita más investigación.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult wants to use social media more safely and confidently, a group program built around personal goals may be worth exploring. You could start by asking which goals matter to them. This was a pilot randomized trial: 25 autistic adults were assigned to the nine-week SELFI program or to a waitlist. More people in the program were seen as improving their Facebook activity, and they reported less difficulty reaching their own goal. It is a small, early study, so it does not show the program works for everyone; more research is needed.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen vill använda sociala medier tryggare och med mer självförtroende kan ett gruppprogram utifrån personliga mål vara värt att undersöka. Du kan börja med att fråga vilka mål som är viktiga för personen. Det här var en randomiserad pilotstudie: 25 autistiska vuxna lottades till det nio veckor långa programmet SELFI eller till väntelista. Fler i programmet bedömdes ha förbättrad Facebook-aktivitet, och de upplevde mindre svårigheter att nå sitt eget mål. Studien är liten och tidig, så den visar inte att programmet fungerar för alla; mer forskning behövs.

title: Measurement invariance of the parent-reported Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire in autistic adolescents.
authors: Turcan C, Delamain H, Loke A, Pender R, Mandy W, Saunders R
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic people are more likely than non-autistic people to experience mental health difficulties. The Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire is often used to screen for these difficulties and to otherwise make important decisions about mental health treatment and research in populations of autistic people. However, this study suggests that parent-reported Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire scores may not be useful for comparing autistic and non-autistic adolescents at 11, 14 and 17 years old, as well as screening for mental health conditions in autistic adolescents. In addition, several items may be more likely to be endorsed by parents of autistic 17-year-olds than by parents of non-autistic 17-year-olds (and vice versa), which might suggest caution is needed when comparing groups on specific items.

sheet.es: Si le entregan un cuestionario de fortalezas y dificultades (SDQ) para rellenar sobre su hijo o hija autista, tome el resultado con cautela: conviene hablar de lo que usted observa y de cómo se siente la persona, y no basarse solo en la puntuación. La evidencia es un estudio de investigación sobre el cuestionario respondido por familias de adolescentes autistas y no autistas de 11, 14 y 17 años. Sugiere que estas puntuaciones quizá no sirvan para comparar a ambos grupos ni para detectar problemas de salud mental en adolescentes autistas. Es un solo estudio y no dice qué le pasa a cada persona.
sheet.en: If you are asked to fill in a Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ) about your autistic teenager, treat the score with caution: talk about what you observe and how they feel, rather than relying on the number alone. The evidence is a research study of this questionnaire completed by parents of autistic and non-autistic adolescents aged 11, 14 and 17. It suggests these scores may not be useful for comparing the two groups or for screening for mental health conditions in autistic adolescents. It is a single study and cannot tell you what is true for any one person.
sheet.sv: Om du ombeds fylla i ett frågeformulär om styrkor och svårigheter (SDQ) om din autistiska tonåring, ta resultatet med försiktighet: prata om vad du ser och hur tonåringen mår i stället för att lita enbart på poängen. Underlaget är en forskningsstudie av formuläret ifyllt av föräldrar till autistiska och icke-autistiska tonåringar som var 11, 14 och 17 år. Den tyder på att poängen kanske inte går att använda för att jämföra grupperna eller för att screena för psykisk ohälsa hos autistiska tonåringar. Det är en enda studie och säger inte vad som gäller för en enskild person.

title: Video Training and Telepractice for Parents of Nonverbal Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder: a Randomized Control Trial.
authors: Rezai H, Dadgar H, Kasaeian A
journal: Medical journal of the Islamic Republic of Iran
abstract: Background Many children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) are unable to benefit from timely interventions. This research aimed to indirectly enhance play and communication skills in ASD children by providing a video educational package and distance education for their parents. Methods In this clinical trial study, 32 parents and their children with ASD were randomly assigned to either the intervention or waitlist control groups. The intervention group received an educational video package along with 24 one-hour online sessions. The frequency of communication, engagement in functional games, and the use of conventional and unconventional gestures were assessed before, immediately after, and 3 months following the completion of the intervention in the participating children. The variables were analyzed within and between the two groups using a mixed between-within-subjects analysis of variance (ANOVA). Results The intervention group achieved significantly higher scores than the control group in the frequency of communication ( P = 0.003), functional play ( P P P Conclusion The observed improvements in both parents and children within the intervention group provide compelling support for the effectiveness of telepractice in speech therapy. This suggests that incorporating remote training methods into speech therapy sessions could enhance access for children with ASD to these interventions.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija autista no usa el habla, la formación en vídeo para madres y padres, junto con sesiones en línea, puede ser una vía para practicar el juego y la comunicación en casa, sobre todo si es difícil acudir a terapia presencial. Es un ensayo aleatorizado con 32 madres o padres y sus hijos autistas, comparados con un grupo en lista de espera. El grupo con formación mostró más comunicación y juego funcional. Es un estudio pequeño, y no demuestra que funcione igual para todas las familias. Conviene comentarlo con el equipo profesional.
sheet.en: If your autistic child doesn't use speech, video training for parents plus online sessions may be a way to practise play and communication at home, especially when in-person therapy is hard to reach. This was a randomized trial with 32 parents and their autistic children, compared with a waitlist group. The trained group showed more communication and functional play. It is a small study and does not show the approach works the same way for every family. It is worth discussing with your professional team.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn inte använder tal kan videoutbildning för föräldrar tillsammans med digitala sessioner vara ett sätt att öva lek och kommunikation hemma, särskilt när det är svårt att komma till träffar på plats. Det var en randomiserad studie med 32 föräldrar och deras autistiska barn, jämförda med en väntelistegrupp. Gruppen som fick utbildningen visade mer kommunikation och funktionell lek. Studien är liten och visar inte att det fungerar likadant för alla familjer. Ta gärna upp det med ert professionella team.

title: Bringing the autistic lifeworld to supportive technology design: an enactive approach.
authors: van Huizen JC, van Dijk J, Staal WG, van der Voort MC
journal: CoDesign : international journal of cocreation in design and the arts
abstract: Supportive technologies for autistic individuals are promising in principle, yet their uptake remains limited. Critics argue that in current designs of supportive technologies, autism is mostly framed as a 'disorder' whose limitations can be pragmatically compensated for. To increase uptake, designers should get a better handle on how to incorporate the full richness of the autistic experience into the design process. This paper presents an integrative framework of the autistic lifeworld, called Autistic Lifeworld Design (hereafter: ALD). ALD evolved in a transdisciplinary research setting, substantiated by 11 design case studies with autistic young adults as well as theoretical inquiries into enactivism, design and autism. It consists of four dimensions of experience - sensory , habitual , social , and affective -, each providing specific pointers on how to better understand how autistic people experience the world and how supportive technologies may complement that experience. By adopting an enactive approach, ALD enables a reframing of supportive technology as helping to sustain different levels of homoeostasis. It offers a novel lens that allows designers to put the lived experiences of autistic individuals at the centre of the design process, with special attention to the role of bodily structures and processing in shaping these experiences.

sheet.es: Si estás pensando en una app o un dispositivo de apoyo, empieza por preguntar a la persona autista cómo vive el mundo: lo sensorial, los hábitos, lo social y lo emocional. Ese es el enfoque que propone este estudio. Se basó en 11 estudios de caso de diseño con jóvenes autistas y en trabajo teórico sobre diseño y autismo. Es un marco para diseñadores, no prueba que una tecnología concreta funcione, y no sirve igual para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you are considering an app or device for support, start by asking the autistic person how they experience the world: sensory, habitual, social and emotional aspects. That is the approach this study proposes. It drew on 11 design case studies with autistic young adults, plus theoretical work on design and autism. It is a framework for designers, not proof that any particular technology works, and it will not fit every person in the same way.
sheet.sv: Om du funderar på en app eller ett stöd som teknik, börja med att fråga den autistiska personen hur hen upplever världen: sinnesintryck, vanor, socialt och känslomässigt. Det är angreppssättet i den här studien. Den bygger på 11 designfallstudier med autistiska unga vuxna samt teoretiskt arbete om design och autism. Det är ett ramverk för designers, inte ett bevis för att en viss teknik fungerar, och det passar inte alla på samma sätt.

title: Association of self-harm and suicidality with psychiatric co-occurring conditions in autistic individuals: a systematic review and pooled analysis.
authors: Kim JH, Lee J, Shim S, Cheon KA
abstract: Background Autistic individuals frequently experience psychiatric co-occurring conditions, but the association with self-harm/suicidality according to these conditions was not yet elucidated. We aimed to summarize the association between self-harm/suicidality and psychiatric co-occurring conditions in autistic people. Methods We systematically searched PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews until June 4, 2024 (PROSPERO registration number: CRD42023412860). Observational studies were included that provided information to calculate the odds ratio (OR) regarding the association between self-harm/suicidality and psychiatric co-occurring conditions in autistic individuals. We summarized the identified associations by presenting OR range or meta-analyzing when 7 or more estimates are available. Findings The systematic search found 20 eligible studies with 301,841 participants. Our findings suggested that autistic individuals with any psychiatric disorder ( k = 1; OR 3.55; 95% CI 1.27-9.98), ADHD ( k = 3; OR range: 1.07-1.65), or mood disorder ( k = 1; OR 1.26; 95% CI 1.05-1.51) may be associated with higher odds of self-harm than those without these conditions. We identified potential positive associations between suicidality and the following co-occurring conditions: any psychiatric disorder ( k = 1; OR 11.65; 95% CI 10.68-12.71), psychotic disorder ( k = 4; OR range: 1.95-10.97), mood disorder ( k = 3; OR range: 1.75-9.82), bipolar disorder ( k = 2; OR range: 2.55-4.95), depressive disorder ( k = 10; pooled OR 2.29; 95% CI 1.39-3.77), trauma- and stress-related disorder ( k = 2; OR range: 1.28-10.47), and adjustment disorder ( k = 1; OR 3.52; 95% CI 2.89-4.28). Interpretation We found psychiatric co-occurring conditions that may be associated with higher odds of self-harm/suicidality in autistic individuals. However, our findings should be interpreted with caution considering the limited number of included studies. We suggested that clinicians should remain vigilant for autistic individuals with psychiatric co-occurring conditions for their potentially higher likelihood of self-harm and suicidality. Funding This research was supported by a grant of the R&D project, funded by the National Center for Mental Health (grant number: MHER22A01).

sheet.es: Si una persona autista también tiene depresión, TDAH u otras condiciones psiquiátricas, conviene prestar más atención a su bienestar emocional y hablar abiertamente con ella sobre cómo se siente. Es una revisión sistemática de 20 estudios observacionales con 301,841 participantes autistas. Encontró asociaciones posibles entre esas condiciones y más autolesiones o suicidalidad, por ejemplo con el trastorno depresivo (OR combinado 2.29). Los autores piden cautela: hay pocos estudios por condición y una asociación no significa que una cosa cause la otra ni que le ocurra a cada persona. Si te preocupa a alguien, consulta con un profesional clínico, un servicio de salud o un servicio de crisis; en peligro inmediato, llama al número de emergencias de tu país.
sheet.en: If an autistic person also has depression, ADHD or another psychiatric condition, it is worth paying closer attention to their emotional wellbeing and talking openly with them about how they feel. This is a systematic review of 20 observational studies with 301,841 autistic participants. It found possible associations between these conditions and more self-harm or suicidality, for example with depressive disorder (pooled OR 2.29). The authors urge caution: there were few studies per condition, and an association does not mean one thing causes the other or that it applies to every person. If you are worried about someone, contact a clinician, a health service or a crisis service; in immediate danger, call your country's emergency number.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person också har depression, ADHD eller annat psykiatriskt tillstånd är det värt att vara extra uppmärksam på hens känslomässiga mående och prata öppet om hur hen har det. Detta är en systematisk översikt av 20 observationsstudier med 301,841 autistiska deltagare. Den fann möjliga samband mellan dessa tillstånd och mer självskada eller suicidalitet, till exempel vid depressiv sjukdom (sammanvägd OR 2.29). Författarna manar till försiktighet: det fanns få studier per tillstånd, och ett samband betyder inte att det ena orsakar det andra eller att det gäller alla. Om du oroar dig för någon, kontakta en läkare, sjukvården eller en krisjour; vid akut fara, ring ditt lands nödnummer.

title: Effects of Mozart-Orff parent-child music therapy among mothers and their preschool children with autism spectrum disorder: A mixed-methods randomised controlled trial.
authors: He Y, Wong A, Zhang Y, Lin J, Li H, Zhao B, Chen T, Huang S, Hu R, Liu G
abstract: Background Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) negatively impacts mental health, particularly in mothers of autistic children who experience heightened stress. Applied behaviour analysis (ABA) and music therapy are recognised interventions for improving ASD symptoms. However, the specific benefits of parent-child music therapy and ABA for autistic children and their mothers remain uncertain. This study evaluated the effects of parent-child music therapy on preschool autistic children and their mothers. Method A randomised controlled trial was conducted with 100 mother-child pairs assigned to either the control group receiving ABA or the intervention group receiving both music therapy and ABA. Qualitative interviews were conducted post-intervention for 12 mothers. Results Children in the intervention group exhibited lower scores for ASD symptoms than those in the control group. Moreover, mothers in the intervention group demonstrated reduced dysfunctional parent-child interaction, lower overall parental stress, significantly improved family functioning, and increased levels of hope compared with those in the control group. Mothers held positive views regarding music therapy. Conclusions Combining ABA with parent-child music therapy can alleviate ASD symptoms in children and reduce stress in mothers. Improved parent-child interaction and enhanced family functioning further support the benefits of this combined approach. Parent-child music therapy, combined with ABA demonstrated positive outcomes for autistic children, including reduced ASD symptoms, improved parent-child interaction, decreased parental stress, enhanced family functioning, and increased hope. These findings highlight the potential of incorporating music therapy as a valuable component in the comprehensive treatment of ASD. Trial registration This study was registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial registry (05/07/2021, ChiCTR2100048261, https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=128957 ). Ethical approval was obtained from the Research Ethics Committee of Fujian Medical University and the study hospital (Fujian Provincial Maternity and Child Health Hospital; 2017 - 105), and informed consent was obtained from all subjects and/or their legal guardian(s).

sheet.es: Si criáis a un niño autista en edad preescolar, la música compartida entre madre e hijo puede ser una actividad a considerar, además de otros apoyos. En este ensayo aleatorizado participaron 100 parejas de madre e hijo: un grupo recibió ABA y el otro, ABA más musicoterapia entre padres e hijos. El segundo grupo tuvo menos puntuaciones de síntomas de autismo, menos estrés materno, mejor funcionamiento familiar y más esperanza. Las madres entrevistadas valoraron bien la musicoterapia. Límites: solo hubo madres, el estudio se hizo en un contexto concreto, las entrevistas fueron a 12 madres y los resultados no valen para todas las familias. Conviene hablarlo con el equipo profesional.
sheet.en: If you are raising an autistic preschooler, shared music between mother and child may be one activity worth considering alongside other supports. In this randomised trial, 100 mother-child pairs took part: one group received ABA, the other ABA plus parent-child music therapy. The second group had lower autism symptom scores, less maternal stress, better family functioning and more hope. Mothers who were interviewed spoke positively about the music therapy. Limits: only mothers took part, it was set in one context, interviews covered 12 mothers, and results do not apply to every family. It is worth discussing with your professional team.
sheet.sv: Om du har ett autistiskt förskolebarn kan gemensam musik mellan mamma och barn vara en aktivitet att överväga vid sidan av andra stöd. I denna randomiserade studie deltog 100 par av mor och barn: en grupp fick ABA, den andra ABA plus musikterapi för förälder och barn. Den andra gruppen hade lägre poäng för autismsymtom, mindre stress hos mammorna, bättre familjefunktion och mer hopp. Mammorna som intervjuades var positiva till musikterapin. Begränsningar: bara mammor deltog, studien gjordes i en särskild miljö, intervjuerna gällde 12 mammor och resultaten gäller inte alla familjer. Det kan vara bra att prata om det med ert professionella team.

title: Social media shaping autism perception and identity.
authors: Skafle I, Gabarron E, Nordahl-Hansen A
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract This study suggested that social media can provide important information about autism to autistic people. We interviewed 12 autistic adults (aged 18-49 years) and talked to them about the use of social media to find both general information and content specifically about autism, autism identity and online autistic communities. There is little research exploring how autistic people find information about autism on social media and how that makes them feel. Therefore, it is important to ask autistic people about their experiences with using social media to obtain content about autism. The 12 participants explained that when they searched for information about autism on the official health pages, they often felt that the information they found was insufficient and could not answer their questions. In addition, they searched on social media platforms for information about autism despite that they perceived social media as an unreliable source. On the social media platforms, many found content that was positive in relation to their autistic identities. The participants also found comfort in some of the forums and social media groups and received helpful advice. Nevertheless, some of the discussions were aggressive and the participants felt alienated, which did not provide a sense of community online. The findings from the study may advice on what is missing in the official pages about autism, and highlight the need to involve the autistic community in writing the content on such platforms.

sheet.es: Si buscas información sobre el autismo, social media puede ser un complemento útil, pero conviene mirarla con ojo crítico. Puedes ayudar a explorar grupos y foros, y hablar después de cómo se siente esa persona con lo que lee. Es un estudio con entrevistas a 12 adultos autistas (18-49 años). Contaron que las páginas oficiales de salud les parecían insuficientes, y que en redes encontraron contenido positivo sobre su identidad, consejos y consuelo, aunque también discusiones agresivas que les hicieron sentir ajenos. Con tan pocas personas adultas, los resultados no valen para todas las personas autistas ni para niños o adolescentes.
sheet.en: If someone is looking for information about autism, social media can be a useful addition, but it helps to read it critically. You can offer to explore groups and forums together, then talk about how the content makes them feel. This was an interview study with 12 autistic adults (aged 18-49). They found official health pages insufficient, and on social media they found identity-affirming content, advice and comfort, but also aggressive discussions that left them feeling alienated. With so few adults, the findings cannot be applied to every autistic person, nor to children or teenagers.
sheet.sv: Om någon söker information om autism kan sociala medier vara ett användbart komplement, men det hjälper att läsa kritiskt. Du kan erbjuda dig att utforska grupper och forum tillsammans och sedan prata om hur innehållet känns. Detta är en intervjustudie med 12 autistiska vuxna (18-49 år). De tyckte att officiella hälsosidor var otillräckliga, och på sociala medier fann de innehåll som stärkte identiteten, råd och tröst, men också aggressiva diskussioner som fick dem att känna utanförskap. Med så få vuxna gäller resultaten inte alla autistiska personer, och inte barn eller tonåringar.

title: Career progression for autistic people: A scoping review.
authors: Davies J, Romualdez AM, Pellicano E, Remington A
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Lots of autistic people are unemployed. Even when they are employed, autistic people might be given fewer opportunities than non-autistic people to progress in their careers. For example, assumptions about autistic people's differences in social communication might mean they are not given as many promotions. Indeed, we know that many autistic people are in jobs lower than their abilities (known as 'underemployment'). We reviewed 33 studies that tell us something about career progression for autistic people. Our review found that lots of autistic people want to progress in their careers, but there are many barriers in their way. For example, when they told their employer about being autistic, some people were given fewer opportunities. Research has also shown that autistic people do not get enough support to progress and that gaps in their employment history can make it difficult to progress. Our review suggested that good employment support (e.g. mentors) might help autistic people to progress in their careers. However, not much research has evaluated employment support for autistic people, which means we do not know how useful it is. Future research should find the best support that allows autistic people to live and work in ways that are meaningful to them.

sheet.es: Si apoyas a una persona autista en el trabajo, pregúntale si quiere crecer profesionalmente y qué apoyos le ayudarían, por ejemplo un mentor. Esta revisión examinó 33 estudios sobre la progresión profesional de personas autistas. Muchas quieren avanzar, pero encuentran barreras: algunas tuvieron menos oportunidades tras contar que eran autistas, recibieron poco apoyo y los vacíos en su historial laboral lo complicaron. Como límite, se ha evaluado poco el apoyo al empleo, así que no sabemos cuánto sirve. Tampoco describe a todas las personas autistas: cada una decide qué comparte y qué desea.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person at work, ask whether they want to progress in their career and what support would help, such as a mentor. This review looked at 33 studies on career progression for autistic people. Many want to move forward but meet barriers: some were given fewer opportunities after telling employers they were autistic, received too little support, and found gaps in their work history made progress harder. A limit is that little research has evaluated employment support, so we do not know how useful it is. It also does not describe every autistic person: each decides what to share and what they want.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person på jobbet, fråga om hen vill utvecklas i sin karriär och vilket stöd som skulle hjälpa, till exempel en mentor. Den här översikten granskade 33 studier om karriärutveckling för autistiska personer. Många vill gå vidare men möter hinder: vissa fick färre möjligheter efter att ha berättat för arbetsgivaren att de är autistiska, fick för lite stöd, och luckor i arbetshistoriken försvårade utvecklingen. En begränsning är att stöd i arbetslivet knappt har utvärderats, så vi vet inte hur användbart det är. Den beskriver inte alla autistiska personer: var och en avgör vad hen delar och vill.

title: Camouflaging, not sensory processing or autistic identity, predicts eating disorder symptoms in autistic adults.
authors: Bradley S, Moore F, Duffy F, Clark L, Suratwala T, Knightsmith P, Gillespie-Smith K
