sheet.sv: För att stödja autonomin hos en autistisk person med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning: erbjud verkliga val och låt personen bestämma, ta emot personens eget sätt att kommunicera och se till att miljön är trygg. Det var en studie med autistiska personer: åtta autistiska unga vuxna med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning samtalade i små grupper under flera tillfällen, med konst, spel och icke-verbal kommunikation. Få personer deltog, så resultaten gäller inte alla; fråga alltid personen själv vad hen behöver.

title: The meaning of autistic movements.
authors: Petty S, Ellis A
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract What is already known? Moving the body in 'stereotyped', 'repetitive', 'ritualised' or 'unusual' ways is part of the criteria for receiving a diagnosis of autism. However, the reasons for these movements and their personal value are not well understood. Certain ways of moving have become part of a disorder, and have received negative judgements, whereas other movements have not. What this paper adds? We searched online blogs for descriptions of movement written by autistic adults, using their preferred language and definitions. The blog authors said that many types of movement attracted negative judgement, including mis-coordination shown during sports, dancing in unusual places or moving repetitively, such as when stimming. However, movement provided personal benefits, and could enhance thinking and focus, provide meaningful routine, contribute to sensory regulation, release energy, increase body awareness, emotion regulation and strengthen self-identity. Implications for practice and policy Movement could be a well-being resource, used to reduce distraction, overwhelm, confusion and distress for autistic people. This should be considered within personal coping strategies and psychological therapies. The examples provided in this study could inform autism assessments, to ensure that the meanings of movements are considered alongside the appearances of movement. Some movements such as stimming have the same functions as many other ways of moving, including dancing and exercising, which could help to reduce stigma around being autistic if reflected in policy and practice. Improving understanding is important for informing how autism is assessed, and how personal experiences of being autistic are heard.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista se mueve de forma repetitiva, como al hacer stimming, antes de frenarla conviene preguntarle qué le aporta. El estudio analizó blogs escritos por personas autistas adultas. Según ellas, el movimiento puede ayudar a pensar y concentrarse, dar una rutina con sentido, regular los sentidos, soltar energía, notar el cuerpo, gestionar emociones y reforzar la identidad. También decían que muchos movimientos reciben juicios negativos. Es un estudio con textos de blogs, no con una muestra elegida, así que no sirve como regla para todas las personas ni sustituye preguntar a cada una.
sheet.en: If an autistic person moves repetitively, such as when stimming, ask what the movement gives them before trying to stop it. The study looked at blogs written by autistic adults. They described movement as helping thinking and focus, providing meaningful routine, supporting sensory regulation, releasing energy, increasing body awareness, helping with emotions and strengthening self-identity. They also said many movements attract negative judgement. This is a study of blog writing, not a chosen sample, so it is not a rule for every person and does not replace asking each individual.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person rör sig repetitivt, till exempel när hen stimmar, fråga vad rörelsen ger innan du försöker stoppa den. Studien granskade bloggar skrivna av autistiska vuxna. De beskrev att rörelse kan hjälpa tänkandet och fokus, ge meningsfull rutin, stödja sensorisk reglering, frigöra energi, öka kroppsuppfattningen, hjälpa med känslor och stärka självidentiteten. De sa också att många rörelser möts av negativa omdömen. Studien bygger på bloggtexter, inte på ett utvalt urval, så den är ingen regel för alla och ersätter inte att fråga varje person.

title: Suicidal Thoughts and Behaviors in People on the Autism Spectrum.
authors: Reid M, Delgado D, Heinly J, Kiernan B, Shapiro S, Morgan L, Maddox B, Jager-Hyman S
abstract: Purpose of review This review synthesizes recent research on suicidal thoughts and behaviors among autistic individuals. We present literature on risk and protective factors, risk assessment, intervention, and crisis services, and recommendations for future research. Recent findings Literature on this topic has grown substantially in recent years. Areas of advancement include improved understanding of risk factors (e.g., Interpersonal Theory of Suicide constructs, autistic burnout, mental health conditions, cognitive factors, diagnosis timing, emotion dysregulation), screening, assessment, acute-care services, and suicide-specific psychosocial treatments (e.g., safety planning, dialectical behavior therapy). Gaps include protective factors, impact of intersectional identities, and tailored approaches to screening, assessment, and intervention. Heightened awareness of suicide risk in autistic individuals has led to increased understanding of why autistic individuals think about and attempt suicide and the strategies used to identify and reduce suicide risk. We recommend community-partnered, multi-faceted, and strength-based approaches to inform tailored prevention and intervention efforts.

title: Neurodivergence, intersectionality, and eating disorders: a lived experience-led narrative review.
authors: Cobbaert L, Millichamp AR, Elwyn R, Silverstein S, Schweizer K, Thomas E, Miskovic-Wheatley J
abstract: Autistic people and those with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder are at a high risk of developing an eating disorder. While there is limited evidence on the relationship between other forms of neurodivergence and eating disorders, research suggests associations between giftedness, intellectual disability, obsessive-compulsive disorder, psychosis, Tourette's syndrome, and disordered eating. Factors underlying disordered eating and/or eating disorder risk for neurodivergent people are multifaceted and complex, encompassing a wide range of intertwined psychosocial, environmental, and biological processes. Moreover, research shows that neurodivergent individuals experience poorer treatment outcomes compared to neurotypical individuals. However, there is a paucity of research in this area overall. More specifically, lived experience-led research remains rare, despite its critical role for improving individualised eating disorder care, as well as mental healthcare more broadly. Indeed, the importance of eating disorder care individuation is increasingly being recognised, particularly within the context of neurodivergence, given the heterogeneous experiences and support needs of neurodivergent people affected by disordered eating and/or eating disorders. Furthermore, despite documented overlaps between various forms of neurodivergence (e.g., co-occurring autism and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder), research looking at eating disorders in the context of neurodivergence through a transdiagnostic perspective is scarce. This lived experience-led narrative review aims to shed light on the intersectional factors underlying elevated disordered eating and/or eating disorder risk for neurodivergent individuals. First, an overview of prevalence data is provided, followed by a thematic framework identifying factors underlying disordered eating and/or eating disorder risk in relation to neurodivergence. A critical appraisal of current eating disorder research and care is then offered before suggestions for neurodiversity-affirming eating disorder care are made. In this view, this paper offers a foundation for future empirical work in this nascent field of inquiry by providing a lived experience-led, transdiagnostic, and intersectional account of eating disorders in the context of neurodivergence.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista o con TDAH de tu entorno cambia su forma de comer, conviene observarlo con calma y curiosidad, sin juzgar. Las razones pueden ser sensoriales, emocionales, sociales o de rutina, y suelen mezclarse. Pregunta qué le resulta difícil, respeta sus necesidades y busca profesionales que adapten el apoyo a la persona en lugar de aplicar un modelo único. Esta es una revisión narrativa dirigida por personas con experiencia vivida, que reúne estudios previos sobre neurodivergencia y trastornos alimentarios. Sus límites: no aporta datos nuevos, la investigación disponible es escasa y sus propuestas aún deben comprobarse en estudios futuros.
sheet.en: If an autistic person or someone with ADHD in your life changes how they eat, notice it calmly and with curiosity, without judgement. Reasons can be sensory, emotional, social or routine-related, and often overlap. Ask what feels hard, respect their needs, and look for professionals who adapt support to the person rather than using one fixed model. This is a narrative review led by people with lived experience, bringing together earlier research on neurodivergence and eating disorders. Its limits: it offers no new data, the existing research is scarce, and its suggestions still need testing in future studies.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person eller någon med ADHD i din närhet ändrar sitt sätt att äta, lägg märke till det lugnt och nyfiket, utan att döma. Orsakerna kan vara sensoriska, känslomässiga, sociala eller kopplade till rutiner, och de hänger ofta ihop. Fråga vad som känns svårt, respektera personens behov och sök professionella som anpassar stödet efter individen i stället för att följa en enda modell. Detta är en narrativ översikt ledd av personer med egen erfarenhet, som sammanställer tidigare forskning om neurodivergens och ätstörningar. Begränsningar: den ger inga nya data, forskningen är fortfarande begränsad och förslagen behöver prövas i framtida studier.

title: Attitudes of autistic adults toward genetic testing for autism.
authors: Gallion T, Williams ZJ, Niarchou M, Duncan L, Hooker G, Taylor KA
abstract: Genetic testing for autism has been a controversial topic within the autistic community. Opinions regarding the benefits, risks, and limitations of genetic testing often differ between autistic people, researchers, and healthcare providers. The present study sought to understand the beliefs, attitudes, and intentions to pursue genetic testing of autistic adults and compare perspectives of autistic people who have had genetic testing with those who have not. An international sample of 173 autistic adults (19 [11%] who had previously undergone autism-related genetic testing) completed an online survey with questions assessing beliefs, attitudes, and intentions to pursue genetic testing. Beliefs and attitudes about genetic testing varied widely across the sample. Autistic individuals who had received prior genetic testing had much more positive beliefs about autism-related genetic testing (d = 0.87, 95% CI [0.37, 1.36]) and attitudes toward genetic testing (d = 1.14, 95% CI [0.66, 1.61]) compared to those who had not received such testing, although there were no meaningful differences between those same groups regarding beliefs about genetic testing unrelated to autism (d = 0.02, 95% CI [-0.45, 0.49], p = 0.93). Intention to genetically test oneself or one's (hypothetical) children was also significantly predicted by autism-specific beliefs, attitudes, and prior genetic testing status. A large majority of the sample (78.6%) also agreed that autistic individuals would benefit from contact with a genetic counselor in certain situations. These findings suggest that the autistic community does not have a singular view of genetic testing, and for those Autistic individuals who are interested in pursuing genetic testing for themselves or a family member, genetic counselors have the potential to play a key role in clinical care.

sheet.es: Si en su familia se habla de pruebas genéticas para el autismo, conviene escuchar la opinión de cada persona autista y no dar por hecho que todas piensan igual. Es un tema en el que hay posturas muy distintas. Se trata de una encuesta en línea con 173 adultos autistas de varios países; 19 (11%) ya se habían hecho una prueba genética relacionada con el autismo. Las opiniones variaron mucho, y quienes se la habían hecho la valoraban más positivamente. Un 78.6% estuvo de acuerdo en que el contacto con un asesor genético podría ayudar en algunas situaciones. Límites: es una encuesta, solo muestra opiniones y no demuestra causas, y el grupo que se hizo la prueba era pequeño. Cualquier decisión médica corresponde a cada persona con su profesional sanitario.
sheet.en: If genetic testing for autism comes up in your family, make room for each autistic person's own view rather than assuming everyone feels the same. Opinions on this topic differ widely. This was an online survey of 173 autistic adults from several countries; 19 (11%) had already had autism-related genetic testing. Views varied a lot, and those who had been tested were more positive about it. 78.6% agreed that contact with a genetic counselor could help in certain situations. Limits: a survey only shows opinions, not causes, and the tested group was small. Any medical decision belongs to each person together with their healthcare professional.
sheet.sv: Om genetisk testning för autism kommer upp i familjen: lyssna på varje autistisk persons egen syn i stället för att anta att alla tycker lika. Åsikterna går starkt isär. Studien var en webbenkät med 173 autistiska vuxna från flera länder; 19 (11%) hade redan gjort autismrelaterad genetisk testning. Åsikterna varierade mycket, och de som testats var mer positiva. 78.6% höll med om att kontakt med en genetisk vägledare kan hjälpa i vissa situationer. Begränsningar: en enkät visar bara åsikter, inte orsaker, och gruppen som testats var liten. Medicinska beslut fattar varje person tillsammans med sin vårdgivare.

title: Natural Disasters as a Maternal Prenatal Stressor and Children's Neurodevelopment: A Systematic Review.
authors: Ünsel-Bolat G, Yıldırım S, Kılıçaslan F, Caparros-Gonzalez RA
abstract: The intrauterine period is a time of high sensitivity in the development of the embryo and the fetus. Therefore, low levels of maternal stress are closely associated with healthy brain development in the neonatal and early childhood periods. There is increasing evidence linking natural disasters as prenatal maternal stress (PNMS) to neurodevelopmental disorders (including subclinical manifestations). Natural disasters involve many factors in addition to the trauma they cause, including loss and the physical and psychosocial difficulties that result from that trauma. This review article aims to bring together research findings on the neurodevelopmental effects of natural disasters on children as PNMS. It also looks at how factors such as gestational age and gender contribute to these effects. We conducted a systematic review on PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus, with 30 studies meting the inclusion criteria. This systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines. A total of 1,327,886 mother-child dyads participated in the included studies. The results of the studies indicate that natural disasters have a negative impact on children's outcomes in terms of cognitive development, language development, autism/autism-like features, motor skills, performance in mathematics, mental development, sleep, attention, behavioral and emotional problems, and various psychiatric comorbidities.

sheet.es: Si una familia vivió un desastre natural durante el embarazo, conviene que la persona cuidadora esté atenta al desarrollo (lenguaje, motricidad, sueño, atención) y pida apoyo temprano si lo desea, sin culpa. Es una revisión sistemática de 30 estudios, con 1,327,886 díadas madre-hijo. Sus límites: muestra asociaciones, no demuestra que el desastre cause por sí solo cada resultado, mezcla muchos factores (pérdidas, dificultades sociales) y no sirve como regla para cada niño o niña. Muchas criaturas se desarrollan de formas diversas y sin dificultades.
sheet.en: If a family lived through a natural disaster during pregnancy, caregivers can keep an eye on development (language, motor skills, sleep, attention) and seek early support if they wish, without guilt. This is a systematic review of 30 studies, covering 1,327,886 mother-child dyads. Its limits: it shows associations, not that the disaster alone causes each outcome, it mixes many factors (loss, social hardship), and it is not a rule for every child. Many children develop in varied ways and do well.
sheet.sv: Om en familj upplevde en naturkatastrof under graviditeten kan vårdnadshavare följa utvecklingen (språk, motorik, sömn, uppmärksamhet) och söka stöd tidigt om de vill, utan skuld. Det är en systematisk översikt av 30 studier med 1,327,886 mor-barn-par. Begränsningar: den visar samband, inte att katastrofen ensam orsakar varje utfall, den blandar många faktorer (förluster, sociala svårigheter) och är ingen regel för varje barn. Många barn utvecklas på olika sätt och mår bra.

title: Autistic Sensory Traits and Psychological Distress: Mediating Role of Worry and Intolerance of Uncertainty.
authors: Recio P, Pozo P, García-López C, Sarriá E
abstract: Background/objectives Autistic adults exhibit core and comorbid features that can have an impact on their daily functioning and lead to considerable psychological distress. Significant and consistent associations have been identified between autism characteristics-restricted repetitive behaviors and sensory features-and high levels of stress and anxiety. For a better understanding of the issue, it is necessary to consider the cognitive aspects that can help explain variations in stress and anxiety levels among adults with autism. We therefore aimed to model the contributions of worry and intolerance of uncertainty on the relationship between autism characteristics (sensory sensitivities and repetitive behaviors) and psychological distress (stress and anxiety). Methods The sample comprised 144 autistic individuals with a mean age of 35.15 (SD = 11.44). They participated in the study by completing an online questionnaire to assess the study variables. Most of the participants reported being diagnosed with Asperger syndrome (63.6%) or Level 1 autism spectrum disorder (27.1%). Results The model fit index values tested through path analysis indicated a good fit (χ 2 = 5.65; p = 0.13 ns; CFI = 0.993; NFI = 0.985; RMSEA = 0.079; SRMR = 0.025) and identified worry and intolerance of uncertainty as significant mediating variables within a comprehensive explanatory model. Conclusions These findings highlight the importance of worry and intolerance of uncertainty as specific targets in interventions aimed at improving stress and anxiety problems in autistic adults.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista se angustia con facilidad ante los sentidos o la incertidumbre, puede ayudar anticipar lo que va a pasar (horarios, cambios, lugares) y hablar con calma de las preocupaciones que surgen. Es una idea para probar, no una regla. Evidencia: estudio con 144 personas autistas adultas que respondieron un cuestionario en línea; la preocupación y la dificultad para tolerar la incertidumbre ayudaron a explicar la relación entre rasgos sensoriales y repetitivos y el estrés y la ansiedad. Límites: un solo cuestionario en un momento, casi todas con diagnóstico de Asperger o autismo de nivel 1, así que no muestra causas ni sirve para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person gets distressed easily by sensory input or uncertainty, it may help to make what is coming more predictable (schedules, changes, places) and to talk calmly about the worries that arise. This is an idea to try, not a rule. Evidence: a study of 144 autistic adults who completed an online questionnaire; worry and intolerance of uncertainty helped explain the link between sensory and repetitive traits and stress and anxiety. Limits: one questionnaire at one point in time, with most participants diagnosed with Asperger syndrome or Level 1 autism, so it cannot show cause and may not apply to everyone.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person lätt blir stressad av sinnesintryck eller osäkerhet kan det hjälpa att göra det som väntar mer förutsägbart (scheman, förändringar, platser) och att prata lugnt om oron som dyker upp. Det är en idé att pröva, inte en regel. Evidens: en studie med 144 autistiska vuxna som besvarade ett webbaserat frågeformulär; oro och svårighet att tåla osäkerhet hjälpte till att förklara sambandet mellan sensoriska och repetitiva drag och stress och ångest. Begränsningar: ett enda formulär vid ett tillfälle, de flesta med diagnosen Asperger eller autism nivå 1, så studien visar inte orsak och gäller inte nödvändigtvis alla.

title: The Effect of Autism Spectrum Disorder on Family Mental Health: Challenges, Emotional Impact, and Coping Strategies.
authors: Sánchez Amate JJ, Luque de la Rosa A
abstract: Background Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) impacts not only diagnosed individuals, but also significantly affects the quality of life of both primary and secondary caregivers. These effects are particularly pronounced when compared to caregivers of individuals with other neurodevelopmental disorders. The emotional and physical demands of caring for someone with ASD can profoundly alter family dynamics and interpersonal relationships, creating challenges that require a comprehensive approach to be understood and addressed. Methods The methodological design is a narrative review study, based on a search conducted during May, June, July, and August 2024 in the Scopus, Dialnet, and WoS databases concerning the object of study. As a result, a total of 197 articles were qualitatively analyzed. Of these, 36 articles were selected for a more detailed qualitative analysis, leading to a final sample of 14 documents. The selected studies were examined through qualitative content analysis. The inclusion criteria for this selection were as follows: empirical studies or research published in English or Spanish; open access via the Internet; categories limited to "education/educational research" relevant to the proposed objectives; and specific documents related to students with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). Results The care of individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) has a significant and multifaceted impact on family life, deeply affecting the mental health of caregivers. These effects manifest in the form of chronic stress, anxiety, and interpersonal difficulties, altering family dynamics. The quality of life of caregivers varies depending on the coping strategies they employ, which are crucial for their emotional well-being. Conclusions Understanding and optimizing these strategies is essential to mitigate the negative effects of caregiving and improving the overall well-being of families living with ASD.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista, tu cansancio y tu estrés son reales y merecen atención: buscar apoyo y probar estrategias de afrontamiento que te sirvan puede ayudar a tu bienestar y al de la familia. Es una revisión narrativa que analizó 14 documentos finales, centrados en estudiantes autistas y sus familias. Encontró estrés crónico, ansiedad y dificultades en las relaciones, y que la calidad de vida de quienes cuidan varía según las estrategias que usan. Tiene límites: es una revisión narrativa, con pocos documentos, limitada al ámbito educativo, y no indica qué estrategia funciona para cada familia.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic person, your tiredness and stress are real and deserve attention: seeking support and trying coping strategies that suit you may help your wellbeing and your family's. This was a narrative review that analysed a final sample of 14 documents, focused on autistic students and their families. It found chronic stress, anxiety and relationship difficulties, and that caregivers' quality of life varied with the coping strategies they used. It has limits: it is a narrative review with few documents, limited to education research, and it cannot say which strategy works for any one family.
sheet.sv: Om du ger omsorg till en autistisk person är din trötthet och din stress verklig och förtjänar uppmärksamhet: att söka stöd och prova copingstrategier som passar dig kan hjälpa ditt och familjens välbefinnande. Det här var en narrativ översikt som analyserade ett slutligt urval på 14 dokument, med fokus på autistiska elever och deras familjer. Den fann kronisk stress, ångest och svårigheter i relationer, och att omsorgsgivares livskvalitet varierade med de copingstrategier de använde. Begränsningarna: det är en narrativ översikt med få dokument, begränsad till utbildningsforskning, och den kan inte säga vilken strategi som fungerar för en enskild familj.

title: Older Autistic People, Access and Experiences of Services, and the Factors That Affect This.
authors: Hersh M, Mery P, Dawson M
journal: International journal of environmental research and public health
abstract: This paper presents new empirical data obtained from interviews and focus groups on older (50 and over) autistic people's experiences of accessing a variety of services. The involvement of older autistic people and giving voice to their experiences was central to all aspects of the research process. This work makes a significant contribution to the scarce literature on older autistic people. In particular, it discusses the factors that act as barriers and enablers to the access to and productive use of services, the strategies used by participants to manage and improve their experiences, and the success of these strategies. It shows older autistic people as autonomous adults and active protagonists in their own lives, taking action to overcome the barriers they experience to accessing services on the same terms as everyone else, but that lack of understanding and support from service providers and the general public can undermine their strategies. Finally, this work provides a series of recommendations for service providers to improve (older) autistic people's service access and experiences.

sheet.es: Si cuidas o acompañas a una persona autista mayor, pregúntale qué le facilita usar un servicio y qué se lo dificulta, y respeta las estrategias que ya emplea. Puedes ayudar explicando sus necesidades al personal de los servicios. La evidencia viene de un estudio con entrevistas y grupos de discusión con personas autistas de 50 años o más, que participaron en todo el proceso de investigación. Sus límites: el resumen no indica cuántas personas participaron y las experiencias no son iguales para todas, así que no sirven como regla general.
sheet.en: If you support an older autistic person, ask what makes a service easier or harder to use, and respect the strategies they already use. You can help by explaining their needs to service staff. The evidence comes from a study using interviews and focus groups with autistic people aged 50 and over, who were involved throughout the research process. Its limits: the abstract does not say how many people took part, and experiences differ from person to person, so the findings are not a rule for everyone.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en äldre autistisk person, fråga vad som gör en tjänst lättare eller svårare att använda och respektera de strategier personen redan har. Du kan hjälpa till genom att förklara behoven för personalen. Underlaget är en studie med intervjuer och fokusgrupper med autistiska personer från 50 år och uppåt, som var delaktiga i hela forskningsprocessen. Begränsningar: sammanfattningen anger inte hur många som deltog, och erfarenheter varierar mellan personer, så resultaten är ingen regel för alla.

title: A scoping review of interaction dynamics in minimally verbal autistic individuals.
authors: Boorom O, Liu T
abstract: Interaction dynamics provide information about how social interactions unfold over time and have implications for communication development. Characterizing social interaction in autistic people who are minimally verbal (MV) has the potential to illuminate mechanisms of change in communication development and intervention. The purpose of this scoping review was to investigate the current evidence characterizing interaction dynamics in MV autistic individuals, methods used to measure interaction dynamics in this population, and opportunities for future research. Articles were included if participants were diagnosed with autism, considered MV, if interaction occurred with a human communication partner during live in-person interaction, and if variables were derived by measuring the relationship between behaviors in both partners. The seven articles included in this review demonstrate that limited research describes interaction dynamics in this population, and that behavioral coding measures can be leveraged to assess constructs such as turn-taking, social contingency, and balance in social interactions. While there is some evidence describing how MV autistic individuals and their communication partners construct reciprocal interaction, there is variability in how interaction dynamics are measured and limited evidence describing individual differences. Recommendations for future research are discussed.

sheet.es: Mire la interacción como algo que construyen dos personas: fíjese en los turnos, en cómo responde usted a lo que la persona autista con poco lenguaje hablado hace o expresa, y en si hay equilibrio entre ambos. Esto es una reflexión, no una regla. La evidencia es una revisión de alcance de siete artículos sobre interacciones en vivo entre personas autistas con poco lenguaje hablado y sus interlocutores. Sus límites: hay poca investigación, las formas de medir varían mucho y se sabe poco sobre las diferencias entre personas.
sheet.en: Think of interaction as something two people build together: notice turn-taking, how you respond to what the minimally verbal autistic person does or expresses, and whether the exchange feels balanced. This is food for thought, not a rule. The evidence is a scoping review of seven articles on live, in-person interaction between minimally verbal autistic people and their communication partners. Its limits: little research exists, measurement methods vary a lot, and little is known about individual differences.
sheet.sv: Se interaktion som något två personer bygger tillsammans: lägg märke till turtagning, hur du svarar på det den autistiska personen med lite talat språk gör eller uttrycker, och om samspelet känns balanserat. Detta är något att fundera på, inte en regel. Underlaget är en kartläggande översikt av sju artiklar om direkt samspel ansikte mot ansikte mellan autistiska personer med lite talat språk och deras kommunikationspartner. Begränsningar: det finns lite forskning, mätmetoderna varierar mycket och kunskapen om individuella skillnader är liten.

title: Perceptual Experiences of Autistic People With an Intellectual Disability and People With Williams Syndrome: A Reflexive Thematic Analysis.
authors: Elise F, Irvine B, Brinkert J, Hamilton C, Farran EK, Milne E, Scerif G, Remington A
journal: Journal of applied research in intellectual disabilities : JARID
abstract: Background Autistic people without intellectual disabilities have increased perceptual capacity: they can process more information at any given time compared to non-autistic people. We examined whether increased perceptual capacity is evident across the autistic spectrum (i.e. for autistic people with intellectual disabilities) and whether it is specific to autism, or also experienced by people with Williams Syndrome (WS). Methods Five autistic adults with intellectual disabilities and five adults with WS took part in accessible, qualitative interviews. Responses were analysed using thematic analysis. Results Both groups expressed enjoyment of focussed attention, with autistic participants preferring multiple simultaneous inputs. Responses suggested increased perceptual capacity for autistic participants only. The sensory environment was reported to be anxiety-inducing for both groups. Conclusions This study gives preliminary evidence that increased perceptual capacity may be universal across the autistic spectrum, and specific to autism. Understanding differences in capacity offers more targeted suggestions to support sensory challenges.

sheet.es: Pregunta a la persona autista con discapacidad intelectual cómo vive su entorno sensorial y qué le ayuda. Algunas personas disfrutan de varios estímulos a la vez, y a la vez el ambiente puede generarles ansiedad, así que ofrece opciones en lugar de reducir todo por defecto. Evidencia: estudio cualitativo con entrevistas accesibles a cinco adultos autistas con discapacidad intelectual y cinco adultos con síndrome de Williams. Límites: la muestra es muy pequeña y los resultados son preliminares, por lo que no valen como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: Ask the autistic person with an intellectual disability how they experience their sensory environment and what helps. Some may enjoy several inputs at once, yet the environment can also cause anxiety, so offer choices rather than automatically reducing everything. Evidence: a qualitative study using accessible interviews with five autistic adults with intellectual disabilities and five adults with Williams Syndrome. Limits: the sample is very small and the findings are preliminary, so they are not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Fråga den autistiska personen med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning hur hen upplever sin sinnesmiljö och vad som hjälper. Vissa tycker om flera intryck samtidigt, men miljön kan också väcka oro, så erbjud val i stället för att automatiskt dämpa allt. Evidens: en kvalitativ studie med tillgängliga intervjuer med fem autistiska vuxna med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning och fem vuxna med Williams syndrom. Begränsningar: urvalet är mycket litet och resultaten är preliminära, så de gäller inte som regel för varje person.

title: Autistic adults' experiences of managing wellbeing and implications for social prescribing.
authors: Featherstone C, Sharpe R, Axford N, Asthana S, Husk K
abstract: Autistic people demonstrate poor outcomes on objective measures of wellbeing, yet research centring lived experience provides a more nuanced picture. There is growing support for person-centred, holistic and community approaches to enhancing wellbeing for autistic people. Social prescribing may be one such approach. This qualitative study explored the concept of wellbeing for autistic adults - including barriers and self-management - and the implications of this for modifying social prescribing. It involved semi-structured interviews with 21 autistic adults in the UK. Reflexive thematic analysis of the data supports research suggesting that self-determination may underlie many aspects of wellbeing for autistic people. The COVID-19 pandemic provided new opportunities to develop wellbeing strategies but also had negative impacts. Social prescribing could promote self-determination by signposting autistic people to peer support opportunities building on intrinsic interests.

sheet.es: Si apoyas el bienestar de una persona autista adulta, empieza por preguntarle qué le ayuda y deja que decida ella. Ofrecer opciones, como grupos de apoyo entre iguales basados en sus intereses, puede encajar mejor que imponer actividades. La evidencia es un estudio cualitativo con entrevistas a 21 personas autistas adultas en el Reino Unido. El análisis sugiere que la autodeterminación sustenta muchos aspectos del bienestar. Sus límites: son experiencias de un grupo pequeño y no valen como regla para todas las personas autistas ni para otros países.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult's wellbeing, start by asking what helps them and let them decide. Offering choices, such as peer support groups built around their interests, may fit better than imposing activities. The evidence is a qualitative study with interviews of 21 autistic adults in the UK. The analysis suggests self-determination underlies many aspects of wellbeing. Its limits: these are the experiences of a small group, so they are not a rule for every autistic person or for other countries.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxens välbefinnande, börja med att fråga vad som hjälper och låt personen bestämma. Att erbjuda val, till exempel kamratstöd utifrån egna intressen, kan passa bättre än att styra aktiviteter. Underlaget är en kvalitativ studie med intervjuer av 21 autistiska vuxna i Storbritannien. Analysen tyder på att självbestämmande ligger bakom många delar av välbefinnande. Begränsningar: det är erfarenheter från en liten grupp och gäller inte som regel för alla autistiska personer eller i andra länder.

title: Effect of physical activity on social communication impairments in children with autism spectrum disorder: A meta-analysis.
authors: Qi K, Wang X, Xu Q, Hu B, Wang Z, Białas M
abstract: This meta-analysis aims to systematically evaluate if different physical activities (PA) improve the social communication impairments (SCI) seen in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). For this meta-analysis, five databases (Web of Science, PubMed and Cochrane Library database in English, and CNKI and Wanfang Data Knowledge Service Platform in Chinese) were searched from database inception to September 11, 2024. The eligibility criteria included (1) study population comprised children with ASD, with no gender restriction; (2) experimental group consisted of a PA intervention; (3) control group consisted of nonPA interventions or routine activities; (4) outcomes were assessed using validated SCI scales (e.g., social cognition, social motivation, and/or social awareness); and (5) study design involved a randomized parallel group design. The quality of the evidence for each study was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool. From a pool of 2714 potentially relevant articles, 17 were eligible for inclusion in this review. The results of overall response of PA intervention to SCI illustrated a Medium degree of statistical heterogeneity between studies (I 2 = 53.3 %, p < 0.01); the effect size of PA intervention on SCI (expressed as standardized mean difference) was -0.34 (95 % CI: -0.57, -0.11), which was statistically significant. SCI of autistic children could be potentially improved by PA interventions, though further research is needed to clarify if benefits achieve clinical significance in addition to statistical significance. Proper design of PA interventions (45-90 min per session, more than 3 times per week and for 8-12 weeks) may enhance their effectiveness in treating SCI in children with ASD.

sheet.es: Si le interesa, puede probar actividades físicas que a la niña o al niño autista le gusten, de forma regular y sin presión, y observar cómo se siente y cómo se relaciona. Es un metaanálisis que reunió 17 estudios aleatorizados con niños autistas; las actividades físicas se asociaron con una posible mejora en la comunicación social. Los autores señalan que falta saber si el beneficio es relevante en la vida diaria, no solo estadístico, y que los estudios difieren entre sí. No es una norma para todas las personas: cada niño tiene sus propios gustos y necesidades sensoriales.
sheet.en: If it suits your family, you could try physical activities your autistic child enjoys, regularly and without pressure, and notice how they feel and connect with others. This is a meta-analysis that pooled 17 randomized studies with autistic children; physical activity was linked to a possible improvement in social communication. The authors note it is still unclear whether the benefit matters in everyday life, not just statistically, and the studies differed from one another. It is not a rule for every person: each child has their own preferences and sensory needs.
sheet.sv: Om det passar er familj kan ni prova fysiska aktiviteter som ert autistiska barn tycker om, regelbundet och utan press, och lägga märke till hur barnet mår och umgås. Det är en metaanalys av 17 randomiserade studier med autistiska barn; fysisk aktivitet hängde ihop med en möjlig förbättring av social kommunikation. Författarna påpekar att det återstår att veta om nyttan spelar roll i vardagen, inte bara statistiskt, och att studierna skilde sig åt. Det är ingen regel för alla: varje barn har egna preferenser och sensoriska behov.

title: Effects of remote support courses on parental mental health and child development in autism: A randomized controlled trial.
authors: Lu JH, Wei H, Zhang Y, Fei F, Huang HY, Dong QJ, Chen J, Ao DQ, Chen L, Li TY, Li Y, Dai Y
abstract: Background Sustaining the mental health of autistic children's parents can be demanding. Aim To determine the effect of remote support courses on the mental health of parents and the development of autistic children. Methods Parents of 140 autistic children were randomly assigned to two groups receiving a 2-week intervention: The control group received caregiver-mediated intervention (CMI); the experimental group received CMI with remote family psychological support courses (R-FPSC). The Parenting Stress Index-Short Form, Parenting Sense of Competence Scale, Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7, and Patient Health Questionnaire-9 were used to measure parents' mental health. The Childhood Autism Rating Scale and Gesell Developmental Schedules were used to evaluate children's development. Results Improved parenting stress, sense of competence, depression, and anxiety were found in both groups, but improvements in parenting stress (81.10 ± 19.76 vs 92.10 ± 19.26, P vs 63.91 ± 10.86, P vs 11.57 ± 3.15, P Conclusion Integrating R-FPSC with CMI may be effective in reducing parenting stress, enhancing parents' sense of competence, and increasing parents' training enthusiasm.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a un niño autista y te sientes agotado, un curso de apoyo psicológico a distancia para familias, añadido a la formación para cuidadores, puede ayudar a reducir el estrés y reforzar tu confianza como madre o padre. Es un ensayo aleatorizado: los padres de 140 niños autistas recibieron durante 2 semanas la formación para cuidadores, con o sin los cursos a distancia. Ambos grupos mejoraron, pero el grupo con cursos mejoró más en estrés parental y sensación de competencia. Límites: la intervención fue muy corta, el resumen no detalla el seguimiento y los resultados no valen para todas las familias.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic child and feel worn out, a remote psychological support course for families, added to caregiver training, may help lower stress and strengthen your confidence as a parent. This was a randomized trial: parents of 140 autistic children took part in a 2-week caregiver training, with or without the remote courses. Both groups improved, but the group with the courses improved more in parenting stress and sense of competence. Limits: the intervention was very short, the abstract gives no follow-up details, and results will not fit every family.
sheet.sv: Om du tar hand om ett autistiskt barn och känner dig slutkörd kan en psykologisk stödkurs på distans för familjer, som tillägg till utbildning för vårdnadshavare, hjälpa till att minska stressen och stärka din tillit som förälder. Det var en randomiserad studie: föräldrar till 140 autistiska barn deltog i 2 veckors utbildning för vårdnadshavare, med eller utan distanskurserna. Båda grupperna förbättrades, men gruppen med kurserna förbättrades mer i föräldrastress och känsla av kompetens. Begränsningar: insatsen var mycket kort, sammanfattningen beskriver ingen uppföljning, och resultaten passar inte alla familjer.

title: Effects of Massage on Self-regulatory Difficulties, Tactile and Oral Abnormalities, and Parenting Stress in Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD): A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
authors: Fadlalmola HA, Abedelwahed HH, Hamid HI, Ali AB, Algadi HAA, Farg SJ, Ali NMA, Elbashir AA, Mohammed MH, Mohmmed SS, Mousa SA, Gaafar DA, Eltyeb AA
journal: International journal of therapeutic massage & bodywork
abstract: Background The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention stated that about 1 in every 44 children between the ages of 4 and 8 years old had been identified with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Complementary interventions such as massage are crucial for the improvement of the health outcomes of ASD patients, such as abnormal sensory response; Autism Behavior Checklist; parenting stress, self-regulatory difficulties, social, language, and communication abilities; tactile or oral abnormalities; Vineland daily living skills; Vineland socialization; Childhood Autism Rating Scale; Preschool Language Scale 5th Edition (PLS-5) auditory communication; and PLS-5 expressive communication. Purpose We aim to systematically investigate the effects of different types of massage on self-regulatory difficulties, tactile and oral abnormalities, and parenting stress in children with ASD. Methods PubMed, Cochrane Library, Scopus, and Web of Science were scoured from their inception through November 15, 2022. Research comparing massage efficacy in children with ASD to other methods or a control group was included. For randomized controlled trials (RCTs), we utilized the Cochrane risk of bias tool; and for cohort studies, we used the tool developed by the National Institutes of Health. Meta-analysis was carried out with Review Manager 5.4. For our continuous data, we calculated the mean difference (MD) and 95% confidence interval (95% CI). Results We included 10 studies with a total number of 485 children with autism. Our analysis showed a significant decrease in the massage group regarding self-regulatory difficulties (MD = -9.15; 95% CI (-13.69 to -4.60), p Conclusion Qigong and traditional Thai massage improved self-regulatory difficulties and decreased tactile or oral abnormalities in children with autism. Moreover, they decreased parenting stress. However, we need more RCTs with larger sample sizes with high quality to assess the different types of massage effects on autistic children and produce more valid results. So, Qigong and traditional Thai massage could be used as a complement to educational and training interventions in children with autism.

sheet.es: Si le interesa el masaje, puede probar con calma un masaje suave, como el qigong o el masaje tradicional tailandés, como complemento de otros apoyos, y observar cómo responde su hijo o hija y si lo desea. Esta revisión sistemática con metaanálisis reunió 10 estudios con 485 niños autistas; el grupo de masaje mostró menos dificultades de autorregulación, menos anomalías táctiles u orales y menos estrés parental. Sin embargo, los autores piden más ensayos aleatorizados, de mayor calidad y con muestras más grandes, así que los resultados no valen para todas las personas. El consentimiento y el confort de la persona van primero.
sheet.en: If massage interests you, you could gently try a soft approach, such as qigong or traditional Thai massage, alongside other supports, watching how your child responds and whether they want it. This systematic review and meta-analysis pooled 10 studies with 485 autistic children; the massage groups showed fewer self-regulation difficulties, fewer tactile or oral abnormalities and less parenting stress. However, the authors call for larger, higher-quality randomized trials, so the results do not apply to every person. The person's consent and comfort come first.
sheet.sv: Om massage intresserar dig kan du försiktigt prova en mjuk form, som qigong eller traditionell thaimassage, vid sidan av andra stöd, och se hur ditt barn reagerar och om det vill det. Den här systematiska översikten med metaanalys sammanställde 10 studier med 485 autistiska barn; massagegrupperna visade färre svårigheter med självreglering, färre taktila eller orala avvikelser och mindre föräldrastress. Författarna efterlyser dock större randomiserade studier av högre kvalitet, så resultaten gäller inte alla. Personens samtycke och trygghet kommer först.

title: Internet-Delivered Psychoeducation (SCOPE) for Transition-Aged Autistic Youth: Pragmatic Randomized Controlled Trial.
authors: Backman A, Roll-Pettersson L, Mellblom A, Norman-Claesson E, Sundqvist E, Zander E, Vigerland S, Hirvikoski T
abstract: Background Psychoeducation is a recommended first-line intervention for transition-aged autistic youth, but it has not been previously evaluated in an internet-delivered format. SCOPE (Spectrum Computerized Psychoeducation) is an 8-week individual, internet-delivered, therapist-supported psychoeducative intervention. Objective This study aimed to investigate the effectiveness of SCOPE through a 3-armed randomized controlled trial. The intervention aims to increase participants' understanding of autism and, in doing so, increase their quality of life (QoL). Methods SCOPE was codeveloped with clinicians and autistic young adults. It contains 8 autism-related modules, each with (1) text describing the module topic, (2) four video vignettes with recurring characters who describe their lives and perspectives on the module topic, (3) a list of neurotypical characteristics related to the module's topic, and (4) self-reflection using 3 or 4 questions about the module topic, answered by multiple-choice bullets and voluntary open-ended written comments. Participants were randomized (2:1:1) to SCOPE, an active control (web-based self-study), or treatment as usual (TAU). The primary outcome was participants' autism knowledge, assessed using the Autism Spectrum Disorder Quiz, and secondary outcomes included acceptance of diagnosis, QoL, and symptoms of mental health problems. All outcomes were assessed at the baseline, postintervention, and 3-month follow-up time points, using mixed-effects models to assess change in outcome measures across time points. Results Between 2014 and 2020, a total of 141 participants were randomized to 1 of the 3 treatment arms. The SCOPE participants had significantly greater autism knowledge gains at the posttreatment time point compared to TAU participants with a moderate effect size (d=0.47; P=.05); gains were maintained at the 3-month follow-up (d=0.46; P=.05). The self-study participants also had increased knowledge gains compared to TAU participants at the posttreatment time point with a moderate effect size (d=0.60; P=.03) but did not maintain these gains at the 3-month follow-up, and their autism knowledge scores returned to baseline (mean change score: -0.13, 95% CI -1.20 to 0.94; P=.81). In addition, SCOPE participants reported improved QoL at the postintervention (d=0.37, P=.02) and 3-month follow-up time points (d=0.60; P=.001), compared to the combined controls. The gained autism knowledge was not mirrored by changes in symptoms of anxiety or depression. Conclusions Effective internet-delivered interventions may facilitate first-line service access to individuals who are unable or unwilling to use traditional health care interventions or who live in geographically remote locations. Additionally, an intervention such as SCOPE could impart and sustain the knowledge gained through psychoeducation in transition-aged autistic youth. For future research, qualitative studies could further our understanding of the lived experiences of intervention participation and outcomes after internet-delivered psychoeducation. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03665363; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03665363.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista joven quiere entender mejor el autismo, un programa online de psicoeducación con apoyo de un terapeuta puede ser una opción útil, sobre todo si le cuesta acudir a servicios presenciales o vive lejos. Puede preguntarle si le interesa y ofrecerle elegir. La evidencia es un ensayo aleatorizado con 141 participantes jóvenes autistas: SCOPE, de 8 semanas, mejoró el conocimiento sobre el autismo, y esa mejora se mantuvo a los 3 meses. También informaron mejor calidad de vida. No cambiaron los síntomas de ansiedad ni de depresión. Como límites, los resultados son promedios de grupo y no sirven para predecir a cada persona; faltan estudios sobre cómo lo vivieron los participantes.
sheet.en: If a young autistic person wants to understand autism better, an online, therapist-supported psychoeducation programme may be a useful option, especially if in-person services are hard to reach or they live far away. You could ask whether it interests them and let them choose. The evidence is a randomized trial with 141 young autistic participants: the 8-week SCOPE programme improved autism knowledge, and this was kept at 3 months. Participants also reported better quality of life. Anxiety and depression symptoms did not change. As limits, results are group averages and cannot predict any one person; studies on how participants experienced it are still needed.
sheet.sv: Om en ung autistisk person vill förstå autism bättre kan ett nätbaserat psykoedukationsprogram med stöd av en terapeut vara ett bra alternativ, särskilt om det är svårt att ta sig till mottagningar eller om personen bor långt bort. Du kan fråga om det är av intresse och låta personen välja. Underlaget är en randomiserad studie med 141 unga autistiska deltagare: programmet SCOPE, som pågick i 8 veckor, ökade kunskapen om autism, och ökningen fanns kvar efter 3 månader. Deltagarna rapporterade också bättre livskvalitet. Symtom på ångest och depression förändrades inte. Begränsningar: resultaten är gruppgenomsnitt och kan inte förutsäga hur det går för en enskild person; fler studier om hur deltagarna upplevde programmet behövs.

title: An Update on Microbial Interventions in Autism Spectrum Disorder with Gastrointestinal Symptoms.
authors: Moreno RJ, Ashwood P
abstract: In the United States, autism spectrum disorder (ASD) affects 1 in 33 children and is characterized by atypical social interactions, communication difficulties, and intense, restricted interests. Microbial dysbiosis in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract is frequently observed in individuals with ASD, potentially contributing to behavioral manifestations and correlating with worsening severity. Moreover, dysbiosis may contribute to the increased prevalence of GI comorbidities in the ASD population and exacerbate immune dysregulation, further worsening dysbiosis. Over the past 25 years, research on the impact of microbial manipulation on ASD outcomes has gained substantial interest. Various approaches to microbial manipulation have been preclinically and clinically tested, including antibiotic treatment, dietary modifications, prebiotics, probiotics, and fecal microbiota transplantation. Each method has shown varying degrees of success in reducing the severity of ASD behaviors and/or GI symptoms and varying long-term efficacy. In this review, we discuss these microbiome manipulation methods and their outcomes. We also discuss potential microbiome manipulation early in life, as this is a critical period for neurodevelopment.

title: Dental Adaptation Strategies for Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder-A Systematic Review of Randomized Trials.
authors: Prynda M, Pawlik AA, Niemczyk W, Wiench R
abstract: Background: Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) often struggle with dental care due to sensory sensitivities and behavioral issues, increasing their risk for oral health problems. Adaptation strategies such as visual aids, video modeling, and sensory-adapted environments aim to improve their dental experiences. Methods: A systematic review of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines using the PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Cochrane databases. Of the 1072 records screened, nine RCTs were included in the analysis. Studies included children with ASD under 18 years and compared dental adaptation techniques with traditional care. The risk of bias and study quality were assessed. The quality of evidence for the results was determined using the GRADE tool. Results: Nine RCTs with sample sizes ranging from 25 to 138 participants showed significant improvements in oral hygiene, reduced anxiety, and increased cooperation. Video modeling and sensory-adapted environments were particularly effective in lowering distress during dental visits. Conclusions: Dental adaptation strategies, especially video modeling and sensory-adapted environments, effectively improve oral health outcomes and reduce anxiety in children with ASD. More research is needed to explore the long-term effects and include children with severe ASD.

sheet.es: Antes de la próxima visita al dentista, prueba a preparar a tu hijo o hija con un vídeo que muestre paso a paso lo que ocurrirá, y pregunta si la consulta puede adaptar el entorno a sus sensibilidades sensoriales. Se trata de una revisión sistemática de nueve ensayos aleatorizados con niños autistas menores de 18 años; los tamaños de muestra iban de 25 a 138 participantes. Los estudios apuntaron a menos ansiedad, más colaboración y mejor higiene oral. Sin embargo, faltan datos a largo plazo y se incluyó poco a niños con mayores necesidades de apoyo, así que no todo funcionará igual para cada persona.
sheet.en: Before the next dental visit, try preparing your child with a video that shows step by step what will happen, and ask whether the clinic can adapt the space to their sensory sensitivities. This is a systematic review of nine randomized trials with autistic children under 18; sample sizes ranged from 25 to 138 participants. The studies pointed to less anxiety, more cooperation and better oral hygiene. However, long-term effects are still unknown and children with higher support needs were barely included, so what helps one person may not work the same for another.
sheet.sv: Inför nästa tandläkarbesök kan du förbereda ditt barn med en film som visar steg för steg vad som kommer att hända, och fråga om mottagningen kan anpassa miljön efter barnets sensoriska känslighet. Detta är en systematisk översikt av nio randomiserade studier med autistiska barn under 18 år; urvalen varierade från 25 till 138 deltagare. Studierna tydde på mindre oro, bättre samarbete och bättre munhygien. Långtidseffekter är dock okända och barn med större stödbehov ingick knappt, så det som hjälper en person fungerar inte likadant för alla.

title: Participatory longitudinal qualitative interview study to understand Autistic gynaecological and obstetric health: the Autism from menstruation to menopause study protocol.
authors: Grant A, Williams GL, Axbey H, Wilkins A, Firth E, Lim H, Cave H, Williams K, Ribbons K, Sinfield M, Craine M, Caemawr S, Holloway W, Brown A, Nicolaidis C, Kara H, Ellis R
abstract: Introduction Autism is a lifelong minority neurotype present from birth. There is a dearth of credible evidence to suggest gender variation in Autism prevalence, despite historical under-diagnosis of women. Autistic people Assigned Female At Birth (AFAB) have worse physical and mental health compared with non-Autistic peers. To date, the reproductive health experiences of Autistic AFAB people have been under-investigated. Methods and analysis This study aims to co-develop a quality improvement intervention to improve the reproductive health of Autistic people. The study uses Community Partnered Participatory Research (an approach similar to Community-Based Participatory Research), largely through a Community Council that co-governs the study. To understand reproductive health needs, a longitudinal qualitative investigation using creative methods will be undertaken with 100 Autistic AFAB people with 10 waves of data collection over 5 years (interview n=500-1000). Participants will be purposively selected to include harder-to-reach members of the Autistic community, including those who are non-speaking or semi-speaking, have a learning disability and those from marginalised ethnicities. Data will be analysed thematically with Community Council involvement. Intervention development will be undertaken from 2029 onwards. Ethics and dissemination We are an Autistic-led team that adopts a social model of disability. However, this study raises ethical issues relating to sensitive topics and marginalised populations. Accordingly, we have robust procedures in place to assess capacity to ensure informed consent and to allow participants to take part without opting into data sharing. Ethical approval has been awarded by the Swansea University School of Health and Social Care Research Ethics Committee. We will publish our findings as open access articles in peer-reviewed journals.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista asignada mujer al nacer, o lo eres, puede ser útil recordar que su salud reproductiva (menstruación, embarazo, menopausia) merece atención propia y que sus experiencias importan. Este documento es un protocolo: describe un estudio cualitativo planificado, dirigido por un equipo autista, con 100 personas autistas y 10 rondas de recogida de datos a lo largo de 5 años. Incluye a personas que no hablan o hablan poco. Aún no hay resultados, así que no ofrece conclusiones ni consejos probados. Ante dudas de salud, consulta a un profesional sanitario.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person assigned female at birth, or you are one, it may help to know that reproductive health (periods, pregnancy, menopause) deserves its own attention and that their experiences matter. This is a study protocol: it describes a planned qualitative study, led by an autistic team, with 100 autistic people and 10 waves of data collection over 5 years. It includes people who are non-speaking or semi-speaking. There are no results yet, so it offers no findings or tested advice. For health concerns, speak with a healthcare professional.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person som tilldelades kvinnligt kön vid födseln, eller själv är det, kan det vara bra att veta att reproduktiv hälsa (mens, graviditet, klimakteriet) förtjänar egen uppmärksamhet och att deras erfarenheter spelar roll. Detta är ett studieprotokoll: det beskriver en planerad kvalitativ studie, ledd av ett autistiskt team, med 100 autistiska personer och 10 datainsamlingsomgångar under 5 år. Den inkluderar personer som inte talar eller talar lite. Det finns ännu inga resultat, så inga fynd eller beprövade råd ges. Vid hälsofrågor, kontakta sjukvården.

title: 'I can't relate to it': Exploring autistic and non-autistic adults' perceptions of the Australian Physical Activity and Sedentary Behaviour Guidelines.
authors: Thompson C, Gorey T, Lawler T, Watson G, Wells B, McVeigh JA
journal: Health promotion journal of Australia : official journal of Australian Association of Health Promotion Professionals
abstract: Background Despite sufficient physical activity (PA) being strongly associated with better health outcomes, half of the Australian population does not meet the Australian PA and Sedentary Behaviour Guidelines. This shortfall is more pronounced among autistic adults, who exhibit poorer health outcomes and lower PA levels than non-autistic adults. Despite these disparities, there is a limited understanding of how autistic and non-autistic individuals perceive and interpret the PA guidelines. Methods This study investigated how autistic and non-autistic adults perceive and comprehend the Australian PA guidelines. This study used interpretative phenomenological analysis. Results A total of 15 autistic and 20 non-autistic adults were interviewed, and 4 themes that were largely similar between both groups were identified: (1) Lack of Awareness and Engagement with the PA Guidelines, (2) Misinterpretation of Key Terms and Concepts, (3) Perceived lack of Relevance and Relatability of the PA Guidelines and (4) Lack of Inclusivity. Conclusion The findings underscore the importance of crafting health communication and promotion materials that are more visible, clear, inclusive and engaging for non-autistic and autistic individuals in Australia. SO WHAT?: This study highlights the potential for improving the number of people correctly understanding the PA guidelines by addressing dissemination methods, knowledge and interpretation of the guidelines as some components of the multifaceted process required to achieve behaviour change.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista no se siente reflejada en las guías oficiales de actividad física, no es raro: puede ayudar traducirlas juntos a ejemplos concretos, con palabras claras y actividades que realmente le interesen. Es un estudio de entrevistas con 15 adultos autistas y 20 adultos no autistas en Australia, que encontraron temas en gran parte similares: poco conocimiento de las guías, términos mal entendidos, falta de relevancia y de inclusión. Sus límites: son experiencias de un grupo pequeño en un solo país, no demuestran que cambiar los materiales aumente la actividad, y no valen igual para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person doesn't see themselves in official physical activity guidelines, that's understandable: it may help to translate them together into concrete examples, in plain words, using activities they actually enjoy. This was an interview study with 15 autistic and 20 non-autistic adults in Australia, and the themes were largely similar in both groups: little awareness of the guidelines, misunderstood terms, a sense they were not relevant, and a lack of inclusion. Limits: it reflects the views of a small group in one country, does not show that changing the materials increases activity, and will not fit every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person inte känner igen sig i de officiella riktlinjerna för fysisk aktivitet är det begripligt: det kan hjälpa att översätta dem tillsammans till konkreta exempel, med enkla ord och aktiviteter som personen faktiskt gillar. Det här var en intervjustudie med 15 autistiska och 20 icke-autistiska vuxna i Australien, och temana var i stort sett likartade i båda grupperna: låg kännedom om riktlinjerna, missförstådda termer, upplevd brist på relevans och bristande inkludering. Begränsningar: studien speglar en liten grupp i ett land, visar inte att ändrat material ökar aktiviteten och passar inte alla.

title: Factors Influencing the Oral Health Behaviours of Autistic Children and Young People: A Qualitative Study.
authors: Erwin J, Neill S, Vassallo T, Vassallo I, Witton R, Paisi M
journal: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy
abstract: Background Poor oral health (OH) in childhood can cause pain, affect quality of life and significantly impact adult OH. Autistic children and young people (CYP) experience inequalities in OH and are at higher risk of cavities and gum disease than neurotypical CYP. Objective To provide evidence and insights into the factors affecting the OH behaviours of ACYP from the perspective of ACYP, their parents/carers and Dental Health Professionals (DHPs). Method Semi-structured online or face-to-face interviews were conducted with CYP, parents/carers and DHPs in Southwest England. Results Nineteen ACYP (aged 5-18 years old), 20 parents/carers and 16 DHPs were interviewed. The themes identified were as follows: Sensory sensitivities and diet; Toothbrushing 'battles'; Coping with the stresses of daily life in a neurotypical world; Awareness of autism and understanding of challenges to good OH; The impact on parents of trying to care their child's OH; CYP and parent/carers difficulties in obtaining OH support; What 'good support' looks like. Conclusions An increased awareness among DHPs, health and social care professionals of autism and the challenges to OH that CYP face is needed. Providing early support, strategies and resources to CYP and their parents/carers has the potential to help establish positive OH behaviours. Public contribution The research team worked closely with members of the autistic community on this project. The methods used in this project were developed together with a research advisory group which included four ACYP (aged 9-17) and their parents. The team also worked with members of a youth club for ACYP aged 10-17 years old. All research documents and materials were co-produced. Members of the advisory group (T.V. and I.V.) contributed to the interpretation of the research findings and the writing of this manuscript.

sheet.es: Si cepillar los dientes se vuelve una lucha, conviene mirar primero lo sensorial: el sabor, la textura, el ruido o el estrés acumulado del día pueden pesar más que la voluntad. Pedir apoyo temprano a profesionales dentales también ayuda. Este estudio cualitativo entrevistó a 19 niños y jóvenes autistas de 5-18 años, a 20 madres, padres o cuidadores y a 16 profesionales dentales del suroeste de Inglaterra. Las personas autistas participaron en el diseño de la investigación. Sus límites: refleja experiencias de una sola región y no demuestra qué estrategia funciona para cada persona.
sheet.en: If toothbrushing turns into a battle, look at the sensory side first: taste, texture, noise or the stress built up during the day may matter more than willingness. Asking dental professionals for support early can also help. This qualitative study interviewed 19 autistic children and young people aged 5-18, 20 parents or carers and 16 dental professionals in Southwest England. Autistic people helped shape the research. Its limits: it reflects experiences from one region and does not show which strategy works for any one person.
sheet.sv: Om tandborstningen blir en kamp, titta först på det sensoriska: smak, textur, ljud eller dagens samlade stress kan väga tyngre än viljan. Att be tandvårdspersonal om stöd tidigt kan också hjälpa. Denna kvalitativa studie intervjuade 19 autistiska barn och unga i åldern 5-18, 20 föräldrar eller vårdare och 16 tandvårdsprofessionella i sydvästra England. Autistiska personer var med och utformade forskningen. Begränsningar: den speglar erfarenheter från en region och visar inte vilken strategi som fungerar för en enskild person.

title: Comparative efficacy of an early intervention "parent and me" program for infants showing signs of autism: The Baby JASPER model.
authors: Gulsrud AC, Shih W, Paparella T, Kasari C
abstract: Despite important advancements into the early detection of autism, there are still few empirically supported interventions for children under the age of two years who are showing early signs. Caregiver-mediated interventions have gained in popularity as a method for delivering support to the child and family. The current study builds on current work by enrolling a comparatively large cohort of infants (ages 12-22 months of age) displaying early signs of autism into a randomized controlled intervention program. Infants and parents received a group-based program using a standard early childhood curriculum. In addition, all families were randomly assigned to receive parent training in the form of either parent-mediated Joint Attention Symbolic Play Engagement and Regulation (JASPER) training or psychoeducation. Infants in both classrooms made substantial gains in social-communication, play, and cognition during a brief, 8-week period. All infants gained over an average of 10 points in DQ and increased in standardized measures of social-communication and play, with these gains maintaining at a 2-month follow-up visit. The classroom that also received JASPER increased in child initiated joint engagement and play level during dyadic interactions with their parents, while the classroom that received psychoeducation increased in joint attention during a standardized assessment delivered by an independent assessor. Infant familial risk for autism (older sibling with autism) also moderated the effect of treatment on child initiated joint engagement where infants in the JASPER classroom without familial risk made the most gains from baseline to exit of the program. This study highlights the promise of intervening at the earliest stages to promote positive outcomes for children and families.

sheet.es: Un programa grupal breve en el que madres y padres participan junto a su bebé puede ser una vía para apoyar el juego y la comunicación compartida desde muy temprano. Pueden probarse rutinas de juego en las que el bebé lleva la iniciativa. La evidencia es un ensayo aleatorizado con una cohorte comparativamente grande de bebés de 12-22 meses con signos tempranos de autismo. Ambos grupos, con formación parental JASPER o con psicoeducación, mostraron avances durante 8 semanas, que se mantuvieron a los 2 meses. Los resultados variaron entre grupos y según el antecedente familiar, y no demuestran que cada bebé vaya a responder igual.
sheet.en: A short group program where parents take part alongside their baby may be one way to support shared play and communication very early on. Caregivers could try play routines in which the baby leads. The evidence is a randomized trial with a comparatively large cohort of infants aged 12-22 months showing early signs of autism. Both groups, with JASPER parent training or with psychoeducation, made gains over 8 weeks, which held at a 2-month follow-up. Results differed between groups and by family history, and they do not show that every baby will respond in the same way.
sheet.sv: Ett kort gruppprogram där föräldrar deltar tillsammans med sitt barn kan vara ett sätt att stödja gemensamt lekande och kommunikation tidigt. Man kan prova lekrutiner där barnet leder. Underlaget är en randomiserad studie med en jämförelsevis stor grupp barn i åldern 12-22 månader med tidiga tecken på autism. Båda grupperna, med JASPER-föräldraträning eller psykoedukation, gjorde framsteg under 8 veckor, och dessa höll i sig vid uppföljning efter 2 månader. Resultaten skilde sig mellan grupperna och efter släktskap med autism, och visar inte att alla barn svarar likadant.

title: Autistic adults' perspectives and experiences of diagnostic assessments that include play across the lifespan.
authors: Pritchard-Rowe E, de Lemos C, Howard K, Gibson J
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Play is often included in autism diagnostic assessments. These assessments tend to focus on negatives and how people who are not autistic interpret observable behaviours. It is important to take a neurodiversity-affirmative assessment approach. This involves focusing on what autistic people say and looking at strengths and needs. We wanted to find out how autistic adults experience diagnostic assessments that include play. We asked autistic and non-autistic people to help us design our study and interview questions. We then interviewed 22 autistic adults to find out what they think about the use of play in assessments. We used a qualitative method called interpretative phenomenological analysis to analyse the data. Autistic adults told us about the different ways play was included in their diagnostic assessments. For example, some completed a diagnostic tool called the Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule. Autistic adults also talked about the importance of considering how autistic people are different to each other. For example, we found that play may not be useful for assessing women or girls who mask. This suggests that professionals should adopt a personalised approach to diagnostic assessments that use play catering to each person's needs. Our findings also suggested that professionals should assess strengths and differences as well as needs.

sheet.es: Si va a haber una evaluación diagnóstica que incluya juego, pregunte antes cómo se usará el juego y pida que se adapte a la persona: sus intereses, su manera de jugar y su necesidad de enmascarar o no. Conviene que se valoren también fortalezas y diferencias, no solo dificultades. La evidencia es un estudio cualitativo con entrevistas a 22 personas adultas autistas sobre su experiencia. Sus límites: refleja relatos de un grupo concreto de adultos, no a niñas, niños ni a todas las personas, y no demuestra qué método de evaluación es mejor.
sheet.en: If a diagnostic assessment will include play, ask beforehand how play will be used, and ask for it to be adapted to the person: their interests, their way of playing, and whether they mask. It helps to ask that strengths and differences are assessed too, not only difficulties. The evidence is a qualitative study based on interviews with 22 autistic adults about their experiences. Its limits: it reflects the accounts of one particular group of adults, not children or everyone, and it does not show which assessment method is best.
sheet.sv: Om en diagnostisk utredning ska innehålla lek, fråga i förväg hur leken ska användas och be om att den anpassas efter personen: intressen, sätt att leka och om personen maskerar. Be gärna om att styrkor och skillnader bedöms, inte bara svårigheter. Underlaget är en kvalitativ studie med intervjuer med 22 autistiska vuxna om deras erfarenheter. Begränsningar: den speglar berättelser från en viss grupp vuxna, inte barn eller alla personer, och visar inte vilken utredningsmetod som är bäst.

title: (Re)thinking about self-harm and autism: Findings from an online qualitative study on self-harm in autistic adults.
authors: Marsden SJ, Eastham R, Kaley A
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract There is a higher prevalence of self-harming behaviours within the autistic community than is experienced by the general population, in addition to co-occurring mental health conditions such as anxiety and depression. To date, research has focused on quantifying and categorising the numbers of autistic people self-harming, what types of harming they are engaging in and what functions the harming performs. Autism research has historically focused on the opinions and experiences of parents, carers and clinicians, with a belief that autistic people are unable to present their own experiences and thoughts accurately. This study adopted a qualitative method to develop themes arising from online forum discussions, using the words of autistic adults talking about how they experience and understand their self-harming behaviours. The analysis discovered that self-harming behaviours are used by autistic people as a way of coping with anxiety and depression and to relieve the build up of stress and sensory or mental overload that can otherwise lead to a meltdown. Repetitive behaviours such as stimming are also used to relieve the buildup of sensory over-stimulation and anxiety, but both stimming and meltdowns can also be self-harming behaviours if they cause tissue damage, and are believed to be childhood presentations which are stigmatised if expressed by an autistic adult. Many autistic adults find it hard to get help with self-harming behaviours because they are not taken seriously by professionals, as it is seen as part of autism and cannot be helped, or the professionals do not have enough knowledge of autism.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista se autolesiona, conviene preguntarle con calma qué le ayuda a sobrellevar y qué la sobrecarga (ansiedad, estrés, exceso sensorial o mental), y creerle. No lo trate como algo inevitable por ser autista. El estudio fue cualitativo: analizó debates en un foro en línea donde adultos autistas describían sus propias experiencias. Allí contaron que se autolesionan para afrontar la ansiedad, la depresión y la acumulación de sobrecarga, y que a menudo los profesionales no les toman en serio. Sus límites: refleja a quienes escriben en foros y no vale para todas las personas.
