Busque apoyo profesional (clínico, servicio de salud o servicio de crisis); si hay peligro inmediato, llame al número de emergencias de su país.
sheet.en: If an autistic person self-harms, calmly ask what helps them cope and what overwhelms them (anxiety, stress, sensory or mental overload), and believe them. Do not treat it as inevitable because they are autistic. This was a qualitative study that analysed online forum discussions in which autistic adults described their own experiences. They said they self-harm to cope with anxiety, depression and built-up overload, and that professionals often do not take them seriously. Its limits: it reflects people who write in forums and does not apply to everyone. Please seek professional help (a clinician, a health service or a crisis service); if there is immediate danger, call your country's emergency number.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person skadar sig själv, fråga lugnt vad som hjälper hen att klara sig och vad som överbelastar (ångest, stress, sensorisk eller mental överbelastning), och tro på hen. Se det inte som oundvikligt för att personen är autistisk. Studien var kvalitativ och analyserade diskussioner på ett nätforum där autistiska vuxna beskrev sina egna erfarenheter. De berättade att de skadar sig för att hantera ångest, depression och uppbyggd överbelastning, och att yrkespersoner ofta inte tar dem på allvar. Begränsning: den speglar personer som skriver i forum och gäller inte alla. Sök professionell hjälp (läkare, vårdcentral eller krisstöd); vid akut fara, ring ditt lands nödnummer.

title: Health care transition quadruple aim outcomes for IDD: Scoping review.
authors: Fremion E, Irby K, Jan S, Somerville CS, Shanske S, Szalda D, Uluer A, Shah P
abstract: Purpose Structured HCT models addressing planning, transfer, and integration into adult care for adolescents and young adults with childhood-acquired chronic conditions are becoming more prevalent. However, consensus on outcome measures to assess health care transition (HCT) interventions particularly for intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD) population is lacking. This scoping review identified potential HCT outcome measures for young adults (aged 18-26) with IDD using the Quadruple Aim Framework. Methods On August 6, 2021 and April 27, 2023, Medline Ovid, Embase, Web of Science, PsycINFO, and Cochrane databases were searched using the terms "young adult," "intellectual disability," "developmental disability, "cognitive dysfunction," "autism," "cerebral palsy," "spina bifida," and "transition to adult care." Searches were limited to publications in English and published from 2000 to present. Observational and experimental (qualitative or quantitative) studies were included if participants were young adults (median/mean ages 18-26) with IDD (Autism, cerebral palsy, Down syndrome, spina bifida, or other IDD-related conditions) and study outcomes addressed one of the Quadruple Aim domains (population health, patient/family experience, cost/utilization, and healthcare provider/caregiver experience). Studies were excluded if participants had attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder or learning disability only, if outcomes were primarily educational or vocational, or if publications were reviews, abstracts, or not in English. Results One hundred and three articles were included data extraction. Articles were categorized under the Quadruple Aim domains: Population Health (43), Patient/Caregiver Healthcare Experience included (23), Cost/Utilization (24), and Healthcare Provider/Caregiver Experience (15). Most articles were observational and utilized a variety of assessments or internally developed questions as measures. Conclusions While studies describing HCT outcomes for the IDD population are limited and measures are inconsistent, studies pertaining to Quadruple Aim outcomes identified in this review can further direct efforts towards consensus and standardization of HCT outcome measures to address the needs of individuals with IDD, their families, and caregivers/providers.

title: Application of clown care in hospitalized children: A scoping review.
authors: Xin G, Yingping F, Yue C, Jiaming W, Xue H
abstract: Purpose This study aims to provide healthcare providers with insights into relevant interventions by examining the timing, format, content, outcome measures, and effects of clown care interventions on hospitalized children. Methods This study utilized a scoping review methodology based on the framework by Arksey and O'Malley. The search for Chinese and English literature on the utilization of clown care for hospitalized children was conducted in databases including CNKI, VIP, Wanfang, China Biology Medicine Database, PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, CINAHL, and Cochrane Library. At the same time, the references and other grey literatures included in the paper were also manually searched. covering publications from inception to December 10, 2023. Screening of the literature was done based on predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria, with data extraction and synthesis carried out independently by two researchers. Results Out of 1084 articles screened, 18 were included. Clown care can be used with children who have burns, perioperative care, fracture rehabilitation, autism, puncture therapy, chemotherapy, respiratory pathologies and disabled children, according to a review of the literature. Clown care is feasible and available for these kids, and it has been shown to have favorable impacts. The main interventions used in clown care are guided imagery, cognitive coping, emotional reflection, distraction, and empowerment. Physical(reduced children's pain levels), psychological(reduced anxiety, improved coping skills, quicker recovery), cognitive-behavioral(for example, the number of meaningful words that children with autism say in 10 minutes.), and other indications are the several types of clown care outcome indicators. Conclusions Clown care can lessen a hospitalized child's pain, alleviate their worry, and divert their focus from illness and suffering. However, not all pediatric patients benefit from clown care. Every youngster is an independent individual with unique personality traits, and some may experience intense pain along with a terror of the clown role. Future research should concentrate on understanding the characteristics of hospitalized children to develop tailored clown care programs that can enhance clinical effectiveness. Trial registration number https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/B4KMV.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija va a ser hospitalizado, puede preguntar al equipo si hay visitas de payasos de hospital, pero conviene ver antes cómo reacciona esa persona. Algunas niñas y niños se asustan con el payaso, así que ofrezca siempre la opción de decir que no. La evidencia es una revisión de alcance de 18 artículos, de 1084 revisados, con niñez hospitalizada, incluida la autista. Indica menos dolor y menos ansiedad. Sus límites: no todos los niños se benefician, los estudios son variados y no demuestran qué funcionará con su hijo o hija.
sheet.en: If your child is going to be in hospital, you can ask the team whether hospital clown visits are available, but first consider how your child usually reacts to this kind of thing. Some children are frightened by the clown, so always make saying no an option. The evidence is a scoping review of 18 articles, from 1084 screened, covering hospitalized children, including autistic children. It points to less pain and less anxiety. Its limits: not every child benefits, the studies vary, and it cannot show what will work for your child.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn ska läggas in på sjukhus kan du fråga vårdteamet om det finns sjukhusclowner, men tänk först på hur ditt barn brukar reagera. Vissa barn blir rädda för clownen, så låt det alltid vara okej att säga nej. Underlaget är en kartläggande översikt av 18 artiklar, av 1084 granskade, om inlagda barn, bland annat autistiska barn. Den pekar på mindre smärta och mindre oro. Begränsningar: inte alla barn har nytta av det, studierna är olika och översikten kan inte visa vad som fungerar för just ditt barn.

title: Camouflaging in neurodivergent and neurotypical girls at the transition to adolescence and its relationship to mental health: A participatory methods research study.
authors: McKinney A, O'Brien S, Maybin JA, Chan SWY, Richer S, Rhodes S
abstract: Background Adolescent girls with diagnoses of autism, ADHD and/or developmental coordination disorder (DCD) are at higher risk for mental health problems than boys with the same diagnoses and neurotypical girls. These girls are called neurodivergent here, though neurodivergence includes a broader range of diagnoses. One possible reason for this mental health disparity could be camouflaging, a coping strategy used more by girls. Camouflaging is when the individual pretends to be neurotypical, often involving substantial effort. This study aims to understand: (a) if the use of camouflaging has started by early adolescence, (b) how components of camouflaging (assimilation, masking, and compensation) present at this age, (c) if age predicts camouflaging and (d) what is the relationship with mental health. Methods Participatory methods: A co-production team of 15 adult neurodivergent women co-produced the project and ranked camouflaging as their most important research theme. Main Study: Participants were 119 girls (70 neurodivergent, 49 neurotypical) aged 11-14 years. A transdiagnostic approach was adopted and the neurodivergent group had a diagnosis of autism, ADHD and/or DCD. Girls completed self-report measures of camouflaging, anxiety, and depression in an online meeting with a researcher. Results Neurodivergent and neurotypical girls presented similarly on two components of camouflaging namely masking and compensation, components related to presenting in a socially acceptable way and mimicry. Groups differed on the assimilation component, which is related to trying to fit in and involves the feelings of pretending/acting. Age had a medium effect on camouflaging with higher levels of camouflaging observed in older girls. Camouflaging scores strongly predicted anxiety and depression scores in both groups. Conclusions The use of camouflaging, specifically assimilation, is evident in a transdiagnostic sample of 11-14 year old neurodivergent girls. Importantly, the strong relationship between camouflaging and poor mental health is present at this early age, substantiating the co-production team's insights.

sheet.es: Si cuidas de una chica neurodivergente de 11 a 14 años, puede ayudar preguntarle con calma si a veces siente que tiene que fingir para encajar, y ofrecerle espacios donde pueda ser ella misma sin esfuerzo. Es un estudio con métodos participativos: un equipo de 15 mujeres neurodivergentes adultas co-produjo el proyecto, y 119 chicas de 11-14 años (70 neurodivergentes, 49 neurotípicas) respondieron cuestionarios en línea. Más camuflaje se relacionó con más ansiedad y depresión en ambos grupos, y fue mayor en las chicas mayores. Sus límites: mide asociaciones en un momento dado, no demuestra causa, y no describe a todas las chicas.
sheet.en: If you support a neurodivergent girl aged 11 to 14, it may help to ask her calmly whether she sometimes feels she has to pretend in order to fit in, and to offer spaces where she can be herself without effort. This was a participatory study: a team of 15 adult neurodivergent women co-produced it, and 119 girls aged 11-14 (70 neurodivergent, 49 neurotypical) completed online questionnaires. More camouflaging went with more anxiety and depression in both groups, and was higher in older girls. Its limits: it shows links at one point in time, not cause, and it does not describe every girl.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en neurodivergent flicka i åldern 11 till 14 kan det hjälpa att lugnt fråga om hon ibland känner att hon måste låtsas för att passa in, och att erbjuda miljöer där hon kan vara sig själv utan ansträngning. Studien använde deltagande metoder: ett team med 15 vuxna neurodivergenta kvinnor medskapade projektet, och 119 flickor i åldern 11-14 (70 neurodivergenta, 49 neurotypiska) fyllde i enkäter online. Mer kamouflering hängde ihop med mer ångest och depression i båda grupperna, och var högre hos äldre flickor. Begränsningar: den visar samband vid en tidpunkt, inte orsak, och beskriver inte alla flickor.

title: Understanding early maladaptive schemas in autistic and ADHD individuals: exploring the impact, changing the narrative, and schema therapy considerations.
authors: Spicer L, DeCicco E, Clarke A, Ambrosius R, Yalcin O
abstract: Autistic/ADHD individuals are increasingly recognised as a valid minority group, with consistent research demonstrating a higher prevalence of co-occurring mental health conditions such as PTSD, anxiety, depression, substance use, and eating disorders among other mental health challenges. Due to this, there is increasing focus on the adaptations required for Autistic and ADHD individuals of current therapeutic approaches such as Schema Therapy. Particular emphasis when creating these adaptations needs to include looking at the developmental experiences, social influences, and continued adversity faced by Autistic and ADHD individuals across the lifespan, and how the narrative around Autism and ADHD within psychotherapy in general needs to change. This paper critically examines the role of attachment, unmet needs, and adverse childhood experiences in Autistic and ADHD individuals and the subsequent impact on schema development and maintenance and mental health. This will include an overview of the current literature in this area, reconsideration of understandings of Autism and ADHD, particular therapeutic considerations and adjustments and importantly discussion around the wider societal changes that need to occur to prevent schema development and reinforcement across the lifespan.

sheet.es: Si buscas apoyo terapéutico para una persona autista o con TDAH, pregunta si el profesional adapta su enfoque y entiende cómo las experiencias vividas, las necesidades no cubiertas y la adversidad influyen en cómo se ve a sí misma. Esta es una revisión de la bibliografía sobre terapia de esquemas, apego y experiencias adversas en la infancia en personas autistas y con TDAH. Es una revisión crítica, no un ensayo con participantes, y no demuestra qué adaptación funciona mejor. No es una norma para todas las personas; cada una necesita un apoyo propio, y los cambios sociales también importan.
sheet.en: If you are looking for therapy for an autistic or ADHD person, ask whether the professional adapts their approach and understands how lived experiences, unmet needs and ongoing adversity shape the way a person sees themselves. This is a review of the literature on schema therapy, attachment and adverse childhood experiences in autistic and ADHD people. It is a critical review, not a trial with participants, so it cannot show which adaptation works best. It is not a rule for everyone; each person needs their own support, and wider social change matters too.
sheet.sv: Om du söker terapi för en autistisk person eller en person med ADHD, fråga om terapeuten anpassar sitt arbetssätt och förstår hur levda erfarenheter, obemötta behov och pågående motgångar formar hur personen ser på sig själv. Detta är en översikt av litteraturen om schematerapi, anknytning och svåra upplevelser i barndomen hos autistiska personer och personer med ADHD. Det är en kritisk översikt, inte en studie med deltagare, så den visar inte vilken anpassning som fungerar bäst. Den är ingen regel för alla; varje person behöver eget stöd, och samhällsförändringar spelar också roll.

title: Wearable Solutions Using Physiological Signals for Stress Monitoring on Individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD): A Systematic Literature Review.
authors: Cano S, Cubillos C, Alfaro R, Romo A, García M, Moreira F
abstract: Some previous studies have focused on using physiological signals to detect stress in individuals with ASD through wearable devices, yet few have focused on how to design such solutions. Wearable technology may be a valuable tool to aid parents and caregivers in monitoring the emotional states of individuals with ASD who are at high risk of experiencing very stressful situations. However, effective wearable devices for individuals with ASD may need to differ from solutions for those without ASD. People with ASD often have sensory sensitivity and may, therefore, not tolerate certain types of accessories and experience discomfort when using them. We used the Scopus, PubMed, WoS, and IEEE-Xplore databases to search for studies published from 2014 to 2024 to answer four research questions related to wearable solutions for individuals with ASD, physiological parameters, and techniques/processes used for stress detection. Our review found 31 articles; not all studies considered individuals with ASD, and some were beyond the scope of this review. Most of the studies reviewed are based on cardiac activity for stress monitoring using photoplethysmography (PPG) and electrocardiography (ECG). However, limitations include small sample sizes, variability in study conditions, and the need for customization in stress detection algorithms. In addition, there is a need to customize the stress threshold due to the device's high individual variability and sensitivity. The potential of wearable solutions for stress monitoring in ASD is evident, but challenges include the need for user-friendly and unobtrusive designs and integrating these technologies into comprehensive care plans.

sheet.es: Si piensa usar un dispositivo para vigilar el estrés de una persona autista, pruebe primero si tolera el accesorio: la sensibilidad sensorial puede hacer que le resulte incómodo. Pregúntele a ella y observe su comodidad. Además, el umbral de estrés debería ajustarse a cada persona. Esta revisión sistemática de estudios de 2014 a 2024 encontró 31 artículos; no todos incluían a personas autistas. La mayoría usaba la actividad cardiaca. Sus límites: muestras pequeñas, condiciones de estudio variables y algoritmos que necesitan personalizarse. No demuestra que estos dispositivos sirvan a todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you are thinking of using a wearable to monitor stress in an autistic person, first check whether they tolerate the device: sensory sensitivity can make accessories uncomfortable. Ask them and watch how they respond. The stress threshold also needs to be adjusted to each person. This systematic review of studies from 2014 to 2024 found 31 articles; not all included autistic people. Most used heart activity. Its limits: small samples, varied study conditions and algorithms that need customizing. It does not show that these devices work for everyone.
sheet.sv: Om du funderar på en bärbar enhet för att följa stress hos en autistisk person, kolla först om hen tolererar den: sensorisk känslighet kan göra tillbehör obekväma. Fråga hen och se hur hen reagerar. Stressgränsen behöver också anpassas till varje person. Denna systematiska översikt av studier från 2014 till 2024 hittade 31 artiklar; inte alla inkluderade autistiska personer. De flesta använde hjärtaktivitet. Begränsningar: små urval, varierande studieförhållanden och algoritmer som behöver anpassas. Den visar inte att enheterna fungerar för alla.

title: Approaches to improving mental healthcare for autistic people: systematic review.
authors: Loizou S, Pemovska T, Stefanidou T, Foye U, Cooper R, Kular A, Greenburgh A, Baldwin H, Griffiths J, Saunders KRK, Barnett P, Minchin M, Brady G, Ahmed N, Parker J, Chipp B, Olive RR, Jackson R, Timme
abstract: Background Autistic people have a high likelihood of developing mental health difficulties but a low chance of receiving effective mental healthcare. Therefore, there is a need to identify and examine strategies to improve mental healthcare for autistic people. Aims To identify strategies that have been implemented to improve access, experiences of care and mental health outcomes for autistic adults, and to examine evidence on their acceptability, feasibility and effectiveness. Method A co-produced systematic review was conducted. MEDLINE, PsycINFO, CINHAL, medRxiv and PsyArXiv were searched. We included all study designs reporting acceptability or feasibility outcomes and empirical quantitative study designs reporting effectiveness outcomes. Data were synthesised using a narrative approach. Results A total of 30 articles were identified. These included 16 studies of adapted mental health interventions, eight studies of service improvements and six studies of bespoke mental health interventions developed for autistic people. There was no conclusive evidence on effectiveness. However, most bespoke and adapted approaches appeared to be feasible and acceptable. Identified adaptations appeared to be acceptable and feasible, including increasing knowledge and detection of autism, providing environmental adjustments and communication accommodations, accommodating individual differences and modifying the structure and content of interventions. Conclusion Many identified strategies are feasible and acceptable, and can be readily implemented in services with the potential to make mental healthcare more suitable for autistic people, but important research gaps remain. Future research should address these and investigate a co-produced package of service improvement measures.

sheet.es: Antes de una cita de salud mental, pregunta al servicio qué adaptaciones ofrecen: un espacio tranquilo, comunicación clara (por ejemplo, por escrito), flexibilidad en el ritmo y en la estructura de las sesiones. Pedirlas es razonable. La evidencia es una revisión sistemática coproducida que reunió 30 artículos sobre adaptaciones y mejoras de servicios para personas autistas adultas. La mayoría de los enfoques parecían factibles y aceptables. Sin embargo, no hay pruebas concluyentes de que mejoren los resultados y siguen existiendo importantes lagunas de investigación. No todas las personas necesitan lo mismo, así que conviene decidir cada ajuste con la persona autista.
sheet.en: Before a mental health appointment, ask the service what adjustments they can offer: a quiet space, clear communication (for example in writing), and flexibility in pace and in how sessions are structured. Asking for these is reasonable. The evidence is a co-produced systematic review that gathered 30 articles on adaptations and service improvements for autistic adults. Most approaches appeared feasible and acceptable. However, there was no conclusive evidence that they improve outcomes, and important research gaps remain. Not everyone needs the same things, so it helps to decide each adjustment together with the autistic person.
sheet.sv: Inför ett besök inom psykisk hälsovård: fråga vilka anpassningar vården kan erbjuda, till exempel ett lugnt rum, tydlig kommunikation (till exempel skriftlig) och flexibilitet i tempo och upplägg. Det är rimligt att be om dem. Underlaget är en samskapad systematisk översikt med 30 artiklar om anpassningar och förbättringar av vård för autistiska vuxna. De flesta tillvägagångssätten verkade genomförbara och acceptabla. Det fanns dock inga entydiga belägg för att de förbättrar resultaten, och viktiga kunskapsluckor finns kvar. Alla behöver inte samma sak, så bestäm varje anpassning tillsammans med den autistiska personen.

title: Addressing Stigma-Related Health Disparities for Autistic Individuals Through Cultural Competemility: Insights from Research and Lived Experience.
authors: Hotez E, Phan JM, Truong DM
abstract: Purpose of review Autistic individuals experience disproportionate stigma across the life course in interpersonal, healthcare, and educational contexts. These experiences contribute to negative health and healthcare outcomes for this population. This paper seeks to describe autistic individuals' experiences of stigma and marginalization; discuss frameworks such as Campinha-Bacote's innovative concept of cultural competemility and its relevance to autistic populations; offer recommendations to healthcare providers based on this framework; and apply theory to practice in a case study. Recent findings Autistic individuals increasingly understand autism as an important aspect of their identity. There are, however, few culturally informed healthcare efforts that reflect this understanding. As a result, efforts to address stigma-related health disparities for this population have limited effectiveness. In this manuscript, we highlight opportunities within clinical encounters, medical training, healthcare offices and systems, and research to provide higher quality culturally informed care to autistic populations and address stigma-related health disparities.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista a una consulta médica, puedes avisar de antemano que ser autista forma parte de su identidad y pedir que el equipo la trate con respeto y curiosidad, no con prejuicios. Es una revisión que recoge investigación y experiencia vivida de personas autistas. Señala que el estigma afecta a la salud y a la atención recibida, y que hay pocos servicios sanitarios que reflejen esa visión de la identidad. Sus recomendaciones son para profesionales, y el estudio incluye un caso de ejemplo, no una prueba en personas. No garantiza resultados en cada persona ni en cada consulta.
sheet.en: If you go with an autistic person to a medical appointment, you can say beforehand that being autistic is part of their identity and ask the team to respond with respect and curiosity rather than assumptions. This is a review drawing on research and the lived experience of autistic people. It describes how stigma affects health and the care people receive, and notes that few healthcare services reflect this view of identity. Its recommendations are aimed at professionals, and it uses an example case rather than testing anything with people. It cannot promise the same results for every person or every appointment.
sheet.sv: Om du följer med en autistisk person till ett läkarbesök kan du i förväg berätta att autism är en del av personens identitet och be teamet bemöta den med respekt och nyfikenhet, inte med förutfattade meningar. Detta är en översikt som bygger på forskning och autistiska människors egna erfarenheter. Den beskriver hur stigma påverkar hälsa och vård, och att få vårdtjänster speglar denna syn på identitet. Rekommendationerna riktar sig till vårdpersonal, och studien använder ett exempelfall i stället för att testa något på människor. Den kan inte lova samma resultat för varje person eller varje besök.

title: The Effect of Narrative Intervention on Spoken Narrative and Reading Comprehension Abilities in Farsi-Speaking Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
authors: Masoumi E, Soleymani Z, Modarresi Y, Maroufizadeh S, Mohseni F
journal: Medical journal of the Islamic Republic of Iran
abstract: Background Children with autism spectrum disorders (ASD) show prominent deficits in pragmatic aspects of language such as spoken narrative. Deficits in spoken narrative in school years lead to deficits in reading comprehension. Therefore, this randomized clinical trial research examined the influence of narrative intervention on spoken narrative and reading comprehension abilities in children with ASD. Methods In the current double-blind, randomized clinical trial study, 21 students with ASD from second to seventh grade participated in the study. Two intervention methods were provided three times a week and a total of 24 sessions of 45 minutes. The experimental group received the Supporting Knowledge in Language and Literacy (SKILL) program and the control group received Traditional Language Therapy (TLT). The score of macrostructures, microstructures, perspective-taking index, narrative complexity, Story knowledge index, and reading comprehension score were measured pre and post-intervention. ANCOVA was used for between- within-group comparisons analysis. Results The experimental group indicated significant improvement in macrostructure ( P 2 = 0.614), microstructure ( P = 0.012, η 2 = 0.303), narrative complexity ( P 2 = 0.585), story knowledge index ( P 2 = 0.574) and perspective taking index ( P 2 = 0.553) compared to the control group. However, the difference between the two groups in reading comprehension skills was not significant in post-intervention ( P = 0.457, η 2 = 0.031). Conclusion The results showed the efficacy of the three stages of the SKILL program compared to TLT in spoken narrative. Also, the results of the study showed that the SKILL program and TLT have the same effect on improving reading comprehension.

sheet.es: Si una niña o un niño autista tiene dificultades para contar historias, puede valer la pena preguntar al equipo de logopedia por programas centrados en la narración, como SKILL. No hay que esperar que mejore por sí sola la comprensión lectora. Evidencia: ensayo aleatorizado con 21 estudiantes autistas de segundo a séptimo grado, que hablaban farsi; recibieron 24 sesiones de 45 minutos, SKILL o terapia del lenguaje tradicional. El grupo SKILL mejoró más al contar historias; en comprensión lectora no hubo diferencia significativa. Límites: muestra pequeña, un solo idioma y contexto, y cada persona es distinta, así que no es una regla general.
sheet.en: If an autistic child finds telling stories hard, it may be worth asking their speech-language team about narrative-focused programmes such as SKILL. Don't assume reading comprehension will improve by itself. Evidence: a randomized trial with 21 Farsi-speaking autistic students from second to seventh grade, who received 24 sessions of 45 minutes of either SKILL or traditional language therapy. The SKILL group improved more in spoken storytelling; reading comprehension showed no significant difference between groups. Limits: small sample, one language and setting, and every child is different, so this is not a rule for everyone.
sheet.sv: Om ett autistiskt barn tycker det är svårt att berätta historier kan det löna sig att fråga logopedteamet om program med fokus på berättande, som SKILL. Räkna inte med att läsförståelsen förbättras av sig själv. Evidens: en randomiserad studie med 21 persisktalande autistiska elever från andra till sjunde klass, som fick 24 pass på 45 minuter med antingen SKILL eller traditionell språkterapi. SKILL-gruppen förbättrades mer i muntligt berättande; i läsförståelse fanns ingen signifikant skillnad mellan grupperna. Begränsningar: litet urval, ett språk och en miljö, och alla barn är olika, så det är ingen regel för alla.

title: Differential diagnosis of autism, attachment disorders, complex post-traumatic stress disorder and emotionally unstable personality disorder: A Delphi study.
authors: Sarr R, Spain D, Quinton AMG, Happé F, Brewin CR, Radcliffe J, Jowett S, Miles S, González RA, Albert I, Scholwin A, Stirling M, Markham S, Strange S, Rumball F
abstract: Individuals diagnosed with autism, attachment disorders, emotionally unstable personality disorder (EUPD) or complex post-traumatic stress disorder (CPTSD) can present with similar features. This renders differential and accurate diagnosis of these conditions difficult, leading to diagnostic overshadowing and misdiagnosis. The purpose of this study was to explore professionals' perspectives on the differential diagnosis of autism, attachment disorders and CPTSD in young people; and of autism, CPTSD and EUPD in adults. A co-produced three-round Delphi study gathered information through a series of questionnaires from 106 international professionals with expertise in assessing and/or diagnosing at least one of these conditions. To provide specialist guidance and data triangulation, working groups of experts by experience, clinicians and researchers were consulted. Delphi statements were considered to have reached consensus if at least 80% of participants were in agreement. Two hundred and seventy-five Delphi statements reached consensus. Overlapping and differentiating features, methods of assessment, difficulties encountered during differential diagnosis and suggestions for improvements were identified. The findings highlight current practices for differential diagnosis of autism, attachment disorders, CPTSD and EUPD in young people and adults. Areas for future research, clinical and service provision implications, were also identified.

title: Development and Psychometric Properties of the Pain and Sensitivity Reactivity Scale in a Diverse Sample of Autistic People.
authors: Martínez-González AE, Cervin M, Piqueras JA, Infante-Cañete L, Pérez-Sánchez S
abstract: Background Recent studies indicate the need to examine how the gut microbiota-brain axis is implicated in pain, sensory reactivity and gastro-intestinal symptoms in autism spectrum disorder (ASD), but no scale exists that assesses all these constructs simultaneously. Methods We created a pool of 100 items based on the real-world experience of autistic people, and a multidisciplinary team and stakeholders reduced this pool to 50 items assessing pain, sensory hypersensitivity, and sensory hyposensitivity. In the present study, we present this new assessment tool, the Pain and Sensitivity Reactivity Scale (PSRS), and examine its psychometric properties in a sample of 270 individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD; mean age = 9.44, SD = 4.97), of which almost half (45%) had intellectual disability (ID). Results A factorial model of three factors (pain, hyporeactivity, and hyperreactivity) and five specific factors for sensory hypo- and hyperreactivity, respectively, fitted the data well. Good to excellent internal consistency and adequate test-retest reliability was found for most PSRS scales. Sound psychometric properties were found in individuals with and without ID. Correlations with other measures of sensory sensitivity and pain indicated sound convergent validity. Conclusions PSRS shows promise as a reliable measure to analyze pain and sensory reactivity in autistic people regardless of whether they have ID or not. The measure overcomes several limitations of previous assessment tools and includes variables that are important for the understanding of the gut microbiota-brain axis in ASD.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista, esta escala puede ayudarte a ordenar cómo vive el dolor y los sentidos: qué le resulta demasiado intenso, qué apenas nota y cómo expresa el dolor. Puedes llevar tus observaciones a su profesional de salud. Es un estudio de desarrollo de una escala, creada a partir de la experiencia de personas autistas, con 270 personas autistas (edad media 9.44), casi la mitad (45%) con discapacidad intelectual. Mostró buena fiabilidad en general, con y sin discapacidad intelectual. Sus límites: es una herramienta de medición, no un diagnóstico, y no dice cómo es cada persona ni qué hacer en cada caso.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person, this scale may help you organise how they experience pain and the senses: what feels too intense, what they barely notice, and how they show pain. You can bring your observations to their health professional. This is a scale-development study, built from autistic people's own experience, with 270 autistic people (mean age 9.44), almost half (45%) with intellectual disability. It showed good reliability overall, with and without intellectual disability. Its limits: it is a measurement tool, not a diagnosis, and it cannot tell you how any one person is or what to do in each case.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person kan skalan hjälpa dig att reda ut hur personen upplever smärta och sinnesintryck: vad som känns för starkt, vad som knappt märks och hur smärta visas. Du kan ta med dina observationer till personens vårdgivare. Det är en studie där en skala utvecklades utifrån autistiska personers egna erfarenheter, med 270 autistiska personer (medelålder 9.44), varav nästan hälften (45%) hade intellektuell funktionsnedsättning. Skalan visade överlag god tillförlitlighet, både med och utan intellektuell funktionsnedsättning. Begränsningar: det är ett mätverktyg, inte en diagnos, och det säger inte hur en enskild person är eller vad som ska göras i varje fall.

title: The experience of mothers of autistic children with a pathological demand avoidance profile: an interpretative phenomenological analysis.
authors: Curtis S, Izett E
abstract: Purpose Emergent research literature has identified emotional and behavioural challenges for autistic children with a pathological demand avoidance profile. However, understanding of their parents' experience is limited. This study aimed to explore the experience of parents of autistic children with a pathological demand avoidance profile. Methods Semi-structured interviews were completed with ten parents of autistic children with a pathological demand avoidance profile, aged between 5 and 11 years (M = 8.5, SD = 1.90). All participants were mothers, aged 33-50 years (M = 42, SD = 5.35). To explore what meaning participants gave to their lived experience, an interpretative phenomenological analysis was conducted on interview data. Results Four main themes were developed from the interpretative phenomenological analysis; the benefit of a shared understanding about pathological demand avoidance to the parents and their children, the power of pathological demand avoidance and the impact on families, the emotional experience of mothers, and the various ways in which they coped. Conclusion The need for further recognition and understanding about pathological demand avoidance is emphasised through recommendations for future research. As is the need for flexible, informed, and appropriate support for demand avoidant children and their families.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a un niño autista con perfil de evitación patológica de demandas, buscar a personas y profesionales que entiendan este perfil puede ayudar a toda la familia, y también tu propio apoyo importa. Es un estudio cualitativo con entrevistas a diez madres de niños autistas de 5 a 11 años. Las madres hablaron de la comprensión compartida, del impacto en las familias, de sus emociones y de cómo se las arreglaban. Sus límites: solo participaron madres, son pocas y sus experiencias no representan a todas las familias. Tampoco recoge la voz de los niños.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic child with a pathological demand avoidance profile, finding people and professionals who understand this profile may help the whole family, and your own support matters too. This is a qualitative study using interviews with ten mothers of autistic children aged 5 to 11. They described the value of shared understanding, the impact on families, their emotions and how they coped. Limits: only mothers took part, the group is small, and their experiences do not represent every family. The children's own voices were not included.
sheet.sv: Om du ger omsorg till ett autistiskt barn med profil för patologisk kravundvikande kan det hjälpa hela familjen att hitta människor och yrkespersoner som förstår profilen, och ditt eget stöd räknas också. Det är en kvalitativ studie med intervjuer av tio mammor till autistiska barn i åldrarna 5 till 11. De berättade om värdet av delad förståelse, påverkan på familjer, sina känslor och hur de hanterade situationen. Begränsningar: bara mammor deltog, gruppen är liten och deras erfarenheter gäller inte alla familjer. Barnens egna röster ingick inte.

title: Autistic and transgender/gender diverse people's experiences of health and healthcare.
authors: Green K, Weir E, Wright L, Allison C, Baron-Cohen S
abstract: Background Autistic people and transgender/gender diverse people experience poorer healthcare experiences and greater risk of diagnosed, suspected, and assessment recommended health conditions, compared to non-autistic and cisgender individuals, respectively. Despite this, there is a paucity of studies on the healthcare experiences and health outcomes of transgender/gender diverse autistic individuals. Methods We compared the healthcare experiences and health outcomes of cisgender autistic (n = 1094), transgender/gender diverse autistic (n = 174), and cisgender non-autistic adults (n = 1295) via an anonymous, self-report survey. All individuals whose sex assigned at birth did not match their current gender identity were categorized as transgender/gender diverse; this was possible to determine, as the survey asked about sex assigned at birth and gender in separate questions. Unfortunately, n = 57 transgender/gender diverse non-autistic participants were excluded from these analyses a priori, due to low power. Unadjusted and adjusted binomial logistic regression models with FDR correction were employed to assess healthcare experiences and rates of co-occurring mental and physical health conditions. Results Both transgender/gender diverse and cisgender autistic adults had higher rates of all health conditions (including conditions that are formally diagnosed, suspected, or recommended for assessment), compared to cisgender non-autistic adults. Transgender/gender diverse autistic adults were 2.3 times more likely to report a physical health condition, 10.9 times more likely to report a mental health condition, and 5.8 times more likely to report self-harm than cisgender non-autistic adults. Both autistic groups also reported significantly poorer healthcare experiences across 50/51 items. Limitations These data were not originally collected to understand the experiences of transgender/gender diverse individuals. In addition, our recruitment strategies, use of a convenience sampling method, and the use of a self-report survey limit the generalizability of the study. As our sample was biased towards white individuals, UK residents, relatively highly educated individuals, those assigned female at birth, and those who currently identify as female, our findings may be less applicable to individuals of differing demographics. Finally, the present study does not include information on the experiences of transgender/gender diverse non-autistic people. Conclusions Autistic people have poorer self-reported health and healthcare; however, being gender diverse is associated with further risk for certain adverse experiences and outcomes. Future research on the health and healthcare experiences of transgender/gender diverse autistic people is urgently needed. In particular, forthcoming studies in this area should aim to recruit large-scale and representative studies and should compare the experiences of transgender/gender diverse autistic people to those of transgender/gender diverse non-autistic people. Greater recognition of challenges and reasonable adjustments are essential for people with marginalized, intersectional identities in clinical practice.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista, sobre todo si también es trans o de género diverso, conviene preparar con ella las citas médicas y pedir ajustes razonables, como más tiempo o información por escrito. Es una encuesta anónima de autoinforme con adultos: 1094 autistas cisgénero, 174 autistas trans o de género diverso y 1295 no autistas cisgénero. Las personas autistas informaron peores experiencias sanitarias en 50/51 ítems y más autolesiones; en el grupo trans o de género diverso, 5.8 veces más que el grupo de comparación. Limitaciones: muestra de conveniencia, mayoría blanca, británica y con estudios, y sin grupo trans no autista. No sirve como regla para cada persona. Si hay preocupación por autolesiones o suicidio, acude a un profesional de la salud o a un servicio de crisis; ante peligro inmediato, llama al número de emergencias de tu país.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person, especially one who is also transgender or gender diverse, it helps to prepare medical appointments together and ask for reasonable adjustments, such as more time or written information. This was an anonymous self-report survey of adults: 1094 cisgender autistic, 174 transgender/gender diverse autistic and 1295 cisgender non-autistic people. Autistic people reported poorer healthcare experiences on 50/51 items and more self-harm; in the transgender/gender diverse group it was 5.8 times more likely than in the comparison group. Limits: a convenience sample, mostly white, UK-based and highly educated, with no transgender non-autistic comparison group. It is not a rule for every person. If you are worried about self-harm or suicide, contact a clinician, a health service or a crisis service; in immediate danger, call your country's emergency number.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person, särskilt om hen också är transperson eller könsdiverse, kan det hjälpa att förbereda vårdbesök tillsammans och be om rimliga anpassningar, till exempel mer tid eller skriftlig information. Det var en anonym enkät med vuxna: 1094 cisgender autistiska, 174 transpersoner eller könsdiversa autistiska och 1295 cisgender icke-autistiska. Autistiska personer rapporterade sämre vårderfarenheter på 50/51 punkter och mer självskada; i gruppen transpersoner eller könsdiversa var det 5.8 gånger mer sannolikt än i jämförelsegruppen. Begränsningar: bekvämlighetsurval, mest vita, brittiska och högutbildade, och ingen icke-autistisk transgrupp. Det är ingen regel för alla. Om du oroar dig för självskada eller självmord, kontakta sjukvården, en läkare eller en krisjour; vid akut fara, ring ditt lands nödnummer.

title: The global epidemiology and health burden of the autism spectrum: findings from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021.
authors: Global Burden of Disease Study 2021 Autism Spectrum Collaborators
abstract: Background High-quality estimates of the epidemiology of the autism spectrum and the health needs of autistic people are necessary for service planners and resource allocators. Here we present the global prevalence and health burden of autism spectrum disorder from the Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study (GBD) 2021 following improvements to the epidemiological data and burden estimation methods. Methods For GBD 2021, a systematic literature review involving searches in PubMed, Embase, PsycINFO, the Global Health Data Exchange, and consultation with experts identified data on the epidemiology of autism spectrum disorder. Eligible data were used to estimate prevalence via a Bayesian meta-regression tool (DisMod-MR 2.1). Modelled prevalence and disability weights were used to estimate health burden in years lived with disability (YLDs) as the measure of non-fatal health burden and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) as the measure of overall health burden. Data by ethnicity were not available. People with lived experience of autism were involved in the design, preparation, interpretation, and writing of this Article. Findings An estimated 61·8 million (95% uncertainty interval 52·1-72·7) individuals (one in every 127 people) were on the autism spectrum globally in 2021. The global age-standardised prevalence was 788·3 (663·8-927·2) per 100 000 people, equivalent to 1064·7 (898·5-1245·7) autistic males per 100 000 males and 508·1 (424·6-604·3) autistic females per 100 000 females. Autism spectrum disorder accounted for 11·5 million (7·8-16·3) DALYs, equivalent to 147·6 (100·2-208·2) DALYs per 100 000 people (age-standardised) globally. At the super-region level, age-standardised DALY rates ranged from 126·5 (86·0-178·0) per 100 000 people in southeast Asia, east Asia, and Oceania to 204·1 (140·7-284·7) per 100 000 people in the high-income super-region. DALYs were evident across the lifespan, emerging for children younger than age 5 years (169·2 [115·0-237·4] DALYs per 100 000 people) and decreasing with age (163·4 [110·6-229·8] DALYs per 100 000 people younger than 20 years and 137·7 [93·9-194·5] DALYs per 100 000 people aged 20 years and older). Autism spectrum disorder was ranked within the top-ten causes of non-fatal health burden for people younger than 20 years. Interpretation The high prevalence and high rank for non-fatal health burden of autism spectrum disorder in people younger than 20 years underscore the importance of early detection and support to autistic young people and their caregivers globally. Work to improve the precision and global representation of our findings is required, starting with better global coverage of epidemiological data so that geographical variations can be better ascertained. The work presented here can guide future research efforts, and importantly, decisions concerning allocation of health services that better address the needs of all autistic individuals. Funding Queensland Health and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation.

sheet.es: Su familia no está sola: alrededor de 1 de cada 127 personas en el mundo es autista, y las necesidades de apoyo existen a lo largo de toda la vida, especialmente en la infancia y la juventud. Esto respalda pedir evaluación temprana y apoyos concretos en la escuela y los servicios de salud, también para usted como cuidador. Puede usar estas cifras al solicitar recursos. Se trata de una revisión sistemática mundial (GBD 2021) que combinó estudios de muchos países mediante modelos estadísticos, con participación de personas autistas en su diseño y redacción. Sus límites: faltan datos de muchas regiones y por etnia, y las cifras promedio no describen a ninguna persona concreta.
sheet.en: Your family is not alone: about 1 in 127 people worldwide is autistic, and support needs exist across the lifespan, especially in childhood and youth. This backs up asking for early assessment and concrete support at school and in health services, including support for you as a caregiver. You can cite these figures when requesting resources. This is a global systematic review (GBD 2021) that combined studies from many countries using statistical modelling, with autistic people involved in its design and writing. Its limits: data are missing for many regions and by ethnicity, and average figures do not describe any individual person.
sheet.sv: Er familj är inte ensam: ungefär 1 av 127 människor i världen är autistisk, och behov av stöd finns genom hela livet, särskilt i barndomen och ungdomen. Det stärker er rätt att be om tidig utredning och konkret stöd i skolan och vården, även stöd till dig som anhörig. Du kan hänvisa till siffrorna när du ansöker om resurser. Det här är en global systematisk översikt (GBD 2021) som sammanställde studier från många länder med statistiska modeller, och autistiska personer deltog i design och skrivande. Begränsningar: data saknas för många regioner och om etnicitet, och genomsnitt beskriver inte en enskild person.

title: Effectiveness of the mobile Stress Autism Mate Junior application in reducing stress and improving quality of life in adolescents with autism: a pilot study.
authors: van Asselt A, Hoeberichts K, Demirel S, Scheeren A, Roke Y
abstract: Objective Studies indicate that stress levels of autistic adolescents may be particularly high. Therefore, support is needed to help them deal with their stressors. Stress Autism Mate (SAM) Junior, a mobile self-help tool, was designed in co-creation with adolescents with autism to help reduce daily stress levels. The app is based on the SAM app, which was previously shown to be effective in reducing stress in autistic adults. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of the SAM Junior app in reducing perceived stress and maladaptive coping styles, and increasing adaptive coping styles and quality of life in adolescents with autism. Methods A total of 24 Dutch adolescents with autism participated in this Single Case Experimental Design study. Sixteen of them (9 girls and 7 boys; M age = 15.0 years, SD = 1.9) completed all research phases. Data were collected at four time points separated by four weeks: Control, pre-test, post-test and follow-up. Linear mixed-effects models were used to analyze the data. Results At post-test, use of the SAM Junior app had no significant effects on participants' perceived stress (B = 0.31; 95% CI [-1.59, 2.22], p = .73), adaptive coping (B = -1.38; 95% CI [-5.69, 2.94], p = .51), maladaptive coping (B = -0.63; 95% CI [-4.56, 3.30], p = .74) and quality of life (B = -4.13; 95% CI [-12.19, 3.94], p = .29). These non-significant effects persisted at follow-up. Discussion Current preliminary results do not show effectiveness of the SAM Junior app to support adolescents with autism. Using the app as intended, without professional supervision, may have been too complex for this population. Further research is needed to determine the potential effects of the SAM Junior app with more certainty.

sheet.es: No des por hecho que una app de autoayuda reducirá el estrés de un adolescente autista; si la prueba, acompáñale al principio y observa cómo le va. Este estudio piloto con 24 adolescentes autistas neerlandeses (16 completaron todas las fases) probó la app SAM Junior y no encontró efectos significativos en el estrés, las formas de afrontamiento ni la calidad de vida, ni tras el uso ni en el seguimiento. Es un estudio pequeño y preliminar. Las autoras y autores sugieren que usarla sin supervisión profesional pudo resultar demasiado complejo, pero hace falta más investigación. Esto no significa que no pueda ayudar a alguien en concreto.
sheet.en: Don't assume a self-help app will lower an autistic teenager's stress; if they try one, sit with them at the start and notice how it goes for them. This pilot study followed 24 Dutch autistic adolescents (16 completed all phases) using the SAM Junior app. It found no significant effects on stress, coping styles or quality of life, either after use or at follow-up. The study was small and preliminary. The researchers suggest that using the app without professional supervision may have been too complex, and more research is needed. This does not mean it cannot help a particular person.
sheet.sv: Utgå inte från att en självhjälpsapp minskar en autistisk tonårings stress; om hen provar en, var med i början och se hur det fungerar för hen. Denna pilotstudie följde 24 nederländska autistiska ungdomar (16 slutförde alla faser) som använde appen SAM Junior. Den fann inga signifikanta effekter på stress, copingstrategier eller livskvalitet, varken efter användningen eller vid uppföljningen. Studien var liten och preliminär. Forskarna menar att det kan ha varit för komplicerat att använda appen utan professionell handledning, och mer forskning behövs. Det betyder inte att den inte kan hjälpa en enskild person.

title: The multifaceted role of mitochondria in autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Khaliulin I, Hamoudi W, Amal H
abstract: Normal brain functioning relies on high aerobic energy production provided by mitochondria. Failure to supply a sufficient amount of energy, seen in different brain disorders, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), may have a significant negative impact on brain development and support of different brain functions. Mitochondrial dysfunction, manifested in the abnormal activities of the electron transport chain and impaired energy metabolism, greatly contributes to ASD. The aberrant functioning of this organelle is of such high importance that ASD has been proposed as a mitochondrial disease. It should be noted that aerobic energy production is not the only function of the mitochondria. In particular, these organelles are involved in the regulation of Ca 2+ homeostasis, different mechanisms of programmed cell death, autophagy, and reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (ROS and RNS) production. Several syndromes originated from mitochondria-related mutations display ASD phenotype. Abnormalities in Ca 2+ handling and ATP production in the brain mitochondria affect synaptic transmission, plasticity, and synaptic development, contributing to ASD. ROS and Ca 2+ regulate the activity of the mitochondrial permeability transition pore (mPTP). The prolonged opening of this pore affects the redox state of the mitochondria, impairs oxidative phosphorylation, and activates apoptosis, ultimately leading to cell death. A dysregulation between the enhanced mitochondria-related processes of apoptosis and the inhibited autophagy leads to the accumulation of toxic products in the brains of individuals with ASD. Although many mitochondria-related mechanisms still have to be investigated, and whether they are the cause or consequence of this disorder is still unknown, the accumulating data show that the breakdown of any of the mitochondrial functions may contribute to abnormal brain development leading to ASD. In this review, we discuss the multifaceted role of mitochondria in ASD from the various aspects of neuroscience.

sheet.es: Para mañana por la mañana: este trabajo no cambia nada en la rutina diaria ni ofrece pasos prácticos. Si te preocupa la energía, el cansancio o la salud de una persona autista, habla con su equipo médico. Es una revisión científica que reúne investigaciones sobre cómo las mitocondrias, que producen energía en las células, podrían relacionarse con el desarrollo cerebral en el autismo. Sus límites: aún no se sabe si estos mecanismos son causa o consecuencia, y no describe a todas las personas autistas. Cualquier decisión médica corresponde a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: For tomorrow morning: this paper changes nothing in daily routines and offers no practical steps. If you are concerned about energy, tiredness or the health of an autistic person, talk with their medical team. It is a scientific review gathering research on how mitochondria, which produce energy in cells, may relate to brain development in autism. Its limits: it is still unknown whether these mechanisms are a cause or a consequence, and it does not describe every autistic person. Any medical decision belongs to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Imorgon bitti: den här studien ändrar inget i vardagen och ger inga praktiska steg. Om du oroar dig för energi, trötthet eller hälsan hos en autistisk person, prata med personens vårdteam. Det är en forskningsöversikt som samlar studier om hur mitokondrier, som producerar energi i cellerna, kan hänga ihop med hjärnans utveckling vid autism. Begränsningar: det är fortfarande okänt om mekanismerna är orsak eller följd, och den beskriver inte alla autistiska personer. Medicinska beslut hör hemma hos en läkare.

title: Autism Spectrum Social Stories in Schools Trial 2 (ASSSIST-2): a pragmatic randomised controlled trial of the Social Stories™ intervention to address the social and emotional health of autistic children in UK primary schools.
authors: Wright B, Blackwell JE, Bell KJ, Teige C, Mandefield L, Wang HI, Welch C, Scantlebury A, Watson J, McMillan D, Standley E, Attwell L, Carrick H, Taylor A, Taylor O, Hodkinson R, Edwards H, Pearson H,
abstract: Background Autistic children can experience mental health, social and emotional difficulties. Carol Gray's Social Stories™ are a highly personalised intervention that provide social information in a short individually tailored story. Methods A multi-site pragmatic cluster randomised controlled trial to evaluate the clinical and cost-effectiveness of Social Stories™ alongside care as usual in autistic children aged 4-11 years. The primary outcome was the Social Responsiveness Scale-2 completed by teachers 6 months post-randomisation, analysed on an intention-to-treat basis. Trial registration ISRCTN11634810. Results Eighty-seven schools, including 249 children, were randomised (intervention 44 schools with 129 children, and usual care 43 schools with 120 children). After 6 months, a reduction of 1.61 points was found on the Social Responsiveness Scale-2 in the intervention group (95% CI -4.18 to 0.96, p = .220) and for those who attended at least six sessions a reduction of 3.37 points (CACE 95% CI -6.65 to -0.10, p = .043). Children in the intervention group met their individual socio-emotional goal more frequently than children receiving usual care alone and this was statistically significant. No statistically significant differences were found in other secondary outcomes including anxiety, depression, general health or parental stress. Conclusions Social Stories™ represent a low-cost, low-burden intervention. Benefits are seen in individual socio-emotional goals but without clinically evident impact on social responsiveness, anxiety, depression, parental stress or general health.

sheet.es: Si el colegio ofrece Historias Sociales™, puede probarlas para un objetivo concreto y personal de su hijo o hija, sin esperar cambios generales. Es un ensayo aleatorizado en 87 colegios del Reino Unido, con 249 niños autistas de 4-11 años; los docentes valoraron la capacidad de respuesta social a los 6 meses. Los niños con Historias Sociales™ lograron su objetivo socioemocional individual más a menudo, pero no hubo diferencias claras en ansiedad, depresión, salud general ni estrés parental. El resultado principal tampoco fue estadísticamente significativo. Los resultados no valen para todas las personas; conviene hablar con el equipo escolar.
sheet.en: If your child's school offers Social Stories™, you could try them for one specific, personal goal, without expecting broad changes. This was a randomised trial in 87 UK primary schools, with 249 autistic children aged 4-11; teachers rated social responsiveness at 6 months. Children using Social Stories™ met their individual socio-emotional goal more often, but there were no clear differences in anxiety, depression, general health or parental stress. The main outcome was not statistically significant either. Results do not apply to every child, so talk it through with the school team.
sheet.sv: Om barnets skola erbjuder Social Stories™ kan ni prova dem för ett konkret, personligt mål, utan att förvänta er breda förändringar. Det var en randomiserad studie i 87 brittiska grundskolor med 249 autistiska barn i åldern 4-11 år; lärare bedömde social responsivitet efter 6 månader. Barn som fick Social Stories™ nådde sitt individuella socioemotionella mål oftare, men det fanns inga tydliga skillnader i ångest, depression, allmän hälsa eller föräldrars stress. Huvudresultatet var inte heller statistiskt signifikant. Resultaten gäller inte alla barn, så prata med skolans team.

title: Stressful but Not Unhappy: A Review of the Positive Aspects of Parenting a Child with Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Curley K, Hughes R, Kotera Y
abstract: This review aimed to identify and synthesise the evidence for the positive aspects of parenting a child with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). To date, ASD parental research has predominantly focused on the negative aspects; parents and carers are left uninformed of how to strengthen their positive mental wellbeing. Three electronic databases-PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science -were searched for literature reporting positive aspects of parenting a child with ASD, published between January 2013 and December 2023. The PRISMA 2020 checklist was used for reporting. Two hundred and fifty-four articles were retrieved from the databases. After title/abstract screening ( n = 213) and full-text reviews ( n = 32), six papers were included ( n = 6). Sixteen positive aspects of parenting a child with ASD were identified and grouped into three themes: joyful moments, journey to resilience, and social connection. These three themes are eudaimonic wellbeing constructs and often under-represented in ASD parental studies. Focusing on joyful moments, building resilience through the parenting journey, and finding support and connection with others in similar situations can support the mental wellbeing of parents and carers of children with ASD. Future research is needed to further evaluate the positive aspects of parenting a child with ASD.

sheet.es: Mañana puede ayudar fijarse en los momentos alegres con su hijo o hija autista, reconocer lo que ya ha aprendido en el camino y buscar contacto con otras familias en situaciones parecidas. Es una revisión de la literatura: reunió seis artículos publicados entre enero de 2013 y diciembre de 2023 sobre madres, padres y cuidadores. Identificó tres temas: momentos alegres, camino hacia la resiliencia y conexión social. Sus límites: son pocos estudios, no prueban que estas acciones mejoren el bienestar de cada familia, y los propios autores piden más investigación. Úselo como idea, no como regla.
sheet.en: Tomorrow, it may help to notice joyful moments with your autistic child, acknowledge what you have already learned along the way, and reach out to other families in similar situations. This is a review of the literature: it brought together six papers published between January 2013 and December 2023 about parents and carers. It identified three themes: joyful moments, a journey to resilience, and social connection. Its limits: few studies were included, it does not prove these actions improve wellbeing for every family, and the authors call for more research. Treat it as an idea, not a rule.
sheet.sv: I morgon kan det hjälpa att uppmärksamma glada stunder med ditt autistiska barn, se vad du redan har lärt dig längs vägen och söka kontakt med andra familjer i liknande situationer. Det är en översikt av litteraturen: den sammanställde sex artiklar publicerade mellan januari 2013 och december 2023 om föräldrar och vårdnadshavare. Den fann tre teman: glada stunder, en resa mot resiliens och social gemenskap. Begränsningar: få studier ingick, den visar inte att detta förbättrar måendet i varje familj, och författarna efterlyser mer forskning. Använd den som en idé, inte som en regel.

title: HERVs Endophenotype in Autism Spectrum Disorder: Human Endogenous Retroviruses, Specific Immunoreactivity, and Disease Association in Different Family Members.
authors: Bo M, Carta A, Cipriani C, Cavassa V, Simula ER, Huyen NT, Phan GTH, Noli M, Matteucci C, Sotgiu S, Balestrieri E, Sechi LA
abstract: Increasing evidence indicates that human endogenous retroviruses (HERVs) are important to human health and are an underexplored component of many diseases. Certain HERV families show unique expression patterns and immune responses in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) patients compared to healthy controls, suggesting their potential as biomarkers. Despite these interesting findings, the role of HERVs in ASD needs to be further investigated. In this review, we discuss recent advances in genetic research on ASD, with a particular emphasis on the implications of HERVs on neurodevelopment and future genomic initiatives aimed at discovering ASD-related genes through Artificial Intelligence. Given their pro-inflammatory and autoimmune characteristics, the existing literature suggests that HERVs may contribute to the onset or worsening of ASD in individuals with a genetic predisposition. Therefore, we propose that investigating their fundamental properties could not only improve existing therapies but also pave the way for new therapeutic strategies.

sheet.es: Por ahora, este estudio no cambia nada en el día a día: no hay nada que hacer distinto mañana por la mañana. Si tienes dudas sobre pruebas o tratamientos, coméntalas con un profesional sanitario. Es una revisión de la literatura sobre retrovirus endógenos humanos (HERV), fragmentos de material genético presentes en el ADN humano. Señala que ciertas familias de HERV muestran patrones de expresión y respuestas inmunitarias distintos en personas autistas frente a controles sanas, lo que podría servir como biomarcadores. Sus límites: los propios autores indican que el papel de los HERV en el autismo requiere más investigación, y que sus ideas sobre nuevas terapias son propuestas, no resultados. No aplica a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: For now, this study changes nothing in daily life: there is nothing to do differently tomorrow morning. If you have questions about tests or treatments, raise them with a health professional. It is a review of the literature on human endogenous retroviruses (HERVs), fragments of genetic material found in human DNA. It reports that certain HERV families show different expression patterns and immune responses in autistic people compared with healthy controls, which might serve as biomarkers. Its limits: the authors themselves say the role of HERVs in autism needs more research, and their ideas about new therapies are proposals, not results. It does not apply to every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Just nu ändrar den här studien inget i vardagen: det finns inget att göra annorlunda i morgon bitti. Har du frågor om tester eller behandlingar, ta upp dem med hälso- och sjukvården. Det är en översikt av litteraturen om humana endogena retrovirus (HERV), bitar av genetiskt material som finns i människans DNA. Den beskriver att vissa HERV-familjer visar andra uttrycksmönster och immunsvar hos autistiska personer än hos friska kontroller, vilket kan fungera som biomarkörer. Begränsningar: författarna säger själva att HERV:s roll vid autism behöver utforskas mer, och deras idéer om nya terapier är förslag, inte resultat. Det gäller inte alla autistiska personer.

title: Investigating the Presence of Autistic Traits and Prevalence of Autism Spectrum Disorder Symptoms in Anorexia Nervosa: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Inal-Kaleli I, Dogan N, Kose S, Bora E
journal: The International journal of eating disorders
abstract: Objective The present meta-analysis aims to assess whether individuals with anorexia nervosa (AN) demonstrate elevated autistic traits, to explore potential associations between autistic traits and eating disorder symptoms; as well as to estimate the prevalence of a positive screen for autism spectrum disorder (ASD) assessed via Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule (ADOS), in AN. Method A systematic literature search was conducted in PsycINFO, MEDLINE, and Web of Science in August 2023 and later updated in April 2024 to identify relevant studies. Twenty-two studies with 1172 AN patients and 2747 healthy controls (HCs) met the inclusion criteria. Results There was a significant difference between AN and HC groups in autistic traits (g = 0.88, CI = 0.65-1.12), and a significant but modest correlation was found between autistic traits and severity of eating disorder symptoms (r = 0.28, CI = 0.11-0.44). Proportion meta-analysis indicated that 29% (CI = 0.19-0.38) of children and adults scored above the cut-off for ASD. Discussion The current findings suggest that AN frequently overlaps with both autistic traits and autistic symptomatology. Therefore, it is essential to evaluate autism and autistic traits in individuals with AN to tailor individualized treatment plans.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista o con rasgos autistas tiene anorexia nervosa, conviene que el equipo clínico tenga en cuenta el autismo al planificar el apoyo. Puedes pedir que se evalúen sus rasgos y necesidades sensoriales y de comunicación. La evidencia es un metaanálisis de 22 estudios con 1172 personas con anorexia nervosa y 2747 controles sanos. Las personas con anorexia nervosa mostraron más rasgos autistas, y el 29% superó el punto de corte de la prueba ADOS. Sin embargo, la relación entre rasgos autistas y síntomas alimentarios fue modesta, y el estudio no indica qué ocurre en cada persona ni qué tratamiento funciona mejor.
sheet.en: If an autistic person, or someone with autistic traits, has anorexia nervosa, it helps to ask the clinical team to consider autism when planning support. You can ask them to look at the person's traits, sensory needs and communication needs. The evidence is a meta-analysis of 22 studies with 1172 people with anorexia nervosa and 2747 healthy controls. People with anorexia nervosa showed more autistic traits, and 29% scored above the ADOS cut-off. However, the link between autistic traits and eating symptoms was modest, and the study cannot say what is true for any one person or which treatment works best.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person, eller någon med autistiska drag, har anorexia nervosa kan du be vårdteamet ta hänsyn till autism när stödet planeras. Du kan be dem se över personens drag samt sensoriska behov och kommunikationsbehov. Underlaget är en metaanalys av 22 studier med 1172 personer med anorexia nervosa och 2747 friska kontroller. Personer med anorexia nervosa hade fler autistiska drag, och 29% översteg gränsvärdet på ADOS. Sambandet mellan autistiska drag och ätstörningssymtom var dock måttligt, och studien kan inte säga vad som gäller för en enskild person eller vilken behandling som fungerar bäst.

title: A Mixed Method Systematic Review Into the Impact of ED Treatment in Autistic People and Those With High Autistic Traits.
authors: Nimbley E, Sharpe H, Maloney E, Gillespie-Smith K, Tchanturia K, Duffy F
journal: The International journal of eating disorders
abstract: Objective Our understanding of the impact of eating disorders (ED) treatment in Autistic people remains elusive. Research has begun to explore ED treatment outcomes and experiences in this population, however current understandings are poorly integrated. The current review therefore sought to explore the impact of ED treatment on Autistic people and those with higher Autistic traits. Method A convergent, segregated approach was used, independently evaluating quantitative then qualitative studies before integrating findings into a coherent narrative synthesis. Results Autistic people and people with higher Autistic traits report poorer experiences of treatment and may be at increased risk of inpatient admission and prolonged inpatient treatment, possibly explained by difficulties with treatment timeframes and a lack of autism-informed support. Both groups reported similar improvements in ED symptoms and BMI. Higher rates of psychosocial difficulties pre-and post-treatment were reported in those with higher Autistic traits, and emotion-focused interventions were felt to be particularly relevant to Autistic presentations of EDs. Concerns were reported as to how well aligned group-based programs and cognitive-based interventions are for Autistic individuals and those reporting higher Autistic traits. Discussion Future research in diagnosed autism samples is urgently needed to develop a more robust understanding of Autistic outcomes and experiences. Review findings demonstrate the need for increased understanding of ED presentations and the possible need for treatment adaptations, for Autistic people or those with higher Autistic traits.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista a tu cargo recibe tratamiento para un trastorno de la conducta alimentaria, puede ayudar pedir al equipo adaptaciones: plazos más flexibles, apoyo informado sobre el autismo y atención a las emociones, no solo a pensamientos o a sesiones grupales. Los síntomas y el peso pueden mejorar igual que en otras personas, pero la experiencia del tratamiento suele ser peor y puede haber más ingresos o ingresos más largos. Esta revisión sistemática combinó estudios cuantitativos y cualitativos con personas autistas y con rasgos autistas elevados. Su límite: muchos estudios no incluían diagnósticos confirmados de autismo, y cada persona es distinta.
sheet.en: If an autistic person you support is in eating disorder treatment, it may help to ask the team for adaptations: more flexible timeframes, autism-informed support, and attention to emotions rather than only thought-focused or group-based work. Symptoms and weight can improve just as for others, but the treatment experience is often worse, and there may be more or longer inpatient stays. This systematic review combined quantitative and qualitative studies of autistic people and people with higher autistic traits. Its limit: many studies did not include confirmed autism diagnoses, and every person is different.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person du stöttar får behandling för en ätstörning kan det hjälpa att be teamet om anpassningar: mer flexibla tidsramar, autismkunnigt stöd och fokus på känslor, inte bara på tankearbete eller gruppbehandling. Symtom och vikt kan förbättras lika mycket som för andra, men upplevelsen av behandlingen är ofta sämre och det kan bli fler eller längre slutenvårdsperioder. Denna systematiska översikt kombinerade kvantitativa och kvalitativa studier med autistiska personer och personer med fler autistiska drag. Begränsning: många studier saknade bekräftade autismdiagnoser, och varje person är unik.

title: Sensory seeking and its influence on sustained attention performance in adult males with Autism Spectrum Condition.
authors: Itahashi T, Aoki R, Nakamura M, Ohta H, Hashimoto RI
abstract: Atypical sensory responses and seeking behaviors constitute the core symptoms of autism spectrum condition (ASC). There are possible links between atypical sensory profiles and attentional challenges in ASC. Due to the paucity of studies in adults, the nature of attentional challenges and their associations with sensory profiles in autistic adults remain elusive. Here, we investigated sustained attention performance and its associations with sensory profiles in 28 autistic adult males and 23 typically developing controls (TDCs). A gradual-onset continuous performance task and the Adolescent/Adult Sensory Profile were employed to assess sustained attention performance and sensory profiles, respectively. Our results revealed that the two groups exhibited comparable sustained attention performance quantified by d-prime. A statistically significant negative correlation between d-prime and sensory seeking was observed only in the ASC group. Moreover, an interaction effect of group-by-sensory seeking was observed in d-prime, suggesting a unique interplay between sensory profiles and attention in autistic individuals. In the ASC group, omission error rate and post-error slowing were statistically significantly associated with difficulties in social communication and interactions. These results contribute to understanding attentional processes in ASC and highlight the potential influence of sensory profiles on cognitive functions in this population.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista busca mucho estímulo sensorial (moverse, tocar, escuchar sonidos), puede ayudar observar si eso influye en su concentración en tareas largas y ofrecer opciones sensoriales, preguntándole qué le resulta útil. Este estudio comparó a 28 hombres autistas adultos con 23 controles de desarrollo típico mediante una tarea de atención sostenida y un cuestionario sensorial. Ambos grupos rindieron de forma comparable, pero solo en el grupo autista más búsqueda sensorial se asoció con menor rendimiento. Es un estudio pequeño, solo con hombres adultos, y muestra asociaciones, no causas; no sirve como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If an autistic person seeks a lot of sensory input (moving, touching, listening to sounds), it may help to notice whether this affects their focus on long tasks and to offer sensory options, asking what feels useful to them. This study compared 28 autistic adult males with 23 typically developing controls using a sustained attention task and a sensory questionnaire. Both groups performed comparably, but only in the autistic group was more sensory seeking linked to lower performance. It is a small study, only with adult males, and shows associations, not causes; it is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person söker mycket sensoriska intryck (att röra sig, ta på saker, lyssna på ljud) kan det hjälpa att se om det påverkar fokus vid långa uppgifter och att erbjuda sensoriska alternativ, med frågan om vad som känns användbart. Studien jämförde 28 autistiska vuxna män med 23 typiskt utvecklade kontroller med en uppgift för ihållande uppmärksamhet och ett sensoriskt frågeformulär.
