Grupperna presterade jämförbart, men bara i den autistiska gruppen hängde mer sensoriskt sökande ihop med sämre prestation. Studien är liten, omfattar bara vuxna män och visar samband, inte orsaker; den är ingen regel för varje person.

title: Program for the Education and Enrichment of Relational Skills (PEERS ® ) for Italy: A Randomized Controlled Trial of a Social Skills Intervention for Autistic Adolescents.
authors: Fatta LM, Laugeson EA, Bianchi D, Italian Peers® team support group, Laghi F, Scattoni ML
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: The Program for the Education and Enrichment of Relational Skills (PEERS ® ) is an intervention targeting social skills for autistic adolescents and those with other social challenges. The efficacy of the PEERS ® on adolescents has been extensively explored but the program has not been validated in Italy. In the present study, we adapted PEERS ® to Italian culture and evaluated its efficacy in an Italian sample. A Randomized Controlled Trial was conducted, analyzing the results of 37 autistic adolescents who were randomly assigned to two groups: experimental group (TG) and waitlist group (WL). The primary outcomes (social abilities) and secondary outcomes (co-occurring conditions, executive functions) were assessed at four time points. No differences were found at pre-treatment between groups on baseline measures and primary outcomes. At post-treatment, significant group differences emerged in primary outcomes (social knowledge and social performance) and secondary outcomes (emotion regulation). The groups' results pooled together (TG + WL) confirmed the findings at post-treatment and showed further changes in primary outcomes (global social competence and social cognition) and secondary outcomes (externalizing problems, emotive and behavioral total problems, functional problems related to depressive symptoms). The improvements were maintained at a 3-month follow-up, except for global social competence and social cognition. Additionally, new results emerged regarding internalizing problems and global executive functioning. The efficacy of the Italian version of PEERS ® was ascertained on primary and secondary outcomes. Innovative findings on emotion regulation, behavioral problems, and depression symptoms also emerged.Clinical trial registration information Program for the Education and Enrichment of Relational Skills (PEERS ® ) for Italy. An RCT's Study on Social Skills Intervention for Adolescents with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). URL: http://clinicaltrials.gov . TRN: NCT05473104. Release Date: July 21, 2022.

sheet.es: Si un o una adolescente autista quiere practicar habilidades sociales, un programa estructurado en grupo como PEERS puede ser una opción que merece la pena consultar con su equipo profesional. Es un ensayo controlado aleatorizado en Italia con 37 adolescentes autistas, divididos entre un grupo que hizo el programa y otro en lista de espera. Tras el programa mejoraron el conocimiento y el desempeño social, y también la regulación emocional; la mayoría de las mejoras se mantuvo a los 3 meses. Es un grupo pequeño, un solo país, y no todas las personas se benefician igual. Conviene escuchar qué quiere cada adolescente.
sheet.en: If an autistic teen wants to practise social skills, a structured group programme like PEERS may be worth discussing with their care team. This was a randomized controlled trial in Italy with 37 autistic adolescents, split between a group that took the programme and a waitlist group. After the programme, social knowledge, social performance and emotion regulation improved, and most gains were kept at a 3-month follow-up. The sample was small, from one country, and not everyone benefits in the same way. It helps to ask what each teen actually wants.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk tonåring vill öva sociala färdigheter kan ett strukturerat gruppprogram som PEERS vara värt att ta upp med vårdteamet. Det här var en randomiserad kontrollerad studie i Italien med 37 autistiska tonåringar, fördelade på en grupp som deltog i programmet och en väntelistgrupp. Efter programmet förbättrades social kunskap, socialt agerande och känsloreglering, och de flesta förbättringarna fanns kvar vid uppföljningen efter 3 månader. Gruppen var liten, från ett enda land, och alla har inte samma nytta. Det hjälper att fråga vad varje tonåring själv vill.

title: "What does 'often' even mean?" Revising and validating the Comprehensive Autistic Trait Inventory in partnership with autistic people.
authors: Hechler FC, Tuomainen O, Weber N, Fahr F, Karlek B, Maroske M, Misia M, Caruana N
abstract: Background In this study, we revised the comprehensive autistic trait inventory (CATI)-a self-report inventory of autistic traits, in collaboration with autistic people and provided preliminary evidence for its validity as a self-report measure of autistic traits in the general population. An established strength of the CATI is its ability to capture female autistic traits. Our project aimed to extend this further, to increase the inventory's accessibility, and to minimise stigma induced by deficit-based representations of autistic experience. Methods Together with 22 individuals from the autism and autistic communities, we created the Revised Comprehensive Autistic Trait Inventory (CATI-R). Revisions included rewording items to increase clarity or reduce stigma and expanding items to capture diverse autistic experiences. We also present a series of guidelines for developing self-report inventories of subclinical neurodivergent traits. We validated the CATI-R within a large sample (n = 1439), comprising people with a self-reported autism diagnosis (n = 331), people who self-identified as autistic (n = 44), and non-autistic participants (n = 1046). Results We successfully validated a revision of the CATI. A confirmatory factor analysis supported the six-subscale structure (two-factor bifactors model: Chi-squared = 2705.73, p .56, ps Limitations Our study presents only initial evidence for the validity of the CATI-R that should be enriched with further analyses and types of data, including a larger number of participants who do not identify as male or female. Conclusions This project provides a revised trait inventory that resonates with actual autistic experience, along with guidelines for creating self-report measures that are sensitive, accessible, and non-stigmatising.

sheet.es: Si usas cuestionarios de rasgos autistas, conviene elegir los que se hayan creado con personas autistas y con un lenguaje claro y no estigmatizante. Este estudio revisó un cuestionario de autoinforme, el CATI, junto con 22 personas de las comunidades autista y del autismo, y creó el CATI-R. Se validó con 1439 participantes: 331 con diagnóstico autoinformado, 44 que se identificaban como autistas y 1046 no autistas. Los resultados apoyaron una estructura de seis subescalas. Sus límites: la evidencia es inicial y faltan más participantes que no se identifiquen como hombre o mujer. No es una herramienta diagnóstica.
sheet.en: If you use questionnaires about autistic traits, it helps to choose ones built with autistic people, in clear and non-stigmatising language. This study revised a self-report questionnaire, the CATI, together with 22 people from the autism and autistic communities, creating the CATI-R. It was tested with 1439 participants: 331 with a self-reported autism diagnosis, 44 who identified as autistic, and 1046 non-autistic people. Results supported a six-subscale structure. Limits: the evidence is only initial, and more participants who do not identify as male or female are needed. It is not a diagnostic tool.
sheet.sv: Om du använder frågeformulär om autistiska drag är det bra att välja sådana som utvecklats tillsammans med autistiska personer och som har tydligt, icke-stigmatiserande språk. Studien reviderade ett självskattningsformulär, CATI, tillsammans med 22 personer från autismgemenskaperna och skapade CATI-R. Det prövades på 1439 deltagare: 331 med självrapporterad autismdiagnos, 44 som identifierade sig som autistiska och 1046 icke-autistiska. Resultaten stödde en struktur med sex delskalor. Begränsningar: bevisen är bara preliminära, och fler deltagare som inte identifierar sig som man eller kvinna behövs. Det är inget diagnosverktyg.

title: Practitioner Adherence and Competence in MEYA, a Free Online Self-Instruction Program in Modular Psychotherapy and Counseling for Children's Autism-Related Clinical Needs.
authors: Wood JJ, Wood KS, Rosenau KA, Cho AC, Johnson AR, Muscatello VS, Tien IS, Straus J, Wolpe S, Zeldin A, Kazlauskas K, McLeod BD
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: The quality of care in public schools and other community settings for school-aged youths on the autism spectrum is variable and often not evidence-based. Training practitioners in these settings to deliver evidence-based practices (EBPs) may improve the quality of care. We developed a free internet-based training and clinical guidance system synthesizing multiple EBPs for youth on the autism spectrum addressing a range of mental health needs and autism-related behaviors, entitled Modular EBPs for Youth on the Autism Spectrum (MEYA; meya.ucla.edu). A multiple baseline study was conducted with seven practitioners recruited from mental health practice settings across the United States who were providing services to children on the autism spectrum (aged 6 to 17 years). Practitioners were randomly assigned to undergo baseline conditions of 2 to 8 weeks. Once online training in MEYA commenced, practitioners engaged in algorithm-guided self-instruction in EBPs for autism. Participants video-recorded sessions. Independent coders used the MEYA Fidelity Scale (MEYA-FS) to rate adherence and competence in EBPs for autism. Practitioners also completed measures pertaining to implementation outcomes and parents rated youth outcomes on personalized target behaviors. Five of seven practitioners increased their adherence to MEYA practices (i.e., MEYA-FS scores) following MEYA training. Findings for competence were similar, though somewhat less robust. Practitioners generally viewed MEYA as feasible, understandable, and acceptable. Most youth outcomes improved during MEYA. A randomized, controlled trial of MEYA would be helpful in characterizing its effectiveness for supporting practitioner EBP implementation and youth outcomes in school and community service settings.

sheet.es: Si trabaja con un profesional de salud mental o de un centro escolar, puede preguntarle si conoce MEYA, un programa gratuito en línea para formar a profesionales en prácticas basadas en la evidencia para jóvenes autistas. Es un estudio de diseño de línea base múltiple con siete profesionales de Estados Unidos que atendían a niños autistas de 6 a 17 años. Cinco de siete aplicaron mejor las prácticas tras la formación, la mayoría lo vio viable y aceptable, y la mayoría de los resultados de los jóvenes mejoraron según sus familias. Es un grupo muy pequeño y sin grupo de comparación aleatorizado, así que no demuestra que funcione para cada persona.
sheet.en: If you work with a mental health or school practitioner, you could ask whether they know MEYA, a free online program that trains practitioners in evidence-based practices for autistic youth. This was a multiple baseline study with seven practitioners across the United States who supported autistic children aged 6 to 17 years. Five of seven followed the practices more closely after training, most found it feasible and acceptable, and most youth outcomes improved according to parents. The group was very small and had no randomized comparison group, so it cannot show that this works for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du har kontakt med en behandlare eller skolpersonal kan du fråga om de känner till MEYA, ett gratis webbprogram som utbildar yrkesverksamma i evidensbaserade metoder för autistiska unga. Det var en studie med flera baslinjer och sju behandlare i USA som stöttade autistiska barn i åldern 6 till 17 år. Fem av sju följde metoderna bättre efter utbildningen, de flesta såg programmet som genomförbart och acceptabelt, och de flesta resultat för de unga förbättrades enligt föräldrarna. Gruppen var mycket liten och utan randomiserad jämförelsegrupp, så studien visar inte att det fungerar för alla.

title: A critical hit: Dungeons and Dragons as a buff for autistic people.
authors: Atherton G, Hathaway R, Visuri I, Cross L
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Tabletop role-playing games (TTRPGs) are popular hobbies that may offer specific social benefits for autistic people. This study investigated the ability of TTRPGs to provide a safe space where autistic adults could develop relationships with other autistic adults while engaging in character and world-building. A group of eight autistic adults were split into two groups and taken through a short-form online Dungeons and Dragons campaign over 6 weeks run by one of the researchers. The researcher then led a series of individual semi-structured interviews discussing how participants felt interacting in and out of the TTRPG. Several key themes were identified as important aspects of why autistic people could benefit from such an environment. Analysis showed that while real-life interactions could be challenging, in TTRPG play, they felt they experienced significantly fewer struggles. Results suggested that TTRPGs can provide a safe space environment where autistic adults can engage in productive social interactions with like-minded individuals. It also may allow autistic participants to experience 'bleed' or the ability to take on a new character that changes the way they feel about themselves outside of the game. Future directions for this work are discussed.

sheet.es: Si a una persona autista le atraen los juegos de rol de mesa, como Dungeons and Dragons, puede valer la pena ofrecerle una partida con otras personas autistas, en un entorno tranquilo y sin presión. Sobre la evidencia: ocho adultos autistas jugaron en dos grupos una campaña en línea de 6 semanas y luego hablaron en entrevistas individuales. Dijeron sentir menos dificultades en el juego que en la vida cotidiana, y algunos notaron que su personaje cambiaba cómo se sentían consigo mismos. Límites: el grupo fue muy pequeño y no hubo comparación con otras actividades, así que no sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person is drawn to tabletop role-playing games like Dungeons and Dragons, it may be worth offering a game with other autistic people, in a calm, low-pressure setting. On the evidence: eight autistic adults played in two groups in a 6-week online campaign, then took part in individual interviews. They described fewer struggles in the game than in everyday interactions, and some felt their character changed how they felt about themselves. Limits: the group was very small and there was no comparison with other activities, so this is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person lockas av rollspel vid bordet, som Dungeons and Dragons, kan det vara värt att erbjuda en spelrunda med andra autistiska personer i en lugn miljö utan press. Om underlaget: åtta autistiska vuxna spelade i två grupper en kampanj online under 6 veckor och intervjuades sedan enskilt. De beskrev färre svårigheter i spelet än i vardagliga möten, och några upplevde att deras rollfigur förändrade hur de kände inför sig själva. Begränsningar: gruppen var mycket liten och jämfördes inte med andra aktiviteter, så det är ingen regel för alla.

title: Post-diagnostic support for adults diagnosed with autism in adulthood in the UK: A systematic review with narrative synthesis.
authors: Norris JE, Harvey R, Hull L
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract More adults than ever before are seeking an autism diagnosis in adulthood. While receiving a diagnosis may be beneficial, many autistic people struggle to navigate their new diagnosis, and require support. This study conducted a systematic review of previous research on the support available after diagnosis (post-diagnostic support) for autistic adults without intellectual disability who were diagnosed in adulthood in the UK. A systematic review is a pre-planned method of searching for all relevant studies, before combining these to answer a larger question. The study aimed to investigate the availability of such support and its effectiveness, and to explore autistic adults' experiences of accessing support. We also used publicly available information to create a map of the post-diagnostic support services currently available across the UK. A systematic search of seven databases was conducted, to identify UK-based studies published after 2012. Nineteen studies were eligible to be included in the study. Although some form of post-diagnostic support is available across most areas in the UK, this mostly consists of providing information and 'signposting' the person to other services. These options may not meet the needs of autistic people, who want services such as psychoeducation (therapy whereby an individual receives education about their diagnosis to improve understanding and self-management), and peer support. Findings highlight the need for adequate support to alleviate the post-diagnostic challenges autistic adults face. The study could not evaluate the effectiveness of support options in the UK due to a lack of information about this in published research. Research shows that autistic adults would like low-level support services, psychoeducation, and peer support, and may also prefer autistic-led support. Further research is required to develop and evaluate post-diagnostic support programmes which include these elements.

sheet.es: Si tú o alguien a quien cuidas recibió un diagnóstico de autismo siendo adulto, conviene pedir, además de información y orientación hacia otros servicios, apoyo entre iguales y psicoeducación, que es aprender sobre el propio diagnóstico. También puede buscarse apoyo dirigido por personas autistas. Es una revisión sistemática de 19 estudios realizados en el Reino Unido con personas autistas adultas sin discapacidad intelectual. Tiene límites: no pudo evaluar si el apoyo funciona, porque faltan datos publicados, y no se aplica igual a todas las personas ni a otros países.
sheet.en: If you or someone you support was diagnosed with autism as an adult, it may help to ask for more than information and signposting to other services: peer support and psychoeducation (learning about your own diagnosis) are what autistic adults say they want. Autistic-led support may also be preferred. This is a systematic review of 19 UK studies with autistic adults without intellectual disability. Its limits: it could not judge whether support works, because published evidence is lacking, and it may not apply to every person or to other countries.
sheet.sv: Om du eller någon du stöttar fick en autismdiagnos som vuxen kan det vara bra att be om mer än information och hänvisning till andra tjänster: kamratstöd och psykoedukation (att lära sig om sin egen diagnos) är sådant autistiska vuxna säger sig vilja ha. Autistledd stöd kan också föredras. Detta är en systematisk översikt av 19 brittiska studier med autistiska vuxna utan intellektuell funktionsnedsättning. Begränsningar: den kunde inte bedöma om stödet fungerar, eftersom publicerad forskning saknas, och den gäller inte nödvändigtvis alla personer eller andra länder.

title: Insistence on sameness, repetitive negative thinking and mental health in autistic and non-autistic adults.
authors: Cooper K, Russell A
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic people are more likely to have mental health problems than non-autistic people. We know that having repetitive and negative thoughts can contribute to multiple mental health problems such as depression and obsessive-compulsive disorder. Autistic people often do the same behaviours repetitively, and they may also have more repetitive thinking styles. This could contribute to higher rates of mental health problems in autistic people. In this research, we wanted to find out if higher rates of repetitive behaviours contributed to depression and anxiety, and whether this relationship was because of repetitive negative thinking. We asked three groups of autistic adults to take part in the research. Sixty-seven autistic clinical participants were recruited from clinical settings and had moderate depression. Fifty-four autistic community participants and 66 non-autistic community participants were recruited from community settings. All participants completed measures of repetitive behaviours; a measure of anxiety and depression; and two measures of repetitive negative thinking (ruminating and obsessing). Autistic community participants had significantly higher repetitive behaviours, rumination and obsessing scores than non-autistic community participants. We found that higher rates of repetitive behaviours contributed to more repetitive thinking (obsessing and ruminating), which contributed to higher rates of depression and anxiety. The higher rates of repetitive negative thinking found in autistic individuals may contribute to higher rates of mental health problems in this group. Mental health assessments and interventions for autistic people should therefore consider the role of multiple forms of repetitive negative cognition and behaviour, which cut across diagnostic categories such as anxiety, depression and obsessive-compulsive disorder. These should be considered when aiming to understand why individuals develop mental health conditions and why these conditions persist.

title: The experiences of autistic adults who were previously diagnosed with borderline or emotionally unstable personality disorder: A phenomenological study.
authors: Tamilson B, Eccles JA, Shaw SCK
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic people face many barriers to receiving an autism diagnosis. Often, they may be misdiagnosed with borderline personality disorder instead. For our study, we interviewed 10 autistic adults who had previously been diagnosed with borderline personality disorder. This helped us to better understand their experiences. They explained how borderline personality disorder is quite stigmatised and may suggest that people are to blame for their differences in behaviour. They found the treatments they had to try for borderline personality disorder to be harmful. For example, these treatments promoted 'masking'. Previous research showed that masking can be harmful for autistic people, linking it to risk of suicide. This diagnosis also led to healthcare professionals neglecting them and discounting their beliefs. Once they were diagnosed with borderline personality disorder, it was hard to access an autism assessment. When they did receive their autism diagnoses, this was much more positive. This diagnosis was validating. It also improved their mental health, as they were no longer expected to mask - their differences were now accepted. They still felt that autism was stigmatised in society. However, this was very different to the stigma around borderline personality disorder. They felt autism stigma was more about their competence as people, whereas borderline personality disorder stigma was about how they were broken and might be harmful to others. This study is important because it allows their stories to be heard by researchers and healthcare professionals alike. Adding their voices helps to humanise them, promoting positive change in mental health services. More research is now needed.

title: The development, feasibility and acceptability of Empower-Autism: A new psychoeducational and psychotherapeutic programme for caregivers of children recently diagnosed with autism.
authors: Leadbitter K, Harrison L, Langhorne S, Ellis C, Smallman R, Pearson A, Hackett L, Kroll L, Dunkerley A, Beach H, Gilbert J, van Gils A, Hutton T, Green J, Bee P, REACH-ASD Team
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract What is already known about the topic? Parents and carers face many challenges following their child's autism diagnosis. They often look for information, and social and emotional support. There has been relatively little research into how best to provide this support and this means that there is no evidence to guide the delivery of services. Studies have suggested that an approach called Acceptance and Commitment Therapy can help parents and carers with their adjustment and emotional wellbeing. What does this article add? This article describes the development of a new group-based programme to address the diverse needs of caregivers after their child's autism diagnosis. The new programme was developed with caregivers, autistic people and professionals. It was called Empower-Autism and contained lots of information about autism and strategies to support autistic children, alongside therapeutic aspects based on Acceptance and Commitment Therapy. The programme was delivered to 29 parents/carers in three groups. Attendance at the groups was satisfactory. Both parents/carers and facilitators liked and valued the programme and found it accessible. They made suggestions for improvements. After the programme, parents and carers described improved wellbeing. They felt more positive and more connected to other people. They also described parenting their child in a more informed and sensitive way. Implications for practice, research or policy The new programme is being tested within a large clinical trial. If there are positive results, the programme could be recommended for delivery and this would address an important gap in evidence-based practice.

sheet.es: Tras el diagnóstico de autismo de su hijo o hija, puede ayudar buscar un grupo que combine información sobre autismo, estrategias de apoyo y espacio para las emociones del cuidador. Este estudio describe el desarrollo de Empower-Autism, un programa grupal creado con cuidadores, personas autistas y profesionales. Se ofreció a 29 madres, padres o cuidadores en tres grupos. Valoraron el programa, refirieron mejor bienestar, más conexión con otras personas y una crianza más informada y sensible. Es un estudio inicial y pequeño, sin evidencia todavía de que funcione para todas las familias; se está probando en un ensayo clínico mayor.
sheet.en: After a child's autism diagnosis, it may help to look for a group that combines information about autism, practical support strategies and room for caregivers' own feelings. This study describes the development of Empower-Autism, a group programme built with caregivers, autistic people and professionals. It was delivered to 29 parents/carers in three groups. They valued it and described better wellbeing, feeling more connected to others, and parenting in a more informed and sensitive way. This was an early, small study, so it cannot show the programme works for every family; it is now being tested in a larger clinical trial.
sheet.sv: Efter ett barns autismdiagnos kan det vara till hjälp att söka en grupp som kombinerar information om autism, stödstrategier och utrymme för vårdnadshavarens egna känslor. Studien beskriver utvecklingen av Empower-Autism, ett gruppprogram som skapades tillsammans med vårdnadshavare, autistiska personer och yrkesverksamma. Det gavs till 29 föräldrar/vårdnadshavare i tre grupper. De värdesatte programmet och beskrev bättre välmående, mer kontakt med andra och ett mer informerat och lyhört föräldraskap. Studien var liten och tidig, så den visar inte att programmet fungerar för alla familjer; det prövas nu i en större klinisk studie.

title: Out of Sight, Out of Mind-Explaining and Challenging the Re-Institutionalisation of People With Learning Disabilities and/or Autistic People.
authors: Glasby J, Waring J, Miller R, Glasby AM, Ince R
abstract: During the twentieth century, many countries underwent processes of 'de-institutionalisation'-closing 'asylums' for people with mental health problems, learning disabilities and dementia. Despite this, the UK has witnessed a subsequent process of 're-institutionalisation' with the creation of new public/private sector facilities providing 'secure' care to large numbers of people, who can be residents for many years with no sense of when they may leave. In 2023, 2035 people with learning disabilities and/or autistic people were receiving inpatient hospital care in England, with 54% in hospital for over two years. Drawing on the lived experience of people in hospital/families, and the practice knowledge of front-line staff, this paper critically analyses why this process of re-institutionalisation may be taking place. Our argument is that institutional forms of care have gradually been re-introduced-despite the influence of neoliberal health policies that have previously aimed at deinstitutionalisation and self-care-because some people are viewed as 'too difficult' to govern through the prevailing dispositive of self-care, and therefore become the subjects of more disciplinary forms of power. Once in hospital, the primary routes to 'escape' require performative acts of 'good conduct' that give confidence to professionals of a person's capacity for self-government.

sheet.es: Si su familiar autista o con discapacidad intelectual está ingresado en un hospital, pregunte con regularidad cuál es el plan concreto y el calendario para volver a casa, y pida que quede por escrito. El estudio analiza, con experiencias de personas ingresadas, familias y personal de primera línea, por qué en Inglaterra vuelven a crearse centros de atención cerrada. Según el resumen, en 2023 había 2035 personas ingresadas y el 54% llevaba más de dos años. Sugiere que salir depende de mostrar «buena conducta». Es un análisis centrado en Inglaterra y no ofrece una regla para cada persona ni una solución concreta.
sheet.en: If your autistic or learning-disabled family member is in a hospital, ask regularly for a concrete plan and timeline for returning home, and ask for it in writing. This study draws on the lived experience of people in hospital, families and front-line staff to analyse why locked-type care is being re-created in England. The abstract reports 2035 people in inpatient care in 2023, with 54% there for over two years. It suggests leaving depends on showing 'good conduct'. It is an analysis focused on England, not a rule for every person, and it offers no ready-made fix.
sheet.sv: Om din autistiska eller utvecklingsstörda närstående vårdas på sjukhus: fråga regelbundet efter en konkret plan och tidsram för att komma hem, och be att få den skriftligt. Studien bygger på erfarenheter från inlagda personer, familjer och personal och analyserar varför sluten vård återskapas i England. Enligt sammanfattningen vårdades 2035 personer 2023, och 54% hade varit där över två år. Den antyder att vägen ut kräver visad ”gott uppförande”. Det är en analys med fokus på England, inte en regel för alla och ingen färdig lösning.

title: Collaborative arts therapies as a supportive intervention for autism spectrum disorders: Bibliometric analysis, insights, and directions.
authors: Zhang A, Luo X, Ying F, Wang J, Huang G
abstract: Purpose Arts therapies (ATs) for the treatment of autism spectrum disorders (ASD) has attracted widespread attention from scholars. However, resources, technical, and ethical issues still pose significant obstacles to current research. A collaborative design approach is needed to guide the intervention treatment process involving multiple stakeholders. Therefore, this study focuses on exploring the current status, development and potential value of the collaborative arts therapies (CATs), providing a comprehensive perspective for subsequent research. Methods The Web of Science, PubMed, ScienceDirect, and Cochrane Library were searched for publications up to August 30, 2023, related to the use of CATs for the treatment of ASD. CiteSpace was used to build a knowledge graph to achieve visual analysis of current research countries, institutions, journals, authors, and hot topics. Results A total of 845 articles met the inclusion criteria. In terms of quantity, the USA is the leading country which has the greatest influence in advancing the field. The University of Haifa is the most productive institution. Arteterapia Papeles De Arteterapia Y Educacion Artistica and Frontiers in Psychology occupy key publishing positions. The most central keywords were related to the quality of life of people with ASD. "family", "social robot" and "participation" are emerging topics in the research field. The positive impact of the combination of caregivers, technology and artistic media on enhancing connections between people with ASD and their everyday environment is the focus of current research. Conclusions Research on CATs as an adjunctive therapy for the treatment of ASD is evolving. Providing comprehensive rehabilitation and support intervention for patients with ASD is a key research direction. The research process requires more interdisciplinary resources and technical assistance. Collaboration will be the best way to improve the effectiveness of ATs.

sheet.es: Si le interesan las terapias artísticas (música, arte, drama), busque propuestas en las que la familia participe y se tenga en cuenta la vida cotidiana de la persona autista, no solo la sesión. Es una revisión bibliométrica: analizó 845 artículos hasta el 30 de agosto de 2023 para mapear países, temas y tendencias. Señala que "familia", "robot social" y "participación" son temas emergentes. Sus límites: no mide si estas terapias funcionan ni para quién, así que no sirve como prueba de eficacia ni como regla para todas las personas. Cualquier decisión sobre apoyos conviene hablarla con profesionales y con la propia persona autista.
sheet.en: If you are interested in arts therapies (music, art, drama), look for approaches where the family takes part and where the autistic person's everyday life is considered, not only the session itself. This is a bibliometric review: it mapped 845 articles up to August 30, 2023, covering countries, topics and trends. It notes that "family", "social robot" and "participation" are emerging themes. Its limits: it does not measure whether these therapies work or for whom, so it is not proof of effectiveness or a rule for every person. Decisions about supports are best discussed with professionals and with the autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om du är intresserad av konstterapier (musik, bild, drama), leta efter upplägg där familjen deltar och där den autistiska personens vardag beaktas, inte bara själva sessionen. Det här är en bibliometrisk översikt: den kartlade 845 artiklar fram till 30 augusti 2023, med länder, ämnen och trender. Den lyfter "familj", "social robot" och "delaktighet" som framväxande teman. Begränsningar: den mäter inte om terapierna fungerar eller för vem, så den är inget bevis på effekt och ingen regel för alla. Beslut om stöd bör diskuteras med yrkesverksamma och med den autistiska personen.

title: Action execution and observation in autistic adults: A systematic review of fMRI studies.
authors: Stillesjö S, Hjärtström H, Johansson AM, Rudolfsson T, Säfström D, Domellöf E
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Motor impairments are common in individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) although less is known about the neural mechanisms related to such difficulties. This review provides an outline of functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) findings associated with execution and observation of naturalistic actions in autistic adults. Summarized outcomes revealed that adults with ASD recruit similar brain regions as neurotypical adults during action execution and during action observation, although with a difference in direction and/or magnitude. For action execution, this included higher and lower activity bilaterally in the precentral cortex, the parietal cortex, the inferior frontal gyrus (IFG), the middle temporal gyrus (MTG), the occipital cortex, and the cerebellum. For action observation, differences mainly concerned both higher and lower activity in bilateral IFG and right precentral gyrus, and lower activity in MTG. Activity overlaps between action execution and observation highlight atypical recruitment of IFG, MTG, precentral, and parieto-occipital regions in ASD. The results show atypical recruitment of brain regions subserving motor planning and/or predictive control in ASD. Atypical brain activations during action observation, and the pattern of activity overlaps, indicate an association with difficulties in understanding others' actions and intentions.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista tiene dificultades con el movimiento o con interpretar lo que hacen otros, conviene dar más tiempo, mostrar las acciones paso a paso y decir en voz alta la intención, sin dar nada por entendido. Esta revisión sistemática reunió estudios de resonancia magnética funcional con personas autistas adultas que ejecutaban y observaban acciones naturales. Halló que usan regiones cerebrales similares a las de adultos neurotípicos, pero con actividad a veces mayor y a veces menor. Sus límites: describe patrones de grupo en adultos, no explica a cada persona ni indica qué apoyo funciona, y la asociación con entender intenciones ajenas no es una regla general.
sheet.en: If an autistic person finds movement or reading other people's actions harder, it can help to allow extra time, show actions step by step and say the intention out loud rather than assuming it is clear. This systematic review gathered fMRI studies of autistic adults carrying out and watching natural actions. It found they use brain regions similar to those of neurotypical adults, but with activity that is sometimes higher and sometimes lower. Its limits: it describes group patterns in adults, cannot explain any one person or show which support works, and the link to understanding others' intentions is not a rule for everyone.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person tycker att rörelser eller att tolka andras handlingar är svårare kan det hjälpa att ge extra tid, visa handlingar steg för steg och säga avsikten högt i stället för att anta att den är tydlig. Den här systematiska översikten samlade fMRI-studier av autistiska vuxna som utförde och såg naturliga handlingar. Den fann att de använder liknande hjärnregioner som neurotypiska vuxna, men med aktivitet som ibland är högre och ibland lägre. Begränsningar: den beskriver gruppmönster hos vuxna, kan inte förklara en enskild person eller visa vilket stöd som fungerar, och kopplingen till att förstå andras avsikter gäller inte alla.

title: Reading between the lines: exploring the discriminative ability of the Short-Story Task in identifying autistic individuals within autism outpatient services.
authors: Jarvers I, Sommer M, Ullmann M, Simmel V, Blaas L, Gorski S, Krüger-Lassen S, Vogel M, Langguth B
abstract: Introduction The correct diagnosis of autistic individuals is an everyday challenge within autism outpatient services. While the short-story task (SST), a task measuring fiction-based mentalizing, has demonstrated promise in differentiating between autistic and non-autistic adults, its discriminative ability has not been investigated in a sample of individuals seeking autism diagnostics at outpatient services. Methods This study aimed to evaluate the utility of the SST in individuals seeking autism diagnostics between 2016 and 2022 at the Clinic and Polyclinic for Psychiatry & Psychotherapy of the University of Regensburg at medbo District Hospital Regensburg. The sample consisted of 211 individuals. In 100 of them an autism spectrum disorder has been diagnosed and 111 individuals were diagnosed with other conditions or none at all. Results Performance on the SST did not significantly differ between the two groups, and receiver operator curve analysis did not support the SST as a reliable discriminator. However, linear regression analyses revealed that autism diagnosis was the sole significant predictor of SST mentalizing performance. Additionally, specific items of the SST showed significant differences between autistic and non-autistic individuals and constituted a significant predictor of autism diagnosis. Discussion While the SST may not be robust enough to accurately identify autistic individuals on its own, it does offer clinicians valuable insights into how individuals interpret others' actions and whether they grasp the broader context of a story versus focusing solely on details.

sheet.es: Si vas a una evaluación diagnóstica, no esperes que una sola tarea de lectura decida el resultado. Este estudio analizó la tarea de relato corto (SST), que mide cómo se interpretan las acciones de otras personas en una historia. Participaron 211 personas que buscaban diagnóstico en una clínica ambulatoria; a 100 se les diagnosticó autismo. El rendimiento en la tarea no difirió de forma significativa entre los grupos, aunque algunos ítems concretos sí ayudaron a los clínicos a entender cómo cada persona interpreta una historia. Es un solo centro y un solo tipo de tarea, así que no vale como regla para todas las personas. Las decisiones diagnósticas corresponden a profesionales.
sheet.en: If you are going to a diagnostic assessment, don't expect one reading task to decide the outcome. This study looked at the short-story task (SST), which shows how people interpret others' actions in a story. It included 211 people seeking a diagnosis at one outpatient clinic; 100 were diagnosed autistic. Overall performance did not differ significantly between the groups, though some specific items helped clinicians understand how a person reads a story. It was a single centre and one kind of task, so it is not a rule for every person. Diagnostic decisions belong to qualified professionals.
sheet.sv: Om du ska på en utredning ska du inte förvänta dig att en enskild läsuppgift avgör resultatet. Studien undersökte korta berättelseuppgiften (SST), som visar hur man tolkar andras handlingar i en berättelse. Den omfattade 211 personer som sökte utredning vid en öppenvårdsmottagning; 100 fick en autismdiagnos. Resultaten skilde sig inte signifikant mellan grupperna totalt, men vissa enskilda frågor hjälpte kliniker att förstå hur en person tolkar en berättelse. Det var en enda klinik och en typ av uppgift, så det är ingen regel för alla. Diagnosbeslut fattas av yrkespersoner.

title: The image of autism in the Polish press 2009-2020 and the role of first-person testimonies.
authors: Wodziński M, Kamińska N, Moskalewicz M
abstract: This study examines the representation of autism in Polish press discourse from 2009 to 2020 in five major Polish daily newspapers, specifically focusing on the influence of first-person testimonies of autistic individuals. Quantitative discourse analysis was conducted using deductive coding of 1352 press articles concerning ASC. In analyzed press reports, autism was primarily portrayed as a negative and deficit-laden phenomenon that should be addressed by bringing autistic people in line with the neurotypical majority, reinforcing social stereotypes and stigma. Autistic people's perspective was mostly neglected. However, when autistic people's voice and first-person perspective was presented, as in the case of 3.7% of the analyzed media, such stereotypical and negative perspectives on ASC significantly changed for the better.Research outcomes highlight the disparities in autism portrayal, particularly contrasting the deficit-driven narratives with perspectives emerging from the inclusion of first-person narratives. The latter can mitigate harmful stereotypes and promote a more accurate and positive understanding of autism. Treating autistic people as an essential source of information about themselves significantly changes the press image of autism and may indirectly contribute to their quality of life.

sheet.es: Cuando leas noticias sobre autismo, fíjate en si hablan las propias personas autistas, y si puedes, busca y comparte textos escritos por ellas. En este estudio se analizaron 1352 artículos de cinco diarios polacos entre 2009 y 2020. El autismo se presentaba sobre todo como algo negativo y deficitario, y casi no se escuchaba a las personas autistas. Cuando sí se incluía su voz, como en el 3,7% de los medios analizados, la imagen mejoraba de forma notable. Es un análisis de prensa de un solo país, no mide cómo afecta a cada familia ni a cada persona, y no sirve como regla general.
sheet.en: When you read news about autism, notice whether autistic people speak for themselves, and if you can, seek out and share pieces written by them. This study analysed 1352 articles from five Polish daily newspapers between 2009 and 2020. Autism was mostly portrayed as negative and deficit-focused, and autistic people were rarely heard. When their voice was included, as in 3.7% of the media analysed, the picture changed markedly for the better. It is a press analysis from one country, it does not measure effects on any family or person, and it is not a rule for everyone.
sheet.sv: När du läser nyheter om autism, lägg märke till om autistiska personer själva kommer till tals, och dela gärna texter skrivna av dem. Studien analyserade 1352 artiklar från fem polska dagstidningar mellan 2009 och 2020. Autism beskrevs mest som negativt och bristfokuserat, och autistiska personer hördes sällan. När deras röst fanns med, som i 3,7% av medierna som analyserades, blev bilden märkbart bättre. Det är en analys av press i ett enda land, den mäter inte effekter för enskilda familjer eller personer och är ingen regel för alla.

title: Dynamic functional adaptations during touch observation in autism: connectivity strength is linked to attitudes towards social touch and social responsiveness.
authors: Lee Masson H
abstract: Background Autistic adults experience differences in social interactions involving physical contact. Brain imaging studies suggest that these differences may be related to atypical brain responses to social-affective cues, affecting both the experience of receiving touch and observing it in others. However, it remains unclear whether these atypical responses are limited to specific brain regions or represent broader alterations in brain connectivity. The current study investigated how the functional network architecture is modulated during touch observation associated with autism and explored the extent to which changes in this architecture are associated with individual differences in social touch preferences and social responsiveness. Methods By integrating generalized psychophysiological interaction (gPPI) analysis with independent component analysis (ICA), the current study analyzed existing fMRI datasets, in which 21 autistic and 21 non-autistic male adults viewed videos of social and nonsocial touch while undergoing MRI scans. Results A gPPI analysis of regions of interest revealed that autistic adults exhibited increased connectivity between sensory and social brain regions. The strength of some of these connections was positively associated with a higher preference for social touch and greater social responsiveness, suggesting neural compensatory mechanisms that may help autistic adults better understand the meaning of touch. At the level of large-scale brain networks extracted using ICA, atypical connectivity was predominantly observed between the sensorimotor network and other networks involved in social-emotional processing. Increased connectivity was observed in the sensorimotor network during nonsocial touch, suggesting that embodied simulation, the process by which individuals internally simulate touch experience of others in this context, may be more engaged when observing human-object interactions than during human-to-human touch. Limitations This study focused on a specific subgroup of 21 autistic male adults with minimal support needs. Future research would benefit from including a more diverse autistic sample. Conclusions This study reveals atypical context-dependent modulation of functional brain architecture associated with autism during touch observation. Neural compensatory mechanisms in autistic individuals who enjoy social touch and show higher social responsiveness may function as adaptive social responses. However, these compensations may be limited to specific brain regions, rather than occurring at the level of large-scale brain networks.

sheet.es: Pregunte a la persona autista qué tipo de contacto físico le resulta agradable, en lugar de suponerlo; sus preferencias sobre el tacto social son válidas y distintas en cada persona. Este estudio analizó datos de resonancia magnética de 21 adultos autistas y 21 adultos no autistas que veían vídeos de contacto social y no social. Las personas autistas mostraron más conexión entre regiones cerebrales sensoriales y sociales, y algunas de estas conexiones se relacionaron con gustar más del tacto social. Límites: solo participaron hombres adultos con necesidades mínimas de apoyo, así que los resultados no sirven para todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: Ask the autistic person what kind of physical contact feels good to them rather than assuming; their preferences about social touch are valid and differ from person to person. This study analysed existing brain scan data from 21 autistic adults and 21 non-autistic adults who watched videos of social and nonsocial touch. Autistic adults showed more connectivity between sensory and social brain regions, and some of these connections were linked to liking social touch more. Limits: only adult men with minimal support needs took part, so the findings cannot be applied to all autistic people.
sheet.sv: Fråga den autistiska personen vilken sorts fysisk beröring som känns bra, istället för att anta det; preferenser kring social beröring är giltiga och skiljer sig mellan människor. Studien analyserade befintliga hjärnskanningsdata från 21 autistiska och 21 icke-autistiska vuxna som tittade på filmer med social och icke-social beröring. De autistiska vuxna hade ökad koppling mellan sensoriska och sociala hjärnregioner, och vissa kopplingar hängde ihop med att man tyckte mer om social beröring. Begränsningar: bara vuxna män med minimala stödbehov deltog, så resultaten gäller inte alla autistiska personer.

title: Barriers to and Facilitators for Finding and Keeping Competitive Employment: A Focus Group Study on Autistic Adults With and Without Paid Employment.
authors: Brouwers EPM, Bergijk M, van Weeghel J, Detaille S, Kerkhof H, Dewinter J
abstract: Purpose The aim of the study was to gain more insight into barriers to and facilitators for finding and keeping competitive employment for autistic adults. Research questions were: (1) What barriers and facilitators do autistic adults report in finding and keeping competitive employment?; and (2) What are differences and similarities between autistic adults with and without paid employment regarding barriers and facilitators for sustainable employment? Methods Eight focus groups were conducted (N = 64 autistic adults). Four groups included only participants without paid employment (N = 24), and four groups consisted exclusively of participants with current paid employment (including part-time, N = 40). All discussions were audiotaped and transcribed verbatim to enable inductive thematic content analysis. Data were analyzed using ATLAS.ti 9. Results Ten themes and thirty-four subthemes were found. Many were interconnected. Themes facilitating sustainable employment included a positive workplace atmosphere, a supportive supervisor, being able to do work that aligns with interests and talents, favorable physical working conditions, coaching, higher self-insight, higher self-esteem, and proactivity. Most themes and subthemes emerged from both groups. Differences between the groups were that those with paid employment seemed to have experienced more friendly workplaces and supervisors, had received better coaching in finding and keeping employment, had higher self-insight and higher self-esteem, were more assertive and proactive. Conclusions As many (sub-)themes were interrelated, the results suggest that to improve work participation, particularly two key areas are promising: (1) to realize more friendly, well-being oriented and inclusive workplaces, and (2) to increase autistic adults' self-insight into personal needs for positive wellbeing and self-knowledge regarding talents, wishes and well-being boundaries.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista en su vida laboral, puede ayudar hablar con ella de qué tareas encajan con sus intereses y talentos, qué condiciones físicas necesita y dónde están sus límites de bienestar. También cuenta buscar entornos con buen ambiente y un supervisor que apoye. La evidencia: ocho grupos de discusión con 64 personas autistas adultas, 24 sin empleo remunerado y 40 con empleo, analizados por temas. Límites: son experiencias contadas por los participantes, no miden qué intervención funciona, y no todas las personas lo vivirán igual.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person with work, it may help to talk with them about which tasks fit their interests and talents, what physical conditions they need, and where their well-being limits are. Looking for workplaces with a good atmosphere and a supportive supervisor also matters. The evidence: eight focus groups with 64 autistic adults, 24 without paid employment and 40 with it, analysed by themes. Limits: these are experiences reported by participants, the study does not test which support works, and not everyone will experience work in the same way.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person i arbetslivet kan det hjälpa att prata om vilka uppgifter som passar hens intressen och styrkor, vilka fysiska förhållanden hen behöver och var gränserna för välmående går. Det spelar också roll att söka arbetsplatser med god stämning och en stöttande chef. Evidensen: åtta fokusgrupper med 64 autistiska vuxna, 24 utan betalt arbete och 40 med, analyserade i teman. Begränsningar: det är deltagarnas egna berättelser, studien testar inte vilket stöd som fungerar, och alla upplever inte arbete på samma sätt.

title: Effectiveness of Virtual Reality Technology Interventions in Improving the Social Skills of Children and Adolescents With Autism: Systematic Review.
authors: Yang X, Wu J, Ma Y, Yu J, Cao H, Zeng A, Fu R, Tang Y, Ren Z
abstract: Background Virtual reality (VR) technology has shown significant potential in improving the social skills of children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Objective This study aimed to systematically review the evidence supporting the effectiveness of VR technology in improving the social skills of children and adolescents with ASD. Methods The search for eligible studies encompassed 4 databases: PubMed, Web of Science, IEEE, and Scopus. Two (XY and JW) researchers independently assessed the extracted studies according to predefined criteria for inclusion and exclusion. These researchers also independently extracted information regarding gathered data on the sources, samples, measurement methods, primary results, and data related to the main results of the studies that met the inclusion criteria. The quality of the studies was further evaluated using the Physiotherapy Evidence Database scale. Results This review analyzed 14 studies on using VR technology interventions to improve social skills in children and adolescents with ASD. Our findings indicate that VR interventions have a positive effect on improving social skills in children and adolescents with ASD. Compared with individuals with low-functioning autism (LFA), those with high-functioning autism (HFA) benefited more from the intervention. The duration and frequency of the intervention may also influence its effectiveness. In addition, immersive VR is more suitable for training complex skills in individuals with HFA. At the same time, nonimmersive VR stands out in terms of lower cost and flexibility, making it more appropriate for basic skill interventions for people with LFA. Finally, while VR technology positively enhances social skills, some studies have reported potential adverse side effects. According to the quality assessment using the Physiotherapy Evidence Database scale, of the 14 studies, 6 (43%) were classified as high quality, 4 (29%) as moderate quality, and 4 (29%) as low quality. Conclusions This systematic review found that VR technology interventions positively impact social skills in children and adolescents with ASD, with particularly significant effects on the enhancement of complex social skills in individuals with HFA. For children and adolescents with LFA, progress was mainly observed in basic skills. Immersive VR interventions are more suitable for the development of complex skills. At the same time, nonimmersive VR, due to its lower cost and greater flexibility, also holds potential for application in specific contexts. However, the use of VR technology may lead to side effects such as dizziness, eye fatigue, and sensory overload, particularly in immersive settings. These potential issues should be carefully addressed in intervention designs to ensure user comfort and safety. Future research should focus on optimizing individualized interventions and further exploring the long-term effects of VR interventions. Trial registration International Platform of Registered Systematic Review and Meta-analysis Protocols INPLASY202420079U1; https://inplasy.com/inplasy-2024-2-0079/.

sheet.es: Si piensa probar realidad virtual (RV) para practicar habilidades sociales, empiece con sesiones cortas y observe cómo se siente la persona: mareo, fatiga visual o sobrecarga sensorial son motivos para parar o cambiar de formato. La RV sin inmersión es más barata y flexible. Esta revisión sistemática analizó 14 estudios con niñas, niños y adolescentes autistas y encontró efectos positivos en habilidades sociales, sobre todo las complejas en quienes usan RV inmersiva. De los 14 estudios, 6 (43%) fueron de alta calidad. Los resultados varían, algunos estudios notificaron efectos adversos y se sabe poco de los efectos a largo plazo. No es una regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you are thinking of trying virtual reality (VR) to practise social skills, start with short sessions and watch how the person feels: dizziness, eye fatigue or sensory overload are reasons to stop or change format. Nonimmersive VR is cheaper and more flexible. This systematic review analysed 14 studies with autistic children and adolescents and found positive effects on social skills, especially complex ones with immersive VR. Of the 14 studies, 6 (43%) were high quality. Results vary, some studies reported adverse effects, and long-term effects are still little known. It is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du funderar på att prova virtuell verklighet (VR) för att öva social förmåga, börja med korta pass och se hur personen mår: yrsel, ögontrötthet eller sensorisk överbelastning är skäl att avbryta eller byta format. VR utan full inlevelse är billigare och mer flexibel. Den här systematiska översikten gick igenom 14 studier med autistiska barn och ungdomar och fann positiva effekter på social förmåga, särskilt komplexa färdigheter med immersiv VR. Av de 14 studierna höll 6 (43%) hög kvalitet. Resultaten varierar, några studier rapporterade biverkningar och långtidseffekter är dåligt kända. Det är ingen regel för alla.

title: Nutritional Intake and Sensory Processing in School-Aged Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Olson A, Krall JR, Baranova A, Slavin M
abstract: Background: Individuals diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) commonly experience sensory processing that differs from general-population norms, and the autistic lived experience of eating includes preferences for routine, and sensory processing difficulty related to scents, tastes, temperatures, and textures of food. Meanwhile, research indicates that nutrients involved in one-carbon metabolism (OCM) may be related to sensory processing. Methods: This study enrolled 33 school-aged children with autism to assess whether OCM nutrient intake is associated with sensory processing. Parents completed two parent-report assessments: the youth and adult food frequency questionnaire (YAFFQ), and a sensory processing tool, Sensory Profile 2 (SP2). Results: Participant data showed generally good nutritional profiles mirroring those of general-population U.S. children. A group-binarized linear regression model showed the following relationships ( p Conclusions: These results support the possible existence of a relationship between sensory symptoms and OCM nutrient consumption levels in school-aged children diagnosed with autism. Future research is needed to confirm and explore the potential for causality.

sheet.es: Mañana, si la comida es un tema difícil, puede ayudar fijarse en cómo se sienten los olores, sabores, temperaturas y texturas para cada niño o niña autista, y respetar su necesidad de rutina al comer. Este estudio observacional incluyó a 33 niños autistas en edad escolar; sus familias completaron cuestionarios sobre alimentación y procesamiento sensorial. Sugiere una posible relación entre las diferencias sensoriales y el consumo de ciertos nutrientes, aunque la muestra es pequeña, los datos los aportaron los padres y no demuestra que una cosa cause la otra. No es una regla para todas las personas. Para dudas sobre la alimentación, consulte a un profesional sanitario.
sheet.en: Tomorrow, if food is hard, it may help to notice how smells, tastes, temperatures and textures feel for your autistic child, and to respect their need for routine around eating. This observational study included 33 autistic school-aged children; their parents completed questionnaires on diet and sensory processing. It suggests a possible link between sensory differences and intake of certain nutrients. However, the sample is small, parents reported the data, and it cannot show that one causes the other. It is not a rule for every person. For questions about diet, talk with a health professional.
sheet.sv: I morgon, om mat är svårt, kan det hjälpa att uppmärksamma hur lukter, smaker, temperaturer och texturer känns för ditt autistiska barn, och att respektera behovet av rutiner vid måltider. Studien var observerande och omfattade 33 autistiska barn i skolåldern; föräldrarna fyllde i frågeformulär om kost och sensorisk bearbetning. Den tyder på ett möjligt samband mellan sensoriska skillnader och intag av vissa näringsämnen. Urvalet är litet, föräldrarna rapporterade uppgifterna och studien kan inte visa att det ena orsakar det andra. Den är ingen regel för alla. Vid frågor om kost, kontakta en vårdgivare.

title: Daily living skill support for autistic people through a neurodiversity-affirming practice lens.
authors: Morrison C, Cashin A, Foley KR
abstract: Introduction Supporting daily living skill (DLS) development for autistic people is a component of occupational therapy practice. DLSs are essential for an increased quality of life (QoL), independent living, and community participation. Autistic young people experience poorer outcomes in terms of QoL and independent living than non-autistic peers. Finding a balance between targeted DLS support to maximise independent living and improve QoL, while avoiding attempts to 'normalise' or 'change' autistic people, presents as a dilemma for therapists striving to align with neurodiversity-affirming practice. Methods This theoretical paper explored literature pertaining to DLS and the neurodiversity movement in the context of occupational therapy values and the Canadian Model of Occupational Participation. Consideration of whether targeted DLS support is neurodiversity-affirming or whether occupational therapists are compelling autistic people to mimic behavioural norms perceived by society was discussed. Results DLSs are an important factor for maximising QoL, regardless of neurotype. Occupational therapy values align with the core tenets of the neurodiversity movement, and occupational therapists are equipped with the values and skills to support the development of DLSs utilising affirming practice. Conclusion Occupational therapists should critically reflect on their practice to ensure alignment with the professions core values and recent occupational therapy models, to ensure affirming practice. Further research investigating DLS and neurodiversity-affirming practice would benefit occupational therapists striving to align with neurodiversity-affirming practice. Consumer and community involvement No consumer or community involvement. Consumers have been considered throughout the development of this paper through their representation in the literature. This involved a process of reviewing the literature and considering it in the scope of the questions and how occupational therapy sits within the neurodiversity movement. Plain language summary It is important to help autistic people to learn to do everyday things. Everyday things include activities like showering, cleaning, and cooking. These things are important so that autistic people can live on their own. It has shown that autistic young people are less likely to be able to do everyday activities on their own. It is important that therapists help autistic people learn how to do everyday things; however, do not try and change who they are. This is because completing everyday activities is an important part of QoL for all people.

sheet.es: Apoyar las habilidades de la vida diaria, como ducharse, limpiar o cocinar, puede ser valioso si se hace sin intentar que la persona autista parezca «normal». Pregunte qué quiere lograr la persona y qué le resulta útil, y respete su forma de hacerlo. La evidencia es un artículo teórico que revisó literatura sobre terapia ocupacional y el movimiento de la neurodiversidad; no incluyó participantes ni probó un método. Sus conclusiones son una reflexión profesional, no una pauta para todas las personas, y los autores piden más investigación. Si trabaja con un terapeuta ocupacional, puede conversar con él sobre este enfoque.
sheet.en: Supporting daily living skills, like showering, cleaning or cooking, can be valuable when it is done without trying to make an autistic person seem "normal". Ask what the person wants to achieve and what helps them, and respect their way of doing things. The evidence is a theoretical paper that reviewed literature on occupational therapy and the neurodiversity movement; it had no participants and did not test a method. Its conclusions are a professional reflection, not a rule for every person, and the authors call for more research. If you work with an occupational therapist, you can talk with them about this approach.
sheet.sv: Stöd i vardagliga färdigheter, som att duscha, städa eller laga mat, kan vara värdefullt om det sker utan att försöka få en autistisk person att verka "normal". Fråga vad personen vill uppnå och vad som hjälper, och respektera hens sätt att göra saker. Underlaget är en teoretisk artikel som gick igenom litteratur om arbetsterapi och neurodiversitetsrörelsen; den hade inga deltagare och testade ingen metod. Slutsatserna är en yrkesmässig reflektion, inte en regel för alla, och författarna efterlyser mer forskning. Om ni har en arbetsterapeut kan ni prata med hen om det här förhållningssättet.

title: Weak ties and the value of social connections for autistic people as revealed during the COVID-19 pandemic.
authors: Pellicano E, Heyworth M
abstract: A diverse portfolio of social relationships matters for people's wellbeing, including both strong, secure relationships with others ('close ties') and casual interactions with acquaintances and strangers ('weak ties'). Almost all of autism research has focused on Autistic people's close ties with friends, family and intimate partners, resulting in a radically constrained understanding of Autistic sociality. Here, we sought to understand the potential power of weak-tie interactions by drawing on 95 semi-structured interviews with Autistic young people and adults conducted during the COVID-19 pandemic. We analysed the qualitative data using reflexive thematic analysis within an essentialist framework. During the COVID-19 lockdowns, Autistic people deeply missed not only their close personal relationships but also their "incidental social contact" with acquaintances and strangers. These weak-tie interactions appear to serve similar functions for Autistic people as they do for non-autistic people, including promoting wellbeing. These findings have important implications both for future research into Autistic sociality and for the design of practical services and supports to enhance Autistic people's opportunities to flourish.

sheet.es: Tenga en cuenta que el contacto social breve y casual, como saludar a un vecino o charlar con alguien en una tienda, puede importar para el bienestar de una persona autista, además de las relaciones cercanas. Pregunte qué pequeños contactos echa de menos y ayude a mantenerlos si le apetecen. La evidencia procede de 95 entrevistas semiestructuradas con jóvenes y adultos autistas durante los confinamientos por la COVID-19, analizadas de forma cualitativa. Los límites: son experiencias contadas por quienes participaron en un momento muy particular, y no todas las personas autistas desean o viven estos contactos igual.
sheet.en: Keep in mind that brief, casual contact, like greeting a neighbour or chatting with someone in a shop, may matter for an autistic person's wellbeing, alongside close relationships. Ask which small contacts they miss, and help keep them going if they want them. The evidence comes from 95 semi-structured interviews with autistic young people and adults during the COVID-19 lockdowns, analysed qualitatively. The limits: these are experiences shared by participants at a very particular time, and not every autistic person wants or experiences these contacts in the same way.
sheet.sv: Tänk på att korta, vardagliga kontakter, som att hälsa på en granne eller småprata i en butik, kan betyda mycket för en autistisk persons välbefinnande, vid sidan av nära relationer. Fråga vilka små kontakter personen saknar och hjälp till att behålla dem om hen vill det. Underlaget är 95 semistrukturerade intervjuer med autistiska unga och vuxna under covid-19-nedstängningarna, analyserade kvalitativt. Begränsningar: det är erfarenheter från deltagare under en mycket speciell tid, och inte alla autistiska personer vill ha eller upplever dessa kontakter på samma sätt.

title: Loneliness and susceptibility to social pain mediate the association between autistic traits and psychotic experiences in young non-clinical adults.
authors: Fekih-Romdhane F, Sarra Chaibi L, Alhuwailah A, Sakr F, Helmy M, Shuwiekh HAM, Boudouda NE, Zarrouq B, Naser AY, Jebreen K, Roubi ML, Hassan ARB, Merdad N, Amin R, Nawajah I, Mohammed AH, Farhan SS, A
abstract: Understanding of the mechanisms involved in the occurrence of psychotic experiences (PEs) in highly autistic individuals is crucial for identifying appropriate prevention and intervention strategies. This study aimed to investigate the mediating role of susceptibility to social pain and loneliness in the relationship between autistic traits (ATs) and PEs in adults from the general population of 12 Arab countries. This cross-sectional study is part of a large-scale multi-country research project. A total of 7646 young adults (age range 18-35 years, mean age of 22.55 ± 4.00 years and 75.5% females) from twelve Arab countries (i.e., Algeria, Bahrain, Egypt, Iraq, Jordan, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Lebanon, Morocco, Oman, Palestine, and Tunisia) were included. Mediation analyses showed that, after adjusting over confounding variables, both loneliness (indirect effect: Beta = 0.18; Boot SE = 0.02; Boot CI 0.14; 0.21) and social pain (indirect effect: Beta = 0.03; Boot SE = 0.01; Boot CI 0.001; 0.05) partially mediated the association between ATs and PEs. Higher ATs were significantly associated with more loneliness and susceptibility to social pain, and directly associated with more severe PEs. Finally, higher loneliness and susceptibility to social pain were significantly associated with greater PEs scores. Findings indicated that individuals with higher ATs tend to experience greater loneliness and feel more pain from rejection, which can in turn be associated with higher levels of PEs. Interventions targeting susceptibility to social pain and loneliness as a means of mitigating PEs among highly autistic adults should be considered.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista joven, vale la pena prestar atención a su soledad y a cuánto le duele el rechazo; facilitar vínculos en los que se sienta aceptada puede ayudar. Se trata de un estudio transversal con 7646 adultos jóvenes de 18-35 años de doce países árabes, de la población general. Encontró que más rasgos autistas se asociaban con más soledad y dolor social, y estos con más experiencias psicóticas. Sus límites: es una fotografía en un momento, no prueba causa y efecto, medía rasgos autistas y no diagnósticos, y no sirve como regla para cada persona. Si te preocupa algo, consulta con un profesional.
sheet.en: If you support a young autistic person, it is worth noticing their loneliness and how much rejection hurts them; helping them find connections where they feel accepted may help. This was a cross-sectional study of 7646 young adults aged 18-35 from the general population of twelve Arab countries. Higher autistic traits were linked with more loneliness and social pain, and these with more psychotic experiences. Its limits: it is a snapshot in time, so it cannot show cause and effect, it measured autistic traits rather than diagnoses, and it is not a rule for every person. If you are worried, talk with a professional.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en ung autistisk person är det värt att uppmärksamma ensamhet och hur mycket avvisning gör ont; att hjälpa till med relationer där personen känner sig accepterad kan hjälpa. Det var en tvärsnittsstudie med 7646 unga vuxna i åldern 18-35 från allmänbefolkningen i tolv arabiska länder. Fler autistiska drag hängde ihop med mer ensamhet och social smärta, och dessa med fler psykotiska upplevelser. Begränsningar: det är en ögonblicksbild som inte visar orsak och verkan, den mätte autistiska drag och inte diagnoser, och den är ingen regel för alla. Om du är orolig, tala med en professionell.

title: Caregiving for autistic children in Nigeria: experiences and challenges.
authors: Azubuike AO, Azubuike PC, Afape AO, Enyam MO, Akinreni T, Imo UF, Nwadiche M, Ogbonna CK, Timothy PN, Uchegbu ER, Adai GS
abstract: Background Raising autistic children poses a daunting task for their caregivers. Providing care may take a toll on caregivers' physical, psychological, social, and financial wellbeing. This study explored the experience of the responsibility of care among caregivers of autistic children in Nigeria and informed targeted psychosocial support interventions. Methods This phenomenology qualitative study was conducted among 103 caregivers in Cross River, Nigeria. The PREPARE tool was used for the data collection. Data were analyzed using the inductive and deductive approaches qualitatively, using NVivo software. Results Stigma and misunderstanding of autism, emotional impact and acceptance, transportation and accessibility, lack of support networks, and balancing responsibilities and care responsibilities with personal commitments were the major challenges reported by our participants. These factors contributed to emotional strain, underscoring the complexities associated with caregiving experiences. Conclusion Given the significant responsibilities of caregivers, targeted intervention must be taken to properly enlighten Nigerian societies on autistic people, and the need for acceptance. Key stakeholders must provide suitable healthcare facilities and resources for autistic people. Also, social support groups would help establish a sense of belonging and support.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista, lo que sientes puede ser compartido: pide ayuda concreta (transporte, relevo, alguien con quien hablar) y busca grupos de apoyo de otras familias, porque pueden dar sensación de pertenencia. Es un estudio cualitativo con 103 cuidadores en Cross River, Nigeria. Describieron estigma, falta de comprensión del autismo, dificultades de transporte y acceso, poca red de apoyo y tensión emocional al conciliar el cuidado con su vida personal. Sus límites: refleja un lugar y unas voces concretas, no mide qué intervención funciona y no representa a todas las familias ni a las propias personas autistas.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic person, what you feel may be widely shared: ask for concrete help (transport, respite, someone to talk to) and look for support groups with other families, which can bring a sense of belonging. This was a qualitative study with 103 caregivers in Cross River, Nigeria. They described stigma, misunderstanding of autism, transport and access problems, few support networks, and emotional strain from balancing care with personal commitments. Its limits: it reflects one place and particular voices, does not test which support works, and does not speak for all families or for autistic people themselves.
sheet.sv: Om du ger omsorg till en autistisk person kan det du känner vara vanligt: be om konkret hjälp (transport, avlösning, någon att prata med) och sök stödgrupper med andra familjer, som kan ge en känsla av tillhörighet. Det var en kvalitativ studie med 103 vårdgivare i Cross River, Nigeria. De beskrev stigma, bristande förståelse för autism, svårigheter med transport och tillgänglighet, få stödnätverk och känslomässig belastning när omsorgen skulle kombineras med personliga åtaganden. Begränsningar: studien speglar en plats och vissa röster, prövar inte vilket stöd som fungerar och talar inte för alla familjer eller för autistiska personer själva.

title: A systematic review: Which psycho-social-environmental factors do autistic students identify as being important for positive experiences in mainstream secondary school?
authors: McKinlay M, Thorpe D, Cage E, Grainger C, Jasper C, Stewart M
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Mainstream secondary school can be a challenging environment for autistic students, in part due to social and sensory factors. Research to date has focussed on identifying the negative aspects of school experience; however, few studies have identified factors that promote positive experiences. We take a neuro-affirmative approach when exploring how schools can support autistic students, informed by both the social and the human rights models of disability. We conducted a systematic review of qualitative studies in which autistic adolescents and adults identified factors that related to positive experiences in mainstream secondary school. We identified 117 relevant studies and 36 met inclusion criteria. Through thematic synthesis, we developed overarching themes: 'Understanding and Acceptance', 'Environments that suit me' and 'Agency to meet my needs', with additional subthemes.
