This study identified that agency, understanding and acceptance by both staff and peers, as well as access to engaging activities, were key factors in creating a positive and supportive environment for autistic students. Adaptation to both the social and sensory contexts were important to meet the needs of autistic students. The findings suggest that policy and practice should focus on creating a positive environment in schools for autistic students, in addition to addressing current challenges.Lay abstractResearch has shown that many autistic students do not thrive in mainstream secondary schools. Often studies focus on the challenges autistic people face rather than what supports thriving. We reviewed published articles, exploring what factors helped autistic people create a positive experience in school from their own perspective. We identified 36 studies and analysed the direct quotes made by autistic adolescents and adults in these studies. Factors important for positive experience included the autistic student feeling understood and accepted by adults and peers in school, being able to shape sensory and social environments in ways that suited them and accessing engaging activities. This review highlighted ways in which schools can become more inclusive and positive environments for autistic students.

sheet.es: Mañana, pregunte a su hijo o hija autista qué le ayuda en el instituto y qué cambiaría en el entorno social y sensorial. Puede llevar esas ideas al centro. Según esta revisión sistemática de estudios cualitativos con adolescentes y adultos autistas, ayuda sentirse comprendido y aceptado por el profesorado y los compañeros, poder adaptar el entorno y tener actividades que le interesen. Se incluyeron 36 estudios. Aun así, resume experiencias de grupos y no dice qué necesita cada persona, así que lo suyo debe decidirlo cada estudiante.
sheet.en: Tomorrow, ask your autistic young person what helps them at secondary school and what they would change in the social and sensory environment. You can bring those ideas to the school. This systematic review of qualitative studies, using quotes from autistic adolescents and adults, found that feeling understood and accepted by staff and peers, being able to shape their surroundings, and having engaging activities helped. It included 36 studies. However, it summarises group experiences and cannot say what any one student needs, so each student's own views matter most.
sheet.sv: Fråga i morgon din autistiska tonåring vad som hjälper i skolan och vad hen vill ändra i den sociala och sensoriska miljön. Ta gärna med idéerna till skolan. Den här systematiska översikten av kvalitativa studier med citat från autistiska ungdomar och vuxna visar att det hjälper att känna sig förstådd och accepterad av personal och klasskamrater, att kunna påverka sin miljö och att ha engagerande aktiviteter. Den omfattade 36 studier. Den sammanfattar dock gruppers erfarenheter och kan inte säga vad en enskild elev behöver, så elevens egna åsikter väger tyngst.

title: 'It's designed for someone who is not me': A reflexive thematic analysis of the unmet healthcare support needs in UK autistic adults aged 65 years and over.
authors: Mansour H, Gillions A, Brown J, Pattenden A, Hartley S, Patel S, James S, Styles M, Mandy W, Stott J, O'Nions E
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Autistic people are more likely to experience physical and mental health difficulties across the lifespan, leading to an increased risk of premature mortality likely due to health disparities. At present, little is known about the healthcare experiences of autistic older adults. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 19 autistic adults aged 65 years or over living in the United Kingdom. Reflexive thematic analysis produced these themes: (1) A lifetime of being misunderstood; (2) Autistic people falling between the gaps; (3) Processing autism diagnosis in later life; (4) Concerns about service pressures and scarce resources; (5) Lack of continuity of care, empathy and understanding; (6) Anxiety, alexithymia and sensory overload; and (7) Reduced social support and concerns for the future. Some of the challenges autistic older adults faced were like those experienced by younger or middle-aged autistic adults. However, they also reported additional difficulties related to ageing and lifelong experiences of social exclusion. These difficulties were made worse by increased service pressures. A comprehensive approach is needed, including enhanced staff training, personalised care, targeted support and policy changes. Services should also consult with autistic older adults so they can advocate for their care, shape policy and co-design services.Lay abstractAutistic people often face both physical and mental health challenges throughout their lives, which can lead to a higher risk of premature death due to health inequalities. However, we know very little about the healthcare experiences of autistic older adults. In this study, we talked with 19 autistic adults aged 65 years or above living in the United Kingdom. We found these main themes: (1) A lifetime of being misunderstood; (2) Autistic people falling between the gaps; (3) Processing autism diagnosis in later life; (4) Concerns about service pressures and scarce resources; (5) Lack of continuity of care, empathy and understanding; (6) Anxiety, alexithymia and sensory overload; and (7) Reduced social support and concerns for the future. Themes show that autistic older adults face unique healthcare access challenges because services don't consider their lifelong experiences of social exclusion. Participants also worried about age-related decline coupled with reduced social support, which makes it harder for them to get support. To address these challenges, healthcare services should provide more targeted support, make policies and funding consistent, and improve healthcare provision by providing staff training. Importantly, they must also speak with autistic older adults so they can advocate for their current and future care.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista mayor, antes de una cita médica prepara con ella por escrito lo que necesita decir, avisa de sus necesidades sensoriales y de comunicación, y pide, si es posible, ver al mismo profesional. Un estudio cualitativo entrevistó a 19 personas autistas de 65 años o más en el Reino Unido y encontró incomprensión mantenida, falta de continuidad en la atención, ansiedad, sobrecarga sensorial y menos apoyo social. Son experiencias de un grupo pequeño en un solo país, así que no describen a todas las personas mayores autistas. Cada persona decide qué apoyo le sirve.
sheet.en: If you support an older autistic person, before a healthcare appointment prepare in writing with them what they need to say, tell the clinic about sensory and communication needs, and ask, if possible, to see the same professional. A qualitative study interviewed 19 autistic adults aged 65 years or over in the United Kingdom. They described a lifetime of being misunderstood, poor continuity of care, anxiety, sensory overload and reduced social support. These are the experiences of a small group in one country, so they do not describe every older autistic person. Each person knows best which support works for them.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en äldre autistisk person: förbered tillsammans med hen i förväg skriftligt vad som behöver sägas på vårdbesöket, berätta om sensoriska behov och kommunikationsbehov, och be om möjligt att få träffa samma vårdpersonal. En kvalitativ studie intervjuade 19 autistiska vuxna som var 65 år eller äldre i Storbritannien. De beskrev att de ofta blivit missförstådda, bristande kontinuitet i vården, ångest, sensorisk överbelastning och minskat socialt stöd. Det är erfarenheter från en liten grupp i ett land och gäller inte alla äldre autistiska personer. Varje person vet bäst vilket stöd som fungerar.

title: Exploring the construct validity of the Camouflaging Autistic Traits Questionnaire: A factor analytic study.
authors: McKinnon K, McKinnon K, Bougoure M, Zhuang S, Tan DW, Magiati I
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: 'Camouflaging' is a set of strategies used by autistic people to hide or compensate for their autistic characteristics to fit into predominantly non-autistic social environments. Many researchers have used the Camouflaging Autistic Traits Questionnaire (CAT-Q) to measure camouflaging. However, there have been questions about the construct validity of the CAT-Q as a measurement of camouflaging. The present study examined the extent to which CAT-Q items were distinguishable from other theoretically and empirically related measures of social anxiety, fear of negative evaluation and autistic social traits. Autistic adults ( N = 308) completed the CAT-Q and social anxiety, fear of negative evaluation and autistic social traits measures. The small-to-large positive associations between camouflaging and social anxiety, fear of negative evaluation and autistic social traits ( r = 0.14-0.65) were not indicative of collinearity. Three exploratory factor analyses, in which CAT-Q items were factor-analysed together with social anxiety, fear of negative evaluation and autistic social traits items respectively, showed that CAT-Q items generally loaded onto different factors from social anxiety, fear of negative evaluation and autistic social traits items, with the exception of the CAT-Q Assimilation subscale items, which cross-loaded mostly with autistic social traits items. Overall, the CAT-Q items were positively associated with, but also differentiated from, most social anxiety, fear of negative evaluation and autistic social traits items, providing support for the measure's construct validity.Lay abstractAutistic people describe having to mask or 'camouflage' their autistic selves to fit into certain social settings. Many researchers have used the CAT-Q to measure the extent to which autistic people engage in camouflaging. However, some researchers have questioned whether the CAT-Q measures camouflaging or whether it measures other related experiences and behaviours associated with social anxiety, fear of being negatively judged or social autistic traits. In our study, we analysed the CAT-Q to check whether it is indeed similar to or different from these related experiences. To do this, we asked 308 autistic adults to complete the CAT-Q and questionnaires about social anxiety, fear of being negatively judged and autistic social features. Then, we put all the CAT-Q items together with the items from each of the other measures in three separate analyses (called factor analyses) to see how the items would group together. These analyses showed us whether camouflaging behaviours are distinguishable and different from, or cluster together with, these other experiences. We found that most of CAT-Q items grouped together separately from the other measures' items, suggesting that camouflaging differs from these other related experiences. Only some items from one of the CAT-Q subscales clustered together with some social anxiety and autistic items, suggesting these may need to be teased out better in the future. Generally, our findings show that we can use the CAT-Q to measure camouflaging behaviours among autistic people.

sheet.es: Si hablas con una persona autista sobre su camuflaje (esconder rasgos autistas para encajar), puedes tratarlo como una experiencia propia, no como simple ansiedad social ni como miedo al juicio ajeno. Pregúntale cómo lo vive y qué le cuesta. La evidencia: un estudio con 308 personas autistas adultas que rellenaron un cuestionario de camuflaje y otros sobre ansiedad social, miedo a la evaluación negativa y rasgos sociales autistas. La mayoría de los ítems de camuflaje se agrupó aparte de los otros. Límites: es un estudio sobre un cuestionario, solo con personas adultas, y no dice cómo ayudar a una persona concreta; una parte del cuestionario se solapó con rasgos sociales autistas.
sheet.en: When you talk with an autistic person about camouflaging (hiding autistic traits to fit in), you can treat it as its own experience, not simply social anxiety or fear of being judged. Ask how they experience it and what it costs them. The evidence: a study of 308 autistic adults who completed a camouflaging questionnaire plus others on social anxiety, fear of negative evaluation and autistic social traits. Most camouflaging items grouped separately from the others. Limits: it tests a questionnaire, only with adults, and does not say how to support one particular person; one part of the questionnaire overlapped with autistic social traits.
sheet.sv: När du pratar med en autistisk person om kamouflering (att dölja autistiska drag för att passa in) kan du se det som en egen upplevelse, inte bara social ångest eller rädsla för att bli dömd. Fråga hur personen upplever det och vad det kostar. Evidensen: en studie med 308 autistiska vuxna som fyllde i ett kamouflageformulär och andra om social ångest, rädsla för negativ bedömning och autistiska sociala drag. De flesta kamouflagefrågorna grupperades separat från de andra. Begränsningar: studien prövar ett formulär, bara hos vuxna, och säger inte hur man stöttar en enskild person; en del av formuläret överlappade med autistiska sociala drag.

title: Quality-of-life measurement in randomised controlled trials of mental health interventions for autistic adults: A systematic review.
authors: Timmerman A, Totsika V, Lye V, Crane L, Linden A, Pellicano E
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Autistic people are more likely to have co-occurring mental health conditions compared to the general population, and mental health interventions have been identified as a top research priority by autistic people and the wider autism community. Autistic adults have also communicated that quality of life is the outcome that matters most to them in relation to mental health research and that they want to be involved more actively in the research process. Our systematic review aimed to determine the extent and nature of (1) quality of life measurement in randomised controlled trials of mental health interventions for autistic adults and (2) community involvement taking place within identified randomised controlled trials. We searched Medline, Embase, APA PsycInfo, Web of Science and grey literature sources. After screening over 10,000 records, 19 studies were eligible and five of those studies measured quality of life as an outcome. Of those five, three included community involvement and two did not report on community involvement. We conclude there is a need for increased use of quality of life measurement when trialling mental health interventions, including the use of measures validated for autistic adults - which would be facilitated by greater autistic involvement in the research process.Lay AbstractAutistic people are more likely to have health problems than the general population. They, and people who care about them, have said mental health research is very important, and some autistic adults have said quality of life is the most helpful area to research when focusing on mental health. Autistic people should also be more deeply involved in making decisions in research. Our review aimed to find out if and how quality of life is being measured when mental health treatments are being tested, and how autistic people and the wider autism community are involved in these studies. We searched four databases and other sources and found over 10,000 records. But just 19 research studies were testing mental health treatments for autistic adults, and only five of those measured quality of life. When they did measure quality of life, it was measured in different ways and there was not much information given on how communities were involved. We suggest mental health research should measure quality of life more often and in ways that are more helpful for autistic people. Our analysis found that mental health research needs to include a wider variety of autistic people, and autistic people should be more involved in the various parts of research.

title: Autism, ADHD, and Their Traits in Adults with Obesity: A Scoping Review.
authors: Makin L, Meyer A, Zesch E, Mondelli V, Tchanturia K
abstract: Introduction: Autism and ADHD shape behaviours related to food, exercise, and body image, potentially influencing obesity treatment outcomes, as seen in eating disorder research. Resultantly, autistic and ADHD patients with obesity may have distinct experiences and differences compared to non-autistic and non-ADHD patients. This review maps existing literature on autism and ADHD in adults with obesity. Methods: Following PRISMA guidelines, six databases (Embase, MEDLINE, PsycINFO, Web of Science, CENTRAL, and Scopus) were searched for studies on autism and/or ADHD (diagnosed, probable, or traits) in adults with obesity. Screening and data extraction were conducted twice independently for each record. Results: Thirty-one studies were included, with 1,027,773 participants. Two case reports described successful use of weight loss drugs in autistic people with obesity. Eight prevalence studies suggested ADHD is overrepresented in obesity, regardless of binge eating status. Nineteen studies examined clinical profiles: ADHD patients had lower socioeconomic status, poorer health-related quality of life, increased impulsivity, cognitive inflexibility, and neuroticism, alongside lower agreeableness, conscientiousness, self-directedness, and cooperativeness. ADHD patients also exhibited higher psychopathology, problematic alcohol use, and disordered eating. Eight studies assessed treatment responses, noting poorer outcomes from behavioural programs and obesity pharmacotherapy, but similar post-surgical weight outcomes, despite increased complications. Two studies considered ADHD-specific treatment adaptions, one reporting a successful trial of ADHD medication for weight loss and the other reporting on switching to transdermal ADHD medications after bariatric surgery. Conclusions: This review underscores the need for more research on autism and obesity. For ADHD, findings suggest frequent co-occurrence with obesity, but lived experiences and tailored interventions remain underexplored.

sheet.es: Si una persona adulta autista o con TDAH busca apoyo para el peso, conviene pedir al equipo de salud que adapte el plan: rutinas claras, recordatorios, opciones sensoriales aceptables y menos dependencia de la fuerza de voluntad. Un programa estándar que no funcione no es un fracaso personal. La evidencia es una revisión de alcance de 31 estudios con adultos con obesidad; el TDAH aparecía con más frecuencia y los programas conductuales daban peores resultados. Sus límites: casi no hay investigación sobre adultos autistas (solo dos casos) y faltan las experiencias vividas, así que no es una regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If an autistic or ADHD adult is seeking support around weight, it is reasonable to ask the health team to adapt the plan: clear routines, reminders, sensory-acceptable food options and less reliance on willpower. If a standard programme does not work, that is not a personal failure. The evidence comes from a scoping review of 31 studies of adults with obesity; ADHD appeared more often, and behavioural programmes gave poorer results. Its limits: there is almost no research on autistic adults (only two case reports), and lived experience is missing, so this is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen eller en vuxen med adhd söker stöd kring vikt är det rimligt att be vårdteamet anpassa upplägget: tydliga rutiner, påminnelser, mat som fungerar sensoriskt och mindre fokus på viljestyrka. Om ett standardprogram inte fungerar är det inget personligt misslyckande. Underlaget är en översikt av 31 studier om vuxna med fetma; adhd var vanligare och beteendeprogram gav sämre resultat. Begränsningar: det finns nästan ingen forskning om autistiska vuxna (bara två fallrapporter) och levda erfarenheter saknas, så det är ingen regel för alla.

title: The impact of physical exercise interventions on social, behavioral, and motor skills in children with autism: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
authors: Wang Y, Qian G, Mao S, Zhang S
abstract: Background Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by social impairments, sensory processing issues, repetitive behavior patterns, motor abnormalities, and executive function impairments. Objective To systematically review and meta-analyze the effects of various exercise modalities on flexibility and cognitive control, social skills, behavioral problems, motor skills, and coordination in children with ASD, providing scientific evidence for clinical practice to guide effective exercise interventions for children with ASD. Methods Literature searches were conducted in PubMed, EMbase, Cochrane Library, EBSCOhost, and Web of Science databases, covering the period from database inception to February 15, 2024. Inclusion criteria included studies involving children with ASD, any form of exercise intervention, reporting at least one ASD-related outcome, and designed as randomized controlled trials (RCTs) or quasi-experimental studies. Exclusion criteria included reviews, conference abstracts, commentary articles, and studies lacking sufficient statistical data for meta-analysis. Study quality was assessed using the PEDro scale. Effect sizes were calculated using standardized mean differences (SMD). Heterogeneity was assessed with the I 2 statistic. Multiple subgroup analyses were conducted, and publication bias was evaluated using Begg's Test and Egger's Test. Results 23 RCTs were included in this study, showing positive effects of exercise interventions in various domains.Upper grade students showed significant improvement in flexibility and cognitive control (SMD = -0.282, p = 0.161). Lower grade children showed the most significant improvement in motor skills and coordination (SMD = 0.475, p = 0.043). Preschool children showed significant enhancement in social skills (SMD = 0.312, p = 0.041). Behavioral problems improved significantly across all age groups (SMD = -0.674, p 0.001). Martial arts and ball games were particularly effective in enhancing these domains, and appropriate periodic exercise interventions effectively improved various abilities in children with ASD. Results varied across different ages and intervention types. Conclusion Exercise interventions significantly improve flexibility, cognitive control, motor skills, coordination, social skills, and behavioral problems in children with ASD. This study supports exercise interventions as an effective method to enhance multiple abilities in children with ASD and emphasizes the importance of designing personalized intervention programs tailored to different ages and needs. Future research should focus on larger sample sizes and long-term follow-ups to confirm the sustainability and generalizability of intervention effects.

sheet.es: Si quiere probar actividad física con una niña o un niño autista, puede empezar con juegos de pelota o artes marciales, a un ritmo regular y adaptado a su edad, sus intereses y sus sentidos. Es una revisión sistemática con metaanálisis de 23 ensayos controlados aleatorizados con niños autistas. Los autores hallaron mejoras en habilidades sociales, motoras y de conducta, que variaron según la edad y el tipo de ejercicio. Sus límites: los resultados no son iguales para todos, un dato citado no alcanzó significación (p = 0.161) y los propios autores piden estudios más grandes y con seguimiento a largo plazo.
sheet.en: If you want to try physical activity with an autistic child, you could start with ball games or martial arts, done regularly and adapted to their age, interests and sensory needs. This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of 23 randomized controlled trials with autistic children. The authors found improvements in social, motor and behavioural measures, varying by age and type of exercise. Limits: results are not the same for everyone, one reported result was not statistically significant (p = 0.161), and the authors call for larger studies with long-term follow-up.
sheet.sv: Om du vill prova fysisk aktivitet med ett autistiskt barn kan du börja med bollspel eller kampsport, regelbundet och anpassat efter barnets ålder, intressen och sinnesbehov. Det här är en systematisk översikt med metaanalys av 23 randomiserade kontrollerade studier med autistiska barn. Forskarna fann förbättringar i sociala, motoriska och beteendemässiga mått, som varierade med ålder och typ av träning. Begränsningar: resultaten är inte desamma för alla, ett redovisat resultat var inte statistiskt signifikant (p = 0.161), och forskarna efterlyser större studier med långtidsuppföljning.

title: Review: Dopamine, Serotonin, and the Translational Neuroscience of Aggression in Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Martin H, Choi JE, Rodrigues AR, Eshel N
abstract: Objective Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder with a 1% to 2% prevalence in children. In addition to social communication deficits and restricted or repetitive behavior, ASD is often characterized by a heightened propensity for aggression. In fact, aggressive behavior is the primary reason for hospitalization in children with ASD, and current treatment options, despite some efficacy, are often associated with prominent side effects. Despite such high clinical toll, the neurobiology of aggression in ASD remains poorly understood. Method The neural circuits linked to both ASD and aggression were reviewed, with the goal of identifying overlapping components to help guide future treatment development. In discussing the clinical phenotype of aggression in ASD, some of the triggers and risk factors were noted to differ from those that cause aggression in neurotypical children. Preclinical and clinical studies on the neurobiology of aggression and ASD were synthesized to combine evidence from genetics, neuroimaging, pharmacology, and circuit manipulations. Dopamine and serotonin, 2 neuromodulators that contribute to development and behavioral control, were specifically studied. Results The literature indicates that the intricate interplay of the dopamine and serotonin systems has a pivotal role in shaping behavior, including the expression of aggression. Conclusion Understanding the balance between dopamine as an accelerator and serotonin as a brake may provide insights into the mechanisms of aggression in children with ASD. Although much work remains to be done, new perspectives promise to bridge the gap between human and animal studies and pinpoint the neurobiology of aggression in ASD. Diversity & inclusion statement One or more of the authors of this paper self-identifies as a member of one or more historically underrepresented sexual and/or gender groups in science. We actively worked to promote sex and gender balance in our author group.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista muestra conductas agresivas, conviene buscar primero qué las desencadena (sobrecarga sensorial, dolor, cambios imprevistos, dificultad para comunicarse) y comentarlo con su equipo clínico. Esta revisión de la literatura reunió estudios con animales y con personas sobre genética, neuroimagen y farmacología. Sugiere que dos sistemas cerebrales, dopamina y serotonina, intervienen en la agresión, y que sus desencadenantes pueden diferir de los de niños no autistas. Es una revisión teórica: no ofrece pautas probadas para el día a day, y no es válida para todas las personas. Cualquier decisión médica corresponde a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If an autistic person shows aggression, it helps to look first for what triggers it (sensory overload, pain, unexpected changes, difficulty communicating) and to talk it through with their clinical team. This review of the literature brought together animal and human studies on genetics, brain imaging and pharmacology. It suggests that two brain systems, dopamine and serotonin, play a role in aggression, and that triggers may differ from those in non-autistic children. It is a theoretical review: it offers no tested day-to-day strategies and does not apply to every person. Any medical decision belongs to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person uppvisar aggression hjälper det att först söka efter vad som utlöser den (sensorisk överbelastning, smärta, oväntade förändringar, svårigheter att kommunicera) och prata om det med det kliniska teamet. Den här översikten sammanställde djurstudier och studier på människor om genetik, hjärnavbildning och farmakologi. Den antyder att två system i hjärnan, dopamin och serotonin, påverkar aggression och att utlösarna kan skilja sig från dem hos icke-autistiska barn. Det är en teoretisk översikt: den ger inga prövade strategier för vardagen och gäller inte för alla personer. Medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker.

title: The global prevalence of autism spectrum disorder in children: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Issac A, Halemani K, Shetty A, Thimmappa L, Vijay VR, Koni K, Mishra P, Kapoor V
journal: Osong public health and research perspectives
abstract: Background The objective of this review was to analyze quantitative data on autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and to increase the accuracy of estimates of the prevalence of ASD. Methods This review, which was reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses statement, included studies conducted from January 2008 to June 2024 on children aged 3 to 18 years that used standardized measurement tools and reported cut-off scores for ASD. The prevalence of ASD was the primary outcome analyzed in this review. The PubMed, Clinical Key, Scopus, Embase, CINAHL, and Web of Science databases were reviewed for relevant studies. The review protocol was registered with PROSPERO and followed the Cochrane collaboration guidelines. Results A total of 66 studies reported on the prevalence of ASD, screening 21,313,061 children worldwide. Among these, 25 studies were conducted in Europe, 22 in Asia, and 13 in America. Additionally, 3 studies each were reported from Africa and Australia. According to a meta-analysis, 0.77% of children globally are diagnosed with ASD, with boys comprising 1.14% of this group. Notably, Australia showed the highest prevalence rate, with an effect size of 2.18, highlighting it as a critical area for public health focus. Conclusion ASD represents a significant global health burden. Early detection, increased awareness among parents, and prompt intervention are crucial for mitigating developmental problems in children later in life. It is essential for health policymakers to acknowledge the prevalence and growing trends of ASD in order to implement effective interventions.

sheet.es: Si le preocupa cómo se desarrolla su hijo o hija, hablar con el pediatra o el centro de salud sobre una valoración puede ser un buen primer paso; conocer pronto sus necesidades ayuda a organizar apoyos. Se trata de un metaanálisis que reunió 66 estudios y evaluó a 21,313,061 niños y niñas de 3 a 18 años en el mundo. Estimó que el 0.77% de los niños y niñas recibe un diagnóstico de autismo. Sus límites: son promedios entre países y métodos distintos, y no dicen nada sobre una persona concreta ni sobre qué apoyos le irán mejor.
sheet.en: If you are wondering about your child's development, talking with a paediatrician or health centre about an assessment can be a good first step; knowing a child's needs early helps in arranging supports. This is a meta-analysis that pooled 66 studies covering 21,313,061 children aged 3 to 18 worldwide. It estimated that 0.77% of children receive an autism diagnosis. Its limits: these are averages across different countries and methods, and they say nothing about any one person or which supports will suit them best.
sheet.sv: Om du funderar på hur ditt barn utvecklas kan det vara ett bra första steg att prata med barnläkare eller vårdcentral om en utredning; att känna till barnets behov tidigt gör det lättare att ordna stöd. Detta är en metaanalys som sammanställde 66 studier med 21,313,061 barn i åldern 3 till 18 år över hela världen. Den uppskattade att 0.77% av barnen får en autismdiagnos. Begränsningar: siffrorna är genomsnitt från olika länder och metoder, och säger inget om en enskild person eller vilket stöd som passar henne eller honom bäst.

title: Pathways to Anxiety and Depression in Autistic Adolescents and Adults.
authors: Richdale AL, Lawson LP, Chalmers A, Uljarević M, Uljarević M, Morris EMJ, Arnold SRC, Trollor JN
abstract: Individuals diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder (autism) commonly experience co-occurring anxiety and depression, which are significantly associated. These mental health conditions are also variously associated with increased autistic traits, insomnia, intolerance of uncertainty (IU), sensory sensitivity, and autonomic symptoms. However, no research has explored the relationships between IU, sensory sensitivity, autonomic symptoms, insomnia, and autistic traits and how they might be associated with anxiety and depression in autism. This study took a transdiagnostic approach to explore the relationships between anxiety, depression, autistic traits, insomnia, IU, sensory sensitivities, and autonomic arousal in 222 autistic people aged 15-80 years (55.7% female) using path analysis. Four plausible, theoretical models were tested, with model 1 providing best fit and explaining 48% of variance in depression, 37% of variance in anxiety, and 29% of variance in insomnia. Autistic traits and IU were directly associated with anxiety and indirectly associated with depression through anxiety. Anxiety, insomnia, IU, and sensory sensitivity were all directly associated with depression; autonomic arousal and sensory sensitivity were also indirectly associated with depression through insomnia. Thus, multiple pathways can lead to anxiety and depression in autism, not only via known paths such as insomnia and IU but additionally via autonomic arousal and sensory sensitivities which are also elevated in autism. These findings suggest that careful clinical evaluation and individualised treatment plans are needed for autistic adults with anxiety or depression. When considering prevention, programs that help autistic adults reduce arousal, maintain good sleep, and reduce IU may prove fruitful.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista tiene ansiedad o tristeza persistente, conviene mirar varios factores a la vez: el sueño, la dificultad con la incertidumbre, la sensibilidad sensorial y la activación del cuerpo. Apoyar rutinas de sueño, avisar de los cambios y reducir la sobrecarga sensorial puede ayudar. Es un estudio de asociaciones con 222 personas autistas de 15-80 años. Muestra relaciones, no causas, y no vale igual para todas las personas. Las decisiones clínicas corresponden a profesionales.
sheet.en: If an autistic person has ongoing anxiety or low mood, it helps to look at several things together: sleep, difficulty with uncertainty, sensory sensitivity and how aroused the body feels. Supporting sleep routines, giving notice of changes and easing sensory overload may help. This was a study of associations with 222 autistic people aged 15-80 years. It shows links, not causes, and will not fit every person. Clinical decisions belong to a professional.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person har långvarig ångest eller nedstämdhet kan det hjälpa att se på flera saker samtidigt: sömn, svårigheter med osäkerhet, sensorisk känslighet och kroppens upphetsning. Stöd för sömnrutiner, förvarning om förändringar och mindre sensorisk överbelastning kan hjälpa. Studien undersökte samband hos 222 autistiska personer i åldern 15-80 år. Den visar samband, inte orsaker, och passar inte alla. Kliniska beslut hör till vårdpersonal.

title: A randomized controlled trial of the effects of dog-assisted versus robot dog-assisted therapy for children with autism or Down syndrome.
authors: Van Der Steen S, Kamphorst E, Griffioen RE
abstract: Research with controlled or crossover designs in animal-assisted therapy have largely used control groups receiving no treatment or treatment as usual, which can potentially inflate the effects of these interventions. It is therefore not always clear whether this type of therapy has a positive effect on, for example, the social skills of children with special support needs. To address this, the current study compared children (7-16 years, n = 65) with autism or Down syndrome who received five sessions of dog-assisted therapy (n = 24; 9 female) with an active control group who received five similar sessions of robot dog-assisted therapy (n = 21; 8 female) and a no-treatment control group (n = 20; 8 female). The robot dog was capable of performing autonomous behavior and responding to the child's actions and verbalizations. Using parental questionnaires, we assessed children's social and emotional skills before and after the therapy sessions or waiting period and included a follow-up measurement after 4-6 weeks. On a group level, multilevel analyses showed that children who received dog-assisted therapy improved significantly more in terms of emotional attunement and emotion regulation than children in the two other conditions. No significant differences were found for social confidence, conversational attunement, social cognition, and social motivation. Change from post-test to follow-up was also less apparent. Yet, on a more individual level, when looking at the Reliable Change Index (RCI), most of the highest RCIs (within the 90th percentile) were found in the dog-assisted therapy group. In contrast, most of the lowest RCIs (within the 10th percentile) were found in the robot-assisted group. We discuss the pros and cons of a more individualized approach in this field of study and propose a possible alternative by focusing on interaction dynamics.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija disfruta de los animales, una actividad tranquila con un perro de terapia puede ser una opción para practicar la conexión emocional y la regulación de emociones, siempre según sus gustos. Es un ensayo controlado aleatorizado con 65 niños y niñas de 7-16 años, autistas o con síndrome de Down, que recibieron cinco sesiones con perro, cinco con perro robot, o ninguna intervención. Los padres respondieron cuestionarios. El grupo con perro mejoró más en sintonía emocional y regulación emocional. No hubo diferencias en confianza social, conversación, cognición social ni motivación social. Los efectos fueron menos claros en el seguimiento, y las respuestas individuales variaron.
sheet.en: If your child enjoys animals, a calm session with a therapy dog may be one way to practise emotional connection and emotion regulation, always following their preferences. This randomized controlled trial included 65 autistic children or children with Down syndrome aged 7-16. They had five sessions with a dog, five with a robot dog, or no treatment. Parents completed questionnaires. The dog group improved more in emotional attunement and emotion regulation. There were no differences in social confidence, conversation, social cognition or social motivation. Effects were less clear at follow-up, and individual responses varied, so results may not apply to every child.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn gillar djur kan ett lugnt tillfälle med en terapihund vara ett sätt att öva känslomässig samklang och känsloreglering, alltid utifrån barnets önskemål. Det är en randomiserad kontrollerad studie med 65 barn i åldern 7-16 år, autistiska eller med Downs syndrom. De fick fem tillfällen med hund, fem med robothund eller ingen behandling. Föräldrar fyllde i enkäter. Hundgruppen förbättrades mer i känslomässig samklang och känsloreglering. Inga skillnader sågs i social trygghet, samtal, social kognition eller social motivation. Effekterna var otydligare vid uppföljningen, och individerna svarade olika, så resultaten gäller inte alla barn.

title: Protocol for socioecological study of autism, suicide risk, and mental health care: Integrating machine learning and community consultation for suicide prevention.
authors: Marlow NM, Kramer JM, Kirby AV, Jacobs MM
abstract: Introduction Autistic people experience higher risk of suicidal ideation (SI) and suicide attempts (SA) compared to non-autistic people, yet there is limited understanding of complex, multilevel factors that drive this disparity. Further, determinants of mental health service receipt among this population are unknown. This study will identify socioecological factors associated with increased risk of SI and SA for autistic people and evaluate determinants of mental health care receipt. Methods This study will link information for individuals aged 12-64 years in healthcare claims data (IBM® MarketScan® Research Database and CMS Medicaid) to publicly available databases containing community and policy factors, thereby creating a unique, multilevel dataset that includes health, demographic, community, and policy information. Machine learning data reduction methods will be applied to reduce the dimensionality prior to nested, multilevel empirical estimation. These techniques will allow for robust identification of clusters of socioecological factors associated with 1) risk of SI and SA and 2) receipt of mental health services (type, dose, delivery modality). Throughout, the research team will partner with an established group of autistic partners to promote community relevance, as well as receive input and guidance from a council of policy and practice advisors. Discussion We hypothesize that nested individual (co-occurring conditions, age, sex), community (healthcare availability, social vulnerabilities), and policy factors (state mental health legislation, state Medicaid expansion) will be associated with heightened risk of SI and SA, and that receipt, dose, and delivery of mental health services will be associated with interdependent factors at all three levels. The approach will lead to identification of multilevel clusters of risk and factors that facilitate or impede mental health service delivery. The study team will then engage the community partners, and policy and practice advisors to inform development of recommendations to reduce risk and improve mental health for the autistic population.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista, tómate en serio cualquier mención de pensamientos suicidas o autolesión: pregunta con calma y sin juzgar, escucha y busca apoyo profesional. Este es un protocolo, es decir, un plan de investigación, y aún no ofrece resultados. Usará datos de reclamaciones de salud de personas de 12-64 años para estudiar factores personales, comunitarios y de políticas ligados al riesgo y al acceso a atención de salud mental, con la colaboración de personas autistas como socias. Sus límites: no sabemos qué encontrará y no describe a cada persona. Si te preocupa alguien, contacta con un profesional clínico, un servicio de salud o un servicio de crisis; ante peligro inmediato, llama al número de emergencias de tu país.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person, take any mention of suicidal thoughts or self-injury seriously: ask calmly and without judgement, listen, and look for professional support. This is a protocol, meaning a research plan, so it has no results yet. It will use health claims data for people aged 12-64 to study personal, community and policy factors linked to risk and to getting mental health care, working with autistic partners. Its limits: we do not yet know what it will find, and it cannot describe every person. If you are worried about someone, contact a clinician, a health service or a crisis service; in immediate danger, call the emergency number of your country.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person: ta alla uttalanden om självmordstankar eller självskada på allvar. Fråga lugnt och utan att döma, lyssna och sök professionellt stöd. Det här är ett protokoll, alltså en forskningsplan, och det har inga resultat än. Det ska använda data från sjukvårdsersättningar för personer i åldern 12-64 för att studera personliga, lokala och politiska faktorer kopplade till risk och till tillgång till psykisk vård, tillsammans med autistiska partner. Begränsningar: vi vet ännu inte vad det visar, och det beskriver inte varje person. Om du är orolig för någon, kontakta en läkare, vården eller en krisjour; vid akut fara, ring nödnumret i ditt land.

title: Parent Outcomes from a Randomized Controlled Trial Investigating a Modular Behavioral Intervention for Young Autistic Children.
authors: Levato L, Hochheimer S, Wang H, Wallace L, Hyman S, Anderson C, Warren Z, Butter E, Martin R, Lee E, Smith T, Johnson C
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: We assessed parent stress and competence outcomes from participation in a randomized controlled trial of a modular behavioral intervention (Modular Approach for Young Autistic Children; MAYAC) compared to a treatment-as-usual comprehensive behavioral intervention (CBI). Throughout their participation, parents of military families were included in their child's treatment (e.g., identifying goals, learning strategies to support their child) and reported on their feelings of stress using the Parenting Stress Index-4, Short Form (PSI-4), as well as their feelings of satisfaction and efficacy as a parent on the Parenting Sense of Competence (PSOC) scale. A linear mixed model evaluated the differences in stress and competence from baseline to each assessment period through follow-up. There were no significant differences between groups in stress or competence ratings; however, there were within-group changes in both treatment arms over the course of the trial. In both groups, parent stress decreased, and competence increased over time, continuing to suggest that behavioral analytic intervention for young children with autism can promote positive parent outcomes. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrial.gov identifier: NCT04078061.

sheet.es: Si su hijo autista pequeño recibe una intervención conductual, conviene que usted participe: que ayude a elegir metas y aprenda estrategias. Este ensayo aleatorizado comparó dos formas de intervención conductual en familias militares. En ambos grupos, el estrés de los padres bajó y su sensación de competencia subió con el tiempo, sin diferencias significativas entre los grupos. Como los dos grupos mejoraron, no sabemos qué parte se debe a la intervención y qué parte al paso del tiempo. Tampoco sabemos si ocurriría igual en otras familias. Los resultados no valen como regla para cada familia.
sheet.en: If your young autistic child receives a behavioral intervention, it may help for you to take part: choosing goals together and learning strategies. This randomized trial compared two kinds of behavioral intervention with military families. In both groups, parent stress decreased and parent competence increased over time, with no significant differences between the groups. Because both groups improved, we cannot tell how much came from the intervention and how much from time passing. It also may not apply to other families. These results are not a rule for every family.
sheet.sv: Om ditt lilla autistiska barn får en beteendeintervention kan det hjälpa att du är med: att ni väljer mål tillsammans och att du lär dig strategier. Den här randomiserade studien jämförde två former av beteendeintervention med militärfamiljer. I båda grupperna minskade föräldrarnas stress och deras känsla av kompetens ökade över tid, utan signifikanta skillnader mellan grupperna. Eftersom båda grupperna förbättrades vet vi inte hur mycket som beror på interventionen och hur mycket på tiden. Resultaten gäller kanske inte andra familjer och är ingen regel för alla.

title: The Relationships, Employment, Autonomy, and Life Satisfaction (REALS) Measures for Autistic Adults and Adults With Other Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities: Psychometric Testing of the Self-Report and Proxy Versions.
authors: Conner CM, Yu L, MacKenzie KT, Zeglen KN, Rutenberg EL, Pilkonis PA, Eack SM, Mazefsky CA
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Research and clinical work demonstrate that adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDDs; including autistic adults and adults with other IDDs) struggle with key outcomes in adult life, including social relationships, employment, autonomy, and life satisfaction. However, few validated measures exist to measure these outcomes in adults with IDDs. The Relationships, Employment, Autonomy, and Life Satisfaction (REALS) Measures were created using methods developed by the Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) to assess these outcomes. Large item pools were generated for the four domains, and, in field testing, 875 adults with IDDs (90% autistic; 18.4% with intellectual disability or a non-autism IDD) and 911 proxy reporters (caregivers; 79% autistic; 48.3% with intellectual disability or a non-autism IDD) completed 108 and 74 items, respectively, using response options capturing frequency, level of support needed, and satisfaction. The structure and item content of the REALS Measures were determined through an iterative process using both classical test theory and item response theory analyses. The final versions include 19 self-report and 14 proxy-report measures, with a range of 3 to 14 items each. The measures have excellent psychometric properties, high precision, and acceptable respondent burden. Thus, they are applicable for service provision, clinical, and research arenas for autistic adults and adults with other IDDs, though additional testing in IDD is warranted and evidence supporting self-report use in IDD is more limited.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista adulta, las medidas REALS pueden ayudar a conversar sobre sus relaciones, su trabajo, su autonomía y su satisfacción con la vida, preguntándole a ella directamente y, si hace falta, también a quien la apoya. Es un estudio de validación de cuestionarios: 875 adultos con discapacidades intelectuales y del desarrollo (90% autistas) y 911 informantes, es decir, cuidadores, los respondieron. Las versiones finales tienen 19 medidas de autoinforme y 14 de informante, con entre 3 y 14 ítems cada una. Los autores las describen como precisas y poco pesadas de responder. Límites: hace falta más prueba en otras discapacidades del desarrollo y hay menos evidencia sobre el autoinforme en esos grupos. No sustituye la escucha de cada persona.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult, the REALS Measures can help structure a conversation about their relationships, work, autonomy and life satisfaction, asking the person directly and, where useful, the people who support them too. This was a questionnaire validation study: 875 adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities (90% autistic) and 911 proxy reporters, meaning caregivers, completed items. The final versions include 19 self-report and 14 proxy-report measures, with 3 to 14 items each. The authors describe them as precise and not too burdensome to answer. Limits: more testing is needed in other developmental disabilities, and evidence for self-report in those groups is more limited. The measures do not replace listening to each person.
sheet.sv: Om du stödjer en autistisk vuxen kan REALS-måtten hjälpa till att strukturera ett samtal om personens relationer, arbete, självbestämmande och livstillfredsställelse. Fråga personen själv och, när det är till nytta, även dem som ger stöd. Studien testade och validerade frågeformulär: 875 vuxna med intellektuell och utvecklingsmässig funktionsnedsättning (90 % autistiska) och 911 ombud, alltså vårdgivare, besvarade frågor. De slutliga versionerna har 19 självskattningsmått och 14 ombudsmått, med 3 till 14 frågor vardera. Forskarna beskriver dem som precisa och lätta att besvara. Begränsningar: fler tester behövs vid andra utvecklingsrelaterade funktionsnedsättningar, och stödet för självskattning där är mer begränsat. Måtten ersätter inte att lyssna på varje person.

title: Central Sensitivity Symptoms and Autistic Traits in Autistic and Non-Autistic Adults.
authors: Grant S, Norton S, Hoekstra RA
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Central sensitivity syndromes (CSSs) are a group of health conditions thought to include an underlying sensitisation of the central nervous system. Evidence suggests autistic adults experience poorer physical health than the general population and are more likely to have a CSS. This study examined CSS diagnoses and symptoms in autistic and non-autistic adults, to determine whether CSS symptoms were related to autistic traits, mental health, sensory sensitivity, age or gender. Participants included 534 adults with clinical diagnoses of autism, CSS, both diagnoses or neither (i.e., comparison group), who were recruited through social media, support groups and institutional affiliations. Participants completed online self-report validated questionnaires, including the Autism Spectrum Quotient (AQ), Central Sensitization Inventory (CSI), Sensory Perception Quotient (SPQ), and the PHQ-9 and GAD-7. Autistic people without a diagnosed CSS reported significantly more CSS symptoms than the comparison group, with a mean score above the clinical cut-off. Non-autistic participants with a CSS had significantly more autistic traits than the comparison group. Autistic people with a CSS reported the most sensory sensitivity, with autism only and CSS only groups reporting similar levels of sensory sensitivity and all diagnostic groups reporting more sensory sensitivity than the comparison group. Sensory sensitivity, anxiety, autistic traits, age and gender were all significant predictors of CSS symptoms. The overlap in symptoms between autistic individuals and those with CSS suggests diagnostic overshadowing and possible under-diagnosis or misdiagnosis. Furthermore, these symptoms may exacerbate or mask one another. Notwithstanding potential limitations of representativeness and selection bias, increased awareness of the association between autistic traits and CSS symptoms is important for clinicians to improve diagnostic accuracy and treatment.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista tiene dolor persistente, fatiga o mucha sensibilidad sensorial, conviene anotar estos síntomas y comentarlos con su profesional de salud, sin darlos por 'parte del autismo'. El estudio, con 534 adultos que respondieron cuestionarios en línea, encontró que las personas autistas sin un síndrome de sensibilización central diagnosticado señalaron más síntomas de este tipo que el grupo de comparación. La sensibilidad sensorial y la ansiedad se relacionaron con más síntomas. Es un estudio de un solo momento, no prueba causas, y la selección de participantes puede no representar a todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person has ongoing pain, fatigue or strong sensory sensitivity, it helps to note these symptoms and raise them with a health professional, rather than assuming they are simply 'part of autism'. The study had 534 adults who completed online questionnaires. Autistic people without a diagnosed central sensitivity syndrome reported more of these symptoms than the comparison group. Sensory sensitivity and anxiety were linked to more symptoms. It is a single-time-point study, so it cannot show causes, and the way participants were recruited may not represent everyone.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person har ihållande smärta, trötthet eller stark sensorisk känslighet kan det hjälpa att anteckna symtomen och ta upp dem med vårdpersonal, i stället för att anta att de bara hör till autismen. I studien fyllde 534 vuxna i frågeformulär online. Autistiska personer utan diagnostiserat centralt sensitiseringssyndrom rapporterade fler sådana symtom än jämförelsegruppen. Sensorisk känslighet och ångest hängde ihop med fler symtom. Studien mäter vid ett tillfälle och kan inte visa orsaker, och urvalet kanske inte speglar alla.

title: Treatments for Eating Disorders in People with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Scoping Review.
authors: Simeon R, Galeoto G, Cracolici S, Panuccio F, Berardi A
abstract: Background This scoping review aims to synthesize existing evidence on non-pharmacological interventions for managing food selectivity in individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Specifically, it explores sensory, behavioral, and environmental factors influencing intervention outcomes and examines the role of occupational therapists (OTs) within multidisciplinary teams. Methods A search was conducted across MEDLINE, EBSCO, Web of Science, OTseeker, and SCOPUS from August 2023 to October 2023. Only experimental studies published in English were included, focusing on behavioral treatments and/or occupational therapy interventions. Results A total of 1618 studies were identified. After removing duplicates (170 records), 259 full-text articles were assessed for eligibility, resulting in 61 studies included for qualitative synthesis. Conclusions The findings highlight a wide range of interventions, yet methodological inconsistencies and small sample sizes limit the strength of the evidence. While occupational therapists play an increasing role in feeding interventions, their specific impact remains underexplored. Future research should focus on larger, well-designed studies with standardized outcome measures to better define the effectiveness of interventions and the role of OTs within multidisciplinary teams.

sheet.es: Si la alimentación selectiva preocupa en casa, conviene buscar apoyo de un equipo que combine enfoques conductuales y de terapia ocupacional, y tener en cuenta los factores sensoriales y del entorno de cada persona. Es una revisión de alcance que incluyó 61 estudios experimentales, en inglés, sobre intervenciones no farmacológicas en personas autistas. Hay muchas intervenciones distintas, pero los métodos son poco coherentes y las muestras pequeñas, así que la evidencia es débil. El papel concreto de la terapia ocupacional apenas se ha estudiado. Ninguna conclusión vale como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If selective eating is a worry at home, it may help to look for a team that combines behavioural and occupational therapy approaches, and to consider each person's sensory needs and environment. This is a scoping review that included 61 experimental studies, published in English, on non-medication interventions for autistic people. There are many different interventions, but the methods are inconsistent and the samples small, so the evidence is weak. The specific role of occupational therapy is still little studied. No finding works as a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om selektivt ätande oroar hemma kan det hjälpa att söka ett team som kombinerar beteendeinriktade metoder och arbetsterapi, och att ta hänsyn till varje persons sensoriska behov och miljö. Det är en översikt (scoping review) som inkluderade 61 experimentella studier på engelska om icke-medicinska insatser för autistiska personer. Det finns många olika insatser, men metoderna är inkonsekventa och grupperna små, så underlaget är svagt. Arbetsterapeutens specifika roll är fortfarande föga studerad. Inga resultat gäller som regel för alla personer.

title: Continuation of Pediatric Care after Transfer to Adult Care Among Autistic Youth Overlap of Pediatric and Adult Care.
authors: Sirrianni J, Hanks C, Rust S, Hart LC
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: The transition from pediatric to adult health care is a vulnerable time period for autistic adolescents and young adults (AYA) and for some autistic AYA may include a period of receiving care in both the pediatric and adult health systems. We sought to assess the proportion of autistic AYA who continued to use pediatric health services after their first adult primary care appointment and to identify factors associated with continued pediatric contact. We analyzed electronic medical record (EMR) data from a cohort of autistic AYA seen in a primary-care-based program for autistic people. Using logistic and linear regression, we assessed the relationship between eight patient characteristics and (1) the odds of a patient having ANY pediatric visits after their first adult appointment and (2) the number of pediatric visits among those with at least one pediatric visit. The cohort included 230 autistic AYA, who were mostly white (68%), mostly male (82%), with a mean age of 19.4 years at the time of their last pediatric visit before entering adult care. The majority (n = 149; 65%) had pediatric contact after the first adult visit. Younger age at the time of the first adult visit and more pediatric visits prior to the first adult visit were associated with continued pediatric contact. In this cohort of autistic AYA, most patients had contact with the pediatric system after their first adult primary care appointment.

sheet.es: Si su joven autista empieza a ir a un médico de adultos, no es raro que siga viendo también a su equipo pediátrico durante un tiempo. Conviene preguntar a ambos equipos quién se encarga de qué y cómo se pasará la información. Este estudio analizó historiales médicos electrónicos de 230 jóvenes autistas atendidos en un programa de atención primaria. El 65% tuvo contacto pediátrico después de su primera cita de adultos, sobre todo quienes eran más jóvenes en esa cita y habían tenido más visitas pediátricas antes. Sus límites: es un solo programa, con mayoría de varones y de personas blancas, y los resultados pueden no aplicarse a todas las familias.
sheet.en: If your autistic young person is starting with an adult doctor, it is not unusual for them to keep seeing their pediatric team for a while too. It helps to ask both teams who handles what and how information will be shared. This study looked at electronic medical records of 230 autistic young people seen in a primary-care program. 65% had pediatric contact after their first adult appointment, especially those who were younger at that appointment and had more pediatric visits beforehand. Its limits: it covers a single program, mostly male and white participants, so the results may not apply to every family.
sheet.sv: Om din autistiska unga person börjar hos en vuxenläkare är det inte ovanligt att hen också fortsätter träffa barnsjukvården ett tag. Fråga båda teamen vem som ansvarar för vad och hur information förs över. Studien granskade elektroniska journaler för 230 autistiska unga som fick vård i ett primärvårdsbaserat program. 65% hade barnkontakt efter sitt första vuxenbesök, särskilt de som var yngre vid det besöket och hade haft fler barnbesök tidigare. Begränsningar: studien gäller ett enda program med mest män och vita deltagare, så resultaten gäller kanske inte alla familjer.

title: The Social Validity of Behavioral Interventions: Seeking Input from Autistic Adults.
authors: Baiden KMP, Williams ZJ, Schuck RK, Dwyer P, Wang M
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Many in the autistic community have expressed concerns regarding the use of behavioral interventions with autistic children, suggesting that these interventions may not be socially valid. Though behavioral interventions have evolved to be more naturalistic and child-centered, little structured research has been done to explicitly seek autistic perspectives on the acceptability of specific components of behavioral interventions. Autistic adults (N = 235) were recruited online to take the Autism Intervention Attitudes Scale (AIAS), a questionnaire designed to gather feedback on common intervention goals and practices. Results indicate that participants find goals and practices that highlight quality of life, safety, and autistic interactions acceptable, while those that focus on normalization based on neurotypical standards are not. An exploratory graph analysis revealed three communities of goals ("uncontroversial goals", "controversial goals", and "social goals"). Comparison between naturalistic and structured intervention components additionally showed that autistic participants favored naturalistic strategies. These findings are in line with known criticisms of behavioral intervention from autistic adults, but also provide more information on the specific ways in which behavioral interventions can be reformed. This information can guide professionals in the development of appropriate goals and decisions around intervention planning.

sheet.es: Al revisar los objetivos de apoyo de tu hijo o hija, pregúntate si buscan calidad de vida, seguridad y bienestar, o si solo buscan que parezca no autista. Puedes pedir al equipo que priorice objetivos como comunicarse, estar a salvo y disfrutar, y que use estrategias naturales, dentro del juego y la rutina diaria, en lugar de ejercicios rígidos. Este estudio preguntó con un cuestionario en línea a 235 adultos autistas qué objetivos y prácticas de intervención conductual consideraban aceptables. Sus límites: participaron solo personas reclutadas por internet que pueden responder un cuestionario, así que no representa todas las voces autistas, y mide opiniones, no resultados de las intervenciones.
sheet.en: When you review your child's support goals, ask whether each one serves quality of life, safety and wellbeing, or mainly aims to make them look less autistic. You can ask the team to prioritise goals like communicating, staying safe and enjoying life, and to use naturalistic strategies woven into play and daily routines rather than rigid drills. This study used an online questionnaire with 235 autistic adults, asking which behavioural intervention goals and practices they found acceptable. Its limits: participants were recruited online and able to complete a questionnaire, so not every autistic voice is represented, and it measures opinions, not intervention outcomes.
sheet.sv: När du går igenom ditt barns stödmål, fråga dig om varje mål handlar om livskvalitet, trygghet och välmående, eller mest om att barnet ska verka mindre autistiskt. Du kan be teamet prioritera mål som att kommunicera, vara säker och trivas, och att använda naturliga strategier i lek och vardagsrutiner i stället för stela övningar. Studien använde ett webbformulär där 235 autistiska vuxna fick bedöma vilka mål och metoder inom beteendeinterventioner de tyckte var acceptabla. Begränsningar: deltagarna rekryterades på nätet och kunde fylla i en enkät, så alla autistiska röster finns inte med, och studien mäter åsikter, inte effekter av insatser.

title: Schizophrenia in Autistic People with Intellectual Disabilities. Treatment and Interventions.
authors: Bakken TL, Askeland Hellerud JM, Kildahl AN, Solheim-Inderberg AM, Hove O, Berge Helverschou S
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Autistic people with intellectual disabilities appear to be at increased risk of schizophrenia. While current recommendations emphasize adapting interventions used for people with schizophrenia in general, few studies to date have investigated treatment of co-occurring schizophrenia in this specific population. To explore what interventions are provided to autistic people with intellectual disabilities and co-occurring schizophrenia in specialized mental health services, and to investigate whether changes in mental health symptoms and challenging behavior occurred during treatment. Using data from a longitudinal, national multicenter study, interventions provided to 26 autistic individuals with intellectual disabilities and co-occurring schizophrenia were explored. Symptoms were measured using the Psychopathology in Autism Checklist (PAC) and the Aberrant Behavior Checklist ABC) at referral (T1), at the end of treatment (T2), and at follow-up 12 months after T2 (T3). A broad range of interventions were provided to the participants, including inpatient admission, psychopharmacological treatment, various psychosocial interventions, and supportive interventions. Scores on the PAC and ABC were significantly lower at T2 than T1 for most scales, and no significant change was found from T2 to T3.Treatment of co-occurring schizophrenia appears feasible and effective in autistic people with intellectual disabilities.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista con discapacidad intelectual muestra cambios marcados en su estado mental, conviene consultar pronto con los servicios de salud mental, porque el tratamiento de la esquizofrenia asociada parece posible y útil. Es un estudio con 26 personas autistas con discapacidad intelectual y esquizofrenia, atendidas en servicios especializados; sus síntomas se midieron al inicio, al final del tratamiento y 12 meses después. Las puntuaciones bajaron en casi todas las escalas y no cambiaron después. Los límites: el grupo es pequeño y no se comparó con otro grupo sin tratamiento. Las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If an autistic person with an intellectual disability shows marked changes in their mental state, it is worth contacting mental health services early, because treating co-occurring schizophrenia appears feasible and helpful. This was a study of 26 autistic people with intellectual disabilities and schizophrenia in specialized services; symptoms were measured at referral, at the end of treatment and 12 months later. Scores were lower on most scales after treatment and did not change afterwards. Limits: the group is small and there was no comparison group without treatment. Medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning visar tydliga förändringar i sitt psykiska mående är det värt att kontakta psykiatrin tidigt, eftersom behandling av samtidig schizofreni verkar möjlig och till hjälp. Studien omfattade 26 autistiska personer med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning och schizofreni i specialiserad vård; symtomen mättes vid remiss, vid behandlingens slut och 12 månader senare. Poängen var lägre på de flesta skalor efter behandlingen och ändrades inte därefter. Begränsningar: gruppen är liten och det fanns ingen jämförelsegrupp utan behandling. Medicinska beslut hör till en läkare.

title: Reasonable adjustments for autistic clinicians: A qualitative study.
authors: Smith H, Shaw SCK, Doherty M, Ives J
abstract: Autistic people experience barriers to accessing healthcare. Autistic clinical professionals may be able to help improve this situation. Previous research, however, has shown that Autistic clinical professionals experience numerous challenges in the workplace. If there is a 'substantial' and 'long-term' negative effect on the person's ability to do normal daily activities, then Autism may be considered a disability under The Equality Act 2010; the jurisdiction of which covers Great Britain. Autistic clinical professionals working in healthcare settings across England, Wales, and Scotland are therefore entitled to reasonable adjustments to aid them in their clinical practice. This is a qualitative study. We recruited 82 Autistic clinical professionals via social media to complete an online survey. Questions broadly explored: 1) the challenges they faced in their clinical workplaces; and 2) the reasonable adjustments that they needed, had, or needed but did not have. Data were analysed quasi-thematically, also drawing on the principles of content analysis. Respondents reported multiple challenges from our analysis, from which we developed 8 themes: gaining and attending employment, reasonable adjustments under the radar, connecting and integrating (specifically, the communication mismatches between Autistic professionals and non-autistic colleagues, and fitting in socially and professionally), executive functioning, change, working environment, working practices/cultures, and the consequences and effects on Autistic clinical professionals). We recommend that Autistic clinical professionals and their employers individually discuss and iteratively revisit the unique combination of reasonable adjustments suitable for each person. In this way, employers may provide equitable workplaces for their staff which will benefit not only them, but their patients, and healthcare as a whole.

sheet.es: Si trabajas con una persona autista que es profesional clínica, o lo eres tú, conviene hablar con el empleador sobre qué adaptaciones razonables le sirven a cada persona y volver a revisarlas con el tiempo. Se trata de un estudio cualitativo en el que 82 profesionales clínicos autistas de Inglaterra, Gales y Escocia, reclutados por redes sociales, respondieron una encuesta en línea. Señalaron temas como la comunicación con colegas no autistas, el entorno de trabajo, el cambio y las funciones ejecutivas. Tiene límites: son relatos de quienes decidieron participar y no representan a todas las personas, ni a otros países ni a otros trabajos.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic clinical professional, or you are one, it helps to talk with the employer about which reasonable adjustments suit that person, and to revisit them over time. This was a qualitative study in which 82 autistic clinical professionals in England, Wales and Scotland, recruited through social media, completed an online survey. They described themes such as communication with non-autistic colleagues, the working environment, change and executive functioning. It has limits: these are accounts from people who chose to take part, and they do not speak for everyone, other countries or other jobs.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk kliniskt verksam person, eller själv är det, kan det hjälpa att prata med arbetsgivaren om vilka rimliga anpassningar som passar just den personen och ta upp dem igen med tiden. Det var en kvalitativ studie där 82 autistiska kliniska yrkespersoner i England, Wales och Skottland, rekryterade via sociala medier, besvarade en webbenkät. De beskrev teman som kommunikation med icke-autistiska kollegor, arbetsmiljön, förändring och exekutiva funktioner. Studien har begränsningar: det är berättelser från dem som valde att delta, och de gäller inte alla personer, andra länder eller andra arbeten.

title: Barriers and facilitators to primary healthcare encounters as reported by autistic adults: a qualitative study.
authors: Stein Duker LI, Giffin W, Taylor EE, Shkhyan L, Pomponio Davidson A, Mosqueda L
abstract: Background Primary care is designed to co-manage health concerns, contribute to preventive care, and provide medical care coordination. Receiving primary care may be especially vital for autistic people, many of whom disproportionately experience psychiatric and physical health conditions. However, autistic adults often face barriers to receiving primary care, and first-hand accounts of these challenges are limited. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to describe barriers and facilitators to primary care encounters as reported by autistic adults. Methods Interviews were conducted with 34 autistic adults in Los Angeles and Philadelphia, lasted an average of 26 min, were transcribed verbatim, and analyzed using thematic analysis. This dataset is part of a larger study that interviewed autistic adults, caregivers, and primary care providers (PCPs). Results Participants were primarily White, non-Hispanic, and had a mean age of 32 years. Five overarching themes describing challenges and potential strategies to improve care emerged from the interviews: (1) finding a primary care provider , (2) the physical environment , (3) communication, (4) autism-specific knowledge, and (5) support for primary care encounters , while simultaneously highlighting the importance of tailoring care for autistic adults to improve primary care experiences. Results, specifically in the communication and autism-specific knowledge themes, were consistent with the neurodiversity model of autism, as participants highlighted stigma and mutual communication as key healthcare barriers. Conclusion Findings provide a nuanced understanding of autistic adult participants' primary care experiences, highlighting their perception of barriers and facilitators to these healthcare encounters. These results offer valuable insights for improving the accessibility and quality of care for autistic people, many of which are practical, low/no cost, and easy to implement. Strategies also emphasized the diversity of experiences and preferences for autistic patients, highlighting the importance of tailoring accommodations in the primary care setting.

sheet.es: Antes de la próxima cita médica, pensad juntos qué ayudaría: el ambiente, cómo comunicarse y si alguien puede acompañar. Se puede avisar a la consulta con antelación. Es un estudio cualitativo con entrevistas a 34 adultos autistas en Los Angeles y Filadelfia, que señalaron cinco temas: encontrar profesional, el entorno físico, la comunicación, el conocimiento sobre autismo y el apoyo en la consulta. Tiene límites: los participantes eran sobre todo blancos no hispanos, con una edad media de 32 años, y las preferencias varían mucho de una persona a otra, así que conviene preguntar a cada persona qué necesita.
sheet.en: Before the next medical appointment, think together about what would help: the environment, how to communicate, and whether someone can come along. You can tell the clinic in advance. This was a qualitative study with interviews of 34 autistic adults in Los Angeles and Philadelphia, who described five themes: finding a provider, the physical environment, communication, knowledge about autism, and support during visits. It has limits: participants were mostly White, non-Hispanic, with a mean age of 32 years, and preferences differ a lot between people, so ask each person what they need.
sheet.sv: Inför nästa vårdbesök kan ni fundera tillsammans på vad som skulle hjälpa: miljön, hur man kommunicerar och om någon kan följa med. Ni kan berätta det för mottagningen i förväg. Det här var en kvalitativ studie med intervjuer av 34 autistiska vuxna i Los Angeles och Philadelphia, som beskrev fem teman: att hitta vårdgivare, den fysiska miljön, kommunikation, kunskap om autism och stöd under besöket. Studien har begränsningar: deltagarna var mest vita, icke-latinamerikanska, med medelåldern 32 år, och behoven varierar mycket, så fråga alltid vad just den personen behöver.

title: Incorporating Psychoeducational Care in the Autism Diagnosis Pathway: Experiences, Views, and Recommendations of UK Autistic Adults and Autism Professionals.
authors: Beresford B, Mukherjee S
abstract: Background When someone receives a diagnosis they may need support with information and emotional needs. These are called psychoeducational needs. For adults diagnosed with autism, these can include needing to understand and make sense of the diagnosis and finding self-management strategies that work for them. When autistic adults do not receive the psychoeducational support they need their mental health and self-confidence in managing everyday life is affected. However, many diagnostic services do not provide psychoeducational care. In this study, we investigated autistic adults' and autism specialist staff's views on the psychoeducational care that diagnostic services should provide. Methods We recruited 26 autistic adults and 30 staff working in 8 UK autism services commissioned to provide both diagnostic assessments and post-diagnostic care.
