Receiving > 1 neurodevelopmental diagnosis on completion was uncommon. Demographic factors did not significantly affect waiting times. Children/adolescents with more complex developmental and medical histories experienced longer waits (100.3 weeks vs. 67.7 weeks; p < 0.001), while adults with similar histories had shorter waits (32.7 weeks vs. 57.4 weeks; p = 0.016). Adults with ADHD experienced longer waits than autistic adults (63.4 weeks vs. 38.6 weeks, p = 0.002). Adherence to best-practice quality standards was associated with shorter waits for children (β = 0.27, p = 0.002), but the relationship between standard adherence at different stages and for adults was less clear. More frequent appointments correlated with shorter adult waits (33.7 weeks vs. 59.2 weeks, p = 0.015). Gender distribution was balanced among adults, but children's services included more boys. The study highlights long waits and the need for improvement in processes.

sheet.es: Si esperas una evaluación, prepara un resumen ordenado de la historia del desarrollo y de salud, y pregunta al servicio cómo y cuándo contactará contigo; las esperas largas no dependen de ti. Es un estudio retrospectivo de 408 casos evaluados en Scotland por 30 equipos. La mediana de espera fue de 525 días en niñez y adolescencia y de 252 días en personas adultas. Las historias más complejas se asociaron con esperas más largas en la infancia. Solo describe servicios de un país y un periodo, y no explica por qué ocurre cada espera; tu situación puede ser distinta.
sheet.en: If you are waiting for an assessment, prepare a clear summary of developmental and medical history, and ask the service how and when it will contact you; long waits are not your fault. This was a retrospective review of 408 cases assessed by 30 diagnosing teams in Scotland. Median waits were 525 days for children and adolescents and 252 days for adults. More complex histories were linked to longer waits in childhood. It covers services in one country and period, and cannot explain why any single wait happens, so your situation may differ.
sheet.sv: Om du väntar på en utredning kan du förbereda en tydlig sammanfattning av utvecklings- och sjukdomshistorik och fråga verksamheten hur och när de kontaktar dig; de långa väntetiderna är inte ditt fel. Detta var en retrospektiv genomgång av 408 fall som bedömts av 30 team i Scotland. Mediantiden var 525 dagar för barn och ungdomar och 252 dagar för vuxna. Mer komplex historik hängde ihop med längre väntan hos barn. Studien gäller tjänster i ett land och en period och kan inte förklara varje enskild väntetid, så din situation kan se annorlunda ut.

title: Altered Patterns of Dynamic Functional Connectivity Underpin Reduced Expressions of Social-Emotional Reciprocity in Autistic Adults.
authors: Czekóová K, Mareček R, Staněk R, Hartley C, Kessler K, Hlavatá P, Ošlejšková H, Brázdil M, Shaw DJ
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: To identify the neurocognitive mechanisms underpinning the social difficulties that characterize autism, we performed functional magnetic resonance imaging on pairs of autistic and non-autistic adults simultaneously whilst they interacted with one another on the iterated Ultimatum Game (iUG)-an interactive task that emulates the reciprocal characteristic of naturalistic interpersonal exchanges. Two age-matched sets of male-male dyads were investigated: 16 comprised an autistic Responder and a non-autistic Proposer, and 19 comprised non-autistic pairs of Responder and Proposer. Players' round-by-round behavior on the iUG was modeled as reciprocal choices, and dynamic functional connectivity (dFC) was measured to identify the neural mechanisms underpinning reciprocal behaviors. Behavioral expressions of reciprocity were significantly reduced in autistic compared with non-autistic Responders, yet no such differences were observed between the non-autistic Proposers in either set of dyads. Furthermore, we identified latent dFC states with temporal properties associated with reciprocity. Autistic interactants spent less time in brain states characterized by dynamic inter-network integration and segregation among the Default Mode Network and cognitive control networks, suggesting that their reduced expressions of social-emotional reciprocity reflect less efficient reconfigurations among brain networks supporting flexible cognition and behavior. These findings advance our mechanistic understanding of the social difficulties characterizing autism.

sheet.es: Una idea práctica: la reciprocidad social puede depender del tipo de intercambio y de la pareja, así que conviene dar tiempo, turnos claros y mensajes explícitos en las interacciones. Evidencia: estudio con resonancia magnética en parejas de hombres adultos que jugaban un juego de turnos; 16 parejas incluían a una persona autista y 19 eran parejas no autistas. Las personas autistas mostraron menos reciprocidad en el juego y pasaron menos tiempo en ciertos estados de actividad cerebral. Límites: solo hombres, muestra pequeña, una tarea de laboratorio; no describe a todas las personas autistas ni sirve para diagnosticar.
sheet.en: Practical takeaway: social reciprocity may depend on the kind of exchange and the partner, so it helps to allow time, use clear turn-taking and say things explicitly in interactions. Evidence: a brain-imaging study of adult male pairs playing a turn-taking game; 16 pairs included an autistic person and 19 were non-autistic pairs. The autistic players showed less reciprocity in the game and spent less time in certain brain activity states. Limits: only men, a small sample and a lab task; it does not describe every autistic person and cannot be used to diagnose.
sheet.sv: Praktiskt tips: social ömsesidighet kan bero på typen av utbyte och på motparten, så det hjälper att ge tid, ha tydlig turtagning och uttrycka saker uttryckligen. Evidens: en hjärnavbildningsstudie på vuxna manliga par som spelade ett turtagningsspel; 16 par bestod av en autistisk person och 19 var icke-autistiska par. De autistiska spelarna visade mindre ömsesidighet i spelet och tillbringade mindre tid i vissa hjärnaktivitetstillstånd. Begränsningar: endast män, litet urval och en laboratorieuppgift; den beskriver inte alla autistiska personer och kan inte användas för diagnos.

title: K-12 Life Skills Education, Independence, and Employment of Autistic Individuals: Giving Voice to Autistic Adults.
authors: Zatz JC, Harrison JR
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Autistic adults are often challenged to engage in and complete life skill tasks independently and are underrepresented in employment. No prior study has explored the perceptions of autistic individuals regarding K-12 life skills experiences and postsecondary employment. As such, the purposes of this study were to explore the association between components of life skills instruction and employment for 12 autistic individuals, and to elicit the perspectives of and experiences in K-12 education and employment of six autistic adults. As this was a mixed methods study, surveys and semi-structured interviews were conducted. Results of Fisher's test indicated no statistically significant associations between employment and instructional components; however, the associations between employment and household chores [Cramer's V = .60]; cooking [Cramer's V = .66]; one-on-one instruction [Cramer's V = .63]; and field trips [Cramer's V = .41]) were large. The associations between employment and job site training [Cramer's V = .33] and token boards [Cramer's V = .33]) were moderate. Three themes and 10 subthemes emerged. Specifically, participants remembered Memorable Components from K-12 instruction: (a) job site training, (b) field trips, and (c) household chores. Participants perceived Beneficial Practices as: (a) job site training and (b) skills learned. Participants described shortcomings of K-12 instruction as need (a) for more skills training, (c) for social skills training, (d) to eliminate unnecessary instruction and (e) to carefully consider student placement. In conclusion, participants described experiences that helped them gain and attain post-secondary employment. More specific individualized programming in K-12 instruction would be beneficial to develop independence and post-secondary employment.

sheet.es: Si apoyas a un joven autista en su etapa escolar, pregúntale qué habilidades de la vida diaria recuerda como útiles y plantea programas individualizados, con práctica real como tareas del hogar, salidas y formación en un puesto de trabajo. La evidencia es un estudio con métodos mixtos: encuestas a 12 personas autistas y entrevistas a seis adultos autistas sobre su educación y empleo. Sus límites: la muestra es muy pequeña, no se hallaron asociaciones estadísticamente significativas con el empleo y las experiencias de estas personas no valen para todas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic young person at school, ask them which daily life skills they find useful, and push for individualised programmes with real practice, such as household chores, field trips and job site training. The evidence is a mixed methods study: surveys with 12 autistic people and interviews with six autistic adults about their schooling and employment. Its limits: the sample is very small, no statistically significant associations with employment were found, and these experiences will not apply to everyone.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk ungdom i skolan, fråga vilka vardagsfärdigheter hen upplever som användbara och be om individanpassade program med verklig övning, som hushållssysslor, studiebesök och arbetsplatsträning. Underlaget är en studie med blandade metoder: enkäter med 12 autistiska personer och intervjuer med sex autistiska vuxna om skolgång och arbete. Begränsningar: urvalet är mycket litet, inga statistiskt signifikanta samband med anställning hittades, och erfarenheterna gäller inte alla.

title: Applicability and Psychometric Properties of General Mental Health Assessment Tools in Autistic People: A Systematic Review.
authors: Halvorsen MB, Kildahl AN, Kaiser S, Axelsdottir B, Aman MG, Helverschou SB
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: In recent years, there has been a proliferation of instruments for assessing mental health (MH) among autistic people. This study aimed to review the psychometric properties of broadband instruments used to assess MH problems among autistic people. In accordance with the PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO: CRD42022316571) we searched the APA PsycINFO via Ovid, Ovid MEDLINE, Ovid Embase and the Web of Science via Clarivate databases from 1980 to March 2022, with an updated search in January 2024, to identify very recent empirical studies. Independent reviewers evaluated the titles and abstracts of the retrieved records (n = 11,577) and full-text articles (n = 1000). Data were extracted from eligible studies, and the quality of the included papers was appraised. In all, 164empirical articles reporting on 35 instruments were included. The review showed variable evidence of reliability and validity of the various instruments. Among the instruments reported in more than one study, the Aberrant Behavior Checklist had consistently good or excellent psychometric evidence. The reliability and validity of other instruments, including: the Developmental Behavior Checklist, Emotion Dysregulation Inventory, Eyberg Child Behavior Inventory, Autism Spectrum Disorder-Comorbid for Children Scale, and Psychopathology in Autism Checklist, were less documented. There is a need for a greater evidence-base for MH assessment tools for autistic people.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista va a pasar por una evaluación de salud mental, conviene preguntar al profesional qué cuestionarios usa y si se han comprobado con personas autistas. Una revisión sistemática buscó estudios publicados y encontró 164 artículos sobre 35 instrumentos. La evidencia de fiabilidad y validez fue variable; la Aberrant Behavior Checklist mostró evidencia buena o excelente de forma constante entre las herramientas usadas en más de un estudio. Otras herramientas tenían menos respaldo. Límites: es una revisión de estudios, no dice qué herramienta es mejor para una persona concreta, y las puntuaciones deben interpretarse junto con la voz de la persona y su contexto.
sheet.en: If an autistic person is having a mental health assessment, it is reasonable to ask the professional which questionnaires they use and whether those tools have been checked with autistic people. A systematic review searched published studies and found 164 articles covering 35 instruments. Evidence of reliability and validity varied; among tools used in more than one study, the Aberrant Behavior Checklist consistently showed good or excellent evidence. Other tools had less support. Limits: it reviews studies, does not say which tool suits a particular person, and results should be read alongside the person's own voice and context.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person ska genomgå en bedömning av psykisk hälsa kan det vara bra att fråga vilka formulär som används och om de har prövats på autistiska personer. En systematisk översikt sökte i publicerade studier och hittade 164 artiklar om 35 instrument. Bevisen för tillförlitlighet och validitet varierade; bland verktyg som användes i mer än en studie visade Aberrant Behavior Checklist genomgående goda eller utmärkta belägg. Andra verktyg hade mindre stöd. Begränsningar: det är en översikt av studier, den säger inte vilket verktyg som passar en enskild person, och resultat bör tolkas tillsammans med personens egen röst och sammanhang.

title: Equitable access to sustainable healthcare services for children with autism.
authors: Sultan MA
abstract: This perspective article addresses the critical issue of equitable access to sustainable healthcare services for children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Despite the increasing prevalence of ASD globally, significant disparities persist in accessing appropriate healthcare services. The lack of comprehensive data on autism prevalence and incidence in many regions further exacerbates this challenge, hindering the development of targeted interventions and equitable resource allocation. This paper sheds light on barriers to equitable access, including geographical disparities, cultural stigma, communication barriers and inadequate training of healthcare providers. Strategies for achieving sustainable solutions are proposed, including the expansion of telehealth services, financial assistance programmes, competency training, community-based support programmes and investment in high-quality research. By addressing these challenges and implementing evidence-based interventions, we can work towards ensuring that all children with autism have access to the healthcare services they need for optimal development and well-being.

sheet.es: Si buscas atención sanitaria para tu hijo autista, puede ayudarte preguntar por opciones de telesalud, ayudas económicas y programas comunitarios, y avisar a los profesionales de cómo se comunica mejor tu hijo. El estudio es un artículo de perspectiva (una revisión), no un experimento con participantes. Describe barreras como la distancia, el estigma cultural, las dificultades de comunicación y la formación insuficiente de los profesionales, y propone soluciones. Sus límites: ofrece opiniones y propuestas, no prueba que cada medida funcione, y la situación cambia mucho según la región y cada familia.
sheet.en: If you are looking for healthcare for your autistic child, it may help to ask about telehealth options, financial assistance and community-based programmes, and to tell professionals how your child communicates best. This is a perspective article (a review), not an experiment with participants. It describes barriers such as distance, cultural stigma, communication difficulties and limited training of healthcare providers, and proposes solutions. Its limits: it offers views and proposals rather than proof that each measure works, and the situation varies a great deal between regions and families.
sheet.sv: Om du söker vård för ditt autistiska barn kan det hjälpa att fråga efter vård på distans, ekonomiskt stöd och lokala stödprogram, och att berätta för personalen hur ditt barn kommunicerar bäst. Studien är en perspektivartikel (en översikt), inte ett experiment med deltagare. Den beskriver hinder som avstånd, kulturellt stigma, kommunikationssvårigheter och bristande utbildning hos vårdpersonal, och föreslår lösningar. Begränsningar: den bygger på synpunkter och förslag, inte på bevis för att varje åtgärd fungerar, och situationen skiljer sig mycket mellan regioner och familjer.

title: Study protocol for a randomized controlled trial of Regulating Together (RT), a group therapy for emotion dysregulation in school-age autistic youth and their caregivers.
authors: McKinney WS, Tadevich LJ, Schmitt LM, Horn PS, Ruberg JR, White SW, Reisinger DL, Burkett KW, Sarawgi S, Kang S, Shaffer RC
abstract: Background Emotion dysregulation is a common concern in autistic youth. Growing evidence suggests emotion dysregulation underlies multiple co-occurring issues in autism, including externalizing (e.g., aggression, irritability) and internalizing (e.g., anxiety, depression) disorders, and thus may serve as a key transdiagnostic treatment target. Emotion dysregulation during middle childhood (8-12 years) is concurrently and longitudinally associated with social difficulties and poorer quality of life for autistic individuals, highlighting a key window for intervention. There is an urgent need for treatments for emotion dysregulation in school-age autistic youth that involve caregivers to maximize skill generalization. To address this need, our group developed Regulating Together, an intensive outpatient group program targeting emotion dysregulation in 8- to 12-year-old autistic youth that integrates strategies from cognitive behavioral therapy, mindfulness and acceptance-based therapies, and parent training programs. Building on our previous non-randomized trials of Regulating Together, we document the study protocol for our first, and ongoing, randomized controlled trial comparing Regulating Together to an active control condition. Methods This is a five-year randomized controlled trial comparing Regulating Together to Achieving Independence and Mastery in School (AIMS), an active control condition targeting executive functioning difficulties, in an outpatient hospital setting. Enrollment is ongoing and the study is expected to be completed in late Fall of 2026. Participants will be 144 autistic youth (8-12 years; IQ ≥ 65) randomized to either 5-week treatment condition. A comprehensive assessment battery integrating self-, caregiver-, and clinician-report information, functional outcomes (i.e., number of psychiatric hospitalizations), objective outcomes (probabilistic reversal learning task), and biobehavioral measures (heart rate variability) will be collected and compared between baseline (Week 0), post-treatment (Week 7), post-generalization (Week 16), and at long-term follow-up (Week 29). Discussion This is the first comparison of the Regulating Together program to an active treatment condition. Findings from this study will build on previous piloted iterations of Regulating Together by characterizing its efficacy in relation to active treatment, testing moderators of treatment response, and identifying barriers and facilitators to treatment access, impact, and sustainability. Following completion of this study, we will pursue implementation studies (e.g., testing program implementation and effectiveness in community settings). Dissemination and external provider training efforts are ongoing. Trial registration Trial registration took place through ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05803369) on March 14th, 2023.

sheet.es: Este estudio aún no ofrece resultados, así que no hay nada que aplicar mañana. Sí muestra que existe un programa grupal, Regulating Together, para niñas y niños autistas de 8 a 12 años y sus cuidadores, pensado para las dificultades de regulación emocional, y que se está evaluando. Si le interesa, puede preguntar a un profesional si hay programas similares cerca. Evidencia: es el protocolo de un ensayo aleatorizado en curso; participarán 144 jóvenes autistas (8-12 años; CI ≥ 65), con un programa de 5 semanas comparado con otro programa activo. Límites: aún no sabemos si funciona, y los resultados no valdrán para todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: This study has no results yet, so there is nothing to apply tomorrow. It does show that a group program, Regulating Together, exists for autistic children aged 8-12 and their caregivers, aimed at emotion regulation difficulties, and that it is being tested. If you are interested, you could ask a professional whether similar programs are available near you. Evidence: this is the protocol of an ongoing randomized trial; 144 autistic youth (8-12 years; IQ ≥ 65) will take part, comparing a 5-week program with another active program. Limits: we do not yet know whether it works, and results will not apply to every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Studien har inga resultat än, så det finns inget att tillämpa i morgon. Den visar dock att det finns ett gruppprogram, Regulating Together, för autistiska barn i åldern 8-12 år och deras vårdnadshavare, riktat mot svårigheter med känsloreglering, och att det nu prövas. Om du är intresserad kan du fråga en yrkesperson om liknande program finns i närheten. Evidens: detta är protokollet för en pågående randomiserad studie; 144 autistiska unga (8-12 år; IQ ≥ 65) ska delta, och ett 5 veckor långt program jämförs med ett annat aktivt program. Begränsningar: vi vet ännu inte om det fungerar, och resultaten gäller inte alla autistiska personer.

title: The Complexities of Navigating the Healthcare System as an Autistic Individual with Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome: A Patient Perspective.
authors: Clark S
abstract: Autistic individuals with hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (hEDS) often face unique challenges navigating healthcare systems due to lack of clinician awareness, diagnostic delays, misdiagnoses, and systemic barriers. Drawing on my own lived experience within the UK's National Health Service (NHS), this patient perspective article integrates personal narratives with the research and literature, highlighting critical gaps in clinical care, offering practical recommendations to enhance equity and inclusion. Recommendations include: improved clinician education on neurodivergence and overlapping conditions, improving holistic patient-centred communication, and collaborative care models that prioritise patient needs, learning from lived expertise.

sheet.es: Antes de una cita médica, puede ayudar escribir una lista breve de síntomas, otras condiciones (como autismo y síndrome de Ehlers-Danlos hipermóvil) y lo que necesitas de la comunicación, y pedir que quede anotado. Este artículo es una perspectiva de una persona autista con hEDS, basada en su experiencia en el NHS del Reino Unido y combinada con literatura científica. Señala falta de conocimiento clínico, retrasos diagnósticos y errores de diagnóstico. Propone formar mejor a los profesionales, comunicar de forma más holística y trabajar en colaboración. Es una sola experiencia personal, no un estudio con muestra, y puede no reflejar la de otras personas ni la de otros sistemas sanitarios.
sheet.en: Before a medical appointment, it can help to write a short list of symptoms, your other conditions (such as autism and hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome) and what you need from communication, and ask for it to be recorded. This article is a patient perspective by an autistic person with hEDS, drawing on their experience in the UK's NHS and combined with research literature. It points to clinicians' lack of awareness, diagnostic delays and misdiagnoses. It recommends better clinician education, more holistic communication and collaborative care. It is one personal account, not a sample-based study, so it may not reflect other people's experiences or other health systems.
sheet.sv: Inför ett läkarbesök kan det hjälpa att skriva en kort lista över symtom, andra tillstånd (som autism och hypermobilt Ehlers-Danlos syndrom) och vad du behöver av kommunikationen, och be att det förs in i journalen. Artikeln är ett patientperspektiv från en autistisk person med hEDS, baserat på erfarenheter inom brittiska NHS och kopplat till forskningslitteratur. Den lyfter bristande kunskap hos vårdpersonal, försenade diagnoser och felaktiga diagnoser. Den föreslår bättre utbildning av personal, mer helhetsinriktad kommunikation och samarbetande vård. Det är en enskild personlig berättelse, inte en studie med urval, och den speglar kanske inte andras erfarenheter eller andra vårdsystem.

title: Sensory-movement underpinnings of lifelong neurodivergence: getting a grip on autism.
authors: Kapp SK
abstract: While the autism diagnosis emphasizes "deficits" in social communication, the article advances that sensory-movement differences underpin autism through a review of the following sources of evidence. This account critically challenges "autistic regression", with evidence that sensory-movement features appear by birth as the earliest signs of autism and underlie the behavioral differences used for diagnosis, which may reflect adaptations to inherent differences and misunderstandings from others. Sensory and motor differences are salient to autistic people, but they often go underrecognized by others. They cause cascading effects in infancy on behavior and communication through differences in sensorimotor learning, automatic imitation, eye contact, sensory perception, and interests. The article then explains how sensory processing differences may influence reduced perceptual narrowing, which involves a bottom-up information processing style grounded in the surrounding environment. Furthermore, this bottom-up processing may grow from reduced sensory integration in feedback loops potentially involving the cerebellum of the brain. The article then moves into implications for the widespread consequences of these inherent differences on quality of life. The article closes with implications for autism as a construct (including underestimated empathy and pain), testing the theory, providing sensory-sensitive support and acceptance of autistic people, and applications to diverse autistic people. The theory may apply particularly well to autistic women and girls, autistic people with speech divergence, autistic people with ADHD, and autistic people with co-occurring sensory and motor-related neurodivergences. Throughout the article, the theory also provides clinical, neurological, and experiential evidence for sensory and motor differences as lifelong, challenging the notion of "losing" (an) autism (diagnosis) as instead reflecting (risky and not necessarily "successful") camouflaging.

sheet.es: Mañana, antes de pensar en la conducta, fíjate en lo sensorial y motor: ruidos, luces, texturas, el movimiento del cuerpo. Ajustar el entorno y aceptar esas diferencias puede ayudar más que corregir. El artículo es una revisión teórica de distintas fuentes de evidencia sobre personas autistas. Defiende que estas diferencias aparecen desde el nacimiento y duran toda la vida. Sus límites: es una propuesta que aún debe ponerse a prueba y no describe a todas las personas autistas por igual. Úsalo como una idea para observar, no como una regla.
sheet.en: Tomorrow morning, before thinking about behaviour, notice the sensory and movement side: sounds, lights, textures, how the body moves. Adjusting the environment and accepting these differences may help more than trying to correct them. The article is a theoretical review drawing on several sources of evidence about autistic people. It argues that these differences are present from birth and last throughout life. Its limits: it is a proposal that still needs testing, and it does not describe every autistic person in the same way. Use it as an idea to observe with, not as a rule.
sheet.sv: I morgon bitti: titta först på det sensoriska och motoriska, som ljud, ljus, material och hur kroppen rör sig, innan du tänker på beteendet. Att anpassa miljön och acceptera skillnaderna kan hjälpa mer än att försöka korrigera dem. Artikeln är en teoretisk översikt av flera typer av evidens om autistiska personer. Den hävdar att skillnaderna finns från födseln och varar hela livet. Begränsningar: det är ett förslag som ännu måste prövas, och det beskriver inte alla autistiska personer lika. Använd det som en idé att observera med, inte som en regel.

title: Supporting Autistic Children's Participation in Research Studies: A Mixed-Methods Study of Familiarizing Autistic Children with A Humanoid Robot.
authors: McGregor C, von dem Hagen E, Wallbridge C, Dobbs J, Svenson-Tree C, Jones CR
abstract: It is important that autism research is inclusive and supports the participation of a wide range of autistic people. However, there has been limited research on how to make studies accessible for autistic participants. This mixed-methods study explored how to promote the comfort of autistic children in research, using the specific example of visiting a research lab and meeting a humanoid robot. In Phase 1, 14 parents of autistic children were interviewed about how their child could be made comfortable during a lab visit, including different approaches for familiarizing their child with the robot. In Phase 2, autistic children of the parents in Phase 1 ( n = 10) visited the lab and completed familiarization activities with a humanoid robot. The opinions of the children and their parents about the children's experiences were recorded. Using reflexive thematic analysis, five overarching themes reflected how to best support autistic child participants. These themes encompassed elements of particular relevance to robot studies but also many practices of general relevance to participating in research: (1) preparation is key, (2) consideration of environmental factors, (3) using familiarization, (4) a supportive and engaged researcher, and (5) individualized approaches. Based on our findings, we report preliminary and generalizable best-practice recommendations to support autistic children in a research setting and promote positive experiences.

sheet.es: Si su hijo autista va a participar en un estudio o visitar un laboratorio, prepárelo con antelación, pregunte por el entorno, deje que se familiarice con lo nuevo (por ejemplo, un robot) y adapte todo a su manera de ser. Pida que el equipo investigador sea atento y esté implicado. La evidencia es un estudio de métodos mixtos: se entrevistó a 14 madres y padres de niños autistas y 10 de esos niños visitaron el laboratorio y conocieron un robot humanoide. Sus límites: la muestra es pequeña y las recomendaciones son preliminares, así que no sirven igual para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If your autistic child is going to take part in a study or visit a lab, prepare them ahead of time, ask about the environment, let them get familiar with new things (such as a robot), and adapt everything to who they are. Ask for a supportive, engaged research team. The evidence is a mixed-methods study: 14 parents of autistic children were interviewed, and 10 of those children visited the lab and met a humanoid robot. Its limits: the sample is small and the recommendations are preliminary, so they will not fit every person equally.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn ska delta i en studie eller besöka ett labb: förbered barnet i förväg, fråga om miljön, låt barnet bekanta sig med det nya (till exempel en robot) och anpassa allt efter just ditt barn. Be om ett stödjande och engagerat forskarteam. Underlaget är en studie med blandade metoder: 14 föräldrar till autistiska barn intervjuades och 10 av barnen besökte labbet och träffade en humanoid robot. Begränsningar: urvalet är litet och rekommendationerna är preliminära, så de passar inte alla lika bra.

title: 'It depends entirely on the nature of those supports': Community perceptions of the appropriateness of early support services for autistic children.
authors: Sulek R, Edwards C, Monk R, Patrick L, Pillar S, Whitehouse AJ, Waddington H
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Autistic advocates emphasise the need for neurodiversity-affirming and strengths-based approaches to support services; however, little is known about broader community perspectives regarding the appropriateness of offering early support services to autistic children. This co-designed mixed-methods study employed surveys to gather insights from 253 participants in Australia and New Zealand, including autistic adults, parents, and professionals. Participants shared views on the appropriateness of early support services for autistic children. About half of participants indicated that it was appropriate to provide early support services, while the other half indicated that it depended on the nature of those support services. Reflexive thematic analysis resulted in three overarching themes which explain these views. 'They are children first, after all' emphasises the importance of preserving childhood experiences and involving children in decision-making. 'We shouldn't be aiming to fix the child' underscores the need for support services to align with neurodiversity-affirming approaches. Finally, 'Supports are beneficial' highlights the perceived positive impact that early, individualised support services can provide for autistic children. These findings predominantly signal a shift away from medicalised models towards a neurodiversity-affirming approach across participant groups.Lay abstractWe do not know much about what support services people think are okay for young autistic children. This study was a survey of 253 people. We asked autistic adults, parents, and professionals from Australia and New Zealand whether they thought it was okay to provide support services to autistic children. About half the people who shared their thoughts said it was okay to provide support services to autistic children and the other half said it depended on what the support service was like. They had three main ideas about whether support services were okay or not. The first one is that we should remember that these autistic children are children first, so we need to keep their childhood experiences in mind and let them have a say in decisions. The second is that we should not try to 'fix' the child, but instead, use supports that respect and understand the unique ways the child thinks. The final idea is that early, personalised help is good for autistic children and can make a positive difference in their lives. This study suggests that we should focus on what each child needs, think about how children can join in, and provide help in ways that respect autistic children.

sheet.es: Al elegir apoyos tempranos para un niño autista, conviene preguntar cómo es el apoyo, no solo si existe: que respete su infancia, lo incluya en las decisiones, no busque «arreglarlo» y se ajuste a lo que necesita. La evidencia es un estudio con encuestas a 253 personas de Australia y Nueva Zelanda: adultos autistas, madres, padres y profesionales. Cerca de la mitad veía apropiado ofrecer apoyos tempranos y la otra mitad decía que dependía de cómo fueran. Sus límites: recoge opiniones, no mide si un apoyo concreto funciona, y no representa a todas las familias ni a todos los niños.
sheet.en: When choosing early support for an autistic child, it helps to ask what the support is like, not only whether it exists: does it protect childhood, include the child in decisions, avoid trying to 'fix' them, and fit what they need? The evidence is a survey study of 253 autistic adults, parents and professionals in Australia and New Zealand. About half thought offering early support was appropriate; the other half said it depended on the nature of the support. Limits: it reports opinions, not whether any particular support works, and it cannot speak for every family or child.
sheet.sv: När du väljer tidigt stöd till ett autistiskt barn hjälper det att fråga hur stödet ser ut, inte bara om det finns: skyddar det barndomen, involverar det barnet i besluten, undviker det att försöka «fixa» barnet och passar det barnets behov? Underlaget är en enkätstudie med 253 autistiska vuxna, föräldrar och yrkesverksamma i Australien och Nya Zeeland. Ungefär hälften tyckte att tidigt stöd var lämpligt, medan andra hälften sa att det berodde på stödets karaktär. Begränsningar: studien visar åsikter, inte om ett visst stöd fungerar, och gäller inte alla familjer eller barn.

title: Secondary effects of dialectical behaviour therapy on social functioning, quality of life, and autism traits in autistic adults with suicidality.
authors: Huntjens A, van den Bosch LW, Sizoo B, Kerkhof A, Smit F, van der Gaag M
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: The effect of psychological treatment on social functioning, quality of life and autism traits in autistic people with suicidal behaviour remains largely unknown. At six Dutch mental health centres, 123 adult outpatients with Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (5th edition) diagnosed autism spectrum condition and suicidal behaviours were randomly assigned to dialectical behaviour therapy ( n = 63) or treatment as usual ( n = 60) to address their suicidal behaviours. This article analysed secondary outcomes on social functioning, quality of life and autism traits. Outcomes were compared at baseline, post-treatment at 6 months, and 12-month follow-up. At post-treatment, both social functioning ( p p = 0.002) were significantly improved in the treatment condition compared to the control condition and remained so at 12-month follow-up ( p = 0.003; p = 0.002). Autism traits did not differ between conditions. Autistic individuals with suicidal behaviours benefit modestly from treatment with dialectical behaviour therapy in social functioning and quality of life.Lay abstractDialectical behaviour therapy is a comprehensive treatment that helps individuals improve distress tolerance, mindfulness, interpersonal effectiveness and emotion regulation. It is commonly used to assist those experiencing self-harm and suicidal thoughts or behaviours. Despite its broad application, our understanding of how dialectical behaviour therapy impacts autistic individuals with suicidal behaviour remains limited. This study compared dialectical behaviour therapy with treatment as usual in 123 autistic adults experiencing suicidal behaviours. Participants were recruited from six mental health centres, with 63 receiving dialectical behaviour therapy and 60 receiving treatment as usual. The study assessed outcomes such as social functioning, quality of life and specific autism traits over 12 months. Findings revealed that dialectical behaviour therapy led to significant improvements in social functioning and quality of life compared to treatment as usual, though there were no effects on autism traits. These improvements suggest that dialectical behaviour therapy holds promise as an effective treatment for autistic individuals grappling with suicidal behaviour. The findings strongly support the broader implementation of dialectical behaviour therapy in mental health centres, especially given the limited treatment options available for autistic individuals with suicidal tendencies.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta tiene conductas suicidas, conviene preguntar a su equipo de salud mental si la terapia dialéctico-conductual (DBT) es una opción. En este ensayo con asignación al azar participaron 123 adultos autistas de seis centros de salud mental de Países Bajos: 63 recibieron DBT y 60 el tratamiento habitual. La DBT mejoró de forma modesta el funcionamiento social y la calidad de vida frente al tratamiento habitual, y la mejora seguía a los 12 meses. Los rasgos autistas no cambiaron, y no tendrían por qué hacerlo. Los resultados son promedios de un grupo, no valen para todas las personas, y la mejora fue modesta. Si tú o alguien cercano está en peligro, busca ayuda profesional (un clínico, tu servicio de salud o un servicio de crisis) y, ante peligro inmediato, llama al número de emergencias de tu país.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult is having suicidal thoughts or behaviours, it is worth asking their mental health team whether dialectical behaviour therapy (DBT) is an option. In this randomised trial, 123 autistic adults from six Dutch mental health centres received either DBT (63 people) or treatment as usual (60 people). DBT led to modest improvements in social functioning and quality of life compared with treatment as usual, and these were still present at 12 months. Autism traits did not change, and they need not. These are group averages from one country, the gains were modest, and results will not apply to everyone. If you or someone close to you is struggling, contact a professional (a clinician, your health service or a crisis service). In immediate danger, call your country's emergency number.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen har självmordstankar eller självmordsbeteenden är det värt att fråga vårdteamet om dialektisk beteendeterapi (DBT) är ett alternativ. I den här randomiserade studien fick 123 autistiska vuxna från sex nederländska psykiatriska mottagningar antingen DBT (63 personer) eller sedvanlig behandling (60 personer). DBT gav måttliga förbättringar av social funktion och livskvalitet jämfört med sedvanlig behandling, och förbättringarna fanns kvar efter 12 månader. Autistiska drag förändrades inte, och det behöver de inte göra. Resultaten är gruppgenomsnitt från ett land, förbättringarna var måttliga och gäller inte alla. Om du eller någon nära dig mår dåligt, kontakta professionell hjälp (en läkare, vården eller en krisjour). Vid akut fara, ring ditt lands nödnummer.

title: Lifetime stressor exposure is related to suicidality in autistic adults: A multinational study.
authors: Moseley RL, Hedley D, Gamble-Turner JM, Uljarević M, Uljarević M, Bury SM, Shields GS, Trollor JN, Stokes MA, Slavich GM
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Despite very high rates of suicidal thoughts and behaviors (STB) in autistic adults, the key psychosocial drivers of this phenomenon remain unknown. To investigate, we examined how lifetime stressor exposure and severity, which have been found to predict STB in non-autistic populations, related to STB in a multinational dataset of 226 autistic adults from the United Kingdom and Australia (67% female; M age = 41.8, SD = 13.6, range = 19-73 years old). Results revealed that autistic men and women differ with respect to the count, severity, and type of stressors they experienced over the life course. Whereas autistic men were exposed to more numerous legal/crime-related stressors, autistic women experienced more stressors related to social relationships and chronic humiliation and typically experienced stressors as more severe. In addition, whereas chronic interpersonal loss was related to STB for men, acute stressors involving physical danger and lower exposure to chronic entrapment were related to STB in autistic women. These findings indicate that certain lifetime stressors may be differentially experienced, and relevant to STB, in autistic men versus women. They also suggest that screening for lifetime stressor exposure may help identify autistic individuals at greatest risk of suicide.Lay abstractWhen we encounter life events that we experience as stressful ("stressors"), it sets off a biological stress response that can impact mental health and contribute to suicidal thoughts and behaviors (STB). Although we know about specific stressors that are associated with STB in the general population, little is known about the kinds of stressors that increase the risk of STB in autistic people and whether these associations differ by gender. To examine this issue, we cataloged the life stressors that autistic men and women experienced over the entire life course and investigated how these stressors were related to STB. Data were derived from a multinational sample of 226 autistic adults from the United Kingdom and Australia who completed the Stress and Adversity Inventory for Adults. We found that autistic men and women differed in terms of both the lifetime stressors they experienced as well as their perceived severity. Whereas men experienced more legal/crime-related stressors, women experienced more stressors related to relationships with other people and more long-lasting stressors associated with humiliation. Autistic women often perceived life stressors as more severe than men, which is important given that it is the perceived severity of stressors that most strongly affects our health. We also found that different stressors may predict STB in autistic men versus women. Whereas loss of loved ones was most strongly associated with STB for men, for women, physically dangerous stressors were most relevant. In addition, women with fewer lifetime stressors involving entrapment had higher lifetime STB. These results suggest that lifetime stressor exposure may be important to assess to understand suicide risk in autistic people. Additional research is needed to confirm these associations and to examine possible mechanisms linking stress and STB.

sheet.es: Si cuida a una persona autista adulta, conviene tener presente que las experiencias estresantes vividas a lo largo de la vida pueden pesar en su bienestar, y que hablar de ellas con calma y sin juzgar puede ayudar. Este estudio transversal con 226 personas autistas adultas del Reino Unido y Australia halló que hombres y mujeres autistas vivieron tipos distintos de estresores, y que distintos estresores se relacionaron con pensamientos y conductas suicidas. Es una asociación: no prueba causas ni vale para todas las personas, y hace falta más investigación. Si le preocupa a alguien, busque ayuda profesional: un clínico, un servicio de salud o un servicio de crisis. En peligro inmediato, llame al número de emergencias de su país.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult, it helps to remember that stressful experiences across a lifetime can weigh on wellbeing, and that talking about them calmly and without judgement may help. This study of 226 autistic adults from the United Kingdom and Australia found that autistic men and women lived through different kinds of stressors, and that different stressors were linked to suicidal thoughts and behaviors. It shows associations only: it does not prove causes, it does not apply to every person, and more research is needed. If you are worried about someone, reach out to professional help: a clinician, a health service or a crisis service. In immediate danger, call the emergency number of your country.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen är det bra att komma ihåg att stressande upplevelser under livet kan väga tungt för måendet, och att det kan hjälpa att prata om dem lugnt och utan att döma. Denna studie av 226 autistiska vuxna från Storbritannien och Australien fann att autistiska män och kvinnor hade varit med om olika typer av stressorer, och att olika stressorer hängde ihop med självmordstankar och självmordsbeteenden. Det är bara samband: studien visar inte orsaker, gäller inte alla, och mer forskning behövs. Om du är orolig för någon, sök professionell hjälp: en läkare, vården eller en krisjour. Vid akut fara, ring ditt lands nödnummer.

title: "I made friends a lot more easily": children and families' experiences of social group programs for children on the autism spectrum.
authors: Hayden-Evans M, Afsharnejad B, Lee EAL, Milbourn B, Picen T, Johnson M, Bölte S, Girdler S
abstract: Background Social Skills Group Programs (SSGP) target the social communication and interaction skills of children on the autism spectrum. This qualitative study explored lived experiences of children and families who participated in a randomised controlled trial (RCT) evaluating the efficacy of KONTAKT™ adapted for younger children (8 to 12 years) in comparison to an active control social art group (ART Legends). Methods Semi-structured interviews were conducted online with parents (n = 37) and children (n = 35) who participated in the RCT, immediately following the interventions. Interview questions were designed to elicit responses relating to program content, structure, and experiences. The data were analysed using a deductive coding framework. Results Findings suggest SSGPs such as KONTAKT™, implementing multiple teaching strategies, and less structured social group activities such as ART Legends can both have a perceived positive influence on outcomes. More children in the KONTAKT™ group reportedly improved their social skills than those in the art group. Overall, participants' experiences were predominantly positive. Both barriers (e.g., session timing, distance from home) and facilitators (e.g., support of family members) to participation were identified; feelings towards individual aspects of the groups were dependent on a range of personal factors (e.g., existing commitments). Conclusion This study describes experiences of organised social group participation from the perspectives of children on the spectrum and their families, supporting the positive influence of such contexts for autistic youth. Suggestions made by participants to improve social groups are presented, contributing to ongoing development of SSGPs for children on the spectrum. Trial registration (1) Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry (ANZCTR): ACTRN12619000994189, registered 12 July 2019, anzctr.org.au; (2) ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04024111 registered 1 December 2019, https://clinicaltrials.gov .

sheet.es: Si piensa en un grupo social para su hijo o hija autista, mire primero lo práctico: el horario, la distancia desde casa y si la familia puede apoyar la asistencia. Pregunte también qué le gustaría a su hijo o hija. La evidencia: entrevistas en línea con padres y madres (n = 37) y niños y niñas de 8 a 12 años (n = 35) que habían participado en un ensayo aleatorizado de dos grupos, uno de habilidades sociales y otro de arte. Las experiencias fueron en general positivas. Límites: son opiniones y percepciones, y a cada persona le gustaron cosas distintas, así que no sirve como regla para todos.
sheet.en: If you are thinking about a social group for your autistic child, start with the practical side: session timing, distance from home, and whether family can support attendance. Ask your child what they would enjoy too. The evidence: online interviews with parents (n = 37) and children aged 8 to 12 (n = 35) who took part in a randomised trial comparing a social skills group with a social art group. Experiences were mostly positive. Limits: these are views and perceptions, and people liked different things, so it is not a rule for every child.
sheet.sv: Om du funderar på en social grupp för ditt autistiska barn, börja med det praktiska: tider, avstånd hemifrån och om familjen kan stötta deltagandet. Fråga också vad barnet själv skulle vilja. Evidensen: onlineintervjuer med föräldrar (n = 37) och barn i åldern 8 till 12 år (n = 35) som deltagit i en randomiserad studie som jämförde en social färdighetsgrupp med en social konstgrupp. Upplevelserna var mestadels positiva. Begränsningar: det är åsikter och uppfattningar, och människor gillade olika saker, så det är ingen regel för alla barn.

title: Therapeutic effects of singing bowls: A systematic review of clinical studies.
authors: Cai Y, Yang G, Liu Y, Zou X, Yin H, Jin X, Liu X, Wang C, Robinson N, Liu J
abstract: Background Singing bowl has traditionally been utilized to promote healing and relaxation. This systematic review aimed to analyze all available clinical evidence, and determine any beneficial or adverse effects of singing bowl in any population. Methods Databases searched included PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, PsyINFO, CINAHL, CNKI, VIP, Wanfang, Sinomed from database inception to July 2024. Clinical studies of singing bowl therapy, regardless of research type, population, and intervention were included. The risk of bias of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was assessed using the Cochrane tool. Data from randomized trials were analyzed and presented as the mean difference with 95 % confidence interval, and the results from two or more separate trials with same study type that evaluated similar populations, interventions, comparisons and outcomes were statistical pooled using meta-analysis by Stata.16 software. Results Nineteen clinical studies originated from eight countries and published between 2008 and 2024 were identified. Half were RCTs (9), the remainder included case series studies (7), randomized crossover studies (2) and non-RCT (1). Evidence showed that singing bowl has been applied to a wide range of conditions, including the elderly, surgery, Parkinson's disease, pain, cancer, neurological function, sleep disorder, depression, anxiety, autism spectrum disorder, as well as physiological and psychological function, and it has mainly focused on outcomes related to mental health. Conclusion Singing bowl may have potential to alleviate anxiety, depression, improve quality of sleep and cognitive function in various patient groups, and change autistic behavior. It also shows potential benefits in physiological improvements like electroencephalography. Protocol registration PROSPERO, CRD42025639808.

sheet.es: Si quieres probar cuencos tibetanos con una persona autista, hazlo como una actividad tranquila y opcional, atenta a su comodidad, y detén la sesión si muestra malestar. Se trata de una revisión sistemática de 19 estudios clínicos de ocho países, en poblaciones muy variadas; solo una parte se centró en el autismo. Sus límites: los estudios eran de tipos distintos, el resumen no detalla resultados concretos para personas autistas y no demuestra que funcione para todas. Los beneficios son solo posibles, no seguros.
sheet.en: If you would like to try singing bowls with an autistic person, offer it as a calm, optional activity, watch their comfort, and stop if they seem distressed. This is a systematic review of 19 clinical studies from eight countries, covering many different groups; only some involved autism. Its limits: the studies were of different types, the abstract gives no specific results for autistic people, and it does not show that singing bowls work for everyone. Benefits are only possible, not certain.
sheet.sv: Om du vill prova klangskålar med en autistisk person, erbjud det som en lugn och frivillig aktivitet, var uppmärksam på personens välbefinnande och avbryt om personen verkar obekväm. Det här är en systematisk översikt av 19 kliniska studier från åtta länder, med många olika grupper; bara en del gällde autism. Begränsningar: studierna var av olika slag, sammanfattningen redovisar inga specifika resultat för autistiska personer och visar inte att klangskålar fungerar för alla. Fördelarna är bara möjliga, inte säkra.

title: Food and Nutrition in Autistic Adults: Knowledge Gaps and Future Perspectives.
authors: Remón S, Ferrer-Mairal A, Sanclemente T
abstract: Proper nutrition is a critical component in supporting the overall health and development of individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) who experience eating difficulties associated with their autistic traits. Evidence regarding the prevalence, origins, and consequences of eating issues related to ASD is largely derived from studies on autistic children, while information pertaining to adults remains scarce. It is therefore essential to critically review existing research focusing on autistic adults to draw robust conclusions and identify clear research gaps. A computer-aided search in PubMed, Science Direct, Scopus, and Web of Science databases spanning the years 2013-2024 using the search terms covering ASD/Autism, Adult, Nutrition/Nutritional Status, and Diet yielded 43 full-text articles. In our literature review, we explored three critical aspects of nutrition in adults with ASD: their food preferences and sensory processing patterns, studies on nutritional status, and whether dietary and nutritional interventions have improved their adherence to healthier diets. Autistic adults appear to select food based on sensory perceptions. This selection pattern can affect their nutritional status, with a tendency toward overweight and nutritional deficiencies. The most promising intervention strategies incorporate sensory adaptation and structured meal planning. Further research should apply rigorous methodologies that account for this population's specific characteristics.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista adulta, empieza por respetar cómo percibe los alimentos: textura, olor y sabor suelen guiar lo que elige. Probad adaptaciones sensoriales y un plan de comidas estructurado, que fueron las estrategias más prometedoras. Es una revisión de 43 artículos publicados entre 2013 y 2024 sobre adultos autistas. Casi toda la evidencia previa viene de niñez y hay pocos estudios en adultos, así que no sirve como regla para cada persona. Si te preocupa su nutrición o su peso, consulta con un profesional sanitario.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult, start by respecting how they experience food: texture, smell and taste often guide what they choose. Try sensory adaptations and a structured meal plan, which were the most promising strategies. This is a review of 43 articles published between 2013 and 2024 about autistic adults. Most earlier evidence comes from children and adult studies are scarce, so it is not a rule for every person. If you worry about their nutrition or weight, talk with a health professional.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen: börja med att respektera hur personen upplever mat. Textur, lukt och smak styr ofta valen. Prova sensoriska anpassningar och en strukturerad måltidsplan, som var de mest lovande strategierna. Detta är en översikt av 43 artiklar publicerade 2013–2024 om autistiska vuxna. Det mesta av tidigare evidens kommer från barn och studier på vuxna är få, så resultaten gäller inte som regel för varje person. Om du oroar dig för kost eller vikt, prata med vårdpersonal.

title: Implementation Insights from the PEACE Pathway Across UK Eating Disorder Services.
authors: Tchanturia K, Chubinidze D, Duffy F, Nimbley E, Li Z, Holliday J
abstract: Background/objectives Autistic individuals with eating disorders (ED) face socio-emotional, sensory, and communication difficulties that influence engagement and treatment outcomes. We examined how the PEACE Pathway-an autism-informed approach to ED treatment-addresses these challenges through tailored adaptations in clinical care. Methods A qualitative multiple case studies design was employed, drawing data from clinical documentation, stakeholder feedback, and service evaluations. Results We identified eight core domains essential for implementation: pathway knowledge, assessment and planning, psychological interventions, sensory management, nutritional care, lived-experience feedback, family/community engagement, and staff training. These domains informed the development of the PEACE Self-Assessment Checklist to support the wider adoption of the pathway. Conclusions The PEACE Pathway offers a structured approach to adapting ED treatment for autistic individuals. The checklist provides practical guidance for implementing autism-friendly adaptions.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista recibe tratamiento por un trastorno de la conducta alimentaria, conviene preguntar al servicio cómo adapta la evaluación, el trabajo con los sentidos, la comida, la comunicación y la implicación de la familia. Este estudio cualitativo analizó casos de servicios del Reino Unido a partir de documentos clínicos, opiniones de las partes implicadas y evaluaciones. Identificó ocho áreas clave, entre ellas el manejo sensorial, el cuidado nutricional y la formación del personal, y de ahí salió una lista de autoevaluación para los servicios. No mide si el tratamiento funciona mejor, y cada persona necesita adaptaciones propias.
sheet.en: If an autistic person is being treated for an eating disorder, it is reasonable to ask the service how it adapts assessment, sensory needs, food, communication and family involvement. This qualitative study looked at cases from UK services, using clinical records, stakeholder feedback and service evaluations. It identified eight key areas, including sensory management, nutritional care and staff training, and from them produced a self-assessment checklist for services. It does not measure whether treatment works better, and each person will need their own adaptations.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person får behandling för en ätstörning är det rimligt att fråga vården hur den anpassar bedömning, sensoriska behov, mat, kommunikation och närståendes delaktighet. Den här kvalitativa studien granskade fall från brittiska verksamheter med hjälp av kliniska dokument, synpunkter från berörda och utvärderingar. Den fann åtta nyckelområden, bland annat sensorisk hantering, näringsvård och personalutbildning, och utifrån dem togs en självskattningslista för verksamheter fram. Studien mäter inte om behandlingen fungerar bättre, och varje person behöver sina egna anpassningar.

title: Examining the Impact of a Brief Compassion Focused Intervention on Everyday Experiences of Compassion in Autistic Adults Through Psychophysiology and Experience Sampling.
authors: Sherwell CS, Varley D, Kinnane C, Turner W, Zimmerman D, Kirby JN
abstract: Autistic adults experience greater rates of anxiety and depression compared to the general population. Compassion-focused therapy interventions, aimed at promoting self-compassion capabilities, have shown efficacy in improving mental health outcomes in autistic and non-autistic samples suffering from self-criticism that contribute to difficulties in emotion regulation. We explored the experiences of autistic adults during a brief one-week online self-compassion exercise to evaluate it's feasibility and acceptability through self-report, experience sampling, and parasympathetic activity measured via HRV. Pre- to post-intervention comparisons showed significant improvement in trait self-compassion and fears of self-compassion, but this did not extend to acute measures of psychological distress (depression, anxiety, and stress) nor difficulties in emotion regulation. HRV measures displayed significant increases during self-compassionate practice, although there were no significant changes in physiological reactivity pre- to post-intervention. Experience sampling measures found that whether participants acted on opportunities to be self-compassionate was predictive of concurrent evaluations of affective system activation, whereby acting self-compassionately was associated with greater reported activation of the soothing affective system. Together, our findings support the use of multimodal approaches to investigating the accessibility and efficacy of compassion-focused approaches to resolving emotional difficulties experienced by autistic adults.

sheet.es: Si eres una persona autista, un ejercicio breve de autocompasión en línea puede ser algo que probar con calma, sin esperar que cambie todo de golpe. Es un estudio de investigación con personas autistas adultas, que hicieron un ejercicio en línea durante una semana. Tras él, mejoraron la autocompasión y los miedos a la autocompasión, pero no la angustia (depresión, ansiedad, estrés) ni las dificultades de regulación emocional. Cuando actuaron con autocompasión, refirieron más sensación de calma. Límites: fue un ejercicio breve, centrado en su viabilidad, y no demuestra que sirva a todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you are an autistic person, a brief online self-compassion exercise may be something to try gently, without expecting it to change everything at once. This was a research study with autistic adults, who did an online exercise for one week. Afterwards, self-compassion improved and fears of self-compassion decreased, but distress (depression, anxiety, stress) and difficulties with emotion regulation did not change. When people acted self-compassionately, they reported a stronger soothing feeling. Limits: the exercise was brief, the study focused on feasibility, and it does not show that it works for everyone.
sheet.sv: Om du är autistisk kan en kort självmedkänsloövning online vara något att prova i lugn takt, utan att förvänta sig att allt förändras på en gång. Det här var en forskningsstudie med autistiska vuxna som gjorde en onlineövning under en vecka. Efteråt hade självmedkänslan förbättrats och rädslan för självmedkänsla minskat, men det syntes ingen förändring i psykisk ansträngning (depression, ångest, stress) eller svårigheter med känsloreglering. När deltagarna handlade självmedkännande uppgav de en starkare känsla av lugn. Begränsningar: övningen var kort, studien handlade om genomförbarhet och visar inte att den fungerar för alla.

title: Outcomes of participating in the Let's Play programme on 0-5-year-old autistic children's engagement and caregivers' stress: study protocol for a parallel randomised controlled trial.
authors: Hinten AE, Schluter PJ, van Deurs J, van Noorden L, McLay L
abstract: Introduction Vast empirical evidence highlights the importance of early identification, diagnosis and support for autistic children. Caregivers of autistic children often experience high levels of psychological distress; hence there is a need for parallel child and caregiver support. Autism New Zealand's Let's Play programme is a caregiver-mediated, community-based programme based on the principles of developmental and relational interventions (henceforth, developmental). Developmental interventions are evidence-based supports designed to enhance children's learning within the context of developmentally appropriate, naturalistic settings (eg, everyday routines, play). We aim to evaluate the effects of the Let's Play programme on autistic children's engagement and caregiver stress. Methods and analysis This study will be a single-blind (rater) randomised controlled trial with two parallel arms: immediate programme access (intervention) versus a waitlist control. Participants will be 64 caregivers of children aged 0-5 years with diagnosed or suspected autism, allowing for 20% attrition, based on power calculations. The Let's Play programme will be delivered over 9 weeks using a combination of small group workshops and in-home coaching. Primary outcome variables include child engagement and caregiver stress. Caregivers will complete measures at three time points (baseline, immediately post-programme and at the 6-month follow-up), and effectiveness will be analysed using generalised estimating equation models and intention-to-treat and per protocol analyses. Ethics and dissemination This trial was approved by Aotearoa New Zealand Ministry of Health's Health and Disability Ethics Committee (2022 FULL 13041). Findings will be communicated nationally and internationally via conferences, journal publications and stakeholder groups (eg, service providers for autistic children). Results will be shared regardless of magnitude or direction of effect. Trial registration number ACTRN12622001139763.

sheet.es: Si cuida a un niño autista de 0 a 5 años, este estudio aún no ofrece resultados: describe cómo se evaluará Let's Play, un programa comunitario en el que las familias aprenden a apoyar la participación de su hijo en la rutina diaria y el juego. Mientras tanto, puede observar qué momentos de juego le interesan a su hijo y seguirlos con calma. Es el protocolo de un ensayo aleatorizado: 64 cuidadores recibirían el programa de inmediato o tras una lista de espera, durante 9 semanas, y se medirán la participación infantil y el estrés de los cuidadores. Al ser un protocolo, no sabemos aún si el programa funciona, y no servirá igual para todas las familias.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic child aged 0-5, this study has no results yet: it describes how Let's Play will be evaluated, a community programme where caregivers learn to support their child's engagement in everyday routines and play. Meanwhile, you can notice which play moments interest your child and follow them calmly. It is a protocol for a randomised trial: 64 caregivers would get the programme straight away or after a waitlist, over 9 weeks, and child engagement and caregiver stress will be measured. As it is only a protocol, we do not yet know whether the programme works, and it may not suit every family.
sheet.sv: Om du vårdar ett autistiskt barn i åldern 0-5 år har den här studien inga resultat än: den beskriver hur Let's Play ska utvärderas, ett lokalt program där vårdnadshavare lär sig stödja barnets delaktighet i vardagsrutiner och lek. Du kan under tiden lägga märke till vilka lekstunder som intresserar ditt barn och följa dem lugnt. Det är ett protokoll för en randomiserad studie: 64 vårdnadshavare får programmet direkt eller efter en väntelista, under 9 veckor, och barnets delaktighet och vårdnadshavarnas stress mäts. Eftersom det bara är ett protokoll vet vi ännu inte om programmet fungerar, och det passar inte nödvändigtvis alla familjer.

title: Parent-mediated interventions versus usual care in children with autism spectrum disorders: A protocol for a systematic review with meta-analysis and Trial Sequential Analysis.
authors: Conrad CE, Ziegler SMT, Bilenberg N, Christiansen J, Fagerlund B, Jakobsen RH, Jeppesen P, Kamp CB, Thomsen PH, Jakobsen JC, Lauritsen MB
abstract: Introduction Autism spectrum disorder encompasses diverse patterns of social communication and repetitive, restricted behaviours. Various interventions have been developed to reduce the negative consequences of this disorder and improve levels of functioning, and recently interest in parent-mediated interventions has increased. Previous reviews and meta-analyses have investigated the effects of the parent-mediated interventions, however; a systematic review with meta-analysis of high quality has not been performed since 2013. This protocol for a systematic review with meta-analysis aims to describe the methods and purpose of synthesising current evidence regarding the effects (both positive and adverse) of parent-mediated interventions in both children with autism and their parents. Methods Electronic searches will be conducted in Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), Medical Literature Analysis and Retrieval System Online (MEDLINE), Excerpta Medica database (EMBASE), Latin American and Caribbean Health Sciences Literature (LILACS), American Psychological Association PsycInfo (PsycInfo) and Science Citation Index Expanded (SCI-EXPANDED). Randomised clinical trials of parent-mediated interventions for children with autism and control groups of usual care, waiting list or no treatment will be included. Two reviewers will independently screen, select and collect data. Methodological quality of included studies will be evaluated using Cochrane methodology. The primary outcome will be autism symptom severity as measured by the Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule. Secondary outcomes will be adaptive functioning, adverse effects, child language, child´s quality of life, parental quality of life and parental stress. Meta-analyses and Trial Sequential Analysis will be performed. Discussion This is the study protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis of parent-mediated interventions versus usual care for children with ASD. Results of the review will inform clinicians and parents about the current evidence of the effects, both positive and negative, of parent-mediated interventions on younger children with autism and their parents, through improved methodology and inclusion of new studies. PROSPERO registration number: 385188.

sheet.es: Si le ofrecen un programa en el que usted aprende estrategias para apoyar a su hijo o hija autista, vale la pena preguntar qué se medirá y si también se tendrá en cuenta su propio bienestar. Este estudio es un protocolo de metaanálisis: describe cómo se revisarán ensayos aleatorizados que comparan estos programas con la atención habitual, lista de espera o ausencia de tratamiento. Todavía no ofrece resultados, así que no indica si estos programas funcionan. Tampoco sirve como regla para todas las familias. Mirará efectos positivos y adversos, en niños autistas y en sus madres y padres.
sheet.en: If you are offered a programme where you learn strategies to support your autistic child, it is worth asking what will be measured and whether your own wellbeing will be considered too. This study is a meta-analysis protocol: it describes how randomised trials will be reviewed that compare these programmes with usual care, a waiting list or no treatment. It has no results yet, so it cannot say whether such programmes work, and it is not a rule for every family. It plans to look at positive and adverse effects, in autistic children and in their parents.
sheet.sv: Om du erbjuds ett program där du lär dig strategier för att stödja ditt autistiska barn är det värt att fråga vad som ska mätas och om även ditt eget välbefinnande beaktas. Studien är ett protokoll för en metaanalys: den beskriver hur randomiserade studier ska granskas som jämför dessa program med vanlig vård, väntelista eller ingen behandling. Den har inga resultat än, så den kan inte säga om programmen fungerar, och den är ingen regel för alla familjer. Den planerar att undersöka både positiva och negativa effekter, hos autistiska barn och deras föräldrar.

title: Dialectical Behaviour Therapy to Treat Emotion Dysregulation in Autistic Adults without Intellectual Disability: A Randomised Controlled Trial.
authors: Bemmouna D, Rabot E, Coutelle R, Lefebvre F, Weibel S, Weiner L
abstract: Introduction Emotion dysregulation is prevalent in autistic adults without intellectual disability, whereby it has been associated with heightened non-suicidal self-injury and suicidal behaviours. Dialectical behaviour therapy (DBT) has shown to be feasible and preliminary findings suggest that it might reduce emotion dysregulation in this population. Yet studies evaluating the efficacy of DBT in this context are lacking. Methods Sixty-three autistic adults presenting with emotional dysregulation as well as self-harm and/or suicidal behaviours were randomised either to the DBT condition (18-week treatment) or to the waiting list condition. Participants completed self-report scales, including emotion dysregulation, alexithymia, depression and quality of life, at 4 time points (pre-, mid-, post-therapy, 6-month follow-up). Results Emotion dysregulation improved in the DBT condition relative to the waiting list condition mid-therapy (β01 = -18.59 [-27.67 to -9.44], Pr [β01 Conclusion DBT was found to be effective in reducing emotional dysregulation in autistic adults presenting with self-harm and/or suicidal behaviour. Additionally, improvements in depression and quality of life were observed post-therapy. Interestingly, the improvements in emotion dysregulation were mediated by a decrease in alexithymia, consistent with research showing that alexithymia is a central mechanism of emotion dysregulation in autistic adults.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta tiene emociones muy intensas y difíciles de regular, o piensa en hacerse daño, vale la pena preguntar a un profesional por la terapia dialéctico-conductual (DBT). Evidencia: ensayo aleatorizado con 63 adultos autistas con emociones desreguladas y autolesiones o conductas suicidas; un grupo hizo 18 semanas de DBT y otro esperó. La DBT redujo la desregulación emocional, y después de la terapia mejoraron la depresión y la calidad de vida. Límites: se usaron cuestionarios de autoinforme y los resultados no valen para todas las personas. Si hay riesgo, busca ayuda profesional: un médico, un servicio de salud o un servicio de crisis. En peligro inmediato, llama al número de emergencias de tu país.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult has very intense emotions that are hard to regulate, or thoughts of self-harm, it is worth asking a professional about dialectical behaviour therapy (DBT). Evidence: a randomised trial with 63 autistic adults with emotion dysregulation and self-harm and/or suicidal behaviours; one group had 18 weeks of DBT and the other waited. DBT reduced emotion dysregulation, and depression and quality of life improved after therapy. Limits: results came from self-report questionnaires and will not fit every person. If there is risk, seek professional help: a clinician, a health service or a crisis service. In immediate danger, call the emergency number of your country.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen har mycket starka känslor som är svåra att reglera, eller tankar på att skada sig själv, kan man fråga en professionell om dialektisk beteendeterapi (DBT). Evidens: en randomiserad studie med 63 autistiska vuxna med känsloreglerande svårigheter och självskador och/eller suicidala beteenden; en grupp fick 18 veckors DBT och den andra väntade. DBT minskade den känslomässiga dysregleringen, och depression och livskvalitet förbättrades efter terapin. Begränsningar: resultaten bygger på självskattningsformulär och gäller inte alla. Vid risk, sök professionell hjälp: en läkare, en vårdinstans eller en krisjour. Vid akut fara, ring ditt lands nödnummer.

title: A Practical Guide for Improving Orthopaedic Care in Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Maloy GC, Kaszuba SV, Stoeckel M, Mariotti EC, Frumberg DB
journal: Journal of the Pediatric Orthopaedic Society of North America
abstract: Given the increasing prevalence of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), medical professionals' understanding of the presentation of ASD is essential to ensuring patients with ASD receive high-quality healthcare. Previous studies have found that individuals with ASD have a lower average bone density and higher fracture risk than those without ASD, increasing the likelihood that these patients will seek orthopaedic care. Early coordination with the patient's family, identification of stressors and coping strategies, and flexibility during the visit are key to promoting a positive medical encounter. Based on a review of the literature, we present a practical guide for orthopaedic providers to better care for pediatric patients with ASD and their families. Key Concepts •Children with ASD have more successful interfaces with pediatric orthopedists when the visits are tailored to meet their unique needs.•A multidisciplinary team, especially with ASD resources, can improve the experience of surgical admissions.•A phone call by a team member prior to an outpatient visit is an efficient way to ensure all of a child's needs will be met.•Children may have nonverbal communication strategies, including challenges in externalizing pain.

sheet.es: Antes de una visita de traumatología, llame o responda a la llamada del equipo para contarles qué le estresa a su hijo o hija, qué le ayuda a calmarse y cómo comunica el dolor, que a veces es de forma no verbal. Pida flexibilidad durante la consulta. Es una revisión de la literatura que propone una guía práctica para profesionales de ortopedia pediátrica. Sus límites: reúne recomendaciones generales, no prueba un método concreto y no sirve igual para todas las personas autistas.
