This was a study of U.S. national hospital data from 2019, comparing autistic and non-autistic adults. Of mental health admissions in autistic adults, 17 % had a readmission within 30 days, with differences between groups. It only shows patterns in records; it does not explain causes or predict what will happen for any one person.
sheet.sv: När en autistisk vuxen skrivs ut efter en inläggning för psykisk ohälsa hjälper det att planera uppföljningen före utskrivningen: vem som ger vård, när och hur, med tydlig och tillgänglig information. Studien använde nationella amerikanska sjukhusdata från 2019 och jämförde autistiska och icke-autistiska vuxna. Av inläggningarna för psykisk ohälsa hos autistiska vuxna ledde 17 % till en återinläggning inom 30 dagar, med skillnader mellan grupper. Den visar bara mönster i register, förklarar inte orsaker och förutsäger inte vad som händer för en enskild person.

title: Acceptance and Commitment Training for Parents of Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
authors: Li SN, Chien WT
abstract: Importance Parents of children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) experience significant stress and caregiving burden and urgently require targeted psychological support and parenting guidance. Integrating acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT) into the World Health Organization's caregiver skills training has demonstrated good feasibility, acceptability, and potential benefits in addressing these parents' unmet psychological and informational needs; however, its effectiveness remains unexplored. Objective To evaluate the effectiveness of an evidence-based ACT-based parenting program on parental stress and that of other health outcomes on parents and their children with ASD immediately and 6 months after intervention. Design, setting, and participants This randomized clinical trial using the intention-to-treat principle was conducted across 7 government-designated rehabilitation institutions in Shenzhen, China, from February 18, 2024, to January 20, 2025. Participants were adult parents serving as the primary caregivers of their children with ASD (aged 3-9 years). Interventions Participants were randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to either an intervention group or a control group using block randomization. Participants in the intervention group received usual care plus an 8-week, group-format ACT-based parenting program, while the control group received usual care only. Main outcomes and measures Parental stress was the primary outcome, assessed by the Chinese version of the Parenting Stress Index-Short Form. Secondary outcomes included parental depressive symptoms, anxiety, psychological flexibility, and parenting competence and children's emotional and behavioral problems. Results Among 154 parents (mean [SD] age, 36.55 [4.92] years; 135 [87.66%] mothers) caring for children with ASD (mean [SD] age, 5.69 [1.75] years; 118 [76.62%] boys), 77 participants were randomized to the ACT-based intervention group and 77 were randomized to the control group. Those in the intervention group reported significantly greater improvements in parental stress (group × time effect, β = -2.04 [95% CI, -3.51 to -0.57]; P = .007), psychological flexibility (β = 1.12 [95% CI, 0.29 to 1.95]; P = .008), and parenting competence (β = 2.45 [95% CI, 0.53 to 4.36]; P = .01) and children's emotional and behavioral problems (β = -1.16 [95% CI, -2.26 to -0.05]; P = .04) during the 6-month follow-up. Significant effects on parental depressive symptoms (β = -1.61 [95% CI, -3.12 to -0.10]; P = .04) and anxiety (β = -1.62 [95% CI, -2.81 to -0.44]; P = .007) were observed in the ACT-based intervention group immediately post intervention. Conclusion and relevance In this randomized clinical trial of an ACT-based parenting program, the intervention was effective in helping parents manage their stress in caregiving and the emotions and behaviors of their children with ASD, underscoring the need for future studies among more diverse populations globally. Trial registration ChiCTR Identifier: 2400080472.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a un niño autista, un programa grupal de apoyo psicológico para madres y padres puede ayudar a manejar el estrés y a sentirte más competente. Pregunta en el centro de terapia o rehabilitación si ofrecen algo similar. Es un ensayo aleatorizado con 154 madres y padres de niños autistas de 3-9 años en Shenzhen, China: quienes hicieron un programa de 8 semanas basado en aceptación y compromiso, además de la atención habitual, informaron mayor mejoría en estrés que quienes solo recibieron la atención habitual. Sus límites: un solo contexto y casi todas las participantes eran madres, así que puede no servir igual a todas las familias.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic child, a group psychological support program for parents may help you manage stress and feel more confident. Ask your therapy or rehabilitation centre whether something similar is offered. This was a randomized trial with 154 parents of autistic children aged 3-9 in Shenzhen, China: those who joined an 8-week acceptance and commitment based program, on top of usual care, reported greater improvement in stress than those receiving usual care alone. Its limits: one setting, and most participants were mothers, so results may not apply equally to every family.
sheet.sv: Om du tar hand om ett autistiskt barn kan ett psykologiskt stödprogram i grupp för föräldrar hjälpa dig att hantera stress och känna dig tryggare. Fråga din habilitering eller ditt terapicenter om något liknande finns. Det var en randomiserad studie med 154 föräldrar till autistiska barn i åldern 3-9 år i Shenzhen, Kina: de som deltog i ett 8 veckor långt program baserat på acceptans och engagemang, utöver vanlig vård, rapporterade större förbättring av stress än de som fick enbart vanlig vård. Begränsningar: en enda miljö och de flesta deltagare var mammor, så resultaten gäller inte nödvändigtvis alla familjer.

title: Dog-assisted therapy on Hong Kong children with autism spectrum disorder: an exploratory randomized controlled trial.
authors: Wong WHS, Chen C, Tso A, So HK, Wong JPY, Tinsley H, Chung CHY, Luk RKW, Ip P
abstract: Dog-assisted therapy (DAT) has become a promising complementary approach, providing social and emotional support for children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Research on the effects of DAT on multiple functions in children with ASD is limited, and the results are inconsistent. Our study aimed to evaluate the effect of DAT with an RCT study on both psychosocial problems and overall well-being in children with ASD in Hong Kong. An exploratory randomized controlled trial was conducted from February 2023 to November 2024, involving 64 children with ASD aged 6 to 15 years. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1 ratio) to DAT group and control group. The DAT group participated in a structured 8-session DAT training program while the control group received a conventional education curriculum. Before and after the intervention, the Paediatric Quality of Life Inventory scale and Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire were used to evaluate children's quality of life and psychosocial problems, respectively. The paired t-test and independent t-test/Mann-Whitney U test were employed to analyze pre-post differences and group differences. In the DAT group, the mean total score of quality of life was significantly improved (pre vs. post: 58.32 vs. 63.71, P = 0.007) and the mean score of total difficulties was significantly reduced (pre vs. post: 15.63 vs. 13.16, P = 0.003). The decreased scores of several subscales of SDQ, such as externalizing behavior, conduct problems, and hyperactivity were also observed (all P 0.05). Conclusion The preliminary finding shows DAT has a comparable effect to the school's educational curriculum in improving the psychosocial health and quality of life of children with ASD. DAT could potentially serve as a beneficial supplemental therapy for children with ASD who receive conventional curriculum training. Trial registration The trial was registered on https://www. Clinicaltrials gov (NCT06609122) on 25 Sep 2024. What is known • Animal-assisted intervention (AAI) has emerged as a promising adjunct, offering social and emotional support for children with ASD. • Evidence on the impact of dog-assisted therapy (DAT) on important outcomes (e.g., emotional and behavioral problems, quality of life) were not fully explored. What is new • DAT demonstrates a similar impact to the school's educational curriculum in enhancing the psychosocial well-being and quality of life of children with ASD. • Most cases in pediatric outbreaks occurred among healthcare workers pointing to the need to protect HCW from infections and a limited role of pediatric patients and caregivers.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija disfruta con los animales, un programa breve con perros puede ser una opción para añadir al apoyo escolar habitual, siempre que la persona autista se sienta cómoda con el perro. Conviene observar su ritmo y respetar si quiere parar. Evidencia: ensayo aleatorizado exploratorio en Hong Kong con 64 niños y niñas autistas de 6 a 15 años; 8 sesiones con perros dieron resultados comparables al currículo escolar habitual en calidad de vida y dificultades psicosociales. Límites: estudio pequeño y preliminar, resultados que no valen para todas las personas, y no demuestra que sea mejor que la escuela.
sheet.en: If your child enjoys animals, a short dog-assisted programme may be an option to add to usual school support, as long as the autistic child feels comfortable with the dog. Watch their pace and respect it if they want to stop. Evidence: an exploratory randomized trial in Hong Kong with 64 autistic children aged 6 to 15; 8 sessions with dogs gave results comparable to the usual school curriculum for quality of life and psychosocial difficulties. Limits: a small, preliminary study, not true for every person, and it does not show dogs work better than school.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn tycker om djur kan ett kort program med hund vara ett komplement till det vanliga skolstödet, så länge det autistiska barnet känner sig tryggt med hunden. Följ barnets tempo och respektera om hen vill avbryta. Evidens: en explorativ randomiserad studie i Hongkong med 64 autistiska barn i åldern 6 till 15 år; 8 tillfällen med hund gav resultat som liknade den vanliga skolundervisningen när det gällde livskvalitet och psykosociala svårigheter. Begränsningar: en liten, preliminär studie som inte gäller alla och som inte visar att hund är bättre än skolan.

title: Knowledge, perceptions, and use of psychedelics for mental health among autistic adults: An online survey.
authors: Afsharnia S, Liang V, Lunsky Y, Orsini AP, Tint A, Lin HY
abstract: Psychedelics such as psilocybin, LSD, and MDMA have shown promise in treating mental health conditions (e.g., depression, post-traumatic stress disorder) among neurotypical individuals, i.e., typically developing individuals without a diagnosed neurodevelopmental condition. However, their therapeutic potential for treating co-occurring mental-health conditions in autistic individuals remains under-explored. Autistic individuals often face co-occurring mental health challenges but are frequently excluded from clinical trials, creating a gap in effective treatments. This study aimed to explore knowledge, perceptions, and experiences of autistic adults regarding psychedelics. In this survey, "psychedelics" included classical psychedelics such as psilocybin and LSD, as well as MDMA. A cross-sectional online survey was conducted with English-speaking autistic adults. We assessed participants' knowledge of psychedelics, willingness to use them for mental health treatment, and any past psychedelic experiences. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and chi-square tests to assess group differences. A total of 424 participants began the survey, with 261 completing it. Nearly half resided in Canada. Participants generally viewed psychedelics positively, with 77.8% expressing a willingness to try them, and 69.7% reported past use-most commonly psilocybin mushrooms. Higher doses and highly meaningful experiences correlated with longer-lasting mental health improvements. Barriers included legal concerns, health risks, and logistical challenges. Participants with prior experience reported greater perceived knowledge and lower perceived risks. Autistic adults in this self-selecting sample demonstrated strong interest in psychedelics as potential treatments for mental health, despite significant barriers to access and research participation. These results highlight the importance of considering education, policy reform, and inclusive research practices to ensure that autistic people have opportunities to explore psychedelic therapies. These findings should be interpreted cautiously, as the sample may not be representative of the broader autistic population. Future trials should optimize dosing and explore long-term benefits of psychedelics in this population.

sheet.es: Si te planteas esta cuestión, habla con un profesional sanitario de confianza antes de decidir nada; las decisiones médicas le corresponden a él. Este estudio no indica qué hacer. Fue una encuesta en línea con adultos autistas que hablan inglés: 261 la completaron. 77.8% dijo estar dispuesto a probar psicodélicos y 69.7% informó de uso previo. Señalaron barreras legales, riesgos para la salud y dificultades prácticas. Es una encuesta, no un ensayo: solo recoge opiniones y experiencias propias. La muestra se autoseleccionó y puede no representar a todas las personas autistas, así que no sirve como regla general.
sheet.en: If this topic comes up, talk with a trusted health professional before deciding anything; medical decisions belong to a clinician. This study does not tell anyone what to do. It was an online survey of English-speaking autistic adults, and 261 completed it. 77.8% said they were willing to try psychedelics and 69.7% reported past use. People named legal worries, health risks and practical hurdles as barriers. It was a survey, not a trial, so it only captures opinions and self-reported experiences. The sample chose to take part and may not represent all autistic people, so it is not a rule for any one person.
sheet.sv: Om ämnet kommer upp, prata med en betrodd vårdgivare innan något beslutas; medicinska beslut hör till en läkare. Studien säger inte vad någon bör göra. Det var en webbenkät med engelskspråkiga autistiska vuxna, och 261 fullföljde den. 77.8% sa sig vara villiga att prova psykedeliska medel och 69.7% rapporterade tidigare användning. Hinder var juridisk oro, hälsorisker och praktiska svårigheter. Det var en enkät, inte en prövning, så den visar bara åsikter och egna erfarenheter. Deltagarna valde själva att delta och kan skilja sig från autistiska personer i allmänhet, så resultaten är ingen regel för den enskilda personen.

title: Emotion regulation in autistic adolescents: a mixed methods systematic review.
authors: Micheel J, Zapf H, Hohmann S, Bindt C, Boettcher J
abstract: Background Emotion regulation (ER) difficulties are common in autistic individuals and may contribute to co-occurring psychopathology during adolescence. However, age-group heterogeneity in existing research limits understanding of ER processes in autistic adolescents. Therefore, this mixed methods systematic review synthesizes current knowledge on ER in autistic adolescents aged 10-24 years. Methods We systematically searched MEDLINE, PsycINFO, Web of Science, and Scopus for empirical studies on ER in autistic adolescents. 32 studies (including two qualitative) met inclusion criteria and were synthesized using a convergent integrated approach. Results Autistic adolescents consistently exhibited more ER difficulties than non-autistic peers, which were associated with internalizing and externalizing symptoms. Greater autism symptom severity, lower theory of mind, and social challenges were frequently linked to lower ER, while no consistent associations with age, gender, or IQ were found. Few studies examined physiological or neurobiological factors, but evidence suggested associations between ER difficulties, lower heart rate variability, and atypical neural responses. Cognitive-behavioral and mindfulness-based interventions generally led to improvements in ER, though results varied and discrepancies between self- and proxy-reports were common. Conclusion ER challenges are pronounced in autistic adolescents and are closely associated with mental health symptoms. While interventions show promise, future research should address measurement heterogeneity, examine neurobiological underpinnings, and include more longitudinal and ecologically valid designs. Trial registration CRD42024529184 (registered April 06, 2024).

sheet.es: Si cuidas de un adolescente autista, conviene prestar atención a cómo gestiona las emociones intensas y preguntarle a él directamente cómo las vive, porque lo que cuenta y lo que observamos pueden no coincidir. Es una revisión sistemática de 32 estudios (dos cualitativos) con adolescentes autistas de 10-24 años. Encontró más dificultades de regulación emocional que en pares no autistas, ligadas a síntomas de salud mental. Las intervenciones cognitivo-conductuales y de atención plena suelen ayudar, aunque los resultados varían. Límites: los estudios miden de formas distintas y pocos son a largo plazo, así que no sirve como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic teenager, it helps to notice how they handle intense emotions and to ask them directly how they experience them, because what they report and what we observe may differ. This is a systematic review of 32 studies (two qualitative) with autistic adolescents aged 10-24. It found more emotion regulation difficulties than in non-autistic peers, linked to mental health symptoms. Cognitive-behavioral and mindfulness-based approaches generally helped, though results varied. Limits: studies measured things in different ways and few followed people over time, so it is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk tonåring kan det hjälpa att lägga märke till hur hen hanterar starka känslor och fråga hen direkt hur det upplevs, eftersom det hen berättar och det vi ser kan skilja sig åt. Det här är en systematisk översikt av 32 studier (två kvalitativa) med autistiska ungdomar i åldern 10-24. Den fann fler svårigheter med känsloreglering än hos icke-autistiska jämnåriga, kopplade till psykisk ohälsa. Kognitiv beteendeterapi och mindfulnessbaserade metoder hjälpte oftast, men resultaten varierade. Begränsningar: studierna mätte på olika sätt och få följde personer över tid, så det är ingen regel för varje person.

title: 'I fit the category of the box, it just doesn't describe me well.' Exploring the perspectives of autistic women and gender-diverse individuals on self-report autism measures.
authors: Uglik-Marucha N, Show S, Vitoratou S, Happé F, Belcher H
abstract: Psychological assessments play a significant role in both clinical decision-making and the interpretation of research findings, with the quality of these inferences depending on the validity of the measures used. Recent evidence suggests there are gender differences in the presentation of autism, raising concerns about the validity of existing autism tools to measure autistic traits in women and the subsequent implications for clinical inferences and research. This study explored the perspectives of autistic women on the relevance of existing autism questionnaires to their lived experience, alongside additional input from gender-diverse individuals assigned female at birth (AFAB). Through interviews, focus groups, and online surveys, 22 autistic women and AFAB gender-diverse individuals shared their experiences using and perspectives on the Autism Spectrum Quotient-10, 14-item Ritvo Autism & Asperger Diagnostic Scale, and Broad Autism Phenotype Questionnaire. The interview data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis, identifying two overarching themes: (1) questionnaires measure only one way to be autistic, and not in an autism-friendly manner, and (2) enhancing questionnaires' relevance for autistic women and individuals socialised as female: key missing experiences to include. The findings suggest that some of the most frequently used autism measures may not fully capture the experiences of autistic women and AFAB gender diverse individuals. Significant gaps were identified, indicating that important aspects of the participants' lived experiences were missing. Furthermore, concerns were raised about the questionnaires' lack of relevance to the autistic population as a whole. The findings underscore the non-satisfactory content validity of these tools for measuring autism in autistic women and AFAB gender-diverse individuals. This highlights the need for their refinement to better reflect contemporary understandings of different presentations of autistic traits, particularly the impact of gendered experiences, in a way that avoids the introduction of possible new biases and remains relevant and accessible to autistic individuals.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista, sobre todo una mujer o una persona de género diverso asignada mujer al nacer, siente que un cuestionario de autismo no la describe, conviene tomarlo en serio: puede ser un fallo de la herramienta, no de la persona. Antes de una evaluación, se puede preguntar a la clínica cómo se interpretan los resultados y aportar ejemplos propios. El estudio contó con entrevistas, grupos focales y encuestas en línea con 22 mujeres autistas y personas de género diverso asignadas mujer al nacer, que opinaron sobre tres cuestionarios. Es un grupo pequeño y no representa a todas las personas, ni prueba cómo funcionan estas herramientas en la práctica clínica.
sheet.en: If an autistic person, especially a woman or gender-diverse person assigned female at birth, feels an autism questionnaire does not describe them, take that seriously: the tool may be the problem, not the person. Before an assessment, you can ask the clinic how results are interpreted and bring your own examples. The study used interviews, focus groups and online surveys with 22 autistic women and gender-diverse people assigned female at birth, who gave their views on three questionnaires. It is a small group, does not represent everyone, and cannot show how these tools work in everyday clinical practice.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person, särskilt en kvinna eller könsmångfaldig person tilldelad kvinnligt kön vid födseln, upplever att ett autismformulär inte beskriver hen, ta det på allvar: det kan vara verktyget som brister, inte personen. Inför en utredning kan du fråga kliniken hur resultaten tolkas och ta med egna exempel. Studien använde intervjuer, fokusgrupper och webbenkäter med 22 autistiska kvinnor och könsmångfaldiga personer tilldelade kvinnligt kön vid födseln, som delade sina synpunkter på tre formulär. Gruppen är liten, representerar inte alla och visar inte hur verktygen fungerar i klinisk praktik.

title: Are we getting better at identifying and diagnosing neurodivergent girls and women? Insights into sex ratios and age of diagnosis from clinical population data in Scotland.
authors: Maciver D, Singh Roy A, Johnston L, Boilson M, Curnow E, Johnstone-Cooke V, Rutherford M
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: This study examined differences in referral and diagnosis based on sex recorded at birth (hereafter, 'sex'), using case notes from 408 individuals diagnosed by 30 multidisciplinary teams across Scotland. Analyses focused on male-to-female ratios and median ages at referral and diagnosis across attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, autism and intellectual disability. The lifespan male-to-female ratio across all diagnoses was 1.31, varying by category and age. In autism, the male-to-female ratio was 2.21 for children under 10 years, but there were more females in adolescence (male-to-female ratio = 0.79) and adulthood (male-to-female ratio = 0.94). Across the lifespan, combining all diagnoses, females were referred later (median ages: 14.4 vs 19.7 years; p < 0.001) and diagnosed later (median ages: 15.2 vs 20.2 years; p < 0.001), indicating a 5-year delay. Among autistic children and adolescents, females were referred later (median age: 7.5 vs 10.5 years; p = 0.002) and diagnosed later (median age: 9.3 vs 11.9 years; p = 0.003). However, no significant differences were found in age of referral or diagnosis for autistic adults. Overall, the results indicate increasing balance in sex ratios with age, greater asymmetry in younger age groups, and consistent delays in referral and diagnosis ages for females.Lay abstractThis article looks at how males and females are diagnosed with neurodevelopmental differences including autism, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and intellectual disabilities. It studies the case notes of 408 people (adults and children) assessed by 30 different teams during their diagnosis process. The results show overall that more males were diagnosed with neurodevelopmental differences and that males are diagnosed at younger ages compared to females. The increased diagnosis of males compared to females is most common in younger ages, but and as people get older, the number of males and females diagnosed becomes more equal, showing that more women are coming forward for and being diagnosed, for example with autism and ADHD. This research shows that although there are increasing amounts of females diagnosed, that girls and women are still missed when they are young, with more boys gaining a diagnosis as children. It seems there is a pattern of females being diagnosed at later ages (meaning less access to support and self-understanding). The study calls for better diagnostic practices and more research to address these gender differences.

sheet.es: Si cuidas de una niña o adolescente y sospechas que es autista, puedes anotar con calma lo que observas y pedir la valoración sin esperar a que «sea más evidente». Este estudio revisó las historias clínicas de 408 personas diagnosticadas por 30 equipos multidisciplinares de Escocia. Entre niñas y adolescentes autistas, la mediana de edad al diagnóstico fue 9.3 años frente a 11.9 en chicos, es decir, más tarde. En adultos autistas no hubo diferencias significativas. Como límites: son datos clínicos de un solo país, muestran patrones de grupo y no explican las causas, ni sirven como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If you care for a girl or teenager you think may be autistic, you can calmly note what you observe and ask for an assessment without waiting for things to become "more obvious". This study reviewed case notes of 408 people diagnosed by 30 multidisciplinary teams across Scotland. Among autistic girls and adolescents, median age at diagnosis was 9.3 years, versus 11.9 for boys, so later. For autistic adults, no significant differences were found. Limits: the data are clinical records from one country, show group patterns, do not explain the causes, and are not a rule for any one person.
sheet.sv: Om du stödjer en flicka eller tonåring som du tror kan vara autistisk kan du lugnt anteckna det du ser och be om en utredning, utan att vänta tills det blir "tydligare". Studien gick igenom journaler för 408 personer som diagnosticerats av 30 multidisciplinära team i Skottland. Bland autistiska flickor och tonåringar var mediandiagnosåldern 9.3 år, jämfört med 11.9 för pojkar, alltså senare. För autistiska vuxna fanns inga signifikanta skillnader. Begränsningar: det är kliniska data från ett land, de visar gruppmönster, förklarar inte orsakerna och är ingen regel för den enskilda personen.

title: Understanding autistic identity contingencies: The chain mediation effect of autism acceptance and loneliness in ableist microaggressions and social camouflage.
authors: Guan S, Takahashi F, Wada M, Takashina HN, Ueda M, Kawashima M, Kawaguchi Y, Kato T, Ogawa S, Tsuchiya K, Oshima F
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Ableist microaggressions-subtle forms of disability-based discrimination-constitute a key minority stressor. Amplified by autistic identity contingencies that shape how autistic identity is judged and treated in social contexts, these factors drive social camouflage in autistic adults, compelling them to conceal autistic characteristics for adapting to non-autistic groups, often resulting in negative mental health outcomes. This study proposes a novel autistic identity contingencies model to explore how autism acceptance and loneliness mediate the relationship between ableist microaggressions and social camouflage. An online survey of 330 autistic adults was conducted, followed by hierarchical multiple regression and chain mediation analyses. Results revealed that, ableist microaggressions positively predicted three social camouflage phenotypes: compensation, masking, and assimilation, with loneliness also positively predicting assimilation. Furthermore, after controlling for personal attributes, general stress and mental health conditions, lower external autism acceptance and higher loneliness mediated the positive relationship between ableist microaggressions and assimilation, whereas internal autism acceptance showed no significant effect. Assimilation is uniquely shaped by social autistic identity threats and loneliness, distinguishing it from compensation and masking. These findings highlight social camouflage as responses to minority stressors driven by social autistic identity contingencies, rooted in stigmatised behaviours rather than in stigmatised personal autistic identity.Lay AbstractSociety's perceptions of autism, reflected in subtle discrimination against autistic people, cause autistic adults to hide their true selves. They may hide their autistic traits to fit in with others, especially in groups that do not understand autism. Although this can help autistic people be accepted, it often leads to exhaustion and problems with mental health. However, the invisible ways in which autistic adults are judged and treated in daily social activities and how this impacts their strategies for camouflaging their autistic traits is poorly understood. This study examined the effects of feeling accepted as an autistic person, either by oneself or by others, and experiencing loneliness on how autistic adults camouflage being autistic when facing subtle discrimination related to their disability status. We surveyed 330 autistic adults using online questionnaires. After accounting for personal differences, subtle discrimination was positively associated with three camouflaging strategies: compensating for social challenges, covering up differences, and blending in with others. Feeling lonely was also positively associated with blending in with others. Additionally, after accounting for personal differences, stress levels, and mental health, feeling accepted by others as an autistic person and feeling lonely affected how subtle discrimination led to blending in with others. However, self-acceptance of being autistic was not associated with this relationship.This suggests that treatment by others shapes autistic adults' need to hide their identity more than their self-acceptance of being autistic. Therefore, addressing how autistic adults are judged and treated in daily social activities is more critical than focusing on personal change.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista a tu cargo oculta rasgos autistas, mira primero cómo la tratan en su entorno, antes de pensar en cambiarla a ella. Puedes ofrecer espacios donde no tenga que disimular, escuchar sus experiencias de trato injusto y reducir la soledad. La evidencia es una encuesta en línea con 330 adultos autistas: más microagresiones capacitistas se asociaron con más camuflaje social, y la soledad y la menor aceptación por parte de otros ayudaron a explicar el "asimilarse". Límites: es una encuesta en un momento concreto, así que no prueba causas, y no describe a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person in your care hides autistic traits, look first at how others treat them, rather than at changing them. You can offer spaces where they need not mask, listen to their experiences of unfair treatment, and help reduce loneliness. The evidence is an online survey of 330 autistic adults: more ableist microaggressions went with more social camouflage, and loneliness and lower acceptance by others helped explain blending in. Limits: it is a survey at one point in time, so it cannot prove cause, and it does not describe every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person du stöttar döljer autistiska drag, titta först på hur omgivningen bemöter hen, snarare än på att förändra hen. Du kan erbjuda miljöer där hen inte behöver maskera, lyssna på upplevelser av orättvist bemötande och hjälpa till att minska ensamhet. Underlaget är en webbenkät med 330 autistiska vuxna: fler förminskande kommentarer om funktionsnedsättning hängde ihop med mer social kamouflering, och ensamhet och lägre acceptans från andra bidrog till att förklara anpassning. Begränsningar: det är en enkät vid ett tillfälle, så den kan inte bevisa orsak, och den beskriver inte alla autistiska personer.

title: Exploring the autism and functional neurological disorder association: Considerations from biopsychosocial, neuropsychological and computational models.
authors: Cole RH, Smythe L, Edwards MJ, Happé F, Nicholson TR
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Evidence is accumulating regarding an association between autism and functional neurological disorder, a common cause for a wide range of neurological symptoms affecting motor, sensory and cognitive systems. Symptoms can include paralysis, tremors, sensory disturbance, vision loss and dizziness. Functional neurological disorder exists at the complex intersection of physical and mental health, neurology and psychiatry, and body and mind. Despite a recent resurgence in clinical and scientific interest, functional neurological disorder has lagged behind other causes of neurological symptoms in research, service development and acceptance. The nature of the association between autism and functional neurological disorder remains uncertain, but several plausible mechanisms can be identified from overlapping areas of research, highlighting endogenous factors such as atypical interoception, motor function, emotional processing and sensorimotor integration, alongside exogenous influences including adversity, healthcare inequality and stigma. This review first provides an overview of functional neurological disorder through various explanatory frameworks before applying biopsychosocial, neuropsychological and computational perspectives to conceptualise its intersection with autism. It then considers how this association might be understood and explores how services could be adapted to better recognise and support autistic individuals with functional neurological disorder across the diagnostic and treatment pathway.Lay AbstractFunctional neurological disorder causes real and often disabling symptoms, such as seizures, paralysis, tremors or sensory changes, even though standard medical tests do not show physical damage to the nervous system. Research suggests that autistic people are more likely to experience functional neurological disorder than their non-autistic peers, but the reasons for this are not yet understood. This article explores why autism and functional neurological disorder might occur together. It draws on research into how the brain processes body signals (like pain or movement), handles emotions and responds to uncertainty. It also looks at life experiences that affect health, including trauma, barriers to healthcare and stigma. This article shows that both internal factors (such as differences in movement, emotional awareness and sensory processing) and external factors (such as stress, inequality and misdiagnosis) may increase the chances of functional neurological disorder in some autistic individuals. Several models are introduced to help explain how these influences might interact. Finally, this article outlines how healthcare services could better support autistic people with functional neurological disorder. It encourages functional neurological disorder services to adapt communication styles, provide appropriate adjustments and include autistic voices in research and treatment planning to improve care and outcomes.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista tiene síntomas como temblores, parálisis, mareos o cambios sensoriales, conviene tomarlos en serio y consultar a un profesional de la salud, pidiendo adaptaciones: comunicación clara, más tiempo y apoyo sensorial. Es una revisión de la literatura que reúne investigación sobre el trastorno neurológico funcional y el autismo. Sugiere que factores internos (como diferencias sensoriales y de movimiento) y externos (estrés, desigualdad en la atención, estigma) podrían influir. Sus límites: la relación aún no se comprende, no prueba causas y no vale para todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person has symptoms such as tremors, paralysis, dizziness or sensory changes, take them seriously and see a health professional, asking for adjustments: clear communication, more time and sensory support. This is a review that brings together research on functional neurological disorder and autism. It suggests that internal factors (such as sensory and movement differences) and external ones (stress, healthcare inequality, stigma) may play a part. Its limits: the link is still not understood, it does not prove causes, and it does not apply to every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person har symtom som skakningar, förlamning, yrsel eller sensoriska förändringar bör de tas på allvar och tas upp med vården, med önskemål om anpassningar: tydlig kommunikation, mer tid och sensoriskt stöd. Det här är en översikt som samlar forskning om funktionell neurologisk störning och autism. Den antyder att inre faktorer (som sensoriska skillnader och skillnader i motorik) och yttre faktorer (stress, ojämlik vård, stigma) kan spela in. Begränsningar: sambandet är ännu inte förstått, översikten visar inte orsaker och gäller inte alla autistiska personer.

title: Workplace Accommodations and Employment Outcomes Among Employees With Autism: A Systematic Review.
authors: Heinze C
abstract: Individuals with autism often face challenges in achieving and maintaining meaningful employment, but workplace accommodations can bridge these gaps by enabling inclusion, satisfaction, and productivity. The goal of this review was to systematically evaluate and synthesize the existing evidence base on workplace accommodations for adults with autism. After conducting a systematic search of numerous databases, ten empirical studies published between 2010 and 2025, including randomized controlled trials, cohort studies, surveys, and qualitative studies, were included. The quality of studies was assessed using the Critical Appraisal Skills Programme (CASP), the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI), and Risk-of-Bias (RoB) instruments, with the majority of studies being assessed as moderate-to-high quality but having small sample sizes and relying on self-report. Accommodation reports fall into four groups: assistive technology; organizational, sensory, and environmental adaptations; supervisory and relational support; and skills and psychosocial support. In general, the evidence indicated that accommodations were linked to better job acquisition, stability, satisfaction, and productivity, albeit with variability in effectiveness based on relational quality, disclosure practice, and organizational culture. Consistent results highlighted the value of individually tailored support and respectful supervisory relationships, while variations indicated lingering barriers to stigma, ignorance, and uneven policy implementation. However, the heterogeneity of methods and the exclusion of broader autism groups limit the generalizability of findings in these studies. Longitudinal and intervention studies, participatory approaches to design, and representation of underrepresented groups are essential priorities for future research to further develop evidence-based practice and guide employer training and policy.

sheet.es: Si apoyas a un adulto autista que trabaja o busca empleo, puede ayudar hablar juntos sobre qué ajustes le servirían: tecnología de apoyo, cambios sensoriales o del entorno (luz, ruido, espacio tranquilo), instrucciones claras de la supervisión y apoyo en habilidades o bienestar. Lo que más parece importar es que el apoyo se adapte a la persona y que la relación con quien supervisa sea respetuosa. La decisión de revelar el diagnóstico es suya. Esta revisión sistemática reunió diez estudios (2010-2025) con adultos autistas y encontró vínculos entre ajustes y mejor acceso, estabilidad, satisfacción y productividad. Sus límites: estudios pequeños, basados en autoinforme y poco representativos de todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult who works or is job-seeking, it may help to talk together about which accommodations would suit them: assistive technology, sensory or environmental changes (lighting, noise, a quiet space), clear communication from supervisors, and support with skills or wellbeing. What seems to matter most is support tailored to the person and a respectful relationship with their manager. Whether to disclose is their choice. This systematic review pooled ten studies (2010-2025) with autistic adults and found accommodations linked to better hiring, job stability, satisfaction and productivity. Limits: the studies were small, relied on self-report and did not represent all autistic people.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen som arbetar eller söker jobb kan det hjälpa att tillsammans prata om vilka anpassningar som skulle passa: hjälpmedel och teknik, sensoriska eller miljömässiga ändringar (ljus, ljud, en lugn plats), tydlig kommunikation från chefen och stöd med färdigheter eller välmående. Det som verkar betyda mest är att stödet är individuellt och att relationen till chefen är respektfull. Om man berättar om sin diagnos är personens eget val. Denna systematiska översikt samlade tio studier (2010-2025) med autistiska vuxna och fann samband mellan anpassningar och bättre anställning, stabilitet, trivsel och produktivitet. Begränsningar: små studier, självrapportering och bristande representation av alla autistiska personer.

title: An integrative approach between neurodiversity perspectives and quality of life models for autistic people across the spectrum of support needs.
authors: Liñares-de-Marcos J, Palomero-Sierra B, Sánchez-Gómez V, Fernández-Álvarez CJ, Canal-Bedia R
abstract: Introduction Autism is increasingly understood not through deficit-based frameworks but through approaches that emphasize rights, inclusion, and well-being for autistic people across the spectrum of support needs, including non-speaking individuals, those with intellectual disability, and those experiencing mental health challenges. Two perspectives have been central to this shift: Quality of Life (QoL) models, rooted in applied disability research, and the neurodiversity paradigm, arising from autistic self-advocacy and social justice movements. Aim This mini review examines the convergences and tensions between these perspectives, generating a set of integrative principles to guide support providers, researchers, and policymakers. Evidence is synthesized across three thematic perspectives: socio-political and paradigmatic debates, particularly language, identity, and representation; applied and clinical practice, including the aims, role, and risks of supports and interventions; and research, with attention to participatory approaches, lived-experience priorities, and the representation of autistic people with extensive support needs. Discussion Six principles emerge: (i) well-being depends on both self-acceptance and the quality of supports; (ii) language should balance contextual function with individual preference; (iii) identity has transformative value, requiring diagnostic practices that are inclusive, participatory, and non-deficit oriented; (iv) supports are essential mechanisms for participation, not threats to identity; (v) interventions should promote autonomy, belonging, and growth without enforcing normalization; and (vi) research must ensure autistic participation across all stages, with accessible processes and priorities aligned with autistic preferences. Together, these principles offer a framework for integrating QoL and neurodiversity approaches in ways that advance rights, inclusion, and well-being.

sheet.es: Mañana, al pensar en los apoyos, plantéate dos preguntas: ¿la persona autista se siente aceptada tal como es? ¿Los apoyos le ayudan a participar, a tener autonomía y a sentirse parte, sin obligarla a parecer no autista? Pregúntale, o observa sus preferencias, también si no habla. Es una revisión breve que reúne investigación y propone seis principios; no hay participantes propios. Son principios generales, no una receta, y no prueban qué apoyo funciona mejor para una persona concreta.
sheet.en: Tomorrow, when you think about supports, ask two questions: does the autistic person feel accepted as they are? Do the supports help them take part, have autonomy and belong, without pushing them to seem non-autistic? Ask them, or watch for their preferences, including when they do not speak. This is a mini review that brings together existing research and proposes six principles; it has no participants of its own. The principles are general guidance, not a recipe, and they do not show which support works best for one particular person.
sheet.sv: I morgon, när du tänker på stöd, ställ två frågor: känner sig den autistiska personen accepterad som hon eller han är? Hjälper stödet personen att delta, ha självbestämmande och höra till, utan att pressa fram att verka icke-autistisk? Fråga personen, eller notera preferenser, även om hen inte talar. Det här är en kort översikt som sammanställer befintlig forskning och föreslår sex principer; den har inga egna deltagare. Principerna är allmänna riktlinjer, inget recept, och visar inte vilket stöd som fungerar bäst för en enskild person.

title: Insomnia severity and its association with gaming behavior and perceived health in autistic adults.
authors: Bouder S, K McNulty L, Lee D
abstract: BACKGROUND: Insomnia is a prevalent and growing health concern among autistic adults, profoundly impacting their well-being. Empirical studies suggest that autistic adults tend to spend extensive time playing online or video games, which may contribute to sleep disturbances and low health perceptions in this population. This study aimed to explore the associations between insomnia, gaming behavior, and perceived physical and mental health among autistic adults, including those with co-occurring mild intellectual disabilities (ID). METHODS: A total of 117 autistic adults (Mage33.7 ± 9.2; 63.2% female) participated in this cross-sectional study. Standardized self-report instruments were utilized to assess demographics, insomnia severity, gaming behavior, and perceived physical and mental health. Descriptive statistics, independent t-tests, Spearman’s rank correlations, and stepwise multiple regression analyses were performed to answer the research questions. RESULTS: Of the 117 autistic adult participants, 32.5% reported moderate-to-severe insomnia, and 14.5% were identified as potentially meeting the criteria for gaming disorder. Significantly higher gaming time was reported in autistic adults with co-occurring mild ID (M = 672.6 ± 941.6 min/week) compared to those without mild ID (M = 334.8 ± 354.3 min/week, t(115) = 2.432, p < .001), and in males (M = 615.9 ± 830.3 min/week) compared to females (M = 404.3 ± 592.1 min/week, t(115) = 1.469, p = .038). Perceived mental health was negatively correlated with both gaming disorder risk (ρ = -0.221, p < .05) and insomnia severity (ρ = -0.341, p < .01), indicating modest yet noteworthy associations. Perceived mental health was the strongest predictor of insomnia severity (β = -0.273, t(113) = -3.186, p = .002.), while a more recent autism diagnosis and gaming disorder risk were also significant predictors in the regression model, which explained 22.2% of the variance in insomnia scores (F(3, 113) = 10.76, p < .001). CONCLUSIONS: The findings of this study indicate that insomnia may co-occur with lower perceived mental health and problematic gaming behaviors among autistic adults, and these patterns appear pronounced in autistic males with co-occurring mild ID.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista duerme mal, conviene mirar con ella su sueño, su estado de ánimo y cuánto y cómo juega, sin culparla. Hablar de ello con calma y con un profesional puede ayudar. El estudio fue transversal, con 117 personas autistas adultas que respondieron cuestionarios. El 32.5% refirió insomnio de moderado a grave. Peor salud mental percibida se asoció con más insomnio y con más riesgo de uso problemático del juego. Sus límites: solo muestra asociaciones en un momento, no demuestra qué causa qué, y no vale para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person is sleeping badly, it may help to look together, without blame, at their sleep, their mood and how much and how they game. Talking about it calmly, and with a professional, can help. This was a cross-sectional study: 117 autistic adults answered questionnaires. 32.5% reported moderate-to-severe insomnia. Lower perceived mental health was linked with more insomnia and with higher risk of problematic gaming. Limits: it shows links at one point in time, not what causes what, and it does not apply to every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person sover dåligt kan det hjälpa att tillsammans och utan skuld se på sömnen, måendet och hur mycket och hur personen spelar. Att prata lugnt om det, gärna med en yrkesperson, kan hjälpa. Studien var tvärsnittsstudie där 117 autistiska vuxna besvarade enkäter. 32.5% rapporterade måttlig till svår sömnlöshet. Sämre upplevd psykisk hälsa hängde ihop med mer sömnlöshet och högre risk för problematiskt spelande. Begränsningar: den visar samband vid ett tillfälle, inte orsak och verkan, och gäller inte alla personer.

title: Effectiveness of Digital Health Technologies in the Management of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children and Adolescents: A Systematic Review.
authors: Hamid S, Ul Hoque T, Bahaj B, Mohiuddin R
abstract: Limited access to specialist services, driven by workforce shortages and increasing demand, has constrained timely face-to-face management of autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Children and adolescents with ASD frequently engage with digital technologies, prompting growing interest in digital health interventions as potential adjuncts to traditional care; however, their effectiveness remains uncertain. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the evidence from randomised controlled trials assessing digital health interventions for the management of ASD-related symptoms in children and adolescents. Embase, MEDLINE, and Web of Science were searched in March 2023, and findings were synthesised narratively. Twelve randomised controlled trials comprising 622 participants met inclusion criteria, evaluating heterogeneous interventions including tablet- and computer-based applications, web-delivered video-modelling programmes, mobile health interventions, and wearable augmented-reality systems. While results for primary outcomes were mixed, with several trials reporting null findings for core social communication deficits, consistent positive effects were observed for functional and additional outcomes. Specifically, interventions grounded in established behavioural principles demonstrated benefits for receptive language, emotional comprehension, and adolescent vocational skills (e.g. employment interview performance and conflict negotiation). However, few studies directly compared digital interventions with active face-to-face therapies, and the overall risk of bias was mixed largely due to concerns regarding the randomisation process and high risk of bias in outcome measurement stemming from the use of unblinded, subjective parent-reported measures. Digital health interventions, therefore, show promise as adjunctive tools for supporting ASD management in children and adolescents, but larger, longer-term randomised trials across more diverse populations are required to establish their effectiveness, durability, and role alongside conventional ASD services.

sheet.es: Si le interesan las aplicaciones o programas digitales, pueden probarse como complemento, no como sustituto del apoyo en persona, y conviene observar con calma qué le resulta útil a la persona autista. Es una revisión sistemática de 12 ensayos aleatorizados con 622 participantes, niños y adolescentes. Los resultados sobre comunicación social fueron mixtos, y hubo beneficios en lenguaje receptivo, comprensión emocional y habilidades laborales adolescentes. Los límites: las intervenciones eran muy distintas, casi no se compararon con terapias presenciales y muchas medidas eran informes subjetivos de los padres, sin cegamiento. No sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If digital apps or programmes appeal to you, they can be tried as an add-on to in-person support, not a replacement, while you calmly watch what actually helps the autistic person. This is a systematic review of 12 randomised trials with 622 child and adolescent participants. Results for social communication were mixed, with benefits seen for receptive language, emotional comprehension and adolescent job skills. Limits: the interventions varied widely, few were compared with face-to-face therapy, and many measures were subjective, unblinded parent reports. It is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om digitala appar eller program lockar kan de prövas som ett komplement till stöd på plats, inte som ersättning, medan du lugnt följer vad som faktiskt hjälper den autistiska personen. Detta är en systematisk översikt av 12 randomiserade studier med 622 deltagare, barn och ungdomar. Resultaten för social kommunikation var blandade, och fördelar sågs för receptivt språk, känsloförståelse och yrkesfärdigheter hos ungdomar. Begränsningar: insatserna var mycket olika, få jämfördes med behandling på plats och många mått var subjektiva föräldrarapporter utan blindning. Det är ingen regel för alla personer.

title: White matter alterations linked to social cognitive improvements following theta burst stimulation of the right inferior frontal gyrus in autism.
authors: Yeh CH, Chen JR, Chao YP, Wu CT, Chou TL, Gau SS, Ni HC, Lin HY
abstract: Objectives Intermittent theta burst stimulation (iTBS) over the right inferior frontal gyrus (RIFG) has been shown to improve social cognitive function in autistic individuals. However, whether this intervention modulates underlying brain structure remains unknown. This study aimed to investigate the impact of iTBS over the RIFG on white matter macro- and micro-structure in intellectually able autistic children and young adults. Materials and methods In this 8-week double-blind, parallel, sham-controlled trial, autistic participants (aged 8-30 years) were randomized to receive twice-weekly neuro-navigated iTBS targeting the RIFG or sham stimulation using a sham coil applied over the same target. The social cognitive performance was measured with the Frith-Happé Animations Test. Diffusion MRI and behavioral assessments were acquired at baseline, week 8 (immediately after intervention), and week 12 (four-week follow-up). After quality control, data from 26 participants in the active group and 23 in the sham group were included in the final longitudinal whole-brain fixel-based analysis (FBA). Results No significant treatment-by-time interaction emerged: changes in the composite fiber-density-and-cross-section (FDC) metric did not differ between groups at either week 8 or week 12. Within the active group, however, a significant negative association was found between the change in FDC in the rostral body of the corpus callosum and the improvement in social cognitive performance from baseline to week 12. Conclusions An 8-week course of neuro-navigated RIFG iTBS did not produce significant group-level white matter macro/microstructural changes compared to sham stimulation in our autistic cohort. Nevertheless, the finding that individual improvements in social cognition correlated with specific white matter alterations in the active group suggests a potential link between treatment-induced benefits and neural plasticity. Future studies should investigate whether different TBS parameters could induce more pronounced or detectable structural changes on MRI in autistic individuals and further explore the intricate mechanisms underlying observed brain-behavior relationships.

sheet.es: Esta investigación no ofrece nada que cambiar mañana en casa; sirve para entender mejor una técnica experimental que aún se estudia. Fue un ensayo doble ciego con grupo de comparación simulado, en personas autistas de 8-30 años sin discapacidad intelectual. Recibieron estimulación cerebral no invasiva (theta burst) o una simulada durante 8 semanas. Al comparar los grupos, no hubo cambios significativos en la sustancia blanca. Solo en el grupo activo, la mejora social se relacionó con cambios en una zona concreta. Los límites: la muestra final fue pequeña (26 y 23 personas), la relación no prueba causa y no vale para todas las personas autistas. Las decisiones sobre tratamientos corresponden a profesionales sanitarios.
sheet.en: Nothing here changes what you do tomorrow at home; it helps explain an experimental technique that is still being studied. It was a double-blind, sham-controlled trial with autistic people aged 8-30 years who were intellectually able. They received non-invasive brain stimulation (theta burst) or a sham version for 8 weeks. Comparing the groups, there were no significant changes in white matter. Only in the active group did social improvement relate to changes in one specific area. Limits: the final sample was small (26 and 23 people), a link does not prove cause, and results do not apply to every autistic person. Decisions about treatment belong with a clinician.
sheet.sv: Den här studien ger inget att ändra hemma i morgon; den hjälper oss förstå en experimentell teknik som fortfarande undersöks. Det var en dubbelblind, skenkontrollerad studie med autistiska personer i åldern 8-30 år utan intellektuell funktionsnedsättning. De fick icke-invasiv hjärnstimulering (theta burst) eller en låtsasversion i 8 veckor. När grupperna jämfördes syntes inga signifikanta förändringar i vit substans. Bara i den aktiva gruppen hängde social förbättring ihop med förändringar i ett visst område. Begränsningar: det slutliga urvalet var litet (26 och 23 personer), samband visar inte orsak och resultaten gäller inte alla autistiska personer. Beslut om behandling hör hemma hos en kliniker.

title: Perceived Benefits and Barriers for Autistic Adults Accessing Therapeutic Horse Riding for Mental Health.
authors: Brumpton HL, Kargas N
abstract: Therapeutic horse riding (THR) is a non-traditional intervention that may support mental well-being in individuals with autism spectrum conditions. Despite growing interest, most research has focused on children and has tended to privilege practitioner or caregiver perspectives, leaving autistic adults underrepresented. This qualitative study explores the psychological benefits and systemic barriers associated with THR among Autistic adults, drawing on perspectives from both clients and practitioners. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with six Autistic clients and four practitioners, and the data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Five overarching themes were constructed: Facing the Puissance: barriers to accessing THR, Pathways to Participation, Embodied Engagement, To Understand and To Be Understood, and Beyond the Arena-Impacts That Last. Participants described enjoyment, increased confidence, and a sense of achievement, with effects accumulating over time and often extending beyond the riding arena into daily life. Barriers included cost, accessibility, and limited availability of appropriately trained staff and facilities. These findings add to the limited evidence base on THR for Autistic adults by providing an in-depth, contextually grounded account of participants' experiences. They suggest that, for verbally fluent Autistic adults who choose to access THR in similar settings, THR can enhance well-being, self-agency, and relationship-building, whilst also revealing structural obstacles that restrict equitable access.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta siente curiosidad por la equitación terapéutica, puede ser una opción que explorar a su ritmo, preguntando antes por el coste, el acceso y si el personal tiene formación adecuada. Es un estudio cualitativo con entrevistas a seis clientes autistas y cuatro profesionales. Las personas describieron disfrute, más confianza y sensación de logro, con efectos que a menudo seguían fuera de la pista. Como la muestra es pequeña y las personas participantes se expresaban con fluidez verbal, no sirve como regla para todas, y no mide cuánto ayuda. También se señalaron barreras como el coste y la poca disponibilidad.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult is curious about therapeutic horse riding, it may be an option to explore at their own pace, first asking about cost, access and whether staff are appropriately trained. This is a qualitative study with interviews of six autistic clients and four practitioners. People described enjoyment, more confidence and a sense of achievement, with effects that often continued beyond the riding arena. The sample is small and the participants were verbally fluent, so it is not a rule for everyone, and it does not measure how much it helps. Barriers such as cost and limited availability were also reported.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen är nyfiken på terapeutisk ridning kan det vara ett alternativ att utforska i egen takt, och man kan först fråga om kostnad, tillgång och om personalen har lämplig utbildning. Det här är en kvalitativ studie med intervjuer av sex autistiska klienter och fyra yrkesverksamma. Deltagarna beskrev glädje, ökat självförtroende och en känsla av att ha åstadkommit något, med effekter som ofta fortsatte utanför ridbanan. Urvalet är litet och deltagarna uttryckte sig verbalt flytande, så resultaten är ingen regel för alla, och studien mäter inte hur mycket det hjälper. Hinder som kostnad och begränsad tillgång framkom också.

title: Sensory Phenotypes in Autism Spectrum Disorder Associated with Distinct Patterns of Social Communication, Repetitive and Restrictive Behaviors or Interests, and Comorbidities: A State-of-the-Art Review.
authors: Consoli C, Turriziani L, Antoci M, Lo Monaco M, Ceraolo G, Spoto G, Nicotera AG, Di Rosa G
abstract: Sensory processing differences, reported in up to 97% of individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), are increasingly recognized as a defining feature of the condition, shaping perception, cognition, and adaptive behavior. Atypical sensory responsivity, ranging from hyper- to hypo-reactivity and sensory seeking, emerges early in development and contributes to the clinical and neurobiological heterogeneity of autism. Alterations in neural connectivity, the balance of excitation and inhibition, and multisensory integration are thought to underlie these sensory profiles, influencing emotional regulation, attention, and social interaction. Sensory features also interact with co-occurring conditions such as anxiety, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, and sleep and feeding difficulties, thereby shaping developmental trajectories and influencing adaptive behavior. Clinically, these sensory dysfunctions have a significant impact on daily participation and quality of life, extending their effects to family functioning. Understanding individual sensory phenotypes is therefore essential for accurate assessment and personalized intervention. Current therapeutic approaches include Sensory Integration Therapy, Sensory-Based Interventions, Sequential Oral Sensory Approach, and structured physical activity programs, often complemented by behavioral and mindfulness-based techniques. Emerging neuroplasticity-oriented methods for targeted modulation of sensory processing networks include neurofeedback and non-invasive brain stimulation. Overall, current evidence highlights the central role of sensory processing in ASD and underscores the need for multidisciplinary, individualized approaches to optimize developmental trajectories and enhance adaptive functioning. This review provides an updated synthesis of sensory processing in ASD, integrating neurobiological, developmental, and clinical evidence to highlight established knowledge, unresolved questions, and priorities for future research.

sheet.es: Mañana, observa con calma qué sonidos, luces, texturas o sabores le resultan intensos, o cuáles busca, a la persona autista que acompañas, y ajusta el entorno según lo que notes. Anotar esos patrones puede ayudar a hablar con profesionales sobre apoyos individualizados. Es una revisión de la literatura que reúne evidencia neurobiológica, del desarrollo y clínica; señala diferencias sensoriales en hasta 97% de las personas con autismo. Sus límites: es una síntesis general, deja preguntas abiertas y no describe a cada persona. Las decisiones sobre terapias o tratamientos corresponden a profesionales clínicos.
sheet.en: Tomorrow, calmly notice which sounds, lights, textures or tastes feel intense to the autistic person you support, or which they seek out, and adjust their surroundings to what you see. Writing these patterns down can help when talking with professionals about individualized support. This is a review of the literature that brings together neurobiological, developmental and clinical evidence; it reports sensory differences in up to 97% of people with autism. Its limits: it is a broad synthesis, leaves questions open, and does not describe every person. Decisions about therapies or treatments belong to clinicians.
sheet.sv: I morgon kan du lugnt lägga märke till vilka ljud, ljus, material eller smaker som känns intensiva för den autistiska person du stödjer, eller som personen söker sig till, och anpassa miljön efter det. Att skriva ner mönstren kan hjälpa i samtal med yrkespersoner om individanpassat stöd. Detta är en översikt som samlar neurobiologisk, utvecklingsmässig och klinisk evidens; den beskriver sensoriska skillnader hos upp till 97% av personer med autism. Begränsningar: det är en bred sammanfattning, lämnar frågor öppna och beskriver inte varje person. Beslut om terapier eller behandlingar hör till kliniker.

title: Effects of Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy on Parental Mental Health and Child Behavior in Families of Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
authors: Papadopoulos D, Maniadaki K
abstract: Background/Objectives : Caring for a child with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is often associated with elevated psychological distress and reduced life satisfaction. Mindfulness-based interventions may offer substantial benefits by enhancing emotion regulation, reducing maladaptive cognitive patterns, and strengthening mindful parenting. This randomized controlled trial (RCT) examined the effectiveness of an eight-week Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy (MBCT) program, enriched with mindful parenting practices, delivered to parents of children with ASD. The primary aim was to improve parental mental health, while secondary analyses explored potential indirect, parent-perceived changes in child behavior outcomes. Methods : Fifty-six parents of children with ASD were randomly assigned to an MBCT intervention group ( n = 30) or a waitlist control group ( n = 26). Parents completed assessments at baseline (T0), post-intervention (T1), and at one-month follow-up (T2), including the Depression Anxiety Stress Scales-21 (DASS-21), the Positive and Negative Affect Schedule (PANAS), and the Satisfaction With Life Scale (SWLS). They also rated the overall severity of their child's behavior problems to explore indirect treatment effects. Results : All parents receiving MBCT (100%) completed the program successfully and reported high acceptability. At baseline, no significant differences were observed between groups. At T1, the MBCT group demonstrated significant reductions in depression, anxiety, and stress, alongside increases in positive affect and life satisfaction. These improvements were maintained or strengthened at T2. However, the control group showed no significant changes over time. Additionally, parents in the MBCT group reported indirect improvements in their children's behavioral adjustment at T1 and T2. Conclusions : Findings demonstrate that MBCT constitutes an effective intervention for reducing parental psychopathology and indirectly supporting parent-perceived improvements in child behavior, emphasizing the importance of incorporating mindfulness and mindful parenting components into family-centered interventions for parents of children with ASD.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista y notas agotamiento, un programa de mindfulness para madres y padres puede ser una opción para tu propio bienestar. Puedes preguntar si existe algo así cerca de ti. Evidencia: ensayo aleatorizado con 56 madres y padres de niños autistas; quienes hicieron un programa de ocho semanas informaron menos depresión, ansiedad y estrés, y más satisfacción con la vida, frente a un grupo en lista de espera. Límites: el grupo es pequeño, los cambios en la conducta del niño los valoraron los propios padres y el seguimiento fue de solo un mes. No significa que funcione igual para todas las familias.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic person and feel worn down, a mindfulness programme for parents may be one option for your own wellbeing. You could ask whether one exists near you. Evidence: a randomized trial with 56 parents of autistic children; those who took an eight-week programme reported less depression, anxiety and stress, and more life satisfaction, compared with a waitlist group. Limits: the group was small, changes in the child's behaviour were rated by the parents themselves, and follow-up lasted only one month. It does not mean it will work the same way for every family.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person och känner dig slitten kan ett mindfulnessprogram för föräldrar vara ett alternativ för ditt eget välmående. Du kan fråga om något sådant finns i närheten. Evidens: en randomiserad studie med 56 föräldrar till autistiska barn; de som gick ett åtta veckor långt program rapporterade mindre depression, ångest och stress samt högre livstillfredsställelse jämfört med en väntelistgrupp. Begränsningar: gruppen var liten, förändringar i barnets beteende bedömdes av föräldrarna själva och uppföljningen varade bara en månad. Det betyder inte att det fungerar likadant för alla familjer.

title: Effectiveness and experiences of early intensive behavioral and naturalistic developmental behavior interventions for autism spectrum disorders: a mixed-methods systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Han DG, Lee Y, Kim HS, Suh HW, Lee J, Shin SH, Yang M, Choi H, Kim TH, Kang JG, Ko E, Lee J, Park MH
journal: Child and adolescent psychiatry and mental health
abstract: Background Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition marked by social communication deficits and restricted, repetitive behaviors. Among evidence-based practices (EBPs), interventions grounded in applied behavior analysis (ABA) principles-including Early Intensive Behavioral Intervention and naturalistic developmental behavioral interventions-are widely used. While the evidence suggests potential benefits, the findings are inconsistent, most studies carry a high risk of bias, and the quality of evidence is generally low to very low. Gaps also remain in comparisons with treatment as usual (TAU) and across intervention intensities. Aims This mixed-methods systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the quantitative effectiveness and qualitative experiences of ABA-based interventions for children and adolescents with ASD, addressing the methodological limitations of earlier studies, and examining comparisons with TAU. Methods Seven databases were searched up to August 2023 following the PRISMA guidelines. Twenty-five studies met the inclusion criteria (16 randomized controlled trials, 9 qualitative). The quantitative outcomes included adaptive behavior, cognitive ability (IQ/DQ), language, daily living skills, socialization, joint attention, and autism symptom severity. Qualitative studies explored parents' and practitioners' experiences. Random-effects models were used, with subgroup analyses by intervention intensity and TAU comparisons. Results The meta-analysis revealed significant improvements in adaptive behavior (SMD = 0.31, 95% CI: 0.04-0.59, GRADE = low), daily living skills (SMD = 0.36, 95% CI: 0.08-0.64, GRADE = low), language skills (SMD = 0.42, 95% CI: 0.24-0.60, GRADE = moderate), and joint attention behavior (SMD = 0.27, 95% CI: 0.04-0.49, GRADE = low) compared with the controls. High-intensity interventions had a notably greater effect on language skills (SMD = 0.72, 95% CI: 0.42-1.01) than low-intensity interventions (SMD = 0.34, 95% CI: 0.13-0.55). Comparisons with TAU revealed significant effects on adaptive behavior (SMD = 0.34, 95% CI: 0.02-0.66), daily living skills (SMD = 0.39, 95% CI: 0.07-0.71), and language skills (SMD = 0.51, 95% CI: 0.24-0.78). Qualitative findings highlighted perceived family and practitioner benefits but also barriers such as financial constraints and variability in training quality. Conclusion This study confirms the effectiveness of ABA in improving developmental and behavioral outcomes in children with ASD. However, systemic challenges and variability in outcomes underscore the need for targeted policy initiatives, enhanced training programs, and further research on the impact of ABA on core ASD symptoms.

sheet.es: Si valora una intervención basada en ABA para su hijo o hija autista, pregunte qué objetivos se plantean, cómo se forma al equipo y cuánto cuesta, y pida que se tengan en cuenta sus preferencias y su bienestar. La evidencia es un metaanálisis de 25 estudios (16 ensayos aleatorizados y 9 cualitativos) con niñas, niños y adolescentes autistas, y sus familias y profesionales. Halló mejoras pequeñas o moderadas en lenguaje, conducta adaptativa, vida diaria y atención conjunta; la calidad de la evidencia fue baja en casi todos los resultados y moderada en lenguaje. Las familias señalaron barreras como el coste y la calidad desigual de la formación. No es una regla para cada persona ni indica qué enfoque es mejor.
sheet.en: If you are considering an ABA-based intervention for your autistic child, ask what the goals are, how the team is trained and what it costs, and ask that your child's preferences and wellbeing are taken into account. The evidence is a meta-analysis of 25 studies (16 randomized trials and 9 qualitative) involving autistic children and adolescents, plus their families and practitioners. It found small to moderate gains in language, adaptive behavior, daily living skills and joint attention; the quality of evidence was low for most outcomes and moderate for language. Families reported barriers such as cost and uneven training quality. This is not a rule for every person and does not show which approach is best.
sheet.sv: Om du överväger en ABA-baserad insats för ditt autistiska barn: fråga vilka mål som sätts, hur teamet utbildas och vad det kostar, och be att barnets önskemål och välbefinnande beaktas. Underlaget är en metaanalys av 25 studier (16 randomiserade studier och 9 kvalitativa) med autistiska barn och ungdomar samt deras familjer och yrkesverksamma. Den fann små till måttliga förbättringar i språk, adaptivt beteende, dagliga färdigheter och gemensam uppmärksamhet; evidensens kvalitet var låg för de flesta utfall och måttlig för språk. Familjer beskrev hinder som kostnad och ojämn utbildningskvalitet. Detta är ingen regel för alla och visar inte vilken metod som är bäst.

title: Does genetic testing impact stigma in autism: A scoping review.
authors: Molloy CJ, Miles A, Christoff C, Cunningham J, Reilly J, Vorstman J, Austin J, Hawke LD, Gallagher L
abstract: Public stigma is a society’s negative attitude toward a person or groups of people, self-stigma relates to the internalisation of these negative attitudes, and affiliate stigma is experienced by those associated with a stigmatised group. Both autism and genetic testing results can be stigmatised. This scoping review explored relationships between genetic testing and stigma in autism, to understand any perceived positive or negative effects. Embase Classic, and APA PsycINFO via Ovid databases were searched on May 30th, 2023, and updated January 9th, 2025. Included articles related to experiences of or attitudes toward genetic testing or genetic counselling, and involved autistic people, people with autism-related genetic conditions, or their parents, and explored stigma and stigma-related factors. Twenty-five articles were included: three included autistic adults and twenty-two included parents of autistic people or those with autism-related genetic conditions. Stigma-related factors included both autistic people’s and parent concerns surrounding social and insurance discrimination, parental experiences of isolation and ignorance in relation to the healthcare system, and perceptions of labelling. Findings were mixed regarding self-blame, worry and stress among autistic adults. Some parents reported an increase in worry and stress relating to discrimination, while others reported relief related to genetic test results and enhanced biological understanding. This review highlights the lack of focus on perspectives of autistic adolescents and individuals with autism-related genetic conditions, regarding genetic testing impacts on stigma. Future research should address these gaps to inform more supportive clinical and societal practices.

sheet.es: Si está valorando una prueba genética, hable antes con su familia y con el equipo clínico sobre cómo podría afectar al estigma, tanto el temor a la discriminación como el posible alivio de tener una explicación. Es una decisión personal y no hay una respuesta única. Es una revisión de alcance de 25 artículos: tres incluían a adultos autistas y veintidós a madres y padres de personas autistas o con condiciones genéticas relacionadas. Los resultados fueron mixtos: algunas familias sintieron más preocupación y otras alivio. Casi no hay datos de adolescentes autistas ni de personas con condiciones genéticas relacionadas con el autismo, así que puede no reflejar su caso.
sheet.en: If you are considering genetic testing, talk with your family and the clinical team beforehand about how it might affect stigma, including worry about discrimination and the possible relief of having an explanation. It is a personal decision and there is no single right answer.
