This was a scoping review of 25 articles: three included autistic adults and twenty-two included parents of autistic people or of people with autism-related genetic conditions. Findings were mixed: some families felt more worry, others felt relief. There is very little evidence from autistic adolescents or people with autism-related genetic conditions, so it may not reflect your situation.
sheet.sv: Om ni funderar på genetisk testning, prata först med familjen och vårdteamet om hur det kan påverka stigma, både oro för diskriminering och den möjliga lättnaden i att få en förklaring. Det är ett personligt beslut och det finns inget enda rätt svar. Detta var en kartläggande översikt av 25 artiklar: tre inkluderade autistiska vuxna och tjugotvå inkluderade föräldrar till autistiska personer eller personer med autismrelaterade genetiska tillstånd. Resultaten var blandade: vissa familjer kände mer oro, andra lättnad. Det finns mycket lite kunskap från autistiska tonåringar och personer med autismrelaterade genetiska tillstånd, så resultaten kanske inte speglar er situation.

title: Psychiatric Emergency Visits of Autistic Adults With or Without Documented Borderline Personality Disorder.
authors: Lee CJ, Man LLY, Morra A, Pace-Tonna C, Castelino C, Courchesne V, Frayne M, Luk V, Baharikhoob P, Jachyra P, Zaheer J, Ameis SH, Lin HY, Sawyer A, Lunsky Y, Lai MC
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Autism and borderline personality disorder (BPD) are each associated with increased psychiatric emergency department (PsyED) use, yet the service impact of coexisting autism-BPD remains unclear. We conducted a retrospective chart review of 1027 PsyED visits by 345 autistic adults (2018-2020) at an urban Canadian psychiatric hospital to compare service patterns between those with and without a BPD diagnosis. Sociodemographics, presenting reasons, restraint use, and disposition were analyzed using mixed-effects logistic regression. BPD was documented in 33.5% of visits and in 11.0% of unique autistic individuals, more often in birth-assigned females. Among all autistic individuals' PsyED visits, an autism diagnosis was documented in 60.2% of their text-based charts. Furthermore, autism was documented less frequently when BPD was recorded, suggesting possible diagnostic overshadowing. Suicidality as the primary reason for visit was associated with documented BPD (OR 4.366, 95% CI 2.659-7.169; p < 0.001). No significant differences were observed in disposition (discharge vs. admission) or restraint use between birth-assigned sex, BPD status, or documentation of autism within the visit. Findings underscore the need for sex-sensitive, autism-aware assessments and trauma-informed care in PsyED settings, and caution against diagnostic overshadowing that influences clinical decision-making. Limitations include a single-site sample and lack of autism diagnosis timing data, precluding temporal inferences. Future work should test targeted interventions and clarify mechanisms of suicidality among autistic individuals with coexisting BPD. Integrated autism-BPD care pathways, with specialized outpatient supports, sensory-friendly adaptations, and structured referrals, may improve care and reduce PsyED visits.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista a urgencias psiquiátricas, conviene decir con claridad que es autista y pedir una evaluación que tenga en cuenta el autismo, el trauma y las necesidades sensoriales. Evidencia: revisión retrospectiva de historias de 1027 visitas de 345 adultos autistas en un hospital psiquiátrico urbano de Canadá. El autismo se registraba menos cuando constaba un trastorno límite de la personalidad, lo que sugiere que podría quedar eclipsado. La suicidalidad como motivo principal se asoció con ese diagnóstico. Límites: un solo centro y sin datos sobre cuándo se diagnosticó el autismo, así que no explica causas ni vale para todas las personas. Si hay riesgo de suicidio o autolesión, busca ayuda profesional (clínico, servicio de salud o servicio de crisis); ante peligro inmediato, llama al número de emergencias de tu país.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person in a psychiatric emergency department, it helps to state clearly that they are autistic and to ask for an assessment that accounts for autism, trauma and sensory needs. Evidence: a retrospective chart review of 1027 visits by 345 autistic adults at an urban psychiatric hospital in Canada. Autism was documented less often when borderline personality disorder was recorded, suggesting it may be overshadowed. Suicidality as the main reason for the visit was linked to that diagnosis. Limits: one site and no data on when autism was diagnosed, so it cannot explain causes or apply to everyone. If there is a risk of suicide or self-injury, contact professional help (a clinician, a health service or a crisis service); in immediate danger, call your country's emergency number.
sheet.sv: Om du stödjer en autistisk person på en psykiatrisk akutmottagning är det bra att tydligt säga att personen är autistisk och be om en bedömning som tar hänsyn till autism, trauma och sensoriska behov. Evidens: en retrospektiv journalgenomgång av 1027 besök av 345 autistiska vuxna på ett urbant psykiatriskt sjukhus i Kanada. Autism dokumenterades mer sällan när borderline personlighetsstörning fanns antecknad, vilket tyder på att den kan hamna i skymundan. Suicidalitet som främsta besöksorsak hängde ihop med den diagnosen. Begränsningar: en enda plats och inga uppgifter om när autismdiagnosen ställdes, så studien förklarar inte orsaker och gäller inte alla. Vid risk för självmord eller självskada, kontakta professionell hjälp (läkare, vårdcentral eller kristjänst); vid akut fara, ring ditt lands nödnummer.

title: Traumatic Experiences, Psychological Distress and Suicide-Related Behaviors in Autistic Adults.
authors: Chikaura TA, Weir E, Griffiths S, Procyshyn T, Pelton M, Allison C, Hodges H, White SR, Ford T, Baron-Cohen S
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Autistic adults have increased risks of trauma, suicide, and poor mental health compared to non-autistic adults, with 1 in 4 autistic adults attempting suicide. We administered an anonymized, self-report survey to 424 autistic and 345 non-autistic adults through a convenience sampling framework. Binomial logistic regression models identified whether trauma and autism diagnosis were related to (i) self-harm, (ii) suicide attempts, (iii) suicide plans, (iv) a mental health condition that impacts daily life, and (v) substance use to cope. Heatmaps were generated to identify traumas that frequently co-occur with psychological distress and SRB. After accounting for trauma and demographic differences, autism remained a significant predictor of all outcomes, except whether individuals used substances to cope (OR: 0.78, 95% CI: 0.54-1.12, p = 0.18). Autistic people were more likely to report self-harm (OR: 2.71, 95% CI: 1.85-4.00, p < 0.01), suicide attempts (OR: 2.45, 95% CI: 1.65-3.68, p < 0.01), suicide plans (OR: 2.00, 95% CI: 1.41-2.83, p < 0.01), and experiencing a mental health condition that impacts daily life (OR: 3.58, 95% CI: 2.42-5.33, p < 0.01) than non-autistic people. Among autistic people, childhood victimization co-occurred with a mental health condition that impacts daily life, self-harm, and suicide plans most frequently. This study provides evidence of complex relationships between autism, trauma, self-harm, suicide attempts, suicide plans, and a mental health condition that impacts daily life. Focusing on the prevention of trauma, coping strategies, and recovery from traumatic events through safeguarding and support may be critical tools for suicide prevention among autistic people.

title: A Coordinated Project-Management Approach to Multisite Implementation of Motor-Rehabilitation Programs for Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder in United States Healthcare Systems: A Narrative Review.
authors: Omo Enabulele AB, Oyebamiji I, Ikubanni O, Okwah MN, Babalola WS, Azeez OM, Olaniyi AO
abstract: Motor impairments are common in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and contribute to reduced functional independence, participation, and quality of life. Although motor-rehabilitation interventions can improve motor and adaptive outcomes, services are often fragmented, inconsistently delivered, and difficult to scale beyond single clinical settings. Multisite implementation of ASD motor-rehabilitation programs remains limited, underscoring the need for coordinated approaches that address both clinical and organizational challenges. This integrative narrative review synthesizes representative literature on motor-rehabilitation interventions for children with ASD alongside implementation-science and project-management frameworks relevant to multisite healthcare delivery in the United States. A broad search of peer-reviewed literature and policy sources published between 2000 and 2025 was conducted. Evidence was synthesized qualitatively with attention to implementation-relevant factors, governance structures, and scalability considerations; no quantitative synthesis or statistical analysis was performed. The reviewed literature indicates that motor-rehabilitation interventions can improve motor proficiency, adaptive behavior, and participation in children with ASD. However, the evidence base is dominated by small, single-site studies with substantial heterogeneity in intervention design and outcome reporting. Key barriers to multisite implementation include variability in workforce training, infrastructure, reimbursement models, data systems, and family engagement across settings. Implementation-science frameworks (e.g., the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR), Reach-Effectiveness-Adoption-Implementation-Maintenance (RE-AIM), and Normalization Process Theory) and project-management methodologies offer complementary strategies to address these barriers but are rarely integrated within ASD motor-rehabilitation research. Drawing on these domains, this review proposes a Coordinated Project-Management Framework to guide multisite implementation through iterative phases of initiation, planning, delivery, monitoring and evaluation, and sustainability. Scaling effective motor-rehabilitation services for children with ASD will require coordinated, multisite implementation rather than isolated clinic-based efforts. Future research should prioritize piloting and evaluating this framework in real-world healthcare networks using hybrid effectiveness-implementation designs to improve access, consistency, and equity in ASD motor rehabilitation.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija autista tiene dificultades de movimiento, puede preguntar a su equipo sanitario qué programas de rehabilitación motora hay cerca y si coordinan con otros servicios. Esta es una revisión narrativa de literatura publicada entre 2000 y 2025, sobre programas en Estados Unidos. Indica que estos programas pueden mejorar la competencia motora, la conducta adaptativa y la participación. Sin embargo, casi todos los estudios son pequeños, de un solo centro y muy distintos entre sí. Además, propone un marco de gestión que aún no se ha probado, y los servicios varían según el lugar. No sirve como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If your autistic child has movement difficulties, you can ask their care team which motor-rehabilitation programs exist nearby and whether services are coordinated. This is a narrative review of literature published between 2000 and 2025, focused on programs in the United States. It suggests these programs can improve motor skills, adaptive behavior and participation. However, most studies are small, from a single site, and very different from one another. The review also proposes a project-management framework that has not yet been tested, and services vary by place. It is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn har svårigheter med motoriken kan du fråga vårdteamet vilka program för motorisk rehabilitering som finns i närheten och om tjänsterna samordnas. Detta är en narrativ översikt av litteratur publicerad mellan 2000 och 2025, med fokus på program i USA. Den tyder på att programmen kan förbättra motorisk förmåga, adaptivt beteende och delaktighet. De flesta studier är dock små, görs på en enda plats och skiljer sig mycket åt. Översikten föreslår också ett ramverk för projektledning som ännu inte har testats, och tjänsterna varierar mellan platser. Det är ingen regel för varje person.

title: Prevention and Reduction of Anxiety in Autistic Preschoolers Through an Autism-Specific Parent-Mediated Intervention: A Pilot Randomised Controlled Trial Evaluating Short and Longer Term Outcomes.
authors: Adams D, Malone S, Dargue N, Keen D, Rodgers J, Simpson K, Wicks R, Bullot A, Rapee R
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Anxiety is a common co-occurring condition for autistic preschoolers. Whilst there has been extensive research evaluating anxiety prevention/reduction interventions for neurotypical preschoolers, such research is limited for autistic children. Fifty-seven parents of autistic 4-5-year olds, with varying levels of anxiety, participated in a randomised controlled trial of an autism-specific, parent-mediated intervention (CLK-CUES) to prevent or reduce anxiety in autistic preschoolers. Baseline, short-term (post-intervention) and longer term (12 months follow-up) assessments included child anxiety (ASC-ASD-P and PAS-R), intolerance of uncertainty, and parent well-being. (Trial registration ACTRN12620001322921). There were no reports of harmful effects of the intervention or trial. Linear mixed models show a significant group x time interaction for ASC-ASD-P Total score and the Uncertainty subscale with medium and large effect sizes. Post-hoc analyses show a significant decline for only the intervention group in anxiety (specifically, anxiety around uncertainty) from pre-post intervention, maintained at one year follow-up. There was no change on the PAS-R or other ASC-ASD-P subscales. CLK-CUES shows promise as a way to prevent and reduce anxiety in young autistic children, specifically anxiety related to uncertainty. Trials with larger samples are warranted. Findings also highlight the importance of using measures designed for autistic children.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija autista de 4-5 años se angustia ante lo imprevisto, puede ayudar prepararle con antelación para los cambios y apoyar a la familia con un programa pensado para autistas. Un ensayo piloto aleatorizado con 57 madres y padres probó el programa CLK-CUES. La ansiedad ante la incertidumbre bajó solo en el grupo que lo recibió, y el cambio se mantuvo a los 12 meses. No se notificaron efectos dañinos. Sin embargo, la muestra es pequeña, no hubo cambios en otra escala de ansiedad ni en otras subescalas, y no sirve como regla para cada niño. Hacen falta estudios más grandes.
sheet.en: If your autistic 4-5-year-old gets distressed by the unexpected, it may help to prepare them for changes in advance and to join a parent-mediated programme designed for autistic children. A pilot randomised controlled trial with 57 parents tested the CLK-CUES programme. Anxiety around uncertainty fell only in the group that received it, and the change held at 12 months. No harmful effects were reported. However, the sample was small, another anxiety scale and other subscales showed no change, and results are not a rule for every child. Larger trials are needed.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn på 4-5 år blir oroligt av det oväntade kan det hjälpa att förbereda barnet på förändringar i förväg och att delta i ett föräldrastött program utformat för autistiska barn. En pilotstudie med slumpmässig fördelning och 57 föräldrar testade programmet CLK-CUES. Ångest kring osäkerhet minskade bara i gruppen som fick programmet, och förändringen höll i sig vid 12 månader. Inga skadliga effekter rapporterades. Studien var dock liten, ett annat ångestmått och andra delskalor visade ingen förändring, och resultaten gäller inte alla barn. Större studier behövs.

title: Parent Training for Disruptive Behaviors in Referred Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
authors: Breider S, de Bildt A, Greaves-Lord K, Dietrich A, Hoekstra PJ, van den Hoofdakker BJ
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: The purpose of this study was to investigate whether face-to-face and therapist-assisted online (i.e., blended) behavioral parent training are effective on reducing disruptive behaviors in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in routine mental health care. Ninety-seven children with ASD (4-13 years; 76 boys) were randomized to face-to-face parent training, blended parent training, or a waitlist control condition. We assessed treatment effects on parent-rated child noncompliance (primary outcome) and irritability (secondary outcome). This involved comparing both formats separately to the control condition using linear regression models. Child behaviors at 6 months follow-up were also examined. Children in the face-to-face parent training condition improved significantly more on noncompliance and irritability than children in the waitlist condition and improvements sustained to 6 months follow-up. Children in the blended condition did not improve more than children in the waitlist condition and attrition was high. Our results extend findings from efficacy studies to routine mental health care and advocate the use of face-to-face parent training for disruptive behaviors in children with ASD. More research into blended parent training programs for children with ASD and disruptive behaviors in routine mental health care should be conducted to draw more definite conclusions about the value of blended parent training for these children. Trial registration number NL4712; date of registration 22-10-2014.

sheet.es: Si buscas apoyo para las conductas que te cuestan en casa, el entrenamiento presencial para madres y padres puede ser una opción que merece consultarse con el servicio de salud mental. En un ensayo aleatorizado participaron 97 niños autistas de 4-13 años. Quienes recibieron el entrenamiento presencial mejoraron más en la colaboración con las peticiones y en la irritabilidad, según las familias, que quienes esperaban, y la mejora siguió a los 6 meses. El formato combinado con parte en línea no mostró mejoras mayores y muchas familias lo abandonaron. Sin embargo, la mayoría eran niños, y los resultados no valen para todas las familias; hace falta más investigación sobre el formato combinado.
sheet.en: If you are looking for support with situations that feel hard at home, face-to-face parent training may be worth discussing with your mental health service. In a randomized trial, 97 autistic children aged 4-13 took part. Parents who received face-to-face training reported more improvement in their child's cooperation with requests and in irritability than parents on a waitlist, and the gains lasted to 6 months. The blended format with online parts did not show greater improvement, and many families dropped out. Most participants were boys, and results will not fit every family; more research is needed on the blended format.
sheet.sv: Om du söker stöd kring situationer som känns svåra hemma kan föräldrautbildning på plats vara värd att ta upp med den psykiatriska vården. I en randomiserad studie deltog 97 autistiska barn i åldern 4-13 år. Föräldrar som fick utbildning på plats rapporterade större förbättring i barnets samarbete med önskemål och i irritabilitet än de som stod på väntelista, och förbättringen höll i sig i 6 månader. Den blandade varianten med delar online gav inte större förbättring, och många familjer avbröt. De flesta deltagarna var pojkar och resultaten passar inte alla familjer; mer forskning behövs om den blandade varianten.

title: "Am I My Sibling's Keeper?": the Lived experiences of adult siblings of individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder in China.
authors: Han F, Gao X
journal: International journal of qualitative studies on health and well-being
abstract: Background Research on families of individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) often marginalizes adult neurotypical (NT) siblings, particularly outside of Western contexts. Objective This study aimed to provide an in-depth exploration of the lived experiences of adult NT siblings of individuals with ASD (IWASD) in China. Methods Using an Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis (IPA) approach, this study conducted semi-structured in-depth interviews with eight adult NT siblings of IWASD from China. Data were analyzed following IPA procedures. Results The analysis yielded three group experiential themes: 1) the inescapable responsibility within a culture of blood-ties, 2) the struggle between "flesh-and-blood kin" and "spiritual isolation", and 3) finding identity between "fulfilling others" and "losing the self". The findings reveal that participants' lived experience is a dynamic process shaped by cultural responsibility, mediated by a paradoxical relationship, and ultimately characterized by identity negotiation through sacrifice. Conclusions The study concludes that in the Chinese context, the experience of adult NT siblings of IWASD dialectically unifies risk (e.g., ceded ideals) and resilience (e.g., pride as family stabilizer) under the core tenet of "sacrificing for the family". This offers a culturally centered, integrative perspective that supplements the dichotomous risk-resilience discussion in existing literature.

sheet.es: Si eres hermano o hermana adulta de una persona autista, es normal sentir a la vez cercanía, responsabilidad y soledad. Hablar de ello con alguien de confianza puede ayudar. Y si cuidas de una familia, vale la pena preguntar también a los hermanos cómo están. Es un estudio cualitativo con entrevistas a 8 hermanos adultos no autistas de China. Sus experiencias reflejan una cultura concreta y un grupo muy pequeño, así que no representan a todas las familias ni incluyen la voz de las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If you are an adult sibling of an autistic person, it is common to feel closeness, responsibility and isolation all at once. Talking about it with someone you trust may help. If you support a family, it is also worth asking the siblings how they are doing. This was a qualitative study based on interviews with 8 adult non-autistic siblings in China. Their experiences reflect one culture and a very small group, so they do not represent every family, and the autistic siblings' own views were not part of it.
sheet.sv: Om du är vuxen syskon till en autistisk person är det vanligt att känna närhet, ansvar och ensamhet på samma gång. Det kan hjälpa att prata om det med någon du litar på. Om du stöttar en familj är det också värt att fråga syskonen hur de mår. Detta var en kvalitativ studie med intervjuer av 8 vuxna icke-autistiska syskon i Kina. Deras erfarenheter speglar en specifik kultur och en mycket liten grupp, så de gäller inte alla familjer, och de autistiska syskonens egna röster ingick inte.

title: Protocol for a feasibility and acceptability trial of Bloom, a co-produced and co-facilitated parent group to enhance the quality of life and well-being of young autistic children.
authors: Adams D, Ambrose K, Bowen R, Heyworth M, Heussler H, Roth J, Pellicano E, Downes M, Houting JD, Paynter J, Simpson K, Trembath D, Westerveld M, Carroll A, Johnston A
abstract: Background The autistic and autism communities have identified improving the quality of life and well-being of autistic people as a key priority. Despite this, to date, there are no evidence-based supports for autistic children which specifically focus on improvements in these areas. This project seeks to address this gap by evaluating the acceptability and feasibility of Bloom, an 8-week co-produced and co-facilitated parent group that aims to enhance the quality of life and well-being of young autistic children. Methods This is a feasibility and acceptability study of a parent group, Bloom, which has been co-designed and co-produced between researchers and representatives from community organisations. The study aims to recruit 80 parents of autistic children aged 3-8 years through community organisations and social media networks. Once informed consent is provided, participants will be asked to complete baseline assessments (questionnaires and semi-structured interviews). These include measures of demographic as well as child, family, and parent well-being. Participants will be invited to attend the Bloom group for eight consecutive weeks during school term times. Groups will either be online or face to face, depending on parent preference and availability. Each group will be co-facilitated between an autistic person and an allied health professional. The assessments conducted at baseline (T1) will be repeated after completion of the group (T2) and at follow-up, 3 months after group completion (T3). At T2 and T3, participants will also be asked about their experiences of both the group and of their participation in the study. Discussion This feasibility and acceptability trial will provide essential data that, if positive, will inform the design of a fully powered randomised controlled trial (RCT). This includes the acceptability and feasibility of recruitment, study processes, the Bloom parent group, and baseline/outcome measures, including adherence to processes and the group. Additional data will be collected on retention from baseline to follow-up; effect sizes will be calculated for each outcome measure, both of which will inform the sample size of a future RCT. Findings of this study will be disseminated through written and/or audiovisual lay summaries to all participants and partner community organisations, as well as through peer-reviewed manuscripts and conference presentations. Conclusions This study is one small, but important, step towards autism-specific, relevant, and accessible supports that combine professional and lived experience to improve outcomes for autistic people and their families. Trial registration Ethical clearance was provided by Griffith University Human Research Ethics Committee (HREC 2023/934). The Universal Trial Number is U1111-1305-0305, and the study has been registered with the Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry (ANZCTR) number ACTRN12624000350527.

sheet.es: Todavía no hay resultados que aplicar mañana, pero si buscas apoyo, puedes preguntar a organizaciones comunitarias por grupos para familias dirigidos junto con personas autistas y centrados en el bienestar. Este es el protocolo de un estudio piloto sobre Bloom, un grupo de 8 semanas para madres y padres de niños autistas de 3-8 años, codiseñado con organizaciones comunitarias y dirigido por una persona autista y un profesional sanitario. Prevé reclutar a 80 familias. Sus límites: aún no se han publicado resultados y solo comprobará si el grupo es viable y aceptable, no si mejora la calidad de vida.
sheet.en: There are no results to act on tomorrow, but if you are looking for support, you can ask community organisations about parent groups led together with autistic people and focused on well-being. This is the protocol for a pilot study of Bloom, an 8-week group for parents of autistic children aged 3-8, co-designed with community organisations and co-led by an autistic person and an allied health professional. It plans to recruit 80 parents. Its limits: no results have been reported yet, and it only tests whether the group is feasible and acceptable, not whether it improves quality of life.
sheet.sv: Det finns inga resultat att använda i morgon, men om du söker stöd kan du fråga samhällsorganisationer om föräldragrupper som leds tillsammans med autistiska personer och fokuserar på välbefinnande. Detta är protokollet för en pilotstudie om Bloom, en 8 veckor lång grupp för föräldrar till autistiska barn i åldern 3-8 år, utformad med samhällsorganisationer och ledd av en autistisk person och en vårdprofessionell. Man planerar att rekrytera 80 föräldrar. Begränsningar: inga resultat har publicerats ännu, och studien prövar bara om gruppen är genomförbar och acceptabel, inte om den förbättrar livskvaliteten.

title: Suicide prevention interventions and supports for the Autistic community: a scoping review protocol.
authors: Russell A, Cremen C, Rainbow E, Melia R
abstract: Introduction Suicide is a leading cause of death among Autistic adults globally. Autistic people are up to six times more likely to die by suicide than people in the general population. Research highlights a lack of appropriate support for Autistic individuals experiencing suicidal thoughts and behaviours. Methods and analysis A scoping review will be conducted to map available literature on Suicide Prevention Interventions and Supports used with the Autistic community. This scoping review will use the methodological guidelines set out by the Joanna Briggs Institute Manual for Evidence Synthesis. The searches will be conducted in January 2025. The following electronic databases will be searched; PubMed, CINAHL Ultimate, PsycINFO and EMBASE, as well as the reference lists of included articles and grey literature (including conference abstracts, PhD theses, grey literature databases and preprints). The search strategy will be used to identify literature with an aim of preventing suicide in Autistic individuals. Only literature published in English will be included. Two reviewers will independently screen all literature based on predetermined inclusion and exclusion criteria. Data extraction will be piloted by two reviewers and continued by one reviewer. The extracted data will be checked for accuracy by a second reviewer. Any disagreements that arise between the reviewers will be resolved through discussion or with a third reviewer. A narrative summary of findings will be conducted. Results will be reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Review statement. Ethics and dissemination Ethics approval is not required for this study as it is protocol for a review of published literature and does not involve human participants or private data. Findings will be disseminated through professional networks, conference presentations and publication in a scientific journal. Trial registration number This protocol has been registered on the Open Science Framework (https://osf.io/bpxnf/overview).

sheet.es: Tómate en serio cualquier mención de pensamientos suicidas en una persona autista y busca apoyo profesional; no esperes a que sea "más claro". Este documento es un protocolo de revisión: describe cómo se buscará y resumirá la literatura sobre prevención del suicidio y apoyos para la comunidad autista, y aún no ofrece resultados. Señala que el suicidio es una de las principales causas de muerte entre adultos autistas y que las personas autistas tienen hasta seis veces más probabilidad de morir por suicidio que la población general. También indica que falta apoyo adecuado. Como todavía no hay hallazgos, no sabemos qué intervenciones funcionan. Si tú o alguien cercano está en riesgo, contacta con un profesional sanitario o un servicio de crisis; ante un peligro inmediato, llama al número de emergencias de tu país.
sheet.en: Take any mention of suicidal thoughts by an autistic person seriously and seek professional support; don't wait for it to become "clearer". This paper is a review protocol: it describes how literature on suicide prevention interventions and supports for the autistic community will be searched and summarised, and it does not yet give results. It notes that suicide is a leading cause of death among autistic adults and that autistic people are up to six times more likely to die by suicide than the general population. It also says appropriate support is lacking. Because there are no findings yet, we cannot say which interventions work. If you or someone close to you is at risk, contact a clinician, a health service or a crisis service; in immediate danger, call the emergency number of your country.
sheet.sv: Ta alla uttryck för självmordstankar hos en autistisk person på allvar och sök professionellt stöd; vänta inte tills det blir "tydligare". Den här texten är ett protokoll för en översikt: den beskriver hur litteratur om suicidprevention och stöd för den autistiska gemenskapen ska sökas och sammanfattas, och den redovisar ännu inga resultat. Den uppger att suicid är en av de vanligaste dödsorsakerna bland autistiska vuxna och att autistiska personer har upp till sex gånger högre sannolikhet att dö i suicid än befolkningen i allmänhet. Den säger också att lämpligt stöd saknas. Eftersom det inte finns några fynd ännu vet vi inte vilka insatser som fungerar. Om du eller någon nära dig är i riskzonen, kontakta en läkare, vården eller en krisjour; vid akut fara, ring det nödnummer som gäller i ditt land.

title: Study protocol for a comparative effectiveness randomized controlled trial comparing the emotion awareness and skills enhancement program to the unified protocol in autistic youth and young adults with emotion dysregulation.
authors: Mazefsky CA, Bradley M, Duman K, Beck KB, Conner CM, Powell N, Siegle GJ, Jones S, Trabert C, Tonarely-Busto N, Shaw AM, de Abril Cameron F, Kolko DJ, Kang C, Ehrenreich-May J, Farchione TJ, White SW
abstract: BACKGROUND: Many autistic people seek therapy for mental health concerns or to improve emotional wellbeing. Unfortunately, there is limited guidance for providers on the most effective approach to improve mental health for autistic people. Therapies that target emotion dysregulation may be clinically effective and parsimonious. However, it remains unclear if emotion dysregulation interventions that were not developed for autism are effective or if interventions developed for autistic clients may confer additional benefits in terms of effectiveness and ease of implementation by community clinicians. The Emotion Awareness and Skills Enhancement (EASE) Program was developed to target emotion dysregulation specifically in autism, and has been shown to be efficacious for autistic youth and young adults in a standard clinical trial conducted in a research setting. METHODS: In this Hybrid Type 1 comparative effectiveness randomized controlled trial, we examine clinical impact and implementation outcomes across two treatments. The target intervention is a mindfulness-based curriculum developed for autistic clients (EASE) compared to the child, adolescent, and adult Unified Protocols (UP), established interventions rooted in cognitive-behavioral therapy that were not developed for autistic clients. This research is based on a community-driven, advisory model, including two community partner groups that provide input on project implementation. Providers are community clinicians at mental health agencies in Pennsylvania and Alabama, with randomization by agency. Clients include autistic individuals aged 10 to 30 years, with a target sample size of 400. Data are collected at pre-, mid-, post-, and 3 months following therapy. The primary aim is to test comparative effectiveness. The secondary aim is to evaluate the feasibility, benefits, harms, and implementation outcomes. A third exploratory aim focuses on moderators of outcome. EASE is hypothesized to outperform UP. The primary outcomes are client emotion dysregulation and provider-rated acceptability and feasibility of implementation. Secondary outcomes include responder status determined by a condition-naive interviewer, questionnaires of mental health, quality of life, and client satisfaction, and coder-rated therapeutic alliance. Qualitative data on feasibility and implementation outcomes is collected from clients, providers, and agency leaders. DISCUSSION: Findings will inform clinical decision-making and hopefully help increase access to evidence-based mental healthcare for autistic individuals. TRIAL REGISTRATION: This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov ID NCT06158581. It was first registered on 11/27/23.

sheet.es: Si buscas apoyo emocional o terapia para una persona autista, puedes preguntar al profesional qué enfoque usa para la regulación emocional y si tiene experiencia con personas autistas. Este artículo es un protocolo: describe un ensayo aleatorizado que aún no da resultados. Compara dos terapias, EASE (basada en mindfulness y creada para personas autistas) y los Protocolos Unificados (basados en terapia cognitivo-conductual), en personas autistas de 10 a 30 años, con una muestra objetivo de 400. Como no hay resultados, no sabemos cuál funciona mejor y no debe tomarse como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you are looking for emotional support or therapy for an autistic person, you can ask the clinician which approach they use for emotion regulation and whether they have experience with autistic clients. This paper is a protocol: it describes a randomized trial that has not reported results yet. It compares two therapies, EASE (mindfulness-based and made for autistic people) and the Unified Protocols (based on cognitive-behavioral therapy), in autistic people aged 10 to 30 years, with a target sample size of 400. Because there are no results, we cannot yet say which works better, and it should not be taken as a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du söker känslomässigt stöd eller terapi för en autistisk person kan du fråga behandlaren vilket arbetssätt hen använder för känsloreglering och om hen har erfarenhet av autistiska klienter. Den här artikeln är ett protokoll: den beskriver en randomiserad studie som ännu inte har redovisat resultat. Den jämför två terapier, EASE (mindfulnessbaserad och utvecklad för autistiska personer) och Unified Protocols (baserade på kognitiv beteendeterapi), hos autistiska personer i åldern 10 till 30 år, med ett mål på 400 deltagare. Eftersom resultat saknas vet vi ännu inte vilken som fungerar bäst, och den bör inte ses som en regel för alla.

title: Common and unique menopause experiences among autistic and non-autistic people: A qualitative study.
authors: Piper MA, Charlton RA
abstract: Autistic people face both similar challenges to non-autistic people as they navigate menopause and additional unique challenges. Semi-structured interviews with 15 autistic and 14 non-autistic adults (assigned female at birth), explored experiences of menopause. Thematic analysis was carried out for the autistic and non-autistic groups separately. Analysis yielded four overarching themes: information about menopause, experiences of menopause, medical support for menopause and backdrop to the menopause. Each of these contained subthemes which indicated both shared and unique experiences between the groups. Both groups reported a lack of information about menopause, endured negative psychological changes during menopause and experienced menopause alongside other important life events. Autistic people faced unique challenges during menopause, including medical professionals not accommodating autistic differences, uncertainty-induced anxiety and the lifelong impact of living without an autism diagnosis. This study highlights the need for tailored care for this group during the menopause transition.

sheet.es: Si estás acompañando a una persona autista en la menopausia, puede ayudar buscar información clara juntas y preparar la cita médica con antelación, anotando preguntas y cambios, y pedir que se tengan en cuenta sus necesidades autistas. La evidencia es un estudio cualitativo con entrevistas a 15 adultos autistas y 14 no autistas (asignados mujer al nacer). Ambos grupos echaron en falta información; las personas autistas señalaron además profesionales que no se adaptaban, ansiedad por la incertidumbre y el peso de no haber tenido diagnóstico. Los límites: son experiencias de un grupo pequeño y no valen para todas las personas. Las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person through menopause, it may help to look for clear information together and prepare for medical appointments in advance, writing down questions and changes, and asking that their autistic needs be accommodated. The evidence is a qualitative study using interviews with 15 autistic and 14 non-autistic adults (assigned female at birth). Both groups lacked information; autistic people also described professionals who did not adapt, anxiety caused by uncertainty, and the lifelong impact of having no diagnosis. Limits: these are the experiences of a small group and do not apply to everyone. Medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person genom klimakteriet kan det hjälpa att söka tydlig information tillsammans och förbereda vårdbesök i förväg, med skrivna frågor och förändringar, och be om att autistiska behov tas hänsyn till. Underlaget är en kvalitativ studie med intervjuer av 15 autistiska och 14 icke-autistiska vuxna (tilldelade kvinnligt kön vid födseln). Båda grupperna saknade information; autistiska personer beskrev också vårdpersonal som inte anpassade sig, oro orsakad av osäkerhet och livslång påverkan av att sakna diagnos. Begränsningar: det är erfarenheter från en liten grupp och gäller inte alla. Medicinska beslut hör hemma hos en kliniker.

title: Efficacy of smartphone-based behavioral activation, assertiveness training, and problem-solving therapy for parenting stress in parents raising autistic children: a multicenter, randomized, open-label, parallel-group trial.
authors: Yamada A, Nakanishi D, Nogimura A, Luo Y, Katsuki F, Ito Y, Imai F, Watanabe N, Sakata M, Akechi T, Horikoshi M, Furukawa TA
abstract: BACKGROUND: Parents of autistic children often experience high levels of stress and depressive symptoms. Although cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is effective in alleviating depression and reducing stress, its delivery requires trained personnel and considerable time, limiting accessibility. Smartphone applications may provide a feasible alternative. This study evaluated the efficacy of smartphone-delivered behavioral activation, assertiveness training, and problem-solving therapy in improving depressive symptoms and reducing stress among parents of autistic children. METHODS: This was an individually randomized, parallel-group, multicenter trial. Eligible participants were parents aged 24 to < 60 years caring for biological children aged 6 to < 16 years diagnosed with autism by child psychiatrists. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to a smartphone-based intervention or a control group that received psychoeducation only. Both groups continued treatment as usual. The intervention consisted of an 8-week smartphone application program delivering behavioral activation, assertiveness training, and problem-solving therapy. The primary endpoint was the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) score at Week 8. Secondary outcomes included Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) scores at Weeks 4 and 8, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Skills Scale scores, presenteeism assessed with the Health and Work Performance Questionnaire (HPQ) at Week 8, and app usage. RESULTS: A total of 63 parents were randomized to the intervention group (n = 31) or control group (n = 32). Changes in PHQ-9 scores from baseline to Week 8 did not differ significantly between groups. No significant between-group differences were observed for GAD-7, CBT Skills, or HPQ presenteeism at Week 8. CONCLUSIONS: The smartphone-based intervention did not demonstrate additional benefits over psychoeducation alone in reducing depressive symptoms. Although symptoms improved in both groups, no significant between-group differences were observed, and the findings should be interpreted cautiously given the limited statistical power. TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was retrospectively registered in UMINCTR (ID UMIN000052319) on October 1, 2023.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a un niño autista y te sientes agotado o con el ánimo bajo, una app de móvil con ejercicios no es necesariamente mejor que recibir buena información. Puedes probarla si te apetece, pero no hace falta sentirte culpable si no te funciona; buscar apoyo profesional sigue siendo válido. La evidencia es un ensayo aleatorizado con 63 madres y padres de niños autistas, que comparó 8 semanas de una app con solo psicoeducación. No hubo diferencias significativas entre los grupos en síntomas depresivos, y los síntomas mejoraron en ambos. Como el grupo era pequeño, los resultados deben leerse con cautela y no valen para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic child and feel worn out or low, a smartphone app with exercises is not necessarily better than good information alone. You can try one if it appeals to you, but there is no need to feel guilty if it does not help; seeking professional support remains valid. The evidence is a randomized trial with 63 parents of autistic children, comparing an 8-week app with psychoeducation only. There were no significant differences between groups in depressive symptoms, and symptoms improved in both. Because the sample was small, the results should be read cautiously and do not apply to every person.
sheet.sv: Om du har ett autistiskt barn och känner dig slutkörd eller nedstämd är en mobilapp med övningar inte nödvändigtvis bättre än bra information. Du kan prova en om du vill, men du behöver inte känna skuld om den inte hjälper; att söka professionellt stöd är fortfarande helt rimligt. Underlaget är en randomiserad studie med 63 föräldrar till autistiska barn, där en app under 8 veckor jämfördes med enbart psykoeducation. Det fanns inga signifikanta skillnader mellan grupperna i depressiva symtom, och symtomen förbättrades i båda. Eftersom gruppen var liten bör resultaten tolkas försiktigt och gäller inte alla.

title: Autistic traits and suicidality in midlife and old age: investigating mediating effects of mental health and social connectedness.
authors: Nuzum E, Medeisyte R, Eshetu A, Hoare S, Corbett A, Ballard C, Hampshire A, O'Nions E, John A, Stewart GR, Stott J
abstract: Suicidality is increased among middle-aged and older autistic adults, but little is known about the underlying factors linking autism with suicidality in midlife and older age. Here we report a cross-sectional observational study of 9,979 adults (76% female) aged 50+ years who completed questionnaires measuring autistic traits, current mental health, social connections and suicidality (suicidal ideation and suicidal self-harm). We use path analysis to explore the relationship between autistic traits and suicidality and the mediating effects of current mental health, social connectedness and male/female sex. Our results find that depression, anxiety, post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), loneliness and social isolation all significantly mediate the relationship between autistic traits and suicidal ideation, with small effect sizes. For suicidal self-harm, male sex, depression, PTSD and social isolation were found to be mediators. We conclude that mental health difficulties and social isolation mediate higher rates of suicidality in 50+-year-olds with high autistic traits. Targeted and individually tailored interventions for people on the autism spectrum across the lifespan are important.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista de 50 años o más, conviene preguntarle con calma y sin juzgar cómo se siente, y prestar atención a la soledad, al aislamiento y a su salud mental. Es un estudio observacional transversal con 9,979 adultos de 50+ años (76% mujeres) que respondieron cuestionarios. Encontró que depresión, ansiedad, PTSD, soledad y aislamiento social se relacionaban con más ideación suicida, con efectos pequeños. Sus límites: no prueba causas, se basa en rasgos autistas medidos por cuestionario y no vale para todas las personas. Si te preocupa a alguien, habla con un profesional sanitario o un servicio de crisis; en peligro inmediato, llama al número de emergencias de tu país.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person aged 50 or over, it helps to ask calmly and without judgement how they are feeling, and to notice loneliness, isolation and mental health needs. This was a cross-sectional observational study of 9,979 adults aged 50+ (76% female) who completed questionnaires. Depression, anxiety, PTSD, loneliness and social isolation were linked to suicidal ideation, with small effect sizes. Its limits: it cannot prove cause, it measured autistic traits by questionnaire, and it does not describe every person. If you are worried about someone, contact a clinician, a health service or a crisis service; in immediate danger, call your country's emergency number.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person som är 50 år eller äldre kan det hjälpa att lugnt och utan dömande fråga hur hen mår, och att vara uppmärksam på ensamhet, isolering och psykisk hälsa. Studien var en tvärsnittsstudie med 9,979 vuxna över 50 år (76% kvinnor) som besvarade frågeformulär. Depression, ångest, PTSD, ensamhet och social isolering hängde samman med självmordstankar, med små effekter. Begränsningar: studien kan inte visa orsak, autistiska drag mättes med frågeformulär och resultaten gäller inte alla. Om du är orolig för någon, kontakta sjukvården, en läkare eller en krisjour; vid akut fara, ring ditt lands nödnummer.

title: Non-Suicidal Self-Injury in Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review of Associated Factors and Management Difficulties.
authors: Coll-Oltra JV, Lambrou-Martínez Á, Camacho-Ruiz JA, Limiñana-Gras RM, Galvez-Sánchez CM
abstract: Background : Non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) is defined as the intentional damage to one's body tissue without suicidal intent and for reasons that are not socially sanctioned. While NSSI has been widely studied in the general population, its clinical correlates and management in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) remain less clearly characterized, and it is often conflated with self-injurious behavior (SIB) described within restricted and repetitive behaviors (RRBs). In individuals with ASD, NSSI may be associated with emotional, behavioral, cognitive, social, medical, and demographic factors, and it differs from SIB typically observed among individuals with severe intellectual disabilities. Methods : A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Studies published between 2000 and 2025 that assessed NSSI in individuals with a formal ASD diagnosis were included. Etiological/clinical correlates, explanatory mechanisms, and management challenges were examined. Sixteen studies were selected from PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science. Findings were synthesized using narrative and thematic approaches. Results: The prevalence of NSSI among individuals with ASD ranged from 24% to 50%. Associated factors included emotion dysregulation (including alexithymia and affective distress), behavioral dysregulation (e.g., impulsivity/hyperactivity and aggression), sensory processing difficulties, communication and social impairments, and medical comorbidities (i.e., gastrointestinal and sleep problems), with preliminary evidence also implicating perinatal factors. NSSI was linked to emotion regulation, sensation seeking, and social communication processes. Early intervention and parental involvement were identified as protective factors. Conclusions : NSSI in ASD is a complex, multifactorial phenomenon frequently linked to emotion-regulation needs. Affective imbalance represents a central-though not exclusive-pathway. The review supports standardized terminology, function-based assessment, and clearer differentiation from SIB/RRBs, with implications for individualized interventions and sustained monitoring in persistent or severe cases. Routine screening for medical and sensory contributors may further improve case management and reduce preventable clinical burden.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista se hace daño a propósito sin intención de morir, conviene preguntarse qué función cumple: puede estar regulando emociones, buscando sensaciones o comunicando algo. Vale la pena revisar también el dolor físico, el sueño, los problemas digestivos y lo sensorial. La implicación de la familia y la ayuda temprana aparecen como protectoras. La evidencia es una revisión sistemática de 16 estudios con personas con diagnóstico formal de autismo; la frecuencia de esta conducta iba de 24% a 50%. Sus límites: los estudios son diversos, algunos hallazgos son preliminares y no describen a cada persona. Si te preocupa, consulta con un profesional sanitario o un servicio de crisis; ante peligro inmediato, llama al número de emergencias de tu país.
sheet.en: If an autistic person hurts themselves on purpose without intending to die, it helps to ask what purpose it serves: they may be regulating emotions, seeking sensation or communicating something. It is also worth checking for physical pain, sleep, digestive and sensory issues. Family involvement and early support appear protective. The evidence is a systematic review of 16 studies of people with a formal autism diagnosis; the frequency of this behaviour ranged from 24% to 50%. Its limits: the studies vary, some findings are preliminary, and they do not describe every person. If you are worried, talk to a clinician, a health service or a crisis service; in immediate danger, call your country's emergency number.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person skadar sig själv med avsikt men utan att vilja dö är det bra att fråga sig vilken funktion det har: personen kan reglera känslor, söka sinnesintryck eller förmedla något. Det är också värt att se över smärta, sömn, magproblem och sensoriska svårigheter. Föräldrars delaktighet och tidigt stöd framstår som skyddande. Underlaget är en systematisk översikt av 16 studier med personer med formell autismdiagnos; förekomsten låg mellan 24% och 50%. Begränsningar: studierna skiljer sig åt, vissa fynd är preliminära och beskriver inte varje person. Är du orolig, kontakta sjukvården, en vårdgivare eller en krisjour; vid akut fara, ring ditt lands nödnummer.

title: Effects of Respite Care on the Quality of Life of Caregivers of Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder in Comparison With Parent Training: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Takatani S, Nakaguchi H, Honda J, Soejima T, Kitao M, Lin Q, Nishimura N
abstract: Parents of children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) experience substantial psychological, social, and physical burdens that negatively affect their quality of life (QoL). Although parent training (PT) is a well-recognized intervention for improving parental well-being, the effectiveness of respite care (RC) remains unclear. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effects of RC-containing programs in improving caregivers' QoL compared to PT programs. Six electronic databases were searched until September 2025 for quantitative studies that examined RC-containing or PT programs targeting caregivers of children with ASD aged 0-18 years. Eligible designs included randomized, quasi-randomized, pre-post, and cross-sectional studies. Outcomes were QoL measured using validated scales. The risk of bias was assessed using RoBANS-2. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted using standardized mean differences (SMD). Five studies met the inclusion criteria for RC-containing programs, and 10 met those for PT programs. RC-containing programs showed a significant moderate effect on caregiver QoL (SMD = 0.45, 95% CI: 0.32-0.58; I² = 1%) with low heterogeneity (I² = 1%, τ² = 0.0057, p = 0.40). PT programs also demonstrated a significant but smaller effect (SMD = 0.31, 95% CI: 0.14-0.47; I² = 42%) with high heterogeneity (I² = 42%, τ² < 0.0001, p = 0.08). Although all included studies in both RC-containing and PT programs showed a high risk of bias, the point estimate suggested a comparative improvement in QoL among caregivers who received RC-containing support. RC-containing programs appear beneficial for improving the QoL of caregivers of children with ASD, and their effects are comparable to those of PT programs. This highlights the importance of recognizing RC as an essential component of family support and of integrating flexible, needs-based RC into clinical practice.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a un niño autista, buscar y pedir descansos organizados (respiro) puede ser una parte valiosa de tu apoyo, junto con la formación para madres y padres. Es un meta-análisis: reunió 5 estudios de programas con respiro y 10 de formación para familias que cuidan a niños autistas de 0-18 años, y ambos mejoraron la calidad de vida de quienes cuidan. Límites: todos los estudios tenían alto riesgo de sesgo, son pocos, y los resultados no valen igual para cada familia. Habla con los servicios de apoyo de tu zona sobre opciones flexibles.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic child, seeking out planned breaks (respite care) can be a worthwhile part of your support, alongside parent training. This is a meta-analysis that pooled 5 studies of programs with respite care and 10 of parent training for caregivers of autistic children aged 0-18, and both were linked to better caregiver quality of life. Limits: all the studies had a high risk of bias, there were few of them, and results will not apply equally to every family. Ask local support services about flexible options.
sheet.sv: Om du ger omsorg till ett autistiskt barn kan planerad avlastning vara en värdefull del av ditt stöd, vid sidan av föräldrautbildning. Det här är en metaanalys som slog ihop 5 studier av program med avlastning och 10 av föräldrautbildning för vårdnadshavare till autistiska barn i åldern 0-18, och båda hängde ihop med bättre livskvalitet hos vårdnadshavarna. Begränsningar: alla studier hade hög risk för bias, de var få, och resultaten gäller inte lika för alla familjer. Fråga lokala stödtjänster om flexibla alternativ.

title: Priorities for change for autistic people across Europe.
authors: Binte Mohd Ikhsan SN, Holt R, Ruigrok A, Man J, Parsons T, Gibbs K, Bullock E, Baranger A, Allison C, Doherty M, Ghosh A, Terčon J, Van den Bosch K, Baron-Cohen S
abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite rising rates of autism prevalence, there remains a pressing need to enhance the quality of life for autistic people in Europe and around the world. METHODS: We conducted the 10 Points for Change survey to identify the 10 most important areas that require improvement for autistic people across the region. Data from 1,709 autistic people, parents/carers and members of autism-related organisations residing within the European Union (EU) and the United Kingdom (UK) were analysed, together with autism-related differences (autistic vs. non-autistic; formal vs. no formal autism diagnosis) and gender differences (male vs. female) in results. RESULTS: Across groups, areas that require the most urgent changes are education, public awareness and understanding of autism, employment, and government funding for autism-specific services. Differences in results between groups reflect their specific needs and experiences. Discrimination is a crucial area for change according to autistic people with formal diagnosis of autism, whereas autistic people without formal diagnosis indicate diagnostic services as a priority for change. According to parents/carers and members of autism-related organisations, changes are also needed to improve social inclusion of autistic people. Other areas of priority for change across all groups include mental healthcare (within top 10 for autistic participants and parents/carers), support with daily living, and post-diagnostic services (the latter two within top 10 for parents/carers and members of autism-related organisations). For some areas, their identification and importance as priorities for change significantly varied with whether participants were autistic or formally diagnosed and autistic participants’ gender. Comparisons across countries with the greatest representation in the survey – Germany, the UK, France, Spain and Poland – revealed consistent priorities. LIMITATIONS: Consideration should be given to issues related to methodology and data availability such as how representative the sample is of countries across the EU and the UK. Autistic people with high support needs might have also been unable to participate directly and responses from carers representing them might not fully reflect their views or provide representative data. CONCLUSION: Change through concerted legislative actions within and across countries in Europe is needed to address the priority areas for change for autistic people.

sheet.es: Si quieres apoyar cambios, empieza por lo que más se repite: educación, comprensión pública del autismo, empleo y financiación de servicios específicos. Puedes preguntar a la persona autista qué le importa más a ella. Se hizo una encuesta a 1,709 personas autistas, familiares o cuidadores y miembros de organizaciones en la Unión Europea y el Reino Unido. Las prioridades variaron: la discriminación pesó más entre quienes tenían diagnóstico formal, y los servicios de diagnóstico entre quienes no lo tenían. Como límites, la muestra puede no representar a todos los países, y las personas con grandes necesidades de apoyo quizá no pudieron participar directamente, así que las respuestas de cuidadores pueden no reflejar sus opiniones.
sheet.en: If you want to support change, start with what came up most often: education, public understanding of autism, employment and funding for autism-specific services. You can ask the autistic person what matters most to them. This was a survey of 1,709 autistic people, parents/carers and members of autism organisations in the European Union and the United Kingdom. Priorities differed: discrimination mattered more to people with a formal diagnosis, and diagnostic services to those without one. As limits, the sample may not represent every country, and autistic people with high support needs may not have been able to take part directly, so carers' answers may not fully reflect their views.
sheet.sv: Om du vill stödja förändring kan du börja med det som nämndes oftast: utbildning, allmänhetens förståelse för autism, arbete och finansiering av autismspecifika tjänster. Du kan fråga den autistiska personen vad som är viktigast för hen. Det här var en enkät med 1,709 autistiska personer, föräldrar/vårdare och medlemmar i autismorganisationer i Europeiska unionen och Storbritannien. Prioriteringarna skilde sig åt: diskriminering vägde tyngre för personer med formell diagnos, och utredning för dem utan. Begränsningar: urvalet kanske inte representerar alla länder, och autistiska personer med stora stödbehov kanske inte kunde delta själva, så vårdares svar kanske inte helt speglar deras åsikter.

title: The effectiveness, cost-effectiveness and experiences of interventions to reduce suicidality for autistic people: A scoping review.
authors: Orr N, Shaw L, Briscoe S, Lawal HM, Martin-Pintado C, Turner M, Thompson Coon J, Garside R, Melendez-Torres GJ
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Autistic people and people with elevated autistic traits are at a higher risk of suicidality (suicidal ideation, suicide plans, suicide attempts) than the general population, with over a third of autistic and possibly autistic people experiencing suicidal ideation, suicidal attempts and/or behaviour. The high prevalence of suicidality has been associated with lack of support and interventions to meet the specific needs of autistic people. This scoping review aimed to better understand the quantity and nature of existing primary research evaluating interventions to support autistic people experiencing suicidality, to inform the commissioning of future primary research. Twenty-seven studies were included: 18 focused on evaluating or developing interventions to reduce suicidality, and nine on evaluating/developing screening procedures to identify autistic people potentially at risk of dying by suicide. Findings suggest researchers are adapting and testing interventions to reduce suicidality in partnership with autistic people, but there is still work needed to enable autistic people to communicate suicidal thoughts and behaviours and develop clinician knowledge and understanding. While the number of completed studies using robust methods such as randomised controlled trials was small, this review indicates a nascent body of research evidence on interventions to reduce suicidality in the autistic population.Lay abstractAutistic, or potentially autistic, people are at higher risk of experiencing suicidality than the general population. This has been linked to a lack of support and treatments that meet the specific needs of autistic people. This scoping review brings together research developing or evaluating strategies that aim to reduce the risk of autistic people dying by suicide. We reviewed 27 studies and found that there is a small but growing number of research projects that involve autistic people to develop treatments to reduce suicidality. For example, we found a study that has adapted and tested safety planning for autistic people. Other research has been testing tools that identify and assess suicidality and understanding healthcare professionals' perspectives on assessing suicidality. More work is needed to develop training for professionals and on adapting assessment tools so that autistic people find it easier to talk about suicidal thoughts. Future research should also aim to be inclusive of the autistic population and ensure gender and cultural diversity in those that participate in research projects. Larger trials will be needed in the future to investigate the effectiveness of treatments for autistic people and build on existing evidence.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista, puedes preguntarle con calma y sin juicio cómo se siente, y ofrecerle formas de comunicarlo que le resulten fáciles, como escribir. Esta revisión de alcance reunió 27 estudios sobre intervenciones y herramientas de detección de la suicidalidad en personas autistas. Encontró un conjunto pequeño pero creciente de investigaciones, algunas hechas junto a personas autistas, como la adaptación de planes de seguridad. Sus límites: pocos ensayos controlados aleatorizados, y aún falta saber qué funciona mejor y formar a los profesionales. Los resultados no valen igual para todas las personas. Busca apoyo profesional con un clínico, un servicio de salud o un servicio de crisis; si hay peligro inmediato, llama al número de emergencias de tu país.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person, you can ask calmly and without judgement how they are feeling, and offer ways to say it that feel easier for them, such as writing. This scoping review gathered 27 studies on interventions and screening tools for suicidality in autistic people. It found a small but growing body of research, some done in partnership with autistic people, such as adapting safety planning. Its limits: few randomised controlled trials, and more work is needed to know what works best and to train professionals. Findings do not apply equally to every person. Please seek support from a clinician, a health service or a crisis service; in immediate danger, call the emergency number of your country.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person kan du fråga lugnt och utan att döma hur hen mår, och erbjuda sätt att berätta som känns enklare, till exempel att skriva. Den här kartläggande översikten samlade 27 studier om insatser och screeningverktyg för suicidalitet hos autistiska personer. Den fann en liten men växande forskning, delvis gjord tillsammans med autistiska personer, till exempel anpassad säkerhetsplanering. Begränsningar: få randomiserade kontrollerade studier, och mer arbete behövs för att veta vad som fungerar bäst och för att utbilda personal. Resultaten gäller inte lika för alla. Sök stöd hos en läkare, hälso- och sjukvården eller en krisjour; vid akut fara, ring ditt lands nödnummer.

title: Scoping review: Facilitators, barriers, and cultural adaptations in the caregiver skills training program for children with developmental concerns.
authors: Montiel-Nava C, Montenegro MC, Ramirez AC, Villarreal V, Murillo Chacko L, Dixon P, Dababnah S
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Autism interventions are predominantly developed in high-income countries, limiting access for families in low- and middle-income countries due to systemic, cultural, and logistical barriers. The Caregiver Skills Training program aims to address this disparity by equipping caregivers with practical skills. This scoping review examines the cultural adaptations, facilitators, and barriers to the implementation of Caregiver Skills Training, focusing on its accessibility, feasibility, and acceptability. A comprehensive search of ERIC, PsycINFO, PubMed, and Web of Science identified eligible studies that reported cultural or linguistic adaptations of Caregiver Skills Training. Forward searches and manual reference checks supplemented the review. Data were extracted using the Cultural Adaptation Checklist framework and analyzed for patterns in adaptation, training, barriers, and facilitators. Seventeen studies across Asia, Africa, Europe, and North America highlighted diverse adaptations in language, content, and delivery methods. Facilitators included community partnerships and task-shifting with non-specialists, while barriers involved logistical challenges, stigma, and resource constraints. Caregiver Skills Training's flexible, culturally responsive framework makes it a viable model for scaling autism interventions globally. Tailored adaptations and strong support systems for facilitators are essential to overcoming systemic challenges and ensuring equitable access in low- and middle-income countries.Lay abstract How the Caregiver Skills Training Program Helps Families Worldwide The Caregiver Skills Training program was designed to help families of children with autism and other developmental challenges in low-resource settings. Caregiver Skills Training empowers parents and caregivers by teaching them practical strategies to improve their child's communication, social interaction, and daily living skills. This program is unique because it does not require a formal diagnosis and is designed to be delivered by trained non-specialists, such as community health workers. A review of 17 studies from different countries examined how the Caregiver Skills Training program was adapted to fit the cultural and practical needs of families in each region. For example, materials were translated, simplified, and paired with visual aids to help parents with lower literacy levels. Non-specialist facilitators helped make the program more accessible, and online or hybrid delivery methods increased participation during the COVID-19 pandemic. However, challenges remain. Families often face barriers like limited transportation, stigma, and lack of Internet access, which can prevent them from fully participating in the program. Facilitators also need more training and support to maintain program quality. Despite these obstacles, Caregiver Skills Training shows promise as a global solution to bridge the gap in autism care, especially in underserved communities. This review highlights the importance of adapting programs like Caregiver Skills Training to meet the unique needs of families worldwide, ensuring that every child has the opportunity to thrive, regardless of where they live.

sheet.es: Si le ofrecen un programa de formación para cuidadores, pregunte si está en su idioma, si usa apoyos visuales y si hay opción en línea o híbrida, porque esto facilitó la participación. También conviene preguntar por transporte y conexión a Internet. Evidencia: una revisión de alcance de 17 estudios de Asia, África, Europa y Norteamérica sobre el programa Caregiver Skills Training y sus adaptaciones culturales. Límites: describe cómo se aplicó el programa, no demuestra qué beneficios tiene para cada niño o niña autista, y los resultados pueden variar según el lugar y la familia.
sheet.en: If you are offered a caregiver skills training program, ask whether it is in your language, uses visual aids, and has an online or hybrid option, since these helped people take part. It is also worth asking about transport and Internet access. Evidence: a scoping review of 17 studies from Asia, Africa, Europe and North America on the Caregiver Skills Training program and how it was culturally adapted. Limits: it describes how the program was delivered, not what benefits it brings to each autistic child, and results may differ by place and family.
sheet.sv: Om du erbjuds ett utbildningsprogram för vårdnadshavare, fråga om det finns på ditt språk, om det använder visuellt stöd och om det finns en digital eller blandad form, eftersom detta underlättade deltagandet. Fråga också om transport och Internetåtkomst. Evidens: en kartläggande översikt av 17 studier från Asien, Afrika, Europa och Nordamerika om programmet Caregiver Skills Training och dess kulturella anpassningar. Begränsningar: den beskriver hur programmet genomfördes, inte vilken nytta det ger varje autistiskt barn, och resultaten kan variera mellan platser och familjer.

title: Sleep and activity patterns in autism.
authors: Weissenkampen JD, Ghorai A, Carneiro TN, Fasolino M, Gehringer BN, Rajan M, Dow HC, Kunatharaju S, Roenneberg T, Sebro R, Rader DJ, Keenan BT, Almasy L, Brodkin ES, Bućan M
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Autism is a heritable neurodevelopmental condition marked by impaired social interaction, repetitive behavior, and co-occurring conditions. Sleep disturbances are common in autism. This study uses low-cost wearable devices to compare sleep, physical activity, and circadian behavior in autistic adults and their non-autistic relatives. We recruited 318 autistic individuals and 130 family members, collecting accelerometer data over 3 weeks (8249 days). Using a data-driven approach, we identified actimetry-derived features associated with autism. We examined 308 traits using the elastic net algorithm and linear mixed effects regressions. We identified 52 actimetry measures associated with autism (area under the curve: 0.812; confidence interval: 0.761-0.862), validated in a test set (area under the curve: 0.756; confidence interval: 0.700-0.813). Both mean and day-to-day variability in several measures (e.g., time spent sedentary, total light physical activity) were associated with autism. In autistic individuals, reduced physical activity during wake was more strongly associated with shorter sleep time than in non-autistic relatives (likelihood ratio: 41.6; p = 1.13e-10). Reduced physical activity in autistic individuals was linked to increased social impairment, as measured by the Social Responsiveness Scale. Long inactivity periods and lower physical activity levels were associated with autism, correlating with less sleep and later sleep onset. Interventional studies are needed to explore if improving sleep and physical activity can improve the quality of life for autistic individuals.Lay AbstractAutistic individuals frequently report problems with their sleep, though what aspects of sleep are most affected is not well understood. In this study, we recruited 318 adult autistic participants without intellectual disability and 130 of their non-autistic family members to measure their sleep, physical activity, and daily routines. Study participants wore accelerometer-based wrist-worn devices over 3 consecutive weeks to record their movement and activity. In total, 154 distinct physical activity, sleep, and behavioral traits were identified from the recordings, 52 of which were found to associate with autism. Many of these traits were related to physical activity, where autistic individuals were more likely to be less active for longer periods and have lower overall physical activity levels. Long periods of inactivity also associated with less sleep, with a stronger association in those with autism. For example, for every hour of inactivity, autistic participants had on average ~23 min less of sleep compared to ~17 min in their family members. Autistic individuals with lower levels of physical activity showed higher social impairment as measured by the Social Responsiveness Scale. Overall, lower physical activity may impair sleep and worsen the core features of autism. Interventional studies aimed to increase physical activity may improve the quality of life of autistic individuals.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista duerme poco, puede ser útil observar cuánto se mueve durante el día y si pasa muchas horas seguidas sin actividad. Probar con calma pequeñas pausas para moverse, a su ritmo y según sus gustos, puede ser una idea. Este estudio observacional usó pulseras con acelerómetro durante 3 semanas en 318 adultos autistas sin discapacidad intelectual y 130 familiares no autistas. Las personas autistas tendían a tener menos actividad y menos sueño. Sus límites: no prueba que moverse más mejore el sueño, y no sirve como regla para cada persona. Los autores piden estudios de intervención.
sheet.en: If an autistic person sleeps little, it may help to notice how much they move during the day and whether they spend long stretches inactive. Gently trying short movement breaks, at their pace and matching their interests, could be an idea. This observational study used wrist accelerometers for 3 weeks with 318 autistic adults without intellectual disability and 130 non-autistic relatives. Autistic participants tended to be less active and to sleep less. Limits: it does not show that moving more improves sleep, and it is not a rule for every person. The authors call for intervention studies.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person sover lite kan det vara bra att lägga märke till hur mycket hen rör sig under dagen och om hen är inaktiv under långa perioder. Att lugnt prova korta rörelsepauser, i egen takt och efter intresse, kan vara en idé. Denna observationsstudie använde accelerometrar på handleden under 3 veckor hos 318 autistiska vuxna utan intellektuell funktionsnedsättning och 130 icke-autistiska släktingar. De autistiska deltagarna var i genomsnitt mindre aktiva och sov mindre. Begränsningar: studien visar inte att mer rörelse ger bättre sömn och är ingen regel för alla. Författarna efterlyser interventionsstudier.

title: "My Sensory Experiences Tool": A Neurodiversity-Affirming Therapeutic Tool to Support the Sensory Challenges and Preferences of Autistic Children and Adults.
authors: Ashburner J, Tomkins V, Downing C, Reitberg E, Hill J, Copley J, Bobir N
abstract: Background My Sensory Experiences Tool (MYSET) is a picture-based card-sort tool designed to support conversations with autistic people about their sensory experiences with a view to enabling better understanding and accommodation of their sensory challenges. Purpose This study aimed firstly to describe MYSET and the considerations that guided the development of the tool, and secondly to explore the perceptions of autistic people, family members and professional practitioners of the usefulness of MYSET and ways it could be improved. Method We gathered the perspectives of 18 professional practitioners, five autistic individuals and four family members through semi-structured interviews and focus groups. The data was analysed through inductive content analysis.
