Findings The participants perceived that MYSET enabled the gathering of individualised qualitative information about the person's sensory experiences. MYSET was also perceived to be accessible, including people ranging in age from 5 years to adulthood and people with abilities ranging from mild intellectual disability to average/high IQ. The tool facilitates conversations about the links between the person's sensory responses and their daily life experiences. A key perceived outcome of MYSET was the enhancement of others' capacity to understand and accommodate the autistic person's sensory challenges. The tool was refined in response to participant feedback. Conclusion MYSET enables the gathering of detailed, individualised qualitative data on the sensory experiences of an autistic person and the collaborative design of accommodations that are compatible with their lifestyle.

sheet.es: Si quieres hablar con una persona autista sobre sus experiencias sensoriales, una herramienta de tarjetas con imágenes como MYSET puede ayudar a empezar la conversación y a pensar juntos en adaptaciones para su día a día. Es un estudio con entrevistas y grupos de conversación en el que participaron 18 profesionales, cinco personas autistas y cuatro familiares; opinaron que la herramienta era útil y accesible, y se mejoró con sus comentarios. Sus límites: la muestra es pequeña, recoge percepciones y no mide si las adaptaciones mejoran la vida de las personas. No sirve igual para todas.
sheet.en: If you want to talk with an autistic person about their sensory experiences, a picture card-sort tool like MYSET can help start the conversation and plan adaptations together that fit their daily life. This was a study using interviews and focus groups with 18 professional practitioners, five autistic individuals and four family members; they saw the tool as useful and accessible, and it was refined using their feedback. Its limits: the group was small, it captured opinions, and it did not measure whether the adaptations improved people's lives. It will not suit everyone equally.
sheet.sv: Vill du prata med en autistisk person om hens sensoriska upplevelser kan ett bildbaserat korttillverktyg som MYSET hjälpa dig att inleda samtalet och tillsammans planera anpassningar som passar vardagen. Studien använde intervjuer och fokusgrupper med 18 yrkespersoner, fem autistiska personer och fyra anhöriga; de såg verktyget som användbart och tillgängligt, och det förbättrades utifrån deras synpunkter. Begränsningar: gruppen var liten, studien fångade åsikter och mätte inte om anpassningarna förbättrade människors liv. Verktyget passar inte alla lika bra.

title: Cultural Adaptation of RUBI Intervention with Korean Families (K-RUBI): A Mixed Method Study.
authors: Lee JD, Kang VY, Kim G, Jung S, Joo S, Kim H, Son J, Bearss K
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Challenging behaviors of young autistic children remain a major parenting challenge for many of their family members, including caregivers. Caregivers from underrepresented cultural or linguistic backgrounds may experience exacerbated difficulties related to challenging behaviors due to limited access to culturally sustaining and responsive interventions. Evidence-based behavior parent training programs, such as RUBI, are highly effective in increasing caregivers' capacity in preventing and responding to these behaviors in naturalistic settings using behavior analytic principles. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to examine the effectiveness, acceptability, and feasibility of the culturally adapted RUBI program with underserved families. We conduct a convergent mixed-methods study using a pilot randomized controlled trial with a waitlist control group and focus group interviews with 31 Korean families of young children with or suspected of autism. The Korean RUBI underwent rigorous cultural adaptation using the Cultural Adaptation Checklist, including the use of multiple community advisory boards to inform cultural adaptation. Both quantitative and qualitative findings revealed significant improvements in parents' confidence and knowledge in behavioral principles and decrease in severity of challenging behaviors, which suggest clinical utility of RUBI in an underrepresented, low-resourced community. A culturally adapted intervention for a different population can be perceived as a newly constructed intervention. This study provides insight on the systematic process of cultural adaptation of an established autism intervention and effectiveness, feasibility, and acceptability of RUBI.

sheet.es: Si cuidas de un niño autista pequeño y te cuesta entender o responder a conductas que te preocupan, un programa de formación para familias adaptado a su cultura e idioma puede ayudarte a ganar confianza y conocimientos. Es un ensayo piloto aleatorizado con grupo de lista de espera y grupos focales, con 31 familias coreanas de niños autistas o con sospecha de autismo. Las familias informaron más confianza y conocimientos, y menor gravedad de esas conductas. Es un estudio pequeño, de un solo grupo cultural, y no demuestra que funcione igual en todas las familias. Habla con los profesionales que os acompañan antes de decidir.
sheet.en: If you care for a young autistic child and want help understanding and responding to behaviours that worry you, a parent training programme adapted to your culture and language may help you feel more confident and knowledgeable. This was a pilot randomized trial with a waitlist control group, plus focus group interviews, with 31 Korean families of young children who are autistic or suspected of being autistic. Families reported more confidence and knowledge, and less severe challenging behaviours. It is a small study of one cultural group, so it cannot show the programme works the same way for every family. Talk with the professionals who support you before deciding.
sheet.sv: Om du tar hand om ett litet autistiskt barn och vill få stöd att förstå och bemöta beteenden som oroar dig, kan ett föräldraprogram anpassat till din kultur och ditt språk öka ditt självförtroende och dina kunskaper. Studien var en randomiserad pilotstudie med väntelistkontroll samt fokusgruppintervjuer med 31 koreanska familjer med små barn som är autistiska eller misstänks vara det. Familjerna rapporterade mer självförtroende och kunskap samt lägre svårighetsgrad på beteendena. Studien är liten och gäller en enda kulturell grupp, så den visar inte att programmet fungerar likadant för alla familjer. Prata med dem som stöttar er innan ni bestämmer er.

title: Gastrointestinal, Behaviour and Anxiety Outcomes in Autistic Children Following an Open Label, Randomised Pilot Study of Synbiotics vs Synbiotics and Gut-Directed Hypnotherapy.
authors: Mitchell LK, Heussler HS, Burgess CJ, Rehman A, Steinert RE, Davies PSW
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Alterations of the microbiome-gut-brain (MGB) axis have been associated with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and disorders of gut-brain interaction (DGBI). DGBI are highly prevalent in autistic children and are associated with worsening behaviour and anxiety. Treatments such as probiotics, prebiotics and gut-directed hypnotherapy (GDH) have shown efficacy in improving gut symptoms in children. The primary objective of the study was to compare changes in gastrointestinal (GI) scores following a 12-week intervention of synbiotics (prebiotic + probiotic) +/- GDH with a follow-up at 24 weeks. Secondary objectives included changes in behavioural and anxiety symptoms, while changes in gut microbiome composition were assessed as an exploratory objective. Children diagnosed with ASD aged 5.00-10.99 years (n = 40) were recruited and randomised (1:1) to a 12-week intervention of either synbiotics (SYN group) or synbiotics + GDH (COM group). Both the SYN and COM group experienced significant reductions in total GI scores post-intervention and at follow-up (p < 0.001), with no superiority of the COM treatment over the SYN treatment. The COM group showed beneficial reductions in anxiety scores (p = 0.002) and irritability behaviours (p < 0.001) which were not present in the SYN group. At follow-up, only those in the COM group maintained significant reductions in GI pain scores (p < 0.001). There were significant changes in gut microbiota such as increases in Bifidobacterium animalis and Dialister in both groups over time. In conclusion, synbiotics with or without GDH may help support standard care for autistic children who suffer comorbid DGBI. The trial was prospectively registered at clinicialtrials.gov on 16 November 2020 (NCTO4639141).

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija autista tiene molestias de tripa frecuentes, puede valer la pena comentar con su pediatra o gastroenterólogo opciones como los simbióticos o la hipnoterapia dirigida al intestino, siempre como apoyo al cuidado habitual. Es un estudio piloto aleatorizado y abierto con 40 niños autistas de 5.00-10.99 años, durante 12 semanas. Ambos grupos redujeron sus puntuaciones digestivas; añadir hipnoterapia no fue mejor en ese aspecto, pero sí se vio menos ansiedad e irritabilidad solo en ese grupo. Límites: muestra pequeña, sin ocultar el tratamiento, y no sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If your autistic child has frequent tummy troubles, it may be worth asking your paediatrician or gastroenterologist about options such as synbiotics or gut-directed hypnotherapy, as a support alongside usual care. This was an open-label, randomised pilot study of 40 autistic children aged 5.00-10.99 years, over 12 weeks. Both groups had lower gut scores; adding hypnotherapy was not better for that, but only that group showed reduced anxiety and irritability. Limits: small sample, no blinding, and the results are not a rule for every child.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn ofta har magproblem kan det vara värt att fråga barnläkare eller gastroenterolog om till exempel synbiotika eller magfokuserad hypnoterapi, som ett stöd vid sidan av vanlig vård. Det var en öppen, randomiserad pilotstudie med 40 autistiska barn i åldern 5.00-10.99 år under 12 veckor. Båda grupperna fick lägre magpoäng; hypnoterapi var inte bättre för det, men bara den gruppen hade minskad oro och irritabilitet. Begränsningar: litet urval, ingen blindning, och resultaten gäller inte alla barn.

title: A PhotoVoice Study with Canadian Immigrant and Racialized Family Caregivers of Children on the Autism Spectrum.
authors: Sam J, Ahmad F, Khalaf T, Sathies A, Dada S
journal: International journal of environmental research and public health
abstract: Background Immigrant and racialized families raising children on the autism spectrum in Canada navigate intersecting inequities shaped by racism, language barriers, immigration status, and fragmented health and education systems. Yet their perspectives remain underrepresented in autism and health policy research. Methods Guided by the socioecological and critical social science lens, this community-based participatory study employed a PhotoVoice approach in partnership with SMILE Canada-Support Services. Ten immigrant and/or racialized family caregivers from the Greater Toronto area participated in four in-person sessions involving ethical training, guided photo-taking, group-based reflections, and collaborative theme refinement. The data included 38 participant-generated photographs, narratives, and an audio-recorded final group discussion. Results Seven interrelated themes were identified: (1) family support and child needs; (2) physical and emotional burden on caregivers; (3) school support or its missingness; (4) stigma and discrimination; (5) overall journey with barriers; (6) transitions and uncertainty; and (7) two sides of a coin: isolation and strength, loneliness and hope. Caregivers highlighted extensive invisible labor, exclusionary schooling, financial and systemic barriers, and cumulative stress. Simultaneously, they articulated resilience, mutual support, and a strong sense of collective responsibility. The PhotoVoice process itself was experienced as validating, unifying, and empowering, with participants expressing readiness to disseminate findings through exhibitions, school boards, universities, and policy-engagement initiatives. Conclusions Caregiving among immigrant and racialized families is both a profound act of love and a site of structural injustice. Centering on caregivers as co-researchers and knowledge holders reveals urgent needs for equity-oriented autism policies and culturally responsive, accessible support systems in Canada.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a un niño autista y vives con barreras de idioma, racismo o sistemas fragmentados, el cansancio y el aislamiento no son un fallo tuyo. Buscar a otras familias que compartan tu situación y pedir a la escuela apoyos concretos puede aliviar la carga. Es un estudio participativo con PhotoVoice: diez cuidadores inmigrantes o racializados del área de Toronto tomaron fotos y conversaron en cuatro sesiones. Contaron trabajo invisible, estigma, escuelas excluyentes, y también fortaleza y apoyo mutuo. Es un grupo pequeño de una sola zona de Canadá, así que no describe a todas las familias, y no mide qué ayuda funciona.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic child and face language barriers, racism or fragmented systems, your exhaustion and isolation are not your failing. Finding other families in similar situations and asking the school for specific supports may ease the load. This was a participatory PhotoVoice study: ten immigrant or racialized caregivers in the Greater Toronto area took photos and talked together over four sessions. They described invisible labour, stigma, exclusionary schooling, and also strength and mutual support. It is a small group from one area of Canada, so it does not describe every family, and it did not test which supports work.
sheet.sv: Om du tar hand om ett autistiskt barn och möter språkbarriärer, rasism eller splittrade system är din trötthet och ensamhet inte ditt fel. Att hitta andra familjer i liknande situation och be skolan om konkret stöd kan lätta bördan. Det var en deltagande PhotoVoice-studie: tio invandrade eller rasifierade vårdnadshavare i Stortorontoområdet tog bilder och samtalade vid fyra träffar. De beskrev osynligt arbete, stigma, utestängande skola, men också styrka och ömsesidigt stöd. Gruppen är liten och från ett område i Kanada, så studien beskriver inte alla familjer och testade inte vilket stöd som fungerar.

title: Feasibility of the ICF CoreSets for Autism Strengths and Needs Assessment in NHS diagnostic services in England: protocol for a randomised pilot trial.
authors: Day M, Scargill K, Poole D, Kellar I, Young TA, Bölte S, Clarke S, Lodge KM, Woods A, Freeth M
abstract: Introduction There are approximately 700 000 autistic people in the UK, and autism is increasingly being diagnosed in adulthood. Diagnosis on its own does not provide adequate information to plan post-diagnostic support for autistic people, and clinicians often plan support without the use of validated standardised tools which may exacerbate inequities in care. This study will evaluate a novel strengths and needs assessment, based on the WHO's International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health CoreSet for Autism, for use in adult diagnostic services immediately on receipt of an autism diagnosis. Potential issues, including the length of the assessment, timing of delivery and selection bias, will be explored as part of the trial process evaluation. Methods and analysis A two-arm, multisite, randomised pilot trial design will be used to evaluate the ICF CoreSets for Autism Strengths and Needs Assessment in three diagnostic services in England. A total of 72 newly diagnosed autistic adults will be recruited across the three sites over a 6-month period and randomised into an assessment group (strengths and needs assessment plus standard care) and a treatment as usual group (standard care only). The assessment group will receive a summary report of their strengths and needs on completion of the assessment. Both groups will complete measures of mental health and quality of life at baseline and 3 months follow-up (Patient Health Questionnaire-9, Generalised Anxiety Disorder questionnaire-7, Recovering Quality of Life questionnaire-10, EuroQoL-5D). Acceptability and feasibility will be measured for the strengths and needs assessment and for trial procedures using standardised measures, progression criteria and qualitative data from clinician focus groups and interviews with a subsample of autistic participants. The study design and procedures are being co-produced with an autistic advisor/patient and public involvement lead and with a steering group of autistic adults. Ethics and dissemination This study was reviewed by the East Midlands-Nottingham 2 Research Ethics Committee and was given Health Research Authority approval on 18 March 2025 (REC reference:25/EM/0041). The results will be disseminated via reports to the funder (NIHR), a peer-reviewed journal paper and academic conferences. We will email a summary report of findings to study participants and will invite participants to an information dissemination event at the end of the study. Links to reports and a lay summary will be provided on the research group's website: https://sharl.sites.sheffield.ac.uk/home TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: ISRCTN10283350.

sheet.es: Tras un diagnóstico, pregunte si el servicio ofrece una evaluación de fortalezas y necesidades, para planificar apoyos a medida y no solo con el diagnóstico. Este es el protocolo de un ensayo piloto aleatorizado, aún sin resultados: se prevé reclutar a 72 personas autistas adultas recién diagnosticadas en tres servicios de Inglaterra. Un grupo recibirá la evaluación más la atención habitual y otro solo la atención habitual. Se medirá si la evaluación es aceptable y viable, con participación de personas autistas en el diseño. Aún no sabemos si ayuda, y los resultados no valen para todas las personas.
sheet.en: After a diagnosis, ask whether the service offers a strengths and needs assessment, so support can be planned around the person and not only the diagnosis. This is the protocol for a randomised pilot trial, so there are no results yet: it plans to recruit 72 newly diagnosed autistic adults across three services in England. One group gets the assessment plus standard care, the other standard care only. The study checks whether the assessment is acceptable and feasible, and autistic people helped design it. We do not yet know if it helps, and findings will not apply to everyone.
sheet.sv: Fråga efter en diagnos om verksamheten erbjuder en kartläggning av styrkor och behov, så att stödet kan planeras utifrån personen och inte bara diagnosen. Detta är protokollet för en randomiserad pilotstudie och det finns ännu inga resultat: man planerar att rekrytera 72 nydiagnostiserade autistiska vuxna vid tre verksamheter i England. En grupp får kartläggningen plus vanlig vård, den andra enbart vanlig vård. Studien undersöker om kartläggningen är acceptabel och genomförbar, och autistiska personer har varit med och utformat den. Vi vet ännu inte om den hjälper, och resultaten gäller inte alla.

title: Assessment accommodations for autistic learners in South African schools: Stakeholder perspectives.
authors: Nell Y, Kritzinger A, Graham MA, Eccles R
abstract: Background Autistic learners benefit from demonstrating academic knowledge with the help of assessment accommodations, guided by South African examination policies, such as the National Policy Pertaining to the Conduct, Administration and Management of Examinations and Assessment for the National Senior Certificate Examination . However, stakeholder perspectives on accommodations remain under-explored. Objectives This study explored stakeholder perspectives (autistic adults, caregivers, educators, psychologists, speech-language therapists and occupational therapists) on assessment accommodations for autistic learners in South African schools. Method A web-based questionnaire was distributed nationally to professionals and caregivers ( n = 92). Quantitative data were analysed descriptively, and qualitative responses were thematically coded. Results Stakeholders reported a persistent policy-practice disconnect, with educators lacking the knowledge of accommodation policies, as well as the training to implement accommodations, particularly for autistic learners. Similarly, current policies do not adequately accommodate the needs related to sensory regulation and anxiety. Considerable variability emerged in accommodation preferences, reflecting both the heterogeneity of autistic learners and the differences across stakeholder groups. Respondents also prioritised universal design elements such as simplified language, redundancy and clearer assessment layouts, which are not currently considered in South African policy. Overall, findings highlight the need for expanded and individually tailored assessment accommodations informed by diverse stakeholder input. Conclusion The findings highlight a disconnect between policy and practice. Broader autism-specific accommodations are crucial to support equitable assessment conditions in South African schools, especially for learners with sensory and communication challenges. Contribution This study provides insight into stakeholder experiences and suggests that current assessment policies may inadvertently exclude autistic learners. The findings support the need for inclusive, contextually relevant assessment strategies. The contribution aligns with the focus of the journal on disability inclusion by advancing evidence-based recommendations that promote full participation of neurodivergent learners in education systems, particularly within under-resourced and diverse settings.

sheet.es: Antes de la próxima evaluación, hable con el centro educativo sobre ajustes concretos: lenguaje más sencillo, instrucciones repetidas de otra forma, un formato de examen más claro y apoyo para la regulación sensorial y la ansiedad. Pregunte qué prefiere la persona estudiante, porque las preferencias varían mucho. La evidencia es un cuestionario en línea en Sudáfrica con personas autistas adultas, cuidadores y profesionales (n = 92). Señala que el profesorado conoce poco las políticas y tiene poca formación. Sus límites: la muestra es pequeña, se basa en opiniones y no prueba qué ajuste funciona mejor para cada estudiante.
sheet.en: Before the next assessment, talk with the school about specific accommodations: simpler language, instructions repeated in another way, a clearer test layout, and support for sensory regulation and anxiety. Ask the learner what they prefer, since preferences varied widely. The evidence is an online questionnaire in South Africa with autistic adults, caregivers and professionals (n = 92). It found educators often know little about accommodation policies and have limited training. Its limits: the sample is small, it relies on opinions, and it does not show which accommodation works best for any individual learner.
sheet.sv: Inför nästa bedömning kan du prata med skolan om konkreta anpassningar: enklare språk, instruktioner som upprepas på ett annat sätt, tydligare provlayout och stöd för sensorisk reglering och oro. Fråga eleven vad hen föredrar, eftersom önskemålen varierade mycket. Underlaget är ett webbaserat frågeformulär i Sydafrika med autistiska vuxna, vårdnadshavare och yrkesverksamma (n = 92). Det visade att lärare ofta känner till policyerna dåligt och har begränsad utbildning. Begränsningar: urvalet är litet, bygger på åsikter och visar inte vilken anpassning som fungerar bäst för en enskild elev.

title: Targeting intolerance of uncertainty in young children diagnosed with autism: A randomized controlled trial of a parent-mediated group intervention.
authors: Ong CSY, Rodgers J, Cooper MN, Dempsey Z, Eaton R, Haines K, Kuzminski R, Magiati I, Maybery MT, Uljarević M, Wray J, Whitehouse AJO, Alvares GA
abstract: Background Young children diagnosed with autism experience high rates of co-occurring anxiety, with uncertainty-related concerns commonly reported. This randomized controlled trial investigated an 8-week parent-mediated group anxiety intervention, "Coping with Uncertainty in Everyday Situations" (CUES-Junior©). Methods Parents of 4-7-year-old children diagnosed with autism and experiencing uncertainty-related anxiety were recruited. The primary outcome was change from baseline in blinded assessor ratings of child responses to uncertainty and impact on family, measured post-intervention and 2-month follow-up. Secondary outcomes were parent-reported child anxiety and intolerance of uncertainty (IU), parental IU and mental health, parenting sense of competence, along with intervention feasibility and acceptability. Results Sixty-four children were randomized to CUES-Junior© ( n = 33) or waitlist ( n = 31); five families withdrew post-randomization. Immediately post-intervention, significantly more CUES-Junior© participants were rated as clinically improved from baseline in child responses to uncertainty (OR = 34.48; 95% CI = 1.72-690.04, p = 0.02) and in family impact (OR = 8.99; 95% CI = 1.52-53.05, p = 0.02) compared to waitlist. Significant improvements were also observed in parent-reported child IU and parenting satisfaction, favoring CUES-Junior©. At subsequent 2-month follow-up, CUES-Junior© participants showed sustained improvements in the impact of uncertainty on children, and parental ratings of child IU and anxiety, parenting sense of competence, and parental stress, compared to baseline. The program was feasible to administer and acceptable to parents. Conclusions CUES-Junior© had an immediate treatment effect on child responses to uncertain situations and impact on families, with maintained improvements observed at follow-up. This novel mechanism-targeted and autism-informed program holds promise for addressing early uncertainty-related anxiety in young children diagnosed with autism.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija autista de 4 a 7 años se angustia ante lo imprevisto, puede ser útil preguntar a profesionales por programas grupales para familias que trabajen la incertidumbre. Mientras tanto, anticipar los cambios con calma puede ayudar. Evidencia: ensayo controlado aleatorizado de 8 semanas con 64 niños, en el que el programa CUES-Junior© mejoró las respuestas ante la incertidumbre y el impacto familiar frente a la lista de espera, con mejoras mantenidas a los 2 meses. Límites: muestra pequeña, intervalos de confianza muy amplios, seguimiento corto, y no sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If your autistic child aged 4 to 7 gets very distressed by the unexpected, it may be worth asking professionals about parent group programmes that work on uncertainty. Meanwhile, calmly preparing your child for changes may help. Evidence: an 8-week randomized controlled trial with 64 children, where the CUES-Junior© programme improved responses to uncertainty and impact on the family compared with a waitlist, with gains kept at 2 months. Limits: small sample, very wide confidence intervals, short follow-up, and results are not a rule for every child or family.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn i åldern 4 till 7 år blir mycket stressat av det oväntade kan det vara värt att fråga yrkespersoner om föräldragrupper som arbetar med osäkerhet. Under tiden kan det hjälpa att lugnt förbereda barnet på förändringar. Evidens: en randomiserad kontrollerad studie på 8 veckor med 64 barn, där programmet CUES-Junior© förbättrade barnens reaktioner på osäkerhet och påverkan på familjen jämfört med väntelista, med bibehållna förbättringar efter 2 månader. Begränsningar: litet urval, mycket breda konfidensintervall, kort uppföljning, och resultaten gäller inte alla barn eller familjer.

title: Double-blind, sham-controlled, pilot study of trigeminal nerve stimulation for autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Han JH, Kim YR, Lee Y, Park Y, Kim D, Bong G, Yoo HJ
journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
abstract: Trigeminal nerve stimulation (TNS) is a minimal-risk, noninvasive neuromodulation method with growing evidence of efficacy across psychiatric conditions. However, its safety and potential effects in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) remain underexplored. This exploratory pilot study aimed primarily to evaluate the safety and tolerability, and secondarily to explore changes in ASD-related symptoms - including impairments in social communication and reciprocity, attention, executive functioning, emotional regulation, sleep, and sensory processing - in children with ASD, and to examine associated changes using quantitative electroencephalography (qEEG). This double-blind, sham-controlled, randomized exploratory pilot trial enrolled 29 children aged 7-12 years with ASD. The participants were randomized to receive 28 nightly sessions of active or sham TNS over 4 weeks. At baseline and week 4, we assessed safety, clinical outcomes and Clinical Global Impression scales, in addition to analyzing qEEG band power. No serious adverse events were observed, and TNS was well tolerated. Exploratory analyses showed nominal between-group differences (unadjusted) favoring the TNS group in maladaptive behavior (Vineland-II: 1.38 vs 0.08; p = .017) and social reciprocity (Social Responsiveness Scale-2: 12.07 vs -1.43; p = .025). Exploratory qEEG analyses revealed decreased gamma/high-frequency and increased alpha power in the left frontal and parietal regions, changes that significantly correlated with improvements in social (r = -0.917; p = .001) and overall (r = -0.680; p = .030) functioning. TNS was safe and showed preliminary evidence of potential benefits in improving behavioral and social functioning in children with ASD. Larger trials are required to confirm these findings. Clinical trial registration information: http://clinicaltrials.gov/; NCT06233279.

sheet.es: Por ahora, esta técnica no es algo que probar en casa: si le interesa, hable antes con el equipo clínico que acompaña a su hijo o hija. Es un ensayo piloto, aleatorizado y con doble ciego, con 29 niños y niñas autistas de 7-12 años. Recibieron 28 sesiones nocturnas de estimulación del nervio trigémino real o simulada durante 4 semanas. No hubo eventos adversos graves y se toleró bien. Los resultados sobre conducta y reciprocidad social fueron exploratorios. Límites: muestra pequeña, resultados preliminares y no ajustados; hacen falta estudios más grandes y cada persona es distinta.
sheet.en: For now, this technique is not something to try at home: if you are curious, talk first with the clinical team supporting your child. This was a randomized, double-blind pilot trial with 29 autistic children aged 7-12 years. They received 28 nightly sessions of real or sham trigeminal nerve stimulation over 4 weeks. No serious adverse events were seen and it was well tolerated. Findings on behaviour and social reciprocity were exploratory. Limits: small sample, preliminary and unadjusted results; larger studies are needed, and every person is different.
sheet.sv: Just nu är tekniken inget att prova hemma: om du är nyfiken, prata först med teamet som stöttar ditt barn. Det var en randomiserad, dubbelblind pilotstudie med 29 autistiska barn i åldern 7-12 år. De fick 28 nattliga sessioner med verklig eller låtsad stimulering av trigeminusnerven under 4 veckor. Inga allvarliga biverkningar sågs och den tolererades väl. Resultaten om beteende och social ömsesidighet var explorativa. Begränsningar: litet urval, preliminära och ojusterade resultat; större studier behövs, och alla människor är olika.

title: Procedural Support for Neurodivergent Children During Medical Procedures: A Scoping Review.
authors: Takashima M, Robertson H, Plummer K, Kotzur C, Wesley A, Donaldson A, Hjelmgren H, Stålberg A, Burgess L, Friedman AJ, Mimmo L, Choi J, Barker N, Gooley S, Walsh N, Cobham VE, Ullman A
journal: Clinical child and family psychology review
abstract: Neurodivergent children face unique challenges during medical procedures due to distinct sensory processing patterns and communication difficulties. Evidence-based interventions for procedural pain/distress may inadequately address their specific needs, leading to undertreated distress and negative healthcare experiences.Following Joanna Briggs Institute methodology, we conducted comprehensive searches across six databases on January 10, 2025, for studies published 2014-2025 focusing on neurodivergent children (0-21 years) undergoing medical procedures. Two independent reviewers screened studies and extracted data, with results presented as a narrative synthesis with evidence mapping.From 14,393 initial records, 144 studies met the inclusion criteria. Most studies (n = 121, 84.0%) focused on autism spectrum disorder, with limited representation of other neurodivergent diagnoses. Hospital outpatient settings (n = 93, 64.6%) and dental specialty (n = 50, 34.7%) were most commonly studied. The most frequently used support strategies were visit preparation and support (n = 61, 42.4%), pharmacological agents (n = 48, 33.3%), and patient care plans/pathways (n = 43, 29.9%). Few studies used validated pain and distress assessment tools, with only 4.2% (n = 6) reporting child-reported pain measures. While 74.3% (n = 107) of studies reported distress outcomes, these were primarily observational rather than validated measures.Findings highlight significant gaps in procedural support strategies for neurodivergent children, particularly for conditions beyond autism. There is a critical need for research using validated pain and distress measures, especially those capturing the child's perspective. Future studies should prioritise diverse neurodivergent populations, incorporate structured assessment tools, and evaluate tailored interventions across wider clinical settings.

title: Digital Health Interventions for Sexual Health Education Among Adolescents With Autism Spectrum Disorder: Scoping Review.
authors: Rahmadani E, Ahmed IA
abstract: Background Adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) experience persistent barriers to accessing comprehensive and developmentally appropriate sexual health education. Conventional curricula often fail to reflect their cognitive, social, and communication needs, increasing vulnerability to misinformation and sexual exploitation. Digital health interventions offer a promising avenue to deliver tailored, interactive, and accessible learning experiences for adolescents with ASD. Objective This scoping review aimed to map and synthesize the evidence on digital health interventions designed to provide sexual health education to adolescents with ASD. Methods A scoping review was conducted using Arksey and O'Malley's framework, refined with Joanna Briggs Institute guidance and reported following the PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews) standards. In total, 6 databases (ie, PubMed, Scopus, CINAHL, ERIC, PsycINFO, and Web of Science) were searched from 2010 to June 2025. Eligible studies involved adolescents aged 10 to 19 years with ASD, used digital platforms to deliver sexual or reproductive health education, and were published in English. Two reviewers independently screened, extracted, and synthesized data using descriptive and thematic approaches. Results A total of 16 studies met the inclusion criteria. Most studies were conducted in high-income countries and delivered content through video-based, web-based, or mobile modalities. Key features associated with positive learning outcomes included personalization, strong visual interactivity, and caregiver involvement. Reported improvements focused on sexual knowledge, behavioral understanding, and user acceptability. However, methodological limitations were common, including small and nonrepresentative samples, a lack of standardized outcome measures, and minimal gender-specific or culturally adapted content. Notably, co-design with autistic adolescents and implementation in low- and middle-income countries was scarce. Conclusions Digital health interventions demonstrate promising early effectiveness for delivering inclusive, developmentally appropriate sexual health education to adolescents with ASD. To advance this field, future research must strengthen methodological rigor, include diverse and gender-balanced populations, use participatory design, and ensure cultural adaptability to support equitable access globally.

sheet.es: Si quiere apoyar la educación sexual de un adolescente autista, pruebe materiales digitales como vídeos, webs o apps que sean visuales, interactivos y adaptados a su manera de aprender, y acompáñelo usted. Esta revisión de alcance reunió 16 estudios con adolescentes autistas de 10 a 19 años; los programas con personalización, interactividad visual y participación de cuidadores se asociaron con mejoras en conocimiento, comprensión de conductas y aceptación. Pero los estudios eran pequeños, poco representativos, usaban medidas distintas y casi no contaron con adolescentes autistas en el diseño. No es una regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you want to support an autistic teenager's sexual health education, try digital materials such as videos, websites or apps that are visual, interactive and fitted to how they learn, and be involved yourself. This scoping review gathered 16 studies with autistic adolescents aged 10 to 19; programmes with personalization, strong visual interactivity and caregiver involvement were linked to better knowledge, behavioural understanding and acceptability. However, the studies were small, not representative, used different outcome measures, and rarely involved autistic adolescents in design. It is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du vill stötta en autistisk tonårings sexualundervisning kan du prova digitalt material som filmer, webbplatser eller appar som är visuella, interaktiva och anpassade till hur personen lär sig, och själv vara delaktig. Den här kartläggande översikten samlade 16 studier med autistiska ungdomar i åldern 10 till 19 år. Program med personanpassning, tydlig visuell interaktivitet och delaktiga vårdnadshavare kopplades till bättre kunskap, förståelse av beteenden och acceptans. Studierna var dock små, inte representativa, använde olika mått och involverade sällan autistiska ungdomar i utformningen. Det är ingen regel för alla.

title: School-Based Interventions for Increasing Autistic Pupils' Social Inclusion in Mainstream Schools: A Systematic Review.
authors: Tsou YT, Kovács LV, Louloumari A, Stockmann L, Blijd-Hoogewys EMA, Koutamanis A, Rieffe C
journal: Review journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: School-based interventions for socially including autistic pupils in mainstream schools were systematically reviewed. Included interventions targeted at least one level of the school environment: the autistic children, the peers, the staff, and/or the physical environment, and assessed autistic pupils' quantity and/or quality of social participation as outcome measures. Findings from 56 studies showed increased accessibility of school activities to autistic pupils, but the reciprocity and friendship between the autistic pupils and the peers were not necessarily improved. Moreover, limited interventions were available for modifying the physical environment. A more holistic strategy that moves the focus from individual children's social skills to the larger context surrounding children, should be considered for a better inclusion of autistic children in school routine.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a un alumno autista, pregunta al centro qué se hace más allá de entrenar sus habilidades sociales: cómo se prepara a los compañeros, qué formación tiene el personal y si el espacio físico se puede adaptar. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 56 estudios sobre intervenciones escolares en colegios ordinarios. Hallaron que las actividades escolares se volvían más accesibles, pero la reciprocidad y la amistad con los compañeros no siempre mejoraban. Además, había pocas intervenciones sobre el entorno físico. Es una síntesis general: no dice qué funcionará con cada alumno, y el resumen no detalla quiénes participaron.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic pupil, ask the school what it does beyond training their social skills: how classmates are prepared, what training staff have, and whether the physical space can be adapted. This systematic review brought together 56 studies of school-based interventions in mainstream schools. It found school activities became more accessible, but reciprocity and friendship with peers did not always improve. Few interventions addressed the physical environment. It is a broad overview: it cannot say what will work for each pupil, and the abstract does not describe who took part.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk elev, fråga skolan vad den gör utöver att träna elevens sociala färdigheter: hur klasskamraterna förbereds, vilken utbildning personalen har och om den fysiska miljön kan anpassas. Den här systematiska översikten samlade 56 studier om skolbaserade insatser i vanliga skolor. Den fann att skolaktiviteter blev mer tillgängliga, men att ömsesidighet och vänskap med klasskamrater inte alltid förbättrades. Få insatser gällde den fysiska miljön. Det är en bred sammanställning: den visar inte vad som fungerar för varje elev, och sammanfattningen beskriver inte vilka som deltog.

title: The Assessment and Treatment of Post-traumatic Stress Disorder in Autistic People: A Systematic Review.
authors: Quinton AMG, Ali D, Danese A, Happé F, Rumball F
journal: Review journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Adverse life events and mental health conditions are unfortunately common amongst autistic adults and children; this may present a vulnerability to developing post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). This systematic review provides an update of Rumball's ( Review Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders , 6 , 294-324, 2019) systematic review of PTSD in autistic individuals and identifies 18 new studies published from 2017 to 2022, reflecting increased research interest in PTSD in autistic populations. Included literature suggests that autistic adults and children experience more severe PTSD symptoms compared to their non-autistic peers, with at least comparable rates of occurrence. We provide a comprehensive overview of this emerging field and identify the need for future research to validate PTSD symptom assessment tools and treatment strategies and investigate unique manifestations of trauma-related symptoms in autistic individuals.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista a su cargo ha vivido experiencias difíciles, conviene tomarse en serio posibles señales de trauma: cambios en el sueño, más ansiedad, evitación de lugares o personas, o pérdida de habilidades. Estas señales pueden verse distintas en personas autistas, así que anote lo que observa y compártalo con profesionales que conozcan tanto el autismo como el trauma. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 18 estudios nuevos (2017-2022) con niños y adultos autistas, y sugiere que el TEPT es al menos igual de frecuente y a menudo más intenso que en personas no autistas. Sus límites: las herramientas de evaluación y los tratamientos aún no están validados para personas autistas, y cada persona es diferente.
sheet.en: If an autistic person you support has been through hard experiences, it is worth taking possible signs of trauma seriously: changes in sleep, more anxiety, avoiding places or people, or losing skills. These signs can look different in autistic people, so note what you notice and share it with professionals who understand both autism and trauma. This systematic review gathered 18 new studies (2017-2022) with autistic children and adults, and suggests PTSD is at least as common and often more severe than in non-autistic peers. Its limits: assessment tools and treatments are not yet validated for autistic people, and every person is different.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person du stöttar har varit med om svåra händelser är det klokt att ta möjliga tecken på trauma på allvar: förändrad sömn, mer oro, att undvika platser eller personer, eller att tappa förmågor. Tecknen kan se annorlunda ut hos autistiska personer, så anteckna vad du ser och dela det med yrkespersoner som förstår både autism och trauma. Denna systematiska översikt samlade 18 nya studier (2017-2022) med autistiska barn och vuxna och tyder på att PTSD är minst lika vanligt och ofta mer intensivt än hos icke-autistiska. Begränsningar: bedömningsverktyg och behandlingar är ännu inte validerade för autistiska personer, och varje person är unik.

title: The impact of autism on the relations between social anxiety, camouflaging, and depression in Taiwanese adolescents.
authors: Liu CH, Chen YL, Ai W, Ni HC, Lai MC
journal: Child and adolescent psychiatry and mental health
abstract: Background Both camouflaging and social anxiety are adolescence-emerging phenomenon, rooted in social situations, and associated with mental health. The directionality between camouflaging and social anxiety in autistic versus non-autistic adolescents is underexplored. This study aims to investigate the inter-relations between camouflaging, social anxiety, and depression, and the moderating role of autism diagnosis on these inter-relations. Methods A total of 205 Taiwanese adolescents (100 autistic, 105 non-autistic) completed self-reported measures, including the Camouflaging Autistic Traits Questionnaire, Chinese version (CAT-Q-Ch), Social Interaction Anxiety Scale, Chinese version (SIAS-C), Generalized Anxiety Disorder 7-item (GAD-7), and Patient Health Questionnaire 9-item (PHQ-9). Network analysis was used to examine the inter-relations among items of the CAT-Q-Ch and SIAS-C. Moderated mediation models, adjusted for generalized anxiety, examined the inter-relations among camouflaging, social anxiety, and depression, and how these associations varied by autism diagnosis. Results Autistic adolescents reported significantly higher scores on camouflaging, depression, generalized anxiety, and social anxiety than non-autistic adolescents. A network analysis showed that items from the CAT-Q-Ch formed two communities, and most SIAS-C items formed a third community, supporting the interpretation that camouflaging and social anxiety are related yet distinct constructs. For both autistic and non-autistic adolescents, social anxiety and camouflaging showed bidirectional indirect associations with depression. Critically, having an autism diagnosis significantly weakened the link between camouflaging and depression, as part of the indirect association between social anxiety and depression via camouflaging. Conclusion The findings highlight the complex inter-relations among camouflaging, social anxiety, and depression, which may differ between autistic and non-autistic adolescents in Taiwan. Camouflaging may serve different functional roles and have different mental health implications for autistic and non-autistic adolescents. Future research should focus on teasing apart the complex conceptual, measurement, and causal mechanisms underlying the inter-relations between social anxiety and camouflaging in autistic versus non-autistic people.

sheet.es: Si un o una adolescente autista se esfuerza mucho por ocultar sus rasgos autistas (camuflaje) y siente ansiedad en situaciones sociales, conviene preguntarle con calma cómo se siente después y ofrecerle espacios donde no tenga que camuflarse. Es un estudio con 205 adolescentes de Taiwán (100 autistas y 105 no autistas) que respondieron cuestionarios. Las personas autistas indicaron más camuflaje, ansiedad social y depresión, y estos aspectos se relacionaron entre sí. Sin embargo, solo muestra asociaciones, no causas, se basa en autoinformes y no sirve como regla para cada persona ni para otros países.
sheet.en: If an autistic teenager works hard to hide their autistic traits (camouflaging) and feels anxious in social situations, it helps to ask calmly how they feel afterwards and to offer spaces where they don't have to camouflage. This study had 205 adolescents in Taiwan (100 autistic, 105 non-autistic) fill in questionnaires. Autistic adolescents reported more camouflaging, social anxiety and depression, and these were linked to one another. However, it shows associations, not causes, relies on self-report, and is not a rule for every person or for other countries.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk tonåring anstränger sig mycket för att dölja sina autistiska drag (kamouflering) och känner oro i sociala situationer, hjälper det att lugnt fråga hur hen mår efteråt och erbjuda miljöer där hen slipper kamouflera. Studien omfattade 205 tonåringar i Taiwan (100 autistiska, 105 icke-autistiska) som fyllde i frågeformulär. De autistiska tonåringarna rapporterade mer kamouflering, social ångest och depression, och dessa hängde ihop. Studien visar dock samband, inte orsaker, bygger på självskattning och är ingen regel för varje person eller för andra länder.

title: Describing the communication of autistic people during experiences of distress: A scoping review.
authors: Oldenburg K, Gibbons T, Welch C, Tint A, Albin M
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Autistic people can experience distress for many reasons. Some of these reasons may include unsupportive environments; experiences of trauma; sensory overload; burnout, inertia, meltdown and shutdown; pain; and mental health diagnoses such as anxiety. Little is known about how distress can impact communication and what others can do to provide support in these moments. This scoping review explores how communication is described during experiences of distress for autistic people, including communication partner strategies to support these interactions. Following a comprehensive database search, 18 articles were included in this scoping review. Firsthand perspectives of autistic people were discussed in 10 studies. Distress was most often characterized by instances of anxiety and/or stress. Eleven studies discussed non-spoken methods of communication, including gestures, facial expressions and behavioural manifestations (e.g. hitting, screaming) during experiences of distress. Identified facilitators to communication during experiences of distress included the presence of a calm, supportive environment and communicative aids. Understanding the impact distress has on communication is beneficial to both autistic people and those who support them. This review contributes to the body of literature aiming to better understand and support autistic people during moments of distress.Lay abstractPast research talks about (1) how autistic people may communicate and (2) how and why autistic people may experience periods of distress. There is not much research about the way autistic people communicate during periods of distress. We therefore looked at research exploring how autistic people of all ages communicate during periods of distress. Communication includes various methods of sending and receiving information, including spoken and non-spoken communication methods (e.g. observable behaviours, typing, gestures). We explored how often researchers collected firsthand perspectives from autistic people. We also collected information on what made communication easier, or more difficult, during periods of distress. We used a methodological approach called a scoping review to identify and evaluate 18 articles that met our criteria. The most common communication method described in the articles was non-verbal communication, including gestures, facial expressions and observable behaviours such as screaming and hitting. Firsthand autistic perspectives were included in just over half of the studies. Facilitators to communication included a calm, supportive environment and communicative aids relevant to the situation, such as a pain scale. This study will help those who support autistic people, and autistic people themselves, by showing the many ways autistic people may communicate when experiencing distress and describing strategies that can be used to support autistic people in those moments.

sheet.es: Cuando una persona autista está en un momento de angustia, conviene fijarse en toda su comunicación, no solo en las palabras: gestos, expresiones de la cara y conductas también transmiten algo. Ayuda mantener un entorno tranquilo y de apoyo, y tener a mano apoyos de comunicación adecuados a la situación, como una escala de dolor. La evidencia es una revisión de alcance de 18 artículos; 10 estudios recogieron la voz de personas autistas. Sus límites: describe lo que la investigación ha contado, no prueba qué estrategia funciona mejor, y cada persona se comunica de forma distinta.
sheet.en: When an autistic person is distressed, look at all of their communication, not only words: gestures, facial expressions and behaviours can carry meaning too. It helps to keep the environment calm and supportive, and to have communication aids suited to the situation within reach, such as a pain scale. The evidence is a scoping review of 18 articles; 10 studies included the firsthand views of autistic people. Its limits: it describes what research has reported, does not prove which strategy works best, and every person communicates differently.
sheet.sv: När en autistisk person är i en stressad eller ångestfylld stund, se på all kommunikation, inte bara orden: gester, ansiktsuttryck och beteenden kan också betyda något. Det hjälper att hålla miljön lugn och stödjande och ha kommunikationsstöd som passar situationen nära till hands, till exempel en smärtskala. Underlaget är en kartläggande översikt av 18 artiklar; 10 studier inkluderade autistiska personers egna perspektiv. Begränsningar: den beskriver vad forskningen har rapporterat, visar inte vilken strategi som fungerar bäst, och alla kommunicerar på olika sätt.

title: How does 'autistic burnout' feel? A qualitative study exploring experiences of earlier and later-diagnosed autistic adults.
authors: Ali D, Mandy W, Happé F
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: 'Autistic burnout' is increasingly conceptualised as an experience of severe exhaustion, increased sensory difficulties and need for solitude, resulting from not having needs met across contexts. We interviewed 20 autistic adults (eight diagnosed with autism in childhood) about their experiences of autistic burnout. In this reflexive thematic analysis, we focused on how burnout felt, comparing the experiences of those diagnosed in childhood versus adulthood. We created five themes. We understood burnout to be, at times, (1) a powering down and/or (2) the overactivation, of the mind and body , resulting in (3) a craving for sensory and social rest . For those diagnosed in adulthood, burnout seemed to be experienced as more chronic and confusing. Some participants diagnosed in adulthood (4) made the world more bearable by using substances , coping with the contributors to and effects of burnout. Especially affecting those diagnosed in adulthood, (5) not knowing why this was happening took a (sometimes dangerous) toll; for a few, it led to contemplating suicide. This study brings new insights into burnout experiences of adults diagnosed with autism at different life points.Lay abstractSome autistic people experience severe exhaustion as a result of not having their needs met that sometimes prevents them from being able to take part in daily life. Some people refer to this as 'autistic burnout'. In this study, we spoke to 20 autistic adults, eight of whom were diagnosed with autism in childhood. We analysed our participants' interviews through an approach called reflexive thematic analysis. Through this process, we created five themes around the question of how autistic burnout felt for these participants. We were also interested in how participants diagnosed with autism in childhood versus in adulthood described their burnout experiences. This is because research has shown that not having an autism diagnosis earlier in life could, indirectly, lead to not understanding one's own needs accurately and not having the right support from others. The five themes we created were (1) the powering down of the mind and body, (2) the overactivation of the mind and body, (3) craving social and sensory rest, (4) making the world more manageable by using substances and (5) not knowing why this is happening to you can take a (sometimes dangerous) toll. Themes 1, 2 and 3 seemed to be shared between participants regardless of age at autism diagnosis. However, these experiences seemed to be more disabling for participants diagnosed in adulthood. Themes 4 and 5 related particularly to those diagnosed with autism in adulthood. This study adds an important insight: perspectives on burnout experiences from adults diagnosed with autism at different life points.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista está agotada, necesita más soledad o tolera peor los sentidos, conviene tratarlo como una señal de que faltan apoyos: reducir exigencias, dar descanso sensorial y social y ayudarle a entender sus necesidades. El estudio entrevistó a 20 adultos autistas, 8 de ellos diagnosticados en la infancia, y analizó cómo se vivía el agotamiento. Quienes recibieron el diagnóstico de adultos lo describieron como más crónico y confuso; algunos usaron sustancias para sobrellevarlo y unos pocos pensaron en el suicidio. Son experiencias de una muestra pequeña y no valen para todas las personas. Si te preocupa a alguien, busca ayuda profesional (clínico, servicio de salud o servicio de crisis); en peligro inmediato, llama al número de emergencias de tu país.
sheet.en: If an autistic person is exhausted, needs more solitude or finds sensory input harder, it helps to treat this as a sign that support is missing: lower demands, offer sensory and social rest, and help them understand their own needs. The study interviewed 20 autistic adults, 8 of them diagnosed in childhood, about how burnout felt. Those diagnosed in adulthood described it as more chronic and confusing; some used substances to cope and a few contemplated suicide. This is a small sample and does not describe every person. If you are worried about someone, contact professional help (a clinician, a health service or a crisis service); in immediate danger, call the emergency number of your country.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person är utmattad, behöver mer ensamhet eller har svårare med sinnesintryck kan det ses som en signal om att stöd saknas: sänk kraven, ge sensorisk och social vila och hjälp personen att förstå sina behov. Studien intervjuade 20 autistiska vuxna, varav 8 fick sin diagnos som barn, om hur utbrändhet kändes. De som fick diagnos som vuxna beskrev den som mer långvarig och förvirrande; några använde substanser för att klara sig och ett fåtal funderade på självmord. Urvalet är litet och gäller inte alla personer. Om du är orolig för någon, sök professionell hjälp (läkare, vården eller en krisjour); vid akut fara, ring larmnumret i ditt land.

title: Discrepancies between feeling and expressing: Perceptions of autistic and non-autistic emotional expressions by non-autistic observers.
authors: Foster SJ, Dunn D, Patel S, Pinkham AE, Ackerman RA, Sasson NJ
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Non-autistic observers often interpret autistic emotional expressions more negatively, though it is unclear whether this reflects observer bias or genuine differences in autistic people's emotional experience and expression. To examine this, 20 autistic and 20 non-autistic adults reported the intensity of their felt emotion while re-experiencing video-recorded events eliciting mild and strong happiness, sadness, and anger. A total of 379 non-autistic observers, half blind to diagnostic status, viewed the recordings and identified the emotion and its intensity. iMotions emotion recognition software also classified the emotional valence of the expressions. Overall, autistic and non-autistic participants reported comparable levels of felt emotion, although differences emerged in how their expressions were perceived. Observers more accurately identified happiness in non-autistic participants and sadness and anger in autistic participants. They also judged autistic participants as expressing sadness and anger more intensely. Informing observers of the diagnostic status of participants largely did not modulate effects. iMotions more often classified mild autistic expressions as neutral and mild non-autistic expressions as positive. Because observer and iMotion findings emerged despite autistic and non-autistic participants not differing in felt emotion, they suggest that non-autistic observers and emotion recognition algorithms differentially interpret authentic autistic and non-autistic emotional expressions, which may contribute to misinterpretations of autistic people.Lay AbstractAutistic people may express emotions in ways that differ from non-autistic people, and non-autistic people sometimes misinterpret them as flat, overly intense, or hard to read. This misunderstanding can affect how autistic people are judged in everyday life, including in job interviews, friendships, and other important situations. In this study, we wanted to know how well non-autistic people-and emotion recognition software-can identify emotions on the faces of autistic and non-autistic people when they are actually feeling emotion. To do this, autistic and non-autistic adults were videotaped while recounting personal experiences that made them feel mild and strong happiness, sadness, and anger. They rated how strongly they felt each emotion during the videotaping. Later, short video clips of their facial expressions were shown (without sound) to a large group of non-autistic viewers, who identified the emotion and rated its intensity. Some viewers were told whether the person in the video was autistic or not. We found that autistic and non-autistic people reported feeling emotions at comparable levels, but non-autistic viewers were better at recognizing happy expressions in non-autistic people compared to autistic people, and better at recognizing sad and angry expressions in autistic people compared to non-autistic people. Viewers tended to rate autistic expressions, especially sadness and anger, as more intense than those of non-autistic people, even though the computer software rated autistic expressions as more neutral compared to non-autistic participants. These results suggest that autistic people feel emotions just as deeply as non-autistic people, but differences in expressive style and non-autistic biases may lead to misinterpretation. These findings highlight the need for greater awareness of communication differences in autism and for reducing misinterpretations in how autistic people are perceived.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista parece inexpresiva o demasiado intensa, no asumas lo que siente: pregúntale con calma y créele. Puede sentir lo mismo que tú con una expresión distinta. Este estudio con 20 adultos autistas y 20 no autistas comparó lo que sentían con cómo 379 observadores no autistas interpretaban sus rostros en vídeo. Sintieron emociones en niveles comparables, pero los observadores leyeron su felicidad peor y su tristeza e ira como más intensas. Como límite, eran adultos, vídeos sin sonido y emociones recordadas, así que no vale para todas las personas ni situaciones.
sheet.en: If an autistic person looks flat or overly intense, don't assume what they feel: ask calmly and believe their answer. They may feel the same as you with a different expression. This study of 20 autistic and 20 non-autistic adults compared what they felt with how 379 non-autistic observers read their faces on video. Felt emotion was comparable, but observers read their happiness less accurately and judged their sadness and anger as more intense. A limit: participants were adults, clips had no sound and emotions were recalled, so it cannot speak for every person or situation.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person verkar uttryckslös eller överdrivet intensiv, anta inte vad hen känner: fråga lugnt och tro på svaret. Hen kan känna samma sak som du fast uttrycka det annorlunda. Studien jämförde 20 autistiska och 20 icke-autistiska vuxnas upplevda känslor med hur 379 icke-autistiska observatörer tolkade deras ansikten på video. Känslorna var jämförbara, men observatörerna läste glädjen sämre och bedömde sorg och ilska som intensivare. En begränsning: deltagarna var vuxna, klippen saknade ljud och känslorna var återskapade, så resultatet gäller inte alla personer eller situationer.

title: Tier 1 evaluating the implementation of the Oliver McGowan Mandatory Training in learning disabilities and autism across interdisciplinarity health-related courses at Aston University.
authors: Bashir A, Rana KS, Murphy J, Drozd M
abstract: Introduction The Oliver McGowan Mandatory Training (OMMT) on Learning Disability and Autism was developed to address recognized gaps in healthcare professionals' education and training. Under the Health and Care Act, 2022, healthcare providers are required to ensure staff receive role-appropriate training in autism and learning disabilities. In response, NHS England introduced OMMT as a standardized national programme to support the development of a skilled and inclusive healthcare workforce, aligned with the NHS Long Term Workforce Plan (2023). This study reports on the first pilot implementation of Tier 1 OMMT within a higher education institution, involving students enrolled in Nursing, Biomedical Science, Physician Associate, Optometry, and Pharmacy programmes at Aston University, UK. Materials and methods The interdisciplinary Tier 1 training consisted of a 90-min e-learning module and a 1-h interactive webinar featuring experts by experience and facilitators. This study evaluated healthcare students' understanding pre- and post-training. Data on autism and learning disabilities awareness was collected via Jisc Online Surveys. Likert scale data were analyzed quantitatively, and free-text responses examined using thematic analysis to evaluate training effectiveness. Results Post-OMMT training results showed significant improvements in students' confidence in verbal communication and using various methods to communicate with autistic individuals and those with learning disabilities ( p p Discussion This interdisciplinary training enhanced healthcare students' understanding of autism and learning disabilities, equipping them with key skills for future NHS roles and supporting improved outcomes for neurodivergent populations. Embedding such training across all HEIs is essential to prepare professionals to not only treat, but also understand, respect, and advocate for autistic and learning-disabled individuals.

sheet.es: Si acudes a una cita sanitaria, puedes pedir que el personal comunique de varias maneras (palabras, apoyos visuales, escritura) y que cuente con tu experiencia. Se evaluó la formación obligatoria Oliver McGowan (Nivel 1) en estudiantes de salud de Aston University (Reino Unido): se compararon encuestas antes y después, y tras la formación declararon más confianza para comunicarse con personas autistas y con discapacidad intelectual. Límites: mide la confianza que dicen tener los estudiantes, no la experiencia de las personas autistas en consulta, y fue un piloto en una sola universidad.
sheet.en: If you attend a healthcare appointment, you can ask staff to communicate in more than one way (spoken words, visual supports, writing) and to listen to your expertise. This study looked at Oliver McGowan Mandatory Training (Tier 1) for health students at Aston University, UK, using surveys before and after training. Afterwards, students reported more confidence communicating with autistic people and people with learning disabilities. Limits: it measures students' own reported confidence, not autistic people's experiences in appointments, and it was a pilot at a single university.
sheet.sv: Om du går på ett vårdbesök kan du be personalen kommunicera på flera sätt (tal, visuellt stöd, skrift) och lyssna på din expertis. Studien undersökte Oliver McGowan-utbildningen (nivå 1) för vårdstudenter vid Aston University i Storbritannien, med enkäter före och efter. Efteråt uppgav studenterna större tillförsikt i att kommunicera med autistiska personer och personer med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning. Begränsningar: den mäter studenternas egen upplevda tillförsikt, inte autistiska personers erfarenheter i vårdmöten, och det var en pilot vid ett enda universitet.

title: Foxp2 mutations and abnormal brain and gastrointestinal development: insights from animal models of speech-language and autism spectrum disorders.
authors: Fujita-Jimbo E, Kawahara G, Momoi T
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and speech and language disorder (SLD) are distinct neurodevelopmental conditions, yet both share overlapping communication impairments. Forkhead box P2 ( FOXP2 ), a key transcription factor involved in speech and language development, harbors pathogenic mutations such as R553H, which cause SLD and have been suggested to contribute to aspects of ASD-related phenotypes. This review synthesizes insights from animal models to explore the molecular mechanisms by which Foxp2 mutations disrupt the development of the cerebral cortex, thalamus, and enteric nervous system. We highlight findings from heterozygous Foxp2 mutants and discuss severe phenotypes observed in homozygous Foxp2 mutants ( Foxp 2 R552H/R552H and Foxp 2 R552H/R552H /mCherry-Tg mice), including profound ultrasonic vocalization deficits, brain malformations, and early lethality. Notably, these mice exhibit gastrointestinal abnormalities involving the epithelium, smooth muscle, and enteric nervous system, which are linked to impaired autoregulation and interference with Wnt signaling during development. Such observations underscore the relevance of the brain-gut-microbiome axis and Hirschsprung-like pathology in neurodevelopmental disorders. Finally, this review discusses future directions using gene-editing approaches in non-mammalian models-zebra finches, zebrafish, and Drosophila -to dissect neural networks underlying intellectual disability and communication deficits. Collectively, these studies provide a framework for understanding FOXP2 -related molecular mechanisms in the pathogenesis of ASD and SLD.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista con dificultades de comunicación o de digestión, esta revisión no ofrece nada para aplicar mañana, pero invita a tratar ambos aspectos con atención y a comentarlos con su equipo clínico. Es una revisión de estudios con modelos animales, sobre todo ratones, que analiza cómo mutaciones del gen Foxp2 alteran el desarrollo del cerebro y del intestino. Sus límites: no incluye personas, los resultados en animales no se trasladan directamente a los humanos y no describen a todas las personas autistas, pues solo una parte se relaciona con este gen.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person with communication or digestive differences, this review offers nothing to apply tomorrow, but it is a reminder to take both seriously and to raise them with their clinical team. It is a review of animal-model studies, mostly mice, looking at how Foxp2 gene mutations alter brain and gut development. Its limits: no people took part, animal results do not transfer directly to humans, and they do not describe every autistic person, since only some are linked to this gene.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person med kommunikations- eller magskillnader ger denna översikt inget att tillämpa i morgon, men den påminner om att ta båda på allvar och ta upp dem med personens vårdteam. Det är en översikt av djurmodellstudier, främst på möss, om hur mutationer i genen Foxp2 förändrar hjärnans och tarmens utveckling. Begränsningar: inga människor deltog, djurresultat går inte direkt att överföra till människor och de beskriver inte alla autistiska personer, eftersom bara några kopplas till denna gen.

title: Effectiveness of a five-component multimodal intervention on executive function in children with Autism spectrum disorder: A study protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
authors: Hossain KMA, Sharna SY, Sharmin F, Hossain T, Naim JH, Amin A, Badhon TI
abstract: Background Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is characterized by persistent deficits in social interaction, communication, and executive functions such as inhibitory control, cognitive flexibility, and working memory. These deficits hinder daily functioning and learning outcomes in children. Exercise-based interventions improve executive function; however, most previous studies have focused on single-modality programs with limited generalizability. This trial aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a structured, five-component multimodal intervention-comprising yoga, aerobic, strengthening, neurocognitive, and music-based mindfulness activities-on improving executive functioning in children with ASD. Methods This assessor-blinded, double-center randomized controlled trial will enroll 130 children aged 4-18 years diagnosed with ASD in Bangladesh. Participants will be randomly assigned (1:1) to either the experimental group receiving the multimodal intervention or a wait-list control group receiving healthy lifestyle guidelines. The intervention will include five supervised sessions per week for 12 weeks, followed by a 12-week follow-up. An additional group of 65 typically developing children will serve as healthy controls. Primary outcomes will assess executive function domains: inhibitory control (Go/No-Go Task), cognitive flexibility (Trail Making Test A-B), and working memory (Corsi Block Tapping Task; Forward and Backward Digit Span). Secondary outcomes include social responsiveness (Social Responsiveness Scale-2) and ASD-related behaviors (Autism Treatment Evaluation Checklist). Outcomes will be evaluated at baseline, 12 weeks, and 24 weeks by blinded assessors. Data will be analyzed using SPSS following the intention-to-treat principle. Discussion This trial will address an important evidence gap by evaluating a comprehensive, low-cost, non-pharmacological multimodal intervention targeting multiple domains of executive function in children with ASD. The findings may help clinicians, educators, and policymakers adopt structured exercise-based programs within rehabilitation, school, and community settings. Although limited to two centers, the results could guide future large-scale studies and support the development of standardized multimodal intervention guidelines for ASD. Trial registration This trial is prospectively registered with the Clinical Trial Registry of India: CTRI/2025/11/096943 [Registered on: 06/11/2025]. Link: https://ctri.nic.in/Clinicaltrials/pmaindet2.php?EncHid=MTQ1NDEy&Enc=&userName=.

sheet.es: Por ahora no hay resultados que aplicar: este estudio es solo un protocolo. Si le interesa el movimiento, puede probar actividades como yoga, ejercicio aeróbico, fuerza o música con atención plena, según los gustos y el ritmo de cada niño o niña autista. Evidencia: es el plan de un ensayo aleatorizado en Bangladesh con 130 niños y niñas autistas de 4-18 años, más 65 sin diagnóstico, con sesiones durante 12 semanas. Límites: aún no hay datos sobre si funciona, solo participan dos centros y no sirve como regla para todas las personas. Consulte a profesionales antes de cambiar rutinas.
sheet.en: There are no results to act on yet: this study is only a protocol. If movement interests your child, you could try activities like yoga, aerobic exercise, strength work or music with mindfulness, following each autistic child's preferences and pace. Evidence: it is the plan for a randomized trial in Bangladesh with 130 autistic children aged 4-18, plus 65 children without a diagnosis, with sessions over 12 weeks. Limits: there are no data yet on whether it works, only two centers take part, and it is not a rule for every person. Talk with professionals before changing routines.
sheet.sv: Det finns inga resultat att använda ännu: studien är bara ett protokoll. Om ditt barn gillar rörelse kan du prova aktiviteter som yoga, konditionsträning, styrketräning eller musik med mindfulness, utifrån varje autistiskt barns önskemål och tempo. Evidens: det är planen för en randomiserad studie i Bangladesh med 130 autistiska barn i åldern 4-18, plus 65 barn utan diagnos, med träning under 12 veckor. Begränsningar: det finns ännu inga data om effekten, bara två centra deltar och studien är ingen regel för alla. Prata med yrkespersoner innan du ändrar rutiner.

title: From Participants to Community Partners: A Novel Community-Based Participatory Research (CBPR) Approach to Autistic-Led Inquiry in Digital and Virtual Environments.
authors: Grillo VD, Zani M, Veronesi V, Venuti P
abstract: Background/Objectives : Autism research has often interpreted autistic sociality through neurotypical norms, limiting ecological accounts of autistic meaning-making and context-sensitive support needs. Social virtual environments (SVEs), such as VRChat, allow modulation of sensory exposure, social distance, and participation pace, potentially enabling autistic-led interaction with greater autonomy and predictability. This study examined how autistic young adults co-construct meanings around social interaction, identity, and self-regulation in peer-led discussions within an SVE; identified context-sensitive processes relevant to well-being; and evaluated the feasibility and acceptability of SVEs as a participatory research setting. Methods : Sixteen autistic young adults (18-38 years; DSM-5-TR, Level 1) participated in nine remote sessions conducted in VRChat, coordinated via a co-designed Discord server. The peer-led discussions were audio-video recorded, transcribed, and anonymized. Data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis, combining inductive session-level coding, cross-session thematic clustering, and participatory refinement with community partners. Results : Autistic experience was framed as a context-dependent negotiation of interpretive risk, interactional workload, masking-related energy costs, and epistemic injustice, alongside future-oriented accounts emphasizing access, dignity, and systemic redesign. Observational memos documented multimodal participation, distributed peer facilitation, and accessibility-relevant sensitivities to environmental stability. Community partners reported positive experiences and supported the acceptability of private-world VRChat sessions. Conclusions : Peer-led discussions in an SVE can support ecologically grounded, participant-centered qualitative research, offering methodological opportunities to study autistic meaning-making under conditions that reduce demands and risks.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista joven o adulta prefiere hablar con sus iguales desde casa, un espacio virtual social como VRChat puede ser una opción para conversar con más control: ajustar el ruido, la distancia y el ritmo. Ofrézcalo como una posibilidad, no como una obligación. La evidencia es un estudio cualitativo con dieciséis jóvenes autistas (18-38 años) que mantuvieron nueve sesiones remotas de debate dirigidas por pares; las personas participantes valoraron bien la experiencia.
