Los resultados no son una regla general y faltan más investigaciones, sobre todo con adultos.
sheet.en: If it appeals, theatre and dramatic play can be an activity to explore with an autistic person, following their interests and at their pace. This scoping review gathered eleven studies on theatre-based interventions. All included children and adolescents, and only one included adults. Improvements were described in social interaction, language and anxiety, along with keeping the skills learned. The studies were few and varied in length and number of sessions, so we cannot know what works for each person. The findings are not a rule for everyone, and more research is needed, especially with adults.
sheet.sv: Om det väcker intresse kan teater och dramalek vara en aktivitet att utforska med en autistisk person, utifrån personens intressen och i dess takt. Den här kartläggande översikten samlade elva studier om teaterbaserade insatser. Alla inkluderade barn och ungdomar, och bara en inkluderade vuxna. Förbättringar beskrevs i social interaktion, språk och ångest, liksom i att behålla det man lärt sig. Studierna var få och varierade i längd och antal tillfällen, så vi vet inte vad som fungerar för varje person. Resultaten är ingen regel för alla, och mer forskning behövs, särskilt med vuxna.

title: A systematic review of existing brief interventions for youth following suicide attempt: informing the development of an autism-adapted intervention.
authors: Howe SJ, Andreasen S, Schwartzman JM, Exner-Cortens D, Thompson-Hodgetts S, Weiss JA, Chaput K, Maroney MR, Jacobs AX, Mattingly J, McMorris CA
abstract: Background Autistic youth are at elevated suicide risk, yet they face multiple barriers to mental health care, including a lack of interventions adapted to their unique needs and lived experiences. In the general population, brief interventions have been shown to reduce suicide risk during the high-risk period immediately following discharge from acute care for a suicide attempt. However, no suicide prevention intervention has been designed specifically for Autistic youth during this critical post-discharge period. The overarching aim of the current systematic review was to lay the groundwork for the development of a brief suicide intervention for Autistic youth following discharge from acute care. This review aimed to: (1) identify existing brief post-discharge interventions for general population youth (15-24 years) who have made a suicide attempt; (2) describe core strategies used; and (3) summarize evidence of intervention effectiveness. Methods Following PRISMA reporting guidelines, five bibliographic databases were searched. Articles were included based on a rigorous selection process, and their quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Results Twenty-four studies were included in the review, representing sixteen interventions. No studies reported including Autistic individuals, and Autistic people were explicitly excluded from two studies. Articles presented mixed findings, with eight studies indicating that the brief intervention was associated with a reduction in suicide outcomes. Common strategies included follow-up contact, safety planning, and teaching coping skills. Discussion Several brief suicide interventions and strategies show promise for non-Autistic youth post-discharge, their relevance for Autistic youth remains unclear, underscoring the need for autism-adapted approaches informed by Autistic youth.

sheet.es: Tras el alta por un intento de suicidio, suelen ayudar el contacto de seguimiento, un plan de seguridad y aprender estrategias para afrontar la situación, pero aún no sabemos si funcionan igual para jóvenes autistas. Conviene hablar con el equipo clínico para adaptarlas a cada persona. La evidencia es una revisión sistemática de 24 estudios sobre dieciséis intervenciones breves en jóvenes de 15-24 años de la población general. Sus límites: ningún estudio incluyó a personas autistas, en dos se las excluyó, y los resultados fueron mixtos. Si tú o alguien cercano está en riesgo, busca ayuda profesional: un clínico, un servicio de salud o un servicio de crisis. En peligro inmediato, llama al número de emergencias de tu país.
sheet.en: After discharge following a suicide attempt, follow-up contact, a safety plan and learning coping skills are common supports, but we do not yet know if they work the same way for autistic youth. It is worth talking with the clinical team about adapting them to the person. The evidence is a systematic review of 24 studies covering sixteen brief interventions for general-population youth aged 15-24 years. Its limits: no study included autistic people, two explicitly excluded them, and findings were mixed. If you or someone close to you is at risk, seek professional help: a clinician, a health service or a crisis service. In immediate danger, call your country's emergency number.
sheet.sv: Efter utskrivning från vård efter ett självmordsförsök är uppföljande kontakt, en säkerhetsplan och att lära sig copingstrategier vanliga stöd, men vi vet ännu inte om de fungerar likadant för autistiska ungdomar. Prata med vårdteamet om hur stödet kan anpassas till personen. Underlaget är en systematisk översikt av 24 studier om sexton korta insatser för ungdomar i den allmänna befolkningen, 15-24 år. Begränsningar: ingen studie inkluderade autistiska personer, två uteslöt dem uttryckligen, och resultaten var blandade. Om du eller någon nära dig är i riskzonen, sök professionell hjälp: en läkare, vårdcentral eller krisjour. Vid akut fara, ring ditt lands nödnummer.

title: "Shutdowns Are Like You're Stuck on the Blue Screen of Death": A Metaphor Analysis of Autistic Shutdowns.
authors: Paris K, Lodestone AZ, Houser M, Lewis LF
abstract: Background Autistic adults commonly experience shutdowns, which are distressing events widely discussed within Autistic communities. Yet, few studies to date have explored firsthand accounts of shutdown experiences. In this study, we aimed to identify figurative language that Autistic adults use to describe shutdowns, thereby broadening the understanding of and providing language for this complex phenomenon. Methods We used a participatory research approach to conduct a secondary analysis of qualitative data from two prior studies on shutdowns in Autistic adults. Primary studies used asynchronous interviews and a survey, with a total sample size of 86 participants. We analyzed a corpus of 87 typed pages using the Pragglejaz Group's metaphor identification procedure to identify figurative language that Autistic adults used to describe shutdowns. Results Autistic adults in this sample used six metaphors to explain shutdowns, including the following: being frozen, a computer crash, going inside myself, when I can't keep up, survival mode, and playing a role. Discussion These metaphors help to externalize the internal experience of shutdowns. Participants described shutdowns as a state of being stuck, often involving physical and/or vocal immobilization. They frequently described shutdowns as a response to perceived threats, connecting them to a sense of survival and self-protection. Metaphors provide a rich context for understanding and talking about shutdowns. Findings also highlight how Autistic adults organically construct metaphors to articulate their experiences. Future studies could use metaphor analysis to explore other affective experiences of Autistic individuals. Community brief Why is this an important issue?: Many Autistic people experience shutdowns, but there is not much research on what shutdowns feel like. Studies that have looked at shutdowns found they can be hard to explain, especially to people who have not had a shutdown before. People often describe shutdowns as feeling frozen or stuck. We need to better understand shutdowns from the perspectives of people who experience them. What was the purpose of this study?: We wanted to understand how Autistic adults describe shutdowns. Metaphors can help explain an experience by comparing it with something else. Our goal was to find out what metaphors Autistic adults use to describe shutdowns and if those metaphors can help explain what a shutdown feels like. What did the researchers do?: In two earlier studies, we asked 86 Autistic adults about their experiences with shutdowns. Some answered questions in interviews, while others filled out surveys. Using these data, we used a method called "metaphor identification procedure," meaning we looked for words or phrases where participants used metaphors or other figurative language to compare their experience with a shutdown with something else. Once we identified these metaphors, we grouped them together to find metaphors that summarized the experience for participants. What were the results of the study?: We found six common metaphors that participants used to compare shutdowns with something else to help explain their experiences. Participants compared shutdowns with the following: being frozen, a computer crash, going inside myself, when I can't keep up, survival mode, and playing a role. What do these findings add to what was already known?: Few studies have looked at what it feels like to have a shutdown for Autistic people. Our findings add a rich description of what shutdowns feel like and add Autistic voices to the literature. What are potential weaknesses in the study?: Most participants in this study were White, so we are not sure if these findings are relevant for people of other racial backgrounds. Since people needed internet access to take part in this study, we may also be missing the perspectives of people who do not have access to a computer or internet. How will these findings help Autistic adults now or in the future?: These findings give non-Autistic people a better way of understanding what shutdowns are like for Autistic people. This knowledge can guide future research and help clinicians better support Autistic people who experience shutdowns.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista entra en un shutdown, puede ayudar verlo como un estado de bloqueo y no como mala voluntad: reducir exigencias, bajar estímulos y esperar con calma. Preguntarle más tarde qué imágenes o palabras describen lo que vive puede facilitar la comunicación. Es un análisis de metáforas con datos de dos estudios previos: 86 adultos autistas respondieron entrevistas escritas o una encuesta. Usaron seis metáforas, como estar congelado, un fallo de ordenador o modo supervivencia. Limitaciones: la mayoría de participantes eran blancas y hacía falta acceso a internet, así que no refleja a todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person goes into a shutdown, it may help to see it as a state of being stuck, not as unwillingness: lower demands, reduce input and wait calmly. Later, asking which images or words describe what it feels like can make talking about it easier. This was a metaphor analysis of data from two earlier studies: 86 autistic adults answered written interviews or a survey. They used six metaphors, such as being frozen, a computer crash or survival mode. Limits: most participants were White and internet access was needed, so it does not speak for everyone.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person går in i en shutdown kan det hjälpa att se den som ett fastlåst tillstånd, inte som ovilja: minska krav, dämpa intryck och vänta lugnt. Efteråt kan du fråga vilka bilder eller ord som beskriver upplevelsen, vilket kan underlätta samtalet. Det var en metaforanalys av data från två tidigare studier: 86 autistiska vuxna svarade på skriftliga intervjuer eller en enkät. De använde sex metaforer, till exempel att vara frusen, en datorkrasch eller överlevnadsläge. Begränsningar: de flesta deltagarna var vita och internetaccess krävdes, så resultaten gäller inte alla.

title: Relationship Satisfaction Among Autistic Populations: How Partner Neurotype Influences Relationship Satisfaction Factors for Autistic Adults.
authors: Khaw J, Vernon T
abstract: Background Autistic individuals report high levels of interest in pursuing and maintaining romantic relationships but indicate fewer and less satisfying relationships when compared with non-autistic populations. In this mixed-methods study, we investigated the self-identified factors that contribute to successful romantic relationships for autistic adults with the additional goal of understanding if and how their partners' neurotypes may influence relationship satisfaction. Methods We compared levels of relationship satisfaction among 106 autistic individuals by categorizing each participant into one of three groups based on the specific neurotype of their partner: (1) autistic/autistic (A/A) dyads; (2) autistic/neurotypical (A/NT) dyads; and (3) autistic/non-autistic but neurodivergent (A/ND) dyads. All participants completed a series of online surveys to gather information about their autistic traits, overall relationship satisfaction, reciprocal communication and support, and perceived impact of autism on relationships. Results Across the three dyads, participants reported similar levels of relationship satisfaction, and we found no statistically significant differences when comparing the mean satisfaction of each sample group. Participants indicated a wide variety of positive and negative relational aspects, with a few themes changing in frequency based on partner neurotype. Participants with autistic partners tended to focus on an inherent and deep sense of understanding when discussing the positive aspects of their relationships, while those with non-autistic partners were more likely to discuss the presence of mutual support and accommodation. In addition to some differences in reported themes, participants tended to report that their autistic traits positively impacted satisfaction in A/A dyads, while those in A/NT and A/ND dyads tended to report that their autistic traits posed challenges in their relationships. Conclusions The results of this study indicate that the neurotype of an autistic individual's partner may influence some of the reported positive and challenging aspects of their relationships. However, survey results indicate that autistic populations generally find comparable levels of satisfaction in romantic relationships irrespective of neurotype, which suggests that while partner neurotype may shape the enabling and barring factors for relationship success, it does not directly affect the overall health of a relationship. Finally, how an autistic individual perceives the impact of autism on their relationship may be affected by the neurotype of their partner. Community brief Why is this an important issue?: Many autistic folks seek out and thrive in romantic relationships, but studies report that autistic people experience lower relationship satisfaction than non-autistic people. Despite this, the autism research field has made little progress toward understanding (a) why this is the case and (b) how we can better support autistic individuals who are navigating romantic relationships. To best understand what autistic people seek in relationships, we created a space where autistic participants could share their experiences without comparison with those of non-autistic people. What was the purpose of this study?: We contributed to the current body of literature by learning more about what autistic people seek in relationships. We also wanted to see what they may struggle with and if these factors are influenced by whether their partner is neurotypical (referring to someone whose brain works in a way that is socially "typical"), neurodivergent (broadly referring to someone whose brain works differently from what is considered "typical"), and/or autistic. In doing this, we hope to help develop more effective ways of supporting autistic individuals who seek romantic connections. What did the researchers do?: The lead researcher, J.K., developed the project based on her experiences navigating romantic relationships as an autistic person. She recruited 106 autistic participants to complete a series of surveys regarding relationship satisfaction. Then, participants completed free-response questions about the most positive and negative parts of those relationships. She asked how they felt autism affected their relationships and gathered these components to identify what increased and decreased relationship satisfaction. What were the results of the study?: We found that autistic people are similarly satisfied in their relationships regardless of whether their partners are autistic or not. Despite this, participants consistently identified different positive and challenging factors within their relationships that tended to align with the neurotype of their partners. We found an interesting link between how autistic people view positive and negative factors in successful romantic relationships and their partners' neurotypes. What do these findings add to what was already known?: We added to a broad body of knowledge about relationship satisfaction by including a greater, more detailed consideration of autistic adults. Instead of comparing survey responses between autistic and non-autistic participants, we compared how autistic people viewed relationship satisfaction based on if their partners were autistic, non-autistic but still neurodivergent, or neurotypical. What are potential weaknesses in the study?: Potential limitations include the following: (1) we recruited a low number of male-identified participants, (2) we did not collect co-occurring diagnoses and conditions from the autistic participants, and (3) we did not verify partner neurotype. How will these findings help autistic adults now or in the future?: Through this project, we were able to highlight positive communication and interpersonal skills among autistic adults. We hope that the results of this study will help autistic people and their partners find some peace and community by reading about others with similar relationship experiences. We also hope to help them further understand what factors might serve as potential strengths and weaknesses in their relationships.

sheet.es: Si apoyas a una persona autista adulta en sus relaciones de pareja, puedes partir de que una pareja autista, neurotípica o neurodivergente no autista no determina por sí sola que la relación sea satisfactoria. Pregunta qué le funciona a ella: comprensión profunda, apoyo mutuo, adaptaciones. Es un estudio con encuestas y respuestas abiertas de 106 adultos autistas; la satisfacción fue similar en los tres tipos de pareja. Tiene límites: participaron pocos hombres, no se recogieron diagnósticos asociados y no se verificó el neurotipo de la pareja. No es una regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult with romantic relationships, you can start from this: having an autistic, neurotypical or non-autistic neurodivergent partner does not by itself decide whether a relationship is satisfying. Ask what works for them: deep understanding, mutual support, accommodations. This was a survey study with free-response questions, involving 106 autistic adults; satisfaction was similar across the three partner types. Its limits: few male-identified participants, co-occurring conditions were not collected, and partner neurotype was not verified. It is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen i parrelationer kan du utgå från att en autistisk, neurotypisk eller icke-autistisk neurodivergent partner inte ensam avgör om relationen blir tillfredsställande. Fråga vad som fungerar för just den personen: djup förståelse, ömsesidigt stöd, anpassningar. Det var en enkätstudie med fritextsvar från 106 autistiska vuxna; nöjdheten var likartad i alla tre partnertyper. Begränsningar: få manligt identifierade deltagare, samtidiga diagnoser samlades inte in och partnerns neurotyp verifierades inte. Det är ingen regel för alla.

title: Learning from the Experiences of Autistic Professionals Working in Health and Education.
authors: Curnow E, Maciver D, Johnston L, Murray M, Johnstone-Cooke V, Utley I, Jenkins N, Meff T, Muggleton J, Rutherford M
abstract: Background This study aimed to explore the experiences of autistic professionals working in the public sector in Scotland and investigate the factors that supported them in achieving employment in their chosen career. Methods We interviewed 34 autistic adults employed in professional roles in the health and education sectors in Scotland about their successes and challenges during training, recruitment, and employment. Interview conversations of 60-90-minute duration were transcribed verbatim. The research team, which included autistic and non-autistic researchers, conducted inductive thematic analysis. Results Resultant themes included complexity of disclosure; navigating differences in social communication and across employment stages; and control of the environment. Autistic professionals face inequalities and unsupportive environments. Participants described multifaceted decision-making processes behind choices to disclose or withhold their autism diagnosis, which could determine their right to workplace accommodations or provoke unfavorable treatment. The styles of communication preferred by colleagues could engender misunderstanding and lead to challenges negotiating social situations, recruitment processes, and organizational culture. Participants' needs and preferences for predictability and routine required them to use strategies to overcome the negative impacts of suboptimal social and physical environments. Conclusion Findings confirm the importance of acceptance and inclusion and demonstrate that there is a need for culture change within public sector education and health workplaces to improve accessibility. Applying minor changes to the environment and individual communication styles can enhance workplace conditions for autistic employees. Community brief Why is this an important issue?: Fewer autistic people are employed in skilled jobs than we would expect, and autistic graduates are less likely to be employed than graduates with any other disability. We need research to understand what helps autistic people in skilled work and career development, for example, through promotion. It is important that autistic people can follow their chosen career paths without risk to their health. What was the purpose of this study?: We wanted to know more about the experiences of autistic people employed in public sector professional roles in Scotland. We wanted to find out about work, training, and recruitment from their point-of-view. We wanted to understand what worked well, and what employers can improve. What did the researchers do?: We interviewed 34 autistic people working in professional roles in health or education in Scotland (including nurses, doctors, teachers, occupational therapists, clinical scientists, and radiographers). We thought about what people told us to help us understand their experiences. What were the results of the study?: Autistic professionals said that the decision to share their autism diagnosis at work was complicated. Before deciding to share this information, they thought about the risk of discrimination or stigma. They thought about how this might affect their access to support at work, and their wish to raise awareness of autism by acting as a role model. Sometimes colleagues communicated in ways which led to misunderstandings. Autistic employees told us that the habits and ways of working at their workplace did not suit them. They reported that work environments did not support their needs. This caused them stress and meant that they needed to find ways to stay in employment and look after their health. What do these findings add to what is already known?: We already know that autistic employees face discrimination and stress in the workplace. Our research confirms that there is a need for changes to support autistic professionals. The untrue or unfair views that colleagues have about autism (and other distinctions such as age, ethnicity, race, sex, social and economic status, or gender) create discrimination and prevent people receiving support at work or progressing in their career. What are the potential weaknesses in the study?: People who took part in this research were all professionals working in Scotland and were mainly White, female graduates. They had all been working for at least 2 years. This means that the training and recruitment they talked about may have happened some years ago. How will these findings help autistic adults now or in the future?: Participants highlighted challenges and difficulties they face at work that affect their health and limit career progression. Findings show that employers and colleagues need better understanding of autism to reduce discrimination and help autistic professionals feel supported and safe to talk about their needs. This would help employers work with autistic professionals to identify changes to workplace habits and ways of working, which can support the well-being and career progression of autistic professionals.

sheet.es: Si trabajas con una persona autista o eres su colega, pregúntale qué le ayudaría: comunicación clara y directa, rutinas previsibles y un entorno físico ajustado. Decidir si contar el diagnóstico es complejo, así que no la presiones. La evidencia viene de entrevistas con 34 profesionales autistas de salud y educación en Escocia. Sus límites: eran en su mayoría mujeres blancas con título universitario, con al menos 2 años de trabajo, y describen experiencias de un solo país que pueden haber cambiado. No sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you work alongside an autistic person or support one, ask what would help them: clear, direct communication, predictable routines and an adjusted physical environment. Deciding whether to share a diagnosis is complex, so avoid pressuring anyone. The evidence comes from interviews with 34 autistic professionals in health and education in Scotland. Its limits: participants were mainly White, female graduates who had worked for at least 2 years, in one country, and what they described about training and recruitment may be from some years ago. It is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du arbetar med en autistisk person eller stöttar en, fråga vad som skulle hjälpa: tydlig och direkt kommunikation, förutsägbara rutiner och en anpassad fysisk miljö. Att välja om man berättar om sin diagnos är komplicerat, så pressa ingen. Underlaget är intervjuer med 34 autistiska yrkesverksamma inom hälso- och sjukvård och utbildning i Skottland. Begränsningarna: deltagarna var främst vita, kvinnliga akademiker som arbetat i minst 2 år, i ett enda land, och det de berättade om utbildning och rekrytering kan ligga några år tillbaka. Det är ingen regel för alla.

title: Developing a consensus research definition for profound autism using a modified Delphi method.
authors: Siegel M, Lord CL, Tager-Flusberg H, Ursitti J, Halladay A, Singer AT
abstract: Background The diagnostic term, autism spectrum disorder, encompasses the full range of impairments associated with the autism spectrum, a significant change from earlier DSM definitions that identified various subtypes of autism. However, the majority of autism-related research and cultural representations in recent years has focused on autistic individuals with strong language and cognitive abilities. In 2021, the administrative term Profound Autism (PA) was proposed by a Lancet Commission to draw attention to autistic people whose impairments require lifelong, round-the-clock care. The initial definition of PA included a minimum age and requiring 24/7 access to an adult to ensure safety, and suggested considering IQ, and verbal ability when defining this group. However, researchers have subsequently utilized widely varying criteria in studies of this group, producing results that are difficult to compare and limit the potential for the identification of this group to advance knowledge about their strengths and needs. Methods To address the need for studies that use comparable samples and increase clarity in communication and interpretation of results, we carried out a systematic, multi-stage Delphi consensus study with over 70 participants who identified as researchers, caregivers, autistic individuals, and clinicians, to measure consensus on components of a research definition of PA. A series of questions was developed for the primary domains of interest. Results After two rounds of review and voting, 76% of the respondents agreed on a research definition of PA of: adaptive functioning well below age level, requiring adult supervision to ensure physical and mental health, safety and well-being, being at least 8 years old, diagnosed with ASD, and having severely impaired cognitive abilities (reflected by IQ score below 50) and/or not verbally communicating other than single words or fixed phrases used predominantly to have their basic needs met. Limitations Variations in access to measurement tools, as well as access to services across the world, limit the utility of this definition outside research practices, and a response rate of 58% yielded a final round sample size of 78 that may underrepresent portions of the stakeholder community and was overwhelmingly composed of respondents from the United States. Conclusions Based on these findings, a new working research definition of profound autism is proposed. Adoption of this definition could improve comparability across research studies, enhance the impact and generalizability of results, and better target interventions and supports for this high-needs group.

sheet.es: Si lees estudios sobre autismo profundo, fíjate en qué definición usan, porque varía mucho y los resultados no siempre se pueden comparar. Este trabajo propone una definición solo para investigación, no para decidir apoyos de una persona concreta. Fue un estudio Delphi con personas investigadoras, cuidadoras, autistas y clínicas: tras dos rondas, el 76% estuvo de acuerdo con una definición. Tiene límites: la tasa de respuesta fue del 58%, la muestra final fue de 78, casi toda de Estados Unidos, y el acceso a herramientas y servicios cambia según el país.
sheet.en: If you read studies on profound autism, check which definition they use, because it varies widely and results are not always comparable. This work proposes a definition for research only, not for deciding the supports of any one person. It was a Delphi study with researchers, caregivers, autistic people and clinicians: after two rounds, 76% agreed on a definition. It has limits: the response rate was 58%, the final sample was 78 and mostly from the United States, and access to tools and services differs between countries.
sheet.sv: Om du läser studier om djupt autism, kolla vilken definition de använder, eftersom den varierar mycket och resultaten inte alltid går att jämföra. Arbetet föreslår en definition enbart för forskning, inte för att avgöra en enskild persons stöd. Det var en Delphi-studie med forskare, anhöriga, autistiska personer och kliniker: efter två omgångar var 76% överens om en definition. Begränsningar: svarsfrekvensen var 58%, det slutliga urvalet var 78 och mest från USA, och tillgången till verktyg och insatser skiljer sig mellan länder.

title: Autonomic Function in Fragile X Syndrome: A Systematic Review.
authors: Weissgold S, Eley SEA, Wright D, McKechanie AG, Stanfield AC
journal: Journal of intellectual disability research : JIDR
abstract: Background Fragile X syndrome (FXS) is a monogenic X-linked cause of intellectual disability and autism. Individuals with FXS often have high levels of anxiety and sometimes display challenging behaviours. Autonomic dysfunction has been suggested to be one physiological mechanism that may contribute to these. Therefore, the objective of this review is to systematically examine existing evidence on autonomic function in FXS. Method An electronic literature search was conducted on OVID platforms (Medline, Embase and PsycINFO) and Web of Knowledge databases for references published before 22 April 2025, which physiologically measured autonomic function in FXS. A preregistered search strategy was designed to gather literature on the autonomic nervous system in FXS. Results A total of 1426 articles were identified, and 28 studies met the inclusion criteria. Samples comprised individuals across the lifespan (ages Conclusions The findings demonstrate evidence for autonomic hyperarousal as a clinical phenotype in FXS across the lifespan. Future work is required to define whether overactivation of the sympathetic nervous system, as indicated by hyperarousal in FXS, can be linked to clinical symptoms. Variations in sample demographics as well as in methodological approaches to measuring autonomic function both hinder accurate comparison of the results from included studies.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona con síndrome X frágil, puede ayudar tener en cuenta que su cuerpo quizá se active con más facilidad ante el estrés. Reducir ruido, imprevistos y exigencias, y ofrecer pausas tranquilas, es una idea razonable que probar. Es una revisión sistemática: de 1426 artículos identificados, 28 estudios cumplieron los criterios, con personas de distintas edades con síndrome X frágil. Sus resultados apuntan a hiperactivación autonómica a lo largo de la vida. Aún no se sabe si esto se relaciona con síntomas clínicos, y los estudios difieren en muestras y métodos, así que no vale igual para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you support someone with fragile X syndrome, it may help to know their body might become activated more easily under stress. Lowering noise, surprises and demands, and offering calm breaks, is a reasonable thing to try. This is a systematic review: of 1426 articles identified, 28 studies met the criteria, including people of different ages with fragile X syndrome. The findings point to autonomic hyperarousal across the lifespan. It is not yet clear whether this links to clinical symptoms, and the studies differed in samples and methods, so it will not apply equally to every person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en person med fragilt X-syndrom kan det vara bra att veta att kroppen kanske aktiveras lättare vid stress. Att minska buller, överraskningar och krav, och erbjuda lugna pauser, är rimligt att pröva. Detta är en systematisk översikt: av 1426 identifierade artiklar uppfyllde 28 studier kriterierna, med personer i olika åldrar med fragilt X-syndrom. Resultaten tyder på autonom överaktivering genom hela livet. Det är ännu oklart om detta hänger ihop med kliniska symtom, och studierna skilde sig i urval och metoder, så det gäller inte lika för alla.

title: Outcomes from the ASPEN intervention program: a randomized clinical trial of a culturally adapted parent-mediated intervention program in low-resource settings.
authors: Vanegas SB, Magaña S
abstract: This randomized controlled study examined the efficacy of a culturally adapted parent-mediated intervention for parents and young children with autism ( n = 45) from low-resource households (ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04505488). Families from these settings are often left out of autism intervention studies and arguably have unique needs not considered in autism intervention work. Parent/child dyads were randomized to the intervention group, which received 12 weekly sessions that included psychoeducation and coaching of evidence-based (EB) strategies with their children, or the comparison group who received all materials and 4 triweekly check-in sessions. We found that parents in the intervention group showed improvement in their self-efficacy (confidence) in using EB strategies, compared to the comparison group, and both groups improved in the use of EB strategies. Parents in the comparison group also improved in feeling more empowered and their children improved in social communication skills. These findings suggest that less intense parent interventions may be just as efficacious as those that require more regular participation for families from low-resource households. More research is needed to find the right balance and active ingredients to benefit these families. Clinical trial registration https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04505488, identifier NCT04505488.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a un niño autista pequeño y tienes poco tiempo o recursos, un programa breve con materiales y pocas revisiones puede ayudarte a practicar estrategias basadas en la evidencia con tu hijo. Los coaches semanales no son la única vía. Se trata de un ensayo aleatorizado con 45 familias con pocos recursos: un grupo tuvo 12 sesiones semanales con psicoeducación y coaching, y el otro recibió los materiales y 4 sesiones de seguimiento. Ambos grupos usaron mejor las estrategias; quienes tuvieron coaching ganaron más confianza. El grupo de comparación también mejoró en sentirse empoderado y sus hijos en comunicación social. El estudio es pequeño y aún no aclara qué componentes funcionan, así que no sirve como regla para todas las familias.
sheet.en: If you care for a young autistic child and have limited time or resources, a lighter program with materials and a few check-ins may help you practise evidence-based strategies with your child. Weekly coaching is not the only route. This was a randomized trial with 45 low-resource families: one group had 12 weekly sessions of psychoeducation and coaching, the other received the materials and 4 check-in sessions. Both groups used the strategies better; the coaching group gained more confidence. The comparison group also felt more empowered, and their children improved in social communication. The study is small and cannot show which parts work best, so it is not a rule for every family.
sheet.sv: Om du har ett litet autistiskt barn och begränsat med tid eller resurser kan ett lättare program med material och några uppföljningar hjälpa dig att öva evidensbaserade strategier med ditt barn. Veckovis coachning är inte den enda vägen. Det var en randomiserad studie med 45 familjer med små resurser: en grupp fick 12 veckovisa träffar med psykoedukation och coachning, den andra fick materialen och 4 uppföljningsträffar. Båda grupperna blev bättre på att använda strategierna; coachningsgruppen fick mer självförtroende. Jämförelsegruppen kände sig också mer stärkt och barnen förbättrades i social kommunikation. Studien är liten och visar inte vilka delar som fungerar bäst, så den är ingen regel för alla familjer.

title: Vowel acoustic parameters in speech assessment and rehabilitation of minimally verbal and speech-motor-impaired autistic children: a narrative review.
authors: Chen Y, Chen D
abstract: Speech production difficulties in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) are heterogeneous and are not uniformly characterized by articulatory impairment across the spectrum. However, some autistic subgroups, particularly minimally verbal children, children with low expressive-language ability, and those with suspected co-occurring speech-motor difficulties, may show atypical vowel-acoustic patterns. Because vowel production can be quantified through measures such as formant frequencies, vowel-space area, duration, and variability, these parameters may offer useful objective information for characterizing speech impairment and informing rehabilitation planning in selected phenotypes. This narrative review critically examined the literature on vowel-acoustic characteristics in autistic children and their possible relevance to rehabilitation-oriented systems. Structured searches of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were conducted for studies published up to September 2025. Evidence suggests that some autistic subgroups may exhibit reduced vowel distinctiveness, greater acoustic variability, and atypical temporal or dynamic speech features, although findings are heterogeneous and do not support a single uniform acoustic profile across ASD. Direct intervention evidence remains limited. Most rehabilitation-related studies are small, exploratory investigations, and the available literature is concentrated largely around Auditory-Motor Mapping Training (AMMT), an indirectly relevant speech-motor intervention that reports vowel-related outcomes but does not directly target vowel-acoustic parameters in isolation.Overall, vowel-acoustic measures are better regarded as candidate quantitative tools for subgroup characterization, monitoring, and rehabilitation planning rather than as universal biomarkers across ASD. Their translational potential is promising but remains insufficiently validated, requiring stronger longitudinal, mechanistic, and intervention research before broad clinical application can be justified.

sheet.es: Si una niña o un niño autista habla poco o con dificultad, conviene pedir a su logopeda una evaluación individual del habla, que puede incluir medir con precisión cómo produce las vocales. No todas las personas autistas tienen dificultades de articulación, así que no hay que suponerlo. Esta revisión narrativa analizó estudios publicados hasta septiembre de 2025. En algunos subgrupos, como niñas y niños con poco lenguaje verbal, las vocales pueden ser menos distintas y más variables. Los resultados son heterogéneos y los estudios de intervención son pocos y pequeños. Estas medidas aún no están suficientemente validadas para uso clínico general.
sheet.en: If an autistic child speaks little or finds speaking physically hard, you can ask their speech-language therapist about an individual speech assessment, which may include measuring precisely how they produce vowels. Not every autistic person has articulation difficulties, so it should not be assumed. This narrative review covered studies published up to September 2025. In some subgroups, such as minimally verbal children, vowels may be less distinct and more variable. Findings were mixed, and intervention studies were few and small. These measures are not yet well enough validated for general clinical use.
sheet.sv: Om ett autistiskt barn pratar lite eller har svårt att forma talet motoriskt kan du be barnets logoped om en individuell talbedömning, som kan inkludera att mäta exakt hur barnet uttalar vokaler. Alla autistiska personer har inte artikulationssvårigheter, så det bör inte antas. Den här narrativa översikten gick igenom studier publicerade till och med september 2025. I vissa undergrupper, till exempel minimalt verbala barn, kan vokalerna vara mindre tydligt åtskilda och mer varierande. Resultaten var blandade, och interventionsstudierna var få och små. Måtten är ännu inte tillräckligt validerade för bred klinisk användning.

title: Who benefits most? A randomized controlled trial for Parent-implemented social communication intervention for chinese-speaking autistic preschoolers.
authors: Wang L, Shi Y, So HC, Hirai HW, Qi X, To CKS, Ng FF, Wong PCM
abstract: Background Parent-implemented interventions (PIIs) are well established for improving developmental outcomes in autistic children. As evidence has accumulated, the field has increasingly shifted toward understanding for whom, and through which delivery formats PIIs can be most effectively implemented. These questions are pressing in non-Western contexts, where access to professional services is limited and culturally appropriate interventions are needed. This RCT, one of the largest of its kind in China, addressed this gap by comparing two scalable delivery formats (speech-language therapist [SLT]-led online groups vs. flexible Self-study format) of a culturally adapted social communication program and examining differential intervention responses and sustained engagement. Methods A total of 112 Chinese-speaking autistic children aged 24-60 months with limited spontaneous expressive language were randomized to a 20-week SLT-led or Self-study intervention. Autism severity, social functioning, and language skills were assessed at baseline, post-intervention, and 12 months after baseline. Parental stress, parenting sense of competence, and strategy use were also measured. Child, parent, and family baseline characteristics predicting differential outcomes and engagement were examined. Results No consistent differences between delivery formats were observed across most outcomes. Children's social functioning, expressive and receptive language showed improvement, and parental self-efficacy increased while stress decreased in both formats. Individualized analyses indicated greater benefits of the SLT-led format for children from lower-income families and those with greater developmental needs, whereas families with stronger baseline functioning showed comparable gains in the Self-study format. Attrition was higher in the Self-study format and was associated with lower child social skills and receptive languages, along with lower parental use of engagement-promoting behaviors and lower broader autism-related traits. Limitations Despite being one of the largest RCTs of its kind in China, the study may have been underpowered to detect small between-format differences, and the relatively modest sample size for the individualized machine-learning analyses limits the interpretation of these exploratory findings. Parental strategy use was measured using a general interaction coding scheme rather than intervention-specific behaviors. Higher attrition in the Self-study format warrants cautious interpretation, although sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of findings. Conclusions This study provides evidence supporting a culturally grounded PII associated with improvements in social functioning and language outcomes in autistic preschoolers, alongside increases in parental self-efficacy and reductions in parenting stress. Although no consistent differences between delivery formats were observed, SLT-led support appeared particularly beneficial for families with greater needs, whereas the Self-study format was sufficient for families with stronger baseline capacity, underscoring the importance of tailoring intervention formats to child and family characteristics. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05635760, registered on 23 November 2022.

sheet.es: Si le ofrecen un programa de comunicación social para madres y padres, conviene pensar qué formato encaja con su familia: con apoyo de una logopeda en línea o de estudio por cuenta propia. Un ensayo aleatorizado con 112 niños autistas chinos de 24-60 meses comparó ambos formatos durante 20 semanas. En general no hubo diferencias consistentes: el lenguaje y la comunicación social mejoraron, y el estrés de las familias bajó en los dos. El apoyo de la logopeda pareció ayudar más a familias con menos ingresos o con mayores necesidades. Límites: la muestra era modesta, esos análisis fueron exploratorios y más familias abandonaron el estudio por cuenta propia. No es una regla para cada niño.
sheet.en: If you are offered a parent-delivered social communication program, it is worth thinking about which format suits your family: online support from a speech-language therapist, or self-study. A randomized trial with 112 Chinese-speaking autistic children aged 24-60 months compared both formats over 20 weeks. Overall there were no consistent differences: social functioning and language improved, and parental stress fell in both. Therapist-led support seemed to help more for families with lower income or greater needs. Limits: the sample was modest, those analyses were exploratory, and more families dropped out of self-study. This is not a rule for every child.
sheet.sv: Om ni erbjuds ett socialt kommunikationsprogram för föräldrar kan det vara bra att fundera på vilket format som passar er familj: onlinestöd från en logoped eller självstudier. En randomiserad studie med 112 kinesisktalande autistiska barn i åldern 24-60 månader jämförde formaten under 20 veckor. I stort sett sågs inga konsekventa skillnader: social förmåga och språk förbättrades, och föräldrars stress minskade i båda. Logopedlett stöd verkade hjälpa mer för familjer med lägre inkomst eller större behov. Begränsningar: urvalet var måttligt, dessa analyser var utforskande och fler familjer hoppade av självstudierna. Det är ingen regel för varje barn.

title: Behavioral parent training for disruptive behaviors in school-age children with autism: Secondary outcomes of a randomized controlled trial.
authors: Dekkers TJ, Woelk M, Breider S, Hoekstra PJ, van den Hoofdakker BJ, de Bildt A
abstract: Children with autism often show disruptive behavior problems, which may cause significant impairment. Behavioral parent training is an effective intervention for other children with disruptive behavior, but research in children with autism is relatively scarce. We here report the secondary outcomes of a three-arm randomized controlled trial, comparing face-to-face and blended parent training to a waitlist control condition for children with autism and disruptive behavior. We previously found that face-to-face, but not blended parent training, relative to waitlist control, significantly improved children's noncompliance and irritability. Knowledge about its effects on parental functioning and other domains of children's functioning is limited. Using linear regression analyses on an intention-to-treat basis, we investigated parent training effects on a range of parenting (parental satisfaction, parental efficacy, parenting stress, and lax, overreactive and verbose parenting styles) and child outcomes (hyperactivity, emotional problems, conduct problems, peer problems, prosocial behavior, and adaptive behavior). We found that face-to-face, but not blended parent training, improved parental self-efficacy and decreased overreactive parenting relative to the waitlist condition. We found no intervention effects of either parent training format on any of the other outcomes. Overall, our findings add to the evidence for face-to-face behavioral parent training as an effective intervention for disruptive behavior in children with autism by illustrating that not only children but also parents improve. This randomized controlled trial was registered in the Dutch Trial Register (#22,042).

sheet.es: Si su hijo autista tiene conductas disruptivas y usted busca apoyo, puede valer la pena preguntar por programas de formación para madres y padres en formato presencial. En este estudio, ese formato mejoró la autoeficacia de los progenitores y redujo la crianza reactiva en exceso, frente a la lista de espera. El formato combinado (blended) no mostró esos efectos. Es un ensayo controlado aleatorizado con niños autistas en edad escolar y sus familias. Límites: no hubo efectos en otras áreas, como hiperactividad, problemas con compañeros o conducta adaptativa, y los resultados no valen igual para todas las familias.
sheet.en: If your autistic child has disruptive behavior and you are looking for support, it may be worth asking about face-to-face parent training programs. In this study, that format improved parents' sense of self-efficacy and reduced overreactive parenting compared with a waitlist. The blended format did not show these effects. It was a randomized controlled trial with school-age autistic children and their families. Limits: no effects were found in other areas, such as hyperactivity, peer problems or adaptive behavior, and results will not apply equally to every family.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn har störande beteenden och du söker stöd kan det vara värt att fråga efter föräldrastöd i form av träffar på plats. I den här studien stärkte det föräldrarnas tilltro till sin egen förmåga och minskade överreagerande föräldrastil jämfört med väntelista. Den kombinerade (blended) varianten gav inte dessa effekter. Det var en randomiserad kontrollerad studie med autistiska barn i skolåldern och deras familjer. Begränsningar: inga effekter sågs på andra områden, som hyperaktivitet, kamratproblem eller adaptivt beteende, och resultaten gäller inte lika för alla familjer.

title: Prevalence and incidence of autism in children and adolescents in Manitoba, Canada: An updated estimate using population-based administrative health data from 2011 to 2022.
authors: Singal D, Enns JE, Friesen K, Bopp K, Cameranesi M, Hanlon-Dearman A, Lai J, Nickel NC, Shooshtari S, Zwaigenbaum L, Brownell M
journal: Canadian journal of public health = Revue canadienne de sante publique
abstract: Objectives Estimates of autism prevalence are critical for informing evidence-based decisions, allocating resources, and developing effective strategies to support autistic individuals and their families. In Canada, such estimates remain limited, with the most recent population-based data on autism prevalence and incidence in Manitoba spanning 2004-2015, underscoring the need for more current data. Methods We used linked, whole-population administrative health and clinical data to develop a validated identification algorithm. We determined annual prevalence and incidence rates of autism among Manitoba children and adolescents aged 0-17 from 2011 to 2022, and conducted regression modelling to examine changes over time, adjusting for sex, geography, and socioeconomic variables. Results We identified 9396 children and adolescents diagnosed with autism during the study period. The prevalence of autism diagnoses was 0.58% (95% CI 0.55-0.60) in 2011 and 1.67% (95% CI 1.63-1.72) in 2022. The incidence of autism diagnoses was 0.79/1000 (95% CI 0.69-0.90) in 2011 and 3.06/1000 (95% CI 2.87-3.27) in 2022. We found statistically significant year-over-year increases in both prevalence and incidence. Conclusions Increasing autism prevalence indicates a pressing public health need for sustained investment in specialized healthcare services and supports that promote the full inclusion of autistic people in society. Strengthening surveillance systems across Canada is essential for generating high-quality population-based data to inform policy development and resource allocation and ensuring the health and social needs of autistic people and their families are met.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista en Manitoba, este estudio sugiere que cada vez más niñas, niños y adolescentes reciben un diagnóstico, así que conviene preguntar en tu zona por servicios y apoyos, y contar con que puede haber listas de espera. Es un estudio con datos administrativos de salud de toda la población de Manitoba, de 0 a 17 años, de 2011 a 2022. La prevalencia de diagnósticos pasó de 0.58% en 2011 a 1.67% en 2022. Sus límites: solo recoge personas con diagnóstico registrado, no explica por qué aumenta y no describe a cada persona ni otros lugares.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person in Manitoba, this study suggests more children and teenagers are being diagnosed, so it is worth asking locally about services and supports, and expecting that waiting lists may exist. It is a study of administrative health data covering the whole Manitoba population aged 0-17, from 2011 to 2022. The prevalence of autism diagnoses rose from 0.58% in 2011 to 1.67% in 2022. Its limits: it only counts people with a recorded diagnosis, it does not explain why the numbers rise, and it cannot describe any one person or other places.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person i Manitoba tyder studien på att allt fler barn och tonåringar får diagnos, så det är värt att fråga lokalt om tjänster och stöd och räkna med att det kan finnas väntelistor. Det är en studie av administrativa hälsodata för hela befolkningen i Manitoba, 0-17 år, från 2011 till 2022. Förekomsten av autismdiagnoser steg från 0.58% år 2011 till 1.67% år 2022. Begränsningar: den räknar bara personer med registrerad diagnos, förklarar inte varför siffrorna ökar och kan inte beskriva en enskild person eller andra platser.

title: The Relationship Between Interoception, Alexithymia, Autistic Traits and Eating Pathology in Autistic Adults.
authors: Westwood H, Mandy W, Brewer R
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: This study investigated the mechanisms underlying disordered eating of autistic adults, by investigating associations between eating disorder (ED) symptoms and autistic traits; autism-specific atypical eating; alexithymia; interoception; and body image in autistic and non-autistic participants. Autistic adults (n = 196) and non-autistic adults (n = 206) completed online self-report measures assessing ED pathology, atypical eating, body image dissatisfaction, interoception, alexithymia, and autistic traits. Structural Equation Modelling tested a theoretical model of the relationships between these variables, and whether these relationships were moderated by autism diagnosis. Autistic adults self-reported higher ED pathology than non-autistic adults. The proposed model and the strength of the relationship between body image and ED pathology did not differ between the autistic and non-autistic groups. Atypical eating (not related to over-evaluation of weight/shape), however, was only associated with ED pathology in the autistic group. Both traditional and additional factors, including eating disturbances not driven by weight/shape concern, appear to contribute to ED pathology in autism.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista tiene dificultades con la comida, conviene mirar más allá de la imagen corporal: también pueden influir formas atípicas de comer que no se deben a la preocupación por el peso o la figura. Si te preocupa, habla con un profesional sanitario que conozca el autismo. Es un estudio con 196 adultos autistas y 206 adultos no autistas que respondieron cuestionarios en línea. Los autistas informaron más síntomas de trastorno alimentario. Sus límites: son autoinformes en un solo momento, así que no muestran causas y no valen igual para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person struggles with eating, it helps to look beyond body image: atypical eating that is not driven by concern about weight or shape may also play a part. If you are worried, talk with a health professional who understands autism. This was a study of 196 autistic adults and 206 non-autistic adults who completed online questionnaires. Autistic adults reported more eating disorder symptoms. Its limits: it relied on self-report at one point in time, so it cannot show causes and does not apply equally to every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person har svårigheter med mat är det bra att se bortom kroppsbilden: ovanligt ätande som inte drivs av oro för vikt eller form kan också spela in. Om du är orolig, prata med vårdpersonal som förstår autism. Det var en studie med 196 autistiska vuxna och 206 icke-autistiska vuxna som fyllde i enkäter online. De autistiska vuxna rapporterade fler symtom på ätstörning. Begränsningar: studien bygger på självrapportering vid ett tillfälle, så den visar inte orsaker och gäller inte lika för alla.

title: Promoting Self-Determination in Young Adults with Autism: A Multicenter, Mixed Methods Study.
authors: Andrés-Gárriz C, Farriols Hernando N, Gómez Hinojosa AM, Pretel-Luque T, Fàbregues S, Mumbardó-Adam C
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Young people with autism have support needs related to self-determination that are currently not adequately addressed in Spain. This study aimed to assess the effectiveness, implementation, and acceptability of a program to support self-determination for young adults with autism in Spain. A multicenter, mixed methods randomized controlled trial (RCT) study was conducted (2020-2022). Young adults with autism between 17 and 30 years of age were recruited, and 40 were randomly assigned to the intervention or waiting-list group. Quantitative and qualitative data on outcomes relating to self-determination, program implementation and acceptability were collected at baseline, during, and after the intervention using several tools, including the SDI: SR and focus groups. Joint displays were used to integrate the quantitative and qualitative results for a comprehensive evaluation of the program. The quantitative results revealed no significant differences between the intervention and waiting list groups but indicated positive impacts on agentic actions and overall self-determination as reported by participants and caregivers. The qualitative results expanded the quantitative results by identifying personal and contextual barriers and facilitators of self-determination while offering deeper insights into the quantitative outcomes. Implementation fidelity was high, and the qualitative data provided areas for improvement and identified challenges and best practices. Program acceptability was high, and the group format proved useful. Our study provides the first empirical evidence of an intervention designed to promote self-determination in individuals with autism in Spain, but further research is needed. This trial was retrospectively registered at www.clinicaltrial.org (NCT05938751) on January 1 st , 2023.

sheet.es: Si apoyas a un joven autista, puedes ofrecerle ocasiones reales para elegir, fijarse metas y decidir sobre su día, mejor en grupo y con apoyo del entorno. Un ensayo aleatorizado en España incluyó a 40 jóvenes autistas de entre 17 y 30 años, asignados a un programa o a lista de espera. No hubo diferencias significativas entre grupos, aunque participantes y cuidadores percibieron mejoras en la acción autónoma y la autodeterminación. El programa se aplicó con fidelidad y fue muy aceptado, y el formato grupal resultó útil. Es un estudio pequeño y los autores indican que hace falta más investigación; no sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you support a young autistic person, you can offer real chances to choose, set goals and make decisions about their day, ideally in a group and with support from their surroundings. A randomized trial in Spain included 40 autistic young adults aged 17 to 30, assigned to a program or a waiting list. There were no significant differences between groups, although participants and caregivers reported positive impacts on agentic actions and overall self-determination. The program was delivered faithfully and was very well accepted, and the group format proved useful. It is a small study and the authors say more research is needed; it is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en ung autistisk person kan du ge verkliga möjligheter att välja, sätta mål och fatta beslut om sin dag, gärna i grupp och med stöd från omgivningen. En randomiserad studie i Spanien omfattade 40 autistiska unga vuxna mellan 17 och 30 år, fördelade på ett program eller en väntelista. Det fanns inga signifikanta skillnader mellan grupperna, men deltagare och vårdare upplevde positiva effekter på handlande på eget initiativ och på självbestämmande överlag. Programmet genomfördes som tänkt och togs emot mycket väl, och gruppformatet var användbart. Studien är liten och författarna menar att mer forskning behövs; den är ingen regel för alla.

title: Autistic Burnout on Reddit: A Sisyphean Struggle with Daily Tasks.
authors: Clarey MM, Abel S, Ireland MJ, Brownlow C
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: The crippling impacts of autistic burnout are well known to the autistic community, yet research is only in its early stages. While research to date has chiefly relied on structured interviews and Delphi studies, it has focused on defining and measuring burnout. What is missing from the research is an analysis of the broader experiences of autistic burnout, and the very real implications that autistic people face when impacted by it. This study reviewed the narratives of autistic people discussing their experiences of autistic burnout on the social media platform Reddit. Using data scraped from Reddit, quantitative and qualitative analyses were undertaken to elicit meaning from the online discourse. After analysing 249 Reddit threads using quantitative content analysis, the results supported existing research identifying three core components of autistic burnout, those being: chronic exhaustion; increased sensory sensitivities; and social withdrawal. New insights were found with users reporting physiological ailments as a complicating factor in their burnout experience. The research also found evidence supporting suggested treatment options for autistic burnout including reducing/stopping social obligations, reducing sensory inputs as much as possible, and time spent alone to reset and recharge. Most importantly, users identified that being autonomous in their recovery choices was critical to the success of their recovery.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista está en burnout, puede ayudar reducir o dejar las obligaciones sociales, bajar los estímulos sensoriales y dar tiempo a solas para recargar. Lo más importante es que ella misma decida cómo recuperarse. El estudio analizó 249 hilos de Reddit en los que personas autistas contaban su experiencia. Encontró agotamiento crónico, más sensibilidad sensorial y retraimiento social, además de molestias físicas que complican el burnout. Sus límites: son publicaciones en línea, no sabemos quién escribe ni si hay diagnóstico, y no prueba qué funciona para cada persona.
sheet.en: If an autistic person is in burnout, it may help to reduce or stop social obligations, cut sensory input as much as possible, and allow time alone to recharge. Most importantly, let them choose how to recover. The study analysed 249 Reddit threads where autistic people described their experiences. It found chronic exhaustion, increased sensory sensitivities and social withdrawal, plus physical ailments that complicate burnout. Its limits: these are online posts, so we cannot know who wrote them or confirm diagnoses, and it does not prove what works for any one person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person är i utbrändhet kan det hjälpa att minska eller sluta med sociala förpliktelser, dra ner på sinnesintryck så mycket som möjligt och ge tid ensam för att ladda om. Viktigast är att personen själv väljer hur hon eller han återhämtar sig. Studien analyserade 249 Reddit-trådar där autistiska personer beskrev sina erfarenheter. Den fann kronisk utmattning, ökad sensorisk känslighet och social tillbakadragenhet, samt kroppsliga besvär som försvårar utbrändheten. Begränsningar: det är inlägg på nätet, så vi vet inte vem som skrivit eller om diagnoser finns, och studien visar inte vad som fungerar för varje person.

title: Can a Short-Term Intervention Promote Growth Among Parents of Children with ASD?
authors: Baransi N, Scharf M
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: The present study investigated the effects of a short-term synergic growth mindset intervention towards abilities and towards stress on reducing parental stress and promoting stress-related growth (SRG) among Arab parents of children diagnosed with Autistic Spectrum Disorder (ASD). One hundred and seven parents (70 mothers, 37 fathers) of male children with ASD, completed several questionnaires, including a demographic questionnaire; the Childhood Autism Rating Scale, the Parenting Stress Index-Short Form, the revised Stress- Related Growth Scale, The Implicit Self-Theories Scale, and the Stress Mindset Scale. Seventy- two parents were randomly assigned to an "intervention group", and 35 to a comparison group. Members of the intervention group participated in a short synergic growth mindset intervention, created especially for this research. Six months after the intervention, all participants re-completed the same questionnaires. The intervention significantly increased growth mindset and SRG and decreased parental stress. This study demonstrates the effectiveness of a short-term intervention in promoting growth mindsets, reducing parental stress, and fostering SRG among parents of children with a chronic disorder. These findings are particularly important since many parents of children with chronic disorders often exhibit fixed mindset patterns due to their children's slow progress in various developmental domains.

title: AutInsight: A Pilot Randomised Controlled Trial (RCT) of a Consumer-Informed Parent Support Program for Parents of Autistic Children.
authors: Lee JYS, Whittingham K, Mitchell AE
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: AutInsight is an innovative, consumer-informed parent support program for parents of autistic children grounded in perspectives from qualitative research with autistic adults. The current study outlines the development and evaluation of AutInsight through a pilot randomised controlled trial. Parents (N = 41) of autistic children (10 years and younger) were randomly allocated to AutInsight (n = 20) or care-as-usual (n = 21) and completed online questionnaires across three timepoints (baseline, post-program and 3-month follow-up). Measures include parental sensitivity, parental acceptance and understanding, psychological flexibility, mindful parenting, parental mental health, overall family experience, quality of life, and child behaviours. Intent-to-treat analyses indicated greater rates of improvement for parents allocated to the AutInsight program, with small- to medium-sized effects for parent-reported parental sensitivity (EA-SR mutual attunement d = 0.84, EA-SR child involvement d = 0.50), as well as overall autism family experience (AFEQ total d = 0.38, AFEQ family life d = 0.29). Greater rates of improvement were also found in parent-reported child conduct problems (SDQ d = 0.62) and prosocial behaviours (SDQ d = 0.48). No significant results were found in observed parental sensitivity or any other measure. Results suggest preliminary evidence of effectiveness, feasibility and acceptability of the AutInsight program. A larger, fully powered trial is warranted. This trial was prospectively registered with the Australian and New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry (Trial ID: ACTRN12623000806662).

sheet.es: Si cuidas a un niño autista de 10 años o menos, puede valer la pena buscar programas de apoyo para madres y padres que se basen en la voz de personas autistas adultas, como AutInsight. Fue un ensayo piloto aleatorizado con 41 madres y padres, repartidos entre AutInsight o la atención habitual. Quienes hicieron el programa informaron más mejoras en sintonía con su hijo o hija y en la experiencia familiar. No hubo resultados significativos en la sensibilidad parental observada ni en otras medidas. Es un estudio pequeño, con cuestionarios respondidos por los propios padres, y hace falta un ensayo mayor. No es una regla para todas las familias.
sheet.en: If you parent an autistic child aged 10 or younger, it may be worth looking for parent support programs built on the voices of autistic adults, like AutInsight. This was a pilot randomised trial with 41 parents, assigned to AutInsight or care-as-usual. Parents in the program reported more improvement in attunement with their child and in overall family experience. There were no significant results for observed parental sensitivity or other measures. The study is small, relied on questionnaires parents filled in themselves, and a larger trial is needed. It is not a rule for every family.
sheet.sv: Om du är förälder till ett autistiskt barn som är 10 år eller yngre kan det vara värt att leta efter föräldrastöd som bygger på autistiska vuxnas perspektiv, som AutInsight. Studien var en randomiserad pilotstudie med 41 föräldrar, som fick antingen AutInsight eller vanlig vård. Föräldrarna i programmet rapporterade större förbättring i samspel med barnet och i familjens upplevelse. Inga signifikanta resultat sågs för observerad föräldrasensitivitet eller andra mått. Studien är liten, bygger på enkäter som föräldrarna själva fyllde i, och en större studie behövs. Den är ingen regel för alla familjer.

title: Professional Development in Autism and Multilingualism for Behavior Analysts: A Randomized Waitlist Control Trial.
authors: Martin Loya MR, Meadan H, Yan X
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Purpose Autistic children and their families from heritage-language-speaking homes are underrepresented in empirical research and would benefit from receiving care tailored to their linguistic and cultural needs. Board Certified Behavior Analysts (BCBAs) commonly support autistic children in the United States but have reported limited knowledge and training in how to support bilingual children, their families, nor the bilingual staff who support them. The following research question was addressed: Do BCBA leaders in autism care who complete an asynchronous online professional development training demonstrate (a) increased knowledge, (b) improved self-efficacy, and (c) improved attitudes toward supporting multilingual Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) staff and recipients of multilingual ABA services compared to BCBA leaders in a waitlist-control group? Method Part of a larger sequential exploratory mixed methods study, this randomized waitlist control trial measured the impacts of a professional development training related to autism and multilingualism in ABA care on BCBAs' knowledge, self-efficacy, and attitudes. Social validity data were also collected and analyzed using descriptive statistics. Results The training significantly increased the intervention group's knowledge and reported self-efficacy compared to participants in the waitlist control group but had no significant effect on participants' attitudes. In addition, participants perceived the training as socially valid. Conclusion Implications highlight the need for more attention on professional development research for autism providers, to examine pre-service training, and for clinical leaders to examine their workplace environment to promote effective and fair practices.

sheet.es: Si su hijo autista crece en un hogar donde se habla otra lengua, puede preguntar al equipo de análisis de conducta si ha recibido formación sobre multilingüismo y cómo tendrá en cuenta la lengua y la cultura de su familia. Este ensayo aleatorizado comparó a líderes BCBA que hicieron una formación en línea con otros en lista de espera. La formación aumentó su conocimiento y su autoeficacia, pero no cambió sus actitudes. Los participantes la consideraron útil. Sus límites: no midió resultados en niños ni familias, y no garantiza que cada profesional atienda mejor.
sheet.en: If your autistic child grows up in a home where another language is spoken, you can ask the behavior analysis team whether they have training in multilingualism and how they will respect your family's language and culture. This randomized trial compared BCBA leaders who took an online training with others on a waitlist. The training increased their knowledge and self-efficacy but did not change their attitudes. Participants found it socially valid. Limits: it did not measure outcomes for children or families, and it does not guarantee that every professional will offer better support.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn växer upp i ett hem där man talar ett annat språk kan du fråga beteendeanalysteamet om de har utbildning i flerspråkighet och hur de tar hänsyn till familjens språk och kultur. Denna randomiserade studie jämförde BCBA-ledare som gick en nätbaserad utbildning med andra på väntelista. Utbildningen ökade deras kunskap och tilltro till sin förmåga, men ändrade inte deras attityder. Deltagarna uppfattade den som användbar. Begränsningar: studien mätte inte resultat för barn eller familjer och garanterar inte att varje yrkesperson ger bättre stöd.

title: Using Artificial Intelligence to Improve Empathetic Statements in Autistic Adolescents and Adults: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
authors: Koegel LK, Ponder E, Bruzzese T, Wang M, Semnani SJ, Chi N, Koegel BL, Lin TY, Swarnakar A, Lam MS
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Challenges with social communication and social interaction are a defining characteristic of autism spectrum disorder (ASD). These challenges frequently interfere with making friendships, securing and maintaining employment, and can lead to co-occurring conditions. While face-to-face clinical interventions with trained professionals can be helpful in improving social conversation, they can be costly and are unavailable to many, particularly given the high prevalence of ASD and lack of professional training. The purpose of this study was to assess whether an AI program using a Large Language Model (LLM) would improve verbal empathetic responses during social conversation. Autistic adolescents and adults, 11-35 years of age, who were able to engage in conversation but demonstrated challenges with empathetic responses participated in this study. A randomized clinical trial design was used to assess the effects of the AI program (Noora) compared to a waitlist control group. Noora asks participants to respond to leading statements and provides feedback on their answers. In this study, participants were asked to respond to 10 statements per day 5 days per week for 4 weeks for an expected total of 200 trials. Pre- and post-intervention conversation samples were collected to assess generalization during natural conversation. Additionally pre- and post-intervention questionnaires regarding each participant's comfort during social conversation and participants' satisfaction with the AI program were collected. The results of this study demonstrated that empathetic responses could be greatly improved by using an AI program for a short period of time. Participants in the experimental group showed statistically significant improvements in empathetic responses, which generalized to social conversation, compared to the waitlist control group. Some participants in the experimental group reported improved confidence in targeted areas and most reported high levels of satisfaction with the program. These findings suggest that AI using LLMs can be used to improve empathetic responses, thereby providing a time- and cost-efficient support program for improving social conversation in autistic adolescents and adults.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista quiere practicar cómo responder con empatía en una conversación, un programa de IA como Noora puede ser una opción para ensayar en casa, siempre que ella lo desee. Conviene preguntarle qué objetivos tiene antes de empezar. Evidencia: ensayo clínico aleatorizado con adolescentes y adultos autistas de 11-35 años, que respondían a 10 frases al día, 5 días por semana durante 4 semanas, frente a un grupo en lista de espera. El grupo del programa mejoró sus respuestas empáticas, y la mayoría estuvo muy satisfecha. Límites: solo algunas personas refirieron más confianza, el estudio fue breve y no sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person wants to practise responding with empathy in conversation, an AI program like Noora may be one option to try at home, if they want to. It helps to ask what goals they have first. Evidence: a randomized clinical trial with autistic adolescents and adults aged 11-35, who answered 10 statements a day, 5 days a week for 4 weeks, compared with a waitlist group. The program group improved their empathetic responses, and most reported high satisfaction. Limits: only some reported more confidence, the study was short, and it is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person vill öva på att svara empatiskt i samtal kan ett AI-program som Noora vara ett alternativ att prova hemma, om personen själv vill det. Fråga gärna först vilka mål hen har.
