Evidens: en randomiserad klinisk studie med autistiska tonåringar och vuxna i åldern 11-35 år, som svarade på 10 påståenden om dagen, 5 dagar i veckan i 4 veckor, jämfört med en väntelistgrupp. Gruppen som använde programmet förbättrade sina empatiska svar, och de flesta var mycket nöjda. Begränsningar: bara några uppgav ökat självförtroende, studien var kort och gäller inte som regel för alla.

title: User experiences of the mobile stress autism mate (SAM) application: a qualitative study among autistic adults not receiving mental health care.
authors: van Asselt A, Roke Y, Hoeberichts K, Begeer S, Scheeren A
abstract: Background Autistic adults typically experience greater daily stress than their non-autistic counterparts, but professional mental health care is not always accessible or fitting. This qualitative study explored the user experiences of the Stress Autism Mate (SAM), a free co-created mobile application designed to reduce stress, among autistic adults not receiving mental health care. Methods A total of 15 autistic users (8 satisfied, 7 dissatisfied; aged 27-70; 4 men, 10 women, 1 non-binary) were recruited through a prior SAM trial database and autism-related social media groups for semi-structured online interviews. Interview questions were informed by the User Experience Technology Acceptance Model (UX-TAM), whereas themes were developed inductively through thematic analysis. Results Participants generally appreciated the SAM app's focus on enhancing stress recognition and its non-coercive, intuitive, and minimalist interface. Nevertheless, they found the app's stress tips insufficiently tailored to their context and the repeated login requirement frustrating. Satisfied users expressed a stronger need for stress-reducing support and greater trust in the app's developers and its scientific foundations. Dissatisfied users perceived the app's features as superficial and reported greater strain from attempting to adhere to its demands. Conclusions Despite the diverse user experiences, the findings highlight various avenues to improve the SAM app and similar standalone mHealth tools for autistic adults. Future adaptations should carefully balance the provision of structure and support with the risk of inducing technostress.

sheet.es: Si usas o piensas probar una app para el estrés, elige una que no presione, y deja de usarla si te genera más carga que alivio. Esto es un estudio cualitativo con entrevistas a 15 personas autistas adultas que usaron la app SAM y no recibían atención de salud mental. Valoraron que ayudara a reconocer el estrés y su diseño sencillo, pero los consejos les parecían poco adaptados y el inicio de sesión repetido les frustraba. Es un grupo pequeño y los resultados no sirven para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you use or want to try a stress app, choose one that doesn't pressure you, and stop using it if it adds more strain than relief. This was a qualitative study with interviews of 15 autistic adults who used the SAM app and were not receiving mental health care. They valued how it helped them recognise stress and its simple design, but found the tips poorly tailored and the repeated logins frustrating. It was a small group, so the findings do not apply to every person.
sheet.sv: Om du använder eller vill prova en stressapp, välj en som inte pressar dig, och sluta om den ger mer belastning än lättnad. Detta var en kvalitativ studie med intervjuer av 15 autistiska vuxna som använde appen SAM och inte fick psykiatrisk vård. De uppskattade att appen hjälpte dem att känna igen stress och dess enkla design, men tyckte att tipsen var dåligt anpassade och att de upprepade inloggningarna var frustrerande. Gruppen var liten, så resultaten gäller inte alla.

title: Enactivism in Autism Healthcare Practices: A Scoping Review.
authors: van Huizen JC, Teunisse JP, van Doormaal RH, Orgassa A, Staal WG, Strijbos DW
journal: Inquiry : a journal of medical care organization, provision and financing
abstract: IntroductionAutism support needs can be viewed as 'wicked problems', underpinned by various disrupting factors distributed across time and space. This complexity strains care providers' ability to act swiftly and decisively. An integrative autopoietic-enactive approach may offer guidance by taking the individual's interactional social-ecological system as the central unit of analysis. In clinical practice and research, however, this approach is only beginning to take shape. A lack of definition and codification hinders practical guidance and clinical innovation.MethodTo explore what autopoietic-enactive autism healthcare might mean in practice, this scoping review maps healthcare practices that are already based on autopoietic enactivism or bear affinity with it.ResultsForty-nine publications met with inclusion, representing 2.21% of the initial corpus. Findings were synthesized using four analytical lenses: aspects of (I) ecological-, (II) tangible-, (III), intersubjective- , and (IV) socio-cultural life , representing distinguishable albeit not separable dimensions of a person's social-ecological system.ConclusionOur findings present a rich but still loosely integrated picture of healthcare practices. This scoping review provides a reference point from which the approach may be further defined and consolidated into a clinical research field.

title: The impact of pregestational stress on neurodevelopment: Implications for autism spectrum disorder and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder.
authors: Ahmadian-Moghadam S, Saboory E, Roshan-Milani S
abstract: Emerging evidence indicates that stress experienced by parents before conception can influence offspring neurodevelopment through enduring neuroendocrine and epigenetic mechanisms. This review addresses the central question of how pregestational stress (PGS) might alter developmental trajectories and increase vulnerability to autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). We examined human and animal studies investigating the effects of PGS on germline epigenetic regulation, GABAergic signalling maturation and hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis programming. We synthesized key findings using a narrative review approach, integrating mechanistic data, developmental neurobiology and evidence for transgenerational inheritance, and we summarized the converging results in a conceptual figure and comprehensive table. The findings indicate that PGS can disrupt germline DNA methylation patterns, alter early GABA system development and shift hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis responsivity, thereby influencing fetal brain maturation and increasing the risk for ASD- and ADHD-related phenotypes. Additional evidence highlights that PGS might exert effects comparable to prenatal stress exposure, suggesting an overlooked but physiologically meaningful window of vulnerability. The conclusions emphasize that PGS represents a novel and under-recognized factor contributing to neurodevelopmental risk and that its mechanistic pathways offer new insight into how early-life vulnerability might begin even prior to pregnancy. The take-home message is that parental stress reduction and preconception health optimization might serve as promising strategies to mitigate intergenerational neurodevelopmental risk. The wider context underscores the broader physiological significance of PGS and raises important questions regarding the reversibility of epigenetic alterations, the timing and type of stressors most critical, and potential interventions to enhance resilience across generations.

sheet.es: Si estás pensando en tener un hijo, cuidar tu bienestar y buscar apoyo para reducir el estrés puede ser valioso en sí mismo, pero no es una garantía sobre el desarrollo futuro. Esta es una revisión narrativa de estudios en personas y en animales sobre el estrés de los progenitores antes de la concepción y su posible relación con el autismo y el TDAH. Sus límites: gran parte de los datos son mecanísticos o de animales, no prueba causas en una familia concreta y no debe usarse para culpar a nadie. El autismo tiene muchos orígenes.
sheet.en: If you are thinking about having a child, looking after your wellbeing and finding support to reduce stress can be worthwhile in itself, but it is not a guarantee about future development. This is a narrative review of human and animal studies on parents' stress before conception and its possible link to autism and ADHD. Its limits: much of the evidence is mechanistic or from animals, it does not show the cause in any one family, and it should never be used to blame anyone. Autism has many origins.
sheet.sv: Om du funderar på att skaffa barn kan det vara värdefullt i sig att ta hand om ditt mående och söka stöd för att minska stress, men det är ingen garanti för barnets framtida utveckling. Detta är en narrativ översikt av studier på människor och djur om föräldrars stress före befruktningen och dess möjliga koppling till autism och ADHD. Begränsningar: mycket av underlaget är mekanistiskt eller från djur, det visar inte orsaken i en enskild familj och ska aldrig användas för att lägga skuld på någon. Autism har många ursprung.

title: "My child before and now": parental perceptions of changes in functioning following participation in the global integration method (Método de Integração Global) in children with autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Netto RDCP, Souto DO, Rodrigues IC, Nascimento AAAC, Schumann CO, Nunes MC, Fernandes ACS, Silva ACC, Santana PAN, Cruz TKF
abstract: Introduction Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) impacts children's functioning and participation. Functionality-centered interventions, such as the Global Integration Method (Método de Integração Global-MIG), have been proposed in this context. Understanding parental perceptions is relevant to evaluate their effects on children's daily lives. Objective: To explore parental perceptions of changes in functioning following participation in the MIG program among children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), interpreted through the framework of the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF). Methods This qualitative study was conducted as an embedded component of an ongoing randomized controlled trial evaluating outcomes associated with participation in the MIG program in children with ASD. Parents of children allocated to the intervention group ( n = 18; aged 6-12 years), diagnosed with ASD and classified at support levels I and II, participated in three post-intervention focus groups. Results Findings were organized into three categories: previous experiences with conventional interventions, perceived changes following participation in MIG, and general perceptions of the program. Parents described previous interventions as fragmented, difficult to access, and associated with inconsistent functional experiences. Following participation in MIG, caregivers reported perceived changes related to body functions, particularly motor and communicative aspects, as well as changes in daily activities and social and school participation. Parents also described positive experiences regarding program organization, family support, and expectations regarding future participation and autonomy. Conclusion Parents reported perceived changes in functioning following participation in MIG and described positive experiences related to the intervention process.

sheet.es: Si valoras un programa para tu hijo o hija, pregunta cómo se organiza, si acompaña a la familia y qué objetivos cotidianos persigue, y observa qué cambios notas tú en casa y en la escuela. En este estudio cualitativo, integrado en un ensayo aleatorizado en curso, 18 madres y padres de niños autistas de 6-12 años (niveles de apoyo I y II) hablaron en tres grupos de discusión tras el programa MIG. Contaron cambios percibidos en lo motor, la comunicación, la vida diaria y la participación social y escolar. Límites: son percepciones de las familias, sin medidas objetivas, y no demuestran que el programa funcione ni sirva para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you are weighing up a programme for your child, ask how it is organised, whether it supports the family, and what everyday goals it aims for, then note what changes you see at home and at school. This qualitative study, embedded in an ongoing randomised trial, held three focus groups with parents of 18 autistic children aged 6-12 (support levels I and II) after the MIG programme. Parents described perceived changes in movement, communication, daily activities, and social and school participation. Limits: these are parents' perceptions, not objective measures, so they do not show that the programme works or suits every child.
sheet.sv: Om du överväger ett program för ditt barn, fråga hur det är upplagt, om det stöttar familjen och vilka vardagsmål det har, och notera vilka förändringar du själv ser hemma och i skolan. Den här kvalitativa studien, en del av en pågående randomiserad studie, höll tre fokusgrupper med föräldrar till 18 autistiska barn i åldern 6-12 år (stödnivå I och II) efter programmet MIG. Föräldrarna beskrev upplevda förändringar i motorik, kommunikation, vardagsaktiviteter samt social och skolrelaterad delaktighet. Begränsningar: det är föräldrarnas upplevelser, inte objektiva mått, och de visar inte att programmet fungerar eller passar alla barn.

title: Beyond the Outburst: Charting a New Frontier for Understanding and Treating Irritability in Autistic Adults.
authors: Lin HY, Westover AN, Lutz ASF, Jha MK
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Irritability is a prevalent and impairing feature associated with autism, yet remains poorly understood, particularly in adults. Drawing heavily on insights translated from pediatric and transdiagnostic literatures, we propose that irritability in autistic individuals often reflects a psychophysiological stress or threat response, rooted in a vulnerable neurobiology (e.g., sensory sensitivities, intolerance of uncertainty), but may also stem from intrinsic neurobiological dysregulation independent of environmental triggers. The current treatment paradigm for autistic adults, largely extrapolated from pediatric antipsychotic trials, leaves these adults critically underserved due to a lack of evidence-based treatments, clinical trials, or validated tools to measure their internal experience. This viewpoint deconstructs irritability, differentiating its affective nature from aggression, and highlights heterogeneity across the lifespan and support needs. We critique the limitations of current assessment methods and recommend a shift toward a multi-modal strategy integrating self-report (when feasible) with objective, physiologically-informed tools (e.g., wearable biosensors) and nuanced observer reports. We argue that the field is poised for neuroscience-informed treatment innovation-including novel pharmacological agents and adapted psychosocial interventions-but is hampered by a lack of rigorous clinical trials in adults. Finally, we call for mechanistically driven trials to address the large unmet burden of inadequately treated irritability, ultimately improving the quality of life for autistic adults and their families/caregivers.

sheet.es: Cuando una persona autista adulta esté irritable, conviene mirar primero qué puede estar estresándola: sensibilidades sensoriales, incertidumbre o cambios inesperados. Reducir esos factores y preguntarle cómo se siente, si puede explicarlo, suele ser un buen comienzo. Es una revisión con enfoque de punto de vista, basada en literatura sobre infancia y otros diagnósticos, no un estudio con participantes nuevos. Sus autores proponen que la irritabilidad puede ser una respuesta de estrés o amenaza, y señalan que faltan ensayos clínicos en adultos. No sirve como regla para todas las personas. Si surgen dudas médicas, corresponde decidirlas con un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: When an autistic adult is irritable, it helps to first look at what may be stressing them: sensory sensitivities, uncertainty or unexpected changes. Reducing those and asking how they feel, if they can say, is often a good start. This is a viewpoint-style review drawing on literature about children and other diagnoses, not a study with new participants. Its authors suggest irritability can be a stress or threat response, and note that clinical trials in adults are lacking. It is not a rule for every person. Any medical questions are for a clinician to decide with the person.
sheet.sv: När en autistisk vuxen är irriterad kan det hjälpa att först se vad som kan stressa: sensoriska känsligheter, osäkerhet eller oväntade förändringar. Att minska dem och fråga hur personen mår, om hen kan förklara det, är ofta en bra början. Detta är en översikt i åsiktsform som bygger på litteratur om barn och andra diagnoser, inte en studie med nya deltagare. Författarna menar att irritabilitet kan vara en stress- eller hotrespons och påpekar att kliniska studier på vuxna saknas. Det är ingen regel för alla. Medicinska frågor avgörs tillsammans med en kliniker.

title: Diagnostic inflation in autism spectrum disorder: an epistemological and methodological reappraisal.
authors: Croce L, Fusaro I
abstract: Background The reported prevalence of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) has risen nearly fourfold over two decades, fuelling debate about whether DSM-5 boundaries still demarcate a coherent clinical category. Between 2020 and 2025, multiple independent research groups have produced a convergent body of critical reflection on this question. Aim This narrative review is an argumentative reappraisal addressing three convergent failures - classificatory, sociocultural, and methodological - and asking what minimum evidentiary standards should govern adult ASD differential diagnosis in complex cases. Four sub-themes traditionally treated separately (sensory profile, female phenotype, personality-disorder differential diagnosis, care-pathway implications) are presented as convergent illustrations of one underlying problem. Methods Narrative integration of peer-reviewed publications (2015-2026) on ASD diagnostic validity, phenotypic and genetic heterogeneity (Type I/Type II partition; Litman et al. SPARK analysis), sensory processing specificity, female phenotype and camouflaging, and differential diagnosis with seven conditions: Borderline, Avoidant, and Schizotypal Personality Disorders; Complex PTSD; ADHD with affective dysregulation; Bipolar Spectrum; OCD-spectrum disorders; and adult disorganised attachment. Literature-identification methods and AI-assisted search with author verification are detailed in Section 1.3. Findings The category aggregates at least two neurobiologically distinct phenotypes - Type I, prototypical, often syndromic, with high genetic load; and Type II, polygenically driven, milder, overlapping with general psychopathology - differentially affected by routine-assessment limitations. The DSM-5 sensory criterion, though neurobiologically grounded, lacks diagnostic specificity. The cross-sectional, single-source, self-report-based model dominating practice is structurally inadequate for Type II presentations and the female phenotype. Recommendations Six minimum standards are specified: structured developmental history with ≥2 informants; multi-context behavioural observation; neuropsychological profiling; granular sensory assessment by modality, direction, and contextual stability; systematic evaluation of alternative diagnoses; and longitudinal formulation with revisability. Specialised pathways should use stepped multidisciplinary triage when differential diagnosis remains unresolved, directing individuals to appropriate parallel or alternative services rather than denying care. A minimum feasible standard for under-resourced settings is articulated alongside the ideal one. Conclusion Restoring diagnostic specificity to ASD is not opposed to the neurodiversity framework. It is the precondition for ensuring that the diagnostic label, when applied, identifies a population for which evidence-based interventions exist and the care pathway is appropriate.

sheet.es: Si buscas una evaluación diagnóstica de autismo para un adulto en un caso complejo, puede ayudar preguntar si incluirá la historia del desarrollo con al menos 2 informantes, observación en varios contextos, una evaluación sensorial detallada y el estudio de otras explicaciones posibles. Es una revisión narrativa de publicaciones sobre validez diagnóstica, y propone seis estándares mínimos. También plantea que, si el diagnóstico sigue sin aclararse, la persona sea derivada a otros servicios en lugar de quedarse sin atención. Sus límites: es una argumentación de los autores, no un ensayo, y no demuestra qué ocurre en una persona concreta. Conviene comentar cada caso con el equipo clínico.
sheet.en: If you are seeking an autism assessment for an adult in a complex case, it may help to ask whether it will include developmental history from at least 2 informants, observation in several settings, detailed sensory assessment, and checking other possible explanations. This is a narrative review of published work on diagnostic validity, and it proposes six minimum standards. It also says that when the diagnosis stays unclear, people should be directed to other suitable services rather than denied care. Its limits: it is the authors' argued position, not a trial, and it cannot show what will be true for one particular person. Discuss each case with the clinical team.
sheet.sv: Om du söker en autismutredning för en vuxen i ett komplext fall kan det hjälpa att fråga om den omfattar utvecklingshistoria från minst 2 informanter, observation i flera miljöer, en detaljerad sensorisk bedömning och prövning av andra möjliga förklaringar. Det är en narrativ översikt av publicerad forskning om diagnostisk validitet och den föreslår sex minimistandarder. Den menar också att den som inte får ett klart svar bör hänvisas till andra lämpliga insatser i stället för att nekas vård. Begränsningar: det är författarnas argumentation, inte en studie med deltagare, och den visar inte vad som gäller för en enskild person. Diskutera varje fall med det kliniska teamet.

title: Psychiatric difficulties in females with fragile X syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analyses.
authors: Jenner L, Koenig C, Hantman RM, Hogan AL, Roberts JE, Klusek J
abstract: Introduction Fragile X syndrome (FXS) is the most common monogenic cause of autism, yet research has largely prioritized males. Females show more variable phenotypes and remain comparatively understudied. This paper provides the first systematic review and meta-analysis of psychiatric difficulties in females with FXS, examines associations with intellectual ability and co-occurring autism, and evaluates sex representation within the FXS psychiatric literature. Methods Systematic searches of PsycINFO, MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science identified English-language, peer-reviewed studies published between 1980 and 2025 reporting psychiatric conditions or symptoms in females with FXS. Of 3,533 records screened, 37 studies met inclusion criteria. Findings were synthesized narratively, and random-effects meta-analyses estimated prevalence of psychiatric difficulties. Results A pronounced sex imbalance was observed, with male-focused studies outnumbering female-focused studies by approximately 4:1. Anxiety, depression, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), aggression, and self-injury were most commonly reported. Meta-analyses indicated high prevalence of anxiety (57%) and depression (41%), with substantial heterogeneity partly attributable to age variability across samples. Less heterogeneous prevalence estimates were observed for ADHD (33%), aggression (20%), and self-injury (14%). Co-occurring autism was consistently associated with greater psychiatric vulnerability, whereas intellectual ability showed no consistent associations. Conclusion Females with FXS exhibit a marked vulnerability to psychiatric difficulties. However, their ongoing underrepresentation in research suggests that the present findings likely underestimate the true level of psychiatric risk. These findings highlight the importance of developing more refined, sex-specific models of psychopathology in FXS, informed by advances in autism research, to enhance the recognition, understanding, and support for females.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una niña o mujer con síndrome del X frágil, conviene fijarse con regularidad en señales de ansiedad, tristeza, atención o malestar, y hablar de ellas con su profesional de salud, aunque parezca que le va bien. La evidencia es un metaanálisis de 37 estudios en mujeres con este síndrome; la ansiedad aparecía en el 57% y la depresión en el 41%, y la autolesión en el 14%. Los límites: hay muchos más estudios con hombres, las edades variaban mucho y las cifras pueden quedarse cortas; no describen a cada persona. Si te preocupa una autolesión o su seguridad, consulta con un profesional de salud o un servicio de crisis; si hay peligro inmediato, llama al número de emergencias de tu país.
sheet.en: If you support a girl or woman with fragile X syndrome, it helps to check in regularly about anxiety, low mood, attention or distress, and to raise them with her health professional, even when things seem to be going well. The evidence is a meta-analysis of 37 studies of females with this syndrome: anxiety appeared in 57%, depression in 41% and self-injury in 14%. Limits: far more studies focused on males, ages varied a lot, and the figures may be underestimates; they do not describe any one person. If you are worried about self-injury or her safety, contact a clinician, a health service or a crisis service; in immediate danger, call your country's emergency number.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en flicka eller kvinna med fragilt X-syndrom är det bra att regelbundet fråga om oro, nedstämdhet, uppmärksamhet eller obehag och ta upp det med hennes vårdkontakt, även när det verkar gå bra. Underlaget är en metaanalys av 37 studier av kvinnor med syndromet: ångest förekom hos 57 %, depression hos 41 % och självskada hos 14 %. Begränsningar: många fler studier handlade om män, åldrarna varierade mycket och siffrorna kan vara för låga; de beskriver inte en enskild person. Om du oroar dig för självskada eller hennes säkerhet, kontakta en läkare, vården eller en krisjour; vid akut fara, ring landets nödnummer.

title: "I Accept Them, They Accept Me, We Enjoy Our Time Together": Autistic Adults' Preferences and Perceptions of Relationships With Other Autistic People.
authors: Minnell H, Waddington H, Jordan P, Noble B, Bowden CJ
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Autistic adults may have distinct relationship preferences and perceptions compared to non-autistic individuals. The Double Empathy Problem suggests that autistic people often experience greater mutual understanding and connection when interacting with other autistic individuals. While some research has examined these relationships, few studies have focused on a range of relationship types. This study aimed to address this gap by qualitatively exploring how autistic adults prefer and perceive their relationships with other autistic people across friendships, romantic relationships, mentoring/support, employment, and volunteering relationships. We surveyed autistic adults living in Australia and New Zealand to better understand their preferences and perceptions regarding these relationships. Written responses from 142 participants were analysed using a reflexive thematic analysis framework. Many autistic adults valued intersubjectivity, mutual understanding, and acceptance in their relationships with other autistic individuals. Within these relationships, they could be authentic and unmask; however, they also had to consider and balance their relational capacity. In addition, some participants experienced conflict in their relationships due to differences in compatibility. While within-neurotype relationships are beneficial for many autistic individuals, they are not always seamless, and challenges and conflicts can still arise. Like all relationships, autistic-autistic relationships are complex and nuanced.Lay AbstractMany autistic people enjoy spending time with other autistic individuals because they feel more comfortable and better understood in these relationships. While some research has explored autistic adults' relationships with other autistic people, less is known about their preferences and perceptions within these relationships. To learn more, we surveyed autistic adults in Australia and New Zealand about a range of relationship types they may have with other autistic people (i.e. friendships, romantic relationships, mentoring/support, employment, and volunteering relationships). We then analysed written responses from 142 participants using a reflexive thematic analysis to identify themes within the data set. Participants valued intersubjectivity, mutual understanding, acceptance, and a sense of belonging and described being able to unmask and be authentic in these relationships. However, they also had to consider and balance their relational capacity. While shared neurotype was important, other factors like shared interests, values, and emotional compatibility also influenced relationship satisfaction. Some participants also described challenges or conflicts due to differences in compatibility. These findings highlight that many autistic adults have meaningful relationships with other autistic people, challenging a deficit-based perspective. At the same time, they show that shared neurotype alone does not guarantee compatibility. Instead, the Double Empathy Problem should be understood as a spectrum influenced by factors such as shared life experience and social understanding, reminding us that, like all relationships, those between autistic people are complex and nuanced.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista adulta, puedes ofrecerle oportunidades de conocer a otras personas autistas (amistad, apoyo entre iguales, voluntariado), sin darlo por garantizado. Pregúntale qué le gustaría. Este estudio cualitativo encuestó a 142 personas autistas adultas de Australia y Nueva Zelanda; sus respuestas escritas se analizaron por temas. Muchas valoraron sentirse comprendidas y aceptadas, y poder ser auténticas sin enmascarar. También señalaron que compartir neurotipo no asegura compatibilidad: importan los intereses, los valores y la energía social disponible, y a veces surgen conflictos. Los resultados reflejan solo a quienes respondieron y no valen como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult, you can offer chances to meet other autistic people (friendship, peer support, volunteering) without assuming it will suit them. Ask what they would like. This qualitative study surveyed 142 autistic adults in Australia and New Zealand, and their written answers were analysed for themes. Many valued feeling understood and accepted, and being able to be authentic and unmask. They also said a shared neurotype does not guarantee compatibility: interests, values and available social energy matter, and conflicts sometimes arise. The findings reflect only the people who responded and are not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen kan du erbjuda möjligheter att träffa andra autistiska personer (vänskap, kamratstöd, volontärarbete), utan att anta att det passar. Fråga vad personen vill. Den här kvalitativa studien undersökte 142 autistiska vuxna i Australien och Nya Zeeland, och deras skriftliga svar analyserades tematiskt. Många värdesatte att känna sig förstådda och accepterade och att kunna vara autentiska utan att maskera. De sa också att delad neurotyp inte garanterar kompatibilitet: intressen, värderingar och social energi spelar roll, och ibland uppstår konflikter. Resultaten speglar bara dem som svarade och är ingen regel för alla.

title: Understanding Autistic Adults' Psychological Experiences of Anxiety Problems: A Qualitative Interview Study.
authors: Roberts-Davis RJ, Happé FG, Lau-Zhu A
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Our understanding of psychological experiences of anxiety in autism could be improved if it were shaped by autistic individuals. However, anxiety research in autism often begins with cognitive conceptualisations drawn from neurotypical or non-autistic individuals. This qualitative study aimed to explore psychological experiences of anxiety using semi-structured one-to-one interviews with a diverse sample of 20 U.K.-based, autistic adults, aged 18-55 years. Transcripts were analysed using two complementary methods: conceptual content analysis, where existing theories were tested against the data with predefined codes; and reflexive thematic analysis, where meaning was constructed from the data while considering research subjectivity. Our sample highly endorsed existing cognitive constructs: intolerance of uncertainty (100% of participants), repetitive negative thinking (100%), attentional biases (70%) and intrusive mental imagery (70%). Some autism-specific characteristics were indicated. The endorsement of imagery is particularly striking given claims that autism is often associated with weak imagery. Autistic adults described the way in which being autistic interacted with anxiety, through psychological and lived experiences. Existing support for anxiety problems was deemed insufficient and may be improved by further refining our understanding of anxiety in autism through future quantitative and qualitative research.Lay AbstractAnxiety is a top priority for research for the autistic community. We could increase our understanding of what might contribute to anxiety problems in autism by speaking to autistic people and learning about the different experiences they have had. We interviewed 20 U.K.-based autistic adults (aged 18-55 years) and asked them about their anxiety problems, including how they felt about well-known ideas of what might be involved in anxiety in autism. We looked at the answers to the interviews in two ways. The first way considers what autistic people think about the well-known ideas. The second way looks at similarities in the answers that autistic people gave. All participants' anxiety problems involved repeated negative thoughts and struggling with uncertain situations. Most also said that they tend to focus on noises or other sensory experiences within their environment and imagine situations in their mind when they are anxious. Being autistic came with challenges that could make them more anxious, including struggling with changes to routine and being bullied. Autistic people described how anxiety made their life difficult and ways in which current support for anxiety is not helpful enough. We discuss ways that we could better understand anxiety in autism and improve the support given to autistic people.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista adulta que vive con ansiedad, pregúntale cómo la vive ella, en lugar de suponer que sabes qué la causa. Este estudio de entrevistas incluyó a 20 personas autistas adultas del Reino Unido, de 18-55 años. Todas describieron pensamientos negativos repetidos y dificultad con la incertidumbre; el 70% habló de imágenes mentales intrusivas. También mencionaron los cambios de rutina y el acoso como fuentes de ansiedad, y dijeron que el apoyo actual no les basta. Como es un estudio cualitativo con una muestra pequeña, no sirve como regla para todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult who lives with anxiety, ask how they experience it rather than assuming you know what drives it. This interview study included 20 autistic adults from the U.K., aged 18-55 years. All described repeated negative thoughts and difficulty with uncertainty; 70% described intrusive mental imagery. They also named changes to routine and being bullied as things that raised anxiety, and said current support was not enough. It is a qualitative study with a small sample, so it is not a rule for every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen som lever med ångest: fråga hur hen själv upplever den, i stället för att anta att du vet vad som ligger bakom. Den här intervjustudien omfattade 20 autistiska vuxna i Storbritannien, 18-55 år. Alla beskrev upprepade negativa tankar och svårigheter med osäkerhet; 70% beskrev påträngande inre bilder. De nämnde också ändrade rutiner och mobbning som saker som ökade ångesten, och sa att dagens stöd inte räcker. Studien är kvalitativ med ett litet urval och gäller därför inte som regel för alla autistiska personer.

title: Artificial intelligence, autism care, and health equity: a public health narrative review.
authors: Han X, Weng L, Xu H
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a common, lifelong neurodevelopmental condition whose recorded prevalence, diagnostic delays, and uneven distribution of specialist services create a growing public health challenge. Conventional screening and diagnostic pathways depend heavily on scarce specialist expertise, contributing to long waiting times and unequal access across income settings, regions, sex, ethnicity, language, and social position. This narrative review synthesises current applications of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning in autism screening, diagnostic support, intervention, and longitudinal monitoring, and reframes the evidence through a public health and health equity lens. We argue that AI's most important contribution to autism care is unlikely to lie in marginal improvements in classification accuracy alone. Rather, its potential value lies in expanding access, supporting task-sharing, shortening diagnostic pathways, enabling population-oriented screening, and reaching under-recognised groups such as girls and women, adults, ethnic and linguistic minorities, and populations in low-resource settings. At the same time, AI may create an equity paradox: technologies intended to reduce disparities may reproduce or amplify them if they are trained on non-representative data, deployed across a digital divide, or governed without adequate attention to privacy, accountability, and community trust. Whether AI narrows or widens autism-related health inequalities will depend on choices about data diversity, low-resource design, co-design with autistic communities, equity-sensitive evaluation, clinical integration, and proportionate regulation.

sheet.es: Si le ofrecen una herramienta de inteligencia artificial para cribado o apoyo diagnóstico, úsela como ayuda y no como veredicto: pregunte con qué datos se entrenó, cómo se protege la privacidad y quién revisa el resultado. Es una revisión narrativa que reúne usos de la IA en cribado, diagnóstico, intervención y seguimiento, con enfoque de equidad en salud. Sostiene que la IA puede ampliar el acceso, pero también aumentar desigualdades si usa datos poco representativos o si hay brecha digital. Es una revisión, no una prueba de que una herramienta concreta funcione para cada persona autista, y no sustituye la valoración de profesionales.
sheet.en: If you are offered an artificial intelligence tool for autism screening or diagnostic support, treat it as an aid, not a verdict: ask what data it was trained on, how privacy is protected, and who reviews the result. This is a narrative review that brings together uses of AI in screening, diagnosis, intervention and monitoring, seen through a health equity lens. It argues AI could widen access, but may also deepen inequalities if trained on non-representative data or used across a digital divide. As a review, it does not show that any specific tool works for every autistic person, and it cannot replace assessment by professionals.
sheet.sv: Om du erbjuds ett AI-verktyg för autismscreening eller diagnostiskt stöd, se det som ett hjälpmedel och inte som ett utlåtande: fråga vilken data det tränats på, hur integriteten skyddas och vem som granskar resultatet. Det här är en narrativ översikt som samlar användningar av AI i screening, diagnostik, insatser och uppföljning, sedd ur ett jämlikhetsperspektiv. Den menar att AI kan öka tillgången, men också förstärka ojämlikhet om den tränas på icke-representativ data eller används trots digitala klyftor. Som översikt visar den inte att ett visst verktyg fungerar för varje autistisk person, och den ersätter inte bedömning av yrkespersoner.

title: Beyond Behavior Reduction: A Clinical Perspective on Integrating Developmental, Psychological, and Family-Centered Frameworks into Community ABA Implementation.
authors: Mambuca AF
abstract: Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) is recognized as among the most empirically supported interventions for autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and related neurodevelopmental conditions. This clinical perspective examines the gap between controlled research efficacy and community-based implementation by integrating insights from developmental psychology, family systems theory, and implementation science. The paper argues that several limitations sometimes observed in long-term functional outcomes are better understood as challenges of community-level implementation rather than deficiencies of behavioral principles themselves. Furthermore, dimensions occasionally described as "missing" from behavioral practice-including attention to covert behavior, family systems, emotional regulation, and lifespan adaptation-already fall within contemporary best practice, though they may be applied inconsistently across diverse service contexts. Rather than positioning these dimensions as external to behavior analysis, this paper proposes an explicitly interdisciplinary, family-centered, and lifespan-oriented framework in which behavioral science is embedded within structured caregiver preparation, clear referral pathways, and neurodiversity-affirming goals. Key recommendations include flexible service delivery models aligned with family realities; integrated family stress screening and mental-health referral pathways; workforce training in developmental psychology and emotional regulation; and lifespan-oriented outcome measurement beyond behavior reduction. The paper concludes that ABA's contributions to autism intervention are profound and not in dispute; rather, the field benefits from expanding implementation contexts to address the full scope of neurodevelopmental care and family support. This perspective is intended to generate empirical investigation of proposed service-design innovations and to inform clinical practice in community-based ABA settings serving diverse, underserved populations.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija recibe ABA, pregunte al equipo cómo trabajan con la familia, qué lugar tienen las emociones y qué metas piensan a largo plazo, más allá de reducir conductas. También puede preguntar si hay apoyo para el estrés familiar y derivación a salud mental. La evidencia es una revisión de perspectiva clínica: un texto que argumenta, no un estudio con participantes ni mediciones nuevas. Sus límites: propone ideas que aún necesitan investigación empírica y no demuestra que funcionen. No es una regla para todas las personas ni sustituye el criterio de los profesionales que conocen a su familia.
sheet.en: If your child receives ABA, ask the team how they involve the family, how they approach emotions, and what long-term goals they hold beyond reducing behaviours. You can also ask whether family stress support and mental-health referral are available. The evidence is a clinical perspective review: an argued paper, not a study with participants or new measurements. Its limits: it proposes ideas that still need empirical research and does not show that they work. It is not a rule for every person and does not replace the judgement of professionals who know your family.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn får ABA kan du fråga teamet hur de involverar familjen, hur de arbetar med känslor och vilka långsiktiga mål de har utöver att minska beteenden. Du kan också fråga om det finns stöd vid familjestress och vägar till psykisk hälsovård. Underlaget är en översikt med klinisk utgångspunkt: en argumenterande text, inte en studie med deltagare eller nya mätningar. Begränsningar: den föreslår idéer som ännu behöver empirisk forskning och visar inte att de fungerar. Den är ingen regel för alla och ersätter inte bedömningen från yrkespersoner som känner er familj.

title: Autism and Neurodegeneration: Distinct Disorders or a Shared Biological Continuum?
authors: Manzo J, Hernández-Aguilar ME
abstract: Background/objectives Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is traditionally classified as a neurodevelopmental condition, whereas neurodegenerative diseases are defined by progressive neuronal decline in later life. This separation has shaped research and clinical practice, yet emerging evidence suggests potential biological overlap. This review aims to evaluate whether ASD and neurodegenerative disorders represent distinct entities or are linked through shared mechanisms operating across the lifespan. Methods This narrative review synthesizes findings from genetic, molecular, cellular, circuit-level, and epidemiological studies examining ASD and major neurodegenerative conditions, including Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Emphasis is placed on identifying convergent pathways and evaluating evidence within a lifespan-oriented framework. Results Across multiple levels of analysis, ASD and neurodegenerative diseases share partially overlapping biological mechanisms, including mitochondrial dysfunction, impaired proteostasis, neuroimmune alterations, and network-level instability. Genetic and molecular data reveal pleiotropic pathways influencing both early neurodevelopment and later neuronal resilience. Circuit-level studies highlight shared principles of network vulnerability, including cerebellar involvement and excitation-inhibition imbalance. Epidemiological data further indicate increased risk of dementia and parkinsonian features in autistic adults. These convergences suggest that early neurodevelopmental alterations may establish latent vulnerabilities that, under specific conditions, intersect with neurodegenerative processes later in life. Conclusions ASD and neurodegenerative diseases are best understood as distinct clinical conditions that share partially overlapping biological substrates. Rather than implying a deterministic progression, the evidence supports a model of lifespan convergence in which timing, context, and individual susceptibility shape outcomes. This framework highlights the need for integrated research and clinical approaches that consider brain health as a continuous process from development through aging.

sheet.es: Conviene que las personas autistas adultas y sus cuidadores cuiden la salud cerebral a lo largo de la vida y, si notan cambios en memoria o movimiento, los comenten con un profesional sanitario. Es una revisión narrativa que reúne estudios genéticos, moleculares, de circuitos cerebrales y epidemiológicos sobre autismo y enfermedades como el alzhéimer, el párkinson y la ELA. Señala que hay mecanismos biológicos parcialmente compartidos y mayor riesgo de demencia y rasgos parkinsonianos en adultos autistas. No implica que ocurra en todas las personas ni una progresión inevitable, y al ser narrativa no mide cuánto riesgo hay en cada caso.
sheet.en: Autistic adults and their caregivers can look after brain health across the whole lifespan and, if they notice changes in memory or movement, raise them with a health professional. This is a narrative review pulling together genetic, molecular, brain-circuit and epidemiological studies on autism and conditions such as Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease and ALS. It reports partly shared biological mechanisms and an increased risk of dementia and parkinsonian features in autistic adults. It does not mean this happens to every person or that decline is inevitable, and as a narrative review it cannot say how much risk applies to any one individual.
sheet.sv: Autistiska vuxna och deras anhöriga kan värna om hjärnhälsan under hela livet och ta upp förändringar i minne eller rörelse med en vårdgivare. Det här är en berättande översikt som samlar genetiska, molekylära, kretsrelaterade och epidemiologiska studier om autism och tillstånd som Alzheimers sjukdom, Parkinsons sjukdom och ALS. Den beskriver delvis gemensamma biologiska mekanismer och ökad risk för demens och parkinsonliknande drag hos autistiska vuxna. Det betyder inte att det drabbar alla eller att försämring är oundviklig, och som berättande översikt kan den inte visa hur stor risken är för en enskild person.

title: Motor Training Integrating Cognitive-Behavioral Strategies and Narrative Grammar in Children with Autism Using the Global Integration Method (MIG): A Randomized Clinical Trial.
authors: Flores Cruz TK, Netto RDCP, Fernandes EBC, Nascimento AAAC, Barreto SR, Silva ACC, Rodrigues IC, Fernandes ACS, Rocha GC, Souto DO
abstract: Introduction: A high prevalence of motor deficits has been documented in individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD); these deficits negatively impact participation and functional performance. Conventional interventions, which are often fragmented, may limit skill acquisition and generalization. The Global Integration Method (MIG) proposes an integrative approach that combines motor training, proprioceptive stimulation, and cognitive-behavioral strategies mediated through narrative. This study evaluated its effectiveness compared with conventional treatments. Methods: This study was designed as a three-arm randomized controlled clinical trial with assessor blinding, including 66 children with ASD aged 6-12 years. Participants were allocated to MIG, conventional physiotherapy, or conventional psychology groups. Interventions were delivered over five weeks. Assessments were performed at baseline, post-intervention, and at a three-month follow-up. Primary outcomes included motor skills (TGMD-2) and functional performance (COPM). Secondary outcomes included balance (PBS) and socio-communicative skills (PROC, ABFW). Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle using repeated-measures ANOVA. Results: The MIG group showed significant improvement compared with control groups in the primary outcomes, with a significant group × time interaction for fundamental motor skills and functional performance ( p p Conclusions: MIG was associated with greater improvements in motor and functional outcomes compared with conventional interventions. However, these findings should be interpreted as preliminary evidence of an intensive, multicomponent intervention package, in which treatment dose and combined therapeutic components may jointly contribute to the observed effects.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija autista tiene dificultades con el movimiento, puede valer la pena preguntar a un profesional por programas que combinen práctica motora, estimulación corporal y una historia o narración que dé sentido a cada actividad. Es un ensayo aleatorizado con 66 niños autistas de 6-12 años, que compararon el método MIG con fisioterapia o psicología convencionales durante cinco semanas. El grupo MIG mejoró más en habilidades motoras y desempeño funcional. Sin embargo, es evidencia preliminar: el programa era intensivo y tenía varios componentes, así que no se sabe qué parte causó el efecto, ni que sirva para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If your autistic child finds movement hard, it may be worth asking a professional about programmes that combine motor practice, body-based stimulation and a story or narrative that gives each activity meaning. This was a randomized trial with 66 autistic children aged 6-12, comparing the MIG method with conventional physiotherapy or psychology over five weeks. The MIG group improved more in motor skills and functional performance. However, this is preliminary evidence: the programme was intensive and had several components, so we cannot tell which part made the difference, or that it suits every child.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn tycker att rörelse är svårt kan det vara värt att fråga en yrkesperson om upplägg som kombinerar motorisk träning, kroppsbaserad stimulering och en berättelse som ger varje aktivitet mening. Det var en randomiserad studie med 66 autistiska barn i åldern 6-12 som jämförde MIG-metoden med vanlig fysioterapi eller psykologi under fem veckor. MIG-gruppen förbättrades mer i motoriska färdigheter och funktionell förmåga. Det är dock preliminära resultat: programmet var intensivt och hade flera delar, så vi vet inte vilken del som gav effekten eller om det passar alla barn.

title: Interventions to Promote Communication in Minimally Verbal Autistic Children: A Systematic Review.
authors: Privitera R, Piccolo A, De Domenico C, Leonardi G, Alito A, Quartarone A, Cucinotta F, Di Cara M
abstract: Background/objectives Minimally verbal autistic children face profound communication challenges that significantly affect daily functioning, including social interaction, behavioral regulation, and overall well-being. Identifying effective interventions is a key clinical-educational priority. This systematic review examines communication-focused interventions for these children, including both spoken language approaches and augmentative and alternative communication (AAC) strategies. Methods The review was registered in PROSPERO and conducted following PRISMA-S guidelines. Four electronic databases were searched, and 18 studies met the inclusion criteria. Due to heterogeneity in study designs and outcome measures, a narrative synthesis was conducted, with subgroup analyses exploring sample characteristics, intervention types, targeted outcomes, and reported effects. Methodological quality of randomized controlled trials was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool. Results Interventions were implemented across clinical, educational, and home settings, using strategies such as Joint Attention, Symbolic Play, and Emotion Regulation, often combined with AAC technologies. Most included studies reported improvements in at least one communication outcome, although findings were heterogeneous and several studies reported mixed, subgroup-specific, or non-significant effects. The most consistent improvements were observed in spontaneous communication, particularly in interventions integrating developmental approaches with technological support. Conclusions These findings highlight the value of individualized interventions. Future research should establish standardized definitions of "minimally verbal", assess long-term outcomes, and adopt broader measures capturing both language and social-emotional development to enhance quality of life and inclusion.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a un niño autista con pocas palabras habladas, puedes probar apoyos que combinen juego compartido, atención conjunta y herramientas de comunicación aumentativa (CAA), adaptándolos a su ritmo e intereses. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 18 estudios, aplicados en clínicas, escuelas y hogares. La mayoría informó mejoras en al menos un aspecto de la comunicación, sobre todo en la comunicación espontánea cuando se unían enfoques del desarrollo y apoyo tecnológico. Sin embargo, los resultados fueron muy variados, y algunos estudios hallaron efectos mixtos o no significativos. Además, no hay una definición común de «mínimamente verbal» ni datos a largo plazo. Consulta con su equipo profesional qué encaja con tu hijo.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic child who uses few spoken words, you can try supports that combine shared play, joint attention and augmentative and alternative communication (AAC) tools, fitted to their pace and interests. This systematic review pulled together 18 studies run in clinics, schools and homes. Most reported improvement in at least one communication outcome, most consistently in spontaneous communication when developmental approaches were paired with technology. However, results varied a lot, and some studies found mixed or non-significant effects. There is also no shared definition of "minimally verbal" and little long-term data. Talk with your child's professional team about what fits them.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar ett autistiskt barn som använder få talade ord kan du pröva stöd som kombinerar gemensam lek, delad uppmärksamhet och förstärkande och alternativ kommunikation (AKK), anpassat efter barnets tempo och intressen. Denna systematiska översikt samlade 18 studier som genomfördes i kliniker, skolor och hem. De flesta rapporterade förbättring i minst ett kommunikationsmått, mest konsekvent i spontan kommunikation när utvecklingsinriktade metoder kombinerades med teknik. Resultaten varierade dock mycket, och vissa studier visade blandade eller icke-signifikanta effekter. Det saknas också en gemensam definition av "minimalt verbal" och långtidsdata. Prata med barnets professionella team om vad som passar just ditt barn.

title: Exercise dose architecture as a precision-informed developmental framework in autism spectrum disorder: a narrative review of mechanisms, sex- and development-related heterogeneity, and clinical translation.
authors: Zhou Z, Peng D, Peng P, Li X
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition characterized not only by differences in social communication and restricted or repetitive behaviors, but also by variable profiles of motor function, sleep, cognition, sensory processing, and adaptive participation. Exercise and structured physical activity have emerged as promising non-pharmacological interventions in ASD, with growing evidence supporting benefits across multiple outcome domains, including executive function, stereotyped behaviors, sleep, motor competence, social communication, and quality of life. However, this field is constrained by fragmented concepts, inconsistent dose documentation, lack of mechanistic integration, and inadequate clinical translation. Exercise is often treated as a generic intervention rather than as a well-defined and physiologically meaningful exposure. This narrative review proposes a precision-informed framework in which exercise in ASD is conceptualized as a structured developmental exposure whose potential therapeutic value may depend on dose architecture rather than modality labels alone. Beyond traditional descriptors such as frequency, intensity, time, and type, exercise dose in ASD should be understood as a multidimensional construct that also includes motor complexity, cognitive demand, social embeddedness, sensory load, predictability, progression rate, and adherence burden. We synthesize ASD-specific clinical evidence together with indirect evidence from broader exercise neuroscience and animal models, while explicitly distinguishing established clinical findings from candidate or hypothesis-generating mechanisms. We also examine how exercise responses may differ according to developmental stage, pubertal changes, gender-associated traits, and the lack of female representation in existing evidence. Overall, we investigate how efficacy findings can inform individualized exercise plans, mechanism-linked trials, and scalable interventions in real-world settings. Taken together, this review offers a conceptual and translational framework for future ASD exercise research, emphasizing standardized dose reporting, evidence-level distinctions, developmental stratification, safety monitoring, and clinically meaningful outcomes.

sheet.es: Si quiere probar actividad física con una persona autista, no basta con elegir un deporte: conviene fijarse en cuánta coordinación, concentración, contacto social, carga sensorial y previsibilidad exige, y subir el ritmo poco a poco según lo que la persona disfrute y tolere. Esta publicación es una revisión narrativa que reúne estudios con personas autistas y también evidencia indirecta de otros ámbitos y de animales. Sus límites: propone un marco conceptual, no una pauta fija, y señala que hay pocas mujeres y niñas en los estudios, así que puede no servir igual para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you want to try physical activity with an autistic person, choosing a sport is not enough: it helps to notice how much coordination, concentration, social contact, sensory load and predictability it asks for, and to increase the pace gradually based on what the person enjoys and tolerates. This is a narrative review that brings together studies with autistic people and also indirect evidence from other fields and from animals. Its limits: it offers a conceptual framework, not a fixed plan, and it notes that few females are included in the studies, so it may not apply equally to everyone.
sheet.sv: Om du vill prova fysisk aktivitet med en autistisk person räcker det inte att välja en sport: det hjälper att se hur mycket koordination, koncentration, social kontakt, sensorisk belastning och förutsägbarhet den kräver, och att öka takten gradvis utifrån vad personen tycker om och klarar. Det här är en berättande översikt som samlar studier med autistiska personer samt indirekta belägg från andra områden och från djur. Begränsningar: den föreslår ett begreppsligt ramverk, inte en fast plan, och påpekar att få kvinnor och flickor ingår i studierna, så den passar kanske inte alla lika bra.

title: From risk to resilience: a narrative overview of modifiable factors influencing anxiety in children with autism spectrum disorder (part II).
authors: Mihai EE, Ciobanu I, Teodorescu M, Marin AG, Maharatna K, Berteanu M
abstract: Background Anxiety disorders are highly prevalent in children and adolescents with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and contribute substantially to functional impairment and reduced quality of life (QoL). Objective This paper represents the second part of a two-part narrative overview addressing internalizing symptoms in ASD. Complementing the first paper focused on depression, the present work examines anxiety, emphasizing shared and distinct modifiable risk and protective factors within a unified conceptual framework. Methods A structured narrative overview was conducted, synthesizing evidence from systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and robust clinical studies. Studies were selected based on relevance and scientific rigor, and findings were organized across biological, psychological, and environmental domains. Results Anxiety in ASD is associated with multiple interacting factors, including sensory hypersensitivity, intolerance of uncertainty (IU), social challenges, and neurobiological vulnerability. Protective factors such as cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT), structured physical activity, and supportive environments may mitigate anxiety symptoms and promote adaptive functioning. Nevertheless, variability in study design and population characteristics limits generalizability. Conclusions Addressing anxiety in ASD requires a comprehensive, multidisciplinary strategy that integrates risk reduction with resilience-building interventions. Together with the first part of this overview, these findings support transdiagnostic and personalized approach to mental health in children and adolescents.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija autista parece ansioso, puede ayudar mirar qué lo desencadena: sensibilidad sensorial, dificultad con la incertidumbre o situaciones sociales exigentes. Anticipar los cambios, cuidar los entornos y ofrecer actividad física estructurada pueden ser apoyos; la terapia cognitivo-conductual también aparece como factor protector. Es una revisión narrativa que reúne revisiones sistemáticas, metaanálisis y estudios clínicos sobre niños y adolescentes autistas. Sus límites: los estudios son muy distintos entre sí, por lo que los resultados no valen igual para todas las personas. Conviene adaptar los apoyos a cada niño y consultar con profesionales.
sheet.en: If your autistic child seems anxious, it can help to look at what sets it off: sensory sensitivity, difficulty with uncertainty, or demanding social situations. Preparing for changes, adjusting the environment and offering structured physical activity may help; cognitive-behavioral therapy is also described as a protective factor. This is a narrative review drawing on systematic reviews, meta-analyses and clinical studies of autistic children and adolescents. Its limits: the studies differ a lot in design and participants, so findings do not apply equally to every person. Adapt supports to your child and talk with professionals.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn verkar oroligt kan det hjälpa att se vad som utlöser det: sensorisk känslighet, svårigheter med osäkerhet eller krävande sociala situationer. Att förbereda förändringar, anpassa miljön och erbjuda strukturerad fysisk aktivitet kan stödja; kognitiv beteendeterapi beskrivs också som en skyddande faktor. Det är en narrativ översikt som bygger på systematiska översikter, metaanalyser och kliniska studier om autistiska barn och ungdomar. Begränsning: studierna skiljer sig mycket åt i upplägg och deltagare, så resultaten gäller inte lika för alla. Anpassa stödet efter ditt barn och rådgör med yrkespersoner.

title: Experiencing Independence: Perspectives from Autistic Adults.
authors: Bhattacharya P, Matthews RJ, Field R, Heath H, Woodcock KA, Surtees ADR
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Autism diagnostic criteria relate to difficulties in functioning across multiple developmental domains, that often impact on a person's independence. There are different ways to conceptualise and exercise independence, but no previous studies have questioned how autistic adults do so. This qualitative study aimed to understand how autistic adults define and experience independence. It was designed to further our understanding of how autistic adults account for and use coping strategies to overcome barriers to independent living and navigate their way to their desired level of independence. Twelve semi-structured interviews were conducted with autistic adults living in the United Kingdom. The data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. The researchers generated three major themes. The first theme 'Independence is "not a one-size-fits-all"' highlights that there is no one definition or concept of independence for autistic people; these are relative and uniquely individual. The second theme '"Being autistic has its setbacks" in a neurotypical world' describes the obstacles encountered by autistic adults seeking independence within a society that favours neurotypical norms. The third theme 'Finding ways of making it work' captures strategies autistic adults use in achieving or maintaining independence. The findings from this study provide a foundation for future research exploring domains of independence for autistic adults. The perceived desirability of achieving different degrees of in(ter)dependence and the fluctuating nature of self-sufficiency are explored through lived experience. Increasing understanding of barriers and challenges to independence has the potential to empower autistic adults and improve services and support.

sheet.es: Pregunta a la persona autista qué significa para ella la independencia y qué apoyo quiere, en lugar de suponerlo. Para unas personas será vivir sola; para otras, decidir cómo y cuándo pedir ayuda. Evidencia: estudio cualitativo con 12 entrevistas a adultos autistas del Reino Unido, analizadas por temas. Mostró que la independencia es individual, que una sociedad pensada para personas neurotípicas pone obstáculos y que las personas usan estrategias propias para que funcione. Límites: muestra pequeña de un solo país, así que no sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: Ask the autistic person what independence means to them and what support they want, rather than assuming. For some it may be living alone; for others, deciding how and when to ask for help. Evidence: a qualitative study of 12 interviews with autistic adults in the United Kingdom, analysed by themes. It found independence is individual, that a society built around neurotypical norms creates obstacles, and that people use their own strategies to make things work. Limits: a small sample from one country, so it is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Fråga den autistiska personen vad självständighet betyder för henne eller honom och vilket stöd som önskas, i stället för att anta det. För någon är det att bo själv, för någon annan att själv avgöra hur och när man ber om hjälp. Evidens: en kvalitativ studie med 12 intervjuer med autistiska vuxna i Storbritannien, analyserade i teman. Den visade att självständighet är individuell, att ett samhälle byggt för neurotypiska normer skapar hinder och att människor använder egna strategier. Begränsningar: litet urval från ett land, så resultaten gäller inte alla.

title: The Behavioral Presentation of Autistic Adults in a Forensic Interview.
authors: Logos K, Lim A, Brewer N, Young RL
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Autism diagnostic criteria, and research primarily involving autistic children, highlight verbal and nonverbal behaviors likely to manifest during social interaction that may generate unfavorable impressions of interaction partners (e.g., poor credibility, incompetence). These behaviors are thought to bias evaluations of autistic individuals, particularly within high-stakes contexts (e.g., police or employment interviews). However, the prevalence of those behaviors in autistic adults is unclear. IQ-matched samples of autistic (n = 43) and non-autistic (n = 41) adults participated in a simulated chatroom, exposed to text-based conversations about illegal hacking. Participants were then interviewed about the chatroom in a one-on-one video-recorded online interview with the researcher. We measured the prevalence of 19 verbal and nonverbal behaviors, and memory report characteristics displayed by the interviewees, and investigated differences between the diagnostic groups. Diagnosis had a strong effect on overall behavioral displays but was only associated with minor differences in individual behaviors. Three significant effects indicated greater difficulty interpreting figurative language, longer speech hesitations, and greater verbal intonation for autistic than non-autistic adults. Inter-individual variability within groups and within-individual variability across behaviors highlighted that behaviors were neither ubiquitous nor consistently displayed in combination. There was also a suggestion of more noticeable differences in the behavior of male than female autistic adults. Although minor behavioral differences were detected based on diagnosis, they included behaviors that could lead to negative outcomes for autistic individuals during high-stakes interactions. Whether more pronounced behavioral differences are detected during face-to-face interactions warrants further research.

sheet.es: Antes de una entrevista importante (policial, laboral), conviene avisar a quien entrevista de que algunas personas autistas pueden hacer pausas más largas, entonación más marcada o interpretar de forma literal el lenguaje figurado. Usar frases claras y directas ayuda. Estas conductas no indican falta de credibilidad. Evidencia: estudio con 43 adultos autistas y 41 no autistas, con entrevista en vídeo en línea tras un chat simulado. Hubo solo diferencias pequeñas en conductas concretas, y variaron mucho entre personas. Límites: la entrevista fue en línea y simulada, no cara a cara, y no sirve como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: Before an important interview (police, job), it can help to tell the interviewer that some autistic people may pause longer, use more vocal intonation, or take figurative language literally. Clear, direct wording helps. These behaviors do not signal a lack of credibility. Evidence: a study of 43 autistic and 41 non-autistic adults, interviewed on video online after a simulated chatroom. Differences in individual behaviors were small, and people varied a lot. Limits: the interview was online and simulated, not face to face, and it is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Inför en viktig intervju (polis, jobb) kan det hjälpa att berätta för intervjuaren att vissa autistiska personer kan ha längre pauser, tydligare intonation eller tolka bildligt språk bokstavligt. Klara, direkta formuleringar hjälper. Detta betyder inte att personen är mindre trovärdig. Evidens: en studie med 43 autistiska och 41 icke-autistiska vuxna, som intervjuades via video online efter en simulerad chattrumsövning. Skillnaderna i enskilda beteenden var små, och personerna varierade mycket. Begränsningar: intervjun var online och simulerad, inte ansikte mot ansikte, och gäller inte som regel för alla.

title: Intact but Protracted Facial and Prosodic Emotion Recognition Among Autistic Adults.
authors: Jertberg RM, Begeer S, Geurts HM, Chakrabarti B, Van der Burg E
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Despite extensive research efforts, it is unclear how autistic and non-autistic individuals compare in their ability to recognize emotions. Differences in demographic and task factors have been proposed as explanations for divergent findings, but limitations in samples and designs have obscured insight into this possibility. This study investigated the extent of emotion recognition differences among autistic adults and the influence of these factors upon them. We recruited a large sample of autistic and non-autistic adults (N = 1,239) spanning across adulthood (18-76 years). In three online experiments, we compared their performance in recognizing emotions from basic facial expressions, complex expressions conveyed by the eyes alone, and prosodic elements of speech. Autistic individuals performed as well as non-autistic ones in terms of recognition accuracy/sensitivity across measures and emotional categories but took longer to do so. We also detected comparable influences of age, estimated intelligence quotient, and gender (as well as task demands) on both groups. While autistic adults may differ in how they process emotional stimuli, they can do so effectively when given sufficient time. Accordingly, efforts to help autistic individuals improve their ability to recognize emotions may be more fruitful if they focus on efficiency over accuracy. Additionally, reaction time data may offer greater insight than accuracy into differences between autistic and non-autistic individuals on emotion recognition tasks. The similar effects of the demographic and task factors we analyzed on both groups suggest that explanations of the discrepancies in prior literature lie elsewhere.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista necesita más tiempo para interpretar una cara, la mirada o el tono de voz, conviene darle ese tiempo y no apresurarla ni dar por hecho que no entiende. Un estudio con personas adultas autistas y no autistas (N = 1,239, de 18 a 76 años) hizo tres experimentos en línea. Las personas autistas acertaron tanto como las no autistas, pero tardaron más. Límites: fueron tareas en línea y no situaciones reales; los resultados describen grupos, no a cada persona, y no sirven como regla general.
sheet.en: If an autistic person needs more time to read a face, the eyes or a tone of voice, give them that time rather than rushing them or assuming they don't understand. A study with autistic and non-autistic adults (N = 1,239, aged 18-76) ran three online experiments. Autistic participants were as accurate as non-autistic ones, but took longer. Limits: these were online tasks, not real-life situations; results describe groups, not every individual, and should not be treated as a rule for everyone.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person behöver mer tid för att tolka ett ansikte, ögonen eller en röstton, ge då den tiden i stället för att stressa eller anta att personen inte förstår. En studie med autistiska och icke-autistiska vuxna (N = 1,239, 18-76 år) gjorde tre onlineexperiment. De autistiska deltagarna var lika träffsäkra som de icke-autistiska, men tog längre tid. Begränsningar: det var uppgifter på nätet, inte verkliga situationer; resultaten beskriver grupper, inte varje person, och är ingen regel för alla.

title: Accelerated intermittent theta burst stimulation targeting personalized fronto-parietal control network improves core symptoms of autism spectrum disorder: a double-blind, randomized controlled trial.
authors: Liu Q, Zhang J, Duan X, Zhang P, Yang Y, Yao G, Jiaerheng B, Shou XJ, He Y, Han K, Jia M, Wang L, Gong W, Xie W, Sun K, Wang D, Wu XD, Cao H, Zhang H, Liu H
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) presents a substantial global challenge, yet no pharmacological treatments effectively target its core symptoms, especially in individuals with severe cognitive or adaptive impairments. This double-blind, sham-controlled, randomized clinical trial assessed accelerated intermittent theta burst stimulation (iTBS) targeting the personalized fronto-parietal network (FPN) in ASD. Participants (6-30 years) were randomized in a 2:1 ratio to active or sham iTBS (three daily sessions, 1800 pulses/session) over 12 weeks (324k pulses) alongside behavioral training. The primary outcome was defined as the response rate, charaterized by a ≥ 1-point reduction in ADOS-2 SA at week 12. Of 132 individuals screened, 67 were randomized (mean age 10.04 ± 4.22 years; 88.1% male; all with cognitive/adaptive delays), with 59 completing the study. Active iTBS resulted in a significantly higher response rate (55% vs. 29%) and higher symptom improvement than sham (cohen's d = -0.53), with mild local pain in only 5% of iTBS group. In the profound autism subgroup, the active group exhibited language improvement alongside amelioration of core symptoms. These findings suggest that prolonged, accelerated FPN-targeted iTBS is a safe and efficacious intervention for severe ASD, offering a promising therapeutic approach.Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05890846.

sheet.es: Si alguien valora la estimulación magnética transcraneal para una persona autista, es una decisión para hablar con un profesional clínico; este estudio no es una guía para decidir por su cuenta. Fue un ensayo aleatorizado, doble ciego y con placebo, en 67 participantes de 6-30 años, todos con retrasos cognitivos o adaptativos, que recibieron estimulación real o simulada durante 12 semanas junto con entrenamiento conductual. La tasa de respuesta fue 55% frente a 29%, y el dolor local leve apareció en 5% del grupo activo. Límites: muestra pequeña, mayoría varones, y la mejoría se midió con una escala de observación clínica, no con la experiencia de las personas.
sheet.en: If you are weighing transcranial magnetic stimulation for an autistic person, that is a conversation for a clinician; this study is not a guide for deciding alone. It was a double-blind, sham-controlled randomized trial with 67 participants aged 6-30, all with cognitive or adaptive delays, who received real or sham stimulation over 12 weeks alongside behavioral training. The response rate was 55% versus 29%, and mild local pain occurred in 5% of the active group. Limits: a small sample, mostly male, and improvement was measured with a clinician-rated observation scale, not the person's own experience.
sheet.sv: Om du överväger transkraniell magnetstimulering för en autistisk person är det en fråga för en kliniker; studien är ingen vägledning för att välja på egen hand.
