Det var en dubbelblind, skenkontrollerad randomiserad studie med 67 deltagare i åldern 6-30 år, alla med kognitiva eller adaptiva förseningar, som fick riktig eller sken-stimulering under 12 veckor tillsammans med beteendeträning. Svarsfrekvensen var 55% mot 29%, och lindrig lokal smärta förekom hos 5% i aktiva gruppen. Begränsningar: litet urval, mest pojkar och män, och förbättringen mättes med en klinikerskattad observationsskala, inte med personens egen upplevelse.

title: Enhancing emergency department care for individuals with autism spectrum disorder across the lifespan: a systematic review.
authors: Hamad O, Klára S, Elmadani M, Mbaabu G, Tóth L, Horváth É, Mesmar A, Máté O
abstract: Objective This systematic review aims to synthesize existing evidence on emergency department (ED) experiences, service-delivery challenges, and environmental and communication factors affecting autistic people and to identify strategies and interventions reported to improve patient comfort, safety, and satisfaction. Methods A comprehensive search was conducted across databases, including PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library, for peer-reviewed articles published between January 1, 2014, and December 31, 2024. Data extraction was performed using standardized forms, and quality assessment was conducted using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Data synthesis involved narrative thematic analysis to identify key barriers and facilitators to emergency department care for autistic people. The reporting of this review follows the PRISMA guidelines. Results Eleven studies met the inclusion criteria and revealed consistent barriers affecting autistic people in emergency departments. Across settings, communication difficulties, sensory overload, long waiting times, and limited staff preparedness were the most frequently reported challenges. These factors contributed to heightened distress, behavioral escalation, and reduced satisfaction for patients and families. Facilitators identified in the literature included ASD-specific staff training, sensory-adapted environments, structured care routines, and active caregiver involvement. While not all barriers are easily modifiable, several environmental, communication, and workflow-related factors appear potentially amenable to service-level interventions. The findings further indicate that autism-specific staff training, sensory-friendly adaptations, and caregiver-supported care approaches may improve the ED experience for autistic patients and their families. Discussion The findings underscore the multifaceted challenges ASD patients face in EDs, exacerbated by sensory overload and communication difficulties. Addressing these issues requires a comprehensive approach, including staff education, environmental adjustments, and efficient triage systems. Engaging parents as partners in care also emerged as critical for delivering patient-centered care. Conclusion This review emphasizes the urgent need for systemic reforms in ED care for ASD patients. Strategies such as sensory-friendly environments, enhanced staff training, and patient-centered policies can improve patient outcomes and satisfaction. Future research should focus on evaluating the long-term impacts of these interventions and identifying innovative solutions to meet the complex needs of this vulnerable population. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42024532107, PROSPERO CRD42024532107.

sheet.es: Si tienes que ir a urgencias con una persona autista, avisa al personal desde el principio de sus necesidades sensoriales y de comunicación, pide un espacio más tranquilo si es posible y explica a la persona qué va a pasar paso a paso. Participa activamente: el personal puede contar contigo. La evidencia es una revisión sistemática de 11 estudios sobre la atención en urgencias. Encontró que la comunicación, la sobrecarga sensorial, las esperas largas y la poca preparación del personal son barreras frecuentes. Sus límites: son pocos estudios, no prueban qué medida funciona mejor y no sirven como regla para toda persona.
sheet.en: If you need to take an autistic person to the emergency department, tell staff early about their sensory and communication needs, ask for a quieter space if possible, and explain step by step what will happen. Take an active part: staff can work with you. The evidence is a systematic review of 11 studies on emergency care. It found that communication difficulties, sensory overload, long waits and limited staff preparation were commonly reported barriers. Its limits: it covers few studies, it cannot show which measure works best, and it is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du behöver följa en autistisk person till akutmottagningen, berätta tidigt för personalen om personens sensoriska behov och kommunikationsbehov, be om ett lugnare rum om det går och förklara steg för steg vad som ska hända. Var delaktig: personalen kan samarbeta med dig. Underlaget är en systematisk översikt av 11 studier om akutvård. Den fann att kommunikationssvårigheter, sensorisk överbelastning, långa väntetider och begränsad förberedelse hos personalen ofta rapporterades som hinder. Begränsningar: det är få studier, översikten visar inte vilken åtgärd som fungerar bäst och den är ingen regel för alla.

title: Intermittent Theta Burst Stimulation Improves Sleep in Autism Spectrum Disorder by Reorganizing Overlapping Brain Networks With Neurochemical and Transcriptomic Signatures: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
authors: Zhang H, Xiong B, Liu H, Huang Y, Zhang J, Yu R, Jiang W, She T
abstract: Background Overlapping network architecture supports functional integration and multifunctional regional engagement in the brain, and may serve as a candidate biomarker for interventions in autism spectrum disorder (ASD). However, the biological context underlying intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS)-related changes in overlapping network architecture remains poorly understood. Methods Seventy patients with ASD and chronic insomnia were randomly assigned to receive either real or sham iTBS targeting the left orbitofrontal cortex, administered once daily for 8 weeks. The Insomnia Severity Index (ISI) and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data were collected at baseline and after the intervention. The Shannon-entropy diversity coefficient was calculated to characterize overlapping network architecture. The JuSpace toolbox was used to assess spatial correspondence between iTBS-related network changes and neurotransmitter systems. Transcriptomic-neuroimaging association analyses were then performed using gene-expression data from the Allen Human Brain Atlas. Results Sleep improvement following real iTBS was accompanied by changes in overlapping network architecture across 13 cortical regions. These changes showed spatial correspondence with mGluR5 and GABA_A receptor density maps. Regions showing iTBS-related network changes were associated with glutamatergic synaptic transmission and calcium-dependent signaling, enriched for cortical excitatory neuronal signatures with peak expression during adolescence, and organized into a highly interconnected protein-protein interaction network centered on the Ca 2+ -PKA signaling axis. Conclusions This study provides multiscale evidence for the biological context underlying iTBS-related changes in overlapping network architecture in ASD with chronic insomnia.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista tiene insomnio crónico, vale la pena hablar con su equipo clínico sobre opciones para dormir; la estimulación cerebral es una vía en investigación, no algo que se pueda probar en casa. Es un ensayo aleatorizado con 70 personas autistas con insomnio crónico: unas recibieron iTBS real y otras simulada, una vez al día durante 8 semanas, y las que recibieron la real mostraron mejora del sueño junto con cambios en redes cerebrales. Límites: el resumen no indica cuánto duran los efectos ni si se aplican a todas las personas, y gran parte del estudio describe mecanismos cerebrales, no la vida diaria. Las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If an autistic person has chronic insomnia, it may be worth talking with their clinical team about sleep options; brain stimulation is a research approach, not something to try at home. This was a randomized trial with 70 autistic people with chronic insomnia: some received real iTBS and others sham, once daily for 8 weeks, and sleep improvement after real iTBS came with changes in brain networks. Limits: the abstract does not say how long effects last or whether they apply to everyone, and much of the work describes brain mechanisms rather than daily life. Medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person har kronisk insomni kan det vara värt att prata med vårdteamet om alternativ för sömn; hjärnstimulering är ett forskningsspår och inget att pröva hemma. Det var en randomiserad studie med 70 autistiska personer med kronisk insomni: några fick riktig iTBS och andra sken-behandling, en gång om dagen i 8 veckor, och förbättrad sömn efter riktig iTBS kom tillsammans med förändringar i hjärnans nätverk. Begränsningar: sammanfattningen anger inte hur länge effekterna varar eller om de gäller alla, och mycket av studien beskriver hjärnmekanismer snarare än vardagen. Medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker.

title: Seeing the Child Within: A Randomized Controlled Trial of Reflective Functioning Intervention for Parents of Autistic Children.
authors: Enav Y, Kirsman N, Erhard Weiss D, Mayer Y
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Parents of autistic children often face elevated emotional demands and challenges in interpreting their child's inner experience. Parental reflective functioning (PRF), the capacity to understand behavior in terms of underlying mental states, is considered a key mechanism in fostering emotionally attuned and adaptive caregiving. Despite its importance, few interventions directly target PRF, and fewer still have tested brief, group-based formats designed for broad accessibility. We conducted a randomized controlled trial to evaluate a brief, virtual PRF intervention delivered via Zoom to 249 parents of autistic children. Participants were randomly assigned to either an intervention group (n = 129) or a waitlist control group (n = 130), and completed assessments at baseline and postintervention. PRF was measured using a standardized interview, while self-report questionnaires assessed parenting self-efficacy, beliefs about emotional malleability, depressive symptoms, and child adaptive functioning. Generalized estimating equations revealed significant time-by-group interactions favoring the intervention group across several outcomes. Relative to controls, intervention participants reported greater gains in reflective functioning, parenting self-efficacy, and emotional beliefs, alongside improvements in children's communication and conceptual adaptive functioning. Effects were most pronounced among parents of younger children. Within the intervention group, additional follow-up assessments indicated sustained benefits on workshop-specific outcomes. Findings support the feasibility and efficacy of brief, scalable PRF-based programs for caregivers of autistic children. To our knowledge, this is the first randomized trial to demonstrate that a short, online, parent-focused intervention can enhance reflective parenting and promote emotional and relational benefits in this population.

sheet.es: Si te interesa entender mejor qué puede sentir o necesitar tu hijo o hija autista, un taller breve en línea para madres y padres sobre pensar en sus estados internos puede ser una opción. Es un ensayo aleatorizado con 249 madres y padres de niños autistas, repartidos entre un grupo con taller (129) y una lista de espera (130). El grupo del taller informó más reflexión parental, más confianza como cuidador y mejores creencias sobre las emociones; también mejoraron la comunicación y las habilidades conceptuales de los niños. Los efectos fueron mayores con niños más pequeños. Límites: el seguimiento posterior fue solo dentro del grupo del taller y no todas las familias responderán igual.
sheet.en: If you want to understand better what your autistic child may feel or need, a brief online workshop for parents about thinking through their child's inner experience may be worth considering. This was a randomized trial with 249 parents of autistic children, split between a workshop group (129) and a waitlist group (130). The workshop group reported more reflective parenting, more parenting confidence and healthier beliefs about emotions; children's communication and conceptual skills also improved. Effects were strongest with younger children. Limits: later follow-up was only within the workshop group, and families will not all respond in the same way.
sheet.sv: Om du vill förstå bättre vad ditt autistiska barn kan känna eller behöva kan en kort digital workshop för föräldrar om barnets inre upplevelse vara värd att överväga. Det var en randomiserad studie med 249 föräldrar till autistiska barn, fördelade på en workshopgrupp (129) och en väntelista (130). Workshopgruppen rapporterade mer reflekterande föräldraskap, större tilltro till sin föräldraförmåga och mer positiva föresällningar om känslor. Barnens kommunikation och begreppsliga färdigheter förbättrades också. Effekterna var störst hos yngre barn. Begränsningar: den senare uppföljningen gjordes bara i workshopgruppen, och alla familjer reagerar inte likadant.

title: The Effect of Online Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction Program on Sleep Quality in Mothers of Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
authors: Miryounesi F, Ghezelbash S, Alavi M
journal: Iranian journal of nursing and midwifery research
abstract: Background Mothers of children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) would experience elevated levels of stress and psychological distress. This study examined the effect of an online Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) Program on sleep quality in mothers of children with ASD. Materials and methods This was a randomized single-blinded controlled trial that was conducted in 2022 on 72 mothers of children with ASD from Fatemeh Zahra and Parnian Autism Centers in Isfahan City, Iran. Participants were recruited through a convenient sampling and randomly assigned to intervention ( n = 36) and control ( n = 36) groups. The intervention group underwent eight 90-min MBSR sessions twice a week. Data were collected using a demographic information form and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) at baseline, immediately after, and one month after the intervention. Data were analyzed using independent samples: t -test, Chi-square, and one-way repeated-measure. Results The intervention group showed significantly improved sleep quality scores immediately after ( F = 107.004, P F = 107.004, P F = 107.004, P F = 1.292, P > 0.05). Conclusions The findings of this study demonstrate that MBSR effectively improves sleep in mothers of children with ASD. Given its cost-effectiveness, MBSR should be integrated into healthcare protocols.

sheet.es: Si cuida a un niño autista y duerme mal, un programa de mindfulness en línea puede ser una opción de apoyo para usted. Es un ensayo aleatorizado con 72 madres de niños autistas de centros de Isfahán, Irán: 36 hicieron ocho sesiones de 90 minutos, dos veces por semana, y 36 formaron el grupo de control. El grupo del programa mostró una mejora significativa en la calidad del sueño, medida con un cuestionario. Los límites: participó solo un grupo de madres, elegido por conveniencia, en un lugar y un momento concretos, y solo se midió el sueño un mes después. No sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic child and your own sleep is poor, an online mindfulness program may be one supportive option for you. This was a randomized trial with 72 mothers of autistic children from centers in Isfahan, Iran: 36 took eight 90-minute sessions, twice a week, and 36 were in the control group. The program group showed significantly improved sleep quality on a questionnaire. Limits: only mothers took part, chosen by convenience, in one place and time, and sleep was followed for only one month afterwards. It is not a rule for everyone.
sheet.sv: Om du tar hand om ett autistiskt barn och sover dåligt kan ett mindfulnessprogram på nätet vara ett stöd att överväga. Det var en randomiserad studie med 72 mödrar till autistiska barn från centra i Isfahan i Iran: 36 deltog i åtta sessioner på 90 minuter, två gånger i veckan, och 36 ingick i kontrollgruppen. Programgruppen fick betydligt bättre sömnkvalitet enligt ett frågeformulär. Begränsningar: bara mödrar deltog, valda utifrån tillgänglighet, på en plats och vid en tidpunkt, och sömnen följdes bara en månad efteråt. Det är ingen regel för alla.

title: Integration of specialized residential interventions with community-based services for autistic adults with severe challenging behaviors: preliminary evidence from the Piedmont model.
authors: Keller R, Giacchero M, Capiotto F, Masoero M, Corna S, Figliano G, De Matos MB, Liloia D
abstract: Background Severe challenging behaviors in autistic adults are difficult to manage in generic psychiatric settings and impose a heavy burden on individuals, families, and services. The Piedmont Region (Italy) established a specialized third-level inpatient unit for these presentations, embedded within an integrated, three-tier regional network. This study reports preliminary effectiveness data from this model. Materials and methods In a prospective, pre-post design, 10 autistic adult males admitted for severe challenging behaviors received an intensive, individualized psychoeducational program based on Applied Behavior Analysis during a time-limited specialized admission. Psychopathology (Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale, BPRS), challenging behaviors (Aberrant Behavior Checklist, ABC), global clinical severity (Clinical Global Impression, CGI), and social support (Social and Affective Functional Support Scale, SSAF) were assessed before admission (T0) and at discharge (T1). Change was examined with paired-samples t-tests and standardized effect sizes; given the sample size and number of comparisons, analyses were exploratory. Results Improvement was selective rather than uniform. On the BPRS, significant reductions emerged across several dimensions, concentrated in a coherent behavioral-disorganization and agitation cluster (i.e., motor tension, distractibility, bizarre behavior, conceptual disorganization, and anxiety) with large effect sizes. The ABC showed significant reductions in lethargy/social withdrawal and hyperactivity, whereas stereotypic behavior, irritability, and inappropriate speech did not change significantly. CGI and SSAF showed non-significant trends toward improvement. Trait-like, affective, and global dimensions appeared least responsive to the admission. Conclusion A time-limited, specialized inpatient program delivered within an integrated regional network was associated with improvement concentrated in observable, modifiable behavioral dimensions. These preliminary findings support the development of specialized, coordinated care pathways for severe challenging behaviors in autistic adults and warrant controlled studies with larger, sex-diverse samples and post-discharge follow-up.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta vive una crisis grave y los servicios generales no consiguen apoyarla, conviene preguntar si existe una unidad especializada coordinada con los servicios de la comunidad. Es un estudio con 10 hombres autistas adultos ingresados en una unidad especializada de Piamonte (Italia), medidos antes del ingreso y al alta. Tras un programa psicoeducativo individualizado, mejoraron sobre todo la agitación, la tensión motora y la desorganización; la irritabilidad y las conductas repetitivas no cambiaron de forma significativa. Es un grupo muy pequeño, sin grupo de comparación, solo hombres y sin seguimiento posterior, así que no sirve como regla para todas las personas. Las decisiones de apoyo deben tomarse con la persona y su equipo.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult is in serious distress and general services are not managing to support them, it is worth asking whether a specialized unit coordinated with community services exists. This study followed 10 autistic adult men admitted to a specialized unit in Piedmont (Italy), measured before admission and at discharge. After an individualized psychoeducational program, agitation, motor tension and disorganization improved most; irritability and stereotyped behavior did not change significantly. The group was very small, had no comparison group, included only men and had no follow-up after discharge, so it is not a rule for everyone. Support decisions should be made with the person and their team.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen är i allvarlig kris och vanliga tjänster inte räcker, kan man fråga om det finns en specialiserad enhet som samarbetar med stödet i kommunen. Studien följde 10 autistiska vuxna män som lades in på en specialiserad enhet i Piemonte (Italien), med mätningar före inskrivning och vid utskrivning. Efter ett individanpassat psykoedukativt program förbättrades främst agitation, motorisk spänning och oorganiserat beteende; irritabilitet och stereotypt beteende förändrades inte signifikant. Gruppen var mycket liten, utan jämförelsegrupp, bestod bara av män och saknade uppföljning efter utskrivning, så resultaten är ingen regel för alla. Beslut om stöd bör fattas tillsammans med personen och teamet.

title: From risk to resilience: a narrative overview of modifiable factors influencing depression in children with autism spectrum disorder (part I).
authors: Mihai EE, Ciobanu I, Teodorescu M, Marin AG, Maharatna K, Berteanu M
abstract: Background Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a complex neurodevelopmental condition frequently associated with internalizing disorders, particularly depression, which significantly impacts functioning and quality of life (QoL) in children and adolescents. Objective This paper represents the first part of a two-part structured narrative overview examining internalizing psychopathology in children and adolescents with ASD. Given the high co-occurrence and shared neurobiological, psychological, and environmental mechanisms linking depression and anxiety, the multidisciplinary research team elected to develop two complementary overviews to allow a more comprehensive and clinically meaningful synthesis of the evidence. The present review specifically aims to identify and synthesize current evidence on modifiable risk and protective factors influencing depression in children and adolescents with ASD. Methods A structured narrative overview was conducted, integrating evidence from systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and robust clinical studies. Studies were selected based on relevance and methodological quality, and findings were synthesized across biological, psychosocial, and lifestyle domains. Results Growing body of evidence indicates that depression in ASD is influenced by a complex interplay of genetic vulnerability, sensory and emotional dysregulation, social stressors, and environmental factors. At the same time, modifiable protective factors-including physical activity, psychosocial interventions, digital health approaches, and family-centered care-show potential in enhancing resilience and emotional well-being. However, the evidence base remains heterogeneous and often limited by methodological constraints. Conclusions A multidisciplinary and prevention-oriented approach that simultaneously addresses risk and strengthens protective pathways may optimize mental health outcomes and improve QoL in children and adolescents with ASD.

sheet.es: Para mañana: observa con calma cómo están el ánimo, el sueño y el interés de la persona autista, y dale espacio a lo que le sienta bien, como el movimiento físico, el apoyo emocional y una atención que cuente con la familia. Esta revisión narrativa reunió revisiones sistemáticas, metaanálisis y estudios clínicos sobre niñas, niños y adolescentes autistas, y sugiere que actividad física, intervenciones psicosociales, apoyos digitales y atención centrada en la familia podrían fortalecer el bienestar. Sus límites: la evidencia es heterogénea, con limitaciones metodológicas, y no es una regla para cada persona. Si te preocupa su ánimo, consulta con un profesional.
sheet.en: For tomorrow: gently notice how the autistic young person's mood, sleep and interests are going, and make room for what helps them, such as physical movement, emotional support and care that involves the family. This narrative review brought together systematic reviews, meta-analyses and clinical studies on autistic children and adolescents. It suggests that physical activity, psychosocial interventions, digital health approaches and family-centered care may strengthen wellbeing. Its limits: the evidence is mixed and often has methodological weaknesses, and it is not a rule for every person. If you are worried about their mood, talk with a professional.
sheet.sv: Till i morgon: lägg lugnt märke till hur den autistiska personens humör, sömn och intressen mår, och ge utrymme för det som hjälper, som fysisk aktivitet, känslomässigt stöd och vård som involverar familjen. Den här berättande översikten samlade systematiska översikter, metaanalyser och kliniska studier om autistiska barn och ungdomar. Den antyder att fysisk aktivitet, psykosociala insatser, digitala hälsoverktyg och familjecentrerad vård kan stärka välbefinnandet. Begränsningar: underlaget är varierande och har ofta metodproblem, och det gäller inte som regel för varje person. Oroar du dig för humöret, tala med en professionell.

title: Parent perspectives on services available to autistic children in Canada: A mixed methods survey study.
authors: Caven I, Hamdani Y, Lunsky Y, Weaver C, Penner M
abstract: Objectives Given the differing opinions among interest holders on services that are commonly accessed by autistic children, exploration of parent perspectives is needed to contribute to this knowledge base. Our objective was to explore perspectives of parents of autistic children on select services accessed by autistic children in Canada. Methods Using a mixed methods survey, the perspectives of parents of autistic children living in Canada on occupational therapy (OT), speech-language pathology (SLP) services, and applied behaviour analysis (ABA) based therapies were sought. The Theoretical Framework of Acceptability (TFA) and its constructs were used to develop the survey and served as a framework for qualitative content analysis. Results Eighty-seven parents completed the survey. Acceptability scores were higher for OT and SLP compared to ABA (F (2, 239) = 43.42, p Conclusions Across OT, SLP, and ABA, Ethicality, Perceived Effectiveness, and Self-Efficacy informed the perceived acceptability of autism services. This work highlights that many parents are concerned with promoting a positive autistic identity for their children, including through therapies. Future work should seek to develop shared definitions and goals for therapy between clinicians, parents/care partners, and autistic people.

sheet.es: Al elegir o revisar terapias, conviene preguntarse si encajan con la ética de la familia, si parecen eficaces y si usted se siente capaz de apoyarlas en casa, y hablar de los objetivos con el equipo y con la propia persona autista. Es un estudio con encuesta de métodos mixtos en el que participaron 87 madres y padres de niñas y niños autistas en Canadá. Valoraron mejor la terapia ocupacional y del habla y el lenguaje que las terapias basadas en ABA, y muchos querían fomentar una identidad autista positiva. Es una muestra pequeña, recoge solo la opinión de las familias y no muestra qué terapia funciona mejor para cada persona.
sheet.en: When choosing or reviewing therapies, it can help to ask whether they fit your family's values, seem effective, and feel manageable for you to support at home, and to talk through goals with the team and with the autistic person. This was a mixed methods survey of 87 parents of autistic children in Canada. They rated occupational therapy and speech-language therapy as more acceptable than ABA-based therapies, and many wanted to support a positive autistic identity. The sample is small, it reflects only parents' views, and it cannot show which therapy works best for any one person.
sheet.sv: När ni väljer eller ser över terapier kan det hjälpa att fråga sig om de passar familjens värderingar, verkar effektiva och känns görbara att stödja hemma, och att prata om målen med teamet och med den autistiska personen. Detta var en enkätstudie med blandade metoder där 87 föräldrar till autistiska barn i Kanada deltog. De bedömde arbetsterapi och logopedi som mer acceptabla än ABA-baserade terapier, och många ville stärka en positiv autistisk identitet. Urvalet är litet, det speglar bara föräldrarnas åsikter och visar inte vilken terapi som fungerar bäst för en enskild person.

title: Exploring the Experiences of First Nations Caregivers of Autistic Children in Canada: A Qualitative Community-Based Participatory Research Study.
authors: Bruno G, Ahmad M, Cutknife C, Littlechild H, Ertman T, Smith J, Zwaigenbaum L, Nicholas D
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Autism exists across all populations, including among Indigenous Peoples, yet the experiences of First Nations caregivers of Autistic children remain significantly under-researched. This study explores the lived realities of caregivers in two First Nations communities: Maskwacîs (Alberta) and Six Nations of the Grand River (Ontario). Guided by a Community-Based Participatory Research (CBPR) approach and grounded in the nêhiyaw concept of wâhkôtowin (relationality), this research was co-led by the Autism Community Research Circle, which included Elders, Autistic individuals, caregivers, and professionals. Fourteen caregivers participated in semi-structured interviews, and thematic analysis revealed eight key themes: lack of understanding and recognition; caregiver burnout; challenges with diagnosis and clinical navigation; school experiences; advocacy; stigma and ableism; culture and ceremony; and acceptance and transformation. Caregivers identified barriers including jurisdictional divides, racism, and lack of culturally appropriate services, but also emphasized the importance of kinship, cultural identity, and community acceptance. Autism was often reframed through Indigenous worldviews as a gift from the Creator, highlighting a strength-based perspective rooted in relationality. This study addresses a critical gap in the literature and calls for culturally grounded, community-led autism supports that align with Indigenous knowledge systems. Findings offer essential insights to inform more responsive policy, programming, and future research.Lay AbstractAutism exists in every community, including among First Nations Peoples in Canada, yet very little research has explored the experiences of Indigenous families raising Autistic children. This study looked at what life is like for First Nations caregivers of Autistic children in two communities, Maskwacîs in Alberta and Six Nations of the Grand River in Ontario. The project was led in partnership with community members, including Autistic people, Elders, caregivers, and professionals, through the Autism Community Research Circle. Together, we used a community-based approach that followed local teachings and values, especially the Cree concept of wâhkôtowin, which means kinship and relationship. Fourteen caregivers took part in interviews where they shared their stories and perspectives. We learned that caregivers often face major challenges in getting autism diagnoses and finding appropriate supports and services. Many spoke about burnout, stigma, and racism, as well as frustration with school systems and health care providers. Despite these barriers, caregivers described the strength they draw from family, culture, and community. Cultural teachings, ceremonies, and language helped caregivers and their children feel proud, connected, and supported. Some families described autism as a gift from the Creator, showing how Indigenous ways of understanding autism can promote acceptance and belonging. This research shows the need for autism programs, services, and policies that are guided by Indigenous knowledge, community leadership, and cultural safety. It also highlights the importance of seeing autism through a strengths-based lens that values family relationships, community, and identity. By listening to First Nations caregivers, we can build more inclusive and culturally grounded supports for Autistic children and their families.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una niña o un niño autista, apoyarte en la familia, la cultura, la ceremonia y la comunidad puede ser una fuente real de fuerza, y está bien pedir apoyos que respeten tu cultura. Es un estudio cualitativo participativo en el que 14 cuidadoras y cuidadores de dos comunidades de las Primeras Naciones de Canadá compartieron su experiencia en entrevistas. Describieron agotamiento, estigma, racismo y dificultades con el diagnóstico y la escuela. Es un grupo pequeño de dos comunidades, así que no representa a todas las familias indígenas ni a todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic child, leaning on family, culture, ceremony and community can be a real source of strength, and it is fair to ask for supports that respect your culture. This was a qualitative, community-based participatory study: 14 First Nations caregivers in two communities in Canada shared their experiences in interviews. They described burnout, stigma, racism, and difficulties with diagnosis and school. It is a small group from two communities, so it cannot speak for all Indigenous families or for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du tar hand om ett autistiskt barn kan stödet från familj, kultur, ceremonier och gemenskap vara en verklig styrka, och det är rimligt att be om stöd som respekterar din kultur. Det var en kvalitativ, deltagarbaserad studie där 14 vårdnadshavare från First Nations i två samhällen i Kanada berättade om sina erfarenheter i intervjuer. De beskrev utmattning, stigma, rasism och svårigheter med utredning och skola. Gruppen är liten och kommer från två samhällen, så den kan inte tala för alla urfolksfamiljer eller för varje person.

title: Redefining autism in adulthood interventions in and through social virtual environments: an exploratory cross-cultural study.
authors: Grillo VD, Tanini G, Rana FC, Venuti P
journal: Frontiers in child and adolescent psychiatry
abstract: Background Autism intervention research has largely prioritized children and adolescents, with limited guidance for adults. Social virtual environments (SVEs; e.g., VRChat) are widely used by autistic adults for connection, yet their role as intervention settings remains under-examined. This study explores clinicians' perspectives on feasibility, risks, and essential design requirements for clinician-informed SVE-based socio-relational interventions for autistic young adults with low support needs. Methods We conducted nine semi-structured focus groups with Italian clinicians ( N = 26) across three regions (Veneto, Trentino, Lazio) and five semi-structured international interviews (U.S. n = 4; Australia n = 1). Transcripts were analyzed via inductive, codebook-informed thematic analysis grounded in reflexive qualitative principles. Because the study involved four coders working across two linguistically distinct datasets, a shared coding framework was used as a pragmatic coordination tool to support transparency, interpretive consistency, and auditability across the research team (the intent was not to establish positivist inter-rater reliability or eliminate researcher subjectivity). Datasets were first coded separately and then integrated through matrix-based synthesis to identify contextually situated points of convergence and divergence. Results Italian clinicians emphasized neurodiversity-affirming aims, context-dependent social difficulty (including anxiety/overwhelm), structured scaffolding and mediation, ecological generalization, and SVEs as conditional tools requiring boundaries. International clinicians foregrounded autonomy and choice, emotional safety in relation to masking, neurotype composition as an ingredient for belonging, identity-affirming collaboration, and regulation/repair practices. Across datasets, clinicians emphasized safety-contingent participation, non-negotiable personalization/controllability of demands (i.e., sensory, social), and the protective value of supported pauses and exits. Contextual differences centered on the dominant logic of support (competence-building scaffolding vs. liberation/identity integration), mediator-led structure vs. neurotype-aligned spaces, intersectionality as primary vs. contextual framing, and distinct risk emphases (avoidance/overuse vs. relational ambiguity and rejection). Conclusion Clinicians conceptualize SVEs not as inherently therapeutic technologies but as conditional social infrastructures whose potential value depends on how safety, autonomy, and identity are supported. Clinician-informed SVE-based interventions for autistic adults may therefore require integrating structured mediation with explicit autonomy- and identity-affirming safeguards, offering a pathway beyond the traditional' skills vs. acceptance' divide in autism intervention research.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta usa espacios sociales virtuales como VRChat, conviene que pueda elegir y ajustar las exigencias sensoriales y sociales, y que tenga pausas y salidas fáciles y sin presión. La evidencia es un estudio cualitativo con 26 profesionales clínicos italianos en grupos focales y 5 entrevistas internacionales. Recoge opiniones de profesionales, no de personas autistas, ni prueba si estos entornos ayudan. Los profesionales los ven como herramientas condicionadas a la seguridad, la autonomía y la identidad, no como terapia en sí. No sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult uses social virtual spaces like VRChat, it helps when they can choose and adjust the sensory and social demands, and have easy, pressure-free pauses and exits. The evidence is a qualitative study of focus groups with 26 Italian clinicians, plus 5 international interviews. It reflects professionals' views, not those of autistic people, and does not test whether these spaces help. Clinicians saw them as tools that depend on safety, autonomy and identity support, not as therapy in themselves. It is not a rule for everyone.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen använder sociala virtuella miljöer som VRChat hjälper det när personen kan välja och justera sensoriska och sociala krav, och har enkla pauser och utvägar utan press. Underlaget är en kvalitativ studie med fokusgrupper med 26 italienska kliniker samt 5 internationella intervjuer. Den speglar yrkesverksammas syn, inte autistiska personers, och prövar inte om miljöerna hjälper. Klinikerna såg dem som verktyg som beror på stöd för trygghet, autonomi och identitet, inte som terapi i sig. Det är ingen regel för alla.

title: Psychological Interventions for Children with Neurodevelopmental Disabilities in the Context of Neurodiversity: A Systematic Review.
authors: Megari K, Katsarou DV, Mantsos E, Papadopoulou S, Efthymiou E, Theodoratou M, Sofologi M, Toki E
abstract: Background/objectives This systematic review examines psychological interventions for children with neurodevelopmental disabilities within a neurodiversity framework, emphasizing that variations in cognition, behavior, and neurological functioning represent natural forms of human diversity rather than deficits. Methods A systematic literature search was conducted across the PubMed, PsycINFO, and Google Scholar databases for studies published between 2010 and 2025. Studies were included if they focused on children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), learning or intellectual disabilities (LD/ID), or specific learning disabilities (SpLD), and evaluated psychological or behavioral interventions. Results A total of 34 studies met the inclusion criteria after screening and full-text review. The findings indicate that traditional interventions, such as Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) and Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), demonstrate effectiveness in improving adaptive behavior, emotional regulation, and cognitive functioning. However, more recent approaches, including Naturalistic Developmental Behavioral Interventions (NDBI), person-centered therapies, and gamified interventions, show greater alignment with neurodiversity principles by emphasizing individual strengths, autonomy, and environmental adaptation. Conclusions Despite promising outcomes, the evidence base remains uneven, with a predominant focus on autism and limited high-quality studies addressing other neurodevelopmental conditions. The review highlights the need for more rigorous, inclusive, and longitudinal research, as well as the integration of neurodivergent perspectives in intervention design. Overall, the findings suggest that interventions incorporating individualized, strengths-based, and context-sensitive adaptations are associated with more consistent improvements in both functional outcomes and quality of life.

sheet.es: Al elegir apoyo psicológico para un niño o niña, conviene priorizar enfoques que partan de sus fortalezas, respeten su autonomía y adapten el entorno, en lugar de pedirle que cambie. Es una revisión sistemática de 34 estudios (2010-2025) con niños autistas y con discapacidades del aprendizaje o intelectuales. Enfoques como ABA y TCC mostraron mejoras, y los más recientes encajan mejor con la neurodiversidad. Limitaciones: la evidencia es desigual, se centra sobre todo en el autismo y hay pocos estudios de calidad sobre otras condiciones. No es una regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: When choosing psychological support for a child, it helps to favour approaches that build on their strengths, respect their autonomy and adapt the environment, rather than asking the child to change. This is a systematic review of 34 studies (2010-2025) with children who are autistic or have learning or intellectual disabilities. ABA and CBT showed improvements, and newer approaches fit better with neurodiversity principles. Limits: the evidence is uneven, focuses mostly on autism, and has few high-quality studies on other conditions. It is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: När du väljer psykologiskt stöd till ett barn är det bra att prioritera upplägg som utgår från barnets styrkor, respekterar dess autonomi och anpassar miljön, i stället för att be barnet förändras. Detta är en systematisk översikt av 34 studier (2010-2025) med barn som är autistiska eller har inlärnings- eller intellektuella funktionsnedsättningar. ABA och KBT visade förbättringar, och nyare angreppssätt passar bättre med neurodiversitet. Begränsningar: underlaget är ojämnt, fokuserar mest på autism och har få högkvalitativa studier om andra tillstånd. Det är ingen regel för alla.

title: Cultural Responsiveness in Community Early Intervention: A Mixed-Methods Observational Study of Coaching Practices.
authors: Dueñas AD, Caplan B, R Gallardo T, Ochoa W, Orendain-Soto C, Lopez KV, Valladares M, Rieth S
abstract: Background and purpose Caregiver-mediated early intervention (EI) for autistic children depends on meaningful caregiver engagement, yet Latine families face persistent structural and cultural barriers to equitable participation. Despite growing recognition of cultural responsiveness (CR) as a core EI component, few studies have examined how providers enact culturally responsive practices or whether those practices relate to observed caregiver engagement. This mixed-methods study examined that relationship in community-based EI services for Latine families of autistic children. Methods This secondary analysis drew from a larger community effectiveness trial conducted across EI agencies in California. Using an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design, Parent Participatory Engagement (PPE) scores from 95 videos were used to purposively sample sessions reflecting high (75th percentile; n = 26) and low (25th percentile; n = 25) caregiver engagement, yielding 51 videos for all quantitative and qualitative analyses. The sample included 16 EI providers (56.3% Latine) and 24 caregivers (87.5% Latine; 95.8% mothers) of children ages 12-36 months. A novel 12-item CR codebook was applied to sampled videos. Two ordinary least square regression models examined whether CR predicted PPE scores and which provider and session-level variables predicted CR. Inductive thematic analysis explored qualitative patterns in culturally responsive and unresponsive coaching. Results CR and caregiver engagement were significantly positively associated ( r = .44, p = .001; R 2 = .198). Provider and session-level predictors explained 51.1% of CR variance ( F (10,40) = 4.18, p p personalismo ) and validated caregiver concerns, non-exemplary practices were common-including failing to inquire about cultural alignment of strategies, not soliciting caregiver perspectives, and framing interventions as separate from everyday family routines. Conclusions and implications Findings reveal a gap between Individuals with Disabilities Education Act Part C mandates for family-centered EI and actual culturally responsive practice with Latine families. Providers frequently defaulted to hierarchical, practitioner-driven models that centered dominant cultural norms over families' values and daily practices. EI professional development must intentionally build providers' capacity for cultural humility, collaborative goal-setting, and embedding strategies within families' lived contexts.

sheet.es: Si participas en una intervención temprana, puedes pedir que las estrategias encajen con los valores y la rutina de tu familia, y que te pregunten tu opinión. Es un estudio observacional de métodos mixtos con 51 vídeos de sesiones, 16 profesionales y 24 cuidadores de niños autistas de 12-36 meses, casi todos familias latinas en California. Las sesiones más sensibles a la cultura se asociaron con mayor participación de los cuidadores, pero a menudo no se preguntaba por la adecuación cultural ni se recogía la perspectiva familiar. Es una asociación, no prueba causa, y no representa a todas las familias ni servicios.
sheet.en: If you take part in early intervention, you can ask that strategies fit your family's values and daily routines, and that providers ask for your views. This was an observational mixed-methods study of 51 session videos, with 16 providers and 24 caregivers of autistic children aged 12-36 months, mostly Latine families in California. Sessions that were more culturally responsive were linked to higher caregiver engagement, yet providers often did not ask about cultural fit or seek caregiver perspectives. It shows an association, not cause, and does not represent every family or service.
sheet.sv: Om du deltar i tidig intervention kan du be att strategierna passar familjens värderingar och vardagsrutiner, och att personalen frågar efter dina synpunkter. Det var en observationsstudie med blandade metoder, med 51 sessionsvideor, 16 yrkespersoner och 24 vårdnadshavare till autistiska barn i åldern 12-36 månader, mest latinofamiljer i Kalifornien. Mer kulturellt lyhörda sessioner hängde ihop med större engagemang hos vårdnadshavare, men personalen frågade ofta inte om kulturell passform eller om familjens perspektiv. Studien visar ett samband, inte orsak, och gäller inte alla familjer eller verksamheter.

title: Mixed Methods Findings from a Stepped Wedge Hybrid Implementation Trial of ATTAIN NAV: A Mental Health Family Navigation Intervention for Autistic Youth.
authors: Stadnick NA, Martinez K, Navarro F, Gomez-Patino P, Holmquist K, Negriff S, Roesch S, Bouchard I, Walpole S, Espinosa R, Broder-Fingert S, Barnett M, Brookman-Frazee L
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: ATTAIN NAV (Access to Tailored Autism Integrated Care through Family Navigation) was delivered by family navigators to promote access to and engagement with mental health services for school-age autistic youth. This study used a mixed method, stepped wedge design to test the effects of family navigation on service and clinical outcomes while gathering information on implementation. Primary care providers from six clinics in California and 56 caregiver-child dyads enrolled in and completed the study. Clinics were randomized to either a technology-enhanced or standard family navigation condition. Caregivers completed assessments at baseline and post about child, family and services outcomes, and a subset participated in a post qualitative interview. Quantitative findings demonstrated improvements in child challenging behavior and parent activation across conditions although these improvements were more pronounced for families in the standard FN condition. At post-intervention, families in the standard FN condition reported higher levels of navigation satisfaction, a shorter time to attend their first mental health appointment, and higher engagement with their navigator. Qualitative findings complemented and expanded the quantitative survey findings. The ATTAIN NAV model of family navigation for autistic children with co-occurring mental health needs demonstrates promising implementation, service, and clinical benefits. Clinical Trials Registration. NCT05344378.

sheet.es: Si buscas apoyo de salud mental para tu hijo o hija autista, pregunta si hay un servicio de orientación familiar: una persona que te acompañe a encontrar y llegar a las citas. Es un ensayo con 56 parejas de cuidador y menor autista en edad escolar, atendidas en seis clínicas de California. Las familias mejoraron en la activación de los padres y en la conducta del menor, y quienes tuvieron la orientación estándar mostraron más satisfacción, primera cita más pronta y mayor implicación con la persona orientadora. El estudio es pequeño, se hizo en un solo estado y no sirve como regla para todas las familias.
sheet.en: If you are looking for mental health support for your autistic child, ask whether a family navigation service exists: a person who helps you find services and get to appointments. This was a trial with 56 caregiver and school-age autistic child pairs at six clinics in California. Families improved in parent activation and child behaviour, and those receiving standard navigation reported higher satisfaction, a shorter wait for the first appointment and more engagement with their navigator. The study is small, took place in one state, and is not a rule for every family.
sheet.sv: Om du söker psykisk hälsostöd för ditt autistiska barn, fråga om det finns familjenavigering: en person som hjälper dig att hitta tjänster och ta dig till besöken. Detta var en studie med 56 par av vårdnadshavare och autistiska skolbarn vid sex kliniker i Kalifornien. Familjerna förbättrades i föräldraaktivering och barnets beteende, och de som fick standardnavigering rapporterade högre nöjdhet, kortare tid till första besöket och mer engagemang med sin navigatör. Studien är liten, gjordes i en enda delstat och är ingen regel för alla familjer.

title: Social Responsiveness as a Mediator in Adapted Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Autistic Youth with Maladaptive and Interfering Anxiety.
authors: Wood JJ, Storch EA, Sung K, Wood KS, Kendall PC
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Numerous adaptations to interventions have been included in cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) for autistic youth. This study examines the degree to which CBT adapted to the social needs of autistic youth confers significant benefit by promoting social responsiveness. A secondary analysis was conducted on a multisite randomized clinical trial (Wood et al. in JAMA Psychiatry 77:474-483, 2020) comparing adapted CBT with standard-of-practice CBT and treatment-as-usual (TA). Autistic youth (N = 167; aged 7-13) with maladaptive and interfering anxiety participated. The adapted CBT (BIACA) uses a modular format, with an emphasis on supplementing common CBT practice elements (reframing and graded exposure) with social skill supports. The primary outcome measure was the Pediatric Anxiety Rating Scale. Social responsiveness was assessed with the Social Responsiveness Scale, Second Edition. Participants' general mental health was assessed as a secondary outcome using the Brief Problem Checklist. Mediation was tested using the SPSS PROCESS macro. Analyses suggested that the effect of adapted CBT on anxiety was mediated by its effects on social responsiveness, with a statistically significant indirect effect. Youth randomly assigned to adapted CBT exhibited better overall mental health at posttreatment compared to those randomized to the other conditions, and this effect was also mediated by improved social responsiveness. CBT adapted to address some of the social needs of autistic youth may enhance mental health outcomes by supporting social responsiveness, perhaps increasing the ease and effectiveness with which some youth can navigate potentially stressful situations such as entering and participating in group activities.

sheet.es: Si buscas apoyo para la ansiedad de un niño o una niña autista, puedes preguntar a los terapeutas si su terapia cognitivo-conductual incluye apoyos para las habilidades sociales, como practicar situaciones de grupo paso a paso. Este análisis secundario de un ensayo aleatorizado incluyó a 167 jóvenes autistas de 7-13 años con ansiedad. La terapia adaptada se asoció con menos ansiedad y mejor salud mental, en parte por una mejor respuesta social. Es un análisis de mediación: no prueba por sí solo la causa, y no sirve igual para todas las personas. Las decisiones sobre tratamientos deben hablarse con un profesional.
sheet.en: If you are looking for anxiety support for an autistic child or teen, you can ask therapists whether their cognitive behavioral therapy includes social skill supports, such as practising group situations step by step. This secondary analysis of a randomized trial included 167 autistic youth aged 7-13 with anxiety. The adapted therapy was linked to less anxiety and better mental health, partly through improved social responsiveness. It is a mediation analysis, so it cannot prove cause on its own, and it will not fit every person in the same way. Treatment decisions are best discussed with a professional.
sheet.sv: Om du söker stöd för ångest hos ett autistiskt barn eller en autistisk tonåring kan du fråga terapeuter om deras kognitiva beteendeterapi innehåller stöd för sociala färdigheter, till exempel att öva gruppsituationer steg för steg. Denna sekundäranalys av en randomiserad studie omfattade 167 autistiska ungdomar i åldern 7-13 med ångest. Den anpassade terapin hängde ihop med mindre ångest och bättre psykisk hälsa, delvis genom bättre social responsivitet. Det är en medieringsanalys, så den kan inte ensam bevisa orsak och passar inte alla på samma sätt. Beslut om behandling bör diskuteras med en yrkesperson.

title: Autism and Dementia: A Summative Report from the 2nd International Summit on Intellectual Disabilities and Dementia.
authors: Janicki MP, McCallion P, Jokinen N, Larsen FK, Mughal D, Palanisamy V, Santos F, Service K, Shih A, Shooshtari S, Thakur A, Tiziano G, Watchman K
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: This article synthesizes findings, from the Autism/Dementia Work Group of the 2nd International Summit on Intellectual Disabilities and Dementia, on the nature of autism/autism spectrum disorder and later-age neuropathologies, particularly dementia. The convened group of experts explored genetic, neurobiological, and environmental risk factors that may affect the lifespan and lived experiences of older adults with autism. A review of current literature indicates a lack of comprehensive information on the demographics and factors associated with aging in autistic adults. However, our understanding of autism is evolving, challenging traditional views of it as a static, inherited neurodevelopmental disorder. The relationship between autism and other neurodevelopmental conditions-such as Down syndrome, fragile X syndrome, and tuberous sclerosis complex-reflects the complex genetic landscape of neurodevelopmental disorders. These genetic and familial factors may contribute to progressive health challenges and cognitive decline in later life. Key findings reveal a complex link between autism and dementia, despite limited research on this relationship, particularly among older adults. The overall prevalence of dementia in this population appears to be influenced by co-occurring intellectual disabilities, particularly Down syndrome. While the association between autism and specific types of dementia is still not well understood, the reviewed evidence suggests a notable connection with frontotemporal dementia, although causality has not been established. Exploration of biomarkers may offer further insights. Currently, the relationship between autism, cognitive health, and cognitive decline in older adults remains a complex and underexplored area of research.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista que envejece, merece la pena anotar su forma habitual de comunicarse, sus rutinas y habilidades, para notar a tiempo cambios nuevos y comentarlos con su equipo de salud. Un cambio no significa demencia: el estrés, el dolor o el agotamiento también influyen. La evidencia procede de un informe de expertos de una cumbre internacional que revisó la investigación sobre autismo y demencia; sugiere un posible vínculo, sobre todo con la demencia frontotemporal y cuando hay síndrome de Down. Sus límites: hay muy pocos estudios con personas autistas mayores, no se ha demostrado causalidad y no predice lo que vivirá cada persona.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person who is getting older, it can help to note their usual ways of communicating, routines and skills, so new changes are noticed early and shared with their health team. A change does not mean dementia: stress, pain or burnout matter too. The evidence comes from an expert summit report reviewing research on autism and dementia; it suggests a possible link, especially with frontotemporal dementia and when Down syndrome is present. Its limits: very few studies include older autistic adults, causation has not been shown, and it cannot predict any individual's future.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person som blir äldre kan det hjälpa att anteckna hur hen brukar kommunicera, sina rutiner och förmågor, så att nya förändringar upptäcks tidigt och kan tas upp med vården. En förändring betyder inte demens: stress, smärta eller utmattning spelar också roll. Underlaget är en rapport från en internationell expertkonferens som granskat forskning om autism och demens; den antyder ett möjligt samband, särskilt med frontotemporal demens och vid Downs syndrom. Begränsningar: mycket få studier omfattar äldre autistiska vuxna, orsakssamband är inte visat och rapporten kan inte förutsäga enskilda personers framtid.

title: Sensitivity and Expected Change of Commonly Used Social Communication Measures in Longitudinal Research of Young Autistic Children.
authors: Sterrett K, Pizzano M
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Social communication measures used to track change in autistic children have not undergone rigorous psychometric evaluation. There is little data on their expected change or sensitivity to change. Meta-analytic techniques were used to examine sensitivity to change and expected change over time and whether these are influenced by factors like children's age and the presence of intervention. Pooled effect sizes were generated within measures, rather than within broader constructs. Change over time was small to medium, although there was variability. Most outcomes were not sensitive to change over time. Change in some measures was influenced by child characteristics and methodological characteristics of included studies such as study quality and the method of scoring measures (e.g., using age-equivalents versus standard scores). Tests measuring similar constructs can vary in their expected change, and so care is needed when selecting them.

sheet.es: Si un profesional o un equipo de investigación usa pruebas de comunicación social para seguir el progreso de un niño autista, conviene preguntar qué prueba es y cómo se puntúa, porque no todas detectan los cambios igual. Se trata de un metaanálisis que reunió estudios longitudinales con niños autistas pequeños. El cambio con el tiempo fue de pequeño a medio, con variabilidad, y la mayoría de los resultados no fue sensible al cambio. Como límite, el resultado depende de la calidad de los estudios y de cómo se puntuó cada prueba, así que no describe a ningún niño en concreto. Una cifra baja no significa que no haya avances.
sheet.en: If a professional or research team uses social communication tests to track an autistic child's progress, it helps to ask which test it is and how it is scored, because they do not all pick up change equally well. This is a meta-analysis that pooled longitudinal studies of young autistic children. Change over time was small to medium, with variability, and most outcomes were not sensitive to change. A limit is that results depended on study quality and on how each test was scored, so they do not describe any one child. A flat score does not necessarily mean no progress.
sheet.sv: Om en yrkesperson eller ett forskarteam använder sociala kommunikationstest för att följa en autistisk barns utveckling är det bra att fråga vilket test det är och hur det poängsätts, eftersom de inte fångar förändring lika bra. Detta är en metaanalys som sammanställde longitudinella studier av små autistiska barn. Förändringen över tid var liten till medelstor, med variation, och de flesta utfall var inte känsliga för förändring. En begränsning är att resultaten berodde på studiernas kvalitet och på hur varje test poängsattes, så de beskriver inte ett enskilt barn. Ett oförändrat resultat betyder inte nödvändigtvis att det inte finns framsteg.

title: Excitation/Inhibition Balance as a Mechanistic Link Between Sleep Disturbance and Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Bidirectional Framework.
authors: Wu Y, Wu D, Zhong W, Ma J
abstract: Sleep disturbances are highly prevalent in autism spectrum disorder (ASD), yet their significance may extend beyond that of a common co-occurring condition. Growing evidence suggests that excitation/inhibition (E/I)-related network dysregulation may provide a valuable framework for understanding the association between sleep disturbances and variability in core ASD symptom expression. This review synthesizes findings from polysomnography, actigraphy, circadian rhythm research, neuroimaging, electrophysiological studies, and animal models to examine how E/I-related vulnerability in ASD may contribute to impaired sleep initiation and maintenance. It further explores how sleep and circadian disruption may, in turn, influence daytime symptom expression through alterations in synaptic homeostasis and network rebalancing. By proposing a bidirectional framework, this review aims to integrate current evidence on sleep-related symptom variability in ASD and to inform future longitudinal, mechanistic, and biomarker-driven research.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista duerme mal, vale la pena tratar el sueño como algo importante en sí mismo y no como un detalle secundario. Mañana puede anotar a qué hora se duerme, cuántas veces se despierta y cómo es el día siguiente, y compartirlo con su profesional de salud. Esto es una revisión que reúne estudios de sueño, ritmos circadianos, neuroimagen y modelos animales, y propone que sueño y rasgos diurnos podrían influirse en ambos sentidos. Sus límites: es un marco teórico, no demuestra causas y pide más estudios a lo largo del tiempo. No sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person sleeps poorly, it is worth treating sleep as important in its own right, not a minor side issue. Tomorrow you could note bedtime, night waking and how the next day goes, and share this with a health professional. This is a review pulling together sleep studies, circadian rhythm research, brain imaging and animal models. It proposes that sleep and daytime traits may influence each other in both directions. Its limits: it is a theoretical framework, does not prove causes, and calls for more studies following people over time. It is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person sover dåligt är det värt att se sömnen som viktig i sig och inte som en bisak. I morgon kan du notera läggtid, nattliga uppvaknanden och hur nästa dag blir, och dela det med vårdpersonal. Det här är en översikt som samlar sömnstudier, forskning om dygnsrytm, hjärnavbildning och djurmodeller. Den föreslår att sömn och dagtida drag kan påverka varandra åt båda håll. Begränsningar: det är ett teoretiskt ramverk, bevisar inga orsaker och efterlyser fler studier över tid. Det är ingen regel för alla.

title: A Systematic Review of Help-Seeking Barriers for Racial-Ethnic Minority Caregivers Accessing Autism Diagnostic and Intervention Services.
authors: Khalil A, Yatcilla J, Christie N, Zhou X
journal: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities
abstract: Caregivers play an essential role in early help-seeking and intervention for children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). Caregivers, therefore, provide a crucial role in helping to address the racial and ethnic disparity identified in accessing ASD intervention and diagnostic services (Bejarano-Martín et al., Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders 50(9), 3380-3394, 2020). Unfortunately, racial-ethnic minority caregivers of children with autism (CCA) are less likely to contact a physician or healthcare professionals about their concerns and more likely to delay their contact to have their child evaluated (Zeleke et al., Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders 49(10), 4320-4331, 2019). However, little evidence exists to explain why such a gap exists in the help-seeking behaviors between White and racial-ethnic minority CCA. To address this knowledge gap, we conducted a systematic literature review to identify articles that have studied barriers in help-seeking for racial-ethnic minority CCA. A broad literature search across four databases was conducted (i.e., PubMed, PsycINFO, Education Resources Information Center, and Child Development and Adolescent Studies). The coding team identified 17 articles on help-seeking barriers for racial-ethnic minority CCA. A thematic analysis was used to narratively synthesize the help-seeking barriers identified across these 17 studies. Four themes emerged from our findings: logistical barriers, provider competence, ASD literacy, and cultural stigma. We also provided clinical recommendations for healthcare providers working with families with racial-ethnic minority CCA.

sheet.es: Si buscas una evaluación o apoyo y encuentras obstáculos, no es culpa tuya: la investigación señala barreras del sistema. Anota tus preocupaciones, pide intérprete o información clara si la necesitas y expresa qué te dificulta el acceso. La evidencia es una revisión sistemática de 17 artículos sobre cuidadores de minorías raciales y étnicas. Surgieron cuatro temas: barreras logísticas, competencia de los profesionales, conocimiento sobre el autismo y estigma cultural. Como límite, es una síntesis narrativa y no explica la situación de cada familia ni demuestra qué soluciones funcionan.
sheet.en: If you are seeking an assessment or support and hit obstacles, it is not your fault: research points to barriers in the system. Write down your concerns, ask for an interpreter or clear information if you need it, and say what makes access hard. The evidence is a systematic review of 17 articles about racial-ethnic minority caregivers. Four themes emerged: logistical barriers, provider competence, autism literacy and cultural stigma. A limit is that it is a narrative synthesis, so it cannot describe every family's situation or prove which solutions work.
sheet.sv: Om du söker utredning eller stöd och stöter på hinder är det inte ditt fel: forskningen pekar på hinder i systemet. Skriv ner dina funderingar, be om tolk eller tydlig information om du behöver det och berätta vad som gör det svårt att få tillgång. Underlaget är en systematisk översikt av 17 artiklar om vårdnadshavare från rasifierade och etniska minoriteter. Fyra teman framträdde: logistiska hinder, vårdgivares kompetens, kunskap om autism och kulturellt stigma. En begränsning är att det är en narrativ sammanställning som inte beskriver varje familjs situation eller visar vilka lösningar som fungerar.

title: Gastrointestinal Microbiota Imbalance and Sensory Processing Dysregulation in Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review.
authors: Bonner-Reid FT
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by challenges with social communication and repetitive behaviors. Many people with ASD also experience gastrointestinal symptoms and sensory processing dysfunction. New research has identified a potential role for microbial dysbiosis (imbalance of gut microbiota) in these comorbidities. This systematic review aimed to explore the links between gut microbiota composition, gastrointestinal symptoms, sensory processing differences, and dietary patterns in individuals with ASD, as well as the potential for a bidirectional relationship and dietary-based interventions targeting the microbiota. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were used to retrieve publications from 2011 to 2026, and a systematic review was conducted. Studies were chosen that examined gut microbiota, gastrointestinal symptoms, and sensory processing in people with ASD. Only intervention and observational studies were included. Many people with ASD reported gastrointestinal symptoms, sensory processing differences, restricted dietary patterns, and gut microbiota composition. However, the majority of studies included were cross-sectional, which does not allow for an inference of temporal direction or causality. The evidence indicates there may be a bidirectional relationship between gastrointestinal and sensory symptoms and microbial differences, and the sensory symptoms, food selectivity, food restriction, stool consistency, use of medication, and clinical characteristics may also affect the composition of the microbiota. Initial microbiome interventions had some potential for improvement in selected outcomes, but with limited confidence due to small sample sizes, heterogeneity in methods used, and potential for bias. The current evidence suggests that changes in the gut microbiota composition are associated with gastrointestinal symptoms, sensory dysregulation, and dietary patterns in ASD, but does not provide evidence to indicate that microbial dysbiosis is a primary mechanism. The possibility of reverse causation exists, as the food environment could be influenced by sensory sensitivity and/or eating habits, and, in turn, these factors could affect the composition of the microbiota. To better understand directionality and the efficacy of microbiome-targeted interventions, longitudinal studies and sufficiently powered randomized controlled trials are warranted.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista tiene molestias digestivas, sensibilidades sensoriales o una alimentación muy selectiva, conviene observar estos aspectos juntos y comentarlos con su profesional de salud, sin culpar a la persona ni forzar cambios en la dieta. Es una revisión sistemática de estudios publicados entre 2011 y 2026 sobre microbiota intestinal, síntomas digestivos y procesamiento sensorial en personas autistas. Sus límites: la mayoría de los estudios eran transversales, así que no muestran qué causa qué, y las primeras intervenciones sobre la microbiota eran pequeñas y poco fiables. No es una regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person has digestive discomfort, sensory sensitivities or a very selective diet, it helps to notice these together and raise them with their health professional, without blaming the person or forcing diet changes. This is a systematic review of studies published between 2011 and 2026 on gut microbiota, digestive symptoms and sensory processing in autistic people. Its limits: most studies were cross-sectional, so they cannot show what causes what, and early microbiome interventions were small and uncertain. It is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person har magproblem, sensoriska känsligheter eller en mycket selektiv kost kan det hjälpa att se dem tillsammans och ta upp dem med hälso- och sjukvården, utan att skuldbelägga personen eller tvinga fram kostförändringar. Det här är en systematisk översikt av studier publicerade mellan 2011 och 2026 om tarmflora, magsymtom och sensorisk bearbetning hos autistiska personer. Begränsningar: de flesta studierna var tvärsnittsstudier och kan därför inte visa vad som orsakar vad, och tidiga interventioner på tarmfloran var små och osäkra. Det är ingen regel för alla.

title: Reclaiming selfhood: towards a conceptualisation of the autistic unmasking process.
authors: Hedlund Å, Unéus D, Wik J, Ingard C, Isakson K, Black MH, Hirvikoski T, Bertilsdotter Rosqvist H
abstract: Introduction Many autistic people adapt to a neurotypical world through masking, which can lead to exhaustion and harm to mental and physical health. As a result, there is increasingly interest in 'unmasking' in ways that improve quality of life and reduce stress. This study analyses qualitative data to explore unmasking among autistic adults. Methods This was a neurodivergent-led study. Twenty-nine autistic adults (17 with co-occurring ADHD) were interviewed one to four times as part of a larger project on autistic flourishing. Data related to unmasking were analysed using qualitative content analysis. Results Unmasking occurred through a circular process consisting of four categories (1): Identify the need to unmask (2), Gain a deeper understanding of one's masking (3), Using unmasking strategies, and (4) Managing the consequences of unmasking. Conclusion Unmasking can be both challenging and freeing for autistic adults and may be best approached gradually. Supportive environments and professionals who understand masking and its long-term impact and do not encourage masking are important.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista quiere dejar de enmascarar, puede ayudar ir poco a poco y ofrecer entornos donde no tenga que fingir. Escuchar sin presionar ni animar a enmascarar es un buen punto de partida. Este estudio entrevistó a 29 adultos autistas (17 con TDAH asociado), en un trabajo dirigido por personas neurodivergentes, y describió el desenmascaramiento como un proceso circular de cuatro pasos. Libera, pero también puede resultar difícil. Sus límites: es un estudio cualitativo con pocas personas adultas, y no muestra cómo será el proceso de cada persona, ni el de niños o adolescentes.
sheet.en: If an autistic person wants to mask less, going gradually can help, along with spaces where they don't have to pretend. Listening without pressure, and without encouraging masking, is a good place to start. This study interviewed 29 autistic adults (17 with co-occurring ADHD) in a neurodivergent-led project, and described unmasking as a circular process with four steps. It can be freeing, but also difficult. Its limits: it is a qualitative study with a small group of adults, and it cannot show how the process will look for any one person, or for children and teenagers.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person vill maskera mindre kan det hjälpa att gå fram gradvis och att finnas i miljöer där hen inte behöver låtsas. Att lyssna utan press, och utan att uppmuntra maskering, är en bra start. Studien intervjuade 29 autistiska vuxna (17 med samtidig ADHD) i ett neurodivergent lett projekt och beskrev avmaskering som en cirkulär process i fyra steg. Den kan vara befriande men också svår. Begränsningar: det är en kvalitativ studie med en liten grupp vuxna, och den visar inte hur processen blir för en enskild person eller för barn och tonåringar.

title: AllPlay Dance autism: protocol for a randomised controlled trial of a community-based dance programme for children with autism.
authors: Chadha M, Lindor E, Millard O, Moss S, Rinehart N
abstract: Introduction Motor skills are integral to numerous developmental domains throughout infancy and childhood. In autism, motor impairments are prevalent and pervasive, often appearing before core symptoms. These motor difficulties have a cascading effect on a child's broader physical and psychological health, including social, cognitive, emotional and behavioural functioning. Accordingly, researchers are increasingly interested in interventions that improve motor functioning, as these may have a downstream effect on broader developmental domains. One intervention that could address motor difficulties is the AllPlay Dance programme, which provides inclusive dance classes to children in community settings, with pilot data demonstrating acceptability and feasibility among parents and their children with autism and cerebral palsy. This pragmatic randomised controlled trial (pRCT) is thus designed to evaluate whether the AllPlay Dance programme creates the conditions for motor, cognitive and social abilities to thrive in children with autism. Method and analysis This pRCT intends to enrol 70 families of children with autism, aged 7-12 years, living in Victoria, Australia. We will also enrol up to 60 participants with previous dance experience, called buddies, to support the participation of our dancers with autism. We will use our clinical, research, university and community networks to recruit participants. Interested families will complete an online screening survey, followed by questionnaires that parents complete and assessments of the motor functioning in the children. Interested buddies will also complete an online screening survey followed by a baseline questionnaire. Families will be randomly allocated to the intervention group or the treatment-as-usual waitlist control group. The intervention group will attend 9 weeks of community-based dance classes led by disability and dance experts and supported by buddies. The primary outcome is change in motor functioning, as assessed through performance-based measures, with parent reports providing complementary information about everyday motor functioning. Secondary outcomes include improvements in the executive, social, emotional and behavioural functioning of the children, as well as decreases in the stress of parents. We will also evaluate the acceptability and feasibility of this programme, as well as whether families decide to enrol and engage with other dance programmes in the community following the intervention. Ethics and dissemination The study has received approval from the Monash University Human Research Ethics Committee and the Deakin University Human Research Ethics Committee.
