Findings will be disseminated through a PhD thesis, peer-reviewed publications, presentations at scientific conferences and reports to participants, community organisations and the wider community. Trial registration number Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry (ANZCTR); ACTRN12625000600448; registered on 11 June 2025; https://anzctr.org.au/Trial/Registration/TrialReview.aspx?id=389672.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija disfruta del movimiento, una clase de baile inclusiva en la comunidad puede ser una opción que vale la pena explorar, sin presión y a su ritmo. Este estudio es un protocolo: describe un ensayo aleatorizado que aún debe mostrar resultados. Prevé 70 familias de niños autistas de 7-12 años en Victoria, Australia; un grupo hará 9 semanas de clases de baile y otro esperará. Se medirán habilidades motoras y también otros aspectos. Límites: no hay resultados todavía, así que no sabemos si el programa ayuda, y los efectos pueden variar mucho entre personas.
sheet.en: If your child enjoys movement, an inclusive community dance class may be worth exploring, at their own pace and without pressure. This study is a protocol: it describes a randomised trial that has yet to report results. It plans to include 70 families of autistic children aged 7-12 years in Victoria, Australia; one group will do 9 weeks of dance classes while another waits. Motor skills will be measured, along with other areas. Limits: there are no results yet, so we do not know whether the programme helps, and experiences may differ a lot between people.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn gillar rörelse kan en inkluderande danskurs i närsamhället vara värd att utforska, i barnets egen takt och utan press. Studien är ett protokoll: den beskriver en randomiserad studie som ännu inte har redovisat resultat. Den planerar att inkludera 70 familjer med autistiska barn i åldern 7-12 år i Victoria, Australien; en grupp går 9 veckors danskurs medan en annan väntar. Motoriska färdigheter mäts, tillsammans med andra områden. Begränsningar: inga resultat finns än, så vi vet inte om programmet hjälper, och upplevelser kan skilja sig mycket mellan personer.

title: Artificial intelligence-supported therapeutic interventions for autism spectrum disorder: a systematic review.
authors: Kuca J, Stencel M, Pilarski B, Florek S, Pudlo R
abstract: Background The increased prevalence of ASD has generated a pressing demand for flexible therapeutic and educational tools. AI has been suggested as a potential bridge to this gap, but the translation from a model to a clinical application necessitates rigorous assessment. The purpose of the present review is to compile and examine the existing literature to demonstrate AI interventions that have advanced from a proposed model to being used with human participants. Methods We systematically searched five databases (Embase, PubMed, ScienceDirect, IEEE Xplore, Web of Science; Jan 2016-Dec 2025) for AI-based ASD interventions. Two reviewers independently assessed eligibility. Inclusion criteria were as followed: (1) participants with confirmed ASD diagnoses; (2) an intervention sample size of N ≥ 6; (3) AI as a central therapeutic, educational, or rehabilitative component; and (4) multi-session protocols with specified timeframes. Study types ranged from system development and feasibility trials to RCTs. Results 14 studies met inclusion criteria. AI (e.g. robotics, VR, and wearables) functioned as a social mediator, improving social-emotional outcomes (e.g., ADOS, SRS scores) by reducing cognitive load. Significant mechanisms included real-time task adaptation and precise behavioral monitoring via e.g. eye-tracking. However, significant heterogeneity was observed in intervention dosage (median 4-12 hours). Most studies were limited by small, male-dominated samples (N Conclusion Based on the findings, AI seems highly promising for patient-specific ASD therapy via proactive, data-driven scaffolding. In order to move toward implementation of AI in ASD care, more RCTs and crucial augmentation of representation gaps concerning adult and female ASD phenotype studies are required.

sheet.es: Si le ofrecen herramientas con inteligencia artificial (robots, realidad virtual, dispositivos portátiles), pueden ser una opción para practicar habilidades sociales, pero conviene probarlas con calma y fijarse en cómo responde la persona autista. La evidencia es una revisión sistemática de 14 estudios con participantes con diagnóstico confirmado de autismo, que describe cambios en resultados sociales y emocionales. Sus límites: la dosis varió mucho (mediana de 4-12 horas), las muestras eran pequeñas y mayoritariamente masculinas, y faltan estudios en adultos y mujeres, además de más ensayos aleatorizados. No sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you are offered AI-based tools (robots, virtual reality, wearables), they may be one option for practising social skills, but try them gently and watch how the autistic person responds. The evidence is a systematic review of 14 studies with participants who had a confirmed autism diagnosis, describing changes in social and emotional outcomes. Its limits: the amount of intervention varied widely (median 4-12 hours), samples were small and mostly male, and studies with adults and women, plus more randomised trials, are still needed. It is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du erbjuds AI-baserade verktyg (robotar, virtuell verklighet, bärbar teknik) kan de vara ett alternativ för att öva social samvaro, men prova försiktigt och se hur den autistiska personen reagerar. Underlaget är en systematisk översikt av 14 studier med deltagare som hade en bekräftad autismdiagnos och som beskriver förändringar i sociala och känslomässiga resultat. Begränsningar: mängden insats varierade mycket (median 4-12 timmar), urvalen var små och mest manliga, och det behövs fler studier med vuxna och kvinnor samt fler randomiserade studier. Det är ingen regel för alla.

title: Autistic interests: wide-ranging and intellectually oriented.
authors: Caldwell-Harris CL
abstract: Introduction The interests of autistic individuals have traditionally been described as circumscribed and restricted, serving the functions of self-regulation by reducing prediction error. Historically, this may have seemed reasonable when applied to autistic children and adults with intellectual disability. The current study investigated the restrictiveness and function of focused interests of autistic adults with typical intellectual ability. Methods To hear from autistic adults themselves, bypassing interviewers' agendas, online discussion posts were analyzed from threads that opened with questions such as What are your special interests ? Content analysis was utilized to categorize the special interest topics into a taxonomy (e.g., Academic, Entertainment) and to code for functions, including knowledge seeking (systemizing), mastery, self-regulation, and socializing. Word frequency analyses tallied terms associated with intellectual content and intensity, to evaluate whether interests serve knowledge-seeking vs self-regulation. Results Academic topics dominated the interests mentioned, appearing in approximately half of all posts, with psychology-related topics being the most frequent, appearing in 29% of posts. Interests were often highly specific, but were frequently the opposite of restricted. Many posts described a large, diverse range of interests, spanning disparate domains, which was labeled wide-ranging intellectual appetite . Knowledge seeking emerged as the primary function, with 52% of posts containing relevant terms (e.g., learn, read, research ). Intellectual approaches to an interest were frequently reported even for non-academic topics like fictional worlds, cooking, pets and true crime. Posts describing the purpose of interests as self-regulation appeared in 9% of posts, career, 6% of posts, and socializing, 4% of posts. Discussion The findings challenge the traditional deficit perspective by demonstrating that focused interests in autistic adults are characterized by knowledge seeking, a construct similar to systemizing, but more explicitly on a continuum with academic interests. These interests are not restricted but wide-ranging, resembling the explorations of polymaths. The established view, that intense interests reduce anxiety by promoting predictability, originated in historical attention to autistic individuals with atypical intellectual ability. Intellectual disability obscured how repetitive behaviors such as object manipulation are 'experiments to see'. I propose that knowledge-seeking is the primary function of systemizing and intense interests, thus unifying focused interests across multiple levels of intellectual ability of the autism spectrum.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista adulta, pregúntale por sus intereses y deja espacio para que aprenda, lea e investigue sobre ellos, sin darlos por repetitivos o limitados. Este estudio analizó publicaciones en foros en línea de personas autistas adultas con capacidad intelectual típica. El 52% de las publicaciones mencionaba buscar conocimiento, y el 9% hablaba de autorregulación. Muchas describían intereses amplios y variados. Sus límites: se basa en textos en línea de quienes escriben en foros, no en entrevistas, y no representa a todas las personas autistas, por ejemplo a quienes tienen discapacidad intelectual. Cada persona es distinta.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult, ask about their interests and leave room for them to learn, read and research them, rather than assuming they are narrow or repetitive. This study analysed online forum posts by autistic adults with typical intellectual ability. Knowledge seeking appeared in 52% of posts, and self-regulation in 9%. Many posts described wide, varied interests. Limits: it relies on forum text from people who choose to write online, not interviews, and it does not represent every autistic person, for example those with intellectual disability. Every person is different.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen, fråga om hens intressen och ge utrymme att lära sig, läsa och forska om dem, i stället för att anta att de är snäva eller repetitiva. Studien analyserade inlägg i nätforum från autistiska vuxna med typisk intellektuell förmåga. Kunskapssökande fanns i 52% av inläggen och självreglering i 9%. Många beskrev breda, varierande intressen. Begränsningar: den bygger på forumtext från personer som väljer att skriva online, inte intervjuer, och gäller inte alla autistiska personer, till exempel dem med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning. Alla är olika.

title: Outcomes of Experiencing Interpersonal Violence in Autism: A Mixed Methods Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Cooke K, Ridgway K, Pecora L, Westrupp E, Hedley D, Hooley M, Stokes MA
abstract: In this review and meta-analysis, we aimed to examine outcomes of interpersonal violence among autistic people. Intersectionality and minority theories suggest that negative outcomes are heightened among people with multiple marginalized identities. Thus, we also aimed to investigate gender-related outcomes of interpersonal violence among autistic people. We conducted a systematic database search with inclusion criteria including mixed methods, peer-reviewed research examining any harmful interpersonal act (e.g., physical, sexual, and psychological) experienced by autistic people. We undertook a random-effects meta-analysis with pooled data from 9 studies, comprising 3,647 autistic participants aged 1 to 80 years. Violence was associated with worsened mental health, with the strongest association for internalizing symptoms ( d = 0.66, p d = 0.63, p < .001; [0.44, 0.82]). Narrative synthesis of 57 studies comprising 37,418 participants (13,127 autistic, 24,291 non-autistic) found violence was associated with numerous adverse health, development, and functional outcomes, including worsened mental health and behavioral difficulties compared to non-autistic controls from childhood. Females and gender minorities reported greater intra- and interpersonal health and development difficulties related to violence, emerging in early childhood and enduring into adulthood. Findings provide strong evidence of lifelong negative outcomes associated with interpersonal violence experienced by autistic people, providing evidence for the relevance of minority stress and intersectionality theories in understanding risk. Indeed, our results raise concerns that autistic people, and particularly non-male (female, gender diverse) individuals, have higher susceptibility for abuse from a young age, while being conditioned to respond with social desirability, superficial adaptivity, and dissociation.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista, tómate en serio cualquier cambio en su ánimo, su sueño o su conducta, y pregúntale con calma si alguien le hace daño. Ofrece formas seguras de contarlo, como hablar, escribir o señalar. Una apariencia tranquila o complaciente no garantiza que esté bien. Es un metaanálisis con 9 estudios y 3,647 participantes autistas de 1 a 80 años, más una síntesis de 57 estudios. La violencia se asoció con peor salud mental, sobre todo síntomas internalizados. Son asociaciones, no prueban causa, y no describen a cada persona.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person, take any change in their mood, sleep or behaviour seriously, and calmly ask whether anyone is hurting them. Offer safe ways to tell you, such as talking, writing or pointing. Looking calm or compliant does not mean they are fine. This is a meta-analysis of 9 studies with 3,647 autistic participants aged 1 to 80 years, plus a synthesis of 57 studies. Violence was linked with worse mental health, most strongly internalizing symptoms. These are associations, not proof of cause, and they do not describe every person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person: ta alla förändringar i humör, sömn eller beteende på allvar och fråga lugnt om någon gör hen illa. Erbjud trygga sätt att berätta, som att prata, skriva eller peka. Att hen verkar lugn eller medgörlig betyder inte att allt är bra. Det här är en metaanalys av 9 studier med 3,647 autistiska deltagare i åldrarna 1 till 80 år, plus en sammanställning av 57 studier. Våld hängde ihop med sämre psykisk hälsa, starkast för internaliserade symtom. Det är samband, inte bevis på orsak, och gäller inte alla individer.

title: Electrodermal Activity, Behavior, and Context in Autistic People with High Support Needs: A Retrospective Ecological Study.
authors: Baquerizo-Sedano M, Lancho Pedrazo M, Merino Martínez M, Taype-Rondan Á, Cuesta Gómez JL, Sáiz-Manzanares MC
abstract: Background/Objectives : Wearable biometric sensors may help characterize autonomic arousal in everyday settings among autistic people with high support needs, a population underrepresented in naturalistic research. This study aimed to describe patterns of autonomic arousal measured using electrodermal activity (EDA) and to explore their relationship with behavioral and contextual records compatible with distress or maladaptive stress. Methods : We retrospectively analyzed routine-care data from 57 autistic people with high support needs attending two specialized services. EDA was recorded for up to 10 days and integrated with behavioral and contextual records collected through a mobile application and stored in ABmonitor. Phase 1 retrospectively analyzed these data using principles derived from Ecological Momentary Assessment. Phase 2 descriptively compared pre- and post-adjustment EDAmax values in five cases with documented contextual adjustments, drawing on principles of Ecological Momentary Intervention, without causal inference. Results : In Phase 1, 19.3% of participants remained within the same arousal category across days, whereas 80.7% showed variable levels. Overall, 22 of 57 participants (38.6%) showed high autonomic arousal on at least one day; among them, 12 had behavioral records compatible with distress, and 5 had a specific contextual factor documented. In Phase 2, descriptive reductions in EDAmax ranging from 4 to 23 µS were observed after contextual adjustments. Conclusions : EDA provides relevant information about autonomic arousal but should not be interpreted as a direct marker of stress. Multimodal ecological monitoring may help generate person-centered clinical hypotheses and inform individualized support in real-world settings.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista con grandes necesidades de apoyo se altera, conviene anotar qué ocurría alrededor (lugar, ruido, rutina, personas) y no atribuirlo solo a la persona. Un sensor de la piel puede aportar una pista, pero no dice por sí solo si hay estrés. Este estudio retrospectivo analizó datos de rutina de 57 personas autistas con grandes necesidades de apoyo en dos servicios; la actividad electrodérmica se registró hasta 10 días junto con registros de conducta y contexto. El nivel de activación varió entre días en 80,7% de los participantes. En cinco casos, tras ajustes del entorno, se observaron descensos descriptivos, sin poder afirmar que fueran la causa. Los resultados no valen como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: When an autistic person with high support needs seems distressed, it helps to note what was happening around them (place, noise, routine, people) rather than attributing it only to the person. A skin sensor can offer a clue, but it cannot tell on its own whether someone is stressed. This retrospective study analysed routine-care data from 57 autistic people with high support needs at two services; electrodermal activity was recorded for up to 10 days alongside behaviour and context records. Arousal levels varied across days in 80.7% of participants. In five cases, descriptive decreases were seen after environmental adjustments, but the study cannot show they caused them. Findings are not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: När en autistisk person med stora stödbehov verkar må dåligt hjälper det att notera vad som hände runt omkring (plats, ljud, rutin, människor) i stället för att bara söka orsaken hos personen. En hudsensor kan ge en ledtråd, men säger inte ensam om någon är stressad. Denna retrospektiva studie analyserade rutinvårdsdata från 57 autistiska personer med stora stödbehov vid två verksamheter; elektrodermal aktivitet registrerades i upp till 10 dagar tillsammans med beteende- och kontextanteckningar. Nivån av kroppslig upphetsning varierade mellan dagar hos 80,7 % av deltagarna. I fem fall sågs beskrivande minskningar efter miljöanpassningar, men studien kan inte visa att de orsakade dem. Resultaten är ingen regel för alla.

title: Immune and Autoimmune Mechanisms in Autism Spectrum Disorder: Linking Molecular Pathways to Neuropsychological Trajectories Across the Lifespan.
authors: Viterbo RG, Tritto R, Sardella D, Iaffaldano P, De Giacomo A
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition with wide differences in cognitive, behavioral, and adaptive outcomes across the lifespan. Current evidence suggests that part of this heterogeneity may be related to interactions among genetic susceptibility, environmental exposures, and immune processes acting during important periods of brain development. This narrative review examines the molecular and cellular mechanisms through which immune dysregulation and autoimmunity may contribute to neurodevelopmental variability in ASD. It also explores possible links with age-related neuropsychological trajectories. Main topics include maternal immune activation, maternal brain-reactive autoantibodies, cytokine signaling, peripheral immune cell changes, microglial and astrocytic function, complement-mediated synaptic remodeling, and gut-immune-brain pathways. These mechanisms are discussed in relation to language, attention, executive functions, sensory processing, social cognition, emotional regulation, adaptive functioning, and psychiatric comorbidity from childhood to adulthood. Current evidence supports immune dysfunction as a possible modifier of ASD phenotypes rather than a universal or isolated cause. Direct longitudinal evidence linking specific immune profiles to defined neuropsychological trajectories is still limited, especially in adults. Integrating molecular, immunological, and neuropsychological data may help identify biologically meaningful ASD subgroups and support future biomarker development, developmental stratification, and more personalized therapeutic approaches.

sheet.es: Esto no cambia nada que debas hacer mañana por la mañana: no indica ninguna acción para casa. Si te preocupa la salud general o inmunitaria de una persona autista, coméntalo con su profesional sanitario. Es una revisión narrativa que reúne investigación sobre cómo los procesos inmunitarios podrían relacionarse con la variedad de perfiles autistas a lo largo de la vida. Sus límites: considera la disfunción inmunitaria un posible modificador, no una causa universal ni única, y la evidencia que sigue a las personas en el tiempo es todavía limitada, sobre todo en adultos.
sheet.en: This doesn't change anything you need to do tomorrow morning: it points to no action at home. If you have concerns about an autistic person's general or immune health, raise them with their health professional. It is a narrative review gathering research on how immune processes might relate to the wide variety of autistic profiles across life. Its limits: it treats immune dysfunction as a possible modifier, not a universal or sole cause, and evidence following people over time is still limited, especially in adults.
sheet.sv: Detta ändrar inget du behöver göra i morgon bitti: den pekar inte på någon åtgärd hemma. Om du oroar dig för en autistisk persons allmänna hälsa eller immunförsvar, ta upp det med personens vårdgivare. Det är en narrativ översikt som samlar forskning om hur immunprocesser kan hänga ihop med den stora variationen av autistiska profiler genom livet. Begränsningar: den ser immunstörning som en möjlig modifierande faktor, inte en universell eller enda orsak, och evidens som följer människor över tid är fortfarande begränsad, särskilt hos vuxna.

title: Care pathways, service access, and psychosociaasl support needs in children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder: a narrative review.
authors: Han X, Weng L, Xu H
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition that often requires long-term support across healthcare, education, and social care systems. Despite increasing recognition, many children and adolescents continue to experience delayed identification, fragmented care pathways, and unequal access to services. This narrative review synthesizes recent evidence on care pathways, service access, and psychosocial support needs in children and adolescents with ASD, drawing on literature published from 2020 onward, with emphasis on recognition, barriers to diagnosis and post-diagnostic support, service access, family burden, school participation, and transition-related needs. Recent evidence indicates that ASD-related care remains uneven across regions and systems. Delays in referral and assessment, workforce shortages, long waiting times, socioeconomic and geographic disparities, and poor coordination across healthcare, education, and social care remain major barriers to timely support. These structural constraints increase caregiver burden, complicate school participation, and weaken continuity of care during adolescence and transition to adulthood. Families frequently report difficulties navigating complex systems, while schools function as both a major site of support and a major source of unmet need. Improving outcomes requires earlier recognition, more equitable access to multidisciplinary services, stronger family and school support, and better coordination across healthcare, education, and social care sectors. A developmental and systems-oriented approach is likely to better address the changing needs of children and adolescents with ASD.

sheet.es: Si buscas apoyo para tu hijo o hija autista, anota en un solo lugar las citas, los contactos y lo que cada servicio (salud, escuela, servicios sociales) ha dicho, y pide que se comuniquen entre sí. Es una revisión narrativa de estudios publicados desde 2020 sobre niños y adolescentes autistas y sus familias. Describe esperas largas, falta de profesionales y mala coordinación entre sistemas, que aumentan la carga de las familias. Es una revisión general: no mide qué estrategia concreta funciona y la situación varía según la región y cada familia.
sheet.en: If you are seeking support for your autistic child or teen, keep appointments, contacts and what each service (health, school, social care) has said in one place, and ask them to communicate with each other. This is a narrative review of studies published from 2020 onward about autistic children and adolescents and their families. It describes long waits, workforce shortages and poor coordination between systems, which add to family burden. It is a broad overview: it does not test which specific strategy works, and experiences vary by region and by family.
sheet.sv: Om du söker stöd för ditt autistiska barn eller din tonåring: samla tider, kontakter och vad varje verksamhet (vård, skola, socialtjänst) har sagt på ett ställe, och be dem samarbeta med varandra. Detta är en narrativ översikt av studier publicerade från 2020 och framåt om autistiska barn och ungdomar och deras familjer. Den beskriver långa väntetider, brist på personal och dålig samordning mellan system, vilket ökar familjers belastning. Det är en bred översikt: den testar inte vilken enskild strategi som fungerar, och erfarenheterna varierar mellan regioner och familjer.

title: Special Interests in Autism: Functions, Benefits, and Challenges.
authors: Bayer M, Dziobek I
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Special interests are a highly prevalent feature of autism spectrum conditions (ASC) and have long been described primarily from a deficit-oriented perspective. More recent work has pointed to their potential as psychological resources, yet systematic evidence and direct comparisons with non-autistic groups remain limited. The present study examined the significance of special interests for well-being, self-related aspects and emotion regulation in autistic adults, as well as negative consequences and stigma. Furthermore, we directly compared the likelihood of engaging in special interests versus seeking social contact across a range of emotional contexts. A total of 182 participants (60 autistic and 122 non-autistic) completed an online survey on multiple aspects of their (special) interests and measures of social anxiety and self-esteem. Autistic individuals reported a stronger role of special interests in emotion regulation and as a source of learning and knowledge, while also experiencing greater stigma and negative consequences compared with non-autistic participants. Autistic participants further showed a higher likelihood of relying on their interests as a coping strategy in negative and exhausting situations, highlighting their particular relevance for emotion regulation. Our findings emphasize the unique functions of special interests in autism and point to their therapeutic potential as adaptive resources.Lay AbstractMany autistic people have special interests - topics or activities they pursue with great passion. We asked autistic and non-autistic adults how meaningful their interests are and how they use them in different emotional situations. Autistic people reported that interests are especially helpful for coping with stress and regulating emotions, and that they are an important source of learning and knowledge. On the other hand, autistic individuals also experienced more stigma and negative reactions from others than non-autistic individuals. Our findings show that special interests are an important source of well-being and should be recognized as a valuable resource in autism.

sheet.es: Tras un día agotador, deja que la persona autista dedique tiempo a su interés especial sin prisas ni críticas: puede ser su forma de calmarse y recuperarse. Es una encuesta en línea con 182 participantes (60 autistas y 122 no autistas). Las personas autistas contaron que usan sus intereses más para regular las emociones y aprender, y también que sufren más estigma y consecuencias negativas. Es un solo estudio con autoinformes de adultos, así que no describe a todas las personas autistas ni a los niños, y no prueba causa y efecto.
sheet.en: After an exhausting day, let the autistic person spend time on their special interest without hurrying or criticising: it may be how they calm down and recover. This was an online survey of 182 participants (60 autistic and 122 non-autistic). Autistic people reported using their interests more for emotion regulation and learning, and also reported more stigma and negative consequences. It is a single study based on adults' self-reports, so it does not describe every autistic person or any children, and it cannot show cause and effect.
sheet.sv: Efter en slitsam dag kan du låta den autistiska personen ägna tid åt sitt specialintresse utan stress eller kritik: det kan vara sättet att varva ner och återhämta sig. Studien var en webbenkät med 182 deltagare (60 autistiska och 122 icke-autistiska). Autistiska personer berättade att de använder sina intressen mer för att reglera känslor och för att lära sig, och att de också möter mer stigma och negativa följder. Det är en enskild studie baserad på vuxnas egna svar, så den beskriver inte alla autistiska personer eller barn och visar inte orsak och verkan.

title: Common and Differing Elements Across Caregiver-Mediated Social Communication Programs Supporting Autistic Children: A Scoping Review With Content Analysis.
authors: Rajesh Kumar V, Choi L, Oram J, Binns A
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Caregiver-mediated interventions are widely used to support social communication development in young autistic children. While many such interventions are evidence-informed, limited information exists about their shared and unique elements, making it challenging for caregivers and clinicians to tailor program selection to individual needs and preferences-an essential part of personalized care in autism. This scoping review with content analysis examined 18 commercially available, caregiver-mediated social communication interventions to identify similarities and differences in child skills targeted and caregiver-coached strategies. Data were extracted from program manuals, fidelity tools, published literature, and program websites for eight developmental social pragmatic (DSP) programs and 10 naturalistic developmental behavioral interventions (NDBIs). Programs varied in scope, with some supporting a broad range of child skills and others focusing on specific areas. Across all programs, 70 caregiver-coached strategies were identified, and then thematically grouped into eight categories aligned with the developmental skills the strategies aim to support. Although some strategies were common across all programs, some unique strategies were also identified. In addition, there were notable differences in how these strategies were operationalized despite using similar terminology, underscoring the need for more precise, clearly defined fidelity measures to enable accurate assessment of caregiver implementation and meaningful comparisons across programs. This study lays the groundwork for future research to identify active ingredients of interventions and supports more informed, individualized decision-making in clinical practice.Lay AbstractYoung autistic children may engage with others and communicate in ways that differ from non-autistic peers, and may need support to develop skills to communicate with, and navigate interactions with others. Many programs have been developed for this purpose, with a growing number of programs including caregivers in this process. In programs where caregivers play a primary role, professionals coach them to use certain techniques that can support social communication. Although many such programs exist, we still lack clarity on how these programs are similar or different, making it tough for families to choose among them. To address this gap, we reviewed 18 well-known caregiver-led programs to compare the skills they aim to support children with, and the specific techniques they teach caregivers. We gathered information from program resource materials, published research, and official program websites. We found that some programs focused on supporting a wide range of skills, whereas others targeted only certain developmental areas. In total, we identified 70 distinct caregiver-coached techniques, which we organized into eight categories. Many techniques were common across all programs, but others were unique to specific programs. Even among the shared techniques, there were differences in the way they were practiced, despite using the same strategy name. For example, a technique like "following the child's lead" could look quite different depending on the program. These findings show that having descriptions of how techniques should be used is important to understanding and comparing different programs. Overall, these findings provide families with information about program ingredients and can be used to guide clinicians toward programs that match individuals' needs and wants. This work also paves way for future research exploring how these social communication programs work, and evaluating which techniques are most effective for specific groups of children and families.

sheet.es: Si estás pensando en un programa de comunicación social para tu hijo autista en el que las familias aprenden técnicas, pregunta a los profesionales qué habilidades trabaja y cómo se practica cada técnica, por ejemplo «seguir el interés del niño», que puede variar mucho entre programas. Es una revisión de alcance que comparó 18 programas comerciales dirigidos por cuidadores, a partir de manuales, literatura publicada y sitios web. Encontró 70 estrategias agrupadas en ocho categorías, algunas comunes y otras exclusivas. No evalúa qué programa funciona mejor ni para quién, así que sirve para comparar y conversar, no para elegir por sí sola.
sheet.en: If you are considering a social communication program for your autistic child in which caregivers learn techniques, ask the professionals which skills it targets and how each technique is practiced, because a technique like "following the child's lead" can look quite different across programs. This was a scoping review comparing 18 commercially available caregiver-led programs, using manuals, published literature and program websites. It found 70 strategies grouped into eight categories, some shared and some unique. It did not test which program works best or for whom, so it helps you compare and ask questions, not choose on its own.
sheet.sv: Om du överväger ett program för social kommunikation för ditt autistiska barn där vårdnadshavare lär sig tekniker, fråga professionella vilka färdigheter det riktar sig mot och hur varje teknik utförs, eftersom en teknik som "att följa barnets ledning" kan se ganska olika ut mellan program. Detta var en kartläggande översikt som jämförde 18 kommersiellt tillgängliga program ledda av vårdnadshavare, utifrån manualer, publicerad litteratur och webbplatser. Den fann 70 strategier i åtta kategorier, vissa gemensamma och vissa unika. Den testade inte vilket program som fungerar bäst eller för vem, så den hjälper till att jämföra och ställa frågor, inte att välja på egen hand.

title: The Use of the Clinical Global Impressions Scale in Psychosocial Interventions for Autism Characteristics: A Systematic Review.
authors: Glod M, Grahame V, Rodgers J
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: The increase in intervention diversity to improve core difficulties in autism has resulted in the development and proliferation of a variety of measures to assess change. The Clinical Global Impressions (CGI) scale has been recommended for use in pharmacological autism clinical trials to monitor individuals' progress. No specific recommendations have been made for an outcome measure for psychosocial interventions. This review aimed to evaluate available evidence of a use of the CGI scale as an outcome measure in psychosocial interventions for autism characteristics. A systematic search of electronic databases identified 22 primary studies utilising the CGI scale to evaluate change across a range of social, communication and behavioural interventions for autistic people. The lack of consistency in the use of the measure was evident. This applied to the variety of constructs being measured, inconsistent application and scoring methods, which all limited the CGI scale's reliability and validity. Despite the widespread use of the CGI scale in psychosocial clinical trials for autistic people, the lack of standardisation hampers conclusions regarding the evidence of its effectiveness in measuring change. Standardisation of the use of the CGI scale is essential to ensure comprehensive evaluation of interventions.Lay AbstractMany different therapies and supports exist to help autistic people with social, communication, and behavioural differences. To understand whether these interventions are working, researchers need good tools to measure change. One commonly used tool in medical studies is the Clinical Global Impressions (CGI) scale, which helps clinicians rate a person's overall improvement. Although the CGI scale is recommended for autism medication studies, there are no clear guidelines for using it in psychosocial (non-medical) interventions. In this review, we looked at research studies that used the CGI scale to measure change after psychosocial interventions for autistic people. We found 22 studies that used the CGI scale in very different ways. The studies measured a wide range of skills and behaviours, and they often used the CGI scale differently from one another. This inconsistency makes it difficult to trust the results or compare findings across studies. Although the CGI scale is widely used, the lack of standard guidelines means it may not reliably show whether psychosocial interventions are effective. To improve research and ensure that interventions are properly evaluated, it is important to develop clear, standardised ways of using the CGI scale.

sheet.es: Si un informe sobre una terapia o apoyo dice que hubo 'mejoría global' según la escala CGI, tómalo con cautela y pregunta qué se midió exactamente y quién lo valoró. Se trata de una revisión sistemática que encontró 22 estudios que usaron la escala CGI para evaluar cambios tras intervenciones sociales, de comunicación y de conducta para personas autistas. Los estudios la usaron de formas muy distintas, midiendo cosas diferentes y puntuando de manera desigual, así que es difícil confiar en los resultados o compararlos. La revisión no dice qué intervenciones funcionan ni si sirven a una persona concreta.
sheet.en: If a report on a therapy or support says there was 'overall improvement' on the CGI scale, treat it with caution and ask what exactly was measured and who rated it. This is a systematic review that found 22 studies using the CGI scale to evaluate change after social, communication and behavioural interventions for autistic people. The studies used it in very different ways, measuring different things and scoring inconsistently, so results are hard to trust or compare. The review does not say which interventions work, or whether any would suit a particular person.
sheet.sv: Om en rapport om en terapi eller ett stöd säger att det skett en 'övergripande förbättring' enligt CGI-skalan, ta det med försiktighet och fråga vad som mättes och vem som bedömde. Det här är en systematisk översikt som hittade 22 studier som använde CGI-skalan för att utvärdera förändring efter sociala interventioner, kommunikationsinterventioner och beteendeinterventioner för autistiska personer. Studierna använde skalan på mycket olika sätt, mätte olika saker och poängsatte olika, så resultaten är svåra att lita på eller jämföra. Översikten visar inte vilka insatser som fungerar eller om någon passar en enskild person.

title: Rapid Review of the Brief Observation of Social Communication Change (BOSCC) Shows It Can Detect Behavioural Changes in Social Communication in Autism.
authors: Howlin C, Kovalova A, Jaschke A, Greenberg DM, Mason B, Pallás-Ferrer I, Merriam E, Brushwood C, Pool J, Allison C, Odell-Miller H, Hayden K, Moore CS, Atkinson R, Wilfred RT, Baron-Cohen S
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Reliable measurement of social communication change remains a major challenge in autism research. The Brief Observation of Social Communication Change (BOSCC) was developed to detect subtle changes in communication. This rapid review synthesised current evidence on the BOSCC's responsiveness, validity, and suitability as a clinical trial endpoint. Systematic searches of PubMed, PsycINFO, CINAHL, and Web of Science identified 19 eligible studies ( n = 789). Within-group meta-analyses estimated pre-post standardised mean change (Hedges' g ) for BOSCC and ADOS (Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule) outcomes, using random-effect (RE) models. The BOSCC total score for intervention arms showed a moderate, significant change ( g = -0.32, 95% confidence interval [CI] = [-0.42, -0.22]), with a smaller, non-significant change in control arms ( g = -0.15). The Social Communication subscale yielded consistent effects on the intervention arm ( g = -0.34, 95% CI = [-0.49, -0.19]), indicating sensitivity to improvements in reciprocal interaction. The restricted and repetitive behaviour (RRB) subscale also showed a moderate significant effect on the intervention arm but with wide confidence intervals indicating a large degree of heterogeneity in this result ( g = -0.40, 95% CI = [-0.74, -0.06]). ADOS scores showed a similar pattern of results for the intervention arms, based on a sub-analysis of four studies that included both BOSCC and ADOS scores. Findings indicate that the BOSCC captures clinically meaningful behavioural change across diverse contexts. Variability in RRB outcomes may arise because they are not routinely targeted by supports for social communication, in line with neuro-affirmative approaches.Lay AbstractAutism research often aims to understand how different supports can help autistic children develop skills that are important to them and their families, such as social communication. However, changes in social communication are very difficult to measure. The Brief Observation of Social Communication Change (BOSCC) was developed to help address this. It focuses on observing natural, everyday interactions to capture subtle shifts in social communication and patterns of behaviour, and restricted and repetitive behaviours. In this review, we gathered and summarised all available studies up to March 2025 that used the BOSCC with autistic children, including both intervention studies and studies examining how well the BOSCC works. Across 19 studies including 789 children, we found that the BOSCC was consistently able to detect changes that occurred during a wide range of supports and programmes. The Social Communication subscale was particularly good at picking up changes, but the scale designed to measure repetitive behaviours was more inconsistent. The lack of changes in repetitive behaviours may reflect the diversity and important self-regulatory roles that repetitive behaviours can have, as well as the fact that many short-term interventions do not focus on changing them. The BOSCC was also found to be better at picking up changes in social communication compared to a diagnostic tool called the Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule (ADOS). Overall, the evidence suggests that the BOSCC, particularly the Social Communication subscale, may be a useful way to detect changes in autistic communication over time. Future work should acknowledge that repetitive behaviours are not routinely targeted by supports intended to enhance communication and may serve a self-regulatory function, to manage sensory input, or to express emotions. This will help ensure that the BOSCC is used in a way that aligns with neurodiversity-affirming principles and supports ethically grounded research.

sheet.es: Si un profesional o un programa usa la BOSCC, puede preguntar qué cambios en la comunicación social observa y cómo se tienen en cuenta las conductas repetitivas, que pueden ayudar a regular los sentidos o expresar emociones. Es una revisión rápida con metaanálisis de 19 estudios con 789 niños autistas. La BOSCC detectó cambios durante distintos apoyos, sobre todo en la subescala de comunicación social; la de conductas repetitivas fue más irregular. Límites: mide grupos, no predice a una persona concreta, y no demuestra qué apoyo es mejor ni que el cambio sea siempre deseable.
sheet.en: If a professional or programme uses the BOSCC, you can ask what changes in social communication it is picking up, and how repetitive behaviours are treated, since they may help with sensory regulation or expressing emotions. This was a rapid review with meta-analysis of 19 studies including 789 autistic children. The BOSCC detected change during a wide range of supports, especially on its Social Communication subscale; the repetitive behaviour subscale was less consistent. Limits: it describes group results, cannot predict any one person, and does not show which support is best or that every change is wanted.
sheet.sv: Om en yrkesperson eller ett program använder BOSCC kan du fråga vilka förändringar i social kommunikation den fångar upp och hur repetitiva beteenden hanteras, eftersom de kan hjälpa till med sensorisk reglering eller att uttrycka känslor. Det här var en snabböversikt med metaanalys av 19 studier med 789 autistiska barn. BOSCC upptäckte förändring under många olika stöd, särskilt i delskalan för social kommunikation; delskalan för repetitiva beteenden var mindre konsekvent. Begränsningar: resultaten gäller grupper, förutsäger inte en enskild person och visar inte vilket stöd som är bäst eller att varje förändring är önskvärd.

title: Integrating Gut-Brain Axis: Exploring the Neurogastrointestinal Interactions and Therapeutic Potentials in Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Kumar M, Mehan S, Sharma T, Kumar A, Khan Z, Sharma AK, Gupta GD, Kumar N
journal: Endocrine, metabolic & immune disorders drug targets
abstract: This comprehensive review critically examines the gut-brain axis (GBA) and its implications in autism spectrum disorder (ASD). The GBA is a complex, bidirectional communication network that integrates the gastrointestinal tract, the central nervous system, and the gut microbiota. This axis is mediated through various physiological pathways, including the enteric nervous system (ENS), the vagus nerve, immune responses, and metabolic activities of gut microorganisms. ASD, a developmental disorder marked by social impairments and repetitive behaviors, presents with notable neurological irregularities. The review highlights the increased prevalence of gastrointestinal (GI) disturbances in individuals with ASD, suggesting a potential link between GI symptoms and the severity of ASD-related behaviors. This correlation is supported by evidence of altered gut microbiota composition in ASD, indicating significant interactions between the gut environment and neurological health. Moreover, the pathophysiology of ASD is explored with an emphasis on genetic and environmental contributions to neurodevelopmental impairments. Key topics include synaptic dysfunction, the roles of neurotransmitters like GABA and serotonin, and the impact of gut-brain interactions on ASD progression. Specifically, this review addresses how gut microbiota may influence metabolic alterations, immune dysregulation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial function, and neurotransmitter production in ASD. Emerging research on microbiome-based therapies for ASD is discussed, focusing on the potential of probiotics, prebiotics, and faecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) as novel interventions. Ethical considerations in this burgeoning field are also considered, highlighting the necessity for rigorous scientific inquiry and ethical oversight. The review advocates for a multidisciplinary approach to understanding and addressing the complexities of ASD. By integrating insights from genetics, neuroscience, psychology, and gastroenterology, a more comprehensive understanding of the role of GBA in ASD can be achieved. This interdisciplinary perspective is crucial for developing effective, individualized treatments and improving the quality of life for individuals with ASD.

title: Different effects of social cognitive skills training in schizophrenia and autism spectrum disorder: A rater-blinded, multicenter, randomized controlled trial.
authors: Otsuka S, Oe S, Yamada S, Kumoi H, Suwabe R, Iwane T, Tsurumi K, Murai T
abstract: Aim Schizophrenia (SCZ) and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) are both characterized by social cognitive impairments that strongly predict poor functional outcomes. However, evidence-based social cognitive interventions have been developed only for SCZ. This study investigated the feasibility and efficacy of social cognitive skills training (SCST), focusing on both common and different effects on SCZ and ASD. Methods Forty-seven adults with SCZ and/or ASD were randomly assigned to SCST (n = 24) or a treatment-as-usual control (CON; n = 23). The Japanese version of SCST developed for this study comprised weekly 2-h group sessions over 6 weeks and targeted two social cognition levels: lower-level emotional processing and higher-level theory of mind. Blinded raters assessed social cognition, neurocognition, clinical symptoms, and functioning at baseline, post-intervention, and 6-week follow-up. Results SCST significantly improved facial emotion perception across diagnoses and demonstrated a trend-level ASD-specific improvement in theory of mind. These effects were maintained and generalized to improved global functioning only for ASD at follow-up. High attendance and positive participant feedback in both groups indicated the intervention's feasibility. Conclusion This study provides initial evidence supporting the feasibility and efficacy of social cognitive interventions as a transdiagnostic approach for SCZ and ASD and is the first to show functional benefits in adults with ASD. The findings highlight both shared and disorder-specific mechanisms of social cognitive impairments and support the development of hybrid interventions that integrate transdiagnostic core components with tailored, diagnosis-sensitive modules for diverse psychiatric populations. Clinical trial registration The study protocol was preregistered on the University Hospital Medical Information Network Clinical Trials Registry (UMIN000041619; https://center6.umin.ac.jp/cgi-open-bin/ctr/ctr_view.cgi?recptno=R000047105; September 7, 2020).

sheet.es: Si valoráis un grupo de entrenamiento en habilidades sociales, este estudio sugiere que un programa estructurado de reconocimiento de emociones y comprensión de lo que piensan otras personas puede ser útil para algunas personas adultas autistas. Conviene preguntar qué se trabaja y si encaja con lo que la persona desea. Evidencia: ensayo aleatorizado con evaluadores ciegos, con 47 personas adultas con esquizofrenia y/o autismo, en sesiones grupales semanales de 2 horas durante 6 semanas. Mejoró la percepción de emociones faciales y, solo en autismo, el funcionamiento global en el seguimiento. Límites: muestra pequeña, resultados de teoría de la mente solo en tendencia, y no sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you are considering a social skills group, this study suggests a structured programme on recognising emotions and understanding what other people think may help some autistic adults. It is worth asking what is taught and whether it fits what the person wants. Evidence: a randomised trial with blinded raters, including 47 adults with schizophrenia and/or autism, in weekly 2-hour group sessions over 6 weeks. Recognising facial emotions improved, and global functioning improved at follow-up only in autism. Limits: small sample, theory of mind results were only a trend, and the findings are not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om ni överväger en social färdighetsgrupp tyder den här studien på att ett strukturerat program om att känna igen känslor och förstå vad andra tänker kan hjälpa en del autistiska vuxna. Fråga vad som tränas och om det passar det personen själv vill. Evidens: en randomiserad studie med blindade bedömare och 47 vuxna med schizofreni och/eller autism, med veckovisa gruppträffar på 2 timmar under 6 veckor. Igenkänning av ansiktsuttryck förbättrades, och globalt fungerande förbättrades vid uppföljningen endast vid autism. Begränsningar: litet urval, resultaten för theory of mind var bara en tendens, och fynden gäller inte alla personer.

title: Targeting the mTOR Pathway with Natural Products: A Potential Therapeutic Approach for Autism Spectrum Disorders.
authors: Noori T, Hosseini SZ, Alavi SD, Sureda A, Shirooie S
abstract: Autism spectrum disorders (ASD) are complex neurodevelopmental conditions characterized by a diverse range of challenges and strengths in social communication, behavior, and sensory processing, with wide variation in presentation and severity among individuals. Treatment for ASD symptoms typically includes stimulants, modafinil, atomoxetine, antidepressants, antipsychotics, and natural products. The mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR), a serine/threonine kinase, is dysregulated in many human diseases, leading to abnormal synapse formation, neuroinflammation, and mitochondrial dysfunction. Natural products, due to their wide range of bioactive compounds and relatively low toxicity, have emerged as promising modulators of this pathway. Several phytochemicals-including curcumin, resveratrol, and epigallocatechin gallate-have demonstrated the ability to modulate mTOR signaling and improve neurobehavioral outcomes in preclinical models of ASD. mTORC1 and mTORC2 are key regulators of cellular processes, with mTORC1 being largely sensitive to nutrient availability and mTORC2 playing a crucial role in cell growth, proliferation, motility, and autophagy, which is modulated by the PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway. Future research should examine the relationship between autism and the mTOR signaling pathway, as well as the phytochemicals that may contribute to improving the condition through this pathway.

sheet.es: Por ahora, esta revisión no cambia nada práctico para mañana por la mañana. Trata de sustancias naturales y de una vía celular llamada mTOR, y las decisiones médicas, incluidos suplementos o tratamientos, corresponden a un profesional clínico. Es una revisión de la literatura que resume sobre todo estudios preclínicos en modelos de autismo, no personas. Sus límites: no prueba que ningún producto ayude a personas autistas, y el autismo es muy diverso, así que no sirve como regla general. Los propios autores piden más investigación.
sheet.en: For now, this review changes nothing practical for tomorrow morning. It looks at natural substances and a cell pathway called mTOR, and medical decisions, including supplements or treatments, belong to a clinician. It is a review of the literature, mostly summarising preclinical studies in models of autism rather than people. Its limits: it does not show that any product helps autistic people, and autism is very diverse, so it is not a rule for everyone. The authors themselves call for more research.
sheet.sv: Just nu ändrar den här översikten inget praktiskt för i morgon bitti. Den handlar om naturliga ämnen och en cellväg som kallas mTOR, och medicinska beslut, även om kosttillskott eller behandlingar, hör till en kliniker. Det är en litteraturöversikt som mest sammanfattar prekliniska studier i modeller av autism, inte människor. Begränsningar: den visar inte att någon produkt hjälper autistiska personer, och autism är mycket varierande, så den är ingen regel för alla. Författarna efterlyser själva mer forskning.

title: Shared heritability of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder and autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Rommelse NN, Franke B, Geurts HM, Hartman CA, Buitelaar JK
abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) are both highly heritable neurodevelopmental disorders. Evidence indicates both disorders co-occur with a high frequency, in 20-50% of children with ADHD meeting criteria for ASD and in 30-80% of ASD children meeting criteria for ADHD. This review will provide an overview on all available studies [family based, twin, candidate gene, linkage, and genome wide association (GWA) studies] shedding light on the role of shared genetic underpinnings of ADHD and ASD. It is concluded that family and twin studies do provide support for the hypothesis that ADHD and ASD originate from partly similar familial/genetic factors. Only a few candidate gene studies, linkage studies and GWA studies have specifically addressed this co-occurrence, pinpointing to some promising pleiotropic genes, loci and single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), but the research field is in urgent need for better designed and powered studies to tackle this complex issue. We propose that future studies examining shared familial etiological factors for ADHD and ASD use a family-based design in which the same phenotypic (ADHD and ASD), candidate endophenotypic, and environmental measurements are obtained from all family members. Multivariate multi-level models are probably best suited for the statistical analysis.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista muestra también rasgos de TDAH, o al revés, no es algo raro: conviene observar ambas facetas y buscar apoyos que atiendan las dos. Esta revisión recoge estudios familiares, de gemelos y genéticos. Indica que el TDAH y el autismo comparten en parte factores familiares y genéticos, y que ambos aparecen juntos con frecuencia. Sus límites: pocos estudios genéticos analizaron esa coincidencia, los autores piden estudios mejor diseñados y no sirve para saber qué ocurre en una familia o persona concreta.
sheet.en: If an autistic person also shows ADHD traits, or the other way round, that is not unusual: it helps to look at both and seek supports that cover both. This review gathered family, twin and genetic studies. It reports that ADHD and autism partly share familial and genetic factors, and that the two often appear together. Its limits: few genetic studies looked at this overlap, the authors call for better designed studies, and it cannot tell you what is true for one particular family or person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person också har ADHD-drag, eller tvärtom, är det inte ovanligt: det hjälper att se båda delar och söka stöd som täcker båda. Den här översikten samlar familje-, tvillings- och genetiska studier. Den visar att ADHD och autism delvis delar familjära och genetiska faktorer och att de ofta förekommer tillsammans. Begränsningar: få genetiska studier har undersökt överlappningen, författarna efterlyser bättre upplagda studier, och översikten kan inte säga vad som gäller för en enskild familj eller person.

title: Parent-mediated communication-focused treatment in children with autism (PACT): a randomised controlled trial.
authors: Green J, Charman T, McConachie H, Aldred C, Slonims V, Howlin P, Le Couteur A, Leadbitter K, Hudry K, Byford S, Barrett B, Temple K, Macdonald W, Pickles A, PACT Consortium

title: A randomized controlled study of parent-assisted Children's Friendship Training with children having autism spectrum disorders.
authors: Frankel F, Myatt R, Sugar C, Whitham C, Gorospe CM, Laugeson E
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: This study evaluated Children's Friendship Training (CFT), a manualized parent-assisted intervention to improve social skills among second to fifth grade children with autism spectrum disorders. Comparison was made with a delayed treatment control group (DTC). Targeted skills included conversational skills, peer entry skills, developing friendship networks, good sportsmanship, good host behavior during play dates, and handling teasing. At post-testing, the CFT group was superior to the DTC group on parent measures of social skill and play date behavior, and child measures of popularity and loneliness, At 3-month follow-up, parent measures showed significant improvement from baseline. Post-hoc analysis indicated more than 87% of children receiving CFT showed reliable change on at least one measure at post-test and 66.7% after 3 months follow-up.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija autista quiere tener amistades, un programa estructurado que implique a la familia puede ofrecer práctica concreta: cómo conversar, unirse a un juego, ser buen anfitrión en una quedada y responder a las burlas. Es un ensayo controlado aleatorizado con niños autistas de segundo a quinto grado, comparado con un grupo en lista de espera. Tras el programa, las familias vieron más habilidades sociales y mejor conducta en las quedadas, y los niños refirieron más popularidad y menos soledad. El estudio no demuestra que sirva a todas las personas, y las mejoras se midieron sobre todo con informes de los padres.
sheet.en: If your autistic child wants friendships, a structured programme that involves the family can give concrete practice: how to hold a conversation, join a game, host a play date well and handle teasing. This was a randomized controlled trial with autistic children in second to fifth grade, compared with a delayed treatment group. Afterwards, parents reported better social skills and play date behaviour, and children reported more popularity and less loneliness. The study does not show it suits every person, and much of the improvement was measured through parent reports.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn vill ha vänner kan ett strukturerat program där familjen deltar ge konkret övning: att samtala, gå med i en lek, vara en bra värd vid lekträffar och hantera retningar. Det var en randomiserad kontrollerad studie med autistiska barn i årskurs två till fem, jämförd med en grupp som fick vänta på behandling. Efteråt rapporterade föräldrar bättre social förmåga och beteende vid lekträffar, och barnen rapporterade mer popularitet och mindre ensamhet. Studien visar inte att det passar alla, och förbättringarna mättes till stor del genom föräldrarnas skattningar.

title: Autism from a biometric perspective.
authors: Kostyuk N, Rajnarayanan RV, Isokpehi RD, Cohly HH
journal: International journal of environmental research and public health
abstract: Purpose The aim of this pilot study was to test autistic children, siblings and their parents using a biometric device based on the gas discharge visualization (GDV) technique in order to assess their psycho-emotional and physiological functional state based on the activity of the autonomic nervous system. Hypothesis We hypothesize that the biometric assessment based on GDV will enable us: (1) to evaluate some specific features associated with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) as well as to compare autistic children to their siblings and to controls; (2) to analyze the differences in individual values of parents of autistic children versus parents of normal children. Results Out of total of 48 acupuncture points present on ten fingertips of both hands and associated to organs/organ systems, autistic children differed significantly from controls (p Conclusions All compared groups have shown significant difference on both psycho-emotional (images without filter) and physiological (images with filter) levels. However, the differences between autistic children and controls expressed on psycho-emotional level were the most significant as compared to the other groups. Therefore, the activity of the sympathetic autonomic nervous system is significantly altered in children with autism. The biometric method based on GDV is a promising step in autism research that may lead towards creating a disease profile and identify unique signature/biomarker for autism. Further work should involve more participants in order to augment our findings.

sheet.es: Este estudio no ofrece nada que cambiar mañana por la mañana en casa: no es una herramienta para evaluar ni orientar a una persona concreta. Se trata de un estudio piloto en el que se midió con un dispositivo de visualización de descarga de gas (GDV) a niños autistas, sus hermanos, sus padres y grupos de control, para estudiar la actividad del sistema nervioso autónomo. Los grupos mostraron diferencias, sobre todo entre niños autistas y controles. Sus límites: fue pequeño, el método es experimental y los propios autores piden más participantes. Describe diferencias de grupo, no sirve para diagnosticar ni vale para todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: This study offers nothing to change at home tomorrow morning: it is not a tool for assessing or guiding any one person. It was a pilot study that used a gas discharge visualization (GDV) device to measure autistic children, their siblings, their parents and control groups, looking at autonomic nervous system activity. The groups differed, most clearly autistic children versus controls. Its limits: it was small, the method is experimental, and the authors themselves call for more participants. It describes group differences, cannot be used to diagnose, and does not apply to every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Den här studien ger inget att ändra hemma i morgon bitti: den är inget verktyg för att bedöma eller vägleda en enskild person. Det var en pilotstudie där en enhet för gasurladdningsvisualisering (GDV) mätte autistiska barn, deras syskon, deras föräldrar och kontrollgrupper, för att se aktiviteten i det autonoma nervsystemet. Grupperna skilde sig åt, tydligast autistiska barn jämfört med kontroller. Begränsningar: studien var liten, metoden är experimentell och forskarna efterlyser själva fler deltagare. Den beskriver gruppskillnader, kan inte användas för diagnos och gäller inte alla autistiska personer.

title: Randomized controlled caregiver mediated joint engagement intervention for toddlers with autism.
authors: Kasari C, Gulsrud AC, Wong C, Kwon S, Locke J
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: This study aimed to determine if a joint attention intervention would result in greater joint engagement between caregivers and toddlers with autism. The intervention consisted of 24 caregiver-mediated sessions with follow-up 1 year later. Compared to caregivers and toddlers randomized to the waitlist control group the immediate treatment (IT) group made significant improvements in targeted areas of joint engagement. The IT group demonstrated significant improvements with medium to large effect sizes in their responsiveness to joint attention and their diversity of functional play acts after the intervention with maintenance of these skills 1 year post-intervention. These are among the first randomized controlled data to suggest that short-term parent-mediated interventions can have important effects on core impairments in toddlers with autism. Clinical Trials #: NCT00065910.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a un niño autista pequeño, puede ayudar practicar momentos de atención compartida en el juego, mirando y jugando juntos a lo que le interesa a él o ella. Se trata de un ensayo aleatorizado: familias de niños autistas pequeños recibieron 24 sesiones guiadas para cuidadores, o esperaron en lista. El grupo con intervención inmediata mejoró en responder a la atención conjunta y en la variedad de juego funcional, y lo mantuvo 1 año después. Los límites: el resumen no indica cuántas familias participaron, y los resultados no valen igual para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you care for a young autistic child, it may help to practise shared attention during play, looking at and playing with what interests them together. This was a randomized trial: families of autistic toddlers either received 24 caregiver-mediated sessions or joined a waitlist. The immediate treatment group improved in responding to joint attention and in the variety of functional play, and kept these gains 1 year later. Limits: the abstract does not say how many families took part, and results will not apply equally to every child or family.
sheet.sv: Om du tar hand om ett litet autistiskt barn kan det hjälpa att öva delad uppmärksamhet i leken, genom att tillsammans titta på och leka med det som barnet är intresserat av. Studien var en randomiserad studie: familjer med autistiska småbarn fick antingen 24 sessioner med vårdnadshavare som medverkande eller hamnade på väntelista. Gruppen med omedelbar insats förbättrades i att svara på gemensam uppmärksamhet och i variationen av funktionell lek, och behöll detta 1 år senare. Begränsningar: sammanfattningen anger inte hur många familjer som deltog, och resultaten gäller inte alla barn eller familjer lika.

title: Anxiety disorders and sensory over-responsivity in children with autism spectrum disorders: is there a causal relationship?
authors: Green SA, Ben-Sasson A
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Anxiety disorders and sensory over-responsivity (SOR) are common in children with autism spectrum disorders (ASD), and there is evidence for an association between these two conditions. Currently, it is unclear what causal mechanisms may exist between SOR and anxiety. We propose three possible theories to explain the association between anxiety and SOR: (a) SOR is caused by anxiety; (b) Anxiety is caused by SOR; or (c) SOR and anxiety are causally unrelated but are associated through a common risk factor or diagnostic overlap. In this paper, we examine support for each theory in the existing anxiety, autism, and neuroscience literature, and discuss how each theory informs choice of interventions and implications for future studies.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija autista reacciona con fuerza a ruidos, texturas o luces, y además muestra ansiedad, puede ayudar observar ambas cosas juntas: anota qué estímulos aparecen antes de los momentos de angustia y ofrece opciones como cascos, pausas o un rincón tranquilo. Reducir la carga sensorial y anticipar situaciones nuevas puede aliviar a la vez el malestar sensorial y la preocupación. Se trata de una revisión teórica de estudios previos sobre ansiedad, autismo y neurociencia; no incluyó participantes nuevos. Su límite principal es que no demuestra qué causa qué: solo plantea hipótesis, y cada niño o niña es diferente.
sheet.en: If your autistic child reacts strongly to sounds, textures or lights and also shows anxiety, it may help to watch both together: note which sensations come before moments of distress, and offer options like ear defenders, breaks or a quiet corner. Lowering sensory load and previewing new situations may ease both sensory discomfort and worry at once. This is a theoretical review of earlier research on anxiety, autism and neuroscience; it did not involve new participants. Its main limit is that it does not prove which causes which: it only proposes possible explanations, and every child is different.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn reagerar starkt på ljud, texturer eller ljus och samtidigt visar oro kan det hjälpa att se på båda sakerna tillsammans: notera vilka sinnesintryck som kommer före stunder av stress, och erbjud till exempel hörselkåpor, pauser eller en lugn vrå. Att minska sinnesbelastningen och förbereda nya situationer kan lindra både obehaget och oron. Detta är en teoretisk översikt av tidigare forskning om ångest, autism och neurovetenskap; inga nya deltagare ingick. Den största begränsningen är att den inte visar vad som orsakar vad, utan bara föreslår möjliga förklaringar, och varje barn är olika.

title: Randomized controlled trial of the focus parent training for toddlers with autism: 1-year outcome.
authors: Oosterling I, Visser J, Swinkels S, Rommelse N, Donders R, Woudenberg T, Roos S, van der Gaag RJ, Buitelaar J
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: This randomized controlled trial compared results obtained after 12 months of nonintensive parent training plus care-as-usual and care-as-usual alone. The training focused on stimulating joint attention and language skills and was based on the intervention described by Drew et al. (Eur Child Adolesc Psychiatr 11:266-272, 2002). Seventy-five toddlers with autism spectrum disorder (65 autism, 10 PDD-NOS, mean age = 34.4 months, SD = 6.2) were enrolled. Analyses were conducted on a final sample of 67 children (lost to follow-up = 8). No significant intervention effects were found for any of the primary (language), secondary (global clinical improvement), or mediating (child engagement, early precursors of social communication, or parental skills) outcome variables, suggesting that the 'Focus parent training' was not of additional value to the more general care-as-usual.

sheet.es: Si ya recibís la atención habitual, este estudio no mostró que añadir este curso concreto para madres y padres aportara una mejora extra. Puede ayudar a decidir con calma qué apoyos priorizar, hablando con el equipo profesional. Fue un ensayo controlado aleatorizado con 75 niñas y niños pequeños con autismo; el análisis final incluyó a 67 niños. Tras 12 meses no hubo efectos significativos en lenguaje, mejoría clínica global, implicación del niño, precursores de la comunicación social ni habilidades parentales. Límites: probó un solo programa no intensivo, centrado en atención conjunta y lenguaje, y no dice cómo le irá a cada familia ni si otros enfoques funcionarían.
sheet.en: If your child already receives usual care, this study did not find that adding this particular parent training gave extra benefit. It may help you weigh which supports to prioritise, in conversation with your professional team. It was a randomized controlled trial with 75 autistic toddlers; the final analysis included 67 children. After 12 months there were no significant effects on language, global clinical improvement, child engagement, early precursors of social communication, or parental skills. Limits: it tested one non-intensive programme focused on joint attention and language, and it cannot tell how any single family will fare or whether other approaches would work.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn redan får vanligt stöd visade den här studien inte att just denna föräldrautbildning gav någon extra nytta. Det kan hjälpa dig att fundera på vilka stöd som är viktigast, tillsammans med ditt professionella team. Det var en randomiserad kontrollerad studie med 75 autistiska småbarn; den slutliga analysen omfattade 67 barn. Efter 12 månader sågs inga signifikanta effekter på språk, global klinisk förbättring, barnets engagemang, tidiga föregångare till social kommunikation eller föräldrarnas färdigheter. Begränsningar: studien prövade ett enda icke-intensivt program med fokus på delad uppmärksamhet och språk, och kan inte säga hur det går för en enskild familj eller om andra metoder fungerar.

title: Employment and post-secondary educational activities for young adults with autism spectrum disorders during the transition to adulthood.
authors: Taylor JL, Seltzer MM
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders

claim.es: Tras la escuela, una gran parte de jóvenes autistas queda sin empleo ni formación, sobre todo quienes necesitan más apoyo: la transición a la vida adulta exige planificación.
claim.en: After school, a large share of autistic young adults have no job or training, especially those needing more support: the transition to adulthood needs planning.
claim.sv: Efter skolan saknar en stor andel autistiska unga vuxna arbete eller utbildning, särskilt de med större stödbehov: övergången till vuxenlivet kräver planering.

supports.es: Empezar a planificar la transición años antes de que acabe la escuela.
supports.en: Starting transition planning years before school ends.
supports.sv: Att börja planera övergången flera år innan skolan tar slut.

doesNotSupport.es: Que los resultados estén fijados; los apoyos los cambian.
doesNotSupport.en: That outcomes are fixed; supports change them.
doesNotSupport.sv: Att utfallen är givna; stöd förändrar dem.

title: Effects of cognitive behavioral therapy on daily living skills in children with high-functioning autism and concurrent anxiety disorders.
authors: Drahota A, Wood JJ, Sze KM, Van Dyke M
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: CBT is a promising treatment for children with autism spectrum disorders (ASD) and focuses, in part, on children's independence and self-help skills. In a trial of CBT for anxiety in ASD (Wood et al. in J Child Psychol Psychiatry 50:224-234, 2009), children's daily living skills and related parental intrusiveness were assessed. Forty children with ASD (7-11 years) and their primary caregiver were randomly assigned to an immediate treatment (IT; n = 17) or 3-month waitlist (WL; n = 23) condition. In comparison to WL, IT parents reported increases in children's total and personal daily living skills, and reduced involvement in their children's private daily routines. Reductions correlated with reduced anxiety severity. These results provide preliminary evidence that CBT may yield increased independence and daily living skills among children with ASD.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija autista tiene ansiedad, puede valer la pena preguntar a un profesional por la terapia cognitivo-conductual (TCC) adaptada al autismo, y observar también las rutinas diarias de autocuidado, no solo la ansiedad. Se trata de un ensayo aleatorizado con 40 niños autistas de 7-11 años y su cuidador principal. Quienes recibieron la TCC de inmediato, frente a una lista de espera de 3 meses, informaron más habilidades de la vida diaria y menos participación de los padres en las rutinas privadas del niño. Los autores lo describen como evidencia preliminar, el grupo era pequeño y los datos venían de los padres. No sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If your autistic child has anxiety, it may be worth asking a professional about autism-adapted cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), and noticing daily self-care routines as well as anxiety. This was a randomized trial with 40 autistic children aged 7-11 and their primary caregiver. Compared with a 3-month waitlist, parents of children who got CBT right away reported more daily living skills and less involvement in their child's private routines. The authors call the evidence preliminary, the group was small, and the reports came from parents. It is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn har ångest kan det vara värt att fråga en yrkesperson om autismanpassad kognitiv beteendeterapi (KBT) och att även uppmärksamma vardagliga rutiner för egenvård, inte bara ångesten. Det var en randomiserad studie med 40 autistiska barn i åldern 7-11 år och deras främsta vårdnadshavare. Jämfört med en väntelista på 3 månader rapporterade föräldrar till barn som fick KBT direkt fler vardagsfärdigheter och mindre inblandning i barnets privata rutiner. Författarna kallar bevisen preliminära, gruppen var liten och uppgifterna kom från föräldrarna. Det är ingen regel för alla.
