title: Why are autism spectrum conditions more prevalent in males?
authors: Baron-Cohen S, Lombardo MV, Auyeung B, Ashwin E, Chakrabarti B, Knickmeyer R
abstract: Autism Spectrum Conditions (ASC) are much more common in males, a bias that may offer clues to the etiology of this condition. Although the cause of this bias remains a mystery, we argue that it occurs because ASC is an extreme manifestation of the male brain. The extreme male brain (EMB) theory, first proposed in 1997, is an extension of the Empathizing-Systemizing (E-S) theory of typical sex differences that proposes that females on average have a stronger drive to empathize while males on average have a stronger drive to systemize. In this first major update since 2005, we describe some of the evidence relating to the EMB theory of ASC and consider how typical sex differences in brain structure may be relevant to ASC. One possible biological mechanism to account for the male bias is the effect of fetal testosterone (fT). We also consider alternative biological theories, the X and Y chromosome theories, and the reduced autosomal penetrance theory. None of these theories has yet been fully confirmed or refuted, though the weight of evidence in favor of the fT theory is growing from converging sources (longitudinal amniocentesis studies from pregnancy to age 10 years old, current hormone studies, and genetic association studies of SNPs in the sex steroid pathways). Ultimately, as these theories are not mutually exclusive and ASC is multi-factorial, they may help explain the male prevalence of ASC.

sheet.es: Para mañana por la mañana: no hace falta asumir que una persona autista encaja con una teoría sobre el cerebro. Observa sus intereses, su forma de comunicarse y lo que necesita, sin importar su sexo. Esta es una revisión de 2011 que repasa teorías sobre por qué el diagnóstico es más frecuente en varones, como la del cerebro masculino extremo y la de la testosterona fetal. Sus límites: según el texto, ninguna teoría está confirmada ni refutada, y no explica a cada persona. Tampoco indica qué hacer en casa.
sheet.en: For tomorrow morning: there is no need to assume an autistic person fits a theory about the brain. Notice their interests, how they communicate and what they need, whatever their sex. This is a 2011 review of theories about why autism is identified more often in males, including the extreme male brain theory and fetal testosterone. Its limits: the authors say none of the theories is fully confirmed or refuted, and none explains every person. It also gives no guidance for daily life at home.
sheet.sv: Till i morgon bitti: du behöver inte utgå från att en autistisk person passar en teori om hjärnan. Lägg märke till intressen, sätt att kommunicera och behov, oavsett kön. Detta är en översikt från 2011 om teorier kring varför autism upptäcks oftare hos män, bland annat teorin om den extrema manliga hjärnan och fetal testosteron. Begränsningar: författarna skriver att ingen teori är helt bekräftad eller avfärdad, och ingen förklarar varje person. Den ger inte heller råd för vardagen hemma.

title: Theory of Mind training in children with autism: a randomized controlled trial.
authors: Begeer S, Gevers C, Clifford P, Verhoeve M, Kat K, Hoddenbach E, Boer F
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Many children with Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASD) participate in social skills or Theory of Mind (ToM) treatments. However, few studies have shown evidence for their effectiveness. The current study used a randomized controlled design to test the effectiveness of a 16-week ToM treatment in 8-13 year old children with ASD and normal IQs (n = 40). The results showed that, compared to controls, the treated children with ASD improved in their conceptual ToM skills, but their elementary understanding, self reported empathic skills or parent reported social behaviour did not improve. Despite the effects on conceptual understanding, the current study does not indicate strong evidence for the effectiveness of a ToM treatment on the daily life mindreading skills.

sheet.es: Si su hijo participa o va a participar en un programa de teoría de la mente, conviene esperar mejoras en la comprensión conceptual, pero no dar por hecho que cambiará la vida diaria. Observe con calma si le resulta útil y qué apoyos prácticos necesita. Es un ensayo aleatorizado con 40 niños de 8-13 años con TEA y CI normal, que recibieron 16 semanas de tratamiento. Mejoró la comprensión conceptual frente al grupo de control, pero no la comprensión elemental, la empatía autoinformada ni la conducta social según los padres. Es un grupo pequeño y no representa a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If your child takes part in, or is about to start, a Theory of Mind programme, you can expect gains in conceptual understanding, but don't assume daily life will change. Watch calmly whether it helps them and what practical supports they need. This was a randomized controlled trial with 40 children aged 8-13 with ASD and normal IQs, who had a 16-week treatment. Compared with controls, conceptual understanding improved, but elementary understanding, self-reported empathy and parent-reported social behaviour did not. The group was small and does not represent every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn går, eller ska gå, ett program i teory of mind (förståelse för andras tankar) kan du räkna med förbättrad begreppslig förståelse, men anta inte att vardagen förändras. Se lugnt efter om det hjälper och vilket praktiskt stöd barnet behöver. Det var en randomiserad kontrollerad studie med 40 barn i åldern 8-13 med ASD och normal IQ, som fick 16 veckors behandling. Jämfört med kontrollgruppen förbättrades den begreppsliga förståelsen, men inte den elementära förståelsen, självrapporterad empati eller socialt beteende enligt föräldrarna. Gruppen var liten och representerar inte alla autistiska personer.

title: Alterations of GABAergic signaling in autism spectrum disorders.
authors: Pizzarelli R, Cherubini E
abstract: Autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) comprise a heterogeneous group of pathological conditions, mainly of genetic origin, characterized by stereotyped behavior, marked impairment in verbal and nonverbal communication, social skills, and cognition. Interestingly, in a small number of cases, ASDs are associated with single mutations in genes encoding for neuroligin-neurexin families. These are adhesion molecules which, by regulating transsynaptic signaling, contribute to maintain a proper excitatory/inhibitory (E/I) balance at the network level. Furthermore, GABA, the main inhibitory neurotransmitter in adult life, at late embryonic/early postnatal stages has been shown to depolarize and excite targeted cell through an outwardly directed flux of chloride. The depolarizing action of GABA and associated calcium influx regulate a variety of developmental processes from cell migration and differentiation to synapse formation. Here, we summarize recent data concerning the functional role of GABA in building up and refining neuronal circuits early in development and the molecular mechanisms regulating the E/I balance. A dysfunction of the GABAergic signaling early in development leads to a severe E/I unbalance in neuronal circuits, a condition that may account for some of the behavioral deficits observed in ASD patients.

sheet.es: Este estudio no ofrece nada que cambiar mañana por la mañana en casa: es investigación básica sobre el cerebro. Lo útil es saber que la ciencia explora cómo se desarrollan las conexiones cerebrales en las personas autistas, sin que eso indique qué hacer en el día a día. Es una revisión que resume datos recientes sobre la señalización del GABA y el equilibrio entre excitación e inhibición en los circuitos neuronales al inicio del desarrollo. Sus límites: plantea una posible explicación para algunas diferencias, no una regla para todas las personas, y no evalúa ninguna ayuda concreta. Cualquier decisión médica corresponde a un clínico.
sheet.en: This study offers nothing to change at home tomorrow morning: it is basic brain research. What is useful to know is that science is exploring how brain connections develop in autistic people, without telling us what to do day to day. It is a review summarising recent data on GABA signalling and the balance between excitation and inhibition in neuronal circuits early in development. Its limits: it suggests one possible explanation for some differences, not a rule for every person, and it does not test any practical support. Any medical decision belongs to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Den här studien ger inget att ändra hemma i morgon bitti: den är grundforskning om hjärnan. Det användbara är att veta att forskningen undersöker hur hjärnans kopplingar utvecklas hos autistiska personer, utan att säga vad man ska göra i vardagen. Det är en översikt som sammanfattar färska data om GABA-signalering och balansen mellan excitation och inhibition i nervnätverk tidigt i utvecklingen. Begränsningar: den föreslår en möjlig förklaring till vissa skillnader, inte en regel för alla, och prövar inget praktiskt stöd. Medicinska beslut hör till en läkare.

title: Autism: a "critical period" disorder?
authors: LeBlanc JJ, Fagiolini M
abstract: Cortical circuits in the brain are refined by experience during critical periods early in postnatal life. Critical periods are regulated by the balance of excitatory and inhibitory (E/I) neurotransmission in the brain during development. There is now increasing evidence of E/I imbalance in autism, a complex genetic neurodevelopmental disorder diagnosed by abnormal socialization, impaired communication, and repetitive behaviors or restricted interests. The underlying cause is still largely unknown and there is no fully effective treatment or cure. We propose that alteration of the expression and/or timing of critical period circuit refinement in primary sensory brain areas may significantly contribute to autistic phenotypes, including cognitive and behavioral impairments. Dissection of the cellular and molecular mechanisms governing well-established critical periods represents a powerful tool to identify new potential therapeutic targets to restore normal plasticity and function in affected neuronal circuits.

sheet.es: Por ahora, este trabajo no ofrece nada que cambie mañana la rutina en casa: es una hipótesis sobre cómo se desarrolla el cerebro, no una guía de cuidado. Sigue siendo útil observar con calma qué entornos sensoriales le sientan bien a la persona autista y respetarlos. Es una revisión teórica que reúne evidencia previa y propone que cambios en el equilibrio entre señales excitadoras e inhibidoras, y en el momento de ciertos periodos tempranos de refinamiento cerebral, podrían contribuir a rasgos autistas. Sus límites: es una propuesta, no una prueba, no describe a todas las personas autistas y no indica ninguna intervención concreta.
sheet.en: For now, this paper offers nothing that changes tomorrow's routine at home: it is a hypothesis about brain development, not a care guide. It is still useful to calmly notice which sensory environments suit the autistic person and to respect them. It is a theoretical review that gathers earlier evidence and proposes that changes in the balance of excitatory and inhibitory signals, and in the timing of certain early periods of brain refinement, may contribute to autistic traits. Its limits: it is a proposal, not proof, it does not describe every autistic person, and it points to no specific intervention.
sheet.sv: Just nu ger den här artikeln inget som ändrar morgondagens rutiner hemma: det är en hypotes om hjärnans utveckling, inte en vårdguide. Det är ändå bra att lugnt lägga märke till vilka sinnesmiljöer som passar den autistiska personen och respektera dem. Det är en teoretisk översikt som samlar tidigare forskning och föreslår att förändringar i balansen mellan retande och hämmande signaler, och i tidpunkten för vissa tidiga perioder av hjärnans förfining, kan bidra till autistiska drag. Begränsningar: det är ett förslag, inte ett bevis, det beskriver inte alla autistiska personer och pekar inte ut någon konkret insats.

title: Anxiety disorders in children and adolescents with autistic spectrum disorders: a meta-analysis.
authors: van Steensel FJ, Bögels SM, Perrin S
journal: Clinical child and family psychology review
abstract: There is considerable evidence that children and adolescents with autistic spectrum disorders (ASD) are at increased risk of anxiety and anxiety disorders. However, it is less clear which of the specific DSM-IV anxiety disorders occur most in this population. The present study used meta-analytic techniques to help clarify this issue. A systematic review of the literature identified 31 studies involving 2,121 young people (aged <18 years) with ASD, and where the presence of anxiety disorder was assessed using standardized questionnaires or diagnostic interviews. Across studies, 39.6% of young people with ASD had at least one comorbid DSM-IV anxiety disorder, the most frequent being specific phobia (29.8%) followed by OCD (17.4%) and social anxiety disorder (16.6%). Associations were found between the specific anxiety disorders and ASD subtype, age, IQ, and assessment method (questionnaire versus interview). Implications for the identification and treatment of anxiety in young people with ASD are discussed.

sheet.es: Si cuida a una persona autista joven, vale la pena observar con calma señales de ansiedad, como miedos intensos, rituales o evitar situaciones sociales, y hablarlo con su equipo sanitario. Es un metaanálisis de 31 estudios con 2,121 jóvenes autistas menores de 18 años. Encontró que 39.6% tenía al menos un trastorno de ansiedad; los más frecuentes fueron la fobia específica (29.8%), el TOC (17.4%) y la ansiedad social (16.6%). Sus límites: son promedios de estudios distintos, que no describen a cada persona, y los resultados variaron según la edad, el CI y el método de evaluación. Solo un profesional puede valorar la ansiedad.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic young person, it is worth calmly noticing signs of anxiety, such as intense fears, rituals or avoiding social situations, and talking about them with their health team. This is a meta-analysis of 31 studies with 2,121 autistic young people under 18. It found that 39.6% had at least one anxiety disorder; the most common were specific phobia (29.8%), OCD (17.4%) and social anxiety disorder (16.6%). Its limits: these are averages across different studies, not a description of every person, and results varied by age, IQ and assessment method. Only a professional can assess anxiety.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk ung person är det värt att lugnt uppmärksamma tecken på oro, som starka rädslor, ritualer eller att undvika sociala situationer, och ta upp det med vårdteamet. Det här är en metaanalys av 31 studier med 2,121 autistiska unga under 18 år. Den fann att 39.6% hade minst en ångestdiagnos; vanligast var specifik fobi (29.8%), OCD (17.4%) och social ångest (16.6%). Begränsningar: siffrorna är genomsnitt från olika studier och beskriver inte varje person, och resultaten varierade med ålder, IQ och bedömningsmetod. Bara en yrkesperson kan bedöma ångest.

claim.es: Cerca del 40 % de niños y adolescentes autistas tienen al menos un trastorno de ansiedad; la ansiedad es común, no rara.
claim.en: About 40% of autistic children and adolescents have at least one anxiety disorder; anxiety is common, not rare.
claim.sv: Omkring 40 % av autistiska barn och ungdomar har minst ett ångestsyndrom; ångest är vanligt, inte ovanligt.

supports.es: Leer la agitación o el rechazo como posible ansiedad y reducir la incertidumbre.
supports.en: Reading agitation or refusal as possible anxiety and reducing uncertainty.
supports.sv: Att tolka oro eller vägran som möjlig ångest och minska osäkerheten.

doesNotSupport.es: Diagnosticar ansiedad en casa; eso es cosa de profesionales clínicos.
doesNotSupport.en: Diagnosing anxiety at home; that is for clinicians.
doesNotSupport.sv: Att diagnostisera ångest hemma; det är klinikers sak.

title: Autism spectrum disorders and schizophrenia: meta-analysis of the neural correlates of social cognition.
authors: Sugranyes G, Kyriakopoulos M, Corrigall R, Taylor E, Frangou S
abstract: Context Impaired social cognition is a cardinal feature of Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASD) and Schizophrenia (SZ). However, the functional neuroanatomy of social cognition in either disorder remains unclear due to variability in primary literature. Additionally, it is not known whether deficits in ASD and SZ arise from similar or disease-specific disruption of the social cognition network. Objective To identify regions most robustly implicated in social cognition processing in SZ and ASD. Data sources Systematic review of English language articles using MEDLINE (1995-2010) and reference lists. Study selection Studies were required to use fMRI to compare ASD or SZ subjects to a matched healthy control group, provide coordinates in standard stereotactic space, and employ standardized facial emotion recognition (FER) or theory of mind (TOM) paradigms. Data extraction Activation foci from studies meeting inclusion criteria (n = 33) were subjected to a quantitative voxel-based meta-analysis using activation likelihood estimation, and encompassed 146 subjects with ASD, 336 SZ patients and 492 healthy controls. Results Both SZ and ASD showed medial prefrontal hypoactivation, which was more pronounced in ASD, while ventrolateral prefrontal dysfunction was associated mostly with SZ. Amygdala hypoactivation was observed in SZ patients during FER and in ASD during more complex ToM tasks. Both disorders were associated with hypoactivation within the Superior Temporal Sulcus (STS) during ToM tasks, but activation in these regions was increased in ASD during affect processing. Disease-specific differences were noted in somatosensory engagement, which was increased in SZ and decreased in ASD. Reduced thalamic activation was uniquely seen in SZ. Conclusions Reduced frontolimbic and STS engagement emerged as a shared feature of social cognition deficits in SZ and ASD. However, there were disease- and stimulus-specific differences. These findings may aid future studies on SZ and ASD and facilitate the formulation of new hypotheses regarding their pathophysiology.

title: Randomised controlled trial of improvisational music therapy's effectiveness for children with autism spectrum disorders (TIME-A): study protocol.
authors: Geretsegger M, Holck U, Gold C
abstract: Background Previous research has suggested that music therapy may facilitate skills in areas typically affected by autism spectrum disorders such as social interaction and communication. However, generalisability of previous findings has been restricted, as studies were limited in either methodological accuracy or the clinical relevance of their approach. The aim of this study is to determine effects of improvisational music therapy on social communication skills of children with autism spectrum disorders. An additional aim of the study is to examine if variation in dose of treatment (i.e., number of music therapy sessions per week) affects outcome of therapy, and to determine cost-effectiveness. Methods/design Children aged between 4;0 and 6;11 years who are diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder will be randomly assigned to one of three conditions. Parents of all participants will receive three sessions of parent counselling (at 0, 2, and 5 months). In addition, children randomised to the two intervention groups will be offered individual, improvisational music therapy over a period of five months, either one session (low-intensity) or three sessions (high-intensity) per week. Generalised effects of music therapy will be measured using standardised scales completed by blinded assessors (Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule, ADOS) and parents (Social Responsiveness Scale, SRS) before and 2, 5, and 12 months after randomisation. Cost effectiveness will be calculated as man years. A group sequential design with first interim look at N = 235 will ensure both power and efficiency. Discussion Responding to the need for more rigorously designed trials examining the effectiveness of music therapy in autism spectrum disorders, this pragmatic trial sets out to generate findings that will be well generalisable to clinical practice. Addressing the issue of dose variation, this study's results will also provide information on the relevance of session frequency for therapy outcome. Trial registration Current Controlled Trials ISRCTN78923965.

sheet.es: Si valoras la musicoterapia para tu peque autista, este estudio aún no ofrece resultados: describe cómo se va a comprobar si ayuda. Puedes hablar con profesionales sobre qué metas te importan, como la comunicación y la interacción social. La evidencia es un protocolo de ensayo controlado aleatorizado: niños de 4;0 a 6;11 años con diagnóstico de autismo se asignarían al azar a uno de tres grupos, con musicoterapia improvisada una o tres sesiones por semana durante cinco meses, o sin ella. Todas las familias recibirían orientación. Como solo es un plan, no sabemos aún si funciona ni cuántas sesiones convienen, y no sirve como regla para cada niño.
sheet.en: If you are considering music therapy for your autistic child, this paper does not give results yet: it describes how researchers plan to test whether it helps. You can talk with professionals about which goals matter to you, such as communication and social interaction. The evidence is a randomised controlled trial protocol: children aged 4;0 to 6;11 years with an autism diagnosis would be randomly assigned to one of three groups, with improvisational music therapy one or three sessions per week for five months, or without it. All parents would receive counselling. Because it is only a plan, we do not yet know whether it works or how many sessions help, and it is not a rule for every child.
sheet.sv: Om du funderar på musikterapi för ditt autistiska barn ger den här artikeln inga resultat ännu: den beskriver hur forskarna planerar att testa om det hjälper. Du kan prata med yrkespersoner om vilka mål som är viktiga för er, till exempel kommunikation och socialt samspel. Underlaget är ett protokoll för en randomiserad kontrollerad studie: barn i åldern 4;0 till 6;11 år med autismdiagnos skulle slumpas till en av tre grupper, med improvisationsbaserad musikterapi en eller tre gånger i veckan i fem månader, eller utan. Alla föräldrar skulle få rådgivning. Eftersom det bara är en plan vet vi ännu inte om det fungerar eller hur många tillfällen som behövs, och det är ingen regel för varje barn.

title: Mitochondrial dysfunction in autism spectrum disorders: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Rossignol DA, Frye RE
abstract: A comprehensive literature search was performed to collate evidence of mitochondrial dysfunction in autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) with two primary objectives. First, features of mitochondrial dysfunction in the general population of children with ASD were identified. Second, characteristics of mitochondrial dysfunction in children with ASD and concomitant mitochondrial disease (MD) were compared with published literature of two general populations: ASD children without MD, and non-ASD children with MD. The prevalence of MD in the general population of ASD was 5.0% (95% confidence interval 3.2, 6.9%), much higher than found in the general population (≈ 0.01%). The prevalence of abnormal biomarker values of mitochondrial dysfunction was high in ASD, much higher than the prevalence of MD. Variances and mean values of many mitochondrial biomarkers (lactate, pyruvate, carnitine and ubiquinone) were significantly different between ASD and controls. Some markers correlated with ASD severity. Neuroimaging, in vitro and post-mortem brain studies were consistent with an elevated prevalence of mitochondrial dysfunction in ASD. Taken together, these findings suggest children with ASD have a spectrum of mitochondrial dysfunction of differing severity. Eighteen publications representing a total of 112 children with ASD and MD (ASD/MD) were identified. The prevalence of developmental regression (52%), seizures (41%), motor delay (51%), gastrointestinal abnormalities (74%), female gender (39%), and elevated lactate (78%) and pyruvate (45%) was significantly higher in ASD/MD compared with the general ASD population. The prevalence of many of these abnormalities was similar to the general population of children with MD, suggesting that ASD/MD represents a distinct subgroup of children with MD. Most ASD/MD cases (79%) were not associated with genetic abnormalities, raising the possibility of secondary mitochondrial dysfunction. Treatment studies for ASD/MD were limited, although improvements were noted in some studies with carnitine, co-enzyme Q10 and B-vitamins. Many studies suffered from limitations, including small sample sizes, referral or publication biases, and variability in protocols for selecting children for MD workup, collecting mitochondrial biomarkers and defining MD. Overall, this evidence supports the notion that mitochondrial dysfunction is associated with ASD. Additional studies are needed to further define the role of mitochondrial dysfunction in ASD.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija autista ha perdido habilidades que ya tenía, tiene convulsiones, retraso motor o problemas digestivos persistentes, puedes anotar cuándo ocurren y comentarlo con su equipo médico; a veces vale la pena revisar cómo funciona la energía de las células (mitocondrias). No es motivo de alarma ni afecta a la mayoría de personas autistas. Este metaanálisis reunió estudios publicados, incluidos 112 niños autistas con enfermedad mitocondrial, y estimó que alrededor del 5 % de los niños autistas podría tenerla. Sus límites: muestras pequeñas, sesgos de derivación y publicación, y criterios muy distintos entre estudios; los datos sobre suplementos son escasos y no sirven como recomendación.
sheet.en: If your autistic child has lost skills they once had, has seizures, motor delays or ongoing digestive problems, you can note when these happen and bring them to their medical team; sometimes it is worth looking at how their cells produce energy (mitochondria). This is not cause for alarm and does not apply to most autistic people. This meta-analysis pooled published studies, including 112 autistic children with mitochondrial disease, and estimated that about 5% of autistic children may have it. Its limits: small samples, referral and publication bias, and very different criteria across studies; evidence on supplements is scarce and is not a recommendation.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn har tappat färdigheter det tidigare hade, har epileptiska anfall, motorisk försening eller långvariga magproblem kan du anteckna när det händer och ta upp det med barnets vårdteam; ibland kan det vara värt att undersöka hur cellernas energiproduktion (mitokondrierna) fungerar. Det är ingen anledning till oro och gäller inte de flesta autistiska personer. Denna metaanalys sammanställde publicerade studier, bland annat 112 autistiska barn med mitokondriell sjukdom, och uppskattade att omkring 5 % av autistiska barn kan ha det. Begränsningar: små urval, remiss- och publiceringsbias samt olika kriterier mellan studierna; underlaget om kosttillskott är litet och utgör ingen rekommendation.

title: A systematic review with meta-analysis of comprehensive interventions for preschool children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD): study protocol.
authors: Tachibana Y, Green J, Hwang Y, Emsley R
abstract: Introduction The aims of this study are to (1) conduct a systematic review of the intervention literature in preschool children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), including types of interventions that are tested and the classification of outcome measures used and (2) to undertake a meta-analysis of the studies, allowing for the first time the comparison of different approaches to intervention using comparative outcomes. There are a number of alternative modalities of intervention for preschool children with ASD in use with different theoretical background and orientation, each of which tend to use different trial designs and outcome measures. There is at this time an urgent need for comprehensive systematic review and meta-analyses of intervention studies for preschool children with ASD, covering studies of adequate quality across different intervention types and measurement methods, with a view to identifying the best current evidence for preschool interventions in the disorder. Methods and analysis The authors will perform a systematic review of randomised controlled trials for preschool children with ASD aged 0-6 years, along with a meta-analysis of qualifying studies across intervention modality. The authors will classify the interventions for preschool children with ASD under three models: behaviour, multimodal developmental and communication focused. First, the authors will perform a systematic review. Then, the authors will conduct a meta-analysis by comparing the three models with various outcomes using an inverse variance method in a random effect model. The authors will synthesise each outcome of the studies for the three models using standardised mean differences. Dissemination and ethics This study will identify each intervention's strengths and weaknesses. This study may also suggest what kinds of elements future intervention programmes for children with ASD should have. The authors strongly believe those findings will be able to translated into the clinical practices and patients and their family benefits. Review registration: PROSPERO CRD42011001349.

sheet.es: Esta publicación no ofrece resultados todavía, así que no cambia nada mañana por la mañana. Sirve para saber que, al elegir apoyos para un niño autista en edad preescolar, conviene preguntar en qué modelo se basan: conductual, multimodal del desarrollo o centrado en la comunicación, y qué se mide. Es un protocolo de una revisión sistemática con metaanálisis de ensayos controlados aleatorizados con niños de 0-6 años. Como solo describe el plan, no dice qué enfoque funciona mejor, y no vale como regla para todas las personas. Las decisiones conviene hablarlas con el equipo profesional y con la propia familia.
sheet.en: This paper reports no results yet, so it changes nothing tomorrow morning. It helps you know that, when choosing supports for an autistic preschool child, it is worth asking which model they follow: behaviour, multimodal developmental or communication focused, and what they measure. It is the protocol for a systematic review with meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials with children aged 0-6 years. Because it only describes the plan, it cannot say which approach works best, and it is not a rule for every person. Talk decisions through with the professional team and your own family.
sheet.sv: Den här artikeln har inga resultat än, så den ändrar ingenting i morgon bitti. Den är till hjälp för att veta att när man väljer stöd till ett autistiskt förskolebarn kan man fråga vilken modell det bygger på: beteendeinriktad, multimodal utvecklingsinriktad eller kommunikationsinriktad, och vad som mäts. Det är ett protokoll för en systematisk översikt med metaanalys av randomiserade kontrollerade studier med barn i åldern 0-6 år. Eftersom den bara beskriver planen kan den inte säga vilket arbetssätt som fungerar bäst, och den är ingen regel för alla. Diskutera besluten med yrkesteamet och i familjen.

title: Age-related change in brain metabolite abnormalities in autism: a meta-analysis of proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy studies.
authors: Aoki Y, Kasai K, Yamasue H
abstract: Abnormal trajectory of brain development has been suggested by previous structural magnetic resonance imaging and head circumference findings in autism spectrum disorders (ASDs); however, the neurochemical backgrounds remain unclear. To elucidate neurochemical processes underlying aberrant brain growth in ASD, we conducted a comprehensive literature search and a meta-analysis of (1)H-magnetic resonance spectroscopy ((1)H-MRS) studies in ASD. From the 22 articles identified as satisfying the criteria, means and s.d. of measure of N-acetylaspartate (NAA), creatine, choline-containing compounds, myo-Inositol and glutamate+glutamine in frontal, temporal, parietal, amygdala-hippocampus complex, thalamus and cerebellum were extracted. Random effect model analyses showed significantly lower NAA levels in all the examined brain regions but cerebellum in ASD children compared with typically developed children (n=1295 at the maximum in frontal, P<0.05 Bonferroni-corrected), although there was no significant difference in metabolite levels in adulthood. Meta-regression analysis further revealed that the effect size of lower frontal NAA levels linearly declined with older mean age in ASD (n=844, P<0.05 Bonferroni-corrected). The significance of all frontal NAA findings was preserved after considering between-study heterogeneities (P<0.05 Bonferroni-corrected). This first meta-analysis of (1)H-MRS studies in ASD demonstrated robust developmental changes in the degree of abnormality in NAA levels, especially in frontal lobes of ASD. Previously reported larger-than-normal brain size in ASD children and the coincident lower-than-normal NAA levels suggest that early transient brain expansion in ASD is mainly caused by an increase in non-neuron tissues, such as glial cell proliferation.

sheet.es: Este estudio no cambia nada en la rutina de mañana: no ofrece ninguna pauta para la crianza ni para el apoyo diario. Si te interesa, puedes comentar con un profesional de confianza lo que significa la investigación sobre el cerebro. Evidencia: metaanálisis de 22 artículos que midieron sustancias químicas cerebrales con espectroscopia por resonancia magnética. Halló niveles de NAA más bajos en niños autistas que en niños con desarrollo típico, pero no diferencias en la edad adulta. Límites: son promedios de grupo, no describen a una persona concreta, no sirven para diagnosticar y la explicación sobre el tejido cerebral es solo una hipótesis.
sheet.en: This study changes nothing about tomorrow morning's routine: it offers no guidance for parenting or daily support. If you are curious, you can talk with a professional you trust about what brain research means. Evidence: a meta-analysis of 22 articles that measured brain chemicals using magnetic resonance spectroscopy. It found lower NAA levels in autistic children than in typically developing children, but no differences in adulthood. Limits: these are group averages, they do not describe any one person, they cannot be used to diagnose, and the explanation about brain tissue is only a suggestion.
sheet.sv: Den här studien ändrar inget i morgondagens rutiner: den ger ingen vägledning för föräldraskap eller vardagligt stöd. Om du är nyfiken kan du prata med en professionell du litar på om vad hjärnforskningen betyder. Evidens: en metaanalys av 22 artiklar som mätte kemiska ämnen i hjärnan med magnetisk resonansspektroskopi. Den fann lägre NAA-nivåer hos autistiska barn än hos barn med typisk utveckling, men inga skillnader i vuxen ålder. Begränsningar: det är gruppmedelvärden som inte beskriver en enskild person, de kan inte användas för diagnos, och förklaringen om hjärnvävnad är bara en hypotes.

title: Age-dependent brain gene expression and copy number anomalies in autism suggest distinct pathological processes at young versus mature ages.
authors: Chow ML, Pramparo T, Winn ME, Barnes CC, Li HR, Weiss L, Fan JB, Murray S, April C, Belinson H, Fu XD, Wynshaw-Boris A, Schork NJ, Courchesne E
abstract: Autism is a highly heritable neurodevelopmental disorder, yet the genetic underpinnings of the disorder are largely unknown. Aberrant brain overgrowth is a well-replicated observation in the autism literature; but association, linkage, and expression studies have not identified genetic factors that explain this trajectory. Few studies have had sufficient statistical power to investigate whole-genome gene expression and genotypic variation in the autistic brain, especially in regions that display the greatest growth abnormality. Previous functional genomic studies have identified possible alterations in transcript levels of genes related to neurodevelopment and immune function. Thus, there is a need for genetic studies involving key brain regions to replicate these findings and solidify the role of particular functional pathways in autism pathogenesis. We therefore sought to identify abnormal brain gene expression patterns via whole-genome analysis of mRNA levels and copy number variations (CNVs) in autistic and control postmortem brain samples. We focused on prefrontal cortex tissue where excess neuron numbers and cortical overgrowth are pronounced in the majority of autism cases. We found evidence for dysregulation in pathways governing cell number, cortical patterning, and differentiation in young autistic prefrontal cortex. In contrast, adult autistic prefrontal cortex showed dysregulation of signaling and repair pathways. Genes regulating cell cycle also exhibited autism-specific CNVs in DNA derived from prefrontal cortex, and these genes were significantly associated with autism in genome-wide association study datasets. Our results suggest that CNVs and age-dependent gene expression changes in autism may reflect distinct pathological processes in the developing versus the mature autistic prefrontal cortex. Our results raise the hypothesis that genetic dysregulation in the developing brain leads to abnormal regional patterning, excess prefrontal neurons, cortical overgrowth, and neural dysfunction in autism.

sheet.es: Este estudio no ofrece nada que cambie la rutina de mañana. Sirve para recordar que el cerebro autista puede cambiar con la edad, y que lo que ayuda a una criatura pequeña quizá no sea lo que necesita una persona adulta. Se trata de un metaanálisis de laboratorio con muestras de cerebro de personas autistas y de control tras su fallecimiento, centrado en la corteza prefrontal. Encontró diferencias en la actividad de genes según la edad. Sus límites: no estudia a personas vivas, no explica ninguna conducta concreta y no vale como regla para cada persona autista.
sheet.en: This study offers nothing that changes tomorrow's routine. It is a reminder that autistic brains may change with age, so what suits a young child may not be what an adult needs. It is a meta-analysis of laboratory work using postmortem brain samples from autistic and control people, focused on the prefrontal cortex. It found differences in gene activity between younger and older ages. Its limits: it does not study living people, does not explain any particular behaviour, and cannot be treated as a rule for every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Den här studien ger inget som ändrar morgondagens rutiner. Den påminner om att autistiska hjärnor kan förändras med åldern, så det som passar ett litet barn kanske inte passar en vuxen. Det är en metaanalys av laboratoriearbete med hjärnprover efter döden från autistiska och kontrollpersoner, med fokus på prefrontala hjärnbarken. Den fann skillnader i genaktivitet mellan yngre och äldre åldrar. Begränsningar: den studerar inte levande personer, förklarar inget enskilt beteende och kan inte ses som en regel för varje autistisk person.

title: A review of research trends in physiological abnormalities in autism spectrum disorders: immune dysregulation, inflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction and environmental toxicant exposures.
authors: Rossignol DA, Frye RE
abstract: Recent studies have implicated physiological and metabolic abnormalities in autism spectrum disorders (ASD) and other psychiatric disorders, particularly immune dysregulation or inflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction and environmental toxicant exposures ('four major areas'). The aim of this study was to determine trends in the literature on these topics with respect to ASD. A comprehensive literature search from 1971 to 2010 was performed in these four major areas in ASD with three objectives. First, publications were divided by several criteria, including whether or not they implicated an association between the physiological abnormality and ASD. A large percentage of publications implicated an association between ASD and immune dysregulation/inflammation (416 out of 437 publications, 95%), oxidative stress (all 115), mitochondrial dysfunction (145 of 153, 95%) and toxicant exposures (170 of 190, 89%). Second, the strength of evidence for publications in each area was computed using a validated scale. The strongest evidence was for immune dysregulation/inflammation and oxidative stress, followed by toxicant exposures and mitochondrial dysfunction. In all areas, at least 45% of the publications were rated as providing strong evidence for an association between the physiological abnormalities and ASD. Third, the time trends in the four major areas were compared with trends in neuroimaging, neuropathology, theory of mind and genetics ('four comparison areas'). The number of publications per 5-year block in all eight areas was calculated in order to identify significant changes in trends. Prior to 1986, only 12 publications were identified in the four major areas and 51 in the four comparison areas (42 for genetics). For each 5-year period, the total number of publications in the eight combined areas increased progressively. Most publications (552 of 895, 62%) in the four major areas were published in the last 5 years (2006-2010). Evaluation of trends between the four major areas and the four comparison areas demonstrated that the largest relative growth was in immune dysregulation/inflammation, oxidative stress, toxicant exposures, genetics and neuroimaging. Research on mitochondrial dysfunction started growing in the last 5 years. Theory of mind and neuropathology research has declined in recent years. Although most publications implicated an association between the four major areas and ASD, publication bias may have led to an overestimation of this association. Further research into these physiological areas may provide insight into general or subset-specific processes that could contribute to the development of ASD and other psychiatric disorders.

sheet.es: Este estudio no ofrece nada que cambiar mañana por la mañana: sirve para entender hacia dónde se orienta la investigación. Si le preocupa la salud física de una persona autista, hable con su equipo clínico. Es una revisión de la literatura científica de 1971 a 2010 sobre inmunidad e inflamación, estrés oxidativo, función mitocondrial y exposición a tóxicos. Una gran parte de las publicaciones halló alguna asociación con el autismo, y el número de publicaciones creció mucho en los últimos años. Sus límites: los propios autores advierten que el sesgo de publicación pudo exagerar esa asociación, y una asociación no demuestra una causa ni vale para todas las personas.
sheet.en: This study gives nothing to change tomorrow morning; it helps you understand where research is heading. If you worry about an autistic person's physical health, talk with their clinical team. It is a review of the scientific literature from 1971 to 2010 on immunity and inflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial function and toxicant exposures. Most publications found some association with autism, and the number of publications grew sharply in recent years. Its limits: the authors themselves warn that publication bias may have overestimated this association, and an association does not prove a cause or apply to every person.
sheet.sv: Den här studien ger inget att ändra i morgon bitti; den hjälper dig att förstå vart forskningen är på väg. Om du oroar dig för en autistisk persons fysiska hälsa, prata med personens vårdteam. Det är en översikt av forskningslitteraturen från 1971 till 2010 om immunförsvar och inflammation, oxidativ stress, mitokondriefunktion och exponering för giftiga ämnen. De flesta publikationerna fann något samband med autism, och antalet publikationer ökade kraftigt de senaste åren. Begränsningar: författarna varnar själva för att publiceringsbias kan ha överskattat sambandet, och ett samband bevisar ingen orsak och gäller inte alla personer.

title: The broader autism phenotype and its implications on the etiology and treatment of autism spectrum disorders.
authors: Gerdts J, Bernier R
abstract: The presence of autism-related traits has been well documented in undiagnosed family members of individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). The most common finding is mild impairments in social and communication skills that are similar to those shown by individuals with autism, but exhibited to a lesser degree. Termed the broader autism phenotype (BAP), these traits suggest a genetic liability for autism-related traits in families. Genetic influence in autism is strong, with identical twins showing high concordance for the diagnosis and related traits and approximately 20% of all ASD cases having an identified genetic mechanism. This paper highlights the studies conducted to date regarding the BAP and considers the implications of these findings for the etiology and treatment of ASD.

sheet.es: Es normal que algunas personas de una familia compartan rasgos parecidos, como una forma particular de comunicarse o de socializar. Verlo como variación familiar, y no como un fallo, puede ayudar a entender mejor las necesidades de cada persona. La evidencia es una revisión de estudios previos sobre familiares de personas autistas sin diagnóstico; menciona que aproximadamente 20% de los casos de TEA tiene un mecanismo genético identificado. Sus límites: es una revisión general, no un ensayo, y no sirve para predecir qué ocurrirá en una familia concreta ni para explicar a cada persona.
sheet.en: It is common for relatives in one family to share similar traits, such as a particular way of communicating or socialising. Seeing this as family variation rather than a fault can help you understand each person's needs. The evidence is a review of earlier studies on undiagnosed relatives of autistic people; it notes that approximately 20% of ASD cases have an identified genetic mechanism. Its limits: it is a general overview, not a trial, and it cannot predict what will happen in any particular family or explain any one person.
sheet.sv: Det är vanligt att släktingar i en familj delar liknande drag, till exempel ett visst sätt att kommunicera eller umgås. Att se det som variation i familjen, inte som ett fel, kan hjälpa dig att förstå varje persons behov. Underlaget är en översikt av tidigare studier om släktingar utan diagnos till autistiska personer; den nämner att approximately 20% av ASD-fallen har en identifierad genetisk mekanism. Begränsningar: det är en allmän översikt, inte en prövning, och den kan inte förutsäga vad som händer i en enskild familj eller förklara en enskild person.

title: Autism in developing countries: lessons from iran.
authors: Samadi SA, McConkey R
abstract: Most research into Autism Spectrum Disorders has been conducted in affluent English-speaking countries which have extensive professional support services. This paper describes a series of investigations that was undertaken in Iran, and these findings, together with reviews of research in other low-income countries, are used to identify key lessons in three areas of service provision of particular relevance to developing countries with scarce professional resources: first, the issues to be considered in establishing the prevalence of the condition nationally; second, identification of parental understanding of ASD and the impact it has on them as carers; third, the education and training that could be provided to families when professional supports are sparse. It is concluded that culturally sensitive, parental support strategies must be central to the planning and development of services. Moreover, future research should further elucidate the needs of families and evaluate the impact of culturally tailored interventions designed to promote the children's development and overall family quality of life.

sheet.es: Si vives en un lugar con pocos servicios especializados, el apoyo a las familias, adaptado a su cultura, puede ser un punto de partida valioso. Conviene conocer cómo entiende la familia el autismo y qué necesita quien cuida. La evidencia: una serie de investigaciones realizadas en Iran, junto con revisiones de estudios en otros países de bajos ingresos. Sus límites: no se indican resultados concretos sobre qué estrategia funciona mejor, y las conclusiones no valen igual para todas las familias ni todos los contextos. Hacen falta más estudios que evalúen intervenciones adaptadas culturalmente.
sheet.en: If you live where specialist services are scarce, culturally sensitive support for families can be a valuable starting point. It helps to explore how your family understands autism and what carers themselves need. The evidence: a series of investigations carried out in Iran, together with reviews of research in other low-income countries. Its limits: the abstract gives no specific results on which strategy works best, and the conclusions will not fit every family or setting equally. More studies are needed to evaluate culturally tailored interventions.
sheet.sv: Om du bor där specialiserade tjänster är få kan kulturanpassat stöd till familjer vara en värdefull utgångspunkt. Det hjälper att utforska hur familjen förstår autism och vad de som ger omsorg själva behöver. Evidensen: en serie undersökningar i Iran, tillsammans med översikter av forskning i andra låginkomstländer. Begränsningar: sammanfattningen redovisar inga konkreta resultat om vilken strategi som fungerar bäst, och slutsatserna passar inte alla familjer eller miljöer lika väl. Fler studier behövs för att utvärdera kulturanpassade insatser.

title: Infant siblings and the investigation of autism risk factors.
authors: Newschaffer CJ, Croen LA, Fallin MD, Hertz-Picciotto I, Nguyen DV, Lee NL, Berry CA, Farzadegan H, Hess HN, Landa RJ, Levy SE, Massolo ML, Meyerer SC, Mohammed SM, Oliver MC, Ozonoff S, Pandey J, Schr
abstract: Infant sibling studies have been at the vanguard of autism spectrum disorders (ASD) research over the past decade, providing important new knowledge about the earliest emerging signs of ASD and expanding our understanding of the developmental course of this complex disorder. Studies focused on siblings of children with ASD also have unrealized potential for contributing to ASD etiologic research. Moving targeted time of enrollment back from infancy toward conception creates tremendous opportunities for optimally studying risk factors and risk biomarkers during the pre-, peri- and neonatal periods. By doing so, a traditional sibling study, which already incorporates close developmental follow-up of at-risk infants through the third year of life, is essentially reconfigured as an enriched-risk pregnancy cohort study. This review considers the enriched-risk pregnancy cohort approach of studying infant siblings in the context of current thinking on ASD etiologic mechanisms. It then discusses the key features of this approach and provides a description of the design and implementation strategy of one major ASD enriched-risk pregnancy cohort study: the Early Autism Risk Longitudinal Investigation (EARLI).

sheet.es: Para una familia, lo práctico es saber que muchos estudios con hermanos de niños autistas buscan comprender mejor los primeros años, y que participar en ellos es una decisión voluntaria que se puede preguntar y valorar con calma. Esto es una revisión que propone seguir a embarazos de familias que ya tienen un hijo autista, para estudiar factores de riesgo antes y alrededor del nacimiento. Describe el diseño de un estudio llamado EARLI. Sus límites: es una propuesta de método, no muestra resultados sobre causas ni dice qué hacer en casa, y no se aplica igual a cada persona.
sheet.en: For a family, the practical point is that many studies with siblings of autistic children aim to understand the early years better, and joining one is a voluntary choice you can ask about and weigh calmly. This is a review proposing to follow pregnancies in families that already have an autistic child, to study risk factors before and around birth. It describes the design of one study, called EARLI. Its limits: it outlines a research method, not results about causes, and it gives no advice for daily life, so it does not apply the same way to every person.
sheet.sv: Det praktiska för en familj är att många studier med syskon till autistiska barn vill förstå de första åren bättre, och att delta är frivilligt – du kan fråga och fundera i lugn och ro. Detta är en översikt som föreslår att följa graviditeter i familjer som redan har ett autistiskt barn, för att studera riskfaktorer före och runt födseln. Den beskriver upplägget för en studie kallad EARLI. Begränsningar: den beskriver en forskningsmetod, inte resultat om orsaker, och ger inga råd för vardagen, så den gäller inte likadant för alla.

title: Of mice and monkeys: using non-human primate models to bridge mouse- and human-based investigations of autism spectrum disorders.
authors: Watson KK, Platt ML
abstract: The autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) arise from a diverse array of genetic and environmental origins that disrupt the typical developmental trajectory of neural connectivity and synaptogenesis. ASDs are marked by dysfunctional social behavior and cognition, among other deficits. Greater understanding of the biological substrates of typical social behavior in animal models will further our understanding of the etiology of ASDs. Despite the precision and tractability of molecular genetics models of ASDs in rodents, these organisms lack the complexity of human social behavior, thus limiting their impact on understanding ASDs to basic mechanisms. Non-human primates (NHPs) provide an attractive, complementary model for ASDs, due in part to the complexity and dynamics of social structures, reliance on vision for social signaling, and deep homology in brain circuitry mediating social behavior and reward. This knowledge is based on a rich literature, compiled over 50 years of observing primate behavior in the wild, which, in the case of rhesus macaques, is complemented by a large body of research characterizing neuronal activity during cognitive behavior. Several recent developments in this field are directly relevant to ASDs, including how the brain represents the perceptual features of social stimuli, how social information influences attention processes in the brain, and how the value of social interaction is computed. Because the symptoms of ASDs may represent extreme manifestations of traits that vary in intensity within the general population, we will additionally discuss ways in which nonhuman primates also show variation in social behavior and reward sensitivity. In cases where variation in species-typical behavior is analogous to similar variations in human behavior, we believe that study of the neural circuitry underlying this variation will provide important insights into the systems-level mechanisms contributing to ASD pathology.

sheet.es: Este artículo no ofrece nada que cambiar mañana en casa: es un trabajo de ciencia básica, no una guía práctica. Si te interesa, puedes verlo como una muestra de cómo se investiga la socialización. Sobre la evidencia: es una revisión de 2012 que plantea que los primates no humanos, como los macacos rhesus, podrían complementar los estudios en ratones para entender la conducta social y la recompensa. Límites: no incluyó a personas autistas, no probó ninguna ayuda y usa términos de déficit que no reflejan la perspectiva de la neurodiversidad. No debe tomarse como regla para ninguna persona.
sheet.en: This article offers nothing to change at home tomorrow: it is basic science, not practical guidance. If you are curious, you can read it as a glimpse of how social behaviour is studied. On the evidence: it is a 2012 review arguing that non-human primates, such as rhesus macaques, could complement mouse studies in understanding social behaviour and reward. Limits: it included no autistic people, tested no support or approach, and uses deficit-based wording that does not reflect a neurodiversity view. It should not be taken as a rule for any individual person.
sheet.sv: Den här artikeln ger inget att ändra hemma i morgon: det är grundforskning, inte praktisk vägledning. Om du är nyfiken kan du läsa den som en inblick i hur socialt beteende studeras. Om evidensen: det är en översikt från 2012 som menar att icke-mänskliga primater, som rhesusapor, kan komplettera musstudier när man vill förstå socialt beteende och belöning. Begränsningar: inga autistiska personer deltog, inget stöd eller arbetssätt prövades, och texten använder bristfokuserade ord som inte speglar ett neurodiversitetsperspektiv. Den ska inte ses som en regel för någon enskild person.

title: The discovery of autism: Indian parents' experiences of caring for their child with an autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Desai MU, Divan G, Wertz FJ, Patel V
abstract: The current study investigated the lived experience of 12 parents of children with an Autism Spectrum Disorder in everyday cultural contexts in Goa, India. Narratives from parents collected between 2009 and 2010 were analyzed using the procedures of phenomenological psychology. Four temporal phases of parents' experience emerged from these data. Findings showed that the earliest phase of the child's life was a period of relative normalcy and social cohesion. In the second phase, the child's behaviors began to disrupt the everyday social order, but parents viewed these unexpected behaviors as temporary. In the third phase, parents' observations in public situations, along with assessments of others, led to a qualitative shift in which parents began to perceive that there was a persisting problem interfering with their child's social and practical activities. In the fourth phase, parents grappled with developing their child's capacities to meet existing practical opportunities in the local society, while attempting to reshape the social world to accommodate the abilities and limits of children like their own. Parents' fundamental concerns throughout their journey were: learning to meet new and unfamiliar challenges as parents, caring for their child's basic needs, and finding an engaging niche with a sense of belonging for their child in the everyday milieu. Both culture-specific and potentially universal levels of experience are delineated in the overall findings. Implications for culturally sensitive research and practice in India and other low- and middle-income countries are discussed.

sheet.es: Si te reconoces en este recorrido, no estás solo ni sola: muchas familias pasan por dudas, cambios y búsqueda de un lugar donde su hijo o hija pueda pertenecer. Puede ayudar hablar con otras familias y buscar espacios acordes a sus capacidades. La evidencia es un estudio cualitativo con 12 madres y padres de niños autistas en Goa, India, con relatos recogidos entre 2009 y 2010. Sus límites: es un grupo pequeño, de un solo lugar, y no recoge la voz de las propias personas autistas, así que no vale como regla para todas las familias.
sheet.en: If you recognise yourself in this journey, you are not alone: many families go through doubt, change, and the search for a place where their child can belong. It may help to talk with other families and look for settings that fit your child's abilities. The evidence is a qualitative study of 12 parents of autistic children in Goa, India, using accounts collected between 2009 and 2010. Its limits: the group is small, from one place, and it does not include the voices of autistic people themselves, so it is not a rule for every family.
sheet.sv: Om du känner igen dig i den här resan är du inte ensam: många familjer går igenom tvivel, förändring och sökandet efter en plats där barnet kan känna tillhörighet. Det kan hjälpa att prata med andra familjer och söka miljöer som passar barnets förmågor. Underlaget är en kvalitativ studie med 12 föräldrar till autistiska barn i Goa, Indien, med berättelser insamlade 2009 och 2010. Begränsningar: gruppen är liten, från en plats, och studien innehåller inte autistiska personers egna röster, så den är ingen regel för alla familjer.

title: Perinatal stress, brain inflammation and risk of autism-review and proposal.
authors: Angelidou A, Asadi S, Alysandratos KD, Karagkouni A, Kourembanas S, Theoharides TC
abstract: Background Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASD) are neurodevelopmental disorders characterized by varying deficits in social interactions, communication, and learning, as well as stereotypic behaviors. Despite the significant increase in ASD, there are few if any clues for its pathogenesis, hampering early detection or treatment. Premature babies are also more vulnerable to infections and inflammation leading to neurodevelopmental problems and higher risk of developing ASD. Many autism "susceptibility" genes have been identified, but "environmental" factors appear to play a significant role. Increasing evidence suggests that there are different ASD endophenotypes. Discussion We review relevant literature suggesting in utero inflammation can lead to preterm labor, while insufficient development of the gut-blood-brain barriers could permit exposure to potential neurotoxins. This risk apparently may increase in parents with "allergic" or autoimmune problems during gestation, or if they had been exposed to stressors. The presence of circulating auto-antibodies against fetal brain proteins in mothers is associated with higher risk of autism and suggests disruption of the blood-brain-barrier (BBB). A number of papers have reported increased brain expression or cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines, especially TNF, which is preformed in mast cells. Recent evidence also indicates increased serum levels of the pro-inflammatory mast cell trigger neurotensin (NT), and of extracellular mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), which is immunogenic. Gene mutations of phosphatase and tensin homolog (PTEN), the negative regulator of the mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR), have been linked to higher risk of autism, but also to increased proliferation and function of mast cells. Summary Premature birth and susceptibility genes may make infants more vulnerable to allergic, environmental, infectious, or stress-related triggers that could stimulate mast cell release of pro-inflammatory and neurotoxic molecules, thus contributing to brain inflammation and ASD pathogenesis, at least in an endophenotype of ASD patients.

sheet.es: Mañana por la mañana, este estudio no pide cambiar nada en vuestra rutina. Si os preocupa algo sobre el embarazo, el parto prematuro o las alergias, podéis hablarlo con un profesional sanitario, sin culpa: nada aquí señala a una familia concreta. Es una revisión de la bibliografía, no un estudio con participantes propios. Reúne trabajos que relacionan el parto prematuro, la inflamación, el estrés y los genes con el autismo, y propone una hipótesis sobre la inflamación cerebral en algunas personas autistas. Sus límites: es una propuesta, no una prueba; no demuestra causas ni sirve como regla para todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: Tomorrow morning, this study does not ask you to change anything in your routine. If you wonder about pregnancy, preterm birth or allergies, you can talk it through with a health professional, without guilt: nothing here points at any particular family. It is a review of the literature, not a study with its own participants. It gathers work linking preterm birth, inflammation, stress and genes with autism, and proposes a hypothesis about brain inflammation in some autistic people. Its limits: it is a proposal, not proof; it does not show causes and is not a rule for every autistic person.
sheet.sv: I morgon bitti ber den här studien dig inte ändra något i vardagen. Om du funderar på graviditet, för tidig födsel eller allergier kan du prata med en vårdgivare, utan skuld: ingenting här pekar ut en särskild familj. Det är en översikt av litteraturen, inte en studie med egna deltagare. Den samlar arbeten som kopplar för tidig födsel, inflammation, stress och gener till autism, och föreslår en hypotes om hjärninflammation hos vissa autistiska personer. Begränsningar: det är ett förslag, inte ett bevis; den visar inte orsaker och är ingen regel för alla autistiska personer.

title: An exploration of sensory and movement differences from the perspective of individuals with autism.
authors: Robledo J, Donnellan AM, Strandt-Conroy K
abstract: Parents, teachers, and people who themselves experience sensory and movement differences have consistently reported disturbances of sensation and movement associated with autism. Our review of the literature has revealed both historical and recent references to and research about sensory and movement difference characteristics and symptoms for individuals with autism. What is notably infrequent in this literature, however, is research that highlights the perspective of the individual with autism. If we wish to truly understand the experience of sensory and movement differences for individuals with autism, we must explore their experiences and perspectives. This study presents a qualitative analysis of more than 40 h in-depth inquiry into the lives of five individuals with the autism label. Data were sorted into six categories: perception, action, posture, emotion, communication, and cognition. The insights into sensory and movement differences and autism offered by these individuals was illuminating. We found that the data strongly supported the presence of disruption of organization and regulation of sensory and movement differences in the lived experience of these participants with autism. The present data suggests that in autism this disruption of organization and regulation is amplified in terms of quantity, quality, intensity, and may affect everyday life. These data contribute to a more expansive view of autism that incorporates the possibility that autism is a disorder that affects motor planning, behavior, communication, the sensory motor system, and the dynamic interaction of all of these.

title: Autism risk factors: genes, environment, and gene-environment interactions.
authors: Chaste P, Leboyer M
abstract: The aim of this review is to summarize the key findings from genetic and epidemiological research, which show that autism is a complex disorder resulting from the combination of genetic and environmental factors. Remarkable advances in the knowledge of genetic causes of autism have resulted from the great efforts made in the field of genetics. The identification of specific alleles contributing to the autism spectrum has supplied important pieces for the autism puzzle. However, many questions remain unanswered, and new questions are raised by recent results. Moreover, given the amount of evidence supporting a significant contribution of environmental factors to autism risk, it is now clear that the search for environmental factors should be reinforced. One aspect of this search that has been neglected so far is the study of interactions between genes and environmental factors.

sheet.es: Qué significa para el día a día: este trabajo no ofrece nada que haya que cambiar mañana por la mañana. Si te preocupa la culpa o el "porqué", puede ayudarte saber que el autismo se relaciona con una combinación de factores genéticos y ambientales, no con una sola causa ni con algo que una familia haya hecho. Es mejor centrarse en los apoyos que la persona necesita hoy. Evidencia: es una revisión que resume investigación genética y epidemiológica. Límites: no es un estudio con participantes nuevos, es de 2012, deja muchas preguntas abiertas y no explica a ninguna persona en concreto.
sheet.en: What this means day to day: this paper offers nothing you need to change tomorrow morning. If you are worried about blame or the "why", it may help to know that autism is linked to a mix of genetic and environmental factors, not a single cause and not something a family did. It is usually more useful to focus on the supports the person needs today. Evidence: this is a review summarising genetic and epidemiological research. Limits: it is not a new study with participants, it dates from 2012, it leaves many questions open, and it cannot explain any one individual.
sheet.sv: Vad det betyder i vardagen: den här artikeln ger inget du behöver ändra i morgon bitti. Om du oroar dig för skuld eller för "varför" kan det hjälpa att veta att autism hänger ihop med en kombination av genetiska faktorer och miljöfaktorer, inte en enda orsak och inte något en familj har gjort. Det är oftast mer användbart att fokusera på det stöd personen behöver i dag. Evidens: det är en översikt som sammanfattar genetisk och epidemiologisk forskning. Begränsningar: den är ingen ny studie med deltagare, är från 2012, lämnar många frågor öppna och kan inte förklara någon enskild person.

title: Mechanisms of change in psychosocial interventions for autism spectrum disorders.
authors: Lerner MD, White SW, McPartland JC
abstract: Research into psychosocial interventions (particularly cognitive-behavior therapies and social skills training) for social-communication deficits among individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) has proliferated over the past decade. While this research has provided some empirical support for the efficacy of these interventions, little work has begun to elucidate therapeutic mechanisms-the when, why, how, for whom, and under what conditions an intervention may produce change, identification of mechanisms underlying these effects should help advance ASD intervention research. This article describes methods for assessing such mechanisms (ie, mediators and moderators) and presents promising candidates for common mechanisms impacting treatment response: behavior modification, therapeutic relationship, social knowledge, social motivation, social information processing, executive functioning, and internalizing comorbidities. Finally, future directions are discussed as a program of psychosocial intervention research designed to identify predictors of individual differences in treatment response (including biomarkers), isolate active therapeutic ingredients, and promote dissemination of optimized interventions.

sheet.es: Si piensas en apoyos como la terapia cognitivo-conductual o el entrenamiento en habilidades sociales, conviene preguntar qué componente ayuda a cada persona y por qué. La relación de confianza con quien apoya, la motivación social y la ansiedad o el ánimo pueden influir en los resultados. Es una revisión de la investigación, no un estudio con participantes propios. Señala que se sabe poco sobre cómo y para quién funcionan estas intervenciones, y que varias ideas aún son solo prometedoras. Ningún enfoque sirve igual a todas las personas autistas; observa cómo responde la persona y habla con el equipo profesional.
sheet.en: If you are considering supports such as cognitive-behavioural therapy or social skills training, it helps to ask which parts are working for this person, and why. The trusting relationship with the practitioner, social motivation, and anxiety or low mood may all shape results. This is a review of existing research, not a study with its own participants. It notes that little is yet known about how and for whom these interventions work, and several ideas are still only promising. No approach suits every autistic person equally; watch how the person responds and talk with the professional team.
sheet.sv: Om du funderar på stöd som kognitiv beteendeterapi eller social färdighetsträning kan du fråga vilka delar som fungerar för just den här personen, och varför. Den förtroendefulla relationen till behandlaren, social motivation samt oro eller nedstämdhet kan påverka resultatet. Detta är en översikt av befintlig forskning, inte en studie med egna deltagare. Den påpekar att det ännu är lite känt om hur och för vem insatserna fungerar, och flera idéer är bara lovande. Ingen metod passar alla autistiska personer lika bra; se hur personen reagerar och prata med teamet.

title: Individual differences in the efficacy of a short theory of mind intervention for children with autism spectrum disorder: a randomized controlled trial.
authors: Hoddenbach E, Koot HM, Clifford P, Gevers C, Clauser C, Boer F, Begeer S
abstract: Background Having a 'theory of mind', or having the ability to attribute mental states to oneself or others, is considered one of the most central domains of impairment among children with an autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Many interventions focus on improving theory of mind skills in children with ASD. Nonetheless, the empirical evidence for the effect of these interventions is limited. The main goal of this study is to examine the effectiveness of a short theory of mind intervention for children with ASD. A second objective is to determine which subgroups within the autism spectrum profit most from the intervention. Methods This study is a randomized controlled trial. One hundred children with ASD, aged 7 to 12 years will be randomly assigned to an intervention or a waiting list control group. Outcome measures include the completion of theory of mind and emotion understanding tasks, and parent and teacher questionnaires on children's social skills. Follow-up data for the intervention group will be collected 6 months after the interventions. Discussion This study evaluates the efficacy of a theory of mind intervention for children with ASD. Hypotheses, strengths, and limitations of the study are discussed. Trial registration Netherlands Trial Register NTR2327.

title: Rethinking autism: implications of sensory and movement differences for understanding and support.
authors: Donnellan AM, Hill DA, Leary MR
abstract: For decades autism has been defined as a triad of deficits in social interaction, communication, and imaginative play. Though there is now broad acknowledgment of the neurological basis of autism, there is little attention paid to the contribution of such neurological differences to a person's development and functioning. Communication, relationship, and participation require neurological systems to coordinate and synchronize the organization and regulation of sensory information and movement. Developmental differences in these abilities are likely to result in differences in the way a person behaves and expresses intention and meaning. The present paper shares our emerging awareness that people may struggle with difficulties that are not immediately evident to an outsider. This paper explores the symptoms of sensory and movement differences and the possible implications for autistic people. It provides a review of the history and literature that describes the neurological basis for many of the socalled behavioral differences that people experience. The paper emphasizes the importance of our acknowledgment that a social interpretation of differences in behavior, relationship, and communication can lead us far away from the lived experience of individuals with the autism label and those who support them. We suggest alternative ways to address the challenges faced by people with autism.

sheet.es: Cuando tu hijo o hija autista no responde, se queda inmóvil o repite un movimiento, puede no ser falta de interés ni desobediencia: quizá su cuerpo tarda en organizar lo que percibe y en iniciar o detener una acción. Mañana prueba a dar más tiempo, ofrecer apoyo físico o visual si lo acepta, reducir ruido o luz, y preguntar qué le ayuda. Interpreta la conducta con curiosidad, no como un mensaje social. Este artículo revisa la historia y la literatura sobre diferencias sensoriales y de movimiento, e incluye experiencias de personas autistas. Es una revisión narrativa de 2012, no un ensayo que compare apoyos, y cada persona es distinta.
sheet.en: When your autistic child doesn't respond, freezes, or repeats a movement, it may not mean disinterest or defiance: their body may need time to organise what they sense and to start or stop an action. Tomorrow, try giving extra time, offering physical or visual support if welcome, lowering noise or light, and asking what helps. Read behaviour with curiosity rather than as a social message. This paper reviews the history and literature on sensory and movement differences, drawing on autistic people's experiences. It is a 2012 narrative review, not a trial comparing supports, and every person is different.
sheet.sv: När ditt autistiska barn inte svarar, fastnar eller upprepar en rörelse behöver det inte betyda ointresse eller trots: kroppen kan behöva tid att organisera sinnesintryck och att starta eller stoppa en handling. I morgon kan du ge mer tid, erbjuda fysiskt eller visuellt stöd om det är välkommet, sänka ljud eller ljus och fråga vad som hjälper. Tolka beteendet med nyfikenhet snarare än som ett socialt budskap. Artikeln går igenom historik och forskning om sensoriska och motoriska skillnader och bygger på autistiska personers erfarenheter. Det är en berättande översikt från 2012, ingen studie som jämför stödformer, och varje person är olik.

title: The group-based social skills training SOSTA-FRA in children and adolescents with high functioning autism spectrum disorder--study protocol of the randomised, multi-centre controlled SOSTA--net trial.
authors: Freitag CM, Cholemkery H, Elsuni L, Kroeger AK, Bender S, Kunz CU, Kieser M
abstract: Background Group-based social skills training (SST) has repeatedly been recommended as treatment of choice in high-functioning autism spectrum disorder (HFASD). To date, no sufficiently powered randomised controlled trial has been performed to establish efficacy and safety of SST in children and adolescents with HFASD. In this randomised, multi-centre, controlled trial with 220 children and adolescents with HFASD it is hypothesized, that add-on group-based SST using the 12 weeks manualised SOSTA-FRA program will result in improved social responsiveness (measured by the parent rated social responsiveness scale, SRS) compared to treatment as usual (TAU). It is further expected, that parent and self reported anxiety and depressive symptoms will decline and pro-social behaviour will increase in the treatment group. A neurophysiological study in the Frankfurt HFASD subgroup will be performed pre- and post treatment to assess changes in neural function induced by SST versus TAU. Methods/design The SOSTA - net trial is designed as a prospective, randomised, multi-centre, controlled trial with two parallel groups. The primary outcome is change in SRS score directly after the intervention and at 3 months follow-up. Several secondary outcome measures are also obtained. The target sample consists of 220 individuals with ASD, included at the six study centres. Discussion This study is currently one of the largest trials on SST in children and adolescents with HFASD worldwide. Compared to recent randomised controlled studies, our study shows several advantages with regard to in- and exclusion criteria, study methods, and the therapeutic approach chosen, which can be easily implemented in non-university-based clinical settings.
