Trial registration ISRCTN94863788--SOSTA--net: Group-based social skills training in children and adolescents with high functioning autism spectrum disorder.

sheet.es: Si valoras un grupo de habilidades sociales para un niño o adolescente autista, pregunta qué se trabaja, cuánto dura y si encaja con sus intereses y su ritmo. Este es el protocolo de un ensayo aleatorizado y controlado en varios centros, con 220 niños y adolescentes autistas, que compara un programa grupal de 12 semanas con la atención habitual. Describe cómo se hará el estudio, pero no ofrece resultados, así que aún no sabemos si el programa ayuda. Tampoco sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you are considering a social skills group for an autistic child or teenager, ask what it covers, how long it lasts and whether it fits their interests and pace. This is the protocol of a randomised, controlled, multi-centre trial with 220 autistic children and adolescents, comparing a 12-week group programme with usual care. It describes how the study will be run but reports no results, so we do not yet know whether the programme helps. It is also not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du överväger en social färdighetsgrupp för ett autistiskt barn eller en tonåring, fråga vad den innehåller, hur lång den är och om den passar personens intressen och tempo. Detta är protokollet för en randomiserad, kontrollerad studie vid flera centra med 220 autistiska barn och ungdomar, som jämför ett 12 veckors gruppprogram med vanlig vård. Det beskriver hur studien ska genomföras men redovisar inga resultat, så vi vet ännu inte om programmet hjälper. Det är inte heller en regel för alla.

title: Embodiment and sense-making in autism.
authors: De Jaegher H
abstract: In this article, I sketch an enactive account of autism. For the enactive approach to cognition, embodiment, experience, and social interaction are fundamental to understanding mind and subjectivity. Enaction defines cognition as sense-making: the way cognitive agents meaningfully connect with their world, based on their needs and goals as self-organizing, self-maintaining, embodied agents. In the social realm, the interactive coordination of embodied sense-making activities with others lets us participate in each other's sense-making (social understanding = participatory sense-making). The enactive approach provides new concepts to overcome the problems of traditional functionalist accounts of autism, which can only give a piecemeal and disintegrated view because they consider cognition, communication, and perception separately, do not take embodied into account, and are methodologically individualistic. Applying the concepts of enaction to autism, I show: How embodiment and sense-making connect, i.e., how autistic particularities of moving, perceiving, and emoting relate to how people with autism make sense of their world. For instance, restricted interests or preference for detail will have certain sensorimotor correlates, as well as specific meaning for autistic people.That reduced flexibility in interactional coordination correlates with difficulties in participatory sense-making. At the same time, seemingly irrelevant "autistic behaviors" can be quite attuned to the interactive context. I illustrate this complexity in the case of echolalia. An enactive account of autism starts from the embodiment, experience, and social interactions of autistic people. Enaction brings together the sensorimotor, cognitive, social, experiential, and affective aspects of autism in a coherent framework based on a complex non-linear multi-causality. This foundation allows to build new bridges between autistic people and their often non-autistic context, and to improve quality of life prospects.

sheet.es: Mañana, cuando tu hijo o hija repita frases (ecolalia), se mueva de forma particular o se centre en detalles, prueba a preguntarte qué sentido tiene eso para él o ella en ese momento, en lugar de verlo como algo sin importancia. Muchas veces estas conductas encajan con lo que está pasando en la interacción. Ajustar tu ritmo, tus movimientos y tu forma de hablar al suyo puede facilitar que construyáis significado juntos. La evidencia: es un artículo teórico (2013) que propone el enfoque «enactivo», uniendo cuerpo, percepción, emoción e interacción social en el autismo. Límites: no recoge datos nuevos de participantes; son ideas para comprender, no una regla válida para cada persona.
sheet.en: Tomorrow, when your child repeats phrases (echolalia), moves in their own way, or focuses on details, try asking what that means for them right now, rather than treating it as irrelevant. These behaviours are often tuned to what is happening in the interaction. Matching your pace, movement and way of speaking to theirs can help you build meaning together. The evidence: this is a 2013 theoretical article proposing an 'enactive' approach that connects body, perception, emotion and social interaction in autism. Limits: it does not report new data from participants; it offers a way of understanding, not a rule that fits every autistic person.
sheet.sv: I morgon, när ditt barn upprepar fraser (ekolali), rör sig på sitt eget sätt eller fokuserar på detaljer, försök fråga dig vad det betyder för barnet just nu, i stället för att se det som oviktigt. Sådana beteenden är ofta anpassade till det som händer i samspelet. Att matcha ditt tempo, dina rörelser och ditt sätt att prata med barnets kan hjälpa er att skapa mening tillsammans. Evidensen: en teoretisk artikel från 2013 som föreslår ett ”enaktivt” synsätt där kropp, perception, känslor och socialt samspel hänger ihop vid autism. Begränsningar: den redovisar inga nya data från deltagare; den ger ett sätt att förstå, inte en regel för varje autistisk person.

title: Comparison of healthcare experiences in autistic and non-autistic adults: a cross-sectional online survey facilitated by an academic-community partnership.
authors: Nicolaidis C, Raymaker D, McDonald K, Dern S, Boisclair WC, Ashkenazy E, Baggs A

claim.es: Adultos autistas informan peor comunicación con profesionales sanitarios y más necesidades no atendidas que adultos no autistas.
claim.en: Autistic adults report worse communication with healthcare providers and more unmet needs than non-autistic adults.
claim.sv: Autistiska vuxna rapporterar sämre kommunikation med vårdpersonal och fler ouppfyllda behov än icke-autistiska vuxna.

supports.es: Llevar a las citas un resumen escrito y las preferencias de comunicación de la persona.
supports.en: Bringing a written summary and the person's communication preferences to appointments.
supports.sv: Att ta med en skriftlig sammanfattning och personens kommunikationspreferenser till besök.

doesNotSupport.es: Que haya que evitar la sanidad; significa que debe hacerse accesible.
doesNotSupport.en: That healthcare should be avoided; it means it must be made accessible.
doesNotSupport.sv: Att vården ska undvikas; det betyder att den måste göras tillgänglig.

title: Sniffing around oxytocin: review and meta-analyses of trials in healthy and clinical groups with implications for pharmacotherapy.
authors: Bakermans-Kranenburg MJ, van I Jzendoorn MH
abstract: The popularity of oxytocin (OT) has grown exponentially during the past decade, and so has the number of OT trials in healthy and clinical groups. We take stock of the evidence from these studies to explore potentials and limitations of pharmacotherapeutic applications. In healthy participants, intranasally administered OT leads to better emotion recognition and more trust in conspecifics, but the effects appear to be moderated by context (perceived threat of the 'out-group'), personality and childhood experiences. In individuals with untoward childhood experiences, positive behavioral or neurobiological effects seem lowered or absent. In 19 clinical trials, covering autism, social anxiety, postnatal depression, obsessive-compulsive problems, schizophrenia, borderline personality disorder and post-traumatic stress, the effects of OT administration were tested, with doses ranging from 15 IU to more than 7000 IU. The combined effect size was d=0.32 (N=304; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.18-0.47; P<0.01). However, of all disorders, only studies on autism spectrum disorder showed a significant combined effect size (d=0.57; N=68; 95% CI: 0.15-0.99; P<0.01). We hypothesize that for some of the other disorders, etiological factors rooted in negative childhood experiences may also have a role in the diminished effectiveness of treatment with OT.

title: Pain sensitivity and observer perception of pain in individuals with autistic spectrum disorder.
authors: Allely CS
abstract: The peer-reviewed literature investigating the relationship between pain expression and perception of pain in individuals with ASD is sparse. The aim of the present systematic PRIMSA review was twofold: first, to see what evidence there is for the widely held belief that individuals with ASD are insensitive to pain or have a high pain threshold in the peer-reviewed literature and, second, to examine whether individuals with ASD react or express pain differently. Fifteen studies investigating pain in individuals with ASD were identified. The case studies all reported pain insensitivity in individuals with ASD. However, the majority of the ten experimental studies reviewed indicate that the idea that individuals with ASD are pain insensitive needs to be challenged. The findings also highlight the strong possibility that not all children with ASD express their physical discomfort in the same way as a neurotypical child would (i.e., cry, moan, seek comfort, etc.) which may lead caregivers and the medical profession to interpret this as pain insensitivity or incorrectly lead them to believe that the child is in no pain. These results have important implications for the assessment and management of pain in children with ASD.

sheet.es: No des por hecho que una persona autista no siente dolor porque no llora ni se queja. Fíjate en otras señales, como cambios en su rutina, su postura, su comida o su sueño, y pregúntale con apoyos visuales si lo necesita. Esta revisión sistemática reunió quince estudios sobre dolor en personas autistas: los estudios de caso describían insensibilidad al dolor, pero la mayoría de los diez estudios experimentales cuestiona esa idea. Los autores señalan que muchos niños autistas quizá no expresen el malestar como otros niños. Como límite, la literatura sobre el tema es escasa y los resultados no valen para todas las personas.
sheet.en: Don't assume an autistic person feels no pain just because they don't cry or complain. Look for other signs, such as changes in routine, posture, eating or sleep, and offer visual supports to ask them about it if helpful. This systematic review gathered fifteen studies on pain in autistic people: the case studies described pain insensitivity, but most of the ten experimental studies challenge that idea. The authors note that many autistic children may not express discomfort the way other children do. A limit is that research on this topic is sparse, and the findings do not apply to every person.
sheet.sv: Utgå inte från att en autistisk person inte känner smärta bara för att hen inte gråter eller klagar. Titta efter andra tecken, som förändrade rutiner, hållning, ätande eller sömn, och fråga gärna med visuellt stöd om det hjälper. Denna systematiska översikt samlade femton studier om smärta hos autistiska personer: fallstudierna beskrev smärtokänslighet, men de flesta av de tio experimentella studierna ifrågasätter den idén. Författarna påpekar att många autistiska barn kanske inte uttrycker obehag som andra barn gör. En begränsning är att forskningen är knapp och att resultaten inte gäller alla personer.

title: A chinese mind-body exercise improves self-control of children with autism: a randomized controlled trial.
authors: Chan AS, Sze SL, Siu NY, Lau EM, Cheung MC
abstract: Self-control problems commonly manifest as temper outbursts and repetitive/rigid/impulsive behaviors, in children with autism spectrum disorders (ASD), which often contributes to learning difficulties and caregiver burden. The present study aims to compare the effect of a traditional Chinese Chan-based mind-body exercise, Nei Yang Gong, with that of the conventional Progressive Muscle Relaxation (PMR) technique in enhancing the self-control of children with ASD. Forty-six age- and IQ-matched ASD children were randomly assigned to receive group training in Nei Yang Gong (experimental group) or PMR (control group) twice per week for four weeks. The participants' self-control was measured by three neuropsychological tests and parental rating on standardized questionnaires, and the underlying neural mechanism was assessed by the participants' brain EEG activity during an inhibitory-control task before and after intervention. The results show that the experimental group demonstrated significantly greater improvement in self-control than the control group, which concurs with the parental reports of reduced autistic symptoms and increased control of temper and behaviors. In addition, the experimental group showed enhanced EEG activity in the anterior cingulate cortex, a region that mediates self-control, whereas the PMR group did not. The present findings support the potential application of Chinese Chan-based mind-body exercises as a form of neuropsychological rehabilitation for patients with self-control problems. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry; Registration No.: ChiCTR-TRC-12002561; URL: www.chictr.org.

sheet.es: Si le interesa probar una actividad corporal tranquila con su hijo o hija autista, un ejercicio de mente y cuerpo en grupo puede ser una opción, siempre que a la persona le resulte agradable y no se imponga. Es un ensayo aleatorizado con 46 niños autistas, que hicieron Nei Yang Gong o relajación muscular progresiva dos veces por semana durante 4 semanas. El grupo de Nei Yang Gong mejoró más en autocontrol, según pruebas y según las familias. Límites: muestra pequeña, periodo corto y no sabemos si los resultados se mantienen ni si sirven a cada persona.
sheet.en: If you are curious about a calm, body-based activity for your autistic child, a group mind-body exercise may be one option, as long as they enjoy it and it is not forced. This was a randomized trial with 46 autistic children, who did either Nei Yang Gong or progressive muscle relaxation twice per week for four weeks. The Nei Yang Gong group improved more in self-control, on tests and in parent reports. Limits: a small sample, a short period, and we do not know whether the benefits last or suit every person.
sheet.sv: Om du är nyfiken på en lugn, kroppsbaserad aktivitet för ditt autistiska barn kan en mind-body-övning i grupp vara ett alternativ, så länge barnet tycker om den och den inte tvingas fram. Studien var en randomiserad studie med 46 autistiska barn som gjorde antingen Nei Yang Gong eller progressiv muskelavslappning två gånger i veckan i fyra veckor. Nei Yang Gong-gruppen förbättrades mer i självkontroll, både i tester och enligt föräldrarna. Begränsningar: litet urval, kort period, och vi vet inte om effekten består eller passar alla.

title: Autism as a developmental disorder in intentional movement and affective engagement.
authors: Trevarthen C, Delafield-Butt JT
abstract: We review evidence that autistic spectrum disorders have their origin in early prenatal failure of development in systems that program timing, serial coordination and prospective control of movements, and that regulate affective evaluations of experiences. There are effects in early infancy, before medical diagnosis, especially in motor sequencing, selective or exploratory attention, affective expression and intersubjective engagement with parents. These are followed by retardation of cognitive development and language learning in the second or third year, which lead to a diagnosis of ASD. The early signs relate to abnormalities that have been found in brain stem systems and cerebellum in the embryo or early fetal stage, before the cerebral neocortex is functional, and they have clear consequences in infancy when neocortical systems are intensively elaborated. We propose, with evidence of the disturbances of posture, locomotion and prospective motor control in children with autism, as well as of their facial expression of interest and affect, and attention to other persons' expressions, that examination of the psychobiology of motor affective disorders, rather than later developing cognitive or linguistic ones, may facilitate early diagnosis. Research in this area may also explain how intense interaction, imitation or "expressive art" therapies, which respond intimately with motor activities, are effective at later stages. Exceptional talents of some autistic people may be acquired compensations for basic problems with expectant self-regulations of movement, attention and emotion.

sheet.es: Si observas que tu criatura se mueve, mira o expresa emociones de forma distinta, anótalo y coméntalo con su profesional de referencia; no hace falta esperar a que haya diferencias en el lenguaje. Este trabajo es una revisión de estudios previos, no un experimento nuevo. Propone que las diferencias de movimiento y de expresión afectiva en la infancia temprana podrían ayudar a detectar el autismo antes. Sus límites: es una propuesta teórica, no demuestra nada por sí sola, usa un lenguaje de déficit y no vale como regla para todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If you notice your child moves, looks or expresses feelings differently, jot it down and share it with their professional; there is no need to wait for language differences. This paper is a review of earlier studies, not a new experiment. It proposes that differences in movement and emotional expression in early infancy could help identify autism sooner. Its limits: it is a theoretical proposal, proves nothing by itself, uses deficit-based language, and is not a rule for every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om du ser att ditt barn rör sig, tittar eller uttrycker känslor på ett annat sätt, anteckna det och ta upp det med barnets vårdkontakt; du behöver inte vänta på skillnader i språket. Arbetet är en översikt av tidigare studier, inte ett nytt experiment. Det föreslår att skillnader i rörelse och känslouttryck tidigt i spädbarnstiden kan hjälpa till att upptäcka autism tidigare. Begränsningar: det är ett teoretiskt förslag, bevisar inget i sig, använder ett bristfokuserat språk och är ingen regel för alla autistiska personer.

title: Studying autism in rodent models: reconciling endophenotypes with comorbidities.
authors: Argyropoulos A, Gilby KL, Hill-Yardin EL
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) patients commonly exhibit a variety of comorbid traits including seizures, anxiety, aggressive behavior, gastrointestinal problems, motor deficits, abnormal sensory processing, and sleep disturbances for which the cause is unknown. These features impact negatively on daily life and can exaggerate the effects of the core diagnostic traits (social communication deficits and repetitive behaviors). Studying endophenotypes relevant to both core and comorbid features of ASD in rodent models can provide insight into biological mechanisms underlying these disorders. Here we review the characterization of endophenotypes in a selection of environmental, genetic, and behavioral rodent models of ASD. In addition to exhibiting core ASD-like behaviors, each of these animal models display one or more endophenotypes relevant to comorbid features including altered sensory processing, seizure susceptibility, anxiety-like behavior, and disturbed motor functions, suggesting that these traits are indicators of altered biological pathways in ASD. However, the study of behaviors paralleling comorbid traits in animal models of ASD is an emerging field and further research is needed to assess altered gastrointestinal function, aggression, and disorders of sleep onset across models. Future studies should include investigation of these endophenotypes in order to advance our understanding of the etiology of this complex disorder.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista, merece la pena prestar atención a cosas como el sueño, la ansiedad, las diferencias sensoriales, el malestar digestivo o la motricidad, porque pueden afectar mucho al día a día. Anótalas y coméntalas con su profesional de salud. Este trabajo es una revisión de estudios en modelos animales (roedores), no con personas. Sugiere que estos rasgos podrían estar ligados a vías biológicas alteradas. Sus límites: los resultados en roedores no se aplican sin más a las personas, y faltan estudios sobre digestión, agresividad y sueño.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person, it is worth noticing things like sleep, anxiety, sensory differences, stomach discomfort or movement, because they can affect daily life a lot. Jot them down and talk them through with their health professional. This is a review of studies in animal models (rodents), not in people. It suggests these traits may be linked to altered biological pathways. Its limits: rodent findings do not simply carry over to people, and more research is needed on digestion, aggression and sleep.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person lönar det sig att vara uppmärksam på saker som sömn, ångest, sensoriska skillnader, magbesvär eller motorik, eftersom de kan påverka vardagen mycket. Anteckna dem och ta upp dem med personens vårdgivare. Detta är en översikt av studier på djurmodeller (gnagare), inte på människor. Den antyder att ddessa drag kan hänga ihop med förändrade biologiska vägar. Begränsningar: resultat från gnagare gäller inte automatiskt för människor, och mer forskning behövs om mage, aggression och sömn.

title: A cognitive-behavioral intervention for emotion regulation in adults with high-functioning autism spectrum disorders: study protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
authors: Kuroda M, Kawakubo Y, Kuwabara H, Yokoyama K, Kano Y, Kamio Y
abstract: Background Adults with high-functioning autism spectrum disorders (ASD) have difficulties in social communication; thus, these individuals have trouble understanding the mental states of others. Recent research also suggests that adults with ASD are unable to understand their own mental states, which could lead to difficulties in emotion-regulation. Some studies have reported the efficacy of cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) in improving emotion-regulation among children with ASD. The current study will investigate the efficacy of group-based CBT for adults with ASD. Methods/design The study is a randomized, waitlist controlled, single-blinded trial. The participants will be 60 adults with ASD; 30 will be assigned to a CBT group and 30 to a waitlist control group. Primary outcome measures are the 20-item Toronto Alexithymia Scale, the Coping Inventory for Stressful Situations, the Motion Picture Mind-Reading task, and an ASD questionnaire. The secondary outcome measures are the Center for Epidemiological Studies Depression Scale, the World Health Organization Quality of Life Scale 26-item version, the Global Assessment of Functioning, State-trait Anxiety Inventory, Social Phobia and Anxiety Inventory, and Liebowitz Social Anxiety Scale. All will be administered during the pre- and post-intervention, and 12 week follow-up periods. The CBT group will receive group therapy over an 8 week period (one session per week) with each session lasting approximately 100 minutes. Group therapy will consist of four or five adults with ASD and two psychologists. We will be using visual materials for this program, mainly the Cognitive Affective Training kit. Discussion This trial will hopefully indicate the efficacy of group-based CBT for adults with high- functioning ASD. Trial registration This trial was registered in The University Hospital Medical Information Network Clinical Trials Registry No. UMIN000006236.

sheet.es: Si buscas apoyo para la regulación emocional de una persona autista adulta, esta línea de trabajo explora una terapia cognitivo-conductual en grupo con materiales visuales, pero aún no hay resultados que digan si ayuda. Evidencia: es el protocolo de un ensayo aleatorizado, no sus resultados; prevé 60 adultos autistas, 30 en el grupo de terapia y 30 en lista de espera, con sesiones semanales durante 8 semanas. Límites: no informa de efectos, y lo que funcione en un grupo no sirve igual para todas las personas. Conviene hablarlo con un profesional y respetar lo que la persona quiera probar.
sheet.en: If you are looking for support with emotion regulation for an autistic adult, this work explores group cognitive-behavioural therapy with visual materials, but it does not yet show whether it helps. Evidence: this is the protocol of a randomized trial, not its results; it plans 60 autistic adults, 30 in the therapy group and 30 on a waitlist, with weekly sessions over 8 weeks. Limits: it reports no effects, and what works in a group may not suit everyone. Talk it over with a professional and respect what the person wants to try.
sheet.sv: Om du söker stöd för känsloreglering hos en autistisk vuxen utforskar den här studien grupp-KBT med visuellt material, men den visar ännu inte om det hjälper. Evidens: detta är protokollet för en randomiserad studie, inte resultaten; den planerar 60 autistiska vuxna, 30 i terapigruppen och 30 på väntelista, med veckovisa sessioner under 8 veckor. Begränsningar: inga effekter redovisas, och det som fungerar i en grupp passar inte alla. Prata med en yrkesperson och respektera vad personen själv vill prova.

title: Comparison of white matter integrity between autism spectrum disorder subjects and typically developing individuals: a meta-analysis of diffusion tensor imaging tractography studies.
authors: Aoki Y, Abe O, Nippashi Y, Yamasue H
abstract: Background Aberrant brain connectivity, especially with long-distance underconnectivity, has been recognized as a candidate pathophysiology of autism spectrum disorders. However, a number of diffusion tensor imaging studies investigating people with autism spectrum disorders have yielded inconsistent results. Methods To test the long-distance underconnectivity hypothesis, we performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of diffusion tensor imaging studies in subjects with autism spectrum disorder. Diffusion tensor imaging studies comparing individuals with autism spectrum disorders with typically developing individuals were searched using MEDLINE, Web of Science and EMBASE from 1980 through 1 August 2012. Standardized mean differences were calculated as an effect size of the tracts. Results A comprehensive literature search identified 25 relevant diffusion tensor imaging studies comparing autism spectrum disorders and typical development with regions-of-interest methods. Among these, 14 studies examining regions of interest with suprathreshold sample sizes were included in the meta-analysis. A random-effects model demonstrated significant fractional anisotropy reductions in the corpus callosum (P = 0.023, n = 387 (autism spectrum disorders/typically developing individuals: 208/179)), left uncinate fasciculus (P = 0.011, n = 242 (117/125)), and left superior longitudinal fasciculus (P = 0.016, n = 182 (96/86)), and significant increases of mean diffusivity in the corpus callosum (P = 0.006, n = 254 (129/125)) and superior longitudinal fasciculus bilaterally (P = 0.031 and 0.011, left and right, respectively, n = 109 (51/58)), in subjects with autism spectrum disorders compared with typically developing individuals with no significant publication bias. Conclusion The current meta-analysis of diffusion tensor imaging studies in subjects with autism spectrum disorders emphasizes important roles of the superior longitudinal fasciculus, uncinate fasciculus, and corpus callosum in the pathophysiology of autism spectrum disorders and supports the long-distance underconnectivity hypothesis.

sheet.es: Este estudio no ofrece nada que hacer mañana por la mañana: describe diferencias medias en la estructura cerebral, no una pauta para cada persona. Puede servir para recordar que el cerebro autista se organiza de forma distinta, no peor. Es un metaanálisis de estudios de imagen cerebral (tensor de difusión) que comparó a personas autistas con personas de desarrollo típico; incluyó 14 estudios. Encontró diferencias en algunas vías de conexión, como el cuerpo calloso. Sus límites: son promedios de grupo, no sirven para valorar a una persona concreta, y no explican causas ni indican qué apoyos necesita alguien.
sheet.en: This study offers nothing to act on tomorrow morning: it describes average differences in brain structure, not guidance for any one person. It can be a reminder that autistic brains are organised differently, not worse. It is a meta-analysis of brain imaging (diffusion tensor) studies comparing autistic people with typically developing people; 14 studies were included. It found differences in some connecting pathways, such as the corpus callosum. Its limits: these are group averages, they cannot assess an individual, and they do not explain causes or show what support someone needs.
sheet.sv: Den här studien ger inget att göra i morgon bitti: den beskriver genomsnittliga skillnader i hjärnans struktur, inte råd för en enskild person. Den kan påminna om att autistiska hjärnor är organiserade annorlunda, inte sämre. Det är en metaanalys av hjärnavbildningsstudier (diffusionstensor) som jämförde autistiska personer med personer med typisk utveckling; 14 studier ingick. Den fann skillnader i vissa förbindelsebanor, till exempel hjärnbalken. Begränsningar: det rör sig om gruppmedelvärden, de kan inte bedöma en enskild person och förklarar varken orsaker eller vilket stöd någon behöver.

title: Mixed emotions: the contribution of alexithymia to the emotional symptoms of autism.
authors: Bird G, Cook R
abstract: It is widely accepted that autism is associated with disordered emotion processing and, in particular, with deficits of emotional reciprocity such as impaired emotion recognition and reduced empathy. However, a close examination of the literature reveals wide heterogeneity within the autistic population with respect to emotional competence. Here we argue that, where observed, emotional impairments are due to alexithymia-a condition that frequently co-occurs with autism-rather than a feature of autism per se. Alexithymia is a condition characterized by a reduced ability to identify and describe one's own emotion, but which results in reduced empathy and an impaired ability to recognize the emotions of others. We briefly review studies of emotion processing in alexithymia, and in autism, before describing a recent series of studies directly testing this 'alexithymia hypothesis'. If found to be correct, the alexithymia hypothesis has wide-reaching implications for the study of autism, and how we might best support subgroups of autistic individuals with, and without, accompanying alexithymia. Finally, we note the presence of elevated rates of alexithymia, and inconsistent reports of emotional impairments, in eating disorders, schizophrenia, substance abuse, Parkinson's Disease, multiple sclerosis and anxiety disorders. We speculate that examining the contribution of alexithymia to the emotional symptoms of these disorders may bear fruit in the same way that it is starting to do in autism.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista tiene dificultad para reconocer emociones, conviene preguntarse si también hay alexitimia, es decir, dificultad para identificar y describir las propias emociones. Puede ayudar ofrecer apoyos para poner nombre a lo que siente, como listas de palabras o imágenes. Este trabajo es una revisión teórica de estudios previos que plantea la "hipótesis de la alexitimia": las diferencias emocionales se deberían a la alexitimia que a menudo coexiste con el autismo, y no al autismo en sí. Sus límites: es una propuesta que aún debe confirmarse y no vale para todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person finds it hard to recognise emotions, it may be worth considering whether alexithymia is also present, meaning difficulty identifying and describing one's own feelings. Supports for naming feelings, such as word lists or pictures, may help. This paper is a theoretical review of earlier studies that puts forward the "alexithymia hypothesis": emotional differences may come from alexithymia, which often co-occurs with autism, rather than from autism itself. Its limits: it is a proposal that still needs confirming, and it does not apply to every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person har svårt att känna igen känslor kan det vara värt att fundera på om alexitymi också finns med, alltså svårigheter att identifiera och beskriva sina egna känslor. Stöd för att sätta ord på känslor, som ordlistor eller bilder, kan hjälpa. Artikeln är en teoretisk översikt av tidigare studier som lägger fram "alexitymihypotesen": känslomässiga skillnader kan bero på alexitymi, som ofta förekommer tillsammans med autism, snarare än på autismen i sig. Begränsningar: det är ett förslag som ännu behöver bekräftas och gäller inte alla autistiska personer.

title: Group-based social skills interventions for adolescents with higher-functioning autism spectrum disorder: a review and looking to the future.
authors: McMahon CM, Lerner MD, Britton N
abstract: In this paper, we synthesize the current literature on group-based social skills interventions (GSSIs) for adolescents (ages 10-20 years) with higher-functioning autism spectrum disorder and identify key concepts that should be addressed in future research on GSSIs. We consider the research participants, the intervention, the assessment of the intervention, and the research methodology and results to be integral and interconnected components of the GSSI literature, and we review each of these components respectively. Participant characteristics (eg, age, IQ, sex) and intervention characteristics (eg, targeted social skills, teaching strategies, duration and intensity) vary considerably across GSSIs; future research should evaluate whether participant and intervention characteristics mediate/moderate intervention efficacy. Multiple assessments (eg, parent-report, child-report, social cognitive assessments) are used to evaluate the efficacy of GSSIs; future research should be aware of the limitations of current measurement approaches and employ more accurate, sensitive, and comprehensive measurement approaches. Results of GSSIs are largely inconclusive, with few consistent findings across studies (eg, high parent and child satisfaction with the intervention); future research should employ more rigorous methodological standards for evaluating efficacy. A better understanding of these components in the current GSSI literature and a more sophisticated and rigorous analysis of these components in future research will lend clarity to key questions regarding the efficacy of GSSIs for individuals with autism spectrum disorder.

sheet.es: Si valoran un grupo de habilidades sociales para un adolescente autista, pregúntenle qué le gustaría practicar y si le apetece ir, y revisen qué se enseña y cómo. Es una revisión de la literatura sobre estos grupos en adolescentes de 10-20 años con autismo de los llamados 'mayor funcionamiento'. Encontró que los programas varían mucho y los resultados son en gran parte no concluyentes; lo más constante fue la alta satisfacción de familias y adolescentes. Límites: no prueba que los grupos funcionen ni sirve como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If you are considering a social skills group for an autistic teenager, ask what they would like to practise and whether they want to go, and check what is taught and how. This is a review of the literature on such groups for adolescents aged 10-20 with autism described as higher-functioning. It found that programmes vary widely and results are largely inconclusive; the most consistent finding was high satisfaction among parents and teens. Limits: it does not show that groups work, and it is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om ni överväger en social färdighetsgrupp för en autistisk tonåring: fråga vad hen vill öva på och om hen vill gå, och ta reda på vad som lärs ut och hur. Detta är en översikt av forskning om sådana grupper för ungdomar i åldern 10-20 år med autism som beskrivs som högre funktionsnivå. Programmen varierar mycket och resultaten är till stor del osäkra; det mest konsekventa fyndet var hög nöjdhet hos föräldrar och ungdomar. Begränsningar: den visar inte att grupperna fungerar och gäller inte som regel för varje person.

title: Global prevalence of autism and other pervasive developmental disorders.
authors: Elsabbagh M, Divan G, Koh YJ, Kim YS, Kauchali S, Marcín C, Montiel-Nava C, Patel V, Paula CS, Wang C, Yasamy MT, Fombonne E
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: We provide a systematic review of epidemiological surveys of autistic disorder and pervasive developmental disorders (PDDs) worldwide. A secondary aim was to consider the possible impact of geographic, cultural/ethnic, and socioeconomic factors on prevalence estimates and on clinical presentation of PDD. Based on the evidence reviewed, the median of prevalence estimates of autism spectrum disorders was 62/10 000. While existing estimates are variable, the evidence reviewed does not support differences in PDD prevalence by geographic region nor of a strong impact of ethnic/cultural or socioeconomic factors. However, power to detect such effects is seriously limited in existing data sets, particularly in low-income countries. While it is clear that prevalence estimates have increased over time and these vary in different neighboring and distant regions, these findings most likely represent broadening of the diagnostic concets, diagnostic switching from other developmental disabilities to PDD, service availability, and awareness of autistic spectrum disorders in both the lay and professional public. The lack of evidence from the majority of the world's population suggests a critical need for further research and capacity building in low- and middle-income countries.

sheet.es: Si te preocupa que el autismo sea "más común" en unos lugares que en otros, esta revisión sugiere no sacar esa conclusión: no encontró diferencias claras por región, cultura o nivel socioeconómico. Es una revisión sistemática de encuestas epidemiológicas de todo el mundo. La mediana de las estimaciones fue 62/10 000. El aumento a lo largo del tiempo probablemente refleja criterios diagnósticos más amplios, más servicios y más conocimiento. Límites: hay muy pocos datos de países de ingresos bajos y medios, así que no sirve para predecir nada sobre una persona concreta.
sheet.en: If you wonder whether autism is "more common" in some places than others, this review suggests not drawing that conclusion: it found no clear differences by region, culture or socioeconomic level. It is a systematic review of epidemiological surveys from around the world. The median of the estimates was 62/10 000. The rise over time most likely reflects broader diagnostic concepts, more services and more awareness. Limits: there is very little data from low- and middle-income countries, and it says nothing about any one person.
sheet.sv: Om du undrar om autism är "vanligare" på vissa platser än andra, tyder den här översikten på att man inte bör dra den slutsatsen: den fann inga tydliga skillnader mellan regioner, kulturer eller socioekonomisk nivå. Det är en systematisk översikt av epidemiologiska enkäter från hela världen. Medianen av uppskattningarna var 62/10 000. Ökningen över tid speglar sannolikt vidare diagnostiska begrepp, fler tjänster och större kännedom. Begränsningar: det finns mycket lite data från låg- och medelinkomstländer, och resultaten säger inget om en enskild person.

title: Thimerosal exposure and the role of sulfation chemistry and thiol availability in autism.
authors: Kern JK, Haley BE, Geier DA, Sykes LK, King PG, Geier MR
journal: International journal of environmental research and public health
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurological disorder in which a significant number of the children experience a developmental regression characterized by a loss of previously acquired skills and abilities. Typically reported are losses of verbal, nonverbal, and social abilities. Several recent studies suggest that children diagnosed with an ASD have abnormal sulfation chemistry, limited thiol availability, and decreased glutathione (GSH) reserve capacity, resulting in a compromised oxidation/reduction (redox) and detoxification capacity. Research indicates that the availability of thiols, particularly GSH, can influence the effects of thimerosal (TM) and other mercury (Hg) compounds. TM is an organomercurial compound (49.55% Hg by weight) that has been, and continues to be, used as a preservative in many childhood vaccines, particularly in developing countries. Thiol-modulating mechanisms affecting the cytotoxicity of TM have been identified. Importantly, the emergence of ASD symptoms post-6 months of age temporally follows the administration of many childhood vaccines. The purpose of the present critical review is provide mechanistic insight regarding how limited thiol availability, abnormal sulfation chemistry, and decreased GSH reserve capacity in children with an ASD could make them more susceptible to the toxic effects of TM routinely administered as part of mandated childhood immunization schedules.

sheet.es: Lo práctico: esta revisión no ofrece ninguna medida que usted deba tomar mañana. Si le preocupan las vacunas o la salud de su hijo, hable con su pediatra o clínico, que es quien decide sobre temas médicos. Sobre la evidencia: es una revisión crítica que reúne estudios previos sobre química del azufre, tioles y glutatión en niños con diagnóstico de autismo, y propone una explicación posible sobre el timerosal. Límites: es una hipótesis de mecanismos, no una prueba; sugiere una relación temporal, que no demuestra causa, y no debe tomarse como regla para todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: Practical takeaway: this review offers nothing you need to act on tomorrow. If you have worries about vaccines or your child's health, talk with your paediatrician or clinician, who is the right person for medical decisions. On the evidence: it is a critical review gathering earlier studies on sulfation chemistry, thiols and glutathione in children diagnosed with autism, and it proposes a possible explanation involving thimerosal. Limits: it is a hypothesis about mechanisms, not proof; it points to a timing link, which does not show cause, and it should not be treated as a rule for every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Praktiskt: den här översikten ger inget du behöver göra i morgon. Om du oroar dig för vacciner eller ditt barns hälsa, prata med barnläkare eller annan klinisk personal, som fattar medicinska beslut. Om evidensen: det är en kritisk översikt som samlar tidigare studier om svavelkemi, tioler och glutation hos barn med autismdiagnos och föreslår en möjlig förklaring kopplad till tiomersal. Begränsningar: det är en hypotes om mekanismer, inte ett bevis; den pekar på ett tidssamband, vilket inte visar orsak, och den ska inte ses som en regel för alla autistiska personer.

title: Increased glutamate and homocysteine and decreased glutamine levels in autism: a review and strategies for future studies of amino acids in autism.
authors: Ghanizadeh A
abstract: There are many reports about the significant roles of some amino acids in neurobiology and treatment of autism. This is a critical review of amino acids levels in autism. No published review article about the level of amino acids in autism was found. The levels of glutamate and homocystein are increased in autism while the levels of glutamine and tryptophan are decreased. Findings regarding the plasma levels of taurine and lysine are controversial. The urinary levels of homocysteine and essential amino acids in both the untreated and treated autistic children are significantly less than those in the controls. The current literature suffers from many methodological shortcomings which needed to be considered in future studies. Some of them are age, gender, developmental level, autism symptoms severity, type of autism spectrum disorders, medical comorbidities, intelligent quotient, diet, concomitant medications, body mass index, and technical method of assessment of amino acids.

sheet.es: Esta revisión no ofrece nada que cambiar mañana en casa: no sirve para decidir alimentación ni suplementos. Si tienes dudas sobre la dieta o la salud de una persona autista, coméntalas con su pediatra o su clínico. La evidencia es una revisión crítica de la literatura sobre aminoácidos en el autismo; los autores señalan que no encontraron otra revisión previa. Indica que el glutamato y la homocisteína están aumentados, y la glutamina y el triptófano disminuidos, pero que los resultados sobre taurina y lisina son controvertidos. Sus límites: la literatura tiene muchas deficiencias metodológicas, como no considerar la edad, el sexo, la dieta o la medicación, así que no vale como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: This review gives nothing to change at home tomorrow: it should not guide food or supplement choices. If you have questions about an autistic person's diet or health, talk with their paediatrician or clinician. The evidence is a critical review of the literature on amino acids in autism; the authors say they found no earlier review. It reports glutamate and homocysteine as increased, and glutamine and tryptophan as decreased, while findings on taurine and lysine are controversial. Its limits: the research has many methodological shortcomings, such as not accounting for age, gender, diet or medication, so it is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Den här översikten ger inget att ändra hemma i morgon: den bör inte styra val av mat eller kosttillskott. Har du frågor om en autistisk persons kost eller hälsa, prata med barnläkare eller annan klinisk personal. Underlaget är en kritisk översikt av litteraturen om aminosyror vid autism; författarna säger att de inte hittade någon tidigare översikt. Den rapporterar att glutamat och homocystein är förhöjda och glutamin och tryptofan sänkta, medan resultaten om taurin och lysin är motstridiga. Begränsningar: forskningen har många metodbrister, till exempel att ålder, kön, kost eller medicinering inte beaktas, så den är ingen regel för varje person.

title: Caregiver-mediated approaches to managing challenging behaviors in children with autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Grofer Klinger L, Ence W, Meyer A
abstract: A significant proportion of children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) are referred to mental health centers due to the presence of challenging behaviors. Because challenging behaviors in children and adolescents with ASD often result from underlying social and communication difficulties and comorbid anxiety, traditional caregiver-mediated behavior intervention techniques developed for children with disruptive behavior disorders may need to be adapted for this population. Behavioral interventions that target communication skills, social skills, anxiety, and sensory responsiveness in children with ASD may be needed. Notably, while best practice necessitates the involvement of caregivers in treating children and adolescents with ASD, few randomized control studies have examined the effectiveness of caregiver-implemented interventions in reducing challenging behaviors. This review summarizes the current literature with regard to caregiver-mediated behavioral interventions for children with ASD, and suggests areas for intervention development and research.

sheet.es: Cuando una conducta te preocupe, pregúntate primero qué necesita comunicar la niña o el niño: puede haber dificultades de comunicación, ansiedad o sensibilidad sensorial detrás. Apoyar la comunicación, las habilidades sociales y la calma suele ser más útil que aplicar técnicas pensadas para otros niños. Esta revisión resume estudios previos sobre intervenciones guiadas por cuidadores en niñez autista. Señala que pocos ensayos aleatorizados han comprobado si funcionan para reducir estas conductas. Por eso no es una regla para todas las personas: conviene consultar con profesionales que conozcan a tu hijo o hija.
sheet.en: When a behavior worries you, first ask what the child may be trying to communicate: communication difficulties, anxiety or sensory responses may sit behind it. Supporting communication, social skills and calm is likely more useful than techniques designed for other children. This review summarizes earlier studies on caregiver-led approaches for autistic children. It notes that few randomized controlled studies have tested whether they reduce these behaviors. So it is not a rule for every person: it is worth talking with professionals who know your child.
sheet.sv: När ett beteende oroar dig, fråga först vad barnet kan försöka förmedla: bakom det kan det finnas kommunikationssvårigheter, ångest eller sensoriska reaktioner. Att stödja kommunikation, social förmåga och lugn är troligen mer användbart än metoder som utformats för andra barn. Den här översikten sammanfattar tidigare studier om föräldra- och vårdnadshavarledda insatser för autistiska barn. Den konstaterar att få randomiserade kontrollerade studier har prövat om de minskar sådana beteenden. Det är alltså ingen regel för alla: prata gärna med yrkespersoner som känner ditt barn.

title: TEACCH-based group social skills training for children with high-functioning autism: a pilot randomized controlled trial.
authors: Ichikawa K, Takahashi Y, Ando M, Anme T, Ishizaki T, Yamaguchi H, Nakayama T
abstract: Background Although social skills training programs for people with high-functioning autism (HFA) are widely practiced, the standardization of curricula, the examination of clinical effectiveness, and the evaluation of the feasibility of future trials have yet to be done in Asian countries. To compensate for this problem, a Japanese pilot randomized controlled trial (RCT) of the Treatment and Education of Autistic and Related Communication Handicapped Children (TEACCH)-based group social skills training for children with HFA and their mothers was conducted. Methods Eleven children with HFA, aged 5-6 years, and their mothers were randomly assigned to the TEACCH program (n=5) or a waiting-list control group (n=6). The program involved comprehensive group intervention and featured weekly 2-hour sessions, totaling 20 sessions over six months. The adaptive behaviors and social reciprocity of the children, parenting stress, and parent-child interactions were assessed using the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ), Parenting Stress Index (PSI), Beck depression inventory-II (BDI-II), and Interaction Rating Scale (IRS). Results Through this pilot trial, the intervention and evaluation of the program has been shaped. There were no dropouts from the program and the mothers' satisfaction was high. The outcome measurements improved more in the program group than in the control group, with moderate effect sizes (SDQ, 0.71; PSI, 0.58; BDI-II, 0.40; and IRS, 0.69). This pilot trial also implied that this program is more beneficial for high IQ children and mothers with low stress than for those who are not. Conclusion We have standardized the TEACCH program, confirmed the feasibility of a future trial, and successfully estimated the positive effect size. These findings will contribute to a larger trial in the future and to forthcoming systematic reviews with meta-analyses. Trial registration UMIN000004560.

sheet.es: Si piensa en un programa de habilidades sociales en grupo, conviene saber que este estudio piloto japonés probó uno basado en TEACCH que incluía a niñas y niños autistas y a sus madres, y que las familias lo valoraron bien. Fue un ensayo aleatorizado piloto con 11 niños de 5-6 años y sus madres: 5 en el programa y 6 en lista de espera. No hubo abandonos y la satisfacción de las madres fue alta. Sus límites: la muestra es muy pequeña, solo participaron madres y los autores sugieren que podría beneficiar más a quienes tienen CI alto y menos estrés. No es una regla para todas las personas; sirve para conversar con el equipo profesional.
sheet.en: If you are considering a group social skills programme, this Japanese pilot study tested a TEACCH-based one for autistic children and their mothers, and families rated it well. It was a pilot randomized controlled trial with 11 children aged 5-6 and their mothers: 5 joined the programme and 6 were on a waiting list. Nobody dropped out and the mothers' satisfaction was high. Limits: the sample is very small, only mothers took part, and the authors suggest it may suit children with high IQ and mothers with lower stress better. It is not a rule for every person; use it as a starting point for talking with your professional team.
sheet.sv: Om ni funderar på ett socialt färdighetsprogram i grupp har denna japanska pilotstudie testat ett TEACCH-baserat program för autistiska barn och deras mammor, och familjerna var nöjda. Det var en randomiserad kontrollerad pilotstudie med 11 barn i åldern 5-6 år och deras mammor: 5 deltog i programmet och 6 stod på väntelista. Ingen hoppade av och mammornas nöjdhet var hög. Begränsningar: urvalet är mycket litet, bara mammor deltog och forskarna antyder att programmet kan passa barn med hög IQ och mammor med mindre stress bättre. Det är ingen regel för alla; använd det som underlag för samtal med ert team.

title: Management of children with autism spectrum disorder in the dental setting: concerns, behavioural approaches and recommendations.
authors: Delli K, Reichart PA, Bornstein MM, Livas C
journal: Medicina oral, patologia oral y cirugia bucal
abstract: Objectives This article reviews the present literature on the issues encountered while coping with children with autistic spectrum disorder from the dental perspective. The autistic patient profile and external factors affecting the oral health status of this patient population are discussed upon the existing body of evidence. Material and methods The MEDLINE database was searched using the terms 'Autistic Disorder', 'Behaviour Control/methods', 'Child', 'Dental care for disabled', 'Education', 'Oral Health', and 'Pediatric Dentistry' to locate related articles published up to January 2013. Results Most of the relevant studies indicate poor oral hygiene whereas they are inconclusive regarding the caries incidence in autistic individuals. Undergraduate dental education appears to determine the competence of dental professionals to treat developmentally disabled children and account partly for compromised access to dental care. Dental management of an autistic child requires in-depth understanding of the background of the autism and available behavioural guidance theories. The dental professional should be flexible to modify the treatment approach according to the individual patient needs.

sheet.es: Antes de la cita, cuenta al equipo dental cómo es tu hijo o hija: qué le tranquiliza, qué le agobia y cómo se comunica. Pide que adapten el trato a sus necesidades. Esta es una revisión de la bibliografía publicada hasta enero de 2013, buscada en MEDLINE. Indica que la higiene bucal suele ser deficiente, pero no aclara si hay más caries. También señala que la formación de los dentistas influye en el acceso a la atención. Es una revisión, no una prueba de un método, y no describe a cada persona autista. Sus conclusiones no valen como regla general.
sheet.en: Before the appointment, tell the dental team how your child communicates, what calms them and what overwhelms them. Ask them to adapt their approach to your child's needs. This is a review of published literature up to January 2013, searched in MEDLINE. It found that oral hygiene is often poor, but it is inconclusive on whether cavities are more common. It also notes that dentists' training affects access to care. It is a review, not a test of one method, and it cannot describe every autistic person. Its conclusions are not a rule for everyone.
sheet.sv: Berätta för tandvårdsteamet före besöket hur ditt barn kommunicerar, vad som lugnar och vad som blir överväldigande. Be dem anpassa sitt sätt efter barnets behov. Detta är en översikt av litteratur publicerad till och med januari 2013, sökt i MEDLINE. Den visar att munhygienen ofta är dålig, men är oklar om hål i tänderna är vanligare. Den noterar också att tandläkares utbildning påverkar tillgången till vård. Det är en översikt, inte ett test av en enskild metod, och den kan inte beskriva varje autistisk person. Slutsatserna är ingen regel för alla.

title: Non-specialist psychosocial interventions for children and adolescents with intellectual disability or lower-functioning autism spectrum disorders: a systematic review.
authors: Reichow B, Servili C, Yasamy MT, Barbui C, Saxena S
abstract: Background The development of effective treatments for use by non-specialists is listed among the top research priorities for improving the lives of people with mental illness worldwide. The purpose of this review is to appraise which interventions for children with intellectual disabilities or lower-functioning autism spectrum disorders delivered by non-specialist care providers in community settings produce benefits when compared to either a no-treatment control group or treatment-as-usual comparator. Methods and findings We systematically searched electronic databases through 24 June 2013 to locate prospective controlled studies of psychosocial interventions delivered by non-specialist providers to children with intellectual disabilities or lower-functioning autism spectrum disorders. We screened 234 full papers, of which 34 articles describing 29 studies involving 1,305 participants were included. A majority of the studies included children exclusively with a diagnosis of lower-functioning autism spectrum disorders (15 of 29, 52%). Fifteen of twenty-nine studies (52%) were randomized controlled trials and just under half of all effect sizes (29 of 59, 49%) were greater than 0.50, of which 18 (62%) were statistically significant. For behavior analytic interventions, the best outcomes were shown for development and daily skills; cognitive rehabilitation, training, and support interventions were found to be most effective for improving developmental outcomes, and parent training interventions to be most effective for improving developmental, behavioral, and family outcomes. We also conducted additional subgroup analyses using harvest plots. Limitations include the studies' potential for performance bias and that few were conducted in lower- and middle-income countries. Conclusions The findings of this review support the delivery of psychosocial interventions by non-specialist providers to children who have intellectual disabilities or lower-functioning autism spectrum disorders. Given the scarcity of specialists in many low-resource settings, including many lower- and middle-income countries, these findings may provide guidance for scale-up efforts for improving outcomes for children with developmental disorders or lower-functioning autism spectrum disorders. Protocol registration PROSPERO CRD42012002641

sheet.es: Si no tienes acceso a especialistas, no estás sin opciones: los apoyos aplicados por familias, docentes o personal comunitario formado pueden ayudar. Pide a tu servicio local formación para madres y padres, o apoyo práctico para habilidades cotidianas, y adáptalo al ritmo y los intereses de tu hijo o hija. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 29 estudios con 1.305 niños y adolescentes autistas con altas necesidades de apoyo o con discapacidad intelectual; la formación a familias mostró beneficios en desarrollo, conducta y bienestar familiar. Límites: muchos estudios podían tener sesgos, pocos se hicieron en países de ingresos bajos y medios, y los resultados no se aplican igual a cada persona.
sheet.en: If specialists are hard to reach, you still have options: support delivered by trained parents, teachers or community workers can help. Ask your local service about parent training or practical support for everyday skills, and shape it around your child's pace and interests. This systematic review pooled 29 studies with 1,305 autistic children and teens with high support needs or with intellectual disability; parent training showed benefits for development, behaviour and family wellbeing. Limits: many studies risked bias, few were done in low- and middle-income countries, and results won't apply the same way to every person.
sheet.sv: Om specialister är svåra att nå finns ändå möjligheter: stöd som ges av utbildade föräldrar, lärare eller personal i närmiljön kan hjälpa. Fråga din lokala verksamhet om föräldrautbildning eller praktiskt stöd för vardagsfärdigheter, och anpassa det efter ditt barns tempo och intressen. Denna systematiska översikt samlade 29 studier med 1 305 autistiska barn och unga med stora stödbehov eller med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning; föräldrautbildning gav fördelar för utveckling, beteende och familjens välmående. Begränsningar: många studier riskerade snedvridning, få gjordes i låg- och medelinkomstländer, och resultaten gäller inte likadant för alla.

title: Systematic review of the properties of tools used to measure outcomes in anxiety intervention studies for children with autism spectrum disorders.
authors: Wigham S, McConachie H
abstract: Background Evidence about relevant outcomes is required in the evaluation of clinical interventions for children with autism spectrum disorders (ASD). However, to date, the variety of outcome measurement tools being used, and lack of knowledge about the measurement properties of some, compromise conclusions regarding the most effective interventions. Objectives This two-stage systematic review aimed to identify the tools used in studies evaluating interventions for anxiety for high-functioning children with ASD in middle childhood, and then to evaluate the tools for their appropriateness and measurement properties. Methods Electronic databases including Medline, PsychInfo, Embase, and the Cochrane database and registers were searched for anxiety intervention studies for children with ASD in middle childhood. Articles examining the measurement properties of the tools used were then searched for using a methodological filter in PubMed, and the quality of the papers evaluated using the COSMIN checklist. Results Ten intervention studies were identified in which six tools measuring anxiety and one of overall symptom change were used as primary outcomes. One further tool was included as it is recommended for standard use in UK children's mental health services. Sixty three articles on the properties of the tools were evaluated for the quality of evidence, and the quality of the measurement properties of each tool was summarised. Conclusions Overall three questionnaires were found robust in their measurement properties, the Spence Children's Anxiety Scale, its revised version - the Revised Children's Anxiety and Depression Scale, and also the Screen for Child Anxiety Related Emotional Disorders. Crucially the articles on measurement properties provided almost no evidence on responsiveness to change, nor on the validity of use of the tools for evaluation of interventions for children with ASD. Prospero registration number CRD42012002684.

sheet.es: Si quiere seguir la ansiedad de un niño autista, conviene preguntar al profesional qué cuestionario usa y por qué. Esta revisión sistemática encontró diez estudios de intervención sobre ansiedad en niños autistas de la infancia media y evaluó las herramientas de medida. Tres cuestionarios resultaron sólidos: la Spence Children's Anxiety Scale, su versión revisada (Revised Children's Anxiety and Depression Scale) y la Screen for Child Anxiety Related Emotional Disorders. Limitación: casi no había pruebas sobre si detectan cambios, ni sobre su validez para evaluar intervenciones en niños autistas. Estos resultados no valen igual para cada persona.
sheet.en: If you want to track an autistic child's anxiety, it helps to ask the professional which questionnaire they use and why. This systematic review found ten intervention studies on anxiety in autistic children in middle childhood and evaluated the measurement tools. Three questionnaires were robust: the Spence Children's Anxiety Scale, its revised version (the Revised Children's Anxiety and Depression Scale), and the Screen for Child Anxiety Related Emotional Disorders. Limitation: there was almost no evidence on whether they detect change, or on their validity for evaluating interventions for autistic children. Findings may not fit every person.
sheet.sv: Om du vill följa ett autistiskt barns oro kan du fråga yrkespersonen vilket frågeformulär som används och varför. Denna systematiska översikt hittade tio interventionsstudier om ångest hos autistiska barn i mellanbarndomen och granskade mätverktygen. Tre frågeformulär var robusta: Spence Children's Anxiety Scale, dess reviderade version (Revised Children's Anxiety and Depression Scale) och Screen for Child Anxiety Related Emotional Disorders. Begränsning: det fanns nästan inga belägg för om de fångar förändring, eller för hur giltiga de är när insatser utvärderas för autistiska barn. Resultaten gäller inte alla på samma sätt.

title: Reaching and grasping in autism spectrum disorder: a review of recent literature.
authors: Sacrey LA, Germani T, Bryson SE, Zwaigenbaum L
abstract: Impairments in motor functioning, which, until recently, have rarely been a primary focus in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) research, may play a key role in the early expression of biological vulnerability and be associated with key social-communication deficits. This review summarizes current knowledge of motor behavior in ASD, focusing specifically on reaching and grasping. Convergent data across the lifespan indicate that impairments to reaching and grasping emerge early in life, affect the planning and execution of motor programs, and may be impacted by additional impairments to sensory control of motor behavior. The relationship between motor impairments and diagnostic outcomes will be discussed.

sheet.es: Si notas que una persona autista tiene dificultad para alcanzar o agarrar objetos, puede ser una diferencia motora y no falta de interés o de esfuerzo. Ofrece objetos fáciles de sujetar, da tiempo extra y evita apresurar. Esta es una revisión de la bibliografía reciente sobre alcanzar y agarrar en el autismo; indica que estas diferencias aparecen pronto en la vida, afectan a la planificación y ejecución del movimiento y pueden relacionarse con el control sensorial. Sus límites: es un resumen de otros estudios, usa un enfoque de déficits y no sirve como regla para cada persona. Si te preocupa, consulta a un profesional de terapia ocupacional o de salud.
sheet.en: If an autistic person has difficulty reaching for or grasping objects, it may be a motor difference rather than lack of interest or effort. Offer items that are easy to hold, allow extra time and avoid rushing. This is a review of recent literature on reaching and grasping in autism; it reports that these differences appear early in life, affect how movements are planned and carried out, and may relate to sensory control of movement. Its limits: it summarises other studies, uses a deficit-focused framing and is not a rule for every person. If you are concerned, talk to an occupational therapist or health professional.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person har svårt att nå eller greppa föremål kan det vara en motorisk skillnad snarare än bristande intresse eller ansträngning. Erbjud saker som är lätta att hålla i, ge extra tid och undvik att stressa. Detta är en översikt av nyare litteratur om att nå och greppa vid autism. Den beskriver att skillnaderna framträder tidigt i livet, påverkar planering och utförande av rörelser och kan hänga ihop med sensorisk kontroll av rörelse. Begränsningar: den sammanfattar andra studier, utgår från ett bristperspektiv och gäller inte som regel för varje person. Vid oro, tala med en arbetsterapeut eller annan vårdpersonal.

title: Auditory processing in fragile x syndrome.
authors: Rotschafer SE, Razak KA
abstract: Fragile X syndrome (FXS) is an inherited form of intellectual disability and autism. Among other symptoms, FXS patients demonstrate abnormalities in sensory processing and communication. Clinical, behavioral, and electrophysiological studies consistently show auditory hypersensitivity in humans with FXS. Consistent with observations in humans, the Fmr1 KO mouse model of FXS also shows evidence of altered auditory processing and communication deficiencies. A well-known and commonly used phenotype in pre-clinical studies of FXS is audiogenic seizures. In addition, increased acoustic startle response is seen in the Fmr1 KO mice. In vivo electrophysiological recordings indicate hyper-excitable responses, broader frequency tuning, and abnormal spectrotemporal processing in primary auditory cortex of Fmr1 KO mice. Thus, auditory hyper-excitability is a robust, reliable, and translatable biomarker in Fmr1 KO mice. Abnormal auditory evoked responses have been used as outcome measures to test therapeutics in FXS patients. Given that similarly abnormal responses are present in Fmr1 KO mice suggests that cellular mechanisms can be addressed. Sensory cortical deficits are relatively more tractable from a mechanistic perspective than more complex social behaviors that are typically studied in autism and FXS. The focus of this review is to bring together clinical, functional, and structural studies in humans with electrophysiological and behavioral studies in mice to make the case that auditory hypersensitivity provides a unique opportunity to integrate molecular, cellular, circuit level studies with behavioral outcomes in the search for therapeutics for FXS and other autism spectrum disorders.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista con síndrome del X frágil reacciona con fuerza a ciertos sonidos, conviene tomarlo en serio: puede ser una diferencia sensorial real. Mañana puedes probar a reducir el ruido, ofrecer pausas en lugares tranquilos y dejar que use protección auditiva si ella lo desea. La evidencia es una revisión que reúne estudios clínicos y de conducta en personas con síndrome del X frágil y estudios en un modelo de ratón. Sus límites: gran parte del trabajo es con ratones y no prueba qué ayuda a cada persona. Las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If an autistic person with fragile X syndrome reacts strongly to certain sounds, take it seriously: it may be a real sensory difference. Tomorrow you could try lowering background noise, offering breaks in quiet places, and letting them use ear protection if they want it. The evidence is a review bringing together clinical and behavioral studies in people with fragile X syndrome and studies in a mouse model. Its limits: much of the work is in mice, and it does not show what helps each individual person. Medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person med fragilt X-syndrom reagerar starkt på vissa ljud, ta det på allvar: det kan vara en verklig sensorisk skillnad. I morgon kan du pröva att sänka bakgrundsljud, erbjuda pauser på tysta platser och låta personen använda hörselskydd om hen vill. Underlaget är en översikt som sammanställer kliniska studier och beteendestudier på personer med fragilt X-syndrom samt studier på en musmodell. Begränsningar: mycket av arbetet är gjort på möss och visar inte vad som hjälper varje enskild person. Medicinska beslut hör hemma hos en kliniker.

title: Environmental toxicants and autism spectrum disorders: a systematic review.
authors: Rossignol DA, Genuis SJ, Frye RE
abstract: Although the involvement of genetic abnormalities in autism spectrum disorders (ASD) is well-accepted, recent studies point to an equal contribution by environmental factors, particularly environmental toxicants. However, these toxicant-related studies in ASD have not been systematically reviewed to date. Therefore, we compiled publications investigating potential associations between environmental toxicants and ASD and arranged these publications into the following three categories: (a) studies examining estimated toxicant exposures in the environment during the preconceptional, gestational and early childhood periods; (b) studies investigating biomarkers of toxicants; and (c) studies examining potential genetic susceptibilities to toxicants. A literature search of nine electronic scientific databases through November 2013 was performed. In the first category examining ASD risk and estimated toxicant exposures in the environment, the majority of studies (34/37; 92%) reported an association. Most of these studies were retrospective case-control, ecological or prospective cohort studies, although a few had weaker study designs (for example, case reports or series). Toxicants implicated in ASD included pesticides, phthalates, polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), solvents, toxic waste sites, air pollutants and heavy metals, with the strongest evidence found for air pollutants and pesticides. Gestational exposure to methylmercury (through fish exposure, one study) and childhood exposure to pollutants in water supplies (two studies) were not found to be associated with ASD risk. In the second category of studies investigating biomarkers of toxicants and ASD, a large number was dedicated to examining heavy metals. Such studies demonstrated mixed findings, with only 19 of 40 (47%) case-control studies reporting higher concentrations of heavy metals in blood, urine, hair, brain or teeth of children with ASD compared with controls. Other biomarker studies reported that solvent, phthalate and pesticide levels were associated with ASD, whereas PCB studies were mixed. Seven studies reported a relationship between autism severity and heavy metal biomarkers, suggesting evidence of a dose-effect relationship. Overall, the evidence linking biomarkers of toxicants with ASD (the second category) was weaker compared with the evidence associating estimated exposures to toxicants in the environment and ASD risk (the first category) because many of the biomarker studies contained small sample sizes and the relationships between biomarkers and ASD were inconsistent across studies. Regarding the third category of studies investigating potential genetic susceptibilities to toxicants, 10 unique studies examined polymorphisms in genes associated with increased susceptibilities to toxicants, with 8 studies reporting that such polymorphisms were more common in ASD individuals (or their mothers, 1 study) compared with controls (one study examined multiple polymorphisms). Genes implicated in these studies included paraoxonase (PON1, three of five studies), glutathione S-transferase (GSTM1 and GSTP1, three of four studies), δ-aminolevulinic acid dehydratase (one study), SLC11A3 (one study) and the metal regulatory transcription factor 1 (one of two studies). Notably, many of the reviewed studies had significant limitations, including lack of replication, limited sample sizes, retrospective design, recall and publication biases, inadequate matching of cases and controls, and the use of nonstandard tools to diagnose ASD. The findings of this review suggest that the etiology of ASD may involve, at least in a subset of children, complex interactions between genetic factors and certain environmental toxicants that may act synergistically or in parallel during critical periods of neurodevelopment, in a manner that increases the likelihood of developing ASD. Because of the limitations of many of the reviewed studies, additional high-quality epidemiological studies concerning environmental toxicants and ASD are warranted to confirm and clarify many of these findings.

sheet.es: Para mañana: no hay nada que su familia deba cambiar por culpa de este estudio. Si le preocupa la exposición a contaminantes, como pesticidas o aire contaminado, puede comentarlo con el equipo pediátrico o de salud. Es una revisión sistemática de estudios publicados hasta noviembre de 2013 sobre tóxicos ambientales y autismo. Halló asociaciones en 34 de 37 estudios de exposición, con la evidencia más fuerte para contaminantes del aire y pesticidas. Sus límites: muchos estudios eran pequeños o retrospectivos, los resultados con biomarcadores fueron irregulares y asociación no significa causa. No explica el autismo de cada persona, y las autoras piden más estudios de calidad.
sheet.en: For tomorrow morning: nothing here means your family must change anything because of this study. If you worry about exposure to pollutants such as pesticides or air pollution, you can talk it over with a paediatric or health team. This is a systematic review of published studies up to November 2013 on environmental toxicants and autism. It found an association in 34/37 exposure studies, with the strongest evidence for air pollutants and pesticides. Its limits: many studies were small or retrospective, biomarker results were mixed, and association is not cause. It does not explain any one person's autism, and the authors call for more high-quality studies.
sheet.sv: Till i morgon: inget i denna studie betyder att din familj behöver ändra något. Om du oroar dig för exponering för föroreningar, som bekämpningsmedel eller luftföroreningar, kan du ta upp det med barnläkare eller vårdteamet. Det är en systematisk översikt av publicerade studier till och med november 2013 om miljögifter och autism. Den fann samband i 34/37 studier om exponering, med starkast stöd för luftföroreningar och bekämpningsmedel. Begränsningar: många studier var små eller retrospektiva, resultaten för biomarkörer var blandade och samband är inte orsak. Den förklarar inte en enskild persons autism, och författarna efterlyser fler studier av hög kvalitet.

title: Potential Role of Selenoenzymes and Antioxidant Metabolism in relation to Autism Etiology and Pathology.
authors: Raymond LJ, Deth RC, Ralston NV
abstract: Autism and autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) are behaviorally defined, but the biochemical pathogenesis of the underlying disease process remains uncharacterized. Studies indicate that antioxidant status is diminished in autistic subjects, suggesting its pathology is associated with augmented production of oxidative species and/or compromised antioxidant metabolism. This suggests ASD may result from defects in the metabolism of cellular antioxidants which maintain intracellular redox status by quenching reactive oxygen species (ROS). Selenium-dependent enzymes (selenoenzymes) are important in maintaining intercellular reducing conditions, particularly in the brain. Selenoenzymes are a family of ~25 genetically unique proteins, several of which have roles in preventing and reversing oxidative damage in brain and endocrine tissues. Since the brain's high rate of oxygen consumption is accompanied by high ROS production, selenoenzyme activities are particularly important in this tissue. Because selenoenzymes can be irreversibly inhibited by many electrophiles, exposure to these organic and inorganic agents can diminish selenoenzyme-dependent antioxidant functions. This can impair brain development, particularly via the adverse influence of oxidative stress on epigenetic regulation.
