Here we review the physiological roles of selenoproteins in relation to potential biochemical mechanisms of ASD etiology and pathology.

sheet.es: Este estudio no ofrece nada que cambiar mañana por la mañana: es una revisión teórica, no una guía de cuidado. No indica que haya que modificar la dieta ni tomar suplementos; cualquier decisión sobre salud o nutrición corresponde a un profesional sanitario. Es una revisión de la literatura que plantea si las enzimas dependientes del selenio, que ayudan a proteger el cerebro del daño oxidativo, podrían tener relación con el desarrollo autista. Sus límites: es una hipótesis, no prueba una causa y no se aplica a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: This study offers nothing to change tomorrow morning: it is a theoretical review, not a care guide. It does not say to change diet or take supplements; any health or nutrition decision belongs with a healthcare professional. It is a literature review asking whether selenium-dependent enzymes, which help protect the brain from oxidative damage, might relate to autistic development. Its limits: it is a hypothesis, it does not prove a cause, and it does not apply to every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Studien ger inget att ändra i morgon bitti: det är en teoretisk översikt, inte en vårdguide. Den säger inte att man ska ändra kosten eller ta kosttillskott; beslut om hälsa eller kost hör hemma hos vårdpersonal. Det är en litteraturöversikt som undersöker om selenberoende enzymer, som hjälper till att skydda hjärnan mot oxidativ skada, kan ha samband med autistisk utveckling. Begränsningar: det är en hypotes, den bevisar ingen orsak och gäller inte alla autistiska personer.

title: Developmental pathways to autism: a review of prospective studies of infants at risk.
authors: Jones EJ, Gliga T, Bedford R, Charman T, Johnson MH
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASDs) are neurodevelopmental disorders characterized by impairments in social interaction and communication, and the presence of restrictive and repetitive behaviors. Symptoms of ASD likely emerge from a complex interaction between pre-existing neurodevelopmental vulnerabilities and the child's environment, modified by compensatory skills and protective factors. Prospective studies of infants at high familial risk for ASD (who have an older sibling with a diagnosis) are beginning to characterize these developmental pathways to the emergence of clinical symptoms. Here, we review the range of behavioral and neurocognitive markers for later ASD that have been identified in high-risk infants in the first years of life. We discuss theoretical implications of emerging patterns, and identify key directions for future work, including potential resolutions to several methodological challenges for the field. Mapping how ASD unfolds from birth is critical to our understanding of the developmental mechanisms underlying this disorder. A more nuanced understanding of developmental pathways to ASD will help us not only to identify children who need early intervention, but also to improve the range of interventions available to them.

sheet.es: Si tu bebé tiene un hermano o hermana autista, puede ayudar observar con calma cómo se comunica, juega y se relaciona, y comentar cualquier duda con su pediatra sin esperar. Una señal aislada no significa nada por sí sola. La evidencia es una revisión de estudios que siguieron a lo largo del tiempo a bebés con un hermano mayor con diagnóstico de autismo, y que describe marcadores conductuales y neurocognitivos en los primeros años. Sus límites: habla de grupos, no predice a cada niño, y los propios autores señalan retos metodológicos y la necesidad de más investigación.
sheet.en: If your baby has an autistic older sibling, it can help to calmly notice how they communicate, play and connect, and to raise any questions with their paediatrician without waiting. A single sign means nothing on its own. The evidence is a review of studies that followed infants over time who had an older sibling with an autism diagnosis, describing behavioural and neurocognitive markers in the first years. Its limits: it describes groups, not what will happen for any one child, and the authors note methodological challenges and the need for more research.
sheet.sv: Om din bebis har ett äldre syskon som är autistiskt kan det hjälpa att lugnt lägga märke till hur barnet kommunicerar, leker och knyter kontakt, och att ta upp frågor med barnläkaren utan att vänta. Ett enskilt tecken betyder ingenting i sig. Underlaget är en översikt av studier som över tid följde spädbarn med ett äldre syskon med autismdiagnos, och som beskriver beteendemässiga och neurokognitiva markörer under de första åren. Begränsningar: den beskriver grupper, inte vad som händer för ett enskilt barn, och författarna pekar på metodproblem och behov av mer forskning.

title: CYFIP family proteins between autism and intellectual disability: links with Fragile X syndrome.
authors: Abekhoukh S, Bardoni B
abstract: Intellectual disability (ID) and autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) have in common alterations in some brain circuits and brain abnormalities, such as synaptic transmission and dendritic spines morphology. Recent studies have indicated a differential expression for specific categories of genes as a cause for both types of disease, while an increasing number of genes is recognized to produce both disorders. An example is the Fragile X mental retardation gene 1 (FMR1), whose silencing causes the Fragile X syndrome, the most common form of ID and autism, also characterized by physical hallmarks. Fragile X mental retardation protein (FMRP), the protein encoded by FMR1, is an RNA-binding protein with an important role in translational control. Among the interactors of FMRP, CYFIP1/2 (cytoplasmic FMRP interacting protein) proteins are good candidates for ID and autism, on the bases of their genetic implication and functional properties, even if the precise functional significance of the CYFIP/FMRP interaction is not understood yet. CYFIP1 and CYFIP2 represent a link between Rac1, the WAVE (WAS protein family member) complex and FMRP, favoring the cross talk between actin polymerization and translational control.

sheet.es: Este estudio no ofrece nada que hacer mañana por la mañana; es ciencia básica sobre biología. Si cuidas a una persona autista o con discapacidad intelectual, puedes seguir basándote en lo que ella te muestra que necesita, en sus apoyos y en lo que dicen sus profesionales. Es una revisión de la literatura científica, sin participantes propios, que describe cómo las proteínas CYFIP1 y CYFIP2 se relacionan con la proteína FMRP del síndrome X frágil. Sus límites: el propio texto dice que aún no se entiende el significado funcional de esa interacción, y no sirve para decidir nada sobre una persona concreta. Las decisiones médicas corresponden a su clínico.
sheet.en: This study offers nothing to do tomorrow morning; it is basic science about biology. If you support an autistic person or a person with intellectual disability, you can keep relying on what they show you they need, their supports and their professionals' advice. It is a review of the scientific literature, with no participants of its own, describing how the proteins CYFIP1 and CYFIP2 relate to FMRP, the protein involved in Fragile X syndrome. Its limits: the text itself says the functional meaning of this interaction is not yet understood, and it cannot guide decisions about any one person. Medical decisions belong to their clinician.
sheet.sv: Den här studien ger inget att göra i morgon bitti; det är grundforskning om biologi. Om du stöttar en autistisk person eller en person med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning kan du fortsätta utgå från det personen visar att hen behöver, från stöden och från vad de professionella rekommenderar. Det är en översikt av forskningslitteratur, utan egna deltagare, som beskriver hur proteinerna CYFIP1 och CYFIP2 hänger ihop med FMRP, proteinet vid fragilt X-syndrom. Begränsningar: texten säger själv att den funktionella betydelsen av samspelet ännu inte är förstådd, och den kan inte styra beslut om en enskild person. Medicinska beslut hör till personens läkare.

title: The association between self-injurious behaviors and autism spectrum disorders.
authors: Minshawi NF, Hurwitz S, Fodstad JC, Biebl S, Morriss DH, McDougle CJ
abstract: A key area of concern in children with autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) are self-injurious behaviors (SIBs). These are behaviors that an individual engages in that may cause physical harm, such as head banging, or self-biting. SIBs are more common in children with ASD than those who are typically developing or have other neurodevelopmental disabilities. Therefore, it is important that clinicians who work with children with ASD have a solid understanding of SIB. The purpose of this paper is to review the research on the epidemiology of SIB in children with ASD, factors that predict the presence of SIB in this population, and the empirically supported behavioral treatments available.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista a su cargo se golpea la cabeza o se muerde, anote cuándo, dónde y qué ocurría justo antes, y llévelo a un profesional que conozca el autismo. Puede ayudar a entender qué lo desencadena. Es una revisión de investigaciones sobre cuán frecuentes son estas conductas en niños autistas, qué factores se asocian con ellas y qué tratamientos conductuales cuentan con respaldo empírico. Según la revisión, son más comunes que en niños con desarrollo típico u otras discapacidades del neurodesarrollo. Sus límites: el resumen no da cifras ni detalles, y no describe a cada persona. Busque apoyo profesional (clínico, servicio de salud o servicio de crisis); ante peligro inmediato, llame al número de emergencias de su país.
sheet.en: If an autistic person in your care bangs their head or bites themselves, note when and where it happens and what came just before, then bring this to a professional who knows autism. It may help show what sets it off. This is a review of research on how common these behaviors are in autistic children, which factors are linked to them, and which behavioral treatments have empirical support. The review reports they are more common than in typically developing children or those with other neurodevelopmental disabilities. Limits: the abstract gives no figures or details, and it does not describe every person. Seek professional help (a clinician, a health service or a crisis service); in immediate danger, call your country's emergency number.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person du stödjer slår huvudet eller biter sig själv, anteckna när och var det sker och vad som hände precis före, och ta med det till en yrkesperson som kan autism. Det kan visa vad som utlöser det. Detta är en översikt av forskning om hur vanligt beteendet är hos autistiska barn, vilka faktorer som hänger ihop med det och vilka beteendeinriktade behandlingar som har empiriskt stöd. Enligt översikten är det vanligare än hos barn med typisk utveckling eller andra neuroutvecklingsrelaterade funktionsnedsättningar. Begränsningar: sammanfattningen ger inga siffror eller detaljer och beskriver inte varje person. Sök professionell hjälp (läkare, vårdcentral eller krisstöd); vid akut fara, ring ditt lands nödnummer.

title: Evidence linking oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and inflammation in the brain of individuals with autism.
authors: Rossignol DA, Frye RE
abstract: Autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) are a heterogeneous group of neurodevelopmental disorders that are defined solely on the basis of behavioral observations. Therefore, ASD has traditionally been framed as a behavioral disorder. However, evidence is accumulating that ASD is characterized by certain physiological abnormalities, including oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction and immune dysregulation/inflammation. While these abnormalities have been reported in studies that have examined peripheral biomarkers such as blood and urine, more recent studies have also reported these abnormalities in brain tissue derived from individuals diagnosed with ASD as compared to brain tissue derived from control individuals. A majority of these brain tissue studies have been published since 2010. The brain regions found to contain these physiological abnormalities in individuals with ASD are involved in speech and auditory processing, social behavior, memory, and sensory and motor coordination. This manuscript examines the evidence linking oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction and immune dysregulation/inflammation in the brain of ASD individuals, suggesting that ASD has a clear biological basis with features of known medical disorders. This understanding may lead to new testing and treatment strategies in individuals with ASD.

sheet.es: Para el día a día: este estudio no ofrece nada que haya que cambiar mañana. Si te preocupa la salud o el bienestar físico de una persona autista, anota lo que observas y coméntalo con su profesional sanitario. Es una revisión de estudios, que recoge investigaciones en tejido cerebral de personas diagnosticadas con TEA y de personas de control; señala diferencias en estrés oxidativo, función mitocondrial e inflamación. Límites: es una revisión, no prueba causas, el abstract no da cifras y no vale como regla para todas las personas autistas. Las decisiones médicas corresponden siempre a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: For everyday life: this study gives nothing you need to change tomorrow. If you are concerned about an autistic person's physical health or wellbeing, note what you observe and discuss it with their healthcare professional. It is a review of studies, gathering research on brain tissue from people diagnosed with ASD and from control individuals; it points to differences in oxidative stress, mitochondrial function and inflammation. Limits: a review cannot prove causes, the abstract gives no figures, and it is not a rule for every autistic person. Medical decisions always belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: I vardagen: studien ger inget du behöver ändra i morgon. Om du oroar dig för en autistisk persons fysiska hälsa eller välbefinnande, anteckna vad du ser och ta upp det med personens vårdgivare. Det är en översikt som samlar studier av hjärnvävnad från personer med ASD-diagnos och från kontrollpersoner; den pekar på skillnader i oxidativ stress, mitokondriefunktion och inflammation. Begränsningar: en översikt kan inte bevisa orsaker, sammanfattningen anger inga siffror och resultaten är ingen regel för alla autistiska personer. Medicinska beslut hör alltid till en kliniker.

title: The co-occurrence of autism and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder in children - what do we know?
authors: Leitner Y
abstract: Symptoms of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and autistic spectrum disorder (ASD) often co-occur. The DSM-IV had specified that an ASD diagnosis is an exclusion criterion for ADHD, thereby limiting research of this common clinical co-occurrence. As neurodevelopmental disorders, both ASD and ADHD share some phenotypic similarities, but are characterized by distinct diagnostic criteria. The present review will examine the frequency and implications of this clinical co-occurrence in children, with an emphasis on the available data regarding pre-school age. The review will highlight possible etiologies explaining it, and suggest future research directions necessary to enhance our understanding of both etiology and therapeutic interventions, in light of the new DSM-V criteria, allowing for a dual diagnosis.

sheet.es: Si una niña o un niño autista también muestra rasgos de atención o mucha actividad, vale la pena tenerlo en cuenta y comentarlo con el equipo sanitario o educativo, porque ambas cosas pueden darse a la vez. Observa cuándo y dónde aparecen las dificultades y anótalo. La evidencia es una revisión de la literatura sobre niños, con énfasis en la edad preescolar. Sus límites: durante años el diagnóstico previo impidió estudiar bien esta coexistencia, así que hay pocos datos, y no dice qué ocurrirá en cada persona ni qué apoyo es mejor.
sheet.en: If an autistic child also shows attention differences or high activity levels, it is worth noting and discussing with their health or education team, because both can occur together. Jot down when and where these things show up. The evidence is a review of the literature on children, with an emphasis on pre-school age. Its limits: for years earlier diagnostic rules kept this overlap from being studied well, so data are limited, and it cannot say what will happen for any one person or which support works best.
sheet.sv: Om ett autistiskt barn också har uppmärksamhetsskillnader eller mycket hög aktivitet är det värt att notera och ta upp med vård- eller skolteamet, eftersom båda kan förekomma samtidigt. Skriv ner när och var det syns. Underlaget är en översikt av litteratur om barn, med fokus på förskoleåldern. Begränsningar: tidigare diagnosregler hindrade länge god forskning på detta, så data är begränsade, och översikten kan inte säga vad som gäller för en enskild person eller vilket stöd som fungerar bäst.

title: Parent training interventions for toddlers with autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Beaudoin AJ, Sébire G, Couture M
abstract: Background. Now that early identification of toddlers with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is possible, efforts are being made to develop interventions for children under three years of age. Most studies on early intervention have focused on intensive and individual interventions. However, parent training interventions that help parents interact and communicate with their toddlers with ASD might be a good alternative to promote the development of their child's sociocommunicative skills. Objective. This review aims to systematically examine (1) the use of parent training interventions for children with ASD under three years of age and (2) their effects on children's development, parents' well-being and parent-child interactions. Methods. Systematic searches were conducted to retrieve studies in which at least one parent was trained to implement ASD-specific techniques with their toddlers (0-36 months old) with a diagnosis of or suspected ASD. Results. Fifteen studies, involving 484 children (mean age: 23.26 months), were included in this review. Only two of them met criteria for conclusive evidence. Results show that parents were able to implement newly learned strategies and were generally very satisfied with parent training programs. However, findings pertaining to the children's communication and socioemotional skills, parent-child interactions, and parental well-being were inconclusive.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija autista es menor de tres años, un programa de formación para madres y padres puede ser una opción a explorar con el equipo profesional, además de las terapias individuales. Es una revisión sistemática de 15 estudios con 484 niños (edad media: 23.26 meses). Las familias lograron aplicar las estrategias aprendidas y se mostraron muy satisfechas. Sin embargo, solo dos estudios aportaron evidencia concluyente, y los resultados sobre comunicación, habilidades socioemocionales, interacción entre padres e hijos y bienestar de los progenitores no fueron concluyentes. No es una regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If your autistic child is under three, a parent training programme may be worth exploring with your professional team, alongside individual therapies. This is a systematic review of 15 studies with 484 children (mean age: 23.26 months). Parents were able to use the strategies they learned and were generally very satisfied. However, only two studies gave conclusive evidence, and findings on communication, socioemotional skills, parent-child interaction and parental well-being were inconclusive. It is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn är under tre år kan ett föräldraträningsprogram vara värt att utforska med ert professionella team, vid sidan av individuella insatser. Det är en systematisk översikt av 15 studier med 484 barn (medelålder: 23.26 månader). Föräldrarna kunde använda strategierna de lärt sig och var i allmänhet mycket nöjda. Bara två studier gav dock slutgiltiga belägg, och resultaten om kommunikation, socioemotionella färdigheter, samspel mellan förälder och barn samt föräldrarnas välbefinnande var inte slutgiltiga. Det är ingen regel för alla.

title: An intervention for sensory difficulties in children with autism: a randomized trial.
authors: Schaaf RC, Benevides T, Mailloux Z, Faller P, Hunt J, van Hooydonk E, Freeman R, Leiby B, Sendecki J, Kelly D
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: This study evaluated a manualized intervention for sensory difficulties for children with autism, ages 4-8 years, using a randomized trial design. Diagnosis of autism was confirmed using gold standard measures. Results show that the children in the treatment group (n = 17) who received 30 sessions of the occupational therapy intervention scored significantly higher (p = 0.003, d = 1.2) on Goal Attainment Scales (primary outcome), and also scored significantly better on measures of caregiver assistance in self-care (p = 0.008 d = 0.9) and socialization (p = 0.04, d = 0.7) than the Usual Care control group (n = 15). The study shows high rigor in its measurement of treatment fidelity and use of a manualized protocol, and provides support for the use of this intervention for children with autism. Findings are discussed in terms of their implications for practice and future research.

sheet.es: Si su hija o hijo autista de 4-8 años tiene dificultades sensoriales, puede preguntar a un terapeuta ocupacional por una intervención estructurada y con manual, y fijar con él o ella metas concretas para el día a día. Evidencia: ensayo aleatorizado con niños autistas de 4-8 años; el grupo de tratamiento (n = 17) recibió 30 sesiones de terapia ocupacional y alcanzó más metas y necesitó menos ayuda de cuidadores en autocuidado y socialización que el grupo de atención habitual (n = 15). Límites: el grupo era pequeño, no sabemos si los resultados valen para todos los niños, y cada persona tiene necesidades sensoriales propias.
sheet.en: If your autistic child aged 4-8 has sensory difficulties, you could ask an occupational therapist about a structured, manualized intervention, and agree with them on concrete goals for everyday life. Evidence: a randomized trial with autistic children aged 4-8; the treatment group (n = 17) received 30 sessions of occupational therapy and reached more of their goals and needed less caregiver assistance in self-care and socialization than the usual care group (n = 15). Limits: the groups were small, we cannot assume the results apply to every child, and each person has their own sensory needs.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn i åldern 4-8 år har sensoriska svårigheter kan du fråga en arbetsterapeut om en strukturerad, manualbaserad insats och tillsammans sätta konkreta mål för vardagen. Evidens: en randomiserad studie med autistiska barn i åldern 4-8 år; behandlingsgruppen (n = 17) fick 30 sessioner arbetsterapi och nådde fler mål och behövde mindre hjälp från vårdnadshavare med egenvård och socialt samspel än gruppen med sedvanlig vård (n = 15). Begränsningar: grupperna var små, resultaten gäller inte nödvändigtvis alla barn, och varje person har egna sensoriska behov.

title: Predictors of outcomes in autism early intervention: why don't we know more?
authors: Vivanti G, Prior M, Williams K, Dissanayake C
abstract: Response to early intervention programs in autism is variable. However, the factors associated with positive versus poor treatment outcomes remain unknown. Hence the issue of which intervention/s should be chosen for an individual child remains a common dilemma. We argue that lack of knowledge on "what works for whom and why" in autism reflects a number of issues in current approaches to outcomes research, and we provide recommendations to address these limitations. These include: a theory-driven selection of putative predictors; the inclusion of proximal measures that are directly relevant to the learning mechanisms demanded by the specific educational strategies; the consideration of family characteristics. Moreover, all data on associations between predictor and outcome variables should be reported in treatment studies.

sheet.es: Si le ofrecen un programa de intervención temprana, no espere una respuesta única: lo que ayuda a un niño autista puede no ayudar a otro. Pregunte a los profesionales qué meta concreta persigue cada estrategia y cómo encaja con su hijo y con su familia, y observe sus avances. Esta revisión, de 2014, sostiene que aún no sabemos qué funciona para quién ni por qué, y propone mejorar la investigación, por ejemplo considerando las características de las familias. Al ser una revisión argumentativa, no prueba qué programa elegir y no sirve como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If you are offered an early intervention programme, don't expect one standard result: what helps one autistic child may not help another. Ask professionals what specific goal each strategy has and how it fits your child and your family, then watch how your child responds. This 2014 review argues that we still don't know what works for whom and why, and suggests better research, including looking at family characteristics. As a review that makes an argument, it cannot tell you which programme to choose and is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du erbjuds ett program för tidiga insatser, förvänta dig inte ett givet resultat: det som hjälper ett autistiskt barn kanske inte hjälper ett annat. Fråga professionella vilket konkret mål varje strategi har och hur den passar ditt barn och din familj, och följ hur ditt barn svarar. Denna översikt från 2014 menar att vi ännu inte vet vad som fungerar för vem och varför, och föreslår bättre forskning, bland annat genom att beakta familjers egenskaper. Som en resonerande översikt kan den inte avgöra vilket program du ska välja och är ingen regel för alla.

title: GABAergic signaling as therapeutic target for autism spectrum disorders.
authors: Cellot G, Cherubini E
abstract: γ-Aminobutyric acid (GABA), the main inhibitory neurotransmitter in the adult brain, early in postnatal life exerts a depolarizing and excitatory action. This depends on accumulation of chloride inside the cell via the cation-chloride importer NKCC1, being the expression of the chloride exporter KCC2 very low at birth. The developmentally regulated expression of KCC2 results in extrusion of chloride with age and a shift of GABA from the depolarizing to the hyperpolarizing direction. The depolarizing action of GABA leads to intracellular calcium rise through voltage-dependent calcium channels and/or N-methyl-d-aspartate receptors. GABA-mediated calcium signals regulate a variety of developmental processes from cell proliferation migration, differentiation, synapse maturation, and neuronal wiring. Therefore, it is not surprising that some forms of neuro-developmental disorders such as autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) are associated with alterations of GABAergic signaling and impairment of the excitatory/inhibitory balance in selective neuronal circuits. In this review, we will discuss how changes of GABAA-mediated neurotransmission affect several forms of ASDs including the Fragile X, the Angelman, and Rett syndromes. Then, we will describe various animal models of ASDs with GABAergic dysfunctions, highlighting their behavioral deficits and the possibility to rescue them by targeting selective components of the GABAergic synapse. In particular, we will discuss how in some cases, reverting the polarity of GABA responses from the depolarizing to the hyperpolarizing direction with the diuretic bumetanide, a selective blocker of NKCC1, may have beneficial effects on ASDs, thus opening new therapeutic perspectives for the treatment of these devastating disorders.

sheet.es: Este trabajo es de ciencia básica y no cambia nada en la rutina de mañana. Es una revisión que resume cómo el GABA, un mensajero del cerebro, podría influir en el desarrollo de algunos circuitos neuronales en ciertas formas de autismo, como los síndromes X frágil, Angelman y Rett. Incluye modelos animales y menciona un fármaco: es un estudio médico, y cualquier decisión sobre medicamentos corresponde a un profesional clínico. Límites: es una revisión, no una prueba con personas, gran parte del trabajo es en animales, y no se aplica a todas las personas autistas. Puede comentarlo con su equipo de salud si tiene dudas.
sheet.en: This is basic science and changes nothing about tomorrow's routine. It is a review summarising how GABA, a brain messenger, may shape the development of some neural circuits in certain forms of autism, such as Fragile X, Angelman and Rett syndromes. It draws on animal models and mentions a drug: this was a medical study, and any decision about medication belongs to a clinician. Limits: it is a review, not a test with autistic people, much of the work is in animals, and it does not apply to every autistic person. If you have questions, raise them with your healthcare team.
sheet.sv: Detta är grundforskning och ändrar inget i morgondagens rutiner. Det är en översikt som sammanfattar hur GABA, en signalsubstans i hjärnan, kan påverka utvecklingen av vissa nervkretsar vid några former av autism, som fragilt X-, Angelman- och Rettsyndrom. Den bygger på djurmodeller och nämner ett läkemedel: det är en medicinsk studie, och beslut om medicinering hör till en läkare. Begränsningar: det är en översikt, inte ett test på autistiska personer, mycket av arbetet är på djur, och det gäller inte alla autistiska personer. Ta gärna upp frågor med vårdteamet.

title: Autism Spectrum Social Stories In Schools Trial (ASSSIST): study protocol for a feasibility randomised controlled trial analysing clinical and cost-effectiveness of Social Stories in mainstream schools.
authors: Wright B, Marshall D, Collingridge Moore D, Ainsworth H, Hackney L, Adamson J, Ali S, Allgar V, Cook L, Dyson L, Littlewood E, Hargate R, McLaren A, McMillan D, Trépel D, Whitehead J, Williams C
abstract: Introduction Current evidence suggests that Social Stories can be effective in tackling problem behaviours exhibited by children with autism spectrum disorder. Exploring the meaning of behaviour from a child's perspective allows stories to provide social information that is tailored to their needs. Case reports in children with autism have suggested that these stories can lead to a number of benefits including improvements in social interactions and choice making in educational settings. Methods and analysis The feasibility of clinical and cost-effectiveness of a Social Stories toolkit will be assessed using a randomised control framework. Participants (n=50) will be randomised to either the Social Stories intervention or a comparator group where they will be read standard stories for an equivalent amount of time. Statistics will be calculated for recruitment rates, follow-up rates and attrition. Economic analysis will determine appropriate measures of generic health and resource use categories for cost-effectiveness analysis. Qualitative analysis will ascertain information on perceptions about the feasibility and acceptability of the intervention. Ethics and dissemination National Health Service Ethics Approval (NHS; ref 11/YH/0340) for the trial protocol has been obtained along with NHS Research and Development permission from Leeds and York Partnership NHS Foundation Trust. All adverse events will be closely monitored, documented and reported to the study Data Monitoring Ethics Committee. At least one article in a peer reviewed journal will be published and research findings presented at relevant conferences. Trial registration number ISRCTN96286707.

sheet.es: Si el colegio usa Historias Sociales, pregunte cómo se escriben: lo ideal es partir de lo que la conducta significa para la niña o el niño y ofrecerle información social adaptada a sus necesidades. Este documento es un protocolo de un ensayo de viabilidad aleatorizado en colegios ordinarios: planea que 50 participantes reciban Historias Sociales o cuentos estándar durante el mismo tiempo. Aún no presenta resultados, así que no demuestra que las Historias Sociales funcionen ni que sirvan a todas las personas autistas; solo describe cómo se va a evaluar si el estudio es factible y aceptable.
sheet.en: If your child's school uses Social Stories, ask how they are written: the aim is to start from what a behaviour means from the child's perspective and give social information tailored to their needs. This is a protocol for a randomised feasibility trial in mainstream schools: it plans for 50 participants to receive either Social Stories or standard stories read for an equal amount of time. It reports no results yet, so it cannot show that Social Stories work or suit every autistic person; it only describes how feasibility and acceptability will be assessed.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barns skola använder sociala berättelser, fråga hur de skrivs: tanken är att utgå från vad ett beteende betyder ur barnets perspektiv och ge social information anpassad efter barnets behov. Detta är ett protokoll för en randomiserad genomförbarhetsstudie i vanliga skolor: man planerar att 50 deltagare ska få antingen sociala berättelser eller vanliga berättelser lika länge. Inga resultat redovisas ännu, så den visar inte att sociala berättelser fungerar eller passar alla autistiska personer; den beskriver bara hur genomförbarhet och acceptans ska bedömas.

title: Breast cancer and autism.
authors: Radcliff L
journal: Journal of the advanced practitioner in oncology
abstract: Case Study Amy is a 44-year-old woman with severe autism. She lives with her sister Susan, who is her caregiver and guardian. Amy is ambulatory and able to dress and feed herself. She is a healthy individual with no other significant comorbidities. She walks daily and enjoys her sister's company. Amy's life expectancy is greater than 10 years. However, she is difficult to care for medically, as she will not allow a physical examination and strikes out when strangers try to touch her. She is nonverbal and unable to participate in decision-making. INITIAL DIAGNOSIS Amy has a history of breast cancer diagnosed 2 years ago, originally presenting as a stage I lesion (T2N0) that was palpated by her caregiver while bathing. She underwent right simple mastectomy with sentinel lymph node resection. Susan recalls that the mastectomy was a very challenging ordeal, as Amy kept pulling out IV lines, drains, and dressings. Susan felt that Amy withdrew from her after the procedure as she most likely associated Susan with the cause of the pain, making her role as caregiver more difficult. Pathology confirmed an invasive ductal carcinoma, moderately differentiated, 2.4 cm, estrogen/progesterone receptor negative, HER2/neu negative, with negative surgical margins. Two right axillary sentinel lymph nodes were negative for disease. The standard of care for a patient with these tumor features is surgery plus adjuvant chemotherapy (National Comprehensive Cancer Network [NCCN], 2012). According to the Adjuvant Online! database (2012), Amy's risk for relapse was approximately 40% without adjuvant treatment; her risk for mortality was approximately 29%. After meeting with a medical oncologist, Amy did not receive adjuvant chemotherapy. According to Susan, she was not offered the choice, and the decision was not explained to them. She was simply told that it was not necessary. Aside from pathology, previous records were unavailable for review. Medical assessment of Amy's level of autism reveals marked impairments in the use of multiple nonverbal behaviors such as eye-to-eye gaze, facial expression, body posture, and gestures to regulate social interaction. She exhibits a total lack of development of spoken language, with no attempt to compensate through alternative modes of communication such as gesture. During the visit, she occupies herself with repetitive motor mannerisms. Susan believes that Amy struggles with overstimulation from tactile input. Therefore, she is combative with health-care providers and intolerant of invasive devices. Susan has an intimate understanding of Amy's ability to communicate her needs and wants through nonverbal changes. RECURRENCE Approximately 2 months ago, Amy began favoring her right arm and appeared to be in pain when participating in various activities. Susan became aware of Amy's pain issues by noticing that her posture was slightly altered and she was carrying herself differently. Further investigation with a CT scan showed concern for local disease recurrence involving the axillary lymph nodes. No distant metastases were seen. The standard of care for this diagnosis is surgical resection and consideration of radiation therapy, followed by adjuvant chemotherapy (NCCN, 2012). Susan does not want Amy to undergo further surgery and believes radiation would be too difficult to maneuver. The next best option would be a medical approach with chemotherapy as the main modality. DIFFICULT DECISIONS If treatment is pursued, the advanced practitioner will need to perform regular examinations and prescribe and monitor chemotherapy. The delivery of therapy, requiring frequent blood draws and IV access, will be a challenge for the health-care staff. The APN is apprehensive about the ability to accomplish these tasks safely given Amy's limited capacity to participate. The APN is also concerned with how treatment will affect Amy's life. The APN may have her own individual conflict of morals to contend with, given the limited understanding of the patient vs. nontreatment of a potentially curative malignancy. Chemotherapy is not an easy task for any patient to undertake, especially for a patient with challenges such as Amy has. Although Susan can give legal consent for her sister, Amy is unable to participate in this decision-making. Susan strongly believes that Amy's quality of life is much more important than the quantity. Withholding treatment may shorten the natural course of Amy's life, yet administering chemotherapy will alter the quality of life that she now enjoys without her understanding or consent. Should Amy receive chemotherapy or should Susan refuse treatment on her behalf?

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista que no usa lenguaje hablado, tu conocimiento de sus señales no verbales es información médica valiosa: cuenta al equipo sanitario cómo comunica dolor o malestar y pide que se te explique cada opción y cada decisión. Este artículo es una revisión que presenta un solo caso: una mujer autista de 44 años con cáncer de mama, cuya hermana cuidadora notó cambios en su postura que indicaban dolor. Es un caso único y no demuestra qué es lo correcto para otras personas. Las decisiones médicas corresponden a cada clínico junto con la persona y su familia.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person who does not use spoken language, your knowledge of their nonverbal signals is valuable medical information: tell the health team how they show pain or distress, and ask for every option and decision to be explained to you. This article is a review presenting a single case: a 44-year-old autistic woman with breast cancer, whose caregiver sister noticed posture changes that signalled pain. It is one case and does not show what is right for other people. Medical decisions belong to a clinician, together with the person and their family.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person som inte använder talat språk är din kunskap om hens icke-verbala signaler värdefull medicinsk information: berätta för vårdteamet hur hen visar smärta eller obehag och be att få varje alternativ och beslut förklarat. Artikeln är en översikt som beskriver ett enda fall: en 44-årig autistisk kvinna med bröstcancer, vars syster och vårdare märkte hållningsförändringar som visade smärta. Det är ett enskilt fall och visar inte vad som är rätt för andra. Medicinska beslut hör till en behandlare, tillsammans med personen och familjen.

title: Optogenetic insights on the relationship between anxiety-related behaviors and social deficits.
authors: Allsop SA, Vander Weele CM, Wichmann R, Tye KM
abstract: Many psychiatric illnesses are characterized by deficits in the social domain. For example, there is a high rate of co-morbidity between autism spectrum disorders and anxiety disorders. However, the common neural circuit mechanisms by which social deficits and other psychiatric disease states, such as anxiety, are co-expressed remains unclear. Here, we review optogenetic investigations of neural circuits in animal models of anxiety-related behaviors and social behaviors and discuss the important role of the amygdala in mediating aspects of these behaviors. In particular, we focus on recent evidence that projections from the basolateral amygdala (BLA) to the ventral hippocampus (vHPC) modulate anxiety-related behaviors and also alter social interaction. Understanding how this circuit influences both social behavior and anxiety may provide a mechanistic explanation for the pathogenesis of social anxiety disorder, as well as the prevalence of patients co-diagnosed with autism spectrum disorders and anxiety disorders. Furthermore, elucidating how circuits that modulate social behavior also mediate other complex emotional states will lead to a better understanding of the underlying mechanisms by which social deficits are expressed in psychiatric disease.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista se retrae en situaciones sociales, conviene preguntarse si también hay ansiedad, y reducir la presión: ofrecer pausas, avisar de los planes y dejar que elija cuánto interactuar. Este trabajo es una revisión de estudios con optogenética en modelos animales; no incluyó personas. Señala que una conexión entre la amígdala y el hipocampo ventral influye tanto en conductas de ansiedad como en la interacción social. Sus límites: es investigación animal básica, no ofrece consejos para la vida diaria y no demuestra que ocurra igual en cada persona autista. Ante dudas sobre ansiedad, consulte a un profesional.
sheet.en: If an autistic person pulls back in social situations, it is worth asking whether anxiety is also involved, and easing the pressure: offer breaks, share plans ahead of time and let them choose how much to interact. This is a review of optogenetic studies in animal models; it did not involve people. It describes a connection between the amygdala and the ventral hippocampus that influences both anxiety-related behaviours and social interaction. Its limits: it is basic animal research, offers no everyday guidance, and does not show the same happens in every autistic person. For concerns about anxiety, speak with a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person drar sig undan socialt är det värt att fråga sig om ångest också spelar in, och att minska pressen: erbjud pauser, berätta om planer i förväg och låt personen välja hur mycket att interagera. Detta är en översikt av optogenetiska studier på djurmodeller; inga människor deltog. Den beskriver en koppling mellan amygdala och ventrala hippocampus som påverkar både ångestrelaterat beteende och social interaktion. Begränsningar: det är grundforskning på djur, ger inga råd för vardagen och visar inte att detsamma gäller varje autistisk person. Vid oro för ångest, kontakta en kliniker.

title: A randomized controlled study of a social skills training for preadolescent children with autism spectrum disorders: generalization of skills by training parents and teachers?
authors: Dekker V, Nauta MH, Mulder EJ, Timmerman ME, de Bildt A
abstract: Background Social skills training (SST) is a common intervention for children with autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) to improve their social and communication skills. Despite the fact that SSTs are often applied in clinical practice, the evidence for the effectiveness of these trainings for children with ASD is inconclusive. Moreover, long term outcome and generalization of learned skills are little evaluated. Additionally, there is no research on the influence of involvement of parents and teachers on effectiveness of SST and on the generalization of learned social skills to daily life. We expect parent and teacher involvement in SST to enhance treatment efficacy and to facilitate generalization of learned skills to daily life. Method/design In a randomized controlled trial (RCT) with three conditions, 120 participants with ASD at the end of primary school (10-12 years of calendar age) have been randomized to SST, SST-PTI (SST with Parent & Teacher Involvement), or care-as-usual. The SST consists of 18 group sessions of 1.5 hours for the children. In the SST-PTI condition, parents additionally participate in 8 parent sessions and parents and teachers are actively involved in homework assignments. Assessment takes place at three moments: before and immediately after the intervention period and at 6 months follow-up. Primary outcome is socialization, as an aspect of adaptive functioning. Secondary outcomes focus on specific social skills children learn during SST and on more general social skills pertaining to home and community settings from a multi-informant perspective. Additionally, possible predictors of treatment outcome will be assessed. Discussion The current study is an RCT study evaluating SST in a large sample of Dutch children with ASD in a specific age range (10-12 years). Strengths of the study are the use of one manualized protocol, application of standardized and internationally used rating instruments, use of multiple raters, investigation of generalization of learned skills to daily life, and the evaluation of efficacy in the longer term by follow-up measures at 6 months after the end of training. Trial registration NTR2405.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija autista participa en un entrenamiento en habilidades sociales, puede ser útil preguntar cómo se puede implicar a la familia y a la escuela en las tareas para casa. Este artículo describe el diseño de un ensayo aleatorizado con 120 participantes autistas de 10-12 años, en Países Bajos, que compara tres opciones: el entrenamiento, el entrenamiento con participación de madres, padres y docentes, y la atención habitual. Aún no presenta resultados, así que no sabemos si implicar a la familia y a la escuela funciona mejor. Tampoco sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If your autistic child takes part in a social skills training, it may help to ask how family and school can be involved in the homework. This paper describes the design of a randomized trial with 120 autistic participants aged 10-12 in the Netherlands, comparing three options: the training, the training with parent and teacher involvement, and care-as-usual. It reports no results yet, so we cannot know whether involving home and school works better. It is also not a rule that applies to every person.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn deltar i social färdighetsträning kan det vara bra att fråga hur familjen och skolan kan involveras i hemuppgifterna. Artikeln beskriver upplägget för en randomiserad studie med 120 autistiska deltagare i åldern 10-12 i Nederländerna, som jämför tre alternativ: träningen, träningen med föräldrar och lärare involverade samt vanlig vård. Inga resultat redovisas ännu, så vi vet inte om det är bättre att involvera hem och skola. Den är heller ingen regel för alla.

title: From early markers to neuro-developmental mechanisms of autism.
authors: Gliga T, Jones EJ, Bedford R, Charman T, Johnson MH
abstract: A fast growing field, the study of infants at risk because of having an older sibling with autism (i.e. infant sibs) aims to identify the earliest signs of this disorder, which would allow for earlier diagnosis and intervention. More importantly, we argue, these studies offer the opportunity to validate existing neuro-developmental models of autism against experimental evidence. Although autism is mainly seen as a disorder of social interaction and communication, emerging early markers do not exclusively reflect impairments of the "social brain". Evidence for atypical development of sensory and attentional systems highlight the need to move away from localized deficits to models suggesting brain-wide involvement in autism pathology. We discuss the implications infant sibs findings have for future work into the biology of autism and the development of interventions.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a un bebé con un hermano mayor autista, puedes observar con calma cómo explora, atiende y responde a sonidos, luces y texturas, no solo cómo interactúa con otras personas. Si algo te inquieta, coméntalo con el pediatra o un equipo de desarrollo. Se trata de una revisión sobre estudios con bebés hermanos de personas autistas. Sugiere que las primeras señales no son solo sociales, sino también sensoriales y de atención. Es un resumen teórico: no sirve para predecir el desarrollo de un niño concreto ni para diagnosticar.
sheet.en: If you care for a baby with an older autistic sibling, you can calmly notice how they explore, pay attention and respond to sounds, lights and textures, not only how they interact with people. If something worries you, mention it to your paediatrician or a developmental team. This is a review of studies of infant siblings of autistic people. It suggests early signs are not only social but also involve sensory and attention systems. It is a theoretical overview: it cannot predict the development of any particular child or be used to diagnose.
sheet.sv: Om du tar hand om en bebis med ett äldre autistiskt syskon kan du lugnt lägga märke till hur barnet utforskar, riktar uppmärksamhet och reagerar på ljud, ljus och material, inte bara hur det samspelar med andra. Om något oroar dig, ta upp det med barnläkaren eller ett utvecklingsteam. Detta är en översikt av studier på spädbarn som har autistiska syskon. Den antyder att tidiga tecken inte bara är sociala utan också rör sinnesintryck och uppmärksamhet. Det är en teoretisk sammanfattning: den kan inte förutsäga ett enskilt barns utveckling eller användas för diagnos.

title: Gene × Environment interactions in autism spectrum disorders: role of epigenetic mechanisms.
authors: Tordjman S, Somogyi E, Coulon N, Kermarrec S, Cohen D, Bronsard G, Bonnot O, Weismann-Arcache C, Botbol M, Lauth B, Ginchat V, Roubertoux P, Barburoth M, Kovess V, Geoffray MM, Xavier J
abstract: Several studies support currently the hypothesis that autism etiology is based on a polygenic and epistatic model. However, despite advances in epidemiological, molecular and clinical genetics, the genetic risk factors remain difficult to identify, with the exception of a few chromosomal disorders and several single gene disorders associated with an increased risk for autism. Furthermore, several studies suggest a role of environmental factors in autism spectrum disorders (ASD). First, arguments for a genetic contribution to autism, based on updated family and twin studies, are examined. Second, a review of possible prenatal, perinatal, and postnatal environmental risk factors for ASD are presented. Then, the hypotheses are discussed concerning the underlying mechanisms related to a role of environmental factors in the development of ASD in association with genetic factors. In particular, epigenetics as a candidate biological mechanism for gene × environment interactions is considered and the possible role of epigenetic mechanisms reported in genetic disorders associated with ASD is discussed. Furthermore, the example of in utero exposure to valproate provides a good illustration of epigenetic mechanisms involved in ASD and innovative therapeutic strategies. Epigenetic remodeling by environmental factors opens new perspectives for a better understanding, prevention, and early therapeutic intervention of ASD.

sheet.es: Lo práctico: el autismo surge de una mezcla compleja de muchos genes y factores del entorno; no hay una sola causa ni nada que usted hiciera «mal». Si le preocupan antecedentes familiares o medicamentos tomados en el embarazo (como el valproato), puede comentarlo con calma con su equipo médico o de genética, sin culpas. Lo más útil hoy sigue siendo apoyar a su hijo o hija tal como es. Evidencia: es una revisión narrativa de 2014 que resume estudios de familias, gemelos y factores prenatales y posnatales, y propone la epigenética como mecanismo. Límites: no aporta datos nuevos, muchas hipótesis no están confirmadas y no ofrece pautas aplicables a cada persona.
sheet.en: The practical point: autism arises from a complex mix of many genes and environmental factors; there is no single cause and nothing you did "wrong". If you have questions about family history or medicines taken during pregnancy (such as valproate), you can raise them calmly with your medical or genetics team, without blame. The most useful thing today is still supporting your child as they are. Evidence: this is a 2014 narrative review summarising family, twin and prenatal and postnatal studies, proposing epigenetics as a mechanism. Limits: it adds no new data, many hypotheses remain unconfirmed, and it offers no guidance that applies to every person.
sheet.sv: Det praktiska: autism uppstår ur en komplex blandning av många gener och miljöfaktorer; det finns ingen enskild orsak och inget du gjort "fel". Har du frågor om ärftlighet eller läkemedel under graviditeten (som valproat) kan du lugnt ta upp dem med vården eller en genetisk mottagning, utan skuld. Det mest värdefulla idag är fortfarande att stötta ditt barn som det är. Evidens: en narrativ översikt från 2014 som sammanfattar familje- och tvillingstudier samt pre- och postnatala faktorer, och föreslår epigenetik som mekanism. Begränsningar: inga nya data, många hypoteser är obekräftade och den ger inga råd som gäller varje person.

title: Biomarkers in autism.
authors: Goldani AA, Downs SR, Widjaja F, Lawton B, Hendren RL
abstract: Autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) are complex, heterogeneous disorders caused by an interaction between genetic vulnerability and environmental factors. In an effort to better target the underlying roots of ASD for diagnosis and treatment, efforts to identify reliable biomarkers in genetics, neuroimaging, gene expression, and measures of the body's metabolism are growing. For this article, we review the published studies of potential biomarkers in autism and conclude that while there is increasing promise of finding biomarkers that can help us target treatment, there are none with enough evidence to support routine clinical use unless medical illness is suspected. Promising biomarkers include those for mitochondrial function, oxidative stress, and immune function. Genetic clusters are also suggesting the potential for useful biomarkers.

sheet.es: Por ahora no existe un análisis de sangre, una imagen cerebral ni una prueba genética que sirva de rutina para saber si una persona es autista o para elegir apoyos. Si ofrecen una prueba así, conviene preguntar al equipo clínico qué evidencia la respalda. Solo tiene sentido buscar pruebas médicas si se sospecha una enfermedad. Es una revisión de estudios publicados sobre posibles biomarcadores en genética, neuroimagen, expresión génica y metabolismo. Concluye que hay promesas, como la función mitocondrial, el estrés oxidativo y la inmunidad, pero ninguna con evidencia suficiente. No presenta resultados válidos para cada persona autista, y la investigación sigue en desarrollo.
sheet.en: For now, there is no blood test, brain scan or genetic test that is ready for routine use to tell whether someone is autistic or to choose supports. If a test like this is offered, it is fair to ask the clinical team what evidence backs it. Medical testing makes sense mainly when a medical illness is suspected. This is a review of published studies on possible biomarkers in genetics, neuroimaging, gene expression and metabolism. It concludes there is promise, for example in mitochondrial function, oxidative stress and immune function, but nothing with enough evidence yet. It does not describe every autistic person, and the research is still developing.
sheet.sv: Just nu finns det inget blodprov, ingen hjärnundersökning och inget gentest som är redo för rutinmässig användning för att avgöra om någon är autistisk eller för att välja stöd. Om ett sådant test erbjuds är det rimligt att fråga vårdteamet vilken evidens som finns. Medicinska tester är främst meningsfulla om man misstänker en medicinsk sjukdom. Detta är en översikt av publicerade studier om möjliga biomarkörer inom genetik, hjärnavbildning, genuttryck och ämnesomsättning. Den drar slutsatsen att det finns löften, till exempel kring mitokondriefunktion, oxidativ stress och immunfunktion, men inget med tillräcklig evidens. Den gäller inte alla autistiska personer, och forskningen utvecklas fortfarande.

title: Technologies as support tools for persons with autistic spectrum disorder: a systematic review.
authors: Aresti-Bartolome N, Garcia-Zapirain B
journal: International journal of environmental research and public health
abstract: This study analyzes the technologies most widely used to work on areas affected by the Autistic Spectrum Disorder (ASD). Technologies can focus on the strengths and weaknesses of this disorder as they make it possible to create controlled environments, reducing the anxiety produced by real social situations. Extensive research has proven the efficiency of technologies as support tools for therapy and their acceptation by ASD sufferers and the people who are with them on a daily basis. This article is organized by the types of systems developed: virtual reality applications, telehealth systems, social robots and dedicated applications, all of which are classified by the areas they center on: communication, social learning and imitation skills and other ASD-associated conditions. 40.5% of the research conducted is found to be focused on communication as opposed to 37.8% focused on learning and social imitation skills and 21.6% which underlines problems associated with this disorder. Although most of the studies reveal how useful these tools are in therapy, they are generic tools for ASD sufferers in general, which means there is a lack of personalised tools to meet each person's needs.

sheet.es: Si piensa en usar tecnología con una persona autista, pruebe herramientas que se ajusten a sus intereses y a su ritmo, como aplicaciones o entornos de práctica controlados, y observe si le resultan útiles. Es una revisión sistemática de estudios sobre realidad virtual, telesalud, robots sociales y aplicaciones, centrados en comunicación, aprendizaje social e imitación. La mayoría de los estudios halló utilidad en terapia. Sus límites: las herramientas son genéricas, falta personalización, y el texto usa un lenguaje centrado en el déficit. Cada persona es distinta, así que lo que funciona para una puede no servir para otra.
sheet.en: If you are thinking of using technology with an autistic person, try tools that fit their interests and pace, such as apps or controlled practice settings, and watch whether they help. This is a systematic review of studies on virtual reality, telehealth, social robots and dedicated apps, focused on communication, social learning and imitation. Most studies found them useful in therapy. Limits: the tools are generic, with a lack of personalisation, and the review uses deficit-focused language. Every person is different, so what works for one may not suit another.
sheet.sv: Om du funderar på teknik för en autistisk person, prova verktyg som passar personens intressen och tempo, som appar eller kontrollerade övningsmiljöer, och se om de hjälper. Det här är en systematisk översikt av studier om virtuell verklighet, telehälsa, sociala robotar och särskilda appar, med fokus på kommunikation, socialt lärande och imitation. De flesta studier fann att verktygen var användbara i terapi. Begränsningar: verktygen är generiska, det saknas anpassning, och översikten använder ett bristfokuserat språk. Alla människor är olika, så det som fungerar för en passar kanske inte en annan.

title: Meta-analysis of SHANK Mutations in Autism Spectrum Disorders: a gradient of severity in cognitive impairments.
authors: Leblond CS, Nava C, Polge A, Gauthier J, Huguet G, Lumbroso S, Giuliano F, Stordeur C, Depienne C, Mouzat K, Pinto D, Howe J, Lemière N, Durand CM, Guibert J, Ey E, Toro R, Peyre H, Mathieu A, Amselle
abstract: SHANK genes code for scaffold proteins located at the post-synaptic density of glutamatergic synapses. In neurons, SHANK2 and SHANK3 have a positive effect on the induction and maturation of dendritic spines, whereas SHANK1 induces the enlargement of spine heads. Mutations in SHANK genes have been associated with autism spectrum disorders (ASD), but their prevalence and clinical relevance remain to be determined. Here, we performed a new screen and a meta-analysis of SHANK copy-number and coding-sequence variants in ASD. Copy-number variants were analyzed in 5,657 patients and 19,163 controls, coding-sequence variants were ascertained in 760 to 2,147 patients and 492 to 1,090 controls (depending on the gene), and, individuals carrying de novo or truncating SHANK mutations underwent an extensive clinical investigation. Copy-number variants and truncating mutations in SHANK genes were present in ∼1% of patients with ASD: mutations in SHANK1 were rare (0.04%) and present in males with normal IQ and autism; mutations in SHANK2 were present in 0.17% of patients with ASD and mild intellectual disability; mutations in SHANK3 were present in 0.69% of patients with ASD and up to 2.12% of the cases with moderate to profound intellectual disability. In summary, mutations of the SHANK genes were detected in the whole spectrum of autism with a gradient of severity in cognitive impairment. Given the rare frequency of SHANK1 and SHANK2 deleterious mutations, the clinical relevance of these genes remains to be ascertained. In contrast, the frequency and the penetrance of SHANK3 mutations in individuals with ASD and intellectual disability-more than 1 in 50-warrant its consideration for mutation screening in clinical practice.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija autista tiene además una discapacidad intelectual moderada o profunda, puede valer la pena preguntar al equipo médico si un estudio genético (incluido el gen SHANK3) tiene sentido en su caso. Un resultado puede orientar el seguimiento y conectar con otras familias, pero no cambia quién es tu hijo ni lo que necesita hoy. Este metaanálisis reunió datos genéticos de miles de personas autistas y controles; los cambios en genes SHANK aparecieron en cerca del 1 %, y en SHANK3 en más de 1 de cada 50 personas con discapacidad intelectual. Límites: los cambios en SHANK1 y SHANK2 son muy raros y su relevancia clínica aún no está clara.
sheet.en: If your autistic child also has a moderate to profound intellectual disability, it may be worth asking your medical team whether genetic testing (including the SHANK3 gene) makes sense for them. A result can guide follow-up and connect you with other families, but it does not change who your child is or what they need today. This meta-analysis pooled genetic data from thousands of autistic people and controls; SHANK gene changes appeared in about 1%, and SHANK3 changes in more than 1 in 50 people with intellectual disability. Limits: SHANK1 and SHANK2 changes are very rare, and their clinical relevance is still unclear.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn också har en måttlig till svår intellektuell funktionsnedsättning kan det vara värt att fråga vårdteamet om en genetisk utredning (inklusive genen SHANK3) är meningsfull. Ett resultat kan vägleda uppföljningen och ge kontakt med andra familjer, men det ändrar inte vem ditt barn är eller vad hen behöver i dag. Denna metaanalys samlade genetiska data från tusentals autistiska personer och kontrollpersoner; förändringar i SHANK-gener fanns hos ungefär 1 %, och i SHANK3 hos mer än 1 av 50 personer med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning. Begränsningar: förändringar i SHANK1 och SHANK2 är mycket ovanliga och deras kliniska betydelse är fortfarande oklar.

title: Parent skills training for parents of children or adults with developmental disorders: systematic review and meta-analysis protocol.
authors: Reichow B, Kogan C, Barbui C, Smith I, Yasamy MT, Servili C
abstract: Introduction Developmental disorders, including intellectual disability and autism spectrum disorders, may limit an individual's capacity to conduct daily activities. The emotional and economic burden on families caring for an individual with a developmental disorder is substantial, and quality of life may be limited by a lack of services. Therefore, finding effective treatments to help this population should be a priority. Recent work has shown parent skills training interventions improve developmental, behavioural and family outcomes. The purpose of this review protocol is to extend previous findings by systematically analysing randomised controlled trials of parent skills training programmes for parents of children with developmental disorders including intellectual disabilities and autism spectrum disorders and use meta-analytic techniques to identify programme components reliably associated with successful outcomes of parent skills training programmes. Methods and analysis We will include all studies conducted using randomised control trials designs that compare a group of parents receiving a parent skills training programme to a group of parents in a no-treatment control, waitlist control or treatment as usual comparison group. To locate studies, we will conduct an extensive electronic database search and then use snowball methods, with no limits to publication year or language. We will present a narrative synthesis including visual displays of study effects on child and parental outcomes and conduct a quantitative synthesis of the effects of parent skills training programmes using meta-analytic techniques. Ethics and dissemination No ethical issues are foreseen and ethical approval is not required given this is a protocol for a systematic review. The findings of this study will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and international conference presentations. Updates of the review will be conducted, as necessary, to inform and guide practice. Trial registration number PROSPERO (CRD42014006993).

sheet.es: Si cuida a una persona autista o con otra discapacidad del desarrollo, puede preguntar a los servicios locales si ofrecen programas de formación para madres y padres, y qué incluyen. Este artículo es un protocolo: describe cómo se revisarán ensayos controlados aleatorizados que comparan a familias que reciben esa formación con familias en lista de espera, sin tratamiento o con la atención habitual. Todavía no presenta resultados, así que no demuestra que estos programas funcionen ni sirvan a todas las familias. Su objetivo es identificar qué componentes se asocian con buenos resultados para hijos e hijas y para sus familias.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person or someone with another developmental disability, you could ask local services whether they offer parent skills training programmes, and what they include. This paper is a protocol: it describes how a review will analyse randomised controlled trials comparing families who receive such training with families on a waitlist, with no treatment or with usual care. It reports no results yet, so it cannot show that these programmes work, or that they suit every family. Its aim is to identify which programme components are linked to good outcomes for children and for their families.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person eller någon med en annan utvecklingsrelaterad funktionsnedsättning kan du fråga lokala verksamheter om de erbjuder föräldrautbildning och vad den innehåller. Artikeln är ett protokoll: den beskriver hur en översikt ska analysera randomiserade kontrollerade studier som jämför familjer som får sådan utbildning med familjer på väntelista, utan behandling eller med vanlig vård. Den redovisar inga resultat än, så den visar inte att programmen fungerar eller passar alla familjer. Syftet är att identifiera vilka delar av programmen som hänger ihop med goda resultat för barn och familjer.

title: An evo-devo approach to thyroid hormones in cerebral and cerebellar cortical development: etiological implications for autism.
authors: Berbel P, Navarro D, Román GC
abstract: The morphological alterations of cortical lamination observed in mouse models of developmental hypothyroidism prompted the recognition that these experimental changes resembled the brain lesions of children with autism; this led to recent studies showing that maternal thyroid hormone deficiency increases fourfold the risk of autism spectrum disorders (ASD), offering for the first time the possibility of prevention of some forms of ASD. For ethical reasons, the role of thyroid hormones on brain development is currently studied using animal models, usually mice and rats. Although mammals have in common many basic developmental principles regulating brain development, as well as fundamental basic mechanisms that are controlled by similar metabolic pathway activated genes, there are also important differences. For instance, the rodent cerebral cortex is basically a primary cortex, whereas the primary sensory areas in humans account for a very small surface in the cerebral cortex when compared to the associative and frontal areas that are more extensive. Associative and frontal areas in humans are involved in many neurological disorders, including ASD, attention deficit-hyperactive disorder, and dyslexia, among others. Therefore, an evo-devo approach to neocortical evolution among species is fundamental to understand not only the role of thyroid hormones and environmental thyroid disruptors on evolution, development, and organization of the cerebral cortex in mammals but also their role in neurological diseases associated to thyroid dysfunction.

sheet.es: Si estás embarazada o acompañas un embarazo, la salud de la tiroides merece una conversación con el equipo médico; no es algo que haya que resolver solo ni con culpa. Esta es una revisión de la literatura, no un estudio con personas nuevas. Recoge trabajos en ratones y ratas, y menciona estudios recientes que asocian la carencia materna de hormonas tiroideas con un riesgo cuatro veces mayor de autismo. Sus límites: el cerebro de los roedores difiere del humano, la asociación no demuestra una causa y el autismo tiene muchos orígenes. Las decisiones médicas corresponden siempre a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If you are pregnant or supporting someone who is, thyroid health is worth raising with the medical team; it is not something to handle alone or with guilt. This is a review of existing research, not a new study with people. It gathers work in mice and rats, and mentions recent studies linking maternal thyroid hormone deficiency to a fourfold higher risk of autism. Its limits: rodent brains differ from human ones, an association does not prove a cause, and autism has many origins. Medical decisions always belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om du är gravid eller stöttar någon som är det är sköldkörtelhälsan värd att ta upp med vårdteamet; det är inget du ska hantera ensam eller med skuldkänslor. Detta är en översikt av befintlig forskning, inte en ny studie med människor. Den samlar arbete på möss och råttor och nämner nyare studier som kopplar moderns brist på sköldkörtelhormon till fyra gånger högre risk för autism. Begränsningar: gnagares hjärnor skiljer sig från människors, ett samband bevisar inte orsak, och autism har många ursprung. Medicinska beslut hör alltid till en läkare.

title: Mental health services for individuals with high functioning autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Lake JK, Perry A, Lunsky Y
abstract: Adolescents and adults with an autism spectrum disorder (ASD) who do not have an intellectual impairment or disability (ID), described here as individuals with high-functioning autism spectrum disorder (HFASD), represent a complex and underserved psychiatric population. While there is an emerging literature on the mental health needs of children with ASD with normal intelligence, we know less about these issues in adults. Of the few studies of adolescents and adults with HFASD completed to date, findings suggest that they face a multitude of cooccurring psychiatric (e.g., anxiety, depression), psychosocial, and functional issues, all of which occur in addition to their ASD symptomatology. Despite this, traditional mental health services and supports are falling short of meeting the needs of these adults. This review highlights the service needs and the corresponding gaps in care for this population. It also provides an overview of the literature on psychiatric risk factors, identifies areas requiring further study, and makes recommendations for how existing mental health services could include adults with HFASD.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista sin discapacidad intelectual, conviene preguntar con regularidad por su ánimo, su ansiedad y su vida diaria, y buscar servicios de salud mental que conozcan el autismo. Esta es una revisión de la literatura sobre adolescentes y adultos autistas sin discapacidad intelectual. Señala que presentan con frecuencia ansiedad, depresión y otras dificultades psicosociales, y que los servicios habituales no cubren sus necesidades. Tiene límites: se basa en pocos estudios, el término "alto funcionamiento" es poco preciso y no describe a cada persona. No sustituye la valoración de un profesional.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person without intellectual disability, it helps to check in regularly about their mood, anxiety and daily life, and to look for mental health services that understand autism. This is a review of the literature on autistic adolescents and adults without intellectual disability. It reports that they often face anxiety, depression and other psychosocial difficulties, and that usual services fall short of their needs. It has limits: it draws on few studies, the term "high-functioning" is imprecise, and it does not describe every person. It does not replace an assessment by a professional.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person utan intellektuell funktionsnedsättning kan det hjälpa att regelbundet fråga om humör, ångest och vardag, och att söka psykiatrisk vård som förstår autism. Det här är en översikt av litteraturen om autistiska ungdomar och vuxna utan intellektuell funktionsnedsättning. Den visar att de ofta möter ångest, depression och andra psykosociala svårigheter, och att vanliga tjänster inte räcker till. Begränsningar: den bygger på få studier, termen "högfungerande" är oprecis och beskriver inte alla individer. Den ersätter inte en bedömning av yrkespersoner.

title: Modulation of the GABAergic pathway for the treatment of fragile X syndrome.
authors: Lozano R, Hare EB, Hagerman RJ
abstract: Fragile X syndrome (FXS) is the most common genetic cause of intellectual disability and the most common single-gene cause of autism. It is caused by mutations on the fragile X mental retardation gene (FMR1) and lack of fragile X mental retardation protein, which in turn, leads to decreased inhibition of translation of many synaptic proteins. The metabotropic glutamate receptor (mGluR) hypothesis states that the neurological deficits in individuals with FXS are due mainly to downstream consequences of overstimulation of the mGluR pathway. The main efforts have focused on mGluR5 targeted treatments; however, investigation on the gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) system and its potential as a targeted treatment is less emphasized. The fragile X mouse models (Fmr1-knock out) show decreased GABA subunit receptors, decreased synthesis of GABA, increased catabolism of GABA, and overall decreased GABAergic input in many regions of the brain. Consequences of the reduced GABAergic input in FXS include oversensitivity to sensory stimuli, seizures, and anxiety. Deficits in the GABA receptors in different regions of the brain are associated with behavioral and attentional processing deficits linked to anxiety and autistic behaviors. The understanding of the neurobiology of FXS has led to the development of targeted treatments for the core behavioral features of FXS, which include social deficits, inattention, and anxiety. These symptoms are also observed in individuals with autism and other neurodevelopmental disorders, therefore the targeted treatments for FXS are leading the way in the treatment of other neurodevelopmental syndromes and autism. The GABAergic system in FXS represents a target for new treatments. Herein, we discuss the animal and human trials of GABAergic treatment in FXS. Arbaclofen and ganaxolone have been used in individuals with FXS. Other potential GABAergic treatments, such as riluzole, gaboxadol, tiagabine, and vigabatrin, will be also discussed. Further studies are needed to determine the safety and efficacy of GABAergic treatments for FXS.

sheet.es: Esta revisión no ofrece nada que probar mañana en casa. Sí recuerda que, en el síndrome X frágil, la sensibilidad a los estímulos sensoriales, la ansiedad y las crisis pueden tener una base biológica, así que conviene tomarlas en serio y adaptar el entorno. Es una revisión de la literatura sobre estudios en animales y en personas, centrada en tratamientos médicos. Las decisiones médicas corresponden siempre a un profesional clínico. Sus límites: los propios autores indican que hacen falta más estudios para saber si esos tratamientos son seguros y eficaces, y lo hallado en ratones no se aplica a toda persona.
sheet.en: This review offers nothing to try at home tomorrow. It does remind us that in fragile X syndrome, sensory sensitivity, anxiety and seizures may have a biological basis, so it makes sense to take them seriously and adapt the environment. It is a review of the literature covering animal and human studies, focused on medical treatments. Medical decisions always belong to a clinician. Its limits: the authors say more studies are needed to know whether these treatments are safe and effective, and findings from mice do not apply to every person.
sheet.sv: Den här översikten ger inget att prova hemma i morgon. Den påminner dock om att känslighet för sinnesintryck, ångest och krampanfall vid fragilt X-syndrom kan ha en biologisk grund, så det är rimligt att ta dem på allvar och anpassa miljön. Det är en litteraturöversikt över djurstudier och studier på människor, med fokus på medicinska behandlingar. Medicinska beslut hör alltid till en läkare. Begränsningar: författarna skriver att fler studier behövs för att veta om behandlingarna är säkra och effektiva, och resultat från möss gäller inte alla människor.

title: Learning and behavioral deficits associated with the absence of the fragile X mental retardation protein: what a fly and mouse model can teach us.
authors: Santos AR, Kanellopoulos AK, Bagni C
abstract: The Fragile X syndrome (FXS) is the most frequent form of inherited mental disability and is considered a monogenic cause of autism spectrum disorder. FXS is caused by a triplet expansion that inhibits the expression of the FMR1 gene. The gene product, the Fragile X Mental Retardation Protein (FMRP), regulates mRNA metabolism in brain and nonneuronal cells.
