During brain development, FMRP controls the expression of key molecules involved in receptor signaling, cytoskeleton remodeling, protein synthesis and, ultimately, spine morphology. Symptoms associated with FXS include neurodevelopmental delay, cognitive impairment, anxiety, hyperactivity, and autistic-like behavior. Twenty years ago the first Fmr1 KO mouse to study FXS was generated, and several years later other key models including the mutant Drosophila melanogaster, dFmr1, have further helped the understanding of the cellular and molecular causes behind this complex syndrome. Here, we review to which extent these biological models are affected by the absence of FMRP, pointing out the similarities with the observed human dysfunction. Additionally, we discuss several potential treatments under study in animal models that are able to partially revert some of the FXS abnormalities.

sheet.es: Este artículo es sobre biología de laboratorio, no ofrece pasos para hacer mañana. Sí puede ayudar a entender que, en el síndrome X frágil, que a veces se da en personas autistas, hay una base genética que influye en cómo se desarrolla el cerebro. Si cuidas a alguien con este diagnóstico, observa sus necesidades concretas, como la ansiedad o el aprendizaje, y coméntalas con su equipo de profesionales. Es una revisión de estudios con modelos de ratón y mosca, no con personas. Sus conclusiones no se aplican directamente a cada persona. Sobre posibles tratamientos, solo indica que se estudian en animales; las decisiones médicas corresponden a un clínico.
sheet.en: This article is about laboratory biology, so it offers no steps for tomorrow. It can help you understand that in fragile X syndrome, which can occur in autistic people, a genetic difference shapes how the brain develops. If you support someone with this diagnosis, notice their specific needs, such as anxiety or learning, and share them with their care team. It is a review of studies in mouse and fly models, not in people. Its conclusions do not apply directly to every person. Treatments are only mentioned as being studied in animals; medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Artikeln handlar om laboratoriebiologi och ger inga konkreta steg för i morgon. Den kan ändå hjälpa dig att förstå att vid fragilt X-syndrom, som kan förekomma hos autistiska personer, påverkar en genetisk skillnad hur hjärnan utvecklas. Om du stöttar någon med denna diagnos kan du uppmärksamma personens egna behov, till exempel oro eller lärande, och ta upp dem med vårdteamet. Det är en översikt av studier på mus- och flugmodeller, inte på människor. Slutsatserna gäller inte direkt för varje person. Behandlingar nämns bara som studerade på djur; medicinska beslut hör till en läkare.

title: Behavioural aspects of patients with Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASD) that affect their dental management.
authors: Limeres-Posse J, Castaño-Novoa P, Abeleira-Pazos M, Ramos-Barbosa I
journal: Medicina oral, patologia oral y cirugia bucal
abstract: Dental treatment in patients with Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASD) can be complicated due to the presence of behavioral alterations. In this group, there are no specific behavioral profiles that allow dentist to anticipate the attitude that a patient will show during a visit. Thus, behavioral attitudes have been described that vary from total permissiveness and collaboration during even bloody procedures, to the absolute impossibility in conducting a simple oral examination. There is no effective behavioral management technique for all ASD patients. Prior information, such as the type of ASD or the presence of certain concurrent pathologies can help predict the patient's likely behavior. Therefore, gathering all the information in a preliminary interview with the parents/guardians of the patient is recommended. Knowing these factors will allow individualized behavioral management strategies to be designed and facilitates the planning of dental treatment.

title: Peer-mediated theatrical engagement for improving reciprocal social interaction in autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Corbett BA, Qualls LR, Valencia B, Fecteau SM, Swain DM
abstract: The hallmark characteristic of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is poor reciprocal social communication. Interventions designed to improve this core deficit are critically needed. Social skills interventions such as direct training, peer mediation, and video modeling have contributed to improvements in various social skills in children with ASD. This paper reviews existing social competence interventions available for children with ASD while highlighting hypothesized critical components for advancing, maintaining, and generalizing skills, which include (1) peer mediation, (2) active learning, and (3) implementation in supportive, natural contexts. As a framework for these approaches, this conceptual paper describes SENSE Theatre, a novel intervention that combines trained peers that facilitate the performance-based theatrical treatment delivered in a supportive, community-based environment. A review of previous research shows early feasibility, setting the stage for more rigorous studies to aid in developing a standardized intervention package.

sheet.es: Si buscas apoyar la interacción social de una persona autista, puede valer la pena explorar actividades con compañeros que se aprenden haciendo, como el teatro, en un entorno comunitario acogedor. Se trata de una idea para considerar, no de una receta. Es un artículo de revisión y conceptual sobre intervenciones de competencia social para niños autistas; describe un programa llamado SENSE Theatre. Los estudios previos solo muestran una viabilidad inicial, y faltan estudios más rigurosos. Que algo sea viable no prueba que ayude a cada persona, y a algunas puede no gustarles. Pregunta siempre a la persona qué le interesa.
sheet.en: If you want to support an autistic person's social connection, it may be worth exploring hands-on activities with peers, such as theatre, in a welcoming community setting. This is an idea to consider, not a recipe. This is a review and conceptual paper about social competence interventions for autistic children, describing a programme called SENSE Theatre. Earlier research only shows early feasibility, and more rigorous studies are still needed. Feasible does not mean it helps everyone, and some people may not enjoy it. Always ask the person what interests them.
sheet.sv: Om du vill stödja en autistisk persons sociala kontakter kan det vara värt att utforska aktiviteter där man lär sig genom att göra tillsammans med jämnåriga, till exempel teater, i en välkomnande miljö i närsamhället. Det är en idé att överväga, inte ett recept. Detta är en översikts- och konceptuell artikel om insatser för social kompetens hos autistiska barn, som beskriver ett program kallat SENSE Theatre. Tidigare forskning visar bara att det verkar genomförbart, och mer rigorösa studier behövs. Genomförbart betyder inte att det hjälper alla, och vissa gillar det kanske inte. Fråga alltid personen vad hen är intresserad av.

title: Views on researcher-community engagement in autism research in the United Kingdom: a mixed-methods study.
authors: Pellicano E, Dinsmore A, Charman T
abstract: There has been a substantial increase in research activity on autism during the past decade. Research into effective ways of responding to the immediate needs of autistic people is, however, less advanced, as are efforts at translating basic science research into service provision. Involving community members in research is one potential way of reducing this gap. This study therefore investigated the views of community involvement in autism research both from the perspectives of autism researchers and of community members, including autistic adults, family members and practitioners. Results from a large-scale questionnaire study (n = 1,516) showed that researchers perceive themselves to be engaged with the autism community but that community members, most notably autistic people and their families, did not share this view. Focus groups/interviews with 72 participants further identified the potential benefits and remaining challenges to involvement in research, especially regarding the distinct perspectives of different stakeholders. Researchers were skeptical about the possibilities of dramatically increasing community engagement, while community members themselves spoke about the challenges to fully understanding and influencing the research process. We suggest that the lack of a shared approach to community engagement in UK autism research represents a key roadblock to translational endeavors.

sheet.es: Si le invitan a participar en una investigación sobre autismo, pregunte cómo se tendrán en cuenta las opiniones de las personas autistas y sus familias, y cómo recibirá los resultados. Es una pregunta razonable. Este estudio de métodos mixtos en el Reino Unido incluyó un cuestionario con n = 1,516 y grupos focales o entrevistas con 72 participantes: personas investigadoras, adultos autistas, familiares y profesionales. Las personas investigadoras se veían implicadas con la comunidad, pero las personas autistas y sus familias no lo percibían así. Como límite, recoge opiniones, no prueba qué método de participación funciona mejor, y se centra en el Reino Unido, así que puede no reflejar otros lugares ni a todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you are invited to take part in autism research, it is reasonable to ask how autistic people's and families' views will be included, and how you will hear about the results. This mixed-methods study in the United Kingdom used a questionnaire (n = 1,516) plus focus groups or interviews with 72 participants, including researchers, autistic adults, family members and practitioners. Researchers felt they were engaged with the autism community, but autistic people and their families did not share that view. A limit: it records opinions rather than testing which way of involving people works best, and it focuses on the UK, so it may not reflect other places or every person.
sheet.sv: Om du blir inbjuden att delta i autismforskning är det rimligt att fråga hur autistiska personers och familjers åsikter tas med, och hur du får veta resultaten. Den här studien med blandade metoder i Storbritannien använde ett frågeformulär (n = 1,516) samt fokusgrupper eller intervjuer med 72 deltagare, bland dem forskare, autistiska vuxna, familjemedlemmar och yrkesverksamma. Forskarna ansåg sig vara engagerade i autismgemenskapen, men autistiska personer och deras familjer delade inte den bilden. En begränsning är att studien samlar åsikter och inte testar vilket sätt att involvera människor som fungerar bäst, och den gäller Storbritannien, så den speglar kanske inte andra platser eller alla personer.

title: A Randomised Control Trial of the Impact of a Computer-Based Activity Programme upon the Fitness of Children with Autism.
authors: Dickinson K, Place M
abstract: The poor levels of fitness in children with autism are prompting concern for the children's future health. This study looked to assess if a computer-based activity programme could improve fitness levels (as reflected in cardiopulmonary function) of these children, and achieve a reduction in their body mass index. In a randomised controlled trial, 50 children with autism (of which 33 were under the age of 11 years and 39 were boys) were allocated to an intervention group which encouraged them to use the Nintendo Wii and the software package "Mario and Sonics at the Olympics" in addition to their routine physical education classes. 50 children with autism (34 under the age of 11 years and 40 being boys) acted as controls. At the end of one year, analysis of the changes in scores using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) on the Eurofit fitness tests showed that the intervention group had made statistically significant improvement on all tests other than flexibility. These improvements were also significantly better than controls. This type of intervention appears to be an effective addition to standard fitness training in order to help children with autism improve their fitness levels.

sheet.es: Si a un niño autista le atraen los videojuegos, un juego activo con consola, como complemento de la educación física, puede ser una forma de moverse más. Puedes probarlo como opción, sin imponerlo. La evidencia es un ensayo aleatorizado de un año con 50 niños autistas en el grupo de intervención, que usó la Nintendo Wii con "Mario and Sonics at the Olympics", y 50 como grupo control. El grupo de intervención mejoró en todas las pruebas de condición física Eurofit salvo la flexibilidad, y más que el grupo control. Como límites, el estudio no dice cómo vivió el juego cada niño y sus resultados no valen para todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If an autistic child enjoys video games, active console play alongside physical education may be one more way to get moving. You can offer it as an option, not a demand. The evidence is a one-year randomised controlled trial: 50 autistic children in the intervention group used the Nintendo Wii with "Mario and Sonics at the Olympics", and 50 were controls. The intervention group improved on all Eurofit fitness tests except flexibility, and more than the controls did. As limits, the abstract does not describe how each child experienced the games, and results cannot be assumed to apply to every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om ett autistiskt barn gillar dataspel kan aktivt spelande med konsol vid sidan av idrottslektionerna vara ett sätt att röra sig mer. Erbjud det som ett val, inte som ett krav. Underlaget är en randomiserad kontrollerad studie under ett år: 50 autistiska barn i interventionsgruppen använde Nintendo Wii med "Mario and Sonics at the Olympics" och 50 var kontroller. Interventionsgruppen förbättrades på alla Eurofit-konditionstester utom rörlighet, och mer än kontrollgruppen. Som begränsningar beskriver sammanfattningen inte hur varje barn upplevde spelen, och resultaten gäller inte automatiskt alla autistiska personer.

title: Group cognitive behavioural therapy and group recreational activity for adults with autism spectrum disorders: a preliminary randomized controlled trial.
authors: Hesselmark E, Plenty S, Bejerot S
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Although adults with autism spectrum disorder are an increasingly identified patient population, few treatment options are available. This preliminary randomized controlled open trial with a parallel design developed two group interventions for adults with autism spectrum disorders and intelligence within the normal range: cognitive behavioural therapy and recreational activity. Both interventions comprised 36 weekly 3-h sessions led by two therapists in groups of 6-8 patients. A total of 68 psychiatric patients with autism spectrum disorders participated in the study. Outcome measures were Quality of Life Inventory, Sense of Coherence Scale, Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale and an exploratory analysis on measures of psychiatric health. Participants in both treatment conditions reported an increased quality of life at post-treatment (d = 0.39, p < 0.001), with no difference between interventions. No amelioration of psychiatric symptoms was observed. The dropout rate was lower with cognitive behavioural therapy than with recreational activity, and participants in cognitive behavioural therapy rated themselves as more generally improved, as well as more improved regarding expression of needs and understanding of difficulties. Both interventions appear to be promising treatment options for adults with autism spectrum disorder. The interventions' similar efficacy may be due to the common elements, structure and group setting. Cognitive behavioural therapy may be additionally beneficial in terms of increasing specific skills and minimizing dropout.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta busca apoyo en grupo, tanto un grupo de terapia cognitivo-conductual como uno de actividades recreativas pueden ser opciones a valorar con su equipo de salud. Conviene fijarse en que haya estructura clara y un grupo estable. Evidencia: ensayo aleatorizado preliminar con 68 pacientes psiquiátricos adultos con inteligencia dentro de la norma; ambos grupos, de 36 sesiones semanales, informaron mayor calidad de vida (d = 0.39, p < 0.001). No se observó mejora de síntomas psiquiátricos. Quienes hicieron terapia abandonaron menos y se sintieron más mejorados. Límites: estudio preliminar, abierto, sin personas con discapacidad intelectual; no es una regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult is looking for group support, either a cognitive behavioural therapy group or a recreational activity group may be worth discussing with their care team. Look for clear structure and a steady group. Evidence: a preliminary randomized trial with 68 adult psychiatric patients with intelligence in the normal range; both groups, 36 weekly sessions, reported higher quality of life (d = 0.39, p < 0.001). No improvement in psychiatric symptoms was seen. Fewer people dropped out of the therapy group, and they rated themselves as more improved. Limits: it was preliminary and open, did not include people with intellectual disability, and is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen söker stöd i grupp kan både en grupp med kognitiv beteendeterapi och en grupp med fritidsaktiviteter vara värda att diskutera med vårdteamet. Titta efter tydlig struktur och en stabil grupp. Evidens: en preliminär randomiserad studie med 68 vuxna psykiatriska patienter med normal intelligens; båda grupperna, med 36 veckosessioner, rapporterade bättre livskvalitet (d = 0.39, p < 0.001). Ingen förbättring av psykiatriska symtom sågs. Färre hoppade av terapigruppen, och deltagarna där bedömde sig som mer förbättrade. Begränsningar: studien var preliminär och öppen, omfattade inte personer med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning och är ingen regel för alla.

title: What should autism research focus upon? Community views and priorities from the United Kingdom.
authors: Pellicano E, Dinsmore A, Charman T
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: The rise in the measured prevalence of autism has been accompanied by much new research and research investment internationally. This study sought to establish whether the pattern of current UK autism research funding maps on to the concerns of the autism community. Interviews and focus groups were conducted with autistic adults, family members, practitioners and researchers to identify their priorities for research. We also captured the views of a large number of stakeholders via an online survey. There was a clear disparity between the United Kingdom's pattern of funding for autism research and the priorities articulated by the majority of participants. There was general consensus that future priorities for autism research should lie in those areas that make a difference to people's day-to-day lives. There needs to be greater involvement of the autism community both in priority setting and in research more broadly to ensure that resources reach where they are most needed and can make the most impact.

sheet.es: Su experiencia diaria cuenta como conocimiento. Si le ofrecen participar en investigación, puede preguntar cómo ayudará en la vida cotidiana y si personas autistas y familias participaron en su diseño. También puede compartir sus prioridades, como apoyos prácticos, servicios o bienestar, con profesionales y organizaciones. Este estudio del Reino Unido combinó entrevistas y grupos focales con adultos autistas, familiares, profesionales e investigadores, más una encuesta en línea amplia; la mayoría quería investigación que mejore el día a día, algo distinto de lo que se financiaba. Sus límites: refleja opiniones de un país en 2014 y quienes respondieron quizá no representen a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: Your everyday experience counts as knowledge. If you are invited to take part in research, you can ask how it will help daily life and whether autistic people and families helped shape it. You can also share your own priorities, such as practical support, services or wellbeing, with professionals and organisations. This UK study combined interviews and focus groups with autistic adults, family members, practitioners and researchers, plus a large online survey; most wanted research that improves day-to-day life, which differed from what was being funded. Its limits: it reflects views from one country in 2014, and those who responded may not represent all autistic people.
sheet.sv: Din vardagserfarenhet räknas som kunskap. Om du blir tillfrågad att delta i forskning kan du fråga hur den ska hjälpa i vardagen och om autistiska personer och familjer varit med och utformat den. Du kan också berätta om dina egna prioriteringar, som praktiskt stöd, tjänster eller välmående, för yrkesverksamma och organisationer. Denna brittiska studie kombinerade intervjuer och fokusgrupper med autistiska vuxna, anhöriga, yrkesverksamma och forskare, samt en stor webbenkät; de flesta ville ha forskning som förbättrar vardagen, vilket skilde sig från vad som finansierades. Begränsningar: den speglar åsikter från ett land 2014, och de som svarade representerar kanske inte alla autistiska personer.

title: The relationship between sleep and behavior in autism spectrum disorder (ASD): a review.
authors: Cohen S, Conduit R, Lockley SW, Rajaratnam SM, Cornish KM
abstract: Although there is evidence that significant sleep problems are common in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and that poor sleep exacerbates problematic daytime behavior, such relationships have received very little attention in both research and clinical practice. Treatment guidelines to help manage challenging behaviors in ASD fail to mention sleep at all, or they present a very limited account. Moreover, limited attention is given to children with low-functioning autism, those individuals who often experience the most severe sleep disruption and behavioral problems. This paper describes the nature of sleep difficulties in ASD and highlights the complexities of sleep disruption in individuals with low-functioning autism. It is proposed that profiling ASD children based on the nature of their sleep disruption might help to understand symptom and behavioral profiles (or vice versa) and therefore lead to better-targeted interventions. This paper concludes with a discussion of the limitations of current knowledge and proposes areas that are important for future research. Treating disordered sleep in ASD has great potential to improve daytime behavior and family functioning in this vulnerable population.

sheet.es: Si un día resulta especialmente difícil para tu hijo o hija, vale la pena mirar también cómo durmió. Anotar durante unas semanas horas de sueño, despertares y cómo fue el día puede ayudar a ver patrones y a hablar con el equipo de salud sobre el descanso, no solo sobre la conducta. Esta revisión de 2014 reunió estudios sobre sueño y conducta en niños y niñas autistas, incluidos quienes necesitan más apoyo, y señala que el sueño suele quedar fuera de las guías. Su límite: no aporta datos nuevos y la investigación disponible era escasa, sobre todo en autistas con más necesidades de apoyo.
sheet.en: If your child is having an especially hard day, it can help to also look at how they slept. Keeping simple notes for a few weeks on sleep times, night waking and how the day went may reveal patterns and help you raise sleep, not just behaviour, with your healthcare team. This 2014 review brought together studies on sleep and daytime behaviour in autistic children, including those with higher support needs, and notes that sleep is often missing from guidelines. Its limit: it adds no new data, and the research it drew on was sparse, especially for autistic children with higher support needs.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn har en särskilt tung dag kan det hjälpa att också titta på hur hen har sovit. Att under några veckor anteckna sovtider, nattliga uppvaknanden och hur dagen blev kan visa mönster och göra det lättare att ta upp sömnen, inte bara beteendet, med vården. Den här översikten från 2014 samlade studier om sömn och beteende under dagen hos autistiska barn, även barn med stora stödbehov, och påpekar att sömn ofta saknas i riktlinjer. Begränsning: den tillför inga nya data, och forskningen den byggde på var tunn, särskilt för autistiska barn med stora stödbehov.

title: A role for synaptic zinc in ProSAP/Shank PSD scaffold malformation in autism spectrum disorders.
authors: Grabrucker AM
abstract: The establishment and maintenance of synaptic contacts as well as synaptic plasticity are crucial factors for normal brain function. The functional properties of a synapse are largely dependent on the molecular setup of synaptic proteins. Multidomain proteins of the ProSAP/Shank family act as major organizing scaffolding elements of the postsynaptic density (PSD). Interestingly, ProSAP/Shank proteins at glutamatergic synapses have been linked to a variety of Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASDs) including Phelan McDermid Syndrome, and deregulation of ProSAP/Shank has been reported in Alzheimer's disease. Although the precise molecular mechanism of the dysfunction of these proteins remains unclear, an emerging model is that mutations or deletions impair neuronal circuitry by disrupting the formation, plasticity and maturation of glutamatergic synapses. Several PSD proteins associated with ASDs are part of a complex centered around ProSAP/Shank proteins and many ProSAP/Shank interaction partners play a role in signaling within dendritic spines. Interfering with any one of the members of this signaling complex might change the output and drive the system towards synaptic dysfunction. Based on recent data, it is possible that the concerted action of ProSAP/Shank and Zn(2+) is essential for the structural integrity of the PSD. This interplay might regulate postsynaptic receptor composition, but also transsynaptic signaling. It might be possible that environmental factors like nutritional Zn(2+) status or metal ion homeostasis in general intersect with this distinct pathway centered around ProSAP/Shank proteins and the deregulation of any of these two factors may lead to ASDs.

sheet.es: Esto es investigación básica y no ofrece ningún cambio práctico para mañana. Si le preocupa la alimentación de una persona autista, hable con su pediatra o con un profesional sanitario antes de modificar nada. La evidencia es una revisión de la literatura sobre proteínas de las sinapsis (ProSAP/Shank) y el zinc; no describe a un grupo de participantes. Sus propias autoras y autores plantean que el papel del zinc es una posibilidad y que el mecanismo molecular sigue sin estar claro. No demuestra causas ni sirve como regla para todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: This is basic science and offers no practical change for tomorrow. If you wonder about an autistic person's diet, talk with a paediatrician or health professional before changing anything. The evidence is a review of the literature on synaptic proteins (ProSAP/Shank) and zinc; it does not describe a group of participants. The authors themselves say zinc's role is a possibility and the molecular mechanism remains unclear. It does not prove causes and is not a rule for every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Detta är grundforskning och ger ingen praktisk förändring till imorgon. Om du funderar över en autistisk persons kost, prata med barnläkare eller annan vårdpersonal innan du ändrar något. Underlaget är en översikt av litteraturen om synapsproteiner (ProSAP/Shank) och zink; den beskriver inte en grupp deltagare. Författarna själva anger att zinkets roll är en möjlighet och att den molekylära mekanismen fortfarande är oklar. Den visar inte orsaker och är ingen regel för alla autistiska personer.

title: Sex/gender differences and autism: setting the scene for future research.
authors: Lai MC, Lombardo MV, Auyeung B, Chakrabarti B, Baron-Cohen S
journal: Journal of the American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry
abstract: Objective The relationship between sex/gender differences and autism has attracted a variety of research ranging from clinical and neurobiological to etiological, stimulated by the male bias in autism prevalence. Findings are complex and do not always relate to each other in a straightforward manner. Distinct but interlinked questions on the relationship between sex/gender differences and autism remain underaddressed. To better understand the implications from existing research and to help design future studies, we propose a 4-level conceptual framework to clarify the embedded themes. Method We searched PubMed for publications before September 2014 using search terms "'sex OR gender OR females' AND autism." A total of 1,906 articles were screened for relevance, along with publications identified via additional literature reviews, resulting in 329 articles that were reviewed. Results Level 1, "Nosological and diagnostic challenges," concerns the question, "How should autism be defined and diagnosed in males and females?" Level 2, "Sex/gender-independent and sex/gender-dependent characteristics," addresses the question, "What are the similarities and differences between males and females with autism?" Level 3, "General models of etiology: liability and threshold," asks the question, "How is the liability for developing autism linked to sex/gender?" Level 4, "Specific etiological-developmental mechanisms," focuses on the question, "What etiological-developmental mechanisms of autism are implicated by sex/gender and/or sexual/gender differentiation?" Conclusions Using this conceptual framework, findings can be more clearly summarized, and the implications of the links between findings from different levels can become clearer. Based on this 4-level framework, we suggest future research directions, methodology, and specific topics in sex/gender differences and autism.

title: Recent update of autism spectrum disorders.
authors: Kim SK
abstract: In patients with a language developmental delay, it is necessary to make a differential diagnosis for autism spectrum disorders (ASDs), specific language impairment, and mental retardation. It is important that pediatricians recognize the signs and symptoms of ASDs, as many patients with language developmental delays are ultimately diagnosed with ASDs. Pediatricians play an important role in the early recognition of ASDs, because they are usually the first point of contact for children with ASDs. A revision of the diagnostic criteria of ASDs was proposed in the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, fifth edition (DSM-5) that was released in May 2013. The autism spectrum describes a range of conditions classified as neurodevelopmental disorders in the fifth edition of the DSM. The new diagnostic criteria encompasses previous elements from the diagnosis of autistic disorder, Asperger disorder, childhood disintegrative disorder, and pervasive developmental disorder-not otherwise specified. An additional change to the DSM includes synthesizing the section on social and communication deficits into one domain. In ASD patients, the appropriate behavioral therapies and rehabilitation treatments significantly affect the prognosis. Therefore, this makes early diagnosis and treatment very important. In conclusion, pediatricians need to be able to recognize the signs and symptoms of ASDs and be attentive to them in order to make an early diagnosis and provide treatment.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija tiene un retraso en el lenguaje, puede llevar sus observaciones a la consulta pediátrica y pedir que se valoren distintas explicaciones, entre ellas el autismo. Anote cuándo y cómo se comunica en el día a día. Esta revisión indica que muchos niños con retraso del lenguaje acaban recibiendo un diagnóstico de autismo, y que las terapias conductuales y de rehabilitación adecuadas influyen en el pronóstico. Es una revisión de la literatura, no un estudio con participantes propios, y se centra en el papel de pediatras y en los criterios del DSM-5. No describe cómo viven las personas autistas su propia experiencia, y no sirve como regla para cada niño.
sheet.en: If your child has a language delay, you can bring your observations to the pediatric visit and ask that several explanations be considered, including autism. Jot down when and how they communicate day to day. This review says many children with language delay are later diagnosed as autistic, and that suitable behavioral and rehabilitation therapies affect prognosis. It is a review of the literature, not a study with its own participants, and it focuses on the role of pediatricians and the DSM-5 criteria. It does not describe how autistic people experience their own lives, and it is not a rule for every child.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn har en språklig försening kan du ta med dina observationer till barnläkaren och be att flera förklaringar övervägs, däribland autism. Anteckna när och hur barnet kommunicerar i vardagen. Den här översikten uppger att många barn med språklig försening senare får en autismdiagnos, och att lämpliga beteendeterapier och rehabilitering påverkar prognosen. Det är en översikt av litteraturen, inte en studie med egna deltagare, och den handlar om barnläkares roll och DSM-5-kriterierna. Den beskriver inte hur autistiska personer själva upplever sitt liv och är ingen regel för varje barn.

title: Update on the implication of potassium channels in autism: K(+) channelautism spectrum disorder.
authors: Guglielmi L, Servettini I, Caramia M, Catacuzzeno L, Franciolini F, D'Adamo MC, Pessia M
abstract: Autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) are characterized by impaired ability to properly implement environmental stimuli that are essential to achieve a state of social and cultural exchange. Indeed, the main features of ASD are impairments of interpersonal relationships, verbal and non-verbal communication and restricted and repetitive behaviors. These aspects are often accompanied by several comorbidities such as motor delay, praxis impairment, gait abnormalities, insomnia, and above all epilepsy. Genetic analyses of autistic individuals uncovered deleterious mutations in several K(+) channel types strengthening the notion that their intrinsic dysfunction may play a central etiologic role in ASD. However, indirect implication of K(+) channels in ASD has been also reported. For instance, loss of fragile X mental retardation protein (FMRP) results in K(+) channels deregulation, network dysfunction and ASD-like cognitive and behavioral symptoms. This review provides an update on direct and indirect implications of K(+) channels in ASDs. Owing to a mounting body of evidence associating a channelopathy pathogenesis to autism and showing that nearly 500 ion channel proteins are encoded by the human genome, we propose to classify ASDs - whose susceptibility is significantly enhanced by ion channels defects, either in a monogenic or multigenic condition - in a new category named " c hannel A utism S pectrum D isorder" (channelASD; cASD) and introduce a new taxonomy (e.g., Kv x.y-channelASD and likewise Nav x.y-channelASD, Cav x.y-channelASD; etc.). This review also highlights some degree of clinical and genetic overlap between K(+) channelASDs and K(+) channelepsies, whereby such correlation suggests that a subcategory characterized by a channelASD-channelepsy phenotype may be distinguished. Ultimately, this overview aims to further understand the different clinical subgroups and help parse out the distinct biological basis of autism that are essential to establish patient-tailored treatments.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista que además tiene epilepsia, trastornos del sueño o dificultades motoras, coméntalo con su equipo clínico: pueden estar relacionados y merece una evaluación conjunta. Esta es una revisión de la literatura científica, no un estudio con participantes nuevos. Resume hallazgos genéticos que vinculan los canales de potasio con algunas presentaciones del autismo y propone nuevas categorías. Sus límites: es una propuesta teórica, no demuestra causas en cada persona, usa lenguaje de déficit y no ofrece pautas prácticas directas. Cualquier decisión médica corresponde a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person who also has epilepsy, sleep difficulties or motor differences, mention this to their clinical team: these may be connected and are worth looking at together. This is a review of existing scientific literature, not a study with new participants. It summarises genetic findings linking potassium channels to some presentations of autism and proposes new categories. Its limits: it is a theoretical proposal, it does not show a cause in any one person, it uses deficit-based language, and it gives no direct practical guidance. Any medical decision belongs with a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person som också har epilepsi, sömnsvårigheter eller motoriska skillnader kan du ta upp det med personens vårdteam: det kan hänga ihop och är värt att se över tillsammans. Det här är en översikt av befintlig forskning, inte en studie med nya deltagare. Den sammanfattar genetiska fynd som kopplar kaliumkanaler till vissa former av autism och föreslår nya kategorier. Begränsningar: det är ett teoretiskt förslag, det visar inte orsaken hos en enskild person, språket utgår från brister och det ger inga direkta praktiska råd. Medicinska beslut hör till en läkare.

title: Zinc in gut-brain interaction in autism and neurological disorders.
authors: Vela G, Stark P, Socha M, Sauer AK, Hagmeyer S, Grabrucker AM
abstract: A growing amount of research indicates that abnormalities in the gastrointestinal (GI) system during development might be a common factor in multiple neurological disorders and might be responsible for some of the shared comorbidities seen among these diseases. For example, many patients with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) have symptoms associated with GI disorders. Maternal zinc status may be an important factor given the multifaceted effect of zinc on gut development and morphology in the offspring. Zinc status influences and is influenced by multiple factors and an interdependence of prenatal and early life stress, immune system abnormalities, impaired GI functions, and zinc deficiency can be hypothesized. In line with this, systemic inflammatory events and prenatal stress have been reported to increase the risk for ASD. Thus, here, we will review the current literature on the role of zinc in gut formation, a possible link between gut and brain development in ASD and other neurological disorders with shared comorbidities, and tie in possible effects on the immune system. Based on these data, we present a novel model outlining how alterations in the maternal zinc status might pathologically impact the offspring leading to impairments in brain functions later in life.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista tiene molestias digestivas, merece la pena anotarlas y comentarlas con su profesional de salud; el intestino y el bienestar general pueden estar relacionados. Esta es una revisión de la literatura, no un ensayo con participantes: reúne estudios previos sobre el zinc, el desarrollo del intestino y el cerebro, y propone un modelo nuevo. Sus límites: el modelo es una hipótesis, no demuestra que el zinc cause nada ni sirve como regla para todas las personas. Cualquier decisión sobre suplementos o alimentación debe tomarse con un profesional sanitario.
sheet.en: If an autistic person has digestive discomfort, it is worth noting it down and raising it with their health professional; gut health and general wellbeing may be connected. This is a review of existing literature, not a trial with participants: it gathers earlier research on zinc, gut development and brain development, and proposes a new model. Its limits: the model is a hypothesis, it does not show that zinc causes anything, and it is not a rule for every person. Any decision about supplements or diet belongs with a health professional.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person har magproblem är det värt att anteckna dem och ta upp dem med vårdpersonal; tarmen och det allmänna måendet kan hänga ihop. Det här är en översikt av tidigare litteratur, inte en studie med deltagare: den samlar forskning om zink, tarmens utveckling och hjärnans utveckling och föreslår en ny modell. Begränsningar: modellen är en hypotes, den visar inte att zink orsakar något och gäller inte som regel för alla. Beslut om kosttillskott eller kost fattas tillsammans med vårdpersonal.

title: Measuring autistic traits in the general population: a systematic review of the Autism-Spectrum Quotient (AQ) in a nonclinical population sample of 6,900 typical adult males and females.
authors: Ruzich E, Allison C, Smith P, Watson P, Auyeung B, Ring H, Baron-Cohen S
abstract: The Autism-Spectrum Quotient (AQ) is a self-report measure of autistic traits. It is frequently cited in diverse fields and has been administered to adults of at least average intelligence with autism and to nonclinical controls, as well as to clinical control groups such as those with schizophrenia, prosopagnosia, anorexia, and depression. However, there has been no empirical systematic review of the AQ since its inception in 2001. The present study reports a comprehensive systematic review of the literature to estimate a reliable mean AQ score in individuals without a diagnosis of an autism spectrum condition (ASC), in order to establish a reference norm for future studies. A systematic search of computerized databases was performed to identify studies that administered the AQ to nonclinical participant samples representing the adult male and female general population. Inclusion was based on a set of formalized criteria that evaluated the quality of the study, the usage of the AQ, and the population being assessed. After selection, 73 articles, detailing 6,934 nonclinical participants, as well as 1,963 matched clinical cases of ASC (from available cohorts within each individual study), were analyzed. Mean AQ score for the nonclinical population was 16.94 (95% CI 11.6, 20.0), while mean AQ score for the clinical population with ASC was found to be 35.19 (95% CI 27.6, 41.1). In addition, in the nonclinical population, a sex difference in autistic traits was found, although no sex difference in AQ score was seen in the clinical ASC population. These findings have implications for the study of autistic traits in the general population. Here, we confirm previous norms with more rigorous data and for the first time establish average AQ scores based on a systematic review, for populations of adult males and females with and without ASC. Finally, we advise future researchers to avoid risk of bias by carefully considering the recruitment strategy for both clinical and nonclinical groups and to demonstrate transparency by reporting recruitment methods for all participants.

sheet.es: Un cuestionario como el AQ puede servir como una pista orientativa sobre rasgos autistas, pero no es un diagnóstico ni define a una persona. Si lo usáis, tomadlo como punto de partida para conversar. La evidencia es una revisión sistemática de 73 artículos con 6,934 participantes adultos sin diagnóstico y 1,963 personas adultas autistas, que aportó puntuaciones medias de referencia: 16.94 y 35.19. Sus límites: es un autoinforme, incluye adultos de inteligencia media o superior, y los autores advierten de posibles sesgos en cómo se reclutó a los grupos. No sirve como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: A questionnaire like the AQ can be a rough pointer to autistic traits, but it is not a diagnosis and does not define a person. If you use it, treat it as a starting point for conversation. The evidence is a systematic review of 73 articles, covering 6,934 adult participants without a diagnosis and 1,963 autistic adults, which gave reference average scores of 16.94 and 35.19. Its limits: it is a self-report, it covers adults of at least average intelligence, and the authors warn of possible bias in how groups were recruited. It is not a rule for any one person.
sheet.sv: Ett frågeformulär som AQ kan ge en grov fingervisning om autistiska drag, men det är ingen diagnos och definierar inte en person. Om ni använder det, se det som en startpunkt för samtal. Underlaget är en systematisk översikt av 73 artiklar med 6,934 vuxna deltagare utan diagnos och 1,963 autistiska vuxna, som gav genomsnittliga referenspoäng på 16.94 och 35.19. Begränsningar: det är ett självskattningsformulär, det gäller vuxna med minst genomsnittlig intelligens, och forskarna varnar för risk för snedvridning i hur grupperna rekryterades. Det är ingen regel för en enskild person.

title: Complementary and Alternative Therapies for Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Brondino N, Fusar-Poli L, Rocchetti M, Provenzani U, Barale F, Politi P
journal: Evidence-based complementary and alternative medicine : eCAM
abstract: Background. Complementary and alternative medicine (CAM) represents a popular therapeutic option for patients with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Unfortunately, there is a paucity of data regarding the efficacy of CAM in ASD. The aim of the present systematic review is to investigate trials of CAM in ASD. Material and Methods. We searched the following databases: MEDLINE, EMBASE, Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, CINAHL, Psychology and Behavioral Sciences Collection, Agricola, and Food Science Source. Results. Our literature search identified 2687 clinical publications. After the title/abstract screening, 139 publications were obtained for detailed evaluation. After detailed evaluation 67 studies were included, from hand search of references we retrieved 13 additional studies for a total of 80. Conclusion. There is no conclusive evidence supporting the efficacy of CAM therapies in ASD. Promising results are reported for music therapy, sensory integration therapy, acupuncture, and massage.

sheet.es: Si piensa en terapias complementarias o alternativas, trátelas como opciones por explorar con calma, no como soluciones probadas. Observe cómo responde la persona autista y pida su opinión. Esta revisión sistemática buscó en varias bases de datos y, al final, incluyó 80 estudios. Concluye que no hay evidencia concluyente de que estas terapias funcionen; se informaron resultados prometedores para musicoterapia, integración sensorial, acupuntura y masaje. Los resultados prometedores no son una prueba firme y no valen para todas las personas. El resumen no detalla quiénes participaron. Si una terapia implica un producto o tratamiento médico, la decisión corresponde a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If you are considering complementary or alternative therapies, treat them as options to explore calmly, not as proven solutions. Watch how the autistic person responds and ask for their view. This systematic review searched several databases and ended up including 80 studies. It concludes there is no conclusive evidence that these therapies work; promising results were reported for music therapy, sensory integration therapy, acupuncture and massage. Promising results are not firm proof and do not apply to every person. The abstract does not say who took part. If a therapy involves a product or medical treatment, that decision belongs with a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om ni funderar på komplementära eller alternativa terapier, se dem som alternativ att utforska i lugn takt, inte som beprövade lösningar. Observera hur den autistiska personen reagerar och fråga efter hens egen uppfattning. Denna systematiska översikt sökte i flera databaser och inkluderade till sist 80 studier. Slutsatsen är att det inte finns några avgörande belägg för att dessa terapier fungerar; lovande resultat rapporterades för musikterapi, sensorisk integrationsterapi, akupunktur och massage. Lovande resultat är inget säkert bevis och gäller inte alla. Sammanfattningen anger inte vilka som deltog. Om en terapi innefattar en produkt eller medicinsk behandling hör beslutet hemma hos en läkare eller annan kliniker.

title: The Role of Epigenetic Change in Autism Spectrum Disorders.
authors: Loke YJ, Hannan AJ, Craig JM
abstract: Autism spectrum disorders (ASD) are a heterogeneous group of neurodevelopmental disorders characterized by problems with social communication, social interaction, and repetitive or restricted behaviors. ASD are comorbid with other disorders including attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, epilepsy, Rett syndrome, and Fragile X syndrome. Neither the genetic nor the environmental components have been characterized well enough to aid diagnosis or treatment of non-syndromic ASD. However, genome-wide association studies have amassed evidence suggesting involvement of hundreds of genes and a variety of associated genetic pathways. Recently, investigators have turned to epigenetics, a prime mediator of environmental effects on genomes and phenotype, to characterize changes in ASD that constitute a molecular level on top of DNA sequence. Though in their infancy, such studies have the potential to increase our understanding of the etiology of ASD and may assist in the development of biomarkers for its prediction, diagnosis, prognosis, and eventually in its prevention and intervention. This review focuses on the first few epigenome-wide association studies of ASD and discusses future directions.

sheet.es: Esta revisión no ofrece nada que cambie la rutina de mañana: no hay pruebas ni pautas nuevas para casa o la escuela. Puede servir como contexto: la investigación sobre la biología del autismo sigue en marcha y, por ahora, no sustituye lo que sabe la persona autista ni su entorno. Es una revisión de los primeros estudios epigenéticos del autismo, es decir, de cambios moleculares que se suman a la secuencia del ADN. Los propios autores dicen que estos estudios están en sus comienzos y que aún no se conocen bien los componentes genéticos ni ambientales. No sirve para diagnosticar ni para predecir nada en una persona concreta.
sheet.en: This review gives nothing that changes tomorrow's routine: there are no new tests or guidance for home or school. It is useful as background: research into the biology of autism continues, and for now it does not replace what the autistic person and those around them know. It reviews the first epigenetic studies of autism, meaning molecular changes layered on top of DNA sequence. The authors themselves say these studies are in their infancy and that the genetic and environmental components are not yet well understood. It cannot be used to diagnose or predict anything for an individual person.
sheet.sv: Den här översikten ger inget som ändrar morgondagens rutiner: den innehåller inga nya tester eller råd för hemmet eller skolan. Den är användbar som bakgrund: forskningen om autismens biologi pågår, och just nu ersätter den inte det som den autistiska personen och människorna runt omkring vet. Den går igenom de första epigenetiska studierna om autism, alltså molekylära förändringar utöver DNA-sekvensen. Författarna skriver själva att studierna är i sin linda och att de genetiska och miljömässiga delarna ännu inte är väl kartlagda. Den kan inte användas för att diagnostisera eller förutsäga något hos en enskild person.

title: Sex differences in brain plasticity: a new hypothesis for sex ratio bias in autism.
authors: Mottron L, Duret P, Mueller S, Moore RD, Forgeot d'Arc B, Jacquemont S, Xiong L
abstract: Several observations support the hypothesis that differences in synaptic and regional cerebral plasticity between the sexes account for the high ratio of males to females in autism. First, males are more susceptible than females to perturbations in genes involved in synaptic plasticity. Second, sex-related differences in non-autistic brain structure and function are observed in highly variable regions, namely, the heteromodal associative cortices, and overlap with structural particularities and enhanced activity of perceptual associative regions in autistic individuals. Finally, functional cortical reallocations following brain lesions in non-autistic adults (for example, traumatic brain injury, multiple sclerosis) are sex-dependent. Interactions between genetic sex and hormones may therefore result in higher synaptic and consecutively regional plasticity in perceptual brain areas in males than in females. The onset of autism may largely involve mutations altering synaptic plasticity that create a plastic reaction affecting the most variable and sexually dimorphic brain regions. The sex ratio bias in autism may arise because males have a lower threshold than females for the development of this plastic reaction following a genetic or environmental event.

sheet.es: Para el día a día, este trabajo no cambia lo que haces mañana: es una idea teórica sobre por qué se diagnostica autismo con más frecuencia en chicos que en chicas. Un recordatorio útil: si cuidas a una niña o mujer, sus rasgos autistas pueden ser igual de reales aunque se noten menos o se expresen de otra forma; confía en lo que observas y en lo que ella cuenta. En cuanto a la evidencia, es una hipótesis que reúne estudios previos de genética, imagen cerebral y lesiones cerebrales en adultos no autistas; no recogió datos nuevos con participantes. Su límite: es una propuesta por comprobar, no una explicación demostrada ni válida para cada persona.
sheet.en: For daily life, this paper does not change what you do tomorrow: it is a theoretical idea about why autism is diagnosed more often in boys than in girls. One useful reminder: if you support a girl or woman, her autistic traits can be just as real even when they are less visible or show up differently; trust what you notice and what she tells you. On the evidence, this is a hypothesis paper that brings together earlier studies on genetics, brain imaging and brain injury in non-autistic adults; it did not collect new data from participants. Its limit: it is a proposal still to be tested, not a proven explanation or one that fits every person.
sheet.sv: I vardagen ändrar den här artikeln inte vad du gör i morgon: den är en teoretisk idé om varför autism oftare diagnostiseras hos pojkar än hos flickor. En användbar påminnelse: om du stöttar en flicka eller kvinna kan hennes autistiska drag vara lika verkliga även när de syns mindre eller visar sig på andra sätt; lita på det du ser och det hon berättar. När det gäller underlaget är detta en hypotesartikel som sammanför tidigare studier om genetik, hjärnavbildning och hjärnskador hos icke-autistiska vuxna; inga nya data samlades in från deltagare. Begränsningen: det är ett förslag som behöver prövas, inte en bevisad förklaring eller något som gäller varje person.

title: The effectiveness of psychosocial interventions for anxiety in children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Kreslins A, Robertson AE, Melville C
journal: Child and adolescent psychiatry and mental health
abstract: Anxiety is a common problem in children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). This meta-analysis aimed to systematically evaluate the evidence for the use of psychosocial interventions to manage anxiety in this population. Cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) was the primary intervention modality studied. A comprehensive systematic search and study selection process was conducted. Separate statistical analyses were carried out for clinician-, parent-, and self-reported outcome measures. Sensitivity analyses were conducted by removing any outlying studies and any studies that did not use a CBT intervention. A subgroup analysis was performed to compare individual and group delivery of treatment. Ten randomised control trials involving a total of 470 participants were included. The overall SMD was d = 1.05 (95 % CI 0.45, 1.65; z = 3.45, p = 0.0006) for clinician- reported outcome measures; d = 1.00 (95%CI 0.21, 1.80; z = 2.47, p = 0.01) for parent-reported outcome measures; and d = 0.65 (95%CI -0.10, 1.07; z = 1.63, p = 0.10) for self-reported outcome measures. Clinician- and parent-reported outcome measures showed that psychosocial interventions were superior to waitlist and treatment-as-usual control conditions at post-treatment. However, the results of self-reported outcome measures failed to reach significance. The sensitivity analyses did not significantly change these results and the subgroup analysis indicated that individual treatment was more effective than group treatment. The main limitations of this review were the small number of included studies as well as the clinical and methodological variability between studies.

sheet.es: Si le preocupa la ansiedad de un niño o adolescente autista, puede preguntar a un profesional por la terapia cognitivo-conductual (TCC), que fue la intervención psicosocial más estudiada, y comentar si conviene en formato individual o grupal. Es un metaanálisis de 10 ensayos aleatorizados con 470 participantes. Según clínicos y familias, las intervenciones psicosociales superaron a la lista de espera y al tratamiento habitual; según los propios jóvenes, el resultado no alcanzó significación. El formato individual resultó más eficaz que el grupal. Hay pocos estudios y varían mucho entre sí, así que no sirve como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If you are worried about anxiety in an autistic child or teenager, you can ask a professional about cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT), the most studied psychosocial approach, and discuss whether individual or group sessions might suit them. This is a meta-analysis of 10 randomised trials with 470 participants. Clinicians and parents reported that psychosocial interventions beat waitlist and treatment-as-usual; the young people's own reports did not reach significance. Individual treatment worked better than group treatment. Few studies were included and they differed a lot, so this is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du oroar dig för ångest hos ett autistiskt barn eller en autistisk tonåring kan du fråga en yrkesperson om kognitiv beteendeterapi (KBT), den mest studerade psykosociala metoden, och prata om individuella eller gruppsessioner passar bäst. Detta är en metaanalys av 10 randomiserade studier med 470 deltagare. Kliniker och föräldrar rapporterade att psykosociala insatser var bättre än väntelista och sedvanlig behandling; de unga egna skattningar nådde inte signifikans. Individuell behandling fungerade bättre än gruppbehandling. Få studier ingick och de skilde sig mycket åt, så resultaten är ingen regel för varje person.

title: The effect of the video game Mindlight on anxiety symptoms in children with an Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Wijnhoven LA, Creemers DH, Engels RC, Granic I
abstract: Background In the clinical setting, a large proportion of children with an autism spectrum disorder (ASD) experience anxiety symptoms. Because anxiety is an important cause of impairment for children with an ASD, it is necessary that effective anxiety interventions are implemented for these children. Recently, a serious game called Mindlight has been developed that is focused on decreasing anxiety in children. This approach is based on recent research suggesting that video games might be suitable as an intervention vehicle to enhance mental health in children. In the present study it will be investigated whether Mindlight is effective in decreasing (sub) clinical anxiety symptoms in children who are diagnosed with an ASD. Methods/design The present study involves a randomized controlled trial (RCT) with two conditions (experimental versus control), in which it is investigated whether Mindlight is effective in decreasing (sub) clinical anxiety symptoms in children with an ASD. For this study, children of 8-16 years old with a diagnosis of an ASD and (sub) clinical anxiety symptoms will be randomly assigned to the experimental (N = 60) or the control (N = 60) condition. Children in the experimental condition will play Mindlight for one hour per week, for six consecutive weeks. Children in the control condition will play the puzzle game Triple Town, also for one hour per week and for six consecutive weeks. All children will complete assessments at baseline, post-intervention and 3-months follow-up. Furthermore, parents and teachers will also complete assessments at the same time points. The primary outcome will be child report of anxiety symptoms. Secondary outcomes will be parent report of child anxiety, child/parent report of depressive symptoms, and parent/teacher report of social functioning and behavior problems. Discussion This paper aims to describe a study that will examine the effect of the serious game Mindlight on (sub) clinical anxiety symptoms of children with an ASD in the age of 8-16 years old. It is expected that children in the experimental condition will show lower levels of anxiety symptoms at 3-months follow-up, compared to children in the control condition. If Mindlight turns out to be effective, it could be an important contribution to the already existing interventions for anxiety in children with an ASD. Mindlight could then be implemented as an evidence-based treatment for anxiety symptoms in children with an ASD in mental health institutes and special education schools. Trial registration Dutch Trial Register NTR5069 . Registered 20 April 2015.

sheet.es: Por ahora no hay resultados que indiquen si Mindlight ayuda; lo útil es saber que se está probando un videojuego para la ansiedad en niñez autista. Si su hijo o hija vive con ansiedad, puede comentarlo con su equipo de salud o su escuela. Evidencia: es el protocolo de un ensayo aleatorizado que incluirá a niños y niñas autistas de 8-16 años con síntomas de ansiedad; 60 jugarán Mindlight y 60 jugarán Triple Town, una hora por semana durante seis semanas. Límites: el texto describe el plan, no resultados, y no puede aplicarse a todas las personas.
sheet.en: There are no results yet showing whether Mindlight helps; what is useful to know is that a video game for anxiety is being tested with autistic children. If your child lives with anxiety, you can raise it with their health team or school. Evidence: this is the protocol of a randomized controlled trial that will include autistic children aged 8-16 with anxiety symptoms; 60 will play Mindlight and 60 will play Triple Town, one hour per week for six weeks. Limits: the paper describes the plan, not findings, and cannot be applied to every person.
sheet.sv: Det finns ännu inga resultat som visar om Mindlight hjälper; det användbara är att veta att ett datorspel mot ångest testas med autistiska barn. Om ditt barn har ångest kan du ta upp det med vården eller skolan. Evidens: detta är protokollet för en randomiserad kontrollerad studie med autistiska barn i åldern 8-16 år med ångestsymtom; 60 ska spela Mindlight och 60 ska spela Triple Town, en timme per vecka i sex veckor. Begränsningar: texten beskriver planen, inte resultat, och gäller inte alla personer.

title: Broader Autism Phenotype in Siblings of Children with ASD--A Review.
authors: Pisula E, Ziegart-Sadowska K
abstract: Although less pronounced, social, cognitive, and personality characteristics associated with autism spectrum disorders (ASD) may be present in people who do not meet ASD diagnostic criteria, especially in first-degree relatives of individuals with ASD. Research on these characteristics, referred to as broader autism phenotype (BAP), provides valuable data on potential expressions of autism-specific deficits in the context of family relations. This paper offers a review of research on BAP in siblings of individuals with ASD, focusing on reports regarding social, communication, and cognitive deficits, published from 1993 to 2014. The studies are divided into two groups based on participants' age: papers on preschool and older siblings of individuals with ASD; and publications on infants at risk for ASD. On the basis of this review, suggestions are offered for further research and its significance for our understanding of the genetic determinants of autism.

sheet.es: Si tienes un hijo autista y otros hijos, puede ser útil saber que algunos hermanos muestran rasgos sociales, de comunicación o de pensamiento parecidos, aunque más leves, sin ser autistas. Obsérvalos con curiosidad y apoya sus fortalezas y necesidades, sin etiquetarlos. Es una revisión de estudios publicados de 1993 a 2014 sobre hermanos de personas autistas, de edad preescolar o mayores, y bebés con mayor probabilidad de ser autistas. Sus límites: el resumen no da detalles de los resultados, usa un enfoque de déficits y no indica qué pasará en cada familia. Ante dudas, consulta a un profesional.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic child and have other children, it may help to know that some siblings show similar social, communication or thinking traits, usually milder, without being autistic. Notice them with curiosity and support their strengths and needs, without labelling them. This is a review of studies published from 1993 to 2014 on siblings of autistic people, preschool-age and older, and on infants more likely to be autistic. Its limits: the abstract gives no detailed results, it uses a deficit-focused lens, and it cannot tell you what will happen in any one family. If you have questions, talk to a professional.
sheet.sv: Om du har ett autistiskt barn och fler barn kan det vara bra att veta att vissa syskon har liknande sociala drag, kommunikationsdrag eller tankesätt, oftast mildare, utan att vara autistiska. Möt dem nyfiket och stötta deras styrkor och behov, utan att sätta etiketter. Detta är en översikt av studier publicerade 1993 till 2014 om syskon till autistiska personer, i förskoleåldern och äldre, samt spädbarn med större sannolikhet att vara autistiska. Begränsningar: sammanfattningen ger inga detaljerade resultat, har ett bristfokuserat synsätt och kan inte säga vad som gäller i en enskild familj. Vid frågor, prata med en yrkesperson.

title: A Novel System for Supporting Autism Diagnosis Using Home Videos: Iterative Development and Evaluation of System Design.
authors: Nazneen N, Rozga A, Smith CJ, Oberleitner R, Abowd GD, Arriaga RI
abstract: Background Observing behavior in the natural environment is valuable to obtain an accurate and comprehensive assessment of a child's behavior, but in practice it is limited to in-clinic observation. Research shows significant time lag between when parents first become concerned and when the child is finally diagnosed with autism. This lag can delay early interventions that have been shown to improve developmental outcomes. Objective To develop and evaluate the design of an asynchronous system that allows parents to easily collect clinically valid in-home videos of their child's behavior and supports diagnosticians in completing diagnostic assessment of autism. Methods First, interviews were conducted with 11 clinicians and 6 families to solicit feedback from stakeholders about the system concept. Next, the system was iteratively designed, informed by experiences of families using it in a controlled home-like experimental setting and a participatory design process involving domain experts. Finally, in-field evaluation of the system design was conducted with 5 families of children (4 with previous autism diagnosis and 1 child typically developing) and 3 diagnosticians. For each family, 2 diagnosticians, blind to the child's previous diagnostic status, independently completed an autism diagnosis via our system. We compared the outcome of the assessment between the 2 diagnosticians, and between each diagnostician and the child's previous diagnostic status. Results The system that resulted through the iterative design process includes (1) NODA smartCapture, a mobile phone-based application for parents to record prescribed video evidence at home; and (2) NODA Connect, a Web portal for diagnosticians to direct in-home video collection, access developmental history, and conduct an assessment by linking evidence of behaviors tagged in the videos to the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders criteria. Applying clinical judgment, the diagnostician concludes a diagnostic outcome. During field evaluation, without prior training, parents easily (average rating of 4 on a 5-point scale) used the system to record video evidence. Across all in-home video evidence recorded during field evaluation, 96% (26/27) were judged as clinically useful, for performing an autism diagnosis. For 4 children (3 with autism and 1 typically developing), both diagnosticians independently arrived at the correct diagnostic status (autism versus typical). Overall, in 91% of assessments (10/11) via NODA Connect, diagnosticians confidently (average rating 4.5 on a 5-point scale) concluded a diagnostic outcome that matched with the child's previous diagnostic status. Conclusions The in-field evaluation demonstrated that the system's design enabled parents to easily record clinically valid evidence of their child's behavior, and diagnosticians to complete a diagnostic assessment. These results shed light on the potential for appropriately designed telehealth technology to support clinical assessments using in-home video captured by families. This assessment model can be readily generalized to other conditions where direct observation of behavior plays a central role in the assessment process.

sheet.es: Si esperáis una valoración de autismo, preguntad al equipo clínico si aceptan vídeos grabados en casa, donde el niño o la niña se muestra en su entorno habitual. Este estudio desarrolló y probó un sistema con una aplicación móvil para familias y un portal web para quienes diagnostican. Participaron 5 familias y 3 profesionales del diagnóstico. Los padres lo usaron con facilidad (valoración media de 4 sobre 5) y 26 de 27 vídeos se consideraron útiles clínicamente. Los límites: la muestra fue muy pequeña, el sistema es un prototipo y no se puede asumir que sirva para todas las familias. El diagnóstico lo decide siempre un profesional.
sheet.en: If you are waiting for an autism assessment, ask the clinical team whether they accept videos recorded at home, where your child is in their usual surroundings. This study developed and tested a system with a mobile app for families and a web portal for diagnosticians. Five families and 3 diagnosticians took part. Parents used it easily (average rating of 4 on a 5-point scale), and 26 of 27 videos were judged clinically useful. The limits: the sample was very small, the system was a prototype, and it cannot be assumed to suit every family. A diagnosis is always made by a professional.
sheet.sv: Om ni väntar på en autismutredning kan ni fråga vårdteamet om de tar emot filmer från hemmet, där barnet är i sin vanliga miljö. Studien utvecklade och testade ett system med en mobilapp för familjer och en webbportal för utredare. Fem familjer och 3 utredare deltog. Föräldrarna använde det enkelt (medelbetyg 4 på en 5-gradig skala) och 26 av 27 filmer bedömdes som kliniskt användbara. Begränsningar: urvalet var mycket litet, systemet var en prototyp och det går inte att anta att det passar alla familjer. Diagnosen ställs alltid av en professionell.

title: Study protocol: a randomized controlled trial investigating the effects of a psychosexual training program for adolescents with autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Visser K, Greaves-Lord K, Tick NT, Verhulst FC, Maras A, van der Vegt EJ
abstract: Background Previous research shows that adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) run several risks in their psychosexual development and that these adolescents can have limited access to reliable information on puberty and sexuality, emphasizing the need for specific guidance of adolescents with ASD in their psychosexual development. Few studies have investigated the effects of psychosexual training programs for adolescents with ASD and to date no randomized controlled trials are available to study the effects of psychosexual interventions for this target group. Methods/design The randomized controlled trial (RCT) described in this study protocol aims to investigate the effects of the Tackling Teenage Training (TTT) program on the psychosexual development of adolescents with ASD. This parallel clinical trial, conducted in the South-West of the Netherlands, has a simple equal randomization design with an intervention and a waiting-list control condition. Two hundred adolescents and their parents participate in this study. We assess the participants in both conditions using self-report as well as parent-report questionnaires at three time points during 1 year: at baseline (T1), post-treatment (T2), and for follow-up (T3). Discussion To our knowledge, the current study is the first that uses a randomized controlled design to study the effects of a psychosexual training program for adolescents with ASD. It has a number of methodological strengths, namely a large sample size, a wide range of functionally relevant outcome measures, the use of multiple informants, and a standardized research and intervention protocol. Also some limitations of the described study are identified, for instance not making a comparison between two treatment conditions, and no use of blinded observational measures to investigate the ecological validity of the research results. Trial registration Dutch Trial Register NTR2860. Registered on 20 April 2011.

title: Sensory Adapted Dental Environments to Enhance Oral Care for Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders: A Randomized Controlled Pilot Study.
authors: Cermak SA, Stein Duker LI, Williams ME, Dawson ME, Lane CJ, Polido JC
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders

claim.es: Un entorno dental adaptado (luz baja, menos ruido, presión profunda) redujo el estrés y el malestar de niños autistas durante la limpieza.
claim.en: A sensory-adapted dental environment (dim light, less noise, deep pressure) reduced stress and discomfort for autistic children during cleaning.
claim.sv: En sensoriskt anpassad tandvårdsmiljö (dämpat ljus, mindre ljud, djupt tryck) minskade stress och obehag hos autistiska barn vid rengöring.

supports.es: Pedir a la clínica menos luz y sonido y una secuencia predecible.
supports.en: Asking a clinic for lower light and sound and a predictable sequence.
supports.sv: Att be kliniken om mindre ljus och ljud och en förutsägbar ordning.

doesNotSupport.es: Que la adaptación elimine la necesidad de consentimiento y pausas.
doesNotSupport.en: That adaptation removes the need for consent and pauses.
doesNotSupport.sv: Att anpassning tar bort behovet av samtycke och pauser.

title: The Impact of Neuroimmune Alterations in Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Gottfried C, Bambini-Junior V, Francis F, Riesgo R, Savino W
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) involves a complex interplay of both genetic and environmental risk factors, with immune alterations and synaptic connection deficiency in early life. In the past decade, studies of ASD have substantially increased, in both humans and animal models. Immunological imbalance (including autoimmunity) has been proposed as a major etiological component in ASD, taking into account increased levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines observed in postmortem brain from patients, as well as autoantibody production. Also, epidemiological studies have established a correlation of ASD with family history of autoimmune diseases; associations with major histocompatibility complex haplotypes and abnormal levels of immunological markers in the blood. Moreover, the use of animal models to study ASD is providing increasing information on the relationship between the immune system and the pathophysiology of ASD. Herein, we will discuss the accumulating literature for ASD, giving special attention to the relevant aspects of factors that may be related to the neuroimmune interface in the development of ASD, including changes in neuroplasticity.

sheet.es: Esta revisión no ofrece nada que cambie la rutina de mañana. Sirve como contexto: si una persona autista tiene problemas de salud o antecedentes familiares de enfermedades autoinmunes, puede comentarlo con su profesional sanitario. Es una revisión de estudios en personas y en modelos animales; señala que las alteraciones inmunitarias podrían estar relacionadas con el autismo, por ejemplo con marcadores en sangre y antecedentes familiares de enfermedades autoinmunes. Sus límites: muestra asociaciones, no causas, no se aplica a todas las personas autistas y no orienta decisiones individuales. Las decisiones médicas corresponden siempre a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: This review offers nothing that changes tomorrow's routine. It is background: if an autistic person has health concerns or a family history of autoimmune disease, you can mention it to their healthcare professional. It is a review of studies in people and in animal models, and it reports that immune differences may be linked to autism, for example markers in the blood and family history of autoimmune disease. Its limits: it shows associations, not causes, it does not apply to every autistic person, and it cannot guide individual decisions. Medical decisions always belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Den här översikten ger inget som ändrar morgondagens rutiner. Den är bakgrund: om en autistisk person har hälsobekymmer eller autoimmuna sjukdomar i släkten kan du ta upp det med personens vårdpersonal. Det är en översikt av studier på människor och djurmodeller, och den beskriver att skillnader i immunförsvaret kan hänga ihop med autism, till exempel markörer i blodet och autoimmuna sjukdomar i familjen. Begränsningar: den visar samband, inte orsaker, gäller inte alla autistiska personer och kan inte styra individuella beslut. Medicinska beslut hör alltid till en läkare eller annan klinisk personal.

title: Parent Management Training and Collaborative & Proactive Solutions: A Randomized Control Trial for Oppositional Youth.
authors: Ollendick TH, Greene RW, Austin KE, Fraire MG, Halldorsdottir T, Allen KB, Jarrett MA, Lewis KM, Whitmore Smith M, Cunningham NR, Noguchi RJ, Canavera K, Wolff JC
journal: Journal of clinical child and adolescent psychology : the official journal for the Society of Clinical Child and Adolescent Psychology, American Psychological Association, Division 53

claim.es: En un ensayo aleatorizado con niños y adolescentes con conducta oposicionista, Soluciones Colaborativas y Proactivas (CPS) y el entrenamiento de padres (PMT) funcionaron mejor que la lista de espera y de forma parecida entre sí, con mejoras mantenidas meses después.
claim.en: In a randomized trial with oppositional children and adolescents, Collaborative & Proactive Solutions (CPS) and Parent Management Training (PMT) both did better than a waitlist and about equally well, with gains kept months later.
claim.sv: I en randomiserad studie med trotsiga barn och ungdomar gav både Collaborative & Proactive Solutions (CPS) och föräldraträning (PMT) bättre resultat än väntelista och ungefär lika bra som varandra, med förbättringar som höll i sig månader senare.

supports.es: Resolver problemas junto con la persona (qué le cuesta y qué necesita) como alternativa con evidencia a premios y castigos.
supports.en: Solving problems together with the person (what is hard and what they need) as an evidence-based alternative to rewards and punishments.
