supports.sv: Att lösa problem tillsammans med personen (vad som är svårt och vad den behöver) som ett evidensbaserat alternativ till belöningar och straff.

doesNotSupport.es: Que el resultado se traslade sin más a personas autistas o que no hablan: el estudio fue sobre conducta oposicionista, no sobre autismo.
doesNotSupport.en: That the result carries over directly to autistic or non-speaking people: the study was about oppositional behaviour, not autism.
doesNotSupport.sv: Att resultatet direkt gäller autistiska eller icke-talande personer: studien handlade om trotsbeteende, inte autism.

title: Cerebro-cerebellar circuits in autism spectrum disorder.
authors: D'Mello AM, Stoodley CJ
abstract: The cerebellum is one of the most consistent sites of abnormality in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and cerebellar damage is associated with an increased risk of ASD symptoms, suggesting that cerebellar dysfunction may play a crucial role in the etiology of ASD. The cerebellum forms multiple closed-loop circuits with cerebral cortical regions that underpin movement, language, and social processing. Through these circuits, cerebellar dysfunction could impact the core ASD symptoms of social and communication deficits and repetitive and stereotyped behaviors. The emerging topography of sensorimotor, cognitive, and affective subregions in the cerebellum provides a new framework for interpreting the significance of regional cerebellar findings in ASD and their relationship to broader cerebro-cerebellar circuits. Further, recent research supports the idea that the integrity of cerebro-cerebellar loops might be important for early cortical development; disruptions in specific cerebro-cerebellar loops in ASD might impede the specialization of cortical regions involved in motor control, language, and social interaction, leading to impairments in these domains. Consistent with this concept, structural, and functional differences in sensorimotor regions of the cerebellum and sensorimotor cerebro-cerebellar circuits are associated with deficits in motor control and increased repetitive and stereotyped behaviors in ASD. Further, communication and social impairments are associated with atypical activation and structure in cerebro-cerebellar loops underpinning language and social cognition. Finally, there is converging evidence from structural, functional, and connectivity neuroimaging studies that cerebellar right Crus I/II abnormalities are related to more severe ASD impairments in all domains. We propose that cerebellar abnormalities may disrupt optimization of both structure and function in specific cerebro-cerebellar circuits in ASD.

sheet.es: Lo práctico para mañana: las diferencias en movimiento, coordinación, lenguaje y en lo social pueden tener una base cerebral real, no son falta de esfuerzo ni mala voluntad. Ofrece tiempo extra para tareas motoras, divide los pasos, acepta los movimientos repetitivos que regulan y apoya la comunicación de la forma que funcione para la persona. Esta es una revisión de 2015 que reúne estudios de neuroimagen sobre los circuitos entre el cerebelo y la corteza en personas autistas. Límites: propone una hipótesis, no ofrece pruebas directas ni orientaciones prácticas, y los hallazgos de grupo no describen a cada persona autista.
sheet.en: Practical takeaway for tomorrow: differences in movement, coordination, language and social connection may have a real brain basis; they are not a lack of effort or willingness. Allow extra time for motor tasks, break steps down, accept repetitive movements that help with regulation, and support communication in whatever way works for the person. This is a 2015 review bringing together brain-imaging studies on circuits linking the cerebellum and the cerebral cortex in autistic people. Limits: it proposes a hypothesis rather than testing it directly, gives no practical guidance, and group findings do not describe every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Praktiskt för i morgon: skillnader i rörelse, koordination, språk och socialt samspel kan ha en verklig grund i hjärnan; de handlar inte om brist på ansträngning eller vilja. Ge extra tid för motoriska uppgifter, dela upp moment i små steg, acceptera upprepade rörelser som hjälper till att reglera och stötta kommunikationen på det sätt som fungerar för personen. Detta är en översikt från 2015 som sammanställer hjärnavbildningsstudier om kretsar mellan lillhjärnan och hjärnbarken hos autistiska personer. Begränsningar: den föreslår en hypotes snarare än att pröva den direkt, ger inga praktiska råd, och gruppfynd beskriver inte varje autistisk person.

title: Autism spectrum disorders and neuropathology of the cerebellum.
authors: Hampson DR, Blatt GJ
abstract: The cerebellum contains the largest number of neurons and synapses of any structure in the central nervous system. The concept that the cerebellum is solely involved in fine motor function has become outdated; substantial evidence has accumulated linking the cerebellum with higher cognitive functions including language. Cerebellar deficits have been implicated in autism for more than two decades. The computational power of the cerebellum is essential for many, if not most of the processes that are perturbed in autism including language and communication, social interactions, stereotyped behavior, motor activity and motor coordination, and higher cognitive functions. The link between autism and cerebellar dysfunction should not be surprising to those who study its cellular, physiological, and functional properties. Postmortem studies have revealed neuropathological abnormalities in cerebellar cellular architecture while studies on mouse lines with cell loss or mutations in single genes restricted to cerebellar Purkinje cells have also strongly implicated this brain structure in contributing to the autistic phenotype. This connection has been further substantiated by studies investigating brain damage in humans restricted to the cerebellum. In this review, we summarize advances in research on idiopathic autism and three genetic forms of autism that highlight the key roles that the cerebellum plays in this spectrum of neurodevelopmental disorders.

sheet.es: Esta revisión no ofrece una pauta para el día a día, pero sugiere una idea útil: el cerebelo no solo interviene en el movimiento, también en el lenguaje, la comunicación y el pensamiento. Si una persona autista tiene dificultades de coordinación o de comunicación, conviene ofrecer apoyos y tiempo sin juzgar. Es una revisión que reúne estudios posmortem, estudios en ratones y casos de daño cerebral en personas. Tiene límites: no es un estudio nuevo, no indica qué apoyo funciona y no describe a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: This review gives no day-to-day instructions, but it offers a useful idea: the cerebellum is involved not only in movement but also in language, communication and thinking. If an autistic person has coordination or communication differences, offer support and extra time without judgement. The review brings together postmortem studies, mouse studies and cases of brain damage in people. Its limits: it is not a new study, it does not say which support works, and it does not describe every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Den här översikten ger inga råd för vardagen, men en användbar tanke: lillhjärnan är inte bara viktig för rörelse, utan också för språk, kommunikation och tänkande. Om en autistisk person har skillnader i koordination eller kommunikation kan du erbjuda stöd och extra tid utan att döma. Översikten samlar studier av hjärnor efter döden, musstudier och fall av hjärnskada hos människor. Begränsningar: det är ingen ny studie, den visar inte vilket stöd som fungerar och beskriver inte alla autistiska personer.

title: Annual research review: Child and adolescent mental health interventions: a review of progress in economic studies across different disorders.
authors: Beecham J
journal: Journal of child psychology and psychiatry, and allied disciplines
abstract: Background Resources for supporting children and adolescents with psychiatric disorders continue to be scarce. Economics research can identify current patterns of expenditure, and help inform allocation of treatment and support resources between competing needs or uses. Scope and methods The aim was to identify the costs of supporting children and adolescents, the economic impacts of childhood psychiatric disorders in adulthood and any new evidence on the cost-effectiveness of interventions. An electronic search of databases (including PubMed, Medline and Psychinfo) identified peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2005 and 2012. Findings Sixty-seven papers provided data on support and treatment costs now or in the future, or cost-effectiveness analyses of services. Half the articles came from the United States. Most articles focussed on autism spectrum disorder (ASD; 23 articles), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD; n = 15), conduct disorder (CD; n = 7), and anxiety or depression (n = 8). Conclusion Only 14 studies used a cost perspective wider than health care; most included education costs (n = 11), but only five included costs to the justice system. The number of studies estimating costs to the family has increased, particularly for children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). In the United Kingdom, support costs for children and adolescents with conduct disorder (CD) appear to be lower than for those with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), although for the United States, the opposite may be true. Support costs for children and adolescents with ASD may be higher than both CD and ADHD. However, there were many differences between the samples and the methods employed making comparisons between studies difficult. Outcomes in adulthood include negative impacts on (mental) health, quality of life, public sector services, employment status and income. The evidence base is improving for child and adolescent psychiatric disorders, although only one full cost-effectiveness analysis was identified since the previous review published in 2012. However, we still do not know enough about the economic implications of support and treatment for specific disorders.

sheet.es: Si buscas apoyos para tu hijo o hija autista, es razonable preguntar a los servicios cuánto cuestan y qué ayudas cubren, incluidas las de educación y las que recaen en la familia. Es una revisión de estudios económicos publicados entre 2005 y 2012: 67 artículos, 23 sobre autismo, la mitad de Estados Unidos. Los costes de apoyo en autismo podrían ser más altos que en otras condiciones, pero los estudios eran muy distintos y no se pueden comparar bien. Solo se halló un análisis completo de coste-efectividad, así que no sirve para decidir qué apoyo elegir en una persona concreta.
sheet.en: If you are seeking support for an autistic child or teen, it is reasonable to ask services what it costs and what help is covered, including education and the costs families carry. This is a review of economic studies published between 2005 and 2012: 67 articles, 23 on autism, half from the United States. Support costs for autism may be higher than for some other conditions, but the studies differed a lot and cannot be compared well. Only one full cost-effectiveness analysis was found, so it cannot tell you which support is right for a particular person.
sheet.sv: Om du söker stöd till ett autistiskt barn eller en autistisk tonåring är det rimligt att fråga verksamheterna vad stödet kostar och vad som täcks, även skola och kostnader som familjen bär. Detta är en översikt av ekonomiska studier publicerade mellan 2005 och 2012: 67 artiklar, 23 om autism, hälften från USA. Stödkostnaderna för autism kan vara högre än för vissa andra tillstånd, men studierna skilde sig mycket åt och går inte att jämföra väl. Bara en fullständig kostnadseffektivitetsanalys hittades, så översikten kan inte avgöra vilket stöd som passar en enskild person.

title: Highlighting consensus among medical scientists increases public support for vaccines: evidence from a randomized experiment.
authors: van der Linden SL, Clarke CE, Maibach EW
abstract: Background A substantial minority of American adults continue to hold influential misperceptions about childhood vaccine safety. Growing public concern and refusal to vaccinate poses a serious public health risk. Evaluations of recent pro-vaccine health communication interventions have revealed mixed results (at best). This study investigated whether highlighting consensus among medical scientists about childhood vaccine safety can lower public concern, reduce key misperceptions about the discredited autism-vaccine link and promote overall support for vaccines. Methods American adults (N = 206) were invited participate in an online survey experiment. Participants were randomly assigned to either a control group or to one of three treatment interventions. The treatment messages were based on expert-consensus estimates and either normatively described or prescribed the extant medical consensus: "90 % of medical scientists agree that vaccines are safe and that all parents should be required to vaccinate their children". Results Compared to the control group, the consensus-messages significantly reduced vaccine concern (M = 3.51 vs. M = 2.93, p Conclusion These findings suggest that emphasizing the medical consensus about (childhood) vaccine safety is likely to be an effective pro-vaccine message that could help prevent current immunization rates from declining. We recommend that clinicians and public health officials highlight and communicate the high degree of medical consensus on (childhood) vaccine safety when possible.

sheet.es: Si una conversación sobre vacunas te preocupa, puede ayudarte saber que la comunidad médica coincide ampliamente en que son seguras. Puedes pedir a un profesional sanitario que te explique ese consenso y resolver tus dudas con calma. Es un ensayo aleatorizado en línea con 206 adultos estadounidenses: quienes leyeron mensajes sobre el consenso médico expresaron menos preocupación que el grupo de control. Sus límites: fue una encuesta breve, sin seguimiento de decisiones reales, y no sustituye el consejo médico individual. Las decisiones médicas corresponden a cada familia junto con su clínico.
sheet.en: If vaccine worries come up, it may help to know that medical scientists broadly agree vaccines are safe. You can ask a health professional to explain that consensus and talk through your questions calmly. This was an online randomized trial with 206 American adults: people who read messages about medical consensus reported less vaccine concern than the control group. Its limits: it was a short survey, did not follow real vaccination decisions, and cannot replace individual medical advice. Medical decisions belong to each family together with their clinician.
sheet.sv: Om oro kring vaccin dyker upp kan det hjälpa att veta att medicinska forskare i stort är överens om att vaccin är säkra. Du kan be en vårdgivare förklara den samsynen och gå igenom dina frågor i lugn och ro. Det var en slumpmässig onlinestudie med 206 vuxna amerikaner: de som läste budskap om medicinsk samsyn uttryckte mindre oro än kontrollgruppen. Begränsningarna: det var en kort enkät, den följde inga verkliga vaccinationsbeslut och ersätter inte individuell medicinsk rådgivning. Medicinska beslut hör hemma hos varje familj tillsammans med en kliniker.

title: At the cross-roads of participatory research and biomarker discovery in autism: the need for empirical data.
authors: Yusuf A, Elsabbagh M
abstract: Background Identifying biomarkers for autism can improve outcomes for those affected by autism. Engaging the diverse stakeholders in the research process using community-based participatory research (CBPR) can accelerate biomarker discovery into clinical applications. However, there are limited examples of stakeholder involvement in autism research, possibly due to conceptual and practical concerns. We evaluate the applicability of CBPR principles to biomarker discovery in autism and critically review empirical studies adopting these principles. Methods Using a scoping review methodology, we identified and evaluated seven studies using CBPR principles in biomarker discovery. Results and conclusions The limited number of studies in biomarker discovery adopting CBPR principles coupled with their methodological limitations suggests that such applications are feasible but challenging. These studies illustrate three CBPR themes: community assessment, setting global priorities, and collaboration in research design. We propose that further research using participatory principles would be useful in accelerating the pace of discovery and the development of clinically meaningful biomarkers. For this goal to be successful we advocate for increased attention to previously identified conceptual and methodological challenges to participatory approaches in health research, including improving scientific rigor and developing long-term partnerships among stakeholders.

sheet.es: Si te piden participar en un estudio sobre biomarcadores, pregunta cómo se incluirá la voz de las personas autistas y de sus familias en el diseño y en las prioridades. Se trata de una revisión exploratoria que encontró siete estudios que aplicaron principios de investigación participativa comunitaria al descubrimiento de biomarcadores en autismo. Sus autores concluyen que es posible, pero difícil. Los estudios son pocos y tienen limitaciones metodológicas, así que no muestra qué funciona mejor ni sirve como regla para cada persona o familia.
sheet.en: If you are invited to join a study on biomarkers, ask how autistic people and their families will have a say in its design and priorities. This was a scoping review that found seven studies applying community-based participatory research principles to biomarker discovery in autism. Its authors conclude that this is feasible but challenging. The studies are few and have methodological limitations, so the review cannot show what works best, and it is not a rule for every person or family.
sheet.sv: Om du blir tillfrågad att delta i en studie om biomarkörer, fråga hur autistiska personer och deras familjer får vara med och påverka utformning och prioriteringar. Detta var en kartläggande översikt som hittade sju studier som använde principer för deltagarbaserad forskning i upptäckten av biomarkörer vid autism. Författarna drar slutsatsen att det är möjligt men svårt. Studierna är få och har metodologiska brister, så översikten visar inte vad som fungerar bäst och är ingen regel för varje person eller familj.

title: Mutations and Modeling of the Chromatin Remodeler CHD8 Define an Emerging Autism Etiology.
authors: Barnard RA, Pomaville MB, O'Roak BJ
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a common neurodevelopmental disorder with a strong but complex genetic component. Recent family based exome-sequencing strategies have identified recurrent de novo mutations at specific genes, providing strong evidence for ASD risk, but also highlighting the extreme genetic heterogeneity of the disorder. However, disruptions in these genes converge on key molecular pathways early in development. In particular, functional enrichment analyses have found that there is a bias toward genes involved in transcriptional regulation, such as chromatin modifiers. Here we review recent genetic, animal model, co-expression network, and functional genomics studies relating to the high confidence ASD risk gene, CHD8. CHD8, a chromatin remodeling factor, may serve as a "master regulator" of a common ASD etiology. Individuals with a CHD8 mutation show an ASD subtype that includes similar physical characteristics, such as macrocephaly and prolonged GI problems including recurrent constipation. Similarly, animal models of CHD8 disruption exhibit enlarged head circumference and reduced gut motility phenotypes. Systems biology approaches suggest CHD8 and other candidate ASD risk genes are enriched during mid-fetal development, which may represent a critical time window in ASD etiology. Transcription and CHD8 binding site profiles from cell and primary tissue models of early development indicate that CHD8 may also positively regulate other candidate ASD risk genes through both direct and indirect means. However, continued study is needed to elucidate the mechanism of regulation as well as identify which CHD8 targets are most relevant to ASD risk. Overall, these initial studies suggest the potential for common ASD etiologies and the development of personalized treatments in the future.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista tiene una mutación conocida en CHD8, conviene comentar con su equipo médico los problemas digestivos persistentes, como el estreñimiento recurrente, y no darlos por normales. Esta es una revisión de estudios genéticos, de modelos animales y de redes de expresión génica. Señala que quienes tienen una mutación en CHD8 comparten rasgos físicos, como macrocefalia, y estos problemas digestivos. Sus límites: describe un subgrupo concreto, no a todas las personas autistas, y aún falta saber qué genes regulados por CHD8 importan más. Las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If an autistic person has a known CHD8 mutation, it is worth raising ongoing gut problems, such as recurrent constipation, with their medical team rather than assuming they are just part of life. This is a review of genetic studies, animal models and gene-expression network studies. It reports that people with a CHD8 mutation share some physical traits, such as macrocephaly, along with these gut problems. Its limits: it describes one specific subgroup, not all autistic people, and it is still unclear which genes regulated by CHD8 matter most. Medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person har en känd CHD8-mutation är det värt att ta upp långvariga magproblem, som återkommande förstoppning, med vårdteamet i stället för att anta att de bara hör till. Detta är en översikt av genetiska studier, djurmodeller och studier av genuttrycksnätverk. Den beskriver att personer med en CHD8-mutation delar vissa fysiska drag, som makrocefali, och dessa magproblem. Begränsningar: den gäller en specifik undergrupp, inte alla autistiska personer, och det är fortfarande oklart vilka gener som regleras av CHD8 som betyder mest. Medicinska beslut hör till en läkare.

title: Social cognitive impairment and autism: what are we trying to explain?
authors: Leekam S
journal: Philosophical transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series B, Biological sciences
abstract: Early psychological theories of autism explained the clinical features of this condition in terms of perceptual and sensory processing impairments. The arrival of domain-specific social cognitive theories changed this focus, postulating a 'primary' and specific psychological impairment of social cognition. Across the years, evidence has been growing in support of social cognitive and social attention explanations in autism. However, there has also been evidence for general non-social cognitive impairments in representational understanding, attention allocation and sensory processing. Here, I review recent findings and consider the case for the specificity and primacy of the social cognitive impairment, proposing that we should focus more explicitly on clinically valid features for insights on the integration of 'social' and 'non-social' cognition.

sheet.es: Tómate con calma las explicaciones sobre la "cognición social": no hay una única causa que explique a todas las personas autistas. Observa con curiosidad qué cosas sociales y no sociales (atención, sensaciones, comprensión) le resultan más fáciles o más difíciles a la persona, y adapta el entorno a eso. Este estudio es una revisión de teorías y hallazgos recientes; el resumen no indica quiénes participaron. Sus límites: no ofrece consejos prácticos directos y plantea que aún se debate si lo social es lo primordial o si se integra con lo no social.
sheet.en: Be wary of any single explanation of autism, including "social cognition" ones: no one cause fits every autistic person. Notice with curiosity which social and non-social things (attention, sensations, understanding) come more easily or harder to the person, and adapt their environment accordingly. This is a review of theories and recent findings; the abstract does not say who took part. Its limits: it gives no direct practical advice, and it shows it is still debated whether social differences come first or are integrated with non-social ones.
sheet.sv: Var försiktig med enkla förklaringar av autism, även dem om "social kognition": ingen enskild orsak passar alla autistiska personer. Lägg märke till vad som är lättare eller svårare för personen, både socialt och icke-socialt (uppmärksamhet, sinnesintryck, förståelse), och anpassa miljön efter det. Studien är en översikt av teorier och nyare resultat; sammanfattningen anger inte vilka som deltog. Begränsningar: den ger inga direkta praktiska råd, och det är fortfarande omdebatterat om sociala skillnader kommer först eller hänger ihop med icke-sociala.

title: Cost-effectiveness analysis of a communication-focused therapy for pre-school children with autism: results from a randomised controlled trial.
authors: Byford S, Cary M, Barrett B, Aldred CR, Charman T, Howlin P, Hudry K, Leadbitter K, Le Couteur A, McConachie H, Pickles A, Slonims V, Temple KJ, Green J, PACT Consortium
abstract: Background Autism is associated with impairments that have life-time consequences for diagnosed individuals and a substantial impact on families. There is growing interest in early interventions for children with autism, yet despite the substantial economic burden, there is little evidence of the cost-effectiveness of such interventions with which to support resource allocation decisions. This study reports an economic evaluation of a parent-mediated, communication-focused therapy carried out within the Pre-School Autism Communication Trial (PACT). Methods 152 pre-school children with autism were randomly assigned to treatment as usual (TAU) or PACT + TAU. Primary outcome was severity of autism symptoms at 13-month follow-up. Economic data included health, education and social services, childcare, parental productivity losses and informal care. Results Clinically meaningful symptom improvement was evident for 53 % of PACT + TAU versus 41 % of TAU (odds ratio 1.91, p = 0.074). Service costs were significantly higher for PACT + TAU (mean difference £4,489, p Conclusions Improvements in outcome generated by PACT come at a cost. Although this cost is lower when burden on parents is included, the cost and effectiveness results presented do not support the cost-effectiveness of PACT + TAU compared to TAU alone. Trial registration Current Controlled Trials ISRCTN58133827.

sheet.es: Si valora una terapia de comunicación mediada por madres y padres, tenga en cuenta que el coste también cuenta, y pregunte a los servicios locales qué apoyo hay disponible. Este ensayo aleatorizado incluyó a 152 niños autistas en edad preescolar: unos recibieron la atención habitual y otros la terapia PACT más la atención habitual. La mejoría de síntomas fue del 53 % con PACT frente al 41 % con la atención habitual (p = 0,074), y los costes de los servicios fueron mayores con PACT. Los autores concluyeron que no se demostró que fuera rentable. El estudio es económico, no dice si la terapia sirve a cada niño ni mide lo que las familias valoran.
sheet.en: If you are considering a parent-mediated communication therapy, remember that cost matters too, and ask local services what support is available. This randomised trial included 152 autistic pre-school children: some received usual care, others received the PACT therapy plus usual care. Symptom improvement was seen for 53 % with PACT versus 41 % with usual care (p = 0.074), and service costs were higher with PACT. The authors concluded it was not shown to be cost-effective. This is an economic study; it cannot say whether the therapy suits any one child, and it does not measure what families value.
sheet.sv: Om du överväger en kommunikationsterapi där föräldrar medverkar, kom ihåg att kostnaden också spelar roll, och fråga lokala verksamheter vilket stöd som finns. Denna randomiserade studie omfattade 152 autistiska förskolebarn: några fick vanlig vård, andra fick PACT-terapi plus vanlig vård. Symtomförbättring sågs hos 53 % med PACT jämfört med 41 % med vanlig vård (p = 0,074), och vårdkostnaderna var högre med PACT. Författarna drog slutsatsen att kostnadseffektivitet inte kunde visas. Studien är ekonomisk; den kan inte säga om terapin passar ett enskilt barn och mäter inte det som familjer värdesätter.

title: Characteristics of Brains in Autism Spectrum Disorder: Structure, Function and Connectivity across the Lifespan.
authors: Ha S, Sohn IJ, Kim N, Sim HJ, Cheon KA
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a highly prevalent neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by impaired social communication and restricted and repetitive behaviors (RRBs). Over the past decade, neuroimaging studies have provided considerable insights underlying neurobiological mechanisms of ASD. In this review, we introduce recent findings from brain imaging studies to characterize the brains of ASD across the human lifespan. Results of structural Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) studies dealing with total brain volume, regional brain structure and cortical area are summarized. Using task-based functional MRI (fMRI), many studies have shown dysfunctional activation in critical areas of social communication and RRBs. We also describe several data to show abnormal connectivity in the ASD brains. Finally, we suggest the possible strategies to study ASD brains in the future.

sheet.es: Qué puede aportar a tu día a día: esta revisión no ofrece pasos concretos, pero recuerda que las diferencias en la comunicación social y en los intereses o rutinas repetitivas de una persona autista tienen una base en cómo funciona su cerebro. Conviene adaptar el entorno y la comunicación en lugar de intentar «corregir». Sobre la evidencia: es una revisión de estudios de neuroimagen (resonancia magnética) que abarca distintas edades de la vida. Límites: describe patrones generales de grupo, no sirve para valorar a una persona concreta y no indica qué hacer en casa. Cada persona autista es distinta.
sheet.en: What it can mean for your day: this review gives no concrete steps, but it is a reminder that differences in social communication and in repetitive behaviours or routines in autistic people have a basis in how the brain works. It makes sense to adapt the environment and the way you communicate rather than trying to "fix" the person. On the evidence: it is a review of brain imaging (MRI) studies covering different stages of life. Limits: it describes general group patterns, cannot assess any one person, and does not say what to do at home. Every autistic person is different.
sheet.sv: Vad det kan betyda i vardagen: den här översikten ger inga konkreta steg, men påminner om att skillnader i social kommunikation och i repetitiva beteenden eller rutiner hos autistiska personer har en grund i hur hjärnan fungerar. Det är rimligt att anpassa miljön och sättet att kommunicera i stället för att försöka "rätta till" personen. Om evidensen: det är en översikt av hjärnavbildningsstudier (magnetkamera) som omfattar olika åldrar i livet. Begränsningar: den beskriver generella gruppmönster, kan inte bedöma en enskild person och säger inte vad man ska göra hemma. Varje autistisk person är unik.

title: Exploring the Validity of Valproic Acid Animal Model of Autism.
authors: Mabunga DF, Gonzales EL, Kim JW, Kim KC, Shin CY
abstract: The valproic acid (VPA) animal model of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is one of the most widely used animal model in the field. Like any other disease models, it can't model the totality of the features seen in autism. Then, is it valid to model autism? This model demonstrates many of the structural and behavioral features that can be observed in individuals with autism. These similarities enable the model to define relevant pathways of developmental dysregulation resulting from environmental manipulation. The uncovering of these complex pathways resulted to the growing pool of potential therapeutic candidates addressing the core symptoms of ASD. Here, we summarize the validity points of VPA that may or may not qualify it as a valid animal model of ASD.

sheet.es: Esta revisión no ofrece nada que hacer mañana en casa: trata de la investigación de laboratorio, no de la vida diaria de una persona autista. Revisa si un modelo animal basado en ácido valproico sirve para estudiar el autismo. Según el resumen, el modelo muestra rasgos estructurales y conductuales parecidos a los observados en personas autistas, y ayuda a identificar vías del desarrollo alteradas. Como estudio con medicamento, solo cabe decir que es investigación médica y que las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico. Es una revisión, no un ensayo con personas, y el propio texto admite que ningún modelo reproduce todos los rasgos del autismo. No debe leerse como una regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: This review offers nothing to do tomorrow at home: it is laboratory research, not about an autistic person's daily life. It examines whether an animal model based on valproic acid is useful for studying autism. According to the abstract, the model shows structural and behavioural features similar to those seen in autistic people, and helps identify altered developmental pathways. Because a medicine is involved, all we can say is that this is medical research, and medical decisions belong to a clinician. It is a review, not a trial with people, and the authors admit that no model captures every feature of autism. It should not be read as a rule for any individual person.
sheet.sv: Den här översikten ger inget att göra i morgon hemma: den handlar om laboratorieforskning, inte om en autistisk persons vardag. Den granskar om en djurmodell baserad på valproinsyra är användbar för att studera autism. Enligt sammanfattningen visar modellen strukturella och beteendemässiga drag som liknar dem hos autistiska personer, och den hjälper till att identifiera förändrade utvecklingsvägar. Eftersom ett läkemedel ingår kan vi bara säga att det är medicinsk forskning och att medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker. Det är en översikt, inte en studie med människor, och författarna medger att ingen modell fångar alla drag av autism. Den ska inte läsas som en regel för varje person.

title: Systematic Review of the Measurement Properties of Tools Used to Measure Behaviour Problems in Young Children with Autism.
authors: Hanratty J, Livingstone N, Robalino S, Terwee CB, Glod M, Oono IP, Rodgers J, Macdonald G, McConachie H
abstract: Background Behaviour problems are common in young children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). There are many different tools used to measure behavior problems but little is known about their validity for the population. Objectives To evaluate the measurement properties of behaviour problems tools used in evaluation of intervention or observational research studies with children with ASD up to the age of six years. Methods Behaviour measurement tools were identified as part of a larger, two stage, systematic review. First, sixteen major electronic databases, as well as grey literature and research registers were searched, and tools used listed and categorized. Second, using methodological filters, we searched for articles examining the measurement properties of the tools in use with young children with ASD in ERIC, MEDLINE, EMBASE, CINAHL, and PsycINFO. The quality of these papers was then evaluated using the COSMIN checklist. Results We identified twelve tools which had been used to measure behaviour problems in young children with ASD, and fifteen studies which investigated the measurement properties of six of these tools. There was no evidence available for the remaining six tools. Two questionnaires were found to be the most robust in their measurement properties, the Child Behavior Checklist and the Home Situations Questionnaire-Pervasive Developmental Disorders version. Conclusions We found patchy evidence on reliability and validity, for only a few of the tools used to measure behaviour problems in young children with ASD. More systematic research is required on measurement properties of tools for use in this population, in particular to establish responsiveness to change which is essential in measurement of outcomes of intervention. Prospero registration number CRD42012002223.

sheet.es: Si le piden rellenar un cuestionario sobre conducta de su hijo o hija autista pequeño, pregunte qué herramienta es y si se ha comprobado con niñez autista. Es una revisión sistemática: halló doce herramientas usadas con niños autistas de hasta seis años, y solo seis tenían estudios de sus propiedades de medición (quince estudios). Dos cuestionarios, el Child Behavior Checklist y el Home Situations Questionnaire-Pervasive Developmental Disorders version, tuvieron la evidencia más sólida. Límites: la evidencia es escasa e irregular, sobre todo para detectar cambios tras una intervención. Sus resultados no sustituyen la opinión de los profesionales que conocen a su hijo o hija.
sheet.en: If you are asked to fill in a questionnaire about your young autistic child's behaviour, ask which tool it is and whether it has been checked with autistic children. This was a systematic review: it found twelve tools used with autistic children up to age six, and only six had studies of their measurement properties (fifteen studies). Two questionnaires, the Child Behavior Checklist and the Home Situations Questionnaire-Pervasive Developmental Disorders version, had the strongest evidence. Limits: the evidence was patchy, especially on detecting change after an intervention. It does not replace the view of professionals who know your child.
sheet.sv: Om du ombeds fylla i ett frågeformulär om beteende hos ditt lilla autistiska barn, fråga vilket verktyg det är och om det har prövats på autistiska barn. Det här var en systematisk översikt: den hittade tolv verktyg som använts med autistiska barn upp till sex år, och bara sex hade studier av sina mätegenskaper (femton studier). Två formulär, Child Behavior Checklist och Home Situations Questionnaire-Pervasive Developmental Disorders version, hade starkast stöd. Begränsning: underlaget var ojämnt, särskilt när det gäller att fånga förändring efter en insats. Det ersätter inte bedömningen från yrkespersoner som känner ditt barn.

title: Parent-mediated intervention versus no intervention for infants at high risk of autism: a parallel, single-blind, randomised trial.
authors: Green J, Charman T, Pickles A, Wan MW, Elsabbagh M, Slonims V, Taylor C, McNally J, Booth R, Gliga T, Jones EJ, Harrop C, Bedford R, Johnson MH, BASIS team
abstract: Background Risk markers for later autism identified in the first year of life present plausible intervention targets during early development. We aimed to assess the effect of a parent-mediated intervention for infants at high risk of autism on these markers. Methods We did a two-site, two-arm assessor-blinded randomised controlled trial of families with an infant at familial high risk of autism aged 7-10 months, testing the adapted Video Interaction to Promote Positive Parenting (iBASIS-VIPP) versus no intervention. Families were randomly assigned to intervention or no intervention groups using a permuted block approach stratified by centre. Assessors, but not families or therapists, were masked to group assignment. The primary outcome was infant attentiveness to parent. Regression analysis was done on an intention-to-treat basis. This trial is registered with ISCRTN Registry, number ISRCTN87373263. Findings We randomly assigned 54 families between April 11, 2011, and Dec 4, 2012 (28 to intervention, 26 to no intervention). Although CIs sometimes include the null, point estimates suggest that the intervention increased the primary outcome of infant attentiveness to parent (effect size 0.29, 95% CI -0.26 to 0.86, thus including possibilities ranging from a small negative treatment effect to a strongly positive treatment effect). For secondary outcomes, the intervention reduced autism-risk behaviours (0.50, CI -0.15 to 1.08), increased parental non-directiveness (0.81, 0.28 to 1.52), improved attention disengagement (0.48, -0.01 to 1.02), and improved parent-rated infant adaptive function (χ(2)[2] 15.39, p=0.0005). There was a possibility of nil or negative effect in language and responsivity to vowel change (P1: ES-0.62, CI -2.42 to 0.31; P2: -0.29, -1.55 to 0.71). Interpretation With the exception of the response to vowel change, our study showed positive estimates across a wide range of behavioural and brain function risk-markers and developmental outcomes that are consistent with a moderate intervention effect to reduce the risk for later autism. However, the estimates have wide CIs that include possible nil or small negative effects. The results are encouraging for development and prevention science, but need larger-scale replication to improve precision. Funding Autistica, Waterloo Foundation, Autism Speaks, and the UK Medical Research Council.

sheet.es: Si tiene un bebé con familiares autistas, puede probar momentos de juego en los que siga su iniciativa: mirar lo que le interesa al bebé, esperar y responder sin dirigir. Es una idea para explorar, no una obligación. Evidencia: ensayo aleatorizado con 54 familias con bebés de 7-10 meses con alta probabilidad familiar de autismo; se comparó un programa de videos de interacción con no recibir programa. Límites: muestra pequeña, resultados imprecisos, algunos podrían ser nulos o negativos, y hacen falta estudios más grandes. No sirve como regla para todas las familias.
sheet.en: If your baby has autistic relatives, you could try play moments where you follow their lead: notice what interests them, wait, and respond without directing. This is an idea to explore, not a duty. Evidence: a randomised trial with 54 families of infants aged 7-10 months at familial high likelihood of autism, comparing a video-feedback interaction programme with no programme. Limits: the sample was small, results were imprecise, some effects could be null or negative, and larger studies are needed. It is not a rule for every family.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn har autistiska släktingar kan du prova lekstunder där du följer barnets initiativ: lägg märke till vad barnet intresserar sig för, vänta och svara utan att styra. Det är en idé att utforska, inte ett krav. Evidens: en randomiserad studie med 54 familjer med spädbarn i åldern 7-10 månader med hög familjär sannolikhet för autism, som jämförde ett videobaserat samspelsprogram med inget program. Begränsningar: litet urval, osäkra resultat, vissa effekter kan vara noll eller negativa, och större studier behövs. Det är ingen regel för alla familjer.

title: Autism, oxytocin and interoception.
authors: Quattrocki E, Friston K
abstract: Autism is a pervasive developmental disorder characterized by profound social and verbal communication deficits, stereotypical motor behaviors, restricted interests, and cognitive abnormalities. Autism affects approximately 1% of children in developing countries. Given this prevalence, identifying risk factors and therapeutic interventions are pressing objectives—objectives that rest on neurobiologically grounded and psychologically informed theories about the underlying pathophysiology. In this article, we review the evidence that autism could result from a dysfunctional oxytocin system early in life. As a mediator of successful procreation, not only in the reproductive system, but also in the brain, oxytocin plays a crucial role in sculpting socio-sexual behavior. Formulated within a (Bayesian) predictive coding framework, we propose that oxytocin encodes the saliency or precision of interoceptive signals and enables the neuronal plasticity necessary for acquiring a generative model of the emotional and social 'self.' An aberrant oxytocin system in infancy could therefore help explain the marked deficits in language and social communication—as well as the sensory, autonomic, motor, behavioral, and cognitive abnormalities—seen in autism.

title: Using the Autism-Spectrum Quotient to Measure Autistic Traits in Anorexia Nervosa: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Westwood H, Eisler I, Mandy W, Leppanen J, Treasure J, Tchanturia K
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Interest in the link between Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and Anorexia Nervosa (AN) has led to estimates of the prevalence of autistic traits in AN. This systematic review and meta-analysis assessed the use of the Autism-Spectrum Quotient (AQ) or abbreviated version (AQ-10) to examine whether patients with AN have elevated levels of autistic traits. Seven studies were identified and subsequent meta-analysis indicated that those with AN appear to have significant difficulties of a manner characteristic of ASD, relative to controls. Whilst this analysis supports previous indications of higher prevalence of ASD in AN, the aetiology of these traits remains unclear. Studies using more robust clinical measures of ASD within AN are needed to confirm what self-report measures appear to show.

sheet.es: Si una persona que cuidas vive con anorexia, puede ser útil considerar también rasgos autistas: preferencias sensoriales, necesidad de rutina o diferencias sociales pueden influir en la alimentación y en qué apoyo le resulta cómodo. Pregunta con calma por esas experiencias y compártelas con el equipo de salud, sin sacar conclusiones por tu cuenta. Este metaanálisis reunió siete estudios que usaron el cuestionario AQ o AQ-10; las personas con anorexia puntuaron más alto en rasgos autistas que los grupos de comparación. Como límite, el AQ es un autoinforme, no un diagnóstico, y no se sabe si los rasgos son previos o efecto de la propia anorexia.
sheet.en: If someone you support lives with anorexia, it may help to also consider autistic traits: sensory preferences, a need for routine or social differences can shape eating and which kinds of support feel manageable. Gently ask about these experiences and share them with the care team, rather than drawing conclusions yourself. This meta-analysis pooled seven studies using the AQ or AQ-10 questionnaire; people with anorexia scored higher on autistic traits than comparison groups. A key limit: the AQ is self-report, not a diagnosis, and it remains unclear whether these traits came first or partly reflect the effects of anorexia itself.
sheet.sv: Om någon du stöttar lever med anorexi kan det hjälpa att också tänka på autistiska drag: sensoriska preferenser, behov av rutiner eller sociala skillnader kan påverka ätandet och vilket stöd som känns hanterbart. Fråga lugnt om sådana erfarenheter och dela dem med vårdteamet, istället för att dra egna slutsatser. Denna metaanalys sammanställde sju studier som använde enkäten AQ eller AQ-10; personer med anorexi skattade högre på autistiska drag än jämförelsegrupper. En viktig begränsning: AQ är självskattning, inte en diagnos, och det är oklart om dragen fanns före anorexin eller delvis speglar dess effekter.

title: Striatal Circuits as a Common Node for Autism Pathophysiology.
authors: Fuccillo MV
abstract: Autism spectrum disorders (ASD) are characterized by two seemingly unrelated symptom domains-deficits in social interactions and restrictive, repetitive patterns of behavioral output. Whether the diverse nature of ASD symptomatology represents distributed dysfunction of brain networks or abnormalities within specific neural circuits is unclear. Striatal dysfunction is postulated to underlie the repetitive motor behaviors seen in ASD, and neurological and brain-imaging studies have supported this assumption. However, as our appreciation of striatal function expands to include regulation of behavioral flexibility, motivational state, goal-directed learning, and attention, we consider whether alterations in striatal physiology are a central node mediating a range of autism-associated behaviors, including social and cognitive deficits that are hallmarks of the disease. This review investigates multiple genetic mouse models of ASD to explore whether abnormalities in striatal circuits constitute a common pathophysiological mechanism in the development of autism-related behaviors. Despite the heterogeneity of genetic insult investigated, numerous genetic ASD models display alterations in the structure and function of striatal circuits, as well as abnormal behaviors including repetitive grooming, stereotypic motor routines, deficits in social interaction and decision-making. Comparative analysis in rodents provides a unique opportunity to leverage growing genetic association data to reveal canonical neural circuits whose dysfunction directly contributes to discrete aspects of ASD symptomatology. The description of such circuits could provide both organizing principles for understanding the complex genetic etiology of ASD as well as novel treatment routes. Furthermore, this focus on striatal mechanisms of behavioral regulation may also prove useful for exploring the pathogenesis of other neuropsychiatric diseases, which display overlapping behavioral deficits with ASD.

sheet.es: Mañana no hace falta cambiar nada en casa por este estudio. Sugiere que una zona del cerebro, el estriado, podría estar relacionada con la repetición, la flexibilidad, la motivación y la atención en el autismo. Para quien cuida, puede ayudar a ver los movimientos repetitivos y la necesidad de rutinas como parte de cómo funciona ese cerebro, no como algo que haya que corregir: anticipar cambios y respetar formas de autorregularse sigue siendo útil. Es una revisión de estudios con ratones modificados genéticamente; no participaron personas autistas. Sus límites son claros: los ratones no reflejan la experiencia humana y no ofrece tratamientos ni conclusiones válidas para cada persona.
sheet.en: Nothing needs to change at home tomorrow because of this study. It suggests that one brain area, the striatum, may be linked to repetition, flexibility, motivation and attention in autism. For caregivers, it can help frame repetitive movements and the need for routine as part of how that brain works, not something to fix: preparing for changes and respecting ways of self-regulating remain helpful. This is a review of studies in genetically modified mice; no autistic people took part. Its limits are clear: mice cannot reflect human experience, and it offers no treatments or conclusions that apply to every person.
sheet.sv: Ingenting behöver ändras hemma i morgon på grund av den här studien. Den antyder att ett hjärnområde, striatum, kan ha samband med upprepning, flexibilitet, motivation och uppmärksamhet vid autism. För dig som stöttar kan den hjälpa till att se upprepade rörelser och behovet av rutiner som en del av hur hjärnan fungerar, inte något som ska rättas till: att förbereda förändringar och respektera sätt att självreglera är fortfarande värdefullt. Det är en översikt av studier på genmodifierade möss; inga autistiska personer deltog. Begränsningarna är tydliga: möss speglar inte mänsklig erfarenhet, och översikten ger inga behandlingar eller slutsatser som gäller alla.

title: A Short Review on the Current Understanding of Autism Spectrum Disorders.
authors: Park HR, Lee JM, Moon HE, Lee DS, Kim BN, Kim J, Kim DG, Paek SH
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a set of neurodevelopmental disorders characterized by a deficit in social behaviors and nonverbal interactions such as reduced eye contact, facial expression, and body gestures in the first 3 years of life. It is not a single disorder, and it is broadly considered to be a multi-factorial disorder resulting from genetic and non-genetic risk factors and their interaction. Genetic studies of ASD have identified mutations that interfere with typical neurodevelopment in utero through childhood. These complexes of genes have been involved in synaptogenesis and axon motility. Recent developments in neuroimaging studies have provided many important insights into the pathological changes that occur in the brain of patients with ASD in vivo. Especially, the role of amygdala, a major component of the limbic system and the affective loop of the cortico-striatothalamo-cortical circuit, in cognition and ASD has been proved in numerous neuropathological and neuroimaging studies. Besides the amygdala, the nucleus accumbens is also considered as the key structure which is related with the social reward response in ASD. Although educational and behavioral treatments have been the mainstay of the management of ASD, pharmacological and interventional treatments have also shown some benefit in subjects with ASD. Also, there have been reports about few patients who experienced improvement after deep brain stimulation, one of the interventional treatments. The key architecture of ASD development which could be a target for treatment is still an uncharted territory. Further work is needed to broaden the horizons on the understanding of ASD.

sheet.es: Para mañana por la mañana: el autismo no es una sola cosa y cada persona autista es distinta, así que conviene observar qué le ayuda a ella en concreto y no seguir una receta general. Esta es una revisión de la literatura sobre genética, estudios de imagen cerebral y tratamientos; no describe a un grupo concreto de participantes. Resume que los apoyos educativos y conductuales son la base del abordaje. Sobre otros tratamientos, las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico. Sus límites: es breve, usa un lenguaje centrado en déficits y concluye que aún se entiende poco cómo se desarrolla el autismo. No sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: For tomorrow morning: autism is not one single thing and every autistic person is different, so it helps to notice what works for this particular person rather than follow a general recipe. This is a review of the literature on genetics, brain imaging and treatments; it does not describe a specific group of participants. It reports that educational and behavioural supports are the mainstay of support. For any other treatments, medical decisions belong to a clinician. Its limits: it is brief, uses deficit-focused language, and concludes that how autism develops is still poorly understood. It is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Inför i morgon bitti: autism är inte en enda sak och varje autistisk person är olika, så det hjälper att lägga märke till vad som fungerar för just den personen i stället för att följa ett generellt recept. Det här är en översikt av litteraturen om genetik, hjärnavbildning och behandlingar; den beskriver ingen särskild grupp deltagare. Den uppger att pedagogiskt och beteendeinriktat stöd är grunden i stödet. När det gäller andra behandlingar hör medicinska beslut till en läkare eller annan kliniker. Begränsningar: den är kort, använder ett bristfokuserat språk och drar slutsatsen att vi fortfarande förstår lite av hur autism utvecklas. Den är ingen regel för alla.

title: Autism and sleep disorders.
authors: Devnani PA, Hegde AU
abstract: "Autism Spectrum Disorders" (ASDs) are neurodevelopment disorders and are characterized by persistent impairments in reciprocal social interaction and communication. Sleep problems in ASD, are a prominent feature that have an impact on social interaction, day to day life, academic achievement, and have been correlated with increased maternal stress and parental sleep disruption. Polysomnography studies of ASD children showed most of their abnormalities related to rapid eye movement (REM) sleep which included decreased quantity, increased undifferentiated sleep, immature organization of eye movements into discrete bursts, decreased time in bed, total sleep time, REM sleep latency, and increased proportion of stage 1 sleep. Implementation of nonpharmacotherapeutic measures such as bedtime routines and sleep-wise approach is the mainstay of behavioral management. Treatment strategies along with limited regulated pharmacotherapy can help improve the quality of life in ASD children and have a beneficial impact on the family. PubMed search was performed for English language articles from January 1995 to January 2015. Following key words: Autism spectrum disorder, sleep disorders and autism, REM sleep and autism, cognitive behavioral therapy, sleep-wise approach, melatonin and ASD were used. Only articles reporting primary data relevant to the above questions were included.

sheet.es: Si el sueño de su hijo autista es difícil, pruebe una rutina fija a la hora de dormir y observe qué le ayuda; es un buen primer paso. Esta revisión de estudios publicados entre enero de 1995 y enero de 2015 señala que los problemas de sueño son frecuentes en el autismo, afectan la vida diaria y pueden aumentar el estrés y alterar el sueño de las familias. Indica que las rutinas y los enfoques sin medicación son la base del manejo. Sus límites: reúne trabajos de distinto tipo, solo en inglés, y no todas las personas autistas duermen igual. Las decisiones médicas corresponden a un clínico.
sheet.en: If sleep is hard for your autistic child, try a steady bedtime routine and notice what helps; it is a sensible first step. This review of studies published between January 1995 and January 2015 reports that sleep problems are common in autism, affect daily life, and can raise stress and disrupt sleep for families. It describes routines and non-medication approaches as the mainstay of support. Its limits: it pools varied studies, only in English, and autistic people do not all sleep the same way. Medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om sömnen är svår för ditt autistiska barn kan du prova en fast kvällsrutin och lägga märke till vad som hjälper; det är ett rimligt första steg. Den här översikten av studier publicerade mellan januari 1995 och januari 2015 beskriver att sömnproblem är vanliga vid autism, påverkar vardagen och kan öka stressen och störa sömnen hos familjen. Den beskriver rutiner och metoder utan läkemedel som grunden i stödet. Begränsningar: den sammanfattar olika slags studier, bara på engelska, och autistiska personer sover inte alla likadant. Medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker.

title: Lurasidone for the Treatment of Irritability Associated with Autistic Disorder.
authors: Loebel A, Brams M, Goldman RS, Silva R, Hernandez D, Deng L, Mankoski R, Findling RL
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: The aim of this study was to evaluate the short-term efficacy and safety of lurasidone in treating irritability associated with autistic disorder. In this multicenter trial, outpatients age 6-17 years who met DSM-IV-TR criteria for autistic disorder, and who demonstrated irritability, agitation, and/or self-injurious behaviors were randomized to 6 weeks of double-blind treatment with lurasidone 20 mg/day (N = 50), 60 mg/day (N = 49), or placebo (N = 51). Efficacy measures included the Aberrant Behavior Checklist Irritability subscale (ABC-I, the primary endpoint) and the Clinical Global Impressions, Improvement (CGI-I) scale, and were analyzed using a likelihood-based mixed model for repeated measures. Least squares (LS) mean (standard error [SE]) improvement from baseline to Week 6 in the ABC-I was not significantly different for lurasidone 20 mg/day (-8.8 [1.5]) and lurasidone 60 mg/day (-9.4 [1.4]) versus placebo (-7.5 [1.5]; p = 0.55 and 0.36, respectively). CGI-I scores showed significantly greater LS mean [SE] improvement at Week 6 for lurasidone 20 mg/day versus placebo (2.8 [0.2] vs. 3.4 [0.2]; p = 0.035) but not for lurasidone 60 mg/day (3.1 [0.2]; p = 0.27). Discontinuation rates due to adverse events were: lurasidone 20 mg/day, 4.1%; 60 mg/day, 3.9%; and placebo, 8.2%. Adverse events with an incidence ≥10% (lurasidone combined, placebo) included vomiting (18.0, 4.1%) and somnolence (12.0, 4.1%). Modest changes were observed in weight and selected metabolic parameters. In this study, once-daily, fixed doses of 20 and 60 mg/day of lurasidone were not demonstrated to be efficacious compared to placebo for the short-term treatment of children and adolescents with moderate-to-severe irritability associated with autistic disorder.

sheet.es: Si a una persona autista le cuesta mucho la irritabilidad, la agitación o se hace daño, anota cuándo ocurre y qué pasa antes; eso ayuda a buscar apoyos concretos. Este fue un estudio médico, y las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico. Fue un ensayo con doble ciego en el que participaron niños y adolescentes de 6-17 años durante 6 semanas, comparados con placebo. Sus límites: fue de corta duración y no representa a todas las personas. Si hay autolesiones o riesgo, consulta cuanto antes con un profesional clínico, un servicio de salud o un servicio de crisis; si hay peligro inmediato, llama al número de emergencias de tu país.
sheet.en: If an autistic person is very irritable, agitated or hurting themselves, note when it happens and what comes before it; this helps you look for concrete supports. This was a medical study, and medical decisions belong to a clinician. It was a double-blind trial in children and adolescents aged 6-17 years, lasting 6 weeks and compared with placebo. Its limits: it was short and does not describe every person. If there is self-injury or risk, contact a clinician, a health service or a crisis service soon; in immediate danger, call the emergency number of your country.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person är mycket irriterad, orolig eller skadar sig själv, anteckna när det sker och vad som föregår det; det hjälper dig att hitta konkret stöd. Detta var en medicinsk studie, och medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker. Det var en dubbelblind studie med barn och ungdomar i åldern 6-17 år, under 6 veckor, jämfört med placebo. Begränsningar: den var kort och gäller inte alla personer. Vid självskada eller risk, kontakta en kliniker, vården eller en krisjour i god tid; vid omedelbar fara, ring ditt lands nödnummer.

title: Toward Developmental Connectomics of the Human Brain.
authors: Cao M, Huang H, Peng Y, Dong Q, He Y
abstract: Imaging connectomics based on graph theory has become an effective and unique methodological framework for studying structural and functional connectivity patterns of the developing brain. Normal brain development is characterized by continuous and significant network evolution throughout infancy, childhood, and adolescence, following specific maturational patterns. Disruption of these normal changes is associated with neuropsychiatric developmental disorders, such as autism spectrum disorders or attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder. In this review, we focused on the recent progresses regarding typical and atypical development of human brain networks from birth to early adulthood, using a connectomic approach. Specifically, by the time of birth, structural networks already exhibit adult-like organization, with global efficient small-world and modular structures, as well as hub regions and rich-clubs acting as communication backbones. During development, the structure networks are fine-tuned, with increased global integration and robustness and decreased local segregation, as well as the strengthening of the hubs. In parallel, functional networks undergo more dramatic changes during maturation, with both increased integration and segregation during development, as brain hubs shift from primary regions to high order functioning regions, and the organization of modules transitions from a local anatomical emphasis to a more distributed architecture. These findings suggest that structural networks develop earlier than functional networks; meanwhile functional networks demonstrate more dramatic maturational changes with the evolution of structural networks serving as the anatomical backbone. In this review, we also highlighted topologically disorganized characteristics in structural and functional brain networks in several major developmental neuropsychiatric disorders (e.g., autism spectrum disorders, attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder and developmental dyslexia). Collectively, we showed that delineation of the brain network from a connectomics perspective offers a unique and refreshing view of both normal development and neuropsychiatric disorders.

sheet.es: Este estudio no ofrece una pauta para mañana por la mañana: describe cómo se organizan y cambian las redes del cerebro desde el nacimiento hasta la edad adulta temprana. Puede ayudar a recordar que cada cerebro se desarrolla a su propio ritmo y que conviene ir sin prisa. Es una revisión de investigaciones que usan imágenes cerebrales; el resumen no indica cuántas personas participaron. Incluye resultados sobre autismo, pero no explica qué hacer en la vida diaria, usa un lenguaje de trastornos que no compartimos y no sirve como regla para cada persona autista.
sheet.en: This study offers no step for tomorrow morning: it describes how brain networks are organised and change from birth to early adulthood. It may be a reminder that every brain develops at its own pace, so there is no need to rush. It is a review of research using brain imaging; the abstract does not say how many people took part. It includes findings on autism, but it does not explain what to do in daily life, it uses disorder-based language we do not share, and it cannot be taken as a rule for every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Studien ger inget konkret att göra i morgon bitti: den beskriver hur hjärnans nätverk är uppbyggda och förändras från födseln till tidig vuxenålder. Den kan påminna om att varje hjärna utvecklas i sin egen takt, så det finns ingen anledning att stressa. Det är en översikt av forskning med hjärnavbildning; sammanfattningen anger inte hur många personer som deltog. Den tar upp resultat om autism, men säger inte vad man ska göra i vardagen, använder ett språk om sjukdomar som vi inte delar och kan inte ses som en regel för alla autistiska personer.

title: A review of executive function deficits in autism spectrum disorder and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder.
authors: Craig F, Margari F, Legrottaglie AR, Palumbi R, de Giambattista C, Margari L
abstract: Executive dysfunction has been shown to be a promising endophenotype in neurodevelopmental disorders such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). This article reviewed 26 studies that examined executive function comparing ASD and/or ADHD children. In light of findings from this review, the ASD + ADHD group appears to share impairment in both flexibility and planning with the ASD group, while it shares the response inhibition deficit with the ADHD group. Conversely, deficit in attention, working memory, preparatory processes, fluency, and concept formation does not appear to be distinctive in discriminating from ASD, ADHD, or ASD + ADHD group. On the basis of neurocognitive endophenotype, the common co-occurrence of executive function deficits seems to reflect an additive comorbidity, rather than a separate condition with distinct impairments.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija es autista, y quizá también tiene TDAH, puede ayudar observar qué le cuesta concretamente: cambiar de plan, organizar pasos o frenar un impulso. Avisar de los cambios con antelación, dividir tareas en pasos visibles y dar pausas antes de responder son apoyos sencillos que puedes probar mañana, ajustándolos a la persona. Esta revisión reunió 26 estudios con niños y niñas autistas, con TDAH o con ambos; quienes tenían ambos mostraban a la vez las dificultades típicas de cada uno, sumadas. Limitación: compara promedios de grupos con pruebas de laboratorio, así que no describe a cada niño ni su vida diaria.
sheet.en: If your child is autistic, and perhaps also has ADHD, it can help to notice what specifically is hard: switching plans, organising steps, or pausing before acting. Announcing changes ahead of time, breaking tasks into visible steps, and allowing a pause before responding are simple supports you can try tomorrow, adjusted to the person. This review gathered 26 studies of autistic children, children with ADHD, and children with both; those with both showed the typical differences of each, added together. Limitation: it compares group averages from lab tests, so it does not describe every child or their daily life.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn är autistiskt, och kanske också har ADHD, kan det hjälpa att lägga märke till vad som konkret är svårt: att byta plan, organisera steg eller hejda en impuls. Att förvarna om förändringar, dela upp uppgifter i synliga steg och ge en paus innan svar är enkla stöd du kan prova i morgon, anpassade efter personen. Översikten samlade 26 studier med autistiska barn, barn med ADHD och barn med båda; de med båda visade de typiska skillnaderna från vardera, sammanlagda. Begränsning: den jämför gruppgenomsnitt från labbtester och beskriver därför inte varje barn eller dess vardag.

title: Alteration of functional connectivity in autism spectrum disorder: effect of age and anatomical distance.
authors: Long Z, Duan X, Mantini D, Chen H
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is associated with disruption of local- and long-range functional connectivity (FC). The direction of those changes in FC (increase or decrease), however, is inconsistent across studies. Further, age-dependent changes of distance-specific FC in ASD remain unclear. In this study, we used resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging data from sixty-four typical controls (TC) and sixty-four patients with ASD, whom we further classified into child ( 18 years). Functional connectivity (FC) analysis was conducted at voxel level. We employed a three-way analysis of covariance on FC to conduct statistical analyses. Results revealed that patients with ASD had lower FC than TC in cerebellum, fusiform gyrus, inferior occipital gyrus and posterior inferior temporal gyrus. Significant diagnosis-by-distance interaction was observed in ASD patients with reduced short-range and long-range FC in posterior cingulate cortex and medial prefrontal cortex. Importantly, we found significant diagnosis-by-age-by-distance interaction in orbitofrontal cortex with short-range FC being lower in autistic children, but -to a less extent- higher in autistic adults. Our findings suggest a major role of connection length in development changes of FC in ASD. We hope our study will facilitate deeper understanding of the neural mechanisms underlying ASD.

sheet.es: Este estudio no ofrece algo que cambie la rutina de mañana. Sí recuerda que el cerebro autista no es igual en todas las edades, así que conviene no suponer que lo observado en la infancia se mantiene en la adultez. Fue un estudio con resonancia magnética en reposo, con 64 personas autistas y 64 controles típicos, que midió cómo se conectan distintas zonas del cerebro. Halló menos conexión en varias regiones, y diferencias según la edad y la distancia entre zonas. Sus límites: es una comparación en un único momento, no sigue a cada persona en el tiempo, y no indica qué hacer en casa ni vale como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: This study offers nothing that changes tomorrow's routine. It is a reminder that autistic brains are not the same at every age, so it helps not to assume that what is seen in childhood stays the same in adulthood. It was a resting-state brain scan study with 64 autistic people and 64 typical controls, measuring how different brain areas connect. It found lower connectivity in several regions, with differences by age and by distance between areas. Its limits: it compares groups at one point in time rather than following each person, and it gives no advice for home and is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Den här studien ger inget som ändrar morgondagens rutiner. Den påminner om att autistiska hjärnor inte är likadana i alla åldrar, så det är bra att inte anta att det som syns i barndomen består i vuxen ålder. Det var en hjärnavbildningsstudie i vila med 64 autistiska personer och 64 typiska kontroller, som mätte hur olika delar av hjärnan samspelar. Den fann lägre konnektivitet i flera områden, med skillnader efter ålder och avstånd mellan områden. Begränsningar: den jämför grupper vid ett tillfälle och följer inte varje person över tid, ger inga råd för hemmet och gäller inte som regel för varje person.

title: Toward an Interdisciplinary Understanding of Sensory Dysfunction in Autism Spectrum Disorder: An Integration of the Neural and Symptom Literatures.
authors: Schauder KB, Bennetto L
abstract: Sensory processing differences have long been associated with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), and they have recently been added to the diagnostic criteria for the disorder. The focus on sensory processing in ASD research has increased substantially in the last decade. This research has been approached from two different perspectives: the first focuses on characterizing the symptoms that manifest in response to real world sensory stimulation, and the second focuses on the neural pathways and mechanisms underlying sensory processing. The purpose of this paper is to integrate the empirical literature on sensory processing in ASD from the last decade, including both studies characterizing sensory symptoms and those that investigate neural response to sensory stimuli. We begin with a discussion of definitions to clarify some of the inconsistencies in terminology that currently exist in the field. Next, the sensory symptoms literature is reviewed with a particular focus on developmental considerations and the relationship of sensory symptoms to other core features of the disorder. Then, the neuroscience literature is reviewed with a focus on methodological approaches and specific sensory modalities. Currently, these sensory symptoms and neuroscience perspectives are largely developing independently from each other leading to multiple, but separate, theories and methods, thus creating a multidisciplinary approach to sensory processing in ASD. In order to progress our understanding of sensory processing in ASD, it is now critical to integrate these two research perspectives and move toward an interdisciplinary approach. This will inevitably aid in a better understanding of the underlying biological basis of these symptoms and help realize the translational value through its application to early identification and treatment. The review ends with specific recommendations for future research to help bridge these two research perspectives in order to advance our understanding of sensory processing in ASD.

sheet.es: Tome en serio las diferencias sensoriales de la persona autista: observe qué sonidos, luces, texturas o contactos le resultan abrumadores o agradables, y ajuste el entorno según eso. Esta es una revisión de estudios de la última década sobre procesamiento sensorial en el autismo, que reúne trabajos sobre síntomas sensoriales y sobre respuestas neuronales. Sus autores señalan que ambas líneas se han desarrollado por separado y que hay que integrarlas. No ofrece una guía práctica concreta ni describe a cada persona: las experiencias sensoriales varían mucho. Lo que la persona le cuente o muestre pesa más que cualquier generalización.
sheet.en: Take the autistic person's sensory differences seriously: notice which sounds, lights, textures or touch feel overwhelming or pleasant to them, and adjust the environment accordingly. This is a review of the last decade of studies on sensory processing in autism, bringing together work on sensory symptoms and on neural responses. Its authors note that these two lines of research have developed separately and need to be integrated. It offers no concrete practical guidance and does not describe every individual: sensory experiences vary a lot. What the person tells or shows you matters more than any generalisation.
sheet.sv: Ta den autistiska personens sensoriska skillnader på allvar: lägg märke till vilka ljud, ljus, material eller beröring som känns överväldigande eller sköna, och anpassa miljön efter det. Detta är en översikt av det senaste decenniets studier om sensorisk bearbetning vid autism, som samlar forskning om sensoriska symtom och om hjärnans svar. Författarna menar att de två forskningslinjerna utvecklats separat och behöver föras samman. Den ger ingen konkret praktisk vägledning och beskriver inte varje person: sensoriska upplevelser varierar mycket. Det personen berättar eller visar väger tyngre än alla generaliseringar.

title: Aggression in autism spectrum disorder: presentation and treatment options.
authors: Fitzpatrick SE, Srivorakiat L, Wink LK, Pedapati EV, Erickson CA
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by persistent difficulties in social communication and social interaction, coupled with restricted, repetitive patterns of behavior or interest. Research indicates that aggression rates may be higher in individuals with ASD compared to those with other developmental disabilities. Aggression is associated with negative outcomes for children with ASD and their caregivers, including decreased quality of life, increased stress levels, and reduced availability of educational and social support. Therapeutic strategies including functional behavioral assessment, reinforcement strategies, and functional communication training may have a significant impact in reducing the frequency and intensity of aggressive behavior in individuals with ASD. Pharmacologic treatments, particularly the use of second-generation antipsychotics, may also be of some benefit in reducing aggression in individuals with ASD. With the ever-increasing rate of ASD diagnosis, development of effective therapeutic and pharmacologic methods for preventing and treating aggression are essential to improving outcomes in this disorder.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista muestra agresividad, conviene buscar primero qué función cumple: qué intenta comunicar, evitar u obtener. Una evaluación funcional de la conducta, el refuerzo de alternativas y el entrenamiento en comunicación funcional pueden ayudar a reducir su frecuencia e intensidad. Es una revisión de la literatura, sin participantes propios. Menciona también tratamientos médicos, pero esas decisiones corresponden siempre a un profesional clínico. Sus límites: resume estudios muy diversos, no garantiza que algo funcione para cada persona y no sustituye una valoración individual con profesionales que conozcan a la persona.
sheet.en: If an autistic person shows aggression, a useful first step is to look for its purpose: what they may be trying to communicate, avoid or get. Functional behavioral assessment, reinforcing alternative responses and functional communication training may help reduce how often and how intensely it happens. This is a review of existing literature, so it had no participants of its own. It also covers medical treatments, but those decisions belong to a clinician. Limits: it summarizes varied studies, cannot promise that an approach works for every person, and does not replace an individual assessment by professionals who know the person.
