sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person visar aggression kan det hjälpa att först söka dess funktion: vad personen kanske försöker uttrycka, undvika eller få. Funktionell beteendeanalys, förstärkning av alternativa sätt och funktionell kommunikationsträning kan minska hur ofta och hur starkt det sker. Detta är en översikt av befintlig forskning, utan egna deltagare. Den tar också upp medicinska behandlingar, men sådana beslut hör till en kliniker. Begränsningar: den sammanfattar skilda studier, kan inte lova att ett upplägg fungerar för alla och ersätter inte en individuell bedömning av yrkespersoner som känner personen.

title: Incidence of oral health in paediatric patients with disabilities: Sensory disorders and autism spectrum disorder. Systematic review II.
authors: Bartolomé-Villar B, Mourelle-Martínez MR, Diéguez-Pérez M, de Nova-García MJ
journal: Journal of clinical and experimental dentistry
abstract: Introduction We are currently witnessing an increase in the number of disabled patients, creating the need for knowledge of each of the pathologies and of the different oral and dental conditions they present, in order to achieve efficient management and treatment. Objectives To analyse the existing scientific literature on the oral conditions of children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and children with sensory deficits (SD), in comparison with the healthy child population. Material and methods The bibliographic search was carried out in Pubmed/Medline, Scopus and Cochrane Library and included articles taking a sample of children between 0 and 18 years of age diagnosed with the abovementioned disorders and including at least one of the following oral hygiene conditions - oral hygiene, dental caries, malocclusion, oral habits, dental trauma, and gingival-periodontal status - comparing them with a healthy population. Results A total of 10 articles were obtained for autism spectrum disorder and six for sensory deficits. Conclusions Of all the variables studied, only the state of oral, gingival and/or periodontal hygiene can be considered worse in patients with ASD and SD, although we believe a larger number of research studies is needed to corroborate these results. Key words Oral health, dental caries, malocclusion, oral habits, dental trauma, oral hygiene, disabled child, autism, autism spectrum disorder, deaf, blind.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista, puede ayudar prestar atención extra a la higiene de la boca y las encías, y preparar el cepillado con apoyos sensoriales y rutinas predecibles. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 10 artículos sobre autismo y seis sobre déficits sensoriales, con niños de 0 a 18 años comparados con población sin estas condiciones. Encontró que solo la higiene oral, gingival o periodontal parecía peor; en caries, maloclusión, hábitos orales y traumatismos no se concluyó lo mismo. Los autores indican que hacen falta más estudios, y los resultados no valen para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person, it may help to give extra attention to mouth and gum care, and to make brushing easier with sensory adjustments and predictable routines. This systematic review gathered 10 articles on autism and six on sensory deficits, with children aged 0 to 18 compared with children without these conditions. Only oral, gingival or periodontal hygiene appeared worse; the other areas, such as caries, malocclusion, oral habits and dental trauma, did not show the same. The authors say more research is needed, and the findings do not apply to every person.
sheet.sv: Om du stödjer en autistisk person kan det hjälpa att vara extra uppmärksam på munhygien och tandkött, och att göra tandborstningen lättare med sensoriska anpassningar och förutsägbara rutiner. Denna systematiska översikt samlade 10 artiklar om autism och sex om sensoriska funktionsnedsättningar, med barn från 0 till 18 år jämfört med barn utan dessa tillstånd. Bara munhygien, tandköttets och tandfästets tillstånd verkade sämre; för karies, bettavvikelser, orala vanor och tandskador sågs inte samma sak. Författarna menar att mer forskning behövs, och resultaten gäller inte alla personer.

title: Atopic diseases and inflammation of the brain in the pathogenesis of autism spectrum disorders.
authors: Theoharides TC, Tsilioni I, Patel AB, Doyle R
abstract: Autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) affect as many as 1 in 45 children and are characterized by deficits in sociability and communication, as well as stereotypic movements. Many children also show severe anxiety. The lack of distinct pathogenesis and reliable biomarkers hampers the development of effective treatments. As a result, most children with ASD are prescribed psychopharmacologic agents that do not address the core symptoms of ASD. Autoantibodies against brain epitopes in mothers of children with ASD and many such children strongly correlate with allergic symptoms and indicate an aberrant immune response, as well as disruption of the blood-brain barrier (BBB). Recent epidemiological studies have shown a strong statistical correlation between risk for ASD and either maternal or infantile atopic diseases, such as asthma, eczema, food allergies and food intolerance, all of which involve activation of mast cells (MCs). These unique tissue immune cells are located perivascularly in all tissues, including the thalamus and hypothalamus, which regulate emotions. MC-derived inflammatory and vasoactive mediators increase BBB permeability. Expression of the inflammatory molecules interleukin (IL-1β), IL-6, 1 L-17 and tumor necrosis factor (TNF) is increased in the brain, cerebrospinal fluid and serum of some patients with ASD, while NF-kB is activated in brain samples and stimulated peripheral blood immune cells of other patients; however, these molecules are not specific. Instead the peptide neurotensin is uniquely elevated in the serum of children with ASD, as is corticotropin-releasing hormone, secreted from the hypothalamus under stress. Both peptides trigger MC to release IL-6 and TNF, which in turn, stimulate microglia proliferation and activation, leading to disruption of neuronal connectivity. MC-derived IL-6 and TGFβ induce maturation of Th17 cells and MCs also secrete IL-17, which is increased in ASD. Serum IL-6 and TNF may define an ASD subgroup that benefits most from treatment with the natural flavonoid luteolin. Atopic diseases may create a phenotype susceptible to ASD and formulations targeting focal inflammation of the brain could have great promise in the treatment of ASD.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija autista tiene asma, eccema o alergias alimentarias, merece la pena tratarlas bien con su equipo de salud: el malestar físico, el picor o la dificultad para respirar pueden afectar al sueño, la ansiedad y el día a día. Anote síntomas y momentos difíciles para compartirlos en la consulta. Esta revisión narrativa reúne estudios previos que relacionan las alergias y la inflamación con el autismo; no incluyó participantes propios. Sus límites: plantea hipótesis sobre causas biológicas aún no confirmadas, y no demuestra que ningún suplemento o tratamiento antiinflamatorio sea adecuado para cada persona.
sheet.en: If your autistic child has asthma, eczema or food allergies, it is worth managing them well with your health team: physical discomfort, itching or breathing difficulties can affect sleep, anxiety and everyday life. Keep brief notes on symptoms and hard moments to share at appointments. This narrative review brings together earlier studies linking allergies and inflammation with autism; it did not recruit its own participants. Its limits: it proposes biological explanations that are not yet confirmed, and it does not show that any supplement or anti-inflammatory treatment suits every person.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn har astma, eksem eller matallergi är det värt att behandla dem ordentligt tillsammans med vården: kroppsligt obehag, klåda eller andningsbesvär kan påverka sömn, oro och vardagen. Skriv korta anteckningar om symtom och svåra stunder att ta med till besöken. Denna narrativa översikt sammanställer tidigare studier som kopplar allergier och inflammation till autism; den hade inga egna deltagare. Begränsningar: den föreslår biologiska förklaringar som ännu inte är bekräftade, och den visar inte att något kosttillskott eller antiinflammatorisk behandling passar alla.

title: Historical evolution of the concept of anorexia nervosa and relationships with orthorexia nervosa, autism, and obsessive-compulsive spectrum.
authors: Dell'Osso L, Abelli M, Carpita B, Pini S, Castellini G, Carmassi C, Ricca V
abstract: Eating disorders have been defined as "characterized by persistence disturbance of eating or eating-related behavior that results in the altered consumption or absorption of food and that significantly impairs health or psychosocial functioning". The psychopathology of eating disorders changed across time under the influence of environmental factors, determining the emergence of new phenotypes. Some of these conditions are still under investigation and are not clearly identified as independent diagnostic entities. In this review, the historic evolution of the eating disorder concept up to the recent Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition, has been evaluated. We also examined literature supporting the inclusion of new emergent eating behaviors within the eating disorder spectrum, and their relationship with anorexia, autism, and obsessive-compulsive disorder. In particular, we focused on what is known about the symptoms, epidemiology, assessment, and diagnostic boundaries of a new problematic eating pattern called orthorexia nervosa that could be accepted as a new psychological syndrome, as emphasized by an increasing number of scientific articles in the last few years.

title: Autism spectrum disorder in adults: diagnosis, management, and health services development.
authors: Murphy CM, Wilson CE, Robertson DM, Ecker C, Daly EM, Hammond N, Galanopoulos A, Dud I, Murphy DG, McAlonan GM
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a common neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by pervasive difficulties since early childhood across reciprocal social communication and restricted, repetitive interests and behaviors. Although early ASD research focused primarily on children, there is increasing recognition that ASD is a lifelong neurodevelopmental disorder. However, although health and education services for children with ASD are relatively well established, service provision for adults with ASD is in its infancy. There is a lack of health services research for adults with ASD, including identification of comorbid health difficulties, rigorous treatment trials (pharmacological and psychological), development of new pharmacotherapies, investigation of transition and aging across the lifespan, and consideration of sex differences and the views of people with ASD. This article reviews available evidence regarding the etiology, legislation, diagnosis, management, and service provision for adults with ASD and considers what is needed to support adults with ASD as they age. We conclude that health services research for adults with ASD is urgently warranted. In particular, research is required to better understand the needs of adults with ASD, including health, aging, service development, transition, treatment options across the lifespan, sex, and the views of people with ASD. Additionally, the outcomes of recent international legislative efforts to raise awareness of ASD and service provision for adults with ASD are to be determined. Future research is required to identify high-quality, evidence-based, and cost-effective models of care. Furthermore, future health services research is also required at the beginning and end of adulthood, including improved transition from youth to adult health care and increased understanding of aging and health in older adults with ASD.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista adulta, es normal que encuentres pocos servicios pensados para su edad. Anota sus necesidades de salud, sus preferencias y lo que le funciona, y llévalo a las citas; pregúntale siempre su opinión. Es una revisión de la literatura sobre diagnóstico, tratamiento y servicios para adultos autistas. Concluye que faltan investigaciones sobre salud, envejecimiento, el paso de la juventud a la atención adulta, las diferencias por sexo y la voz de las propias personas autistas. No ofrece una pauta válida para todas las personas, y los temas médicos deben consultarse con un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult, it is common to find few services designed for their age. Write down their health needs, preferences and what works for them, bring it to appointments, and always ask for their own view. This is a review of the literature on diagnosis, management and services for autistic adults. It concludes that more research is urgently needed on health, aging, the move from youth to adult care, sex differences and the views of autistic people themselves. It is not a rule for every person, and medical questions belong with a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen är det vanligt att det finns få tjänster anpassade för åldern. Skriv ner hälsobehov, önskemål och vad som fungerar, ta med det till besök och fråga alltid personen själv. Det här är en översikt av litteraturen om diagnos, insatser och vård för autistiska vuxna. Slutsatsen är att det behövs mer forskning om hälsa, åldrande, övergången från ungdoms- till vuxenvård, skillnader mellan könen och autistiska personers egna perspektiv. Den är ingen regel för alla, och medicinska frågor hör hemma hos en läkare.

title: Social Stories in mainstream schools for children with autism spectrum disorder: a feasibility randomised controlled trial.
authors: Marshall D, Wright B, Allgar V, Adamson J, Williams C, Ainsworth H, Cook L, Varley D, Hackney L, Dempster P, Ali S, Trepel D, Collingridge Moore D, Littlewood E, McMillan D
abstract: Objectives To assess the feasibility of recruitment, retention, outcome measures and intervention training/delivery among teachers, parents and children. To calculate a sample size estimation for full trial. Design A single-centre, unblinded, cluster feasibility randomised controlled trial examining Social Stories delivered within a school environment compared with an attentional control. Setting 37 primary schools in York, UK. Participants 50 participants were recruited and a cluster randomisation approach by school was examined. Participants were randomised into the treatment group (n=23) or a waiting list control group (n=27). Outcome measures Acceptability and feasibility of the trial, intervention and of measurements required to assess outcomes in a definitive trial. Results An assessment of the questionnaire completion rates indicated teachers would be most appropriate to complete the primary outcome measure. 2 outcome measures: the Social Responsiveness Scale (SRS)-2 and a goal-based measure showed both the highest levels of completion rates (above 80%) at the primary follow-up point (6 weeks postintervention) and captured relevant social and behaviour outcomes. Power calculations were based on these 2 outcome measures leading to a total proposed sample size of 180 participant groups. Conclusions Results suggest that a future trial would be feasible to conduct and could inform the policy and practice of using Social Stories in mainstream schools. Trial registration number ISRCTN96286707; Results.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija autista usa o podría usar Historias Sociales en la escuela, puede hablar con el profesorado sobre objetivos concretos y cómo se aplicarían. Este estudio no probó si las historias funcionan: fue un ensayo de viabilidad aleatorizado, con 50 participantes de escuelas primarias de York (Reino Unido), y comprobó si un estudio mayor sería posible. Los resultados indican que el profesorado era quien mejor podía completar los cuestionarios, y dos medidas se completaron en más del 80%. Límites: es un estudio pequeño, de una sola zona y sin cegamiento, y no demuestra beneficios para cada persona.
sheet.en: If your autistic child uses, or might use, Social Stories at school, you can talk with their teacher about specific goals and how the stories would be used. This study did not test whether they work: it was a randomised feasibility trial with 50 participants in primary schools in York, UK, checking whether a larger study would be possible. Teachers were best placed to complete the questionnaires, and two measures were completed more than 80% of the time. Limits: it was small, from one area and unblinded, and it does not show benefits for any individual child.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn använder eller kan komma att använda Sociala berättelser i skolan kan du prata med läraren om konkreta mål och hur berättelserna ska användas. Studien testade inte om de fungerar: det var en randomiserad genomförbarhetsstudie med 50 deltagare i grundskolor i York, Storbritannien, som undersökte om en större studie vore möjlig. Lärare var bäst lämpade att fylla i enkäterna, och två mått besvarades i över 80 %. Begränsningar: den var liten, från ett enda område och inte blind, och visar inte nytta för varje enskilt barn.

title: Heritability of autism spectrum disorders: a meta-analysis of twin studies.
authors: Tick B, Bolton P, Happé F, Rutter M, Rijsdijk F
journal: Journal of child psychology and psychiatry, and allied disciplines
abstract: Background The etiology of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) has been recently debated due to emerging findings on the importance of shared environmental influences. However, two recent twin studies do not support this and instead re-affirm strong genetic effects on the liability to ASD, a finding consistent with previous reports. This study conducts a systematic review and meta-analysis of all twin studies of ASD published to date and explores the etiology along the continuum of a quantitative measure of ASD. Methods A PubMed Central, Science Direct, Google Scholar, Web of Knowledge structured search conducted online, to identify all twin studies on ASD published to date. Thirteen primary twin studies were identified, seven were included in the meta-analysis by meeting Systematic Recruitment criterion; correction for selection and ascertainment strategies, and applied prevalences were assessed for these studies. In addition, a quantile DF extremes analysis was carried out on Childhood Autism Spectrum Test scores measured in a population sample of 6,413 twin pairs including affected twins. Results The meta-analysis correlations for monozygotic twins (MZ) were almost perfect at .98 (95% Confidence Interval, .96-.99). The dizygotic (DZ) correlation, however, was .53 (95% CI .44-.60) when ASD prevalence rate was set at 5% (in line with the Broad Phenotype of ASD) and increased to .67 (95% CI .61-.72) when applying a prevalence rate of 1%. The meta-analytic heritability estimates were substantial: 64-91%. Shared environmental effects became significant as the prevalence rate decreased from 5-1%: 07-35%. The DF analyses show that for the most part, there is no departure from linearity in heritability. Conclusions We demonstrate that: (a) ASD is due to strong genetic effects; (b) shared environmental effects become significant as a function of lower prevalence rate; (c) previously reported significant shared environmental influences are likely a statistical artefact of overinclusion of concordant DZ twins.

title: A trial of an iPad™ intervention targeting social communication skills in children with autism.
authors: Fletcher-Watson S, Petrou A, Scott-Barrett J, Dicks P, Graham C, O'Hare A, Pain H, McConachie H
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: This study evaluated a technology-based early intervention for social communication skills in pre-schoolers in a randomised controlled trial. Participants were 54 children aged under 6 years with a diagnosis of autism, assigned to either intervention or control conditions. The app engaged children, who played consistently, regardless of developmental level, and was rated highly by parents. There were no significant group differences in parent-report measures post-intervention, nor in a measure of parent-child play at follow-up. Therefore, this intervention did not have an observable impact on real-world social communication skills and caution is recommended about the potential usefulness of iPad(™) apps for amelioration of difficulties in interaction. However, positive attitudes among participants, lack of harms and the potential of apps to deliver therapeutic content at low economic cost suggest this approach is worth pursuing further, perhaps targeting other skill domains.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija usa una app de iPad, puede ser una actividad agradable, pero no cuente con que mejore por sí sola la comunicación social. Observe qué le gusta y siga practicando la interacción en el juego compartido. Fue un ensayo aleatorizado con 54 niños autistas menores de 6 años, repartidos entre intervención y control. Los niños jugaron de forma constante y los padres valoraron bien la app, pero no hubo diferencias significativas en las medidas de los padres ni en el juego entre padres e hijos en el seguimiento. Es un solo estudio, con una app concreta, y no dice cómo responderá cada niño.
sheet.en: If your child enjoys an iPad app, it can be a pleasant activity, but don't count on it to improve social communication by itself. Notice what they enjoy and keep practising interaction through shared play. This was a randomised controlled trial with 54 autistic children under 6 years, assigned to intervention or control. The children played consistently and parents rated the app highly, but there were no significant group differences in parent-report measures or in parent-child play at follow-up. It is one study of one particular app, and it cannot tell how any individual child will respond.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn tycker om en iPad-app kan den vara en trevlig aktivitet, men räkna inte med att den ensam förbättrar social kommunikation. Lägg märke till vad barnet gillar och fortsätt öva samspel i gemensam lek. Det här var en randomiserad kontrollerad studie med 54 autistiska barn under 6 år, fördelade på intervention eller kontroll. Barnen spelade jämnt och föräldrarna gav appen höga betyg, men inga signifikanta gruppskillnader sågs i föräldrarapporterade mått eller i lek mellan förälder och barn vid uppföljningen. Det är en enda studie av en specifik app och säger inte hur varje barn kommer att reagera.

title: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Multiple Airborne Pollutants and Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Lam J, Sutton P, Kalkbrenner A, Windham G, Halladay A, Koustas E, Lawler C, Davidson L, Daniels N, Newschaffer C, Woodruff T
abstract: Background Exposure to ambient air pollution is widespread and may be detrimental to human brain development and a potential risk factor for Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). We conducted a systematic review of the human evidence on the relationship between ASD and exposure to all airborne pollutants, including particulate matter air pollutants and others (e.g. pesticides and metals). Objective To answer the question: "is developmental exposure to air pollution associated with ASD?" Methods We conducted a comprehensive search of the literature, identified relevant studies using inclusion/exclusion criteria pre-specified in our protocol (registered in PROSPERO, CRD # 42015017890), evaluated the potential risk of bias for each included study and identified an appropriate subset of studies to combine in a meta-analysis. We then rated the overall quality and strength of the evidence collectively across all air pollutants. Results Of 1,158 total references identified, 23 human studies met our inclusion criteria (17 case-control, 4 ecological, 2 cohort). Risk of bias was generally low across studies for most domains; study limitations were related to potential confounding and accuracy of exposure assessment methods. We rated the quality of the body of evidence across all air pollutants as "moderate." From our meta-analysis, we found statistically significant summary odds ratios (ORs) of 1.07 (95% CI: 1.06, 1.08) per 10-μg/m3 increase in PM10 exposure (n = 6 studies) and 2.32 (95% CI: 2.15, 2.51) per 10-μg/m3 increase in PM2.5 exposure (n = 3 studies). For pollutants not included in a meta-analysis, we collectively evaluated evidence from each study in rating the strength and quality of overall evidence considering factors such as inconsistency, imprecision, and evidence of dose-response. All included studies generally showed increased risk of ASD with increasing exposure to air pollution, although not consistently across all chemical components. Conclusion After considering strengths and limitations of the body of research, we concluded that there is "limited evidence of toxicity" for the association between early life exposure to air pollution as a whole and diagnosis of ASD. The strongest evidence was between prenatal exposure to particulate matter and ASD. However, the small number of studies in the meta-analysis and unexplained statistical heterogeneity across the individual study estimates means that the effect could be larger or smaller (including not significant) than these studies estimate. Our research supports the need for health protective public policy to reduce exposures to harmful airborne contaminants among pregnant women and children and suggests opportunities for optimizing future research.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija ya es autista, este estudio no significa que hicieras algo mal: el aire que respiramos depende sobre todo de decisiones colectivas, no de una familia. Lo útil es apoyar políticas de aire limpio y, si estás embarazada o planeas estarlo, hablar con tu equipo de salud sobre formas sencillas de reducir la exposición a contaminación. Es una revisión sistemática con metaanálisis de 23 estudios en humanos que encontró una asociación entre partículas finas en el embarazo y diagnósticos de autismo. Sus límites: pocos estudios combinados, resultados variables y posibles factores de confusión; muestra asociación, no causa, y la evidencia se calificó como limitada.
sheet.en: If your child is already autistic, this study does not mean you did something wrong: the air we breathe depends mostly on collective decisions, not on one family. A useful step is supporting clean-air policies and, if you are pregnant or planning to be, talking with your health team about simple ways to reduce pollution exposure. This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of 23 human studies that found an association between fine particulate matter during pregnancy and autism diagnoses. Its limits: few studies were combined, results varied, and confounding is possible; it shows association, not cause, and the evidence was rated as limited.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn redan är autistiskt betyder studien inte att du gjort något fel: luften vi andas beror främst på gemensamma beslut, inte på en enskild familj. Ett användbart steg är att stödja politik för ren luft och, om du är gravid eller planerar att bli det, prata med vårdpersonal om enkla sätt att minska exponeringen för luftföroreningar. Detta är en systematisk översikt och metaanalys av 23 studier på människor som fann ett samband mellan fina partiklar under graviditeten och autismdiagnoser. Begränsningar: få studier kunde slås samman, resultaten varierade och störfaktorer är möjliga; studien visar samband, inte orsak, och evidensen bedömdes som begränsad.

title: A Developmental and Sequenced One-to-One Educational Intervention for Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Randomized Single-Blind Controlled Trial.
authors: Tanet A, Hubert-Barthelemy A, Crespin GC, Bodeau N, Cohen D, Saint-Georges C, GPIS Study Group
abstract: Introduction Individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) who also exhibit severe-to-moderate ranges of intellectual disability (ID) still face many challenges (i.e., less evidence-based trials, less inclusion in school with peers). Methods We implemented a novel model called the "Developmental and Sequenced One-to-One Educational Intervention" (DS1-EI) in 5- to 9-year-old children with co-occurring ASD and ID. The treatment protocol was adapted for school implementation by designing it using an educational agenda. The intervention was based on intensity, regular assessments, updating objectives, encouraging spontaneous communication, promoting skills through play with peers, supporting positive behaviors, providing supervision, capitalizing on teachers' unique skills, and providing developmental and sequenced learning. Developmental learning implies that the focus of training is what is close to the developmental expectations given a child's development in a specific domain. Sequenced learning means that the teacher changes the learning activities every 10-15 min to maintain the child's attention in the context of an anticipated time agenda. We selected 11 French institutions in which we implemented the model in small classrooms. Each institution recruited participants per dyads matched by age, sex, and developmental quotient. Patients from each dyad were then randomized to a DS1-EI group or a Treatment as usual (TAU) group for 36 months. The primary variables - the Childhood Autism Rating scale (CARS) and the psychoeducational profile (PEP-3) - will be blindly assessed by independent raters at the 18-month and 36-month follow-up. Discussion and baseline description We enrolled 75 participants: 38 were randomized to the DS1-EI and 37 to the TAU groups. At enrollment, we found no significant differences in participants' characteristics between groups. As expected, exposure to school was the only significant difference [9.4 (±4.1) h/week in the DS1-EI group vs. 3.4 (±4.5) h/week in the TAU group, Student's t -test, t = 5.83, p Ethics and dissemination The protocol was authorized by the competent national regulatory authority ( Agence nationale de sécurité du médicament et des produits de santé ) and approved by the local Ethics Committee ( Comité de Protection des Personnes ) at the University Hospital Saint-Antoine (May 7, 2013). The findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed journals and national and international conferences. Trial registration numbers ANSM130282B-31 (April 16 2013) and ACTRN12616000592448 (May 6 2016).

sheet.es: Si cuidas a un niño autista de 5 a 9 años con discapacidad intelectual, esta propuesta sugiere probar clases pequeñas con atención individual: actividades que cambian cada 10-15 min, objetivos cercanos a su nivel de desarrollo, juego con compañeros y apoyo a la comunicación espontánea. Es un ensayo aleatorizado con evaluadores ciegos en 11 centros franceses, con 75 participantes: 38 en la intervención y 37 en la atención habitual. El artículo describe el protocolo y el punto de partida; aún no ofrece resultados de eficacia. Por eso no permite saber si funciona, ni para cada niño. Habla con su equipo educativo.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic child aged 5 to 9 with intellectual disability, this approach suggests trying small classes with one-to-one teaching: activities that change every 10-15 min, goals close to the child's developmental level, play with peers and support for spontaneous communication. This is a randomized trial with blind raters in 11 French institutions, with 75 participants: 38 in the intervention and 37 in treatment as usual. The paper describes the protocol and starting point; it does not yet report effectiveness results. So it cannot tell us whether it works, or for every child. Talk with the school team.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar ett autistiskt barn på 5 till 9 år med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning pekar denna modell mot små klasser med individuell undervisning: aktiviteter som byts var 10-15 min, mål nära barnets utvecklingsnivå, lek med jämnåriga och stöd för spontan kommunikation. Det är en randomiserad studie med blindade bedömare vid 11 franska institutioner, med 75 deltagare: 38 i interventionen och 37 i vanlig behandling. Artikeln beskriver protokollet och utgångsläget, inte några resultat om effekt. Den kan därför inte visa om modellen fungerar, eller för alla barn. Prata med skolans team.

title: The role of augmentative and alternative communication for children with autism: current status and future trends.
authors: Iacono T, Trembath D, Erickson S
abstract: Background Augmentative and alternative communication (AAC) interventions are used for children with autism, often as stand-alone communication interventions for those who are minimally verbal. Our aim was to synthesize the evidence for AAC interventions for children (up to 21 years), and then consider the role of AAC within established, comprehensive, evidence-based autism interventions targeting learning across multiple developmental domains. Design We completed a systematic search of three databases (OVID Medline, PsycINFO, ERIC) as well as forward citation and hand searches to identify systematic reviews of AAC intervention efficacy research including children with autism, published between 2000 and March 2016 in peer-reviewed journals. Data pertaining to the quality indicators of included studies, effect sizes for intervention outcomes, and evidence for effectiveness were extracted for descriptive analysis. Results The search yielded 17 systematic reviews. Most provided indicators of research quality for included studies, of which only relatively few provided conclusive results. Communication targets tended to be focused on teaching children to make requests. Still, effect size measures for included studies indicated that AAC was effective to highly effective. Conclusion There is growing evidence for the potential benefits of AAC for children with autism, but there is a need for more well-designed studies and broader, targeted outcomes. Furthermore, a lack of evidence for the role of AAC within comprehensive intervention programs may account for a tendency by autism researchers and practitioners to neglect this intervention. Attempts to compare evidence for AAC with other interventions for children with autism, including those in which the use of AAC is delayed or excluded in pursuit of speech-only communication, must take into account the needs of children with the most significant learning needs. These children pose the greatest challenges to achieving large and consistent intervention effects, yet stand to gain the most from AAC interventions.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista habla poco o nada, conviene considerar la comunicación aumentativa y alternativa (CAA), como pictogramas o dispositivos de voz, sin esperar a que aparezca el habla. Puede empezar por ofrecer formas de pedir lo que quiere. Es una revisión de 17 revisiones sistemáticas sobre CAA en niños y jóvenes autistas de hasta 21 años. Indica beneficios potenciales, pero pocos estudios dieron resultados concluyentes y hacen falta estudios mejor diseñados y con objetivos más amplios. No es una regla para todas las personas; un profesional de la comunicación puede ayudar a elegir el sistema adecuado.
sheet.en: If an autistic person speaks little or not at all, it is worth considering augmentative and alternative communication (AAC), such as picture symbols or speech devices, rather than waiting for speech to appear. A good starting point is offering ways to ask for what they want. This is a review of 17 systematic reviews on AAC for autistic children and young people up to 21 years. It points to potential benefits, but only a few studies gave conclusive results, and better-designed studies with broader goals are needed. It is not a rule for everyone; a communication professional can help choose a suitable system.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person talar lite eller inte alls kan det vara värt att överväga kompletterande och alternativ kommunikation (AKK), som bildstöd eller talande hjälpmedel, i stället för att vänta på att talet kommer. Ett bra första steg är att erbjuda sätt att be om det hen vill ha. Detta är en översikt av 17 systematiska översikter om AKK för autistiska barn och unga upp till 21 år. Den pekar på möjliga fördelar, men bara få studier gav säkra resultat och fler väl utformade studier med bredare mål behövs. Det är ingen regel för alla; en kommunikationsexpert kan hjälpa till att välja rätt system.

title: Environmental Enrichment Therapy for Autism: Outcomes with Increased Access.
authors: Aronoff E, Hillyer R, Leon M
abstract: We have previously shown in two randomized clinical trials that environmental enrichment is capable of ameliorating symptoms of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), and in the present study, we determined whether this therapy could be effective under real-world circumstances. 1,002 children were given daily Sensory Enrichment Therapy, by their parents, using personalized therapy instructions given over the Internet. Parents were asked to assess the symptoms of their child every 2 weeks for up to 7 months. An intention-to-treat analysis showed significant overall gains for a wide range of symptoms in these children, including learning, memory, anxiety, attention span, motor skills, eating, sleeping, sensory processing, self-awareness, communication, social skills, and mood/autism behaviors. The children of compliant caregivers were more likely to experience a significant improvement in their symptoms. The treatment was effective across a wide age range and there was equal progress reported for males and females, for USA and international subjects, for those who paid and those who did not pay for the therapy, and for individuals at all levels of initial symptom severity. Environmental enrichment, delivered via an online system, therefore appears to be an effective, low-cost means of treating the symptoms of ASD.

sheet.es: Si le interesa probar actividades sensoriales diarias en casa, puede hacerlo con calma, observando cómo responde la persona autista y respetando sus señales. Este estudio fue un ensayo con 1,002 niños; sus padres aplicaron a diario una terapia de enriquecimiento sensorial con instrucciones personalizadas por Internet y valoraron los síntomas cada 2 semanas durante un máximo de 7 meses. Los padres informaron mejoras en varias áreas, sobre todo cuando seguían la terapia con constancia. Límites: los resultados los valoraron las propias familias, no hubo grupo de comparación en este estudio, y no sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you are curious about daily sensory activities at home, you can try them calmly, watching how the autistic person responds and respecting their signals. This was a trial with 1,002 children; parents gave Sensory Enrichment Therapy daily, using personalized instructions given over the Internet, and rated symptoms every 2 weeks for up to 7 months. Parents reported gains in many areas, especially when they followed the therapy consistently. Limits: the families themselves rated the results, this study had no comparison group, and it is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du är nyfiken på dagliga sensoriska aktiviteter hemma kan du prova dem lugnt, följa hur den autistiska personen reagerar och respektera hens signaler. Studien var en prövning med 1,002 barn; föräldrar gav daglig sensorisk berikningsterapi med personliga instruktioner över internet och skattade symtomen var 2:a vecka i upp till 7 månader. Föräldrarna rapporterade framsteg på många områden, särskilt när de följde terapin regelbundet. Begränsningar: familjerna bedömde resultaten själva, studien hade ingen jämförelsegrupp och gäller inte som regel för alla människor.

title: Randomised controlled trial of an iPad based early intervention for autism: TOBY playpad study protocol.
authors: Granich J, Dass A, Busacca M, Moore D, Anderson A, Venkatesh S, Duong T, Vellanki P, Richdale A, Trembath D, Cairns D, Marshall W, Rodwell T, Rayner M, Whitehouse AJ
abstract: Background Evidence for early intensive behavioural interventions (EIBI) by therapists as an effective treatment for children with an Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is growing. High-intensity and sustained delivery of quality EIBI is expensive. The TOBY (Therapy Outcomes by You) Playpad is an App-based platform delivering EIBI to facilitate learning for young children with ASD, while enabling parents to become co-therapists. Intervention targets include increasing joint attention, imitation and communication of children with ASD. The primary aim of the study presented in this protocol is to determine the effectiveness of the TOBY App in reducing ASD symptoms when used as a complement to conventional EIBI. The secondary aim is to examine parental attributes as a result of TOBY App use. Methods and design Children aged less than 4;3 years diagnosed with ASD and parents will be recruited into this single-blind, randomised controlled trial using a pragmatic approach. Eligible participants will be randomised to the treatment group 'TOBY therapy + therapy as usual' or, the control group 'therapy as usual' for six months. The treatment will be provided by the TOBY App and parent where a combination of learning environments such as on-iPad child only (solo), partner (with parent) and off-iPad - Natural Environment (with parent) Tasks will be implemented. Parents in the treatment group will participate in a TOBY training workshop. Treatment fidelity will be monitored via an App-based reporting system and parent diaries. The primary outcome measure is the Autism Treatment Evaluation Checklist. The secondary outcome measures involve diagnostics, functional and developmental assessments, including parent questionnaires at baseline (T0), three months (T1) and six months (T2). Discussion This trial will determine the effectiveness of the TOBY App as a therapeutic complement to other early interventions children with ASD receive. The trial will also determine the feasibility of a parent delivered early intervention using the iPad as an educational platform, and assess the impact of the TOBY App on parents' self-efficacy and empowerment in an effort to reduce children's ASD symptoms. The outcomes of this trial may have EIBI services implications for newly diagnosed children with ASD and parents. Trial registration ACTRN12614000738628 retrospectively registered on 1 st of July, 2014. UTN: U1111-1158-6423.

sheet.es: Si su hijo recibe terapia temprana, esta app podría ser algo que comentar con su equipo, pero aún no sabemos si funciona. Este artículo es un protocolo de un ensayo aleatorizado: describe cómo se evaluará la app TOBY en iPad como complemento de la terapia habitual durante seis meses, con niños autistas de menos de 4;3 años y sus madres o padres, que actuarían como coterapeutas. Sus límites: no presenta resultados, así que no demuestra beneficios, y el objetivo es reducir síntomas, un enfoque que no todas las personas autistas comparten. Cada niño es distinto.
sheet.en: If your child is in early therapy, this app may be something to discuss with their team, but we do not yet know whether it works. This paper is a randomised trial protocol: it describes how the TOBY iPad app will be tested as an addition to usual therapy over six months, with autistic children aged under 4;3 years and their parents, who would act as co-therapists. Its limits: it reports no results, so it shows no benefit, and its aim of reducing symptoms is not a goal every autistic person shares. Every child is different.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn får tidiga insatser kan du ta upp den här appen med teamet, men vi vet ännu inte om den fungerar. Artikeln är ett protokoll för en randomiserad studie: den beskriver hur iPad-appen TOBY ska prövas som komplement till vanlig terapi under sex månader, med autistiska barn under 4;3 år och deras föräldrar, som blir medterapeuter. Begränsningar: inga resultat redovisas, så ingen nytta är visad, och målet att minska symtom delas inte av alla autistiska personer. Varje barn är olika.

title: First evidence of the feasibility of gaze-contingent attention training for school children with autism.
authors: Powell G, Wass SV, Erichsen JT, Leekam SR
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: A number of authors have suggested that attention control may be a suitable target for cognitive training in children with autism spectrum disorder. This study provided the first evidence of the feasibility of such training using a battery of tasks intended to target visual attentional control in children with autism spectrum disorder within school-based settings. Twenty-seven children were recruited and randomly assigned to either training or an active control group. Of these, 19 completed the initial assessment, and 17 (9 trained and 8 control) completed all subsequent training sessions. Training of 120 min was administered per participant, spread over six sessions (on average). Compliance with the training tasks was generally high, and evidence of within-task training improvements was found. A number of untrained tasks to assess transfer of training effects were administered pre- and post-training. Changes in the trained group were assessed relative to an active control group. Following training, significant and selective changes in visual sustained attention were observed. Trend training effects were also noted on disengaging visual attention, but no convincing evidence of transfer was found to non-trained assessments of saccadic reaction time and anticipatory looking. Directions for future development and refinement of these new training techniques are discussed.

sheet.es: Si le interesa un entrenamiento de la atención visual, este estudio sugiere que puede hacerse en el colegio y que muchos niños autistas lo siguen bien. Conviene probarlo con calma, observando cómo responde cada niño. Fue un ensayo con asignación al azar: 27 niños autistas fueron asignados a entrenamiento o a un grupo de control activo, y 17 completaron todas las sesiones. Hubo cambios en la atención visual sostenida, pero no se vio una mejora clara en otras tareas no entrenadas. Es un estudio pequeño y preliminar, y no demuestra beneficios en la vida diaria ni sirve para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you are curious about visual attention training, this study suggests it can be run in school and that many autistic children stick with it. It is worth trying gently, watching how each child responds. It was a randomised trial: 27 autistic children were assigned to training or an active control group, and 17 completed all sessions. Changes appeared in sustained visual attention, but there was no convincing improvement on other untrained tasks. The study was small and early, so it does not show everyday benefits and cannot be applied to every person.
sheet.sv: Om du är nyfiken på träning av visuell uppmärksamhet visar den här studien att den kan genomföras i skolan och att många autistiska barn klarar den bra. Det kan vara värt att pröva lugnt och se hur varje barn reagerar. Det var en randomiserad studie: 27 autistiska barn fick antingen träning eller en aktiv kontrollgrupp, och 17 genomförde alla tillfällen. Förändringar sågs i bibehållen visuell uppmärksamhet, men inga övertygande förbättringar i andra otränade uppgifter. Studien var liten och tidig, visar inga effekter i vardagen och gäller inte alla.

title: A Group-Administered social Skills Training for 8- to 12- Year-Old, high-Functioning Children With Autism Spectrum Disorders: An Evaluation of its Effectiveness in a Naturalistic Outpatient Treatment Setting.
authors: Deckers A, Muris P, Roelofs J, Arntz A
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: A social skills training (SST) for high-functioning children with autism spectrum disorders (ASD) was evaluated in an outpatient setting using a combined between- and within-subject design in which SST and a waiting list condition were compared. According to parents and teachers, the SST produced greater improvement of social skills than the waiting list, and these effects were maintained at 3 months follow-up. No between-group effects were found for loneliness, although in general scores on this outcome measure decreased from pre- to follow-up. The effects of SST were unaffected by social anxiety, ADHD symptoms, Theory of Mind, or desire for social interaction. Altogether, SST seems an effective intervention for high-functioning children with ASD that can be applied in daily clinical practice.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija autista de 8 a 12 años quiere practicar habilidades sociales, un grupo de entrenamiento puede ser una opción que merezca explorar con su equipo profesional, respetando sus intereses y su ritmo. Evidencia: un ensayo en un centro ambulatorio comparó el entrenamiento en grupo con una lista de espera. Según padres y docentes, las habilidades sociales mejoraron más con el entrenamiento, y la mejora se mantuvo a los 3 meses. No hubo diferencias entre grupos en soledad. Límites: los resultados provienen de informes de adultos, no de la propia voz de los niños, y el estudio habla de niños descritos como de alto funcionamiento, así que no sirve como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If your autistic child aged 8 to 12 wants to practise social skills, a group training may be worth exploring with your care team, while respecting their interests and pace. Evidence: a trial in an outpatient setting compared group training with a waiting list. According to parents and teachers, social skills improved more with the training, and this was maintained at 3 months. There was no difference between groups in loneliness. Limits: results rest on adult reports rather than the children's own voices, and the study involved children described as high-functioning, so it is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn i åldern 8 till 12 år vill öva sociala färdigheter kan en gruppträning vara värd att undersöka tillsammans med vårdteamet, med respekt för barnets intressen och tempo. Evidens: en studie i öppenvård jämförde gruppträning med väntelista. Enligt föräldrar och lärare förbättrades de sociala färdigheterna mer med träningen, och effekten höll i sig efter 3 månader. Ingen skillnad mellan grupperna ssågs för ensamhet. Begränsningar: resultaten bygger på vuxnas skattningar, inte på barnens egna röster, och studien gällde barn beskrivna som högfungerande, så den är ingen regel för alla.

title: Autism Spectrum Disorder Updates - Relevant Information for Early Interventionists to Consider.
authors: Allen-Meares P, MacDonald M, McGee K
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a pervasive developmental disorder characterized by deficits in social communication skills as well as repetitive, restricted or stereotyped behaviors (1). Early interventionists are often found at the forefront of assessment, evaluation, and early intervention services for children with ASD. The role of an early intervention specialist may include assessing developmental history, providing group and individual counseling, working in partnership with families on home, school, and community environments, mobilizing school and community resources, and assisting in the development of positive early intervention strategies (2, 3). The commonality among these roles resides in the importance of providing up-to-date, relevant information to families and children. The purpose of this review is to provide pertinent up-to-date knowledge for early interventionists to help inform practice in working with individuals with ASD, including common behavioral models of intervention.

sheet.es: Si trabaja con un profesional de atención temprana, pregúntele qué enfoques usa, por qué los eligió y cómo incluyen a su familia y a la persona autista. Esta revisión, publicada en 2016, reúne información actualizada para quienes trabajan en atención temprana, incluidos modelos de intervención conductual habituales. Es una revisión, no un estudio con participantes, y el resumen no ofrece resultados concretos. Tampoco indica qué enfoque conviene a cada niño o niña, así que sirve como punto de partida para conversar, no como regla.
sheet.en: If you work with an early intervention professional, ask which approaches they use, why they chose them, and how they involve your family and the autistic person. This 2016 review gathers up-to-date information for early interventionists, including common behavioural models of intervention. It is a review, not a study with participants, and the abstract gives no specific results. It also does not say which approach suits which child, so use it as a starting point for conversation, not as a rule.
sheet.sv: Om ni arbetar med en professionell inom tidiga insatser kan ni fråga vilka metoder hen använder, varför de valts och hur familjen och den autistiska personen involveras. Den här översikten från 2016 samlar aktuell kunskap för personal inom tidiga insatser, inklusive vanliga beteendebaserade interventionsmodeller. Det är en översikt, inte en studie med deltagare, och sammanfattningen redovisar inga konkreta resultat. Den säger inte heller vilken metod som passar vilket barn, så använd den som underlag för samtal, inte som regel.

title: Audience effects: what can they tell us about social neuroscience, theory of mind and autism?
authors: Hamilton AFC, Lind F
abstract: An audience effect arises when a person's behaviour changes because they believe someone else is watching them. Though these effects have been known about for over 110 years, the cognitive mechanisms of the audience effect and how it might vary across different populations and cultures remains unclear. In this review, we examine the hypothesis that the audience effect draws on implicit mentalising abilities. Behavioural and neuroimaging data from a number of tasks are consistent with this hypothesis. We further review data suggest that how people respond to audiences may vary over development, personality factors, cultural background and clinical diagnosis including autism and anxiety disorder. Overall, understanding and exploring the audience effect may contribute to our models of social interaction, including reputation management and mentalising.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista actúa distinto cuando se siente observada, puede ser una reacción social habitual y no un problema. Conviene fijarse en cuándo, con quién y en qué contexto ocurre, y ofrecer espacios con menos miradas si ayudan. Es una revisión de estudios previos sobre el efecto de la audiencia: cambiar la conducta al creer que alguien nos mira. Indica que la respuesta puede variar según el desarrollo, la personalidad, la cultura y el diagnóstico, incluido el autismo. Sus límites: es una revisión teórica, no da consejos directos y no vale como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If an autistic person acts differently when they feel watched, it may be a common social response rather than a problem. Notice when, with whom and in what setting it happens, and offer spaces with fewer watching eyes if that helps. This is a review of earlier studies on the audience effect: changing behaviour when we believe someone is watching. It suggests responses can vary with development, personality, culture and diagnosis, including autism. Its limits: it is a theoretical review, gives no direct advice, and cannot be treated as a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person agerar annorlunda när hen känner sig betraktad kan det vara en vanlig social reaktion och inte ett problem. Lägg märke till när, med vem och i vilken miljö det sker, och erbjud gärna platser med färre blickar om det hjälper. Detta är en översikt av tidigare studier om publikeffekten: att ändra beteende när vi tror att någon tittar. Den antyder att reaktionen kan variera med utveckling, personlighet, kultur och diagnos, även autism. Begränsningar: det är en teoretisk översikt, ger inga direkta råd och gäller inte som regel för varje person.

title: Synaptopathies: synaptic dysfunction in neurological disorders - A review from students to students.
authors: Lepeta K, Lourenco MV, Schweitzer BC, Martino Adami PV, Banerjee P, Catuara-Solarz S, de La Fuente Revenga M, Guillem AM, Haidar M, Ijomone OM, Nadorp B, Qi L, Perera ND, Refsgaard LK, Reid KM, Sabbar
abstract: Synapses are essential components of neurons and allow information to travel coordinately throughout the nervous system to adjust behavior to environmental stimuli and to control body functions, memories, and emotions. Thus, optimal synaptic communication is required for proper brain physiology, and slight perturbations of synapse function can lead to brain disorders. In fact, increasing evidence has demonstrated the relevance of synapse dysfunction as a major determinant of many neurological diseases. This notion has led to the concept of synaptopathies as brain diseases with synapse defects as shared pathogenic features. In this review, which was initiated at the 13th International Society for Neurochemistry Advanced School, we discuss basic concepts of synapse structure and function, and provide a critical view of how aberrant synapse physiology may contribute to neurodevelopmental disorders (autism, Down syndrome, startle disease, and epilepsy) as well as neurodegenerative disorders (Alzheimer and Parkinson disease). We finally discuss the appropriateness and potential implications of gathering synapse diseases under a single term. Understanding common causes and intrinsic differences in disease-associated synaptic dysfunction could offer novel clues toward synapse-based therapeutic intervention for neurological and neuropsychiatric disorders. In this Review, which was initiated at the 13th International Society for Neurochemistry (ISN) Advanced School, we discuss basic concepts of synapse structure and function, and provide a critical view of how aberrant synapse physiology may contribute to neurodevelopmental (autism, Down syndrome, startle disease, and epilepsy) as well as neurodegenerative disorders (Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases), gathered together under the term of synaptopathies. Read the Editorial Highlight for this article on page 783.

sheet.es: Qué significa para mañana: este estudio no ofrece nada que cambie la rutina diaria. Es una base para comprender mejor cómo se comunican las neuronas, no una guía de actuación. Si tiene dudas sobre una persona concreta, hable con su equipo de profesionales. Evidencia: es una revisión de la bibliografía, no un experimento con participantes; comenta cómo los fallos en las sinapsis podrían contribuir a varias condiciones del neurodesarrollo, entre ellas el autismo, y a enfermedades neurodegenerativas. Límites: no estudia a personas autistas concretas, no prueba ninguna ayuda y no demuestra que las sinapsis expliquen el autismo de todas las personas. Agrupar condiciones bajo un solo término es también objeto de debate.
sheet.en: What this means tomorrow: this study offers nothing that changes daily routines. It is background for understanding how neurons communicate, not a guide for action. If you have questions about a particular person, talk with their professional team. Evidence: it is a review of the literature, not an experiment with participants; it discusses how problems at synapses might contribute to several neurodevelopmental conditions, including autism, and to neurodegenerative diseases. Limits: it does not study specific autistic people, test any support, or show that synapses explain autism for everyone. Grouping different conditions under one term is also debated.
sheet.sv: Vad det betyder i morgon: studien ger inget som ändrar den dagliga rutinen. Den är bakgrund för att förstå hur nervceller kommunicerar, inte en vägledning för handling. Har du frågor om en enskild person, prata med personens professionella team. Evidens: det är en översikt av litteraturen, inte ett experiment med deltagare; den diskuterar hur problem i synapser kan bidra till flera neuroutvecklingsrelaterade tillstånd, bland annat autism, och till neurodegenerativa sjukdomar. Begränsningar: den studerar inga enskilda autistiska personer, prövar inget stöd och visar inte att synapser förklarar autism hos alla. Att samla olika tillstånd under en term är också omdiskuterat.

title: A Systematic Review of Research on Autism Spectrum Disorders in Sub-Saharan Africa.
authors: Abubakar A, Ssewanyana D, Newton CR
abstract: The burden of autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) is not well known. We carried out a systematic review of the literature to identify published work from SSA. We have systematically searched four databases, namely, Medline, PsycINFO, CINAHL, and Child Development & Adolescent Studies, through EBSCO and identified studies from across SSA. Based on predefined inclusion criteria, 47 studies were included in this review. Most of the identified studies (74%) were conducted in only 2 African countries, that is, South Africa and Nigeria. Additionally, most of these studies (83%) were carried out in the last decade. These studies had four major themes: development of measurement tools of ASD in Africa, examining the prevalence of ASD, identifying risk factors and risk markers, and examining psychosocial issues. We identified only a single population level study aimed at documenting the prevalence of ASD and could not identify a single case-control study aimed at examining a comprehensive set of potential risk factors. All intervention studies were based on very small sample sizes. Put together, our findings suggest that current evidence base is too scanty to provide the required information to plan adequately for effective intervention strategies for children with ASD in Africa.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista en África subsahariana, o vienes de allí, es normal sentir que la información disponible no refleja tu realidad. Puedes confiar en lo que observas a diario, anotar qué ayuda a tu familiar y buscar redes locales de familias y personas autistas. Esta revisión sistemática analizó 47 estudios publicados sobre autismo en la región; la mayoría se hicieron en Sudáfrica y Nigeria, y se centraron en herramientas de evaluación, prevalencia, factores de riesgo y aspectos sociales. Su límite principal es que la evidencia es escasa: solo hubo un estudio poblacional y los estudios de apoyo tenían muy pocos participantes, así que no ofrece pautas válidas para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person in sub-Saharan Africa, or your family comes from there, it is understandable to feel that available information does not reflect your reality. You can trust what you observe day to day, note what helps your family member, and look for local networks of families and autistic people. This systematic review examined 47 published studies on autism in the region; most came from South Africa and Nigeria and focused on assessment tools, prevalence, risk factors and social issues. Its main limit is how thin the evidence is: there was only one population study and support studies had very few participants, so it offers no rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person i Afrika söder om Sahara, eller om din familj kommer därifrån, är det begripligt att känna att tillgänglig information inte speglar er verklighet. Du kan lita på det du ser i vardagen, anteckna vad som hjälper din närstående och söka lokala nätverk av familjer och autistiska personer. Denna systematiska översikt granskade 47 publicerade studier om autism i regionen; de flesta kom från Sydafrika och Nigeria och handlade om bedömningsverktyg, förekomst, riskfaktorer och sociala frågor. Den största begränsningen är att underlaget är tunt: bara en befolkningsstudie fanns och stödstudierna hade mycket få deltagare, så den ger ingen regel för alla.

title: The role of sex-differential biology in risk for autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Werling DM
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a developmental condition that affects approximately four times as many males as females, a strong sex bias that has not yet been fully explained. Understanding the causes of this biased prevalence may highlight novel avenues for treatment development that could benefit patients with diverse genetic backgrounds, and the expertise of sex differences researchers will be invaluable in this endeavor. In this review, I aim to assess current evidence pertaining to the sex difference in ASD prevalence and to identify outstanding questions and remaining gaps in our understanding of how males come to be more frequently affected and/or diagnosed with ASD. Though males consistently outnumber females in ASD prevalence studies, prevalence estimates generated using different approaches report male/female ratios of variable magnitude that suggest that ascertainment or diagnostic biases may contribute to the male skew in ASD. Here, I present the different methods applied and implications of their findings. Additionally, even as prevalence estimations challenge the degree of male bias in ASD, support is growing for the long-proposed female protective effect model of ASD risk, and I review the relevant results from recurrence rate, quantitative trait, and genetic analyses. Lastly, I describe work investigating several sex-differential biological factors and pathways that may be responsible for females' protection and/or males' increased risk predicted by the female protective effect model, including sex steroid hormone exposure and regulation and sex-differential activity of certain neural cell types. However, much future work from both the ASD and sex differences research communities will be required to flesh out our understanding of how these factors act to influence the developing brain and modulate ASD risk.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una niña o mujer y notas rasgos autistas, vale la pena pedir una evaluación aunque no encaje en la imagen típica: el autismo en chicas puede pasar desapercibido. Anota ejemplos concretos de su día a día (sensorialidad, cansancio social, intereses intensos) y llévalos a la consulta. Esta es una revisión narrativa de estudios sobre por qué se diagnostica autismo más en varones; sugiere que influyen tanto sesgos diagnósticos como factores biológicos, como hormonas y genética. Sus límites: no aporta datos nuevos, muchas hipótesis biológicas siguen sin confirmar y no sirve para predecir nada sobre una persona concreta.
sheet.en: If you support a girl or woman and notice autistic traits, it is worth asking for an assessment even if she does not fit the typical picture: autism in girls can be overlooked. Write down concrete everyday examples (sensory experiences, social exhaustion, intense interests) and bring them to appointments. This is a narrative review of research on why autism is diagnosed more often in males; it suggests both diagnostic bias and biological factors, such as hormones and genetics, play a part. Its limits: it adds no new data, many biological ideas remain unconfirmed, and it cannot predict anything about one individual.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en flicka eller kvinna och ser autistiska drag kan det vara värt att be om en utredning även om hon inte passar den typiska bilden: autism hos flickor kan förbises. Skriv ner konkreta vardagsexempel (sinnesintryck, social utmattning, starka intressen) och ta med dem till besöket. Detta är en narrativ översikt av forskning om varför autism oftare diagnostiseras hos pojkar och män; den pekar på både diagnostiska skevheter och biologiska faktorer, som hormoner och genetik. Begränsningar: den tillför inga nya data, många biologiska hypoteser är obekräftade och den kan inte förutsäga något om en enskild person.

title: Study protocol: implementation of a computer-assisted intervention for autism in schools: a hybrid type II cluster randomized effectiveness-implementation trial.
authors: Pellecchia M, Beidas RS, Marcus SC, Fishman J, Kimberly JR, Cannuscio CC, Reisinger EM, Rump K, Mandell DS
abstract: Background The number of children diagnosed with autism has rapidly outpaced the capacities of many public school systems to serve them, especially under-resourced, urban school districts. The intensive nature of evidence-based autism interventions, which rely heavily on one-to-one delivery, has caused schools to turn to computer-assisted interventions (CAI). There is little evidence regarding the feasibility, effectiveness, and implementation of CAI in public schools. While CAI has the potential to increase instructional time for students with autism, it may also result in unintended consequences such as reduction in the amount of interpersonal (as opposed to computerized) instruction students receive. The purpose of this study is to test the effectiveness of one such CAI-TeachTown-its implementation, and its effects on teachers' use of other evidence-based practices. Methods This study protocol describes a type II hybrid cluster randomized effectiveness-implementation trial. We will train and coach 70 teachers in autism support classrooms in one large school district in the use of evidence-based practices for students with autism. Half of the teachers then will be randomly selected to receive training and access to TeachTown: Basics, a CAI for students with autism, for the students in their classrooms. The study examines: (1) the effectiveness of TeachTown for students with autism; (2) the extent to which teachers implement TeachTown the way it was designed (i.e., fidelity); and (3) whether its uptake increases or reduces the use of other evidence-based practices. Discussion This study will examine the implementation of new technology for children with ASD in public schools and will be the first to measure the effectiveness of CAI. As importantly, the study will investigate whether adding a new technology on top of existing practices increases or decreases their use. This study presents a unique method to studying both the implementation and exnovation of evidence-based practices for children with autism in school settings. Trial registration NCT02695693 . Retrospectively registered on July 8, 2016.

sheet.es: Si el colegio incorpora un programa informático para el alumnado autista, conviene preguntar si sigue habiendo tiempo de enseñanza cara a cara y si se mantienen otras prácticas que ya funcionan. Este es un protocolo de ensayo: describe un estudio planificado con 70 docentes de aulas de apoyo al autismo, la mitad elegida al azar para usar TeachTown: Basics. No presenta resultados todavía, así que no sabemos si ayuda. Además, se hará en un solo distrito escolar y no demuestra lo que le irá bien a cada niño o niña autista.
sheet.en: If your school adds a computer program for autistic students, it is worth asking whether face-to-face teaching time continues and whether other practices that already work are kept. This is a trial protocol: it describes a planned study with 70 teachers in autism support classrooms, half chosen at random to use TeachTown: Basics. It reports no results yet, so we do not know whether it helps. It will also take place in one school district and cannot show what will suit each autistic child.
sheet.sv: Om skolan inför ett datorprogram för autistiska elever kan du fråga om undervisningen ansikte mot ansikte finns kvar och om andra fungerande arbetssätt behålls. Detta är ett studieprotokoll: det beskriver en planerad studie med 70 lärare i autismklassrum, där hälften slumpas att använda TeachTown: Basics. Inga resultat redovisas ännu, så vi vet inte om programmet hjälper. Studien görs dessutom i ett skoldistrikt och visar inte vad som passar varje autistiskt barn.

title: The neuroanatomy of autism - a developmental perspective.
authors: Donovan AP, Basson MA
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASDs) are a heterogeneous group of neurodevelopmental disorders that are diagnosed solely on the basis of behaviour. A large body of work has reported neuroanatomical differences between individuals with ASD and neurotypical controls. Despite the huge clinical and genetic heterogeneity that typifies autism, some of these anatomical features appear to be either present in most cases or so dramatically altered in some that their presence is now reasonably well replicated in a number of studies. One such finding is the tendency towards overgrowth of the frontal cortex during the early postnatal period. Although these reports have been focused primarily on the presumed pathological anatomy, they are providing us with important insights into normal brain anatomy and are stimulating new ideas and hypotheses about the normal trajectory of brain development and the function of specific anatomical brain structures. The use of model systems that include genetic model organisms such as the mouse and, more recently, human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived brain organoids to model normal and pathological human cortical development, is proving particularly informative. Here we review some of the neuroanatomical alterations reported in autism, with a particular focus on well-validated findings and recent advances in the field, and ask what these observations can tell us about normal and abnormal brain development.

sheet.es: Para mañana por la mañana: esta revisión no ofrece ninguna pauta práctica concreta, pero recuerda que las personas autistas son muy distintas entre sí y que ninguna diferencia cerebral dice cómo es una persona concreta ni qué necesita. Observe a la persona que cuida y siga sus propias señales y preferencias. Es una revisión de estudios previos sobre la anatomía cerebral en el autismo, incluidos modelos animales y organoides cerebrales. Entre los hallazgos citados está la tendencia al sobrecrecimiento de la corteza frontal en la etapa postnatal temprana. Sus límites: describe grupos, no individuos, y no sirve para diagnosticar ni para decidir apoyos.
sheet.en: For tomorrow morning: this review offers no specific practical routine, but it is a reminder that autistic people differ widely, and that no brain difference tells you what a particular person is like or needs. Keep watching the person you support and follow their own signals and preferences. It is a review of earlier research on brain anatomy in autism, including animal models and brain organoids. One finding it discusses is a tendency towards overgrowth of the frontal cortex in the early postnatal period. Its limits: it describes groups, not individuals, and it cannot be used to diagnose or to decide on supports.
sheet.sv: Till imorgon bitti: den här översikten ger ingen konkret rutin, men den påminner om att autistiska personer skiljer sig mycket åt, och att ingen skillnad i hjärnan säger hur en enskild person är eller vad hen behöver. Fortsätt att lägga märke till personen du stöttar och följ hens egna signaler och önskemål. Det är en översikt av tidigare forskning om hjärnans anatomi vid autism, inklusive djurmodeller och hjärnorganoider. En av de omtalade iakttagelserna är en tendens till överväxt av frontalbarken under den tidiga postnatala perioden. Begränsningar: den beskriver grupper, inte individer, och kan inte användas för diagnos eller för att välja stöd.

title: Pediatric Traumatic Brain Injury and Autism: Elucidating Shared Mechanisms.
authors: Singh R, Turner RC, Nguyen L, Motwani K, Swatek M, Lucke-Wold BP
abstract: Pediatric traumatic brain injury (TBI) and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) are two serious conditions that affect youth. Recent data, both preclinical and clinical, show that pediatric TBI and ASD share not only similar symptoms but also some of the same biologic mechanisms that cause these symptoms. Prominent symptoms for both disorders include gastrointestinal problems, learning difficulties, seizures, and sensory processing disruption. In this review, we highlight some of these shared mechanisms in order to discuss potential treatment options that might be applied for each condition. We discuss potential therapeutic and pharmacologic options as well as potential novel drug targets. Furthermore, we highlight advances in understanding of brain circuitry that is being propelled by improved imaging modalities. Going forward, advanced imaging will help in diagnosis and treatment planning strategies for pediatric patients. Lessons from each field can be applied to design better and more rigorous trials that can be used to improve guidelines for pediatric patients suffering from TBI or ASD.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista tiene problemas digestivos, dificultades de aprendizaje, convulsiones o diferencias en el procesamiento sensorial, conviene observarlos y comentarlos con su equipo sanitario, que sabrá valorarlos en cada caso. Esta es una revisión de la literatura que compara la lesión cerebral traumática pediátrica y el autismo; señala síntomas y mecanismos biológicos que podrían compartirse. Se habla de opciones de tratamiento, pero las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico. Es una revisión, no un ensayo con personas concretas, y no demuestra que ambas condiciones funcionen igual en cada niño o niña. Úsela como contexto, no como regla.
sheet.en: If an autistic person has digestive problems, learning difficulties, seizures or differences in sensory processing, it is worth noticing them and raising them with their health team, who can assess each person individually. This is a review of the literature comparing pediatric traumatic brain injury and autism; it points to symptoms and biological mechanisms that may be shared. It mentions treatment options, but medical decisions belong to a clinician. It is a review, not a trial with specific participants, and it does not show that the two conditions work the same way in every child. Use it as background, not as a rule.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person har magproblem, inlärningssvårigheter, krampanfall eller skillnader i sensorisk bearbetning är det värt att uppmärksamma detta och ta upp det med vårdteamet, som kan bedöma varje person individuellt. Detta är en översikt av litteraturen som jämför traumatisk hjärnskada hos barn och autism; den pekar på symtom och biologiska mekanismer som kan vara gemensamma. Behandlingsalternativ nämns, men medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker. Det är en översikt, inte en studie med särskilda deltagare, och den visar inte att tillstånden fungerar likadant hos varje barn. Använd den som bakgrund, inte som regel.

title: Resting-State Functional Connectivity in Autism Spectrum Disorders: A Review.
authors: Hull JV, Dokovna LB, Jacokes ZJ, Torgerson CM, Irimia A, Van Horn JD
abstract: Ongoing debate exists within the resting-state functional MRI (fMRI) literature over how intrinsic connectivity is altered in the autistic brain, with reports of general over-connectivity, under-connectivity, and/or a combination of both. Classifying autism using brain connectivity is complicated by the heterogeneous nature of the condition, allowing for the possibility of widely variable connectivity patterns among individuals with the disorder. Further differences in reported results may be attributable to the age and sex of participants included, designs of the resting-state scan, and to the analysis technique used to evaluate the data. This review systematically examines the resting-state fMRI autism literature to date and compares studies in an attempt to draw overall conclusions that are presently challenging. We also propose future direction for rs-fMRI use to categorize individuals with autism spectrum disorder, serve as a possible diagnostic tool, and best utilize data-sharing initiatives.
