sheet.es: Esta revisión no ofrece nada que cambie la rutina de mañana: no sirve para decidir apoyos ni para valorar a una persona concreta. Lo útil es saber que los estudios de conectividad cerebral en reposo no coinciden: unos hallan más conexión, otros menos y otros ambas, y las personas autistas son muy diferentes entre sí. Es una revisión de la literatura de resonancia magnética funcional en reposo. Como límites, los resultados varían según la edad, el sexo, el diseño del escáner y el método de análisis, y por ahora es difícil sacar conclusiones generales. Confíe más en lo que observa y en lo que la propia persona le dice.
sheet.en: This review offers nothing that changes tomorrow's routine: it can't guide supports or assess any one person. What is useful is knowing that resting-state brain connectivity studies disagree: some find more connection, some less, some both, and autistic people differ widely from one another. It is a review of the resting-state functional MRI literature. Its limits: results vary with age, sex, scan design and analysis method, and general conclusions are currently hard to draw. Trust what you observe and what the person themselves tells you.
sheet.sv: Den här översikten ger inget som ändrar morgondagens rutiner: den kan inte styra stöd eller bedöma en enskild person. Det användbara är att veta att studier av hjärnans vilokonnektivitet spriker: vissa ser mer koppling, andra mindre, andra båda, och autistiska personer skiljer sig mycket åt. Det är en översikt av litteraturen om funktionell magnetkamera i vila. Begränsningar: resultaten varierar med ålder, kön, skanningens upplägg och analysmetod, och generella slutsatser är för tillfället svåra att dra. Lita mer på det du själv ser och på det personen berättar.

title: Autism Spectrum Disorder Screening Instruments for Very Young Children: A Systematic Review.
authors: Towle PO, Patrick PA
abstract: Research on ASD in infancy has provided a rationale for developing screening instruments for children from the first year of life to age of 18 months. A comprehensive literature search identified candidate screening tools. Using methodological probe questions adapted from the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies (QUADAS), two Level 1 and three Level 2 screening instruments were reviewed in detail. Research evidence conclusions were that instrument development was in beginning phases, is not yet strong, and requires further development. Clinical recommendations were to continue vigilant developmental and autism surveillance from the first year on but to use the screening instruments per se only for high-risk children rather than for population screening, with considerations regarding feasibility for individual settings, informing caregivers about strengths and weaknesses of the tool, and monitoring new research.

title: Sensory, Emotional and Cognitive Contributions to Anxiety in Autism Spectrum Disorders.
authors: South M, Rodgers J
abstract: Severe symptoms of anxiety add substantial additional burden to many individuals diagnosed with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). Improved understanding of specific factors that contribute to anxiety in ASD can aid research regarding the causes of autism and also provide targets for more effective intervention. This mini-review article focuses on emerging evidence for three concepts that appear to be related to each other and which also strongly predict anxiety in ASD samples. Atypical sensory function is included in the diagnostic criteria for ASD and is likely an important contributor to anxiety. Difficulties in understanding and labeling emotions ( alexithymia ), although a co-morbidity, may arise in part from atypical sensory function and can lead to confusion and uncertainty about how to respond to social and emotional situations. Intolerance of uncertainty (IU) describes people who have a particularly hard time with ambiguity and is known to be a key mechanism underlying some anxiety disorders. While evidence for linking these ideas is to date incomplete, we put forward a model including each concept as a framework for future studies. Specifically, we propose that IU is a critical mediator for anxiety in ASD, and explore the relationships between sensory function, alexithymia and IU. We further explore the role of the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) in regulating emotional response, in connection with limbic and insula-based networks, and suggest that disrupted integration in these networks underlies difficulties with habituation to strong emotional stimuli, which results in an enhanced perception of threat in many people with ASD. Behavioral and biologically-based treatments for anxiety in ASD will benefit from attending to these specific mechanisms as adjunct to traditional interventions.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista a tu cargo se muestra ansiosa, puede ayudar fijarse en tres cosas: cómo vive los sonidos, luces o texturas; si le cuesta reconocer o nombrar lo que siente; y cuánto le pesa no saber qué va a pasar. Mañana podrías anticipar los cambios del día con claridad, reducir estímulos molestos y ofrecer palabras o imágenes para expresar emociones, sin presionar. Se trata de una mini-revisión que reúne estudios previos y propone un modelo que conecta sensorialidad, dificultad para identificar emociones (alexitimia) e intolerancia a la incertidumbre con la ansiedad. Es una propuesta teórica: la evidencia aún es incompleta y cada persona es distinta.
sheet.en: If an autistic person you support seems anxious, it may help to look at three things: how they experience sounds, lights or textures; whether naming their feelings is hard; and how much not knowing what comes next weighs on them. Tomorrow you could preview the day's changes clearly, reduce bothersome sensory input, and offer words or pictures for emotions, without pressure. This is a mini-review that gathers earlier research and proposes a model linking sensory experience, difficulty identifying emotions (alexithymia) and intolerance of uncertainty to anxiety. It is a theoretical proposal: the evidence is still incomplete, and every person is different.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person du stöttar verkar orolig kan det hjälpa att titta på tre saker: hur hen upplever ljud, ljus eller texturer; om det är svårt att sätta ord på känslor; och hur tungt det är att inte veta vad som händer härnäst. I morgon kan du tydligt förbereda dagens förändringar, minska störande sinnesintryck och erbjuda ord eller bilder för känslor, utan press. Detta är en kort översikt som samlar tidigare forskning och föreslår en modell som kopplar sinnesupplevelser, svårighet att identifiera känslor (alexitymi) och intolerans mot osäkerhet till ångest. Det är ett teoretiskt förslag: evidensen är ännu ofullständig och varje person är olik.

title: d-Cycloserine enhances durability of social skills training in autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Wink LK, Minshawi NF, Shaffer RC, Plawecki MH, Posey DJ, Horn PS, Adams R, Pedapati EV, Schaefer TL, McDougle CJ, Swiezy NB, Erickson CA
abstract: Background d-Cycloserine (DCS) enhances extinction learning across species, but it has proven challenging to identify consistent benefit of DCS when added to therapeutic interventions. We conducted a placebo-controlled trial of DCS to potentiate social skills training in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) but found substantial improvement in both the DCS and placebo groups at the conclusion of active treatment. Here, we assess the impact of DCS 11 weeks following active treatment to evaluate the impact of DCS on treatment response durability. Methods Study participants included 60 outpatient youth with ASD, ages 5-11 years, all with IQ above 70, and significantly impaired social functioning who completed a 10-week active treatment phase during which they received weekly single doses of 50 mg of DCS or placebo administered 30 min prior to group social skills training. Following the 10-week active treatment phase, blinded follow-up assessments occurred at week 11 and week 22. The primary outcome measure for our durability of treatment evaluation was the parent-rated social responsiveness scale (SRS) total raw score at week 22. Results Analysis of the SRS total raw score demonstrated significant decrease for the DCS group compared to the placebo group ( p = 0.042) indicating greater maintenance of treatment effect in the DCS group. DCS was well tolerated, with irritability being the most frequently reported adverse effect in both groups. Conclusions The findings of this study suggest that DCS may help youth with ASD to maintain skills gained during sort-term social skills training. Larger-scale studies with longer follow-up will be necessary to further understand the long-term impact of DCS paired with structured social skills training. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT01086475.

sheet.es: Esta es una investigación médica: las decisiones sobre medicación corresponden siempre a un profesional clínico. Mañana, lo útil es otra cosa: si su hijo participa en un entrenamiento de habilidades sociales, pregunte al equipo cómo practicar lo aprendido en casa y cómo mantenerlo con el tiempo. Evidencia: ensayo con control de placebo en 60 jóvenes autistas de 5-11 años, con seguimiento hasta la semana 22. Límites: muestra pequeña, el resultado principal fue un cuestionario respondido por familias, y los autores piden estudios más amplios y largos; no sirve como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: This was a medical study, so decisions about medication belong to a clinician. What helps tomorrow is something else: if your child takes part in social skills training, ask the team how to practise what they learn at home and keep it going over time. Evidence: a placebo-controlled trial with 60 autistic youth aged 5-11 years, followed up to week 22. Limits: a small sample, the main outcome was a questionnaire completed by parents, and the authors say larger, longer studies are needed; it is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Det här var en medicinsk studie, så beslut om läkemedel hör till en kliniker. Det som kan hjälpa i morgon är något annat: om ditt barn går i social färdighetsträning, fråga teamet hur ni kan öva det som lärs ut hemma och behålla det över tid. Evidens: en placebokontrollerad studie med 60 autistiska barn och unga i åldern 5-11 år, med uppföljning till vecka 22. Begränsningar: litet urval, huvudmåttet var ett frågeformulär som föräldrar fyllde i, och forskarna efterlyser större och längre studier; det är ingen regel för alla.

title: Specificity, contexts, and reference groups matter when assessing autistic traits.
authors: Gernsbacher MA, Stevenson JL, Dern S
abstract: Many of the personality and behavioral traits (e.g., social imperviousness, directness in conversation, lack of imagination, affinity for solitude, difficulty displaying emotions) that are known to be sensitive to context (with whom?) and reference group (according to whom?) also appear in questionnaire-based assessments of autistic traits. Therefore, two experiments investigated the effects of specifying contexts and reference groups when assessing autistic traits in autistic and non-autistic participants. Experiment 1 (124 autistic and 124 non-autistic participants) demonstrated that context matters when assessing autistic traits (F(1,244) = 267.5, p < .001, η2p = .523). When the context of the Broad Autism Phenotype Questionnaire was specified as the participants' out-group (e.g., "I like being around non-autistic people" or "I like being around autistic people"), both autistic and non-autistic participants self-reported having more autistic traits; when the context was specified as the participants' in-group, participants reported having fewer autistic traits. Experiment 2 (82 autistic and 82 non-autistic participants) demonstrated that reference group matters when assessing autistic traits (F(2,160) = 94.38, p < .001, η2p = .541). When the reference group on the Social Responsiveness Scale was specified as the participants' out-group (e.g., "According to non-autistic people, I have unusual eye contact"), autistic participants reported having more autistic traits; when the reference group was their in-group, autistic participants reported having fewer autistic traits. Non-autistic participants appeared insensitive to reference group on the Social Responsiveness Scale. Exploratory analyses suggested that when neither the context nor the reference group is specified (for assessing autistic traits on the Autism-Spectrum Quotient), both autistic and non-autistic participants use the majority ("non-autistic people") as the implied context and reference group.

sheet.es: Si rellenas o interpretas un cuestionario sobre rasgos autistas, fíjate en con quién y según quién se responde: el resultado puede cambiar. Es un estudio con personas autistas: en el primer experimento participaron 124 autistas y 124 no autistas, y en el segundo 82 autistas y 82 no autistas. Los participantes contestaron cuestionarios; cuando el contexto era su exogrupo, decían tener más rasgos autistas, y con su propio grupo, menos. Sin especificar nada, parecían usar a las personas no autistas como referencia. Es un estudio con cuestionarios, no mide a cada persona, y no sirve para decidir nada sobre un diagnóstico.
sheet.en: If you fill in or interpret a questionnaire about autistic traits, notice with whom and according to whom the answers are given: the result can change. This is a study with autistic people: the first experiment included 124 autistic and 124 non-autistic participants, and the second 82 autistic and 82 non-autistic participants. Participants answered questionnaires; when the context was their out-group they reported more autistic traits, and with their own group, fewer. When nothing was specified, they seemed to use non-autistic people as the reference. It relied on questionnaires, does not describe any one person, and cannot settle questions about a diagnosis.
sheet.sv: Om du fyller i eller tolkar ett frågeformulär om autistiska drag, notera med vem och enligt vem svaren ges: resultatet kan ändras. Det är en studie med autistiska personer: i första experimentet deltog 124 autistiska och 124 icke-autistiska, i det andra 82 autistiska och 82 icke-autistiska. Deltagarna besvarade frågeformulär; när sammanhanget var deras ut-grupp rapporterade de fler autistiska drag, och med den egna gruppen färre. När inget angavs verkade de använda icke-autistiska som referens. Studien bygger på frågeformulär, beskriver inte någon enskild person och kan inte avgöra frågor om diagnos.

title: The Effect of Pivotal Response Treatment in Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders: A Non-randomized Study with a Blinded Outcome Measure.
authors: Duifhuis EA, den Boer JC, Doornbos A, Buitelaar JK, Oosterling IJ, Klip H
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Purpose of this quasi-experimental trial was to investigate the effect of Pivotal response treatment (PRT) versus treatment as usual (TAU) on autism symptoms. Children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), aged 3-8 years, received either PRT (n = 11) or TAU (n = 13). Primary outcome measure was the total score on the Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule at pre- and posttreatment. Additionally, general problem behavior and parental stress levels were measured. Children in the PRT condition improved on the primary outcome measure compared to the TAU group with a small effect size [partial η 2 = 0.22 (95 % CI 0.00-0.46)]. Neither group demonstrated significant changes in the secondary outcomes. This study suggests that PRT may improve autism symptoms in children with ASD over TAU.

sheet.es: Si valoras una intervención para tu hijo o hija, puedes preguntar a los profesionales por el Tratamiento de Respuesta Central (PRT), que trabaja la motivación y la comunicación en situaciones cotidianas. Es un estudio casi experimental, sin asignación al azar, con niños autistas de 3-8 años: 11 recibieron PRT y 13 el tratamiento habitual. Quienes recibieron PRT mejoraron más en una medida de síntomas autistas, con un efecto pequeño. Ningún grupo cambió de forma significativa en problemas de conducta generales ni en estrés parental. El grupo es muy pequeño y no hubo azar, así que no sirve como regla para cada niño o niña.
sheet.en: If you are weighing up support for your child, you could ask professionals about Pivotal Response Treatment (PRT), which works on motivation and communication in everyday situations. This was a quasi-experimental study, without random assignment, with autistic children aged 3-8 years: 11 received PRT and 13 received treatment as usual. Those who received PRT improved more on a measure of autism symptoms, with a small effect. Neither group changed significantly in general problem behavior or parental stress. The groups were very small and not randomised, so the findings are not a rule for every child.
sheet.sv: Om du överväger stöd till ditt barn kan du fråga yrkespersoner om Pivotal Response Treatment (PRT), som tränar motivation och kommunikation i vardagliga situationer. Studien var kvasiexperimentell, utan slumpmässig fördelning, med autistiska barn i åldern 3-8 år: 11 fick PRT och 13 fick sedvanlig behandling. De som fick PRT förbättrades mer på ett mått på autismsymtom, med en liten effekt. Ingen grupp förändrades signifikant i generella beteendeproblem eller föräldrastress. Grupperna var mycket små och inte slumpade, så resultaten gäller inte som regel för varje barn.

title: Metabolic Dysfunction Underlying Autism Spectrum Disorder and Potential Treatment Approaches.
authors: Cheng N, Rho JM, Masino SA
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is characterized by deficits in sociability and communication, and increased repetitive and/or restrictive behaviors. While the etio-pathogenesis of ASD is unknown, clinical manifestations are diverse and many possible genetic and environmental factors have been implicated. As such, it has been a great challenge to identify key neurobiological mechanisms and to develop effective treatments. Current therapies focus on co-morbid conditions (such as epileptic seizures and sleep disturbances) and there is no cure for the core symptoms. Recent studies have increasingly implicated mitochondrial dysfunction in ASD. The fact that mitochondria are an integral part of diverse cellular functions and are susceptible to many insults could explain how a wide range of factors can contribute to a consistent behavioral phenotype in ASD. Meanwhile, the high-fat, low-carbohydrate ketogenic diet (KD), used for nearly a century to treat medically intractable epilepsy, has been shown to enhance mitochondrial function through a multiplicity of mechanisms and affect additional molecular targets that may address symptoms and comorbidities of ASD. Here, we review the evidence for the use of metabolism-based therapies such as the KD in the treatment of ASD as well as emerging co-morbid models of epilepsy and autism. Future research directions aimed at validating such therapeutic approaches and identifying additional and novel mechanistic targets are also discussed.

sheet.es: Esta revisión no ofrece una pauta para aplicar mañana. Si en casa surge el interés por la dieta cetogénica (alta en grasas y baja en carbohidratos) u otros enfoques metabólicos, conviene hablarlo primero con el equipo médico, que decide si tiene sentido en cada caso. Es una revisión de la literatura sobre el posible papel de las mitocondrias en el autismo y sobre terapias basadas en el metabolismo, como esa dieta, usada desde hace casi un siglo en epilepsia resistente. Sus límites: el origen del autismo sigue sin conocerse, la evidencia en autismo es todavía emergente y los autores plantean que hace falta más investigación para validar estos enfoques.
sheet.en: This review does not give a routine to try tomorrow. If you are curious about the ketogenic diet (high-fat, low-carbohydrate) or other metabolism-based approaches, talk with the medical team first; they decide whether it makes sense for a particular person. It is a review of existing literature on the possible role of mitochondria in autism and on metabolism-based therapies, such as that diet, used for nearly a century for epilepsy that does not respond to medicines. Its limits: the origin of autism is still unknown, the evidence in autism is still emerging, and the authors say more research is needed to validate these approaches.
sheet.sv: Den här översikten ger ingen rutin att prova i morgon. Om du är nyfiken på ketogen kost (fettrik och kolhydratsnål) eller andra metabolismbaserade angreppssätt, prata först med vårdteamet, som avgör om det passar just den personen. Det är en litteraturöversikt om mitokondriernas möjliga roll vid autism och om metabolismbaserade behandlingar, som den kosten, som i nästan ett sekel använts vid epilepsi som inte svarar på läkemedel. Begränsningar: orsaken till autism är fortfarande okänd, evidensen för autism är ännu under utveckling, och författarna menar att mer forskning behövs för att validera dessa angreppssätt.

title: Parenting for Autism, Language, And Communication Evaluation Study (PALACES): protocol for a pilot randomised controlled trial.
authors: Williams ME, Hastings R, Charles JM, Evans S, Hutchings J
abstract: Introduction Children with autistic spectrum disorder (ASD) often have associated behavioural difficulties that can present a challenge for parents and parenting. There are several effective social learning theory-based parenting programmes for dealing with behavioural difficulties, including the Incredible Years (IY) parent programmes. However, these programmes typically do not specifically target parents of children with ASD. Recently, a new addition to the IY suite of programmes known as the IY Autistic Spectrum and Language Delays (IY-ASLD) parent programme was developed. The main aims of the present study are to examine the feasibility of delivering this programme within child health services and to provide initial evidence for effectiveness and economic costs. Methods and analysis The Parenting for Autism, Language, And Communication Evaluation Study (PALACES) trial is a pragmatic, multicentre, pilot randomised controlled trial comparing the IY-ASLD programme with a wait-list control condition. 72 parents of children with ASD (aged 3-8 years) will be randomly allocated to either the intervention or control condition. Data will be collected prior to randomisation and 6 months postrandomisation for all families. Families in the intervention condition only will also be followed up at 12 and 18 months postrandomisation. This study will provide initial evidence of effectiveness for the newly developed IY-ASLD parenting programme. It will also add to the limited economic evidence for an intervention targeting parents of children with ASD and provide longer term data, an important component for evaluations of parenting programmes. Ethics and dissemination Approval for the study was granted by the Research Ethics Committee at the School of Psychology, Bangor University (reference number: 2016-15768) and the North Wales Research Ethics Committee, UK (reference number: 16/WA/0224). The findings will be disseminated through research conferences and peer-reviewed journals. Trial registration number ISRCTN57070414; Pre-results.

sheet.es: Si cuida a una niña o un niño autista de 3 a 8 años, puede preguntar a los servicios de salud infantil si ofrecen programas para familias centrados en la comunicación y el lenguaje, como este. Este documento describe el plan de un ensayo piloto aleatorizado: 72 madres, padres o cuidadores recibirán el programa Incredible Years para autismo y retrasos del lenguaje, o quedarán en lista de espera. Aún no hay resultados, así que no sabemos si ayuda. Además, es un estudio pequeño y no debe tomarse como regla para todas las familias.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic child aged 3-8, you could ask your child health services whether they offer family programmes focused on communication and language, like this one. This paper describes the plan for a pilot randomised trial: 72 parents will either receive the Incredible Years programme for autism and language delays or join a wait-list. There are no results yet, so we do not know whether it helps. It is also a small study and should not be taken as a rule for every family.
sheet.sv: Om du har hand om ett autistiskt barn i åldern 3-8 år kan du fråga barnhälsovården om de erbjuder föräldraprogram med fokus på kommunikation och språk, som detta. Artikeln beskriver planen för en randomiserad pilotstudie: 72 föräldrar får antingen programmet Incredible Years för autism och språkförsening eller hamnar på väntelista. Det finns ännu inga resultat, så vi vet inte om det hjälper. Studien är dessutom liten och ska inte ses som en regel för alla familjer.

title: Social outcomes in children with autism spectrum disorder: a review of music therapy outcomes.
authors: LaGasse AB
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) affects approximately one in 68 children, substantially affecting the child's ability to acquire social skills. The application of effective interventions to facilitate and develop social skills is essential due to the lifelong impact that social skills may have on independence and functioning. Research indicates that music therapy can improve social outcomes in children with ASD. Outcome measures are primarily assessed using standardized nonmusical scales of social functioning from the parent or clinician perspective. Certified music therapists may also assess musical engagement and outcomes as a part of the individual's profile. These measures provide an assessment of the individual's social functioning within the music therapy session and generalizability to nonmusical settings.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija disfruta de la música, un musicoterapeuta certificado puede ser una opción que vale la pena explorar para apoyar las habilidades sociales. Conviene preguntar cómo se evaluarán los avances, tanto dentro de la sesión como en otros entornos cotidianos. Esta es una revisión que recoge investigaciones sobre musicoterapia en niños autistas; indica que puede mejorar resultados sociales, medidos sobre todo con escalas completadas por familias o profesionales. Sus límites: el resumen no detalla cuántos estudios incluye ni cuán grandes fueron los efectos, y no todas las personas responderán igual.
sheet.en: If your child enjoys music, a certified music therapist may be worth exploring as one way to support social skills. It helps to ask how progress will be checked, both within sessions and in everyday settings. This is a review of research on music therapy with autistic children; it indicates music therapy can improve social outcomes, mostly measured with scales completed by parents or clinicians. Its limits: the abstract does not say how many studies were included or how large the effects were, and not every child will respond in the same way.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn tycker om musik kan en certifierad musikterapeut vara värd att utforska som ett sätt att stödja sociala färdigheter. Fråga gärna hur framstegen följs upp, både under sessionerna och i vardagen. Det här är en översikt av forskning om musikterapi för autistiska barn; den visar att musikterapi kan förbättra sociala resultat, mest mätt med skalor som föräldrar eller kliniker fyllt i. Begränsningar: sammanfattningen anger inte hur många studier som ingår eller hur stora effekterna var, och alla barn svarar inte likadant.

title: Physical activity, sedentary behavior and their correlates in children with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A systematic review.
authors: Jones RA, Downing K, Rinehart NJ, Barnett LM, May T, McGillivray JA, Papadopoulos NV, Skouteris H, Timperio A, Hinkley T
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder affects up to 2.5% of children and is associated with harmful health outcomes (e.g. obesity). Low levels of physical activity and high levels of sedentary behaviors may contribute to harmful health outcomes. To systematically review the prevalence and correlates of physical activity and sedentary behaviors in children with Autism Spectrum Disorder, electronic databases (PsycINFO, SPORTDiscus, EMBASE, Medline) were searched from inception to November 2015. The review was registered with PROSPERO (CRD42014013849). Peer-reviewed, English language studies were included. Two reviewers screened potentially relevant articles. Outcomes of interest were physical activity and sedentary behaviour levels and their potential correlates. Data were collected and analysed in 2015. Of 35 included studies, 15 reported physical activity prevalence, 10 reported physical activity correlates, 18 reported sedentary behavior prevalence, and 10 reported sedentary behavior correlates. Estimates of children's physical activity (34-166 mins/day, average 86 mins/day) and sedentary behavior (126-558 mins/day in screen time, average 271 mins/day; 428-750 mins/day in total sedentary behavior, average 479 mins/day) varied across studies. Age was consistently inversely associated, and sex inconsistently associated with physical activity. Age and sex were inconsistently associated with sedentary behavior. Sample sizes were small. All but one of the studies were classified as having high risk of bias. Few correlates have been reported in sufficient studies to provide overall estimates of associations. Potential correlates in the physical environment remain largely unexamined. This review highlights varying levels of physical activity and sedentary behavior in children with Autism Spectrum Disorder. Research is needed to consistently identify the correlates of these behaviors. There is a critical need for interventions to support healthy levels of these behaviors.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija autista se mueve menos a medida que crece, no es algo raro: en esta revisión, la actividad física solía bajar con la edad. Mañana puedes buscar una forma de movimiento que le resulte agradable y predecible, como un paseo con ruta conocida, saltar en una cama elástica o nadar, y reservar momentos sin pantallas que no se vivan como castigo. Se trata de una revisión sistemática de 35 estudios con niños y niñas autistas, con cifras muy variables entre estudios. Sus límites: muestras pequeñas, casi todos los estudios con alto riesgo de sesgo y poca información sobre el entorno; no sirve como norma para cada niño.
sheet.en: If your autistic child moves less as they get older, you are not alone: in this review, physical activity tended to drop with age. Tomorrow you could look for one kind of movement your child enjoys and finds predictable, such as a familiar walking route, a trampoline or swimming, and plan some screen-free moments that don't feel like punishment. This is a systematic review of 35 studies of autistic children, and activity and screen-time levels varied widely between them. Its limits: samples were small, nearly all studies had high risk of bias, and the physical environment was barely studied, so it is not a rule for every child.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn rör sig mindre ju äldre det blir är ni inte ensamma: i den här översikten minskade fysisk aktivitet ofta med åldern. I morgon kan du leta efter en rörelseform som barnet tycker om och som känns förutsägbar, till exempel en välbekant promenadrunda, studsmatta eller simning, och planera skärmfria stunder som inte upplevs som straff. Det är en systematisk översikt av 35 studier med autistiska barn, där nivåerna av aktivitet och skärmtid varierade mycket. Begränsningar: små urval, nästan alla studier hade hög risk för bias och den fysiska miljön var knappt undersökt, så resultaten är ingen regel för varje barn.

title: Relationship between Long Chain n-3 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids and Autism Spectrum Disorder: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Case-Control and Randomised Controlled Trials.
authors: Mazahery H, Stonehouse W, Delshad M, Kruger MC, Conlon CA, Beck KL, von Hurst PR
abstract: Omega-3 long chain polyunsaturated fatty acid supplementation ( n -3 LCPUFA) for treatment of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is popular. The results of previous systematic reviews and meta-analyses of n -3 LCPUFA supplementation on ASD outcomes were inconclusive. Two meta-analyses were conducted; meta-analysis 1 compared blood levels of LCPUFA and their ratios arachidonic acid (ARA) to docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), ARA to eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA), or total n -6 to total n -3 LCPUFA in ASD to those of typically developing individuals (with no neurodevelopmental disorders), and meta-analysis 2 compared the effects of n -3 LCPUFA supplementation to placebo on symptoms of ASD. Case-control studies and randomised controlled trials (RCTs) were identified searching electronic databases up to May, 2016. Mean differences were pooled and analysed using inverse variance models. Heterogeneity was assessed using I ² statistic. Fifteen case-control studies ( n = 1193) were reviewed. Compared with typically developed, ASD populations had lower DHA (-2.14 [95% CI -3.22 to -1.07]; p I ² = 97%), EPA (-0.72 [95% CI -1.25 to -0.18]; p = 0.008; I ² = 88%), and ARA (-0.83 [95% CI, -1.48 to -0.17]; p = 0.01; I ² = 96%) and higher total n -6 LCPUFA to n -3 LCPUFA ratio (0.42 [95% CI 0.06 to 0.78]; p = 0.02; I ² = 74%). Four RCTs were included in meta-analysis 2 ( n = 107). Compared with placebo, n -3 LCPUFA improved social interaction (-1.96 [95% CI -3.5 to -0.34]; p = 0.02; I ² = 0) and repetitive and restricted interests and behaviours (-1.08 [95% CI -2.17 to -0.01]; p = 0.05; I ² = 0). Populations with ASD have lower n -3 LCPUFA status and n -3 LCPUFA supplementation can potentially improve some ASD symptoms. Further research with large sample size and adequate study duration is warranted to confirm the efficacy of n -3 LCPUFA.

title: Environmental risk factors for autism: an evidence-based review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
authors: Modabbernia A, Velthorst E, Reichenberg A
abstract: Background According to recent evidence, up to 40-50% of variance in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) liability might be determined by environmental factors. In the present paper, we conducted a review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses of environmental risk factors for ASD. We assessed each review for quality of evidence and provided a brief overview of putative mechanisms of environmental risk factors for ASD. Findings Current evidence suggests that several environmental factors including vaccination, maternal smoking, thimerosal exposure, and most likely assisted reproductive technologies are unrelated to risk of ASD. On the contrary, advanced parental age is associated with higher risk of ASD. Birth complications that are associated with trauma or ischemia and hypoxia have also shown strong links to ASD, whereas other pregnancy-related factors such as maternal obesity, maternal diabetes, and caesarian section have shown a less strong (but significant) association with risk of ASD. The reviews on nutritional elements have been inconclusive about the detrimental effects of deficiency in folic acid and omega 3, but vitamin D seems to be deficient in patients with ASD. The studies on toxic elements have been largely limited by their design, but there is enough evidence for the association between some heavy metals (most important inorganic mercury and lead) and ASD that warrants further investigation. Mechanisms of the association between environmental factors and ASD are debated but might include non-causative association (including confounding), gene-related effect, oxidative stress, inflammation, hypoxia/ischemia, endocrine disruption, neurotransmitter alterations, and interference with signaling pathways. Conclusions Compared to genetic studies of ASD, studies of environmental risk factors are in their infancy and have significant methodological limitations. Future studies of ASD risk factors would benefit from a developmental psychopathology approach, prospective design, precise exposure measurement, reliable timing of exposure in relation to critical developmental periods and should take into account the dynamic interplay between gene and environment by using genetically informed designs.

sheet.es: Si te preguntas si algo que hiciste causó el autismo de tu hijo o hija, esta revisión ofrece calma: las vacunas, el timerosal y fumar en el embarazo no se asocian con el autismo. Algunos factores, como la edad avanzada de los padres o complicaciones en el parto, muestran asociaciones, pero asociación no significa culpa ni causa directa. Puedes soltar la culpa y centrar tu energía en apoyar a tu hijo tal como es hoy. Es una revisión de revisiones sistemáticas y metaanálisis que evaluó la calidad de la evidencia sobre factores ambientales. Sus límites: muchos estudios incluidos tienen diseños débiles y no pueden demostrar causa ni aplicarse a cada familia.
sheet.en: If you wonder whether something you did caused your child's autism, this review offers calm: vaccines, thimerosal and smoking during pregnancy are not linked to autism. Some factors, such as older parental age or birth complications, show associations, but association does not mean blame or direct cause. You can let go of guilt and put your energy into supporting your child as they are today. This is a review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses that rated the quality of evidence on environmental factors. Its limits: many included studies had weak designs, cannot prove cause, and do not apply to every family.
sheet.sv: Om du undrar om något du gjorde orsakade ditt barns autism ger denna översikt lugn: vaccin, timerosal och rökning under graviditeten har inget samband med autism. Vissa faktorer, som högre ålder hos föräldrar eller förlossningskomplikationer, visar samband, men samband betyder inte skuld eller direkt orsak. Du kan släppa skulden och lägga din energi på att stötta ditt barn som det är i dag. Detta är en översikt av systematiska översikter och metaanalyser som bedömde evidensens kvalitet om miljöfaktorer. Begränsningar: många ingående studier hade svag design, kan inte bevisa orsak och gäller inte varje familj.

title: An Overview of Autism Spectrum Disorder, Heterogeneity and Treatment Options.
authors: Masi A, DeMayo MM, Glozier N, Guastella AJ
abstract: Since the documented observations of Kanner in 1943, there has been great debate about the diagnoses, the sub-types, and the diagnostic threshold that relates to what is now known as autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Reflecting this complicated history, there has been continual refinement from DSM-III with 'Infantile Autism' to the current DSM-V diagnosis. The disorder is now widely accepted as a complex, pervasive, heterogeneous condition with multiple etiologies, sub-types, and developmental trajectories. Diagnosis remains based on observation of atypical behaviors, with criteria of persistent deficits in social communication and restricted and repetitive patterns of behavior. This review provides a broad overview of the history, prevalence, etiology, clinical presentation, and heterogeneity of ASD. Factors contributing to heterogeneity, including genetic variability, comorbidity, and gender are reviewed. We then explore current evidence-based pharmacological and behavioral treatments for ASD and highlight the complexities of conducting clinical trials that evaluate therapeutic efficacy in ASD populations. Finally, we discuss the potential of a new wave of research examining objective biomarkers to facilitate the evaluation of sub-typing, diagnosis, and treatment response in ASD.

sheet.es: Tome este texto como recordatorio de que cada persona autista es distinta: lo que ayuda a una puede no ayudar a otra, así que conviene observar sus necesidades y preferencias concretas antes de elegir apoyos. Es una revisión de la literatura de 2017 que repasa la historia, las causas, la diversidad del autismo (genética, otras condiciones y género) y los tratamientos conductuales y farmacológicos. Sus límites: no es un estudio con participantes propios, no ofrece una guía para un caso individual y señala que evaluar tratamientos en autismo es complejo. Las decisiones médicas corresponden siempre a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: Take this as a reminder that every autistic person is different: what helps one person may not help another, so it is worth observing their specific needs and preferences before choosing supports. This is a 2017 review of the literature covering history, causes, the diversity of autism (genetics, co-occurring conditions and gender) and behavioural and pharmacological treatments. Its limits: it is not a study with its own participants, it gives no guide for an individual case, and it notes that testing treatments in autism is complex. Medical decisions always belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Se detta som en påminnelse om att varje autistisk person är olika: det som hjälper en kanske inte hjälper en annan, så det är värt att utgå från personens egna behov och preferenser när stöd väljs. Det är en översikt från 2017 som går igenom historia, orsaker, autismens mångfald (genetik, samtidiga tillstånd och kön) samt beteendemässiga och farmakologiska behandlingar. Begränsningar: den har inga egna deltagare, ger ingen vägledning för enskilda fall och påpekar att det är svårt att utvärdera behandlingar vid autism. Medicinska beslut hör alltid till en kliniker.

title: The Immune System, Cytokines, and Biomarkers in Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Masi A, Glozier N, Dale R, Guastella AJ
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a pervasive neurodevelopmental condition characterized by variable impairments in communication and social interaction as well as restricted interests and repetitive behaviors. Heterogeneity of presentation is a hallmark. Investigations of immune system problems in ASD, including aberrations in cytokine profiles and signaling, have been increasing in recent times and are the subject of ongoing interest. With the aim of establishing whether cytokines have utility as potential biomarkers that may define a subgroup of ASD, or function as an objective measure of response to treatment, this review summarizes the role of the immune system, discusses the relationship between the immune system, the brain, and behavior, and presents previously-identified immune system abnormalities in ASD, specifically addressing the role of cytokines in these aberrations. The roles and identification of biomarkers are also addressed, particularly with respect to cytokine profiles in ASD.

title: Whose Expertise Is It? Evidence for Autistic Adults as Critical Autism Experts.
authors: Gillespie-Lynch K, Kapp SK, Brooks PJ, Pickens J, Schwartzman B
abstract: Autistic and non-autistic adults' agreement with scientific knowledge about autism, how they define autism, and their endorsement of stigmatizing conceptions of autism has not previously been examined. Using an online survey, we assessed autism knowledge and stigma among 636 adults with varied relationships to autism, including autistic people and nuclear family members. Autistic participants exhibited more scientifically based knowledge than others. They were more likely to describe autism experientially or as a neutral difference, and more often opposed the medical model. Autistic participants and family members reported lower stigma. Greater endorsement of the importance of normalizing autistic people was associated with heightened stigma. Findings suggest that autistic adults should be considered autism experts and involved as partners in autism research.

sheet.es: Cuando busque información sobre autismo, dé mucho peso a lo que cuentan las propias personas autistas: pueden ser fuentes expertas. Pregunte y escuche cómo describen su experiencia. Este estudio fue una encuesta en línea con 636 personas adultas con distintas relaciones con el autismo, incluidas personas autistas y familiares directos. Las personas autistas mostraron más conocimiento científico y menos estigma, y describían el autismo más como una diferencia neutral. Es una encuesta de un momento concreto, y las respuestas no representan a todas las personas autistas ni a todas las familias.
sheet.en: When you look for information about autism, give real weight to what autistic people themselves say: they can be expert sources. Ask, and listen to how they describe their own experience. This study was an online survey of 636 adults with different relationships to autism, including autistic people and close family members. Autistic participants showed more scientifically based knowledge and reported lower stigma, and they more often described autism as a neutral difference. It is a survey from one point in time, and the answers do not speak for every autistic person or every family.
sheet.sv: När du söker information om autism, väg in det autistiska personer själva berättar: de kan vara experter. Fråga och lyssna på hur de beskriver sin egen erfarenhet. Studien var en webbenkät med 636 vuxna med olika relationer till autism, bland annat autistiska personer och nära familjemedlemmar. Autistiska deltagare visade mer vetenskapligt baserad kunskap och rapporterade lägre stigma, och beskrev oftare autism som en neutral skillnad. Det är en enkät vid ett enda tillfälle, och svaren gäller inte alla autistiska personer eller alla familjer.

title: Therapeutic Horseback Riding Crossover Effects of Attachment Behaviors with Family Pets in a Sample of Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Petty JD, Pan Z, Dechant B, Gabriels RL
journal: International journal of environmental research and public health
abstract: The unique needs of individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) have implications for animal welfare. This nested pilot study examined the effects of a randomized trial of 10-week therapeutic horseback riding (THR) intervention versus a no-horse barn activity (BA) control group on children's behaviors with family pets. Sixty-seven (THR n = 31; BA n = 36) participants with ASD (ages 6-16 years) with one or more family pet, were enrolled from a larger trial ( n = 116) following their randomization to intervention groups, stratified by nonverbal intellectual ability. A consistent caregiver completed questionnaires about participants' interactions with their household pets pre- and post-intervention. Caregivers of THR group participants reported significant improvements in participants' caring actions with the family pet compared with the BA group ( p = 0.013; effect size = 0.74). Engaging with horses during a standard THR intervention protocol may generalize to improving caring actions toward family pets in children and adolescents with ASD.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija autista convive con una mascota, puede observar con calma cómo se relaciona con ella y ofrecerle ocasiones tranquilas para cuidarla, sin presionar. Los resultados sugieren que la equitación terapéutica podría ayudar a que estos gestos de cuidado se extiendan a casa. Es un ensayo piloto aleatorizado con 67 participantes autistas de 6-16 años que tenían mascota; las familias informaron de más acciones de cuidado tras 10 semanas de equitación terapéutica que en el grupo de actividad en el establo sin caballos. Sus límites: es un estudio pequeño, se basa en lo que informan las familias y no demuestra que ocurra igual en cada persona.
sheet.en: If your autistic child lives with a family pet, you can calmly notice how they relate to the animal and offer relaxed chances to help care for it, without pressure. The findings suggest therapeutic horseback riding may help caring actions carry over to home. This was a randomized pilot trial with 67 autistic participants aged 6-16 years who had a pet; after 10 weeks, caregivers reported more caring actions toward the pet than in the barn activity group without horses. Limits: it was small, relied on caregiver reports, and does not show the same result would happen for every person.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn har ett husdjur hemma kan du lugnt lägga märke till hur barnet samspelar med djuret och erbjuda avslappnade tillfällen att hjälpa till med omsorgen, utan press. Resultaten tyder på att terapeutisk ridning kan bidra till att omsorgsfulla handlingar följer med hem. Det var en randomiserad pilotstudie med 67 autistiska deltagare i åldern 6-16 år som hade husdjur; efter 10 veckor rapporterade vårdnadshavare fler omsorgsfulla handlingar mot djuret än i gruppen med stallaktivitet utan hästar. Begränsningar: studien var liten, byggde på vårdnadshavares rapporter och visar inte att det blir likadant för alla.

title: Impact of the Early Start Denver Model on the cognitive level of children with autism spectrum disorder: study protocol for a randomised controlled trial using a two-stage Zelen design.
authors: Touzet S, Occelli P, Schröder C, Manificat S, Gicquel L, Stanciu R, Schaer M, Oreve MJ, Speranza M, Denis A, Zelmar A, Falissard B, Georgieff N, Bahrami S, Geoffray MM, IDEA Study Group
abstract: Introduction Early intervention for autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in the European French-speaking countries is heterogeneous and poorly evaluated to date. Early intervention units applying the Early Start Denver Model (ESDM) for toddlers and young children with ASD have been created in France and Belgium to improve this situation. It is essential to evaluate this intervention for the political decision-making process regarding ASD interventions in European French-speaking countries. We will evaluate the effectiveness of 12 hours per week ESDM intervention on the cognitive level of children with ASD, over a 2-year period. Methods and analysis The study will be a multicentre, randomised controlled trial, using a two-stage Zelen design. Children aged 15-36 months, diagnosed with ASD and with a developmental quotient (DQ) of 30 or above on the Mullen Scale of Early Learning (MSEL) will be included. We will use a stratified minimisation randomisation at a ratio 1:2 in favour of the control group. The sample size required is 180 children (120 in the control and 60 in the intervention group). The experimental group will receive 12 hours per week ESDM by trained therapists 10 hours per week in the centre and 2 hours in the toddlers' natural environment (alternatively by the therapist and the parent). The control group will receive care available in the community. The primary outcome will be the change in cognitive level measured with the DQ of the MSEL scored at 2 years. Secondary outcomes will include change in autism symptoms, behavioural adaptation, communicative and productive language level, sensory profile and parents' quality of life. The primary analysis will use the intention-to-treat principle. An economic evaluation will be performed. Dissemination Findings from the study will be disseminated through peer reviewed publications and meetings. Trial registration number NCT02608333 (clinicaltrials.gov); Pre-results.

sheet.es: Si valora una intervención temprana para su hijo o hija autista, este estudio aún no ofrece resultados, pero puede ayudarle a hacer preguntas: qué se trabaja, cuántas horas, y cómo participa la familia. Es el protocolo de un ensayo aleatorizado que evaluará el Early Start Denver Model, con 12 horas por semana durante 2 años, en niños de 15-36 meses, comparándolo con la atención disponible en la comunidad. Mide el nivel cognitivo y también el lenguaje, la adaptación y la calidad de vida de los padres. Como aún no hay resultados, no permite concluir que funcione ni que convenga a cada niño o familia.
sheet.en: If you are weighing early intervention for your autistic child, this study does not give results yet, but it can help you ask good questions: what is worked on, how many hours, and how the family takes part. It is a protocol for a randomised trial that will test the Early Start Denver Model, 12 hours per week over 2 years, in children aged 15-36 months, compared with care available in the community. It will measure cognitive level, and also language, adaptation and parents' quality of life. Since there are no results yet, it cannot show that the approach works or suits every child or family.
sheet.sv: Om du överväger tidiga insatser för ditt autistiska barn ger den här studien inga resultat än, men den kan hjälpa dig att ställa frågor: vad som tränas, hur många timmar och hur familjen deltar. Det är ett protokoll för en randomiserad studie som ska testa Early Start Denver Model, 12 timmar per vecka under 2 år, för barn i åldern 15-36 månader, jämfört med den vård som finns i samhället. Den ska mäta kognitiv nivå, men också språk, anpassning och föräldrars livskvalitet. Eftersom resultat saknas kan den inte visa att metoden fungerar eller passar alla barn och familjer.

title: Environmental factors influencing the risk of autism.
authors: Karimi P, Kamali E, Mousavi SM, Karahmadi M
journal: Journal of research in medical sciences : the official journal of Isfahan University of Medical Sciences
abstract: Autism is a developmental disability with age of onset in childhood (under 3 years old), which is characterized by definite impairments in social interactions, abnormalities in speech, and stereotyped pattern of behaviors. Due to the progress of autism in recent decades, a wide range of studies have been done to identify the etiological factors of autism. It has been found that genetic and environmental factors are both involved in autism pathogenesis. Hence, in this review article, a set of environmental factors involved in the occurrence of autism has been collected, and finally, some practical recommendations for reduction of the risk of this devastating disease in children are represented.

sheet.es: Si te preguntas si hiciste algo que «causó» el autismo de tu hijo o hija, puedes soltar esa culpa: el autismo surge de una mezcla compleja de genética y entorno, y ninguna decisión aislada lo explica. Mañana, la energía rinde más dedicada a entender cómo se comunica tu hijo, qué le calma y qué apoyos necesita. Esta revisión de 2017 reunió estudios previos sobre factores ambientales asociados al autismo, sin datos nuevos de participantes. Sus límites: describe el autismo como «enfermedad devastadora», un enfoque que no compartimos, y las asociaciones que recoge no prueban causa ni se aplican a cada persona.
sheet.en: If you wonder whether something you did "caused" your child's autism, you can let go of that guilt: autism arises from a complex mix of genetics and environment, and no single choice explains it. Tomorrow, your energy is better spent understanding how your child communicates, what calms them and what support they need. This 2017 review gathered earlier studies on environmental factors linked to autism, with no new participant data. Its limits: it frames autism as a "devastating disease", a view we do not share, and the associations it collects do not prove cause or apply to every person.
sheet.sv: Om du undrar om något du gjorde "orsakade" ditt barns autism kan du släppa den skulden: autism uppstår ur en komplex blandning av genetik och miljö, och inget enskilt val förklarar det. I morgon gör din energi mer nytta när du försöker förstå hur ditt barn kommunicerar, vad som lugnar och vilket stöd som behövs. Denna översikt från 2017 samlade tidigare studier om miljöfaktorer kopplade till autism, utan nya deltagardata. Begränsningar: den beskriver autism som en "förödande sjukdom", ett synsätt vi inte delar, och sambanden den samlar bevisar inte orsak och gäller inte varje person.

title: Guideline recommendations for diagnosis and clinical management of Ring14 syndrome-first report of an ad hoc task force.
authors: Rinaldi B, Vaisfeld A, Amarri S, Baldo C, Gobbi G, Magini P, Melli E, Neri G, Novara F, Pippucci T, Rizzi R, Soresina A, Zampini L, Zuffardi O, Crimi M
abstract: Background Ring chromosome 14 syndrome is a rare chromosomal disorder characterized by early onset refractory epilepsy, intellectual disability, autism spectrum disorder and a number of diverse health issues. Results The aim of this work is to provide recommendations for the diagnosis and management of persons affected by ring chromosome 14 syndrome based on evidence from literature and experience of health professionals from different medical backgrounds who have followed for several years subjects affected by ring chromosome 14 syndrome. The literature search was performed in 2016. Original papers, meta-analyses, reviews, books and guidelines were reviewed and final recommendations were reached by consensus. Conclusion Conventional cytogenetics is the primary tool to identify a ring chromosome. Children with a terminal deletion of chromosome 14q ascertained by molecular karyotyping (CGH/SNP array) should be tested secondarily by conventional cytogenetics for the presence of a ring chromosome. Early diagnosis should be pursued in order to provide medical and social assistance by a multidisciplinary team. Clinical investigations, including neurophysiology for epilepsy, should be performed at the diagnosis and within the follow-up. Following the diagnosis, patients and relatives/caregivers should receive regular care for health and social issues. Epilepsy should be treated from the onset with anticonvulsive therapy. Likewise, feeding difficulties should be treated according to need. Nutritional assessment is recommended for all patients and nutritional support for malnourishment can include gastrostomy feeding in selected cases. Presence of autistic traits should be carefully evaluated. Many patients with ring chromosome 14 syndrome are nonverbal and thus maintaining their ability to communicate is always essential; every effort should be made to preserve their autonomy.

sheet.es: Si cuida a una persona con síndrome del cromosoma 14 en anillo, busque un equipo multidisciplinar con revisiones regulares de salud, alimentación y apoyo social, y proteja siempre su forma de comunicarse y su autonomía. La evidencia es una revisión con recomendaciones de un grupo de trabajo, basada en literatura y en la experiencia de profesionales de distintas especialidades, alcanzadas por consenso. Sus límites: es una enfermedad rara, son recomendaciones generales y no sustituyen a cada equipo clínico. Las decisiones médicas, como el tratamiento de la epilepsia, corresponden a su profesional de salud.
sheet.en: If you support a person with ring chromosome 14 syndrome, look for a multidisciplinary team with regular check-ups on health, eating and social support, and always protect the person's way of communicating and their autonomy. The evidence is a review with recommendations from a task force, drawing on literature and the experience of professionals from different specialities, agreed by consensus. Its limits: the condition is rare, the advice is general, and it cannot replace the person's own clinical team. Medical decisions, such as epilepsy treatment, belong to their clinician.
sheet.sv: Om du stödjer en person med ringkromosom 14-syndrom, sök ett multidisciplinärt team med regelbundna kontroller av hälsa, ätande och socialt stöd, och skydda alltid personens sätt att kommunicera och dess självbestämmande. Underlaget är en översikt med rekommendationer från en arbetsgrupp, byggd på litteratur och yrkesfolks erfarenhet från olika specialiteter, enade genom konsensus. Begränsningar: tillståndet är sällsynt, råden är generella och ersätter inte personens eget vårdteam. Medicinska beslut, till exempel om epilepsibehandling, hör till en läkare.

title: Rural Trends in Diagnosis and Services for Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Antezana L, Scarpa A, Valdespino A, Albright J, Richey JA
abstract: Rural communities face significant challenges regarding the adequate availability of diagnostic-, treatment-, and support-services for individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Specifically, a variety of factors, including geographic distance between families and service providers, low reliance on health care professionals, and cultural characteristics, contribute to the diminished availability and utilization of services. Together, these factors lead to risks for delayed ASD screening and diagnosis, yielding lower educational and functional outcomes. The purpose of this review is to outline the specific diagnosis and treatment barriers that affect individuals with ASD and their families in rural settings. Telehealth feasibility and efficacy research is also reviewed, suggesting that telecommunication services may offer an inroad for addressing the specific service barriers faced by rural communities. Together, the current review identifies specific needs for both research and support services that address the specific access barriers characteristic of rural settings.

sheet.es: Si vives en una zona rural, preguntar por opciones de telesalud (consultas por vídeo o teléfono) con servicios de evaluación y apoyo puede ahorrar viajes largos. Es razonable pedir una valoración pronto si tienes dudas, sin esperar. Se trata de una revisión de la bibliografía sobre barreras de diagnóstico y servicios en comunidades rurales, que también repasa estudios sobre telesalud; el resumen sugiere que podría ayudar a superar esas barreras. Sus límites: es una revisión, no indica qué opción funciona mejor para cada familia, y la disponibilidad de servicios varía mucho según el lugar.
sheet.en: If you live in a rural area, ask services about telehealth options (video or phone appointments) for assessment and support, which may save long journeys. It is reasonable to ask for an assessment early if you have questions, rather than waiting. This is a review of the literature on diagnosis and service barriers in rural communities, and it also covers research on telehealth, which the abstract suggests may help address those barriers. Its limits: it is a review, it does not show which option works best for each family, and what services exist varies a great deal from place to place.
sheet.sv: Om du bor på landsbygden kan du fråga vården om telehälsa (video- eller telefonbesök) för utredning och stöd, vilket kan spara långa resor. Det är rimligt att be om en bedömning tidigt om du har frågor, i stället för att vänta. Detta är en översikt av litteraturen om hinder för diagnos och stöd i landsbygdssamhällen, och den går också igenom forskning om telehälsa, som enligt sammanfattningen kan hjälpa till att möta hindren. Begränsningar: det är en översikt, den visar inte vilket alternativ som passar varje familj bäst, och utbudet av tjänster varierar mycket mellan platser.

title: A systematic review of pragmatic language interventions for children with autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Parsons L, Cordier R, Munro N, Joosten A, Speyer R
abstract: There is a need for evidence based interventions for children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) to limit the life-long, psychosocial impact of pragmatic language impairments. This systematic review identified 22 studies reporting on 20 pragmatic language interventions for children with ASD aged 0-18 years. The characteristics of each study, components of the interventions, and the methodological quality of each study were reviewed. Meta-analysis was conducted to assess the effectiveness of 15 interventions. Results revealed some promising approaches, indicating that active inclusion of the child and parent in the intervention was a significant mediator of intervention effect. Participant age, therapy setting or modality were not significant mediators between the interventions and measures of pragmatic language. The long-term effects of these interventions and the generalisation of learning to new contexts is largely unknown. Implications for clinical practice and directions for future research are discussed.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija participa en apoyos para la comunicación social (cómo conversar, turnarse, entender contextos), merece la pena pedir que tanto el niño como tú tengáis un papel activo: practicar juntos, opinar sobre los objetivos y llevar lo aprendido a la vida diaria. Respeta su forma natural de comunicarse; el objetivo es apoyar, no corregir quién es. Esta revisión sistemática analizó 22 estudios sobre 20 intervenciones con niños y adolescentes autistas de 0 a 18 años; la participación activa del niño y de la familia se asoció con mejores resultados, independientemente de la edad o el formato. Sus límites: se sabe poco sobre los efectos a largo plazo y si lo aprendido se traslada a nuevos lugares.
sheet.en: If your child takes part in social communication support (conversation, turn-taking, reading context), it is worth asking that both your child and you play an active role: practising together, having a say in goals, and carrying skills into everyday life. Respect your child's natural ways of communicating; the aim is support, not changing who they are. This systematic review looked at 22 studies of 20 interventions with autistic children and teenagers aged 0–18; active involvement of the child and parent was linked to better results, regardless of age, setting or format. Its limits: little is known about long-term effects or whether skills carry over to new situations.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn får stöd i social kommunikation (samtal, turtagning, att läsa av sammanhang) kan det vara värt att be om att både barnet och du får en aktiv roll: öva tillsammans, vara med och bestämma mål och ta med färdigheterna in i vardagen. Respektera barnets egna sätt att kommunicera; målet är stöd, inte att ändra vem barnet är. Denna systematiska översikt granskade 22 studier om 20 insatser för autistiska barn och unga 0–18 år; aktivt deltagande från barn och förälder hängde ihop med bättre resultat, oavsett ålder, miljö eller format. Begränsningar: det är oklart hur länge effekterna håller och om färdigheterna används i nya situationer.

title: The Gut Microbiota and Autism Spectrum Disorders.
authors: Li Q, Han Y, Dy ABC, Hagerman RJ
abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms are a common comorbidity in patients with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), but the underlying mechanisms are unknown. Many studies have shown alterations in the composition of the fecal flora and metabolic products of the gut microbiome in patients with ASD. The gut microbiota influences brain development and behaviors through the neuroendocrine, neuroimmune and autonomic nervous systems. In addition, an abnormal gut microbiota is associated with several diseases, such as inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), ASD and mood disorders. Here, we review the bidirectional interactions between the central nervous system and the gastrointestinal tract (brain-gut axis) and the role of the gut microbiota in the central nervous system (CNS) and ASD. Microbiome-mediated therapies might be a safe and effective treatment for ASD.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista muestra molestias digestivas, como dolor de barriga o estreñimiento, vale la pena observarlas con calma, anotarlas y comentarlas con un profesional sanitario, sin suponer que son "parte del autismo". La evidencia procede de una revisión de estudios que describe diferencias en la flora intestinal y en sus productos en personas con TEA, y la conexión entre intestino y cerebro. Sus límites: no explica las causas, no demuestra que la microbiota provoque rasgos autistas, y la idea de que las terapias basadas en el microbioma sean seguras y eficaces es solo una hipótesis. Cualquier decisión médica corresponde a un clínico.
sheet.en: If an autistic person has digestive discomfort, such as stomach pain or constipation, it is worth noticing it calmly, keeping notes and raising it with a health professional, rather than assuming it is "just part of autism". The evidence is a review of earlier studies describing differences in gut bacteria and their products in people with ASD, and links between gut and brain. Its limits: it does not explain the causes, does not show that gut bacteria cause autistic traits, and the suggestion that microbiome-based therapies might be safe and effective is only a possibility. Medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person har magbesvär, som magont eller förstoppning, är det värt att lägga märke till det i lugn och ro, föra anteckningar och ta upp det med sjukvårdspersonal, i stället för att anta att det "bara hör till autismen". Underlaget är en översikt av tidigare studier som beskriver skillnader i tarmflora och dess produkter hos personer med ASD, samt kopplingar mellan tarm och hjärna. Begränsningar: den förklarar inte orsakerna, visar inte att tarmbakterier orsakar autistiska drag, och att behandlingar via mikrobiomet skulle vara säkra och effektiva är bara en möjlighet. Medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker.

title: Is functional brain connectivity atypical in autism? A systematic review of EEG and MEG studies.
authors: O'Reilly C, Lewis JD, Elsabbagh M
abstract: Background Although it is well recognized that autism is associated with altered patterns of over- and under-connectivity, specifics are still a matter of debate. Little has been done so far to synthesize available literature using whole-brain electroencephalography (EEG) and magnetoencephalography (MEG) recordings. Objectives 1) To systematically review the literature on EEG/MEG functional and effective connectivity in autism spectrum disorder (ASD), 2) to synthesize and critically appraise findings related with the hypothesis that ASD is characterized by long-range underconnectivity and local overconnectivity, and 3) to provide, based on the literature, an analysis of tentative factors that are likely to mediate association between ASD and atypical connectivity (e.g., development, topography, lateralization). Methods Literature reviews were done using PubMed and PsychInfo databases. Abstracts were screened, and only relevant articles were analyzed based on the objectives of this paper. Special attention was paid to the methodological characteristics that could have created variability in outcomes reported between studies. Results Our synthesis provides relatively strong support for long-range underconnectivity in ASD, whereas the status of local connectivity remains unclear. This observation was also mirrored by a similar relationship with lower frequencies being often associated with underconnectivity and higher frequencies being associated with both under- and over-connectivity. Putting together these observations, we propose that ASD is characterized by a general trend toward an under-expression of lower-band wide-spread integrative processes compensated by more focal, higher-frequency, locally specialized, and segregated processes. Further investigation is, however, needed to corroborate the conclusion and its generalizability across different tasks. Of note, abnormal lateralization in ASD, specifically an elevated left-over-right EEG and MEG functional connectivity ratio, has been also reported consistently across studies. Conclusions The large variability in study samples and methodology makes a systematic quantitative analysis (i.e. meta-analysis) of this body of research impossible. Nevertheless, a general trend supporting the hypothesis of long-range functional underconnectivity can be observed. Further research is necessary to more confidently determine the status of the hypothesis of short-range overconnectivity. Frequency-band specific patterns and their relationships with known symptoms of autism also need to be further clarified.

sheet.es: Este estudio no ofrece nada que cambiar mañana por la mañana en casa. Sí ayuda a entender que el cerebro de muchas personas autistas puede comunicar sus zonas distantes de otra manera, sin que eso diga nada sobre el valor de una persona. Es una revisión sistemática de estudios de EEG y MEG, que miden la actividad cerebral. Aunque se etiquetó como metaanálisis, sus autores indican que no fue posible un análisis cuantitativo por la gran variedad de muestras y métodos. Por eso las conclusiones son tendencias, no reglas, y no sirven para predecir a una persona concreta. Ante dudas, consulte con un profesional.
sheet.en: This study offers nothing to change at home tomorrow morning. It does help to know that many autistic people's brains may link distant areas in a different way, which says nothing about a person's worth. It is a systematic review of EEG and MEG studies, which measure brain activity. Although labelled a meta-analysis, its authors say a quantitative analysis was not possible because samples and methods varied so much. The findings are therefore trends, not rules, and cannot predict anything about one particular person. If you have questions, talk with a professional.
sheet.sv: Den här studien ger inget att ändra hemma i morgon bitti. Den kan ändå hjälpa att veta att hjärnan hos många autistiska personer kan koppla ihop avlägsna områden på ett annat sätt, vilket inte säger något om en människas värde. Det är en systematisk översikt av EEG- och MEG-studier, som mäter hjärnaktivitet. Trots att den kallas metaanalys säger författarna att en kvantitativ analys inte var möjlig, eftersom urval och metoder varierade mycket. Resultaten är alltså tendenser, inte regler, och kan inte förutsäga något om en enskild person. Har du frågor, prata med en yrkesperson.

title: Prenatal, perinatal, and postnatal factors associated with autism: A meta-analysis.
authors: Wang C, Geng H, Liu W, Zhang G
abstract: Background The aim of this meta-analysis was to investigate the prenatal, perinatal, and postnatal risk factors for children autism. Methods PubMed, Embase, Web of Science were used to search for studies that examined the prenatal, perinatal, and postnatal risk factors for children autism. A fixed-effects model or random-effects model was used to pool the overall effect estimates. Results Data from 37,634 autistic children and 12,081,416 nonautistic children enrolled in 17 studies were collated. During the prenatal period, the factors associated with autism risk were maternal and paternal age≥35 years, mother's and father's race: White and Asian, gestational hypertension, gestational diabetes, maternal and paternal education college graduate+, threatened abortion, and antepartum hemorrhage. During perinatal period, the factors associated with autism risk were caesarian delivery, gestational age≤36 weeks, parity≥4, spontaneous labor, induced labor, no labor, breech presentation, preeclampsia, and fetal distress. During the postnatal period, the factors associated with autism risk were low birth weight, postpartum hemorrhage, male gender, and brain anomaly. Parity≥4 and female were associated with a decreased risk of autism. In addition, exposure to cigarette smoking, urinary infection, mother's and father's race: Black and Hispanic, mother's country of birth outside Europe and North America, umbilical cord around neck, premature membrane rupture, 5-minutes Apgar score Conclusion The present meta-analysis confirmed the relation between some prenatal, perinatal, and postnatal factors with autism. All these factors were examined individually, thus it was still unclear that whether these factors are causal or play a secondary role in the development of autism. Further studies are needed to verify our findings, and investigate the effects of multiple factors on autism, rather than the single factor.

title: Effectiveness of Non-Pharmacological Interventions on Stereotyped and Repetitive Behaviors of Pre-school Children With Autism: A Systematic Review.
authors: Zarafshan H, Salmanian M, Aghamohammadi S, Mohammadi MR, Mostafavi SA
abstract: Introduction The present study aimed to review the literature on non-pharmacological interventions used to treat stereotyped and repetitive behaviors by a systematic method. Methods Two authors independently performed a search strategy on Medline/PubMed, Scopus and PsycINFO on English articles published up to April 23, 2014 with relevant search keywords. We also reviewed the bibliographies of retrieved articles and conference proceedings to obtain additional citations and references. We examined those articles that addressed non-pharmacological interventions on reducing stereotyped and repetitive behaviors in preschool children with autism. Four independent reviewers screened relevant articles for inclusion criteria and assessed the quality of eligible articles with CONSORT checklist. Results In our search, 664 relevant articles were found. After removing duplicates and screening based on title, abstract, and full text, 15 high-quality studies were finally included in data analyses. The included articles were published from 1987 to 2013. Three studies were designed as A-B, two as A-B-A, and reminders as A-B-A-B. The data and results of 3 clinical trials were synthesized; two of them were parallel randomized clinical trial and another one was designed as cross-over. Interventions were completely heterogeneous in case studies, including non-contingent auditory stimulation, response interruption and redirection, teaching the children to request assistance on difficult tasks, family-implemented treatment for behavioral inflexibility with treatment approach, vocal or motor response interruption and redirection, brushing, water mist treatment, exposure response prevention, tangible reinforcement or social reinforcement, and music. Interventions in clinical trials included touch therapy, kata techniques training program, and aerobic exercise. Conclusion The results of our review indicate that different kinds of non-pharmacological interventions can be used to treat repetitive behaviors in children with autism; however, sufficient evidence for their effectiveness does not exist. Future research using more precise methods (RCTs) can clarify which methods and techniques are effective in reducing repetitive behavior of children with autism.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija autista tiene conductas repetitivas, no hay un método no farmacológico con eficacia demostrada. Conviene observar qué función cumplen (calma, juego, regulación) y consultar con un profesional antes de intentar reducirlas. Es una revisión sistemática de 15 estudios de calidad con niños autistas en edad preescolar, que exploraron intervenciones muy distintas, como música, ejercicio aeróbico o redirección. Sus límites: las intervenciones eran muy diversas, pocos estudios eran ensayos aleatorizados y los autores concluyen que no existe evidencia suficiente de eficacia. Tampoco sirve como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If your autistic child has repetitive behaviors, this review found no non-pharmacological approach with proven effectiveness. It can help to notice what the behavior does for them (calming, play, regulation) and talk with a professional before trying to reduce it. This is a systematic review of 15 high-quality studies with autistic preschool children, covering very different approaches such as music, aerobic exercise or redirection. Its limits: the interventions were highly varied, few studies were randomized trials, and the authors conclude that sufficient evidence of effectiveness does not exist. It is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn har repetitiva beteenden visar den här översikten ingen icke-medicinsk metod med belagd effekt. Det kan hjälpa att lägga märke till vad beteendet ger barnet (lugn, lek, reglering) och prata med en yrkesperson innan man försöker minska det. Det är en systematisk översikt av 15 studier med hög kvalitet om autistiska förskolebarn, med mycket olika metoder som musik, aerob träning eller omdirigering.
