Begränsningar: insatserna var mycket varierande, få studier var randomiserade, och författarna menar att tillräckligt stöd för effekt saknas. Den gäller inte som regel för varje person.

title: Meta-analysis of GWAS of over 16,000 individuals with autism spectrum disorder highlights a novel locus at 10q24.32 and a significant overlap with schizophrenia.
authors: Autism Spectrum Disorders Working Group of The Psychiatric Genomics Consortium
abstract: Background Over the past decade genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have been applied to aid in the understanding of the biology of traits. The success of this approach is governed by the underlying effect sizes carried by the true risk variants and the corresponding statistical power to observe such effects given the study design and sample size under investigation. Previous ASD GWAS have identified genome-wide significant (GWS) risk loci; however, these studies were of only of low statistical power to identify GWS loci at the lower effect sizes (odds ratio (OR) Methods We conducted a large-scale coordinated international collaboration to combine independent genotyping data to improve the statistical power and aid in robust discovery of GWS loci. This study uses genome-wide genotyping data from a discovery sample (7387 ASD cases and 8567 controls) followed by meta-analysis of summary statistics from two replication sets (7783 ASD cases and 11359 controls; and 1369 ASD cases and 137308 controls). Results We observe a GWS locus at 10q24.32 that overlaps several genes including PITX3 , which encodes a transcription factor identified as playing a role in neuronal differentiation and CUEDC2 previously reported to be associated with social skills in an independent population cohort. We also observe overlap with regions previously implicated in schizophrenia which was further supported by a strong genetic correlation between these disorders (Rg = 0.23; P = 9 × 10 -6 ). We further combined these Psychiatric Genomics Consortium (PGC) ASD GWAS data with the recent PGC schizophrenia GWAS to identify additional regions which may be important in a common neurodevelopmental phenotype and identified 12 novel GWS loci. These include loci previously implicated in ASD such as FOXP1 at 3p13, ATP2B2 at 3p25.3, and a 'neurodevelopmental hub' on chromosome 8p11.23. Conclusions This study is an important step in the ongoing endeavour to identify the loci which underpin the common variant signal in ASD. In addition to novel GWS loci, we have identified a significant genetic correlation with schizophrenia and association of ASD with several neurodevelopmental-related genes such as EXT1 , ASTN2 , MACROD2 , and HDAC4.

title: Embodied Conversational Agents in Clinical Psychology: A Scoping Review.
authors: Provoost S, Lau HM, Lau HM, Ruwaard J, Riper H
abstract: Background Embodied conversational agents (ECAs) are computer-generated characters that simulate key properties of human face-to-face conversation, such as verbal and nonverbal behavior. In Internet-based eHealth interventions, ECAs may be used for the delivery of automated human support factors. Objective We aim to provide an overview of the technological and clinical possibilities, as well as the evidence base for ECA applications in clinical psychology, to inform health professionals about the activity in this field of research. Methods Given the large variety of applied methodologies, types of applications, and scientific disciplines involved in ECA research, we conducted a systematic scoping review. Scoping reviews aim to map key concepts and types of evidence underlying an area of research, and answer less-specific questions than traditional systematic reviews. Systematic searches for ECA applications in the treatment of mood, anxiety, psychotic, autism spectrum, and substance use disorders were conducted in databases in the fields of psychology and computer science, as well as in interdisciplinary databases. Studies were included if they conveyed primary research findings on an ECA application that targeted one of the disorders. We mapped each study's background information, how the different disorders were addressed, how ECAs and users could interact with one another, methodological aspects, and the study's aims and outcomes. Results This study included N=54 publications (N=49 studies). More than half of the studies (n=26) focused on autism treatment, and ECAs were used most often for social skills training (n=23). Applications ranged from simple reinforcement of social behaviors through emotional expressions to sophisticated multimodal conversational systems. Most applications (n=43) were still in the development and piloting phase, that is, not yet ready for routine practice evaluation or application. Few studies conducted controlled research into clinical effects of ECAs, such as a reduction in symptom severity. Conclusions ECAs for mental disorders are emerging. State-of-the-art techniques, involving, for example, communication through natural language or nonverbal behavior, are increasingly being considered and adopted for psychotherapeutic interventions in ECA research with promising results. However, evidence on their clinical application remains scarce. At present, their value to clinical practice lies mostly in the experimental determination of critical human support factors. In the context of using ECAs as an adjunct to existing interventions with the aim of supporting users, important questions remain with regard to the personalization of ECAs' interaction with users, and the optimal timing and manner of providing support. To increase the evidence base with regard to Internet interventions, we propose an additional focus on low-tech ECA solutions that can be rapidly developed, tested, and applied in routine practice.

sheet.es: Si te ofrecen una aplicación con un personaje virtual que «enseña habilidades sociales», puedes verla como algo experimental, no como un tratamiento probado. Si la probáis, observa si tu hijo o hija la disfruta, si se siente cómodo y si le aporta algo en su propia vida, sin presión por cambiar su forma natural de comunicarse. Esta revisión de alcance reunió 49 estudios sobre agentes conversacionales virtuales en salud mental; más de la mitad trataban sobre personas autistas, sobre todo entrenamiento social. Su límite: la mayoría eran prototipos en fase piloto y casi ningún estudio comparó resultados de forma controlada, así que aún no sabemos si ayudan ni a quién.
sheet.en: If you are offered an app with a virtual character that "teaches social skills", treat it as experimental, not a proven treatment. If you try it, notice whether your child enjoys it, feels comfortable, and gains something meaningful in their own life, without pressure to change their natural way of communicating. This scoping review gathered 49 studies on virtual conversational agents in mental health; more than half involved autistic people, mostly for social training. Its limit: most were prototypes still in pilot stages, and very few studies tested outcomes in a controlled way, so we do not yet know whether they help, or whom.
sheet.sv: Om du erbjuds en app med en virtuell figur som ”lär ut sociala färdigheter” kan du se den som något experimentellt, inte en beprövad behandling. Om ni testar den, lägg märke till om ditt barn tycker om den, känner sig bekvämt och får ut något meningsfullt i sitt eget liv, utan press att ändra sitt naturliga sätt att kommunicera. Denna översikt samlade 49 studier om virtuella samtalsagenter inom psykisk hälsa; över hälften gällde autistiska personer, främst social träning. Begränsning: de flesta var prototyper i pilotfas och mycket få studier jämförde resultat kontrollerat, så vi vet ännu inte om de hjälper, eller vem.

title: Autism Spectrum Disorder in Anorexia Nervosa: An Updated Literature Review.
authors: Westwood H, Tchanturia K
abstract: Purpose of review There is growing interest in the relationship between anorexia nervosa (AN) and autism spectrum disorder (ASD). This review aimed to synthesise the most recent research on this topic to identify gaps in current knowledge, directions for future research and reflect on implications for treatment. Recent findings Eight studies assessing the presence of ASD in AN were identified in the literature along with three studies examining the impact of symptoms of ASD on treatment outcome. Research with young people and using parental-report measures suggest lower rates of co-morbidity than previous adult studies. Conclusions The wide range of diagnostic tools, methodologies and populations studied make it difficult to determine the prevalence of ASD in AN. Despite this, studies consistently report over-representation of symptoms of ASD in AN. Co-morbid AN and ASD may require more intensive treatment or specifically tailored interventions. Future longitudinal research and female-specific diagnostic tools would help elucidate the relationship between these two disorders.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista tiene dificultades con la alimentación o un diagnóstico de anorexia, conviene que el equipo de tratamiento conozca su perfil autista y adapte el apoyo, por ejemplo con apoyos más específicos o intensivos. Se trata de una revisión sistemática: reunió ocho estudios sobre la presencia de autismo en la anorexia y tres sobre cómo influyen los rasgos autistas en el tratamiento. Los estudios usaron herramientas y poblaciones muy distintas, así que no se puede saber con qué frecuencia coinciden ambas condiciones. No es una regla para todas las personas; las decisiones sobre el tratamiento corresponden a profesionales sanitarios.
sheet.en: If an autistic person has eating difficulties or an anorexia diagnosis, it helps when the treatment team knows about their autistic profile and adapts support, for example with more specific or more intensive approaches. This is a systematic review: it gathered eight studies on autism in anorexia and three on how autistic traits affect treatment. The studies used very different tools and populations, so how often the two occur together cannot be determined. It is not a rule for every person, and treatment decisions belong with health professionals.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person har svårigheter med ätandet eller diagnosen anorexi hjälper det när vårdteamet känner till personens autistiska profil och anpassar stödet, till exempel med mer riktade eller mer intensiva insatser. Det här är en systematisk översikt: den samlade åtta studier om autism vid anorexi och tre om hur autistiska drag påverkar behandlingen. Studierna använde mycket olika verktyg och grupper, så det går inte att fastställa hur ofta de två förekommer tillsammans. Det är ingen regel för alla, och behandlingsbeslut fattas tillsammans med vårdpersonal.

title: Challenges and opportunities to improve autism services in low-income countries: lessons from a situational analysis in Ethiopia.
authors: Tekola B, Baheretibeb Y, Roth I, Tilahun D, Fekadu A, Hanlon C, Hoekstra RA
abstract: Background Little has been reported about service provision for children with autism in low-income countries. This study explored the current service provision for children with autism and their families in Ethiopia, the existing challenges and urgent needs, and stakeholders' views on the best approaches to further develop services. Methods A situational analysis was conducted based on (i) qualitative interviews with existing service providers; (ii) consultation with a wider group of stakeholders through two stakeholder workshops; and (iii) information available in the public domain. Findings were triangulated where possible. Results Existing diagnostic and educational services for children with autism are scarce and largely confined to Ethiopia's capital city, with little provision in rural areas. Families of children with autism experience practical and psychosocial challenges, including severe stigma. Informants further raised the lack of culturally and contextually appropriate autism instruments as an important problem to be addressed. The study informants and local stakeholders provided several approaches for future service provision expansion, including service decentralisation, mental health training and awareness raising initiatives. Conclusions Services for children with autism in Ethiopia are extremely limited; appropriate care for these children is further impeded by stigma and lack of awareness. Ethiopia's plans to scale up mental healthcare integrated into primary care provide an opportunity to expand services for children with autism and other developmental disorders. These plans, together with the additional strategies outlined in this paper can help to address the current service provision gaps and may also inform service enhancement approaches in other low-income countries.

sheet.es: Si vives en un lugar con pocos servicios, buscar a otras familias, hablar con tu centro de salud local y pedir información sobre autismo puede ayudar a que tu entorno entienda mejor a tu hijo o hija autista. Este estudio fue un análisis de la situación en Etiopía, con entrevistas a profesionales y dos talleres con distintos actores. Encontró que los servicios de diagnóstico y educación son escasos y se concentran en la capital, y que las familias afrontan un fuerte estigma. Sus límites: describe un solo país y no prueba qué intervención funciona, así que no sirve como regla para cada familia.
sheet.en: If you live where services are scarce, connecting with other families, talking with your local health centre and asking for information about autism can help the people around your autistic child understand them better. This study was a situational analysis in Ethiopia, using interviews with service providers and two stakeholder workshops. It found that diagnostic and educational services are scarce and mostly in the capital, and that families face severe stigma. Its limits: it describes one country and does not test which support works, so it is not a rule for every family.
sheet.sv: Om du bor där det finns få tjänster kan det hjälpa att få kontakt med andra familjer, prata med din lokala vårdcentral och be om information om autism, så att omgivningen förstår ditt autistiska barn bättre. Studien var en lägesanalys i Etiopien med intervjuer med vårdgivare och två workshoppar med olika intressenter. Den fann att utrednings- och utbildningstjänster är få och oftast finns i huvudstaden, och att familjer möter svårt stigma. Begränsningar: den beskriver bara ett land och testar inte vilket stöd som fungerar, så den är ingen regel för varje familj.

title: Prader-Willi Syndrome and Schaaf-Yang Syndrome: Neurodevelopmental Diseases Intersecting at the MAGEL2 Gene.
authors: Fountain MD, Schaaf CP
abstract: Prader-Willi syndrome (PWS) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by neonatal hypotonia, developmental delay/intellectual disability, and characteristic feeding behaviors with failure to thrive during infancy; followed by hyperphagia and excessive weight gain later in childhood. Individuals with PWS also manifest complex behavioral phenotypes. Approximately 25% meet criteria for autism spectrum disorder (ASD). PWS is caused by the absence of paternally expressed, maternally silenced genes at chromosome 15q11-q13. MAGEL2 is one of five protein-coding genes in the PWS-critical domain. Truncating point mutations of the paternal allele of MAGEL2 cause Schaaf-Yang syndrome, which has significant phenotypic overlap with PWS, but is also clinically distinct; based on the presence of joint contractures, and a particularly high prevalence of autism spectrum disorder (up to 75% of affected individuals). The clinical and molecular overlap between PWS and Schaaf-Yang syndrome, but also their distinguishing features provide insight into the pathogenetic mechanisms underlying both disorders.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona con síndrome de Prader-Willi o de Schaaf-Yang, conviene saber que ambos pueden ir acompañados de autismo, y que apoyos de alimentación, desarrollo y comunicación se planifican con su equipo clínico. Esta es una revisión que reúne conocimiento previo; indica que aproximadamente el 25% de las personas con Prader-Willi cumple criterios de autismo, y hasta el 75% en Schaaf-Yang. Sus límites: es una revisión centrada en genética, no prueba qué apoyos funcionan y no describe a cada persona.
sheet.en: If you support someone with Prader-Willi or Schaaf-Yang syndrome, it helps to know that either can come with autism, and that feeding, developmental and communication supports are best planned with their clinical team. This is a review that gathers existing knowledge; it reports that approximately 25% of people with Prader-Willi meet criteria for autism, and up to 75% in Schaaf-Yang. Its limits: it focuses on genetics, does not test which supports work, and cannot describe any one person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en person med Prader-Willis eller Schaaf-Yangs syndrom är det bra att veta att båda kan förekomma tillsammans med autism, och att stöd kring mat, utveckling och kommunikation bäst planeras med personens vårdteam. Detta är en översikt som sammanställer befintlig kunskap; den anger att ungefär 25% av personer med Prader-Willi uppfyller kriterier för autism, och upp till 75% vid Schaaf-Yang. Begränsningar: den fokuserar på genetik, testar inte vilket stöd som fungerar och kan inte beskriva en enskild person.

title: Autism spectrum disorder in the scope of tactile processing.
authors: Mikkelsen M, Wodka EL, Mostofsky SH, Puts NAJ
abstract: Sensory processing abnormalities are among the most common behavioral phenotypes seen in autism spectrum disorder (ASD), typically characterized by either over- or under-responsiveness to stimulation. In this review, we focus on tactile processing dysfunction in ASD. We firstly review clinical studies wherein sensitivity to tactile stimuli has traditionally been assessed by self-, parent- and experimenter-reports. We also discuss recent investigations using psychophysical paradigms that gauge individual tactile thresholds. These more experimentally rigorous studies allow for more objective assessments of tactile abnormalities in ASD. However, little is understood about the neurobiological mechanisms underlying these abnormalities, or the link between tactile abnormalities and ASD symptoms. Neurobiological research that has been conducted has pointed toward dysfunction in the excitation/inhibition balance of the central nervous system of those with ASD. This review covers recent efforts that have investigated tactile dysfunction in ASD from clinical and behavioral perspectives, and some of the efforts to link these to neurobiology. On the whole, findings are inconsistent, which can be ascribed to the subjectivity of clinical assessments, the heterogeneity of ASD cohorts, and the diversity of tactile sensitivity measures. Future endeavors into understanding tactile processing differences in ASD will greatly benefit from controlled experiments driven by neurobiological hypotheses.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista reacciona de forma intensa o muy poco al tacto (ropa, etiquetas, abrazos, lavarse el pelo), tómalo como información real sobre su experiencia y pregúntale, o observa, qué le resulta cómodo. Esta es una revisión de estudios sobre el procesamiento del tacto en autismo, que combina informes de la propia persona, de familiares y de investigadores con pruebas de umbrales táctiles. Los resultados son inconsistentes: las evaluaciones son subjetivas, los grupos son muy diversos y las medidas varían. Por eso no sirve como regla para cada persona, y se sabe poco de las causas biológicas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person reacts strongly to touch, or hardly at all (clothing, labels, hugs, hair washing), treat it as real information about their experience, and ask or observe what feels comfortable. This is a review of studies on touch processing in autism, combining reports from the person, family members and researchers with tests of tactile thresholds. Findings are inconsistent: assessments are subjective, groups are very diverse and measures differ. So it is not a rule for every person, and little is known about the biological causes.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person reagerar starkt på beröring, eller knappt alls (kläder, etiketter, kramar, hårtvätt), se det som verklig information om hens upplevelse och fråga eller observera vad som känns bekvämt. Detta är en översikt av studier om beröringsbearbetning vid autism, som kombinerar rapporter från personen själv, anhöriga och forskare med tester av taktila trösklar. Resultaten är inkonsekventa: bedömningarna är subjektiva, grupperna är mycket varierade och måtten skiljer sig. Den är därför ingen regel för varje person, och man vet lite om de biologiska orsakerna.

title: Binocular rivalry in children on the autism spectrum.
authors: Karaminis T, Lunghi C, Neil L, Burr D, Pellicano E
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: When different images are presented to the eyes, the brain is faced with ambiguity, causing perceptual bistability: visual perception continuously alternates between the monocular images, a phenomenon called binocular rivalry. Many models of rivalry suggest that its temporal dynamics depend on mutual inhibition among neurons representing competing images. These models predict that rivalry should be different in autism, which has been proposed to present an atypical ratio of excitation and inhibition [the E/I imbalance hypothesis; Rubenstein & Merzenich, 2003]. In line with this prediction, some recent studies have provided evidence for atypical binocular rivalry dynamics in autistic adults. In this study, we examined if these findings generalize to autistic children. We developed a child-friendly binocular rivalry paradigm, which included two types of stimuli, low- and high-complexity, and compared rivalry dynamics in groups of autistic and age- and intellectual ability-matched typical children. Unexpectedly, the two groups of children presented the same number of perceptual transitions and the same mean phase durations (times perceiving one of the two stimuli). Yet autistic children reported mixed percepts for a shorter proportion of time (a difference which was in the opposite direction to previous adult studies), while elevated autistic symptomatology was associated with shorter mixed perception periods. Rivalry in the two groups was affected similarly by stimulus type, and consistent with previous findings. Our results suggest that rivalry dynamics are differentially affected in adults and developing autistic children and could be accounted for by hierarchical models of binocular rivalry, including both inhibition and top-down influences. Autism Res 2017. ©2017 The Authors Autism Research published by Wiley Periodicals, Inc. on behalf of International Society for Autism Research Autism Res 2017, 10: 1096-1106. © 2017 International Society for Autism Research, Wiley Periodicals, Inc.

sheet.es: Tomorrow no hace falta cambiar nada: este estudio no ofrece consejos para la rutina diaria. Sugiere que la forma de ver cuando cada ojo recibe una imagen distinta puede ser parecida en niñas y niños autistas y no autistas, con diferencias pequeñas. Si le preocupa la visión de su criatura, consulte a un profesional de la salud. Es un estudio de investigación con niños autistas y niños no autistas de edad y capacidad intelectual similares. Sus límites: es una tarea de laboratorio, no muestra cómo ve cada niño en la vida diaria y no sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: Nothing needs to change tomorrow: this study gives no advice for daily routines. It suggests that the way of seeing when each eye receives a different image can be similar in autistic and non-autistic children, with some small differences. If you have concerns about your child's vision, talk with a health professional. This was a research study with autistic children and non-autistic children matched for age and intellectual ability. Its limits: it was a lab task, it does not show how any one child sees in daily life, and it is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Inget behöver ändras i morgon: studien ger inga råd för vardagen. Den tyder på att sättet att se när varje öga får en olika bild kan vara likartat hos autistiska och icke-autistiska barn, med några små skillnader. Om du är orolig för ditt barns syn, prata med vårdpersonal. Det var en forskningsstudie med autistiska barn och icke-autistiska barn som matchats efter ålder och intellektuell förmåga. Begränsningar: det var en laboratorieuppgift, den visar inte hur ett enskilt barn ser i vardagen och är ingen regel för alla.

title: Moderating Effects of Parental Characteristics on the Effectiveness of a Theory of Mind Training for Children with Autism: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
authors: de Veld DMJ, Howlin P, Hoddenbach E, Mulder F, Wolf I, Koot HM, Lindauer R, Begeer S
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: This RCT investigated whether the effect of a Theory of Mind (ToM) intervention for children with ASD was moderated by parental education level and employment, family structure, and parental ASD. Children with autism aged 8-13 years (n = 136) were randomized over a waitlist control or treatment condition. At posttest, children in the treatment condition had more ToM knowledge, showed fewer autistic features, and more ToM-related behavior than children in the control condition. Children who had one or two parents with at least a college degree, and children with parents not diagnosed with/suspected of having ASD themselves benefitted from the training. These findings provide valuable information about family variables that need to be taken into account in treatment design and implementation.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija va a hacer un programa para entender pensamientos y emociones ajenos (teoría de la mente), conviene pensar en el apoyo que la familia necesita para acompañarlo, porque el contexto familiar puede influir. Es un ensayo aleatorizado con 136 niños autistas de 8-13 años, asignados a entrenamiento o lista de espera. Tras el entrenamiento, el grupo tratado mostró más conocimiento de teoría de la mente y más conductas relacionadas. Los beneficios aparecieron en niños con al menos un progenitor con título universitario y con progenitores sin diagnóstico ni sospecha de autismo. Es un solo estudio y no significa que el programa no sirva a otras familias ni que valga igual para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If your child is going to take part in a programme about understanding other people's thoughts and feelings (theory of mind), think about what support your family may need to take part, because family context may matter. This was a randomized trial with 136 autistic children aged 8-13, assigned to training or a waitlist. After training, the treated group showed more theory of mind knowledge and more related behaviour. Benefits appeared in children with at least one parent with a college degree, and whose parents had no diagnosis or suspicion of autism. It is a single study, so it does not mean the programme cannot help other families, or that it fits every person.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn ska delta i ett program om att förstå andras tankar och känslor (theory of mind), fundera på vilket stöd din familj kan behöva, eftersom familjens situation kan spela roll. Det var en randomiserad studie med 136 autistiska barn i åldern 8-13, fördelade till träning eller väntelista. Efter träningen visade den behandlade gruppen mer kunskap om theory of mind och mer relaterat beteende. Nyttan syntes hos barn där minst en förälder hade högskoleexamen och där föräldrarna inte hade en autismdiagnos eller misstanke om autism. Det är en enskild studie, så den visar inte att programmet inte kan hjälpa andra familjer, och det passar inte alla.

title: Anxiety Levels in Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Meta-Analysis.
authors: van Steensel FJA, Heeman EJ
journal: Journal of child and family studies
abstract: The aim of the current study was to meta-analytically examine whether anxiety levels in children with autism spectrum disorders (ASD) are elevated. A total of 83 articles were selected from a systematic literature search and were included in the meta-analyses. Results demonstrated that children with ASD had higher anxiety levels compared to typically developing children, and this difference increased with IQ. Youth with ASD also tended to have higher anxiety levels compared to clinically referred children, and this difference increased with age. Children with ASD had higher anxiety levels compared to youth with externalizing or developmental problems, but not when compared to youth with internalizing problems. The study findings highlight the importance of more research in order to fully understand the nature and development of anxiety in children with ASD. More specifically, the results suggest that especially high-functioning adolescents with ASD may be at risk for developing anxiety disorders. Therefore, it seems important to carefully follow and monitor children with ASD transcending to adolescence.

sheet.es: Conviene prestar atención al bienestar emocional de niñas, niños y jóvenes autistas, y observar con calma señales de ansiedad, sobre todo al llegar a la adolescencia. Hablar del tema con la persona y con su equipo de apoyo puede ayudar. La evidencia es un metaanálisis que reunió 83 artículos: la ansiedad fue mayor en la infancia autista que en niños con desarrollo típico, y la diferencia aumentaba con el CI. Es un promedio de grupos, no describe a cada persona, y los autores piden más investigación para entender cómo surge y se desarrolla la ansiedad.
sheet.en: It is worth paying calm attention to the emotional wellbeing of autistic children and young people, and noticing signs of anxiety, especially as they move into adolescence. Talking about it with the person and their support team can help. The evidence is a meta-analysis that combined 83 articles: anxiety was higher in autistic children than in typically developing children, and the gap grew with IQ. These are group averages, not a description of every person, and the authors call for more research on how anxiety develops.
sheet.sv: Det är värt att med lugn uppmärksamma autistiska barns och ungas känslomässiga mående och lägga märke till tecken på ångest, särskilt när de närmar sig tonåren. Det kan hjälpa att prata om det med personen och stödteamet. Underlaget är en metaanalys som sammanställde 83 artiklar: ångesten var högre hos autistiska barn än hos barn med typisk utveckling, och skillnaden ökade med IQ. Det är gruppgenomsnitt och beskriver inte varje person, och forskarna efterlyser mer forskning om hur ångest uppstår och utvecklas.

title: Siblings of Children with Autism: the Siblings Embedded Systems Framework.
authors: Kovshoff H, Cebula K, Tsai HJ, Hastings RP
abstract: Purpose of review A range of interacting factors/mechanisms at the individual, family, and wider systems levels influences siblings living in families where one sibling has autism. We introduce the Sibling Embedded Systems Framework which aims to contextualise siblings' experience and characterise the multiple and interacting factors influencing family and, in particular, sibling outcomes. Recent findings Findings from studies that have reported outcomes for siblings of children with autism are equivocal, ranging from negative impact, no difference, to positive experience. This is likely due to the complex nature of understanding the sibling experience. We focus on particular elements of the framework and review recent novel literature to help guide future directions for research and practice including the influence of culture, methodological considerations, and wider participatory methods. Summary The Siblings Embedded System Framework can be used to understand interactive factors that affect sibling adjustment and to develop clinically, educationally and empirically based work that aims to enhance and support sibling adjustment, relationships, and well-being in families of children with autism.

sheet.es: Si tienes un hijo autista y otros hijos, no hay una sola forma «normal» de vivir ser hermano. Algunos hermanos lo viven como algo positivo, otros no notan diferencia y otros necesitan más apoyo. Mañana puedes preguntar a cada hermano cómo está, reservar un rato a solas con él y fijarte también en lo que ayuda: la escuela, la familia extensa, la cultura y los recursos cercanos. Es una revisión que propone un marco para entender cómo interactúan factores individuales, familiares y sociales en los hermanos de niños autistas. Su límite: no aporta datos nuevos y los estudios que revisa muestran resultados contradictorios, así que no es una regla para cada familia.
sheet.en: If you have an autistic child and other children, there is no single "normal" way to experience being a sibling. Some siblings find it positive, some notice little difference, and some need more support. Tomorrow you could ask each sibling how they are doing, set aside a little one-to-one time, and notice what helps around them: school, extended family, culture and local resources. This is a review proposing a framework for how individual, family and wider social factors interact for siblings of autistic children. Its limit: it offers no new data, and the studies it reviews show mixed results, so it is not a rule for every family.
sheet.sv: Om du har ett autistiskt barn och andra barn finns det inget enda ”normalt” sätt att vara syskon på. En del syskon upplever det som positivt, en del märker ingen skillnad och en del behöver mer stöd. I morgon kan du fråga varje syskon hur hen mår, avsätta lite egen tid tillsammans och lägga märke till vad som hjälper runt omkring: skolan, släkten, kulturen och resurser i närheten. Det här är en översikt som föreslår en modell för hur individuella, familjära och samhälleliga faktorer samspelar för syskon till autistiska barn. Begränsning: den bidrar inte med nya data och de granskade studierna visar blandade resultat, så den är ingen regel för varje familj.

title: Pivotal response treatment for autism spectrum disorder: current perspectives.
authors: Lei J, Ventola P
abstract: Pivotal response treatment (PRT) is an evidence-based behavioral intervention based on applied behavior analysis principles aimed to improve social communication skills in individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). PRT adopts a more naturalistic approach and focuses on using a number of strategies to help increase children's motivation during intervention. Since its conceptualization, PRT has received much empirical support for eliciting therapeutic gains in greater use of functional social communication skills in individuals with ASD. Building upon the empirical evidence supporting PRT, recent advancements have increasingly turned to using interdisciplinary research integrating neuroimaging techniques and behavioral measures to help identify objective biomarkers of treatment, which have two primary purposes. First, neuroimaging results can help characterize how PRT may elicit change, and facilitate partitioning of the heterogeneous profiles of neural mechanisms underlying similar profile of behavioral changes observed over PRT. Second, neuroimaging provides an objective means to both map and track how biomarkers may serve as reliable and sensitive predictors of responder profiles to PRT, assisting clinicians to identify who will most likely benefit from PRT. Together, a better understanding of both mechanisms of change and predictors of responder profile will help PRT to serve as a more precise and targeted intervention for individuals with ASD, thus moving towards the goal of precision medicine and improving quality of care. This review focuses on the recent emerging neuroimaging evidences supporting PRT, offering current perspectives on the importance of interdisciplinary research to help clinicians better understand how PRT works and predict who will respond to PRT.

sheet.es: Si valoráis apoyos para la comunicación social, podéis preguntar a un profesional cómo trabaja la terapia de respuesta pivotal (PRT): usa situaciones naturales y busca aumentar la motivación de la niña o el niño, y conviene que respete sus intereses y su ritmo. La evidencia es una revisión que resume estudios sobre PRT y trabajos recientes de neuroimagen para entender cómo actúa y quién podría beneficiarse. Sus límites: no es un estudio con un grupo concreto de participantes, la neuroimagen aún es emergente y no puede predecir con seguridad qué le irá bien a cada persona autista.
sheet.en: If you are considering support for social communication, you can ask a professional how pivotal response treatment (PRT) works: it uses natural everyday situations and aims to build a child's motivation, and it should respect their interests and pace. The evidence is a review summarising studies of PRT and recent brain imaging work on how it may work and who might benefit. Its limits: it is not a single study with its own participants, the imaging research is still emerging, and it cannot reliably predict what will suit each autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om ni överväger stöd för social kommunikation kan ni fråga en yrkesperson hur pivotal response treatment (PRT) fungerar: den bygger på naturliga vardagssituationer och försöker öka barnets motivation, och den bör respektera barnets intressen och tempo. Underlaget är en översikt som sammanfattar studier om PRT och ny hjärnavbildningsforskning om hur den kan verka och vem som kan ha nytta av den. Begränsningar: det är inte en enskild studie med egna deltagare, hjärnavbildningen är fortfarande ny och kan inte säkert förutsäga vad som passar varje autistisk person.

title: Maternal smoking and autism spectrum disorder: meta-analysis with population smoking metrics as moderators.
authors: Jung Y, Lee AM, McKee SA, Picciotto MR
abstract: While exposure to nicotine during developmental periods can significantly affect brain development, studies examining the association between maternal smoking and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in offspring have produced conflicting findings, and prior meta-analyses have found no significant association. Our meta-analysis used a novel approach of investigating population-level smoking metrics as moderators. The main meta-analysis, with 22 observational studies comprising 795,632 cases and 1,829,256 control participants, used a random-effects model to find no significant association between maternal smoking during pregnancy and ASD in offspring (pooled odds ratio (OR) = 1.16, 95% CI: 0.97-1.40). However, meta-regression analyses with moderators were significant when we matched pooled ORs with adult male smoking prevalence (z = 2.55, p = 0.01) in each country, using World Health Organization data. Our study shows that using population-level smoking metrics uncovers significant relationships between maternal smoking and ASD risk. Correlational analyses show that male smoking prevalence approximates secondhand smoke exposure. While we cannot exclude the possibility that our findings reflect the role of paternal or postnatal nicotine exposure, as opposed to maternal or in utero nicotine exposure, this study underlines the importance of investigating paternal and secondhand smoking in addition to maternal smoking in ASD.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista o estás embarazada, no hay una conclusión firme de que fumar durante el embarazo cause autismo; hablar con el equipo de salud sobre cómo reducir el humo del tabaco en casa es una medida general de cuidado. Es un metaanálisis de 22 estudios observacionales, con 795.632 casos y 1.829.256 controles; no halló una asociación significativa (OR = 1,16, IC 95 %: 0,97-1,40). Al usar la prevalencia de fumadores varones por país, sí apareció una relación. Sus límites: son estudios observacionales, que no prueban causa, y no distingue entre humo paterno, secundario o posnatal. No aplica a cada persona.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic person or are pregnant, there is no firm conclusion that smoking in pregnancy causes autism; talking with your health team about reducing tobacco smoke at home is a general caring step. This is a meta-analysis of 22 observational studies, with 795,632 cases and 1,829,256 controls; it found no significant association (OR = 1.16, 95% CI: 0.97-1.40). Using male smoking prevalence by country, a relationship did appear. Limits: observational studies cannot prove cause, and it cannot separate paternal, secondhand or postnatal smoke. It does not apply to every person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person eller är gravid finns ingen säker slutsats att rökning under graviditeten orsakar autism; att prata med vårdteamet om hur man minskar tobaksrök hemma är en allmän omsorgsåtgärd. Det här är en metaanalys av 22 observationsstudier, med 795 632 fall och 1 829 256 kontroller; den fann ingen signifikant koppling (OR = 1,16, 95 % KI: 0,97-1,40). När man använde andelen manliga rökare per land syntes ett samband. Begränsningar: observationsstudier kan inte bevisa orsak, och de kan inte skilja mellan pappans rökning, passiv rökning eller rök efter födseln. Det gäller inte alla personer.

title: Vagus nerve stimulation as a potential adjuvant to behavioral therapy for autism and other neurodevelopmental disorders.
authors: Engineer CT, Hays SA, Kilgard MP
abstract: Background Many children with autism and other neurodevelopmental disorders undergo expensive, time-consuming behavioral interventions that often yield only modest improvements. The development of adjunctive interventions that can increase the benefit of rehabilitation therapies is essential in order to improve the lives of individuals with neurodevelopmental disorders. Main text Vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) is an FDA approved therapy that is safe and effective in reducing seizure frequency and duration in individuals with epilepsy. Individuals with neurodevelopmental disorders often exhibit decreased vagal tone, and studies indicate that VNS can be used to overcome an insufficient vagal response. Multiple studies have also documented significant improvements in quality of life after VNS therapy in individuals with neurodevelopmental disorders. Moreover, recent findings indicate that VNS significantly enhances the benefits of rehabilitative training in animal models and patients, leading to greater recovery in a variety of neurological diseases. Here, we review these findings and provide a discussion of how VNS paired with rehabilitation may yield benefits in the context of neurodevelopmental disorders. Conclusions VNS paired with behavioral therapy may represent a potential new approach to enhance rehabilitation that could significantly improve the outcomes of individuals with neurodevelopmental disorders.

sheet.es: Por ahora no hay nada que cambiar mañana en casa: esta revisión plantea una idea para el futuro, no una recomendación. Si os interesa, podéis comentarla con el equipo clínico. Es una revisión de estudios previos, con trabajos en animales y en personas con epilepsia u otras condiciones neurológicas. Plantea que estimular el nervio vago junto con terapia conductual podría mejorar sus resultados. Es un procedimiento médico, y las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico. Como revisión, no prueba que funcione en personas autistas, y no todas querrían o necesitarían este enfoque.
sheet.en: There is nothing to change at home tomorrow: this review sets out an idea for the future, not a recommendation. If it interests you, you can raise it with your clinical team. It is a review of earlier studies, including work in animals and in people with epilepsy or other neurological conditions. It suggests that vagus nerve stimulation alongside behavioral therapy might improve its results. This is a medical approach, and medical decisions belong to a clinician. As a review, it does not show that this works for autistic people, and not everyone would want or need this approach.
sheet.sv: Det finns inget att ändra hemma i morgon: den här översikten presenterar en idé för framtiden, inte en rekommendation. Om den intresserar er kan ni ta upp den med det kliniska teamet. Det är en översikt av tidigare studier, bland annat på djur och på personer med epilepsi eller andra neurologiska tillstånd. Den antyder att stimulering av vagusnerven tillsammans med beteendeterapi kanske kan ge bättre resultat. Det är en medicinsk metod, och medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker. Som översikt visar den inte att metoden fungerar för autistiska personer, och inte alla skulle vilja eller behöva den.

title: A self-affirmation exercise does not improve intentions to vaccinate among parents with negative vaccine attitudes (and may decrease intentions to vaccinate).
authors: Reavis RD, Ebbs JB, Onunkwo AK, Sage LM
abstract: Two studies investigated the effectiveness of a self-affirmation exercise on vaccine safety beliefs and intent to vaccinate future children. In Study 1, a sample of 585 parents with at least one child under the age of 18 in the home participated through Amazon's MTurk. Participants were randomly assigned to one of four conditions in a 2 x 2 design. Participants read either correcting information refuting a link between the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine and autism or a control passage about bird feeding. Additionally, participants either completed a self-affirmation exercise where they reflected on their personal values or in a control condition in which they reflected on least-personally-important values that might be important to others. Participants exposed to the correcting information were less likely to believe that vaccines cause serious side effects, but no less likely to believe that the MMR vaccine causes autism. For parents with initially positive vaccine attitudes, there was no effect of condition on intent to vaccinate a future child. For parents with initially negative vaccine attitudes, self-affirmation was ineffective in the presence of correcting information and resulted in less intention to vaccinate in the absence of correcting information. This effect was partially replicated in Study 2 (N = 576), which provided no correcting information but otherwise followed the same procedure as Study 1.

sheet.es: Si hablas con otras familias sobre vacunas, conviene saber que pedir a alguien que reflexione sobre sus valores personales no mejoró la intención de vacunar en padres y madres con actitudes previas negativas, y pudo reducirla. Las decisiones de salud se hablan con un profesional sanitario. La evidencia son dos estudios aleatorizados en línea con 585 y 576 progenitores de niños menores de 18 años. Límites: fue una encuesta en internet, midió intenciones y no conductas reales, y el segundo estudio solo replicó el efecto en parte. No sirve como regla para cada familia.
sheet.en: If you talk with other families about vaccines, it helps to know that asking people to reflect on their personal values did not improve intent to vaccinate among parents with negative vaccine attitudes, and may have lowered it. Health decisions are best discussed with a health professional. The evidence is two randomised online studies with 585 and 576 parents of children under 18. Limits: it was an internet survey, measured intentions rather than real actions, and the second study only partly replicated the effect. It is not a rule for every family.
sheet.sv: Om du pratar med andra familjer om vaccin är det bra att veta att en övning där man reflekterar över sina personliga värderingar inte förbättrade viljan att vaccinera hos föräldrar med negativa attityder till vaccin, och kan ha minskat den. Hälsobeslut bör diskuteras med vårdpersonal. Underlaget är två randomiserade nätstudier med 585 och 576 föräldrar till barn under 18 år. Begränsningar: det var en webbenkät, den mätte avsikter snarare än verkliga handlingar, och den andra studien replikerade effekten bara delvis. Det är ingen regel för alla familjer.

title: "Putting on My Best Normal": Social Camouflaging in Adults with Autism Spectrum Conditions.
authors: Hull L, Petrides KV, Allison C, Smith P, Baron-Cohen S, Lai MC, Mandy W
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Camouflaging of autistic characteristics in social situations is hypothesised as a common social coping strategy for adults with autism spectrum conditions (ASC). Camouflaging may impact diagnosis, quality of life, and long-term outcomes, but little is known about it. This qualitative study examined camouflaging experiences in 92 adults with ASC, with questions focusing on the nature, motivations, and consequences of camouflaging. Thematic analysis was used to identify key elements of camouflaging, which informed development of a three-stage model of the camouflaging process. First, motivations for camouflaging included fitting in and increasing connections with others. Second, camouflaging itself comprised a combination of masking and compensation techniques. Third, short- and long-term consequences of camouflaging included exhaustion, challenging stereotypes, and threats to self-perception.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista a tu cargo parece «estar bien» en público, puede estar camuflando: ocultando rasgos autistas o compensando con esfuerzo para encajar y conectar con otros. Esto puede dejarla agotada después y afectar cómo se ve a sí misma. Mañana, puedes ofrecer tiempo tranquilo tras situaciones sociales, preguntar sin presionar cómo le fue y dejar claro que en casa no necesita fingir. Este estudio cualitativo recogió las experiencias de 92 adultos autistas y propuso un modelo en tres etapas: motivos, técnicas y consecuencias. Sus límites: se basa en relatos personales de adultos y no mide cuánto camufla cada persona ni aplica igual a todos.
sheet.en: If an autistic person you support seems "fine" in public, they may be camouflaging: hiding autistic traits or working hard to compensate so they fit in and connect with others. This can leave them exhausted afterwards and affect how they see themselves. Tomorrow, you could offer quiet recovery time after social situations, gently ask how it went without pressure, and make clear that at home they don't need to pretend. This qualitative study gathered experiences from 92 autistic adults and proposed a three-stage model: motivations, techniques and consequences. Its limits: it relies on adults' self-reports, doesn't measure how much each person camouflages, and won't apply the same way to everyone.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person du stöttar verkar "må bra" bland andra kan hen kamouflera: dölja autistiska drag eller anstränga sig för att kompensera, för att passa in och få kontakt. Det kan leda till utmattning efteråt och påverka hur hen ser på sig själv. I morgon kan du erbjuda lugn återhämtningstid efter sociala situationer, varsamt fråga hur det gick utan press och visa att hen inte behöver låtsas hemma. Denna kvalitativa studie samlade erfarenheter från 92 autistiska vuxna och föreslog en modell i tre steg: motiv, tekniker och konsekvenser. Begränsningar: den bygger på vuxnas egna berättelser, mäter inte hur mycket var och en kamouflerar och gäller inte alla på samma sätt.

claim.es: Muchos adultos autistas, y en especial mujeres, camuflan sus rasgos para encajar; lo describen como agotador y con coste para la salud mental.
claim.en: Many autistic adults, especially women, camouflage their traits to fit in; they describe it as exhausting and costly for mental health.
claim.sv: Många autistiska vuxna, särskilt kvinnor, kamouflerar sina drag för att passa in; de beskriver det som utmattande och kostsamt för den psykiska hälsan.

supports.es: Permitir descanso y tiempo «sin máscara» en casa y en la escuela.
supports.en: Allowing rest and 'unmasked' time at home and school.
supports.sv: Att tillåta vila och tid «utan mask» hemma och i skolan.

doesNotSupport.es: Que el camuflaje sea solo un fenómeno femenino.
doesNotSupport.en: That camouflaging is only a female phenomenon.
doesNotSupport.sv: Att kamouflering bara är ett kvinnligt fenomen.

title: Typical versus delayed speech onset influences verbal reporting of autistic interests.
authors: Chiodo L, Majerus S, Mottron L
abstract: Background The distinction between autism and Asperger syndrome has been abandoned in the DSM-5. However, this clinical categorization largely overlaps with the presence or absence of a speech onset delay which is associated with clinical, cognitive, and neural differences. It is unknown whether these different speech development pathways and associated cognitive differences are involved in the heterogeneity of the restricted interests that characterize autistic adults. Method This study tested the hypothesis that speech onset delay, or conversely, early mastery of speech, orients the nature and verbal reporting of adult autistic interests. The occurrence of a priori defined descriptors for perceptual and thematic dimensions were determined, as well as the perceived function and benefits, in the response of autistic people to a semi-structured interview on their intense interests. The number of words, grammatical categories, and proportion of perceptual / thematic descriptors were computed and compared between groups by variance analyses. The participants comprised 40 autistic adults grouped according to the presence ( N = 20) or absence ( N = 20) of speech onset delay, as well as 20 non-autistic adults, also with intense interests, matched for non-verbal intelligence using Raven's Progressive Matrices. Results The overall nature, function, and benefit of intense interests were similar across autistic subgroups, and between autistic and non-autistic groups. However, autistic participants with a history of speech onset delay used more perceptual than thematic descriptors when talking about their interests, whereas the opposite was true for autistic individuals without speech onset delay. This finding remained significant after controlling for linguistic differences observed between the two groups. Conclusions Verbal reporting, but not the nature or positive function, of intense interests differed between adult autistic individuals depending on their speech acquisition history: oral reporting of intense interests was characterized by perceptual dominance for autistic individuals with delayed speech onset and thematic dominance for those without. This may contribute to the heterogeneous presentation observed among autistic adults of normal intelligence.

sheet.es: Cuando una persona autista hable de sus intereses intensos, escuche con curiosidad: puede describirlos de maneras distintas, y eso no dice nada sobre cuánto le importan. Algunas personas hablan más de sensaciones (cómo se ve, suena o se siente) y otras más de temas e ideas. Este ensayo con 40 adultos autistas (20 con retraso en el inicio del habla y 20 sin él) y 20 adultos no autistas encontró que la naturaleza, la función y los beneficios de los intereses eran parecidos entre grupos; solo cambiaba cómo los contaban. Es un estudio pequeño, solo con adultos, y no describe a cada persona.
sheet.en: When an autistic person talks about their intense interests, listen with curiosity: they may describe them in different ways, and that says nothing about how much the interests matter. Some people talk more about sensory details (how things look, sound or feel), others more about topics and ideas. This trial included 40 autistic adults (20 with delayed speech onset and 20 without) and 20 non-autistic adults. The nature, function and benefits of the interests were similar across groups; only the way they were described differed. It is a small study of adults only, and it does not describe every person.
sheet.sv: När en autistisk person pratar om sina intensiva intressen, lyssna nyfiket: hen kan beskriva dem på olika sätt, och det säger inget om hur viktiga de är. Vissa berättar mer om sinnesintryck (hur något ser ut, låter eller känns), andra mer om teman och idéer. Studien omfattade 40 autistiska vuxna (20 med försenad talstart och 20 utan) samt 20 icke-autistiska vuxna. Intressenas karaktär, funktion och nytta var likartade mellan grupperna; det var bara sättet att berätta som skilde sig. Det är en liten studie med enbart vuxna och den beskriver inte varje person.

title: Altered expression of histamine signaling genes in autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Wright C, Shin JH, Rajpurohit A, Deep-Soboslay A, Collado-Torres L, Brandon NJ, Hyde TM, Kleinman JE, Jaffe AE, Cross AJ, Weinberger DR
abstract: The histaminergic system (HS) has a critical role in cognition, sleep and other behaviors. Although not well studied in autism spectrum disorder (ASD), the HS is implicated in many neurological disorders, some of which share comorbidity with ASD, including Tourette syndrome (TS). Preliminary studies suggest that antagonism of histamine receptors 1-3 reduces symptoms and specific behaviors in ASD patients and relevant animal models. In addition, the HS mediates neuroinflammation, which may be heightened in ASD. Together, this suggests that the HS may also be altered in ASD. Using RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), we investigated genome-wide expression, as well as a focused gene set analysis of key HS genes (HDC, HNMT, HRH1, HRH2, HRH3 and HRH4) in postmortem dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) initially in 13 subjects with ASD and 39 matched controls. At the genome level, eight transcripts were differentially expressed (false discovery rate <0.05), six of which were small nucleolar RNAs (snoRNAs). There was no significant diagnosis effect on any of the individual HS genes but expression of the gene set of HNMT, HRH1, HRH2 and HRH3 was significantly altered. Curated HS gene sets were also significantly differentially expressed. Differential expression analysis of these gene sets in an independent RNA-seq ASD data set from DLPFC of 47 additional subjects confirmed these findings. Understanding the physiological relevance of an altered HS may suggest new therapeutic options for the treatment of ASD.

sheet.es: Este estudio no ofrece nada que hacer mañana por la mañana: es investigación básica sobre biología cerebral. Si te preocupan el sueño o la atención de una persona autista, observa qué la ayuda y coméntalo con su profesional de referencia. Las decisiones médicas corresponden siempre a un clínico. Evidencia: metaanálisis de expresión génica en tejido cerebral postmortem de la corteza prefrontal, con 13 personas autistas y 39 controles, y una confirmación en otro conjunto de datos con 47 personas más. Límites: son datos de laboratorio con muestras pequeñas, no prueban causas y no describen a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: This study offers nothing to do tomorrow morning: it is basic research on brain biology. If sleep or attention is a concern for an autistic person, notice what helps them and talk it over with their usual professional. Medical decisions belong to a clinician. Evidence: a meta-analysis of gene expression in postmortem brain tissue from the prefrontal cortex, with 13 autistic people and 39 controls, confirmed in another data set of 47 additional people. Limits: this is laboratory data with small samples, it does not show causes, and it does not describe every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Den här studien ger inget att göra i morgon bitti: det är grundforskning om hjärnans biologi. Om sömn eller uppmärksamhet oroar kring en autistisk person, notera vad som hjälper och prata med personens vanliga kontakt inom vården. Medicinska beslut hör hemma hos en läkare. Evidens: en metaanalys av genuttryck i hjärnvävnad efter döden från prefrontala cortex, med 13 autistiska personer och 39 kontroller, bekräftad i ett annat dataset med 47 ytterligare personer. Begränsningar: det är laboratoriedata med små urval, visar inte orsaker och beskriver inte alla autistiska personer.

title: Parent-Mediated Intervention Training Delivered Remotely for Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder Living Outside of Urban Areas: Systematic Review.
authors: Parsons D, Cordier R, Vaz S, Lee HC
abstract: Background Parent training programs for families living outside of urban areas can be used to improve the social behavior and communication skills in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). However, no review has been conducted to investigate these programs. Objective The aim of this study was to (1) systematically review the existing evidence presented by studies on parent-mediated intervention training, delivered remotely for parents having children with ASD and living outside of urban areas; (2) provide an overview of current parent training interventions used with this population; (3) and provide an overview of the method of delivery of the parent training interventions used with this population. Methods Guided by the preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses (PRISMA) statement, we conducted a comprehensive review across 5 electronic databases (CINAHL, Embase, ERIC, PsycINFO, and Pubmed) on July 4, 2016, searching for studies investigating parent-mediated intervention training for families living outside of urban centers who have a child diagnosed with ASD. Two independent researchers reviewed the articles for inclusion, and assessment of methodological quality was based on the Kmet appraisal checklist. Results Seven studies met the eligibility criteria, including 2 prepost cohort studies, 3 multiple baseline studies, and 2 randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Interventions included mostly self-guided websites: with and without therapist assistance (n=6), with training videos, written training manuals, and videoconferencing. Post intervention, studies reported significant improvements (P Conclusions There is preliminary evidence that parent-mediated intervention training delivered remotely may improve parent knowledge, increase parent intervention fidelity, and improve the social behavior and communication skills for children with ASD. A low number of RCTs, difficulty in defining the locality of the population, and a paucity of standardized measures limit the generalization of the findings to the target population. Future studies should investigate the appropriateness and feasibility of the interventions, include RCTs to control for bias, and utilize standard outcome measures.

sheet.es: Si vives lejos de la ciudad y de los servicios especializados, la formación online para familias puede ser una opción real: sitios web guiados, vídeos, manuales y videollamadas con profesionales pueden ayudarte a apoyar la comunicación y la interacción de tu hijo o hija autista en la rutina diaria, a tu ritmo y según lo que a tu hijo le funcione. Esta revisión sistemática reunió siete estudios con familias de zonas no urbanas; mostraron mejoras en el conocimiento de los padres y en la comunicación y conducta social de los niños. Sus límites: pocos ensayos aleatorizados, medidas poco estandarizadas y evidencia todavía preliminar.
sheet.en: If you live far from cities and specialist services, online training for families can be a real option: guided websites, videos, manuals and video calls with professionals may help you support your autistic child's communication and social connection within everyday routines, at your own pace and in ways that suit your child. This systematic review brought together seven studies with families living outside urban areas; they reported gains in parents' knowledge and in children's communication and social behaviour. Its limits: few randomised trials, little use of standardised measures, and evidence that is still preliminary.
sheet.sv: Om du bor långt från städer och specialistvård kan digital föräldrautbildning vara ett verkligt alternativ: guidade webbplatser, filmer, manualer och videosamtal med yrkespersoner kan hjälpa dig att stötta ditt autistiska barns kommunikation och samspel i vardagens rutiner, i din egen takt och på sätt som passar ditt barn. Denna systematiska översikt samlade sju studier med familjer utanför tätorter; de visade förbättringar i föräldrarnas kunskap och i barnens kommunikation och sociala samspel. Begränsningar: få randomiserade studier, få standardiserade mått och evidensen är fortfarande preliminär.

title: DSM-5 Changes in Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder and Autism Spectrum Disorder: Implications for Comorbid Sleep Issues.
authors: Ramtekkar UP
abstract: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) and Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) are the most common neurodevelopmental disorders. Despite significant comorbidity, the previous diagnostic criteria prohibited the simultaneous diagnosis of both disorders. Sleep problems are highly prevalent in both disorders; however, these have been studied independently for ADHD and ASD. In the context of revised criteria in the Diagnostic Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders 5th edition (DSM-5) that allows combined diagnosis of ADHD and ASD, this short review presents an overview of relationship between sleep problems, ADHD and ASD, as well as conceptualizing the shared pathophysiology. The practical considerations for clinical management of sleep problems in combination with ADHD and ASD are also discussed.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista que también tiene TDAH, conviene prestar atención a su sueño y comentarlo con su profesional de referencia, porque ambas condiciones se asocian a menudo con problemas de sueño. Anota horarios, despertares y rutinas para compartirlos en la consulta. La evidencia es una revisión breve que resume estudios previos sobre sueño, TDAH y autismo, y comenta el cambio del DSM-5 que permite diagnosticar ambos a la vez. Sus límites: no es un estudio con participantes propios, no ofrece una pauta válida para todas las personas y las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person who also has ADHD, it is worth paying attention to their sleep and raising it with their clinician, because both are often linked with sleep problems. Jot down bedtimes, night waking and routines to share at the appointment. The evidence is a short review that brings together earlier research on sleep, ADHD and autism, and discusses the DSM-5 change that allows both to be diagnosed together. Its limits: it did not study its own participants, it is not a rule for every person, and medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person som också har ADHD är det värt att uppmärksamma sömnen och ta upp den med en kliniker, eftersom båda ofta hör ihop med sömnproblem. Skriv ner läggtider, nattliga uppvaknanden och rutiner att ta med till besöket. Underlaget är en kort översikt som sammanfattar tidigare forskning om sömn, ADHD och autism och beskriver DSM-5-ändringen som tillåter båda diagnoserna samtidigt. Begränsningar: den har inga egna deltagare, gäller inte som regel för alla och medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker.

title: Assessment of Sleep in Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Moore M, Evans V, Hanvey G, Johnson C
abstract: Sleep disturbances in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) are significantly more prevalent than found in typically developing (TD) children. Given the detrimental impact of poor sleep on cognitive, emotional, and behavioral functioning, it is imperative to screen and assess for sleep disturbances in this population. In this paper, we describe the screening and assessment process, as well as specific measures commonly used for assessing sleep in children with ASD. Advantages and limitations for use in children with ASD are discussed. While subjective measures, such as parent-report questionnaires and sleep diaries, are the most widely used, more objective measures such as actigraphy, polysomnography, and videosomnography provide additional valuable information for both diagnostic purposes and treatment planning. These objective measures, nonetheless, are limited by cost, availability, and feasibility of use with children with ASD. The current review provides an argument for the complementary uses of both subjective and objective measures of sleep specifically for use in children with ASD.

sheet.es: Si le preocupa el sueño de su hijo autista, empiece por anotar cómo duerme: un diario del sueño o un cuestionario para familias puede dar información útil que puede llevar a su profesional de salud. Esta es una revisión que describe cómo se evalúa el sueño en niños autistas y qué medidas se usan. Señala que los cuestionarios y diarios son lo más habitual, y que medidas objetivas como la actigrafía, la polisomnografía y la videosomnografía aportan datos adicionales, aunque pueden ser costosas, poco accesibles o difíciles de usar con algunos niños. No es una guía para todos los casos: cada niño duerme de forma distinta, y las decisiones sobre evaluación o tratamiento corresponden a un profesional.
sheet.en: If you are concerned about your autistic child's sleep, a good first step is to keep a sleep diary or fill in a parent questionnaire, then share it with a health professional. This is a review describing how sleep is assessed in autistic children and which measures are commonly used. It reports that questionnaires and diaries are the most widely used, while objective tools such as actigraphy, polysomnography and videosomnography add useful information, but can be limited by cost, availability and how practical they are for some children. It is not a rule for every child: each child sleeps differently, and decisions about assessment or support belong with a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om du oroar dig för ditt autistiska barns sömn kan du börja med att föra sömndagbok eller fylla i ett frågeformulär för föräldrar och sedan ta med det till en vårdgivare. Det här är en översikt som beskriver hur sömn bedöms hos autistiska barn och vilka mått som ofta används. Den uppger att frågeformulär och dagböcker används mest, medan objektiva metoder som aktigrafi, polysomnografi och videosomnografi ger ytterligare information, men kan begränsas av kostnad, tillgång och hur genomförbara de är för vissa barn. Det är ingen regel för alla barn: varje barn sover olika, och beslut om bedömning eller stöd fattas tillsammans med vårdpersonal.

title: Clinical impact of early diagnosis of autism on the prognosis and parent-child relationships.
authors: Elder JH, Kreider CM, Brasher SN, Ansell M
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) refers to a lifelong condition that usually appears in late infancy or early childhood, and is characterized by social and communication deficits that impede optimal functioning. Despite widespread research and greater public awareness, ASD has an unclear etiology and no known cure, making it difficult to acquire accurate and timely diagnoses. In addition, once an ASD diagnosis is made, parents find it challenging to navigate the healthcare system and determine which interventions are most effective and appropriate for their child. A growing body of evidence supports the value of early diagnosis and treatment with evidence-based interventions, which can significantly improve the quality of life of individuals with ASD as well as of their carers and families. Particularly noteworthy are early interventions that occur in natural surroundings and can be modified to address age-related goals throughout the lifespan. Therefore, the purpose of this review is to: 1) provide readers with a brief background related to ASD; 2) describe commonly used screening instruments and tools for early diagnosis; 3) describe early interventions that have empirical support; and 4) discuss how the parent-child and family relationships can be affected through this process. This information can provide professionals with information they can use to assist families who make critical and potentially life-changing decisions for children with ASD.

sheet.es: Si le preocupa el desarrollo de su hijo o hija, hablar pronto con un profesional sanitario sobre una evaluación puede ayudarle a acceder antes a apoyos. Conviene preguntar por intervenciones con respaldo empírico, que se adapten a la vida diaria y a los objetivos de cada edad. Es una revisión de la literatura que describe herramientas de cribado, intervenciones y cómo el proceso afecta a la relación entre padres e hijos y a la familia. Sus límites: no es un estudio con participantes propios, y no indica qué funcionará para cada persona autista ni para cada familia.
sheet.en: If you are worried about your child's development, talking early with a health professional about an assessment may help you reach supports sooner. It is worth asking about interventions with empirical support that fit everyday life and age-related goals. This is a review of existing literature, describing screening tools, interventions and how the process can affect the parent-child relationship and the family. Its limits: it is not a study with its own participants, and it cannot tell what will work for each autistic person or each family.
sheet.sv: Om du är orolig för ditt barns utveckling kan det hjälpa att tidigt prata med vårdpersonal om en utredning, så att stöd kan komma igång förr. Fråga gärna efter insatser med vetenskapligt stöd som passar vardagen och målen för barnets ålder. Detta är en översikt av befintlig forskning som beskriver screeningverktyg, insatser och hur processen kan påverka relationen mellan förälder och barn samt familjen. Begränsningar: den har inga egna deltagare och kan inte säga vad som fungerar för varje autistisk person eller familj.

title: Medical comorbidities in children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorders and attention deficit hyperactivity disorders: a systematic review.
authors: Muskens JB, Velders FP, Staal WG
abstract: Somatic disorders occur more often in adult psychiatric patients than in the general adult population. However, in child and adolescent psychiatry this association is unclear, mainly due to a lack of integration of existing data. To address this issue, we here present a systematic review on medical comorbidity in the two major developmental disorders autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and formulate clinical recommendations. The literature was searched using the PubMed and PsycINFO databases (2000-1 May 2016) with the keywords "[((child and adolescent) AND (Autism OR Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder* OR ADHD)) AND ("Cardiovascular Diseases" [Mesh] OR "Endocrine System Diseases" [Mesh] OR "Immune System Diseases" [Mesh] OR "Neurobehavioral Manifestations" [Mesh] OR "Gastrointestinal Disorders" [Mesh] OR Somatic OR Autoimmune disease OR Nervous system disease OR Infection OR Infectious disease)]. Two raters independently assessed the quality of the eligible studies. The initial search identified 5278 articles. Based on inclusion and exclusion criteria 104 papers were selected and subsequently subjected to a quality control. This quality was assessed according to a standardized and validated set of criteria and yielded 29 studies for inclusion. This thorough literature search provides an overview of relevant articles on medical comorbidity in ADHD and/or ASD, and shows that medical disorders in these children and adolescents appear to be widespread. Those who work with children with ASD and/or ADHD should be well aware of this and actively promote routine medical assessment. Additionally, case-control studies and population-based studies are needed to provide reliable prevalence estimates. Future studies should furthermore focus on a broader evaluation of medical disorders in children and adolescents with ADHD and/or ASD to improve treatment algorithm in this vulnerable group.

sheet.es: Los niños y adolescentes autistas o con TDAH parecen tener con frecuencia otros problemas de salud física, como dificultades digestivas, inmunitarias o neurológicas. En la práctica: si notas cambios en el sueño, el apetito, el ánimo o la conducta, considera que puede haber una causa física (dolor, estreñimiento, infección) y pide una revisión médica. Llevar un registro sencillo de síntomas ayuda al profesional. Se trata de una revisión sistemática de 2017 que incluyó 29 estudios de calidad sobre menores autistas y/o con TDAH. Sus límites: faltan estudios poblacionales, por lo que no ofrece cifras fiables de frecuencia y no describe a cada niño.
sheet.en: Autistic children and teenagers, and those with ADHD, seem to often have physical health conditions too, such as digestive, immune or neurological problems. In practice: if you notice changes in sleep, appetite, mood or behaviour, consider a possible physical cause (pain, constipation, infection) and ask for a medical check-up. Keeping a simple symptom diary can help the clinician. This is a 2017 systematic review that included 29 quality-checked studies of autistic young people and/or those with ADHD. Its limits: population-based studies are lacking, so it gives no reliable figures on how common these conditions are, and it does not describe every child.
sheet.sv: Autistiska barn och ungdomar, och de med ADHD, verkar ofta också ha kroppsliga hälsotillstånd, till exempel mag-tarm-, immun- eller neurologiska besvär. I praktiken: om du märker förändringar i sömn, aptit, humör eller beteende, tänk på att det kan finnas en kroppslig orsak (smärta, förstoppning, infektion) och be om en läkarundersökning. En enkel symtomdagbok kan hjälpa vården. Detta är en systematisk översikt från 2017 som omfattade 29 kvalitetsgranskade studier om autistiska unga och/eller unga med ADHD. Begränsningar: befolkningsstudier saknas, så den ger inga säkra siffror på hur vanligt det är, och den beskriver inte varje barn.

title: Association among obesity, overweight and autism spectrum disorder: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Zheng Z, Zhang L, Li S, Zhao F, Wang Y, Huang L, Huang J, Zou R, Qu Y, Mu D
abstract: Obesity, overweight and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) remain serious public health problems. Although lots of studies have recently explored the association among obesity, overweight and ASD, the findings are inconsistent. Thus, we conducted a meta-analysis of epidemiological studies to examine the association among obesity, overweight and ASD. PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were used for literature searches to identify eligible studies published in English before November 15, 2016. Relevant studies estimating the association among obesity, overweight and ASD were included. Fifteen studies encompassing 49,937,078 participants and 1,045,538 individuals with ASD were included in this study. A random effects model was chosen to synthesize the effect sizes of individual studies. The prevalence of obesity was significantly higher in individuals with ASD than in controls (OR = 1.84, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.37-2.48, P < 0.001). However, the prevalence of overweight in individuals with ASD was not significantly different from that in controls (OR = 1.07, 95% CI: 0.83-1.38, P = 0.62). Both sensitivity analysis and publication bias testing revealed that the findings were robust. The meta-analysis showed a significant association between obesity and ASD. However, no significant association was identified between overweight and ASD.

sheet.es: Conviene incluir el peso y la salud física en los controles médicos habituales de una persona autista, con una conversación tranquila y sin culpas con su profesional de salud. Esta revisión con metaanálisis reunió 15 estudios con 49,937,078 participantes, entre ellos 1,045,538 personas con autismo.
