La obesidad fue más frecuente en personas autistas que en el grupo de comparación (OR = 1.84), pero el sobrepeso no mostró una diferencia significativa (OR = 1.07). Límites: muestra una asociación, no explica la causa, y no significa que ocurra en cada persona autista. Solo incluyó estudios en inglés.
sheet.en: It is worth including weight and physical health in an autistic person's regular health checks, discussed calmly and without blame with their health professional. This systematic review and meta-analysis combined 15 studies with 49,937,078 participants, including 1,045,538 autistic people. Obesity was more common in autistic people than in the comparison group (OR = 1.84), but overweight showed no significant difference (OR = 1.07). Limits: it shows an association, not a cause, and does not mean this applies to every autistic person. It only included studies published in English.
sheet.sv: Det är värt att ta med vikt och fysisk hälsa i en autistisk persons regelbundna hälsokontroller, och att prata om det lugnt och utan skuld med vårdpersonalen. Den här systematiska översikten och metaanalysen slog ihop 15 studier med 49,937,078 deltagare, varav 1,045,538 autistiska personer. Fetma var vanligare hos autistiska personer än i jämförelsegruppen (OR = 1.84), men övervikt visade ingen signifikant skillnad (OR = 1.07). Begränsningar: den visar ett samband, inte en orsak, och gäller inte varje autistisk person. Den omfattade bara studier på engelska.

title: Tracing the temporal stability of autism spectrum diagnosis and severity as measured by the Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Bieleninik Ł, Posserud MB, Geretsegger M, Thompson G, Elefant C, Gold C
abstract: Background Exploring ways to improve the trajectory and symptoms of autism spectrum disorder is prevalent in research, but less is known about the natural prognosis of autism spectrum disorder and course of symptoms. The objective of this study was to examine the temporal stability of autism spectrum disorder and autism diagnosis, and the longitudinal trajectories of autism core symptom severity. We furthermore sought to identify possible predictors for change. Methods We searched PubMed, PsycInfo, EMBASE, Web of Science, Cochrane Library up to October 2015 for prospective cohort studies addressing the autism spectrum disorder/autism diagnostic stability, and prospective studies of intervention effects. We included people of all ages with autism spectrum disorder/autism or at risk of having autism spectrum disorder, who were diagnosed and followed up for at least 12 months using the Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule (ADOS). Both continuous ADOS scores and dichotomous diagnostic categories were pooled in random-effects meta-analysis and meta-regression. Results Of 1443 abstracts screened, 44 were eligible of which 40 studies contained appropriate data for meta-analysis. A total of 5771 participants from 7 months of age to 16.5 years were included. Our analyses showed no change in ADOS scores across time as measured by Calibrated Severity Scores (mean difference [MD] = 0.05, 95% CI -0.26 to 0.36). We observed a minor but statistically significant change in ADOS total raw scores (MD = -1.51, 95% CI -2.70 to -0.32). There was no improvement in restricted and repetitive behaviours (standardised MD [SMD] = -0.04, 95% CI -0.19 to 0.11), but a minor improvement in social affect over time (SMD = -0.31, 95% CI -0.50 to -0.12). No changes were observed for meeting the autism spectrum disorder criteria over time (risk difference [RD] = -0.01, 95% CI -0.03 to 0.01), but a significant change for meeting autism criteria over time (RD = -0.18, 95% CI -0.29 to -0.07). On average, there was a high heterogeneity between studies (I2 range: 65.3% to 93.1%). Discussion While 18% of participants shifted from autism to autism spectrum disorder diagnosis, the overall autism spectrum disorder prevalence was unchanged. Overall autism core symptoms were remarkably stable over time across childhood indicating that intervention studies should focus on other areas, such as quality of life and adaptive functioning. However, due to high heterogeneity between studies and a number of limitations in the studies, the results need to be interpreted with caution.

sheet.es: Un diagnóstico de autismo en la infancia suele mantenerse con el tiempo, y los rasgos autistas centrales cambian poco. Esto puede liberarte de perseguir que tu hijo o hija «deje de ser autista» y orientar la energía hacia lo que sí mejora la vida diaria: bienestar, autonomía, comunicación que funcione para la persona y entornos adaptados. Algunos niños pasaron de «autismo» a la categoría más amplia de «espectro autista». Es un metaanálisis de 40 estudios con 5771 participantes de 7 meses a 16,5 años evaluados con la ADOS durante al menos un año. Los estudios eran muy distintos entre sí, no incluyeron adultos y la ADOS no mide calidad de vida.
sheet.en: An autism diagnosis given in childhood usually stays stable, and core autistic traits change little over time. This can free you from trying to make your child "less autistic" and let you focus on what genuinely improves daily life: wellbeing, independence, communication that works for your child, and supportive environments. Some children moved from "autism" to the broader "autism spectrum" category. This meta-analysis pooled 40 studies with 5,771 participants aged 7 months to 16.5 years, assessed with the ADOS over at least a year. The studies varied widely, adults were not included, and the ADOS does not measure quality of life.
sheet.sv: En autismdiagnos som ställs i barndomen brukar bestå, och kärndragen i autism förändras lite över tid. Det kan befria dig från att försöka göra ditt barn "mindre autistiskt" och i stället lägga kraften på det som verkligen förbättrar vardagen: välmående, självständighet, kommunikation som fungerar för barnet och anpassade miljöer. Vissa barn gick från "autism" till den bredare kategorin "autismspektrum". Metaanalysen sammanställde 40 studier med 5 771 deltagare mellan 7 månader och 16,5 år, bedömda med ADOS under minst ett år. Studierna skilde sig mycket åt, vuxna ingick inte och ADOS mäter inte livskvalitet.

title: The Endocannabinoid System and Autism Spectrum Disorders: Insights from Animal Models.
authors: Zamberletti E, Gabaglio M, Parolaro D
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) defines a group of neurodevelopmental disorders whose symptoms include impaired communication and social interaction with restricted or repetitive motor movements, frequently associated with general cognitive deficits. Although it is among the most severe chronic childhood disorders in terms of prevalence, morbidity, and impact to the society, no effective treatment for ASD is yet available, possibly because its neurobiological basis is not clearly understood hence specific drugs have not yet been developed. The endocannabinoid (EC) system represents a major neuromodulatory system involved in the regulation of emotional responses, behavioral reactivity to context, and social interaction. Furthermore, the EC system is also affected in conditions often present in subsets of patients diagnosed with ASD, such as seizures, anxiety, intellectual disabilities, and sleep pattern disturbances. Despite the indirect evidence suggestive of an involvement of the EC system in ASD, only a few studies have specifically addressed the role of the EC system in the context of ASD. This review describes the available data on the investigation of the presence of alterations of the EC system as well as the effects of its pharmacological manipulations in animal models of ASD-like behaviors.

sheet.es: Este estudio no ofrece nada que probar mañana en casa: es investigación básica. Lo útil es saber que se investiga el sistema endocannabinoide, que interviene en las emociones y la interacción social. Es una revisión de estudios en modelos animales, no en personas autistas. Los propios autores señalan que hay pocos estudios específicos y que la evidencia es indirecta. Incluye pruebas farmacológicas, así que es un estudio médico: cualquier decisión sobre tratamientos corresponde a un profesional clínico. Sus resultados no se pueden aplicar a todas las personas autistas ni a su vida diaria.
sheet.en: This study offers nothing to try at home tomorrow: it is basic research. What may help is knowing that researchers are looking at the endocannabinoid system, which is involved in emotions and social interaction. It is a review of studies in animal models, not in autistic people. The authors note that few studies address this directly and that the evidence is indirect. It includes pharmacological tests, so it is a medical study: any treatment decision belongs to a clinician. Its findings cannot be applied to every autistic person or to daily life.
sheet.sv: Den här studien ger inget att prova hemma i morgon: det är grundforskning. Det som kan vara bra att veta är att forskare undersöker det endocannabinoida systemet, som är involverat i känslor och social interaktion. Det är en översikt av studier på djurmodeller, inte på autistiska personer. Författarna påpekar att få studier tar upp detta direkt och att belägget är indirekt. Den omfattar farmakologiska tester och är alltså en medicinsk studie: beslut om behandling hör till en kliniker. Resultaten kan inte överföras till alla autistiska personer eller till vardagen.

title: Toward a conceptual framework for early brain and behavior development in autism.
authors: Piven J, Elison JT, Zylka MJ
abstract: Studies of infant siblings of older autistic probands, who are at elevated risk for autism, have demonstrated that the defining features of autism are not present in the first year of life but emerge late in the first and into the second year. A recent longitudinal neuroimaging study of high-risk siblings revealed a specific pattern of brain development in infants later diagnosed with autism, characterized by cortical surface area hyper-expansion in the first year followed by brain volume overgrowth in the second year that is associated with the emergence of autistic social deficits. Together with new observations from genetically defined autism risk alleles and rodent model, these findings suggest a conceptual framework for the early, post-natal development of autism. This framework postulates that an increase in the proliferation of neural progenitor cells and hyper-expansion of cortical surface area in the first year, occurring during a pre-symptomatic period characterized by disrupted sensorimotor and attentional experience, leads to altered experience-dependent neuronal development and decreased elimination of neuronal processes. This process is linked to brain volume overgrowth and disruption of the refinement of neural circuit connections and is associated with the emergence of autistic social deficits in the second year of life. A better understanding of the timing of developmental brain and behavior mechanisms in autism during infancy, a period which precedes the emergence of the defining features of this disorder, will likely have important implications for designing rational approaches to early intervention.

sheet.es: Si tienes un bebé con un hermano o hermana autista, puedes observar con calma cómo explora, se mueve y presta atención durante el primer y segundo año, y compartir lo que notes con el equipo de salud infantil. Los rasgos autistas suelen hacerse visibles entre el final del primer año y el segundo, no antes, así que no hace falta buscar señales en cada gesto. Esta es una revisión que reúne estudios de imagen cerebral en bebés hermanos de niños autistas, datos genéticos y modelos animales. Sus límites: propone un marco teórico, no una prueba diagnóstica, y no describe a cada niño ni indica qué apoyo concreto funciona.
sheet.en: If you have a baby whose older sibling is autistic, you can calmly notice how they explore, move and pay attention across the first two years, and share what you see with your child health team. Autistic traits usually become visible from late in the first year into the second, not earlier, so there is no need to search every gesture for signs. This is a review bringing together brain-imaging studies of infant siblings of autistic children, genetic findings and animal research. Its limits: it proposes a theoretical framework, not a diagnostic test, and it does not describe every child or say which specific support works.
sheet.sv: Om du har en bebis vars äldre syskon är autistiskt kan du i lugn och ro lägga märke till hur barnet utforskar, rör sig och riktar uppmärksamhet under de första två åren, och berätta vad du ser för barnhälsovården. Autistiska drag blir oftast synliga från slutet av första året och under andra året, inte tidigare, så du behöver inte leta tecken i varje gest. Detta är en översikt som samlar hjärnavbildningsstudier av småsyskon till autistiska barn, genetiska fynd och djurforskning. Begränsningar: den föreslår en teoretisk modell, inte ett diagnostiskt test, och beskriver inte varje barn eller vilket konkret stöd som fungerar.

title: Transition to school for children with autism spectrum disorder: A systematic review.
authors: Marsh A, Spagnol V, Grove R, Eapen V
abstract: Aim To identify factors that promote a positive start to school for children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Methods Web of Science, MEDLINE, Scopus, and PsychINFO searches were conducted to identify literature published after 1991 and relevant to school transition processes in children with ASD. Twenty studies were deemed eligible for inclusion. These studies evaluated a range of factors including school readiness, parent and teacher perspectives on transition practices, characteristics of children with ASD that are associated with successful transition to school and the impact of school based intervention programs. Results A review of these studies showed that children with ASD are less school ready emotionally than their peers and those children with ASD appear to have more externalising behaviours and self-regulation difficulties that affect their school engagement and their relationships with their teachers. There was a paucity of research looking at interventions targeting school readiness. However, school-based behavioural interventions appear to improve cognitive, language and daily living skills, but have less impact on socialisation and peer inclusion. Conclusion Children with ASD face more challenges transitioning to school, particularly with social interaction. Further development and implementation of specific school-based interventions is needed in order to assist children with autism to maximise their success in starting school.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija autista va a empezar el colegio, hable pronto con el profesorado sobre cómo se regula emocionalmente, qué le ayuda a calmarse y cómo se relaciona con los adultos, y prepare juntos apoyos concretos. Es una revisión sistemática de 20 estudios sobre el inicio escolar de niños autistas. La revisión halló que el apoyo en regulación emocional y en la relación con el profesorado puede importar, y que hay poca investigación sobre cómo preparar para el colegio. Sus límites: reúne estudios muy distintos y describe tendencias de grupo, no lo que le ocurrirá a cada niño o niña.
sheet.en: If your autistic child is starting school, talk early with the teachers about how your child regulates emotions, what helps them settle, and how they relate to adults, and plan concrete supports together. This is a systematic review of 20 studies on starting school for autistic children. It found that emotional regulation and the relationship with teachers may matter for school engagement, and that little research looks at preparing children for school. Its limits: the studies are very varied and describe group trends, not what will happen for any individual child.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn ska börja skolan, prata tidigt med lärarna om hur barnet reglerar känslor, vad som hjälper hen att varva ner och hur hen relaterar till vuxna, och planera konkreta stöd tillsammans. Det här är en systematisk översikt av 20 studier om skolstart för autistiska barn. Den fann att stöd kring känsloreglering och relationen till lärare kan spela roll för delaktigheten i skolan, och att det finns lite forskning om hur man förbereder barn inför skolan. Begränsningar: studierna är mycket olika och visar gruppmönster, inte vad som gäller för varje enskilt barn.

title: Cognitive Behaviour Therapy Versus a Counselling Intervention for Anxiety in Young People with High-Functioning Autism Spectrum Disorders: A Pilot Randomised Controlled Trial.
authors: Murphy SM, Chowdhury U, White SW, Reynolds L, Donald L, Gahan H, Iqbal Z, Kulkarni M, Scrivener L, Shaker-Naeeni H, Press DA
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: The use of cognitive-behavioural therapy (CBT) as a treatment for children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) has been explored in a number of trials. Whilst CBT appears superior to no treatment or treatment as usual, few studies have assessed CBT against a control group receiving an alternative therapy. Our randomised controlled trial compared use of CBT against person-centred counselling for anxiety in 36 young people with ASD, ages 12-18. Outcome measures included parent- teacher- and self-reports of anxiety and social disability. Whilst each therapy produced improvements in participants, neither therapy was superior to the other to a significant degree on any measure. This is consistent with findings for adults.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adolescente vive con ansiedad, tanto la terapia cognitivo-conductual (TCC) como el counselling centrado en la persona pueden ser opciones útiles; conviene hablar con profesionales sobre cuál encaja mejor con sus preferencias. Es un ensayo piloto aleatorizado con 36 jóvenes autistas de 12-18 años. Ambas terapias mostraron mejoras y ninguna fue claramente mejor en ninguna medida. Es un estudio pequeño y preliminar, así que no sirve como regla para todas las personas, y no dice qué funciona mejor en cada caso concreto.
sheet.en: If an autistic teenager is living with anxiety, both cognitive-behavioural therapy (CBT) and person-centred counselling may be useful options; it is worth talking with professionals about which fits their preferences best. This was a pilot randomised controlled trial with 36 autistic young people aged 12-18. Both therapies brought improvements, and neither was clearly better on any measure. It is a small, early study, so it is not a rule for everyone, and it cannot say what works best for any one person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk tonåring har ångest kan både kognitiv beteendeterapi (KBT) och personcentrerad rådgivning vara användbara alternativ; prata med vårdpersonal om vad som passar personens önskemål bäst. Studien var en randomiserad pilotstudie med 36 autistiska ungdomar i åldern 12-18. Båda terapierna gav förbättringar, och ingen var tydligt bättre på något mått. Studien är liten och tidig, så den är ingen regel för alla och kan inte avgöra vad som fungerar bäst för en enskild person.

title: Mental Wellbeing of Family Members of Autistic Adults.
authors: Herrema R, Garland D, Osborne M, Freeston M, Honey E, Rodgers J
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Family members are often the primary caregiver for autistic adults and this responsibility may impact on the carer's wellbeing and quality of life. 109 family members of autistic adults completed an online survey assessing their wellbeing relating to their caring role for their autistic relative. Family members who were supporting an autistic relative with co-occurring mental health difficulties and who they reported as unprepared for the future, self-reported higher levels of worry, depression, anxiety and stress, and poorer quality of life. These findings emphasise the importance of support for family members of autistic adults, whether through external services to support their relative or individual mental health support for the carer.

title: Supplementation of omega 3 fatty acids may improve hyperactivity, lethargy, and stereotypy in children with autism spectrum disorders: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
authors: Cheng YS, Tseng PT, Chen YW, Stubbs B, Yang WC, Yang WC, Chen TY, Wu CK, Lin PY
abstract: Aim Deficiency of omega 3 fatty acids may be linked to autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Evidence about the potential therapeutic effects of supplementation of omega 3 fatty acids is lacking in ASD patients. Methods We searched major electronic databases from inception to June 21, 2017, for randomized clinical trials, which compared treatment outcomes between supplementation of omega 3 fatty acids and placebo in patients with ASD. An exploratory random-effects meta-analysis of the included studies was undertaken. Results and conclusion Six trials were included (n=194). Meta-analysis showed that supplementation of omega 3 fatty acids improved hyperactivity (difference in means =-2.692, 95% confidence interval [CI] =-5.364 to -0.020, P =0.048, studies =4, n=109), lethargy (difference in means =-1.969, 95% CI =-3.566 to -0.372, P =0.016, studies =4, n=109), and stereotypy (difference in means =-1.071, 95% CI =-2.114 to -0.029, P =0.044, studies =4, n=109). No significant differences emerged between supplementation of omega 3 fatty acids and placebo in global assessment of functioning (n=169) or social responsiveness (n=97). Our preliminary meta-analysis suggests that supplementation of omega 3 fatty acids may improve hyperactivity, lethargy, and stereotypy in ASD patients. However, the number of studies was limited and the overall effects were small, precluding definitive conclusions. Future large-scale randomized clinical trials are needed to confirm or refute our findings.

sheet.es: Si te planteas probar omega 3 en una persona autista, no hay una conclusión firme: coméntalo antes con su profesional de salud, que es quien debe decidir sobre cualquier suplemento. Y observa qué cambia para la persona, sin esperar un resultado concreto. La evidencia es un metaanálisis de ensayos aleatorizados que comparaban omega 3 con placebo: se incluyeron 6 ensayos (n=194). Hubo pequeñas mejoras en hiperactividad, letargo y estereotipias, pero no en el funcionamiento global ni en la respuesta social. Los límites: pocos estudios, efectos pequeños y resultados preliminares que no permiten conclusiones definitivas. No es una regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you are wondering about omega 3 for an autistic person, there is no firm conclusion: talk first with their health professional, who should make any decision about supplements. Watch what actually changes for the person, without expecting a particular result. The evidence is a meta-analysis of randomized trials comparing omega 3 with placebo: 6 trials were included (n=194). There were small improvements in hyperactivity, lethargy and stereotypy, but not in global functioning or social responsiveness. The limits: few studies, small effects, and preliminary results that cannot give definitive conclusions. It is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du funderar på omega 3 för en autistisk person finns ingen säker slutsats: tala först med personens vårdpersonal, som ska fatta beslut om kosttillskott. Se vad som faktiskt förändras för personen, utan att förvänta dig ett visst resultat. Underlaget är en metaanalys av randomiserade studier som jämförde omega 3 med placebo: 6 studier ingick (n=194). Det fanns små förbättringar i hyperaktivitet, letargi och stereotypier, men inte i övergripande funktion eller social responsivitet. Begränsningar: få studier, små effekter och preliminära resultat som inte ger definitiva slutsatser. Det är ingen regel för alla personer.

title: Effectiveness of the BOOST-A™ online transition planning program for adolescents on the autism spectrum: a quasi-randomized controlled trial.
authors: Hatfield M, Falkmer M, Falkmer T, Ciccarelli M
journal: Child and adolescent psychiatry and mental health
abstract: Background The majority of existing transition planning programs are focused on people with a disability in general and may not meet the specific need of adolescents on the autism spectrum. In addition, these interventions focus on specific skills (e.g. job readiness or self-determination) rather than the overall transition planning process and there are methodological limitations to many of the studies determining their effectiveness. The Better OutcOmes & Successful Transitions for Autism (BOOST-A™) is an online program that supports adolescents on the autism spectrum to prepare for leaving school. This study aimed to determine the effectiveness of the BOOST-A™ in enhancing self-determination. Methods A quasi-randomized controlled trial was conducted with adolescents on the autism spectrum enrolled in years 8 to 11 in Australian schools (N = 94). Participants had to have basic computer skills and the ability to write at a year 5 reading level. Participants were allocated to a control (n = 45) or intervention (n = 49) group and participants were blinded to the trial hypothesis. The intervention group used the BOOST-A™ for 12 months, while the control group participated in regular practice. Outcomes included self-determination, career planning and exploration, quality of life, environmental support and domain specific self-determination. Data were collected from parents and adolescents. Results There were no significant differences in overall self-determination between groups. Results indicated significant differences in favor of the intervention group in three areas: opportunity for self-determination at home as reported by parents; career exploration as reported by parents and adolescents; and transition-specific self-determination as reported by parents. Conclusions Results provide preliminary evidence that the BOOST-A™ can enhance some career-readiness outcomes. Lack of significant outcomes related to self-determination at school and career planning may be due to the lack of face-to-face training and parents being the primary contacts in the study. Further research is needed to determine effectiveness of the BOOST-A™ related to post-secondary education and employment. Trial registration #ACTRN12615000119594.

sheet.es: Si su adolescente autista se acerca al final de la escuela, un programa en línea de planificación de la transición, como BOOST-A™, puede ser un apoyo para explorar carreras y hablar del futuro en casa. Es un ensayo cuasialeatorizado con 94 adolescentes autistas de escuelas australianas, que usaron el programa durante 12 meses. No hubo diferencias en la autodeterminación general, pero madres y padres informaron más oportunidades de autodeterminación en casa, y familias y adolescentes informaron más exploración de carreras. Los límites: la evidencia es preliminar, no hubo formación presencial y no se sabe qué pasa después con estudios o empleo. Cada persona es distinta.
sheet.en: If your autistic teenager is nearing the end of school, an online transition planning program like BOOST-A™ may help them explore careers and talk about the future at home. This was a quasi-randomized controlled trial with 94 autistic adolescents in Australian schools, who used the program for 12 months. There was no difference in overall self-determination, but parents reported more opportunities for self-determination at home, and parents and teens reported more career exploration. Limits: the evidence is preliminary, there was no face-to-face training, and effects on later study or work are unknown. Every person is different.
sheet.sv: Om din autistiska tonåring snart slutar skolan kan ett digitalt program för övergångsplanering, som BOOST-A™, vara ett stöd för att utforska yrken och prata om framtiden hemma. Det var en kvasirandomiserad kontrollerad studie med 94 autistiska ungdomar i australiska skolor, som använde programmet i 12 månader. Den övergripande självbestämmandet skilde sig inte åt, men föräldrar rapporterade fler möjligheter till självbestämmande hemma, och föräldrar och ungdomar rapporterade mer yrkesutforskning. Begränsningar: bevisen är preliminära, ingen träning på plats gavs och effekter på senare studier eller arbete är okända. Alla är olika.

title: Comparative safety of antiepileptic drugs for neurological development in children exposed during pregnancy and breast feeding: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
authors: Veroniki AA, Rios P, Cogo E, Straus SE, Finkelstein Y, Kealey R, Reynen E, Soobiah C, Thavorn K, Hutton B, Hemmelgarn BR, Yazdi F, D'Souza J, MacDonald H, Tricco AC
abstract: Objectives Compare the safety of antiepileptic drugs (AEDs) on neurodevelopment of infants/children exposed in utero or during breast feeding. Design and setting Systematic review and Bayesian random-effects network meta-analysis (NMA). MEDLINE, EMBASE and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched until 27 April 2017. Screening, data abstraction and quality appraisal were completed in duplicate by independent reviewers. Participants 29 cohort studies including 5100 infants/children. Interventions Monotherapy and polytherapy AEDs including first-generation (carbamazepine, clobazam, clonazepam, ethosuximide, phenobarbital, phenytoin, primidone, valproate) and newer-generation (gabapentin, lamotrigine, levetiracetam, oxcarbazepine, topiramate, vigabatrin) AEDs. Epileptic women who did not receive AEDs during pregnancy or breast feeding served as the control group. Primary and secondary outcome measures Cognitive developmental delay and autism/dyspraxia were primary outcomes. Attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder, language delay, neonatal seizures, psychomotor developmental delay and social impairment were secondary outcomes. Results The NMA on cognitive developmental delay (11 cohort studies, 933 children, 18 treatments) suggested that among all AEDs only valproate was statistically significantly associated with more children experiencing cognitive developmental delay compared with control (OR=7.40, 95% credible interval (CrI) 3.00 to 18.46). The NMA on autism (5 cohort studies, 2551 children, 12 treatments) suggested that oxcarbazepine (OR 13.51, CrI 1.28 to 221.40), valproate (OR 17.29, 95% CrI 2.40 to 217.60), lamotrigine (OR 8.88, CrI 1.28 to 112.00) and lamotrigine+valproate (OR 132.70, CrI 7.41 to 3851.00) were associated with significantly greater odds of developing autism compared with control. The NMA on psychomotor developmental delay (11 cohort studies, 1145 children, 18 treatments) found that valproate (OR 4.16, CrI 2.04 to 8.75) and carbamazepine+phenobarbital+valproate (OR 19.12, CrI 1.49 to 337.50) were associated with significantly greater odds of psychomotor delay compared with control. Conclusions Valproate alone or combined with another AED is associated with the greatest odds of adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes compared with control. Oxcarbazepine and lamotrigine were associated with increased occurrence of autism. Counselling is advised for women considering pregnancy to tailor the safest regimen. Trial registration number PROSPERO database (CRD42014008925).

sheet.es: Si usted o alguien a su cargo toma medicación antiepiléptica y está pensando en un embarazo o está embarazada, no cambie nada por su cuenta: hable antes con su profesional clínico, porque las decisiones médicas le corresponden. Es un metaanálisis en red de 29 estudios de cohortes con 5100 niñas y niños expuestos a estos fármacos durante el embarazo o la lactancia. Encontró asociaciones con más retraso del desarrollo y más autismo para algunos fármacos, pero asociación no significa causa, los intervalos son muy amplios y no describe a cada persona. Las autoras y autores recomiendan asesoramiento previo al embarazo.
sheet.en: If you or someone you support takes epilepsy medication and is pregnant or planning a pregnancy, don't change anything on your own: talk with your clinician first, because medical decisions belong to them. This was a medical study, a network meta-analysis of 29 cohort studies with 5100 infants and children exposed to these drugs during pregnancy or breast feeding. It found associations between some drugs and more developmental delay and more autism, but association is not cause, the ranges are very wide, and it does not describe any one person. The authors advise counselling before pregnancy.
sheet.sv: Om du eller någon du stödjer tar epilepsiläkemedel och är gravid eller planerar graviditet: ändra inget på egen hand, utan prata först med din läkare, eftersom medicinska beslut hör till vården. Detta var en medicinsk studie, en nätverksmetaanalys av 29 kohortstudier med 5100 spädbarn och barn som exponerats under graviditet eller amning. Den fann samband mellan vissa läkemedel och mer utvecklingsförsening och mer autism, men samband är inte orsak, osäkerhetsintervallen är mycket vida och resultaten beskriver inte en enskild person. Forskarna rekommenderar rådgivning före graviditet.

title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of a School-Based Cognitive Behavioural Therapy Intervention for Anxiety in Adolescents Diagnosed with Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Luxford S, Hadwin JA, Kovshoff H
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: This study evaluated the effectiveness of a school-based Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT) on symptoms of anxiety, social worry and social responsiveness, and indices of attentional control and attentional biases to threat in adolescents diagnosed with Autism Spectrum Disorder. Thirty-five young people (11-14 years; IQ > 70) with ASD and elevated teacher or parent reported anxiety were randomly assigned to 6 sessions of the Exploring Feelings CBT intervention (Attwood in Exploring feelings (anxiety). Future Horizons, Arlington, 2004) (n = 18) or a wait-list control group (n = 17). The intervention (compared to the wait-list control) group showed positive change for parent, teacher and self-reported anxiety symptoms, and more marginal effects of increased teacher-reported social responsiveness. The discussion highlights the potential value and limitations of school-based CBT for young people with ASD.

sheet.es: Si una persona adolescente autista muestra ansiedad en el colegio, puede valer la pena preguntar al centro educativo si ofrece un programa breve de terapia cognitivo-conductual (TCC) adaptado, como el usado aquí. La evidencia es un ensayo aleatorizado con 35 jóvenes autistas de 11-14 años (IQ > 70) con ansiedad elevada. Quienes hicieron 6 sesiones mostraron, frente a la lista de espera, cambios positivos en la ansiedad según familias, profesorado y ellos mismos. Los efectos en la respuesta social fueron más marginales. Límites: el grupo era pequeño, solo incluyó a jóvenes con IQ > 70 y no sirve como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If an autistic teenager seems anxious at school, it may be worth asking the school whether it offers a short, adapted cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) programme like the one used here. The evidence is a randomised trial with 35 autistic young people aged 11-14 (IQ > 70) with elevated anxiety. Those who took 6 sessions showed, compared with a wait-list group, positive change in anxiety reported by parents, teachers and themselves. Effects on social responsiveness were more marginal. Limits: the group was small, included only young people with IQ > 70, and the results are not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk tonåring verkar orolig i skolan kan det vara värt att fråga skolan om den erbjuder ett kort, anpassat program med kognitiv beteendeterapi (KBT) som det som användes här. Underlaget är en randomiserad studie med 35 autistiska ungdomar i åldern 11-14 år (IQ > 70) med förhöjd ångest. De som fick 6 sessioner visade, jämfört med en väntelista, positiv förändring i ångest enligt föräldrar, lärare och dem själva. Effekterna på social responsivitet var mer marginella. Begränsningar: gruppen var liten, omfattade bara ungdomar med IQ > 70 och resultaten gäller inte som regel för alla.

title: Gastrointestinal symptoms and autism spectrum disorder: links and risks - a possible new overlap syndrome.
authors: Wasilewska J, Klukowski M
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a genetically determined neurodevelopmental brain disorder presenting with restricted, repetitive patterns of behaviors, interests, and activities, or persistent deficits in social communication and social interaction. ASD is characterized by many different clinical endophenotypes and is potentially linked with certain comorbidities. According to current recommendations, children with ASD are at risk of having alimentary tract disorders - mainly, they are at a greater risk of general gastrointestinal (GI) concerns, constipation, diarrhea, and abdominal pain. GI symptoms may overlap with ASD core symptoms through different mechanisms. These mechanisms include multilevel pathways in the gut-brain axis contributing to alterations in behavior and cognition. Shared pathogenetic factors and pathophysiological mechanisms possibly linking ASD and GI disturbances, as shown by most recent studies, include intestinal inflammation with or without autoimmunity, immunoglobulin E-mediated and/or cell-mediated GI food allergies as well as gluten-related disorders (celiac disease, wheat allergy, non-celiac gluten sensitivity), visceral hypersensitivity linked with functional abdominal pain, and dysautonomia linked with GI dysmotility and gastroesophageal reflux. Dysregulation of the gut microbiome has also been shown to be involved in modulating GI functions with the ability to affect intestinal permeability, mucosal immune function, and intestinal motility and sensitivity. Metabolic activity of the microbiome and dietary components are currently suspected to be associated with alterations in behavior and cognition also in patients with other neurodegenerative diseases. All the above-listed GI factors may contribute to brain dysfunction and neuroinflammation depending upon an individual patient's genetic vulnerability. Due to a possible clinical endophenotype presenting as comorbidity of ASD and GI disorders, we propose treating this situation as an "overlap syndrome". Practical use of the concept of an overlap syndrome of ASD and GI disorders may help in identifying those children with ASD who suffer from an alimentary tract disease. Unexplained worsening of nonverbal behaviors (agitation, anxiety, aggression, self-injury, sleep deprivation) should alert professionals about this possibility. This may shorten the time to diagnosis and treatment commencement, and thereby alleviate both GI and ASD symptoms through reducing pain, stress, or discomfort. Furthermore, this may also protect children against unnecessary dietary experiments and restrictions that have no medical indications. A personalized approach to each patient is necessary. Our understanding of ASDs has come a long way, but further studies and more systematic research are warranted.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista muestra un empeoramiento inexplicable de su comportamiento no verbal (agitación, ansiedad, agresión, autolesión, falta de sueño), conviene pensar en posible dolor o malestar digestivo y consultarlo con su equipo médico. Anote cuándo ocurre y cómo son sus deposiciones y comidas. Esta es una revisión de la literatura sobre niños autistas; señala mayor riesgo de estreñimiento, diarrea y dolor abdominal. Sus límites: propone un posible "síndrome de superposición" y pide más investigación, así que no vale para todas las personas. Evite restringir la dieta sin indicación médica. Si hay autolesión o pensamientos de hacerse daño, busque ayuda profesional: un médico, un servicio de salud o un servicio de crisis. Ante peligro inmediato, llame al número de emergencias de su país.
sheet.en: If an autistic person shows an unexplained worsening of nonverbal behaviors (agitation, anxiety, aggression, self-injury, sleep deprivation), consider that digestive pain or discomfort may be involved, and raise it with their medical team. Note when it happens, plus bowel habits and meals. This is a review of the literature on autistic children; it points to a greater risk of constipation, diarrhea and abdominal pain. Its limits: it proposes a possible "overlap syndrome" and calls for more research, so it does not apply to every person. Avoid diet restrictions without a medical reason. If there is self-injury or thoughts of self-harm, seek professional help: a clinician, a health service or a crisis service. In immediate danger, call the emergency number of your country.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person plötsligt får oförklarligt förändrade icke-verbala beteenden (oro, ångest, aggression, självskada, sömnbrist) kan magont eller obehag spela roll, och det är bra att ta upp med vårdteamet. Anteckna när det sker samt avföring och måltider. Detta är en översikt om autistiska barn; den pekar på högre risk för förstoppning, diarré och buksmärta. Begränsningar: den föreslår ett möjligt "överlappningssyndrom" och efterlyser mer forskning, så den gäller inte alla. Undvik kostrestriktioner utan medicinsk orsak. Vid självskada eller tankar på att skada sig själv, sök professionell hjälp: en läkare, en vårdinrättning eller en krisjour. Vid akut fara, ring nödnumret i ditt land.

title: Outcomes and benefits of pediatric cochlear implantation in children with additional disabilities: a review and report of family influences on outcomes.
authors: Cejas I, Hoffman MF, Quittner AL
abstract: The number of children with hearing loss with additional disabilities receiving cochlear implantation has increased dramatically over the past decade. However, little is known about their auditory and speech and language development following implantation. The purpose of this review is to evaluate the effects of cochlear implantation on the most common genetic and developmental disorders in children with hearing loss. Benefits of cochlear implantation for children with autism spectrum disorder, developmental delay, CHARGE syndrome, cerebral palsy, learning disorders, Usher syndrome, Waardenburg syndrome, and attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder are reviewed. Our review indicates that children with hearing loss and additional disabilities benefit from cochlear implantation, especially when implanted early. Thus, early interventions seem as important for these children as for deaf children without additional disabilities. Comparisons of outcomes across these disabilities indicate that children with little to no cognitive impairment (eg, Waardenburg sydrome, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder) have better outcomes than those with greater deficits in intellectual functioning (eg, autism, CHARGE syndrome). In addition, parents of children with hearing loss and additional disabilities report higher levels of parenting stress and greater child behavior problems than those without comorbid diagnoses. However, these parents are as sensitive when interacting with their children as parents with typically developing children using cochlear implantation. Given these results, it is critical to evaluate these children's developmental milestones to provide early implantation and intervention, appropriately counsel families regarding realistic expectations for the implant, and facilitate family adaptation.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija es autista y además tiene pérdida auditiva, no descarte de entrada el implante coclear: hable pronto con el equipo de audiología sobre sus hitos de desarrollo y sobre qué esperar de forma realista. Esta es una revisión de estudios sobre niños con pérdida auditiva y otras discapacidades, entre ellas el autismo. Concluye que se benefician del implante, sobre todo si es temprano, aunque los resultados fueron mejores con menos dificultades cognitivas. También indica más estrés parental, pero igual sensibilidad al interactuar. Es una revisión, no dice qué ocurrirá en cada niño, y las decisiones médicas corresponden a su clínico.
sheet.en: If your child is autistic and also has hearing loss, don't rule out a cochlear implant at the outset: talk early with the audiology team about developmental milestones and realistic expectations. This is a review of studies on children with hearing loss and other disabilities, including autism. It found that these children benefit from implants, especially when implanted early, though outcomes were better with fewer cognitive difficulties. Parents reported more stress, yet were just as sensitive when interacting with their children. It is a review, so it cannot predict any one child's results, and medical decisions belong to your clinician.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn är autistiskt och även har hörselnedsättning, avfärda inte cochleaimplantat på förhand: prata tidigt med audiologteamet om utvecklingsmilstolpar och realistiska förväntningar. Detta är en översikt av studier om barn med hörselnedsättning och andra funktionsnedsättningar, bland annat autism. Den fann att barnen har nytta av implantat, särskilt om det sätts in tidigt, men resultaten var bättre vid färre kognitiva svårigheter. Föräldrar rapporterade mer stress men var lika lyhörda i samspelet. Det är en översikt och kan inte förutsäga ett enskilt barns resultat, och medicinska beslut hör till din kliniker.

title: Methods to improve joint attention in young children with autism: a review.
authors: Paparella T, Freeman SFN
abstract: We provide an overview of studies in the past 10 years (2004-2014) that have aimed to improve joint attention (JA) in young children at risk for, or with, autism spectrum disorder. Thirteen randomized controlled trial (RCT) interventions were found, which received particular focus. Three studies used intervention methods with a developmental orientation and focused on caregiver-mediated methods. Others used combined developmental and behavioral approaches and delivered intervention via trained interventionists, caregivers, and teachers. Interventions ranged widely in density, both with respect to the amount of intervention delivered weekly and the total duration of intervention. Fourteen single-subject research design (SSRD) studies and one quasi-experimental pre-post design study were also included. Notably absent in the RCTs were studies using only behavioral methods, while behavioral methods dominated in the SSRDs. The outcomes of the RCTs using combined behavioral and developmental methods generally demonstrate short-term social communication gains. While some studies demonstrated long-term maintenance and positive outcomes in related areas such as language, many did not. The mixed results for language outcomes indicate a need for further investigation. In addition, future studies should further examine participants' developmental readiness and intervention dose in relation to outcome, as well as aim to isolate active ingredients of interventions.

sheet.es: Si quiere apoyar la atención conjunta (compartir con otra persona la atención hacia un objeto o evento), pruebe juegos cortos y cotidianos en los que usted siga el interés de su hijo o hija y comparta ese momento, y consulte con profesionales sobre programas que incluyan a la familia. Esta es una revisión de estudios de 2004 a 2014 con niños pequeños autistas o con probabilidad de serlo, que incluyó 13 ensayos controlados aleatorizados. Los métodos que combinan enfoques del desarrollo y conductuales mostraron en general mejoras sociales y comunicativas a corto plazo; los resultados a largo plazo y en lenguaje fueron mixtos. Cada niño es distinto y los resultados no valen para todos.
sheet.en: If you want to support joint attention (sharing attention with another person toward an object or event), try short, everyday play moments where you follow your child's interest and share it, and ask professionals about programmes that involve the family. This is a review of studies from 2004 to 2014 with young autistic children or children at risk of autism, including 13 randomized controlled trials. Methods combining developmental and behavioral approaches generally showed short-term social communication gains; long-term and language results were mixed. Every child is different, and these findings do not apply to everyone.
sheet.sv: Om du vill stödja delad uppmärksamhet (att dela uppmärksamhet med en annan person kring ett föremål eller en händelse) kan du prova korta vardagliga lekstunder där du följer barnets intresse och delar det, och fråga fackfolk om program som involverar familjen. Detta är en översikt av studier från 2004 till 2014 med små autistiska barn eller barn med risk för autism, bland annat 13 randomiserade kontrollerade studier. Metoder som kombinerar utvecklingsinriktade och beteendeinriktade angreppssätt gav överlag kortsiktiga framsteg i social kommunikation; resultaten på lång sikt och för språk var blandade. Alla barn är olika, och fynden gäller inte alla.

title: Fundamental Elements in Autism: From Neurogenesis and Neurite Growth to Synaptic Plasticity.
authors: Gilbert J, Man HY
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a set of neurodevelopmental disorders with a high prevalence and impact on society. ASDs are characterized by deficits in both social behavior and cognitive function. There is a strong genetic basis underlying ASDs that is highly heterogeneous; however, multiple studies have highlighted the involvement of key processes, including neurogenesis, neurite growth, synaptogenesis and synaptic plasticity in the pathophysiology of neurodevelopmental disorders. In this review article, we focus on the major genes and signaling pathways implicated in ASD and discuss the cellular, molecular and functional studies that have shed light on common dysregulated pathways using in vitro , in vivo and human evidence. Highlights Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) has a prevalence of 1 in 68 children in the United States.ASDs are highly heterogeneous in their genetic basis.ASDs share common features at the cellular and molecular levels in the brain.Most ASD genes are implicated in neurogenesis, structural maturation, synaptogenesis and function.

sheet.es: Este artículo no ofrece nada que cambiar mañana por la mañana en casa: es un panorama de la biología del cerebro. Lo útil es saber que la base genética del autismo es muy diversa, así que cada persona autista es distinta y conviene guiarse por sus necesidades concretas. Es una revisión que reúne estudios celulares, en animales y en personas; los autores indican una prevalencia de 1 de cada 68 niños en Estados Unidos. Como es una revisión sobre mecanismos, no prueba qué apoyos funcionan ni explica a una persona concreta.
sheet.en: This article offers nothing to change at home tomorrow morning: it is an overview of brain biology. What is useful is knowing that the genetic basis of autism is very varied, so each autistic person is different and it helps to follow their specific needs. It is a review bringing together cell studies, animal studies and human evidence; the authors cite a prevalence of 1 in 68 children in the United States. As a review of mechanisms, it does not show which supports work and cannot explain any one person.
sheet.sv: Den här artikeln ger inget att ändra hemma i morgon bitti: den är en översikt över hjärnans biologi. Det användbara är att veta att autismens genetiska bas är mycket varierad, så varje autistisk person är olika och det hjälper att utgå från just hens behov. Det är en översikt som samlar cellstudier, djurstudier och studier på människor; författarna anger en förekomst på 1 av 68 barn i USA. Eftersom den handlar om mekanismer visar den inte vilka stöd som fungerar och kan inte förklara en enskild person.

title: Self-Injury in Autism Spectrum Disorder and Intellectual Disability: Exploring the Role of Reactivity to Pain and Sensory Input.
authors: Summers J, Shahrami A, Cali S, D'Mello C, Kako M, Palikucin-Reljin A, Savage M, Shaw O, Lunsky Y
abstract: This paper provides information about the prevalence and topography of self-injurious behavior in children and adults with autism spectrum disorder and intellectual disability. Dominant models regarding the etiology of self-injury in this population are reviewed, with a focus on the role of reactivity to pain and sensory input. Neuroimaging studies are presented and suggestions are offered for future research.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista con discapacidad intelectual se autolesiona, conviene observar con calma qué ocurre antes y después, y si influyen el dolor o los estímulos sensoriales (ruido, luz, tacto). Anota lo que veas y compártelo con su equipo de salud. La evidencia es una revisión que describe la frecuencia y las formas de autolesión en niños y adultos autistas con discapacidad intelectual, repasa modelos sobre sus causas, con foco en la reactividad al dolor y a lo sensorial, y presenta estudios de neuroimagen. Es una revisión: no ofrece una regla válida para cada persona y propone más investigación. Si te preocupa la seguridad de alguien, consulta a un profesional sanitario o a un servicio de crisis; ante un peligro inmediato, llama al número de emergencias de tu país.
sheet.en: If an autistic person with intellectual disability hurts themselves, it helps to calmly notice what happens before and after, and whether pain or sensory input (noise, light, touch) plays a part. Write down what you see and share it with their health team. The evidence is a review describing how common and how varied self-injury is in autistic children and adults with intellectual disability, covering models of its causes, with a focus on reactivity to pain and sensory input, plus neuroimaging studies. As a review, it gives no rule that fits every person, and it calls for more research. If you are worried about someone's safety, contact a clinician, a health service or a crisis service; in immediate danger, call the emergency number of your country.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning skadar sig själv kan det hjälpa att lugnt notera vad som händer före och efter, och om smärta eller sensoriska intryck (ljud, ljus, beröring) spelar in. Skriv ner det du ser och dela det med personens vårdteam. Underlaget är en översikt som beskriver hur vanligt och hur varierande självskadande är hos autistiska barn och vuxna med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning, går igenom modeller för orsaker med fokus på reaktivitet för smärta och sensoriska intryck, och presenterar neuroavbildningsstudier. Som översikt ger den ingen regel som passar alla och efterlyser mer forskning. Oroar du dig för någons säkerhet, kontakta en läkare, vården eller en krisjour; vid omedelbar fara, ring larmnumret i ditt land.

title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of comprehensive interventions for pre-school children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD).
authors: Tachibana Y, Miyazaki C, Ota E, Mori R, Hwang Y, Kobayashi E, Terasaka A, Tang J, Kamio Y
abstract: Background There has an increasing number of published trials on psychosocial intervention programmes for pre-school children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). To achieve better quality of unbiased evidence for the effectiveness of ASD interventions, it is necessary to conduct a comprehensive review that covers studies with adequate quality standards, such as randomised controlled trials (RCTs), and different types of intervention In this study, we categorize interventions for ASD as behavioural, social-communication focused, and multimodal developmental based on Howlin's classification of early interventions for children with ASD. The aim of this study was to compare these three models and investigate the strengths and weaknesses of each type of intervention and to identify the approaches that contribute to a successful outcome for children with autism. Methods We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis. We included RCTs targeting children with ASD 6 years old or younger. A random effects model was used to present the effect estimate for the outcomes. This study also performed combined meta-analyses of all the three models to investigate the overall effectiveness of the intervention programmes. Results 32 randomized controlled studies were found to be eligible for inclusion. The synthesized data included 594 children from 14 RCTs. There was no statistically significant difference in the effects on autism general symptoms between the social-communication-focused model and the multimodal developmental model (p = 0.83). The results suggest that there is evidence of an effect on 'reciprocity of social interaction towards others' (standard mean difference [95% confidential interval] = 0.53[0.29,0.78], p Conclusion The small number of studies included in the present study limited the ability to make inferences when comparing the three models and investigating the strengths and weaknesses of each type of intervention with respect to important outcomes. Since the outcome of 'reciprocity of social interaction towards others' could be a dependent variable that might be context-bound to interactions with the child's parent, we cannot conclude the interventions for pre-school children with ASD have significant effects on a generalized skill to engage in reciprocal interactions with others. However, the outcomes of 'reciprocity of social interaction towards others' and 'parental synchrony' may be promising targets for interventions involving pre-school children with ASD. Trial registration Prospero CRD42011001349.

sheet.es: Si valora apoyos tempranos para un niño autista en edad preescolar, puede fijarse en programas que trabajen la interacción social con la familia y la sincronía entre madre o padre e hijo, pues parecen metas prometedoras. Es un metanálisis: reunió ensayos aleatorizados con niños autistas de 6 años o menos; los datos sintetizados incluyeron 594 niños de 14 ensayos. Sus límites: pocos estudios, no permite comparar bien los tres modelos, y los avances en interacción pueden depender del contexto con la madre o el padre, así que no se sabe si se generalizan a otras personas. No es una regla para todos los niños.
sheet.en: If you are considering early support for an autistic pre-school child, you could look at programmes that work on social interaction with the family and on synchrony between parent and child, as these seem promising goals. This is a meta-analysis: it pooled randomised trials with autistic children aged 6 or younger; the synthesized data included 594 children from 14 trials. Its limits: few studies, so the three models could not be compared well, and gains in interaction may depend on the context with a parent, so it is unclear whether they carry over to other people. It is not a rule for every child.
sheet.sv: Om du överväger tidigt stöd för ett autistiskt förskolebarn kan du titta på program som tränar social interaktion med familjen och synkronin mellan förälder och barn, eftersom det verkar vara lovande mål. Detta är en metaanalys som slog ihop randomiserade studier med autistiska barn som var 6 år eller yngre; de sammanställda data omfattade 594 barn från 14 studier. Begränsningar: få studier gör att de tre modellerna inte kunde jämföras väl, och framstegen i interaktion kan vara knutna till sammanhanget med föräldern, så det är oklart om de gäller med andra människor. Det är ingen regel för alla barn.

title: Randomised trial of a parent-mediated intervention for infants at high risk for autism: longitudinal outcomes to age 3 years.
authors: Green J, Pickles A, Pasco G, Bedford R, Wan MW, Elsabbagh M, Slonims V, Gliga T, Jones E, Cheung C, Charman T, Johnson M, British Autism Study of Infant Siblings (BASIS) Team
journal: Journal of child psychology and psychiatry, and allied disciplines
abstract: Background There has been increasing interest in the potential for pre-emptive interventions in the prodrome of autism, but little investigation as to their effect. Methods A two-site, two-arm assessor-blinded randomised controlled trial (RCT) of a 12-session parent-mediated social communication intervention delivered between 9 and 14 months of age (Intervention in the British Autism Study of Infant Siblings-Video Interaction for Promoting Positive Parenting), against no intervention. Fifty-four infants (28 intervention, 26 nonintervention) at familial risk of autism but not otherwise selected for developmental atypicality were assessed at 9-month baseline, 15-month treatment endpoint, and 27- and 39-month follow-up. Primary outcome severity of autism prodromal symptoms, blind-rated on Autism Observation Schedule for Infants or Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule 2nd Edition across the four assessment points. Secondary outcomes blind-rated parent-child interaction and child language; nonblind parent-rated communication and socialisation. Prespecified intention-to-treat analysis combined estimates from repeated measures within correlated regressions to estimate the overall effect of the infancy intervention over time. Results Effect estimates in favour of intervention on autism prodromal symptoms, maximal at 27 months, had confidence intervals (CIs) at each separate time point including the null, but showed a significant overall effect over the course of the intervention and follow-up period (effect size [ES] = 0.32; 95% CI 0.04, 0.60; p = .026). Effects on proximal intervention targets of parent nondirectiveness/synchrony (ES = 0.33; CI 0.04, 0.63; p = .013) and child attentiveness/communication initiation (ES = 0.36; 95% CI 0.04, 0.68; p = .015) showed similar results. There was no effect on categorical diagnostic outcome or formal language measures. Conclusions Follow-up to 3 years of the first RCT of a very early social communication intervention for infants at familial risk of developing autism has shown a treatment effect, extending 24 months after intervention end, to reduce the overall severity of autism prodromal symptoms and enhance parent-child dyadic social communication over this period. We highlight the value of extended follow-up and repeat assessment for early intervention trials.

sheet.es: Si tiene un bebé con hermanos autistas, puede probar a seguir su ritmo: observar qué le interesa, esperar sus iniciativas y responder sin dirigir. Este ensayo aleatorizado comparó 12 sesiones de comunicación social con las familias, entre los 9 y los 14 meses de edad, frente a ninguna intervención. Participaron 54 bebés con riesgo familiar de autismo. Hubo un efecto global en señales tempranas y en la interacción entre progenitores e hijo, pero no en el diagnóstico ni en las pruebas formales de lenguaje. Es un grupo pequeño y no sirve como regla para cada niño o familia.
sheet.en: If your baby has an autistic sibling, you might try following their lead: notice what interests them, wait for their initiations and respond without directing. This randomised trial compared 12 parent-mediated social communication sessions, delivered between 9 and 14 months of age, with no intervention. It included 54 infants at familial risk of autism. There was an overall effect on early signs and on parent-child interaction, but not on diagnosis or formal language measures. The group was small, and the results are not a rule for every child or family.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn har ett autistiskt syskon kan du prova att följa barnets ledning: lägg märke till vad som intresserar, vänta in barnets initiativ och svara utan att styra. Denna randomiserade studie jämförde 12 sessioner i social kommunikation med föräldrar, mellan 9 och 14 månaders ålder, med ingen insats. Den omfattade 54 spädbarn med ärftlig sannolikhet för autism. Det fanns en samlad effekt på tidiga tecken och på samspelet mellan förälder och barn, men inte på diagnos eller formella språktest. Gruppen var liten, och resultaten är ingen regel för alla barn eller familjer.

title: Feasibility study of a randomised controlled trial to investigate the effectiveness of using a humanoid robot to improve the social skills of children with autism spectrum disorder (Kaspar RCT): a study protocol.
authors: Mengoni SE, Irvine K, Thakur D, Barton G, Dautenhahn K, Guldberg K, Robins B, Wellsted D, Sharma S
abstract: Introduction Interventions using robot-assisted therapy may be beneficial for the social skills development of children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD); however, randomised controlled trials (RCTs) are lacking. The present research aims to assess the feasibility of conducting an RCT evaluating the effectiveness of a social skills intervention using Kinesics and Synchronisation in Personal Assistant Robotics (Kaspar) with children with ASD. Methods and analysis Forty children will be recruited. Inclusion criteria are the following: aged 5-10 years, confirmed ASD diagnosis, IQ over 70, English-language comprehension, a carer who can complete questionnaires in English and no current participation in a private social communication intervention. Children will be randomised to receive an intervention with a therapist and Kaspar, or with the therapist only. They will receive two familiarisation sessions and six treatment sessions for 8 weeks. They will be assessed at baseline, and at 10 and 22 weeks after baseline. The primary outcome of this study is to evaluate whether the predetermined feasibility criteria for a full-scale trial are met. The potential primary outcome measures for a full-scale trial are the Social Communication Questionnaire and the Social Skills Improvement System. We will conduct a preliminary economic analysis. After the study has ended, a sample of 20 participants and their families will be invited to participate in semistructured interviews to explore the feasibility and acceptability of the study's methods and intervention. Ethics and dissemination Parents/carers will provide informed consent, and children will give assent, where appropriate. Care will be taken to avoid pressure or coercion to participate. Aftercare is available from the recruiting NHS Trust, and a phased withdrawal protocol will be followed if children become excessively attached to the robot. The results of the study will be disseminated to academic audiences and non-academic stakeholders, for example, families of children with ASD, support groups, clinicians and charities. Trial registration number ISRCTN registry (ISRCTN14156001); Pre-results.

sheet.es: Por ahora este estudio no ofrece resultados que puedan guiar su día a día. Si le interesa que su hijo o hija pruebe un robot social como Kaspar, pregunte a su equipo clínico qué se sabe y qué participación es posible. Es un protocolo de ensayo de viabilidad: describe cómo se probará con 40 niños de 5-10 años con diagnóstico de TEA, que trabajarán con un terapeuta con Kaspar o solo con el terapeuta. Límites: aún no hay resultados sobre eficacia, y los criterios (IQ superior a 70, comprensión del inglés) excluyen a muchas personas autistas.
sheet.en: This study does not yet give results that can guide everyday life. If you are curious about a social robot like Kaspar for your child, ask your clinical team what is known and whether taking part is possible. It is a feasibility trial protocol: it describes how 40 children aged 5-10 years with a confirmed ASD diagnosis will be tested, working with a therapist and Kaspar or with the therapist only. Limits: there are no effectiveness results yet, and the criteria (IQ over 70, English comprehension) leave out many autistic people.
sheet.sv: Den här studien ger ännu inga resultat som kan vägleda vardagen. Om du är nyfiken på en social robot som Kaspar för ditt barn, fråga vårdteamet vad som är känt och om det går att delta. Det är ett protokoll för en genomförbarhetsstudie: den beskriver hur 40 barn i åldern 5-10 år med bekräftad ASD-diagnos ska testas, antingen med en terapeut och Kaspar eller bara med terapeuten. Begränsningar: det finns inga resultat om effekt ännu, och kriterierna (IQ över 70, engelskförståelse) utesluter många autistiska personer.

title: Protocol for a feasibility study and randomised pilot trial of a low-intensity psychological intervention for depression in adults with autism: the Autism Depression Trial (ADEPT).
authors: Russell A, Cooper K, Barton S, Ensum I, Gaunt D, Horwood J, Ingham B, Kessler D, Metcalfe C, Parr J, Rai D, Wiles N
abstract: Introduction High rates of co-occurring depression are reported in autism spectrum disorder (ASD), a neurodevelopmental condition characterised by social communication impairments and repetitive behaviours. Cognitive-behavioural interventions adapted for ASD have been effective for anxiety problems. There have been evaluation studies of group cognitive-behavioural therapy for co-occurring depression, but no randomised trials investigating low-intensity psychological interventions as recommended in clinical guidelines for mild-moderate depression. Methods and analysis A feasibility study comprising a randomised controlled trial (RCT) and nested qualitative evaluation is under way as preparation for a definitive RCT. Participants (n=70) will be randomised to Guided Self-Help: a low-intensity psychological intervention based on behavioural activation adapted for ASD or treatment as usual. Outcomes including depression symptoms, anxiety, social function and service use will be measured at 10, 16 and 24 weeks postrandomisation and will be blind to group allocation for measures that are not self-administered. The analysis will aim to establish the rates of recruitment and retention for a larger-scale RCT as well as the most appropriate measure of depression to serve as primary outcome. The qualitative study will purposively sample up to 24 participants from each treatment group to consider the acceptability and feasibility of the intervention and the trial design. Ethics and dissemination Ethical approval has been received from WALES REC 3 (IRAS project ID: 191558) and the Health Research Authority with R&D approval from Avon and Wiltshire Mental Health Partnership and Northumberland, Tyne and Wear Foundation NHS Trusts. To our knowledge, this is the first study of a low-intensity intervention for depression in adults with autism. The results will inform the design of a definitive RCT. Dissemination will include peer-reviewed journal publications reporting the quantitative and qualitative research findings of the study and presentations at national and international conferences. Trial registration number ISRCTN54650760; Pre-results.

sheet.es: Por ahora no hay resultados que indiquen qué hacer mañana. Si una persona autista adulta tiene ánimo bajo, puede ser útil hablar con su médico o servicio de salud mental sobre apoyos de baja intensidad, como la autoayuda guiada basada en activación conductual adaptada al autismo. Este artículo es el protocolo de un ensayo piloto aleatorizado que planea incluir a 70 personas adultas autistas y compararlas con la atención habitual. Su objetivo es comprobar si un ensayo mayor es viable. Como aún no presenta resultados, no demuestra que la intervención funcione ni que sirva a todas las personas. Las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: There are no results yet that tell you what to do tomorrow. If an autistic adult you support has a low mood, it may help to ask their doctor or mental health service about low-intensity support, such as guided self-help based on behavioural activation adapted for autism. This paper is the protocol for a randomised pilot trial planning to include 70 autistic adults and compare the approach with usual care. Its aim is to check whether a larger trial is feasible. Because it reports no results, it does not show that the approach works or suits everyone. Medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Det finns ännu inga resultat som säger vad du bör göra i morgon. Om en autistisk vuxen du stöttar har nedstämdhet kan det hjälpa att fråga läkare eller psykiatrin om lågintensivt stöd, som guidad självhjälp baserad på beteendeaktivering anpassad för autism. Artikeln är protokollet för en randomiserad pilotstudie som planerar att inkludera 70 autistiska vuxna och jämföra metoden med sedvanlig vård. Syftet är att se om en större studie är genomförbar. Eftersom inga resultat redovisas visar den inte att metoden fungerar eller passar alla. Medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker.

title: Epilepsy in patients with autism: links, risks and treatment challenges.
authors: Besag FM
abstract: Autism is more common in people with epilepsy, approximately 20%, and epilepsy is more common in people with autism with reported rates of approximately 20%. However, these figures are likely to be affected by the current broader criteria for autism spectrum disorder (ASD), which have contributed to an increased prevalence of autism, with the result that the rate for ASD in epilepsy is likely to be higher and the figure for epilepsy in ASD is likely to be lower. Some evidence suggests that there are two peaks of epilepsy onset in autism, in infancy and adolescence. The rate of autism in epilepsy is much higher in those with intellectual disability. In conditions such as the Landau-Kleffner syndrome and nonconvulsive status epilepticus, the epilepsy itself may present with autistic features. There is no plausible mechanism for autism causing epilepsy, however. The co-occurrence of autism and epilepsy is almost certainly the result of underlying factors predisposing to both conditions, including both genetic and environmental factors. Conditions such as attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, anxiety and sleep disorders are common in both epilepsy and autism. Epilepsy is generally not a contraindication to treating these conditions with suitable medication, but it is important to take account of relevant drug interactions. One of the greatest challenges in autism is to determine why early childhood regression occurs in perhaps 25%. Further research should focus on finding the cause for such regression. Whether epilepsy plays a role in the regression of a subgroup of children with autism who lose skills remains to be determined.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista, conviene conocer los signos de epilepsia: ausencias, miradas fijas, sacudidas o pérdida repentina de habilidades. Anota cuándo ocurren y coméntalo con su equipo médico, sobre todo en la primera infancia y la adolescencia, cuando la epilepsia parece aparecer con más frecuencia. Si toma medicación para el sueño, la ansiedad o el TDAH, pregunta por posibles interacciones. Esta revisión resume estudios previos: cerca de un 20 % de personas autistas tienen epilepsia, más a menudo si hay discapacidad intelectual. Sus límites: las cifras varían según los criterios diagnósticos y no aporta datos nuevos ni aclara si la epilepsia influye en la regresión.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person, it helps to know possible signs of epilepsy: absence moments, staring spells, jerking movements or a sudden loss of skills. Note when they happen and share this with their healthcare team, especially in early childhood and adolescence, when epilepsy seems to start more often. If they take medication for sleep, anxiety or ADHD, ask about possible interactions. This review summarises earlier research: around 20% of autistic people have epilepsy, more often when intellectual disability is present. Its limits: figures shift with changing diagnostic criteria, it adds no new data, and it cannot say whether epilepsy plays a role in skill regression.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person är det bra att känna till möjliga tecken på epilepsi: frånvaroattacker, stirrande, ryckningar eller att förmågor plötsligt försvinner. Anteckna när det händer och berätta för vårdteamet, särskilt under tidig barndom och tonår, då epilepsi verkar debutera oftare. Om personen tar läkemedel för sömn, ångest eller ADHD, fråga om möjliga interaktioner. Denna översikt sammanfattar tidigare forskning: ungefär 20 % av autistiska personer har epilepsi, oftare vid intellektuell funktionsnedsättning. Begränsningar: siffrorna påverkas av ändrade diagnoskriterier, översikten ger inga nya data och kan inte avgöra om epilepsi bidrar till förlust av förmågor.

title: Antidepressant use during pregnancy and risk of autism spectrum disorder and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder: systematic review of observational studies and methodological considerations.
authors: Morales DR, Slattery J, Evans S, Kurz X
abstract: Background Antidepressant exposure during pregnancy has been associated with an increased risk of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in several observational studies. We performed a systematic review of these studies to highlight the effect that important methodological limitations have on such analyses and to consider approaches to the conduct, reporting and interpretation of future studies. Methods A review of MEDLINE and EMBASE identified case-control, cohort and sibling studies assessing the risk of ASD and ADHD with antidepressant use during pregnancy. Approaches to confounding adjustment were described. Crude and adjusted effect estimates for comparisons between antidepressant exposure during pregnancy vs. all unexposed women were first meta-analysed using a generic inverse variance method of analysis, followed by effect estimates for alternative pre-selected comparison groups. Results A total of 15 studies measuring ASD as an outcome (involving 3,585,686 children and 40,585 cases) and seven studies measuring ADHD as an outcome (involving 2,765,723 patients and 52,313 cases) were identified. Variation in confounding adjustment existed between studies. Updated effect estimates for the association between maternal antidepressant exposure during pregnancy vs. all unexposed women remained statistically significant for ASD (adjusted random-effects risk ratio [RaRR] 1.53, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.31-1.78). Similar significant associations were observed using pre-pregnancy maternal antidepressant exposure (RaRR 1.48, 95% CI 1.29-1.71) and paternal antidepressant exposure during pregnancy (1.29, 95% CI 1.08-1.53), but analyses restricted to using women with a history of affective disorder (1.18, 95% CI 0.91-1.52) and sibling studies (0.96, 95% CI 0.65-1.42) were not statistically significant. Corresponding associations for risk of ADHD with exposure were: RaRR 1.38, 95% CI 1.13-1.69 (during pregnancy), RaRR 1.38, 95% CI 1.14-1.69 (during pre-pregnancy), RaRR 1.71, 95% CI 1.31-2.23 (paternal exposure), RaRR 0.98, 95% CI 0.77-1.24 (women with a history of affective disorder) and RaRR 0.88, 95% CI 0.70-1.11 (sibling studies). Conclusions Existing observational studies measuring the risk of ASD and ADHD with antidepressant exposure are heterogeneous in their design. Classical comparisons between exposed and unexposed women during pregnancy are at high risk of residual confounding. Alternative comparisons and sibling designs may aid the interpretation of causality and their utility requires further evaluation, including understanding potential limitations of undertaking meta-analyses with such data.

sheet.es: Si estás embarazada o cuidas a alguien que lo está, y tomas antidepresivos, no cambies nada por tu cuenta: las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico. Esta revisión con metaanálisis de estudios observacionales halló asociaciones entre antidepresivos en el embarazo y autismo, pero no en todos los análisis: con mujeres con antecedentes de trastorno afectivo y con estudios de hermanos no fueron significativas.
