Incluyó 15 estudios sobre autismo. Sus límites: los estudios observacionales no prueban causa y hay riesgo alto de factores de confusión que no se pudieron separar.
sheet.en: If you are pregnant, or support someone who is, and take antidepressants, do not change anything on your own: medical decisions belong to a clinician. This meta-analysis of observational studies found associations between antidepressants in pregnancy and autism, but not in every analysis: those limited to women with a history of affective disorder and sibling studies were not statistically significant. It included 15 studies on autism. Its limits: observational studies cannot prove cause, and there is a high risk of confounding that could not be fully separated out.
sheet.sv: Om du är gravid, eller stödjer någon som är det, och tar antidepressiva läkemedel: ändra inget på egen hand, eftersom medicinska beslut hör till en läkare. Denna metaanalys av observationsstudier fann samband mellan antidepressiva under graviditet och autism, men inte i alla analyser: de som begränsades till kvinnor med tidigare affektiv sjukdom och syskonstudierna var inte statistiskt signifikanta. Den omfattade 15 studier om autism. Begränsningar: observationsstudier kan inte bevisa orsak, och risken för störfaktorer som inte kunde särskiljas är hög.

title: Experiences of Autism Acceptance and Mental Health in Autistic Adults.
authors: Cage E, Di Monaco J, Newell V
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Mental health difficulties are highly prevalent in individuals on the autism spectrum. The current study examined how experiences and perceptions of autism acceptance could impact on the mental health of autistic adults. 111 adults on the autism spectrum completed an online survey examining their experiences of autism acceptance, along with symptoms of depression, anxiety and stress. Regression analyses showed that autism acceptance from external sources and personal acceptance significantly predicted depression. Acceptance from others also significantly predicted stress but acceptance did not predict anxiety. Further analyses suggested that experiences of "camouflaging" could relate to higher rates of depression. The current study highlights the importance of considering how autism acceptance could contribute to mental health in autism.

sheet.es: Mostrar aceptación del autismo en el día a día puede importar para el bienestar emocional de una persona autista: escucha sin corregir, valora su forma de ser y deja espacio para que no tenga que ocultarla. Es una pista, no una regla. Evidencia: 111 personas adultas autistas respondieron una encuesta en línea sobre aceptación, depresión, ansiedad y estrés. La aceptación de otras personas y la personal se relacionaron con la depresión, la de otras personas también con el estrés, y el "camuflaje" se asoció con más depresión. Límites: la encuesta solo muestra relaciones, no causas, y no refleja a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: Showing acceptance of autism in everyday life may matter for an autistic person's emotional wellbeing: listen without correcting, value how they are, and leave room so they don't have to hide it. This is a clue, not a rule. Evidence: 111 autistic adults completed an online survey about acceptance, depression, anxiety and stress. Acceptance from others and personal acceptance were linked to depression, acceptance from others was also linked to stress, and "camouflaging" was associated with higher depression. Limits: a survey shows links, not causes, and it does not represent every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Att visa acceptans för autism i vardagen kan spela roll för en autistisk persons psykiska välmående: lyssna utan att korrigera, värdera hur personen är och ge utrymme så att hen inte behöver dölja det. Det är en fingervisning, inte en regel. Evidens: 111 autistiska vuxna besvarade en webbenkät om acceptans, depression, ångest och stress. Acceptans från andra och egen acceptans hängde ihop med depression, acceptans från andra även med stress, och "kamouflering" kopplades till mer depression. Begränsningar: en enkät visar samband, inte orsaker, och speglar inte alla autistiska personer.

title: Designing a Summer Transition Program for Incoming and Current College Students on the Autism Spectrum: A Participatory Approach.
authors: Hotez E, Shane-Simpson C, Obeid R, DeNigris D, Siller M, Costikas C, Pickens J, Massa A, Giannola M, D'Onofrio J, Gillespie-Lynch K
abstract: Students with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) face unique challenges transitioning from high school to college and receive insufficient support to help them navigate this transition. Through a participatory collaboration with incoming and current autistic college students, we developed, implemented, and evaluated two intensive week-long summer programs to help autistic students transition into and succeed in college. This process included: (1) developing an initial summer transition program curriculum guided by recommendations from autistic college students in our ongoing mentorship program, (2) conducting an initial feasibility assessment of the curriculum [Summer Transition Program 1 (STP1)], (3) revising our initial curriculum, guided by feedback from autistic students, to develop a curriculum manual, and (4) pilot-testing the manualized curriculum through a quasi-experimental pre-test/post-test assessment of a second summer program [Summer Transition Program 2 (STP2)]. In STP2, two autistic college students assumed a leadership role and acted as "mentors" and ten incoming and current autistic college students participated in the program as "mentees." Results from the STP2 pilot-test suggested benefits of participatory transition programming for fostering self-advocacy and social skills among mentees. Autistic and non-autistic mentors (but not mentees) described practicing advanced forms of self-advocacy, specifically leadership, through their mentorship roles. Autistic and non-autistic mentors also described shared (e.g., empathy) and unique (an intuitive understanding of autism vs. an intuitive understanding of social interaction) skills that they contributed to the program. This research provides preliminary support for the feasibility and utility of a participatory approach in which autistic college students are integral to the development and implementation of programming to help less experienced autistic students develop the self-advocacy skills they will need to succeed in college.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a un joven autista que empieza la universidad, busca programas de transición de verano en los que estudiantes autistas con más experiencia participen como mentores y ayuden a diseñarlos. Practicar cómo pedir apoyos antes de empezar puede ayudar. La evidencia es una prueba piloto con diez estudiantes autistas, además de dos que actuaron como mentores, que sugirió beneficios para la autodefensa y las habilidades sociales. Los límites: el grupo era muy pequeño, el apoyo es preliminar y los resultados no valen para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic young person starting college, look for summer transition programs where more experienced autistic students act as mentors and help shape the program. Practising how to ask for support before term starts may help. The evidence is a pilot test with ten autistic students, plus two who acted as mentors, which suggested benefits for self-advocacy and social skills. Limits: the group was very small, the support is preliminary, and the results will not apply to every person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk ung person som ska börja på college eller universitet, leta efter sommarprogram för övergången där mer erfarna autistiska studenter är mentorer och är med och utformar programmet. Att öva på att be om stöd innan terminen börjar kan hjälpa. Underlaget är ett pilottest med tio autistiska studenter, plus två som var mentorer, och det tydde på fördelar för självadvokatur och sociala färdigheter. Begränsningar: gruppen var mycket liten, stödet är preliminärt och resultaten gäller inte alla personer.

title: Understanding, Recognising and Treating Co-occurring Anxiety in Autism.
authors: Rodgers J, Ofield A
abstract: Purpose of review Autistic people are at increased risk of anxiety, with around 50% of autistic adults and children experiencing this debilitating mental health condition. The purpose of this review is to consider some contemporary ideas about underlying mechanisms for anxiety in autism, explore issues in the identification and assessment of anxiety and discuss emerging trends in anxiety interventions for autistic people, before identifying some important next steps in the field. Recent findings Emerging evidence suggests that anxiety may present differently in autism compared to the general population and that whilst CBT holds promise, there may be important differences in neurobiological, affective and cognitive responses to stressors for autistic people, which warrant tailored anxiety models, assessments and interventions. Summary We conclude that research is needed to develop and evaluate theoretical frameworks, assessment methods and interventions for anxiety in autism, particularly for autistic adults and those with co-occurring intellectual disability.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista, tenlo presente: la ansiedad puede mostrarse de forma distinta y conviene observarla con atención, sin darla por "carácter". Anota qué situaciones la preceden y habla con un profesional de la salud sobre lo que ves. Esta es una revisión de la literatura sobre ansiedad en personas autistas, niñas, niños y adultas. Indica que alrededor del 50% la experimenta y que la TCC es prometedora, pero que hacen falta enfoques adaptados. Sus límites: no es un estudio nuevo, no ofrece una pauta para cada persona y hay poca investigación con adultas y con discapacidad intelectual.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person, keep in mind that anxiety may look different and deserves close attention rather than being dismissed as personality. Note which situations come before it, and talk with a health professional about what you see. This is a review of the literature on anxiety in autistic children and adults. It reports that around 50% experience anxiety and that CBT is promising, but that tailored approaches are needed. Its limits: it is not a new study, it is not a rule for every person, and there is little research on autistic adults or those with co-occurring intellectual disability.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person: ångest kan se annorlunda ut och förtjänar uppmärksamhet, snarare än att avfärdas som personlighet. Notera vilka situationer som föregår den och prata med en vårdgivare om det du ser. Det här är en översikt av forskning om ångest hos autistiska barn och vuxna. Den anger att omkring 50% upplever ångest och att KBT är lovande, men att anpassade angreppssätt behövs. Begränsningar: det är inte en ny studie, den ger ingen regel för alla, och det finns lite forskning om autistiska vuxna eller de med samtidig intellektuell funktionsnedsättning.

title: Study protocol: a randomized controlled trial study on the effect of a game-based exercise training program on promoting physical fitness and mental health in children with autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Yu CCW, Wong SWL, Lo FSF, So RCH, Chan DFY
abstract: Background Suboptimal physical activity levels and tolerance, poor motor skills and poor physical health are demonstrated in children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). We speculate that social interaction and communication deficits in children with ASD are two major factors that hinder these children from actively participating in group physical activities. While previous studies have demonstrated that exercise intervention improves motor skills and behavioral outcomes in children with ASD, these programs tend to focus only on a single sport, which may not cater to the interests of different children with ASD. In this protocol, a game-based exercise training program designed by a multi-disciplinary team (pediatrics, physical education and psychology) will be implemented by front-line healthcare providers trained following the train-the-trainer (TTT) model and subjected to validation. Method Using a randomized controlled trial design, the effectiveness of the game-based exercise program will be examined for 112 young children with ASD. These children were randomly assigned to two groups, which will be tested and trained in either one of the two arms of the waitlist conditions (control and intervention). The assessment of physical and psychological traits will be conducted at baseline (pre-test), at 16-weeks (post-treatment) and at 32-weeks (follow-up) of the program. Discussion Most of the interventions designed for ASD children target either their psychological traits or physical conditions, without bridging the two states. With the recognition of bidirectional relations between mental and physical health, the present game-based exercise program which includes multiple level of difficulties was developed to equip ASD children with the necessary skills for engaging in sustainable team sports or even professional sport training. The program, if effective, will provide an entertaining and engaging training for whole-person development among children with ASD. Trial registration This study is registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry ( ChiCTR-IOR-17011898 ). Registered 6 th July 2017.

sheet.es: Si quiere animar a una niña o un niño autista a moverse, puede probar juegos con distintos niveles de dificultad en lugar de un solo deporte, y elegir los que más le interesen. Este es un protocolo de un ensayo aleatorizado: describe cómo se evaluará un programa de juegos con ejercicio en 112 niños autistas pequeños, con evaluaciones a las 16 y a las 32 semanas. Aún no ofrece resultados, así que no sabemos si el programa funciona. Tampoco significa que sirva a todas las personas; los intereses y necesidades sensoriales de cada niño cuentan.
sheet.en: If you want to encourage an autistic child to move, you could try games with different levels of difficulty rather than a single sport, and follow the ones that interest them most. This is a protocol for a randomized controlled trial: it describes how a game-based exercise program will be tested with 112 young autistic children, with assessments at 16 and 32 weeks. It reports no results yet, so we do not know whether the program works. It also cannot tell us what suits every child; each child's interests and sensory needs matter.
sheet.sv: Om du vill uppmuntra ett autistiskt barn att röra sig kan du prova lekar med olika svårighetsnivåer i stället för en enda sport, och utgå från det som barnet tycker mest om. Detta är ett protokoll för en randomiserad kontrollerad studie: det beskriver hur ett lekbaserat träningsprogram ska testas med 112 små autistiska barn, med bedömningar efter 16 och 32 veckor. Det redovisar inga resultat än, så vi vet inte om programmet fungerar. Det säger heller inte vad som passar alla barn; varje barns intressen och sensoriska behov räknas.

title: Assessing Quality of Program Environments for Children and Youth with Autism: Autism Program Environment Rating Scale (APERS).
authors: Odom SL, Cox A, Sideris J, Hume KA, Hedges S, Kucharczyk S, Shaw E, Boyd BA, Reszka S, Neitzel J
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: The purpose of this study was to examine the psychometric properties of the Autism Program Environment Rating Scale (APERS), an instrument designed to assess quality of program environments for students with autism spectrum disorder. Data sets from two samples of public school programs that provided services to children and youth with autism spectrum disorder were utilized. Cronbach alpha analyses indicated high coefficients of internal consistency for the total APERS and moderate levels for item domains for the first data set, which was replicated with the second data set. A factor analysis of the first data set indicated that all domain scores loaded on one main factor, in alignment with the conceptual model, with this finding being replicated in the second data set. Also, the APERS was sensitive to changes resulting from a professional development program designed to promote program quality.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a un niño o joven autista en un programa escolar, puedes preguntar si el centro evalúa la calidad de su entorno con una herramienta como la APERS, y usar esa información para pedir mejoras concretas. Es un estudio que analizó las propiedades de medición de esta escala con datos de dos muestras de programas escolares públicos que atienden a estudiantes autistas. La escala resultó consistente y detectó cambios tras un programa de formación profesional. Sin embargo, el estudio mide la herramienta, no el bienestar de cada estudiante, y no demuestra que sirva igual en todos los centros ni para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic child or young person in a school program, you can ask whether the school assesses the quality of their environment with a tool like the APERS, and use the results to request specific improvements. This study examined the measurement properties of the scale, using data from two samples of public school programs serving autistic students. The scale was consistent and picked up changes after a professional development program. However, the study tests the tool, not each student's wellbeing, and it does not show that it works the same in every school or for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar ett autistiskt barn eller en ung person i en skolverksamhet kan du fråga om skolan bedömer kvaliteten på miljön med ett verktyg som APERS, och använda resultaten för att be om konkreta förbättringar. Studien undersökte skalans mätegenskaper med data från två urval av offentliga skolprogram för autistiska elever. Skalan var tillförlitlig och fångade upp förändringar efter ett fortbildningsprogram för personal. Studien prövar dock verktyget, inte varje elevs välbefinnande, och visar inte att det fungerar likadant i alla skolor eller för alla personer.

title: Mental Health Interventions for Parent Carers of Children with Autistic Spectrum Disorder: Practice Guidelines from a Critical Interpretive Synthesis (CIS) Systematic Review.
authors: Catalano D, Holloway L, Mpofu E
journal: International journal of environmental research and public health
abstract: Parent carers of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) often report increased levels of stress, depression, and anxiety. Unmet parent carer mental health needs pose a significant risk to the psychological, physical, and social well-being of the parents of the child affected by ASD and jeopardize the adaptive functioning of the family as well as the potential of the child affected by ASD. This systematic review identifies key qualities of interventions supporting the mental health of parent carers and proposes practitioner-parent carer support guidelines. A search of four databases (Medline, PubMed, PsycINFO, and Social Science Data) was conducted to identify studies that met the following criteria: (1) an intervention was delivered to parent carers of a child with ASD under the age of 18 years; (2) the research design allowed for a comparison on outcomes across groups; and (3) outcome measures of the parent carers' mental health were used. A total of 23 studies met the inclusion criteria. A critical interpretive synthesis approach was used to produce an integrated conceptualization of the evidence. Findings suggest practitioner guidelines to support the mental health and wellbeing of parent carers should include addressing the parent's self-perspective taking and skill for real time problem-solving.

sheet.es: Cuidar tu propia salud mental no es un lujo: también sostiene a tu familia. Si buscas apoyo, puede ayudarte elegir programas que te enseñen a mirar tus propios pensamientos y emociones con más amabilidad y a resolver problemas en el momento, en situaciones reales del día a día. Pedir ayuda para ti es legítimo. Esta revisión sistemática analizó 23 estudios con grupos de comparación sobre intervenciones para madres y padres de niños y niñas autistas menores de 18 años, y propone pautas para profesionales. Sus límites: los estudios eran variados, el método es interpretativo y no indica qué programa concreto funciona mejor para cada familia.
sheet.en: Looking after your own mental health is not a luxury: it also supports your whole family. If you look for support, it may help to choose programmes that teach you to notice your own thoughts and feelings with more kindness and to solve problems in the moment, in real everyday situations. Asking for help for yourself is legitimate. This systematic review looked at 23 studies with comparison groups on interventions for parents of autistic children under 18, and proposes guidelines for practitioners. Its limits: the studies varied widely, the method is interpretive, and it does not show which specific programme works best for each family.
sheet.sv: Att ta hand om din egen psykiska hälsa är ingen lyx: det stöttar också hela familjen. Om du söker stöd kan det hjälpa att välja program som lär dig att se dina egna tankar och känslor med mer vänlighet och att lösa problem i stunden, i verkliga vardagssituationer. Att be om hjälp för din egen skull är helt rimligt. Denna systematiska översikt granskade 23 studier med jämförelsegrupper om insatser för föräldrar till autistiska barn under 18 år och föreslår riktlinjer för yrkesverksamma. Begränsningar: studierna var mycket olika, metoden är tolkande och den visar inte vilket program som fungerar bäst för varje familj.

title: The Autism Family Experience Questionnaire (AFEQ): An Ecologically-Valid, Parent-Nominated Measure of Family Experience, Quality of Life and Prioritised Outcomes for Early Intervention.
authors: Leadbitter K, Aldred C, McConachie H, Le Couteur A, Kapadia D, Charman T, Macdonald W, Salomone E, Emsley R, Green J, PACT Consortium
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: There is a lack of measures that reflect the intervention priorities of parents of children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and that assess the impact of interventions on family experience and quality of life. The Autism Family Experience Questionnaire (AFEQ) was developed through focus groups and online consultation with parents, and reflected parental priorities. It was then administered to the parents of children enrolled in the Pre-school Autism Communication Trial and its 6-year follow-up study. The AFEQ showed good convergent validity with well-established measures of child adaptive functioning, parental mental health and parental wellbeing. It was sensitive to change in response to a parent-mediated intervention for young children with autism, showing treatment effect at treatment endpoint which increased at six-year follow-up.

sheet.es: Si participas en una intervención temprana, puedes pedir que también se valore cómo vive la familia el día a día y su calidad de vida, no solo lo que hace tu hijo o hija. Este estudio, dentro de un ensayo, creó un cuestionario con grupos de debate y consulta en línea con madres y padres, y lo usó con familias del Pre-school Autism Communication Trial y su seguimiento a 6 años. Mostró relación con medidas de bienestar y salud mental de los padres, y detectó cambios tras una intervención mediada por los padres. Es una herramienta de investigación; no sustituye la conversación con tu equipo profesional ni vale igual para todas las familias.
sheet.en: If you take part in early support, you can ask that it also looks at how family life feels day to day and at family quality of life, not only at what your child does. This study, part of a trial, built a questionnaire with parent focus groups and online consultation, then used it with families from the Pre-school Autism Communication Trial and its 6-year follow-up. It linked with measures of parental wellbeing and mental health, and picked up change after a parent-mediated intervention. It is a research tool; it does not replace talking with your professional team, and it may not fit every family.
sheet.sv: Om ni deltar i tidigt stöd kan du be om att man också tittar på hur familjelivet känns i vardagen och på familjens livskvalitet, inte bara på vad ditt barn gör. Studien, som ingick i en prövning, tog fram ett frågeformulär med fokusgrupper och onlinesamråd med föräldrar och använde det med familjer från Pre-school Autism Communication Trial och dess uppföljning efter 6 år. Formuläret hängde ihop med mått på föräldrars välbefinnande och psykiska hälsa och fångade förändring efter en förälderförmedlad insats. Det är ett forskningsverktyg; det ersätter inte samtal med ert team och passar inte nödvändigtvis alla familjer.

title: Color Afterimages in Autistic Adults.
authors: Maule J, Stanworth K, Pellicano E, Franklin A
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: It has been suggested that attenuated adaptation to visual stimuli in autism is the result of atypical perceptual priors (e.g., Pellicano and Burr in Trends Cogn Sci 16(10):504-510, 2012. doi: 10.1016/j.tics.2012.08.009 ). This study investigated adaptation to color in autistic adults, measuring both strength of afterimage and the influence of top-down knowledge. We found no difference in color afterimage strength between autistic and typical adults. Effects of top-down knowledge on afterimage intensity shown by Lupyan (Acta Psychol 161:117-130, 2015. doi: 10.1016/j.actpsy.2015.08.006 ) were not replicated for either group. This study finds intact color adaptation in autistic adults. This is in contrast to findings of attenuated adaptation to faces and numerosity in autistic children. Future research should investigate the possibility of developmental differences in adaptation and further examine top-down effects on adaptation.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta ve colores de forma intensa o distinta, no hay que suponer que su adaptación al color funcione de otra manera: este estudio no encontró esa diferencia. Es una investigación con personas autistas adultas y adultas no autistas, que midió la intensidad de las posimágenes de color, esas manchas de color que se ven al mirar a otro lado tras fijar la vista en una imagen. No hubo diferencias entre ambos grupos. Sus límites: no explica las experiencias sensoriales de cada persona, y los resultados en niños o con otros estímulos, como las caras, pueden ser distintos. Lo más útil sigue siendo preguntar a cada persona cómo percibe su entorno.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult sees or experiences colour in their own way, don't assume their colour adaptation works differently: this study found no such difference. It was research with autistic adults and non-autistic adults, measuring how strong colour afterimages were, the ghostly colours you see when you look away after staring at an image. The two groups did not differ. Its limits: it cannot explain any one person's sensory experiences, and results in children or with other things, such as faces, may be different. The most useful step is still to ask each person how they experience their surroundings.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen upplever färger på sitt eget sätt, anta inte att färganpassningen fungerar annorlunda: den här studien fann ingen sådan skillnad. Det var forskning med autistiska vuxna och icke-autistiska vuxna, där man mätte hur starka färgefterbilder var, de färgskuggor man ser när man tittar bort efter att ha stirrat på en bild. Grupperna skilde sig inte åt. Begränsningar: studien kan inte förklara en enskild persons sinnesupplevelser, och resultat hos barn eller med andra stimuli, som ansikten, kan se annorlunda ut. Det mest användbara är fortfarande att fråga varje person hur hen upplever sin omgivning.

title: Parents Suggest Which Indicators of Progress and Outcomes Should be Measured in Young Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: McConachie H, Livingstone N, Morris C, Beresford B, Le Couteur A, Gringras P, Garland D, Jones G, Macdonald G, Williams K, Parr JR
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Evaluation of interventions for children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is hampered by the multitude of outcomes measured and tools used. Measurement in research with young children tends to focus on core impairments in ASD. We conducted a systematic review of qualitative studies of what matters to parents. Parent advisory groups completed structured activities to explore their perceptions of the relative importance of a wide range of outcome constructs. Their highest ranked outcomes impacted directly on everyday life and functioning (anxiety, distress, hypersensitivity, sleep problems, happiness, relationships with brothers and sisters, and parent stress). Collaboration between professionals, researchers and parents/carers is required to determine an agreed core set of outcomes to use across evaluation research.

sheet.es: Cuando valores si un apoyo funciona para tu hijo o hija, puedes fijarte en lo que cambia el día a día: si duerme mejor, si siente menos ansiedad o malestar, cómo vive las sensibilidades sensoriales, si se le ve feliz, cómo se relaciona con sus hermanos y cuánto estrés hay en casa. Es legítimo pedir a los profesionales que midan también estas cosas. La evidencia procede de una revisión sistemática de estudios cualitativos sobre lo que importa a las familias, junto con grupos asesores de padres y madres de niños pequeños autistas. Sus límites: refleja la visión de los padres, no la de los propios niños autistas, y las prioridades de cada familia pueden ser distintas.
sheet.en: When you judge whether a support is working for your child, you can look at what changes everyday life: better sleep, less anxiety or distress, how sensory sensitivities are going, whether your child seems happy, how they get on with siblings, and how much stress there is at home. It is reasonable to ask professionals to track these things too. The evidence comes from a systematic review of qualitative studies on what matters to families, plus advisory groups of parents of young autistic children. Its limits: it reflects parents' views rather than those of autistic children themselves, and each family's priorities may differ.
sheet.sv: När du bedömer om ett stöd fungerar för ditt barn kan du titta på det som förändrar vardagen: bättre sömn, mindre oro eller stress, hur sensoriska känsligheter fungerar, om barnet verkar glatt, hur relationen till syskonen är och hur mycket stress det finns i familjen. Det är rimligt att be yrkespersoner att följa upp även detta. Underlaget är en systematisk översikt av kvalitativa studier om vad som är viktigt för familjer, kompletterad med rådgivande grupper av föräldrar till unga autistiska barn. Begränsningar: den speglar föräldrarnas syn snarare än de autistiska barnens egen, och varje familjs prioriteringar kan skilja sig.

title: Rationale and design for cognitive behavioral therapy for anxiety disorders in children with autism spectrum disorder: a study protocol of a randomized controlled trial.
authors: Kilburn TR, Sørensen MJ, Thastum M, Rapee RM, Rask CU, Arendt KB, Thomsen PH
abstract: Background Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is found in approximately 1% of the population and includes core symptoms that affect general and social development. Beside these core symptoms, it is suggested that up to 60% of children with ASD suffer from comorbid anxiety disorders which may further affect educational, social and general development as well as quality of life. The main goal of this study is to examine the effectiveness of a manualized cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) anxiety program adapted for children with ASD. Methods This study is a randomized controlled trial (RCT). Fifty children with ASD and anxiety, aged 7 to 13 years, will be randomly assigned to group CBT or a wait-list control (WL) condition. The design will follow a two (CBT and WL) by two (pre-post assessment) mixed between-within design. The control group will receive intervention after the waitlist period of 13 weeks. Primary outcomes are diagnostic status and severity of the anxiety disorders, measured with The Anxiety Disorder Interview Schedule for DSM-IV, Parent and Child Versions. Secondary outcomes are parent and child ratings on questionnaires on the child's level of anxiety and impact on everyday life. Additional outcomes entail information gathered from parents, child and teachers on the child's behavior and negative self-statements, together with social and adaptive skills. Follow-up data will be collected 3 months after intervention. Discussion This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a manualized CBT program in Danish children with ASD and anxiety within a mental health clinic setting. The hypothesis is that training anxiety reduction skills will decrease anxiety in children, as well as ensure better psychosocial development for the child in general. Trial registration https://ClinicalTrials.gov ( NCT02908321 ). Registered 19th of September 2016.

sheet.es: Si su hijo autista tiene mucha ansiedad, existen programas de terapia cognitivo-conductual (TCC) en grupo adaptados para niños autistas, y puede preguntar por ellos en un servicio de salud mental infantil. Este artículo es el protocolo de un ensayo aleatorizado: describe cómo se evaluará, no presenta resultados. Participarán 50 niños autistas con ansiedad, de 7 a 13 años, en TCC en grupo o en lista de espera de 13 semanas. Como aún no hay resultados, no sabemos si funciona, y el estudio es danés, en una clínica, así que puede no aplicarse a todas las personas.
sheet.en: If your autistic child has a lot of anxiety, group cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) programs adapted for autistic children exist, and you can ask about them at a child mental health service. This paper is the protocol of a randomized trial: it describes how the study will be done, not results. It plans to include 50 autistic children with anxiety, aged 7 to 13 years, assigned to group CBT or a 13-week wait-list. Because there are no results yet, we do not know whether it works, and the study is Danish and clinic-based, so it may not fit every person.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn har mycket ångest finns det gruppbaserad kognitiv beteendeterapi (KBT) anpassad för autistiska barn, och du kan fråga om den hos barnpsykiatrin eller en annan vårdgivare. Artikeln är ett protokoll för en randomiserad studie: den beskriver hur studien ska genomföras, inte några resultat. Den planerar att inkludera 50 autistiska barn med ångest, 7 till 13 år, som lottas till grupp-KBT eller en väntelista på 13 veckor. Eftersom resultat saknas vet vi ännu inte om det fungerar, och studien är dansk och klinikbaserad, så den passar inte nödvändigtvis alla.

title: Enhancing the Validity of a Quality of Life Measure for Autistic People.
authors: McConachie H, Mason D, Parr JR, Garland D, Wilson C, Rodgers J
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Accurate measurement of quality of life (QoL) is important for evaluation of autism services and trials of interventions. We undertook psychometric validation of the World Health Organisation measure-WHOQoL-BREF, examined construct validity of the WHO Disabilities module and developed nine additional autism-specific items (ASQoL) from extensive consultation with the autism community. The sample of 309 autistic people was recruited from the Adult Autism Spectrum Cohort-UK. The WHOQoL-BREF had good psychometric properties, including criterion, convergent, divergent and discriminant validity. The WHO Disabilities module showed adequate construct validity and reliability. The ASQoL items form a unitary factor of QoL, with one global item. Future studies can use the WHO measures alongside the ASQoL items to measure QoL of autistic people.

sheet.es: Si una clínica, un servicio o un estudio quiere medir la calidad de vida de una persona autista adulta, puede preguntar qué cuestionario usa y si incluye preguntas específicas sobre autismo. Este estudio con 309 personas autistas del Adult Autism Spectrum Cohort-UK validó un cuestionario de la OMS, el WHOQoL-BREF, y creó nueve preguntas adicionales (ASQoL) tras consultar con la comunidad autista. El cuestionario mostró buenas propiedades de medición y las preguntas nuevas forman un único factor de calidad de vida. Límites: es una prueba de un instrumento de medida, no de una ayuda concreta, y no dice cómo vive cada persona ni qué le conviene.
sheet.en: If a clinic, service or study wants to measure the quality of life of an autistic adult, you can ask which questionnaire it uses and whether it includes autism-specific questions. This study of 309 autistic people from the Adult Autism Spectrum Cohort-UK tested a World Health Organisation questionnaire, the WHOQoL-BREF, and created nine extra items (ASQoL) after consulting the autism community. The questionnaire showed good measurement properties, and the new items form a single quality of life factor. Limits: it tests a measurement tool, not a support or intervention, and it cannot say how any one person lives or what would help them.
sheet.sv: Om en klinik, en verksamhet eller en studie vill mäta livskvaliteten hos en autistisk vuxen kan du fråga vilket frågeformulär som används och om det har autismspecifika frågor. Studien omfattade 309 autistiska personer från Adult Autism Spectrum Cohort-UK. Den prövade ett frågeformulär från WHO, WHOQoL-BREF, och tog fram nio extra frågor (ASQoL) efter samråd med autismgemenskapen. Formuläret hade goda mätegenskaper, och de nya frågorna bildar en gemensam faktor för livskvalitet. Begränsningar: studien prövar ett mätverktyg, inte ett stöd eller en insats, och säger inte hur en enskild person har det eller vad som hjälper.

title: Parenting Stress and Resilience in Parents of Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) in Southeast Asia: A Systematic Review.
authors: Ilias K, Cornish K, Kummar AS, Park MS, Golden KJ
abstract: Background: This paper aimed to review the literature on the factors associated with parenting stress and resilience among parents of children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in the South East Asia (SEA) region. Methods: An extensive search of articles in multiple online databases (PsycNET, ProQuest, PudMed, EMBASE, CINAHL, Web of Science, and Google Scholar) resulted in 28 papers that met the inclusion criteria (i.e., conducted in the SEA region, specific to ASD only, published in a peer-reviewed journal, full text in English). Studies found were conducted in the following countries: Brunei, n = 1; Indonesia, n = 2; Malaysia, n = 12; Philippines, n = 5; Singapore, n = 5, Thailand, n = 2; and Vietnam, n = 1, but none from Cambodia, East Timor, Laos, and Myanmar were identified. Results: Across the studies, six main factors were found to be associated with parenting stress: social support, severity of autism symptoms, financial difficulty, parents' perception and understanding toward ASD, parents' anxiety and worries about their child's future, and religious beliefs. These six factors could also be categorized as either a source of parenting stress or a coping strategy/resilience mechanism that may attenuate parenting stress. Conclusion: The findings suggest that greater support services in Western countries may underlie the cultural differences observed in the SEA region. Limitations in the current review were identified. The limited number of studies yielded from the search suggests a need for expanded research on ASD and parenting stress, coping, and resilience in the SEA region especially in Cambodia, East Timor, Laos, and Myanmar. The identified stress and resilience factors may serve as sociocultural markers for clinicians, psychologists, and other professionals to consider when supporting parents of children with ASD.

sheet.es: Su propio bienestar importa. Mañana puede dar un paso pequeño: pedir ayuda concreta a alguien de confianza, buscar información fiable sobre el autismo o anotar qué le preocupa del futuro para hablarlo con un profesional. En esta revisión, el apoyo social, comprender mejor el autismo y, para algunas familias, la fe se asociaron con menos estrés; las dificultades económicas y la preocupación por el futuro, con más. Es una revisión sistemática de 28 estudios con madres y padres de niños autistas en siete países del Sudeste Asiático. Sus límites: los estudios eran pocos y desiguales (casi la mitad de Malasia), solo en inglés, y muestran asociaciones, no causas; lo que ayuda varía en cada familia.
sheet.en: Your own wellbeing matters. Tomorrow you could take one small step: ask someone you trust for a specific kind of help, look for reliable information about autism, or jot down your worries about the future to discuss with a professional. In this review, social support, understanding autism better and, for some families, faith were linked with lower stress; money difficulties and worry about the future were linked with higher stress. It is a systematic review of 28 studies of parents of autistic children in seven Southeast Asian countries. Limits: studies were few and uneven (nearly half from Malaysia), English-only, and show associations rather than causes; what helps differs between families.
sheet.sv: Ditt eget mående spelar roll. I morgon kan du ta ett litet steg: be någon du litar på om en konkret sorts hjälp, söka pålitlig information om autism eller skriva ner dina oror inför framtiden för att ta upp med en professionell. I denna översikt hängde socialt stöd, bättre förståelse för autism och, för vissa familjer, tro ihop med mindre stress; ekonomiska svårigheter och oro för framtiden hängde ihop med mer stress. Det är en systematisk översikt av 28 studier med föräldrar till autistiska barn i sju länder i Sydostasien. Begränsningar: studierna var få och ojämnt fördelade (nästan hälften från Malaysia), bara på engelska, och visar samband, inte orsaker; vad som hjälper skiljer sig mellan familjer.

title: Systematic review: cultural adaptation and feasibility of screening for autism in non-English speaking countries.
authors: Al Maskari TS, Melville CA, Willis DS
journal: International journal of mental health systems
abstract: Background Screening children for autism has gained wider acceptance within clinical practice, and early intervention has improved outcomes. Increasingly, adapting an existing screening instrument is a common, fast method to create a usable screening tool, especially for countries with limited resources and/or expertise. However, concerns have been raised regarding adaptation adequacy and the feasibility of screening across cultural groups. This study systematically examined the levels of cultural adaptation and feasibility aspects considered when screening for autism in non-English speaking countries to build upon the sparse knowledge that exists on this topic in the literature. Methods Nineteen studies, obtained from five electronic databases, were examined. PRISMA guidance was used for this review. The Ecological Validity Framework model, and Bowen Recommendations for Feasibility were adopted to extract relevant data, which was synthesised narratively. Results Cultural adaptation within the included studies mostly involved language translation with little information offered to enable conclusions on how the processes were guided and maintained. Few cultural adjustments involved modifying screening methods; clarifying difficult concepts and changing instrument content were employed to address the core values, competence, beliefs, and norms of the adapted culture. However, less attention was given to adapt the screening goals within the context of cultural values, and customs or to consider interactional match between the clients and assessors. The review also highlighted an acceptable level of practicality to screen for autism but did not encourage integrating autism screening within routine practice or beyond the study context for different cultures. Conclusion Concurring with previous literature, we agree that knowledge on cultural adaptation for autism screening instruments is limited and not sufficiently documented to establish adaptation levels (process and/or contents), and prove adequacy. However, this review provides an infrastructure to improve future adaptation processes. Integrating autism screening as routine medical practice is not encouraged and warrants further feasibility studies to minimize wasted resources and improve screening effectiveness in various health care systems.

sheet.es: Si su familia usa un cuestionario de cribado del autismo traducido, recuerde que traducir no basta: pregunte si se adaptaron los conceptos, los ejemplos y las costumbres a su cultura, y comente con el profesional cómo encajan con su hijo o hija. La evidencia es una revisión sistemática de 19 estudios sobre cribado del autismo en países donde no se habla inglés. Encontró que la adaptación fue sobre todo lingüística y poco documentada, así que no permite saber si fue adecuada. Tampoco recomienda integrar el cribado en la práctica rutinaria. No indica qué es mejor para cada persona.
sheet.en: If your family is offered a translated autism screening questionnaire, remember that translation alone is not enough: ask whether the concepts, examples and customs were adapted to your culture, and talk with the professional about how they fit your child. The evidence is a systematic review of 19 studies on autism screening in non-English speaking countries. It found that adaptation was mostly language translation and poorly documented, so it cannot show whether adaptation was adequate. It also did not encourage routine use of screening. It cannot tell what is best for any one person.
sheet.sv: Om er familj erbjuds ett översatt screeningformulär för autism: översättning räcker inte. Fråga om begrepp, exempel och sedvänjor har anpassats till er kultur, och prata med den professionella om hur det passar ert barn. Underlaget är en systematisk översikt av 19 studier om autismscreening i länder där man inte talar engelska. Anpassningen bestod mest av språköversättning och var dåligt dokumenterad, så det går inte att säga om den var tillräcklig. Översikten förordade inte heller rutinmässig screening. Den kan inte säga vad som är bäst för en enskild person.

title: Meta-analyses of individual versus group interventions for pre-school children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD).
authors: Tachibana Y, Miyazaki C, Mikami M, Ota E, Mori R, Hwang Y, Terasaka A, Kobayashi E, Kamio Y
abstract: There is little evidence regarding the effects of individual and group intervention for children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) on important outcomes. We performed meta-analyses using a random effects model to investigate the effectiveness of the individual and group intervention studies and to compare the effectiveness of these two types if possible. The main analysis which excluded studies at a high risk of bias (Analysis I) included 14 randomised controlled trials targeting children with ASD≤6 years of age (594 children). The results suggested that both individual and group interventions showed significant effects compared to the control condition on "reciprocity of social interaction towards others" (standard mean difference[SMD] [95%confidence interval{CI}] = 0.59[0.25, 0.93], p = 0.16; 0.45[0.02, 0.88], p = 0.39, respectively). Only individual interventions showed significant effects compared to the control condition on "parental synchrony" (SMD [95%CI] = 0.99 [0.70, 1.29], p Trial registration (CRD42011001349).

sheet.es: Tanto las intervenciones individuales como las grupales pueden ayudar a la interacción social de niños autistas pequeños; si estás eligiendo, pregunta qué formato encaja mejor con tu criatura y tu familia. Es un metaanálisis que reunió 14 ensayos controlados aleatorizados con 594 niños de 6 años o menos. Solo las intervenciones individuales mostraron efectos en la sincronía de los padres. Los límites: el resumen no permite comparar bien ambos formatos, y los resultados son promedios que no valen para cada niño. Comenta las opciones con los profesionales que os acompañan.
sheet.en: Both individual and group interventions may support social interaction in young autistic children, so when choosing, ask which format suits your child and family best. This is a meta-analysis that combined 14 randomised controlled trials with 594 children aged 6 or under. Only individual interventions showed effects on parental synchrony. Limits: the abstract does not allow a clear comparison of the two formats, and results are averages that do not apply to every child. Talk through the options with the professionals who support you.
sheet.sv: Både individuella insatser och gruppinsatser kan stödja socialt samspel hos små autistiska barn, så fråga vilket format som passar ditt barn och din familj bäst. Det här är en metaanalys som sammanställde 14 randomiserade kontrollerade studier med 594 barn som var 6 år eller yngre. Bara individuella insatser visade effekt på föräldrars synkronisering. Begränsningar: sammanfattningen gör ingen tydlig jämförelse mellan formaten, och resultaten är genomsnitt som inte gäller varje barn. Diskutera alternativen med de yrkespersoner som stöttar er.

title: Self-reported sex differences in high-functioning adults with autism: a meta-analysis.
authors: Moseley RL, Hitchiner R, Kirkby JA
abstract: Background Sex differences in autistic symptomatology are believed to contribute to the mis- and missed diagnosis of many girls and women with an autism spectrum condition (ASC). Whilst recent years have seen the emergence of clinical and empirical reports delineating the profile of young autistic girls, recognition of sex differences in symptomatology in adulthood is far more limited. Methods We chose here to focus on symptomatology as reported using a screening instrument, the Ritvo Autism Asperger Diagnostic Scale-Revised (RAADS-R). In a meta-analysis, we pooled and analysed RAADS-R data from a number of experimental groups. Analysis of variance (ANOVA) searched for the presence of main effects of Sex and Diagnosis and for interactions between these factors in our sample of autistic and non-autistic adults. Results In social relatedness and circumscribed interests, main effects of Diagnosis revealed that as expected, autistic adults reported significantly greater lifetime prevalence of symptoms in these domains; an effect of Sex, in circumscribed interests, also suggested that males generally reported more prevalent symptoms than females. An interaction of Sex and Diagnosis in language symptomatology revealed that a normative sex difference in language difficulties was attenuated in autism. An interaction of Sex and Diagnosis in the sensorimotor domain revealed the opposite picture: a lack of sex differences between typically developing men and women and a greater prevalence of sensorimotor symptoms in autistic women than autistic men. Conclusions We discuss the literature on childhood sex differences in relation to those which emerged in our adult sample. Where childhood sex differences fail to persist in adulthood, several interpretations exist, and we discuss, for example, an inherent sampling bias that may mean that only autistic women most similar to the male presentation are diagnosed. The finding that sensorimotor symptomatology is more highly reported by autistic women is a finding requiring objective confirmation, given its potential importance in diagnosis.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una mujer autista, pregúntale con calma por su experiencia sensorial y motora: sonidos, texturas, luces, equilibrio o coordinación. En este estudio, las mujeres autistas describieron más diferencias sensoriomotoras que los hombres autistas, algo que puede pasar desapercibido y que merece espacio en la vida diaria, por ejemplo con pausas, auriculares o ropa cómoda. Es un metaanálisis que reunió respuestas de adultos autistas y no autistas al cuestionario RAADS-R. Sus límites: los datos son autoinformados, las personas participantes ya tenían diagnóstico (quizá mujeres con perfiles más parecidos a los masculinos) y los resultados necesitan confirmación con medidas objetivas. No describe a todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic woman, gently ask about her sensory and motor experiences: sounds, textures, light, balance or coordination. In this study, autistic women reported more sensorimotor differences than autistic men, something that is easy to overlook and worth making room for in daily life, such as breaks, headphones or comfortable clothing. This is a meta-analysis pooling autistic and non-autistic adults' answers to the RAADS-R screening questionnaire. Its limits: the data are self-reported, participants already had diagnoses (possibly favouring women whose profiles resemble men's), and the findings still need objective confirmation. It does not describe every person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk kvinna, fråga lugnt om hennes sensoriska och motoriska upplevelser: ljud, texturer, ljus, balans eller koordination. I den här studien beskrev autistiska kvinnor fler sensomotoriska skillnader än autistiska män, något som lätt förbises och som förtjänar utrymme i vardagen, till exempel pauser, hörlurar eller bekväma kläder. Det är en metaanalys som slog samman autistiska och icke-autistiska vuxnas svar på screeningformuläret RAADS-R. Begränsningar: svaren är självrapporterade, deltagarna hade redan diagnos (kanske kvinnor med profiler som liknar mäns) och resultaten behöver bekräftas med objektiva mått. Studien beskriver inte alla.

title: Current Enlightenment About Etiology and Pharmacological Treatment of Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Eissa N, Al-Houqani M, Sadeq A, Ojha SK, Sasse A, Sadek B
abstract: Autistic Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a complex neurodevelopmental brain disorder characterized by two core behavioral symptoms, namely impairments in social communication and restricted/repetitive behavior. The molecular mechanisms underlying ASD are not well understood. Recent genetic as well as non-genetic animal models contributed significantly in understanding the pathophysiology of ASD, as they establish autism-like behavior in mice and rats. Among the genetic causes, several chromosomal mutations including duplications or deletions could be possible causative factors of ASD. In addition, the biochemical basis suggests that several brain neurotransmitters, e.g., dopamine (DA), serotonin (5-HT), gamma-amino butyric acid (GABA), acetylcholine (ACh), glutamate (Glu) and histamine (HA) participate in the onset and progression of ASD. Despite of convincible understanding, risperidone and aripiprazole are the only two drugs available clinically for improving behavioral symptoms of ASD following approval by Food and Drug Administration (FDA). Till date, up to our knowledge there is no other drug approved for clinical usage specifically for ASD symptoms. However, many novel drug candidates and classes of compounds are underway for ASD at different phases of preclinical and clinical drug development. In this review, the diversity of numerous aetiological factors and the alterations in variety of neurotransmitter generation, release and function linked to ASD are discussed with focus on drugs currently used to manage neuropsychiatric symptoms related to ASD. The review also highlights the clinical development of drugs with emphasis on their pharmacological targets aiming at improving core symptoms in ASD.

sheet.es: Este trabajo trata de medicación, así que las decisiones médicas corresponden siempre a un profesional clínico; hablen con él antes de cambiar nada. Lo útil para casa: las causas de la autismo son diversas y todavía no se conocen bien, y apoyar a la persona autista no depende de esperar un fármaco. Es una revisión de la literatura que reúne estudios con animales y trabajos clínicos sobre genética y neurotransmisores. Sus límites: se centra en un enfoque médico, gran parte viene de modelos animales y no indica qué le conviene a una persona concreta.
sheet.en: This work is about medication, so medical decisions always belong to a clinician; talk with one before changing anything. What helps at home: the causes of autism are varied and still not well understood, and supporting an autistic person does not depend on waiting for a drug. This is a review that brings together animal studies and clinical work on genetics and neurotransmitters. Its limits: it takes a medical approach, much of it comes from animal models, and it cannot say what suits any one person.
sheet.sv: Den här studien handlar om läkemedel, så medicinska beslut hör alltid till en kliniker; prata med en innan något ändras. Det praktiska hemma: orsakerna till autism är många och ännu inte väl förstådda, och stödet till en autistisk person behöver inte vänta på ett läkemedel. Det är en översikt som samlar djurstudier och kliniskt arbete om genetik och signalämnen i hjärnan. Begränsningar: den har ett medicinskt perspektiv, mycket kommer från djurmodeller och den kan inte säga vad som passar en enskild person.

title: The role of oxytocin receptor gene (OXTR) DNA methylation (DNAm) in human social and emotional functioning: a systematic narrative review.
authors: Maud C, Ryan J, McIntosh JE, Olsson CA
abstract: Background The neuropeptide Oxytocin (OXT) plays a central role in birthing, mother-infant bonding and a broad range of related social behaviours in mammals. More recently, interest has extended to epigenetic programming of genes involved in oxytocinergic neurotransmission. This review brings together early findings in a rapidly developing field of research, examining relationships between DNA methylation (DNAm) of the Oxytocin Receptor Gene (OXTR) and social and emotional behaviour in human populations. Method A systematic search across Web of Knowledge/Science, Scopus, Medline and EMBASE captured all published studies prior to June 2017 examining the association between OXTR DNAm and human social and emotional outcomes. Search terms included 'oxytocin gene' or 'oxytocin receptor gene' and 'epigenetics' or 'DNA methylation'. Any article with a focus on social and emotional functioning was then identified from this set by manual review. Results Nineteen studies met eligibility criteria. There was considerable heterogeneity of study populations, tissue samples, instrumentation, measurement, and OXTR site foci. Only three studies examined functional consequences of OXTR DNAm on gene expression and protein synthesis. Increases in OXTR DNAm were associated with callous-unemotional traits in youth, social cognitive deficits in Autistic Spectrum Disorder (ASD), rigid thinking in anorexia nervosa, affect regulation problems, and problems with facial and emotional recognition. In contrast, reductions in DNAm were associated with perinatal stress, postnatal depression, social anxiety and autism in children. Conclusions Consistent with an emerging field of inquiry, there is not yet sufficient evidence to draw conclusions about the role of OXTR DNAm in human social and emotional behaviour. However, taken together, findings point to increased OXTR DNAm in general impairments in social, cognitive and emotional functioning, and decreased OXTR DNAm in specific patterns of impairment related to mood and anxiety disorders (but not in all). Future progress in this field would be enhanced by adequately powered designs, greater phenotypic precision, and methodological improvements including longitudinal studies with multiple time-points to facilitate causal inference.

title: The Relationship between Sleep Problems, Neurobiological Alterations, Core Symptoms of Autism Spectrum Disorder, and Psychiatric Comorbidities.
authors: Mazzone L, Postorino V, Siracusano M, Riccioni A, Curatolo P
abstract: Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) are at an increased risk for sleep disturbances, and studies indicate that between 50 and 80% of children with ASD experience sleep problems. These problems increase parental stress and adversely affect family quality of life. Studies have also suggested that sleep disturbances may increase behavioral problems in this clinical population. Although understanding the causes of sleep disorders in ASD is a clinical priority, the causal relationship between these two conditions remains unclear. Given the complex nature of ASD, the etiology of sleep problems in this clinical population is probably multi-factorial. In this overview, we discuss in detail three possible etiological explanations of sleep problems in ASD that can all contribute to the high rate of these symptoms in ASD. Specifically, we examine how neurobiological alterations, genetic mutations, and disrupted sleep architecture can cause sleep problems in individuals with ASD. We also discuss how sleep problems may be a direct result of core symptoms of ASD. Finally, a detailed examination of the relationship between sleep problems and associated clinical features and psychiatric comorbidities in individuals with ASD is described.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista duerme mal, conviene tomarlo en serio y observar con calma qué ayuda: horarios, ambiente, sensibilidad a la luz o al ruido. Anótalo y coméntalo con su profesional de salud. Esta revisión resume estudios previos y señala que entre 50 y 80% de los niños autistas tienen problemas de sueño, que pueden aumentar el estrés familiar. Los autores plantean varias posibles causas, biológicas y ligadas a rasgos autistas. Sus límites: la relación causal sigue sin estar clara y no explica a cada persona; no es una regla general.
sheet.en: If an autistic person sleeps badly, take it seriously and calmly watch what might help: routines, the bedroom, sensitivity to light or noise. Note what you see and share it with their health professional. This review summarises earlier studies and reports that between 50 and 80% of children with ASD experience sleep problems, which can raise family stress. The authors describe several possible causes, biological and linked to autistic traits. Its limits: the causal relationship remains unclear, and it cannot explain any one person, so it is not a rule for everyone.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person sover dåligt är det värt att ta på allvar och i lugn och ro se vad som kan hjälpa: rutiner, sovrummet, känslighet för ljus eller ljud. Anteckna och ta upp det med personens vårdgivare. Den här översikten sammanfattar tidigare studier och uppger att mellan 50 och 80% av barn med ASD har sömnproblem, vilket kan öka familjens stress. Författarna beskriver flera möjliga orsaker, biologiska och kopplade till autistiska drag. Begränsningar: orsakssambandet är fortfarande oklart, och översikten förklarar inte en enskild person, så det är ingen regel för alla.

title: Role of mTOR Complexes in Neurogenesis.
authors: LiCausi F, Hartman NW
abstract: Dysregulation of neural stem cells (NSCs) is associated with several neurodevelopmental disorders, including epilepsy and autism spectrum disorder. The mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) integrates the intracellular signals to control cell growth, nutrient metabolism, and protein translation. mTOR regulates many functions in the development of the brain, such as proliferation, differentiation, migration, and dendrite formation. In addition, mTOR is important in synaptic formation and plasticity. Abnormalities in mTOR activity is linked with severe deficits in nervous system development, including tumors, autism, and seizures. Dissecting the wide-ranging roles of mTOR activity during critical periods in development will greatly expand our understanding of neurogenesis.

sheet.es: Este estudio no ofrece nada que hacer mañana por la mañana: es ciencia básica sobre cómo se desarrolla el cerebro. Puedes guardarlo como contexto, sin cambiar la rutina ni sacar conclusiones sobre una persona concreta. Es una revisión que resume trabajos previos sobre la proteína mTOR, que según el resumen interviene en el crecimiento celular, la formación de sinapsis y el desarrollo cerebral, y cuya actividad alterada se vincula con el autismo, entre otras condiciones. Sus límites: no describe a personas autistas concretas, no prueba causas ni propone apoyos. Cualquier decisión médica corresponde a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: This study offers nothing to do tomorrow morning: it is basic science about how the brain develops. You can keep it as background, without changing routines or drawing conclusions about any one person. It is a review summarising earlier work on the mTOR protein, which the abstract says helps control cell growth, synapse formation and brain development, and whose altered activity is linked with autism, among other conditions. Its limits: it does not describe individual autistic people, does not prove causes and suggests no supports. Any medical decision belongs to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Den här studien ger inget att göra i morgon bitti: det är grundforskning om hur hjärnan utvecklas. Du kan spara den som bakgrund, utan att ändra rutiner eller dra slutsatser om en enskild person. Det är en översikt som sammanfattar tidigare arbete om proteinet mTOR, som enligt sammanfattningen styr bland annat celltillväxt, synapsbildning och hjärnans utveckling, och vars förändrade aktivitet kopplas till bland annat autism. Begränsningar: den beskriver inte enskilda autistiska personer, bevisar inga orsaker och föreslår inget stöd. Alla medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker.

title: Autism spectrum disorders: a meta-analysis of executive function.
authors: Demetriou EA, Lampit A, Quintana DS, Naismith SL, Song YJC, Pye JE, Hickie I, Guastella AJ
abstract: Evidence of executive dysfunction in autism spectrum disorders (ASD) across development remains mixed and establishing its role is critical for guiding diagnosis and intervention. The primary objectives of this meta-analysis is to analyse executive function (EF) performance in ASD, the fractionation across EF subdomains, the clinical utility of EF measures and the influence of multiple moderators (for example, age, gender, diagnosis, measure characteristics). The Embase, Medline and PsychINFO databases were searched to identify peer-reviewed studies published since the inclusion of Autism in DSM-III (1980) up to end of June 2016 that compared EF in ASD with neurotypical controls. A random-effects model was used and moderators were tested using subgroup analysis. The primary outcome measure was Hedges' g effect size for EF and moderator factors. Clinical sensitivity was determined by the overlap percentage statistic (OL%). Results were reported according to the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) guidelines. A total of 235 studies comprising 14 081 participants were included (N, ASD=6816, Control=7265). A moderate overall effect size for reduced EF (Hedges' g=0.48, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.43-0.53) was found with similar effect sizes across each domain. The majority of moderator comparisons were not significant although the overall effect of executive dysfunction has gradually reduced since the introduction of ASD. Only a small number of EF measures achieved clinical sensitivity. This study confirms a broad executive dysfunction in ASD that is relatively stable across development. The fractionation of executive dysfunction into individual subdomains was not supported, nor was diagnostic sensitivity. Development of feasible EF measures focussing on clinical sensitivity for diagnosis and treatment studies should be a priority.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista tiene dificultades con planificar, cambiar de tarea o organizarse, conviene ofrecer apoyos concretos: rutinas visuales, pasos escritos y avisos previos de los cambios. Es una pauta útil, no una regla para todas las personas. Evidencia: metaanálisis de 235 estudios con 14 081 participantes que comparó la función ejecutiva de personas autistas con la de controles neurotípicos; halló una diferencia moderada (g=0.48), similar en todas las áreas. Límites: es un promedio, hay mucha variación individual, y pocas pruebas sirvieron para identificar el autismo, así que no deben usarse para diagnosticar.
sheet.en: If an autistic person finds planning, switching tasks or getting organised hard, offer concrete supports: visual routines, written steps and advance notice of changes. This is a helpful starting point, not a rule for every person. Evidence: a meta-analysis of 235 studies with 14 081 participants compared executive function in autistic people with neurotypical controls and found a moderate difference (g=0.48), similar across all areas. Limits: this is an average, individuals vary a lot, and only a few tests were sensitive enough to point to autism, so they should not be used to diagnose.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person har svårt att planera, byta uppgift eller organisera sig kan du erbjuda konkret stöd: visuella rutiner, skrivna steg och förvarning om förändringar. Det är en användbar utgångspunkt, inte en regel för alla. Evidens: en metaanalys av 235 studier med 14 081 deltagare jämförde exekutiva funktioner hos autistiska personer med neurotypiska kontroller och fann en måttlig skillnad (g=0.48), likartad i alla områden. Begränsningar: det är ett genomsnitt, individer varierar mycket, och bara få test var tillräckligt känsliga för att peka mot autism, så de bör inte användas för diagnos.

title: Balance Performance in Autism: A Brief Overview.
authors: Stins JF, Emck C
abstract: Children with autism not only have limited social and communicative skills but also have motor abnormalities, such as poor timing and coordination of balance. Moreover, impaired gross motor skills hamper participation with peers. Balance control is interesting from a cognitive science perspective, since it involves a complex interplay between information processing, motor planning, and timing and sequencing of muscle movements. In this paper, we discuss the background of motor problems in children with autism, focusing on how posture is informed by sensory information processing. We also discuss the neurobiological basis of balance problems, and how this is related to anxiety in this group. We then discuss possible avenues for treatment of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) symptoms, especially as regards movement-related interventions. Finally, we present a theoretical outlook and discuss whether some of the symptoms in ASD can be understood from an embodied cognition perspective.

sheet.es: Si una niña o un niño autista parece torpe o inseguro al moverse, conviene tener en cuenta que el equilibrio puede costarle más y que puede relacionarse con la ansiedad. Ofrezca actividades de movimiento a su ritmo, con apoyo y sin presión, para que pueda participar con otros niños. Esto es una revisión: reúne y comenta estudios previos sobre niños autistas, el equilibrio, el procesamiento sensorial y las intervenciones basadas en el movimiento. Sus límites: es un panorama breve, en parte teórico, y no demuestra qué actividad funciona para cada persona. Consulte con un profesional de fisioterapia o terapia ocupacional si tiene dudas.
sheet.en: If an autistic child seems clumsy or unsure when moving, it helps to remember that balance may take more effort for them and may be linked to anxiety. Offer movement activities at their own pace, with support and no pressure, so they can join in with peers. This is a review: it gathers and discusses earlier research on autistic children, balance, sensory processing and movement-based interventions. Its limits: it is a brief overview, partly theoretical, and it does not show which activity works for each person. Ask a physiotherapist or occupational therapist if you have questions.
sheet.sv: Om ett autistiskt barn verkar klumpigt eller osäkert när det rör sig kan det hjälpa att veta att balansen kan kräva mer av barnet och kan hänga ihop med oro. Erbjud rörelseaktiviteter i barnets eget tempo, med stöd och utan press, så att det kan delta med kamrater. Detta är en översikt: den samlar och diskuterar tidigare forskning om autistiska barn, balans, sensorisk bearbetning och rörelsebaserade insatser. Begränsningar: den är kort, delvis teoretisk och visar inte vilken aktivitet som fungerar för varje person. Fråga en fysioterapeut eller arbetsterapeut om du undrar något.

title: Measurement properties of tools used to assess depression in adults with and without autism spectrum conditions: A systematic review.
authors: Cassidy SA, Bradley L, Bowen E, Wigham S, Rodgers J
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Depression is the most commonly experienced mental health condition in adults with autism spectrum conditions (ASC). However, it is unclear what tools are currently being used to assess depression in ASC, or whether tools need to be adapted for this group. This systematic review therefore aimed to identify tools used to assess depression in adults with and without ASC, and then evaluate these tools for their appropriateness and measurement properties. Medline, PsychINFO and Web of Knowledge were searched for studies of depression in: (a) adults with ASC, without co-morbid intellectual disability; and (b) adults from the general population without co-morbid conditions. Articles examining the measurement properties of these tools were then searched for using a methodological filter in PubMed, and the quality of the evidence was evaluated using the COSMIN checklist. Twelve articles were identified which utilized three tools to assess depression in adults with ASC, but only one article which assessed the measurement properties of one of these tools was identified and thus evaluated. Sixty-four articles were identified which utilized five tools to assess depression in general population adults, and fourteen articles had assessed the measurement properties of these tools. Overall, two tools were found to be robust in their measurement properties in the general population-the Beck Depression Inventory (BDI-II), and the patient health questionnaire (PHQ-9). Crucially only one study was identified from the COSMIN search, which showed weak evidence in support of the measurement properties of the BDI-II in an ASC sample. Implications for effective measurement of depression in ASC are discussed. Autism Res 2018, 11: 738-754. © 2018 The Authors Autism Research published by International Society for Autism Research and Wiley Periodicals, Inc. Lay summary Depression is the most common mental health problem experienced by adults with autism. However, the current study found very limited evidence regarding how useful tools developed for the general population are for adults with autism. We therefore suggest how these tools could be adapted to more effectively assess depression in adults with autism, and improve these individuals access to mental health assessment and support.

sheet.es: Si te preocupa que una persona autista adulta pueda estar deprimida, un cuestionario por sí solo no basta: cuéntale lo que has notado y busca a un profesional de salud mental que conozca el autismo. Esta revisión sistemática buscó herramientas para evaluar la depresión en personas adultas con y sin autismo. Solo encontró un estudio sobre las propiedades de medición de una de ellas, el BDI-II, en personas autistas, y mostró evidencia débil. Límites: incluyó a adultos sin discapacidad intelectual, y no demuestra que estas herramientas fallen en cada persona; indica que faltan pruebas. Las decisiones sobre evaluación y apoyo corresponden a profesionales.
sheet.en: If you worry that an autistic adult may be depressed, a questionnaire alone is not enough: share what you have noticed and look for a mental health professional who understands autism. This systematic review searched for tools that assess depression in adults with and without autism. It found only one study on the measurement properties of one of them, the BDI-II, in autistic people, and that evidence was weak. Limits: it covered adults without intellectual disability, and it does not show these tools fail for every person; it shows evidence is missing. Decisions about assessment and support belong with professionals.
sheet.sv: Om du oroar dig för att en autistisk vuxen kan vara deprimerad räcker det inte med ett frågeformulär: berätta vad du har märkt och sök en psykiatrisk yrkesperson som förstår autism. Den här systematiska översikten sökte verktyg för att bedöma depression hos vuxna med och utan autism. Den hittade bara en studie om mätegenskaperna hos ett av dem, BDI-II, hos autistiska personer, och beläggen var svaga. Begränsningar: den omfattade vuxna utan intellektuell funktionsnedsättning, och den visar inte att verktygen fungerar dåligt för alla; den visar att evidens saknas. Beslut om bedömning och stöd tas av vårdpersonal.

title: Case-control meta-analysis of blood DNA methylation and autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Andrews SV, Sheppard B, Windham GC, Schieve LA, Schendel DE, Croen LA, Chopra P, Alisch RS, Newschaffer CJ, Warren ST, Feinberg AP, Fallin MD, Ladd-Acosta C
abstract: Background Several reports have suggested a role for epigenetic mechanisms in ASD etiology. Epigenome-wide association studies (EWAS) in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) may shed light on particular biological mechanisms. However, studies of ASD cases versus controls have been limited by post-mortem timing and severely small sample sizes. Reports from in-life sampling of blood or saliva have also been very limited in sample size and/or genomic coverage. We present the largest case-control EWAS for ASD to date, combining data from population-based case-control and case-sibling pair studies. Methods DNA from 968 blood samples from children in the Study to Explore Early Development (SEED 1) was used to generate epigenome-wide array DNA methylation (DNAm) data at 485,512 CpG sites for 453 cases and 515 controls, using the Illumina 450K Beadchip. The Simons Simplex Collection (SSC) provided 450K array DNAm data on an additional 343 cases and their unaffected siblings. We performed EWAS meta-analysis across results from the two data sets, with adjustment for sex and surrogate variables that reflect major sources of biological variation and technical confounding such as cell type, batch, and ancestry. We compared top EWAS results to those from a previous brain-based analysis. We also tested for enrichment of ASD EWAS CpGs for being targets of meQTL associations using available SNP genotype data in the SEED sample. Findings In this meta-analysis of blood-based DNA from 796 cases and 858 controls, no single CpG met a Bonferroni discovery threshold of p - 7 . Seven CpGs showed differences at p - 5 and 48 at 1 × 10 - 4 . Of the top 7, 5 showed brain-based ASD associations as well, often with larger effect sizes, and the top 48 overall showed modest concordance ( r = 0.31) in direction of effect with cerebellum samples. Finally, we observed suggestive evidence for enrichment of CpG sites controlled by SNPs (meQTL targets) among the EWAS CpG hits, which was consistent across EWAS and meQTL discovery p value thresholds. Conclusions No single CpG site showed a large enough DNAm difference between cases and controls to achieve epigenome-wide significance in this sample size. However, our results suggest the potential to observe disease associations from blood-based samples.
