Among the seven sites achieving suggestive statistical significance, we observed consistent, and stronger, effects at the same sites among brain samples. Discovery-oriented EWAS for ASD using blood samples will likely need even larger samples and unified genetic data to further understand DNAm differences in ASD.

sheet.es: Este estudio no ofrece nada que cambie la rutina de mañana: es investigación básica sobre biología, no una guía de apoyo. Combinó datos de análisis de sangre de niños, de dos conjuntos de datos, con 796 casos autistas y 858 controles. Ninguna marca de metilación del ADN mostró una diferencia lo bastante grande para ser concluyente, aunque algunas pistas coincidían con muestras de cerebro. Es un metaanálisis con límites claros: la muestra aún era pequeña para este tipo de pregunta, y nada de esto sirve para evaluar a una persona ni vale para todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: This study offers nothing that changes tomorrow's routine: it is basic biology research, not a support guide. It combined blood-test data from children in two data sets, with 796 autistic cases and 858 controls. No single DNA methylation mark showed a difference large enough to be conclusive, though some hints matched brain samples. It is a meta-analysis with clear limits: the sample was still too small for this kind of question, and nothing here can be used to assess an individual or applies to every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Den här studien ger inget som ändrar morgondagens rutiner: det är biologisk grundforskning, inte en stödguide. Den slog ihop blodprovsdata från barn i två datamaterial, med 796 autistiska fall och 858 kontroller. Ingen enskild DNA-metyleringsmarkör visade en skillnad som var stor nog för att vara avgörande, även om vissa spår stämde med hjärnprover. Det är en metaanalys med tydliga gränser: urvalet var ändå för litet för den här typen av fråga, och inget av detta kan användas för att bedöma en enskild person eller gäller alla autistiska personer.

title: Therapeutic body wraps (TBW) for treatment of severe injurious behaviour in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD): A 3-month randomized controlled feasibility study.
authors: Delion P, Labreuche J, Deplanque D, Cohen D, Duhamel A, Lallié C, Ravary M, Goeb JL, Medjkane F, Xavier J, Therapeutic Body Wrap Study group
abstract: Introduction The use of therapeutic body wraps (TBW) has been reported in small series or case reports, but has become controversial. Objectives This is a feasibility, multicentre, randomized, controlled, open-label trial with blinded outcome assessment (PROBE design). Setting Children with autism and severe-injurious behaviours (SIB) were enrolled from 13 specialized clinics. Interventions Dry-sheet TBW (DRY group) vs. wet-sheet TBW (WET group). Primary outcome measures 3-month change in the Aberrant Behaviour Checklist irritability score (ABC-irritability) within per-protocol (PP) sample. Results From January 2008 to January 2015, we recruited 48 children (age range: 5.9 to 9.9 years, 78.1% male). Seven patients (4 in the DRY group, 3 in the WET group) were dropped from the study early and were excluded from PP analysis. At endpoint, ABC-irritability significantly improved in both groups (means (standard deviation) = -11.15 (8.05) in the DRY group and -10.57 (9.29) in the WET group), as did the other ABC scores and the Children Autism Rating scale score. However, there was no significant difference between groups. All but 5 patients were rated as much or very much improved. A repeated-measures analysis confirmed the significant improvement in ABC-irritability scores according to time (p Conclusions We found that feasibility was overall satisfactory with a slow recruitment rate and a rather good attrition rate. TBW was a safe complementary therapy in this population. There was no difference between wet and dry TBW at 3 months, and ABC-irritability significantly decreased with both wet and dry sheet TBW. To assess whether TBW may constitute an alternative to medication or behavioural intervention for treating SIB in ASD patients, a larger randomized comparative trial (e.g. TBW vs. antipsychotics) is warranted. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03164746.

sheet.es: Si le preocupan las conductas de autolesión intensas, hable con el equipo clínico antes de probar envolturas corporales terapéuticas; no son algo para hacer por cuenta propia. Este ensayo aleatorizado de viabilidad incluyó a 48 niños autistas de 13 clínicas especializadas y comparó sábanas secas y húmedas. La irritabilidad mejoró en ambos grupos, sin diferencia entre ellos, y se describió como complementaria y segura. Límites: no había grupo sin envolturas, el estudio fue pequeño y abierto, y los autores piden un ensayo mayor. No sirve como regla para cada persona; sus preferencias y su comodidad cuentan.
sheet.en: If intense self-injury worries you, talk with the clinical team before trying therapeutic body wraps; they are not something to start on your own. This randomized feasibility trial included 48 autistic children from 13 specialized clinics and compared dry and wet sheets. Irritability scores improved in both groups, with no difference between them, and the wraps were described as a safe complementary therapy. Limits: there was no group without wraps, the study was small and open-label, and the authors call for a larger trial. It is not a rule for every person; the child's preferences and comfort matter.
sheet.sv: Om kraftigt självskadande oroar dig, prata med vårdteamet innan ni provar terapeutiska kroppsinpackningar; det är inget att starta på egen hand. Denna randomiserade genomförbarhetsstudie omfattade 48 autistiska barn från 13 specialiserade kliniker och jämförde torra och våta lakan. Irritabilitetspoängen förbättrades i båda grupperna, utan skillnad mellan dem, och inpackningarna beskrevs som en säker kompletterande behandling. Begränsningar: ingen grupp saknade inpackning, studien var liten och öppen, och forskarna efterlyser en större studie. Det är ingen regel för alla; barnets önskemål och trygghet räknas.

title: Inflammation and Neuro-Immune Dysregulations in Autism Spectrum Disorders.
authors: Siniscalco D, Schultz S, Brigida AL, Antonucci N
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is characterized by persistent deficits in social communication and interaction and restricted-repetitive patterns of behavior, interests, or activities. Strong inflammation states are associated with ASD. This inflammatory condition is often linked to immune system dysfunction. Several cell types are enrolled to trigger and sustain these processes. Neuro-inflammation and neuro-immune abnormalities have now been established in ASD as key factors in its development and maintenance. In this review, we will explore inflammatory conditions, dysfunctions in neuro-immune cross-talk, and immune system treatments in ASD management.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista, este texto no pide cambiar nada mañana. Puede ayudar a entender que algunos equipos de investigación estudian la relación entre el sistema inmunitario, la inflamación y el autismo. Si te preocupa su salud física, anota lo que observas y coméntalo con su profesional sanitario. Es una revisión de la literatura científica; el resumen no indica quiénes participaron ni cuántas personas. Sus límites: una revisión no prueba causas, no sirve como regla para todas las personas autistas y las decisiones médicas corresponden siempre a un clínico.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person, this paper does not ask you to change anything tomorrow. It may help to know that some researchers study links between the immune system, inflammation and autism. If you are concerned about their physical health, note what you observe and talk it through with their healthcare professional. This is a review of the scientific literature; the abstract does not say who took part or how many people. Its limits: a review cannot prove causes, it is not a rule for every autistic person, and medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person ber den här texten dig inte ändra något i morgon. Det kan vara bra att veta att vissa forskare studerar kopplingar mellan immunförsvaret, inflammation och autism. Om du oroar dig för personens fysiska hälsa kan du anteckna vad du ser och ta upp det med hens vårdpersonal. Det här är en översikt av forskningslitteratur; sammanfattningen säger inte vilka som deltog eller hur många. Begränsningar: en översikt kan inte bevisa orsaker, gäller inte som regel för alla autistiska personer, och medicinska beslut hör hemma hos en kliniker.

title: Clinical practice guidelines for diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder in adults and children in the UK: a narrative review.
authors: Hayes J, Ford T, Rafeeque H, Russell G
abstract: Background Research suggests that diagnostic procedures for Autism Spectrum Disorder are not consistent across practice and that diagnostic rates can be affected by contextual and social drivers. The purpose of this review was to consider how the content of clinical practice guidelines shapes diagnoses of Autism Spectrum Disorder in the UK; and investigate where, within those guidelines, social factors and influences are considered. Methods We electronically searched multiple databases (NICE Evidence Base; TRIP; Social Policy and Practice; US National Guidelines Clearinghouse; HMIC; The Cochrane Library; Embase; Global health; Ovid; PsychARTICLES; PsychINFO) and relevant web sources (government, professional and regional NHS websites) for clinical practice guidelines. We extracted details of key diagnostic elements such as assessment process and diagnostic tools. A qualitative narrative analysis was conducted to identify social factors and influences. Results Twenty-one documents were found and analysed. Guidelines varied in recommendations for use of diagnostic tools and assessment procedures. Although multidisciplinary assessment was identified as the 'ideal' assessment, some guidelines suggested in practice one experienced healthcare professional was sufficient. Social factors in operational, interactional and contextual areas added complexity to guidelines but there were few concrete recommendations as to how these factors should be operationalized for best diagnostic outcomes. Conclusion Although individual guidelines appeared to present a coherent and systematic assessment process, they varied enough in their recommendations to make the choices available to healthcare professionals particularly complex and confusing. We recommend a more explicit acknowledgement of social factors in clinical practice guidelines with advice about how they should be managed and operationalised to enable more consistency of practice and transparency for those coming for diagnosis.

sheet.es: Si está buscando una valoración diagnóstica para usted o para alguien a su cargo, pregunte con antelación cómo será el proceso: qué herramientas se usarán, si participará un equipo o un solo profesional y cómo se tendrá en cuenta el contexto social. Esta revisión narrativa analizó 21 documentos de guías clínicas del Reino Unido. Las guías diferían en herramientas y procedimientos, y daban pocas indicaciones concretas sobre los factores sociales. Es un análisis de guías, no de personas, así que no muestra qué proceso funciona mejor ni describe lo que ocurrirá en un servicio concreto.
sheet.en: If you are seeking a diagnostic assessment for yourself or someone you support, ask in advance how the process will work: which tools will be used, whether a team or a single professional will be involved, and how social context will be considered. This narrative review analysed 21 UK clinical practice guideline documents. Guidelines differed in tools and procedures, and gave few concrete directions on social factors. It reviews guidelines, not people, so it cannot show which process works best or describe what will happen at any particular service.
sheet.sv: Om du söker en diagnostisk utredning för dig själv eller någon du stöttar, fråga i förväg hur den går till: vilka verktyg som används, om ett team eller en enskild yrkesperson deltar och hur den sociala miljön beaktas. Denna narrativa översikt analyserade 21 brittiska dokument med kliniska riktlinjer. Riktlinjerna skilde sig åt i verktyg och arbetssätt och gav få konkreta råd om sociala faktorer. Den granskar riktlinjer, inte människor, så den visar inte vilken process som fungerar bäst eller vad som händer vid en enskild mottagning.

title: Long-Term Effect of Therapeutic Horseback Riding in Youth With Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Randomized Trial.
authors: Gabriels RL, Pan Z, Guérin NA, Dechant B, Mesibov G
abstract: This paper presents 6-month follow-up data of 44% ( N = 64/116) of participants (ages 6-16 years) with a diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder, who participated in a previously-published randomized controlled trial of therapeutic horseback riding (THR) compared to a no-horse contact active control. The objective of this study was to examine whether significant improvements of irritability, hyperactivity, social, and communication behaviors observed in participants randomized to receive a 10-week manual-based THR intervention were sustained 6 months after the intervention conclusion. Participants' caregivers from both the THR ( n = 36) and active control ( n = 28) groups completed a measure of irritability and hyperactivity behaviors (primary outcome variables). Additionally, only the THR group participants completed the full battery of study outcomes assessments. Between group comparisons examining the extended interval from baseline (1-month pre-intervention assessment) to 6-months after the intervention revealed that the THR group maintained reductions in irritability behavior at a 0.1 level (effect size = 0.32, p = 0.07). (Effect size = 0.32, p = 0.07), which was 73% of efficacy preserved from the primary post-intervention endpoint (within 1-month post-intervention). Hyperactivity behaviors did not sustain this same trend. Comparisons from baseline and 6-months after the intervention revealed that the THR group sustained significant initial improvements made in social and communication behaviors, along with number of words and different words spoken during a standard language sample. This is the first known study to examine and demonstrate the longer-term effects of THR for individuals with ASD and warrants a more thorough evaluation of whether the effects of THR are maintained for at least 6-months after the intervention compared to a control. Clinical trial registration information Trial of Therapeutic Horseback Riding in Children and Adolescents with Autism Spectrum Disorder; http://clinicaltrials.gov; NCT02301195.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista disfruta de los caballos, la equitación terapéutica puede ser una actividad que merezca la pena probar, siempre según sus gustos y su comodidad. Es un seguimiento de un ensayo aleatorizado con 64 participantes de 6 a 16 años, de 116 iniciales, a los 6 meses de un programa de 10 semanas. Las mejoras en conducta social y comunicación parecían mantenerse en el grupo de equitación, y la irritabilidad mostró una tendencia (p = 0.07). La hiperactividad no. Límites: faltaron datos de muchos participantes y solo el grupo de equitación completó todas las pruebas, así que los resultados no valen para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person enjoys horses, therapeutic horseback riding may be an activity worth trying, always guided by their preferences and comfort. This is a follow-up of a randomized trial with 64 participants aged 6-16 (of 116 originally), checked 6 months after a 10-week programme. Improvements in social and communication behaviours seemed to be maintained in the riding group, and irritability showed a trend (p = 0.07). Hyperactivity did not. Limits: data were missing for many participants and only the riding group completed the full set of assessments, so the results cannot be applied to everyone.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person tycker om hästar kan terapeutisk ridning vara värt att prova, alltid utifrån personens egna önskemål och trygghet. Detta är en uppföljning av en randomiserad studie med 64 deltagare i åldern 6–16 år (av ursprungligen 116), sex månader efter ett program på 10 veckor. Förbättringar i socialt beteende och kommunikation verkade bestå i ridgruppen, och irritabilitet visade en tendens (p = 0.07). Hyperaktivitet gjorde det inte. Begränsningar: många deltagare saknades och bara ridgruppen genomförde alla bedömningar, så resultaten gäller inte alla.

title: Social decision making in autism: On the impact of mirror neurons, motor control, and imitative behaviors.
authors: Khalil R, Tindle R, Boraud T, Moustafa AA, Karim AA
abstract: The Mirror Neuron System (MNS) plays a crucial role in action perception and imitative behavior, which is suggested to be impaired in Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASDs). In this review, we discuss the plausibility and empirical evidence of a neural interaction between the MNS, action perception, empathy, imitative behavior, and their impact on social decision making in ASDs. To date, there is no consensus regarding a particular theory in ASDs and its underlying mechanisms. Some theories have completely focused on social difficulties, others have emphasized sensory aspects. Based on the current studies, we suggest a multilayer neural network model including the MNS on a first layer and transforming this information to a higher layer network responsible for reasoning. Future studies with ASD participants combining behavioral tasks with neuroimaging methods and transcranial brain stimulation as well as computational modeling can help validate and complement this suggested model. Moreover, we propose applying the behavioral paradigms, and the neurophysiological markers mentioned in this review article for evaluating psychiatric treatment approaches in ASDs. The investigation of modulating effects of different treatment approaches on the neurophysiological markers of the MNS can help find specific subgroups of ASDs patients and support tailored psychiatric interventions.

sheet.es: Mañana, no hace falta corregir la imitación ni forzar el contacto social: puede ayudar observar cómo la persona autista percibe las acciones de otros y qué apoyos sensoriales y sociales le sirven. Esto es una revisión de estudios sobre el sistema de neuronas espejo, la imitación, la empatía y la toma de decisiones sociales en el autismo; los autores proponen un modelo en capas. Sus límites: es una propuesta teórica, no hay consenso entre teorías y hacen falta más estudios con personas autistas. No es una regla para todas las personas. Las decisiones médicas corresponden a profesionales clínicos.
sheet.en: Tomorrow, there is no need to correct imitation or push social contact: it may help to notice how an autistic person perceives other people's actions and which sensory and social supports work for them. This is a review of studies on the mirror neuron system, imitation, empathy and social decision making in autism; the authors propose a layered model. Its limits: it is a theoretical proposal, there is no consensus among theories, and more studies with autistic participants are needed. It is not a rule for every person. Medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: I morgon behöver du inte rätta imitation eller pressa fram social kontakt: det kan hjälpa att lägga märke till hur den autistiska personen uppfattar andras handlingar och vilket sensoriskt och socialt stöd som fungerar. Detta är en översikt av studier om spegelneuronsystemet, imitation, empati och sociala beslut vid autism; författarna föreslår en modell i lager. Begränsningar: det är ett teoretiskt förslag, forskarna är oeniga om teorierna och fler studier med autistiska deltagare behövs. Det är ingen regel för alla. Medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker.

title: Towards a Treatment for Intolerance of Uncertainty for Autistic Adults: A Single Case Experimental Design Study.
authors: Rodgers J, Herrema R, Honey E, Freeston M
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Intolerance of uncertainty (IU) is indicated as an important transdiagnostic process variable in a range of anxiety disorders. Anxiety is very common in autistic adults. This study evaluates a manualised treatment programme for autistic adults, which focused on IU. An eight session programme (CUES-A©) was developed and delivered to four autistic adults on an individual basis. A single case experimental design was used to provide a preliminary evaluation of the feasibility, acceptability and preliminary effectiveness of the programme. Data regarding retention, acceptability and feasibility indicate that the participants valued the programme. Analyses of outcome measures indicate that the programme has promise as a treatment option for autistic adults experiencing IU.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta se angustia mucho ante lo incierto o lo imprevisto, puede valer la pena preguntar a su equipo de salud por programas centrados en la «intolerancia a la incertidumbre», adaptados a personas autistas. Mientras tanto, se puede hablar con calma de qué situaciones inciertas pesan más y qué ayuda a afrontarlas paso a paso, respetando su ritmo. Este estudio de diseño de caso único probó un programa individual de ocho sesiones (CUES-A) con cuatro adultos autistas, que lo valoraron positivamente y mostraron señales prometedoras. Al ser solo cuatro personas y sin grupo de comparación, los resultados son preliminares y no aplican a todos.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult feels very anxious when things are uncertain or unexpected, it may be worth asking their health team about programmes that focus on 'intolerance of uncertainty' and are adapted for autistic people. Meanwhile, you can calmly talk together about which uncertain situations feel hardest and what helps to face them step by step, at their own pace. This single case experimental design study tested an eight-session individual programme (CUES-A) with four autistic adults, who valued it and showed promising changes. With only four people and no comparison group, the findings are early and will not fit everyone.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen blir mycket orolig när saker är osäkra eller oväntade kan det vara värt att fråga vården om program som fokuserar på 'intolerans för osäkerhet' och är anpassade för autistiska personer. Under tiden kan ni lugnt prata om vilka osäkra situationer som känns svårast och vad som hjälper att möta dem steg för steg, i personens egen takt. Studien, en experimentell single case-design, prövade ett individuellt program med åtta sessioner (CUES-A) med fyra autistiska vuxna, som uppskattade det och visade lovande förändringar. Med bara fyra deltagare och ingen jämförelsegrupp är resultaten preliminära och passar inte alla.

title: Risk markers for suicidality in autistic adults.
authors: Cassidy S, Bradley L, Shaw R, Baron-Cohen S
abstract: Background Research has shown high rates of suicidality in autism spectrum conditions (ASC), but there is lack of research into why this is the case. Many common experiences of autistic adults, such as depression or unemployment, overlap with known risk markers for suicide in the general population. However, it is unknown whether there are risk markers unique to ASC that require new tailored suicide prevention strategies. Methods Through consultation with a steering group of autistic adults, a survey was developed aiming to identify unique risk markers for suicidality in this group. The survey measured suicidality (SBQ-R), non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI-AT), mental health problems, unmet support needs, employment, satisfaction with living arrangements, self-reported autistic traits (AQ), delay in ASC diagnosis, and 'camouflaging' ASC. One hundred sixty-four autistic adults (65 male, 99 female) and 169 general population adults (54 males, 115 females) completed the survey online. Results A majority of autistic adults (72%) scored above the recommended psychiatric cut-off for suicide risk on the SBQ-R; significantly higher than general population (GP) adults (33%). After statistically controlling for a range of demographics and diagnoses, ASC diagnosis and self-reported autistic traits in the general population significantly predicted suicidality. In autistic adults, non-suicidal self-injury, camouflaging, and number of unmet support needs significantly predicted suicidality. Conclusions Results confirm previously reported high rates of suicidality in ASC, and demonstrate that ASC diagnosis, and self-reported autistic traits in the general population are independent risk markers for suicidality. This suggests there are unique factors associated with autism and autistic traits that increase risk of suicidality. Camouflaging and unmet support needs appear to be risk markers for suicidality unique to ASC. Non-suicidal self-injury, employment, and mental health problems appear to be risk markers shared with the general population that are significantly more prevalent in the autistic community. Implications for understanding and prevention of suicide in ASC are discussed.

title: Interoceptive impairments do not lie at the heart of autism or alexithymia.
authors: Nicholson TM, Williams DM, Grainger C, Christensen JF, Calvo-Merino B, Gaigg SB
abstract: Quattrocki and Friston (2014) argued that abnormalities in interoception-the process of representing one's internal physiological states-could lie at the heart of autism, because of the critical role interoception plays in the ontogeny of social-affective processes. This proposal drew criticism from proponents of the alexithymia hypothesis, who argue that social-affective and underlying interoceptive impairments are not a feature of autism per se, but of alexithymia (a condition characterized by difficulties describing and identifying one's own emotions), which commonly co-occurs with autism. Despite the importance of this debate for our understanding of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), and of the role of interoceptive impairments in psychopathology, more generally, direct empirical evidence is scarce and inconsistent. Experiment 1 examined in a sample of 137 neurotypical (NT) individuals the association among autistic traits, alexithymia, and interoceptive accuracy (IA) on a standard heartbeat-tracking measure of IA. In Experiment 2, IA was assessed in 46 adults with ASD (27 of whom had clinically significant alexithymia) and 48 NT adults. Experiment 1 confirmed strong associations between autistic traits and alexithymia, but yielded no evidence to suggest that either was associated with interoceptive difficulties. Similarly, Experiment 2 provided no evidence for interoceptive impairments in autistic adults, irrespective of any co-occurring alexithymia. Bayesian analyses consistently supported the null hypothesis. The observations pose a significant challenge to notions that interoceptive impairments constitute a core feature of either ASD or alexithymia, at least as far as the direct perception of interoceptive signals is concerned. (PsycINFO Database Record

sheet.es: No des por hecho que una persona autista percibe mal las señales de su cuerpo. Si le cuesta poner nombre a lo que siente, conviene explorar la alexitimia con calma, sin culparle, y ofrecer apoyos para identificar emociones. Evidencia: dos experimentos, uno con 137 personas neurotípicas y otro con 46 adultos autistas y 48 adultos neurotípicos, usando una tarea de seguimiento del latido del corazón. No encontraron dificultades en esa percepción, tuvieran o no alexitimia. Límites: solo midió la percepción directa de los latidos, en adultos, y no refleja a cada persona; otras formas de sentir el cuerpo pueden variar.
sheet.en: Don't assume an autistic person misreads their body's signals. If they find it hard to name what they feel, it may be worth gently exploring alexithymia, without blame, and offering supports for identifying emotions. Evidence: two experiments, one with 137 neurotypical people and one with 46 autistic adults and 48 neurotypical adults, using a heartbeat-tracking task. They found no difficulty in this kind of perception, whether or not alexithymia was present. Limits: it measured only direct perception of the heartbeat, in adults, and cannot describe every person; other ways of sensing the body may differ.
sheet.sv: Utgå inte från att en autistisk person uppfattar kroppens signaler fel. Om det är svårt att sätta ord på känslor kan det vara värt att varsamt utforska alexitymi, utan skuld, och erbjuda stöd för att identifiera känslor. Evidens: två experiment, ett med 137 neurotypiska personer och ett med 46 autistiska vuxna och 48 neurotypiska vuxna, med en uppgift där man följer sin hjärtrytm. Man fann inga svårigheter med denna uppfattning, oavsett alexitymi. Begränsningar: studien mätte bara direkt uppfattning av hjärtslag hos vuxna och gäller inte varje person; andra sätt att känna kroppen kan skilja sig.

title: Management of Autistic Patients in Dental Office: A Clinical Update.
authors: Chandrashekhar S, S Bommangoudar J
journal: International journal of clinical pediatric dentistry
abstract: Autism is an intellectual developmental disorder characterized by insidious disability in communication, social interaction, and using language and abstract concepts. This organic disorder is known to have deformities in brain, i.e., cerebellum and limbic system, showing wide spectrum of systemic and behavioral symptoms. The oral health care of such patients can be complicated as they cannot verbalize complaints about any dental problems they may be experiencing and can display a variety of behaviors and reactions to small changes also. This study summarizes etiology and diagnosis of this disorder with the special emphasis on the issues encountered while coping with children with autistic spectrum. How to cite this article: Chandrashekhar S, Bommangoudar JS. Management of Autistic Patients in Dental Office: A Clinical Update. Int J Clin Pediatr Dent 2018;11(3):219-227.

sheet.es: Antes de la cita dental, avise al equipo de que la persona es autista y cuéntele qué le ayuda: qué le incomoda, cómo comunica el dolor y qué cambios le cuestan. Como a veces no explica con palabras que algo le duele, conviene observar gestos o cambios de conducta. Se trata de una revisión que resume causas, diagnóstico y dificultades al atender a niñas y niños autistas en la consulta dental. Es un resumen general, con un lenguaje a veces centrado en déficits, y no prueba un método concreto; cada persona es distinta, así que adapte las ideas a la suya.
sheet.en: Before a dental visit, tell the team that the person is autistic and share what helps: what bothers them, how they show pain, and which changes are hard. Because someone may not say in words that something hurts, watch for gestures or shifts in behaviour. This is a review that summarises causes, diagnosis and the difficulties of caring for autistic children in the dental office. It is a general overview, sometimes written in deficit-focused language, and it does not test a specific method. Every person is different, so adapt these ideas to the person you support.
sheet.sv: Berätta för tandvårdsteamet före besöket att personen är autistisk och dela vad som hjälper: vad som är obehagligt, hur personen visar smärta och vilka förändringar som är svåra. Eftersom någon kanske inte säger med ord att det gör ont kan du vara uppmärksam på gester eller förändringar i beteende. Detta är en översikt som sammanfattar orsaker, diagnos och svårigheter när autistiska barn får tandvård. Den är en allmän sammanfattning, ibland med bristfokuserat språk, och prövar ingen särskild metod. Alla är olika, så anpassa idéerna till den person du stödjer.

title: Social Skills Deficits in Autism Spectrum Disorder: Potential Biological Origins and Progress in Developing Therapeutic Agents.
authors: Frye RE
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder is defined by two core symptoms: a deficit in social communication and the presence of repetitive behaviors and/or restricted interests. Currently, there is no US Food and Drug Administration-approved drug for these core symptoms. This article reviews the biological origins of the social function deficit associated with autism spectrum disorder and the drug therapies with the potential to treat this deficit. A review of the history of autism demonstrates that a deficit in social interaction has been the defining feature of the concept of autism from its conception. Abnormalities identified in early social skill development and an overview of the pathophysiology abnormalities associated with autism spectrum disorder are discussed as are the abnormalities in brain circuits associated with the social function deficit. Previous and ongoing clinical trials examining agents that have the potential to improve social deficits associated with autism spectrum disorder are discussed in detail. This discussion reveals that agents such as oxytocin and propranolol are particularly promising and undergoing active investigation, while other agents such as vasopressin agonists and antagonists are being activity investigated but have limited published evidence at this time. In addition, agents such as bumetanide and manipulation of the enteric microbiome using microbiota transfer therapy appear to have promising effects on core autism spectrum disorder symptoms including social function. Other pertinent issues associated with developing treatments in autism spectrum disorder, such as disease heterogeneity, high placebo response rates, trial design, and the most appropriate way of assessing effects on social skills (outcome measures), are also discussed.

sheet.es: Esta revisión trata de fármacos, así que es un estudio médico: cualquier decisión sobre medicación corresponde a un profesional clínico. Mientras tanto, puede ayudar valorar con la persona autista qué apoyos sociales le resultan útiles, sin esperar a un tratamiento. Es una revisión de la bibliografía, no un ensayo propio, y no reúne a participantes nuevos. Describe ensayos previos y en curso sobre la comunicación social. Sus límites: la propia revisión señala la diversidad entre personas autistas, respuestas altas al placebo y dudas sobre cómo medir los efectos, así que sus conclusiones no valen para todas las personas.
sheet.en: This review looks at drugs, so it is a medical study: any decision about medication belongs to a clinician. Meanwhile, it can help to ask the autistic person which social supports feel useful to them, without waiting for any treatment. The evidence is a review of existing literature, not a new trial with its own participants. It describes earlier and ongoing trials on social communication. Its limits: the review itself notes differences between autistic people, high placebo responses and doubts about how to measure effects, so its conclusions do not apply to everyone.
sheet.sv: Den här översikten handlar om läkemedel, så den är en medicinsk studie: beslut om medicinering hör till en kliniker. Under tiden kan det hjälpa att fråga den autistiska personen vilket socialt stöd som känns användbart, utan att vänta på någon behandling. Underlaget är en översikt av befintlig litteratur, inte en ny studie med egna deltagare. Den beskriver tidigare och pågående studier om social kommunikation. Begränsningar: översikten själv nämner skillnader mellan autistiska personer, höga placebosvar och osäkerhet kring hur effekter ska mätas, så slutsatserna gäller inte alla.

title: Effectiveness of Virtual Reality for Children and Adolescents with Autism Spectrum Disorder: An Evidence-Based Systematic Review.
authors: Mesa-Gresa P, Gil-Gómez H, Lozano-Quilis JA, Gil-Gómez JA
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disease that is specially characterized by impairments in social communication and social skills. ASD has a high prevalence in children, affecting 1 in 160 subjects. Virtual reality (VR) has emerged as an effective tool for intervention in the health field. Different recent papers have reviewed the VR-based treatments in ASD, but they have an important limitation because they only use clinical databases and do not include important technical indexes such as the Web of Science index or the Scimago Journal & Country Rank. To our knowledge, this is the first contribution that has carried out an evidence-based systematic review including both clinical and technical databases about the effectiveness of VR-based intervention in ASD. The initial search identified a total of 450 records. After the exclusion of the papers that are not studies, duplicated articles, and the screening of the abstract and full text, 31 articles met the PICO (Population, Intervention, Comparison and Outcomes) criteria and were selected for analysis. The studies examined suggest moderate evidence about the effectiveness of VR-based treatments in ASD. VR can add many advantages to the treatment of ASD symptomatology, but it is necessary to develop consistent validations in future studies to state that VR can effectively complement the traditional treatments.

sheet.es: La realidad virtual puede ser una opción más para practicar habilidades sociales con niñas, niños y adolescentes autistas, pero conviene probarla con calma y observar si a cada persona le resulta cómoda y útil. Es una revisión sistemática: se analizaron 31 artículos que cumplían los criterios, de 450 registros iniciales, y sugieren evidencia moderada de efectividad. Sus límites: los autores indican que faltan validaciones consistentes para afirmar que complemente eficazmente las intervenciones tradicionales, y no sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: Virtual reality may be one more option for practising social skills with autistic children and adolescents, but try it gently and watch whether it feels comfortable and useful for that person. This is a systematic review: 31 articles that met the criteria were analysed, from 450 records initially found, and they suggest moderate evidence of effectiveness. Its limits: the authors say more consistent validation is needed before saying it effectively complements traditional approaches, and it is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Virtual reality kan vara ett alternativ till för att öva social förmåga med autistiska barn och ungdomar, men prova försiktigt och se om det känns bekvämt och användbart för just den personen. Det är en systematisk översikt: 31 artiklar som uppfyllde kriterierna analyserades, av 450 poster från början, och de tyder på måttliga belägg för effekt. Begränsningar: författarna menar att fler konsekventa valideringar behövs för att kunna säga att det effektivt kompletterar traditionella metoder, och det är ingen regel för alla.

title: Study protocol for the Australian autism biobank: an international resource to advance autism discovery research.
authors: Alvares GA, Dawson PA, Dissanayake C, Eapen V, Gratten J, Grove R, Henders A, Heussler H, Lawson L, Masi A, Raymond E, Rose F, Wallace L, Wray NR, Whitehouse AJO, Australian Autism Biobank team
abstract: Background The phenotypic and genetic heterogeneity of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) presents considerable challenges in understanding etiological pathways, selecting effective therapies, providing genetic counselling, and predicting clinical outcomes. With advances in genetic and biological research alongside rapid-pace technological innovations, there is an increasing imperative to access large, representative, and diverse cohorts to advance knowledge of ASD. To date, there has not been any single collective effort towards a similar resource in Australia, which has its own unique ethnic and cultural diversity. The Australian Autism Biobank was initiated by the Cooperative Research Centre for Living with Autism (Autism CRC) to establish a large-scale repository of biological samples and detailed clinical information about children diagnosed with ASD to facilitate future discovery research. Methods The primary group of participants were children with a confirmed diagnosis of ASD, aged between 2 and 17 years, recruited through four sites in Australia. No exclusion criteria regarding language level, cognitive ability, or comorbid conditions were applied to ensure a representative cohort was recruited. Both biological parents and siblings were invited to participate, along with children without a diagnosis of ASD, and children who had been queried for an ASD diagnosis but did not meet diagnostic criteria. All children completed cognitive assessments, with probands and parents completing additional assessments measuring ASD symptomatology. Parents completed questionnaires about their child's medical history and early development. Physical measurements and biological samples (blood, stool, urine, and hair) were collected from children, and physical measurements and blood samples were collected from parents. Samples were sent to a central processing site and placed into long-term storage. Discussion The establishment of this biobank is a valuable international resource incorporating detailed clinical and biological information that will help accelerate the pace of ASD discovery research. Recruitment into this study has also supported the feasibility of large-scale biological sample collection in children diagnosed with ASD with comprehensive phenotyping across a wide range of ages, intellectual abilities, and levels of adaptive functioning. This biological and clinical resource will be open to data access requests from national and international researchers to support future discovery research that will benefit the autistic community.

sheet.es: Este estudio no cambia nada en el día a día de su familia: describe cómo se creó un gran banco de datos y muestras para investigar el autismo en el futuro. Si alguna vez le invitan a participar en un biobanco, puede preguntar qué se recogerá, cómo se protegerán los datos y quién podrá usarlos; participar es siempre voluntario. Es un protocolo australiano que reunió a niños y niñas autistas de 2 a 17 años, sin excluir a nadie por lenguaje o capacidad cognitiva, junto con padres, hermanos y otros niños. Su límite: no ofrece resultados ni conclusiones, solo explica el método.
sheet.en: This study changes nothing in your family's daily life: it describes how a large bank of data and samples was set up for future autism research. If you are ever invited to join a biobank, you can ask what will be collected, how the data will be protected and who can use it; taking part is always voluntary. It is an Australian protocol that included autistic children aged 2 to 17, without excluding anyone based on language or cognitive ability, along with parents, siblings and other children. Its limit: it offers no findings or conclusions, it only explains the method.
sheet.sv: Den här studien förändrar ingenting i er familjs vardag: den beskriver hur en stor bank med data och prover byggdes upp för framtida autismforskning. Om ni någon gång blir inbjudna till en biobank kan ni fråga vad som samlas in, hur uppgifterna skyddas och vem som får använda dem; att delta är alltid frivilligt. Det är ett australiskt protokoll med autistiska barn mellan 2 och 17 år, där ingen uteslöts på grund av språk eller kognitiv förmåga, samt föräldrar, syskon och andra barn. Begränsningen: den ger inga resultat eller slutsatser, utan förklarar bara metoden.

title: Supporting and hindering environments for participation of adolescents diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder: A scoping review.
authors: Krieger B, Piškur B, Schulze C, Jakobs U, Beurskens A, Moser A
abstract: The influence of a person's environment and its modifying potential on participation is well recognized for most childhood disabilities, but scarcely studied for adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). A scoping review was conducted, the aim of which was to map the existing literature about supporting and hindering environments for the participation of adolescents with ASD. Sources of scientific evidence were searched for in four databases. Inclusion criteria were the perspectives of adolescents between 12 and 21, families, peers, or significant others; ecologic validity; and a clear connection between environment and participation. The publication dates ranged from 2001 to 2014 and partly up to 2018. The International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) served as the guiding framework for inclusion/exclusion during the selection process. Thematic analysis was performed by five independent reviewers. Results were additionally validated by stakeholders. This scoping review identified 5528 articles, and finally included 31 studies. Two main themes were found: "providing security" indicates how the environment, and specifically the parental, physical, and informational environments, have a securing or intimidating effect. The second theme, "helping to connect", indicates which environments support or hinder social relationships or social activities, and hence participation. An additional third main theme, "tension in participation", relates to ambiguities that seem essential to understand participation or isolation of adolescents with ASD. Results show that participation is a value-laden concept. This research widens the field of dealing with adolescents with ASD, as it directs attention towards the responsibility of the environment regarding participation.

sheet.es: Mañana, antes de pedir que la persona adolescente se adapte, mira el entorno: ¿es predecible, está explicado con claridad y ofrece formas de conectar con otras personas a su ritmo? Cambiar el entorno puede apoyar su participación. La evidencia es una revisión de alcance de 31 estudios, sobre adolescentes autistas de 12 a 21 años, sus familias y otras personas cercanas. Sus límites: reúne estudios muy distintos, no mide qué cambios funcionan mejor y la participación es un concepto con valores propios, así que cada persona puede querer cosas diferentes. Pregúntale qué le da seguridad y qué le gustaría hacer.
sheet.en: Tomorrow, before asking the autistic teenager to adapt, look at the environment: is it predictable, clearly explained, and does it offer ways to connect with others at their own pace? Changing the setting can support participation. The evidence is a scoping review of 31 studies about autistic adolescents aged 12 to 21, their families and other people close to them. Its limits: the studies are very varied, it does not test which changes work best, and participation is a value-laden idea, so each person may want different things. Ask them what makes them feel secure and what they would like to join.
sheet.sv: I morgon, innan du ber den autistiska tonåringen anpassa sig, titta på miljön: är den förutsägbar, tydligt förklarad och ger den möjlighet att få kontakt med andra i egen takt? Att förändra miljön kan stödja delaktighet. Underlaget är en kartläggande översikt av 31 studier om autistiska tonåringar mellan 12 och 21 år, deras familjer och andra närstående. Begränsningar: studierna är mycket olika, översikten prövar inte vilka förändringar som fungerar bäst, och delaktighet är ett värdeladdat begrepp, så olika personer kan vilja olika saker. Fråga vad som ger trygghet och vad personen vill delta i.

title: Autism and the right to education in the EU: Policy mapping and scoping review of the United Kingdom, France, Poland and Spain.
authors: Roleska M, Roman-Urrestarazu A, Griffiths S, Ruigrok ANV, Holt R, van Kessel R, McColl K, Sherlaw W, Brayne C, Czabanowska K
abstract: Introduction Autistic people may have different educational needs that need to be met to allow them to develop their full potential. Education and disability policies remain within the competence of EU Member States, with current educational standards and provisions for autistic people implemented locally. This scoping review aims to map EU and national special education policies with the goal of scoping the level of fulfilment of the right to education of autistic people. Methods Four EU countries (United Kingdom, France, Poland and Spain) were included in this scoping review study. Governmental policies in the field of education, special education needs and disability law were included. Path dependency framework was used for data analysis; a net of inter-dependencies between international, EU and national policies was created. Results and discussion Each country created policies where the right to free education without discrimination is provided. Poland does not have an autism specific strategy, whereas the United Kingdom, France and Spain have policies specifically designed for autistic individuals. Within the United Kingdom, all countries created different autism plans, nevertheless all aim to reach the same goal-inclusive education for autistic children that leads to the development of their full potential. Conclusion Policy-making across Europe in the field of education has been changing through the years in favour of autistic people. Today their rights are noticed and considered, but there is still room for improvement. Results showed that approaches and policies vastly differ between countries, more Member States should be analysed in a similar manner to gain a broader and clearer view with a special focus on disability rights in Central and Eastern Europe.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a un niño autista, conviene saber que las políticas educativas de cada país establecen el derecho a una educación gratuita y sin discriminación; puedes consultar qué recoge la normativa de tu país o región al hablar con el centro escolar. La evidencia es una revisión sistemática de alcance que analizó políticas gubernamentales de cuatro países: Reino Unido, Francia, Polonia y España. Polonia no tiene una estrategia específica sobre autismo; los otros tres sí. Sus límites: estudia leyes y planes, no la experiencia real en las aulas, solo incluye cuatro países y las políticas difieren mucho entre ellos, así que no describe lo que ocurrirá en tu caso.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic child, it helps to know that education policies in each country set out the right to free education without discrimination; you can ask the school what the rules in your country or region say. The evidence is a scoping review that mapped government policies in four countries: the United Kingdom, France, Poland and Spain. Poland has no autism-specific strategy, while the other three do. Its limits: it looks at laws and plans, not what actually happens in classrooms, it covers only four countries, and approaches differ widely, so it cannot tell you what will happen in your situation.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar ett autistiskt barn är det bra att veta att utbildningspolicyer i varje land slår fast rätten till gratis utbildning utan diskriminering; du kan fråga skolan vad reglerna i ditt land eller din region säger. Underlaget är en kartläggande översikt av regeringars policyer i fyra länder: Storbritannien, Frankrike, Polen och Spanien. Polen saknar en autismspecifik strategi, medan de andra tre har det. Begränsningar: studien granskar lagar och planer, inte vad som faktiskt sker i klassrummen, omfattar bara fyra länder och synsätten skiljer sig mycket, så den kan inte säga vad som gäller i just din situation.

title: Sex: A Significant Risk Factor for Neurodevelopmental and Neurodegenerative Disorders.
authors: Pinares-Garcia P, Stratikopoulos M, Zagato A, Loke H, Lee J
abstract: Males and females sometimes significantly differ in their propensity to develop neurological disorders. Females suffer more from mood disorders such as depression and anxiety, whereas males are more susceptible to deficits in the dopamine system including Parkinson's disease (PD), attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and autism. Despite this, biological sex is rarely considered when making treatment decisions in neurological disorders. A better understanding of the molecular mechanism(s) underlying sex differences in the healthy and diseased brain will help to devise diagnostic and therapeutic strategies optimal for each sex. Thus, the aim of this review is to discuss the available evidence on sex differences in neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders regarding prevalence, progression, symptoms and response to therapy. We also discuss the sex-related factors such as gonadal sex hormones and sex chromosome genes and how these might help to explain some of the clinically observed sex differences in these disorders. In particular, we highlight the emerging role of the Y-chromosome gene, SRY, in the male brain and its potential role as a male-specific risk factor for disorders such as PD, autism, and ADHD in many individuals.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista, recuerda que el sexo biológico puede influir en cómo se presentan y se atienden las diferencias neurológicas, así que merece la pena comentar con su clínico cómo encaja cada persona. Es una revisión que reúne la evidencia disponible sobre diferencias entre sexos en prevalencia, progresión, síntomas y respuesta a terapias en varios trastornos, entre ellos el autismo. Sus límites: es una revisión y propone ideas biológicas, como un gen del cromosoma Y, que aún son emergentes; no sirve como regla para ninguna persona concreta ni para tomar decisiones médicas, que corresponden a un clínico.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person, remember that biological sex may shape how neurological differences show up and are supported, so it is worth discussing with their clinician how things fit that individual. This is a review gathering available evidence on sex differences in prevalence, progression, symptoms and response to therapy across several conditions, including autism. Its limits: it is a review and proposes biological ideas, such as a Y-chromosome gene, that are still emerging. It is not a rule for any one person, and medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person kan det vara bra att veta att biologiskt kön kan påverka hur neurologiska skillnader visar sig och bemöts, så det är värt att prata med personens kliniker om hur det passar just den personen. Detta är en översikt som samlar tillgänglig evidens om könsskillnader i förekomst, utveckling, symtom och svar på behandling vid flera tillstånd, bland annat autism. Begränsningar: det är en översikt och lyfter biologiska idéer, till exempel en gen på Y-kromosomen, som fortfarande är under utveckling. Den är ingen regel för en enskild person, och medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker.

title: The impact of robotic intervention on joint attention in children with autism spectrum disorders.
authors: Kumazaki H, Yoshikawa Y, Yoshimura Y, Ikeda T, Hasegawa C, Saito DN, Tomiyama S, An KM, Shimaya J, Ishiguro H, Matsumoto Y, Minabe Y, Kikuchi M
abstract: Background A growing body of anecdotal evidence indicates that the use of robots may provide unique opportunities for assisting children with autism spectrum disorders (ASD). However, previous studies investigating the effects of interventions using robots on joint attention (JA) in children with ASD have shown insufficient results. The robots used in these studies could not turn their eyes, which was a limitation preventing the robot from resembling a human agent. Methods We compared the behavior of children with ASD with that of children with typical development (TD) during a JA elicitation task while the children interacted with either a human or a robotic agent. We used the robot "CommU," which has clear eyes and can turn its eyes, for the robotic intervention. The age range of the participants was limited to 5-6 years. Results Sixty-eight participants participated in this study, including 30 (10 females and 20 males) children with ASD and 38 (13 females and 25 males) children with TD. The participants were randomly assigned to one of the following two groups: the robotic intervention group or the control group. JA in the children with ASD was better during the robotic intervention than during the human agent intervention. These children exhibited improved performance in the JA task with human after interacting with the robot CommU. JA was differentially facilitated by the human and robotic agents between the ASD and TD children. Conclusions The findings of this study significantly contribute to the literature on the impact of robots on JA and provide information regarding the suitability of specific robot types for therapeutic use.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija autista tiene entre 5 y 6 años, puede probar actividades de atención conjunta (mirar juntos lo mismo) con un robot sencillo cuyos ojos se mueven, siempre que le resulte agradable, y luego repetirlas con una persona. Es un ensayo con 68 participantes: 30 niños con TEA y 38 con desarrollo típico. Los niños con TEA mostraron mejor atención conjunta con el robot CommU que con una persona, y mejoraron después con la persona. Es un estudio pequeño, de una sola edad y un solo robot, así que no sirve como regla para cada niño.
sheet.en: If your autistic child is 5 to 6 years old, you could try joint attention activities (looking at the same thing together) with a simple robot whose eyes move, if they enjoy it, and then repeat them with a person. This was a trial with 68 participants: 30 children with ASD and 38 with typical development. The children with ASD showed better joint attention with the robot CommU than with a person, and improved afterwards with the person. It was a small study, with one age group and one robot, so it is not a rule for every child.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn är 5–6 år kan du prova övningar i delad uppmärksamhet (att titta på samma sak tillsammans) med en enkel robot vars ögon rör sig, om barnet tycker om det, och sedan upprepa dem med en person. Det var en studie med 68 deltagare: 30 barn med ASD och 38 med typisk utveckling. Barnen med ASD visade bättre delad uppmärksamhet med roboten CommU än med en person, och förbättrades sedan med personen. Studien var liten, med en åldersgrupp och en robot, så den gäller inte som regel för varje barn.

title: Effectiveness of cognitive, developmental, and behavioural interventions for Autism Spectrum Disorder in preschool-aged children: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Su Maw S, Haga C
abstract: Background Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is characterised by significant impairment in social communication and the presence of restrictive and repetitive behaviour or interest. Intervention during early childhood could decrease ASD symptoms. We aimed to identify the most effective intervention based on cognitive, developmental, and behavioural approaches and the factors that impact the effectiveness of the intervention. Methods We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of existing interventions for ASD in preschool-aged children. Electronic databases were searched for related articles with randomised controlled trial (RCT) designs published between 2001 to 2015. Outcome measures were communication, behavioural and cognitive skills, reported as standardised mean differences (SMD) compared to a control group. A Random-effects model was utilised to calculate the pooled estimate effect. Between-study variability was also assessed. The registering number of this study is CRD42017035354. Findings Out of the initial 5174 studies that were identified, there were 14 RCTs (746 children) that were included in the final systematic review and meta-analysis. Pooled estimate effect provided by random-effects model was 0.23 (95% confidence interval, CI [0.08-0.37]) with no between-study heterogeneity ( I 2 = 0.00%, p = 0.0018). Three studies of music therapy interventions provided the greatest outcome effects with a shorter duration and lower intensity. SMD for music therapies ranged from 0.40 to 0.62 with 95% CI [0.22 to 1.85]. The quality of the health care provider, the duration, and the intensity of intervention played an important role in the effectiveness of the intervention. Interpretation Music therapy appears to be an effective tool for improving social interaction in preschool-aged children with ASD. However, more evidence-based trials are required to further validate the effectiveness of music therapy in ASD.

sheet.es: Si buscas apoyo para tu hija o hijo autista en edad preescolar, puede merecer la pena explorar la musicoterapia junto con otras intervenciones, y fijarte en la calidad de quien las ofrece, la duración y la intensidad. Es un metaanálisis de 14 ensayos controlados aleatorizados con 746 niñas y niños autistas de edad preescolar. Tres estudios de musicoterapia mostraron los mayores efectos con menor duración e intensidad. Los límites: los propios autores piden más ensayos para confirmarlo, y los resultados son promedios que no predicen lo que ayudará a cada niña o niño. Conviene observar sus preferencias y comentarlo con su equipo profesional.
sheet.en: If you are looking for support for your autistic preschool-aged child, music therapy may be worth exploring alongside other approaches, and it helps to look at the quality of the provider, the duration and the intensity. This is a meta-analysis of 14 randomised controlled trials with 746 autistic preschool-aged children. Three music therapy studies showed the greatest effects with shorter duration and lower intensity. Limits: the authors say more trials are needed to confirm this, and the results are averages that cannot predict what will help each child. Watch your child's preferences and discuss options with their professional team.
sheet.sv: Om du söker stöd för ditt autistiska förskolebarn kan musikterapi vara värt att utforska vid sidan av andra insatser, och det hjälper att se på utförarens kvalitet, varaktighet och intensitet. Detta är en metaanalys av 14 randomiserade kontrollerade studier med 746 autistiska barn i förskoleåldern. Tre studier om musikterapi visade störst effekt med kortare varaktighet och lägre intensitet. Begränsningar: författarna menar att fler studier behövs för att bekräfta detta, och resultaten är genomsnitt som inte förutsäger vad som hjälper just ditt barn. Lägg märke till barnets preferenser och diskutera alternativen med barnets professionella team.

title: Clinical and Molecular Characteristics of Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Rose S, Niyazov DM, Rossignol DA, Goldenthal M, Kahler SG, Frye RE
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) affects ~ 2% of children in the United States. The etiology of ASD likely involves environmental factors triggering physiological abnormalities in genetically sensitive individuals. One of these major physiological abnormalities is mitochondrial dysfunction, which may affect a significant subset of children with ASD. Here we systematically review the literature on human studies of mitochondrial dysfunction related to ASD. Clinical aspects of mitochondrial dysfunction in ASD include unusual neurodevelopmental regression, especially if triggered by an inflammatory event, gastrointestinal symptoms, seizures, motor delays, fatigue and lethargy. Traditional biomarkers of mitochondrial disease are widely reported to be abnormal in ASD, but appear non-specific. Newer biomarkers include buccal cell enzymology, biomarkers of fatty acid metabolism, non-mitochondrial enzyme function, apoptosis markers and mitochondrial antibodies. Many genetic abnormalities are associated with mitochondrial dysfunction in ASD, including chromosomal abnormalities, mitochondrial DNA mutations and large-scale deletions, and mutations in both mitochondrial and non-mitochondrial nuclear genes. Mitochondrial dysfunction has been described in immune and buccal cells, fibroblasts, muscle and gastrointestinal tissue and the brains of individuals with ASD. Several environmental factors, including toxicants, microbiome metabolites and an oxidized microenvironment are shown to modulate mitochondrial function in ASD tissues. Investigations of treatments for mitochondrial dysfunction in ASD are promising but preliminary. The etiology of mitochondrial dysfunction and how to define it in ASD is currently unclear. However, preliminary evidence suggests that the mitochondria may be a fruitful target for treatment and prevention of ASD. Further research is needed to better understand the role of mitochondrial dysfunction in the pathophysiology of ASD.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija autista pierde habilidades que ya tenía (sobre todo tras una fiebre o infección), o tiene cansancio inusual, problemas digestivos, convulsiones o retrasos motores, anótalo con fechas y coméntalo con su equipo médico; puede valer la pena una evaluación del metabolismo energético. Esta revisión sistemática reúne estudios en humanos sobre el funcionamiento de las mitocondrias en personas autistas. Sus límites: los marcadores son poco específicos, no hay una definición clara del problema, los tratamientos estudiados son preliminares, y no describe a todas las personas autistas ni busca cambiar quién es tu hijo.
sheet.en: If your autistic child loses skills they already had (especially after a fever or infection), or has unusual tiredness, gut problems, seizures or motor delays, write it down with dates and raise it with their medical team; an assessment of energy metabolism may be worth discussing. This systematic review gathers human studies on how mitochondria work in autistic people. Its limits: the markers are not very specific, there is no clear definition of the problem, the treatments studied are preliminary, and it does not describe every autistic person or aim to change who your child is.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn tappar förmågor det redan hade (särskilt efter feber eller infektion), eller har ovanlig trötthet, magbesvär, krampanfall eller motoriska förseningar, skriv ner det med datum och ta upp det med barnets vårdteam; en utredning av energiomsättningen kan vara värd att diskutera. Denna systematiska översikt samlar studier på människor om hur mitokondrierna fungerar hos autistiska personer. Begränsningar: markörerna är ospecifika, problemet saknar tydlig definition, studerade behandlingar är preliminära, och den beskriver inte alla autistiska personer eller syftar till att ändra vem ditt barn är.

title: Scoping Review of the Driving Behaviour of and Driver Training Programs for People on the Autism Spectrum.
authors: Wilson NJ, Lee HC, Vaz S, Vindin P, Cordier R
abstract: Gaining a driver's licence represents increased independence and can lead to improved quality of life for individuals and their families. Learning to drive a motor vehicle and maintaining safe on-road skills are often more difficult for people on the autism spectrum. Many countries currently have no autism-specific licencing requirements for learner drivers, and there is a general lack of ASD-specific support and training packages for individuals, their families, and driving instructors. This review synthesises the peer-reviewed literature about the driving characteristics of drivers on the spectrum and driver training available for the cohort. The evidence in this review showed that individuals on the autism spectrum drive differently from their neurotypical counterparts. There are shortcomings in tactical skills of drivers on the autism spectrum, but the extent to which this affects their own safety or the safety of other road users is unclear. Tactical skills can be improved through training programs. There are few autism spectrum-specific learner training programs available. Development of an effective training program will benefit individuals on the spectrum to learn to drive, be independent, and be safe on the road.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista quiere aprender a conducir, conviene buscar práctica y apoyo que se ajusten a ella, y hablar con la autoescuela sobre cómo prefiere aprender. Es una revisión sistemática de la literatura científica sobre cómo conducen las personas autistas y qué formación existe. Indica que conducen de forma distinta a las personas neurotípicas, que las habilidades tácticas pueden mejorar con programas de formación y que hay pocos programas específicos para autistas. Sus límites: no está claro cómo influye esto en la seguridad, y no vale como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If an autistic person wants to learn to drive, look for practice and support that fit how they learn, and talk with the driving school about their preferred way of being taught. This is a systematic review of published research on how autistic people drive and what training exists. It found that they drive differently from neurotypical drivers, that tactical skills can improve with training programs, and that few autism-specific programs exist. Its limits: it is unclear how this affects safety, and it is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person vill lära sig köra bil, sök övning och stöd som passar hur hen lär sig, och prata med trafikskolan om hur hen helst undervisas. Detta är en systematisk översikt av publicerad forskning om hur autistiska personer kör och vilken utbildning som finns. Den fann att de kör annorlunda än neurotypiska förare, att taktiska färdigheter kan förbättras med utbildningsprogram och att det finns få autismspecifika program. Begränsningar: det är oklart hur detta påverkar säkerheten, och resultaten gäller inte som regel för varje person.

title: Developmental disabilities among children younger than 5 years in 195 countries and territories, 1990-2016: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2016.
authors: Global Research on Developmental Disabilities Collaborators
abstract: Background The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) mandate systematic monitoring of the health and wellbeing of all children to achieve optimal early childhood development. However, global epidemiological data on children with developmental disabilities are scarce. The Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study 2016 provides a comprehensive assessment of prevalence and years lived with disability (YLDs) for development disabilities among children younger than 5 years in 195 countries and territories from 1990 to 2016. Methods We estimated prevalence and YLDs for epilepsy, intellectual disability, hearing loss, vision loss, autism spectrum disorder, and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder. YLDs were estimated as the product of the prevalence estimate and the disability weight for each mutually exclusive disorder, corrected for comorbidity. We used DisMod-MR 2.1, a Bayesian meta-regression tool, on a pool of primary data derived from systematic reviews of the literature, health surveys, hospital and claims databases, cohort studies, and disease-specific registries. Findings Globally, 52·9 million (95% uncertainty interval [UI] 48·7-57·3; or 8·4% [7·7-9·1]) children younger than 5 years (54% males) had developmental disabilities in 2016 compared with 53·0 million (49·0-57·1; or 8·9% [8·2-9·5]) in 1990. About 95% of these children lived in low-income and middle-income countries. YLDs among these children increased from 3·8 million (95% UI 2·8-4·9) in 1990 to 3·9 million (2·9-5·2) in 2016. These disabilities accounted for 13·3% of the 29·3 million YLDs for all health conditions among children younger than 5 years in 2016. Vision loss was the most prevalent disability, followed by hearing loss, intellectual disability, and autism spectrum disorder. However, intellectual disability was the largest contributor to YLDs in both 1990 and 2016. Although the prevalence of developmental disabilities among children younger than 5 years decreased in all countries (except for North America) between 1990 and 2016, the number of children with developmental disabilities increased significantly in sub-Saharan Africa (71·3%) and in North Africa and the Middle East (7·6%). South Asia had the highest prevalence of children with developmental disabilities in 2016 and North America had the lowest. Interpretation The global burden of developmental disabilities has not significantly improved since 1990, suggesting inadequate global attention on the developmental potential of children who survived childhood as a result of child survival programmes, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa and south Asia. The SDGs provide a framework for policy and action to address the needs of children with or at risk of developmental disabilities, particularly in resource-poor countries. Funding The Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation.

sheet.es: Si cuida a un niño autista menor de 5 años, este estudio recuerda que conviene pedir pronto apoyo al desarrollo y que los servicios no llegan por igual a todos los lugares. Es una revisión sistemática con análisis global de datos de 195 países y territorios entre 1990 y 2016, que estimó cuántos niños menores de 5 años tenían discapacidades del desarrollo, entre ellas el autismo. Sus límites: son estimaciones estadísticas basadas en datos muy desiguales, no describen a ningún niño en concreto y no indican qué apoyo necesita su hijo.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic child under 5, this study is a reminder that asking early for developmental support is worthwhile, and that services do not reach every place equally. It is a systematic review with a global analysis of data from 195 countries and territories between 1990 and 2016, estimating how many children under 5 had developmental disabilities, autism among them. Its limits: these are statistical estimates built on very uneven data, they do not describe any individual child, and they cannot tell you what support your child needs.
sheet.sv: Om du tar hand om ett autistiskt barn under 5 år påminner studien om att det är värt att be om stöd för utvecklingen tidigt, och att insatserna inte når alla platser lika. Det är en systematisk översikt med en global analys av data från 195 länder och territorier mellan 1990 och 2016, som uppskattade hur många barn under 5 år som hade utvecklingsrelaterade funktionsnedsättningar, bland dem autism. Begränsningar: det är statistiska uppskattningar baserade på mycket ojämna data, de beskriver inget enskilt barn och säger inte vilket stöd just ditt barn behöver.

title: Paediatric Autism Communication Therapy-Generalised (PACT-G) against treatment as usual for reducing symptom severity in young children with autism spectrum disorder: study protocol for a randomised controlled trial.
authors: Green J, Aldred C, Charman T, Le Couteur A, Emsley RA, Grahame V, Howlin P, Humphrey N, Leadbitter K, McConachie H, Parr JR, Pickles A, Slonims V, Taylor C, PACT-G Group
abstract: Background Prior evidence shows that behaviours closely related to the intervention delivered for autism are amenable to change, but it is more difficult to generalise treatment effects beyond the intervention context. We test an early autism intervention designed to promote generalisation of therapy-acquired skills into home and school contexts to improve adaptive function and reduce symptoms. A detailed mechanism study will address the process of such generalisation. Objective 1 will be to test if the PACT-G intervention improves autism symptom outcome in the home and school context of the intervention as well as in the primary outcome research setting. Objective 2 will use the mechanism analysis to test for evidence of acquired skills from intervention generalizing across contexts and producing additive effects on primary outcome. Methods/design This is a three-site, two-parallel-group, randomised controlled trial of the experimental treatment plus treatment as usual (TAU) versus TAU alone. Children aged 2-11 years (n = 244 (122 intervention/122 TAU; ~ 82/site) meeting criteria for core autism will be eligible. The experimental intervention builds on a clinic-based Pre-school Autism Communication Treatment model (PACT), delivered with the primary caregiver, combined with additional theory- and evidence-based strategies designed to enhance the generalisation of effects into naturalistic home and education contexts. The control intervention will be TAU. Primary outcome autism symptom outcome, researcher-assessed using a standardised protocol. Secondary outcomes autism symptoms, child interaction with parent or teacher, language and reported functional outcomes in home and school settings. Outcomes measured at baseline and 12-month endpoint in all settings with interim interaction measurements (7 months) to test treatment effect mechanisms. Primary analysis will estimate between-group difference in primary outcome using analysis of covariance with test of homogeneity of effect across age group. Mechanism analysis will use regression models to test for mediation on primary outcome by parent-child and teaching staff-child social interaction. Discussion This is an efficacy and mechanism trial of generalising evidence-based autism treatment into home and school settings. It will provide data on whether extending treatment across naturalistic contexts enhances overall effect and data on the mechanism in autism development of the generalisation of acquired developmental skills across contexts. Trial registration ISRCTN, ID: 25378536 . Prospectively registered on 9 March 2016.

sheet.es: Este estudio es un protocolo, así que aún no ofrece resultados que puedan guiar su día a día. Plantea una idea útil: que las habilidades de comunicación practicadas en terapia se lleven también a casa y a la escuela, con la familia y el profesorado como apoyo. Si le interesa, puede preguntar a los profesionales qué se practica y cómo se traslada al entorno cotidiano. Evidencia: describe un ensayo aleatorizado previsto en tres centros, con 244 niños y niñas de 2-11 años, que compara la intervención más la atención habitual con la atención habitual sola. Límites: no presenta hallazgos, y aunque se publicaran no valdrían para todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: This is a study protocol, so it has no results yet that could guide your day. It raises a useful idea: communication skills practised in therapy should also be carried into home and school, with caregivers and teaching staff supporting them. If this interests you, you could ask professionals what is practised and how it is brought into everyday settings. Evidence: it describes a planned randomised trial at three sites, with 244 children aged 2-11 years, comparing the intervention plus treatment as usual against treatment as usual alone. Limits: it reports no findings, and even once results exist they would not apply to every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Detta är ett studieprotokoll, så det finns ännu inga resultat som kan vägleda din vardag. Det lyfter en användbar tanke: kommunikationsfärdigheter som tränas i terapi bör också föras in i hemmet och skolan, med stöd av anhöriga och skolpersonal. Om du är intresserad kan du fråga yrkespersoner vad som tränas och hur det förs in i vardagen. Evidens: det beskriver en planerad randomiserad studie på tre platser med 244 barn i åldern 2-11 år, som jämför insatsen plus sedvanlig vård med enbart sedvanlig vård. Begränsningar: inga resultat redovisas, och även när de finns gäller de inte alla autistiska personer.

title: The Association Between Emotional and Behavioral Problems in Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder and Psychological Distress in Their Parents: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
authors: Yorke I, White P, Weston A, Rafla M, Charman T, Simonoff E
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
