This suggests that the pathogenesis of ASD may, at least in part, be attributed to synaptic dysfunction. In this article, we will review major genes and signaling pathways implicated in synaptic abnormalities underlying ASD, and discuss molecular, cellular and functional studies of ASD experimental models.

sheet.es: Esta revisión no ofrece nada que aplicar mañana por la mañana en casa; sirve para entender mejor la investigación. Resume lo que se sabe sobre genes que influyen en cómo se forman y funcionan las sinapsis, las conexiones entre neuronas, en el autismo. Es una revisión de estudios previos, incluidos modelos experimentales, no un estudio con personas concretas. Sugiere que la diferencia sináptica podría explicar en parte el autismo, pero no sirve para valorar a una persona ni para decidir apoyos. Las necesidades de cada persona autista son distintas; ante dudas médicas, consulte a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: This review gives nothing to apply at home tomorrow morning; it helps you understand the research. It summarises what is known about genes that affect how synapses, the connections between neurons, form and work in autism. It is a review of earlier studies, including experimental models, not a study of particular people. It suggests synaptic differences may partly explain autism, but it cannot be used to assess one person or to choose supports. Every autistic person's needs differ; for medical questions, talk to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Den här översikten ger inget att tillämpa hemma i morgon bitti; den hjälper dig att förstå forskningen. Den sammanfattar vad som är känt om gener som påverkar hur synapser, kopplingarna mellan nervceller, bildas och fungerar vid autism. Det är en översikt av tidigare studier, bland annat experimentella modeller, inte en studie av enskilda personer. Den antyder att skillnader i synapser delvis kan förklara autism, men kan inte användas för att bedöma en person eller välja stöd. Varje autistisk person har olika behov; vid medicinska frågor, kontakta en kliniker.

title: Investigating alexithymia in autism: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Kinnaird E, Stewart C, Tchanturia K
journal: European psychiatry : the journal of the Association of European Psychiatrists
abstract: Background New research suggests that, rather than representing a core feature of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), emotional processing difficulties reflect co-occurring alexithymia. Autistic individuals with alexithymia could therefore represent a specific subgroup of autism who may benefit from tailored interventions. The aim of this systematic review and meta-analysis was to explore the nature and prevalence of alexithymia in autism using the Toronto Alexithymia Scale (TAS). Methods Online scientific databases were searched systematically for studies on ASD popu lations using the TAS. Meta-analyses were performed to evaluate differences in scores between the ASD and neurotypical groups, and to determine the prevalence of alexithymia in these populations. Results 15 articles comparing autistic and neurotypical (NT) groups were identified. Autistic people scored significantly higher on all scores compared to the NT group. There was also a higher prevalence of alexithymia in the ASD group (49.93% compared to 4.89%), with a significantly increased risk of alexithymia in autistic participants. Conclusions This review highlights that alexithymia is common, rather than universal, in ASD, supporting a growing body of evidence that co-occurring autism and alexithymia represents a specific subgroup in the ASD population that may have specific clinical needs. More research is needed to understand the nature and implications of co-occurring ASD and alexithymia.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista tiene dificultad para identificar o describir lo que siente, conviene probar apoyos concretos: ofrecer opciones visuales o escritas, preguntar por sensaciones del cuerpo y dar tiempo, sin presionar. Es una posible pista, no un diagnóstico. Evidencia: metaanálisis de 15 artículos que compararon a personas autistas y no autistas con la Escala de Alexitimia de Toronto; las autistas puntuaron más alto, y la alexitimia fue frecuente (49.93% frente a 4.89%), pero no universal. Límites: es un promedio de grupos, no dice qué le ocurre a cada persona, y hacen falta más estudios sobre qué apoyos ayudan. Cualquier valoración clínica corresponde a profesionales.
sheet.en: If an autistic person finds it hard to identify or describe what they feel, try concrete supports: offer visual or written choices, ask about body sensations, and allow time without pressure. This is a possible clue, not a diagnosis. Evidence: a meta-analysis of 15 articles comparing autistic and non-autistic people on the Toronto Alexithymia Scale; autistic people scored higher, and alexithymia was common (49.93% compared to 4.89%) but not universal. Limits: these are group averages, so they cannot tell you what is true for one person, and more research is needed on which supports help. Any clinical assessment belongs with professionals.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person har svårt att känna igen eller beskriva vad hen känner kan du prova konkreta stöd: erbjud visuella eller skriftliga val, fråga om kroppsliga förnimmelser och ge tid utan press. Det är en möjlig ledtråd, inte en diagnos. Evidens: en metaanalys av 15 artiklar som jämförde autistiska och icke-autistiska personer med Toronto Alexithymia Scale; autistiska personer fick högre poäng, och alexitymi var vanligt (49.93% jämfört med 4.89%) men inte universellt. Begränsningar: det är gruppgenomsnitt som inte säger vad som gäller för en enskild person, och mer forskning behövs om vilka stöd som hjälper. Klinisk bedömning hör till yrkespersoner.

title: Overlaps and distinctions between attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder and autism spectrum disorder in young adulthood: Systematic review and guiding framework for EEG-imaging research.
authors: Lau-Zhu A, Fritz A, McLoughlin G
abstract: Attention deficit/hyperactivity disorders (ADHD) and autism spectrum disorders (ASD) frequently co-occur. However, we know little about the neural basis of the overlaps and distinctions between these disorders, particularly in young adulthood - a critical time window for brain plasticity across executive and socioemotional domains. Here, we systematically review 75 articles investigating ADHD and ASD in young adult samples (mean ages 16-26) using cognitive tasks, with neural activity concurrently measured via electroencephalography (EEG) - the most accessible neuroimaging technology. The majority of studies focused on event-related potentials (ERPs), with some beginning to capitalise on oscillatory approaches. Overlapping and specific profiles for ASD and ADHD were found mainly for four neurocognitive domains: attention processing, performance monitoring, face processing and sensory processing. No studies in this age group directly compared both disorders or considered dual diagnosis with both disorders. Moving forward, understanding of ADHD, ASD and their overlap in young adulthood would benefit from an increased focus on cross-disorder comparisons, using similar paradigms and in well-powered samples and longitudinal cohorts.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a un joven autista con rasgos de TDAH, o lo eres tú, es útil saber que ambos perfiles pueden solaparse y que cada persona es distinta; observar qué le ayuda en atención, cambios sensoriales y situaciones sociales sirve más que una etiqueta. La evidencia es una revisión sistemática de 75 artículos con adultos jóvenes (edad media 16-26) que midieron la actividad cerebral con EEG durante tareas. Encontró solapamientos y rasgos propios en atención, control del propio rendimiento, procesamiento de caras y procesamiento sensorial. Sus límites: ningún estudio comparó directamente ambos perfiles ni incluyó a personas con los dos diagnósticos, así que no ofrece pautas individuales.
sheet.en: If you support a young autistic person with ADHD traits, or you are one, it helps to know the two profiles can overlap and that every person differs; noticing what helps with attention, sensory changes and social situations is more useful than a label. The evidence is a systematic review of 75 articles with young adults (mean ages 16-26) whose brain activity was measured with EEG during tasks. It found overlaps and distinct features in attention, monitoring one's own performance, face processing and sensory processing. Limits: no study compared the two profiles directly or included people with both diagnoses, so it offers no individual guidance.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en ung autistisk person med ADHD-drag, eller själv är det, är det bra att veta att profilerna kan överlappa och att alla är olika; att lägga märke till vad som hjälper vid uppmärksamhet, sensoriska förändringar och sociala situationer är mer användbart än en etikett. Underlaget är en systematisk översikt av 75 artiklar med unga vuxna (medelålder 16-26) där hjärnaktivitet mättes med EEG under uppgifter. Den fann överlapp och särdrag i uppmärksamhet, prestationsövervakning, ansiktsbearbetning och sensorisk bearbetning. Begränsningar: ingen studie jämförde profilerna direkt eller inkluderade personer med båda diagnoserna, så den ger ingen individuell vägledning.

title: EEG Frequency Bands in Psychiatric Disorders: A Review of Resting State Studies.
authors: Newson JJ, Thiagarajan TC
abstract: A significant proportion of the electroencephalography (EEG) literature focuses on differences in historically pre-defined frequency bands in the power spectrum that are typically referred to as alpha, beta, gamma, theta and delta waves. Here, we review 184 EEG studies that report differences in frequency bands in the resting state condition (eyes open and closed) across a spectrum of psychiatric disorders including depression, attention deficit-hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), autism, addiction, bipolar disorder, anxiety, panic disorder, post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), obsessive compulsive disorder (OCD) and schizophrenia to determine patterns across disorders. Aggregating across all reported results we demonstrate that characteristic patterns of power change within specific frequency bands are not necessarily unique to any one disorder but show substantial overlap across disorders as well as variability within disorders. In particular, we show that the most dominant pattern of change, across several disorder types including ADHD, schizophrenia and OCD, is power increases across lower frequencies (delta and theta) and decreases across higher frequencies (alpha, beta and gamma). However, a considerable number of disorders, such as PTSD, addiction and autism show no dominant trend for spectral change in any direction. We report consistency and validation scores across the disorders and conditions showing that the dominant result across all disorders is typically only 2.2 times as likely to occur in the literature as alternate results, and typically with less than 250 study participants when summed across all studies reporting this result. Furthermore, the magnitudes of the results were infrequently reported and were typically small at between 20% and 30% and correlated weakly with symptom severity scores. Finally, we discuss the many methodological challenges and limitations relating to such frequency band analysis across the literature. These results caution any interpretation of results from studies that consider only one disorder in isolation, and for the overall potential of this approach for delivering valuable insights in the field of mental health.

sheet.es: Por ahora, los patrones de ondas cerebrales en reposo no sirven para entender ni valorar a una persona autista concreta. Si alguien le ofrece una prueba de EEG como respuesta clara, pregunte qué aporta realmente. Es una revisión de 184 estudios de EEG en reposo en varios trastornos psiquiátricos, entre ellos el autismo. Los patrones se solapaban mucho entre condiciones y variaban dentro de cada una; en el autismo no apareció una tendencia dominante. Límites: no se centra en el autismo, los métodos de los estudios difieren y los resultados no valen como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: For now, resting brain-wave patterns cannot help us understand or assess an individual autistic person. If someone offers an EEG as a clear answer, ask what it would actually add. This is a review of 184 resting-state EEG studies across several psychiatric conditions, including autism. Patterns overlapped a lot between conditions and varied within each one; for autism, no dominant trend appeared. Limits: the review is not focused on autism, the studies used differing methods, and the findings are not a rule for any one person.
sheet.sv: Just nu kan vilovågsmönster i hjärnan inte hjälpa oss att förstå eller bedöma en enskild autistisk person. Om någon erbjuder EEG som ett tydligt svar, fråga vad det faktiskt tillför. Detta är en översikt av 184 EEG-studier i vila över flera psykiatriska tillstånd, bland dem autism. Mönstren överlappade mycket mellan tillstånden och varierade inom varje tillstånd; för autism syntes ingen dominerande trend. Begränsningar: översikten fokuserar inte på autism, studiernas metoder skiljer sig och resultaten gäller inte som regel för någon enskild person.

title: Altered composition and function of intestinal microbiota in autism spectrum disorders: a systematic review.
authors: Liu F, Li J, Wu F, Zheng H, Peng Q, Zhou H
abstract: At present, the pathophysiology of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) remains unclear. Increasing evidence suggested that gut microbiota plays a critical role in gastrointestinal symptoms and behavioral impairment in ASD patients. The primary aim of this systematic review is to investigate potential evidence for the characteristic dysbiosis of gut microbiota in ASD patients compared with healthy controls (HCs). The MEDLINE, EMBASE, Web of Science and Scopus were systematically searched before March 2018. Human studies that compared the composition of gut microbiota in ASD patients and HCs using culture-independent techniques were included. Independent data extraction and quality assessment of studies were conducted according to PRISMA statement and Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Phylogenetic Investigation of Communities by Reconstruction of Unobserved States (PICRUSt) was used to infer biological functional changes of the shifted microbiota with the available data in four studies. Sixteen studies with a total sample size of 381 ASD patients and 283 HCs were included in this systematic review. The quality of the studies was evaluated as medium to high. The overall changing of gut bacterial community in terms of β-diversity was consistently observed in ASD patients compared with HCs. Furthermore, Bifidobacterium, Blautia, Dialister, Prevotella, Veillonella, and Turicibacter were consistently decreased, while Lactobacillus, Bacteroides, Desulfovibrio, and Clostridium were increased in patients with ASD relative to HCs in certain studies. This systematic review demonstrated significant alterations of gut microbiota in ASD patients compared with HCs, strengthen the evidence that dysbiosis of gut microbiota may correlate with behavioral abnormality in ASD patients. However, results of inconsistent changing also existed and further big-sampled well-designed studies are needed. Generally, as a potential mediator of risk factors, the gut microbiota could be a novel target for ASD patients in the future.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija autista tiene molestias digestivas como dolor, estreñimiento o diarrea, merece la pena anotarlas y comentarlas con su pediatra o médico de cabecera: son reales y tratables. Esta revisión sugiere que la flora intestinal de muchas personas autistas es distinta, pero no indica ninguna dieta, suplemento ni tratamiento concreto. Desconfía de productos que prometan «curar» el autismo por el intestino. Evidencia: revisión sistemática de 16 estudios con 381 personas autistas y 283 no autistas. Límites: muestras pequeñas, resultados a veces contradictorios y diseños que muestran asociación, no causa; cada persona es diferente.
sheet.en: If your autistic child has digestive discomfort such as pain, constipation or diarrhoea, it is worth noting it down and raising it with their doctor: these problems are real and treatable. This review suggests gut bacteria often differ in autistic people, but it does not point to any specific diet, supplement or treatment. Be wary of products promising to "fix" autism through the gut. Evidence: a systematic review of 16 studies including 381 autistic and 283 non-autistic people. Limits: small samples, some inconsistent findings, and designs that show association, not cause; every person is different.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn har magbesvär som smärta, förstoppning eller diarré är det värt att anteckna dem och ta upp dem med barnets läkare: besvären är verkliga och går att behandla. Översikten tyder på att tarmbakterierna ofta skiljer sig hos autistiska personer, men den pekar inte ut någon särskild kost, något kosttillskott eller någon behandling. Var försiktig med produkter som lovar att ”bota” autism via magen. Evidens: en systematisk översikt av 16 studier med 381 autistiska och 283 icke-autistiska personer. Begränsningar: små urval, delvis motstridiga resultat och studier som visar samband, inte orsak; varje person är olik.

title: Characterizing the Interplay Between Autism Spectrum Disorder and Comorbid Medical Conditions: An Integrative Review.
authors: Tye C, Runicles AK, Whitehouse AJO, Alvares GA
abstract: Co-occurring medical disorders and associated physiological abnormalities in individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) may provide insight into causal pathways or underlying biological mechanisms. Here, we review medical conditions that have been repeatedly highlighted as sharing the strongest associations with ASD-epilepsy, sleep, as well as gastrointestinal and immune functioning. We describe within each condition their prevalence, associations with behavior, and evidence for successful treatment. We additionally discuss research aiming to uncover potential aetiological mechanisms. We then consider the potential interaction between each group of conditions and ASD and, based on the available evidence, propose a model that integrates these medical comorbidities in relation to potential shared aetiological mechanisms. Future research should aim to systematically examine the interactions between these physiological systems, rather than considering these in isolation, using robust and sensitive biomarkers across an individual's development. A consideration of the overlap between medical conditions and ASD may aid in defining biological subtypes within ASD and in the development of specific targeted interventions.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista, vale la pena prestar atención a su sueño, su digestión, su salud inmunitaria y a posibles crisis epilépticas, y comentar cualquier preocupación con su profesional sanitario. A veces el malestar físico se expresa a través de cambios en la conducta. Esta es una revisión integradora que reunió estudios sobre epilepsia, sueño, y funcionamiento gastrointestinal e inmunitario en personas autistas. Sus límites: no es un estudio con participantes propios, propone un modelo que aún requiere más investigación y no explica a cada persona. Las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person, it is worth paying attention to their sleep, digestion, immune health and possible seizures, and raising any worries with their healthcare professional. Physical discomfort can sometimes show up as changes in behaviour. This was an integrative review that brought together studies on epilepsy, sleep, and gastrointestinal and immune functioning in autistic people. Its limits: it did not recruit its own participants, it proposes a model that still needs more research, and it cannot explain every individual. Medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person är det värt att uppmärksamma sömn, matsmältning, immunhälsa och möjliga epileptiska anfall, och ta upp oro med personens vårdpersonal. Fysiskt obehag kan ibland visa sig som förändringar i beteende. Detta var en integrativ översikt som sammanställde studier om epilepsi, sömn samt mag-tarm- och immunfunktion hos autistiska personer. Begränsningar: den hade inga egna deltagare, den föreslår en modell som behöver mer forskning och den kan inte förklara varje enskild person. Medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker.

title: Psychophysiological Arousal and Auditory Sensitivity in a Cross-Clinical Sample of Autistic and Non-autistic Anxious Adults.
authors: Top DN, Luke SG, Stephenson KG, South M
abstract: Many autistic people report overwhelming sensory experiences and also elevated levels of anxiety. Understanding how these experiences are linked to each other can contribute to improved support and intervention for reducing sensory overload and anxiety. This study included 95 young adult participants including autistic adults, non-autistic adults reporting to a psychotherapy clinic with high levels of anxiety, and neurotypical adults with no psychiatric concerns. We measured pupil size using including a baseline task with no auditory stimulus followed by two blocks of simple auditory habituation. In a subset of 80 participants we also measured self-report levels of sensory processing, anxious apprehension, and intolerance of uncertainty. The autism group showed atypical sensory processing on all four measured domains of the Adolescent and Adult Sensory Profile including sensory sensitivity, sensory seeking, sensory avoidance, and low registration subscales. Dimensional analyses across all participants showed significant positive correlations between sensory sensitivity, sensory seeking, and sensory avoidance domains with scores from the Intolerance of Uncertainty Scale-Short Form and Penn State Worry Questionnaire. The autism group showed significantly larger pupil size than other groups at baseline, before any auditory stimulation. There were no group differences in the rate of auditory habituation, nonetheless the overall, absolute larger pupil size remained in the autism group throughout the experiment. We suggest that this and other findings could indicate chronic hyperarousal in many autistic people. Treatment for anxiety in autism should be informed by knowledge of unique aspects of anxiety in autism and consider the role of sensory experience and everyday psychophysiological arousal.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista se siente ansiosa, conviene mirar también el entorno sensorial: ruidos, luces y falta de previsibilidad pueden sumar. Mañana, pruebe a reducir un ruido, avisar de los cambios con antelación y ofrecer una pausa tranquila. La evidencia es un estudio con 95 adultos jóvenes: autistas, no autistas con mucha ansiedad y sin preocupaciones psiquiátricas. Midieron el tamaño de la pupila ante sonidos y cuestionarios. El grupo autista tuvo pupilas más grandes desde el inicio, y más sensibilidad sensorial se relacionó con más intolerancia a la incertidumbre y preocupación. Límites: es un grupo pequeño de adultos, muestra una asociación y no explica a cada persona ni prueba causas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person seems anxious, it can help to look at the sensory environment too: noise, lights and unpredictability may add up. Tomorrow, try lowering one sound, giving notice of changes and offering a quiet break. The evidence is a study of 95 young adults: autistic adults, non-autistic adults with high anxiety, and adults with no psychiatric concerns. Researchers measured pupil size during sounds, plus questionnaires. The autistic group had larger pupils from the start, and more sensory sensitivity went with more intolerance of uncertainty and worry. Limits: it is a small adult sample, shows an association, and does not explain every person or prove causes.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person verkar orolig kan det hjälpa att också se över sinnesmiljön: ljud, ljus och oförutsägbarhet kan läggas ihop. I morgon kan du prova att sänka ett ljud, säga till i förväg om förändringar och erbjuda en lugn paus. Underlaget är en studie med 95 unga vuxna: autistiska vuxna, icke-autistiska vuxna med mycket ångest och vuxna utan psykiatriska besvär. Forskarna mätte pupillstorlek vid ljud samt frågeformulär. Den autistiska gruppen hade större pupiller från start, och mer sensorisk känslighet hängde ihop med mer svårighet att tåla osäkerhet och oro. Begränsningar: litet urval av vuxna, visar ett samband och förklarar inte varje person eller bevisar orsaker.

title: Sensory integration therapy versus usual care for sensory processing difficulties in autism spectrum disorder in children: study protocol for a pragmatic randomised controlled trial.
authors: Randell E, McNamara R, Delport S, Busse M, Hastings RP, Gillespie D, Williams-Thomas R, Brookes-Howell L, Romeo R, Boadu J, Ahuja AS, McKigney AM, Knapp M, Smith K, Thornton J, Warren G
abstract: Background Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a common lifelong condition affecting 1 in 100 people. ASD affects how a person relates to others and the world around them. Difficulty responding to sensory information (noise, touch, movement, taste, sight) is common, and might include feeling overwhelmed or distressed by loud or constant low-level noise (e.g. in the classroom). Affected children may also show little or no response to these sensory cues. These 'sensory processing difficulties' are associated with behaviour and socialisation problems, and affect education, relationships, and participation in daily life. Sensory integration therapy (SIT) is a face-to-face therapy or treatment provided by trained occupational therapists who use play-based sensory-motor activities and the just-right challenge to influence the way the child responds to sensation, reducing distress, and improving motor skills, adaptive responses, concentration, and interaction with others. With limited research into SIT, this protocol describes in detail how the intervention will be defined and evaluated. Methods This is a two-arm pragmatic individually 1:1 randomised controlled trial with an internal pilot of SIT versus usual care for primary school aged children (aged 4 to 11 years) with ASD and sensory processing difficulties; 216 children will be recruited from multiple sources. Therapy will be delivered in clinics meeting full fidelity criteria for manualised SIT over 26 weeks (face-to-face sessions: two per week for 10 weeks, two per month for 2 months; telephone call: one per month for 2 months). Follow-up assessments will be completed at 6 and 12 months post-randomisation. Prior to recruitment, therapists will be invited to participate in focus groups/interviews to explore what is delivered as usual care in trial regions; carers will be invited to complete an online survey to map out their experience of services. Following recruitment, carers will be given diaries to record their contact with services. Following intervention, carer and therapist interviews will be completed. Discussion Results of this trial will provide high-quality evidence on the clinical and cost effectiveness of SIT aimed at improving behavioural, functional, social, educational, and well-being outcomes for children and well-being outcomes for carers and families. Trial registration ISRCTN14716440 . Registered on 8 November 2016.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija autista tiene dificultades con el ruido, el tacto o el movimiento, puede anotar qué situaciones le abruman y comentarlo con un terapeuta ocupacional. Este estudio es el protocolo de un ensayo aleatorizado que comparará la terapia de integración sensorial, basada en el juego, con la atención habitual en 216 niños y niñas de 4 a 11 años. Aún no hay resultados: solo describe cómo se evaluará. Por tanto, no demuestra que la terapia funcione ni sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If your autistic child struggles with noise, touch or movement, you can note which situations overwhelm them and talk it over with an occupational therapist. This study is the protocol of a randomised trial that will compare play-based sensory integration therapy with usual care in 216 children aged 4 to 11. There are no results yet: it only describes how the therapy will be evaluated. So it does not show that the therapy works, and it is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn har svårt med ljud, beröring eller rörelse kan du anteckna vilka situationer som blir övermäktiga och prata om det med en arbetsterapeut. Studien är ett protokoll för en randomiserad studie som ska jämföra lekbaserad sensorisk integrationsterapi med vanlig vård hos 216 barn i åldern 4 till 11 år. Några resultat finns ännu inte: den beskriver bara hur terapin ska utvärderas. Den visar alltså inte att terapin fungerar och gäller inte som regel för alla.

title: Genetics and epigenetics of autism spectrum disorder-current evidence in the field.
authors: Wiśniowiecka-Kowalnik B, Nowakowska BA
abstract: Autism spectrum disorders (ASD) is a heterogenous group of neurodevelopmental disorders characterized by problems in social interaction and communication as well as the presence of repetitive and stereotyped behavior. It is estimated that the prevalence of ASD is 1-2% in the general population with the average male to female ratio 4-5:1. Although the causes of ASD remain largely unknown, the studies have shown that both genetic and environmental factors play an important role in the etiology of these disorders. Array comparative genomic hybridization and whole exome/genome sequencing studies identified common and rare copy number or single nucleotide variants in genes encoding proteins involved in brain development, which play an important role in neuron and synapse formation and function. The genetic etiology is recognized in ~ 25-35% of patients with ASD. In this article, we review the current state of knowledge about the genetic etiology of ASD and also propose a diagnostic algorithm for patients.

sheet.es: Si te preguntas por qué una persona es autista, esta revisión sugiere que la genética influye, pero no explica todos los casos. Si os interesa un estudio genético, hablad con un profesional sanitario o de genética. Es una revisión de la literatura científica sobre genética del autismo, no un estudio con participantes propios. Señala que la causa sigue siendo en gran parte desconocida y que influyen factores genéticos y ambientales. Indica que se reconoce un origen genético en ~ 25-35% de los casos. Sus límites: es un resumen general, no dice qué es mejor para una persona concreta y no debe leerse como una regla para todas. Ser autista no es algo que haya que corregir.
sheet.en: If you wonder why someone is autistic, this review suggests genetics plays a part but does not explain every case. If you are curious about genetic testing, talk with a health professional or a genetics clinician. This is a review of the scientific literature on the genetics of autism, not a study with its own participants. It notes that the causes remain largely unknown and that genetic and environmental factors both matter. It reports a genetic cause is recognised in ~ 25-35% of cases. Its limits: it is a general overview, it cannot say what is best for one particular person, and it should not be read as a rule for everyone. Being autistic is not something that needs fixing.
sheet.sv: Om du undrar varför någon är autistisk tyder den här översikten på att genetik spelar roll men inte förklarar alla fall. Om ni är nyfikna på genetisk utredning, prata med vårdpersonal eller en genetiker. Det är en översikt av forskningslitteratur om autismens genetik, inte en studie med egna deltagare. Den konstaterar att orsakerna till stor del är okända och att både genetiska faktorer och miljöfaktorer spelar roll. Den anger att en genetisk orsak identifieras i ~ 25-35% av fallen. Begränsningar: det är en allmän sammanfattning, den kan inte säga vad som är bäst för en enskild person och ska inte läsas som en regel för alla. Att vara autistisk är inget som behöver fixas.

title: Telehealth as a Model for Providing Behaviour Analytic Interventions to Individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review.
authors: Ferguson J, Ferguson J, Craig EA, Dounavi K
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Interventions based on applied behaviour analysis are considered evidence based practice for autism spectrum disorders. Due to the shortage of highly qualified professionals required for their delivery, innovative models should be explored, such as telehealth. Telehealth utilises technology for remote training and supervision. The purpose of our study was to systematically review the literature researching telehealth and ABA. We analysed intervention characteristics, outcomes and research quality in 28 studies and identified gaps. Intervention characteristics were: (1) research design (2) participants (3) technology (4) dependent variables (5) aims. Outcomes were favourable with all studies reporting improvements in at least one variable. Quality ratings were significantly low. Implications for future research and practice are discussed in light of identified methodological downfalls.

sheet.es: Si el acceso a profesionales cualificados de análisis conductual aplicado (ABA) es difícil donde vive, puede preguntar si ofrecen formación y supervisión a distancia por telesalud. Es una opción que conviene valorar con la persona autista, atendiendo a sus preferencias y a su comodidad. Esta revisión sistemática analizó 28 estudios y en todos se informó de mejoras en al menos una variable. Sin embargo, la calidad de la investigación se valoró como significativamente baja, así que los resultados deben tomarse con prudencia. No demuestra que funcione para cada persona ni que sea mejor que la atención presencial.
sheet.en: If it is hard to reach qualified applied behaviour analysis (ABA) professionals where you live, you can ask whether they offer remote training and supervision through telehealth. It is an option to weigh together with the autistic person, considering their preferences and comfort. This systematic review analysed 28 studies, and all of them reported improvements in at least one variable. However, the quality of the research was rated as significantly low, so the results should be treated with caution. It does not show that telehealth works for every person or that it is better than in-person support.
sheet.sv: Om det är svårt att nå kvalificerade yrkespersoner inom tillämpad beteendeanalys (ABA) där ni bor, kan ni fråga om de erbjuder utbildning och handledning på distans via telehälsa. Det är ett alternativ att väga in tillsammans med den autistiska personen, med hänsyn till hens önskemål och trygghet. Denna systematiska översikt analyserade 28 studier, och alla rapporterade förbättringar i minst en variabel. Forskningens kvalitet bedömdes dock som signifikant låg, så resultaten bör tolkas med försiktighet. Den visar inte att telehälsa fungerar för alla eller är bättre än stöd på plats.

title: Scoping Review: Physical Activity and Social Functioning in Young People With Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Reinders NJ, Branco A, Wright K, Fletcher PC, Bryden PJ
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) affects ~1 in 59 people in North America and diagnoses continue to rise (Center for Disease Control and Prevention, 2018). Unfortunately, the exact cause of ASD is unknown and therapy remains the primary means of intervention. People with ASD experience social and behavioral deficits associated with the disorder, which affect all aspects of life such as academics, relationships, and physical activity. Research has shown a relationship between physical activity and social skills in typically developing individuals; however, this relationship is less understood in people with ASD. The purpose of this scoping review was to uncover what is known about ASD, physical activity, and social functioning. The authors searched four databases and included 40 primary research articles in the review, most of which demonstrated a relationship between physical activity and social functioning for people with ASD. The relationship appears bidirectional: social functioning influences physical activity (to a lesser extent) and physical activity influences social functioning (to a greater extent). Regrettably, there were many limitations in these articles, such as small sample sizes and the under-representation of females and adults. Therefore, the review highlights several directions for future research.

sheet.es: Si le interesa, ofrezca a su hijo o hija opciones de actividad física que le gusten, y observe si disfruta de hacerlas con otras personas; puede ser una vía agradable de convivencia, sin presión. La evidencia es una revisión de alcance que incluyó 40 artículos de investigación sobre jóvenes autistas; la mayoría halló una relación entre actividad física y funcionamiento social, sobre todo de la actividad hacia lo social. Sus límites: muchos estudios eran pequeños y había poca representación de mujeres y adultos, y una relación no prueba que una cosa cause la otra. No sirve como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If it suits your child, offer physical activities they enjoy and notice whether they like doing them alongside others; it can be a pleasant way to spend time together, without pressure. The evidence is a scoping review of 40 research articles on autistic young people; most found a relationship between physical activity and social functioning, more strongly from activity toward social functioning. Its limits: many studies were small, females and adults were under-represented, and a relationship does not prove that one thing causes the other. It is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om det passar ditt barn kan du erbjuda fysisk aktivitet som hen tycker om och se om hen gillar att göra den tillsammans med andra; det kan vara ett trevligt sätt att umgås, utan press. Underlaget är en kartläggande översikt av 40 forskningsartiklar om autistiska unga; de flesta fann ett samband mellan fysisk aktivitet och social funktion, starkare från aktivitet mot socialt samspel. Begränsningar: många studier var små, kvinnor och vuxna var underrepresenterade, och ett samband visar inte att det ena orsakar det andra. Det är ingen regel för alla.

title: Stigma of living as an autism carer: a brief psycho-social support intervention (SOLACE). Study protocol for a randomised controlled feasibility study.
authors: Lodder A, Papadopoulos C, Randhawa G
abstract: Background Stigma is prominent in the lives of autistic individuals and their families and contributes significantly to the challenges faced by families raising an autistic child. Parents and carers can feel blamed for their child's behaviour, feel socially excluded and isolated and suffer from low self-esteem and poor psychological well-being. This increases the risk of experiencing self-stigma which further exacerbates these and other negative consequences. Therefore, there is a need for interventions that help parents/family carers cope with autism-related stigma as well as prevent the internalisation of stigma. Objectives The primary objective of this study is to assess the feasibility and acceptability of a stigma support intervention for parents and carers of autistic children titled 'Stigma of Living as an Autism Carer (SOLACE)'. The secondary objective is to explore the preliminary impact of the intervention on the mental health of the parents and carers. Methods A pilot randomised controlled trial feasibility study will be implemented. A group receiving the SOLACE stigma support intervention ( n = 12) will be compared against a control group not receiving any additional intervention ( n = 12). Family carers of autistic children up to the age of 10, who have been recently diagnosed or are currently undergoing diagnosis, will be recruited for the study. Participants will be randomly allocated to the intervention or control group and will take part in eight weekly group-based sessions designed to improve the well-being of the parents primarily through increasing their resilience to stigma. Feasibility will be determined by recruitment and retention rates and a qualitative focus group evaluating the acceptability of the intervention and outcome measures. The primary outcome of interest is psychological well-being, and depending on the normality of distribution, independent samples T tests will be used to compare the outcome scores between the two groups and dependent samples T tests for differences within the group. Other outcomes of interest are stigma, self-stigma, self-esteem, self-blame, social isolation, self-compassion and perceived responsibility and control. Discussion Results from the feasibility randomised controlled trial will be used to refine the study protocol and inform the design of an intervention for future use in a larger, powered trial. SOLACE could potentially improve the psychological well-being of parents/family carers of autistic children through increased resistance to stigma. Trial registration ISRCTN Registry number ISRCTN61093625 (October 13, 2017).

sheet.es: Si cuidas a un niño autista y sientes culpa, juicio ajeno o aislamiento, no eres la única persona: el estigma es una experiencia descrita en muchas familias. Hablar con otras familias y buscar apoyo para tu bienestar puede ser un paso útil. Este documento es un protocolo de un ensayo piloto aleatorizado: describe un plan, no ofrece resultados. Prevé 12 personas en el grupo de apoyo y 12 en el grupo de comparación, con ocho sesiones semanales para familias de niños autistas de hasta 10 años. Su límite: aún no sabemos si el programa funciona, solo si es viable, y no sirve como regla para todas las familias.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic child and feel blamed, judged or isolated, you are not alone: stigma is described as common in families like yours. Talking with other families and seeking support for your own well-being may be a useful step. This paper is a protocol for a randomised pilot trial: it describes a plan and reports no results. It plans 12 people in a support group and 12 in a comparison group, with eight weekly sessions for carers of autistic children up to the age of 10. Its limit: we do not yet know whether the programme works, only whether it is feasible, and it is not a rule for every family.
sheet.sv: Om du tar hand om ett autistiskt barn och känner dig skuldbelagd, dömd eller isolerad är du inte ensam: stigma beskrivs som vanligt i familjer som din. Att prata med andra familjer och söka stöd för ditt eget välmående kan vara ett användbart steg. Texten är ett protokoll för en randomiserad pilotstudie: den beskriver en plan och redovisar inga resultat. Planen är 12 personer i en stödgrupp och 12 i en jämförelsegrupp, med åtta veckovisa träffar för föräldrar till autistiska barn upp till 10 år. Begränsning: vi vet ännu inte om programmet fungerar, bara om det är genomförbart, och det gäller inte som regel för alla familjer.

title: Development and Validation of the Camouflaging Autistic Traits Questionnaire (CAT-Q).
authors: Hull L, Mandy W, Lai MC, Baron-Cohen S, Allison C, Smith P, Petrides KV
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: There currently exist no self-report measures of social camouflaging behaviours (strategies used to compensate for or mask autistic characteristics during social interactions). The Camouflaging Autistic Traits Questionnaire (CAT-Q) was developed from autistic adults' experiences of camouflaging, and was administered online to 354 autistic and 478 non-autistic adults. Exploratory factor analysis suggested three factors, comprising of 25 items in total. Good model fit was demonstrated through confirmatory factor analysis, with measurement invariance analyses demonstrating equivalent factor structures across gender and diagnostic group. Internal consistency (α = 0.94) and preliminary test-retest reliability (r = 0.77) were acceptable. Convergent validity was demonstrated through comparison with measures of autistic traits, wellbeing, anxiety, and depression. The present study provides robust psychometric support for the CAT-Q.

sheet.es: Si tu familiar autista parece «estar bien» en público pero llega agotado a casa, puede estar camuflando: ocultando o compensando rasgos autistas para encajar. Vale la pena hablarlo con calma, ofrecer tiempo de recuperación sin exigencias y espacios donde no tenga que fingir. El CAT-Q es un cuestionario de 25 preguntas que puede ayudar a poner palabras a esa experiencia. Evidencia: estudio en línea con 354 adultos autistas y 478 no autistas; el cuestionario mostró buena fiabilidad y se relacionó con ansiedad, depresión y bienestar. Límites: solo adultos que respondieron en internet sobre sí mismos; no sirve para diagnosticar ni describe a todas las personas.
sheet.en: If your autistic family member seems fine in public but comes home exhausted, they may be camouflaging: hiding or compensating for autistic traits to fit in. It can help to talk about it gently, offer recovery time without demands, and create spaces where they don't have to perform. The CAT-Q, a 25-item questionnaire, can help put words to this experience. Evidence: an online study with 354 autistic and 478 non-autistic adults; the questionnaire showed good reliability and was linked to anxiety, depression and wellbeing. Limits: only adults self-reporting online; it is not a diagnostic tool and does not describe every person.
sheet.sv: Om din autistiska närstående verkar må bra bland andra men kommer hem helt slut kan hen kamouflera: dölja eller kompensera autistiska drag för att passa in. Det kan hjälpa att prata lugnt om det, erbjuda återhämtning utan krav och skapa platser där hen inte behöver spela en roll. CAT-Q, ett frågeformulär med 25 frågor, kan hjälpa till att sätta ord på upplevelsen. Evidens: en webbstudie med 354 autistiska och 478 icke-autistiska vuxna; formuläret visade god tillförlitlighet och hängde ihop med ångest, depression och välmående. Begränsningar: bara vuxna som själva svarade på nätet; det är inget diagnosverktyg och beskriver inte alla.

title: Selection bias on intellectual ability in autism research: a cross-sectional review and meta-analysis.
authors: Russell G, Mandy W, Elliott D, White R, Pittwood T, Ford T
abstract: Background Current global estimates suggest the proportion of the population with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) who have intellectual disability (ID) is approximately 50%. Our objective was to ascertain the existence of selection bias due to under-inclusion of populations with ID across all fields of autism research. A sub-goal was to evaluate inconsistencies in reporting of findings. Methods This review covers all original research published in 2016 in autism-specific journals with an impact factor greater than 3. Across 301 included studies, 100,245 participants had ASD. A random effects meta-analysis was used to estimate the proportion of participants without ID. Selection bias was defined as where more than 75% of participants did not have ID. Results Meta-analysis estimated 94% of all participants identified as being on the autism spectrum in the studies reviewed did not have ID (95% CI 0.91-0.97). Eight out of ten studies demonstrated selection bias against participants with ID. The reporting of participant characteristics was generally poor: information about participants' intellectual ability was absent in 38% of studies ( n = 114). Where there was selection bias on ID, only 31% of studies mentioned lack of generalisability as a limitation. Conclusions We found selection bias against ID throughout all fields of autism research. We recommend transparent reporting about ID and strategies for inclusion for this much marginalised group.

sheet.es: Al leer estudios sobre autismo, conviene fijarse en si incluyeron a personas autistas con discapacidad intelectual, porque sus resultados quizá no describan a todas las personas. Este metaanálisis revisó la investigación sobre autismo publicada en 2016 en revistas especializadas: 301 estudios, con 100,245 participantes autistas. Estimó que el 94% no tenía discapacidad intelectual, y ocho de cada diez estudios mostraron sesgo de selección en su contra. Además, 38% de los estudios no informaba sobre la capacidad intelectual. Límites: solo cubre un año y revistas con alto factor de impacto, y no dice nada sobre una persona concreta. Las personas autistas con discapacidad intelectual están poco representadas.
sheet.en: When reading autism studies, check whether they included autistic people with intellectual disability, because the results may not describe everyone. This meta-analysis reviewed autism research published in 2016 in autism-specific journals: 301 studies, with 100,245 autistic participants. It estimated that 94% did not have intellectual disability, and eight out of ten studies showed selection bias against those who did. Also, 38% of studies gave no information on intellectual ability. Limits: it covers only one year and journals with a higher impact factor, and it says nothing about any one person. Autistic people with intellectual disability are underrepresented in research.
sheet.sv: När du läser studier om autism är det bra att kolla om autistiska personer med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning ingick, eftersom resultaten kanske inte gäller alla. Den här metaanalysen granskade autismforskning publicerad 2016 i autismspecifika tidskrifter: 301 studier med 100,245 autistiska deltagare. Den uppskattade att 94% inte hade intellektuell funktionsnedsättning, och åtta av tio studier visade urvalsskevhet mot dem som hade det. Dessutom saknade 38% av studierna information om intellektuell förmåga. Begränsningar: den omfattar bara ett år och tidskrifter med högre impact factor, och säger inget om en enskild person. Autistiska personer med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning är underrepresenterade i forskningen.

title: Resting-state abnormalities in Autism Spectrum Disorders: A meta-analysis.
authors: Lau WKW, Leung MK, Lau BWM
abstract: The gold standard for clinical assessment of Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASD) relies on assessing behavior via semi-structured play-based interviews and parent interviews. Although these methods show good sensitivity and specificity in diagnosing ASD cases, behavioral assessments alone may hinder the identification of asymptomatic at-risk group. Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) could be an appropriate approach to produce objective neural markers to supplement behavioral assessments due to its non-invasive and task-free nature. Previous neuroimaging studies reported inconsistent resting-state abnormalities in ASD, which may be explained by small sample sizes and phenotypic heterogeneity in ASD subjects, and/or the use of different analytical methods across studies. The current study aims to investigate the local resting-state abnormalities of ASD regardless of subject age, IQ, gender, disease severity and methodological differences, using activation likelihood estimation (ALE). MEDLINE/PubMed databases were searched for whole-brain rs-fMRI studies on ASD published until Feb 2018. Eight experiments involving 424 subjects were included in the ALE meta-analysis. We demonstrate two ASD-related resting-state findings: local underconnectivity in the dorsal posterior cingulate cortex (PCC) and in the right medial paracentral lobule. This study contributes to uncovering a consistent pattern of resting-state local abnormalities that may serve as potential neurobiological markers for ASD.

sheet.es: Para mañana no cambia nada en la práctica: el diagnóstico y el apoyo siguen basándose en conocer a la persona, sus necesidades y sus fortalezas, no en escáneres cerebrales. Este estudio busca diferencias en la actividad cerebral en reposo que algún día podrían complementar la evaluación, pero hoy no es una prueba disponible ni dice nada sobre cómo apoyar a tu familiar. Es un metaanálisis de ocho estudios de resonancia magnética con 424 participantes, que encontró menor conectividad local en dos zonas del cerebro. Sus límites: pocos estudios, muestras pequeñas y variadas, y diferencias de grupo que no describen a cada persona autista.
sheet.en: Nothing changes in practice tomorrow: diagnosis and support still rest on knowing the person, their needs and strengths, not on brain scans. This study looks for differences in resting brain activity that might one day add to assessment, but it is not an available test today and says nothing about how to support your family member. It is a meta-analysis of eight brain-imaging (MRI) studies with 424 participants, finding lower local connectivity in two brain areas. Its limits: few studies, small and varied samples, and group-level differences that do not describe every autistic person.
sheet.sv: I praktiken ändras ingenting i morgon: utredning och stöd bygger fortfarande på att känna personen, hennes behov och styrkor, inte på hjärnröntgen. Studien letar efter skillnader i hjärnans viloaktivitet som kanske en dag kan komplettera bedömningar, men det är inget test som finns i dag och säger inget om hur du stöttar din närstående. Det är en metaanalys av åtta hjärnavbildningsstudier (MR) med 424 deltagare, som fann lägre lokal konnektivitet i två hjärnområden. Begränsningar: få studier, små och varierade urval, och skillnader på gruppnivå som inte beskriver varje autistisk person.

title: Risk and Protective Environmental Factors Associated with Autism Spectrum Disorder: Evidence-Based Principles and Recommendations.
authors: Emberti Gialloreti L, Mazzone L, Benvenuto A, Fasano A, Alcon AG, Kraneveld A, Moavero R, Raz R, Riccio MP, Siracusano M, Zachor DA, Marini M, Curatolo P
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a complex condition with early childhood onset, characterized by a set of common behavioral features. The etiology of ASD is not yet fully understood; however, it reflects the interaction between genetics and environment. While genetics is now a well-established risk factor, several data support a contribution of the environment as well. This paper summarizes the conclusions of a consensus conference focused on the potential pathogenetic role of environmental factors and on their interactions with genetics. Several environmental factors have been discussed in terms of ASD risk, namely advanced parental age, assisted reproductive technologies, nutritional factors, maternal infections and diseases, environmental chemicals and toxicants, and medications, as well as some other conditions. The analysis focused on their specific impact on three biologically relevant time windows for brain development: the periconception, prenatal, and early postnatal periods. Possible protective factors that might prevent or modify an ASD trajectory have been explored as well. Recommendations for clinicians to reduce ASD risk or its severity have been proposed. Developments in molecular biology and big data approaches, which are able to assess a large number of coexisting factors, are offering new opportunities to disentangle the gene⁻environment interplay that can lead to the development of ASD.

sheet.es: Si te preocupa qué causó el autismo de tu hijo o hija, este texto no apunta a ninguna culpa: la causa no se conoce del todo y combina genética y entorno. Es una revisión que resume las conclusiones de una conferencia de consenso sobre factores ambientales (edad de los progenitores, nutrición, infecciones maternas, sustancias químicas, medicamentos) en el periodo periconcepcional, prenatal y posnatal temprano. Como limitación, no es un estudio con participantes y no demuestra que un factor concreto cause autismo en una persona. Las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If you wonder what led to your child's autism, this paper points to no one to blame: the cause is not fully understood and involves genetics interacting with the environment. It is a review summarising the conclusions of a consensus conference on environmental factors (parental age, nutrition, maternal infections, chemicals, medications) across the periconception, prenatal and early postnatal periods. A limit: it is not a study with participants and does not show that any one factor caused autism in a particular person. Medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om du funderar på vad som låg bakom ditt barns autism pekar den här artikeln inte ut någon att skylla på: orsaken är inte helt känd och handlar om samspel mellan gener och miljö. Det är en översikt som sammanfattar slutsatser från en konsensuskonferens om miljöfaktorer (föräldrars ålder, kost, infektioner hos modern, kemikalier, läkemedel) under perioden kring befruktning, graviditeten och spädbarnstiden. En begränsning är att det inte är en studie med deltagare och att den inte visar att en enskild faktor orsakat autism hos en viss person. Medicinska beslut hör till en läkare.

title: Social skills group training in children with autism spectrum disorder: a randomized controlled trial.
authors: Dekker V, Nauta MH, Timmerman ME, Mulder EJ, van der Veen-Mulders L, van den Hoofdakker BJ, van Warners S, Vet LJJ, Hoekstra PJ, de Bildt A
abstract: In 122 high-functioning children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD; 9-13 years; 19 girls), we investigated the effectiveness of a 15-session social skills group training (SST) with and without parent and teacher involvement (PTI) in a randomized controlled trial with three conditions: SST (n = 47), SST-PTI (n = 51), and care-as-usual (CAU, n = 24). Hierarchical linear modeling was used for immediate and 6-month follow-up analyses. Measures were administered before randomization (blind), post-treatment and at follow-up (not blind). Trial registration: Dutch Trial Register; http://www.trialregister.nl ; NTR2405. At post-treatment, children in both SSTs had improved significantly more than CAU on the primary outcome, Vineland Socialization (SST: Cohen's d = 0.39; 95% CI - 2.23 to 3.11 and SST-PTI: d = 0.43; 95% CI - 2.19 to 3.15) and on the secondary outcome parent-SSRS "Cooperation" (SST: d = 0.43; 95% CI - 0.23 to 1.15 and SST-PTI: d = 0.45; 95% CI - 0.21 to 1.17), with no difference between post-treatment and follow-up. Additionally, children in SST-PTI improved significantly more on the teacher-SSRS than in CAU ["Cooperation" d =0.42 (95% CI - 0.33 to 1.13); "Assertion" d =0.34 (95% CI - 0.39 to 1.11); "Self-Control" d =0.61 (95% CI - 0.08 to 1.34)] and in SST ["Cooperation" d =0.34 (95% CI - 0.37 to 1.05); "Self-Control" d =0.59 (95% CI - 0.13 to 1.32)]. The current study corroborates earlier findings in smaller samples and wider age ranges, with small but statistically significant effects of SST for high-functioning pre-adolescent children with ASD. Parental and teacher involvement intensified treatment, yet did not yield an additional effect relative to SST for children only, as reported by parents. 6 months after training, no further improvement or decline was found.

sheet.es: Si te planteas un grupo de habilidades sociales para un niño autista de entre 9 y 13 años, puede ser una opción que explorar con su equipo, sobre todo si él quiere participar. Informar a la familia y a la escuela puede ayudar a que lo practicado se note en el aula. Evidencia: ensayo aleatorizado con 122 niños autistas, que comparó 15 sesiones de grupo, con o sin implicación de familia y docentes, frente a la atención habitual. Los efectos fueron pequeños y no se mantuvieron mejorando a los 6 meses. Límites: el estudio incluyó solo a niños descritos como de alto funcionamiento, y los resultados no valen igual para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you are considering a social skills group for an autistic child aged 9 to 13, it may be worth exploring with their team, especially if the child wants to take part. Keeping family and school informed may help what is practised show up in class. Evidence: a randomized trial with 122 autistic children compared 15 group sessions, with or without parent and teacher involvement, against usual care. Effects were small, and there was no further improvement at 6 months. Limits: the study included only children described as high-functioning, so results will not apply equally to every person.
sheet.sv: Om du funderar på en social färdighetsgrupp för ett autistiskt barn mellan 9 och 13 år kan det vara värt att utforska med barnets team, särskilt om barnet själv vill delta. Att hålla familj och skola informerade kan hjälpa det som övas att synas i klassrummet. Evidens: en randomiserad studie med 122 autistiska barn jämförde 15 gruppträffar, med eller utan medverkan av föräldrar och lärare, med vanlig vård. Effekterna var små och ingen ytterligare förbättring sågs efter 6 månader. Begränsningar: studien omfattade bara barn som beskrevs som högfungerande, så resultaten gäller inte lika för alla.

title: The contribution of environmental exposure to the etiology of autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Bölte S, Girdler S, Marschik PB
journal: Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition of heterogeneous etiology. While it is widely recognized that genetic and environmental factors and their interactions contribute to autism phenotypes, their precise causal mechanisms remain poorly understood. This article reviews our current understanding of environmental risk factors of ASD and their presumed adverse physiological mechanisms. It comprehensively maps the significance of parental age, teratogenic compounds, perinatal risks, medication, smoking and alcohol use, nutrition, vaccination, toxic exposures, as well as the role of extreme psychosocial factors. Further, we consider the role of potential protective factors such as folate and fatty acid intake. Evidence indicates an increased offspring vulnerability to ASD through advanced maternal and paternal age, valproate intake, toxic chemical exposure, maternal diabetes, enhanced steroidogenic activity, immune activation, and possibly altered zinc-copper cycles and treatment with selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors. Epidemiological studies demonstrate no evidence for vaccination posing an autism risk. It is concluded that future research needs to consider categorical autism, broader autism phenotypes, as well as autistic traits, and examine more homogenous autism variants by subgroup stratification. Our understanding of autism etiology could be advanced by research aimed at disentangling the causal and non-causal environmental effects, both founding and moderating, and gene-environment interplay using twin studies, longitudinal and experimental designs. The specificity of many environmental risks for ASD remains unknown and control of multiple confounders has been limited. Further understanding of the critical windows of neurodevelopmental vulnerability and investigating the fit of multiple hit and cumulative risk models are likely promising approaches in enhancing the understanding of role of environmental factors in the etiology of ASD.

sheet.es: Lo práctico: si te preocupa qué causó el autismo de tu hijo o hija, esta revisión indica que no hay una causa única ni una culpa que repartir. Las vacunas no aumentan la probabilidad de autismo. Si tienes dudas sobre medicación o embarazo, consúltalas con un profesional sanitario. La evidencia es una revisión de estudios sobre factores ambientales, como la edad de los progenitores o la exposición a sustancias tóxicas. Sus límites: los mecanismos causales siguen poco claros, se controlaron pocos factores de confusión y no explica a ninguna persona concreta.
sheet.en: Practical takeaway: if you wonder what caused your child's autism, this review suggests there is no single cause and no one to blame. Vaccines were not found to raise the chance of autism. For questions about medication or pregnancy, talk with a health professional. The evidence is a review of studies on environmental factors, such as parental age or toxic exposures. Its limits: the causal mechanisms remain poorly understood, control of other influences was limited, and it cannot explain any one person's autism.
sheet.sv: Praktiskt: om du funderar på vad som orsakade ditt barns autism tyder den här översikten på att det inte finns en enda orsak och ingen att skuldbelägga. Vaccin visade sig inte öka sannolikheten för autism. Frågor om medicin eller graviditet tas upp med vårdpersonal. Underlaget är en översikt av studier om miljöfaktorer, till exempel föräldrars ålder eller giftiga ämnen. Begränsningar: de orsakande mekanismerna är fortfarande dåligt förstådda, kontrollen av andra påverkansfaktorer var begränsad, och översikten kan inte förklara en enskild persons autism.

title: The Role of Eye Gaze During Natural Social Interactions in Typical and Autistic People.
authors: Cañigueral R, Hamilton AFC
abstract: Social interactions involve complex exchanges of a variety of social signals, such as gaze, facial expressions, speech and gestures. Focusing on the dual function of eye gaze, this review explores how the presence of an audience, communicative purpose and temporal dynamics of gaze allow interacting partners to achieve successful communication. First, we focus on how being watched modulates social cognition and behavior. We then show that the study of interpersonal gaze processing, particularly gaze temporal dynamics, can provide valuable understanding of social behavior in real interactions. We propose that the Interpersonal Gaze Processing model, which combines both sensing and signaling functions of eye gaze, provides a framework to make sense of gaze patterns in live interactions. Finally, we discuss how autistic individuals process the belief in being watched and interpersonal dynamics of gaze, and suggest that systematic manipulation of factors modulating gaze signaling can reveal which aspects of social eye gaze are challenging in autism.

sheet.es: Mañana, si comparte un rato con una persona autista, no hace falta exigirle que mantenga la mirada. Cuente con que mirar y ser mirado puede sentirse distinto para cada persona, y ofrezca otras formas de conectar, como hablar mientras se hace algo juntos. La evidencia es una revisión de estudios sobre la mirada en interacciones naturales, con personas autistas y no autistas. Propone un modelo para entender los patrones de mirada, pero el resumen no da resultados concretos y no indica qué hace cada persona. Las conclusiones no valen como regla para todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: Tomorrow, when you spend time with an autistic person, there is no need to insist on eye contact. Gaze and being watched can feel different for each person, so offer other ways to connect, such as talking while doing something side by side. The evidence is a review of studies on eye gaze in natural interactions, covering autistic and non-autistic people. It proposes a model for making sense of gaze patterns, but the abstract gives no concrete results and does not say what any individual does. Its conclusions are not a rule for every autistic person.
sheet.sv: I morgon, när du tillbringar tid med en autistisk person, behöver du inte kräva ögonkontakt. Att se och bli sedd kan kkännas olika för varje person, så erbjud andra sätt att få kontakt, till exempel att prata medan ni gör något tillsammans. Underlaget är en översikt av studier om blickens roll i naturliga samspel, med både autistiska och icke-autistiska personer. Den föreslår en modell för att förstå blickmönster, men sammanfattningen ger inga konkreta resultat och säger inte vad en enskild person gör. Slutsatserna gäller inte som regel för alla autistiska personer.

title: Systematic Review of the Relationship Between Autism Stigma and Informal Caregiver Mental Health.
authors: Papadopoulos C, Lodder A, Constantinou G, Randhawa G
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Families play a crucial role in determining the mental health of the autistic individual(s) they are caring for. However, the stigma associated with autism can impair caregiver health. To investigate this, empirical evidence pertaining to stigma's impact on informal caregivers' mental health was systematically reviewed. All twelve included studies (n = 1442 informal caregivers) consistently reported the impact of autism related stigma upon caregiver mental health to be significant, meaningful and complex. A new theoretical framework describing the relationship between stigma and caregiver mental health is constructed. Moderating variables include those both changeable through intervention (e.g. hopelessness, self-esteem, self-compassion) and not changeable (gender, culture, financial burden and time since diagnosis). Implications and recommendations for professionals, interventions and future research are proposed.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista, es normal que el estigma social te pese. Hablar con alguien de confianza y buscar apoyo para ti no es egoísmo: forma parte de cuidar. Una revisión sistemática reunió doce estudios con 1442 cuidadores informales y todos observaron que el estigma relacionado con el autismo afecta de forma significativa y compleja a su salud mental. Algunos factores, como la autoestima y la autocompasión, podrían trabajarse con apoyo; otros, como la cultura o la carga económica, no. Sin embargo, la revisión no dice qué le ocurrirá a cada familia, y los resultados no se aplican por igual a todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic person, it makes sense that stigma can weigh on you. Talking with someone you trust and seeking support for yourself is not selfish; it is part of caring. A systematic review brought together twelve studies with 1442 informal caregivers, and all found that autism-related stigma affected caregiver mental health in a significant and complex way. Some factors, such as self-esteem and self-compassion, may be worked on with support; others, such as culture or financial burden, cannot be changed. However, the review cannot say what will happen in any one family, and the findings do not apply equally to everyone.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person är det begripligt att stigma kan tynga dig. Att prata med någon du litar på och söka stöd för egen del är inte själviskt, det är en del av omsorgen. En systematisk översikt samlade tolv studier med 1442 informella vårdare, och alla fann att autismrelaterat stigma påverkade vårdarnas psykiska hälsa på ett betydande och komplext sätt. Vissa faktorer, som självkänsla och självmedkänsla, kan kanske arbetas med genom stöd; andra, som kultur eller ekonomisk börda, går inte att ändra. Översikten kan dock inte säga vad som gäller för en enskild familj, och resultaten gäller inte alla lika.

title: A 'choice', an 'addiction', a way 'out of the lost': exploring self-injury in autistic people without intellectual disability.
authors: Moseley RL, Gregory NJ, Smith P, Allison C, Baron-Cohen S
abstract: Background Non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) describes a phenomenon where individuals inflict deliberate pain and tissue damage to their bodies. Self-injurious behaviour is especially prevalent across the autism spectrum, but little is understood about the features and functions of self-injury for autistic individuals without intellectual disability, or about the risk factors that might be valuable for clinical usage in this group. Methods One hundred and three autistic adults who responded to an online advertisement were classified as current, historic or non-self-harmers in accordance with responses to the Non-Suicidal Self-Injury Assessment Tool (NSSI-AT). Multinomial regression aimed to predict categorisation of participants in accordance with scores on tests of autistic traits, alexithymia, depression, anxiety, mentalising and sensory sensitivity. Linear regression examined relationships between these predictors and the range, frequency, lifetime occurrence and functional purposes of NSSI. Qualitative analysis explored the therapeutic interventions that participants had found helpful, and what they wished people understood about self-injury. Results Current, historic and non-self-harming participants did not differ in age, age at diagnosis, male-to-female ratio, level of employment or education (the majority qualified to at least degree level). The most common function of NSSI was the regulation of low-energy affective states (depression, dissociation), followed by the regulation of high-energy states such as anger and anxiety. Alexithymia significantly predicted the categorisation of participants as current, historic or non-self-harmers, and predicted use of NSSI for regulating high-energy states and communicating distress to others. Depression, anxiety and sensory-sensitivity also differentiated participant groups, and sensory differences also predicted the range of bodily areas targeted, lifetime incidence and frequency of NSSI. Sensory differences, difficulty expressing and identifying emotions also emerged as problematic in the qualitative analysis, where participants expressed the need for compassion, patience, non-judgement and the need to recognise diversity between self-harmers, with some participants perceiving NSSI as a practical, non-problematic coping strategy. Conclusions Alexithymia, depression, anxiety and sensory differences may place some autistic individuals at especial risk of self-injury. Investigating the involvement of these variables and their utility for identification and treatment is of high importance, and the voices of participants offer guidance to practitioners confronted with NSSI in their autistic clients.

title: Autism Spectrum Disorders and the Gut Microbiota.
authors: Fattorusso A, Di Genova L, Dell'Isola GB, Mencaroni E, Esposito S
abstract: In recent years, there has been an emerging interest in the possible role of the gut microbiota as a co-factor in the development of autism spectrum disorders (ASDs), as many studies have highlighted the bidirectional communication between the gut and brain (the so-called "gut-brain axis"). Accumulating evidence has shown a link between alterations in the composition of the gut microbiota and both gastrointestinal and neurobehavioural symptoms in children with ASD. The aim of this narrative review was to analyse the current knowledge about dysbiosis and gastrointestinal (GI) disorders in ASD and assess the current evidence for the role of probiotics and other non-pharmacological approaches in the treatment of children with ASD. Analysis of the literature showed that gut dysbiosis in ASD has been widely demonstrated; however, there is no single distinctive profile of the composition of the microbiota in people with ASD. Gut dysbiosis could contribute to the low-grade systemic inflammatory state reported in patients with GI comorbidities. The administration of probiotics (mostly a mixture of Bifidobacteria , Streptococci and Lactobacilli ) is the most promising treatment for neurobehavioural symptoms and bowel dysfunction, but clinical trials are still limited and heterogeneous. Well-designed, randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trials are required to validate the effectiveness of probiotics in the treatment of ASD and to identify the appropriate strains, dose, and timing of treatment.

title: Music Therapy and Other Music-Based Interventions in Pediatric Health Care: An Overview.
authors: Stegemann T, Geretsegger M, Phan Quoc E, Riedl H, Smetana M
abstract: Background: In pediatric health care, non-pharmacological interventions such as music therapy have promising potential to complement traditional medical treatment options in order to facilitate recovery and well-being. Music therapy and other music-based interventions are increasingly applied in the clinical treatment of children and adolescents in many countries world-wide. The purpose of this overview is to examine the evidence regarding the effectiveness of music therapy and other music-based interventions as applied in pediatric health care. Methods: Surveying recent literature and summarizing findings from systematic reviews, this overview covers selected fields of application in pediatric health care (autism spectrum disorder; disability; epilepsy; mental health; neonatal care; neurorehabilitation; pain, anxiety and stress in medical procedures; pediatric oncology and palliative care) and discusses the effectiveness of music interventions in these areas. Results: Findings show that there is a growing body of evidence regarding the beneficial effects of music therapy, music medicine, and other music-based interventions for children and adolescents, although more rigorous research is still needed. The highest quality of evidence for the positive effects of music therapy is available in the fields of autism spectrum disorder and neonatal care. Conclusions: Music therapy can be considered a safe and generally well-accepted intervention in pediatric health care to alleviate symptoms and improve quality of life. As an individualized intervention that is typically provided in a person-centered way, music therapy is usually easy to implement into clinical practices. However, it is important to note that to exploit the potential of music therapy in an optimal way, specialized academic and clinical training and careful selection of intervention techniques to fit the needs of the client are essential.

sheet.es: Si a tu hijo o hija le atrae la música, puede valer la pena explorar la musicoterapia con un profesional formado: suele ser segura, bien aceptada y adaptable a cada persona. En casa, la música compartida puede ser un espacio tranquilo de conexión, siguiendo sus preferencias y su ritmo, sin forzar. Esta es una revisión general de 2019 que resume revisiones sistemáticas sobre niños y adolescentes en distintos ámbitos de salud; la evidencia más sólida se encontró en autismo y en cuidados neonatales. Sus límites: es un resumen amplio, no un estudio nuevo, los autores piden investigación más rigurosa y los resultados no aplican igual a cada persona.
sheet.en: If your child is drawn to music, it may be worth exploring music therapy with a trained professional: it is generally safe, well accepted and tailored to each person. At home, shared music can be a calm space for connection, following their preferences and pace, never forced. This is a 2019 overview summarising systematic reviews on children and adolescents across several areas of health care; the strongest evidence was found for autism and neonatal care. Its limits: it is a broad summary rather than a new study, the authors call for more rigorous research, and results will not apply the same way to every person.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn dras till musik kan det vara värt att utforska musikterapi med en utbildad terapeut: den är i regel säker, väl accepterad och anpassas till varje person. Hemma kan gemensam musik bli en lugn stund av kontakt, på barnets villkor och i dess takt, utan tvång. Detta är en översikt från 2019 som sammanfattar systematiska översikter om barn och ungdomar inom flera vårdområden; starkast evidens fanns för autism och neonatalvård. Begränsningar: det är en bred sammanfattning, inte en ny studie, författarna efterlyser mer rigorös forskning och resultaten gäller inte alla personer på samma sätt.

title: Understanding the Reasons, Contexts and Costs of Camouflaging for Autistic Adults.
authors: Cage E, Troxell-Whitman Z
