Here, we describe the development of a program evaluation for a specialized medical-dental community clinic serving adults with autism and intellectual disabilities in Montreal, Canada. Method Using a Participatory Action-oriented approach, researchers and staff co-designed an evaluation for a primary care service for this population. We performed an evaluability assessment to identify the processes and outcomes that were feasible to capture and elicited perspectives at both clinical and health system levels. The RE-AIM framework was used to categorize and select tools to capture data elements that would inform practice at the clinic. Results We detail the process of conceptualizing the evaluation framework and operationalizing the domains using a mixed-methods approach. Our experience demonstrated (1) the utility of a comprehensive framework that captures contextual factors in addition to clinical outcomes, (2) the need for validated measures that are not cumbersome for everyday practice, (3) the importance of understanding the functional needs of the organization and building a sustainable data infrastructure that addresses those needs, and (4) the need to commit to an evolving, "living" evaluation in a dynamic health system. Conclusions Evaluation employing rigorous patient-centered and systems-relevant metrics can help organizations effectively implement and continuously improve service models. Using an established framework and a collaborative approach provides an important blueprint for a program evaluation in a learning health system. This work provides insight into the process of integrating care for vulnerable populations with chronic conditions in health care systems and integrated knowledge generation processes between research and health systems.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista con discapacidad intelectual a un servicio médico o dental, puedes preguntar cómo ese servicio comprueba si su atención funciona y cómo tiene en cuenta la opinión de las personas usuarias y sus familias. Este estudio describe cómo investigadores y personal de una clínica médico-dental de Montreal, Canadá, diseñaron juntos una evaluación de su servicio para personas adultas autistas con discapacidad intelectual, usando el marco RE-AIM. Sugiere que conviene medir también el contexto, usar herramientas que no sobrecarguen el trabajo diario y revisar la evaluación con el tiempo. No midió resultados en las personas atendidas y describe una sola clínica, así que no sirve como regla general.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult with an intellectual disability at a medical or dental service, you can ask how that service checks whether its care works and how it takes users' and families' views into account. This study describes how researchers and staff at a medical-dental clinic in Montreal, Canada, co-designed an evaluation of their service for autistic adults with intellectual disabilities, using the RE-AIM framework. It suggests measuring context as well as clinical outcomes, using tools that do not burden daily work, and revising the evaluation over time. It did not measure outcomes for the people receiving care and describes a single clinic, so it is not a rule for every service.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning hos en medicinsk eller tandvårdsmottagning kan du fråga hur mottagningen följer upp om vården fungerar och hur den tar hänsyn till patienters och anhörigas åsikter. Studien beskriver hur forskare och personal vid en medicinsk-odontologisk klinik i Montreal, Kanada, tillsammans utformade en utvärdering av sin verksamhet för autistiska vuxna med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning, med ramverket RE-AIM. Den föreslår att man mäter även sammanhanget, använder verktyg som inte tynger vardagen och låter utvärderingen utvecklas över tid. Studien mätte inte resultat hos de patienter som fick vård och beskriver en enda klinik, så den är ingen regel för alla verksamheter.

title: Age at identification, prevalence and general health of children with autism: observational study of a whole country population.
authors: Rydzewska E, Hughes-McCormack LA, Gillberg C, Henderson A, MacIntyre C, Rintoul J, Cooper SA
abstract: Objectives Reported childhood prevalence of autism varies considerably between studies and over time, and general health status has been little investigated. We aimed to investigate contemporary prevalence of reported autism by age, and general health status of children/young people with and without autism. Design Secondary analysis of Scotland's Census, 2011 data. Cross-sectional study. Setting General population of Scotland. Participants All children (n=916 331) and young people (n=632 488) in Scotland. Main outcome measures Number (%) of children/young people reported to have autism and their general health status; prevalence of autism; prevalence of poor health (fair, bad and very bad health); odds ratios (95% confidence intervals) of autism predicting poor health, adjusted for age and gender and OR for age and gender in predicting poor health within the population with reported autism. Results Autism was reported for 17 348/916 331 (1.9%) children aged 0-15, and 7715/632 488 (1.2%) young people aged 16-24. The rate increased to age 11 in boys and age 10 in girls, reflecting age at diagnosis. Prevalence was 2.8% at age 10 (4.4% for boys; 1.1% for girls), and 2.9% at age 11 (4.5% for boys; 1.1% for girls). 22.0% of children and 25.5% of young people with autism reported poor health, compared with 2.0% and 4.4% without autism. Autism had OR=11.3 (11.0 to 11.7) in predicting poor health. Autistic females had poorer health than autistic males, OR=1.6 (1.5 to 1.8). Conclusion Accurate information on the proportion of autistic children and their health status is essential plan appropriate prevention and intervention measures and provide resources for those who may put demand on services designed for autistic people.

sheet.es: Si cuidas de una persona autista, conviene incluir su salud general en las revisiones habituales y preguntarle, o observar, cómo se siente físicamente. Este estudio transversal analizó datos del censo de Escocia de 2011 con toda la población infantil y joven: 916 331 niñas y niños y 632 488 jóvenes. Un 22.0% de los niños y un 25.5% de los jóvenes autistas indicaron mala salud, frente a un 2.0% y un 4.4% sin autismo. Sus límites: la salud se comunicó de forma general, el autismo figuraba como informado y no se explican las causas. No describe a cada persona.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person, it is worth including general health in regular check-ups and asking, or watching for, how they feel physically. This cross-sectional study used Scotland's 2011 census data covering the whole child and youth population: 916 331 children and 632 488 young people. Poor health was reported for 22.0% of autistic children and 25.5% of autistic young people, compared with 2.0% and 4.4% of those without autism. Limits: health was reported in a general way, autism was recorded as reported, and the study does not explain the causes. It does not describe every person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person är det värt att ta med den allmänna hälsan vid vanliga kontroller och fråga om, eller uppmärksamma, hur personen mår fysiskt. Denna tvärsnittsstudie använde Skottlands folkräkning 2011 för hela barn- och ungdomsbefolkningen: 916 331 barn och 632 488 unga. Dålig hälsa uppgavs för 22.0% av autistiska barn och 25.5% av autistiska unga, jämfört med 2.0% och 4.4% utan autism. Begränsningar: hälsan angavs i allmänna termer, autism räknades som rapporterad och studien förklarar inte orsakerna. Den beskriver inte varje person.

title: A Systematic Review of What Barriers and Facilitators Prevent and Enable Physical Healthcare Services Access for Autistic Adults.
authors: Mason D, Ingham B, Urbanowicz A, Michael C, Birtles H, Woodbury-Smith M, Brown T, James I, Scarlett C, Nicolaidis C, Parr JR
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Autistic people are more likely to: be diagnosed with a range of physical health conditions (i.e. cardio-vascular disease); experience premature mortality (for most disease categories); and experience barriers to effectively accessing healthcare. This systematic review sought to identify studies that report on barriers and facilitators to physical healthcare access for autistic people. A total of 3111 records were screened and six studies were included: two quantitative, two qualitative, and two mixed-methodology studies. Patient-provider communication, sensory sensitivities, and executive functioning/planning issues emerged as important barriers to healthcare. Recommendations for clinicians and those planning services are discussed.

sheet.es: Antes de una cita médica, puede ayudar preparar juntos una nota breve con los síntomas y preguntas, pedir la cita a una hora tranquila, avisar de sensibilidades sensoriales (luces, ruido, tacto) y solicitar que el profesional explique los pasos con claridad o por escrito. Organizar la cita, el transporte y el seguimiento también puede repartirse con apoyo. Esta revisión sistemática reunió seis estudios con adultos autistas y encontró que la comunicación con el profesional, la sensorialidad y la planificación eran barreras importantes para acceder a la atención física. Sus límites: pocos estudios, métodos distintos, y cada persona puede necesitar apoyos diferentes.
sheet.en: Before a medical appointment, it can help to prepare a short note together with symptoms and questions, ask for a quiet appointment time, mention sensory sensitivities (lights, noise, touch) and request that the clinician explain each step clearly or in writing. Booking, travel and follow-up can also be shared with support. This systematic review brought together six studies with autistic adults and found that patient-clinician communication, sensory experiences and planning were key barriers to physical healthcare. Its limits: very few studies, mixed methods, and each person may need different supports.
sheet.sv: Inför ett läkarbesök kan det hjälpa att tillsammans skriva en kort lapp med symtom och frågor, be om en lugn tid, berätta om sensoriska känsligheter (ljus, ljud, beröring) och be vårdpersonalen förklara varje steg tydligt eller skriftligt. Bokning, resa och uppföljning kan också delas upp med stöd. Denna systematiska översikt samlade sex studier med autistiska vuxna och fann att kommunikation med vårdpersonal, sensoriska upplevelser och planering var viktiga hinder för fysisk vård. Begränsningar: mycket få studier, blandade metoder, och varje person kan behöva olika stöd.

title: Risk Factors for Unhealthy Weight Gain and Obesity among Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Dhaliwal KK, Orsso CE, Richard C, Haqq AM, Zwaigenbaum L
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a developmental disorder characterized by social and communication deficits and repetitive behaviors. Children with ASD are also at a higher risk for developing overweight or obesity than children with typical development (TD). Childhood obesity has been associated with adverse health outcomes, including insulin resistance, diabetes, heart disease, and certain cancers. Importantly some key factors that play a mediating role in these higher rates of obesity include lifestyle factors and biological influences, as well as secondary comorbidities and medications. This review summarizes current knowledge about behavioral and lifestyle factors that could contribute to unhealthy weight gain in children with ASD, as well as the current state of knowledge of emerging risk factors such as the possible influence of sleep problems, the gut microbiome, endocrine influences and maternal metabolic disorders. We also discuss some of the clinical implications of these risk factors and areas for future research.

sheet.es: Si te preocupa el peso de tu hijo autista, puede ayudar mirar el conjunto con calma: sueño, actividad física que disfrute, alimentación selectiva y posibles efectos de medicamentos. Llevar unas notas sencillas sobre sueño, comidas y movimiento puede facilitar una conversación tranquila con el equipo de salud, sin culpas ni dietas estrictas. Esta revisión resume investigaciones previas sobre factores que podrían contribuir al aumento de peso en niños autistas, incluidos el sueño, la microbiota intestinal, las hormonas y la salud metabólica materna. Su límite: no aporta datos nuevos y muchos de estos factores emergentes aún están poco estudiados, así que no se aplican igual a cada niño.
sheet.en: If you are concerned about your autistic child's weight, it can help to look calmly at the whole picture: sleep, physical activity they actually enjoy, selective eating and possible medication side effects. Keeping simple notes on sleep, meals and movement can support a relaxed conversation with your health team, without blame or strict diets. This review summarises earlier research on factors that may contribute to weight gain in autistic children, including sleep, gut microbiome, hormones and maternal metabolic health. Its limit: it adds no new data, and many of these emerging factors are still poorly understood, so they will not apply the same way to every child.
sheet.sv: Om du oroar dig för ditt autistiska barns vikt kan det hjälpa att lugnt se helheten: sömn, rörelse som barnet faktiskt tycker om, selektivt ätande och möjliga biverkningar av läkemedel. Enkla anteckningar om sömn, måltider och rörelse kan underlätta ett lugnt samtal med vården, utan skuld eller strikta dieter. Den här översikten sammanfattar tidigare forskning om faktorer som kan bidra till viktuppgång hos autistiska barn, bland annat sömn, tarmflora, hormoner och mammans metabola hälsa. Begränsning: den tillför inga nya data och många av de nya faktorerna är fortfarande dåligt utforskade, så de gäller inte på samma sätt för alla barn.

title: Linking knowledge and attitudes: Determining neurotypical knowledge about and attitudes towards autism.
authors: Kuzminski R, Netto J, Wilson J, Falkmer T, Chamberlain A, Falkmer M
abstract: "Why are neurotypicals so pig-ignorant about autism?" an autistic person wrote on the Curtin Autism Research Group's on-line portal as a response to a call for research questions. Co-produced with an autistic researcher, knowledge about and attitudes towards autism were analysed from 1,054 completed surveys, representing the Australian neurotypical adult population. The majority, 81.5% of participants had a high level of knowledge and 81.3% of participants had a strong positive attitude towards autism. Neither age, nor education level had an impact on attitudes. However, attitudes were influenced by knowledge about 'Societal Views and Ideas'; 'What it Could be Like to Have Autism'; and the demographic variables 'Knowing and having spent time around someone with autism'; and gender (women having more positive attitudes than men). Thus, targeted interventions, geared more towards men than women, to increase knowledge about autism could further improve attitudes and increase acceptance of the autistic community.

sheet.es: Lo práctico: las actitudes hacia el autismo mejoran cuando la gente entiende cómo puede ser la vida de una persona autista y pasa tiempo con ella. Mañana puede compartir con familiares, docentes o vecinos algo concreto sobre su hijo o hija (qué le ayuda, qué le cuesta), y crear ocasiones tranquilas de convivencia; los hombres del entorno quizá se beneficien especialmente. Evidencia: encuesta coproducida con un investigador autista, con 1.054 adultos neurotípicos australianos; la mayoría mostró buen conocimiento y actitudes positivas. Límites: es una encuesta en un solo país, mide lo que la gente declara y no demuestra que informar cambie la conducta real.
sheet.en: The practical point: attitudes towards autism improve when people understand what life can be like for an autistic person and spend time with them. Tomorrow you might share something concrete with relatives, teachers or neighbours about your child (what helps, what is hard) and create calm chances to spend time together; men around you may benefit especially. Evidence: a survey co-produced with an autistic researcher, involving 1,054 neurotypical Australian adults; most showed good knowledge and positive attitudes. Limits: it is a single-country survey, measures what people report, and does not show that sharing information changes real behaviour.
sheet.sv: Det praktiska: attityder till autism blir bättre när människor förstår hur livet kan vara för en autistisk person och tillbringar tid tillsammans. I morgon kan du berätta något konkret för släkt, lärare eller grannar om ditt barn (vad som hjälper, vad som är svårt) och skapa lugna tillfällen att umgås; män i omgivningen kan ha särskild nytta av det. Evidens: en enkät som utformats tillsammans med en autistisk forskare, med 1 054 neurotypiska vuxna i Australien; de flesta hade god kunskap och positiva attityder. Begränsningar: enkäten gäller ett land, mäter självrapporterade svar och visar inte att information förändrar verkligt beteende.

title: Depression and anxiety in parents of children with intellectual and developmental disabilities: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Scherer N, Verhey I, Kuper H
abstract: Introduction Although caring for a child with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD) can have positive outcomes, parents may be at a greater risk of depression and anxiety, due to a number of associated stressors, such as increased caregiver demands and financial strain. This systematic review updates previous data, exploring the relationship between parenting a child with IDD and parental depression and anxiety. Methods Five electronic databases were searched for eligible English-language articles, published between January 2004 and July 2018. All epidemiological study designs were eligible, provided the level of depression and/or anxiety was compared between parents of children (aged Results Of the 5,839 unique records screened, 19 studies fulfilled the inclusion criteria. The majority of studies were conducted in high-income (n = 8, 42%) or upper-middle income countries (n = 10, 53%). Of the 19 studies, 69% focused on parents of children with cerebral palsy (n = 7, 37%) or autism (n = 6, 32%). Nearly all studies found a positive association between parenting a child with IDD and depression (n = 18, 95%) and anxiety (n = 9, 90%) symptoms. Factors associated with higher levels of depression symptoms amongst parents of children with IDD included disability severity (n = 8, 78%) and lower household income (n = 4, 80%). Approximately one third (31%) of parents of children with IDD reach the clinical cut-off score for moderate depression, compared with 7% of parents of children without IDD. 31% of parents of children with IDD reach the cut-off score for moderate anxiety, compared with 14% of parents of children without IDD. The meta-analyses demonstrated moderate effect sizes for elevated depression amongst parents of children with autism and cerebral palsy. Conclusions Results indicate elevated levels of depressive symptoms amongst parents of children with IDD. Quality concerns amongst the existing literature support the need for further research, especially in low- and middle-income countries.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a un niño con discapacidad intelectual o del desarrollo, tu propio bienestar también importa. Sentirte agotado, triste o ansioso es frecuente y no es un fallo personal: conviene hablarlo con tu médico, buscar apoyo práctico (respiro, grupos de familias, ayudas económicas) y reservar pequeños momentos para ti. Esta revisión sistemática con metaanálisis reunió 19 estudios; cerca de un tercio de los padres de niños con discapacidad, incluidos niños autistas, superaba el umbral de depresión moderada, frente al 7% de otros padres, y los ingresos bajos se asociaban a más síntomas. Límites: estudios de calidad desigual, solo en inglés y pocos de países de ingresos bajos; no describe a cada familia.
sheet.en: If you care for a child with an intellectual or developmental disability, your own wellbeing matters too. Feeling worn out, low or anxious is common and not a personal failing: it is worth talking to your doctor, seeking practical support (respite, family groups, financial help) and protecting small moments for yourself. This systematic review and meta-analysis pooled 19 studies; about one third of parents of disabled children, including autistic children, reached the cut-off for moderate depression, compared with 7% of other parents, and lower income was linked to more symptoms. Limits: study quality varied, only English-language papers were included, and few came from low-income countries; it does not describe every family.
sheet.sv: Om du tar hand om ett barn med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning eller utvecklingsrelaterad funktionsnedsättning spelar ditt eget mående också roll. Att känna sig utmattad, nedstämd eller orolig är vanligt och inget personligt misslyckande: prata gärna med din läkare, sök praktiskt stöd (avlösning, föräldragrupper, ekonomiskt stöd) och skydda små stunder för dig själv. Denna systematiska översikt med metaanalys samlade 19 studier; ungefär en tredjedel av föräldrarna till barn med funktionsnedsättning, även autistiska barn, nådde gränsen för måttlig depression, jämfört med 7 % av andra föräldrar, och lägre inkomst hängde ihop med fler symtom. Begränsningar: studiernas kvalitet varierade, bara engelskspråkiga artiklar ingick och få kom från låginkomstländer; resultaten beskriver inte varje familj.

title: Association Between Gut Microbiota and Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Xu M, Xu X, Li J, Li F
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is characterized by stereotyped behavior and deficits in communication and social interactions. Gastrointestinal (GI) dysfunction is an ASD-associated comorbidity, implying a potential role of the gut microbiota in ASD GI pathophysiology. Several recent studies found that autistic individuals harbor an altered bacterial gut microbiota. In some cases, remodeling the gut microbiota by antibiotic administration and microbiota transfer therapy reportedly alleviated the symptoms of ASD. However, there is little consensus on specific bacterial species that are similarly altered across individual studies. The aim of this study is to summarize previously published data and analyze the alteration of the relative abundance of bacterial genera in the gut microbiota in controls and individuals with ASD using meta-analysis. We analyzed nine studies, including 254 patients with ASD, and found that children with ASD had lower percentages of Akkermansia , Bacteroides , Bifidobacterium , and Parabacteroides and a higher percentage of Faecalibacterium in the total detected microflora compared to controls. In contrast, children with ASD had lower abundance of Enterococcus , Escherichia coli , Bacteroides , and Bifidobacterium and higher abundance of Lactobacillus . This meta-analysis suggests an association between ASD and alteration of microbiota composition and warrants additional prospective cohort studies to evaluate the association of bacterial changes with ASD symptoms, which would provide further evidence for the precise microbiological treatment of ASD.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista tiene molestias digestivas frecuentes, vale la pena anotarlas y comentarlas con su pediatra o médico; no hay nada en este estudio que indique cambiar la dieta o el tratamiento por cuenta propia. La evidencia es un metaanálisis de nueve estudios, con 254 pacientes con TEA, que encontró diferencias en las bacterias intestinales de niños autistas frente a los controles. Sus límites: los resultados no coinciden del todo entre estudios, solo muestran una asociación (no una causa) y no sirven para predecir a cada persona. Las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If an autistic person has frequent tummy or digestive discomfort, it is worth noting it down and raising it with their paediatrician or doctor; nothing in this study suggests changing diet or treatment on your own. The evidence is a meta-analysis of nine studies, including 254 patients with ASD, which found differences in gut bacteria between autistic children and controls. Its limits: results do not fully agree across studies, it shows an association rather than a cause, and it cannot predict any one person. Medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person ofta har ont i magen eller andra matsmältningsbesvär är det bra att anteckna det och ta upp det med barnläkare eller läkare; studien ger inget stöd för att ändra kost eller behandling på egen hand. Underlaget är en metaanalys av nio studier med 254 patienter med ASD, som fann skillnader i tarmbakterier mellan autistiska barn och kontroller. Begränsningar: resultaten stämmer inte helt överens mellan studierna, det visar ett samband och inte en orsak, och det säger inget säkert om en enskild person. Medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker.

title: A Short Commentary on Non-specialist-mediated Interventions for Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Afzaal T, Waqas A, Naveed S
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a lifelong neurodevelopmental disability delineated by social and communication impairments, restricted interests and repetitive behaviors, and sensory hypo- or hyper reactivity to sensory inputs. Early recognition and timely intervention are essential for individuals with ASD and the long-term prognosis for these individuals. The specialist-mediated interventions can be expensive for patients, their families, and the healthcare system. It is important to provide a naturalistic intervention, especially in the context of cost issues, the impact of early intervention of prognosis, limited resources in developing countries, lack of healthcare providers, and healthcare disparities. The current article reviews non-specialist-mediated interventions of children and adolescents with ASD.

sheet.es: Si no tienes acceso a especialistas, o cuesta mucho, las intervenciones guiadas por personas que no son especialistas pueden ser una opción que conviene explorar con el equipo sanitario o educativo de tu hijo o hija. Es un comentario breve de revisión sobre este tipo de intervenciones para niños y adolescentes autistas. Los autores señalan que son útiles cuando faltan recursos y profesionales. El resumen no da resultados concretos, así que no sabemos cuánto funcionan ni para quién. No es una regla para todas las personas: cada niño o niña necesita su propio apoyo.
sheet.en: If specialists are costly or hard to reach, interventions led by people who are not specialists may be an option worth exploring with your child's health or education team. This is a short review commentary on such interventions for autistic children and adolescents. The authors point to them as useful where resources and professionals are limited. The abstract gives no specific results, so we cannot say how well they work or for whom. It is not a rule for everyone: each child needs support that fits them.
sheet.sv: Om specialister är dyra eller svåra att nå kan insatser som leds av personer som inte är specialister vara ett alternativ att utforska tillsammans med barnets vård- eller skolteam. Det här är en kort översiktskommentar om sådana insatser för autistiska barn och ungdomar. Författarna lyfter dem som användbara när resurser och personal saknas. Sammanfattningen redovisar inga konkreta resultat, så vi vet inte hur väl de fungerar eller för vem. Det är ingen regel för alla: varje barn behöver stöd som passar just det barnet.

title: State of the Field: Differentiating Intellectual Disability From Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Thurm A, Farmer C, Salzman E, Lord C, Bishop S
abstract: The topic of this special issue on secondary versus idiopathic autism allows for discussion of how different groups may come to manifest autism spectrum disorder (ASD) or ASD-like symptoms despite important etiological differences. A related issue is that, because many of the social communication deficits that define ASD represent a failure to acquire developmentally expected skills, these same deficits would be expected to occur to some extent in all individuals with intellectual disability (ID). Thus, regardless of etiology, ASD symptoms may appear across groups of individuals with vastly different profiles of underlying deficits and strengths. In this focused review, we consider the impact of ID on the diagnosis of ASD. We discuss behavioral distinctions between ID and ASD, in light of the diagnostic criterion mandating that ASD should not be diagnosed if symptoms are accounted for by ID or general developmental delay. We review the evolution of the autism diagnosis and ASD diagnostic tools to understand how this distinction has been conceptualized previously. We then consider ways that operationalized criteria may be beneficial for making the clinical distinction between ID with and without ASD. Finally, we consider the impact of the blurred diagnostic boundaries between ID and ASD on the study of secondary versus idiopathic ASD. Especially pertinent to this discussion are findings that a diagnosis of ID in the context of an ASD diagnosis may be one of the strongest indicators that an associated condition or specific etiological factor is present (i.e., secondary autism).

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija tiene discapacidad intelectual, algunas diferencias en comunicación social pueden deberse a su ritmo general de desarrollo y no necesariamente al autismo. Puede ayudar pedir a los profesionales que expliquen cómo distinguen ambas cosas y que comparen sus habilidades sociales con su nivel de desarrollo, no solo con su edad. Cuando hay autismo y discapacidad intelectual juntos, vale la pena preguntar si conviene explorar causas asociadas, como factores genéticos. Esto es una revisión narrativa de investigaciones y herramientas diagnósticas, sin participantes nuevos. Su límite: ofrece reflexiones y propuestas, no criterios definitivos, y cada persona tiene un perfil propio.
sheet.en: If your child has an intellectual disability, some differences in social communication may reflect their overall developmental pace rather than autism specifically. It can help to ask professionals how they tell the two apart, and to compare social skills with your child's developmental level, not just their age. When autism and intellectual disability occur together, it may be worth asking whether exploring associated causes, such as genetic factors, makes sense. This is a narrative review of earlier research and diagnostic tools, with no new participants. Its limit: it offers reflections and proposals, not settled criteria, and every person has their own profile.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn har en intellektuell funktionsnedsättning kan vissa skillnader i social kommunikation hänga ihop med barnets övergripande utvecklingstakt snarare än specifikt med autism. Det kan hjälpa att fråga professionella hur de skiljer på de två och att jämföra sociala färdigheter med barnets utvecklingsnivå, inte bara ålder. När autism och intellektuell funktionsnedsättning finns samtidigt kan det vara värt att fråga om det är meningsfullt att utreda bakomliggande orsaker, till exempel genetiska. Detta är en översikt över tidigare forskning och diagnosverktyg, utan nya deltagare. Begränsning: den ger resonemang och förslag, inte fastställda kriterier, och varje person har sin egen profil.

title: Changing Developmental Trajectories of Toddlers With Autism Spectrum Disorder: Strategies for Bridging Research to Community Practice.
authors: Wetherby AM, Woods J, Guthrie W, Delehanty A, Brown JA, Morgan L, Holland RD, Schatschneider C, Lord C
journal: Journal of speech, language, and hearing research : JSLHR
abstract: Purpose The need for community-viable, evidence-based intervention strategies for toddlers with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a national priority. The purpose of this research forum article is to identify gaps in intervention research and needs in community practice for toddlers with ASD, incorporate published findings from a randomized controlled trial (RCT) of the Early Social Interaction (ESI) model (Wetherby et al., 2014) to illustrate community-based intervention, report new findings on child active engagement from the ESI RCT, and offer solutions to bridge the research-to-community practice gap. Method Research findings were reviewed to identify gaps in the evidence base for toddlers with ASD. Published and new findings from the multisite ESI RCT compared the effects of two different ESI conditions for 82 toddlers with ASD to teach parents how to support active engagement in natural environments. Results The RCT of the ESI model was the only parent-implemented intervention that reported differential treatment effects on standardized measures of child outcomes, including social communication, developmental level, and adaptive behavior. A new measure of active engagement in the natural environment was found to be sensitive to change in 3 months for young toddlers with ASD and to predict outcomes on the standardized measures of child outcomes. Strategies for utilizing the Autism Navigator collection of web-based courses and tools using extensive video footage for families and professional development are offered for scaling up in community settings to change developmental trajectories of toddlers with ASD. Conclusions Current health care and education systems are challenged to provide intervention of adequate intensity for toddlers with ASD. The use of innovative technology can increase acceleration of access to evidence-based early intervention for toddlers with ASD that addresses health disparities, enables immediate response as soon as ASD is suspected, and rapidly bridges the research-to-practice gap.

sheet.es: Si tiene un niño autista pequeño, puede empezar ya a apoyar su participación activa en la rutina diaria: juegos, comidas, baños. Observe qué le interesa y responda a sus intentos de comunicarse. Esta revisión incluye un ensayo aleatorizado con 82 niños autistas pequeños, en el que se enseñó a las familias a favorecer esa participación en entornos naturales. Los autores también proponen cursos web con vídeos para familias y profesionales. Límites: es una revisión con una parte de datos nuevos; no garantiza los mismos resultados en cada niño ni en cada familia, y no sustituye la orientación de profesionales.
sheet.en: If you have an autistic toddler, you can start now by supporting their active engagement in daily routines: play, meals, bath time. Notice what interests them and respond to their attempts to communicate. This review includes a randomized trial with 82 autistic toddlers, in which families were taught to support that engagement in natural settings. The authors also suggest web courses with video for families and professionals. Limits: it is a review with some new data; it cannot promise the same results for every child or family, and it does not replace guidance from professionals.
sheet.sv: Har du ett litet autistiskt barn kan du börja redan nu stödja barnets aktiva delaktighet i vardagen: lek, måltider, badet. Notera vad barnet är intresserat av och svara på barnets försök att kommunicera. Översikten omfattar en randomiserad studie med 82 autistiska småbarn, där föräldrar lärde sig stödja delaktighet i naturliga miljöer. Författarna föreslår också webbkurser med video för familjer och yrkesverksamma. Begränsningar: det är en översikt med viss ny data; den garanterar inte samma resultat för varje barn eller familj och ersätter inte råd från yrkespersoner.

title: Mast Cells, Stress, Fear and Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Theoharides TC, Kavalioti M, Tsilioni I
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a developmental condition characterized by impaired communication and obsessive behavior that affects 1 in 59 children. ASD is expected to affect 1 in about 40 children by 2020, but there is still no distinct pathogenesis or effective treatments. Prenatal stress has been associated with higher risk of developing ASD in the offspring. Moreover, children with ASD cannot handle anxiety and respond disproportionately even to otherwise benign triggers. Stress and environmental stimuli trigger the unique immune cells, mast cells, which could then trigger microglia leading to abnormal synaptic pruning and dysfunctional neuronal connectivity. This process could alter the "fear threshold" in the amygdala and lead to an exaggerated "fight-or-flight" reaction. The combination of corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH), secreted under stress, together with environmental stimuli could be major contributors to the pathogenesis of ASD. Recognizing these associations and preventing stimulation of mast cells and/or microglia could greatly benefit ASD patients.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista reacciona con mucha intensidad ante algo que parece menor, conviene pensar que el estrés y los estímulos del entorno pueden pesarle más. Reducir esos estímulos y ofrecer calma puede ayudar. Este trabajo es una revisión que reúne investigaciones previas; no estudió a un grupo concreto de personas. Propone que el estrés activaría células inmunitarias llamadas mastocitos, lo que podría influir en la reacción de miedo. Es una hipótesis, no una prueba: no demuestra causas y no sirve como regla para cada persona. Cualquier decisión médica debe tomarla un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If an autistic person reacts very strongly to something that seems minor, it may help to consider that stress and environmental stimuli can weigh more heavily on them. Lowering those stimuli and offering calm may help. This is a review that brings together earlier research; it did not study a specific group of people. It suggests stress may activate immune cells called mast cells, which could influence the fear response. This is a hypothesis, not proof: it does not show causes and is not a rule for every person. Any medical decision belongs to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person reagerar mycket starkt på något som verkar litet kan det hjälpa att tänka på att stress och stimuli i omgivningen kan väga tyngre för hen. Att minska stimuli och erbjuda lugn kan vara till hjälp. Detta är en översikt som sammanställer tidigare forskning; den studerade inte en särskild grupp människor. Den föreslår att stress kan aktivera immunceller som kallas mastceller, vilket kan påverka rädsloreaktionen. Det är en hypotes, inte ett bevis: den visar inte orsaker och är ingen regel för varje person. Medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker.

title: Temporal Changes in Effect Sizes of Studies Comparing Individuals With and Without Autism: A Meta-analysis.
authors: Rødgaard EM, Jensen K, Vergnes JN, Soulières I, Mottron L
abstract: Importance The definition and nature of autism have been highly debated, as exemplified by several revisions of the DSM (DSM-III, DSM-IIIR, DSM-IV, and DSM-5) criteria. There has recently been a move from a categorical view toward a spectrum-based view. These changes have been accompanied by a steady increase in the prevalence of the condition. Changes in the definition of autism that may increase heterogeneity could affect the results of autism research; specifically, a broadening of the population with autism could result in decreasing effect sizes of group comparison studies. Objective To examine the correlation between publication year and effect size of autism-control group comparisons across several domains of published autism neurocognitive research. Data sources This meta-analysis investigated 11 meta-analyses obtained through a systematic search of PubMed for meta-analyses published from January 1, 1966, through January 27, 2019, using the search string autism AND (meta-analysis OR meta-analytic). The last search was conducted on January 27, 2019. Study selection Meta-analyses were included if they tested the significance of group differences between individuals with autism and control individuals on a neurocognitive construct. Meta-analyses were only included if the tested group difference was significant and included data with a span of at least 15 years. Data extraction and synthesis Data were extracted and analyzed according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses (PRISMA) reporting guideline using fixed-effects models. Main outcomes and measures Estimated slope of the correlation between publication year and effect size, controlling for differences in methods, sample size, and study quality. Results The 11 meta-analyses included data from a total of 27 723 individuals. Demographic data such as sex and age were not available for the entire data set. Seven different psychological and neurologic constructs were analyzed based on data from these meta-analyses. Downward temporal trends for effect size were found for all constructs (slopes: -0.067 to -0.003), with the trend being significant in 5 of 7 cases: emotion recognition (slope: -0.028 [95% CI, -0.048 to -0.007]), theory of mind (-0.045 [95% CI, -0.066 to -0.024]), planning (-0.067 [95% CI, -0.125 to -0.009]), P3b amplitude (-0.048 [95% CI, -0.093 to -0.004]), and brain size (-0.047 [95% CI, -0.077 to -0.016]). In contrast, 3 analogous constructs in schizophrenia, a condition that is also heterogeneous but with no reported increase in prevalence, did not show a similar trend. Conclusions and relevance The findings suggest that differences between individuals with autism and those without the diagnosis have decreased over time and that possible changes in the definition of autism from a narrowly defined and homogenous population toward an inclusive and heterogeneous population may reduce our capacity to build mechanistic models of the condition.

sheet.es: Si lee que las personas autistas «tienen menos teoría de la mente» o «reconocen peor las emociones», tómelo con cautela: esas diferencias medias se han ido reduciendo con los años, a medida que la definición de autismo se amplió. Lo que dice un estudio sobre «el grupo» puede no describir a su hijo o a usted; observe a la persona concreta, sus fortalezas y lo que necesita. Esta es un metaanálisis de 11 metaanálisis con datos de 27 723 personas, que comparó grupos autistas y no autistas a lo largo de décadas. Límites: faltaban datos de edad y sexo, y analiza tendencias en publicaciones, no cambios en personas reales.
sheet.en: If you read that autistic people "lack theory of mind" or "struggle to recognise emotions", hold it lightly: these average group differences have shrunk over the years as the definition of autism broadened. What research says about "the group" may not describe your child or you; look at the actual person, their strengths and what they need. This is a meta-analysis of 11 earlier meta-analyses, covering 27,723 people, comparing autistic and non-autistic groups across decades. Limits: age and sex data were missing, and it tracks trends in published studies, not changes in real individuals.
sheet.sv: Om du läser att autistiska personer "saknar mentaliseringsförmåga" eller "har svårt att känna igen känslor", ta det med en nypa salt: sådana genomsnittliga gruppskillnader har minskat över åren i takt med att autismdefinitionen breddats. Det forskningen säger om "gruppen" behöver inte stämma för ditt barn eller dig; utgå från personen, dennes styrkor och behov. Detta är en metaanalys av 11 tidigare metaanalyser med data från 27 723 personer, som jämförde autistiska och icke-autistiska grupper över flera decennier. Begränsningar: uppgifter om ålder och kön saknades, och studien följer trender i publicerad forskning, inte förändringar hos enskilda människor.

title: Effectiveness of non-pharmacological interventions for insomnia in children with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Keogh S, Bridle C, Siriwardena NA, Nadkarni A, Laparidou D, Durrant SJ, Kargas N, Law GR, Curtis F
abstract: Background Autism spectrum disorders (ASD) are a set of neurodevelopmental disorders characterised by behavioural, communication and social impairments. The prevalence of sleep disturbances in children with ASD is 40-80%, with significant effects on quality of life for the children and carers. This systematic review aimed to synthesise evidence of the effects of behavioural interventions to improve sleep among children with ASD. Methods Databases (MEDLINE, PsycINFO, CINAHL, ScienceDirect, Autism Data, CENTRAL, ClinicalTrials.gov and Current Controlled Trials) were searched for published, unpublished and ongoing randomised controlled trials evaluating the effect of non-pharmacological interventions for insomnia in children with autism spectrum conditions. Results Three studies met the inclusion criteria, one provided actigraphy data, one Children's Sleep Habits Questionnaire (CSHQ) data, and one both actigraphy and CSHQ data for use in meta-analyses. There were significant differences between the behavioural intervention and comparison groups (actigraphy data) for total sleep time (24.41 minutes, 95% CI 5.71, 43.11, P = 0.01), sleep latency (-18.31 minutes, 95% CI -30.84, -5.77, P = 0.004) and sleep efficiency (5.59%, 95% CI 0.87, 10.31, P = 0.02). There was also a favourable intervention effect evident for the subjective CSHQ data (-4.71, 95% CI -6.70, -2.73, P Conclusions There are very few high quality randomised controlled trials in this area. Here we provide initial synthesised quantitative evidence of the effectiveness of behavioural interventions for treating sleep problems in children with ASD. Trial registration Protocol was registered (CRD42017081784) on the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (http://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO).

sheet.es: Si el sueño de su hijo autista es difícil, pueden probar un enfoque conductual, como rutinas de sueño consistentes, y hablarlo con un profesional de la salud. Es un metaanálisis de ensayos aleatorizados: solo tres estudios con niños autistas cumplieron los criterios. En los datos de actigrafía, el tiempo total de sueño fue 24.41 minutos mayor y la latencia del sueño 18.31 minutos menor frente a la comparación. Los límites: hay muy pocos ensayos de calidad y los resultados no valen para todos los niños. Cada niño es distinto.
sheet.en: If sleep is hard for your autistic child, a behavioural approach, such as consistent bedtime routines, may be worth trying and discussing with a health professional. This is a meta-analysis of randomised trials: only three studies with autistic children met the criteria. In actigraphy data, total sleep time was 24.41 minutes longer and sleep latency 18.31 minutes shorter than in the comparison groups. The limits: there are very few high quality trials, and results will not apply to every child. Each child is different.
sheet.sv: Om sömnen är svår för ditt autistiska barn kan ett beteendebaserat angreppssätt, som fasta kvällsrutiner, vara värt att pröva och ta upp med en vårdgivare. Det här är en metaanalys av randomiserade studier: bara tre studier med autistiska barn uppfyllde kriterierna. I aktigrafidata var total sömntid 24.41 minuter längre och insomningstiden 18.31 minuter kortare jämfört med jämförelsegrupperna. Begränsningar: det finns mycket få högkvalitativa studier, och resultaten gäller inte alla barn. Varje barn är unikt.

title: Genetic Causes and Modifiers of Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Rylaarsdam L, Guemez-Gamboa A
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is one of the most prevalent neurodevelopmental disorders, affecting an estimated 1 in 59 children. ASD is highly genetically heterogeneous and may be caused by both inheritable and de novo gene variations. In the past decade, hundreds of genes have been identified that contribute to the serious deficits in communication, social cognition, and behavior that patients often experience. However, these only account for 10-20% of ASD cases, and patients with similar pathogenic variants may be diagnosed on very different levels of the spectrum. In this review, we will describe the genetic landscape of ASD and discuss how genetic modifiers such as copy number variation, single nucleotide polymorphisms, and epigenetic alterations likely play a key role in modulating the phenotypic spectrum of ASD patients. We also consider how genetic modifiers can alter convergent signaling pathways and lead to impaired neural circuitry formation. Lastly, we review sex-linked modifiers and clinical implications. Further understanding of these mechanisms is crucial for both comprehending ASD and for developing novel therapies.

sheet.es: Si te preguntas si la genética explica a tu hijo o hija: esta revisión sugiere que no hay una sola respuesta. Los genes influyen, pero no determinan por sí solos cómo es cada persona autista. Puedes hablar con un profesional de genética si tienes dudas concretas. Es una revisión que resume estudios previos; describe cientos de genes implicados, que según el resumen solo explican 10-20% de los casos. Sus límites: es un texto sobre mecanismos biológicos, no ofrece pautas para el día a día, y no vale como regla para todas las personas. Las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If you wonder whether genetics explains your child: this review suggests there is no single answer. Genes play a part, but they do not alone determine what each autistic person is like. If you have specific questions, a genetics professional can talk them through with you. This is a review summarising earlier studies; it describes hundreds of genes involved, which the abstract says account for only 10-20% of cases. Its limits: it covers biological mechanisms, gives no day-to-day guidance, and is not a rule for every person. Medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om du undrar om genetiken förklarar ditt barn: den här översikten tyder på att det inte finns ett enda svar. Gener spelar roll, men avgör inte ensamma hur varje autistisk person är. Har du konkreta frågor kan du prata med en genetikexpert. Det är en översikt som sammanfattar tidigare studier; den beskriver hundratals gener, som enligt sammanfattningen bara står för 10-20% av fallen. Begränsningar: den handlar om biologiska mekanismer, ger inga råd för vardagen och är ingen regel för alla. Medicinska beslut hör hemma hos en läkare.

title: Eating as an autistic adult: An exploratory qualitative study.
authors: Kinnaird E, Norton C, Pimblett C, Stewart C, Tchanturia K
abstract: Background Although eating difficulties are known to be common in children on the autism spectrum, there is a lack of research on whether these behaviours persist or change into adulthood. Emerging evidence suggests that autistic adults may experience higher levels of disordered eating than the general population, indicating the impact of autism on eating in this adult population warrants further exploration. Method This study interviewed 12 autistic adults about their eating habits, with a focus on the continuing or changing presence of behaviours often seen in autistic children such as sensory sensitivity or a preference for routines. Interviews were transcribed and analysed using thematic analysis. Results Overall, participants suggested that autism did continue to impact their eating into adulthood, particularly in the areas of sensory sensitivity, medical difficulties, executive functioning difficulties, and rigidity, but that they had learned to adapt so that these issues no longer represented a problem. However, a minority of participants did feel that their autism had a negative effect on their eating, particularly those diagnosed with eating disorders. Additionally, eating behaviours associated with autism were identified as potentially contributing to having an unhealthy body weight. Conclusions Certain traits associated with autism, such as cognitive rigidity and sensory sensitivity, could potentially continue to influence the eating behaviours of autistic adults. These traits are typically experienced as differences which can be adapted around and managed, rather than specific problems. However, these traits can potentially contribute to difficulties such as disordered eating and weight gain, and the implications of these should be explored by future research.

sheet.es: Si la persona autista que acompañas es adulta, sus diferencias al comer (sensibilidad a texturas u olores, preferencia por rutinas, dificultad para planificar comidas) pueden seguir presentes, y muchas personas aprenden estrategias propias que funcionan. Pregunta qué le ayuda: comidas seguras, menús repetidos, preparación sencilla. Respeta esas adaptaciones y presta atención, sin alarmarte, si comer le causa malestar o cambios de peso; ahí puede valer la pena buscar apoyo profesional. La evidencia viene de entrevistas cualitativas con 12 adultos autistas que describieron su experiencia. Es un grupo pequeño y exploratorio, así que no representa a todas las personas autistas ni mide causas.
sheet.en: If the autistic person you support is an adult, their eating differences (sensitivity to textures or smells, preference for routines, difficulty planning meals) may still be present, and many people develop their own strategies that work. Ask what helps: safe foods, repeated menus, simple preparation. Respect those adaptations, and calmly notice if eating causes distress or weight changes; that may be a moment to seek professional support. The evidence comes from qualitative interviews with 12 autistic adults describing their own experiences. It is a small, exploratory group, so it does not represent all autistic people or measure causes.
sheet.sv: Om den autistiska person du stöttar är vuxen kan skillnader kring mat (känslighet för konsistens eller lukt, behov av rutiner, svårt att planera måltider) finnas kvar, och många hittar egna strategier som fungerar. Fråga vad som hjälper: trygga livsmedel, återkommande menyer, enkel matlagning. Respektera anpassningarna och var lugnt uppmärksam om ätandet orsakar obehag eller viktförändringar; då kan professionellt stöd vara värt att söka. Underlaget kommer från kvalitativa intervjuer med 12 autistiska vuxna om deras egna erfarenheter. Gruppen är liten och studien utforskande, så den representerar inte alla autistiska personer och mäter inte orsaker.

title: Association of Cesarean Delivery With Risk of Neurodevelopmental and Psychiatric Disorders in the Offspring: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
authors: Zhang T, Sidorchuk A, Sevilla-Cermeño L, Vilaplana-Pérez A, Chang Z, Larsson H, Mataix-Cols D, Fernández de la Cruz L
abstract: Importance Birth by cesarean delivery is increasing globally, particularly cesarean deliveries without medical indication. Children born via cesarean delivery may have an increased risk of negative health outcomes, but the evidence for psychiatric disorders is incomplete. Objective To evaluate the association between cesarean delivery and risk of neurodevelopmental and psychiatric disorders in the offspring. Data sources Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and PsycINFO were searched from inception to December 19, 2018. Search terms included all main mental disorders in the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (Fifth Edition). Study selection Two researchers independently selected observational studies that examined the association between cesarean delivery and neurodevelopmental and psychiatric disorders in the offspring. Data extraction and synthesis Two researchers independently extracted data according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses (PRISMA) and Meta-analysis of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (MOOSE) reporting guidelines and assessed study quality using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Random-effects meta-analyses were used to pool odds ratios (ORs) with 95% CIs for each outcome. Sensitivity and influence analyses tested the robustness of the results. Main outcomes and measures The ORs for the offspring with any neurodevelopmental or psychiatric disorder who were born via cesarean delivery compared with those were born via vaginal delivery. Results A total of 6953 articles were identified, of which 61 studies comprising 67 independent samples were included, totaling 20 607 935 deliveries. Compared with offspring born by vaginal delivery, offspring born via cesarean delivery had increased odds of autism spectrum disorders (OR, 1.33; 95% CI, 1.25-1.41; I2 = 69.5%) and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (OR, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.07-1.26; I2 = 79.2%). Estimates were less precise for intellectual disabilities (OR, 1.83; 95% CI, 0.90-3.70; I2 = 88.2%), obsessive-compulsive disorder (OR, 1.49; 95% CI, 0.87-2.56; I2 = 67.3%), tic disorders (OR, 1.31; 95% CI, 0.98-1.76; I2 = 75.6%), and eating disorders (OR, 1.18; 95% CI, 0.96-1.47; I2 = 92.7%). No significant associations were found with depression/affective psychoses or nonaffective psychoses. Estimates were comparable for emergency and elective cesarean delivery. Study quality was high for 82% of the cohort studies and 50% of the case-control studies. Conclusions and relevance The findings suggest that cesarean delivery births are associated with an increased risk of autism spectrum disorder and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, irrespective of cesarean delivery modality, compared with vaginal delivery. Future studies on the mechanisms behind these associations appear to be warranted.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija nació por cesárea, no hay nada que corregir ni de lo que culparse: esta información no cambia cómo acompañarle hoy. Lo útil es seguir atendiendo sus necesidades y apoyos. La evidencia es un metaanálisis de estudios observacionales, con 61 estudios y 20 607 935 partos, que encontró una asociación entre cesárea y autismo (OR, 1.33) y TDAH (OR, 1.17). Sus límites: una asociación no prueba que la cesárea cause autismo o TDAH, los resultados variaron mucho entre estudios y no sirven para predecir a una persona concreta. Las decisiones sobre el parto son de cada familia y su equipo médico.
sheet.en: If your child was born by cesarean, there is nothing to fix and nothing to blame yourself for: this finding does not change how you support them today. What helps is continuing to respond to their needs and supports. The evidence is a meta-analysis of observational studies, with 61 studies and 20 607 935 deliveries, which found an association between cesarean birth and autism (OR, 1.33) and ADHD (OR, 1.17). Its limits: an association does not show that cesarean delivery causes autism or ADHD, results varied a lot between studies, and they cannot predict any one person. Decisions about birth belong to each family and their medical team.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn föddes med kejsarsnitt finns inget att rätta till och inget att skuldbelägga sig för: resultatet ändrar inte hur du stöttar barnet idag. Det som hjälper är att fortsätta möta barnets behov och ge stöd. Underlaget är en metaanalys av observationsstudier, med 61 studier och 20 607 935 förlossningar, som fann ett samband mellan kejsarsnitt och autism (OR, 1.33) samt ADHD (OR, 1.17). Begränsningar: ett samband visar inte att kejsarsnitt orsakar autism eller ADHD, resultaten varierade mycket mellan studier och säger inget om en enskild person. Beslut om förlossning fattas av varje familj tillsammans med vården.

title: The Role of Gut Microbiota in Gastrointestinal Symptoms of Children with ASD.
authors: Martínez-González AE, Andreo-Martínez P
abstract: Background and objectives : Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by impaired communication, social interaction disorder, and repetitive behavior. Dysbiotic gut microbiota (GM) could be a contributing factor to the appearance of ASD, as gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms are comorbidities frequently reported in ASD. As there is a lack of reviews about the role played by GM in the GI symptoms of ASD, this work aimed to carry out a systematic review of current studies comparing the GM of children with ASD and GI symptoms with those of healthy controls in the last six years. Materials and Methods: The systematic review was performed following the PRISMA guidelines. The databases chosen were Web of Science, Scopus, PubMed, and PsycINFO, and the keywords were (gut* OR intestine* OR bowel* OR gastrointestinal*) AND (microbiota* OR microflora* OR bacteria* OR microbiome* OR flora* OR bacterial* OR bacteria* OR microorganism* OR feces* OR stool*) AND (autistic* OR autism* OR ASD*). Results : A total of 16 articles were included. Ten articles performed correlations analysis between GI symptoms and ASD. Among those 10 articles, 7 found differences between the GI symptoms present in children with ASD and healthy controls. The most common GI symptom was constipation. Among the seven articles that found differences, three performed correlations analysis between GI symptoms and gut microbe abundance. Candida , Prevotella , Streptococcus , and Veillonella showed higher and lower abundance, respectively, in children with ASD and GI symptoms in more than one article. Bacteroidetes , Firmicutes , Actinomyces , Dorea , Lactobacillus , Faecalibacterium prausnitzii , and Bacteroidetes / Firmicutes ratios showed abundance discrepancies. Conclusions : It is still too early to draw a conclusion about the gut microbes involved in GI symptoms of ASD. Future research should consider the relationship between ASD behavior, GM, and GI symptoms in a multidisciplinary way and homogenize sample characteristics.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo autista tiene molestias de tripa, como estreñimiento, tómalas en serio y coméntalas con su pediatra o equipo médico; no hace falta esperar a que la ciencia aclare el papel de las bacterias intestinales. Anota cuándo aparecen y cómo son. Esta revisión sistemática analizó 16 artículos que comparaban la microbiota intestinal de niños autistas con síntomas digestivos con la de niños sin autismo. El síntoma más común fue el estreñimiento. Sus límites: los resultados fueron inconsistentes entre estudios y los autores concluyen que aún es pronto para sacar conclusiones sobre qué microbios intervienen. No sirve como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If your autistic child has tummy troubles such as constipation, take them seriously and raise them with a paediatrician or medical team; there is no need to wait for science to settle the role of gut bacteria. Note when symptoms appear and what they look like. This systematic review looked at 16 articles comparing the gut microbiota of autistic children with digestive symptoms to that of children without autism. The most common symptom was constipation. Limits: results were inconsistent across studies, and the authors conclude it is still too early to say which microbes are involved. It is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn har magproblem, till exempel förstoppning, ta dem på allvar och ta upp dem med barnläkare eller vårdteam; du behöver inte vänta på att forskningen klarlagt tarmbakteriernas roll. Anteckna när symtomen uppstår och hur de ser ut. Den här systematiska översikten gick igenom 16 artiklar som jämförde tarmfloran hos autistiska barn med magsymtom och hos barn utan autism. Det vanligaste symtomet var förstoppning. Begränsningar: resultaten skilde sig mellan studierna, och författarna menar att det ännu är för tidigt att säga vilka mikrober som är inblandade. Det gäller inte som regel för varje person.

title: 'People should be allowed to do what they like': Autistic adults' views and experiences of stimming.
authors: Kapp SK, Steward R, Crane L, Elliott D, Elphick C, Pellicano E, Russell G
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: 'Stereotyped or repetitive motor movements' are characterised as core features in the diagnosis of autism, yet many autistic adults (and the neurodiversity movement) have reclaimed them as 'stimming'. Supported by a growing body of scientific research, autistic adults argue that these behaviours may serve as useful coping mechanisms, yet little research has examined stimming from the perspective of autistic adults. Through interviews and focus groups, we asked 32 autistic adults to share their perceptions and experiences of stimming, including the reasons they stim, any value doing so may hold for them and their perceptions of others' reactions to stimming. Using thematic analysis, we identified two themes: stimming as (1) a self-regulatory mechanism and (2) lacking in social acceptance, but can become accepted through understanding. Autistic adults highlighted the importance of stimming as an adaptive mechanism that helps them to soothe or communicate intense emotions or thoughts and thus objected to treatment that aims to eliminate the behaviour.

sheet.es: Mañana, si tu familiar se balancea, aletea o repite sonidos, prueba a no interrumpirlo: para muchas personas autistas el stimming ayuda a calmarse o a expresar emociones intensas. Observa qué le aporta y, si un stim causa daño, busquen juntos alternativas en lugar de eliminarlo. Explicar a otras personas qué es el stimming puede reducir miradas y juicios. La evidencia: entrevistas y grupos de discusión con 32 adultos autistas, que describieron el stimming como autorregulación y rechazaron tratamientos para suprimirlo. Límites: es un estudio cualitativo y pequeño, con adultos que pudieron hablar de su experiencia; puede no reflejar a niños ni a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: Tomorrow, if your family member rocks, flaps or repeats sounds, try not to stop them: for many autistic people, stimming helps them calm down or express intense feelings. Notice what it gives them, and if a stim causes harm, look for alternatives together rather than removing it. Explaining stimming to others can reduce stares and judgement. The evidence: interviews and focus groups with 32 autistic adults, who described stimming as self-regulation and objected to treatments aimed at eliminating it. Limits: this is a small qualitative study of adults able to talk about their experiences; it may not reflect children or every autistic person.
sheet.sv: I morgon, om din närstående gungar, flaxar eller upprepar ljud, försök att inte avbryta: för många autistiska personer hjälper stimming dem att lugna sig eller uttrycka starka känslor. Lägg märke till vad det ger, och om en stim orsakar skada, sök alternativ tillsammans i stället för att ta bort den. Att förklara stimming för andra kan minska blickar och dömande. Evidensen: intervjuer och fokusgrupper med 32 autistiska vuxna, som beskrev stimming som självreglering och motsatte sig behandling som syftar till att få bort den. Begränsningar: en liten kvalitativ studie med vuxna som kunde berätta om sina erfarenheter; den speglar kanske inte barn eller alla autistiska personer.

claim.es: Adultos autistas describen el stimming (movimientos repetitivos) como una forma de regularse ante sobrecarga; suprimirlo hace daño.
claim.en: Autistic adults describe stimming (repetitive movement) as a way to self-regulate under overload; suppressing it is harmful.
claim.sv: Autistiska vuxna beskriver stimming (repetitiva rörelser) som ett sätt att reglera sig vid överbelastning; att stoppa det skadar.

supports.es: Dejar espacio a la autorregulación en vez de «manos quietas».
supports.en: Leaving room for self-regulation instead of 'quiet hands'.
supports.sv: Att ge utrymme för självreglering i stället för «stilla händer».

doesNotSupport.es: Ignorar movimientos que lesionan a la persona; la seguridad sigue siendo lo primero.
doesNotSupport.en: Ignoring movement that injures the person; safety still comes first.
doesNotSupport.sv: Att ignorera rörelser som skadar personen; säkerheten kommer fortfarande först.

title: Inside, outside and in-between: The process and impact of co-producing knowledge about autism in a UK Somali community.
authors: Aabe NO, Fox F, Rai D, Redwood S
journal: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy
abstract: Background Co-production is predicated on equal power-sharing and responsibility in research partnerships. However, relatively few accounts exist that explore the subjective experience of how co-researchers achieve such equality, from the perspectives of public contributors and researchers. Aim This paper aims to provide a unique insight into the process of co-production, by weaving personal reflections with principles to evaluate the impact arising from co-produced knowledge. It is based upon participatory research that was initiated by a 'lay' person, on behalf of a community organization, seeking support for Somali families who are affected by autism. The paper explores the evolving partnerships that began with community theatre and qualitative research and leading to extensive dissemination and impact, all of which has been jointly owned and negotiated by the co-researchers and community organizations. Discussion Initially, this paper reflects on the process, drawing on principles defined for co-production in health research and combining it with the co-researcher's personal reflections of their experiences as insiders and outsiders, stepping in and out of each other's worlds. The value of reciprocity, flexibility and continuous reflection is illustrated. The latter part of the paper explores the impact of this co-produced knowledge using a theoretical framework, to assess the specific impacts and its broader transformative potential. It demonstrates how (1) opportunities for all partners to be equitably involved to the maximum degree possible throughout the research process can affect social change and (2) co-produced research can become a catalyst that is dynamic and complex, achieving multi-layered impact.

sheet.es: Si trabaja con una comunidad o un grupo de familias, incluya desde el principio a las personas implicadas como socias con el mismo poder de decisión, y deje espacio para la flexibilidad y la reflexión continua. Este artículo es un relato reflexivo sobre una investigación participativa en una comunidad somalí del Reino Unido, iniciada por una persona no investigadora en nombre de una organización comunitaria que buscaba apoyo para familias somalíes afectadas por el autismo. Comenzó con teatro comunitario e investigación cualitativa. Sus límites: es una experiencia concreta, basada en reflexiones personales, y no demuestra que el mismo camino funcione igual en otras comunidades o familias.
sheet.en: If you work with a community or a group of families, involve the people concerned from the start as partners with equal decision-making power, and leave room for flexibility and ongoing reflection. This paper is a reflective account of participatory research in a UK Somali community, started by a non-researcher on behalf of a community organisation seeking support for Somali families affected by autism. It began with community theatre and qualitative research. Its limits: it describes one specific experience based on personal reflections, and it does not show that the same approach will work the same way in other communities or families.
sheet.sv: Om du arbetar med en gemenskap eller en grupp familjer, involvera de berörda från början som jämlika partner med lika beslutsmakt, och lämna utrymme för flexibilitet och fortlöpande reflektion. Artikeln är en reflekterande beskrivning av deltagande forskning i en somalisk gemenskap i Storbritannien, som startades av en person utan forskarbakgrund för en lokal organisation som sökte stöd till somaliska familjer berörda av autism. Den började med gemenskapsteater och kvalitativ forskning. Begränsningar: den beskriver en enskild erfarenhet byggd på personliga reflektioner och visar inte att samma arbetssätt fungerar likadant i andra gemenskaper eller familjer.

title: Is There a Link Between Autistic People Being Perceived Unfavorably and Having a Mind That Is Difficult to Read?
authors: Alkhaldi RS, Sheppard E, Mitchell P
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: The link between autistic people having a mind that is difficult to read (by neurotypical participants) and being perceived unfavorably was investigated. Videoed Autistic and neurotypical targets from Sheppard et al. (PLOS ONE 7(11):e49859, 2016) were scored for how readable they were when reacting to a distinctive greeting from the experimenter. These videos were presented to new groups of perceivers (neurotypical adults) who rated neurotypical targets more socially favorably than autistic targets irrespective of whether details of the experimenter's greeting were concealed (Study 1) or disclosed (Study 2). Target readability correlated with ratings of target favorability (r = .58 and r = .63), independent of target diagnosis. Perceivers might rate targets unfavorably because they experience difficulty reading them, though other interpretations of the correlation are also possible.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista a veces recibe una impresión social más negativa, puede deberse en parte a que a otras personas les cuesta interpretar su expresión, no a que haya algo malo en ella. Tras un saludo poco habitual, se grabó en vídeo a personas autistas y neurotípicas. Adultos neurotípicos las valoraron y puntuaron mejor a las neurotípicas. Cuanto más fácil era leer a alguien, mejor lo valoraban (r = .58 y r = .63), con independencia del diagnóstico. Es un estudio con personas autistas y adultos neurotípicos, y la relación admite otras explicaciones. No vale como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person sometimes gets a less favourable social impression, part of the reason may be that others find their expressions hard to read, not that something is wrong with them. Autistic and neurotypical people were videoed reacting to an unusual greeting. Neurotypical adults rated them, and gave neurotypical people more favourable ratings. The easier someone was to read, the more favourably they were rated (r = .58 and r = .63), whatever their diagnosis. This is a study with autistic people and neurotypical adult raters, and the link has other possible explanations. It is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person ibland får ett mindre gynnsamt socialt intryck kan det delvis bero på att andra har svårt att tolka uttrycken, inte på att något är fel på personen. Autistiska och neurotypiska personer filmades när de reagerade på en ovanlig hälsning. Neurotypiska vuxna bedömde dem och gav neurotypiska personer mer gynnsamma omdömen. Ju lättare någon var att läsa, desto mer gynnsamt bedömdes personen (r = .58 och r = .63), oavsett diagnos. Det är en studie med autistiska personer och neurotypiska vuxna bedömare, och sambandet kan ha andra förklaringar. Det är ingen regel för alla.

title: Comparing Intellectual and Memory Abilities of Older Autistic Adults with Typically Developing Older Adults Using WAIS-IV and WMS-IV.
authors: Tse VWS, Crabtree J, Islam S, Stott J
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: This study aimed to compare cognitive and memory abilities between older adults with and without autism over the age of 50. Twenty-eight individuals with autism and 29 typically developing (TD) older adults took part in the current study. Participants' cognitive and memory abilities were assessed by WAIS-IV and WMS-IV. Older autistic adults were found to have poorer performance in processing speed and visual working memory, but they performed at a similar level as TD controls in all other domains. Poorer processing speed and visual working memory are also often found to be associated with age-related decline in neurotypical adults. Longitudinal studies are warranted to explore how the combination of ageing and autism affects cognitive functioning in older adults.

sheet.es: Con personas autistas mayores, conviene dar más tiempo para procesar la información y apoyar la memoria visual: instrucciones escritas, pausas y no exigir respuestas rápidas. Es un estudio con 28 adultos autistas y 29 adultos mayores no autistas, todos de más de 50 años, evaluados con pruebas de capacidad intelectual y memoria. Las personas autistas rindieron peor en velocidad de procesamiento y memoria de trabajo visual, y de forma similar en los demás ámbitos. Es un grupo pequeño, mide un solo momento y no muestra cómo evoluciona cada persona con la edad; cada persona es distinta.
sheet.en: With older autistic people, it may help to allow extra time to process information and to support visual memory: written instructions, pauses, and no pressure for quick answers. This study compared 28 autistic adults and 29 typically developing older adults, all over 50, using tests of intellectual ability and memory. The autistic adults scored lower in processing speed and visual working memory, and similarly in all other areas. The group was small, it looked at one point in time, and it cannot show how each person changes with age. Every person is different.
sheet.sv: När du stöttar äldre autistiska personer kan det hjälpa att ge extra tid att bearbeta information och stödja det visuella minnet: skriftliga instruktioner, pauser och inga krav på snabba svar. Studien jämförde 28 autistiska vuxna och 29 typiskt utvecklade äldre vuxna, alla över 50 år, med tester av intellektuell förmåga och minne. De autistiska vuxna presterade sämre på bearbetningshastighet och visuellt arbetsminne, och likvärdigt inom övriga områden. Gruppen var liten, studien mätte vid ett tillfälle och visar inte hur varje person förändras med åldern. Alla är olika.

title: Does Theory of Mind Training Enhance Empathy in Autism?
authors: Holopainen A, de Veld DMJ, Hoddenbach E, Begeer S
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Youth with ASD often show limited or atypical empathic responsiveness. The direct effects of social skills interventions on enhancing empathic responsiveness is unknown. Data from a randomized controlled trial were used to investigate whether a Theory of Mind training improves the empathic responsiveness, measured through structured observations. The current study included a large sample (n = 135) of 8-13-year-old children with ASD. When comparing the change scores of empathic responsiveness from baseline to post-test, the intervention group performed significantly better than the waitlist group. Thus, the current findings support the use of Theory of Mind training as intervention of ASD by showing its efficacy also in improving one's empathic responsiveness, in addition to previous knowledge regarding the improvements in empathic understanding.

sheet.es: Si valoras un programa que trabaje la comprensión de los pensamientos y sentimientos ajenos, este estudio sugiere que puede ayudar a algunos niños autistas a responder con más empatía en situaciones sociales. Es un ensayo aleatorizado con 135 niños autistas de 8-13 años; quienes hicieron el entrenamiento mejoraron más que los de lista de espera, según observaciones estructuradas. Sus límites: muestra solo una medida de empatía y un grupo de edad, no dice cómo les fue a cada niño ni si el cambio mejora su bienestar, y no sirve como regla para todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If you are considering a program that builds understanding of other people's thoughts and feelings, this study suggests it may help some autistic children respond more empathically in social situations.
