abstract: The prevalence of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) has increased dramatically in recent decades, supporting the claim of an autism epidemic. Systematic monitoring of ASD allows estimating prevalence and identifying potential sources of variation over time and geographical areas. At present, ASD prevalence estimates are available worldwide, coming either from surveillance systems using existing health and educational databases or from population studies specifically performed. In the present article, we present a review of the ASD prevalence estimates published since 2014. Data confirm a high variability in prevalence across the world, likely due to methodological differences in case detection, and the consistent increase of prevalence estimates within each geographical area.

sheet.es: Si te preguntas por qué las cifras de autismo varían tanto entre países, esta revisión ayuda: las diferencias dependen mucho de cómo se identifica a las personas autistas. Conviene mirar cada cifra con cautela y recordar que reconocer el autismo ayuda a facilitar apoyos y acceso a servicios. Es una revisión de estimaciones de prevalencia publicadas desde 2014 en todo el mundo. Los autores señalan una gran variabilidad y un aumento constante de las estimaciones en cada zona geográfica. Como límite, esa variabilidad probablemente se debe a diferencias de método, y la revisión no explica por qué suben las cifras ni dice nada sobre una persona concreta.
sheet.en: If you wonder why autism figures differ so much between countries, this review helps: the differences seem to depend a lot on how autistic people are identified. It is worth reading any single number with care, and remembering that recognising autism helps make support and services easier to reach. This is a review of prevalence estimates published worldwide since 2014. The authors report high variability and a consistent rise in estimates within each geographical area. As a limit, the variability is likely due to differences in methods, and the review does not explain why estimates rise or say anything about one particular person.
sheet.sv: Om du undrar varför siffrorna för autism skiljer sig så mycket mellan länder kan den här översikten hjälpa: skillnaderna verkar bero mycket på hur autistiska personer identifieras. Det är klokt att läsa varje enskild siffra med försiktighet och minnas att ett erkännande av autism kan göra stöd och tjänster lättare att nå. Det är en översikt av prevalensskattningar som publicerats i världen sedan 2014. Författarna beskriver stor variation och en jämn ökning av skattningarna inom varje geografiskt område. En begränsning är att variationen sannolikt beror på olika metoder, och översikten förklarar inte varför siffrorna ökar eller säger något om en enskild person.

title: The Sensory Abnormalities and Neuropsychopathology of Autism and Anxiety.
authors: Gara SK, Chhetri AG, Alrjoob M, Abbasi SAA, Rutkofsky IH
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a developmental disorder of interpersonal communications and restricted interest and deficits in sensory and social interactions. It co-occurs with anxiety and mostly in 30% of cases related to specific phobia. This review article summarises the sensory association between anxiety and ASD. The role of emotions and neurobiology discussed and sensory over-reactivity (SOR) was related to ASD and anxiety. PubMed database systematically searched for related articles on ASD and anxiety. The keywords used are autism spectrum disorder, autism spectrum disorder and emotion, anxiety disorder, sensory in autism and anxiety, and psychopathology. The results were most significant and related to the sensory association between ASD and anxiety. Out of 19 studies discussed, there were eight systematic reviews with meta-analysis, seven systematic reviews, three traditional reviews, and one included both systematic reviews with randomized controlled trials (RCTs). However, due to possible limitations and considerations, like small sample size and few clinical trials; hence, further recommendations to randomized clinical trials and cohort studies warranted. This review article helps scientists to plan and focus on necessary studies and possible screening for the disease to improve possible clinical outcomes. People gain awareness of the disease. Early recognition, as well as educational, behavioral, and family therapy, might decrease symptoms and support learning and development in children.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista parece ansiosa, conviene fijarse también en lo sensorial: ruidos, luces, texturas o multitudes pueden influir. Anotar qué situaciones le abruman y ajustar el entorno puede ayudar, y un profesional puede orientar más. La evidencia es una revisión de 19 estudios, casi todos revisiones previas, que relaciona la ansiedad y la sobrerreactividad sensorial en el autismo. Sus límites: muestras pequeñas y pocos ensayos clínicos, así que no sirve como regla para cada persona y hacen falta más estudios.
sheet.en: If an autistic person seems anxious, it is worth looking at the sensory side too: noises, lights, textures or crowds may play a part. Noting which situations overwhelm them and adjusting the environment may help, and a professional can guide you further. The evidence is a review of 19 studies, mostly earlier reviews, linking anxiety and sensory over-reactivity in autism. Its limits: small samples and few clinical trials, so it is not a rule for every person and more research is needed.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person verkar ängslig är det värt att också titta på det sensoriska: ljud, ljus, material eller folksamlingar kan spela in. Att anteckna vilka situationer som överväldigar och anpassa miljön kan hjälpa, och en yrkesperson kan ge mer vägledning. Underlaget är en översikt av 19 studier, mest tidigare översikter, som kopplar ångest och sensorisk överreaktivitet vid autism. Begränsningar: små urval och få kliniska studier, så den gäller inte som regel för alla och mer forskning behövs.

title: Autism Spectrum Social Stories In Schools Trial 2 (ASSSIST2): study protocol for a randomised controlled trial analysing clinical and cost-effectiveness of Social Stories™ in primary schools.
authors: Wright B, Teige C, Watson J, Hodkinson R, Marshall D, Varley D, Allgar V, Mandefield L, Parrott S, Kingsley E, Hargate R, Mitchell N, Ali S, McMillan D, Wang H, Hewitt C
abstract: Background Interventions designed to support children with a diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Conditions (ASC) can be time consuming, needing involvement of outside experts. Social Stories™ are a highly personalised intervention aiming to give children with ASC social information or describing an otherwise difficult situation or skill. This can be delivered daily by staff in education settings. Studies examining Social Story™ use have yielded mostly positive results but have largely been single case studies with a lack of randomised controlled trials (RCTs). Despite this numerous schools are utilising Social Stories™, and a fully powered RCT is timely. Methods A multi-site pragmatic cluster RCT comparing care as usual with Social Stories™ and care as usual. This study will recruit 278 participants (aged 4-11) with a clinical diagnosis of ASC, currently attending primary school in the North of England. Approximately 278 school based staff will be recruited to provide school based information about participating children with approximately 140 recruited to deliver the intervention. The study will be cluster randomised by school. Potential participants will be screened for eligibility prior to giving informed consent. Follow up data will be collected at 6 weeks and 6 months post randomisation and will assess changes in participants' social responsiveness, goal based outcomes, social and emotional health. The primary outcome measure is the Social Responsiveness Scale Second Edition (SRS-2) completed by school based staff at 6 months. Approvals have been obtained from the University of York's Research Governance Committee, Research Ethics Committee and the Health Research Authority. Study results will be submitted for publication in peer-reviewed journals and disseminated to participating families, educational staff, local authority representatives, community groups and Patient and Participant Involvement representatives. Suggestions will be made to NICE about treatment evidence dependent on findings. Discussion This study addresses a much used but currently under researched intervention and results will inform school based support for primary school children with a diagnosis of ASC. Trial registration The trial is registered on the ISRCTN registry (registration number: ISRCTN11634810). The trial was retrospectively registered on 23rd April 2019.

sheet.es: Si un niño autista en primaria se enfrenta a una situación social difícil, el personal escolar puede probar una Historia Social™: un texto muy personalizado que explica la situación o una habilidad. Conviene observar cómo responde cada niño y comentarlo con el colegio. Este es el protocolo de un ensayo aleatorizado que aún no da resultados: planea reclutar a 278 niños de 4-11 años con diagnóstico de autismo en escuelas del norte de Inglaterra y comparar la atención habitual con la atención habitual más Historias Sociales™. Límite: al ser un protocolo, no sabemos todavía si funcionan, y los resultados pueden no valer para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic primary school child finds a social situation hard, school staff can try a Social Story™: a highly personalised text that explains the situation or a skill. Watch how your child responds and talk it through with the school. This is the protocol of a randomised trial, so it has no results yet. It plans to recruit 278 children aged 4-11 with an autism diagnosis in schools in the North of England, comparing usual care with usual care plus Social Stories™. Limit: as a protocol, it cannot yet tell us whether Social Stories™ work, and findings may not apply to every child.
sheet.sv: Om ett autistiskt barn i grundskolan har svårt med en social situation kan skolans personal prova en Social Story™: en mycket personligt anpassad text som förklarar situationen eller en färdighet. Se hur ditt barn reagerar och prata med skolan. Detta är protokollet för en randomiserad studie och har därför inga resultat än. Den planerar att rekrytera 278 barn i åldern 4-11 med autismdiagnos i skolor i norra England och jämföra vanligt stöd med vanligt stöd plus Social Stories™. Begränsning: ett protokoll kan ännu inte visa om metoden fungerar, och resultaten gäller kanske inte alla barn.

title: Simulation-Based Education for Staff Managing Aggression and Externalizing Behaviors in Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder in the Hospital Setting: Pilot and Feasibility Study Protocol for a Cluster Randomized Controlled Trial.
authors: Mitchell MJ, Newall FH, Sokol J, Williams KJ
abstract: Background Children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) frequently demonstrate aggression and externalizing behaviors in the acute care hospital environment. Pediatric acute care nursing staff are often not trained in managing aggression and, in particular, lack confidence in preventing and managing externalizing behaviors in children with ASD. High-fidelity simulation exercises will be used in this study to provide deliberate practice for acute care pediatric nursing staff in the management of aggressive and externalizing behaviors. Objective The purpose of this study is to conduct a pilot and feasibility cluster randomized controlled trial (RCT) to evaluate the effectiveness of simulation-based education for staff in managing aggression and externalizing behaviors of children with ASD in the hospital setting. Methods This study has a mixed design, with between-group and within-participant comparisons to explore the acceptability and feasibility of delivering a large-scale cluster RCT. The trial process, including recruitment, completion rates, contamination, and completion of outcome measures, will be assessed and reported as percentages. This study will assess the acceptability of the simulation-based training format for two scenarios involving an adolescent with autism, with or without intellectual disability, who displays aggressive and externalizing behaviors and the resulting change in confidence in managing clinical aggression. Two pediatric wards of similar size and patient complexity will be selected to participate in the study; they will be randomized to receive either simulation-based education plus web-based educational materials or the web-based educational materials only. Change in confidence will be assessed using pre- and posttraining surveys for bedside nursing staff exposed to the training and the control group who will receive the web-based training materials. Knowledge retention 3 months posttraining, as well as continued confidence and exposure to clinical aggression, will be assessed via surveys. Changes in confidence and competence will be compared statistically with the chi-square test using before-and-after data to compare the proportion of those who have high confidence between the two arms at baseline and at follow-up. The simulation-based education will be recorded with trained assessors reviewing participants' abilities to de-escalate aggressive behaviors using a validated tool. This data will be analyzed using mean values and SDs to understand the variation in performance of individuals who undertake the training. Data from each participating ward will be collected during each shift for the duration of the study to assess the number of aggressive incidents and successful de-escalation for patients with ASD. Total change in Code Grey activations will also be assessed, with both datasets analyzed using descriptive statistics. Results This study gained ethical approval from The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne Human Research Ethics Committee (HREC) on November 1, 2019 (HREC reference number: 56684). Data collection was completed in February 2020. Data analysis is due to commence with results anticipated by August 2020. Conclusions We hypothesize that this study is feasible to be conducted as a cluster RCT and that simulation-based training will be acceptable for acute care pediatric nurses. We anticipate that the intervention ward will have increased confidence in managing clinical aggression in children with ASD immediately and up to 3 months posttraining. Trial registration Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry (ANZCTR) ACTRN12620000139976; http://www.ANZCTR.org.au/ACTRN12620000139976.aspx. International registered report identifier (irrid) DERR1-10.2196/18105.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija autista va a ingresar en un hospital, puede avisar al equipo con antelación de qué le angustia, cómo se comunica y qué le calma, y pedir que lo anoten. Este es un protocolo de un ensayo piloto en un hospital pediátrico de Melbourne: dos plantas recibirán formación con simulaciones más materiales web, o solo materiales web, para ver si el método es viable y si aumenta la confianza del personal de enfermería. Aún no ofrece resultados, así que no demuestra que la formación ayude a las personas autistas, ni sirve como norma para todas.
sheet.en: If your autistic child is going into hospital, you can tell the team beforehand what distresses them, how they communicate and what helps them settle, and ask for it to be written down. This is a protocol for a pilot trial at a children's hospital in Melbourne: two wards will get simulation training plus web materials, or web materials only, to see whether the approach is feasible and raises nursing staff confidence. It reports no results yet, so it does not show that the training helps autistic people, and it is not a rule for everyone.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn ska läggas in på sjukhus kan du i förväg berätta för teamet vad som stressar, hur barnet kommunicerar och vad som hjälper till ro, och be dem skriva ner det. Detta är ett protokoll för en pilotstudie på ett barnsjukhus i Melbourne: två avdelningar får simuleringsträning plus webbmaterial, eller bara webbmaterial, för att se om upplägget går att genomföra och ökar sjuksköterskors trygghet. Inga resultat finns ännu, så studien visar inte att utbildningen hjälper autistiska personer och gäller inte som regel för alla.

title: Role of Neuroinflammation in Autism Spectrum Disorder and the Emergence of Brain Histaminergic System. Lessons Also for BPSD?
authors: Eissa N, Sadeq A, Sasse A, Sadek B
abstract: Many behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia (BPSD) share similarities in executive functioning and communication deficits with those described in several neuropsychiatric disorders, including Alzheimer's disease (AD), epilepsy, schizophrenia (SCH), and autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Numerous studies over the last four decades have documented altered neuroinflammation among individuals diagnosed with ASD. The purpose of this review is to examine the hypothesis that central histamine (HA) plays a significant role in the regulation of neuroinflammatory processes of microglia functions in numerous neuropsychiatric diseases, i.e., ASD, AD, SCH, and BPSD. In addition, this review summarizes the latest preclinical and clinical results that support the relevance of histamine H1-, H2-, and H3-receptor antagonists for the potential clinical use in ASD, SCH, AD, epilepsy, and BPSD, based on the substantial symptomatic overlap between these disorders with regards to cognitive dysfunction. The review focuses on the histaminergic neurotransmission as relevant in these brain disorders, as well as the effects of a variety of H3R antagonists in animal models and in clinical studies.

sheet.es: Esta revisión no ofrece nada que cambiar mañana en casa; es investigación biológica temprana. Si la inflamación o la medicación le preocupan, consulte a un profesional clínico, porque las decisiones médicas le corresponden a él. Evidencia: es una revisión de la literatura que reúne estudios en animales y estudios clínicos sobre la histamina cerebral y la neuroinflamación en el autismo y otras condiciones, como el alzhéimer. Límites: es una hipótesis, mezcla condiciones distintas, no prueba que ayude a ninguna persona autista y no sirve como regla general.
sheet.en: This review offers nothing to change at home tomorrow; it is early biological research. If inflammation or medication worries you, talk with a clinician, because medical decisions belong to them. Evidence: it is a literature review gathering animal studies and clinical studies on brain histamine and neuroinflammation in autism and other conditions, such as Alzheimer's disease. Limits: it presents a hypothesis, mixes different conditions, does not show that anything helps any autistic person, and should not be read as a rule for everyone.
sheet.sv: Den här översikten ger inget du behöver ändra hemma i morgon; det är tidig biologisk forskning. Om inflammation eller medicin oroar dig, prata med en läkare, eftersom medicinska beslut hör till vården. Evidens: det är en litteraturöversikt som samlar djurstudier och kliniska studier om histamin i hjärnan och neuroinflammation vid autism och andra tillstånd, som Alzheimers sjukdom. Begränsningar: den lägger fram en hypotes, blandar olika tillstånd, visar inte att något hjälper någon autistisk person och ska inte läsas som en regel för alla.

title: "Having All of Your Internal Resources Exhausted Beyond Measure and Being Left with No Clean-Up Crew": Defining Autistic Burnout.
authors: Raymaker DM, Teo AR, Steckler NA, Lentz B, Scharer M, Delos Santos A, Kapp SK, Hunter M, Joyce A, Nicolaidis C
abstract: Background: Although autistic adults often discuss experiencing "autistic burnout" and attribute serious negative outcomes to it, the concept is almost completely absent from the academic and clinical literature. Methods: We used a community-based participatory research approach to conduct a thematic analysis of 19 interviews and 19 public Internet sources to understand and characterize autistic burnout. Interview participants were autistic adults who identified as having been professionally diagnosed with an autism spectrum condition. We conducted a thematic analysis, using a hybrid inductive-deductive approach, at semantic and latent levels, through a critical paradigm. We addressed trustworthiness through multiple coders, peer debriefing, and examination of contradictions. Results: Autistic adults described the primary characteristics of autistic burnout as chronic exhaustion, loss of skills, and reduced tolerance to stimulus. They described burnout as happening because of life stressors that added to the cumulative load they experienced, and barriers to support that created an inability to obtain relief from the load. These pressures caused expectations to outweigh abilities resulting in autistic burnout. Autistic adults described negative impacts on their health, capacity for independent living, and quality of life, including suicidal behavior. They also discussed a lack of empathy from neurotypical people and described acceptance and social support, time off/reduced expectations, and doing things in an autistic way/unmasking as associated in their experiences with recovery from autistic burnout. Conclusions: Autistic burnout appears to be a phenomenon distinct from occupational burnout or clinical depression. Better understanding autistic burnout could lead to ways to recognize, relieve, or prevent it, including highlighting the potential dangers of teaching autistic people to mask or camouflage their autistic traits, and including burnout education in suicide prevention programs. These findings highlight the need to reduce discrimination and stigma related to autism and disability. Lay summary Why was this study done?: Autistic burnout is talked about a lot by autistic people but has not been formally addressed by researchers. It is an important issue for the autistic community because it is described as leading to distress; loss of work, school, health, and quality of life; and even suicidal behavior. What was the purpose of this study?: This study aimed to characterize autistic burnout, understand what it is like, what people think causes it, and what helps people recover from or prevent it. It is a first step in starting to understand autistic burnout well enough to address it. What did the researchers do?: Our research group-the Academic Autism Spectrum Partnership in Research and Education-used a community-based participatory research approach with the autistic community in all stages of the study. We analyzed 9 interviews from our study on employment, 10 interviews about autistic burnout, and 19 public Internet sources (five in-depth). We recruited in the United States by publicizing on social media, by word of mouth, and through community connections. When analyzing interviews, we took what people said at face value and in deeper social context, and looked for strong themes across data. What were the results of the study?: The primary characteristics of autistic burnout were chronic exhaustion , loss of skills , and reduced tolerance to stimulus . Participants described burnout as happening because of life stressors that added to the cumulative load they experienced, and barriers to support that created an inability to obtain relief from the load. These pressures caused expectations to outweigh abilities resulting in autistic burnout . From this we created a definition:Autistic burnout is a syndrome conceptualized as resulting from chronic life stress and a mismatch of expectations and abilities without adequate supports. It is characterized by pervasive, long-term (typically 3+ months) exhaustion, loss of function, and reduced tolerance to stimulus.Participants described negative impacts on their lives, including health , capacity for independent living , and quality of life , including suicidal behavior. They also discussed a lack of empathy from neurotypical people. People had ideas for recovering from autistic burnout including acceptance and social support , time off/reduced expectations , and doing things in an autistic way/unmasking . How do these findings add to what was already known?: We now have data that autistic burnout refers to a clear set of characteristics, and is different from workplace burnout and clinical depression. We have the start of a model for why autistic burnout might happen. We know that people have been able to recover from autistic burnout and have some insights into how. What are the potential weaknesses in the study?: This was a small exploratory study with a convenience sample. Although we were able to bring in some diversity by using three data sources, future work would benefit from interviewing a wider range of participants, especially those who are not white, have higher support needs, and have either very high or very low educational attainment. More research is needed to understand how to measure, prevent, and treat autistic burnout. How will these findings help autistic adults now or in the future?: These findings validate the experience of autistic adults. Understanding autistic burnout could lead to ways to help relieve it or prevent it. The findings may help therapists and other practitioners recognize autistic burnout, and the potential dangers of teaching autistic people to mask autistic traits. Suicide prevention programs should consider the potential role of burnout. These findings highlight the need to reduce discrimination and stigma around autism and disability.

claim.es: El 'burnout autista' —agotamiento profundo, pérdida de habilidades, menos tolerancia a estímulos— lo describen adultos autistas como resultado de exigencias sostenidas sin apoyo.
claim.en: 'Autistic burnout' — deep exhaustion, loss of skills, less tolerance to stimuli — is described by autistic adults as the result of sustained demands without support.
claim.sv: 'Autistisk utmattning' — djup trötthet, förlust av färdigheter, mindre tolerans för stimuli — beskrivs av autistiska vuxna som följden av ihållande krav utan stöd.

supports.es: Reducir exigencias y carga sensorial cuando baja la capacidad, en vez de forzar.
supports.en: Reducing demands and sensory load when capacity drops, instead of pushing through.
supports.sv: Att minska krav och sensorisk belastning när kapaciteten sjunker, i stället för att pressa på.

doesNotSupport.es: Un diagnóstico clínico; es una definición desde la experiencia vivida.
doesNotSupport.en: A clinical diagnosis; this is a lived-experience definition.
doesNotSupport.sv: En klinisk diagnos; det här är en definition utifrån levd erfarenhet.

title: Accelerometer-measured physical activity levels in children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder: A systematic review.
authors: Liang X, Li R, Wong SHS, Sum RKW, Sit CHP
abstract: Associations between physical activity (PA) and health benefits are well documented. Evidence indicates that children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) are less physically active than their typically developing peers. The purpose of this systematic review is to provide a comprehensive summary of the PA levels of children and adolescents with ASD and the associated factors that affect their PA levels by applying a socio-ecological model (SEM). Seven databases (PubMed, CINAHL, SPORTDiscus with Full Text, MEDLINE, EMBASE, ERIC, and PsychINFO) were searched in June 2019 to identify studies examining accelerometer-measured PA and factors affecting the PA levels of children and adolescents with ASD, aged 6-17 years. Two researchers independently screened studies, assessed methodological quality, and summarized relevant data. Twenty-one studies were included in the detailed review. Only 42% of the participants met the PA guidelines (i.e., children and adolescents aged 5-17 years should do at least 60 min of moderate to vigorous PA daily). By applying the SEM, multi-level factors ranging from intrapersonal to community levels that positively or negatively influenced PA levels in children and adolescents with ASD were identified. This review indicates that children and adolescents with ASD have low PA levels, and that there are multi-level factors that affect their PA. There is a pressing need to design effective PA interventions that promote activity accrual in the school, family, and community settings for children and adolescents with ASD.

sheet.es: Si quiere apoyar el movimiento de un niño o adolescente autista, piense en el entorno: la escuela, la familia y la comunidad influyen en cuánto se mueve, y conviene buscar actividades que le resulten accesibles y agradables. Es una revisión sistemática de 21 estudios con niños y adolescentes autistas de 6-17 años, cuya actividad se midió con acelerómetros. Solo el 42% cumplía la pauta de al menos 60 min diarios de actividad moderada a vigorosa. Sus límites: resume promedios de grupo, no explica a cada persona, y no prueba qué intervención funciona mejor.
sheet.en: If you want to support an autistic child or teen to move more, look at their surroundings: school, family and community all shape how much they move, so try activities that feel accessible and enjoyable to them. This is a systematic review of 21 studies of autistic children and adolescents aged 6-17, whose activity was measured with accelerometers. Only 42% met the guideline of at least 60 min of moderate to vigorous activity daily. Its limits: it summarises group averages, does not describe every individual, and does not show which approach works best.
sheet.sv: Om du vill stötta ett autistiskt barn eller en tonåring att röra sig mer, titta på omgivningen: skola, familj och samhälle påverkar hur mycket hen rör sig, så pröva aktiviteter som känns tillgängliga och roliga. Detta är en systematisk översikt av 21 studier om autistiska barn och ungdomar i åldern 6-17, där aktiviteten mättes med accelerometrar. Bara 42% nådde riktlinjen på minst 60 min måttlig till intensiv aktivitet per dag. Begränsningar: den sammanfattar gruppgenomsnitt, beskriver inte varje individ och visar inte vilket tillvägagångssätt som fungerar bäst.

title: A Review of Default Mode Network Connectivity and Its Association With Social Cognition in Adolescents With Autism Spectrum Disorder and Early-Onset Psychosis.
authors: Nair A, Jolliffe M, Lograsso YSS, Bearden CE
abstract: Recent studies have demonstrated substantial phenotypic overlap, notably social impairment, between autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and schizophrenia. However, the neural mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis of social impairments across these distinct neuropsychiatric disorders has not yet been fully examined. Most neuroimaging studies to date have focused on adults with these disorders, with little known about the neural underpinnings of social impairments in younger populations. Here, we present a narrative review of the literature available through April 2020 on imaging studies of adolescents with either ASD or early-onset psychosis (EOP), to better understand the shared and unique neural mechanisms of social difficulties across diagnosis from a developmental framework. We specifically focus on functional connectivity studies of the default mode network (DMN), as the most extensively studied brain network relevant to social cognition across both groups. Our review included 29 studies of DMN connectivity in adolescents with ASD (Mean age range = 11.2-21.6 years), and 14 studies in adolescents with EOP (Mean age range = 14.2-24.3 years). Of these, 15 of 29 studies in ASD adolescents found predominant underconnectivity when examining DMN connectivity. In contrast, findings were mixed in adolescents with EOP, with five of 14 studies reporting DMN underconnectivity, and an additional six of 14 studies reporting both under- and over-connectivity of the DMN. Specifically, intra-DMN networks were more frequently underconnected in ASD, but overconnected in EOP. On the other hand, inter-DMN connectivity patterns were mixed (both under- and over-connected) for each group, especially DMN connectivity with frontal, sensorimotor, and temporoparietal regions in ASD, and with frontal, temporal, subcortical, and cerebellar regions in EOP. Finally, disrupted DMN connectivity appeared to be associated with social impairments in both groups, less so with other features distinct to each condition, such as repetitive behaviors/restricted interests in ASD and hallucinations/delusions in EOP. Further studies on demographically well-matched groups of adolescents with each of these conditions are needed to systematically explore additional contributing factors in DMN connectivity patterns such as clinical heterogeneity, pubertal development, and medication effects that would better inform treatment targets and facilitate prediction of outcomes in the context of these developmental neuropsychiatric conditions.

title: Bridging the Gap Between Physical Health and Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Sala R, Amet L, Blagojevic-Stokic N, Shattock P, Whiteley P
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a highly complex and heterogeneous developmental disorder that affects how individuals communicate with other people and relate to the world around them. Research and clinical focus on the behavioural and cognitive manifestations of ASD, whilst important, have obscured the recognition that ASD is also commonly associated with a range of physical and mental health conditions. Many physical conditions appear with greater frequency in individuals with ASD compared to non-ASD populations. These can contribute to a worsening of social communication and behaviour, lower quality of life, higher morbidity and premature mortality. We highlight some of the key physical comorbidities affecting the immune and the gastrointestinal systems, metabolism and brain function in ASD. We discuss how healthcare professionals working with individuals with ASD and parents/carers have a duty to recognise their needs in order to improve their overall health and wellbeing, deliver equality in their healthcare experiences and reduce the likelihood of morbidity and early mortality associated with the condition.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista, tómate en serio los signos de malestar físico: dolor de tripa, problemas de sueño o cambios bruscos pueden tener una causa corporal, y conviene comentarlo con su profesional de salud. Esta es una revisión de la bibliografía, no un estudio con participantes propios. Señala que ciertas condiciones físicas, como las inmunitarias, digestivas, metabólicas y cerebrales, aparecen con más frecuencia en personas autistas, y pide a profesionales y familias atender estas necesidades. Sus límites: es un resumen general, no demuestra qué le pasa a cada persona, y muchas personas autistas no tendrán estas condiciones. Las decisiones médicas corresponden siempre a un clínico.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person, take signs of physical discomfort seriously: tummy pain, sleep problems or sudden changes may have a bodily cause, so it is worth raising them with their health professional. This is a review of existing literature, not a study with its own participants. It reports that some physical conditions, such as immune, digestive, metabolic and brain-related ones, appear more often in autistic people, and it asks professionals and families to attend to these needs. Its limits: it is a broad overview, it cannot tell you what is happening for one person, and many autistic people will not have these conditions. Medical decisions always belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person: ta tecken på fysiskt obehag på allvar. Magont, sömnsvårigheter eller plötsliga förändringar kan ha en kroppslig orsak, så det är värt att ta upp med personens vårdgivare. Detta är en översikt av tidigare forskning, inte en studie med egna deltagare. Den beskriver att vissa fysiska tillstånd, som immunologiska, matsmältningsrelaterade, ämnesomsättningsrelaterade och hjärnrelaterade, förekommer oftare hos autistiska personer, och uppmanar vårdpersonal och familjer att uppmärksamma behoven. Begränsningar: den är en bred sammanställning, kan inte säga vad som gäller för en enskild person, och många autistiska personer har inte dessa tillstånd. Medicinska beslut hör alltid till en kliniker.

title: Alteration of Gut Microbiota in Autism Spectrum Disorder: An Overview.
authors: Oh D, Cheon KA
journal: Soa--ch'ongsonyon chongsin uihak = Journal of child & adolescent psychiatry
abstract: The microbiota-gut-brain axis, which refers to the bidirectional communication pathway between gut bacteria and the central nervous system, has a profound effect on important brain processes, from the synthesis of neurotransmitters to the modulation of complex behaviors such as sociability and anxiety. Previous studies have revealed that the gut microbiota is potentially related to not only gastrointestinal disturbances, but also social impairment and repetitive behavior-core symptoms of autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Although studies have been conducted to characterize the microbial composition in patients with ASD, the results are heterogeneous. Nevertheless, it is clear that there is a difference in the composition of the gut microbiota between ASD and typically developed individuals, and animal studies have repeatedly suggested that the gut microbiota plays an important role in ASD pathophysiology. This possibility is supported by abnormalities in metabolites produced by the gut microbiota and the association between altered immune responses and the gut microbiota observed in ASD patients. Based on these findings, various attempts have been made to use the microbiota in ASD treatment. The results reported to date suggest that microbiota-based therapies may be effective for ASD, but largescale, well-designed studies are needed to confirm this.

sheet.es: Si observas molestias digestivas en tu hijo o familiar autista, vale la pena comentarlas con su profesional de salud: el intestino y el cerebro se comunican y el malestar del cuerpo puede afectar al día a día. Esta es una revisión que reúne estudios previos, incluidos estudios con animales. Señala que la composición de las bacterias intestinales parece diferir entre personas autistas y no autistas, aunque los resultados son heterogéneos. Sus límites: aún no se sabe qué significa esa diferencia en cada persona, y se necesitan estudios grandes y bien diseñados para confirmar si los tratamientos basados en la microbiota sirven. Las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If your autistic child or relative seems to have stomach or bowel discomfort, it is worth raising it with their health professional: the gut and brain communicate, and bodily discomfort can affect daily life. This is a review that brings together earlier studies, including animal studies. It reports that gut bacteria composition seems to differ between autistic and non-autistic people, though results are mixed. Its limits: it is still unclear what this difference means for any one person, and large, well-designed studies are needed to confirm whether microbiota-based treatments work. Medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn eller din anhöriga verkar ha magont eller andra problem med magen är det värt att ta upp det med vården: tarmen och hjärnan kommunicerar, och kroppsligt obehag kan påverka vardagen. Detta är en översikt som samlar tidigare studier, bland annat djurstudier. Den beskriver att sammansättningen av tarmbakterier verkar skilja sig mellan autistiska och icke-autistiska personer, men resultaten varierar. Begränsningar: det är fortfarande oklart vad skillnaden betyder för en enskild person, och stora, välgjorda studier behövs för att bekräfta om behandlingar baserade på tarmfloran fungerar. Medicinska beslut hör till en läkare.

title: Increased Accuracy of Emotion Recognition in Individuals with Autism-Like Traits after Five Days of Magnetic Stimulations.
authors: Liu P, Xiao G, He K, Zhang L, Wu X, Li D, Zhu C, Tian Y, Hu P, Qiu B, Ji GJ, Wang K
abstract: Individuals with autism-like traits (ALT) belong to a subclinical group with similar social deficits as autism spectrum disorders (ASD). Their main social deficits include atypical eye contact and difficulty in understanding facial expressions, both of which are associated with an abnormality of the right posterior superior temporal sulcus (rpSTS). It is still undetermined whether it is possible to improve the social function of ALT individuals through noninvasive neural modulation. To this end, we randomly assigned ALT individuals into the real ( n = 16) and sham ( n = 16) stimulation groups. All subjects received five consecutive days of intermittent theta burst stimulation (iTBS) on the rpSTS. Eye tracking data and functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data were acquired on the first and sixth days. The real group showed significant improvement in emotion recognition accuracy after iTBS, but the change was not significantly larger than that in the sham group. Resting-state functional connectivity (rsFC) between the rpSTS and the left cerebellum significantly decreased in the real group than the sham group after iTBS. At baseline, rsFC in the left cerebellum was negatively correlated with emotion recognition accuracy. Our findings indicated that iTBS of the rpSTS could improve emotion perception of ALT individuals by modulating associated neural networks. This stimulation protocol could be a vital therapeutic strategy for the treatment of ASD.

sheet.es: Este estudio no ofrece nada que hacer mañana en casa: probó una técnica médica de estimulación cerebral, así que cualquier decisión sobre ella corresponde a un profesional clínico. Fue un ensayo con personas con rasgos similares al autismo, repartidas al azar en estimulación real (16) o simulada (16), durante cinco días consecutivos. El grupo real mejoró en reconocer emociones, pero el cambio no fue significativamente mayor que en el grupo simulado. Los límites: muestra pequeña, participantes sin diagnóstico de autismo y una conclusión del texto más optimista que sus propios datos. No sirve como regla para ninguna persona.
sheet.en: This study offers nothing to try at home tomorrow: it tested a medical brain stimulation technique, so any decision about it belongs to a clinician. It was a trial with people who have autism-like traits, randomly assigned to real (16) or sham (16) stimulation over five consecutive days. The real group improved at recognising emotions, but the change was not significantly larger than in the sham group. Limits: a small sample, participants without an autism diagnosis, and a conclusion more optimistic than its own data. It is not a rule for any individual person.
sheet.sv: Den här studien ger inget att prova hemma i morgon: den testade en medicinsk hjärnstimuleringsmetod, så beslut om den hör till en läkare. Det var en randomiserad studie med personer med autismliknande drag, fördelade på verklig (16) eller overksam skenstimulering (16) under fem dagar i följd. Gruppen med verklig stimulering blev bättre på att känna igen känslor, men förändringen var inte signifikant större än i skengruppen. Begränsningar: litet urval, deltagare utan autismdiagnos och en slutsats som är mer optimistisk än de egna resultaten. Den är ingen regel för någon enskild person.

title: Genetics of structural and functional brain changes in autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Hashem S, Nisar S, Bhat AA, Yadav SK, Azeem MW, Bagga P, Fakhro K, Reddy R, Frenneaux MP, Haris M
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurological and developmental disorder characterized by social impairment and restricted interactive and communicative behaviors. It may occur as an isolated disorder or in the context of other neurological, psychiatric, developmental, and genetic disorders. Due to rapid developments in genomics and imaging technologies, imaging genetics studies of ASD have evolved in the last few years. Increased risk for ASD diagnosis is found to be related to many specific single-nucleotide polymorphisms, and the study of genetic mechanisms and noninvasive imaging has opened various approaches that can help diagnose ASD at the nascent level. Identifying risk genes related to structural and functional changes in the brain of ASD patients provide a better understanding of the disease's neuropsychiatry and can help identify targets for therapeutic intervention that could be useful for the clinical management of ASD patients.

sheet.es: Este estudio no ofrece nada que hacer mañana por la mañana: sirve para entender mejor, no para cambiar la rutina. Lo que sí puede recordar es que la genética y el cerebro de cada persona autista son distintos, y que sus necesidades se conocen mejor escuchándola y observándola. Es una revisión que reúne investigaciones que combinan genética e imágenes del cerebro en el autismo. El resumen no indica qué personas participaron ni cuántas. Sus límites: no da pautas para la vida diaria, habla de posibles futuros usos en el diagnóstico y no debe tomarse como regla para toda persona autista. Las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: This study offers nothing to do tomorrow morning: it helps understanding, not changing a routine. What you can keep in mind is that the genetics and the brain of each autistic person are different, and that their needs are best learned by listening to and observing them. It is a review that brings together research combining genetics and brain imaging in autism. The abstract does not say who took part or how many. Its limits: it gives no guidance for daily life, it discusses possible future uses in diagnosis, and it should not be taken as a rule for every autistic person. Medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Den här studien ger inget att göra i morgon bitti: den hjälper oss förstå, inte ändra en rutin. Det du kan ta med dig är att genetiken och hjärnan hos varje autistisk person är olika, och att behoven bäst förstås genom att lyssna på och observera personen. Det är en översikt som samlar forskning som kombinerar genetik och hjärnavbildning vid autism. Sammanfattningen anger inte vilka eller hur många som deltog. Begränsningar: den ger inga råd för vardagen, tar upp möjliga framtida användningar vid diagnostik och ska inte ses som en regel för alla autistiska personer. Medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker.

title: Clinical Assessment, Genetics, and Treatment Approaches in Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD).
authors: Genovese A, Butler MG
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) consists of a genetically heterogenous group of neurobehavioral disorders characterized by impairment in three behavioral domains including communication, social interaction, and stereotypic repetitive behaviors. ASD affects more than 1% of children in Western societies, with diagnoses on the rise due to improved recognition, screening, clinical assessment, and diagnostic testing. We reviewed the role of genetic and metabolic factors which contribute to the causation of ASD with the use of new genetic technology. Up to 40 percent of individuals with ASD are now diagnosed with genetic syndromes or have chromosomal abnormalities including small DNA deletions or duplications, single gene conditions, or gene variants and metabolic disturbances with mitochondrial dysfunction. Although the heritability estimate for ASD is between 70 and 90%, there is a lower molecular diagnostic yield than anticipated. A likely explanation may relate to multifactorial causation with etiological heterogeneity and hundreds of genes involved with a complex interplay between inheritance and environmental factors influenced by epigenetics and capabilities to identify causative genes and their variants for ASD. Behavioral and psychiatric correlates, diagnosis and genetic evaluation with testing are discussed along with psychiatric treatment approaches and pharmacogenetics for selection of medication to treat challenging behaviors or comorbidities commonly seen in ASD. We emphasize prioritizing treatment based on targeted symptoms for individuals with ASD, as treatment will vary from patient to patient based on diagnosis, comorbidities, causation, and symptom severity.

sheet.es: Si le preocupa por qué una persona autista es como es, sepa que no hay una única causa: la genética y el entorno intervienen juntos, y cada persona es distinta. Si desea una evaluación genética, consúltelo con su equipo clínico. Esto es una revisión de la literatura sobre evaluación, genética y tratamientos; el resumen indica que hasta un 40 por ciento de las personas con TEA recibe un diagnóstico de síndrome genético o alteración cromosómica. Sus límites: no es un estudio con participantes propios, no sirve como regla para cada persona y las decisiones sobre medicación corresponden siempre a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If you wonder why an autistic person is the way they are, know that there is no single cause: genetics and environment work together, and every person is different. If you are interested in genetic testing, talk it through with your clinical team. This is a review of the literature on assessment, genetics and treatment; the abstract says up to 40 percent of people with ASD are diagnosed with a genetic syndrome or chromosomal abnormality. Its limits: it is not a study with its own participants, it is not a rule for every person, and any decision about medication belongs to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om du undrar varför en autistisk person är som hen är: det finns ingen enskild orsak. Gener och miljö samverkar, och varje person är olika. Vill du veta mer om genetisk utredning, prata med ditt kliniska team. Detta är en översikt av litteraturen om bedömning, genetik och behandling; sammanfattningen anger att upp till 40 procent av personer med ASD får diagnosen genetiskt syndrom eller kromosomavvikelse. Begränsningar: den har inga egna deltagare, gäller inte som regel för varje person, och beslut om läkemedel hör alltid till en kliniker.

title: Healthcare access for autistic adults: A systematic review.
authors: Calleja S, Islam FMA, Kingsley J, McDonald R
abstract: Background People with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) have an increased susceptibility for many chronic health conditions compared with their peers. An increasing number of adolescents are transitioning from pediatric to adult healthcare services. Thus, being able to access appropriate healthcare services that can not only address specific needs of the person but enable them to better manage healthcare conditions and decrease the development of preventable disease is necessary. A systematic review was conducted to identify barriers and enablers of healthcare access for autistic adults. Methods The studies included in the review were quantitative and qualitative and were published between 2003 and 2019. The participants for the review are considered to be adults (over 18 years of age) with a primary diagnosis of ASD. Results In total, 1290 studies were initially identified and 13 studies were included based on the inclusion and exclusion criteria outlined in a previous protocol paper. The analysis of these studies identified areas of concern to access appropriate healthcare, such as clinician knowledge, the environment, and life events. Conclusion Identifying the barriers to healthcare, highlights ways healthcare services can regulate scope of practice, the physical environment, and the process of managing health conditions, thus, autistic adults can strive for optimal health. This review contributes to peer-reviewed evidence for future research and up-to-date information when developing and piloting health interventions for autistic adults. Ethics and dissemination There are no human participants, data, or tissue being directly studied for the purposes of the review; therefore, ethics approval and consent to participate is not applicable. Registration and status PROSPERO 2018 CRD42018116093.

sheet.es: Antes de una cita médica, puede ayudar preparar juntos una nota breve sobre cómo se comunica la persona, qué le resulta difícil del entorno (luz, ruido, esperas) y qué apoyos necesita. Pedir la primera o última cita del día, o esperar fuera, puede reducir la carga sensorial. Si el profesional sabe poco sobre autismo, compartir esa información con calma es útil. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 13 estudios (2003-2019) con adultos autistas y encontró barreras en el conocimiento clínico, el entorno y los cambios vitales, como pasar a servicios para adultos. Sus límites: pocos estudios, diseños distintos y resultados que quizá no reflejen la experiencia de cada persona ni de cada país.
sheet.en: Before a medical appointment, it can help to prepare a short note together about how the person communicates, what is hard about the setting (lights, noise, waiting) and what support they need. Asking for the first or last slot of the day, or waiting outside, may ease sensory load. If the clinician knows little about autism, calmly sharing that note is useful. This systematic review pooled 13 studies (2003-2019) with autistic adults and found barriers in clinician knowledge, the environment and life events such as moving to adult services. Its limits: few studies, mixed designs, and findings that may not match every person's or country's experience.
sheet.sv: Inför ett vårdbesök kan det hjälpa att tillsammans skriva en kort lapp om hur personen kommunicerar, vad som är svårt i miljön (ljus, ljud, väntan) och vilket stöd som behövs. Att be om dagens första eller sista tid, eller att vänta utomhus, kan minska den sensoriska belastningen. Om vårdpersonalen kan lite om autism är det bra att lugnt dela lappen. Denna systematiska översikt samlade 13 studier (2003-2019) med autistiska vuxna och fann hinder i vårdpersonalens kunskap, miljön och livshändelser som övergången till vuxenvården. Begränsningar: få studier, olika upplägg och resultat som kanske inte stämmer för varje person eller varje land.

title: Conceptualising compensation in neurodevelopmental disorders: Reflections from autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Livingston LA, Happé F
abstract: Within research into neurodevelopmental disorders, little is known about the mechanisms underpinning changes in symptom severity across development. When the behavioural presentation of a condition improves/symptoms lessen, this may be because core underlying atypicalities in cognition/neural function have ameliorated. An alternative possibility is 'compensation'; that the behavioural presentation appears improved, despite persisting deficits at cognitive and/or neurobiological levels. There is, however, currently no agreed technical definition of compensation or its behavioural, cognitive and neural characteristics. Furthermore, its workings in neurodevelopmental disorders have not been studied directly. Here, we review current evidence for compensation in neurodevelopmental disorders, using Autism Spectrum Disorder as an example, in order to move towards a better conceptualisation of the construct. We propose a transdiagnostic framework, where compensation represents the processes responsible for an observed mismatch between behaviour and underlying cognition in a neurodevelopmental disorder, at any point in development. Further, we explore potential cognitive and neural mechanisms driving compensation and discuss the broader relevance of the concept within research and clinical settings.

title: Towards a brain-based predictome of mental illness.
authors: Rashid B, Calhoun V
abstract: Neuroimaging-based approaches have been extensively applied to study mental illness in recent years and have deepened our understanding of both cognitively healthy and disordered brain structure and function. Recent advancements in machine learning techniques have shown promising outcomes for individualized prediction and characterization of patients with psychiatric disorders. Studies have utilized features from a variety of neuroimaging modalities, including structural, functional, and diffusion magnetic resonance imaging data, as well as jointly estimated features from multiple modalities, to assess patients with heterogeneous mental disorders, such as schizophrenia and autism. We use the term "predictome" to describe the use of multivariate brain network features from one or more neuroimaging modalities to predict mental illness. In the predictome, multiple brain network-based features (either from the same modality or multiple modalities) are incorporated into a predictive model to jointly estimate features that are unique to a disorder and predict subjects accordingly. To date, more than 650 studies have been published on subject-level prediction focusing on psychiatric disorders. We have surveyed about 250 studies including schizophrenia, major depression, bipolar disorder, autism spectrum disorder, attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder, social anxiety disorder, posttraumatic stress disorder, and substance dependence. In this review, we present a comprehensive review of recent neuroimaging-based predictomic approaches, current trends, and common shortcomings and share our vision for future directions.

sheet.es: Este estudio no ofrece nada que hacer mañana por la mañana en casa: trata de investigación con escáneres cerebrales, no de apoyos cotidianos. Si alguien le propone usar un escáner para valorar a una persona autista, recuerde que esta línea de trabajo sigue siendo de investigación. Es una revisión sistemática que examinó unos 250 estudios sobre varios diagnósticos, entre ellos el autismo, que usan imágenes cerebrales y aprendizaje automático para predecir trastornos. Sus límites: no es específica del autismo, habla de «enfermedad mental» con un enfoque médico y señala deficiencias comunes en los estudios. No sirve como regla para ninguna persona.
sheet.en: This study offers nothing to do at home tomorrow morning: it is about brain-scan research, not everyday support. If anyone suggests using a scan to assess an autistic person, remember that this line of work is still research. It is a systematic review that surveyed about 250 studies across several diagnoses, autism among them, which use brain imaging and machine learning to predict disorders. Its limits: it is not specific to autism, it uses a medical framing of "mental illness", and it points out common shortcomings in the studies. It is not a rule for any individual person.
sheet.sv: Den här studien ger inget att göra hemma i morgon bitti: den handlar om forskning med hjärnavbildning, inte om vardagligt stöd. Om någon föreslår att en hjärnskanning ska användas för att bedöma en autistisk person, minns att detta fortfarande är forskning. Det är en systematisk översikt som gick igenom cirka 250 studier om flera diagnoser, bland annat autism, där hjärnavbildning och maskininlärning används för att förutsäga sjukdomstillstånd. Begränsningar: den är inte specifik för autism, utgår från en medicinsk syn på "psykisk sjukdom" och lyfter vanliga brister i studierna. Den är ingen regel för någon enskild person.

title: 'I never realised everybody felt as happy as I do when I am around autistic people': A thematic analysis of autistic adults' relationships with autistic and neurotypical friends and family.
authors: Crompton CJ, Hallett S, Ropar D, Flynn E, Fletcher-Watson S
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Although autistic people may struggle to interact with others, many autistic people have said they find interacting with other autistic people more comfortable. To find out whether this was a common experience, we did hour-long interviews with 12 autistic adults. We asked them questions about how it feels when spending time with their friends and family, and whether it felt different depending on whether the friends and family were autistic or neurotypical. We analysed the interviews and found three common themes in what our participants said. First, they found spending with other autistic people easier and more comfortable than spending time with neurotypical people, and felt they were better understood by other autistic people. Second, autistic people often felt they were in a social minority, and in order to spend time with neurotypical friends and family, they had to conform with what the neurotypical people wanted and were used to. Third, autistic people felt like they belonged with other autistic people and that they could be themselves around them. These findings show that having time with autistic friends and family can be very beneficial for autistic people and played an important role in a happy social life.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista, vale la pena facilitar tiempo con otras personas autistas: grupos, clubes de intereses, comunidades en línea o familiares autistas. Muchas personas autistas cuentan que con sus pares se sienten comprendidas, pueden ser ellas mismas y no tienen que adaptarse constantemente a normas neurotípicas. También ayuda reducir la presión de "encajar" en reuniones familiares y respetar sus formas de comunicarse. Evidencia: estudio cualitativo con entrevistas de una hora a 12 adultos autistas sobre sus relaciones con amigos y familiares autistas y neurotípicos. Límites: muestra pequeña, solo adultos que pueden participar en entrevistas; no representa a cada persona ni mide efectos a largo plazo.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person, it is worth making room for time with other autistic people: groups, interest clubs, online communities or autistic relatives. Many autistic people say that with autistic peers they feel understood, can be themselves and do not have to keep adapting to neurotypical expectations. It also helps to ease the pressure to "fit in" at family gatherings and to respect their ways of communicating. Evidence: a qualitative study using hour-long interviews with 12 autistic adults about relationships with autistic and neurotypical friends and family. Limits: a small sample of adults able to take part in interviews; it does not speak for every person or measure long-term effects.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person kan det vara värt att skapa tillfällen att umgås med andra autistiska personer: grupper, intresseklubbar, nätgemenskaper eller autistiska släktingar. Många autistiska personer berättar att de med autistiska jämlikar känner sig förstådda, kan vara sig själva och slipper anpassa sig hela tiden till neurotypiska förväntningar. Det hjälper också att minska trycket att "passa in" på familjeträffar och att respektera personens sätt att kommunicera. Evidens: en kvalitativ studie med timslånga intervjuer med 12 autistiska vuxna om relationer med autistiska och neurotypiska vänner och familj. Begränsningar: litet urval av vuxna som kunde delta i intervjuer; resultaten gäller inte alla och mäter inte långsiktiga effekter.

title: 'When my autism broke': A qualitative study spotlighting autistic voices on menopause.
authors: Moseley RL, Druce T, Turner-Cobb JM
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic girls are known to struggle with the onset of menstruation, reporting that during their period, sensory sensitivities are heightened, it becomes more difficult to think clearly and control their emotions and they struggle more with everyday life and self-care. Yet surprisingly, nothing is known about how autistic women handle the menopausal transition in midlife. In non-autistic women, the menopause brings many physical changes and challenging symptoms from hot flushes to feeling more anxious and depressed. Because autistic women are already vulnerable to suicide, poor physical and mental health, and because they may already struggle with planning, controlling their emotions and coping with change, the menopause may be an especially challenging time. Yet, not one single study exists on the menopause in autism, so we conducted an online discussion (focus group) with seven autistic women. They confirmed that very little is known about menopause in autistic people, very little support is available and that menopause might be especially difficult for autistic people. Autism-related difficulties (including sensory sensitivity, socializing with others and communicating needs) were reported to worsen during the menopause, often so dramatically that some participants suggested they found it impossible to continue to mask their struggles. Participants also reported having extreme meltdowns, experiencing anxiety and depression, and feeling suicidal. This study highlights how important it is that professionals pay attention to menopause in autism, and discusses future research directions.

sheet.es: Si estás en la menopausia o acompañas a una mujer autista que lo está, conviene hablar de ello con un profesional de salud que conozca el autismo. Los cambios sensoriales, sociales o emocionales pueden intensificarse, y anotarlos ayuda a pedir apoyo. Es un estudio cualitativo: un grupo de discusión en línea con siete mujeres autistas. Dijeron que hay muy poco apoyo, que las dificultades autistas empeoraban y que les costaba más enmascarar. También mencionaron ansiedad, depresión y pensamientos suicidas. Es un grupo muy pequeño y no representa a todas las personas. Si aparecen pensamientos suicidas, busca ayuda profesional: un clínico, un servicio de salud o un servicio de crisis. Si hay peligro inmediato, llama al número de emergencias de tu país.
sheet.en: If you are going through menopause, or support an autistic woman who is, it is worth talking with a health professional who understands autism. Sensory, social and emotional difficulties may intensify, and keeping notes can help you ask for support. This was a qualitative study: an online focus group with seven autistic women. They said very little support exists, autism-related difficulties got worse, and masking became harder. They also described anxiety, depression and feeling suicidal. The group was very small and cannot speak for everyone. If suicidal thoughts appear, seek professional help: a clinician, a health service or a crisis service. If there is immediate danger, call the emergency number of your country.
sheet.sv: Om du går igenom klimakteriet, eller stöttar en autistisk kvinna som gör det, är det värt att prata med en vårdgivare som förstår autism. Sensoriska, sociala och känslomässiga svårigheter kan öka, och anteckningar kan hjälpa dig att be om stöd. Detta var en kvalitativ studie: en fokusgrupp online med sju autistiska kvinnor. De berättade att det finns mycket lite stöd, att autismrelaterade svårigheter förvärrades och att det blev svårare att maskera. De beskrev också ångest, depression och självmordstankar. Gruppen var mycket liten och kan inte tala för alla. Om självmordstankar uppstår, sök professionell hjälp: en läkare, en vårdinstans eller en krisjour. Vid akut fara, ring ditt lands nödnummer.

title: A framework of evidence-based practice for digital support, co-developed with and for the autism community.
authors: Zervogianni V, Fletcher-Watson S, Herrera G, Goodwin M, Pérez-Fuster P, Brosnan M, Grynszpan O
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Digital supports are any type of technologies that have been intentionally developed to improve daily living in some way. A wide array of digital supports (such as apps) have been developed for the autism community specifically, but there is little or no evidence of whether they work or not. This study sought to identify what types of evidence the autistic community valued and wanted to see provided to enable an informed choice to be made regarding digital supports. A consensus was developed between autistic people and their families, practitioners (such as therapists and teachers) as well as researchers, to identify the core aspects of evidence that everyone agreed were useful. In all, 27 people reached agreement on three categories for which evidence is required: reliability, engagement and the effectiveness of the technology. Consensus was also reached on four key sources of evidence for these three categories: hands-on experience, academic sources, expert views and online reviews. The resulting framework allows for any technology to be evaluated for the level of evidence identifying how effective it is. The framework can be used by autistic people, their families, practitioners and researchers to ensure that decisions concerning the provision of support for autistic people is informed by evidence, that is, 'evidence-based practice'.

sheet.es: Antes de elegir una app o tecnología de apoyo, pregunten tres cosas: ¿es fiable?, ¿engancha, es decir, la persona autista quiere usarla?, ¿funciona? Para responder, combinen la experiencia práctica, fuentes académicas, opiniones de especialistas y reseñas en línea. Es un estudio con personas autistas, familias, profesionales e investigadores; 27 personas llegaron a un consenso sobre estas categorías y fuentes. Como límite, el estudio propone un marco para valorar la evidencia, no demuestra que ninguna app concreta funcione, y cada persona es distinta.
sheet.en: Before choosing an app or other digital support, ask three things: is it reliable, is it engaging (does the autistic person actually want to use it), and does it work? To find out, combine hands-on experience, academic sources, expert views and online reviews. This was a study with autistic people, families, practitioners and researchers; 27 people reached agreement on these categories and sources. A limit: it offers a framework for judging evidence, not proof that any particular app works, and every person is different.
sheet.sv: Innan ni väljer en app eller annat digitalt stöd, fråga er tre saker: är det pålitligt, är det engagerande (vill den autistiska personen verkligen använda det) och fungerar det? Kombinera egen praktisk erfarenhet, akademiska källor, experters åsikter och recensioner på nätet. Det var en studie med autistiska personer, familjer, yrkesverksamma och forskare; 27 personer enades om dessa kategorier och källor. En begränsning är att studien ger ett ramverk för att bedöma evidens, inte bevis för att en viss app fungerar, och alla människor är olika.

title: Interviewing autistic adults: Adaptations to support recall in police, employment, and healthcare interviews.
authors: Norris JE, Crane L, Maras K
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract During many types of interviews (e.g. in employment, with the police, and in healthcare), we need to recall detailed memories of specific events, which can be difficult for autistic people in response to commonly used questions. This is especially because these tend to be open questions (i.e. very broad). Autistic people have disproportionately high rates of physical and mental health conditions, are more likely to interact with police, and are the most underemployed disability group. However, interviewers are often unsure about how to adapt their communication for autistic people.Our research tested whether different types of prompts enabled autistic people to recall specific memories (memories of a single event within one day). Participants were asked about situations relating to witnessing a crime (e.g. at the bank), physical or mental health scenarios and employment interviews (e.g. a time you've met a deadline).We tested the following: Open questions : basic questions only (e.g. 'tell me about a time you went to the cinema'), Semantic prompting : a general prompt (e.g. 'do you enjoy going to the cinema?') before asking for a specific instance ('tell me about a time you went to the cinema?'), Visual-verbal prompting : asking participants to recall when it happened, who was there, the actions that occurred, the setting , and any objects .With visual-verbal prompting, autistic and typically developing participants' memories were more specific and detailed. Semantic prompting was also effective for employment questions. Our study shows that autistic people can recall specific memories when they are appropriately prompted. Visual-verbal prompting may be effective across different situations.

sheet.es: Si va a entrevistar a una persona autista (en el trabajo, la salud o con la policía), evite preguntas muy abiertas. Pruebe a guiar el recuerdo: pregunte cuándo ocurrió, quién estaba, qué pasó, dónde fue y qué objetos había. En preguntas de empleo, también puede ayudar empezar con una pregunta general antes de pedir un ejemplo concreto. La evidencia es un estudio con personas autistas y participantes de desarrollo típico, que recordaron con más detalle usando estas guías visuales y verbales. Sus límites: se probaron situaciones planteadas, no entrevistas reales, y cada persona es distinta, así que conviene preguntarle qué apoyo prefiere.
sheet.en: If you are interviewing an autistic person (for work, healthcare or police), avoid very broad open questions. Try guiding the memory: ask when it happened, who was there, what happened, where it was, and which objects were present. For employment questions, starting with a general question before asking for a specific example may also help. The evidence is a study with autistic and typically developing participants, whose memories were more specific and detailed with these visual-verbal prompts. Its limits: it tested set scenarios, not real interviews, and every person is different, so it is worth asking what support they prefer.
sheet.sv: Om du intervjuar en autistisk person (för jobb, vård eller polis), undvik mycket breda öppna frågor. Prova att vägleda minnet: fråga när det hände, vem som var där, vad som hände, var det var och vilka föremål som fanns. Vid anställningsfrågor kan det också hjälpa att börja med en allmän fråga innan du ber om ett konkret exempel. Underlaget är en studie med autistiska och typiskt utvecklade deltagare, vars minnen blev mer specifika och detaljerade med dessa visuellt-verbala stöd. Begränsningar: studien testade givna scenarier, inte verkliga intervjuer, och alla är olika, så fråga gärna vilket stöd personen föredrar.

title: Alexithymia may explain the relationship between autistic traits and eating disorder psychopathology.
authors: Vuillier L, Carter Z, Teixeira AR, Moseley RL
abstract: Background Autistic people are disproportionately vulnerable to anorexia nervosa and other eating disorders (ED), and within the general population, autistic traits correlate with ED psychopathology. A putative mechanism which may underpin this heightened risk is alexithymia, a difficulty identifying and describing emotional states which is observed in both autism and ED. In two experiments with independent non-clinical samples, we explored whether alexithymia might mediate the heightened risk of eating psychopathology in individuals high in autistic traits. Methods Our first experiment used the PROCESS macro for SPSS to examine relationships between alexithymia (measured by the Toronto Alexithymia Scale (TAS-20)), autistic traits (autism quotient (AQ)), and eating psychopathology (Eating Attitudes Test (EAT-26)) in 121 participants. Our second experiment (n = 300) replicated and furthered this analysis by examining moderating effects of sex and controlling for anxiety and depression as covariates. We also included an additional performance-based measure of alexithymia, the Levels of Emotional Awareness Scale (LEAS). Results Study 1 suggested that TAS-20 scores mediated the relationship between heightened autistic traits and eating psychopathology. Replication and further scrutiny of this finding, in study 2, revealed that this mediation effect was partial and specific to the female participants in this sample. The mediation effect appeared to be carried by the difficulty identifying feelings subscale of the TAS-20, even when depression and anxiety were controlled for. LEAS scores, however, were not significantly related to autistic traits or eating psychopathology. Limitations Cross-sectional data prevents any conclusions around the direction and causality of relationships between alexithymia, autistic traits, and eating psychopathology (alongside depression and anxiety), necessitating longitudinal research. Our non-clinical sample was predominantly Caucasian undergraduate students, so it remains to be seen if these results would extrapolate to clinical and/or autistic samples. Divergence between the TAS-20 and LEAS raises crucial questions regarding the construct validity of these measures. Conclusions Our findings with respect to autistic traits suggest that alexithymia could partially explain the prevalence of ED in autistic people and may as such be an important consideration in the pathogenesis and treatment of ED in autistic and non-autistic people alike. Further research with clinical samples is critical to explore these ideas. Differences between men and women, furthermore, emphasize the importance of looking for sex-specific as well as generic risk factors in autistic and non-autistic men and women.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista tiene problemas con la comida, conviene preguntar también cómo identifica y describe lo que siente; esa dificultad podría ser parte del cuadro. Si hay preocupación por la alimentación, consulten con un profesional sanitario. Es un estudio con estudiantes no clínicos, 121 personas en el primer experimento y 300 en el segundo, que midió rasgos autistas, alexitimia y actitudes ante la comida. La alexitimia explicó solo en parte la relación, y solo en las mujeres de la muestra. Los datos son de un único momento, no prueban causa, y la muestra era sobre todo de estudiantes caucásicos, no de personas autistas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person has a difficult relationship with food, it may help to also ask how they identify and describe what they feel; that difficulty could be part of the picture. If eating is a worry, talk with a health professional. This study used non-clinical students, 121 people in the first experiment and 300 in the second, measuring autistic traits, alexithymia and eating attitudes. Alexithymia explained the link only partly, and only in the women in the sample. The data come from one point in time, so they cannot show cause, and the sample was mostly Caucasian students, not autistic people.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person har en svår relation till mat kan det hjälpa att också fråga hur hen identifierar och beskriver sina känslor; den svårigheten kan vara en del av bilden. Om maten oroar, prata med vårdpersonal. Studien omfattade icke-kliniska studenter, 121 personer i det första experimentet och 300 i det andra, och mätte autistiska drag, alexitymi och attityder till mat. Alexitymi förklarade sambandet bara delvis, och bara hos kvinnorna i urvalet. Data kommer från en enda tidpunkt och visar därför inte orsak, och urvalet var mest vita studenter, inte autistiska personer.

title: Sleeping without Prescription: Management of Sleep Disorders in Children with Autism with Non-Pharmacological Interventions and Over-the-Counter Treatments.
authors: Esposito D, Belli A, Ferri R, Bruni O
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASD) are lifelong neurodevelopmental conditions characterized by abnormal social interaction, communication, and behavior. Sleep disturbances represent a common comorbidity in children and adolescents with ASD, with prevalence ranging from 50 to 80%.
