It has been proved that sleep disruption worsens the symptoms of autism and results in challenging behaviors. Improving sleep should therefore be a primary therapeutic goal. Treatment options range from lifestyle modifications to pharmacological therapy. Several reviews have been written on pharmacological treatments, but very few on the beneficial effects of non-pharmacological interventions, over-the-counter drugs, and nutritional supplements. This study consists of a narrative review of the literature, presenting the available evidence on the following treatments: sleep education, behavioral interventions, complementary and alternative medicine (special mattresses and blankets, massage, aromatherapy, yoga, physical activity), and commonly used over-the-counter medications and supplements (antihistamines, melatonin, tryptophan, carnosine, iron, vitamins, and herbal remedies). For some treatments-such as melatonin and behavioral interventions-effectiveness in ASD is well established in the literature, while other interventions appear of benefit in clinical practice, even if specific studies in children and adolescents with ASD are lacking. Conversely, other treatments only seem to show anecdotal evidence supporting their use.

sheet.es: Si el sueño de su hijo autista es difícil, puede empezar por rutinas y educación del sueño y por apoyos conductuales, y comentar con un profesional sanitario cualquier suplemento o producto sin receta. Se trata de una revisión narrativa de la literatura sobre tratamientos no farmacológicos, productos sin receta y suplementos para niños y adolescentes con autismo. Según la revisión, las intervenciones conductuales tienen eficacia bien establecida, otras parecen útiles en la práctica clínica y algunas solo tienen evidencia anecdótica. Como limitación, para varias opciones faltan estudios específicos en autismo, y lo que sirve a una persona puede no servir a otra. Las decisiones sobre productos con efecto médico corresponden a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If sleep is hard for your autistic child, you can start with sleep routines, sleep education and behavioural supports, and talk to a health professional before trying any over-the-counter product or supplement. This is a narrative review of the literature on non-pharmacological approaches, over-the-counter products and supplements for children and adolescents with autism. It reports that behavioural interventions have well-established effectiveness, others seem helpful in clinical practice, and some have only anecdotal evidence. A limit is that specific studies in autism are lacking for several options, and what helps one person may not help another. Decisions about anything with a medical effect belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om sömnen är svår för ditt autistiska barn kan du börja med sömnrutiner, sömnutbildning och beteendemässigt stöd, och prata med vårdpersonal innan du provar receptfria produkter eller kosttillskott. Detta är en narrativ översikt av litteraturen om icke-farmakologiska metoder, receptfria produkter och tillskott för barn och ungdomar med autism. Enligt översikten har beteendeinriktade insatser väl belagd effekt, andra verkar hjälpa i klinisk praxis och vissa har bara anekdotiska belägg. En begränsning är att specifika studier på autism saknas för flera alternativ, och det som hjälper en person kanske inte hjälper en annan. Beslut om sådant som har medicinsk effekt hör till en kliniker.

title: Self-guided mindfulness and cognitive behavioural practices reduce anxiety in autistic adults: A pilot 8-month waitlist-controlled trial of widely available online tools.
authors: Gaigg SB, Flaxman PE, McLaven G, Shah R, Bowler DM, Meyer B, Roestorf A, Haenschel C, Rodgers J, South M
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Anxiety in autism is an important target for psychological therapies because it is very common and because it significantly impacts upon quality of life and well-being. Growing evidence suggests that cognitive behaviour therapies and mindfulness-based therapies can help autistic individuals learn to manage feelings of anxiety but access to such therapies remains problematic. In the current pilot study, we examined whether existing online cognitive behaviour therapy and mindfulness-based therapy self-help tools can help reduce anxiety in autistic adults. Specifically, 35 autistic adults were asked to try either an existing online cognitive behaviour therapy (n = 16) or mindfulness-based therapy (n = 19) programme while a further 19 autistic adults served as a waitlist comparison group. A first important finding was that 23 of the 35 (66%) participants who tried the online tools completed them, suggesting that such tools are, in principle, acceptable to many autistic adults. In addition, adults in the cognitive behaviour therapy and mindfulness-based therapy conditions reported significant decreases in anxiety over 3 and to some extent also 6 months that were less apparent in the waitlist group of participants. On broader measures of mental health and well-being, the benefits of the online tools were less apparent. Overall, the results suggest that online self-help cognitive behaviour therapy and mindfulness-based therapy tools should be explored further as a means of providing cost-effective mental health support to at least those autistic individuals who can engage effectively with such online tools.

title: Autism and Epilepsy in Patients With Tuberous Sclerosis Complex.
authors: Specchio N, Pietrafusa N, Trivisano M, Moavero R, De Palma L, Ferretti A, Vigevano F, Curatolo P
abstract: Introduction: Individuals with Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC) are at increased risk of developing both epilepsy and autism spectrum disorder (ASD), but the relationship between these conditions is little understood. We reviewed published reports to elucidate the relationship between ASD, epilepsy, and TSC, and to define the genetic and neurological risk factors. Methods: Articles (January 2004-May 2019) were identified via PubMed, EMBASE, and CENTRAL databases. Article inclusion required report on individuals with TSC-associated ASD and epilepsy with prevalence, odds ratio, or rate report on the comorbidity of ASD in epileptic patients due to TSC. Results: A total of 841 abstracts were identified in the original search. Thirty-six articles were included, which identified study populations, ASD measures used, and study confounders as bias factors. This review included 2,666 TSC patients, with a mean age of 15.9 years (range 1.94-30.3 years). The percentage of TSC patients with epilepsy and autism was 33.7%. Patients with TSC and autism showed more frequent seizures and earlier epilepsy onset than TSC patients without autism. ASD and intractable epilepsy were both predicted by a higher number of areas with dysplastic features revealed in brain MR scans. ASD, the onset of seizures in children 3 tubers have all been associated with an increased risk of refractory epilepsy in TSC patients. However, the direction of the relationship is not clear because a history of epilepsy, or infantile spasms in patients with TSC is also associated with an increased likelihood of ASD. Overall, 73.2% of patients carried TSC2 genetic variant and, among patients with TSC and autism, the percentage of TSC2 individuals was 85.6%. Conclusions: The complex interrelationship between TSC, autism, and epilepsy, coupled with limited knowledge on the neurobiological basis for the interrelationship, limits overall understanding and opportunities for management. The results of this review highlight the need for early identification and management to optimize favorable outcomes in the most vulnerable individuals with TSC. Regardless of whether studies are considered individually or collectively, interpretation is made difficult due to the differences between the studies, most notably between methods and diagnostic criteria used to assess intellectual ability.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista tiene complejo de esclerosis tuberosa (CET), conviene hablar con su equipo médico sobre la epilepsia y el desarrollo desde pronto, y anotar cuándo ocurren las crisis para compartirlo en las consultas. Es una revisión sistemática de 36 artículos, con 2,666 personas con CET, de edad media 15.9 años. Las personas con CET y autismo tuvieron crisis más frecuentes y epilepsia más temprana. No está claro qué causa qué, y los estudios diferían mucho en métodos y criterios. No es una regla para cada persona; las decisiones médicas corresponden a su clínico.
sheet.en: If an autistic person has tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC), it helps to talk with their medical team early about epilepsy and development, and to note when seizures happen so you can share it at appointments. This is a systematic review of 36 articles, covering 2,666 people with TSC, with a mean age of 15.9 years. People with TSC and autism had more frequent seizures and earlier epilepsy onset. The direction of the relationship is unclear, and the studies differed a lot in methods and criteria. It is not a rule for every person; medical decisions belong to their clinician.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person har tuberös skleros (TSC) kan det hjälpa att tidigt prata med vårdteamet om epilepsi och utveckling, och att anteckna när anfall inträffar så att du kan ta upp det på besök. Detta är en systematisk översikt av 36 artiklar med 2,666 personer med TSC, medelålder 15.9 år. Personer med TSC och autism hade tätare anfall och tidigare debut av epilepsi. Det är oklart vad som orsakar vad, och studierna skilde sig mycket i metoder och kriterier. Det är ingen regel för varje person; medicinska beslut hör till den behandlande kliniker.

title: Prevalence of physical and mental health conditions in Medicare-enrolled, autistic older adults.
authors: Hand BN, Angell AM, Harris L, Carpenter LA
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: While there is emerging evidence on the prevalence of physical and mental health conditions among autistic adults, less is known about this population's needs during older adulthood (aged 65+). We conducted a cross-sectional retrospective cohort study of 2016-2017 Medicare data to compare the prevalence of physical and mental health conditions in a national sample of autistic older adults (N = 4685) to a matched population comparison (N = 46,850) cohort. Autistic older adults had significantly greater odds of nearly all physical health conditions including epilepsy (odds ratio = 18.9; 95% confidence interval = 17.2-20.7), Parkinson's disease (odds ratio = 6.1; 95% confidence interval = 5.3-7.0), and gastrointestinal conditions (odds ratio = 5.2; 95% confidence interval = 4.9-5.5). Most mental health conditions were more common among autistic older adults, including schizophrenia and psychotic disorders (odds ratio = 25.3; 95% confidence interval = 22.4-28.7), attention deficit disorders (odds ratio = 24.4; 95% confidence interval = 16.2-31.0), personality disorders (odds ratio = 24.1; 95% confidence interval = 17.8-32.5), and suicidality or self-inflicted injury (odds ratio = 11.1; 95% confidence interval = 8.9-13.8). Health conditions commonly associated with advanced age in the general population (e.g. osteoporosis, cognitive disorders, heart disease, cancer, cerebrovascular disease, osteoarthritis) were also significantly more common among autistic older adults. By highlighting the significant physical and mental health needs for which autistic older adults require care, our findings can inform healthcare systems, healthcare providers, and public health initiatives seeking to promote well-being in this growing population.

sheet.es: Si cuidas de una persona autista mayor, conviene llevar a las consultas un registro de su salud física y mental y pedir revisiones periódicas de ambas. Es un estudio retrospectivo transversal con datos de Medicare de 2016-2017: se comparó a 4685 personas autistas mayores con 46,850 personas de una comparación poblacional. Casi todas las afecciones físicas y la mayoría de las mentales, incluidas suicidalidad o autolesión, eran más frecuentes entre las personas autistas. Solo muestra asociaciones en registros de seguros, no explica causas ni predice a cada persona. Si te preocupa una posible autolesión o suicidio, busca ayuda profesional: un clínico, un servicio de salud o un servicio de crisis; en peligro inmediato, llama al número de emergencias de tu país.
sheet.en: If you support an older autistic person, it helps to bring a record of their physical and mental health to appointments and to ask for regular check-ups covering both. This was a cross-sectional retrospective cohort study of 2016-2017 Medicare data, comparing 4685 autistic older adults with a matched population comparison group of 46,850. Nearly all physical conditions and most mental health conditions, including suicidality or self-inflicted injury, were more common among autistic older adults. It only shows associations in insurance records, does not explain causes, and cannot predict any one person. If you are worried about possible self-harm or suicide, contact professional help: a clinician, a health service or a crisis service; in immediate danger, call your country's emergency number.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en äldre autistisk person kan det hjälpa att ta med en överblick över hens fysiska och psykiska hälsa till vårdbesök och be om regelbundna kontroller av båda. Studien var en tvärsnittsstudie med retrospektiv kohort av Medicare-data från 2016-2017, där 4685 äldre autistiska vuxna jämfördes med en matchad jämförelsegrupp på 46,850 personer. Nästan alla fysiska tillstånd och de flesta psykiska tillstånd, inklusive suicidalitet eller självskada, var vanligare bland äldre autistiska vuxna. Den visar bara samband i försäkringsregister, förklarar inte orsaker och kan inte förutsäga en enskild person. Om du oroar dig för möjlig självskada eller suicid, kontakta professionell hjälp: en läkare, vården eller en kristjänst; vid akut fara, ring nödnumret i ditt land.

title: ENACT (ENvironmental enrichment for infants; parenting with Acceptance and Commitment Therapy): a randomised controlled trial of an innovative intervention for infants at risk of autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Whittingham K, McGlade A, Kulasinghe K, Mitchell AE, Heussler H, Boyd RN
abstract: Introduction Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition with impacts on behaviour, cognition, communication, social interaction and family mental health. This paper reports the protocol of a randomised controlled trial (RCT) of a very early intervention, ENACT (ENvironmental enrichment for infants; parenting with Acceptance and Commitment Therapy), for families of infants at risk of ASD. Methods and analysis We aim to recruit 66 mothers of infants at risk of ASD (ie, infants with a sibling or parent diagnosed with ASD) to this RCT. Families will be randomly assigned to care-as-usual or ENACT. ENACT is a very early intervention, leveraging parent-child interactions to improve early social reciprocity, while supporting parental mental health and the parent-child relationship through Acceptance and Commitment Therapy. Intervention content is delivered online (approximately 8 hours) and supported by more than 7 consultations with a clinician. Parents will perform the social reciprocity intervention with their child (30 min per day). Assessments at four time points (baseline, 3 months, 6 months, and 12 months corrected age) will assess parent-infant interaction, parental mental health, infant development and early ASD markers. Analysis will be by intention to treat using general linear models for RCTs. Ethics and dissemination This protocol has been approved by the Children's Health Queensland Hospital and Health Service Human Research Ethics Committee (HREC/19/QCHQ/50131) and the University of Queensland Human Research Ethics Committee (2019000558). If efficacy is demonstrated, the intervention has the potential for wide and accessible dissemination. Trial registration number Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry (ACTRN12618002046280).

sheet.es: Si tienes un bebé con una hermana, hermano, madre o padre autista, quizá te interese saber que se está probando un programa muy temprano que usa los momentos de juego e interacción diarios y apoya también tu salud mental como cuidador. Aún no hay resultados. Este artículo solo describe el plan de un ensayo aleatorizado: se prevé reclutar 66 madres, y las familias recibirían el programa en línea o la atención habitual. Su límite: sin resultados no sabemos si ayuda, y no sirve como regla para todas las familias.
sheet.en: If your baby has an autistic sibling or parent, you may like to know that a very early programme is being tested. It uses everyday play and interaction, and also supports your own mental health as a caregiver. There are no results yet. This paper only describes the plan for a randomised trial: it aims to recruit 66 mothers, and families would get either the online programme or usual care. The limit: without results we do not know if it helps, and it is not a rule for every family.
sheet.sv: Om din bebis har ett autistiskt syskon eller en autistisk förälder kan det vara bra att veta att ett mycket tidigt program prövas. Det använder vardagligt samspel och lek och stöder också din egen psykiska hälsa som vårdare. Några resultat finns ännu inte. Artikeln beskriver bara planen för en randomiserad studie: man vill rekrytera 66 mödrar, och familjerna får antingen det webbaserade programmet eller vanlig vård. Begränsningen: utan resultat vet vi inte om det hjälper, och det gäller inte som regel för alla familjer.

title: Characteristics of university students supported by counseling services: Analysis of psychological tests and pulse rate variability.
authors: Adachi Y, Yoshikawa H, Yokoyama S, Iwasa K
abstract: Objective Mental health is an essential issue during adolescence. The number of students who use counseling services is increasing in universities. We attempted to confirm the characteristics of the students who access counseling services using both psychological tests and pulse rate variability (PRV) for better support for students' academic success. Methods We recruited the participants for this study from the students who had counseling sessions at Kanazawa University (Group S). As a control group, we also recruited students who had no experience in counseling services (Group H). We obtained health information from the database of annual health checkups. Participants received the Wechsler Adult Intelligence Scale (WAIS)-III, Autism-Spectrum Quotient (AQ), Sukemune-Hiew (S-H) Resilience Test, and State-Trait Anxiety Inventory-JYZ (STAI). We also studied the 12-Item Short-Form Health Survey (SF-12v2) for testing Health-Related Quality of Life (HRQOL). As a physiological test, we examined the spectral analyses of pulse rate variability (PRV) by accelerating plethysmography. We performed a linear analysis of PRV for low-frequency power (LF: 0.02-0.15 Hz) and high-frequency power (HF: 0.15-0.50 Hz). We also conducted a non-linear analysis of PRV for the largest Lyapunov exponent (LLE). Additionally, we examined participants' blood for autoantibodies against glutamate decarboxylase (GAD) 65. Results A total of 105 students participated in this study. Group S had 37 participants (Male: 26, Female: 11), and Group H had 68 participants (Male: 27, Female 41). There were five males and one female in Group S who had diagnoses of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), and three males in Group S were diagnosed with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) by medical institutes. Additionally, four males and two females in Group S had diagnoses of ASD with ADHD by medical institutes. A male with ASD in Group S had epilepsy. The students of Group S had characteristics as follows: 1) lower power of Working Memory Index (WMI) despite high Full-Scale Intelligent Quotient (FSIQ), 2) higher ASD traits especially in Male, 3) lower resilience powers, 4) higher anxiety trait, 5) lower Health-Related Quality of Life (HRQOL) in Role/social component in both Male and Female, 6) lower HRQOL in Mental component in Male 7) shifting of autonomic nervous balance toward higher sympathetic activity. Conclusion We could confirm the characteristics of students who visited counseling rooms for mental support (Group S). We also found gender differences in specificities of Group S. The educational system is changing rapidly to adjust social requests. These changes make conflict with the features of students of Group S. We should think about appropriate supports for the students who would pioneer the future of humanity.

sheet.es: Si apoyas a un estudiante universitario autista o con ansiedad, conviene mirar más allá de las notas: la memoria de trabajo, el cansancio social y la tensión del cuerpo pueden influir en cómo vive los estudios. Pregúntale qué le ayuda y qué le pesa, y ofrécele apoyos concretos. Es un estudio con 105 estudiantes de una universidad de Japón: 37 que usaban orientación psicológica y 68 que no. El grupo de orientación mostró más rasgos autistas, más ansiedad y menos resiliencia. Sus límites: es una muestra pequeña, de un solo lugar, y no explica causas ni sirve como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If you support a university student who is autistic or anxious, look beyond grades: working memory, social exhaustion and bodily tension may shape how they experience study. Ask what helps and what weighs on them, and offer concrete supports. This study involved 105 students at one Japanese university: 37 who used counseling services and 68 who had not. The counseling group showed more autistic traits, more anxiety and lower resilience. Its limits: the sample is small and from one place, it cannot explain causes, and it is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en student som är autistisk eller ängslig: se bortom betygen. Arbetsminne, social trötthet och kroppslig anspänning kan påverka hur studierna upplevs. Fråga vad som hjälper och vad som tynger, och erbjud konkret stöd. Studien omfattade 105 studenter vid ett japanskt universitet: 37 som använde studievägledning eller samtalsstöd och 68 som inte gjort det. Samtalsgruppen visade fler autistiska drag, mer oro och lägre motståndskraft. Begränsningar: urvalet är litet och från en plats, studien förklarar inte orsaker och gäller inte som regel för varje person.

title: Understanding Different Aspects of Caregiving for Individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASDs) a Narrative Review of the Literature.
authors: Samadi H, Samadi SA
abstract: Background There has been a considerable endeavor to understand associated challenges of caregiving for a child with Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASDs) and to develop the necessary skills and approaches to assist parents of children with ASD. Different studies have been stressed the importance and need for parental involvement in the intervention process to increase positive impacts. Methods The process of caregiving and the associated challenges should be understood from different aspects to be able to facilitate parent involvement in intervention implementation. In a narrative literature review, ten selected reviews were considered and each review considered a special aspect of caregiving for an individual with ASD. Results Five main different factors in the available literature and reviews were considered as different themes that needed to be reconsidered in the studies on the impacts of caregiving for an individual with ASD. Conclusions It is concluded that to facilitate parental involvement in the intervention process, and to support caregivers of this group of individuals this review highlights the need for improved research in some proposed areas in this field and to bridge the gap between research and practice in this field.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista, tu experiencia y tu bienestar importan también en las intervenciones: pide que te escuchen y que te expliquen cómo participar de forma realista, sin cargarte más. Esta es una revisión narrativa de 2020 que analizó diez revisiones previas, cada una centrada en un aspecto del cuidado, y agrupó lo hallado en cinco temas. Sus límites: no ofrece pautas concretas, no detalla qué funciona para cada familia y pide más investigación para acercar la práctica a lo que se estudia.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic person, your experience and wellbeing matter in any intervention too: ask professionals to listen to you and to explain realistically how you can take part, without adding to your load. This is a 2020 narrative review that looked at ten earlier reviews, each focused on one aspect of caregiving, and grouped what it found into five themes. Its limits: it gives no concrete step-by-step guidance, does not show what works for each family, and calls for more research to bring practice closer to research.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person är också din egen upplevelse och ditt välmående viktiga i insatser: be att få bli lyssnad på och att få veta realistiskt hur du kan delta, utan att få mer att bära. Detta är en narrativ översikt från 2020 som gick igenom tio tidigare översikter, var och en inriktad på en sida av omsorgsarbetet, och samlade resultaten i fem teman. Begränsningar: den ger inga konkreta steg, visar inte vad som fungerar för varje familj och efterlyser mer forskning för att föra praktik och forskning närmare varandra.

title: Managing job stress in teachers of children with autism: A rational emotive occupational health coaching control trial.
authors: Ogba FN, Onyishi CN, Victor-Aigbodion V, Abada IM, Eze UN, Obiweluozo PE, Ugodulunwa CN, Igu NCN, Okorie CO, Onu JC, Eze A, Ezeani EO, Ebizie EN, Onwu AO
abstract: Background/objective Teaching has been found to be 1 of the most stressful occupations worldwide. Stress associated with teaching is more critical among teachers teaching children with special needs in general and those with autism specifically, partly due to the heterogeneous nature of the disorders. The purpose of this study was to investigate the effectiveness of Rational Emotive Occupational Health Coaching (REOHC) in minimizing job stress in teachers of children with autism (CWA). Methods A group-randomized waitlist control-trial design was adopted. A sample of 87 teachers of CWA who participated in the study was randomized into the immediate intervention group (IIG) and waitlist group (WLG). Participants were evaluated on 3 occasions: pretest, post-test and follow-up. Three instruments (Occupational Stress Index, Perceived Occupational Stress Scale and Stress Symptom Scale) were used to measure dimensions of job stress. After the pretest exercise, the IIG participated in a 2-hour REOHC programme weekly for a period of 12 weeks. Post- and follow-up evaluations were conducted respectively at 2 weeks and 3 months after the REOHC programme. Those in WLG were exposed to the REOHC after the follow-up assessment. Data collected were analysed using t-test statistics, repeated measures analysis of variance and bar charts. Results Results revealed that the perceived stress and stress symptoms of the REOHC group reduced significantly over WLG at post-test, and follow-up assessments. Changes in the occupational stress index scores across pre-, post- and follow-up measurements were minimal and could not account for a significant difference between the IIG and WLG. Conclusion It was concluded that REOHC is effective in reducing subjective feelings and physiological symptoms of job stress, even when the objective stressors remain constant among teachers of CWA and other employees who work in stressful occupational environments.

sheet.es: Si cuidas o enseñas a niños autistas, tu propio estrés laboral importa y se puede trabajar con apoyo estructurado. Este ensayo con asignación aleatoria incluyó a 87 docentes de niños autistas. Quienes hicieron un programa semanal de coaching de 2 horas durante 12 semanas refirieron menos estrés percibido y menos síntomas de estrés que el grupo en lista de espera, también en el seguimiento. Los factores de estrés del trabajo apenas cambiaron. Límites: participaron solo docentes, no familias, y no demuestra que le sirva a cada persona ni que cambie las condiciones del trabajo.
sheet.en: If you teach or support autistic children, your own job stress matters, and structured support may help you manage it. This randomized trial included 87 teachers of autistic children. Those who took a weekly 2-hour coaching programme for 12 weeks reported less perceived stress and fewer stress symptoms than a waitlist group, including at follow-up. The stressors of the job itself barely changed. Limits: only teachers took part, not families, and it does not show the programme works for everyone or that it changes working conditions.
sheet.sv: Om du undervisar eller stöttar autistiska barn spelar din egen arbetsstress roll, och strukturerat stöd kan hjälpa dig hantera den. Denna randomiserade studie omfattade 87 lärare till autistiska barn. De som gick ett coachingprogram på 2 timmar i veckan under 12 veckor rapporterade mindre upplevd stress och färre stressymtom än väntelistgruppen, även vid uppföljningen. Själva stressfaktorerna i arbetet förändrades knappt. Begränsningar: bara lärare deltog, inte familjer, och studien visar inte att programmet fungerar för alla eller att det ändrar arbetsvillkoren.

title: Autism spectrum disorder at the crossroad between genes and environment: contributions, convergences, and interactions in ASD developmental pathophysiology.
authors: Cheroni C, Caporale N, Testa G
abstract: The complex pathophysiology of autism spectrum disorder encompasses interactions between genetic and environmental factors. On the one hand, hundreds of genes, converging at the functional level on selective biological domains such as epigenetic regulation and synaptic function, have been identified to be either causative or risk factors of autism. On the other hand, exposure to chemicals that are widespread in the environment, such as endocrine disruptors, has been associated with adverse effects on human health, including neurodevelopmental disorders. Interestingly, experimental results suggest an overlap in the regulatory pathways perturbed by genetic mutations and environmental factors, depicting convergences and complex interplays between genetic susceptibility and toxic insults. The pervasive nature of chemical exposure poses pivotal challenges for neurotoxicological studies, regulatory agencies, and policy makers. This highlights an emerging need of developing new integrative models, including biomonitoring, epidemiology, experimental, and computational tools, able to capture real-life scenarios encompassing the interaction between chronic exposure to mixture of substances and individuals' genetic backgrounds. In this review, we address the intertwined roles of genetic lesions and environmental insults. Specifically, we outline the transformative potential of stem cell models, coupled with omics analytical approaches at increasingly single cell resolution, as converging tools to experimentally dissect the pathogenic mechanisms underlying neurodevelopmental disorders, as well as to improve developmental neurotoxicology risk assessment.

sheet.es: Para mañana por la mañana: este estudio no ofrece nada que cambiar en la rutina diaria. Lo útil es saber que el autismo no se explica por una sola causa y que nadie tiene que sentirse culpable por lo que hizo o no hizo. Es una revisión que reúne investigación sobre genes y exposición a sustancias químicas del ambiente, y sugiere que ambos pueden influirse entre sí. Sus límites: gran parte de los resultados son experimentales, no se basan en personas concretas, y no permiten decir qué causó el autismo de nadie. Para dudas de salud, consulta a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: For tomorrow morning: this study offers nothing to change in your daily routine. What it can give you is the reminder that autism is not explained by a single cause, and that no caregiver needs to feel guilty about what they did or did not do. It is a review that brings together research on genes and on exposure to chemicals in the environment, suggesting the two may influence each other. Its limits: much of the evidence is experimental rather than drawn from individual people, and it cannot tell anyone what caused their own autism. For health questions, talk to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Till i morgon bitti: den här studien ger inget att ändra i vardagen. Det den kan ge är en påminnelse om att autism inte förklaras av en enda orsak, och att ingen vårdnadshavare behöver känna skuld över vad hen gjort eller inte gjort. Det är en översikt som samlar forskning om gener och om exponering för kemikalier i miljön, och den antyder att de två kan påverka varandra. Begränsningar: mycket av underlaget är experimentellt och inte hämtat från enskilda personer, och det kan inte säga vad som orsakade någons autism. Vid hälsofrågor, prata med en kliniker.

title: A Measurement Invariance Analysis of the Interpersonal Needs Questionnaire and Acquired Capability for Suicide Scale in Autistic and Non-Autistic Adults.
authors: Pelton MK, Crawford H, Robertson AE, Rodgers J, Baron-Cohen S, Cassidy S
abstract: Background: Autistic adults are more likely to engage in suicidal thoughts and behaviors, but there is little research to explore the underlying reasons. It is unclear whether self-report suicide scales that have been designed for non-autistic people accurately measure suicide risk constructs in autistic people. Therefore, this study explored, for the first time, whether the measurement properties of the self-report scales of the Interpersonal Theory of Suicide are equivalent in autistic and non-autistic adults. Methods: In this study, responses from 342 autistic and 353 non-autistic people on the Interpersonal Needs Questionnaire-10 (INQ-10) and Acquired Capability for Suicide Scale-Fearlessness about Death (ACSS-FAD) were compared by using measurement invariance analysis. Data were gathered through an online cross-sectional survey of the self-report measures. Results: Results suggest that measurement properties of the INQ-10 were different in autistic people. Autistic characteristics, such as different theory of mind and preference for concrete language, may have led the scale items to load differently on the factors in the autistic group than in the non-autistic group. The measurement properties of the ACSS-FAD were invariant between autistic and non-autistic people. Conclusions: Scores on the INQ-10 cannot be meaningfully compared between autistic and non-autistic people due to different measurement properties. Future research could explore how autistic people experience the concepts of burdensomeness and belonging, to consider how measures could accurately capture this. This would allow researchers to explore the role of these constructs in the development of suicidal thoughts and behaviors in autistic people. Clinicians should be aware that suicide risk factors may present differently in autistic people. Scores on the ACSS-FAD can be meaningfully compared, but the negatively worded scale items may pose similar response difficulties to autistic and non-autistic people.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista rellena un cuestionario sobre pensamientos suicidas, conviene hablar con ella sobre lo que entendió de cada pregunta, sin dar por hecho que significan lo mismo que para otras personas. Es un estudio con encuesta en línea en el que participaron 342 personas autistas y 353 no autistas. Una de las escalas, la INQ-10, midió de forma distinta en las personas autistas, y no se pudieron comparar sus puntuaciones. La otra, la ACSS-FAD, sí fue comparable. El estudio no indica qué hacer en cada caso y no vale para todas las personas. Si te preocupa la seguridad de alguien, acude a un profesional clínico, a un servicio de salud o a un servicio de crisis. Si hay peligro inmediato, llama al número de emergencias de tu país.
sheet.en: If an autistic person fills in a questionnaire about suicidal thoughts, it helps to talk with them about what each question meant to them, rather than assuming it means the same as for other people. This was an online survey study with 342 autistic and 353 non-autistic adults. One scale, the INQ-10, measured differently in autistic people, so its scores could not be compared. The other, the ACSS-FAD, was comparable. The study does not say what to do in individual cases and does not apply to everyone. If you are worried about someone's safety, contact a clinician, a health service or a crisis service. In immediate danger, call the emergency number of your country.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person fyller i ett formulär om självmordstankar är det bra att prata med hen om hur varje fråga uppfattades, i stället för att anta att den betyder samma sak som för andra. Studien var en webbenkät med 342 autistiska och 353 icke-autistiska vuxna. Ett formulär, INQ-10, mätte annorlunda hos autistiska personer, så poängen kunde inte jämföras. Det andra, ACSS-FAD, gick att jämföra. Studien säger inte vad man ska göra i enskilda fall och gäller inte alla. Om du oroar dig för någons säkerhet, kontakta en läkare eller annan behandlare, en vårdinstans eller en kristjänst. Vid akut fara, ring ditt lands nödnummer.

title: Social Capital and Autism in Young Adulthood: Applying Social Network Methods to Measure the Social Capital of Autistic Young Adults.
authors: McGhee Hassrick E, Sosnowy C, Graham Holmes L, Walton J, Shattuck PT
abstract: Social isolation is a core challenge associated with autism. Interpersonal relationships and the resources and support embedded in the social networks of autistic young adults could impact key adult outcomes, including quality of life, mental health, employment, and independence. However, little research systematically measures the networks of autistic young adults and network impact on key adult outcomes. This article demonstrates how social network analysis can be adapted for the field of autism to measure young adult networks. We provide examples as to how this approach could be implemented to yield key insights into the amount and quality of interpersonal relationships and the types of resources embedded in the networks of autistic young adults. The network protocol was feasibility tested with autistic adults during the posthigh school transition period ( n = 17, 19-27 years). The parents of three of the recruited young adults also successfully completed a complementary network survey, allowing for the inclusion of the parent-reported network using duocentric network analysis, never before applied to parent-child networks. The implementation data collected from the study suggest feasibility of egocentric and duocentric approaches, with several important modifications to adapt the measure for the field of autism. The future potential of social network research for understanding autism in adulthood is discussed.

sheet.es: Para mañana: si acompañas a un joven autista adulto, puedes preguntarle con calma quién forma parte de su vida y qué apoyo recibe de cada persona, en vez de suponer que está aislado. Este estudio probó con 17 adultos autistas de 19-27 años, tras terminar el instituto, una forma de medir sus redes sociales. Tres familias también respondieron. Mostró que es viable con adaptaciones. Es una prueba de viabilidad, con pocas personas, y no mide resultados ni sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: For tomorrow: if you support an autistic young adult, you can calmly ask who is part of their life and what support each person gives, rather than assuming they are isolated. This study tested a way to map social networks with 17 autistic adults aged 19-27, after leaving high school. Parents of three of them also took part. It was feasible with some adaptations. It was a small feasibility test that did not measure outcomes, and it is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Till i morgon: om du stöttar en autistisk ung vuxen kan du lugnt fråga vilka som ingår i personens liv och vilket stöd var och en ger, i stället för att anta att personen är isolerad. Studien testade ett sätt att kartlägga sociala nätverk med 17 autistiska vuxna i åldern 19-27 år efter gymnasiet. Föräldrar till tre av dem deltog också. Det fungerade med vissa anpassningar. Det var ett litet genomförbarhetstest som inte mätte resultat, och det är ingen regel för alla.

title: Is Camouflaging Autistic Traits Associated with Suicidal Thoughts and Behaviours? Expanding the Interpersonal Psychological Theory of Suicide in an Undergraduate Student Sample.
authors: Cassidy SA, Gould K, Townsend E, Pelton M, Robertson AE, Rodgers J
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: The current study explored whether people who camouflage autistic traits are more likely to experience thwarted belongingness and suicidality, as predicted by the Interpersonal Psychological Theory of Suicide (IPTS). 160 undergraduate students (86.9% female, 18-23 years) completed a cross-sectional online survey from 8th February to 30th May 2019 including self-report measures of thwarted belongingness and perceived burdensomeness, autistic traits, depression, anxiety, camouflaging autistic traits, and lifetime suicidality. Results suggest that camouflaging autistic traits is associated with increased risk of experiencing thwarted belongingness and lifetime suicidality. It is important for suicide theories such as the IPTS to include variables relevant to the broader autism phenotype, to increase applicability of models to both autistic and non-autistic people.

title: Measurement Properties of the Suicidal Behaviour Questionnaire-Revised in Autistic Adults.
authors: Cassidy SA, Bradley L, Cogger-Ward H, Shaw R, Bowen E, Glod M, Baron-Cohen S, Rodgers J
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: We explored the appropriateness and measurement properties of a suicidality assessment tool (SBQ-R) developed for the general population, in autistic adults-a high risk group for suicide. 188 autistic adults and 183 general population adults completed the tool online, and a sub-sample (n = 15) were interviewed while completing the tool. Multi-group factorial invariance analysis of the online survey data found evidence for metric non-invariance of the SBQ-R, particularly for items three (communication of suicidal intent) and four (likelihood of suicide attempt in the future). Cognitive interviews revealed that autistic adults did not interpret these items as intended by the tool designers. Results suggest autistic adults interpret key questions regarding suicide risk differently to the general population. Future research must adapt tools to better capture suicidality in autistic adults.

sheet.es: Si usas un cuestionario de riesgo de suicidio con una persona autista, no te fíes solo de la puntuación: pregunta con calma qué entendió en cada pregunta y conversa con ella. Se estudió con 188 adultos autistas y 183 adultos de la población general que completaron en línea el cuestionario SBQ-R; 15 de ellos también hicieron entrevistas mientras lo respondían. Los adultos autistas interpretaron de forma distinta dos preguntas: la comunicación de la intención suicida y la probabilidad de un intento futuro. Es un solo estudio, con una herramienta concreta, y no dice nada sobre una persona en particular. Si te preocupa alguien, busca ayuda profesional: un clínico, un servicio de salud o un servicio de crisis. Ante peligro inmediato, llama al número de emergencias de tu país.
sheet.en: If a suicide-risk questionnaire is used with an autistic person, don't rely on the score alone: calmly ask what they understood each question to mean, and talk it through together. In this study, 188 autistic adults and 183 general population adults completed the SBQ-R online, and 15 were also interviewed while answering. Autistic adults interpreted two questions differently: communicating suicidal intent and the likelihood of a future attempt. It is one study of one tool, and it cannot tell you about any individual person. If you are worried about someone, seek professional help from a clinician, a health service or a crisis service. In immediate danger, call the emergency number of your country.
sheet.sv: Om ett frågeformulär om självmordsrisk används med en autistisk person, lita inte bara på poängen: fråga lugnt hur personen förstod varje fråga och prata igenom det tillsammans. I studien fyllde 188 autistiska vuxna och 183 vuxna i allmänbefolkningen i SBQ-R online, och 15 intervjuades också medan de svarade. De autistiska vuxna tolkade två frågor annorlunda: att berätta om självmordsavsikt och sannolikheten för ett framtida försök. Det är en enda studie av ett enda verktyg och säger inget om en enskild person. Om du är orolig för någon, sök professionell hjälp hos en kliniker, en vårdinrättning eller en krisjour. Vid akut fara, ring det nödnummer som gäller i ditt land.

title: Eating and Mealtime Behaviors in Patients with Autism Spectrum Disorder: Current Perspectives.
authors: Margari L, Marzulli L, Gabellone A, de Giambattista C
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by impaired social and communication skills and repetitive and restrictive behaviors. Children and adolescents with ASD are more likely to present feeding problems than their typically developing peers are. The present narrative review of literature aims to highlight the most recent evidence about epidemiology and presentations of eating and mealtime behavioral abnormalities in ASD from infancy to adolescence. Abnormalities in breastfeeding and acceptance of complementary foods have been described by most of the studies evaluating ASD early feeding history. Among the various eating and mealtime behaviors identified in ASD children and adolescents, the most common was food selectivity. The present review also provides brief overviews of the various aspects of food that may influence food acceptance by ASD patients and of the correlation between eating problems and ASD core symptoms, as well as with cognitive level, language skills, and family environment. However, studies evaluating eating problems in ASD children and adolescents are very heterogeneous and they show methodological differences. Moreover, the absence of unique definitions of eating and mealtime behaviors in ASD further limits the comparability of studies.

sheet.es: Si la comida es difícil, probablemente no sea cuestión de caprichos: la selectividad con los alimentos es lo más habitual en niños y adolescentes autistas. Observe qué aspectos de la comida (como se describe en la revisión) influyen en que la acepte y anótelos con calma, sin presionar. Es una revisión narrativa de estudios sobre alimentación desde la infancia hasta la adolescencia. Sus límites: los estudios son muy heterogéneos, usan métodos distintos y no comparten definiciones, así que no sirve como regla para cada persona. Si le preocupa la alimentación, consulte con un profesional sanitario.
sheet.en: If mealtimes are hard, it is probably not about being difficult: food selectivity was the most common eating pattern found in autistic children and adolescents. Notice which features of the food seem to affect whether it is accepted, and note them calmly, without pressure. This is a narrative review of studies on eating from infancy to adolescence. Its limits: the studies are very heterogeneous, use different methods and lack shared definitions, so it is not a rule for every person. If eating worries you, talk with a health professional.
sheet.sv: Om måltider är svåra handlar det troligen inte om olydnad: selektivitet kring mat var det vanligaste ätmönstret hos autistiska barn och ungdomar. Lägg märke till vilka egenskaper hos maten som verkar påverka om den accepteras, och anteckna lugnt utan press. Det här är en narrativ översikt av studier om ätande från spädbarnsår till tonår. Begränsningar: studierna är mycket olikartade, använder olika metoder och saknar gemensamma definitioner, så resultaten är ingen regel för varje person. Om maten oroar dig, prata med en vårdgivare.

title: Differential mirror neuron system (MNS) activation during action observation with and without social-emotional components in autism: a meta-analysis of neuroimaging studies.
authors: Chan MMY, Han YMY
abstract: Background Impaired imitation has been found to be an important factor contributing to social communication deficits in individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). It has been hypothesized that the neural correlate of imitation, the mirror neuron system (MNS), is dysfunctional in ASD, resulting in imitation impairment as one of the key behavioral manifestations in ASD. Previous MNS studies produced inconsistent results, leaving the debate of whether "broken" mirror neurons in ASD are unresolved. Methods This meta-analysis aimed to explore the differences in MNS activation patterns between typically developing (TD) and ASD individuals when they observe biological motions with or without social-emotional components. Effect size signed differential mapping (ES-SDM) was adopted to synthesize the available fMRI data. Results ES-SDM analysis revealed hyperactivation in the right inferior frontal gyrus and left supplementary motor area in ASD during observation of biological motions. Subgroup analysis of experiments involving the observation of stimuli with or without emotional component revealed hyperactivation in the left inferior parietal lobule and left supplementary motor during action observation without emotional components, whereas hyperactivation of the right inferior frontal gyrus was found during action observation with emotional components in ASD. Subgroup analyses of age showed hyperactivation of the bilateral inferior frontal gyrus in ASD adolescents, while hyperactivation in the right inferior frontal gyrus was noted in ASD adults. Meta-regression within ASD individuals indicated that the right cerebellum crus I activation increased with age, while the left inferior temporal gyrus activation decreased with age. Limitations This meta-analysis is limited in its generalization of the findings to individuals with ASD by the restricted age range, heterogeneous study sample, and the large within-group variation in MNS activation patterns during object observation. Furthermore, we only included action observation studies which might limit the generalization of our results to the imitation deficits in ASD. In addition, the relatively small sample size for individual studies might also potentially overestimate the effect sizes. Conclusion The MNS is impaired in ASD. The abnormal activation patterns were found to be modulated by the nature of stimuli and age, which might explain the contradictory results from earlier studies on the "broken mirror neuron" debate.

sheet.es: Tomorrow no hace falta cambiar nada en casa por este estudio: no hay una estrategia nueva que probar. Lo útil es recordar que cada persona autista procesa lo que observa a su manera, y que enseñar con modelos claros y sin prisa puede ayudar a algunas. Evidencia: metaanálisis que reunió estudios de resonancia magnética funcional y comparó la actividad cerebral de personas autistas y no autistas al observar movimientos, con o sin componente emocional. Encontró más activación en algunas zonas, según el tipo de estímulo y la edad. Límites: edades restringidas, muestras variadas y pequeñas, y solo observación de acciones, no imitación real. No describe a cada persona.
sheet.en: This study doesn't call for any change at home tomorrow: there is no new strategy to try. What may help is remembering that each autistic person processes what they watch in their own way, and that clear, unhurried modelling can suit some people. Evidence: a meta-analysis that pooled functional MRI studies comparing brain activity in autistic and non-autistic people while watching movements, with or without an emotional element. It found more activation in some areas, depending on the type of stimulus and on age. Limits: restricted age ranges, varied and small samples, and only action observation, not actual imitation. It does not describe every individual.
sheet.sv: Den här studien kräver ingen förändring hemma i morgon: det finns ingen ny strategi att pröva. Det som kan vara till hjälp är att minnas att varje autistisk person bearbetar det hen ser på sitt sätt, och att tydliga förebilder utan stress kan passa vissa. Evidens: en metaanalys som slog ihop studier med funktionell magnetkamera och jämförde hjärnaktivitet hos autistiska och icke-autistiska personer som såg rörelser, med eller utan känslomässigt inslag. Den fann mer aktivering i vissa områden, beroende på typ av stimulus och ålder. Begränsningar: begränsade åldrar, varierande och små urval, och endast observation av handlingar, inte verklig imitation. Den beskriver inte varje person.

title: Cognitive-behavioral family therapy as psychoeducation for adolescents with high-functioning autism spectrum disorders: Aware and Care for my Autistic Traits (ACAT) program study protocol for a pragmatic multisite randomized controlled trial.
authors: Oshima F, Oshima F, William M, Takahashi N, Tsuchiyagaito A, Kuwabara H, Shiina A, Seto M, Hongo M, Iwama Y, Hirano Y, Sutoh C, Taguchi K, Yoshida T, Kawasaki Y, Ozawa Y, Masuya J, Sato N, Nakamura S,
abstract: Background One aim of an autism spectrum disorder (ASD) diagnosis is to obtain special support for the disorder, though this does not guarantee practical support. We developed a psychoeducational program using cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) and Aware and Care for my Autistic Traits (ACAT) for Japanese adolescents with high-functioning ASD and their parents. Methods This multisite study is a randomized controlled trial. In total, 24 participants will be assigned to the ACAT group and 24 to the treatment-as-usual (TAU) group. The ACAT group will receive a weekly 100-min session for 6 weeks, regular medical care, and one follow-up session. In this ongoing clinical trial, we will compare the scores of the measures recorded in the pre- and post-intervention stages between the ACAT and TAU groups. A total of 41 patients out of a target of 48 have participated in the trial to date. The primary outcome measure is the Autism Knowledge Questionnaire. Secondary outcome measures include Barriers to Access to Care Evaluation 3rd Edition, the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire, the Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scales second edition, the Parenting Resilience Elements Questionnaire, the General Health Questionnaire 12, and the Depression Self-Rating Scale for Children assessments, as well as an electroencephalographic recording. Discussion It is expected that participants in the ACAT group will significantly increase their self-understanding and awareness of ASD symptoms compared to those in the TAU group. Additionally, the ACAT group is expected to exhibit improved social adaptation and mental health if children and parents are able to better understand the ASD characteristics through sessions. This intervention will contribute to the establishment of an effective evidence-based treatment strategy for adolescents with ASD. Trial registration UMIN Register 000029851 . Registered on January 06, 2018.

sheet.es: Un programa de psicoeducación en familia puede ayudar a que adolescentes autistas y sus padres comprendan mejor las características autistas. Si os interesa, preguntad a vuestro equipo clínico por programas de este tipo. La evidencia es un protocolo de un ensayo aleatorizado en Japón: 24 participantes recibirían el programa de 6 sesiones semanales y 24 la atención habitual. Aún no hay resultados, solo expectativas de que mejore la comprensión de uno mismo. Además, el programa se probó con adolescentes descritos como de alto funcionamiento, así que puede no servir a todas las personas ni a todas las familias.
sheet.en: A family psychoeducation program may help autistic teenagers and their parents understand autistic traits better. If this appeals to you, ask your clinical team about programs like it. The evidence is a protocol for a randomized trial in Japan: 24 participants would get the program, with weekly sessions for 6 weeks, and 24 would get usual care. There are no results yet, only expectations that self-understanding will improve. It was also designed for teenagers described as high-functioning, so it may not suit every person or family.
sheet.sv: Ett psykoedukationsprogram för hela familjen kan hjälpa autistiska tonåringar och deras föräldrar att förstå autistiska drag bättre. Om det låter intressant kan ni fråga ert vårdteam om liknande program. Underlaget är ett protokoll för en randomiserad studie i Japan: 24 deltagare skulle få programmet med veckovisa träffar i 6 veckor och 24 vanlig vård. Det finns inga resultat än, bara förväntningar om bättre självförståelse. Programmet riktar sig dessutom till tonåringar som beskrivs som högfungerande, så det passar kanske inte alla personer eller familjer.

title: The relationship between intolerance of uncertainty and anxiety in autism: A systematic literature review and meta-analysis.
authors: Jenkinson R, Milne E, Thompson A
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract People who find it especially hard to cope with the unexpected or unknown are said to have an intolerance of uncertainty. Autistic individuals often report a preference for certainty and experience levels of anxiety that can interfere with their daily life. Understanding more about the link between the intolerance of uncertainty and anxiety in autistic people might lead to better treatments for anxiety being developed. Therefore, this work aimed to review previous research in order to explore this link. Twelve studies were found and their results were compared and contrasted. The autistic people who participated in the studies completed questionnaires that suggested a large number of them experienced very high levels of anxiety and intolerance of uncertainty. Of 10 studies that used relevant statistics, nine found a statistically significant link between anxiety and the intolerance of uncertainty. In general, the strength of the link was about the same as previous research found in people who did not have a diagnosis of autism. This might mean that interventions that aim to help people who are intolerant of uncertainty could be effective for autistic individuals.

sheet.es: Si la persona autista que acompañas se angustia ante lo imprevisto, reducir la incertidumbre puede aliviar su ansiedad: anticipa cambios, usa agendas visuales y explica qué va a pasar y cuándo. También puede ayudar ensayar juntos, con calma y a su ritmo, pequeñas situaciones inciertas. Este metaanálisis reunió 12 estudios con personas autistas; en nueve de diez análisis relevantes, la intolerancia a la incertidumbre se relacionó con más ansiedad, de forma similar a personas no autistas. Sus límites: se basa en cuestionarios, muestra una relación pero no prueba causa, y cada persona es distinta.
sheet.en: If the autistic person you support becomes distressed by the unexpected, reducing uncertainty may ease their anxiety: give advance notice of changes, use visual schedules, and explain what will happen and when. Gently practising small uncertain situations together, at their pace, may also help. This meta-analysis combined 12 studies with autistic participants; in nine of ten relevant analyses, intolerance of uncertainty was linked to higher anxiety, about as strongly as in non-autistic people. Limits: it relies on questionnaires, shows a link rather than cause, and every person is different.
sheet.sv: Om den autistiska person du stöttar blir orolig av det oväntade kan mindre osäkerhet lindra ångesten: förvarna om förändringar, använd bildscheman och förklara vad som ska hända och när. Att lugnt öva på små osäkra situationer tillsammans, i personens egen takt, kan också hjälpa. Denna metaanalys sammanställde 12 studier med autistiska deltagare; i nio av tio relevanta analyser hängde svårigheter att tåla osäkerhet ihop med mer ångest, ungefär lika starkt som hos icke-autistiska personer. Begränsningar: den bygger på enkäter, visar samband men inte orsak, och varje person är unik.

title: Alexithymic and autistic traits: Relevance for comorbid depression and social phobia in adults with and without autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Albantakis L, Brandi ML, Zillekens IC, Henco L, Weindel L, Thaler H, Schliephake L, Timmermans B, Schilbach L
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Adults with autism often develop mental health problems such as depression and social phobia. The reasons for this are still unclear. Many studies found that alexithymia plays an important role in mental health problems like depression. People with alexithymia have difficulties identifying and describing their emotions. Almost every second person with autism has alexithymia. Therefore, we explored in this study whether alexithymia is linked to worse mental health in autistic people. We looked at two common diagnoses, depression and social phobia. We found that alexithymia increased symptoms of depression, while autistic traits increased symptoms of social phobia. Our results suggest that alexithymia and autistic traits can increase the risk of mental health problems. An early assessment could help prevent mental health problems and improve quality of life.

sheet.es: Si la persona autista a la que cuidas tiene dificultad para identificar o describir lo que siente, puede ayudar ofrecerle apoyos para poner nombre a sus emociones (imágenes, listas, escalas) y estar atento a señales de ánimo bajo o de ansiedad social. Es un estudio de investigación con personas autistas y sin autismo, adultas. Encontró que la alexitimia se asoció con más síntomas de depresión y los rasgos autistas con más síntomas de fobia social. Sus límites: muestra una relación, no prueba causa, y no vale para todas las personas. Si tienes dudas, consulta con un profesional.
sheet.en: If the autistic person you support finds it hard to identify or describe what they feel, it may help to offer tools for naming emotions (pictures, word lists, scales) and to watch for signs of low mood or social anxiety. This was a research study with adults, autistic and non-autistic. It found that alexithymia was linked to more depression symptoms, and autistic traits to more social phobia symptoms. Its limits: it shows a link, not a cause, and it does not apply to every person. If you are worried, talk with a professional.
sheet.sv: Om den autistiska person du stöttar har svårt att identifiera eller beskriva vad hen känner kan det hjälpa att erbjuda stöd för att sätta ord på känslor (bilder, ordlistor, skalor) och att vara uppmärksam på tecken på nedstämdhet eller social ångest. Detta var en forskningsstudie med vuxna, både autistiska och icke-autistiska. Den fann att alexitymi hängde ihop med fler symtom på depression och autistiska drag med fler symtom på social fobi. Begränsningar: den visar ett samband, inte orsak, och gäller inte alla personer. Prata med en yrkesperson om du är orolig.

title: The face validity of an initial sub-typology of people with autism spectrum disorders detained in psychiatric hospitals.
authors: Barnoux M, Alexander R, Bhaumik S, Devapriam J, Duggan C, Shepstone L, Staufenberg E, Turner D, Tyler N, Viding E, Langdon PE
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic adults who have a history of committing crimes pose challenges for the criminal justice system in terms of disposal and treatment. For this reason, we investigated the validity of a proposed sub-typology of autistic adults detained in secure psychiatric hospitals. Initially, we ran a focus group with psychiatrists, clinical psychologists, healthcare workers, family members and autistic adults who had been detained in hospital to consider a sub-typology of autistic adults who may come into contact with secure psychiatric hospitals. We asked 15 psychiatrists and clinical psychologists to rate 10 clinical vignettes based on our sub-typology with three rounds; revisions to the vignettes to improve clarity were made following each round. The findings indicated that these subtypes possess face validity and raters were able to classify all 10 clinical case vignettes into the sub-typology and percentage of agreement ranged from 96% to 100% for overall subtype classification. The findings suggested that the further validity of the sub-typology should be investigated within a larger study using a clinical sample. These subtypes may help inform treatment and care pathways within hospital.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista de tu entorno está o podría estar ingresada en un hospital psiquiátrico seguro, puedes preguntar al equipo clínico cómo planifican su tratamiento y cuidados según sus necesidades concretas, y pedir participar. Este estudio consultó a un grupo con profesionales, familiares y adultos autistas, y luego 15 psiquiatras y psicólogos clínicos valoraron 10 casos clínicos ficticios; el acuerdo al clasificarlos fue del 96% al 100%. Sin embargo, no usó personas reales ni una muestra clínica, así que la clasificación aún no está confirmada y no describe a ninguna persona concreta.
sheet.en: If an autistic person you support is, or might be, in a secure psychiatric hospital, you can ask the clinical team how they plan treatment and care around their specific needs, and ask to be involved. This study first consulted a group of professionals, family members and autistic adults, then 15 psychiatrists and clinical psychologists rated 10 fictional clinical cases; agreement when classifying them ranged from 96% to 100%. However, it used no real patients or clinical sample, so the sub-typology is not yet confirmed and does not describe any individual person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person du stödjer är, eller kan komma att bli, inlagd på en säker psykiatrisk klinik kan du fråga vårdteamet hur de planerar behandling och omsorg utifrån personens egna behov, och be att få vara delaktig. Studien rådfrågade först en grupp med yrkespersoner, anhöriga och autistiska vuxna, därefter bedömde 15 psykiatriker och kliniska psykologer 10 fiktiva fall; enigheten vid klassificeringen låg mellan 96% och 100%. Den använde dock inga verkliga patienter eller något kliniskt urval, så indelningen är ännu inte bekräftad och beskriver ingen enskild person.

title: Autistic peer-to-peer information transfer is highly effective.
authors: Crompton CJ, Ropar D, Evans-Williams CV, Flynn EG, Fletcher-Watson S
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Sharing information with other people relies on the ability to communicate well. Autism is defined clinically by deficits in social communication. It may therefore be expected that autistic people find it difficult to share information with other people. We wanted to find out whether this was the case, and whether it was different when autistic people were sharing information with other autistic people or with non-autistic people. We recruited nine groups, each with eight people. In three of the groups, everyone was autistic; in three of the groups, everyone was non-autistic; and three of the groups were mixed groups where half the group was autistic and half the group was non-autistic. We told one person in each group a story and asked them to share it with another person, and for that person to share it again and so on, until everyone in the group had heard the story. We then looked at how many details of the story had been shared at each stage. We found that autistic people share information with other autistic people as well as non-autistic people do with other non-autistic people. However, when there are mixed groups of autistic and non-autistic people, much less information is shared. Participants were also asked how they felt they had got on with the other person in the interaction. The people in the mixed groups also experienced lower rapport with the person they were sharing the story with. This finding is important as it shows that autistic people have the skills to share information well with one another and experience good rapport, and that there are selective problems when autistic and non-autistic people are interacting.

sheet.es: Si tienes que transmitir información importante, prueba a hacerlo también entre personas autistas, o ten en cuenta que la comunicación entre personas autistas y no autistas puede requerir más apoyo mutuo y más comprobación de lo entendido. Evidencia: estudio con personas autistas en nueve grupos de ocho personas (autistas, no autistas y mixtos) que se pasaban una historia de una a otra. Las personas autistas compartieron detalles tan bien como las no autistas dentro de su grupo; en los grupos mixtos se compartió menos y el entendimiento fue menor. Límites: fue una tarea concreta en un entorno de investigación y no demuestra qué ocurrirá con cada persona o situación.
sheet.en: If important information needs to pass between people, consider letting autistic people share it with each other, and remember that communication between autistic and non-autistic people may need more mutual support and more checking that things were understood. Evidence: a study with autistic people in nine groups of eight (autistic, non-autistic and mixed) passing a story from one person to the next. Autistic people shared details as well as non-autistic people did within their own groups; in mixed groups less was shared and rapport was lower. Limits: it was one specific task in a research setting, and it cannot tell you what will happen for any one person or situation.
sheet.sv: Om viktig information ska föras vidare kan du låta autistiska personer dela den med varandra, och komma ihåg att kommunikation mellan autistiska och icke-autistiska personer kan behöva mer ömsesidigt stöd och fler kontroller av att allt uppfattats. Evidens: en studie med autistiska personer i nio grupper om åtta (autistiska, icke-autistiska och blandade) som förde en berättelse vidare från person till person. Autistiska personer delade detaljer lika bra som icke-autistiska inom sina grupper; i blandade grupper delades mindre och samförståndet var lägre. Begränsningar: det var en särskild uppgift i en forskningsmiljö och säger inte vad som gäller för en enskild person eller situation.

claim.es: Entre personas autistas la información fluye tan bien como entre no autistas; se pierde en los grupos mixtos.
claim.en: Information flows between autistic people as well as between non-autistic people; it breaks down in mixed groups.
claim.sv: Information flödar lika bra mellan autistiska personer som mellan icke-autistiska; den bryts i blandade grupper.

supports.es: Valorar a iguales autistas y autodefensores como un recurso.
supports.en: Valuing autistic peers and self-advocates as a resource.
supports.sv: Att värdera autistiska jämlikar och självförespråkare som en resurs.

doesNotSupport.es: Que las personas autistas carezcan de capacidad social.
doesNotSupport.en: That autistic people lack social ability.
doesNotSupport.sv: Att autistiska personer saknar social förmåga.

title: The Gut Microbiota and Oxidative Stress in Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASD).
authors: Hu T, Dong Y, He C, Zhao M, He Q
abstract: Autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) are a kind of neurodevelopmental disorder with rapidly increasing morbidity. In recent years, many studies have proposed a possible link between ASD and multiple environmental as well as genetic risk factors; nevertheless, recent studies have still failed to identify the specific pathogenesis. An analysis of the literature showed that oxidative stress and redox imbalance caused by high levels of reactive oxygen species (ROS) are thought to be integral parts of ASD pathophysiology. On the one hand, this review aims to elucidate the communications between oxidative stress, as a risk factor, and ASD. As such, there is also evidence to suggest that early assessment and treatment of antioxidant status are likely to result in improved long-term prognosis by disturbing oxidative stress in the brain to avoid additional irreversible brain damage. Accordingly, we will also discuss the possibility of novel therapies regarding oxidative stress as a target according to recent literature. On the other hand, this review suggests a definite relationship between ASD and an unbalanced gastrointestinal tract (GIT) microbiota (i.e., GIT dysbiosis). A variety of studies have concluded that the intestinal microbiota influences many aspects of human health, including metabolism, the immune and nervous systems, and the mucosal barrier. Additionally, the oxidative stress and GIT dysfunction in autistic children have both been reported to be related to mitochondrial dysfunction. What is the connection between them? Moreover, specific changes in the GIT microbiota are clearly observed in most autistic children, and the related mechanisms and the connection among ASD, the GIT microbiota, and oxidative stress are also discussed, providing a theory and molecular strategies for clinical practice as well as further studies.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista tiene molestias digestivas, vale la pena anotarlas y comentarlas con su profesional de salud, sin cambiar dieta ni tratamientos por cuenta propia. Esta es una revisión de la literatura científica, no un estudio con participantes propios; analiza posibles vínculos entre el estrés oxidativo, la microbiota intestinal y el autismo en niños autistas. Sus límites: los autores indican que aún no se ha identificado la causa concreta, hablan de teorías y mecanismos, y no prueban qué ayuda a cada persona. No sirve como regla general. Cualquier decisión médica corresponde a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If an autistic person has digestive discomfort, it is worth noting it down and raising it with their health professional, rather than changing diet or treatments alone. This is a review of the existing literature, not a study with its own participants; it explores possible links between oxidative stress, gut microbiota and autism in autistic children. Its limits: the authors say the specific cause has still not been identified, and they discuss theories and mechanisms rather than proving what helps any one person. It is not a rule for everyone. Medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person har magbesvär är det värt att anteckna dem och ta upp dem med vårdpersonal, i stället för att ändra kost eller behandling på egen hand. Det här är en översikt av befintlig litteratur, inte en studie med egna deltagare; den utforskar möjliga samband mellan oxidativ stress, tarmflora och autism hos autistiska barn. Begränsningar: författarna uppger att den specifika orsaken fortfarande inte är identifierad, och de diskuterar teorier och mekanismer snarare än att visa vad som hjälper en enskild person. Det är ingen regel för alla. Medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker.

title: Bilingualism in autism: Language learning profiles and social experiences.
authors: Digard BG, Sorace A, Stanfield A, Fletcher-Watson S
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Bilingualism changes the way people relate to others. This is particularly interesting in the case of autism, where social interaction presents many challenges. A better understanding of the overlap between the social variations of bilingualism and autism could unveil new ways to support the social experiences of autistic people. This research aims to understand the language learning and social experiences of autistic people who speak one, two or more languages. A total of 297 autistic adults (aged between 16 and 80 years) completed an online questionnaire that included general demographic questions, social life quality self-rating questions, language history questions, and open questions about the respondents' bilingualism experience. Respondents had a wide range of language experiences: there were 89 monolingual English speakers, 98 bilinguals, 110 respondents knew three languages or more, all with a wide range of abilities in their languages. In the full group, younger respondents were more satisfied with their social life, and respondents with many languages were more satisfied with their social life than respondents with few languages. In the multilingual group, younger respondents were more satisfied with their social life, and the more skilled in their third language the more satisfied with their social life. This is the first study describing the language history and social experiences of a large group of bilingual and multilingual autistic adults. It highlights how autistic people can encounter a new language, learn it and use it in their daily life, and how their bilingualism experiences shape their social life.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista tiene interés en aprender otro idioma o ya habla varios, puede apoyarla: no hay motivo para frenarlo por ser autista. Es un estudio con cuestionario en línea en el que participaron 297 personas autistas adultas (de 16 a 80 años), con una gran variedad de experiencias con los idiomas. Quienes hablaban más idiomas se declararon más satisfechas con su vida social. Sin embargo, solo muestra una relación, no que los idiomas causen esa satisfacción, y las respuestas fueron autoinformadas. No sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person is curious about learning another language, or already speaks several, you can support it; being autistic is no reason to hold them back. This was an online questionnaire study with 297 autistic adults (aged 16 to 80), who had a wide range of language experiences. Those who knew more languages rated their social life as more satisfying. However, this shows only a link, not that languages cause the satisfaction, and answers were self-reported. It is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person är nyfiken på att lära sig ett annat språk, eller redan talar flera, kan du stödja det. Att vara autistisk är ingen anledning att avstyra det. Detta var en enkätstudie på nätet med 297 autistiska vuxna (16 till 80 år) med mycket varierande språkerfarenheter. De som kunde fler språk skattade sitt sociala liv som mer tillfredsställande. Studien visar dock bara ett samband, inte att språken orsakar nöjdheten, och svaren var självrapporterade. Det är ingen regel för alla.

title: Development and evaluation of a novel caregiver-report tool to assess barriers to physical healthcare for people on the autism spectrum.
authors: Walsh C, Lydon S, Hehir A, O'Connor P
abstract: Introduction People on the autism spectrum often experience poorer health than the general population despite higher engagement with the health services. This suggests a disparity in the accessibility of appropriate healthcare for autistic individuals. To improve access, barriers the autism community experience in healthcare first need to be identified. This paper aimed to: 1) develop and evaluate a caregiver-report tool; 2) identify barriers to physical healthcare for autistic individuals; and 3) identify potential contributing factors.
