Methods A previously established taxonomy of barriers to healthcare for autistic individuals informed the development of the tool; this was then distributed to caregivers of autistic adults and children. Exploratory factor analysis (EFA) assessed validity and reliability of the tool. Multiple Regressions were performed to identify predictors of barriers. Results In total, caregivers of 194 autistic children or adults participated in the study. The EFA produced four factors: 1) patient-level barriers; 2) healthcare provider-level (HCP) barriers; 3) healthcare system-level barriers; and 4) barriers related to managing healthcare. The greatest barriers included difficulties with identifying/reporting symptoms (endorsed by 62.4% of participants); difficulties handling the waiting area (60.3% of participants); and a lack of HCP knowledge regarding autism (52.1% of participants). Autism severity, general adjustment problems, anxiety, age and having unmet needs predicted the frequency and/or severity of barriers. Conclusions A tool that allows assessment of patient-, HCP-, and system-level barriers to healthcare was developed and evaluated. Patient-level barriers appear to occur frequently and pose substantial challenges. This tool will help identify areas most in need of intervention and support intervention evaluation.

sheet.es: Antes de una cita médica, piense en qué puede resultar difícil: explicar o notar síntomas, esperar en la sala o que el personal conozca poco el autismo. Avisar al centro con antelación y preparar notas sobre lo que le pasa a la persona puede ayudar. Evidencia: estudio que creó una herramienta de cuestionario y la respondieron cuidadores de 194 niños o adultos autistas. Entre ellos, el 62.4% señaló dificultad para identificar o comunicar síntomas y el 60.3% dificultad con la sala de espera. Límites: son opiniones de cuidadores, no de las propias personas autistas, y no describe a todas las personas ni indica qué solución funciona.
sheet.en: Before a medical appointment, think about what may be hard: noticing or explaining symptoms, waiting in the waiting area, or staff knowing little about autism. Telling the clinic in advance and bringing notes about what the person is experiencing may help. Evidence: a study that built a questionnaire tool, answered by caregivers of 194 autistic children or adults. Of them, 62.4% reported difficulty identifying or reporting symptoms and 60.3% difficulty with the waiting area. Limits: these are caregivers' reports, not the views of autistic people themselves, and the study does not describe everyone or show which solution works.
sheet.sv: Inför ett läkarbesök kan du fundera på vad som kan bli svårt: att upptäcka eller förklara symtom, att vänta i väntrummet eller att personalen kan lite om autism. Det kan hjälpa att meddela mottagningen i förväg och ta med anteckningar om vad personen upplever. Evidens: en studie som tog fram ett frågeformulär, besvarat av vårdnadshavare till 194 autistiska barn eller vuxna. Av dem rapporterade 62.4% svårigheter att identifiera eller rapportera symtom och 60.3% svårigheter med väntrummet. Begränsningar: svaren kommer från vårdnadshavare, inte från autistiska personer själva, och studien beskriver inte alla eller visar vilken lösning som fungerar.

title: Development of a Web-Based Resource for Parents of Young Children Newly Diagnosed With Autism: Participatory Research Design.
authors: Rabba AS, Dissanayake C, Barbaro J
abstract: Background The internet provides an ideal avenue to share information, advice, and support regarding autism. However, many websites lack quality control and rarely provide a one-stop resource for families to access necessary, evidence-based information. Objective This study aims to use participatory action research (PAR) with end users (ie, parents) and clinicians to develop a web-based resource (Pathways Beyond Diagnosis) to improve timely access to quality, evidence-based information, and support for families after their child is diagnosed with autism. Methods The PAR approach involves 4 phases: (1) cooperative researcher-stakeholder planning, (2) cooperative researcher-stakeholder-based action, (3) stakeholder observation, and (4) cooperative researcher-stakeholder reflection. A total of 15 participants (parents, n=3; clinicians, n=9; and researchers, n=3) attended individual or group participatory design workshops. This was followed by the translation of knowledge and ideas generated during the workshops to produce mockups of webpages and content, rapid prototyping, and one-on-one consultations with end users to assess the usability of the website developed. Results A total of 3 participatory design workshops were held with the participants, each followed by a knowledge translation session. At the end of the PAR cycle, an alpha prototype of the website was built and a series of one-on-one end user consultation sessions were conducted. The PAR cycle revealed the importance of 6 key topic areas (understanding autism, accessing services, support, gaining funding, putting it all together, and looking into the future) associated with the time of diagnosis, which were incorporated into the beta version of the website. Conclusions The development of the Pathways Beyond Diagnosis website using PAR ensures that families have ready access to practical and evidence-based information following a young child's diagnosis. The website guides families to access relevant, reputable, and evidence-based information in addition to summarizing key challenges encountered after diagnosis (ie, grief, sharing the diagnosis) and the importance of self-care.

sheet.es: Tras el diagnóstico de un niño pequeño, puede ayudar buscar un único recurso web fiable que reúna información basada en evidencia, en lugar de navegar por muchas páginas sin control de calidad. Piense en temas como entender el autismo, acceder a servicios, apoyo, financiación y el futuro, y reserve tiempo para cuidarse. La evidencia es un estudio de investigación participativa: 15 personas (3 madres o padres, 9 profesionales clínicos y 3 investigadores) diseñaron el sitio web Pathways Beyond Diagnosis en talleres. Sus límites: participaron pocas familias, no hubo personas autistas entre quienes se describen, y el estudio describe el desarrollo del sitio, no demuestra que ayude. Cada familia tiene necesidades distintas.
sheet.en: After a young child's diagnosis, it can help to look for one reliable website that gathers evidence-based information, rather than searching many pages with no quality control. Useful topics include understanding autism, accessing services, support, funding and the future, plus time for your own self-care. The evidence is a participatory research study: 15 people (3 parents, 9 clinicians and 3 researchers) designed the Pathways Beyond Diagnosis website in workshops. Its limits: few parents took part, no autistic participants are described, and the study describes how the site was built, not whether it helps. Every family's needs differ.
sheet.sv: Efter att ett litet barn fått sin diagnos kan det hjälpa att leta efter en enda pålitlig webbplats med evidensbaserad information, i stället för att söka bland många sidor utan kvalitetskontroll. Användbara teman är att förstå autism, få tillgång till stöd och tjänster, finansiering och framtiden, samt tid för egen återhämtning. Underlaget är en deltagande forskningsstudie: 15 personer (3 föräldrar, 9 kliniker och 3 forskare) utformade webbplatsen Pathways Beyond Diagnosis i workshoppar. Begränsningar: få föräldrar deltog, inga autistiska deltagare beskrivs, och studien visar hur webbplatsen togs fram, inte om den hjälper. Varje familjs behov är olika.

title: The Prevalence of Self-injurious Behaviour in Autism: A Meta-analytic Study.
authors: Steenfeldt-Kristensen C, Jones CA, Richards C
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Self-injurious behaviour is purportedly common in autism, but prevalence rates have not yet been synthesised meta-analytically. In the present study, data from 14,379 participants in thirty-seven papers were analysed to generate a pooled prevalence estimate of self-injury in autism of 42% (confidence intervals 0.38-0.47). Hand-hitting topography was the most common form of self-injury (23%), self-cutting topography the least common (3%). Sub-group analyses revealed no association between study quality, participant intellectual disability or age and overall prevalence rate of self-injury. However, females obtained higher prevalence rates than males (p = .013) and hair pulling and self-scratching were associated with intellectual disability (p = .008 and p = .002, respectively). The results confirm very high rates of self-injury in autism and highlight within group risk-markers.

sheet.es: Si cuida de una persona autista, conviene tener presente que la autolesión es frecuente y que merece atención y apoyo, no reproche. Observe cuándo ocurre y qué la rodea (dolor, ruido, cansancio, frustración) y compártalo con su equipo sanitario. Evidencia: metaanálisis de 37 artículos con 14.379 participantes, que estimó una prevalencia conjunta del 42% (intervalos de confianza 0.38-0.47). Los golpes con la mano fueron la forma más común (23%) y los cortes la menos común (3%). Límites: son promedios de grupo y no predicen a una persona concreta. Si le preocupa una persona, busque ayuda profesional: un clínico, un servicio de salud o un servicio de crisis. Ante un peligro inmediato, llame al número de emergencias de su país.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person, it helps to know that self-injury is common and calls for understanding and support, not blame. Notice when it happens and what surrounds it (pain, noise, tiredness, frustration), and share this with their health team. Evidence: a meta-analysis of 37 papers with 14,379 participants, which estimated a pooled prevalence of 42% (confidence intervals 0.38-0.47). Hand-hitting was the most common form (23%) and self-cutting the least common (3%). Limits: these are group averages and cannot predict any one person. If you are worried about someone, seek professional help from a clinician, a health service or a crisis service. In immediate danger, call your country's emergency number.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person är det bra att veta att självskada är vanligt och kräver förståelse och stöd, inte skuldbeläggning. Lägg märke till när det sker och vad som finns runt omkring (smärta, ljud, trötthet, frustration) och dela det med personens vårdteam. Evidens: en metaanalys av 37 artiklar med 14 379 deltagare uppskattade en sammanslagen prevalens på 42% (konfidensintervall 0.38-0.47). Slag med handen var vanligast (23%) och skärande minst vanligt (3%). Begränsningar: det är gruppmedelvärden som inte förutsäger en enskild person. Om du är orolig för någon, sök professionell hjälp hos en kliniker, en vårdinstans eller en krisjour. Vid akut fara, ring ditt lands nödnummer.

title: Attunement in Music Therapy for Young Children with Autism: Revisiting Qualities of Relationship as Mechanisms of Change.
authors: Mössler K, Schmid W, Aßmus J, Fusar-Poli L, Gold C
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: This study examined whether musical and emotional attunement predicts changes in improvisational music therapy with children with autism (4-7 years, N = 101, majority: no/limited speech, low IQ), assessed over 12 months. Attunement, as observed from session videos, and changes in generalized social skills, judged by blinded assessors and parents, were evaluated using standardized tools (Assessment of the Quality of Relationship, Improvisational Music Therapy Principles, ADOS, SRS). In contrast to the smaller pilot, we did not find significant effects between attunement and changes in outcomes, only tendencies in the same direction are observed. Findings suggest that symptom severity is associated with the therapist's ability to attune to the child. They further raise questions concerning outcome selection and user involvement.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija participa en musicoterapia, puede fijarse en si la persona terapeuta sigue su ritmo, sus sonidos y sus emociones, y comentarlo con ella. Es una pregunta útil, no una garantía. Evidencia: ensayo con 101 niños autistas de 4 a 7 años, seguidos durante 12 meses. No se hallaron efectos significativos entre la sintonía y los cambios en habilidades sociales; solo tendencias en esa dirección. Límites: los resultados no confirmaron un estudio piloto anterior más pequeño, y los autores cuestionan qué resultados se miden. No sirve como regla para cada niño.
sheet.en: If your child takes part in music therapy, you can notice whether the therapist follows their rhythm, sounds and emotions, and talk about it with them. It is a useful question, not a guarantee. Evidence: a trial with 101 autistic children aged 4-7, followed for 12 months. No significant effects were found between attunement and changes in social skills, only tendencies in that direction. Limits: results did not confirm an earlier, smaller pilot study, and the authors question which outcomes are measured. It is not a rule for every child.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn går i musikterapi kan du lägga märke till om terapeuten följer barnets rytm, ljud och känslor, och prata om det med terapeuten. Det är en användbar fråga, ingen garanti. Evidens: en studie med 101 autistiska barn i åldern 4–7 år, följda i 12 månader. Inga signifikanta samband hittades mellan samstämdhet och förändringar i sociala färdigheter, bara tendenser åt det hållet. Begränsningar: resultaten bekräftade inte en tidigare, mindre pilotstudie, och forskarna ifrågasätter vilka utfall som mäts. Det är ingen regel för varje barn.

title: Tele-Assisted Behavioral Intervention for Families with Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders: A Randomized Control Trial.
authors: Marino F, Chilà P, Failla C, Crimi I, Minutoli R, Puglisi A, Arnao AA, Tartarisco G, Ruta L, Vagni D, Pioggia G
abstract: Background Telehealth is useful for both autism spectrum disorder (ASD) diagnosis and treatment, but studies with a direct comparison between teletherapy and traditional in-person therapy are limited. Methods This randomized control trial-ISRCTN (International Standard Randomised Controlled Trial Number) primary clinical trial registry ID ISRCTN15312724-was aimed at comparing the effect of a tele-assisted and in-person intervention based on a behavioral intervention protocol for families with children affected by ASDs. Forty-two parents with children with autism (30 months to 10 years old) were randomly assigned to 12 sessions of an applied behavioral analysis (ABA) intervention implemented in an individual and group setting, either with or without the inclusion of tele-assistance. Pre- and postintervention assessments were conducted using the Home Situation Questionnaire (HSQ-ASD) and the Parental Stress Index (PSI/SF). Results Substantial improvements in the perception and management of children's behavior by parents, as well as in the influence of a reduction in parent stress levels on said children's behavior through the use of a tele-assisted intervention, were obtained. Conclusions This randomized controlled trial demonstrates the evidence-based potential for telehealth to improve treatment of ASDs.

sheet.es: Si el acceso a sesiones presenciales es difícil, una intervención conductual para familias ofrecida con apoyo por telesalud puede ser una opción que merezca consulta con el equipo profesional. Fue un ensayo aleatorizado con 42 madres y padres de niñas y niños autistas de 30 months a 10 años, que hicieron 12 sesiones de ABA, con o sin teleasistencia. Las familias con teleasistencia informaron mejoras en cómo percibían y manejaban la conducta de sus hijos, y menos estrés parental. Es un grupo pequeño, midió la experiencia de los progenitores y no la de las personas autistas, y no garantiza el mismo resultado en cada familia.
sheet.en: If getting to in-person sessions is hard, a behavioral programme for families delivered with telehealth support may be worth discussing with your professional team. This was a randomized trial with 42 parents of autistic children aged 30 months to 10 years, who took 12 sessions of ABA, with or without tele-assistance. Families using tele-assistance reported improvements in how they perceived and managed their child's behavior, and lower parent stress. The group was small, the study measured parents' experience rather than autistic people's own views, and results may differ for each family.
sheet.sv: Om det är svårt att ta sig till fysiska träffar kan ett beteendeinriktat program för familjer med stöd via telehälsa vara värt att diskutera med ert professionella team. Det var en randomiserad studie med 42 föräldrar till autistiska barn i åldern 30 months till 10 år, som fick 12 sessioner ABA, med eller utan teleassistans. Familjer med teleassistans rapporterade förbättringar i hur de uppfattade och hanterade barnets beteende, och mindre föräldrastress. Gruppen var liten, studien mätte föräldrarnas upplevelse och inte autistiska personers egna perspektiv, och resultaten kan skilja sig mellan familjer.

title: A developmental and sequenced one-to-one educational intervention (DS1-EI) for autism spectrum disorder and intellectual disability: A three-year randomized, single-blind controlled trial.
authors: Saint-Georges C, Pagnier M, Ghattassi Z, Hubert-Barthelemy A, Tanet A, Clément MN, Soumille F, Crespin GC, Pellerin H, Cohen D, GPIS study group
abstract: Background Children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and intellectual disability (ID) are an understudied population whose school inclusion is challenging. Methods We assessed the effects of "Developmental and Sequenced one-to-one Educational Intervention" (DS1-EI), a ten-hour-per-week adapted instruction programme for five- to nine-year-old children with ASD and ID treated in outpatient health care institutions. A single-blind multisite randomized controlled trial was conducted to compare DS1-EI given for three years with treatment as usual (TAU)(trial registration numbers: ANSM130282B-31 (April 16, 2013) and ACTRN12616000592448). The primary outcome was the change in the psycho-educational profile (PEP). Secondary variables included the Childhood Autism Rating Scale (CARS), Autism Diagnostic Interview-Revised (ADI-R), Vineland Adaptive Behaviour Scale-II (VABS-II), Children's Global Assessment Scale (CGAS) and annual assessment of educational achievement. Statistical analyses used linear mixed models. Findings Seventy-two participants with severe ASD and ID were recruited. Intention-to-treat and per-protocol analyses showed no significant group*time interaction for the PEP, CARS, ADI-R, VABS-II and CGAS but a significant effect for educational achievement with a better improvement in the DS1-EI group. At the 36-month time point, more DS1-EI children were included in mainstream classrooms. Additional analyses using multivariate models taking into account moderating variables at the baseline (e.g., Developmental Quotient) confirmed that DS1-EI had a significant effect on educational outcomes. Interpretation DS1-EI did not improve communication or social skills in children with ASD and ID compared with TAU. However, DS1-EI enhanced school skills in four domains (language, mathematics, inter modality, and school autonomy) favouring inclusion in mainstream classrooms more than TAU. Providing such adapted instruction is feasible and should be encouraged. Funding CNSA; Fondation Bettencourt-Schueller; Fondation EDF.

sheet.es: Si su hijo tiene autismo y discapacidad intelectual, un programa de enseñanza individual, adaptado y secuenciado puede ayudar con las habilidades escolares, como lenguaje, matemáticas y autonomía en el aula. Conviene hablar con el equipo educativo sobre esta opción. La evidencia es un ensayo aleatorizado de tres años con 72 participantes de cinco a nueve años. Comparado con la atención habitual, no mejoró la comunicación ni las habilidades sociales, pero más niños pasaron a aulas ordinarias. Sus límites: la muestra es pequeña, incluye solo niños con autismo severo y discapacidad intelectual, y no garantiza el mismo resultado para cada persona.
sheet.en: If your child is autistic and has an intellectual disability, adapted, step-by-step one-to-one teaching may help with school skills such as language, mathematics and autonomy in class. It is worth discussing this option with the education team. The evidence is a three-year randomized trial with 72 participants aged five to nine. Compared with usual care, it did not improve communication or social skills, but more children joined mainstream classrooms. Its limits: the sample is small, includes only children with severe autism and intellectual disability, and cannot promise the same result for every person.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn är autistiskt och har intellektuell funktionsnedsättning kan anpassad, stegvis enskild undervisning stödja skolfärdigheter som språk, matematik och självständighet i klassrummet. Det är värt att ta upp alternativet med skolans team. Underlaget är en treårig randomiserad studie med 72 deltagare i åldrarna fem till nio. Jämfört med vanlig vård förbättrades inte kommunikation eller sociala färdigheter, men fler barn placerades i ordinarie klasser. Begränsningar: urvalet är litet, omfattar bara barn med svår autism och intellektuell funktionsnedsättning, och kan inte lova samma resultat för varje person.

title: Interests and Strengths in Autism, Useful but Misunderstood: A Pragmatic Case-Study.
authors: Courchesne V, Langlois V, Gregoire P, St-Denis A, Bouvet L, Ostrolenk A, Mottron L
abstract: Background Studies on autistic strengths are often focused on what they reveal about autistic intelligence and, in some cases, exceptional and atypical reasoning abilities. An emerging research trend has demonstrated how interests and strengths often evident in autism can be harnessed in interventions to promote the well-being, adaptive, academic and professional success of autistic people. However, abilities in certain domains may be accompanied by major limitations in others, as well as psychiatric and behavioral issues, which may challenge their inclusion in support programs. Objectives To provide an in-depth, pragmatic, real-life example of the psychological and psychiatric management of interests and strengths in an autistic adolescent. Method An autistic teenager, C.A., with above-average calendar calculation and musical abilities, received psychiatric, neuropsychological, and language standardized and clinical assessments, combined with a measurement of his musical and calendar calculation abilities. C.A. and his parents then received psychiatric and psychological support over a 14-month period, targeting their perceptions of C.A.'s interests, strengths, and co-occurring difficulties. Results C.A. had a verbal IQ within the intellectual disability range and a non-verbal IQ in the low mean range. Modest calendar calculation, absolute pitch, and matrix abilities coexisted with severe receptive and expressive language disorder. The discrepancy between his abilities in areas of strengths and his limitations in other domains led to anxiety, frustration, and sometimes behavioral issues. Displacing the focus from academic performance to interests, as well as promoting the use of his strengths to develop new skills independently of their short-term adaptive benefits yielded positive effects on C.A.'s self-assessment, quality of life, and behavior at follow up. Discussion The appealing idea that abilities mostly found in autistic people, such as calendar calculation, can be directly harnessed into academic achievement and lead to paid employment may have detrimental effects, especially when such abilities are modest and associated with other limitations. These abilities should be primarily used to maximize well-being and quality of life, independently of their short-term adaptive function, which may or may not be positive.

sheet.es: Tomorrow, prueba a valorar los intereses y puntos fuertes de tu hijo o hija por sí mismos, para su bienestar y disfrute, sin exigir que den un resultado académico o laboral. Este estudio de caso describe a un adolescente autista con habilidades de cálculo de calendario y música, y a sus padres, que recibieron apoyo psicológico y psiquiátrico durante 14 meses. Al pasar el foco del rendimiento académico a sus intereses, mejoraron su autovaloración, su calidad de vida y su conducta. Límites: es un solo caso, así que no vale como regla para otras personas.
sheet.en: Tomorrow, try valuing your child's interests and strengths for their own sake, for wellbeing and enjoyment, rather than expecting them to lead to school or work results. This case study followed one autistic teenager with calendar calculation and musical abilities, and his parents, who received psychological and psychiatric support over 14 months. Shifting the focus from academic performance to his interests was linked to better self-assessment, quality of life and behaviour. Limits: it is a single case, so it cannot be treated as a rule for other people.
sheet.sv: Imorgon kan du prova att värdera ditt barns intressen och styrkor för deras egen skull, för välmående och glädje, i stället för att förvänta dig skol- eller jobbresultat. Denna fallstudie följde en autistisk tonåring med kalenderberäkning och musikalisk förmåga, samt hans föräldrar, som fick psykologiskt och psykiatriskt stöd under 14 månader. När fokus flyttades från skolprestation till hans intressen förbättrades hans självbedömning, livskvalitet och beteende. Begränsning: det är bara ett enda fall och kan därför inte ses som en regel för andra.

title: Dropping out and moving on: A qualitative study of autistic people's experiences of university.
authors: Cage E, Howes J
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Many autistic people now go to university, but many of them also drop out of their studies. In fact, it is believed that autistic people are at higher risk of dropping out, but little research has been done to understand why this is happening. This research used interviews to take an in-depth look at 14 autistic people's experiences of dropping out of university. All the things the participants talked about were examined closely by the researchers who identified common themes in what the participants discussed. The first set of themes captured some overarching issues faced by autistic people, such as difficulties with getting diagnosed, a lack of autism understanding, mental health challenges and feeling like an outsider. The next themes were organised within challenges faced at university, including a feeling of culture shock, becoming disengaged from one's studies, a lack of proactive support from their university and a feeling that dropping out became inevitable. Finally, there were themes about life after dropping out, which involved a sense that the experience at university had been traumatic and shameful, but they believed people had to do what is right for them. All of these themes suggest that universities need to be better at supporting autistic people when they first come to university, and that they should actively offer clear support throughout and try and make the university environment more accessible for everyone, to ensure more autistic people have a positive university experience.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista en la universidad, ofrece apoyo claro desde el principio y no esperes a que lo pida: pregunta qué necesita y ayúdala a contactar con la universidad. Es un estudio cualitativo con entrevistas a 14 personas autistas que dejaron la universidad. Contaron falta de comprensión, choque cultural, desconexión con los estudios y poco apoyo proactivo. Hablaron de la experiencia como traumática y vergonzosa, pero creían que cada persona debe hacer lo que es mejor para sí. Es un grupo pequeño y no representa a todas las personas autistas ni a todas las universidades.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person at university, offer clear support from the start rather than waiting for them to ask: check what they need and help them contact the university. This was a qualitative study, with interviews of 14 autistic people who had dropped out of university. They described a lack of understanding, culture shock, becoming disengaged from their studies and little proactive support. They called the experience traumatic and shameful, but believed people must do what is right for them. It was a small group and cannot speak for all autistic people or all universities.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person på universitetet: erbjud tydligt stöd från start i stället för att vänta på att hen ber om det. Fråga vad som behövs och hjälp till med kontakten med universitetet. Detta var en kvalitativ studie med intervjuer av 14 autistiska personer som hade hoppat av universitetet. De beskrev bristande förståelse, kulturchock, att tappa kontakten med studierna och lite proaktivt stöd. De beskrev upplevelsen som traumatisk och skamfylld, men menade att man måste göra det som är rätt för en själv. Gruppen var liten och kan inte tala för alla autistiska personer eller alla universitet.

title: Face individual identity recognition: a potential endophenotype in autism.
authors: Minio-Paluello I, Porciello G, Pascual-Leone A, Baron-Cohen S
abstract: Background Face individual identity recognition skill is heritable and independent of intellectual ability. Difficulties in face individual identity recognition are present in autistic individuals and their family members and are possibly linked to oxytocin polymorphisms in families with an autistic child. While it is reported that developmental prosopagnosia (i.e., impaired face identity recognition) occurs in 2-3% of the general population, no prosopagnosia prevalence estimate is available for autism. Furthermore, an autism within-group approach has not been reported towards characterizing impaired face memory and to investigate its possible links to social and communication difficulties. Methods The present study estimated the prevalence of prosopagnosia in 80 autistic adults with no intellectual disability, investigated its cognitive characteristics and links to autism symptoms' severity, personality traits, and mental state understanding from the eye region by using standardized tests and questionnaires. Results More than one third of autistic participants showed prosopagnosia. Their face memory skill was not associated with their symptom's severity, empathy, alexithymia, or general intelligence. Face identity recognition was instead linked to mental state recognition from the eye region only in autistic individuals who had prosopagnosia, and this relationship did not depend on participants' basic face perception skills. Importantly, we found that autistic participants were not aware of their face memory skills. Limitations We did not test an epidemiological sample, and additional work is necessary to establish whether these results generalize to the entire autism spectrum. Conclusions Impaired face individual identity recognition meets the criteria to be a potential endophenotype in autism. In the future, testing for face memory could be used to stratify autistic individuals into genetically meaningful subgroups and be translatable to autism animal models.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista a menudo no reconoce caras conocidas, conviene tomarlo como una diferencia real y no como falta de interés. Ayuda facilitar pistas como el nombre, la voz, la ropa o el peinado. El estudio incluyó a 80 adultos autistas sin discapacidad intelectual y usó pruebas y cuestionarios estandarizados. Más de un tercio mostró prosopagnosia, y las propias personas no eran conscientes de su memoria facial. Como no se evaluó una muestra epidemiológica, los resultados quizá no valgan para todo el espectro ni para cada persona.
sheet.en: If an autistic person often doesn't recognise familiar faces, it can be treated as a real difference, not a lack of interest. It helps to offer other cues such as a name, a voice, clothing or a hairstyle. The study included 80 autistic adults with no intellectual disability and used standardized tests and questionnaires. More than one third showed prosopagnosia, and participants were not aware of their own face memory skills. It did not test an epidemiological sample, so results may not apply to the whole spectrum or to every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person ofta inte känner igen bekanta ansikten kan det ses som en verklig skillnad, inte som brist på intresse. Det hjälper att erbjuda andra ledtrådar, som namn, röst, kläder eller frisyr. Studien omfattade 80 autistiska vuxna utan intellektuell funktionsnedsättning och använde standardiserade test och frågeformulär. Mer än en tredjedel visade prosopagnosi, och deltagarna var inte medvetna om sin egen ansiktsminnesförmåga. Ingen epidemiologisk grupp testades, så resultaten gäller kanske inte hela spektrumet eller varje person.

title: Autism Spectrum Disorder Associated With Gut Microbiota at Immune, Metabolomic, and Neuroactive Level.
authors: Garcia-Gutierrez E, Narbad A, Rodríguez JM
abstract: There is increasing evidence suggesting a link between the autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and the gastrointestinal (GI) microbiome. Experimental and clinical studies have shown that patients diagnosed with ASD display alterations of the gut microbiota. These alterations do not only extend to the gut microbiota composition but also to the metabolites they produce, as a result of its connections with diet and the bidirectional interaction with the host. Thus, production of metabolites and neurotransmitters stimulate the immune system and influence the central nervous system (CNS) by stimulation of the vagal nerve, as an example of the gut-brain axis pathway. In this review we compose an overview of the interconnectivity of the different GI-related elements that have been associated with the development and severity of the ASD in patients and animal models. We review potential biomarkers to be used in future studies to unlock further connections and interventions in the treatment of ASD.

sheet.es: Si la persona autista tiene molestias de ttripa, estreñimiento o una alimentación muy limitada, vale la pena anotarlo y comentarlo con su profesional de salud; no hay ningún cambio que esta revisión indique hacer mañana. Es una revisión que reúne estudios clínicos y experimentales, incluidos modelos animales, sobre la microbiota intestinal y su relación con el sistema inmunitario y el cerebro. Sus límites: muestra asociaciones, no demuestra causas, y no sirve como regla para todas las personas. Los biomarcadores que menciona son posibilidades para estudios futuros, no pruebas disponibles hoy.
sheet.en: If an autistic person has tummy discomfort, constipation or a very limited diet, it is worth noting it down and raising it with their health professional; this review does not point to any change to make tomorrow. It is a review gathering clinical and experimental studies, including animal models, on the gut microbiota and its links with the immune system and the brain. Its limits: it shows associations, not causes, and it is not a rule for every person. The biomarkers it mentions are possibilities for future studies, not tests available today.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person har magont, förstoppning eller en mycket begränsad kost är det värt att anteckna det och ta upp det med vårdpersonal; översikten pekar inte på någon förändring att göra i morgon. Det är en översikt som samlar kliniska och experimentella studier, även djurmodeller, om tarmfloran och dess samband med immunsystemet och hjärnan. Begränsningar: den visar samband, inte orsaker, och är ingen regel för alla personer. De biomarkörer som nämns är möjligheter för framtida studier, inte tester som finns idag.

title: Physical health of autistic girls and women: a scoping review.
authors: Kassee C, Babinski S, Tint A, Lunsky Y, Brown HK, Ameis SH, Szatmari P, Lai MC, Einstein G
abstract: Background There is a growing recognition of sex and gender influences in autism. Increasingly, studies include comparisons between sexes or genders, but few have focused on clarifying the characteristics of autistic girls'/women's physical health. Methods A scoping review was conducted to determine what is currently known about the physical health of autistic girls/women. We screened 1112 unique articles, with 40 studies meeting the inclusion criteria. We used a convergent iterative process to synthesize this content into broad thematic areas. Results Autistic girls/women experience more overall physical health challenges compared to non-autistic girls/women and to autistic boys/men. Emerging evidence suggests increased prevalence of epilepsy in autistic girls/women compared to non-autistic girls/women and to autistic boys/men. The literature also suggests increased endocrine and reproductive health conditions in autistic girls/women compared to non-autistic girls/women. Findings regarding gastrointestinal, metabolic, nutritional, and immune-related conditions are preliminary and inconsistent. Limitations The literature has substantial heterogeneity in how physical health conditions were assessed and reported. Further, our explicit focus on physical health may have constrained the ability to examine interactions between mental and physical health. The widely differing research aims and methodologies make it difficult to reach definitive conclusions. Nevertheless, in keeping with the goals of a scoping review, we were able to identify key themes to guide future research. Conclusions The emerging literature suggests that autistic girls/women have heightened rates of physical health challenges compared to non-autistic girls/women and to autistic boys/men. Clinicians should seek to provide holistic care that includes a focus on physical health and develop a women's health lens when providing clinical care to autistic girls/women.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una niña o mujer autista, vale la pena prestar atención también a su salud física: pide revisiones regulares y comenta con su médico cualquier señal de epilepsia (ausencias, sacudidas), cambios hormonales, problemas menstruales o de salud reproductiva. Llevar un registro sencillo de síntomas puede ayudar en la consulta. Esta revisión de alcance analizó 40 estudios y encontró que, en conjunto, las niñas y mujeres autistas presentan más problemas de salud física que las no autistas y que los varones autistas. Sus límites: los estudios midieron la salud de formas muy distintas y los datos sobre digestión, metabolismo, nutrición e inmunidad son preliminares; no describe a cada persona.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic girl or woman, it is worth keeping her physical health in view too: ask for regular check-ups and mention to her doctor any possible signs of epilepsy (absences, jerks), hormonal changes, or menstrual and reproductive health concerns. A simple symptom diary can make appointments easier. This scoping review looked at 40 studies and found that, overall, autistic girls and women had more physical health conditions than non-autistic girls and women and than autistic boys and men. Its limits: studies measured health in very different ways, and findings on digestion, metabolism, nutrition and immunity are early and inconsistent; it does not describe every person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk flicka eller kvinna är det värt att också hålla ögonen på hennes fysiska hälsa: be om regelbundna kontroller och nämn för läkaren eventuella tecken på epilepsi (frånvaroattacker, ryckningar), hormonella förändringar eller besvär med mens och reproduktiv hälsa. En enkel symtomdagbok kan underlätta besöken. Denna översikt (scoping review) gick igenom 40 studier och fann att autistiska flickor och kvinnor sammantaget hade fler fysiska hälsotillstånd än icke-autistiska flickor och kvinnor och än autistiska pojkar och män. Begränsningar: studierna mätte hälsa på mycket olika sätt, och resultaten om mage, ämnesomsättning, näring och immunförsvar är preliminära och spretiga; de gäller inte alla.

title: Modeling flexible behavior in childhood to adulthood shows age-dependent learning mechanisms and less optimal learning in autism in each age group.
authors: Crawley D, Zhang L, Jones EJH, Ahmad J, Oakley B, San José Cáceres A, Charman T, Buitelaar JK, Murphy DGM, Chatham C, den Ouden H, Loth E, EU-AIMS LEAP group
abstract: Flexible behavior is critical for everyday decision-making and has been implicated in restricted, repetitive behaviors (RRB) in autism spectrum disorder (ASD). However, how flexible behavior changes developmentally in ASD remains largely unknown. Here, we used a developmental approach and examined flexible behavior on a probabilistic reversal learning task in 572 children, adolescents, and adults (ASD N = 321; typical development [TD] N = 251). Using computational modeling, we quantified latent variables that index mechanisms underlying perseveration and feedback sensitivity. We then assessed these variables in relation to diagnosis, developmental stage, core autism symptomatology, and associated psychiatric symptoms. Autistic individuals showed on average more perseveration and less feedback sensitivity than TD individuals, and, across cases and controls, older age groups showed more feedback sensitivity than younger age groups. Computational modeling revealed that dominant learning mechanisms underpinning flexible behavior differed across developmental stages and reduced flexible behavior in ASD was driven by less optimal learning on average within each age group. In autistic children, perseverative errors were positively related to anxiety symptoms, and in autistic adults, perseveration (indexed by both task errors and model parameter estimates) was positively related to RRB. These findings provide novel insights into reduced flexible behavior in relation to clinical symptoms in ASD.

sheet.es: Si a tu hijo o hija autista le cuesta adaptarse cuando las reglas cambian, puede ayudar avisar con antelación, explicar el cambio con claridad y dar tiempo y ejemplos repetidos, sin interpretarlo como terquedad. En niños, esta dificultad se relacionó con ansiedad, así que reducir la incertidumbre puede aliviar. Este estudio con 572 niños, adolescentes y adultos (321 autistas) usó una tarea de aprendizaje con reglas cambiantes y modelos computacionales; las estrategias de aprendizaje variaron con la edad. Límites: es una tarea de laboratorio, muestra promedios de grupo y no describe a cada persona ni prueba qué apoyos funcionan.
sheet.en: If your autistic child finds it hard to adjust when rules change, it may help to give advance notice, explain the change clearly, and allow time and repeated examples, rather than reading it as stubbornness. In children, this difficulty was linked to anxiety, so reducing uncertainty may ease things. This study of 572 children, adolescents and adults (321 autistic) used a learning task with shifting rules and computational modelling; learning strategies differed by age. Limits: it is a lab task, shows group averages, does not describe every individual, and did not test which supports work.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn har svårt att ställa om när regler ändras kan det hjälpa att förvarna, förklara förändringen tydligt och ge tid och upprepade exempel, i stället för att tolka det som envishet. Hos barn hängde svårigheten ihop med oro, så mindre osäkerhet kan underlätta. Studien omfattade 572 barn, ungdomar och vuxna (321 autistiska) som gjorde en inlärningsuppgift med skiftande regler, analyserad med datormodeller; inlärningsstrategierna skilde sig mellan åldrar. Begränsningar: det är en laboratorieuppgift som visar gruppgenomsnitt, beskriver inte varje individ och testade inte vilket stöd som fungerar.

title: Prevalence of and Factors Associated with School Bullying in Students with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Cross-Cultural Meta-Analysis.
authors: Park I, Gong J, Lyons GL, Hirota T, Takahashi M, Kim B, Lee SY, Kim YS, Lee J, Leventhal BL
abstract: Through this meta-analysis, we sought to examine the prevalence of, risks for, and factors associated with bullying involvement (victimization, perpetration, perpetration-victimization) among students with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Additionally, we attempted to examine sources of variance in the prevalence and effect sizes of bullying in students with ASD across studies. Systematic database and literature review identified 34 relevant studies (31 for Western countries, three for Eastern countries). Pooled prevalence estimates for victimization, perpetration, and perpetration-victimization in general were 67%, 29%, and 14%, respectively. The risk of victimization in students with ASD was significantly higher than that in typically developing students and students with other disabilities. Further, deficits in social interaction and communication, externalizing symptoms, internalizing symptoms, and integrated inclusive school settings were related to higher victimization, and externalizing symptoms were related to higher perpetration. Finally, moderation analyses revealed significant variations in the pooled prevalences thereof depending on culture, age, school settings, and methodological quality and in the pooled effect sizes according to publication year and methodological quality. Our results highlight needs for bullying intervention for students with ASD, especially those who are younger, are in an inclusive school setting, and have higher social difficulties and externalizing/internalizing symptoms; for intensive research of bullying experiences among students with ASD in Eastern countries; and for efforts to improve the methodological quality of such research.

sheet.es: Mañana, pregunte con calma a su hijo o hijo autista cómo van los recreos y los trayectos, y avise al centro si detecta señales de acoso. Este metaanálisis reunió 34 estudios sobre estudiantes autistas; estimó una victimización del 67 %, y esta fue mayor que en estudiantes con desarrollo típico y con otras discapacidades. Se asoció con más dificultades sociales, síntomas internalizantes y externalizantes, y aulas inclusivas. Límites: casi todos los estudios eran de países occidentales (31, frente a tres orientales), la calidad variaba y los datos describen grupos, no a cada persona.
sheet.en: Tomorrow, calmly ask your autistic child how break times and the journey to school are going, and tell the school if you notice signs of bullying. This meta-analysis pooled 34 studies of autistic students; it estimated victimization at 67%, and that was higher than in typically developing students and students with other disabilities. It was linked to more social difficulties, internalizing and externalizing symptoms, and inclusive classrooms. Limits: most studies came from Western countries (31, versus three Eastern), quality varied, and the results describe groups, not every individual person.
sheet.sv: I morgon kan du lugnt fråga ditt autistiska barn hur rasterna och vägen till skolan fungerar, och berätta för skolan om du ser tecken på mobbning. Denna metaanalys sammanställde 34 studier om autistiska elever; den uppskattade utsatthet till 67 %, vilket var högre än hos elever med typisk utveckling och elever med andra funktionsnedsättningar. Det hängde ihop med fler sociala svårigheter, internaliserande och externaliserande symtom samt inkluderande klassrum. Begränsningar: de flesta studierna kom från västländer (31, jämfört med tre östliga), kvaliteten varierade och resultaten beskriver grupper, inte varje enskild person.

title: Effects of Non-invasive Neurostimulation on Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review.
authors: Khaleghi A, Zarafshan H, Vand SR, Mohammadi MR
journal: Clinical psychopharmacology and neuroscience : the official scientific journal of the Korean College of Neuropsychopharmacology
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a complex neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by major impairments in social communication, stereotyped and ritualistic behaviors and deficits in sensory reactivity. Recently, noninvasive brain stimulation (NIBS) methods, namely transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) and transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), have been examined as possible new therapeutic options for modifying the pathological neuroplasticity involved in neuropsychiatric disorders including ASD. Therefore, we conducted a systematic review on the therapeutic uses of tDCS and repetitive TMS (rTMS) in ASD patients. A systematic search was performed on Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, Cochrane and Embase. Original articles reporting the use of tDCS or rTMS to treat ASD were screened and studied by two researchers independently based on PRISMA guidelines. We found 32 eligible studies including 8 tDCS reports, 23 rTMS reports and one report with both tDCS and rTMS. These studies comprised 6 case-reports, 9 non-controlled trials and 17 controlled trials which assessed NIBS effects on the three cognitive, behavioral and biological dimensions in ASD. Existing evidence demonstrates that NIBS methods could be helpful for treating some dimensions of ASD such as repetitive behavior, sociability or some aspects of executive and cognitive functions. However, such evidence should be regarded with care because of the quality of original researches and serious publication bias as well as the heterogeneity of data. Further randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trials with appropriate follow-up periods should be designed to assess the efficacy of NIBS methods for ASD treatment.

sheet.es: Por ahora, esta revisión no ofrece nada que cambie la rutina de mañana. Si alguien se plantea la estimulación cerebral no invasiva, conviene hablarlo con un profesional clínico, que es quien debe valorar estas decisiones médicas. La revisión sistemática reunió 32 estudios sobre dos técnicas, tDCS y rTMS, en personas autistas. Algunos resultados apuntan a posibles mejoras en conductas repetitivas, sociabilidad o ciertas funciones ejecutivas y cognitivas. Sus límites son importantes: la calidad de los estudios originales, un sesgo de publicación serio y datos muy heterogéneos. Los propios autores piden ensayos mejores, así que no sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: For now, this review offers nothing that should change tomorrow's routine. If someone is considering non-invasive brain stimulation, talk it through with a clinician, who is the right person for these medical decisions. The systematic review gathered 32 studies of two techniques, tDCS and rTMS, in autistic people. Some results pointed to possible benefits for repetitive behaviour, sociability or certain executive and cognitive functions. The limits matter: the quality of the original studies, serious publication bias and very varied data. The authors themselves call for better trials, so this is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Just nu ger den här översikten inget som bör ändra morgondagens rutiner. Om någon funderar på icke-invasiv hjärnstimulering är det bra att prata med en kliniker, som ska bedöma sådana medicinska beslut. Den systematiska översikten samlade 32 studier om två tekniker, tDCS och rTMS, hos autistiska personer. Vissa resultat tydde på möjliga förbättringar av repetitivt beteende, social förmåga eller vissa exekutiva och kognitiva funktioner. Begränsningarna är viktiga: de ursprungliga studiernas kvalitet, allvarlig publikationsbias och mycket varierande data. Författarna efterlyser själva bättre studier, så detta är ingen regel för alla.

title: Increased prevalence of non-communicable physical health conditions among autistic adults.
authors: Weir E, Allison C, Warrier V, Baron-Cohen S
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Previous research indicates autistic individuals die at a younger age than others and that this is possibly due in part to chronic physical health conditions. The present study used an anonymous, online survey to determine how common certain physical health conditions are among autistic adults, compared with non-autistic adults. We found autistic adults are more likely to develop heart conditions, lung conditions, and diabetes than non-autistic adults. Autistic females may be at higher risk of developing certain conditions (including respiratory conditions, asthma, and prediabetes) than autistic males. Finally, autistic individuals have increased health risks even when considering lifestyle factors (such as smoking, alcohol, and body mass index). This is still a relatively small study, and future research needs to confirm these findings and identify why these risks exist.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista adulta, puede ayudar planificar revisiones médicas periódicas que incluyan corazón, pulmones y azúcar en sangre, y preparar la cita juntos: anotar síntomas, adaptar el entorno sensorial y pedir explicaciones claras. Las mujeres autistas pueden necesitar especial atención a la respiración, el asma y la prediabetes. Esto no significa que vaya a enfermar, sino que vale la pena estar atentos. La evidencia viene de una encuesta anónima en línea que comparó adultos autistas y no autistas; el riesgo seguía siendo mayor aun teniendo en cuenta tabaco, alcohol y peso. Sus límites: es un estudio relativamente pequeño, basado en autoinforme, y aún no explica por qué existen estos riesgos.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult, it may help to plan regular health check-ups that include heart, lungs and blood sugar, and to prepare appointments together: noting symptoms, adapting the sensory environment and asking for clear explanations. Autistic women may benefit from extra attention to breathing, asthma and prediabetes. This does not mean illness is coming, only that staying attentive is worthwhile. The evidence comes from an anonymous online survey comparing autistic and non-autistic adults; risks remained higher even after accounting for smoking, alcohol and body weight. Its limits: it is a relatively small, self-reported study, and it does not yet explain why these risks exist.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen kan det hjälpa att planera regelbundna hälsokontroller som omfattar hjärta, lungor och blodsocker, och att förbereda besöken tillsammans: skriva ner symtom, anpassa den sensoriska miljön och be om tydliga förklaringar. Autistiska kvinnor kan behöva extra uppmärksamhet på andning, astma och prediabetes. Det betyder inte att sjukdom väntar, bara att det är värt att vara uppmärksam. Underlaget kommer från en anonym webbenkät som jämförde autistiska och icke-autistiska vuxna; riskerna var högre även med hänsyn till rökning, alkohol och vikt. Begränsningar: studien är relativt liten, bygger på självrapportering och förklarar ännu inte varför riskerna finns.

title: Ethical dimensions of translational developmental neuroscience research in autism.
authors: Manzini A, Jones EJH, Charman T, Elsabbagh M, Johnson MH, Singh I
journal: Journal of child psychology and psychiatry, and allied disciplines
abstract: Background Since the 1990s, increasing research has been devoted to the identification of biomarkers for autism to help attain more objective diagnosis; enable early prediction of prognosis; and guide individualized intervention options. Early studies focused on the identification of genetic variants associated with autism, but more recently, research has expanded to investigate neurodevelopmental markers. While ethicists have extensively discussed issues around advances in autism genomics, much less ethical scrutiny has focused on research on early neurodevelopment and on the interventions being developed as a result. Objectives We summarize the current state of the science on the identification of early markers for autism and its potential clinical applications, before providing an overview of the ethical issues arising from increasing understanding of children's neurodevelopment in very early life. Results Advances in the understanding of brain and behavioral trajectories preceding later autism diagnosis raise ethical concerns around three themes: (a) New models for understanding autism; (b) Risks and benefits of early identification and intervention; and (c) Communication of early concerns to families. These ethical issues should be further investigated in research conducted in partnership with autistic people and their families. Conclusions This paper highlights the need for ethical scrutiny of early neurodevelopmental research in autism. Scrutiny requires expertise and methods from the basic sciences and bioethics, as well as constructive collaborations among autistic people, their parents, and autism researchers to anticipate early interventions that serve the community's interests and accommodate the varied experiences and preferences of people on the spectrum and their families.

sheet.es: Si le ofrecen participar en investigación sobre señales tempranas del autismo, pregunte qué se busca, qué riesgos y beneficios hay y cómo se comunicarán los resultados. Su familia y la persona autista tienen voz. Esta es una revisión que resume el estado de la ciencia y señala tres temas éticos: nuevos modelos para entender el autismo, riesgos y beneficios de la identificación e intervención tempranas, y cómo se comunican a las familias las primeras inquietudes. Es un texto de análisis, no un estudio con resultados para aplicar a cada niño, y no dice qué hacer en un caso concreto. Pide más investigación junto a personas autistas y sus familias.
sheet.en: If you are invited to join research on early signs of autism, ask what it is looking for, what the risks and benefits are, and how results will be shared. Your family and the autistic person have a voice. This is a review that summarises the state of the science and points to three ethical themes: new models for understanding autism, risks and benefits of early identification and intervention, and how early concerns are communicated to families. It is an analysis, not a study with results to apply to every child, and it does not say what to do in a specific case. It calls for more research done in partnership with autistic people and their families.
sheet.sv: Om ni blir tillfrågade att delta i forskning om tidiga tecken på autism, fråga vad man letar efter, vilka risker och fördelar som finns och hur resultaten delas. Din familj och den autistiska personen har en röst. Detta är en översikt som sammanfattar kunskapsläget och pekar på tre etiska teman: nya modeller för att förstå autism, risker och fördelar med tidig identifiering och tidigt stöd, samt hur tidiga farhågor förmedlas till familjer. Det är en analys, inte en studie med resultat att tillämpa på varje barn, och den säger inte vad som ska göras i ett enskilt fall. Den efterlyser mer forskning i samarbete med autistiska personer och deras familjer.

title: Identifying the most important research, policy and practice questions for substance use, problematic alcohol use and behavioural addictions in autism (SABA-A): A priority setting partnership.
authors: Sinclair JMA, Aslan B, Agabio R, Anilkumar A, Brosnan M, Day E, Dowling NA, Flood C, Grant JE, Halliday R, Hofvander B, Howes L, Moseley R, Myers B, O'Connor V, Shaya G, Thomas S, Robinson J, Chamberl
abstract: Background Autistic people are more likely to report problematic alcohol and other substance use when compared to the general population. Evidence suggests that up to one in three autistic adults may have an alcohol or other substance use disorder (AUD/SUD), although the evidence base for behavioural addictions is less clear. Autistic people may use substances or engage in potentially addictive behaviours as a means of coping with social anxiety, challenging life problems, or camouflaging in social contexts. Despite the prevalence and detrimental effects of AUD, SUD and behavioural addictions in community samples, literature focusing on the intersection between autism and these conditions is scarce, hindering health policy, research, and clinical practice. Methods We aimed to identify the top 10 priorities to build the evidence for research, policy, and clinical practice at this intersection. A priority-setting partnership was used to address this aim, comprising an international steering committee and stakeholders from various backgrounds, including people with declared lived experience of autism and/or addiction. First, an online survey was used to identify what people considered key questions about Substance use, alcohol use, or behavioural addictions in autistic people (SABA-A). These initial questions were reviewed and amended by stakeholders, and then classified and refined to form the final list of top priorities via an online consensus process. Outcomes The top ten priorities were identified: three research, three policy, and four practice questions. Future research suggestions are discussed.

sheet.es: Si te preocupa el consumo de alcohol, otras sustancias o conductas con potencial adictivo en una persona autista, puedes hablar con ella, sin juzgar, sobre para qué le sirve: calmar la ansiedad social, afrontar problemas o disimular en lo social. Si hace falta, consulten con un profesional sanitario que conozca el autismo. Este estudio reunió a personas con experiencia vivida de autismo y/o adicción, y mediante una encuesta en línea y un consenso acordaron las diez preguntas prioritarias: tres de investigación, tres de políticas y cuatro de práctica. Límites: no ofrece respuestas ni recomendaciones de tratamiento, solo señala qué falta por investigar.
sheet.en: If you are worried about alcohol, other substances or potentially addictive behaviours in an autistic person, you can talk with them without judgement about what the use does for them: easing social anxiety, coping with problems or camouflaging socially. If needed, consult a health professional who understands autism. This study brought together people with lived experience of autism and/or addiction, who used an online survey and a consensus process to agree the top ten questions: three on research, three on policy and four on practice. Limits: it gives no answers or treatment advice, only what still needs to be researched.
sheet.sv: Om du oroar dig för alkohol, andra substanser eller potentiellt beroendeframkallande beteenden hos en autistisk person kan du prata med personen utan att döma om vad användningen ger: lindrar social ångest, hjälper att klara problem eller att kamouflera sig socialt. Vid behov kan ni kontakta en vårdgivare som kan autism. Studien samlade personer med egen erfarenhet av autism och/eller beroende, som med en webbenkät och en konsensusprocess enades om de tio viktigaste frågorna: tre om forskning, tre om policy och fyra om praktik. Begränsningar: den ger inga svar eller behandlingsråd, bara vad som behöver undersökas.

title: Menstruation and Autism: a qualitative systematic review.
authors: Ellis R, Williams G, Caemawr S, Craine M, Holloway W, Williams K, Shaw SCK, Grant A
abstract: Background Menstruation is a biological process which can be irregular, painful, and co-occur with fatigue, social withdrawal, and increased emotions. There is some evidence to suggest Autistic people experience menstruation differently to non-Autistic people. Methods This systematic review (PROSPERO registration: CRD42023399674) searched four databases in February 2023. We used thematic synthesis to analyse qualitative studies of experiences related to menstruation for Autistic people and people providing support to Autistic people. We also appraised the quality of studies with CASP. Results Our thematic synthesis of twelve (eight peer-reviewed; four grey literature) sources identified differing priorities between parents, professionals, and Autistic people. Autistic people reported physical, emotional and social impacts of menstruation. Furthermore, there were reports of increased Autism-specific experiences during menstruation such as increased sensory sensitivities, burnout and anxiety, which were often unseen by those who supported them. Autistic people's menstruation priorities were obtaining knowledge and skills ahead of their first period. However, parents and professionals focused on external behaviours including hygiene and obtaining independence in managing periods. Sources poorly described participant demographics and had a limited focus on Autistic perspectives. Conclusions We conclude there needs to be tailored support to meet the needs of both Autistic individuals and those who support them. This should be informed by research which centers Autistic people.

sheet.es: Pregunte a la persona autista qué necesita saber y practicar antes de su primera regla, y no se centre solo en la higiene o en la autonomía. Observe también que durante la menstruación pueden aumentar la sensibilidad sensorial, el agotamiento (burnout) y la ansiedad, aunque quizá no se vean desde fuera. La evidencia es una revisión sistemática de doce fuentes cualitativas, ocho revisadas por pares y cuatro de literatura gris, sobre personas autistas y quienes las apoyan. Sus límites: las fuentes describían poco a los participantes y daban poco espacio a las voces autistas, así que no vale para todas las personas.
sheet.en: Ask the autistic person what they want to know and practise before a first period, rather than focusing only on hygiene or independence. Also watch for more sensory sensitivity, burnout and anxiety around menstruation, which may not be visible from outside. The evidence is a systematic review of twelve qualitative sources, eight peer-reviewed and four grey literature, covering autistic people and those who support them. Its limits: the sources described participants poorly and gave limited space to autistic perspectives, so it cannot be applied to every person.
sheet.sv: Fråga den autistiska personen vad hen vill veta och öva på inför sin första mens, i stället för att bara fokusera på hygien eller självständighet. Var också uppmärksam på ökad sensorisk känslighet, utbrändhet och ångest kring mens, som kanske inte syns utifrån. Underlaget är en systematisk översikt av tolv kvalitativa källor, åtta granskade av experter och fyra grå litteratur, om autistiska personer och de som stöttar dem. Begränsningar: källorna beskrev deltagarna dåligt och lyfte autistiska perspektiv i liten utsträckning, så resultaten gäller inte alla.

title: "A combination of everything": a mixed-methods approach to the factors which autistic people consider important in suicidality.
authors: Moseley RL, Marsden SJ, Allison CL, Parsons TA, Cassidy S, Procyshyn T, Pelton M, Weir EM, Chikaura T, Mosse D, Hall I, Owens L, Cheyette J, Crichton D, Rodgers J, Hodges H, Baron-Cohen S
abstract: Background Suicide is a leading cause of death for autistic people, but inadequately explained by theories derived in non-autistic populations. Autistic people's perceptions of the factors underpinning suicidal experiences are vital for guiding conceptual understanding, risk assessment, and policy and clinical practice towards preventing suicide. Methods We recruited 1369 autistic participants for an online survey designed through consultation with autistic people. Participants were 326 cisgender men, 718 cisgender women, and 325 transgender or gender-divergent individuals, ranging from 16-89 years old. We asked them to rate the importance of 19 contributing factors to their suicidal thoughts and feelings, and enter their own explanations of additional factors if desired. Alongside thematically analysing this qualitative data, we examined whether ratings of contributing factors differed by age and gender, and whether ratings statistically predicted levels of lifetime suicidality. Results Loneliness, feelings of worthlessness/failure, hopelessness and mental illness were the highest rated contributing factors to suicidal thoughts and feelings, particularly by autistic women and sex/gender minorities; ratings also differed by age. Qualitative responses indicated the complexity of suicidality, wherein autistic status influenced both the nature of the stressors (e.g. societal stigma) and cognitive-emotional states (e.g. feeling disconnected through feeling different to others) that participants identified. Greater perceived importance of bullying, difficulties accessing support and past trauma characterised participants with experience of suicide plans or attempts. Conclusion While some of the experiences and mental states identified by participants resembled those identified in non-autistic groups, the psychological profile of autistic participants and their experiences of marginalisation appeared to heavily contextualise expressions of hopelessness, burdensomeness, worthlessness, loneliness and entrapment. Autistic people vary with regards the factors perceived to underpin suicidality. However, associations between suicidality and the perceived importance of bullying, trauma, and inability to access support highlight the necessity of societal and systemic change to prevent suicide.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista habla de pensamientos suicidas, escúchala sin juzgar y pregunta qué pesa más para ella: las razones varían mucho. Preguntar por soledad, sensación de fracaso, desesperanza, acoso, trauma o falta de apoyo puede ayudar. Es una encuesta en línea con 1369 personas autistas de 16-89 años, que valoraron 19 posibles factores y añadieron explicaciones propias. Los resultados reflejan percepciones, no causas demostradas, y no valen igual para cada persona. Si tú o alguien cercano pensáis en hacerse daño, buscad ayuda profesional: un profesional clínico, un servicio de salud o un servicio de crisis. Si hay peligro inmediato, llamad al número de emergencias de vuestro país.
sheet.en: If an autistic person talks about suicidal thoughts, listen without judging and ask what weighs most for them: the reasons vary a lot. Asking about loneliness, feeling like a failure, hopelessness, bullying, trauma or lack of support may help. This was an online survey of 1369 autistic people aged 16-89, who rated 19 possible factors and added their own explanations. The results reflect perceptions, not proven causes, and do not apply equally to every person. If you or someone close is thinking of self-harm, seek professional help: a clinician, a health service or a crisis service. In immediate danger, call the emergency number of your country.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person pratar om självmordstankar, lyssna utan att döma och fråga vad som väger tyngst för just hen: skälen varierar mycket. Det kan hjälpa att fråga om ensamhet, känsla av misslyckande, hopplöshet, mobbning, trauma eller brist på stöd. Detta var en webbenkät med 1369 autistiska personer i åldern 16-89, som bedömde 19 möjliga faktorer och la till egna förklaringar. Resultaten visar upplevelser, inte bevisade orsaker, och gäller inte lika för alla. Om du eller någon nära dig tänker på att skada sig själv, sök professionell hjälp: en läkare eller annan vårdgivare, en vårdinstans eller en krisjour. Vid akut fara, ring ditt lands larmnummer.

title: Autism and the Menopause Transition: A Mixed-Methods Systematic Review.
authors: Grant A, Axbey H, Holloway W, Caemawr S, Craine M, Lim H, Shaw SCK, Ellis R
abstract: Background The menopause transition commonly occurs between the ages of 45 and 55 years. In a general population, hormonal shifts result in a range of biological, psychological, and social changes. Recently, research has begun to focus on Autistic people's experiences of the menopause. Methods We undertook a prospectively registered (PROSPERO: CRD42023450736) systematic review of research and first-hand accounts from grey literature related to Autism and menopause. We utilised the Joanna Briggs Institute convergent integrated synthesis approach. Results Our search identified eight studies and seven pieces of grey literature, primarily comprising Autistic people. No studies evaluated interventions or provided data from those supporting Autistic people. We developed three themes. First, "knowledge of the menopause transition and peer support" focused on Autistic people's lack of knowledge of menopause symptoms, including differences for Autistic people, and the role of peer support in obtaining knowledge. Second, "Autistic people's experiences of menopausal symptoms" describes a broad range of negative symptoms which sometimes had significant impacts on mental health and daily activities. Limited quantitative evidence highlighted increased menopause symptom severity for Autistic people compared to non-Autistic comparison groups. Menopause symptoms impacted on work and relationships, and there was an inter-relationship between menopausal symptoms and Autistic identities. Third, "treatment of menopause symptoms" describes non-medical and medical approaches, including Hormone Replacement Therapy, to reduce symptom impacts. Most reports of medical treatment highlighted barriers to access, or negative experiences of appointments. Conclusion There is a clear need for better menopause supports for Autistic people. This should include Autism-friendly information to increase knowledge of menopause, and how it may impact Autistic people. Corresponding information should also be available for health professionals, with systemic barriers to healthcare also reduced to allow the best chance for Autistic people to receive menopause support. Autism-specific menopause peer support may be worthy of evaluation.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista de entre 45 y 55 años, o lo eres tú, conviene hablar pronto de la menopausia: buscar información clara y accesible, llevar anotados los síntomas a la consulta y, si es posible, contactar con otras personas autistas que la hayan vivido. Es una revisión sistemática de ocho estudios y siete textos de otras fuentes, sobre todo de personas autistas. Contó experiencias de síntomas negativos que afectaban al trabajo y a las relaciones, y a menudo había barreras para acceder a la atención médica. Ningún estudio evaluó intervenciones, y la evidencia cuantitativa era limitada, así que no vale para todas las personas. Las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional sanitario.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person aged 45 to 55, or you are one, it helps to talk about menopause early: look for clear, accessible information, bring a written list of symptoms to appointments and, if possible, connect with other autistic people who have been through it. This is a systematic review of eight studies and seven pieces of grey literature, mostly involving autistic people. It described negative symptoms that affected work and relationships, and frequent barriers to getting medical care. No study evaluated interventions and the quantitative evidence was limited, so it cannot be applied to everyone. Medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person mellan 45 och 55 år, eller själv är det, hjälper det att prata om klimakteriet i god tid: leta efter tydlig, tillgänglig information, ta med en skriven lista över symtom till vårdbesök och, om det går, ta kontakt med andra autistiska personer som varit med om det. Detta är en systematisk översikt av åtta studier och sju andra källor, främst med autistiska personer. Den beskrev negativa symtom som påverkade arbete och relationer, och ofta hinder för att få medicinsk vård. Ingen studie utvärderade insatser och den kvantitativa evidensen var begränsad, så resultaten gäller inte alla. Medicinska beslut hör till en läkare eller annan vårdgivare.

title: Neurotype-Matching, but Not Being Autistic, Influences Self and Observer Ratings of Interpersonal Rapport.
authors: Crompton CJ, Sharp M, Axbey H, Fletcher-Watson S, Flynn EG, Ropar D
abstract: The Double Empathy Problem suggests that communicative difficulties between autistic and non-autistic people are due to bi-directional differences in communicative style and a reciprocal lack of understanding. If true, there should be increased similarity in interaction style, resulting in higher rapport during interactions between pairs of the same neurotype. Here, we provide two empirical tests of rapport, with data revealing whether self- and observer- rated rapport varies depending on the match or mismatch in autism status within a pair. An additional opportunity afforded by these data is to examine the effect of the autism status of the rater on the perceived rapport between matched and mismatched pairs. In Study 1 72 participants were allocated to one of three dyad conditions: autistic pairs ( n = 24), non-autistic pairs ( n = 24) and mixed pairs ( n = 12 autistic; n = 12 non-autistic). Each participant completed three semi-structured interactions with their partner, rating rapport after each interaction. Non-autistic pairs experienced higher self-rated rapport than mixed and autistic pairs, and autistic pairs experienced higher rapport than mixed pairs. In Study 2 ( n = 80) autistic and non-autistic observers rated interactional rapport while watching videoed interactions between autistic pairs, non-autistic pairs, and mixed pairs ( n = 18, a subset of participants in Study 1). Mixed pairs were rated significantly lower on rapport than autistic and non-autistic pairs, and autistic pairs were rated more highly for rapport than non-autistic pairs. Both autistic and non-autistic observers show similar patterns in how they rate the rapport of autistic, non-autistic, and mixed pairs. In summary, autistic people experience high interactional rapport when interacting with other autistic people, and this is also detected by external observers. Rather than autistic people experiencing low rapport in all contexts, their rapport ratings are influenced by a mismatch of diagnosis. These findings suggest that autistic people possess a distinct mode of social interaction style, rather than demonstrating social skills deficits. These data are considered in terms of their implications for psychological theories of autism, as well as practical impact on educational and clinical practice.

title: Same or Different: The Overlap Between Children With Auditory Processing Disorders and Children With Other Developmental Disorders: A Systematic Review.
authors: de Wit E, van Dijk P, Hanekamp S, Visser-Bochane MI, Steenbergen B, van der Schans CP, Luinge MR
abstract: Objectives Children diagnosed with auditory processing disorders (APD) experience difficulties in auditory functioning and with memory, attention, language, and reading tasks. However, it is not clear whether the behavioral characteristics of these children are distinctive from the behavioral characteristics of children diagnosed with a different developmental disorder, such as specific language impairment (SLI), dyslexia, attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), learning disorder (LD), or autism spectrum disorder. This study describes the performance of children diagnosed with APD, SLI, dyslexia, ADHD, and LD to different outcome measurements. The aim of this study was to determine (1) which characteristics of APD overlap with the characteristics of children with SLI, dyslexia, ADHD, LD, or autism spectrum disorder; and (2) if there are characteristics that distinguish children diagnosed with APD from children diagnosed with other developmental disorders. Design A systematic review.
