Six electronic databases (Pubmed, CINAHL, Eric, PsychINFO, Communication & Mass Media Complete, and EMBASE) were searched to find peer-reviewed studies from 1954 to May 2015. The authors included studies reporting behaviors and performance of children with (suspected) APD and children diagnosed with a different developmental disorder (SLI, Dyslexia, ADHD, and LD). Two researchers identified and screened the studies independently. Methodological quality of the included studies was assessed with the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association's levels-of-evidence scheme. Results In total, 13 studies of which the methodological quality was moderate were included in this systematic review. In five studies, the performance of children diagnosed with APD was compared with the performance of children diagnosed with SLI: in two with children diagnosed with dyslexia, one with children diagnosed with ADHD, and in another one with children diagnosed with LD. Ten of the studies included children who met the criteria for more than one diagnosis. In four studies, there was a comparison made between the performances of children with comorbid disorders. There were no studies found in which the performance of children diagnosed with APD was compared with the performance of children diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder. Children diagnosed with APD broadly share the same characteristics as children diagnosed with other developmental disorders, with only minor differences between them. Differences were determined with the auditory and visual Duration Pattern Test, the Children's Auditory Processing Performance Scale questionnaire, and the subtests of the Listening in Spatialized Noise-Sentences test, in which noise is spatially separated from target sentences. However, these differences are not consistent between studies and are not found in comparison to all groups of children with other developmental disorders. Conclusions Children diagnosed with APD perform equally to children diagnosed with SLI, dyslexia, ADHD, and LD on tests of intelligence, memory or attention, and language tests. Only small differences between groups were found for sensory and perceptual functioning tasks (auditory and visual). In addition, children diagnosed with dyslexia performed poorer in reading tasks compared with children diagnosed with APD. The result is possibly confounded by poor quality of the research studies and the low quality of the used outcome measures. More research with higher scientific rigor is required to better understand the differences and similarities in children with various neurodevelopmental disorders.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo tiene dificultades para escuchar en lugares ruidosos, recordar instrucciones orales o prestar atención, la etiqueta concreta importa menos que observar qué le ayuda: reducir el ruido de fondo, dar instrucciones cortas y apoyos visuales, y comprobar la audición. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 13 estudios que compararon a niños con trastorno del procesamiento auditivo con niños con trastorno del lenguaje, dislexia, TDAH o dificultades de aprendizaje, y encontró que se parecen mucho, con pocas diferencias. Límites: la calidad de los estudios era moderada, las pruebas eran débiles y no se incluyó a ningún niño autista, así que no dice nada directo sobre el autismo.
sheet.en: If your child struggles to listen in noisy places, remember spoken instructions or keep attention, the exact label may matter less than noticing what helps: lowering background noise, giving short instructions with visual supports, and checking hearing. This systematic review pooled 13 studies comparing children with auditory processing disorder to children with language disorder, dyslexia, ADHD or learning disorders, and found they were largely similar, with only small, inconsistent differences. Limits: study quality was moderate, the tests used were weak, and no autistic children were compared, so it tells us nothing direct about autism.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn har svårt att lyssna i bullriga miljöer, minnas muntliga instruktioner eller hålla uppmärksamheten kan den exakta diagnosen betyda mindre än att se vad som hjälper: mindre bakgrundsljud, korta instruktioner med bildstöd och en hörselkontroll. Denna systematiska översikt samlade 13 studier som jämförde barn med auditiv processningsstörning med barn med språkstörning, dyslexi, ADHD eller inlärningssvårigheter, och fann att grupperna var mycket lika, med bara små och ojämna skillnader. Begränsningar: studiernas kvalitet var måttlig, testerna svaga och inga autistiska barn jämfördes, så resultatet säger inget direkt om autism.

title: An Overview of the Main Genetic, Epigenetic and Environmental Factors Involved in Autism Spectrum Disorder Focusing on Synaptic Activity.
authors: Masini E, Loi E, Vega-Benedetti AF, Carta M, Doneddu G, Fadda R, Zavattari P
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder that affects social interaction and communication, with restricted interests, activity and behaviors. ASD is highly familial, indicating that genetic background strongly contributes to the development of this condition. However, only a fraction of the total number of genes thought to be associated with the condition have been discovered. Moreover, other factors may play an important role in ASD onset. In fact, it has been shown that parental conditions and in utero and perinatal factors may contribute to ASD etiology. More recently, epigenetic changes, including DNA methylation and micro RNA alterations, have been associated with ASD and proposed as potential biomarkers. This review aims to provide a summary of the literature regarding ASD candidate genes, mainly focusing on synapse formation and functionality and relevant epigenetic and environmental aspects acting in concert to determine ASD onset.

sheet.es: Esta revisión no ofrece nada que haya que hacer mañana por la mañana, pero sirve de contexto: el autismo no se explica por una sola causa, y nada de lo que hizo o dejó de hacer una familia queda señalado aquí. Es una revisión de la literatura que resume estudios sobre genes candidatos, sobre todo los relacionados con las sinapsis, además de cambios epigenéticos y factores ambientales, como condiciones de los progenitores y factores durante el embarazo y el parto. Sus límites: según el texto, solo se ha descubierto una parte de los genes implicados, y los marcadores epigenéticos solo se proponen como posibles. No sirve para explicar a una persona concreta ni para tomar decisiones individuales.
sheet.en: This review offers nothing to do tomorrow morning, but it gives useful context: autism is not explained by a single cause, and nothing here points to anything a family did or did not do. It is a review of the literature summarising studies on candidate genes, mainly those linked to synapses, plus epigenetic changes and environmental factors, such as parental conditions and factors during pregnancy and birth. Its limits: the text says only a fraction of the genes involved have been found, and epigenetic markers are only proposed as possibilities. It cannot explain any one person or guide individual decisions.
sheet.sv: Den här översikten ger inget att göra i morgon bitti, men den ger bakgrund: autism förklaras inte av en enda orsak, och inget här pekar på något som en familj gjort eller inte gjort. Det är en litteraturöversikt som sammanfattar studier om kandidatgener, främst sådana kopplade till synapser, samt epigenetiska förändringar och miljöfaktorer, till exempel föräldrars tillstånd och faktorer under graviditet och förlossning. Begränsningar: enligt texten har bara en del av de inblandade generna hittats, och epigenetiska markörer föreslås bara som möjliga. Den kan inte förklara en enskild person eller styra individuella beslut.

title: No preference for direct versus averted gaze in autistic adults: a reinforced preferential looking paradigm.
authors: Clin E, Maes P, Stercq F, Kissine M
abstract: Background With the overarching objective to gain better insights into social attention in autistic adults, the present study addresses three outstanding issues about face processing in autism. First, do autistic adults display a preference for mouths over eyes; second, do they avoid direct gaze; third, is atypical visual exploration of faces in autism mediated by gender, social anxiety or alexithymia? Methods We used a novel reinforced preferential looking paradigm with a group of autistic adults (n = 43, 23 women) pairwise matched on age with neurotypical participants (n = 43, 21 women). Participants watched 28 different pairs of 5 s video recordings of a speaking person: the two videos, simultaneously displayed on the screen, were identical except that gaze was directed at the camera in one video and averted in the other. After a 680 ms transition phase, a short reinforcement animation appeared on the side that had displayed the direct gaze. Results None of the groups showed a preference for mouths over eyes. However, neurotypical participants fixated significantly more the stimuli with direct gaze, while no such preference emerged in autistic participants. As the experiment progressed, neurotypical participants also increasingly anticipated the appearance of the reinforcement, based on the location of the stimulus with the direct gaze, while no such anticipation emerged in autistic participants. Limitations Our autistic participants scored higher on the social anxiety and alexithymia questionnaires than neurotypicals. Future studies should match neurotypical and autistic participants on social anxiety and alexithymia and complement questionnaires with physiological measures of anxiety. Conclusions The absence of preference for direct versus averted gaze in the autistic group is probably due to difficulties in distinguishing eye gaze direction, potentially linked to a reduced spontaneous exploration or avoidance of the eye region. Social attention and preference for direct versus averted gaze correlated with alexithymia and social anxiety scores, but not gender.

sheet.es: No hace falta exigir contacto visual a una persona autista adulta. Si algo importa, dilo con palabras claras en lugar de esperar que se entienda por la mirada, y deja que cada persona elija dónde mirar. Es un estudio con 43 adultos autistas y 43 adultos neurotípicos, que miraron pares de vídeos de una persona hablando, con la mirada dirigida a la cámara o desviada. El grupo neurotípico prefirió la mirada directa y el grupo autista no mostró esa preferencia. Tiene límites: el grupo autista puntuó más alto en ansiedad social y alexitimia, y los resultados no describen a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: There is no need to expect eye contact from an autistic adult. If something matters, say it in clear words rather than relying on gaze, and let each person choose where to look. This was a study with 43 autistic adults and 43 neurotypical adults, who watched pairs of videos of a person speaking, with gaze directed at the camera or averted. The neurotypical group preferred direct gaze, while the autistic group showed no such preference. It has limits: the autistic group scored higher on social anxiety and alexithymia questionnaires, and the results do not describe every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Du behöver inte kräva ögonkontakt av en autistisk vuxen. Om något är viktigt, säg det med tydliga ord i stället för att förlita dig på blicken, och låt varje person välja var hen tittar. Det var en studie med 43 autistiska vuxna och 43 neurotypiska vuxna som tittade på videopar med en talande person, där blicken var riktad mot kameran eller bortvänd. Den neurotypiska gruppen föredrog direkt blick, medan den autistiska gruppen inte visade någon sådan preferens. Studien har begränsningar: den autistiska gruppen skattade högre på social ångest och alexitymi, och resultaten gäller inte alla autistiska personer.

title: A Pilot Randomised Control Trial of Digitally-Mediated Social Stories for Children on the Autism Spectrum.
authors: Hanrahan R, Smith E, Johnson H, Constantin A, Brosnan M
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Social stories is a widely used intervention for children on the autism spectrum, particularly within an educational context. To date, systematic reviews and meta analyses of the research evaluating social stories has produced mixed results, often due to a lack of methodological rigour and variability in the development and delivery of the social stories. To address the gap in methodological rigour, a pilot Randomised Control Trial (RCT) was conducted, incorporating a social stories intervention group (n = 9 children on the autism spectrum) and an attentional control group who received a poem (n = 6 children on the autism spectrum) using a digital platform to address variability. Digitally-mediated social stories were found to be effective in producing beneficial changes in behaviour outcomes, which were sustained at a six-week follow up.

sheet.es: Si piensa usar historias sociales con un niño autista, puede probar una versión digital, breve y a medida de una situación concreta, y observar con él si le resulta útil. En este ensayo piloto aleatorizado, 9 niños autistas recibieron historias sociales digitales y 6 niños autistas recibieron un poema como grupo de control. Los autores hallaron cambios beneficiosos en la conducta, que se mantuvieron en un seguimiento a las seis semanas. Es un estudio muy pequeño y piloto, así que no demuestra que funcione para cada niño. Conviene contar siempre con la opinión del propio niño.
sheet.en: If you are thinking of using social stories with an autistic child, you could try a short digital version written around one specific situation, and watch with the child whether it helps. In this pilot randomised trial, 9 autistic children received digitally delivered social stories and 6 autistic children received a poem as a control group. The authors found beneficial changes in behaviour, which lasted at a six-week follow-up. This is a very small pilot study, so it does not show the approach will work for every child. Always include the child's own views.
sheet.sv: Om du funderar på sociala berättelser för ett autistiskt barn kan du prova en kort digital version kopplad till en specifik situation och se tillsammans med barnet om den hjälper. I denna randomiserade pilotstudie fick 9 autistiska barn digitala sociala berättelser och 6 autistiska barn fick en dikt som kontrollgrupp. Forskarna fann gynnsamma förändringar i beteende, som höll i sig vid uppföljning efter sex veckor. Studien är mycket liten och en pilot, så den visar inte att metoden fungerar för varje barn. Ta alltid med barnets egna synpunkter.

title: SOLACE: A Psychosocial Stigma Protection Intervention to Improve the Mental Health of Parents of Autistic Children-A Feasibility Randomised Controlled Trial.
authors: Lodder A, Papadopoulos C, Randhawa G
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: This study presents findings from a feasibility trial, testing an 8-week psychosocial stigma protection intervention (SOLACE) designed to improve the mental health of parents of autistic children. Seventeen parents were stratified then randomly assigned to either SOLACE (n = 9) or control group (n = 8). Retention and adherence rates were excellent with minimal missing data suggesting SOLACE had good acceptability and feasibility. Quantitative analysis revealed that mental health scores had significantly improved for those who took part in SOLACE compared to no significant changes for control group participants. In addition, changes in secondary outcome measures (e.g. stigma, self-esteem and self-compassion) were in favour of SOLACE. Focus group interviews revealed that SOLACE was acceptable to parents. Results suggest that a full randomised controlled trial is warranted.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una criatura autista y sientes el peso del estigma, puede ayudarte buscar apoyo pensado para madres y padres, como un programa breve que trabaje la autocompasión y la autoestima. Este estudio fue un ensayo de viabilidad aleatorizado: 17 madres y padres de niños autistas recibieron SOLACE, un programa de 8 semanas (n = 9), o formaron parte del grupo de control (n = 8). Quienes participaron en SOLACE mejoraron su salud mental y valoraron bien el programa. El grupo es muy pequeño, y es un primer paso: los autores indican que hace falta un ensayo mayor. No sirve como regla para todas las familias.
sheet.en: If you parent an autistic child and feel the weight of stigma, it may help to look for support designed for parents, such as a short programme that works on self-compassion and self-esteem. This was a randomised feasibility trial: 17 parents of autistic children either took part in SOLACE, an 8-week programme (n = 9), or were in the control group (n = 8). Parents in SOLACE improved in mental health scores and found the programme acceptable. The group was very small and this is only a first step: the authors say a full trial is needed. It is not a rule for every family.
sheet.sv: Om du är förälder till ett autistiskt barn och känner tyngden av stigma kan det hjälpa att söka stöd riktat till föräldrar, till exempel ett kort program som tränar självmedkänsla och självkänsla. Studien var en randomiserad genomförbarhetsstudie: 17 föräldrar till autistiska barn deltog antingen i SOLACE, ett program på 8 veckor (n = 9), eller i kontrollgruppen (n = 8). Föräldrarna i SOLACE förbättrade sina värden för psykisk hälsa och tyckte att programmet var acceptabelt. Gruppen var mycket liten och detta är bara ett första steg: forskarna menar att en fullskalig studie behövs. Det är ingen regel för alla familjer.

title: Examining the relationship between measures of autistic traits and neural synchrony during movies in children with and without autism.
authors: Lyons KM, Stevenson RA, Owen AM, Stojanoski B
abstract: Children who have been diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) often show a marked deficit in measures of social cognition. In autistic adults, measures of social cognition have been shown to relate to differences in brain synchronization (as measured by fMRI) when individuals are processing naturalistic stimuli, such as movies. However, whether children who differ in their degree of autistic traits, with or without a diagnosis of ASD, differ in their neural responses to movies has not yet been investigated. In the current study, neural synchrony, measured using fMRI, was examined in three groups of children aged 7 to 12, who differed with respect to scores on a measure of autistic traits associated with social impairment and whether or not they had been diagnosed with ASD. While watching the movie 'Despicable Me', those diagnosed with ASD had significantly less neural synchrony in areas that have been previously shown to be associated with social cognition (e.g. areas related to 'theory of mind'), and plot following (e.g. the lateral prefrontal cortex), than those who did not have an ASD diagnosis. In contrast, two groups who differed in their degree of autistic traits, but did not have a diagnosis of ASD, showed no significant differences in neural synchrony across the whole brain. These results shed some light on how autistic traits may contribute to an individual's conscious experience of the world, and how, for children with ASD, that experience may differ markedly from that of those without ASD.

sheet.es: Mañana, si ve una película con su hijo o hija autista, no dé por hecho que ambos viven la historia igual: puede preguntarle qué le llamó la atención y qué entendió, y escuchar su versión sin corregirla. Evidencia: estudio con resonancia magnética en tres grupos de niños de 7 a 12 años que veían la película 'Despicable Me'; los niños con diagnóstico de autismo mostraron menos sincronía cerebral con otros en áreas ligadas a la cognición social y al seguimiento de la trama. Límites: es un estudio de grupos, no explica a ninguna persona concreta, y la menor sincronía no significa que disfrute o comprenda menos.
sheet.en: Tomorrow, if you watch a film with your autistic child, don't assume you both experience the story the same way: ask what caught their attention and what they understood, and listen to their version without correcting it. Evidence: an fMRI study of three groups of children aged 7 to 12 watching 'Despicable Me'; children diagnosed with autism showed less brain synchrony with others in areas linked to social cognition and following the plot. Limits: it compares groups, cannot explain any one child, and lower synchrony does not mean they enjoy or understand the film less.
sheet.sv: I morgon, om du tittar på film med ditt autistiska barn, anta inte att ni upplever berättelsen likadant: fråga vad som fångade uppmärksamheten och vad barnet förstod, och lyssna på barnets version utan att rätta. Evidens: en fMRI-studie med tre grupper barn i åldern 7 till 12 som såg 'Despicable Me'; barn med autismdiagnos hade lägre hjärnsynkronisering med andra i områden kopplade till social kognition och att följa handlingen. Begränsningar: studien jämför grupper, kan inte förklara ett enskilt barn, och lägre synkronisering betyder inte att barnet tycker mindre om filmen eller förstår den sämre.

title: Using Zebrafish to Model Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Comparison of ASD Risk Genes Between Zebrafish and Their Mammalian Counterparts.
authors: Rea V, Van Raay TJ
abstract: Autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) are a highly variable and complex set of neurological disorders that alter neurodevelopment and cognitive function, which usually presents with social and learning impairments accompanied with other comorbid symptoms like hypersensitivity or hyposensitivity, or repetitive behaviors. Autism can be caused by genetic and/or environmental factors and unraveling the etiology of ASD has proven challenging, especially given that different genetic mutations can cause both similar and different phenotypes that all fall within the autism spectrum. Furthermore, the list of ASD risk genes is ever increasing making it difficult to synthesize a common theme. The use of rodent models to enhance ASD research is invaluable and is beginning to unravel the underlying molecular mechanisms of this disease. Recently, zebrafish have been recognized as a useful model of neurodevelopmental disorders with regards to genetics, pharmacology and behavior and one of the main foundations supporting autism research (SFARI) recently identified 12 ASD risk genes with validated zebrafish mutant models. Here, we describe what is known about those 12 ASD risk genes in human, mice and zebrafish to better facilitate this research. We also describe several non-genetic models including pharmacological and gnotobiotic models that are used in zebrafish to study ASD.

sheet.es: Este estudio no ofrece nada que aplicar mañana por la mañana en casa: es investigación de laboratorio. Sirve para entender que el autismo tiene muchas variantes y que no hay una única explicación. Es una revisión que resume lo que se sabe sobre 12 genes de riesgo en personas, ratones y peces cebra, además de algunos modelos no genéticos. No incluyó a personas autistas ni probó apoyos, y sus resultados no valen como regla para cada persona. Si tiene dudas médicas, consulte a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: This study offers nothing to apply at home tomorrow morning: it is laboratory research. What it can help you remember is that autism has many variations and no single explanation. It is a review summarising what is known about 12 risk genes in humans, mice and zebrafish, plus some non-genetic models. It did not involve autistic people or test any supports, and its findings are not a rule for every person. For medical questions, talk to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Den här studien ger inget du kan använda hemma i morgon bitti: det är laboratorieforskning. Den kan påminna om att autism har många variationer och ingen enskild förklaring. Det är en översikt som sammanfattar vad som är känt om 12 riskgener hos människor, möss och zebrafisk, samt några icke-genetiska modeller. Den omfattade inga autistiska personer och testade inga stöd, och resultaten gäller inte som regel för varje person. Vid medicinska frågor, prata med en läkare.

title: Leveraging large genomic datasets to illuminate the pathobiology of autism spectrum disorders.
authors: Searles Quick VB, Wang B, State MW
journal: Neuropsychopharmacology : official publication of the American College of Neuropsychopharmacology
abstract: "Big data" approaches in the form of large-scale human genomic studies have led to striking advances in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) genetics. Similar to many other psychiatric syndromes, advances in genotyping technology, allowing for inexpensive genome-wide assays, has confirmed the contribution of polygenic inheritance involving common alleles of small effect, a handful of which have now been definitively identified. However, the past decade of gene discovery in ASD has been most notable for the application, in large family-based cohorts, of high-density microarray studies of submicroscopic chromosomal structure as well as high-throughput DNA sequencing-leading to the identification of an increasingly long list of risk regions and genes disrupted by rare, de novo germline mutations of large effect. This genomic architecture offers particular advantages for the illumination of biological mechanisms but also presents distinctive challenges. While the tremendous locus heterogeneity and functional pleiotropy associated with the more than 100 identified ASD-risk genes and regions is daunting, a growing armamentarium of comprehensive, large, foundational -omics databases, across species and capturing developmental trajectories, are increasingly contributing to a deeper understanding of ASD pathology.

sheet.es: Qué significa para usted mañana: nada cambia en la rutina diaria. Este trabajo trata de genética, no de estrategias de apoyo. Si tiene dudas sobre la genética de su familiar, un servicio de genética clínica puede orientarle. Sobre la evidencia: es una revisión de estudios genómicos grandes en familias, y menciona más de 100 genes y regiones de riesgo identificados. Límites: no evalúa apoyos ni intervenciones, y que existan genes asociados no explica a una persona concreta ni la define. La autonomía y las necesidades de cada persona autista siguen siendo lo central.
sheet.en: What this means for you tomorrow: nothing changes in daily routines. This work is about genetics, not support strategies. If you have questions about your family member's genetics, a clinical genetics service can guide you. On the evidence: it is a review of large genomic studies, including family-based cohorts, and it mentions more than 100 identified risk genes and regions. Limits: it does not test supports or interventions, and associated genes do not explain or define any one person. Each autistic person's needs and autonomy stay at the centre.
sheet.sv: Vad det betyder för dig i morgon: inget ändras i vardagsrutinerna. Arbetet handlar om genetik, inte om stödstrategier. Har du frågor om genetiken hos en anhörig kan en klinisk genetisk mottagning vägleda dig. Om underlaget: det är en översikt av stora genomstudier, bland annat i familjebaserade grupper, och den nämner mer än 100 identifierade riskgener och regioner. Begränsningar: den testar inte stöd eller insatser, och associerade gener förklarar eller definierar inte en enskild person. Varje autistisk persons behov och självbestämmande står fortfarande i centrum.

title: Developmental-behavioral profiles in children with autism spectrum disorder and co-occurring gastrointestinal symptoms.
authors: Restrepo B, Angkustsiri K, Taylor SL, Rogers SJ, Cabral J, Heath B, Hechtman A, Solomon M, Ashwood P, Amaral DG, Nordahl CW
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms are frequently reported in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). We evaluated the frequency and severity of GI symptoms in preschool-aged children with ASD compared to participants with typical development (TD). Our goal was to ascertain whether GI symptoms are associated with differences in sex or developmental and behavioral measures. Participants were between 2 and 3.5 years of age and included 255 children with ASD (184 males/71 females) and 129 age-matched TD controls (75 males/54 females). A parent interview was used to assess GI symptoms (abdominal pain, gaseousness/bloating, diarrhea, constipation, pain on stooling, vomiting, difficulty swallowing, blood in stool or in vomit). Children with GI symptoms in each diagnostic group were compared to children without GI symptoms on measures of developmental, behavioral, and adaptive functioning. GI symptoms were reported more frequently in children with ASD compared to the TD group (47.8% vs. 17.8%, respectively). Children with ASD were also more likely to experience multiple GI symptoms (30.6% vs. 5.4%). GI symptoms were equally common in males and females across both diagnostic groups. There were no statistically significant differences in developmental or adaptive measures based on presence of GI symptoms in either ASD or TD children. Co-occurring GI symptoms were, however, associated with increased self-injurious behaviors, restricted stereotyped behaviors, aggressive behaviors, sleep problems and attention problems in both ASD and TD children. In children with ASD, a higher number of GI symptoms was associated with an increase in self-injurious behaviors, somatic complaints, reduced sleep duration, and increased parasomnias. LAY SUMMARY: ASD is characterized by challenges in social communication and repetitive behaviors. But, people with autism have many other difficulties including gastrointestinal problems. Children with ASD were three times more likely to experience GI symptoms than typically developing peers. Increased GI symptoms are associated with increased problem behaviors such as sleep problems, self-injury, and body aches. Since GI symptoms are often treatable, it is important to recognize them as soon as possible. Both clinicians and parents should become more aware of the high occurrence of GI problems in autistic people. Autism Res 2020, 13: 1778-1789. © 2020 International Society for Autism Research and Wiley Periodicals LLC.

sheet.es: Si su hijo autista muestra cambios en el sueño, dolor aparente o conductas de autolesión, vale la pena preguntarse si hay molestias digestivas y comentarlo con su pediatra. Este estudio de investigación con 255 niños autistas y 129 niños de desarrollo típico, de 2 a 3.5 años, usó una entrevista a madres y padres. Los síntomas digestivos se informaron más en niños autistas (47.8% frente a 17.8%) y se asociaron con más autolesiones y problemas de sueño. Sin embargo, no prueba que una cosa cause la otra y no vale para todos los niños. Si le preocupa la autolesión, busque ayuda profesional: un clínico, un servicio de salud o un servicio de crisis. Ante peligro inmediato, llame al número de emergencias de su país.
sheet.en: If your autistic child shows changes in sleep, seeming pain or self-injury, it may be worth asking whether stomach or bowel discomfort is involved, and raising it with your child's doctor. This research study included 255 autistic children and 129 typically developing children aged 2 to 3.5 years, using a parent interview. Gut symptoms were reported more often in autistic children (47.8% vs. 17.8%) and were linked with more self-injury and sleep problems. It cannot show that one causes the other, and it does not apply to every child. If self-injury worries you, please contact professional help: a clinician, a health service or a crisis service. In immediate danger, call your country's emergency number.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn får förändrad sömn, verkar ha ont eller skadar sig själv kan det vara värt att fundera på om magen eller tarmarna spelar in, och ta upp det med barnets läkare. Forskningsstudien omfattade 255 autistiska barn och 129 barn med typisk utveckling, 2 till 3.5 år, och bygger på en intervju med föräldrar. Magsymtom rapporterades oftare hos autistiska barn (47.8% mot 17.8%) och hängde ihop med mer självskadande och sömnproblem. Studien visar inte att det ena orsakar det andra och gäller inte alla barn. Om självskadande oroar dig, sök professionell hjälp: en läkare, vården eller en krisjour. Vid akut fara, ring ditt lands nödnummer.

title: Multinutrients for the Treatment of Psychiatric Symptoms in Clinical Samples: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
authors: Johnstone JM, Hughes A, Goldenberg JZ, Romijn AR, Rucklidge JJ
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis focused on randomized controlled trials (RCT) of multinutrients consisting of at least four vitamins and/or minerals as interventions for participants with psychiatric symptoms. A systematic search identified 16 RCTs that fit the inclusion criteria ( n = 1719 participants) in six psychiatric categories: depression, post-disaster stress, antisocial behavior, behavioral deficits in dementia, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, and autism. Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluations (GRADE) was used to rate the evidence base. Significant clinical benefit was assessed using minimal clinically important differences (MIDs). Due to heterogeneity in participants, multinutrient formulas, outcome measures, and absence of complete data, only the Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) category was eligible for meta-analyses. In ADHD populations, statistically and clinically significant improvements were found in global functioning, Mean Difference (MD) -3.3, p = 0.001, MID -3.26; Standardized Mean Difference (SMD) -0.49 p = 0.001 MD -0.5), clinician ratings of global improvement (MD -0.58, p = 0.001, MID -0.5) and ADHD improvement (MD -0.54, p = 0.002, MID -0.5), and clinician (but not observer) measures of ADHD inattentive symptoms (MD -1.53, p = 0.05, MID -0.5). Narrative synthesis also revealed a pattern of benefit for global measures of improvement, for example: in autism, and in participants with behavioral deficits in dementia. Post-natural disaster anxiety and the number of violent incidents in prison populations also improved. Broad-spectrum formulas (vitamins + minerals) demonstrated more robust effects than formulas with fewer ingredients. This review highlights the need for robust methodology-RCTs that report full data, including means and standard deviations for all outcomes-in order to further elucidate the effects of multinutrients for psychiatric symptoms.

sheet.es: Si te planteas darle multivitamínicos a una persona autista, habla antes con su médico o dietista: es una decisión sanitaria y no hay una pauta general. Este metaanálisis reunió 16 ensayos aleatorizados con 1719 participantes en seis categorías, entre ellas autismo. Solo el TDAH tuvo datos suficientes para combinarse; en autismo hubo un patrón de mejora global, pero solo descrito de forma narrativa. Como los ensayos eran muy distintos y faltaban datos, no permite concluir que ayude a una persona concreta.
sheet.en: If you are wondering about giving a multivitamin or mineral formula to an autistic person, talk with their doctor or dietitian first: it is a health decision, and there is no general rule. This meta-analysis pooled 16 randomized trials with 1719 participants across six categories, including autism. Only ADHD had enough data to combine; in autism there was a pattern of global improvement, but it was only described narratively. Because the trials differed a lot and some data were missing, it cannot show that this helps any one person.
sheet.sv: Om du funderar på att ge en autistisk person multivitamin eller mineraltillskott, tala först med hens läkare eller dietist: det är ett medicinskt beslut och det finns ingen allmän regel. Den här metaanalysen samlade 16 randomiserade studier med 1719 deltagare i sex kategorier, bland dem autism. Bara ADHD hade tillräckligt med data för att slås ihop; för autism sågs ett mönster av förbättring överlag, men det beskrevs bara berättande. Eftersom studierna skilde sig mycket och data saknades kan den inte visa att det hjälper en enskild person.

title: The Relationship between Autism and Ehlers-Danlos Syndromes/Hypermobility Spectrum Disorders.
authors: Casanova EL, Baeza-Velasco C, Buchanan CB, Casanova MF
abstract: Considerable interest has arisen concerning the relationship between hereditary connective tissue disorders such as the Ehlers-Danlos syndromes (EDS)/hypermobility spectrum disorders (HSD) and autism, both in terms of their comorbidity as well as co-occurrence within the same families. This paper reviews our current state of knowledge, as well as highlighting unanswered questions concerning this remarkable patient group, which we hope will attract further scientific interest in coming years. In particular, patients themselves are demanding more research into this growing area of interest, although science has been slow to answer that call. Here, we address the overlap between these two spectrum conditions, including neurobehavioral, psychiatric, and neurological commonalities, shared peripheral neuropathies and neuropathologies, and similar autonomic and immune dysregulation. Together, these data highlight the potential relatedness of these two conditions and suggest that EDS/HSD may represent a subtype of autism.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o tú sois autistas y notáis articulaciones muy flexibles, dolor frecuente, mareos al levantarse, cansancio o piel frágil, vale la pena anotarlo y comentarlo con un profesional sanitario: a veces autismo y Ehlers-Danlos o trastornos del espectro de hipermovilidad aparecen juntos, también dentro de la misma familia. Escuchar estas señales corporales con calma puede ayudar a entender mejor el día a día. Se trata de una revisión narrativa que reúne estudios previos sobre síntomas neurológicos, autonómicos e inmunitarios compartidos. Sus límites: no aporta datos nuevos, muchas conclusiones son hipótesis y la idea de que sea un subtipo de autismo aún no está demostrada.
sheet.en: If you or your child are autistic and notice very flexible joints, frequent pain, dizziness when standing, fatigue or fragile skin, it is worth writing this down and raising it with a health professional: autism and Ehlers-Danlos syndromes or hypermobility spectrum disorders sometimes occur together, including within the same family. Calmly paying attention to these body signals may help make sense of daily life. This is a narrative review bringing together earlier studies on shared neurological, autonomic and immune features. Its limits: it offers no new data, many conclusions are hypotheses, and the idea that this is a subtype of autism has not yet been proven.
sheet.sv: Om du eller ditt barn är autistiska och märker mycket rörliga leder, ofta återkommande smärta, yrsel när man reser sig, trötthet eller skör hud kan det vara värt att anteckna och ta upp med vårdpersonal: autism och Ehlers-Danlos syndrom eller hypermobilitetsspektrumstörning förekommer ibland tillsammans, även inom samma familj. Att lugnt lyssna på kroppens signaler kan hjälpa till att förstå vardagen bättre. Detta är en narrativ översikt som samlar tidigare studier om gemensamma neurologiska, autonoma och immunologiska drag. Begränsningar: den ger inga nya data, många slutsatser är hypoteser och tanken att det skulle vara en undergrupp av autism är ännu inte bevisad.

title: Autism spectrum heterogeneity: fact or artifact?
authors: Mottron L, Bzdok D
abstract: The current diagnostic practices are linked to a 20-fold increase in the reported prevalence of ASD over the last 30 years. Fragmenting the autism phenotype into dimensional "autistic traits" results in the alleged recognition of autism-like symptoms in any psychiatric or neurodevelopemental condition and in individuals decreasingly distant from the typical population, and prematurely dismisses the relevance of a diagnostic threshold. Non-specific socio-communicative and repetitive DSM 5 criteria, combined with four quantitative specifiers as well as all their possible combinations, render limitless variety of presentations consistent with the categorical diagnosis of ASD. We propose several remedies to this problem: maintain a line of research on prototypical autism; limit the heterogeneity compatible with a categorical diagnosis to situations with a phenotypic overlap and a validated etiological link with prototypical autism; reintroduce the qualitative properties of autism presentations and of current dimensional specifiers, language, intelligence, comorbidity, and severity in the criteria used to diagnose autism in replacement of quantitative "social" and "repetitive" criteria; use these qualitative features combined with the clinical intuition of experts and machine-learning algorithms to differentiate coherent subgroups in today's autism spectrum; study these subgroups separately, and then compare them; and question the autistic nature of "autistic traits".

sheet.es: Lo práctico: esta revisión trata sobre cómo los investigadores definen el autismo, no sobre cómo apoyar a tu familiar. Si notas que estudios o consejos generales no encajan con la persona que conoces, puede deberse a que el espectro autista agrupa perfiles muy distintos. Observa a la persona concreta: qué le ayuda, qué la agota, cómo se comunica. Es una revisión teórica de investigadores que proponen estudiar subgrupos más definidos y cuestionan los criterios diagnósticos actuales; no participaron personas. Su límite: es una opinión experta debatida, no aporta datos nuevos y no cambia el diagnóstico ni el valor de la identidad autista de nadie.
sheet.en: The practical point: this review is about how researchers define autism, not about how to support your family member. If studies or general advice don't fit the person you know, it may be because the autism spectrum groups very different profiles together. Focus on the actual person: what helps them, what drains them, how they communicate. It is a theoretical review by researchers who argue for studying more defined subgroups and question current diagnostic criteria; no participants were involved. Its limit: it is a debated expert opinion, offers no new data, and does not change anyone's diagnosis or the worth of their autistic identity.
sheet.sv: Det praktiska: denna översikt handlar om hur forskare definierar autism, inte om hur du stöttar din närstående. Om studier eller allmänna råd inte passar den person du känner kan det bero på att autismspektrumet rymmer mycket olika profiler. Utgå från personen själv: vad som hjälper, vad som tar energi, hur hen kommunicerar. Det är en teoretisk översikt där forskare föreslår att man studerar tydligare avgränsade undergrupper och ifrågasätter dagens diagnoskriterier; inga deltagare ingick. Begränsning: det är en omdebatterad expertåsikt utan nya data, och den ändrar varken någons diagnos eller värdet av ens autistiska identitet.

title: Music therapy as social skill intervention for children with comorbid ASD and ID: study protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
authors: Yum YN, Lau WK, Poon K, Ho FC
abstract: Background Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a developmental impairment characterized by persistent deficits in social communication and interactions, and over half of children with ASD possess below average intellectual ability (IQ Method A randomized controlled trial (RCT) with two parallel groups of 40 children each (1:1 allocation ratio) is planned. Participants will receive 45 min of music therapy or non-musical intervention targeting social skills once a week for 12 weeks. Primary outcome measures will be independent ratings on the Childhood Autism Rating Scale and parent ratings on the Social Responsiveness Scale-2. Linear mixed-effects models for these two outcome measures will be created for data collected at 2-week pre-intervention, 2-week post-intervention, and 4-month post-intervention sessions. In-session behaviors at the first and last intervention will be videotaped and coded offline and compared. Pretreatment neural response of quantitative electroencephalograms (qEEG) to social scenes will be used to predict the outcomes of musical and non-musical social skill interventions, whereas qEEG responses to music will be used to predict the effectiveness of musical social skill intervention. Discussion If neural markers of social skill development are found, then the long-term goal is to develop individualized intervention based on pre-treatment markers to maximize treatment efficacy. The proposed study's results may also suggest directions to development and provision of music therapy services in Hong Kong. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov ( NCT04557488 ). Registered September 21, 2020.

sheet.es: Todavía no hay resultados que aplicar mañana. Si su hijo o hija autista con discapacidad intelectual disfruta de la música, puede usarla como un espacio compartido para practicar turnos y comunicación, sin presión. Este documento es el protocolo de un ensayo aleatorizado: planea comparar 2 grupos de 40 niños, con 45 minutos semanales de musicoterapia o de una intervención no musical durante 12 semanas. Como solo describe un plan, no sabemos si la musicoterapia funciona, ni para quién. Cualquier decisión sobre apoyos debe tomarse con el equipo profesional que conoce a su hijo o hija.
sheet.en: There are no results to act on tomorrow yet. If your autistic child with intellectual disability enjoys music, you can use it as a shared, low-pressure space to practise turn-taking and communication. This paper is the protocol of a randomized controlled trial: it plans to compare 2 groups of 40 children, with 45 minutes a week of music therapy or a non-musical intervention for 12 weeks. Because it only describes a plan, we do not know whether music therapy works, or for whom. Decisions about supports are best made with the professionals who know your child.
sheet.sv: Det finns inga resultat att använda i morgon ännu. Om ditt autistiska barn med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning gillar musik kan ni använda den som en gemensam, avslappnad plats för att öva turtagning och kommunikation. Artikeln är ett protokoll för en randomiserad kontrollerad studie: den planerar att jämföra 2 grupper med 40 barn vardera, med 45 minuter i veckan av musikterapi eller en icke-musikalisk insats under 12 veckor. Eftersom den bara beskriver en plan vet vi inte om musikterapi fungerar, eller för vem. Beslut om stöd bör fattas tillsammans med de yrkespersoner som känner ditt barn.

title: The effectiveness of parent training for children with autism spectrum disorder: a systematic review and meta-analyses.
authors: Deb SS, Retzer A, Roy M, Acharya R, Limbu B, Roy A
abstract: Background Various parent training interventions have been shown to have some effect on the symptoms of children with autism. We carried out a systematic review and meta-analyses to assess effectiveness of parental training for children with autism on their symptoms and parental stress. Methods Four electronic databases, CINAHL, EMBASE, MEDLINE and PsycINFO were searched until March 2020 for relevant literature. Two reviewers independently screened bibliographies using an eligibility checklist and extracted data using a structured proforma. We have also carried out meta-analyses when data were available for pooling. Results Seventeen papers from 15 studies were included for data analysis. Fifteen papers showed a positive treatment effect when compared with the control group, although not always significant. Meta-analysis based on pooled data from only two studies in each respective intervention, showed small to moderate treatment effects for three interventions, DIR/Floortime, Pivotal Response and Parent focused training respectively. Conclusions As in previous systematic reviews there was a mild to moderate treatment effects of three specific types of interventions respectively. However, it was difficult to draw any definitive conclusion about the effectiveness and generalisability of any intervention because of the wide variation in the interventions, control groups, outcome measures, small sample size, small number of studies in meta-analysis, overlap between the intervention and control procedures used in the included studies. There is an urgent need for experts in various international centres to jointly standardise a parent training intervention for children with autism and carry out a large scale RCT to assess its clinical and economic effectiveness. Research Registry Unique Identifying Number: reviewregistry915.

sheet.es: Si te planteas un programa de formación para madres y padres, puedes considerarlo como una opción más, sin esperar resultados iguales para todas las familias. Conviene preguntar qué se trabaja, cómo y si encaja con tu hijo o hija autista y con vuestra rutina. La evidencia es un metaanálisis de 17 artículos de 15 estudios sobre formación parental; 15 artículos mostraron un efecto positivo frente al grupo control, aunque no siempre significativo. Sus límites: los programas, grupos control y medidas variaban mucho, las muestras eran pequeñas y no permite sacar conclusiones firmes sobre ningún programa concreto.
sheet.en: If you are considering a parent training programme, you can see it as one option, without expecting the same results for every family. It helps to ask what is taught, how, and whether it fits your autistic child and your daily routine. The evidence is a meta-analysis of 17 papers from 15 studies on parent training; 15 papers showed a positive effect compared with the control group, though not always significant. Its limits: programmes, control groups and measures varied widely, samples were small, and no firm conclusions can be drawn about any specific programme.
sheet.sv: Om du funderar på en föräldrautbildning kan du se den som ett alternativ bland flera, utan att förvänta dig samma resultat för alla familjer. Det hjälper att fråga vad som tränas, hur, och om det passar ditt autistiska barn och er vardag. Underlaget är en metaanalys av 17 artiklar från 15 studier om föräldrautbildning; 15 artiklar visade en positiv effekt jämfört med kontrollgruppen, men inte alltid signifikant. Begränsningar: programmen, kontrollgrupperna och måtten varierade mycket, urvalen var små, och inga säkra slutsatser kan dras om något enskilt program.

title: Social Cognition, Social Skill, and Social Motivation Minimally Predict Social Interaction Outcomes for Autistic and Non-Autistic Adults.
authors: Morrison KE, DeBrabander KM, Jones DR, Ackerman RA, Sasson NJ
abstract: Social cognition, social skill, and social motivation have been extensively researched and characterized as atypical in autistic people, with the assumption that each mechanistically contributes to the broader social interaction difficulties that diagnostically define the condition. Despite this assumption, research has not directly assessed whether or how these three social domains contribute to actual real-world social interaction outcomes for autistic people. The current study administered standardized measures of social cognition, social skill, and social motivation to 67 autistic and 58 non-autistic (NA) adults and assessed whether performance on these measures, both individually and relationally between dyadic partners, predicted outcomes for autistic and NA adults interacting with unfamiliar autistic and NA partners in a 5 minute unstructured "get to know you" conversation. Consistent with previous research, autistic adults scored lower than NA adults on the three social domains and were evaluated less favorably by their conversation partners. However, links between autistic adults' performance on the three social domains and their social interaction outcomes were minimal and, contrary to prediction, only the social abilities of NA adults predicted some interaction outcomes within mixed diagnostic dyads. Collectively, results suggest that reduced performance by autistic adults on standardized measures of social cognition, social skill, and social motivation do not correspond in clear and predictable ways with their real-world social interaction outcomes. They also highlight the need for the development and validation of more ecological assessments of autistic social abilities and the consideration of relational dynamics, not just individual characteristics, when assessing social disability in autism.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista puntúa distinto en pruebas sociales, eso no basta para prever cómo le irá en una conversación real. Mañana, fíjese en el contexto y en la relación entre las personas, no solo en la persona autista. Es un estudio con 67 adultos autistas y 58 adultos no autistas, que mantuvieron una conversación de 5 minutos para conocerse con personas desconocidas. Los vínculos entre las pruebas y los resultados fueron mínimos. Limitaciones: fue una conversación breve entre desconocidos, en adultos, y no refleja todas las situaciones ni a todas las personas.
sheet.en: How an autistic person scores on social tests does not clearly predict how a real conversation will go. Tomorrow, look at the context and the relationship between the people talking, not only at the autistic person. This study involved 67 autistic adults and 58 non-autistic adults, who had a 5 minute "get to know you" conversation with people they did not know. Links between test scores and conversation outcomes were minimal. Limits: it was a short chat between strangers, with adults, so it does not reflect every situation or every person.
sheet.sv: Hur en autistisk person presterar på sociala tester förutsäger inte tydligt hur ett verkligt samtal går. I morgon: titta på sammanhanget och relationen mellan de som pratar, inte bara på den autistiska personen. Studien omfattade 67 autistiska vuxna och 58 icke-autistiska vuxna, som hade ett 5 minuter långt "lär känna"-samtal med personer de inte kände. Sambanden mellan testresultat och samtalsutfall var minimala. Begränsningar: det var ett kort samtal mellan främlingar, med vuxna, och det speglar inte alla situationer eller alla personer.

title: Natural Antioxidants: A Novel Therapeutic Approach to Autism Spectrum Disorders?
authors: Pangrazzi L, Balasco L, Bozzi Y
abstract: Autism spectrum disorders (ASD) are a group of neurodevelopmental syndromes with both genetic and environmental origins. Several recent studies have shown that inflammation and oxidative stress may play a key role in supporting the pathogenesis and the severity of ASD. Thus, the administration of anti-inflammatory and antioxidant molecules may represent a promising strategy to counteract pathological behaviors in ASD patients. In the current review, results from recent literature showing how natural antioxidants may be beneficial in the context of ASD will be discussed. Interestingly, many antioxidant molecules available in nature show anti-inflammatory activity. Thus, after introducing ASD and the role of the vitamin E/vitamin C/glutathione network in scavenging intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) and the impairments observed with ASD, we discuss the concept of functional food and nutraceutical compounds. Furthermore, the effects of well-known nutraceutical compounds on ASD individuals and animal models of ASD are summarized. Finally, the importance of nutraceutical compounds as support therapy useful in reducing the symptoms in autistic people is discussed.

sheet.es: Si te preguntas si los antioxidantes naturales o los alimentos funcionales ayudarían a una persona autista, esta revisión no basta para decidirlo. Lo práctico: puedes hablar de la alimentación y los suplementos con su profesional sanitario antes de cambiar nada. La evidencia es una revisión de literatura reciente que resume efectos de compuestos nutracéuticos en personas autistas y en modelos animales. Sus límites: no aporta una recomendación para cada persona, parte de la idea de que la inflamación y el estrés oxidativo podrían influir, y los estudios en animales no equivalen a la vida de una persona. Las decisiones médicas corresponden a un clínico.
sheet.en: If you wonder whether natural antioxidants or functional foods might help an autistic person, this review is not enough to decide. Practically: you can talk through food and supplements with their healthcare professional before changing anything. The evidence is a review of recent literature summarising the effects of nutraceutical compounds in autistic people and in animal models. Its limits: it gives no recommendation that fits every person, it rests on the idea that inflammation and oxidative stress may play a role, and animal studies are not the same as a person's real life. Medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om du undrar om naturliga antioxidanter eller funktionella livsmedel kan hjälpa en autistisk person räcker den här översikten inte för att avgöra det. Praktiskt: du kan prata om kost och kosttillskott med personens vårdpersonal innan du ändrar något. Underlaget är en översikt av nyare litteratur som sammanfattar effekter av nutraceutiska ämnen hos autistiska personer och i djurmodeller. Begränsningar: den ger ingen rekommendation som passar alla, bygger på tanken att inflammation och oxidativ stress kan spela roll, och djurstudier motsvarar inte en människas vardag. Medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker.

title: Early Intervention with Parents of Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders: A Review of Programs.
authors: Rojas-Torres LP, Alonso-Esteban Y, Alcantud-Marín F
abstract: The aim of this article was to analyze the evidence regarding the effectiveness of intervention programs for children with autism based on the participation of their parents. To obtain the data, a systematic search was carried out in four databases (PsycARTICLES (ProQuest), ERIC (ProQuest), PubMed (ProQuest), and Scopus). The retrieved documents were refined under the inclusion/exclusion criteria, and a total of 51 empirical studies were selected. These studies were first classified according to the function of the intervention objective and, later, by the methodology applied (19 studies were based on comprehensive interventions, 11 focused on the nuclear symptoms of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), 12 focused on the promotion of positive parenting, and nine interactions focused on child play). Once all of the documents had been analyzed, the evidence indicated scientific efficacy in most studies, mainly in those based on child development and the application of behavioral analysis principles. Moreover, the positive influence of parent participation in such programs was demonstrated.

sheet.es: Si le ofrecen un programa de intervención temprana, pregunte si incluye a las familias y si se adapta a los intereses y ritmos de su hijo o hija autista. Se trata de una revisión sistemática que analizó 51 estudios empíricos de programas con participación de madres y padres. En la mayoría hallaron eficacia, sobre todo en programas basados en el desarrollo infantil y en principios de análisis conductual, y la participación de las familias resultó positiva. Límites: la revisión reúne programas muy distintos y no dice cuál sirve a cada persona, ni cómo vive cada niña o niño estos programas. Úsela como guía para conversar con profesionales, no como regla.
sheet.en: If you are offered an early intervention program, ask whether it involves families and whether it fits your autistic child's interests and pace. This is a systematic review that analyzed 51 empirical studies of programs with parent participation. Most showed effectiveness, mainly programs based on child development and behavioral analysis principles, and parent participation was found to be positive. Limits: the review combines very different programs and does not say which one suits each person, or how each child experiences them. Use it as a guide for conversations with professionals, not as a rule.
sheet.sv: Om ni erbjuds ett program för tidiga insatser, fråga om det involverar föräldrar och om det anpassas efter ert autistiska barns intressen och tempo. Detta är en systematisk översikt som analyserade 51 empiriska studier av program där föräldrar deltog. De flesta visade effekt, främst program baserade på barns utveckling och principer från beteendeanalys, och föräldrarnas deltagande visade sig vara positivt. Begränsningar: översikten slår ihop mycket olika program och säger inte vilket som passar varje person, eller hur varje barn upplever dem. Använd den som stöd i samtal med yrkespersoner, inte som regel.

title: Listening to the autistic voice: Mental health priorities to guide research and practice in autism from a stakeholder-driven project.
authors: Benevides TW, Shore SM, Palmer K, Duncan P, Plank A, Andresen ML, Caplan R, Cook B, Gassner D, Hector BL, Morgan L, Nebeker L, Purkis Y, Rankowski B, Wittig K, Coughlin SS
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic adults commonly experience mental health conditions. However, research rarely involves autistic adults in deciding priorities for research on mental healthcare approaches that might work for them. The purpose of this article is to describe a stakeholder-driven project that involved autistic adults in co-leading and designing research about priorities to address mental health needs. Through a large online survey, two large meetings, and three face-to-face focus group discussions involving over 350 stakeholders, we identified five priorities for mental health research desired by autistic adults. These priorities and preferred outcomes should be used to guide research and practice for autistic adults.

sheet.es: Si apoyas a una persona autista adulta, pregúntale qué necesita para cuidar su salud mental y qué resultados le importan, en lugar de suponerlo. Este estudio, hecho con personas autistas, usó una encuesta en línea, dos reuniones grandes y tres grupos de discusión presenciales con más de 350 participantes, y señaló cinco prioridades de investigación sobre salud mental. El resumen no detalla cuáles son, ni indica si reflejan a todas las personas autistas. Úsalo como invitación a conversar, no como regla.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult, ask them what they need for their mental health and which outcomes matter to them, rather than assuming. This study, done together with autistic people, used an online survey, two large meetings and three face-to-face focus groups involving over 350 stakeholders, and identified five priorities for mental health research. The abstract does not list them, nor does it show that they reflect every autistic person. Use it as a prompt for conversation, not as a rule.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen, fråga vad hen behöver för sin psykiska hälsa och vilka resultat som är viktiga för hen, i stället för att anta det. Studien gjordes tillsammans med autistiska personer och använde en webbenkät, två stora möten och tre fokusgrupper på plats med över 350 intressenter. Den identifierade fem prioriteringar för forskning om psykisk hälsa. Sammanfattningen anger inte vilka de är, eller om de gäller alla autistiska personer. Använd den som underlag för samtal, inte som regel.

title: Interventions to address health outcomes among autistic adults: A systematic review.
authors: Benevides TW, Shore SM, Andresen ML, Caplan R, Cook B, Gassner DL, Erves JM, Hazlewood TM, King MC, Morgan L, Murphy LE, Purkis Y, Rankowski B, Rutledge SM, Welch SP, Wittig K
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic adults have more health problems then their same-aged peers. Yet little research has been conducted that focuses on addressing these health problems. In order to guide future research, it is important to know what intervention studies have been done to improve health outcomes among autistic adults. The project team and student assistants read studies that were published between 2007 and 2018 in the online research database, PubMed. We looked for studies published in English, which were peer-reviewed and included (1) an intervention, (2) an outcome that was related to health, and (3) a study group that included autistic adults. We did not include studies that had outcomes about employment (unless there was a health outcome), studies about caregivers or caregiving, or expert opinions about interventions. Of 778 reviewed articles, 19 studies met all of the criteria above. Within these studies, two approaches were found to have emerging evidence for their use in autistic adults: cognitive behavioral interventions and mindfulness-based approaches for improved mental health outcomes. The remaining intervention approaches did not have enough articles to support their use. Many of the outcomes were about reduced symptoms of co-occurring mental health diagnoses (e.g. reduced anxiety, depression). Most of the participants in these studies were male and did not have intellectual disability. Most study participants were adults younger than 40. There are not many intervention studies that address health outcomes among autistic adults. More research is needed on interventions which are desired by the adult autism community and address preferred health outcomes such as increased quality of life or well-being.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta busca apoyo para su salud mental, conviene saber que las terapias cognitivo-conductuales y los enfoques basados en mindfulness son las opciones con más indicios iniciales. Aun así, que existan indicios no significa que sirvan a todas las personas: lo mejor es hablar con un profesional de confianza y preguntar a la propia persona qué desea. Es una revisión sistemática de estudios publicados entre 2007 y 2018: de 778 artículos revisados, 19 cumplían los criterios. Tiene límites: la mayoría de participantes eran hombres, sin discapacidad intelectual y menores de 40 años, y hay pocos estudios sobre bienestar o calidad de vida.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult is looking for support with mental health, it helps to know that cognitive behavioral approaches and mindfulness-based approaches have the most emerging evidence. Emerging evidence does not mean they suit everyone, so talk with a professional you trust and ask the person what they want. This is a systematic review of studies published between 2007 and 2018: of 778 articles reviewed, 19 met the criteria. It has limits: most participants were male, did not have intellectual disability and were younger than 40, and few studies looked at well-being or quality of life.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen söker stöd för sin psykiska hälsa kan det vara bra att veta att kognitiva beteendeterapeutiska och mindfulnessbaserade metoder har mest tidiga belägg. Tidiga belägg betyder inte att de passar alla, så prata med en professionell du litar på och fråga personen själv vad hen vill ha. Det är en systematisk översikt av studier publicerade mellan 2007 och 2018: av 778 granskade artiklar uppfyllde 19 kriterierna. Den har begränsningar: de flesta deltagarna var män, hade ingen intellektuell funktionsnedsättning och var yngre än 40, och få studier handlade om välbefinnande eller livskvalitet.

title: Oxidative stress marker aberrations in children with autism spectrum disorder: a systematic review and meta-analysis of 87 studies (N = 9109).
authors: Chen L, Shi XJ, Liu H, Mao X, Gui LN, Wang H, Cheng Y
abstract: There is increasing awareness that oxidative stress may be implicated in the pathophysiology of autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Here we aimed to investigate blood oxidative stress marker profile in ASD children by a meta-analysis. Two independent investigators systematically searched Web of Science, PubMed, and Cochrane Library and extracted data from 87 studies with 4928 ASD children and 4181 healthy control (HC) children. The meta-analysis showed that blood concentrations of oxidative glutathione (GSSG), malondialdehyde, homocysteine, S-adenosylhomocysteine, nitric oxide, and copper were higher in children with ASD than that of HC children. In contrast, blood reduced glutathione (GSH), total glutathione (tGSH), GSH/GSSG, tGSH/GSSG, methionine, cysteine, vitamin B9, vitamin D, vitamin B12, vitamin E, S-adenosylmethionine/S-adenosylhomocysteine, and calcium concentrations were significantly reduced in children with ASD relative to HC children. However, there were no significance differences between ASD children and HC children for the other 17 potential markers. Heterogeneities among studies were found for most markers, and meta-regressions indicated that age and publication year may influence the meta-analysis results. These results therefore clarified blood oxidative stress profile in children with ASD, strengthening clinical evidence of increased oxidative stress implicating in pathogenesis of ASD. Additionally, given the consistent and large effective size, glutathione metabolism biomarkers have the potential to inform early diagnosis of ASD.

sheet.es: Este estudio no cambia lo que haces mañana por la mañana: no indica que debas hacer pruebas de sangre ni cambiar la dieta o suplementos. Si te preocupa la salud de tu hijo, coméntalo con su pediatra, que es quien toma las decisiones médicas. Es un metaanálisis de 87 estudios con 4928 niños autistas y 4181 niños sin autismo, que comparó marcadores en sangre y halló diferencias promedio en varios. Sus límites: los estudios eran muy dispares, la edad y el año de publicación influyeron en los resultados, y las diferencias de grupo no describen a cada persona ni muestran causas.
sheet.en: This study doesn't change what you do tomorrow morning: it gives no reason to seek blood tests or change diet or supplements. If you have health worries about your child, raise them with their paediatrician, who makes medical decisions. It is a meta-analysis of 87 studies with 4928 autistic children and 4181 non-autistic children, comparing blood markers and finding average group differences in several. Its limits: the studies varied a lot, age and publication year influenced results, and group averages don't describe any one person or show causes.
sheet.sv: Den här studien förändrar inte vad du gör i morgon bitti: den ger ingen anledning att be om blodprover eller ändra kost eller kosttillskott. Om du oroar dig för ditt barns hälsa, ta upp det med barnläkaren, som fattar medicinska beslut. Det är en metaanalys av 87 studier med 4928 autistiska barn och 4181 barn utan autism, som jämförde blodmarkörer och fann genomsnittliga skillnader i flera. Begränsningar: studierna skilde sig mycket åt, ålder och publiceringsår påverkade resultaten, och gruppgenomsnitt beskriver inte en enskild person eller visar orsaker.

title: Oral Health and Autism Spectrum Disorders: A Unique Collaboration between Dentistry and Occupational Therapy.
authors: Como DH, Stein Duker LI, Polido JC, Cermak SA
journal: International journal of environmental research and public health
abstract: Children with autism spectrum disorders (ASD) are at risk for oral health disparities. With the dramatic rise in ASD prevalence to 1 in 54 children, it is likely that an increasing number of dental practitioners will encounter or be asked to treat children with ASD. This paper reviews explanations related to the increasing prevalence of ASD, provides reasons why children with ASD are at increased risk for poor oral health, and discusses unique interprofessional collaborations between dental practitioners and occupational therapists. Occupational therapists and dentists can work together to plan modifications to the dental environment or adapt dental protocols to reduce some of the barriers encountered by those with ASD, provide desensitization strategies before the clinic visit, or help a child with emotional regulation during clinical treatments.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija autista tiene una cita con el dentista, pregunte si pueden adaptar el entorno o el protocolo y si un terapeuta ocupacional puede ayudar a preparar la visita con estrategias de desensibilización y apoyo para la regulación emocional. La evidencia es una revisión que analiza por qué los niños con TEA tienen más riesgo de mala salud bucodental y cómo pueden colaborar dentistas y terapeutas ocupacionales. Como revisión, no prueba qué adaptación funciona mejor, y cada persona necesita apoyos distintos.
sheet.en: If your autistic child has a dental appointment, ask whether the setting or the usual routine can be adapted, and whether an occupational therapist can help prepare the visit with desensitization strategies and support with emotional regulation. The evidence is a review looking at why children with ASD are at higher risk of poor oral health and how dentists and occupational therapists can work together. As a review, it does not show which adaptation works best, and every person needs different supports.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn har en tandläkartid, fråga om miljön eller rutinerna kan anpassas och om en arbetsterapeut kan hjälpa till att förbereda besöket med desensibilisering och stöd för känsloreglering. Underlaget är en översikt som tar upp varför barn med ASD har högre risk för sämre munhälsa och hur tandläkare och arbetsterapeuter kan samarbeta. Som översikt visar den inte vilken anpassning som fungerar bäst, och alla behöver olika stöd.

title: Treatment of Aggression in Adults with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Review.
authors: Im DS
abstract: Background Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by markedly impaired social interaction, impaired communication, and restricted/repetitive patterns of behavior, interests, and activities. In addition to challenges caused by core symptoms, maladaptive behaviors such as aggression can be associated with ASD and can further disrupt functioning and quality of life. For adults with ASD, these behaviors can portend adverse outcomes (e.g., harm to others or to the individual with ASD, hindering of employment opportunities, criminal justice system involvement). This article reviews the scientific literature to provide an update on evidence-based interventions for aggression in adults with ASD. Method A search of the electronic databases CINAHL, EMBASE, and PsycINFO was conducted using relevant search terms. After reviewing titles, abstracts, full-length articles, and reference lists, 70 articles were identified and reviewed. Results The strongest (controlled trial) evidence suggests beneficial effects of risperidone, propranolol, fluvoxamine, vigorous aerobic exercise, and dextromethorphan/quinidine for treating aggression in adults with ASD, with lower levels of evidence supporting behavioral interventions, multisensory environments, yokukansan, and other treatments. Conclusions Additional randomized, controlled trials using consistent methodology that adequately addresses sources of bias are needed to determine which treatments are reliably effective in addressing aggression in adults with ASD. In the meantime, considering efficacy and adverse effect/long-term risk profiles, a practical approach could start with functional assessment-informed behavioral interventions along with encouragement of regular, vigorous aerobic exercise to target aggression in adults with ASD, with pharmacotherapy employed if these interventions are unavailable or inadequate based on symptom acuity.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta tiene episodios de agresión, un primer paso razonable es entender qué los provoca (por ejemplo, con una evaluación funcional) y apoyarse en intervenciones conductuales, además de animarla a hacer ejercicio aeróbico intenso con regularidad, si le apetece. Es una revisión de la literatura que analizó 70 artículos sobre adultos autistas. Sus límites: faltan ensayos controlados aleatorizados consistentes, así que no se sabe con certeza qué funciona. Algunos estudios fueron médicos; las decisiones sobre medicación corresponden a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult has episodes of aggression, a reasonable first step is to understand what triggers them (for example, through a functional assessment) and use behavioral supports, along with encouraging regular, vigorous aerobic exercise if the person is willing. This is a review of the literature that looked at 70 articles on autistic adults. Its limits: more consistent randomized controlled trials are needed, so it is not certain what reliably works. Some studies were medical; decisions about medication belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen har aggressiva episoder är ett rimligt första steg att förstå vad som utlöser dem (till exempel genom en funktionell bedömning) och använda beteendeinriktat stöd, samt uppmuntra regelbunden, intensiv konditionsträning om personen vill. Det är en litteraturöversikt som granskade 70 artiklar om autistiska vuxna. Begränsningar: det behövs fler enhetliga randomiserade kontrollerade studier, så det är osäkert vad som pålitligt fungerar. Vissa studier var medicinska; beslut om läkemedel hör till en kliniker.

title: Autism Spectrum Disorders: Multiple Routes to, and Multiple Consequences of, Abnormal Synaptic Function and Connectivity.
authors: Carroll L, Braeutigam S, Dawes JM, Krsnik Z, Kostovic I, Coutinho E, Dewing JM, Horton CA, Gomez-Nicola D, Menassa DA
journal: The Neuroscientist : a review journal bringing neurobiology, neurology and psychiatry
abstract: Autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) are a heterogeneous group of neurodevelopmental disorders of genetic and environmental etiologies. Some ASD cases are syndromic: associated with clinically defined patterns of somatic abnormalities and a neurobehavioral phenotype (e.g., Fragile X syndrome). Many cases, however, are idiopathic or non-syndromic. Such disorders present themselves during the early postnatal period when language, speech, and personality start to develop. ASDs manifest by deficits in social communication and interaction, restricted and repetitive patterns of behavior across multiple contexts, sensory abnormalities across multiple modalities and comorbidities, such as epilepsy among many others. ASDs are disorders of connectivity, as synaptic dysfunction is common to both syndromic and idiopathic forms. While multiple theories have been proposed, particularly in idiopathic ASDs, none address why certain brain areas (e.g., frontotemporal) appear more vulnerable than others or identify factors that may affect phenotypic specificity. In this hypothesis article, we identify possible routes leading to, and the consequences of, altered connectivity and review the evidence of central and peripheral synaptic dysfunction in ASDs. We postulate that phenotypic specificity could arise from aberrant experience-dependent plasticity mechanisms in frontal brain areas and peripheral sensory networks and propose why the vulnerability of these areas could be part of a model to unify preexisting pathophysiological theories.

sheet.es: Qué hacer mañana: no hay un cambio concreto que este texto pida. Puede servir para recordar que cada persona autista es distinta y que sus sentidos y su forma de comunicarse merecen atención y respeto. Evidencia: es una revisión que plantea una hipótesis sobre cómo las conexiones entre neuronas (sinapsis) podrían intervenir en el autismo; no describe a un grupo de participantes.
