El resumen solo señala que esto afecta a la evaluación y al apoyo, y pide más investigación.
sheet.en: If a child doesn't speak in certain places, such as school, it helps not to pressure them to talk, and to consider both social anxiety and autism. It is worth raising this with a professional who knows both. This is a review that pulls together studies on selective mutism, social anxiety and autism, and argues that autism is sometimes involved too. It is the authors' argument, not a rule: it does not say how often this happens, and every person is different. The abstract only says this matters for assessment and support, and calls for more research.
sheet.sv: Om ett barn inte pratar på vissa platser, till exempel i skolan, hjälper det att inte pressa barnet att tala och att tänka på både social ångest och autism. Ta gärna upp det med en yrkesperson som känner till båda. Det här är en översikt som sammanfattar studier om selektiv mutism, social ångest och autism och menar att autism ibland också spelar in. Det är författarnas resonemang, inte en regel: den anger inte hur ofta det gäller, och alla är olika. Sammanfattningen säger bara att detta påverkar bedömning och stöd, och efterlyser mer forskning.

title: Racial and ethnic disparities in benefits eligibility and spending among adults on the autism spectrum: A cohort study using the Medicare Medicaid Linked Enrollees Analytic Data Source.
authors: Benevides TW, Carretta HJ, Rust G, Shea L
abstract: Background Research on children and youth on the autism spectrum reveal racial and ethnic disparities in access to healthcare and utilization, but there is less research to understand how disparities persist as autistic adults age. We need to understand racial-ethnic inequities in obtaining eligibility for Medicare and/or Medicaid coverage, as well as inequities in spending for autistic enrollees under these public programs. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional cohort study of U.S. publicly-insured adults on the autism spectrum using 2012 Medicare-Medicaid Linked Enrollee Analytic Data Source (n = 172,071). We evaluated differences in race-ethnicity by eligibility (Medicare-only, Medicaid-only, Dual-Eligible) and spending. Findings The majority of white adults (49.87%) were full-dual eligible for both Medicare and Medicaid. In contrast, only 37.53% of Black, 34.65% Asian/Pacific Islander, and 35.94% of Hispanic beneficiaries were full-dual eligible for Medicare and Medicare, with most only eligible for state-funded Medicaid. Adjusted logistic models controlling for gender, intellectual disability status, costly chronic condition, rural status, county median income, and geographic region of residence revealed that Black beneficiaries were significantly less likely than white beneficiaries to be dual-eligible across all ages. Across these three beneficiary types, total spending exceeded $10 billion. Annual total expenditures median expenditures for full-dual and Medicaid-only eligible beneficiaries were higher among white beneficiaries as compared with Black beneficiaries. Conclusions Public health insurance in the U.S. including Medicare and Medicaid aim to reduce inequities in access to healthcare that might exist due to disability, income, or old age. In contrast to these ideals, our study reveals that racial-ethnic minority autistic adults who were eligible for public insurance across all U.S. states in 2012 experience disparities in eligibility for specific programs and spending. We call for further evaluation of system supports that promote clear pathways to disability and public health insurance among those with lifelong developmental disabilities.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a un adulto autista en EE. UU., conviene revisar con un trabajador social o un asesor de beneficios a qué programas públicos (Medicare, Medicaid o ambos) puede acceder, sin dar por hecho que ya recibe todo lo que le corresponde. Este estudio de cohorte transversal analizó datos de 2012 de 172,071 adultos autistas con seguro público. El 49.87% de los adultos blancos tenía ambas coberturas, frente al 37.53% de los negros, el 34.65% de los asiáticos/isleños del Pacífico y el 35.94% de los hispanos. Sus límites: son datos de 2012, solo de EE. UU., y no muestran las causas ni lo que vive cada persona.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult in the U.S., it is worth checking with a social worker or benefits adviser which public programs (Medicare, Medicaid or both) they can access, rather than assuming they already receive everything they are eligible for. This cross-sectional cohort study used 2012 data on 172,071 publicly insured autistic adults. Of white adults, 49.87% had both coverages, compared with 37.53% of Black, 34.65% of Asian/Pacific Islander and 35.94% of Hispanic adults. Limits: the data are from 2012, cover only the U.S., and cannot show the causes or what any one person experiences.
sheet.sv: Om du stödjer en autistisk vuxen i USA är det värt att fråga en socialarbetare eller bidragsrådgivare vilka offentliga program (Medicare, Medicaid eller båda) personen kan få, i stället för att anta att hen redan får allt hen har rätt till. Studien var en tvärsnittsstudie av kohort med data från 2012 om 172,071 offentligt försäkrade autistiska vuxna. Bland vita vuxna hade 49.87% båda försäkringarna, jämfört med 37.53% av svarta, 34.65% av asiatiska/Stillahavsöbor och 35.94% av latinamerikanska vuxna. Begränsningar: datan är från 2012, gäller bara USA och visar varken orsaker eller vad den enskilda personen upplever.

title: Wearable-Sensors-Based Platform for Gesture Recognition of Autism Spectrum Disorder Children Using Machine Learning Algorithms.
authors: Siddiqui UA, Ullah F, Iqbal A, Khan A, Ullah R, Paracha S, Shahzad H, Kwak KS
abstract: Autistic people face many challenges in various aspects of daily life such as social skills, repetitive behaviors, speech, and verbal communication. They feel hesitant to talk with others. The signs of autism vary from one individual to another, with a range from mild to severe. Autistic children use fewer communicative gestures compared with typically developing children (TD). With time, the parents may learn their gestures and understand what is occurring in their child's mind. However, it is difficult for other people to understand their gestures. In this paper, we propose a wearable-sensors-based platform to recognize autistic gestures using various classification techniques. The proposed system defines, monitors, and classifies the gestures of the individuals. We propose using wearable sensors that transmit their data using a Bluetooth interface to a data acquisition and classification server. A dataset of 24 gestures is created by 10 autistic children performing each gesture about 10 times. Time- and frequency-domain features are extracted from the sensors' data, which are classified using k-nearest neighbor (KNN), decision tree, neural network, and random forest models. The main objective of this work is to develop a wearable-sensor-based IoT platform for gesture recognition in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). We achieve an accuracy of about 91% with most of the classifiers using dataset cross-validation and leave-one-person-out cross-validation.

sheet.es: Mañana por la mañana, lo más útil es seguir atendiendo a los gestos de la niña o el niño autista como una forma real de comunicarse, y compartir con otras personas lo que usted ya ha aprendido sobre ellos. Este estudio probó un sistema con sensores que se llevan puestos para reconocer gestos. Participaron 10 niños autistas, que hicieron 24 gestos, cada uno unas 10 veces. La precisión fue de alrededor del 91% con la mayoría de los clasificadores. Es un grupo pequeño, con gestos preparados y no de la vida diaria, y no sustituye el conocimiento de quienes conocen bien a cada niño.
sheet.en: Tomorrow morning, the most useful step is to keep treating an autistic child's gestures as real communication, and to share with others what you have already learned about them. This study tested a wearable-sensor system that recognises gestures. Ten autistic children took part, performing 24 gestures, each about 10 times. Accuracy was about 91% with most of the classifiers. The group was small, the gestures were set tasks rather than everyday life, and a system cannot replace the knowledge of people who know each child well.
sheet.sv: I morgon bitti är det mest användbara att fortsätta se autistiska barns gester som verklig kommunikation och att dela med andra det du redan har lärt dig om dem. Studien testade ett system med bärbara sensorer som känner igen gester. Tio autistiska barn deltog och gjorde 24 gester, var och en ungefär 10 gånger. Träffsäkerheten var cirka 91% med de flesta klassificerarna. Gruppen var liten, gesterna var förberedda uppgifter och inte vardagen, och ett system kan inte ersätta kunskapen hos dem som känner varje barn väl.

title: Relationship between Autism Spectrum Disorder and Pesticides: A Systematic Review of Human and Preclinical Models.
authors: Biosca-Brull J, Pérez-Fernández C, Mora S, Carrillo B, Pinos H, Conejo NM, Collado P, Arias JL, Martín-Sánchez F, Sánchez-Santed F, Colomina MT
journal: International journal of environmental research and public health
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a complex set of neurodevelopmental pathologies characterized by impoverished social and communicative abilities and stereotyped behaviors. Although its genetic basis is unquestionable, the involvement of environmental factors such as exposure to pesticides has also been proposed. Despite the systematic analyses of this relationship in humans, there are no specific reviews including both human and preclinical models. The present systematic review summarizes, analyzes, and discusses recent advances in preclinical and epidemiological studies. We included 45 human and 16 preclinical studies. These studies focused on Organophosphates (OP), Organochlorine (OC), Pyrethroid (PT), Neonicotinoid (NN), Carbamate (CM), and mixed exposures. Preclinical studies, where the OP Chlorpyrifos (CPF) compound is the one most studied, pointed to an association between gestational exposure and increased ASD-like behaviors, although the data are inconclusive with regard to other ages or pesticides. Studies in humans focused on prenatal exposure to OP and OC agents, and report cognitive and behavioral alterations related to ASD symptomatology. The results of both suggest that gestational exposure to certain OP agents could be linked to the clinical signs of ASD. Future experimental studies should focus on extending the analysis of ASD-like behaviors in preclinical models and include exposure patterns similar to those observed in human studies.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista, este estudio no es motivo de culpa: el autismo tiene una base genética fuerte y nadie puede saber qué causó el autismo de un niño concreto. La revisión sugiere que la exposición durante el embarazo a algunos pesticidas organofosforados, como el clorpirifós, podría estar asociada a rasgos autistas; en la vida diaria, lavar frutas y verduras y evitar el uso de pesticidas en casa son medidas sensatas para toda la familia. Es una revisión sistemática de 45 estudios en humanos y 16 en animales. Sus límites: muestra asociaciones, no causas, los datos sobre otros pesticidas y edades no son concluyentes, y los estudios con animales no se trasladan directamente a las personas.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic person, this study is not a reason for guilt: autism has a strong genetic basis, and no one can know what led to any individual child being autistic. The review suggests that exposure during pregnancy to some organophosphate pesticides, such as chlorpyrifos, may be associated with autistic traits; day to day, washing fruit and vegetables and avoiding pesticide use at home are sensible steps for the whole family. It is a systematic review of 45 human and 16 animal studies. Its limits: it shows associations, not causes, data on other pesticides and ages are inconclusive, and animal findings do not translate directly to people.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person är den här studien ingen anledning till skuld: autism har en stark genetisk grund, och ingen kan veta vad som ledde till att ett enskilt barn är autistiskt. Översikten tyder på att exponering under graviditeten för vissa organofosfatbekämpningsmedel, som klorpyrifos, kan ha ett samband med autistiska drag; i vardagen är det klokt för hela familjen att skölja frukt och grönsaker och undvika bekämpningsmedel hemma. Det är en systematisk översikt av 45 studier på människor och 16 på djur. Begränsningar: den visar samband, inte orsaker, data om andra medel och åldrar är osäkra, och djurfynd går inte direkt att överföra till människor.

title: Differences Between Autistic and Non-Autistic Adults in the Recognition of Anger from Facial Motion Remain after Controlling for Alexithymia.
authors: Keating CT, Fraser DS, Sowden S, Cook JL
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: To date, studies have not established whether autistic and non-autistic individuals differ in emotion recognition from facial motion cues when matched in terms of alexithymia. Here, autistic and non-autistic adults (N = 60) matched on age, gender, non-verbal reasoning ability and alexithymia, completed an emotion recognition task, which employed dynamic point light displays of emotional facial expressions manipulated in terms of speed and spatial exaggeration. Autistic participants exhibited significantly lower accuracy for angry, but not happy or sad, facial motion with unmanipulated speed and spatial exaggeration. Autistic, and not alexithymic, traits were predictive of accuracy for angry facial motion with unmanipulated speed and spatial exaggeration. Alexithymic traits, in contrast, were predictive of the magnitude of both correct and incorrect emotion ratings.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista no reconoce que alguien está enfadado, quizá ayude decirlo con palabras en lugar de esperar que lo deduzca por la cara. Puede ser tan simple como "estoy molesto" o "estoy tranquilo". Evidencia: un estudio con 60 personas adultas, autistas y no autistas, emparejadas por edad, género, razonamiento no verbal y alexitimia. Veían expresiones faciales en movimiento, mostradas como puntos de luz. Las personas autistas acertaron menos con el enfado, pero no con la alegría ni la tristeza. Límites: fue una tarea de laboratorio con adultos y no muestra cómo es cada persona ni lo que ocurre en la vida diaria.
sheet.en: If an autistic person misses that someone is angry, it may help to say it in words rather than expecting them to read it from the face. It can be as simple as "I'm annoyed" or "I'm calm". Evidence: a study of 60 autistic and non-autistic adults, matched on age, gender, non-verbal reasoning and alexithymia. They viewed moving facial expressions shown as point lights. Autistic participants were less accurate with anger, but not with happy or sad expressions. Limits: it was a lab task with adults, and it does not show what any one person is like or what happens in daily life.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person missar att någon är arg kan det hjälpa att säga det med ord i stället för att förvänta sig att personen läser av ansiktet. Det kan vara så enkelt som "jag är irriterad" eller "jag är lugn". Evidens: en studie med 60 autistiska och icke-autistiska vuxna, matchade på ålder, kön, icke-verbalt resonerande och alexitymi. De såg ansiktsuttryck i rörelse, visade som ljuspunkter. De autistiska deltagarna var mindre träffsäkra på ilska, men inte på glädje eller sorg. Begränsningar: det var en laboratorieuppgift med vuxna, och den visar inte hur en enskild person är eller vad som händer i vardagen.

title: Anxiety and intellectual functioning in autistic children: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Mingins JE, Tarver J, Waite J, Jones C, Surtees AD
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic children often experience higher levels of anxiety than their peers. It can be difficult to diagnose and treat anxiety disorders in autistic children, in part because of the high degree of variability in their underlying abilities and presentations. Some evidence suggests that autistic children with higher intelligence (as measured by intelligence quotient) experience higher levels of anxiety than autistic children with lower intelligence. However, the evidence is inconsistent, with other papers not finding a difference or finding higher levels of anxiety in autistic children with lower intelligence. In this article, we review existing literature to see whether autistic children with higher intelligence quotients have higher anxiety than autistic children with lower intelligence quotients. A systematic search of the literature was conducted which identified 49 papers on the topic. The methods of all the papers were reviewed using an objective quality assessment framework. When combining the data statistically, there was evidence that autistic children with higher intelligence quotients are more anxious than autistic children with lower intelligence quotients. The quality review raised common weaknesses across studies. Most importantly, few studies used measures of anxiety that have been shown to be valid for children with very low intelligence quotients. Similarly, many studies used measures of anxiety that have not been shown to be valid for autistic children. These factors are important because autistic children and those with low intelligence quotient may experience or understand anxiety differently. Future research should use fully validated measures to test whether high intelligence quotient is associated with high levels of anxiety in autistic children.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a un niño autista, no des por hecho que la ansiedad se vea igual en todos: obsérvala también en quienes parecen "llevarlo bien" y pregunta cómo se siente, con apoyos visuales si ayudan. La evidencia es un metaanálisis que reunió 49 artículos sobre niños autistas; en conjunto, quienes tenían un cociente intelectual más alto mostraron más ansiedad que quienes lo tenían más bajo. Sus límites: pocos estudios usaron medidas de ansiedad validadas para niños con cociente intelectual muy bajo, y muchas no estaban validadas para niños autistas. Es un patrón general, no una regla para cada niño.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic child, don't assume anxiety looks the same in everyone: watch for it even in children who seem to be coping well, and ask how they feel, using visual supports if they help. The evidence is a meta-analysis that combined 49 papers about autistic children; overall, those with higher intelligence quotients showed more anxiety than those with lower ones. Its limits: few studies used anxiety measures validated for children with very low intelligence quotients, and many used measures not validated for autistic children. This is a general pattern, not a rule for every child.
sheet.sv: Om du tar hand om ett autistiskt barn: utgå inte från att oro ser likadan ut hos alla. Var uppmärksam även på barn som verkar klara sig bra, och fråga hur de mår, gärna med visuellt stöd om det hjälper. Underlaget är en metaanalys som sammanställde 49 studier om autistiska barn; överlag visade barn med högre intelligenskvot mer ångest än barn med lägre. Begränsningar: få studier använde ångestmått som är validerade för barn med mycket låg intelligenskvot, och många använde mått som inte är validerade för autistiska barn. Det är ett allmänt mönster, inte en regel för varje barn.

title: A Randomized Case Series Approach to Testing Efficacy of Interventions for Minimally Verbal Autistic Children.
authors: Saul J, Norbury C
abstract: Background Randomized Controlled Trials (RCTs) are the gold standard for assessing whether an intervention is effective; however, they require large sample sizes in order to detect small effects. For rare or complex populations, we advocate a case series approach as a more realistic and useful first step for intervention evaluation. We consider the importance of randomization to such designs, and advocate for the use of Randomization Tests and Between Case Effect Sizes to provide a robust and statistically powerful evaluation of outcomes. In this tutorial, we describe the method, procedures, and analysis code necessary to conduct robust single case series, using an empirical example with minimally verbal autistic children. Method We applied a pre-registered (https://osf.io/9gvbs) randomized baseline design with between-case effect size to a case series ( n = 19), to test the efficacy of a novel, parent-mediated, app-based speech production intervention (BabbleBooster) for minimally verbal autistic children. Parent-rated probe scores were used to densely sample performance accuracy over time. Results Parents were able to reliably code their children's speech productions using BabbleBooster. A non-significant Randomization Test and small Between-Case Effect Size ( d = 0.267), suggested there was no evidence that BabbleBooster improved speech production in minimally verbal autistic children, relative to baseline scores, during this brief period of intervention. Conclusion The current analyses exemplify a more robust approach to examining treatment effects in rare or complex populations, where RCT may be difficult or premature to implement. To facilitate adoption of this method by researchers and practitioners, we provide analysis code that can be adapted using open source R packages. Future studies could use this case series design to evaluate interventions aiming to improve speech and language outcomes for minimally verbal autistic children, and other heterogeneous and hard to reach populations.

sheet.es: Una app de producción del habla para niños autistas con poco lenguaje verbal, usada por madres y padres, no mostró mejoras en este estudio, así que no hace falta sentir presión por probarla. Si ya la usáis, observad qué le gusta y le sirve a vuestro hijo o hija. La evidencia es una serie de casos con 19 niños autistas minimamente verbales, cuyas familias puntuaron el habla; el efecto fue pequeño (d = 0.267) y no significativo. Límites: el periodo de intervención fue breve, el grupo pequeño y cada persona es distinta, así que no vale como regla general.
sheet.en: A speech-production app used by parents with autistic children who speak little or not at all showed no improvement in this study, so there is no need to feel pressure to try it. If you already use it, watch what your child enjoys and finds useful. The evidence is a case series of 19 minimally verbal autistic children, with parents scoring their speech; the effect was small (d = 0.267) and not significant. Limits: the intervention period was brief, the group small, and every person is different, so this is not a rule for everyone.
sheet.sv: En app för talproduktion som föräldrar använde med autistiska barn som talar lite eller inte alls visade ingen förbättring i den här studien, så du behöver inte känna press att prova den. Om ni redan använder den, lägg märke till vad ditt barn tycker om och har nytta av. Underlaget är en fallserie med 19 minimalt verbala autistiska barn, där föräldrarna bedömde talet; effekten var liten (d = 0.267) och inte signifikant. Begränsningar: interventionstiden var kort, gruppen liten och alla är olika, så resultatet är ingen regel för alla.

title: Yoga complemented cognitive behavioral therapy on job burnout among teachers of children with autism spectrum disorders.
authors: Dike IC, Onyishi CN, Adimora DE, Ugodulunwa CA, Adama GN, Ugwu GC, Eze UN, Eze A, Ogba FN, Obiwluozo PE, Onu JC, Onu AO, Omenma ZO, Nwaeze VC, Ani C, Ngwu CN, Uzodinma UE, Iremeka FU
abstract: Background/objective Job burnout is a syndrome of reaction to chronic job-related stress which affects overall health, limits occupational efficacy, and personal accomplishments of employees thereby thwarting organizational outcomes. Burnout symptoms are common among teachers of children with autism spectrum disorders (ASD) and affect the academic progress of the children. This study investigated the effectiveness of Yoga-based cognitive behavioral therapy (Y-CBT) in reducing occupational burnout among teachers of children with autism in Lagos States, Nigeria. Methods A group-randomized control-trial with immediate intervention and waitlist control groups was design was adopted. Participants included 58 teachers of children with autism in public and private special schools in the area. Participants were randomly assigned to Y-CBT (N = 29) and waitlist control (N = 29) groups. The Y-CBT group participated in a 2 hours Y-CBT program weekly for 12 weeks. Three instruments Demographic variable, Single Item Stress Questionnaire (SISQ), and Maslach Burnout Inventory-Educators' Survey (MBI-ES) were used to collect data. Data were collected at baseline; post-test and follow-up evaluations. Data were analyzed using means, standard deviations, t test statistics, repeated measures analysis of variance, and bar charts. Results Results revealed that job-burnout reduced significantly at post-test assessment among the Y-CBT group compared to the waitlisted group. The reduction in the participant was sustained across 3months follow-up evaluation. Conclusion It was concluded that Y-CBT modalities could help to reduce the burnout symptoms among teachers of children with ASD.

sheet.es: Si cuidas o enseñas a niños autistas y sientes agotamiento laboral, un programa grupal que combine yoga y terapia cognitivo-conductual podría ser una opción de apoyo para ti; puedes comentarlo con un profesional. Es un ensayo aleatorizado con 58 docentes de niños autistas en escuelas especiales de Lagos, Nigeria. Quienes hicieron 12 semanas de sesiones semanales de 2 horas mostraron menos agotamiento que el grupo en lista de espera, y la mejora se mantuvo 3 meses después. Límites: es un solo estudio, en un lugar concreto, con docentes y no con familias, y no sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you teach or care for autistic children and feel job burnout, a group programme combining yoga and cognitive behavioural therapy may be one support option to explore with a professional. This was a randomised trial with 58 teachers of autistic children in special schools in Lagos, Nigeria. Those who attended 2-hour weekly sessions for 12 weeks reported less burnout than the waitlist group, and the improvement held at 3 months follow-up. Limits: it is a single study in one place, with teachers rather than family caregivers, so it cannot be treated as a rule for everyone.
sheet.sv: Om du undervisar eller tar hand om autistiska barn och känner utbrändhet i arbetet kan ett gruppprogram som kombinerar yoga och kognitiv beteendeterapi vara ett stöd att utforska tillsammans med en yrkesperson. Studien var en randomiserad studie med 58 lärare till autistiska barn i särskilda skolor i Lagos, Nigeria. De som deltog i veckovisa pass på 2 timmar under 12 veckor hade mindre utbrändhet än väntelistegruppen, och förbättringen höll i sig vid uppföljning efter 3 månader. Begränsningar: det är en enskild studie på en plats, med lärare och inte familjemedlemmar, så den kan inte ses som en regel för alla.

title: Psychometric validation and refinement of the Interoception Sensory Questionnaire (ISQ) in adolescents and adults on the autism spectrum.
authors: Suzman E, Williams ZJ, Feldman JI, Failla M, Cascio CJ, Wallace MT, Niarchou M, Sutcliffe JS, Wodka E, Woynaroski TG
abstract: Background Individuals on the autism spectrum are reported to display alterations in interoception, the sense of the internal state of the body. The Interoception Sensory Questionnaire (ISQ) is a 20-item self-report measure of interoception specifically intended to measure this construct in autistic people. The psychometrics of the ISQ, however, have not previously been evaluated in a large sample of autistic individuals. Methods Using confirmatory factor analysis, we evaluated the latent structure of the ISQ in a large online sample of adults on the autism spectrum and found that the unidimensional model fit the data poorly. Using misspecification analysis to identify areas of local misfit and item response theory to investigate the appropriateness of the seven-point response scale, we removed redundant items and collapsed the response options to put forth a novel eight-item, five-response choice ISQ. Results The revised, five-response choice ISQ (ISQ-8) showed much improved fit while maintaining high internal reliability. Differential item functioning (DIF) analyses indicated that the items of the ISQ-8 were answered in comparable ways by autistic adolescents and adults and across multiple other sociodemographic groups. Limitations Our results were limited by the fact that we did not collect data for typically developing controls, preventing the analysis of DIF by diagnostic status. Additionally, while this study proposes a new 5-response scale for the ISQ-8, our data were not collected using this method; thus, the psychometric properties for the revised version of this instrument require further investigation. Conclusion The ISQ-8 shows promise as a reliable and valid measure of interoception in adolescents and adults on the autism spectrum, but additional work is needed to examine its psychometrics in this population. A free online score calculator has been created to facilitate the use of ISQ-8 latent trait scores for further studies of autistic adolescents and adults (available at https://asdmeasures.shinyapps.io/ISQ_score/ ).

sheet.es: Si quieres hablar de las sensaciones internas del cuerpo (hambre, sed, dolor, latidos), una versión corta de un cuestionario, el ISQ-8 de ocho ítems, podría ayudar a ordenar la conversación, pero aún es una herramienta de investigación. Es un estudio de validación con una muestra grande en línea de personas autistas, adolescentes y adultas, que acortó un cuestionario de 20 ítems a 8 y mostró buena fiabilidad interna. Sus límites: no incluyó grupo de comparación sin autismo y la nueva escala de cinco respuestas no se aplicó tal cual, así que necesita más estudio. No sustituye la voz de cada persona.
sheet.en: If you want to talk about the body's inner sensations (hunger, thirst, pain, heartbeat), a short eight-item questionnaire, the ISQ-8, may help structure the conversation, but it is still a research tool. This was a validation study with a large online sample of autistic adolescents and adults, which shortened a 20-item questionnaire to 8 items and showed high internal reliability. Its limits: it had no comparison group without autism, and the new five-response scale was not used as such in data collection, so it needs more study. It does not replace each person's own voice.
sheet.sv: Om du vill prata om kroppens inre signaler (hunger, törst, smärta, hjärtslag) kan en kort version av ett frågeformulär, ISQ-8 med åtta frågor, hjälpa till att strukturera samtalet, men det är fortfarande ett forskningsverktyg. Det var en valideringsstudie med ett stort onlineurval av autistiska ungdomar och vuxna, där ett formulär med 20 frågor kortades till 8 och visade hög intern reliabilitet. Begränsningar: ingen jämförelsegrupp utan autism, och den nya skalan med fem svarsalternativ användes inte som sådan vid datainsamlingen, så mer forskning behövs. Det ersätter inte varje persons egen röst.

title: Employing Evidence-Based Practices for Children with Autism in Elementary Schools.
authors: Sam AM, Odom SL, Tomaszewski B, Perkins Y, Cox AW
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: The purpose of this study was to test the efficacy of a comprehensive program model originally developed by the National Professional Development Center on Autism Spectrum Disorder (NPDC). Sixty elementary schools with 486 participants were randomly assigned to an NPDC and services as usual condition (SAU). Significantly greater changes in program quality occurred in the inclusive NPDC programs as compared with the SAU schools. Teachers in NPDC schools reported using more evidence-based practices (EBPs) and implemented EBPs with significantly greater fidelity than teachers in SAU schools. Autistic students in NPDC schools had significantly higher total attainment of educational goals than students in SAU schools, and the two groups made equivalent progress on standardized assessment outcomes across the school year.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a un niño autista en primaria, pregunta al equipo docente qué prácticas basadas en la evidencia usan y cómo comprueban que se aplican bien. Es un ensayo aleatorizado con 60 escuelas primarias y 486 participantes. Las escuelas con el modelo NPDC mejoraron más la calidad del programa, y sus docentes usaron más esas prácticas y con mayor fidelidad. El alumnado autista alcanzó más objetivos educativos, aunque el progreso en las pruebas estandarizadas fue equivalente al de las escuelas habituales. El estudio no detalla cómo vivió cada niño el programa ni si estos resultados se darían en cualquier escuela o en cualquier persona.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic child in elementary school, ask the teaching team which evidence-based practices they use and how they check these are carried out well. This was a randomised trial with 60 elementary schools and 486 participants. Schools using the NPDC model improved program quality more, and their teachers used more of these practices, with greater fidelity. Autistic students reached more of their educational goals, though progress on standardized assessments was equivalent to that in usual-service schools. The study does not describe how each child experienced the program, and results may not apply to every school or every person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar ett autistiskt barn i grundskolan kan du fråga lärarlaget vilka evidensbaserade arbetssätt de använder och hur de kontrollerar att de genomförs väl. Detta var en randomiserad studie med 60 grundskolor och 486 deltagare. Skolor med NPDC-modellen förbättrade programmets kvalitet mer, och lärarna använde fler sådana arbetssätt med högre följsamhet. Autistiska elever nådde fler av sina utbildningsmål, men framstegen på standardiserade tester var likvärdiga med dem i skolor med vanligt stöd. Studien beskriver inte hur varje barn upplevde programmet, och resultaten gäller inte nödvändigtvis alla skolor eller alla personer.

title: Autistic Adult Health and Professional Perceptions of It: Evidence From the ASDEU Project.
authors: Micai M, Ciaramella A, Salvitti T, Fulceri F, Fatta LM, Poustka L, Diehm R, Iskrov G, Stefanov R, Guillon Q, Rogé B, Staines A, Sweeney MR, Boilson AM, Leósdóttir T, Saemundsen E, Moilanen I, Ebeling
abstract: The Autism Spectrum Disorders in the European Union (ASDEU) survey investigated the knowledge and health service experiences of users and providers to generate new hypotheses and scientific investigations that would contribute to improvement in health care for autistic adults. An online survey designed for autistic adults, carers of autistic adults, and professionals in adult services was translated into 11 languages and distributed electronically by organizations and in-country adult service facilities in 2017; 522 autistic adults, 442 carers, and 113 professionals provided answers to the health questions. Professionals, the majority in non-medical services, appeared to be poorly informed about whether certain co-occurring conditions were more frequent in autistic adults than typical adults-especially some medical conditions, suicide attempts, accidents, and pain. A minority of autistic adults reported preventive health behaviors such as routine health check-ups. The majority of users and providers expressed the desire to make health care services more user-friendly for autistic adults. Among the three groups, <20% of responders knew an organization or clinician which has developed a way to monitor health, and prevent poor health, that works well for adults on the autism spectrum. The results point to means for better management of co-occurring conditions associated with autism in adulthood in order to reduce hospital admissions and potential areas of improvement in health and social services for autistic adults. Specifically, efforts should be focused on (1) professionals' education on risks for co-occurring conditions in autistic adults; (2) promoting preventive health behaviors; (3) making services user-friendly for autistic adults and their families; and (4) encouraging knowledge of good local services.

sheet.es: Antes de una cita de salud, conviene preparar por escrito los temas importantes (dolor, accidentes, pensamientos suicidas, chequeos de rutina) y pedir que el servicio se adapte a la persona autista. Los profesionales pueden no saber que algunas condiciones son más frecuentes en adultos autistas. La evidencia es una encuesta en línea en 11 idiomas, con 522 adultos autistas, 442 cuidadores y 113 profesionales. Refleja percepciones, no mide la salud de cada persona, y no sirve como regla para todas. Si te preocupa un posible suicidio o autolesión, habla con un profesional sanitario o un servicio de crisis; ante peligro inmediato, llama al número de emergencias de tu país.
sheet.en: Before a health appointment, it helps to write down what matters (pain, accidents, suicidal thoughts, routine check-ups) and to ask the service to adapt to the autistic person. Professionals may not know that some conditions are more common in autistic adults. The evidence is an online survey in 11 languages with 522 autistic adults, 442 carers and 113 professionals. It captures perceptions, does not measure each person's health, and is not a rule for everyone. If you are worried about suicide or self-injury, talk to a clinician, a health service or a crisis service; in immediate danger, call the emergency number of your country.
sheet.sv: Inför ett vårdbesök kan det hjälpa att skriva ner det som är viktigt (smärta, olyckor, självmordstankar, rutinkontroller) och be vården anpassa sig efter den autistiska personen. Personal kanske inte vet att vissa tillstånd är vanligare hos autistiska vuxna. Underlaget är en enkät på nätet på 11 språk med 522 autistiska vuxna, 442 anhöriga och 113 yrkespersoner. Den visar uppfattningar, mäter inte varje persons hälsa och är ingen regel för alla. Om du oroar dig för självmord eller självskada, kontakta en läkare, vården eller en krisjour; vid akut fara ring larmnumret i ditt land.

title: Assessment and Treatment of Anxiety in Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder in School Settings: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Perihan C, Bicer A, Bocanegra J

title: REM Sleep EEG Activity and Clinical Correlates in Adults With Autism.
authors: Gagnon K, Bolduc C, Bastien L, Godbout R
abstract: We tested the hypothesis of an atypical scalp distribution of electroencephalography (EEG) activity during Rapid Eye Movement (REM) sleep in young autistic adults. EEG spectral activity and ratios along the anteroposterior axis and across hemispheres were compared in 16 neurotypical (NT) young adults and 17 individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). EEG spectral power was lower in the ASD group over the bilateral central and right parietal (beta activity) as well as bilateral occipital (beta, theta, and total activity) recording sites. The NT group displayed a significant posterior polarity of intra-hemispheric EEG activity while EEG activity was more evenly or anteriorly distributed in ASD participants. No significant inter-hemispheric EEG lateralization was found. Correlations between EEG distribution and ASD symptoms using the Autism Diagnostic Interview-Revised (ADI-R) showed that a higher posterior ratio was associated with a better ADI-R score on communication skills, whereas a higher anterior ratio was related to more restricted interests and repetitive behaviors. EEG activity thus appears to be atypically distributed over the scalp surface in young adults with autism during REM sleep within cerebral hemispheres, and this correlates with some ASD symptoms. These suggests the existence in autism of a common substrate between some of the symptoms of ASD and an atypical organization and/or functioning of the thalamo-cortical loop during REM sleep.

sheet.es: Este estudio no ofrece nada que cambiar mañana por la mañana: sirve para entender mejor el sueño, no para actuar. Si le preocupa cómo duerme una persona autista, anote lo que observa y coméntelo con un profesional sanitario. Es un estudio de investigación con 17 adultos jóvenes autistas y 16 adultos jóvenes neurotípicos, que comparó la actividad eléctrica cerebral (EEG) durante el sueño REM. Encontró una distribución distinta en el grupo autista, relacionada con algunas puntuaciones de una entrevista diagnóstica. Sus límites: la muestra es pequeña y la relación no demuestra causa. No describe a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: This study gives nothing to change tomorrow morning: it helps us understand sleep better, not act on it. If you are worried about how an autistic person sleeps, note what you observe and talk it over with a health professional. It is a research study with 17 young autistic adults and 16 young neurotypical adults, comparing brain electrical activity (EEG) during REM sleep. It found a different distribution in the autistic group, linked to some scores on a diagnostic interview. Its limits: the sample is small and a link does not show cause. It does not describe every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Den här studien ger inget att ändra i morgon bitti: den hjälper oss förstå sömn bättre, inte att agera. Om du oroar dig för hur en autistisk person sover, anteckna vad du ser och prata med en vårdgivare. Det är en forskningsstudie med 17 unga autistiska vuxna och 16 unga neurotypiska vuxna, som jämförde hjärnans elektriska aktivitet (EEG) under REM-sömn. Den fann en annorlunda fördelning i den autistiska gruppen, kopplad till vissa poäng i en diagnostisk intervju. Begränsningar: urvalet är litet och ett samband visar inte orsak. Den beskriver inte alla autistiska personer.

title: Visual Sensory Experiences From the Viewpoint of Autistic Adults.
authors: Parmar KR, Porter CS, Dickinson CM, Pelham J, Baimbridge P, Gowen E
abstract: Although previous research has investigated altered sensory reactivity in autistic individuals, there has been no specific focus on visual sensory experiences, particularly in adults. Using qualitative methods, this study aimed to characterize autistic visual sensory symptoms, contextualize their impact and document any associated coping strategies. A total of 18 autistic adults took part in four focus groups which involved questions around visual experiences, the impact of these on daily life, and strategies for their reduction. Transcripts of each session were thematically analyzed allocating six key themes. Participants described a range of visual hypersensitivities, including to light, motion, patterns and particular colors, which contributed to distraction and were frequently part of a wider multisensory issue. Such experiences had significant negative impacts on personal wellbeing and daily life with participants describing fatigue, stress and hindrances on day-to-day activities (e.g., travel and social activities). However, the degree of understanding that participants had about their visual experiences influenced their emotional response, with greater understanding reducing concern. Participants employed a variety of coping strategies to overcome visual sensory experiences but with varied success. Discussions also highlighted that there may be a poor public understanding of sensory issues in autism affecting how well autistic individuals are able manage their sensory symptoms. In summary, autistic adults expressed significant concern about their visual experiences and there is a need to improve understanding of visual experiences on a personal and public level as well as for developing potential support.

sheet.es: Pregunte a la persona autista qué le molesta visualmente: luz intensa, movimiento, patrones o ciertos colores. Ajustar la iluminación, permitir gafas de sol o gorra, reducir el desorden visual y planificar descansos antes de viajes o actividades sociales puede disminuir el cansancio y el estrés. Entender las propias reacciones visuales parecía reducir la preocupación, así que hablar de ello con calma ayuda. Las estrategias funcionan de forma distinta para cada persona; pruebe y observe. Evidencia: estudio cualitativo con cuatro grupos focales de 18 adultos autistas que describieron sus experiencias. Límites: muestra pequeña, solo adultos y relatos personales, sin medir qué estrategias funcionan mejor.
sheet.en: Ask the autistic person what bothers them visually: bright light, motion, patterns or certain colours. Adjusting lighting, allowing sunglasses or a cap, reducing visual clutter and planning breaks before travel or social activities may ease fatigue and stress. Understanding one's own visual reactions seemed to reduce worry, so talking about it calmly can help. Strategies work differently for each person; try things and notice what helps. Evidence: a qualitative study with four focus groups of 18 autistic adults describing their own experiences. Limits: a small sample, adults only, and personal accounts, without testing which strategies work best.
sheet.sv: Fråga den autistiska personen vad som stör visuellt: starkt ljus, rörelse, mönster eller vissa färger. Att justera belysningen, tillåta solglasögon eller keps, minska visuellt rörigt och planera pauser inför resor eller sociala aktiviteter kan minska trötthet och stress. Att förstå sina egna visuella reaktioner verkade minska oron, så att lugnt prata om dem kan hjälpa. Strategier fungerar olika för olika personer; prova och se vad som hjälper. Evidens: en kvalitativ studie med fyra fokusgrupper där 18 autistiska vuxna beskrev sina erfarenheter. Begränsningar: litet urval, endast vuxna och egna berättelser, utan test av vilka strategier som fungerar bäst.

title: Development and validation of the suicidal behaviours questionnaire - autism spectrum conditions in a community sample of autistic, possibly autistic and non-autistic adults.
authors: Cassidy SA, Bradley L, Cogger-Ward H, Rodgers J
abstract: Background Autistic people and those with high autistic traits are at high risk of experiencing suicidality. Yet, there are no suicidality assessment tools developed or validated for these groups. Methods A widely used and validated suicidality assessment tool developed for the general population (SBQ-R), was adapted using feedback from autistic adults, to create the Suicidal Behaviours Questionnaire-Autism Spectrum Conditions (SBQ-ASC). The adapted tool was refined through nine interviews, and an online survey with 251 autistic adults, to establish clarity and relevance of the items. Subsequently, 308 autistic, 113 possibly autistic, and 268 non-autistic adults completed the adapted tool online, alongside self-report measures of autistic traits (AQ), camouflaging autistic traits (CAT-Q), depression (PHQ-9), anxiety (ASA-A), thwarted belongingness and perceived burdensomeness (INQ-15), lifetime non-suicidal self-injury, and the original version of the suicidality assessment tool (SBQ-R). Analyses explored the appropriateness and measurement properties of the adapted tool between the groups. Results There was evidence in support of content validity, structural validity, internal consistency, convergent and divergent validity, test-retest validity, sensitivity and specificity (for distinguishing those with or without lifetime experience of suicide attempt), and hypothesis testing of the adapted tool (SBQ-ASC) in each group. The structure of the SBQ-ASC was equivalent between autistic and possibly autistic adults, regardless of gender, or use of visual aids to help quantify abstract rating scales. Limitations The samples involved in the development and validation of the adapted tool were largely female, and largely diagnosed as autistic in adulthood, which limits the generalisability of results to the wider autistic population. The SBQ-ASC has been developed for use in research and is not recommended to assess risk of future suicide attempts and/or self-harm. The SBQ-ASC has been designed with and for autistic and possibly autistic adults, and is not appropriate to compare to non-autistic adults given measurement differences between these groups. Conclusions The SBQ-ASC is a brief self-report suicidality assessment tool, developed and validated with and for autistic adults, without co-occurring intellectual disability. The SBQ-ASC is appropriate for use in research to identify suicidal thoughts and behaviours in autistic and possibly autistic people, and model associations with risk and protective factors.

title: International Expert Opinions and Recommendations on the Use of Melatonin in the Treatment of Insomnia and Circadian Sleep Disturbances in Adult Neuropsychiatric Disorders.
authors: Palagini L, Manni R, Aguglia E, Amore M, Brugnoli R, Bioulac S, Bourgin P, Micoulaud Franchi JA, Girardi P, Grassi L, Lopez R, Mencacci C, Plazzi G, Maruani J, Minervino A, Philip P, Royant Parola S,
abstract: Introduction: Insomnia and circadian rhythm disorders, such as the delayed sleep phase syndrome, are frequent in psychiatric disorders and their evaluation and management in early stages should be a priority. The aim of this paper was to express recommendations on the use of exogenous melatonin, which exhibits both chronobiotic and sleep-promoting actions, for the treatment of these sleep disturbances in psychiatric disorders. Methods: To this aim, we conducted a systematic review according to PRISMA on the use of melatonin for the treatment of insomnia and circadian sleep disorders in neuropsychiatry. We expressed recommendations for the use of melatonin in psychiatric clinical practice for each disorder using the RAND/UCLA appropriateness method. Results: We selected 41 studies, which included mood disorders, schizophrenia, substance use disorders, attention deficit hyperactivity disorders, autism spectrum disorders, neurocognitive disorders, and delirium; no studies were found for both anxiety and eating disorders. Conclusion: The administration of prolonged release melatonin at 2-10 mg, 1-2 h before bedtime, might be used in the treatment of insomnia symptoms or comorbid insomnia in mood disorders, schizophrenia, in adults with autism spectrum disorders, neurocognitive disorders and during sedative-hypnotics discontinuation. Immediate release melatonin at <1 mg might be useful in the treatment of circadian sleep disturbances of neuropsychiatric disorders.

title: Brain-based sex differences in autism spectrum disorder across the lifespan: A systematic review of structural MRI, fMRI, and DTI findings.
authors: Walsh MJM, Wallace GL, Gallegos SM, Braden BB
abstract: Females with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) have been long overlooked in neuroscience research, but emerging evidence suggests they show distinct phenotypic trajectories and age-related brain differences. Sex-related biological factors (e.g., hormones, genes) may play a role in ASD etiology and have been shown to influence neurodevelopmental trajectories. Thus, a lifespan approach is warranted to understand brain-based sex differences in ASD. This systematic review on MRI-based sex differences in ASD was conducted to elucidate variations across the lifespan and inform biomarker discovery of ASD in females We identified articles through two database searches. Fifty studies met criteria and underwent integrative review. We found that regions expressing replicable sex-by-diagnosis differences across studies overlapped with regions showing sex differences in neurotypical cohorts. Furthermore, studies investigating age-related brain differences across a broad age-span suggest distinct neurodevelopmental patterns in females with ASD. Qualitative comparison across youth and adult studies also supported this hypothesis. However, many studies collapsed across age, which may mask differences. Furthermore, accumulating evidence supports the female protective effect in ASD, although only one study examined brain circuits implicated in "protection." When synthesized with the broader literature, brain-based sex differences in ASD may come from various sources, including genetic and endocrine processes involved in brain "masculinization" and "feminization" across early development, puberty, and other lifespan windows of hormonal transition. Furthermore, sex-related biology may interact with peripheral processes, in particular the stress axis and brain arousal system, to produce distinct neurodevelopmental patterns in males and females with ASD. Future research on neuroimaging-based sex differences in ASD would benefit from a lifespan approach in well-controlled and multivariate studies. Possible relationships between behavior, sex hormones, and brain development in ASD remain largely unexamined.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una niña, adolescente o mujer autista, recuerda que la investigación sobre el cerebro se ha centrado mucho en varones, así que su experiencia puede no coincidir con lo que se describe en general. Observa su trayectoria individual y escucha lo que ella cuenta. Es una revisión sistemática de 50 estudios de resonancia magnética en distintas edades. Sugiere patrones de desarrollo cerebral distintos en mujeres autistas. Sin embargo, muchos estudios no separaron por edad, pocos examinaron la "protección" y la relación con la conducta y las hormonas apenas se ha estudiado. No sirve para valorar a una persona concreta.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic girl, teen or woman, remember that brain research has focused heavily on males, so her experience may not match what is generally described. Watch her own path and listen to what she tells you. This is a systematic review of 50 MRI studies across different ages. It suggests autistic females may have distinct patterns of brain development. However, many studies did not separate results by age, only one looked at brain circuits linked to "protection", and links between behaviour, hormones and brain development are largely unexamined. It cannot be used to assess any one person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk flicka, tonåring eller kvinna: komma ihåg att hjärnforskningen främst har handlat om killar och män, så hennes upplevelse kanske inte stämmer med den allmänna bilden. Följ hennes egen utveckling och lyssna på det hon berättar. Detta är en systematisk översikt av 50 MRI-studier i olika åldrar. Den antyder att autistiska kvinnor kan ha andra mönster i hjärnans utveckling. Många studier slog dock ihop åldrarna, bara en studie undersökte hjärnkretsar kopplade till "skydd", och sambanden mellan beteende, hormoner och hjärnutveckling är i stort sett outforskade. Den kan inte användas för att bedöma en enskild person.

title: Auditory Discrimination in Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Rotschafer SE
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is increasingly common with 1 in 59 children in the United States currently meeting the diagnostic criteria. Altered sensory processing is typical in ASD, with auditory sensitivities being especially common; in particular, people with ASD frequently show heightened sensitivity to environmental sounds and a poor ability to tolerate loud sounds. These sensitivities may contribute to impairments in language comprehension and to a worsened ability to distinguish relevant sounds from background noise. Event-related potential tests have found that individuals with ASD show altered cortical activity to both simple and speech-like sounds, which likely contribute to the observed processing impairments. Our goal in this review is to provide a description of ASD-related changes to the auditory system and how those changes contribute to the impairments seen in sound discrimination, sound-in-noise performance, and language processing. In particular, we emphasize how differences in the degree of cortical activation and in temporal processing may contribute to errors in sound discrimination.

sheet.es: Mañana, reduzca el ruido de fondo cuando hable con una persona autista: apague la tele, acérquese y use frases breves. Ofrezca también auriculares o un lugar más tranquilo si lo desea. La evidencia es una revisión que resume estudios sobre el sistema auditivo en el autismo. Señala que muchas personas autistas son sensibles a los sonidos del entorno y que pueden tener más dificultad para distinguir el habla entre ruido. Sus límites: es un resumen general, no una guía para cada persona, y las experiencias auditivas varían mucho. Pregunte siempre a la persona qué sonidos le molestan y qué le ayuda.
sheet.en: Tomorrow, lower background noise when talking with an autistic person: switch off the TV, move closer and use short sentences. Offer headphones or a quieter space if they want them. The evidence is a review summarising studies on the auditory system in autism. It reports that many autistic people are sensitive to environmental sounds and may find it harder to pick out speech in noise. Its limits: it is a general overview, not a guide for every person, and auditory experiences vary widely. Always ask the person which sounds bother them and what helps.
sheet.sv: I morgon kan du minska bakgrundsljud när du pratar med en autistisk person: stäng av tv:n, kom närmare och använd korta meningar. Erbjud hörlurar eller ett lugnare rum om personen vill det. Underlaget är en översikt som sammanfattar studier om hörselsystemet vid autism. Den beskriver att många autistiska personer är känsliga för ljud i omgivningen och kan ha svårare att urskilja tal i buller. Begränsningar: det är en allmän sammanfattning, inte en vägledning för varje person, och upplevelser av ljud varierar mycket. Fråga alltid personen vilka ljud som stör och vad som hjälper.

title: Neurobiological and behavioural outcomes of biofeedback-based training in autism: a randomized controlled trial.
authors: Surgent O, Dean DC, Alexander AL, Dadalko OI, Guerrero-Gonzalez J, Taylor D, Skaletski E, Travers BG
abstract: The human brain has demonstrated the power to structurally change as a result of movement-based interventions. However, it is unclear whether these structural brain changes differ in autistic individuals compared to non-autistic individuals. The purpose of the present study was to pilot a randomized controlled trial to investigate brain, balance, autism symptom severity and daily living skill changes that result from a biofeedback-based balance intervention in autistic adolescents (13-17 years old). Thirty-four autistic participants and 28 age-matched non-autistic participants underwent diagnostic testing and pre-training assessment (neuroimaging, cognitive, autism symptom severity and motor assessments) and were then randomly assigned to 6 weeks of a balance-training intervention or a sedentary-control condition. After the 6 weeks, neuroimaging, symptom severity and motor assessments were repeated. Results found that both the autistic and non-autistic participants demonstrated similar and significant increases in balance times with training. Furthermore, individuals in the balance-training condition showed significantly greater improvements in postural sway and reductions in autism symptom severity compared to individuals in the control condition. Daily living scores did not change with training, nor did we observe hypothesized changes to the microstructural properties of the corticospinal tract. However, follow-up voxel-based analyses found a wide range of balance-related structures that showed changes across the brain. Many of these brain changes were specific to the autistic participants compared to the non-autistic participants, suggesting distinct structural neuroplasticity in response to balance training in autistic participants. Altogether, these findings suggest that biofeedback-based balance training may target postural stability challenges, reduce core autism symptoms and influence neurobiological change. Future research is encouraged to examine the superior cerebellar peduncle in response to balance training and symptom severity changes in autistic individuals, as the current study produced overlapping findings in this brain region.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adolescente quiere probar ejercicios de equilibrio con retroalimentación (biofeedback), puede ser una actividad útil para trabajar la estabilidad postural; conviene probarla con calma y según sus preferencias. Evidencia: ensayo piloto aleatorizado con 34 adolescentes autistas y 28 no autistas (13-17 años); 6 semanas de entrenamiento de equilibrio o condición sedentaria. Mejoró el equilibrio y la oscilación postural, y bajó la gravedad de síntomas autistas según las medidas del estudio; las habilidades de la vida diaria no cambiaron. Límites: estudio piloto, pequeño, solo adolescentes, y los resultados no valen para todas las personas. Cualquier decisión médica corresponde a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If an autistic teenager is interested in biofeedback-based balance exercises, they may be a useful way to work on postural stability; try them calmly and follow the young person's preferences. Evidence: a pilot randomized controlled trial with 34 autistic and 28 non-autistic adolescents (13-17 years old), who did 6 weeks of balance training or a sedentary condition. Balance and postural sway improved, and autism symptom severity scores dropped on the study's measures; daily living skills did not change. Limits: it was a small pilot, only with teenagers, and results do not apply to every person. Any medical decision belongs to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk tonåring är intresserad av balansövningar med biofeedback kan det vara ett sätt att träna postural stabilitet; prova i lugn takt och utgå från ungdomens önskemål. Evidens: en randomiserad pilotstudie med 34 autistiska och 28 icke-autistiska ungdomar (13-17 år) som tränade balans i 6 veckor eller hade en stillasittande kontrollvillkor. Balans och posturalt svaj förbättrades, och graden av autistiska symtom minskade enligt studiens mått; vardagsfärdigheter förändrades inte. Begränsningar: liten pilotstudie, enbart tonåringar, och resultaten gäller inte alla. Medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker.

title: Development and Psychometric Properties of a New Questionnaire to Assess Mental Health and Concerning Behaviors in Children and Young People with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD): The Assessment of Concerning Behavior (ACB) Scale.
authors: Tarver J, Vitoratou S, Mastroianni M, Heaney N, Bennett E, Gibbons F, Fiori F, Absoud M, Ramasubramanian L, Simonoff E, Santosh P
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Although 70% of autistic children and young people meet criteria for co-occurring psychiatric conditions, there are few screening measures specifically for autistic individuals. We describe the development and validation of the Assessment of Concerning Behavior (ACB), an instrument co-developed with the autistic community to assess mental health and problematic/risky behaviors. Items include descriptions to facilitate symptom recognition by autistic people, and carers/professionals. The ACB was completed by 255 parents, 149 autistic children and young people and 30 teachers. Internal consistency, stability and validity was assessed. The ACB parent-version fit a two-factor model (internalizing and externalizing problems) and showed adequate test-retest reliability, internal consistency and construct validity. The ACB is a promising new measure for research and clinical use in autism.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija autista tiene dificultades emocionales o conductas que te preocupan, quizá en el futuro un cuestionario pensado para personas autistas ayude a ponerlas en palabras en la consulta. Por ahora, anota ejemplos concretos para compartirlos con un profesional. El estudio presentó y probó la escala ACB, creada junto con la comunidad autista, con 255 madres y padres, 149 niños y jóvenes autistas y 30 docentes. La versión para familias mostró resultados adecuados de fiabilidad y validez. Es una medida prometedora, pero no es una herramienta de diagnóstico ni sirve igual para todas las personas; no sustituye la valoración clínica.
sheet.en: If your autistic child or young person has emotional difficulties or behaviours that worry you, a questionnaire designed for autistic people may one day help put them into words at appointments. For now, jot down concrete examples to share with a professional. This study developed and tested the ACB scale, co-developed with the autistic community, with 255 parents, 149 autistic children and young people and 30 teachers. The parent version showed adequate reliability and validity. It is a promising measure, but it is not a diagnostic tool, it may not fit every person equally, and it does not replace a clinical assessment.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn eller din autistiska unga har känslomässiga svårigheter eller beteenden som oroar dig, kan ett frågeformulär anpassat för autistiska personer kanske i framtiden hjälpa dig att sätta ord på dem vid besök. Anteckna tills vidare konkreta exempel att dela med en professionell. Studien utvecklade och testade ACB-skalan, som togs fram tillsammans med den autistiska gemenskapen, med 255 föräldrar, 149 autistiska barn och unga och 30 lärare. Föräldraversionen visade god tillförlitlighet och validitet. Måttet är lovande, men det är inget diagnosverktyg, passar inte alla lika bra och ersätter inte en klinisk bedömning.

title: Effectiveness of Virtual/Augmented Reality-Based Therapeutic Interventions on Individuals With Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Comprehensive Meta-Analysis.
authors: Karami B, Koushki R, Arabgol F, Rahmani M, Vahabie AH
abstract: In recent years, the application of virtual reality (VR) for therapeutic purposes has escalated dramatically. Favorable properties of VR for engaging patients with autism, in particular, have motivated an enormous body of investigations targeting autism-related disabilities with this technology. This study aims to provide a comprehensive meta-analysis for evaluating the effectiveness of VR on the rehabilitation and training of individuals diagnosed with an autism spectrum disorder. Accordingly, we conducted a systematic search of related databases and, after screening for inclusion criteria, reviewed 33 studies for more detailed analysis. Results revealed that individuals undergoing VR training have remarkable improvements with a relatively large effect size with Hedges g of 0.74. Furthermore, the results of the analysis of different skills indicated diverse effectiveness. The strongest effect was observed for daily living skills ( g = 1.15). This effect was moderate for other skills: g = 0.45 for cognitive skills, g = 0.46 for emotion regulation and recognition skills, and g = 0.69 for social and communication skills. Moreover, five studies that had used augmented reality also showed promising efficacy ( g = 0.92) that calls for more research on this tool. In conclusion, the application of VR-based settings in clinical practice is highly encouraged, although their standardization and customization need more research.

title: Exploring an e-learning community's response to the language and terminology use in autism from two massive open online courses on autism education and technology use.
authors: Lei J, Jones L, Brosnan M
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Within the neurodiversity movement, one recent divergence is in the semantic choice of language when describing autism, as members of the autism and autistic community preferred to use identity - first language (autistic person), whereas professionals were more likely to use person-first language (person with autism). This study explored 803 e-learners' responses from their comments across two massive open online courses on autism education held between 2017 and 2019. Learners agreed that autistic individuals should guide others on which terminology to use when describing autism, and although identity-first language acknowledges autism as part of an individual's identity, it can also conjure up negative stereotypes and be stigmatising. Although family, friends and professionals highlighted that the diagnostic label is a way to facilitate understanding across stakeholder groups and help autistic individuals gain access to support, autistic self-advocates found the process of disclosing autism as a form of disability to conflict with their sense of identity, and broader terms such as 'autism spectrum' failed to capture individual strengths and weaknesses. Semantic language choices may matter less as long as the person's difficulties are clearly acknowledged, with adaptations made to meet their specific needs. Adding to a growing body of literature on terminology use in autism research and practice, we highlight that language used when describing autism should follow the autistic individual's lead, with the primary focus on communicating an individual's strengths and difficulties, to foster a sense of positive autism identity and inclusivity, and enable access to appropriate support.

sheet.es: Pregunta a la persona autista cómo quiere que se hable de ella y sigue su preferencia: muchas personas prefieren «persona autista», pero no todas. Más que la etiqueta exacta, importa describir con claridad sus fortalezas y dificultades y ajustar los apoyos a sus necesidades concretas. Puedes acordar con ella qué palabras usar en el colegio, en el médico o con la familia. La evidencia procede de un análisis de comentarios de 803 participantes en dos cursos en línea sobre educación y autismo (2017-2019), entre ellos personas autistas, familias y profesionales. Su límite: eran comentarios voluntarios de un grupo concreto de estudiantes, no una muestra representativa, así que no fija una norma para todos.
sheet.en: Ask the autistic person how they want to be described and follow their lead: many prefer "autistic person", but not everyone does. More than the exact label, what matters is clearly describing their strengths and difficulties and adapting support to their specific needs. You might agree together on which words to use at school, at the doctor's or with relatives. The evidence comes from an analysis of comments by 803 learners in two online courses on autism education (2017-2019), including autistic people, families and professionals. Its limit: these were voluntary comments from a specific group of learners, not a representative sample, so it does not set a rule for everyone.
sheet.sv: Fråga den autistiska personen hur hen vill bli beskriven och följ hens önskemål: många föredrar ”autistisk person”, men inte alla. Viktigare än den exakta etiketten är att tydligt beskriva personens styrkor och svårigheter och anpassa stödet efter hens egna behov. Ni kan tillsammans bestämma vilka ord som används i skolan, hos läkaren eller med släkten. Underlaget är en analys av kommentarer från 803 deltagare i två onlinekurser om autism och utbildning (2017–2019), bland dem autistiska personer, familjer och yrkesverksamma. Begränsning: det var frivilliga kommentarer från en viss grupp kursdeltagare, inte ett representativt urval, så studien ger ingen regel som gäller alla.

title: A systematic review of the experience of being a sibling of a child with an autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Watson L, Hanna P, Jones CJ
abstract: Difficulties associated with Autism Spectrum Disorders can cause considerable impact on personal, familial, social, educational and occupational functioning. Living with a child who has an Autism Spectrum Disorder can therefore pose a challenge to family members, including typically developing siblings. However, it is only in recent years that the experience of typically developing siblings has become a focal point. A systematic review using keywords across six databases was undertaken to summarise qualitative studies that focused on the experience of being a sibling of a child with an Autism Spectrum Disorder. Fifteen studies met inclusion criteria and a thematic synthesis was completed. The synthesis found that having a sibling who has an Autism Spectrum Disorder can impact typically developing sibling's self-identity and personal development in a number of ways. Similarly, interactions with the sibling who has Autism Spectrum Disorders and with other individuals can evoke a myriad of experiences that can both benefit and challenge typically developing siblings. The ability of typically developing siblings to cope with adverse experiences needs to remain a focus. This synthesis concludes that further research is needed to identify which methods are the most effective in supporting typically developing siblings of children with Autism Spectrum Disorders.

sheet.es: Dedique un rato a escuchar a las hermanas y hermanos no autistas: pregúnteles cómo viven la convivencia y qué les ayudaría. Su experiencia puede traer beneficios y también dificultades, y conviene dejar espacio para ambas. La evidencia es una revisión sistemática de quince estudios cualitativos que resumió sus experiencias con un análisis temático. Sugiere que tener un hermano autista puede influir en su identidad y desarrollo personal. Sus límites: no indica qué métodos de apoyo funcionan mejor, los autores piden más investigación, y cada familia y cada hermano o hermana es distinto.
sheet.en: Take some time to listen to non-autistic siblings: ask how they experience life at home and what would help them. Their experience can bring benefits as well as difficulties, so leave room for both. The evidence is a systematic review of fifteen qualitative studies, summarised with a thematic synthesis. It suggests that having an autistic sibling can shape a sibling's identity and personal development. Its limits: it does not show which support methods work best, the authors call for more research, and every family and every sibling is different.
sheet.sv: Ta en stund för att lyssna på syskon som inte är autistiska: fråga hur de upplever vardagen hemma och vad som skulle hjälpa dem. Deras erfarenhet kan ge både fördelar och svårigheter, så lämna plats för båda. Underlaget är en systematisk översikt av femton kvalitativa studier, sammanfattade med en tematisk syntes. Den tyder på att ett autistiskt syskon kan påverka syskonets identitet och personliga utveckling. Begränsningar: den visar inte vilka stödmetoder som fungerar bäst, forskarna efterlyser mer forskning, och varje familj och varje syskon är olika.

title: Demographic and psychological predictors of alcohol use and misuse in autistic adults.
authors: Bowri M, Hull L, Allison C, Smith P, Baron-Cohen S, Lai MC, Mandy W
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Alcohol use and misuse are associated with a variety of negative physical, psychological and social consequences. The limited existing research on substance use including alcohol use in autistic adults has yielded mixed findings, with some studies concluding that autism reduces the likelihood of substance use and others suggesting that autism may increase an individual's risk for substance misuse. This study investigated demographic and psychological predictors of alcohol use and misuse in a sample of 237 autistic adults. An online survey was used to obtain data on demographic information, autistic traits, depression, generalised anxiety, social anxiety, mental well-being, social camouflaging and alcohol use. The sample was divided into three groups (non-drinkers, non-hazardous drinkers and hazardous drinkers) in order to investigate associations between alcohol use and demographic factors, autistic traits, mental health variables and social camouflaging. Our results demonstrated a U-shaped pattern among autistic adults, with non-drinkers and hazardous drinkers scoring higher than non-hazardous drinkers on levels of autistic traits, depression, generalised anxiety and social anxiety. Autistic non-drinkers were less likely to be male and had more autistic traits. Gender and level of autistic traits may be the most significant factors in predicting alcohol use in the autistic community.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista adulta, puede ser útil hablar de alcohol con calma y sin juzgar, y preguntar también por su ánimo, su ansiedad y su vida social, porque el consumo suele relacionarse con ellos. La evidencia es un estudio con encuesta en línea en el que participaron 237 adultos autistas. Quienes no bebían y quienes bebían de forma peligrosa mostraron más rasgos autistas, depresión y ansiedad que quienes bebían sin riesgo. Los límites: es una encuesta en un único momento, así que no demuestra causas, y no describe a cada persona.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult, it may help to talk about alcohol calmly and without judgement, and to ask also about their mood, anxiety and social life, since drinking seems linked to these. The evidence is an online survey study of 237 autistic adults. People who did not drink and people who drank hazardously scored higher on autistic traits, depression and anxiety than those who drank without hazard. Limits: it is a survey taken at one point in time, so it cannot show causes, and it does not describe every person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen kan det hjälpa att prata om alkohol lugnt och utan att döma, och att också fråga om humör, oro och socialt liv, eftersom drickandet verkar hänga ihop med dem. Underlaget är en webbenkätstudie med 237 autistiska vuxna. De som inte drack och de som drack riskabelt hade fler autistiska drag, mer depression och mer ångest än de som drack utan risk. Begränsningar: det är en enkät vid ett enda tillfälle, så den kan inte visa orsaker, och den beskriver inte varje person.

title: Autistic adults' subjective experiences of hoarding and self-injurious behaviors.
authors: Goldfarb Y, Zafrani O, Hedley D, Yaari M, Gal E
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Hoarding and self-injurious behaviors are relatively common in autism, but knowledge about their expressions in adulthood is scarce. Through interviews collecting subjective experiences of autistic adults, these behaviors were explored, and categorized to their underlying purposes. Findings portray the occurrence of these behaviors in the lives of autistic adults, their self-regulatory purposes, and their relationship to other behaviors in the domain of Restrictive and Repetitive Behaviors and Interests.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista acumula objetos o se hace daño, conviene preguntarle con calma qué función cumple para ella en ese momento, por ejemplo ayudarla a regularse, en lugar de centrarse solo en detener la conducta. Es un estudio con entrevistas a personas autistas adultas sobre sus experiencias subjetivas de acumulación y autolesiones, que se agruparon según su propósito. El resumen no detalla cuántas personas participaron ni da resultados concretos, y la experiencia de cada persona es distinta. Si te preocupa una autolesión, busca ayuda profesional: un médico, un servicio de salud o un servicio de crisis. Si hay peligro inmediato, llama al número de emergencias de tu país.
sheet.en: If an autistic person hoards objects or hurts themselves, it can help to ask, calmly, what the behavior does for them at that moment, such as helping them regulate, rather than only trying to stop it.
