This was an interview study with autistic adults about their own experiences of hoarding and self-injury, grouped by purpose. The abstract does not say how many people took part or give detailed results, and every person's experience differs. If you are worried about self-injury, seek professional help from a clinician, a health service or a crisis service. In immediate danger, call your country's emergency number.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person samlar på saker eller skadar sig själv kan du lugnt fråga vad beteendet gör för personen just då, till exempel om det hjälper till att reglera sig, i stället för att bara försöka stoppa det. Det här var en intervjustudie med autistiska vuxna om deras egna upplevelser av samlande och självskadebeteende, grupperade efter syfte. Sammanfattningen anger inte hur många som deltog eller några detaljerade resultat, och varje människas upplevelse är olika. Om du oroar dig för självskada, sök professionell hjälp hos en läkare, en vårdinstans eller en krisjour. Vid akut fara, ring ditt lands nödnummer.

title: Camouflaging in an everyday social context: An interpersonal recall study.
authors: Cook J, Crane L, Bourne L, Hull L, Mandy W
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Many autistic people report that, despite personal costs, they use strategies to hide their autistic characteristics or appear non-autistic at work, school or university, when speaking with health professionals, or while socialising with certain friends and family members. These strategies are often referred to as camouflaging. This study explores camouflaging during everyday social interactions. A total of 17 autistic adults were filmed taking part in a common everyday social situation - a conversation with a stranger. They then watched the video of this conversation with a researcher and answered questions about camouflaging. These autistic people told us that they (1) had a strong desire to socialise with and be valued by other people but, because of negative past experiences, they often felt unsure about their ability to do so; (2) used camouflaging to help them to socialise and be valued by others; (3) experienced negative consequences when camouflaging (e.g. fatigue, anxiety and difficulties in friendships); and (4) sometimes socialised in more autistic ways instead of camouflaging. This study shows us how autistic people often change their behaviour because of the way they are treated by nonautistic people and that autistic people may benefit from programmes that help them to socialise in more authentically autistic ways, but only if their autistic social behaviour is met with understanding and acceptance from non-autistic people.

sheet.es: Si la persona autista que acompañas parece agotada o ansiosa después de reuniones sociales, puede que haya estado camuflando: ocultando rasgos autistas para encajar. Ofrece espacios donde pueda socializar a su manera, sin corregir el contacto visual, los movimientos o los temas de interés, y deja tiempo de descanso después. El cambio también depende del entorno: la aceptación de las personas no autistas hace posible ser auténtico. Evidencia: estudio cualitativo en el que 17 adultos autistas fueron grabados conversando con un desconocido y luego comentaron el vídeo. Límites: muestra pequeña, solo adultos y una única situación; las experiencias pueden variar mucho entre personas.
sheet.en: If the autistic person you support seems exhausted or anxious after social time, they may have been camouflaging: hiding autistic traits to fit in. Offer spaces where they can socialise their own way, without correcting eye contact, movement or special interests, and plan rest afterwards. Change also depends on the environment: acceptance from non-autistic people is what makes being authentic possible. Evidence: a qualitative study in which 17 autistic adults were filmed talking with a stranger, then discussed the video with a researcher. Limits: a small sample, adults only and one type of situation; experiences can differ greatly between people.
sheet.sv: Om den autistiska person du stöttar verkar utmattad eller orolig efter sociala sammanhang kan hen ha kamouflerat: dolt autistiska drag för att passa in. Erbjud miljöer där hen kan umgås på sitt eget sätt, utan att rätta ögonkontakt, rörelser eller specialintressen, och planera vila efteråt. Förändring beror också på omgivningen: acceptans från icke-autistiska personer gör det möjligt att vara äkta. Evidens: en kvalitativ studie där 17 autistiska vuxna filmades i samtal med en främling och sedan diskuterade filmen med en forskare. Begränsningar: litet urval, bara vuxna och en enda typ av situation; upplevelser kan skilja sig mycket mellan personer.

title: Do animated triangles reveal a marked difficulty among autistic people with reading minds?
authors: Wilson AC
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic people are thought to have difficulty with mentalising (our drive to track and understand the minds of other people). Mentalising is often measured by the Frith-Happé Animations task, where individuals need to interpret the interactions of abstract shapes. This review article collated results from over 3000 people to assess how autistic people performed on the task. Analysis showed that autistic people tended to underperform compared to non-autistic people on the task, although the scale of the difference was moderate rather than large. Also, autistic people showed some difficulty with the non-mentalising as well as mentalising aspects of the task. These results raise questions about the scale and specificity of mentalising difficulties in autism. It also remains unclear how well mentalising difficulties account for the social challenges diagnostic of autism.

sheet.es: Si alguien da por hecho que tu hijo o familiar autista «no entiende la mente de los demás», esta revisión invita a cuestionarlo. En una prueba común con triángulos animados, las personas autistas obtuvieron de media puntuaciones algo más bajas, pero la diferencia fue moderada, no enorme, y también apareció en partes de la prueba que no tratan sobre mentes. En el día a día, conviene preguntar directamente cómo interpreta una situación, en lugar de suponer que no la entiende. Evidencia: revisión que reunió resultados de más de 3000 personas autistas y no autistas. Límites: se basa en una sola tarea de laboratorio y no aclara cómo se relaciona con la vida social real.
sheet.en: If someone assumes your autistic child or relative "can't read other minds", this review gives reason to question that. On a common task with animated triangles, autistic people scored somewhat lower on average, but the difference was moderate rather than large, and it also showed up in parts of the task that aren't about minds at all. In daily life, try asking directly how they understand a situation instead of assuming they don't. Evidence: a review pooling results from over 3,000 autistic and non-autistic people. Limits: it rests on one lab task, and it remains unclear how these scores relate to real-life social experiences.
sheet.sv: Om någon utgår från att ditt autistiska barn eller din autistiska anhörige "inte kan förstå andras tankar" ger den här översikten skäl att ifrågasätta det. På ett vanligt test med animerade trianglar fick autistiska personer i genomsnitt något lägre resultat, men skillnaden var måttlig snarare än stor och syntes även i delar av testet som inte handlar om tankar. I vardagen kan du fråga direkt hur personen uppfattar en situation i stället för att anta att den inte förstår. Evidens: en översikt som samlade resultat från över 3 000 autistiska och icke-autistiska personer. Begränsningar: den bygger på ett enda labbtest, och kopplingen till verkligt socialt liv är oklar.

title: Mental Health and Resilient Coping in Caregivers of Autistic Individuals during the COVID-19 Pandemic: Findings from the Families Facing COVID Study.
authors: Friesen KA, Weiss JA, Howe SJ, Kerns CM, McMorris CA
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders

title: A Self-Determination Theory Approach to Work Motivation of Autistic Adults: A Qualitative Exploratory Study.
authors: Goldfarb Y, Golan O, Gal E
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders

title: Effects of an attachment-based parent intervention on mothers of children with autism spectrum disorder: preliminary findings from a non-randomized controlled trial.
authors: Kubo N, Kitagawa M, Iwamoto S, Kishimoto T
journal: Child and adolescent psychiatry and mental health
abstract: Background Caregivers of children with autism spectrum disorders (ASD) often experience difficulties in responding appropriately to the needs of those children, who typically express attachment in distinct and nonconventional ways. This highlights the need for an attachment-based approach targeted at caregivers of children with ASD. Circle of Security Parenting (COSP), an attachment-based parenting program, is designed to increase caregivers' sensitivity to children's attachment needs. The aim of this study was to provide verification of the effectiveness of COSP in mothers of children with ASD. Methods This study was a non-randomized controlled trial. Sixty mothers of children with ASD aged 4-12 were recruited. Twenty mothers received the COSP intervention, while 40 did not. The characteristics of children in the control group were matched with those of the intervention group. To evaluate the outcomes of the intervention, changes in parental self-efficacy and mental health were assessed using the Tool to Measure Parenting Self-Efficacy (TOPSE) and the General Health Questionnaire-30 (GHQ-30). The children's improvement in emotional and behavioral problems was assessed from the mothers' perspective using the Child Behavior Checklist (CBCL). Both groups completed the assessments in parallel. Evaluations were compared between baseline (T1) and 6-month follow-up (T2). Results Scores for self-efficacy and mental health of mothers and behavior of children were significantly improved from T1 to T2 in the intervention group, but not in the control group. Participants' mental health was markedly worsened in the control group. Conclusion This study demonstrated that the COSP program for mothers of children with ASD improved their parental self-efficacy and mental health, and reduced their subjective sense of difficulties related to their children's behaviors. Our findings support the effectiveness of the attachment-based program for mothers of children with ASD, providing the groundwork for further studies of the attachment-based intervention for children with ASD and their families. Future studies with larger samples and randomization are also needed for direct evaluation of the improvement of children's attachment security, and for exploration of the synergistic relationship between various family support strategies and COSP. Trial Registration This trial was registered with the University Hospital Medical Information Network Clinical Trial Registry (No. UMIN000039574).

sheet.es: Si cuidas a un niño autista, un programa de crianza basado en el apego, como Circle of Security Parenting, puede ser una opción de apoyo para ti y merece que lo consultes. Se trata de aprender a reconocer cómo tu hijo expresa su necesidad de vínculo. Es un ensayo controlado no aleatorizado con 60 madres de niños autistas de 4-12 años: 20 hicieron el programa y 40 no. A los 6 meses, las madres del programa mostraron mejor autoeficacia y salud mental, y vieron menos dificultades en la conducta de sus hijos. Límites: no hubo asignación al azar, la muestra es pequeña y las conductas las valoraron las propias madres. No sirve como regla para todas las familias.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic child, an attachment-based parenting program such as Circle of Security Parenting may be a support option for you, and it is worth asking about. It focuses on learning to recognise how your child expresses their need for connection. This was a non-randomized controlled trial with 60 mothers of autistic children aged 4-12: 20 took the program and 40 did not. At 6 months, mothers in the program reported better parenting self-efficacy and mental health, and saw fewer difficulties in their children's behavior. Limits: families were not assigned by chance, the sample was small, and the mothers themselves rated the behavior. It is not a rule for every family.
sheet.sv: Om du har en autistisk Barn i din omsorg kan ett anknytningsbaserat föräldraprogram som Circle of Security Parenting vara ett stöd för dig, och det är värt att fråga om. Fokus ligger på att lära sig känna igen hur barnet uttrycker sitt behov av närhet. Studien var en icke-randomiserad kontrollerad studie med 60 mammor till autistiska barn i åldern 4-12: 20 deltog i programmet och 40 gjorde det inte. Efter 6 månader rapporterade mammorna i programmet bättre föräldraförmåga och psykisk hälsa, och upplevde färre svårigheter med barnens beteende. Begränsningar: familjerna lottades inte, gruppen var liten och mammorna bedömde själva beteendet. Resultatet gäller inte alla familjer.

title: The Effect of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy for Improving Psychological Well-Being in Parents of Individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorders: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
authors: Marino F, Failla C, Chilà P, Minutoli R, Puglisi A, Arnao AA, Pignolo L, Presti G, Pergolizzi F, Moderato P, Tartarisco G, Ruta L, Vagni D, Cerasa A, Pioggia G
abstract: Background Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) has been demonstrated as effective in improving psychological well-being in several clinical domains, but there is no evidence regarding the parents of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). Methods In this randomized controlled trial, we evaluated the efficacy of the ACT matrix behavioral protocol in comparison to the Parent Training (PT) program, measuring several primary and secondary outcomes prior to and following treatments. Twelve parents were randomly and equally assigned to two demographically matched groups wherein individuals underwent 24 weekly meetings of ACT protocol (experimental group) or conventional PT (control group). Results Parents enrolled in the ACT protocol demonstrated significant improvement in psychological flexibility, awareness states, personal values in everyday life, and parental stress, whereas reduced scores were elicited in parents' perceptions of their child's disruptive behaviors. Conclusions The results of this randomized controlled trial, if repeated with a large number of subjects, could open the way to include ACT protocols in daily practice to support the development of new parenting skills.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista y notas mucho estrés, quizá te ayude buscar apoyo psicológico para ti, como un programa basado en la aceptación y en tus valores personales. Es un ensayo controlado aleatorizado con 12 progenitores, repartidos en dos grupos: uno recibió 24 encuentros semanales de terapia de aceptación y compromiso (ACT) y otro un programa convencional de formación para padres. Quienes hicieron ACT mostraron mejoras en flexibilidad psicológica, atención plena a lo vivido, valores personales y estrés parental. Límites: el grupo es muy pequeño y los autores indican que hay que repetirlo con más personas. No garantiza el mismo resultado en tu caso.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic person and feel a lot of stress, it may help to look for psychological support for yourself, such as a programme built around acceptance and your personal values. This was a randomized controlled trial with 12 parents split into two groups: one had 24 weekly meetings of acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT), the other a conventional parent training programme. Parents who did ACT showed improvements in psychological flexibility, awareness, personal values and parental stress. Limits: the group was very small, and the authors say it needs repeating with more people. It does not guarantee the same result for you.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person och känner mycket stress kan det hjälpa att söka psykologiskt stöd för egen del, till exempel ett program som bygger på acceptans och dina personliga värderingar. Det var en randomiserad kontrollerad studie med 12 föräldrar i två grupper: den ena fick 24 veckomöten med acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT), den andra ett vanligt föräldraträningsprogram. De som fick ACT visade förbättring i psykologisk flexibilitet, medvetenhet, personliga värderingar och föräldrastress. Begränsningar: gruppen var mycket liten, och forskarna menar att studien behöver upprepas med fler personer. Den garanterar inte samma resultat för dig.

title: Mental health of parents of children with autism spectrum disorder during COVID-19 pandemic: A systematic review.
authors: Yılmaz B, Azak M, Şahin N
abstract: Background Children diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) may have great difficulties when their routines change, and this may affect the psychological well-being of their parents. For this reason, it is important to examine studies that address the mental health of parents in order to adapt to the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic. Aim To determine the mental health status of parents with children diagnosed with ASD in the COVID-19 pandemic. Methods The study, which is a systematic review, was conducted between December 15, 2020 and December 30, 2020 by scanning articles in English. The Scopus, Science Direct, PubMed, Cochrane, Web of Science, and Google Scholar databases were used for scanning. The keywords COVID-19 AND ("autism" OR "autistic" OR "autism spectrum disorder") AND parent AND ("mental health" OR "anxiety" OR "stress") were used in the search process. The inclusion criteria in the study were findings regarding the mental health of parents with children diagnosed with ASD in the COVID-19 pandemic, addressing their anxiety and stress situations, being a research article, and accessing the full text of the article. Results In the study, a total of 6389 articles were reached, and the full texts of 173 articles were evaluated for eligibility. After the articles excluded by the full-text search were eliminated, 12 studies involving 7105 parents were included in the analysis. The findings obtained from the articles containing data on mental health in the COVID-19 pandemic of parents with children with autism spectrum disorder were discussed in three groups. These were findings on the experiences of parents with children with ASD in the COVID-19 pandemic regarding the areas where parents with children with ASD need support in the COVID-19 pandemic and methods of coping with the COVID-19 pandemic for parents with children with ASD. In the systematic review, it was determined that the anxiety and stress of the parents increased, they needed more support compared to the pre-pandemic period, and they had difficulty coping. Conclusion In this systematic review, it was concluded that the COVID-19 pandemic negatively affected the mental health of the parents of children with ASD.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista y los cambios de rutina te han dejado con más ansiedad o estrés, no es un fallo tuyo: es una reacción frecuente. Buscar apoyo, de otras familias o de profesionales, es una medida razonable. Esta revisión sistemática analizó 12 estudios con 7105 madres y padres de niños con diagnóstico de autismo durante la pandemia de COVID-19 y encontró más ansiedad y estrés, más necesidad de apoyo y dificultad para afrontarlo. Como limitaciones, solo incluyó artículos en inglés, se centró en un periodo excepcional y no muestra que le pase a todas las familias.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic person and routine changes have left you more anxious or stressed, that is not your failing: it is a common reaction. Reaching out for support, from other families or professionals, is a reasonable step. This systematic review looked at 12 studies with 7105 parents of children diagnosed with autism during the COVID-19 pandemic. It found increased anxiety and stress, a greater need for support, and difficulty coping. Its limits: it included only articles in English, covered an exceptional period, and does not show that every family experienced this.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person och rutinförändringar har gjort dig mer orolig eller stressad är det inget misslyckande: det är en vanlig reaktion. Att söka stöd, hos andra familjer eller yrkesverksamma, är ett rimligt steg. Den här systematiska översikten granskade 12 studier med 7105 föräldrar till barn med autismdiagnos under covid-19-pandemin. Den fann ökad oro och stress, större behov av stöd och svårigheter att hantera situationen. Begränsningar: bara artiklar på engelska ingick, perioden var ovanlig och resultaten visar inte att alla familjer upplevde detta.

title: "No Way Out Except From External Intervention": First-Hand Accounts of Autistic Inertia.
authors: Buckle KL, Leadbitter K, Poliakoff E, Gowen E
abstract: This study, called for by autistic people and led by an autistic researcher, is the first to explore 'autistic inertia,' a widespread and often debilitating difficulty acting on their intentions. Previous research has considered initiation only in the context of social interaction or experimental conditions. This study is unique in considering difficulty initiating tasks of any type in real life settings, and by gathering qualitative data directly from autistic people. Four face-to-face and 2 online (text) focus groups were conducted with 32 autistic adults (19 female, 8 male, and 5 other), aged 23-64 who were able to express their internal experiences in words. They articulate in detail the actions they have difficulty with, what makes it easier or harder to act, and the impact on their lives. Thematic analysis of the transcripts found four overarching themes: descriptions of inertia, scaffolding to support action, the influence of wellbeing, and the impact on day-to-day activities. Participants described difficulty starting, stopping and changing activities that was not within their conscious control. While difficulty with planning was common, a subset of participants described a profound impairment in initiating even simple actions more suggestive of a movement disorder. Prompting and compatible activity in the environment promoted action, while mental health difficulties and stress exacerbated difficulties. Inertia had pervasive effects on participants' day-to-day activities and wellbeing. This overdue research opens the door to many areas of further investigation to better understand autistic inertia and effective support strategies.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista no logra empezar, parar o cambiar de actividad, conviene creer que no lo controla de forma consciente. Puede ayudar ofrecer un aviso o apoyo externo y facilitar un entorno donde haya actividad compatible con lo que quiere hacer. El estrés y el malestar emocional pueden empeorarlo. La evidencia es un estudio cualitativo con grupos de discusión, con 32 personas autistas adultas de 23-64 años que podían expresar sus experiencias con palabras. Sus límites: no prueba qué estrategias funcionan mejor y puede no reflejar a quienes no se expresan con palabras ni a todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person struggles to start, stop or switch activities, it helps to accept that this is not within their conscious control. Offering a prompt or outside support may help, as may an environment with activity that fits what they want to do. Stress and poor wellbeing can make it harder. The evidence is a qualitative study using focus groups with 32 autistic adults aged 23-64 who could express their inner experiences in words. Its limits: it does not test which supports work best, and it may not reflect people who do not use words or everyone's experience.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person har svårt att börja, sluta eller byta aktivitet hjälper det att utgå från att hen inte kan styra det medvetet. En påminnelse eller stöd utifrån kan hjälpa, liksom en miljö med aktivitet som passar det hen vill göra. Stress och dåligt mående kan göra det svårare. Underlaget är en kvalitativ studie med fokusgrupper med 32 autistiska vuxna i åldern 23-64 som kunde uttrycka sina upplevelser i ord. Begränsningar: den testar inte vilka stöd som fungerar bäst och speglar kanske inte personer som inte använder ord eller alla människors erfarenhet.

title: Association between Social Skills and Motor Skills in Individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review.
authors: Ohara R, Kanejima Y, Kitamura M, Izawa KP
journal: European journal of investigation in health, psychology and education
abstract: Social communication and motor skill deficits are prevalent characteristics of individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). This systematic research review investigates whether and how broad social skills and motor skills may be related among individuals with ASD. We performed a PubMed search of articles written in English, using these study inclusion criteria: (a) an association between social and motor and skills among individuals previously diagnosed with autism; (b) one or more social skills measures were used; and (c) one or more measures of gross or fine motor skills were used. We classified data into two categories, and we based the association of these variables on correlation coefficients, p -values, coefficients of determination, and authors' description of "may be associated" and "may not be associated." Despite heterogeneity among these relevant studies, a highly likely association between social and motor skills emerged. Of a total of 16 studies reviewed, 12 reported associations between these skill sets. Three studies reported that fine motor skills had a stronger relationship with social skills than did gross motor skills. Among the gross motor skills associated with social skills, object control skills seemed most closely linked to social skills. Among fine motor skills, manual dexterity seemed to most closely related to social skills.

sheet.es: Si a tu hijo o hija autista le cuesta coordinar movimientos, como lanzar y atrapar una pelota o usar las manos con precisión, esto puede influir en cómo participa en juegos con otras personas. Mañana puedes ofrecer juegos sencillos con objetos (pasarse una pelota, construir juntos) a su ritmo, sin presión y valorando su forma de participar. Las ayudas motrices, como la terapia ocupacional, pueden facilitar momentos compartidos. Es una revisión sistemática de 16 estudios con personas autistas; 12 encontraron una relación entre habilidades motrices y sociales, sobre todo motricidad fina y manejo de objetos. Sus límites: los estudios eran muy distintos, solo se buscó en una base de datos en inglés, y una asociación no demuestra causa.
sheet.en: If your autistic child finds coordination harder, such as throwing and catching a ball or precise hand movements, this may shape how they join in play with others. Tomorrow you could offer simple object-based games (rolling a ball back and forth, building together) at their pace, without pressure, and value however they choose to take part. Motor support, such as occupational therapy, may help create more shared moments. This is a systematic review of 16 studies with autistic people; 12 found a link between motor and social skills, especially fine motor skills and object control. Limits: the studies varied widely, only one English-language database was searched, and an association does not prove cause.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn tycker att koordination är svårt, som att kasta och fånga en boll eller göra precisa handrörelser, kan det påverka hur barnet deltar i lek med andra. I morgon kan du erbjuda enkla lekar med föremål (rulla en boll fram och tillbaka, bygga tillsammans) i barnets takt, utan press, och uppskatta det sätt barnet väljer att delta på. Motoriskt stöd, till exempel arbetsterapi, kan ge fler delade stunder. Detta är en systematisk översikt av 16 studier med autistiska personer; 12 fann ett samband mellan motoriska och sociala färdigheter, särskilt finmotorik och bollhantering. Begränsningar: studierna skilde sig mycket åt, bara en engelskspråkig databas söktes och ett samband bevisar inte orsak.

title: Social identities and mental well-being in autistic adults.
authors: Maitland CA, Rhodes S, O'Hare A, Stewart ME
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Social identities are groups that we are part of and influence how we think about ourselves. However, up until now there has been little examination of the groups that autistic people may belong to, and how these groups may influence their mental health. This survey-based study investigated whether autistic adults answer questions about social groups in a similar way to non-autistic non-autistic adults, including the types and number of social groups they may belong to, and whether these are associated with depression, anxiety and positive traits of mental well-being. In total, 184 autistic adults completed an online survey with questionnaires about their demographics, social groups and mental health. The results found that autistic adults reported on their social groups similarly to non-autistic people. There was a variety in the types and numbers of groups that autistic adults identified with. Some participants reported having no groups that they identified with, whereas others reported up to four groups. These included other autistic people, their family, friends, work colleagues and activity clubs among others. Autistic adults who felt connected with more groups reported better mental well-being. Feelings of connection to other autistic people and the family were also associated with better mental well-being. These results show that it is important for autistic people to be given opportunity to be part of groups that are meaningful to them, as this may be beneficial for their mental health.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista adulta, puede ayudar ofrecerle oportunidades, sin presión, de formar parte de grupos que le resulten significativos: otras personas autistas, la familia, amistades, compañeros de trabajo o clubes de actividades. Sentirse conectado con más grupos, y especialmente con otras personas autistas y con la familia, se asoció con un mejor bienestar mental. Lo importante es que el grupo tenga sentido para ella, no la cantidad impuesta. La evidencia viene de una encuesta en línea respondida por 184 adultos autistas. Sus límites: muestra una asociación en un solo momento, no demuestra causa y efecto, y quienes responden encuestas en línea pueden no representar a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult, it may help to offer low-pressure opportunities to belong to groups that feel meaningful to them: other autistic people, family, friends, work colleagues or activity clubs. Feeling connected to more groups, and especially to other autistic people and to family, was linked with better mental well-being. What matters is that the group feels right to the person, not reaching a set number. The evidence comes from an online survey completed by 184 autistic adults. Its limits: it shows an association at one point in time, cannot prove cause and effect, and people who answer online surveys may not represent all autistic people.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen kan det hjälpa att erbjuda möjligheter, utan press, att höra till grupper som känns meningsfulla för personen: andra autistiska personer, familjen, vänner, arbetskamrater eller aktivitetsklubbar. Att känna samhörighet med fler grupper, och särskilt med andra autistiska personer och familjen, hängde ihop med bättre psykiskt välbefinnande. Det viktiga är att gruppen känns rätt för personen, inte att nå ett visst antal. Underlaget är en webbenkät som besvarades av 184 autistiska vuxna. Begränsningar: studien visar ett samband vid ett enda tillfälle, kan inte bevisa orsak och verkan, och de som svarar på webbenkäter representerar kanske inte alla autistiska personer.

title: Feeding and eating problems in children and adolescents with autism: A scoping review.
authors: Baraskewich J, von Ranson KM, McCrimmon A, McMorris CA
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Feeding problems, such as picky eating and food avoidance, are common in youth with autism. Other, broader difficulties with feeding and eating (eating disorder symptoms such as restricting food intake or preoccupation with body shape or weight and insistence on specific food presentation) are also common in autistic individuals. Here, we describe the nature and extent of feeding and eating problems in youth with autism. We found no common characteristics (such as severity of autism symptoms) that best describe autistic youth who experience problems with feeding or eating. Almost all studies we reviewed focused on problems with feeding (selective or picky eating), and only a few studies focused on eating disorder symptoms (concern with weight, shape, and/or body image). However, some researchers reported that eating disorder symptoms may occur more often in autistic individuals compared to their peers without autism. Many studies used the terms "feeding" and "eating" problems interchangeably, but understanding the difference between these problems is important for researchers to be consistent, as well as for proper identification and treatment. We suggest future researchers use "eating problems" when behaviors involve preoccupation with food, eating, or body image, and "feeding problems" when this preoccupation is absent. We highlight the importance of understanding whether feeding or eating problems are separate from autism traits, and the role of caregivers and other adults in the child's treatment. Considerations for health-care providers to assist with diagnosis and treatment are also provided.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija come pocos alimentos o necesita que la comida se presente de una forma concreta, no estás solo: es muy común en jóvenes autistas. Merece la pena observar si hay preocupación por el peso, la figura o la comida, porque eso puede ser algo distinto y conviene comentarlo con un profesional de salud. Anota qué come, cómo y cuándo; esa información ayuda en una consulta. Esta revisión de alcance reunió estudios sobre niños y adolescentes autistas y no encontró un rasgo común que prediga estas dificultades. Su límite: casi todos los estudios trataban la selectividad alimentaria, pocos los síntomas de trastornos alimentarios, y usaban términos de forma inconsistente.
sheet.en: If your child eats a narrow range of foods or needs food presented a certain way, you are not alone: this is very common in autistic young people. It is worth noticing whether there is also worry about weight, body shape or food itself, because that may be something different and is worth raising with a health professional. Jotting down what, how and when your child eats can help at an appointment. This scoping review gathered studies on autistic children and adolescents and found no single trait that predicts these difficulties. Its limit: almost all studies looked at selective eating, few at eating disorder symptoms, and terms were used inconsistently.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn äter få sorters mat eller behöver att maten serveras på ett visst sätt är du inte ensam: det är mycket vanligt hos autistiska unga. Var uppmärksam på om det också finns oro kring vikt, kroppsform eller själva maten, eftersom det kan vara något annat och är värt att ta upp med vården. Att anteckna vad, hur och när barnet äter kan hjälpa vid ett besök. Denna översikt samlade studier om autistiska barn och ungdomar och fann inget enskilt drag som förutsäger svårigheterna. Begränsning: nästan alla studier handlade om selektivt ätande, få om ätstörningssymtom, och begreppen användes inkonsekvent.

title: A Meta-analysis of Outcome Studies of Autistic Adults: Quantifying Effect Size, Quality, and Meta-regression.
authors: Mason D, Capp SJ, Stewart GR, Kempton MJ, Glaser K, Howlin P, Happé F
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Longitudinal studies have generally reported poor outcomes in adulthood for the majority of individuals (c.50-60%) with autism. Several factors putatively predict outcome (e.g. IQ), but findings remain mixed. This paper presents an updated meta-analysis of autism outcome studies and extends previous findings with additional analyses (including meta-regression). A total of 4088 records was screened and 18 studies, involving 1199 individuals, were included in the quantitative analysis. Estimated percentages indicated that 20.0% of participants were rated as having a good outcome, 26.6% a fair outcome, and 49.3% a poor outcome. Meta-regression indicated that lower IQ in adulthood was predictive of poor outcome; other meta-regression models did not survive correction for multiple comparisons. Overall, outcomes for autistic people are on average poor, and higher IQ appears to be protective against having a poor outcome. The limitations of current constructs of outcome are discussed.

sheet.es: Cuando leas cifras sobre «resultados» en la vida adulta, recuerda que describen medias de grupos y no el futuro de una persona autista concreta. Lo útil es fijarse en qué apoyos y entornos le ayudan a vivir bien. Es un metaanálisis que reunió 18 estudios con 1199 personas autistas. Los autores estimaron que el 49.3% tuvo un resultado malo y que un CI más bajo en la edad adulta se asoció con peor resultado. Limitaciones: los propios autores discuten que las formas actuales de medir el «resultado» son limitadas, y las asociaciones no explican causas ni valen para cada persona.
sheet.en: When you read figures about adult "outcomes", remember they describe group averages, not the future of any one autistic person. A more useful focus is which supports and environments help this person live well. This is a meta-analysis that pooled 18 studies involving 1199 autistic people. The authors estimated that 49.3% had a poor outcome, and that lower IQ in adulthood was linked to poorer outcome. Limits: the authors themselves discuss that current ways of defining "outcome" are limited, and these associations do not explain causes or apply to every person.
sheet.sv: När du läser siffror om vuxnas "utfall" är det bra att minnas att de beskriver gruppmedelvärden, inte framtiden för en enskild autistisk person. Mer användbart är att fundera på vilka stöd och miljöer som hjälper just den här personen att leva väl. Detta är en metaanalys som sammanställde 18 studier med 1199 autistiska personer. Forskarna uppskattade att 49.3% hade ett dåligt utfall och att lägre IQ i vuxen ålder hängde samman med sämre utfall. Begränsningar: författarna diskuterar själva att dagens sätt att definiera "utfall" är begränsade, och sambanden förklarar inte orsaker och gäller inte alla.

title: Interoceptive training to target anxiety in autistic adults (ADIE): A single-center, superiority randomized controlled trial.
authors: Quadt L, Garfinkel SN, Mulcahy JS, Larsson DE, Silva M, Jones AM, Strauss C, Critchley HD
abstract: Background This trial tested if a novel therapy, Aligning Dimensions of Interoceptive Experience (ADIE), reduces anxiety in autistic adults. ADIE targets the association of anxiety with mismatch between subjective and behavioral measures of an individual's interocepti ve sensitivity to bodily signals, including heartbeats. Methods In this superiority randomized controlled trial, autistic adults (18-65 years) from clinical and community settings in Southern England were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive six sessions of ADIE or an active 'exteroceptive' control therapy (emotional prosody identification). Researchers conducting outcome assessments were blind to allocation. ADIE combines two modified heartbeat detection tasks with performance feedback and physical activity manipulation that transiently increases cardiac arousal. Participants were followed-up one-week (T1) and 3-months post-intervention (T2). The primary outcome was Spielberger Trait Anxiety Score (STAI-T) at T2. Outcomes were assessed on an intention-to-treat basis using multiple imputation for dealing with missing values. This trial was registered at International Standard Randomized Controlled Trial Registry, ISRCTN14848787. Findings Between July 01, 2017, and December 31, 2019, 121 participants were randomly allocated to ADIE ( n = 61) or prosody ( n = 60) intervention groups. Data at T1 was provided by 85 (70%) participants (46 [75%] ADIE; 39 [65%] prosody). Data at T2 was provided by 61 (50%) participants (36 [59%] ADIE; 25 [42%] prosody). One adverse event (cardiac anxiety following ADIE) was recorded. A statistically significant group effect of ADIE on trait anxiety continued at T2 (estimated mean difference 3•23 [95% CI 1•13 to 5•29]; d = 0•30 [95% CI 0•09 to 0•51]; p = 0•005) with 31% of ADIE group participants meeting trial criteria for recovery (compared to 16% in the control group). Interpretation ADIE can reduce anxiety in autistic adults, putatively improving regulatory control over internal stimuli. With little reliance on language and emotional insight, ADIE may constitute an inclusive intervention. Funding mq Transforming Mental Health PsyImpact Grant .

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta quiere trabajar la ansiedad, puede preguntar a un profesional por terapias que ayuden a percibir las señales del cuerpo, como los latidos del corazón, y que no dependan mucho del lenguaje. Este ensayo aleatorizado incluyó a 121 personas autistas adultas, que recibieron seis sesiones de ADIE o de una terapia de control. A los 3 meses, la ansiedad fue menor en el grupo ADIE: el 31% cumplió los criterios de recuperación del ensayo, frente al 16% del grupo de control. Límites: solo 61 personas (50%) aportaron datos a los 3 meses, se registró un efecto adverso (ansiedad cardíaca tras ADIE) y el resultado no vale para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult wants support with anxiety, they could ask a professional about therapies that build awareness of body signals, such as heartbeats, and that rely little on language. This randomized trial included 121 autistic adults who received six sessions of either ADIE or a control therapy. At 3 months, anxiety was lower in the ADIE group: 31% met the trial's criteria for recovery, compared with 16% in the control group. Limits: only 61 people (50%) provided data at 3 months, one adverse event (cardiac anxiety after ADIE) was recorded, and results will not apply to everyone.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen vill få stöd med ångest kan hen fråga en yrkesperson om terapier som tränar uppmärksamhet på kroppens signaler, som hjärtslag, och som inte kräver mycket språk. I denna randomiserade studie deltog 121 autistiska vuxna som fick sex sessioner av antingen ADIE eller en kontrollterapi. Efter 3 månader var ångesten lägre i ADIE-gruppen: 31% uppfyllde studiens kriterier för återhämtning, jämfört med 16% i kontrollgruppen. Begränsningar: bara 61 personer (50%) lämnade data efter 3 månader, en biverkning (hjärtångest efter ADIE) registrerades, och resultaten gäller inte alla.

title: Cognitive, Language, and Behavioral Outcomes in Children With Autism Spectrum Disorders Exposed to Early Comprehensive Treatment Models: A Meta-Analysis and Meta-Regression.
authors: Shi B, Wu W, Dai M, Zeng J, Luo J, Cai L, Wan B, Jing J
abstract: Background: Early comprehensive treatment models (CTMs) have been developed as effective treatments for children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Numerous studies have suggested that CTMs can improve short-term outcomes, but little is known about precise outcome information in childhood. The current meta-analysis reviewed studies reporting broader outcomes in children with ASD who had ever participated in a CTM and examined the predictors of developmental gains. Methods: We searched eight databases up to June 13, 2019, for relevant trials and natural experiments. Longitudinal studies were selected if they investigated the outcomes of CTMs. Two meta-analyses were undertaken to provide a summary estimate of change in treatment outcomes and to evaluate the effect of CTMs; one used the standardized mean change between the pretest and posttest, and the other was a classical meta-analysis. Stratified and random-effects meta-regression analyses were performed to search for outcome differences among studies. Results: Eighteen intervention studies (involving 495 children with ASD) met all the inclusion criteria: 12 used early intensive behavioral intervention (EIBI), and two used the Early Start Denver Model (ESDM). Outcomes were categorized into three parts: cognitive, language and behavioral (e.g., adaptive functioning and symptomatology). Overall, most children with ASD who had ever participated in an early CTM made gains in many areas of functioning, especially in terms of symptom- and language-related outcomes. Stratified analyses indicated that the ESDM displayed the largest effect on IQ improvement (ES = 1.37, 95% CI: 0.95 to 1.80), while EIBI was more effective for symptom reduction (ES = -1.27, 95% CI: -1.96 to -0.58). Further, meta-regression suggested that interventions with parent involvement, higher intensity, and longer treatment hours yielded greater improvements in IQ and social adaptive functioning, respectively. Conclusion: The results demonstrate a positive association between CTMs and better prognosis in childhood, especially regarding symptoms, and language. However, most extant research involves small, non-randomized studies, preventing definitive conclusions from being drawn. Clearly, the outcomes of children with ASD are still far from normal, especially with respect to adaptive functioning, and the four mediating variables pertaining to treatment elements can affect their gains, including approach, implementer, intensity, and total treatment hours. Systematic Review Registration: [www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO], identifier [CRD42019146859].

sheet.es: Si valora un programa de intervención temprana, puede preguntar cuánta participación familiar incluye, qué objetivos persigue y si respeta el ritmo, las preferencias y el bienestar de su hijo o hija autista. Esta revisión con metaanálisis reunió 18 estudios con 495 niños y niñas autistas que participaron en modelos de tratamiento integral temprano; la mayoría mostró avances, sobre todo en lenguaje y síntomas. Los límites: casi todos los estudios eran pequeños y no aleatorizados, por lo que no permiten conclusiones definitivas, y los resultados no valen para todas las personas. Además, medir los "síntomas" no equivale a medir el bienestar.
sheet.en: If you are weighing an early intervention program, you can ask how much family involvement it includes, what goals it pursues, and whether it respects your autistic child's pace, preferences and wellbeing. This meta-analysis combined 18 studies with 495 autistic children who took part in early comprehensive treatment models; most made gains, especially in language and symptom-related outcomes. Limits: most studies were small and non-randomized, so no firm conclusions can be drawn, and results do not apply to every person. Also, measuring "symptoms" is not the same as measuring wellbeing.
sheet.sv: Om du överväger ett tidigt insatsprogram kan du fråga hur mycket föräldradeltagande det ingår, vilka mål det har och om det respekterar ditt autistiska barns tempo, önskemål och välmående. Denna metaanalys sammanställde 18 studier med 495 autistiska barn som deltog i tidiga omfattande behandlingsmodeller; de flesta gjorde framsteg, särskilt i språk och symtomrelaterade mått. Begränsningar: de flesta studier var små och icke-randomiserade, så säkra slutsatser kan inte dras, och resultaten gäller inte alla. Att mäta "symtom" är dessutom inte samma sak som att mäta välmående.

title: Improving the measurement of alexithymia in autistic adults: a psychometric investigation of the 20-item Toronto Alexithymia Scale and generation of a general alexithymia factor score using item response theory.
authors: Williams ZJ, Gotham KO
abstract: Background Alexithymia, a personality trait characterized by difficulties interpreting emotional states, is commonly elevated in autistic adults, and a growing body of literature suggests that this trait underlies several cognitive and emotional differences previously attributed to autism. Although questionnaires such as the 20-item Toronto Alexithymia Scale (TAS-20) are frequently used to measure alexithymia in the autistic population, few studies have investigated the psychometric properties of these questionnaires in autistic adults, including whether differential item functioning (I-DIF) exists between autistic and general population adults. Methods This study is a revised version of a previous article that was retracted due to copyright concerns (Williams and Gotham in Mol Autism 12:1-40). We conducted an in-depth psychometric analysis of the TAS-20 in a large sample of 743 cognitively able autistic adults recruited from the Simons Foundation SPARK participant pool and 721 general population controls enrolled in a large international psychological study. The factor structure of the TAS-20 was examined using confirmatory factor analysis, and item response theory was used to generate a subset of the items that were strong indicators of a "general alexithymia" factor. Correlations between alexithymia and other clinical outcomes were used to assess the nomological validity of the new alexithymia score in the SPARK sample. Results The TAS-20 did not exhibit adequate model fit in either the autistic or general population samples. Empirically driven item reduction was undertaken, resulting in an 8-item general alexithymia factor score (GAFS-8, with "TAS" no longer referenced due to copyright) with sound psychometric properties and practically ignorable I-DIF between diagnostic groups. Correlational analyses indicated that GAFS-8 scores, as derived from the TAS-20, meaningfully predict autistic trait levels, repetitive behaviors, and depression symptoms, even after controlling for trait neuroticism. The GAFS-8 also presented no meaningful decrement in nomological validity over the full TAS-20 in autistic participants. Limitations Limitations of the current study include a sample of autistic adults that was majority female, later diagnosed, and well educated; clinical and control groups drawn from different studies with variable measures; only 16 of the TAS-20 items being administered to the non-autistic sample; and an inability to test several other important psychometric characteristics of the GAFS-8, including sensitivity to change and I-DIF across multiple administrations. Conclusions These results indicate the potential of the GAFS-8 to robustly measure alexithymia in both autistic and non-autistic adults. A free online score calculator has been created to facilitate the use of norm-referenced GAFS-8 latent trait scores in research applications (available at https://asdmeasures.shinyapps.io/alexithymia ).

sheet.es: Si una persona autista quiere entender mejor cómo identifica y describe sus emociones, conviene que quien use un cuestionario sobre alexitimia sepa que el habitual (TAS-20) quizá no sea el más fiable y que se ha propuesto una versión más corta de 8 ítems (GAFS-8). Es un estudio de investigación con 743 adultos autistas y 721 adultos de la población general. Sus límites: la muestra autista era mayoritariamente femenina, diagnosticada tarde y con estudios altos, y los grupos venían de estudios distintos. Además, la nueva escala aún no se ha probado para medir cambios. No sustituye una valoración profesional ni sirve para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person wants to understand how they notice and describe emotions, it helps to know that the commonly used alexithymia questionnaire (TAS-20) may not measure well, and a shorter 8-item version (GAFS-8) has been proposed. This was a research study with 743 autistic adults and 721 adults from the general population. Its limits: the autistic sample was mostly female, diagnosed later in life and well educated, and the groups came from different studies. The new scale has also not yet been tested for measuring change. It does not replace a professional assessment and may not fit everyone.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person vill förstå hur hen uppfattar och beskriver känslor är det bra att veta att det vanliga alexitymiformuläret (TAS-20) kanske inte mäter så bra, och att en kortare version med 8 frågor (GAFS-8) har föreslagits. Det är en forskningsstudie med 743 autistiska vuxna och 721 vuxna ur allmänbefolkningen. Begränsningar: den autistiska gruppen var mest kvinnor, diagnostiserade sent och högutbildade, och grupperna kom från olika studier. Den nya skalan har inte heller testats för att mäta förändring. Den ersätter inte en professionell bedömning och passar inte nödvändigtvis alla.

title: Overcoming the Double Empathy Problem Within Pairs of Autistic and Non-autistic Adults Through the Contemplation of Serious Literature.
authors: Chapple M, Davis P, Billington J, Myrick JA, Ruddock C, Corcoran R
abstract: Recent research based on the needs of the autistic community has explored the frequent social misunderstandings that arise between autistic and non-autistic people, known as the double empathy problem. Double empathy understandings require both groups to respect neurodiversity by focussing on individuality across groups. This study aimed to explore how literature, through its ability to uncover nuanced emotional response differences between readers, could facilitate double empathy understandings within pairs of autistic and non-autistic adults. A longitudinal, qualitative design was used, with 4 gender-matched pairs. Participants read Of Mice and Men for 1 week, whilst completing a structured, reflective diary. This was followed by 4 one-hour paired reading sessions, where pairs discussed the book and their reflections in depth. Participants were then invited to a final one-on-one interview to discuss their thoughts and experiences of the paired reading sessions. Thematic and literary analysis of the session and interview data revealed four themes (1) The Book as Social Oil; (2) From a World of Difference to a World of Affinity; (3) Emotional Intelligence: From Thinking About to Feeling with; and (4) From Overwhelming to Overcoming. All participants reported having achieved an individualised view of one another to explore their nuanced differences. The non-autistic group reported a more sensitive understanding of what it means to be autistic, while the autistic group overcame concerns about non-autistic people stereotyping autism, and instead reported feeling valued and accommodated by their non-autistic partners.

sheet.es: Si quieres favorecer la comprensión mutua entre una persona autista y una no autista, prueba una actividad compartida con un tema de conversación, como leer el mismo libro y comentarlo juntas, sin prisa y con apoyos. Evidencia: estudio cualitativo con 4 parejas de adultos autistas y no autistas del mismo género. Leyeron Of Mice and Men durante 1 semana con un diario, tuvieron 4 sesiones de lectura en pareja de una hora y una entrevista final. Todas las personas dijeron que llegaron a verse de forma más individual. Límites: la muestra es muy pequeña, solo adultos y un único libro, así que no sirve como regla para todas las personas ni sabemos si funcionaría en otros contextos.
sheet.en: If you want to support mutual understanding between an autistic and a non-autistic person, try a shared activity that gives them something to talk about, such as reading the same book and discussing it together, at an unhurried pace and with supports. Evidence: a qualitative study with 4 gender-matched pairs of autistic and non-autistic adults. They read Of Mice and Men for 1 week while keeping a diary, then had 4 one-hour paired reading sessions and a final interview. All participants said they came to see each other more as individuals. Limits: the sample is very small, only adults and one book, so it is not a rule for everyone and we cannot say it would work in other settings.
sheet.sv: Vill du stödja ömsesidig förståelse mellan en autistisk och en icke-autistisk person kan ni prova en gemensam aktivitet med något att prata om, till exempel att läsa samma bok och diskutera den tillsammans, i lugn takt och med stöd. Evidens: en kvalitativ studie med 4 könsmatchade par av autistiska och icke-autistiska vuxna. De läste Of Mice and Men under 1 vecka med dagbok, hade sedan 4 parläsningar på en timme och en avslutande intervju. Alla deltagare sa att de kom att se varandra mer som individer. Begränsningar: urvalet är mycket litet, enbart vuxna och en enda bok, så det är ingen regel för alla och vi vet inte om det fungerar i andra sammanhang.

title: Personal Identity After an Autism Diagnosis: Relationships With Self-Esteem, Mental Wellbeing, and Diagnostic Timing.
authors: Corden K, Brewer R, Cage E
abstract: Adults are increasingly seeking autism diagnoses, although less is known about their experiences of diagnosis and personal identity (i.e., autism as part of "me"), and how this relates to self-esteem and wellbeing. One-hundred and fifty-one autistic adults completed an online survey including measures of self-esteem, psychological wellbeing, and autistic personal identity, which considered whether participants took pride in or were dissatisfied with being autistic. Fifty-four participants answered a qualitative question about the impact of receiving an autism diagnosis on their sense of self. Regression analyses found that greater time elapsed since diagnosis related to less dissatisfaction with autistic personal identity. We also found that more dissatisfaction with autistic personal identity predicted lower self-esteem, and more autism pride predicted higher self-esteem. Content analysis of participants' experiences supported the quantitative findings and was suggestive of an emotive post-diagnostic adjustment process. Future research should aim to identify ways to promote the development of a positive autistic personal identity post-diagnosis in adulthood.

title: The Use of Analog and Digital Games for Autism Interventions.
authors: Atherton G, Cross L
abstract: Many interventions that target improvements in social communication and other cognitive, learning, and physical issues have been developed to help autistic people. The gamification of interventions offers an alternative approach to fostering and assessing desired behaviors and cognitions in a more naturalistic and emergent setting. In this scoping review aimed at educators, practitioners, and parents of those with autism, we detail studies that have tested game-based approaches to improving the lives of autistic children, adolescents, and adults, focusing on how research into gamification and autism can both progress and can be progressed and implemented. We offer parents, professionals and academics resources to incorporate game-based psycho-educational programs into their current practice.

sheet.es: Si quieres probar juegos, de mesa o digitales, como apoyo para la comunicación social o el aprendizaje, puedes empezar por uno que a la persona autista le interese y observar cómo lo vive. Si le gusta, puedes seguir; si le agobia, puedes parar. Es una revisión de alcance que describe estudios sobre enfoques basados en juegos con niñez, adolescencia y adultez autistas, y ofrece recursos a familias, profesionales y docentes. El resumen no indica qué juegos funcionan mejor ni cuánto ayudan, así que no sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you want to try games, board or digital, as a support for social communication or learning, you could start with one the autistic person is already interested in and watch how they experience it. If they enjoy it, carry on; if it overwhelms them, you can stop. This is a scoping review describing studies of game-based approaches with autistic children, adolescents and adults, and it offers resources for parents, professionals and educators. The abstract does not say which games work best or how much they help, so it is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du vill prova spel, brädspel eller digitala, som stöd för social kommunikation eller lärande kan du börja med ett som den autistiska personen redan är intresserad av och se hur hen upplever det. Trivs hen kan ni fortsätta; blir det övermäktigt kan ni sluta. Detta är en kartläggande översikt som beskriver studier av spelbaserade metoder med autistiska barn, ungdomar och vuxna, och den ger resurser till föräldrar, yrkespersoner och lärare. Sammanfattningen säger inte vilka spel som fungerar bäst eller hur mycket de hjälper, så det är ingen regel för alla.

title: Protocol for targeting insomnia in school-aged children with autism spectrum disorder without intellectual disability: a randomised control trial.
authors: McCrae CS, Mazurek MO, Curtis AF, Beversdorf DQ, Deroche CB, Golzy M, Sohl KA, Ner ZH, Davis BE, Stearns MA, Nair N
abstract: Introduction Insomnia affects up to 80% of children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Negative consequences of insomnia in ASD include decreased quality of life (QOL), impaired learning and cognition, increased stereotypic and challenging behaviours, and increased parental stress. Cognitive behavioural treatment for childhood insomnia (CBT-CI) is a promising treatment for dealing with insomnia and its negative consequences but has not yet been studied in school-aged children with ASD and comorbid insomnia. Access to healthcare is another challenge for children with ASD, particularly in rural and underserved regions. Previous studies indicate that ASD and insomnia share common arousal-based underpinnings, and we hypothesise that CBT-CI will reduce the hyperarousal associated with insomnia and ASD. This trial will be the first to examine CBT-CI adapted for children with ASD and will provide new information about two different modes of delivery across a variety of primary and secondary child and parent sleep and related outcomes. Knowledge obtained from this trial might allow us to develop new or modify current treatments to better target childhood insomnia and ASD. Methods and analysis Children (N=180) 6-12 years of age with ASD and insomnia will be recruited from an established autism database, a paediatric clinic and community outreach in the Columbia, MO and surrounding areas. Participants will be randomised to CBT-CI adapted for children with ASD (in-person or remote using computers with cameras) or Sleep Hygiene and Related Education. Participants will be assessed at baseline, post-treatment, 6-month and 12-month follow-ups. The following assessments will be completed regarding the children: objective and subjective sleep, daytime functioning (adaptive functioning, attention, challenging behaviours, anxiety), QOL and physiological arousal (heart rate variability) and parents: objective and subjective sleep, daytime functioning (anxiety, depression, fatigue), QOL, physiological arousal and parental burden/stress. Ethics and dissemination Ethics approval was obtained in January 2020 from the University of Missouri. Ethics approval was obtained in July 2020 from the US Army Medical Research and Development Command, Office of Research Protections and Human Research Protection Office. All data are expected to be collected by 2024. Full trial results are planned to be published by 2025. Secondary analyses of baseline data will be subsequently published. Trial registration number NCT04545606; Pre-results.

sheet.es: Si su hijo autista de 6-12 años duerme mal, conviene saber que se está probando una terapia conductual para el insomnio, adaptada a niños autistas, en persona o por videollamada. Aún no hay resultados, así que no hay nada que aplicar como método probado. Mientras tanto, puede hablar del sueño con el pediatra. Este documento es el protocolo de un ensayo aleatorizado: participarán 180 niños autistas con insomnio, que recibirán la terapia o educación sobre higiene del sueño. Su límite principal es que todavía no ofrece conclusiones, y lo que funcione en el grupo estudiado podría no servir a todas las personas.
sheet.en: If your autistic child aged 6-12 sleeps poorly, it helps to know that a behavioural therapy for insomnia, adapted for autistic children, is being tested, either in person or by video call. There are no results yet, so it is not a proven method you can apply. Meanwhile, you can talk about sleep with your paediatrician. This is the protocol of a randomised trial: 180 autistic children with insomnia will receive either the therapy or sleep hygiene education. Its main limit is that it offers no conclusions yet, and what works for the studied group may not suit every person.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn i åldern 6-12 år sover dåligt kan det vara bra att veta att en beteendeterapi mot sömnsvårigheter, anpassad för autistiska barn, nu prövas, antingen på plats eller via videosamtal. Det finns ännu inga resultat, så den är ingen beprövad metod att använda. Under tiden kan du ta upp sömnen med barnläkaren. Detta är protokollet för en randomiserad studie: 180 autistiska barn med sömnsvårigheter får antingen terapin eller utbildning om sömnhygien. Den största begränsningen är att den ännu inte ger några slutsatser, och det som fungerar för den studerade gruppen passar inte nödvändigtvis alla.

title: FMR1 and Autism, an Intriguing Connection Revisited.
authors: Fyke W, Velinov M
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) represents a distinct phenotype of behavioral dysfunction that includes deficiencies in communication and stereotypic behaviors. ASD affects about 2% of the US population. It is a highly heritable spectrum of conditions with substantial genetic heterogeneity. To date, mutations in over 100 genes have been reported in association with ASD phenotypes. Fragile X syndrome (FXS) is the most common single-gene disorder associated with ASD. The gene associated with FXS, FMR1 is located on chromosome X. Accordingly, the condition has more severe manifestations in males. FXS results from the loss of function of FMR1 due to the expansion of an unstable CGG repeat located in the 5'' untranslated region of the gene. About 50% of the FXS males and 20% of the FXS females meet the Diagnostic Statistical Manual 5 (DSM-5) criteria for ASD. Among the individuals with ASD, about 3% test positive for FXS. FMRP, the protein product of FMR1 , is a major gene regulator in the central nervous system. Multiple pathways regulated by FMRP are found to be dysfunctional in ASD patients who do not have FXS. Thus, FXS presents the opportunity to study cellular phenomena that may have wider applications in the management of ASD and to develop new strategies for ASD therapy.

sheet.es: Si en tu familia hay una persona autista, saber que existen pruebas genéticas como la del síndrome del X frágil puede ser un tema para hablar con su profesional de salud, sin urgencia. Esta revisión recoge investigaciones previas: indica que alrededor del 3% de las personas con autismo dan positivo en X frágil y que mucha gente con X frágil no cumple criterios de autismo. Es una revisión, no un estudio con participantes nuevos, y se centra en la biología del gen FMR1. No dice qué hacer en cada caso ni sirve como regla para todas las personas. Cualquier decisión médica corresponde a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If there is an autistic person in your family, knowing that genetic testing such as testing for fragile X syndrome exists can be something to raise with their health professional, with no urgency. This review gathers earlier research: it reports that about 3% of autistic people test positive for fragile X, and that many people with fragile X do not meet criteria for autism. It is a review, not a study with new participants, and it focuses on the biology of the FMR1 gene. It does not say what to do in any individual case and is not a rule for everyone. Any medical decision belongs to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om du har en autistisk person i familjen kan det vara bra att veta att genetiska tester, till exempel för fragilt X-syndrom, finns. Det kan tas upp med personens vårdgivare, utan brådska. Den här översikten sammanfattar tidigare forskning: ungefär 3% av autistiska personer testar positivt för fragilt X, och många med fragilt X uppfyller inte kriterierna för autism. Det är en översikt, inte en studie med nya deltagare, och den handlar mest om biologin bakom genen FMR1. Den säger inte vad man ska göra i ett enskilt fall och gäller inte alla. Medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker.

title: Folic Acid and Autism: A Systematic Review of the Current State of Knowledge.
authors: Hoxha B, Hoxha M, Domi E, Gervasoni J, Persichilli S, Malaj V, Zappacosta B
abstract: Folic acid has been identified to be integral in rapid tissue growth and cell division during fetal development. Different studies indicate folic acid's importance in improving childhood behavioral outcomes and underline its role as a modifiable risk factor for autism spectrum disorders. The aim of this systematic review is to both elucidate the potential role of folic acid in autism spectrum disorders and to investigate the mechanisms involved. Studies have pointed out a potential beneficial effect of prenatal folic acid maternal supplementation (600 µg) on the risk of autism spectrum disorder onset, but opposite results have been reported as well. Folic acid and/or folinic acid supplementation in autism spectrum disorder diagnosed children has led to improvements, both in some neurologic and behavioral symptoms and in the concentration of one-carbon metabolites. Several authors report an increased frequency of serum auto-antibodies against folate receptor alpha (FRAA) in autism spectrum disorder children. Furthermore, methylene tetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) polymorphisms showed a significant influence on ASD risk. More clinical trials, with a clear study design, with larger sample sizes and longer observation periods are necessary to be carried out to better evaluate the potential protective role of folic acid in autism spectrum disorder risk.

title: The Effectiveness of Cobalamin (B12) Treatment for Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Rossignol DA, Frye RE
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a common neurodevelopmental disorder affecting 2% of children in the United States. Biochemical abnormalities associated with ASD include impaired methylation and sulphation capacities along with low glutathione (GSH) redox capacity. Potential treatments for these abnormalities include cobalamin (B12). This systematic review collates the studies using B12 as a treatment in ASD. A total of 17 studies were identified; 4 were double-blind, placebo-controlled studies (2 examined B12 injections alone and 2 used B12 in an oral multivitamin); 1 was a prospective controlled study; 6 were prospective, uncontrolled studies, and 6 were retrospective (case series and reports). Most studies (83%) used oral or injected methylcobalamin (mB12), while the remaining studies did not specify the type of B12 used. Studies using subcutaneous mB12 injections (including 2 placebo-controlled studies) used a 64.5-75 µg/kg/dose. One study reported anemia in 2 ASD children with injected cyanocobalamin that resolved with switching to injected mB12. Two studies reported improvements in markers of mitochondrial metabolism. A meta-analysis of methylation metabolites demonstrated decreased S-adenosylhomocysteine (SAH), and increased methionine, S-adenosylmethionine (SAM), SAM/SAH ratio, and homocysteine (with small effect sizes) with mB12. Meta-analysis of the transsulfuration and redox metabolism metabolites demonstrated significant improvements with mB12 in oxidized glutathione (GSSG), cysteine, total glutathione (GSH), and total GSH/GSSG redox ratio with medium to large effect sizes. Improvements in methylation capacity and GSH redox ratio were significantly associated with clinical improvements (with a mean moderate effect size of 0.59) in core and associated ASD symptoms, including expressive communication, personal and domestic daily living skills, and interpersonal, play-leisure, and coping social skills, suggesting these biomarkers may predict response to B12. Other clinical improvements observed with B12 included sleep, gastrointestinal symptoms, hyperactivity, tantrums, nonverbal intellectual quotient, vision, eye contact, echolalia, stereotypy, anemia, and nocturnal enuresis. Adverse events identified by meta-analysis included hyperactivity (11.9%), irritability (3.4%), trouble sleeping (7.6%), aggression (1.8%), and worsening behaviors (7.7%) but were generally few, mild, not serious, and not significantly different compared to placebo. In one study, 78% of parents desired to continue mB12 injections after the study conclusion. Preliminary clinical evidence suggests that B12, particularly subcutaneously injected mB12, improves metabolic abnormalities in ASD along with clinical symptoms. Further large multicenter placebo-controlled studies are needed to confirm these data. B12 is a promising treatment for ASD.

title: Overlapping and specific neural correlates for empathizing, affective mentalizing, and cognitive mentalizing: A coordinate-based meta-analytic study.
authors: Arioli M, Cattaneo Z, Ricciardi E, Canessa N
abstract: While the discussion on the foundations of social understanding mainly revolves around the notions of empathy, affective mentalizing, and cognitive mentalizing, their degree of overlap versus specificity is still unclear. We took a meta-analytic approach to unveil the neural bases of cognitive mentalizing, affective mentalizing, and empathy, both in healthy individuals and pathological conditions characterized by social deficits such as schizophrenia and autism. We observed partially overlapping networks for cognitive and affective mentalizing in the medial prefrontal, posterior cingulate, and lateral temporal cortex, while empathy mainly engaged fronto-insular, somatosensory, and anterior cingulate cortex. Adjacent process-specific regions in the posterior lateral temporal, ventrolateral, and dorsomedial prefrontal cortex might underpin a transition from abstract representations of cognitive mental states detached from sensory facets to emotionally-charged representations of affective mental states. Altered mentalizing-related activity involved distinct sectors of the posterior lateral temporal cortex in schizophrenia and autism, while only the latter group displayed abnormal empathy related activity in the amygdala. These data might inform the design of rehabilitative treatments for social cognitive deficits.

sheet.es: Entender a los demás no es una sola habilidad: pensar qué piensa alguien, sentir qué siente y compartir su emoción pueden funcionar de forma distinta, así que conviene no tratarlas como lo mismo. Es un meta-análisis, que reúne estudios de imagen cerebral de personas sin diagnóstico y de personas con esquizofrenia o autismo. Encontró redes cerebrales en parte compartidas y en parte propias para cada proceso, con diferencias en el autismo. Sus límites: describe grupos, no a una persona concreta, usa un lenguaje de 'déficits' que no compartimos y no dice qué apoyo elegir. Cada persona autista es distinta.
sheet.en: Understanding other people is not one single skill: working out what someone thinks, feeling what they feel and sharing their emotion may work differently, so it helps not to treat them as the same thing. This is a meta-analysis, pooling brain imaging studies of people without a diagnosis and of people with schizophrenia or autism. It found brain networks that partly overlap and partly differ for each process, with some differences in autism. Its limits: it describes groups, not any one person, it uses 'deficit' wording we do not share, and it does not say which support to choose. Every autistic person is different.
sheet.sv: Att förstå andra är inte en enda förmåga: att tänka ut vad någon tänker, känna vad hen känner och dela känslan kan fungera olika, så det hjälper att inte behandla dem som samma sak. Det här är en metaanalys som slår ihop hjärnavbildningsstudier av personer utan diagnos och av personer med schizofreni eller autism. Den fann hjärnnätverk som delvis överlappar och delvis skiljer sig åt för varje process, med vissa skillnader vid autism. Begränsningar: den beskriver grupper, inte en enskild person, använder ett 'brist'-språk som vi inte delar och säger inte vilket stöd man bör välja. Varje autistisk person är olika.

title: Autistic adults' personal experiences of navigating a social world prior to and during Covid-19 lockdown in Spain.
authors: Lois Mosquera M, Mandy W, Pavlopoulou G, Dimitriou D

title: Peer preferences and characteristics of same-group and cross-group social interactions among autistic and non-autistic adolescents.
authors: Chen YL, Senande LL, Thorsen M, Patten K
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic students often experience challenges in peer interactions, especially for young adolescents who are navigating the increased social expectations in secondary education. Previous research on the peer interactions of autistic adolescents mainly compared the social behaviors of autistic and non-autistic students and overlooked the peers in the social context. However, recent research has shown that the social challenges faced by autistic may not be solely contributed by their social differences, but a mismatch in the social communication styles between autistic and non-autistic people. As such, this study aimed to investigate the student-and-peer match in real-world peer interactions between six autistic and six non-autistic adolescents in an inclusive school club. We examined the odds of autistic and non-autistic students interacting with either an autistic peer, a non-autistic peer, or multiple peers, and the results showed that autistic students were more likely to interact with autistic peers then non-autistic peers. This preference for same-group peer interactions strengthened over the 5-month school club in both autistic and non-autistic students. We further found that same-group peer interactions, in both autistic and non-autistic students, were more likely to convey a social interest rather than a functional purpose or need, be sharing thoughts, experiences, or items rather than requesting help or objects, and be highly reciprocal than cross-group social behaviors. Collectively, our findings support that peer interaction outcomes may be determined by the match between the group memberships of the student and their peers, either autistic or non-autistic, rather than the student's autism diagnosis.

sheet.es: Si puede, facilite que los adolescentes autistas tengan ocasiones de estar con otros jóvenes autistas, por ejemplo en un club escolar, y no dé por hecho que interactuar con cualquier compañero es lo mismo. Es un estudio observacional con seis adolescentes autistas y seis no autistas en un club escolar inclusivo durante 5 meses. Los estudiantes autistas interactuaron más con pares autistas, y esas interacciones eran más recíprocas y buscaban compartir más que pedir. Es un grupo muy pequeño en un solo club, así que no sirve como regla para cada persona; pregunte siempre a cada adolescente qué prefiere.
