Both disorders pose a cumulative threat to human health, with the rate of incidences increasing considerably worldwide. In the context of recent developments, we aimed to review correlated symptoms and genetics, and overlapping aspects in the mechanisms of the pathogenesis of ASD and AD. Dementia, insomnia, and weak neuromuscular interaction, as well as communicative and cognitive impairments, are shared symptoms. A number of genes and proteins linked with both disorders have been tabulated, including MECP2, ADNP, SCN2A, NLGN, SHANK, PTEN, RELN, and FMR1. Theories about the role of neuron development, processing, connectivity, and levels of neurotransmitters in both disorders have been discussed. Based on the recent literature, the roles of FMRP (Fragile X mental retardation protein), hnRNPC (heterogeneous ribonucleoprotein-C), IRP (Iron regulatory proteins), miRNAs (MicroRNAs), and α-, β0, and γ-secretases in the posttranscriptional regulation of cellular synthesis and processing of APP (amyloid-β precursor protein) have been elaborated to describe the parallel and overlapping routes and mechanisms of ASD and AD pathogenesis. However, the interactive role of genetic and environmental factors, oxidative and metal ion stress, mutations in the associated genes, and alterations in the related cellular pathways in the development of ASD and AD needs further investigation.

sheet.es: Tómelo como contexto, no como guía para actuar mañana: esta revisión no ofrece pautas concretas. Si una persona autista tiene problemas de sueño o dudas sobre su salud a largo plazo, conviene comentarlo con su profesional de referencia. Se trata de una revisión de literatura científica que compara síntomas, genes y mecanismos biológicos del autismo y del alzheimer; no describe a personas concretas. Sus límites: señala coincidencias, no demuestra que una condición lleve a la otra, y los propios autores indican que hace falta más investigación sobre genes, entorno y otros factores.
sheet.en: Treat this as background, not a guide for tomorrow morning: the review offers no concrete steps. If an autistic person has sleep difficulties or questions about long-term health, it is worth raising them with their usual clinician. This is a review of the scientific literature comparing symptoms, genes and biological mechanisms in autism and Alzheimer's disease; it does not follow particular people. Its limits: it points to overlaps but does not show that one condition leads to the other, and the authors say more research is needed on genes, environment and other factors.
sheet.sv: Se detta som bakgrund, inte som en handledning för i morgon: översikten ger inga konkreta råd. Om en autistisk person har sömnsvårigheter eller frågor om hälsan på lång sikt är det värt att ta upp det med personens vanliga vårdkontakt. Det är en översikt av forskningslitteratur som jämför symtom, gener och biologiska mekanismer vid autism och Alzheimers sjukdom; den följer inga enskilda personer. Begränsningar: den visar likheter men inte att det ena tillståndet leder till det andra, och författarna anger att mer forskning behövs om gener, miljö och andra faktorer.

title: The Implementation of Application Software to Improve Verbal Communication in Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Review.
authors: Maseri M, Mamat M, Yew HT, Chekima A
abstract: Autism-assistive apps offer therapists and caregivers new approaches for educating and assisting individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), mainly in social interaction. Even though these apps are deemed effective, they are not. These autism-assistive apps are not highly customizable, which limits their usefulness. This article examined the application software that was applied to encourage verbal communication in the intervention for children with ASD. The aim was to determine the minimum requirements for a verbal communication intervention app that adequately satisfies children with ASD, caregivers, and therapists. Databases were searched, including Scopus, Springer, PubMed, Education Resources Information Centre, and Google Scholar, with the following free-text terms combining Boolean operators: autism, children, intervention, verbal communication, software, app, and technology. A total of fifteen studies were found relevant, and the following information was collected: participant characteristics, information on the devices and apps, target behaviors, intervention procedures, and intervention outcomes. The findings suggest that the autism-assistive apps effectively improve verbal communication of children with ASD. For that, the apps should be attractive and engaging to the children with ASD, able to identify the child's capability and suggest appropriate lesson activities, as well as encompass specific learning outcomes with multilevel lesson strategy. The apps should also use systematic evidence-based intervention procedures in the activities, be able to evaluate the child's learning progress, and allow caregivers or therapists to keep track of application usage and performance. The use of apps in intervention does provide many benefits. However, they should never replace qualified therapists. App-based interventions make home-based treatment more focused, systematic, and economical.

sheet.es: Si pensáis usar una aplicación para apoyar la comunicación verbal, buscad una que resulte atractiva para la niña o el niño, que ajuste las actividades a lo que ya sabe hacer, que muestre su progreso y que permita al adulto ver cómo se usa. Úsala como complemento, nunca en lugar de profesionales cualificados. La evidencia es una revisión de quince estudios sobre apps con niños autistas. Sus límites: las apps no suelen ser muy personalizables y los resultados no sirven como regla para todas las personas, así que conviene observar qué funciona para vuestro hijo o hija.
sheet.en: If you are thinking of using an app to support verbal communication, look for one that the child finds attractive, that adjusts activities to what they can already do, that shows their progress and lets the adult see how it is used. Treat it as an addition, never a replacement for qualified therapists. The evidence is a review of fifteen studies on apps with autistic children. Its limits: apps are often not very customizable, and the findings are not a rule for every person, so watch what works for your own child.
sheet.sv: Om ni funderar på en app för att stödja verbal kommunikation, leta efter en som barnet tycker är lockande, som anpassar övningarna efter vad barnet redan kan, som visar framsteg och låter den vuxne följa hur appen används. Använd den som ett komplement, aldrig som ersättning för kvalificerade terapeuter. Underlaget är en översikt av femton studier om appar med autistiska barn. Begränsningar: apparna är ofta inte särskilt anpassningsbara, och resultaten är ingen regel för alla, så se efter vad som fungerar för just ert barn.

title: The Role of Occupational Therapy in Managing Food Selectivity of Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Scoping Review.
authors: Reche-Olmedo L, Torres-Collado L, Compañ-Gabucio LM, Garcia-de-la-Hera M
abstract: Food selectivity is common in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). It can be defined as the unwillingness to eat common or new foods, resulting in a lack of variety in the diet or limited food consumption for multiple reasons, such as inflexibility or sensory alterations. We conducted a peer scoping review to describe the interventions that are carried out from occupational therapy (OT) in children with ASD with food selectivity. Two authors independently searched the databases PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and EMBASE, as well as the OT journals indexed in Journal Citation Reports. Articles exploring OT interventions in children (≤12 years) with ASD and food selectivity, published in Spanish or English, with experimental design, and with full text available were included. Of the 1445 articles identified, 8 articles met the inclusion criteria. Three main intervention categories were identified: sensory-behavioral, family focused, and other interventions. Most of the interventions from OT were aimed at treating sensory-behavioral aspects. Only three articles described interventions led exclusively by occupational therapists, and the rest were led by a multidisciplinary team. Finally, although these interventions are not exclusive to OT, occupational therapists can participate together with other professionals as an essential component in the treatment of food selectivity in children with ASD.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija autista come pocos alimentos, puede consultar con un terapeuta ocupacional, que suele trabajar los aspectos sensoriales y también puede acompañar a la familia, a menudo junto con otros profesionales. Se trata de una revisión de alcance: de 1445 artículos identificados, 8 cumplieron los criterios, con niños de 12 años o menos. La mayoría de las intervenciones se centraban en lo sensorial y conductual; solo tres las dirigía únicamente terapia ocupacional. Es una descripción de lo que se hace, no una prueba de qué funciona mejor, y no sirve igual para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If your autistic child eats only a few foods, you can ask an occupational therapist for support. They often work on sensory aspects and can also support the family, frequently alongside other professionals. This was a scoping review: of 1445 articles identified, 8 met the criteria, involving children aged 12 or under. Most interventions focused on sensory and behavioural aspects; only three were led solely by occupational therapists. It describes what is being done rather than proving what works best, and it will not fit every child in the same way.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn äter få livsmedel kan du fråga en arbetsterapeut om stöd. Arbetsterapeuter arbetar ofta med sensoriska aspekter och kan även stödja familjen, ofta tillsammans med andra yrkesgrupper. Det här var en översikt (scoping review): av 1445 identifierade artiklar uppfyllde 8 kriterierna, med barn upp till 12 år. De flesta insatserna riktade sig mot sensoriska och beteendemässiga aspekter; bara tre leddes enbart av arbetsterapeuter. Studien beskriver vad som görs, den bevisar inte vad som fungerar bäst och passar inte alla barn på samma sätt.

title: Parent-Mediated Interventions for Children and Adolescents With Autism Spectrum Disorders: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Conrad CE, Rimestad ML, Rohde JF, Petersen BH, Korfitsen CB, Tarp S, Cantio C, Lauritsen MB, Händel MN
abstract: There has been increasing interest in parent-mediated interventions (PMIs) for children with autism spectrum disorders (ASDs). The objective of this systematic review and meta-analysis was to examine the effect of PMIs compared to no PMI for children with ASD aged 2-17 years. The primary outcome was adaptive functioning rated by a parent or clinician. The secondary outcomes were long-term adaptive functioning rated by the parents, adverse events, core symptoms of ASD, disruptive behavior, parental well-being, quality of life of the child rated by the parents and anxiety. The MEDLINE, PsycInfo, Embase, and CINAHL databases were searched in March 2020. The Cochrane Risk of Bias Tool was used to rate the individual studies, and the certainty in the evidence was evaluated using GRADE. We identified 30 relevant randomized controlled trials (RCTs), including 1,934 participants. A clinically relevant effect of PMIs on parent-rated adaptive functioning was found with a low certainty of evidence [Standard mean difference (SMD): 0.28 (95% CI: -0.01, 0.57)] on Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scales (VABS), whereas no clinically relevant effect was seen for clinician-rated functional level, with a very low certainty of evidence [SMD on Clinical Global Impressions (CGI)-severity scale: SMD -0.45 [95% CI: -0.87, -0.03)]. PMIs may slightly improve clinician-rated autism core symptoms [SMD: -0.35 (95% CI: -0.71, 0.02)]. Additionally, no effect of PMIs on parent-rated core symptoms of ASD, parental well-being or adverse effects was identified, all with a low certainty of evidence. There was a moderate certainty of evidence for a clinically relevant effect on disruptive behavior [SMD: 0.55 (95% Cl: 0.36, 0.74)]. The certainty in the evidence was downgraded due to serious risk of bias, lack of blinding, and serious risk of imprecision due to few participants included in meta-analyses. The present findings suggest that clinicians may consider introducing PMIs to children with ASD, but more high-quality RCTs are needed because the effects are not well-established, and the results are likely to change with future studies. The protocol for the systematic review is registered at the Danish Health Authority website (www.sst.dk).

sheet.es: Si le ofrecen un programa en el que las familias aprenden a apoyar a su hijo autista en la vida diaria, puede ser una opción que vale la pena valorar con el equipo profesional, sin esperar resultados iguales para todos. La evidencia es un metaanálisis de 30 ensayos controlados aleatorizados con 1,934 participantes de 2 a 17 años. Se vio un efecto en la conducta disruptiva con certeza moderada; para el funcionamiento adaptativo y otros resultados la certeza fue baja o muy baja. Los límites: pocos participantes en algunos análisis, falta de cegamiento, y los resultados pueden cambiar con estudios futuros.
sheet.en: If you are offered a programme where families learn ways to support their autistic child in daily life, it may be worth discussing with the professional team, without expecting the same results for everyone. The evidence is a meta-analysis of 30 randomized controlled trials with 1,934 participants aged 2-17 years. An effect on disruptive behavior was seen with moderate certainty; for adaptive functioning and other outcomes certainty was low or very low. Limits: few participants in some analyses, lack of blinding, and results may change with future studies.
sheet.sv: Om ni erbjuds ett program där familjer lär sig stötta sitt autistiska barn i vardagen kan det vara värt att diskutera med teamet, utan att förvänta er samma resultat för alla. Underlaget är en metaanalys av 30 randomiserade kontrollerade studier med 1,934 deltagare i åldern 2-17 år. En effekt på störande beteende sågs med måttlig säkerhet; för adaptiv funktion och andra utfall var säkerheten låg eller mycket låg. Begränsningar: få deltagare i vissa analyser, avsaknad av blindning, och resultaten kan ändras med framtida studier.

title: Sensory Sensitivity and Intolerance of Uncertainty Influence Anxiety in Autistic Adults.
authors: Normansell-Mossa KM, Top DN, Russell N, Freeston M, Rodgers J, South M
abstract: Several models of anxiety in autistic adults have focused on the role of intolerance of uncertainty which has biological and evolutionary bases, as a cognitive explanation for the high prevalence of anxiety in autism. This framework suggests that all people are born with a healthy level of intolerance of uncertainty, and as we develop, this intolerance is lessened as we learn when situations are safe and begin to understand and manage the uncertainty. This process of learning about managing uncertainty does not happen in the same way in those who are high in autistic traits, which could be the reason for the high levels of anxiety symptoms commonly seen in this population. We examined archival data of 199 non-autistic and 55 autistic adults from prior studies in which we collected self-report measures of autistic traits, intolerance of uncertainty, sensory processing, and anxiety. We conducted two path analyses to examine the role of intolerance of uncertainty in anxiety in autistic adults. The first model tested the idea that intolerance of uncertainty, an evolutionary phenomenon common for all people, could explain some of the cognitive aspects of anxiety in autism. The second model suggests that primary neurodevelopmental differences associated with autistic traits underlie the sensory sensitivity and sensory seeking behaviors, which in turn increase intolerance of uncertainty and subsequent anxiety. We found that the "neurodevelopmental" model had better model fit than the "evolutionary stress" model, suggesting that the neurodevelopmental impact of higher levels of autistic traits could moderate a non-autistic trajectory of learning to manage uncertainty as children develop and understand that uncertainty is common and acceptable.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista se angustia ante lo imprevisto, conviene mirar también el entorno sensorial (ruido, luz, texturas) y avisar de los cambios con antelación, además de ofrecer calma. Es un estudio con adultos: se analizaron datos previos de 199 adultos no autistas y 55 adultos autistas, que respondieron cuestionarios sobre rasgos autistas, intolerancia a la incertidumbre, procesamiento sensorial y ansiedad. El modelo que parte de diferencias del neurodesarrollo y de la sensibilidad sensorial encajó mejor que el evolutivo. Límites: son autoinformes, no prueban causa y efecto, y no describen a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person gets distressed by the unexpected, it may help to look at the sensory environment too (noise, light, textures) and give notice of changes ahead of time, alongside offering calm. This was a study with adults: it analysed earlier data from 199 non-autistic and 55 autistic adults who completed self-report measures of autistic traits, intolerance of uncertainty, sensory processing and anxiety. A model based on neurodevelopmental differences and sensory sensitivity fitted better than an evolutionary one. Limits: self-reports cannot prove cause and effect, and results do not describe every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person blir stressad av det oväntade kan det hjälpa att också se på sinnesmiljön (ljud, ljus, texturer) och att berätta om förändringar i förväg, utöver att erbjuda lugn. Det var en studie med vuxna: man analyserade tidigare data från 199 icke-autistiska och 55 autistiska vuxna som fyllde i självskattningar om autistiska drag, svårighet att tåla osäkerhet, sensorisk bearbetning och ångest. En modell som utgick från neuroutvecklingsskillnader och sensorisk känslighet passade bättre än en evolutionär modell. Begränsningar: självskattningar kan inte visa orsak och verkan, och resultaten gäller inte alla autistiska personer.

title: Effects of Creative Movement Therapies on Social Communication, Behavioral-Affective, Sensorimotor, Cognitive, and Functional Participation Skills of Individuals With Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review.
authors: Amonkar N, Su WC, Bhat AN, Srinivasan SM
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder affecting multiple developmental domains including social communication, behavioral-affective, sensorimotor, and cognitive systems. There is growing evidence for the use of holistic, whole-body, Creative Movement Therapies (CMT) such as music, dance, yoga, theater, and martial arts in addressing the multisystem impairments in ASD. We conducted a comprehensive quantitative and qualitative review of the evidence to date on the effects of CMT on multiple systems in individuals with ASD. The strongest evidence, both in terms of quantity and quality, exists for music and martial arts-based interventions followed by yoga and theater, with very limited research on dance-based approaches. Our review of 72 studies ( N = 1,939 participants) across participants with ASD ranging from 3 to 65 years of age suggests that at present there is consistent evidence from high quality studies for small-to-large sized improvements in social communication skills following music and martial arts therapies and medium-to-large improvements in motor and cognitive skills following yoga and martial arts training, with insufficient evidence to date for gains in affective, sensory, and functional participation domains following CMT. Although promising, our review serves as a call for more rigorous high-quality research to assess the multisystem effects of CMT in ASD. Based on the existing literature, we discuss implications of our findings for autism researchers and also provide evidence-based guidelines for clinicians to incorporate CMT approaches in their plan of care for individuals with ASD.

sheet.es: Si a tu hijo o familiar autista le atrae la música, las artes marciales, el yoga o el teatro, puede valer la pena probar una actividad así, a su ritmo y respetando sus preferencias sensoriales. La música y las artes marciales se asociaron con mejoras en la comunicación social, y el yoga y las artes marciales con mejoras motoras y cognitivas. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 72 estudios con 1.939 personas autistas de 3 a 65 años. Sus límites: la calidad de los estudios varía, hay poca investigación sobre danza y no hay pruebas suficientes sobre bienestar emocional, sensorial o participación diaria. Lo que ayuda a una persona puede no ayudar a otra.
sheet.en: If your autistic child or family member enjoys music, martial arts, yoga or theatre, trying one of these activities may be worthwhile, at their own pace and with respect for their sensory preferences. Music and martial arts were linked to gains in social communication, and yoga and martial arts to gains in motor and thinking skills. This systematic review pooled 72 studies with 1,939 autistic people aged 3 to 65. Its limits: study quality varies, dance has barely been researched, and there is not enough evidence about emotional, sensory or everyday participation outcomes. What helps one person may not help another.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn eller din anhörige tycker om musik, kampsport, yoga eller teater kan det vara värt att prova en sådan aktivitet, i egen takt och med respekt för sensoriska behov. Musik och kampsport kopplades till förbättrad social kommunikation, och yoga och kampsport till förbättrad motorik och kognition. Denna systematiska översikt samlade 72 studier med 1 939 autistiska personer mellan 3 och 65 år. Begränsningar: studiernas kvalitet varierar, dans är knappt undersökt och det saknas tillräckliga belägg för effekter på känslor, sinnesintryck och vardagligt deltagande. Det som hjälper en person hjälper inte nödvändigtvis en annan.

title: The feasibility of low-intensity psychological therapy for depression co-occurring with autism in adults: The Autism Depression Trial (ADEPT) - a pilot randomised controlled trial.
authors: Russell A, Gaunt DM, Cooper K, Barton S, Horwood J, Kessler D, Metcalfe C, Ensum I, Ingham B, Parr JR, Rai D, Wiles N
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Low-intensity cognitive behaviour therapy including behavioural activation is an evidence-based treatment for depression, a condition frequently co-occurring with autism. The feasibility of adapting low-intensity cognitive behaviour therapy for depression to meet the needs of autistic adults via a randomised controlled trial was investigated. The adapted intervention (guided self-help) comprised materials for nine individual sessions with a low-intensity psychological therapist. Autistic adults (n = 70) with depression (Patient Health Questionnaire-9 score ⩾10) recruited from National Health Service adult autism services and research cohorts were randomly allocated to guided self-help or treatment as usual. Outcomes at 10-, 16- and 24-weeks post-randomisation were blind to treatment group. Rates of retention in the study differed by treatment group with more participants attending follow-up in the guided self-help group than treatment as usual. The adapted intervention was well-received, 86% (n = 30/35) of participants attended the pre-defined 'dose' of five sessions of treatment and 71% (25/35) attended all treatment sessions. The findings of this pilot randomised controlled trial indicate that low-intensity cognitive behaviour therapy informed by behavioural activation can be successfully adapted to meet the needs of autistic people. Evaluation of the effectiveness of this intervention in a full scale randomised controlled trial is now warranted.

sheet.es: Si un adulto autista de tu entorno vive con depresión, puede valer la pena preguntar a su servicio de salud por una terapia guiada de baja intensidad adaptada al autismo, con materiales claros y sesiones individuales centradas en retomar actividades significativas. Este estudio piloto aleatorizado incluyó a 70 adultos autistas con depresión en el Reino Unido: la terapia adaptada de nueve sesiones fue bien recibida, y el 71 % asistió a todas las sesiones. Su límite es que solo comprobó si la terapia era viable y aceptable, no si reduce la depresión; hace falta un ensayo más grande, y cada persona puede necesitar algo distinto.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult in your life is living with depression, it may be worth asking their health service about low-intensity guided self-help adapted for autism, with clear materials and one-to-one sessions focused on gently returning to meaningful activities. This pilot randomised controlled trial included 70 autistic adults with depression in the UK: the adapted nine-session therapy was well received, and 71% attended every session. Its limit is that it only tested whether the therapy was feasible and acceptable, not whether it reduces depression; a larger trial is needed, and each person may need something different.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen i din närhet lever med depression kan det vara värt att fråga vården om lågintensiv guidad självhjälp anpassad för autism, med tydligt material och enskilda samtal som fokuserar på att varsamt återuppta meningsfulla aktiviteter. Denna randomiserade pilotstudie omfattade 70 autistiska vuxna med depression i Storbritannien: den anpassade terapin med nio sessioner togs emot väl, och 71 % deltog i alla sessioner. Begränsningen är att studien bara undersökte om terapin var genomförbar och accepterad, inte om den minskar depression; en större studie behövs, och varje person kan behöva något annat.

title: The impact of COVID-19 on the mental health and wellbeing of caregivers of autistic children and youth: A scoping review.
authors: Lee V, Albaum C, Tablon Modica P, Ahmad F, Gorter JW, Khanlou N, McMorris C, Lai J, Harrison C, Hedley T, Johnston P, Putterman C, Spoelstra M, Weiss JA
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Caregivers and families of autistic people have experienced stress and increase in demands due to the COVID-19 pandemic that may have long-term negative consequences for both their own and their children's mental health. A scoping review was conducted to identify pandemic related demands experienced by caregivers and families of autistic children and youth. The review also consolidated information on coping strategies and parenting-related guidelines that have emerged to help parents meet these demands. Search strategies were approved by a research librarian and were conducted in peer-reviewed and gray literature databases between May 2020 and February 2021. Additional resources were solicited through author networks and social media. All articles were published between December 2019 and February 2021. Article summaries were charted, and a thematic analysis was conducted with confirmation of findings with our knowledge users. Twenty-three published articles and 14 pieces of gray literature were included in the review. The majority of articles characterized and highlighted the increase in demands on caregivers of autistic children and youth during the pandemic globally. Both quantitative and qualitative studies suggest that parents have experienced an increase in stress and mental health-related symptoms during lockdown measures. Findings suggest that families are employing coping strategies, but there no evidence-based supports were identified. The review highlighted the potential long-term impact of prolonged exposure to increasing demands on the mental health and wellbeing of caregivers and families of autistic people, and pointed to a need for the rapid development and evaluation of flexible and timely support programs. LAY SUMMARY: Caregivers and families of autistic children and youth have faced increased demands due to pandemic-related lockdown measures. We reviewed the literature to outline sources of stress, links to their influence on caregiver mental health, and if support programs have emerged to help them. Our findings suggest a number of demands have increased caregivers' risk to mental health challenges, and their potential impact on family wellbeing. Ongoing development of evidence-based supports of all families of autistic children and youth are needed.

sheet.es: Si la pandemia o cualquier cambio brusco de rutinas te ha dejado agotado, no es un fallo personal: muchas familias de niños y jóvenes autistas vivieron más estrés y más exigencias. Mañana puedes reservar un momento breve para ti, pedir ayuda concreta a alguien de confianza y hablar con tu centro de salud si notas ansiedad o tristeza persistentes. Tu bienestar también cuenta. Esta revisión exploratoria reunió 23 artículos publicados y 14 documentos de literatura gris (2019–2021) sobre cuidadores de todo el mundo. Sus límites: se hizo muy rápido, al inicio de la pandemia, con estudios variados, y no encontró apoyos con evidencia probada; cada familia vive su situación de forma distinta.
sheet.en: If the pandemic, or any sudden change in routines, has left you exhausted, it is not a personal failing: many families of autistic children and youth faced more stress and more demands. Tomorrow you could set aside a short moment for yourself, ask someone you trust for one concrete kind of help, and talk to your health centre if anxiety or low mood persists. Your wellbeing matters too. This scoping review gathered 23 published articles and 14 grey-literature pieces (2019–2021) about caregivers worldwide. Its limits: it was done quickly, early in the pandemic, with varied studies, and found no evidence-based supports yet; every family's experience is different.
sheet.sv: Om pandemin, eller andra plötsliga förändringar i rutinerna, har gjort dig utmattad är det inte ett personligt misslyckande: många familjer till autistiska barn och unga upplevde mer stress och fler krav. I morgon kan du avsätta en kort stund för dig själv, be någon du litar på om en konkret sorts hjälp och kontakta vårdcentralen om oro eller nedstämdhet håller i sig. Ditt välmående spelar också roll. Denna översikt (scoping review) samlade 23 publicerade artiklar och 14 texter ur grå litteratur (2019–2021) om omsorgsgivare i hela världen. Begränsningar: den gjordes snabbt, tidigt i pandemin, med varierande studier, och fann inga evidensbaserade stöd ännu; varje familjs upplevelse är olika.

title: The association between COVID-19, personal wellbeing, depression, and suicide risk factors in Australian autistic adults.
authors: Hedley D, Hayward SM, Denney K, Uljarević M, Uljarević M, Bury S, Sahin E, Brown CM, Clapperton A, Dissanayake C, Robinson J, Trollor J, Stokes MA
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has had a significant impact on the mental health and wellbeing of the world's population, with particularly negative effects on vulnerable populations, including autistic people. Although some consensus regarding specific impact on aspects of wellbeing and mental health in autism is starting to emerge, it is unclear whether the pandemic has increased suicide risk. The goals of this study were to examine (a) potential associations between COVID-19 impact and depression, personal wellbeing, and suicide risk factors in Australian autistic adults and (b) age and gender effects. The COVID-19 Impact Scale (CIS), Personal Wellbeing Index, Patient Health Questionnaire, and the Suicide Behavior Questionnaire, Revised (SBQ-R), were administered to 111 autistic adults aged 20 to 71 years during the second wave of the COVID-19 pandemic in Australia. COVID-19 impact showed small associations with poorer personal wellbeing (r = -0.224, p = 0.023, [-0.409, -0.016]) and higher depressive symptoms (r = 0.268, p = 0.006, [0.056, 0.445]) and was not associated with the SBQ-R suicide risk score (r = 0.081, p = 0.418, [-0.118, 0.264). No significant effects were identified for age. Although model results were similar for women and men, the strength of the associations between personal wellbeing and depression (z = -2.16, p = 0.015), and depression and SBQ-R suicide risk (z = 1.961, p = 0.025), were stronger in women than in men. Qualitative analysis of an open response question from the CIS suggested that the pandemic had both positive and negative impacts on participants. The COVID-19 pandemic has had a large impact on the mental health and wellbeing of the world's population, particularly vulnerable populations such as autistic people. It is not known if these impacts on mental health and wellbeing have increased suicide risk. Our findings suggest that the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic may be associated with poorer wellbeing and higher depression, but is not associated with suicide risk. Overall, autistic people reported both positive and negative impacts of the pandemic on their lives.

title: Challenges Surrounding the Diagnosis of Autism in Children.
authors: Hus Y, Segal O
abstract: This comprehensive thematic review aims to highlight and familiarize readers with the challenges and pitfalls encountered in differential diagnosis of autism spectrum disorders (ASD) in children to facilitate the process of accurate identification by stakeholders. Accordingly, articles that best answer our questions and highlight our concerns were chosen from well-established publishers with prime peer reviewed journals. Included are studies showing alternate views of the issues so as to point readers to other possibilities. ASD, a complex dynamic biological-neurodevelopmental disorder, is underscored by its heterogeneous symptomology, severity, and phenotypes - all characterized by social communication deficits and presence of restricted interests and repetitive behaviours (RRBs), the core symptoms in ASD. Language and intellectual capacities do not form ASD core symptoms although vary considerably. Accurate identification is challenging as ASD is often enmeshed with other neurodevelopmental disorders, and medical comorbidities, a situation now recognized as the rule rather than the exception in child psychiatry and developmental medicine. ASD is a disorder with varying performance and severity of symptoms over time, including unexpected loss of early skills, and lost diagnosis in some children following treatment. The review reiterates the urgency in accurate diagnosis in face of the rapid rise in ASD prevalence globally, and risk-increase in delayed or denied treatment with undesirable life-long consequences for most of the affected children. In addition, a call for change is advised to circumvent the ethical dilemma posed by the present "deficit model" in ASD diagnosis. Here, ASD prevalence is presented first, followed by emphasis on importance of accurate early diagnosis, and challenges in its accomplishment due to flaws in diagnostic instruments and other contributing factors. Next follow the required criteria for accurate identification, and its difficulties attributed to comorbid conditions, gender differences, and socio-economic and cultural influences. The conclusion includes future directions and a take away message.

sheet.es: Si el proceso de evaluación de tu hijo o hija parece lento o confuso, no es culpa tuya: identificar el autismo en la infancia es realmente complejo. Puede ayudar anotar ejemplos concretos del día a día, mencionar otras condiciones de salud o del desarrollo, y preguntar cómo se tienen en cuenta el género, la cultura y el idioma. Pedir una segunda opinión es razonable. Esta es una revisión temática de estudios publicados que analiza las dificultades del diagnóstico y critica el enfoque basado en déficits. Sus límites: no es una revisión sistemática, los artículos se eligieron a criterio de los autores y no aporta datos nuevos ni pautas válidas para cada niño.
sheet.en: If your child's assessment feels slow or confusing, it is not your fault: recognising autism in childhood is genuinely complex. It can help to write down concrete everyday examples, mention any other health or developmental conditions, and ask how gender, culture and language are taken into account. Asking for a second opinion is reasonable. This is a thematic review of published studies that examines why diagnosis is difficult and questions the deficit-focused approach. Its limits: it is not a systematic review, the authors chose the articles themselves, and it offers no new data or guidance that fits every child.
sheet.sv: Om utredningen av ditt barn känns långsam eller förvirrande är det inte ditt fel: att känna igen autism hos barn är verkligen komplext. Det kan hjälpa att skriva ner konkreta exempel från vardagen, nämna andra hälso- eller utvecklingsrelaterade tillstånd och fråga hur kön, kultur och språk vägs in. Att be om en second opinion är rimligt. Detta är en tematisk översikt av publicerade studier som belyser varför diagnostik är svår och ifrågasätter det bristfokuserade synsättet. Begränsningar: det är ingen systematisk översikt, författarna valde själva artiklarna och den ger inga nya data eller råd som passar alla barn.

title: Understanding the impact of dog ownership on autistic adults: implications for mental health and suicide prevention.
authors: Barcelos AM, Kargas N, Packham C, Mills DS
abstract: Mental health problems and suicide are more frequent in autistic adults than general population. Dog ownership can improve human well-being. This study aimed to generate a framework of well-being outcomes for dog-related activities in autistic adults and compare it to the framework generated for a general adult population. Thirty-six autistic dog owners (18-74 years old, 18 males) from diverse UK regions were interviewed and transcripts thematically analysed. 16.7% reported that their dogs prevented them from taking their own lives, mainly due to the dog's affection and the need to care for the animal. Close dog-owner interactions (e.g., cuddling, walking, dog's presence) were the most frequent activities improving emotions/moods and life functioning, whereas routine-like activities (e.g., feeding the animal) particularly enhanced life functioning. Well-being worsening was mainly linked to dog behaviour problems, dog poor health/death and obligations to the dog. Despite some negatives associated with ownership, having a dog could improve the well-being of many autistic adults and assist suicide prevention strategies in this high-risk group. The framework was consistent with that generated previously, indicating its robustness and the potential opportunity to focus on dog-related activities rather than the vague concept of "ownership" when considering the impact of ownership on well-being.

title: A Randomized Feasibility Trial of a Fundamental Motor Skill Parent-Mediated Intervention for Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders.
authors: Columna L, Prieto LA, Beach P, Russo N, Foley JT
journal: International journal of environmental research and public health
abstract: The purpose of this pilot study was to examine the feasibility of a fundamental motor skills (FMS) intervention with two groups on the acquisition of FMS of children with autism spectrum disorders (ASD). We randomly assigned families ( n = 15) of children with ASD aged 4-11 years into two groups (a workshop or a home-based group) focused on FMS development. Both groups participated in a 10-week intervention and were given the same instructional manual and adapted physical activity equipment. The workshop group also attended four in-person workshops targeting the needs of children with ASD and their parents. Children were tested on their FMS using the third edition of the Test of Gross Motor Development at the start and end of the intervention and then three months following the intervention. The recruitment rate was 50%, and the retention rate was 80% for all participants. The intervention for groups was safe and accepted by the participants as evaluated by post-program interviews. The outcomes of this pilot study suggest that parents can facilitate the acquisition of FMS of their children with ASD. Although these results are positive, there is a need to further identify effective interventions for FMS development in children with ASD.

sheet.es: Si quiere apoyar las habilidades motoras básicas (correr, lanzar, atrapar) de su hijo autista, puede practicarlas en casa con un manual sencillo y material de actividad física adaptado, en sesiones breves y a su ritmo. Este es un ensayo piloto aleatorizado con 15 familias de niños autistas de 4-11 años: durante 10 semanas, un grupo hizo talleres presenciales y otro trabajó en casa. La intervención fue segura y las familias la aceptaron; los resultados sugieren que madres y padres pueden facilitar estas habilidades. Es un estudio muy pequeño, pensado para ver si era viable, así que no demuestra eficacia ni sirve para todos los niños.
sheet.en: If you want to support your autistic child's fundamental motor skills, such as running, throwing and catching, you can practise them at home with a simple manual and adapted physical activity equipment, in short sessions at your child's pace. This was a randomized pilot trial with 15 families of autistic children aged 4-11 years: for 10 weeks, one group attended in-person workshops and the other worked at home. The programme was safe and families accepted it, and results suggest parents can help children build these skills. It was a very small study designed to test feasibility, so it cannot prove effectiveness or apply to every child.
sheet.sv: Om du vill stödja ditt autistiska barns grundläggande motoriska färdigheter, som att springa, kasta och fånga, kan ni öva hemma med en enkel manual och anpassad utrustning för fysisk aktivitet, i korta pass i barnets takt. Detta var en randomiserad pilotstudie med 15 familjer med autistiska barn i åldern 4-11 år: under 10 veckor gick en grupp på workshoppar och en annan arbetade hemma. Programmet var säkert och familjerna tyckte det fungerade, och resultaten tyder på att föräldrar kan underlätta dessa färdigheter. Studien var mycket liten och gjord för att pröva genomförbarhet, så den visar inte effekt och gäller inte alla barn.

title: Childhood diagnoses in individuals identified as autistics in adulthood.
authors: Rødgaard EM, Jensen K, Miskowiak KW, Mottron L
abstract: Background Autism is a developmental condition, where symptoms are expected to occur in childhood, but a significant number of individuals are diagnosed with autism for the first time in adulthood. Here, we examine diagnoses given in childhood among individuals that are diagnosed with autism in adulthood, to investigate whether the late autism diagnosis might be explained by misdiagnosis in childhood or diagnostic overshadowing. Methods Through the Danish National Patient Registry, we identified individuals diagnosed with autism in adulthood (N = 2199), as well as a control sample with no records of an autism diagnosis (N = 460,798) and calculated how many had received different psychiatric or neurological diagnoses in childhood. Results We found that most childhood diagnoses were overrepresented in those with an adult autism diagnosis, and attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder, affective disorders, anxiety, and stress disorders were the most prevalent childhood conditions in this group. However, 69% of males and 61% of females with adult autism diagnoses were not found to have received any of the investigated diagnoses before 18 years of age, and most childhood diagnoses were given after the age of 12. Limitations Milder to moderate cases of psychiatric conditions that have been solely treated by family physicians or school psychologists may not be fully included in our dataset. The study is based on data from the Danish health care system, and further research is needed to assess whether the findings can be generalized to other countries. Conclusion A majority of those with an adult autism diagnosis had no records of having received any of the investigated diagnoses in childhood. In these cases, the late autism diagnosis is therefore unlikely to be explained by either misdiagnosis or overshadowing. This result is at odds with the prevailing notion that autistic symptoms tend to diminish with age. Therefore, further research is warranted to examine how and if early signs of autism may have manifested among these individuals, and how similar they are to autistic people diagnosed earlier in their development.

sheet.es: Si una persona recibe el diagnóstico de autismo siendo adulta, conviene no asumir que en la infancia «se equivocaron». Puede ayudar recopilar recuerdos, informes escolares y observaciones de la familia, y compartirlos con el equipo evaluador. Este estudio usó registros de salud de Dinamarca: 2199 personas diagnosticadas de autismo en la adultez y un grupo de comparación. El 69% de los hombres y el 61% de las mujeres no tenían registrado ninguno de los diagnósticos investigados antes de los 18 años. Como límites, los casos más leves tratados solo por médicos de familia o psicólogos escolares pueden faltar, y los resultados quizá no valgan para otros países. No describe a todas las personas.
sheet.en: If someone is diagnosed autistic as an adult, it may not mean something was "missed" or mislabelled in childhood. It can help to gather memories, school reports and family observations and share them with the assessment team. This study used Danish health registry data: 2199 people diagnosed with autism in adulthood, plus a comparison group. 69% of males and 61% of females had no record of any of the investigated diagnoses before age 18. As limits, milder cases treated only by family doctors or school psychologists may be missing, and the findings may not apply in other countries. It does not describe every person.
sheet.sv: Om någon får en autismdiagnos som vuxen betyder det inte nödvändigtvis att något missades eller feltolkades i barndomen. Det kan hjälpa att samla minnen, skolintyg och familjens iakttagelser och dela dem med utredningsteamet. Studien använde danska registerdata: 2199 personer som fått autismdiagnos som vuxna, plus en jämförelsegrupp. 69% av männen och 61% av kvinnorna hade ingen registrerad av de undersökta diagnoserna före 18 års ålder. Begränsningar: mildare fall som bara behandlats av husläkare eller skolpsykologer kan saknas, och resultaten gäller kanske inte i andra länder. Studien beskriver inte alla personer.

title: An update on the cause and treatment of sleep disturbance in children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Seo WS
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by abnormalities in social communication/interaction and restrictive, repetitive patterns of behavior. ASD is a relatively common psychiatric disorder, with a prevalence of approximately 1.7% in children. Although many children and adolescents with ASD visit the hospital for medical help for emotional and behavioral problems such as mood instability and self-harming behavior, there are also many visits for sleep disturbances such as insomnia and sleep resistance. Sleep disturbances are likely to increase fatigue and daytime sleepiness, impaired concentration, negatively impact on daytime functioning, and pose challenges in controlling anger and aggressive behavior. Sleep disturbance in children and adolescents with ASD negatively affects the quality of life, nothing to say the quality of life of their families and school members. In this review, sleep disturbances that are common in children and adolescents with ASD and adolescents are presented. The developmental and behavioral impacts of sleep disturbances in ASD were also considered. Finally, non-pharmacological and pharmacological treatments for sleep disturbances in children and adolescents with ASD and adolescents are reviewed.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija autista duerme mal, conviene tomarlo en serio y comentarlo con su profesional de salud: el sueño puede influir en la concentración, el cansancio diurno y la regulación emocional. Puede empezar por observar rutinas y entorno de sueño y anotar lo que ve. Esta es una revisión de la literatura sobre niños y adolescentes autistas; menciona tratamientos no farmacológicos y farmacológicos, y las decisiones médicas corresponden a un clínico. No es un estudio con participantes propios y no sirve como regla para cada persona. Como el texto menciona autolesiones, si le preocupan, busque ayuda profesional en un servicio de salud o de crisis; ante peligro inmediato, llame al número de emergencias de su país.
sheet.en: If your autistic child or teen sleeps poorly, it is worth taking seriously and raising with a health professional: sleep can affect concentration, daytime tiredness and emotional regulation. You could start by noticing sleep routines and the sleep environment, and noting what you see. This is a review of the literature on autistic children and adolescents; it covers non-drug and drug treatments, and medical decisions belong to a clinician. It did not recruit its own participants and is not a rule for every person. Because the text mentions self-harm, if you are worried, seek professional help from a clinician, health service or crisis service; in immediate danger, call your country's emergency number.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn eller din tonåring sover dåligt är det värt att ta på allvar och ta upp med vården: sömnen kan påverka koncentration, trötthet på dagen och känsloreglering. Du kan börja med att se över sömnrutiner och sovmiljö och anteckna vad du ser. Detta är en översikt av litteraturen om autistiska barn och ungdomar; den tar upp behandlingar utan och med läkemedel, och medicinska beslut hör till en läkare. Den har inga egna deltagare och är ingen regel för alla. Eftersom texten nämner självskada: om du är orolig, sök professionell hjälp hos en läkare, vårdcentral eller krisjour; vid akut fara, ring ditt lands nödnummer.

title: The Brain-Gut-Microbiome System: Pathways and Implications for Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Chernikova MA, Flores GD, Kilroy E, Labus JS, Mayer EA, Aziz-Zadeh L
abstract: Gastrointestinal dysfunction is one of the most prevalent physiological symptoms of autism spectrum disorder (ASD). A growing body of largely preclinical research suggests that dysbiotic gut microbiota may modulate brain function and social behavior, yet little is known about the mechanisms that underlie these relationships and how they may influence the pathogenesis or severity of ASD. While various genetic and environmental risk factors have been implicated in ASD, this review aims to provide an overview of studies elucidating the mechanisms by which gut microbiota, associated metabolites, and the brain interact to influence behavior and ASD development, in at least a subgroup of individuals with gastrointestinal problems. Specifically, we review the brain-gut-microbiome system and discuss findings from current animal and human studies as they relate to social-behavioral and neurological impairments in ASD, microbiota-targeted therapies (i.e., probiotics, fecal microbiota transplantation) in ASD, and how microbiota may influence the brain at molecular, structural, and functional levels, with a particular interest in social and emotion-related brain networks. A deeper understanding of microbiome-brain-behavior interactions has the potential to inform new therapies aimed at modulating this system and alleviating both behavioral and physiological symptomatology in individuals with ASD.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista tiene molestias digestivas frecuentes, como dolor de barriga o estreñimiento, vale la pena anotarlas y comentarlas con su profesional de salud; el malestar físico puede influir en cómo se siente y se comporta. Esta es una revisión de estudios, en su mayoría preclínicos (con animales), junto con algunos estudios en personas, sobre la relación entre el intestino, la microbiota y el cerebro. Sus límites: se sabe poco sobre los mecanismos, no demuestra que la microbiota cause el autismo y puede aplicar solo a un subgrupo con problemas digestivos. Las decisiones sobre tratamientos corresponden a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If an autistic person often has digestive discomfort, such as tummy pain or constipation, it is worth noting it down and discussing it with a health professional; physical discomfort can affect how someone feels and acts. This is a review of studies, mostly preclinical (animal), plus some human studies, on how the gut, its microbes and the brain interact. Its limits: little is known about the mechanisms, it does not show that gut microbes cause autism, and it may apply only to a subgroup with gut problems. Decisions about treatments belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person ofta har magbesvär, som magont eller förstoppning, är det värt att anteckna dem och ta upp dem med vårdpersonal; fysiskt obehag kan påverka hur personen mår och agerar. Detta är en översikt av studier, mestadels prekliniska (djurstudier) samt några studier på människor, om hur tarmen, dess mikrober och hjärnan samspelar. Begränsningar: man vet lite om mekanismerna, den visar inte att tarmbakterier orsakar autism, och den kan gälla bara en undergrupp med magproblem. Beslut om behandlingar hör till en läkare.

title: A Review of Data Gathering Methods for Evaluating Socially Assistive Systems.
authors: Qiu S, An P, Kang K, Hu J, Han T, Rauterberg M
abstract: Social interactions significantly impact the quality of life for people with special needs (e.g., older adults with dementia and children with autism). They may suffer loneliness and social isolation more often than people without disabilities. There is a growing demand for technologies to satisfy the social needs of such user groups. However, evaluating these systems can be challenging due to the extra difficulty of gathering data from people with special needs (e.g., communication barriers involving older adults with dementia and children with autism). Thus, in this systematic review, we focus on studying data gathering methods for evaluating socially assistive systems (SAS). Six academic databases (i.e., Scopus, Web of Science, ACM, Science Direct, PubMed, and IEEE Xplore) were searched, covering articles published from January 2000 to July 2021. A total of 65 articles met the inclusion criteria for this systematic review. The results showed that existing SASs most often targeted people with visual impairments, older adults, and children with autism. For instance, a common type of SASs aimed to help blind people perceive social signals (e.g., facial expressions). SASs were most commonly assessed with interviews, questionnaires, and observation data. Around half of the interview studies only involved target users, while the other half also included secondary users or stakeholders. Questionnaires were mostly used with older adults and people with visual impairments to measure their social interaction, emotional state, and system usability. A great majority of observational studies were carried out with users in special age groups, especially older adults and children with autism. We thereby contribute an overview of how different data gathering methods were used with various target users of SASs. Relevant insights are extracted to inform future development and research.

sheet.es: Si alguien le propone una tecnología de apoyo social a una persona autista, conviene preguntar cómo se evaluó con las personas usuarias y si se les escuchó directamente. Esta es una revisión sistemática de 65 artículos publicados entre enero de 2000 y julio de 2021, sobre cómo se recogen datos para evaluar estos sistemas con personas con necesidades especiales, entre ellas niñas y niños autistas. Las entrevistas, los cuestionarios y la observación fueron los métodos más habituales. Límites: es una revisión de métodos, no prueba que estos sistemas funcionen, y no dice qué le conviene a cada persona.
sheet.en: If someone suggests a social-support technology for an autistic person, it helps to ask how it was evaluated and whether the people who use it were asked directly. This is a systematic review of 65 articles published from January 2000 to July 2021, looking at how data are gathered to evaluate these systems with people with special needs, including autistic children. Interviews, questionnaires and observation were the most common methods. Limits: it reviews methods, it does not show that these systems work, and it cannot say what suits any one person.
sheet.sv: Om någon föreslår en teknik för socialt stöd till en autistisk person är det bra att fråga hur den utvärderats och om användarna själva fått komma till tals. Detta är en systematisk översikt av 65 artiklar publicerade från januari 2000 till juli 2021, om hur data samlas in för att utvärdera sådana system med personer med särskilda behov, bland annat autistiska barn. Intervjuer, enkäter och observation var de vanligaste metoderna. Begränsningar: översikten gäller metoder, den visar inte att systemen fungerar och säger inte vad som passar en enskild person.

title: Self-reported parkinsonism features in older autistic adults: A descriptive study.
authors: Geurts HM, McQuaid GA, Begeer S, Wallace GL
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic adults without a suspected intellectual disability reported several motor features such as having tremors, and stiffness in one's legs which are considered to be part of a complex of motor features called parkinsonism. This so-called parkinsonism was remarkably prevalent in middle-aged and older autistic adults in two independent studies (Dutch study: 50-81 years, 183 males, 113 females, all adulthood diagnoses; the USA study: 50-83 years, 110 females, 109 males, majority adulthood diagnosis). Parkinsonism can be part of the progressive motor disease-Parkinson's disease. Therefore, it is important that future studies, including in-person neurological assessment, determine if (and if so, why) autistic adults who report these motor features are at increased risk for developing Parkinson's disease.

title: Participatory autism research: Early career and established researchers' views and experiences.
authors: Pickard H, Pellicano E, den Houting J, Crane L
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract 'Participatory autism research' refers to ways of involving autistic people and their allies (e.g. family members) in making decisions about research. These decisions can include what research gets done, how it gets done and how research findings are used. While there is more and more interest in participatory autism research, we know little about how researchers at different stages of their careers use this approach. To find out more, we discussed these issues with 25 researchers. Fourteen of these were at an early stage of their careers, and 11 were more senior researchers. We spoke to people in individual interviews or in groups. We then used a technique called thematic analysis to analyse our data, which involved us looking for common topics or 'themes' discussed by our participants. What did we find? Our participants told us that participatory autism research was a flexible approach, meaning that autistic people can be involved in research in many different ways. While people viewed this flexibility in a positive way, it also caused some confusion about what does or does not 'count' as participatory research. Our participants also spoke about how important it was to build relationships with those involved in their research, but they also said it could be difficult to communicate well with diverse groups of people who may not have much experience of research. Finally, our participants said it was hard to do participatory research when there was not much time, funding or support available to researchers. In this article, we discuss these findings, focusing on what needs to change to ensure that autistic people and their allies are meaningfully involved in autism research.

title: Face memory and face perception in autism.
authors: Stantić M, Ichijo E, Catmur C, Bird G
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract It is well known that some people with autism have difficulties recognizing faces. It is generally thought that this is not because autistic individuals cannot perceive faces, but because autistic individuals have greater problems than people without autism in remembering faces. Here, we worked with a group of autistic adults and a group of non-autistic adults to test their ability to perceive and remember faces. We also asked each person to report any difficulties that they have with recognizing faces in everyday life. We find that, as a group, people with autism have difficulties with both remembering and perceiving faces, and report more problems recognizing faces in everyday life. However, it is worth noting that we observed a wide range of scores in the group of people with autism, with some autistic participants scoring as well as the group of people without autism.

sheet.es: Si a una persona autista le cuesta reconocer caras, no es descuido ni desinterés: puede deberse tanto a cómo percibe los rostros como a cómo los recuerda. Mañana puedes presentarte por tu nombre al saludar, avisar quién va a venir y animar a usar pistas como la voz, la ropa o el contexto. Pregúntale cómo le va con las caras en su día a día. Evidencia: estudio que comparó a adultos autistas y no autistas en tareas de percepción y memoria de caras, junto con su experiencia cotidiana. Límites: solo participaron adultos y hubo mucha variación; algunas personas autistas puntuaron igual que el grupo no autista, así que no aplica a todos.
sheet.en: If an autistic person finds it hard to recognise faces, it is not carelessness or lack of interest: it may relate both to how faces are perceived and how they are remembered. Tomorrow, you could say your name when greeting, mention who is coming, and encourage using cues like voice, clothing or context. Ask how faces work for them in daily life. Evidence: a study comparing autistic and non-autistic adults on face perception and face memory tasks, plus their everyday experiences. Limits: only adults took part and scores varied widely; some autistic participants scored as well as the non-autistic group, so this does not apply to everyone.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person har svårt att känna igen ansikten handlar det inte om slarv eller ointresse: det kan hänga ihop både med hur ansikten uppfattas och hur de minns. I morgon kan du säga ditt namn när du hälsar, berätta vem som kommer och uppmuntra ledtrådar som röst, kläder eller sammanhang. Fråga hur ansikten fungerar för personen i vardagen. Evidens: en studie som jämförde autistiska och icke-autistiska vuxna i uppgifter om ansiktsuppfattning och ansiktsminne, samt deras vardagserfarenheter. Begränsningar: bara vuxna deltog och resultaten varierade mycket; vissa autistiska deltagare presterade lika bra som den icke-autistiska gruppen, så det gäller inte alla.

title: Objective and subjective psychosocial outcomes in adults with autism spectrum disorder: A 6-year longitudinal study.
authors: Scheeren AM, Buil JM, Howlin P, Bartels M, Begeer S
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Previous research has shown that relatively few adults with autism have a paid job or live on their own. However, outcomes also vary a lot and may depend on many different factors. In this study, we examined the level of functioning and happiness of 917 adults with autism (425 men and 492 women) aged 18-65 years. Most of them were of average to high intellectual ability. Over 6 years, we measured whether they had a paid job, close friendships and lived on their own (i.e. their objective functioning). We also measured how happy they felt. Objectively, most autistic adults did fairly to very well. Those with better objective outcomes (e.g. those with paid work) also tended to be happier. Most adults improved in objective functioning and happiness over 6 years. Participants with a lower intellectual ability, more autism traits, mental health problems and younger age had poorer objective outcomes. Participants with more autism traits and mental health problems were less happy. Autistic men and women functioned at similar levels and were equally happy. We found important factors that predict a better (or worse) outcome for autistic adults. Overall, compared with some previous research, our findings give a more positive picture of the outcomes for autistic adults with average to high intellectual abilities.

sheet.es: Pensar en el futuro de una persona autista adulta no tiene por qué centrarse solo en lo que le falta: conviene fijarse en el trabajo, las amistades, la vivienda y, sobre todo, en cómo se siente ella. Este estudio longitudinal siguió durante 6 años a 917 personas autistas de 18 a 65 años, la mayoría con capacidad intelectual media o alta. La mayoría tuvo resultados de aceptables a muy buenos y mejoró en funcionamiento y bienestar con el tiempo. Más rasgos autistas y problemas de salud mental se asociaron con menos bienestar, y esto puede orientar qué apoyos ofrecer. Límites: son asociaciones, no causas, y no representan a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: Thinking about an autistic adult's future doesn't have to focus only on what is missing: look at work, friendships, housing and, above all, how they feel themselves. This longitudinal study followed 917 autistic adults aged 18-65 for 6 years, most with average to high intellectual ability. Most did fairly to very well and improved in functioning and happiness over time. More autism traits and mental health problems were linked to lower happiness, which can help guide which supports to offer. Limits: these are associations, not causes, and the results do not apply to every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Att tänka på en autistisk vuxens framtid behöver inte handla bara om vad som saknas: titta på arbete, vänskap, boende och framför allt hur personen själv mår. Den här longitudinella studien följde 917 autistiska vuxna i åldern 18-65 i 6 år, de flesta med genomsnittlig till hög intellektuell förmåga. De flesta klarade sig ganska bra till mycket bra och förbättrades i funktion och lycka över tid. Fler autistiska drag och psykisk ohälsa hängde ihop med lägre lycka, vilket kan vägleda vilket stöd som erbjuds. Begränsningar: det rör sig om samband, inte orsaker, och resultaten gäller inte alla autistiska personer.

title: AUTS2 Gene: Keys to Understanding the Pathogenesis of Neurodevelopmental Disorders.
authors: Hori K, Shimaoka K, Hoshino M
abstract: Neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs), including autism spectrum disorders (ASD) and intellectual disability (ID), are a large group of neuropsychiatric illnesses that occur during early brain development, resulting in a broad spectrum of syndromes affecting cognition, sociability, and sensory and motor functions. Despite progress in the discovery of various genetic risk factors thanks to the development of novel genomics technologies, the precise pathological mechanisms underlying the onset of NDDs remain elusive owing to the profound genetic and phenotypic heterogeneity of these conditions. Autism susceptibility candidate 2 ( AUTS2 ) has emerged as a crucial gene associated with a wide range of neuropsychological disorders, such as ASD, ID, schizophrenia, and epilepsy. AUTS2 has been shown to be involved in multiple neurodevelopmental processes; in cell nuclei, it acts as a key transcriptional regulator in neurodevelopment, whereas in the cytoplasm, it participates in cerebral corticogenesis, including neuronal migration and neuritogenesis, through the control of cytoskeletal rearrangements. Postnatally, AUTS2 regulates the number of excitatory synapses to maintain the balance between excitation and inhibition in neural circuits. In this review, we summarize the knowledge regarding AUTS2, including its molecular and cellular functions in neurodevelopment, its genetics, and its role in behaviors.

sheet.es: Para mañana por la mañana: este estudio no ofrece nada que cambie la rutina diaria, pero ayuda a recordar que cada persona autista es distinta y que las causas biológicas son diversas. Es una revisión de la literatura sobre el gen AUTS2, que se asocia con autismo, discapacidad intelectual y otras condiciones, y que interviene en el desarrollo del cerebro. No incluye participantes propios. Sus límites: trata de genes y células, no de apoyos prácticos, y no sirve para explicar a una persona concreta. Las dudas médicas o genéticas conviene consultarlas con un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: For tomorrow morning: this study offers nothing that changes your daily routine, but it is a reminder that every autistic person is different and that the biology behind autism is diverse. It is a review of the literature on the AUTS2 gene, which is linked to autism, intellectual disability and other conditions, and which takes part in brain development. It has no participants of its own. Its limits: it is about genes and cells, not practical supports, and it cannot explain any one person. Medical or genetic questions are best raised with a clinician.
sheet.sv: Inför i morgon bitti: studien ger inget som ändrar vardagsrutinerna, men påminner om att varje autistisk person är olika och att biologin bakom autism är mångfacetterad. Det är en översikt av litteraturen om genen AUTS2, som kopplas till autism, intellektuell funktionsnedsättning och andra tillstånd och som är med i hjärnans utveckling. Den har inga egna deltagare. Begränsningar: den handlar om gener och celler, inte om praktiskt stöd, och kan inte förklara en enskild person. Medicinska eller genetiska frågor tas bäst upp med en läkare.

title: Workplace Adjustments for Autistic Employees: What is 'Reasonable'?
authors: Petty S, Tunstall L, Richardson H, Eccles N
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders

title: The role of alexithymia and autistic traits in predicting quality of life in an online sample.
authors: Mason D, Happé F
abstract: Background Autistic people tend to report poorer Quality of Life (QOL) than comparison groups, though some studies do report more optimistic findings. Higher autistic traits are also related to poorer QOL. However, the role of alexithymia in this relationship has not been explored. Method A total of 163 participants (N = 53 autistic and N = 111 comparison) consented to take part; however, 30 participants were excluded due to missing data (who did not differ from those who were retained on age, gender, education, employment, or living status), leaving a final sample of 133 (N = 42 Autistic and 91 Comparison participants). Demographic information (including age, gender) was collected, alongside self-report measures of autistic traits, mental health, alexithymia, and QOL. We estimated regression models based on pre-registered analysis, and we conducted exploratory network analyses. Results Alexithymic traits did not predict QOL when controlling for covariates. Depression significantly predicted Physical, Psychological, and Social QOL. When examining the impact of just alexithymic traits and autistic traits, both were significantly associated with Physical and Psychological QOL. For participants with a low depression score, the correlation between alexithymia and QOL was strong; suggesting that depression occludes the association between alexithymia and QOL. Network analyses suggested that depression and anxiety exert direct effects on Physical and Psychological QOL, whereas alexithymia scores may influence Physical QOL via autistic traits. Conclusion In sum, depression is a pervasive negative predictor of multiple QOL domains. The role of alexithymia in predicting QOL dimensionally and categorically was not ruled out, given our exploratory analyses, we suggest that interventions which target alexithymia may positively impact QOL for those who score low on depressive symptoms.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista dice que su calidad de vida es baja, conviene preguntar también por su estado de ánimo, como tristeza o desánimo, y por la ansiedad, y ofrecerle apoyo para eso. Entender y poner nombre a las emociones también puede importar. Es un estudio con cuestionarios en línea: 42 personas autistas y 91 de comparación. La depresión predijo varias áreas de la calidad de vida. Los autores señalan que la alexitimia no se descartó como factor. Sin embargo, el grupo es pequeño, los datos son de autoinforme y los análisis en red son exploratorios, así que no sirve como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If an autistic person reports a low quality of life, it is worth asking about their mood, such as low mood or hopelessness, and about anxiety, and offering support with those. Understanding and naming feelings may matter too. This was an online questionnaire study with 42 autistic and 91 comparison participants. Depression predicted several areas of quality of life, and the authors say alexithymia was not ruled out as a factor. However, the sample is small, the data are self-reported and the network analyses were exploratory, so this is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person uppger att livskvaliteten är låg är det värt att också fråga om humöret, som nedstämdhet, och om oro, och att erbjuda stöd kring det. Att förstå och sätta ord på känslor kan också spela roll. Detta var en webbaserad enkätstudie med 42 autistiska deltagare och 91 i jämförelsegruppen. Depression förutsade flera områden av livskvalitet, och författarna menar att alexitymi inte kunde uteslutas som faktor. Urvalet är dock litet, uppgifterna är självrapporterade och nätverksanalyserna var utforskande, så det är ingen regel för varje person.

title: Cost-utility analysis of LEGO based therapy for school children and young people with autism spectrum disorder: results from a randomised controlled trial.
authors: Wang HI, Wright BD, Bursnall M, Cooper C, Kingsley E, Le Couteur A, Teare D, Biggs K, McKendrick K, de la Cuesta GG, Chater T, Barr A, Solaiman K, Packham A, Marshall D, Varley D, Nekooi R, Gilbody S,
abstract: Objectives To assess the cost-effectiveness of LEGO-based therapy compared with usual support. Design Cost-utility analysis alongside randomised control trial. Setting Mainstream primary and secondary schools in the UK. Participants 248 children and young people (CYP) with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) aged 7-15 years. Intervention LEGO-based therapy is a group social skills intervention designed specifically for CYP with ASD. Through play, CYP learn to use the skills such as joint attention, sharing, communication and group problem-solving. CYP randomised to the intervention arm received 12 weekly sessions of LEGO-based therapy and usual support, while CYP allocated to control arm received usual support only. Main outcome measures Average costs based on National Health Service (NHS) and personal social services perspective and quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) measured by EQ-5D-Y over time horizon of 1 year were collected during the trial. Incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) was calculated, and non-parametric bootstrapping was conducted. The uncertainty around the ICER estimates was presented using cost-effectiveness acceptability curve (CEAC). A set of sensitivity analyses were conducted to assess the robustness of the primary findings. Results After adjustment and bootstrapping, on average, CYP in LEGO-based therapy group incurred less costs (incremental cost was -£251 (95% CI -£752 to £268)) and gained marginal improvement in QALYs (QALYs gained 0.009 (95% CI -0.008 to 0.028)). The CEAC shows that the probability of LEGO-based therapy being cost-effective was 94% at the willingness-to-pay threshold of £20 000 per QALY gained. Results of sensitivity analyses were consistent with the primary outcomes. Conclusion Compared with usual support, LEGO-based therapy produced marginal reduction in costs and improvement in QALYs. Results from both primary and sensitivity analyses suggested that LEGO-based therapy was likely to be cost-effective. Trial registration number ISRCTN64852382.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija autista disfruta construyendo, un grupo escolar de terapia con LEGO puede ser una opción de apoyo social que vale la pena consultar con el colegio. Se trabaja la atención compartida, la comunicación y la resolución de problemas en grupo mediante el juego. La evidencia procede de un análisis de costes dentro de un ensayo aleatorizado con 248 niños y jóvenes autistas de 7-15 años en escuelas del Reino Unido, con 12 sesiones semanales. Los autores hallaron un coste algo menor y una mejora mínima en calidad de vida, pero los intervalos de confianza incluyen cero y la mejora es marginal. No dice si funciona para cada persona; importa lo que la persona disfrute y necesite.
sheet.en: If your autistic child enjoys building, a school-based LEGO therapy group may be a social support option worth asking the school about. Through play, it works on joint attention, sharing, communication and group problem-solving. The evidence is a cost analysis within a randomised trial of 248 autistic children and young people aged 7-15 in UK schools, with 12 weekly sessions. The authors found slightly lower costs and a marginal gain in quality of life, but the confidence intervals include zero and the improvement was marginal. It cannot tell you whether it works for any one person; what they enjoy and need matters most.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn gillar att bygga kan en LEGO-terapigrupp i skolan vara ett socialt stöd värt att fråga skolan om. Genom lek övas delad uppmärksamhet, kommunikation och gemensam problemlösning. Underlaget är en kostnadsanalys inom en randomiserad studie med 248 autistiska barn och unga i åldern 7-15 i brittiska skolor, med 12 veckovisa tillfällen. Forskarna fann något lägre kostnader och en marginell förbättring i livskvalitet, men konfidensintervallen inkluderar noll och förbättringen var marginell. Studien säger inte om det fungerar för just din person; det som personen trivs med och behöver är viktigast.

title: The Psychological Impact of the COVID-19 Lockdown: A Comparison between Caregivers of Autistic and Non-Autistic Individuals in Italy.
authors: Fusar-Poli L, Martinez M, Surace T, Meo V, Patania F, Avanzato C, Signorelli MS, Aguglia E
abstract: The COVID-19 outbreak has disrupted the daily routine of the population worldwide, including autistic people and their caregivers, with severe consequences on mental health. On one hand, the reduced social contacts and the interruption of outpatient and daycare services during the lockdown have represented a real challenge for autistic people and their caregivers. On the other hand, confinement has allowed individuals to spend more time pursuing their interests and stay home with their family members without feeling the pressure of social expectations.
