The present study aimed to compare the levels of personal wellbeing, family distress, insomnia, and resilience between caregivers of autistic people and caregivers of people with other neurodevelopmental, psychiatric, or relational disabilities. A web survey was completed by 383 participants, of which 141 were primary caregivers of autistic people. We did not find any significant difference between caregivers of autistic and non-autistic people in any of the considered psychological variables. Lower age of the autistic family member and lower resilience levels were significantly associated with higher individual distress in the group of caregivers of autistic people. Our findings do not corroborate the hypothesis that caregivers of autistic individuals have had more severe consequences than other caregivers during the lockdown. However, they confirm the importance of promoting resilient coping strategies in autistic people and their caregivers.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista, ten presente que el cansancio o el malestar que sientas no indican que lo estés haciendo mal, y que apoyar formas de afrontar las dificultades que os funcionen puede ayudar. Se trata de una encuesta en línea en Italia durante el confinamiento por COVID-19, con 383 participantes, 141 de ellos cuidadores principales de personas autistas. No hubo diferencias significativas de bienestar, malestar familiar, insomnio ni resiliencia frente a quienes cuidaban a personas con otras discapacidades. Menor resiliencia y menor edad de la persona autista se asociaron con más malestar. Es una encuesta puntual: no prueba causas y no describe a todas las familias.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic person, remember that feeling tired or distressed does not mean you are doing something wrong, and building coping strategies that work for you both may help. This was an online survey in Italy during the COVID-19 lockdown, with 383 participants, 141 of them primary caregivers of autistic people. Caregivers of autistic people did not differ significantly in wellbeing, family distress, insomnia or resilience from caregivers of people with other disabilities. Lower resilience and a younger autistic family member were linked to more distress. It was a one-time survey, so it cannot show causes and does not describe every family.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person: att du känner dig trött eller pressad betyder inte att du gör fel, och det kan hjälpa att bygga strategier för att hantera svårigheter som fungerar för er båda. Detta var en webbenkät i Italien under covid-19-nedstängningen med 383 deltagare, varav 141 var huvudsakliga vårdgivare till autistiska personer. Det fanns inga signifikanta skillnader i välbefinnande, familjebelastning, sömnlöshet eller resiliens jämfört med dem som stöttade personer med andra funktionsnedsättningar. Lägre resiliens och yngre autistisk familjemedlem hängde ihop med mer belastning. Det var en enkät vid ett tillfälle, så den visar inte orsaker och beskriver inte alla familjer.

title: The Association between Parenting Stress, Positive Reappraisal Coping, and Quality of Life in Parents with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) Children: A Systematic Review.
authors: Ni'matuzahroh, Suen MW, Ningrum V, Widayat, Yuniardi MS, Hasanati N, Wang JH
abstract: Parents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) children generally suffer from poor coping and an impaired quality of life (QoL). This systematic review investigates parenting stress, positive reappraisal coping, and QoL in parents with ASD children. A literature search was carried out for publications written in English on the selected investigation topics using five databases, namely, Scopus, PubMed, Wiley, ScienceDirect Online, and EBSCO. Only studies investigating or measuring parenting stress, positive reappraisal coping, and QoL in ASD were included. Our results indicate that parents with ASD children have high stress levels. This is associated with the ineffective use of coping strategies and a low QoL. Adaptive coping strategies are related to a higher QoL, whereas maladaptive coping techniques are related to a worse QoL. Positive reappraisal coping is negatively correlated to meaningfulness, and it is used by parents to change their daily routines in order to motivate themselves towards new and evolving goals in life. Finally, we found a significant negative correlation between parenting stress, positive reappraisal coping, and the QoL of parents with ASD children. Positive reappraisal coping as a strategy helps parents adapt to stress and was found to be a potential mediatory function between parental stress and QoL.

sheet.es: Su bienestar también importa. Cuando el día se complica, puede ayudar detenerse y buscar otra forma de ver la situación: qué salió bien, qué aprendió, qué pequeña meta nueva es posible. Esto no significa negar el cansancio, y pedir apoyo práctico sigue siendo válido. En esta revisión, este tipo de afrontamiento, llamado reevaluación positiva, se relacionó con menos estrés y mejor calidad de vida. Se trata de una revisión sistemática de estudios publicados en inglés con madres y padres de niños autistas. Sus límites: muestra asociaciones, no causas, y no incluye la perspectiva de las personas autistas. Además, lo que ayuda a una familia puede no servir a otra.
sheet.en: Your wellbeing matters too. When a day gets hard, it can help to pause and look for another way to see the situation: what went well, what you learned, what small new goal is possible. This does not mean ignoring exhaustion, and asking for practical support is still valid. In this review, this kind of coping, called positive reappraisal, was linked to lower stress and better quality of life. It is a systematic review of English-language studies with parents of autistic children. Its limits: it shows associations, not causes, and it does not include autistic people's own perspectives. What helps one family may not help another.
sheet.sv: Ditt eget välmående spelar också roll. När en dag blir tung kan det hjälpa att stanna upp och se situationen på ett annat sätt: vad gick bra, vad lärde du dig, vilket litet nytt mål är möjligt? Det betyder inte att du ska förneka tröttheten, och att be om praktiskt stöd är fortfarande rimligt. I översikten var den här typen av hantering, kallad positiv omvärdering, kopplad till mindre stress och bättre livskvalitet. Det är en systematisk översikt av engelskspråkiga studier med föräldrar till autistiska barn. Begränsningar: den visar samband, inte orsaker, och saknar autistiska personers egna perspektiv. Det som hjälper en familj passar inte alltid en annan.

title: Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on Daily Life: Diverse Experiences for Autistic Adults.
authors: Maljaars J, Gijbels E, Evers K, Spain D, Rumball F, Happé F, Noens I
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders

title: Beyond Friendship: The Spectrum of Social Participation of Autistic Adults.
authors: Chan DV, Doran JD, Galobardi OD
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders

title: Catatonia in autism spectrum disorders: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Vaquerizo-Serrano J, Salazar De Pablo G, Singh J, Santosh P
journal: European psychiatry : the journal of the Association of European Psychiatrists
abstract: Background Catatonic features can appear in autism spectrum disorders (ASDs). There can be overlap in symptoms across catatonia and ASD. The overall aim of this review is to provide evidence for the presence of catatonic features in subjects with ASD. Methods A systematic literature search using the Web of Science database from inception to July 10, 2021 was conducted following PRISMA, MOOSE guidelines and the PROSPERO protocol. (CRD42021248615). Twelve studies with information about catatonia and ASD were reviewed. Data from a subset was used to conduct meta-analyses of the presence of catatonia in ASD. Results The systematic review included 12 studies, seven of which were used for the meta-analysis, comprising 969 individuals. The mean age was 21.25 (7.5) years. Two studies (16.6%) included only children and adolescents. A total of 70-100% were males. Our meta-analysis showed that 10.4% (5.8-18.0 95%CI) of individuals with ASD have catatonia. Motor disturbances were common in ASD subjects with catatonia. No differences were found in comorbidity. Several treatments have been used in ASD with catatonic features, including benzodiazepines, antipsychotics, and electroconvulsive therapy (ECT). The findings of the systematic review showed that ECT might help manage catatonic symptoms. Conclusions Different features of catatonia can exist in individuals with ASD and core symptoms of catatonia are reported in ASD. Longitudinal and longer-term studies are required to understand the relationship between catatonia and ASD, and the response of catatonic symptoms to treatment.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista muestra cambios marcados en el movimiento, como quedarse inmóvil, o pierde habilidades que tenía, conviene consultar pronto con un profesional clínico y anotar cuándo empezó. Es un metaanálisis con revisión sistemática de 12 estudios; siete entraron en el metaanálisis, con 969 personas. Estimó que 10.4% de las personas autistas tienen catatonia. Los tratamientos mencionados son médicos, y las decisiones sobre ellos corresponden a un clínico. Como límites, los estudios son pocos y el propio trabajo pide estudios más largos; no describe a cada persona autista.
sheet.en: If an autistic person shows marked changes in movement, such as freezing in place, or loses skills they had, it is worth seeing a clinician soon and noting when it started. This is a systematic review with a meta-analysis of 12 studies; seven were pooled, with 969 people. It estimated that 10.4% of autistic people have catatonia. Treatments mentioned are medical, and decisions about them belong to a clinician. As limits, the studies are few and the authors call for longer-term research; it does not describe every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person får tydliga förändringar i rörelser, till exempel att stelna till, eller förlorar färdigheter hen hade, är det värt att snart kontakta en läkare och notera när det började. Detta är en systematisk översikt med metaanalys av 12 studier; sju vägdes samman, med 969 personer. Den uppskattade att 10.4% av autistiska personer har katatoni. De behandlingar som nämns är medicinska, och beslut om dem hör till en kliniker. Begränsningar: studierna är få och forskarna efterlyser långsiktiga studier; resultaten beskriver inte varje autistisk person.

title: Autistic Adults May Be Erroneously Perceived as Deceptive and Lacking Credibility.
authors: Lim A, Young RL, Brewer N
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: We hypothesized that autistic adults may be erroneously judged as deceptive or lacking credibility due to demonstrating unexpected and atypical behaviors. Thirty autistic and 29 neurotypical individuals participated in video-recorded interviews, and we measured their demonstration of gaze aversion, repetitive body movements, literal interpretation of figurative language, poor reciprocity, and flat affect. Participants (N = 1410) viewed one of these videos and rated their perception of the individual's truthfulness or credibility. The hypothesis was partially supported, with autistic individuals perceived as more deceptive and less credible than neurotypical individuals when telling the truth. However, this relationship was not influenced by the presence of any of the target behaviors, but instead, by the individual's overall presentation.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista a una entrevista, una cita médica, una reunión escolar o un trámite legal, puede ayudar avisar con antelación de que su forma de comunicarse puede ser malinterpretada, y pedir que se valore lo que dice, no cómo lo dice. Preparar notas escritas o llevar a alguien de confianza también puede apoyar su voz. En este estudio, 30 adultos autistas y 29 no autistas fueron grabados en entrevistas, y 1410 personas valoraron su credibilidad: los autistas que decían la verdad fueron vistos como menos creíbles, por su presentación general y no por conductas concretas como evitar la mirada. Es un estudio con vídeos y pocos participantes grabados, así que no refleja todas las situaciones reales.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person at a job interview, medical visit, school meeting or legal process, it may help to explain in advance that their communication style can be misread, and to ask others to focus on what is said rather than how. Written notes or a trusted companion can also support their voice. In this study, 30 autistic and 29 non-autistic adults were video-recorded in interviews, and 1,410 viewers rated their credibility: autistic people telling the truth were seen as less credible, linked to their overall presentation rather than specific behaviours like avoiding eye contact. It used videos and a small number of recorded people, so it may not reflect every real-life situation.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person vid en anställningsintervju, ett läkarbesök, ett skolmöte eller en rättslig process kan det hjälpa att i förväg förklara att personens sätt att kommunicera kan misstolkas, och be andra fokusera på vad som sägs snarare än hur. Skriftliga anteckningar eller en betrodd person med kan också stärka personens röst. I studien filmades 30 autistiska och 29 icke-autistiska vuxna under intervjuer, och 1 410 personer bedömde deras trovärdighet: autistiska personer som talade sanning uppfattades som mindre trovärdiga, kopplat till helhetsintrycket snarare än enskilda beteenden som att undvika ögonkontakt. Studien byggde på filmer och få filmade deltagare, så den speglar inte alla verkliga situationer.

title: Understanding Camouflaging as a Response to Autism-Related Stigma: A Social Identity Theory Approach.
authors: Perry E, Mandy W, Hull L, Cage E
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Camouflaging refers to strategies used by autistic people to mask or hide social difficulties. The current study draws on Social Identity Theory to examine the relationship between camouflaging and autism-related stigma, testing the hypothesis that camouflaging represents an individualistic strategy in response to stigma. Two hundred and twenty-three autistic adults completed an online survey measuring perceived autism-related stigma, individualistic and collective strategies, camouflaging and mental wellbeing. Results indicated that higher camouflaging was positively associated with autism-related stigma and both individualistic and collective strategy use. Autism-related stigma was associated with lower wellbeing however this relationship was not mediated by camouflaging. These findings demonstrate how stigma contributes to camouflaging and highlight the complexities of navigating autistic identity while still camouflaging.

title: Self-reported camouflaging behaviours used by autistic adults during everyday social interactions.
authors: Cook J, Crane L, Hull L, Bourne L, Mandy W
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Camouflaging can be thought of as the process through which autistic people modify their natural social behaviours to adapt to, cope within or influence the largely neurotypical (non-autistic) social world. Many autistic people experience negative reactions to their natural or intuitive social behaviours when interacting with non-autistic people. Over time, in response to these negative reactions, autistic people's social behaviour often changes. We refer to autistic people's changed behaviours as 'camouflaging behaviours'. Research exploring camouflaging behaviours is still at an early stage. This study investigated camouflaging behaviours used by autistic adults in everyday social interactions using a research method that was new to the field of autism. Specifically, 17 autistic adults were filmed taking part in a common everyday social situation - a conversation with a stranger. With the help of the video of this conversation, they then showed and described their camouflaging behaviours to a researcher. These autistic people identified and described a total of 38 different camouflaging behaviours. The detailed and specific information provided by autistic adults about camouflaging behaviours generated important new insights into the ways in which autistic people adapt to, cope within and influence the neurotypical (non-autistic) social world.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista, puedes preguntarle con curiosidad cómo se siente al adaptar su comportamiento en conversaciones, sin juzgar y sin presionarla para que lo haga o lo deje. Respetar su ritmo y ofrecer espacios donde pueda ser ella misma puede ayudar. Evidencia: estudio con 17 adultos autistas, filmados en una conversación con una persona desconocida; después vieron el vídeo y describieron sus conductas de camuflaje, 38 en total. Límites: grupo pequeño, basado en lo que cada persona cuenta, y no muestra qué le conviene a cada persona ni se aplica a todas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person, you can ask them, with curiosity, how it feels to adapt their behaviour in conversations, without judging and without pressing them to do it or stop. Respecting their pace and offering spaces where they can be themselves may help. Evidence: a study with 17 autistic adults who were filmed in a conversation with a stranger, then watched the video and described their camouflaging behaviours, 38 in total. Limits: a small group, based on what each person reports, and it does not show what suits any one person or apply to everyone.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person kan du nyfiket fråga hur det känns att anpassa sitt beteende i samtal, utan att döma och utan att pressa personen att göra det eller sluta. Att respektera personens tempo och erbjuda miljöer där hen kan vara sig själv kan hjälpa. Evidens: en studie med 17 autistiska vuxna som filmades i ett samtal med en främling, tittade på videon och beskrev sina kamouflagebeteenden, 38 totalt. Begränsningar: en liten grupp, baserad på vad varje person berättar, och den visar inte vad som passar en enskild person eller gäller alla.

title: In their own words: The impact of subtle language and communication difficulties as described by autistic girls and boys without intellectual disability.
authors: Sturrock A, Chilton H, Foy K, Freed J, Adams C
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Subtle language and communication difficulties are experienced by many autistic individuals even when they do not have additional learning disabilities. These difficulties may affect a person's day-to-day living, social relationships and emotional well-being. However, currently, there is not much research into this topic. To date, no one has asked autistic children about their own language and communication difficulties or how they feel it affects them. Asking the children could provide valuable new insights. In this study, 12 autistic children (9-14 years), without learning disability, were interviewed on this topic. We developed interview questions, resources and interview procedures with the support of the autistic community. We also worked with an autistic researcher to analyse our results. We aimed to get the most genuine report of the autistic child's experiences. Our results showed that the children could give detailed insight into their language and communication difficulties if they were given the right support. They told us about how subtle language and communication difficulties affected their ability to learn, take part in certain activities and seek help. They talked about how subtle difficulties affect their ability to talk to new people, talk in groups and ultimately make friends. They also told us about the emotional upset that these subtle difficulties could have. They suggest that communication breakdown leads to negative feelings, but also that negative feelings can lead to more difficulties explaining themselves. The results of this study suggest that we should do more research on the effects of subtle language and communication difficulties. There are also implications for clinical practice. We should identify subtle language and communication difficulties through thorough assessment because these are often missed. We should also develop therapy and strategies that are aimed at individuals with subtle language and communication difficulties because this could help prevent additional difficulties with learning, help-seeking, friendship-making and emotional well-being.

sheet.es: Pregunte a su hijo o hija autista cómo le resulta hablar y explicarse, y ofrézcale apoyos para hacerlo: tiempo, preguntas concretas, quizá dibujos o tarjetas. Un estudio con entrevistas incluyó a 12 niñas y niños autistas de 9-14 años sin discapacidad intelectual; con el apoyo adecuado, describieron con detalle cómo las dificultades sutiles de lenguaje y comunicación influyen en aprender, pedir ayuda, hablar en grupo, hacer amigos y en sus emociones. Contaron que sentirse mal puede dificultar aún más explicarse. Es un grupo muy pequeño y no representa a todas las personas autistas; cada niño vive esto de forma distinta.
sheet.en: Ask your autistic child how talking and explaining themselves feels, and offer supports to help: time, concrete questions, perhaps drawings or cards. In an interview study, 12 autistic children aged 9-14 without learning disability described in detail how subtle language and communication difficulties affect learning, asking for help, talking in groups, making friends and emotions, once given the right support. They said feeling upset can make explaining even harder. The group was very small and cannot speak for all autistic people; every child experiences this differently.
sheet.sv: Fråga ditt autistiska barn hur det känns att prata och förklara sig, och erbjud stöd: tid, konkreta frågor, kanske teckningar eller kort. I en intervjustudie beskrev 12 autistiska barn i åldern 9-14 år utan intellektuell funktionsnedsättning i detalj hur subtila språk- och kommunikationssvårigheter påverkar lärande, att be om hjälp, att prata i grupp, att få vänner och känslorna, när de fick rätt stöd. De sa att känslomässig oro kan göra det ännu svårare att förklara sig. Gruppen var mycket liten och representerar inte alla autistiska personer; varje barn upplever detta olika.

title: A scoping review of telehealth diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Stavropoulos KK, Bolourian Y, Blacher J
abstract: Background Considering the COVID-19 pandemic, understanding the reliability, validity, social validity, and feasibility of using telehealth to diagnose ASD is a critical public health issue. This paper examines evidence supporting the use of telehealth methods to diagnose ASD and outlines the necessary modifications and adaptations to support telehealth diagnosis. Methods and procedures Studies were identified by searching PubMed and PsychInfo electronic databases and references lists of relevant articles. Only peer reviewed articles published in English with a focus on using telehealth for the purposes of diagnosing ASD were included. Searches were conducted through June 3rd, 2021. Outcomes and results A total of 10 studies were identified as meeting inclusion criteria. Of the eight papers that reported on reliability (e.g., accuracy), telehealth methods to diagnose ASD were between 80-91% accurate when compared with traditional in-person diagnosis. Six studies reported on validity (i.e., sensitivity and/or specificity). All six studies calculated sensitivity, with values ranging from 75% and 100%. Five of the six studies calculated specificity, with values ranging from 68.75% and 100%. The seven papers that reported social validity indicated that caregivers, as well as adult participants and clinicians, were mostly satisfied with telehealth. Feasibility was reported by seven studies and suggests that telehealth methods appear largely viable, though some challenges were reported. Conclusions and implications Although findings reviewed here are promising, more research is needed to verify the accuracy, validity, and feasibility of utilizing telehealth to diagnose ASD. Studies with larger sample sizes and samples across sites will be critical, as these will allow clinicians to identify subjects most likely to benefit from telehealth as well as those more likely to require an in-person assessment. This research is important not only due to the current pandemic, but also due to increased prevalence rates of ASD and an insufficient number of diagnostic providers-particularly in rural and/or otherwise under-served communities.

sheet.es: Si esperas una evaluación de autismo, puedes preguntar si ofrecen una opción por telesalud y si, en tu caso, bastaría o sería mejor una cita presencial. Una revisión de 10 estudios encontró que los métodos de telesalud coincidían con el diagnóstico presencial entre el 80-91% de las veces. Familias, personas autistas adultas y profesionales se mostraron en general satisfechas, aunque se señalaron algunas dificultades. Los límites: son pocos estudios, con muestras pequeñas, y los autores indican que hace falta más investigación para saber a quién le conviene la telesalud y a quién una evaluación presencial.
sheet.en: If you are waiting for an autism assessment, you can ask whether a telehealth option is offered, and whether it would be enough in your case or an in-person visit would suit better. A review of 10 studies found telehealth methods matched in-person diagnosis 80-91% of the time. Caregivers, autistic adults and clinicians were mostly satisfied, though some difficulties were reported. The limits: there are few studies with small samples, and the authors say more research is needed to learn who benefits from telehealth and who needs an in-person assessment.
sheet.sv: Om du väntar på en autismutredning kan du fråga om det finns ett alternativ via telehälsa, och om det skulle räcka i ditt fall eller om ett besök på plats passar bättre. En översikt av 10 studier fann att telehälsometoder stämde med diagnos på plats 80-91% av gångerna. Vårdnadshavare, autistiska vuxna och kliniker var i huvudsak nöjda, men vissa svårigheter rapporterades. Begränsningar: det finns få studier med små urval, och författarna menar att mer forskning behövs för att veta vem som har nytta av telehälsa och vem som behöver bedömning på plats.

title: The Vocabulary of Infants with an Elevated Likelihood and Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Infant Language Studies Using the CDI and MSEL.
authors: Belteki Z, Lumbreras R, Fico K, Haman E, Junge C
journal: International journal of environmental research and public health
abstract: Diagnoses of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) are typically accompanied by atypical language development, which can be noticeable even before diagnosis. The siblings of children diagnosed with ASD are at elevated likelihood for ASD diagnosis and have been shown to have higher prevalence rates than the general population. In this paper, we systematically reviewed studies looking at the vocabulary size and development of infants with autism. One inclusion criterion was that infants were grouped either pre-diagnostically as elevated or typical likelihood or post-diagnostically as ASD or without ASD. This review focused on studies that tested infants up to 24 months of age and that assessed vocabulary either via the parent-completed MacArthur-Bates Communicative Developmental Inventory (CDI) or the clinician-administered Mullen Scales of Early Learning (MSEL). Our systematic search yielded 76 studies. A meta-analysis was performed on these studies that compared the vocabulary scores of EL and TL infants pre-diagnostically and the scores of ASD and non-ASD infants post-diagnostically. Both pre- and post-diagnostically, it was found that the EL and ASD infants had smaller vocabularies than their TL and non-ASD peers, respectively. The effect sizes across studies were heterogenous, prompting additional moderator analyses of age and sub-group analyses of the language measure used (CDI or MSEL) as potential moderators of the effect size. Age was found to be a moderator both in the pre- and post-diagnostical groups, however, language measure was not a moderator in either diagnostic group. Interpretations and future research directions are discussed based on these findings.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a un bebé autista o con hermanos autistas, recuerda que un vocabulario más pequeño en los primeros meses es una pauta frecuente en grupo, no una regla para cada niño. Observa cómo se comunica con gestos, sonidos y miradas, y comenta dudas con su pediatra. Es un metaanálisis de 76 estudios con bebés de hasta 24 meses; en promedio, quienes tenían mayor probabilidad de autismo o un diagnóstico tenían vocabularios más pequeños, y la edad influía en la diferencia. Los resultados variaron mucho entre estudios y los promedios no describen a cada bebé.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic baby or one with an autistic sibling, a smaller vocabulary in the first months is a common pattern across groups, not a rule for every child. Notice how your child communicates through gestures, sounds and looks, and bring any questions to their paediatrician. This is a meta-analysis of 76 studies with infants up to 24 months; on average, infants with an elevated likelihood of autism or a diagnosis had smaller vocabularies, and age influenced the gap. Results varied a lot between studies, and group averages do not describe any single baby.
sheet.sv: Om du tar hand om en autistisk bebis eller en bebis med autistiskt syskon är ett mindre ordförråd under de första månaderna ett vanligt mönster i grupp, inte en regel för varje barn. Lägg märke till hur barnet kommunicerar med gester, ljud och blickar, och ta upp frågor med barnets barnläkare. Detta är en metaanalys av 76 studier med spädbarn upp till 24 månader. I genomsnitt hade barn med förhöjd sannolikhet för autism eller diagnos mindre ordförråd, och åldern påverkade skillnaden. Resultaten varierade mycket mellan studierna, och gruppgenomsnitt beskriver inte ett enskilt barn.

title: The Human Gut Microbiome as a Potential Factor in Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Alharthi A, Alhazmi S, Alburae N, Bahieldin A
abstract: The high prevalence of gastrointestinal (GI) disorders among autism spectrum disorder (ASD) patients has prompted scientists to look into the gut microbiota as a putative trigger in ASD pathogenesis. Thus, many studies have linked the gut microbial dysbiosis that is frequently observed in ASD patients with the modulation of brain function and social behavior, but little is known about this connection and its contribution to the etiology of ASD. This present review highlights the potential role of the microbiota-gut-brain axis in autism. In particular, it focuses on how gut microbiota dysbiosis may impact gut permeability, immune function, and the microbial metabolites in autistic people. We further discuss recent findings supporting the possible role of the gut microbiome in initiating epigenetic modifications and consider the potential role of this pathway in influencing the severity of ASD. Lastly, we summarize recent updates in microbiota-targeted therapies such as probiotics, prebiotics, dietary supplements, fecal microbiota transplantation, and microbiota transfer therapy. The findings of this paper reveal new insights into possible therapeutic interventions that may be used to reduce and cure ASD-related symptoms. However, well-designed research studies using large sample sizes are still required in this area of study.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista tiene molestias digestivas frecuentes, vale la pena anotarlas y comentarlas con su médico o pediatra, sin esperar que cambiar la dieta o tomar suplementos cambie su forma de ser. Esto es una revisión que reúne estudios sobre la relación entre la flora intestinal, el cerebro y el sistema inmune en personas autistas. Sus límites: el vínculo aún se conoce poco, no prueba causa y los propios autores piden estudios mejor diseñados y con muestras grandes. Cualquier decisión médica o de tratamiento corresponde a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If an autistic person often has stomach or bowel discomfort, it is worth noting it down and raising it with their doctor or paediatrician, without expecting that changing diet or adding supplements will change who they are. This is a review that gathers studies on links between gut bacteria, the brain and the immune system in autistic people. Its limits: the connection is still poorly understood, it does not prove cause, and the authors themselves call for better-designed studies with large samples. Any medical or treatment decision belongs with a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person ofta har ont i magen eller problem med tarmen är det värt att anteckna det och ta upp det med läkaren eller barnläkaren, utan att förvänta sig att ändrad kost eller kosttillskott förändrar vem personen är. Detta är en översikt som samlar studier om kopplingar mellan tarmbakterier, hjärna och immunförsvar hos autistiska personer. Begränsningar: sambandet är fortfarande dåligt känt, det visar inte orsak, och författarna efterlyser själva bättre utformade studier med stora urval. Medicinska beslut och behandlingsbeslut hör hemma hos en läkare.

title: Autism and chronic ill health: an observational study of symptoms and diagnoses of central sensitivity syndromes in autistic adults.
authors: Grant S, Norton S, Weiland RF, Scheeren AM, Begeer S, Hoekstra RA
abstract: Background Autistic adults, particularly women, are more likely to experience chronic ill health than the general population. Central sensitivity syndromes (CSS) are a group of related conditions that are thought to include an underlying sensitisation of the central nervous system; heightened sensory sensitivity is a common feature. Anecdotal evidence suggests autistic adults may be more prone to developing a CSS. This study aimed to investigate the occurrence of CSS diagnoses and symptoms in autistic adults, and to explore whether CSS symptoms were related to autistic traits, mental health, sensory sensitivity, or gender. Methods The full sample of participants included 973 autistic adults (410 men, 563 women, mean age = 44.6) registered at the Netherlands Autism Register, who completed questionnaires assessing autistic traits, sensory sensitivity, CSS, physical and mental health symptoms. The reliability and validity of the Central Sensitization Inventory (CSI) in an autistic sample was established using exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses. Chi 2 analyses, independent t-tests, hierarchical regression and path analysis were used to analyse relationships between CSS symptoms, autistic traits, measures of mental health and wellbeing, sensory sensitivity, age and gender. Results 21% of participants reported one or more CSS diagnosis, and 60% scored at or above the clinical cut-off for a CSS. Autistic women were more likely to report a CSS diagnosis and experienced more CSS symptoms than men. Sensory sensitivity, anxiety, age and gender were significant predictors of CSS symptoms, with sensory sensitivity and anxiety fully mediating the relationship between autistic traits and CSS symptoms. Limitations Although this study included a large sample of autistic adults, we did not have a control group or a CSS only group. We also could not include a non-binary group due to lack of statistical power. Conclusions CSS diagnoses and symptoms appear to be very common in the autistic population. Increased awareness of an association between autism and central sensitisation should inform clinicians and guide diagnostic practice, particularly for women where CSS are common and autism under recognised.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta tiene dolor, fatiga u otros síntomas físicos persistentes, vale la pena anotarlos junto con la sensibilidad sensorial y la ansiedad, y llevar esas notas a su médico o médica. Es un estudio observacional con 973 personas autistas adultas del registro neerlandés que respondieron cuestionarios. El 21% refirió algún diagnóstico de síndrome de sensibilización central y el 60% alcanzó o superó el punto de corte clínico; las mujeres refirieron más síntomas. No hubo grupo de comparación ni grupo no binario, y los datos no prueban causas ni valen para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult has ongoing pain, fatigue or other physical symptoms, it can help to note them alongside sensory sensitivity and anxiety, and bring those notes to their doctor. This was an observational study of 973 autistic adults from the Netherlands Autism Register who completed questionnaires. 21% reported one or more central sensitivity syndrome diagnoses and 60% scored at or above the clinical cut-off; women reported more symptoms. There was no comparison group and no non-binary group, so the findings show links, not causes, and do not apply to everyone.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen har ihållande smärta, trötthet eller andra kroppsliga symtom kan det hjälpa att anteckna dem tillsammans med sensorisk känslighet och ångest och ta med anteckningarna till läkaren. Studien var en observationsstudie med 973 autistiska vuxna från det nederländska autismregistret som besvarade enkäter. 21% uppgav minst en diagnos på central sensitiseringssyndrom och 60% nådde eller översteg den kliniska gränsen; kvinnor uppgav fler symtom. Det fanns ingen jämförelsegrupp och ingen icke-binär grupp, så resultaten visar samband, inte orsaker, och gäller inte alla.

title: Mortality in Persons With Autism Spectrum Disorder or Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
authors: Catalá-López F, Hutton B, Page MJ, Driver JA, Ridao M, Alonso-Arroyo A, Valencia A, Macías Saint-Gerons D, Tabarés-Seisdedos R
abstract: Importance Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) are childhood-onset disorders that may persist into adulthood. Several studies have suggested that they may be associated with an increased risk of mortality; however, the results are inconsistent. Objective To assess the risk of mortality among persons with ASD or ADHD and their first-degree relatives. Data sources A search of MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and PsycINFO (published from inception to April 1, 2021) was supplemented by searching reference lists of the retrieved articles. Study selection Cohort and case-control studies that reported mortality rate ratios (RRs) in persons with ASD or ADHD and/or their first-degree relatives compared with the general population or those without ASD/ADHD were included. Data extraction and synthesis Screening, data extraction, and quality assessment were performed by at least 2 researchers independently. A random-effects model was used to meta-analyze individual studies and assessed heterogeneity (I2). Main outcomes and measures All-cause mortality in association with ASD or ADHD. Secondary outcome was cause-specific mortality. Results Twenty-seven studies were included, with a total of 642 260 individuals. All-cause mortality was found to be higher for persons with ASD (154 238 participants; 12 studies; RR, 2.37; 95% CI, 1.97-2.85; I2, 89%; moderate confidence) and persons with ADHD (396 488 participants; 8 studies; RR, 2.13; 95% CI, 1.13-4.02; I2, 98%; low confidence) than for the general population. Among persons with ASD, deaths from natural causes (4 studies; RR, 3.80; 95% CI, 2.06-7.01; I2, 96%; low confidence) and deaths from unnatural causes were increased (6 studies; RR, 2.50; 95% CI, 1.49-4.18; I2, 95%; low confidence). Among persons with ADHD, deaths from natural causes were not significantly increased (4 studies; RR, 1.62; 95% CI, 0.89-2.96; I2, 88%; low confidence), but deaths from unnatural causes were higher than expected (10 studies; RR, 2.81; 95% CI, 1.73-4.55; I2, 92%; low confidence). Conclusions and relevance This systematic review and meta-analysis found that ASD and ADHD are associated with a significantly increased risk of mortality. Understanding the mechanisms of these associations may lead to targeted strategies to prevent avoidable deaths in high-risk groups. The substantial heterogeneity between studies should be explored further.

sheet.es: Conviene que las personas autistas o con TDAH tengan acceso regular a atención médica y apoyo en salud mental, y que quienes las acompañan presten atención a señales de malestar físico o emocional y las comuniquen a profesionales sanitarios. Se trata de un metaanálisis que reunió 27 estudios de cohortes y casos y controles, con 642 260 personas. Encontró un mayor riesgo de mortalidad que en la población general: RR 2,37 en autismo y 2,13 en TDAH. Sus límites: los estudios difieren mucho entre sí, la confianza en varios resultados es baja y no explica las causas. Son promedios de grupo, no predicen lo que le ocurrirá a cada persona.
sheet.en: Make sure autistic people and people with ADHD have regular access to healthcare and mental health support, and that caregivers notice signs of physical or emotional distress and raise them with health professionals. This was a meta-analysis of 27 cohort and case-control studies, with 642,260 people. It found a higher risk of death than in the general population: RR 2.37 for autism and 2.13 for ADHD. Limits: the studies differed a lot from one another, confidence in several results was low, and it cannot explain the causes. These are group averages and do not predict what will happen to any one person.
sheet.sv: Se till att autistiska personer och personer med ADHD har regelbunden tillgång till sjukvård och stöd för psykisk hälsa, och att anhöriga uppmärksammar tecken på fysiskt eller känslomässigt obehag och tar upp dem med vårdpersonal. Detta var en metaanalys av 27 kohort- och fall-kontrollstudier med 642 260 personer. Den fann högre risk för död än i den allmänna befolkningen: RR 2,37 vid autism och 2,13 vid ADHD. Begränsningar: studierna skilde sig mycket åt, tilliten till flera resultat var låg och orsakerna förklaras inte. Det är gruppmedelvärden och förutsäger inte vad som händer en enskild person.

title: Evaluating the Potential Use of Serotonergic Psychedelics in Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Markopoulos A, Inserra A, De Gregorio D, Gobbi G
abstract: Recent clinical and preclinical evidence points towards empathogenic and prosocial effects elicited by psychedelic compounds, notably the serotonin 5-HT 2A agonists lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD), psilocybin, N,N-Dimethyltryptamine (DMT), and their derivatives. These findings suggest a therapeutic potential of psychedelic compounds for some of the behavioural traits associated with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), a neurodevelopmental condition characterized by atypical social behaviour. In this review, we highlight evidence suggesting that psychedelics may potentially ameliorate some of the behavioural atypicalities of ASD, including reduced social behaviour and highly co-occurring anxiety and depression. Next, we discuss dysregulated neurobiological systems in ASD and how they may underlie or potentially limit the therapeutic effects of psychedelics. These phenomena include: 1) synaptic function, 2) serotonergic signaling, 3) prefrontal cortex activity, and 4) thalamocortical signaling. Lastly, we discuss clinical studies from the 1960s and 70s that assessed the use of psychedelics in the treatment of children with ASD. We highlight the positive behavioural outcomes of these studies, including enhanced mood and social behaviour, as well as the adverse effects of these trials, including increases in aggressive behaviour and dissociative and psychotic states. Despite preliminary evidence, further studies are needed to determine whether the benefits of psychedelic treatment in ASD outweigh the risks associated with the use of these compounds in this population, and if the 5-HT 2A receptor may represent a target for social-behavioural disorders.

sheet.es: Este artículo no ofrece nada que hacer mañana por la mañana: no hay pruebas suficientes para usar psicodélicos en personas autistas, y las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico. Es una revisión de la literatura, no un ensayo nuevo; reúne estudios previos, entre ellos ensayos con niños autistas de los años 1960 y 70. Esos trabajos describieron mejor ánimo y conducta social, pero también más agresividad y estados disociativos y psicóticos. Los límites son claros: la evidencia es preliminar, antigua y no sirve como regla para cada persona. Los propios autores piden más estudios.
sheet.en: This paper offers nothing to act on tomorrow morning: the evidence is not enough to support psychedelics for autistic people, and medical decisions belong to a clinician. It is a review of the literature, not a new trial, and it gathers earlier work, including studies with autistic children from the 1960s and 70s. Those reported better mood and social behaviour, but also more aggression and dissociative and psychotic states. The limits are clear: the evidence is preliminary, old, and cannot serve as a rule for any individual. The authors themselves call for further studies.
sheet.sv: Den här artikeln ger inget att göra i morgon bitti: underlaget räcker inte för att använda psykedelika för autistiska personer, och medicinska beslut hör till en läkare. Det är en översikt av litteraturen, inte en ny studie, och den samlar tidigare arbeten, bland annat studier med autistiska barn från 1960- och 70-talen. De beskrev bättre humör och socialt beteende, men också mer aggression samt dissociativa och psykotiska tillstånd. Begränsningarna är tydliga: underlaget är preliminärt, gammalt och kan inte användas som regel för en enskild person. Författarna efterlyser själva fler studier.

title: Effectiveness of music therapy for autism spectrum disorder, dementia, depression, insomnia and schizophrenia: update of systematic reviews.
authors: Gassner L, Geretsegger M, Mayer-Ferbas J
abstract: Background Music therapy (MT) aims at maintaining, restoring and furthering physical/emotional/mental health. This review assesses effectiveness of MT and its methods for autism spectrum disorder (ASD), dementia, depression, insomnia and schizophrenia. Methods A search for systematic reviews and health technology assessment reports was conducted and yielded 139 hits. Given the large amount, we focused on five frequent diagnostic groups with available Cochrane reviews. A second search was conducted in four databases. Two authors independently performed study selection, data extraction and assessed methodological quality. Only trials with moderate/low risk of bias (RoB) were selected. Results Ten randomized controlled trials (1.248 participants) met inclusion criteria. For schizophrenia, no studies with low/moderate RoB were found; therefore, updating was not possible. The Cochrane authors stated that quality of life (QoL), social functioning, global/mental state improved for schizophrenia, but not global functioning. For ASD, MT improved behaviour, social communication, brain connectivity and parent-child relationship. For depression, mood was enhanced, and for insomnia, sleep quality, stress, anxiety, total sleep time, disease severity and psychological QoL improved. MT positively affected mood, neuropsychiatric behaviour, apathy, communication and physical functions for dementia; behavioural/psychological symptoms improved only in severe, and memory and verbal fluency only in mild Alzheimer's disease. Cognition improved for dementia in one of four studies. Both active (playing music) and receptive (listening to music) methods were used for dementia, whereas for ASD and depression, active methods were applied. For insomnia, only receptive methods were used. Conclusion These findings provide evidence that MT helps patients improving their physical/psychosocial health. More research investigating long-term effects is needed.

sheet.es: Si la música ya es parte de la vida de la persona autista a la que cuidas, puedes probar sesiones de música compartidas, como tocar o cantar juntos, y observar con calma si le resultan agradables. Es una revisión sistemática de ensayos aleatorizados: para el autismo, la terapia musical mejoró la conducta, la comunicación social, la conectividad cerebral y la relación entre padres e hijos. Es una revisión que abarcó cinco condiciones y diez ensayos con 1.248 participantes en total, así que la información específica sobre autismo es limitada. Los autores piden más estudios sobre efectos a largo plazo. No sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If music is already part of the life of the autistic person you support, you could try shared music time, such as playing or singing together, and calmly notice whether they enjoy it. This is a systematic review of randomized trials: for autism, music therapy improved behaviour, social communication, brain connectivity and the parent-child relationship. The review covered five conditions and ten trials with 1.248 participants in total, so the autism-specific evidence is limited. The authors call for more research on long-term effects. It is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om musik redan är en del av livet för den autistiska person du stöttar kan du prova gemensam musikstund, till exempel att spela eller sjunga tillsammans, och lugnt se om personen trivs med det. Detta är en systematisk översikt av randomiserade studier: för autism förbättrade musikterapi beteende, social kommunikation, hjärnans konnektivitet och relationen mellan förälder och barn. Översikten omfattade fem tillstånd och tio studier med 1.248 deltagare totalt, så underlaget om autism är begränsat. Forskarna efterlyser mer forskning om långtidseffekter. Det är ingen regel för alla.

title: Dopamine in Autism Spectrum Disorders-Focus on D2/D3 Partial Agonists and Their Possible Use in Treatment.
authors: Mandic-Maravic V, Grujicic R, Milutinovic L, Munjiza-Jovanovic A, Pejovic-Milovancevic M
abstract: Autism spectrum disorders (ASD) are a group of disorders characterized by impairment in social communication and repetitive and stereotyped behaviors. ASD etiology is very complex, including the effect of both genetic and environmental factors. So far, no specific treatment for the core symptoms of ASD has been developed, although attempts have been made for the treatment of repetitive behavior. The pharmacological treatment is aimed at treating non-specific symptoms such as irritability and aggression. Recent studies pointed out to the possible role of altered dopamine signaling in mesocorticolimbic and nigrostriatal circuits in ASD. In addition, several research pointed out to the association of dopamine receptors polymorphism and ASD, specifically repetitive and stereotyped behavior. In this paper, we will provide a review of the studies regarding dopamine signaling in ASD, existing data on the effects of D2/D3 partial agonists in ASD, possible implications regarding their individual receptor profiles, and future perspectives of their possible use in ASD treatment.

sheet.es: Esta revisión trata de medicamentos, así que es un estudio médico y cualquier decisión sobre ellos corresponde a un profesional clínico. Lo útil mañana: si le preocupa algo del día a día de una persona autista, anote cuándo ocurre y qué lo rodea, y llévelo a la consulta. La evidencia es una revisión de estudios sobre la señalización de la dopamina en el autismo, sin participantes propios. Sus límites: resume investigaciones previas y plantea posibilidades futuras, no confirma que algo funcione. Tampoco describe a todas las personas autistas, que son muy distintas entre sí.
sheet.en: This review is about medicines, so it is a medical study, and any decision about them belongs to a clinician. What helps tomorrow: if something in an autistic person's day worries you, note when it happens and what surrounds it, and bring those notes to an appointment. The evidence is a review of earlier studies on dopamine signalling in autism, with no participants of its own. Its limits: it summarises past research and points to future possibilities, so it does not confirm that anything works. It also does not describe every autistic person, as autistic people differ greatly.
sheet.sv: Den här översikten handlar om läkemedel, så det är en medicinsk studie, och alla beslut om dem hör till en läkare. Det som hjälper i morgon: om något i en autistisk persons dag oroar dig, anteckna när det sker och vad som finns runt omkring, och ta med anteckningarna till ett besök. Underlaget är en översikt av tidigare studier om dopaminsignalering vid autism, utan egna deltagare. Begränsningar: den sammanfattar tidigare forskning och pekar på framtida möjligheter, så den visar inte att något fungerar. Den beskriver heller inte alla autistiska personer, som skiljer sig mycket åt.

title: "It's Not Just in My Head, and It's Not Just Irrelevant": Autistic Negotiations of Menopausal Transitions.
authors: Karavidas M, de Visser RO
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Physical and psychological changes during menopause can be especially tumultuous for autistic people: difficulties with sensory sensitivity and daily functioning may be exacerbated. Through individual interviews, we examined the language used by seven peri- or post-menopausal autistic people to construct their experiences, and to consider the implications for their wellbeing and identities. Our analysis, which utilised thematic decomposition, yielded three discursive themes. The theme "Uncertainty about Changes" addressed how limited awareness and understanding of menopause combined with difficulties recognising internal states. However, with "Growing Self-Awareness and Self-Care", some participants made conscious efforts to resist negative societal constructions of both autism and menopause. The theme "Navigating Support Options" addressed the interpersonal and systemic barriers participants faced when seeking support. There is a need for accessible information for autistic people experiencing menopause, and greater professional awareness.

sheet.es: Si cuidas o acompañas a una persona autista en la menopausia, créele cuando describa cambios y ayúdale a buscar información accesible y profesionales que conozcan ambas realidades. Puede costar reconocer lo que ocurre en el cuerpo, así que hablar de ello con calma ayuda. La evidencia viene de entrevistas individuales a siete personas autistas en la perimenopausia o posmenopausia, que describieron incertidumbre, autocuidado creciente y barreras para encontrar apoyo. Es un grupo muy pequeño y sus experiencias no representan a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person going through menopause, believe them when they describe changes, and help them find accessible information and professionals who understand both autism and menopause. Recognising what is happening in the body can be hard, so talking about it calmly can help. The evidence comes from individual interviews with seven autistic people who were peri- or post-menopausal. They described uncertainty, growing self-care and barriers to finding support. It is a very small group, and their experiences do not represent every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person under klimakteriet: tro på hen när hen beskriver förändringar, och hjälp till att hitta lättillgänglig information och yrkespersoner som förstår både autism och klimakteriet. Det kan vara svårt att känna igen vad som händer i kroppen, så lugna samtal om det kan hjälpa. Underlaget är individuella intervjuer med sju autistiska personer i eller efter övergångsåldern. De beskrev osäkerhet, växande egenvård och hinder när de sökte stöd. Gruppen är mycket liten och deras erfarenheter gäller inte alla autistiska personer.

title: Feasibility and Initial Efficacy of an Adapted Telepractice Listening Comprehension Intervention for School-Aged Children with Autism.
authors: Henry AR, Conner C, Zajic MC, Solari EJ
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders

title: GABAergic System Dysfunction in Autism Spectrum Disorders.
authors: Zhao H, Mao X, Zhu C, Zou X, Peng F, Yang W, Li B, Li G, Ge T, Cui R
journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) refers to a series of neurodevelopmental diseases characterized by two hallmark symptoms, social communication deficits and repetitive behaviors. Gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) is one of the most important inhibitory neurotransmitters in the central nervous system (CNS). GABAergic inhibitory neurotransmission is critical for the regulation of brain rhythm and spontaneous neuronal activities during neurodevelopment. Genetic evidence has identified some variations of genes associated with the GABA system, indicating an abnormal excitatory/inhibitory (E/I) neurotransmission ratio implicated in the pathogenesis of ASD. However, the specific molecular mechanism by which GABA and GABAergic synaptic transmission affect ASD remains unclear. Transgenic technology enables translating genetic variations into rodent models to further investigate the structural and functional synaptic dysregulation related to ASD. In this review, we summarized evidence from human neuroimaging, postmortem, and genetic and pharmacological studies, and put emphasis on the GABAergic synaptic dysregulation and consequent E/I imbalance. We attempt to illuminate the pathophysiological role of structural and functional synaptic dysregulation in ASD and provide insights for future investigation.

title: Dynamic and Systemic Perspective in Autism Spectrum Disorders: A Change of Gaze in Research Opens to A New Landscape of Needs and Solutions.
authors: Panisi C, Marini M
abstract: The first step for a harmonious bio-psycho-social framework in approaching autism spectrum disorders (ASD) is overcoming the conflict between the biological and the psychosocial perspective. Biological research can provide clues for a correct approach to clinical practice, assuming that it would lead to the conceptualization of a pathogenetic paradigm able to account for epidemiologic and clinical findings. The upward trajectory in ASD prevalence and the systemic involvement of other organs besides the brain suggest that the epigenetic paradigm is the most plausible one. The embryo-fetal period is the crucial window of opportunity for keeping neurodevelopment on the right tracks, suggesting that women's health in pregnancy should be a priority. Maladaptive molecular pathways beginning in utero, in particular, a vicious circle between the immune response, oxidative stress/mitochondrial dysfunction, and dysbiosis-impact neurodevelopment and brain functioning across the lifespan and are the basis for progressive multisystemic disorders that account for the substantial health loss and the increased mortality in ASD. Therefore, the biological complexity of ASD and its implications for health requires the enhancement of clinical skills on these topics, to achieve an effective multi-disciplinary healthcare model. Well-balanced training courses could be a promising starting point to make a change.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista, conviene mencionar a su equipo de salud cualquier molestia física, como dolor, problemas digestivos o de sueño, y pedir que se revise el cuerpo además de la conducta. Se trata de una revisión que propone mirar el autismo de forma integrada, biológica y psicosocial, y sugiere que el embarazo y varios sistemas del cuerpo importan. Sus límites: es una propuesta de enfoque, no prueba causas en una persona concreta, y no sustituye la valoración de profesionales sanitarios.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person, it helps to tell their health team about any physical discomfort, such as pain, digestive or sleep difficulties, and to ask that the body be checked as well as behaviour. This is a review that argues for looking at autism in an integrated way, both biological and psychosocial, and suggests that pregnancy and several body systems matter. Its limits: it is a proposed approach, it does not prove causes in any one person, and it does not replace assessment by health professionals.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person kan det hjälpa att berätta för vårdteamet om fysiskt obehag, som smärta, magproblem eller sömnsvårigheter, och be dem undersöka kroppen och inte bara beteendet. Det här är en översikt som förespråkar ett samlat synsätt på autism, både biologiskt och psykosocialt, och som antyder att graviditeten och flera kroppssystem spelar roll. Begränsningar: det är ett förslag på arbetssätt, det bevisar inte orsaker hos en enskild person och ersätter inte bedömning av vårdpersonal.

title: A Review of Parent-Implemented Early Start Denver Model for Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Jhuo RA, Chu SY
abstract: The purpose of this review is to provide an overview of findings from selected research published between 2012 and 2022 in English-language peer-reviewed journals to evaluate the effectiveness of the parent-implemented Early Start Denver Model (P-ESDM). Thirteen studies used quantitative methods to examine the relationship between variables. We considered four categories of variables in the analysis: child characteristics, intervention intensity and duration, child outcome measures, and parent-related outcome measures and parental fidelity. The findings revealed positive child-parent-related outcomes. In addition, the quality of implementation, relating to parent fidelity, should be considered when evaluating the efficacy of the intervention. However, only half the studies revealed that the standard benchmark for acceptable fidelity was being achieved. Implications for future research and practice are discussed.

sheet.es: Si piensa en un programa de apoyo temprano para su hijo o hija autista, esta revisión sugiere que el Modelo Denver de Atención Temprana aplicado por madres y padres puede aportar beneficios, siempre que se aprenda y se practique bien con acompañamiento profesional. Es una revisión de 13 estudios cuantitativos publicados entre 2012 y 2022, que encontró resultados positivos tanto en niños como en familias. Sus límites: solo la mitad de los estudios alcanzó el nivel aceptable de fidelidad al método, y cada niño y cada familia son distintos, así que no sirve como regla general. Hable con el equipo profesional sobre qué encaja con su familia.
sheet.en: If you are considering an early support program for your autistic child, this review suggests that the Early Start Denver Model delivered by parents may help, especially when parents are well coached and practise the methods accurately. It reviewed 13 quantitative studies published between 2012 and 2022 and found positive outcomes for both children and parents. Its limits: only half the studies reached the standard benchmark for acceptable fidelity, and every child and family is different, so this is not a rule for everyone. Talk with your professional team about what fits your family.
sheet.sv: Om du funderar på ett tidigt stödprogram för ditt autistiska barn tyder denna översikt på att Early Start Denver Model, när föräldrar genomför den, kan hjälpa, särskilt om föräldrarna får bra handledning och använder metoden korrekt. Översikten omfattar 13 kvantitativa studier publicerade mellan 2012 och 2022 och fann positiva resultat för både barn och föräldrar. Begränsningar: bara hälften av studierna nådde den godtagbara nivån för följsamhet till metoden, och alla barn och familjer är olika, så detta är ingen regel för alla. Prata med ditt professionella team om vad som passar din familj.

title: Cerebellar and Striatal Implications in Autism Spectrum Disorders: From Clinical Observations to Animal Models.
authors: Thabault M, Turpin V, Maisterrena A, Jaber M, Egloff M, Galvan L
abstract: Autism spectrum disorders (ASD) are complex conditions that stem from a combination of genetic, epigenetic and environmental influences during early pre- and postnatal childhood. The review focuses on the cerebellum and the striatum, two structures involved in motor, sensory, cognitive and social functions altered in ASD. We summarize clinical and fundamental studies highlighting the importance of these two structures in ASD. We further discuss the relation between cellular and molecular alterations with the observed behavior at the social, cognitive, motor and gait levels. Functional correlates regarding neuronal activity are also detailed wherever possible, and sexual dimorphism is explored pointing to the need to apprehend ASD in both sexes, as findings can be dramatically different at both quantitative and qualitative levels. The review focuses also on a set of three recent papers from our laboratory where we explored motor and gait function in various genetic and environmental ASD animal models. We report that motor and gait behaviors can constitute an early and quantitative window to the disease, as they often correlate with the severity of social impairments and loss of cerebellar Purkinje cells. The review ends with suggestions as to the main obstacles that need to be surpassed before an appropriate management of the disease can be proposed.

sheet.es: Si notas diferencias en el movimiento o la forma de caminar de una persona autista, anótalas con calma y coméntalas con su equipo de profesionales: pueden ser parte de cómo funciona su cuerpo y merecen atención. Es una revisión que resume estudios clínicos y de laboratorio sobre el cerebelo y el estriado, incluidos modelos animales. Sugiere que el movimiento y la marcha podrían ser una señal temprana, pero es investigación básica, no una guía para decidir nada en casa. Además, los hallazgos pueden diferir entre sexos y no se aplican a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If you notice differences in how an autistic person moves or walks, jot them down calmly and share them with their professional team: they may simply be part of how their body works and deserve attention. This is a review summarising clinical and laboratory studies on the cerebellum and striatum, including animal models. It suggests movement and gait could be an early signal, but this is basic research, not a guide for decisions at home. Findings may also differ between sexes and do not apply to every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om du ser skillnader i hur en autistisk person rör sig eller går, anteckna dem lugnt och ta upp dem med personens team: de kan vara en del av hur kroppen fungerar och förtjänar uppmärksamhet. Detta är en översikt av kliniska studier och laboratoriestudier om lillhjärnan och striatum, även djurmodeller. Den antyder att rörelse och gång kan vara en tidig signal, men det är grundforskning, inte en vägledning för beslut hemma. Resultaten kan också skilja sig mellan kön och gäller inte alla autistiska personer.

title: Automatic Emotion Recognition in Children with Autism: A Systematic Literature Review.
authors: Landowska A, Karpus A, Zawadzka T, Robins B, Erol Barkana D, Kose H, Zorcec T, Cummins N
abstract: The automatic emotion recognition domain brings new methods and technologies that might be used to enhance therapy of children with autism. The paper aims at the exploration of methods and tools used to recognize emotions in children. It presents a literature review study that was performed using a systematic approach and PRISMA methodology for reporting quantitative and qualitative results. Diverse observation channels and modalities are used in the analyzed studies, including facial expressions, prosody of speech, and physiological signals. Regarding representation models, the basic emotions are the most frequently recognized, especially happiness, fear, and sadness. Both single-channel and multichannel approaches are applied, with a preference for the first one. For multimodal recognition, early fusion was the most frequently applied. SVM and neural networks were the most popular for building classifiers. Qualitative analysis revealed important clues on participant group construction and the most common combinations of modalities and methods. All channels are reported to be prone to some disturbance, and as a result, information on a specific symptoms of emotions might be temporarily or permanently unavailable. The challenges of proper stimuli, labelling methods, and the creation of open datasets were also identified.

sheet.es: Por ahora, la mejor forma de entender cómo se siente tu hijo o hija autista sigue siendo conocerle: observa sus propias señales, pregúntale de la forma que le resulte cómoda y no des por hecho que su cara o su voz muestran lo que siente. Las herramientas automáticas que "leen" emociones aún están en investigación y no sustituyen tu conocimiento. Esta revisión sistemática analizó estudios que usaban expresiones faciales, voz y señales fisiológicas para reconocer emociones en niños autistas, sobre todo felicidad, miedo y tristeza. Sus límites: los datos son poco fiables por interferencias, faltan bases de datos abiertas y los métodos de etiquetado son discutibles.
sheet.en: For now, the best way to understand how your autistic child feels is still to know them: notice their own signals, ask in a way that works for them, and don't assume their face or voice shows what they feel. Automatic tools that "read" emotions are still at the research stage and don't replace your knowledge. This systematic review examined studies that used facial expressions, speech and physiological signals to recognise emotions in autistic children, mostly happiness, fear and sadness. Its limits: signals are often disrupted, open datasets are scarce, and the ways emotions were labelled remain uncertain.
sheet.sv: Just nu är det bästa sättet att förstå hur ditt autistiska barn mår fortfarande att känna barnet: lägg märke till barnets egna signaler, fråga på ett sätt som fungerar för hen och utgå inte från att ansikte eller röst visar vad hen känner. Automatiska verktyg som "läser av" känslor är fortfarande forskning och ersätter inte din kunskap. Denna systematiska översikt granskade studier som använde ansiktsuttryck, röst och fysiologiska signaler för att känna igen känslor hos autistiska barn, främst glädje, rädsla och ledsenhet. Begränsningar: signalerna störs ofta, öppna dataset saknas och sätten att märka känslor är osäkra.

title: Barriers to healthcare and self-reported adverse outcomes for autistic adults: a cross-sectional study.
authors: Doherty M, Neilson S, O'Sullivan J, Carravallah L, Johnson M, Cullen W, Shaw SCK
abstract: Objectives Autistic people experience poor physical and mental health along with reduced life expectancy compared with non-autistic people. Our aim was to identify self-reported barriers to primary care access by autistic adults compared with non-autistic adults and to link these barriers to self-reported adverse health consequences. Design Following consultation with the autistic community at an autistic conference, Autscape , we developed a self-report survey, which we administered online through social media platforms. Setting A 52-item, international, online survey. Participants 507 autistic adults and 157 non-autistic adults. Primary and secondary outcome measures Self-reported barriers to accessing healthcare and associated adverse health outcomes. Results Eighty per cent of autistic adults and 37% of non-autistic respondents reported difficulty visiting a general practitioner (GP). The highest-rated barriers by autistic adults were deciding if symptoms warrant a GP visit (72%), difficulty making appointments by telephone (62%), not feeling understood (56%), difficulty communicating with their doctor (53%) and the waiting room environment (51%). Autistic adults reported a preference for online or text-based appointment booking, facility to email in advance the reason for consultation, the first or last clinic appointment and a quiet place to wait. Self-reported adverse health outcomes experienced by autistic adults were associated with barriers to accessing healthcare. Adverse outcomes included untreated physical and mental health conditions, not attending specialist referral or screening programmes, requiring more extensive treatment or surgery due to late presentations and untreated potentially life-threatening conditions. There were no significant differences in difficulty attending, barriers experienced or adverse outcomes between formally diagnosed and self-identified autistic respondents. Conclusions Reduction of healthcare inequalities for autistic people requires that healthcare providers understand autistic perspectives, communication needs and sensory sensitivities. Adjustments for autism-specific needs are as necessary as ramps for wheelchair users.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista adulta al médico de cabecera, puedes pedir ajustes concretos: reservar cita por internet o mensaje en lugar de por teléfono, enviar por correo antes el motivo de la consulta, solicitar la primera o la última cita del día y un lugar tranquilo para esperar. También puede ayudar decidir juntos, con calma, si un síntoma merece consulta. Estos ajustes son tan necesarios como una rampa. La evidencia procede de una encuesta internacional en línea, diseñada con la comunidad autista, con 507 adultos autistas y 157 no autistas. Sus límites: son datos autoinformados, de personas que usan redes sociales, y muestran asociaciones, no causas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult with GP visits, you can ask for concrete adjustments: booking online or by text instead of by phone, emailing the reason for the visit in advance, requesting the first or last appointment of the day, and a quiet place to wait. It can also help to calmly decide together whether a symptom is worth a visit. These adjustments are as necessary as a ramp. The evidence comes from an international online survey, designed with the autistic community, with 507 autistic and 157 non-autistic adults. Its limits: answers are self-reported, from people reached through social media, and show associations, not causes.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen vid läkarbesök kan du be om konkreta anpassningar: boka tid via nätet eller sms i stället för telefon, mejla orsaken till besöket i förväg, be om dagens första eller sista tid och en lugn plats att vänta på. Det kan också hjälpa att i lugn och ro tillsammans avgöra om ett symtom behöver ett besök. Sådana anpassningar är lika nödvändiga som en ramp. Underlaget är en internationell webbenkät, utformad tillsammans med autistiska personer, med 507 autistiska och 157 icke-autistiska vuxna. Begränsningar: svaren är självrapporterade, från personer som nåddes via sociala medier, och visar samband, inte orsaker.

title: Pharmacological and dietary-supplement treatments for autism spectrum disorder: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
authors: Siafis S, Çıray O, Wu H, Schneider-Thoma J, Bighelli I, Krause M, Rodolico A, Ceraso A, Deste G, Huhn M, Fraguas D, San José Cáceres A, Mavridis D, Charman T, Murphy DG, Parellada M, Arango C, Leucht
abstract: Background There is still no approved medication for the core symptoms of autism spectrum disorder (ASD). This network meta-analysis investigated pharmacological and dietary-supplement treatments for ASD. Methods We searched for randomized-controlled-trials (RCTs) with a minimum duration of seven days in ClinicalTrials.gov, EMBASE, MEDLINE, PsycINFO, WHO-ICTRP (from inception up to July 8, 2018), CENTRAL and PubMed (up to November 3, 2021). The co-primary outcomes were core symptoms (social-communication difficulties-SCD, repetitive behaviors-RB, overall core symptoms-OCS) measured by validated scales and standardized-mean-differences (SMDs). Associated symptoms, e.g., irritability/aggression and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) symptoms, dropouts and important side-effects, were investigated as secondary outcomes. Studies in children/adolescents and adults were analyzed separately in random-effects pairwise and network meta-analyses. Results We analyzed data for 41 drugs and 17 dietary-supplements, from 125 RCTs (n = 7450 participants) in children/adolescents and 18 RCTs (n = 1104) in adults. The following medications could improve at least one core symptom domain in comparison with placebo: aripiprazole (k = 6 studies in analysis, SCD: SMD = 0.27 95% CI [0.09, 0.44], RB: 0.48 [0.26, 0.70]), atomoxetine (k = 3, RB:0.49 [0.18, 0.80]), bumetanide (k = 4, RB: 0.35 [0.09, 0.62], OCS: 0.61 [0.31, 0.91]), and risperidone (k = 4, SCM: 0.31 [0.06, 0.55], RB: 0.60 [0.29, 0.90]; k = 3, OCS: 1.18 [0.75, 1.61]) in children/adolescents; fluoxetine (k = 1, RB: 1.20 [0.45, 1.96]), fluvoxamine (k = 1, RB: 1.04 [0.27, 1.81]), oxytocin (k = 6, RB:0.41 [0.16, 0.66]) and risperidone (k = 1, RB: 0.97 [0.21,1.74]) in adults. There were some indications of improvement by carnosine, haloperidol, folinic acid, guanfacine, omega-3-fatty-acids, probiotics, sulforaphane, tideglusib and valproate, yet imprecise and not robust. Confidence in these estimates was very low or low, except moderate for oxytocin. Medications differed substantially in improving associated symptoms, and in their side-effect profiles. Limitations Most of the studies were inadequately powered (sample sizes of 20-80 participants), with short duration (8-13 weeks), and about a third focused on associated symptoms. Networks were mainly star-shaped, and there were indications of reporting bias. There was no optimal rating scale measuring change in core symptoms. Conclusions Some medications could improve core symptoms, although this could be likely secondary to the improvement of associated symptoms. Evidence on their efficacy and safety is preliminary; therefore, routine prescription of medications for the core symptoms cannot be recommended. Trial registration PROSPERO-ID CRD42019125317.

sheet.es: Si le preocupa algún fármaco o suplemento, hable con el equipo clínico antes de cambiar nada: las decisiones médicas les corresponden a ellos. Este fue un estudio médico: un metaanálisis de ensayos aleatorizados con niñez, adolescencia y personas adultas autistas. Reunió 125 ensayos en niñez y adolescencia y 18 en adultos. Sus autores concluyen que la evidencia es preliminar y que no recomiendan recetar de forma rutinaria para los rasgos centrales del autismo. Limitaciones: muchos estudios eran pequeños y breves, había indicios de sesgo de publicación y las escalas de medida eran imperfectas. Tampoco vale como regla para toda persona.
sheet.en: If you are wondering about a medicine or supplement, talk with the clinical team before changing anything: medical decisions belong to a clinician. This was a medical study: a meta-analysis of randomized trials with autistic children, teenagers and adults. It pooled 125 trials in children and adolescents and 18 in adults. The authors conclude that the evidence is preliminary and do not recommend routine prescribing for the core features of autism. Limits: many studies were small and short, there were signs of reporting bias, and the rating scales were imperfect. It is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du funderar på ett läkemedel eller kosttillskott, prata med vårdteamet innan du ändrar något: medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker.
