Detta var en medicinsk studie: en metaanalys av randomiserade studier med autistiska barn, ungdomar och vuxna. Den sammanställde 125 studier på barn och ungdomar och 18 på vuxna. Författarna drar slutsatsen att evidensen är preliminär och rekommenderar inte rutinmässig förskrivning för autismens kärndrag. Begränsningar: många studier var små och korta, det fanns tecken på publiceringsbias och mätskalorna var ofullkomliga. Det är ingen regel för alla personer.

title: Behavioural and psychological features of PTEN mutations: a systematic review of the literature and meta-analysis of the prevalence of autism spectrum disorder characteristics.
authors: Cummings K, Watkins A, Jones C, Dias R, Welham A
abstract: Background Phosphatase and tensin homologue (PTEN) is a cancer suppressor gene. Constitutional mutations affecting this gene are associated with several conditions, collectively termed PTEN hamartoma tumour syndromes (PHTS). In addition to hamartomas, PTEN aberrations have been associated with a range of non-tumoural phenotypes such as macrocephaly, and research indicates possibly increased rates of developmental delay and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) for people with germline mutations affecting PTEN. Method A systematic review of literature reporting behavioural and psychological variables for people with constitutional PTEN mutations/PHTS was conducted using four databases. Following in-depth screening, 25 articles met the inclusion criteria and were used in the review. Fourteen papers reported the proportion of people with PTEN mutations/PTHS meeting criteria for or having characteristics of ASD and were thus used in a pooled prevalence meta-analysis. Results Meta-analysis using a random effects model estimated pooled prevalence of ASD characteristics at 25% (95% CI 16-33%), although this should be interpreted cautiously due to possible biases in existing literature. Intellectual disability and developmental delay (global, motor and speech and language) were also reported frequently. Emotional difficulties and impaired cognitive functioning in specific domains were noted but assessed/reported less frequently. Methods of assessment of psychological/behavioural factors varied widely (with retrospective examination of medical records common). Conclusions Existing research suggests approximately 25% of people with constitutional PTEN mutations may meet criteria for or have characteristics of ASD. Studies have also begun to establish a range of possible cognitive impairments in affected individuals, especially when ASD is also reported. However, further large-scale studies are needed to elucidate psychological/behavioural corollaries of this mutation, and how they may relate to physiological/physical characteristics.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona con una mutación PTEN, conviene tener presente que pueden aparecer rasgos autistas, retrasos del desarrollo o dificultades emocionales, y que vale la pena hablar con su equipo sanitario sobre apoyos desde pronto. Se trata de una revisión sistemática con metaanálisis de 25 artículos; 14 informaron cuántas personas con mutaciones PTEN cumplían criterios o tenían características de autismo, con una prevalencia combinada del 25% (IC 95% 16-33%). Límites: los estudios evaluaron de formas muy distintas, a menudo con historiales médicos, y pueden tener sesgos. No describe a cada persona.
sheet.en: If you support someone with a PTEN mutation, it helps to know that autistic traits, developmental delays or emotional difficulties may be present, and it is worth talking with their health team early about supports. This was a systematic review with meta-analysis of 25 articles; 14 reported how many people with PTEN mutations met criteria for or had characteristics of autism, giving a pooled prevalence of 25% (95% CI 16-33%). Limits: studies assessed people in very different ways, often using medical records, and may be biased. It does not describe every individual.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar någon med en PTEN-mutation är det bra att veta att autistiska drag, utvecklingsförsening eller känslomässiga svårigheter kan förekomma, och att det är värt att tidigt prata med vårdteamet om stöd. Det var en systematisk översikt med metaanalys av 25 artiklar; 14 redovisade hur många personer med PTEN-mutationer som uppfyllde kriterier för eller hade drag av autism, med en sammanvägd förekomst på 25% (95% KI 16-33%). Begränsningar: studierna bedömde människor på mycket olika sätt, ofta via journaler, och kan vara snedvridna. Den beskriver inte varje individ.

title: Stage 2 registered report: investigating a preference for certainty in conversation among autistic adults.
authors: Wilson AC, Bishop DVM
abstract: Social communication difficulties are a diagnostic feature in autism. These difficulties are sometimes attributed, at least in part, to impaired ability in making inferences about what other people mean. In this registered report, we tested a competing hypothesis that the communication profile of adults on the autism spectrum can be more strongly characterised by reduced confidence in making inferences in the face of uncertain information. We tested this hypothesis by comparing the performance of 102 autistic and 109 non-autistic adults on a test of implied meaning, using a test of grammaticality judgements as a control task. We hypothesised that autistic adults would report substantially lower confidence, allowing for differences in accuracy, than non-autistic adults on the test of implied meaning compared to the grammaticality test. However, our results did not suggest this. Instead, we found that accuracy and confidence were both reduced to a similar extent on the test of implied meaning in the autistic group compared to the control group, although these were only subtle differences. This pattern of results was specific to inference-making, as the autistic and non-autistic groups did not differ on the grammar test. This supports the idea that specific differences in pragmatic language processing can exist in autism in the absence of core language problems. Importantly, this pattern of results (differences on the test of implied meaning and no differences on the grammar test) was reversed in a group with self-reported reading difficulties, indicating that the differences in inference-making were specific to the autistic group. Lastly, we found relationships between Intolerance of Uncertainty, performance on the test of implied meaning, and self-reported social communication challenges. This supports the idea that discomfort with uncertainty plays a role in the pragmatic language and communication challenges in autism.

sheet.es: Si hablas con una persona autista, conviene decir con claridad lo que quieres decir y evitar dejar los sentidos implícitos solo a la inferencia. Ante la duda, preguntar o confirmar ayuda a todos. Este estudio comparó a 102 adultos autistas y 109 adultos no autistas en una prueba de significado implícito y en otra de gramática. En el significado implícito, la precisión y la confianza fueron algo menores en el grupo autista, con diferencias sutiles; en gramática no hubo diferencias. También hubo relación con la intolerancia a la incertidumbre. Límites: son promedios de grupo, no describen a cada persona, y la relación encontrada no prueba una causa.
sheet.en: When talking with an autistic person, it helps to say plainly what you mean rather than leaving meaning implied. When in doubt, asking or checking in helps everyone. This study compared 102 autistic adults and 109 non-autistic adults on a test of implied meaning and a grammar test. On implied meaning, accuracy and confidence were both a little lower in the autistic group, with only subtle differences; on grammar there were no differences. Intolerance of uncertainty was also linked to performance. Limits: these are group averages, they do not describe every person, and the links found do not prove a cause.
sheet.sv: När du pratar med en autistisk person hjälper det att säga tydligt vad du menar i stället för att lämna betydelsen outtalad. Vid osäkerhet hjälper det alla att fråga eller stämma av. Studien jämförde 102 autistiska vuxna och 109 icke-autistiska vuxna på ett test av underförstådd betydelse och ett grammatiktest. På underförstådd betydelse var både träffsäkerhet och självförtroende något lägre i den autistiska gruppen, med små skillnader; på grammatik syntes ingen skillnad. Intolerans mot osäkerhet hängde också samman med resultaten. Begränsningar: det är gruppmedelvärden som inte beskriver varje person, och sambanden visar inte orsak.

title: "We couldn't think in the box if we tried. We can't even find the damn box": A qualitative study of the lived experiences of autistic adults and relatives of autistic adults.
authors: Finch TL, Mackintosh J, Petrou A, McConachie H, Le Couteur A, Garland D, Parr JR
abstract: Autistic children grow to become autistic adults, and autism is increasingly diagnosed in adulthood and later life. This qualitative study aimed to understand experiences of autism throughout adulthood. A national cohort study of autistic adults and relatives of autistic adults (ASC-UK), enabled purposive recruitment of a diverse sample. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 29 autistic adults (aged 20-71 years), mostly diagnosed in adulthood, and 16 relatives (aged 31-81 years) of autistic adults diagnosed across both childhood and adulthood (including some with learning disability). Interview topics included health, relationships, education, employment, quality of life and everyday experiences. Thematic analysis of the accounts of the autistic adults identified six key themes relating to their experiences: (1) diagnosis as validating yet limiting; (2) supportive and non-supportive social agents; (3) the "invisibility" of the needs of autistic adults; (4) health in the context of autism; (5) staying 'outside' the circle; and (6) multiple lives with autism. Data from relatives about autistic adult experiences gave additional perspectives on these themes. Experiences reported in other studies-of 'difference' from others, challenges of social engagement, and learning to 'conform' to society's expectations-were evident and relevant to male and female autistic adults, across all age groups, and unrelated to stage of life when diagnosed. Some expressed disappointment with their lives, but others were proud of their achievements. Education and employment, whilst challenging for many, were also rewarding for some. Health care and social services were often experienced as inaccessible, inappropriate, or lacking understanding of the individual's needs. We conclude that greater public understanding of autism as experienced in adulthood is needed. Key priorities are improving the availability of 'appropriate' health and social care services for autistic adults and families, and providing practical support to enable enhanced participation in life.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista adulta, pregúntale qué apoyo le sirve en la salud, el trabajo o la vida diaria, y no supongas que sus necesidades se ven desde fuera. Es un estudio cualitativo con entrevistas a 29 adultos autistas (20-71 años), la mayoría diagnosticados de adultos, y a 16 familiares. Muchas personas encontraron los servicios de salud y sociales inaccesibles o poco comprensivos, aunque algunas se sentían orgullosas de sus logros. Limitaciones: son experiencias de un grupo concreto en el Reino Unido, no valen como regla para todas las personas ni miden qué ayuda funciona.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult, ask what help works for them in health care, work or daily life, and don't assume their needs are visible from outside. This is a qualitative study with interviews of 29 autistic adults (aged 20-71 years), most diagnosed in adulthood, and 16 relatives. Many found health and social services inaccessible or lacking understanding, though some were proud of their achievements. Limits: these are experiences from one group in the UK, not a rule for every person, and the study does not test which supports work.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen, fråga vilket stöd som fungerar för hen inom vård, arbete eller vardag, och anta inte att behoven syns utifrån. Det här är en kvalitativ studie med intervjuer av 29 autistiska vuxna (20-71 år), de flesta diagnostiserade som vuxna, och 16 anhöriga. Många upplevde att vård och sociala tjänster var otillgängliga eller saknade förståelse, men några var stolta över sina prestationer. Begränsningar: det är erfarenheter från en grupp i Storbritannien, ingen regel för alla, och studien testar inte vilket stöd som fungerar.

title: Visual consciousness dynamics in adults with and without autism.
authors: Skerswetat J, Bex PJ, Baron-Cohen S
abstract: Sensory differences between autism and neuro-typical populations are well-documented and have often been explained by either weak-central-coherence or excitation/inhibition-imbalance cortical theories. We tested these theories with perceptual multi-stability paradigms in which dissimilar images presented to each eye generate dynamic cyclopean percepts based on ongoing cortical grouping and suppression processes. We studied perceptual multi-stability with Interocular Grouping (IOG), which requires the simultaneous integration and suppression of image fragments from both eyes, and Conventional Binocular Rivalry (CBR), which only requires global suppression of either eye, in 17 autistic adults and 18 neurotypical participants. We used a Hidden-Markov-Model as tool to analyze the multistable dynamics of these processes. Overall, the dynamics of multi-stable perception were slower (i.e. there were longer durations and fewer transitions among perceptual states) in the autistic group compared to the neurotypical group for both IOG and CBR. The weighted Markovian transition distributions revealed key differences between both groups and paradigms. The results indicate overall lower levels of suppression and decreased levels of grouping in autistic than neurotypical participants, consistent with elements of excitation/inhibition imbalance and weak-central-coherence theories.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista describe que ve o interpreta las imágenes de otro modo, conviene tomarlo en serio y dejar tiempo extra para mirar y procesar lo visual. Es un estudio con 17 adultos autistas y 18 participantes neurotípicos, a quienes se mostraron imágenes distintas en cada ojo. En el grupo autista, la percepción cambió más despacio, con menos transiciones entre lo que se veía. Es un estudio pequeño, de laboratorio, solo con adultos, y no dice cómo es la experiencia visual de cada persona ni qué ajustes cotidianos funcionan.
sheet.en: If an autistic person describes seeing or interpreting images differently, take it seriously and allow extra time to look at and process visual information. This was a study with 17 autistic adults and 18 neurotypical participants, who were shown a different image in each eye. In the autistic group, perception switched more slowly, with fewer transitions between what was seen. It was a small laboratory study with adults only, so it cannot tell us how any one person experiences vision or which everyday adjustments will help.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person beskriver att hen ser eller tolkar bilder annorlunda, ta det på allvar och ge extra tid att titta och bearbeta visuell information. Studien omfattade 17 autistiska vuxna och 18 neurotypiska deltagare, som fick se olika bilder i varje öga. I den autistiska gruppen växlade seendet långsammare, med färre övergångar mellan det som sågs. Det var en liten laboratoriestudie med enbart vuxna, så den visar inte hur varje person upplever synintryck eller vilka anpassningar i vardagen som hjälper.

title: Oxidative Stress in Autism Spectrum Disorder-Current Progress of Mechanisms and Biomarkers.
authors: Liu X, Lin J, Zhang H, Khan NU, Zhang J, Tang X, Cao X, Shen L
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a type of neurodevelopmental disorder that has been diagnosed in an increasing number of children around the world. Existing data suggest that early diagnosis and intervention can improve ASD outcomes. However, the causes of ASD remain complex and unclear, and there are currently no clinical biomarkers for autism spectrum disorder. More mechanisms and biomarkers of autism have been found with the development of advanced technology such as mass spectrometry. Many recent studies have found a link between ASD and elevated oxidative stress, which may play a role in its development. ASD is caused by oxidative stress in several ways, including protein post-translational changes (e.g., carbonylation), abnormal metabolism (e.g., lipid peroxidation), and toxic buildup [e.g., reactive oxygen species (ROS)]. To detect elevated oxidative stress in ASD, various biomarkers have been developed and employed. This article summarizes recent studies about the mechanisms and biomarkers of oxidative stress. Potential biomarkers identified in this study could be used for early diagnosis and evaluation of ASD intervention, as well as to inform and target ASD pharmacological or nutritional treatment interventions.

sheet.es: Para mañana por la mañana: este estudio no cambia nada en la rutina diaria. No hay ninguna prueba de laboratorio para el autismo que usted deba pedir ni ninguna medida que tomar en casa a partir de él. Es una revisión de estudios recientes sobre el estrés oxidativo, un proceso del cuerpo que algunos trabajos relacionan con el autismo, y sobre posibles biomarcadores. Sus límites: el propio texto indica que las causas del autismo siguen siendo complejas y poco claras, y que hoy no existen biomarcadores clínicos. Que algo se asocie no significa que explique a cada persona autista. Las decisiones médicas o nutricionales conviene hablarlas con un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: For tomorrow morning: this study changes nothing in daily routines. There is no lab test for autism that you need to request, and nothing to do at home because of it. It is a review of recent studies on oxidative stress, a process in the body that some research links to autism, and on possible biomarkers. Its limits: the authors say the causes of autism remain complex and unclear, and that there are currently no clinical biomarkers. An association does not explain every autistic person. Any medical or nutritional decisions belong with a clinician.
sheet.sv: Inför i morgon bitti: den här studien ändrar ingenting i vardagen. Det finns inget laboratorietest för autism som du behöver be om, och inget att göra hemma på grund av den. Det är en översikt av nyare studier om oxidativ stress, en process i kroppen som en del forskning kopplar till autism, och om möjliga biomarkörer. Begränsningar: författarna skriver att orsakerna till autism är komplexa och oklara och att det i dag inte finns några kliniska biomarkörer. Ett samband förklarar inte varje autistisk person. Medicinska eller kostrelaterade beslut hör hemma hos en kliniker.

title: Repetitive Restricted Behaviors in Autism Spectrum Disorder: From Mechanism to Development of Therapeutics.
authors: Tian J, Gao X, Yang L
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a complex neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by deficits in social communication, social interaction, and repetitive restricted behaviors (RRBs). It is usually detected in early childhood. RRBs are behavioral patterns characterized by repetition, inflexibility, invariance, inappropriateness, and frequent lack of obvious function or specific purpose. To date, the classification of RRBs is contentious. Understanding the potential mechanisms of RRBs in children with ASD, such as neural connectivity disorders and abnormal immune functions, will contribute to finding new therapeutic targets. Although behavioral intervention remains the most effective and safe strategy for RRBs treatment, some promising drugs and new treatment options (e.g., supplementary and cell therapy) have shown positive effects on RRBs in recent studies. In this review, we summarize the latest advances of RRBs from mechanistic to therapeutic approaches and propose potential future directions in research on RRBs.

sheet.es: Los movimientos o rutinas repetitivas pueden tener un papel para la persona autista; antes de intentar reducirlos, conviene observar cuándo aparecen y qué le aportan, y consultar con profesionales de confianza. Esta es una revisión que resume avances sobre cómo se explican estas conductas y qué enfoques se han probado en niños autistas. Señala que la intervención conductual es la estrategia más eficaz y segura, y menciona otras opciones aún prometedoras. Sus límites: es una revisión, no un ensayo propio, la clasificación de estas conductas sigue en debate y no sirve como regla para cada persona. Las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: Repetitive movements or routines may serve a purpose for an autistic person, so before trying to reduce them, notice when they happen and what they give the person, and talk with professionals you trust. This is a review summarising advances in how these behaviours are explained and which approaches have been tried with autistic children. It says behavioural intervention is the most effective and safe strategy, and mentions other options that still look promising. Limits: it is a review, not a new trial, how these behaviours are classified is still debated, and it is not a rule for every person. Medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Repetitiva rörelser eller rutiner kan fylla en funktion för en autistisk person. Innan du försöker minska dem kan du observera när de uppstår och vad de ger, och rådgöra med yrkespersoner du litar på. Detta är en översikt som sammanfattar framsteg kring hur dessa beteenden förklaras och vilka tillvägagångssätt som prövats hos autistiska barn. Den uppger att beteendeinriktat stöd är den mest effektiva och säkra strategin och nämner andra alternativ som ännu ser lovande ut. Begränsningar: det är en översikt och inte en ny studie, indelningen av dessa beteenden är omdebatterad och resultaten gäller inte alla. Medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker.

title: Neuroticism Drives Associations Between Repetitive Behaviors and Depression in Autistic Adults.
authors: Schwartzman JM, Williams ZJ, Richards JK, Mattheiss SR, Gotham KO
abstract: Depression is more prevalent among autistic adults than neurotypical adults, yet risk factors are incompletely understood in this population. Some research groups have focused on relationships between negative repetitive thinking and depression in the autistic population, which may explain elevated prevalence rates in line with general population findings on rumination and internalizing disorders. Little is known about associations between depression and more prototypical repetitive cognitions and/or behaviors characteristic of autism (i.e., insistence on sameness [IS] and repetitive sensorimotor [RSM] behaviors). Therefore, the present study aimed to examine associations between IS, RSM behaviors, and depressive symptoms in 762 autistic adults, and whether observed effects are confounded by additional factors (e.g., demographic factors, trait neuroticism). To test if greater IS scores were associated with greater depressive symptoms on the BDI-II, a Bayesian linear regression was conducted with BDI-II scores (dependent variable) regressed on age, gender, educational level, RSM scores, and IS scores (independent variables). To test the effects of neuroticism on observed relationships, a second regression was conducted that included all predictors from the baseline model and neuroticism. Standardized regression coefficients were tested against an interval null hypothesis of [-0.1, 0.1] to assess for practical significance. Results indicated that IS exhibited a moderate positive relationship with depressive symptoms, while RSM behaviors provided only a slight increase in predictive ability. However in the second model, neuroticism exhibited a strong positive relationship with depressive symptoms, completely attenuating the effect of IS. Associations between RSM behaviors and depressive symptoms did not meet our criteria for practical significance, particularly when neuroticism was added to the model. Neither RSM nor IS moderated the effect of neuroticism on depression. The findings from this study add to the literature on risk factors in the pathway to depression in autism, and suggest opportunities for clinical translation to screening and intervention efforts. Screening for IS in autistic individuals is a common diagnostic practice in clinical and research settings that may be leveraged to also identify those at higher risk for depression, and increasing flexibility in daily life may promote emotional regulation and distress tolerance.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta se siente muy decaída, conviene fijarse en su malestar emocional general y en cómo lleva los cambios, no solo en sus rutinas o movimientos repetitivos, y consultar con un profesional de salud mental. Es un estudio con 762 personas autistas adultas que comparó la necesidad de que todo siga igual, los movimientos repetitivos y los síntomas de depresión. El neuroticismo, un rasgo de personalidad, explicó mejor la depresión que la necesidad de igualdad. Es un solo estudio de asociaciones: no demuestra causas y no vale para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult seems very low, it helps to look at their overall emotional distress and how they cope with change, not only at their routines or repetitive movements, and to involve a mental health professional. This study included 762 autistic adults and compared insistence on sameness, repetitive movements and depressive symptoms. Neuroticism, a personality trait, accounted for depression better than insistence on sameness did. It is a single study of associations: it cannot show causes and does not apply to every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen verkar nedstämd är det bra att se till hela det känslomässiga måendet och hur personen hanterar förändringar, inte bara rutiner eller upprepade rörelser, och att ta kontakt med yrkespersonal inom psykisk hälsa. Studien omfattade 762 autistiska vuxna och jämförde behov av att allt förblir lika, upprepade rörelser och depressiva symtom. Neuroticism, ett personlighetsdrag, förklarade depression bättre än behovet av likhet. Det är en enskild studie om samband: den visar inte orsaker och gäller inte alla.

title: Alteration of Gut Microbiota: New Strategy for Treating Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Liu J, Gao Z, Liu C, Liu T, Gao J, Cai Y, Fan X
journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is defined as a complex heterogeneous disorder and characterized by stereotyped behavior and deficits in communication and social interactions. The emerging microbial knowledge has pointed to a potential link between gut microbiota dysbiosis and ASD. Evidence from animal and human studies showed that shifts in composition and activity of the gut microbiota may causally contribute to the etiopathogenesis of core symptoms in the ASD individuals with gastrointestinal tract disturbances and act on microbiota-gut-brain. In this review, we summarized the characterized gut bacterial composition of ASD and the involvement of gut microbiota and their metabolites in the onset and progression of ASD; the possible underlying mechanisms are also highlighted. Given this correlation, we also provide an overview of the microbial-based therapeutic interventions such as probiotics, antibiotics, fecal microbiota transplantation therapy, and dietary interventions and address their potential benefits on behavioral symptoms of ASD. The precise contribution of altering gut microbiome to treating core symptoms in the ASD needs to be further clarified. It seemed to open up promising avenues to develop microbial-based therapies in ASD.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista tiene molestias digestivas frecuentes, vale la pena anotarlas y comentarlas con su equipo médico, sin esperar que cambiar la dieta o tomar suplementos modifique el autismo. Es una revisión de estudios en animales y en personas que describe un posible vínculo entre las bacterias intestinales y el autismo, y repasa intervenciones basadas en la microbiota. Los propios autores señalan que aún falta aclarar su papel real, y no sirve como regla para todas las personas. Las decisiones médicas corresponden siempre a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If an autistic person has frequent digestive discomfort, it is worth noting it down and discussing it with their healthcare team, without expecting that changing diet or taking supplements will change autism itself. This is a review of animal and human studies describing a possible link between gut bacteria and autism, and it surveys interventions based on the microbiota. The authors themselves say the real contribution of these approaches still needs clarifying, and it is not a rule for every person. Medical decisions always belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person ofta har magbesvär är det värt att anteckna dem och ta upp dem med vårdteamet, utan att förvänta sig att ändrad kost eller tillskott förändrar autismen i sig. Detta är en översikt av djurstudier och studier på människor som beskriver ett möjligt samband mellan tarmbakterier och autism, och som går igenom insatser baserade på tarmfloran. Författarna själva menar att den verkliga betydelsen ännu behöver klargöras, och resultaten gäller inte som regel för alla. Medicinska beslut hör alltid hemma hos en kliniker.

title: The impact of schizotypy on quality of life among adults with autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Klang A, Westerberg B, Humble MB, Bejerot S
abstract: Background Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and schizotypal personality disorder can be difficult to distinguish. Deficits in social relationships and social interaction, present in both conditions, are known to impair quality of life. The aim of the present study was to investigate if schizotypal symptoms affect quality of life among adults diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder and to study the association between schizotypy and autistic traits among them. Methods Participants diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder (n = 110) completed questionnaires exploring schizotypy (Schizotypal Personality Questionnaire - Brief Revised (SPQ-BR)), autistic traits (The Ritvo Autism, Asperger Diagnostic Scale-Revised Screen 14 items), anxiety and depression (The Hospital Anxiety and Depression scale) and quality of life (Brunnsviken Brief Quality of Life Scale and the European quality of life index version 5D). Results Schizotypy was found to be associated with anxiety, depressive and autistic symptoms, and poor quality of life. Although schizotypy was a predictor for impaired quality of life, this relationship was mediated by symptoms of anxiety and depression, plausibly inherent to autism. Autistic traits were positively associated with all higher order constructs of the SPQ-BR, i.e. positive and negative schizotypy, disorganization and social anxiety, as well as with poor quality of life. Conclusions There is considerable overlap between schizotypy and autism that needs to be considered in research. Prominent schizotypal traits in people with ASD may constitute an endophenotype coinciding with a particularly poor quality of life. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03570372 : Internet-based Treatment for Adults with Autism Spectrum Disorder (MILAS).

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista adulta, vale la pena preguntarle con calma cómo se siente en cuanto a ansiedad y estado de ánimo, porque pueden influir en su calidad de vida. Este estudio con cuestionarios incluyó a 110 adultos con diagnóstico de autismo. Encontró que los rasgos esquizotípicos se asociaban con más ansiedad, síntomas depresivos y peor calidad de vida, y que esta relación pasaba en gran parte por la ansiedad y la depresión. Tiene límites: es una asociación, no prueba causa, se basa en autoinformes y no sirve como regla para cada persona. Cualquier decisión de salud debe tomarse con un profesional.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult, it may help to gently ask how they are feeling about anxiety and low mood, because these can affect quality of life. This questionnaire study included 110 adults diagnosed with autism. It found that schizotypal traits were linked with more anxiety, depressive symptoms and poorer quality of life, and that this link ran largely through anxiety and depression. Its limits: it shows an association, not a cause, relies on self-report, and is not a rule for every person. Any health decisions belong with a qualified professional.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen kan det hjälpa att varsamt fråga hur hen mår när det gäller oro och nedstämdhet, eftersom det kan påverka livskvaliteten. Denna enkätstudie omfattade 110 vuxna med autismdiagnos. Den fann att schizotypa drag hängde samman med mer ångest, depressiva symtom och sämre livskvalitet, och att sambandet till stor del gick via ångest och depression. Begränsningar: det visar ett samband, inte orsak, bygger på självskattning och är ingen regel för varje person. Beslut om hälsa fattas tillsammans med en kvalificerad vårdgivare.

title: The relevance of the interpersonal theory of suicide for predicting past-year and lifetime suicidality in autistic adults.
authors: Moseley RL, Gregory NJ, Smith P, Allison C, Cassidy S, Baron-Cohen S
abstract: Background While there are known risk factors for suicidality in autistic adults, these are often unconnected from theoretical frameworks that might explain why risk is elevated and guide clinical interventions. The present study investigated the relevance of constructs from the Interpersonal Theory of Suicide (ITS), including perceived burdensomeness, thwarted belongingness and acquired capability for suicide, and explored mechanisms through which certain risk factors (relationship status, age at diagnosis) might elevate suicide risk. Methods Autistic adults (n = 314) completed an online study including measures of depression, anxiety and constructs from the ITS. Linear and multinomial regression analysis disentangled contributions of ITS variables from effects of depression and anxiety for past-year suicide ideation, past-year and lifetime suicide attempts. Mediation analyses examined associations between risk factors and these suicide outcomes via mechanisms proposed by the ITS. Results Past-year suicide ideation was associated with burdensomeness, mental rehearsal of suicide plans (a facet of acquired capability), and depression. Greater feelings of burdensomeness, and reduced fear of death, marked out participants who had attempted suicide in comparison to those who had experienced suicide ideation in the past year. Relationship status was indirectly associated with past-year suicide ideation via the mediators of depression and burdensomeness, and was associated with past-year attempts via its effect on ideation. Age at diagnosis was unrelated to any variables. Limitations Cross-sectional research is insensitive to causality and temporal dynamics, which is likely why interaction hypotheses from the ITS were unsupported. Normative measures may be invalid in autistic samples. There was no control group. The autistic sample was unrepresentative of the whole population, particularly autistic people with intellectual disabilities, ethnic/racial minorities, and gender minorities. Conclusions Perceived burdensomeness and acquired capability appear potentially important to suicide in autistic people, and may mediate the effects of some risk factors. Future research should explore the temporal dynamics of suicide trajectories in longitudinal, prospective designs.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista, tómate en serio cualquier señal de que se siente una carga para los demás; conviene preguntarle con calma y sin juzgar cómo se encuentra. Este estudio online con 314 adultos autistas encontró que sentirse una carga, la depresión y ensayar mentalmente planes de suicidio se asociaban con ideas suicidas el último año. Es un estudio transversal, sin grupo de control, y no muestra causas; además, participaron pocas personas con discapacidad intelectual o de minorías. No describe a cada persona. Si te preocupa alguien, acude a un profesional clínico, un servicio de salud o un servicio de crisis; si hay peligro inmediato, llama al número de emergencias de tu país.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person, take any sign that they feel like a burden seriously; it helps to ask how they are, calmly and without judgement. This online study of 314 autistic adults found that feeling like a burden, depression and mentally rehearsing suicide plans were linked to suicidal thoughts in the past year. It was a cross-sectional study with no control group, so it cannot show causes, and few autistic people with intellectual disabilities or from minority groups took part. It does not describe every person. If you are worried about someone, contact a clinician, a health service or a crisis service; if there is immediate danger, call the emergency number of your country.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person, ta på allvar varje tecken på att hen känner sig som en belastning; det hjälper att fråga lugnt och utan att döma hur hen mår. Den här nätstudien med 314 autistiska vuxna fann att känslan av att vara en belastning, depression och att mentalt öva på självmordsplaner hängde ihop med självmordstankar under det senaste året. Studien var tvärsnittsstudie utan kontrollgrupp och kan inte visa orsaker; få autistiska personer med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning eller från minoriteter deltog. Den beskriver inte varje person. Om du är orolig för någon, kontakta en läkare, vården eller en krisjour; vid akut fara, ring larmnumret i ditt land.

title: Autism Spectrum Disorder and Clinical High Risk for Psychosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
authors: Vaquerizo-Serrano J, Salazar de Pablo G, Singh J, Santosh P
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Psychotic experiences can occur in autism spectrum disorders (ASD). Some of the ASD individuals with these experiences may fulfil Clinical High-Risk for Psychosis (CHR-P) criteria. A systematic literature search was performed to review the information on ASD and CHR-P. A meta-analysis of the proportion of CHR-P in ASD was conducted. The systematic review included 13 studies. The mean age of ASD individuals across the included studies was 11.09 years. The Attenuated Psychosis Syndrome subgroup was the most frequently reported. Four studies were meta-analysed, showing that 11.6% of CHR-P individuals have an ASD diagnosis. Symptoms of prodromal psychosis may be present in individuals with ASD. The transition from CHR-P to psychosis is not affected by ASD.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista cuenta experiencias inusuales, como oír o ver cosas que otros no perciben, o ideas muy extrañas, tómalo en serio, escucha sin juzgar y consúltalo con un profesional clínico. No asumas que son parte del autismo. La evidencia es un metaanálisis con revisión sistemática de 13 estudios; la edad media de las personas autistas fue de 11.09 años, y en cuatro estudios el 11.6% de las personas con alto riesgo clínico de psicosis tenía diagnóstico de autismo. Sus límites: pocos estudios en el metaanálisis y no sirve para predecir lo que ocurrirá en una persona concreta.
sheet.en: If an autistic person describes unusual experiences, such as hearing or seeing things others do not, or very unusual ideas, take it seriously, listen without judging, and raise it with a clinician. Do not assume it is simply part of autism. The evidence is a systematic review and meta-analysis of 13 studies; the mean age of the autistic people was 11.09 years, and in four meta-analysed studies 11.6% of people at clinical high risk for psychosis had an autism diagnosis. Limits: few studies were pooled, and the results cannot predict what will happen for any one person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person berättar om ovanliga upplevelser, som att höra eller se saker andra inte märker, eller mycket ovanliga tankar, ta det på allvar, lyssna utan att döma och ta upp det med en kliniker. Anta inte att det bara hör till autismen. Underlaget är en systematisk översikt och metaanalys av 13 studier; medelåldern bland de autistiska personerna var 11,09 år, och i fyra metaanalyserade studier hade 11,6 % av dem med klinisk hög risk för psykos en autismdiagnos. Begränsningar: få studier ingick i sammanvägningen, och resultaten kan inte förutsäga vad som händer för en enskild person.

title: Intervention Services for Autistic Adults: An ASDEU Study of Autistic Adults, Carers, and Professionals' Experiences.
authors: Micai M, Ciaramella A, Salvitti T, Fulceri F, Fatta LM, Poustka L, Diehm R, Iskrov G, Stefanov R, Guillon Q, Rogé B, Staines A, Sweeney MR, Boilson AM, Leósdóttir T, Saemundsen E, Moilanen I, Ebeling
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: The Autism Spectrum Disorders in the European Union (ASDEU) survey investigated local services' use experiences of autistic adults, carers and professionals with interventions for autistic adults. The majority of the 697 participants experienced recommended considerations prior to deciding on intervention and during the intervention plan and implementation. Psychosocial interventions were the most commonly experienced interventions, while pharmacological interventions NOT recommended for core autistic symptoms were reported by fairly large proportions of participants. Family interventions were experienced slightly more commonly by carers than adults or professionals. Less than the 26% of autistic adult responders who had experienced challenging behaviors reported receiving an intervention to change them. These results provide insights for improving gaps in service provision of interventions among autistic adults.

sheet.es: Si apoyas a una persona autista adulta, antes de elegir una intervención conviene preguntar qué objetivos tiene ella, qué opciones existen y cómo se revisará el plan. Una encuesta europea (ASDEU) recogió las experiencias de 697 personas: adultas autistas, cuidadoras y profesionales. La mayoría vivió las consideraciones recomendadas antes y durante la intervención. Las intervenciones psicosociales fueron las más habituales. Los resultados son de una encuesta, no prueban qué funciona mejor y no valen igual para cada persona. Las decisiones médicas, incluidos los fármacos, corresponden a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult, before choosing an intervention it helps to ask what goals they have, what options exist and how the plan will be reviewed. A European survey (ASDEU) gathered the experiences of 697 people: autistic adults, carers and professionals. Most had experienced the recommended considerations before and during the intervention. Psychosocial interventions were the most common. The results come from a survey, do not prove what works best, and do not apply equally to every person. Medical decisions, including medication, belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen är det bra att fråga, innan en insats väljs, vilka mål personen har, vilka alternativ som finns och hur planen ska följas upp. En europeisk enkät (ASDEU) samlade erfarenheter från 697 personer: autistiska vuxna, anhöriga och yrkesverksamma. De flesta hade upplevt de rekommenderade övervägandena före och under insatsen. Psykosociala insatser var vanligast. Resultaten kommer från en enkät, visar inte vad som fungerar bäst och gäller inte lika för alla. Medicinska beslut, även om läkemedel, hör till en läkare eller annan kliniker.

title: A Personalized Multidisciplinary Approach to Evaluating and Treating Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Frye RE
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a complex neurodevelopmental disorder without a known cure. Current standard-of-care treatments focus on addressing core symptoms directly but have provided limited benefits. In many cases, individuals with ASD have abnormalities in multiple organs, including the brain, immune and gastrointestinal system, and multiple physiological systems including redox and metabolic systems. Additionally, multiple aspects of the environment can adversely affect children with ASD including the sensory environment, psychosocial stress, dietary limitations and exposures to allergens and toxicants. Although it is not clear whether these medical abnormalities and environmental factors are related to the etiology of ASD, there is evidence that many of these factors can modulate ASD symptoms, making them a potential treatment target for improving core and associated ASD-related symptoms and improving functional limitation. Additionally, addressing underlying biological disturbances that drive pathophysiology has the potential to be disease modifying. This article describes a systematic approach using clinical history and biomarkers to personalize medical treatment for children with ASD. This approach is medically comprehensive, making it attractive for a multidisciplinary approach. By concentrating on treatable conditions in ASD, it is possible to improve functional ability and quality of life, thus providing optimal outcomes.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a un niño autista, puede ser útil llevar a las consultas un registro de su historial: sueño, alimentación, malestar digestivo, estrés y entorno sensorial. Así los profesionales pueden valorar cada caso de forma individual. Es una revisión que describe un enfoque que combina historia clínica y biomarcadores en niños autistas. Sus límites: no aporta datos propios de participantes, el propio texto reconoce que no está claro si estos factores causan el autismo, y no sirve como regla para todas las personas. Cualquier decisión médica corresponde a un profesional sanitario.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic child, it may help to bring notes to appointments about their sleep, eating, digestive discomfort, stress and sensory environment, so professionals can look at each person individually. This is a review describing an approach that combines clinical history and biomarkers for autistic children. Its limits: it reports no data from participants, the text itself says it is unclear whether these factors are linked to the origins of autism, and it is not a rule for every person. Any medical decision belongs to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar ett autistiskt barn kan det hjälpa att ta med anteckningar till besök om sömn, mat, magbesvär, stress och sensorisk miljö, så att yrkespersoner kan se till varje barns situation. Detta är en översikt som beskriver ett upplägg där sjukhistoria och biomarkörer kombineras för autistiska barn. Begränsningar: den redovisar inga egna deltagardata, texten säger själv att det är oklart om faktorerna hänger ihop med autismens ursprung, och den gäller inte som regel för alla. Medicinska beslut hör hemma hos en läkare eller annan vårdgivare.

title: PTCHD1 : Identification and Neurodevelopmental Contributions of an Autism Spectrum Disorder and Intellectual Disability Susceptibility Gene.
authors: Pastore SF, Ko SY, Frankland PW, Hamel PA, Vincent JB
abstract: Over the last one and a half decades, copy number variation and whole-genome sequencing studies have illuminated the considerable genetic heterogeneity that underlies the etiologies of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and intellectual disability (ID). These investigations support the idea that ASD may result from complex interactions between susceptibility-related genetic variants (single nucleotide variants or copy number variants) and the environment. This review outlines the identification and neurobiological characterization of two such genes located in Xp22.11, Patched domain-containing 1 ( PTCHD1 ), and its antisense lncRNA PTCHD1-AS . Animal models of Ptchd1 disruption have recapitulated a subset of clinical symptoms related to ASD as well as to ID. Furthermore, these Ptchd1 mouse knockout studies implicate the expression of Ptchd1 in both the thalamic and the hippocampal brain regions as being crucial for proper neurodevelopment and cognitive function. Altered kynurenine metabolic signalling has been postulated as a disease mechanism in one of these animal studies. Additionally, ASD patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) carrying a copy number loss impacting the antisense non-coding RNA PTCHD1-AS have been used to generate 2D neuronal cultures. While copy number loss of PTCHD1-AS does not affect the transcription of PTCHD1 , the neurons exhibit diminished miniature excitatory postsynaptic current frequency, supporting its role in ASD etiology. A more thorough understanding of risk factor genes, such as PTCHD1 and PTCHD1-AS , will help to clarify the intricate genetic and biological mechanisms that underlie ASD and ID, providing a foundation for meaningful therapeutic interventions to enhance the quality of life of individuals who experience these conditions.

sheet.es: Este trabajo es de laboratorio y no cambia lo que haces mañana por la mañana. Puede ayudarte a entender que el autismo y la discapacidad intelectual tienen orígenes genéticos muy variados y que un gen concreto no explica a todas las personas. Es una revisión de estudios sobre el gen PTCHD1, con modelos animales y neuronas cultivadas a partir de células de personas autistas. Sus límites: no hay pautas prácticas, gran parte del trabajo es en ratones y no sirve para decidir nada sobre una persona concreta. Si te preocupan las causas genéticas, consulta con un profesional de genética clínica.
sheet.en: This is laboratory work and it does not change what you do tomorrow morning. It may help you understand that autism and intellectual disability have very varied genetic origins, and that one gene does not explain every person. It is a review of studies on the PTCHD1 gene, using animal models and neurons grown from cells of autistic people. Its limits: it offers no practical guidance, much of the work is in mice, and it cannot settle anything about one particular person. If genetic causes concern you, talk with a clinical genetics professional.
sheet.sv: Det här är laboratorieforskning och ändrar inte vad du gör i morgon bitti. Den kan hjälpa dig att förstå att autism och intellektuell funktionsnedsättning har mycket varierande genetiska ursprung, och att en enskild gen inte förklarar alla personer. Det är en översikt av studier om genen PTCHD1, med djurmodeller och nervceller odlade från celler från autistiska personer. Begränsningar: den ger inga praktiska råd, mycket av arbetet gjordes på möss och den kan inte avgöra något om en enskild person. Om du funderar på genetiska orsaker kan du prata med en klinisk genetiker.

title: Community Knowledge about Autism Spectrum Disorder in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
authors: Abualhommos AK, Aldoukhi AH, Alyaseen AAA, AlQanbar FA, Alshawarib N, Almuhanna ZA
journal: International journal of environmental research and public health
abstract: Objectives To explore the knowledge of the general community in Saudi Arabia about autism spectrum disorder. Method A cross-sectional study was conducted for the period between June and September 2021 in Saudi Arabia using an online questionnaire tool. The questionnaire tool was developed based on a literature review. The questionnaire tool consists of 34 items that assess knowledge about autism spectrum disorder in terms of its etiology, autistic patient features, autistic children's abilities and needs, and autistic adults' abilities and needs. The total score for each subscale was used to define the level of knowledge of it. Correct answers were given a score of one, and the total score for each subscale was used to describe the level of knowledge of it. Logistic regression was used to identify predictors of good knowledge about autism spectrum disorder (defined as a total score equal or above the mean score of the study participants). Results This study enlisted the participation of 500 people. The participants' overall understanding of autism spectrum disorder was moderate, with a mean score of 20.6 (SD: 5.6) out of 34, or 60.6%. The participants' knowledge levels ranged from 32.2% to 77.5%. The items about the abilities and needs of adolescents and young people with autism had the highest degree of knowledge (77.5%). The items about autism's causes had the lowest level of expertise (32.2%). When compared to others, females, those with a master's degree, and those working in the healthcare field had a higher likelihood of knowing more about the autism spectrum condition. ( p ≤ 0.05). Conclusion Knowledge about autism spectrum disorder in Saudi Arabia is moderate. Social media channels and healthcare centers should be used to conduct educational campaigns for parents. The goal of this educational campaign should be to improve parents' ability to recognize the causes of autism.

sheet.es: Si buscas información sobre el autismo para tu familia, conviene contrastar sobre todo lo que se dice de sus causas, porque ahí había menos conocimiento. Hablar con profesionales de la salud o con centros de salud puede ayudar. Es un estudio transversal con cuestionario en línea, con 500 personas de la comunidad general de Arabia Saudita, no con personas autistas. El conocimiento general fue moderado: 20,6 de 34 puntos de media. Sobre las causas, solo 32.2%. Sus límites: refleja a un grupo concreto de un país, no dice nada sobre una persona autista en particular ni sirve como regla para todas las familias.
sheet.en: If you are looking for information about autism for your family, it is worth double-checking what you read about its causes, because that was where knowledge was lowest. Talking with health professionals or health centres can help. This was a cross-sectional study using an online questionnaire with 500 people from the general community in Saudi Arabia, not with autistic people. Overall knowledge was moderate: a mean score of 20.6 out of 34. On causes, only 32.2%. Its limits: it reflects one group in one country, says nothing about any individual autistic person, and is not a rule for every family.
sheet.sv: Om du söker information om autism till din familj är det värt att dubbelkolla det som sägs om orsakerna, eftersom kunskapen var lägst där. Det kan hjälpa att prata med vårdpersonal eller vårdcentraler. Det var en tvärsnittsstudie med webbenkät bland 500 personer i allmänheten i Saudiarabien, inte med autistiska personer. Den samlade kunskapen var måttlig: 20,6 poäng av 34 i genomsnitt. Om orsaker var den bara 32.2%. Begränsningar: studien speglar en grupp i ett land, säger inget om någon enskild autistisk person och är ingen regel för alla familjer.

title: Immune Dysregulation in Autism Spectrum Disorder: What Do We Know about It?
authors: Robinson-Agramonte MLA, Noris García E, Fraga Guerra J, Vega Hurtado Y, Antonucci N, Semprún-Hernández N, Schultz S, Siniscalco D
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a group of complex multifactorial neurodevelopmental disorders characterized by a wide and variable set of neuropsychiatric symptoms, including deficits in social communication, narrow and restricted interests, and repetitive behavior. The immune hypothesis is considered to be a major factor contributing to autism pathogenesis, as well as a way to explain the differences of the clinical phenotypes and comorbidities influencing disease course and severity. Evidence highlights a link between immune dysfunction and behavioral traits in autism from several types of evidence found in both cerebrospinal fluid and peripheral blood and their utility to identify autistic subgroups with specific immunophenotypes; underlying behavioral symptoms are also shown. This review summarizes current insights into immune dysfunction in ASD, with particular reference to the impact of immunological factors related to the maternal influence of autism development; comorbidities influencing autism disease course and severity; and others factors with particular relevance, including obesity. Finally, we described main elements of similarities between immunopathology overlapping neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative disorders, taking as examples autism and Parkinson Disease, respectively.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista tiene problemas de salud frecuentes, como molestias digestivas o infecciones, vale la pena anotarlos y comentarlos con su profesional sanitario; no hace falta cambiar nada por cuenta propia. Esta es una revisión que resume estudios sobre el sistema inmunitario en el autismo, incluidos factores maternos, otras condiciones de salud y la obesidad. Sus límites: es un resumen, no una prueba directa; habla de grupos, no de cada persona, y no permite decir qué ocurre en una persona concreta ni qué decisiones médicas tomar.
sheet.en: If an autistic person often has health problems, such as stomach discomfort or infections, it is worth noting them and discussing them with their health professional; nothing needs to change on your own. This is a review summarising studies on the immune system in autism, including maternal factors, other health conditions and obesity. Its limits: it is a summary, not direct proof; it describes groups, not each person, and it cannot tell us what is happening for one individual or which medical decisions to make.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person ofta har hälsobesvär, som magont eller infektioner, är det värt att anteckna dem och ta upp dem med vårdpersonal; du behöver inte ändra något på egen hand. Detta är en översikt som sammanfattar studier om immunsystemet vid autism, bland annat moderns påverkan, andra hälsotillstånd och fetma. Begränsningar: det är en sammanfattning, inte ett direkt bevis; den beskriver grupper, inte varje person, och kan inte säga vad som gäller för en enskild individ eller vilka medicinska beslut som bör tas.

title: Perspective: Presuming Autistic Communication Competence and Reframing Facilitated Communication.
authors: Heyworth M, Chan T, Lawson W
abstract: Debate surrounding the validity of the method of supported typing known as facilitated communication (FC) has been continuous since its inception in the 1990s. Views are polarized on whether FC can be considered an authenticated method for use by people with complex communication needs (CCN) or significant challenges in speech, language, and communication. This perspective article presents an analysis of the research arguing for-and against-the use of FC, combined with the lived experience knowledge of autistic adults who utilize FC, to rehabilitate its current standing as discredited and unevidenced. By considering extant qualitative and quantitative studies, as well as personal accounts of the use of this particular Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) method, the authors argue that the current dismissal of FC is rooted in ableist and outdated approaches. FC research should be reconsidered and reconducted using current best practice autism research approaches, including coproduction and a presumption of autistic communication competence, to assess its validity as a potential AAC method for autistic individuals.

sheet.es: Presuma siempre que la persona autista es competente para comunicarse y escuche cómo describe ella misma lo que le ayuda. Si usa o quiere probar la escritura con apoyo, hable con su equipo de apoyo sobre qué opciones de comunicación aumentativa existen y cómo comprobar que los mensajes son suyos. Evidencia: es un artículo de perspectiva que analiza investigaciones a favor y en contra, junto con la experiencia vivida de adultos autistas que usan la comunicación facilitada. Límites: no es un experimento nuevo, sus autores defienden una postura y piden nueva investigación; no demuestra que el método funcione para cada persona.
sheet.en: Presume that the autistic person is competent to communicate, and listen to how they describe what helps them. If they use or want to try supported typing, talk with their support team about which augmentative communication options exist and how to check that the messages are their own. Evidence: this is a perspective article that reviews research for and against facilitated communication, together with the lived experience of autistic adults who use it. Limits: it is not a new experiment, the authors argue a position and call for new research, and it does not show the method works for every person.
sheet.sv: Utgå från att den autistiska personen kan kommunicera, och lyssna på hur hen själv beskriver vad som hjälper. Om hen använder eller vill prova stödd skrivning, prata med stödteamet om vilka alternativa kommunikationssätt som finns och hur man kan försäkra sig om att budskapen är personens egna. Evidens: en perspektivartikel som går igenom forskning för och emot faciliterad kommunikation, tillsammans med levd erfarenhet från autistiska vuxna som använder den. Begränsningar: det är inte en ny studie, författarna driver en ståndpunkt och efterlyser ny forskning, och artikeln visar inte att metoden fungerar för alla.

title: Environmental exposures associated with elevated risk for autism spectrum disorder may augment the burden of deleterious de novo mutations among probands.
authors: Pugsley K, Scherer SW, Bellgrove MA, Hawi Z
abstract: Although the full aetiology of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is unknown, familial and twin studies demonstrate high heritability of 60-90%, indicating a predominant role of genetics in the development of the disorder. The genetic architecture of ASD consists of a complex array of rare and common variants of all classes of genetic variation usually acting additively to augment individual risk. The relative contribution of heredity in ASD persists despite selective pressures against the classic autistic phenotype; a phenomenon thought to be explained, in part, by the incidence of spontaneous (or de novo) mutations. Notably, environmental exposures attributed as salient risk factors for ASD may play a causal role in the emergence of deleterious de novo variations, with several ASD-associated agents having significant mutagenic potential. To explore this hypothesis, this review article assesses published epidemiological data with evidence derived from assays of mutagenicity, both in vivo and in vitro, to determine the likely role such agents may play in augmenting the genetic liability in ASD. Broadly, these exposures were observed to elicit genomic alterations through one or a combination of: (1) direct interaction with genetic material; (2) impaired DNA repair; or (3) oxidative DNA damage. However, the direct contribution of these factors to the ASD phenotype cannot be determined without further analysis. The development of comprehensive prospective birth cohorts in combination with genome sequencing is essential to forming a causal, mechanistic account of de novo mutations in ASD that links exposure, genotypic alterations, and phenotypic consequences.

sheet.es: Para el día a día, este estudio no cambia nada: no hay ninguna acción nueva que tomar ni motivo para buscar culpas. Ser autista está ligado sobre todo a la genética, y nada de lo que hizo o dejó de hacer una familia se señala aquí como causa. Es una revisión que reúne estudios epidemiológicos y de laboratorio para plantear una idea: algunas exposiciones ambientales podrían favorecer cambios genéticos nuevos (de novo) asociados al autismo. Su límite es claro: es una hipótesis, no una prueba; los propios autores dicen que hacen falta grandes estudios de seguimiento desde el nacimiento con secuenciación genética para saber si esta relación es real.
sheet.en: For everyday life, this study changes nothing: there is no new action to take and no reason to look for blame. Being autistic is linked mainly to genetics, and nothing a family did or didn't do is identified here as a cause. This is a review that brings together epidemiological and laboratory studies to propose an idea: some environmental exposures might encourage new (de novo) genetic changes associated with autism. Its limit is clear: it is a hypothesis, not proof; the authors themselves say large birth cohort studies with genome sequencing are needed to know whether this link is real.
sheet.sv: I vardagen ändrar den här studien ingenting: det finns ingen ny åtgärd att vidta och ingen anledning att leta efter skuld. Att vara autistisk hänger främst ihop med genetik, och inget en familj gjort eller inte gjort pekas här ut som orsak. Det är en översikt som samlar epidemiologiska studier och laboratoriestudier för att lägga fram en idé: vissa miljöexponeringar skulle kunna bidra till nya (de novo) genetiska förändringar kopplade till autism. Begränsningen är tydlig: det är en hypotes, inte ett bevis; författarna skriver själva att stora födelsekohorter med gensekvensering behövs för att veta om sambandet är verkligt.

title: "A Group of Fellow Travellers Who Understand": Interviews With Autistic People About Post-diagnostic Peer Support in Adulthood.
authors: Crompton CJ, Hallett S, McAuliffe C, Stanfield AC, Fletcher-Watson S
abstract: Receiving a diagnosis of autism in adulthood can be a life changing event, impacting identity, relationships, and mental health. A lack of post-diagnostic support has been highlighted by autistic adults, their allies, clinicians, and service providers. It can be a source of distress for autistic adults, reinforcing feelings of social isolation and rejection. Peer support could be a cost-effective, flexible, and sustainable model to provide community-based support for autistic adults. However, there is little research on the value of peer support, despite calls from the autistic community. This qualitative study explored autistic experiences and needs post-diagnosis, identifying specific ways that peer support may benefit them, and exploring the limitations of peer support. Twelve autistic adults who had all received an autism diagnosis in adulthood completed a semi-structured interview focussing on the diagnostic experience, post-diagnostic support needed and provided, engagement with the autistic community, and post-diagnostic peer support. Thematic analysis of interview transcripts resulted in four themes: (1) Mismatch in support needed and provided; (2) Community connection; (3) Flexible and personalised support; and (4) Sustainability. Participants indicated that peer support may be a useful mechanism to support autistic adults' post-diagnosis and offers unique opportunities not available through other support channels. Though informal peer support exists, it could be more sustainable and effective if well-supported and funded.

sheet.es: Si tú o alguien cercano recibe un diagnóstico de autismo en la adultez, puede ayudar buscar contacto con otras personas autistas: grupos locales, asociaciones o comunidades en línea. Muchas personas encuentran allí comprensión, información práctica y una sensación de pertenencia que los servicios formales a menudo no ofrecen. Conviene que el apoyo sea flexible: cada persona elige el ritmo, el formato (presencial, escrito, en línea) y cuánto participa. Es un estudio cualitativo basado en entrevistas con doce adultos autistas diagnosticados en la adultez. Sus límites: es un grupo pequeño, describe experiencias y no mide resultados, y lo que sirvió a estas personas puede no servir a todas.
sheet.en: If you or someone close to you is diagnosed autistic as an adult, it may help to look for contact with other autistic people: local groups, autistic-led organisations or online communities. Many people find understanding, practical tips and a sense of belonging there that formal services often don't provide. Support works best when it is flexible: each person chooses the pace, the format (in person, written, online) and how much to take part. This is a qualitative interview study with twelve autistic adults diagnosed in adulthood. Its limits: the group is small, it describes experiences rather than measuring outcomes, and what helped these people may not suit everyone.
sheet.sv: Om du eller någon nära dig får en autismdiagnos i vuxen ålder kan det hjälpa att söka kontakt med andra autistiska personer: lokala grupper, föreningar som drivs av autistiska personer eller nätgemenskaper. Många hittar där förståelse, praktiska tips och en känsla av tillhörighet som vården ofta inte erbjuder. Stödet fungerar bäst när det är flexibelt: varje person väljer takt, form (på plats, skriftligt, digitalt) och hur mycket hen vill delta. Det här är en kvalitativ intervjustudie med tolv autistiska vuxna som fått diagnos i vuxen ålder. Begränsningar: gruppen är liten, studien beskriver upplevelser snarare än mäter effekter, och det som hjälpte dessa personer passar inte nödvändigtvis alla.

title: The lived experience of gender dysphoria in autistic young people: a phenomenological study with young people and their parents.
authors: Cooper K, Butler C, Russell A, Mandy W
abstract: Gender dysphoria is distress in relation to incongruence between an individual's gender and sex assigned at birth. Gender clinics offer support for gender dysphoria, and there is a higher prevalence of autism in young people attending such clinics than in the general population. We aimed to investigate the lived experiences of autistic young people who have experienced gender dysphoria, and their parents, using a multi-perspectival IPA design. Young autistic people aged 13-17 years (n = 15), and their parents (n = 16), completed in-depth interviews about the young person's experience of gender dysphoria. We analysed each individual transcript to generate individual themes, and for each of the dyads, developed themes which acknowledged the similarities and differences in parent-child perspectives. The first superordinate theme was coping with distress which had two subordinate themes; understanding difficult feelings and focus on alleviating distress with external support. This theme described how young people were overwhelmed by negative feelings which they came to understand as being about gender incongruence and looked to alleviate these feelings through a gender transition. The second superordinate theme was working out who I am which had two subordinate themes: the centrality of different identities and needs and thinking about gender. This theme described how young people and their parents focused on different needs; while young people more often focused on their gender-related needs, parents focused on autism-related needs. We conclude that young people and parents may have different perspectives and priorities when it comes to meeting the needs of autistic young people who experience gender dysphoria.

sheet.es: Si un joven autista expresa malestar por su género, escúchele con calma y pregúntele qué necesita; es posible que sus prioridades y las suyas no coincidan. Es un estudio cualitativo con entrevistas en profundidad a 15 jóvenes autistas de 13-17 años y a 16 padres o madres. Los jóvenes se centraban más en necesidades relacionadas con el género y las familias, en necesidades relacionadas con el autismo. Es un grupo pequeño, no permite generalizar a todas las personas, y no indica qué decisión tomar; las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If an autistic young person tells you they feel distress about their gender, listen calmly and ask what they need; their priorities and yours may differ. This was a qualitative study using in-depth interviews with 15 autistic young people aged 13-17 and 16 parents. Young people more often focused on gender-related needs, while parents focused on autism-related needs. It was a small group, so it cannot speak for everyone, and it does not say what choices to make; medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk ung person berättar om obehag kring sitt kön, lyssna lugnt och fråga vad hen behöver; era prioriteringar kan skilja sig åt. Det här var en kvalitativ studie med djupintervjuer av 15 autistiska unga i åldern 13-17 år och 16 föräldrar. De unga fokuserade oftare på könsrelaterade behov, medan föräldrarna fokuserade på autismrelaterade behov. Gruppen var liten och kan inte representera alla, och studien säger inte vilka beslut som ska fattas; medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker.

title: Avoiding Ableist Language: Suggestions for Autism Researchers.
authors: Bottema-Beutel K, Kapp SK, Lester JN, Sasson NJ, Hand BN
abstract: In this commentary, we describe how language used to communicate about autism within much of autism research can reflect and perpetuate ableist ideologies (i.e., beliefs and practices that discriminate against people with disabilities), whether or not researchers intend to have such effects. Drawing largely from autistic scholarship on this subject, along with research and theory from disability studies and discourse analysis, we define ableism and its realization in linguistic practices, provide a historical overview of ableist language used to describe autism, and review calls from autistic researchers and laypeople to adopt alternative ways of speaking and writing. Finally, we provide several specific avenues to aid autism researchers in reflecting on and adjusting their language choices. Lay summary Why is this topic important?: In the past, autism research has mostly been conducted by nonautistic people, and researchers have described autism as something bad that should be fixed. Describing autism in this way has negative effects on how society views and treats autistic people and may even negatively affect how autistic people view themselves. Despite recent positive changes in how researchers write and speak about autism, "ableist" language is still used. Ableist language refers to language that assumes disabled people are inferior to nondisabled people. What is the purpose of this article?: We wrote this article to describe how ableism influences the way autism is often described in research. We also give autism researchers strategies for avoiding ableist language in their future work. What is the perspective of the authors?: We believe that ableism is a "system of discrimination," which means that it influences how people talk about and perceive autism whether or not they are aware of it, and regardless of whether or not they actually believe that autistic people are inferior to nonautistic people. We also believe that language choices are part of what perpetuates this system. Because of this, researchers need to take special care to determine whether their language choices reflect ableism and take steps to use language that is not ableist. What is already known about this topic?: Autistic adults (including researchers and nonresearchers) have been writing and speaking about ableist language for several decades, but nonautistic autism researchers may not be aware of this work. We have compiled this material and summarized it for autism researchers. What do the authors recommend?: We recommend that researchers understand what ableism is, reflect on the language they use in their written and spoken work, and use nonableist language alternatives to describe autism and autistic people. For example, many autistic people find terms such as "special interests" and "special needs" patronizing; these terms could be replaced with "focused interests" and descriptions of autistic people's specific needs. Medicalized/deficit language such as "at risk for autism" should be replaced by more neutral terms such as "increased likelihood of autism." Finally, ways of speaking about autism that are not restricted to particular terms but still contribute to marginalization, such as discussion about the "economic burden of autism," should be replaced with discourses that center the impacts of social arrangements on autistic people. How will these recommendations help autistic people now or in the future?: Language is a powerful means for shaping how people view autism. If researchers take steps to avoid ableist language, researchers, service providers, and society at large may become more accepting and accommodating of autistic people.

sheet.es: Tómate un momento para fijarte en cómo hablas de autismo, también delante de la persona autista. Algunas personas autistas encuentran condescendientes expresiones como «intereses especiales» o «necesidades especiales»; puedes probar con «intereses focalizados» y nombrar la necesidad concreta. Este artículo es un comentario de autores que reúne el trabajo de personas autistas y teoría de estudios de la discapacidad; no es un experimento con participantes. Es una propuesta dirigida a investigadores, no una regla para todas las personas: cada persona autista puede preferir palabras distintas, así que lo mejor es preguntárselo.
sheet.en: Take a moment to notice how you talk about autism, including in front of the autistic person. Some autistic people find phrases like "special interests" or "special needs" patronizing; you could try "focused interests" and name the specific need instead. This article is a commentary that gathers work by autistic scholars and theory from disability studies; it is not an experiment with participants. It is written for researchers, not as a rule for everyone: each autistic person may prefer different words, so the best step is to ask them.
sheet.sv: Stanna upp och lägg märke till hur du pratar om autism, även när den autistiska personen hör det. Vissa autistiska personer upplever uttryck som "särskilda intressen" eller "särskilda behov" som nedlåtande; du kan prova "fokuserade intressen" och beskriva det konkreta behovet. Artikeln är en kommentar som samlar autistiska forskares arbete och teori från funktionshinderstudier; det är inte ett experiment med deltagare. Den riktar sig till forskare och är ingen regel för alla: varje autistisk person kan föredra andra ord, så fråga helst personen själv.

claim.es: El lenguaje que usamos sobre el autismo importa: términos como 'conducta desafiante' o 'bajo funcionamiento' estigmatizan.
claim.en: The words we use about autism matter: terms like 'challenging behaviour' or 'low functioning' stigmatise.
claim.sv: Orden vi använder om autism spelar roll: uttryck som 'utmanande beteende' eller 'lågfungerande' stigmatiserar.

supports.es: Describir qué pasó y qué ayudó, sin etiquetar a la persona.
supports.en: Describing what happened and what helped, not labelling the person.
supports.sv: Att beskriva vad som hände och vad som hjälpte, inte att etikettera personen.

doesNotSupport.es: Que todos deban usar las mismas palabras; las preferencias varían y hay que preguntarlas.
doesNotSupport.en: That everyone must use identical words; preferences vary and should be asked.
doesNotSupport.sv: Att alla måste använda samma ord; preferenser varierar och bör efterfrågas.

title: Experiences of Sensory Overload and Communication Barriers by Autistic Adults in Health Care Settings.
authors: Strömberg M, Liman L, Bang P, Igelström K
abstract: Background Autistic adults have an elevated risk of many health problems compared with the general population, making health care access extra critical. Unfortunately, autistic people often find health care settings quite aversive, and many medical providers report feeling unsure about how to interact with autistic patients. We aimed at characterizing specific challenges regarding sensory experiences and communicative barriers in health care settings. Methods We recruited adults to complete an anonymous online questionnaire on the topic of improving health care experiences for everyone.
