The questions covered demographics, sensory experiences in medical settings, and communication with health care providers. We quantified the associations between autism diagnosis and experiences of sensory discomfort and communication barriers in health care settings. We also did a qualitative analysis of text responses to questions on how to improve sensory environments and communication with providers. Results Swedish adults (62 autistic and 36 nonautistic) participated in the study. The cohort was well educated, and autistic participants received their autism diagnosis late in life (median age 36 years, range 13-57). Compared with nonautistic participants, autistic participants reported greater discomfort with background sound levels in health care settings and felt more misunderstood by health care providers. Thematic analyses showed that auditory stimuli and proximity to other people were particularly bothersome for autistic participants, causing stress or avoidance and affecting the ability to interact with providers. Providers contributed to communication barriers by failing to recognize the need for individualized information, especially when respondents' difficulties were not visible or taken seriously. Participants requested greater clarity and supplementary written information. Providers also misunderstood autistic adults' body language or eye contact patterns, as they interpreted their clients through the lens of neurotypical expectations. Conclusions Our results extend previous research by emphasizing sensory aspects of health care settings and suggesting specific and reasonable adaptations. The results also highlight how the provider's implicit expectations of nonverbal communication caused misinterpretations of autistic people who were socially skilled but did not use typical body language. Based on the data, we suggest specific adaptations, many of which may also benefit nonautistic people.

sheet.es: Antes de una cita médica, puede ayudar pedir una sala de espera tranquila o esperar fuera, solicitar información por escrito y explicar al personal que la falta de contacto visual o un lenguaje corporal distinto no significa desinterés ni que todo esté bien. En este estudio, los adultos autistas señalaron el ruido de fondo y la cercanía de otras personas como especialmente estresantes, y se sintieron más incomprendidos por los profesionales. Se trata de una encuesta anónima en línea con 62 adultos autistas y 36 no autistas en Suecia. Sus límites: muestra pequeña, muy formada y con diagnóstico tardío, por lo que no representa a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: Before a medical appointment, it can help to ask for a quiet waiting space or to wait outside, request written information, and tell staff that little eye contact or different body language does not mean disinterest or that everything is fine. In this study, autistic adults described background noise and being close to other people as especially stressful, and felt more misunderstood by providers. It was an anonymous online survey of 62 autistic and 36 non-autistic adults in Sweden. Its limits: a small, highly educated sample, mostly diagnosed late in life, so it does not represent every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Inför ett vårdbesök kan det hjälpa att be om ett lugnt väntrum eller att få vänta utanför, be om skriftlig information och berätta för personalen att lite ögonkontakt eller annorlunda kroppsspråk inte betyder ointresse eller att allt är bra. I studien beskrev autistiska vuxna bakgrundsljud och närhet till andra människor som särskilt stressande, och de kände sig oftare missförstådda av vårdpersonal. Det var en anonym webbenkät med 62 autistiska och 36 icke-autistiska vuxna i Sverige. Begränsningar: urvalet var litet, högutbildat och fick oftast diagnos sent i livet, så resultaten gäller inte alla autistiska personer.

title: Autistic Adults' Experiences of Camouflaging and Its Perceived Impact on Mental Health.
authors: Bradley L, Shaw R, Baron-Cohen S, Cassidy S
abstract: Background: Camouflaging (also referred to as "masking") is a commonly reported strategy used by autistic adults in everyday life to help them cope in social situations. Autistic adults report that camouflaging can have a devastating effect on mental health and well-being, yet little is known about the lived experiences of camouflaging and its impact. Methods: We designed an online survey in partnership with autistic adults, to explore the experiences of camouflaging and its impact on mental health. Participants self-reported the lifetime experience of camouflaging, where they camouflaged the frequency and length of time spent camouflaging. Four open questions allowed participants to elaborate their answers to the closed questions on frequency and length of time, and subsequently any positive and negative aspects of their experience of camouflaging. Two hundred seventy-seven autistic adults who self-reported a diagnosis of an autism spectrum condition (128 female, 78 male) or self-identified as autistic (56 female, 15 male) were included in the analysis of qualitative responses to the open-ended questions. Findings: We thematically analyzed participant answers from the open questions. Three main themes emerged. First, "dangers of camouflaging" described how the amount of time spent camouflaging led to exhaustion, isolation, poor mental and physical health, loss of identity and acceptance of self, others' unreal perceptions and expectations, and delayed diagnosis. Second, "positive aspects of camouflaging" included greater access to social spaces, and protection from harm. Camouflaging was, therefore, seen as necessary to survive in a world designed for the neurotypical majority. Third, autistic adults described being diagnosed and accepted for who they are as reasons for "why I don't need to camouflage like I used to." Conclusions: Time spent camouflaging is what seems to be most damaging for the participants' mental health. The main reason reported for needing to spend so much time camouflaging is society's lack of awareness and acceptance of autism. Lay summary Why is this study being done?: Many autistic adults report that they need to camouflage their autistic behaviors to help them "fit in" and cope in social situations with non-autistic people. This is because society is not as aware and accepting of autistic people as it needs to be. We also know that for most autistic adults camouflaging is exhausting and damaging for their mental health. This study is important, because researchers have not studied camouflaging enough to know what it is like for autistic adults to camouflage in their everyday lives and to understand the impact that camouflaging has on their mental health. What was the purpose of this study?: We wanted to ask autistic adults about their positive and negative experiences of camouflaging. This is important because it will help professionals better understand why autistic adults camouflage, and better support the mental health needs of autistic adults. This increased understanding may also help society become more aware and accepting of autism. If this happens, autistic adults will not need to camouflage as much. Not having to camouflage as much could also help prevent and reduce mental health problems in autistic adults. What did we do?: We asked autistic adults with a clinical diagnosis and those who self-identify as autistic to complete an online survey. The survey asked questions about mental health, self-injury, suicidal thoughts, and suicidal behaviors. One part of the survey asked questions about camouflaging. If research participants said they camouflaged or masked their autistic characteristics to cope with social situations, they would then be asked about when and why they camouflage, and about the positive and negative consequences of camouflaging. What did we find?: We found that autistic people confirmed that they camouflage because of a lack of awareness and acceptance of autism in society. We also found that both autistic males and females camouflage. Although some autistic adults said that "everyone" camouflages, they thought that autistic people spent much more time than non-autistic people camouflaging in their everyday lives. Spending lots of time camouflaging was what was most damaging for autistic adults' mental health. Although most autistic adults thought that camouflaging was damaging to their mental health, some thought that it helped them too. How will knowing this help autistic adults?: Our results suggest that it is important to reduce pressure to camouflage. This could help prevent high rates of mental health problems in autistic people. Our results suggest that this can be achieved if wider society becomes more aware and accepting of autistic people. Our results also suggest that reducing pressure to camouflage could benefit everyone in society.

title: Investigating Markers of Rapport in Autistic and Nonautistic Interactions.
authors: Rifai OM, Fletcher-Watson S, Jiménez-Sánchez L, Crompton CJ
abstract: Background Autism is considered to entail a social impairment whereby autistic people experience difficulty interpreting others' mental states. However, recent research has shown that nonautistic people also have difficulty understanding the mental states of autistic people. This mismatch of understanding may explain lower rapport in interactions between autistic and nonautistic people. As mental states can be expressed externally through socially normed signals, it is important to investigate the role of such signals in autistic, nonautistic, and mixed interactions. This study explores variability in two social signals between autistic, nonautistic, and mixed interactions, and how their use may affect rapport within interactions. Methods Videos from a previous study of autistic, nonautistic, and mixed pair interactions in a diffusion chain context in which participants were aware of others' diagnostic status were video coded for mutual gaze and backchanneling as candidate indicators of interactional rapport. Results Although use of mutual gaze and backchanneling was lower in mixed pairs than in nonautistic pairs, corresponding to lower ratings of interactional rapport, less backchanneling in autistic pairs of both nonverbal and verbal subtypes corresponded to higher ratings of rapport. Conclusions We observed differences in the use of candidate rapport markers between autistic, mixed, and nonautistic interactions, which did not map onto patterns of rapport scores, suggesting differences in reliance on these cues between autistic and nonautistic people. These results suggest that visible markers of rapport may vary by neurotype or pairing and give clues to inform future investigations of autistic interaction.

sheet.es: Tomorrow, si conversas con una persona autista, no des por hecho que la mirada mutua o los gestos y sonidos de asentimiento (como "ajá") indican conexión; pregunta con calma cómo se siente cómoda. El estudio analizó vídeos de un trabajo previo con parejas autistas, no autistas y mixtas, que sabían el diagnóstico de la otra persona. En las parejas mixtas había menos mirada mutua y menos asentimientos, con menor sensación de conexión; en las parejas autistas, menos asentimientos se asociaron con mayor conexión. Es un análisis observacional, no prueba causas, y no sirve como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: Tomorrow, when you talk with an autistic person, don't assume eye contact or small nods and sounds like "mm-hm" show connection; calmly ask what feels comfortable for them. The study coded videos from an earlier project with autistic, nonautistic and mixed pairs who knew each other's diagnostic status. Mixed pairs used less mutual gaze and backchanneling and had lower rapport ratings; in autistic pairs, less backchanneling matched higher rapport. It is observational, cannot show causes, and is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: I morgon, när du pratar med en autistisk person, ta inte för givet att ögonkontakt eller små nickningar och ljud som "mm" visar kontakt; fråga lugnt vad som känns bekvämt. Studien kodade videor från ett tidigare projekt med autistiska, icke-autistiska och blandade par som kände till varandras diagnosstatus. Blandade par använde mindre ömsesidig blick och mindre återkoppling och fick lägre skattad kontakt; i autistiska par hörde mindre återkoppling ihop med högre kontakt. Studien är observerande, visar inte orsaker och är ingen regel för varje person.

title: The Cerebellar Involvement in Autism Spectrum Disorders: From the Social Brain to Mouse Models.
authors: Mapelli L, Soda T, D'Angelo E, Prestori F
abstract: Autism spectrum disorders (ASD) are pervasive neurodevelopmental disorders that include a variety of forms and clinical phenotypes. This heterogeneity complicates the clinical and experimental approaches to ASD etiology and pathophysiology. To date, a unifying theory of these diseases is still missing. Nevertheless, the intense work of researchers and clinicians in the last decades has identified some ASD hallmarks and the primary brain areas involved. Not surprisingly, the areas that are part of the so-called "social brain", and those strictly connected to them, were found to be crucial, such as the prefrontal cortex, amygdala, hippocampus, limbic system, and dopaminergic pathways. With the recent acknowledgment of the cerebellar contribution to cognitive functions and the social brain, its involvement in ASD has become unmistakable, though its extent is still to be elucidated. In most cases, significant advances were made possible by recent technological developments in structural/functional assessment of the human brain and by using mouse models of ASD. Mouse models are an invaluable tool to get insights into the molecular and cellular counterparts of the disease, acting on the specific genetic background generating ASD-like phenotype. Given the multifaceted nature of ASD and related studies, it is often difficult to navigate the literature and limit the huge content to specific questions. This review fulfills the need for an organized, clear, and state-of-the-art perspective on cerebellar involvement in ASD, from its connections to the social brain areas (which are the primary sites of ASD impairments) to the use of monogenic mouse models.

sheet.es: Esta revisión no ofrece ninguna pauta para el día a día, pero sirve para recordar que el autismo es muy diverso y que cada persona tiene su propio perfil. Si alguien en casa tiene dudas sobre su desarrollo, lo útil es observar lo que necesita y hablarlo con su equipo de apoyo. Evidencia: es una revisión de la literatura sobre el cerebelo, las áreas del "cerebro social" y modelos de ratón. Límites: no probó nada con personas, su alcance en el autismo aún no está aclarado y no debe tomarse como una regla para todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: This review gives no everyday guidance, but it is a reminder that autism is very diverse and every person has their own profile. If you have questions about someone's development, it helps to observe what they need and talk it through with their support team. Evidence: it is a review of the literature on the cerebellum, the "social brain" areas and mouse models. Limits: it tested nothing with people, the extent of the cerebellum's role in autism is still unclear, and it should not be treated as a rule for every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Den här översikten ger inga råd för vardagen, men den påminner om att autism är mycket varierande och att varje person har sin egen profil. Har du frågor om någons utveckling hjälper det att observera vad personen behöver och prata om det med stödteamet. Evidens: en översikt av litteraturen om lillhjärnan, det "sociala hjärnan"-områdena och musmodeller. Begränsningar: inget testades på människor, lillhjärnans roll vid autism är fortfarande oklar, och resultaten bör inte ses som en regel för alla autistiska personer.

title: Gastrointestinal Symptoms in Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review.
authors: Leader G, Abberton C, Cunningham S, Gilmartin K, Grudzien M, Higgins E, Joshi L, Whelan S, Mannion A
abstract: This systematic review aims to offer an updated understanding of the relationship between gastrointestinal symptoms (GIS) and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in children and adolescents. The databases PsycINFO, Medline, Cinahl, and ERIC were searched using keywords, and relevant literature was hand-searched. Papers ( n = 3319) were systematically screened and deemed eligible if they were empirical studies published in English since 2014 and measured the GIS of individuals with ASD who were under 18 years old. Thirty studies were included in the final review. The study findings were synthesized under eight themes, including the prevalence and nature of GIS and their relationship with developmental regression, language and communication, ASD severity, challenging behavior, comorbid psychopathology, sleep problems, and sensory issues. The review found that GIS were common and that there was contradictory evidence concerning their relationship with co-occurring conditions. It also identified evidence of some causal relationships that support the existence of the gut-immune-brain pathways. Future research needs to use large prospective designs and objective and standardized GIS measurements to provide a nuanced understanding of GIS in the context of ASD.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista muestra molestias de estómago o intestino, vale la pena tomarlas en serio y comentarlas con su profesional de salud, porque pueden relacionarse con el sueño, las sensaciones o el malestar general. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 30 estudios sobre niñas, niños y adolescentes autistas menores de 18 años. Encontró que los síntomas gastrointestinales eran comunes, aunque la evidencia sobre su relación con otras condiciones era contradictoria. Tiene límites: los diseños no eran ideales y las mediciones no estaban estandarizadas, así que no sirve como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If an autistic person shows stomach or bowel discomfort, it is worth taking seriously and raising with their health professional, since it may connect with sleep, sensory experience or general wellbeing. This systematic review brought together 30 studies of autistic children and adolescents under 18. It found gastrointestinal symptoms were common, while evidence on their links with other co-occurring conditions was contradictory. There are limits: the study designs were not ideal and measurements were not standardized, so it is not a rule for every individual.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person visar obehag i magen eller tarmen är det värt att ta på allvar och ta upp med vårdpersonal, eftersom det kan hänga ihop med sömn, sinnesupplevelser eller allmänt mående. Denna systematiska översikt samlade 30 studier om autistiska barn och ungdomar under 18 år. Den fann att magtarmsymtom var vanliga, medan bevisen för kopplingar till andra samtidiga tillstånd var motsägelsefulla. Det finns begränsningar: studiedesignerna var inte idealiska och mätningarna var inte standardiserade, så resultaten är ingen regel för varje person.

title: Sodium Benzoate-Harmfulness and Potential Use in Therapies for Disorders Related to the Nervous System: A Review.
authors: Walczak-Nowicka ŁJ, Herbet M
abstract: Currently, due to the large number of reports regarding the harmfulness of food additives, more and more consumers follow the so-called "clean label" trend, i.e., prefer and choose the least-processed food products. One of the compounds known as a preservative with a high safety profile is sodium benzoate. While some studies show that it can be used to treat conditions such as depression, pain, schizophrenia, autism spectrum disorders, and neurodegenerative diseases, others report its harmfulness. For example, it was found to cause mutagenic effects, generate oxidative stress, disrupt hormones, and reduce fertility. Due to such disparate results, the purpose of this study is to comprehensively discuss the safety profile of sodium benzoate and its potential use in neurodegenerative diseases, especially in autism spectrum disorder (ASD), schizophrenia, major depressive disorder (MDD), and pain relief.

sheet.es: Esta revisión no ofrece nada que cambiar mañana en casa. Si alguien se pregunta por el benzoato de sodio, un conservante de alimentos, conviene hablarlo con su profesional sanitario antes de tomar decisiones. Es una revisión de estudios sobre su seguridad y su posible uso en afecciones del sistema nervioso, incluido el autismo; el resumen no indica quiénes participaron. Algunos trabajos hablan de beneficios y otros de daños, así que los resultados son dispares. Al tratarse de un enfoque médico, las decisiones corresponden a un clínico, y esto no vale como regla para toda persona autista.
sheet.en: This review gives nothing to change at home tomorrow. If you wonder about sodium benzoate, a food preservative, talk with a health professional before making any decisions. It is a review of studies on its safety and possible use in conditions of the nervous system, including autism; the abstract does not say who took part. Some studies report benefits and others report harm, so results are mixed. Because this is a medical topic, decisions belong to a clinician, and it should not be treated as a rule for every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Den här översikten ger inget att ändra hemma i morgon. Om du undrar över natriumbensoat, ett livsmedelskonserveringsmedel, prata med vårdpersonal innan du fattar beslut. Det är en översikt av studier om dess säkerhet och möjliga användning vid tillstånd i nervsystemet, inklusive autism; sammanfattningen anger inte vilka som deltog. Vissa studier rapporterar nytta och andra skada, så resultaten går isär. Eftersom det är ett medicinskt område hör besluten till en läkare, och det gäller inte som regel för alla autistiska personer.

title: Sociocultural context and autistics' quality of life: A comparison between Québec and France.
authors: Caron V, Jeanneret N, Giroux M, Guerrero L, Ouimet M, Forgeot d'Arc B, Soulières I, Courcy I
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract What is already known about the topic? Quality of life refers to how people perceive aspects of their life such as physical health, material security, and interpersonal relationships. Studies have reported lower quality of life among autistic individuals than in the general population. What does this article contribute? This article contributes to a better understanding of quality of life and its measures from the point of view of autistic adults. By comparing two groups of French-speaking autistic adults from two different places (France and Québec-Canada), this research shows that the perception of quality of life and its determining factors differ for autistic adults living in each country. The Québec group reported a superior quality of life, and some quality of life predictors were different in each group. The social experience of autism-related stigmatization, however, was a powerful predictor of quality of life for all. Implications for practice, research, and policy To promote a higher quality of life for autistic people, it is important to consider the sociocultural context and implement awareness programs and public campaigns aimed at identifying and countering stigmatization processes.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista, tenerlo presente puede ayudar: el estigma que vive por ser autista pesa mucho en su calidad de vida. Escuchar cómo vive esas situaciones y explicar el autismo a su entorno puede ser un buen primer paso. La evidencia es un estudio con personas autistas adultas francófonas de Francia y de Québec; el grupo de Québec refirió mejor calidad de vida, y algunos factores que la predecían diferían entre ambos grupos. Como compara solo dos lugares, no sirve como regla para cada persona ni para otros contextos, y la experiencia individual puede ser distinta.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person, keep in mind that the stigma they experience for being autistic weighs heavily on their quality of life. Listening to how they experience those situations, and explaining autism to people around them, can be a good first step. The evidence is a study with French-speaking autistic adults from France and Québec; the Québec group reported better quality of life, and some factors that predicted it differed between the groups. Because it compares only two places, it is not a rule for every person or every context, and individual experience may differ.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person kan det hjälpa att veta att det stigma hen möter för att vara autistisk väger tungt för livskvaliteten. Att lyssna på hur hen upplever sådana situationer och förklara autism för omgivningen kan vara ett bra första steg. Underlaget är en studie med fransktalande autistiska vuxna från Frankrike och Québec; gruppen i Québec rapporterade bättre livskvalitet, och vissa faktorer som förutsade livskvalitet skilde sig mellan grupperna. Eftersom studien jämför bara två platser är den ingen regel för varje person eller sammanhang, och individuella upplevelser kan skilja sig.

title: A systematic review of person-centred adjustments to facilitate magnetic resonance imaging for autistic patients without the use of sedation or anaesthesia.
authors: Stogiannos N, Carlier S, Harvey-Lloyd JM, Brammer A, Nugent B, Cleaver K, McNulty JP, Dos Reis CS, Malamateniou C
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic patients often undergo magnetic resonance imaging examinations. Within this environment, it is usual to feel anxious and overwhelmed by noises, lights or other people. The narrow scanners, the loud noises and the long examination time can easily cause panic attacks. This review aims to identify any adaptations for autistic individuals to have a magnetic resonance imaging scan without sedation or anaesthesia. Out of 4442 articles screened, 53 more relevant were evaluated and 21 were finally included in this study. Customising communication, different techniques to improve the environment, using technology for familiarisation and distraction have been used in previous studies. The results of this study can be used to make suggestions on how to improve magnetic resonance imaging practice and the autistic patient experience. They can also be used to create training for the healthcare professionals using the magnetic resonance imaging scanners.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista va a hacerse una resonancia magnética, conviene hablar antes con el equipo sanitario sobre ajustes: explicar el proceso de forma personalizada, adaptar el entorno (ruido, luz, personas presentes) y practicar con apoyos tecnológicos de familiarización o distracción. Se trata de una revisión sistemática: de 4442 artículos revisados, se incluyeron 21 estudios sobre adaptaciones sin sedación ni anestesia. Sus límites: el resumen no indica qué ajuste funciona mejor ni para quién, así que cada persona necesitará probar lo que le resulte útil y decidir con su equipo médico.
sheet.en: If an autistic person is going to have an MRI scan, it helps to talk with the healthcare team beforehand about adjustments: explaining the process in a personalised way, adapting the environment (noise, lights, who is in the room) and using technology for familiarisation or distraction. This is a systematic review: of 4442 articles screened, 21 studies on adaptations without sedation or anaesthesia were included. Its limits: the abstract does not say which adjustment works best or for whom, so each person will need to try what suits them and decide together with their medical team.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person ska göra en magnetkameraundersökning är det bra att på förhand prata med vårdteamet om anpassningar: att förklara förloppet på ett personligt sätt, anpassa miljön (ljud, ljus, vilka som är i rummet) och använda teknik för att förbereda och avleda. Det här är en systematisk översikt: av 4442 granskade artiklar ingick 21 studier om anpassningar utan sedering eller narkos. Begränsning: sammanfattningen säger inte vilken anpassning som fungerar bäst eller för vem, så varje person behöver pröva vad som passar och bestämma tillsammans med sitt vårdteam.

title: The lived experience of gender dysphoria in autistic adults: An interpretative phenomenological analysis.
authors: Cooper K, Mandy W, Butler C, Russell A
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic people are more likely to be transgender, which means having a gender identity different to one's sex assigned at birth. Some transgender people experience distress about their gender and sex assigned at birth not matching which is called gender dysphoria. Research has focused on finding out why autistic people are more likely to have gender dysphoria, and less on what the experience of gender dysphoria is like for autistic people. We interviewed 21 autistic adults about their experience of incongruence between their gender identity and sex assigned at birth, and any associated distress. We carefully read the transcripts of the interviews, focusing on how participants understood their experiences. We found a range of themes from the interviews. Participants were distressed because their bodies did not match their gender identities. Participants told us they had to work hard to understand themselves and who they were, and to manage having multiple different needs such as mental health needs. It was upsetting for participants to experience discrimination because of being autistic and/or transgender. Some participants said it was more difficult to get transgender healthcare as an autistic person. Some participants thought being autistic had helped them understand their gender identity more than non-autistic people. Other participants found it was challenging to be both autistic and transgender. For example, most participants wanted to change their bodies to match their gender identity, but some participants were nervous about making changes to themselves and their routine due to being autistic. We conclude that autism can in some ways be helpful and other ways contribute to challenges for transgender autistic people.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista cercana habla de su identidad de género, escúchela sin cuestionar que su autismo invalide lo que siente. Puede necesitar tiempo para entenderse, apoyo con su salud mental y ayuda práctica para gestionar cambios y rutinas si decide hacer una transición. Esté atento a la discriminación que pueda vivir y acompáñela cuando busque atención sanitaria, que a veces resulta más difícil para personas autistas. Este estudio cualitativo entrevistó en profundidad a 21 adultos autistas con experiencias de disforia de género. Al ser un grupo pequeño y basado en entrevistas, describe vivencias diversas, no reglas que se apliquen a todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person close to you talks about their gender identity, listen without assuming their autism makes their feelings less valid. They may need time to understand themselves, support with mental health, and practical help managing changes and routines if they choose to transition. Watch for discrimination they may face, and offer to accompany them when seeking healthcare, which can be harder to access as an autistic person. This qualitative study interviewed 21 autistic adults in depth about their experiences of gender dysphoria. Because it is a small, interview-based group, it describes varied experiences rather than rules that apply to everyone.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person nära dig pratar om sin könsidentitet, lyssna utan att anta att autismen gör känslorna mindre giltiga. Personen kan behöva tid att förstå sig själv, stöd för psykisk hälsa och praktisk hjälp med förändringar och rutiner om hen väljer att transitionera. Var uppmärksam på diskriminering hen kan möta, och erbjud att följa med i kontakter med vården, som kan vara svårare att få tillgång till som autistisk. Denna kvalitativa studie intervjuade 21 autistiska vuxna på djupet om deras erfarenheter av könsdysfori. Eftersom gruppen är liten och bygger på intervjuer beskriver den olika upplevelser, inte regler som gäller alla.

title: Cognitive processes in autism: Repetitive thinking in autistic versus non-autistic adults.
authors: Cooper K, Russell A, Calley S, Chen H, Kramer J, Verplanken B
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract A core feature of autism is the tendency to do the same activity or behaviour repetitively. We wanted to find out if autistic people also experience repetitive thinking, for example, having the same thoughts repeatedly. We thought that there would be a link between repetitive behaviour and repetitive thinking. We asked 54 autistic people and 66 non-autistic people to complete questionnaires measuring repetitive behaviours and obsessive thinking. Next, participants were trained by a researcher to record their thoughts using a structured paper form. They then completed 5 days of thought recording, which they did each time a random alarm sounded on their mobile phone. We found that autistic people had more repetitive thoughts than non-autistic people, but they did not report having more negative or visual thoughts compared with non-autistic people. Autistic people who had more repetitive thoughts during the 5 days of thought recording did not report more repetitive behaviour. However, autistic people who reported more obsessive thinking, for example, more negative and unwanted thoughts, also reported higher levels of repetitive behaviour. We conclude that some repetitive behaviours may be linked to anxiety and that more research is needed to better understand repetitive behaviours in autism.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista repite mucho los mismos pensamientos, puede ser algo habitual y no tiene por qué ser negativo. Pregúntale con calma cómo son esos pensamientos y si le inquietan. Si le generan angustia, ayudar a reducir la ansiedad puede ser útil. Evidencia: estudio con 54 personas autistas y 66 no autistas que respondieron cuestionarios y anotaron sus pensamientos durante 5 días. Las personas autistas tuvieron más pensamientos repetitivos, pero no más negativos ni visuales. Límites: es un solo estudio con adultos, se basa en lo que cada persona cuenta y no demuestra causas; no sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person often has the same thoughts again and again, that may be common and is not necessarily bad. Ask calmly what those thoughts are like and whether they bother them. If they cause distress, supporting ways to reduce anxiety may help. Evidence: a study of 54 autistic and 66 non-autistic adults who completed questionnaires and recorded their thoughts over 5 days. Autistic people had more repetitive thoughts, but not more negative or visual ones. Limits: it is a single study of adults, relies on self-report and cannot show causes, so it is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person ofta har samma tankar om och om igen kan det vara vanligt och behöver inte vara något dåligt. Fråga lugnt hur tankarna känns och om de oroar. Om de skapar ångest kan stöd för att minska oro vara till hjälp. Evidens: en studie med 54 autistiska och 66 icke-autistiska vuxna som fyllde i enkäter och antecknade sina tankar under 5 dagar. De autistiska deltagarna hade fler upprepade tankar, men inte fler negativa eller visuella. Begränsningar: det är en enskild studie med vuxna, den bygger på egna rapporter och visar inte orsaker, så den är ingen regel för alla.

title: Examining the Relationship Between Sleep Quality, Social Functioning, and Behavior Problems in Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review.
authors: Whelan S, Mannion A, Madden A, Berger F, Costello R, Ghadiri S, Leader G
abstract: Over forty percent of autistic children experience poor sleep quality, and social interaction difficulties are a core characteristic of autism. However, the relationship between sleep quality and social functioning and behavior remains poorly understood. This systematic review examined the evidence concerning the impact of sleep quality on the social functioning and behavior problems in autistic children and adolescents. It also identified key related factors and evaluated how this issue has been researched to date. Seven key journals were hand-searched and five databases were systematically searched, using keywords. Titles and abstracts of 4123 items were screened against eligibility criteria by two researchers. Relevant studies were retained if they were peer-reviewed empirical papers, published in English between 2000 and 2021. Then, the full text of 97 papers was screened and if they met the eligibility criteria, their reference lists were hand-searched. Forty-six studies were included in the final review. Data were systematically extracted and two authors critically appraised the strengths and weaknesses of studies using Critical Appraisal Skills Programme tools. Key themes were identified, because a meta-analysis was not possible due to the studies' heterogeneity. The review identified that sleep quality and social functioning are associated with one another and there is a small amount of evidence that a bi-directional causal relationship may exist. Evidence suggests that several nights of suboptimal sleep duration and a lack of deep continuous sleep negatively impact externalizing and internalizing behavior. Sleep quality is also reduced by anxiety and sensory sensitivity. However, longitudinal studies with larger samples are needed to establish causality. Future research needs to examine confounding factors and to develop consensus regarding best-practice processes for the objective measurement of sleep with autistic children. Additional research also needs to further examine the consequences of poor sleep quality on internalizing behavior, and the impact of socio-cultural practices.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija autista ha dormido mal varias noches, es razonable esperar más irritabilidad, tristeza o retraimiento al día siguiente, y ajustar las exigencias sociales. Observar qué afecta al sueño, como la ansiedad o la sensibilidad sensorial (luz, ruido, texturas), puede orientar cambios suaves en la rutina nocturna. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 46 estudios con niños y adolescentes autistas y encontró que sueño y vida social están relacionados, quizá en ambas direcciones. Sus límites: los estudios eran muy distintos entre sí, faltan seguimientos largos con muestras grandes y no se puede afirmar causa y efecto ni aplicarlo igual a cada persona.
sheet.en: If your autistic child has slept poorly for several nights, it is reasonable to expect more irritability, sadness or withdrawal the next day, and to lighten social demands. Noticing what disrupts sleep, such as anxiety or sensory sensitivity (light, noise, textures), can guide gentle changes to the bedtime routine. This systematic review brought together 46 studies of autistic children and adolescents and found that sleep and social life are linked, possibly in both directions. Its limits: the studies differed widely, long-term studies with larger groups are lacking, and cause and effect cannot be confirmed or applied the same way to every person.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn har sovit dåligt flera nätter är det rimligt att räkna med mer irritation, nedstämdhet eller tillbakadragenhet dagen efter, och att minska sociala krav. Att lägga märke till vad som stör sömnen, till exempel oro eller sensorisk känslighet (ljus, ljud, texturer), kan vägleda varsamma ändringar i kvällsrutinen. Denna systematiska översikt samlade 46 studier med autistiska barn och ungdomar och fann att sömn och socialt liv hänger ihop, kanske i båda riktningarna. Begränsningar: studierna skilde sig mycket åt, långa uppföljningar med större grupper saknas och orsak och verkan kan inte fastställas eller gälla lika för alla.

title: Suicidal Thoughts and Behaviours Among Autistic Adults Presenting to the Psychiatric Emergency Department: An Exploratory Chart Review.
authors: Jachyra P, Lai MC, Zaheer J, Fernandes N, Dale M, Sawyer A, Lunsky Y
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Despite increasing attention on suicidality in autistic people, we know little about suicidal presentations when autistic individuals present to hospital emergency departments (ED). We conducted an exploratory retrospective chart review of suicidal thoughts and behaviours (STB) of autistic adults who presented to a psychiatric ED. The analysis included 16 charts over a 10-week period. Findings highlight that reported STB were not always the presenting issue. Life transitions and interpersonal conflicts were common antecedents, and active rumination about STB was distressing and fatiguing. Findings imply that ED visits serve as important opportunities for suicidal risk reduction for autistic individuals, through implementation of strategies for identification of STB such as active screening, and the provision of suicide resources tailored to autistic people.

title: Self-reported COVID-19 vaccination acceptance and hesitancy among autistic adults.
authors: Shea LL, Becker A, Lee BK, Miller KK, Cooper D, Anderson K, Salzer MS, Vanness DJ
abstract: Identifying factors associated with COVID-19 vaccination acceptance among vulnerable groups, including autistic individuals, can increase vaccination rates and support public health. The purpose of this study was to determine differences among autistic adults who reported COVID-19 vaccination acceptance from those who did not. In this study we describe COVID-19 vaccination status and self-reported preferences among autistic adults and identify related factors. Vaccine accepters were more likely to report increased loneliness during COVID-19, lived in more populous counties (p = 0.02), and lived in counties won by President Biden in the 2020 US presidential election (p < 0.001). Positive correlations were found between desire to protect others, concern about contracting COVID-19, and trusting vaccine safety (p < 0.001). Concern about vaccine safety was common among the vaccine hesitant, while lack of concern about COVID-19 overall was not. Identifying health promotion strategies based on self-reported, lived experiences about COVID-19 among vulnerable groups is key for public health impact.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta duda sobre la vacuna contra la COVID-19, conviene preguntarle con calma qué le preocupa y escuchar su experiencia. Aquí, la duda se relacionaba sobre todo con la seguridad de la vacuna, no con restar importancia a la COVID-19. Es un estudio con personas autistas adultas que describieron su propia vacunación y sus preferencias. Los resultados son asociaciones, no causas; reflejan a personas de Estados Unidos y no valen para todas las personas. Las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult is unsure about the COVID-19 vaccine, it helps to calmly ask what worries them and listen to their experience. Here, hesitancy was mostly linked to concern about vaccine safety, not to taking COVID-19 lightly. This was a study with autistic adults who described their own vaccination status and preferences. The findings are associations, not causes; they reflect people in the US and do not apply to everyone. Medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen är tveksam till covid-19-vaccinet kan det hjälpa att lugnt fråga vad som oroar och lyssna på personens erfarenhet. Här hängde tveksamhet mest ihop med oro för vaccinets säkerhet, inte med att man tog covid-19 lätt. Det var en studie med autistiska vuxna som beskrev sin egen vaccinationsstatus och sina preferenser. Resultaten är samband, inte orsaker; de gäller personer i USA och inte alla. Medicinska beslut hör till en läkare eller annan vårdgivare.

title: Coaching While Waiting for Autism Spectrum Disorder Assessment: A Pilot Feasibility Study for a Randomized Controlled Trial on Occupational Performance Coaching and Service Navigation.
authors: Bernie C, Williams K, Graham F, May T
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Aim To determine whether short-phase Occupational Performance Coaching combined with service navigation support is feasible for families waiting for autism assessment. Method A pilot feasibility study was conducted using a blinded randomization procedure that allocated participants to one of three trial arms: (1) face-to-face coaching, (2) videoconference coaching, and (3) usual care. Outcomes included a retention aim of 70-80%, goal attainment and secondary standardised measures of adaptive behaviour, social skills, parenting stress, service access and family quality of life. Results Caregivers and children (n = 16, child mean age of 3 years 7 months) were recruited following referral for an autism assessment. Retention was 75%, with change scores in performance and satisfaction of selected goals higher in the intervention groups than the usual care group. Interpretation Findings support progression to a future randomized controlled trial assessing intervention efficacy.

sheet.es: Si su familia está esperando una evaluación de autismo, puede ser útil pedir apoyo para elegir metas concretas del día a día y para orientarse entre los servicios. Este estudio piloto asignó al azar a 16 cuidadores e hijos pequeños a coaching presencial, coaching por videollamada o atención habitual. La retención fue de 75% y las metas elegidas mejoraron más en los grupos con coaching. Sin embargo, es un estudio muy pequeño, pensado para comprobar si el enfoque es viable, no para demostrar que funciona. No sirve como regla para todas las familias.
sheet.en: If your family is waiting for an autism assessment, it may help to ask for support in choosing concrete everyday goals and in finding your way around services. This small pilot trial randomly assigned 16 caregivers and young children to face-to-face coaching, videoconference coaching or usual care. Retention was 75%, and change scores for the chosen goals were higher in the coaching groups. However, the study was very small and designed to test feasibility, not to prove that the approach works. It is not a rule for every family.
sheet.sv: Om din familj väntar på en autismutredning kan det vara värdefullt att be om stöd med att välja konkreta vardagsmål och hitta bland olika tjänster. I denna lilla pilotstudie lottades 16 vårdnadshavare och små barn till coachning ansikte mot ansikte, coachning via videosamtal eller vanlig vård. Andelen som fullföljde var 75 %, och förändringen i de valda målen var större i coachninggrupperna. Studien var dock mycket liten och gjord för att pröva om upplägget är genomförbart, inte för att bevisa att det fungerar. Den är ingen regel för alla familjer.

title: A Preliminary Evaluation of a Brief Behavioral Parent Training for Challenging Behavior in Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Rohacek A, Baxter EL, Sullivan WE, Roane HS, Antshel KM
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders

title: mHealth apps delivering early intervention to support parents of children with autism: a scoping review protocol.
authors: Bharat R, Uzaina U, Yadav T, Niranjan S, Kurade P
abstract: Objective This review aims to identify the mhealth apps delivering early intervention to support parents of children with autism spectrum disorders (ASD). We aim to explore the concept, context and methodology of implementation that is, theoretical framework, feasibility, quality of evidence, for such apps. Background To improve outcomes for children with autism, early intervention has been found to be promising. Parental training, parent psychoeducation and parent-mediated intervention are regarded as the gold standard, to achieve early childhood development goals. Digital health technologies like tele-health, web-based services, have been used to deliver this at a reduced cost. There is little evidence about their use and efficacy in empowering parents of children with ASD. Inclusion criteria The studies reporting the use of mhealth apps to support parents of children with ASD, in community settings, school settings, special schools, clinics, hospitals or child development centres. There will be no exclusion based on region, gender or sociocultural factors. The types of studies included will be quantitative, qualitative, mixed-methods study designs, case reports, grey literature, systematic reviews, clinical trials and studies reporting feasibility of digital mhealth applications. Method Using the NICE Healthcare Databases Advanced Search, we will search the following databases: MEDLINE, PUBMED, CINAHL, EMBASE, PsycINFO, Cochrane Library, EbscoHost, Sabinet, SAGE Journals, Directory of Open Access Journals, BioMed Central, Scopus, ScienceDirect. Furthermore, grey literature will be searched through Google Scholar, ShodhGanga, JSTOR, CORE, EBSCO, DOAJ, BASE. The searches will be limited to the age range of children between 2 and 6 years with ASD, and the date range is from the inception of the database to the current date. The terms for the ASD will be combined with terms for parent, early intervention and digital mhealth to identify eligible studies.

sheet.es: Si buscas apoyo para ti como madre, padre o cuidador de un niño autista pequeño, las aplicaciones móviles pueden ser una opción, pero por ahora este trabajo no dice cuáles funcionan. Es el protocolo de una revisión: describe cómo se buscarán estudios sobre apps de intervención temprana para familias de niños autistas de 2 a 6 años. Aún no presenta resultados. Sus autores señalan que hay poca evidencia sobre su eficacia. Antes de elegir una app, conviene consultar con el equipo profesional que acompaña a tu hijo o hija.
sheet.en: If you are a parent or caregiver of a young autistic child and looking for support, mobile apps may be one option, but this work does not yet say which ones work. It is the protocol for a review: it describes how studies will be searched for apps delivering early intervention to families of autistic children aged 2 to 6. It reports no results yet. Its authors note there is little evidence on how well such apps work. Before choosing an app, it helps to talk with the professionals who support your child.
sheet.sv: Om du är förälder eller vårdnadshavare till ett litet autistiskt barn och söker stöd kan mobilappar vara ett alternativ, men den här studien säger ännu inte vilka som fungerar. Det är ett protokoll för en översikt: det beskriver hur man ska söka efter studier om appar med tidiga insatser för familjer till autistiska barn i åldern 2 till 6 år. Några resultat redovisas inte ännu. Författarna anger att det finns lite evidens om hur effektiva sådana appar är. Innan du väljer en app kan det vara bra att prata med de yrkesverksamma som stöttar ditt barn.

title: Effectiveness of psychological techniques in dental management for children with autism spectrum disorder: a systematic literature review.
authors: AlBhaisi IN, Kumar MSTS, Engapuram A, Shafiei Z, Zakaria ASI, Mohd-Said S, McGrath C
abstract: Background A rise in the reported numbers of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) highlights the need for dental practitioners to be more familiar with the treatment approaches for these special needs children to ensure comfortable, well-accepted and efficient management while in dental office. Aim This paper aimed to acquire a deeper understanding of some of the innovative and best approaches to managing children with ASD in dental settings. Design A systematic literature search was performed in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane databases, and grey literature based on the PRISMA 2020 statement, using main keywords such as: 'management', 'dental', 'children', and 'Autism Spectrum Disorder'. Original full-text papers including randomised controlled trials (RCT) and all other designs of non-randomised controlled studies (NRS) reporting relevant intervention studies in English were included without any publication time limit. The quality of the evidence found eligible for the review were then assessed using the ROB-2 and ROBINS-I tools. Subsequently, the details of management interventions and impact of treatment approaches were compared and discussed. Results Out of the 204 articles found, 109 unrelated articles were excluded during the initial screening. The full papers of remaining 28 were retrieved and only 15 (7%) articles were eligible to be reviewed; eight RCTs with 'some concerns' and 'high risk' categories particularly concerning their randomisation design, and seven NSRs with 'serious' to 'critical' bias largely due to confounding factors. Conclusion Our review found inconclusive evidence on the strength of recent psychological and non-pharmacological approaches used to manage children with ASD in dental settings. Small sample size and lack of a control group in certain studies affected the strength of evidence and credibility of the findings. Nevertheless, this review shared informative details on some innovative approaches for better understanding of the management of children with ASD for dental professionals.

sheet.es: Antes de la cita dental, hable con el equipo odontológico sobre qué suele ayudar a su hijo o hija autista y pida un ritmo con apoyos previsibles. Esta revisión sistemática buscó en varias bases de datos y revisó 15 estudios sobre técnicas psicológicas y no farmacológicas en la consulta dental con niños autistas: ocho ensayos aleatorizados y siete no aleatorizados. Sus límites son importantes: la evidencia fue no concluyente, con muestras pequeñas, algunos estudios sin grupo de control y riesgo de sesgo de moderado a crítico. Por eso no demuestra que una técnica funcione para todos; sirve como ideas para probar con calma y adaptar a cada niño.
sheet.en: Before a dental visit, talk with the dental team about what usually helps your autistic child, and ask for a pace with predictable supports. This systematic review searched several databases and reviewed 15 studies of psychological and non-pharmacological techniques in dental settings for autistic children: eight randomised trials and seven non-randomised studies. Its limits matter: the evidence was inconclusive, with small samples, some studies lacking a control group, and risk of bias from some concerns to critical. So it does not show that any technique works for everyone; it offers ideas to try calmly and adapt to each child.
sheet.sv: Prata med tandvårdsteamet före besöket om vad som brukar hjälpa ditt autistiska barn, och be om ett tempo med förutsägbart stöd. Den här systematiska översikten sökte i flera databaser och gick igenom 15 studier om psykologiska och icke-farmakologiska tekniker i tandvården för autistiska barn: åtta randomiserade studier och sju icke-randomiserade. Begränsningarna är viktiga: bevisen var inte avgörande, med små urval, vissa studier utan kontrollgrupp och risk för bias från vissa farhågor till kritisk. Den visar alltså inte att en teknik fungerar för alla, utan ger idéer att prova lugnt och anpassa till varje barn.

title: Contributing factors to healthcare costs in individuals with autism spectrum disorder: a systematic review.
authors: Matin BK, Byford S, Soltani S, Kazemi-Karyani A, Atafar Z, Zereshki E, Soofi M, Rezaei S, Rakhshan ST, Jahangiri P
abstract: Background Individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) are more likely to use healthcare than their counterparts without disabilities, which imposes high medical costs to families and health systems. This study aimed to investigate healthcare costs and its determinants among individuals with ASD. Methods In this systematic review, we searched online databases (Web of Science, Medline through PubMed and Scopus) for observational and experimental studies that included data on service use and costs associated with ASD and published between January 2000 and May 2021. Exclusion criteria included non-English language articles, duplicates, abstracts, qualitative studies, gray literature, and non-original papers (e.g., letters to editors, editorials, reviews, etc.). Results Our searches yielded 4015 articles screened according to PRISMA guidelines. Of 4015 studies identified, 37 articles from 10 countries were eligible for final inclusion. Therapeutic interventions, outpatient visits and medications constituted the largest proportion of direct medical expenditure on individuals with ASD. Included studies suggest lack of health insurance, having associated morbidities, more severe symptoms, younger age groups and lower socioeconomic status (SES) are associated with higher medical expenditure in individuals with ASD. Conclusions This systematic review identified a range of factors, including lower SES and lack of health insurance, which are associated with higher healthcare costs in people with ASD. Our study supports the formulation of policy options to reduce financial risks in families of individuals with ASD in countries which do not have a tax-based or universal health coverage system.

sheet.es: Si planificas el presupuesto sanitario de tu familia, conviene prever gastos en terapias, consultas ambulatorias y medicamentos, que fueron la mayor parte del gasto médico directo. Revisa qué cubre tu seguro y pregunta a los servicios por ayudas económicas. Se trata de una revisión sistemática de 37 artículos de 10 países. Asocia mayor gasto con no tener seguro médico, otras condiciones de salud, edad más temprana y menor nivel socioeconómico. Son asociaciones, no reglas para cada familia, y el costo depende mucho del sistema de salud de cada país. Las decisiones médicas deben tomarse con un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If you are planning your family's healthcare budget, expect costs for therapies, outpatient visits and medications, which made up the largest share of direct medical spending. Check what your insurance covers and ask services about financial support. This is a systematic review of 37 articles from 10 countries. It linked higher spending to lack of health insurance, other health conditions, younger age and lower socioeconomic status. These are associations, not rules for every family, and costs depend a lot on each country's health system. Medical decisions belong with a clinician.
sheet.sv: När du planerar familjens vårdbudget kan du räkna med kostnader för terapier, öppenvårdsbesök och läkemedel, som stod för den största delen av de direkta medicinska utgifterna. Kontrollera vad din försäkring täcker och fråga vården om ekonomiskt stöd. Detta är en systematisk översikt av 37 artiklar från 10 länder. Högre kostnader hängde ihop med avsaknad av sjukförsäkring, andra hälsotillstånd, lägre ålder och lägre socioekonomisk status. Det är samband, inte regler för alla familjer, och kostnaderna beror mycket på varje lands vårdsystem. Medicinska beslut hör hemma hos en kliniker.

title: Biological correlates of altered circadian rhythms, autonomic functions and sleep problems in autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Dell'Osso L, Massoni L, Battaglini S, Cremone IM, Carmassi C, Carpita B
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition characterized by a complex and multifaceted neurobehavioral syndrome. In the last decades, several studies highlighted an increased prevalence of sleep problems in ASD, which would be associated with autonomic system and circadian rhythm disruption. The present review aimed to summarize the available literature about sleep problems in ASD subjects and about the possible biological factors implicated in circadian rhythm and autonomic system deregulation in this population, as well as possible therapeutic approaches. Shared biological underpinnings between ASD symptoms and altered circadian rhythms/autonomic functions are also discussed. Studies on sleep showed how ASD subjects typically report more problems regarding insufficient sleep time, bedtime resistance and reduced sleep pressure. A link between sleep difficulties and irritability, deficits in social skills and behavioral problems was also highlighted. Among the mechanisms implicated, alteration in genes related to circadian rhythms, such as CLOCK genes, and in melatonin levels were reported. ASD subjects also showed altered hypothalamic pituitary adrenal (HPA) axis and autonomic functions, generally with a tendency towards hyperarousal and hyper sympathetic state. Intriguingly, some of these biological alterations in ASD individuals were not associated only with sleep problems but also with more autism-specific clusters of symptoms, such as communication impairment or repetitive behaviors Although among the available treatments melatonin showed promising results, pharmacological studies for sleep problems in ASD need to follow more standardized protocols to reach more repeatable and reliable results. Further research should investigate the issue of sleep problems in ASD in a broader perspective, taking into account shared pathophysiological mechanisms for core and associated symptoms of ASD.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista duerme mal, conviene observar su sueño con curiosidad y sin culpas: anotar la hora de acostarse, cuánto tarda en dormirse y cómo se siente de día, y llevar esas notas a su profesional de salud. Esta es una revisión de la literatura sobre sueño, ritmos circadianos y funciones autonómicas en el autismo. Describe más problemas de sueño, como poco tiempo de sueño y resistencia a acostarse, y señales de hiperactivación del cuerpo. Sobre los fármacos, es un tema médico: las decisiones corresponden a un profesional clínico. Sus límites: resume estudios distintos, con protocolos poco uniformes, y no describe a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person sleeps badly, it helps to observe their sleep with curiosity rather than blame: note bedtime, how long it takes to fall asleep and how they feel by day, then share these notes with a health professional. This is a review of the literature on sleep, circadian rhythms and autonomic functions in autism. It describes more sleep problems, such as short sleep time and bedtime resistance, and signs of bodily hyperarousal. Where treatments are concerned, this is a medical matter: decisions belong to a clinician. Its limits: it summarizes varied studies with inconsistent protocols, and it does not describe every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person sover dåligt hjälper det att observera sömnen nyfiket och utan skuld: anteckna läggtid, hur lång tid det tar att somna och hur personen mår på dagen, och ta med anteckningarna till vårdpersonal. Detta är en översikt av litteraturen om sömn, dygnsrytm och autonoma funktioner vid autism. Den beskriver fler sömnproblem, som kort sömntid och motstånd mot att gå och lägga sig, samt tecken på kroppslig överaktivering. När det gäller läkemedel är det en medicinsk fråga: beslut tillhör en läkare. Begränsningar: den sammanfattar olika studier med ojämna protokoll och beskriver inte alla autistiska personer.

title: Evidence That Nine Autistic Women Out of Ten Have Been Victims of Sexual Violence.
authors: Cazalis F, Reyes E, Leduc S, Gourion D
abstract: Background Research indicates that sexual violence affects about 30% of women in the general population and between two to three times as much for autistic women. Materials and methods We investigated prevalence of sexual abuse, autistic traits and a range of symptoms, using an online survey addressed to the women of the French autistic community ( n = 225). We assessed victimization through an open question and through a specific questionnaire, derived from the Sexual Experiences Survey-Short Form Victimization. Results Both case identification methods yielded high figures: 68.9% victimization (open question) compared to 88.4% (standardized questionnaire). Two thirds of the victims were very young when they were first assaulted: among 199 victims, 135 were aged 18 or below and 112 participants were aged 15 or below. 75% of participants included in our study reported several aggressions. Analyses indicate that primo-victimization was highly correlated to revictimization and that being young increased that risk. Young victims were also at higher risk of developing post-traumatic stress disorder. A third of the victims reported the assault. 25% of those were able to file a complaint ( n = 12) and/or receive care ( n = 13). For the remainder 75%, reporting did not lead to action. Discussion Those findings indicate a very large proportion of victims of sexual assault among autistic women, consistently with previous research. The World Health Organization states unambiguously that sexual violence is systemic and that vulnerable individuals are preferably targeted by offenders. We therefore postulate that it would be erroneous to consider that victimization of autistic women is mainly due to autism. On the contrary, autism seems to be just a vulnerability factor. Some authors propose that educating potential victims to better protect themselves would help preventing abuse. We reviewed this proposition in the light of our results and found it to be impossible to apply since more than half of the victims were below or at the age of consent. Literature about sexual violence is discussed. Large-scale prevention programs proposed by World Health Organization and the Center for Disease Control aim at cultural changes in order to diminish gender inequality, that they identify as the very root of sexual violence.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una chica o mujer autista, crea desde hoy espacios tranquilos donde pueda contar cosas difíciles sin ser juzgada, y créela si lo hace. La responsabilidad es de los agresores y de los adultos que protegen, no de ella: enseñarle a «protegerse» no basta, sobre todo en la infancia. Si comparte algo, busca apoyo especializado y acompáñala en la denuncia. Evidencia: encuesta en línea con 225 mujeres de la comunidad autista francesa; casi nueve de cada diez describieron violencia sexual, a menudo antes de los 18 años. Límites: participación voluntaria por internet, sin grupo de comparación, así que las cifras pueden no representar a todas las mujeres autistas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic girl or woman, start building calm, regular moments where she can share difficult things without judgement, and believe her if she does. Responsibility lies with perpetrators and with protective adults, not with her: teaching her to 'protect herself' is not enough, especially in childhood. If she discloses something, seek specialist support and stand by her if she reports it. Evidence: an online survey of 225 women from the French autistic community; nearly nine in ten described sexual violence, often before age 18. Limits: voluntary online participation and no comparison group, so the figures may not reflect all autistic women.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk flicka eller kvinna, skapa redan i dag lugna, återkommande stunder där hon kan berätta svåra saker utan att dömas, och tro på henne om hon gör det. Ansvaret ligger hos förövarna och hos skyddande vuxna, inte hos henne: att lära henne ”skydda sig själv” räcker inte, särskilt i barndomen. Om hon berättar något, sök specialiserat stöd och stå vid hennes sida om hon anmäler. Evidens: en webbenkät med 225 kvinnor i den franska autistiska gemenskapen; nästan nio av tio beskrev sexuellt våld, ofta före 18 års ålder. Begränsningar: frivilligt deltagande via internet och ingen jämförelsegrupp, så siffrorna speglar kanske inte alla autistiska kvinnor.

title: Real-Life Social-Skills Training and Motor-Skills Training in Adults With Autism Spectrum Disorder: The Con-Tatto Project Walking Down the Francigena Route.
authors: Keller R, Ardizzone F, Finardi C, Colella R, Genuario C, Lopez M, Salerno L, Nobile E, Cicinelli G
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder with an early onset and a genetic and epigenetic component. ASD is characterized by deficits in socio-emotional reciprocity, impaired verbal and non-verbal communication skills, and specific difficulties in developing and maintaining adequate social relationships with peers. Indeed, restricted, repetitive patterns of behavior, interests, or activities are required by DSM-5 diagnostic criteria. Autistic people usually need an unchanging environment (or in any case predictable and stable) and may have hypo- or hyper-sensitivity to sensory inputs. The onset of clinical symptoms occurs during the early years of life. Social skills competence is a significant therapeutic aim to be pursued when addressing ASD core symptoms. Several considerable motor difficulties (87%) in people with autism spectrum disorder in adulthood have been found. The Con-tatto project developed a project addressing social, physical, and mental health difficulties in real-life walking down the Francigena route for 9 days with 12 autistic people, by (1) Implementing daily sessions of social skills training program whose abilities were addressed to be immediately generalized and used throughout the day. (2) Educational movement and walking activity programs were led by a fitness coach. (3) The creation of walking peers' social community with a strong and relevant impact on adults with ASD social life respecting every person's individuality. (4) Provision of social reinforcers to reduce the stigma of people with autism and the experienced perception of low self-esteem, especially when they are bullied.

sheet.es: Caminar en grupo durante varios días, con sesiones diarias para practicar habilidades sociales en situaciones reales y con apoyo para moverse, puede ser una idea para explorar con una persona autista adulta, si ella quiere. Conviene respetar su ritmo y su individualidad. La evidencia es la descripción de un proyecto: 9 días por la ruta Francigena con 12 personas autistas, con sesiones de habilidades sociales, actividad guiada por un entrenador y comunidad de compañeros. El resumen no da resultados medidos, así que no sabemos si ayuda ni a quién. Es un grupo pequeño y no sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: Walking together as a group over several days, with daily sessions to practise social skills in real situations and support with movement, may be an idea to explore with an autistic adult, if they want to. It helps to respect their pace and individuality. The evidence is the description of a project: 9 days on the Francigena route with 12 autistic people, including social skills sessions, activity led by a fitness coach and a community of walking peers. The abstract reports no measured results, so we do not know whether it helps or for whom. The group was small, so this is not a rule for everyone.
sheet.sv: Att gå tillsammans i grupp under flera dagar, med dagliga pass där man övar sociala färdigheter i verkliga situationer och får stöd med rörelse, kan vara en idé att utforska med en autistisk vuxen, om personen själv vill. Det hjälper att respektera personens tempo och individualitet. Underlaget är en beskrivning av ett projekt: 9 dagar längs Francigena-leden med 12 autistiska personer, med pass i sociala färdigheter, aktiviteter ledda av en fitnesscoach och en gemenskap av medvandrare. Sammanfattningen redovisar inga uppmätta resultat, så vi vet inte om det hjälper eller för vem. Gruppen var liten, så det är ingen regel för alla.

title: Vitamin D: Before, during and after Pregnancy: Effect on Neonates and Children.
authors: Mansur JL, Oliveri B, Giacoia E, Fusaro D, Costanzo PR
abstract: A worldwide high prevalence of vitamin D (VD) deficiency has become of growing concern because of potential adverse effects on human health, including pregnant women and their offsprings. Beyond its classical function as a regulator of calcium and phosphate metabolism, together with its fundamental role in bone health in every stage of life, its deficiency has been associated to multiple adverse health effects. The classic effects of VD deficiency in pregnancy and neonates have been late hypocalcemia and nutritional rickets. Nevertheless, recent studies have linked VD to fertility and 25(OH)D with several clinical conditions in pregnancy: preeclampsia, gestational diabetes, higher incidence of cesarean section and preterm birth, while in infants, the clinical conditions are low birth weight, lower bone mass and possible relationship with the development of such diseases as bronchiolitis, asthma, type 1 diabetes, multiple sclerosis and autism included as VD non-classical actions. The supplementation with Vitamin D and achievement of optimal levels reduce maternal-fetal and newborn complications. Supplementation in children with VD deficiency reduces the risk of respiratory infections and possibly autoimmune diseases and autism. This review emphasizes the roles of Vitamin D deficiency and the consequences of intervention from preconception to infancy.

title: Cohort profile: Scotland's record-linkage e-cohorts of people with intellectual disabilities, and autistic people (SCIDA).
authors: Cooper SA, Henderson A, Kinnear D, Mackay D, Fleming M, Smith GS, Hughes-McCormack LA, Rydzewska E, Dunn K, Pell JP, Melville C
abstract: Purpose To investigate health, mortality and healthcare inequalities experienced by people with intellectual disabilities, and autistic people, and their determinants; an important step towards identifying and implementing solutions to reduce inequalities. This paper describes the cohorts, record-linkages and variables that will be used. Participants Scotland's Census, 2011 was used to identify Scotland's citizens with intellectual disabilities, and autistic citizens, and representative general population samples with neither. Using Scotland's community health index, the Census data (demography, household, employment, long-term conditions) were linked with routinely collected health, death and healthcare data: Scotland's register of deaths, Scottish morbidity data 06 (SMR06: cancer incidence, mortality, treatments), Prescribing Information System (identifying asthma/chronic obstructive pulmonary disease; angina/congestive heart failure/hypertension; peptic ulcer/reflux; constipation; diabetes; thyroid disorder; depression; bipolar disorders; anxiety/sleep; psychosis; attention deficit hyperactivity disorder; epilepsy; glaucoma), SMR01 (general/acute hospital admissions and causes, ambulatory care sensitive admissions), SMR04 (mental health admissions and causes), Scottish Care Information-Diabetes Collaboration (diabetic care quality, diabetic outcomes), national bowel screening programme and cervical screening. Findings to date Of the whole population, 0.5% had intellectual disabilities, and 0.6% were autistic. Linkage was successful for >92%. The resultant e-cohorts include: (1) 22 538 people with intellectual disabilities (12 837 men and 9701 women), 4509 of whom are children Future plans Analyses will determine the extent of premature mortality, causes of death, and avoidable deaths, profile of health conditions and cancers, healthcare quality and screening and determinants of mortality and healthcare.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista o con discapacidad intelectual, pregunta a su equipo sanitario por revisiones y cribados que le correspondan, y lleva un registro de sus citas. Este artículo describe una base de datos de Escocia que enlazó datos del censo de 2011 con registros de salud, muertes y atención sanitaria, para estudiar desigualdades en salud. Según el resumen, el 0,6% de la población era autista y el enlace se logró en más del 92%. Es solo una descripción del método: aún no presenta resultados sobre desigualdades, y los datos de Escocia no sirven para predecir la situación de cada persona.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person or a person with intellectual disabilities, ask their health team which checks and screenings are due, and keep a record of appointments. This paper describes a Scottish database that linked 2011 census data with health, death and healthcare records, to study health inequalities. According to the abstract, 0.6% of the population was autistic, and linkage succeeded for >92%. It only describes the method: it does not yet report findings on inequalities, and Scottish data cannot predict any one person's situation.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person eller en person med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning, fråga vårdteamet vilka kontroller och screeningar som är aktuella, och för anteckningar om besök. Artikeln beskriver en skotsk databas som kopplade folkräkningen 2011 till register över hälsa, dödsfall och vård, för att studera ojämlikhet i hälsa. Enligt sammanfattningen var 0,6% av befolkningen autistiska, och kopplingen lyckades för >92%. Den beskriver bara metoden: inga resultat om ojämlikhet redovisas ännu, och skotska data kan inte förutsäga en enskild persons situation.

title: Parent-Mediated Interventions for Infants under 24 Months at Risk for Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.
authors: Law ML, Singh J, Mastroianni M, Santosh P
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Prodromal symptoms of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) have been detected within the first year of life. This review evaluated evidence from randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of parent-mediated interventions for infants under 24 months who are at risk for ASD. Electronic databases, including grey literature, were searched up till November 2019. Seven RCTs were identified. There was substantial heterogeneity in recruitment, outcome measures and effect size calculations. Interventions did not reduce the risk of later ASD diagnosis and post-intervention effects on infant outcomes were inconsistent, with five studies reporting significant improvements across both treatment and control groups. Moderate level of evidence of intervention effects on parental interaction skills and the small number of RCTs, and significant limitations restrict generalizability across studies.

sheet.es: Si su bebé tiene más probabilidades de ser autista, los programas en los que las familias aprenden a jugar e interactuar pueden fortalecer su forma de comunicarse con él o ella, pero no cambian la probabilidad de un diagnóstico posterior. Es una revisión sistemática de siete ensayos aleatorizados con bebés menores de 24 meses con riesgo de autismo. Los efectos en los bebés fueron irregulares: cinco estudios hallaron mejoras tanto en el grupo de intervención como en el de control. Hay pocos ensayos, métodos muy distintos y limitaciones importantes, así que no sirve como regla para cada familia. Hable con su equipo de salud o de atención temprana.
sheet.en: If your baby is more likely to be autistic, programmes where families learn ways to play and interact may strengthen how you connect with your child, but they did not change the chance of a later diagnosis. This is a systematic review of seven randomized trials with infants under 24 months at risk for autism. Effects on babies were inconsistent: five studies found improvements in both the intervention and the control groups. There were few trials, very different methods and significant limitations, so it is not a rule for every family. Talk with your health or early support team.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn har större sannolikhet att vara autistiskt kan program där familjer lär sig sätt att leka och samspela stärka hur ni kommunicerar med barnet, men de ändrade inte sannolikheten för en senare diagnos.
