sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person har långvarig förstoppning eller diarré är det värt att notera när det sker och ta upp det med vårdpersonal, eftersom magbesvär påverkar livskvaliteten. Den här systematiska översikten jämförde studier av tarmbakterier i avföring hos autistiska personer och i flera musmodeller av autism. Vissa bakteriesläkten förändrades i båda, medan andra ändrades åt olika håll. Begränsningar: den ger inga råd för hemmet, visar inte orsaker, och möss är inte detsamma som människor. Resultaten är ingen regel för varje autistisk person.

title: Camouflaging Intent, First Impressions, and Age of ASC Diagnosis in Autistic Men and Women.
authors: Belcher HL, Morein-Zamir S, Mandy W, Ford RM
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Camouflaging of autistic traits may make autism harder to diagnose. The current study evaluated the relations between camouflaging intent, first impressions, and age of autism diagnosis. Participants comprised autistic and non-autistic adults (n = 80, 50% female) who completed the Camouflaging of Autistic Traits Questionnaire. They were later video-recorded having a conversation with a person unaware of their diagnostic status. Ten-second clips from half these videos were later shown to 127 non-autistic peers, who rated their first impressions of each participant. Results showed that autistic participants were rated more poorly on first impressions, males were rated less favourably than females, and male raters were particularly harsh in their evaluations of autistic males. Camouflaging intent did not predict first impressions but better first impressions were linked with a later age of diagnosis.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista parece "encajar" en una conversación breve, eso no dice cuánto esfuerzo le cuesta ni qué apoyos necesita. Si sospechas autismo, no te fíes de la primera impresión y cuenta con ejemplos concretos del día a día. El estudio incluyó a 80 adultos autistas y no autistas, que respondieron un cuestionario sobre camuflaje y fueron grabados conversando; 127 pares no autistas valoraron clips de diez segundos. Las personas autistas recibieron peores primeras impresiones, y las mejores impresiones se vincularon con un diagnóstico más tardío. Es un estudio pequeño, con adultos, y no demuestra causas ni vale para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person seems to "fit in" during a brief conversation, that does not show how much effort it takes or what support they need. If you suspect autism, don't rely on first impressions; share concrete examples from everyday life. The study included 80 autistic and non-autistic adults, who completed a camouflaging questionnaire and were recorded in conversation; 127 non-autistic peers rated ten-second clips. Autistic participants received poorer first impressions, and better first impressions were linked with a later age of diagnosis. It is a small study with adults, cannot show cause and effect, and does not apply to every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person verkar "smälta in" i ett kort samtal säger det inte hur mycket ansträngning det kräver eller vilket stöd personen behöver. Om du misstänker autism: lita inte på första intryck, utan berätta konkreta exempel från vardagen. Studien omfattade 80 autistiska och icke-autistiska vuxna som fyllde i ett frågeformulär om maskering och spelades in i samtal; 127 icke-autistiska jämnåriga bedömde tio sekunder långa klipp. Autistiska deltagare fick sämre första intryck, och bättre första intryck hängde ihop med senare diagnos. Studien är liten, gäller vuxna, visar inte orsak och verkan och passar inte alla.

title: Autism Through the Ages: A Mixed Methods Approach to Understanding How Age and Age of Diagnosis Affect Quality of Life.
authors: Atherton G, Edisbury E, Piovesan A, Cross L
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: A significant proportion of autistic adults today were not diagnosed until later in life, a group referred to as the 'lost generation,' which may affect mental health. In Study 1 we explored quality of life and autistic trait levels in 420 autistic and TD adults, and in Study 2 we explored the experiences of 8 autistic adults diagnosed as adults. We found that autistic adults had lower quality of life outcomes and higher autistic trait levels which related to age of diagnosis, and qualitative findings indicated that while adults were empowered by their new diagnosis, they still require specialized supports. Our findings are discussed, emphasizing future directions and implications for the current care system in place for autistic adults.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista recibió su diagnóstico ya de adulta, puede ayudar reconocer que ese diagnóstico a menudo da fuerza y sentido, y que aun así sigue necesitando apoyos especializados. Pregunte qué apoyos le serían útiles y escuche sin presuponer. La evidencia: un estudio con 420 adultos autistas y no autistas (TD) que midió calidad de vida y rasgos autistas, más entrevistas a 8 adultos autistas diagnosticados de adultos. Los adultos autistas tuvieron peores resultados de calidad de vida, relacionados con la edad del diagnóstico. Límites: la muestra cualitativa es muy pequeña y el estudio no demuestra causas ni describe a cada persona.
sheet.en: If an autistic person was diagnosed as an adult, it may help to recognise that the diagnosis often brings empowerment and meaning, yet specialised supports are still needed. Ask what support would be useful to them and listen without assuming. The evidence: a study of 420 autistic and TD adults measuring quality of life and autistic traits, plus interviews with 8 autistic adults diagnosed as adults. Autistic adults had lower quality of life outcomes, related to age of diagnosis. Limits: the interview group is very small, and the study cannot prove causes or describe every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person fick sin diagnos som vuxen kan det hjälpa att se att diagnosen ofta ger egenmakt och mening, men att specialiserat stöd fortfarande behövs. Fråga vilket stöd som skulle vara till nytta och lyssna utan att anta något. Evidensen: en studie med 420 autistiska och TD-vuxna som mätte livskvalitet och autistiska drag, samt intervjuer med 8 autistiska vuxna som fått diagnos som vuxna. Autistiska vuxna hade lägre livskvalitet, kopplat till ålder vid diagnos. Begränsningar: intervjugruppen är mycket liten, och studien kan inte visa orsaker eller beskriva varje person.

title: Annual Research Review: Shifting from 'normal science' to neurodiversity in autism science.
authors: Pellicano E, den Houting J
journal: Journal of child psychology and psychiatry, and allied disciplines
abstract: Since its initial description, the concept of autism has been firmly rooted within the conventional medical paradigm of child psychiatry. Increasingly, there have been calls from the autistic community and, more recently, nonautistic researchers, to rethink the way in which autism science is framed and conducted. Neurodiversity, where autism is seen as one form of variation within a diversity of minds, has been proposed as a potential alternative paradigm. In this review, we concentrate on three major challenges to the conventional medical paradigm - an overfocus on deficits, an emphasis on the individual as opposed to their broader context and a narrowness of perspective - each of which necessarily constrains what we can know about autism and how we are able to know it. We then outline the ways in which fundamental elements of the neurodiversity paradigm can potentially help researchers respond to the medical model's limitations. We conclude by considering the implications of a shift towards the neurodiversity paradigm for autism science.

sheet.es: Una idea práctica para mañana: además de fijarte en lo que a tu hijo o familiar le cuesta, anota también sus fortalezas, intereses y qué cambios en el entorno (ruido, horarios, expectativas) le ayudan. Pregúntale, de la forma que mejor comunique, qué necesita. Esta revisión de investigación, escrita con participación de personas autistas, analiza cómo la ciencia del autismo se ha centrado demasiado en déficits, en el individuo y en una sola perspectiva, y propone el paradigma de la neurodiversidad. Es un artículo de reflexión, no un estudio con participantes ni datos nuevos, así que no ofrece técnicas probadas que funcionen para todas las personas.
sheet.en: A practical idea for tomorrow: alongside noticing what is hard for your child or family member, also write down their strengths, interests and which changes in their surroundings (noise, routines, expectations) help them. Ask them, in whatever way they communicate best, what they need. This research review, written with involvement of autistic people, examines how autism science has focused too much on deficits, on the individual rather than their context, and on a narrow perspective, and it proposes the neurodiversity paradigm instead. It is a reflective paper, not a study with participants or new data, so it does not offer tested techniques that work for every person.
sheet.sv: En praktisk idé för i morgon: lägg märke till vad som är svårt för ditt barn eller din närstående, men skriv också ner styrkor, intressen och vilka förändringar i omgivningen (ljud, rutiner, förväntningar) som hjälper. Fråga personen, på det sätt hen kommunicerar bäst, vad hen behöver. Den här forskningsöversikten, skriven med medverkan av autistiska personer, granskar hur autismforskningen fokuserat för mycket på brister, på individen snarare än sammanhanget och på ett snävt perspektiv, och föreslår neurodiversitetsparadigmet. Det är en reflekterande artikel, inte en studie med deltagare eller nya data, så den ger inga beprövade metoder som passar alla.

title: Parallel age-related cognitive effects in autism: A cross-sectional replication study.
authors: Torenvliet C, Groenman AP, Radhoe TA, Agelink van Rentergem JA, Van der Putten WJ, Geurts HM
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Findings on age-related cognitive effects in autism in adulthood are inconsistent across studies. As these studies substantially differ in their methodology, replication studies are needed. In this replication study frequentist (i.e., null-hypothesis significance testing), and Bayesian statistics were used to investigate the hypothesis that in autistic adults compared to non-autistic adults mostly parallel, but also protective age-related cognitive effects can be observed. Participants were 88 autistic adults, and 88 non-autistic matched comparisons (age range: 30-89 years, mean age: 55 years). Cognitive measures were administered on the following six domains: verbal memory, visual memory, working memory, Theory of Mind (ToM), verbal fluency, and processing speed, and self-reported cognitive failures. Non-autistic adults outperformed autistic adults on ToM, verbal fluency, and verbal memory, but only the first two were confirmed with Bayesian replication analyses. Also, more cognitive failures were reported by autistic adults. No interactions between group and age were observed, suggesting a parallel age-related effect on all cognitive domains. In sum, previously observed difficulties in ToM and verbal fluency were replicated which seem to persist at older age. Previously reported parallel age-related cognitive patterns were replicated, yet no evidence for protective age-related patterns was found. LAY SUMMARY: We investigated whether our previous findings on cognitive aging in autism could be confirmed in a new study measuring the cognitive effects of age in autistic and non-autistic adults. As expected, tasks that younger autistic adults had difficulties with (theory of mind, fluency) were also difficult for older autistic adults, and the effect of age itself was similar in autistic and non-autistic adults. Unexpectedly, we observed no protective effects (less cognitive aging) in autism.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista adulta o mayor, este estudio sugiere que el envejecimiento cognitivo suele seguir un ritmo parecido al de personas no autistas: no hay señales de un deterioro más rápido. Algunas diferencias, como en tareas de comprensión de lo que piensan otros o de fluidez verbal, pueden mantenerse con la edad, así que conviene seguir ofreciendo tiempo extra, instrucciones claras y apoyos escritos. Tomarse en serio los despistes cotidianos que la persona describe también ayuda. Fue un estudio transversal de replicación con 88 adultos autistas y 88 no autistas de 30 a 89 años. Limitación: midió a cada persona una sola vez, por lo que no sigue cambios individuales a lo largo del tiempo.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult who is getting older, this study suggests cognitive ageing tends to follow a similar pace to non-autistic people, with no sign of faster decline. Some differences, such as in tasks about understanding others' thoughts or verbal fluency, may persist with age, so continuing to offer extra time, clear instructions and written supports makes sense. Taking the everyday slips the person describes seriously also helps. This was a cross-sectional replication study with 88 autistic and 88 non-autistic adults aged 30 to 89. Limitation: each person was measured only once, so it cannot track how individuals change over time.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen som blir äldre tyder studien på att det kognitiva åldrandet ofta sker i liknande takt som hos icke-autistiska personer, utan tecken på snabbare försämring. Vissa skillnader, till exempel i uppgifter om att förstå andras tankar eller verbalt flöde, kan finnas kvar med åldern, så det är klokt att fortsätta ge extra tid, tydliga instruktioner och skriftligt stöd. Att ta personens egna beskrivningar av vardagliga missar på allvar hjälper också. Det var en tvärsnittsstudie som upprepade tidigare forskning, med 88 autistiska och 88 icke-autistiska vuxna i åldern 30–89 år. Begränsning: varje person mättes bara en gång, så förändringar hos individen över tid följdes inte.

title: REACH-ASD: a UK randomised controlled trial of a new post-diagnostic psycho-education and acceptance and commitment therapy programme against treatment-as-usual for improving the mental health and adjustment of caregivers of children recently diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Leadbitter K, Smallman R, James K, Shields G, Ellis C, Langhorne S, Harrison L, Hackett L, Dunkerley A, Kroll L, Davies L, Emsley R, Bee P, Green J, REACH-ASD Team
abstract: Background Autism is a neurodevelopmental disability affecting over 1% of UK children. The period following a child's autism diagnosis can present real challenges in adaptation for families. Twenty to 50% of caregivers show clinically significant levels of mental health need within the post-diagnostic period and on an ongoing basis. Best practice guidelines recommend timely post-diagnostic family support. Current provision is patchy, largely unevidenced, and a source of dissatisfaction for both families and professionals. There is a pressing need for an evidenced programme of post-diagnostic support focusing on caregiver mental health and adjustment, alongside autism psycho-education. This trial tests the clinical and cost-effectiveness of a new brief manualised psychosocial intervention designed to address this gap. Methods This is a multi-centre two-parallel-group single (researcher)-blinded randomised controlled trial of the Empower-Autism programme plus treatment-as-usual versus usual local post-diagnostic offer plus treatment-as-usual. Caregivers of children aged 2-15 years with a recent autism diagnosis will be recruited from North West England NHS or local authority centres. Randomisation is individually by child, with one "index" caregiver per child, stratified by centre, using 2:1 randomisation ratio to assist recruitment and timely intervention. Empower-Autism is a group-based, manualised, post-diagnostic programme that combines autism psycho-education and psychotherapeutic components based on Acceptance and Commitment Therapy to support caregiver mental health, stress management and adjustment to their child's diagnosis. The comparator is any usual local group-based post-diagnostic psycho-education offer. Receipt of services will be specified through health economic data. Primary outcome caregiver mental health (General Health Questionnaire-30) at 52-week follow-up. Secondary outcomes key caregiver measures (wellbeing, self-efficacy, adjustment, autism knowledge) at 12-, 26- and 52-week follow-up and family and child outcomes (wellbeing and functioning) at 52-week endpoint. Sample N=380 (approximately 253 intervention/127 treatment-as-usual). Primary analysis will follow intention-to-treat principles using linear mixed models with random intercepts for group membership and repeated measures. Cost-effectiveness acceptability analyses will be over 52 weeks, with decision modelling to extrapolate to longer time periods. Discussion If effective, this new approach will fill a key gap in the provision of evidence-based care pathways for autistic children and their families. Trial registration ISRCTN 45412843 . Prospectively registered on 11 September 2019.

sheet.es: Tras el diagnóstico de autismo de un hijo, cuidar también de tu propia salud mental y de cómo te adaptas es razonable y legítimo; puedes preguntar al equipo que os atiende qué apoyo para familias ofrecen. Este es el protocolo de un ensayo aleatorizado en el noroeste de Inglaterra, con cuidadores de niños de 2-15 años con diagnóstico reciente. Comparará un programa grupal (Empower-Autism, con psicoeducación y terapia de aceptación y compromiso) con la oferta local habitual. Aún no hay resultados, así que no sabemos si funciona ni para quién.
sheet.en: After your child's autism diagnosis, looking after your own mental health and how you are adjusting is reasonable and valid; you can ask your child's team what family support they offer. This is the protocol for a randomised trial in North West England, with caregivers of children aged 2-15 years who were recently diagnosed. It will compare a group programme (Empower-Autism, with psycho-education and acceptance and commitment therapy) with the usual local offer. There are no results yet, so we do not know whether it works or for whom.
sheet.sv: Efter ditt barns autismdiagnos är det rimligt och helt legitimt att ta hand om din egen psykiska hälsa och hur du anpassar dig; du kan fråga barnets team vilket stöd till familjer de erbjuder. Detta är protokollet för en randomiserad studie i nordvästra England med vårdnadshavare till barn i åldern 2-15 år som nyligen fått diagnos. Den ska jämföra ett gruppprogram (Empower-Autism, med psykoedukation och acceptance and commitment therapy) med det vanliga lokala stödet. Inga resultat finns ännu, så vi vet inte om det fungerar eller för vem.

title: Social Story Based Toothbrushing Education Versus Video-Modeling Based Toothbrushing Training on Oral Hygiene Status Among Male Students Aged 7-15 Years Old with Autism Spectrum Disorders in Tehran, Iran: A Quasi-Randomized Controlled Trial.
authors: Piraneh H, Gholami M, Sargeran K, Shamshiri AR
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders

title: Global prevalence of autism: A systematic review update.
authors: Zeidan J, Fombonne E, Scorah J, Ibrahim A, Durkin MS, Saxena S, Yusuf A, Shih A, Elsabbagh M
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Prevalence estimates of autism are essential for informing public policy, raising awareness, and developing research priorities. Using a systematic review, we synthesized estimates of the prevalence of autism worldwide. We examined factors accounting for variability in estimates and critically reviewed evidence relevant for hypotheses about biological or social determinants (viz., biological sex, sociodemographic status, ethnicity/race, and nativity) potentially modifying prevalence estimates of autism. We performed the search in November 2021 within Medline for studies estimating autism prevalence, published since our last systematic review in 2012. Data were extracted by two independent researchers. Since 2012, 99 estimates from 71 studies were published indicating a global autism prevalence that ranges within and across regions, with a median prevalence of 100/10,000 (range: 1.09/10,000 to 436.0/10,000). The median male-to-female ratio was 4.2. The median percentage of autism cases with co-occurring intellectual disability was 33.0%. Estimates varied, likely reflecting complex and dynamic interactions between patterns of community awareness, service capacity, help seeking, and sociodemographic factors. A limitation of this review is that synthesizing methodological features precludes a quality appraisal of studies. Our findings reveal an increase in measured autism prevalence globally, reflecting the combined effects of multiple factors including the increase in community awareness and public health response globally, progress in case identification and definition, and an increase in community capacity. Hypotheses linking factors that increase the likelihood of developing autism with variations in prevalence will require research with large, representative samples and comparable autism diagnostic criteria and case-finding methods in diverse world regions over time. LAY SUMMARY: We reviewed studies of the prevalence of autism worldwide, considering the impact of geographic, ethnic, and socioeconomic factors on prevalence estimates. Approximately 1/100 children are diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder around the world. Prevalence estimates increased over time and varied greatly within and across sociodemographic groups. These findings reflect changes in the definition of autism and differences in the methodology and contexts of prevalence studies.

title: Autism-friendly eyecare: Developing recommendations for service providers based on the experiences of autistic adults.
authors: Parmar KR, Porter CS, Dickinson CM, Baimbridge P, Pelham J, Gowen E
journal: Ophthalmic & physiological optics : the journal of the British College of Ophthalmic Opticians (Optometrists)
abstract: Purpose People with autism face significant barriers when accessing healthcare services. Eye examinations present unique challenges. Accessibility of this healthcare sector for people with autism has not been investigated previously. The aim of this research was to investigate eye examination accessibility for autistic adults and produce recommendations for autism-friendly eyecare. Methods Two qualitative studies were conducted. In Study 1, 18 autistic adults took part in focus groups to elicit their eye examination experiences. Transcripts of the recorded discussions were thematically analysed. Study 1 findings were used to design autism-friendly eye examinations for autistic adults. These were conducted in Study 2. Twenty-four autistic adults participated in these examinations, during which they were interviewed about their experience and how it might be improved by reasonable modifications. Audio recordings of the interviews were content analysed. Results Knowledge of what to expect, in advance of the eye examination, could greatly reduce anxiety. Participants liked the logical structure of the examination, and the interesting instrumentation used. However, the examination and practice environment did include sensory challenges, due to lights, sound and touch. Changes in practice layout, and interacting with multiple staff members, was anxiety provoking. Participants expressed a need for thorough explanations from the optometrist that outlined the significance of each test, and what the patient was expected to do. Conclusion A number of accessiblity barriers were identified. These suggested that UK eye examinations are not very accessible for autistic adults. Barriers began at the point of booking the appointment and continued through to the dispensing of spectacles. These caused anxiety and stress for this population, but could be reduced with easy-to-implement adaptations. Based on the findings, recommendations are presented here for the whole eyecare team which suggest how more autism-friendly eye examinations can be provided.

sheet.es: Antes de una revisión de la vista, pregunta al centro qué va a ocurrir y explícaselo con antelación a la persona autista: qué pruebas habrá, en qué orden y qué se espera de ella. Pide que el óptico explique cada prueba mientras la hace. Avisa de las luces, los sonidos y el contacto físico. Evidencia: estudio cualitativo en el Reino Unido con 18 adultos autistas en grupos de discusión y 24 en exámenes adaptados, con entrevistas. Límites: son experiencias de adultos, no sirven igual para niños, y cada persona vive la consulta de forma distinta.
sheet.en: Before an eye test, ask the practice what will happen and explain it to the autistic person in advance: which tests there will be, in what order, and what is expected of them. Ask the optometrist to explain each test as it is done. Mention the lights, sounds and touch involved. Evidence: a qualitative UK study with 18 autistic adults in focus groups and 24 in adapted eye examinations, followed by interviews. Limits: it reflects adult experiences, may not apply equally to children, and each person experiences the appointment differently.
sheet.sv: Före en synundersökning: fråga mottagningen vad som kommer att hända och förklara det i förväg för den autistiska personen, vilka tester som görs, i vilken ordning och vad som förväntas. Be optikern förklara varje test medan det görs. Förvarna om ljus, ljud och beröring. Evidens: en kvalitativ brittisk studie med 18 autistiska vuxna i fokusgrupper och 24 i anpassade synundersökningar, med intervjuer. Begränsningar: den visar vuxnas erfarenheter, passar kanske inte lika bra för barn, och varje person upplever besöket olika.

title: Beyond group differences: Exploring the preliminary signals of target engagement of an executive function training for autistic children.
authors: Edmunds SR, MacNaughton GA, Rueda MR, Combita LM, Faja S
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Understanding both for whom and how interventions work is a crucial next step in providing personalized care to children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Autistic children present with heterogeneity both within core ASD criteria and with respect to co-occurring mental health challenges, which may affect their ability to benefit from intervention. In a secondary data analysis of a randomized control trial evaluating an executive function (EF) training with 70 7- to 11-year-old autistic children, we explored: (1) whether co-occurring attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) features or anxiety features at baseline moderated the extent to which children benefited from the EF training. In other words, we asked, "For whom is training effective?" We also explored: (2) the extent to which changes in a brain-based measure of target engagement predicted the clinical outcomes of the EF training. This is a step towards asking, "How is training effective?" We found that EF training improved behavioral inhibition only for children with clinically significant co-occurring ADHD features. Anxiety features, while prevalent, did not moderate EF training efficacy. Finally, for the EF training group only, there was a significant correlation between pre-to-post change in an EEG-based measure of target engagement, N2 incongruent amplitude during a flanker task, and change in repetitive behaviors, a behavioral outcome that was reported in the parent RCT to have improved with training compared to waitlist control. This study provides preliminary evidence that EF training may differentially affect subgroups of autistic children and that changes at the neural level may precede changes in behavior. LAY SUMMARY: Understanding both for whom and how interventions work will help us provide personalized care to children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Autistic children present with many different strengths and challenges. Co-occurring mental health challenges may affect how much autistic children benefit from intervention. We analyzed secondary data from a rigorously designed pilot intervention study, a randomized control trial (RCT), that enrolled 70 7- to 11-year-old autistic children to assess whether a set of computer-based executive function (EF) training games improved their performance. Executive functions include being able to shift between tasks, inhibit a response, and keep information in working memory. In the current study, we explored: (1) whether children's co-occurring attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) features or anxiety features, measured before the EF training began, affected how much they benefited from the EF training. In other words, we asked, "For whom is training effective?" We also explored: (2) whether children's brain-based changes in EF predicted their performance in everyday life (e.g., parent report on a survey). This is a step toward asking, "How is training effective?" We found that EF training improved children's inhibition ability, but only for children with clinically significant ADHD features. While many children in our sample also had anxiety features, we found that anxiety levels did not affect how well the EF training worked. Finally, for children who received the EF training, changes in a brain-based measure of conflict monitoring (i.e., being able to noticing differences in stimuli) predicted changes in children's repetitive behaviors. This study provides early evidence that EF training may be more effective for some autistic children than others, especially those with ADHD features.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija autista tiene rasgos de TDAH, un entrenamiento informático de funciones ejecutivas podría ayudarle a frenar respuestas impulsivas; pero no hay que esperar lo mismo en todos los niños. Este análisis secundario de un ensayo aleatorizado incluyó a 70 niños autistas de 7 a 11 años. La mejora en inhibición apareció solo en quienes tenían rasgos de TDAH clínicamente significativos; la ansiedad no cambió el efecto. Es un estudio preliminar, con una muestra pequeña, exploratorio, y los cambios cerebrales medidos con EEG no prueban causa alguna. Conviene comentar cualquier decisión con el equipo profesional.
sheet.en: If your autistic child has ADHD features, a computer-based executive function training may help with holding back impulsive responses, but don't expect the same result for every child. This secondary analysis of a randomized trial included 70 autistic children aged 7 to 11. The improvement in inhibition appeared only in children with clinically significant ADHD features; anxiety did not change the effect. The study is preliminary and exploratory, with a small sample, and the brain changes measured with EEG do not prove cause. Talk over any decisions with your child's professional team.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn har ADHD-drag kan ett datorbaserat träningsprogram för exekutiva funktioner möjligen hjälpa till att hejda impulsiva svar, men räkna inte med samma resultat för alla barn. Denna sekundäranalys av en randomiserad studie omfattade 70 autistiska barn i åldern 7 till 11 år. Förbättringen i hämning sågs bara hos barn med kliniskt betydande ADHD-drag; ångest påverkade inte effekten. Studien är preliminär och utforskande, med litet urval, och hjärnförändringarna som mättes med EEG bevisar inget orsakssamband. Diskutera beslut med barnets professionella team.

title: AGREEing on Clinical Practice Guidelines for Autism Spectrum Disorders in Children: A Systematic Review and Quality Assessment.
authors: Amer YS, Alenezi S, Bashiri FA, Alawami AH, Alhazmi AS, Aladamawi SA, Alnemary F, Alqahtani Y, Buraik MW, AlSuwailem SS, Akhalifah SM, Augusta de Souza Pinhel M, Penner M, Elmalky AM
abstract: Background Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a multifaceted neurodevelopmental disorder requiring multimodal intervention and an army of multidisciplinary teams for a proper rehabilitation plan. Accordingly, multiple practice guidelines have been published for different disciplines. However, systematic evidence to detect and intervene must be updated regularly. Our main objective is to compare and summarize the recommendations made in the clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) for ASD in children released from November 2015 to March 2022. Methods CPGs were subjected to a systematic review. We developed the inclusion and exclusion criteria and health-related questions, then searched and screened for CPGs utilizing bibliographic and CPG databases. Each of the CPGs used in the study were critically evaluated using the Appraisal of Guidelines for REsearch and Evaluation II (AGREE II) instrument. In a realistic comparison table, we summarized the recommendations. Results Four eligible CPGs were appraised: Australian Autism CRC (ACRC); Ministry of Health New Zealand (NZ); National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE); and Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network, Healthcare Improvement Scotland (SIGN-HIS). The overall assessments of all four CPGs scored greater than 80%; these findings were consistent with the high scores in the six domains of AGREE II, including: (1) scope and purpose, (2) stakeholder involvement, (3) rigor of development, (4) clarity of presentation, (5) applicability, and (6) editorial independence domains. Domain (3) scored 84%, 93%, 86%, and 85%; domain (5) 92%, 89%, 54%, and 85%; and domain (6) 92%, 96%, 88%, and 92% for ACRC, NICE, NZ, and SIGN-HIS, respectively. Overall, there were no serious conflicts between the clinical recommendations of the four CPGs, but some were more comprehensive and elaborative than others. Conclusions All four assessed evidence-based CPGs demonstrated high methodological quality and relevance for use in practice.

sheet.es: Si buscas orientación fiable sobre apoyos para niñas y niños autistas, puedes consultar con confianza las guías clínicas de Australia, Nueva Zelanda, NICE (Reino Unido) y Escocia, y llevar sus ideas a la consulta. Es una revisión sistemática que evaluó cuatro guías publicadas entre noviembre de 2015 y marzo de 2022; todas puntuaron más de 80% en calidad global y no tenían conflictos graves entre sus recomendaciones. Sus límites: analiza guías, no personas, no mide si los apoyos funcionan y algunas guías son más detalladas que otras. Cada niño es distinto, y las decisiones médicas corresponden a su profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If you want reliable guidance on supports for autistic children, you can confidently look at the clinical guidelines from Australia, New Zealand, NICE (UK) and Scotland, and bring their ideas to appointments. This was a systematic review of four guidelines published between November 2015 and March 2022; all scored greater than 80% overall for quality, with no serious conflicts between their recommendations. Its limits: it assessed guidelines, not people, it does not show whether any support works for your child, and some guidelines are more detailed than others. Every child is different, and medical decisions belong to their clinician.
sheet.sv: Om du vill ha tillförlitlig vägledning om stöd till autistiska barn kan du med förtroende titta på de kliniska riktlinjerna från Australien, Nya Zeeland, NICE (Storbritannien) och Skottland och ta med dig idéer till besök. Det var en systematisk översikt av fyra riktlinjer som publicerades mellan november 2015 och mars 2022; alla fick över 80% i samlad kvalitet och rekommendationerna stred inte allvarligt mot varandra. Begränsningar: studien bedömde riktlinjer, inte människor, visar inte om ett visst stöd fungerar för ditt barn, och vissa riktlinjer är mer detaljerade än andra. Varje barn är olika, och medicinska beslut hör till barnets läkare.

title: Factors influencing oral health behaviours, access and delivery of dental care for autistic children and adolescents: A mixed-methods systematic review.
authors: Erwin J, Paisi M, Neill S, Burns L, Vassallo I, Nelder A, Facenfield J, Devalia U, Vassallo T, Witton R
journal: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy
abstract: Background Autistic children and young people (CYP) experience oral health (OH) inequalities. They are at high risk of dental disease and show significant levels of unmet need in relation to OH and access to dental care. Aim This study aimed to gather evidence on the factors that influence OH behaviours, access to and delivery of dental care for autistic CYP. Design This was a mixed-methods narrative systematic review. Data sources Embase, Web of Science, Dentistry & Oral Sciences Source, MEDLINE, Psychinfo, Scopus, CINAHL, SocINDEX and grey literature were the data sources for this study. Review methods A systematic search was conducted for qualitative, quantitative and mixed-methods research studies from countries with a High Development Index that related to OH behaviours, access to and delivery of dental care for autistic CYP. Results were analysed using narrative synthesis. Results From 59 eligible studies, 9 themes were generated: (1) affordability and accessibility; (2) autism-related factors and cognitive or motor skill differences; (3) the dental environment; (4) managing CYP's behaviour; (5) responding and adapting to the needs of the autistic CYP and their parent/carer; (6) attitude of dental health professionals (DHPs) towards autistic CYP and their parents/carers; (7) knowledge of how to care for and support CYP's OH; (8) empowerment of parents/carers and collaboration with DHPs; and (9) communication and building rapport. Conclusion The adoption of healthy OH behaviours and access to dental care by autistic CYP is impacted by a range of factors including those intrinsically related to a diagnosis of autism, for example, communication and those often associated with autism, for example, sensory sensitivities. Access to better OH and dental care can be facilitated by responding to the individual needs of autistic CYP through accommodation, education and adaptation. This necessitates greater awareness and knowledge of autism amongst DHPs and the provision of appropriate services. More methodologically robust intervention studies are needed to identify effective ways to support autistic CYP in achieving good OH and access to dental care. Patient and public contribution The review protocol was developed with members of the project patient and public involvement group who provided the autistic voice, contributing to the interpretation of the review findings and writing of the manuscript.

sheet.es: Antes de la cita dental, cuéntele al equipo qué necesita su hijo o hija: cómo se comunica, qué sensaciones le molestan y qué le tranquiliza. Pida adaptaciones, como más tiempo, una visita previa para conocer el lugar o explicaciones claras. La evidencia es una revisión sistemática de 59 estudios sobre salud bucodental y atención dental de niñas, niños y jóvenes autistas, en países con alto desarrollo. Sus límites: faltan estudios de intervención sólidos que muestren qué apoyos funcionan mejor, y cada persona es distinta, así que nada de esto es una regla para todas.
sheet.en: Before the dental visit, tell the team what your child needs: how they communicate, which sensations bother them and what helps them feel calm. Ask for adaptations, such as more time, a earlier visit to get to know the place, or clear explanations. The evidence is a systematic review of 59 studies on oral health and dental care for autistic children and young people, in countries with high development. Its limits: there are too few robust intervention studies showing which supports work best, and every person is different, so none of this is a rule for everyone.
sheet.sv: Berätta för tandvårdsteamet före besöket vad ditt barn behöver: hur hen kommunicerar, vilka känselintryck som stör och vad som skapar lugn. Be om anpassningar, till exempel mer tid, ett förbesök för att lära känna stället eller tydliga förklaringar. Underlaget är en systematisk översikt av 59 studier om munhälsa och tandvård för autistiska barn och unga, i länder med hög utvecklingsnivå. Begränsningar: det saknas starka interventionsstudier som visar vilket stöd som fungerar bäst, och alla är olika, så inget av detta är en regel för alla.

title: Zebrafish Modeling of Autism Spectrum Disorders, Current Status and Future Prospective.
authors: Tayanloo-Beik A, Hamidpour SK, Abedi M, Shojaei H, Tavirani MR, Namazi N, Larijani B, Arjmand B
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) refers to a complicated range of childhood neurodevelopmental disorders which can occur via genetic or non-genetic factors. Clinically, ASD is associated with problems in relationships, social interactions, and behaviors that pose many challenges for children with ASD and their families. Due to the complexity, heterogeneity, and association of symptoms with some neuropsychiatric disorders such as ADHD, anxiety, and sleep disorders, clinical trials have not yielded reliable results and there still remain challenges in drug discovery and development pipeline for ASD patients. One of the main steps in promoting lead compounds to the suitable drug for commercialization is preclinical animal testing, in which the efficacy and toxicity of candidate drugs are examined in vivo . In recent years, zebrafish have been able to attract the attention of many researchers in the field of neurological disorders such as ASD due to their outstanding features. The presence of orthologous genes for ASD modeling, the anatomical similarities of parts of the brain, and similar neurotransmitter systems between zebrafish and humans are some of the main reasons why scientists draw attention to zebrafish as a prominent animal model in preclinical studies to discover highly effective treatment approaches for the ASD through genetic and non-genetic modeling methods.

sheet.es: Este estudio no ofrece nada que hacer mañana en casa: trata de investigación de laboratorio, no de apoyos cotidianos. Si busca pautas prácticas, consulte a profesionales que conozcan a la persona autista. Es una revisión que describe el uso del pez cebra como modelo animal en la investigación del autismo, porque comparte con los humanos genes, partes del cerebro y sistemas de neurotransmisores. Sus límites: no incluyó a personas autistas, no probó ningún apoyo y no demuestra que ningún tratamiento funcione. Cualquier decisión médica corresponde a un clínico.
sheet.en: This study offers nothing to do at home tomorrow: it is laboratory research, not about everyday support. For practical guidance, talk to professionals who know the autistic person. It is a review describing how zebrafish are used as an animal model in autism research, because they share genes, parts of the brain and neurotransmitter systems with humans. Its limits: it involved no autistic people, tested no support, and does not show that any treatment works. Any medical decision belongs to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Den här studien ger inget att göra hemma i morgon: den handlar om laboratorieforskning, inte om stöd i vardagen. För praktisk vägledning, prata med yrkespersoner som känner den autistiska personen. Det är en översikt som beskriver hur zebrafisk används som djurmodell i autismforskning, eftersom den delar gener, delar av hjärnan och signalsubstanssystem med människor. Begränsningar: inga autistiska personer deltog, inget stöd prövades och studien visar inte att någon behandling fungerar. Medicinska beslut hör till en läkare.

title: A Qualitative Study of Self and Caregiver Perspectives on How Autistic Individuals Cope With Trauma.
authors: Ng-Cordell E, Rai A, Peracha H, Garfield T, Lankenau SE, Robins DL, Berkowitz SJ, Newschaffer C, Kerns CM
abstract: Background Coping can moderate the relationship between trauma exposure and trauma symptoms. There are many conceptualisations of coping in the general population, but limited research has considered how autistic individuals cope, despite their above-average rates of traumatic exposure. Objectives To describe the range of coping strategies autistic individuals use following traumatic events. Methods Fourteen autistic adults and 15 caregivers of autistic individuals, recruited via stratified purposive sampling, completed semi-structured interviews. Participants were asked to describe how they/their child attempted to cope with events they perceived as traumatic. Using an existing theoretical framework and reflexive thematic analysis, coping strategies were identified, described, and organized into themes. Results Coping strategies used by autistic individuals could be organized into 3 main themes: (1) Engaging with Trauma, (2) Disengaging from Trauma, and (3) Self-Regulatory Coping. After the three main themes were developed, a fourth integrative theme, Diagnostic Overshadowing, was created to capture participants' reports of the overlap or confusion between coping and autism-related behaviors. Conclusions Autistic individuals use many strategies to cope with trauma, many of which are traditionally recognized as coping, but some of which may be less easily recognized given their overlap with autism-related behaviors. Findings highlight considerations for conceptualizing coping in autism, including factors influencing how individuals cope with trauma, and how aspects of autism may shape or overlap with coping behavior. Research building on these findings may inform a more nuanced understanding of how autistic people respond to adversity, and how to support coping strategies that promote recovery from trauma.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista ha vivido algo que percibe como traumático, conviene observar con curiosidad cómo se calma o se protege, sin dar por hecho que sus conductas son solo parte del autismo. Algunas pueden ser formas de afrontamiento, como buscar actividades que regulan, evitar o hablar de lo ocurrido. Es un estudio cualitativo con entrevistas a 14 adultos autistas y 15 cuidadores. Sus límites: la muestra es pequeña, se basa en relatos y no demuestra qué estrategias funcionan mejor. Cada persona es distinta; si tiene dudas, consulte a un profesional de confianza.
sheet.en: If an autistic person has lived through something they see as traumatic, try noticing with curiosity how they calm or protect themselves, rather than assuming their behaviours are just part of being autistic. Some may be ways of coping, such as regulating activities, avoiding reminders or talking about what happened. This was a qualitative study with interviews of 14 autistic adults and 15 caregivers. Its limits: the sample is small, it relies on personal accounts, and it does not show which strategies work best. Every person is different; if in doubt, talk to a professional you trust.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person har varit med om något som hen upplever som traumatiskt kan du med nyfikenhet lägga märke till hur hen lugnar eller skyddar sig, i stället för att anta att beteendena bara hör till autismen. Vissa kan vara sätt att hantera det, som reglerande aktiviteter, att undvika påminnelser eller att prata om det som hänt. Det var en kvalitativ studie med intervjuer av 14 autistiska vuxna och 15 vårdnadshavare. Begränsningar: urvalet är litet, bygger på berättelser och visar inte vilka strategier som fungerar bäst. Alla är olika; vid osäkerhet, tala med en professionell du litar på.

title: The Impact of Autism Spectrum Disorder on Parents in Arab Countries: A Systematic Literature Review.
authors: Alkhateeb JM, Hadidi MS, Mounzer W
abstract: Background Having a child with autism spectrum disorder can have significant psychological effects on parents. This systematic review summarizes the current state of literature underscoring the impact of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) on parents in Arab countries. Methods A systematic search of seven databases (PubMed, Scopus, ProQuest, Google Scholar, ERIC, Academic Search Complete, and PsycINFO) was performed, which identified 24 studies (20 quantitative studies and four qualitative studies) that included 3,299 parents or caregivers of children with ASD. These studies were conducted in 10 Arab countries (Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Egypt, Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman, Emirates, Palestine, Qatar, and Lebanon). Results The majority of the included studies found that ASD has a significant negative impact on the mental health and wellbeing of Arab parents. It was found that parents of children with ASD have a poor quality of life (QoL) and an increased risk of psychological disorders. These findings were in contrast to findings of parents of typically developing children and children with other developmental disorders. Challenges faced by parents of children with ASD were associated with several child- and parent-related factors. The most common coping strategy used by parents was religious coping. Conclusion The impact of ASD on parents has only recently gained traction among researchers in Arab countries. Despite several knowledge gaps, published studies have provided useful information outlining the impact of ASD on parents in some of these countries. Further research comprising larger random samples and using varied research and data-collection methods is required to understand the multifaceted challenges experienced by parents raising children with ASD in Arab countries.

sheet.es: Si cuidas de un niño autista, tu propio bienestar importa: busca apoyo para ti, de tu familia, tu comunidad o profesionales, y date permiso para pedir ayuda. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 24 estudios con 3,299 madres, padres o cuidadores en 10 países árabes. La mayoría halló un impacto negativo en la salud mental y el bienestar de los progenitores, y el afrontamiento religioso fue la estrategia más común. Sus límites: los estudios son aún escasos y recientes, las muestras son limitadas y los resultados no describen a todas las familias ni a todos los países.
sheet.en: If you care for an autistic child, your own wellbeing matters: look for support for yourself, from family, community or professionals, and allow yourself to ask for help. This systematic review brought together 24 studies with 3,299 parents or caregivers in 10 Arab countries. Most found a negative impact on parents' mental health and wellbeing, and religious coping was the most common strategy. Its limits: research is still recent and limited, samples are small, and the results do not describe every family or every country.
sheet.sv: Om du tar hand om ett autistiskt barn är ditt eget välmående viktigt: sök stöd för dig själv, från familj, gemenskap eller yrkespersoner, och tillåt dig att be om hjälp. Denna systematiska översikt samlade 24 studier med 3,299 föräldrar eller vårdgivare i 10 arabiska länder. De flesta fann en negativ påverkan på föräldrarnas psykiska hälsa och välmående, och religiös coping var den vanligaste strategin. Begränsningar: forskningen är ännu ny och begränsad, urvalen är små och resultaten beskriver inte alla familjer eller alla länder.

title: Exploring interpersonal and environmental factors of autistic adolescents' peer engagement in integrated education.
authors: Chen YL, Schneider M, Patten K
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Peer engagement is essential but often challenging for autistic students in integrated education, especially for adolescents. Although peer engagement is bidirectional and context-dependent, research has largely focused on individual characteristics rather than the interpersonal and environmental factors affecting peer engagement. This mixed-methods study examined peer interactions over a school year among 17 adolescents (seven were autistic) in an inclusive school club at a public middle school in the Northeastern United States. The study began with a quantitative phase identifying sessions in which each student was socially engaged with peers more or less often than usual for them. We then qualitatively compared the social interactions and contexts between sessions where each participant experienced high and low peer engagement. Thematic analysis revealed four themes regarding contextual supports and barriers to autistic peer engagement: (1) peer engagement is a participatory process where a student and their peer(s) navigate mutual understanding, shaped by both student and peer social characteristics, openness, and involvement; (2) student-peer synchronicity, such as shared interests or compatibility of social styles, was essential to autistic peer engagement; (3) peer engagement can be supported by activities facilitating joint engagement and exploration of mutual interests; (4) classroom interventions emphasizing strengths can support peer engagement, while normative behavioral standards without peer education on individual differences and diversity can perpetuate peers' negative perceptions of autistic difficulties. The findings have implications for better inclusive practice to support autistic social participation by modifying the peer environments, activities, and classroom interventions.

sheet.es: Para apoyar la relación con compañeros, conviene pensar en el entorno y no solo en la persona adolescente autista: propicie actividades en las que se comparta algo, partiendo de intereses comunes, y pida a la escuela que informe a los compañeros sobre las diferencias individuales. Es un estudio de métodos mixtos con 17 adolescentes (siete autistas) en un club escolar inclusivo durante un curso, en un colegio de Estados Unidos. Sus límites: es un grupo pequeño y un solo club, así que no sirve como regla para todas las personas ni todos los centros.
sheet.en: To support friendships with peers, look at the environment and not only at the autistic teen: favour activities where students do something together, built on shared interests, and ask the school to teach classmates about individual differences. This was a mixed-methods study following 17 adolescents (seven autistic) in an inclusive school club over a school year at a public middle school in the United States. Its limits: a small group and a single club, so it is not a rule for every person or every school.
sheet.sv: För att stödja kontakten med klasskamrater bör man se på miljön och inte bara på den autistiska tonåringen: välj aktiviteter där man gör något tillsammans, utifrån gemensamma intressen, och be skolan lära klasskamraterna om individuella skillnader. Studien använde blandade metoder och följde 17 ungdomar (sju autistiska) i en inkluderande skolklubb under ett läsår på en offentlig skola i USA. Begränsningar: en liten grupp och en enda klubb, så den är ingen regel för alla personer eller alla skolor.

title: Exploring the impact of adolescent cognitive inflexibility on emotional and behavioural problems experienced by autistic adults.
authors: Hollocks MJ, Charman T, Baird G, Lord C, Pickles A, Simonoff E
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic people experience high levels of co-occurring mental health difficulties. To develop more effective treatments, a greater understanding of the thinking processes that may lead to these difficulties is needed. Cognitive inflexibility, defined as a rigid pattern of thoughts and subsequently behaviours, is one possible thinking trait which has previously been associated with both co-occurring mental health difficulties but also other features of autism such as restricted and repetitive behaviours. Restricted and repetitive behaviours include repetitive movements, ritualistic behaviours, and/or highly focused interests. This study investigates the relationship between, cognitive inflexibility, measured using neuropsychological tasks, and emotional and behavioural problems across adolescence and early adulthood. Eighty-one autistic people who were recruited to be representative of the wider autism population were assessed at 16 and 23 years on measures of emotional and behavioural problems, with cognitive inflexibility, restricted and repetitive behaviours and verbal intelligence measured at 16 years. We used statistical modelling to investigate the relationship between cognitive inflexibility and emotional and behavioural symptoms at both timepoints while accounting for the possible relationship with restricted and repetitive behaviours and verbal intelligence quotient. Our results suggest that cognitive inflexibility may be an important factor associated with emotional difficulties across adolescence and early adulthood. This suggests that developing intervention approaches targeting cognitive inflexibility may be an important step in improving the mental health of those with autism.

sheet.es: Si tu hijo o hija adolescente autista vive con mucha dificultad los cambios de plan o las formas nuevas de pensar algo, conviene prestar atención a cómo se siente emocionalmente, no solo a su conducta. Anticipar cambios, ofrecer apoyos visuales y practicar juntos alternativas pequeñas y seguras puede ayudar, respetando siempre sus intereses y rutinas. Este estudio siguió a 81 personas autistas, representativas de la población autista, a los 16 y 23 años, y encontró que la inflexibilidad cognitiva en la adolescencia se asociaba con más dificultades emocionales después. Es una asociación, no prueba causa, la muestra es pequeña y no se aplica igual a cada persona.
sheet.en: If your autistic teenager finds changes of plan or new ways of thinking about something very hard, it is worth paying attention to how they feel emotionally, not only to what they do. Giving warning before changes, using visual supports and gently practising small, safe alternatives together may help, while respecting their interests and routines. This study followed 81 autistic people, recruited to reflect the wider autistic population, at ages 16 and 23, and found that cognitive inflexibility in adolescence was linked to more emotional difficulties later. It shows a link, not a cause, the group was small, and it does not apply the same way to everyone.
sheet.sv: Om din autistiska tonåring har mycket svårt med ändrade planer eller nya sätt att tänka kring något kan det vara klokt att uppmärksamma hur hen mår känslomässigt, inte bara vad hen gör. Att förvarna om förändringar, använda bildstöd och tillsammans lugnt öva på små, trygga alternativ kan hjälpa, med respekt för hens intressen och rutiner. Studien följde 81 autistiska personer, valda för att spegla den bredare autistiska befolkningen, vid 16 och 23 års ålder och fann att kognitiv oflexibilitet i tonåren hängde ihop med fler känslomässiga svårigheter senare. Det är ett samband, inte ett orsaksbevis, gruppen var liten och resultatet gäller inte alla på samma sätt.

title: A qualitative exploration of autistic mothers' experiences II: Childbirth and postnatal experiences.
authors: Hampton S, Man J, Allison C, Aydin E, Baron-Cohen S, Holt R
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Very little research has looked at how autistic people experience childbirth and the first few months of parenthood. We interviewed 21 autistic and 25 non-autistic women 2-3 months after their baby was born, to find out how they experienced giving birth and being a parent. Some autistic participants found sensory aspects of giving birth difficult, such as noise and being touched. They also wanted healthcare professionals to give them clear information while giving birth. Participants sometimes thought that healthcare professionals did not know enough about autism. Autistic and non-autistic participants both found parenthood difficult at times and autistic parents sometimes had extra difficulties, such as with planning and organising. Autistic participants also felt good at understanding their baby's needs. This research suggests that autistic people would benefit from changes to childbirth and postnatal healthcare such as being communicated with more clearly. It also indicates that healthcare professionals should receive more training about autism.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista durante el parto o los primeros meses con su bebé, ayuda hablar antes con el equipo sanitario sobre el ruido, el contacto físico y la necesidad de información clara en cada paso. Puede ser útil ayudar a planificar y organizar la rutina diaria. El estudio entrevistó a 21 mujeres autistas y 25 no autistas, 2-3 meses después del nacimiento. Las participantes autistas a veces encontraron difíciles los aspectos sensoriales y se sentían capaces de entender las necesidades de su bebé. Es un estudio cualitativo con pocas participantes: no describe a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If you are supporting an autistic person during childbirth or the first months with a baby, it helps to talk with the care team beforehand about noise, touch, and the need for clear information at each step. Help with planning and organising daily routines may also be useful. The study interviewed 21 autistic and 25 non-autistic women 2-3 months after birth. Some autistic participants found sensory aspects difficult, and they felt good at understanding their baby's needs. It is a qualitative study with a small group, so it does not describe every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person under förlossningen eller de första månaderna med bebisen kan det hjälpa att i förväg prata med vårdteamet om ljud, beröring och behovet av tydlig information i varje steg. Stöd med planering och organisering av vardagen kan också vara till nytta. Studien intervjuade 21 autistiska och 25 icke-autistiska kvinnor 2-3 månader efter förlossningen. Några autistiska deltagare upplevde sinnesintryck som svåra, och de kände sig bra på att förstå bebisens behov. Det är en kvalitativ studie med en liten grupp, så den beskriver inte alla autistiska personer.

title: Identifying and describing subtypes of spontaneous empathic facial expression production in autistic adults.
authors: Quinde-Zlibut J, Munshi A, Biswas G, Cascio CJ
abstract: Background It is unclear whether atypical patterns of facial expression production metrics in autism reflect the dynamic and nuanced nature of facial expressions across people or a true diagnostic difference. Furthermore, the heterogeneity observed across autism symptomatology suggests a need for more adaptive and personalized social skills programs. Towards this goal, it would be useful to have a more concrete and empirical understanding of the different expressiveness profiles within the autistic population and how they differ from neurotypicals. Methods We used automated facial coding and an unsupervised clustering approach to limit inter-individual variability in facial expression production that may have otherwise obscured group differences in previous studies, allowing an "apples-to-apples" comparison between autistic and neurotypical adults. Specifically, we applied k-means clustering to identify subtypes of facial expressiveness in an autism group (N = 27) and a neurotypical control group (N = 57) separately. The two most stable clusters from these analyses were then further characterized and compared based on their expressiveness and emotive congruence to emotionally charged stimuli. Results Our main finding was that a subset of autistic adults in our sample show heightened spontaneous facial expressions irrespective of image valence. We did not find evidence for greater incongruous (i.e., inappropriate) facial expressions in autism. Finally, we found a negative trend between expressiveness and emotion recognition within the autism group. Conclusion The results from our previous study on self-reported empathy and current expressivity findings point to a higher degree of facial expressions recruited for emotional resonance in autism that may not always be adaptive (e.g., experiencing similar emotional resonance regardless of valence). These findings also build on previous work indicating that facial expression intensity is not diminished in autism and suggest the need for intervention programs to focus on emotion recognition and social skills in the context of both negative and positive emotions.

sheet.es: Tras leer este estudio: no des por hecho que una persona autista muestra poca expresión facial. Observa cómo expresa cada persona sus emociones, tanto ante cosas agradables como desagradables, y habla con ella de lo que siente en cada situación. Es un estudio de investigación con 27 adultos autistas y 57 adultos neurotípicos que miraron imágenes con carga emocional. Un grupo de adultos autistas mostró más expresiones espontáneas, sin importar si la imagen era positiva o negativa, y no se hallaron más expresiones inadecuadas. Límites: la muestra es pequeña, solo incluye adultos y no sirve como regla para todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: After reading this study: don't assume an autistic person shows little facial expression. Notice how each person expresses feelings, in response to both pleasant and unpleasant things, and talk with them about what they feel in different situations. This was a research study with 27 autistic adults and 57 neurotypical adults who viewed emotionally charged images. A subset of the autistic adults showed more spontaneous facial expressions whether the image was positive or negative, and no evidence of more inappropriate expressions was found. Limits: the sample is small, includes only adults, and is not a rule for every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Efter den här studien: anta inte att en autistisk person visar lite ansiktsuttryck. Lägg märke till hur varje person uttrycker känslor, både inför trevliga och obehagliga saker, och prata med personen om vad hen känner i olika situationer. Det var en forskningsstudie med 27 autistiska vuxna och 57 neurotypiska vuxna som tittade på känslomässigt laddade bilder. En grupp av de autistiska vuxna visade fler spontana ansiktsuttryck oavsett om bilden var positiv eller negativ, och inga belägg hittades för fler olämpliga uttryck. Begränsningar: urvalet är litet, omfattar bara vuxna och gäller inte som regel för alla autistiska personer.

title: A blind spot in mental healthcare? Psychotherapists lack education and expertise for the support of adults on the autism spectrum.
authors: Lipinski S, Boegl K, Blanke ES, Suenkel U, Dziobek I
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Most autistic adults experience mental health problems. There is a great demand for psychotherapeutic support that addresses the specific needs of autistic individuals. However, people with autism encounter difficulties trying to access diagnostic and therapeutic services. This study was conducted by a participatory autism research group: a group in which autistic individuals and scientists collaborate. The group developed a questionnaire for psychotherapists in Germany to assess their knowledge about autism. Psychotherapists also rated their ability to diagnose and treat autistic patients without intellectual disability, and patients with other psychological diagnoses. Many of the 498 psychotherapists that responded reported little knowledge and outdated beliefs about autism, as well as little training on treating patients with autism. Their expertise about other psychological conditions was more comprehensive. However, many psychotherapists were interested in professional training on autism. Those with more knowledge were also more open to treating autistic patients. In conclusion, psychotherapists' lack of knowledge and expertise seem to be a major barrier for adults with autism to receiving helpful psychotherapeutic support. The results demonstrate the need for an advancement in autism education during psychotherapists' training and in continuous education.

sheet.es: Si buscas psicoterapia para un adulto autista, es razonable preguntar al terapeuta, antes de empezar, qué formación y experiencia tiene en autismo y cómo adaptaría las sesiones. Llevar información breve sobre las necesidades de la persona puede ayudar, y cambiar de profesional si no hay comprensión es legítimo. Este estudio, diseñado por un grupo participativo de personas autistas e investigadores, encuestó a 498 psicoterapeutas en Alemania: muchos tenían poco conocimiento, ideas desactualizadas y escasa formación en autismo, aunque muchos querían aprender. Sus límites: se basa en autoevaluaciones de quienes quisieron responder, en un solo país, y no mide la calidad real de la atención.
sheet.en: If you are looking for psychotherapy for an autistic adult, it is reasonable to ask a therapist, before starting, what training and experience they have with autism and how they would adapt sessions. Bringing brief notes on the person's needs can help, and changing professionals if understanding is lacking is legitimate. This study, designed by a participatory group of autistic people and researchers, surveyed 498 psychotherapists in Germany: many reported little knowledge, outdated beliefs and limited autism training, though many wanted to learn more. Its limits: it relies on self-ratings from those who chose to respond, in one country, and does not measure actual quality of care.
sheet.sv: Om du söker psykoterapi för en autistisk vuxen är det rimligt att innan start fråga terapeuten vilken utbildning och erfarenhet hen har av autism och hur sessionerna skulle anpassas. Att ta med korta anteckningar om personens behov kan hjälpa, och det är helt okej att byta behandlare om förståelsen saknas. Studien, utformad av en deltagande grupp av autistiska personer och forskare, var en enkät till 498 psykoterapeuter i Tyskland: många rapporterade lite kunskap, föråldrade föreställningar och begränsad autismutbildning, men många ville lära sig mer. Begränsningar: den bygger på självskattningar från dem som valde att svara, i ett enda land, och mäter inte vårdens faktiska kvalitet.

title: Developing undergraduate autism education for medical students: a qualitative study.
authors: Dhuga Y, Feeney Y, Gallaher L, White A, Wright J, Banerjee S, Daley S
abstract: Background Autistic adults and children experience considerable health inequalities and have high rates of premature mortality, hospital admissions and emergency department visits. This is in part due to a lack of autism awareness in the healthcare and social care workforce. A new educational programme, Time for Autism (TfA), for medical students is being developed to address this challenge. This qualitative study was undertaken to support the development of the new programme in order to (1) understand the medical care experiences of parents of autistic children and (2) assess their views on the acceptability of the new TfA programme and willingness to be involved. Methods A convenience sample of 11 parents of autistic children were recruited across the South of England. The ages of the autistic children ranged from 3 to 17 years. Semistructured interviews were completed between October and December 2019. Interview transcripts were analysed using thematic analysis. Results Three key themes were identified: diagnosis, experiences of doctors and TfA considerations. There was support for and willingness to take part in a dedicated autism education programme for medical students, and constructive feedback to inform and improve its delivery. Conclusion The findings from this study provide insights into the medical care experiences of parents/carers of autistic children. Understanding how parents/carers of autistic children would like medical care to be improved can be used to develop TfA and other autism programmes. Parental/carer support for the development of and involvement in an autism medical education programme enhances the feasibility of the new programme.

sheet.es: Mañana, si vas a una cita médica con tu hijo autista, puedes explicar con calma cómo es mejor atenderle y compartir tu experiencia: a las familias les interesa que los futuros médicos aprendan sobre autismo. Evidencia: estudio cualitativo con entrevistas a 11 madres y padres de niños autistas de 3 a 17 años, en el sur de Inglaterra; los temas fueron el diagnóstico, las experiencias con médicos y el programa educativo. Límites: muestra pequeña y de conveniencia, sin voz directa de las personas autistas, así que no vale para todas las familias.
sheet.en: Tomorrow, if you go to a medical appointment with your autistic child, you can calmly explain how care works best for them and share your experience: families said they support medical students learning about autism. Evidence: a qualitative interview study with 11 parents of autistic children aged 3 to 17 in the South of England; themes were diagnosis, experiences of doctors and the education programme. Limits: a small convenience sample, without autistic people's own voices, so it cannot speak for every family.
sheet.sv: I morgon, om du följer ditt autistiska barn till ett läkarbesök, kan du lugnt förklara hur vården fungerar bäst för barnet och dela med dig av dina erfarenheter: familjer stödde att läkarstudenter lär sig om autism. Evidens: en kvalitativ intervjustudie med 11 föräldrar till autistiska barn i åldern 3 till 17 i södra England; teman var diagnos, erfarenheter av läkare och utbildningsprogrammet. Begränsningar: litet bekvämlighetsurval, utan autistiska personers egna röster, så resultaten gäller inte alla familjer.

title: The Current View on the Paradox of Pain in Autism Spectrum Disorders.
authors: Bogdanova OV, Bogdanov VB, Pizano A, Bouvard M, Cazalets JR, Mellen N, Amestoy A
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder, which affects 1 in 44 children and may cause severe disabilities. Besides socio-communicational difficulties and repetitive behaviors, ASD also presents as atypical sensorimotor function and pain reactivity. While chronic pain is a frequent co-morbidity in autism, pain management in this population is often insufficient because of difficulties in pain evaluation, worsening their prognosis and perhaps driving higher mortality rates. Previous observations have tended to oversimplify the experience of pain in autism as being insensitive to painful stimuli. Various findings in the past 15 years have challenged and complicated this dogma. However, a relatively small number of studies investigates the physiological correlates of pain reactivity in ASD. We explore the possibility that atypical pain perception in people with ASD is mediated by alterations in pain perception, transmission, expression and modulation, and through interactions between these processes. These complex interactions may account for the great variability and sometimes contradictory findings from the studies. A growing body of evidence is challenging the idea of alterations in pain processing in ASD due to a single factor, and calls for an integrative view. We propose a model of the pain cycle that includes the interplay between the molecular and neurophysiological pathways of pain processing and it conscious appraisal that may interfere with pain reactivity and coping in autism. The role of social factors in pain-induced response is also discussed. Pain assessment in clinical care is mostly based on subjective rather than objective measures. This review clarifies the strong need for a consistent methodology, and describes innovative tools to cope with the heterogeneity of pain expression in ASD, enabling individualized assessment. Multiple measures, including self-reporting, informant reporting, clinician-assessed, and purely physiological metrics may provide more consistent results. An integrative view on the regulation of the pain cycle offers a more robust framework to characterize the experience of pain in autism.

sheet.es: No des por hecho que una persona autista no siente dolor: puede expresarlo de forma distinta, y conviene creerle. Si dice o muestra que algo duele, tómalo en serio y combina varias fuentes: lo que cuenta la persona, lo que observas tú y la valoración de un profesional sanitario. Esta es una revisión de estudios previos, no un ensayo con participantes propios. Señala que el dolor crónico es frecuente y que su evaluación suele ser insuficiente. Sus límites: pocos estudios miden los procesos físicos del dolor, los resultados varían mucho y no sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: Don't assume an autistic person doesn't feel pain: they may express it differently, and it is worth believing them. If they say or show that something hurts, take it seriously and combine several sources: what the person tells you, what you observe, and an assessment by a health professional. This is a review of earlier studies, not a trial with its own participants. It notes that chronic pain is common and that its assessment is often insufficient. Its limits: few studies measure the physical processes of pain, findings vary a lot, and it is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Utgå inte från att en autistisk person inte känner smärta: hen kan uttrycka den annorlunda, och det är värt att tro på hen. Om personen säger eller visar att något gör ont, ta det på allvar och kombinera flera källor: vad personen berättar, vad du observerar och en bedömning av vårdpersonal. Detta är en översikt av tidigare studier, inte en studie med egna deltagare. Den visar att kronisk smärta är vanligt och att bedömningen ofta är otillräcklig. Begränsningar: få studier mäter smärtans fysiska processer, resultaten varierar mycket och översikten är ingen regel för alla personer.

claim.es: La vieja idea de 'indiferencia al dolor' en autismo es errónea: el dolor se expresa de forma atípica y a menudo se pasa por alto.
claim.en: The old idea of 'pain indifference' in autism is wrong: pain is expressed atypically and often missed.
claim.sv: Den gamla idén om 'smärtokänslighet' vid autism är fel: smärta uttrycks annorlunda och missas ofta.

supports.es: Tratar un cambio de conducta como posible señal de dolor que merece comprobarse.
supports.en: Treating a change in behaviour as a possible pain signal worth checking.
supports.sv: Att se en beteendeförändring som en möjlig smärtsignal värd att kontrollera.

doesNotSupport.es: Que cuidadores o cámaras puedan medir el dolor; el dolor sigue siendo una hipótesis que se comprueba con sanidad.
doesNotSupport.en: That caregivers or cameras can measure pain; pain remains a hypothesis to check with healthcare.
doesNotSupport.sv: Att vårdgivare eller kameror kan mäta smärta; smärta förblir en hypotes att kontrollera med vården.

title: Autistic adults' views and experiences of requesting and receiving workplace adjustments in the UK.
authors: Davies J, Heasman B, Livesey A, Walker A, Pellicano E, Remington A
abstract: This article examines 181 autistic adults' views toward, and experiences of, requesting and receiving workplace adjustments in the UK. Using an online survey, we collected both qualitative and quantitative data relating to individuals' experiences. While the majority of participants perceived workplace adjustments to be important, many were not receiving them. Analysis of open-ended text responses highlighted specific challenges that autistic people face in requesting and receiving adjustments. Specifically, participants felt the onus fell on them to (1) identify their need for adjustments; (2) establish the specific adjustments that would be beneficial and (3) request adjustments from their employer.
