Yet, they reported struggling with this process. Participants also highlighted a range of social and organisational barriers to the successful implementation of workplace adjustments. Unsurprisingly, the lack of successfully implemented adjustments had far-reaching impacts on participants' wellbeing as well as the choices they made about their future employment. These findings highlight the need for employers to take a more active role in the identification and implementation of workplace adjustments, as well as a need for more understanding and inclusive working environments that truly allow autistic employees to thrive in the workplace.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista que trabaja, puedes ayudarle a identificar qué cambios le facilitarían el día (luz, ruido, horarios, instrucciones por escrito) y a preparar juntos la petición a la empresa, si ella lo desea. No debería cargar sola con todo el proceso: es razonable esperar que el empleador participe activamente. Este estudio fue una encuesta en línea a 181 adultos autistas en el Reino Unido; la mayoría valoraba las adaptaciones, pero muchas no las recibían, y eso afectaba su bienestar y sus decisiones laborales. Sus límites: participaron voluntariamente personas con acceso a internet, en un solo país, y las experiencias pueden no reflejar las de todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person who works, you can help them notice which changes would make the day easier (lighting, noise, schedules, written instructions) and prepare a request to their employer together, if they want that. They shouldn't have to carry the whole process alone: it is reasonable to expect employers to take an active part. This study was an online survey of 181 autistic adults in the UK; most valued workplace adjustments, but many weren't receiving them, which affected their wellbeing and job choices. Its limits: participants volunteered online, all in one country, so their experiences may not reflect every autistic person's.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person som arbetar kan ni tillsammans fundera på vilka anpassningar som skulle göra dagen lättare (ljus, ljud, arbetstider, skriftliga instruktioner) och förbereda en begäran till arbetsgivaren, om personen vill det. Hen ska inte behöva bära hela processen själv: det är rimligt att arbetsgivaren tar en aktiv roll. Studien var en webbenkät med 181 autistiska vuxna i Storbritannien; de flesta tyckte att anpassningar var viktiga, men många fick dem inte, vilket påverkade välmående och framtida jobbval. Begränsningar: deltagarna anmälde sig frivilligt via nätet i ett enda land, så erfarenheterna gäller inte nödvändigtvis alla autistiska personer.

title: Psychometric validation of a brief self-report measure of misophonia symptoms and functional impairment: The duke-vanderbilt misophonia screening questionnaire.
authors: Williams ZJ, Cascio CJ, Woynaroski TG
abstract: Misophonia is a newly described disorder of sound tolerance characterized by strong negative emotional reactions to specific "trigger" sounds, resulting in significant distress, pathological avoidance, and impairment in daily life. Research on misophonia is still in its infancy, and most existing psychometric tools for assessing misophonia symptoms have not been extensively validated. The purpose of the current study was to introduce and psychometrically validate the duke-vanderbilt Misophonia Screening Questionnaire (DVMSQ), a novel self-report measure of misophonia symptoms that can be used to determine misophonia "caseness" in clinical and research settings. Employing large online samples of general population adults ( n = 1403) and adults on the autism spectrum ( n = 936), we rigorously evaluated the internal structure, reliability, validity, and measurement invariance of the DVMSQ. Results indicated that 17 of the 20 original DVMSQ items fit well to a bifactor structure with one "general misophonia" factor and four specific factors (anger/aggression, distress/avoidance, impairment, and global impact). DVMSQ total and subscale scores were highly reliable in both general population and autistic adult samples, and the measure was found to be approximately invariant across age, sex, education level, and autism status. DVMSQ total scores also correlated strongly with another measure of misophonia symptoms (Duke Misophonia Questionnaire-Symptom Scale), with correlations between these two measures being significantly stronger than correlations between the DVMSQ and scales measuring other types of sound intolerance (Inventory of Hyperacusis Symptoms [General Loudness subscale] and DSM-5 Severity Measure for Specific Phobia [modified for phonophobia]). Additionally, DVMSQ items were used to operationalize diagnostic criteria for misophonia derived from the Revised Amsterdam Criteria, which were further updated to reflect a recent consensus definition of misophonia (published after the development of the DVMSQ). Using the new DVMSQ algorithm, 7.3% of general population adults and 35.5% of autistic adults met criteria for clinically significant misophonia. Although additional work is needed to further investigate the psychometric properties of the DVMSQ and validate its theory-based screening algorithm using best-estimate clinical diagnoses, this novel measure represents a potentially useful tool to screen for misophonia and quantify symptom severity and impairment in both autistic adults and the general population.

sheet.es: Si a una persona autista ciertos sonidos concretos (masticar, respirar, teclear) le provocan enfado, angustia o ganas de huir, tómelo en serio: puede ser misofonía, algo frecuente y real. Pregúntele qué sonidos le afectan, acuerden juntos opciones como auriculares, música de fondo o comer en otro espacio, y evite insistir en que «se acostumbre». Este estudio validó un cuestionario breve de autoinforme con 1.403 adultos de población general y 936 adultos autistas en línea; el 35,5 % de los adultos autistas cumplía criterios de misofonía significativa, frente al 7,3 % del resto. Límites: muestras en línea, solo adultos y sin confirmación mediante evaluación clínica; el cuestionario sirve para detectar, no para diagnosticar.
sheet.en: If an autistic person reacts to specific sounds (chewing, breathing, typing) with anger, distress or an urge to escape, take it seriously: it may be misophonia, which is common and real. Ask which sounds affect them, agree together on options like headphones, background music or eating in another room, and avoid pushing them to “get used to it.” This study validated a brief self-report questionnaire with 1,403 general-population adults and 936 autistic adults online; 35.5% of autistic adults met criteria for significant misophonia, versus 7.3% of others. Limits: online samples, adults only, and no confirmation through clinical assessment; the questionnaire screens, it does not diagnose.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person reagerar på vissa specifika ljud (tuggande, andning, tangentknatter) med ilska, obehag eller vilja att fly, ta det på allvar: det kan vara misofoni, som är vanligt och verkligt. Fråga vilka ljud som påverkar, kom gemensamt överens om lösningar som hörlurar, bakgrundsmusik eller att äta i ett annat rum, och undvik att kräva att personen ska ”vänja sig”. Studien validerade ett kort självskattningsformulär med 1 403 vuxna ur befolkningen och 936 autistiska vuxna online; 35,5 % av de autistiska vuxna uppfyllde kriterier för betydande misofoni, jämfört med 7,3 % av övriga. Begränsningar: onlineurval, endast vuxna och ingen bekräftelse genom klinisk bedömning; formuläret är för screening, inte diagnos.

title: Role of Gut Microbiome in Autism Spectrum Disorder and Its Therapeutic Regulation.
authors: Taniya MA, Chung HJ, Al Mamun A, Alam S, Aziz MA, Emon NU, Islam MM, Hong SS, Podder BR, Ara Mimi A, Aktar Suchi S, Xiao J
journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurological disorder that affects normal brain development. The recent finding of the microbiota-gut-brain axis indicates the bidirectional connection between our gut and brain, demonstrating that gut microbiota can influence many neurological disorders such as autism. Most autistic patients suffer from gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms. Many studies have shown that early colonization, mode of delivery, and antibiotic usage significantly affect the gut microbiome and the onset of autism. Microbial fermentation of plant-based fiber can produce different types of short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) that may have a beneficial or detrimental effect on the gut and neurological development of autistic patients. Several comprehensive studies of the gut microbiome and microbiota-gut-brain axis help to understand the mechanism that leads to the onset of neurological disorders and find possible treatments for autism. This review integrates the findings of recent years on the gut microbiota and ASD association, mainly focusing on the characterization of specific microbiota that leads to ASD and addressing potential therapeutic interventions to restore a healthy balance of gut microbiome composition that can treat autism-associated symptoms.

sheet.es: Si la persona autista tiene molestias digestivas, vale la pena anotar cuándo aparecen y qué las acompaña, y comentarlo con su profesional de salud antes de cambiar la dieta o añadir suplementos. Es una revisión de estudios recientes sobre la relación entre la microbiota intestinal y el autismo, y sobre posibles intervenciones. Sus límites: el resumen habla de asociaciones y mecanismos posibles, no demuestra que el intestino cause el autismo ni que un tratamiento funcione para cada persona. El autismo no es algo que haya que curar; cualquier decisión médica corresponde a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If an autistic person has digestive discomfort, it is worth noting when it happens and what goes with it, and raising it with their health professional before changing diet or adding supplements. This is a review of recent studies on the link between gut bacteria and autism, and on possible interventions. Its limits: the abstract describes associations and possible mechanisms, not proof that the gut causes autism or that any approach works for every person. Autism is not something to be cured, and any medical decision belongs with a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person har magbesvär är det värt att anteckna när de uppstår och vad som följer med dem, och ta upp det med vården innan man ändrar kosten eller lägger till kosttillskott. Det här är en översikt av nyare studier om sambandet mellan tarmbakterier och autism, samt möjliga insatser. Begränsningar: sammanfattningen beskriver samband och möjliga mekanismer, inte bevis för att tarmen orsakar autism eller att en metod fungerar för alla. Autism är inget som ska botas, och medicinska beslut hör hemma hos en läkare eller annan vårdgivare.

title: Misinformation About COVID-19 Vaccines on Social Media: Rapid Review.
authors: Skafle I, Nordahl-Hansen A, Quintana DS, Wynn R, Gabarron E
abstract: Background The development of COVID-19 vaccines has been crucial in fighting the pandemic. However, misinformation about the COVID-19 pandemic and vaccines is spread on social media platforms at a rate that has made the World Health Organization coin the phrase infodemic. False claims about adverse vaccine side effects, such as vaccines being the cause of autism, were already considered a threat to global health before the outbreak of COVID-19. Objective We aimed to synthesize the existing research on misinformation about COVID-19 vaccines spread on social media platforms and its effects. The secondary aim was to gain insight and gather knowledge about whether misinformation about autism and COVID-19 vaccines is being spread on social media platforms. Methods We performed a literature search on September 9, 2021, and searched PubMed, PsycINFO, ERIC, EMBASE, Cochrane Library, and the Cochrane COVID-19 Study Register. We included publications in peer-reviewed journals that fulfilled the following criteria: original empirical studies, studies that assessed social media and misinformation, and studies about COVID-19 vaccines. Thematic analysis was used to identify the patterns (themes) of misinformation. Narrative qualitative synthesis was undertaken with the guidance of the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) 2020 Statement and the Synthesis Without Meta-analysis reporting guideline. The risk of bias was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal tool. Ratings of the certainty of evidence were based on recommendations from the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation Working Group. Results The search yielded 757 records, with 45 articles selected for this review. We identified 3 main themes of misinformation: medical misinformation, vaccine development, and conspiracies. Twitter was the most studied social media platform, followed by Facebook, YouTube, and Instagram. A vast majority of studies were from industrialized Western countries. We identified 19 studies in which the effect of social media misinformation on vaccine hesitancy was measured or discussed. These studies implied that the misinformation spread on social media had a negative effect on vaccine hesitancy and uptake. Only 1 study contained misinformation about autism as a side effect of COVID-19 vaccines. Conclusions To prevent these misconceptions from taking hold, health authorities should openly address and discuss these false claims with both cultural and religious awareness in mind. Our review showed that there is a need to examine the effect of social media misinformation on vaccine hesitancy with a more robust experimental design. Furthermore, this review also demonstrated that more studies are needed from the Global South and on social media platforms other than the major platforms such as Twitter and Facebook. Trial registration PROSPERO International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews CRD42021277524; https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/display_record.php?ID=CRD42021277524. International registered report identifier (irrid) RR2-10.31219/osf.io/tyevj.

sheet.es: Si ves en redes sociales que las vacunas causan autismo, puedes comprobar la fuente y hablar de ello con un profesional sanitario de confianza; las decisiones médicas corresponden a la clínica. Es una revisión sistemática de 45 artículos sobre desinformación acerca de las vacunas contra la COVID-19 en redes sociales. Solo 1 estudio contenía desinformación que vinculaba el autismo con estas vacunas. Sus límites: la mayoría de los estudios eran de países occidentales industrializados y se centraban en Twitter y Facebook, y hacen falta diseños más sólidos. No es una regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If you see claims on social media that vaccines cause autism, you can check the source and talk it over with a trusted health professional; medical decisions belong to a clinician. This is a systematic review of 45 articles on misinformation about COVID-19 vaccines on social media. Only 1 study contained misinformation linking autism to these vaccines. Its limits: most studies came from industrialized Western countries and focused on Twitter and Facebook, and stronger study designs are needed. It is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du ser påståenden i sociala medier om att vacciner orsakar autism kan du kontrollera källan och prata om det med en pålitlig vårdgivare; medicinska beslut hör till kliniker. Detta är en systematisk översikt av 45 artiklar om desinformation om covid-19-vacciner i sociala medier. Bara 1 studie innehöll desinformation som kopplade autism till dessa vacciner. Begränsningar: de flesta studier kom från industrialiserade västländer och fokuserade på Twitter och Facebook, och starkare studieupplägg behövs. Det är ingen regel för varje person.

title: Five Ways Providers Can Improve Mental Healthcare for Autistic Adults: A Review of Mental Healthcare Use, Barriers to Care, and Evidence-Based Recommendations.
authors: Gilmore D, Longo A, Krantz M, Radford D, Hand BN

title: Effects of a Gamified, Behavior Change Technique-Based Mobile App on Increasing Physical Activity and Reducing Anxiety in Adults With Autism Spectrum Disorder: Feasibility Randomized Controlled Trial.
authors: Lee D, Frey GC, Cothran DJ, Harezlak J, Shih PC
abstract: Background Physical activity (PA) has an impact on physical and mental health in neurotypical populations, and addressing these variables may improve the prevalent burden of anxiety in adults with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Gamified mobile apps using behavior change techniques present a promising way of increasing PA and reducing sedentary time, thus reducing anxiety in adults with ASD. Objective This study aimed to compare the effectiveness of a gamified and behavior change technique-based mobile app, PuzzleWalk, versus a commercially available app, Google Fit, on increasing PA and reducing sedentary time as an adjunct anxiety treatment for this population. Methods A total of 24 adults with ASD were assigned to either the PuzzleWalk or Google Fit group for 5 weeks using a covariate-adaptive randomization design. PA and anxiety were assessed over 7 days at 3 different data collection periods (ie, baseline, intervention start, and intervention end) using triaxial accelerometers and the Beck Anxiety Inventory. Group differences in outcome variables were assessed using repeated-measures analysis of covariance, adjusting for age, sex, and BMI. Results The findings indicated that the PuzzleWalk group spent a significantly longer amount of time on app use compared with the Google Fit group (F 2,38 =5.07; P=.01; partial η 2 =0.21), whereas anxiety was unfavorably associated with increases in light PA and decreases in sedentary time after intervention (all P Conclusions Further research is needed to clarify the determinants of physical and mental health and their interrelationship in adults with ASD to identify the factors that facilitate the use and adoption of mobile health technologies in these individuals. Despite these mixed results, the small changes in PA or anxiety may be clinically significant for adults with ASD. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05466617; https://clinicaltrials.gov/show/NCT05466617.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta quiere moverse más, una app con juegos puede resultarle atractiva, pero conviene probarla con calma y sin esperar que baje la ansiedad. Es un ensayo de viabilidad con 24 adultos autistas, repartidos al azar entre dos apps durante 5 semanas. Quienes usaron PuzzleWalk pasaron más tiempo con la app que quienes usaron Google Fit. La ansiedad se asoció de forma desfavorable con más actividad ligera y menos tiempo sentado, así que los resultados fueron mixtos. El grupo es pequeño y no sirve como regla para todas las personas. Si la ansiedad preocupa, consulten a un profesional sanitario.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult wants to move more, a game-style app may be appealing, but try it gently and don't expect it to ease anxiety. This was a feasibility trial with 24 autistic adults, randomly assigned to one of two apps for 5 weeks. People using PuzzleWalk spent more time on the app than those using Google Fit. Anxiety was unfavorably associated with more light activity and less sitting time, so results were mixed. The group was small, and the findings are not a rule for every person. If anxiety is a concern, talk with a health professional.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen vill röra sig mer kan en app med spelinslag vara lockande, men prova den i lugn takt och förvänta dig inte att oron minskar. Det var en genomförbarhetsstudie med 24 autistiska vuxna som slumpades till en av två appar i 5 veckor. De som använde PuzzleWalk spenderade mer tid i appen än de som använde Google Fit. Ångest hängde ogynnsamt samman med mer lätt aktivitet och mindre stillasittande, så resultaten var blandade. Gruppen var liten och resultaten är ingen regel för alla. Om ångest oroar, prata med vården.

title: Parent-mediated play-based interventions to improve social communication and language skills of preschool autistic children: A systematic review and meta-analysis protocol.
authors: Deniz E, Francis G, Torgerson C, Toseeb U
abstract: Early years interventions have shown to be effective in improving the social communication and language skills of autistic children. Therefore, various play-based interventions have been developed to support those developmental areas of autistic children. Although researchers have previously reported the overall effectiveness of different types of play-based interventions on the social communication and language skills of autistic children, no previous systematic reviews have yet evaluated the effectiveness of parent-mediated play-based interventions in preschool autistic children. The overarching aims of the study will be to (i) report the key characteristics and (ii) synthesise the results of studies evaluating parent-mediated play-based interventions targeting the social communication and language skills of preschool autistic children using experimental designs. A comprehensive search for and screening of the relevant studies published between 2000 and 2021 will be undertaken. To be included, studies will have to (i) use either a randomised control trial or quasi-experimental design, (ii) focus on preschool autistic children aged six years old or younger, (iii) deliver a play-based intervention in non-educational settings, and (iv) include at least one parent as the mediator of the intervention. Data extraction of all included studies will be undertaken using a specially devised template and they will also be assessed for risk of bias using an adapted form from the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool. The overall characteristics of the included studies will be reported and a narrative synthesis of the results of the included studies will be undertaken. A meta-analysis may be performed (if justified) to report the pooled effect size of the parent-mediated play-based interventions on the social communication and language skills of preschool autistic children. Trial registration: The current study protocol was pre-registered with the international prospective register of systematic reviews (PROSPERO: CRD42022302220).

title: Intensive behavioural interventions based on applied behaviour analysis (ABA) for young children with autism: A cost-effectiveness analysis.
authors: Hodgson R, Biswas M, Palmer S, Marshall D, Rodgers M, Stewart L, Simmonds M, Rai D, Le Couteur A
abstract: Background The economic and social costs of autism are significant. This study evaluates the cost-effectiveness of early intensive Applied Behaviour Analysis (ABA)-based interventions for autistic pre-school children in the UK. Methods A de novo economic analysis was developed in Microsoft Excel comparing early intensive ABA-based interventions compared with treatment as usual (TAU). The analysis used 15.5-year time horizon, with costs and benefits discounted a 3.5%. The model structure was based on cohort structure to capture changes in adaptive behaviour and cognitive ability over time. The analysis was informed by an individual patient data (IPD) meta-analysis of available evidence. Results Adopting a public sector perspective, early intensive ABA-based therapies were associated with greater incremental costs and greater benefits. When pessimistic assumptions were made regarding the long-term effects of treatment incremental costs were £46,103 and incremental quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) were 0.24, resulting in an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) of £189,122 per quality-adjusted life year (QALY). When optimistic assumptions were made about long-term effects, incremental costs were £39,233 with incremental benefits of 0.84 QALYs. The resulting ICER was £46,768 per QALY. Scenario analyses emphasised the importance of assumptions made regarding adult outcomes and type of school attended, both of which significantly affect the results of the analysis. Conclusions The results of this economic analysis suggest that early intensive ABA-based interventions are unlikely to represent value for money, based on a £20,000 to £30,000 per QALY threshold typically adopted to inform UK healthcare funding decisions. However, important gaps in the available evidence, limit the strength of the conclusions that can be drawn from the presented analysis. Further research, focusing on the trajectory of autistic children following intervention is likely to be highly beneficial to resolving some of these uncertainties.

sheet.es: Si le ofrecen un programa intensivo de ABA para un niño autista pequeño, pregunte qué objetivos persigue, cuánto tiempo exige a la familia y cómo se medirá lo que importa a su hijo. Este estudio es un análisis económico basado en un metaanálisis de datos individuales, centrado en niños autistas en edad preescolar del Reino Unido. Concluye que estas intervenciones probablemente no representen buena relación calidad-precio según el umbral de £20,000 a £30,000 por QALY usado en el Reino Unido. Sus límites: faltan datos sobre cómo evolucionan los niños después, y los resultados dependen de supuestos. No dice nada sobre qué conviene a una persona concreta.
sheet.en: If you are offered an intensive ABA programme for a young autistic child, ask what goals it aims for, how much time it asks of the family, and how progress that matters to your child will be measured. This study is an economic analysis built on an individual patient data meta-analysis, focused on autistic pre-school children in the UK. It concluded that these interventions are unlikely to represent value for money against the £20,000 to £30,000 per QALY threshold used in the UK. Its limits: important gaps in evidence on how children fare afterwards, and results depend on assumptions. It does not say what suits any one child.
sheet.sv: Om ni erbjuds ett intensivt ABA-program för ett litet autistiskt barn, fråga vilka mål det har, hur mycket tid det kräver av familjen och hur framsteg som är viktiga för ditt barn ska följas upp. Studien är en hälsoekonomisk analys baserad på en metaanalys av individdata, med autistiska förskolebarn i Storbritannien. Slutsatsen var att insatserna sannolikt inte ger rimlig valuta för pengarna jämfört med tröskeln £20,000 till £30,000 per QALY som används i Storbritannien. Begränsningar: viktiga kunskapsluckor om hur barnen klarar sig efteråt, och resultaten beror på antaganden. Studien säger inget om vad som passar ett enskilt barn.

title: Psychoeducational group intervention for intellectually able adults with autism and their close relations (Prisma) - an open feasibility study.
authors: Hidalgo N, Sjöwall D, Agius H, Byström C, Brar A, Borg J, Hirvikoski T
abstract: Background Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in adulthood is associated with severe impairments in functioning and poor health, while ASD is also affecting close relations. Accessible first-line interventions addressing the complex clinical needs and care coordination are lacking. Methods This study investigated the feasibility and preliminary effects of a new psychoeducational intervention (Prisma) developed for intellectually able adults with ASD and their close relations in an outpatient setting. The manualized Prisma intervention consist of four weekly group sessions guided by trained group leaders and providing information about autism, support, and services. Feasibility was examined through treatment completion rate and group-level comparisons between intervention completers and non-completers (Student's t-test, Fisher's exact test, and Pearson's chi-squared test). Perceived treatment credibility was investigated by within-group comparisons of participant's self-ratings from pre-intervention to post-intervention, as well as by group leaders' ratings using an adjusted questionnaire. Treatment satisfaction was examined quantitatively regarding the session evaluations (Student's t-tests), as well as by a qualitative thematic analysis of participants' feedback. Preliminary efficacy was studied using paired t-tests (pre- and post-intervention). Results Completion rate was 77% (n = 71 of the 92 adults with ASD) and 73% (n = 69 of the 94 close relations), respectively. Participants considered Prisma to be an acceptable intervention indicated by increases in treatment credibility and expectations from pre- to post-intervention. The group leaders reported treatment credibility in the same range as the participants. Both autistic adults and their close relations reported good treatment satisfaction for each session, while the qualitative thematic analysis indicated that Prisma could be improved by enhancing active participation. This participant feedback will be used to further improve the intervention for an upcoming RCT. Preliminary analyses of effects showed promising results with an increase in knowledge of ASD and some indications for improvements in relationship quality, mental health, quality of life, acceptance of diagnosis and burden of care. Conclusions Overall, results indicate that the Prisma is a feasible and acceptable first-line intervention in outpatient services. Randomized controlled trials are needed to further corroborate the evidence base of this novel intervention. Trial registration Clinicaltrials.org NCT0446097, retrospectively registered July 8th 2020.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta y alguien cercano buscan información sobre autismo, apoyos y servicios, un programa grupal corto como Prisma puede ser una vía de partida; conviene preguntar si su servicio ambulatorio ofrece algo similar. La evidencia es un estudio abierto de viabilidad, sin grupo de comparación, con 92 adultos autistas con capacidad intelectual y 94 personas cercanas. Completaron el programa el 77% y el 73%, y valoraron bien las sesiones, aunque pidieron más participación activa. Los posibles beneficios, como más conocimiento sobre el autismo, son preliminares. Faltan ensayos aleatorizados y no sirve para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult and someone close to them want information about autism, support and services, a short group programme like Prisma may be a useful starting point; you could ask whether your outpatient service offers something similar. The evidence is an open feasibility study with no comparison group, including 92 intellectually able autistic adults and 94 close relations. Completion was 77% and 73%, and people rated the sessions well, though they asked for more active participation. Possible benefits, such as more knowledge about autism, are preliminary. Randomised trials are still needed, and it will not suit everyone.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen och en närstående vill ha information om autism, stöd och tjänster kan ett kort gruppprogram som Prisma vara en bra början; du kan fråga om er öppenvård erbjuder något liknande. Underlaget är en öppen genomförbarhetsstudie utan jämförelsegrupp med 92 autistiska vuxna med intellektuell förmåga och 94 närstående. Av dem slutförde 77% respektive 73% programmet, och de var nöjda med träffarna, men ville ha mer aktivt deltagande. Möjliga vinster, som ökad kunskap om autism, är preliminära. Randomiserade studier behövs, och programmet passar inte alla.

title: A narrative review of MRI changes correlated to signs and symptoms of autism.
authors: Faizo NL
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder that occurs during early childhood. The change from being normal across several contexts to displaying the behavioral phenotype of ASD occurs in infants and toddlers with autism. Findings provided by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based research owing to the developmental phase, including potential pathways underlying the pathogenesis of the condition and the potential for signs and symptomatic risk prediction. The present study focuses on the characteristic features of magnetic resonance imaging autistic brain, how these changes are correlated to autism signs and symptoms and the implications of MRI as a potential tool for the early diagnosis of ASD. PRISMA style was used to conduct this review. Research articles related to the key concepts of this review, which is looking at MRI brain changes in autistic patients, were revised and incorporated with what is known with the pathophysiology of brain regions in relation to signs and symptoms of autism. Studies on brain MRI of autism were revied for major brain features and regions such as brain volume, cortex and hippocampus. This review reveals that brain changes seen in MRI are highly correlated with the signs and symptoms of autism. There are numerous distinct features noted in an autistic brain using MRI. Based on these findings, various developmental brain paths and autistic behavior culminate in a typical diagnosis, and it is possible that addressing these trajectories would improve the accuracy in which children are detected and provide the necessary treatment.

sheet.es: Mañana por la mañana, esta investigación no cambia nada en la rutina: no hay nada que hacer en casa a partir de ella. Lo útil es saber que las imágenes cerebrales (resonancia magnética) aún se estudian como posible ayuda para detectar el autismo pronto, pero no sustituyen la valoración de profesionales. Es una revisión narrativa de estudios previos sobre resonancia magnética en personas autistas, centrada en volumen cerebral, corteza e hipocampo. Sus límites: no indica cuántas personas participaron, habla de cambios cerebrales relacionados con rasgos y no de cómo vive cada persona, y no demuestra que la resonancia sirva hoy para diagnosticar a una persona concreta.
sheet.en: Tomorrow morning, this research changes nothing in your routine: there is nothing to do at home because of it. What is useful to know is that brain scans (MRI) are still being studied as a possible aid for spotting autism early, but they do not replace assessment by professionals. It is a narrative review of earlier MRI studies of autistic people, looking at brain volume, cortex and hippocampus. Its limits: it does not say how many people took part, it describes brain differences linked to traits rather than how each person lives, and it does not show that MRI can diagnose any one person today.
sheet.sv: I morgon bitti ändrar den här forskningen ingenting i vardagen: det finns inget att göra hemma utifrån den. Det användbara är att veta att hjärnbilder (MRI) fortfarande studeras som ett möjligt stöd för att upptäcka autism tidigt, men de ersätter inte professionell utredning. Det är en berättande översikt av tidigare MRI-studier av autistiska personer, med fokus på hjärnvolym, hjärnbark och hippocampus. Begränsningar: den anger inte hur många som deltog, den beskriver hjärnskillnader kopplade till drag snarare än hur varje person lever, och den visar inte att MRI idag kan diagnostisera en enskild person.

title: Effect of prednisolone on language function in children with autistic spectrum disorder: a randomized clinical trial.
authors: Brito AR, Vairo GPT, Dias APBH, Olej B, Nascimento OJM, Vasconcelos MM
abstract: Objective To describe the effect of prednisolone on language in children with autism spectrum disorder. This study is based upon two hypotheses: autism etiology may be closely related to neuroinflammation; and, an effective treatment should restore the individual's language skills. Method This is a prospective, double-blinded, randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trial, carried out in a federal university hospital. The initial patient sample consisted of 40 subjects, which were randomized into two parallel groups. Inclusion criteria were: male gender, 3-7 years of age, and meeting the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders - 4th edition (DSM-IV) diagnostic criteria. The final sample consisted of 38 patients, of whom 20 were randomized to the placebo group and 18 to the active group. The latter received prednisolone for 24 weeks, at an initial dose of 1mg/kg/day and a tapering dose from the ninth week onward. Language was measured on four occasions over a 12-month period by applying two Brazilian tools: the Language Development Assessment (ADL) and the Child Language Test in Phonology, Vocabulary, Fluency, and Pragmatics (ABFW). Results The side effects were mild: two patients had hypertension, five had hyperglycemia, and two had varicella. Prednisolone increased the global ADL score in children younger than 5 years of age who had developmental regression (p=0.0057). The ABFW's total of communicative acts also responded favorably in those participants with regression (p=0.054). The ABFW's total of vocal acts showed the most significant results, especially in children younger than 5 years (p=0.004, power=0.913). Conclusions The benefit of prednisolone for language scores was more evident in participants who were younger than five years, with a history of developmental regression, but the trial's low dose may have limited this benefit. The observed side effects do not contraindicate corticosteroid use in autism.

sheet.es: Este estudio fue médico: probó un fármaco y no ofrece nada que aplicar en casa. Cualquier decisión sobre medicación corresponde a un profesional clínico. Mañana, lo útil es seguir apoyando la comunicación de la persona con sus formas habituales y compartir dudas con su equipo de salud. Evidencia: ensayo clínico aleatorizado con placebo en el que participaron 38 niños varones autistas de 3-7 años, con mediciones del lenguaje durante 12 meses. Límites: muestra pequeña, solo varones, un hospital, y los resultados se observaron sobre todo en ciertos subgrupos; no se puede generalizar a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: This was a medical study: it tested a drug, so it offers nothing to apply at home. Any decision about medication belongs to a clinician. Tomorrow, what helps is to keep supporting the person's communication in the ways that already work and to bring questions to their health team. Evidence: a randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trial with 38 autistic boys aged 3-7 years, with language measured over 12 months. Limits: small sample, boys only, one hospital, and results appeared mainly in certain subgroups, so it cannot be generalized to all autistic people.
sheet.sv: Detta var en medicinsk studie: den testade ett läkemedel och ger inget att använda hemma. Alla beslut om medicinering hör till en läkare. I morgon är det mest hjälpsamma att fortsätta stötta personens kommunikation på de sätt som redan fungerar och ta med frågor till vårdteamet. Evidens: en randomiserad, placebokontrollerad klinisk studie med 38 autistiska pojkar i åldern 3-7 år, där språket mättes under 12 månader. Begränsningar: litet urval, bara pojkar, ett sjukhus, och resultaten syntes mest i vissa undergrupper, så de gäller inte alla autistiska personer.

title: The effectiveness of early parental coaching in the autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Malucelli ERS, Antoniuk SA, Carvalho NO
abstract: Objective Analysis of the effectiveness of early Parental Coaching in the Autism Spectrum Disorder. Method Randomized, controlled and blinded clinical trial to analyze parent-child interaction videos. Results The sample consisted of 18 children being followed up at the Autism Outpatient Clinic of a Neuropediatric Center in southern Brazil diagnosed with Autism Spectrum Disorder, between 29 and 42 months of age, randomly allocated to two groups: the Study Group (SG; n=9), which received Parental Coaching performed by a professional certified by the Early Start Denver Model; and the Control Group (CG; n=9), which was in a routine follow-up, without treatment and training of parents by a trained professional. The parents of the SG were willing to attend weekly meetings and to apply the instructional techniques at home with their children. It took 12 weeks and an average of 2h per meeting. Conclusions The learning rate for comprehensive development skills in the Early Start Denver Model checklist, such as receptive communication, expressive communication, social capacity, imitation, cognition, games, fine motor skills, gross motor skills, behavior, and personal independence was significantly higher in the SG, as well as the strategies and the quality of interaction between parents and children. Thus, Parental Coaching presents as a possibility of early intervention in children with Autism Spectrum Disorder.

sheet.es: Si criáis a un niño autista pequeño, puede valer la pena preguntar si hay programas en los que un profesional enseñe a las familias a usar estrategias de juego e interacción en casa. Es un ensayo aleatorizado con 18 niños autistas de entre 29 y 42 meses, en el sur de Brasil. Quienes recibieron coaching parental (12 semanas, reuniones semanales) mostraron mayor ritmo de aprendizaje en la lista del Early Start Denver Model y mejor calidad de interacción que el grupo de seguimiento habitual. Es una muestra muy pequeña, de un solo centro, y no demuestra que sirva a todas las familias ni a todos los niños. Conviene valorarlo con el equipo profesional.
sheet.en: If you are raising a young autistic child, it may be worth asking whether any programmes teach families play and interaction strategies to use at home, guided by a professional. This was a randomized trial with 18 autistic children aged 29 to 42 months in southern Brazil. Those whose parents received coaching (12 weeks, weekly meetings) showed a higher learning rate on the Early Start Denver Model checklist and better parent-child interaction quality than the group in routine follow-up. The sample is very small and from one centre, so it does not show the approach suits every family or every child. Talk it over with your professional team.
sheet.sv: Om du har ett litet autistiskt barn kan det vara värt att fråga om det finns program där en professionell lär föräldrar lek- och samspelsstrategier att använda hemma. Detta var en randomiserad studie med 18 autistiska barn i åldern 29 till 42 månader i södra Brasilien. De vars föräldrar fick coachning (12 veckor, veckovisa möten) hade högre inlärningstakt på checklistan i Early Start Denver Model och bättre samspelskvalitet än gruppen med vanlig uppföljning. Urvalet är mycket litet och från ett enda centrum, så studien visar inte att metoden passar alla familjer eller alla barn. Diskutera det gärna med ert professionella team.

title: A narrative sequencing and mentalizing training for adults with autism: A pilot study.
authors: Bylemans T, Heleven E, Baetens K, Deroost N, Baeken C, Van Overwalle F
abstract: Adults diagnosed with autism experience difficulties with understanding the mental states of others, or themselves (mentalizing) and with adequately sequencing personal stories (narrative coherence). Given that the posterior cerebellum is implicated in both skills, as well as in the etiology of autism, we developed a narrative sequencing and mentalizing training for autistic adults. Participants with an official autism diagnosis were randomly assigned to a Training group ( n = 17) or a waiting-list Control group ( n = 15). The Training group took part in six weekly sessions in groups of three participants lasting each about 60 min. During training, participants had to (re)tell stories from the perspective of the original storyteller and answer questions that required mentalizing. We found significant improvements in mentalizing about others' beliefs and in narrative coherence for the Training group compared to the Control group immediately after the training compared to before the training. Almost all participants from the Training group expressed beneficial effects of the training on their mood and half of the participants reported positive effects on their self-confidence in social situations. All participants recommended the current training to others. Results are discussed in light of cerebellar theories on sequencing of social actions during mentalizing. Further improvements to the program are suggested. Our results highlight the potential clinical utility of adopting a neuroscience-informed approach to developing novel therapeutic interventions for autistic populations.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta quiere practicar cómo contar historias en orden o pensar en lo que creen otras personas, un programa breve en grupos pequeños puede ser una opción que explorar, siempre que ella quiera. Fue un estudio piloto con adultos autistas, asignados al azar a un grupo de entrenamiento (n = 17) o a una lista de espera (n = 15). El entrenamiento duró seis sesiones semanales de unos 60 minutos, en grupos de tres. El grupo de entrenamiento mejoró en comprender las creencias ajenas y en la coherencia al narrar. Es un estudio pequeño, sin seguimiento a largo plazo, y no sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult wants to practise telling stories in order or thinking about what other people believe, a short programme in small groups may be worth exploring, if they want to. This was a pilot study with autistic adults randomly assigned to a training group (n = 17) or a waiting-list group (n = 15). Training was six weekly sessions of about 60 minutes, in groups of three. The training group improved in understanding others' beliefs and in narrative coherence. The study is small, did not show long-term effects, and cannot be taken as a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen vill öva på att berätta historier i rätt ordning eller fundera på vad andra tror, kan ett kort program i små grupper vara värt att utforska, om personen själv vill det. Det var en pilotstudie med autistiska vuxna som lottades till en träningsgrupp (n = 17) eller en väntelista (n = 15). Träningen bestod av sex veckovisa tillfällen på ungefär 60 minuter, i grupper om tre. Träningsgruppen förbättrades i att förstå andras föreställningar och i sammanhang när de berättade. Studien är liten, visar inga långtidseffekter och gäller inte som regel för alla personer.

title: Stress and Anxiety Among Parents of Transition-Aged Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder: a Systematic Review of Interventions and Scales.
authors: Agarwal R, Wuyke G, Sharma U, Burke SL, Howard M, Li T, Sanchez M, Bastida E
journal: Review journal of autism and developmental disorders

title: Ageing and autism: A longitudinal follow-up study of mental health and quality of life in autistic adults.
authors: Roestorf A, Howlin P, Bowler DM
abstract: Background Poor mental health is known to adversely affect functional abilities, social isolation, and quality of life (QoL). It is, therefore, crucial to consider the long-term impacts of mental health conditions as autistic adults grow older. Objectives To explore, in a group of community-based autistic adults, the extent of: (i) autistic traits, co-occurring physical and mental health conditions; (ii) age-related differences in those conditions, and changes over time; and (iii) their impact on everyday living and QoL. Method About Sixty-eight autistic adults (aged 19-80 years) participated in the first study (T1); 49 participants from T1 took part in a follow-up at T2 (mean retest interval 2.4 years). Standardised self-report measures of autistic traits, mental health, and QoL were completed at both time points. Results Over two-thirds (71%) of autistic adult participants experienced at least one co-occurring condition, and over a third (37%) met the criteria for three or more co-occurring conditions. Mental and physical health difficulties were related to autistic traits and difficulties in everyday life and were consistent predictors of poor QoL at T1 and T2. Conclusion Mental health difficulties in autism persisted into older age and did not improve over time. These findings have important implications for mental health provision for autistic adults in older age.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista adulta o mayor, pregúntale con regularidad cómo se siente emocionalmente y de salud, y ayúdale a pedir apoyo en salud mental si lo desea; no esperes a que mejore con la edad. Es un estudio de seguimiento con adultos autistas de la comunidad (19-80 años): 68 participaron al inicio y 49 en el seguimiento, con cuestionarios de autoinforme. Halló que las dificultades de salud mental persistieron y se relacionaron con peor calidad de vida. Es un grupo pequeño y no sirve como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult or older person, check in regularly about how they feel emotionally and physically, and help them reach mental health support if they want it; don't wait for things to improve with age. This was a follow-up study of community-based autistic adults (aged 19-80): 68 took part at the start and 49 at follow-up, using self-report questionnaires. Mental health difficulties persisted and were linked to poorer quality of life. The group was small, so it is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen eller äldre person: fråga regelbundet hur hen mår psykiskt och fysiskt, och hjälp till att få kontakt med psykisk hälsovård om hen vill. Vänta inte på att det blir bättre med åldern. Det var en uppföljningsstudie med autistiska vuxna i samhället (19-80 år): 68 deltog i början och 49 vid uppföljningen, med självskattningsformulär. Psykiska svårigheter höll i sig och hängde ihop med sämre livskvalitet. Gruppen var liten, så resultaten är ingen regel för varje person.

title: From ivory tower to inclusion: Stakeholders' experiences of community engagement in Australian autism research.
authors: den Houting J, Higgins J, Isaacs K, Mahony J, Pellicano E
abstract: Autistic people, and other community stakeholders, are gaining increasing recognition as valuable contributors to autism research, resulting in a growing corpus of participatory autism research. Yet, we know little about the ways in which stakeholders practice and experience community engagement in autism research. In this study, we interviewed 20 stakeholders (academics, autistic people, family members/careers, research students, and service providers) regarding their experiences of community engagement in Australian autism research. Through reflexive thematic analysis of interview data, we generated four themes. First, our participants perceived academia as an "ivory tower," disconnected from community members' lives and priorities. Second, our participants identified that different stakeholders tended to hold different roles within their research projects: academics typically retained power and control, while community members' roles tended toward tokenism. Third, our participants spoke of the need to "bridge the gap" between academia and the community, highlighting communication, accessibility, and planning as key to conducting effective participatory research. Lastly, participants emphasized the changing nature of autism research, describing participatory research as "the way of the future." Our findings reflect both the progress achieved to date, and the challenges that lie ahead, as the field advances toward genuine co-production of autism research.

sheet.es: Si le invitan a participar en una investigación sobre autismo, pregunte qué papel tendrá realmente, cómo se comunicarán con usted y si el lugar y los materiales serán accesibles. Es razonable pedir que la planificación incluya a las personas autistas desde el inicio. Este estudio entrevistó a 20 participantes (personas académicas, autistas, familiares, estudiantes y profesionales de servicios) sobre la participación comunitaria en la investigación australiana. Describieron una academia distante de la vida de la comunidad y papeles a veces simbólicos. Aun así, veían la investigación participativa como el futuro. Son experiencias de un grupo pequeño en un solo país, y no representan a todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you are invited to take part in autism research, ask what your role will really be, how the team will communicate with you, and whether the venue and materials will be accessible. It is reasonable to ask that autistic people help plan the work from the start. This study interviewed 20 people (academics, autistic people, family members, students and service providers) about community involvement in Australian autism research. They described academia as distant from community life and community roles as sometimes tokenistic, yet saw participatory research as the way of the future. These are the views of a small group in one country and do not speak for everyone.
sheet.sv: Om du blir inbjuden att delta i autismforskning, fråga vilken roll du faktiskt får, hur forskarna kommer att kommunicera med dig och om lokalen och materialet är tillgängliga. Det är rimligt att be om att autistiska personer är med i planeringen från början. Studien intervjuade 20 personer (akademiker, autistiska personer, anhöriga, studenter och personal inom tjänster) om samverkan med samhället i australisk autismforskning. De beskrev akademin som avlägsen från människors liv och brukarrollerna som ibland symboliska, men såg deltagande forskning som framtiden. Det är erfarenheter från en liten grupp i ett enda land och gäller inte alla.

title: The Efficacy of Early Interventions for Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Daniolou S, Pandis N, Znoj H
abstract: The superiority of early interventions for children with autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) compared to treatment as usual (TAU) has recently been questioned. This study was aimed to investigate the efficacy of early interventions in improving the cognitive ability, language, and adaptive behavior of pre-school children with ASDs through a systematic review of randomized controlled trials (RCTs). In total, 33 RCTs were included in the meta-analysis using the random effects model. The total sample consisted of 2581 children (age range: 12-132 months). Early interventions led to positive outcomes for cognitive ability ( g = 0.32; 95% CI: 0.05, 0.58; p = 0.02), daily living skills ( g = 0.35; 95% CI: 0.08, 0.63; p = 0.01), and motor skills ( g = 0.39; 95% CI: 0.16, 0.62; p = 0.001), while no positive outcomes were found for the remaining variables. However, when studies without the blinding of outcome assessment were excluded, positive outcomes of early interventions only remained for daily living skills ( g = 0.28; 95% CI: 0.04, 0.52; p = 0.02) and motor skills ( g = 0.40; 95% CI: 0.11, 0.69; p = 0.007). Although early intervention might not have positive impacts on children with ASDs for several outcomes compared to controls, these results should be interpreted with caution considering the great variability in participant and intervention characteristics.

sheet.es: Si piensa en apoyos tempranos para su hijo o hija autista, puede fijarse en metas concretas del día a día, como las rutinas de autonomía y el movimiento, y observar qué le sirve a él o ella. Es un metaanálisis de 33 ensayos aleatorizados con 2581 niños y niñas de 12-132 meses. Las intervenciones tempranas mostraron mejoras en habilidades de la vida diaria y motoras; en otras áreas no se hallaron mejoras claras, y la capacidad cognitiva dejó de destacar al excluir estudios sin evaluación ciega. Los estudios eran muy distintos entre sí, así que los resultados no valen para todas las personas y deben leerse con cautela.
sheet.en: If you are considering early support for your autistic child, you could focus on concrete everyday goals, such as daily routines and movement, and watch what helps your child. This is a meta-analysis of 33 randomized trials with 2581 children aged 12-132 months. Early interventions showed improvements in daily living skills and motor skills; no clear improvements appeared in other areas, and the cognitive result no longer held when studies without blinded assessment were excluded. The studies differed a lot from one another, so the results do not apply to every person and should be read with caution.
sheet.sv: Om du funderar på tidigt stöd för ditt autistiska barn kan du utgå från konkreta vardagsmål, som rutiner och rörelse, och se vad som fungerar för just ditt barn. Det här är en metaanalys av 33 randomiserade studier med 2581 barn i åldern 12-132 månader. Tidiga insatser visade förbättringar i vardagsfärdigheter och motorik; i andra områden syntes inga tydliga förbättringar, och resultatet för kognitiv förmåga höll inte när studier utan blindad bedömning uteslöts. Studierna skilde sig mycket åt, så resultaten gäller inte alla och bör läsas med försiktighet.

title: Applied Behavior Analysis in Children and Youth with Autism Spectrum Disorders: A Scoping Review.
authors: Gitimoghaddam M, Chichkine N, McArthur L, Sangha SS, Symington V
abstract: This manuscript provides a comprehensive overview of the impact of applied behavior analysis (ABA) on children and youth with autism spectrum disorders (ASD). Seven online databases and identified systematic reviews were searched for published, peer-reviewed, English-language studies examining the impact of ABA on health outcomes. Measured outcomes were classified into eight categories: cognitive, language, social/communication, problem behavior, adaptive behavior, emotional, autism symptoms, and quality of life (QoL) outcomes. Improvements were observed across seven of the eight outcome measures. There were no included studies that measured subject QoL. Moreover, of 770 included study records, only 32 (4%) assessed ABA impact, had a comparison to a control or other intervention, and did not rely on mastery of specific skills to mark improvement. Results reinforce the need for large-scale prospective studies that compare ABA with other non-ABA interventions and include measurements of subject QoL to provide policy makers with valuable information on the impacts of ABA and other existing and emerging interventions. Supplementary information The online version contains supplementary material available at 10.1007/s40614-022-00338-x.

sheet.es: Si te ofrecen ABA para tu hijo o hija, puedes preguntar con calma: ¿cómo sabremos si mejora su bienestar y calidad de vida, no solo si domina habilidades concretas? Observa si disfruta, si se respeta su forma de comunicarse y si puede decir que no. Esta revisión de alcance analizó 770 estudios sobre ABA en niños, niñas y jóvenes autistas; muchos informaron mejoras en lenguaje, adaptación o conducta. Sus límites son importantes: ningún estudio midió la calidad de vida y solo el 4 % comparó ABA con otra intervención sin basarse en el dominio de habilidades específicas. Cada niño es distinto.
sheet.en: If ABA is offered for your child, it is fair to calmly ask: how will we know whether their wellbeing and quality of life improve, not just whether they master specific skills? Notice whether they seem to enjoy it, whether their way of communicating is respected, and whether they can say no. This scoping review looked at 770 studies of ABA with autistic children and youth; many reported gains in language, adaptive skills or behaviour. Its limits matter: no study measured quality of life, and only 4% compared ABA with another approach without relying on skill mastery. Every child is different.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn erbjuds ABA är det rimligt att lugnt fråga: hur ska vi veta om barnets välmående och livskvalitet blir bättre, inte bara om hen klarar specifika färdigheter? Lägg märke till om barnet verkar trivas, om hens sätt att kommunicera respekteras och om hen kan säga nej. Denna kartläggande översikt gick igenom 770 studier om ABA för autistiska barn och unga; många rapporterade framsteg i språk, vardagsfärdigheter eller beteende. Begränsningarna är viktiga: ingen studie mätte livskvalitet, och bara 4 % jämförde ABA med ett annat stöd utan att mäta enbart inlärda färdigheter. Varje barn är unikt.

title: The impact of early stages of COVID-19 on the mental health of autistic adults in the United Kingdom: A longitudinal mixed-methods study.
authors: Bundy R, Mandy W, Crane L, Belcher H, Belcher H, Bourne L, Brede J, Hull L, Brinkert J, Cook J
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract During the COVID-19 pandemic, high levels of depression, anxiety and stress have been reported in the general population. However, much less has been reported about the impact of COVID-19 on the mental health of autistic people. What we did: In the present study, we investigated how the mental health of autistic adults in the United Kingdom changed during the early stages of the COVID-19 pandemic. In total, 133 participants completed an online survey at two different time points. Of the 133 participants, 70 completed the survey at the first time point just before the onset of the national lockdown. This allowed us to look at changes in their mental health, from before the lockdown to 10 to 15 weeks during lockdown. All participants (133) told us about their experiences of the pandemic. What we found: While many autistic adults told us that their mental health worsened, people's experience varied. For some autistic adults, aspects of mental health (e.g. anxiety, stress) actually improved. Participants also described social changes that had occurred, at home and in the outside world. They described feelings of uncertainty during the pandemic, and discussed how the pandemic had affected some of their previous coping strategies. Participants also told us about their difficulties in accessing healthcare services and food during the early stages of the pandemic. In our article, we discuss these findings and focus on what needs to change to ensure that autistic people are better supported as the pandemic continues.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista de tu entorno atraviesa un cambio grande e inesperado, pregúntale cómo lo vive en lugar de suponerlo: las reacciones varían. Ayuda revisar juntas qué estrategias de afrontamiento siguen disponibles y cuáles hay que reemplazar, y comprobar que pueda acceder a atención sanitaria y alimentos. La evidencia es un estudio longitudinal de métodos mixtos con 133 adultos autistas del Reino Unido que respondieron una encuesta en línea; 70 la completaron también justo antes del confinamiento. Muchos empeoraron, pero en algunos la ansiedad o el estrés mejoraron. Sus límites: es un grupo pequeño, solo en el Reino Unido y en las primeras etapas de la pandemia, así que no describe a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If an autistic person in your life faces a big, unexpected change, ask how they are experiencing it rather than assuming, because reactions vary. It can help to review together which coping strategies are still available and which need replacing, and to check they can reach healthcare and food. The evidence is a longitudinal mixed-methods study of 133 autistic adults in the United Kingdom who completed an online survey; 70 also completed it just before lockdown. Many said their mental health worsened, but for some, anxiety or stress improved. Its limits: it is a small group, only in the United Kingdom and in the early stages of the pandemic, so it does not describe every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person i din närhet möter en stor, oväntad förändring, fråga hur hen upplever den i stället för att anta något, eftersom reaktionerna varierar. Det kan hjälpa att tillsammans gå igenom vilka copingstrategier som fortfarande fungerar och vilka som behöver ersättas, och att kontrollera att hen når sjukvård och mat. Underlaget är en longitudinell studie med blandade metoder på 133 autistiska vuxna i Storbritannien som besvarade en webbenkät; 70 gjorde det också strax före nedstängningen. Många uppgav att måendet försämrades, men hos vissa blev oro eller stress bättre. Begränsningar: gruppen är liten, bara från Storbritannien och från pandemins tidiga skede, så resultaten gäller inte alla autistiska personer.

title: Autistic mothers' perinatal well-being and parenting styles.
authors: Hampton S, Allison C, Aydin E, Baron-Cohen S, Holt R
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic people can have difficulties during pregnancy and after giving birth, such as difficulty getting health care that meets their needs. Autistic people may therefore have lower well-being than non-autistic people during this time. We asked autistic and non-autistic people to fill in questionnaires measuring stress, depression, anxiety and satisfaction with life. They were asked to do this once during pregnancy, once 2 to 3 months after giving birth and once 6 months after giving birth. At 6 months after giving birth, they also filled in questionnaires about parenting. The autistic parents had higher stress, depression and anxiety scores than the non-autistic parents. For both groups, scores for anxiety went down over time. There were no differences between the groups on satisfaction with their life or how confident they were as a parent. There were no differences between the groups on most areas of parenting style, although autistic parents scored lower on parenting discipline. This study suggests that autistic people may be more stressed, depressed and anxious than non-autistic people during pregnancy and after giving birth. Autistic people therefore need good quality support during this time. This study also suggests that autistic and non-autistic parents may be just as likely to parent in positive ways such as being sensitive to their baby's needs.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista durante el embarazo o el posparto, ofrece apoyo de buena calidad y revisa con ella cómo se siente, con preguntas abiertas y sin prisa. El estudio comparó con cuestionarios a personas autistas y no autistas durante el embarazo y después del parto. Las autistas tuvieron puntuaciones más altas de estrés, depresión y ansiedad, pero no hubo diferencias en satisfacción con la vida ni en confianza como madres o padres. La mayoría de los estilos de crianza fueron similares. Es un solo estudio con cuestionarios y no describe a todas las personas autistas; cada experiencia es distinta.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person during pregnancy or after birth, offer good quality support and check in about how they are feeling, with open questions and no rush. The study used questionnaires to compare autistic and non-autistic people during pregnancy and after giving birth. Autistic parents had higher stress, depression and anxiety scores, but there were no differences in satisfaction with life or confidence as a parent. Most parenting styles were similar. It is a single questionnaire-based study and does not describe every autistic person; each experience is different.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person under graviditeten eller efter förlossningen: erbjud stöd av god kvalitet och fråga öppet hur hen mår, utan stress. Studien jämförde autistiska och icke-autistiska personer med frågeformulär under graviditeten och efter förlossningen. De autistiska föräldrarna hade högre poäng för stress, depression och ångest, men det fanns ingen skillnad i livstillfredsställelse eller i självförtroende som förälder. De flesta föräldrastilar var likartade. Det är en enskild studie med frågeformulär och den beskriver inte alla autistiska personer; varje upplevelse är unik.

title: Social attention in anorexia nervosa and autism spectrum disorder: Role of social motivation.
authors: Kerr-Gaffney J, Jones E, Mason L, Hayward H, Murphy D, Loth E, Tchanturia K
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Research suggests a relationship between autism and anorexia nervosa. For example, rigid and inflexible behaviour, a preference for routine and social difficulties are seen in both conditions. In this study, we examined whether people with anorexia and people with autism show similarities in social attention (where they look while engaging in social interactions or watching a scene with people interacting). This could help us understand why people with anorexia and autism experience difficulties in social situations. Participants with either anorexia or autism, as well as participants with no mental health problems watched a video of a social scene while we recorded which parts of the scene they looked at with an eye-tracker. Participants also completed questionnaires to assess characteristics of autism. We found that autistic participants looked at faces less than typically developing participants. However, participants with anorexia did not show a similar reduction in attention to faces, contrary to our predictions. Autistic features were not related to attention in either group. The results suggest that autistic people may miss important social cues (like facial expressions), potentially contributing to social difficulties. However, this mechanism does not appear explain social difficulties in people with anorexia.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista, puede ayudar recordar que mirar menos a las caras no significa desinterés: puede que se le escapen algunas pistas sociales, como las expresiones faciales. Prueba a decir en voz alta lo que sientes o quieres, en lugar de depender solo de la cara. El estudio de investigación con personas autistas comparó, con un seguimiento ocular, a participantes con autismo, con anorexia y sin problemas de salud mental mientras veían un vídeo social. Las personas autistas miraron menos las caras; quienes tenían anorexia, no. Es un solo estudio, y no describe a todas las personas autistas ni explica por sí solo las dificultades sociales.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person, looking less at faces does not mean a lack of interest: some social cues, like facial expressions, may be missed. Try saying aloud what you feel or want, rather than relying only on your face. This research study with autistic people used eye-tracking while participants with autism, with anorexia, and with no mental health problems watched a video of a social scene. Autistic participants looked at faces less; participants with anorexia did not. It is a single study, it does not describe every autistic person, and it cannot explain social difficulties on its own.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person betyder det inte att hen saknar intresse när hen tittar mindre på ansikten: vissa sociala signaler, som ansiktsuttryck, kan missas. Försök att säga högt vad du känner eller vill, i stället för att bara förlita dig på ansiktet. Studien var forskning med autistiska personer och använde ögonspårning medan deltagare med autism, med anorexi och utan psykisk ohälsa tittade på en video av en social scen. De autistiska deltagarna tittade mindre på ansikten, det gjorde inte deltagarna med anorexi. Det är en enda studie, den beskriver inte alla autistiska personer och kan inte ensam förklara sociala svårigheter.

title: 5-day multi-session intermittent theta burst stimulation over bilateral posterior superior temporal sulci in adults with autism-a pilot study.
authors: Ni HC, Lin HY, Chen YL, Hung J, Wu CT, Wu YY, Liang HY, Chen RS, Gau SS, Huang YZ
abstract: Background Theta burst stimulation (TBS), a patterned repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) protocol with shorter simulation duration and lower stimulus intensity, could be a better protocol for individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Our study aimed to explore the impacts of intermittent TBS (iTBS) over the bilateral posterior superior temporal sulcus (pSTS) on intellectually able adults with ASD. Methods In this randomized, single-blinded, sham-controlled crossover trial, 13 adults with ASD completed iTBS for 5 consecutive days over the bilateral pSTS and inion (as a sham control) in a 16-weeks interval and in a randomly assigned order. The neuropsychological function was measured with the Wisconsin Card Sorting Test (WCST) for cognitive flexibility while the clinical outcomes were measured with both self-rate and parents-rate Autism Spectrum Quotient (AQ) before and after 5-day iTBS interventions. Results The results revealed significantly immediate effects of multi-session iTBS over the bilateral pSTS on parent-rate autistic symptoms in adults with ASD. The post-hoc analysis revealed the impacts of multi-session iTBS on cognitive flexibility were affected by baseline social-communicative impairment and baseline cognitive performance. Besides, the impacts of multi-session iTBS on clinical symptoms was affected by the concurrent psychotropic medication use and baseline autistic symptoms. Conclusions Given the caveat of the small sample size and discrepancy of multiple informants, this pilot study suggests the therapeutic potential of 5-day multi-session iTBS over the pSTS in adults with ASD. Individual factors modulating the response to rTMS should be explicitly considered in the future trial.

sheet.es: Esta es una prueba pequeña de una técnica médica de estimulación cerebral, todavía en fase piloto; no es algo que se pueda aplicar en casa. Si surge interés, la decisión corresponde a un profesional clínico. Evidencia: ensayo aleatorizado con simulación (placebo) en el que 13 adultos autistas con capacidad intelectual recibieron 5 días de estimulación en la zona objetivo y en una zona de control. Límites: la muestra es muy pequeña, las personas informantes no coincidieron del todo y la respuesta varió según factores individuales, así que no puede tomarse como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: This is a small pilot test of a medical brain-stimulation technique, not something that can be used at home. If you are curious about it, decisions belong to a clinician. Evidence: a randomized, sham-controlled crossover trial in which 13 intellectually able autistic adults received 5 days of stimulation over the target area and over a control spot. Limits: the sample was very small, the people reporting did not fully agree, and responses differed by individual factors, so it cannot be taken as a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Det här är ett litet pilotförsök med en medicinsk teknik för hjärnstimulering, inget som kan användas hemma. Om du är nyfiken är beslut en fråga för en läkare eller annan kliniker. Evidens: en randomiserad, skenkontrollerad crossover-studie där 13 autistiska vuxna med intellektuell förmåga fick 5 dagars stimulering över målområdet och över en kontrollpunkt. Begränsningar: urvalet var mycket litet, de som rapporterade var inte helt överens och svaren varierade med individuella faktorer, så resultatet gäller inte som regel för alla.

title: Saudi Expert Consensus-Based Autism Spectrum Disorder Statement: From Screening to Management.
authors: Alenezi S, Alyahya AS, AlKhalifah SM, Bakhsh HR, Alismail EH, Aldhalaan H, Alwazna T, Alzrayer N, AlSuwailem SS, Alnemary F, AlAnsari AMS, Alqulaq EI, Alyamani A, Amer YS, Albawardi IM, Albalawi WM, A
abstract: Background There is a large gap between the needs of individuals diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and the currently available services in Saudi Arabia. Services are often difficult to access, inconsistent in quality, incomplete, unsatisfactory, and costly. As such, there is a national need for expert consensus on the appropriate standards for the assessment and management of children on the autism spectrum. Methodology A guideline development group (GDC) was formed by professionals representing all related specialties and institutions involved in the management of individuals on the autism spectrum in Saudi Arabia. They met on a regular basis over 21 months. The guideline development process consisted of five steps starting from reviewing existing guidelines and ending with discussing and writing this manuscript. A formal voting process was utilized and recommendations were discussed until a consensus was reached. Results There was consensus on the following: A specialized diagnostic assessment needs to be carried out by an experienced multidisciplinary team for children referred to assess for ASD. They should be assessed for medical etiology, their behavioral history carefully reviewed, and symptoms directly observed. Longitudinal assessments are encouraged to reflect the effects of symptoms on the individual's ability to function while with their family, among peers, and in school settings. An additional formal assessment of language, cognitive, and adaptive abilities as well as sensory status is essential to complete the diagnostic process. Interventions should be individualized, developmentally appropriate, and intensive, with performance data relevant to intervention goals to evaluate and adjust interventions. Target symptoms must be identified to address and develop monitoring systems to track change. Conclusion ASD is a complex condition with widely varying clinical manifestations, thus requiring evaluation and intervention by a range of professionals working in coordination. Behavioral and environmental interventions are the key to optimal outcomes, in conjunction with medications when indicated for specific symptoms. Parental involvement in interventions is vital to sustaining therapeutic gains.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija va a ser evaluado, pida una valoración con un equipo multidisciplinario con experiencia, que observe directamente, revise la historia y evalúe lenguaje, capacidades cognitivas y adaptativas y sensorialidad. Pida también objetivos claros y datos para ajustar el apoyo, y participe usted en él. La evidencia es una revisión con consenso de profesionales de distintas especialidades de Arabia Saudí, que se reunieron durante 21 meses. Límites: refleja opiniones de expertos y el contexto saudí, no es una regla para cada persona, y las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If your child is being assessed, ask for an evaluation by an experienced multidisciplinary team that observes directly, reviews history, and looks at language, cognitive and adaptive abilities, and sensory needs. Ask for clear goals and data to adjust support, and take part in it yourself. The evidence is a review built on consensus among professionals from many specialties in Saudi Arabia, who met over 21 months. Limits: it reflects expert opinion and the Saudi context, it is not a rule for every person, and medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn ska utredas, be om en bedömning av ett erfaret multidisciplinärt team som observerar direkt, går igenom historiken och undersöker språk, kognitiva och adaptiva förmågor samt sensoriska behov. Be också om tydliga mål och data för att anpassa stödet, och delta själv. Underlaget är en översikt baserad på samsyn mellan yrkespersoner från många specialiteter i Saudiarabien, som träffades under 21 månader. Begränsningar: den speglar expertåsikter och saudisk kontext, är ingen regel för alla, och medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker.

title: Scoping Review on Play-Based Interventions in Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: López-Nieto L, Compañ-Gabucio LM, Torres-Collado L, Garcia-de la Hera M
abstract: Play as a therapeutic strategy can help to improve daily functioning in children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Play-based intervention can thus be an optimal option for treatment of this population. Our aim was to describe play-based interventions used in children and adolescents with ASD. We conducted a scoping review. A peer-reviewed literature search was conducted on PubMed, Scopus, EMBASE, Web of Science and PsycINFO databases. We included experimental studies which analyzed play-based interventions in children and adolescents with ASD, which were published in English/Spanish with full text available.
