We used three tables elaborated a priori to perform data extraction by two authors. Fifteen studies were included, mostly conducted in Australia and published during the past 10 years. Play-based intervention was categorized into three groups: new technologies, symbolic play or official techniques. Interventions lasted approximately 11 weeks, contained one weekly session of 30-60 min and were delivered by parents and teachers. Play-based interventions using new technologies were the most used. Intervention duration and number of sessions varied between articles. Further studies are needed to create play-based intervention protocols which can be implemented in clinical practice with children and adolescents with ASD, thus promoting evidence-based interventions in this field.

sheet.es: Si quiere probar el juego como apoyo, puede empezar con una sesión semanal de unos 30-60 minutos, en casa o en el aula, siguiendo los intereses de la niña, el niño o le adolescente autista. Se trata de una revisión de alcance que incluyó 15 estudios experimentales con niñez y adolescencia autista; los programas, a menudo guiados por familias y docentes, duraron aproximadamente 11 semanas y usaron tecnologías nuevas, juego simbólico o técnicas oficiales. Sus límites: la duración y el número de sesiones variaron mucho, y aún faltan protocolos claros para la práctica clínica. No es una regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you want to try play as a support, you could start with one weekly session of about 30-60 minutes, at home or in class, following the interests of the autistic child or teen. This was a scoping review of 15 experimental studies with autistic children and adolescents; programmes, often led by parents and teachers, lasted approximately 11 weeks and used new technologies, symbolic play or official techniques. Its limits: duration and number of sessions varied a lot, and clear protocols for clinical practice are still needed. It is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du vill prova lek som stöd kan du börja med en session i veckan på cirka 30-60 minuter, hemma eller i skolan, utifrån den autistiska barnets eller tonåringens intressen. Detta var en kartläggande översikt av 15 experimentella studier med autistiska barn och ungdomar; programmen, ofta ledda av föräldrar och lärare, varade ungefär 11 veckor och använde ny teknik, symbolisk lek eller officiella tekniker. Begränsningar: längd och antal sessioner varierade mycket, och tydliga protokoll för klinisk praktik saknas ännu. Det är ingen regel för alla.

title: The Mediating Effects of Alexithymia, Intolerance of Uncertainty, and Anxiety on the Relationship Between Sensory Processing Differences and Restricted and Repetitive Behaviours in Autistic Adults.
authors: Moore HL, Brice S, Powell L, Ingham B, Freeston M, Parr JR, Rodgers J
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Distress caused by sensory processing differences for autistic individuals may be reduced by repetitive behaviours (RRB), including repetitive motor (RMB) and insistence on sameness (ISB) behaviours. Intolerance of uncertainty (IU) and anxiety mediate the relationship between sensory processing and RRB in autistic children. We replicated this model in autistic adults, extending it to include alexithymia. Serial mediation, using data from 426 autistic adults, identified significant direct effects from sensory processing to RMB and ISB, and indirect effects through alexithymia-IU-anxiety for RMB, and IU alone, and alexithymia-IU for ISB. Different mechanisms may underpin RMB and ISB. Alexithymia alongside, IU and anxiety, should be considered when understanding the relationship between sensory processing and RRB, and when offering interventions to support autistic people.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista repite movimientos o necesita que todo siga igual, puede ayudar fijarse también en cómo vive los sentidos, la incertidumbre, la ansiedad y la dificultad para identificar sus emociones. Son pistas para acompañar mejor, no para frenar esas conductas. El estudio analizó datos de 426 personas autistas adultas. Encontró que los sentidos se relacionaban con las conductas repetitivas, en parte a través de la intolerancia a la incertidumbre, la ansiedad y la alexitimia, y que los movimientos repetitivos y la insistencia en la igualdad podrían tener mecanismos distintos. Sus límites: muestra relaciones, no demuestra causas, y no sirve como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If an autistic person repeats movements or needs things to stay the same, it may help to also notice how they experience their senses, uncertainty, anxiety and difficulty identifying emotions. These are clues for supporting them better, not for stopping those behaviours. The study analysed data from 426 autistic adults. It found that sensory processing was linked to repetitive behaviours, partly through intolerance of uncertainty, anxiety and alexithymia, and that repetitive movements and insistence on sameness may have different mechanisms. Its limits: it shows relationships, not proven causes, and it is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person upprepar rörelser eller behöver att saker förblir lika kan det hjälpa att också se hur personen upplever sina sinnen, osäkerhet, ångest och svårigheten att identifiera känslor. Det är ledtrådar för bättre stöd, inte för att stoppa beteendena. Studien analyserade data från 426 autistiska vuxna. Den fann att sensorisk bearbetning hängde samman med repetitiva beteenden, delvis via intolerans mot osäkerhet, ångest och alexitymi, och att repetitiva rörelser och behov av likhet kan ha olika mekanismer. Begränsningar: den visar samband, inte bevisade orsaker, och är ingen regel för alla.

title: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial of the WHO Caregiver Skills Training in Public Health Services in Italy.
authors: Salomone E, Settanni M, McConachie H, Suma K, Ferrara F, Foletti G, Salandin A, WHO CST Team, Servili C, Adamson LB
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Parents of children with ASD (N = 86; mean age 44.8 months; 67 boys) were randomized to either WHO Caregiver Skills Training (CST) delivered in public health settings in Italy or enhanced treatment-as-usual. Primary blinded outcomes were 3-months post-intervention change scores of autism severity and engagement during caregiver-child interaction. CST was highly acceptable to caregivers and feasibly delivered by trained local clinicians. Intention-to-treat analysis showed a large and significant effect on parent skills supporting joint engagement and a smaller significant effect on flow of interaction. Expected changes in child autism severity and joint engagement did not meet statistical significance. Analysis of secondary outcomes showed a significant effect on parenting stress, self-efficacy, and child gestures. Strategies to improve the effectiveness of CST are discussed.

sheet.es: Un programa breve de formación para cuidadores puede ayudarte a practicar formas de compartir la atención y jugar con tu hijo o hija autista, y quizá a sentirte más capaz. Evidencia: ensayo piloto aleatorizado con 86 familias de niños autistas (edad media 44,8 meses) en servicios públicos de salud de Italia; el programa de la OMS se comparó con la atención habitual reforzada. Las familias lo valoraron mucho y mejoraron sus habilidades de apoyo, el estrés parental, la autoeficacia y los gestos infantiles. Límites: es un estudio piloto, no mostró cambios significativos en la intensidad de los rasgos autistas ni en la atención compartida del niño, y no sirve como regla para todas las familias.
sheet.en: A short caregiver training programme may help you practise ways of sharing attention and playing with your autistic child, and may help you feel more capable. Evidence: a pilot randomized trial with 86 families of autistic children (mean age 44.8 months) in public health services in Italy, comparing the WHO programme with enhanced usual care. Families found it highly acceptable, and parent support skills, parenting stress, self-efficacy and child gestures improved. Limits: it was a pilot study, it showed no significant change in autism severity or the child's joint engagement, and it is not a rule for every family.
sheet.sv: Ett kort utbildningsprogram för vårdnadshavare kan hjälpa dig att öva sätt att dela uppmärksamhet och leka med ditt autistiska barn, och kanske att känna dig tryggare. Evidens: en randomiserad pilotstudie med 86 familjer till autistiska barn (medelålder 44,8 månader) inom offentlig hälso- och sjukvård i Italien, där WHO:s program jämfördes med förstärkt vanlig vård. Familjerna tyckte att det var mycket acceptabelt, och föräldrarnas stödjande färdigheter, föräldrastress, tilltro till egen förmåga och barnets gester förbättrades. Begränsningar: det var en pilotstudie, ingen signifikant förändring syntes i autismens svårighetsgrad eller barnets delade engagemang, och resultaten gäller inte alla familjer.

title: Medicine Insufficient Evidence for the Efficacy of Massage as Intervention for Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review.
authors: Ruan H, Eungpinichpong W, Wu H, Shen M, Zhang A
journal: Evidence-based complementary and alternative medicine : eCAM
abstract: The efficacy of massage therapy in the treatment of children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) remains unclear. This study systematically reviewed the impact of massage therapy on children with ASD according to the preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses (PRISMA) declaration guidelines. A literature search of the PubMed, Web of Science, Science Direct, Scopus, Google Scholar, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) electronic databases from inception to December 20, 2020, was conducted using the term "autistic/autism" along with one of the following terms, "massages," and "Tui na." The risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane risk of bias Tool. Eight randomized controlled trials examining the impact of massage on children with ASD were included. Interventions combining Qigong massage or Tui na with the control group treatments from once a day to twice a week, for a duration of 15-30 mins, and lasting for six weeks to five months were the main interventions. All reviewed studies reported significant improvement in children with ASD who received massage, especially in the sensory domain, and that massage in combination with control treatment was superior to control treatment alone. However, the overall quality of the available studies is poor with a high degree of heterogeneity. The majority of studies showed a high risk of bias with poor study design, inconsistency in massage protocols, and subjective outcome measures. Assessment bias was a common weakness of these studies. Therefore, there is insufficient evidence to conclude that massage is effective for ASD. Future studies should include large sample sizes, incorporate double-blind designs, employ appropriate outcome measures, and allow for long observation and follow-up periods. Furthermore, consensus must be reached on standardized treatments and additional therapies in order to provide better quality evidence for the treatment of ASD.

sheet.es: Si el masaje le resulta agradable a la persona autista, puede probarse como un momento tranquilo y sensorial, pero sin esperar resultados garantizados ni sustituir otros apoyos. Observe sus señales y pare si no lo desea. Es una revisión sistemática de 8 ensayos controlados aleatorizados con niñas y niños autistas, con masaje Qigong o Tui na añadido a otros tratamientos. Todos informaron mejoras, sobre todo sensoriales. Pero la calidad era baja, con mucho riesgo de sesgo, protocolos distintos y medidas subjetivas, así que no hay pruebas suficientes de que el masaje sea eficaz.
sheet.en: If an autistic person enjoys massage, it can be tried as a calm, sensory moment, but without expecting guaranteed results or replacing other supports. Watch their signals and stop if they don't want it. This was a systematic review of 8 randomized controlled trials with autistic children, adding Qigong massage or Tui na to other treatments. All reported improvements, mostly in the sensory area. But quality was poor, with high risk of bias, inconsistent protocols and subjective measures, so there is insufficient evidence that massage is effective.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person tycker om massage kan det prövas som en lugn, sensorisk stund, men utan att vänta sig garanterade resultat eller ersätta annat stöd. Följ personens signaler och avbryt om hen inte vill. Detta var en systematisk översikt av 8 randomiserade kontrollerade studier med autistiska barn, där Qigong-massage eller Tui na lades till andra behandlingar. Alla rapporterade förbättringar, mest på det sensoriska området. Kvaliteten var dock låg, med hög risk för bias, olika protokoll och subjektiva mått, så det finns otillräckligt med belägg för att massage är effektivt.

title: Autism and anorexia nervosa: Longitudinal prediction of eating disorder outcomes.
authors: Leppanen J, Sedgewick F, Halls D, Tchanturia K
abstract: Background Recently, elevated levels of autistic features and autism diagnoses have been reported among people with anorexia nervosa (AN). In clinical settings high levels of autistic features have been linked to more complex, highly comorbid illness presentation and poorer treatment outcome. This study aimed to examine whether autistic features predict AN symptom profile in long term. Methods Altogether 118 women with lived experience of AN completed two autism assessments at time 1, the Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule (ADOS) and the short version of the Autism Quotient (AQ10). Measures assessing AN symptom profile, including eating disorders symptoms, anxiety, depression, OCD symptoms, and Body Mass Index (BMI), were also recorded. The symptom profile measures were administered again 6 months and 2 years later. We conducted two analyses to examine the extent to which the ADOS and AQ10 scores predicted broad AN symptom profile at each three time points. Results Overall, high levels of autistic features were consistently associated with worse psychological symptoms, but not BMI, across all time points. Both the analysis using baseline ADOS scores and self-reported AQ10 scores showed similar pattern. Conclusion The present findings consolidate previously reported associations between autistic features and worse psychological outcome among people with AN. The findings also suggest that self-report measures may be sufficient for assessing the impact of autistic features on illness outcome among people with AN. Importantly, the study highlights the need for development and further investigation of neurodiversity accommodations in the treatment of AN.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista que vive con anorexia, puede ser útil pedir al equipo de tratamiento que adapte la atención a su forma de procesar el mundo: necesidades sensoriales con la comida, rutinas previsibles y comunicación clara. Más rasgos autistas se asociaron con más ansiedad, depresión y síntomas alimentarios, aunque no con el peso, así que un peso estable no siempre significa bienestar. La evidencia procede de un estudio de seguimiento durante dos años con 118 mujeres con experiencia de anorexia. Sus límites: solo participaron mujeres, muestra una asociación y no una causa, y no probó qué adaptaciones funcionan mejor.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person living with anorexia, it may help to ask the treatment team to adapt care to how they experience the world: sensory needs around food, predictable routines and clear communication. More autistic traits were linked to more anxiety, depression and eating-disorder symptoms, but not to weight, so stable weight does not always mean wellbeing. The evidence comes from a two-year follow-up study of 118 women with lived experience of anorexia. Its limits: only women took part, it shows an association rather than a cause, and it did not test which adaptations work best.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person som lever med anorexi kan det hjälpa att be behandlingsteamet anpassa vården efter hur personen upplever världen: sensoriska behov kring mat, förutsägbara rutiner och tydlig kommunikation. Fler autistiska drag hängde ihop med mer ångest, depression och ätstörningssymtom, men inte med vikt, så en stabil vikt betyder inte alltid att personen mår bra. Underlaget är en uppföljningsstudie under två år med 118 kvinnor med egen erfarenhet av anorexi. Begränsningar: bara kvinnor deltog, studien visar samband och inte orsak, och den prövade inte vilka anpassningar som fungerar bäst.

title: Daily living skills of autistic adolescents and young adults: A scoping review.
authors: Auld C, Foley KR, Cashin A
abstract: Introduction Daily living skills (DLS) are essential for an increased quality of life and autonomous living. DLS are a focus of occupational therapy practice; however, there has been no identified review of DLS acquisition in autistic adolescents or adults. A scoping review was undertaken of which the objective was to evaluate and synthesise the extent, range, and nature of research activity, and to identify research gaps in the existing literature as they relate to DLS acquisition and autistic adolescents and adults. Methods A structured search of the literature was conducted. Studies published in English between 2011 and 2021 that included a focus on the acquisition of DLS in autistic adolescents and young adults were included. The titles and abstracts of 103 records were screened, and the full text of 53 records was reviewed. These reference lists were hand searched. Following this process, 25 papers were found to meet the inclusion criteria. Results Findings indicate inconsistencies throughout the literature, with a lack of consensus on best practice methods, mediums, and/or tools to support optimal outcomes in terms of DLS acquisition for the autistic population. Themes related to (1) Generalisation of Skills Across Contexts, (2) Skill Maintenance, (3) Technology as a Teaching Method, (4) Participant and Family Perspectives, and (5) The Balance of Activities of Daily Living (ADL) and Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADL) focus in research were extracted from the reviewed literature. There is a strong consensus in the findings of the identified papers that autistic adolescents and young adults experience poorer outcomes in terms of DLS acquisition than non-autistic peers, and peers with other developmental or intellectual disabilities. Conclusion Future research is needed to fill these identified gaps and provide a clearer understanding on interventions to support optimal outcomes for autistic individuals.

sheet.es: Si apoyas a una persona autista adolescente o joven en las tareas de la vida diaria, practica cada habilidad en distintos lugares y repásala de vez en cuando, y pregúntale qué le resulta útil. Es una revisión de alcance de 25 artículos publicados entre 2011 y 2021 sobre cómo se adquieren estas habilidades. Los estudios coinciden en que a menudo se logran menos resultados que en otros grupos, pero no hay acuerdo sobre qué método o herramienta es mejor. Faltan investigaciones, y los resultados no valen para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic teenager or young adult with daily living skills, try practising each skill in different places, revisit it from time to time, and ask the person what helps. This was a scoping review of 25 papers published between 2011 and 2021 on how these skills are acquired. The studies agree that outcomes are often poorer than in other groups, but there is no consensus on which method or tool works best. More research is needed, and findings do not apply to every person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk tonåring eller ung vuxen med vardagliga färdigheter kan du öva varje färdighet på olika platser, repetera den då och då och fråga personen vad som hjälper. Detta var en kartläggande översikt av 25 artiklar publicerade mellan 2011 och 2021 om hur sådana färdigheter förvärvas. Studierna är överens om att resultaten ofta är sämre än i andra grupper, men det råder ingen enighet om vilken metod eller vilket verktyg som fungerar bäst. Mer forskning behövs, och resultaten gäller inte alla personer.

title: Gaze and social functioning associations in autism spectrum disorder: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Riddiford JA, Enticott PG, Lavale A, Gurvich C
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is characterized by significant social functioning impairments, including (but not limited to) emotion recognition, mentalizing, and joint attention. Despite extensive investigation into the correlates of social functioning in ASD, only recently has there been focus on the role of low-level sensory input, particularly visual processing. Extensive gaze deficits have been described in ASD, from basic saccadic function through to social attention and the processing of complex biological motion. Given that social functioning often relies on accurately processing visual information, inefficient visual processing may contribute to the emergence and sustainment of social functioning difficulties in ASD. To explore the association between measures of gaze and social functioning in ASD, a systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted. A total of 95 studies were identified from a search of CINAHL Plus, Embase, OVID Medline, and psycINFO databases in July 2021. Findings support associations between increased gaze to the face/head and eye regions with improved social functioning and reduced autism symptom severity. However, gaze allocation to the mouth appears dependent on social and emotional content of scenes and the cognitive profile of participants. This review supports the investigation of gaze variables as potential biomarkers of ASD, although future longitudinal studies are required to investigate the developmental progression of this relationship and to explore the influence of heterogeneity in ASD clinical characteristics. LAY SUMMARY: This review explored how eye gaze (e.g., where a person looks when watching a movie) is associated with social functioning in autism spectrum disorder (ASD). We found evidence that better social functioning in ASD was associated with increased eye gaze toward faces/head and eye regions. Individual characteristics (e.g., intelligence) and the complexity of the social scene also influenced eye gaze. Future research including large longitudinal studies and studies investigating the influence of differing presentations of ASD are recommended.

sheet.es: Mirar o no a los ojos no es algo que haya que entrenar a una persona autista: este estudio no ofrece una pauta para eso. Puede ser útil observar con curiosidad dónde mira cada persona y qué le resulta cómodo, sin exigir contacto visual. Es un metaanálisis de 95 estudios que encontró que mirar más hacia la cara y los ojos se asociaba con mejor funcionamiento social y menos síntomas de autismo; la mirada a la boca dependía del tipo de escena y del perfil cognitivo. Sus límites: muestra asociaciones, no causas, no sigue a las personas a lo largo del tiempo y no refleja la diversidad de cada persona.
sheet.en: This study gives no instruction to train an autistic person to look at eyes, and eye contact need not be demanded. A useful step is to notice, with curiosity, where a person looks and what feels comfortable to them. It is a meta-analysis of 95 studies. It found that looking more at the face and eyes was associated with better social functioning and fewer autism symptoms, while looking at the mouth depended on the type of scene and on participants' cognitive profile. Its limits: it shows associations, not causes, it does not follow people over time, and it cannot describe any one person.
sheet.sv: Studien ger ingen anvisning om att träna en autistisk person att titta på ögon, och ögonkontakt behöver inte krävas. Ett användbart steg är att nyfiket lägga märke till var personen tittar och vad som känns bekvämt. Det är en metaanalys av 95 studier. Den fann att mer blickar mot ansikte och ögon hängde ihop med bättre social funktion och färre autismsymtom, medan blick mot munnen berodde på typen av scen och deltagarnas kognitiva profil. Begränsningar: den visar samband, inte orsaker, följer inte människor över tid och kan inte beskriva en enskild person.

title: A systematic review of emotion regulation in parent-mediated interventions for autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Hendrix NM, Pickard KE, Binion GE, Kushner E
abstract: Autistic individuals are at elevated risk for difficulties with emotion regulation (ER) that emerge early in life and are associated with a range of internalizing and externalizing disorders. Existing interventions that support ER have focused on school-age autistic children and adolescents as well as adults. Proactive approaches to improving ER in early childhood are thus needed, as is understanding the approaches by which ER skills can be feasibly supported in this young population. This review summarizes how ER has been measured within parent-mediated interventions for children at or under the age of 6 years and the extent to which ER is measured concurrently with or distinctly from observable behaviors that have been referenced in existing literature as externalizing or challenging behavior. Using PsycInfo, EBSCOhost, and PubMed databases, we searched for peer-reviewed journal articles published through August 2021, that focused on the use of parent-mediated interventions targeting ER and/or challenging behavior. The systematic search resulted in 4,738 publications; following multi-stage screening, the search yielded 20 studies. Eighteen of 20 studies were designed to target challenging behavior using manualized curricula or behavior analytic methodologies and assessed child outcomes through validated caregiver rating scales and/or direct behavioral observation. One study measured changes in ER as secondary to the social communication skills that were targeted in the intervention. Only one study specifically supported ER skill development and measured changes in ER as the primary intervention outcome. Findings highlight the need for better assessment of ER outcomes within the context of parent-mediated interventions for toddlers and young autistic children.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a un niño autista pequeño, puede ayudar fijarte en cómo se siente y se calma, y no solo en lo que hace. Esta revisión sistemática buscó estudios de intervenciones en las que las madres y los padres son quienes aplican las estrategias, con niños de 6 años o menos. De 20 estudios, 18 se centraron en la conducta, y solo uno apoyó específicamente la regulación emocional y la midió como resultado principal. Límites: la revisión describe cómo se ha medido la regulación emocional, no demuestra qué funciona, y no vale igual para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you support a young autistic child, it may help to notice how they feel and settle, not only what they do. This systematic review looked at programmes where parents deliver the strategies, with children aged 6 or under. Of 20 studies, 18 targeted behaviour, and only one specifically supported emotion regulation and measured it as the main outcome. Limits: the review describes how emotion regulation has been measured, not what works best, and its findings do not apply the same way to every child.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar ett litet autistiskt barn kan det hjälpa att lägga märke till hur barnet mår och varvar ner, inte bara vad barnet gör. Den här systematiska översikten granskade program där föräldrar genomför strategierna, med barn i åldern 6 år eller yngre. Av 20 studier riktade sig 18 mot beteende, och bara en stöttade specifikt känsloreglering och mätte den som huvudresultat. Begränsningar: översikten beskriver hur känsloreglering har mätts, inte vad som fungerar bäst, och resultaten gäller inte lika för alla barn.

title: Problematic eating behaviours of autistic women-A scoping review.
authors: Schröder SS, Danner UN, Spek AA, van Elburg AA
journal: European eating disorders review : the journal of the Eating Disorders Association
abstract: Aim Eating and feeding behaviours of autistic individuals and related consequences have been mainly investigated in autistic children or in autistic adults with intellectual disabilities. Behaviours such as food selectivity or food neophobia have been shown to persist into adolescence and adulthood and are associated with aversive consequences. However, much less is known about the eating behaviours of autistic adults without intellectual disabilities, especially those of women. By means of a scoping review, we aim to assess the extent of the scientific literature on what is known about the eating behaviours of these women and the possible consequences of such eating behaviour. Method Medline, Cochrane, PubMed and PsycInfo databases were searched according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Results Five studies met the eligibility criteria and were included in this review. Autistic women not only reported high levels of eating behaviour frequently seen in autism spectrum disorders (ASD), but also high levels of disordered eating behaviour, similar to that of women with eating disorders. Conclusions Autistic women seem to exhibit high levels of eating behaviour frequently seen in ASD as well as disordered eating behaviour. Future research needs to shed light on what underlies these problematic eating behaviours, in order to help to adapt current treatment modalities to meet the unique needs of these women.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una mujer autista adulta, conviene mirar su relación con la comida con curiosidad y sin juicio: la selectividad alimentaria o el rechazo a alimentos nuevos pueden convivir con patrones parecidos a los trastornos alimentarios. Puedes preguntarle con calma qué texturas, rutinas o situaciones le resultan difíciles y, si te preocupa, buscar juntas un profesional que conozca el autismo. Esta revisión exploratoria reunió cinco estudios con mujeres autistas adultas sin discapacidad intelectual. Son pocos estudios, no explican las causas y no describen a todas las mujeres autistas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult woman, it helps to look at her relationship with food with curiosity, not judgement: food selectivity or avoiding new foods can sit alongside patterns similar to eating disorders. You might calmly ask which textures, routines or situations feel hard and, if you are worried, look together for a professional who understands autism. This scoping review brought together five studies with autistic adult women without intellectual disability. There are very few studies, they do not explain causes, and they do not describe every autistic woman.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en vuxen autistisk kvinna kan det hjälpa att se på hennes förhållande till mat med nyfikenhet, inte dömande: selektivt ätande eller att undvika ny mat kan finnas samtidigt som mönster som liknar ätstörningar. Fråga lugnt vilka konsistenser, rutiner eller situationer som känns svåra och, om du är orolig, sök tillsammans en vårdgivare som förstår autism. Denna kartläggande översikt samlade fem studier med vuxna autistiska kvinnor utan intellektuell funktionsnedsättning. Studierna är få, förklarar inte orsaker och beskriver inte alla autistiska kvinnor.

title: Increased perceived stress is negatively associated with activities of daily living and subjective quality of life in younger, middle, and older autistic adults.
authors: McQuaid GA, Weiss CH, Said AJ, Pelphrey KA, Lee NR, Wallace GL
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Few studies have examined self-reported perceived stress in autistic adults. Existing studies have included relatively small, predominantly male samples and have not included older autistic adults. Using a large autistic sample (N = 713), enriched for individuals designated female at birth (59.3%), and spanning younger, middle, and older adulthood, we examined perceived stress and its associations with independence in activities of daily living and subjective quality of life (QoL). Perceived stress for autistic adults designated male or female at birth was compared to their same birth-sex counterparts in a general population sample. In addition, within the autistic sample, effects of sex designated at birth, age, and their interaction were examined. Regression modeling examined associations between perceived stress and independence in activities of daily living and domains of subjective QoL in autistic adults, after controlling for age, sex designated at birth, and household income. Autistic adults reported significantly greater perceived stress than a general population comparison sample. Relative to autistic adults designated male at birth, those designated female at birth demonstrated significantly elevated perceived stress. Perceived stress contributed significantly to all regression models, with greater perceived stress associated with less independence in activities of daily living, and poorer subjective QoL across all domains-Physical, Psychological, Social, Environment, and Autism-related QoL. Findings are contextualized within the literature documenting that autistic individuals experience elevated underemployment and unemployment, heightened rates of adverse life events, and increased exposure to minority stress. LAY SUMMARY: This study looked at self-reported perceived stress in a large sample of autistic adults. Autistic adults reported more perceived stress than non-autistic adults. Autistic individuals designated female at birth reported higher stress than autistic individuals designated male at birth. In autistic adults, greater perceived stress is related to less independence in activities of daily living and poorer subjective quality of life.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta parece tener más dificultades con las tareas diarias, vale la pena preguntar con calma por su nivel de estrés, sin suponer pérdida de capacidades. Reducir presiones concretas (ruido, cambios imprevistos, exigencias sociales, preocupaciones económicas) y ofrecer apoyo práctico puede dar más margen para la vida diaria y el bienestar. Las mujeres autistas, en este estudio, refirieron más estrés y merecen especial atención. Evidencia: estudio con 713 adultos autistas jóvenes, de mediana edad y mayores, comparados con población general mediante cuestionarios. Límites: muestra asociación, no causa, y se basa en autoinformes; no describe a cada persona.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult seems to struggle more with daily tasks, it is worth gently asking about stress rather than assuming lost abilities. Easing concrete pressures (noise, unexpected changes, social demands, money worries) and offering practical support may free up energy for daily life and wellbeing. Autistic women in this study reported more stress and may need particular attention. Evidence: a questionnaire study of 713 younger, middle-aged and older autistic adults, compared with a general population sample. Limits: it shows an association, not cause and effect, relies on self-report, and does not describe every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen verkar få svårare med vardagssysslor kan det vara klokt att lugnt fråga om stress, i stället för att anta att förmågor gått förlorade. Att minska konkreta påfrestningar (ljud, oväntade förändringar, sociala krav, ekonomisk oro) och ge praktiskt stöd kan frigöra kraft till vardag och välmående. Autistiska kvinnor rapporterade mer stress i studien och kan behöva särskild uppmärksamhet. Evidens: enkätstudie med 713 yngre, medelålders och äldre autistiska vuxna, jämförda med ett urval ur befolkningen. Begränsningar: den visar ett samband, inte orsak, bygger på självskattning och beskriver inte varje person.

title: Sensory processing and eating behaviours in autism: A systematic review.
authors: Nimbley E, Golds L, Sharpe H, Gillespie-Smith K, Duffy F
journal: European eating disorders review : the journal of the Eating Disorders Association
abstract: Objectives The aim of this study was to assess the relationship between sensory processing and a broad range of eating behaviours across the lifespan. Methods Five electronic databases of published and unpublished quantitative studies were systematically searched, evaluated for risk of bias and synthesised according to identified eating outcomes. Results Across 25 studies, there was consistent evidence of a relationship between sensory processing and a range of eating behaviours. There was early evidence for the particular role of taste/smell sensitivities, as well as hypersensitivities, although future research is needed looking at different sensory patterns and modalities. There was also tentative evidence to suggest this relationship extends across development. Discussion Study findings are discussed in relation to implications for sensory-based eating and feeding interventions and the development of eating disorders. Methodological and conceptual limitations are discussed and suggestions for future research are made to address these limitations. A broader investigation of multi-sensory issues and clearly defined eating behaviours, including disordered eating in clinically diagnosed samples, will allow for a more comprehensive and robust understanding of the relationship between sensory processing and eating behaviours in autism.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista come de forma limitada o rechaza ciertos alimentos, vale la pena fijarse en cómo percibe el sabor, el olor, la textura y otras sensaciones, porque pueden influir en lo que come. Puede ayudar anotar qué alimentos le resultan tolerables y por qué, sin presionarla. La evidencia es una revisión sistemática de 25 estudios cuantitativos, que halló una relación consistente entre el procesamiento sensorial y distintos comportamientos alimentarios, con indicios iniciales sobre la sensibilidad al gusto y al olfato. Sus límites: faltan estudios sobre otros patrones sensoriales, las conductas alimentarias no siempre estaban bien definidas y no sirve como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If an autistic person eats a limited range of foods or avoids some, it may help to notice how taste, smell, texture and other sensations feel to them, as these may shape what they eat. You could jot down which foods are manageable and why, without pressure. The evidence is a systematic review of 25 quantitative studies, which found a consistent link between sensory processing and a range of eating behaviours, with early signs for taste and smell sensitivities. Its limits: other sensory patterns need more research, eating behaviours were not always clearly defined, and it is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person äter ett begränsat urval eller undviker vissa livsmedel kan det hjälpa att lägga märke till hur smak, lukt, konsistens och andra förnimmelser känns för personen, eftersom de kan påverka vad hen äter. Du kan notera vilka livsmedel som fungerar och varför, utan press. Underlaget är en systematisk översikt av 25 kvantitativa studier som fann ett konsekvent samband mellan sensorisk bearbetning och olika ätbeteenden, med tidiga tecken på betydelse av smak- och luktkänslighet. Begränsningar: andra sensoriska mönster behöver studeras mer, ätbeteenden var inte alltid tydligt definierade, och resultaten är ingen regel för varje person.

title: Atypical structural connectivity of language networks in autism spectrum disorder: A meta-analysis of diffusion tensor imaging studies.
authors: Li M, Wang Y, Tachibana M, Rahman S, Kagitani-Shimono K
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Patients with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) often show pervasive and complex language impairments that are closely associated with aberrant structural connectivity of language networks. However, the characteristics of white matter connectivity in ASD have remained inconclusive in previous diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) studies. The current meta-analysis aimed to comprehensively elucidate the abnormality in language-related white matter connectivity in individuals with ASD. We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Medline databases to identify relevant studies. The standardized mean difference was calculated to measure the pooled difference in DTI metrics in each tract between the ASD and typically developing (TD) groups. The moderating effects of age, sex, language ability, and symptom severity were investigated using subgroup and meta-regression analysis. Thirty-three DTI studies involving 831 individuals with ASD and 836 TD controls were included in the meta-analysis. ASD subjects showed significantly lower fractional anisotropy or higher mean diffusivity across language-associated tracts than TD controls. These abnormalities tended to be more prominent in the left language networks than in the right. In addition, children with ASD exhibit more pronounced and pervasive disturbances in white matter connectivity than adults. These results support the under-connectivity hypothesis and demonstrate the widespread abnormal microstructure of language-related tracts in patients with ASD. Otherwise, white matter abnormalities in the autistic brain could vary depending on the developmental stage and hemisphere. LAY SUMMARY: This meta-analysis explored abnormalities in white matter connectivity in language networks of individuals with ASD. Significantly reduced white matter integrity was found in all language-associated tracts in subjects with ASD compared with TD controls. In addition, structural disturbances of language networks in the autistic brain exhibit a leftward tendency, and more prominent abnormalities are observed in younger people with ASD than in adults.

sheet.es: Esta investigación no ofrece una pauta para mañana por la mañana; lo útil es recordar que las diferencias de lenguaje en una persona autista pueden tener una base en cómo se organiza su cerebro, y que apoyar su comunicación a su ritmo y con sus formas preferidas sigue siendo lo importante. Es un metaanálisis de 33 estudios de imagen cerebral, con 831 personas autistas y 836 controles sin autismo. Encontró diferencias en las vías de sustancia blanca del lenguaje, más marcadas en la izquierda y en la infancia que en adultos. Sus límites: muestra promedios de grupo, no explica a cada persona y no indica qué apoyo funciona.
sheet.en: This research gives no step for tomorrow morning; what it offers is a reminder that language differences in an autistic person may have a basis in how their brain is organised, so supporting communication at their own pace and in their preferred ways remains what matters. It is a meta-analysis of 33 brain imaging studies, with 831 autistic people and 836 non-autistic controls. It found differences in language-related white matter pathways, more marked on the left and in children than in adults. Limits: it shows group averages, cannot explain any one person, and does not say which supports work.
sheet.sv: Den här forskningen ger inget konkret steg för i morgon bitti; den påminner om att språkskillnader hos en autistisk person kan ha sin grund i hur hjärnan är organiserad, så att stötta kommunikationen i personens egen takt och på personens föredragna sätt är fortsatt det viktiga. Det är en metaanalys av 33 hjärnavbildningsstudier med 831 autistiska personer och 836 icke-autistiska kontroller. Den fann skillnader i språkrelaterade banor i vit substans, tydligare i vänster sida och hos barn än hos vuxna. Begränsningar: den visar gruppgenomsnitt, kan inte förklara en enskild person och säger inte vilket stöd som fungerar.

title: Insights on dental care management and prevention in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). What is new?
authors: Zerman N, Zotti F, Chirumbolo S, Zangani A, Mauro G, Zoccante L
abstract: Autistic subjects represent a severe concern to dentistry due to the considerable difficulty in managing their oral health, maintaining routine toothbrushing, and preventing dental and periodontal problems. The social and economic burden of managing dental care in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) children is particularly cumbersome for families and public and private health expenditure, especially when children reach the dentist following a late diagnosis with evident oral health problems. An early diagnosis of ASD helps dentists better address these children's oral health. Unfortunately, insufficient attention is paid to the training and education of general pediatricians, dentists, and dental hygienists, allowing them to get to approach the different clinical aspects of ASD. Usually, children diagnosed with ASD are scheduled for dental appointments like their neurotypical peers, whereas their needs are typically complex and personalized. Scant attention is also devoted to these patients by commercial manufacturers of dental products and devices for oral hygiene and prevention of caries and periodontal diseases, leaving parents without the support and often failing when they address the oral health of autistic children. The difficulties of oral care do not derive simply from the behavior of ASD patients, as is commonly assumed, and therefore cannot be overcome solely by the patience and attention of parents and dentists. Genetics, dietary habits, sensory impairments, and cognition disorders are other causes contributing in various degrees to the impact on the mood and psychological reactions of autistic children towards dentists. How can we prevent teeth caries, periodontal disorders, and other oral health impairments by properly managing ASD children? This manuscript gives an up-to-date overview of these problems and helps to provide good remarks.

sheet.es: Si cuidar los dientes de su hijo autista le resulta difícil, no es solo cuestión de paciencia: pueden influir los sentidos, la alimentación y otros factores. Pida citas pensadas para sus necesidades y hable con el equipo dental de lo que le resulta más difícil. La evidencia es una revisión que ofrece un panorama actualizado del tema; el resumen no indica un número de participantes. Sus límites: no prueba un método concreto, y cada persona es distinta, así que conviene adaptar las ideas con su dentista.
sheet.en: If dental care is hard for your autistic child, it is not just a matter of patience: sensory experiences, diet and other factors can play a part. Ask for appointments planned around your child's needs, and tell the dental team what is hardest. The evidence is a review giving an up-to-date overview of the topic; the abstract does not give a number of participants. Its limits: it does not test a specific method, and every person is different, so adapt the ideas together with your dentist.
sheet.sv: Om tandvård är svårt för ditt autistiska barn handlar det inte bara om tålamod: sinnesintryck, kost och andra faktorer kan spela in. Be om besök som är planerade efter ditt barns behov och berätta för tandvårdsteamet vad som är svårast. Underlaget är en översikt som ger en aktuell bild av ämnet; sammanfattningen anger inte hur många deltagare det rör sig om. Begränsningar: den testar ingen specifik metod, och alla människor är olika, så anpassa idéerna tillsammans med tandläkaren.

title: Virtual and Augmented Reality in Social Skills Interventions for Individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Scoping Review.
authors: Dechsling A, Orm S, Kalandadze T, Sütterlin S, Øien RA, Shic F, Nordahl-Hansen A
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: In the last decade, there has been an increase in publications on technology-based interventions for autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Virtual reality based assessments and intervention tools are promising and have shown to be acceptable amongst individuals with ASD. This scoping review reports on 49 studies utilizing virtual reality and augmented reality technology in social skills interventions for individuals with ASD. The included studies mostly targeted children and adolescents, but few targeted very young children or adults. Our findings show that the mode number of participants with ASD is low, and that female participants are underrepresented. Our review suggests that there is need for studies that apply virtual and augmented realty with more rigorous designs involving established and evidenced-based intervention strategies.

sheet.es: Si a tu hijo o hija autista le atrae la tecnología, la realidad virtual o aumentada puede ser una forma aceptable y cómoda de practicar situaciones sociales, siempre que respete sus intereses y su ritmo, y no sustituya el apoyo de personas de confianza. Pregunta a profesionales en qué estrategia basada en evidencia se apoya cualquier programa antes de probarlo. Esta revisión de alcance reunió 49 estudios, sobre todo con niños, niñas y adolescentes; hubo pocos con niños muy pequeños o personas adultas. Sus límites: los estudios eran pequeños, participaron pocas chicas y mujeres, y los diseños eran poco rigurosos, así que aún no sabemos con certeza qué funciona ni para quién.
sheet.en: If your autistic child enjoys technology, virtual or augmented reality may be an acceptable, comfortable way to practise social situations, as long as it follows their interests and pace and doesn't replace support from trusted people. Before trying any programme, ask professionals which evidence-based strategy it builds on. This scoping review gathered 49 studies, mostly with children and teenagers; very few included very young children or adults. Its limits: most studies were small, girls and women were underrepresented, and designs were not very rigorous, so we don't yet know clearly what works, or for whom.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn tycker om teknik kan virtuell eller förstärkt verklighet vara ett godtagbart och bekvämt sätt att öva sociala situationer, så länge det utgår från barnets intressen och tempo och inte ersätter stöd från trygga personer. Fråga yrkespersoner vilken evidensbaserad metod ett program bygger på innan ni provar det. Denna kartläggande översikt samlade 49 studier, främst med barn och tonåringar; få gällde mycket små barn eller vuxna. Begränsningar: studierna var oftast små, flickor och kvinnor var underrepresenterade och upplägget var inte särskilt rigoröst, så vi vet ännu inte säkert vad som fungerar eller för vem.

title: Implicit and Explicit Gender-Related Cognition, Gender Dysphoria, Autistic-Like Traits, and Mentalizing: Differences Between Autistic and Non-Autistic Cisgender and Transgender Adults.
authors: Kallitsounaki A, Williams DM
abstract: Evidence indicates a link between autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and gender diversity, yet this intersection remains insufficiently understood. Here, we investigated whether (1) ASD affects gender-related cognition (i.e., mental processes of perceiving and interpreting one's own gender self-concept), (2) autistic people have increased gender dysphoria and recall limited gender-typed behavior from childhood, and (3) transgender individuals have increased ASD-like traits and difficulties in mentalizing. A total of 106 non-autistic cisgender (51 birth-assigned female), 107 autistic cisgender (57 birth-assigned female), 78 non-autistic transgender (41 birth-assigned female), and 56 autistic transgender adults (27 birth-assigned female) participated in the study. The mean age of participants was 31.01 years (range = 18 to 70). Using an explicit as well as an implicit measure, for the first time, we found that ASD affected gender-related cognition only in autistic cisgender people. Sex differences were also observed in this group. Whereas autistic cisgender birth-assigned males showed a stronger implicit gender-group identification than non-autistic cisgender birth-assigned males, autistic cisgender birth-assigned females showed a weaker gender-group identification than non-autistic cisgender birth-assigned females. Furthermore, autistic cisgender people reported significantly more gender dysphoric feelings and recalled significantly less gender-typed behavior from childhood than non-autistic cisgender individuals. No difference was observed between non-autistic and autistic transgender people. We also found that relative to non-autistic cisgender individuals, both non-autistic transgender and autistic transgender people reported significantly more ASD-like traits. However, mentalizing difficulties were observed only in the latter group. This research enhances our understanding of the link between ASD and gender diversity.

title: A randomized controlled trial of everolimus for neurocognitive symptoms in PTEN hamartoma tumor syndrome.
authors: Srivastava S, Jo B, Zhang B, Frazier T, Gallagher AS, Peck F, Levin AR, Mondal S, Li Z, Filip-Dhima R, Geisel G, Dies KA, Diplock A, Eng C, Hanna R, Sahin M, Hardan A, Developmental Synaptopathies Con
abstract: PTEN hamartoma tumor syndrome (PHTS) is a complex neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) overactivity. Limited data suggest that mTOR inhibitors may be therapeutic. No placebo-controlled studies have examined mTOR inhibition on cognition and behavior in humans with PHTS with/without autism. We conducted a 6-month phase II, randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial to examine the safety profile and efficacy of everolimus (4.5 mg/m2) in individuals (5-45 years) with PHTS. We measured several cognitive and behavioral outcomes, and electroencephalography (EEG) biomarkers. The primary endpoint was a neurocognitive composite derived from Stanford Binet-5 (SB-5) nonverbal working memory score, SB-5 verbal working memory, Conners' Continuous Performance Test hit reaction time and Purdue Pegboard Test score. Forty-six participants underwent 1:1 randomization: n = 24 (everolimus) and n = 22 (placebo). Gastrointestinal adverse events were more common in the everolimus group (P < 0.001). Changes in the primary endpoint between groups from baseline to Month 6 were not apparent (Cohen's d = -0.10, P = 0.518). However, several measures were associated with modest effect sizes (≥0.2) in the direction of improvement, including measures of nonverbal IQ, verbal learning, autism symptoms, motor skills, adaptive behavior and global improvement. There was a significant difference in EEG central alpha power (P = 0.049) and central beta power (P = 0.039) 6 months after everolimus treatment. Everolimus is well tolerated in PHTS; adverse events were similar to previous reports. The primary efficacy endpoint did not reveal improvement. Several secondary efficacy endpoints moved in the direction of improvement. EEG measurements indicate target engagement following 6 months of daily oral everolimus. Trial Registration Information: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02991807 Classification of Evidence: I.

sheet.es: Este fue un estudio médico sobre un fármaco, así que las decisiones sobre tratamientos corresponden siempre a un profesional clínico. Si su familiar tiene síndrome de tumor hamartomatoso PTEN, puede llevar este resumen a la consulta y preguntar qué opciones y apoyos existen. Evidencia: ensayo aleatorizado con placebo de 6 meses, con 46 participantes de 5-45 años. El resultado principal no mostró mejoría entre grupos, y los efectos digestivos fueron más frecuentes con el fármaco. Límites: muestra pequeña y corta duración, algunas medidas secundarias apuntaron a mejoría modesta, y los resultados no valen para todas las personas.
sheet.en: This was a medical study of a drug, so decisions about treatment belong to a clinician. If your family member has PTEN hamartoma tumor syndrome, you can bring this summary to an appointment and ask what options and supports are available. Evidence: a 6-month randomized, placebo-controlled trial with 46 participants aged 5-45 years. The main outcome showed no clear improvement between groups, and gastrointestinal side effects were more common with the drug. Limits: the sample was small and the follow-up short, some secondary measures pointed to modest improvement, and results do not apply to every person.
sheet.sv: Detta var en medicinsk studie av ett läkemedel, så beslut om behandling hör hemma hos en läkare. Om din närstående har PTEN-hamartomtumörsyndrom kan du ta med dig den här sammanfattningen till ett besök och fråga vilka alternativ och stöd som finns. Evidens: en 6 månader lång randomiserad, placebokontrollerad studie med 46 deltagare i åldern 5-45 år. Det primära resultatet visade ingen tydlig förbättring mellan grupperna, och mag-tarmbiverkningar var vanligare med läkemedlet. Begränsningar: litet urval och kort uppföljning, vissa sekundära mått pekade på måttlig förbättring, och resultaten gäller inte för alla.

title: Efficacy of auricular plaster therapy for sleep disorders in preschool children with autism spectrum disorders: Study protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
authors: Duan D, He L, Chen H, Lei Y, Wu W, Li T
abstract: Background Children with autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) suffer from sleep disorders to a considerable degree; however, there is no safe and effective treatment available in clinical practice. The objective of the trial is to assess the clinical effectiveness of auricular plaster therapy (APT) in treating sleep disorders in children with ASD. Method This is a single-center, patient-assessor blind, randomized controlled trial. A total of 44 preschool children with sleep disorders with ASD will be included in this study. Eligible participants will be randomly assigned to either the auricular plaster group or the sham auricular plaster group in a 1:1 ratio. Participants in the different groups will receive APT or sham APT, respectively, for a total of 30 sessions over 30 days. The primary outcome includes the Children's Sleep Habits Questionnaire (CSHQ), while secondary outcomes include the Autism Behavior Checklist (ABC) and polysomnography (PSG) for total sleep time, sleep latency, awakening duration, and sleep structures. The CSHQ and ABC will be assessed at baseline, 10, 20, 30, 60, 90, and 120 days after randomization, whereas PSG will be assessed at baseline and 30 days after randomization. The follow-up period will be scheduled to be 60, 90, and 120 days after randomization. Discussion The results of this study may provide evidence of the efficacy of APT, as well as offer new alternatives for the treatment of sleep disorders in children with ASD. Trial registration CHiCTR.org.cn (ChiCTR2100048257). Registered on July 5, 2021.

sheet.es: Por ahora no hay resultados que aplicar: este estudio solo describe un plan. Si el sueño de su hijo o hija autista le preocupa, puede anotar horarios de sueño y despertares y comentarlo con su pediatra o profesional de salud antes de probar tratamientos nuevos. Se trata del protocolo de un ensayo aleatorizado que evaluará un tratamiento con parches en la oreja frente a parches simulados en 44 niños y niñas autistas de edad preescolar con problemas de sueño. Aún no informa de resultados, así que no sabemos si funciona ni si es seguro, y lo que se halle quizá no sirva para todas las personas.
sheet.en: There are no results to act on yet: this paper only describes a plan. If your autistic child's sleep worries you, you can note bedtimes and night wakings and discuss them with a paediatrician or health professional before trying new treatments. It is the protocol of a randomized trial that will compare ear plaster therapy with sham plaster in 44 autistic preschool children with sleep problems. It reports no results yet, so we do not know whether it works or is safe, and whatever is found may not apply to every child.
sheet.sv: Det finns ännu inga resultat att använda: artikeln beskriver bara en plan. Om ditt autistiska barns sömn oroar dig kan du anteckna läggtider och nattliga uppvaknanden och ta upp det med barnläkare eller annan vårdpersonal innan du prövar nya behandlingar. Det är ett protokoll för en randomiserad studie som ska jämföra öronplåster med låtsasplåster hos 44 autistiska förskolebarn med sömnproblem. Inga resultat redovisas ännu, så vi vet inte om det fungerar eller är säkert, och det som hittas gäller kanske inte alla barn.

title: Recent Advances of Telepractice for Autism Spectrum Disorders in Speech and Language Pathology.
authors: Christopoulou M, Drosos K, Petinou K
abstract: Telepractice or teletherapy is defined as the means of service delivery via technology-based platforms that allow long-distance interventions across populations, age spans, and geographical locations. Specifically, telepractice capitalizes on communication technologies such as online modules, videoconferencing, and computerized software programs, in servicing populations with communication challenges. Notably, telepractice has emerged as a potentially effective, low-cost, and promising means of conducting and completing online assessment, diagnosis, and intervention sessions for individuals with autism spectrum disorders (ASD). Moreover, telepractice allows the inclusion of parents, caregivers, and educators as potential facilitators in supporting treatment delivery in populations with ASD. This thematic review article aims to highlight and acquaint practitioners and other stakeholders with relatively recent information regarding the advantages and disadvantages of the telepractice service delivery model in ASD. Furthermore, the emergence of the COVID-19 pandemic has impacted service delivery in the field of Health Sciences including speech and language pathology (SLP). Consequently, the need to avoid face-to-face therapy sessions, recommended to SLPs as to all health practitioners, resulted in the call for adaptation and adjustment of service telepractice. This paper attempts to answer this call by suggesting supplementing traditional diagnostic and therapy resources with training modules consisting of online materials and use of animated and specially designed programs in SLP intervention with individuals with ASD. Lastly, the paper includes a discussion of research findings in the field, a conclusion, and a take-home message.

sheet.es: Si el acceso a logopedia es difícil por distancia, coste o salud, pregunte a su logopeda si ofrece sesiones por videollamada y cómo podría usted participar como apoyo durante ellas. Esta es una revisión temática que resume información reciente sobre la telepráctica en logopedia con personas autistas; el resumen no indica cuántos estudios incluye ni quiénes participaron. Describe ventajas y desventajas, y la presenta como una opción potencialmente eficaz y de bajo coste, no como una solución probada para todas las personas. Cada persona autista tiene necesidades y preferencias propias, y lo que funciona por pantalla en un caso puede no servir en otro.
sheet.en: If getting to speech and language therapy is hard because of distance, cost or health, ask your therapist whether they offer video sessions and how you could take part as a support during them. This is a thematic review summarising recent information on telepractice in speech and language pathology with autistic people; the abstract does not say how many studies it covers or who took part. It describes advantages and disadvantages, and presents telepractice as a potentially effective, low-cost option, not a proven answer for everyone. Every autistic person has their own needs and preferences, and what works on a screen for one person may not suit another.
sheet.sv: Om det är svårt att ta sig till logopedi på grund av avstånd, kostnad eller hälsa kan du fråga din logoped om det går att ha videosessioner och hur du kan delta som stöd under dem. Detta är en tematisk översikt som sammanfattar aktuell information om telepraktik inom logopedi med autistiska personer; sammanfattningen anger inte hur många studier som ingår eller vilka som deltog. Den beskriver fördelar och nackdelar och presenterar telepraktik som ett möjligen effektivt och billigt alternativ, inte som en bevisad lösning för alla. Varje autistisk person har egna behov och preferenser, och det som fungerar via skärm för en kanske inte passar en annan.

title: Language and Speech Characteristics in Autism.
authors: Vogindroukas I, Stankova M, Chelas EN, Proedrou A
abstract: The aim of this paper is to provide information regarding diversity in speech and language profiles of individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASD) and try to classify these profiles according to the combination of the communication difficulties. Research findings confirm the existence of heterogeneity of communication challenges in ASD across the lifespan. A lot of children with ASD experience communication challenges and strengths across all language sub-systems including pragmatics, grammar, semantics, syntax, phonology, and morphology in both oral and written language, while some children with autism demonstrate exceptional language abilities incl. linguistic creativity. Communication issues vary on a continuum of severity so that some children may be verbal, whereas others remain non-verbal or minimally-verbal. The diversity of profiles in speech and language development stem from either the presence of comorbid factors, as a core symptom of autistic behavior without comorbidity or both, with the development of complex clinical symptoms. Difficulties with the semantic aspect of language affect the individual's skills in abstract thinking, multiple meanings of words, concept categorization, and so on. Finally, the coexistence of ASD with other communication difficulties such as a Language Disorder, Apraxia of Speech, Speech Sound Disorders or/and other neurodevelopmental disorders raises the need for examining more carefully the emergence of new clinical profiles and clinical markers useful in performing differential diagnosis and different intervention.

sheet.es: Mañana, no asuma que el lenguaje de una persona autista sigue un patrón único: observe con calma qué comunica bien (palabras, gestos, escritura, otros medios) y dónde necesita apoyo, y comparta esas observaciones con el logopeda. La evidencia es una revisión de investigaciones sobre perfiles de habla y lenguaje en personas autistas a lo largo de la vida. Señala mucha diversidad: fortalezas y dificultades en distintas áreas del lenguaje, algunas personas con habilidades lingüísticas excepcionales y otras con poco lenguaje oral o sin él. Sus límites: es una revisión general, no prueba ninguna intervención y no sirve para clasificar a una persona concreta. Cada perfil es individual.
sheet.en: Tomorrow, don't assume an autistic person's language follows one pattern: notice calmly what they communicate well (words, gestures, writing, other means) and where they need support, and share those observations with a speech-language professional. The evidence is a review of research on speech and language profiles in autistic people across the lifespan. It points to great diversity: strengths and difficulties in different areas of language, some people with exceptional language abilities and others with little or no spoken language. Its limits: it is a general review, it does not test any intervention, and it cannot classify one particular person. Every profile is individual.
sheet.sv: I morgon: anta inte att en autistisk persons språk följer ett enda mönster. Lägg märke till vad personen uttrycker bra (ord, gester, skrift, andra sätt) och var stöd behövs, och berätta det för en logoped. Underlaget är en översikt av forskning om tal- och språkprofiler hos autistiska personer genom livet. Den visar stor variation: styrkor och svårigheter inom olika delar av språket, vissa med exceptionella språkliga förmågor och andra med lite eller inget talat språk. Begränsningar: det är en allmän översikt, den prövar ingen insats och kan inte avgöra något om en enskild person. Varje profil är individuell.

title: Feeding and Swallowing Issues in Autism Spectrum Disorders.
authors: Adams SN
abstract: Children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) often experience difficulties related to communication and behaviour. However, their feeding issues are most distressing to their families and healthcare professionals as they impact on the children's adaptive function and health. In comparison to typically developing children, those with ASD experience significantly more feeding difficulties. Children with ASD may display distinctive feeding difficulties and atypical feeding behaviours that include picky eating, limited independent feeding, need for increased feeding times, and a highly restrictive food repertoire. Many of these feeding difficulties continue into childhood, persist in adolescence, and even spill over into adulthood. This proves to be a formidable challenge, as feeding is an essential component for healthy nutrition, growth, and development. This article will highlight how particular food items that are eaten and preferred by affected children may be contributing to their exhibited feeding difficulties. Next, it will be shown how the children's restrictive diets supplant more healthy food options. When this is combined with the children's noted reduced physical activity, the consequences are especially serious, as they include not only malnutrition but also give rise to childhood obesity. In sum, it will be demonstrated that feeding difficulties in young children with ASD are not well understood nor managed. The dearth of knowledge about feeding issues in this population affects both assessment choices and, specifically, management practices - aspects that will be elaborated on in this article. Conclusions will include suggested future directions for enhancing and complementing knowledge of these issues for stakeholders.

sheet.es: Si comer es difícil para tu hijo autista, no estás solo y no es un fallo tuyo. Anota qué alimentos acepta, cuánto tarda en las comidas y si come solo, y comparte esas notas con su pediatra o un profesional de la alimentación. Ofrecer tiempo extra puede ayudar. La evidencia es una revisión de la literatura sobre niños autistas, que describe selectividad, dietas muy restringidas y más tiempo para comer, a veces hasta la adolescencia y la edad adulta. Sus límites: no es un estudio nuevo con participantes, indica que estos problemas se conocen y se manejan poco, y no sirve como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If mealtimes are hard for your autistic child, you are not alone and it is not your failing. Note which foods they accept, how long meals take and whether they feed themselves, then share those notes with their paediatrician or a feeding professional. Allowing extra time may help. The evidence is a review of the literature on autistic children, describing picky eating, very restricted diets and longer feeding times, sometimes continuing into adolescence and adulthood. Its limits: it is not a new study with participants, it says these difficulties are poorly understood and managed, and it cannot be applied as a rule to every person.
sheet.sv: Om måltiderna är svåra för ditt autistiska barn är du inte ensam, och det är inte ditt fel. Anteckna vilka livsmedel barnet accepterar, hur lång tid måltiderna tar och om barnet äter själv, och dela anteckningarna med barnläkaren eller en matexpert. Extra tid kan hjälpa. Underlaget är en översikt av litteraturen om autistiska barn, som beskriver kräsenhet, mycket begränsad kost och längre måltider, ibland ända in i tonåren och vuxenlivet. Begränsningar: det är ingen ny studie med deltagare, den säger att svårigheterna är dåligt förstådda och hanterade, och den gäller inte som regel för varje person.

title: Virtual reality technology enhances the cognitive and social communication of children with autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Zhao J, Zhang X, Lu Y, Wu X, Zhou F, Yang S, Wang L, Wu X, Fei F
abstract: Objective We aimed to explore the impact of using virtual reality technology to intervene in and encourage the developmental behavior areas of cognition, imitation, and social interaction in children with autism spectrum disorder. Methods Forty-four children with autism spectrum disorder were divided randomly into an intervention group and a control group, with each group consisting of 22 participants. Incorporating conventional rehabilitation strategies, virtual reality technology was used with the intervention group to conduct rehabilitation training in areas including cognition, imitation, and social interaction. The control group was provided conventional/routine clinical rehabilitation training. The children's cognitive development was evaluated before and 3 months after intervention. Results After intervention, the developmental abilities of both groups of children in the areas of cognition, imitation, and social interaction were improved over their abilities measured before the intervention ( P P Conclusion Combining virtual reality with conventional rehabilitation training improved the cognitive and social development of children with autism spectrum disorder and supported the goal of improving the rehabilitation effect.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija autista tiene sesiones de rehabilitación, puede preguntar al equipo si la realidad virtual podría complementarlas, siempre según los gustos y la comodidad de la persona. Se trata de un ensayo con 44 niños autistas, repartidos al azar en dos grupos de 22: uno recibió realidad virtual además de la rehabilitación habitual y el otro solo la habitual. Se evaluó antes y 3 meses después. Ambos grupos mejoraron en cognición, imitación e interacción social, y los autores concluyen que sumar la realidad virtual ayudó. Es un grupo pequeño, el resumen no detalla las diferencias, y no sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If your autistic child has rehabilitation sessions, you could ask the team whether virtual reality might be added, always guided by what your child enjoys and tolerates. This was a trial with 44 autistic children, randomly split into two groups of 22: one had virtual reality on top of usual rehabilitation, the other had usual rehabilitation only. They were assessed before and 3 months after. Both groups improved in cognition, imitation and social interaction, and the authors conclude that adding virtual reality helped. The group was small, the abstract gives no detail on the differences, and the results are not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn har rehabiliteringsträning kan du fråga teamet om virtuell verklighet kan läggas till, alltid utifrån vad barnet tycker om och klarar av. Studien var en randomiserad prövning med 44 autistiska barn, fördelade slumpmässigt på två grupper om 22: en fick virtuell verklighet utöver vanlig rehabilitering, den andra bara vanlig rehabilitering. De bedömdes före och 3 månader efter. Båda grupperna förbättrades i kognition, imitation och social interaktion, och författarna menar att virtuell verklighet som tillägg hjälpte. Gruppen var liten, sammanfattningen beskriver inte skillnaderna närmare, och resultaten är ingen regel för alla.

title: Autism as emergent and transactional.
authors: Green J
abstract: The current epistemology of autism as a phenotype derives from the consistency of historical accounts and decades of work within the tradition of descriptive epidemiology, culminating in current categorical descriptions within DSM and ICD nosologies and the concept of "prototypical autism." The demonstrated high heritability of this phenotype has led to an essentialist theory of autism as a biological entity and the concerted search within the developmental brain and genetic science for discrete biological markers. This search has not revealed simple markers explaining autistic outcomes and has led to moves towards a more dimensional account. This article proposes an alternative transactional approach. It proposes to understand autistic states as an emergent property within a complex developmental system; as the neurodivergent brain, and mind and body, encounter their social and physical environment within early development. Key evidence in support of this approach comes from random allocation intervention trials based on such transactional development theory, both in the infancy pre-diagnostic prodrome and the early post-diagnostic period. In replicated evidence, these intervention trials show that a targeted alteration in the quality of social transactional environment available for the child leads to significant, predictable, and sustained alterations in the outcome dimensional autistic phenotype over time; and further, in one prodromal trial, to a significant reduction in later categorical classification status. The inference from this evidence is that the prototypical autistic phenotype is to a degree malleable with a changed experienced social environment and that it is emergent from its constituent traits. Such a transactional approach enlarges our notion of the phenotype and brings the study of autism within mainstream individual difference developmental science. It challenges essentialist views, for instance as to intrinsic autistic "social avoidance" or theory of mind empathy deficits, integrates dimensional and categorical perspectives, and is consistent with the lived experience of autistic people and their advocacy for improved understanding within a social model.

sheet.es: Cómo responde el entorno social importa: la forma en que nos relacionamos con un niño autista puede ser tan relevante como sus rasgos. Mañana, puede observar qué ritmos de interacción, qué apoyos y qué clase de respuestas le resultan cómodos, y adaptar su entorno a eso. La evidencia es una revisión teórica que propone entender el autismo como algo que emerge del encuentro entre el niño y su entorno, apoyada en ensayos de intervención con asignación aleatoria en la infancia temprana. Sus límites: es una propuesta conceptual, no un método para aplicar tal cual, y no significa que el autismo deba cambiarse ni que las familias sean responsables de él. Cada persona es distinta.
sheet.en: How the social environment responds matters: the way we interact with an autistic child may be as relevant as their traits. Tomorrow, you can notice which interaction rhythms, supports and responses feel comfortable for them, and adapt their surroundings accordingly. The evidence is a review that proposes understanding autism as emerging from the encounter between the child and their environment, drawing on randomised intervention trials in early childhood. Its limits: it is a conceptual proposal, not a method to apply as written, and it does not mean autism should be changed or that families are responsible for it. Every person is different.
sheet.sv: Hur den sociala miljön svarar spelar roll: sättet vi samspelar med ett autistiskt barn kan vara lika viktigt som barnets egna drag. I morgon kan du lägga märke till vilka samspelsrytmer, stöd och reaktioner som känns trygga för barnet och anpassa miljön efter det. Underlaget är en översikt som föreslår att autism uppstår i mötet mellan barnet och omgivningen, och som bygger på randomiserade interventionsstudier i tidig barndom. Begränsningar: det är ett teoretiskt förslag, inte en metod att följa rakt av, och det betyder inte att autism bör ändras eller att familjer bär ansvaret. Varje person är olika.

title: Supporting peer engagement for low-income preschool students with autism spectrum disorder during academic instruction: A pilot randomized trial.
authors: Panganiban JL, Shire SY, Williams J, Kasari C
