sheet.sv: Om du erbjuds en studie eller ett program för familjer är det rimligt att fråga hur det passar er kultur, ert språk och era rutiner, och vilket stöd som finns för att kunna fortsätta. Detta är en systematisk översikt av 68 artiklar med experimentella upplägg om interventioner via föräldrar, med barn som har eller riskerar psykisk ohälsa, inte bara autistiska barn. Den sökte sätt att rekrytera och behålla olika familjer. Begränsningar: den bygger på forskning med andra grupper och visar inte vilken strategi som fungerar bäst, så den är vägledning, inte en regel för varje familj.

title: Non-suicidal self-injury and its relation to suicide through acquired capability: investigating this causal mechanism in a mainly late-diagnosed autistic sample.
authors: Moseley RL, Gregory NJ, Smith P, Allison C, Cassidy S, Baron-Cohen S
abstract: Background Non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) has been linked with a higher risk of suicide attempts in autistic and non-autistic people. In the general population, NSSI may confer acquired capability for suicide by eroding one's fear and avoidance of pain and death. The present study aimed to explore acquired capability as the mediator of increased suicide risk conferred by NSSI in autistic and non-autistic adults. Methods Autistic and non-autistic adults (n = 314, n = 312) completed an online survey exploring lifetime suicide attempts, experience with NSSI, and acquired capability for suicide. We explored relationships between lifetime incidence of NSSI and lifetime suicide attempts via three facets of acquired capability (pain tolerance, reduced fear of death, and mental rehearsal of suicide). In self-harming participants (224 autistic and 156 non-autistic), we explored whether particular types and features of NSSI might be especially associated with capability and through that with suicide: namely engagement in scratching, cutting, and self-hitting, and engaging in more numerous forms of NSSI. Results While a higher frequency of NSSI was associated with all three facets of acquired capability, only reduced fear of death and mental rehearsal of suicide mediated an indirect relationship with lifetime suicide attempts. NSSI also directly predicted more numerous suicide attempts. Autistic people tended towards reduced fear of death and mental rehearsal regardless of NSSI status. Among self-harming autistic and non-autistic participants, cutting and an increased number of NSSI behaviours were associated with lifetime suicide attempts directly and indirectly via acquired capability. In both groups, self-hitting was associated with lifetime suicide attempts only via acquired capability. Limitations Our cross-sectional methodology negates inferences of directionality. While we controlled for age, our samples were poorly matched, with the autistic group two times older on average. The autistic sample, predominantly late-diagnosed, female and highly qualified, were unrepresentative of the whole autistic community. Conclusions Our data suggest that acquired capability, as measured herein, is an incomplete explanation for the association between NSSI and suicide risk. A broader construct with stable and transient facets may offer greater explanatory power, but it is probable that other variables explain or provide additional means through which this association arises.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista que se autolesiona, tómalo como una señal que merece atención y apoyo, no como un castigo. Pregúntale con calma cómo está y qué necesita. Un estudio con 314 adultos autistas y 312 no autistas, mediante una encuesta en línea, halló que la autolesión sin intención suicida se relacionaba con más intentos de suicidio, en parte por menos miedo a la muerte y por ensayar mentalmente el suicidio. Es un estudio transversal, así que no muestra qué causa qué; los grupos diferían bastante en edad y la muestra autista, sobre todo diagnosticada tarde, no representa a toda la comunidad. Busca ayuda profesional: un clínico, un servicio de salud o un servicio de crisis. Si hay peligro inmediato, llama al número de emergencias de tu país.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person who self-injures, treat it as a sign they deserve attention and support, not as something to punish. Ask calmly how they are and what they need. A study with 314 autistic and 312 non-autistic adults, using an online survey, found that non-suicidal self-injury was linked with more suicide attempts, partly through less fear of death and mental rehearsal of suicide. It was a cross-sectional study, so it cannot show what causes what; the groups differed a lot in age, and the mostly late-diagnosed autistic sample does not represent the whole community. Please seek professional help: a clinician, a health service or a crisis service. If there is immediate danger, call the emergency number of your country.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person som skadar sig själv, se det som ett tecken på att hen behöver uppmärksamhet och stöd, inte som något att straffa. Fråga lugnt hur hen mår och vad hen behöver. En studie med 314 autistiska och 312 icke-autistiska vuxna, via en enkät på nätet, fann att självskada utan suicidavsikt hängde ihop med fler suicidförsök, delvis genom mindre rädsla för döden och mental inövning av självmord. Studien var tvärsnittsbaserad och kan därför inte visa vad som orsakar vad; grupperna skilde sig mycket i ålder, och det mest sent diagnostiserade urvalet representerar inte hela den autistiska gemenskapen. Sök professionell hjälp: en läkare, en vårdcentral eller en krisjour. Vid akut fara, ring ditt lands nödnummer.

title: Pivotal Response Treatment with and without robot-assistance for children with autism: a randomized controlled trial.
authors: van den Berk-Smeekens I, de Korte MWP, van Dongen-Boomsma M, Oosterling IJ, den Boer JC, Barakova EI, Lourens T, Glennon JC, Staal WG, Buitelaar JK
abstract: Pivotal response treatment (PRT) is a promising intervention focused on improving social communication skills in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Since robots potentially appeal to children with ASD and may contribute to their motivation for social interaction, this exploratory randomized controlled trial (RCT) was conducted comparing PRT (PRT and robot-assisted PRT) with treatment-as-usual (TAU). Seventy-three children (PRT: n = 25; PRT + robot: n = 25; TAU: n = 23) with ASD, aged 3-8 years were assessed at baseline, after 10 and 20 weeks of intervention, and at 3-month follow-up. There were no significant group differences on parent- and teacher-rated general social-communicative skills and blindly rated global functioning directly after treatment. However, at follow-up largest gains were observed in robot-assisted PRT compared to other groups. These results suggest that robot-assistance may contribute to intervention efficacy for children with ASD when using game scenarios for robot-child interaction during multiple sessions combined with motivational components of PRT. This trial is registered at https://www.trialregister.nl/trial/4487 ; NL4487/NTR4712 (2014-08-01).

sheet.es: Si piensa en apoyar la comunicación social de un niño autista pequeño, puede preguntar a los profesionales por enfoques basados en la motivación, como el Pivotal Response Treatment, y por el uso de juegos, incluso con un robot. Fue un ensayo controlado aleatorizado exploratorio con 73 niños autistas de 3-8 años, que comparó este enfoque con y sin robot con la atención habitual. Justo después del tratamiento no hubo diferencias significativas entre grupos; a los 3 meses, las mayores mejoras se vieron en el grupo con robot. Es un estudio exploratorio y pequeño, y no demuestra que sirva a cada niño.
sheet.en: If you are thinking about supporting a young autistic child's social communication, you could ask professionals about motivation-based approaches such as Pivotal Response Treatment, and about game-based activities, including with a robot. This was an exploratory randomized controlled trial with 73 autistic children aged 3-8 years, comparing this approach with and without a robot against treatment-as-usual. Right after treatment there were no significant group differences; at 3-month follow-up, the largest gains were in the robot-assisted group. The study is exploratory and small, and it does not show this will work for every child.
sheet.sv: Om du funderar på att stödja en ung autistisk barns sociala kommunikation kan du fråga yrkespersoner om motivationsbaserade metoder som Pivotal Response Treatment och om spelbaserade aktiviteter, även med en robot. Det var en explorativ randomiserad kontrollerad studie med 73 autistiska barn i åldern 3-8 år, som jämförde metoden med och utan robot mot vanlig behandling. Direkt efter behandlingen fanns inga signifikanta skillnader mellan grupperna; vid uppföljningen efter 3 månader sågs de största förbättringarna i robotgruppen. Studien är explorativ och liten, och visar inte att det fungerar för varje barn.

title: The cost-effectiveness of treatments for attention deficit-hyperactivity disorder and autism spectrum disorder in children and adolescents: a systematic review.
authors: Sampaio F, Feldman I, Lavelle TA, Skokauskas N
abstract: Economic evaluations can help decision makers identify what services for children with neurodevelopmental disorders provide best value-for-money. The aim of this paper is to review the best available economic evidence to support decision making for attention deficit-hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in children and adolescents. We conducted a systematic review of economic evaluations of ADHD and ASD interventions including studies published 2010-2020, identified through Econlit, Medline, PsychINFO, and ERIC databases. Only full economic evaluations comparing two or more options, considering both costs and consequences were included. The quality of the studies was assessed using the Drummond checklist. We identified ten studies of moderate-to-good quality on the cost-effectiveness of treatments for ADHD and two studies of good quality of interventions for ASD. The majority of ADHD studies evaluated pharmacotherapy (n = 8), and two investigated the economic value of psychosocial/behavioral interventions. Both economic evaluations for ASD investigated early and communication interventions. Included studies support the cost-effectiveness of behavioral parenting interventions for younger children with ADHD. Among pharmacotherapies for ADHD, different combinations of stimulant/non-stimulant medications for children were cost-effective at willingness-to-pay thresholds reported in the original papers. Early intervention for children with suspected ASD was cost-effective, but communication-focused therapy for preschool children with ASD was not. Prioritizing more studies in this area would allow decision makers to promote cost-effective and clinically effective interventions for this target group.

sheet.es: Si valoras apoyos para una niña o un niño autista, este estudio ayuda a pensar en el coste, pero no dice qué es mejor para tu hijo o hija. Conviene preguntar qué apoyos están disponibles y qué objetivos tienen. Es una revisión sistemática de evaluaciones económicas publicadas entre 2010 y 2020, con 2 estudios sobre autismo, ambos de intervenciones tempranas y de comunicación. La intervención temprana en niños con sospecha de autismo resultó rentable; una terapia centrada en la comunicación en preescolares no. Los límites: hay muy pocos estudios y el coste no mide el bienestar ni las preferencias de la persona. Las decisiones médicas corresponden a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If you are weighing supports for an autistic child, this study can help you think about cost, but it cannot say what is best for your child. It helps to ask what supports are available and what goals they have. It is a systematic review of economic evaluations published 2010-2020, with 2 studies on autism, both on early and communication interventions. Early intervention for children with suspected autism was cost-effective; a communication-focused therapy for preschool children was not. Limits: there are very few studies, and cost does not measure wellbeing or the person's own preferences. Medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om du överväger stöd för ett autistiskt barn kan den här studien hjälpa dig att tänka på kostnad, men den säger inte vad som är bäst för just ditt barn. Det kan hjälpa att fråga vilket stöd som finns och vilka mål det har. Det är en systematisk översikt av ekonomiska utvärderingar publicerade 2010-2020, med 2 studier om autism, båda om tidiga insatser och kommunikationsinsatser. Tidig insats för barn med misstänkt autism var kostnadseffektiv; en kommunikationsinriktad terapi för förskolebarn var det inte. Begränsningar: det finns mycket få studier, och kostnad mäter inte välbefinnande eller personens egna önskemål. Medicinska beslut hör till en kliniker.

title: Vocational Outcomes in ASD: An Examination of Work Readiness Skills as well as Barriers and Facilitators to Employment Identified by Autistic Adults.
authors: Lee NR, McQuaid GA, Grosman HE, Jayaram S, Wallace GL
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders

title: Preliminary efficacy of cognitive-behavioral therapy on emotion regulation in adults with autism spectrum disorder: A pilot randomized waitlist-controlled study.
authors: Kuroda M, Kawakubo Y, Kamio Y, Yamasue H, Kono T, Nonaka M, Matsuda N, Kataoka M, Wakabayashi A, Yokoyama K, Kano Y, Kuwabara H
abstract: Previous studies have demonstrated the clinical utility of cognitive-behavioral therapy in improving emotion regulation in children on the autism spectrum. However, no studies have elucidated the clinical utility of cognitive-behavioral therapy in improving emotion regulation in autistic adults. The aim of the present pilot study was to explore the preliminary clinical utility of a group-based cognitive-behavioral therapy program designed to address emotion regulation skills in autistic adults. We conducted a clinical trial based on a previously reported protocol; 31 participants were randomly allocated to the intervention group and 29 to the waitlist control group. The intervention group underwent an 8-week program of cognitive-behavioral therapy sessions. Two participants from the intervention group withdrew from the study, leaving 29 participants (93.5%) in the group. Compared with the waitlist group, the cognitive-behavioral therapy group exhibited significantly greater pre-to-post (Week 0-8) intervention score improvements on the attitude scale of the autism spectrum disorder knowledge and attitude quiz (t = 2.21, p = 0.03, d = 0.59) and the difficulty describing feelings scale of the 20-item Toronto Alexithymia Scale (t = -2.07, p = 0.04, d = -0.57) in addition to pre-to-follow-up (Week 0-16) score improvements on the emotion-oriented scale of the Coping Inventory for Stressful Situations (t = -2.14, p = 0.04, d = -0.59). Our study thus provides preliminary evidence of the efficacy of the group-based cognitive-behavioral therapy program on emotion regulation in autistic adults, thereby supporting further evaluation of the effectiveness of the cognitive-behavioral therapy program in the context of a larger randomized clinical trial. However, the modest and inconsistent effects underscore the importance of continued efforts to improve the cognitive-behavioral therapy program beyond current standards.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista adulta quiere trabajar sus emociones, un programa grupal de terapia cognitivo-conductual puede ser una opción que explorar con un profesional, que decidirá si encaja con sus necesidades. Es un ensayo piloto aleatorizado: 31 personas autistas adultas hicieron un programa de 8 semanas y 29 esperaron en lista. El grupo del programa mejoró algo más en describir sentimientos y en una escala de afrontamiento centrada en las emociones. Los efectos fueron modestos e irregulares, la muestra es pequeña y no sabemos si servirá a cada persona. Hacen falta estudios más grandes.
sheet.en: If an autistic adult wants support with emotions, a group cognitive-behavioural therapy programme may be an option to explore with a professional, who can judge whether it fits their needs. This was a pilot randomised trial: 31 autistic adults took an 8-week programme and 29 waited on a list. The programme group improved somewhat more on describing feelings and on an emotion-focused coping scale. Effects were modest and inconsistent, the sample was small, and we cannot say it will help every person. Larger studies are needed.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk vuxen vill ha stöd med sina känslor kan ett gruppbaserat program med kognitiv beteendeterapi vara ett alternativ att utforska med en yrkesperson, som kan bedöma om det passar behoven. Det var en randomiserad pilotstudie: 31 autistiska vuxna deltog i ett åttaveckorsprogram och 29 stod i kö. Programgruppen förbättrades något mer när det gällde att beskriva känslor och på en känslofokuserad copingskala. Effekterna var måttliga och ojämna, urvalet litet, och vi kan inte säga att det hjälper alla. Större studier behövs.

title: Randomised Controlled Trial of a Behavioural Sleep Intervention, 'Sleeping Sound', for Autistic Children: 12-Month Outcomes and Moderators of Treatment.
authors: Pattison E, Papadopoulos N, Fuller-Tyszkiewicz M, Sciberras E, Hiscock H, Williams K, McGillivray J, Mihalopoulos C, Bellows ST, Marks D, Howlin P, Rinehart N
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders

title: Caregiver perspectives on barriers and facilitators to primary care for autistic adults: A qualitative study.
authors: Stein Duker LI, Goodman E, Pomponio Davidson A, Mosqueda L
abstract: Background Primary care is associated with greater access to healthcare services and improved health outcomes. However, autistic adults report challenges accessing and utilizing primary care, in addition to unmet healthcare needs. The need to minimize existing barriers and identify strategies to facilitate successful healthcare encounters is increasingly important as autistic adults represent a growing segment of society. Minimal research has examined primary healthcare encounters for this population. Methods As part of a larger convergent parallel design mixed-methods study that recruited autistic adults, caregivers of autistic adults, and primary care providers treating autistic adults, interviews were conducted with 31 caregivers of autistic adults. Caregivers were predominantly female (94%), and the autistic adult they cared for were primarily male (87%), with a mean age of 24 years. Thematic analysis was employed to elucidate the barriers to care, suggestions to mitigate challenges, and/or successful strategies implemented during care encounters for autistic adults, as reported by their caregivers. Results Reported here are the results only from the caregiver interviews, in which seven themes emerged: (1) finding a primary care provider; (2) patient-provider communication; (3) anxiety due to unpredictability, an overstimulating sensory environment, and waiting time; (4) participation of consumers in the healthcare process; (5) stigma and assumptions about autism; (6) caregiver experiences; and (7) the impact of culture and ethnicity on care. Conclusion Findings from this study have the potential to inform the development of, or improve existing, client-centered interventions to improve primary healthcare services for autistic adults.

sheet.es: Antes de la cita, piense en lo que suele generar ansiedad: lo impredecible, los ruidos o luces y la espera. Puede preguntar qué ajustes ofrece la consulta, avisar de la comunicación que funciona mejor y asegurarse de que la persona autista participe en las decisiones sobre su salud. Es un estudio cualitativo con entrevistas a 31 cuidadores de personas autistas adultas; surgieron siete temas, como encontrar profesional, comunicación, ansiedad, estigma y cultura. Se basa en lo que cuentan los cuidadores, no las propias personas autistas, casi todos eran mujeres y no sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: Before an appointment, think about what tends to raise anxiety: unpredictability, noise or bright lights, and waiting. You can ask what adjustments the clinic offers, explain which communication works best, and make sure the autistic adult takes part in decisions about their own health. This was a qualitative study with interviews of 31 caregivers of autistic adults; seven themes emerged, including finding a provider, communication, anxiety, stigma and culture. It reflects caregivers' views rather than those of autistic adults themselves, most were women, and it is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Fundera före besöket på vad som brukar öka oron: det oförutsägbara, ljud eller starkt ljus och väntetiden. Du kan fråga vilka anpassningar mottagningen erbjuder, berätta vilken kommunikation som fungerar bäst och se till att den autistiska vuxna är delaktig i besluten om sin egen hälsa. Det var en kvalitativ studie med intervjuer av 31 anhöriga till autistiska vuxna; sju teman framkom, bland annat att hitta vårdgivare, kommunikation, oro, stigma och kultur. Den speglar anhörigas syn, inte de autistiska vuxnas egen, de flesta var kvinnor, och den gäller inte som regel för alla.

title: The Challenges of Establishing Healthcare Services in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: The Case of Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASD) in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq-Report from the Field.
authors: Samadi SA
abstract: The present report from the field tries to present challenges associated with establishing healthcare services for individuals with autism spectrum disorders (ASD) in a low- and middle-income area. The given case that has been highlighted is establishing daycare services focusing on rehabilitation and training services for individuals with ASD, and their caregivers and family members, in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq (KRI). Based on my experience, the associated challenges are divided into three primary levels: personal, professional, and organizational. The report highlights the importance of understanding the challenges associated with establishing healthcare services with the desire to put them under control. Plus, understanding the cultural aspects of the healthcare services for individuals with ASD experiences to address the issues at each level shared. It is concluded in the final part of the report that the key to establishing healthcare quality is to understand attitudes toward healthcare at the personal, professional, and organizational levels. This attitude determines the expectation from the services and defines assistance-seeking behaviors. Results offer insight for stakeholders in the healthcare field, allowing for a better understanding and improvement of availability and access to quality-driven healthcare services. A pre- and in-service training approach is practiced to address the associated challenges of establishing healthcare services at the personal level in KRI. A similar policy might be applicable in other LMICs, where there is a lack of professional and skillful healthcare service providers.

sheet.es: Si buscas apoyo para una persona autista en un lugar con pocos recursos, ayuda saber que las actitudes hacia la atención influyen en lo que esperas de los servicios y en cómo pides ayuda. Conviene preguntar qué ofrece cada servicio y cómo forma a su personal. La evidencia es un informe de campo, basado en la experiencia de su autor al crear servicios de día para personas autistas y sus familias en la región del Kurdistán de Irak. Sus límites: es una experiencia personal, no un estudio con participantes, y no sirve como regla para todas las familias ni todos los lugares.
sheet.en: If you are looking for support for an autistic person where resources are limited, it helps to know that attitudes toward care shape what you expect from services and how you ask for help. It is worth asking what a service offers and how it trains its staff. The evidence is a field report based on the author's own experience setting up daycare services for autistic people and their families in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq. Its limits: it is one person's experience, not a study with participants, and it is not a rule for every family or place.
sheet.sv: Om du söker stöd för en autistisk person där resurserna är små kan det hjälpa att veta att attityder till vård påverkar vad man förväntar sig av tjänster och hur man söker hjälp. Det är värt att fråga vad en verksamhet erbjuder och hur personalen utbildas. Underlaget är en fältrapport baserad på författarens egen erfarenhet av att starta dagverksamhet för autistiska personer och deras familjer i Kurdistanregionen i Irak. Begränsningar: det är en persons erfarenhet, inte en studie med deltagare, och det gäller inte som regel för alla familjer eller platser.

title: Effect of Longitudinal Practice in Real and Virtual Environments on Motor Performance, Physical Activity and Enjoyment in People with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Prospective Randomized Crossover Controlled Trial.
authors: Moraes ÍAP, Lima JA, Silva NM, Simcsik AO, Silveira AC, Menezes LDC, Araújo LV, Crocetta TB, Voos MC, Tonks J, Silva TD, Dawes H, Monteiro CBM
journal: International journal of environmental research and public health
abstract: (1) Background: People with ASD commonly present difficulty performing motor skills and a decline in physical activity (PA) level and low enjoyment of PA. We aimed to evaluate whether longitudinal practice of an activity in virtual and real environments improves motor performance and whether this improvement is transferred to a subsequent practice when changing the environment, promoting PA and providing enjoyment; (2) Methods: People with ASD, aged between 10 and 16 years, were included and distributed randomly into two opposite sequences. The participants performed a 10 session protocol, with five sessions practicing in each environment (virtual or real). Heart rate measurement was carried out and an enjoyment scale was applied; (3) Results: 22 participants concluded the protocol. Sequence A (virtual first) presented an improvement in accuracy and precision and transferred this when changing environment; they also had a greater change in heart rate reserve. The majority of participants reported "fun" and "great fun" levels for enjoyment; (4) Conclusions: The virtual reality activity presented a higher level of difficulty, with greater gains in terms of transference to the real environment. Considering PA, our task provided very light to light activity and the majority of participants enjoyed the task.

sheet.es: Si quiere probar una actividad motriz con una persona autista, puede empezar con una versión de realidad virtual y después pasar a la real, y preguntarle cuánto disfruta. Es un ensayo aleatorizado cruzado con 22 participantes autistas de entre 10 y 16 años que completaron 10 sesiones, cinco en cada entorno. El grupo que empezó en virtual mejoró en exactitud y precisión y mantuvo esa mejora al pasar al entorno real. La mayoría describió la tarea como "divertida" o "muy divertida". La actividad fue de intensidad muy ligera a ligera. El grupo fue pequeño y no se puede asumir que sirva para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you want to try a movement activity with an autistic person, you could start with a virtual reality version, move on to the real one, and ask how much they enjoy it. This was a randomized crossover trial with 22 autistic participants aged 10 to 16 who completed 10 sessions, five in each environment. The group that started in virtual improved in accuracy and precision and kept that gain when moving to the real environment. Most described the task as "fun" or "great fun". The activity was very light to light in intensity. The group was small, so it cannot be assumed to suit everyone.
sheet.sv: Om du vill prova en rörelseaktivitet med en autistisk person kan du börja med en virtual reality-version, gå vidare till den verkliga och fråga hur roligt det är. Det var en randomiserad crossover-studie med 22 autistiska deltagare mellan 10 och 16 år som genomförde 10 pass, fem i varje miljö. Gruppen som började virtuellt förbättrade sin träffsäkerhet och precision och behöll förbättringen när miljön byttes till den verkliga. De flesta beskrev uppgiften som "rolig" eller "jätterolig". Aktiviteten hade mycket låg till låg intensitet. Gruppen var liten, så resultatet kan inte antas passa alla.

title: Efficacy of psychosocial interventions for Autism spectrum disorder: an umbrella review.
authors: Gosling CJ, Cartigny A, Mellier BC, Solanes A, Radua J, Delorme R
abstract: Introduction The wide range of psychosocial interventions designed to assist people with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) makes it challenging to compile and hierarchize the scientific evidence that supports the efficacy of these interventions. Thus, we performed an umbrella review of published meta-analyses of controlled clinical trials that investigated the efficacy of psychosocial interventions on both core and related ASD symptoms. Methods Each meta-analysis that was identified was re-estimated using a random-effects model with a restricted maximum likelihood estimator. The methodological quality of included meta-analyses was critically appraised and the credibility of the evidence was assessed algorithmically according to criteria adapted for the purpose of this study. Results We identified a total of 128 meta-analyses derived from 44 reports. More than half of the non-overlapping meta-analyses were nominally statistically significant and/or displayed a moderate-to-large pooled effect size that favored the psychosocial interventions. The assessment of the credibility of evidence pointed out that the efficacy of early intensive behavioral interventions, developmental interventions, naturalistic developmental behavioral interventions, and parent-mediated interventions was supported by suggestive evidence on at least one outcome in preschool children. Possible outcomes included social communication deficits, global cognitive abilities, and adaptive behaviors. Results also revealed highly suggestive indications that parent-mediated interventions improved disruptive behaviors in early school-aged children. The efficacy of social skills groups was supported by suggestive evidence for improving social communication deficits and overall ASD symptoms in school-aged children and adolescents. Only four meta-analyses had a statistically significant pooled effect size in a sensitivity analysis restricted to randomized controlled trials at low risk of detection bias. Discussion This umbrella review confirmed that several psychosocial interventions show promise for improving symptoms related to ASD at different stages of life. However, additional well-designed randomized controlled trials are still required to produce a clearer picture of the efficacy of these interventions. To facilitate the dissemination of scientific knowledge about psychosocial interventions for individuals with ASD, we built an open-access and interactive website that shares the information collected and the results generated during this umbrella review. Pre-registration PROSPERO ID CRD42020212630.

sheet.es: Si buscas apoyos, puedes explorar las intervenciones con parte de la familia, las de desarrollo y los grupos de habilidades sociales, y valorar con la persona autista si encajan con sus metas y su ritmo. La evidencia viene de una revisión de revisiones: reunió 128 metaanálisis de 44 informes sobre intervenciones psicosociales. Hubo indicios sugerentes en niñez preescolar (comunicación social, conductas adaptativas) y en grupos de habilidades sociales en edad escolar y adolescencia. Sus límites: solo cuatro metaanálisis seguían siendo significativos en el análisis con ensayos aleatorizados de bajo riesgo de sesgo, y hacen falta más ensayos bien diseñados. No es una regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you are looking for supports, you could explore parent-mediated approaches, developmental approaches and social skills groups, and check with the autistic person whether they fit their goals and pace. The evidence is an umbrella review: it gathered 128 meta-analyses from 44 reports on psychosocial interventions. There were suggestive signs in preschool children (social communication, adaptive behaviours) and for social skills groups in school-aged children and adolescents. Limits: only four meta-analyses stayed statistically significant in the analysis restricted to randomized trials at low risk of detection bias, and more well-designed trials are needed. This is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du söker stöd kan du utforska föräldramedierade insatser, utvecklingsinriktade insatser och sociala färdighetsgrupper, och stämma av med den autistiska personen om de passar mål och tempo. Underlaget är en översikt av översikter: den samlade 128 metaanalyser från 44 rapporter om psykosociala insatser. Det fanns vägledande tecken hos förskolebarn (social kommunikation, adaptiva beteenden) och för sociala färdighetsgrupper hos skolbarn och tonåringar. Begränsningar: bara fyra metaanalyser var fortsatt statistiskt signifikanta när analysen begränsades till randomiserade studier med låg risk för bias, och fler väl utformade studier behövs. Detta är ingen regel för alla.

title: Parental experience of an early developmental surveillance programme for autism within Australian general practice: a qualitative study.
authors: Eapen V, Winata T, Gilbert M, Nair R, Khan F, Lucien A, Islam R, Masi A, Lam-Cassettari C, Mendoza Diaz A, Dissanayake C, Karlov L, Descallar J, Eastwood J, Hasan I, Jalaludin B, Kohlhoff J, Liaw ST,
abstract: Objectives Implementing support and services early in the life course has been shown to promote positive developmental outcomes for children at high likelihood of developmental conditions including autism. This study examined parents'/caregivers' experiences and perceptions about a digital developmental surveillance pathway for autism, the autism surveillance pathway (ASP), and usual care, the surveillance as usual (SaU) pathway, in the primary healthcare general practice setting. Design This qualitative study involves using a convenience selection process of the full sample of parents/caregivers that participated in the main programme, 'General Practice Surveillance for Autism', a cluster-randomised controlled trial study. All interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed and coded using NVivo V.12 software. An inductive thematic interpretive approach was adopted and data were analysed thematically. Participants Twelve parents/caregivers of children with or without a developmental condition/autism (who participated in the main programme) in South Western Sydney and Melbourne were interviewed. Settings All interviews were completed over the phone. Results There were seven major themes and 20 subthemes that included positive experiences, such as pre-existing patient-doctor relationships and their perceptions on the importance of knowing and accessing early support/services. Barriers or challenges experienced while using the SaU pathway included long waiting periods, poor communication and lack of action plans, complexity associated with navigating the healthcare system and lack of understanding by general practitioners (GPs). Common suggestions for improvement included greater awareness/education for parents/carers and the availability of accessible resources on child development for parents/caregivers. Conclusion The findings support the use of digital screening tools for developmental surveillance, including for autism, using opportunistic contacts in the general practice setting. Trial registration number ANZCTR (ACTRN12619001200178).

sheet.es: Si le preocupa el desarrollo de su hijo o hija, hable con su médico de cabecera y pida por escrito un plan con los pasos siguientes y los plazos. Este estudio cualitativo, dentro de un ensayo aleatorizado, entrevistó por teléfono a 12 madres, padres o cuidadores en Australia. Valoraron la relación previa con su médico y saber pronto qué apoyos existen. Señalaron esperas largas, poca comunicación, falta de planes de acción y un sistema difícil de navegar. Pidieron más información y recursos accesibles. Es una muestra muy pequeña, así que no sirve como regla para todas las familias.
sheet.en: If you have questions about your child's development, talk with your family doctor and ask for a written plan with the next steps and timeframes. This qualitative study, part of a randomised trial, interviewed 12 parents or caregivers by phone in Australia. They valued an existing relationship with their doctor and knowing early what support exists. They described long waits, poor communication, no action plans and a healthcare system that was hard to navigate. They asked for more information and accessible resources. The sample is very small, so it is not a rule for every family.
sheet.sv: Om du undrar över ditt barns utveckling kan du prata med din husläkare och be om en skriftlig plan med nästa steg och tidsramar. Den här kvalitativa studien, en del av en randomiserad studie, intervjuade 12 föräldrar eller vårdnadshavare per telefon i Australien. De värderade en befintlig relation till läkaren och att tidigt få veta vilket stöd som finns. De beskrev långa väntetider, bristande kommunikation, avsaknad av handlingsplaner och en svårnavigerad sjukvård. De efterfrågade mer information och lättillgängliga resurser. Urvalet är mycket litet, så det är ingen regel för alla familjer.

title: Microglia: Synaptic modulator in autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Hu C, Li H, Li J, Luo X, Hao Y
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by variable impairment of social communication and repetitive behaviors, highly restricted interests, and/or sensory behaviors beginning early in life. Many individuals with ASD have dysfunction of microglia, which may be closely related to neuroinflammation, making microglia play an important role in the pathogenesis of ASD. Mounting evidence indicates that microglia, the resident immune cells of the brain, are required for proper brain function, especially in the maintenance of neuronal circuitry and control of behavior. Dysfunction of microglia will ultimately affect the neural function in a variety of ways, including the formation of synapses and alteration of excitatory-inhibitory balance. In this review, we provide an overview of how microglia actively interact with neurons in physiological conditions and modulate the fate and functions of synapses. We put a spotlight on the multi-dimensional neurodevelopmental roles of microglia, especially in the essential influence of synapses, and discuss how microglia are currently thought to influence ASD progression.

sheet.es: Este estudio no ofrece nada que cambiar mañana por la mañana en casa; sirve para entender mejor la investigación sobre el cerebro autista. Es una revisión que reúne trabajos sobre las microglías, células inmunitarias del cerebro, y cómo interactúan con las neuronas y las sinapsis. Según la revisión, en muchas personas autistas las microglías podrían funcionar de otra manera, aunque es una hipótesis en estudio. Límites: no es un ensayo con participantes, no explica a cada persona y no indica qué hacer en la vida diaria. Cualquier duda médica debe consultarse con un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: This study offers nothing to change at home tomorrow morning; it helps you understand research on the autistic brain. It is a review that gathers work on microglia, the brain's immune cells, and how they interact with neurons and synapses. According to the review, many autistic people may have differences in how microglia work, but this is still an idea being explored. Limits: it is not a trial with participants, it does not explain every person, and it gives no guidance for daily life. Any medical questions belong with a clinician.
sheet.sv: Den här studien ger inget att ändra hemma i morgon bitti; den hjälper dig att förstå forskningen om den autistiska hjärnan. Det är en översikt som samlar studier om mikroglia, hjärnans immunceller, och hur de samspelar med nervceller och synapser. Enligt översikten kan mikroglia fungera annorlunda hos många autistiska personer, men det är fortfarande en idé under utforskning. Begränsningar: den är inte en studie med deltagare, förklarar inte varje person och ger ingen vägledning för vardagen. Medicinska frågor hör hemma hos en läkare eller annan kliniker.

title: An exploratory study on emotion regulation strategy use in individuals with Williams syndrome, autism spectrum disorder and intellectual disability.
authors: Samson AC, Sokhn N, Van Herwegen J, Dukes D
abstract: Background Individuals with neurodevelopmental disorders often have atypical emotion profiles, but little is known about how they regulate their emotions. While several studies have examined emotion regulation strategy use in autism spectrum disorder (ASD), only a few have included individuals with intellectual disability (ID) or focused on specific syndromes such as Williams syndrome (WS). Methods A parent-reported survey launched during the first months of the COVID-19 pandemic allowed to exploratorily study emotion regulation strategy use and its link to anxiety in individuals with ASD with (N=785) and without ID (N=596), WS (N=261), and Intellectual Disability not otherwise specified (N=649). Results Using multilevel analyses, besides revealing specific group differences in emotion regulation strategy use, a variety of strategies (e.g., rumination, avoiding information, repetitive behaviors) were found to be linked to elevated levels of anxiety, while focusing on the positive was linked to lower anxiety levels in all groups. Moreover, only autistic people without ID used humor more frequently while experiencing lower anxiety levels. Conclusion This study sheds light on an underexplored area of emotion regulation strategy use in different neurodevelopmental disorders. It also paves the way to further examine emotion regulation in more rigorous ways to better understand emotion regulation in different neurodevelopmental disorders as well as the impact on outcome measures such as anxiety. This exploratory study may help to develop and validate adequate measures to study a broad array of ER strategies used by individuals with neurodevelopmental disorders.

sheet.es: Observe qué estrategias usa la persona para calmarse y apoye las que le ayudan, como centrarse en lo positivo o, si le gusta, el humor. Si aparecen rumiación, evitar información o conductas repetitivas, no las corrija: pueden indicar ansiedad y conviene preguntar qué necesita. Evidencia: encuesta exploratoria respondida por familias de personas autistas con discapacidad intelectual (N=785) y sin ella (N=596), con síndrome de Williams (N=261) y con discapacidad intelectual no especificada (N=649). Límites: es un estudio exploratorio basado en informes de los padres y muestra asociaciones, no causas; no sirve como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: Notice which strategies the person uses to settle themselves, and support the ones that help, such as focusing on the positive or, if they enjoy it, humour. If rumination, avoiding information or repetitive behaviours appear, don't stop them; they may go with anxiety, so ask what the person needs. Evidence: an exploratory survey completed by parents of autistic people with intellectual disability (N=785) and without (N=596), people with Williams syndrome (N=261) and people with intellectual disability not otherwise specified (N=649). Limits: it is exploratory, relies on parent reports and shows links, not causes, so it is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Lägg märke till vilka strategier personen använder för att varva ner och stötta de som hjälper, som att fokusera på det positiva eller, om hen tycker om det, humor. Om grubbel, att undvika information eller repetitiva beteenden dyker upp, avbryt inte; de kan höra ihop med oro, så fråga vad personen behöver. Evidens: en explorativ enkät besvarad av föräldrar till autistiska personer med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning (N=785) och utan (N=596), personer med Williams syndrom (N=261) och personer med ospecificerad intellektuell funktionsnedsättning (N=649). Begränsningar: studien är explorativ, bygger på föräldrarnas rapporter och visar samband, inte orsaker, och är ingen regel för alla.

title: "Autism research is in crisis": A mixed method study of researcher's constructions of autistic people and autism research.
authors: Botha M, Cage E
abstract: Introduction While not all autism research is ableism, autism researchers can be ableist, including by talking about autistic people in sub-human terms (dehumanization), treating autistic people like objects (objectification), and making othering statements which set autistic people apart from non-autistic people, and below in status (stigmatization). Method This mixed-method study aimed to investigate how autism researchers construct autistic people and autism research, and to investigate whether including autistic people more in research relates to lower ableism in narratives about autistic people. We used a survey with autism researchers ( N = 195) asking five open-ended questions about autism and autism research, as well as demographics, career length, contact with autistic people (familial and non-familial) and degree to which researchers involve autistic people in their research. We used content analysis to categorize narratives used by autism researchers and cues for ableism (dehumanization, objectification, and stigmatization). We then used binary-logistic regression to identify whether narrative or higher inclusion of autistic people predicted fewer ableist cues, controlling for career length and connections to autistic people. Results and discussion Using medicalized narratives of autism predicted higher odds of ableist cues compared to employing social model or neutral embodiment narratives. Greater inclusion of autistic people in research predicted significantly lower odds of ableist cues, while controlling for other contact with autistic people and career length. Next, we used reflexive thematic analysis to analyze researcher's perceptions of autistic people and autism research. Narratives reflected core ideological disagreements of the field, such as whether researchers consider autism to be an intrinsic barrier to a good life, and whether researchers prioritize research which tackles "autism" versus barriers to societal inclusion for autistic people. Instrumentality (a form of objectification) was key to whether researchers considered a person to have social value with emphasis revolving around intellectual ability and independence. Lastly, language seemed to act as a tool of normalization of violence. Researchers relied on an amorphous idea of "autism" when talking about prevention or eradication, potentially because it sounds more palatable than talking about preventing "autistic people," despite autism only existing within the context of autistic people.

sheet.es: Al leer sobre autismo o elegir servicios y estudios, puede ayudar fijarse en el lenguaje: ¿habla de la persona autista con respeto, o solo de «déficits» y «curar el autismo»? Merece la pena preguntar si los investigadores o profesionales incluyen a personas autistas en sus decisiones; ese tipo de inclusión se asoció con un lenguaje menos capacitista. Se trata de una encuesta con preguntas abiertas a 195 investigadores en autismo, analizada con métodos cualitativos y estadísticos. Sus límites: refleja lo que escribieron los investigadores que quisieron participar, muestra asociaciones y no causas, y no mide directamente cómo afecta esto a las familias.
sheet.en: When reading about autism or choosing services and studies, it can help to notice the language: does it speak about autistic people with respect, or only about "deficits" and "curing autism"? It is worth asking whether researchers or professionals involve autistic people in their decisions; that kind of inclusion was linked to less ableist language. This was a survey with open-ended questions answered by 195 autism researchers, analysed with qualitative and statistical methods. Its limits: it reflects what volunteering researchers wrote, it shows associations rather than causes, and it does not directly measure effects on families.
sheet.sv: När du läser om autism eller väljer insatser och studier kan det hjälpa att lägga märke till språket: talar det om autistiska personer med respekt, eller bara om "brister" och att "bota autism"? Det är värt att fråga om forskare eller yrkespersoner involverar autistiska personer i sina beslut; sådan delaktighet hängde ihop med mindre funkofobiskt språk. Studien var en enkät med öppna frågor till 195 autismforskare, analyserad med kvalitativa och statistiska metoder. Begränsningar: den speglar vad forskare som valde att delta skrev, visar samband snarare än orsaker och mäter inte direkt hur detta påverkar familjer.

title: Social COmmunication Program supported by E-health (SCOPE) for infants and toddlers at elevated likelihood of autism spectrum disorder: study design of a cluster randomized controlled trial.
authors: Snijder MIJ, Dietz C, van Andel M, Ruiter ELM, Buitelaar JK, Oosterling IJ
abstract: Background Although the importance of early detection and early intervention of autism spectrum disorders (ASD) is widely recognized, multiple barriers exist in accessing early intervention services. As an alternative to these barriers, the SCOPE project presents a new, easy accessible and blended intervention called BEAR (Blended E-health for children at eArly Risk). This paper describes this BEAR intervention and study design of an ongoing two arm cluster randomized controlled trial (RCT). Methods BEAR (Blended E-health for children at eArly Risk) is a blended e-health intervention, based on evidence-based naturalistic developmental behavioral interventions (NDBI's) and can be offered to parents and infants/toddlers at high likelihood for ASD. During the ongoing RCT, N = 88 high risk infants and toddlers will be cluster randomized over the BEAR intervention and care-as-usual (CAU) conditions. The finalized version of the intervention protocol and study design are presented in this paper. The primary outcome measure is joint engagement measured by the Joint Engagement Rating Inventory (JERI) during videotaped parent-child interaction. Secondary outcome measures include severity of ASD symptoms, global level of adaptive functioning, parental well-being, parental skills and satisfaction with healthcare. Also, costs will be estimated from society's perspective. Assessments take place at the start of the study (T1), after eight weeks (T2) and after six months (T3) and include behavioral home observations and parental questionnaires. Discussion The SCOPE project aims to contribute to improved early identification and timely start of suitable interventions for infants and toddlers at elevated likelihood for ASD. This ongoing RCT will offer insight in the feasibility, short-term and six months effects of the innovative BEAR intervention. It is estimated that inclusion for the trial (N = 88) is completed in spring 2023. Trial registration Dutch Trial Register, NTR7695. Registered at December 17 th , 2018, www.trialregister.nl .

sheet.es: Este estudio aún no ofrece resultados, pero describe una idea útil: apoyar a madres y padres de bebés y niños pequeños con alta probabilidad de ser autistas mediante un programa mixto, con componentes en línea, basado en intervenciones del desarrollo que usan el juego y la vida diaria. Si busca apoyo temprano, puede preguntar a los servicios si existen opciones así. Es el diseño de un ensayo aleatorizado en curso, con 88 bebés y niños pequeños que recibirán el programa o la atención habitual. Aún no sabemos si funciona, y los resultados futuros no valdrán para todas las familias.
sheet.en: This paper reports no results yet, but it describes a useful idea: supporting parents of infants and toddlers who are likely to be autistic through a blended programme with online parts, based on developmental approaches that use play and everyday routines. If you are looking for early support, you can ask services whether options like this exist. It is the design of an ongoing randomised trial, with 88 infants and toddlers receiving either the programme or usual care. We do not yet know whether it works, and future results will not apply to every family.
sheet.sv: Den här artikeln har inga resultat än, men beskriver en användbar idé: att stödja föräldrar till spädbarn och små barn som sannolikt är autistiska genom ett blandat program med digitala delar, baserat på utvecklingsinriktade metoder som använder lek och vardag. Om du söker tidigt stöd kan du fråga vården om liknande alternativ finns. Det är upplägget för en pågående randomiserad studie där 88 spädbarn och små barn får antingen programmet eller vanlig vård. Vi vet ännu inte om det fungerar, och kommande resultat gäller inte alla familjer.

title: Homelessness in autistic women: Defining the research agenda.
authors: Lockwood Estrin G, Lockwood Estrin G, Aseervatham V, De Barros CM, Chapple T, Churchard A, Harper M, Jones EJ, Mandy W, Milner V, O'Brien S, Senju A, Smith C, Smith J
abstract: Background Current evidence suggests that autistic individuals are at high risk for becoming and remaining in a cycle of homelessness. Key risk factors for homelessness disproportionately affect autistic people; however, we have limited understanding of how to best support autistic individuals accessing services. This gap in the evidence base is particularly acute for autistic women. Objective As a first step to address this gap, we aimed to (1) map gaps in knowledge and practice; (2) identify priority areas for research and (3) develop recommendations for how to implement novel research and practice in this area. Methods We conducted a collaborative workshop with an interdisciplinary group of 26 stakeholders to address our aims. Stakeholders included autistic women with experience of homelessness, researchers, health professionals, NGO representatives, and service providers. Results and recommendations Two research priority areas were identified to map the prevalence and demographics of autistic women experiencing homelessness, and to delineate risk and protective factors for homelessness. Priority areas for improving provision of support included staff training to improve communication, awareness of autism and building trust with service providers, and recommendations for practical provision of support by services. Conclusions Future research is critical to increase our knowledge of the pathways leading to homelessness for autistic women, and barriers to engaging with homelessness and social services. We need to use this knowledge to develop new ways of delivering targeted and inclusive support for autistic women, which could prevent or shorten periods of homelessness.

sheet.es: Si apoyas a una mujer autista que vive o ha vivido sin hogar, puede ayudar que los servicios se comuniquen con claridad, comprendan el autismo y construyan confianza poco a poco. Puedes pedir esto a quienes la atienden. La evidencia es un taller colaborativo con 26 participantes: mujeres autistas con experiencia de falta de vivienda, investigadores, profesionales de salud, ONG y servicios. Sus límites: es una agenda de prioridades y recomendaciones, no una prueba de qué apoyos funcionan, y no describe a todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic woman who is or has been homeless, it may help when services communicate clearly, understand autism and build trust step by step. You can ask the people supporting her for this. The evidence is a collaborative workshop with 26 participants: autistic women with experience of homelessness, researchers, health professionals, NGO representatives and service providers. Its limits: it sets out research priorities and recommendations, not proof of which supports work, and it does not describe every person.
sheet.sv: Om du stödjer en autistisk kvinna som är eller har varit hemlös kan det hjälpa att tjänster kommunicerar tydligt, förstår autism och bygger förtroende steg för steg. Du kan be dem som stödjer henne om detta. Underlaget är en gemensam workshop med 26 deltagare: autistiska kvinnor med erfarenhet av hemlöshet, forskare, hälso- och sjukvårdspersonal, ideella organisationer och tjänsteleverantörer. Begränsningar: den anger forskningsprioriteringar och rekommendationer, inte bevis för vilket stöd som fungerar, och beskriver inte alla personer.

title: Effects of nonsocial and circumscribed interest images on neural mechanisms of emotion regulation in autistic adults.
authors: Antezana L, Coffman MC, DiCriscio AS, Richey JA
abstract: Introduction Emotion dysregulation is commonly reported among autistic individuals. Prior work investigating the neurofunctional mechanisms of emotion regulation (ER) in autistic adults has illustrated alterations in dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) activity, as well as concurrent atypical patterns of activation in subcortical regions related to affect during cognitive reappraisal of social images. Whereas most research examining ER in autism has focused on regulation of negative emotions, the effects of regulating positive emotions has been generally understudied. This is surprising given the relevance of positive motivational states to understanding circumscribed interests (CI) in autism. Methods Accordingly, the purpose of this study was to use fMRI with simultaneous eye-tracking and pupillometry to investigate the neural mechanisms of ER during passive viewing and cognitive reappraisal of a standardized set of nonsocial images and personalized (self-selected) CI images. Results The autistic group demonstrated comparatively reduced modulation of posterior cingulate cortex (PCC) activation during cognitive reappraisal of CI images compared to viewing of CI, although no eye-tracking/pupillometry differences emerged between-groups. Further, the autistic group demonstrated increased PCC connectivity with left lateral occipital and right supramarginal areas when engaging in cognitive reappraisal vs. viewing CI. Discussion In autistic adults, CI may be differentially modulated via PCC. Considering the documented role of the PCC as a core hub of the default mode network, we further postulate that ER of CI could potentially be related to self-referential cognition.

sheet.es: Los intereses profundos pueden tener un papel propio en cómo una persona autista maneja sus emociones, así que conviene no tratarlos solo como algo que hay que limitar. Puede ayudar preguntar a la persona cómo se siente al hablar de su interés o al pensar en él de otra manera. Es un estudio con personas autistas adultas que usó resonancia magnética funcional y seguimiento ocular. Encontró que el grupo autista mostró menos modulación de la corteza cingulada posterior al reinterpretar imágenes de sus intereses. Sus límites: es un estudio de actividad cerebral, no ofrece pautas de actuación, y no sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: Deep interests may play their own role in how an autistic person manages emotions, so it may help not to treat them only as something to limit. You could ask the person how they feel when talking about their interest or thinking about it in a different way. This was a study with autistic adults using functional MRI and eye-tracking. The autistic group showed less modulation of the posterior cingulate cortex when reappraising images of their interests. Its limits: it looked at brain activity, offers no practical guidelines, and is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Djupa intressen kan ha en egen roll i hur en autistisk person hanterar känslor, så det kan vara bra att inte bara se dem som något att begränsa. Du kan fråga personen hur hen känner när hen pratar om sitt intresse eller tänker på det på ett annat sätt. Det här var en studie med autistiska vuxna som använde funktionell magnetkamera och ögonrörelsemätning. Den autistiska gruppen visade mindre modulering av bakre cingulära cortex när de omvärderade bilder av sina intressen. Begränsningar: studien mätte hjärnaktivitet, ger inga praktiska riktlinjer och är ingen regel för alla personer.

title: Physical Activity, Gut Microbiota, and Genetic Background for Children and Adolescents with Autism Spectrum Disorder.
authors: Plaza-Diaz J, Radar AM, Baig AT, Leyba MF, Costabel MM, Zavala-Crichton JP, Sanchez-Martinez J, MacKenzie AE, Solis-Urra P
abstract: It is estimated that one in 100 children worldwide has been diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Children with ASD frequently suffer from gut dysbiosis and gastrointestinal issues, findings which possibly play a role in the pathogenesis and/or severity of their condition. Physical activity may have a positive effect on the composition of the intestinal microbiota of healthy adults. However, the effect of exercise both on the gastrointestinal problems and intestinal microbiota (and thus possibly on ASD) itself in affected children is unknown. In terms of understanding the physiopathology and manifestations of ASD, analysis of the gut-brain axis holds some promise. Here, we discuss the physiopathology of ASD in terms of genetics and microbiota composition, and how physical activity may be a promising non-pharmaceutical approach to improve ASD-related symptoms.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija autista tiene molestias de tripa, vale la pena anotar cuándo aparecen y comentarlas con su pediatra; moverse puede ser una actividad más para probar, a su ritmo y según sus gustos. Esto es una revisión que reúne investigación sobre genética, microbiota intestinal y actividad física. Señala que el ejercicio podría ayudar a la microbiota en adultos sin autismo, pero que su efecto en niñas y niños autistas, y en sus problemas digestivos, aún se desconoce. No demuestra que el ejercicio mejore nada en una persona concreta y no sirve como regla para todas.
sheet.en: If your autistic child has tummy troubles, it may help to note when they happen and raise them with a paediatrician; movement can be one more activity to try, at their own pace and in ways they enjoy. This is a review that brings together research on genetics, gut microbiota and physical activity. It notes that exercise may benefit the gut microbiota of healthy adults, but its effect on autistic children, and on their digestive problems, is still unknown. It does not show that exercise improves anything for a particular person, and it is not a rule for everyone.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn har magproblem kan det vara bra att anteckna när de uppstår och ta upp dem med en barnläkare. Rörelse kan vara en aktivitet att prova, i barnets egen takt och på sätt barnet gillar. Detta är en översikt som samlar forskning om genetik, tarmflora och fysisk aktivitet. Den menar att motion kan gynna tarmfloran hos friska vuxna, men att effekten hos autistiska barn och på deras magproblem ännu är okänd. Den visar inte att motion förbättrar något för en enskild person och är ingen regel för alla.

title: Factors and experiences that influence school mobility for autistic students: A systematic review.
authors: Mitchelson H, Adams D, Simpson K
journal: The British journal of educational psychology
abstract: Background Autistic students are reported to move schools at a high rate, but little is understood about why this is happening. What is known is that the effects of school mobility can negatively impact both short- and long-term outcomes, particularly the child's learning, behaviours, mental health and school retention. Aims The aim of this systematic review was to synthesize the research on factors and experiences which influence the family's decision to move their autistic child to another school. Methods A protocol was registered with PROPERO (ID: CRD4202120794). Searches were conducted with ERIC, Scopus and Web of Science and seven studies were identified. Results The studies focused on three main types of mobility: mainstream-to-mainstream school moves, moving between mainstream and segregated schools, and moving between mainstream and homeschool. Parents' concerns for their child's learning, social experiences and mental health, as well as their own interactions with their child's school, influenced the decision to leave. Whilst there were similarities across the studies for reasons to move, there were also differences based upon the settings between which students moved. Conclusion The findings highlight the need for further research across all school mobility types to better understand the reasons underpinning high rates of school mobility for autistic students.

sheet.es: Si está pensando en cambiar a su hijo autista de colegio, anote antes qué le preocupa del aprendizaje, las relaciones sociales y la salud mental, y hable con el centro sobre ello. Esta revisión sistemática reunió siete estudios sobre por qué las familias deciden cambiar de escuela; influyeron esas preocupaciones y la relación de los padres con el colegio. Los motivos variaron según el tipo de cambio, por ejemplo entre escuela ordinaria, escuela segregada o educación en casa. Con tan pocos estudios, los resultados no sirven como regla para cada familia y hace falta más investigación.
sheet.en: If you are thinking about moving your autistic child to another school, first write down what worries you about their learning, social experiences and mental health, and talk with the school about it. This systematic review gathered seven studies on why families decide to change schools; those worries and parents' interactions with the school influenced the decision. Reasons differed depending on the type of move, such as between mainstream, segregated or home schooling. With so few studies, the findings are not a rule for every family, and more research is needed.
sheet.sv: Om du funderar på att byta skola för ditt autistiska barn, skriv först ner vad som oroar dig kring lärande, sociala upplevelser och psykisk hälsa, och prata med skolan om det. Den här systematiska översikten samlade sju studier om varför familjer byter skola; oro för just dessa områden och föräldrars kontakt med skolan påverkade beslutet. Skälen skilde sig åt beroende på typ av byte, till exempel mellan ordinarie skola, specialskola eller hemundervisning. Med så få studier gäller resultaten inte alla familjer, och mer forskning behövs.

title: Sleeping Sound Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD): a randomised controlled trial of a brief behavioural sleep intervention in primary school-aged autistic children.
authors: Papadopoulos N, Sciberras E, Hiscock H, Williams K, McGillivray J, Mihalopoulos C, Engel L, Fuller-Tyszkiewicz M, Bellows ST, Marks D, Howlin P, Rinehart N
journal: Journal of child psychology and psychiatry, and allied disciplines
abstract: Background Behavioural sleep problems are common in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD); however, evidence for the efficacy of behavioural sleep interventions is limited. This study examined the efficacy of a brief behavioural sleep intervention in autistic children. It was hypothesised that the intervention would reduce overall child sleep problems (primary outcome), in addition to improvements in children's social, emotional, cognitive, academic functioning, and quality of life, and parent/caregivers' stress, quality of life, and mental health (secondary outcomes). Methods A randomised controlled trial was conducted with participants randomised via a computer-generated sequence to the sleeping sound intervention (n = 123) or treatment as usual (n = 122) group. Participants comprised 245 children with an ASD diagnosis. Inclusion criteria were as follows: confirmation of DSM IV or DSM-5 diagnosis of ASD, participants aged between 5 and 13 years and parent/caregiver report of moderate-severe sleep problems. Exclusion criteria were as follows: parent/caregiver intellectual disability or lacking sufficient English to complete questionnaires; and child participant with co-occurring medical conditions known to impact sleep. The intervention group received the sleeping sound intervention (2 × 50-min face-to-face sessions plus follow-up phone call) by a trained clinician. Results Change in children's sleep problems was measured by the Children's Sleep Habits Questionnaire (CSHQ) at 3 months post randomisation. Parents/caregivers of children in the intervention group reported a reduction in child sleep problems at 3 months post randomisation (effect size: E.S -0.7). There were also small effects in a number of child (internalising symptoms, emotional behavioural disturbance and quality of life) and parent/caregiver (mental health, parenting stress and quality of life) outcomes; however, these did not remain significant when controlling for multiple comparisons. Conclusions The sleeping sound ASD intervention is an efficacious and practical way to reduce sleep problems for autistic children. This brief behavioural intervention has the potential to be embedded easily into the Australian healthcare system.

sheet.es: Si el sueño de su hijo o hija autista le preocupa, puede preguntar a su pediatra o clínico por programas conductuales breves de sueño, que se centran en rutinas y hábitos. Este ensayo controlado aleatorizado incluyó a 245 niños autistas de entre 5 y 13 años con problemas de sueño moderados a graves según sus familias. Quienes recibieron la intervención (2 sesiones de 50 minutos más una llamada de seguimiento) mostraron menos problemas de sueño a los 3 meses (tamaño del efecto -0.7) que quienes recibieron la atención habitual. Otros cambios pequeños no se mantuvieron tras el ajuste estadístico. Los resultados provienen de cuestionarios de las familias y no garantizan el mismo efecto en cada niño.
sheet.en: If sleep is a worry for your autistic child, you could ask a paediatrician or clinician about brief behavioural sleep programmes, which focus on routines and habits. This randomised controlled trial included 245 autistic children aged 5 to 13 whose families reported moderate-severe sleep problems. Those who received the programme (2 sessions of 50 minutes plus a follow-up call) had fewer sleep problems at 3 months (effect size -0.7) than those receiving usual care. Other small changes did not hold after statistical adjustment. Results rely on parent questionnaires and will not apply the same way to every child.
sheet.sv: Om sömnen oroar er kring ert autistiska barn kan ni fråga en barnläkare eller klinisk behandlare om korta beteendebaserade sömnprogram, som fokuserar på rutiner och vanor. Denna randomiserade kontrollerade studie omfattade 245 autistiska barn i åldern 5 till 13 år vars familjer rapporterade måttliga till svåra sömnproblem. De som fick programmet (2 sessioner på 50 minuter plus ett uppföljande samtal) hade färre sömnproblem efter 3 månader (effektstorlek -0.7) än de som fick vanlig vård. Andra små förändringar höll inte efter statistisk justering. Resultaten bygger på föräldrars enkäter och gäller inte på samma sätt för alla barn.

title: Mental health and social difficulties of late-diagnosed autistic children, across childhood and adolescence.
authors: Mandy W, Midouhas E, Hosozawa M, Cable N, Sacker A, Flouri E
journal: Journal of child psychology and psychiatry, and allied disciplines
abstract: Background Autism can be diagnosed from 2 years of age, although most autistic people receive their diagnosis later than this after they have started education. Research is required to understand why some autistic children are diagnosed late, and the level and nature of unmet need prior to diagnosis for late-diagnosed children. Methods We examined trajectories of emotional, behavioural and social difficulties (EBSDs) across childhood and adolescence, comparing 'earlier-diagnosed' (diagnosed 7 years or younger) with 'late-diagnosed' (diagnosed between 8 and 14 years) autistic children. Data were from the Millennium Cohort Study, a population-based UK birth cohort. EBSDs were measured using the parent-report Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire, at 3, 5, 7, 11 and 14 years. We used Growth Curve Modelling to investigate levels and rates of change in these difficulties, and to compare earlier- (n = 146) and late-diagnosed (n = 284) autistic children. Results Aged 5, earlier-diagnosed autistic children had more emotional (i.e., internalising), conduct, hyperactivity and social difficulties; although clinical difficulties in these areas were nevertheless common in late-diagnosed children. There was a faster annual increase in scores for all domains for late-diagnosed children, and by age 14 years, they had higher levels of EBSDs. These results persisted when we ran adjusted models, to account for the late-diagnosed group having higher rates of late-diagnosed attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder, higher IQ, a higher proportion of females and older and more educated mothers. Conclusions Emotional, behavioural and social difficulties are associated with, and may influence, the timing of autism diagnosis. Late-diagnosed autistic children often have high levels of mental health and social difficulties prior to their autism diagnosis, and tend to develop even more severe problems as they enter adolescence.

sheet.es: Si un niño autista aún no tiene diagnóstico y muestra malestar emocional o dificultades sociales, conviene pedir una evaluación y apoyos sin esperar a que empeore, sobre todo al acercarse la adolescencia. Es un estudio de seguimiento con datos de la Millennium Cohort Study, una cohorte británica: 146 niños autistas diagnosticados antes y 284 diagnosticados entre los 8 y los 14 años. Las familias respondieron un cuestionario en varias edades. Sus límites: se basa en informes de los padres y muestra asociaciones, no causas, y no describe a cada niño ni a cada familia.
sheet.en: If an autistic child has no diagnosis yet but shows emotional distress or social difficulties, it is worth asking for an assessment and support without waiting for things to get harder, especially as adolescence approaches. This is a follow-up study using Millennium Cohort Study data, a UK birth cohort: 146 children diagnosed earlier and 284 diagnosed between 8 and 14 years. Parents completed a questionnaire at several ages. Its limits: it relies on parent reports and shows associations, not causes, and it does not describe every child or family.
sheet.sv: Om ett autistiskt barn ännu inte har en diagnos men visar känslomässigt obehag eller sociala svårigheter är det värt att be om utredning och stöd utan att vänta tills det blir svårare, särskilt när tonåren närmar sig. Det är en uppföljningsstudie med data från Millennium Cohort Study, en brittisk födelsekohort: 146 barn diagnostiserade tidigare och 284 diagnostiserade mellan 8 och 14 år. Föräldrar fyllde i ett frågeformulär vid flera åldrar. Begränsningar: studien bygger på föräldrarnas rapporter och visar samband, inte orsaker, och beskriver inte varje barn eller familj.

title: Is traditional back translation enough? Comparison of translation methodology for an ASD screening tool.
authors: DuBay M, Sideris J, Rouch E
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Early identification of autism spectrum disorders (ASD) in non-English speaking children often relies on translation of English ASD screening measures. Most measures employ a forward-back translation approach, despite data suggesting that this method may result in poor psychometric properties. Some studies in non-ASD fields have suggested that a rigorous method of translation with cultural adaptation may yield better psychometric properties, but no studies in the ASD field have compared the two approaches directly. This investigation compares these two translation methodologies to determine if they produce psychometrically similar or dissimilar measures. Three hundred and eighty US-based Spanish-speaking caregivers of children 8-16 months old were randomly assigned to complete either a forward-back Spanish translation or a rigorous translation with cultural adaptation of a parent-report ASD screening tool. Measurement invariance analyses determined that the two translations were psychometrically dissimilar. Additional qualitative explanatory methods using cognitive interviews examined textual differences and participant preferences between non-invariant items. LAY SUMMARY: Autism screening questionnaires created in English need to be translated into other languages so non-English speaking parents can fill them out accurately. Traditionally, researchers have not considered cultural differences when they translate these questionnaires. When we compared a direct translation to a translation with cultural adaptations, the two questionnaires were statistically different. Parents interpreted and responded to the same questions differently, depending on which version they filled out.

title: Reexamining empathy in autism: Empathic disequilibrium as a novel predictor of autism diagnosis and autistic traits.
authors: Shalev I, Warrier V, Greenberg DM, Smith P, Allison C, Baron-Cohen S, Eran A, Uzefovsky F
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: A large body of research showed that autistic people have intact emotional (affective) empathy alongside reduced cognitive empathy. However, there are mixed findings and these call for a more subtle understanding of empathy in autism. Empathic disequilibrium refers to the imbalance between emotional and cognitive empathy and is associated with a higher number of autistic traits in the typical population. Here we examined whether empathic disequilibrium predicts both the number of autistic traits and autism diagnosis. In a large sample of autistic (N = 1905) and typical individuals (N = 3009), we examined empathic disequilibrium and empathy as predictors of autistic traits and autism diagnosis, using a polynomial regression with response surface analysis. Empathy and autistic traits were measured using validated self-report questionnaires. Both empathic disequilibrium and empathy predicted linearly and non-linearly autism diagnosis and autistic traits. Specifically, a tendency towards higher emotional than cognitive empathy (empathic disequilibrium towards emotional empathy) predicted both autism diagnosis and the social domain of autistic traits, while higher cognitive than emotional empathy was associated with the non-social domain of autism. Empathic disequilibrium was also more prominent in autistic females. This study provides evidence that beyond empathy as was measured thus far, empathic disequilibrium offers a novel analytical approach for examining the role of empathy. Empathic disequilibrium allows for a more nuanced understanding of the links between empathy and autism. LAY SUMMARY: Many autistic individuals report feelings of excessive empathy, yet their experience is not reflected by most of the current literature, typically suggesting that autism is characterized by intact emotional and reduced cognitive empathy. To fill this gap, we looked at both ends of the imbalance between these components, termed empathic disequilibrium. We show that, like empathy, empathic disequilibrium is related to autism diagnosis and traits, and thus may provide a more nuanced understanding of empathy and its link with autism.
