sheet.es: Si una persona autista dice que siente mucha empatía, conviene creerle: sentir mucho por los demás y tener más dificultad para interpretar lo que piensan o necesitan pueden coexistir. Se puede ayudar poniendo en palabras lo que la otra persona piensa o pretende, sin dudar de que le importa. La evidencia es un estudio con cuestionarios de autoinforme en 1905 personas autistas y 3009 típicas. Es un estudio de asociaciones, no explica causas, y no describe a cada persona autista ni sirve para diagnosticar.
sheet.en: If an autistic person says they feel a great deal of empathy, it is worth believing them: feeling strongly for others and finding it harder to work out what others think or need can exist together. You can help by putting into words what someone else thinks or intends, without doubting that the person cares. The evidence is a study using self-report questionnaires with 1905 autistic and 3009 typical people. It looks at associations, not causes, does not describe every autistic person, and cannot be used to diagnose.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person säger att hen känner mycket empati är det värt att tro på det: att känna starkt för andra och samtidigt ha svårare att förstå vad andra tänker eller behöver kan finnas samtidigt. Du kan hjälpa genom att sätta ord på vad någon annan tänker eller menar, utan att tvivla på att personen bryr sig. Underlaget är en studie med självskattningsformulär hos 1905 autistiska och 3009 typiska personer. Den visar samband, inte orsaker, beskriver inte alla autistiska personer och kan inte användas för diagnos.

title: Exclusion of females in autism research: Empirical evidence for a "leaky" recruitment-to-research pipeline.
authors: D'Mello AM, Frosch IR, Li CE, Cardinaux AL, Gabrieli JDE
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is characterized by challenges in social communication and the presence of repetitive behaviors or restricted interests. Notably, males are four times as likely as females to be diagnosed with autism. Despite efforts to increase representation and characterization of autistic females, research studies consistently enroll small samples of females, or exclude females altogether. Importantly, researchers often rely on standardized measures to confirm diagnosis prior to enrollment in research studies. We retrospectively analyzed the effects of one such measure (Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule, ADOS) on research inclusion/exclusion rates by sex in autistic adults, all of whom had a preexisting community diagnosis of autism (n = 145, 95 male, 50 female). Using the ADOS as a confirmatory diagnostic measure resulted in the exclusion of autistic females at a rate over 2.5 times higher than that of autistic males. We compared sex ratios in our sample to those in other large, publically available datasets that rely either on community diagnosis (6 datasets, total n = 42,209) or standardized assessments (2 datasets, total n = 214) to determine eligibility of participants for research. Reliance on community diagnosis rather than confirmatory diagnostic assessments resulted in significantly more equal sex ratios. These results provide evidence for a "leaky" recruitment-to-research pipeline for females in autism research. LAY SUMMARY: Despite efforts to increase the representation of autistic females in research, studies consistently enroll small samples of females or exclude females altogether. We find that despite making up almost 50% of the initially recruited sample based upon self-report of community diagnosis, autistic females are disproportonately excluded from research participation as a result of commonly used autism diagnostic measures. In our sample, and several other publically available datasets, reliance on community diagnosis resulted in significantly more equal sex ratios.

sheet.es: Si tu hija, pareja o persona a tu cargo es autista y la han excluido de un estudio por una prueba de confirmación, eso no invalida su diagnóstico. Puedes preguntar a los equipos de investigación cómo deciden quién participa. La evidencia es un análisis retrospectivo con 145 adultos autistas (95 hombres, 50 mujeres), todos con diagnóstico comunitario previo, y una comparación con otras bases de datos. Usar la prueba ADOS excluyó a las mujeres a una tasa superior a 2.5 veces la de los hombres. Límites: es un análisis de reclutamiento, no explica las causas ni vale para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If your daughter, partner or relative is autistic and was left out of a study because of a confirmation test, that does not invalidate their diagnosis. You can ask research teams how they decide who takes part. The evidence is a retrospective analysis of 145 autistic adults (95 male, 50 female), all with an existing community diagnosis, plus a comparison with other datasets. Using the ADOS excluded females at a rate over 2.5 times higher than males. Limits: it looks at recruitment, does not explain the causes, and does not apply equally to every person.
sheet.sv: Om din dotter, partner eller anhörig är autistisk och uteslöts från en studie på grund av ett bekräftande test, gör det inte diagnosen ogiltig. Du kan fråga forskargrupper hur de avgör vem som får delta. Underlaget är en retrospektiv analys av 145 autistiska vuxna (95 män, 50 kvinnor), alla med en tidigare diagnos i vården, samt en jämförelse med andra dataset. Användning av ADOS uteslöt kvinnor i en takt över 2.5 gånger högre än män. Begränsningar: studien gäller rekrytering, förklarar inte orsakerna och gäller inte lika för alla.

title: The effectiveness of an attention-based intervention for school-aged autistic children with anger regulating problems: A randomized controlled trial.
authors: Clifford P, Gevers C, Jonkman KM, Boer F, Begeer S
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Anger regulation is a challenge for children with autism spectrum disorders (ASD). We investigated if attention-based cognitive behavioral treatment, based on mindfulness cognitive therapy (MBCT) and dialectical behavior therapy (DBT), reduces aggressive behavior and improves anger coping in school-aged autistic children (n = 51). Children were randomized to an active-control or a treatment condition. The treatment included nine weekly sessions attention-based individual therapy. Parents in both conditions received three weekly psychoeducation group sessions to heighten awareness of expressed emotion (EE). For aggressive behavior, treatment reduced temper tantrums and arguing. No effect was found on destroying things and physical violence. For anger coping, treatment increased adaptive coping strategies of diffusion and social support seeking, but had no effect on assertion, rumination, and maladaptive coping direct anger out and avoidance. Treatment did not impact secondary outcome measures concerning children's quality of life (QoL) and parental stress-levels and psychological well-being. In conclusion, school-aged autistic children are able to acquire self-regulation skills reducing temper tantrums and arguing and increasing the use of adaptive anger coping strategies. The intervention shows potential to improve behavior and regulation, but little transfer to other domains. Limitations and future directions involving the child's social environment, including parents, siblings, and teachers are discussed. LAY SUMMARY: Children on the autism spectrum often show aggressive behavior. Treatment can train children to be more aware of their emotions. This study found that this can help reducing temper tantrums and arguing and increasing some coping skills, though no impact was found on several other domains of aggression and coping.

sheet.es: Si un niño autista tiene dificultades para regular la rabia, puede ayudar practicar con él la atención a sus emociones y ofrecerle formas de calmarse, como alejarse del conflicto o buscar apoyo. Es un ensayo aleatorizado con 51 niños autistas en edad escolar: nueve sesiones semanales de terapia individual basada en la atención redujeron las rabietas y las discusiones y aumentaron algunas estrategias adaptativas. No hubo efecto en destruir cosas ni en la violencia física, ni en la calidad de vida o el estrés de los padres. Es un solo estudio, y no todos los niños responderán igual; conviene hablarlo con un profesional.
sheet.en: If an autistic child finds anger hard to regulate, it may help to practise noticing their emotions together and to offer ways to settle, such as stepping back from conflict or seeking support. This was a randomized controlled trial with 51 school-aged autistic children: nine weekly sessions of individual attention-based therapy reduced temper tantrums and arguing and increased some adaptive coping strategies. It had no effect on destroying things, physical violence, quality of life or parental stress. It is a single study, and children will not all respond the same way; talk it over with a professional.
sheet.sv: Om ett autistiskt barn har svårt att reglera ilska kan det hjälpa att öva tillsammans på att uppmärksamma känslor och erbjuda sätt att varva ner, som att backa från en konflikt eller söka stöd. Detta var en randomiserad kontrollerad studie med 51 autistiska barn i skolåldern: nio veckovisa sessioner individuell uppmärksamhetsbaserad terapi minskade utbrott och bråk och ökade vissa anpassade strategier. Ingen effekt sågs på att förstöra saker, fysiskt våld, livskvalitet eller föräldrars stress. Det är en enda studie, och barn svarar olika; prata med en yrkesperson.

title: Healthcare clinician perspectives on the intersection of autism and gender dysphoria.
authors: Cooper K, Mandy W, Russell A, Butler C
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic people are more likely to have a gender identity which does not match their sex assigned at birth. Some people experience distress about their sex and gender not matching, which is called gender dysphoria. Such individuals may wish to attend a gender clinic to access healthcare support for gender dysphoria. Currently, there is limited evidence to help clinicians best support autistic people who need healthcare for gender dysphoria. We wanted to find out what healthcare clinicians think about working with autistic patients with gender dysphoria. We interviewed 16 clinicians who work in healthcare services with adults and young people who are autistic and experience gender dysphoria. We recorded the interviews and carefully analysed the content to find key themes. We found that clinicians worked with patients to try and better understand their experiences of gender dysphoria. Clinicians identified features of autism that they believed were related to gender identity and dysphoria including different thinking styles, social differences, and sensory sensitivities. Clinicians noticed that autistic people spoke about their gender in different ways to non-autistic people. Clinicians tried to adapt their practice to better meet the needs of their autistic patients. These adaptations tended to focus on differences in the assessment process, for example, offering longer or shorter appointments and changing their communication style. We conclude that clinicians were offering an individualised approach to autistic patients experiencing gender dysphoria. However, these clinicians were particularly interested in working with autistic people, and so may not be representative of the wider clinician population. Clinicians working in this area should receive training on autism adaptations and the intersection of autism and gender dysphoria.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista necesita apoyo sanitario por disforia de género, puede ser útil pedir adaptaciones en las citas: más o menos duración, y una comunicación clara y adaptada a su manera de expresarse. El estudio entrevistó a 16 profesionales clínicos que trabajan con personas autistas, adultas y jóvenes, con disforia de género. Describieron que adaptaban su práctica, sobre todo en la evaluación, y que las personas autistas a veces hablan de su género de otra forma. Límites: son opiniones de profesionales, no de las propias personas autistas, y quienes participaron tenían especial interés en el autismo, así que quizá no representan a todos. Cada persona es distinta.
sheet.en: If an autistic person needs healthcare support for gender dysphoria, it can help to ask for adjustments to appointments, such as longer or shorter visits and a clear communication style that suits how they express themselves. The study interviewed 16 clinicians who work with autistic adults and young people experiencing gender dysphoria. They described adapting their practice, mainly in assessment, and noticed that autistic people sometimes talk about their gender differently. Limits: these are clinicians' views, not those of autistic people themselves, and the clinicians were particularly interested in autism, so they may not represent all clinicians. Every person is different.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person behöver vård för könsdysfori kan det hjälpa att be om anpassningar av besöken, till exempel längre eller kortare tid och ett tydligt kommunikationssätt som passar hur personen uttrycker sig. Studien intervjuade 16 kliniker som arbetar med autistiska vuxna och unga med könsdysfori. De beskrev att de anpassade sitt arbete, främst i bedömningen, och att autistiska personer ibland talar om sitt kön på ett annat sätt. Begränsningar: det är klinikernas synpunkter, inte autistiska personers egna, och klinikerna var särskilt intresserade av autism, så de representerar kanske inte alla. Varje person är unik.

title: Using EMDR with autistic individuals: A Delphi survey with EMDR therapists.
authors: Fisher N, van Diest C, Leoni M, Spain D
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Eye Movement Desensitisation and Reprocessing (EMDR) is a psychological therapy that can help people process memories and distress about past events, so they have less impact on their daily lives. EMDR can be effective for treating symptoms of post-traumatic stress disorder, including nightmares and anxiety. Psychological therapies usually require adaptation so they are more accessible and effective for autistic people, but minimal research has focused on how best EMDR can be adapted. In this online survey study, we asked 103 EMDR therapists about barriers they think autistic people face when trying to have EMDR and what adaptations they use in their everyday practice. Four barriers were highlighted: client-related characteristics, therapist-related characteristics, differences in the therapeutic relationship and broader issues. Therapists identified a range of adaptations that can potentially be useful for autistic people, relating to being flexible, communicating clearly and having an awareness of individual differences. Many therapists emphasised the importance of not making assumptions about a person based on their autism diagnosis. Overall, the study findings suggest adaptations to EMDR are likely to be useful, but how relevant they are depends on each person.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista va a probar EMDR, conviene hablar antes con la terapeuta o el terapeuta sobre ajustes: flexibilidad en el ritmo, comunicación clara y atención a las diferencias individuales. Es mejor no suponer nada solo por el diagnóstico. La evidencia es una encuesta en línea con 103 terapeutas de EMDR, que describieron barreras y adaptaciones que usan en su práctica. Sus límites: recoge la opinión de terapeutas, no la experiencia de personas autistas que hicieron EMDR, y no prueba que las adaptaciones funcionen. Su utilidad depende de cada persona.
sheet.en: If an autistic person is thinking about trying EMDR, it helps to talk with the therapist beforehand about adjustments: flexibility in pacing, clear communication and attention to individual differences. It is better not to assume anything based only on the diagnosis. The evidence is an online survey of 103 EMDR therapists, who described barriers and the adaptations they use in everyday practice. Its limits: it reflects therapists' views, not the experiences of autistic people who had EMDR, and it does not prove the adaptations work. How useful they are depends on each person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person funderar på att prova EMDR är det bra att prata med terapeuten i förväg om anpassningar: flexibilitet i takten, tydlig kommunikation och uppmärksamhet på individuella skillnader. Det är bättre att inte anta något enbart utifrån diagnosen. Underlaget är en webbenkät med 103 EMDR-terapeuter, som beskrev hinder och anpassningar de använder i sitt dagliga arbete. Begränsningar: den speglar terapeuters åsikter, inte erfarenheter hos autistiska personer som gjort EMDR, och den visar inte att anpassningarna fungerar. Hur användbara de är beror på varje person.

title: Social support and links to quality of life among middle-aged and older autistic adults.
authors: Charlton RA, McQuaid GA, Wallace GL
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Social support can take many forms, such as practical help, time spent socially with others, or the satisfaction with personal relationships. Social support is known to affect quality of life (QoL) in both non-autistic older and autistic young adults. QoL reflects how satisfied an individual is with their life either overall or in a certain area. We know little about middle-aged and older autistic adults' experiences of social support or QoL. In this study, 388 adults aged 40-83 years old, completed online questionnaires asking about background such as age and sex, depression and anxiety symptoms, QoL (physical, psychological, social, environmental, and autism-specific), and different types of social support. Even after taking into account background, depression, and anxiety, social support was important for individuals' QoL. To our knowledge this is the first paper to examine the relationship between social support and QoL in middle-aged and older autistic adults. Improving social support may have a significant impact on the QoL of older autistic adults. Future studies should examine whether age-related changes in social support (size, content, and arrangement of social networks) that are common in non-autistic aging, also occur among older autistic adults.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una persona autista de mediana edad o mayor, vale la pena preguntarle qué tipo de apoyo le sirve: ayuda práctica, tiempo compartido a su ritmo o relaciones de confianza. No se trata de más contacto social, sino del que ella valora. Pequeños gestos regulares, como ayudar con un trámite o un encuentro tranquilo, pueden sumar a su calidad de vida. En este estudio, 388 adultos autistas de 40 a 83 años respondieron cuestionarios en línea; el apoyo social se relacionó con mejor calidad de vida incluso considerando ansiedad y depresión. Límites: es una foto en un momento dado, no prueba causa y efecto, y la muestra en línea no representa a todas las personas autistas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person in midlife or later, it is worth asking which kinds of support actually help them: practical help, time together on their terms, or trusted relationships. The goal is not more socialising, but the kind they value. Small, regular gestures, like help with paperwork or a calm visit, may add to their quality of life. In this study, 388 autistic adults aged 40 to 83 completed online questionnaires; social support was linked to better quality of life even after accounting for anxiety and depression. Limits: it is a single snapshot, cannot show cause and effect, and an online sample does not represent every autistic person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person i medelåldern eller äldre kan det vara värt att fråga vilket stöd som faktiskt hjälper: praktisk hjälp, tid tillsammans på personens villkor eller nära relationer. Målet är inte mer umgänge, utan den sortens kontakt personen själv värdesätter. Små, regelbundna insatser, som hjälp med pappersarbete eller ett lugnt besök, kan bidra till livskvaliteten. I studien besvarade 388 autistiska vuxna mellan 40 och 83 år enkäter på nätet; socialt stöd hängde ihop med bättre livskvalitet även när ångest och depression räknats in. Begränsningar: det är en ögonblicksbild som inte visar orsak och verkan, och ett nätbaserat urval representerar inte alla autistiska personer.

title: 'Someone like-minded in a big place': Autistic young adults' attitudes towards autistic peer support in mainstream education.
authors: Crompton CJ, Hallett S, Axbey H, McAuliffe C, Cebula K
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Autistic young people may struggle in mainstream schools and feel disconnected from their peers and their school. We know that autistic adults can benefit from spending time with other autistic people, but we don't know if this is the case for younger autistic people. We conducted interviews with 13 autistic young adults in the United Kingdom who recently left mainstream schooling. We asked them if they would have been interested in being involved in autistic peer support when they were at school, and if so, what that peer support should look like. Results indicated that autistic young people were enthusiastic about the idea of peer support. They thought it was important that peer support was flexible to suit their needs at different times, as well as inclusive, positive, and embracing neurodiversity. They also discussed the potential benefits and difficulties of having a peer support system within a school setting. This adds to the growing body of research on the potential benefits of autistic-autistic interactions on autistic people's well-being and sense of belonging. Findings can be used to help design pilot peer support projects in schools that can be tested to see how effective they are.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista en un colegio ordinario, puedes preguntarle si le gustaría tener un espacio de apoyo con otras personas autistas y cómo lo imaginaría. Quienes participaron querían algo flexible, inclusivo, positivo y que acoja la neurodiversidad. La evidencia viene de entrevistas con 13 jóvenes autistas del Reino Unido que habían terminado hace poco la educación ordinaria y contaron lo que habrían querido. Sus límites: es un grupo pequeño, habla de actitudes y no prueba que el apoyo entre iguales funcione; esos proyectos aún deben probarse en las escuelas. Las preferencias de cada persona pueden ser distintas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic person in mainstream school, you could ask whether they would like a space to meet other autistic people, and what it should look like. Participants wanted support that was flexible, inclusive, positive and embraced neurodiversity. The evidence comes from interviews with 13 autistic young adults in the United Kingdom who had recently left mainstream school and reflected on what they would have wanted. Its limits: the group is small, it shows attitudes rather than proving that peer support works, and such projects still need to be tested in schools. Each person's preferences may differ.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk person i en vanlig skola kan du fråga om hen skulle vilja ha en plats att träffa andra autistiska personer, och hur den borde se ut. Deltagarna ville ha stöd som var flexibelt, inkluderande, positivt och som välkomnar neurodiversitet. Underlaget är intervjuer med 13 autistiska unga vuxna i Storbritannien som nyligen lämnat den vanliga skolan och berättade vad de hade önskat. Begränsningarna: gruppen är liten, studien visar attityder och bevisar inte att kamratstöd fungerar, och sådana projekt behöver fortfarande prövas i skolor. Varje person kan ha olika önskemål.

title: Benefits and harms of interventions to improve anxiety, depression, and other mental health outcomes for autistic people: A systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
authors: Linden A, Best L, Elise F, Roberts D, Branagan A, Tay YBE, Crane L, Cusack J, Davidson B, Davidson I, Hearst C, Mandy W, Rai D, Smith E, Gurusamy K
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Nearly three out of four autistic people experience mental health problems such as stress, anxiety or depression. The research already done does not guide us on how best to prevent or treat mental health problems for autistic people. Our aim was to look at the benefits and harms of different interventions on mental health outcomes in autistic people. We searched all the published randomised controlled trials (RCTs) about interventions for mental health conditions in autistic people until 17 October 2020. We also searched for RCTs that were not published in peer-reviewed journals. These were obtained from registers of clinical trials online. We then combined the information from all these trials using advanced statistical methods to analyse how good the interventions are. Seventy-one studies (3630 participants) provided information for this research. The studies reported how participants were responding to the intervention for only a short period of time. The trials did not report which interventions worked for people with intellectual disability. In people without intellectual disability, some forms of cognitive behavioural therapy and mindfulness therapy may be helpful. However, further research is necessary. Many trials used medications to target core features of autism rather than targeting mental health conditions, but these medications did not help autistic people. Until we have more evidence, treatment of mental health conditions in autistic people should follow the evidence available for non-autistic people. We plan to widely disseminate the findings to healthcare professionals through medical journals and conferences and contact other groups representing autistic people.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista a tu cargo vive con ansiedad, estrés o tristeza persistente, vale la pena preguntar a su equipo de salud por terapias adaptadas, como la terapia cognitivo-conductual o el mindfulness, que pueden ayudar a algunas personas autistas sin discapacidad intelectual. Mientras haya poca evidencia específica, los profesionales pueden apoyarse en lo que funciona para la población general, ajustándolo a cada persona. Es un metaanálisis de 71 ensayos aleatorizados con 3630 personas autistas. Sus límites: los estudios siguieron a los participantes poco tiempo y no aportan datos sobre qué funciona para personas autistas con discapacidad intelectual.
sheet.en: If an autistic person you support lives with anxiety, stress or ongoing low mood, it is worth asking their health team about adapted therapies, such as cognitive behavioural therapy or mindfulness, which may help some autistic people without intellectual disability. While autism-specific evidence is limited, professionals can draw on what works for the general population, adjusted to the individual. This is a meta-analysis of 71 randomised trials including 3,630 autistic people. Its limits: participants were followed only for a short time, and the trials give no information on what works for autistic people with intellectual disability.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person du stöttar lever med ångest, stress eller långvarig nedstämdhet kan det vara värt att fråga vården om anpassade terapier, till exempel kognitiv beteendeterapi eller mindfulness, som kan hjälpa en del autistiska personer utan intellektuell funktionsnedsättning. Så länge autismspecifik kunskap är begränsad kan vården utgå från det som fungerar för befolkningen i stort, anpassat efter personen. Detta är en metaanalys av 71 randomiserade studier med 3 630 autistiska deltagare. Begränsningar: deltagarna följdes bara under kort tid, och studierna säger inget om vad som fungerar för autistiska personer med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning.

title: Racial/Ethnic Differences in Psychiatric and Medical Diagnoses Among Autistic Adults.
authors: Ames JL, Morgan EH, Giwa Onaiwu M, Qian Y, Massolo ML, Croen LA
abstract: Background Racial/ethnic disparities in access to diagnostic services are pervasive for autistic children. However, a few studies have examined racial/ethnic health disparities among autistic adults, who commonly experience higher rates of health conditions than non-autistic adults. We aimed at examining the intersection of autism and race/ethnicity in association with psychiatric and medical diagnoses. Methods The study population included adult members of Kaiser Permanente Northern California enrolled from 2008 to 2012. We ascertained 1507 adults who had an autism diagnosis documented in their electronic medical records. We sampled a matched control group of adults without an autism diagnosis ( N = 15,070) at a 10:1 ratio. Our sample was 46% White, 17% Hispanic, 16% Asian, 7% Black, and 14% other race/ethnicity. We compared health diagnoses (a) between autistic and non-autistic adults within strata of race/ethnicity and (b) across race/ethnicity within strata of autistic and non-autistic adults. Lastly, we examined the interaction between autism and race/ethnicity on both multiplicative and additive scales. Results Autistic adults were more likely to be diagnosed with most medical and psychiatric conditions compared with their non-autistic counterparts of the same race/ethnicity. Among autistic adults, Black, Hispanic, and Asian adults were less likely to be diagnosed with psychiatric conditions and Black and Hispanic autistic adults were more likely to be diagnosed with obesity than their White counterparts. In interaction models, we found that adults who were Black and autistic were disproportionately less likely to be diagnosed with psychiatric conditions and autoimmune disease and more likely to be diagnosed with hypertension than expected. Conclusion Health vulnerabilities may be compounded at the intersection of autism and race/ethnicity. Future research should continue to apply an intersectional lens toward understanding and addressing these disparities. Our findings likely underestimate the health disparities that exist in uninsured autistic adults and those living in other parts of the United States.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista adulta, sobre todo si es negra, hispana o asiática, conviene pedir revisiones médicas completas y llevar un registro de sus síntomas y preocupaciones. Un diagnóstico que falta no siempre significa que no haya necesidad. Es un estudio con registros médicos de 1507 adultos autistas y 15,070 adultos no autistas de un sistema de salud de California. Encontró más diagnósticos médicos y psiquiátricos en adultos autistas, y diferencias entre grupos raciales o étnicos. Sus límites: solo muestra diagnósticos registrados, no explica las causas, y probablemente no refleja a quienes no tienen seguro ni a otras regiones de Estados Unidos.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult, especially one who is Black, Hispanic or Asian, it helps to ask for full health checks and keep a record of their symptoms and concerns. A missing diagnosis does not always mean there is no need. This study used medical records of 1507 autistic adults and 15,070 non-autistic adults from one California health system. Autistic adults had more medical and psychiatric diagnoses, and patterns differed across racial and ethnic groups. Limits: it shows recorded diagnoses only, cannot explain causes, and likely misses uninsured people and other parts of the United States.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen, särskilt en som är svart, latinamerikansk eller asiatisk, kan det hjälpa att be om grundliga hälsokontroller och föra anteckningar om symtom och oro. En saknad diagnos betyder inte alltid att behovet saknas. Studien använde journaler från 1507 autistiska vuxna och 15 070 icke-autistiska vuxna i ett kalifornisk vårdsystem. Autistiska vuxna hade fler medicinska och psykiatriska diagnoser, och mönstren skilde sig mellan etniska grupper. Begränsningar: den visar bara registrerade diagnoser, förklarar inte orsakerna och missar sannolikt personer utan försäkring och andra delar av USA.

title: Telehealth-delivered caregiver training for autism: Recent innovations.
authors: Pacione L
abstract: Providing treatment to children with autism is a global health priority, and research demonstrates that caregivers can be trained in techniques to promote their child's social interaction, communication, play, positive behavior and skills. These caregiver-mediated interventions have been shown to promote a number of positive outcomes in children with autism, as well as their caregivers. When provided by telehealth, data indicate that caregiver training is acceptable and feasible, and associated with similar positive outcomes as live face-to-face training. Telehealth innovations, which have accelerated during the COVID-19 era, have demonstrated advantages over in-person delivery of services in terms of cost effectiveness and increased accessibility, however, more research is needed on feasibility, acceptability and effectiveness for different populations in different contexts. This brief review will highlight recent caregiver skills training interventions for autism that have been successfully adapted or designed for telehealth delivery. Telehealth interventions that are scalable, adaptable, caregiver-mediated, open-access, and delivered as part of a stepped care model, have the potential to address the global treatment gap for families of children with autism and other neurodevelopmental disabilities. Considerations relevant to the global scale-up of caregiver-mediated interventions will also be discussed.

sheet.es: Si buscas apoyo para acompañar a tu hijo autista en la comunicación, el juego o las habilidades diarias, puedes preguntar si hay formación para cuidadores por videollamada. Esta revisión breve resume investigaciones que indican que esa formación es aceptable y viable, con resultados positivos similares a la formación presencial, además de ser más accesible y rentable. Es una revisión, no un experimento nuevo, y no detalla aquí quiénes participaron. Los propios autores señalan que hace falta más investigación para distintas poblaciones y contextos, así que puede no encajar con todas las familias. Lo que funciona depende de tu hijo y de tu situación.
sheet.en: If you want support helping your autistic child with communication, play or daily skills, you can ask whether caregiver training is offered by video call. This brief review summarises research suggesting that this training is acceptable and feasible, with positive outcomes similar to face-to-face training, and that it can be cheaper and easier to access. It is a review, not a new experiment, and the abstract does not say who took part. The authors note that more research is needed for different populations and contexts, so it may not suit every family. What works depends on your child and your situation.
sheet.sv: Om du vill ha stöd i att hjälpa ditt autistiska barn med kommunikation, lek eller vardagsfärdigheter kan du fråga om utbildning för vårdnadshavare finns via videosamtal. Den här korta översikten sammanfattar forskning som tyder på att utbildningen är acceptabel och genomförbar, med positiva resultat som liknar utbildning på plats, och att den kan vara billigare och lättare att nå. Det är en översikt, inte ett nytt experiment, och sammanfattningen anger inte vilka som deltog. Författarna menar att mer forskning behövs för olika grupper och sammanhang, så det passar kanske inte alla familjer. Vad som fungerar beror på ditt barn och din situation.

title: Barriers to healthcare and their relationship to well-being and social support for autistic adults during COVID-19.
authors: Featherstone C, Sharpe RA, Axford N, Asthana S, Ball S, Husk K
abstract: Aim The present study aimed to investigate barriers to healthcare and their relationships to social and emotional well-being and intersectional inequalities for autistic adults during COVID-19 restrictions in the UK. Background Autistic adults experience severe health inequalities and report more barriers to accessing health services compared to other both disabled and non-disabled populations. The COVID-19 pandemic has impacted many areas of society that may have increased vulnerability of autistic people to social and health inequalities, including delivery of healthcare from in-person to remote methods. Method One hundred twenty-eight autistic adults who lived in the UK took part in an online survey. Measures included the Barriers to Healthcare Checklist (Short Form) and PROMIS outcome measure bank to assess emotional well-being and social support. Participants rated their agreement with items, retrospectively considering three different points of the trajectory of COVID-19 restrictions: before COVID-19, during the first lockdown in spring 2020, and in the month prior to taking the survey during autumn 2020. They completed a follow-up survey six months later to continue to assess change as restrictions in the UK were eased. Findings The average number of barriers to healthcare showed no significant change between all four time points. However, the nature of barriers to healthcare changed at the point of lockdown and persisted beyond the easing of COVID-19 restrictions. Barriers to healthcare were associated with some social and emotional well-being variables and demographic groups including gender, education and presence of additional disabilities. The findings may help to identify areas to target to improve access to both remote and in-person health systems for autistic people as modes of delivery continue to change over time.

title: Repercussions of the COVID-19 pandemic for people with autism and their family members: A scoping review.
authors: Teixeira OFB, Xavier SPL, Félix NDC, Silva JWMD, Abreu RMSX, Miranda KCL
abstract: Objective to map the diverse scientific evidence available about the repercussions of the COVID-19 pandemic for people with Autism Spectrum Disorder and their family members. Method a scoping review conducted in the following databases: MEDLINE, CINAHL, SciELO, SCOPUS, EMBASE and Wiley Online Library, in August and September 2021. The protocol of this review was registered at the Open Science Framework under DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/JYTVD. The data were analyzed and synthesized in a narrative way. Results a total of 46 publications identified indicate that the pandemic period brought about countless repercussions for the population with autism and their family members when experiencing serious difficulties in the changes or irregularities of the scheduled routines and limited access to education, therapies and social support. Conclusion the diverse evidence suggests that the COVID-19 pandemic intensified the inequalities already experienced by individuals with autism and their family members, with negative consequences in the emotional, psychological, behavioral and social aspects, interfering with the quality of life and mental health of this population segment. Future studies on individuals with autism and their families during public health crisis periods are of fundamental importance for planning psychiatric, psychosocial and educational interventions.

sheet.es: Si la rutina se altera de forma imprevista, ayuda avisar con tiempo, explicar qué cambia y mantener cuantos puntos fijos del día sea posible. También conviene buscar apoyo social y educativo para la familia. Es una revisión de alcance que reunió 46 publicaciones sobre la pandemia de COVID-19 en personas autistas y sus familias. Señala que los cambios de rutina y el acceso limitado a educación, terapias y apoyo social fueron muy difíciles. Es una síntesis narrativa, no mide cuánto ayuda cada medida y no describe a todas las personas por igual.
sheet.en: When routines change unexpectedly, it helps to give notice, explain what is changing and keep as many fixed points in the day as you can. It is also worth seeking social and educational support for the whole family. This was a scoping review of 46 publications on the COVID-19 pandemic and autistic people and their families. It found that changes to routine and limited access to education, therapies and social support caused serious difficulties. It is a narrative summary, does not measure how much any single strategy helps, and does not describe every person in the same way.
sheet.sv: När rutiner ändras oväntat hjälper det att ge förvarning, förklara vad som förändras och behålla så många fasta punkter i dagen som möjligt. Det är också värt att söka socialt stöd och utbildningsstöd för hela familjen. Detta var en kartläggande översikt av 46 publikationer om covid-19-pandemin och autistiska personer och deras familjer. Den fann att ändrade rutiner och begränsad tillgång till utbildning, terapier och socialt stöd skapade stora svårigheter. Det är en berättande sammanställning, den mäter inte hur mycket en enskild strategi hjälper och beskriver inte alla personer på samma sätt.

title: Characteristics of children on the autism spectrum who benefit the most from receiving intervention in inclusive versus specialised early childhood education settings.
authors: Vivanti G, Bent C, Capes K, Upson S, Hudry K, Dissanayake C, Victorian ASELCC Team
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: This study examined the factors associated with social-communicative outcomes for children on the autism spectrum receiving early intervention in inclusive versus specialised early childhood education programmes. Fifty-eight preschool-aged children randomly assigned to receive the Group-Early Start Denver Model (G-ESDM) in either inclusive or specialised (i.e., autism-specific) classrooms across one calendar year showed similar outcomes at group mean-level across measures of communication and social behaviour. We examined factors moderating outcomes across settings. Novel moderation analyses revealed that higher baseline social interest and nonverbal cognitive skills were associated with increased social communication gains for children in the inclusive classrooms, but not for those in specialised settings. Children who spend more time paying attention to people and have higher cognitive skills might benefit from receiving early intervention in inclusive settings, whilst these factors might be less relevant for children educated in specialised settings.

sheet.es: Al elegir entre un aula inclusiva y una especializada para un niño autista en edad preescolar, conviene observar sus intereses y su forma de relacionarse, sin dar por hecho que un entorno sea mejor para todos. Este ensayo asignó al azar a 58 niños autistas a recibir el mismo programa (G-ESDM) en uno de los dos tipos de aula durante un año. En promedio, los resultados fueron similares. Los niños con más interés social y mayores habilidades cognitivas no verbales avanzaron más en comunicación social en aulas inclusivas, no en las especializadas. Es un único estudio, con pocos participantes, y no predice qué le irá bien a cada niño. Conviene hablarlo con el equipo educativo.
sheet.en: When choosing between an inclusive and a specialised classroom for a preschool autistic child, it helps to notice their interests and how they engage with people, rather than assuming one setting suits everyone. This trial randomly assigned 58 autistic children to receive the same programme (G-ESDM) in one of the two classroom types for a year. On average, outcomes were similar. Children with more social interest and stronger nonverbal cognitive skills gained more in social communication in inclusive classrooms, but not in specialised ones. It is a single study with a small group, and it cannot predict what will work for an individual child. Talk it through with the educational team.
sheet.sv: När ni väljer mellan en inkluderande och en specialiserad förskoleklass för ett autistiskt barn kan det hjälpa att lägga märke till barnets intressen och hur det engagerar sig med andra, utan att anta att en miljö passar alla. I denna randomiserade studie fick 58 autistiska barn samma program (G-ESDM) i en av de två klasstyperna under ett år. I genomsnitt blev resultaten likartade. Barn med mer socialt intresse och starkare icke-verbal kognitiv förmåga gjorde större framsteg i social kommunikation i inkluderande klasser, men inte i specialiserade. Det är en enskild studie med få deltagare och den kan inte förutsäga vad som fungerar för just ditt barn. Diskutera det med förskolans team.

title: Coping-resilience profiles and experiences of stress in autistic adults.
authors: Muniandy M, Richdale AL, Lawson LP
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
abstract: Emerging studies allude to high stress in autistic adults. Considering the detrimental impact of stress on health outcomes, examining individual resources which may influence the extent to which stress is experienced (e.g., coping and resilience) is vital. Using a person-focused approach, this study aimed to identify coping-resilience profiles, and examine their relations to general perceived stress and daily hassles in a sample of autistic adults (N = 86; aged 19-74 years). Cluster analysis identified four coping-resilience profiles (i.e., high cope/ low resilience, low cope/ high resilience, engage cope/ high resilience, and disengage cope/ low resilience). The high cope/ low resilience and disengage cope/ low resilience groups had significantly higher general perceived stress than the remaining groups. No significant group differences were noted in relation to daily hassles. Jointly addressing coping and resilience may be beneficial on the perceived stress experienced in autistic adults. The use of coping-resilience profiles may also allow for the personalization of stress management and support options in the autistic adult population.

title: Effects of a Parenting Intervention for Emotional and Behavioral Problems in Young Autistic Children Under Conditions of Enhanced Uncertainty: Two-Year Follow-up of a Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial Cohort (ASTAR) During the United Kingdom COVID-19 Pandemic.
authors: Palmer M, Carter Leno V, Hallett V, Mueller JM, Breese L, Pickles A, Slonims V, Scott S, Charman T, Simonoff E
journal: Journal of the American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry
abstract: Objective Most young autistic children display emotional and behavioral problems (EBPs). There is evidence that behavioral parenting interventions (BPIs) reduce these. The COVID-19 pandemic and associated lockdowns can be seen as a natural experiment to test the longer-term effect of BPIs under conditions of increased uncertainty. Method Opportunistic follow-up (n = 49) of a pilot randomized controlled trial (RCT) cohort (n = 62 autistic children aged 6-11 years; originally randomized to a 12-week group BPI [Predictive Parenting; n = 31] or an attention control [Psychoeducation; n = 31]) was conducted during COVID-19-related lockdowns. Measures of parent-reported child irritability and parenting stress were collected at 3 time points (baseline: mean age = 6.7 years; primary endpoint: mean age = 7.1 years, ∼5 months after randomization; and COVID-19 follow-up: mean age = 8.8 years, ∼2 years after randomization). We tested the magnitude of intervention effects using point estimates of differences in child irritability and parenting stress between arms at primary endpoint and COVID-19 follow-up, covarying for baseline scores. We used area under the curve (AUC) analyses to obtain overall estimates of the average intervention effect across all 3 timepoints. Semi-structured qualitative interviews were conducted with a subsample of parents (n = 18). Results A small but significant intervention effect was found from baseline to COVID-19 follow-up in favor of Predictive Parenting on parent-reported child irritability (d = -0.33, 95% CI = -0.65, -0.01) and parenting stress (d = -0.31, 95% CI = -0.59, -0.03). No overall mean intervention effect for these measures as estimated by the AUC analyses (which takes into account the nonsignificant effect at primary endpoint) was found. Interview feedback on the both interventions was positive, and parents reported using strategies from Predictive Parenting during COVID-19-related restrictions. Conclusion This opportunistic follow-up study at a time of stress indicates the need for careful consideration of how and when to measure the effects of BPIs in autistic child populations. Future trials should consider both the most appropriate endpoint and in what context effects may be more likely to be seen. Clinical trial registration information Autism Spectrum Treatment and Resilience (ASTAR); https://www.isrctn.com; 91411078.

sheet.es: Si cuida de un niño autista pequeño, un programa grupal de crianza basado en la previsibilidad puede darle estrategias que siga usando en épocas de incertidumbre. Pruébelas con flexibilidad, según su hijo. Se trata de un ensayo piloto aleatorizado con seguimiento de 49 familias de niños autistas de 6-11 años; en entrevistas, madres y padres valoraron bien los programas y dijeron usar las estrategias durante los confinamientos. Los límites: el efecto fue pequeño, no apareció a los cinco meses ni en el promedio global, la muestra es reducida y los datos los aportaron las familias. No sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you care for a young autistic child, a group parenting programme built around predictability may give you strategies you keep using in uncertain times. Try them flexibly, to fit your child. This was a pilot randomised trial with a follow-up of 49 families of autistic children aged 6-11 years; in interviews, parents rated the programmes positively and said they used the strategies during lockdowns. Limits: the effect was small, it did not appear at about 5 months or in the overall average, the sample was small, and the data came from parent reports. It is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar ett litet autistiskt barn kan ett föräldraprogram i grupp med fokus på förutsägbarhet ge strategier du fortsätter använda i osäkra tider. Prova dem flexibelt, utifrån ditt barn. Studien var en randomiserad pilotstudie med uppföljning av 49 familjer med autistiska barn i åldern 6-11 år; i intervjuer var föräldrarna positiva till programmen och sa att de använde strategierna under nedstängningarna. Begränsningar: effekten var liten, syntes inte efter cirka 5 månader eller i det samlade genomsnittet, urvalet var litet och uppgifterna kom från föräldrarna. Det är ingen regel för alla.

title: Influence of past advanced behavior guidance experience on parental acceptance for autistic individuals in the dental setting.
authors: Manopetchkasem A, Srimaneekarn N, Leelataweewud P, Smutkeeree A
abstract: Background Autism is a lifelong neurodevelopmental disorder that poses challenges during dental treatment. Advanced behavior guidance techniques (BGTs) have been used to provide dental care for autistic people who have specific characteristics and complex dental treatment. This study was conducted to evaluate parental acceptance and analyze parents' opinions of advanced BGTs during dental treatment in autistic people. Methods This cross-sectional study was conducted on 141 parents of autistic people from the Mahidol Dental Hospital and the Autism online community. Informed consent was obtained before enrolling participants in the study. All parents were asked to rate their acceptance after watching VDO clips: passive restraint by device (PRBD), oral sedation (OS), and general anesthesia (GA) to evaluate parental acceptance of advanced BGTs through an online questionnaire survey. The online questionnaire included a visual analog scale (VAS) and open-ended questions to collect their opinions on each advanced BGT. Participants were categorized into two subgroups as follows: 81 in the "Experience group" and 60 in the "No experience group" according to their autistic people' advanced BGT experience. Friedman's two-way analysis of variance and the Mann-Whitney U test were used for statistical analyses. Open-ended questions were analyzed using quantitative content analysis. Results PRBD was ranked the highest, followed by GA and OS. Parents in the "Experience group" rated significantly higher acceptance of their BGT experience than parents in the "No experience group" in all the three advanced BGTs. Conclusions All advanced BGTs were particularly accepted in this study. Previous experience of advanced BGTs had an influence on parental acceptance. Parents commented on their opinions toward each advanced BGT with a variety of perspectives. Trial registration The protocol was approved by the ethical committee of the Faculty of Dentistry/Faculty of Pharmacy, Mahidol University (COA.No.MU-DT/PY-IRB 2021/022.1702) and was registered with Thai Clinical Trials Registry (TCTR20220521001).

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija autista necesita tratamiento dental complejo, hable con antelación con el equipo dental sobre las opciones de apoyo, y pregunte qué incluye cada una. Este estudio transversal encuestó a 141 madres y padres de personas autistas, que valoraron tres técnicas avanzadas tras ver videos: sujeción pasiva con dispositivo, sedación oral y anestesia general. Quienes ya tenían experiencia con estas técnicas las aceptaban más. Límites: recoge opiniones de familias, no la voz de las propias personas autistas ni resultados de salud, y no vale como regla para todas. Las decisiones médicas, incluidas sedación y anestesia, corresponden a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If your autistic child needs complex dental treatment, talk with the dental team beforehand about the support options and ask what each one involves. This cross-sectional study surveyed 141 parents of autistic people, who rated three advanced techniques after watching videos: passive restraint by device, oral sedation and general anesthesia. Parents who already had experience with these techniques accepted them more. Limits: it captures parents' opinions, not the views of autistic people themselves or health outcomes, and it is not a rule for every family. Medical decisions, including sedation and anesthesia, belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn behöver omfattande tandvård, prata med tandvårdsteamet i förväg om stödalternativen och fråga vad vart och ett innebär. Denna tvärsnittsstudie enkätade 141 föräldrar till autistiska personer, som bedömde tre avancerade tekniker efter att ha sett videoklipp: passiv fasthållning med hjälpmedel, oral sedering och narkos. Föräldrar med tidigare erfarenhet av teknikerna accepterade dem i högre grad. Begränsningar: studien visar föräldrars åsikter, inte autistiska personers egna eller hälsoutfall, och är ingen regel för alla familjer. Medicinska beslut, inklusive sedering och narkos, fattas tillsammans med en kliniker.

title: Factors associated with parental resolution of a child's autism diagnosis: A systematic review.
authors: Naicker VV, Bury SM, Hedley D
abstract: Background Receiving a child's autism diagnosis can be stressful; as such, parent resolution contributes to the wellbeing and development of healthy parent-child relationships. In other significant childhood diagnoses (e.g., cerebral palsy, diabetes), the degree to which parents adjust to (a) their child's diagnosis and (b) their changes in expectations concerning their child's development and capacity (referred to as resolution to diagnosis), has been associated with improved outcomes including facilitating parent-child relationships and improved parental wellbeing. Given potential benefits to parent and child, and the heterogenous nature of autism, examining the unique factors associated with resolution to diagnosis is important. In this systematic review we identified factors that support or inhibit parental resolution to their child receiving a diagnosis of autism. Methods We completed a systematic review following PRISMA guidelines of peer-reviewed studies from 2017 to 2022, that investigated parental resolution or acceptance of an autism diagnosis. Papers including "acceptance" needed to encompass both accepting the diagnosis and the implications regarding the child's abilities. We searched six databases (Scopus, Web of Science, MEDLINE, PsycINFO, ProQuest), with additional papers located following review of reference lists. Results Fourteen papers with 592 participants that investigated parental resolution or acceptance of an autism diagnosis, were included. We identified six common factors that facilitate or inhibit parental resolution and acceptance of an autism diagnosis including: symptom severity; religion, belief, and culture; knowledge and uncertainty; negative emotions (i.e., denial, shame, guilt); positive emotions; and support. Greater resolution was associated with improved "attunement and insightfulness" in the parent-child relationship. Limitation The review was limited by the small number of studies meeting inclusion criteria. Second, the quality of included studies was mixed, with over half of the studies being qualitative and only one randomized control trial (RCT) identified. Conclusion Parental resolution can have an impact on parent's perception of their child's capabilities and impact the parent-child relationship. We identified six categories that aid in inhibiting or promoting resolution to diagnosis. Despite taking a broad approach on the definition of resolution, the low number of studies identified in the review indicates a need for more research in this area. Systematic review registration http://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, PROSPERO [ID: CRD42022336283].

sheet.es: Si acabas de recibir el diagnóstico de autismo de tu hijo o hija, es normal que lleve tiempo asimilarlo. Puede ayudar hablar con otras familias, buscar información fiable y pedir apoyo a profesionales. Esta revisión sistemática analizó 14 estudios con 592 participantes e identificó seis factores que influyen en cómo las familias asumen el diagnóstico: intensidad de los rasgos, religión y cultura, conocimiento e incertidumbre, emociones negativas, emociones positivas y apoyo. Una mayor resolución se asoció con una relación más sintonizada entre madre o padre e hijo. Límites: hay pocos estudios, de calidad desigual, más de la mitad cualitativos y solo un ensayo aleatorizado. No es una regla para todas las familias.
sheet.en: If your child has just been diagnosed as autistic, it is normal for it to take time to sink in. Talking with other families, finding reliable information and asking professionals for support may help. This systematic review looked at 14 studies with 592 participants and found six factors linked to how parents come to terms with a diagnosis: symptom severity, religion and culture, knowledge and uncertainty, negative emotions, positive emotions, and support. Greater resolution was associated with a more attuned parent-child relationship. Limits: there were few studies of mixed quality, over half qualitative, with only one randomized trial. It is not a rule for every family.
sheet.sv: Om ditt barn nyss fått en autismdiagnos är det normalt att det tar tid att ta in. Det kan hjälpa att prata med andra familjer, hitta tillförlitlig information och be yrkespersoner om stöd. Den här systematiska översikten granskade 14 studier med 592 deltagare och fann sex faktorer kopplade till hur föräldrar kommer till rätta med en diagnos: symtomens svårighetsgrad, religion och kultur, kunskap och osäkerhet, negativa känslor, positiva känslor samt stöd. Större acceptans hängde samman med en mer avstämd relation mellan förälder och barn. Begränsningar: få studier av varierande kvalitet, över hälften kvalitativa och bara en randomiserad studie. Det är ingen regel för alla familjer.

title: For autistic persons by autistic persons: Acceptability of a structured peer support service according to key stakeholders.
authors: Valderrama A, Martinez A, Charlebois K, Guerrero L, Forgeot d'Arc B
journal: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy
abstract: Introduction Social support is a protective factor in the mental health of autistic people. Furthermore, prejudice regarding autistic people is a constraint for the development of social support programmes by autistic peers. Methods The objective of this study is to describe the anticipated acceptability of structured peer support programmes for and by autistic persons. Fifteen key stakeholders (six autistic adults, four caregivers and five service providers) participated in in-depth semistructured interviews. A qualitative thematic analysis of the content of the verbatim was carried out. Findings We found that while a structured peer social support programme is acceptable to autistic people and caregivers, there was no consensus among service providers. The latter expressed doubts about the ability of autistic people to offer support. The framing of discussions between peers, the training of peer helpers, the support for autistic leadership and an organization that considers the communicational and sensory characteristics of autistic persons, could influence adherence to such a programme. Moreover, a space without service providers is an important condition for the acceptability of a peer support programme. Conclusion A structured peer support service for and by autistic persons could be an innovative way to answer the unmet support needs of autistic people. It seems essential to anticipate potential barriers and facilitators and to communicate among health professionals to promote this approach and reduce possible prejudice about the ability of autistic people to offer support to their peers. More studies are necessary. Patient or public contribution Fifteen key stakeholders who are involved in autistic people's trajectory of service and support participated in this research. We are a research team composed of healthcare professionals and researchers, in addition to one member of our team being an autistic advocate and a mental health peer-support mentor. Two members of our team are also parents of autistic children. The comprehensibility of the questions for the interview was consulted and discussed with one autistic advocate-collaborator.

sheet.es: Si buscas apoyo para una persona autista, vale la pena explorar grupos de apoyo entre iguales dirigidos por personas autistas, con espacios sensoriales y de comunicación adaptados y, si ella lo prefiere, sin profesionales presentes. Es un estudio cualitativo con entrevistas a 15 participantes: seis adultos autistas, cuatro cuidadores y cinco profesionales. Los autistas y los cuidadores vieron el apoyo entre iguales como aceptable; entre los profesionales no hubo consenso. Mide la aceptabilidad prevista, no resultados reales, la muestra es pequeña y hacen falta más estudios. No sirve como regla para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you are looking for support for an autistic person, peer support groups led by autistic people are worth exploring, ideally with adapted communication and sensory settings and, if the person prefers, without service providers present. This was a qualitative interview study with 15 participants: six autistic adults, four caregivers and five service providers. Autistic people and caregivers found peer support acceptable, while providers did not agree. It measured expected acceptability, not real outcomes, the sample is small, and more studies are needed. It is not a rule for every person.
sheet.sv: Om du söker stöd åt en autistisk person är det värt att utforska stödgrupper mellan jämlikar som leds av autistiska personer, helst med anpassad kommunikation och sensorisk miljö och, om personen vill, utan yrkesverksamma närvarande. Det var en kvalitativ intervjustudie med 15 deltagare: sex autistiska vuxna, fyra anhöriga och fem yrkesverksamma. Autistiska personer och anhöriga såg stödet som acceptabelt, medan de yrkesverksamma inte var överens. Studien mätte förväntad acceptans, inte verkliga resultat, urvalet är litet och fler studier behövs. Den är ingen regel för alla.

title: The impact of COVID-19 on sleep for autistic children: A systematic review.
authors: Lewis S, Papadopoulos N, Mantilla A, Hiscock H, Whelan M, McGillivray J, Rinehart N

title: Reduced impact of nonverbal cues during integration of verbal and nonverbal emotional information in adults with high-functioning autism.
authors: Pelzl MA, Travers-Podmaniczky G, Brück C, Jacob H, Hoffmann J, Martinelli A, Hölz L, Wabersich-Flad D, Wildgruber D
abstract: Background When receiving mismatching nonverbal and verbal signals, most people tend to base their judgment regarding the current emotional state of others primarily on nonverbal information. However, individuals with high-functioning autism (HFA) have been described as having difficulties interpreting nonverbal signals. Recognizing emotional states correctly is highly important for successful social interaction. Alterations in perception of nonverbal emotional cues presumably contribute to misunderstanding and impairments in social interactions. Methods To evaluate autism-specific differences in the relative impact of nonverbal and verbal cues, 18 adults with HFA (14 male and four female subjects, mean age 36.7 years (SD 11.4) and 18 age, gender and IQ-matched typically developed controls [14 m/4 f, mean age 36.4 years (SD 12.2)] rated the emotional state of speakers in video sequences with partly mismatching emotional signals. Standardized linear regression coefficients were calculated as a measure of the reliance on the nonverbal and verbal components of the videos for each participant. Regression coefficients were then compared between groups to test the hypothesis that autistic adults base their social evaluations less strongly on nonverbal information. Further exploratory analyses were performed for differences in valence ratings and response times. Results Compared to the typically developed control group, nonverbal cue reliance was reduced in adults with high-functioning autism [ t (23.14) = -2.44, p = 0.01 (one-sided)]. Furthermore, the exploratory analyses showed a tendency to avoid extreme answers in the HFA group, observable via less positive as well as less negative valence ratings in response to emotional expressions of increasingly strong valence. In addition, response time was generally longer in HFA compared to the control group [ F (1, 33) = 10.65, p = 0.004]. Conclusion These findings suggest reduced impact of nonverbal cues and longer processing times in the analysis of multimodal emotional information, which may be associated with a subjectively lower relevance of this information and/or more processing difficulties for people with HFA. The less extreme answering tendency may indicate a lower sensitivity for nonverbal valence expression in HFA or result from a tendency to avoid incorrect answers when confronted with greater uncertainty in interpreting emotional states.

sheet.es: Si hablas con una persona autista, di con palabras lo que sientes o necesitas y no dejes que el tono o el gesto carguen con todo el mensaje. Dale también un poco más de tiempo para responder. El estudio comparó a 18 adultos autistas con 18 adultos no autistas de edad, género y CI similares, que valoraron las emociones de personas en vídeos con señales verbales y no verbales que no coincidían. Los adultos autistas se apoyaron menos en las señales no verbales y tardaron más en responder. Es un estudio pequeño, de una sola tarea en vídeo, y no describe a todas las personas autistas ni la vida cotidiana.
sheet.en: When talking with an autistic person, say in words what you feel or need, rather than letting tone or facial expression carry the whole message. Also allow a little more time for them to answer. The study compared 18 autistic adults with 18 non-autistic adults matched for age, gender and IQ, who rated the emotions of speakers in videos where verbal and nonverbal signals did not match. The autistic adults relied less on nonverbal cues and took longer to respond. It is a small study using one video task, so it does not describe every autistic person or everyday life.
sheet.sv: När du pratar med en autistisk person, säg med ord vad du känner eller behöver i stället för att låta tonfall eller ansiktsuttryck bära hela budskapet. Ge också lite mer tid att svara. Studien jämförde 18 autistiska vuxna med 18 icke-autistiska vuxna, matchade på ålder, kön och IQ, som bedömde känslor hos talare i videor där verbala och icke-verbala signaler inte stämde överens. De autistiska vuxna litade mindre på icke-verbala signaler och svarade långsammare. Studien är liten och använder en enda videouppgift, så den beskriver inte alla autistiska personer eller vardagen.

title: Self-reported Everyday Sources of Happiness and Unhappiness in Autistic Adults.
authors: Parenteau CI, Lampinen LA, Ghods SS, Taylor JL, Adams RE, Bishop SL, Zheng S
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders

title: A Systematic Review of Therapeutic Process Factors in Mental Health Treatment for Autistic Youth.
authors: Albaum CS, Vashi N, Bohr Y, Weiss JA
journal: Clinical child and family psychology review
abstract: Understanding the role of therapeutic process factors in treatment change may prove useful for discerning why some autistic youth benefit from psychosocial interventions that target emotional and psychological aspects of mental health, while others do not. The aim of the current study was to synthesize what is currently known about therapeutic process factors in mental health treatment of emotional and psychological challenges for autistic youth, regarding how process factors have been measured in past research, and the relation between process factors and treatment outcome. A systematic review of the literature was conducted to narratively synthesize all articles published up until June 2021. Methodological quality of included studies was appraised. Twenty-five studies met inclusion criteria. Process factors assessed across studies included relational factors; treatment expectations, readiness, and satisfaction; and treatment engagement from youth and their parents. Process-outcome associations were reported for a limited number of constructs. There is a limited, albeit growing, body of high-quality research evaluating the role of process factors in the treatment of mental health issues for autistic youth. Future research should continue to examine process factors in relation to treatment outcome, and validate measures to accurately capture process-related constructs in mental health treatment for this population. Greater understanding of therapy processes can lead to developing evidence-informed strategies that clinicians can implement to promote positive expectations, relationships, and engagement.

sheet.es: Si su hijo o hija autista va a terapia para el bienestar emocional, puede ayudar fijarse en cómo se siente con el terapeuta, qué espera del tratamiento y cuánto participa, y comentarlo con el profesional. Esta revisión sistemática reunió 25 estudios sobre jóvenes autistas y sus familias. Encontró que estos aspectos del proceso se han medido de formas distintas y que se sabe poco sobre cómo se relacionan con los resultados. Por eso no permite afirmar qué funciona para cada persona; la investigación sigue creciendo.
sheet.en: If your autistic child or teen is in therapy for emotional wellbeing, it may help to notice how they feel about the therapist, what they expect from treatment, and how engaged they are, and to talk about this with the clinician. This systematic review gathered 25 studies on autistic youth and their parents. It found these process factors were measured in different ways, and links with outcomes were reported for only a limited number of them. So it cannot tell us what works for any one person; the research is still growing.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn eller din autistiska tonåring går i terapi för känslomässigt mående kan det hjälpa att lägga märke till hur hen upplever terapeuten, vad hen förväntar sig av behandlingen och hur delaktig hen är, och att ta upp det med behandlaren. Den här systematiska översikten samlade 25 studier om autistiska unga och deras föräldrar. Den visade att dessa processfaktorer mäts på olika sätt och att samband med resultat rapporterades för ett begränsat antal. Den kan därför inte säga vad som fungerar för just din person; forskningen växer fortfarande.

title: Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on Autistic Adults: a Scoping Review.
authors: Scheeren AM, Crane L, Heyworth M, Pellicano E
abstract: Purpose of review The COVID-19 pandemic and its associated restrictions have had a significant impact on people's everyday lives, including the lives of Autistic adults. We aimed to (a) synthesise all papers currently published on the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on autistic adults and (b) identify lessons for the care and support of Autistic adults in pandemic and post-pandemic times. Recent findings Fifty-five papers met the inclusion criteria. Most studies focused on the pandemic's impact on the wellbeing of Autistic adults. Several studies focused on the use of (telehealth) services or the risk of COVID-19 infection/hospitalisation. Summary Autistic adults were significantly impacted by the pandemic, both directly as indicated by higher COVID-19 infection and hospitalisation rates, but also indirectly due to severe service disruptions and social restrictions. Even though there were large differences observed both between as well as within individuals in terms of the negative/positive effects of the COVID-19 pandemic, most studies reported a negative effect on Autistic adults' mental health. We draw several lessons from this review for the future care and support of Autistic adults, all of which must be underpinned by participatory research methods, that is, where Autistic community members are actively involved in setting research questions, testing the acceptability of the methods and interpreting and disseminating the results. Supplementary information The online version contains supplementary material available at 10.1007/s40474-023-00268-6.

sheet.es: Si cuidas o apoyas a una persona autista adulta, pregúntale cómo le han afectado los cambios de rutina y la pérdida de servicios, y qué apoyos le ayudarían ahora. Es una revisión sistemática que reunió 55 artículos sobre el impacto de la pandemia de COVID-19 en personas autistas adultas. La mayoría de los estudios informó un efecto negativo en la salud mental, aunque hubo grandes diferencias entre personas y también efectos positivos. Los resultados no describen a todas las personas, y la revisión no indica qué apoyo concreto funciona mejor. Cada persona vive esta experiencia a su manera.
sheet.en: If you care for or support an autistic adult, ask how changes to routine and lost services affected them, and which supports would help now. This is a systematic review that gathered 55 papers on the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on autistic adults. Most studies reported a negative effect on mental health, though there were large differences between and within individuals, and some positive effects too. The findings do not describe every person, and the review does not show which specific support works best. Each person lives this experience in their own way.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen, fråga hur ändrade rutiner och indragna insatser har påverkat hen och vilket stöd som skulle hjälpa nu. Det här är en systematisk översikt som samlade 55 artiklar om hur covid-19-pandemin påverkade autistiska vuxna. De flesta studierna rapporterade en negativ effekt på den psykiska hälsan, men det fanns stora skillnader mellan och inom individer, och även positiva effekter. Resultaten gäller inte alla, och översikten visar inte vilket specifikt stöd som fungerar bäst. Varje person upplever detta på sitt sätt.

title: Parent-Child Interaction Therapy for Children with Disruptive Behaviors and Autism: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
authors: Allen K, Harrington J, Quetsch LB, Masse J, Cooke C, Paulson JF
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: A relatively large number of children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) exhibit disruptive behavioral problems. While accumulating data have shown behavioral parent training programs to be efficacious in reducing disruptive behaviors for this population, there is a dearth of literature examining the impact of such programs across the range of ASD severity. To evaluate the effectiveness of Parent-Child Interaction Therapy (PCIT), an evidence-based treatment for children with problem behaviors and their families, in reducing disruptive behaviors among children (4-10 years) with ASD (without intellectual disabilities). Fifty-five children (85.5% male, 7.15 years; SD 1.72) were enrolled from pediatric offices and educational settings into a randomized clinical trial (PCIT: N = 30; Control: N = 25). PCIT families demonstrated a significant reduction in child disruptive behaviors, increase in positive parent-child communication, improvement in child compliance, and reduction in parental stress compared to the control group. Exploratory analyses revealed no differential treatment response based on ASD severity, receptive language, and age. Results are promising for the use of PCIT with children demonstrating disruptive behaviors across the autism spectrum.

sheet.es: Si su hijo autista tiene momentos de mucha oposición o explosividad, un programa de entrenamiento para familias como la Terapia de Interacción Padres-Hijos (PCIT) puede ser una opción que vale la pena consultar con un profesional. Se centra en la comunicación positiva entre ambos. Fue un ensayo aleatorizado con 55 niños de 4-10 años con autismo sin discapacidad intelectual (PCIT: 30; control: 25). El grupo PCIT mostró menos conductas disruptivas, más comunicación positiva, más cooperación y menos estrés parental. Límites: muestra pequeña, mayoría de niños varones, sin discapacidad intelectual; los análisis sobre gravedad, lenguaje y edad fueron exploratorios. No sirve igual para todas las familias.
sheet.en: If your autistic child has times of strong opposition or meltdowns, a parent training programme such as Parent-Child Interaction Therapy (PCIT) may be worth discussing with a professional. It focuses on positive communication between you and your child. This was a randomized trial with 55 children aged 4-10 with autism and without intellectual disability (PCIT: 30; control: 25). The PCIT group showed fewer disruptive behaviors, more positive communication, more compliance and less parental stress. Limits: small sample, mostly boys, no children with intellectual disability; the analyses on severity, language and age were exploratory. It will not fit every family the same way.
sheet.sv: Om ditt autistiska barn har stunder med starkt motstånd eller utbrott kan ett föräldraträningsprogram som Parent-Child Interaction Therapy (PCIT) vara värt att diskutera med en professionell. Det fokuserar på positiv kommunikation mellan dig och barnet. Det var en randomiserad studie med 55 barn i åldern 4-10 med autism utan intellektuell funktionsnedsättning (PCIT: 30; kontroll: 25). PCIT-gruppen visade mindre störande beteenden, mer positiv kommunikation, bättre följsamhet och mindre stress hos föräldrarna.
