Begränsningar: litet urval, mest pojkar, inga barn med intellektuell funktionsnedsättning; analyserna av svårighetsgrad, språk och ålder var explorativa. Det passar inte alla familjer lika bra.

title: Dendritic spine and synapse pathology in chromatin modifier-associated autism spectrum disorders and intellectual disability.
authors: Ford TJL, Jeon BT, Lee H, Kim WY
abstract: Formation of dendritic spine and synapse is an essential final step of brain wiring to establish functional communication in the developing brain. Recent findings have displayed altered dendritic spine and synapse morphogenesis, plasticity, and related molecular mechanisms in animal models and post-mortem human brains of autism spectrum disorders (ASD) and intellectual disability (ID). Many genes and proteins are shown to be associated with spines and synapse development, and therefore neurodevelopmental disorders. In this review, however, particular attention will be given to chromatin modifiers such as AT-Rich Interactive Domain 1B (ARID1B), KAT8 regulatory non-specific lethal (NSL) complex subunit 1 (KANSL1), and WD Repeat Domain 5 (WDR5) which are among strong susceptibility factors for ASD and ID. Emerging evidence highlights the critical status of these chromatin remodeling molecules in dendritic spine morphogenesis and synaptic functions. Molecular and cellular insights of ARID1B, KANSL1, and WDR5 will integrate into our current knowledge in understanding and interpreting the pathogenesis of ASD and ID. Modulation of their activities or levels may be an option for potential therapeutic treatment strategies for these neurodevelopmental conditions.

sheet.es: Esta revisión no ofrece nada que hacer mañana por la mañana: es ciencia básica sobre cómo se forman las conexiones cerebrales. Si te preguntan por ella, puedes decir que ayuda a entender algunas bases biológicas de ciertas formas de autismo y discapacidad intelectual. Es una revisión de hallazgos en modelos animales y en cerebros humanos post mortem, centrada en los genes ARID1B, KANSL1 y WDR5. Sus límites: no evalúa ninguna intervención con personas y no se aplica a todas las personas autistas. Cualquier decisión médica corresponde a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: This review offers nothing to act on tomorrow morning: it is basic science on how connections in the brain form. If someone asks, you can say it helps explain some biological foundations of certain forms of autism and intellectual disability. It reviews findings from animal models and post-mortem human brains, focused on the genes ARID1B, KANSL1 and WDR5. Its limits: it tests no support or intervention with people, and it does not apply to every autistic person. Any medical decision belongs to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Den här översikten ger inget att göra i morgon bitti: det är grundforskning om hur kopplingar i hjärnan bildas. Om någon frågar kan du säga att den hjälper till att förklara biologiska grunder för vissa former av autism och intellektuell funktionsnedsättning. Den sammanfattar fynd från djurmodeller och från mänskliga hjärnor efter döden, med fokus på generna ARID1B, KANSL1 och WDR5. Begränsningar: den prövar inget stöd eller någon insats med människor och gäller inte alla autistiska personer. Medicinska beslut hör till en läkare.

title: Sex differences in predictors and outcomes of camouflaging: Comparing diagnosed autistic, high autistic trait and low autistic trait young adults.
authors: Milner V, Mandy W, Happé F, Colvert E
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: Lay abstract Many autistic people use strategies that help them adapt in social situations and hide behaviours that may seem different to non-autistic individuals - this is called camouflaging. Camouflaging may help autistic people fit in socially; however, it might also lead to poorer well-being. It has been suggested that autistic females camouflage more than autistic males. This article explored differences between males and females who have an autism diagnosis, have characteristics of autism but no diagnosis and those with few autistic characteristics. It is important to include these groups as camouflaging may make it more difficult to get an autism diagnosis and therefore make it less likely a person will receive support. We found that autistic women camouflaged more than all other groups. The group with few autistic characteristics (males and females) camouflaged the least. Loneliness was found to be a possible reason for camouflaging for the diagnosed autistic group only. In terms of outcomes related to camouflaging, it was found that those who camouflaged most had a lower quality of life; this was true of all groups. This tells us that there may be different reasons to camouflage, and different outcomes related to camouflaging for those with many characteristics of autism (including those with a diagnosis), and those with few. It is important that clinicians, teachers, parents and other stakeholders are aware of the negative outcomes associated with camouflaging so that more support can be provided for those who need it.

sheet.es: Si tu familiar autista se esfuerza mucho por «encajar» ocultando sus rasgos, ese esfuerzo puede tener un coste. Mañana puedes ofrecer espacios donde no tenga que disimular, preguntar con calma cómo se siente tras situaciones sociales y valorar que la soledad puede empujar a camuflarse. Recuerda que una persona que camufla puede tener más dificultades para obtener diagnóstico y apoyos. Este estudio comparó a adultos jóvenes con diagnóstico autista, con muchos rasgos autistas sin diagnóstico y con pocos rasgos: las mujeres autistas camuflaban más, y camuflar más se asoció con peor calidad de vida en todos los grupos. Es un estudio de asociación, no demuestra causa, y no describe a cada persona.
sheet.en: If your autistic family member works hard to “fit in” by hiding their traits, that effort may come at a cost. Tomorrow you could offer spaces where they don't need to mask, gently ask how they feel after social situations, and notice that loneliness may drive camouflaging. Someone who camouflages may also find it harder to get a diagnosis and support. This study compared young adults with an autism diagnosis, with many autistic traits but no diagnosis, and with few traits: autistic women camouflaged most, and more camouflaging was linked to lower quality of life in every group. It shows associations, not causes, and does not describe every person.
sheet.sv: Om din autistiska närstående anstränger sig mycket för att ”passa in” genom att dölja sina drag kan det ha ett pris. I morgon kan du erbjuda platser där hen inte behöver maskera, lugnt fråga hur hen mår efter sociala situationer och vara uppmärksam på att ensamhet kan driva kamouflering. Den som kamouflerar kan också få svårare att få diagnos och stöd. Studien jämförde unga vuxna med autismdiagnos, med många autistiska drag utan diagnos och med få drag: autistiska kvinnor kamouflerade mest, och mer kamouflering hängde ihop med lägre livskvalitet i alla grupper. Den visar samband, inte orsaker, och gäller inte varje person.

title: The psychological impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on children/adolescents with ASD and their family environment: a systematic review.
authors: Milea-Milea AC, Fernández-Pérez D, Toledano-González A
abstract: The main objective of the review is to analyze the impact of the pandemic in children/teenagers with Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and in their family environment. An electronic search was carried out in different databases (PsycInfo, Web of Science and Scopus) in order to find publications associated with the aim of this project. The search terms used were derived from the combination of the following search string: "((Pandemic OR Epidemic OR Outbreak OR COVID-19 OR Coronavirus) AND (Children OR Adolescents OR Youth OR Child OR Teenager) AND (Autism OR ASD OR Autism Spectrum Disorder))''. In total, 21 articles were included in this review. The findings of the different investigations included in this review show that the pandemic has produced a negative psychological impact in children/teenagers with ASD. Therefore, long-term follow-up studies should be carried out with the objective of creating effective interventions to treat this problematical.

sheet.es: Si la familia atravesó la pandemia, es normal que aún queden huellas emocionales: conviene observar con calma cómo está hoy la persona autista y cómo está el resto de la familia, y pedir apoyo si se necesita. Esta revisión sistemática buscó en tres bases de datos e incluyó 21 artículos sobre niños y adolescentes autistas y sus familias; sus resultados indican un impacto psicológico negativo de la pandemia. Sin embargo, el resumen no detalla qué tan intenso fue ni en quién, y pide estudios de seguimiento a largo plazo. No es una regla para cada persona: cada familia vivió esa etapa de forma distinta.
sheet.en: If your family lived through the pandemic, it is normal that some emotional traces remain: it helps to calmly notice how the autistic young person is doing now, and how the rest of the family is, and to ask for support if needed. This systematic review searched three databases and included 21 articles on autistic children and teenagers and their families; its findings point to a negative psychological impact of the pandemic. However, the abstract does not say how strong the impact was or for whom, and it calls for long-term follow-up studies. It is not a rule for every person: each family experienced that period differently.
sheet.sv: Om din familj genomlevde pandemin är det normalt att några känslomässiga spår finns kvar: det kan hjälpa att lugnt se hur den autistiska personen mår nu, hur resten av familjen mår, och att be om stöd vid behov. Den här systematiska översikten sökte i tre databaser och inkluderade 21 artiklar om autistiska barn och tonåringar och deras familjer; resultaten pekar på en negativ psykologisk påverkan av pandemin. Sammanfattningen anger dock inte hur stark påverkan var eller för vem, och efterlyser långtidsuppföljningar. Det är ingen regel för alla: varje familj upplevde den tiden olika.

title: "Work WITH us": a Delphi study about improving eating disorder treatment for autistic women with anorexia nervosa.
authors: Field SL, Fox JRE, Jones CRG, Williams MO
abstract: Background There is an increased prevalence of anorexia nervosa (AN) in autistic women and this group has poorer treatment outcomes compared to non-autistic women with AN. However, there is little research into improving eating disorder treatment for autistic women. This study investigated how best to support autistic women with AN within eating disorder services. Method A three-stage Delphi study was conducted with 49 participants with relevant expertise as a researcher, clinician, or expert by experience. Results A total of 70 statements were generated, with 56 reaching consensus after the final round. Statements reaching consensus made recommendations for adaptations to treatment, staff training, and service organisation. Conclusions The results highlight the need to distinguish between autism- and AN-related difficulties, accommodate autistic traits such as sensory sensitivities and communication differences, and ensure the autistic voice is present in both the development and delivery of care. Future research should investigate the impact of these adaptations on outcomes. The applicability of these recommendations to autistic people with other eating disorders and of other genders needs to be investigated further.

sheet.es: Si acompañas a una mujer autista en tratamiento por anorexia, puedes pedir al equipo que distinga qué viene del autismo (por ejemplo, rutinas o sensibilidad a texturas) y qué de la anorexia, que adapte el entorno sensorial y la forma de comunicarse, y que ella participe en las decisiones sobre su cuidado. Lleva una lista breve de sus necesidades sensoriales y comunicativas a la próxima cita. Es un estudio Delphi: 49 personas expertas (investigadoras, clínicas y mujeres con experiencia propia) llegaron a consenso en 56 recomendaciones. Su límite: son opiniones expertas, aún no se ha comprobado si mejoran los resultados, ni si sirven para otros géneros u otros trastornos alimentarios.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic woman in treatment for anorexia, you can ask the team to separate what comes from being autistic (such as routines or texture sensitivity) from what comes from anorexia, to adapt the sensory environment and communication style, and to involve her in decisions about her care. Bring a short list of her sensory and communication needs to the next appointment. This was a Delphi study: 49 experts (researchers, clinicians and women with lived experience) reached consensus on 56 recommendations. Its limit: these are expert views; it has not yet been tested whether they improve outcomes, or whether they apply to other genders or other eating disorders.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk kvinna som får behandling för anorexi kan du be teamet skilja på vad som hör till autismen (till exempel rutiner eller känslighet för konsistenser) och vad som hör till anorexin, anpassa sensorisk miljö och kommunikation, och låta henne vara delaktig i beslut om sin vård. Ta med en kort lista över hennes sensoriska och kommunikativa behov till nästa besök. Detta var en Delphistudie: 49 experter (forskare, kliniker och kvinnor med egen erfarenhet) enades om 56 rekommendationer. Begränsning: det är expertåsikter, och det är ännu inte prövat om de förbättrar resultaten eller gäller andra kön och andra ätstörningar.

title: Sex-specific mechanisms for eating disorder risk in men and women with autistic traits: the role of alexithymia.
authors: Moseley RL, Atkinson C, Surman R, Greville-Harris M, May L, Vuillier L
abstract: Background A poorly understood relationship exists between eating disorders (ED) and autism spectrum conditions (ASC: henceforth 'autism'). ED are more prevalent in autistic people and people with high autistic traits, and autistic features are prognostic of longer illness. Aiming to understand what increases the risk of ED in relation to autism and autistic traits, previous research has implicated alexithymia as a causal mechanism in this relationship. These studies could not, however, disentangle whether alexithymia explains the relationship between ED pathology and autistic traits directly or through its impact on anxious/depressive symptoms, which in turn result in higher ED symptomatology. Moreover, despite evidence for sex differences in the aetiology of ED, little research has examined the impact of sex on these relationships. Methods Focusing on the association between autistic traits and ED psychopathology, we examined independent mediating effects of alexithymia and anxious/depressive symptoms, as well as sequential mediation effects where alexithymia affects ED psychopathology via its impact on anxious/depressive symptoms. Participants were 198 men and 265 women with formally diagnosed and suspected ED, who completed an online survey of standardised scales. Results In men, higher autistic traits were associated with ED psychopathology sequentially via greater alexithymia and through that, greater depressive/anxious symptoms. In women, alexithymia mediated the relationship between autistic traits and ED psychopathology both directly and sequentially through its impact on anxious/depressive symptoms. Interestingly, depressive/anxious symptoms also mediated that relationship independently from alexithymia. Conclusions While cross-sectional, these findings suggest that the relationship between autistic traits and ED symptomatology is mediated by other variables. In support of its proposed role in the aetiology of ED, alexithymia was directly associated with ED symptoms in women. It also affected ED symptoms indirectly, in all participants, via its effect on depressive/anxious symptoms. Interventions focusing on alexithymia may facilitate recovery not only via their effect on ED, but via their effect on other forms of state psychopathology which contribute to the maintenance and development of ED. Sex differences, however, reflect that alternative therapeutic targets for men and women may be beneficial.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista tiene dificultades con la comida, puede ayudar prestar atención a cómo identifica y nombra sus emociones (alexitimia), además de la ansiedad y el ánimo bajo. Un profesional de trastornos alimentarios que conozca el autismo puede valorarlo. Es un estudio transversal con una encuesta en línea: 198 hombres y 265 mujeres con trastorno alimentario diagnosticado o sospechado. Los caminos parecían distintos en hombres y mujeres. Sus límites: una sola medición no prueba causas, se midieron rasgos autistas y no todos los participantes eran autistas, y no sirve como regla para cada persona.
sheet.en: If an autistic person struggles with eating, it may help to look at how they notice and name their emotions (alexithymia), alongside anxiety and low mood. An eating disorder clinician who understands autism can assess this. This was a cross-sectional online survey of 198 men and 265 women with diagnosed or suspected eating disorders. The pathways looked different for men and women. Limits: a single time point cannot prove cause, it measured autistic traits rather than only autistic people, and it is not a rule for any one person.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person har svårt med mat kan det hjälpa att se på hur hen märker och sätter ord på känslor (alexitymi), vid sidan av ångest och nedstämdhet. En ätstörningsklinik med kunskap om autism kan bedöma detta. Det var en tvärsnittsstudie med webbenkät bland 198 män och 265 kvinnor med diagnostiserad eller misstänkt ätstörning. Sambanden såg olika ut för män och kvinnor. Begränsningar: ett enda mättillfälle kan inte visa orsak, studien mätte autistiska drag och inte bara autistiska personer, och den är ingen regel för en enskild person.

title: How to Make the Unpredictable Foreseeable? Effective Forms of Assistance for Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) during the COVID-19 Pandemic.
authors: Grzejszczak J, Gabryelska A, Gmitrowicz A, Strzelecki D
abstract: Symptomatology in patients with the diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is very heterogeneous. The symptoms they present include communication difficulties, behavior problems, upbringing problems from their parents, and comorbidities (e.g., epilepsy, intellectual disability). A predictable and stable environment and the continuity of therapeutic interactions are crucial in this population. The COVID-19 pandemic has created much concern, and the need for home isolation to limit the spread of the virus has disrupted the functioning routine of children/adolescents with ASD. Are there effective diagnostic and therapeutic alternatives to limit the consequences of disturbing the daily routine of young patients during the unpredictable times of the pandemic? Modern technology and telemedicine have come to the rescue. This narrative review aims to present a change in the impact profile in the era of isolation and assess the directions of changes that specialists may choose when dealing with patients with ASD.

sheet.es: Cuando la rutina se interrumpe, ayuda anticipar los cambios y mantener todo lo posible la continuidad de los apoyos, por ejemplo con sesiones a distancia si las ofrece el equipo profesional. Es una revisión narrativa que reunió información sobre niños y adolescentes autistas durante el aislamiento por la COVID-19, y señala que un entorno predecible y la continuidad terapéutica son importantes. Sus límites: no es un ensayo que compare métodos, el resumen no indica qué ayuda funcionó mejor y cada persona necesita apoyos distintos. Conviene hablarlo con el equipo que acompaña a su hijo o hija.
sheet.en: When routines are disrupted, it helps to prepare for changes in advance and keep supports as continuous as possible, for example through remote sessions if your professional team offers them. This is a narrative review about autistic children and adolescents during COVID-19 isolation, and it points to a predictable environment and continuity of therapy as important. Its limits: it is not a trial comparing methods, the abstract does not say which support worked best, and every person needs different supports. It is worth discussing with the team who supports your child.
sheet.sv: När rutiner bryts hjälper det att förbereda förändringar i förväg och behålla stödet så sammanhängande som möjligt, till exempel genom distansmöten om vårdteamet erbjuder det. Detta är en narrativ översikt om autistiska barn och ungdomar under isoleringen i covid-19-pandemin, och den lyfter fram en förutsägbar miljö och kontinuitet i insatser som viktiga. Begränsningar: det är inte en studie som jämför metoder, sammanfattningen anger inte vilket stöd som fungerade bäst, och varje person behöver olika stöd. Det är värt att prata om med teamet kring ditt barn.

title: Autism Spectrum Disorder: Neurodevelopmental Risk Factors, Biological Mechanism, and Precision Therapy.
authors: Wang L, Wang B, Wu C, Wang J, Sun M
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous, behaviorally defined neurodevelopmental disorder. Over the past two decades, the prevalence of autism spectrum disorders has progressively increased, however, no clear diagnostic markers and specifically targeted medications for autism have emerged. As a result, neurobehavioral abnormalities, neurobiological alterations in ASD, and the development of novel ASD pharmacological therapy necessitate multidisciplinary collaboration. In this review, we discuss the development of multiple animal models of ASD to contribute to the disease mechanisms of ASD, as well as new studies from multiple disciplines to assess the behavioral pathology of ASD. In addition, we summarize and highlight the mechanistic advances regarding gene transcription, RNA and non-coding RNA translation, abnormal synaptic signaling pathways, epigenetic post-translational modifications, brain-gut axis, immune inflammation and neural loop abnormalities in autism to provide a theoretical basis for the next step of precision therapy. Furthermore, we review existing autism therapy tactics and limits and present challenges and opportunities for translating multidisciplinary knowledge of ASD into clinical practice.

sheet.es: Lo práctico: esta revisión no ofrece nada que cambie la rutina de mañana. Sirve de contexto: describe el autismo como una condición diversa y explica que aún no hay marcadores diagnósticos claros ni tratamientos dirigidos específicos. Si te preocupa algo concreto, habla con el equipo profesional que acompaña a la persona. Sobre la evidencia: es una revisión de la literatura que reúne estudios con modelos animales y de varias disciplinas sobre genes, sinapsis, eje cerebro-intestino e inflamación inmune. Límites: es teórica, no probó ninguna intervención en personas y no debe verse como regla para todas las personas autistas. Las decisiones médicas corresponden siempre a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: The practical takeaway: this review offers nothing that changes tomorrow's routine. It is background reading. It describes autism as a diverse condition and notes there are still no clear diagnostic markers or specifically targeted treatments. If something concerns you, talk with the professional team supporting the person. On the evidence: it is a literature review that brings together animal-model and multidisciplinary studies on genes, synapses, the brain-gut axis and immune inflammation. Its limits: it is theoretical, did not test any intervention with people, and should not be read as a rule for every autistic person. Medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Det praktiska: den här översikten ger inget som ändrar morgondagens rutiner. Den är bakgrundsläsning. Den beskriver autism som ett varierat tillstånd och konstaterar att det ännu saknas tydliga diagnostiska markörer och specifikt riktade behandlingar. Om något oroar dig, prata med teamet som stöttar personen. Om evidensen: det är en litteraturöversikt som samlar djurmodeller och studier från flera discipliner om gener, synapser, tarm-hjärn-axeln och immuninflammation. Begränsningar: den är teoretisk, prövade ingen insats på människor och ska inte ses som en regel för alla autistiska personer. Medicinska beslut hör hemma hos en läkare.

title: Affectivity and Sexuality in Adolescents with Autism Spectrum Disorder from the Perspective of Education and Healthcare Professionals: A Qualitative Study.
authors: Torralbas-Ortega J, Valls-Ibáñez V, Roca J, Sastre-Rus M, Campoy-Guerrero C, Sala-Corbinos D, Sánchez-Fernández M
journal: International journal of environmental research and public health
abstract: People with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) present several different characteristics that predispose them to greater difficulties with intimate emotional and sexual relationships. This qualitative study uncovers the perspective of education and healthcare professionals on the affective and sexual needs of young people with ASD by analysing their narratives in semi-structured focus group sessions. Professionals highlight the inadequate training they receive in this aspect of health. They consider it should be commonplace for professionals working with autistic people as it would aid their collaborative efforts when treating children and adolescents with ASD. They show that, by working together with the families to establish joint objectives, these professionals can appropriately address sex and affective education, preventing risky behaviours among young people with ASD, and improving the interactions these individuals have with others. Sex and affective education is described as an indispensable tool at this stage of development and should be specially adapted for those with ASD.

sheet.es: Hablar de afectividad y sexualidad con adolescentes autistas forma parte de su educación, y conviene hacerlo con adaptaciones. Una idea útil es fijar objetivos comunes entre la familia y los profesionales que les acompañan. Es un estudio cualitativo en el que profesionales de la educación y de la salud compartieron su perspectiva en grupos de discusión. Los propios adolescentes autistas no participaron, así que no recoge su voz, y no demuestra qué método funciona mejor. Los profesionales dijeron que reciben poca formación en este tema. Cada persona es distinta, así que conviene adaptar la conversación a su ritmo y sus necesidades.
sheet.en: Talking about affection and sexuality with autistic teenagers is part of their education, and it helps to adapt it to them. One useful idea is to set shared goals between the family and the professionals who support them. This is a qualitative study in which education and healthcare professionals shared their views in focus groups. The autistic teenagers themselves did not take part, so their voices are missing, and it does not show which approach works best. The professionals said they receive inadequate training on this topic. Every person is different, so adjust the conversation to their pace and needs.
sheet.sv: Att prata om närhet, känslor och sexualitet med autistiska tonåringar är en del av deras utbildning, och det hjälper att anpassa samtalen. En användbar idé är att sätta gemensamma mål mellan familjen och de yrkesverksamma som stödjer dem. Det här är en kvalitativ studie där yrkesverksamma inom utbildning och hälso- och sjukvård delade sina synpunkter i fokusgrupper. De autistiska tonåringarna själva deltog inte, så deras röster saknas, och studien visar inte vilket arbetssätt som fungerar bäst. De yrkesverksamma sa att de får otillräcklig utbildning i ämnet. Alla är olika, så anpassa samtalet efter personens tempo och behov.

title: Effects of Equine-Assisted Activities and Therapies for Individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Xiao N, Shinwari K, Kiselev S, Huang X, Li B, Qi J
journal: International journal of environmental research and public health
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) has become a critical public health issue that affects more than 78 million people. In many recent studies, the authors have demonstrated that equine-assisted activities and therapies (EAATs) can substantially improve the social and behavioral skills of children with ASD. However, the qualities of the studies differ, and some authors reached opposite conclusions. In this review, we systematically and objectively examined the effectiveness of EAATs for people with ASD, combining both qualitative and quantitative methods. We searched five databases (PubMed, Scopus, ERIC, ProQuest, and MEDLINE) and added relevant references, and we identified 25 articles for data extraction and analysis. According to our results, EAAT programs can substantially improve the social and behavioral functioning and language abilities of children with ASD. However, among the subdomains, the results were inconsistent. According to the meta-analyses, there were considerable improvements in the social cognition, communication, irritability, and hyperactivity domains, but not in the domains of social awareness, mannerisms, motivation, lethargy, stereotypy, or inappropriate speech. Moreover, there was a lack of sufficient comparative data to conclude that EAAT programs lead to substantial improvements in motor and sensory functioning. In addition, among the included studies, we noted the indicator of whether EAAT programs decreased parental stress and improved family functioning, and although there were four articles in which the researchers considered this aspect, we were unable to draw any conclusions because of the insufficient data and conflicting descriptive evidence. However, we need to consider the improvement in parental mental health as a factor in the effectiveness of this complementary intervention. We hope that in future studies, researchers will focus on family functioning and conduct more randomized controlled trials (RCTs) with blinded assessments using different scales and measures.

sheet.es: Si piensa en actividades con caballos para una persona autista, puede probarlas como una opción más, observando si a esa persona le gustan y le sientan bien. Es un metaanálisis de 25 artículos, centrado en niños autistas, que halló mejoras en cognición social, comunicación, irritabilidad e hiperactividad, pero no en otras áreas, como la motivación o el habla inapropiada. Los resultados fueron desiguales, faltaron datos sobre lo motor y lo sensorial, y no se pudo concluir nada sobre el estrés de las familias. Los estudios variaban en calidad, y esto no vale para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you are considering horse-based activities for an autistic person, you could try them as one option, watching whether the person enjoys them and feels good. This was a meta-analysis of 25 articles, focused on autistic children. It found improvements in social cognition, communication, irritability and hyperactivity, but not in other areas such as motivation or inappropriate speech. Results were uneven, data on motor and sensory skills were lacking, and nothing could be concluded about family stress. Study quality varied, and this does not apply to every person.
sheet.sv: Om ni funderar på hästaktiviteter för en autistisk person kan ni prova dem som ett alternativ och se om personen trivs och mår bra av det. Detta var en metaanalys av 25 artiklar, med fokus på autistiska barn. Den fann förbättringar i social kognition, kommunikation, irritabilitet och hyperaktivitet, men inte inom andra områden som motivation eller olämpligt tal. Resultaten var ojämna, data om motorik och sinnesintryck saknades, och inga slutsatser kunde dras om familjers stress. Studiernas kvalitet varierade, och resultaten gäller inte alla.

title: The Quality of Life among Siblings of Autistic Individuals: A Scoping Review.
authors: Quatrosi G, Genovese D, Amodio E, Tripi G
abstract: Autism spectrum disorders are a heterogeneous group of neurodevelopmental disorders presenting at a tender age, defined by qualitative deficits in social interactions and communication, thus having a substantial influence on the subject's family unit. Quality of life (QoL) refers to a person's perspective of their life situation, cultural and value background, objectives, expectations, and standards. When focusing on childhood and adolescence, age-related changes should be considered. For this scoping review, the authors used three peer-review literature database sources (PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and ERIC) to delve deeper into components of the QoL of non-autistic siblings of autistic individuals. At the completion of the eligibility phase, 9 studies were included out of the 96 initial records. A total of 4/9 articles (45%) compared the non-autistic siblings of autistic individuals to the siblings of non-autistic people, while 3/9 articles (33%) compared the first group to the non-autistic siblings of patients with other chronic diseases. A total of 5/9 studies adopted specific questionnaires to evaluate QoL. Results from 6/9 articles revealed that the autism condition has varying effects on non-autistic siblings' QoL. According to the considered research, non-autistic siblings of autistic individuals experienced decreased psychological well-being, less perceived social support, increased aggressiveness and conflict-proneness, and higher levels of anxiety and stress impacting their QoL. The present findings provide important implications for additional and more punctual studies in this sector. Furthermore, as being a non-autistic sibling of an autistic individual is commonly undervalued, this review advocates the need to organize and improve support services for siblings.

sheet.es: Mañana, dedique unos minutos a preguntar a las hermanas y hermanos no autistas cómo están, y a escucharles sin prisa. Conviene pensar también en apoyos propios para ellos, como tiempo a solas con usted. La evidencia es una revisión de alcance de 9 estudios, localizados entre 96 registros iniciales, sobre la calidad de vida de hermanos no autistas. Varios estudios señalaron menor bienestar psicológico, menos apoyo social percibido y más ansiedad y estrés, aunque los efectos variaron. Sus límites: son pocos estudios, con métodos distintos, y no describen a cada familia. Muchos hermanos pueden estar bien. Los resultados no son una regla para todos.
sheet.en: Tomorrow, take a few minutes to ask the non-autistic siblings how they are doing, and listen without hurrying. It may also help to think about support just for them, such as one-to-one time with you. The evidence is a scoping review of 9 studies, chosen from 96 initial records, on the quality of life of non-autistic siblings of autistic people. Several studies reported lower psychological well-being, less perceived social support, and more anxiety and stress, though effects varied. Its limits: few studies, using different methods, and it cannot describe every family. Many siblings may be doing well. The findings are not a rule for everyone.
sheet.sv: I morgon kan du ta några minuter och fråga syskonen som inte är autistiska hur de mår, och lyssna utan brådska. Det kan också hjälpa att tänka på stöd just för dem, till exempel enskild tid med dig. Underlaget är en kartläggande översikt av 9 studier, valda bland 96 första träffar, om livskvalitet hos syskon till autistiska personer. Flera studier visade lägre psykiskt välbefinnande, mindre upplevt socialt stöd samt mer ångest och stress, men effekterna varierade. Begränsningar: få studier med olika metoder, och den kan inte beskriva varje familj. Många syskon mår kanske bra. Resultaten är ingen regel för alla.

title: An interdisciplinary nationwide complex intervention for lifespan neurodevelopmental service development: Underpinning principles and realist programme theory.
authors: Maciver D, Rutherford M, Johnston L, Curnow E, Boilson M, Murray M
abstract: Background People seeking support for neurodevelopmental differences often report waiting too long for assessment and diagnosis, as well as receiving inadequate support in educational and health settings. The National Autism Implementation Team (NAIT) developed a new national improvement programme in Scotland, focusing on assessment, diagnosis, educational inclusion, and professional learning. The NAIT programme was conducted within health and education services across the lifespan for a range of neurodevelopmental differences, including autism, developmental coordination disorder, developmental language disorder, and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder. NAIT included a multidisciplinary team, with the involvement of an expert stakeholder group, clinicians, teachers, and people with lived experience. This study explores how the NAIT programme was planned, delivered, and received over three years. Design We performed a retrospective evaluation. We collected data from review of programme documents, consultation with programme leads and consultation with professional stakeholders. A theory-based analysis was completed, drawing on the Medical Research Council Framework for developing and evaluating complex interventions, and realist analysis methods. We developed a programme theory of the contexts (C), mechanisms (M), and outcomes (O) influencing the NAIT programme, based on comparison and synthesis of evidence. A key focus was on identifying the factors that contributed to the successful implementation of NAIT activities across different domains, including practitioner, institutional and macro levels. Results On synthesis of the data, we identified the key principles underlying the NAIT programme, the activities and resources utilised by the NAIT team, 16 aspects of context, 13 mechanisms, and 17 outcome areas. Mechanisms and outcomes were grouped at practitioner level, service level and macro level. The programme theory is pertinent to observed practice changes across all stages of referral, diagnosis and support processes within health and education services for neurodivergent children and adults. Conclusions This theory-informed evaluation has resulted in a clearer and more replicable programme theory that can be used by others with similar aims. This paper illustrates the value of NAIT, as well as realist and complex interventions methodologies as tools for policymakers, practitioners, and researchers.

sheet.es: Si esperas una evaluación o apoyo escolar, puedes preguntar a los servicios cómo organizan la evaluación, el diagnóstico y la inclusión educativa, y si trabajan juntos salud y educación. Es una evaluación retrospectiva de un programa nacional en Escocia, con revisión de documentos y consultas a responsables del programa y profesionales durante tres años. Describe 16 aspectos de contexto, 13 mecanismos y 17 áreas de resultados. Sin embargo, no mide cómo cambió la vida de cada persona y se basa en un programa concreto, por lo que no sirve como regla para todos los servicios ni para todas las personas.
sheet.en: If you are waiting for an assessment or school support, you can ask services how they organise assessment, diagnosis and educational inclusion, and whether health and education work together. This was a retrospective evaluation of a national programme in Scotland, using programme documents and consultations with programme leads and professional stakeholders over three years. It described 16 aspects of context, 13 mechanisms and 17 outcome areas. However, it does not measure how each person's life changed, and it covers one programme, so it is not a rule for every service or every person.
sheet.sv: Om du väntar på utredning eller skolstöd kan du fråga vården och skolan hur de organiserar utredning, diagnos och inkludering, och om hälso- och sjukvård och skola samarbetar. Studien var en retrospektiv utvärdering av ett nationellt program i Skottland, med programdokument samt samtal med programledare och yrkespersoner under tre år. Den beskrev 16 aspekter av kontext, 13 mekanismer och 17 resultatområden. Den mäter dock inte hur varje persons liv förändrades och gäller ett enskilt program, så den är ingen regel för alla verksamheter eller alla människor.

title: The global prevalence of autism spectrum disorder: A three-level meta-analysis.
authors: Talantseva OI, Romanova RS, Shurdova EM, Dolgorukova TA, Sologub PS, Titova OS, Kleeva DF, Grigorenko EL
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is one the most disabling developmental disorders, imposing an extremely high economic burden. Obtaining as accurate prevalence estimates as possible is crucial to guide governments in planning policies for identification and intervention for individuals with ASD and their relatives. The precision of prevalence estimates can be heightened by summative analyses of the data collected around the world. To that end, we conducted a three-level mixed-effects meta-analysis. A systematic search of the Web of Science, PubMed, EMBASE, and PsycINFO databases from 2000 up to 13 July 2020 was performed, and reference lists of previous reviews and existing databases of prevalence studies were screened. Overall, 79 studies were included in the analysis of ASD and 59-in the analysis of previously existing relevant diagnoses: 30 for Autistic Disorder (AD), 15 for Asperger Syndrome (AS), and 14 for Atypical Autism (AA) and Pervasive Developmental Disorder - Not Otherwise Specified (PDD-NOS); these research reports covered the period from 1994 to 2019. Pooled prevalence estimates were 0.72% (95% CI = 0.61-0.85) for ASD, 0.25% (95% CI = 0.18-0.33) for AD, 0.13% (95% CI = 0.07-0.20) for AS, and 0.18% (95% CI = 0.10-0.28) for the combined group of AA and PDD-NOS. Estimates were higher (1) for the studies that used records-review surveillance rather than other designs; (2) in North America compared with other geographical regions; and (3) in high-income compared with lower-income countries. The highest prevalence estimates were registered in the USA. There was an increase in autism prevalence estimates over time. The prevalence was also significantly higher for children aged between 6 and 12 years compared to children under the age of 5 and over the age of 13 years. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/display_record.php?ID=CRD42019131525, identifier CRD42019131525.

sheet.es: Este estudio no ofrece una pauta para mañana por la mañana, pero sirve de contexto: las personas autistas y sus familias son numerosas, y servicios como la identificación y los apoyos deberían existir de forma estable. Si busca apoyos, puede citar que el autismo es frecuente. La evidencia es un metaanálisis que reunió 79 estudios de prevalencia de todo el mundo. Estimó 0.72% para el autismo y halló cifras más altas en Norteamérica, en países de ingresos altos y en niños de 6 a 12 años. Límites: los resultados dependen de cómo cada estudio identificó a las personas y no describen a ninguna persona concreta.
sheet.en: This study gives no routine for tomorrow morning, but it offers context: autistic people and their families are many, and identification and support services should be reliably available. If you are asking for support, you can point out that autism is common. The evidence is a meta-analysis that pooled 79 prevalence studies from around the world. It estimated 0.72% for autism and found higher figures in North America, in high-income countries and in children aged 6 to 12 years. Limits: results depend on how each study identified people, and they say nothing about any one individual.
sheet.sv: Studien ger ingen rutin för i morgon bitti, men den ger sammanhang: autistiska personer och deras familjer är många, och utredning och stöd bör finnas tillgängligt på ett stabilt sätt. Om du ber om stöd kan du peka på att autism är vanligt. Underlaget är en metaanalys som sammanställde 79 prevalensstudier från hela världen. Den uppskattade 0.72% för autism och fann högre siffror i Nordamerika, i höginkomstländer och hos barn i åldern 6 till 12 år. Begränsningar: resultaten beror på hur varje studie identifierade personer och säger ingenting om en enskild person.

title: Physiological and Psychological Effects of Parent-Delivered Traditional Thai Massage in Children With Autism: Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial.
authors: Ruan H, Eungpinichpong W, Wu H, Aonsri C
abstract: Background Although many autistic children receive massage as a complementary therapy, it is not included in evidence-based practice for autism because evidence of its efficacy is lacking. Further, prior studies have failed to identify objective indicators of core symptoms or elucidate their mechanisms. Objective We developed a parent-delivered traditional Thai massage (TTM) intervention for children with autism, aiming to experimentally determine whether children with autism truly experience positive effects from parent-delivered TTM and determine possible mechanisms of the observed effects. Methods A 2-armed, parallel randomized controlled trial was conducted between February 2022 and June 2022. Forty-eight children with autism (aged 7-12 years) were recruited from the Hainan Special Education School and randomly assigned to either a parental TTM or control group at a ratio of 1:1 based on random numbers generated with Online Research Randomizer. The generated sequences were concealed in an opaque envelope. Individuals in the parental TTM group received 16 parent-delivered TTM sessions over 8 weeks at the school's health room after school, and the control group maintained a normal daily routine. Outcomes were assessed on admission, after 8 weeks, and at a 2-month follow-up and included the effect of massage treatment on autism symptoms, measured with the Autism Treatment Evaluation Checklist score (evaluated by parents and a blinded teacher), physiological parameters (ie, heart rate variability and gait), and the Parenting Stress Index, Fourth Edition-Short Form. Results We finished all data collection on June 20, 2022. Data analysis will be started, and we expect to publish results in 2023. Conclusions This study will provide further evidence for massage treatment of autism and provide support for family-based care. Trial registration Chinese Clinical Trial Registry ChiCTR2100051355; https://tinyurl.com/3dwjxsw5. International registered report identifier (irrid) DERR1-10.2196/41839.

sheet.es: Si ya das masajes a tu hijo o hija y a ambos les resulta agradable, no hace falta dejarlo; pero este estudio aún no permite decir que el masaje mejore el autismo. Es el protocolo de un ensayo aleatorizado: 48 niños autistas de 7-12 años recibieron 16 sesiones de masaje tailandés tradicional dadas por sus familias durante 8 semanas, o siguieron su rutina normal. Se midieron síntomas, frecuencia cardíaca, marcha y estrés parental. Aún no hay resultados, así que no sabemos si funciona. Ante dudas sobre terapias, consulta con profesionales de confianza.
sheet.en: If you already give your child massage and you both enjoy it, there is no need to stop, but this study cannot yet tell us that massage helps autism. It is a trial protocol: 48 autistic children aged 7-12 years either received 16 sessions of traditional Thai massage from a parent over 8 weeks, or kept their normal routine. Researchers measured symptoms, heart rate variability, gait and parenting stress. Results are not yet reported, so we do not know whether it works. If you have questions about therapies, talk with professionals you trust.
sheet.sv: Om du redan masserar ditt barn och ni båda tycker om det behöver du inte sluta, men den här studien kan ännu inte visa att massage hjälper vid autism. Det är ett protokoll för en randomiserad studie: 48 autistiska barn i åldern 7-12 år fick antingen 16 tillfällen av traditionell thaimassage av en förälder under 8 veckor, eller behöll sin vanliga rutin. Man mätte symtom, hjärtfrekvensvariabilitet, gång och föräldrastress. Resultat finns ännu inte, så vi vet inte om det fungerar. Har du frågor om terapier, tala med yrkespersoner du litar på.

title: Evaluation of a "Picture Assisted Illustration Reinforcement" (PAIR) System for Oral Hygiene in Children with Autism: A Double-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial.
authors: Pai Khot AJ, Choudhury AR, Ankola AV, Sankeshwari RM, Hampiholi V, Hebbal M, Jalihal S, Kumar RS, Kabra L, Kotha SL
abstract: This study evaluated the potential of a novel pre-validated "Picture Assisted Illustration Reinforcement" (PAIR) communication system and conventional verbal techniques for Oral Health Education (OHE) in terms of dentition status, gingival health, oral hygiene status, and practices in 7- to 18-year-old children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). A double-blind randomized controlled trial was undertaken in a school for children with autism from July to September 2022. A total of 60 children were randomly assigned into two groups: a PAIR group ( n = 30) and a Conventional group ( n = 30). Cognition and pre-evaluation of all the children were assessed by standardized scaling measures. A pre-validated closed-ended questionnaire was administered to caregivers of both groups. At a 12-week post-intervention, a clinical examination was performed using the World Health Organization (WHO) Oral Health Assessment form 2013, gingival and Oral Hygiene Index Simplified (OHI-S). The gingival scores in the PAIR group (0.35 ± 0.12) exhibited a statistically significant decline in scores as compared to Conventional group (0.83 ± 0.37), p = 0.043. Meanwhile, the oral hygiene scores in the PAIR group and Conventional group were 1.22 ± 0.14 and 1.94 ± 0.15, respectively ( p < 0.05). A significant improvement in oral hygiene practices was observed in the PAIR group. Incorporating the PAIR technique resulted in significant progress in child cognitive ability and adaptive behavior, which reduced gingival scores and improved oral hygiene scores, consequently improving oral hygiene practices among children with ASD.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a un niño o adolescente autista, puede ayudar enseñar el cepillado con imágenes ilustradas paso a paso, en lugar de depender solo de explicaciones habladas. Puedes probar con tarjetas o dibujos de cada paso y ver si le resultan más claros. Evidencia: ensayo aleatorizado doble ciego con 60 niños autistas de 7 a 18 años en una escuela; a las 12 semanas, el grupo con imágenes (PAIR) tuvo mejores puntuaciones de encías e higiene oral que el grupo con técnicas verbales. Límites: un solo centro, muestra pequeña y seguimiento corto; cada persona es distinta y los resultados pueden no aplicarse a todas.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic child or teenager, teaching tooth brushing with step-by-step pictures may help, rather than relying only on spoken explanations. You could try cards or drawings for each step and see whether they make things clearer. Evidence: a double-blind randomized controlled trial with 60 autistic children aged 7 to 18 in one school; at 12 weeks, the picture group (PAIR) had better gum and oral hygiene scores than the group taught with verbal techniques. Limits: a single setting, a small sample and short follow-up; every person is different, so results may not apply to everyone.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar ett autistiskt barn eller en tonåring kan det hjälpa att lära ut tandborstning med bilder steg för steg i stället för att bara förklara muntligt. Du kan prova kort eller teckningar för varje steg och se om det blir tydligare. Evidens: en dubbelblind randomiserad kontrollerad studie med 60 autistiska barn i åldern 7 till 18 år på en skola; efter 12 veckor hade bildgruppen (PAIR) bättre tandköttsvärden och munhygien än gruppen som fick verbala metoder. Begränsningar: en enda miljö, litet urval och kort uppföljning; alla är olika, så resultaten gäller inte nödvändigtvis alla.

title: Adapted suicide safety plans to address self-harm, suicidal ideation, and suicide behaviours in autistic adults: protocol for a pilot randomised controlled trial.
authors: Rodgers J, Goodwin J, Nielsen E, Bhattarai N, Heslop P, Kharatikoopaei E, O'Connor RC, Ogundimu E, Ramsay SE, Steele K, Townsend E, Vale L, Walton E, Wilson C, Cassidy S
abstract: Background Suicide prevention is a national priority for the UK government. Autistic people are at greater risk of experiencing self-harm and suicidal thoughts and behaviours than the general population. Safety plans are widely used in suicide prevention but have not yet been designed with and for autistic people. We developed the first safety plan specifically targeting suicidality in autistic adults: the Autism Adapted Safety Plan (AASP). It consists of a prioritised list of hierarchical steps that can be used prior to or during a crisis to mitigate risk of self-harm and suicidal behaviour. This is a pilot study that aims to assess the feasibility and acceptability of the AASPs and the research processes, including the response rates, potential barriers and reach of AASPs, methods of recruitment, what comprises usual care, and economic evaluation methods/tools. Methods This is an external pilot randomised controlled trial of a suicide prevention tool aimed at mitigating the risk of self-harm and suicidal behaviour in autistic adults: AASPs. Participants will be assessed at baseline and followed up 1 month and 6 months later. Assessments include questions about self-harm, suicidality, service use, and their experience of the AASP/taking part in the study. Autistic adults who have a clinical autism diagnosis and self-reported history of self-harm, suicidal thoughts, or suicidal behaviours within the last 6 months will be invited to take part in the study. Informed consent will be obtained. Participants will be recruited via community and third sector services (including community settings, autism charities, and mental health charities). They may also "self-refer" into the study through social media recruitment and word of mouth. Ninety participants will be randomised to either develop an AASP or receive their usual care in a 1:1 ratio. Discussion The present study will provide an evaluation of the suitability of the processes that would be undertaken in a larger definitive study, including recruitment, randomisation, methods, questionnaires, outcome measures, treatment, and follow-up assessments. Trial registration ISRCTN70594445, Protocol v4: 8/2/22.

sheet.es: Si cuidas a una persona autista adulta que ha pensado en hacerse daño o en el suicidio, puede ser útil saber que existe un plan de seguridad creado para personas autistas: una lista ordenada de pasos para usar antes o durante una crisis. Este estudio es el protocolo de un ensayo piloto aleatorizado que probará si el plan es viable y aceptable; participarán 90 personas autistas adultas. Aún no hay resultados, así que no sabemos si el plan funciona. Hable con un profesional de salud o un servicio de crisis; ante peligro inmediato, llame al número de emergencias de su país.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic adult who has thought about self-harm or suicide, it may help to know that a safety plan designed for autistic people now exists: a prioritised list of steps to use before or during a crisis. This study is the protocol for a pilot randomised trial testing whether the plan is feasible and acceptable, with 90 autistic adults taking part. There are no results yet, so we do not know whether the plan works. Please talk to a clinician, a health service or a crisis service; in immediate danger, call your country's emergency number.
sheet.sv: Om du stöttar en autistisk vuxen som har funderat på självskada eller självmord kan det vara bra att veta att det finns en säkerhetsplan utformad för autistiska personer: en prioriterad lista med steg att använda före eller under en kris. Studien är protokollet för en randomiserad pilotstudie som testar om planen är genomförbar och acceptabel, med 90 autistiska vuxna. Det finns inga resultat än, så vi vet inte om planen fungerar. Kontakta en läkare, en vårdtjänst eller en krisjour; vid akut fara, ring ditt lands nödnummer.

title: What do Cochrane systematic reviews say about interventions for autism spectrum disorders?
authors: Lyra L, Rizzo LE, Sunahara CS, Pachito DV, Latorraca COC, Martimbianco ALC, Riera R
journal: Sao Paulo medical journal = Revista paulista de medicina
abstract: Context and objective: Autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) include autistic disorder, Asperger's disorder and pervasive developmental disorder. The manifestations of ASDs can have an important impact on learning and social functioning that may persist during adulthood. The aim here was to summarize the evidence from Cochrane systematic reviews on interventions for ASDs. Design and setting: Review of systematic reviews, conducted within the Discipline of Evidence-Based Medicine, Escola Paulista de Medicina, Universidade Federal de São Paulo. Methods: We included and summarized the results from Cochrane systematic reviews on interventions for ASDs. Results: Seventeen reviews were included. These found weak evidence of benefits from acupuncture, gluten and casein-free diets, early intensive behavioral interventions, music therapy, parent-mediated early interventions, social skill groups, Theory of Mind cognitive model, aripiprazole, risperidone, tricyclic antidepressants and selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRI); this last only for adults. No benefits were found for sound therapies, chelating agents, hyperbaric oxygen therapy, omega-3, secretin, vitamin B6/magnesium and SSRI for children. Conclusion: Acupuncture, gluten and casein-free diets, early intensive behavioral interventions, music therapy, parent-mediated early interventions, social skill groups and the Theory of Mind cognitive model seem to have benefits for patients with autism spectrum disorders (very low to low-quality evidence). Aripiprazole, risperidone, tricyclic antidepressants and SSRI (this last only for adults) also showed some benefits, although associated with higher risk of adverse events. Experimental studies to confirm a link between probable therapies and the disease, and then high-quality long-term clinical trials, are needed.

sheet.es: Si te preguntas qué apoyos tienen respaldo, esta revisión sugiere que ninguno es una respuesta segura para todas las personas autistas. Conviene probar con calma, observar qué ayuda a esa persona concreta y contar con su opinión. Es una revisión de revisiones Cochrane: reunió 17 revisiones sobre intervenciones para el autismo. Encontró pruebas débiles de beneficio en algunas, como la música o los grupos de habilidades sociales, y ningún beneficio en otras, como las terapias de sonido. La calidad de las pruebas era muy baja o baja. Algunos estudios evaluaron medicamentos; las decisiones médicas corresponden siempre a un profesional clínico.
sheet.en: If you are wondering which supports have evidence behind them, this review suggests none is a sure answer for every autistic person. Try things calmly, notice what helps that particular person, and include their views. It is a review of Cochrane reviews, bringing together 17 reviews on autism interventions. It found weak evidence of benefit for some, such as music therapy or social skill groups, and no benefit for others, such as sound therapies. The quality of the evidence was very low to low. Some studies looked at medicines; medical decisions belong to a clinician.
sheet.sv: Om du undrar vilka stöd som har belägg visar den här översikten att inget är ett säkert svar för alla autistiska personer. Prova lugnt, lägg märke till vad som hjälper just den personen och ta med hens egna åsikter. Det är en översikt av Cochrane-översikter som sammanställde 17 översikter om insatser vid autism. Den fann svaga belägg för nytta av vissa, som musikterapi eller sociala färdighetsgrupper, och ingen nytta av andra, som ljudterapier. Kvaliteten på bevisen var mycket låg till låg. Vissa studier gällde läkemedel; medicinska beslut hör hemma hos en kliniker.

title: Concordance of multiple informant assessment of school-based social skills intervention and association with child outcomes: Results from a randomized trial.
authors: Tagavi DM, Ahlers K, Bravo A, McVey AJ, Locke J
abstract: Background Fidelity, or the degree to which an intervention is implemented as designed, is essential for effective implementation. There has been a growing emphasis on assessing fidelity of evidence-based practices for autistic children in schools. Fidelity measurement should be multidimensional and focus on core intervention components and assess their link with program outcomes. This study evaluated the relation between intervention fidelity ratings from multiple sources, tested the relation between fidelity ratings and child outcomes, and determined the relations between core intervention components and child outcomes in a study of an evidence-based psychosocial intervention designed to promote inclusion of autistic children at school, Remaking Recess. Method This study extends from a larger randomized controlled trial examining the effect of implementation support on Remaking Recess fidelity and child outcomes. Schools were randomized to receive the intervention or the intervention plus implementation support. Observers, intervention coaches, and school personnel completed fidelity measures to rate completion and quality of intervention delivery. A measure of peer engagement served as the child outcome. Pearson correlation coefficients were calculated to determine concordance between raters. Two sets of hierarchical linear models were conducted using fidelity indices as predictors of peer engagement. Results Coach- and self-rated completion and quality scores, observer- and self-rated quality scores, and observer- and coach-rated quality fidelity scores were significantly correlated. Higher observer-rated completion and quality fidelity scores were predictors of higher peer engagement scores. No single intervention component emerged as a significant predictor of peer engagement. Conclusions This study demonstrates the importance of using a multidimensional approach for measuring fidelity, testing the link between fidelity and child outcomes, and examining how core intervention components may be associated with child outcomes. Future research should clarify how to improve multi-informant reports to provide "good enough" ratings of fidelity that provide meaningful information about outcomes in community settings. Plain language summary Fidelity is defined as how closely an intervention is administered in the way the creators intended. Fidelity is important because it allows researchers to determine what exactly is leading to changes. In recent years, there has been an interest in examining fidelity of interventions for autistic children who receive services in school. This study looked at the relationship between fidelity ratings from multiple individuals, the relationship between fidelity and child outcomes, and the relationship between individual intervention component and child changes in a study of Remaking Recess, an intervention for autistic children at school. Schools were randomly selected to receive the intervention only or the intervention plus implementation support from the research team. Observers, intervention coaches, and individuals delivering the intervention themselves completed fidelity measures. Child engagement with peers was measured before and after the intervention. Several measures of self-, coach-, and observer-report fidelity were associated with each other. Higher observer-reported fidelity was associated with higher child peer engagement scores. No single intervention step was linked to child peer engagement and both treatment groups had similar outcomes in terms of fidelity. This study shows the importance of having multiple raters assess different parts of intervention fidelity, looking at the link between fidelity and child outcomes, and seeing how individual intervention steps may be related to outcomes. Future research should aim to find out which types of fidelity ratings are "good enough" to lead to positive changes following treatment so that those aspects can be used and targeted in the future.

sheet.es: Si apoyas la inclusión de un niño autista en el recreo, conviene que el programa se aplique tal como fue diseñado y que más de una persona observe cómo va. En este ensayo aleatorizado, los centros escolares aplicaron Remaking Recess, una intervención escolar para favorecer la inclusión; observadores, coaches y personal escolar valoraron cómo se aplicaba. Una mayor fidelidad según los observadores se asoció con más interacción con los compañeros. Ningún componente concreto destacó por sí solo. El estudio no prueba que la fidelidad cause esos resultados, ni sirve como regla para cada niño.
sheet.en: If you support an autistic child's inclusion at recess, it helps when the programme is delivered as designed and more than one person looks at how it is going. In this randomized trial, schools delivered Remaking Recess, a school intervention to promote inclusion, and observers, coaches and school staff rated how it was delivered. Higher observer-rated fidelity was linked to more peer engagement. No single component stood out on its own. The study cannot show that fidelity causes these outcomes, and it is not a rule for every child.
sheet.sv: Om du stödjer en autistisk elevs inkludering på rasten hjälper det att programmet genomförs som det är tänkt och att fler än en person följer hur det går. I denna randomiserade studie genomförde skolor Remaking Recess, en skolinsats för inkludering, och observatörer, coacher och skolpersonal bedömde genomförandet. Högre fidelitet enligt observatörerna hängde ihop med mer engagemang med kamrater. Ingen enskild komponent stack ut. Studien visar inte att fidelitet orsakar resultaten och är ingen regel för varje barn.

title: Comprehensive ABA-based interventions in the treatment of children with autism spectrum disorder - a meta-analysis.
authors: Eckes T, Buhlmann U, Holling HD, Möllmann A
abstract: Background Many studies display promising results for interventions that are based on Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) in the treatment of autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Methods This meta-analysis assessed the effects of such treatments on developmental outcomes in children with ASD and on parental stress based on 11 studies with 632 participants. Results Compared to treatment as usual, minimal or no treatment, comprehensive ABA-based interventions showed medium effects for intellectual functioning (standardized mean difference SMD = 0.51, 95% CI [0.09; 0.92]) and adaptive behavior (SMD = 0.37, 95% CI [0.03; 0.70]). Language abilities, symptom severity or parental stress did not improve beyond the improvement in control groups. Moderator analyses indicate that language abilities at intake could influence the effect sizes and the influence of treatment intensity might decrease with older age. Conclusions Practical implications and limitations are discussed.

sheet.es: Si valoráis una intervención basada en ABA, mirad qué objetivos persigue, si respeta el ritmo y el bienestar de vuestro hijo o hija autista, y no esperéis cambios en todo. Es un metaanálisis de 11 estudios con 632 participantes, niños con TEA. Frente a ningún tratamiento, tratamiento mínimo o habitual, hubo efectos medios en funcionamiento intelectual y conducta adaptativa. El lenguaje, la gravedad de los síntomas y el estrés parental no mejoraron más que en los grupos control. El resumen no detalla la calidad de los estudios y los resultados no valen para todas las personas. Comentad las decisiones con profesionales.
sheet.en: If you are considering an ABA-based programme, look at what goals it sets, whether it respects your autistic child's pace and wellbeing, and don't expect change in every area. This meta-analysis pooled 11 studies with 632 participants, children with ASD. Compared with no, minimal or usual treatment, there were medium effects on intellectual functioning and adaptive behavior. Language abilities, symptom severity and parental stress did not improve beyond control groups. The abstract gives no detail on study quality, and results do not apply to every person. Talk decisions through with professionals.
sheet.sv: Om ni överväger ett ABA-baserat program, titta på vilka mål det har, om det respekterar ert autistiska barns tempo och välmående, och förvänta er inte förändring på alla områden. Det är en metaanalys av 11 studier med 632 deltagare, barn med ASD. Jämfört med ingen, minimal eller vanlig behandling sågs medelstora effekter på intellektuell funktion och adaptivt beteende. Språkliga förmågor, symtomnivå och föräldrastress förbättrades inte mer än i kontrollgrupperna. Sammanfattningen beskriver inte studiernas kvalitet, och resultaten gäller inte alla. Diskutera besluten med yrkespersoner.

title: Autistic traits, emotion regulation, and sensory sensitivities in children and adults with Misophonia.
authors: Rinaldi LJ, Simner J, Koursarou S, Ward J
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Misophonia is an unusually strong aversion to everyday sounds such as chewing, crunching, or breathing. Previous studies have suggested that rates of autism might be elevated in misophonia, and here we examine this claim in detail. We present a comprehensive review of the relevant literature, and two empirical studies examining children and adults with misophonia. We tested 142 children and 379 adults for traits associated with autism (i.e., attention-to-detail, attention-switching, social processing, communication, imagination, emotion regulation, and sensory sensitivity across multiple domains). Our data show that autistic traits are indeed elevated in misophonics compared to controls. We discuss our findings in relation to models of the interface between autism, sensory sensitivities, and the specific features of misophonia.

sheet.es: Si una persona autista o su familia notan un rechazo muy fuerte a sonidos cotidianos como masticar o respirar, puede ser útil considerar que la sensibilidad sensorial y la regulación emocional están relacionadas. Ofrecer pausas, auriculares o un lugar tranquilo en las comidas puede ayudar. La evidencia es una revisión de la literatura con dos estudios empíricos: 142 niños y 379 adultos con misofonía, comparados con controles, mostraron más rasgos autistas. Sin embargo, no demuestra causas ni significa que toda persona con misofonía sea autista, ni que toda persona autista tenga misofonía. Cada experiencia es distinta; ante dudas, conviene consultar a un profesional.
sheet.en: If an autistic person or their family notices a very strong aversion to everyday sounds like chewing or breathing, it may help to know that sensory sensitivity and emotion regulation can be connected. Offering breaks, headphones or a quiet spot at mealtimes may ease things. The evidence is a literature review plus two empirical studies: 142 children and 379 adults with misophonia, compared with controls, showed more autistic traits. However, it cannot show causes, and it does not mean everyone with misophonia is autistic, or that every autistic person has misophonia. Each experience is different; if you have questions, a professional can help.
sheet.sv: Om en autistisk person eller dennes familj märker ett mycket starkt obehag inför vardagsljud som tuggande eller andning kan det vara bra att veta att sensorisk känslighet och känsloreglering kan hänga ihop. Pauser, hörlurar eller en lugn plats vid måltider kan underlätta. Underlaget är en litteraturgenomgång plus två empiriska studier: 142 barn och 379 vuxna med misofoni hade, jämfört med kontroller, fler autistiska drag. Studien kan dock inte visa orsaker, och den betyder inte att alla med misofoni är autistiska eller att alla autistiska personer har misofoni. Varje upplevelse är olika; vid frågor kan en yrkesperson hjälpa till.
